As collagen production declines with age, supplements are marketed for skin, hair, nails, bones, joints and muscle support. Collagen is a structural protein made from amino acids and nutrients including vitamin C, zinc and copper. The 28 collagen types include I, II and III, which are most common in supplements. Sources include fish, cows, pigs and chickens; gelatin and hydrolysed collagen are also available. Hydrolysed collagen is broken into easily digested molecules, enabling rapid absorption, and research suggests it may be the most effective form.

Potential benefits include improved skin firmness, hydration and growth, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails, bone support, joint-pain relief, and support for tendons, ligaments, fascia and muscle repair. Evidence for thicker hair is limited to mouse studies. Study doses range from 2.5 grams daily for joint pain, skin and hydration to 5 grams for bone density, 15 grams for muscle mass with resistance training, and up to 40 milligrams for joint health. Manufacturers commonly recommend at least 12 weeks’ use. A balanced diet and third-party-tested products are advised, while research remains ongoing.

Sensient Technologies reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, beating Zacks’ $0.78 estimate by $0.02, with a 9.13% net margin and 16.73% return on equity. It declared a $0.30 quarterly dividend. KeyCorp raised its price target to $84 with an “overweight” rating, while Zacks upgraded the stock to “hold.”

XYZprinting invited customers and resellers to demonstrate the MfgPro220 xPF ultrafast 3D printer at booth #2142 at the Fort Worth Convention Center, April 24–28, 2018. Priced at $19,950, the “factory-in-a-box” printer has a 16-liter build volume and supports functional prototyping, production tooling and end-use part manufacturing. Its software, sensors, machine-learning algorithms and onboard/cloud controls optimize printing, provide diagnostics and enable local or remote operation of one or multiple printers. LSPc technology and a structured light matrix enable speeds up to 1Z cm per minute, reducing precision-part print cycles from hours to minutes. XYZprinting also announced a three-way partnership with BEGO and Nexa3D to advance digital dentistry, with BEGO exclusively marketing a special-purpose Nexa3D dental printer manufactured by XYZprinting.
A non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint examines bioimpedance phase-angle clusters as an alternative to body mass index; it should not guide clinical practice.

The lecture introduces MIT’s course on discrete stochastic processes and emphasizes that the central challenge in probability is not merely solving well-posed exercises but choosing models that appropriately represent uncertain real-world problems. Although mathematical calculations may be correct, a poorly chosen model can still produce poor decisions, as illustrated by applications to finance, data compression, and risk assessment. Modeling requires balancing simplicity against sufficient detail; Whitehead’s advice to “seek simplicity and distrust it” reflects the danger of retaining a simple model without sufficient evidence. Probability models should therefore be constructed with attention to the problem’s essential features rather than excessive detail.

The course, originally developed to unify communication, control, networking, and queuing theory, now covers broader applications. Planned topics include the relationship between real-world and mathematical probability, discrete stochastic processes, counting, Poisson, renewal, and Markov processes, random walks, martingales, applications, Kolmogorov’s axioms, independence, experiments, and random variables.

Games of chance provide an intuitive introduction to probability because repeated trials reveal relative frequencies and odds, whereas many decisions in life involve uncertainty that cannot be resolved through repetition. Probability is used to express likelihoods and support risk and cost-benefit judgments. The coin-toss example shows that events treated as random may be deterministic at a deeper level, so mathematical random models can be approximations rather than complete descriptions. Consequently, students must learn both mathematical techniques and the judgment required to construct useful models.

A probability model contains a sample space, a collection of events that are subsets of the sample space, and probabilities assigned to those events. For uncountable sample spaces, not every subset can be an event; this restriction connects probability to measure theory. Kolmogorov’s axioms require the whole sample space to have probability one, event probabilities to be nonnegative, and the probability of a countable union of disjoint events to equal the sum of their probabilities. These axioms imply, among other results, that the empty event has probability zero, an event’s complement has probability one minus its probability, event probabilities are monotone under set inclusion, and the union bound holds.

A discrete stochastic process is a probability model whose sample points describe sequences of random variables indexed by discrete time. Such models often extend over an effectively infinite time horizon so that systems need not be designed around a fixed expiration date. Processes to be studied include counting processes, useful for modeling arrivals and departures in queues; Poisson and renewal processes; Markov processes, in which the present state summarizes the relevant past; and random walks and martingales. In applications, probability and stochastic processes support work involving communication and computer networks, queuing, risk and catastrophe management, operations research, biology, medicine, optics, control systems, and the analysis of system failures.

Two events are independent when the probability of their intersection equals the product of their probabilities. Independent probability models can be combined on the Cartesian product of their sample spaces, and the resulting product model also satisfies Kolmogorov’s axioms. The treatment of two dice illustrates a recurring modeling issue: calculations may treat otherwise indistinguishable outcomes as distinguishable, so different chosen models can yield apparent disagreement.

A random variable is defined as a function from sample points to finite real values such that the inverse images of real-number thresholds are events; analogous conditions hold jointly for several random variables. Every such variable has a distribution function. Discrete variables have probability mass functions and staircase-shaped distributions, continuous variables have densities, and mixed or other distributions are also possible. The lecture closes by encouraging rigorous but understandable proof: arguments should be repeatedly checked and refined so that obvious gaps or counterexamples are removed.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016. The company designs, manufactures, and sells fully electric vehicles and Tesla Energy products. It reported 133,944,622 common shares outstanding as of April 29, 2016.

Revenue increased to $1.147 billion from $939.9 million, with automotive revenue of $1.026 billion and services and other revenue of $121.0 million. Gross profit declined to $252.5 million from $260.1 million, and gross margin fell to 22.0% from 27.7%, primarily due to product mix, partially offset by lease-related revenue and material cost savings. Operating expenses rose to $500.7 million from $362.5 million, producing an operating loss of $248.2 million versus $102.4 million. Net loss increased to $282.3 million from $154.2 million, or $2.13 per diluted share versus $1.22.

Cash and cash equivalents increased to $1.442 billion from $1.197 billion at year-end. The company used $249.6 million in operating activities and $233.8 million in investing activities, while financing activities provided $715.4 million. Total assets were $9.192 billion, total liabilities were $8.179 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $970.4 million.

Accounting disclosures addressed revenue recognition, resale value guarantees, vehicle leasing, warranties, inventory valuation, stock-based compensation, foreign currency hedges, income taxes, and financial instrument fair values. Tesla used yen-denominated forward contracts to hedge certain inventory purchases. The 2018 convertible notes were classified as current because holders could convert them during the second quarter of 2016; the 2019 and 2021 notes remained long-term debt. Tesla had $565 million outstanding under its asset-based credit facility at March 31, repaid $350 million in April, and remained in compliance with the facility’s covenants.

Tesla continued producing the Model S and Model X, produced 15,510 vehicles in the quarter, including approximately 2,650 Model X vehicles, and had delivered more than 122,000 vehicles through March 31. The company unveiled the Model 3 and received more than 325,000 reservations within one week. Management expected Model 3 volume production and deliveries in late 2017, 80,000–90,000 Model S and Model X deliveries during 2016, and annual production of 500,000 vehicles by 2018.

The company continued expanding retail, service, and Supercharger infrastructure and developing the Gigafactory, where cell production was expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2016. Management expected 2016 capital expenditures to be approximately 50% above its prior $1.5 billion estimate and operating expenses to increase 20%–25% from 2015. It also anticipated improved automotive gross margin and profitability in the fourth quarter of 2016.

Risks included supplier shortages and reliance on single-source suppliers, international expansion, vehicle residual values, customer financing exposure, foreign exchange fluctuations, and the complexity and cost of the Gigafactory. A securities class action dismissed with prejudice remained pending on appeal.

The Weather Channel is launching a 3.2MB Android app in emerging markets across Asia, Latin America, and Africa. It uses IBM mesh networking, Bluetooth, and Wi‑Fi to relay information directly between phones when centralized networks fail, reaching devices 200–500 feet away. Designed for older 2G networks, it requires no network reconfiguration and uses digital signatures to verify trusted, unmodified messages. Its effectiveness depends on sufficient user adoption.

Bell Academy received a Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi grant in November 2016 to build an indoor P.E. facility behind the school. Parent and community volunteers constructed the building, which includes basketballs, exercise mats, stack cups, and hula-hoops. Teacher Joyce Aycock said the new space enables students to move around, make noise, and play music more freely, while students reported more physical activities and less noise than the former open indoor area. A horizontal rock-climbing wall is planned before the building’s ribbon-cutting ceremony.

The author returns a House bill that would grant states 20,000 acres of public land for each congressional representative, plus additional grants for new representatives. The estimated 6.06 million acres would be worth $7.575 million at $1.25 per acre. States must establish at least one college within five years or repay proceeds from land sales, replace any losses, and use land scrip if they lack qualifying public lands.

The author opposes the bill as both inexpedient and unconstitutional. Its land grants and scrip would flood the market, depress public-land prices, and largely eliminate an important federal revenue source when government finances are already strained. The bill would also blur federal and state authority, encourage states to seek federal support for domestic purposes, and encourage speculation in public lands, harming new states and actual settlers.

Federal officials could not ensure that the grants served their intended educational purposes once transferred to the states. The bill could also weaken existing colleges by creating federally supported rivals, while congressional representatives might compete over how funds were distributed within their states. Direct support for agricultural and mechanical professorships in existing colleges would be preferable.

Constitutionally, the author argues that Congress’s power to “dispose of” federal property permits sale, not unlimited giveaway. Public lands are held in trust and remain subject to the limits of federal power; converting taxed funds into land does not create new authority to give that land away for state purposes. Earlier educational land grants to new states, however, were defended as promoting settlement and increasing land values.

Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus will release for Nintendo Switch on June 29, digitally and physically, with physical cartridges requiring a download. Bethesda has also ported Doom and Skyrim to the popular hybrid console.

The drive concept pairs a tight end running a 10–12-yard basic in-cut route with a slot receiver on a 3–4-yard shallow crossing route from the same side. It creates a triangle read, stresses linebackers, and can function as either a primary or secondary read. The concept is effective against man coverage and Cover 4 but less effective against Cover 2 and Cover 3, where numerous underneath defenders outnumber the running back, tight end, and slot receiver.

Against man coverage, the tight end and slot receiver should keep moving; against zone coverage, they should sit in open voids. The quarterback may consider a pre-snap post-route throw against Cover 4 or a favorable one-on-one matchup. The progression is X receiver on a go route, slot receiver on the shallow cross, tight end on the basic route, and running back on a check-down. Variations include using drive with a bunch formation to create picks and rubs, or attaching it to backside schemes for a quick throw against a blitz and a reliable outlet.

The council says it is coordinating road and utility works, avoiding clashes with the Derriford Transport Scheme and requesting night or off-peak work to reduce congestion. Measures include limiting temporary signals on Tamerton Foliot Road, manually operating lights elsewhere, monitoring traffic and adjusting signal timings, suspending bus-lane restrictions on Tavistock Road, and changing slip-road arrangements at Budshead Roundabout. Proposed lane-marking and signage changes are undergoing safety review. Planned works and disruption alerts are available via the council’s roadworks page, email subscriptions, media, social channels and roadside signs.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS into tertiary institutions as delayed student funding has prompted protests. Minister Naledi Pandor called unresolved funding and data-system problems unacceptable and instructed urgent action, including bursary agreements and closer cooperation with institutional aid offices. The department added R7.2 billion in 2018 for university and TVET bursaries, while NSFAS’s baseline allocation was set to rise from R9.9 billion in 2017–18 to over R35.3 billion in 2020–21, supported by R105 million for administrative capacity. The DA plans to seek an urgent NSFAS meeting over unpaid allowances and unanswered questions on numbers affected, causes, and payment timelines.

ADT appears undervalued versus newly listed peer Verisure, supported by strong revenue growth, improving profitability, and a high share of recurring revenue. Partnerships with Google and State Farm, ongoing debt reduction, and aggressive buybacks boost shareholder yield to 11%. Customer churn and static subscriber counts remain challenges, though AI, remote assistance, and smart home investments aim to improve retention. A 12-14x P/E implies 33%+ upside. The author discloses a beneficial long ADT position and notes past performance is no guarantee of future results. Article links and two charts spanning October 6-10, 2025 with values of 8.385-8.79 follow.

U.S. minister H.N. Allen reported that rebel Kim Ok-kiun, a refugee in Japan, was assassinated in Shanghai by Korean Hong Chong-oo. After Japan removed Hong from the Korean legation for examination, Chinese authorities sent him and Kim’s body to Korea. Kim’s body was mutiled and displayed, prompting Japan’s minister to remonstrate; other representatives advised against interference in the native custom.

U.S. envoy Sill reported growing unrest in Korea’s southern provinces, where populations were revolting against oppressive governors and officials, killing some and driving out others. Officials feared further uprisings, while government troops sent to the area had no apparent effect. At the government’s request, Sill asked Admiral Skerrett to send a ship to Chemulpo, recalled American missionaries from the interior for safety, and suggested more frequent U.S. ship visits would have a salutary moral effect.

The document specifies the Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate format and AMD Key Distribution System (KDS) interface for retrieving certificates used with AMD SEV-SNP. VCEK certificates are X.509v3 certificates associated with a chip-specific ECDSA key and a specific Trusted Compute Base (TCB) version. Certificates are generated per request and are not stored by KDS.

The certificate chain consists of a product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK) and AMD SEV Key (ASK), which issues VCEK certificates. Product names are determined through CPUID Family/Model/Stepping information and are case-sensitive when used in URLs; Siena uses Genoa root-key details. ARK and ASK certificates are available from AMD’s developer site and through KDS.

VCEK certificates contain custom extensions describing TCB elements and the specific silicon stepping. Family 19h products use 64-byte hardware IDs, while Family 1Ah products use 8-byte IDs. Certificates are backdated one day before issuance to reduce clock-related verification failures and are otherwise valid for seven years.

The KDS provides an HTTPS interface using TLS 1.2 for retrieving VCEK certificates, certificate chains, and certificate revocation lists. Certificate chains are returned in PEM format, while CRLs use DER format. VCEK requests specify the product, hardware ID, and security patch level parameters; omitted parameters are treated as zero, with defined value ranges. Responses may include HTTP 429 rate-limit errors with a Retry-After value, HTTP 404 for unsupported URLs or nonexistent device IDs, and HTTP 400 for malformed parameters or excessive SPL values.

Customers may request certificates using legal SPL values above currently released firmware versions, allowing certificates for anticipated TCB versions to be prefetched and cached locally.

Joe Bryant’s Week 10 fantasy football report analyzes passing and rushing matchups using recent four-week performance and fantasy points allowed, while cautioning that matchup analysis is only one tool for deciding starters.

Passing games are divided into five tiers. “Locks” favoring offenses include New Orleans–San Francisco, San Diego–Seattle, Oakland–Kansas City, Green Bay–Minnesota, Indianapolis–Chicago, and Kansas City–Oakland. Notable selections include Jeff Blake, Joe Horn and Ricky Williams; Jim Harbaugh with Freddie Jones as San Diego’s primary target; Rich Gannon; Brett Favre with Bill Schroeder favored over Antonio Freeman; Peyton Manning with Marvin Harrison and Edgerrin James; and Elvis Grbac with Derrick Alexander and Tony Gonzalez.

“Prime” passing matchups include Carolina–St. Louis, Buffalo–New England, Miami–Detroit, Chicago–Indianapolis, Seattle–San Diego, and Minnesota–Green Bay. The report highlights possible beneficiaries including Donald Hayes, Muhsin Muhammad and Biakabutuka; Doug Flutie, Eric Moulds and Jay Reimersma; Jay Fiedler, Orlando Gadsden and Leslie Shepherd; Jim Miller and Marcus Robinson; Jon Kitna and Derrick Mayes; and Daunte Culpepper with Cris Carter and Randy Moss.

“Even” passing matchups cover Detroit–Miami, St. Louis–Carolina, Baltimore–Cincinnati, Denver–the Jets, the Jets–Denver, and Tampa Bay–Atlanta. The analysis discusses Trent Green and Isaac Bruce, Trent Dilfer, Qadry Ismail and Shannon Sharpe, Brian Greise with Rod Smith, Ed McCaffrey and Terrell Davis’ anticipated return, Vinny Testeverde with Wayne Chrebet and Laveranues Coles, and Shaun King continuing to target Keyshawn Johnson.

“Downside” passing matchups include Washington–Arizona, Atlanta–Tampa Bay, Dallas–Philadelphia, San Francisco–New Orleans, the Giants–Cleveland, and Philadelphia–Dallas. Washington quarterback Brad Johnson is out with a knee ligament sprain, and Jeff George will start against Arizona’s strong pass defense. Other calls favor Chris Chandler with Terance Mathis, Randall Cunningham with James McKnight and Raghib Ismail, Jeff Garcia with Terrell Owens and Jerry Rice, Kerry Collins with Amani Toomer and Ike Hilliard, and Donovan McNabb with Charles Johnson.

“Defensive slam dunks” are Tennessee–Pittsburgh, Cincinnati–Baltimore, Cleveland–the Giants, Arizona–Washington, and Pittsburgh–Tennessee. The report particularly avoids Steve McNair, Akili Smith and Peter Warrick, while identifying Tennessee tight end Frank Wycheck as a possible exception against Pittsburgh.

Rushing “locks” include Stephen Davis against Arizona, Ron Dayne and Tiki Barber against Cleveland, Curtis Martin against Denver, Edgerrin James against Chicago, Ricky Williams against San Francisco, and Warrick Dunn and Mike Alstott against Atlanta. “Prime” rushing matchups include Terrell Davis against the Jets, Marshall Faulk against Carolina, San Diego’s expected running-back committee against Seattle, and Philadelphia’s uncertain committee against Dallas.

“Even” rushing matchups include Jamal Anderson, Sammy Morris and Shawn Bryson, Lamar Smith, Jamal Lewis, Emmitt Smith, James Allen, Napoleon Kaufman, and Ahman Green. “Downside” rushing matchups include Biakabutuka against St. Louis, Robert Smith against Green Bay, the Raiders’ running backs against Oakland, Shaun Alexander and Ricky Watters against San Diego, James Stewart against Miami, Corey Dillon against Baltimore, and Thomas Jones and Michael Pittman against Washington.

Rushing “defensive slam dunks” are Cleveland–the Giants, San Francisco–New Orleans, New England–Buffalo, Tennessee–Pittsburgh, and Pittsburgh–Tennessee. Travis Prentice, Charlie Garner, J.R. Redmond and Kevin Faulk, Eddie George, and Jerome Bettis are all highlighted as facing strongly favorable defenses. A news update also reports that Brad Johnson could miss two to four weeks, while Washington receivers Albert Connell and James Thrash are probable and Irving Fryar is questionable.

Mauricio Pochettino named a 26-player U.S. men’s national team roster for friendlies on Oct. 10 in Austin, Texas, and Oct. 14 in Commerce City, Colorado, with players reporting for camp Oct. 4. Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie headline the mostly settled squad following experimentation in September. Antonee Robinson received his first 2025 call-up after knee surgery, while McKennie returned after missing the March Concacaf Nations League. Pulisic had six goals and two assists for AC Milan. Several players were omitted because of injuries or selection decisions, including a Borussia M’gladbach defender and a Norwich City forward. The passage also lists the roster by position, presents additional international soccer and transfer headlines, and ends with ESPN privacy and cookie notices.

UPMSP will announce the UP Board Class 10 and Class 12 results for 2018 on April 29 at 12:30 p.m. Results will be available at upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in, with SMS access via 56263. The exams were held from February 6–22 and February 6–March 12, respectively. In 2016–17, 34,04,571 students appeared for Class 10 and 26,24,681 for Class 12, with both exams recording an 81.6% pass rate.

The team described a tight checking contest, with Hasek aggressive around the net and Detroit making adjustments. Defensive breakdowns and frustration limited scoring. The focus is on tightening play from the defensive zone, reviewing mistakes, and supporting the coaching staff’s lineup decisions.

The invention describes a vehicle sensing and driver-assistance system using radar sensors, and optionally cameras or other sensors, to detect objects around the vehicle. Each radar sensor includes transmitting and receiving antennas arranged as a two-dimensional array. A control applies two-dimensional MIMO processing to the antenna outputs, creating an enlarged virtual aperture and improved horizontal and vertical accuracy and resolution.

An illustrated embodiment uses 12 transmitting antennas in three rows and 16 receiving antennas in four columns, configured as 192 virtual receivers. Other two-dimensional arrangements may be used. Each transmitter emits an independently identifiable waveform, allowing received echoes to be associated with individual transmitting antennas.

Detected objects may trigger visual, audible, or haptic alerts, vehicle steering or braking controls, or object highlighting on displays. The system may support autonomous or semi-autonomous driving, automated parking, blind-spot and cross-traffic detection, lane-change assistance, emergency braking, pedestrian detection, turn assistance, and collision mitigation. Radar data may also be fused with camera imagery for enhanced object detection, and exterior cameras may provide forward, rearward, side, 360-degree surround, top-down, or bird’s-eye views.

Jennifer Thompson was raped at 22 and identified Ronald Cotton as her assailant, leading to his conviction. Eleven years later, post-conviction DNA testing showed Bobby Poole had raped her and Cotton was innocent. Thompson said trauma and questioning can alter memories and that compensation cannot heal the harm. After exoneration, she and Cotton became best friends and reconciled. She found Healing Justice, which brings harmed parties together to share stories; Cotton attends its retreats.

Russia’s central bank cut its key rate to 9.25% from 9.75%, deeper than analysts expected, and hinted at more cuts as inflation fell. It projected 4% annual consumer-price growth by end-2017 and reiterated planned gradual cuts in the second and third quarters.

The government shutdown shows little sign of quick resolution, but an Oct. 15 pay date for 1.3 million active-duty troops could pressure Congress and the White House to compromise. Prediction markets assign a 71% chance the shutdown will extend beyond Oct. 14. A short-term continuing resolution is considered the most likely outcome, though the shutdown could continue into November. Other potential catalysts include TSA staffing, delayed service-member mortgage payments, and Oct. 13 benefits and Nov. 1 Obamacare enrollment deadlines. President Trump has threatened that temporary layoffs could become permanent if no agreement is reached.

Day 1 of the seven-day 2025 World Grand Prix of Darts featured an eight-game slate. Rob Cross won a last-leg decider, Ratajski beat the top seed 2–0 with a 95.94 average, Menzies eliminated the eighth seed, and Cullen recovered from 0–2 in set two to defeat Wade 2–0.

Ghana’s major gold miners welcomed new export-certification tests intended to tighten oversight and improve taxation. The Precious Minerals Marketing Company is working with the Chamber of Mines on the directive, which provides access to gold rooms, assay samples and pre-shipment sealing. Ghana earned $5.78 billion from gold exports last year, while authorities pursue about $5 billion in unaccounted shipments linked to smuggling.

According to a Weekly Standard report, Edina Public Schools in Minnesota introduce students to “white privilege” as early as kindergarten; K–2 pupils at Highlands Elementary participate in the Melanin Project by coloring hand tracings by skin tone and displaying a message that everyone is special. Separately, Michigan State University professor Shreena Gandhi and Lillie Wolff argue that U.S. yoga is tied to white supremacy, colonialism, cultural appropriation, and capitalist exploitation.

In his farewell address, the departing U.S. president thanks Vice President Mondale, his Cabinet, staff, and the American people, and pledges his support for the president-elect and a smooth transition. He describes the presidency as powerful but dependent on popular consent, congressional approval, public scrutiny, and open debate. He warns that special interests can distort the national interest, arguing for a strong presidency that represents all Americans.

Addressing global challenges, he identifies nuclear destruction, environmental degradation, and human rights as urgent priorities. He warns that expanding nuclear arsenals could trigger catastrophe and calls for strong U.S. defense alongside international efforts to control and reduce nuclear weapons. He also emphasizes the need to protect Earth’s air, water, land, and natural resources, while expressing confidence that problems involving population, pollution, food, forests, and farmland can be addressed with courage and foresight.

He declares that America must defend human rights at home and abroad through education, health care, equality, employment, and freedom from injustice and religious intolerance. He urges Americans to renew the principles of liberty and human dignity during a difficult era of political, economic, social, and environmental transition. He also commits to praying for American hostages held in Iran and intends to return home and continue working as a citizen for the nation’s founding values.

Implicit biases can limit hiring decisions and lead to qualified applicants being overlooked. Cited studies found men were twice as likely to be hired for math-required positions despite equal arithmetic performance, white-sounding resume names received 50% more callbacks than African American-sounding names, and applicants with non-English last names received fewer interview callbacks. To improve hiring diversity, the article recommends using behavior-based job-posting language, removing names from resumes, testing skills before collecting personal information, and examining negative “gut feelings” for possible prejudice.

The study fabricated a CMOS-compatible hybrid platform of 100 nm NbN coplanar-waveguide resonators on n-doped Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ quantum-well wafers. Following NbN sputtering, electron-beam patterning, and film etching, a 1 µm deep-etch step recessed the CPW gaps into the heterostructure. This was intended to move substrate interfaces and quantum-well charge-noise sources away from high-electric-field regions and reduce microwave loss. SEM, AFM, and STEM characterized the device structure and epitaxial layers.

Two nominally identical chips were tested over four cooldowns spanning two years. Their fundamental resonances were approximately 5.04 and 5.57 GHz for S1 and 5.08 and 5.60 GHz for S2 at 50 mK. Power-dependent measurements showed resonance shifts of up to 700 kHz, attributed to TLS saturation. Internal quality factors remained stable across measurements, coupling quality factors were nearly constant, and loaded quality factors tracked internal quality factors, indicating that internal loss was limiting. An RLC model gave an effective permittivity of 6.35.

Loss analysis separated temperature- and power-independent scattering, TLS, and quasiparticle contributions. TLS loss was present, but internal scattering associated with defects, dislocations, strain, and the conducting wafer was dominant; quasiparticle loss was negligible at 50 mK but became relevant at higher temperatures. Temperature-dependent measurements from 50 mK to 1.7 K showed thermally saturated TLS behavior at low powers and power-independent loss at higher powers. The platform was reproducible, stable for more than two years, and operated up to 1.7 K, while its estimated maximum gatemon relaxation time was about 14 ns.

Properly designed, high-dosage tutoring can improve academic outcomes while strengthening the teacher pipeline. Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship emphasizes structured training, ongoing coaching and technology that expands human relationships. In its first year, the program reached 40 communities, trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors and delivered nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning. Middle-school math scores grew at up to 2.5 times the expected rate, while elementary readers improved up to three times faster than average. Research cited found that serving as an Ignite tutor nearly triples the likelihood of applying to Teach For America; 550 fellows have joined its teaching corps. The author argues that sustained investment in tutoring could accelerate student learning, address teacher shortages and diversify the educator workforce.

SAFE said China’s capital-outflow pressure eased somewhat in 2016 and the yuan would gain greater exchange-rate flexibility in 2017. Authorities planned measures to attract inflows, while the current-account surplus was expected to remain within a reasonable range. Final 2016 data showed surpluses of $196.4 billion on the current account and $26.3 billion on the capital and financial account.

This case reviews Amazon.com’s first 20 years, from its founding by Jeff Bezos and the launch of its online bookstore in 1995 through its 2017 IPO anniversary. Amazon prioritized expansion, research and development, and long-term market leadership over short-term profitability. Its customer-focused approach included discounts, customer reviews, “1-Click” ordering, broad product selection, fast delivery, and competitive pricing.

Amazon’s May 1997 IPO raised $54 million at $18 per share and ended with a $438 million market capitalization. The company subsequently expanded beyond books into media, electronics, software, and other consumer goods, aided by acquisitions including Audible, Zappos.com, and Quidsi. Launched in 2005, Amazon Prime expanded from two-day shipping into streaming, digital storage, e-book rentals, and member-exclusive deals. Prime Day became a major sales event, and by 2017 nearly half of U.S. households had Prime memberships.

Amazon also developed the Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Echo smart speakers with Alexa. In 2006, it began renting excess network capacity to other companies, creating the basis for Amazon Web Services, which served startups and established companies such as Netflix, Intuit, and Juniper Networks. Some initiatives failed, including the Fire Phone, Amazon Destinations, WebPay, Amazon Auctions, and premium diapers, but Bezos regarded failed experiments as necessary for innovation.

At its IPO anniversary, Amazon had a $458 billion market capitalization, and shareholders had earned a nearly 64,000% return. Cumulative net income from 1997 through 2016 was $4.9 billion, with 60% generated in 2015–2016. From 2014 to 2016, net sales rose from $89.0 billion to $136.0 billion, operating income from $178 million to $4.2 billion, and net income from a $241 million loss to $2.4 billion. Operating cash flow increased from $6.8 billion to $16.4 billion, while free cash flow rose from $1.9 billion to $9.7 billion. Free cash flow after lease principal repayments was $529 million in 2014, $4.7 billion in 2015, and $5.7 billion in 2016.

In 2016, retail generated $123.8 billion in sales and $1.1 billion in operating income, while AWS generated $12.2 billion in sales and $3.1 billion in operating income. Amazon’s expense categories included cost of sales, fulfillment, marketing, technology and content, general and administrative expenses, and other operating expenses.

Bezos’s 1997 shareholder letter emphasized shareholder value and long-term market leadership rather than short-term profits. By 2016, Amazon described its financial objective as sustainable long-term free-cash-flow growth, supported by improving customer experience, sales, operating efficiency, and working-capital management. Market observers anticipated substantial GAAP earnings growth as the IPO anniversary approached.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020 describes its mission to help people and organizations achieve more through software, services, devices, and cloud solutions. Its reportable segments are Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Strategic priorities include reinventing productivity and business processes, building intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and creating more personal computing. Major offerings include Microsoft 365, Office, Dynamics, LinkedIn, Azure, Windows, GitHub, server products, Surface devices, Xbox gaming services, and Bing advertising.

The filing describes Microsoft’s response to COVID-19, including travel policy changes, office closures, remote work, and virtual events, while noting uncertainty about continued effects on operations and technology spending. Sustainability initiatives include a $1 billion investment in climate technology, a goal of carbon-negative operations by 2030, and a $50 million AI for Earth commitment. Microsoft also reported racial-equity and digital-skills initiatives.

Products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, digital marketplaces, and volume-licensing programs. The company operates regional centers and global datacenters, primarily uses third-party manufacturers for devices, and employed approximately 163,000 people at June 30, 2020.

Identified risks include intense competition, cloud-service execution, uncertain returns on investments, acquisition integration and impairment, cybersecurity threats, data misuse, privacy concerns, and regulatory or market conditions affecting technology spending. As of July 27, 2020, 7,567,652,935 common shares were outstanding.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell for discovering regulatory T cells. These immune cells restrain immune activity, prevent autoimmunity and damaging inflammation, and help prevent fetal rejection. Sakaguchi identified them in 1995, while Brunkow and Ramsdell linked mutations affecting them to autoimmune disease in mice and humans. The 11 million Swedish kronor prize was announced October 6.

The paper studies the “free option problem” created by Ethereum’s enshrined Proposer–Builder Separation (ePBS, EIP-7732). Unlike MEV-Boost, which relies on trusted relays, ePBS removes relay trust and lets staked builders delay payload or blob delivery. This creates an approximately eight-second window in which a builder can withhold content to prevent an unfavorable block from becoming canonical, leaving the slot empty without a protocol-level penalty.

The theoretical model links the option to DEX trades influenced by external CEX prices. Option value and exercise probability generally rise with liquidity, volatility, option-window length, and dependence on CEX–DEX arbitrage. Builders can exploit the option to revert losing positions, while liquidity providers bear losses and post-trade DEX prices overshoot CEX prices, weakening price reliability. The same incentives could affect prediction markets and other applications where information arrives during the commitment window.

Using historical Ethereum blocks containing relevant trades by 23 major searchers between January 2024 and March 2025, the paper finds that the option would be profitable to exercise in 0.82% of observed blocks, accounting for 34.6% of missed blocks. Exercise rates and option values spike during high volatility; on the most volatile days, daily missed blocks reach 5.5% and represent 80% of all misses. Builders whose blocks rely more heavily on CEX–DEX flow have substantially higher exercise rates. Trailing MEV discourages exercise in consecutive empty slots.

Two mitigations are evaluated. Shortening the option window reduces exercise probability—by more than 33% at six seconds and over 50% at four seconds—but sacrifices execution and blob-propagation time. Static penalties also reduce exercise substantially, though they raise builder capital requirements and expected blob costs. A dynamic online-gradient penalty mechanism achieves a 0.096% average exercise rate with a 0.104 ETH average penalty and adapts effectively on volatile days.
Geary County deputies investigated an alleged road-rage incident near Fort Riley involving a gun waved from a pickup. Isaac Torgerson was arrested on suspicion of aggravated assault.

The email compiles October 24–25, 2001 press clippings on Enron’s decision to place CFO Andrew Fastow on leave and appoint former treasurer and industrial-markets head Jeffrey McMahon as CFO. Chairman Kenneth Lay said the change was needed to restore investor confidence after an informal SEC inquiry into two Fastow-managed partnerships that raised conflict-of-interest concerns. Enron ended the partnerships, reporting a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Concerns persisted over unclear off-balance-sheet obligations, disclosure, liquidity, credit ratings, and potential stock dilution, although Enron denied wrongdoing. Enron shares fell 17% to $16.41—about half their October 16 level—while other energy traders also declined. Analysts downgraded the stock and said the leadership change alone did not resolve uncertainty. The clippings also report shareholder lawsuits alleging misleading disclosures and insider trading, along with broader market coverage and criticism of Enron’s governance and transparency.

The Yankees will start Paul Goldschmidt at first base and bat him sixth in Game 4 of the ALDS against Toronto, benching Ben Rice. New York will open with Louis Varland and rely on its bullpen. Goldschmidt hit .274 with a .731 OPS and 10 homers in the regular season, while Rice was 2-for-11 in the ALDS. Rice could serve as a pinch-hitter or catching replacement.

After the U.S. ended the de minimis exemption for packages valued under $800, Temu and Shein changed their apps to feature products shipped from local U.S. warehouses, avoiding tariff-related fees. Temu later resumed direct shipping from China amid a trade truce. The author’s Temu toy order arrived after a week or two without a duty bill, although the water balloon and remote-control car disappointed while the Velcro catch set worked. Prices still rose, with a research report citing average summer increases of about 30% on Shein.

Donnell Gibson, known as “Mr. D,” is a behavior intervention specialist and junior varsity basketball coach at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul. After entering a burning house three times in 2015 to save a family of 10, he received the fire department’s highest honor and founded the Gibson Foundation, which mentors young African-American men through motivational speakers, college tours, and basketball. Drawing on his own experiences with homelessness and personal struggles, Gibson encourages students to recognize their potential, pursue education, and apply lessons from basketball and life to overcome challenges.

An October 23, 2001 compilation of press reports documents Enron’s mounting financial, regulatory and legal troubles. A class-action complaint alleges that Enron and certain executives misled investors between January 18, 2000, and October 17, 2001, by failing to disclose weak bandwidth demand, delayed asset write-downs and improper accounting. It cites a $1.01 billion third-quarter charge, more than $1 billion in shareholder-equity reductions and over $73 million in insider stock sales.

The SEC made an informal inquiry into Enron transactions with partnerships managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron said it had responded and would cooperate, while emphasizing that the arrangements had been reviewed, approved, disclosed and used to hedge investments and other assets. The transactions generated a $16 million pretax gain in 1999 and a $36 million loss in 2000. Enron shares fell more than 20% in one session as investors questioned its finances and management credibility. Most major analysts nevertheless retained strong ratings, while others cited vague disclosures and lowered their recommendations.

Enron sought a $750 million loan arranged by Citigroup, reported $3.5 billion in available bank credit lines and relied heavily on commercial-paper financing. Unwinding Fastow-led partnerships reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion and reduced the share count by about 60 million. The SEC inquiry also focused on affiliated trusts and partnerships, including Whitewing and Marlin II. On a contentious investor call, Enron provided few new details, declined to increase earnings guidance despite the lower share count, and faced questions about asset values, liquidity and debt covenants. Kenneth Lay promised greater transparency, while former CEO Jeffrey Skilling had resigned after six months in the post.

A lengthy Texas Monthly profile traced Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a major energy trader under Lay and Skilling. It described aggressive hiring, large bonuses, forced employee rankings, intense work pressure, subjective mark-to-market accounting and expansion into electricity trading, broadband, online commodities and water. The article described the resulting culture as increasingly harsh and secretive. Enron subsequently faced criticism over California energy markets, the Dabhol project in India, collapsing telecommunications investments and questioned accounting practices.

Related reports covered a WTO conference in Qatar, declining 3M profits and copper prices, SEB’s approved Moulinex takeover, Bombardier regional-jet use, Aliant job cuts and a Swissair rescue package. AES also complained to India’s prime minister that Orissa authorities had violated contracts, intimidated company personnel and failed to pay 2.1 billion rupees in bills, while warning that unresolved disputes with Enron’s Dabhol project could deter foreign investment.

The team held a positive meeting about changing parts of its game plan. Although late-season play is physical, the speed-and-skating team needs to improve in those areas. One player has excelled throughout the playoffs and given the team chances in the last two games. Players must prepare mentally, focus on their roles, and bring intensity and home-crowd energy.

The forwarded February 23, 2001 articles describe California’s electricity crisis and Gov. Gray Davis’s effort to stabilize the state’s three largest investor-owned utilities. Davis proposed purchasing about 26,000 miles of transmission lines from Pacific Gas & Electric, Southern California Edison, and San Diego Gas & Electric for an estimated $4.5 billion to $7 billion, using state financing to help the utilities address roughly $13 billion in debt. PG&E remained far from agreement, while Davis announced a tentative $2.7 billion purchase of Edison’s grid, contingent on Edison International providing low-cost power and making other concessions. Negotiations with the utilities remained incomplete.

The state Department of Water Resources was buying electricity for the financially distressed utilities at roughly $50 million to $55 million per day, with projected power-purchase costs exceeding $3 billion by mid-March. Regulators and officials disagreed over whether state borrowing costs would be repaid through bonds or ratepayer revenues; the Public Utilities Commission ruled that PG&E and Edison would not be responsible for revenue shortfalls above customer collections, potentially shifting more of the burden to taxpayers.

California lifted all power alerts on February 23 for the first time since January 13, ending a 40-day sequence of emergencies. Grid officials attributed the improvement to milder weather, additional imports, generators returning from maintenance, and the state scheduling more purchases in advance. They warned that supplies remained tight, conservation was still necessary, and summer demand could produce further shortages. State efforts to secure longer-term, lower-cost contracts progressed slowly, while legislation would reduce prices paid to small renewable and cogeneration generators by roughly half.

The crisis also intensified political debate. Republicans sought to blame Davis but lacked a distinct policy, while polling cited in the articles favored renewed regulation and state acquisition of utility grids. Davis faced criticism for repeatedly missing negotiation deadlines, and potential Republican gubernatorial candidates included Bill Jones, Bill Simon Jr., and Arnold Schwarzenegger. A commentary criticized expanding political control of electricity generation and distribution, while legislation proposed rate discounts and blackout exemptions for residents near power plants.

Separately, Enron North America’s proposed $450 million Lake Elsinore hydroelectric project faced opposition from La Cresta residents concerned about transmission lines through the Cleveland National Forest and San Mateo Wilderness Area. The local water district was considering financing or owning the lines, but the route, final agreement, and regulatory approval remained unsettled. Assemblyman Alan Lowenthal also returned $5,500 in contributions from Edison and Sempra following calls for legislators to avoid energy-industry conflicts.

This medRxiv preprint investigates microtubule (MT) dynamics as a potential biomarker for drug response and resistance in advanced prostate cancer, particularly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). It notes that resistance to androgen-pathway inhibitors is universal, approximately one-third of tumors are primarily refractory to systemic therapy, and docetaxel and cabazitaxel lack reliable patient-selection biomarkers. AR splice variants such as ARv567 and ARv7 are constitutively active and linked to taxane resistance: most ARv567 associates with MTs and is inhibited by paclitaxel, whereas ARv7 shows reduced MT association, is not similarly inhibited, and correlates with docetaxel resistance.

The computational method tracks fluorescent EB1 or EB3 comets marking growing MT tips in time-lapse confocal images. Comet detection uses band-pass filtering and artifact exclusion, while a Kalman-filter algorithm links detections over time. Collinear growth tracks are clustered with a Hungarian linear-assignment algorithm, spatially and temporally constrained search regions, to identify MT growth, pausing, shortening, and catastrophe behavior.

In isogenic M12 prostate cancer cells, ARv7 increased average EB1 speed by more than 40% to 24.6 μm/min, compared with 16.2 μm/min in AR-wild-type cells and 17.3 μm/min in AR-null cells. ARv7 was predominantly nuclear, lacked the cell-edge slowdown observed with wild-type AR, and produced distinct MT organization, consistent with differential regulation in taxane-resistant cells.

Patient-derived organoids were established from primary, lymph-node, and distant-metastatic prostate tumors from 16 patients. Tissue dissociation and Matrigel culture required optimization because primary samples contained benign cells. The ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 favored benign-cell organoid formation, whereas high-grade tumor cells were more apoptosis-resistant and could be temporarily selected by lowering its concentration fourfold. Low-grade tumor cells reportedly differentiated toward normal epithelium in culture, while high-grade tumor cells generally failed to propagate and were overgrown by normal epithelial cells.

The manuscript also describes small PSMA-positive circulating tumor cells in mCRPC, including cells below 7 μm, which may be missed by size-based enrichment methods. Other findings associate AR-null or neuroendocrine phenotypes, Op18 upregulation, altered cell and spindle size, ERG status, and abnormal MT turnover with drug resistance. Paclitaxel suppressed fast MT polymerization and reduced overall growth rates. Both faster-than-normal and slower-than-normal MT turnover were identified as resistance-associated hallmarks. NAD+ and GPX4 inhibitors are proposed as possible sensitizers of drug-tolerant persister cells.

The pVHL–GSK3β axis was shown to regulate MT homeostasis. Loss of pVHL increased MT turnover, while serum starvation produced similar changes through GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation of pVHL. A phosphorylation-resistant pVHL mutant prevented the starvation-associated increase in turnover, supporting a role for pVHL stabilization of MTs in quiescent cells.

A circular Hough transform assay identified circular MT bundles as a hallmark of paclitaxel sensitivity. Tubulin rings formed in 83% of parental A549 cells but only 27% of BRCA1-knockdown cells, with markedly weaker bundle intensity in the resistant cells.

Proposed validation includes correlating organoid MT dynamics with gene-expression and clinical-response data, testing regulator knockdowns in organoids and patient-derived xenografts, analyzing drug-treated tissue slices using three-dimensional imaging and power-spectrum metrics, and performing transcriptomic and organoid–immune-cell screens. Live-cell imaging, EB1-labeled organoids, organoid transduction, and nonparametric statistical analyses are described, with analysis code made available online. The manuscript presents MT-dynamics measurement as a promising approach for anticipating resistance and selecting or sensitizing therapies, while noting that clinical validation remains limited.

The article examines Hungary’s general and special education systems and how demographics, government, the economy, laws, and teacher preparation shape education for students with and without disabilities. Hungary has 9.7 million residents, a declining population, and a multiparty parliamentary democracy. Compulsory education currently covers ages six to sixteen, and school attendance, admissions, entrance examinations, secondary leaving examinations, and vocational pathways are centrally important. Teacher preparation became undivided in 2013, with five-year primary and six-year secondary programs that emphasize pedagogy, psychology, and final-year practical training.

Hungary has a long history of special education, beginning with separate schooling for deaf students and the first special education teacher-training college in the early twentieth century. In 2019, more than 88,000 students had special education needs, and 60% were educated inclusively. Multidisciplinary committees diagnose disabilities and recommend services, while parents choose their children’s placement. Available supports include counseling, early intervention, speech therapy, developmental training, and specialized physical education. The 1993 Act provided financial assistance to families, while the 2011 Act on Public Education guaranteed free and compulsory primary education, generally accessible secondary and vocational education, and expanded compulsory education from age three.

Special education teachers complete a four-year university program in one or two of eight disability areas. They then undertake a compulsory two-year traineeship with examinations and a portfolio before entering a career structure that ranges from novice to master or researcher teacher. Continued professional development is required, and in-service training can provide salary increases.

Current concerns include difficult or delayed diagnoses, particularly for autism, inaccessible older school buildings and transportation, continued reliance on separate schools, limited disability training for general education teachers, lecture-heavy instruction, low teacher pay, and teacher attrition. Recommendations include school-based referral systems, additional autism diagnosticians, ramps and elevators, accessible transportation, disability training for all educators, improved teaching methods, higher salaries and retention incentives, and study of church-run teacher programs, which have higher retention rates.

Richard Donchian’s indicator uses an upper band set by the highest price and a lower band by the lowest price over the last N bars; an optional middle band is omitted in the article. Traditionally used for breakout-based trend following, the channels are described as effective for commodities, currencies, and Treasuries but generally ineffective for stocks, whose markets are faster and less trending. The article notes that scalping with the channels is unlikely to succeed.

Backtests in Curtis Faith’s *The Way of the Turtle*, covering 1996–2007 and excluding stocks, produced annual returns of 29.4% and 57.2% for two channel strategies. A long-only S&P 500 trend-following test from 1960 to October 2021, without reinvested dividends, returned 4.57% annually versus 7.15% for buy-and-hold, while showing a substantially lower maximum drawdown. Optimizing the channel periods reduced returns slightly and drawdown slightly further.

An inverted, mean-reversion strategy tested on SPY from 1993 to October 2021 used a best entry lookback of 15 days. Its best annual return, using a five-day lookback, was 9.16%, approximately matching buy-and-hold, with small drawdowns and a high win rate. Donchian Channels resemble Bollinger Bands visually but remain distinct and may produce different backtest results.

After last week’s sell-off, NVDA’s technical bounce from its rising 50-day trendline supports a bullish outlook toward new highs. MU’s rally is likely short-lived because it remains below a bearish 50-day average and faces resistance at $84, despite an oversold RSI. WDC is introduced but not analyzed in the excerpt.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended a seven-day winning streak. During the federal government shutdown’s seventh day, President Trump said some furloughed workers may not receive back pay, depending on who they are. A draft White House memo said employees on unpaid leave are not guaranteed retroactive pay, conflicting with earlier Office of Personnel Management guidance and a law stating furloughed workers “shall be paid” during funding lapses.

The administration’s position was viewed as pressure on Senate Democrats to support a Republican proposal to restore current funding through late November. Trump also warned of substantial permanent layoffs if the shutdown continues, while Democrats demanded an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits. AFGE rejected the administration’s interpretation and called for Congress to end the shutdown.

In a separate note, it was reported that Trump would meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House on Monday to discuss the Gaza war and the possibility of a further Israeli military offensive. Trump said the United States was helping Israel in the operation. The article also said the administration was weighing whether to use federal emergency powers to impose new tariffs in response to what it described as unfair trade practices by other countries.

BMO downgraded West Fraser, Interfor and Canfor from “outperform” to “market perform,” citing U.S. duties, a stronger Canadian dollar and litigation. Analysts expected near-term earnings pressure despite more positive three-to-five-year prospects.

Japan’s GDP grew an annualized 4% in Q2, exceeding forecasts, driven by stronger consumer spending and capital investment. Private consumption rose 0.9%, exports increased, and Tokyo 2020 Olympics-related investment supported the economy, now in its longest expansion in a decade.

At the University of Virginia, President Ronald Reagan thanked his hosts and jokingly announced a four-week break for attendees. He praised Thomas Jefferson as UVA’s founder and an advocate of science, free inquiry, religious freedom, and popular government. Emphasizing Jefferson’s belief in balance and tolerance, Reagan argued that government must protect society without infringing on citizens’ rights and warned against partisanship, privilege, and intolerance. He compared contemporary resistance to regulation, taxation, and elite foreign policy to Jefferson-era populism.

Reagan described a worldwide democratic and free-market revolution. Citing Freedom House, he said the number of countries rated “not free” had fallen from 71 to 50 over 15 years, while those rated free or partly free had risen from 92 to 117. He said more than 90 percent of the world’s population lived in democratic countries or countries moving toward democracy. He linked political and economic freedom, cited reforms in China and the Soviet Union, and described the proposed U.S.-Canada free-trade agreement as a possible model.

He attributed diplomatic progress to renewed democratic confidence, citing the INF treaty’s elimination of an entire class of nuclear missiles, START’s proposed 50 percent reduction in strategic weapons, progress on testing and chemical weapons, and negotiations on European conventional forces. He also cited settlements in Afghanistan and Cambodia, an accord withdrawing Cuban troops from Angola, Soviet political-prisoner releases and greater religious freedom, and expanded scientific and cultural exchanges. He said U.S. firmness had helped end the Gulf War and led the PLO to accept Israel’s right to exist and relevant U.N. resolutions.

Reagan offered three warnings for sustaining progress. First, Soviet-American dialogue and summits remained vulnerable because the Soviet system retained one-party authoritarian rule, aligned with hostile governments, and maintained a dangerous military imbalance. He urged continued skepticism, strong defenses, rejection of bad treaties, and public candor. Second, Soviet reform was not inevitable; Western strength, resolve, and economic success had pressured Soviet leaders to reconsider prior policies. Third, the president and Congress needed cooperation while respecting their separate constitutional roles. He said progress had followed cooperation in Afghanistan, Cambodia, Angola, and Soviet relations, while adversarial conflict had weakened policies toward Central America. Strong, flexible presidential leadership and congressional support were therefore essential.

Concluding with Jefferson and John Adams’s renewed correspondence after their political estrangement, Reagan presented their tolerance and friendship as a lesson for national unity. He noted that both died on July 4, fifty years after the Declaration of Independence, and closed by invoking the principles of equality, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

In questions and answers, Reagan said U.S.-Soviet normalization should depend on Soviet actions, described his personal summit diplomacy with Mikhail Gorbachev, and called PLO concessions an important step toward Middle East negotiations. He said his anti-terrorism policy would continue, urged young people to register and vote, and cited restored military readiness, tax cuts, deregulation, job growth, increased tax revenue, and a balanced-budget goal among his administration’s accomplishments. After leaving office, he planned to remain active, speak publicly, possibly write a book, and support Nancy Reagan’s antidrug work.

Select Security acquired Intelligent Technology Inc. and Carolina Security Group in Charlotte, adding nearly 1,000 customers, experienced staff, and a downtown branch where it will consolidate western North Carolina operations. The company serves nearly 30,000 customers across 10 states with security, fire alarm, surveillance, access control, life safety, and home automation services.

Newcastle University scientists reported the first 3D printing of human corneas. They combined human corneal stromal stem cells with alginate and collagen to create a printable bio-ink, then extruded it in concentric circles using a low-cost 3D bioprinter. Printing took under 10 minutes, and the cells were shown to grow. Using eye-scan data, the team also produced a cornea matched to an individual patient’s size and shape. The proof-of-concept research, published in Experimental Eye Research, aims to address a worldwide shortage of transplant corneas, but further testing is needed and transplant use is several years away.

Galveston County tests Gulf Coast beach water at 52 sites and issues advisories for fecal bacteria, often after heavy rain. A warning near 57th Street was lifted when samples cleared; conditions usually resolve within 48 hours. Visitors should check water conditions and avoid water under advisories, as exposure may cause illness.

An archival source note for *Foundations of Foreign Policy, 1975–1980* identifies records at the Library of Congress, Reagan Presidential Library, State Department, National Security Council, National Archives, and other repositories, along with published press sources and an online-resources list. The excerpt documents six 1980 campaign appearances: Reagan statements in Florence on January 24 and Los Angeles on China and Taiwan on August 25; speeches in Worcester on February 15 and at the VFW convention in Chicago on August 18; a George Bush address to the Commonwealth Club on September 11; and Reagan’s televised “Strategy of Peace for the 80s” speech in Arlington on October 19. The unclassified materials include press citations and contextual notes.

National Weather Service scientists initially mistook a 70-mile-wide radar blob over Colorado for birds, then determined it was a mass of migrating Painted Lady butterflies after seeking public identification. The butterflies migrate across the continental U.S. to northern Mexico and the Southwest during colder months, follow wind patterns, and can glide hundreds of miles daily.

**Summary**

This service evaluation across seven acute care trusts in Greater Manchester developed a reproducible, data-driven method for selecting which AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities to prioritise for urgent reporting to support faster lung cancer diagnosis. The Annalise Container CXR (version 2.1) AI system, detecting up to 124 findings, was applied in shadow mode to two cohorts: a retrospective cohort of 1,282 confirmed lung cancer patients (June 2020–June 2022) and a prospective cohort of 13,802 GP-referred primary care CXRs (June–July 2024), with 1% cancer prevalence assumed in the latter. Findings were grouped into CRITICAL, HIGH, and STANDARD priority classes, and prevalence ratios between cohorts informed three prioritisation strategies.

Results: Strategy 1 (19 findings, prevalence ratio >5) gave 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity; Strategy 2 (41 HIGH findings, ratio >2) gave 97.27% sensitivity and 62.68% specificity; Strategy 3 (32 findings combining prevalence data with clinical judgement) gave 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, and 99.95% NPV, with 23 CXRs needed to report per cancer case. Age differences between cohorts likely inflated the prevalence of bone-related findings, and specificity for Strategy 3 ranged 78.73%–79.87% across assumed prevalences of 0.5%–2%.

Limitations include single-region data without external validation, an assumed rather than verified reference standard in cohort 2, and count-level rather than study-level analysis, making metrics indicative. Future work requires multicentre prospective validation, assessment of impacts on non-prioritised findings and reporting workflows, and patient involvement. The approach is presented as a blueprint for AI integration into radiology workflows.

The Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, published monthly by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures changes in US nonfarm employment during the preceding month. It is generally released on the first Friday at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time and includes data on jobs added or lost, unemployment, hours worked, wages, sector performance, revisions, and other components. Traders compare actual figures with prior data and consensus expectations.

NFP is a major indicator of US economic health and frequently causes substantial financial-market volatility. Strong employment may signal economic growth and inflation, potentially prompting Federal Reserve rate increases; weak employment may support rate cuts. Higher-than-expected figures generally support the US economy, dollar, and stocks while pressuring bonds through higher rate expectations. Lower-than-expected figures generally have the opposite effect. Forex traders often buy USD-base pairs and sell USD-quote pairs after stronger readings, with commodity markets also reacting to expectations for growth, inflation, and interest rates.

Backtests cited in the passage found an average SPY open-to-close gain of 0.09% on report days since 1993 and an average TLT return of negative 0.02%. Performance during the first several trading days after publication was weaker, with SPY averaging negative 0.04% when exiting five days later. The authors concluded that NFP trading strategies rely on difficult-to-predict figures and that they found no dependable edge in trading macro data.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) launched a nationwide public awareness campaign, "Pehlay Zindagi: Give Way to Ambulances—Give Way to Life," in Islamabad, urging citizens to respect and give way to ambulances. Using television, radio and social media, a public pledge drive invites participants to join the "Friends for Life" virtual platform. Part of the ICRC's global Health Care in Danger project, the campaign is supported by over 30 partner organizations and runs until December 2017. Health Minister Saira Afzal praised the initiative, while ICRC and partners called on the media to help spread awareness and also sought to sensitize people to issues faced by ambulance staff. This is the second edition, following 2016's "Rasta Dein" campaign, which showed a 16% impact; motorists' behaviour will again be assessed before and after through observational studies.

The lecture examines how adjacency-matrix eigenvalues measure pseudorandomness. For an \(n,d,\lambda\) graph, the graph is \(d\)-regular and all nonleading adjacency eigenvalues have absolute value at most \(\lambda\). The expander mixing lemma shows that smaller \(\lambda\) yields stronger control of edge discrepancies between vertex sets.

Cayley graphs are introduced as deterministic pseudorandom examples. Their vertices form a group, and adjacency is determined by multiplication with a symmetric subset. Paley graphs are presented as Cayley graphs built from quadratic residues modulo a prime \(p\equiv1\pmod4\). Fourier eigenvectors yield explicit eigenvalues, and a Gauss-sum calculation shows that all nontrivial eigenvalues are much smaller than the degree \((p-1)/2\), establishing the Paley graph’s pseudorandomness. For abelian groups, these eigenvalues are Fourier coefficients; nonabelian groups instead connect to representation theory.

A Conlon–Zhao theorem states that, for Cayley graphs, discrepancy and eigenvalue conditions are equivalent up to constant factors: \( \mathrm{EIG}(\epsilon d)\) implies \(\mathrm{DISC}(\epsilon)\), while \(\mathrm{DISC}(\epsilon)\) implies \(\mathrm{EIG}(8\epsilon d)\). The converse fails for general graphs: attaching a smaller \(d\)-regular component to a large random \(d\)-regular graph preserves discrepancy while producing two eigenvalues equal to \(d\). The Cayley-graph implication is proved using the min–max characterization of eigenvalues, symmetry under group translations, and Grothendieck’s inequality, which relates sign-valued bilinear forms to an efficiently computable semidefinite relaxation.

The lecture then establishes the Alon–Boppana bound: for fixed degree \(d\) and large \(n\), the second-largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies
\[
\lambda_2\ge 2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1).
\]
A Courant–Fischer proof constructs weighted vectors based on distance neighborhoods, combines vectors centered at two distant vertices to obtain orthogonality to the all-ones vector, and produces the required quotient bound. A second, slightly weaker trace-method proof counts closed walks and compares them with walks on the infinite \(d\)-regular tree; Catalan-number estimates force \(\max(|\lambda_2|,|\lambda_n|)\ge 2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1)\). The threshold is optimal because \(2\sqrt{d-1}\) is exactly the spectral radius of the infinite \(d\)-regular tree. Graphs attaining the bound exist, though related extremal questions remain under investigation.

Rain delayed Game 3 of the Mariners-Tigers ALDS at Comerica Park, with the series tied 1-1. Originally scheduled for 4:08 p.m. ET, the Tigers proposed a 7 p.m. start and MLB aimed for 7:30 p.m., but neither was confirmed. The game moved to FS2 and also airs on MLB Network and the Fox One App.

Bridgeton National Bank sued Ellas Q. Hepner to recover $1,400 on a renewal promissory note. Hepner defended on the ground that the original note was obtained through fraudulent representations and a promise that it would not be negotiated unless certain stock was resold profitably, and that the bank had notice. The trial court excluded testimony that the bank’s cashier, who also served as Kil-Tone Company treasurer, knew of the fraud and promise, because that knowledge could not be attributed to the bank, and directed a verdict for the bank. The court held that an agent’s knowledge is chargeable to a principal only when the principal would have received notice while acting for itself; it would not presume the bank’s board would have been informed. The rule to show cause was discharged.

Morgan Chase offices to reduce rent.

Lower global and U.S. interest rates could drive a housing-sector and cyclical-stock rebound over the next one to four years. Historically, homebuilders and home-improvement stocks outperformed SPY during rate declines, except around the subprime crisis. Lumber and wooden-goods tariffs currently favor domestic manufacturers, though trade deals could alter that advantage. Loose lending creates some housing-crisis risk, but leverage appears lower than in 2007, supporting a diversified, high-upside housing-stock approach. The author uses top-down macroeconomic analysis and bottom-up company research, focusing on strong economies, promising sectors, and quality companies with momentum and consistent results. The author is a Brazil-based regulated investment analyst with an MBA in Macroeconomics and Portfolio Management and discloses no relevant positions or business relationships. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

Apple Inc. reported fiscal first-quarter 2023 results for the 53-week period ended December 31, 2022. Net sales declined 5% to $117.154 billion, while gross margin was $50.332 billion, operating income was $36.016 billion, net income was $29.998 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $1.88. The passage documents AGESA boot-time interfaces, host-environment call-outs, platform configuration, and customization controls. AGESA entry points manage structure allocation, event logging, processor and cache initialization, platform setup, memory initialization, artifact/HOB transfer, graphics and late-boot configuration, ACPI/DMI table generation, and suspend/resume state preservation. Initialization differs between the boot strap processor and application processors, with synchronization and MTRR restrictions; execution-cache allocation follows address, size, alignment, boundary, and resource-limit rules.

Required host call-outs include buffer allocation, deallocation, and lookup; cold or warm reset initiation; DIMM SPD reading; and dispatching tasks to application processors. Optional call-outs support memory voltage adjustments, training hooks, heap rebasing, IDS data retrieval, FCH customization, video BIOS repost, PCIe clock requests, and other platform-specific actions. Memory initialization exposes extensive configurable parameters covering interleaving, ECC, refresh, training, UMA, power management, and timing. Suspend support saves critical and volatile processor context for restoration during resume.

Platform customization can be supplied through build options, configuration elements, wrapper modifications, IDS controls, or defined call-outs. Build options can remove support for unused memory types, processors, sockets, power-management features, and ACPI/DMI tables, while configuration elements specify motherboard characteristics such as VRM limits, CPU frequency, PCI MMIO layout, IO APIC count, and ACPI identifiers.

The Appellate Division, Second Department, reversed Solomon Montlake’s conviction for first-degree grand larceny and ordered a new trial. It rejected his claim of former jeopardy arising from the jury’s dismissal at an earlier trial. The discharge was a proper exercise of discretion after the prosecutor repeatedly accused defense counsel before the jury of being a criminal, and the record indicated Montlake had consented to the action through his counsel.

The court found the alibi instruction erroneous and prejudicial. The trial judge had told the jury that an alibi required proof that the defendants could not possibly have been at the crime scene, effectively placing the burden on them and requiring exclusion of even a bare possibility of their presence. General statements that the prosecution bore the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt did not cure that specific error. The proper rule was that if the alibi evidence, considered with all other proof, raised a reasonable doubt about the defendants’ presence at the crime scene, the defendants were entitled to acquittal.

The court also held that cross-examination about an alibi witness’s failure to pay restaurant rent was an unwise exercise of discretion because it was unrelated to the case and did not indicate moral turpitude, although that ruling alone did not warrant reversal. The reversal and new trial applied only to Montlake; Rosenfeld’s appeal had previously been dismissed.
