Researchers demonstrated in mice that limiting a nutrient used by malaria parasites, alongside conventional drugs, could prevent drug-resistant parasites from emerging. Drug-resistant parasites survived when infected alone, but failed to grow when drug-sensitive parasites were also present, indicating that competition between strains controlled resistance. The ecological approach is a proof of principle for extending existing drugs’ usefulness, treating resistant infections when alternatives are unavailable, and preventing resistance to new drugs. Future applications would require identifying resources that resistant strains need more than sensitive strains, confirming that limiting them eliminates resistance, and determining optimal removal methods and timing. The findings appeared in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Statistics Canada reported that London–St. Thomas unemployment rose to 5.5% in September from 5.4%, while the labour force fell by 3,000 and was 9,300 lower than a year earlier. Only about 75% of residents aged 25–54 were working, ranking London last among 15 major Ontario cities. A King’s University College study found that roughly half of working adults lacked full-time permanent jobs with benefits; precarious work was especially common among young people and minorities and was linked to stress, poor health, depression, anger, and family strain. Nationally, unemployment remained 6.2%, while Ontario employment rose by 35,000 and unemployment fell to 5.6%.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended April 1, 2017 reported quarterly net sales of $52.896 billion, up 5%, net income of $11.029 billion, diluted EPS of $2.10, and a 38.9% gross margin. Six-month net sales were $131.247 billion and net income was $28.920 billion. Quarterly sales rose for Services (18%), Mac (14%), Other Products (31%), and iPhone (1%), while iPad sales fell 12%. All geographic segments grew except Greater China, where sales declined 14%. At April 1, assets totaled $334.532 billion, liabilities were $200.450 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $134.082 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $39.579 billion. Apple repurchased $18.012 billion of stock and paid $6.134 billion in dividends during the six months and issued $11 billion of long-term debt. The filing also disclosed hedging activities, tax contingencies including the EU state-aid decision, supply-chain and legal risks, and anticipated effects of new accounting standards.

This patent application, supported in part by a Department of Navy contract, describes methods, apparatuses, systems, and computer-readable media for classifying objects represented by 3D point clouds, particularly at long range and in near real time. Point clouds may be generated by chirped LIDAR systems using heterodyne or homodyne detection, or by other 3D scanners. Disclosed LIDAR hardware includes a laser source, modulator, beam splitter, reference path, scanning optical coupler, detector, and processor. Range is determined by de-chirping returned and reference optical signals and analyzing their beat frequency.

The classification method obtains a point cloud representing an object’s surface, estimates a surface normal, and uses that normal to establish a translation- and rotation-invariant coordinate system. Feature variables are extracted in that system. A first classifier, using spin images, and a second classifier, using covariance matrices, independently assign the object to one of a fixed number of classes or designate it as unknown. If their classifications agree, the class is assigned. If they disagree, an iterative closest-point statistic compares the input point cloud with occluded or non-occluded model point clouds for only the candidate classes to determine the closest fit. A device may then operate based on the assigned class, including displaying information, controlling a vehicle, or directing a projectile.

Training methods use labeled spin images with linear discriminant analysis and k-d-tree nearest-neighbor searches, while covariance matrices are clustered and compared through a divergence-based distance. Experimental tests using LIDAR-generated point clouds reported strong classification results for several distinguishable objects and for more similar objects, including toy guns.

The passage outlines NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture and GeForce RTX 50 Series, emphasizing generative AI, ray tracing, neural rendering, media processing, and power efficiency.

RTX 50 Series Tensor Cores support FP4 quantization, which requires less than half the memory of FP16 while providing more than twice the prior-generation performance and, with TensorRT Model Optimizer methods, virtually no quality loss. For example, FLUX.dev drops from over 23GB of VRAM at FP16 to less than 10GB at FP4, allowing it to run on more RTX GPUs.

Blackwell’s fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add an Opacity Micromap Engine, a Triangle Cluster Intersection Engine, and hardware acceleration for Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry allows systems such as Unreal Engine 5 and Nanite to ray-trace full-fidelity geometry without low-resolution proxies. Its cluster-level acceleration structures can contain up to 256 triangles and reduce subsequent BVH-build processing by two orders of magnitude, while GPU-driven APIs reduce CPU overhead. Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures update only changed scene partitions, improving scalability for large object counts. Mega Geometry also supports ray tracing of animated subdivision surfaces and is available through DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0 on RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Linear Swept Spheres render common hair use cases about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth the VRAM.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 dynamically reorganizes parallel GPU threads and directs coherent neural workloads to Tensor Cores. Blackwell’s reorder logic is twice as efficient and more precise, and supported applications can benefit without code changes. The programmable AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts, offloading work from the CPU, reducing latency, coordinating AI and graphics workloads, and supporting Windows Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling.

Blackwell adds hardware H.264 and HEVC encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma sampling. Its ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, supports 4:2:2 encoding, and includes an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode offering another 5% improvement and up to 15% overall improvement. The RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, while the sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b supports UHBR 20 at up to 80 Gbps, including 8K at 165Hz and 4K at 480Hz with DSC.

Blackwell’s Max-Q improvements include finer-grained clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, separate control of core and memory power, and faster dynamic frequency switching. Clocks can respond to workloads 1,000 times faster, and the deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada. A small-language-model inference example reports power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model runs 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and executes once per rendered frame. Enhanced Flip Metering shifts pacing to the display engine, whose pixel-processing capacity has doubled. DLSS 4 also replaces CNN-based models with transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, allowing twice as many parameters and improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting detail, and denoising.

Blackwell also enables developer-created neural shaders. The Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan exposes Tensor Cores to pixel and ray-tracing shaders, while Slang supports differentiable shading. Proposed uses include neural texture compression, Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression can reduce textures by as much as seven to one; in one example, material memory falls from 1,110MB to 333MB. Neural Radiance Cache trains small networks on live game data to infer additional lighting bounces, RTX Skin provides real-time subsurface scattering, and Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model to infer a natural face from rasterized geometry and 3D pose data.

The full GB202 chip has 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, and is used in the RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores, and is used in the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores, and is used in the RTX 5070. The passage ends with NVIDIA’s accuracy, liability, licensing, intended-use, and warranty disclaimers.

The study develops a classical embedded atom method (EAM) potential for the tungsten–hydrogen–helium system to simulate radiation damage in irradiated tungsten. Tungsten is a candidate plasma-facing fusion-reactor material, but neutron irradiation and implanted hydrogen and helium can create defects, bubbles, hardening, embrittlement, gas retention, and swelling. Computational models are needed because experiments under reactor conditions are scarce and density functional theory is limited to relatively small systems.

The new potential extends the Mason W–H potential with helium interactions and is designed to reproduce defect formation energies, light-gas binding energies, relaxation volumes, gaseous-state energies, and tungsten surface properties. These quantities determine gas trapping in vacancies and voids and the elastic fields contributing to irradiation-induced swelling. Existing potentials either inadequately describe gaseous behavior, overestimate relaxation volumes, or represent surfaces and voids imprecisely.

The fitting minimizes a weighted loss function based on DFT formation energies, relaxation volumes, defect binding energies, and gaseous total energies. A parallel global optimization algorithm uses Gaussian mixture models to identify low-loss parameter regions before local convergence with the Simplex method. Parameters are first fitted for W–He interactions and then jointly refined.

DFT data are drawn from prior studies and new VASP calculations. Pair potentials use ZBL short-range constraints, while electron-density functions are fitted with smooth spline forms. Negative electron densities are permitted. Helium’s embedding function is constrained to remain repulsive, and its pair interaction is revised to reproduce high-pressure hcp-helium DFT data while retaining reasonable dilute-gas behavior. Its many-body contribution provided no significant improvement, so helium electron densities were constrained to zero. Hydrogen–helium interactions were fitted to DFT dimer data and jointly refined for defect behavior. Charge-density analysis further showed that helium’s electronic interactions within tungsten are non-negligible, despite their omission from earlier potentials.

Renewable Energy Alaska Project is training residents from five Southeast Alaska tribal communities to conduct $25 household energy assessments, making them more accessible than private audits costing thousands. Using tablets, assessors inventory appliances, windows, lighting and occupancy before recommending low-cost improvements. LED bulbs could save about $45 annually, and simple changes could reduce one household’s bill by nearly 10%. Although these measures cannot replace diesel power, trained local assessors may ease financial burdens and help residents remain in their communities. The Home Energy Leader Program runs through July 31.

Research on when children worldwide get their own mobile phones shows wide variation by country. Sara Zaske's daughter Sophia showed little interest in a phone in Berlin, where most classmates' phones were flip phones, but as a fourth-grader in California's Bay Area she was the only classmate without a smartphone; her family plans a flip phone next year and no smartphone until high school. A 2015 study of about 3,500 European children found roughly 80% owned a phone or smartphone (46% smartphone, 33% mobile phone), with variation in school restrictions and sensitivity to cost. In the US, about 45% of children 10–12 have their own smartphone with a service plan, some from age 8, and 42% of children 8 and younger have their own tablet. South Korean children reach 72% smartphone ownership by ages 11–12 (up to 5.4 hours daily versus adults' 3.8); Taiwan rises from 45% of 11-year-olds to 71% of 15-year-olds; Turkish parents are split on timing. In Africa, 81% of South African secondary students own or access a phone, while Ghana and Malawi rates are lower but rose sharply from 2007 to 2014. An Australian study found a median first-phone age of 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no "right" age, recommending no digital media for children under 18–24 months except video-chatting, one hour of screen time for ages 2–5, and screen-free meals with no screens an hour before bed.

NAB executive Andrew Hagger called advisers falsely witnessing superannuation death documents “sloppy and unprofessional.” A royal commission exposed financial-planning wrongdoing at banks and AMP. A CBA planner wiped out much of Hockey’s mother-in-law’s savings through high-risk products; the bank initially offered low compensation.

The Las Vegas City Council is expected Wednesday to introduce an ordinance codifying trash fees Republic Services has charged commercial property owners without approval. Republic is the exclusive waste-management provider in Clark County, Las Vegas, North Las Vegas and Henderson. Local ordinances require city councils or county commissioners to approve fees not covered by existing ordinances or franchise agreements, including container delivery, removal and exchange fees and industrial dry-run fees. Elected officials said they were largely unaware of the charges. Republic maintains it submits annual supplemental-service fee lists to local governments and that this reporting process constitutes approval; a county spokesman said commissioner approval is unnecessary. Henderson officials said the unapproved fees may violate city rules and will be reviewed, while Las Vegas and North Las Vegas deferred to their ordinances. One waste-management company has refused three container fees for five years after requesting proof of approval, saying the avoided charges could total thousands of dollars.

This medRxiv preprint uses two-sample and multivariable Mendelian randomization to assess relationships among gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia using publicly available European GWAS data. Three MR methods and sensitivity analyses identified six gut taxa associated with fibromyalgia: higher levels of Enterobacteriaceae, Butyricicoccus, Coprococcus1, and Enterobacteriales were linked to reduced risk, while Eggerthella and Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were linked to increased risk. No reverse causality was detected.

Eighty-two plasma metabolites were associated with fibromyalgia, including 44 known metabolites, 24 ratios, and 14 unknown metabolites. Pathway enrichment implicated caffeine metabolism, alpha-linolenic acid metabolism, and GLP-1 and incretin synthesis, secretion, and inactivation. AFMU was associated with reduced risk, whereas 7-methylxanthine, 1-methylxanthine, and oleoyl-ethanolamide were associated with increased risk; EPA and stearidonic acid were associated with reduced risk.

Several taxa were linked to specific metabolites. Multivariable MR indicated that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine partially mediated the relationship between Enterobacteriaceae and Enterobacteriales and fibromyalgia, with mediation proportions of 14.91% and 12.34%, respectively.

The authors propose limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 fatty acids, adopting a low-glycemic-index diet, and reducing high-oxalate foods to potentially influence metabolic pathways, inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibromyalgia symptoms. Limitations include unavailable demographic data for subgroup analyses, predominantly European ancestry limiting generalizability, and the need for experimental and clinical validation.

Guinness has partnered with former Arsenal captain Thierry Henry, its first footballer partner, for its Made of Black campaign. Henry will work with Guinness in Nigeria and across Africa to highlight people demonstrating the campaign’s spirit. Guinness will engage football fans through experiences including fan zones with live football and music. Launched on MTV Base in August 2014, the campaign describes Black as an attitude, mindset, and way of life representing Africa’s best. Guinness will also continue sponsoring English Premier League broadcasts on DStv.

The passage describes a continuation patent application concerning magnet management and MRI compatibility in implantable medical devices, particularly cochlear implants. It reviews conductive and sensorineural hearing loss, air- and bone-conduction hearing aids, and cochlear implants that convert sound into electrical cochlear stimulation.

Exemplary implantable devices contain a magnet or magnet apparatus within an elastomeric body, such as silicone. In one configuration, structural plates sandwich the magnet. When an externally generated magnetic field, such as an MRI field of 0.2 T or more, applies torque and rotates the magnet, the magnet cams the plates apart. Separation stretches the surrounding elastomeric material or activates resilient components, producing an increasing restoring force that counteracts the torque and limits rotation after an initial permitted movement. A disclosed 3 T MRI example applies torque up to 0.38 Newton meters.

The magnet apparatus may include a coated magnet or a magnet hermetically isolated within a container and configured to revolve about its longitudinal axis. Surfaces contacting the magnet may be low-friction, and alternative resistance mechanisms include springs, rails, rigid housings, compliant elongated plates, curved plate surfaces, contour-matched magnets, bumpers, and tracks. Plate geometry, dimensions, stiffness, material, and elastomeric properties can be selected to control the force profile and degree of permitted rotation.

The implantable assembly may include an inductive coil, receiver or transceiver, power-storage element, sound processor, stimulator, and cochlear electrode array. Power and data can be transferred transcutaneously from an external device through a magnetic-induction link; sound processing may occur externally, internally, or in both locations. Some embodiments omit stored implant power and operate from real-time external supply.

A side slit in the elastomeric housing can permit insertion or removal of the magnet apparatus between the plates and may be introduced surgically when removal is needed. The disclosed principles may also apply to other magnet-containing implants, including pacemakers, muscle stimulators, bone-conduction devices, direct acoustic cochlear stimulators, middle-ear implants, hybrid devices, and sensory-supplement prostheses.
TCI valued Zodiac Aerospace at €7–10 per share after a first-half loss and is pressuring Safran to withdraw its bid, warning offers above €10 destroy value.

Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell said AI computing demand remains “tremendous,” with no signs yet that too many AI data centers will be built. Dell’s server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter, driven partly by demand from more multimodal and multi-agent AI systems. Shares rose over 3% after Dell raised projected annual revenue growth to 7%–9% from 3%–4%, and expected diluted earnings per share growth to 15% from 8%. The company plans to ship $20 billion in AI servers in fiscal 2026, double last year’s sales.

The tripartite agreement provides minimum purchase quantities of specified Congo products, permits additional purchases, and sets prices through agreements between the Belgian Government and the UK or US governments. Payment follows normal purchasing practice. The UK must ensure that purchased products are not disadvantaged by customs duties relative to British colonial products, while the UK and US will strive to deliver scheduled industrial and other supplies to the Congo. Belgium must maintain controls against transactions aiding wartime enemies and coordinate export licensing with British African systems. The agreement takes effect upon signature.

An accompanying US airgram approves allowing revision if Belgian territory is liberated and requests details on agreed prices, outstanding transactions, payment and title for unshipped goods, and foreign exchange. It rejects a specific shipping guarantee but accepts pooled-shipping arrangements and the lapse of incomplete transactions under the earlier agreement. It also proposes that the UK and US receive options on the entire output of scheduled products and that the agreement include Congo development work, noting reported pyrethrum production of 539 tons in 1942 and a potential 1,470 tons in 1943.

The article presents backtests of three bullish candlestick patterns—Bearish Engulfing, Three Outside Down, and Bullish Harami—using SPY from its 1993 inception through October 2021. Each trade invests 100% of equity and exits when the day’s close exceeds the previous day’s high. Bearish Engulfing produced 296 trades, a 71% win rate, 0.53% average gain, 5% CAGR, 16% maximum drawdown, and 2.5 profit factor. Three Outside Down recorded 112 trades, a 78% win rate, 0.7% average gain, 2.3% CAGR, 14% maximum drawdown, and 2.6 profit factor. Bullish Harami generated 306 trades, a 76% win rate, 0.33% average gain, 3.1% CAGR, 25% maximum drawdown, and 1.65 profit factor. The authors note that most candlestick patterns lack quantified support and rely on anecdotal evidence, although these three performed reasonably well and may improve with additional variables.

Turkey’s Ankara Chief Prosecutor’s Office issued detention warrants for 133 former public servants—101 from the Finance Ministry and 32 from the Labor and Social Security Ministry—over alleged links to the Gülen movement and use of ByLock; four were on active duty. Police also detained 14 women, at least 18 dismissed teachers, 19 military personnel, nine people in Kozan and seven in a Bitlis-based operation. These actions followed the July 15, 2016 coup attempt, after which the government blamed the Gülen movement and began removing alleged supporters from state institutions. The Justice Ministry said 50,510 people had been arrested and 169,013 faced legal proceedings, while more than 150,000 judges, teachers, police and civil servants were suspended or dismissed.

QuantifiedStrategies.com features articles on market timing, market regime indicators, and trend-following strategies, including Bitcoin timing, Sy Harding’s Seasonal Timing Strategy, Yale Hirsch’s Best 6 Months Timing Model, Coppock Curve, Fabian Timing Model, Nelson Freeburg’s PENTAD model, and SuperTrend. Many posts cover trading rules, performance, risk analysis, and backtest findings. The site is managed by independent traders Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette, who have more than 20 years of trading experience.
The Court unanimously ordered the appeal withdrawn according to the parties’ January 11, 2010 stipulation, following argument and deliberation.

On September 20, 2016, Microsoft’s Board amended Section 1.14 of its bylaws to clarify how groups of funds count toward the 3% proxy-access ownership threshold, count loaned shares recallable within five business days as owned, clarify indemnification provisions, and reduce from 25% to 15% the voting support needed to re-nominate a proxy-access candidate in one of the following two years. Microsoft’s 2016 annual shareholders meeting was scheduled for November 30, 2016, with September 30 as the record date. The amended bylaws were filed as Exhibit 3.2.

Leaked benchmarks reportedly from Nvidia's Discord show the Titan V scoring 32,774 in Fire Strike, ahead of the Titan Xp (28,000) and GTX 1080 Ti (28,300) despite lower clockspeeds, thanks to Volta's HBM2 memory and 652.8 GB/s bandwidth. It posts high frame rates at 1440p. Priced near $3,000, it targets AI and developer buyers, with cheaper Volta cards expected in 2018.

Relegation-threatened Sunderland are bottom, seven points from safety with 10 games left after one win in 11. Manager David Moyes urged his players to create chances for Jermain Defoe, who has scored 14 of their 24 league goals.

The passage presents RSI, ADX, and IBS as complementary short-term trading indicators, collectively called the “Big Three.” RSI and IBS can support mean-reversion strategies, while ADX identifies trending markets and measures trend strength without indicating direction.

RSI measures the speed and magnitude of gains and losses on a 0–100 scale. Readings above 70 generally indicate overbought conditions, while readings below 30 indicate oversold conditions. Bullish and bearish divergences can provide buy and sell signals. Stock backtests cited favored two- and three-day RSI periods, though readers are advised to test their own settings.

ADX, developed by Welles Wilder, is part of the Directional Movement System, which includes DMI+, DMI−, and ADX. Cited backtests favored periods of five to ten days and strong-trend thresholds of roughly 30–40. IBS measures the closing price’s position within the day’s high-low range on a 0–1 scale; low readings are bullish and high readings are bearish. A simple strategy buying below 0.2 and selling above 0.8 produced a 1.92 profit factor.

Separate backtests reported average gains of 0.78% for IBS on QQQ, 0.98% for RSI on SPY, and a 6.5% CAGR for ADX on SPY. A combined two-indicator strategy on SPY produced 270 trades, a 0.86% average gain, and a 56% risk-adjusted return while invested only 14% of the time; 2018 was its only losing year, at −5.5%. On QQQ, it averaged 1.3% per trade with no losing years since 2000. The strategy reportedly retained good out-of-sample performance after its October 2020 publication, but the passage stresses that no trading strategy is certain or guaranteed.

Erie Federal Credit Union reopened Erie’s former Glenwood School as its corporate headquarters and ninth branch. The 42,000-square-foot, full-service building provides teller services, loans, wealth management, safe deposits and ATMs; preserves local history; returns the property to the tax rolls; and accommodates future growth.

DNA from Qila and Aurora, a Vancouver Aquarium mother and daughter, will be sequenced to create a near-complete beluga genome for conservation research. Their 2016 deaths resulted from an unidentified toxin, not bacteria or viruses.

Citadel Securities hired Anthony Cronin to lead European Treasuries trading, expanding coverage across Europe’s full trading day, late Asia hours and the Middle East. The firm also hired Michele How for fixed-income sales and is targeting Asian clients, particularly in Hong Kong, mainland China and Japan. Since 2016, its Treasury counterparties have nearly tripled to over 450, while average daily volume has almost quadrupled. Notional Treasury trades reached $6 trillion in 2017, up from $5 trillion. Citadel may seek Federal Reserve primary-dealer status after adding missing products and meeting participation requirements.

Despite unexpected Brexit and Trump victories, the author considers Marine Le Pen’s potential French presidential win plausible, though unlikely. Conservative rival François Fillon’s poll numbers have been hurt by a scandal over employing his wife as a paid parliamentary aide. Riots in French suburbs following an allegation of police rape have resulted in nearly 250 arrests and may benefit Le Pen’s anti-immigrant, tough-on-crime campaign. A secret report cited more than 50 violent incidents near Paris in one night, though no firearms have reportedly been used against police. The unrest could calm when school resumes.

The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, is a little-used momentum indicator that measures accumulation/distribution (distinct from the Chaikin Money Flow Indicator) and oscillates around zero. It is calculated in four steps: money flow multiplier from closing price, money flow volume, the Accumulation/Distribution Line (ADL), and finally the difference between a shorter and longer moving average of the ADL (EMA(ADL,3) – EMA(ADL,10) in the Amibroker code shown). This mirrors MACD methodology, using EMA convergence and divergence to gauge momentum and potential trend reversals. Signals come from crosses above/below zero (above indicating buying pressure/accumulation, below selling pressure/distribution) and from bullish or bearish divergences — bearish when price makes a higher high without the oscillator following, bullish when price makes a new low but the oscillator makes a higher low — which require confirmation. The article also shows the indicator applied to silver miners (SIL).

Quantified tests on the S&P 500 showed little predictive value. A strategy buying above zero and selling below yielded a 2.4% CAGR over twenty years at optimal 10/20-day settings; reversing the criteria improved results given the index's mean-reverting nature (best ~10/50 days), producing 287 trades, 0.54 average per trade, a 1.76 profit factor and 37% max drawdown. A strategy applying two-day RSI to the oscillator (buy when RSI reading below 5, sell when the close exceeds yesterday's high) gave 216 trades, 0.3% average per trade, 1.6 profit factor and 18% drawdown; a third strategy (two-day RSI of the stock below 20 while the oscillator is above zero, same sell rule) yielded 216 trades, 0.3% average, 1.6 profit factor and 17% drawdown. Overall, none of the ten tested strategies proved significantly profitable, though the indicator may still be useful as a gauge of buying versus selling pressure.

Dwyne Wade, Gabrielle Union, and their son Zion visited Miami’s Frost Science museum, where they watched a planetarium show, saw fish and stingrays, wore science sunglasses, and ate tacos. Wade also responded to a Twitter troll who called him the weakest link on the Chicago Bulls.

Players reflected on playoff frustration after disappointing results against Florida and the Rangers, noting that the team generated chances but failed to convert them. They emphasized refocusing, improving passing and puck execution, taking more shots, creating power-play opportunities, and avoiding turnovers as the series tightened. The group welcomed a return to the road, where fewer distractions and less travel could help them concentrate, and hoped extra rest would benefit them. Video review showed the team controlling play and spending time in the offensive zone, but repeated shutouts and shots hitting the crossbar caused frustration. They described the next opponent as an honest, hard-forechecking team with a strong penalty kill and effective blue-line play, making zone entry more difficult than against the Rangers and Flyers. Practice energy remained positive, and the players prepared to focus on a brief warmup and be ready for the game.

KU sociologist Brock Ternes surveyed 864 Kansans and found that private well ownership correlated with more watering during droughts, while conservation varied by well type. He attributes this to well owners’ irrigation needs and awareness of groundwater availability, arguing that extracting water during scarcity does not make them poor environmentalists and that stewardship requires selective timing of withdrawals. Ternes said the overpumped High Plains Aquifer could stop supporting irrigation wells in southwestern Kansas within 25 years unless pumping is curtailed.

The disclosure describes an autonomous vehicle management system for safely controlling autonomous vehicles and machines. The system uses onboard or remote sensor data to build and continually update a consistent, layered 3D internal map of the vehicle and its environment. A planning subsystem uses this map, localization data, goals, safety constraints, route information, and operational history to generate action plans, while a controls subsystem directs braking, steering, propulsion, electrical, and auxiliary systems to execute those plans safely.

The system dynamically controls sensors to adjust what data they collect or transmit, including field of view, resolution, data volume, transmission rate, timing, and format. It also simulates multiple “what-if” scenarios by modifying internal-map parameters and comparing possible outcomes to select safer actions, sometimes using pruned decision trees.

AI techniques include convolutional neural networks for object detection and reinforcement learning for action planning. Confidence scores assess similarity between inference data and training data, allowing unreliable predictions to be overridden. A Safety Sanity Index and interruptible commands help prevent unsafe reinforcement-learning actions. An information subsystem can present planned actions and their reasons to drivers, passengers, remote observers, or others in the environment.

Leon Cooperman believes the market is in the late stage of a bull market, with stretched valuations, irrational exuberance, and momentum-driven buying resembling Warren Buffett’s 1999 warnings. The S&P 500 has risen nearly 40% from its April lows, led by richly valued AI-related mega-cap technology stocks, while the Buffett Indicator has reached 217%, exceeding the Dotcom and 2021 peaks. Cooperman considers stocks less risky than government bonds at current levels because inflation erodes bonds’ fixed nominal returns.

Several large U.S. school districts approved teacher-union raises but later lacked funding to honor them. Philadelphia avoided a strike with 3% annual raises, then sought permission to borrow up to $1.5 billion amid a state budget impasse that added about $15 million in interest costs. Chicago approved raises under a four-year contract while facing a $734 million deficit, ultimately balancing its $10.25 billion budget without a short-term loan. Baltimore County rescinded a scheduled 5% raise after federal relief funding declined and a request for additional money was denied; the union rejected a 1.5% offer before settling on 3.05%. Fairfax County’s first union agreement in nearly 50 years covered 27,500 members, but the district received less than half the funding it requested, and future increases depend on local government funding. U.S. public school debt grew from $415 billion in 2013 to more than $586 billion in 2023.

Seven children awaiting Big Brothers Big Sisters mentors assembled bicycles with Trenton police officers, FBI agents and community figures. The activity promoted teamwork, mentoring and connections with law enforcement. Each team will build a second bicycle for donation to another child through Capital K-9, funded by a community foundation grant.

This is a continuation patent application (Ser. No. 16/258,265, filed Jan. 25, 2019, claiming priority to provisional Ser. No. 62/667,188, filed May 4, 2018) titled "Methods and Apparatus Related to ACK/NACK Feedback with Multi-TRP Transmissions." It relates generally to communication systems, and more particularly to providing acknowledgement (ACK)/negative ACK (NACK) feedback in a wireless network including multiple transmission reception points (TRPs), with background discussion of 5G NR, multiple-access technologies, NR frame/slot structure and numerology, and downlink/uplink channels (PDCCH, PDSCH, PUCCH, PUSCH, reference signals).

A base station may send a UE information indicating PDCCH monitoring occasions for each of a plurality of TRPs; an indication of whether ACK/NACK feedback across the plurality of TRPs is allowed; rules for performing ACK/NACK feedback bundling when it is allowed; and a DAI definition indicating whether the DAIs transmitted by the TRPs are joint (counting PDCCH grants across all TRPs and scheduled carriers) or independent (counting only that TRP's grants across scheduled carriers). Correspondingly, the UE may receive this information and transmit either a joint ACK/NACK feedback in a PUCCH with a determined codebook size based on the bundling rules, or multiple individual ACK/NACK feedbacks in PUCCHs sent separately to each TRP.

The disclosure describes multi-TRP downlink modes (a single DCI granting one transport block with spatial layers from different TRPs; multiple DCIs each granting one transport block), codebook size determination for type 1 (semi-static) and type 2 (dynamic) HARQ codebooks based on PDCCH monitoring occasions, DL-data-DL-acknowledgement slot timing values, and DAIs, and CBG-level versus TB-level ACK/NACK. Bundling rules are described for identical payloads (joint ACK if data from any one TRP is received) and different payloads (joint NACK unless data from both TRPs is received). Joint DAI suits tight coordination/fast backhaul, while independent DAI suits loose coordination, requiring the UE to combine DAIs. Individual PUCCHs may be transmitted in a TDM manner, on different resources, or concurrently from multiple UE antenna arrays. Flowchart methods for the base station and UE and data-flow diagrams for a base station apparatus (reception, control/processing, transmission, monitoring occasion, feedback information, rules, DAI definition, and feedback components) are also described.
SEC establishes a 32-bit C environment and stack via AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. Two PEIMs divide AMD initialization; one initializes processors and publishes AmdCpuEarlyInit PPI.
Tippecanoe Middle School in Tipp City released its principal’s list and honor roll for the second grading period of the 2017–18 school year, naming students in sixth, seventh, and eighth grades.

C-BerryTrans is a GNU GPL 3.0-licensed C++ program for computing intrinsic Berry curvature, anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) directly from WIEN2k first-principles output. It extracts eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements, calculates the antisymmetric band-resolved Berry curvature tensor using a Kubo-like formula, and integrates it over the full Brillouin zone. AHC contributions are weighted by the Fermi–Dirac distribution, while ANC contributions use an entropy-related weighting.

The program avoids Wannier interpolation, thereby eliminating interpolation errors and the difficulty of constructing high-quality Wannier functions for strongly entangled or highly dispersive bands. Spin–orbit coupling is required because, without it, the Berry curvature is antisymmetric under momentum inversion and the intrinsic transverse-response integrals vanish. The formulation describes intrinsic responses in clean to moderately dirty, low-temperature regimes and does not include extrinsic mechanisms or scattering effects significant at higher temperatures.

The workflow begins with self-consistent, SOC-enabled WIEN2k ground-state calculations. Users specify the WIEN2k case directory, crystal structure, k-mesh, spin treatment, chemical-potential and temperature ranges, energy window, thread count, and other parameters. A dedicated module generates the full-Brillouin-zone k-list because momentum matrices do not generally obey the same symmetry relations as eigenvalues. The code processes k-points in batches to control memory use and parallelizes Berry-curvature and transport calculations over k-points using OpenMP.

Band-resolved Berry curvature is stored in compact binary files, reducing storage size substantially. Post-processing then calculates AHC or ANC over requested combinations of temperature and chemical potential without repeating the costly Berry-curvature calculation. The same stored data can therefore be reused for different parameter ranges. A Python visualization module, berryTrans plot.py, provides interactive plots of Fermi- or entropy-weighted Berry curvature.

The code uses dense, uniformly distributed k-meshes; transport calculations commonly require meshes of 400×400×400 or larger. It supports configurable energy windows, thread allocation, k-point batching, spin-polarized systems, and parallel or serial execution. Its workflow consists of generating k-lists, computing eigenvalues and momentum matrices through WIEN2k, evaluating and storing Berry curvature, and performing transport post-processing.

Validation results for Fe, Pd, Fe3Al, and Co2FeAl were compared with literature values for AHC or ANC. The implementation is currently interfaced with WIEN2k but is described as portable to other DFT packages such as ELK and Quantum ESPRESSO.

Markets turned decisively risk-off, with major indexes falling 2.2%–4.2% and forming bearish engulfing patterns near record highs. Negative volume, deteriorating breadth, nearly universal sector losses, and strength in Treasuries and utilities reinforced the bearish shift.

Earnings remained a bright spot: 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies exceeded EPS estimates and 79% beat revenue estimates, while earnings revisions increased. However, economic data raised slowdown concerns. GDP exceeded expectations at 3%, though tariffs skewed imports and personal spending weakened. Nonfarm payrolls rose only 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with unusually large downward revisions, while unemployment held at 4.2%.

The Fed drew two dissents for the first time since the 1990s. Powell emphasized patience and dependence on incoming data as tariff and immigration policies complicated inflation and labor-market signals; markets nevertheless anticipated a September rate cut and three cuts by January.

Policy uncertainty added volatility, including Trump’s planned 100% China tariff, the firing of the labor-data commissioner, a Fed governor’s resignation, and renewed tensions with Russia.

VentureWire’s November 17, 2000 issue reports that e-government provider govWorks laid off about 70 employees, leaving 50, and may close or seek a buyer; Whitney & Co. plans a $2.5 billion global fund; eHitex appointed Robert Lewis CEO; and PlanetOut agreed to merge with Online Partners, parent of Gay.com, forming PlanetOut Partners.

Funding news included Tridium’s $20 million first round, split between kRoad Ventures and Enron North America, and new financing for Symmorphix, Encore Software, Opion, HotDispatch, RAW Communications, Restaurantpro/CriticalArc, Workscape, The Brodia Group and others. BeautyJungle shut down, TheStreet.com closed its U.K. venture and cut 20% of its workforce, and GiftCertificates.com withdrew its IPO.

M&A included Intuit’s $39 million EmployeeMatters acquisition and TCS’s planned $65.2 million Xypoint purchase. The issue also covered new products, directors and CEOs, venture funds, Kodak venture-capital hires and a GreenOrder correction.

Switzerland’s economic ministry will consider industry requests to ease weapons export rules, including longer licences and lifting the ban on exports to countries in internal armed conflict. The industry says stricter rules disadvantage Swiss firms, reduce exports, and threaten jobs. Involved ministries may propose amendments to the Federal Council, though advocates warn this could violate Swiss neutrality and security.

CompareCards presents a hand-selected roundup of credit cards with long 0% introductory APR offers, which can reduce interest on high-interest balances or large purchases. It notes that people who pay balances in full and on time generally come out ahead and says its ratings are not influenced by compensation from listed companies.

Featured offers include:

- A Discover card with 15 months of 0% APR on purchases and balance transfers, 5% quarterly rotating cash back, 1% on other purchases, and a first-year cash-back match that could double $150 to $300. It has no annual fee. Another Discover offer provides 18 months of 0% on transfers, six months on purchases, 2% at gas stations and restaurants, and a first-year match.
- A Bank of America Preferred Rewards card offering 15 billing cycles of 0% APR, a $200 bonus after $1,000 in purchases, 6% cash back in a selected category during the first year, 2% at grocery stores and wholesale clubs, and 1% elsewhere. It has no annual fee.
- A Bank of America travel card earning 1.5 points per dollar on all purchases and 3 points per dollar on travel booked through its travel center, plus 25,000 points after $1,000 in qualifying purchases.
- A Citi balance-transfer card with 18 months of 0% on transfers, 2% cash back on purchases, 5% on travel booked through Citi Travel, and $200 back after $1,500 in purchases.
- Capital One Quicksilver, offering 15 months of 0% on purchases and transfers, unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% back on select travel, and up to $300 in welcome bonuses.
- Capital One VentureOne, offering 15 months of 0% on purchases and transfers, 1.25 miles per dollar, 5 miles on select travel, and up to $300 in travel bonuses.
- Additional cards with 20,000 or 30,000 point bonuses after $1,000 in spending, rewards on dining, travel, gas, transit, streaming and phone purchases, and customizable category bonuses.

The passage explains that low-interest cards generally offer fixed or variable APRs. Fixed rates remain relatively stable, while variable rates typically follow movements in the prime rate. Introductory rates may revert to regular APRs afterward, and balance-transfer fees apply on many cards. It identifies the interest rate as a major borrowing cost and says its editors objectively evaluate more than 100 cards from over 50 issuers.

Global stocks and the dollar rebounded Monday as U.S.-North Korea tensions eased after driving the previous week’s biggest equity losses of 2017. European shares rose 0.9%, Asia-Pacific markets led gains in Australia, Hong Kong and South Korea, and MSCI’s world index advanced 0.2%. Tokyo stocks fell 1% despite Japan’s 1% second-quarter growth, as the yen’s surge weighed on exporters. The dollar gained 0.5% against the yen to 109.70, while U.S. and German 10-year yields rose. Softer but generally solid Chinese data suggested no imminent hard landing and highlighted global recovery, prompting debate over whether central banks might reduce asset purchases. U.S. officials downplayed the risk of nuclear conflict, though North Korea’s Liberation Day festivities could revive tensions. Brent crude fell 42 cents to $51.68 a barrel.

The passage outlines defensive tactics against the Single/Double Offense, which uses double and down screens to free shooters. Because bigs screen for smalls, switching can leave a larger screener posting against a smaller defender; consequently, NBA teams commonly prefer “Show and Recover,” though tactics vary. Defenders influence shooters away from their preferred side and pressure ballhandlers toward the sideline. Against double screens, X4 and X5 show to force shooters wide while X2 and X3 chase; defenders then recover into pass-denial positions, pressure shooters, push posts off the block, and pack the weakside toward the ball. Similar show, chase, and recover principles apply against single screens, with post mismatches potentially trapped.

All-out SOS disruption initiates defensive action and traps wing shooters while the point guard sets the weakside screen. Defenders pressure the ballhandler toward the sideline, use contact switches and Snuggle denial, front posts, double-team shooters, and rotate into Triangle “I” positions. Closeouts begin as passes leave the passer’s hands, and traps can also be applied to drives and post mismatches.

The passage proposes a hybrid method-of-moments (MoM) and generalized scattering matrix (GSM) framework for multiscale antenna problems. Unlike earlier MoM–T-matrix approaches, the electrically large environment is discretized with MoM, while geometrically intricate antennas are represented by compact GSM data, reducing unknowns and enabling modular reuse, analytic transformations, and efficient array synthesis. The formulation uses PMCHWT integral equations with RWG basis functions and Galerkin testing to solve equivalent electric and magnetic currents in penetrable structures. Antenna and structure fields are coupled through vector spherical-wave expansions, with a truncation degree determined from the antenna’s enclosing radius. The framework can be reformulated as a fully coupled GSM–physical-optics hybrid for large reflectors or a GSM–T-matrix hybrid for structures suited to spherical-wave expansions. Overall, it provides a modular, reusable approach for analyzing implantable antennas, radome-enclosed arrays, and reflector antennas.

Pop singer Helgi Bjornsson recently appeared on Icelandic television, where a deadpan reporter challenged him to defend his 1980s hit “I Do Like the Rain” amid Reykjavik’s gloomy weather. Meteorologists say the capital has experienced its worst May and June since 1914, with rain every day in May and only 70 hours of sunshine in June. High pressure over western Europe has shifted the jet stream, directing clouds and rain toward Iceland while Britain and southern Scandinavia face heat waves. Disappointing forecasts have hurt sunshine-dependent businesses and summer tourism, though some visitors prefer the cooler climate. The passage also recalls the biblical rainfall of June 1914 and reflects widespread local resilience and hope.

UBS reaffirmed its dividend increases and a $2 billion share-repurchase programme for 2025–2027 despite Swiss regulators calling for higher capital buffers. CEO Sergio Ermotti said shareholder returns remain on track and UBS has time to strengthen capital without compromising payouts. Following its Credit Suisse acquisition, UBS is progressing with integration; Swiss systems consolidation is expected by early 2026, while most overseas operational and client transfers are complete. Ermotti also pledged annual shareholder guidance. Analysts view the stance as evidence of financial strength and operational stability but caution that worsening market conditions could make it harder to balance regulatory requirements with investor expectations.

Russia seized the American whaling bark Cape Horn Pigeon on September 10 for hunting whales in the closed Okhotsk Sea. Captain Scullun claimed the interruption of his voyage caused substantial losses, including $45,000 for five whales, while Russia’s ministry of marine considered $2,500 adequate for actual losses and requested vouchers for other claims. Scullun alleged that his crew was abandoned without food or lodging at Vladivostok, but naval authorities testified that Scullun declined customary assistance. The U.S. envoy requested an investigation and aid for the crew while doubting their reported condition. The vessel was subsequently liberated, and the Russian inquiry into the crew’s treatment continued.

President Trump called for a world of sovereign, independent nations that defend their citizens, culture, and national interests, rejecting globalism and domination. He cited U.S. economic gains, a major military rebuilding, and stronger alliances, while demanding that partners contribute more to defense.

He advocated fair, reciprocal trade, supporting the USMCA, negotiations with Japan and the United Kingdom, and tariffs on more than $500 billion in Chinese goods. He accused China of subsidies, market barriers, intellectual-property theft, and other unfair practices while demanding changes to its WTO status. He also criticized Iran, withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal, imposed sanctions, and opposed normalization with North Korea until it denuclearizes.

On migration, Trump condemned human smuggling and trafficking, insisted on border enforcement, and praised regional cooperation. He backed efforts to support Cubans, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans, condemned socialism and the Maduro government, and warned about foreign technology and threats to free speech. He also defended LGBTQ rights, women’s economic empowerment, religious freedom, abortion opposition, and the Second Amendment. He concluded by urging world leaders to strengthen their nations and pursue peace, freedom, and progress beginning at home.
Two appeals concerning Christ Guehler’s estate were filed April 7, 1932, with Justice Wolfe delivering the court’s opinion.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 28, 2019 identifies the company as a California corporation headquartered in Cupertino, with common stock traded on Nasdaq under AAPL. The filing describes Apple’s businesses in smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, accessories, digital content, streaming, cloud storage, support, payments and related services. It discusses direct and indirect distribution, intense competition, outsourced manufacturing, component supply risks, research and development, intellectual property, seasonality, and approximately 137,000 full-time equivalent employees.

Risk factors include adverse economic conditions, rapid technological change, dependence on distributors and third-party developers and content, inventory write-downs, component shortages, manufacturing disruptions, product defects, intellectual-property disputes, evolving laws, data-security and privacy obligations, retail-store costs, acquisitions, system failures, dependence on key personnel, geopolitical events, foreign-exchange movements, credit and investment risks, tax changes, and stock-price volatility.

For 2019, net sales declined 2% to $260.174 billion and net income was $55.256 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $11.89. Product sales were $142.381 billion for iPhone, $25.740 billion for Mac, $21.280 billion for iPad, and $24.482 billion for Wearables, Home and Accessories; Services generated $46.291 billion. Geographic net sales were $116.914 billion in the Americas, $60.288 billion in Europe, $43.678 billion in Greater China, $21.506 billion in Japan and $17.788 billion in Rest of Asia Pacific. Total gross margin was $98.392 billion, or 37.8%.

Apple increased its share-repurchase authorization from $100 billion to $175 billion, repurchased $67.1 billion of stock during 2019 and paid $14.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. At September 28, 2019, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $205.898 billion, total assets were $338.516 billion, and $78.9 billion remained available under the repurchase authorization.

The lecture reviews the Weierstrass M-test: if functions \(f_j:S\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) and \(\sum M_j\) converges, then the partial sums of \(\sum f_j\) converge uniformly. A cosine-series example therefore converges uniformly on \(\mathbb R\), and its limit is continuous because a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous.

For a power series \(\sum a_j(x-x_0)^j\) with radius of convergence \(\rho>0\), the series converges uniformly on every closed interval \([x_0-R,x_0+R]\) with \(0<R<\rho\). The M-test applies with \(M_j=|a_j|R^j\), while the root test shows that \(\sum |a_j|R^j\) converges because \(R/\rho<1\).

Within the radius of convergence, the power series may be differentiated and integrated term by term. The formally differentiated series has the same radius of convergence as the original, so uniform convergence justifies the derivative identity. This argument can be iterated: the \(k\)-th derivative is obtained term by term, and at \(x_0\), the \(k\)-th derivative equals \(k!a_k\). Consequently, the power series is the Taylor series of its sum function. The lecture also notes that stronger theorems for interchanging limits occur in the theory of Lebesgue integration and are important in studying Fourier series.

The final topic is Weierstrass’s approximation theorem: every continuous function on \([0,1]\) is the uniform limit on \([0,1]\) of a sequence of polynomials. The proof is first reduced to functions satisfying \(f(0)=f(1)=0\), allowing them to be extended continuously by zero outside the interval.

For the proof, the polynomials
\[
q_n(x)=c_n(1-x^2)^n,\qquad
c_n=\left(\int_{-1}^{1}(1-x^2)^n\,dx\right)^{-1}
\]
are constructed. They are nonnegative on \([-1,1]\), have integral \(1\), and converge uniformly to zero on \(\{x:\delta\le |x|\le1\}\) for every \(0<\delta<1\). Thus their mass concentrates near zero. Using these as approximations to the identity, one defines
\[
p_n(x)=\int_0^1 f(t)q_n(t-x)\,dt.
\]
The binomial theorem shows that each \(p_n\) is a polynomial.

Uniform continuity and boundedness of \(f\) provide a uniform error estimate. For \(|t|<\delta\), \(f(x+t)\) is close to \(f(x)\); outside this region, boundedness controls the error, while the concentration of \(q_n\) makes that contribution small. Choosing \(n\) sufficiently large yields \(\|p_n-f\|_\infty<\varepsilon\), proving the approximation theorem.

Louisville officials warn that neighborhood fireworks create particle pollution that can linger, aggravate respiratory problems, exceed federal limits, and cause more pollution than the city’s fireworks show. Louisville last exceeded federal limits on Independence Day in 2015.

In the Circuit Court for the District of New Jersey, Curtis and Cook’s 1883 patent for portable elevated railroads was held anticipated by an 1866 single-track overhead railway at Camden Iron Works, so claims 1–3 were void. The defendant’s structure infringed claim 4, which covered an elevated main track combined with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler. Because the record did not rebut the presumption of patentability, the court directed a decree for the plaintiff on claim 4.

Kenyon College’s Whiteness Group, run through its multicultural center, educates students about whiteness and privilege and promotes anti-racist action and white allyship. Ground rules prohibit white participants from asking people of color questions, require white participants to answer such questions themselves, and discourage sharing rumors about meeting discussions. Founder Juniper Cruz, a self-described Queer Afro-Latinx Muslim, said the group seeks “a sustainable form of activism” and called racism “a white people problem”; about 50 students attended its first meeting. Chaplain Rachel Kessler said shame about racial privilege and fear of saying something problematic can impede efforts against racism and white supremacy.

In Supreme Court arguments, a majority of justices appeared skeptical of Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy for minors. The 2019 law prohibits mental health professionals from providing such treatment to clients under 18 but exempts religious ministry. Licensed Christian counselor Kaley Chiles, who challenges the law as discriminating against her speech, had earlier lost before the 10th Circuit, which applied rational-basis review. Her lawyer and the Trump administration argued that the law is unconstitutional because it restricts speech and subjects biased professional standards to judicial review. Colorado argued that the law narrowly regulates a harmful medical treatment without preventing clinicians from expressing views. The justices debated Chiles’s standing, the distinction between medical treatment and speech, and whether the law reflects professional standards or ideology. Some justices, including Sotomayor and Jackson, favored returning the case to lower courts for further review; Barrett also suggested openness to remand. Kavanaugh asked no questions.

The excerpt lists terminal functions for DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers 0 and 1. Data strobes are outputs during writes and inputs during reads; DQS[3] serves data bits 31:24 and DQS[0] serves bits 7:0. Controller 0 chip-select termination uses IPD during reset and DIS afterward. Controller 1 pins generally use IPU during reset and DIS afterward, while DQM pins switch from IPU to IPD after reset. DQM[3] serves bits 31:24, DQM[1] bits 15:8, and DQM[0] bits 7:0.

The speaker reflects on a disappointing finals loss but celebrates his brother’s win. He values playing together and sharing family time most. Trust built through playing alongside Randy has been key, along with strong performances from both goaltenders.

This medRxiv preprint, posted January 3, 2025, and not certified by peer review, examines a culture-independent citizen science approach for monitoring household drinking water microbiomes in China. Citizen scientists collected 50 tap-water samples from 32 administrative regions across 19 provinces/regions between December 2020 and August 2021, including opportunistic samples after the 2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa.

The standardized, low-cost protocol provided volunteers with sampling kits, Chinese-language instructions, a video tutorial, and demonstrations. Samples were disinfected, collected in sodium-thiosulfate-treated water to remove residual chlorine, filtered through 0.20-micron Corning syringe filters, frozen, and shipped to the laboratory. Investigators extracted DNA, amplified the V4 region of the bacterial 16S rRNA gene, pooled positive amplicons, and conducted Illumina MiSeq sequencing and DADA2/Silva analysis. Outdoor temperature data were collected for 40 valid samples to account for seasonality.

Twenty-two of the 50 samples tested positive for microbial DNA. Metabarcoding identified 7,635 amplicon sequence variants and a diverse tap-water microbiome. Mycobacterium, Acinetobacter, and Legionella were detected in every PCR-positive sample. Local samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou following the Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa contained additional pathogenic species such as Salmonella enterica and toxin-producing cyanobacteria such as Microcystis. The study concludes that citizen science can expand microbial monitoring and inform future drinking-water safety strategies.

Participants debated whether the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals should expressly enumerate respect for international obligations, including treaties. Pasvolsky considered it inherent but open to specific wording and placement; Honduras and Chile addressed its status in international law and inclusion in the proposals. Venezuela corrected the record on unanimity, after which the minutes were approved.

Discussion turned to Chapter VI and Security Council composition. Pasvolsky said the Council must be efficient, effective, and representative; permanent seats should correspond to capacity and willingness to bear its principal responsibilities, and the five permanent members reflected global military and industrial predominance. He noted the League Council’s growth and the Dumbarton Oaks conclusion that nonpermanent members must outnumber permanent members, while declining at that stage to prescribe Assembly selection rules because alternatives to regional representation had been proposed. Chile preferred not to repeat matters already summarized since the meetings were not to make decisions. Brazil urged permanent Latin American representation and emphasized the Organization’s preventive purpose. Ambassador Martins then introduced Brazil’s position for the forthcoming Mexico and United Nations conferences.

A truck carrying undocumented immigrants crashed near the California–Mexico border sixteen years ago, leaving one severely injured 18- to 20-year-old Mexican boy who woke in a San Diego hospital in a "vegetative state," unable to reveal his name or origins; nurses called him Pancho for paperwork. Websites and Facebook groups devoted to finding missing undocumented immigrants have since spread his story, and two years ago a woman in McAllen, Texas, recognized him in a photo in a group called "Pathway to the North" and sent it to her cousin in Houston, wondering if he was Gilberto.

Quarters coverage is a 4-deep, 3-underneath scheme that combines zone droppers with man-style coverage on the back end. Cornerbacks cover the #1 receiver, safeties track the #2 while supporting the run, outside linebackers handle the flats, and the middle linebacker covers the hook. Its main weaknesses are the flats and middle of the field. Offenses can exploit these areas by reading linebacker movement, using hitch routes, manipulating safeties with play action, creating high-low progressions, running safeties off to open the middle, and using overload concepts to create isolated matchups. The five examples include wide-zone concepts, backside option routes, shallow stings, Colt Y leaks, and play-action slot-cross routes.

In at least 11 North Carolina counties, early-childhood agencies and community colleges run child care academies that provide accelerated, low-cost pathways into licensed child care. Programs last two to six weeks and require 20 to 64 hours of instruction. The classroom-ready model qualifies students for child care jobs but not lead-teacher positions. The teaching credential model adds the EDU 119 curriculum and provides transferable EDU 3119 credit, enabling graduates to qualify as lead teachers or elementary teaching assistants while continuing toward an associate degree.

The expansion follows reports that 60% of licensed North Carolina child care providers faced staffing shortages. Although the House included $1.476 million for an academy pilot, the funding was omitted from legislation signed by Gov. Josh Stein. DCDEE is separately offering grants of up to $50,000 for up to 10 UNC institutions to operate academies through July 31, 2026.

Local programs in Wayne, Johnston, Stanly, McDowell and Durham counties use grants, foundation funding and community partnerships to offer safety training, background checks, job placement and tuition assistance. Reported outcomes include 63 graduates in Wayne and Johnston, six lead-teacher credential recipients in McDowell, and 140 applicants for 20 Durham slots.

A review found caffeine per ounce varies widely: McDonald’s has 9 mg, Dunkin’ 12.7 mg, Peet’s 16.7 mg, Starbucks 20.6 mg, and Death Wish 54.2 mg. Drinking more coffee than previously thought may be safe and linked to longevity.

The patent describes automated parcel and object sortation systems using robotic arms, perception units, conveyors, programmable carriages, and shuttle-wing sorters. It addresses limitations of human-operated sorting and fixed bin assignments, including labor requirements, throughput and divert constraints, space and operating costs, and the mechanical complexity of conventional automated diverts.

In the disclosed embodiments, objects arrive in mixed streams or buffers. Cameras, scanners, and machine-vision systems identify labels, object class, shape, and disposition. Robotic devices acquire objects, including from jumbles, and dynamically assign them to intermediate collection bins associated with destinations. A central controller selects and reuses bins, tracks their contents, removes completed bins based on fullness or expected demand, and routes unidentified or unassigned objects for rescanning or manual handling.

Bin-to-destination mappings may change dynamically using heuristics, current system conditions, historical trends, object and facility characteristics, known deliveries, and network costs. This allows fewer outputs than destinations, reduces space and labor requirements, and improves scalability and resilience.

Further embodiments use a multi-camera drop-perception unit, reciprocating carriages, and parallel shuttle-wing sections whose carriages carry and tip objects into assigned bins. Paired bins can be removed, while indicators and portable scanners or printers support emptying, bagging, and labeling. The architecture can scale to eight wings and 64 bins, with additional robots and parallel stations increasing throughput and bin capacity.

The author argues that the post-election “Trump reflation” rally is vulnerable because high stock valuations leave little room for disappointment, while the administration may fail to deliver tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation. Optimistic investor sentiment and corporate earnings forecasts have outpaced actual economic activity, with Atlanta Fed growth estimates remaining modest and earnings revisions slowing. The rally could continue if fiscal policies boost earnings, but its reliance on policy expectations makes it speculative.

The Federal Reserve may tighten more quickly if it responds to elevated asset prices and risks an earlier-than-expected move. Historically high equity valuations are associated with poor future returns and returns only marginally above bonds, particularly globally. The author expects U.S. tax reform to be limited and piecemeal, with much of the benefit potentially reaching stocks through buybacks rather than broad economic reflation. As a result, stock prices are expected eventually to reflect economic reality more closely.

The passage defines SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication through the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), including requests for AP reset hold, hypervisor feature information, page state changes, Run VMPL, termination, and GHCB GPA management.

For SEV-SNP guests, a vCPU’s GHCB GPA must be registered before the GHCB is first used for a VMGEXIT. Guests may obtain a hypervisor-preferred GPA, register their chosen GPA, or unregister the current GPA. Registered GHCB pages are made hypervisor-owned and shared; registration replaces any previous registration. A hypervisor must terminate a guest that supplies a GPA conflicting with the registered GHCB and must support separate registrations per VMPL when SEV-SNP Multi-VMPL is advertised.

During negotiation, the hypervisor supplies GHCB protocol and page-table encryption information through VMCB offset 0x00a0. The guest obtains protocol versions and the encryption-bit position through intercepted CPUID or MSR requests, configures encrypted page tables, allocates and shares the GHCB page, and writes its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130 before issuing VMGEXIT. SEV-ES guests must establish the encryption-bit position before entering a mode where GHCB communications would otherwise expose encrypted data.

Non-automatic exit events generate a #VC exception. The guest inspects the error code, populates the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and, after resumption, copies returned state back into the faulting context. Guest and hypervisor reset and set the GHCB VALID_BITMAP; the minimum required fields are SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2, with nonzero SW_EXITINFO1 indicating an error. Software should disable interrupts and preemption while accessing the GHCB. Special handling is defined for IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, and MMIO accesses.

Page State Change requests reside in the shared GHCB buffer, which can hold up to 253 entries. They support making pages private or shared and SNP PSMASH and UNSMASH hints. Progress is tracked through cur_entry and cur_page so interrupted requests can resume.

SNP Guest Request events use separate shared request and response pages to access firmware synchronously. The hypervisor translates their GPAs, assigns the response page to firmware, reclaims it afterward, and returns the firmware result in SW_EXITINFO2. Message sequence numbers participate in the AES-GCM IV, so a retry must occur before another request to prevent IV reuse; rate limiting is recommended. The passage also defines guest-reserved secrets-page fields for VMPL message sequence numbers, AP jump-table addresses, and guest use, plus an EFI configuration table for passing SNP secrets and CPUID pages to firmware.

An MIT “Blockchain and Money” class session introduces smart contracts, decentralized applications, token sales, and their legal implications. Smart contracts are described as digitally encoded promises and protocols rather than artificial intelligence; they may be neither “smart” nor legally binding contracts. Their technical foundations include cryptography, decentralization, consensus, and transaction formats. Ethereum is presented as a Turing-complete, account-based platform using state transitions, multiple programming languages, proof of work, faster block creation, and ETH. It contrasts with Bitcoin’s transaction-ledger model and fixed monetary policy, while noting Ethereum’s more centralized leadership, adjustable block rewards, and higher inflation. Competing platforms include EOS, NEO, and Ethereum Classic.

DApp activity remained limited, especially compared with conventional internet applications, but initial coin offerings had raised substantial funds. Thousands of offerings were proposed, fewer than half were live, and estimates of failure or fraud varied widely.

Larry Lessig explains that contracts involve exchange, risk allocation, enforcement, and the state, which determines whether agreements are lawful and enforceable. Although code can automate obligations and potentially substitute for weak legal infrastructure, it cannot independently verify real-world events, eliminate jurisdictional questions, or eliminate the need for courts. Technology may also conflict with legal limitations, as illustrated by DRM and copyright fair use. Lessig argues that ambiguity can be valuable and that smart contracts are best suited to narrow, clearly defined transactions; lawyers will also need greater technical literacy to interpret and regulate code.

In Morris v. Scott, the court held that an action for malicious prosecution need not establish the jurisdiction of the court involved when the complaint’s malice and falsehood are the basis of the claim and the arrest or other trespass is only a consequence. Morris’s claim alleged that Scott falsely and without probable cause sought his arrest; his acquittal disproved probable cause. The lower court improperly excluded evidence and nonsuited him for failing to allege jurisdiction. The judgment was reversed, with a new trial ordered.

Backtests on SPY, GLD, and TLT indicate that consecutive lower highs and lower lows are typically a short-term reversal pattern. For the one-bar strategy, traders enter at the close and exit after 1–10 bars. In SPY, average gains rose from 0.09% with a one-day hold to 0.47% over ten trading days, compared with 0.44% for a random ten-day period. Longer holds performed better in GLD and TLT because those assets also had positive long-term trends during the test.

Requiring two consecutive lower-high/lower-low days slightly improved SPY results but did not materially improve GLD or TLT. A final strategy entering after three consecutive lower highs and lower lows increased average gains and profit factor; its maximum drawdown was 9.9% with a one-day hold. The pattern appears most effective for short-term reversals in stocks, though other signals may offer better short-holding-period returns.

Pompey await FA observations and could be fined; Mark Catlin said the club follows safety procedures but acknowledged prohibited devices can be hard to detect and cause distress.

The court denied enforcement of a tentative settlement reached by three former D.C. Department of Corrections employees who alleged retaliatory termination after media appearances about the halfway-house system. The parties agreed on a $625,000 payment in exchange for dismissal of the plaintiffs’ claims, but disputed whether re-enrollment in the city’s retirement system was also part of the agreement.

Applying D.C. contract law, the court found no “meeting of the minds” on re-enrollment. Defendants’ later statements, failure to initiate the re-enrollment process, absence of a written agreement, and plaintiffs’ refusal to complete the retirement application did not establish mutual assent. Plaintiffs also had not established an unconditional right to retirement benefits because their terminations had not been adjudicated unwarranted or unjustified. The court declined to enforce a separate settlement for one plaintiff because the monetary amount allocated to her had not been agreed upon.

The plaintiffs were given until September 9, 2002, either to accept the $625,000 offer without retirement benefits and dismiss the entire case, or to reject the offer and proceed to a status hearing and trial.

The Midline Option is a persistent concept that programs such as Oregon and Coastal Carolina have modernized. The quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman to decide whether to hand off to a fullback through the A-gap or keep the ball through the B-gap. Its primary strength is that the offense need not block the read defender; it also complements inside and outside veer and can use wingback motion as deception. Its main weakness is exposing the quarterback to repeated hits, so offenses generally use a rugged quarterback.

The passage details assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Two variations are highlighted: Flexbone Midline uses a playside Z instead of a tight end to spread the defense, while Midline “Follow” brings the pitch wingback downhill as an extra lead blocker on quarterback keeps. Army, Navy, and Air Force use Follow in short-yardage situations.

Collagen is a structural protein that supports skin, bones, tendons, ligaments and other tissues, but its natural production declines with age. The body has 28 collagen types, with types I, II and III most common in oral supplements. Supplements are mainly animal-derived, including marine collagen, bovine collagen, porcine collagen and chicken cartilage, and may be hydrolysed for easier digestion and absorption. Research suggests they may improve skin firmness and hydration, support nail, bone and joint health, reduce joint pain, and aid muscle growth or repair; evidence for thicker hair remains limited to mice. Suggested daily doses vary by goal, from 2.5 grams for joint pain, skin and hydration to 15 grams for muscle mass with resistance training. Manufacturers commonly advise at least 12 weeks for noticeable results. Experts recommend third-party-tested products and following label-specific dosages, while noting research is ongoing. A balanced diet with protein, vitamin C, zinc and copper remains the most reliable way to support natural collagen production.

The article backtests the "Santa Claus Rally" (year-end effect) in the German DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 using the liquid ETFs EWG (data to the late 1990s) and FEZ (data to 2002). EWG shows an average gain per trade of 2.1%, an 81% win ratio, and a profit factor of 13; FEZ shows 1.5%, 81%, and 9. In both cases, returns over the last six years fell well below the prior 15 years. Christmas-period performance significantly exceeds random weeks (0.12% for DAX 40, 0.18% for Euro Stoxx 50). Positions are held roughly 6–13 days on average; entering a week later shortens the holding period but reduces gains. The futures backtest runs from 2001, uses 100% margin with no leverage, and compounds from 100,000. The authors conclude the rally exists but caution it is no guarantee for the future.

Tesla handed over the first 30 Model 3s to employee buyers as CEO Elon Musk reported more than 500,000 advance reservations, up from 373,000 in April 2016.
