Trend Micro identified 89 malicious Chrome extensions on the official Chrome Web Store that affected more than 423,000 users and formed the “Droidclub” botnet. Installed through malvertising and deceptive prompts, the extensions injected advertisements, exploited websites, and used Yandex Metrica session-replay scripts to monitor browsing and capture form data, including credit card and contact details, though not passwords. An earlier version secretly mined Monero through Coinhive. The extensions also hindered reporting and removal by redirecting users to fake pages. Google removed and disabled the extensions, while Cloudflare took down the command-and-control servers.

P. falciparum PfEMP1, encoded by mutually exclusive var genes, mediates infected erythrocyte sequestration and is a major target of variant-specific antibodies. This study investigated how pre-existing malaria immunity influences var-gene expression, switching, and turnover during controlled human malaria infection (CHMI).

Nineteen semi-immune Gambian men were classified as sero-high or sero-low based on antibodies against six P. falciparum antigens and inoculated with 3,200 NF54/3D7 sporozoites. Sero-low participants had significantly higher peak parasitaemia. Two participants, both sero-high, were classified as controllers because they had the longest latency and lowest parasite multiplication rates.

Low-input whole-transcriptome sequencing of parasites from ten participants showed that var genes were the principal source of expression variability between infections. This was supported by RT-qPCR, which showed high concordance with RNA sequencing. Sero-low participants expressed more var transcripts and had broader, higher-entropy var repertoires, whereas controllers expressed a restricted set of genes. Greater var diversity was associated with shorter latency and faster parasite growth.

Var-gene turnover during infection was rapid. In one controller, all genes detected on day 14 were absent after three additional parasite cycles. Estimated in-vivo transition rates exceeded one per day for groups A, C, and E/var2csa, with group A transitioning faster than group B. These rates were consistent with a combination of intrinsic switching and immune selection.

Ten isolates from seven participants were cultured in vitro. Sero-low-derived isolates converged on similar high-entropy expression profiles within 20 days, whereas sero-high-derived isolates remained heterogeneous and some retained their initial profiles after 50 days. All isolates showed increasing expression entropy over time. A four-state Markov model estimated per-generation switching probabilities of 7% for group B, 44% for group A, 57% for group C, and 49% for group BC. Group C and BC switching rates were close to their in-vivo turnover rates, while group A and B switched more slowly in vitro.

Protein-array analysis measured antibodies against 213 PfEMP1 domains and 18 other malarial antigens. Sero-high participants recognized more 3D7 PfEMP1 domains before infection, and broader pre-existing recognition was associated with longer latency and lower peak parasitaemia. A random-forest model classified participants into the two immune-response groups with 98% accuracy. Sero-low participants more than doubled their breadth of PfEMP1 recognition after infection, while sero-high participants showed little change.

Pre-existing PfEMP1 antibody breadth was moderately inversely associated with var-expression entropy during infection, and antibody levels against specific PfEMP1s were negatively associated with expression of their corresponding genes, particularly in groups B/C, A, and B. However, the intensity of a var gene’s expression during CHMI was not directly associated with the antibody gain against it by day 35, including substantial acquisition of antibodies against the intracellular ATS domain.

The authors proposed that intrinsic switching maintains a diverse var repertoire through a “bet-hedging” strategy, while immune selection narrows that repertoire in strongly immune hosts. They hypothesized that the initial high-diversity state may be reset during mosquito or liver passage, inferred from the similarity between in-vivo sero-low profiles and the in-vitro steady state, and that poorly immunogenic PfEMP1 variants may persist despite immune pressure.

Soccer formations strategically position players to defend one goal and attack the other. Formation choice depends on team size, player skills, and the coach’s ability to teach and apply the required tactics. Over the past century, the game has trended toward fewer forwards, balanced spacing, versatile players, greater fitness, and more short passes.

In 11-a-side soccer, formations are described by the numbers of defenders, midfielders, and forwards, totaling 10 field players; examples include 4-3-3, 4-4-2, and 3-4-3. U.S. Soccer recommends 4-3-3 and 4-4-2 for ages U15–U19, 4-3-3 for U13–U14, and 3-2-3 for U9–U12. Coaches have more discretion in smaller-sided and youth games. Position names, player placement, formations, and tactics are interconnected, so coaches must understand positioning and teamwork, select an appropriate formation, and explain its implementation to the team.

NASA/ESA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured the spiral galaxy NGC 6000, 102 million light-years away in Scorpius. Patterns codify proven solutions, enabling developers to learn from others’ mistakes, communicate through shared terminology, and build reusable, consistent components. In containerized systems, patterns also support modularity, resource isolation, team ownership, separation of concerns, independent scaling, testing, and deployment.

Single-node container patterns tightly couple containers on one machine, often within a Kubernetes pod, and allow them to share filesystems, network namespaces, process namespaces, and other resources:

- The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a container that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing dynamic configuration into an existing application, providing standardized process introspection, and implementing a simple Git-driven PaaS. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, preferably through environment variables, a stable API, and documentation in image metadata and Dockerfiles.
- The ambassador pattern places a proxy between an application and the outside world. Ambassadors can route requests to storage shards, perform environment-specific service discovery, or split traffic between production and experimental services. They can be implemented beside applications or as shared routing services, with trade-offs involving deployment complexity, latency, and scaling.
- The adapter pattern converts heterogeneous application interfaces into standardized interfaces. Applications use adapters for monitoring, log normalization, and health checks, allowing shared tools to work consistently without modifying third-party or legacy containers. Separate adapters also provide reusable implementations and dedicated resource isolation.

Multi-node distributed systems use looser coupling and network communication. Microservices divide applications into independently developed and scaled components connected by formal APIs. This supports team autonomy, independent release schedules, and tailored scaling, but makes debugging, architecture, and coordination more difficult. Distributed patterns provide shared designs and reusable lessons that help manage these challenges.

A replicated load-balanced service consists of identical stateless instances behind a load balancer. Replication provides redundancy, fault tolerance, and horizontal scaling; at least two replicas are needed for high availability. Readiness probes distinguish running processes from instances prepared to serve traffic. Session tracking can route each user consistently to one replica using IP hashing, cookies, HTTP headers, or consistent hashing to minimize remapping during scaling. A replicated caching tier, such as Varnish, can reduce backend load and latency while also providing rate limiting. A replicated nginx tier can terminate SSL before traffic reaches the cache and application. These layers can be deployed in Kubernetes with Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and secrets.

Sharded services divide data among shards, each responsible for a subset of requests, with a routing root directing traffic appropriately. Sharding is commonly used for stateful data too large for one machine and enables scaling based on data size. Compared with replicated caches, sharded caches store unique data on each shard, improving memory utilization and hit rate. Cache failures or rollouts can increase latency and backend load, so systems should be tested with and without caching. Replicating each shard improves fault tolerance and permits safer rollouts and independent shard scaling. Sharded backends can be accessed through client-side ambassadors or shared routing services. Requests are mapped to shards through a sharding function, commonly based on hashing and modulo, which determines the appropriate destination for each request.

The speaker accepts the chief executive office, takes the constitutional oaths, and acknowledges that future history will determine whether he fulfills his pledges. He grounds the government in popular sovereignty, rejecting divine-right rule and affirming that governmental authority derives from an explicit grant by the governed. Individual citizens retain unalienable rights, including freedom of religion, speech, and participation in government. The Constitution has provided sufficient authority to preserve liberty, administer justice, and maintain union, but disputes over its meaning and the concentration of power in one branch threaten the system.

He identifies unlimited presidential tenure as a constitutional defect because prolonged power encourages corrupt ambition and renews his pledge never to serve a second term. He rejects any presidential role in legislative policymaking and describes the presidential veto as a conservative power to protect the Constitution, guard against hasty legislation, and defend minority rights. He believes repeated recognition of disputed constitutional interpretations by the political branches can establish settled meaning.

The expansion of executive patronage and presidential control over public officers and revenues could gradually give the government a monarchical character. He promises to keep the Treasury independent of executive control, require congressional notice before removing a treasury secretary, prevent federal officers from improperly influencing elections, and protect freedom of the press. He also opposes executive origination of revenue legislation, favors congressional control of public finances, and rejects an exclusively metallic currency as likely to deepen inequality and encourage usury.

Residents of the District of Columbia are free American citizens, not subjects of the states. Congress’s exclusive jurisdiction there should enable it to perform federal functions, while remaining legislation should reflect the residents’ circumstances and wishes.

The speaker urges mutual forbearance among the states and preservation of their reserved powers, warning that attempts by one state to control another would breed distrust, discord, and disunion. National institutions should remain effective only if citizens continually sustain the spirit of liberty, tolerance, and patriotism. Political parties may initially watch public officials, but become destructive when their factional violence supersedes the common interest; he calls for national unity rather than an executive party and pledges not to seek advance confidence in legislative measures.

In foreign relations, he intends to preserve peaceful intercourse, defend American rights and honor, and apply liberality and justice in dealings with aboriginal neighbors. He concludes by affirming Christian religion, religious liberty, sound morals, and individual responsibility as foundations of lasting national happiness.

Riverton Investment Corporation sued the United States for a tax refund concerning payments it made to management employees to repurchase stock. The IRS disallowed RIC’s deductions, characterizing the payments as nondeductible stock redemptions rather than compensation. RIC paid the assessed tax and sought a refund.

Under RIC’s Management Stockholder’s Agreement, managers could sell stock only to RIC or permitted family members, had to sell upon termination of employment, and could receive no more than 60% of the stock’s book value or less than their original purchase price. The central issue was whether RIC transferred the stock to the managers in the 1980s. Under Treasury Regulation 1.83-3, permanent, non-lapse restrictions must be considered when determining whether a transfer occurred.

The court found Paragraph 9 of the agreement ambiguous as to whether all restrictions lapse upon a liquidation, merger, acquisition, or reorganization. It therefore allowed parol evidence, which showed that the sale-timing restriction was temporary, while the restrictions on eligible purchasers and sale prices were permanent. These permanent restrictions prevented the managers from obtaining sufficient beneficial ownership interests for a taxable transfer to have occurred.

Accordingly, RIC’s 1990s payments were not stock redemptions and were deductible as compensation. The court rejected the magistrate judge’s recommendation, denied the United States’s summary-judgment and evidentiary motions, granted RIC’s summary-judgment motion, and entered judgment for RIC. The parties were directed to stipulate to appropriate damages and interest, or report their inability to agree, within 30 days.

The passage traces the evolution of software patterns from procedural programming to object-oriented programming and, later, distributed systems. Patterns provide shared terminology, reusable components, documented solutions, and lessons learned from others’ mistakes, helping teams design more reliable software. Open-source communities were central to developing and sharing the container technologies underlying modern distributed-system patterns.

It then introduces three single-node container patterns in which tightly coupled containers run together on one machine. The **sidecar pattern** augments an application with reusable functionality, such as HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, resource monitoring, or Git-based deployment. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation. The **ambassador pattern** brokers communication between an application and external services, supporting shard routing, service discovery, and request-splitting experiments. The **adapter pattern** transforms heterogeneous application interfaces into standardized interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks, allowing third-party containers to remain unchanged.

The passage then shifts to multi-node distributed systems and microservices. Formal APIs decouple teams, support independent scaling and releases, and improve agility, though they complicate debugging and architecture. Replicated load-balanced services provide redundancy and horizontal scalability for stateless workloads, with readiness probes, session tracking, caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services partition state across machines to handle data too large for one server; caching improves throughput and latency, while replicated shards add resilience to shard failures and deployments.

LeBron James enters his 23rd NBA season with the Lakers and an expiring contract, saying his contract status will not affect his performance and that he is not worried about his future. After exercising his $52.6 million player option, he remains focused on the Lakers’ championship goals, detailed preparation and daily accountability. The 40-year-old is recovering from a Grade 2 MCL sprain and lingering foot problems, is not yet at full condition and could be limited during training camp and the preseason. He is also focused on sustaining his body through an 82-game season. James said his retirement decision will not depend on whether his son Bryce reaches the NBA. He plans to monitor his motivation and physical condition and expects to retire if he falls out of love with the process of preparing for each season.

Facebook acquired the team behind London-based startup Bloomsbury AI through an “acquihire,” gaining its natural language processing talent rather than its product. Bloomsbury created Cape, an AI that reads documents and answers questions about them. The startup’s future remains unclear.

Patrick Cullen, 33, pleaded guilty to snatching a 21-year-old woman’s handbag in Limerick after approaching and pushing her from behind. Found nearby, he led gardaí to the discarded bag. Judge Tom O’Donnell imposed four years’ imprisonment, suspending the final 12 months, and backdated the sentence.

The court affirmed an injunction preventing execution against a married woman’s property for a judgment for family necessaries. Under the applicable statute, a wife’s property is not liable for such debts unless an execution against the husband has first been issued and returned unsatisfied. Because no judgment had been obtained against the husband, the statutory condition precedent was unmet, regardless of whether the underlying judgment established that the debt was for necessaries.

The study examines how digitalization affects online higher education quality and distinguishes digitization as converting analog information into digital formats, digitalization as incorporating digital tools into existing educational practices, and digital transformation as fundamentally redesigning educational models and systems. It identifies five criteria for evaluation: technological infrastructure, accessibility of digital resources, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and adaptability and innovation.

Using the spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP), nine education experts evaluated these criteria through pairwise comparisons. The methodology combines AHP with spherical fuzzy sets to address ambiguity in expert judgments, verifies matrix consistency using a 10% threshold, derives and defuzzifies criterion weights, and ranks their relative importance in Vietnam’s higher education context.

Pedagogical integration ranked first with 23.6%, followed by student engagement at 21.2%, accessibility of digital resources at 20.3%, adaptability and innovation at 18.4%, and technological infrastructure at 16.5%. The findings emphasize effective integration of teaching methods with technology rather than prioritizing either independently and give substantial importance to student engagement.

Recommended strategies include aligning curricula with technology-supported teaching, training educators in digital pedagogy, developing interactive and personalized learning experiences, building online learner communities, expanding equitable access to resources and infrastructure, supporting experimentation with emerging technologies, and investing in reliable technological systems. The authors note that reliance on expert evaluations may not represent all stakeholders and recommend future research incorporating broader perspectives and examining how pedagogical innovation affects the rankings.

After a strong start, the Mets struggled down the stretch, missed the playoffs and lost the final NL Wild Card spot, citing inconsistent starting pitching and bullpen failures. GM David Stearns criticized Kodai Senga’s two inconsistent seasons, acknowledged his potential and doubted he could make 30 starts next season.

Offensive linemen are a selfless, grueling unit whose five players create running lanes, protect the quarterback, and enable production by skill-position teammates. Their work requires communication, technique, strength, athleticism, and awareness while handling varied defensive fronts, blitzes, stunts, and pressures. The positions—center, guard, and tackle—have different physical requirements, with linemen generally estimated at 6'2"–6'8" and 300–340 pounds. Although often overlooked in success and quickly blamed in failure, a cohesive offensive line is crucial throughout a season. Notable players mentioned include Hall of Famers Jim Otto, John Hannah, and Anthony Muñoz.

SCDNR biologists caught and satellite-tagged “Harry-Etta,” a pregnant female tiger shark measuring 12 feet 2 inches and weighing 820 pounds, in St. Helena Sound. Her SPOT tag will transmit her location for about a year, helping researchers study tiger shark movements, lifespan, reproduction, migration, and gestation habitats. Ultrasound confirmed her pregnancy, making her the first known pregnant tiger shark among the 15 tagged by the team with satellite transmitters in South Carolina. SCDNR had previously encountered and conventionally tagged Harry-Etta in 2013 and 2015. Collaborative work with OCEARCH and other researchers has identified southern sounds as important tiger shark foraging areas and possible nursing grounds. Her real-time movements can be followed on the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker. The Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund sponsored the satellite tag and named her in honor of conservationist Harry R.E. Hampton.

A review by Concordia University researcher Sarah Sajedi of more than 140 studies estimates that people ingest 39,000–52,000 microplastic particles annually, with bottled-water drinkers consuming about 90,000 more than tap-water users. Particles from single-use water bottles arise during manufacturing, storage, transport and degradation and are ingested directly. Inside the body, they may enter the bloodstream and reach organs, potentially causing chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, hormonal disruption, impaired reproduction, neurological damage and cancer, though long-term effects remain poorly understood because testing and standardized detection methods are limited. Available measurement techniques have differing limitations, and advanced tools are often costly. Although governments are restricting plastic waste, most policies target bags, straws and packaging rather than water bottles. Sajedi considers emergency use acceptable but says daily consumption creates a chronic-toxicity concern, making education important.

President Martin Van Buren’s January 5, 1838 proclamation reports growing northern frontier unrest amid a civil war in Canada. Insurgents had obtained arms and supplies, organized a force including U.S. citizens at Navy Island, and continued receiving aid. Van Buren urged citizens to return home peacefully and warned that unlawful interference in the British Provinces would bring arrest and punishment, with no government assistance.

A University of Pennsylvania clinical trial randomly assigned 81 healthy adults to transcranial direct-current stimulation or a brief control pulse. The stimulated group reported lower intentions to commit physical assault (47 percent) and sexual assault (70 percent) than controls and judged both acts more morally wrong. Researchers targeted the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex because prior studies linked aggression and antisocial traits with reduced activity in that region, though causation was unclear. Experts cautioned that stated intentions may not predict actual violence and that behavioral effects remain unproven. The lead author suggested repeated sessions might change behavior, while another expert remained skeptical.

An elk hunter’s 2010 discovery in Montana’s Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge led to the identification of a new elasmosaur species that lived about 70 million years ago in an inland sea east of the Rocky Mountains. Published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, the nearly complete fossil represents a marine reptile with a roughly 7½-foot neck and about 40 vertebrae—far shorter than the as many as 76 vertebrae in other elasmosaurs. Researchers said its coexistence with long-necked elasmosaurs challenges the idea that neck length did not vary over millions of years. David Bradt reported the find after initially mistaking the bones for petrified wood; excavation took three days, followed by lengthy cleaning and study.

A webinar featuring the presidents of Middle States, SACSCOC, and WASC discussed credit transfer and possible uses of AI. MSCHE’s president urged accreditors to shift the burden of proof for accepting transfer credits from “no” to “yes,” but the webinar offered no concrete standards or enforceable requirements. Competition from alternative accreditors has weakened regional accreditors’ leverage, while institutional economics often drives credit-transfer decisions. AI could speed transcript assessment and allow transfer decisions alongside admission and financial-aid decisions, though hallucination risks remain. The author supports the direction but views the proposal as an intention rather than an actionable plan.

The lecture gives a compressed introduction to algebra with the goal of constructing and using finite fields in preparation for Reed–Solomon codes. It reviews integer factorization, Euclidean division, modular arithmetic, groups, and finite cyclic groups, noting that finite cyclic groups are isomorphic to \(Z_n\).

Subgroups are introduced as subsets that are themselves groups under the parent group’s operation. Examples in \(Z_{10}\) include \(\{0,5\}\), isomorphic to \(Z_2\), and the even residues \(\{0,2,4,6,8\}\), isomorphic to \(Z_5\). A coset is a translate of a subgroup; distinct cosets are either identical or disjoint, and all distinct cosets partition the group. Under coset addition, they form the quotient group \(G/H\). For integers, the cosets of \(nZ\) represent residue classes, and \(\mathbb Z/nZ\) is isomorphic to \(Z_n\). Lagrange’s theorem follows for finite groups: the size of a subgroup divides the size of the group.

A field is defined as a set with addition and multiplication such that the elements form an abelian group under addition, the nonzero elements form an abelian group under multiplication, and multiplication distributes over addition. These axioms provide additive and multiplicative identities, inverses, subtraction, division, and cancellation. The real, complex, and binary fields are used as examples.

For a prime \(p\), the residues modulo \(p\), denoted \(F_p\), form a field under modular addition and multiplication. Primality ensures that the nonzero residues are closed under multiplication and that multiplication by any nonzero element permutes them; this fails for nonprime moduli, as illustrated by \(2\cdot5\equiv0\pmod{10}\). Every finite field with a prime number of elements is isomorphic to \(F_p\). More generally, every finite field contains a prime subfield generated by repeated addition of \(1\). Its size \(p\) is the field’s characteristic, and \(p\beta=0\) for every field element \(\beta\). In characteristic two, addition and subtraction coincide.

The lecture then reviews polynomials over a field \(F[x]\). Polynomials are finite sums with field coefficients and an indeterminate \(x\). Addition is coefficientwise, multiplication is performed by expansion and collecting terms, and the degree of a nonzero product equals the sum of the degrees of its factors. The polynomial ring is an abelian group under addition and a commutative monoid under multiplication, but it is not a field. Its only invertible elements are nonzero constant polynomials, because a polynomial of positive degree cannot have a multiplicative inverse under the degree rule.

FRSC officer Soji was allegedly slapped by a security aide to Ebonyi State Governor David Umahi for delaying the governor’s convoy near Eagle Square, the PDP convention venue. Soji left after colleagues prevented him from fighting his attacker. FRSC spokesman Bisi Kazeem said no official report had been filed. Security personnel were also observed extorting money from unaccredited people seeking entry.

The seventh annual Julia’s Hope Cup and Carnival will be held Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland, featuring pond hockey, a children’s tournament, food, games and a silent auction. Created in memory of Paul Turner’s daughter Julia, who died of cancer in 2011, it supports The Hope Centre’s fight against homelessness. Last year’s event raised $20,000 and attracted about 1,000 people.

CBS’s drama *Doubt* premieres February 15 and follows the attorneys at Isaiah Roth and Associates, led by Elliot Gould’s Isaiah “The Legal Lion” Roth. The firm includes transgender lawyer Cameron Wirth, former prisoner Nick Brady, and Sadie Ellis, who represents accused murderer and pediatric surgeon Billy Brennan while struggling with personal feelings and professional duty.

Coach Sutter expected another close game and stressed finishing opportunities and not giving up more than one. He praised his team’s first period, while calling the opponent’s goal a marginal offensive-zone call on a harmless puck. He said pressure was on the home-team Devils, who had a hundred-plus points, and noted the series was four of seven, though the next agreement was unknown. He said first goals mattered and described the latest goal as a screened, soft right-side wrister.

Tesla’s 2021 Form 10-K describes a company focused on accelerating the transition to sustainable energy through electric vehicles, energy generation and storage products, and related services. The company operates two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Automotive products include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with Cybertruck, the new Tesla Roadster and Tesla Semi planned for additional consumer and commercial markets. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof.

Tesla develops proprietary battery, powertrain, control, infotainment and self-driving technologies, with vehicles updated regularly through over-the-air software updates. It sells directly through its website and company-owned stores and galleries, operates a global service network, and provides Supercharger, Destination Charging and residential charging infrastructure. It also offers vehicle financing and leasing, insurance, warranties, extended service plans, solar power-purchase agreements and paid in-app upgrades.

Manufacturing facilities include Fremont Factory in California, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York, Gigafactory Shanghai and, with production planned for 2022, Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas. The company sources thousands of parts from hundreds of global suppliers and is expanding localized production and procurement. Tesla reported 99,290 full-time employees worldwide as of December 31, 2021.

The risk factors identify dependence on demand for electric vehicles, intense competition, COVID-19 and macroeconomic disruption, semiconductor and other supply shortages, difficulties scaling factories and production, battery-cell availability and raw-material costs, international regulatory and operating conditions, product defects and liability, and financial risks associated with leasing and residual values. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties and that actual results may differ materially.

Jersey defended well after taking the lead but generated insufficient offense. The team plans to focus on road execution and its successful power play, while finding a solution with Peter unavailable.

Carli Lloyd injured her ankle in the 28th minute of a Dash match against FC Kansas City. X-rays were negative, and she tweeted she is down but not out. The Dash haven't said how many games she'll miss.
Two teens were arrested after a high-speed chase across East Tennessee in a van stolen from a children’s home. The chase ended in a collision near Chickamauga Dam without serious injuries.

The OS can bind a driver to the ACPI-defined TMPM device using HID AMDI0095. A page-migration driver must enable PAGEMIGRATION_EN in IOMMU_MMIO_CNTRL_1 for all IOMMUs once; repeating this is harmless. TMPM uses mailbox registers and a ring buffer for parallel command execution. Firmware controls the Read pointer, software controls the Write pointer, and command order is not guaranteed. Completion occurs when the Read pointer advances past the command or the PM_Status TOGGLE bit changes.

President Ram Nath Kovind, in his first speech since taking office, marked 70 years of independence and urged citizens to help build a “New India” by 2022. He called for cleanliness, an end to open defecation, support for women and girls, compliance with laws, acceptance of GST, pride in paying taxes, better infrastructure and housing, education for underprivileged children, and selflessness inspired by freedom fighters and border soldiers.

Cirque du Soleil will donate $1 million in cash and tickets to support Las Vegas shooting victims’ families and first responders. Half the money will go to victims’ families, while 5,000 tickets for police officers, firefighters and paramedics will provide $500,000 in value. The company also plans a benefit show and reported that all 1,500 local employees were unharmed.

Former Southport MP John Pugh warned that Sefton Council’s approval of a 60,000 sq ft Sainsbury’s at Meols Cop, replacing Homebase, could cause further job losses and hollow out Lord Street despite creating 400 jobs. He urged the council to prepare a fallback plan for town-centre retailers.

GoDaddy gave The Daily Stormer 24 hours to transfer its domain, citing terms-of-service violations over an article denigrating Heather Heyer, who was killed at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville.

Lexus priced the 2017 LC500 V8 and LC500h hybrid equally in the UK at £76,595, with over a third destined for the UK pre-ordered. The V8 produces 467hp versus 354hp for the hybrid; both reach 60mph in under five seconds. Sport and Sport+ packages add equipment.

Zoë Schiffer and WIRED senior politics editor Leah Feiger recap five stories. Rutgers professor Mark Bray, whose 2017 book on antifa led to allegations that he funded antifa, says death threats are driving him and his family to leave for Europe; after checking in and passing security, United Airlines canceled their reservation, though the reason remains unclear.

ICE is reportedly seeking vendors for a multiyear, around-the-clock social-media surveillance program, including about 30 analysts reviewing Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and other platforms to support immigration arrests and deportation raids. Draft documents contemplate AI and tight processing deadlines. A Harvard study also found that simulated users ending conversations with five AI companion apps encountered emotional manipulation 37% of the time, including guilt, discouragement, and simulated physical coercion. Separately, the FDA’s announcement of leucovorin calcium tablets as a possible treatment for autism symptoms—described by the Trump administration but not scientifically proven—has fueled speculation, misinformation, and anti-vaccine discussion in a Facebook group.

Finally, OpenAI’s disclosure of internal tools such as DocuGPT, an AI sales assistant, and a customer-support agent triggered declines in DocuSign, HubSpot, and Salesforce stocks, while an OpenAI mention of Figma lifted its shares. The hosts also considered whether AI is in a bubble, contrasting projected 2026–27 data-center infrastructure spending of $500 billion with roughly $12 billion in consumer spending and noting GPUs’ roughly three-year lifespan.

Research involving more than 24,000 Slimming World members found that those with ambitious weight-loss targets shed an average of 19% of their body weight over 12 months, compared with 11% among those targeting less than 10%. Experts called for guidance encouraging people to pursue their “dream weight” with ongoing support. Participants attended weekly group sessions, and members who set personal targets were 10 times more likely to succeed. One participant lost 8st 6lbs after setting her desired target.

WIRED tested suitcases, backpacks, and personal-item bags for air travel, evaluating size, weight, materials, durability, wheels, handles, straps, pockets, and zippers. Highlights include the Travelpro Platinum Elite as a stylish, expandable favorite; the durable, feature-rich Travelpro Maxlite 5 for travelers spending $100–$150; the innovative but expensive Peak Design Roller Pro; and the exceptionally rugged Rimowa. Other praised options include Antler, Briggs & Riley, Yeti, State, Beis, Tom Bihn, Six Moon Designs, Aer, and Amazon Basics carry-ons and backpacks, each offering features suited to different budgets, trip lengths, and packing needs.

The guide emphasizes checking airline dimensions with a tape measure, noting that rules vary by carrier. It also advises considering hardware and warranty more than shell material: softshells are flexible and expandable but can be permeable and easier to slash, while hardshells are generally lighter but less adaptable. For TSA liquid screening, it explains the 3-1-1 rule: containers no larger than 3.4 ounces must fit in one clear, quart-sized bag per passenger.

Colorado’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board made the first-in-the-nation move to cap payments for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel. The $600-per-unit limit applies to government agencies and commercial health plans covering state residents, equaling about $30,350 annually per person versus roughly $53,000 paid by the average state insurance plan in 2023. The vote may encourage other states to pursue similar prescription-drug spending controls.

The long snapper is a specialized NFL position requiring quick, accurate, and consistent snaps. For extra points and field goals, the snap travels about seven yards to a kneeling holder; for punts, it travels roughly 15 yards to a punter who typically takes three steps before kicking. The snap must reach the target cleanly to allow efficient catches, kick preparation, protection, and punting.

Long snappers must also cover punts, pursue downfield, and occasionally make tackles, requiring athleticism, toughness, balance, and physicality. They are generally 6'1"–6'3", weigh 230–250 pounds, and have a thick, linebacker-like build. Although their work rarely appears in statistics, errors can cause missed field goals or blocked punts. The passage notes that teams blocking a punt win about 90% of the time, increasing the pressure to fill the position well.

Notable long snappers include Zak DeOssie, who played for the New York Giants from 2007–2019 and earned two Super Bowl and two Pro Bowl selections, and Don Mulbach, whose 2004–2020 tenure with the Detroit Lions placed him second in franchise history for games played. He also earned two Pro Bowl selections.

The October 5, 2000 “Inside UT Football” column previewed Texas’ matchup with Oklahoma. Chip Brown reported that Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops emphasized the Sooners’ 4–0 start, improved conditioning, running game and need to reverse a three-game losing streak against Texas. Brown predicted a 24–20 Texas victory, saying the offenses were evenly matched but Texas had the better defense; turnovers could determine the outcome. He viewed Oklahoma’s receivers against Texas’ young secondary as the game’s key matchup.

Brown expected Major Applewhite to start against Oklahoma and play most or all of the game, while Chris Simms was expected to return against Missouri on October 21. Coaches were likely to continue describing both quarterbacks as starters and rotate them against weaker opponents. Applewhite’s performance against Oklahoma State had restored his confidence, but Brown questioned whether a rotation would allow him to build national award consideration.

Other updates included uncertainty about Sean Rogers’ sprained ankle, consideration of redshirting defensive end Adam Doiron, and praise for the offensive line’s gap-blocking scheme against Oklahoma State. Texas’ punt protection was criticized for giving blockers too much room. Brown also discussed possible Royal–Memorial Stadium expansion, the team’s 231-game scoring streak, Texas’ improving schedule and the likelihood of becoming a powerhouse within two or three years as players gained experience.

Brown defended coach Mack Brown amid negative media attention and advised patience with offensive-line coach Tim Nunez. He attributed renewed criticism to inflated expectations following Texas’ 1998 season and 1999 victory over Nebraska. Other topics included limited use of the shotgun, the dry field, David Aaron leaving football for track, Houston’s next season game at Robertson Stadium, freshman punt-return prospects, and the October 14 Colorado game, scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Central but not televised.

Shuckers opening-series attendance rose 21%, with 2,500 more fans than last year. A Jackie Robinson Day game drew a record 4,006 fans, and Johnny Davis’s home-run-robbing catch became SportsCenter’s top play, earning 767,000 Instagram views.

The study developed the 15-item, approximately 10-minute Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA) to measure three language-comprehension phenotypes in young children: Command, Modifier, and Syntactic. The LPA uses toys and brief instructions, with three command, five modifier, and seven syntactic items; each item requires at least three correct responses out of four. A parallel parent-reported Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC) was also created.

The LPA was administered to 116 neurotypical children aged 1.5–7 years and to 79 children with autism aged 2–8 years. Neurotypical children’s median acquisition ages were 1.6 years for Command, 3.0 years for Modifier, and 3.7 years for Syntactic comprehension; all children attained these phenotypes by ages 3, 4, and 5, respectively. Parent reports yielded corresponding ages of 1.6, 2.7, and 3.0 years. LPA and LPEC scores correlated strongly (r = 0.78). The LPA demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92), test-retest reliability (r = 0.96), and inter-observer agreement (κ = 0.97); corresponding LPEC reliability was also strong.

Compared with neurotypical peers, autistic children showed lower rates of attaining the Command, Modifier, and Syntactic phenotypes. At age five and older, 39% of autistic children reached the Syntactic phenotype on the LPA, versus all neurotypical children; the LPEC result for autistic children was 45%. Neurotypical children aged four and older generally understood canonical and noncanonical word orders similarly, whereas autistic children more often relied on learned canonical-order routines.

The findings indicate that the LPA and LPEC may help identify language-comprehension deficits early and monitor syntactic-language development, including in minimally verbal children. The use of physical manipulatives improves attention but is less convenient to store and transport. The manuscript is a medRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed.

Shelley Corman forwarded Ricki Winters the October 17, 2001 PAKK Digest No. 529 and asked to add the sender to her contacts. The digest’s 24 messages focused on adopting children from Kazakhstan. Topics included uncertain HIV-testing requirements for Russian and Kazakh visas, accommodations with host families, apartments, or hotels, and discounted Delta adoption airfares through Travel-On. Members shared experiences and advice about travel to and adoption in Taraz, including flights, trains, lodging, and orphanage visits. Other discussions introduced new members, addressed children’s tantrums, self-abusive behavior, guilt, and parenting approaches, and explained how to remove mistakenly posted messages. A lengthy exchange considered whether to change adopted children’s birth dates for school placement and social adjustment. Parents described legally changing ages, holding children back without altering records, or retaining birth dates as part of the child’s identity, noting that procedures varied by country and U.S. jurisdiction.

Negotiators admitted abolishing line dancing may be necessary to form a working administration with the DUP, which considers it sinful and unsuitable. David Davis defended the compromise as the only realistic option, while Nigel Walker welcomed ending line dancing as the price of Brexit.

The Trump administration’s nuclear posture review largely continues Obama-era modernization plans without a net increase in strategic nuclear weapons, but adopts a more aggressive stance toward Russia, warning of “unacceptably dire costs” for even a limited nuclear attack in Europe. It calls North Korea a “clear and grave threat,” says a nuclear attack would end its regime, and presents China as a potential nuclear adversary.

The review supports existing arms-control agreements, including New START, which limits the U.S. and Russia to 1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 launchers. It would equip a small number of Trident missiles with lower-yield warheads and later develop a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. The administration also emphasizes deterring major nonnuclear attacks. Arms-control groups criticized the review as reckless and said it blurs the boundary between nuclear and conventional warfare. A Pentagon official said Russia would likely oppose the new weapons proposals.

This patent application, a continuation of U.S. Pat. No. 11,904,468 (which continues U.S. Pat. No. 11,345,029, claiming priority to provisional application 62/889,562 filed Aug. 21, 2019), is directed to robotic systems and, more specifically, to robotic multi-gripper assemblies configured to selectively grip and hold objects. The background notes that robots used in manufacturing, packaging, transport and shipping often lack the sensitivity and adaptability to selectively grip individual objects from adjacent or irregularly shaped items.

The described systems and methods relate to gripping selected objects using a transport robot with multi-gripper assemblies that can be operated independently or together to grip one or many objects simultaneously or sequentially, with object selection based on factors such as gripper carrying capability, available space, transport paths, and transport plans. Multi-gripper assemblies include addressable vacuum regions or banks of suction elements that independently draw in air, allowing only selected objects to be held even when other gripping portions contact neighboring packages. Target objects are identified from captured image data, gripped via the selected vacuum regions, transported by the robotic arm, and released together or sequentially.

In illustrative environments, the robotic system includes unloading, transfer, transport and loading units (e.g., devanning and palletizing robots) that move packages between trucks, conveyors, containers and storage locations, together with optional de-palletizing, container-switching, packaging, sorting and piece-picking units. A controller containing processors, storage, communication and input/output devices analyzes image data from cameras, lidar and radar imaging systems, vision sensor devices, and contact/force sensors to generate transport, pickup and stacking plans. Master data and a registration data store hold object attributes (dimensions, shape, weight, color, barcodes, center of mass), object tracking data, and vacuum gripper data, and can be updated automatically to register unknown packages.

The end effector includes a mounting bracket, a force detector assembly (such as a six-axis force/torque sensor), a manifold assembly fluidically coupled to a vacuum source, and grippers with suction elements, bellowed configurations, compressible foam sealing members, valves and vacuum-level sensors. Vision sensor devices positioned below the horizontal plane of the gripping interface provide an unobscured field of view for real-time monitoring, object counting, collision avoidance, and grip verification.

Operational flows describe receiving image data of a pickup environment, identifying and prioritizing target objects, selecting vacuum regions, generating pickup and transport commands, executing a calculated motion plan, and monitoring the established grip against initial and transfer thresholds. If a grip is insufficient, the system can regrip the package up to an iteration limit, otherwise solicit operator input or cancel the plan with an error status.

The Fraser Institute will release a February 16 study examining whether British Columbia’s carbon tax revenue is offset by tax reductions and how much the government collects, revisiting a revenue-neutrality pledge made in 2008.

A national EducationNext poll found that support for charter schools fell from 51% to 39% in one year, while support rose slightly for universal vouchers, at 45%, and tax-credit scholarships, at 55%. Charter support declined across party and racial groups, with no clear explanation, though opposition to new charter expansion may be relevant.

Views are increasingly partisan: 62% of Republicans and 50% of Democrats support vouchers, reversing last year’s pattern. Trump’s endorsement boosts Republican support but reduces Democratic support, though his overall influence was nearly nil. Approval of local public schools remains bipartisan, with 55% of Republicans and 54% of Democrats rating them A or B.

The lecture distinguishes pointwise convergence, where \(f_n(x)\to f(x)\) for each fixed \(x\), from uniform convergence, where for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is an \(M\), independent of \(x\), such that \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\varepsilon\) for all \(n\ge M\) and all \(x\). Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

For \(f_n(x)=x^n\) on \([0,1]\), the pointwise limit is \(f(x)=0\) for \(x<1\) and \(f(1)=1\). The convergence is uniform on every interval \([0,b]\) with \(b<1\), but not on \([0,1]\). A sequence of increasingly tall tent functions converges pointwise to zero but not uniformly.

The lecture frames three questions about interchanging limiting processes: whether a pointwise or uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous; whether convergence of differentiable functions and their derivatives implies differentiability of the limit; and whether limits and integrals may be interchanged. Pointwise convergence alone is insufficient for all three. Counterexamples include \(x^n\), whose limit is discontinuous; \(x^n/n\), whose derivatives converge pointwise but not to the derivative of the limit; and the tent functions, whose integrals remain \(1\) although their pointwise limit is zero.

Under uniform convergence, the corresponding theorems hold: the uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous; the integral of the uniform limit equals the limit of the integrals; and if continuously differentiable functions and their derivatives converge uniformly, the limit is continuously differentiable and its derivative is the uniform limit of the derivatives.

Finally, the Weierstrass \(M\)-test states that if \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) for all \(x\in S\) and \(\sum M_j\) converges, then \(\sum f_j(x)\) converges absolutely at each \(x\), and its partial sums converge uniformly on \(S\). This provides many uniformly convergent series of functions, including series used to construct continuous nowhere-differentiable functions.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya from Myanmar recognized as a refugee by the UNHCR, recounts four years in Manus prison in Papua New Guinea after arriving in October 2013 at age 19. He describes overcrowded Delta and Mike compounds, cramped metal shipping containers, extreme heat, long queues, inadequate sanitation, shortages, food insecurity and conflict over limited television access. Although food and fruit were discarded, detainees were forbidden from taking fruit outside the dining area. Phone calls were restricted, and later internet access was too slow for effective communication. Mohammad avoided other detainees, ate late to bypass queues, and focused on lessons and writing, adopting “the pen is mightier than the sword” as a motto. He describes hunger, despair, crying and thoughts of suicide but says he maintained hope and found strength to continue. After four birthdays in detention, he wishes to be free and reunited with his family.

The De’Longhi Rivelia automates milk-based drinks such as lattes and flat whites through a touchscreen. Its swappable hopper accommodates two bean types, while the “bean adapt” function adjusts settings and brews a test cup. The built-in frother produces silky micro-foam, though it is less hot than a traditional steam wand. Discounted to $1,300, the machine offers easier preparation than manual portafilter brewing but may not match its coffee quality.

Historically, total solar eclipses have often provoked fear and religious interpretation: Greeks saw divine anger, Vikings an apocalypse, and ancient Chinese a dragon consuming the sun. During the predictable 1878 eclipse, many Americans were terrified, and one man killed his son and himself while fleeing what he believed was Judgment Day. Although astronomers reject an eclipse at Jesus’s crucifixion, some Christians feared the upcoming August 21 eclipse signaled the end of days. In Islamic tradition, eclipses are signs of God rather than events associated with a human life or death. Author David Baron says that, even for secular observers, a total eclipse can inspire awe, a sense of human smallness, and a profound experience resembling religion.

The Triangle (1-3-1) offense attacks Diamond & One by isolating the Star at the high post against a chaser focused mainly on pass denial and often unprepared for post defense. The Star can drive in either direction for drop-pass layups, kick out for open shots or dribble penetration, or use post-flash action as teammates rotate into two-guard-front or 2-1-2 alignments and flare for spot-ups. If the defense overplays the entry, the Star can release to the basket for a lob; otherwise, O4 flashes into the middle to shoot or pass while O1 and O3 flare on the wings. Success requires coordinated execution, communication, timing, experience, and preparation in isolations, back cuts, interior passing, and spot-ups. Teams should scout opponents when possible, recognize defensive adjustments, vary entries and alignments, and attack weaker defenders.

A funnel-web spider, described as the world’s most venomous spider, was found in a Springwood, NSW home near Sydney. The spider was about 5 cm in diameter. Funnel-webs occur along Australia’s east coast, from Queensland to NSW, and a newly discovered species reaches northern Tasmania. They have large fangs capable of piercing fingernails and are often found in cool, damp places around homes, including pools, bathrooms and laundries.

Their venom can cause rapid nervous-system shutdown, with symptoms including nausea, muscle cramps, profuse sweating and numbness around the mouth. The Australian Museum has recorded 13 deaths in Australia, though none have occurred since an antivenene was developed in 1981. A Taronga Zoo keeper said funnel-webs are generally defensive rather than aggressive and advised anyone bitten to seek hospital care immediately. He urged people not to handle them, wear gloves while gardening, avoid putting hands into pool filters and leave them alone because they help control insects such as cockroaches, flies and mosquitoes.

The speaker pledges to faithfully discharge his duties, guided by the Constitution and its aims of forming a more perfect union, establishing justice, ensuring domestic tranquillity, providing for common defense, promoting general welfare, and securing liberty. He credits the Constitution with supporting national growth, expanded territory and population, new states, international commerce and treaties, and the advancement of liberty and law, while acknowledging disease, foreign conflict, and sectional dissension as continuing challenges.

He affirms popular sovereignty, regular elections, limited state and federal powers, military preparedness and civilian control, fiscal accountability, freedom of the press and religion, peace, and union. Although earlier European wars intensified party divisions, a decade of domestic and international peace had reduced political animosity. He urges citizens to transcend party prejudice and recognize talent and virtue regardless of affiliation. He also presents the federal structure as balancing state authority with national power, while national representation and social ties promote mutual respect and cohesion.

Reviewing his predecessor’s administration, the speaker highlights peace, debt reduction, tax repeal, military reform, veteran relief, expanded territory, recognition of southern nations’ independence, coastal defenses, suppression of the slave trade, exploration, surveys, and internal improvements. He pledges to continue these policies, especially public works such as roads and aqueducts, arguing that their benefits will extend to future generations and that remaining constitutional objections may be resolved through deliberate discussion. Aware that he initially enjoys less public confidence than his predecessors, he vows devoted service and seeks support from the legislature, executive departments, state governments, and the people, while entrusting the nation’s future to providence.

KGI’s Ming-Chi Kuo said Apple’s second-half 2017 Apple Watch would retain its current form factor, contradicting an earlier report of a new design. The watch would remain available in 38mm and 42mm sizes, with LTE and non-LTE versions. The article notes that a major redesign would be difficult because the interface and functionality depend on the existing shape, though thickness could change. It speculates that LTE could enable a smaller battery and thinner watch or improved battery life, favoring the thinner design.

A recent music-education graduate with hearing problems lives at home with his unemployed mother and feels pressured to pay $480 monthly in rent and phone costs. Facing $1,700 in tuition, about $600 in certification fees, and future car and housing expenses, he plans to earn $1,600 monthly at a three-month minimum-wage job. He reports that his mother previously collected $3,000 from a $5,000 school refund and asks how to manage the conflict without damaging their relationship.

The response advises budgeting and saving any surplus, considering additional work, taking time to explore alternative experiences, and being honest about his own role in their disputes. It also questions the mother’s conduct, suggesting professional help if her behavior is as described, and asks what she would say about the problems between them.

President James Madison’s proclamation of September 1, 1814, condemned the British invasion and destruction of public buildings in Washington, the threatened burning and plunder of Alexandria, and declared plans to devastate coastal towns as violations of humanity and civilized warfare. Rejecting the British justification of retaliation for destruction in Upper Canada, Madison warned of prolonged barbarism and urged Americans to unite in expelling the invader. He directed civil and military officers to defend the country and authorized district commanders to summon nearby militia for threatened areas.
Despite a second-period recovery, the team lost after surrendering two-goal leads and allowing too many chances late. Detroit battled hard, but the team remained committed to rebounding.

A May 9, 2001 compilation of press clippings covered Enron-related news, financial markets and other business developments. Questia Media, an online college library and research service backed by Enron Chairman Ken Lay, laid off 139 employees, reducing its workforce from about 280 to 140 as it slowed book digitization because of fundraising difficulties. Despite the cuts, paying subscribers reportedly exceeded 5,000, and Questia projected positive cash flow in about 18 months.

U.S. markets closed mixed ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting. The Dow fell 51.66 points to 10,883.51, while the Nasdaq gained 25.20 points to 2,198.77. First-quarter worker productivity declined 0.1%, contributing to higher long-term Treasury yields. Cisco reported a large net loss, while energy stocks weakened; Enron fell $1.93 to $56.11.

Enron said Japan’s newly deregulated power market lacked effective competition because of regulations, high transmission-network costs and unclear transmission fees. New entrants represented only 0.2% of the market. Enron called for an independent regulator, arguing that the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry might be unable to act impartially because of its ties to incumbent utilities; it said increased market liquidity, rather than destroying utilities, was the goal.

Williams planned to open a 25-person European operation in London to trade gas and power in the UK, Germany, Scandinavia and Benelux, emphasizing structured transactions, risk management and tolling deals rather than buying physical assets. It was also targeting risk-management contracts in Spain and Italy and later considered trading crude oil and refined products.

Reports in India said families of Enron executives overseeing the Dabhol power project were relocating from Mumbai amid uncertainty over the nearly complete $2.9 billion project. Enron declined to confirm whether the moves were corporate or personal. MSEB denied that it had underutilized its own capacity to justify buying Dabhol power, saying DPC electricity was needed to maintain grid frequency. It also said more power from the idle Uran plant was uneconomic because of insufficient natural gas and high furnace-oil costs, while denying federal pressure to continue the Enron agreement.

MSEB appointed a former Bombay High Court judge as arbitrator in the dispute with DPC; the arbitration was expected to occur in London. The Swadeshi Jagran Manch demanded a judicial probe, alleging inflated power-demand figures, and continued to call for cancellation of the deal. Meanwhile, lenders were prepared to support termination of the power purchase agreement unless the central and state governments resolved the crisis before a May 15 deadline. DPC’s board had authorized the termination notice by a 7–1 vote.

Prize Petroleum also sought to acquire Enron’s 30% interest in the Panna, Mukta and Tapti offshore fields, valuing it at about Rs 600 crore. Prize Petroleum planned to invest Rs 1,900 crore, including Rs 1,300 crore in debt.

In a MOST-framework optimization trial, 97 children aged 9–12 with insufficient sleep received a 7-week mobile health intervention after a 2-week run-in, followed by a 2-week follow-up. All participants received sleep tracking and weekly feedback, while a factorial design tested guideline-based versus personalized sleep goals, child- and caregiver-directed loss-framed incentives, screen-time reduction messaging, and daily-routine messaging. Baseline weeknight sleep averaged 7.7 hours; overall increases were 24 minutes during intervention and 21 minutes at follow-up. No single component met the prespecified target of at least 30 additional minutes. Two combinations did: the core intervention plus a caregiver-directed incentive, screen-time messaging, and routine messaging increased sleep by 39.6 minutes during intervention and 33.2 minutes at follow-up; omitting screen-time messaging yielded increases of 32.0 and 26.6 minutes. Either sleep goal performed equally in these combinations. The results support including sleep tracking, feedback, a sleep goal, caregiver-directed loss-framed incentives, and routine messaging, with screen-time messaging offering added benefit. An evaluation-phase randomized trial is planned. Limitations include a single-site, predominantly non-Hispanic White sample, less tracker data from Black participants, short follow-up, and limitations of the commercial sleep tracker.

The speaker described a tight hockey game in which several defensive plays and board bounces helped the opponents score. His team generated good chances but failed to convert a few, while the opposing team executed and took a one-goal lead. After the game, he struck an opponent who continued talking, hitting him twice-handed on the foot. He also recounted an unusual puck that rolled onto Osgood’s back and remained there as someone covered it, though it did not count as a goal and he was unsure whether it warranted a penalty shot. Despite mistakes by both teams, his side had chances in the second and third periods and remained competitive. He expected a tough series, trusted his team’s approach, and said the short turnaround would help them prepare for the next game.

At least 30 children died at Gorakhpur’s BRD Hospital, which accommodated patients ten times its admission capacity, raising concerns about overcrowding, shared infant warmers, and oxygen supply. Nearby Special Newborn Care Units were absent or nonfunctional, while ministers announced an Rs 85 crore regional medical centre for children’s disease research.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is forecast to grow about 4.5% CAGR, driven by packaging innovation, emerging economies, rising purchasing power, and pharmaceutical and cosmetic demand. Aluminum packaging is protective, waste-reducing, corrosion-resistant, hygienic, chemically neutral, and non-toxic. Deficient recycling processes may impede growth. Asia Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region.

The paper proposes a new semantics for deontic argumentation that supports weak permission in unresolved conflicts between obligations. It defines a Deontic Argumentation Theory as facts and rules yielding arguments with deontic conclusions for obligation, strong permission, or weak permission. Weak permission is treated as the absence of a justified contrary obligation, represented by “imaginary” arguments, while other arguments are “natural.” Attack relations capture opposition between literals and deontic conclusions.

Under existing grounded and stable Dung semantics, theories containing applicable rules that justify both an obligation and its opposite cannot justify either weak permission, so the conflicted literal is not weakly facultative. The new wp-semantics extends Defeasible Logic by distinguishing support from undercut and defining when natural and imaginary arguments are wp-acceptable or wp-rejected. Its fixed-point extension pairs the sets of justified and rejected arguments.

The paper proves that every wp-extension is unique, conflict-free, and contains no argument that is both justified and rejected. It also shows that wp-semantics extends grounded semantics and can justify both weak permissions for a conflicted literal when the relevant conflicting arguments have justified proper subarguments. Consequently, such literals become weakly facultative. In the paper’s legal example, conflicting obligations are rejected, both corresponding weak permissions are justified, and a consequent obligation based on those permissions becomes justified.

The discussion argues that unresolved conflicting obligations within one legal system should not be resolved retroactively or arbitrarily; rejecting both obligations avoids sanctioning a subject regardless of conduct, while failure to justify an obligation expresses weak permission. The semantics also distinguishes weak from strong permission in drafting legal provisions. Related approaches generally either omit weak permission or rely on semantics unable to handle unresolved conflicts; Defeasible Deontic Logic is identified as the closest framework, with characterizing it left for future work.

MyWorld lets players create games in any genre and mode, controlling objects, settings, rules, and single-player, PvP, or cooperative options. Design and constructor modes support creating functional turrets, sensors, and robots. Players can store or share creations, unlock materials through leveling, and customize avatars. Still in development, MyWorld launched a Kickstarter campaign offering early backers exclusive materials.

At Tesla’s 2021 Annual Meeting on October 7, stockholders elected James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk as Class II directors for three-year terms. Proposals to reduce director terms to two years and eliminate supermajority voting requirements were not approved. Stockholders ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla’s independent auditor for fiscal 2021. Advisory proposals to reduce director terms to one year and expand diversity and inclusion reporting were approved, while proposals concerning employee arbitration reporting, human capital oversight, and human rights reporting were rejected.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reported that Senior Vice President, Retail Angela Ahrendts would depart effective April 15, 2019. She was succeeded by Deirdre O’Brien as Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019.

The NTSC and Cloud Security Alliance will promote the CSA STAR registry and related tools to standardize cloud vendor security reviews. They plan to develop a STAR-based questionnaire aligned with common compliance frameworks and publish a joint whitepaper for CISOs and vendors. The organizations will also share events, working groups, and cloud-security research to streamline evaluations, encourage best practices, and improve cloud security.

Successful Forex trading requires understanding market realities rather than believing it is easy, offers quick profits, or demands exceptional talent. Traders should make independent decisions, wait for suitable profitable setups, and develop mental stability to accept losses without taking excessive risks. Profitability depends on mastering technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis. Traders may learn from experts and others, but should not blindly copy them; they should build their own style and judgment, take gradual steps, and critically evaluate advice.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 to offer modest women attractive, concealing swimwear. Customer research revealed demand from women recovering from mastectomies or bariatric surgery and those with skin cancer or psoriasis, prompting built-in mastectomy bras, compression wear, and skin-protective suits. Women with special health needs became a business cornerstone, and Teutsch says some customers felt newly empowered to be active.

As the Supreme Court’s new term begins, legal experts anticipate frequent higher-education disputes, though only *West Virginia v. B.P.J.* and *Little v. Hecox* appear on the main docket. Both address whether state bans on transgender athletes violate Title IX. Hecox’s lawyers have asked the court to dismiss her case as moot because of illness, her father’s death, public scrutiny, and her wish to stop participating; *B.P.J.* is expected to proceed. The ruling’s wording could affect protections involving bathrooms, locker rooms and other university activities.

Experts are also monitoring the increasingly used shadow docket, historically reserved for emergencies. It can produce rulings within weeks or days without normal briefing, oral argument or written explanations, leaving institutions little time to prepare and creating uncertainty. Potential disputes include federal funding, staffing, visas, First Amendment and academic-freedom protections, and transgender identification, including *Trump v. Orr*.

Experts warn that emergency stays can allow administration policies to take effect before full merits review. They say the Supreme Court has invalidated lower-court injunctions in every higher-education case that reached the shadow docket, potentially leaving institutions unable to recover even if later rulings favor them.

Riley Oil Company, one of the area’s last full-service stations in Paoli, Indiana, has operated since 1971, when Glendon Riley opened it. Six family members work there, providing free gas pumping, windshield washing and oil checks. Owners Jo Ann and Jeff Riley say the family-run business offers personalized service and is expected to continue for generations.

Police say a 52-year-old woman threatened Taco Bell employees with a tire iron, damaged registers and windows, ignored an officer’s orders, and was tased. She was hospitalized for cuts and jailed on robbery, malicious injury, and property-destruction charges.

Consumer Electricals Ltd submitted a September 20, 2017 expression of interest for Kenstar’s business and brand after a September 6 invitation from Videocon Industries and affiliates. The bid price was undisclosed; results were pending, with no binding documents or negotiations. Videocon, owing over ₹40,000 crore, was considering asset sales.

Microsoft Corporation updated guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022 due to unfavorable foreign exchange rate movements through May. It furnished revised guidance in Exhibit 99.1 and cautioned that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties.

Molecular-dynamics simulations coupled with orientation-resolved Schmid-factor mapping examined the temperature-dependent nanoindentation response of single-crystalline α-titanium oriented along [0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110] at 10, 300, and 600 K. Simulations used an EAM potential and a spherical indenter, with load–displacement, contact-pressure, dislocation, shear-strain, strain-tensor, and surface-morphology analyses.

All orientations initially showed Hertzian elastic behavior followed by plastic pop-in, most pronounced for [0001]. Contact pressure generally decreased with increasing temperature once deformation became bulk dominated. Basal a-type dislocations dominated plasticity, while pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ slip became more active at higher temperatures. Increasing temperature enhanced atomic and dislocation mobility, broadened shear-strain zones, and promoted recovery, although the extent depended on orientation.

The [0001] orientation primarily activated basal and prismatic slip, with occasional pyramidal activity. It developed localized deformation and a circular pile-up at low temperature, a pronounced quasi-hexagonal pattern at 300 K, and diffuse surface features at 600 K. Local HCP-to-BCC transformation was most favored at low temperature, and a basal a-type dislocation dissociated into Shockley partials at 300 K.

For [10̅10], prismatic and basal slip predominated. At 300 K, expanding prismatic segments formed closed “lasso” loops around the stressed region, producing a symmetric two-lobe pile-up. For [2̅110], basal, prismatic, and pyramidal systems contributed to closed-loop formation and asymmetric, curved pile-up features.

Dislocation density was consistently highest for [0001]: 0.86, 1.09, and 1.52 × 10¹⁶ m⁻² at 10, 300, and 600 K, respectively. Densities decreased with temperature for [10̅10] (0.45 to 0.38) and [2̅110] (0.41 to 0.12), consistent with enhanced annihilation and recovery. The simulated surface morphologies agreed closely with AFM observations, demonstrating that temperature and crystallographic orientation jointly control titanium’s indentation-induced plasticity.

High-seas fishing in areas without regional management organizations is largely unregulated, with limited data on vessels, catches, species, and sizes. In the Southwest Atlantic, over 250 jiggers and trawlers annually take hundreds of thousands of tons of marine resources, complicating stock assessments and increasing overfishing risk. Foreign jumbo squid fishing vessels in the Eastern Pacific have risen to nearly 300, raising regional management concerns. A September 2017 IMARPE workshop in Lima, attended by Falkland Islands scientist Alexander Arkhipkin, produced recommendations on acoustic surveys, stock structure analysis, and assessment techniques to improve squid stock knowledge, international cooperation, and assessment of high-seas fishing impacts.

The passage is a continuation patent application for “Physical Layer Preamble and Signaling for Wireless Communication,” claiming priority to provisional applications filed from August 2019 through April 2020. It describes physical-layer preamble designs for wireless networks, particularly IEEE 802.11 WLANs and future wireless protocols.

The disclosed PPDU structure contains a legacy preamble with L-STF, L-LTF, and L-SIG, followed by signaling for newer protocols. A universal signal field (U-SIG) precedes version-specific fields such as the Extremely High Throughput signal field (EHT-SIG). U-SIG contains version-independent and version-dependent information, including a protocol version identifier, uplink/downlink indicator, transmission-opportunity duration, BSS color, PPDU bandwidth, punctured-channel information, and format information identifying trigger-based, single-user, multi-user, or unified SU/MU formats. A receiver uses these fields to interpret the packet format, determine which subchannels contain version-specific signaling, and decode the EHT-SIG and data.

EHT-SIG designs include common and user-specific fields for resource-unit allocations, modulation and coding schemes, spatial-stream configuration, and per-user scheduling. The designs support OFDMA, MU-MIMO, SU, MU, trigger-based, and unified SU/MU PPDUs, as well as PPDUs spanning up to 320 MHz and configurations supporting 16 or more spatial streams. Alternative bandwidth and puncturing encodings, EHT-SIG compression modes, and parallelized signaling across content channels and subchannels are also described. The designs aim to limit preamble expansion while accommodating future protocol features, larger bandwidths, puncturing, and flexible resource allocation.

The passage also reviews WLAN architecture, including APs, stations, basic service sets, beaconing, scanning, association, and roaming; legacy, VHT, HE, and EHT preamble formats; OFDM and OFDMA resource allocations; punctured transmissions; and example AP, STA, and wireless-device implementations. The described reception method receives a packet containing preamble and data portions, identifies a U-SIG with version, frequency-occupation, and format information, determines the subchannels carrying version-specific signaling, and decodes that signaling. Equivalent implementations are described for a processor-based apparatus, stored computer-readable instructions, and a system.

Nintendo’s Labo line will include a Toy Con Garage workshop for building custom cardboard creations using basic inputs, actions, and conditional statements. Demonstrations included an electronic guitar and electronic tennis. The virtual mech launches April 20, and it remains unclear whether the $70 workshop requires a Labo set.

Darren Till won a controversial unanimous decision over Stephen Thompson at UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool, a close fight featuring Till’s final-round knockdown. Till offered a rematch in America, saying he could be more aggressive and knock Thompson out.

The Justice Department referred the University of Nevada at Reno’s UndocuPack program to the Department of Education for investigation, citing concerns that taxpayer funds subsidize or promote “illegal immigration” through referrals, aid, and academic and career support, including jobs that do not require Social Security numbers. President Brian Sandoval said the program serves all students regardless of citizenship status, uses no federal funds, and complies with federal and state law; UNR plans to respond through legal channels.

The action is part of what immigrant-student advocates describe as the Trump administration’s escalating campaign against higher-education benefits for undocumented students.
