The Justice Department has sued five states over in-state tuition policies, while the Education Department has investigated university scholarships. Advocates fear institutions may scale back lawful support services. They note no court has interpreted PRWORA to prohibit support offices or mentoring centers, and at least 59 such centers exist nationwide. TheDream.US’s Gaby Pacheco said colleges are weighing whether to hide or stand together, warning that reducing services signals undocumented students they do not belong and will not stop federal scrutiny.

The patent application describes methods and systems for processing mobile payments while user devices or merchant payment systems are disconnected from payment servers. An e-wallet-linked user device may be placed in an offline payment mode, allowing transactions through local communications such as NFC, Bluetooth, ZigBee, Z-Wave, LAN, USB, or scanned QR and barcodes. The merchant system sends an offline payment request, and the user device verifies that its remaining offline balance is sufficient, obtains user approval, updates that balance, and returns a payment approval message containing transaction details. The merchant stores the message until connectivity is restored.

Offline mode may be enabled for only one device associated with an e-wallet at a time to prevent overdrawing. It can be transferred between online devices through the payment server or locally between offline devices using confirmation and status messages. The server also pre-authorizes a configurable offline reserve amount based on available account balances.

When connectivity returns, the user device and/or merchant system submits the offline transaction information to the payment server. The server debits the payer, credits the merchant, and updates the pre-authorized reserve amount. Transaction identifiers are checked so each offline transaction is processed only once. The payment server includes repositories for e-wallet configuration and offline-mode status, an offline-status updating module, and a payment-processing module.

The High Post Offense is described as a simple, long-standing basketball system built on quick high post splits, down screens and back cuts that are hard to defend. Its 2-3 high alignment frees the baseline for cuts, involves all five players in scoring, eliminates weakside help, and creates offensive rebounding and second-chance opportunities.

The offense unfolds in phases. In Phase 1, one guard hits the high post and splits while the other guard cuts tight off that screen; the post may feed either guard. Defensive reads and counters include the handoff on split, the fake split, the direct basket cut when defenders collapse on the post, and the two-same-side cut when defenders switch. In Phase 2, when the high post does not feed the splitting guards, wings O3 and O4 set down screens for guards O1 and O2, with the post passing to the guard coming off the screen, to a screener rolling if the defense switches, or shooting/driving in isolation. Counters for defensive reads include the curl, basket curl, fade, back cut, screen-and-roll, and slipping the screen; switches also create post isolation against smaller defenders and wing isolation for the screener on the weakside.

Phase 3 covers high post isolation: the post pivots into a triple-threat position in the "Red Zone" without defensive help, and counters to overplay include the over-the-top lob, wing feeds, post exchange, screen exchange, and using the best triple-threat player in the high post spot. Phase 4 involves strong post ups, with the ballhandler feeding O4 or O5 when the defense focuses on shooters.

Entry variations include the flop/back cut entry, wing pass entry (with reversal and motion continuity), wing double-away entry, and post single/double screen continuity.

The text stresses offensive rebounding as decisive: players should box out, pursue second, third and fourth efforts, and capitalize on the inside rebounding advantage after high post shots. Success depends on spacing, execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, timing and defensive recognition, with individual skill development built into every practice. It concludes that even coaches not using the offense should know how to defend it.

The present application, a continuation of several “Tonneau Cover” applications and patents, describes pickup-truck bed covers that create a covered compartment for concealed storage. An illustrative cover includes a fixed base panel attached to the truck bed’s side walls and multiple movable panel sections. A first panel section pivots relative to the base panel, and a second panel section pivots relative to the first.

Each panel section has a latching assembly with pinch-latch assemblies positioned near opposite side walls. Each pinch latch includes a latch handle portion and an inner pinch handle portion containing a slot, while the latch handle portion contains a latch, spring pocket, and guide tab. A spring biases the latch toward a latched position. Pinching the handles together overcomes the spring resistance, moves the latch away from its retaining clip, and releases the panel section. A longitudinally extending connector links the two pinch latches so actuating one also releases the opposite latch, permitting both sides to be unlatched from one side of the truck. Releasing the handles causes the springs to return the latches to their latched positions.

The latching assemblies can be integrated flush with the panel frames, with aligned handle portions providing accessible touch points. The inner handle can contain a removable light that illuminates the truck bed, locates the latch, and may function as a flashlight. Additional features include a latch guide, connector configurations using a panel, bar, or rod, and optional frame-mounted securement brackets.

Adjustable side rails attach to the truck bed walls through rail brackets and fasteners. The rails contain tracks that receive latch-retaining clips, support vertical gussets, and carry D-shaped seals that help reduce water intrusion. The gussets pivot from a stowed position beneath the panels to upright positions, where they engage the latches and hold folded panels vertically.

Adjacent panels are connected by hinge assemblies containing opposing hinge brackets, a resilient hinge seal and spacer, and seal rods. These components permit folding while providing spacing, sealing, friction, and alignment. A separate securement system uses a channel bracket to hold folded panels upright and a buckle strap to prevent movement or unfolding during transport.

The drawings include perspective, underside, sectional, cross-sectional, and exploded views of the cover, panels, pinch latches, gussets, hinges, rails, seals, and buckle system.

A Bank of England regulator said major Basel III capital and liquidity reforms are largely complete, with future attention on new risks, cyber resilience, and unintended effects of leverage rules on derivatives clearing.

Aaron Judge’s late-July elbow injury sidelined him for 10 days and forced him to DH for nearly a month. He returned to the outfield with reduced arm strength, while his hitting stayed strong. He said the elbow needs work but does not know whether surgery is required.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021. The company describes its mission as empowering people and organizations through software, services, devices, cloud platforms, and AI. Its R&D strategy focuses on reinventing productivity and business processes, building intelligent cloud and edge infrastructure, and creating more personal computing. Major offerings include Microsoft 365, Office, Dynamics, LinkedIn, Teams, Azure, Windows, Surface, Edge, Xbox, and search advertising.

Microsoft reports through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It competes with companies such as Apple, Google, Amazon, Oracle, IBM, Salesforce, Sony, Nintendo, Slack, and Zoom across software, cloud, devices, gaming, advertising, and professional services. The company sells through OEMs, direct channels, distributors, resellers, and cloud partners, and it operates regional operations centers and datacenters globally. Devices are primarily manufactured by third parties.

As of June 30, 2021, Microsoft employed approximately 181,000 people. It reported a growth-mindset culture, diversity and inclusion initiatives, employee learning programs, expanded stock eligibility, and pandemic-related workplace, health, and childcare support. Sustainability commitments include carbon negativity by 2030, water positivity and zero waste by 2030, and a $1 billion climate-technology investment. Microsoft also described initiatives addressing racial injustice and expanding digital-skills training.

The filing identifies material risks from intense competition, competing platform ecosystems, changing business models, cloud-service execution, infrastructure costs, security, developer participation, device supply constraints, and the uncertain adoption of cloud and IoT offerings.

This continuation application describes methods for forming large multi-chip, multi-die integrated fan-out (InFO) semiconductor packages using reconstructed wafers. Known-good interconnect structures containing substrates, through-substrate vias, dielectric and metallization layers, redistribution layers, protective layers, and contacts are tested, singulated, and adhesively bonded to a carrier. They are encapsulated, and the encapsulant is thinned by grinding or CMP to expose contacts and create a planar reconstructed wafer.

Packaged semiconductor devices, including processors and memory cubes, are aligned over individual, adjacent, or shared interconnect structures. Their contacts are joined by direct copper-to-copper bonding at relatively low temperatures or by solder reflow. Underfill supplied by capillary or molded-underfill processes fills gaps and protects the bonds. The assembly is then encapsulated, thinned, debonded from the carrier by altering the adhesive, and provided with external solder bumps, balls, or conductive pillars.

An alternative embodiment embeds a single large universal interconnect structure in the reconstructed wafer. Dielectric and conductive universal redistribution layers are formed over it, followed by passivation, under-bump metallization, contact bumps, and attachment of discrete semiconductor components. These components receive underfill and encapsulation before carrier removal and formation of external contacts.

The disclosed processes accommodate packages exceeding 70 mm by 70 mm for high-performance computing, AI, networking, and server applications requiring high data rates, bandwidth, and low latency. Testing components before assembly, matching coefficients of thermal expansion to those of packaged devices and printed circuit boards, and using lower-temperature bonding are described as reducing stress, delamination, and component- and board-level reliability issues.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, was jailed for 18 weeks after admitting two counts of assault involving a knife. During a January drinking session with his ex-partner and her daughter, after consuming one and a half bottles of vodka, Hodder held a butter knife to his own throat before attacking both women, who suffered cuts. He also received a one-year restraining order. The older victim called the sentence a disgrace, while his lawyer said he had not been in trouble for six years.

On Nov. 26, 2001, Enron shares fell as much as 20%, touched an all-time low of $3.76 and closed at $4.01 amid mounting doubts that Dynegy’s proposed acquisition would be completed on its original terms. Enron had lost more than 90% of its value in 2001 and about half since the Nov. 9 deal announcement. At roughly $4 per share, it traded at less than one-third of its reported book value of $12.90, reflecting concern over financial disclosures following a $1.2 billion equity reduction and a $586 million downward restatement of nearly five years of earnings.

Dynegy’s board remained silent while management said due diligence and efforts to accelerate regulatory approval continued. Analysts noted that the deal’s material-adverse-change provisions could allow Dynegy to withdraw or renegotiate as Enron’s trading business weakened. Enron sought $500 million to $1 billion in financing while restructuring debt. Banks extended a $690 million loan due following a credit-rating downgrade to Dec. 14 and were discussing a further postponement to mid-2002. Enron had less than $2 billion in cash and credit lines, while a downgrade below investment grade could trigger $3.9 billion in repayments. J.P. Morgan and Citigroup pursued financing and equity investments; Citigroup had shifted $2.384 billion of Enron exposure through swaps and credit-linked trusts.

Enron’s 6.4% notes fell to 48 cents on the dollar and yielded 26%. Rating agencies warned that Enron’s credit faced further downgrades and that Dynegy’s acquisition of Enron’s debt could harm Dynegy’s rating; Dynegy bonds fell as much as 9% during November.

At least three employee class-action suits alleged that Enron harmed workers’ 401(k) accounts by encouraging purchases of inflated stock and improperly locking the plan. The latest suit sought $850 million and also claimed Enron omitted a required prospectus.

Petrobras and its Petros pension fund were close to receiving approval to buy Enron’s stakes in CEG and CEG Rio. India’s AV Birla Group denied seeking Enron’s 65% stake in Dabhol Power, while Tata Power and BSES remained in talks. The energy-trading sector’s outlook also weakened after Enron’s collapse, prompting greater investor focus on disclosure, cash-based earnings and the cyclicality of energy-trading businesses.

Enerfax Daily No. 937, dated February 20, 2002, presents North American natural-gas and electric-power prices, futures data, market commentary, industry news, event notices, and sponsor advertisements. Physical gas quotes cover Gulf/Eastern, Western, and Canadian/Rockies hubs, including Henry Hub at $2.32 and New York Citygate at $2.58. Henry Hub futures ranged from a March close of $2.397 to $3.238 in January 2003; the 12- and 18-month strips were $2.7519 and $2.8435. A fund-buying rally and bullish weather forecast were cited as drivers of the March contract’s $0.191 gain, with an expected storage withdrawal of 110–120 Bcf and estimated volume of 111,000 contracts. Physical power averages ranged from $15.85/MWh at ERCOT to $26.90/MWh at NEPOOL, with futures tables for several regional hubs.

News items included SG Resources’ open season for firm storage service at the Southern Pines Energy Center; shareholder litigation against JP Morgan Chase over its Enron exposure and disclosures; El Paso Corp.’s planned $750 million sale of Texas gas assets to El Paso Energy Partners; and AES’s plan to sell $1–$1.5 billion in assets amid liquidity concerns and a reduced capital-spending plan. Other articles attributed Enron’s accounting problems primarily to inconsistent financial disclosure rather than mark-to-market accounting, reported energy marketers’ opposition to broader derivative oversight, and described earlier fears of data-center power shortages as unrealized. MISO, PJM, and SPP announced a meeting to advance a common wholesale electricity market.

The issue also lists daily power and gas headlines, NYMEX volumes and option volatility, storage opportunities, technical-trader views, LDC Forum events, financial-market results, and advertisements for energy analytics, trading, modeling, and risk-management products.

Coach Julien said an injured player was still being evaluated and that no further information was available. He defended inserting a player into the top line despite limited league experience and chemistry. He attributed the team’s third-period improvement to better play after a passive start and praised Kane’s scoring around the net while noting defensive lapses near the crease. He was considering changes between a gritty winger and a more play-oriented defenseman, rejected blaming Zdeno or the opposing goaltender for the scoring, and emphasized that goals can come from anywhere. He credited scouting, team depth and contributions from lower-line players such as Shaw and Paille. Looking ahead, he called the next home game “do or die,” said there would be no panic, and stressed that every player needed to contribute. He described playoff adjustments as creating opportunities through line matching, bench management, faceoffs, offensive-zone play and pursuing the next goal.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 include a Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS) whose peripherals use a typical 32 kHz low-frequency clock for timekeeping or remain active during low-power modes. The LFSS_B variant contains an RTC_B real-time clock and an independent watchdog timer (IWDT). RTC_B operates from a 32 kHz source and provides calendar counters, customizable alarms, periodic wake-up interrupts, binary or BCD format, leap-year correction, standby interrupt support, crystal-offset and temperature-drift compensation, and clock outputs for calibration. IWDT_B uses a separate fixed 32 kHz clock, offers eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours, and generates a power-on reset if software fails to reset it.

The windowed watchdog timer (WWDT) monitors code execution and can generate a reset or interrupt when not serviced within a specified window. It has eight selectable periods, can stop automatically during sleep, and can operate as an interval timer.

Two timer families are documented. TIMGx general-purpose timers provide configurable up, down, or up-down counting, prescaling, repeat-reload operation, capture/compare shadow registers, optional quadrature encoder and Hall-sensor inputs, synchronization and cross-triggering, and interrupt, DMA, and peripheral trigger generation. TIMAx advanced timers provide 16-bit counting, prescaling, repeat counters, shadowed capture/compare registers, complementary PWM outputs with programmable dead band, configurable fault handling, synchronization and cross-triggering, and additional internal-event capture channels.

The IOMUX selects peripheral functions on digital I/O pins and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wake-up logic. Available pin features vary by pin. Enabling DAC_OUT occupies PA15, so external signals on that pin are not recommended. The device also provides a two-wire ARM-compatible serial wire debug interface.

The boot strap loader supports memory programming and configuration through UART or I²C. It is enabled by default, may be disabled, and is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password. It can be invoked through the BSL_invoke pin and reset, automatically on unprogrammed devices, or from application software using a SYSRST command. A memory-mapped FACTORY region provides read-only capability, identification, and factory trim information, including DEVICEID and USERID fields.

Recommended schematic connections include 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS, a 47 kΩ NRST pull-up with a 10 nF pull-down, a 100 kΩ precision resistor from ROSC to VSS when using SYSOSC frequency correction, and a 0.47 µF VCORE capacitor near the device with no other circuits attached. Pull-ups are required for high outputs from 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O.

TI provides development tools including SysConfig, CCS, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain, SDKs, Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, launch pads, BoosterPacks, and cloud-based tools. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental “X” devices from fully qualified “MSP” production devices; only qualified production devices are recommended for production systems.

The April 2025 revision updates device feature comparisons, package previews, electrical and timing specifications, ADC, SPI, flash, SRAM, DMA, security, UART, LFSS, and timer information, and adds cross-trigger mapping. The document also provides package drawings, orderable-part information, ordering statuses, RoHS and moisture-sensitivity ratings, part-marking guidance, package thermal-pad and via guidance, and automotive-qualified versions of the MSPM0G3518 and MSPM0G3519.

Ben Bishop said he felt better after several difficult days and credited his time in the minors with helping him develop as a professional. Reflecting on being drafted by Ottawa, traded by Bryan Murray to Tampa Bay, and facing uncertainty about his starting opportunity, he said his third organization provided a patient path to success. He described the Lightning’s playoff approach as consistent with the regular season, emphasizing preparation, teamwork, and responding to losses the same way every night. He also said the locker room had been enjoyable and successful and that the team could learn from similar situations it had faced previously.

University of Michigan researchers developed a clear, durable “omniphobic” coating that repels nearly every known liquid and prevents grime on tables, floors, walls, and phone screens. Inspired by co-author Anish Tuteja’s child, the coating combines fluorinated polyurethane with F-POSS; researchers are now assessing its toxicity.

Paula Norrell sued Waste Away Group, Inc., alleging sex discrimination in denying her promotion to district sales manager of the combined Montgomery-Opelika district and challenging employment practices as having a disparate impact on women. After interviewing Norrell, Greg Folmar, and Terry White, Waste Away selected White, a male, and offered Norrell a lower-paid construction representative position before she left the company.

The court found that Norrell established a prima facie failure-to-promote claim. Under the McDonnell Douglas framework, however, Waste Away articulated legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons: White had previously held the combined-district sales manager position, had outside-sales and market experience, and possessed organizational and leadership skills, while Norrell had never been an outside sales representative, required close supervision, and lacked knowledge of the Montgomery sales market. The court rejected Norrell’s efforts to show pretext through workplace remarks, finding them unrelated to the promotion decision, made by someone who was not a decisionmaker, or insufficient to overcome the deference afforded to employers’ business judgments. Norrell also failed to show that she was substantially more qualified than White.

Because no genuine issue of material fact existed, the court granted Waste Away’s motion for summary judgment. Norrell had abandoned her disparate-impact claim after discovery. Final judgment was entered for Waste Away, with costs taxed against Norrell.

Plug Power shares fell 1.54%, closing at $1.92. Analysts’ mean 52-week target is $3.22, based on seven opinions, with a $1.30–$5 range. The speaker calls his team’s latest win over New Jersey important and credits improved skating, involvement and physical play, noting two early overtime chances and a fortunate faceoff win. He acknowledges that New Jersey dominated the second period of the series and that his team had surrendered more than expected. He emphasizes puck management, four-skater rushes, speed and disciplined decisions, arguing that skating creates offensive pressure and prevents opponents from playing only defense.

He praises New Jersey’s goaltending and team-oriented play while rejecting the idea that success belongs to one player. He urges his team to ignore outside criticism, remain composed and focus on preparation, hard work and leadership, particularly Carney’s ability to settle teammates. He also notes that winning faceoffs can determine playing time. Despite a strong regular-season record, he says the team must regroup after poor stretches, learn from mistakes and continue improving, expressing confidence that the best team will win the Stanley Cup.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, analyze asset volatility and potential trend changes using a moving average with standard-deviation bands above and below. They help assess price movement relative to the average and identify possible trend reversals or continuations. However, the indicator alone does not guarantee a profitable system and may generate false signals, underperform in range-bound markets, produce delayed signals, and yield different results when settings change.

TradingView supports implementing Bollinger Bands with Pine Script’s simple-moving-average and standard-deviation functions. A breakout strategy seeks to capitalize on prices breaching the bands. The passage recommends backtesting across time frames, defining risk, and optimizing parameters. One H4 example produced considerable returns using all capital per trade, though its drawdown required further research and improvement. Bollinger Bands can support breakout, mean-reversion, and squeeze strategies as a primary or secondary component.

Queen Elizabeth II visited the Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital after the Arena bombing, meeting victims and responders. She called the attack “wicked” and told Evie Mills she had visited for Ariana Grande’s concert.

FTB Advisors and other institutional investors increased their Vanguard Total International Stock ETF (VXUS) positions in Q2, while Brighton Jones opened a new $226,000 position. VXUS traded at $54.8501 Friday and paid a $0.298 quarterly dividend, with a 2.17% annualized yield.

Tex Winter created and refined the Triangle Post Offense, a system built on sound principles, precise spacing, fundamentals, and defensive recognition rather than fixed plays. It combines three components: an entry, a sideline triangle, and a weakside two-person game. Players must recognize defensive deployments and use varied entries, cuts, screens, reversals, post splits, isolations, and passing options to attack them.

Precise spacing, generally 15–20 feet apart, spreads the defense, limits help and double-teams, and creates passing, driving, cutting, and post opportunities. The offense includes multiple ways to form the sideline triangle, strong-post and post-split actions, solo cuts, and weakside two-game options for drives, jumpers, rolls, lobs, fakes, and traps. Defensive overplays create automatic counters such as dribble penetration, post drops, kick-outs, back-door actions, and lob passes.

Success depends on coordinated execution, fundamental skill development, and systematic teaching through two-player, three-player, four-player, and full-court drills. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads, explain counters, monitor adjustments, and vary entries to prevent defenders from focusing on a single option.

The speaker takes an oath to serve the people, emphasizing his responsibility to promote the public welfare and urging citizens to set aside partisan conflict, sectional prejudice, and distrust. He calls for renewed devotion to the Constitution, which should be administered through amity, mutual concession, and careful respect for the division of powers between the federal government, states, and people.

He promises constitutional interpretation, economical administration, civil-service reform based on merit, sound public finances, reduced unnecessary taxation, protection of the public domain, and just treatment of Native Americans, including education toward citizenship. He also advocates suppressing polygamy, restricting servile immigration, and ensuring freedmen equal rights and security as citizens.

The speaker endorses an independent, peaceful, neutral foreign policy—“peace, commerce, and honest friendship with all nations; entangling alliance with none”—and urges practical, united efforts to secure the benefits of republican government while invoking Almighty God’s aid and blessings.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises four radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Each provides a 0.613-V reference with +0.7%/−1% accuracy and supports switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz through an internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary synchronization. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and generate a 5-V VLDO.

TPS7H5001-SP is a dual-output controller optimized for silicon and GaN converters, with integrated synchronous-rectifier controls and programmable dead time and maximum duty cycle. TPS7H5002-SP is a single-output controller for buck and single-ended isolated topologies with configurable dead time and leading-edge blank time. TPS7H5003-SP is a single-output variant with fixed 50-ns dead time and leading-edge blank time. Both support 75% or 100% maximum duty cycles. TPS7H5004-SP is a dual-output controller for non-synchronous push-pull and full-bridge converters, with configurable leading-edge blank time and a fixed 50% maximum duty cycle.

Features include programmable UVLO and enable behavior, capacitor-controlled soft start, resistor-programmed output voltage, pulse skipping, slope compensation, cycle-by-cycle current limiting, hiccup restart, an external fault input, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. Primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs have approximately 150-mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended.

A 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous GaN push-pull example uses the TPS7H5001-SP with a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 25-ns dead time, 33-nF soft-start capacitor, 40-µH transformer primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductor, 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, and 2.3 mF total output capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current paths, a minimal switch-node area, closely placed bypass and compensation components, separation of analog and power grounds, and routing sensitive signals away from noisy switching nodes.

During the second week of motherhood, the author found newborn care overwhelming as initial hormonal highs and support faded. Severe sleep deprivation contributed to exhaustion, depression, insecurity, and emotional volatility. Breastfeeding caused raw, bloody nipples despite using cream and changing positions, while weight-gain problems made her feel like a failure. She also felt isolated, struggled to understand and soothe her crying baby, and fought with her husband over minor issues, doubting their relationship and ability to co-parent. With the baby needing to eat or be held all night, she felt exhausted and viewed as a human pacifier. The period eventually improved, and she came to love the fourth trimester.

Jane Goodall’s legacy extends beyond her observations of living chimpanzees to the unique collection of skeletons she assembled from Gombe National Park. Because each animal’s sex, age, weight, and life history were known, researchers could study how individual development shapes skeletal anatomy and consider ancient hominin fossils from a new perspective. Goodall’s guiding principle was that field researchers “shouldn’t waste anything.” Flo’s skeleton showed that large bones do not necessarily indicate greater body weight and revealed unusual bone loss that contrasted with human osteoporosis, while supporting field observations of her motherhood shortly before death at nearly 50. Goodall, who died October 1 at age 91, maintained that much remained unknown about the collection’s scientific implications.

On June 15, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into a merger agreement with Whole Foods Market, Inc. and Walnut Merger Sub, Inc. Whole Foods Market will survive the merger, and each outstanding share, subject to specified exclusions, will be converted into the right to receive $42 in cash.

Closing requires Whole Foods Market shareholder approval, expiration of applicable waiting periods under U.S. and Canadian antitrust laws, and other customary conditions. The transaction is not conditioned on Amazon obtaining financing. The agreement includes specified termination rights, an outside date of February 15, 2018 that may be extended by 90 days under certain circumstances, and a $400 million termination fee in specified circumstances.

Amazon expects to finance the merger through debt financing and cash on hand. It obtained commitments for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge term loan facility of up to $13.7 billion, subject to specified conditions and reductions. Amazon and Whole Foods Market issued a joint announcement on June 16, 2017.

The filing cautions that the merger’s anticipated benefits, timing, financing, and closing remain subject to risks including shareholder rejection, regulatory and financing uncertainty, delays, business disruption, higher costs, lower revenues, unexpected liabilities, and management distraction.

William J. O’Neil developed the follow-through day concept as part of the CANSLIM market-timing system to identify a shift from a downtrend or market correction to a new uptrend. It generally occurs on Day 4 or later of a valid rally attempt, when a major index closes significantly higher than the prior day with greater volume. Day 1 is an up day; during Days 2 and 3, the index must remain above its recent low. A new low invalidates the rally attempt, while a later fall below the original Day 1 low indicates complete failure.

A follow-through day suggests selling has ended and provides a signal to consider buying leading growth stocks, but it does not guarantee the absolute market low. Investors should also examine leading stocks and market sentiment and follow their own risk tolerance.

The article claims that no bull market since the early 1900s began without a follow-through day. However, a short-term S&P 500 backtest using SPY produced poor results because equity indexes tend to mean-revert and the strategy buys strength. Results improved slightly when filtered for a 25-day RSI below 55, and outcomes for individual stocks or longer holding periods may differ.

The double top is a bearish reversal pattern formed by two swing highs at roughly the same level, with a swing low between them. The highs create resistance, while a neckline connecting the swing low to the preceding swing low provides support. A break below the neckline suggests a potential downward reversal.

Suggested trading rules require an existing uptrend, swing highs within 3% of each other, and a significant-volume break below the neckline to confirm a short trade. Long-term investors may use the pattern as a warning to close long positions, while short sellers may enter after the break or a neckline retest. Profit targets are projected from the pattern’s height; possible stops are above the pattern or near its midpoint.

Bulkowski’s five-year study of 500 stocks found that 39% of double tops reached their targets, compared with 68% for double bottoms. The article notes that detecting and backtesting the pattern is difficult and requires human judgment, making the strategy challenging to trade.

Education policy has become highly politicized amid the pandemic, pandemic-related learning loss, the racial reckoning of 2020, social media organizing, and growing scrutiny of schools, educators, unions, and resource disparities. These developments have intensified polarization and eroded trust, while distracting attention from student outcomes and community relationships. Despite federal gridlock and incentives favoring ideological extremes, states are enacting substantive reforms with cross-partisan support, demonstrating that cooperation across political boundaries remains possible.

Using state-level legislative research and discussions with education leaders, the paper identifies five recurring factors behind successful cross-partisan initiatives. First, proposals must be easy to communicate and broadly appealing. The science of reading and the teacher shortage became policy priorities because their purposes could be expressed in simple, widely understood terms. Second, policies should respond to local needs and have visible local champions. Examples include the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, which helps military spouses obtain equivalent teaching licenses across participating states, and locally tailored career and technical education initiatives in Idaho and North Carolina.

Third, proponents often need political cover from parents, educators, business leaders, governors, or other higher-ranking officials to support risky or unpopular changes. Teachers’ testimony helped advance the science of reading, while Virginia’s required seven-year standards deadline enabled a politically diverse Board of Education to approve revised standards unanimously after a contentious process. Fourth, both political sides must be able to claim a win. Teacher-pay legislation paired with other priorities, such as school choice in Arkansas, allowed Republicans and Democrats to support the same package. Cross-partisan civics initiatives similarly gave states and local officials flexibility to pursue different goals.

Fifth, media coverage can accelerate policy change. The podcast *Sold a Story* helped popularize concern about reading instruction and contributed to laws in 15 states by October 2023, while organized parent activism increased demands for educational options, higher-quality curricula, and school transparency.

Additional recommendations include understanding the political landscape and stakeholders’ motivations, maintaining realistic expectations, establishing a shared definition of the problem, and assessing urgency. Advocates should frame proposals as expanding rather than limiting opportunities, avoid policies perceived as threats to frontline school staff, remain focused on organizational priorities, and understand opponents’ values. Overall, the paper concludes that transparent communication, grassroots support, political maneuvering, and strategic media engagement can produce meaningful education reforms that serve students and communities despite persistent polarization.

On October 29, 2001, Enron’s shares fell roughly 9% to $13.81–$14.02, near a seven-year low, after Moody's cut its senior unsecured long-term debt rating from Baa1 to Baa2 and placed all long-term obligations on review for further downgrade. Moody’s also placed Enron’s P-2 commercial-paper rating on review. Standard & Poor’s had affirmed BBB+ while changing its outlook to negative, and Fitch placed the debt on negative watch. Enron’s 6.4% bonds due in 2006 fell to about 80–83 cents per dollar, with yields rising to 12.1%; the stock had lost more than half its value in two weeks and over $50 billion in market capitalization during 2001.

The ratings actions followed Enron’s reported third-quarter loss of $638 million, including a $1.01 billion charge, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, and disclosures of previously undisclosed investments in partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC began examining possible conflicts of interest involving Fastow’s partnerships, and Enron ousted him.

To bolster liquidity and restore investor confidence, Enron drew approximately $3 billion–$3.3 billion in existing bank lines, used about $2 billion to repay commercial paper, and began seeking another $1 billion–$2 billion in credit. Analysts said new lenders were likely to demand higher rates, collateral, asset-sale commitments, or other more restrictive terms. Enron was also pursuing the $2.9 billion sale of Portland General Electric, with approximately $1.8 billion in proceeds designated for debt reduction and about $1 billion of obligations expected to leave its balance sheet, subject to regulatory approval.

Major U.S. wholesale gas and electricity traders said their dealings with Enron remained at normal levels, though they were monitoring its credit exposure closely. In Europe, several large energy groups had frozen or restricted trading and were discussing letters of credit or other new arrangements. U.S. and British traders said no clear liquidity impact was yet apparent in wholesale energy markets.

The reports appeared amid a broad deterioration in corporate credit. Moody's reviewed 122 U.S. companies with $543 billion of debt for downgrade in the third quarter, compared with 22 companies and $66 billion reviewed for upgrade. Standard & Poor’s forecast that more than 200 companies would default on about $100 billion of debt in 2001, versus 117 defaults and $42.3 billion in 2000. Both agencies cited recession, the September 11 attacks, weak cash-raising conditions, debt-funded acquisitions, share repurchases, and damage to airlines, insurance, and travel.

Other reports said Enron’s bonds had fallen roughly 20%, lenders were likely to impose harsher financing terms, and investors were reluctant to buy debt because further downgrades were possible. A newsletter reported that Royal Dutch/Shell might consider acquiring Enron, but both companies declined to comment.

Commentary included favorable insider buying in other independent power producers—Calpine, AES, Mirant, and NRG—linked to anticipated infrastructure replacement and earnings growth. Another columnist argued that Enron’s losses and disclosure doubts were undermining confidence in corporate assets. A Houston Chronicle contributor praised Enron’s contributions to Houston’s economy and civic life while urging readers not to prejudge its difficulties.

This PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis examined Chikungunya seroprevalence in Ethiopia using five eligible English-language observational studies published from 2016 through November 2023. Four studies were cross-sectional and one was case-control; four used ELISA and one used RT-qPCR. Pooled seroprevalence was 12.35%, ranging from 6.25% in Lare district to 51.58% in Debub Ari district. Regional prevalence ranged from approximately 12% in Dire Dawa to 43.6% in SNNPR. Variation was associated with geography, diagnostic test, occupation, education, age, and sex. Farmers, formally educated individuals, and adults generally had higher prevalence, while sex differences were inconsistent. Random-effects analysis showed substantial heterogeneity (I²=97.72%); ELISA studies were heterogeneous, whereas RT-qPCR studies showed no variability. Begg’s and Egger’s tests indicated no significant small-study or publication bias. Limitations included the small number of studies, predominantly cross-sectional designs, and insufficient nationwide molecular data to predict circulating strains. The authors recommend improved surveillance, operational readiness, collaboration, and public awareness.

The book presents reusable patterns for building reliable, scalable distributed systems with containers and container orchestration, and provides supplemental code examples online. It traces the evolution from purpose-built machines to client-server systems and internet-scale distributed applications, explaining how increased complexity created demand for reusable tools and practices. Drawing on algorithms, object-oriented design patterns, and open-source software, it argues that distributed-system patterns help developers learn from prior mistakes, establish shared terminology, and build reusable components.

The single-node patterns introduced are sidecars, ambassadors, and adapters. A sidecar runs alongside an application to add capabilities such as HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, resource monitoring, or Git-based deployment. A reusable sidecar should be parameterized, expose a stable API, and be documented through its image and Dockerfile. An ambassador brokers an application’s interactions with external systems, including routing requests to sharded storage, discovering services, and splitting traffic for experiments. An adapter translates differing application interfaces into common formats for monitoring, logging, and health checks without modifying the original application.

The text then introduces microservices, which provide team independence, formal API contracts, and independent scaling but make design and debugging harder. It describes replicated stateless services behind load balancers, readiness probes, session tracking, consistent hashing, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination, with Kubernetes examples. Finally, sharded services are introduced as an alternative for stateful workloads whose data is too large for one machine, with a root routing each request to the appropriate shard.

The Piotroski F-Score strategy, developed by Stanford finance professor Joseph Piotroski, selects stocks by evaluating nine binary financial criteria covering profitability, liquidity, and efficiency. Scores of 8–9 indicate strong fundamentals, while scores of 0–4 indicate weak finances. Investors can apply the method to both value and growth stocks and use it to help identify potential outperformance, reduce risk, and diversify portfolios.

Historical backtests cited include Alpha Architect’s NYSE study from 1974–2014, which covered the largest 40% of stocks by market value. Companies scoring at least 6 produced annual returns of 13.3% using Alpha Architect’s modified score and 12.6% using the original Piotroski score, versus 11.2% for the S&P 500, with similar standard deviations. Among the cheapest 20% of shares scoring above 6, annual returns were 15.9%, 15.2%, and 11.2%, respectively. The passage also mentions European testing by ValueSignals from 1999–2011 and a Norwegian and Swedish study by Alexander Eriksen from 1997–2011.

Implementing the strategy involves setting goals, calculating scores, conducting additional research, selecting and diversifying investments, monitoring them, and rebalancing regularly. Although presented as a simple and useful tool, the F-Score does not guarantee success and should be combined with other research and analysis.

Patrick McCaffery committed to Iowa, becoming the program’s first 2019 recruit. The 6-foot-8 wing/forward chose Iowa to play for his father, head coach Fran McCaffery, alongside older brother Connor and near his family. A consensus four-star prospect, he was ranked 30th by Rivals, 42nd by Scout and 36th by the 247Sports Composite.

McCaffery said Iowa’s fast-break offense and his father’s freedom for players to learn through mistakes suited his game. He also planned to recruit four-star point guard D.J. Carton, four-star power forward Trace Jackson-Davis and point guard Tyrell Terry. Iowa had two remaining recruiting slots, and McCaffery said the program had little serious competition for him.

At Supreme Court oral argument, several justices appeared willing to allow trial judges to restrict overnight attorney-client discussions when a defendant is still testifying. The justices disagreed over where to draw the line: Texas proposed barring discussion of testimony’s content or delivery while permitting collateral strategic advice; the United States urged a broader rule barring any discussion of the client’s testimony. The case arose from David Villarreal’s murder conviction after his trial judge prohibited his lawyer from discussing his testimony overnight, though trial strategy and other options remained permissible. Defense attorney Stuart Banner argued that any restriction would chill necessary legal advice and violate the Sixth Amendment, while Texas prosecutor Andrew Warthen defended a narrower prohibition on “management” of testimony. The justices also debated whether advice on matters such as a client’s demeanor, eye contact, or speaking speed constituted impermissible coaching. No ruling had been issued.

Containerizing components of a single application supports resource isolation, clear team ownership, separation of concerns, modular reuse, focused testing, and more reliable deployments. Three tightly coupled single-node patterns are described:

- **Sidecar:** An application container contains the core logic while a colocated sidecar augments it, typically through shared filesystem, network, process, or hostname namespaces. Examples include adding HTTPS through nginx, synchronizing dynamic configuration, exposing process resource usage, and building a Git-based PaaS. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, a stable and backward-compatible API, and clear documentation through Dockerfile directives such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`.
- **Ambassador:** An ambassador container brokers communication between an application and external systems while exposing a simple local interface. Uses include routing requests to sharded storage, discovering and connecting to environment-specific services, and splitting traffic between production and experimental implementations. The pattern separates concerns and allows reusable, consistent infrastructure components.
- **Adapter:** An adapter container translates or normalizes an application’s interface into a standard form. Applications can use Prometheus exporters, Fluentd logging adapters, or dedicated health-check containers without modifying third-party images. This improves consistency, modularity, isolation, and reuse.

Multi-node systems use microservices: small services communicate through defined APIs, enabling independent teams, deployment schedules, and scaling. Their looser coupling also makes debugging and architecture more difficult, which distributed patterns help address.

A replicated load-balanced service uses identical instances behind a load balancer. Replicas provide redundancy and horizontal scaling, while readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching uninitialized instances. Session tracking can route a user consistently to one replica using IP-based hashing, application-level identifiers, or consistent hashing. A caching tier can improve latency and capacity, rate limiting can limit abusive traffic, and a separate nginx tier can terminate SSL. Kubernetes examples use Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and secrets.

Sharded services divide requests or state among shards and use a root or routing layer to select destinations, allowing systems whose state exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharding improves cache memory utilization because replicas store distinct data, but shard failures can increase cache misses and latency. Replicating each shard improves fault tolerance and enables safer rollouts and independent scaling.

Shard selection uses a deterministic, uniformly distributed hashing function, typically `hash(request) % shard_count`. The shard key should include exactly those request attributes that affect the response: overly broad keys share incompatible results, while overly specific keys fragment cache usage. Consistent hashing minimizes request remapping when the number of shards changes, reducing the cache misses associated with re-sharding.

The compilation continues the narrative to January 17, 1893, with further coverage in the report accompanying the President’s February 15, 1893 message transmitting the treaty signed at Washington on February 14 by the U.S. Secretary of State and representatives of the Provisional Government of the Hawaiian Islands. It includes chronologically arranged papers, addenda, a subject index, a bibliography, congressional reports, and documents from 1826 to 1853. The central document is the Treaty of Friendship, Commerce, and Navigation concluded at Oahu on December 23, 1826, by Thomas ap Catesby Jones and King Kauikeaouli with his guardians. Jones reported that the arrangements sought to protect American seamen and secure payment of American claims. A December 25 dispatch instructed Chaplain Stewart to deliver a letter and presents to King Kamehameha and the principal chiefs, remain two or three weeks, cultivate friendly relations, and gather information on American commercial interests.

The final lecture surveys predecessor lower bounds and presents a clean round-elimination proof nearly matching the best upper bounds, \(\min\{\log w,\log_w n\}\), from van Emde Boas and fusion tries. Earlier results include the original \(\Omega(\sqrt{\log w})\) bound, Beame–Fich and Xiau’s pure word- and problem-size bounds, and Sen’s cleaner round-elimination proof. Patrascu and Thorup later established a tight tradeoff among \(n\), \(w\), and space.

The proof targets the easier colored predecessor problem, where queries return only the predecessor’s color. It applies to static randomized structures with polynomial space and success probability above \(1/2\). Communication complexity models the query algorithm as Alice and the data structure as Bob, with each memory read corresponding to a communication round.

Round elimination repeatedly removes a first message while increasing the error probability slightly. It is applied to specially partitioned inputs: one elimination resembles van Emde Boas’s reduction of word size, while the reverse resembles fusion trees’ reduction of problem size. Eliminating every message would leave a zero-message protocol with success probability at most \(1/2\), contradicting the controlled error accumulation. The resulting lower bound is \(\Omega(\min\{\log w,\log_w n\})\) up to a logarithmic-logarithmic factor and implies the earlier pure-\(w\) and pure-\(n\) bounds.
Rudy Gestede urged Middlesbrough to believe they can end their slump and avoid relegation. The promoted side are 19th, six points from safety with seven games remaining and have scored only 22 goals.

This study compared SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine responses in 13 healthy controls and 27 rheumatoid arthritis patients receiving methotrexate (MTX; 11), abatacept (11), or rituximab (5), using serum antibody and neutralization assays and analyses of spike-specific T- and B-cell responses after a second Pfizer or Moderna vaccine dose. Rituximab-treated participants had almost no detectable anti-spike antibodies or neutralization and reduced spike-specific CD4 T-cell responses. Abatacept-treated participants had significantly lower anti-spike IgG and serum neutralization than controls. Although RBD-specific B-cell numbers were similar across control, abatacept, and MTX groups, abatacept was associated with fewer antigen-experienced, activated, class-switched B cells, more naive-phenotype and unswitched IgD-positive cells, and altered memory differentiation. Their production of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 was also reduced. MTX recipients had fewer activated spike-specific CD4 T cells, but no significant differences in antibody levels, neutralization, or B-cell numbers, phenotype, or class switching. Age and sampling time did not explain abatacept-associated antibody reductions. Overall, abatacept impaired T-cell help, B-cell activation and class switching, and humoral immunity, while rituximab nearly eliminated antibody responses. The findings support temporarily discontinuing abatacept before vaccination, when clinically manageable, to improve vaccine-induced protection.

The document describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture, centered on the GA102 and GA104 GPUs, which build on Turing. GA10x adds new capabilities and is stated to be up to 1.7 times faster in traditional raster graphics and twice as fast in ray tracing, while improving performance per area and energy efficiency. GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40, while GA104 powers the GeForce RTX 3070.

The RTX 3090 is positioned for 8K HDR gaming, with 10,496 CUDA cores, 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, and DLSS 8K support. The RTX 3080 provides up to twice the performance of the RTX 2080, while the RTX 3070 rivals the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti. GA10x GPUs also support HDMI 2.1 and AV1 decoding for 8K HDR streaming. The RTX A6000 combines 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, 10,752 CUDA cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6 for rendering, graphics, AI, and compute workloads. The A40 has the same core counts and memory size for data-center, virtual-workstation, and server workloads and is stated to be up to twice as power-efficient as the preceding generation.

GA102 was fabricated using Samsung’s 8 nm 8N process and contains 28.3 billion transistors in a 628.4-square-millimeter die. Its compute resources comprise CUDA cores for programmable shading, RT Cores for BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, and Tensor Cores for neural-network training and inference. A full GA102 GPU has 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores.

The GA10x Streaming Multiprocessor contains four partitions, each with a 64 KB register file, instruction cache, warp scheduler, dispatch unit, and associated processing units. Each SM has 128 CUDA cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, four texture units, one second-generation RT Core, a 256 KB register file, and 128 KB of configurable L1 cache and shared memory. FP32 processing is available on both primary datapaths, doubling peak FP32 throughput compared with Turing. Each partition can execute either 32 FP32 operations per clock or 16 FP32 and 16 INT32 operations, and the complete SM can perform 128 FP32 or 64 FP32 plus 64 INT32 operations per clock. The RTX 3090 delivers more than 35 FP32 TFLOPS.

Second-generation RT Cores retain dedicated BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection hardware, double Turing’s intersection-testing rate, and can run concurrently with graphics or compute work. GA10x also supports simultaneous compute workloads, including denoising alongside ray tracing, with software controls for assigning workload priorities. In the RTX 3080, ray-tracing performance is stated to be up to twice that of the RTX 2080 Super.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support new data types, including TF32, which provides up to five times the training throughput of the preceding generation without code changes. Fine-grained structured sparsity doubles Tensor Core throughput by processing sparse neural networks at twice the rate of Turing Tensor Cores. These cores accelerate AI denoising, DLSS with support for up to 8K, NVIDIA Broadcast, and NVIDIA Canvas.

Memory capabilities include GDDR6X at 19.5 Gbps on the RTX 3090 and 19 Gbps on the RTX 3080. With a 320-bit interface, the RTX 3080 provides 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. The RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB of GDDR6 and can combine two GPUs through NVLink for 96 GB. Third-generation NVLink provides four bidirectional x4 links, totaling 112.5 GB/sec between two GPUs. It supports paired A40 or RTX A6000 configurations and SLI for two RTX 3090 GPUs; three- and four-way SLI are unsupported. GA10x also uses PCIe Gen 4, offering twice the bandwidth of PCIe 3.0 and up to 64 GB/sec in a x16 configuration.

GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, and 84 SMs. Each GPC includes a raster engine and two ROP partitions with eight ROP units each, for 112 ROPs in total, compared with 96 in the similarly memory-configured TU102. Moving ROPs into the GPC is intended to improve raster throughput, multisample anti-aliasing, pixel fill rate, and blending. The GPU has twelve 32-bit memory controllers, a 384-bit interface, and 6 MB of L2 cache.

GA10x’s unified L1 cache, shared memory, and texture cache can be reconfigured by workload. Each SM has 128 KB of combined capacity, double the shared-memory bandwidth of Turing, and 10,752 KB of total L1 cache across GA102. At equivalent performance, Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing GPUs.

This study developed and psychometrically evaluated an Arabic version of the 22-item Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) for adults with malocclusions and dentofacial deformities in Saudi Arabia. The questionnaire was translated, back-translated, reviewed by professionals, and pilot-tested.

The prospective study recruited 74 patients from a private orthodontic practice in Jeddah between January 2021 and December 2022. Fifteen additional patients completed the questionnaire twice for test-retest assessment, and 12 completed it before and after surgery. The Arabic OQLQ showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Overall test-retest reliability was excellent (Spearman correlation = 0.859), while the awareness-of-deformity domain had good reliability (0.601). Construct validity was supported by positive correlations between OQLQ scores and satisfaction, and by better quality-of-life scores among patients reporting improved postoperative appearance. Overall scores decreased after surgery in both the full cohort (median 34 to 10; p<0.0001) and paired subgroup (22 to 11.5; p=0.09); facial-esthetics scores improved significantly in the paired subgroup (p=0.03).

The authors concluded that the Arabic OQLQ is comprehensible, reliable, valid, and responsive and suitable for assessing quality-of-life changes related to orthognathic treatment. Limitations included small test-retest and paired samples, absence of direct comprehension testing and convergent or discriminant validity comparisons, and recruitment from a single private practice.

The Supreme Court will consider whether restitution imposed under the 1996 Mandatory Victims Restitution Act is a criminal punishment subject to the Constitution’s ex post facto clause. If so, Holsey Ellingburg must pay only the restitution required when he robbed a bank; if not, revised rules may increase his obligations. Ellingburg argues that restitution is criminal because it is part of his sentence, follows criminal procedures, can result in incarceration for nonpayment, and serves punitive purposes. The government has conceded that restitution is criminal for ex post facto purposes, while a court-appointed amicus argues the record does not justify reversal. The author predicts the government’s concession will likely prevail.

Steve Pearse, a former CEO, entrepreneur, and angel investor, explains startup strategy, fundraising, and pitching to investors. He notes that most startups fail, but investors may fund experienced founders again after earlier failures. A venture-backed company generally needs an exit, either through an acquisition or an initial public offering, and should plan for going public even if acquisition occurs.

Startups can compete with established companies through speed, flexibility, and employees’ shared incentive to build equity value. To attract investors, founders must create a strong signal amid substantial noise. A pitch should open with an attention-grabbing hook, remain understandable to a nontechnical audience, emphasize customer and financial benefits over technical details, and address the market, business model, sales channels, competition, team, finances, timeline, and investment offer. Presenters should use visuals, keep an individual presentation near 20 minutes, control distracting technical questions, speak slowly, maintain eye contact, and display passion, confidence, and engagement.

Fundraising should begin at least six months before money is needed. Investors should be approached in parallel and orchestrated to create competitive interest, while introductions and a clear differentiator help a pitch stand out. Investors may offer useful networks and credibility, but founders must closely monitor cash flow.

To survive, startups should use rapid prototypes and customer feedback, be willing to pivot, prioritize speed over patents, define a broader mission, build a resilient and compatible team, remain focused, and compensate for weaknesses through complementary people. Pearse concludes that effective leadership, combined with a clear call to action, is central to startup success.

In 1977, amid fear of Peter Sutcliffe and wider threats to women walking at night, the Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group organized two nighttime marches that launched the UK’s first Reclaim the Night event; women in 12 towns and cities marched with banners, chants and torches. The marches continued for over a decade, faded in the early 1990s, and were revived in 2004. Their history inspired RashDash’s The Darkest Corners, a mix of cabaret, physical theatre and live music staged in a Holbeck car park on April 20–22. The work reflects women’s continuing experiences of being followed or harassed at night and celebrates activists who have challenged violence against women.

This systematic review examined how student personality traits relate to satisfaction and success in higher education online learning, motivated by the growth of hybrid education and limited occupational therapy–specific research. Following Cochrane and PRISMA methods, searches of seven databases from January 2000 through June 2024 yielded 848 records, of which 23 studies were synthesized. All were Oxford level IV evidence, and none examined occupational therapy programs.

Across the low-strength evidence, conscientiousness was most consistently associated with engagement, grades, and satisfaction. Agreeableness and openness generally correlated positively with GPA, engagement, or satisfaction, while neuroticism was most consistently negatively associated with these outcomes, although one study found highly neurotic students performed better. Extraversion had mixed results: it was associated with engagement and preference for interactive elements but generally did not affect GPA or satisfaction and sometimes predicted preference for face-to-face classes. Introverts sometimes preferred online learning, while extraverts and intuitive learners performed better on discussion assignments. Conscientious, agreeable, and open students were also more likely to choose online education, whereas neurotic students were least likely.

The review recommends flexible, personality-informed course design, Universal Design for Learning, self-regulated learning support, and targeted assistance for students who may need it. Identified gaps include the low evidence level, inconsistent satisfaction measures, limited occupational therapy research, geographic generalizability, and the need for intervention-based studies.

- NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. It supports VirtualLink, allowing a VR headset’s power, display, and tracking data to travel through one USB-C connection. VirtualLink can simultaneously provide four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes and a SuperSpeed USB 3 link, reducing VR cabling and enabling support for compact devices.

- Turing GPUs use NVLink for SLI transfers. TU102 has two second-generation x8 links, while TU104 has one; each link provides 25 GB/s per direction. Turing supports two-way SLI but not three- or four-way configurations.

- Dedicated RT Cores in every Streaming Multiprocessor accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and BVH structures, they deliver more than 10 gigarays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance. Turing supports NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API for effects such as shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

- NVIDIA NGX uses deep neural networks and Turing Tensor Cores to accelerate graphics and client applications. Deep Learning Super-Sampling produces images comparable to temporal antialiasing with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X combines final-resolution inputs in a larger network to approach 64-times-supersampled quality. Other NGX features include AI Inpainting, AI Slow-Mo, and 2x, 4x, or 8x AI Super Rez.

- Mesh shading adds cooperative task and mesh shader stages, allowing GPU processing of large object lists without a separate CPU draw call for every object. It supports dynamic level-of-detail selection and geometry modifications such as spherical CAD cutaways, and can render hundreds of thousands of objects in real time.

- Variable Rate Shading controls shading separately for each 16×16-pixel region without changing visibility sampling. Applications include content-adaptive shading for low-detail regions, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that reduces peripheral shading. Shading can also be increased for multisample antialiasing, up to the applicable sample count.

- Texture Space Shading decouples appearance shading from screen-space visibility, stores shading in reusable texture-space texels, and supports independent sampling rates and grids. This improves temporal stability, allows reuse across frames and stereo views, and helps meet VR and AR frame-time budgets.

- Multi-View Rendering expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection. Turing hardware supports four views per pass and up to 32 views through the API, allowing geometry to be fetched and shaded once for stereo displays, canted high-field-of-view HMDs, multiple character poses, and cascaded shadow maps. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, resource heaps, and more flexible memory co-location.

- TU104 contains six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and 13.6 billion transistors. It is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but supports neither NVLink nor SLI.

- RTX-OPS is presented as a workload-based metric that weights peak Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput according to their representative use during a frame. The document describes ray tracing as backward tracing from the camera through scene geometry, using BVH tree traversal and denoising to reduce computational cost and produce physically correct lighting, shadows, reflections, refractions, and indirect illumination.

The study compares online learning (OL), an intentionally planned, technology-mediated educational modality, with emergency remote education (ERE), a temporary shift to fully remote teaching during the COVID-19 crisis. It examines Colombian higher-education students’ perceptions and preferences regarding both modalities.

The case study was conducted at a private university in Colombia’s Caribbean region with approximately 10,000 students. Eighty-eight students voluntarily completed an online survey containing 14 rating items covering content quality, interaction, assessment, feedback, time requirements, resources, and technical support, plus open-ended questions about advantages, disadvantages, and future modality choices. Data were analyzed descriptively, through paired t-tests, the add-on preferential groups model with permutation tests, and qualitative content analysis.

Students generally viewed both modalities positively, with 70% to 90% reporting favorable perceptions of both in many areas. OL received higher average ratings on most assessed factors, with statistically significant differences concentrated on learning activities, content, assessment, independent learning time, resources, platforms, and technical support. Preference for OL exceeded 57% for asynchronous activity time (65.34%), assessment strategies (61.39%), content quality and quantity (60.23%), and synchronous session time (58.23%). Preferences for student-student interaction were nearly even.

Qualitative responses associated ERE with pandemic continuity, comfort and flexibility, effective learning, peer interaction, and greater instructor contact and feedback. Its principal weaknesses involved organization, instructors’ limited preparation with digital tools, insufficient interaction or information access, excessive content, and pedagogical strategies. OL was valued for convenience and flexibility, learning effectiveness, structure, interaction, and technological tools. Suggested improvements included stronger instructor-student interaction, more varied activities, fewer assignments, and additional synchronous sessions.

The findings support retaining flexible and asynchronous learning, peer interaction, and timely feedback. They also emphasize instructor training in digital and pedagogical competencies, better course organization, reduced student workload, and authentic, flexible, participatory, and collaborative assessment practices.

The Russell 2000 is a market-weighted index of approximately 2,000 U.S. small-cap stocks and is reconstituted annually on the fourth Friday of June. Rebalancing adds qualifying companies, removes ineligible ones, and adjusts constituent weights to reflect changes in market capitalization. Required buying and selling can create temporary market imbalances and has historically been associated with an end-of-June rally.

The tested strategy buys the Russell 2000 at the close of the first trading day after June 23 and sells at the close of the first trading day of July. Using the cash index from 1988 onward, the article reports an average gain of 1.34% over an average holding period of six trading days, compared with 0.85% for the S&P 500 over the same period. A strategy allocated 50% to the Russell 2000 and 50% to a short S&P 500 position averaged only 0.23%, performing poorly during its first 12 years and remaining relatively flat over the following decade. The exact rebalancing date varies annually and is identified on Russell’s website.

The message rejects a House bill appropriating $1,378,450 for more than 40 harbor and river improvements, arguing that Congress lacks constitutional authority to construct internal improvements within states or fund them from the Treasury. Applying Madison’s construction of federal power, it maintains that such power is neither expressly granted nor incidental and necessary to executing any granted power. Approving the bill would consolidate authority in the federal government, undermine state sovereignty, and require a constitutional amendment.

The message distinguishes federally supported navigation aids connected to foreign commerce, naval protection, or actual shipping from projects involving local inlets, creeks, rivers, and interior sites lacking foreign commerce. Statutory “ports of entry” with no actual trade cannot justify appropriations, yet the bill includes more than twenty such projects and others benefiting only particular neighborhoods.

It also warns that a broad internal-improvement system would encourage sectional favoritism, unequal distribution of the common treasury, waste, public debt, or higher taxes. Spending $1 million to $2 million on nonurgent works during a foreign war would be especially unwise. Although some provisions were acceptable standing alone, approval is withheld because the bill as a whole would establish an unauthorized and expansive federal program.

Digital leaders align teams through transparent, data-driven objectives tied directly to company strategy. A combined top-down and bottom-up process helps employees understand and support their targets. However, mandating OKRs or imposing excessive analytical requirements can create burdens and undermine human intuition in everyday decisions.

Digital laggards often have priorities weakly connected to strategy, leading employees to deprioritize unclear objectives and creating organization-wide misalignment. A “culture of genius” can worsen these problems. By contrast, a strong data culture supports vertical alignment with company goals and horizontal collaboration through shared metrics, common data models, and transparent data access. Culture coordinates behavior when leadership beliefs, company values, and daily actions consistently reinforce one another. Laggards may recognize data’s importance but face entrenched habits, insufficient skills, and inadequate leadership focus.

Digital transformation remains achievable. Successful firms emphasize learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement, while mature organizations must continue improving their cultures. Four organizational profiles are identified: data novices, insight-ready organizations, tech-enabled organizations, and data-reliant organizations that may overuse data and discourage critical thinking. Each can advance by building on its existing strengths.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture supports GeForce RTX 30-series, data-center, and professional GPUs. It introduces GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron using PAM4 signaling, MTA encoding, and updated interface training and equalization. GDDR6X supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, over 52% more than TU102. Its Error Detection and Replay feature identifies failed memory transactions and retries them, helping users recognize when further memory overclocking is unproductive.

NVIDIA RTX IO, paired with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables compressed assets to move from NVMe SSDs directly to GPUs for asynchronous, GPU-based lossless decompression. It is described as improving I/O performance by up to 100 times over hard drives and traditional APIs while reducing CPU use, accelerating loading, improving frame rates, and supporting large games and professional datasets.

GA10x provides up to twice the programmable-shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of the prior generation. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance and add motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores support structural sparsity, doubling effective Tensor Core throughput.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing, offering claimed gains over Quadro RTX 6000 of up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and 5x AI/data-science throughput, or 10x with sparsity. It includes PCIe Gen4, 48 GB of memory expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, vGPU and Quadro Sync support, and EGX compatibility. The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, for large visualization and rendering workloads.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 4K120 and 8K60 output and two 8K60 displays. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1; GA10x provides AV1 hardware decoding up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU use. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102, 24 GB of GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores, while the RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, lacks NVLink, and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti.
