The statistical analysis plan (SAP) defines the analyses for Zealand Pharma A/S protocol ZP4207-17086 and requires deviations from the plan to be documented in the clinical study report. It is based on protocol version 3.0, eCRF version 1.0, and data management plan version 1.0.

This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, parallel-arm trial will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of dasiglucagon versus placebo and GlucaGen® in children with type I diabetes mellitus. The primary objective is to show that 0.6 mg dasiglucagon is superior to placebo for treating hypoglycemia. Secondary objectives are to compare dasiglucagon with GlucaGen®, assess safety, and characterize the pharmacokinetic profile. The trial was expected to involve approximately five centers, including two to three in Europe and one to two in the USA. Periods include screening from Day −30 to −3, treatment on Days 0–1, and follow-up on Day 28.

The primary comparison is dasiglucagon versus placebo. Based on assumed median recovery times of 10 and 50 minutes, respectively, and an exponential time-to-recovery distribution, 20 patients in the dasiglucagon arm and 10 in the placebo arm provide 90% power at a two-sided 5% significance level with 45 minutes of follow-up. Ten patients are expected to provide an adequate GlucaGen® reference comparison.

Analyses will use ICH-numbered tables, listings, and figures. Unless otherwise specified, tests will be two-sided at the 0.05 level, with P values ≤0.05 considered significant. Continuous variables will be summarized using measures such as means, standard deviations, medians, ranges, valid counts, and, where appropriate, geometric means and geometric coefficients of variation. Categorical variables will be summarized by counts and percentages. Individual patient data and derived data will be presented in listings. Analyses defined before unblinding are a priori; subsequent analyses will be labeled post hoc and exploratory. SAS version 9.4 or later will be used for general analyses, and Phoenix WinNonlin version 6.4 or later for PK and PD analyses.

The safety analysis set includes randomized patients who received at least one dose and is analyzed according to treatment received. The full analysis set includes all safety-set patients and uses randomized treatment and planned injection site. The per-protocol set includes full-analysis-set patients without relevant protocol deviations and also uses randomized treatment and planned injection site. The primary endpoint is analyzed in the full analysis set, with a supportive per-protocol analysis; safety analyses use the safety set. Disposition, demographic and baseline characteristics, diabetes and medical history, body measurements, concomitant medications, screening assessments, protocol deviations, and eligibility failures will be summarized or listed by treatment group. Medical history terms are coded using MedDRA version 22.0; concomitant medications and diabetes treatments are coded with WHODrug Global, version March 2018.

The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma-glucose recovery, defined as the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp without rescue intravenous glucose, assessed within 45 minutes after dosing. Secondary efficacy measures are recovery within 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes and glucose changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is the last non-missing value before the first dose. Primary analyses adjust for age group and injection site. Missing efficacy data are not imputed; only observed data are analyzed, and no interim analyses are planned.

Confirmatory testing in the full analysis set follows a hierarchical order: time to recovery, four recovery-time endpoints, and four glucose-change endpoints. Inference continues at the two-sided 0.05 level until the first failure to reject a dasiglucagon-versus-placebo comparison. GlucaGen comparisons are excluded from the hierarchy.

Time to recovery will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier methods, with rescue-glucose recipients and patients not recovering by 45 minutes censored and classified as not recovered. A stratified log-rank test, stratified by age group and injection site, will compare dasiglucagon with placebo; the same method will compare dasiglucagon with GlucaGen® outside the confirmatory hierarchy. Sensitivity analyses will examine rescue-glucose recipients without rescue-related censoring and with censoring at rescue administration. A stratified Wilcoxon test and recovery histograms are also planned. A descriptive discrete-time Cox proportional-hazards model will be used if proportional-hazards conditions and censoring limits are met, incorporating treatment, age group, injection site, and baseline glucose. Homogeneity models will assess sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, and US/non-US status. Linear interpolation of recovery times will provide a supportive analysis.

Recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes will be compared using a Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site, with a non-stratified Fisher test as a fallback for small or zero cell counts. Responder rates and 95% confidence intervals will be presented. Glucose changes from baseline at each time point will be analyzed by an analysis of variance containing treatment, age group, and injection site, with adjusted means, confidence intervals, and treatment differences. Rescue-glucose values will be used when rescue treatment occurs before the relevant time point.

Plasma dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations will be measured before dosing and at 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 90, 140, 220, and 300 minutes. Noncompartmental PK parameters will be calculated and summarized, with individual and mean concentration listings and figures on original and logarithmic scales. Below-quantification values, sampling times, and missing post-dose results will be handled according to specified rules. PK results will be prepared by Synteract from data transferred by York Bioanalytical Solutions and MLM Laboratories.

Plasma glucose will be measured before dosing and at 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20, 30, and 45 minutes, with an additional 60-minute measurement for patients weighing at least 21 kg. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is area under the glucose effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes, calculated with SAS. Concentration summaries, changes from baseline, and individual and mean concentration-time figures will be produced.

Safety analyses will cover insulin use and hypoglycemia induction, trial-drug administration, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory results, vital signs, electrocardiograms, and immunogenicity. Treatment-emergent adverse events are events occurring after dosing or worsening after dosing and will be summarized by treatment group using MedDRA-coded system organ classes and preferred terms. Separate summaries will cover adverse events of special interest, other important events, injection-site reactions, study-drug-related events, serious events, and deaths. Causality and severity rules and handling of incomplete information are specified. Rescue-glucose timing will be described without statistical testing. Local reactions will be summarized by time point, symptom, and intensity.

Laboratory data will include descriptive summaries, reference-range flags, categorical results, and changes from screening to follow-up. Vital signs will be summarized at baseline and post-baseline visits. ECG summaries will include investigator assessments, descriptive parameters, QTcF thresholds, and changes from baseline. Antidrug antibody incidence will be described descriptively, including treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases, without statistical testing.

Compared with the protocol, the SAP reworded the primary efficacy analysis, added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changed secondary efficacy terminology from “within” to “at” specified minutes. Appendices define presentation standards, derived-variable formulas, programming and validation requirements, and proposed tables, figures, and listings. QC procedures cover program structure, SAS logs, outputs, dataset validation, source-data spot checks, figure and listing verification, and documentation of findings and resolutions.

International tribunals have treated loss of use as the proper measure of damages for vessels detained or seized by governments. In *The Hope On*, the Chilean commission awarded damages based on the vessel’s probable catch lost during enforced absence from fishing grounds. In *Col. Lloyd Aspinwall*, the umpire allowed compensation for 114 days of interrupted trade. Bering Sea Commission awards generally applied this rule, awarding estimated catch earnings while excluding ownership interests, duplicate expenses, and legal costs in cases including the *Favorite*, *Alfred Adams*, *Juniata*, *Pathfinder*, *Black Diamond*, *Lily*, and *Triumph*. The passage also states that a government may not forcibly enroll citizens or subjects of a friendly nation into its public service without their consent.

The passage argues that the SPY tends to be higher the day after a down day and lower the day after an up day, a pattern explained through mean reversion. Momentum investing holds that a rising asset is likely to keep rising and works well over longer timeframes, while mean reversion holds that prices and historical returns eventually return to their long-run average — illustrated by the S&P 500's 30-year average P/E ratio of about 17, which has been exceeded in bubbles and undershot in crises before reverting. Because stocks move in bounces and dips rather than straight lines, the authors present the SPY's short-term behavior as mean-reverting.

A simple trading strategy based on this idea — buying after a red day and selling after a green day — was backtested in Python using dividend- and split-adjusted SPY ETF data. The red-day strategy delivered strong returns, spent less time in the market, achieved better risk-adjusted performance and higher CAGR, and had less than half the drawdown of the green-day strategy, with significantly reduced maximum drawdown relative to buy-and-hold. The conclusion is that the S&P 500 is highly mean reverting in the short term, while trend following or momentum remains effective over longer horizons.

Ofcom has proposed automatic cash or bill-credit compensation for fixed broadband and landline customers whose outages are not fixed promptly, whose new service is not working by the promised date, or whose engineer misses an appointment, without requiring a formal claim. Ofcom would set payment amounts and estimates up to 2.6 million customers could receive up to £185 million annually. A consultation closes on 5 June, with a decision expected around year-end.

A forwarded Option Investor Newsletter dated January 21, 1999, reviews a broad market selloff and numerous stock and options plays. The Dow fell 71.83 points to 9,264.08, the Nasdaq lost 70.77 points to 2,344.72, and the VIX rose to 31.95. Internet stocks declined sharply amid bearish commentary, brokerage trading restrictions, and profit-taking. Additional concerns included Brazil, rumors of Chinese or Hong Kong currency devaluation, the trade deficit, and Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan’s caution that financial markets remained fragile and stock gains might be difficult to sustain. Technology issues had rallied on strong Microsoft earnings before retreating.

The newsletter’s market posture was mostly neutral, with hardware rated bullish and insurance and oil-and-gas sectors rated bearish. It warned that many sectors were near 50-day moving averages and potential short-term reversals. Sentiment indicators remained bearish: investors were advised to protect long positions if the Dow stayed below 9,400 and to consider hedging or reducing exposure while the VIX remained above 30%. A review of recent earnings showed that numerous companies exceeded estimates but still sold off sharply, reinforcing the view that holding positions through earnings was risky.

Call recommendations discussed PRIA, Nokia, Dell, Cisco, AOL, MCI WorldCom, AT&T, Microsoft, Tellabs, Maytag, Sun Microsystems, Lexmark, XICOR, Capital One, and Ethan Allen. The newsletter highlighted possible stock splits at Nokia, Cisco, AOL, Maytag, and Lexmark. Microsoft’s post-earnings pullback was described as a buying opportunity, while Sun Microsystems announced a 2-for-1 split and earnings that beat estimates but fell on profit-taking. AOL was presented as the strongest Internet stock and a possible buying opportunity before earnings. Put selections included AVT, Bank of America, Becton Dickinson, Campbell Soup, DuPont, Eastman Kodak, Electronic Arts, Hershey, Eli Lilly, Microchip Technology, Merck, Pennzoil, Remington Arms, and Westlake. Most were described as weakening or trading near specified support levels, with tighter protective stops recommended.

The newsletter dropped call picks on Qualcomm, Disney, Yahoo, Check Point, Lucent, and ATI because their performance, prospects, or role in the strategy had changed. ATI was replaced by Vodafone because ATI’s movement was largely tied to Vodafone’s price.

New call plays included Vodafone and Qwest Communications. Vodafone was presented following its merger with ATI and planned acquisition of AirTouch Communications. Qwest was described as expanding a fiber-optic network, with contracts involving Verio, Ford, Hometown Connections, and Covad Communications. New diagonal-spread plays were recommended in Citrix Systems, Read-Rite, Level 3 Communications, and Sepracor, based on earnings, network expansion, drug-development prospects, and bullish technical patterns.

The portfolio update said prior Tuesday spreads traded near recommended entry levels, LEVL was exited for a $1.12 profit, and PCS had moved deep in the money and might require being rolled to a higher strike. During Thursday’s selloff, no positions were reportedly in danger of being closed out, and losses in Sun Microsystems and MCI WorldCom were favorable relative to the sold strikes.

The 2017 Sonora High School Athletic Hall of Fame class includes 12 former Wildcats who graduated between 1950 and 2008. Inductees are Howard “Socky” Keefe, Dennis Jackson, Don Moore, Cam Fray, Jon Wagner, Mark McCollough, Becky Fray Aguilar, Jodi Gardella Richey, Jessica Peterson McCornack and Lexi Kopf Scoles, along with coaches Lloyd Gaspar and Gary Smith. Their honors span football, basketball, baseball, softball, volleyball, wrestling, track, soccer, golf, water polo and gymnastics, as well as coaching and school administration. Jackson earned All-Star recognition and competed in track and football; Wagner compiled a 115-15 wrestling record; McCollough was the state’s leading football rusher in 1979; Aguilar excelled in volleyball, basketball and softball; Richey captained championship teams in three sports; McCornack received a Fresno State volleyball scholarship; and Scoles holds school records for soccer goals and earned a UC Irvine scholarship. Gaspar won four tennis titles and received California State Athletic Director of the Year honors, while Smith recorded 497 girls’ basketball wins. The induction banquet is scheduled for Nov. 4 at Sonora Elks Lodge, with dinner and an awards ceremony.

A federal judge ruled that FACEA’s religious-freedom protections cover Falun Gong practitioners and rejected a Commerce Clause challenge. U.S. District Judge Jack Weinstein said religion substantially affects interstate commerce and that Congress could reasonably protect places of worship from violence and intimidation. He interpreted “a place of religious worship” broadly, rejecting limits based on formal temples or physical buildings. The ruling followed a Brooklyn lawsuit by 13 Falun Gong practitioners alleging harassment by the Chinese Anti-Cult World Alliance, which denies Falun Gong is a religion and challenged FACEA after Weinstein treated the practice as religion for the case. Weinstein certified the decision for appeal before a trial requiring interpreters and 500 jury decisions.

The passage describes growing censorship in U.S. education, citing PEN America’s report of 22,810 book bans in public schools from 2021–2025. It says book restrictions have spread from a few colleges to campuses nationwide, targeting library materials, curricula, gender and diversity programs, and controversial readings. Examples include Franciscan University, New College of Florida, the U.S. Naval Academy, Princeton, Texas A&M, and a professor’s resignation at West Point.

It also describes right-wing proposals requiring public, searchable syllabi and audits of courses, as well as the Trump administration’s “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education,” which threatens federal funding and institutional penalties for alleged violations. The compact is characterized as an effort to intimidate colleges into suppressing ideas deemed disrespectful to conservatives. Despite these developments, the passage cites broad public opposition to book banning and urges educators, librarians, students, and institutions to form a united defense of academic freedom and free expression.

Under the Carter administration, MONs authorized certain high-risk, costly, or geographically specific covert operations under previously approved general objectives and required coordination among the CIA, State Department, and other agencies. Their use later expanded to significant changes in findings, while new covert actions still required presidential findings. The 1980 Intelligence Oversight Act limited congressional notice to the two intelligence committees and clarified that oversight did not require congressional approval. Presidents facing extraordinary circumstances could withhold prior notice from all but the “Gang of Eight,” but had to notify the intelligence committees afterward and explain the omission.

Archival records describe Secretary of State George Shultz’s January 1983 memorandum to President Ronald Reagan, which presented a four-part U.S.-Soviet agenda covering human rights, arms control, regional issues, and bilateral relations. Records also document Clark’s summary of a Soviet telegram, Reagan’s interest in Dobriansky’s proposals, internal criticism of Shultz’s memorandum, and Lawrence Eagleburger’s briefing of Clark on Shultz’s talks with Dobriansky.

The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe says the official US dollar-to-bond-note exchange rate remains 1:1 and urges the public to use licensed financial institutions. Forty-five institutions are licensed, while fees for exchanging dollars or bond notes for other currencies may not exceed 10% of either currency’s nominal value. The RBZ welcomed arrests of unlicensed money changers under 2017 regulations and said it would act against retailers refusing non-cash payments. It blamed inflated cross-rates and panic messaging for panic buying and artificial shortages.

**St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Co. v. Conarty** (opinion delivered February 3, 1913; McCulloch, C.J.) affirmed a $10,000 judgment recovered by Fannie M. Conarty, as administratrix of W. G. Conarty, deceased, and widow, for his death in a switching collision in the Fort Smith, Arkansas yards.

Four issues were decided:

1. **Removal to federal court.** The Federal Employers Liability Act, as amended April 5, 1910, validly prohibits removal on grounds of diversity of citizenship, following *Kansas City Southern Ry. Co. v. Cook*, 100 Ark. 467. The order denying the defendant's petition and bond was therefore correct.

2. **Single action for pain and suffering and pecuniary loss.** The 1910 amendment made the injured employee's right of action for pain and suffering survive to his personal representatives for the benefit of the surviving widow or husband and children, or, failing these, parents or dependent next of kin, "but in such cases there shall be only one recovery for the same injury." This forbids multiple suits and multiple recoveries, not a single suit covering both elements of damage. Since the decedent had brought no prior action and the plaintiff sought only one recovery, no election between causes of action was required.

3. **Safety Appliance Act — car still in interstate commerce use.** The car, loaded with coal at Huntington, Arkansas and consigned to Texas, was found in Oklahoma with draw-bar, coupling, draft timbers and head-block broken off, and was hauled fourteen miles to Fort Smith for heavy repairs. Because it was awaiting repair and was being moved about the yards where employees handled trains, it remained in use for interstate commerce purposes. The statute imposes an absolute duty to keep cars properly equipped; the 1910 amendment removing the criminal penalty for hauling a defective car to the nearest repair point expressly leaves the carrier at "the sole risk" and does not relieve civil liability for injury to employees. The missing equipment was the direct cause of death, since a sound coupling would have coupled the car to the engine or bumped it aside without injury, notwithstanding the collision.

4. **Testimony of the widow.** Allowing the plaintiff, as administratrix and widow, to testify to the amounts of the deceased's contributions did not violate section 2 of Schedule 2 of the 1874 Constitution, following *St. Louis & SF Rd. Co. v. Fithian*, 106 Ark. 491, and *United States v. Clark*, 96 U.S. 37, because such testimony concerned only the amount of damages and was collateral to the main issue of the defendant's liability.

The dollar began the week at three-week highs as New York Fed President William Dudley said the Fed might pause rate hikes while shrinking its $4.5 trillion bond portfolio, supporting Treasury yields and the dollar’s appeal. It rose 0.3% to 111.43 yen, though speculative net-long dollar positions fell to a five-week low. The euro slipped amid uncertainty in the tightening French presidential race. U.S. March job growth missed forecasts, but unemployment fell to 4.5%, indicating continued labor-market strength. Geopolitical tensions involving Syria and North Korea supported safe-haven demand for the yen.

For continuous-wave interferometry with pair squeezed-state inputs, the passage derives a spectral quantum Cramér–Rao bound for time-dependent phase estimation. Without losses, the bound is \(1/[n(n+2)(\Delta\Omega/\pi)]\), where \(n\) is photon flux per frequency mode and \(\Delta\Omega\) is the squeezing bandwidth. It yields Heisenberg scaling, \(\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}}\sim1/n\), for \(n\gg2\). The bound is attainable using a nonlinear estimator applied to two homodyne records: the difference of their squared, bandwidth-filtered values estimates the phase. At mid-fringe with quadrature-tuned homodyne detectors, the outputs are zero-mean Gaussian processes whose variances oscillate at the signal frequency; rectification recovers that frequency because the rectified mean is linear in phase. A linearized maximum-likelihood estimator and its power spectral density are also analyzed.

The Rubber Band trading strategy is a contrarian, mean-reversion approach for stocks that seeks overbought or oversold conditions likely to revert toward the average. It can use Keltner Channels, Bollinger Bands, or momentum oscillators, encouraging buying during excessive pessimism and selling during market euphoria.

Using a 20-period Keltner Channel with a 10-period ATR, a buy setup occurs when a price bar opens and closes below the lower band, potentially confirmed by a hammer or inside bar. The profit target is the middle band or just below the upper band. A sell setup occurs above the upper band, potentially confirmed by a shooting star or inside bar, targeting the middle band or just above the lower band. Backtesting is advised.

An XLP example with nearly ten years of out-of-sample data produced 328 trades, a 0.45% average gain per trade, 6.1% CAGR, 20% market exposure, a profit factor of 2, and a 16% maximum drawdown. The strategy mainly applies to stocks; gold and commodities are described as more difficult to trade with such systems.

Chronic hepatitis C is an inflammatory liver disease that can progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma and is associated with extrahepatic disorders and increased type 2 diabetes risk. Although the prognostic value of the prognostic nutrition index (PNI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) is established in other cancers, their relationship with clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis complicated by type 2 diabetes remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate their prognostic value in these patients.

The study included 56 patients with chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis and type 2 diabetes, 85 with chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis alone, and 85 with type 2 diabetes alone, treated at Fu Yang Second People’s Hospital from January 2018 to December 2021. After six months of treatment, the cirrhosis-plus-diabetes group was classified into poor prognosis (23 cases) and good prognosis (33 cases). Cirrhosis was diagnosed using laboratory parameters and liver histopathology according to clinical standards. Admission blood data were analyzed to calculate NLR, PNI, and PLR from blood counts and serum albumin. The study received ethics approval and written informed consent.

UK university staff entered a fourth week of strikes over defined-benefit pension changes, with exams expected to be affected. Talks between Universities UK and UCU have failed, prompting 14 more strike days between April and June. UCU says it remains committed to a settlement. Edinburgh was criticised for using recorded lectures during the strike.

Using Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data, the study evaluated whether plasma biomarkers combined with other non-invasive measures could predict domain-specific cognitive decline and progression to dementia. Two cohorts were analyzed: 625 participants with plasma neurofilament light (NfL) and p-tau181, and a 393-participant subset that also had Aβ42/40. Participants included cognitively normal, subjective memory concern, early MCI, and late MCI groups with at least two years of follow-up.

A nested, stratified 10-fold cross-validation framework was used. Ridge linear regression derived an MRI score from regional brain volumes and cortical thickness, after which random forest regression combined this score with demographics, APOE4, baseline cognitive scores, and plasma biomarkers. Basic, plasma, MRI, and combined models were evaluated for rates of decline in memory, executive function, language, and visuospatial functioning.

For memory decline in Cohort 1, the average correlation increased from 0.38 in the basic model to 0.45 with plasma biomarkers, 0.46 with MRI, and 0.50 with the combined model; plasma and MRI performance did not differ significantly. Biomarker additions generally did not significantly improve prediction for the other domains, except language, where the combined model outperformed the basic model (0.49 versus 0.43; p=0.005). Prediction was substantially harder in cognitively unimpaired than MCI participants: memory correlations were 0.17 versus 0.53, executive function 0.19 versus 0.46, and language 0.22 versus 0.52, while the smaller visuospatial difference was not significant.

The MRI score was the strongest predictor of memory decline. Baseline cognitive scores were strongest for executive, language, and visuospatial outcomes. NfL and p-tau181 were important for memory, executive function, and language, whereas Aβ42/40 had the lowest importance among plasma biomarkers. MRI and plasma measures contributed little to visuospatial prediction.

Memory-based predicted decline also distinguished progression risk. In Cohort 2, the combined model achieved concordance indices of 0.76 for progression to MCI or dementia in cognitively unimpaired participants and 0.79 for dementia progression in MCI participants, the highest among the models. The highest versus lowest memory-decline tertiles had hazard ratios of 33.12 and 29.45, respectively. Other cognitive domains showed weaker progression prediction, with memory being significant in cognitively unimpaired participants.

The findings support combining plasma biomarkers, MRI, and cognitive measures, particularly for memory decline and dementia progression, while highlighting difficulty predicting change in cognitively unimpaired individuals. Limitations include the focus on AD-specific biomarkers and an ADNI cohort weighted toward AD, which may limit generalizability to non-memory domains and other dementias.

A National Academy of Sciences and National Academy of Medicine report concludes that scientists should be permitted to edit heritable DNA only to prevent serious, strongly inherited diseases for which reasonable alternatives do not exist. Scientists must demonstrate that the targeted gene causes or strongly predisposes carriers to such a condition and weigh likely risks and benefits. Enhancement of traits such as strength, intelligence, or beauty should remain prohibited.

The report says germline editing is becoming realistic and warrants clinical trials under public scrutiny, including considerations of fairness, dignity, and scientific integrity, plus long-term monitoring of future generations. It calls for continued public debate and international oversight reflecting societal values.

CRISPR-Cas9 has made gene editing easier, more precise, and more accessible. Somatic editing could treat metabolic disorders, certain cancers, and other mutation-related diseases without changing the germline; a Chinese lung-cancer trial is underway, though its results are pending. Ethical reservations in the United States and Europe may disadvantage researchers elsewhere. The international 22-member panel noted that its review was partly funded by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency and the Food and Drug Administration.

During a May 21–27 Singapore police operation, eight women and 15 men were arrested for various offences, including Women’s Charter and gambling-related violations; about 700 people were checked and investigations continue.

Aiden Markram was named South Africa’s cricket captain after Faf du Plessis was ruled out with a finger injury. Markram called the role an honour, welcomed the added pressure and expects support from senior players. South Africa trail India 1-0 in the six-match series and seek an improved performance in Sunday’s second ODI.

Google expanded speech recognition with 30 new languages and locales, bringing total support to 119, including eight Indian languages, Swahili and Amharic. The additions are available in Gboard for Android, Voice Search and the Cloud Speech API, with support in products such as Google Translate planned. The expansion targets emerging markets, especially India and Africa. Google trained its models using native speakers reading common phrases and added emoji voice dictation for U.S. English users.

Saints begin their 2017/18 Anglo-Welsh Cup campaign away to champions Exeter Chiefs on November 4, revisiting their 15-8 loss in the 2014 final. They then host Dragons on November 11, visit Sale Sharks around January 26 and face Harlequins at home in early February. Grouped with Saracens, Scarlets and Worcester Warriors, Saints will face one team from another pool, with each pool winner advancing to the semi-finals.

The paper proposes a more cost-effective approach to soil-transmitted helminth (STH) impact assessment surveys (IAS), which estimate current prevalence and determine whether preventive chemotherapy should continue. WHO recommends suspending preventive chemotherapy when local prevalence of any STH is below 2%.

The proposed model-based geostatistical approach combines baseline prevalence data from geolocated schools, demographic and environmental risk factors, preventive chemotherapy coverage history, and available school locations. Baseline prevalence surfaces are modelled separately for each STH species using binomial mixed models that account for covariates, spatial correlation, and random effects. A five-class Markov model estimates changes in endemicity based on the number of effective chemotherapy rounds, defined as rounds achieving at least 75% coverage, while local thinning projects baseline prevalence forward to the anticipated survey date. Candidate survey designs vary the number of schools, participants per school, location inclusion probabilities, and minimum distance between schools. Designs are evaluated through simulation using sample-size reduction and accuracy of treatment decisions compared with classical random sampling.

The method was evaluated in Kenya, Sierra Leone, and Zimbabwe. Kenya’s longitudinal data were used to estimate transition probabilities, and actual IAS results served as a gold standard. Projected prevalence closely resembled the actual surface in Kenya but differed more in Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe, where endemicity levels differed substantially from Kenya’s. The geostatistical designs achieved the same accuracy as classical surveys with substantially smaller samples, reducing average survey costs by 80%, with reductions of 91% in Kenya, 86% in Zimbabwe, and 62% in Sierra Leone. The approach also produces detailed prevalence maps that may identify residual hotspots requiring further intervention or surveillance.

The paper introduces TeraAgent, a distributed simulation engine that extends BioDynaMo to scale agent-based models across multiple servers. It partitions simulation space by locality, exchanges boundary “aura” data, migrates agents across ranks, and supports global and diffusive load balancing. TeraAgent IO packs agents into contiguous buffers and enables received objects to be used and mutated directly, while delta encoding compares successive messages against shared references and transmits only differences. MPI hybrid and MPI-only modes, global agent identifiers, incremental neighbor-grid updates, and BioDynaMo integration allow simulations to move across laptops, workstations, clouds, and supercomputers with minimal user-facing changes.

Evaluations covering cell clustering, cell proliferation, epidemiology, oncology, and 180 automated tests produced results consistent with BioDynaMo. TeraAgent simulated 250 times more agents than BioDynaMo, achieved an eightfold higher agent update rate per CPU core than Biocellion, and improved in-situ ParaView visualization by 39 times. Median serialization and deserialization speedups were 110 and 37 times, while delta encoding reduced transferred data by up to 3.5 times. Extreme-scale runs reached 102.4 billion agents on 24,576 CPU cores and 501.51 billion agents on 84,096 cores, while additional compute nodes reduced time to result and improved third-party interoperability and hardware flexibility.

CoreLogic reported that U.S. home prices rose 7.1% year over year and 1.1% month over month in May 2018, with limited supply and low-rate mortgages constraining sales. Forty percent of the 100 largest metros were overvalued. Prices were forecast to rise 5.1% by May 2019, while renter demand remained strong.

The application describes a vehicle driver-monitoring and assistance system using exterior and interior cameras, vehicle controls, sensor data, and other contextual inputs to estimate driving workload, distraction workload, and driver attention. Attention is calculated relative to a maximum workload using adjustable weighting and calibration based on the driver, conditions, and observed behavior.

Inputs may include media use, steering behavior, gaze, facial expressions, posture, biometrics, road and weather conditions, traffic, and ADAS data. The system may also monitor passengers to avoid misclassifying passenger activities as driver distraction. It can detect exterior objects, alert the driver, highlight hazards on displayed images, and, when risk exceeds a threshold and the driver is not attentive, autonomously brake or steer to avoid a hazard. The disclosure also covers camera, radar, lidar, image-processing, driver-tracking, and vehicle-to-vehicle or infrastructure communication technologies.

Shonda Rhimes and Shondaland are moving to Netflix to create new shows, while “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Scandal” and “How to Get Away With Murder” will remain on ABC. Financial terms and the deal’s duration were not disclosed.

Alere said misstatements involving South Korean revenue recognition and one Japanese transaction made its 2013–2015 financial statements unreliable. It expects a $1 million timing adjustment, continuing control weaknesses, and may need more time to file its March-quarter Form 10-Q.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says five tests commonly ordered for short, overweight or early-pubertal children may be unnecessary when the child is otherwise healthy. Hormone and endocrine testing has limited value without clear abnormalities, while vitamin D, thyroid and ultrasound testing should be reserved for specific risk signs or findings.

Letters circulated by Grassroots Leadership describe detained women’s mistreatment and separation from their children. One anonymous woman detained with her 9- and 17-year-olds said they slept on floors under “aluminum paper” blankets in chain-link cages and that she could not bathe or brush her teeth for eight days. Her lawyer confirmed the separation and said the children were released to their father on June 19; the woman was released June 26.

Other women wrote letters expressing grief and longing to their children, including a Guatemalan mother whose 5-year-old son was in his father’s custody and Claudia, who said she had spoken with her son only three times. The accounts also describe infants crying from hunger and cold and pregnant women fainting.

Grassroots Leadership posted the letters while circulating a petition to reunite separated families. ICE could not address specific allegations because the writers’ identities and the facilities described were redacted or unclear.

This continuation application describes systems for displaying marker elements for virtual items in team-based virtual scenes. A terminal renders a virtual scene, receives marker indication information identifying an item marked by the user or a teammate, obtains and renders corresponding graphic data, and displays a marker near the target item. In a networked implementation, a terminal identifies the marked item, optionally selects a marker type, and sends the item’s identifier and marker type to a server. The server compares the target’s distance with each team member’s visible distance and sends marker information to qualifying terminals, which display markers directly in the scene. Markers may vary by type or color, show straight-line, horizontal, or height-difference information, appear on a thumbnail map, highlight obscured items, and be removed after preset durations. The application also discloses corresponding terminals, apparatus modules, computer devices, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media.

A Texas State University district court judge ordered history professor Thomas Alter to be reinstated without pay after his termination for allegedly inciting violence during a virtual socialism conference speech. Alter will not teach while the university reviews the case and his free-speech, due-process, and employment-contract lawsuit continues. The report also notes other terminated university faculty, including a South Dakota professor reinstated after posting comments about Charlie Kirk’s death.

Tesla Motors, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2016 reported unaudited financial results and had 149,891,190 common shares outstanding as of October 25, 2016. At September 30, cash and cash equivalents totaled $3.08 billion and total assets were $12.59 billion, compared with $1.20 billion and $8.07 billion at December 31, 2015. Third-quarter revenue was $2.30 billion, versus $936.8 million a year earlier; gross profit was $636.7 million, operating income was $85.6 million, and net income was $21.9 million, or $0.14 per diluted share. For the nine months, revenue was $4.72 billion and net loss was $553.6 million, compared with $2.83 billion and a $568.3 million loss in 2015. Operating cash flow for the period was $324.4 million, versus a $494.7 million outflow.

Tesla completed a May 2016 common-stock offering of 7,915,004 shares for approximately $1.7 billion in net proceeds. It also entered into an agreement on July 31, 2016, to acquire SolarCity through an exchange ratio of 0.110 Tesla shares for each SolarCity share, subject to closing conditions and stockholder approvals.

The company produced approximately 25,180 vehicles in the third quarter, including 10,450 Model X vehicles, a 37% increase from the second quarter. It targeted approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016, Model 3 volume production and deliveries in the second half of 2017, and total production of 500,000 vehicles in 2018. Third-quarter gross margin increased to 27.7% from 24.7%. Tesla continued expanding its sales, service and Supercharger networks and expected cell production at the Gigafactory to begin in the fourth quarter of 2016.

The filing described revenue recognition, resale-value guarantees, leasing, warranties, inventory valuation, stock compensation, debt and other accounting policies. A securities class action dismissed by the trial court remained on appeal. In October 2016, Tesla purchased 24.5 acres adjacent to its Fremont factory for $30.8 million for future manufacturing expansion.

Pairs trading is a market-neutral strategy that simultaneously buys one asset and shorts another, seeking profits as temporary price mispricing between two historically correlated assets converges. The price difference, or spread, may be traded in either direction. Pairs can include stocks, ETFs, futures, currencies, options, and other instruments, with examples such as KO/PEP, GM/F, MS/GS, and SPY/TLT.

Traders assess correlation and cointegration, analyze fundamentals, select pairs, and manage leverage and risk. Cointegration tests such as Johansen and Engle-Granger identify long-term relationships and potential mean-reverting opportunities. Pairs trading is a subset of statistical arbitrage, which generally covers non-structural inefficiencies across groups of assets, whereas pairs trading focuses on two correlated assets.

The strategy aims to profit whether the overall market rises, falls, or remains sideways, although differences in beta, leverage, and fundamentals mean it is not perfectly market-neutral or low-risk. Its potential advantages include uncorrelated portfolio returns and diversification across multiple pairs. However, pairs may diverge permanently as company fundamentals change, cointegration may fail outside historical samples, and sudden spread movements can create black-swan losses. Leverage, short-borrowing costs, commissions, slippage, hard-to-borrow securities, unstable correlations, and overconfidence after losses are additional risks.

Research cited in the passage reports annualized excess returns of up to 11% for simple self-financing pair portfolios and approximately 11%–15.92% for top-pair portfolios, subject to transaction costs and institutional effects. In backtests, a KO/PEP strategy that bought KO and shorted PEP when their ratio fell below 10 produced 113% from 2000 onward but no returns during the latest decade. A GS/MS strategy returned 187% over 310 trades from 2000 to March 2021, or 0.6% per trade before costs; changing the exit to RSI(2) above 75 raised the result to 275% over 286 trades, or 0.96% per trade. Bollinger Bands did not outperform the simple two-day RSI strategy. The KO/PEP and GS/MS backtests still underperformed buying and holding the S&P 500 and required leverage, though their smoother equity curves may produce higher Sharpe ratios.

The author traded pairs intraday from 2001 to 2005 and notes that specialist price improvements are now unlikely, while profitable pair traders still exist. Pairs trading remains used by hedge and proprietary traders, but its easy opportunities have largely been arbitraged away, profitability has diminished, and returns increasingly carry black-swan risk. Understanding earnings, return on invested capital, leverage, and pair fundamentals remains important.

Researchers at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology analyzed blood samples from 40 people with ALS and 28 controls, finding stronger T-cell responses to the neuron-associated protein C9orf72 in ALS patients. Patients with C9orf72 mutations had stronger responses, and those whose immune cells produced more IL-10, an anti-inflammatory signal, were predicted to survive longer. The findings suggest an autoimmune component to ALS and could support future immune-system monitoring or anti-inflammatory treatments, but researchers caution that they do not establish ALS as an autoimmune disease or prove that self-reactive T cells drive its progression. Larger studies, improved methods for isolating autoreactive cells, and animal models are planned to investigate causation.

Investing.com highlights AMD’s rise after an AI-chip deal with OpenAI, a scenario in which Evercore’s Emanuel sees the S&P 500 reaching 9,000 in 2026, and gold moving above $3,900/oz amid yen weakness and U.S. rate-cut bets. A technical review says the S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, remaining in an uptrend, though early-August weakness and overbought, declining breadth signal short-term risks. Volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, investors are increasing tech exposure, and U.S. electricity demand reached a record. The page also promotes AI-selected stock strategies, discusses market topics, and provides trading-risk, data-accuracy, copyright, and advertising disclosures.

Cryptocurrency-related crime is rising in Japan despite a decline in overall reported crime. The Jan. 26 theft of 523 million NEM coins from Coincheck, valued by the company at ¥58 billion, highlighted security concerns after the FSA had warned the exchange about customer-asset management. Other risks include ransomware demanding payment in cryptocurrency, alleged fraud involving the Ripple exchange, and poorly regulated initial coin offerings (ICOs). The FSA warned that ICO token prices can fluctuate sharply or lose all value and that fraudulent schemes pose significant risks. Facebook banned ICO advertisements, while the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission halted an allegedly fraudulent ICO that had raised nearly $600 million. Japan remains a major center for cryptocurrency trading, with more than 30 percent of global bitcoin volume conducted in yen, but regulators have yet to establish clear rules for ICOs, leaving consumers to proceed at their own risk.

The Ontario Liberals’ pre-election report recommends eliminating EQAO tests for Grade 3 and Grade 9 students, removing mandatory high-school literacy tests and weakening Grade 6 and Grade 9 assessments, while shifting more responsibility for evaluation to teachers. Education Minister Indira Naidoo-Harris delayed action on the report’s 18 recommendations until after the June 7 election, pending further consultation; the independent testing agency was not consulted during the review. The article criticizes the changes as pre-election pandering and says they could reduce accountability and delay identification of students’ reading and math difficulties. It acknowledges the report calls for reviewing EQAO testing and making assessments more accessible to First Nations students. EQAO chairman Dave Cooke said further consultation was needed and warned that eliminating primary-division assessments would remove half the independent data available for elementary-school improvement. Under the proposal, students would receive no provincewide testing until Grade 6, and the report suggests school results should not be used to rank schools. The government previously denied plans to scrap Grade 3 testing and mandatory literacy requirements.

Auswide Bank originated from mergers of local building societies in Queensland’s Wide Bay Burnett region, later expanding into Sydney and Melbourne. It listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in 1994 and converted from a building society to a bank in 2015. Its mission emphasizes customer-centered banking and the “power of small.” As of June 30, 2020, it reported AUD3.789 billion in assets, AUD3.206 billion in loans and advances, AUD3.019 billion in deposits and short-term borrowings, AUD70.5 million in net interest revenue, AUD18.5 million in net profit after tax, and AUD13.6 million in dividends. Its 2020 cash flow statement showed operating inflows of AUD7.168 million, investing outflows of AUD183.959 million, financing inflows of AUD178.880 million, and ending cash of AUD106.478 million.

The case provides 15 representative transactions for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2021. These include a common-share issue, a three-year AUD40 million borrowing at 0.25%, office-supply purchases on 60-day credit terms, an AUD700,000 cash purchase of furniture, deposit and withdrawal activity, new and repaid loans, loan interest received and deposit interest incurred, cash-paid employee and mortgage-broker expenses, sale of a loan for AUD850,000, a AUD12 million dividend, depreciation of AUD3 million, loan impairment expense of AUD8 million, and no goodwill impairment. Assignments ask students to record these transactions, prepare a June 30, 2021 balance sheet, and calculate fiscal 2021 net income and cash flow, ignoring taxes.

The article examines the WEA Teacher Residency Program, the first union-led teacher preparation program in the United States, as an alternative pathway for special education certification in Washington state. The program was developed by the Washington Education Association and local districts to address special education teacher shortages, workforce diversity gaps, and barriers faced by underrepresented candidates.

An exploratory case study investigated the program during the 2023–24 academic year. Data came from a needs assessment, document analysis, interviews with residents, mentors, coaches, and instructors, and observations in three districts hosting residents. Sixteen residents participated in the 18-month program, including candidates with emergency substitute credentials, paraprofessional experience, disabilities, and multilingual or diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds.

The program incorporated evidence-based training centered on cultural competence, equity, inclusion, family engagement, Universal Design for Learning, and Washington academic and special education standards. Residents completed coursework through a flexible Hyflex model, four nine-week field placements, competency-based assessments, and sustained mentoring and coaching. Mentors received extensive preparation, while senior faculty coaches provided regular guidance and helped shape the curriculum. Residents also used AI-based Mursion simulations with virtual students with disabilities, Jamboard and speech-generation tools, and assistive or instructional technologies in classrooms.

Residents received a living wage, health insurance, four placements, and mentor and coach support in exchange for a three-year commitment to the placement district after licensure. Funding was shared among WEA, districts, and state grants. The study found that the program combined comprehensive preparation, diverse recruitment, technology integration, and financial incentives, potentially supporting a more representative special education workforce.

Limitations include the short study period, small sample, and uncertain scalability and sustainability. Persistence, certification, and teacher-retention rates could not yet be calculated. The authors recommend longitudinal research, comparisons with traditional certification pathways, and continued evaluation and adaptation.

Motivate launched 250 black Ford GoBike Plus e-bikes at stations across western San Francisco. Their electric pedal assist appears to kick in after the second or third pedal revolution, easing steep climbs and potentially attracting more riders. CEO Jay Walder said the average GoBike trip is about two miles and hopes e-bikes will encourage three-to-five-mile trips. The regional program, sponsored by Ford, has 3,600 bikes at 287 stations in five Bay Area cities. Only San Francisco currently offers e-bikes, and no expansion schedule has been announced. Motivate stressed its coordination with cities over station placement, contrasting the program with the sudden arrival of scooters.

Henrik Lundqvist said his team has not been outplayed and can still turn the series around, despite allowing three or more goals in a loss. He felt he was in position and tracking the puck well but needs to raise his level and match the opposing goalie’s strong performances. The team must accept its disappointment, avoid self-pity, and focus on the next game, starting with the first period and the process of stopping the next shot. Lundqvist believes creating traffic, getting players in front of the net, and finding loose pucks can make the opposing goalie’s job tougher. He chose to skate before the next game and rest the following morning to save energy.
The focus is on stopping opponents from scoring and winning two more games; records and media attention matter little, though prior experience and recognition help.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Health Secretary Abid Majeed directed provincial, district and union council committees headed by paediatricians to oversee the upcoming measles campaign, including technical and communication aspects. The campaign will vaccinate 4.3 million children aged nine to 59 months from October, emphasizing social mobilization, staff training, quality vaccines, logistics and AEFI referral systems.

Industrial enterprises face disruptive pressures that IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics can help address by enabling agile, virtual product and manufacturing development. HPC is becoming essential for complex simulations and modeling, while public cloud and HPCaaS offer alternatives to fully in-house infrastructure. Seamless integration of high-quality data across the product life cycle supports effective feedback loops, innovation, and new digital products, services, and business models.

IDC recommends establishing virtual development, creating process and life-cycle transparency, adopting a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, selecting an HPC operating model based on utilization, cost, performance, security, and skills, prioritizing scalable, secure, and energy-efficient solutions, and drawing on external expertise when needed.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology-related decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The Ayoub Sisters credit their Scottish music education— including specialist tuition, ensembles, and coaching—with their success as classical musicians. They say musical education benefits children generally, even those who do not become professional musicians.

Access to affordable music tuition varies across Scotland. Twenty-two local authorities charge for lessons, and some are cutting services. Renfrewshire is the only non-charging authority to have increased spending, while Clackmannanshire has doubled fees and West Lothian is consulting on cuts. Composer Duncan Chisholm argues that cost should not determine children’s access to music.

Campaigners backed by figures including Dame Evelyn Glennie, Nicola Benedetti, Paolo Nutini, and Patrick Doyle are lobbying for music education. Former Royal Conservatoire head John Wallace warns that council services could disappear if cuts continue, while the EIS reports that the number of music teachers has fallen from 1,100 to 640 over a decade. Scotland’s £1.6m Youth Music Initiative ensures primary pupils receive music tuition regardless of income, but Culture Secretary Fiona Hyslop said decisions on additional tuition rest with local councils and opposed charging for it.

Toy Lykins challenged the Aluminum Workers International Union’s use of his compulsory dues for purposes beyond collective bargaining, contract administration, and grievance adjustment, asserting violations of his First Amendment rights. The court denied the unions’ motion for summary judgment. It found a justiciable controversy because Lykins had paid an initiation fee and monthly dues and the unions had not provided an adequate accounting. His request for an accounting satisfied the relevant disclosure requirement, and he was not obligated to attend union meetings or exhaust other remedies.

The court held that an NLRA-authorized union-shop agreement constitutes governmental action. Nevertheless, it avoided a constitutional ruling by interpreting the NLRA to prohibit unions from compelling dissident employees’ dues to support political candidates or ideological causes against their wishes. Lykins’s general pleading sufficiently implied such an objection, though the precise expenditures and any refund required awaited factual development. The court also held that the expenditures could not violate his rights of free association because he had no right to avoid union membership beyond paying dues and fees if he wished to retain his job.

Jurisdiction was proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1337(a), and a later order eliminated the need to amend the jurisdictional allegation.

A Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found that more than one in four U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing support. Nearly two-thirds report insufficient teaching assistants, aides, paraprofessionals or behavior intervention specialists, while 62% report shortages of mental health resources or special educators. Resource access strongly affects job satisfaction: 77% of teachers with adequate resources are satisfied, compared with 44% of those without.

Teachers also reported inadequate classroom furniture (24%), laptops (25%) and printing supplies (35%). Funding and bureaucratic purchasing processes were identified as barriers. Despite these challenges, teachers expressed interest in professional development, although about half said it is not grounded in students’ needs and only one-third have opportunities to observe other teachers.

Staffing and technology shortages varied by school income. Teachers in wealthier schools were slightly more likely to report staffing shortages, while those in low-income schools were more likely to report inadequate laptops and printing resources.

A player describes joining Detroit after Chris Chelios praised him to Ken Holland, highlights the successful team and Stanley Cup, and says a second stint is easier to enjoy without controversy, though time passes quickly.

The lecture explains graphical implementations of causal discrete-time linear shift-invariant systems described by linear constant-coefficient difference equations. These equations express the current output as a linear combination of past outputs and delayed inputs and require three basic operations: delay, scalar multiplication, and addition. A first-order equation, \(y[n]=ay[n-1]+x[n]\), demonstrates the corresponding block-diagram representation using a \(z^{-1}\) delay element, a multiplier, and an adder.

Signal flow graphs provide an alternative notation. They consist of numbered nodes connected by directed branches, with source nodes providing inputs and sink nodes providing outputs. Each node variable equals the sum of its incoming branch outputs, while each linear branch output equals its input multiplied by a gain or function of \(z\). The example equation is redrawn as a signal flow graph, with the delay represented by a branch of gain \(z^{-1}\).

A flow graph corresponds to a set of linear equations and a matrix representation. The node-vector equation can be separated into immediate coefficient branches and delayed branches, yielding a time-domain formulation involving current and previous node states. This decomposes an \(n\)-th-order difference equation into coupled first-order equations.

Node ordering determines whether the network can be computed sequentially. A computable ordering has no nonzero coefficient-matrix entries on or above the main diagonal. Delay-free loops make a network non-computable in this sequential sense, although its equations may still be solved. Subsequent lectures will address common network structures for IIR recursive and FIR nonrecursive digital filters.

Ron Washington and interim manager Ray Montgomery will not return to the Los Angeles Angels for 2026, prompting a search for the franchise’s sixth manager in nine years. Washington, 74, missed most of 2025 after quadruple-bypass heart surgery but said the Angels declined his option based on their performance, not his health. The team finished 72-90 for its 10th consecutive losing season. Washington went 99-137 in two seasons and remains open to managing or coaching elsewhere; Albert Pujols and Torii Hunter are considered candidates for the Angels’ job.

Lord Aberdeen informed U.S. official Mr. Upshur on June 25, 1843, that Britain’s occupation of the Sandwich Islands was unauthorized and that an inquiry would follow. Aberdeen denied that Great Britain owed compensation and regarded Lord George Paulet’s seizure as not “forcible.” Tensions arose from American predominance amid British-French rivalry, French promotion of a rival religion, and Hawaiian pro-American sentiment. A Hawaiian embassy led by William Richards and Timoteo Haalilio sought international recognition. On December 19, 1842, Mr. Webster recognized the Hawaiian government’s independence, opposed foreign interference, and considered a formal treaty unnecessary. The President communicated the correspondence to Congress on December 30. On November 28, 1843, Britain and France agreed to consider the islands an independent state and never to take possession of Hawaiian territory, directly or under any other arrangement. The convention did not protect Hawaiian autonomy against third powers or express a principle equivalent to Webster’s declaration; it bound only Britain and France to recognize the islands and refrain from taking Hawaiian territory.
Manchester United lost 2-0 to Spurs, falling 15 points behind City, and face Huddersfield Town for Alexis Sanchez’s home debut; Mourinho will discuss Fellaini’s fitness and Pogba’s touchline issues.

The passage presents the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data center GPU built on the Ampere GA100 architecture and TSMC’s 7nm N7 process. Designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics, it extends the Tesla V100 with third-generation Tensor Cores, support for FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data, and fine-grained structured sparsity. TF32 operations are reported as up to 10 times faster than V100 FP32 FMA, while mixed-precision FP16/BF16 operations reach up to 16 times FP32 throughput and use sparsity for further gains. IEEE-compliant FP64 Tensor Core processing provides up to 2.5 times V100’s FP64 performance, and sparse INT8 is reported as up to 20 times faster than V100 INT8.

The A100 implementation has 108 Streaming Multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA Cores, and 432 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance. Its SMs contain 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copy instructions, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, warp-level reductions, and improved cache-management instructions.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, residency controls, and compute data compression. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s aggregate GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 offers 31.5 GB/s bandwidth and SR-IOV support. Multi-Instance GPU technology securely partitions an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances, improving utilization, quality of service, fault isolation, and multi-tenant security.

CUDA 11 advances include task graphs, asynchronous copy and barrier support, and mixed-precision solver capabilities. The cuSOLVER TCAIRS solver achieved a 2.0× geometric-mean speedup over the FP64 reference solver with TF32 and up to 4× on large complex matrices. A100-based DGX, HGX, and EGX systems use NVLink, NVSwitch, and Mellanox networking to scale across tens, hundreds, or thousands of GPUs. The passage also introduces 2:4 structured sparsity, which permits two nonzero values in every four-entry vector and can double Tensor Core throughput.

Elliott Management, holder of roughly 6% of NXP Semiconductors, valued NXP at $135 a share standalone, above Qualcomm’s $110 offer, and said the bid capped NXP’s valuation by exploiting depressed shares. Elliott hired UBS to analyze NXP; NXP traded at $116.30 premarket. Qualcomm rejected Broadcom’s $103 billion acquisition offer.

The Japan Society of Technology Education (JSTE) developed a new framework for technology and engineering education in response to the growing importance of STEM/STEAM education, the underestimated role of technology and engineering, and the need to connect curriculum reform in Japan with Society 5.0 and emerging digital technologies. Building on its influential “Technology Education in the 21st Century,” JSTE used annual Ideathons and conferences to develop and publish “The New Framework for Technology and Engineering Education to Create the Next Generation of Learning” (NGTE) in 2021.

Under Japan’s 2017 curriculum, junior high school Technology covers material processing, biological cultivation, energy conversion, and information technology, with objectives including technological governance and innovation. A survey of 1,656 students in Hyogo Prefecture found generally positive attitudes toward Technology classes, active and collaborative learning, and engagement in planning, design, project management, and troubleshooting. However, students showed limited exploration through inquiry, experimentation, and observation, weak connections between learning and social issues, and insufficient links between design problem-solving and technological innovation and governance. The study therefore identified greater exploratory activity and engineering-focused design learning as priorities.

NGTE distinguishes professional education for technological specialists from general education for technology and engineering literacy. It makes innovation and governance abilities the final goals of literacy education and connects them with scientific, creative, collaborative, critical, computational, and systems-thinking competencies at individual, social, and developmental levels. Its scope retains the four core technology areas while linking each to engineering science and adds “Technological Systems,” addressing AI, the Internet of Things, robotics, Big Data, and the integration of cyber and physical technologies.

The framework’s Triple-Loop Model of the Engineering Design Process consists of Needs Exploration, Seeds Exploration, and Creation. Students identify problems and users’ needs, investigate technological conditions and possible designs through methods such as prototyping and simulation, and then match needs and seeds to create optimized products or systems. NGTE also proposes a STEAM learning model centered on transdisciplinary engineering-based problem-solving, with design connecting science, mathematics, arts, and society through projects that create technological artifacts.

Evaluation by 90 JSTE participants generally supported NGTE: most proposal categories received mean agreement scores of at least 3.00 on a four-point scale. The definition of engineering received a lower score and greater variation, prompting its revision to include both engineering science and the engineering design process. The study concludes that the framework aligns with five established categories of technology-education curriculum design and illustrates a four-stage curriculum-development process: assessing current learning, interpreting it against future needs and social change, developing academic curriculum standards, and revising the national curriculum through collaboration between academic societies and MEXT. Future work will test the framework in classrooms and reform teacher education and training to support implementation.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Compensation Committee approved a new global performance-based restricted stock unit notice and agreement under its Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan on March 6, 2019. On March 8, the committee adopted the Fiscal Year 2020 Variable Compensation Plan, providing eligible executive officers variable cash payments based on achievement of specified revenue goals, with threshold, base, and stretch operating plan levels. Unless otherwise determined, participants must remain employees through the payment date.

Base-plan target awards were: Jen-Hsun Huang, $1.1 million (110% of base salary); Colette Kress, $300,000 (33%); Ajay Puri, $650,000 (68%); Debora Shoquist, $250,000 (29%); and Timothy Teter, $250,000 (29%). The restricted stock unit agreement and compensation plan were filed as Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2.

Garrison was convicted of first-degree rape in Tulsa County after a hung first jury trial and a second trial resulting in a thirty-year sentence. In the second stage of the two-stage proceeding, the court instructed the jury on punishment under 57 O.S.Supp.1969, § 138, which the court had previously held unconstitutional in Williams v. State. Although the erroneous instruction did not justify reversal, it prejudiced the sentence because the jury was led to believe good-time credits allowed him to serve thirty years in about fifteen; such credits depend on strict compliance with institutional rules and may be revoked at the Warden's discretion, and should not be considered by the jury in assessing punishment. The court therefore modified the sentence from thirty years to fifteen years and otherwise affirmed. Judges Brett and Bussey concurred.

On March 13, 2019, Tesla appointed Zachary Kirkhorn as CFO, succeeding Deepak Ahuja, and Vaibhav Taneja as Chief Accounting Officer. Kirkhorn will receive a $12 million stock option grant and $4 million restricted stock unit grant; Taneja will receive a $6 million stock option grant and $2 million restricted stock unit grant. Both grants vest over four years under Tesla’s standard equity policies.

Port Hardy Secondary School’s senior girls’ soccer team finished second at the Island Championships after defeating Duncan Christian 6–1, losing to top-ranked Glenlyon Norfolk 5–4, and beating second-ranked St. Andrews 3–1 in overtime. They fell 4–3 to Glenlyon Norfolk in the final, the only team to score against it all tournament. Their second-place finish qualified them for the BC Single A High School Provincials in Penticton, May 31–June 3.

The Republican presidential nominee accepts the party’s nomination with a pledge to serve the country and faithfully uphold the Constitution. He advocates representative government through the Republican Party, warning that personal or autocratic rule threatens constitutional government and popular liberty. He rejects the League of Nations and any world government that would surrender American sovereignty or delegate the right to wage war, while supporting international cooperation, peace, reduced armaments, and an association of nations based on justice and law.

Domestically, he calls for economic recovery through increased production, thrift, reduced waste, intelligent deflation, limited government borrowing, opposition to profiteering, and cooperation among labor, management, and capital. He supports collective bargaining while protecting individual rights, opposes government ownership of railroads, and urges private railway rehabilitation, federal highway cooperation, and improved water transportation. He also pledges support for agriculture, farmer cooperatives, irrigation, reclamation, Alaska’s development, protective tariffs, a merchant marine, adequate national defense, regulated immigration, housing, child-labor reform, anti-lynching measures, veterans’ assistance, and equal suffrage for women.

He condemns both concentrated executive power during war and political intolerance, while affirming free speech, press, and assembly and the right to suppress sedition or threats to lawful government. He calls for respectful relations with Mexico, honors the nation’s World War veterans, and expresses confidence that constitutional government and American national independence will endure.

A state audit found former Duquesne superintendent Barbara McDonnell and four employees made $41,000 in unauthorized no-interest loans, $22,000 for herself, as the district sat in state receivership. Auditor General DePasquale cited missing documentation for $1.3 million in transportation reimbursements, state overpayment of $180,000, and referred the case to the State Ethics Commission.

Maine’s self-employed lobstermen organized as Lobster 207, an International Association of Machinists local and cooperative business formed in 2013. Responding to depressed prices, regulatory pressures, and industry consolidation, IAM organizers helped lobstermen build collective political and economic power. By November 2017, the union represented about 550 lobstermen, including 250 in good standing.

Lobster 207 used IAM support to organize across Maine’s coast, testify before legislators, influence fishing regulations, protect lobstermen’s military-license status, oppose dredging and right-to-work legislation, and encourage members to hold public office. It then incorporated the Maine Lobstering Union as a statewide marketing cooperative, enabling members to collectively negotiate prices and share profits without violating antitrust laws.

In 2017, members voted to acquire the wholesale operations of the Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound for $4 million. The Bank of Labor provided about half the financing, unsecured loans from IAM locals covered roughly 25%, and the seller provided the remainder. The acquisition gave lobstermen access to an operating wholesale business, facilities, equipment, and established customers. The business increased purchases from 30 boats before the acquisition to 130 member boats afterward and expanded online and national marketing.

By 2016, the average price received by lobstermen statewide was 52% higher than in 2012, its highest level since 2006. However, the cooperative still faced challenges in managing wholesale operations, financing costs, expansion, and profit distribution, leaving its long-term economic impact uncertain.

Warren Buffett is reportedly considering Berkshire Hathaway’s roughly $10 billion purchase of Occidental Petroleum’s OxyChem unit, potentially its largest deal since the $11.6 billion Alleghany acquisition in 2022. Berkshire has a record $344 billion in cash. Buffett is set to remain chairman after stepping down as CEO at year-end.

The U.S. beat Panama 4-0 in World Cup qualifying, ending a three-match winless streak. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a 112-yard move in the eighth minute and assisted Jozy Altidore’s 19th-minute goal. Altidore added a chipped penalty in the 43rd, and Bobby Wood scored in the 63rd. With 12 points, the U.S. moved into third place, two points ahead of Panama and occupying the region’s last automatic World Cup berth. Pulisic, playing his first international match since turning 19, contributed to 11 of the U.S.’s 14 goals in the hexagonal.

A U.S. Department of State certification, signed by Secretary of State John Hay on September 1, 1900, authenticates documents filed with the department for Exhibits M, N, O, and H. Captain George O. Baker, a 58-year-old master mariner from Dartmouth, testified that he had sailed since 1848, served as master since 1863, and made about 15 voyages, including six in the Ochotsk and Japan seas. He described the Ochotsk whaling season as generally running from mid-August to mid-October, with September usually best. Rugged weather, chiefly from northerly and easterly winds, made continued whaling impractical by mid-October, though later catches had been reported. He estimated a typical season’s catch at six to ten whales. Returning from Vladivostok to the whaling grounds after October 1 would take eight to ten days and likely be useless, so he would proceed directly to San Francisco. Nine whales would yield about 10,000 pounds of bone and 900 barrels of oil. These were right whales, not bowheads.

The passage links grievances in the Declaration of Independence to contemporary politics, arguing that Trump’s deference to military leaders violates civilian control, his stance on immigration contradicts the founders’ views and the economic benefits of immigration, and his attacks on the Mueller investigation, Justice Department, and judges undermine judicial independence.

Joel Greenblatt’s Magic Formula is a quantitative stock-selection strategy popularized by *The Little Book That Beats the Market*. It ranks companies by return on invested capital (ROIC), which measures how effectively a company manages its capital, and earnings yield (EY), the inverse of the P/E ratio. The strategy seeks financially strong, undervalued companies that rank highly on both metrics. Investors can rank stocks by adding their ROIC and EY positions, select those with the lowest combined ranks, and invest either in an index fund tracking the selection or in individual stocks. Diversification, rebalancing, and performance monitoring are also recommended.

The passage reports that Greenblatt’s original backtest, covering 1988–2004 and the 3,500 largest U.S. companies, found that the top 30 stocks returned 30.8% annually versus 12.4% for the S&P 500 and outperformed in 14 of 17 years. Tests limited to the 2,500 and 1,000 largest companies produced annual returns of 23.7% and 22.9%, respectively. A separate 1999–2023 backtest reportedly more than doubled the S&P 500’s return with a higher risk-adjusted return but greater drawdown, alongside substantial underperformance from 2014 onward.

International academic studies cited in the passage found favorable results in Sweden, Finland, and Norway, including a thesis reporting annual returns of 15.8% for Greenblatt’s strategy from 1990 to 2010, compared with 7.7% for a passive index. However, critics cite lower or underperforming returns in recent research, a dependence on small-cap stocks, omitted transaction costs, limited theoretical grounding, and insufficient consideration of qualitative factors.

Key risks include selected stocks underperforming, value stocks lagging growth-oriented markets, changing market conditions, concentration by sector or industry, and historical results failing to predict future performance. Portfolio performance can be evaluated using total returns, alpha relative to a benchmark such as the S&P 500, and volatility. The passage concludes that the strategy is simple to implement and can serve as a useful portfolio tool, but it does not guarantee success and requires due diligence, diversification, and ongoing adjustment.
