This motivates probabilistic decoding techniques that exploit all available observations.

The lecture distinguishes orthogonal, simplex, and biorthogonal codes. Removing the mean from a binary orthogonal code produces a one-dimensional antipodal or simplex code. A biorthogonal code adds codewords formed by negating the ones in an orthogonal code; rotating its binary constellation by 45 degrees produces two PAM sets equivalent to 4QAM. A set of codewords and a signal set are essentially the same structure, depending on whether coding and modulation are treated separately or jointly.

Exact error analysis becomes more difficult for three or more dimensions because the error regions are no longer orthogonal. Scaled orthogonal and simplex codes have the same error probability, while simplex coding saves an energy factor of \(1-1/m\). Orthogonal signals remain useful because their mean facilitates frequency and phase recovery, and the energy penalty is small for large alphabets. In the binary case, biorthogonal signaling has the same average energy as its orthogonal counterpart but nearly doubles the error probability.

For large orthogonal signal sets, a refined union-bound calculation conditions on the received component along the transmitted codeword and bounds the remaining independent noise components. The resulting error probability decreases exponentially with the number of transmitted bits. For the white Gaussian channel with unrestricted bandwidth, the analysis identifies the capacity condition \(E_b/N_0=\ln 2\), providing the essence of Shannon’s channel-capacity result.

The lecture then turns to wireless communication. Unlike wired links, wireless systems involve radiated electromagnetic waves, time-varying channels, attenuation, fading, Doppler shift, interference among users, and multiple transmitters and receivers. Cellular networks use moving mobiles, fixed base stations, and mobile telephone switching offices connected to a wired backbone. Simplified diagrams depict uniform hexagonal cells, but actual base-station placement depends on real estate, coverage, and electromagnetic modeling. Selecting a base station, locating a mobile, and routing calls are organizational network problems rather than the physical communication focus of the course.

Wireless terminology calls the mobile-to-base-station direction the reverse channel, corresponding to a multiple-access channel, and the base-station-to-mobile direction the forward channel, corresponding to a broadcast channel that sends separate, private messages. Voice is delay-sensitive, whereas data can tolerate substantial delay and therefore permits different transmission techniques.

Most wireless systems are narrowband, using bandwidths of kilohertz to megahertz and carriers in the gigahertz range; a wideband system instead uses bandwidth that is a significant fraction of its carrier frequency. Physical channel models must account for how rapidly the channel changes, how its behavior depends on frequency, and when different frequencies appear sufficiently decorrelated. The lecture concludes by previewing idealized point-source and reflected-path models for studying these effects.

Nursery school headteachers warned Education Ministers that funding cuts introduced in 2017 could force many schools to close. The Department for Education provided £60 million annually until 2019-20, but continuation after 2020 is not guaranteed. Heads said repeated budget reductions led to staff cuts, while business rates, wages, pension contributions and special-needs funding increased. They asked the government to confirm continued support in the autumn spending review.

Only 400 council-funded nursery schools remain open in England, providing about 30,000 places; more than 60% serve deprived areas. Children and Families Minister Nadhim Zahawi defended existing funding and childcare support, while urging councils not to make premature closure decisions. Conservative MPs Robert Halfon and Craig Tracey said nurseries needed certainty, warning that closures would particularly harm disadvantaged children and those with disabilities or medical needs.

The article strongly recommends Exxon Mobil as a contrarian buy, citing its 4.1% dividend yield, 20% year-over-year cash-flow growth, low price-to-cash-flow valuation, and trading below 16 times forward earnings. It expects earnings to double by 2025 and suggests further dividend increases in April. The author argues that stabilization in crude oil and natural gas indicates the broader post-2008 decline in WTI may be ending, potentially benefiting Exxon through improved sector momentum. Technically, XOM is near a double-bottom and head-and-shoulders neckline around $71.60, with the broader trading range spanning $56.50 to $103.80. Improved energy prospects, weaker technical levels, and the elevated dividend are expected to support a bull rally in the first half of the year. The author discloses being long XOM.

Stefon Diggs starred for the Patriots against his former team, the Bills, recording 10 catches for 146 yards and 61 yards after the catch. His consecutive 100-yard receiving games matched Julian Edelman’s Patriots record, and the victory gave Diggs the last laugh in his first matchup with Buffalo.

TopoSPAM unifies simulations across biological scales, offering active/passive intracellular models, tissue-scale vertex and coarse-grained morphogenesis models, and an HPC framework with interactive visualization.

This patent application (a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 17/013,035, itself continuing U.S. Pat. No. 10,805,736, claiming priority to Korean Patent Applications Nos. 10-2019-0037499 and 10-2018-0096924) discloses a display apparatus including a flexible vibration module and a method of manufacturing the module.

Background: A display apparatus normally needs a separate speaker, which occupies space and limits design; actuator-type speakers are thick, while piezoelectric elements, though thin, are fragile and easily damaged by impact, lowering sound reproduction reliability.

Summary of the disclosure: A flexible vibration module is attached (via an adhesive member that may include a hollow portion/air gap) to the rear surface of a display panel, and vibrates the panel to produce sound and/or haptic feedback. The module comprises a piezoelectric composite layer (PCL) with alternating, coplanar first portions (inorganic, piezoelectric material portions, e.g., perovskite piezoelectric ceramics such as PZT/PZNN/CaTiO₃) and second portions (flexible organic material portions, e.g., PVDF, PVDF-TrFE, or epoxy/acryl/silicon-based non-piezoelectric polymers, optionally with a reinforcing agent). The organic portions fill gaps between, and connect to, the inorganic portions, absorbing impact, relieving stress, and providing flexibility so the module can bend with the panel. The PCL is sandwiched between first and second electrode layers (ITO, IZO, or opaque metals such as Al, Cu, Au, Ag, Mo, Mg) and covered by protection films (PI or PET).

Disclosed embodiments vary the PCL pattern: equal-width line/stripe portions (first embodiment); enlarged first portions to improve high-pitched response (second); enlarged first and second portions for low/mid-pitched response and flatter sound pressure (third); second portions progressively smaller toward the edges to reduce low-band sound-pressure dipping (fourth); circular/dotted first portions for 2D/3D shapes (fifth); and triangular first portions forming 2N-angular shapes (sixth). Another embodiment provides a bimorph stack of two composite layers separated by an insulation layer with four electrode layers, increasing expansive/contractile force and sound pressure. A further embodiment places first and second vibration modules in left/right regions of the panel with partition members (first through fifth) and air gaps AG1–AG3 to separate left and right sounds for two-channel stereo output; the size of the fourth/fifth partitions sets the vibration region, with larger sizes enhancing low-pitched and smaller sizes enhancing high-pitched characteristics.

The display apparatus may include a TFT array substrate, light-emitting device layer, encapsulation substrate, display and non-display areas, bending portions, a rear structure (cover bottom/plate/metal frame), panel fixing member, and an optional front structure that may be omitted to reduce bezel width. Panel types include LCD, OLED, QD-LED, microLED, and electrophoresis panels; the module may be applied to curved, rollable, bendable, and flexible displays.

Manufacturing method: form a piezoelectric composite of inorganic material portions and organic material portions connected between them from an inorganic mother substrate and a flexible organic material; form first and second electrode layers on opposite surfaces of the composite; apply voltage to polarize the inorganic portions in a temperature atmosphere; and form protection films on the electrode layers. Drawings also report experimental sound-pressure results comparing embodiments against a film-speaker comparative example.
Oklahoma received approval to seek rebates from drugmakers when medicines fail as claimed. Participation is voluntary; talks involve 20 companies, with 10 in active negotiations.

Mega Geometry maps subdivision-surface tessellation directly to GPU-driven cluster generation, enabling rapid BVH construction and reducing costly per-frame rebuilds during animations or viewpoint changes. This supports real-time ray tracing of smoothly rendered, quad-based surfaces with displacement.

Kalidou Koulibaly scored a stoppage-time header as Napoli beat Juventus in Turin, cutting the Serie A leaders’ advantage to one point with four games remaining. Napoli’s late win kept their Scudetto hopes alive, while Juventus lost Giorgio Chiellini to injury and face Inter and Roma in their remaining fixtures.

Some Prince Edward Island parents are concerned about inconsistent school supply costs. Cornwall parent Jerica Devos spent about $70 on supplies for her six-year-old son, Jace, and said it is unfair that families must spend more depending on their school. Westwood Primary’s list specifies brands and colours, which she believes should not be required when parents buy their own supplies.

P.E.I. Public Schools Branch guidelines cap school-collected supply fees at $40 and allow parents to opt out and purchase supplies themselves. However, schools without a flat-fee option offer no such alternative. Devos wants parents to be able to volunteer for a flat fee. Branch director Parker Grimmer welcomed feedback and said the issue may prompt a review of the process.

The bullish engulfing pattern is a two-candlestick bullish reversal pattern formed after a downward price swing: a small bearish candle is completely engulfed by a larger bullish candle. It often appears near support and is considered more reliable after a 61.8% Fibonacci pullback in an uptrend, indicating that bullish momentum may be taking control.

A potential trade setup should be evaluated alongside broader market conditions, support and resistance, volume changes, and confirmation such as a follow-through day or another bullish pattern. Trading plans should define entry and exit criteria, including profit targets, stop losses, or an opposite signal, while managing both winning and losing trades.

The passage recommends backtesting all trading ideas by establishing precise rules, using historical price data, simulating trades, and evaluating performance. It also identifies benefits including a reversal signal, confirmation of a trend change, identification of key price levels, and support for risk management.

VentureWire’s December 7, 2000 issue reports that Providence Equity Partners closed a $2.8 billion fund, Insight Capital Partners is raising a $750 million fund, and Caspian Networks raised $85 million in a third round. Technologic Partners named ten Investors’ Choice companies. Numerous financing rounds are covered, including PacketVideo’s planned $80–100 million Series E and rounds at GiantBear, Advent Networks, InfoMedics, Quidnunc and others. The “bad news” section covers HarvardNet cutting 280 jobs and ending DSL operations, Exp.com cutting 15% of staff, @Viso ending planned Diamond.com funding, divine interVentures withdrawing a $10 million commitment, and CarsDirect.com canceling its IPO. Other sections cover new products, a Brightstar-IncuVest alliance, four acquisitions, multiple board and executive appointments, Optical Capital Group’s new San Francisco office, and corrections to prior VentureWire reports. The newsletter also features the First Tuesday event and promotes the Optix 2001 optical-communications conference.

Disability activist research found that only eight of Scotland’s 32 councils had created or planned Section 167 wheelchair-accessible taxi lists by the government’s recommended October deadline. The Equality Act allows fines of up to £1,000 for registered drivers who refuse wheelchair users or charge extra, but protections only apply where such lists exist. Across England, Scotland and Wales, 11% of councils had created lists, 30% intended to do so, and 59% had no firm plans. The research also found that two-fifths had fewer than 10% accessible taxis, 15 had none, and only 30% required disability-awareness training. Activists called for councils to implement lists urgently.

At a March 21, 2018 special meeting, Tesla stockholders approved Elon Musk’s performance-based stock option award, granted January 21, 2018. The award met NASDAQ, Tesla bylaws, and disinterested-stockholder approval standards, receiving approximately 81%, 80%, and 73% support, respectively. Votes were 96,795,092 for and 23,407,632 against under the NASDAQ standard, and 63,014,339 for under the disinterested-stockholder standard.

In a prospective cohort study, 264 adults hospitalized with RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 underwent standardized 12-zone lung ultrasound. Researchers calculated a mean lung ultrasound score (mLUSS, 0–3) using available zones, allowing incomplete scans, and assessed progression to ICU-level respiratory support, ventilation, and 28-day mortality.

Baseline mLUSS increased with clinical severity and showed good inter-reader agreement (r=0.77). Each one-point mLUSS increase was associated with progression to ICU-level care (adjusted HR 3.61, 95% CI 1.27–10.22) and 28-day mortality (adjusted HR 3.10, 95% CI 1.29–7.50), but not the composite of ventilation or death. Findings persisted after adjustments for available zones, symptom duration, and exclusion of asymptomatic participants. More A lines were associated with lower risks of ICU-level care and death, while B lines, pleural abnormalities, consolidations, and effusions generally showed increased risks, though not all estimates were statistically significant. Overall, individual LUS findings and mLUSS were associated with subsequent oxygen requirements or death independent of illness duration, supporting LUS for prognosis and triage.

An international team led by Senckenberg (Germany) and the University of Vienna, with UCL's Tim Blackburn, reports in Nature Communications (2017) that alien species numbers have risen continuously worldwide over the last 200 years, with no sign of saturation. Analysing over 45,000 first records of more than 16,000 alien species from a database built by 45 scientists, the team found 37% of introductions occurred between 1970 and 2014, peaking in 1996 with 585 new species. Rates rose in all taxonomic groups, though the authors note figures underestimate the true scale and that existing prevention policies have not kept pace with globalisation, urging more effective measures.

On December 14, 2000, Todd Kimberlain forwarded to V. Charles Weldon an email from Jack Beven containing National Hurricane Center data from Jim Gross. Gross found a file of watch and warning areas for the continental United States from 1963–1998, constructed by Mark Demaria and assumed complete. The file lists dates and times, storm names and IDs, warning counts, geographic segment pairs, and warning types ranging from tropical-storm watches to hurricane warnings. The segment direction is arbitrary, and the extensive records run from Hurricane Cindy in 1963 through Hurricane Mitch in 1998.

Research cited on NPR says maintaining a 5% weight loss requires 10% fewer calories, possibly explaining regained weight. The column also presents dMeetings, a self-paced diabetes education program with certified educators.

A Providence community health system evaluated pathologist-directed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) using a standardized 523-gene DNA/RNA assay at diagnosis for advanced solid tumors from September 2019 to November 2021. Testing was free to 3,216 patients, and 1,482 had documented treatment and follow-up data for outcome analyses.

OncoKB-based assessment found guideline-actionable biomarkers in 49% of cases. CGP identified basket-trial eligibility in 53% of patients, compared with 26% using a simulated 50-gene panel; 67% had actionable alterations by guideline or trial criteria, versus 33% with the smaller panel. Among patients with relevant biomarkers, 59% received matched targeted therapy, and 63% received immunotherapy with or without chemotherapy.

Biomarker-guided targeted therapy was associated with longer median overall survival than chemotherapy alone across tumor types (25 vs. 17 months; age- and tumor-adjusted HR 0.66). Among non-small-cell lung cancer patients, median survival was 26 versus 16 months, with an age-adjusted HR of 0.55.

The findings support pathologist-directed, comprehensive testing for broader treatment and trial matching than legacy small panels. Remaining barriers include incomplete actionable findings, clinician adoption and education, treatment costs, payer coverage, staffing, and unequal access to precision therapies.

The Legion Go S with SteamOS is $120 off, making it an affordable Steam Deck alternative for travelers and couch gamers. SteamOS provides smoother setup and game optimization than Windows on the handheld. The device is bulky but comfortable, with built-in grips, well-placed controls, a bright 120-Hz IPS screen, 1 TB storage, 32 GB memory, and a MicroSD slot. It performs well with minimal settings adjustments.

Mercedes is offering a limited “Grand Edition” of the seven-seat GLS 500 4MATIC as competition grows from Range Rover and Volvo and BMW prepares the X7. It adds 20-inch wheels, badges, a nappa-leather dashboard, unique wood trim and exclusive brown quilted upholstery. The package is available across non-AMG GLS models as an €8,250 upgrade, with deliveries from March 2018.

George Washington, President of the United States, states that he first delayed mobilizing the militia, hoping opposition to the Constitution and laws in certain western Pennsylvania counties would yield to time and reflection. Because offers of forgiveness conditioned only on submission to law and other conciliatory measures have failed, violence continues, and government is being defied, he resolves, relying on Providence, to restore lawful subordination. A force summoned from New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Virginia is moving toward the affected area. He assures those relying on government protection that U.S. arms will provide it and says qualifying offenders who submit will receive good-faith lenity. Washington exhorts citizens and officers to oppose measures and misinformation leading to insurrection and to defend the Constitution, laws, and stable government. He warns that anyone aiding the insurgents will answer at their peril and requires offenders to be brought before the law.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K current report under Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, dated April 26, 2022. The company, headquartered at One Microsoft Way, Redmond, Washington, has registered securities on NASDAQ: common stock ($0.00000625 par value) and 3.125% notes due 2028 and 2.625% notes due 2033, all trading under MSFT. Under Item 2.02, Microsoft announced via a press release its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2022, furnished as Exhibit 99.1; the report states this information is not deemed "filed" for Section 18 purposes and is not incorporated by reference absent specific reference. Exhibits include the April 26, 2022 press release and the cover page interactive data file. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Ukrainian authorities staged the reported killing of Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko, who appeared alive at a press conference after police said he had been shot. The Security Service said a Ukrainian recruited and paid $40,000 by Russian intelligence hired a former separatist fighter to carry out the attack. Babchenko, a prominent Kremlin critic, had fled Russia in 2017 after threats and continued receiving intimidation while living and working in Kyiv.

The Czech central bank likely will raise interest rates once more in 2018 after three increases since August, though policymakers see no need for an immediate move. The repo rate is 0.75%, with the bank forecasting another increase around year-end or early 2019. Inflation has slowed, the crown has weakened less than expected, and forecast risks appear slightly anti-inflationary, though one policymaker sees upside risks.

FoLix is an FDA-cleared, noninvasive fractional laser treatment that stimulates existing hair follicles through the body’s healing response. Sessions take 20–30 minutes, require no anesthesia, and have little downtime, but typically require three to six treatments during the first year and maintenance thereafter. Costs range from $750 to $1,250 per session. The treatment is intended for early to moderate hair loss with intact follicles, is not suited to complete baldness or extensive scarring, and may cause temporary redness, tightness, sensitivity, or shedding.

The court upheld an award, reduced after defendants’ post-trial motion, as reasonable compensation for an infant with Erb’s palsy and declined to restore the original future pain-and-suffering amount.

Protesters gathered against hatred and racism after deadly violence at a Virginia white supremacist rally, with demonstrations in San Francisco, Seattle, Denver and New York and a vigil in Charlottesville.

The team expresses confidence in both goaltenders, who have performed well under pressure. Despite creating chances, the players must persist, execute better, and support their goaltender rather than be discouraged by bad bounces or outside criticism. Although more physical play may be needed, they must remain disciplined against a skilled opponent that moves the puck well.

This qualitative case study examined COVID-19-era distance education for seven visually impaired undergraduate and graduate music students in Turkey. Data were collected through semi-structured telephone interviews and analyzed thematically.

Although most courses were taught synchronously, participants also used recorded lessons and independent devices. Course materials rarely accommodated visual impairments, forcing students to rely on large print, parental assistance, friends, or other support. Assessment methods varied; individual arrangements were provided in some cases, but written theoretical examinations remained difficult.

Reported strengths included flexibility in time and place and, for some students, greater social acceptance. Weaknesses included unreliable technical infrastructure, poor audio synchronization and transmission, difficulty singing and playing simultaneously, insufficient teacher technology skills, inaccessible interfaces, and compressed lesson content. Students recommended longer lessons, text-to-audio and screen-readable notation, Braille resources, adjustable text, accessible platforms and interfaces, regular technical assistance, prompt problem resolution, alternative communication options, and more constructive teacher attitudes. The study concludes that distance education was particularly difficult for visually impaired music students because systems and materials were generally designed without their needs; accessible materials, assistive technologies, tailored support, and collaboration with students and support personnel were recommended.

At the Palm Beach round of the Florida Winter Tour’s ROK edition, BIREL ART/PSL achieved a double victory among 191 drivers. Ryan Norberg won ROK Senior from second in qualifying, also taking fastest lap and reclaiming the championship lead; Scott Davidson earned his first season win in ROK Shifter Master. Igor Pushkin finished fifth overall, Ryan MacDermid 10th, and Justin Aresneu 12th. The team next targeted the Rotax edition beginning February 16.

The speaker says the team missed scoring chances, including an attempt at an empty net. Despite the loss, they remain positive, focus on the important third game, avoid turnovers and defensive lapses, keep the puck on the outside rather than chipping it into the middle, and continue giving their all.

The author launches a hostile critique of Hillary Clinton, arguing that her ambition, indifference to truth, national-security record, and alleged role in Libya make her unfit for president. They accuse her of enabling slavery’s revival in Libya through the 2003 U.S.-Libya agreement and subsequent regime change, and broadly label her a pathological liar and arrogant politician.

The passage also alleges decades of media and government cover-ups, including Bill Clinton’s reported meeting with Attorney General Loretta Lynch during the FBI email investigation, and references WikiLeaks, the Clintons’ private email server, and purported scandals involving the Clinton Foundation, Whitewater, Filegate, Iran fundraising, Benghazi, Vince Foster, and other matters. It cites Christopher Hitchens’s description of Hillary Clinton as an inadequate liar and says even Donald Trump might be no worse.

The writer mocks continued public support for Clinton and closes by asking whether America has become indifferent to political corruption and responsibility.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture adds dual-datapath FP32 processing, doubling peak FP32 throughput over Turing; the GeForce RTX 3090 delivers over 35 FP32 TFLOPS. Second-generation RT Cores provide dedicated BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection, up to twice Turing’s ray-tracing performance, and can operate concurrently with graphics, compute, or other compute workloads. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur, potentially up to eight times faster than Turing, with one Blender test showing up to fivefold improvement over an RTX 2080 Super.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support, with TF32 providing up to five times the prior generation’s AI training throughput. Fine-grained structured sparsity skips zero-valued matrix elements, doubling Tensor Core throughput; the RTX 3080 delivers 2.7 times the sparse FP16 Tensor throughput of an RTX 2080 Super. Tensor Cores accelerate DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, NVIDIA Canvas, and other inference workloads.

GA10x supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth on the RTX 3090—over 52% more than the RTX 2080 Ti’s TU102 GPU. The RTX 3080 has 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. The professional RTX A6000 and A40 each have 48 GB of GDDR6 memory and can combine two GPUs through third-generation NVLink for 96 GB. NVLink supplies 56.25 GB/s in each direction, or 112.5 GB/s total, between two GPUs. Two RTX 3090s can also use NVLink SLI, while three- and four-way SLI are unsupported.

PCI Express 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, with an x16 interface providing up to 64 GB/s peak bandwidth and improving CPU-to-GPU transfers, DMA operations, and data-intensive AI, data science, and 3D-design workloads. NVIDIA RTX IO, designed for Microsoft DirectStorage, performs lossless asset decompression on the GPU and reports up to 100-times better I/O performance than hard drives and traditional storage APIs while reducing CPU utilization.

A full GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, and 84 SMs. Each SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, a second-generation RT Core, a 256 KB register file, four texture units, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. Four partitions can execute either 128 FP32 operations or 64 FP32 plus 64 INT32 operations per clock. The GPU has 112 ROPs, 168 FP64 units, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Compared with Turing, combined L1 and shared-memory capacity is 33% larger, shared-memory bandwidth is doubled, and Ampere is described as up to 1.9 times more power-efficient at equivalent performance.

The architecture supports 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz, including DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC and HDMI 2.1 at 48 Gbps. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 AV1 playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. GDDR6X interfaces also include Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed memory transactions and retries them.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing, offering up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI-training throughput of a Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, PCIe Gen4, vGPU and Quadro Sync support, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, supports GDDR6X in the architecture but ships with GDDR6, lacks NVLink, and is reported as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 48 GB of GDDR6 expandable to 96 GB, hardware-accelerated motion blur, and accelerated AI denoising.

A three-judge federal district court held that Hale County, Alabama, was covered by Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act because Alabama had been designated under Section 4, which automatically included all political subdivisions within the state. The court rejected the defendants’ argument that Hale County required separate designation.

Alabama had changed Hale County commissioner elections from district-based voting to at-large voting through acts enacted in 1965, 1971, and 1973. None of these enactments or election procedures received the required Section 5 preclearance. The court therefore held that the acts were legally unenforceable and that elections conducted under them were unlawful. The 1959 district-election procedure would govern unless the Attorney General or the District of Columbia district court determined otherwise.

The court allowed the November 2, 1976, election to proceed, with elected and incumbent commissioners serving provisionally. Defendants were ordered to submit the three enactments and requested information to the Attorney General within 15 days for expedited review. If the Attorney General objected, defendants could seek a declaratory judgment in the District of Columbia. Failure to do so, or an unfavorable ruling, required a prompt district-based election for the commission. The court retained jurisdiction to provide further relief.

Anna Gasser won the Olympic debut of women’s Big Air snowboarding, earning 185.00 to edge two-time gold medalist Jamie Anderson, who failed to land her final jump while leading. Gasser’s third-jump double cork 1080 scored 96. Zoi Sadowski Synnott took bronze, earning New Zealand its first Winter Olympic medal since 1992.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier applications concerning electrical connections in quantum computing systems, describes flexible-cable interconnects for cryogenic quantum computers. Flexible cables carry parallel DC, low-frequency, or high-frequency signal lines as striplines, microstrips, or coplanar waveguides and connect to rigid boards at one or both ends, often using fanned-out attachment areas for mechanical integrity. The rigid boards may incorporate filters, attenuators, amplifiers, circulators, isolators, and other electronic components.

The disclosed cable constructions use insulating substrates, metallic striplines and grounding planes, conductive shielding vias, and optional mechanical stiffeners. Conductive or absorptive composites may provide high-frequency attenuation, including in the 10 GHz–1 THz range. Connections between cables and boards may use wire bonds, flip-chip assemblies, solder bumps, indium interfaces, or similar techniques. Filters and attenuators may be integrated into either flex cables or rigid boards through windows in grounding planes.

The interconnects are designed for use across dilution-refrigerator isothermal plates, where they route excitation and readout signals between a superconducting quantum processing unit and other cryogenic or room-temperature components. Compliant spring-contact joints can provide replaceable electrical connections while accommodating thermal contraction, including connections directly between flex cables, quantum processor interposers, and printed circuit boards. Additional embodiments use push-on connectors, copper enclosures, thermally matched clamping plates, and signal-conditioning modules.

Claims cover flexible cables, systems combining non-superconducting and superconducting cable sections, and cryogenic systems containing isothermal plates and superconducting quantum processing units with at least 50 or 100 qubits.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill after resigning from the bench as state ethics regulators agreed to drop charges in exchange for his agreement never to accept judicial office again. Complaints alleged rude, demeaning conduct toward court staff and retaliatory threats against commission staff and witnesses. Nock denied wrongdoing, and no findings were made. He cited family considerations and impending mandatory retirement at 70. Anderson Kill said he disclosed the allegations before joining and that they did not question his conduct or character. Nock served as a New York City civil court judge from 2015 and an acting state supreme court justice from 2018.

This medRxiv preprint reports a post hoc analysis of the phase 3, randomized, double-blind LIVE-AIR trial of lenzilumab, a GM-CSF-neutralizing monoclonal antibody, in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 pneumonia. Overall, lenzilumab improved 28-day survival without invasive mechanical ventilation (SWOV) versus placebo (HR 1.54; 95% CI 1.02–2.32). Baseline CRP was the strongest predictor of progression to invasive mechanical ventilation or death.

The greatest treatment benefit occurred among participants with baseline CRP below 150 mg/L, who had improved SWOV with lenzilumab (HR 2.54; 95% CI 1.46–4.41), fewer IMV, ECMO, or death outcomes, more ventilator-free and fewer ICU days, and faster recovery. Similar benefit was not observed with baseline CRP at or above 150 mg/L. Participants with CRP above 150 mg/L were at high risk of rapidly escalating respiratory support or dying, and lenzilumab reduced CRP more rapidly than placebo. Mortality benefit was not statistically significant, as the trial was not powered for mortality.

No serious adverse events attributable to lenzilumab or infusion-related reactions were reported. The findings support baseline CRP as a potential biomarker for selecting hospitalized COVID-19 patients most likely to benefit from early lenzilumab treatment, but most analyses were exploratory, post hoc, and not prospectively powered; prospective evaluation is planned in ACTIV-5/BET-B.

Teagasc surveyed 314 male farmers in southeast Ireland, who had higher cardiovascular disease and cancer mortality than other occupational groups. Only 57% had seen a doctor in the past year, and 20% had never sought medical advice; 39% reported ill health, mainly back pain, arthritis, or anxiety. Full-time farmers more often reported back pain. Farmers prioritized work over health, and 13% reported rheumatoid arthritis—three times the Irish male average.

The speaker called the upcoming playoff final the biggest game they can play. They are calm, excited, and ready despite nerves, supported by fans and the city; an injured teammate’s possible return would mean a lot.

Donna Adelson was sentenced to life in prison for the 2014 murder of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, and an additional 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. She claimed she was innocent, denied evidence of her participation, and said she would have stopped the murder-for-hire plot had she known of it. Judge Stephen Everett warned that her statements demonstrated an “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors alleged that Adelson plotted the killing with her son and others to move Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to South Florida. Wendi has not been charged, and Donna’s husband supported her account.

The White House confirmed plans to withdraw Kathleen Hartnett White's nomination to chair the Council on Environmental Quality. Trump had announced her in October 2017, but the nomination stalled in the Senate and was returned to the White House when Congress adjourned at the end of 2017; Trump resubmitted it in January. White, a non-scientist and climate change skeptic, had served on a Texas environmental oversight commission under Rick Perry, later Trump's energy secretary. At her November hearing she defended her statement that particulate pollution from burning fuels is not harmful, called carbon dioxide "a necessary nutrient for plant life," praised fossil fuels for ending slavery, and criticized the Obama administration's "imperial EPA." She was a senior fellow at the Koch- and fossil-fuel-funded Texas Public Policy Foundation. The Washington Post first reported the planned withdrawal; a White House official confirmed it. Trump has called climate change a hoax and paved the way for withdrawing the U.S. from the Paris accords, and other administration officials including Pruitt and Zinke question the scientific consensus. Sen. Tom Carper said her nomination withdrawal was "the right thing to do" and urged naming a "thoughtful environmental and public health champion."

A Marquette University study examined the relationship between governance and investment performance among 35 public pension plans representing about 14.5% of the industry by assets. From 2008–2012, annualized returns varied widely, from 15% for the best plan to negative 4.2% for the worst, compared with 1.4% for the S&P 500 and 4.5% for a balanced index portfolio.

Researchers identified several governance factors associated with stronger performance: organizational knowledge and stability, low board turnover, professionalism, effective board composition and engagement, staff involvement, reliable consultants, and diligence. Monthly board meetings performed better than quarterly meetings, and retirees were statistically stronger board members. Investment expenses and required contribution rates were not statistically significant.

Using a Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient (FEQ), the study found that the top 20% of plans outperformed the bottom 20% by nearly two to one. Each one-unit improvement in FEQ was associated with a 0.36% increase in five-year investment performance, with the relationship persisting under a one-year lag.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPUs use RT Cores to enable real-time ray tracing with physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. This required nearly 10 years of collaboration across NVIDIA’s research, GPU hardware, and software engineering teams.

A cross-sectional study assessed contraception knowledge, attitudes, practices, and predictors among 217 female students of NTA TV College in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, using a self-administered questionnaire and multivariable binary logistic regression. The mean age was 21.9 years, and 73.7% had engaged in sexual intercourse. Good knowledge, attitude, and practice rates were 55.3%, 47.5%, and 50.7%, respectively. Friends and the internet were the leading information sources, while condoms and oral contraceptive pills were most commonly used. Fear of side effects or health risks was the most common reason for contraceptive non-use. Being over 19 predicted good knowledge; diploma status, off-campus residence, and good knowledge predicted good attitude; and Plateau indigenous ethnicity and prior sexual intercourse predicted good contraceptive practice. The study concluded that these levels were relatively low and called for targeted advocacy, policy reform, improved youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services, and contraceptive education and counselling. It also noted limited generalizability and possible underreporting due to social-desirability bias.

Hui Ying Financial Holdings Corporation reported 2017 revenue of $46.50 million, up 88.4% from $24.68 million in 2016, driven by higher loan-facilitation volume and the entrusted-loan business launched in June 2017. Loan origination fees rose 52.7% to $26.70 million, repayment management fees increased 153.3% to $18.21 million, and entrusted-loan financing income reached $1.58 million. Operating expenses increased 41.2% to $28.55 million, while operating income climbed 301.6% to $17.95 million. Net income increased 343.9% to $15.27 million, and diluted earnings per share rose to $0.21 from $0.05.

Loans facilitated increased 59.9% to $1.31 billion, with 23,263 loans involving 8,047 borrowers and 69,232 investors. Outstanding loan balances grew to $436.3 million from $246.1 million, while cumulative facilitated loans reached $2.87 billion since the marketplace launched in December 2013.

At year-end, cash and cash equivalents were $12.68 million, the current ratio was 3.16, and operating activities generated $24.07 million in cash. The company also received $13.37 million from convertible-note issuance. Hui Ying operates an online platform in China that connects investors with underserved SME and individual borrowers, maintains risk-reserve funds, and offers a secondary market for investors.

Chrissy Teigen, pregnant with her second child, discussed her family-related susceptibility to stretch marks and her prevention routine. Her belly currently has no marks, so she applies Aquaphor, coconut oil, and Lumière de Vie products each night for 10–15 minutes, focusing on areas prone to stretching. John Legend and daughter Luna help with the process. Teigen says preparing the skin before stretching occurs is key. She receives Lumière products through a prior beauty campaign and has publicly shared her thigh stretch marks, rejecting suggestions that she posted them for praise. She also said she has never known a woman without stretch marks and considers them a common bond among women.

Research of 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10–15 found that girls used social media more than boys and experienced a larger decline in well-being. Girls using social media for at least an hour daily by age 10 had lower well-being at 15. The researchers said early use may affect girls’ well-being later, but noted the study’s self-reported, school-day data may underestimate the association.

The coach said the team must absorb Chris Pronger’s absence during his one-game suspension, with Joe DiPenta and Jackman expected to receive more playing time and Beauchemin, Niedermayer, O’Donnell and Huskins taking on added minutes and power-play responsibility. Chris Kunitz remained a game-time decision after treatment. The team also needed to reduce undisciplined penalties while preserving useful penalty kills.

After an overly emotional, out-of-sync previous game, the group regrouped, established its forechecking and played more effectively as a team. Penalty killing, strong goaltending and contributions from Huskins, Selanne, Penner and Perry helped secure a win without Pronger. Selanne’s assist on Penner’s goal and his leadership were particularly praised. Despite several shots striking the crossbar or posts, the coach said the next game would be the toughest, requiring greater intensity, discipline and preparation to match the opponent’s skill and determination.

A Jan. 26, 2001 compilation of news clippings examines Enron’s role in California’s electricity crisis, Wall Street performance, the Maharashtra power-contract dispute, wind power, and employee evaluations.

The Times of India attributed California’s rolling blackouts and near-bankruptcy of major utilities to flawed deregulation, retail tariff caps, restrictions on long-term power contracts, plant closures, rising Silicon Valley demand, reduced hydroelectric supply, and greater dependence on imports. It argued that supply and demand, adequate long-term capacity, price stabilization without distorting tariffs, and orderly deregulation were essential.

Wall Street investors favored defensive stocks while awaiting 2001 earnings forecasts and a possible Federal Reserve rate cut. The Dow rose 82.55 points to 10,729.52, while the Nasdaq fell 104.87 points and the S&P 500 slipped 6.79 points. Corning plunged nearly 20 percent after warning of reduced customer orders. Enron rose $2.25 to $82 after indicating that 2001 profits would exceed analysts’ expectations.

Boston Globe columnist David Nyhan announced a four-month leave to attend a fellowship at Harvard’s Kennedy School and discussed readers’ political concerns. He cited Enron’s profits from California’s energy shortage and its executives’ campaign contributions.

Business Standard said U.S. ambassador Richard Celeste urged Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh to honor the state’s contract with Enron, signaling possible U.S. displeasure over a breach. The editorial said a proposed review committee was likely to justify nonpayment because politically difficult tariff increases left MSEB unable to compensate Enron, and argued that Maharashtra’s interests required MSEB to follow tariffs set by its regulatory commission.

The San Francisco Chronicle reported that Lamorinda Democrats used gallows humor after President Bush’s inauguration and discussed California’s energy policies. UC Energy Institute director Severin Borenstein proposed time-of-use electricity pricing, including peak rates of up to 50 cents per megawatt-hour, to encourage conservation and reduce the need for polluting power plants.

The Wall Street Journal described wind power’s revival as a partial response to California blackouts and high natural-gas prices. Altamont Pass had about 7,000 turbines, while the 470-turbine Stateline project was expected to cost three to five cents per kilowatt-hour and become one of the first large wind farms profitable without tax credits. Enron operated 2,000 turbines in the Tehachapi Mountains and had recently deployed about 700 more in California, Texas, Minnesota, and Iowa. Wind could be built in about a year, compared with as long as five years for coal or gas plants, but its intermittency limited reliability and it supplied only about 1.5 percent of California’s electricity.

The Wall Street Journal also reported that cash-strapped Maharashtra State Electricity Board was expected to miss a deadline for paying 1.59 billion rupees, or $34.3 million, to Enron’s Dabhol Power unit, potentially prompting Enron to invoke state and federal guarantees.

The Houston Chronicle reported opposition among employees to Enron’s new forced-ranking system, which assigned workers to five categories while requiring managers to compare them against one another. Workers alleged that ratings could be traded between managers, while human-resources executive Cindy Olson denied such bargaining and said the rankings were not final.

The President returned House bill No. 6242 without his signature, objecting that it appropriated public funds for purely local improvements outside Congress’s constitutional powers because they neither supported the common defense or general welfare nor promoted interstate commerce. Although he praised many provisions as nationally beneficial, he warned that local appropriations encourage comparable demands in every state and grow disproportionately. River and harbor appropriations rose from $3,975,900 in 1870 to $18,743,875 under the bill, which he said exceeded current needs and required spending too quickly to be economical. He recommended appropriating half the bill’s total for the fiscal year, allocating it among named purposes under presidential direction, with no purpose receiving more than its stated amount.

A free domestic violence support group for women survivors meets Tuesdays at noon with Rebecca Hunter, MSW, and Helping Hands Against Violence; call 541-400-0186 for details. AARP Tax Aide offers free walk-in help preparing federal and Oregon returns, excluding Sch C losses and Sch E rentals. Registration is open for the Feb. 24 “Chess for Success” K–12 tournament in four counties. Girl Up will collect cleaned bras throughout February for women in need and homeless shelters.

PVF Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob urged the government to build an Islamabad-style sports complex in Abbottabad for summer national camps and international events, citing its moderate weather. He said the distant Rs1.2 billion Narowal Sports Complex was underused and that the non-air-conditioned Liaquat Gymnasium causes difficulties during hot weather. He also recommended another hotel at Pakistan Sports Complex Islamabad.

Yaqoob said Asian Games camps had not begun after financial issues and requested an early start, noting that only 2.5 months remained while four months were needed. Youth and junior camps were shifted to Peshawar, where Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi was expected to arrive and oversee all three camps. The PSB was scheduled to meet federations and the POA on June 6 to finalize preparations.

Chicago granted landmark status to the former Johnson Publishing Company headquarters, which housed Ebony and Jet magazines, before it was sold to 3L Real Estate for $10 million. The developer plans a $20 million conversion into 150 luxury apartments, preserving the magazines’ signs. Construction is slated to begin in 2018 and finish the following year.

The Federal Government unveiled plans for several development projects in the South-East, including the foundation-laying of the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. Science and Technology Minister Ogbonnaya Onu said the centre was established through an MoU with the Vatican City’s Pontifical Council for Culture and advocated using science, technology and innovation to diversify the economy. He urged stakeholders to support the project’s sustainability. Governor Rochas Okorocha pledged state support and encouraged the community to back the centre for future generations.

MIT 2.830J, Control of Manufacturing Processes, is taught live between Cambridge and Singapore by Duane Boning, with David Hardt and teaching assistant Hayden Taylor. Most classes are videotaped, and materials are distributed through the course’s Stellar website; the Singapore class will not meet on Thursday because of Chinese New Year. The course emphasizes prior experience with manufacturing or microfabrication processes and basic probability and statistics, with semiconductor processing used alongside examples such as metal forming, forging, assembly, and injection molding. Required texts are May and Spanos on semiconductor process control and Montgomery’s *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control*.

Assessment consists of approximately eight individual weekly problem sets, worth about 40 percent, and two quizzes, also worth about 40 percent; there is no final exam. The final third of the course is devoted to collaborative team projects, generally involving three students, with presentations in the final two class periods and a joint report. Projects may address process diagnosis, improvement, statistical process control, optimization and robustness, yield modeling, or defect modeling, ideally using existing or newly collected data. Problem sets permit discussion but require independent write-ups that explain and justify the reasoning behind answers.

The course focuses on understanding, modeling, and controlling manufacturing variation to maximize quality and conformance to specifications. It will cover statistical process control, physical versus empirical process models, design of experiments, response-surface modeling, multi-objective optimization, robustness, and feedback control. A manufacturing process is presented as transforming a workpiece’s geometry and material properties through equipment and a controlled process environment. Product characteristics can be represented as outputs determined by controllable and fixed process parameters, while a first-order variation equation separates deviations caused by inherent disturbances from those caused by intentional control changes. Examples include shrinking semiconductor features, microfluidic diagnostic chips, assembly fit, high-density electrical connectors, inspection, rework, and variation arising during manufacturing changes.

CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction) is a long-established affiliate network operating since 1998. It connects advertisers with publishers, tracks resulting sales or leads, and pays commissions under each program’s terms. CJ also provides account management, payment processing, promotional assets such as banners and product feeds, and detailed campaign reporting.

Joining is free. Applicants need a website or social media profile with relevant content and an audience in the United States or Canada. After registration and approval, publishers must describe their site and audience, provide payment and tax information, and apply separately for advertiser programs. Programs can be searched and filtered by niche, commission type, or country, and performance data is available through the account dashboard.

CJ offers thousands of programs across many niches, earning platforms a reputation for advanced tracking, management, payment, and promotional options. Its main drawbacks are a learning curve and potentially strict approval process.

There are no monthly or annual membership fees, but CJ retains a 5–10% commission. Payments are available by direct deposit, check, or Payoneer, generally within 20 days after month-end once the required deposit threshold is met. The guide describes CJ as a legitimate, beginner-friendly platform with alternatives available if it is unsuitable.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Switching frequencies up to 2 MHz are supported, and the controllers require external gate drivers. Supported topologies include buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters.

In peak-current-mode operation, duty cycles above 50% can cause subharmonic oscillation. The TPS7H500x-SP mitigates this with a voltage-ramp slope compensation signal subtracted from the error-amplifier output divided by CCSR. Minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope; the recommended value is one times that slope, because higher values do not improve stability. Slope compensation is calculated using the current-sense transformer ratio, sense resistor, and applicable power-transformer ratio, then programmed with a resistor from RSC to AVSS.

The controllers use a transconductance error amplifier and support Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation. Type 2A adds CHF in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection begins with the desired crossover frequency: RCOMP is calculated from that frequency, CCOMP places the compensation zero at the power-stage dominant pole, and optional CHF compensates for the output-capacitor ESR zero. Power-stage transconductance varies by converter topology.

Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and restarts the power-up sequence below 160°C. During normal operation, the internal oscillator activates a primary output for the gate driver. The external power-switch current is sensed through a resistor and compared with a stepped-down COMP voltage; reaching that level turns the switch off.

A design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP in a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs and a 5-V output. Selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ and 1.4-kΩ feedback divider resistors, 20.5-kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns dead time, a 49.9-kΩ RLEB resistor for roughly 50 ns leading-edge blank time, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor giving approximately 7.5 ms startup. The transformer design uses a 35% target duty cycle, a 2.5 turns ratio, a calculated 33-µH primary inductance, and an actual 40-µH value. Primary GaN FETs were rated at 170 V; an 80-V device was selected for synchronous rectification, with an optional parallel Schottky diode to reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses.

The converter uses a 0.47-µH output inductor with a 40% ripple-current target. Output-capacitance calculations for 2% voltage ripple and 2.5% maximum transient deviation indicated at least 1.3 mF; 2.3 mF was used to provide additional radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. The implementation uses seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors. An optional output filter can further reduce ripple and may require damping to prevent high-frequency peaking. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node voltage, but its initial values require testing and optimization.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A maximum peak inductor current. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω RCS resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover with RCOMP, CCOMP, and CHF values of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, respectively. Slope compensation uses a 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS. Several values, including compensation, blank time, and clamp components, may require optimization during testing.

The controller supply range is 4–14 V and requires close, low-impedance bypassing, including at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS; X5R-or-better ceramic capacitors are recommended. Layout guidance emphasizes keeping feedback and control traces away from magnetics, switch nodes, and high-dv/dt signals; minimizing switch-node copper and high-frequency loop area; separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point; using short, wide high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere; placing filtering, bypass, compensation, and feedback components near their associated pins; filtering CS_ILIM as needed; and using at least 3.3 nF at HICC to reduce SYNC-to-HICC noise. For CFP packages, the backside metallization should connect to the AVSS plane through multiple vias. The controllers also require appropriate ESD handling precautions.

The Eagles held a Monday morning practice at the NovaCare Complex before Thursday’s preseason game against the Buffalo Bills. Jordan Matthews was traded to Buffalo with a third-round pick for cornerback Ronald Darby, who joined the first-team defense Sunday despite limited familiarity with defensive calls. Questions remain about Alshon Jeffery’s preseason debut and Carson Wentz’s playing time.

This study translated and culturally adapted the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised (WFQ-R) into modern standard Arabic for use in Saudi Arabia and evaluated its measurement properties. Translation involved independent forward and back translations, expert review, pilot testing with 30 adults, and evaluation of 290 additional adults from across Saudi Arabia. Only item 9 required expanded wording, and answer-grid abbreviations were replaced with full terms for clarity. Pilot participants judged the WFQ-Ar clear, relevant, and appropriate. Expert review supported its face and content validity, and no floor or ceiling effects were found. Exploratory factor analysis identified one factor, explaining 55.79% of variance after extraction, with item loadings of 0.56–0.82. The scale demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α=0.93), excellent test–retest reliability (ICC=0.94), acceptable test–retest agreement, and a standard error of measurement of 4.5 points, or 10% of the total score. WFQ-Ar scores correlated significantly with a single-item foot-dominance question (r=0.48, p<0.001). The authors concluded that the WFQ-Ar is a valid and reliable tool for assessing footedness in clinical and research settings. Because participants were Saudi, non-disabled adults, formal local testing and further research in other populations and Arabic-speaking countries are recommended.

CoreWeave shares rose as much as 8% Wednesday after the cloud provider announced new tools aimed at individual software developers who want to train and monitor AI models, complementing its existing business of renting Nvidia GPUs to clients such as OpenAI. The new serverless reinforcement learning service automatically adds or removes computing capacity; tests showed developers can train models faster at 40% lower cost than running Nvidia H100 GPUs locally, "with no impact on model quality." Reinforcement learning is a decades-old method of evolving systems through trial and error.

The launch follows CoreWeave's $1 billion acquisition of Weights and Biases five months earlier. The company competes with major cloud providers, though some firms prefer keeping GPUs in their own data centers. In July, CoreWeave announced a $9 billion plan to buy data center infrastructure provider Core Scientific; some Core Scientific shareholders want the offer revised, but CEO Mike Intrator said the bid will not be readdressed. CoreWeave also recently signed a multi-year deal worth up to $6.5 billion.

Related headlines listed include IRS furloughs tied to a government shutdown, SoftBank buying ABB's robotics unit for $5.4 billion, and Tesla pricing the Model Y standard below $40,000.

- Analog TV output pins support composite/S-Video luminance and chrominance. In Normal mode, internal amplifiers drive 75-Ω TV loads, with external feedback resistors placed close to the output and TV_VFB pins. In TVOUT Bypass mode, the amplifier outputs are unused, while the feedback pins provide direct VDDA_VDAC_1P8 video-DAC outputs through a nominal 1.5-kΩ load resistor to ground and an external video amplifier. Unused or powered-down outputs remain unconnected. A mode-dependent Rset resistor connects the video-DAC reference pin to VSSA_VDAC; its bypass-mode nominal value is 10 kΩ. Reserved pins must remain unconnected.

- Supply-voltage tables cover variable core logic rails for CORE_L, ARM_L, and DSP_L, selectable 1.8-V or 3.3-V general-purpose, GPMC, memory-card, and camera I/O, and 1.8-V analog rails. Required 1.8-V and 3.3-V supplies must be connected even when associated peripherals such as PCIe, CSI2, HDMI, USB, or VDAC are unused. LDO and bias pins require 1-µF capacitors to VSS, and designated supply-ground pins must connect to ground.

- At power-on or warm reset deassertion, BTMODE[15:0] is sampled and latched into CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC CS0 bus width, wait enable, and address/data multiplexing; BTMODE[4:0] selects the ordered boot modes, with fallback modes attempted after a primary-mode failure; BTMODE[7:5] is reserved and pulled down. EMAC boot uses BTMODE[9:8] for PHY selection, XIP boot uses BTMODE[10] for GPMC multiplexing, and PCIe boot uses BTMODE[15:12] for addressing. ROM-configured pin lists cover NAND, NAND I²C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boot modes. NAND flash requires shadowing before execution. During XIP NOR boot, the ROM reconfigures internal pulls from their default IPU state to IPD, with Option B retaining IPD after boot until software changes it.

- PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers control pin multiplexing through MUXMODE bits. The default MUXMODE of zero tri-states pin outputs; inputs are generally routed to all sharing peripherals regardless of MUXMODE, although some unselected functions receive constant zero or one. Multimuxed functions are marked MM and may have different timing requirements by device pin.

- Unused signal pins may generally remain unconnected unless otherwise specified. Unused inputs should use an enabled internal pull or an external pull resistor to prevent floating. Internal pullup and pulldown resistors are available on most pins. External pulls are strongly recommended for routed, tri-stated boot-configuration pins even when the internal pull matches the desired state, and are required on other inputs when the internal pull is opposite the desired state. Resistor selection must account for leakage, internal and external pulls, valid logic thresholds, output drive strength, bidirectional nets, tolerances, and supply-rail tolerance. Typical values cited are 1 kΩ for opposing internal pulls and 20 kΩ for boot/configuration pins or pins with disabled internal pulls, subject to application-specific confirmation.

- The device uses an L3/L4 switch-fabric architecture with a switched central resource and bridges. The nonblocking L4 interconnect accepts traffic from up to four initiators and services up to 63 targets, while not every initiator connects to every target. Electrical tables provide absolute-maximum and recommended supply ranges, input thresholds, transition-time limits, power-on-hour guidance, JEDEC injection limits, and HBM/CDM ESD qualifications. Power-on-hour information is provided for convenience and does not extend the standard warranty.

- The PRCM centrally controls power, reset, and clocks. Its power-reset manager handles power, resets, wake-up management, and oscillator-source control, while its clock manager handles clock generation, distribution, and management. SmartReflex advises software to adjust core-domain supply voltages according to process, temperature, and performance; communication with external regulators can use GPIO, I²C, SPI, or other methods. Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling changes a domain’s operating performance point in real time without a reset, with lower-frequency points using lower voltage ranges. Supported domain combinations are restricted, DDR access must stop before changing DDR frequency, and CVDD domain voltage differences must remain below 150 mV. Adaptive Voltage Scaling is identified as unsupported.

- Four core-logic voltage domains use dedicated supply rails that must receive regulated voltage at all times. Four memory voltage domains are independently controlled by internal LDO regulators through RAMLDO_CTRLx registers and are programmed according to their corresponding core-logic voltage. Six power domains supply associated core logic and SRAM; their internal switches default off after reset and are controlled individually through Control Module registers, while modules in an off domain are unavailable. Switchable SRAM enters shutdown whenever its domain turns off, losing its data, and selected ALWAYS_ON SRAM can also be shut down through x_MEM_PWRDN registers.

- DVDD, DVDD_GPMC, DVDD_C, and DVDD_SD groups independently support 1.8 V or 3.3 V. Each DDR interface independently supports 1.5 V or 1.8 V. A PHY must enter power-down mode before its containing domain is turned off. Low-Power Standby requires all switchable domains off, the ARM Cortex-A8 executing an idle loop at its lowest frequency, and unnecessary functional blocks clock-gated.

- Power supplies are divided into core, DDR, 1.8-V, and 3.3-V sequencing groups with prescribed power-up and power-down order. Simultaneous supply ramp-down is allowed when the stated limits are met, but 3.3-V supplies must never exceed the 1.8-V supplies by more than 2 V. PLL and analog rails should use ferrite-bead filtering and nearby capacitors. The guidance calls for 0.1-µF decoupling near the device, at least one capacitor per two power pins, and roughly one bulk capacitor of 10 µF or more per ten power pins without excessively delaying supply ramps.

- A power-on reset resets the full chip, including test/emulation logic and the EMAC switch. External, emulation, watchdog, and software warm resets generally exclude test/emulation logic and can optionally isolate the EMAC switch. Software global cold and warm resets are initiated through specified PRM reset-control bits. TRST affects only emulation logic, while local resets affect only the associated module. If reset requests occur simultaneously, only the highest-priority request is processed. PCIe supports isolated reset and requires idle handling and bus re-enumeration; EMAC-switch isolation can preserve switch traffic and selected registers during non-POR resets.

- RSTOUT_WD_OUT reflects reset status, is always asserted for watchdog resets, and can be externally biased while POR or RESET is active. Its behavior after POR or RESET depends on the latched BTMODE[11] value. During resets other than TRST, most I/O pins become high impedance; emulation pins, conditionally isolated EMAC pins, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT have stated exceptions. DDR pins are tri-stated during reset and subsequently driven according to their internal-pull reset values. PINCNTL registers also reset, except where EMAC isolation preserves them. After reset, the ARM Cortex-A8 begins executing from the Boot ROM, which configures pins for the selected primary and backup boot modes.

- Device clocks derive from reference inputs, PLLs, and dividers. The DEV clock generates most internal references, while AUX is optional for audio and video PLLs. DEV and AUX inputs may use external crystals with internal oscillators or external 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. DEV is normally 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under specified exceptions; AUX may also range from 20–30 MHz. Internal oscillators require crystals, load capacitors, and oscillator-specific grounds that remain separate from board ground. External LVCMOS operation leaves the MXO pins unconnected and connects oscillator grounds to board ground.

- SERDES_CLKN/P requires a high-quality, low-jitter differential AC-coupled source placed close to the device for the PCIe PHY. Optional clocks include 32.768 kHz at CLKIN32 and AUD_CLKIN0/1/2, whose maximum pin frequency is 50 MHz, for HDMI I²S, McASP, McBSP, and timers. CLKOUT0 and CLKOUT1 provide selectable general-purpose clock outputs. The device contains 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs; they start in bypass mode, require filtered external 1.8-V supplies, and must remain within specified reference, internal, output, SYSCLK, and module-frequency limits. PLL_USB must be programmed to 960 MHz.

- The ARM interrupt controller prioritizes up to 128 requests and generates IRQs or FIQs, although general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. The C674x controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts; events 15–95 can be remapped among 24 multiplexed sources through DSP_INTMUX_x registers. It also controls CPU exceptions, nonmaskable interrupts, and emulation interrupts.

- AC timing is specified at device pins, uses defined input and output reference levels, and is tested with an input slew rate below 4 V/ns. Board-routing delay is excluded from the listed timings; IBIS models are recommended for accurate system analysis, while separate PCB routing guidance applies to DDR2. Clock and control signals must transition monotonically between valid input levels.

- The device includes two DCAN interfaces supporting CAN 2.0A/B, configurable identifiers, FIFO and loop-back modes, automatic bus recovery, test-mode Message RAM access, general-purpose pin configuration, and interrupt outputs. EDMA provides up to 64 channels, with synchronization events mapped to 512 parameter-table entries.

- Advanced Event Triggering supports hardware breakpoints, data watchpoints, event counters, and state sequencing. System and Cortex-A8 trace can export through the Embedded Trace Buffer or a five-pin trace interface. JTAG supports testing and emulation, with an internal TRST pulldown and special handling for third-party controllers that do not drive TRST high. The documented JTAG ID value is 0x0B8F202F.

- The EMAC switch is a three-port gigabit design with one internal and two external ports. External ports support 10Base-T, 100BaseTX, and full-duplex 1000BaseT through MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes; a shared MDIO interface controls external PHYs. It conforms to IEEE 802.3-2002, omits the MTXER signal and instead corrupts transmitted frame CRCs to indicate underflow errors, and requires 3.3-V PHY interfaces. Its CPPI block contains 2,048 32-bit words for up to 512 buffer descriptors. Extensive Ethernet-switch register listings cover ports, queues, DMA channels, interrupts, statistics, address lookup, and subsystem interrupt controls.

A lasting peace requires equality of rights among nations based on their common strength, not on differences in size, power, territory, or resources. It must also recognize that governments derive just authority from the consent of the governed and that peoples cannot be transferred between sovereignties as property. An independent Poland and guarantees of life, worship, and social and industrial development are cited as examples of conditions needed to prevent popular resistance from destabilizing peace. Stability also requires access to the sea, freedom of maritime trade, safe navigation, limits on naval armaments, and broader restrictions on armies and military preparation. The author argues that resolving these issues requires candor, accommodation, concession, and sacrifice, and that statesmen should plan for peace as deliberately as they have planned for war. Speaking for the United States government, the author presents these principles as reflecting the wishes of Americans and liberals worldwide.

The passage presents a seasonal silver strategy based on recurring monthly price patterns. Silver’s strongest periods are December–February and July–August, while June and September are generally weakest. The proposed explanation emphasizes annual purchasing by industrial silver users, alongside broader commodity influences such as weather and business cycles. Backtested from 2001, the strategy holds silver for five months annually and earned 3.9% more per year than buy-and-hold, with a reported risk-adjusted return of 26.93% versus 7.33%. Its maximum drawdown was also lower, at -23.34% compared with -71.65% for buy-and-hold.

Parliament will adjourn early on February 7, 2018, to prepare for President Nana Akufo-Addo’s State of the Nation Address on February 8. Members were urged to arrive by 9:15 a.m. and not bring guests.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit successive-approximation ADC with an integrated analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, reference buffer, and input and AVDD alarms. It supports single-ended or differential, bipolar or unipolar inputs, settles to within 1% accuracy in under 5 µs, and has input bandwidth up to 400 kHz.

The internal reference is factory-trimmed and has a nominal output of 4.096 V. It is selected by default through the INTREF_DIS bit and requires a minimum 4.7 µF capacitor between REFIO and REFGND. Mechanical stress, soldering, and repeated reflow can shift its output, so devices exposed to multiple reflows should be soldered in the second pass. The reference is temperature compensated over −40°C to +125°C. An external 4.096 V reference can instead be applied to REFIO; the internal buffer drives REFCAP and requires a minimum 10 µF capacitor plus a nearby 1 µF decoupling capacitor. Neither the internal reference nor buffer should directly drive external loads.

ADC outputs use straight-binary format. The full-scale range equals PFS minus NFS, and each LSB equals the full-scale range divided by 2^16.

The active-high alarm output supports programmable input high and low thresholds with common hysteresis and fixed AVDD thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Each alarm has active and tripped flags: active flags clear at the end of a conversion, while tripped flags clear when ALARM_REG is read. Alarm information can be accessed through the pin, ALARM_REG, or appended to output data.

The multiSPI interface uses 32-bit input and output shift registers and supports four legacy SPI configurations, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation with internal or external clocks. A data-transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on its rising edge; 32 SCLK cycles constitute an optimal frame. Short frames cannot execute writes, while in long frames the last 32 input bits form the command. Daisy-chain operation supports multiple devices with identical configuration, 32 × N SCLK edges per optimal frame, and receives device data in reverse chain order.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST pin can trigger either an application reset or a full power-on reset, selected by RSTn_APP. ACQ acquires the analog input, and a rising CONVST/CS edge initiates conversion. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, data formatting, reference and input-range selection, alarms, and alarm thresholds. Writes to RST_PWRCTL_REG require the 69h protection key. Output data normally contains the latest 16-bit conversion result, with optional device address, range, AVDD-alarm, input-alarm, and parity flags.

An example eight-channel industrial input module combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 differential multiplexer and supports software-configured voltage or current channels. It also demonstrates thermistor temperature monitoring using programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis. AVDD and DVDD require separate decoupling, and recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital routing, places bypass and reference capacitors close to device pins, and uses short ground paths.

India’s selectors were expected to choose a changed 15-member T20I squad for the three-match series against England, with several players injured or being rested before the Champions Trophy. KL Rahul was likely to open if Rohit Sharma remained unfit, alongside Shikhar Dhawan and either Mandeep Singh or Rishabh Pant. Virat Kohli and MS Dhoni were certainties, while Manish Pandey, Karun Nair, Suresh Raina and Deepak Hooda were likely middle-order or all-round options. With Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja likely rested and Jayant Yadav and Axar Patel injured, Amit Mishra was the only established frontline spinner, while Kuldeep Yadav and Shahbaz Nadeem were possible debutants. Jasprit Bumrah, Ashish Nehra and Bhuvneshwar Kumar were expected to complete the squad, with Mohammed Shami and Umesh Yadav likely rested.

- A March 30, 2001 email compiled reports on California’s electricity crisis. Regulators approved rate increases of as much as 46%. PG&E revised upward the share of residential customers facing increases to 69%, while Southern California Edison said about 45% would avoid them. SMUD proposed surcharges linked to low rainfall and reduced hydroelectric production, raising a typical household bill from $67 to $78. California’s average electricity cost was projected at about 12 cents per kilowatt-hour, above every state except Hawaii.
