- Gov. Gray Davis requested $500 million more for state purchases of electricity for Southern California Edison and PG&E, bringing purchases since January to $4.7 billion. The utilities began repaying the state roughly $105 million for electricity supplied in January and February. Republican legislators sued Davis for withholding details of state power contracts, while small generators pursued complaints against utilities over contract rates and payment. State Controller Kathleen Connell projected a $7.4 billion shortfall over 18 months and $26.8 billion in electricity purchases, though the Department of Finance disputed her projection because it did not account for long-term contracts.

- Grid operators forecast a possible 7% June power shortfall. Factors included drought-reduced Pacific Northwest imports, high natural-gas prices, power-plant shutdowns and limited new generation. California had experienced four rolling blackouts that year. The state accelerated permits for natural-gas peaker plants, targeting 1,000 megawatts of summer capacity—enough for roughly 750,000 homes—and shortened environmental reviews to as little as seven days. The state also planned to purchase gas and guarantee operators a reasonable profit. Environmental and public-health groups raised concerns about emissions, water discharges and earthquake risks.

- More than 190 bills addressed the crisis. Two major conservation proposals, involving about $1 billion, could reduce peak demand by as much as 4,000 megawatts through rebates, appliance and air-conditioning incentives, insulation, efficient lighting and other programs. Other proposals covered power-plant approval, California’s right to purchase electricity generated in the state, state ownership of plants and penalties for looting during blackouts. Forecast summer shortfalls ranged from 2,500 to 5,000 megawatts.

- The PUC considered restoring penalties for roughly 1,500 businesses participating in the “interruptibles” program, under which customers receive power discounts in exchange for disconnecting during emergencies. Businesses cited lost productivity and financial strain, while Edison said participation fell to about 5% without penalties. The program could reduce demand enough to supply 1.5 million homes. Police also had issued no tickets under Davis’s order requiring major businesses to reduce outdoor lighting by 50%, citing vague standards, few complaints and limited enforcement resources.

- Following requests from San Francisco and Huntington Beach, utilities were directed to provide detailed outage-block and life-support customer information to local emergency responders under confidentiality restrictions. Utilities generally received only 10 minutes’ warning from the grid operator. PG&E also raised security concerns about revealing outage areas, while an electronic notification system was proposed to help customers and agencies prepare.

- The crisis weakened Gov. Davis politically, prompting radio advertisements supporting his administration and Legislature and potentially opposing future energy-related ballot initiatives. A commentary criticized Davis for distancing himself from regulator decisions on rate increases, while the state Democratic convention was expected to focus on the crisis. Davis retained a large campaign fund and strong Democratic control, but Republicans intensified their criticism and had not identified a leading statewide challenger.

- President Bush called energy a paramount concern, rejected the Kyoto Protocol, rolled back several Clinton-era environmental measures and favored opening Alaska’s Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil and gas development, drawing criticism from European governments, environmentalists and religious organizations. Canada offered to expand U.S. oil and gas supplies and pursue pipelines from Alberta and the Northwest Territories. Business coverage also highlighted San Jose’s electricity needs, an Edison payment to the state and EPRIsolutions’ consulting on distributed generation, fuel cells and other power-supply options.

This application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/872,677, itself a continuation of Ser. No. 15/248,024 (now U.S. Pat. No. 10,687,080), which claims priority from Provisional Ser. No. 62/211,519 filed Aug. 28, 2015.

The disclosure relates to video encoding and decoding, specifically to converting color values between a standard dynamic range (SDR) color volume and a high dynamic range (HDR) color volume so that a single bitstream can be used by both SDR and HDR systems. HDR/WCG video offers greater luminance and color ranges than SDR video, but many displays and decoders lack HDR support (SDR displays may handle roughly 0.5–100 nits, HDR displays 0.01–1000 nits), and generating separate SDR and HDR bitstreams is time-consuming, processor-intensive, and costly in storage and bandwidth, while multiplexing two bitstreams increases transport stream size. A single bitstream encoded from an HDR source is therefore needed, with decoders able to use encoder-generated information to convert decoded values into either an HDR or SDR color volume as appropriate for their display.

Two encoding methods are summarized. In the first, an encoder receives an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and target SDR display properties; finds a color volume transform that converts HDR values into SDR values which, when processed by the target display's SDR operations, substantially match the reference SDR values; generates metadata identifying that transform; and encodes the SDR values into a bitstream. In the second, the encoder receives an HDR master and a reference SDR master, finds a color volume transform converting HDR values into SDR values substantially similar to the reference SDR values, generates metadata identifying the transform, and encodes the HDR values into the bitstream.

The detailed description covers an encoder/decoder/display system in which the bitstream and metadata are delivered over the internet, QAM, or other mechanisms; encoders and decoders may use HEVC, H.264/AVC, or MPEG-2 (e.g., Main 10 HEVC) and may be dedicated hardware or software on servers, computers, or set-top boxes; and displays may be SDR Systems or HDR Systems, with reference to ITU-R BT.709 (SDR gamut), BT.2020 (wide gamut), BT.2035 (luminance), and BT.1886 (electro-optical transfer function, including user gain and black level parameters).

In the SDR-encoding embodiment, the encoder applies color conversion operations (color primary, color space, and transfer function conversions) to HDR master values, then a color volume transform (e.g., tone mapping function, scaling factor, or lookup tables converting HDR YCbCr to SDR YCbCr), then quantization and chroma subsampling (e.g., 16-bit HDR values quantized to 10- or 8-bit; 4:4:4 to 4:2:0). The resulting SDR values are encoded into a bitstream, and metadata describes the color conversion, transform, quantization, and subsampling operations so an HDR System decoder can reverse them. Metadata may be embedded in or separately delivered with the bitstream and may take the form of parameters for a parametric tone mapping function, a scaling factor, a 3D-LUT, or three 1D-LUTs. The SDR System decoder decodes SDR values, may ignore such metadata, and applies SDR display operations (e.g., BT.1886 transfer function, YCbCr-to-RGB conversions with per-component functions) for display. The HDR System decoder decodes the same bitstream, applies inverse quantization and chroma upsampling, performs an inverse color volume transform (SDR YCbCr to HDR YCbCr) based on the metadata, and applies HDR display color space conversions (YCbCr to RGB) for HDR display.

Finding the color volume transform is described as generating candidate transforms by varying parameters of a default transform, converting HDR values with each candidate, emulating the target SDR display's display operations to produce candidate presentation SDR values, comparing these against the reference SDR master, and selecting the candidate with the smallest difference. Alternate approaches find a transform using predefined distortion-minimizing formulas, or find a scaling factor α that relates SDR display RGB values to linearly scaled HDR display RGB values, minimizing a distance function (e.g., Euclidean 2-norm) or minimizing differences in luma components; the encoder can also emulate HDR display operations or use the original captured HDR RGB values directly. α may be communicated as metadata, including as a layer in a multi-layer coding scheme or as 2D maps for per-pixel or per-subset values, and a decoder may instead derive α from decoded values given a known relation between SDR and HDR luma. With a power-function transfer function (C² = C^γ), the SDR Y luma is α^γ times the HDR Y luma, so α can be derived from Y_S/Y_H and used to obtain SDR Cb and Cr as (Y_S/Y_H) times the HDR chroma values.

In the alternate HDR-encoding embodiment, the encoder color-converts, quantizes, and chroma-subsamples HDR values, encodes them, and produces HDR metadata describing those operations plus SDR metadata (from a color volume transform module) telling an SDR System decoder how to convert decoded HDR values into SDR values matching the reference SDR master. The HDR System decoder ignores the SDR metadata and displays HDR values; the SDR System decoder decodes HDR values, applies inverse quantization/upsampling, then applies the color volume transform from the SDR metadata and SDR display operations for display. Converting between HDR and SDR color volumes may also assist quantization and compression, for example by stretching SDR Cb/Cr ranges to allow larger quantization step sizes for equivalent distortion. The description notes that many additional modifications fall within the claimed scope.

WSB obtained LIHI’s first four-month contract to operate city-sanctioned Camp Second Chance. The $75,000 contract covered costs through 2017 and required operation, case management, gate security, and exclusion of anyone under 18; the camp was self-managed, without camper veto power. HSD said the current-year contract remained unfinalized. A second-year renewal was queried, but no reply was included.

Judge Susan Illston temporarily restrained the Trump administration from carrying out federal worker layoffs tied to the government shutdown after unions alleged the administration unlawfully used the shutdown to justify cuts. An OMB filing showed 4,132–4,232 workers initially marked for termination across seven agencies, while OMB chief Russell Vought said total layoffs would reach about 10,000. Furloughed workers described severe financial hardship amid missed pay, prompting bridge-loan offers from several organizations. Around 700 CDC employees mistakenly received reduction-in-force notices, though HHS said they were never separated and the union said more than 600 remained fired. The administration may appeal the ruling.

Model Ella Ravenscroft, 20, is warning about sunbed dangers after using tanning beds once or twice weekly for two years and having four changed moles surgically removed, leaving her with scars. She now urges people to have suspicious moles checked and has stopped using sunbeds in favor of fake tan.

Sunbed use can increase melanoma risk by 16–20%, according to studies cited. Greater Manchester records almost 500 melanoma diagnoses annually, with around one in five patients dying. Although most moles are harmless, changes in a mole’s colour, size, shape, texture or edge can indicate melanoma. Other warning signs include uneven colouring, inflammation, bleeding, oozing, crusting, scabbing, itching, and persistent growths or sores. Experts advise people to know their normal skin appearance, watch for new or unusual changes, and consult a doctor promptly if changes appear, as early treatment can improve outcomes.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation announced the five-year 1Million Project, which aims to connect 1 million high school students lacking home internet. This school year, 180,000 low-income students across 32 states will receive free mobile devices and 3GB of monthly LTE data for up to four years. Sprint will donate about $2.16 billion over five years.

Qatar lost 2.3%, Dubai 0.5% and Abu Dhabi 0.4%, though DXB Entertainments rose 4.1%. Saudi Arabia edged up 0.1% after Al Tayyar reported early loan repayment. Hexane is a six-carbon hydrocarbon solvent found in plants and derived from crude oil. The market offers pure hexane for laboratory use and solvent-based hexane for extracting vegetable oils from soybean, cottonseed, rapeseed, mustard, and safflower seeds. It is also used in textile, printing, furniture, and leather cleaning; glues, gasoline, rubber, cement, and cooking oils; and removing unwanted tastes and odors. Inhalation can cause weakness, numbness, blurred vision, headache, and fatigue, and OSHA’s permissible exposure limit is 500 ppm. A successful sodium hydroxide–methanol alternative for soybean oil extraction is hindered by high moisture, which increases methanol consumption. Asia-Pacific, particularly China, dominates global production and consumption, while North American and European markets are expected to grow with automotive rubber demand.

On Oct. 13, Josie Goodenow will present “All About Bees” to the Laguna Beach Garden Club, covering differences between native Blue Orchard Mason bees and European honeybees and how to raise native bees to boost populations and improve yard health. The meeting begins at 10 a.m. after a 9:30 a.m. social.

Police found the home in deplorable condition with the thermostat at 58°F. Licciardello occasionally dropped off food; both received $10,000 unsecured bail, and the children are staying with family friends.
The speaker praises defensemen Jon Klemm, Greg De Vries and Skoula for their skating, shooting and physical play, and calls an unnamed forward among the league’s best in recent years.

A targeted CAPP-Seq assay was evaluated in 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients with advanced lung adenocarcinoma and suspected leptomeningeal disease (LMD), including 12 patients prospectively treated with osimertinib. CSF tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) variant allele fractions were substantially higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA VAFs (median 32.7% vs. 1.8%; P<0.0001). For definitive LMD, CSF-tDNA had 91.7% sensitivity, compared with 81.8% for cytology and 80.0% for MRI; detectable CSF-tDNA was also associated with worse overall survival (HR 7.1; P=0.02).

Among nine EGFR-mutant patients with paired post-therapy samples, resistance alterations were detected more often in peripheral blood than in CSF, indicating anatomic differences in resistance mechanisms. In the prospective osimertinib cohort, post-treatment CSF-tDNA VAF was strongly associated with CNS progression (HR 6.2; P=0.009), whereas pretreatment VAF was not. CSF-tDNA and osimertinib penetration rates were not significantly correlated.

The findings support CSF-tDNA as a feasible approach for improving LMD detection, prognostication, assessment of targeted-therapy response, and identification of compartment-specific resistance. Limitations included the small number of CSF samples collected at resistance and limited CSF volumes; prospective validation is needed.

In 2016–17, 719 people in Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly were admitted to hospital with eating disorders, including two children under 10. Admissions reached a record high, more than double the 298 recorded in 2010–11, and 94% of cases involved women and girls. Anorexia accounted for 45% of admissions and bulimia 24%. Charity representatives called young-patient admissions worrying, urged early intervention and meeting community-care targets, and said admissions show only the tip of the iceberg. They said the rise could reflect greater awareness or bed availability rather than similarly rising prevalence, raising concerns about inadequate outpatient provision.

On June 14, 2021, NVIDIA Corporation entered an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, as representative of the underwriters, to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured senior notes: $1.25 billion each of 0.309% notes due 2023, 0.584% notes due 2024, 1.550% notes due 2028, and 2.000% notes due 2031. Net proceeds were approximately $4.98 billion after underwriting discounts and estimated offering expenses and will be used for general corporate purposes, potentially including repayment of debt.

The notes are governed by a September 2016 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee, as supplemented by an officers’ certificate dated June 16, 2021. The indenture contains customary covenants and default provisions and permits cash redemptions before maturity with accrued interest and a make-whole premium, subject to specified exceptions. If both a change of control and a downgrade below investment grade by Moody’s and S&P occur within a specified period, NVIDIA must offer to repurchase the affected notes at 101% of principal plus accrued interest. The notes rank equally with NVIDIA’s unsecured and unsubordinated debt but are effectively subordinated to subsidiary liabilities and secured debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, indenture, officers’ certificate, note forms, and a legal opinion.

Poor medication adherence is common among hemodialysis patients, who often take 10–20 tablets daily; reported rates exceed 50% and are associated with inadequate management of kidney disease complications and increased mortality. Person-centered care (PCC), which combines evidence-based care with attention to patient preferences, goals, and values and shared decision-making, may improve adherence through stronger physician-patient communication, care continuity, needs-driven practice, and coordination. Because empirical evidence is limited, this multicenter cross-sectional study examined Japanese hemodialysis patients to assess relationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence and whether trust mediates the PCC–adherence relationship.

Patients and the public were not involved. Adults with kidney failure receiving hemodialysis or combined hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis were recruited from six outpatient dialysis facilities. Eligible participants regularly attended a facility, had regular medication prescriptions, could complete questionnaires, and did not have severe dementia or complete blindness. Data were collected from April 2022 to February 2023 using paper questionnaires. Medication adherence was measured with the Japanese 12-item ASK-12, covering inconvenience or forgetfulness, treatment beliefs, and behavior. Items used a five-point scale, with higher scores indicating greater adherence difficulties. Ethics approval was granted by Fukushima Medical University (ippan2021-292).

Archive360 announced that its Archive2Azure managed compliance storage solution for Microsoft Azure was a finalist for “Best Cloud Storage Solution,” while FastCollect for PSTs was a finalist for “Best Data Storage Solution” in the 2017 DBTA Readers’ Choice Awards. Archive2Azure migrates and manages legacy on-premises email archives and other low-touch data in Azure, supporting retention, regulatory compliance, and eDiscovery readiness. FastCollect automates PST discovery, rehydration, migration, removal, storage, and auditing of message stubs, metadata, and content. Readers could vote online, and winners were to be featured on the DBTA website and in the August 2017 edition of Database Trends and Applications.

The Supreme Court begins the 2025-26 term while considering whether to block the scheduled execution of Victor Tony Jones, convicted of killing Matilda and Jacob Nestor in 1990. Jones is scheduled to be executed Tuesday at 6 p.m. EDT. The court has received more than 30 emergency stay applications this year but has granted none. After a decade of declining executions, 33 had occurred by Tuesday morning—the highest total in roughly a decade. President Trump ended the Biden administration’s federal execution moratorium and made resuming capital punishment a priority.

This term, the court will consider how multiple IQ scores should determine whether a defendant is intellectually disabled and ineligible for execution. The case has moved to an apparent early-December slot; by then, as many as 10 more executions could bring the annual total to 43, the most since 2012.

Dated May 1, 2019, the case examines Tesla’s entry into the U.S. automotive industry and the broader forces reshaping automobile manufacturing, sales, and transportation. Founded in 2003 by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, Tesla was led by Elon Musk from 2008. Its initial strategy was to enter at the luxury end with expensive electric vehicles and progressively reduce prices as production increased. The $100,000 Roadster sold 2,500 units, while the Model S sedan and Model X crossover established Tesla in the luxury market. Each model, however, was delayed and experienced technology, quality, or sales issues.

The $35,000 Model 3 marked Tesla’s first attempt at mass production, offering a 220-mile range or 310 miles with the long-range battery. Although reservations reached 500,000, nearly 25% were reportedly refunded. Model 3 production experienced “production hell”: Tesla skipped conventional prototype production, relied on a highly automated line, used extensive manual assembly, and required rework on an estimated 40% of parts. Tesla’s vertical integration, including in-house production of seats, batteries, electronics, and other components, supported control over quality but departed from industry practice. Tesla also invested heavily in its Nevada Gigafactory and heavily automated Fremont plant. In the second quarter of 2018, Tesla reported a $743 million net loss on $4 billion in revenue, while analysts estimated it needed to produce at least 5,000 vehicles weekly to be profitable. Production eventually reached that level, and Musk acknowledged that excessive automation had been a mistake.

The U.S. new-car market was worth about $270 billion at retail in 2016. GM, Ford, and Chrysler held nearly 46% of 2018 volume, operated with low margins, and faced high exit barriers because of specialized facilities and approximately three million automotive jobs. Customer brand loyalty was also weak. New entrants faced development costs of up to $6 billion, development periods of as long as six years, and the need to build brands, factories, dealer networks, and financing capacity. The automotive supply chain was highly fragmented and generally more profitable than automakers, but EVs’ far fewer components threatened traditional parts demand while increasing the importance of software, advanced driver-assistance systems, and other technologies.

Consumers were changing how they bought and used vehicles. Millennials were becoming a major purchasing segment, researching vehicles extensively online and favoring compact cars and crossovers. Urban residents increasingly sought shorter commutes and car-free mobility, while ride-hailing, car-sharing, bike-sharing, and electric scooters expanded. Dealerships derived most profits from servicing vehicles and parts, but EVs required less maintenance, and dealers often discouraged EV purchases. Online purchasing and direct sales were gaining traction, creating resistance from dealership organizations and franchise laws.

Three forces were reshaping mobility: electrification, autonomous driving, and connectivity. EV sales rose 25% in 2017 to about 200,000 vehicles, battery prices fell 80% from 2010 to 2017, and GM, Ford, Toyota, and BMW announced substantial EV and battery investments. Public charging infrastructure remained limited compared with gas stations, and its cost, funding, and effects on the electric grid were unresolved. Tesla, Uber, Waymo, Apple, and GM were testing autonomous vehicles, with crashes, regulation, and consumer trust limiting adoption. Connected vehicles shifted automotive R&D toward software and were projected to generate revenue rising from $53 billion in 2017 to $156 billion in 2022. Some forecasts anticipated mobility-as-a-service, shared autonomous fleets, and substantially lower private-car ownership by 2030.

Tesla sold directly through company-owned stores, operated its own service centers and a large Supercharger network, and used over-the-air software updates to improve vehicle performance and advance autonomy. Its “Master Plan, Part Deux” proposed Level 5 vehicles that owners could share with others, with an autonomous ride-sharing platform potentially launching by the end of 2019 if regulatory approval was obtained. Many observers credited Tesla and Musk with accelerating industry innovation, while others questioned Tesla’s financial viability. The central unresolved issue was whether Tesla could survive, let alone thrive, in the automotive industry.

DLSS 4 introduces transformer-based neural networks for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. Compared with CNNs, transformers use self-attention to identify long-range patterns across larger pixel windows and scale to models with twice as many parameters. This improves temporal stability, ghosting, anti-aliasing, lighting detail, motion detail, and overall image quality. Super Resolution combines multiple lower-resolution samples with motion and prior-frame data to generate higher-resolution images. Ray Reconstruction uses an NVIDIA-trained network to generate pixels between sampled rays, improving difficult lighting and reducing common denoiser artifacts. DLAA applies Super Resolution technology at native resolution.

Blackwell advances developer-created neural shaders, extending GPU rendering from fixed-function and programmable shaders toward AI-assisted techniques. The Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, developed with Microsoft, and Slang features make Tensor Cores accessible to graphics shaders. Potential applications include neural texture compression, neural materials, radiance caching, skin rendering, and generative facial rendering.

RTX Neural Materials approximates complex layered materials for real-time rendering. Neural Texture Compression uses neural networks to reduce texture storage and bandwidth; one cited demo reduced material memory from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns and supports higher-order filtering. Neural Radiance Cache trains small networks on live game data to infer lighting across many ray bounces after an initial bounce, improving indirect illumination and performance. RTX Skin provides ray-traced subsurface scattering in games. RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model, trained from offline images and 3D pose data, to render more natural-looking faces in real time.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal with prejudice of Lewis Williamson’s challenge to Surf City’s closure of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive. The Town followed the procedures required by N.C.G.S. § 160A-299, including adopting a resolution of intent, providing notice, holding a public hearing, and entering a street-closing order. The closure vested the closed right-of-way in the abutting property owners, including Surf City, which owned adjacent property. Williamson argued that the Town could not lawfully close the street because it intended to construct public facilities on the vested portion, but the court held that § 160A-299 does not restrict a town’s authority based on its intent when all statutory procedures are followed. The court also rejected Williamson’s contention that the statute permits only closing an entire street, ruling that a municipality may close all or part of a street in compliance with the statute.

This application (a continuation of International Application No. PCT/CN2019/130905, claiming priority to Chinese Patent Application No. 201910196567.3 filed Mar. 15, 2019) relates to mobile terminal technologies, specifically to a rotating shaft mechanism and a mobile terminal for foldable devices with flexible displays.

Background: As flexible foldable display technology matures, foldable terminals (e.g., phones, tablets, computers) must meet reliability, operation-experience and industrial-design requirements. Because such a display is continuously foldable, the product structure must deform greatly at the bending part of the mid-position rotating shaft, which common structures cannot achieve, so a special hinge is needed. In the prior art, the bent part of the folded hinge is thicker than the structural design, affecting the folded effect.

Solution: The rotating shaft mechanism is fixedly connected to two housings of the mobile terminal and serves as its folding mechanism, with the housings rotating about it during folding. It comprises a main shaft assembly (a support piece), a swing arm assembly and a support assembly. The main shaft assembly includes a main inner shaft fixedly connected to a main outer shaft (by screws, buckle or rivet), with its first surface supporting the flexible display. The swing arm assembly includes connecting rod groups and swing arm groups: connecting rods are disposed on both sides of the main shaft assembly and rotate about axes parallel to its length direction; swing arms are fixedly connected to the housings, rotate about different parallel axes, and are slidably connected to the connecting rods through sliding slots and protrusions, with notches reducing assembled thickness. Engaging gears on opposite ends of paired connecting rods ensure synchronous folding, and are housed in a cavity in the main shaft assembly. A limiting mechanism—first cams rotating with the connecting rods, opposite second cams with engaging protrusions and notches, and an elastic part such as a compression spring on the camshaft—limits folded/unfolded positions and provides damping. Support plates on both sides of the main shaft assembly connect rotatably and slidably to the swing arms and connecting rods (via pin shafts, sliding slots, or arc-shaped slots and arms) and, when folded, form with the main inner shaft a three-panel concave space accommodating the folded display. A flexible blocking layer (elastic steel or plastic plate), fixed to the surface facing away from the display, either inserts into the two housings or is driven by swing rods, covering the notches to improve appearance.

Mobile terminal: comprises the mechanism, two housings arranged on both sides of the main shaft assembly (each fixed to a same-side swing arm), and a flexible display fixed to the housings. The display is divided into areas A1, B1, C, B2 and A2; in one manner only A1 and A2 are adhered, leaving non-adhesive areas that fold into a droplet shape, while in another manner B1 and B2 are also adhered, leaving the non-adhesive C area as a semi-arc shape.

Effects: the connecting rods rotate while the swing arms slide and rotate relative to the shaft, so the folded mechanism's thickness is approximately equal to that of the two stacked housings with no large gap; the support plates and main shaft assembly enclose space accommodating the flexible display, improving its bending and support, with no relative sliding between the display and the housings.

This medRxiv preprint presents a study of short- and long-term, out-of-sample forecasts of daily COVID-19 confirmed and death cases in the USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and the UK. It notes that COVID-19 time series contain dynamic linear and nonlinear patterns, making single forecasting models such as ARIMA, ARNN, or SVM insufficient or inaccurate. The study therefore adopts hybrid models combining linear and nonlinear techniques to reduce prediction-residual bias and variance and better model the data’s dynamics.

The proposed approaches include ARNN-SVM (ARNNS) and SVM-ARNN (SVMAR). The authors report strong performance for forecasting confirmed and death cases, with the models offering interpretability, robustness, and adaptability to seasonality. ARNN is described as a feed-forward network with one hidden layer that uses lagged time-series values, providing less complexity than some ANN and WBF alternatives.

Daily confirmed- and death-case datasets were obtained from Global Change Data Lab. Their starting dates differ, but all end on January 15, 2021, and each contains more than 300 observations. Unlike previous studies focused mainly on confirmed cases, this research forecasts both confirmed and death cases across all five countries. Preliminary analysis found the datasets non-normal and their epidemic curves still spiky and declining in some periods. The hybrid modeling approach assumes that future trends may continue upward. The paper outlines the datasets and evaluation methods, model formulations, experimental results, practical implications, and conclusions.

A multicenter cross-sectional study assessed SARS-CoV-2 humoral immunity among 1,411 emergency-department patients at five university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, from August to September 2022. Spike-IgG, nucleocapsid-IgG, and serum neutralization against Wu01 and BA.4/5 were measured; a stratified subsample of 423 was also tested against BQ.1.1. Vaccination, infection, medical-history, and demographic data were analyzed using multivariable regression and Bayesian networks.

Spike-IgG was detected in 95.6% of participants and increased with the number of previous vaccination or infection contacts. Lower levels were associated with drug immunosuppression. Nucleocapsid-IgG was detected in 24.0% and, together with vaccination and infection history, strongly predicted spike-IgG levels. Most participants had received at least one vaccine dose, but only 67.7% followed German vaccination recommendations; 45.7% reported prior infection.

Detectable neutralization was present in 94.4% against Wu01, 84.9% against BA.4/5, and 73.8% against BQ.1.1. Neutralization against BA.4/5 was 5.92-fold lower than against Wu01, while BQ.1.1 activity was 23.6-fold lower than against Wu01 and 4.2-fold lower than against BA.4/5. Spike-IgG levels correlated with neutralization and were the strongest predictor, but antibody detection had reduced accuracy, particularly at low levels; 59.6% of participants with spike-IgG below 1,000 BAU/ml had no detectable BQ.1.1 neutralization. Previous antigen contacts also predicted neutralization.

The study population was not representative of the general population, and no clinical outcomes from prior infections were available. The authors emphasized that neutralizing assays are needed alongside IgG testing to assess immunity and concluded that improving vaccine uptake was important for reducing COVID-19 risk during BQ.1.1 waves.

Although Lincoln City FC and Grimsby Town FC are now fierce rivals, the railway line serving Blundell Park was built for economic reasons. The Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway opened the Lincoln–Barnetby–Grimsby route in 1848 to carry goods to and from Grimsby’s port and distribute fish inland. Its River Witham bridge at Stamp End was designed by John Fowler using box-shaped iron girders, then advanced technology. Network Rail has recently replaced it in a £7m project involving one of the world’s biggest cranes.

Fowler initially described the planned bridge as four timber-cased boiler-plate girders but later selected William Fairbairn’s relatively untested tubular design, possibly following a change in alignment. The completed double-track bridge had three spans: a 74-foot central span and timber side spans. An Alan Baxter report for Network Rail says it may be Britain’s oldest surviving wrought-iron box-girder railway bridge, perhaps the world’s oldest, and is certainly Britain’s oldest still carrying trains.

The side spans were replaced with steel plate-girder decks around 1901–03, while the central span was reinforced with a plate girder between the tracks. Cross-girders received additional plates in 1948, and a new steel deck was added centrally in 1968. Sleepers on the bridge caught fire in 1937. Its box-girder technology preceded the Menai Bridge and Royal Albert Bridge.

Researchers developed kirigami-inspired parachutes made from thin Mylar disks perforated with concentric slits. As cargo falls, airflow opens each disk into a latticework vase, generating drag and slowing the descent. The parachutes open automatically and realign to fall straight down regardless of their initial orientation. Laboratory tests found them more accurate than traditional parachutes or uncut disks. In one test, a 1-kilogram bottle dropped from a drone 60 meters with a 0.5-meter parachute reached about 14 meters per second, compared with about 34 meters per second without a parachute. The devices are simple to construct and deploy but produce less drag; a human would require a canopy roughly 100 meters in radius. Potential applications include humanitarian aid drops and drone package delivery, while biodegradable materials such as cardboard are also being considered.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day, including scalping for small price movements and day trading for larger daily moves. It is most common in forex and futures but also occurs in stocks. Its objective is to exploit intraday price movements while managing risks and overnight price gaps. Although profits are possible, the passage states that most intraday traders lose money.

US traders are subject to FINRA pattern day trader rules: four or more day trades within five business days representing more than 6% of margin-account trades require at least $25,000 in equity, and permitted day-trading buying power is generally limited to four times excess maintenance margin. CFD trading may offer higher leverage but is prohibited in the US.

The passage recommends developing and backtesting a strategy with a demonstrated statistical edge. Highly liquid, volatile markets—such as stocks, forex, futures, and options—are considered suitable; the authors see stocks as offering the best opportunities and forex the least. The first two hours after the open have the highest liquidity and volatility. Required capital varies, but should cover trade costs and potential losses.

An hourly lower-low/lower-high strategy tested on WTI crude futures from 2000–2021 performed poorly, with a 47% win rate and an average loss of 0.11% per trade, though a later out-of-sample sample of 21 trades averaged 0.57%. The Buck Sweep is a misdirection off-tackle run, primarily used in the Wing-T but adaptable to the Spread and other offenses. Its layered handoffs, trap fakes, and quarterback boot make the ball carrier difficult to identify, while horizontal blocking angles can benefit undersized linemen.

The play’s main weaknesses are its reliance on precise line and backfield timing, spacing, and effective pullers, plus the extensive practice needed to perfect handoffs, pull paths, and reads. The passage provides blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Variations include a shotgun Wing-T version featuring a quarterback-tailback mesh and possible quarterback keep, and an I-Wing version distinguished by the tailback’s counter step, with largely unchanged blocking and backfield paths.

Container images should be documented in their Dockerfiles using `EXPOSE` with explanatory comments, `ENV` directives for parameter defaults and usage, and `LABEL` directives for maintainer, URL, version, and other standardized metadata. Shared label taxonomies allow tools to visualize, monitor, and use images consistently.

Single-node container patterns include sidecars, ambassadors, and adapters. Sidecars augment an application container with reusable functionality, including updating costly legacy applications. Ambassadors broker communication between an application and external systems, separating concerns and enabling reusable implementations. They can route requests to sharded storage, discover and connect to services across environments, and split traffic between production and experimental implementations. Client-side and service-side sharding architectures trade deployment complexity against application complexity. Kubernetes examples use Redis or Memcached shards with twemproxy, and nginx to direct 90% of traffic to production and 10% to an experiment.

Adapters modify an application’s interface so it conforms to a predefined common interface. They can translate monitoring formats for Prometheus, normalize heterogeneous logs through Fluentd, capture Redis slow logs and Apache Storm events, and provide richer MySQL health checks. Keeping these functions separate avoids modifying third-party images, supports independent upgrades and resource isolation, and enables adapters to be reused and shared across applications.

Distributed container patterns are loosely coupled and communicate through network calls. Microservices divide an application into independently developed components with formal API contracts. This approach enables smaller teams, independent release schedules, and component-specific scaling, but makes debugging and architecture more difficult because failures arise across multiple processes and machines. Distributed patterns provide reusable designs and shared operational lessons.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical instances behind a load balancer for redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Stateless services require readiness probes to distinguish running containers from those ready to serve traffic. Session-tracked variants consistently route a user to one replica through IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing, which minimizes remapping when replica counts change. Replicated caching tiers improve latency and request capacity but require suitable session affinity. They may also provide rate limiting, return HTTP 429 responses with remaining-request headers, and terminate SSL through an additional nginx layer. A complete stateless deployment can use separate replicated nginx, Varnish, and application tiers.

Sharded services divide state among shards, with a root routing each request to the appropriate shard. Unlike replicated caches, whose replicas duplicate data, shards can store unique data and use memory more efficiently. Sharded caches can have greater failure and rollout impact because requests mapped to a failed shard repeatedly miss, so systems must tolerate recalculation and load should be tested with and without caching. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits shard-specific scaling for uneven or “hot” traffic. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, commonly using a hash modulo the shard count. Keys must distinguish requests only when their responses differ; consistent hashing reduces cache misses and disruption during resharding.

Scatter/gather patterns parallelize computation across all leaf nodes, which return partial results that a root combines. They suit large quantities of mostly independent work and can outperform single-machine multithreading by distributing resource bottlenecks. Scatter/gather can also shard data among leaves, as in distributed document search, where the root unions partial matches. More leaves introduce coordination overhead and the straggler problem: overall latency and availability are governed by the slowest or failed leaf. Replicating every shard allows failures and rolling upgrades to occur without user-visible outages.

Function-as-a-service supports event-driven applications that temporarily run in response to requests or events. It differs from the broader serverless concept, which can include managed container platforms. FaaS simplifies deployment because only source code is submitted, automatically scales instances with traffic, restarts failed functions, and provides granular, stateless, modular building blocks. Its central challenge is strong decoupling: functions communicate only over networks, cannot retain local memory, must store state externally, and make service operations more complex.

Freelance writer Oobah Butler created a fictional restaurant, “The Shed at Dulwich,” from his South London garden shed as an experiment to test TripAdvisor. Using a burner phone, an emotion-themed menu, staged food photographs, an address-free appointment-only setup, and fake reviews from friends and family, he had the listing approved in May 2017. It rose from last place among London restaurants to the city’s top-ranked TripAdvisor listing in November, generating calls, free samples, job offers, and worldwide reservation requests, though nobody could obtain a reservation.

Butler later exposed the hoax in a Vice article and opened the restaurant for one night, serving an inexpensive meal to actors and foodies; at least one patron reportedly asked to book again. TripAdvisor said it reviewed and penalized the listing, removing reviews and lowering its ranking. The episode prompted concerns about online misinformation and verification weaknesses, with commentators drawing parallels to false rumors and Russian trolling. TripAdvisor also faced criticism for deleting reviews describing dangerous activity, while a spokesperson said its fraud controls focus more on fake reviews for real businesses than fake businesses.
