This study examines whether a wearable high-density electromyography (HD-EMG) sleeve can characterize forearm muscle coordination during functional movements in people with chronic stroke and able-bodied participants, and whether HD-EMG features may provide motor-related biomarkers.

Seven adults with stroke and hemiparesis (60±5 years) performed movements using a NeuroLife® sleeve on the affected arm. Seven able-bodied adults (27±1 years) served as a benchmark. Stroke participants completed clinical assessments, including the Fugl-Meyer upper-extremity and hand sub-scores, Box and Blocks Test, and Modified Ashworth Scale, and were categorized as mild or severe for subgroup analyses.

Both groups performed 12 hand, wrist, and thumb movements and grasps; able-bodied participants additionally completed 25 dexterous movements and grasps. Participants attempted each movement at approximately 25–50% of maximal effort. EMG was sampled at 3,000 Hz, filtered, corrected for artifacts using blind source separation, and converted to 150-ms RMS windows with a 40-ms stride.

Channels were mapped to a standardized 70-channel right-arm sleeve layout, while preserving original resolution during synergy decomposition. Six forearm muscle groups were identified using agonist-movement activity masks validated at 86.9±0.84% accuracy. Planned analyses included co-contraction index, inter-muscle correlation, and time-invariant and time-varying muscle synergies to compare muscle activation and coordination between groups and relate HD-EMG features to functional ability.

Port Gregory lost electricity for four days, disrupting medical equipment and ruining frozen food; one resident lost about $500. Western Power said storms stretched resources, inspections found no obvious damage, and outages of at least 12 hours qualified customers for payments capped at $80, which did not compensate for lost food.

Divergent nationalist aims within the Allied coalition have produced inconsistent strategy, contributing to Italy’s isolation and military disaster and a similar blunder in Rumania. Unity in both coalitions requires pooling purposes and shifting political power toward middle parties and the moderate left, though the pace may differ by country.

On the Western Front, Germany’s reserves must be exhausted through unprecedented strain on morale and resources, sustained by broad popular consent, moral and administrative economy, and diplomacy exposing “deceptive liberalism” in Germany. Otherwise, German inducements could cause Allied disunion, waste, and weakness.

Germany is expected to seek a winter peace discussion to break Allied morale, which the Allies will resist. In summer, they are expected to seek German withdrawal behind the Meuse and Scheldt and begin a tentative invasion through Lorraine. The anticipated outcome includes destroying submarine bases, recapturing northern France, and possibly invading Germany, with relative reserves of men ultimately decisive as the American reserve becomes available in 1918.

Sonali Bendre announced that she has been diagnosed with high-grade, metastasized cancer and is undergoing treatment in New York. Supported by family, friends, and well-wishers, she remains optimistic and determined to fight the illness.

Apple plans to become approximately net cash neutral over time, meaning its cash and debt would be equal and net to zero. Its current net cash position is $163 billion, and tax reform gives the company greater access to cash held by foreign subsidiaries. To reach its target, Apple could reduce cash, increase debt, or do both. Potential cash-reduction measures include a special dividend, increased share repurchases, or larger annual dividend increases. Apple could also repay or refinance its callable bonds, some of which mature as late as 2047. Management plans to provide more detailed capital allocation plans when it reports second-quarter fiscal results.

Bulk SrTiO3 undergoes an antiferrodistortive transition near 105 K into a non-polar tetragonal phase, but remains a quantum paraelectric: long-range polar order is prevented, likely by quantum fluctuations of opposite polarization states, and can be induced by external tuning such as strain, chemical pressure, or mid-infrared pulses. Because polarization breaks inversion symmetry, it produces asymmetries in dynamical electron scattering that are detectable in 4D-STEM: asymmetry between inversion-related Kikuchi band (Friedel) pairs encodes the polarization, with multislice simulations confirming that the asymmetry direction matches the polarization direction and is absent in the non-polar structure. A new low-vibration liquid-helium-cooled STEM holder with variable temperature control (base ~21 K) enables imaging down to ~20 K.

Below the AFD transition, Δk(r) maps show SrTiO3 is locally polar, with nanoscale domains of opposite polarization within a 40 × 80 nm² field of view at 69 K. Over larger fields, a textured landscape of fluctuating polar nanodomains appears, with an exponential-decay correlation length ξ ≈ 20 ± 0.6 nm. An additional correlation peak at λ ≈ 25 nm indicates periodic spatial ordering among nanodomains; this corresponds to the "roton"-like minimum of the polar-acoustic anomaly rather than a true incommensurate modulation. Fourier transforms show superlattice peaks between 69 and 91 K at q ≈ 0.04 nm⁻¹, matching λ, whose intensity grows down to 69 K.

Below T_q ≈ 40 K, a polar-glass-like transition occurs: domains fragment into smaller, more disordered clusters (ξ ≈ 14 ± 0.4 nm at 35 K) and the periodic ordering is suppressed. Across 111–23 K, domains grow from tiny isolated ones at 111 K to ~20 nm at 69 K, then progressively fragment below 69 K and especially below 40 K. This re-entrant disordering resembles re-entrant spin-glass transitions or inverse melting, and may underlie SrTiO3's anomalous thermal conductivity, glass-like dynamics, and polar-acoustic anomalies; correlations among preformed nanodomains may also mediate field-induced ferroelectric order and relate to doped superconductivity and quantum criticality.

Methods: commercial SrTiO3 crystals (MTI) prepared by Ga FIB lift-out (FEI Helios 660); cryogenic holder from h-Bar Instruments ULT with continuous-flow cryostat, heater/PID control, and silicon diode sensor calibrated in a Quantum Design PPMS; aberration-corrected Thermo Fisher Spectra 300 at 300 kV with first-generation EMPAD detector, 1 mrad convergence semi-angle, 30 pA probe, 140 × 140 nm² scans at ~0.69 nm pixel size, 1 ms dwell plus 0.86 ms readout; abTEM/custom Python multislice simulations (60 nm thickness, 1 nm slices, frozen phonon, 30 configurations/slice); COM-shift mapping via custom Python; 2D autocorrelation from the inverse Fourier transform of summed power spectra of A(r)exp(iφ), radially averaged and exponentially fitted for ξ.

U.S. stocks finished mixed Friday as September nonfarm payrolls fell by 33,000—the first monthly decline in seven years—dampening sentiment after the S&P 500’s six-day record-high streak. Walgreens and CVS each fell 4.9% amid reports Amazon was close to deciding whether to sell prescription drugs. The Dow and S&P 500 slipped slightly, while the Nasdaq gained for a ninth consecutive day and posted its sixth record close. All three indexes rose for the week.

The dollar reached a two-month high against the yen and a seven-week high against the euro after September wage growth surprised investors, while payroll losses were attributed to Hurricanes Harvey and Irma. Improving U.S. data, prospects of tax cuts and a December Fed rate hike have supported the currency; markets priced the hike probability at 93%, up from 84%.

Fior Markets published a 2017 global Cooking Oil market analysis and forecast through 2022. The report examines market size, growth, share, revenue, trends, drivers, restraints, challenges, opportunities, technologies, leading players, and product, application, and regional segmentation, including the USA, Europe, Japan, China, India, and Southeast Asia. It draws on primary and secondary research, industry experts, and analyst recommendations.

PIMS staff continued a fifth day of protests demanding separation from SZABMU, sealing the vice-chancellor’s office and forcing Prof. Javed Akram out. CADD and Law ministries said the PIMS amendment bill’s summary would go to the prime minister and be tabled in Parliament after legal formalities and observations were addressed. Akram offered to resign but urged that medical services continue for up to 20,000 daily patients. Despite assurances that separation had been agreed in principle, protesters maintained their strike. JI and CDA representatives joined them in solidarity.

After three opening wins, Dinbych were beaten by Wrexham in Division Two (North). Wrexham matched them try-for-try, led 12-10 at half-time and earned a losing bonus point. Dinbych had more territory and possession but were frustrated by Wrexham’s defence before taking the lead in the second half. Wrexham answered with a late converted try, while Dinbych held possession to shut them out. Dinbych 2nds lost 16-10 to Flint in Division Three (North), earning a losing bonus point.

The team says it is accustomed to loud arenas and heavy media attention. After a passive Game 7 loss to New Jersey, the players and coach emphasized that they did not skate or work hard enough, despite the difficulty of facing the Devils. They plan to improve, generate more shots against Martin Brodeur, and play a harder, less hesitant game in Game 8. The team remains confident in its structured approach, noting that it has responded to adversity and tight playoff games throughout the postseason.

Singapore Airlines will resume nonstop service between Singapore and Newark on Oct. 12, restoring a route it discontinued in 2013. The 9,537-mile flight is expected to become the world’s longest airline route, surpassing Qatar Airways’ 9,032-mile Doha-Auckland service, with scheduled flight times of 18 hours 45 minutes westbound and 18 hours 25 minutes eastbound. The airline will operate the route with the Airbus A350-900ULR, configured with 161 business- and premium-economy seats and no standard coach seats. Service will initially be three times weekly, with daily flights expected after a second ULR aircraft enters service. Newark will become Singapore Airlines’ fifth U.S. airport, and the carrier also plans to use the ULR aircraft on Singapore-Los Angeles nonstop flights.

An AOTA Academic Fieldwork Coordinators committee conducted an updated mapping review of U.S. occupational therapy fieldwork literature published from 1989 through October 2020. The review assessed the literature over approximately 30 years, mapped it to the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda–Revised (2018), education level (OT or OTA), and fieldwork level (Level I or II), and identified research gaps.

The review searched four bibliographic databases and the Journal of Occupational Therapy Education. Two reviewers independently screened abstracts and full texts, resolving discrepancies through discussion or full-committee review. Of 1,619 screened records, 67 met eligibility criteria. Most addressed OT Level II fieldwork. Fifty-five focused exclusively on OT, five combined OT and OTA, and one focused exclusively on OTA. Forty-six examined Level II exclusively, 16 Level I exclusively, and five both levels.

Mapping to the 2018 agenda showed that learner characteristics and competencies were addressed in 31 articles and instructional methods in 23. Socialization to the profession appeared in six, faculty development and resources in three, and four articles could not be mapped. No studies mapped to theory building, signature pedagogies, or diversity, inclusion, and equity. Overall, Level II OT fieldwork and two agenda categories dominated the literature, while Level I and OTA fieldwork remained substantially underrepresented.

Limitations included the absence of quality assessment, difficulty applying agenda categories designed primarily for didactic education, and inconsistent descriptions of fieldwork levels. The review also excluded non-U.S. studies, gray literature, and descriptive work without research questions.

The authors recommend shifting research toward underrepresented areas, including signature pedagogies such as active engagement, transformative learning, and constructivism; using collaborative team-science approaches involving diverse stakeholders; and incorporating fieldwork more explicitly into future revisions of the AOTA research agenda.

Egypt’s Antiquities Ministry announced a 4,400-year-old tomb near Cairo’s pyramids, likely belonging to Fifth Dynasty official Hetpet. Its wall paintings depict hunting and fishing, including a monkey gathering fruit and dancing before an orchestra. Excavation is underway on another tomb Hetpet is believed to have commissioned.

Peruvian police are considering expelling U.S. citizen John Dougherty and Canadian citizen Jennifer Moore for allegedly inciting rural protests against Hudbay Minerals’ Constancia copper mine. The ministry says they violated tourist-status conditions; the mine suspended operations amid demonstrations.

The article examines Turkey’s highly centralized, directorate-based education administration, arguing that top-down policymaking, appointments, and weak local participation limit accountability, transparency, democracy, efficiency, and responsiveness. It reviews literature on good, corporate, and public governance, emphasizing decentralized decision-making, stakeholder participation, diverse boards and commissions, independent monitoring, and sustainability. Although boards can slow decisions, create conflicts, and be affected by political ties, they distribute authority and can improve representation, knowledge-sharing, communication, and accountability.

The study’s purpose is to develop a Local Education Boards model for Turkey based on the education-management structures of OECD countries and the views of teachers and administrators. It also seeks to examine how OECD countries structure educational governance and how Turkish education could adopt a more modern, participatory system.

A mixed-method, exploratory sequential design was used. Qualitative evidence came from literature, MoNE and OECD reports, and the education systems of 16 OECD countries selected because their PISA and GDP figures exceeded OECD averages. A questionnaire, “How to Manage Education,” was then developed for teachers and administrators in Seyhan district, Adana. The target sample was 370, although 421 people participated. Test-retest correlations were 0.961 for test averages and 0.960 for percentages, while Cronbach’s alpha was 0.978. The proposed model also incorporated the authors’ academic and administrative experience and the quantitative participants’ views.

Findings showed that 61.5% of respondents preferred local administration rather than central administration, and 61% favored elected boards or commissions. Forty-one percent wanted provincial education boards or commissions to lead decentralization, while 32% preferred existing directorates. Respondents supported broad participation by education officials, teachers, principals, students, parents, unions, universities, local authorities, professional organizations, and other representatives. They also favored transferring 22 of 27 administrative duties to local units, while leaving the central ministry responsible for broad objectives, legal procedures, regulations, policy frameworks, monitoring, evaluation, and auditing.

The proposed model includes a National Education Supreme Council for national policy and planning; a central Ministry organization for implementation, oversight, budgets, and technical support; and an autonomous Higher Education Council. At the local level, provincial or district education boards would formulate regional policies, supervise subordinate bodies, and select education directors. Provincial or district organizations would implement decisions and oversee personnel, finance, facilities, curricula, materials, and school operations. Vocational education boards would coordinate regional vocational policy with universities and industry, while school boards would select administrators, manage budgets, plan instruction and activities, and conduct annual audits.

The authors recommend pilot testing the model under expert supervision, revising identified shortcomings, and undertaking further research into board composition and internal operations. The study is limited by its exploratory sequential design, its concentration on one district in the 2016–2017 academic year, its qualitative comparison of only 16 of 36 OECD countries, and the general rather than fully detailed development of the proposed model.

The lecture extends the collective Thomson-scattering spectrum using a spectral density constructed from the squared Fourier transform of electron density. A test-particle plasma response separates this into electron and ion components, although the scattered light comes only from electrons. For Maxwellian electron and ion distributions, the susceptibilities are \(\chi_e=\alpha^2w(\zeta_e)\) and \(\chi_i=\alpha^2(zT_e/T_i)w(\zeta_i)\), where \(\alpha=1/(k\lambda_{D,e})\).

As \(\alpha^2\to0\), collective plasma responses vanish and the spectrum becomes proportional to the electron distribution function, reproducing incoherent scattering. At high frequencies, ions contribute negligibly, while resonances in the electron response recover the electron-plasma-wave dispersion relation, \(\omega_{EPW}^2=\omega_{pe}^2+3T_ek^2/m_e\). These peaks provide information about density and electron temperature; their broadening reflects electron temperature and Landau damping.

At low frequencies, ion-acoustic modes dominate. They are damped and effectively absent when \(zT_e/T_i<3\), while stronger resonances appear above this threshold. Their approximate dispersion is
\[
\omega_{IAW}^2=k^2\left[\alpha^2\left(1+\frac{zT_e}{m_i}\right)+\frac{3T_i}{m_i}\right].
\]
For \(zT_e/T_i\ll1\), the spectrum resembles the ion distribution function; near unity it has a hybrid shape; and for \(zT_e/T_i\gg1\), strong ion-acoustic resonances appear.

A Saltpeter approximation for the frequency-integrated cross section separates electron and ion features. Ion scattering becomes more important as \(\alpha\) increases, while the direct electron feature can disappear at large \(\alpha\). Because electron-plasma and ion-acoustic frequencies are widely separated, spectrometer selection is an important practical constraint.

Ion-acoustic spectra can yield electron temperature, ion temperature, ion bulk velocity, and electron-ion drift. Asymmetry between oppositely directed ion-acoustic peaks indicates drift; fitting the spectrum for drift and combining it with density can determine the local current component and, with spatial measurements and symmetry assumptions, infer a magnetic field. Electron-plasma waves are needed to determine electron density. Magnetic-field measurements are difficult because cyclotron modulation requires precise perpendicular viewing geometry.

Collisions generally damp coherent features and modify the measured spectrum, so neglecting them can lead to incorrect interpretation. Spatial gradients, velocity shear, turbulence, finite collection volumes, and finite detector acceptance can blend or broaden spectral features and bias inferred temperatures or densities. Smaller collection volumes and apertures reduce these effects but lower signal, requiring more laser power; excessive power causes absorption and plasma instabilities.

Current research includes accelerating calculations for non-Maxwellian distributions and developing multi-angle scattering systems that recover two- or three-dimensional distribution information.

A judge declined to delay an order allowing transgender people to enlist in the military from January 1, 2018. The Pentagon is preparing to comply, while the Justice Department is reviewing legal options.

Texas HB 8 replaces STAAR with three shorter tests at the beginning, middle and end of the school year, launching in 2027-28. Districts may choose from TEA-approved assessments for the first two tests, while the agency will create the third. Scores will use Texas peer percentile rankings and be released about two days after testing. The law bans practice and grade 3-8 benchmark tests and directs the TEA to examine testing’s role in school accountability.

Supporters say the changes will reduce preparation time, track growth throughout the year and codify practices already used by many districts. Critics fear three exams, combined with existing STAAR procedures such as lengthy sessions and lockdown-style rules, will increase stress and anxiety. They also note that schools will remain heavily dependent on end-of-year test results until a required progress measure is developed, and that measure will not be available until 2029-30.

Parents and educators want less restrictive testing-day procedures and greater teacher input. An educator committee will review the new end-of-year exam, while some districts hope the approved assessment options include MAP, an adaptive test that measures student growth and generally causes less disruption than STAAR. Debate also continues over whether eliminating practice tests will reduce or worsen student anxiety.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft’s upcoming DirectStorage API to stream compressed game assets directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU for lossless decompression. This offloads work from the CPU, claims twofold I/O performance improvement, and is described as delivering up to 100× throughput with 20× lower CPU utilization on Turing and Ampere GPUs.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing, offering up to 2× FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to 5× AI/data-science throughput (10× with sparsity), PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, and 48 GB of memory expandable to 96 GB through NVLink. It supports virtualization, Quadro Sync, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K120 and 8K60 displays through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including HDR and Display Stream Compression. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for common codecs, including AV1, while GA10x GPUs can decode 8K60 HDR AV1 with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding for streaming and archiving, supporting up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC while reducing CPU demand.

The GA10x architecture provides up to 2× improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core adds concurrent ray tracing and shading, while its third-generation Tensor Core supports structural sparsity. It is also the first GPU architecture to support GDDR6X, reaching 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth in the GeForce RTX 3090.

The GeForce RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores and is stated to be 1.5× faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X, lacks NVLink, and is stated to outperform the previous RTX 2080 Ti.

New GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay technology detects faulty memory transmissions and retries them, helping identify memory-overclocking limits and reducing errors.

The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB of GDDR6, second-generation RT Cores, hardware-accelerated ray tracing and motion blur, AI denoising, and dual-board NVLink expansion to 96 GB. Performance charts cover professional rendering, HPC, and deep-learning workloads. The document closes with NVIDIA’s accuracy, warranty, licensing, product-use, and liability disclaimers.

A vulnerability in widely used Atlassian Jira and Confluence software enabled XSS and SSRF attacks that could expose AWS secret access keys, potentially allowing attackers to take over instances, steal data, or destroy it. NIST rated the flaw 6.1/10; patches exist, but many legacy deployments remain exposed. Researcher Robert Wiggins found over a dozen vulnerable deployments at major companies. Several organizations updated or secured theirs, while three unnamed companies remained vulnerable. Many more may exist, and updating Atlassian software is recommended.

England qualified for the 2018 World Cup after a disappointing 1–0 win over Slovenia, but Southgate’s cautious 4-2-3-1 could lead to another group-stage exit. He is urged to use three centre-backs with advanced wing-backs, deploy Dele Alli as No. 10, keep Sterling on the wing, and exploit Rashford’s speed and Kane’s finishing. Alli’s suspension highlighted his value, while Lallana could add creativity. Southgate should also approach upcoming friendlies against Brazil and Germany courageously, as England have little to lose without a new tactical direction.

Spotify, Comcast and Oracle recently announced co-CEO arrangements, joining companies such as Netflix, Salesforce, Sony Interactive Entertainment and Chipotle that have used the model. Despite its high-profile adoption, co-CEO-led companies represent about 1.2% of the Russell 3000. A Harvard Business Review analysis found that two-CEO companies generated average annual shareholder returns of 9.5% from 1996 to 2020, versus 6.9% for single-leader companies.

Experts said success depends on clearly defined responsibilities, effective communication, alignment and shared accountability. Unclear authority can create power struggles, ambiguity and confusion, while the model also requires two compensation packages. Co-CEOs can provide continuity and help prepare successors, as Comcast’s promotion of President Mike Cavanagh alongside Brian Roberts may do. However, experts urged Comcast to establish explicit authority over operations, strategy and final decisions. Spotify named Gustav Söderström and Alex Norström to succeed founder Daniel Ek, while Oracle appointed two chiefs as Safra Catz became executive chair and co-founder Larry Ellison remained chairman.

This ebook from the U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian contains the full text of *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1902: Whaling and Sealing Claims Against Russia, Appendix I*. The ebook includes search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access; readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than printed page numbers.

Appendix I presents an English translation of a memorandum submitted to arbitrator T. M. C. Asser under the September 3, 1900 exchange of notes between the United States and Russia. As counsel and agent for the United States, Herbert H. D. Peirce sought indemnity for the owners, officers, and crews of the bark *Cape Horn Pigeon* and the schooners *James Hamilton Lewis*, *C. H. White*, and *Kate and Anna*, whose vessels were arrested and seized by Russian agents. John Hay transmitted Peirce’s dispatch to Senator H. C. Lodge, who was asked to arrange printing of the translated memorandum as a public document. The claims were referred to the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations and ordered printed on December 12, 1901.

NVIDIA Corporation filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the 13-week third quarter of fiscal 2016, ended October 25, 2015. The company was a large accelerated filer, and 538 million common shares were outstanding as of November 13, 2015.

Third-quarter revenue was $1.305 billion, up 7% from $1.225 billion a year earlier. Gross profit rose to $734 million from $676 million, operating income increased to $245 million from $213 million, and net income rose to $246 million from $173 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.44 versus $0.31. For the first nine months, revenue increased 5% to $3.609 billion, gross profit rose to $2.020 billion, and operating income declined to $495 million from $528 million. Nine-month net income fell to $406 million from $437 million, while diluted earnings per share declined to $0.72 from $0.77. Gross margin was 56.3% for the quarter and 56.0% for the nine months, compared with 55.2% and 55.4%, respectively. The quarter included a $49 million tax-reserve release related to Icera modem operations, while the nine months included a $27 million deferred-tax-asset write-down.

GPU revenue rose 12% for the quarter to $1.110 billion and 9% for the nine months to $3.009 billion; segment operating income was $367 million and $917 million, respectively. High-end GeForce gaming revenue increased 40% in the quarter and more than 30% for the nine months, while Quadro and mainstream OEM GPU revenue declined. Tegra Processor revenue fell 23% for the quarter to $129 million and 14% for the nine months to $402 million, producing operating losses of $65 million and $164 million. OEM smartphone and tablet sales declined more than 80% in the quarter and almost 90% for the nine months, partially offset by automotive growth of more than 50% and 75%, respectively, along with higher development-service and SHIELD sales. “All Other” revenue, primarily Intel patent licensing, remained $66 million for the quarter and $198 million for the nine months, with operating losses of $57 million and $258 million.

At October 25, 2015, total assets were $7.174 billion, including $471 million of cash, $4.257 billion of marketable securities and $425 million of inventory. Long-term convertible debt was $1.406 billion and shareholders’ equity was $4.465 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $664 million, compared with $463 million a year earlier; investing activities used $187 million, and financing activities used $503 million.

Third-quarter stock-based compensation was $51 million, compared with $42 million a year earlier, and nine-month expense was $145 million, compared with $115 million. Research and development spending declined 3% for the quarter and 2% for the nine months, partly because of the Icera wind-down and organizational efficiencies. Sales, general and administrative expense rose 24% and 22%, respectively, largely because of $15 million and $55 million of litigation-related legal fees.

Recent GPU developments included NVIDIA GRID 2.0 with Microsoft Azure integration, the GeForce GTX 950, GameWorks VR and Pascal architecture plans. Tegra-related developments included NVIDIA-powered vehicles from Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Porsche, Bentley and Honda, Tesla’s Model X, GeForce NOW and expanded SHIELD sales in Europe. More than 50 automotive companies were using the DRIVE PX platform.

NVIDIA completed a $400 million accelerated share repurchase in October, repurchasing 18 million shares at an average price of $21.63. It returned $604 million to shareholders during the first nine months through $452 million of repurchases and $152 million of dividends. On November 9, the company began a separate $135 million accelerated repurchase and received three million shares. It subsequently raised the quarterly dividend 18% to $0.115 per share and announced an intention to return approximately $1.0 billion in fiscal 2017.

The Icera modem wind-down generated $8 million of restructuring charges in the quarter and $97 million over nine months, primarily for severance and asset impairments. NVIDIA expected another $25 million to $35 million of charges in the fourth quarter, affecting about 5% of its workforce. It also recorded a $21 million charge for the SHIELD 8-inch tablet recall.

Patent litigation with Qualcomm and Samsung remained pending. An ITC administrative law judge initially found no violation in NVIDIA’s case, and NVIDIA sought full-commission review. Five Samsung patent claims remained for trial in January 2016, while Samsung’s false-advertising claim had been dismissed and one asserted patent had been ruled noninfringement. NVIDIA recorded no liability for these matters because potential losses were not considered probable and could not be reasonably estimated.

All cash equivalents and marketable securities were classified as available for sale, with $4.353 billion of combined fair value at quarter-end. Unrealized losses totaled $3 million and were considered temporary, with no impairment charges recorded. The company also entered a $200 million cash-flow-hedge interest-rate swap related to financing for its new headquarters and adopted guidance addressing inventory valuation, debt issuance costs, cloud-computing arrangements and revenue recognition.

In this Court of Claims action, Berenice M. Brubaker (later substituted by Ralph Hartwell Brubaker as administrator of her estate) sought damages for four State appropriations of her roughly 365-acre tract near Massena, N.Y., for the International Rapids section of the St. Lawrence River project. The tract was bisected by Middle Road, with about 183 acres north of it and the remainder south, bounded by Denison Cross Road, and it was surrounded by property owned by the Aluminum Company of America and the St. Lawrence River Power Company. It was unimproved, unused since 1945–46, and served by drainage and sight easements. The northern portion was zoned agricultural, the southern portion industrial.

The appropriations were: May 19, 1955, all property north of Middle Road (Parcels 148 and 185); June 12, 1956, a .15-acre flooding easement (Parcel 2202); April 1, 1957, 25.34 acres with reserved farm-use and ingress-and-egress rights (Parcel 2159); and May 1, 1957, a 55.38-acre electric transmission line easement (Parcel 2169). Claimant asserted $309,000 in damages; the State claimed $28,000–$40,000. Claimant's experts valued the whole tract at $331,200–$368,275 in May 1955 but included increases attributable to the project; the State's experts found agricultural use north of Middle Road and residential frontage/industrial rear use south of it, and one found no enhancement from the project.

Applying United States v. Miller and Shoemaker v. United States, the court held that the rule excluding project-caused value increments requires an open and notorious designation of the probable condemnation area, and no such proof existed for the 1955 taking, so claimant's experts' conclusions were inadmissible (though their factual testimony was admitted); the Reynolds Aluminum and General Motors purchases were likewise excluded as reflecting project enhancement. The land north of Middle Road, however, was as suitable for industrial use as the southern portion, and there was no consequential damage to the remainder.

For the later takings, the court found the southern land was adjacent property outside the original project limits, so its value as enhanced by proximity had to be paid: the .15-acre flooding easement fell entirely within the existing drainage easement ($100); the 25.34-acre taking reduced the southern property from $88,500 to $48,750, awarding $12,675 direct and $27,075 consequential damage ($39,750), with no consequential damage east or north; and the transmission line easement destroyed the remaining market value in the 55.38 acres, awarding $27,700. The court awarded $32,000 for the 1955 taking, valuing it for industrial use despite agricultural zoning, with specified periods of interest on each award. The claim was unassigned, and the decision was the signed written decision upon which judgment could be entered.

The application describes a display device with a substrate, thin-film transistors, pixel electrodes, emission members, opposing electrodes, and an encapsulation portion that alternately deposits organic and inorganic layers to prevent moisture and oxygen penetration. A planarization layer containing organic material covers at least part of the encapsulation portion’s downward-sloping edge. Its edge forms a larger angle with the substrate than the encapsulation edge, potentially at least 70 degrees, thereby providing a sharp profile and an expanded, substantially flat upper surface.

The planarization layer may cover the entire encapsulation portion or mainly its edge, while exposing part of the encapsulation portion elsewhere. Patterns, including touch electrodes and touch wiring, may be formed on it. The expanded flat area permits touch-sensor patterns closer to the display edge, reducing dead space and bezel size. The planarization layer may also reduce parasitic capacitance between the opposing electrode and touch-sensor patterns, improving touch sensitivity. Capacitive touch sensors may use alternating electrode arrangements with mutual-sensing or self-sensing capacitors.

Against UCLA’s high-post rub, the preferred NBA defense is “show and recover” rather than switch. The screener shows to force the cutter inside; the chasing defender then recovers into pass denial, while weakside defenders pack the lane. On the final matchup, defenders pressure the ball, deny passes, and front or push posts away from the block. The “All Out SOS” approach disrupts the offense by trapping the wing on the first pass. Because the point guard cuts low, reversing the ball is difficult. When the trapped wing passes, defenders rotate using the near-player concept, close out on the open wing, front the low post, and deny the high post. Rotations begin as the pass leaves the passer’s hands.

At oral arguments in *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, a substantial majority of justices appeared willing to reverse lower courts’ finding that Republican Rep. Michael Bost lacked standing to challenge Illinois’s 14-day mail-ballot receipt deadline. The justices debated whether a candidate must show a substantial risk of electoral disadvantage, an effect on the election’s outcome, or reputational harm. Justice Kagan favored a relatively low threshold, while Justices Sotomayor and Jackson appeared skeptical of Bost’s claim because his seat was considered safe. Justice Kavanaugh and the government raised concerns about delaying pre-election litigation and devising a remedy if deadlines are found unlawful.

Y-Cross is a drop-back passing concept used from varied formations and against multiple coverages. It is a weak-side flood design built around a post route, a crosser, and an RB stretching the flat toward the boundary, with backside route combinations giving the QB progression options. The TE or a speedy slot receiver may run the crossing route.

The concept is effective against man coverage because the post and crosser run away from defenders, and against Cover 4 because the post may beat the boundary safety over the top. Cover 3 is less favorable when the post is the primary throw because the high safety occupies the middle, though other combinations can be used against any defense.

Against man and zone, the TE releases inside the Sam and over the Mike to a landmark of 18–22 yards; the FB checks protection and flares wide; the TB checks down off Will; X runs a post over the free safety; and Z runs a 15-yard speed-cut dig. The base QB progression is post, deep crosser, then RB check-down or backside dig. Against two-high defenses, the QB can high-low the post based on the safety’s movement, then read the Will linebacker before the crosser. Variations include reading a post-wheel combination first and adding a backside curl-flat tag, especially against one-high defenses.

The study combined in-situ SEM four-point-probe measurements with XRD, EDS, and EBSD to separate electrical contributions in overaged Al-Mg-Si alloys. Bulk resistivity was measured by the Van der Pauw method, while microscale probes measured resistivity within grain interiors and across individual Si and Mg2Si precipitates.

Increasing Si and Mg content generally increased bulk resistivity because the secondary-phase volume fraction rose. Among the applied heat treatments, 350°C for 72 hours produced the lowest resistivity for every composition. Grain-interior resistivity, including the Al solid solution and nanoscale precipitates, depended on heat treatment rather than composition; alloys of different compositions treated identically had similar values of 2.81–2.88 μΩ cm. No clear correlation was found between lattice parameters and grain-interior resistivity.

Microscale measurements across Si and Mg2Si precipitates yielded indistinguishable effective resistivities despite differences in morphology, showing that both phases contribute equally and that precipitate volume fraction is more important than phase identity. For each heat treatment, bulk resistivity increased linearly with total Mg and Si concentration, with fitted coefficients depending on the treatment. Vacancies, dislocations, and grain boundaries were neglected because of their low densities, leaving grain interiors and secondary precipitates as the principal contributors.

Bitcoin reached a six-week high as reports of possible entry by major financial institutions lifted cryptocurrency sentiment. The price rose 4.4% to $9,340.88, while total cryptocurrency market capitalization reached $427 billion and 24-hour trading volume hit $28 billion. Reports cited Goldman Sachs hiring a digital-assets markets head, Barclays assessing client interest in a crypto trading desk, and a survey finding one in five financial institutions considering cryptocurrency trading. Increased regulatory scrutiny remains an unresolved challenge.

Only five DWI arrests were made in Wichita Falls over St. Patrick’s Day weekend. Year-to-date arrests fell from 39 in 2016 and 38 in 2017 to 25 this year. Sgt. Harold McClure cited greater awareness, rideshare options, sober drivers, and police presence as possible contributors.

This study conducts a bibliometric citation analysis of artificial intelligence in STEM education research published from 2020 to 2024. Data were obtained from Dimensions using “artificial intelligence” and “stem education” search terms, yielding 101 initial documents and a final dataset of 35 journal articles analyzed with Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer.

The analysis reports that 15 articles received 234 citations in 2024, averaging 15.62 citations per article. The United States led with nine documents and 103 citations, while China had five documents but no citations. Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson each had one article cited 55 times. The International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education received 55 citations, while “Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education” was the most-cited article with 55 citations. Carnegie Mellon University was the most-cited institution.

The literature identifies personalized learning, advanced analytics, instructional automation, improved engagement, and teacher support as major benefits of AI in STEM education. Challenges include ethics, data privacy, learner autonomy, limited AI literacy, and risks of excessive monitoring or control of learning. The study also notes limitations related to its database, timeframe, and reliance on citation counts as impact indicators. Proposed research directions include longitudinal studies, cross-cultural comparisons, ethical frameworks, AI-literacy development, and integration with technologies such as VR and AR.

The Trump administration's proposal to charge employers a $100,000 fee for new H-1B visas could endanger thousands of college jobs, though the proclamation took effect Sept. 21 and doesn't apply to current visa holders. As of June 30, more than 16,000 college and university workers held approved H-1B visas (16,797, about 5% of fiscal year 2025 totals), with at least 930 institutions employing at least one and an average of about 18 visas per institution. Nearly half of those visas were at just 50 institutions—mostly R-1 classifications, averaging 167 approvals each—and the top 100 universities held about 70% of all college and university visas. Applicants previously paid $2,000 to $5,000. The professional, scientific and technical services sector leads with 129,007 visas in fiscal year 2025, a vast majority held by workers from India. H-1B holders may work up to six years before reapplying, and universities, nonprofit research institutions and national labs are exempt from the 85,000 annual cap on new visas. The Homeland Security secretary may exempt groups if hiring foreign talent is in the national interest and poses no threat, and officials have said the fee appears aimed at large corporations. Experts doubt many colleges could afford the fee, while the National Postdoc Association warned it would create an enormous barrier for employers seeking global talent.

The passage presents EUR/USD as the world’s most widely traded currency pair, linking the euro and U.S. dollar to the economic influence of Europe and the United States. Its high liquidity, tight spreads, relatively low volatility, extensive market information, and 24-hour availability make it accessible to novice and experienced traders, although profitability is difficult and forex is described as a zero-sum market.

A comprehensive EUR/USD strategy should combine strict, quantifiable rules with risk management and backtesting. Technical methods include trend analysis, moving averages, support and resistance, Fibonacci retracements, candlestick patterns, breakouts, and momentum indicators. Fundamental analysis considers GDP, inflation, employment, PMIs, central-bank decisions, interest-rate differentials, political developments, and geopolitical events. Market sentiment can help identify initial short-term trends. Interest rates and inflation are presented as major long-term determinants; higher U.S. rates or unexpectedly strong U.S. inflation may strengthen the dollar and lower EUR/USD.

The described strategy was backtested with Yahoo Finance’s “EURUSD=X” data. It produced 713 trades and a reported 53% gain per trade, and the one-day holding period produced a smoother equity curve than the two-day alternative. The passage repeatedly stresses testing strategies before use and notes that spot-futures results may differ.

Trading activity is influenced by the European and U.S. sessions, with the greatest liquidity and volatility generally occurring during their overlap around midday or early afternoon GMT. ECB and Federal Reserve announcements can also create substantial volatility. Position trading holds positions for weeks or months and depends on macroeconomic analysis; swing trading holds positions for days or weeks; day trading and scalping seek short-term gains but are described as extremely difficult, with many traders losing money. Short-term trading requires disciplined position sizing, risk controls, and careful attention to reward-to-risk ratios.

Risk management includes appropriate position sizing, stop-loss or take-profit levels, avoiding excessive leverage, and trading uncorrelated pairs to diversify. Position risk recommendations range from 1% to 5% of account capital, while the position-trading section suggests limiting individual trades to no more than 1%. Leverage magnifies both profits and losses, and correlations often rise during volatile markets. Other covered approaches include carry trades based on rate differentials, hedging with opposite or uncorrelated positions, and adapting stops and exposure to market conditions.

EUR/USD can be traded through spot forex, futures, options, ETFs, and CFDs. CFDs require less capital but involve substantial risk and leverage. Traders are advised to compare platforms, fees, minimum accounts, regulation, security features, educational resources, and customer support when selecting brokers. Demo accounts allow practice without financial loss, although they do not reproduce the psychological effects of live trading; performance should be reviewed before moving to live markets, followed by continued learning and strategy refinement.

Common mistakes include excessive attention to individual news events, impulsive trading, lacking a clear backtested plan, poor risk management, failure to diversify, excessive leverage, inadequate performance monitoring, and insufficient demo practice.

Five European research institutions are collaborating to establish October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day and raise awareness of these microscopic algae. Coccolithophores remove carbon dioxide, release oxygen, support marine food webs, and form calcium-carbonate plates that sink to the seafloor, eventually creating chalk and limestone layers that record Earth’s climate history. Annually, they produce more than 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate, helping transfer carbon into deep-sea sediments for millennia. Climate change is altering ocean temperatures, chemistry, and nutrients, threatening the plankton and dependent ecosystems. Research teams in the UK, Norway, Croatia, Portugal, and through the International Nannoplankton Association are studying coccolithophore carbon uptake, ecological interactions, fossil records, and responses to changing oceans. The campaign aims to increase ocean literacy, public engagement, and policy attention to the organisms’ role in climate regulation and marine ecosystem stability.

This retrospective cross-disorder study analyzed primary-care records from the UK THIN database to compare prodromal symptoms and medication use before diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD; 20,214 patients), Parkinson’s disease (PD; 28,222), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB; 4,682), and 20,214 controls. Selected UK Biobank cohorts were used for replication. Analyses examined 12 health conditions and preselected medication classes in three pre-diagnosis periods, adjusting primarily for age and sex.

All health conditions were more frequent than in controls during the five years before diagnosis. Memory problems predominated before AD, tremor before PD, and confusion, hallucinations, memory problems, and autonomic symptoms before DLB. Constipation, urinary dysfunction, and hypotension occurred before all three disorders but were more strongly associated with PD and DLB; falls were particularly frequent before DLB. Antidepressant, anxiolytic, and constipation treatments were more frequently prescribed, while antihypertensive and antidiabetic use was generally lower before diagnosis. Beta-blockers were prescribed more often before PD and DLB than AD, neuroleptics more often before DLB, and statins less often before PD than before AD or DLB. UK Biobank replication confirmed lower statin use before PD than AD (OR 0.77, p=0.01).

Among patients with PD, prescriptions for hypercholesterolemia, constipation, depression, and psychosis during the five years before PD diagnosis remained independently associated with dementia developing within the following five years; hypertension and anxiety treatments were not individually associated.

The authors emphasized the long prodromal phase and possible predictive value of primary-care records, while noting that delayed diagnoses, overlapping disease boundaries, control matching, retrospective design, and limited UK Biobank sampling constrained interpretation and prevented causal conclusions.

Tesla Motors, Inc. reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2015 in its Form 10-Q. The company designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles, powertrain components and energy-storage products. It was producing the Model S, developing the Model X and planning Model 3 deliveries for late 2017. As of July 30, 2015, 127,142,147 common shares were outstanding.

Second-quarter revenue was $955.0 million, up from $769.3 million in 2014, primarily due to increased Model S deliveries. Automotive revenue rose to $878.1 million from $727.8 million, while services and other revenue increased to $76.9 million from $41.5 million. Gross profit was nearly unchanged at $213.4 million, but gross margin declined to 22.3% from 27.7%, reflecting product and regional mix, manufacturing inefficiencies, obsolete inventory and lower regulatory-credit revenue. Operating expenses rose to $383.6 million from $241.7 million, including higher research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses. The company reported an operating loss of $170.2 million and a net loss of $184.2 million, or $1.45 per share, compared with a net loss of $61.9 million, or $0.50 per share, in the prior-year quarter.

For the six months ended June 30, 2015, revenue was $1.895 billion versus $1.390 billion in 2014. Gross profit was $473.4 million, while the operating loss widened to $272.6 million and the net loss to $338.4 million, or $2.68 per share. Operating cash flow was negative $291.3 million, compared with positive $57.1 million in 2014. Investing activities used $855.2 million, primarily for $831.2 million of capital expenditures, while financing activities provided $404.5 million. Cash and cash equivalents declined to $1.151 billion from $1.906 billion at December 31, 2014.

At June 30, 2015, total assets were $6.468 billion, total liabilities were $5.702 billion and stockholders’ equity was $715.9 million. Inventory rose to $1.212 billion from $953.7 million, largely because of vehicles in transit and pre-owned vehicles, while net property, plant and equipment increased to $2.646 billion from $1.829 billion. Tesla reported $114.3 million borrowed under a warehouse facility and $50.0 million under a $500 million asset-based revolving credit facility. The company also had convertible senior notes due in 2018, 2019 and 2021.

Tesla continued to offer resale-value guarantees and leases through financial partners and Tesla Finance. It had provided guarantees to approximately 13,600 Model S customers, with $67.7 million exercisable within the following year relating to 1,635 vehicles. Approximately 2,300 vehicles had been leased through Tesla Finance and 2,100 through a banking partner.

Management expected 2015 Model S and Model X deliveries of 50,000 to 55,000, with Model X customer deliveries targeted for late in the third quarter and a production ramp in the fourth quarter. Combined Model S and Model X production was expected to reach 1,600 to 1,800 vehicles per week in 2016, with capacity for up to 2,000. Capital expenditures were expected to be approximately $1.5 billion in 2015, while operating expenses were expected to increase 45% to 50%. The Supercharger network had 480 locations globally and was expected to grow by about 50% during 2015. Construction of the Gigafactory continued, with first production anticipated in early 2016; Tesla had incurred $206.6 million of construction costs by June 30.

A securities class action filed in 2013 had been dismissed with prejudice, but the plaintiffs’ appeal was pending. The filing cautioned that forward-looking plans and expectations were subject to risks, including production ramp difficulties, supply constraints, lower gross margins, expansion costs and Gigafactory execution.

The article explains gold trading, its history, and several strategies. Gold is a widely traded precious metal used historically for jewelry, worship, currency, and as a store of value. Traders can speculate on its price through futures, options, spot markets, shares, CFDs, and ETFs; most transactions are cash-settled without physical delivery. Gold prices can fluctuate sharply because of supply and demand and political, social, and economic unrest. Gold may also serve as a “safe haven” and hedge against losses in stocks and bonds.

The focus is a weekend swing strategy that holds gold from Thursday’s close until Monday’s open. The strategy was backtested using GLD from late 2004 through September 2021. Buying Thursday’s close and selling Friday’s close averaged 0.14% per trade with a 1.4 profit factor; holding until Monday’s open averaged 0.19% with a 1.3 profit factor. Adding one parameter improved the results, which the authors considered potentially suitable for small positions. They also note gold’s positive overnight bias and suggest testing futures and alternative entry and exit times.

The study assessed reporting on health-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the latest Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) from 18 Eastern Mediterranean Region countries submitted between 2016 and 2021. It examined 50 health-related SDG targets and indicators, including 32 linked to SDG3, and compared reported data availability with WHO/EMRO data for 47 indicators across mortality, morbidity, means of implementation, risk factors, and determinants.

All 18 countries reported having SDG monitoring mechanisms. Eleven reported on all 17 SDGs, while the others covered seven to 12; reporting was generally more comprehensive in higher-income countries. Although 17 VNRs described adapting targets to national contexts, only eight explicitly stated 2030 country targets for some indicators. Fourteen identified limited data availability as a monitoring challenge, commonly attributing it to insufficient human-resource capacity and also citing poor data quality, limited statistical tools, weak transparency, and inadequate disaggregation.

Maternal mortality, neonatal mortality, and under-five mortality were the most frequently reported indicators, at 100%, 83%, and 78%, respectively. Trend reporting was less common: Qatar alone reported trends for all SDG3 indicators, while other countries covered no more than nine. On average, VNRs included data for about 11 SDG3 indicators and 6.4 non-SDG3 indicators, and frequently omitted routinely reported WHO/EMRO data. Twenty-nine of the 32 SDG3 indicators could be derived from civil registration and vital statistics, national surveys, disease surveillance, and routine health information systems; reporting was highest for indicators based on civil registration and disease surveillance.

The review identified major gaps in data availability, reporting, analytical capacity, and national health information systems. It concluded that stronger regulatory frameworks, collection capacity, civil registration and vital statistics systems, and population-based surveys are needed to improve access to quality data and support progress toward health-related SDGs.

Princeton scientists and international collaborators developed Diag2Diag, an AI system that uses fusion sensor data to generate detailed synthetic measurements that other diagnostics cannot capture, particularly at the plasma edge. Using data from the DIII-D National Fusion Facility, the system aligned with real-world measurements and revealed more about plasma behavior, including evidence supporting the theory that resonant magnetic perturbations suppress edge-localized modes by flattening temperature and density through magnetic islands.

By reducing the need for diagnostic hardware, Diag2Diag could make commercial fusion reactors more compact, affordable, reliable, and easier to maintain. Researchers also see potential applications in other fusion diagnostics, spacecraft, and robotic surgery, where recovering missing or degraded sensor data could improve system reliability. The research was published in Nature Communications.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit SAR data-acquisition device with a differential analog front end, programmable input ranges, an ADC driver, an internal precision reference and buffer, alarm functions, and a multiSPI digital interface.

At maximum sampling rates, the ADC input’s sample-and-hold capacitors must charge and discharge within the acquisition window. The integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise, stable input buffer is intended to meet this requirement.

The device supports an internal or external reference, selected through the INTREF_DIS bit of RANGE_SEL_REG. The internal reference has a nominal 4.096-V output, drives REFIO, and requires at least a 4.7-µF REFIO-to-REFGND decoupling capacitor. REFIO cannot directly drive external loads; an acceptable op-amp buffer is required if an external load must be driven. Mechanical and thermal stress, including soldering and reflow, can shift the internal reference voltage, and multiple reflows can cause additional shifts. The reference is temperature-compensated over −40°C to +125°C. External-reference mode applies a 4.096-V source to REFIO, while the internal buffer drives REFCAP; REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1-µF decoupling capacitor. Typical reference-buffer temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C, with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs and produces straight-binary output. Full-scale range equals positive full scale minus negative full scale, and LSB size equals FSR/2^16.

An active-high alarm output can be assigned to the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin. Input alarms compare converted input values against programmable high and low thresholds with programmable hysteresis. AVDD alarms use fixed typical trip points of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped flags are stored in ALARM_REG; active flags clear after each conversion, while tripped flags remain set until the register is read. Alarms may be observed through the pin, registers, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface exchanges commands and data through 32-bit input and output shift registers. It supports standard SPI, single- or dual-SDO legacy protocols, source-synchronous operation, and daisy-chained devices. In a daisy chain, devices require identical register settings, an optimal frame of 32×N SCLK capture edges for N devices, and MSB-first data returning from the last device to the first.

The device has three functional states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV. The active-low RST input can initiate either a power-on reset or an application reset according to RSTn_APP. Holding RST high allows CONVST/CS transitions to control acquisition and conversion. Conversion begins on the rising edge of CONVST/CS and completes after the specified conversion time; RVS can signal completion. ACQ state supports a low-power NAP mode.

A data-transfer frame begins when CONVST/CS goes low and ends when it rises for conversion. During the frame, commands and data shift through SDI and output data shift through the selected SDO pins. Writes require 32 clocks; short frames cannot execute writes but can provide valid output bits, while long frames execute the last 32 shifted command bits. Output can contain fixed test patterns, register-read data, or the latest conversion result, optionally followed by device address, range, alarm, and parity flags.

The nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power control, SDI protocol, SDO protocol, output formatting, reference and input-range selection, alarms, and alarm thresholds. SPI protocol selection supports four CPOL/CPHA combinations. Dual-SDO mode uses SDO-0 and SDO-1 and can transfer a given number of bits in half as many clock cycles as single-SDO mode. Source-synchronous mode provides an output clock on RVS that is synchronized to either SCLK or the internal device clock.

An eight-channel industrial input-module design combines the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to support software-configured voltage or current channels. The ADS868xW supports bipolar and unipolar ranges, including inputs up to ±12.288 V, and includes overvoltage protection and input and AVDD alarms. An NTC-thermistor example uses programmable input thresholds and hysteresis for temperature monitoring.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies. Recommended decoupling includes at least 10 µF and 1 µF on AVDD and at least 10 µF near DVDD. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption; power-down retains registers and keeps the interface active. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital routing, keeps bypass capacitors close to supply and reference pins, avoids vias between pins and capacitors, and connects grounds through short, low-impedance paths. Proper ESD handling is required.

The 5-Day Low of the Range Strategy goes long at the close when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is below the previous five days’ lowest low, typically exiting after five days. From January 1993 onward, it produced 309 winners among 517 trades, a 60% win rate, and an average return of 0.46% per trade versus 0.11% for any five-day period. Profitability peaks at three to seven days; a five-day exit reportedly yields 10.76% annualized over 510 market days, compared with 2,826 days for buy-and-hold. Performance has weakened recently. A short-selling version uses a 0.75 range criterion, or 0.9 for similar trade frequency, and returned nearly 10%, but short strategies are described as harder and less profitable.

The passage reviews 10 AI content generators and writing tools for 2022, comparing their content formats, SEO features, originality checks, usability, pricing, and limitations. Frase specializes in SEO research, content briefs, keyword optimization, competitor analysis, and content-opportunity insights. Rytr supports blog posts, school papers, social captions, product descriptions, and meta descriptions in 30+ languages and tones, with a plagiarism checker and limited free plan. Another free tool provides marketing, website, and blog copy alongside tone, grammar, and plagiarism checkers.
