Central-laboratory RT-PCR was accurate but slow and reliant on nasopharyngeal swab collection, while early point-of-care assays required additional sample handling that risked contamination, patient identification errors, and operator exposure. The Sal6830 saliva test addresses these issues through patient self-collection directly into a sealed cartridge, with results available in approximately 30 minutes.

At two U.S. clinics, six healthcare workers without laboratory training evaluated 48 blinded samples. All 24 negative samples tested negative; 23 of 24 positive samples tested positive, and one was invalid. The same operators then compared Sal6830 saliva testing with the Cepheid Xpert Xpress nasopharyngeal assay in 119 suspected COVID-19 patients aged 5 years or older. Overall agreement was 93.3%, with positive agreement of 87.2% and negative agreement of 97.2%.

All nine usability survey participants found the system easy to use and results easy to interpret, required no technical support, and were confident operating it without laboratory training. Eight would “definitely recommend” the device and one would “probably recommend” it. The study concluded that Sal6830 can provide accurate point-of-care results with self-collected saliva while eliminating additional sample handling and nurse-collected nasopharyngeal swabs.

Neural Radiance Cache uses a neural shader trained on live game data to infer indirect illumination from path-traced rays after one bounce, approximating many-bounce lighting. It reduces GPU computation, improves real-time global illumination performance and quality, and adapts to varied gameplay scenarios.
Washington appealed a Spokane County judgment; the appellate court reversed and remanded.

In New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen, the Supreme Court adopted a two-step test for Second Amendment challenges: courts first determine whether the amendment’s plain text covers the challenged conduct, then shift the burden to the government to show that its regulation is consistent with the nation’s historical tradition of firearm regulation. Critics argue that this approach requires judges to perform historical research beyond their expertise. The passage responds that judges are lawyers, not historians, and that their task is to decide cases using historical evidence rather than to reconstruct history for its own sake.

Originalists contend that this distinction limits historical uncertainty because legal records are relatively durable and courts must resolve disputes even when the evidence is incomplete. The Second Amendment’s text is generally clear: “people” means members of the political community, “keep” means have, “bear” means carry, and “arms” means weapons. The harder inquiry is whether modern regulations fit an established historical tradition, a question informed by legislative records, statutes, judicial decisions, administrative records, treatises, and manuals. Courts can also manage uncertainty through ordinary legal tools, including assigning burdens of proof; challengers initially must establish textual coverage, after which the government must justify the regulation historically. Means-ends scrutiny does not avoid the historical inquiry and may improperly assign judges a legislative role. Ultimately, understanding the law’s past is necessary because legal knowledge remains incomplete without it.

The application describes a voice-directed inspection system that enables multiple inspectors to work concurrently on the same business asset. A host computer creates or supplies inspection plans to site computers, which divide plans into sections that can be assigned to inspection assistance devices. Each device includes a portable computer and headset, provides audible inspection prompts through speech synthesis, captures spoken results through speech recognition, and sends completion updates to the site computer for aggregation and transmission to the host.

Inspection devices may request a specific unfinished section or any available section. The site computer determines whether multiple unfinished, noninterfering sections exist and distributes them according to factors such as priority, request order, inspector qualifications, or prior work on the asset. Multiple inspector identifiers may be associated with one plan and asset. Updates may be transmitted as each step is completed or in batches. If only one unfinished section remains, it is assigned according to similar criteria; if none remain, the site computer reports that no inspection plan is available.

An inspection plan editor allows operators to create or modify plans and configure textual and audible prompts, numerical limits, confirmations, displayed images, conditional actions, scanner support, and voice entry of times and dates. The editor includes adaptive speech recognition, free-form speech transcription, and review and correction of inspection results. The site computer stores results, permits inspectors to review them before submission, and transmits completed data to the host computer. The disclosed subject matter may be implemented as systems, methods, devices, and computer-readable media.

The speaker celebrates winning the Stanley Cup, praises Buffalo’s strong young team, and reflects on the playoffs’ grueling demands, injuries, and adversity. He credits his teammates—especially an important injured player—for their resilience and hard work, expressing pride in the team’s experience and success.

Many UK ovarian cancer cases are diagnosed late, often as emergencies, despite early diagnosis greatly improving outcomes. The four main symptoms are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, frequent or urgent urination, and persistent pelvic or lower abdominal pain. Because these symptoms can be vague and resemble less serious conditions, they are frequently dismissed, compounded by delays in obtaining appointments.

There is no routine screening test for ovarian cancer. A CA-125 blood test cannot diagnose it on its own because elevated levels can also result from non-cancerous conditions; it is mainly used to monitor treatment or recurrence and assess whether a pelvic mass is cancerous. Symptom awareness and early reporting are therefore essential.

Other warning signs include unusual lower-back pain, ongoing digestive discomfort, bloating or nausea, bleeding after menopause, and unusual fatigue. People with persistent or unusual symptoms should consult a doctor, keep a symptoms diary, and may use Ovarian Cancer Action’s free online symptom checker. Support from friends, family and colleagues may also encourage prompt medical care.

Early-stage diagnosis gives a 95% survival rate, compared with 16% for stage four, yet fewer than one-third of cases are diagnosed at stages one or two. More than 87% of women diagnosed at stage one had experienced symptoms, so the description of ovarian cancer as a “silent killer” is considered misleading.

The lecture emphasizes evaluating poker decisions by expected value rather than by actual outcomes. A credit-card roulette story illustrates the law of large numbers: although one person may pay an unusually large amount, average costs converge on the normal split-bill amount. Similarly, good and bad decisions can produce lucky or unlucky results, so players should analyze whether they chose the most profitable action available rather than judging decisions solely by results.

Poker reasoning is divided into three levels. Level one compares a specific hand with an opponent’s presumed specific hand and depends on accurate “soul reads.” Level two, or exploitative play, compares one’s hand with an opponent’s range of hands. In a worked example, a pair of aces faced an opponent modeled as holding ace-eight through ace-king. Counting combinations gave 25% equity, below the approximately 28% required to call, so the hand was folded. Exploitative play uses an opponent’s tendencies and past actions to refine a range and seek the highest expected value. Its weakness is that models may be inaccurate, costly to build, or exploited by an opponent who adapts.

Level three, or optimal play, considers both players’ ranges. A player chooses call and fold frequencies that prevent an opponent from profiting through one-sided deviations; the lecture relates this to Nash equilibrium and a rock-paper-scissors analogy. Optimal play earns against opponents who make mistakes, while exploitative play can earn heavily against modeled tendencies but risks larger losses when the model is wrong.

Blinds are necessary to create poker’s central incentive: stealing forced money. A “Who’s Taller?” game demonstrated how a contest without mandatory participation can produce no entrants because everyone assumes someone else must be more advantaged. Blinds create a reason to participate, and antes make stealing them more valuable and encourage wider, more action-oriented play.

Stack size is measured in big blinds, but effective stack size depends on the stacks of all players still capable of contesting the pot. Position also matters: players acting later face fewer opponents and can profitably open weaker hands. Equity is the estimated share of the pot one can win. It can be calculated from potential remaining cards and outs, from beliefs about an opponent’s range, or with tools such as PokerStove.

For tournament beginners, the professor advises raising rather than calling when unopened, since a raise may win the blinds without seeing a flop. A common tournament raise is roughly 2.25 big blinds when antes are present. Larger raises risk more but offer worse calling odds; smaller raises risk less but provide better odds to opponents. With an effective stack of about 12 big blinds or less and antes, pushing all-in is generally preferred; without antes, the suggested threshold is closer to 10 big blinds. Although shallow stacks may appear to justify much wider shoving ranges, short stacks are also more likely to be called.

Suggested opening ranges expand with position. In a nine-handed game, the under-the-gun range is about 6.2%, the cutoff about 30%, and the button about 55%. Suited hands are valuable partly because they make flushes less obvious. Small-blind play roughly matches big-blind play in range, although the small blind is out of position postflop; shallow stacks can widen this range substantially. An earlier raiser’s range changes the required hand strength. Very tight strategies can be predictable and invite pressure, so balanced opening and occasional randomized hands are discussed.

Finally, the lecture distinguishes bluffing, which uses a weak hand to induce a fold, from value betting, which uses a strong hand to elicit a call. Medium-strength hands are generally checked toward showdown. A final calculation example used Nash-equilibrium tools to determine calling ranges in an all-in pot, followed by a classroom deal comparing the selected hands’ equities.

DryShips raised $14.5 million through a continuous equity offering by issuing 7.91 million post-reverse-split shares at an average price of $1.79 from April 10–17, well below two requests totaling $30 million. The issuance increased shares outstanding to 54.92 million and caused 16.8% dilution. Kalani Investors fulfilled only 48% of the second request, while issuance represented 8.86% of trading volume, which the author characterized as evidence of weak demand. At the April 17 close, DryShips had a $105.99 million equity market capitalization and $173.4 million remaining to issue. At the recent issuance pace and a 15% discount, completing the offering could require 54 trading days and 105.7 million additional shares. The author expects the company ultimately to pursue debt financing and anticipates further equity issuance, while noting that its market value remained above the $75 million F-3 eligibility threshold.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, with 155-mph sustained winds, gusts up to 190 mph, and rainfall of up to 40 inches. The resulting floods destroyed the electricity grid, disrupted infrastructure, caused more than $82 billion in damages, and destroyed about 80% of the island’s crop value, totaling $780 million in agricultural losses. The study proposes a semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate cause-specific excess mortality after the hurricane while accounting for population size and displacement, temporal mortality trends, pre- and post-emergency periods, within-year variation, and interactions between periods and causes of death. Coefficients are estimated through penalized likelihood, with smoothing parameters determined by restricted maximum likelihood. Excess deaths are calculated by comparing estimated post-emergency and pre-emergency mortality for each cause, avoiding double adjustment for displacement. The model can assess the duration of indirect mortality effects for emergency planning and preparedness.
NASA’s HAMMER plan could divert smaller asteroids or use a nuclear device to destroy Bennu, which has a 1-in-2,700 chance of hitting Earth in 2135.

At the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series final round at Hamilton's Agrisea Raceway, Dylan Drysdale won the Wifiplus KZ2 title, Tim Loughran the Aarque Group KZ2 Masters title and Garry Cullum the KZ2 Restricted title — his fourth. Drysdale took the title by four points after contact ended Mat Kinsman's Final, leaving Aaron Wilson to win the race. Van der Griend's Masters hopes ended in a third-heat crash, and Cullum won by 20 points over Regan Hall.

Hendrik Bessembinder’s 2017 study of about 26,000 stocks listed on U.S. exchanges from 1926 to 2015 found that only 43% earned more than one-month Treasury bills, while just 86 stocks generated half of all returns. Although stocks historically returned about 10% annually, the median stock performed poorly because gains were concentrated among a small number of winners. In one equal-weighted example, 12 of 17 stocks had negative returns, though strong gains from five stocks produced a positive portfolio return.

A similar Oslo Stock Exchange study covering 1985–2017 found that the exchange created NOK 2 trillion in value, but 18 large companies—only 2.7% of IPOs—accounted for the entire value creation. Most shares performed worse than risk-free rates.

The passage concludes that most individual stocks do not outperform Treasury bills and that random stock selection is likely to result in poor performance. Passive funds are presented as the simplest investment option, while investors choosing individual stocks are advised to diversify.

At higher levels, if an injured player remains down while the referee continues play, players may kick the ball out if there is no clear attack or immediate threat. After treatment, the opposing team takes the throw-in backward to a defender, allowing the other team to regain possession. If the referee stops play, a dropped ball may instead be passed backward to an opponent. No team may exploit the courtesy.

Intelligent e-maintenance is presented as a core e-manufacturing component, using real-time smart monitoring, performance assessment, and degradation prognostics to monitor, analyze, compare, reconfigure, and sustain plant assets. Web-enabled agents can connect maintenance decisions with CRM, ERP, and e-commerce systems. Research priorities include predictive algorithms, quality–degradation relationships, data mining, scalable device-to-business platforms, security, distributed decision-making, workforce training, and enterprise cultural change.

Reconfigurable maintenance adapts production systems to customer requirements and demand changes, while configuration, tolerances, and maintenance policies affect quality and cost. Proposed enterprise systems share diagnostic and productivity knowledge among companies to support reconfiguration and lifecycle reliability. Modular maintenance architectures combine distributed control, sensor-based surveillance, telecommunications, historical data, knowledge bases, and expert systems to detect abnormalities, identify faults and degradation causes, and select corrective measures. Maintenance policies must adapt to system changes to enable preventive and remedial action. Under mass customization and market pressure, integrating reconfigurable maintenance is essential to reducing costs, improving quality, and ensuring reliable production.

The authors acknowledge abandoning a bullish market view too early and argue that improving market breadth suggests underlying strength and a possible equity surge despite low VIX. They present 21 charts challenging bearish forecasts for U.S. equities and related securities, while disclosing long positions in U.S. equities and VIX.

Teachers’ Union of Ireland general secretary John MacGabhann advised teachers to avoid Facebook friendships with students, warning these can narrow professional boundaries and cause harm. He urged members to think before posting or responding on social media, as impulsive comments cannot be recalled, may damage careers, and can turn disputes into public cyber conflicts. He also criticized employers’ 24/7 expectations for immediate responses as potentially harassing, advising members they need not reply and can disconnect devices.

VentureWire’s May 17, 2001 edition leads with Tahoe Networks’ launch and $38 million first-round financing, led by Redpoint Ventures with Accel Partners participating. Tahoe plans to expand its staff from 50 to more than 120 and launch commercially in the second half of 2002. Startups.com became market-intelligence firm Startups, Inc. and cut 11 of 35 employees. Hermes Pensions Management said BTPS allocated $965 million for private-company and private-equity investments, including up to $50 million in Botts Capital Partners 2 and a stake in Botts & Co. Other features include Flatiron Partners denying reports that it is being dismantled and Kodiak Venture Partners pursuing data-related deals. Digital-asset manager iBase plans U.S. expansion following a $6 million Series B round, while DataSynapse expects to close a $15 million Series B.

Little; Comlase receiving $3.5 million; Xora raising $7 million; e.Intelligence closing an $8 million second round at an approximately $20 million valuation; Foundstone closing a $9 million Series B; and Yube raising $2 million toward a $7 million Series B. The speaker thanks a free people for their confidence and vows to dedicate his abilities to public service. He outlines his constitutional duties: executing laws, conducting foreign relations and relations among the states, managing revenue, commanding the armed forces, and promoting national interests. He pledges respect for executive limits, peaceful and honorable foreign policy, and states’ reserved powers. He emphasizes strict economy, specific appropriations, and official accountability to advance debt reduction and prevent extravagance. His tariff policy would equally favor agriculture, commerce, and manufacturing, except for products essential to national independence; he also supports internal improvements and the diffusion of knowledge. He rejects expanding the peacetime standing army, supports civilian control, naval growth, military improvements, and a national militia. He promises just treatment of Indigenous tribes and electoral reform, including ending patronage abuses and appointing diligent, talented, and trustworthy officials. Finally, he seeks guidance from his predecessors, the other branches of government, and his fellow citizens, while invoking divine protection of the country.

The study examines how TRNC presidential discourses, Council decisions, and broader historical developments have shaped education policies, particularly the construction and preservation of Turkish Cypriot identity. Since 1974, Turkish Cypriot education has developed as an independent system shaped by close relations with Turkey, national identity goals, and reforms spanning primary through higher education. Earlier periods included Ottoman religious schooling with low literacy, British-era ethnic divisions, and post-1960 disputes over equality, multilingualism, and discrimination.

The Education Council has addressed structural reform, teacher training, curricula, textbooks, infrastructure, higher education, and educational quality. Education has also been associated with modernization, democratization, economic development, and cultural preservation. History textbooks have predominantly presented Turkish-centered narratives of the Cyprus conflict, portraying Turkish Cypriots as victims and emphasizing integration with Turkish national identity. Since the early 2000s, EU harmonization, bicommunal initiatives, and the 2004 Annan Plan encouraged more pluralistic and reconciliatory curricula, although political and societal resistance has caused setbacks.

Presidential priorities have varied: Rauf Denktaş emphasized national identity, history, and integration with Turkey; Mehmet Ali Talat emphasized European harmonization and modernization; Derviş Eroğlu focused on cooperation with Turkey and technical education; Mustafa Akıncı promoted multiculturalism, peace, and intercommunal dialogue; and Ersin Tatar emphasized national identity and Turkish cooperation. Other recurring issues include Turkish as the main teaching language, internationalizing higher education, religious education, secularism, and educational quality.

The study recommends scientifically neutral, multiperspective history curricula, long-term policy frameworks less dependent on leaders’ ideologies, and continued cooperation with Turkey that respects local needs and educational autonomy.

Sergey Lavrov said India’s SCO accession has increased the group’s political profile, capacity to aid stability in Central and South Asia and ability to help resolve the Afghanistan crisis. He praised India’s independent, responsible foreign policy as contributing to global and regional security. Lavrov said bilateral trade was unsatisfactory and aimed to reach $30 billion by 2025, while deeper defence cooperation would bring more Russian technology to India. He doubted a US strategy centred on force in Afghanistan would work, citing NATO’s failure to curb extremism, terrorism and drug trafficking. Lavrov denied Russian support for the Taliban, saying contacts aimed to protect citizens and press the group to negotiate under UN Security Council criteria. He criticised the US for rejecting the Moscow Process and said resolving Afghanistan required the government, Taliban, neighbours and wider regional involvement.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary alleged that DOJ leadership prioritized punishing perceived presidential enemies over public safety and national security. Ben’Ary was fired after pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly linked him to Lisa Monaco and suggested he was involved in internal resistance to James Comey’s indictment. The paper examines the digital accessibility skills gap in computing education and professional training, emphasizing the need to integrate accessibility into India’s computer science curricula and technology workforce. It outlines WCAG’s four principles—Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust—and notes that accessibility is legally mandated in several countries despite low global compliance and significant economic losses from inaccessible digital services.

The authors designed a one-day, hands-on workshop for Indian software professionals, computer science educators, and UX designers. The workshop covered accessibility basics, universal design, accessible software development, testing and reporting, and teaching accessibility. It used five instructional modules, interactive exercises, assistive technology demonstrations, disability simulations, case studies, testing-tool demonstrations, and lightning talks.

Of 73 participants, most had no prior formal accessibility experience. Pre- and post-workshop surveys showed high engagement, increased confidence, perceived effectiveness, and strong intent to apply their learning. All participants would recommend the workshop, while 52% reported a significant shift in their perception of accessibility and personal responsibility for promoting it. Tool demonstrations, hands-on sessions, and emerging-technology talks received particularly positive feedback.

Participants requested further training in advanced inclusive design and development, AI applications, diverse-user needs, organizational policies and compliance, and practice-based learning. Limitations included the technical difficulty of some sessions for certain roles and concerns about using disability simulations rather than lived experiences. Recommendations include distributing preparatory materials, tailoring content by role and domain, adding real-world case studies, encouraging peer learning, and providing follow-up opportunities to sustain engagement and workplace application.

New England Patriots wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell will receive the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance for overcoming literacy struggles and promoting reading to young people. The 23-year-old caught six passes for 70 yards in the Patriots’ 34-28 Super Bowl XVI victory over the Atlanta Falcons.

Mitchell recognized his reading difficulties at the University of Georgia and taught himself by starting with children’s books. Inspired by books’ impact on his life, he created the Read with Malcolm literacy initiative, which promotes book ownership and reading in underserved communities. According to America’s Promise Alliance, children facing poverty, abuse or neglect are more likely to struggle academically and drop out; 65 percent of children who do not graduate have the lowest reading scores, and 61 percent of low-income families lack age-appropriate books.

Mitchell graduated in December 2015 with a communications degree, was drafted by the Patriots the following May and wrote *The Magician’s Hat*. He credits his mother, Pratina Woods, and his siblings for helping him make positive choices, and says his mother taught him to lead rather than follow.

Through Read with Malcolm, Mitchell aims to inspire children to read, expand their opportunities and overcome adversity. He encourages struggling readers never to give up, practice consistently and view adverse situations as chances to improve. He also plans to continue writing, visiting schools and using his football platform to promote literacy. Receiving the award, he said, motivates him to reach more students and spread the message nationwide that reading can change lives.

The article examines whether the Supreme Court can uphold President Donald Trump’s removal of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter without abandoning Humphrey’s Executor, the 1936 decision recognizing Congress’s authority to protect certain agency heads from at-will presidential removal. The author expects the former, but not the latter: the Court is likely to apply Humphrey’s Executor’s agency-specific analysis and adopt a prospective “mend it, don’t end it” approach. Recent cases, especially Seila Law, rejected CFPB independence by focusing on whether an agency exercises executive power rather than treating all independent agencies alike. The modern FTC remains bipartisan and multi-member, but its expanded rulemaking and enforcement authority, ideological leadership, and reduced adjudicatory role make it resemble an executive enforcement agency more than the 1935 FTC. A Supreme Court stay involving the NLRB and MSPB reinforces this comparison. The author nevertheless expects Humphrey’s Executor to survive in some form because the Federal Reserve’s distinct structure and monetary powers require a framework distinguishing agencies by the nature of their powers. The Court has framed the broader issue as whether Humphrey’s Executor itself should be overruled, while treating Slaughter’s individual removal as a narrower question.

In a speech responding to President Zuma’s 2016 State of the Nation Address, DA leader Mmusi Maimane accused the ANC government of using radical economic transformation to enrich politically connected elites. He cited the deaths of 94 patients at Esidemeni, the Marikana 34, alleged presidential corruption, and violence and militarization surrounding the SONA, describing the ANC as having become an “enemy of the people.”

Maimane highlighted a “Lost Generation” of young South Africans, including nearly six million mainly black unemployed young people, about 500,000 children leaving the education system annually, and three million people under 25 who are neither employed nor in education or training. He argued that land reform, black economic empowerment, nuclear energy, mining, and state mining plans primarily benefited ANC cronies rather than ordinary citizens.

The DA’s proposed Rescue Plan emphasized education and employment. It included recruiting and training teachers, creating a National Education Inspectorate, exploring school vouchers, expanding student aid and vocational training, and introducing apprenticeships and government internships. To create jobs, the DA proposed private-sector partnerships, labour-law reform, support for small businesses, a Jobs & Justice Fund, investment in infrastructure, broadband and transport, independent power producers, rejection of the nuclear deal, and partial privatisation of state-owned enterprises.

The party also advocated broad-based black economic empowerment, land redistribution through title deeds and farm equity schemes, and rejection of the MPRDA Bill. Further proposals included adding 50,000 police officers, restoring specialist crime units, improving public health and infrastructure, halving the number of ministries, limiting consultancy spending and government perks, making tenders transparent, and addressing corruption in metros. Maimane concluded by appealing for hope, unity, and a more inclusive South Africa.

Alexa and Echo can simplify cleaning through several skills and connected services. Cleaning Buddy helps users schedule cleaning tasks, while Amazon voice purchasing can order supplies with a four-digit confirmation code. Connected Neato and Roomba robot vacuums can be controlled, scheduled, located, paused, stopped, returned to their base, and checked for battery status via voice commands. Laundrapp offers laundry and dry-cleaning pickup and delivery in about 100 U.S. cities, while Good Housekeeping and Stains Be Gone skills provide stain-removal advice.

The study examines topography introduced by electropolishing (EP) in highly polished, fine-grain bulk niobium used in superconducting radio-frequency cavities. White-light interferometry and atomic force microscopy showed that EP creates sharp intergranular steps that increase surface roughness as material removal grows. These defects can reach about 70 nm in height and 50° in slope. Sequential polishing showed that existing steps are smoothed during further EP but new steps repeatedly form near grain boundaries, indicating diffusion-limited behavior. Step geometry was governed mainly by relative grain orientation rather than polishing depth, while exposure to electrolyte without applied voltage produced only minor additional growth.

London-theory calculations using conformal mapping quantified the resulting magnetic-field enhancement and superheating-field suppression. The measured step geometries can significantly degrade the achievable peak magnetic field, with the estimated limit \(B_{\max}=(\eta/\beta)B_v\), where \(\eta\) is the superheating-field suppression factor and \(\beta\) the magnetic-field enhancement factor. The results indicate a larger degradation than previously expected. Shorter coherence lengths increase sensitivity to superheating-field suppression, whereas larger penetration depths reduce sensitivity to geometric field enhancement. The authors suggest that field enhancement may dominate losses near the clean limit, with a possible crossover as materials become more strongly type-II.

Fick’s diffusion law was used to model impurity migration around the steps. Large slopes reduce impurity concentration at the step bottom, where vortex nucleation is expected, and enhance it near the top. When step dimensions equal or exceed the impurity diffusion length, substantial nonuniformity can result, undermining shallow impurity treatments such as low-temperature baking and nitrogen infusion. Smaller steps preserve more uniform impurity doses.

Overall, the findings identify electropolished grain-boundary steps as important limitations on high-field SRF cavity performance. They demonstrate that visually “mirror-smooth” surfaces may still be inadequate for operation near the niobium superheating field and support developing smoother, potentially less hazardous polishing methods for achieving accelerating gradients of 35 MV/m or higher.

MIT researchers refined prime editing by engineering Cas9 mutations and stabilizing the RNA template, reducing unintended DNA errors by as much as 60-fold. The vPE system, tested in mouse and human cells, could enable safer, more precise treatments for hundreds of genetic diseases. The team is now improving editing efficiency and tissue-specific delivery.

British police declared a “major incident” after a man and a woman in their 40s were found unconscious at an Amesbury home and hospitalized in critical condition following exposure to an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are assisting Wiltshire Police. Officials said no wider risk was believed, suspected contaminated drugs initially, and had not determined whether a crime occurred.

D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P. sought to deny Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak’s Chapter 7 discharge under Bankruptcy Code §§ 727(a)(2)–(5). The court found that the plaintiff failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that Fasolak: fraudulently transferred or concealed property; failed to preserve financial records; knowingly and fraudulently made false oaths; or failed to explain a substantial loss of assets. Although Fasolak transferred funds and a vehicle to his wife and omitted prior bankruptcy filings, stock, and consulting income from initial filings, the evidence indicated these errors and transfers resulted from retirement, financial misunderstanding, and his wife’s management of household finances rather than fraudulent intent. The plaintiff identified no missing records, and the 2002 financial statement did not establish ownership of specific assets whose later loss was unexplained. Final judgment was entered for Fasolak, and he was granted discharge.

Polo originated in Persia more than 2,000 years ago, spread across Asia, and developed into its modern form in India, where “polo” derives from the wooden ball. British travelers brought the sport to England and later the United States. The Milwaukee Polo Club, formed in 1923, is based in Hartland and plays on a field the size of 12 football fields. Thomas Esser says the club aims to make polo accessible, with members of varied occupations and ages, low-cost spectator admission, and opportunities to watch, take lessons, or participate. Games feature six- or seven-minute chukkas and usually last about two hours. Because safety and footing are priorities, outdoor play is generally suspended in unsuitable weather, though horses may give simpler demonstrations on off-days. The club also emphasizes proper care of polo horses, including feeding, grooming, limiting strenuous work, balancing physical and mental exertion, and recognizing horses as essential teammates. Players come from Milwaukee and several other Midwestern cities.

The speaker emphasizes that success in a salary-cap era depends on preparation, focus, execution and team depth rather than momentum or past results. Both teams’ rosters have benefited from multiple contributors, strong goaltending and player development, while poor puck handling, turnovers and positioning have hurt their forecheck. Preparation, sacrifice and competing for one another are presented as the foundations of winning and lasting team bonds. The speaker also urges players to enjoy rare opportunities, accept decisions without second-guessing, respond constructively to setbacks and continue working because the closely contested series is unfinished.

After recent ICE arrests, Austin ISD instructed principals and staff not to distribute unvetted materials or discuss controversial issues on district property, warning of heightened state scrutiny. Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo as overly conservative and said trustees were not briefed. Austin ISD and Education Austin shared immigrant and refugee resources, Know Your Rights information, and immigration-lawyer contacts. Education Austin plans to urge clearer family communication, while the board will discuss the memo.

A 13-year-old girl was shot in the thigh during an incident in an open garage in Guildford, Sydney’s west, on Tuesday night. She was taken to Westmead Children’s Hospital in a serious but stable condition, and police believe the shooting was not random.

The passage argues that penny stocks are highly speculative, high-risk investments rather than a reliable route to quick wealth. Most trade over the counter or on Pink Sheets, where listing requirements, costs, regulation, and financial disclosure are limited. Many companies have unproven or failing business models, and most penny stocks ultimately become worthless.

Other risks include illiquidity, wide bid-ask spreads, slippage, volatility, scarce broker coverage, limited information, and exposure to fraudulent “gurus,” courses, pump-and-dump schemes, share dilution, and deceptive reverse splits. Most traders lose money, consistently profitable strategies are difficult to find, and apparent success stories may reflect scams, pump-and-dump activity, or hindsight.

The passage states that companies often remain off major exchanges because exchange listing requirements are strict and expensive. It concludes that investors should understand the risks, conduct due diligence, and, if trading penny stocks, limit them to a small portion of their assets; however, it recommends avoiding them altogether.

Mark Warner accused Republicans of an unprecedented effort to undermine Robert Mueller’s investigation and the FBI, calling the Nunes memo partisan. Warner and Sen. Richard Burr were denied access before its public release. House Speaker Paul Ryan defended the memo as promoting transparency and supported Democrats releasing their own. Warner said the Russian-election threat requires a whole-of-government response to prevent future cyberwarfare.

Digital leaders distinguish themselves from digital laggards through a strong data culture centered on learning, transparency, measurement, and organizational alignment. Digital laggards tend to focus on short-term imperatives, discourage risk-taking, limit training to immediate job needs, tightly control data, set goals that are poorly grounded in data, and rely on qualitative proof of effort or individual judgment rather than measurable outcomes.

Developing a learning mindset requires sustained effort, even among digital leaders, because deadlines, customer expectations, and regulatory constraints can limit experimentation. In regulated settings, controlled pockets of experimentation can support targeted innovation. One pharmaceutical company created a localized environment for safe experimentation to automate compliance checks. The tool completed checks in one-quarter of the time previously required, improved team morale and autonomy, and was subsequently adopted by other groups.

Digital leaders generally make relevant data widely available across teams while applying controls for privacy, ethics, and proper governance. They view these controls as necessary for trust and encourage collaboration and group decision-making rather than hoarding data as power. Even so, some leading firms restrict access by function, and excessive quantitative analysis can undermine human judgment.

Digital leaders use clear, ambitious, measurable goals to track project and individual progress, often complemented by 360-degree reviews. This structure can give teams flexibility to innovate rather than rigidly prescribe how goals should be achieved. One transforming retailer replaced quarterly, finance-driven reporting with real-time dashboards after upgrading its data systems. Sales data is now pushed three times daily, enabling leaders to make faster decisions about inventory, marketing, supply chains, and other operations.

Data-driven objectives also align employees vertically with strategy and teams horizontally with one another. Effective goals are transparent, strategically aligned, and developed through top-down and bottom-up input so employees understand and support their targets. Digital laggards often lack this clarity, creating misalignment and reinforcing a “culture of genius” in which individual authority outweighs shared evidence.

At most digital leaders, leadership beliefs, stated values, and everyday behavior reinforce one another, making data culture a central coordinating mechanism. At laggards, formal ambitions often conflict with entrenched habits, skills gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Changing these mindsets and behaviors is among the hardest parts of digital transformation, but laggards are not doomed to remain so.

Organizations can occupy four maturity patterns: “data novices” recognize the need for data-driven decisions but lack enabling culture and systems; “insight ready” organizations encourage risk-taking but lack advanced analytical capabilities; “tech enabled” organizations have necessary data and technology but do not consistently foster experimentation; and “data reliant” organizations over-rely on data at the expense of critical thinking. Each can build on its strengths through targeted actions toward a strong data culture and successful digital transformation.

The paper studies many-to-one two-sided matching, where participants are assigned to teams, and identifies that participant-justified envy-freeness can leave teams facing substantial envy. It introduces team-justified EF1, which removes participants who strictly prefer the envied team before allowing one additional participant to be removed, along with ordinal versions based on stochastic dominance: team-justified SD-EF1 and team-SD-EF1.

Two preliminary approaches achieve partial results. Restricting round-robin drafting to participants’ top-choice teams guarantees team-justified SD-EF1 and participant-EF but can be highly unbalanced. Converting team capacities into slots and applying Gale–Shapley guarantees team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, and balancedness, but not swap stability.

The main algorithm combines team slots, participant eligibility sets, and lexicographically optimized matchings. It produces allocations satisfying team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, balancedness, Pareto optimality, and therefore swap stability, and it runs in polynomial time. With fully indifferent participant preferences it reduces to round-robin; with strict preferences it coincides with participant-proposing Gale–Shapley. With augmented tie-breaking, it is also group-strategyproof for participants.

The algorithm is extended to teams with quotas and participants or teams that may prefer being unassigned. Using dummy participants and a dummy unassigned team, the extension is polynomial-time and simultaneously guarantees stability, extended team-justified SD-EF1, Pareto optimality, and participant group-strategyproofness.

The speaker reviews a century of national progress from the Articles of Confederation to the Constitution of 1787, which replaced a weak confederation with a Union founded on the people’s will. The Constitution strengthened freedom, order, and local self-government, survived civil war, and produced national expansion. At the close of the century, the Executive’s paramount duty is to interpret and enforce the people’s will under the Constitution, preserve settled gains, maintain national authority and obedience to law, practice economy, and require honest public service.

The elevation of formerly enslaved people from slavery to full citizenship is presented as the century’s most important political change, though it caused serious disturbance in the South. The speaker rejects any permanent middle ground between slavery and equal citizenship and urges full constitutional protection for Black citizens. He likewise argues that equal suffrage must be protected, because denying the ballot is a crime threatening the government. He identifies voter ignorance as a broad danger, notes alarming illiteracy among voters and their children, and presents universal education as the necessary remedy for both North and South.

The speaker calls for reconciliation over the preservation of the Union, the overthrow of slavery, and equality before the law, while urging citizens to turn from past conflicts toward productive and peaceful achievements. He supports sound public credit and specie payments, a monetary system based on gold and silver, international arrangements preserving both metals, and paper notes redeemable in coin rather than circulating solely by compulsion. National debt should be refunded at a lower interest rate without forcing national-bank notes out of circulation.

He also calls for greater agricultural support through practical science, continued industrial growth, improved harbors and waterways, expanded ocean tonnage, and careful consideration of plans for an interoceanic canal, with American interests protected without seeking exclusive commercial privileges. Religious freedom must be preserved, polygamy should be prohibited, and no church should usurp government functions. Finally, he advocates regulating the civil service by law and establishing fixed tenures and grounds for removal from minor executive offices.

The ATR trailing stop is a volatility-based technical indicator introduced by J. Welles Wilder that helps traders set dynamic stop-loss levels, identify exits or entries, and manage risk. ATR values are multiplied—typically by 3.5—and subtracted from the previous close for long positions or added for short positions. As price moves favorably, the stop can lock in profits, while tighter stops may be used in volatile markets. Traders can also use trailing-stop breaches, ATR bands, and price “cross points” to identify potential trend reversals, breakouts, and changes in market conditions. The indicator can be applied to stocks and other financial instruments and combined with other technical indicators when developing strategies. However, it primarily reflects current volatility, does not fully account for past performance or price movements, and cannot eliminate trading uncertainty or potential losses.

Harvard President Drew Faust will leave the university on June 30, 2018, after 11 years, coinciding with the conclusion of its fundraising campaign, which has raised $8 billion against a $6.5 billion goal. She plans to take a sabbatical and resume her scholarship. During her final year, Faust will focus on research funding, recruiting top talent and advancing inclusion. Harvard will form a search committee for her successor.

Texas A&M enters the 2018 NFL Draft seeking to extend its run of at least one first-round selection each year since 2011. Receiver Christian Kirk, who bypassed his senior season, is the Aggies’ best chance of becoming their 10th first-round pick in eight drafts, though he projects as a fringe prospect outside the first round. Safety Armani Watts is forecast as a mid-round choice and receiver Damion Ratley as a late-round possibility.

A&M’s youth and largely unsuccessful 2013 and 2014 recruiting classes have reduced its pool of draft prospects. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson’s arrest and pending criminal case have moved him from a possible mid-round selection to uncertain draft status.

Recent A&M first-round picks include Von Miller, Ryan Tannehill, Luke Joeckel, Jake Matthews, Mike Evans, Johnny Manziel, Cedric Ogbuehi, Germain Ifedi and Myles Garrett. The draft begins Thursday in Arlington, while Kirk plans to watch from Arizona.

Alphabet settled Donald Trump’s lawsuit over YouTube’s post-January 6 suspension, paying $22 million to Trump and $2.5 million to co-plaintiffs. Trump designated his share for the Trust for the National Mall to support construction of a White House ballroom. The agreement closes the case, with Alphabet admitting no liability.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring after leading the state’s education system since 2019. Chief Deputy Superintendent Sue Carnell will serve as interim until Dearborn Public Schools Superintendent Glenn Maleyko takes over.

Rice urged lawmakers to ensure students receive all 180 legally required instructional days, noting that schools may count up to seven professional-development days as instruction and shift up to 15 days to online learning. Michigan does not require schools to report their use of these flexibilities.

Student performance remains weak, especially in early literacy, though increased funding for vulnerable students, expanded preschool enrollment and a record 82% high school graduation rate show progress. Rice cited Mississippi’s science-of-reading training, literacy coaches, early-literacy materials and small K-3 classes as models. More than 5,000 Michigan teachers have completed LETRS training, and Rice and the State Board of Education want it required for K-5 teachers.

Investments in teacher stipends, scholarships and “grow your own” programs are improving staffing. Annual entrants to the teaching profession increased from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000, but shortages in high-need communities remain.

The article profiles Peter Lynch, born in 1944, whose career began as a golf caddy at Brae Burn, where he encountered corporate executives and discussions of investing. He bought his first stock in 1963, interned at Fidelity in 1966, and returned after military service as an analyst. Lynch managed Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, increasing its assets from $20 million to $14 billion and its holdings from 40 to about 1,200 companies. His average annual return was 29.2%, more than double the S&P 500’s return, and he retired at age 43.

Lynch’s philosophy centered on “invest in what you know,” thorough research, clear business models, promising products, and fundamental indicators rather than market timing or short-term price movements. He favored undervalued companies overlooked by large investors, particularly smaller companies capable of substantial long-term growth. He classified companies as slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, emerging from crisis, or possessing undervalued assets. Slow growers offered stable income and dividends; moderately growing companies provided downturn protection; fast growers offered strong potential but greater risk; cyclical companies depended heavily on economic conditions; turnarounds were risky but could recover quickly; and undervalued-assets companies had potential not yet recognized by the market.

Lynch primarily allocated 30%–40% of Magellan to growth stocks, 10%–20% each to moderately growing and cyclical companies, and the remainder mainly to turnarounds, while consistently investing 1% in 500 smaller potential companies. He reviewed holdings every three months, analyzed earnings and prospects, rebalanced as needed, and remained fully invested. He sold or reduced holdings when prices rose without corresponding fundamental improvement, and increased them when prices fell while fundamentals remained sound or strengthened.

The article also notes that Lynch had Fidelity’s analytical resources and direct access to company management. Although he argued that informed individual investors could find opportunities, his methods produced exceptional results for Magellan.

Ghana Football Association Vice President George Afriyie was relieved of his duties after an Executive Committee meeting on Tuesday, weeks after announcing his intention to contest the GFA’s 2019 elections. The move followed his removal as Black Stars Management Committee head and months of alleged friction with GFA president Kwesi Nyantakyi over financial matters and alleged plotting with critic Nii Lante Vanderpuije.

Nyantakyi, who has led the GFA since late 2005 and has not ruled out seeking a fourth term in 2019, faces internal divisions and public pressure over the declining Ghana Premier League, despite three straight World Cup qualifications and the FA Cup’s revival. Previous vice presidents Fred Pappoe and Fred Crentsil were also sidelined. Afriyie says his three terms on the Executive Committee prepared him to lead and build on the administration’s achievements, while the dispute may embolden his challenge to Nyantakyi.

The June 8, 2001 news clippings centered on the dispute over Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC), a 2,184-MW project 65% owned by Enron. Phase I, with 740 MW, was operational, while the 1,444-MW second phase was 92% complete but had been postponed. The conflict followed the Maharashtra State Electricity Board’s complaint that Dabhol power was too costly, its withholding of about $48 million in payments, Enron’s preliminary termination notice, and MSEB’s decision to stop purchasing power and rescind the power purchase agreement.

At a Singapore meeting, domestic and foreign lenders commissioned Stone & Webster to assess the cost and revenue implications of suspending, mothballing or closing the project for a year. Enron proposed temporary suspension of phase II, including alternatives for completing the power blocks and LNG terminal. Foreign lenders favored suspension, while lenders said phase I should resume and DPC-MSEB legal disputes and power offtake should be resolved through negotiation. A committee led by IDBI was formed to negotiate with MSEB. DPC indicated it could reduce the project’s return from 16% to 11%, and the Godbole renegotiation panel said DPC’s return on equity should not exceed 16%. Other reports said states were unlikely to buy Dabhol power above about Rs 3 per unit because of their existing supply costs and added transmission expenses.

DPC appealed to the Bombay High Court against MERC’s jurisdiction and interim orders restricting international arbitration and reactivation of the escrow account. DPC argued that the 1993 PPA provided for international arbitration and sought to prevent MSEB’s regulatory proceedings; a hearing was scheduled for June 11. MSEB had alleged power-supply defaults and imposed a Rs 401.24 crore penalty.

Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s optimism prompted private power producers to expect an early resolution, although lenders and DPC wanted a more proactive central-government role. Commentators favored negotiated settlement and reforms to state electricity boards and third-party power sales. Meanwhile, Narmada Bachao Andolan leader Medha Patkar demanded a judicial inquiry into the project and announced planned agitation.

Researchers found low cheetah populations in southern Africa and a loss from 91% of the species’ historic range, supporting scientists’ call for Endangered listing by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

The speaker describes the playoff series as competitive, with momentum shifting between teams, and praises both sides’ effort and Detroit’s resilience despite injuries. He views the upcoming home game as a rare opportunity, noting Detroit’s greater comfort, quickness, and assertiveness on home ice. He discusses tactics learned from Igor Larionov and “Nickisms,” emphasizing poise, execution, and focusing on one’s role rather than individual scoring or the pressure of the prize. The Stanley Cup is portrayed as hockey’s greatest prize and an almost once-in-a-lifetime experience for players, coaches, families, and fans. He also highlights Detroit’s strong hockey culture and passionate supporters despite local economic hardship, praises Pittsburgh’s talented roster, and advises Hossa to continue doing what he does best.

Climate change, expanding mosquito ranges, and increased travel are contributing to the spread of mosquito-borne diseases into temperate regions. In the Basque Country, where no autochthonous Aedes-borne disease transmission had been recorded, imported dengue, chikungunya, and Zika cases increased alongside greater Aedes albopictus egg abundance and the establishment of Aedes japonicus.

The study used ovitrap egg counts from 2013–2023 and meteorological data from 2016–2023 in the Basque provinces of Gipuzkoa, Bizkaia, and Araba. Biweekly provincial averages of the 20 highest egg counts were matched with 14-day temperature, humidity, and precipitation data. Missing egg counts were imputed as zero, a central moving average smoothed the egg series, and Araba was excluded because sparse, zero-heavy data were insufficient for reliable modeling. Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia were evaluated using generalized linear, SARIMAX, random forest, and conditional inference tree models with original and lagged variables.

Egg counts were strongly correlated with temperature, including at a two-week lag, while humidity had an intermediate positive relationship and precipitation a weak negative relationship. Lagged variables generally improved model performance. Random forest performed best on training data, but appeared prone to overfitting; the Gaussian generalized linear model performed best on the 2023 test data in both provinces, followed by SARIMAX, while conditional inference trees performed worst. Poor test performance in Bizkaia was attributed to unusually high 2023 egg counts relative to the training period.

Models refitted through 2023 forecast lower mosquito abundance for 2024. The findings identify temperature as the most important climatic predictor and mosquito egg abundance as a key forecasting variable, supporting continued localized surveillance, mosquito-control planning, and disease-risk assessment in non-endemic regions.

Eight years after graduating, the author reflects on college with nostalgia and regret, realizing they took opportunities for granted and missed time for adventure. They valued meeting exceptional people, taking fascinating classes—especially geology—and returning to campus after breaks. Acknowledging that everyone experiences college differently, they focus on their own mistakes.

HPBOSE declared Himachal Pradesh Class 12 results on April 24, 2018, published at hpbose.org. Students can check results online using their roll number or via SMS by sending “HP12ROLLNUMBER” to 56263 and download the result.

Seven candidates qualified in Georgia’s crowded 6th Congressional District race to succeed Tom Price, bringing the field to 15. A special election is set for April 18, with a likely runoff scheduled for June 20.
Liverpool begin the 2017/18 season at Watford on August 12, face Everton and Manchester United twice each, and end at home to Brighton on May 13 after visiting Chelsea; dates may change.

Researchers at Cardiff University and partner universities studied nearly 2.5 million British residents aged 50–75, identifying 8,729 high-risk smokers eligible for lung cancer screening. Eligible participants were invited to receive CT screening or standard quitting information. After two weeks, 10% of the screened group had quit, rising to 15% after two years, compared with 5% in the group not invited for screening. Reassuring results did not reduce smokers’ motivation to quit. Because participants were self-selected and may already have been considering quitting, the authors suggested that concern about lung cancer may help prompt cessation. They concluded that CT screening could serve as a teachable moment for smoking cessation, particularly when paired with other interventions for motivated smokers.

The Geminid meteor shower peaks Wednesday night, with best viewing from midnight to 4 a.m. Thursday and up to 50 meteors. Rural areas may show more; no telescope is needed. A smaller crescent moon and few clouds should improve visibility.

The USGS awarded Caltech and six other institutions $4.9 million to develop West Coast earthquake warnings and bought about $1 million in sensors for ShakeAlert. The system aims to provide seconds of advance notice; full deployment is estimated to require $38.3 million in capital and $16.1 million annually.

Northwestern’s 66–59 upset of Wisconsin put its first NCAA bid within reach, but the Wildcats still have games remaining and must handle increased media attention and expectations. They host Maryland next, with Scottie Lindsey expected to miss his fourth straight game due to mono.

Valmet’s Board approved a long-term share-based incentive plan for key employees covering 2018–2020. The 2018 reward depends on comparable EBITA margin and stable-business order growth and is paid partly in shares and partly in cash in 2019 for taxes. Rewarded shares face a two-year restriction and generally must be returned if employment ends. Executive Team members are advised to hold shares worth 100% of gross annual salary. About 120 participants are eligible, with gross rewards capped at approximately 586,000 shares.

A survey of 202 Illinois daycare administrators, managers and teachers found that nutrition, exercise and toothbrushing ranked above helmets, vaccinations and sun protection as health priorities. Although about half of programs provided sunscreen, 77% did not let children apply it themselves. Many used sprays, sometimes improperly spraying children’s faces. Most reported no sunburns and avoided outdoor activity during extreme heat. The authors called for improved sun-safety education and noted the Illinois-only findings may not apply elsewhere.

An American Airlines email dated November 19, 2001, promoted Net SAAver Weekend Getaway fares to Theresa Staab. Domestic trips departed November 30 after 7 p.m. or December 1, while international trips departed November 29 or 30; both returned December 3 or 4. Tickets had to be purchased by November 23 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Round-trip domestic fares ranged from $59 to $312, and international fares from $59 to $519. Some travel could be on American Eagle.

The email also featured web-only Thanksgiving fares requiring purchase by November 21 and AAdvantage Net SAAver Awards for eligible domestic travel, starting at 4,000 miles plus the fare; these excluded first- and business-class, international, and transborder fares. Fares were booked through AA.com using an AAdvantage number and PIN.

Additional offers included a four-day, three-night Florida vacation package from $115 per person, a Fairmont Scottsdale package from $259, Starwood hotel weekend rates of $49–$179, and Hertz last-minute rentals. Applicable taxes and fees were excluded; tickets were nonrefundable, seats and fares were limited or changeable, and changes could cost up to $100.

A Denver federal jury found radio host David Mueller guilty of assaulting and batterying Taylor Swift by groping her during a 2013 preconcert photo session, awarding Swift the $1 she sought. Swift had countersued after Mueller sued her, alleging her accusation was false. The jury also found that Swift’s mother and her manager had not interfered with Mueller’s contract to secure his firing from KYGO. Mueller had sought about $260,000 in lost wages, while Swift’s lawyer argued the case was about protecting assault victims from being sued by their attackers. Swift said she would donate an unspecified sum to organizations helping sexual assault victims defend themselves and acknowledged the privilege and expense of defending herself in the trial.

Angela B. Ryan recounts becoming pregnant three times while working as a lawyer and experiencing colleagues, judges, opposing counsel, and strangers touching her pregnant belly without consent. Although she never lost a hearing while pregnant, she believes her visible condition created an unfair advantage rooted in spectacle while eroding her autonomy. She describes such conduct as assault and criticizes euphemisms such as “the Rub,” “the Pat,” and “the Rib Rub” for sanitizing it. Ryan notes that pregnancy-based harassment, including unwelcome physical conduct, can constitute unlawful sex discrimination under existing federal law, yet the practice remains largely unaddressed in legal workplaces. She argues it is also a workplace-culture, professionalism, and public-health problem. Calling for explicit consent, she urges courthouses and legal employers to adopt and enforce a simple rule: do not touch pregnant people without permission. She acknowledges her former judgment of pregnant colleagues and calls on the legal profession to address the issue through policy, training, and cultural change.

The team says it has improved puck management and offensive positioning despite scoring few goals, while keeping the puck away from Brodeur and sustaining pressure in the offensive zone. After winning two straight, the group describes itself as confident but not cocky, though Thursday’s game is considered most important. The return of a standout goaltender has provided a major lift and strengthened the team’s confidence. Both teams are viewed as defensively strong and capable of scoring first and coming back. The ten-day layoff affected timing more than conditioning, and the team expects better play Thursday. Travel, home crowds, and home-versus-road performance are not seen as major disadvantages.
Greg Jaffe discussed Pete Hegseth’s address to hundreds of generals and admirals, in which the defense secretary said the military had become “soft” and “woke.”

ACMD23 specifies how many blocks may be pre-erased before a multiple-block write, which can improve write performance on some cards. It should immediately precede CMD25 because other commands may clear the count. If transmission stops early, remaining blocks contain undefined data; if more blocks are sent than specified, blocks are erased as data arrives. The count returns to one after the write, and ACMD22 reports the number successfully written.

ERASE, DISCARD, and Full User Area Logical Erase use CMD32 and CMD33 to define a range followed by CMD38. ERASE removes data while leaving write-protected sectors intact. DISCARD treats affected data as “don’t care,” although implementation may allow some or all previous data to be read. FULE logically erases the entire user area. DISCARD and FULE are supported only by SDHC and SDXC cards over the SD interface. Erase and discard operations indicate activity by holding DAT0 low. The specified busy timeout is 250 ms for DISCARD and one second for FULE.

Three write-protection methods are described: a mechanical switch controlled by the host, optional internal card protection, and password-based locking. Passwords and their lengths are stored in nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP and FEP_LEN registers for Card Ownership Protection (COP). Locked cards accept basic status-related commands but deny normal data access. COP cards with FEP set require CMD42[1Fh] after power-up or reset before COP functions can be used. Setting FEP disables ordinary Force Erase and PWD clearing until FEP is removed. Force Erase erases card data and password registers while leaving the secure area intact; FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP and retains the FEP afterward. Failed lock operations set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED, and ACMD6 is rejected while locked.

CMD55 causes the next command to be interpreted as an ACMD. Defined ACMDs are executed as application-specific commands, while legal undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands. CMD6 switches functions through Mode 0 queries and Mode 1 selections. Defined groups cover access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Only one function can be active per group, invalid selections are rejected, and busy functions cannot be changed. The command returns a 512-bit status containing supported and selected functions, busy states, and maximum current or power consumption. The default power limit is 0.72 W, and hosts select higher limits according to power-supply, thermal, and connector capabilities.

High-Speed mode uses a 50 MHz clock for a 25 MB/s interface and is selected through CMD6. CMD8 checks whether the card supports the host’s supply voltage before ACMD41. Reserved command-system commands have different meanings under standard, vendor-specific, and mobile-commerce functions.

SDSC cards use byte addressing and a CMD16-defined block length. SDHC and SDXC cards use block addressing with fixed 512-byte data blocks, do not support partial or misaligned access, and do not support write-protected groups. CMD42 remains subject to CMD16 and may use up to 512 bytes.

The bus clock may be reduced or stopped to manage data flow, subject to required clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands, most responses, CID, and CSD, while CRC16 protects data blocks; CRC failures and illegal commands set error status bits and prevent command execution. Read and write timeout limits are specified, including 250 ms maximum busy time for most SDHC writes, up to 500 ms in specified SDXC cases, and one second after a UHS-II data burst. Erase timeouts use SD Status parameters when available or may be estimated from write delay.

Commands use a fixed 48-bit format with start, transmission-direction, index, 32-bit argument, CRC, and end bits. Command classes and CCC fields identify supported functionality. In UHS-II mode, TLEN normally controls transfer length, CMD13 is not issued during data transfer, and several SDSC-oriented commands are illegal. R1 responses are 48 bits, R2 responses are 136 bits, and R3 responses are 48 bits without CRC protection.

In 2012, Commander Chris Hadfield spent Christmas aboard the International Space Station, orbiting Earth every 92 minutes and seeing 16 sunrises daily. He played Santa, hiding family messages for his sleeping crew. Hadfield described how astronauts preserve holiday traditions in microgravity: dense fruitcake was velcroed to a table, while the crew also enjoyed reconstituted turkey, potatoes, processed vegetables, an artificial tree, and stockings filled with chocolate and nuts. The American and Russian crew selected holidays from their cultures and planned familiar yet creative celebrations. Hadfield emphasized that holiday preparation is vital to psychological health and well-being during unconventional Christmas observances in space.

Polling began for 69 of Uttarakhand’s 70 assembly seats under tight security, with nearly 30,000 security personnel and 60,000 polling officials at 10,685 booths, including 460 in snowbound areas. Over 7.4 million voters were eligible to decide the fate of 628 candidates in EVMs. Polling for Karnaprayag was rescheduled to March 9 following BSP candidate Kuldeep Singh Kanwasi’s death in a road accident.

A100 has 1.5× V100’s per-SM L1/shared-memory capacity, 40 GB HBM2 delivering 1555 GB/s, and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3× V100’s read bandwidth. SM features, residency controls, and data compression improve programmability and performance.

The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court affirmed a jury verdict for plaintiff Sylvester Michael McGillivray, who was injured when a splinter from a bowling alley’s “sliding floor” penetrated his finger while he delivered a ball with his hand held close to the floor. Evidence showed the approach was old, dirty, uneven, warped, and extensively splintered, and the proprietor had not planed it as was customary when worn. The court held that the evidence supported finding the proprietor negligent for failing to keep the premises reasonably safe and did not justify a directed verdict. Because McGillivray’s hand did not touch the floor, his delivery was not shown to be unusual or improper, and he had not observed the offending splinter before the accident, contributory negligence could not be ruled as a matter of law; it was a question for the jury. The court also rejected requested instructions presuming that using the approach for bowling was negligent. Judgment was entered for the plaintiff on the $750 verdict.

Samsung announced three cheaper, water- and dust-resistant Galaxy A smartphones—the A3, A5 and A7—set to launch in Russia before expanding elsewhere. The models feature a 16-megapixel camera, fingerprint sensors and varied screen sizes, but less processing power and storage than Galaxy S phones.

Under rules dated July 19, 1902, only the Secretary of State could issue U.S. passports. Applicants abroad were to apply to the nearest U.S. diplomatic representative, consul general, or consul; residents of insular possessions applied to the chief executive. Applicants had to owe allegiance to the United States; a declaration of intent to become citizens was insufficient.

Within the United States, applicants submitted a sworn, attested application stating birth, occupation, permanent residence, and intention to travel temporarily and return to reside and perform citizenship duties, taking the oath of allegiance and providing a physical description. At least one credible witness had to verify identity and the affidavit.

Native citizens needed only this application. Persons born abroad to a native father had to establish the father’s U.S. birth, residence, and citizenship at the applicant’s birth. Naturalized citizens had to submit proof of naturalization and details of emigration and residence. Women and children claiming citizenship through a naturalized parent had to establish the relationship and submit the parent’s certificate. Residents of insular possessions had to declare exclusive U.S. allegiance and provide two credible witnesses supporting birth, residence, and loyalty.

Camp Mystic families turned their grief over the July 4 Kerr County flood into a rapid push for Texas camp-safety laws. The disaster killed 25 campers, two counselors and the camp’s director; one camper remains missing. Parents of Chloe Childress, 18, and Lila Bonner, 9, joined other families, pro bono lobbyists and state officials to advocate for tighter regulations, testifying before legislators and meeting with Gov. Greg Abbott, House Speaker Dustin Burrows and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick.

Their efforts resulted in House Bill 1 and Senate Bill 1, signed by Abbott on Sept. 5. The laws require camps to move overnight cabins out of floodplains, monitor weather warnings with radios, install alert systems, train staff on emergency plans and establish evacuation procedures for moving children to higher ground. The parents believed these measures might have saved their daughters, but the reforms could not undo the tragedy or end their families’ grief.

China launched its first talent visa for young professionals and science and technology graduates from top universities, easing study and business entry. It prompted xenophobic backlash as the U.S. imposed a $100,000 H-1B fee.

Large language models could reshape social-science research by expanding access to web-scale information, automating text analysis, simulating demographic groups, supporting stance, sentiment, and coding tasks, and generating hypotheses or theories. However, their use raises concerns about bias, stereotypes, validity, dataset and deployment costs, misinformation, and ethical responsibility. Human–AI collaboration and human oversight remain essential for rigor and meaningful interpretation.

Generative AI also creates regulatory challenges involving misinformation, deepfakes, discrimination, jailbreaking, and rapidly evolving risks. Existing laws, company principles, and industry initiatives provide partial responses, but gaps remain between industry and governments and among countries. The passage calls for forward-looking, human-centered governance combining top-down regulation with bottom-up participation from developers, users, researchers, and communities, supported by industry–academia–policy partnerships, transparent issue reporting, rapid regulatory updates, and monitoring of sector-specific needs.

The passage covers L4 Fast/Slow peripheral memory maps and package pin assignments. Cortex-A8-decoded regions are shown only for reference and reserved for other masters. The DDR DMM TILER adds a 4-GB range enabled by a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; only HDVPSS and ISS can access it fully, while other masters can access one view through the base map’s 512-MB TILER region. Eight bottom-view pin maps are introduced. Terminal-function tables identify signals, multiplexing, ball and package identifiers, pin types, pull states, supplies, functions, PINCNTLx controls, de-selected input states, and multi-mux options. Boot details describe Cortex-A8/GPMC multiplexing, BTMODE sampling, post-reset GPMC_D[15:11] operation, and BTMODE[11] control of watchdog-only versus broader reset assertions.

A cross-sectional analysis of the international COVID-PCD cohort examined diagnostic testing among 747 people with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) from 49 countries. Most participants (92%) reported undergoing diagnostic testing, but use varied markedly by country. Among participants aged at least five years, 49% reported nasal nitric oxide measurement, while 75% of all participants reported biopsy and 58% reported genetic testing. Only 36% of eligible participants reported all three tests, and 9% could not remember which tests had been performed. Recall was lowest for biopsy analysis methods and varied by country, with Switzerland showing particularly poor recall.

Multivariable analysis found that participants diagnosed after 2010 were more likely to undergo nasal nitric oxide measurement, biopsy, and genetic testing than those diagnosed before 2000. Participants with situs abnormalities reported fewer tests than those with situs solitus. Test use also differed by country; age at diagnosis was not associated with testing. Sensitivity analyses assuming that tests had been performed by participants who did not recall them produced similar findings.

The results indicate that many people with PCD have incomplete or uncertain diagnostic work-up, with diagnoses based on clinical features or single tests. The authors conclude that clinicians should review test results with patients and consider additional testing, particularly for people diagnosed long ago and those with situs abnormalities, to improve diagnostic characterization and support personalized treatment. Limitations include self-reported data, inability to verify medical records, and possible selection bias through recruitment via patient support groups.

U.S. District Judge Reed O’Connor of the Northern District of Texas rejected a challenge to the Biden-era gainful-employment rule, siding with the Education Department on every point. The rule requires for-profit and nondegree programs to show graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than high school graduates; programs failing for two consecutive years could lose federal aid. Trump officials defended the rule, and further implementation will undergo rulemaking.
Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million and adjusted EPS of 41 cents, meeting expectations, while revenue of $5.74 billion fell below forecasts.

U.S. international student arrivals fell 19% in August 2025 compared with August 2024, largely reflecting delays and reduced capacity surrounding a freeze on visa interviews.
