Arrival data aligns with reports from institutions but excludes continuing students and some late arrivals, while September SEVIS data showed a disputed 0.8% enrollment increase. Experts said that figure likely overstated enrollment because some institutions had not reported data and F-1 students may have changed visa status.

Arrivals declined especially sharply among students from Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, with the largest national decreases coming from Iran, Syria, Haiti, Ghana, Nigeria, and India. Experts attributed some declines to travel restrictions, visa delays, and uncertainty surrounding a proposed 15% undergraduate international enrollment cap. Although the full effect remains unknown, experts warned enrollment could decline by more than 20%, with potentially larger losses in 2026 as students turn to other countries. Institutional and broader economic impacts are also expected. More definitive fall enrollment figures are due in mid-November from the Institute of International Education’s Fall Snapshot report.

Canada should build on NAFTA’s success by developing a comprehensive plan for expanding trade, rather than relying on new agreements alone. Although Canada has 14 FTAs, exports to most markets outside North America have not grown significantly since their implementation. The plan should improve domestic business competitiveness through tax and regulatory reform; address non-tariff barriers such as product regulations, export subsidies, procurement exemptions and currency manipulation; prioritize trade partners with historical, cultural and legal ties; leverage Canada’s integrated North American supply chains, which produce parts, materials and ingredients for finished goods; and help small and medium-sized manufacturers expand internationally by consolidating export-support programs. The author argues that Canada’s dependence on North American markets and limited global competitiveness require immediate structural reforms, modernization of NAFTA and stronger government action to support exporters, investment, growth and job creation.

In 1975, the S.S. EDGAR M. QUEENY collided with the S.S. CORINTHOS in the Delaware River, causing an explosion, deaths, injuries, and extensive property damage. The QUEENY’s owners sought limitation of liability. attorneys for injured and deceased Indian crewmembers, including Prava Chatterjee, the mother of deceased seaman Pratik Kumar Chatterjee, settled her claim for $87,000. In New Delhi, Chatterjee’s son-in-law, Anil Ranjan Ghosal, purportedly acting under a special power of attorney, signed a release. Settlement funds were transferred to the claimants’ Louisiana lawyers, who gave Ghosal a $29,000 check and allegedly $15,000 in cash. Chatterjee alleged that she had not authorized Ghosal, that her signature on the power of attorney was forged, and that she received none of the settlement proceeds.

Chatterjee petitioned to vacate the settlement and release and later brought a malpractice action against the involved law firms. A commission in Calcutta, India, took testimony from Chatterjee, Ghosal, and family members. After related proceedings, the district court denied Chatterjee’s petition, excluded much of the Calcutta testimony, refused to order a new commission, and found that the shipowners had proved a valid release. The Third Circuit vacated that decision and remanded.

The Third Circuit held that Indian law governed the validity of the special power of attorney because Pennsylvania’s choice-of-law rules directed it to India and Indian fraud standards materially differed from Pennsylvania’s. Federal maritime law governed the release itself. The court held that the admiralty court’s careful scrutiny of seamen’s releases also applies to releases executed by relatives of deceased seamen, requiring shipowners to prove that the release was freely executed, without deception or coercion, and with full understanding of the claimant’s rights. Shipowners could not avoid that burden merely because any fraud might have been committed by Ghosal or counsel; they could have sought court approval of the settlement or deposited contested funds with the court.

The court upheld exclusion of the earlier Calcutta testimony because Chatterjee had not established statutory unavailability and the shipowners lacked an adequate opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses. It nevertheless found that the unexplained denial of a new commission was a gross abuse of discretion. Rule 28(b) limited the district court’s discretion to deny international commissions, and no supporting reason had been given. Together with the evidentiary rulings, this denial prevented Chatterjee from presenting evidence on forgery, fraud, authority, and ratification and deprived her of a fair trial.

The Third Circuit therefore vacated the order denying Chatterjee’s petition and remanded with instructions to invoke a commission under Rule 28(b) to take testimony in India.

The speaker reports to Congress on the Yalta (Crimea) Conference with Britain and the Soviet Union, describing it as a turning point and a successful effort to establish common ground for military victory and lasting peace. The leaders agreed on Germany’s unconditional surrender and closer coordination of Allied forces, including direct liaison between Eastern and Western fronts and coordinated distribution of supplies and transportation.

Yalta also produced agreements on Germany’s postwar treatment: the elimination of Nazism and militarism, complete disarmament, punishment of war criminals, reparations in kind, and temporary occupation by Britain, Russia, France, and the United States in coordinated zones. The remaining differences over Security Council voting were resolved, and preparations were made for the April 25, 1945, San Francisco conference to establish a United Nations organization.

The three major powers accepted joint responsibility for the political and economic problems of liberated and former Axis territories, supporting democratic governments and free elections. They reached a compromise concerning Poland intended to produce a strong, independent, and prosperous state, and also agreed on Yugoslavia. France was invited to participate in Germany’s control, the San Francisco conference, the Security Council, and joint responsibility for liberated Europe.

The conference did not resolve the Pacific war; the speaker warns that defeating Germany will not end it and that Japan’s unconditional surrender and destruction of Japanese militarism remain essential. He urges Congress and the American public to support the Yalta agreements and international cooperation, arguing that unilateral action, exclusive alliances, spheres of influence, and balance-of-power systems have failed and should be replaced by a universal peace organization sustained by continued effort and sacrifice.

A Delhi court deferred to July 6 a hearing on the ED chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram and two companies in the Aircel-Maxis money-laundering case. The ED alleges that Karti helped secure 2006 Foreign Investment Promotion Board clearance while his father was finance minister, set up Advantage Strategic Consulting and promoted Chess Management Services. It says Maxis’ actual Rs 3,565.91 crore investment was shown as Rs 180 crore, exceeding the finance minister’s approval limit. Karti also faces charges in the INX Media case.

The speaker said he was unsure whether a player would play tomorrow, denied fatigue was a factor, and noted the team had won games at home and on the road. He said replays were inconclusive, top players were affected by home distractions, and the last two games went to overtime.

Pokémon GO’s Solstice Event offers three times the XP for catching Pokémon and for nice, great, and excellent throws, curveballs, and first throws. Combined with a discounted Lucky Egg, catch-related actions earn six times the XP, making roaming and catching nearly as productive as navigating the Pokédex. Evolutions receive no special XP bonus, discouraging Lucky Egg use for Pokédex completion. The event mainly helps casual and midcore players level up ahead of upcoming gym changes, while its winter-and-summer theme complements the game’s global setting.

Theresa May faces growing Conservative pressure over Brexit ahead of Friday’s cabinet meeting at Chequers. Andrea Jenkyns warned that failing to deliver Brexit or remaining “half in and half out” would be “catastrophic” for the party, while Jacob Rees-Mogg warned pro-Brexit MPs could revolt if she compromised her red lines. May has promised to leave the EU’s single market and customs union, though some MPs favor a pragmatic “soft Brexit” to avoid business and border disruption. Michael Gove rejected suggestions pro-Brexit ministers could resign, saying May had a clear plan and cabinet would unite behind it.

Following a decade in which the S&P 500 nearly quadrupled from its post-crisis lows, the market entered a period of consolidation marked by a growing expectation of significantly higher volatility. The Federal Reserve was raising interest rates and shrinking its balance sheet, while other major central banks pursued less uniform tightening policies. Strong corporate earnings growth, partly attributed to tax cuts, did little to reassure investors because much of the earnings was expected to fund buybacks and dividends.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose sharply in February 2018 and remained elevated rather than quickly returning to its lows, unlike most post-crisis episodes. In 2017, the S&P moved more than 1% on only eight of 251 trading days; through the cited 2018 date, it had done so on 31 of 79 days. The author compared this with low-volatility periods before prolonged market declines, arguing that sustained volatility could foreshadow a bull-market top even if new highs were reached.

The author expects volatility to persist or increase into 2019 and characterizes the coming bear market as potentially slow and prolonged. He contends that policy-supported markets can impede price discovery and warns investors to identify risks that the broader market overlooks rather than relying on optimistic economic and earnings forecasts.

The article explains two passive, low-cost index-fund strategies popularized by the Bogleheads, followers of Jack Bogle's advice to invest in the entire market rather than individual stocks, sectors, or markets.

The Bogleheads 3 Fund Portfolio holds three index funds: a U.S. Total Stock Market Index Fund (VTI), an International Stock Market Index Fund (VEU), and a U.S. Total Bond Market Index Fund (BND), using a "buy and hold" approach with regular contributions and periodic rebalancing. The Bogleheads 4 Fund Portfolio adds a Total International Bond Market Index Fund (IXUS), giving broader global diversification. Benefits include low costs, simplicity, diversification, and potential long-term growth; risks include exposure to market downturns and concentration in a single asset mix. Suggested allocations are 50% VTI, 30% VEU, 20% BND for the 3 Fund, and 50% VTI, 30% VEU, 10% BND, 10% IXUS for the 4 Fund; a commonly cited balanced mix is roughly 60% stocks and 40% bonds.

Backtests (dividends reinvested, rebalancing at least annually) showed a 7.6% annual return with a 28% maximum drawdown for the 3 Fund Portfolio and a 7.8% annual return with a 31% maximum drawdown for the 4 Fund Portfolio. Market conditions affect both portfolios: volatility can depress stock prices, while rising interest rates lower bond prices. The 4 Fund may better serve global investors, but the choice depends on goals, risk tolerance, allocation, fees, and historical performance.

The broadcast launches a nationwide mobilization to prevent unemployed Americans and their families from suffering hunger and cold during winter. A national organization led by Walter Gifford will work with governors, state and local agencies, businesses, labor and welfare groups, churches, and fraternal and patriotic societies to channel private relief efforts. Existing local relief committees and community chests are to be helped secure funds for work, direct assistance, health services, and character-building programs.

The federal government is expanding public works, providing livelihoods for nearly 700,000 families, halting immigration, protecting credit, and stimulating employment. States, counties, and municipalities are also expanding public works and tax-supported relief, but voluntary local action remains essential. Drawing on successful relief efforts the previous winter, the appeal calls on each community to fund carefully calculated plans and every citizen to contribute according to ability.

The speaker presents this effort as an expression of national unity, individual responsibility, mutual self-help, and the duty to ensure that no one deserves to suffer. He urges Americans to make November 26 an exceptional Thanksgiving and closes by linking the present crisis to the nation’s past sacrifices at Valley Forge and victory at Yorktown.

LG announced the V35 ThinQ, a premium smartphone succeeding the V30S ThinQ. It has a Snapdragon 845, 6GB RAM, 6-inch OLED display, dual 16MP rear cameras, and an 8MP front camera. Features include AI-assisted photography, Google Lens, far-field voice recognition, Hi-Fi audio, IP68/MIL-STD durability, and no notch. Pricing and release details remain unannounced.

Drug repurposing identifies new therapeutic uses for existing drugs and is particularly important for rare diseases, where treatments are limited. Using Elsevier’s Biology Knowledge Graph and proprietary NLP extraction, the study compares open-access (OA) and controlled-access (CA) biomedical literature. OA and CA sources contribute similarly to knowledge-graph relations, although CA literature generates 1.5 times more NLP assertions. OA relations grew substantially after 2006 and now represent more than half of relations relevant to rare-disease drug repurposing. Rare diseases with over 100 relations generally have more than 50% OA support, while drug-target relations show no comparable connectivity bias. Single-reference relations remain common in both corpora, whereas relations supported by four or more references are overwhelmingly OA. CA-only knowledge continues to grow but more slowly than OA knowledge. Citation rates and time to first citation do not differ materially between OA and CA sources. Single-reference and uncited observations accumulate almost exponentially across biomedical literature, mainly as original findings that receive no follow-up, although NLP false positives and untested hypotheses also contribute. Retracted articles are proportionally more common in CA journals. The authors conclude that reference counts alone are insufficient for assessing relation confidence and propose adding discourse analysis, citation-index weighting, graph-alignment scores, and distinctions between self-citations and independent confirmation.

Guyana's cabinet approved hosting the CWWA's 26th Annual Conference and Exhibition (October 16–20) at the Guyana Marriott Hotel. Themed "Promoting Innovation and Creativity in Water, Wastewater and Waste," the forum, expecting over 250 delegates, will review a regional waste management action plan bound for the UN General Assembly in Nairobi in December.

The instructor outlines course deadlines and quiz plans. The current problem set is due the following Tuesday and covers statistical basics, statistical process control, and control charting. The first quiz is closed-book but permits one page of notes and a calculator; statistical tables will be provided. Yield modeling will be covered separately and is excluded from the problem set and quiz.

Control charts are presented as sequential hypothesis tests comparing a nominal distribution with a shifted alternative. The false-alarm probability, alpha, determines control limits, while beta represents a missed alarm after a process shift. Average run length under the nominal condition is \(1/\alpha\), while the expected number of runs to detect a shift is \(1/(1-\beta)\). Increasing sample size while holding alpha constant narrows control limits and reduces beta, although operating-characteristic curves or iterative calculations are needed to select a sample size.

A chart alarm alone cannot reveal whether a process actually changed. Investigation should first verify the measurement, then review historical data for trends, consult operators, and examine equipment, feedstock, and other sources of variation. Requiring consecutive alarms or using wider limits can reduce false responses, and trend rules such as Western Electric rules may supplement single-point alarms.

The lecture distinguishes statistical control limits from design specification limits. Control limits detect unusual events, while specifications define acceptable product performance and must not be used to set control limits. For an in-control normal process, process capability is assessed through CP, which compares the specification width with the process’s six-sigma spread, and CPK, which also penalizes displacement of the process mean from target. Quadratic quality-loss functions likewise encourage centering and variance reduction. CP and CPK values can estimate nonconforming-part probabilities and compare the benefits of reducing bias versus variance. Highly capable processes also tolerate small mean shifts.

For multiple process steps, quality losses are additive when the steps are independent, but correlated steps can amplify, reduce, or compensate for deviations. Likewise, many control charts require an aggregate false-alarm adjustment rather than a three-sigma limit on each chart.

Finally, the lecture reviews limitations of \(\bar X\) charts, including their reliance on samples greater than one and possible time correlation among observations. Running or moving averages can use individual-part data but complicate independence and probability calculations. Future topics include moving-average charts, exponentially weighted moving averages, cumulative-sum charts, and methods for detecting small shifts or drifts more quickly.

President Donald Trump’s first State of the Union address Tuesday night will be used by lawmakers to highlight key issues. Female Democratic representatives plan to wear black to support the #MeToo movement, and Rep. Annie Kuster will host sexual-assault survivor Chessy Prout. Democrats invited young DACA recipients to emphasize immigration, while Republican Rep. Kevin Cramer will host a company president involved in a border-wall prototype. At least eight Democratic representatives plan to boycott the speech. Bill Nye, invited by NASA nominee Jim Bridenstine, hopes Trump will present an ambitious, science-driven space agenda. Rep. Joe Kennedy will deliver the Democratic response.
Iraq began aerial bombardment of Islamic State-held Tal Afar, with a ground assault planned after the air campaign, al-Sumariya reported, citing an Iraqi Defense Ministry spokesman.

Sarahah is a free Android and iOS app for anonymous messaging. Recently popular in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and social media feeds, it has nearly evenly split five- and one-star reviews. Users can send anonymous messages, optionally reveal their identity, and manage, flag, favorite, block, or restrict access to their profiles. Its deliberately barebones design focuses on messaging rather than the public social features of Yik Yak, Secret, and Whisper. However, anonymity has enabled bullying and hateful comments, and it remains unclear whether Sarahah will sustain its popularity.

Managed by Q, founded by Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian, launched in New York in April 2014 to provide transparent, technology-enabled office cleaning, maintenance, and supply services. The founders envisioned Q becoming a comprehensive operating system for customers’ physical spaces, beginning with high-quality cleaning and expanding into maintenance, office supplies, and other services. Q targeted companies occupying 6,000–20,000 square feet in Class B and C commercial buildings. Cleaning cost $25 per hour, maintenance $40–$80 per hour, and supplies were automatically replenished through a monthly subscription. Customers used an iPad dashboard to request and monitor services, review completed tasks and photos, communicate with operators, and request maintenance or supplies.

After initially subcontracting cleaning services, Q replaced the contractor model with directly employed workers because subcontracted performance was inconsistent and conflicted with the founders’ emphasis on quality and a unified company culture. All employees were called “operators.” Cleaning operators earned $12.50 per hour, while helpers and handymen earned $20 and $40–$45, respectively. Operators received paid travel time, and those working at least 30 hours weekly received health insurance, vacation, a 401(k), and workers’ compensation. Hiring emphasized integrity, work ethic, and willingness to learn rather than prior cleaning experience. Training included company orientation, app and dashboard instruction, supervised practice, participation in deep cleans, evaluations, and testing before assignment to accounts. Career paths allowed operators to become mentors and supervisors.

Q used standardized procedures, customer feedback, internal reporting, and a centralized digital repository called Q Knowledge to support consistency across cities. City teams had operational autonomy, while headquarters handled software development, customer acquisition, compensation, and companywide policies. Its culture emphasized transparency, communication, community, and continuous improvement. Operators could communicate problems and suggestions through the app, while managers shared business updates and held town halls every six weeks. Every new employee, including management, performed at least one deep cleaning during their first week.

By July 2015, Q operated in New York, Chicago, and San Francisco, with 228, 25, and 28 customer accounts, respectively. It employed 247 field operators, grew about 33% monthly, and maintained customer retention above 90%. Q had raised $17.4 million by its June 2015 Series A, including a $15 million round. Investors saw potential to extend its platform beyond cleaning into maintenance, supplies, shipping, and third-party vendor services.

The central growth decision was whether to enter new geographic markets or increase customers and services in existing markets. Teran had projected expansion into Boston, Atlanta, and Washington, D.C., and more than 1,400 served offices by December 2015, but each market presented distinct real-estate and labor challenges. An alternative was to broaden Q’s platform: office managers already used it for maintenance, supplies, and some third-party vendors, and investors viewed a vetted vendor marketplace as scalable and high-margin. Maintenance had Q’s highest gross margin, while cleaning remained the primary customer entry point and generated most spending. Teran emphasized that whichever strategy Q selected should not compromise its employee-focused operating model and culture.

A chronological index lists telegrams and related records dated January 8–September 3, 1942, with document references, locations, dispatch times, and receipt times. Most entries are classified as “740.0011 European War 1939” and originate from Helsinki or Washington; others are from Kuibyshev, Stockholm, London, and Ankara.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output, a current-feedback input stage, an internally matched gain-resistor network, and a differential output stage. Eight binary gain settings from 0.5 V/V to 100 V/V are selected through A0, A1, and A2. Target applications include factory automation and control, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test. Its input circuitry operates linearly within 3 V maximum of either supply while maintaining common-mode rejection.

A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1 MSPS SAR ADC. The example uses ±15 V input-stage supplies, a 5.3 V output-stage supply, a REF6250 5 V reference, and an OPA192 buffer to drive the PGA848 reference pin at 2.5 V, shifting the output to ADC midscale. Three filters provide EMI/RFI rejection, noise filtering, and ADC charge-reservoir filtering. A nominal 75 pF feedback capacitor produces a 318 kHz cutoff, or 277 kHz at the high feedback-resistor tolerance limit. The circuit has a nominal 318 kHz f–3dB bandwidth and −0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. C0G capacitors are used throughout the signal path.

Nominal performance is specified with ±15 V input- and output-stage supplies and common-mode and reference voltages at mid-supply. Output-stage supplies must remain within input-stage limits; voltages above 40 V (±20 V) can permanently damage the device.

Layout guidance emphasizes symmetrical input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive and noisy traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, reduced thermal junctions, and distance from heat sources. PSpice for TI and TINA-TI are described for circuit simulation, and TI E2E provides design support. ESD precautions, documentation-update notifications, related documentation, packaging information, and TI’s resource disclaimers are also covered.

Long-duration oxidation of pure tungsten in synthetic air was studied from 400–1050°C using thermogravimetric analysis, with WO₃ sublimation measured from 750–1100°C by coupled TGA-DSC. Oxidation changed from parabolic to linear kinetics, with activation energies of 180.4 ± 3.8 and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol, respectively. Edge oxidation became significant at high perimeter-to-area ratios, producing thicker, brittle scales prone to spalling. Voids and cracks occurred above 600°C and contributed to nonprotective, linear oxide growth.

Raman, XRD, microscopy, and EBSD characterized a layered oxide scale comprising an inner WO₂ layer approximately 30–50 nm thick, a dense 10–20 µm WO₂.₇₂ layer, and outer WO₂.₉/WO₃ regions. Surface heterogeneity, oxide-volume expansion, thermal stresses, and grain-boundary oxidation-rate differences were associated with cracking and cavity formation. The dense WO₂.₇₂ layer was associated with early diffusion-controlled growth, while subsequent void and crack formation enabled faster oxidation.

WO₃ sublimation increased monotonically with temperature and followed zero-order kinetics, with an activation energy of 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol. The confirmed WO₂ layer may contribute to the low detritiation efficiency observed in JET tungsten components by acting as a tritium permeation barrier.
A Missouri detective inhaled fentanyl mixed with heroin while treating an overdose patient with Narcan and rescue breaths. Both recovered, but police warn the combination endangers first responders.

Joseph Nicholson was convicted of first-degree murder for stabbing 16-year-old Joey Tanner three times in the back, severely injuring 17-year-old Jeremy Rodgers, after an altercation outside a Barrie apartment building. The Ontario Court of Appeal overturned the verdict because the trial judge inadequately instructed the jury, ordering Nicholson be sentenced for second-degree murder, which carries a mandatory life sentence with no parole for 10 to 25 years. Crown attorney Ray Williams seeks 16 years before parole eligibility. Tanner’s parents testified about their grief and criticized the appeal decision. Nicholson apologized to Tanner’s mother and asked to rehabilitate himself. Justice Guy Di Tomaso will impose the sentence Aug. 11.

Katie Albert, a Waterloo High School graduate and psychology major with a studio art minor at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, describes the second half of her semester studying abroad in Florence, Italy. Her Italian is improving, and she continues enjoying painting and drawing classes, having completed five paintings and numerous drawings in various mediums while visiting gardens, churches and bridges. The university also offered a cooking class and trips to Siena, Pisa and Lucca.

During spring break she traveled to seven countries in ten days, touring Copenhagen (including the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art), Amsterdam (Van Gogh Museum, canals, Red Light District), Brussels, Luxembourg City, Metz, and Kaiserslautern, where she visited Becherbach, the birthplace of her great-great-grandfather Abraham Maurer, an emotional experience. Her trip ended in Switzerland, with a revisit to Adelboden and tandem paragliding in Geneva.

Back in Florence, she found the tourist season underway and resumed classes and errands. A weekend trip to Split, Croatia, included white water rafting, cliff diving, beach time on Brač and a visit to Krka National Park, marking her milestone of 20 countries by age 20. With three weeks remaining, she anticipates finals, apartment inspections and souvenir shopping, feeling bittersweet about leaving Firenze and her friends.

Australia’s new childcare subsidy combines the Child Care Rebate and means-tested Child Care Benefit into a single means- and activity-tested payment from July 2. Of about 1.2 million registered families, 489,000 could miss out unless they update Centrelink details through myGov with 2018–19 income estimates, activity hours and childcare details. Both parents generally must work, study, volunteer or seek work at least eight hours per fortnight, with exemptions available.

Payments range from 85% of fees for families earning $66,958 or less to no subsidy above $351,248, with tapered rates between. Families earning under $186,958 have no annual rebate cap; above that threshold, the cap rises from $7,500 to just over $10,000 per child. Subsidised care hours depend on activity, from 36 hours per fortnight for 8–16 hours of work to 100 hours for more than 48 hours. Children must meet immunisation requirements or have a valid exemption. The package includes a $1.2 billion safety net and additional assistance for some families, and is estimated to encourage more than 230,000 families to increase workforce involvement. Labor says one in four families will be worse off.

Jeffing, also called the run-walk-run method, was created in the 1970s by Olympian Jeff Galloway. It alternates running with walking breaks, making exercise more manageable and accessible. According to Dr John Gallucci Jr, it can improve aerobic endurance, reduce exhaustion and overuse stress, aid recovery, build confidence, and support consistent training. Beginners may run for one to two minutes and walk for one to two minutes, gradually increasing running intervals as fitness improves. Experienced runners can use Jeffing for long runs and recovery weeks. It may particularly help long-distance runners, but poor progression or mechanics can still cause injury, and it may not suit sports requiring uninterrupted high-intensity effort. The passage also briefly introduces rucking and home gyms.

This survey explores algebraic, algebro-geometric, and combinatorial invariants of matroids and complex hyperplane arrangements, emphasizing how they relate to matroid combinatorics, arrangement topology, and realization. It introduces simple matroids, their lattices of flats, ranks, Möbius functions, direct sums, localization, and realizability.

A major focus is placed on multinets, including weak multinets, reduced multinets, nets, and their base loci. The passage describes connections between realizable 3-nets and Latin squares, more general nets and orthogonal Latin squares, and finite-group realizations by 3-nets in the complex projective plane. It also presents a Riemann–Hurwitz-type inequality for realizable multinets and asks whether it extends to non-realizable matroids.

The Orlik–Solomon algebra is defined as a quotient of an exterior algebra by circuit relations; its Betti numbers are determined by the Möbius function, and for realizable matroids it is isomorphic to the cohomology ring of the arrangement complement. The holonomy Lie algebra and its metabelian holonomy Chen quotient encode flat dependencies; for realizable matroids, their graded ranks correspond over the rationals to lower-central-series and Chen ranks of the complement’s fundamental group. Related constructions include the projective Orlik–Solomon algebra and quadratic Gröbner bases.

The survey also examines resonance varieties, defined as jump loci of Aomoto-complex cohomology, and Koszul modules associated with the Orlik–Solomon algebra. Their supports coincide in degree one away from the origin, and the degree-one Koszul module is identified with the infinitesimal Alexander invariant. Open questions concern higher-degree resonance-variety linearity for non-realizable matroids, possible distinctions via torsion or Koszul-module structure, and whether all 3-nets in the complex projective plane are algebraic.

The passage evaluates the last trading day of the month, distinguishing it from the last calendar day. In SPY since 1993, buying at the close of the second-to-last trading day and selling at month-end close averaged a 0.06% loss per trade and a negative 0.8% annual CAGR, compared with an average daily gain of 0.04%. The overnight return to the final day’s open averaged 0.04%, while its open-to-close return averaged -0.11%, with a 42% win rate and left-tail tendencies. The final trading day is therefore a negative seasonal effect with no end-of-month benefit. Profit-taking is suggested only as a possible explanation.

Sharon Haliwell, 48, died by suicide at her Wigan home after addiction to sleeping pills and abuse by her husband. Her inquest highlighted poor communication between North West Boroughs NHS Foundation Trust teams, who twice assessed her as at risk of suicide, and a missed referral for counselling. The trust introduced staff training, cross-team system alerts, and procedural changes to improve information sharing. A prevention of death notice noted some progress but said communication concerns remained.

During a race to four for the Stanley Cup, the speaker says fatigue is overcome by adrenaline. Despite not yet winning a game, his team has rebounded with strong performances and gained from veteran experience. He praises the chemistry of the Sykora–Elias–Arnott and Sydor–Zubov lines and Joe’s offensive-zone play despite his lack of goals, while emphasizing physical play, shutting down opponents, and creating chances around Joe and Scott Thornton.

Anna Ryder Richardson is leaving Manor House Wildlife Park in Pembrokeshire and divorcing her husband, Colin MacDougall, after attributing their 16-year marriage’s breakdown to the financial pressure, constant work and loss of privacy caused by running the zoo. The couple bought the deteriorating 52-acre park for £1 million in 2008, and Anna invested another £1 million in its renovation while the family lived in a cold cabin as animals occupied warmer homes. Their work on the attraction, which featured in Channel 4’s *Chaos at the Zoo* and other television programmes, intensified their arguments. In 2010, a falling tree seriously injured a young visitor and his mother; the couple faced more than £100,000 in costs and fines, and Colin took responsibility for the case against Anna. Anna now plans to renovate a dilapidated farmhouse near Bordeaux with her remaining money, live there with daughters Bibi and Dixie, learn French, and pursue cooking and gardening. Colin will manage the zoo. She is also returning to television as co-presenter of *60 Minute Makeover* on Quest Red.

Hackers released more unaired HBO episodes, including “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” “Insecure,” “Ballers” and “The Deuce,” but not “Game of Thrones.” HBO says it will not engage with the hacker, who has sought a multi-million-dollar ransom.

The passage is a roundup of The 74’s education and youth-focused headlines, plus newsletter and donation prompts. Coverage includes a west Texas girls’ camp planning to reopen after deadly July floods, teacher Jamal Roberts’s American Idol win, youth vaping litigation, COVID vaccine policy, school accountability, relief spending and court decisions. Features address integration, equity, innovative schools, college access and women in STEM. It also highlights student achievements in gymnastics, spelling and music, veterans receiving diplomas, career programs and youth responses to disasters.

The American Heart Association’s Go Red For Women campaign urges women to prioritize heart health. Tiffany Gholston, born with a heart murmur causing a slow heart rate and low energy, received a pacemaker at 20. She stays active, eats well, meditates, and supports awareness and fundraising for research.

Albert Einstein College of Medicine researchers found that heat-sensitive TRPV1-like receptors on appetite-suppressing POMC neurons in the hypothalamus’s arcuate nucleus help reduce food intake. In mice, capsaicin or heat activated these neurons, while blocking the receptors prevented appetite suppression. A 40-minute treadmill workout raised body temperature and reduced food intake by about 50%, an effect absent in mice lacking the receptors. The findings suggest body temperature regulates feeding like hormones and nutrients.

The passage is a Motley Fool Money credit-card roundup that states compensated offers may affect their placement or coverage, but not product ratings, which are described as independent. It highlights the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card: no annual fee, unlimited 2% cash back, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, 12 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, complimentary Visa Signature concierge service, and up to $600 in cell-phone protection with a $25 deductible. The Texas Supreme Court denied Anna Black’s writ of error concerning documents admitted in the Department’s suit against American Savings Bank. It did not approve the appellate court’s distinction between witness and document identification and emphasized that parties must still establish good cause under Rule 215.5.

Researchers at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics and Tel Aviv University propose a global network of mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts (FRBs) originating within the Milky Way. Phones would continuously monitor radio frequencies, record candidate signals, and upload data to a central site where synchronized detections could confirm a planet-wide FRB. GPS arrival-time triangulation could locate the burst, while dispersion measures could indicate its distance within the galaxy. Researchers estimate that Milky Way FRBs may occur every 30–1,500 years, or as often as weekly if they repeat like FRB 121102. The system would enable citizen scientists to help find and study nearby bursts whose origins remain unknown.

McLaren says reliability problems during pre-season testing—including wheel nut, battery, exhaust and overheating issues—have been addressed at Woking. Eric Boullier and Fernando Alonso expressed confidence in the Renault-powered MCL33’s potential ahead of Australia while acknowledging significant work remains.

After eight years in the league, the speaker celebrates his first Stanley Cup, praising his teammates, leaders, and Larry Murphy. He credits the support of Scotty, his family, and his six-year-old daughter, Dasha. Feeling healthy and motivated, he considers playing another year and emphasizes the need to stay in shape to compete against the best players. He also plans to ask commissioner Gary Bettman to bring the Cup to Moscow, hoping it will increase interest and attract investors to Russian hockey.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for adaptive radiotherapy using biological, physiological, and anatomical data extracted or calculated from imaging acquired during treatment to assess, update, or replan treatment and radiation delivery. Imaging modalities may include PET, MRI, SPECT, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, and magnetic-particle imaging. PET tracer uptake, kinetics, SUV, metabolism, oxygenation, hypoxia, HER2 expression, blood flow, vascularity, and other measures may inform changes to target or organ-at-risk geometry, dose objectives and distributions, fractionation, session number or duration, and delivery parameters. Controllers may calculate dose-volume histograms and plan quality indices, compare them with clinician-approved ranges, and issue visual or audible PASS/GO, tolerance, exception, FAIL/NO GO, or recommendation notifications. Treatment may continue, be adapted, or be terminated based on real-time data. Disclosed systems coordinate imaging and radiation-treatment systems through a controller, including dynamic multi-leaf collimators and rapid gantry and leaf motion for low-latency updates. Methods for bounded DVHs simulate target-volume shifts or SUV changes to establish minimum and maximum curves and flag out-of-range results. Online, real-time, and offline adaptive workflows include pre-session evaluation, repeated updates during treatment, and post-session replanning for future sessions.

Early forecasts suggest clouds may obscure next Monday’s partial solar eclipse in Philadelphia. Philadelphia is outside the path of totality, but Charleston will experience the total eclipse at 2:48 p.m. ET.

The compilation links the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals to the United Nations Charter by documenting the United States’ role in establishing the UN Organization’s legal framework. It presents the American delegation’s positions, emphasizing how major powers reached informal agreements rather than detailing formal conference proceedings. U.S. policy recommendations are traced from early 1945 through the May 2 changes to the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and the May 4 amendments proposed by the United States, United Kingdom, Soviet Union, and China, followed by the conference’s policy development, negotiation, debates, and drafting phases through June 26.

Records include minutes of 79 U.S. delegation meetings, 12 “Big Four” meetings, 29 “Big Five” meetings, and informal meetings with representatives of other American republics. Footnote citations connect them with published proceedings and technical committee actions. Additional materials include Secretary Stettinius’s records, conversations, reports, instructions, correspondence, memoranda, diplomatic notes, policy statements, and presidential correspondence. Sources include State Department files and publications, the Library of Congress, Interior Department, U.S. Mission to the UN, and Franklin D. Roosevelt Library.

NVIDIA Corporation reported that on March 22, 2016, it entered an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank PLC. Intel is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips for it in its foundry business, according to a Semafor report. A deal would be a significant win for Intel Foundry, which is seeking major customers. Intel shares rose 7% Wednesday, and AMD shares gained over 1%. The volume of manufacturing is unclear; both companies declined to comment on the rumor. Intel has recently added other major investors, though Nvidia has not committed to using Intel's foundry.

The May 18, 2001 “Enron Mentions” digest covers California power contracts, options trading, and Saudi Arabia’s gas initiative.

A Dow Jones column said California’s $43 billion in long-term power purchases had lost about 15%, or $6.5 billion, as western forward prices fell and electricity consumption dropped 9% from expectations. The state secured June–September power at $325–$390/MWh, but a failed $12.5 billion legislative bond deal threatened financing for more than 40% of its contracted supply; sellers were not expected to cancel. Enron was among companies that benefited from selling into California’s buying surge. Separately, low options volatility encouraged investors to sell options for upfront income and use covered-call strategies; the VIX fell to 25 and Nasdaq volatility indexes approached eight-month lows. Enron options also saw an institutional spread interpreted as bullish.

Most reports focused on Saudi Arabia awarding three natural-gas ventures totaling about $25 billion to eight international companies, reopening the sector to foreign investment. ExxonMobil was named leader of the estimated $4 billion Red Sea Core Venture 2, with Enron and Occidental receiving stakes. The roughly $15 billion South Ghawar Core Venture 1 consortium comprises ExxonMobil, Shell, BP and Phillips; the Shaybah Core Venture 3 consortium comprises Shell, TotalFinaElf and Conoco. Leaders for ventures 1 and 3 were expected by June 5, with memoranda of understanding to be signed by then, while stakes, management terms and detailed agreements remained unsettled. The coach says Buffalo plans to shorten third-period shifts and have players finish with energy, since fatigue can reduce performance on the next shift. Lineup decisions remain unsettled: Hogue is in the mix, while Sydor and Keane have played with Hrkac. Sydor could provide a distinct, physical forward line and may have the greatest impact, pending medical updates.

Buffalo adjusts defensive matchups according to which opponents are playing well, sometimes moving its best offensive players against Forsberg, Fleury, Sakic, or others. The Stack Offense uses two alignments outside the free-throw line, with three ball handlers and two post players providing stationary screens. In the penetrate-and-pop rotation, a ballhandler drives to a wing and passes to a teammate popping off a screen before taking the stack position. Options include rolling to the basket when overplayed, driving the baseline, making a drop pass to a rolling post, and back-cutting when the passing lane is denied. A post can step out for a return pass before the players reset their alignment.

A cross-sectional secret-shopper audit of 335 retail pharmacies in four New York City boroughs assessed hypothetical dispensing of electronically prescribed, nameless expedited partner therapy (EPT) for chlamydia. Only 40% of pharmacists reported awareness of EPT, and 30% were willing to dispense nameless prescriptions. Awareness was associated with willingness (48% dispensing among aware versus 18% among unaware pharmacists), while neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability was not associated with willingness. National-chain pharmacies were more likely to report EPT awareness than non-chain pharmacies, and awareness was higher in neighborhoods in the second through fourth socioeconomic-vulnerability quartiles than in the lowest quartile.

Among willing pharmacists, approaches varied: 28% used the name “Expedited Partner,” 34% used double prescriptions or refills under the index patient’s name, and 6% required the partner’s name. Overall, 31% refused to fill the prescription or ended the call, commonly citing unfamiliarity with EPT or the belief that a patient name was legally required. Only 46% of potentially fillable prescriptions were handled according to New York State guidelines. Insurance could be used for 86% of potentially fillable prescriptions. Neighborhood chlamydia incidence and borough were not significantly associated with awareness or willingness.

The findings identify limited awareness, low willingness, guideline nonadherence, and legal, insurance, and electronic-prescribing barriers. The authors recommend targeted pharmacist education, policy interventions, standardized workflows, and further evaluation of electronic prescribing and insurance coverage. Limitations include hypothetical telephone scenarios, possible variability between secret shoppers, limited generalizability beyond one metropolitan area, and no direct assessment of pharmacist decision-making.

In a March 7, 2001 email, Steven Kean told James Hughes that Enron’s role in opposing proposed Export-Import Bank budget cuts was smaller than a Wall Street Journal article suggested and commensurate with the company’s level of interest. After discussing OPIC, Ex-Im and other funding organizations with John Hardy, Enron reduced proposed 2001 headcount and spending, and Hardy joined Linda Robertson’s Washington organization rather than leading a standalone effort. Kean nevertheless believed Hardy would continue substantial project-finance work involving existing and prospective projects and asset-sale transfer issues, and asked whether Hughes agreed.

Hardy said Enron was not leading a fight against the Office of Management and Budget and had not participated in meetings on Capitol Hill. However, Enron needed to demonstrate support for federal agencies’ programs and budgets and was negotiating with both Ex-Im and OPIC over Electrobolt and other problem projects. Rebecca McDonald also served on Ex-Im’s private-sector advisory committee.

News reports said major exporters, including Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron and Halliburton, were lobbying Congress to protect Ex-Im from a proposed 25% cut to its $865 million operating budget for the fiscal year ending September 30. The White House characterized the bank as corporate welfare. Exporters planned to contact about 100,000 smaller suppliers that benefited from the bank’s $12.6 billion in prior-year loans, guarantees and insurance and hoped to generate congressional support for restoring funding. Lobbyists also planned to circulate Dick Cheney’s 1997 praise of Ex-Im. Enron received $135 million in Ex-Im financing in fiscal 2000.

Other attached articles reported that Century Development was finalizing a headquarters deal with Reliant Resources for more than two-thirds of an 850,000-square-foot Houston office project. Hines was building a 1.2 million-square-foot Enron tower, while another downtown tower was being anchored by Ernst & Young, reflecting Houston’s office and energy-sector growth.

The Netherlands was developing competitive short-term gas-trading hubs and potential transit routes for northwest Europe, with Enron Europe, Duke Energy, E.On, RWE and Electrabel actively trading. Regulatory disputes remained over Gasunie’s hourly balancing system, transport tariffs and third-party access to storage, which limited the benefits of competition.

Southern California Edison’s tentative $2.7 billion sale of power lines to California could take until 2002 because of legal and documentation issues. Separately, Sierra Pacific’s CEO doubted the SEC would approve the company’s $3.1 billion acquisition of Portland General Electric because of Sierra Pacific’s financial weakness, while proposed sales of 10 power plants were also at risk.

California’s governor announced 40 long-term electricity contracts covering about 629 million megawatt-hours over 10 years and valued at more than $40 billion, but many remained unsigned and subject to litigation or credit concerns. Enron had agreed on terms but still needed to resolve credit-related details. Small independent generators capable of producing 1,800 megawatts had shut down because of unpaid utility bills, contributing to California’s power-supply problems.

A Facebook video showing sixth-grader Keaton Jones describing school bullying went viral, drawing public and celebrity support under #StandWithKeaton. The disclosure describes a hardware-aware Machine Learning Model Scaling (MLMS) system that automatically selects and interchanges machine-learning models or subnets in response to changing hardware, environmental, and operational conditions. It addresses the time and computational expense of manual model optimization and conventional Neural Architecture Search, as well as models that perform suboptimally when deployed on hardware or evaluated against metrics different from those used during their design.

A client supplies an ML configuration through an MLMS interface. The configuration may include a reference supernet, application quality metrics, system constraints, performance-auditor settings, datasets, AI/ML tasks and domains, supported libraries, and target hardware information. The supernet and a pool of candidate subnets are stored in an ML model pool. The system includes an MLMS engine, a subnet selector, an ML model adaptation decision maker, and a performance auditor.

The performance auditor monitors inference results, model quality metrics, hardware conditions, and context data covering operating or power modes, system state, physical environment, and networking environment. System monitoring and sensor mechanisms collect data such as temperature, processor and memory utilization, available cores, power and battery status, network conditions, and silicon-aging effects. When configured thresholds are crossed, the auditor triggers a new subnet search.

Search methods, including NAS and multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, produce candidate subnets that address the current task, remain within a permitted performance difference, and satisfy applicable deployment and changed hardware constraints. The selector then applies a similarity-based strategy, favoring the candidate with the greatest overlap in pretrained parameters with the deployed subnet. Vectorized subnet representations allow unchanged parameters to remain in place and only differing values to be written, reducing data transfer, dynamic write power, memory writes, and model-loading time while preserving comparable inference performance. The disclosed algorithm evaluates candidate transfer costs and selects the lowest-cost replacement.

Example applications include autonomous vehicles, drones, remote sensor arrays, IoT image-recognition devices, edge-computing nodes, and federated-learning systems. The framework may operate on client, edge, or cloud hardware and supports various processors, programmable devices, AI accelerators, neural-network inference engines, memory, and storage configurations.

The chapter argues that globalization has created an interconnected global society in which English serves as a common language for international communication. University EFL curricula should therefore incorporate global issues to develop students’ intercultural knowledge, professional competence, and ability to communicate across cultures. Relevant topics include environmental protection, global warming, energy, war and conflict, public health, economic systems, political structures, cultures, human rights, and education. Curricula can be adapted to students’ majors, with scientific, business, social-science, and humanities students receiving different combinations of global topics.

The study involved two teachers at three Taiwanese universities and 372 non-English-major students in ten classes across Taichung, Yunlin, and Changhwa. Over an 18-week semester, students discussed and presented issues including tourism, music, festivals, food, cultural groups, art, technology, sports, entertainment, endangered animals, the Middle East, traditional stories, alternative energy, therapies, architecture, and environmental protection. Instruction used group and pair discussions, current news, films, websites, multimedia lectures, presentations, and an online Facebook group.

All participants supported incorporating global education into English teaching. Ninety-five percent regarded it as important, 96 percent said it stimulated English learning, 89 percent valued online research and videos, and 79 percent favored including global subjects in formal textbooks. Global warming, energy, and environmental protection were considered especially significant. Students reported greater interest in English, broader knowledge of cultures and lifestyles, and increased confidence in international communication. They also valued travel, films, music, guest speakers, English-language news, interaction with international students, and debates as supplementary methods. The study concludes that global topics make English learning relevant to students’ careers and can prepare Taiwanese university graduates to participate responsibly in international communities. Limitations include the need to vary topics by discipline and the inability of the participants to represent all language learners globally.

Skinimalism is a streamlined facial skincare approach using a few high-quality, targeted products rather than numerous layered steps. GP Hazel Parkinson says it can support the skin barrier, natural texture and long-term skin health while reducing irritation, product clashes and decision fatigue. It may also reduce waste, packaging and costs.

Skinimalism is not suitable for everyone or a reason to neglect specific concerns. Acne, pigmentation, sensitive or menopausal skin may still require selected ingredients, such as retinoids, azelaic acid, salicylic acid, niacinamide, arbutin or hydroquinone, alongside daily SPF, but not several unnecessary extra steps. Gentle cleansers, barrier-supporting moisturisers, fragrance-free emollients and cautiously introduced actives may be better tolerated than complicated routines.

For healthy skin, product choices should reflect age, lifestyle and individual needs. Dry or reactive skin may need hydration and barrier repair, while oily or congested skin may benefit from salicylic acid. Menopausal skin may require richer moisturisers, retinoids, peptides, vitamin C or occasional professional support.

When simplifying an existing routine, Parkinson recommends removing one or two products at a time, allowing two to four weeks for adaptation and monitoring the skin’s response. Professional guidance is advised when uncertain or treating specific conditions.

This single-case study examined whether smartphone touchscreen interactions can track neurobehavioural changes associated with anti-seizure medication changes and seizures in epilepsy. A man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal-lobe epilepsy participated for six months. During a five-day epilepsy-monitoring-unit admission, lamotrigine and perampanel were tapered and withdrawn, video-EEG documented seizures, and a focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion occurred on day 4.

The TapCounter app recorded 718,357 touchscreen interactions over 185 days, with a median of 3,311 daily interactions. Investigators constructed daily two-dimensional joint-interval distributions of successive inter-touch intervals and compared pre-tapering, tapering, and post-tapering profiles using cluster-based permutation testing. They also compared the convulsion day with the preceding three days.

Both comparisons showed significant differences. Tapering was associated with faster next-interval dynamics, which reversed when medication was restarted. The convulsion day showed slower next-interval dynamics than the preceding three days, although its profile mainly reflected post-ictal data because the seizure occurred shortly after awakening.

The findings suggest that regular smartphone use may provide an unobtrusive way to monitor medication- and seizure-related behavioural fluctuations that cross-sectional questionnaires or self-reports may miss. The authors propose that medication exposure and seizures may partly contribute to accelerated behavioural ageing in epilepsy. However, the study examined only one convulsion, did not assess the effects of focal seizures, and requires larger cohorts to establish generalisability and the potential value of touchscreen profiles in epilepsy care.

Market Basket grew from a small Massachusetts market opened by Athanasios “Arthur” Demoulas in 1917 into a major New England supermarket chain. A bitter family dispute eventually divided ownership between the branches led by Arthur T. and Arthur S. Demoulas. Arthur T. became CEO in 2008 and emphasized three elements: employees, low prices supported by a low-cost structure, and no debt. By 2014, the company operated 71 stores in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Maine, employed 25,000 nonunion workers, and generated $4.6 billion in revenue.

The company’s model combined uniform low pricing, high sales volume, extensive private-label products, fast decision-making, and localized merchandise selection. It emphasized customer service through in-store staffing and a “10-foot rule” requiring employees to greet nearby customers. Long-term employees were frequently promoted, received tenure-based bonuses and profit-sharing contributions, and benefited from extensive training. Market Basket also maintained close, long-standing relationships with suppliers, often assisting them with deliveries and merchandising. By the end of 2014, its profit-sharing plan was worth more than $612 million.

Arthur S.’s faction gained control of the board in 2013. The board curtailed Arthur T.’s authority, approved a $300 million shareholder distribution, and questioned his management practices and related-party real-estate dealings. In early 2014, Market Basket reduced prices another 4 percent despite the expected $170 million cost. On June 23, 2014, the board fired Arthur T. and two senior executives and appointed interim co-CEOs Felicia Thornton and James Gooch. Several other longtime executives subsequently resigned.

On July 18, most headquarters employees, warehouse workers, and truck drivers walked out and picketed for Arthur T.’s reinstatement. Store employees, customers, vendors, local businesses, political officials, and union organizations subsequently supported the protest. The action lacked legal protections, while the board fired eight managers and other senior managers resigned. Within two weeks, sales had fallen more than 90 percent. Vendors and nearby businesses suffered losses, competitors gained customers, and replacement-worker hiring efforts drew little interest.

After six weeks, an August 27 agreement allowed Arthur T. and his family to purchase the 50.5 percent stake held by Arthur S.’s side for $1.6 billion. Arthur T. was reinstated with full operational authority, and the interim co-CEOs remained temporarily in monitoring roles. The sale closed in December, financed with a $1 billion mortgage and $600 million in syndicated loans. Operations and customer traffic recovered quickly, and employees received $49 million in bonuses. Nevertheless, the new debt raised questions about whether Market Basket could sustain low prices, employee benefits, and continued growth while meeting its financial obligations.

The 2022 NFL Draft set a record with six wide receivers selected in the first 20 picks, reflecting teams’ increased investment in the position as offenses emphasize passing. Wide receivers complete the passing game by running routes, creating separation, making difficult catches, and working with quarterbacks on accurate play execution. Their value includes winning one-on-one matchups, requiring defensive adjustments, and supporting the run game through perimeter blocking. Essential traits include route-running, blocking, body control, speed, strong hands, coordination, and agility; receivers generally range from 5’10"–6’4" and 180–220 pounds. The position is named for receiving passes while splitting wide from the offensive line, though formations vary. Hall of Fame receivers Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent are highlighted for their records, longevity, and accomplishments.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018 reported revenue of $29.084 billion, up 19% from $24.538 billion a year earlier. Operating income rose 29% to $9.955 billion, net income increased 34% to $8.824 billion, and diluted EPS rose 36% to $1.14. Commercial cloud revenue increased 47% to $8.5 billion, including Azure growth of 76%, Office Commercial growth of 17%, LinkedIn growth of 33%, Dynamics growth of 20%, and Gaming growth of 44%.

Revenue increased across all three reportable segments: Productivity and Business Processes rose 19% to $9.771 billion, Intelligent Cloud increased 24% to $8.567 billion, and More Personal Computing grew 15% to $10.746 billion. Segment operating income increased 29%, 37%, and 23%, respectively. Gross margin rose 18% to $19.179 billion.

At September 30, 2018, Microsoft held $15.137 billion in cash and equivalents and $120.743 billion in short-term investments. Total assets were $257.619 billion, total liabilities were $171.652 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $85.967 billion. Operating activities generated $13.657 billion of cash. Financing activities used $7.384 billion, including $3.744 billion for share repurchases and $3.220 billion for dividends; investing activities used $2.953 billion, including $3.602 billion for property and equipment additions.

Microsoft adopted new guidance on intra-entity asset transfers and financial instruments in the quarter. Future guidance on hedging activities and credit losses was scheduled for fiscal 2020 and fiscal 2021, respectively. The effective tax rate declined to 14% from 18%, primarily due to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act; Microsoft’s fiscal 2018 TCJA accounting remained provisional and included a $13.7 billion net charge.

The company agreed to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion and expected the transaction to close by the end of October 2018. It repurchased 24 million shares for $2.6 billion during the quarter and declared a $0.46-per-share dividend.

Contingencies included patent claims, antitrust matters, a Chinese regulatory investigation, cell-phone litigation, and an appeal in a gender-discrimination case. Microsoft accrued $334 million of legal liabilities and estimated that additional adverse outcomes could reach approximately $1.0 billion. Deloitte reviewed the interim statements and identified no material modifications needed for GAAP conformity.

PerovSegNet is a lightweight YOLOv8x-seg–based framework for segmenting perovskite, lead iodide, and defects in SEM images. It incorporates two modules: ASDCB combines standard, dilated, depthwise separable, and attention-enhanced branches for multi-scale feature extraction and boundary localization, while SAD uses dual-path depthwise separable convolutions and adaptive pooling to retain fine textures and larger structures. The PerovData dataset contains 10,994 augmented images derived from 40 manually annotated SEM images; UMAP analysis showed clear separation among the three classes.

PerovSegNet outperformed Mask R-CNN, Cascade Mask R-CNN, and Cascade InternImage-XL baselines. In ablation testing, adding both modules achieved mAP@0.5 of 87.25 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 79.96 while reducing parameters and computation by 24% and 25% relative to the YOLOv8x-seg baseline. Segmentation accuracy for lead iodide and perovskite increased from 84% and 82% to 88%, while defect accuracy rose from 33% to 64%. Qualitative comparisons showed sharper boundaries and fewer missed small clusters and defects.

The framework automatically extracts area and count measurements, supports analysis across multiple SEM magnifications, and identifies morphological correlates of PCE: perovskite area correlated positively with PCE (r = 0.78), whereas defect area and count correlated negatively (r = −0.27 and −0.32). These correlations are observational and do not establish causality. Limitations include class imbalance, segmentation errors, imaging-condition effects, limited dataset diversity, and the need for faster inference. Dataset and source code are publicly available on GitHub.

A University of Connecticut study using a 3D-printed “organ-on-a-chip” device found that nicotine-based e-cigarette vapor caused DNA damage roughly equivalent to unfiltered tobacco cigarettes. Damage increased with the number of puffs and depended on the amount inhaled and additives present. Because such mutations can lead to cancer, the findings suggest vaping may not be much safer than smoking unfiltered cigarettes.

The article demonstrates a Python backtest of a momentum strategy using SPDR sector ETFs. Historical adjusted-close data is downloaded with yfinance and processed with pandas, numpy, and matplotlib.pyplot. Monthly returns and a rolling nine-month momentum factor are calculated. Each month, the three highest-momentum ETFs are selected and held in an equally weighted portfolio, with portfolio returns calculated since 2005. The strategy’s returns are plotted against SPY. It achieved a 9.89% CAGR versus SPY’s 9.46%, indicating little alpha under these trading rules, though other asset combinations may perform differently.

The Evening Star is a three-candle bearish reversal pattern consisting of a tall bullish candle, a small candle that gaps above it, and a bearish candle that closes below the first candle’s midpoint. It can form during an uptrend or a rally within a downtrend and is considered more reliable when the gap is significant and the third candle is longer. Traders often seek confirmation through trendlines, support and resistance levels, momentum indicators, or other technical tools before opening short positions. Suggested risk controls include placing a stop-loss above the pattern and setting a profit target near support; exits may also use technical signals. Because the pattern is not guaranteed, proper identification, confirmation, backtesting, and risk management are emphasized. Timeframes and indicators should suit each trader’s style and risk tolerance, and combining indicators may provide a broader market view. Key risks include false signals, market volatility, overreliance on technical analysis, lack of diversification, and losses from inadequate risk management.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after allegedly hiding two pistols in her robe and fatally shooting her 72-year-old son in Arizona, following a dispute about assisted living.

The passage criticizes the application of business models to U.S. education, noting that public schools adopted bureaucratic structures, categorical classifications, standardized testing, accountability, and charter-school policies. Efforts to professionalize teaching raised standards and certification requirements but did not improve teachers’ pay, security, or independence, while student reading and math scores showed virtually no corresponding improvement. NCLB imposed standardized assessments and sanctions for failure to meet annual progress targets. Charter schools have achieved isolated success, but research cited indicates mixed outcomes, selective admissions, segregation, financial inefficiency, and no broad test-score gains.

The passage also examines the medical model of learning, which treats differences in learning as innate biological defects that can be diagnosed. Although diagnosis can enable appropriate treatment and support, the passage argues that it can also promote stigma, fixed mindsets, resistance to feedback, reduced persistence, and academic disengagement. Alternative approaches include involving students in diagnostic inquiry, emphasizing strengths and weaknesses, teaching mindfulness, and presenting learning differences as problems that can be investigated and solved rather than immutable deficiencies.

Problem-solving is presented as a fundamental process underlying perception, learning, and development across humans and other systems. It involves interaction with the environment, forming theories, testing predictions, explaining outcomes, correcting errors, and revising hypotheses. The passage links this process to the scientific method, children’s natural “little scientist” behavior, project-based learning, metacognition, and self-directed learning. Perceptions are described as active predictions constructed through environmental interactions and adaptable heuristics rather than direct recordings of reality.

The proposed educational model replaces top-down testing, categorization, and bureaucratic specialization with a recursive, bottom-up structure. Students develop problem-solving and metacognitive abilities with mentor-like support from trained teachers; teachers apply the same process collaboratively and visibly in classrooms; and administrators address issues that exceed classroom capacity. Frequent feedback, reflection, high expectations, and assessment of progress against individual goals are presented as ways to reduce stigma and support self-regulation. Ultimately, the passage calls for restructuring education around universal, self-directed learning rather than profit, diagnosis, or fixed standards.

Twelve autism units are planned for 2018/19 across Sligo/Leitrim and Donegal, including five primary and seven post-primary ASD classes; Leitrim’s ASD classes have risen from two to five since 2011. The passage rejects Ambassador Hartman’s recommendation to trade away the INF deployment option for an arms-control agreement, arguing that abandoning deployment could undermine NATO’s credibility, strengthen anti-American and pacifist forces in Europe, and reduce Soviet incentives to compromise. It portrays European support for INF as stronger than Hartman suggested and recommends maintaining the zero-zero option, demonstrating U.S. sincerity, and deploying INF unless the Soviets substantially revise their position. If the Soviets make a serious move toward balanced theater-nuclear parity through asymmetrical reductions, deployment might be reconsidered.

A separate memorandum reports that Secretary Shultz and Soviet Foreign Minister Dobrynin agreed to regular meetings on arms control and other bilateral issues and discussed a possible Foreign Ministers’ meeting and U.S.-Soviet summit. Dobrynin said arms-control negotiations had made little progress, that the Shultz-Gromyko channel could help resolve difficult problems, and that major disputes required Foreign Ministers’ involvement before negotiators translated agreements into treaty language.

The passage holds that owners of injured vessels are entitled to compensation for lost use during repairs or unjustifiable detention. Damages may be based on market rental value or expected profits, while repair and raising costs are recoverable without deducting the value of new materials. When freight earnings are used, ordinary voyage expenses must be deducted, though this may undercompensate for prolonged detention; the vessel’s earning capacity is the proper measure. These principles were applied to the whaling ships James Maury, General Pike, Mile, and Nile after their capture by the Confederate cruiser Shenandoah forced them to abandon their voyages.

Reserve Bank scrutiny may target AFIC’s savings and loan scheme amid management and banking questions. Ambae’s volcano alert dropped to level 3, though eruptions remain confined to Lake Voui. The study investigates chemical polishing of Cd₁₋ₓZnₓTe₁₋ᵧSᵧ (CZTS) crystals for X-ray and gamma-ray detector fabrication. Cutting and mechanical polishing create damaged surface layers that impede charge collection and cause leakage currents, so chemical removal is required before CZTS samples can function as detectors.

A thermodynamic model is developed to compare the etching of selenium-free CZT and selenium-containing CZTS crystals under identical conditions. It predicts that CZTS should etch more slowly because selenium lowers the excess Gibbs energy of the solid solution. The predicted rate difference diminishes as temperature rises, and the rate reduction should correlate with selenium concentration.

CZTS crystals grown by the vertical Bridgman method under high argon pressure were tested at zinc concentrations near x = 0.1 and selenium concentrations y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, and 0.1. Samples were ground, one pair of faces was mirror-polished, and the crystals were chemically etched in freshly prepared 5% bromine-methanol solution at approximately 19°C for up to eight minutes. Etching depth was determined from dimensional changes, while etching trajectories and stage-specific average etching rates were calculated.

Average etching rates over the full treatment were 24 μm/min for CZT, 18 μm/min for CZTS with y = 0.02, 15 μm/min for y = 0.06, and 13 μm/min for y = 0.1. Thus, even a small selenium concentration produced a substantial rate reduction; for y ≈ 0.02, the experimental decrease was about 24%, compared with a theoretical estimate of 22%. Increasing selenium concentration progressively reduced the etching rate, consistent with hardening of the crystal lattice and the weakening of visible traces around growth defects. At higher selenium concentrations, differences in etching rates among CZTS compositions gradually diminished.

Chemical polishing effects became evident after approximately 30 seconds. Prolonged etching beyond three to five minutes could increase surface roughness, particularly around corners, cracks, grain boundaries, and other damaged regions. Stirring increased etching rates by roughly 1.5–2 times, while initial roughness, residual damage, temperature, solution freshness, and mixing strongly affected results. The findings indicate that selenium strengthens CZTS crystals and provide guidance for selecting processing and chemical-polishing conditions for detector-grade material.

The second edition of *The New Zealand Land and Food Annual*, edited by Professor Claire Massey, was launched at Massey University’s National Field Days. It presents 31 experts’ views on sustainable food production, warning that current farming and processing practices are unsustainable as New Zealand seeks to triple its $33 billion land and food sector by 2025.

The statistical analysis plan specifies pharmacokinetic analyses of plasma dasiglucagon and GlucaGen by treatment group and time point, including change from pre-dose, mean concentration-time curves on original and logarithmic scales, and individual concentration curves. Placebo samples will not be analyzed for dasiglucagon and GlucaGen. Pharmacodynamic analyses include plasma glucose sampling from pre-dose through 45 minutes, with an additional 60-minute sample for patients weighing at least 21 kg; AUE0–30min, summary statistics, changes from baseline, and mean and individual glucose curves will be presented.

Safety analyses based on the safety set will cover hypoglycemia induction procedures, prior insulin use, trial and rescue medication administration, time to first IV glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory results, vital signs, ECG findings, and immunogenicity. TEAEs will be summarized by treatment group and MedDRA system organ class and preferred term, with specified handling of causality, severity, missing dates, and special-interest events.
