The plan also includes time-to-glucose-recovery analyses, Kaplan–Meier curves, sensitivity analyses, response rates, and inferential comparisons. Appendices specify table, figure, and listing formats, derived-variable formulas, conservative handling of incomplete dates, SAS programming QC requirements, and validation with Pinnacle 21.

The passage reviews the formation, evolution, and observational signatures of small-body reservoirs that may supply exocomets, using Solar System populations as analogues. Solar System reservoirs include near-Earth and main-belt asteroids, co-orbitals, Hildas, planetary Trojans, the dynamically quiet and excited Kuiper belt, the scattered and detached discs, Centaurs, Jupiter-family comets, and the Oort cloud. Trans-Neptunian reservoirs are more numerous than inner populations, and their predominantly icy, volatile-rich compositions vary with formation location and history.

Stars form through gravitational collapse of dense molecular clouds. Rotation and infalling material produce protostellar discs, while outflows remove mass and angular momentum. Young stars are classified as Class 0, I, II, or III based on their spectral energy distributions. Discs around Class II stars commonly contain rings and gaps associated with planet formation, whereas Class 0/I discs are generally more massive, thicker, and less structured. Most stars form in clusters where stellar flybys and intense radiation can truncate or destroy discs, reducing material available for planetesimals. Photo-evaporation dominates in massive, long-lived clusters, while flybys are more important in low-mass, short-lived clusters.

Planetesimal composition is strongly affected by disc temperature, dust properties, and snowlines. In solar-mass discs, the CO and water snowlines lie at approximately 20–30 au and 1–2 au, respectively, and shift outward around more luminous stars. Objects forming inside the water snowline contain less ice, whereas those forming beyond it can incorporate abundant water and other volatiles. ALMA observations indicate that gas and ice compositions can also be altered by UV and cosmic-ray processing, turbulent mixing, molecular freeze-out, and anomalous elemental abundances.

Exocomets require both a source reservoir and massive bodies capable of producing cometary orbits. Wide-orbit giant planets appear more common around higher-mass stars, at least up to about twice the Sun’s mass, while lower-mass wide-orbit planets are harder to detect. Detection biases favour A stars, so their apparent prominence does not imply that exocomets form primarily around them. Debris discs occur around stars of many masses and are considered probable exocomet reservoirs.

Dust is expected to grow from roughly 0.1–1 micrometre grains into kilometre-scale planetesimals. Brownian motion dominates collisions among the smallest grains, while larger aggregates undergo inward drift, sedimentation, and collisions that can produce sticking, bouncing, or fragmentation. A “bouncing barrier” can halt simple growth, making the concentration of pebbles in vortices, pressure bumps, and disc midplanes especially important. The streaming instability can amplify local dust-to-gas ratios by about an order of magnitude, but gravitational collapse requires a sufficiently dense pebble cloud, often associated with roughly 2–3 times Solar metallicity, and turbulence low enough to avoid dispersal. Simulations generally produce shallow size distributions favouring large bodies. Solar System evidence, including approximately 100-kilometre primordial objects, Arrokoth, and trans-Neptunian binaries, supports a “born big” formation pathway.

When protoplanetary-disc gas disperses, the remaining solids form a debris disc whose dust is continually produced and depleted through collisions. Disc lifetimes depend strongly on stellar type, typically about 1–4 Myr for A stars and 5–10 Myr for K- and M-type stars. Observed debris-disc structures include gaps, warps, clumps, eccentric shapes, and sharp edges, which may reflect formation conditions, collisions, or planetary interactions. Their dust masses are measured poorly because only small grains are detectable, and inferred total masses are highly model-dependent. Collisional grinding also means older discs generally contain less material available to form active comets.

Orbital distributions, surface colours, JWST spectra, cometary abundances, and samples returned by asteroid and comet missions provide evidence about formation locations, disc composition, and later dynamical processing. Studies of comet 67P constrain a possible formation region around 25–35 au, although interpretations of its D/H ratio remain disputed. These observations must account for substantial post-formation dynamical, physical, chemical, and collisional evolution.

The Oort cloud, divided into inner and outer regions, is the Solar System’s long-period-comet reservoir. Simulations indicate that roughly 1–3% of planetesimals ejected from their parent stars remain bound and eventually form distant, nearly isotropic orbits. Stellar encounters in the Sun’s birth cluster may have substantially modified the cloud and introduced non-native objects; their present fraction is unknown. Close flybys reduce an exo-Oort cloud’s long-term reservoir while temporarily increasing the inward exocomet flux. Exo-Oort clouds are theoretically possible but remain unconfirmed.

Overall, small-body reservoirs are likely around most main-sequence stars, with their stability, composition, and exocomet contribution shaped by disc evolution, stellar environment, snowlines, resonances, and planetary architecture. Open issues include the dominant exocomet source, the roles of binaries and stellar encounters, debris-disc mass and location, the necessity of planets, the contribution of captured objects, and whether Oort clouds form mainly during or after the protoplanetary-disc stage. Future JWST, ALMA, Rubin Observatory, Roman, SPHEREx, and extremely large telescope observations are expected to constrain these questions.

State Department circulars address passport issuance, mission leadership, and charges against officers. Passport officers may not refuse an application merely because the applicant does not intend to return within two years. Passports remain valid for two years and may be renewed, but should not be issued to persons not intending to return or whose return is contradicted by circumstances. Ordinarily, a mission’s first secretary assumes charge when its head is absent; an emergency requiring a second or third secretary requires prior consultation with the Department. The first secretary determines which other secretaries must remain present. An executive order prohibits diplomatic and consular officers from publicly criticizing each other or preferring charges except through confidential communications to the Department of State.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019 describes a business organized into North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. The company serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through online and physical stores, third-party marketplaces, fulfillment, advertising, electronic devices, media, Amazon Prime, publishing, and cloud computing, storage, and database services. Whole Foods Market has been consolidated since August 28, 2017. Amazon reported approximately 798,000 employees, 318.2 million square feet of leased facilities and 15.6 million square feet of owned facilities at year-end. Fourth quarters generated 34%, 31%, and 31% of annual revenue in 2017, 2018, and 2019, respectively.

For 2019, Amazon reported net sales of $280.522 billion, operating income of $14.541 billion, net income of $11.588 billion, diluted earnings per share of $23.01, operating cash flow of $38.514 billion, total assets of $225.248 billion, and total long-term obligations of $75.376 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $55.0 billion. Investing activities used $24.281 billion, including $12.7 billion of cash capital expenditures, while financing activities used $10.066 billion.

Management’s financial focus is long-term sustainable free cash flow through higher operating income, efficient working-capital management, customer-experience improvements, cost efficiency, and continued investment in technology, content, AWS, and infrastructure. Critical accounting judgments include inventory valuation, generally using first-in, first-out and the lower of cost or net realizable value; each additional 1% of inventory valuation allowance at December 31, 2019 would have increased cost of sales by approximately $230 million. Income-tax estimates are also affected by changing laws, operations, acquisitions, geographic mix, and other uncertain factors.

The filing identifies material risks from intense competition, rapid expansion, new products and markets, fluctuating results, international operations and regulation, fulfillment and data-center capacity, seasonality, inventory, commercial agreements, acquisitions, foreign exchange, personnel retention, data and system security, intellectual property, litigation, taxes, suppliers, product liability, payments, and seller misconduct. Unresolved staff comments were reported as none, mine-safety disclosures were not applicable, and Amazon reported no issuer purchases of equity securities during 2019.

Anthology Inc., an education-technology company that pursued growth through mergers and acquisitions, has more than $1 billion in debt and lost nearly $80 million in revenue over two years. To restructure and emerge debt-free by early next year, Oaktree Capital Management and Nexus Capital Management are providing $50 million so Anthology can focus on its Blackboard learning management system. The company is selling its enterprise operations and its life-cycle engagement and student success businesses, with Encoura and Ellucian serving as stalking-horse bidders.

Analysts attribute Anthology’s financial troubles to costly integration of acquired products, inflated operating expenses, slowing revenue, rising interest rates, and a mistaken belief that institutions would buy its full suite of systems. The breakup reflects a broader shift in higher-education technology from growth-at-all-costs expansion toward sustainability, interoperability, affordability, and modular platforms. Experts expect institutions may benefit as the separated businesses focus on their respective specialties.

The passage details component selection and layout guidance for a TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter. A roughly 50-ns leading-edge blank time uses a 49.9-kΩ RLEB resistor, with optimization required for PCB parasitics, gate-driver delay, and minimum on-time. The selected 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides approximately 7.5 ms of soft start. The transformer design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle, below the controller’s 50% limit, with a 2.5 turns ratio and 6% magnetizing-current target. Although the calculated primary inductance was 33 µH, 40 µH was used. Primary GaN FETs were rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while an 80-V synchronous rectifier was selected for an expected maximum stress of about 20 V; a parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp is described for limiting switch-node overshoot.

The output inductor is 0.47 µH with a target ripple of 40%. Calculations require at least 1.3 mF of output capacitance, but 2.3 mF was used for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. This was implemented with seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors having approximately 0.86 mΩ combined ESR. An optional additional output filter can reduce ripple, with a resistor available to damp high-frequency peaking. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at roughly 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω RCS resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF.

Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover with a calculated power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. Selected values are 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF; tuning during testing is recommended. A 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS provides slope compensation. Application curves cover soft start at 10 A and a 5-A load-step response.

The controller supply range is 4 V to 14 V. At least 0.1 µF of ceramic bypass capacitance is required from VIN to AVSS, with additional bulk capacitance recommended for a remote supply. Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and other noise-sensitive traces from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing high-d/dt and high-dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point, using wide and short high-current traces, placing filtering, bypass, and compensation components near their pins, filtering the CS_ILIM signal, and connecting the CFP package’s backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. The document also identifies related evaluation-module and radiation reports, revision history, and mechanical and orderable information.

Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen rejected President Donald Trump’s criticism of Dodd-Frank, saying banks were safe, strong, profitable and more resilient than before the financial crisis. She noted commercial and industrial lending had surpassed its pre-crisis peak and disputed claims that banks were not lending. Yellen also said banks’ Tier 1 capital had nearly doubled due to post-crisis Fed requirements. While acknowledging regulatory burdens on community banks, she favored exempting them from the Volcker Rule. Yellen called for sustainable fiscal policy and productivity-enhancing policies, and said interest rates should rise sooner because prolonged accommodation could force the Fed to raise them rapidly.

The DAWN-plasma study is a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 trial comparing standard care with standard care plus convalescent plasma for hospitalized adults with COVID-19, using a 2:1 allocation. Standard care is primarily supportive and may change with national and international guidance. Outcomes align with the WHO master protocol to facilitate data pooling. Protocol amendments and design rationales are documented, and investigator information appears in Appendix 8.4.

The Education Department confirmed that employees would be affected by federal reduction-in-force layoffs, though the number and offices involved remained unclear. Sources said the Office of Federal Student Aid, which manages Pell Grants and student loans, would not be cut, while elementary and secondary education and communications and outreach staff were expected to be affected. German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki met in Warsaw to discuss EU security, bilateral ties and Poland’s rule-of-law dispute. Merkel welcomed efforts to avert unprecedented EU sanctions over judicial changes, while Morawiecki said agreement required understanding from both sides. This continuation application, “Metal Gates of Transistors Having Reduced Resistivity,” describes FinFET fabrication using low-resistivity cobalt or metal-silicide gate and contact structures. Conventional tungsten gates require a highly resistive tungsten nucleation layer for adhesion, which degrades transistor performance as gate dimensions shrink.

The disclosed process forms semiconductor fins between recessed isolation regions, creates a dummy gate stack and spacers, recesses and epitaxially grows source/drain regions, and deposits and planarizes interlayer dielectric. The dummy gate is removed and replaced with a gate dielectric containing an interfacial oxide and high-k dielectric, work-function and diffusion-barrier layers, a titanium-nitride blocking layer, and a metal-containing layer. The metal-containing layer may be homogeneous cobalt, a metal silicide, or a composite of cobalt silicide and substantially silicon-free cobalt, with continuous or stepwise composition transitions. The replacement gate stack is recessed and covered by a hard mask.

Source/drain contact plugs are formed using a metal layer, a metal-nitride barrier, and a cobalt or metal-silicide layer, while gate contact plugs similarly include a barrier and metal-containing material. Additional interlayer dielectric, etch-stop layers, and conductive vias may also be formed.

Cobalt provides better resistance to acid corrosion than tungsten, lower film roughness, improved adhesion to titanium nitride, and lower resistivity at small dimensions. The passage cites cobalt silicide resistivity of about 5.8 μΩ·cm, compared with about 5.7 μΩ·cm for CVD tungsten and 200–250 μΩ·cm for tungsten nucleation layers.

Germany’s education and special education systems reflect its complex wartime and postwar history. The population is about 83.2 million, including 10.9 million immigrants, and is highly urbanized; one-person households predominate, and fertility averaged 1.58 children per mother in 2021. Demographic shifts, including rising student numbers linked to immigration, may contribute to a teacher shortage.

Following unification in 1871, Bismarck introduced Prussian-influenced, tax-funded compulsory schooling for eight years. Nazi rule standardized secondary education in 1938 to promote ideological conformity, physical fitness, nationalism, and racism. After World War II, West Germany adopted Hauptschule, Realschule, and Gymnasium pathways, while East Germany developed a distinct socialist system. Reunification restored the three-tier model nationwide and made public education free. Education is now primarily governed and funded by the states, so curricula, school offerings, and placement policies vary; some states combine Hauptschule and Realschule, while others retain both.

Special schools, or Hilfsschulen, emerged in the 1920s to serve disabled students and prepare them for low-wage vocational work. In 1960, the Kultusministerkonferenz established legal frameworks and schools for different disabilities. Inclusion has expanded since the early 1990s but remains uneven. About 577,000 disabled students remain in seven special-school categories; in 2019–2020, roughly 2,800 such schools employed 68,500 educators. Inclusive elementary enrollment was 33.6% and secondary enrollment 14.9%, although about 40% of disabled students attended public schools overall.

Special placements reflect disability severity, support needs, state rules, and parental choice. Mildly disabled students are more likely to be included, while those with severe disabilities often enter Sonderschulen earlier. Physical access limitations and Gymnasium’s rigorous, ability-focused structure can restrict options. Referral by a parent or general teacher triggers comprehensive assessment and an individualized plan developed with educators, specialists, families, and sometimes students.

The KMK recognizes six teaching certificates, including special education. General teachers complete university bachelor’s and master’s programs, a first state examination, and a paid two-year Referendariat induction before a final examination. Special educators follow a similar route but usually intern in special schools and receive substantially more coursework in pedagogy, behavior analysis, and managing complex tasks.

Reunification made public schooling free, the 2006 General Equal Treatment Act addressed workplace inclusion, and the 2008 UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities strengthened protections in education and employment. North Rhine-Westphalia’s 2013 inclusive-education law transferred responsibility for many disabled students to general schools. The KMK’s 2015 diversity recommendations supported inclusion and post-school services, although states retain substantial autonomy.

Current challenges include determining appropriate placements, funding specialist resources, teacher attitudes, and access within the ability-tracked secondary system. Inclusion can improve cognitive outcomes but may also contribute to isolation; specialized settings may better meet some needs. Unstable funding limits accommodations, and unsuccessful MTSS/RTI implementation has harmed perceptions of a recognized support model. About half of disabled students in inclusive secondary settings attend Hauptschule, which offers limited job pathways, while Gymnasium remains difficult to enter. Overall, Germany is moving toward inclusion, with special educators increasingly supporting students in general schools.

OpenAI’s new Sora app, powered by Sora 2, lets invited iOS users create a digital likeness and browse a TikTok-style feed of AI-generated videos featuring themselves, friends, influencers, or strangers. Users can add people as “cameos” and generate nine-second clips with scripts, sound, and visuals. Likeness access can be restricted, and users can view clips made with their likeness, including drafts.

WIRED testing found the app capable of producing convincing personalized deepfakes, though outputs sometimes contained errors. OpenAI added guardrails against likeness misuse, sexual content, graphic violence, extremism, hate, self-harm, and disordered eating. Some public-figure, copyrighted-character, and sensitive prompts were blocked, while others succeeded. Altman acknowledged possible addiction and bullying risks. One realistic likeness video fooled the writer’s partner.

Across four experiments in the U.S. and India, researchers found that mothers favored daughters and fathers favored sons when allocating money or prizes. The researchers linked these biases to parents’ stronger identification with same-sex children, although over 90% denied preferring one child.

The Spinlock module provides hardware-assisted synchronization through 128 spinlocks, or hardware semaphores, using single read-access lock operations and avoiding unsupported read-modify-write bus transfers. The Mailbox module enables communication among the ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and other processors through register-based messages and interrupts. It supports flexible mailbox-to-processor assignment, four-message FIFO queues, reception and queue-not-full notifications, and four interrupts.

A unified memory map is used where possible. Tables describe L3 mappings for all system masters, C674x-specific mappings and peripheral access, and L4 Fast and Slow Peripheral regions. Some Cortex-A8-decoded regions are not physically part of L4 Slow and are reserved for other masters. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB range through a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; only HDVPSS and ISS can access the entire range, while other masters access one view through the base map’s 512-MB TILER region.

Terminal-function tables document package pin assignments, multiplexing, pin types, pull states, supply voltages, and functions for boot configuration, camera, CAN, DDR2/DDR3, EMAC, GPIOs, GPMC, HDMI, I²C, McASP, PCIe, resets, interrupts, JTAG, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, video, and power supplies. Multiplexed functions are selected through PINCNTL registers, with deselected-input states and multimuxed options identified.

BTMODE[15:0] inputs are sampled when reset is deasserted to configure boot behavior. BTMODE[4:0] selects the boot-mode sequence, with fallback modes attempted if the primary mode fails; other bits configure GPMC, EMAC PHY, XIP multiplexing, and PCIe addressing. The ROM configures pins for XIP, NAND, I²C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boot modes.

PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 control pin multiplexing. The default MUXMODE value tri-states pin outputs, while inputs are generally routed to all peripherals sharing a pin. Unused pins may remain unconnected unless otherwise specified, but unused inputs require pulls, all supply pins require proper connection, and most pins include internal pullup or pulldown resistors.

Several universities are piloting MicroMasters, online programs intended to make graduate coursework more affordable and serve as a step toward a full master’s degree. MIT, Columbia, Michigan, and Rochester Institute of Technology offer subjects including entrepreneurship, UI design, and artificial intelligence. MIT’s supply chain program costs $67,938 for a year, versus $1,350 for its MicroMasters certification. Employers including GE, Walmart, IBM, and Volvo recognize or encourage the courses. The programs also help universities evaluate applicants worldwide; MIT expects to admit 40 students annually to its blended program and considers online course performance in admissions. Students pursuing the full degree must still complete an on-campus semester at full tuition.

Tomorrow’s game is important, with strong fan support and excitement about a possible win. The speaker recalls Olympic and train memories and wishes to play before Colorado’s supportive fans. Ray’s trade helped during a playoff push, adding leadership, raising expectations, and demonstrating the value of hard work, unselfishness, and teamwork.

The application claims priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/474,562 and incorporates by reference a co-filed application concerning vehicle cabs and fasteners. It describes side-by-side off-highway recreational and utility vehicles comprising a body, structural frame, seating area, cargo box, and two- or four-wheel-drive systems with various differential configurations. Seats may be arranged side by side, have adjustable or removable bases and backs, and include headrests and supports. Additional features include fuel caps and tanks, a receiver hitch, lights, doors, handholds, bumpers, side restraints, and a roll-over protection structure.

Detailed embodiments cover frame members and panels, ROPS connections and accessory mounts, brake pedal assemblies with reservoirs, master cylinders, pressure switches, balancing and power-brake options, front and rear suspensions with A-arms, dampers, anti-roll bars and adjustable shocks, steering racks and tie rods, and a driveline incorporating a prime mover, transmission, CVT, clutches, flywheel, sensor and nested covers. The left rear lower A-arm may pivot about an axis positioned right of the vehicle’s longitudinal centerline. The steering column includes a gear selector and tilting assembly. Floorboards may incorporate drainage gutters, traction features, footrests, raised tunnels and removable service covers, while passenger seat bases can rotate upward and detach for stowage.

NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture builds on prior AI technologies to advance gaming and professional applications. Its Neural Rendering, Neural Shading, and Generative AI capabilities improve graphics, simulations, character creation, and design workflows at lower computational costs. The Blackwell family honors mathematician and statistician David H. Blackwell.

The coaching staff said the previous loss was not due to goaltending, noting that Pekka Rinne had a tremendous game while Matt played solidly. They said Kris Letang will not return for the series. Archie was praised for adding enthusiasm, energy, and speed, while Carter Rowney’s strong play, size, faceoff ability, penalty killing, and physicality were highlighted. The staff believes separating certain players creates better balance. Although disappointed by the loss, they considered it one of the team’s strongest games of the series, citing several high-quality chances and one or two preventable goals conceded. They plan to adjust lines to generate secondary scoring, learn from recent mistakes, and focus on the next game.

The Boston Zone Offense, developed and refined by Tom Davis, assigns players one fixed role rather than requiring them to interchange positions. It emphasizes a strong low-post attack, dribble-entry penetration, fast tempo, and both overloaded and spread principles.

The basic alignment features O1 as ballhandler, O2 as the top-of-circle swing guard and outside shooter, O3 as the baseline/corner runner, O4 as the weakside wing and rebounder, and O5 as the low-post scorer. Sharp sideline-to-sideline passing, skip passes, post feeds, pump-fake passes, reversals, and give-and-go cuts create open shooters and passing lanes, while unnecessary dribbling is discouraged.

Post feeds and reads depend on defender positioning, producing kick-outs, seals, or high-low and lob opportunities. Baseline movement forces dilemmas between protecting the basket, guarding the cutter, and covering open shooters. Overplayed passes can be countered with skip or cross-court “X” passes, back cuts, drop passes, dribble penetration, and kick-outs. Specific reads and counters are provided for attacking 2-3, 1-2-2/3-2, and 1-3-1 zone defenses.

Hawaiʻi is expanding charter preschools as part of its goal to give all 3- and 4-year-olds access to preschool by 2032. Waikīkī Community Preschool recently became the state’s first private preschool converted to a charter, making it tuition-free and eligible for state funding. The state has 33 charter preschool classrooms, opened 26 Department of Education preschool classrooms this fall and plans about 25 more next year. The charter commission also plans 15 additional classrooms by fall 2028.

Charter status can stabilize programs, improve teacher recruitment and provide salaries and benefits comparable to K-12 public schools. Waikīkī has reached full capacity for the first time since the pandemic, serving 98 children with a waitlist of 10 to 30. However, charter preschools must hire licensed educators, which is difficult amid a statewide shortage; five of Waikīkī’s six lead teachers are emergency hires.

Funding remains inadequate. Charters receive $171,000 per classroom, but small programs face higher per-classroom costs for administration, facilities, rent and maintenance. Waikīkī expects a $150,000 to $200,000 shortfall and relies on nonprofit fundraising, while Parkway Village Preschool faces deficits of $50,000 to $60,000 per class. Private preschools serving low-income families can receive up to $300,000 per classroom in subsidies, while public campus preschools receive about $146,000 and already have funding for shared staff and facilities.

Converting private programs does not necessarily create more seats but may keep existing programs from closing. Only two conversion applications were submitted, and one was denied. Separately, $20 million in construction funding is limited to government-owned campuses, though some private-property charter schools are renovating or adding preschool spaces.

STAT’s “Up and down the ladder” feature notes enGene’s hiring of Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer. Sweiti previously worked at Johnson & Johnson as global medical head for oncology clinical development. The article is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers, which are also invited to submit pharmaceutical industry personnel news.

A profile of PIM Capital presents the firm as a specialist in structuring and administering alternative-investment and cross-border funds, particularly in emerging markets. With offices in Sub-Saharan Africa, Mauritius and Guernsey, it emphasizes flexible, locally tailored solutions for complex regulatory environments, including grey-listing and currency volatility. The company stresses upfront planning, appropriate jurisdiction selection and operational design to reduce costly restructuring and support long-term fund success. Its client-focused approach includes dedicating time to bespoke “solutioneering,” absorbing setup costs or reducing fees where needed, and prioritizing five- to ten-year client relationships over immediate margins. The article says PIM Capital’s client base has expanded from smaller emerging businesses to large global asset managers and private-wealth firms, while demand grows among family offices and wealth managers for private debt, private equity and other alternatives. Christopher Erasmus leads its Mauritius team.

Pan Finance is described as a global financial-intelligence publication with more than 200,000 readers across 150 countries, offices in London, Lagos, Barcelona, Miami and Sharjah, and print, online, reporting and news offerings. The surrounding headlines cover banking, technology, energy, infrastructure, markets and OpenAI developments, including Fifth Third’s planned $10.9 billion acquisition of Comerica, JPMorgan Chase’s AI integration, AMD’s OpenAI chip agreement, London’s IPO activity and OpenAI’s $500 billion employee-share valuation.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that at its May 30, 2018 annual meeting, shareholders elected Jeffrey P. Bezos, Tom A. Alberg, Jamie S. Gorelick, Daniel P. Huttenlocher, Judith A. McGrath, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, Patricia Q. Stonesifer, and Wendell P. Weeks as directors.
