Day trading can be profitable, but it requires extensive preparation, patience, strict discipline, and learning from mistakes. The author reports that it took two years of slightly positive trading before finding consistently profitable strategies and identifies surviving the first two to three years as crucial. Because many traders fail and day trading is highly demanding, the author recommends swing trading first.

Using personal stock-trading results from January 2002 through May 2012, the author reports modest drawdowns, strong performance in 2006 and 2009, and that the best 1% of trading days generated 11% of total ten-year profits. Performance declined sharply during parts of 2011 and 2012 amid market changes, a broker switch, relocation stress, and increased competition from automated trading. New research and strategies later produced steady monthly profits, though at lower levels. The author warns that negatively skewed strategies can erase accumulated gains and that adapting to algorithmic trading may require accepting larger drawdowns. Plans to automate several strategies with a programmer are described.

Court documents from the failed prop firm Tuco Trading reportedly showed poor 2007 profitability among mostly day traders. The author attributes such failures to inadequate discipline, the psychological difficulty of trading, and the short-term trading environment’s zero-sum nature, while stating that cautious beginners who learn from mistakes have a reasonable chance of succeeding.
FPI interest in corporate bonds was high: 58 bidders bid Rs 5,898 crore against Rs 3,360 crore notified. The cut-off bid was 15.25 basis points, compared with 1.20 for G-secs.

The Turnaround Tuesday strategy is based on the tendency for market direction to reverse between Monday’s and Tuesday’s closes. It is most effective after a weak Monday—defined in one version as a close at least 1% below Friday’s close—with positions bought at Monday’s close and sold at Tuesday’s close. Historical SPY backtests covering roughly 30 years show positive compounded returns and substantially stronger results than equivalent strategies on other weekdays. The effect also occurred after Black Monday, October 19, 1987, when the market rebounded 5.3% Tuesday and 9.1% Wednesday. Filters, including Intraday Breadth Strength, may improve performance. Buying after a strong Monday is less effective. The article cautions that backtests enter and exit at closing prices that are only known afterward and notes current macroeconomic and geopolitical risks.

The Hawaiian King appointed Allen and Carter to negotiate a reciprocity treaty with the United States. Signed at Washington on January 30, 1875, it took effect September 9, 1876, after congressional ratification of its customs schedule and a proclamation. Disputes with Great Britain and Germany concerned the 1852 Anglo-Hawaiian “parity” or “favored nation” clause. Carter successfully contested Germany’s claim; a proposed 10 percent duty compromise was rejected, and after political turmoil, Hawaii’s foreign minister acknowledged U.S. exclusive privileges and pledged to uphold the treaty as interpreted. An annexation scare prompted Evarts to deny any U.S. designs beyond the treaty. Subsequent treaty-interpretation, customs, and fraud questions were settled through diplomatic notes, although a domestic scandal brought cabinet changes and a briefly retracted request for the recall of foreign representatives. The episode exposed corruption among the King’s advisers and opposition to extending reciprocity. U.S. officials also assisted Hawaiian liquor-law enforcement in the Ralik Islands, sought a consular agent, and helped negotiate a Hawaii-Japan treaty. In 1881, Britain persisted in invoking the parity clause; Comly rejected the claim and noted that a British commissioner had conceded its inapplicability in 1855.

Femtosecond noise correlation spectroscopy (FemNoC) was used to measure correlated, picosecond-scale magnetization fluctuations in the canted antiferromagnet Sm₀.₇Er₀.₃FeO₃ across its spin-reorientation transition (SRT). Temperature and c-axis magnetic-field scans tracked the static magnetization angle, quasi-ferromagnetic (qF) magnon variance and frequency, and random telegraph noise (RTN). Near the lower SRT temperature, qF fluctuations increased while the mode softened, and RTN emerged with overlapping timescales. External magnetic fields suppressed the variance enhancement and RTN, shifted or eliminated critical behavior, and increased the qF frequency. Field-dependent hysteresis and changes from easy-axis-like to hard-axis-like loops accompanied the magnetization rotation from the a-axis toward the c-axis.

Atomistic spin-noise and Monte Carlo simulations reproduced the observed trends. They linked enhanced fluctuations to softening of the temperature-dependent free-energy potential and showed that magnetic-field-induced stiffening suppresses fluctuations while raising the qF magnon frequency. The results demonstrate that FemNoC can characterize magnetization potentials and enable external control of ultrafast spin fluctuations for high-frequency, low-noise spintronic devices.

The passage describes a camera module incorporating a molded circuit board assembly or molded photosensitive assembly. A molded base is integrally formed over a circuit board, or over a circuit board and photosensitive element, and provides an annular light window aligned with the element. Unlike conventional prismatic or rectangular light windows, the disclosed window and molded-base surfaces use acute inclination or draft angles, including stepped, multi-step trapezoidal, and curved configurations. These features facilitate mold release, reduce friction and damage to the molded base and lead wires, simplify removal of light-window blocks, and prevent stray light from reaching the photosensitive element. Predetermined angle ranges also preserve structural strength and sufficient mounting space for lenses, actuators, and optical filters.

Manufacturing equipment includes first and second molds, a base-forming guide groove, light-window forming blocks, material-feeding, mold-positioning, temperature-control, and control units. Liquid molding material is introduced into the guide groove around the blocks, solidified by heating or cooling, and demolded to form the integrated base and light window. Suitable materials include nylon, LCP, polypropylene, and epoxy resin.

The disclosure also describes joint-board-array molding of multiple circuit board or photosensitive assemblies, replaceable mold components, elastic film layers, chamfered edges, and annular blocking elements that protect circuit boards, photosensitive elements, and connecting wires. Embodiments include fixed-focus and automatic-focus modules for devices such as mobile phones, computers, televisions, vehicles, cameras, wearables, and monitoring systems.

The lecture frames manufacturing as an interaction between persistent equipment and changing material through directed energy exchange. Process outputs, represented by geometry and property vectors, are functionally dependent on process parameters. Geometry changes are categorized as material removal, addition, deformation, or formation, while property changes include processes such as hardening and ion implantation.

A control taxonomy combines the transformation mode, energy mode, and spatial application of energy. Mechanical, electrical, thermal, and chemical energy can direct material changes. In serial processes, a small region is affected and the result depends strongly on the trajectory of the moving tool or interaction point. In parallel or distributed processes, energy acts across most or all of the target area, so the result depends on the tool, mold, mask, substrate, or energy-distribution pattern. Some processes, such as rolling, combine both modes.

This spatial distinction affects process control. Serial processes can often be adjusted by changing a tool path, making techniques such as CNC machining highly flexible. Parallel processes often require altering distributed energy patterns or tooling and may be less flexible, although they can achieve much higher production rates. Examples contrast flexible serial machining and 3D printing with rapid parallel processes such as automobile stamping and hot isostatic pressing. Serializing a parallel process can also enable tool-free rapid fabrication, as in stereolithography.

The choice of energy mode affects rate, quality, cost, flexibility, repeatability, and the ability to stop a process. Mechanical interactions can act rapidly and precisely; thermal and chemical interactions may diffuse, produce side effects such as undercutting, operate more slowly, and be harder to interrupt. Parallel processing is generally faster, whereas serial processing generally offers greater geometry flexibility.

Processes can also be divided into equipment and material, and into transient states and inherent properties. Constitutive properties describe how equipment or material responds to energy, such as stiffness, elasticity, yield strength, thermal expansion, viscosity, and chemical reactivity. Transient states include forces, pressures, temperatures, flows, and velocities during processing.

These distinctions help locate sources of variation. Equipment states are generally easiest to control through servos, computer controls, and temperature regulation. Equipment properties are usually known but can degrade, notably through tool wear. Material properties vary with upstream processing and strongly affect sensitive operations such as deformation, while machining is comparatively insensitive. Material states are often difficult to know or control—for example, a polymer’s temperature in a mold may differ from the controlled oven temperature. Uncertain material properties, material states, and equipment–material interfaces therefore contribute to output variation. Effective control generally requires upstream elimination of material variation and direct manipulation of equipment states, with success depending on the process’s controllability and sensitivity.

The speaker describes a cohesive, competitive team with many returning players and finds fulfillment in overcoming the difficulty of attempting back-to-back success. He credits shared sacrifice, veteran additions, and players filling in after absences. He especially praises the goaltenders’ performances during the playoffs and teammates who contributed in crucial moments. The achievement was meaningful given its difficulty and the players’ long careers, and he was happy to pass the honor to a teammate who could appreciate it.

The lecture explains interactions between two neutral atoms through multipole electrodynamics and quantum mechanics. Because the Coulomb contribution vanishes for neutral atoms, the leading interaction is dipole–dipole. Classically, creating correlated dipole fluctuations costs more energy than the interaction returns, so no attraction arises. Quantum zero-point fluctuations instead make the mean-square dipole nonzero; correlated fluctuations produce a van der Waals attraction. Perturbation theory yields a first-order \(C_3/R^3\) potential when one atom is excited and a second-order \(C_6/R^6\) potential for two ground-state atoms.

Equivalent descriptions use coupled harmonic oscillators or LC circuits, where the first-order coupling cancels but quadratic zero-point effects remain. Another description has one atom’s dipole fluctuation induce an aligned dipole in the other atom through polarization. Vacuum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field can also induce correlated dipoles; including propagation effects gives the long-range \(R^{-7}\) Casimir–Polder potential, while the instantaneous, short-range result scales as \(R^{-6}\).

A QED treatment represents the interaction as virtual-photon exchange between the atoms. Fourth-order diagrams and their energy denominators distinguish short-range behavior, where the photon frequency dominates, from long-range behavior, where the atomic resonance dominates. The transition occurs when the atom separation is comparable to the resonant wavelength. The lecture emphasizes that a consistent quantum description quantizes both atomic and electromagnetic-field fluctuations.

The study examined educators’ perceptions of AI’s potential and challenges in education, focusing on academic staff and administrators in Kuwait University’s College of Education, where limited evidence from the Arab region was identified. Literature reviewed highlighted AI’s support for flexible e-learning, data analysis, machine learning, natural language processing, and personalized teaching, alongside concerns about limited teacher interaction, inadequate pedagogy and expertise, assessment difficulties, ethical issues, and the need for teacher development.

A cross-sectional random-sample survey included 63 participants and used three online questionnaires measuring attitudes toward AI, educators’ perspectives, and AI education scenarios and applications. SPSS descriptive statistics, t-tests, and one-way ANOVA were applied.

Faculty members showed medium acceptance of AI (mean 3.37 on a six-point scale), with strong belief that AI would benefit humanity (4.03), while 58.7% reported no prior teaching experience with it. They rated links between education and AI moderately highly (4.21), particularly data analysis and natural language processing. Student-empowerment requirements averaged 4.36, led by identifying AI use cases, assessing system intelligence, and recognizing technical limitations. Challenges were rated high (4.83), especially shortages of suitable teaching materials, insufficient experience, subject complexity, limited best-practice examples, and inadequate class time. AI education scenarios averaged 4.82, with personalized intelligent teaching, smart schools, and online or mobile remote education highest. Table 5 showed substantial opposition to explicit curriculum integration, although the narrative stated that most participants supported it.

Inferential tests reported no significant differences by gender, academic degree, or department, with the gender comparison for challenges reported as an exception (p=.067). The study concluded that AI has educational promise but requires technologically aligned pedagogy, preparation, safeguards, and reforms. Limitations included excluding student perspectives; larger studies across multiple universities were recommended.

The lecture introduces expected utility as economics’ main framework for choices under risk. It assigns utility to final outcomes and weights those utilities by their probabilities, assuming that only final outcomes matter and probabilities enter linearly. Under this model, a concave utility function represents risk aversion: a person prefers a gamble’s expected monetary value for certain to the gamble itself. The framework simplifies away factors such as anxiety, stress, regret, disappointment, and differences between gains and losses.

The lecture identifies three stylized facts: people often reduce risk through insurance and informal arrangements; they accept risk when expected returns are sufficiently high; and some voluntarily seek risky activities with negative expected returns, potentially for entertainment, addiction, self-control problems, beliefs, or preferences. Economists measure risk aversion using absolute or relative risk-aversion coefficients, certainty equivalents, choices between gambles, and insurance choices.

A central problem is that expected utility cannot readily reconcile small- and large-stakes behavior. Under weak concavity, Matthew Rabin’s result shows that consistently rejecting a 50–50 gamble that wins $11 and loses $10 can imply implausibly extreme aversion to large gambles and an extraordinarily rapid decline in marginal utility as wealth rises. Thus, preferences inferred from small gambles appear inconsistent with behavior involving large sums.

The lecture concludes by introducing Justin Sydnor’s analysis of roughly 50,000 home-insurance policies, using customers’ deductible menus, premiums, and claims to place bounds on their risk aversion.

CSUSB veteran students described military education benefits. Active-duty members receive per-class tuition assistance up to $4,500 annually, though training exercises can interrupt school. The Post-9/11 GI Bill offers eligible members and veterans who served at least 90 days up to four years of benefits, covering full tuition at public schools based on service months and credits. Benefits expire after 10–15 years but remain usable after interruptions. The Montgomery GI Bill gives full-time students $1,857 and part-time students half, while recipients pay tuition, fees, books, and other educational expenses.
Sears borrowed $100 million from Lampert’s ESL Investments, which agreed to lend up to $100 million more. Amid declining sales, Sears plans to close more than 300 Kmart and Sears stores in 2017.

R. L. Wells was convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to two years in the penitentiary. His appeal was dismissed because the appeal bond was approved by a special judge rather than Judge Munroe, who presided over the trial, as required by statute.

Background and policy memoranda for President Roosevelt and the American delegation at the Malta and Yalta Conferences were completed on January 16, 1945. The resulting black binder, known as the “Yalta Briefing Book” and including seven memoranda on “World Security,” was soon presented to the President.

In a second conversation with the Soviet ambassador, Special Assistant to the Secretary of State Leo Pasvolsky discussed the Dumbarton Oaks proposals. He clarified that Chapter VIII concerned whether the Security Council should encourage a regional group or agency to settle local or regional disputes peacefully. The ambassador wanted to understand the arguments for the voting formula before departing for Moscow, though the discussion produced no new points.

The ambassador considered the International Court’s substance settled and believed details could readily be agreed upon; Moscow was studying the Dumbarton Oaks documents. He also discussed dependent areas, noting the Soviet Government’s strong interest in Secretary Hull’s memorandum despite having no colonies or colonial-administration experience. Pasvolsky outlined approaches involving trust and colonial areas, general principles, international trusteeship for detached areas, regional commissions, international accountability, and relations between the international organization and regional commissions. He said only trusteeship questions properly belonged on the United Nations Conference agenda, while colonial issues might be addressed later through a special conference or another mechanism. The ambassador asked whether other important powers should participate and whether the future international organization could arrange such discussions; Pasvolsky said any procedure was possible.

In *Shircliff v. State*, the court affirmed the judgment against Alexander Shircliff, who and Edward O’Connor were indicted for conspiring to bribe township trustee Valentine Strange to employ O’Connor as a public-school teacher. The court held the indictment stated an offense without alleging that a school position was vacant, because trustees have a legal duty to employ teachers and the conspiracy’s objective need not be accomplished.

The continuance and evidentiary objections were not reviewable because the supporting materials and exceptions were not incorporated into a valid bill of exceptions. O’Connor’s discharge to serve as a witness could not be challenged on appeal because no objection was made in the lower court. The court presumed the first specially appointed judge was absent or unable to preside, allowing the regular judge to appoint a replacement who could enter judgment. Shircliff’s sentence of two and one-half years’ imprisonment and a $100 fine was affirmed with costs. Justice Niblack did not participate.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats will not support a partisan Republican spending bill that fails to extend enhanced Obamacare tax credits expiring at the end of 2025. With a government shutdown scheduled for 12:01 a.m. Wednesday absent a deal, Jeffries and other Democratic leaders are set to meet President Trump and Republican congressional leadership. Republicans want funding legislation approved before negotiating future tax-credit extensions, while at least seven Senate Democrats would need to support Republicans to avert a shutdown.

H&M reported March local-currency sales growth of 6%, below its preliminary 7% reading, as competition and weak demand threatened its 10–15% full-year growth target. February sales fell for the first time in four years. The retailer operated 4,426 stores, up 11% year over year, while expanding e-commerce and higher-priced brands and investing in a more responsive Asian-sourced supply chain. Analysts with “sell” ratings cited tough conditions and continued store expansion.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022. Its common stock and two note series were listed on Nasdaq. As of December 31, 2021, non-affiliates held approximately $2.5 trillion of common stock, and 7,457,891,872 shares were outstanding as of July 25, 2022. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements depend on assumptions subject to risks and uncertainties.

Microsoft describes itself as a technology company focused on productivity, cloud computing, AI, personal computing, security, and gaming. Its products and services include operating systems, productivity and collaboration applications, server products, business applications, developer tools, cloud services, online advertising, PCs, tablets, consoles, gaming and entertainment products, and other intelligent devices. Its R&D priorities are to reinvent productivity and business processes, build an intelligent cloud and edge platform, and advance more personal computing.

Key offerings include Microsoft 365, Office 365, Dynamics 365, LinkedIn, Teams, Viva, Power Platform, Azure, Azure Stack, Azure Arc, Azure Synapse, Azure Machine Learning, Azure Orbital, Microsoft Mesh, Windows 11, Surface devices, Xbox hardware, Game Pass, and cloud gaming. Microsoft completed its Nuance Communications acquisition in March 2022, acquired ZeniMax Media, acquired Xandr on June 6, 2022, and announced plans in January 2022 to acquire Activision Blizzard.

Microsoft reports three operating segments:

- Productivity and Business Processes: Office Commercial and Consumer, LinkedIn, and Dynamics.
- Intelligent Cloud: Azure and other cloud services, server products, GitHub, Nuance, and enterprise support and consulting services.
- More Personal Computing: Windows, Surface devices and accessories, Xbox content, hardware and services, and search and news advertising.

The company competes with large technology firms, specialized providers, advertising-supported services, open-source offerings, vertically integrated hardware and software companies, and competing application marketplaces. Risks include intense competition, rapidly changing technology and user needs, pressure on revenue and margins, marketplace distribution constraints, and execution risks associated with expanding cloud-based services.

Microsoft operates regional support centers and datacenters across the Americas, Europe, Australia, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. Devices are primarily manufactured by third-party contract manufacturers, although some components have limited supplier flexibility. Product development is organized around Cloud and AI; Experiences and Devices; Security, Compliance, Identity, and Management; Technology and Research; LinkedIn; and Gaming. Microsoft reported more than 69,000 issued patents and over 19,000 pending worldwide.

Products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, licensing partners, digital marketplaces, online stores, and retailers. Volume licensing options include Enterprise Agreements, Microsoft Customer Agreements, Microsoft Online Subscription Agreements, Microsoft Products and Services Agreements, Open Value, and Select Plus. Customers include consumers, small and medium organizations, global enterprises, public institutions, internet service providers, developers, and OEMs.

Microsoft’s sustainability commitments include becoming carbon negative by 2030 and removing all carbon emitted since 1975 by 2050. The company also committed to being water positive and achieving zero waste by 2030, invested $1 billion in climate technologies, purchased the removal of 1.4 million metric tons of carbon, and committed $200 million toward carbon removal by 2030. It also launched Microsoft Cloud for Sustainability.

The company’s racial equity initiative focuses on strengthening communities, evolving its supplier and partner ecosystem, and increasing representation and inclusion. By fiscal 2022, Microsoft reported being 90% toward its goal of doubling Black and African American managers, senior individual contributors, and senior leaders in the United States, and more than 90% toward its goal of spending $500 million with double the number of Black- and African American-owned suppliers.

Microsoft’s global skills initiative assisted more than 30 million people in 249 countries and territories. It also launched a U.S. community-college cybersecurity campaign intended to help train and recruit 250,000 people by 2025, supported training at 150 community colleges, and provided scholarships and resources to 25,000 students.

As of June 30, 2022, Microsoft employed approximately 221,000 full-time workers, including 122,000 in the United States and 99,000 internationally. Its stated culture emphasizes a growth mindset, customer focus, diversity and inclusion, operating as one company, and learning and development. Employees completed more than 4.7 million online courses in fiscal 2022, while Microsoft maintained employee surveys and multiple programs supporting hybrid work, well-being, career development, and pay equity.

In *Canion v. United States*, the court held that section 402(c) foreign value was the proper valuation basis. For the invoiced French merchandise, value equaled invoice unit values plus 12.44% and packing costs; for 40 excess boxes of item 21008, it was 337 French francs each, plus 12.44% and packing. Judgment was rendered accordingly.

The U.S. provided over $55,000 to preserve 3,000–5,000 personal items of Khmer Rouge prisoners at Cambodia’s Tuol Sleng prison, where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and killed. The deteriorating belongings will be conserved, with some displayed at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum to educate Cambodians.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016 presented unaudited consolidated financial statements and management’s analysis. Net sales rose 28% to $29.128 billion from $22.717 billion a year earlier, comprising $20.581 billion of product sales and $8.547 billion of service sales. Operating income increased to $1.071 billion from $255 million, and net income was $513 million versus a $57 million loss. Diluted earnings per share were $1.07, compared with a loss of $0.12.

North America reported sales of $16.996 billion and operating income of $588 million; International reported sales of $9.566 billion and an operating loss of $121 million; and AWS reported sales of $2.566 billion and operating income of $604 million. Sales growth was attributed primarily to increased unit sales, marketplace sales, lower prices and shipping offers, greater inventory availability, and broader selection in North America and International, while AWS benefited from increased customer usage and productivity, partly offset by price reductions. Operating expenses increased with higher sales, fulfillment expansion, marketing, and technology infrastructure investment. Outbound net shipping costs rose 44% to $1.455 billion.

At March 31, 2016, cash and cash equivalents were $12.470 billion, marketable securities were $3.389 billion, total assets were $61.128 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $14.756 billion. Q1 operating, investing, and financing cash flows were negative $2.160 billion, $693 million, and $789 million, respectively. For the trailing twelve months, operating cash flow was $11.258 billion and free cash flow was $6.361 billion. Amazon held $15.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, had no borrowings under its $2.0 billion credit facility, and stated that operating cash flow, liquid balances, and borrowing availability should meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least 12 months.

Total contractual commitments were $34.972 billion, including debt principal and interest of $12.674 billion, capital lease obligations of $7.632 billion, operating leases of $6.939 billion, finance leases of $2.406 billion, purchase obligations of $1.825 billion, and other commitments of $3.496 billion. Purchase obligations and open purchase orders totaled $6.5 billion. Long-term debt had a face value of $8.315 billion, and the board authorized a $5 billion common-stock repurchase program; no shares were repurchased in either Q1 2016 or Q1 2015.

The notes described legal and tax uncertainties, including European digital-media tariff proceedings, patent and wage-and-hour litigation, an IRS transfer-pricing dispute seeking approximately $1.5 billion of additional federal tax, a French assessment of €196 million, and an EU state-aid investigation. Amazon also adopted the non-current classification of deferred tax assets and liabilities and was evaluating new revenue, lease, and stock-compensation accounting guidance. Critical accounting estimates involved inventory valuation, goodwill impairment, stock-based compensation forfeitures, and income taxes. Forward-looking results were subject to risks including economic conditions, foreign exchange changes, competition, investment and expansion decisions, fulfillment operations, inventory management, legal proceedings, and tax audits.

Connor McDavid signed a two-year, $25 million extension with the Edmonton Oilers, completing negotiations within hours of his decision. The 28-year-old center was set to become an unrestricted free agent after his 11th season with Edmonton and had previously signed an eight-year, $100 million deal in 2017. McDavid has 1,082 career points, 361 goals, five scoring titles and three Hart Trophies, and won the Conn Smythe Trophy in 2024 despite a losing playoff run. He chose Edmonton after considering the Oilers’ contention window, an aging roster and goaltending concerns. Edmonton also gave defenseman Jake Walman a seven-year, $49 million extension.

NVIDIA reported unaudited financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2019, ended April 29, 2018. Revenue was $3.207 billion, up 66% year over year, while gross margin increased to 64.5% from 59.4%. Operating income rose to $1.295 billion from $554 million, net income increased to $1.244 billion from $507 million, and diluted earnings per share reached $1.98, compared with $0.79. GPU revenue rose 77% to $2.765 billion, led by gaming and datacenter growth, while Tegra Processor revenue increased 33% to $442 million. Gaming revenue was $1.723 billion, datacenter revenue $701 million, professional visualization revenue $251 million, and automotive revenue $145 million.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.30 billion, and operating activities generated $1.445 billion. Total assets were $11.460 billion, total liabilities $3.743 billion, and shareholders’ equity $7.717 billion. NVIDIA repurchased 3 million shares for $655 million and paid $91 million in dividends during the quarter. It stated that it intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders during fiscal 2019.

The company adopted the new revenue recognition standard using the modified retrospective method, increasing opening retained earnings by $7 million; the quarter’s impact was not significant. Stock-based compensation was $129 million, and income tax expense was $67 million, representing an effective rate of 5.1%.

NVIDIA disclosed patent litigation involving Polaris Innovations and ZiiLabs, along with related U.S. and German proceedings and an ITC investigation. No liability was accrued because potential losses were not considered probable and could not be reasonably estimated. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, no material changes occurred in internal control over financial reporting, and there were no material changes in previously disclosed market risks or risk factors. The company also announced NVIDIA RTX and the DRIVE Constellation server with DRIVE Sim during the quarter.

U.S. plans for dependent areas sought to advance dependent peoples through international cooperation, promote self-government and higher economic and social standards, protect security, and ensure nondiscriminatory treatment. A March 9, 1943 draft declaration distinguished mandated or detached territories, proposed for international trusteeship, from colonial territories. It also proposed regional commissions and progressive self-government leading to full independence on a fixed schedule. British objections were raised at Quebec, Moscow, and during 1944 London talks, after which U.S. plans were refined.

At the Joint Chiefs of Staff’s request, the trusteeship chapter was removed from tentative proposals to avoid contentious territorial questions, so dependent territories were not discussed at Dumbarton Oaks. Three related documents were being revised for presidential approval before intergovernmental discussion. Separately, Britain accepted the President’s proposal on Security Council voting, with a clarification concerning Chapter 8, Section C. Secretary of War Stimson urged the major powers to reach agreement on fundamental organization and a general peace guarantee. He also advised postponing discussion of territorial acquisitions, trusteeships, and adjustments until the Soviet Union committed to the Pacific war, warning that controversy could weaken wartime unity.

The Creek agent invoked U.S. protection after Georgia surveyors entered treaty-secured Indian lands, some reportedly being arrested by the Indians. The Executive cited the 1802 statute prohibiting such surveys and directed U.S. prosecutors in Georgia to pursue civil prosecutions, while assuring the Creeks that their treaty rights would be protected and urging them to avoid hostilities.

Military force was withheld initially because Georgia’s authorities had authorized the surveys, and using troops could have produced a conflict between a state and the federal government. Nevertheless, the Georgia action was declared contrary to treaty and federal law. If Georgia persisted and other legal remedies failed, the Executive pledged to enforce the law and treaty obligations through available military force. Congress was asked to consider whether additional legislation was necessary.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture and its Hybrid Rendering model, which combines real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores in each streaming multiprocessor handle BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing shader cores for graphics and compute work. Combined with BVH acceleration and denoising, these cores make real-time ray tracing practical and deliver roughly tenfold improvements over software ray tracing on Pascal.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only, deep-learning technology stack that uses Tensor Cores and provides pre-trained AI features through a thin API. Its applications include DLSS image enhancement, inpainting, frame interpolation for AI Slow-Mo, and 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling with AI Super Rez.

DLSS is trained using thousands of 64x-supersampled reference images and matching lower-quality inputs. Its standard mode produces TAA-like quality with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X processes target-resolution input with a larger network to approach 64x-supersampled quality. It is intended to avoid common temporal artifacts such as blurring, disocclusion, and transparency.

Mesh shading adds task and mesh shader stages using cooperative thread models. Task shaders process object lists, launch mesh shaders, and select appropriate levels of detail, while mesh shaders generate rasterizer triangles. This reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks, supports hundreds of thousands of objects in real time, and supports dynamic geometric operations such as spherical CAD cutaways.

Variable Rate Shading dynamically controls shading in 16-by-16-pixel regions using multiple pixel footprints, while leaving visibility sampling independent. Its applications include Content Adaptive Shading for spatially or temporally uniform areas, Motion Adaptive Shading for moving objects, and Foveated Rendering that concentrates detail near the viewer’s focus. VRS can also increase shading rates for multisample anti-aliasing.

Texture Space Shading stores computed appearance values in texture-space texels and later samples them for screen pixels. It decouples visibility and appearance sampling, reuses previously shaded texels within or across frames, supports multiple resolution levels, and improves temporal stability. It can also reuse one eye’s shaded results when rendering stereo VR images.

Multi-View Rendering draws multiple viewpoints or character instances in one pass. Turing hardware supports up to four views per pass, while APIs support as many as 32 views. It expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection capabilities and supports stereo and wide-field-of-view VR, multiple shadow maps, and independently varied view-dependent attributes.

Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, permits different resource types within the same heap, supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, and uses RT Cores to accelerate ray-traced audio. VR features include expanded multi-view projection, foveated rendering, and improved indirect sound simulation.

The TU104 full chip contains 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and a 256-bit memory interface. It is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The TU106 used in the GeForce RTX 2070 has 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

For hybrid workloads, NVIDIA proposes RTX-OPS, weighting Tensor operations at 20%, FP32 operations at 80%, RT operations at 40%, and INT32 operations at 28%. A representative Turing frame spends about 20% on DLSS and 80% on rendering, with ray tracing approximately half of the remaining rendering time.

Ray tracing casts rays backward from the camera through image pixels into the scene, where intersections determine color and lighting. Ray casting performs visibility tests, while path tracing follows many rays through multiple interactions. BVH hierarchies reduce intersection tests by traversing progressively smaller bounding boxes; they can be rebuilt or more cheaply refitted as scenes change. Denoising improves sparse, noisy results and reduces the rays required.

Turing ray tracing can provide more physically correct shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections than shadow maps, screen-space ambient occlusion, screen-space reflections, and cubemap probes. NVIDIA attributes real-time ray tracing to the combination of hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH acceleration, and RT Cores. The document also states that NVIDIA provides the specifications without warranties, reserves the right to change them, and limits use of its materials to approved reproduction.

The passage describes container patterns for single-node and distributed systems. In the ambassador pattern, a tightly coupled container brokers communication between an application and external services. Applications connect to a local endpoint while the ambassador handles concerns such as routing requests to storage shards, discovering environment-specific services, or splitting traffic between production and experimental implementations. Kubernetes examples use twemproxy for sharded Redis and memcached and nginx to route 90% of traffic to production and 10% to experiments.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s external interface to conform to a predefined standard without changing the application container itself. It is used to translate metrics into Prometheus-compatible formats, normalize heterogeneous logs through Fluentd, capture Redis slow-query information, convert Apache Storm data into queryable events, and expose richer HTTP health checks for MySQL. Separate adapters promote reuse, isolate failures, simplify upgrades, and avoid maintaining modified third-party images.

The passage then introduces microservices as loosely coupled, network-based components with formal APIs that can be developed, released, and scaled independently, although this increases architectural and debugging complexity. Replicated load-balanced services place identical stateless instances behind a load balancer, use readiness probes, and require multiple replicas for high availability. Session tracking can use IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing. Additional replicated tiers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination, as demonstrated with Varnish and nginx.

Sharded services divide state among machines, with a root routing each request to the appropriate shard. Sharding functions commonly use hashing and modulo, requiring deterministic and uniform distribution. Choosing a suitable shard key and using consistent hashing can reduce redistribution when shard counts change. Replicated shards improve resilience, support upgrades under load, and allow hot shards to scale independently.

Scatter/gather systems distribute each request to all leaf nodes in parallel and combine their partial results at a root. This accelerates independent computation but introduces coordination overhead and straggler effects that can increase latency and reduce availability; replicating leaf shards mitigates these issues.

Finally, function-as-a-service provides automatic scaling, automatic restarts, simple deployment, and stateless modularity. Its forced decoupling complicates debugging and dependency management, requires rigorous monitoring, stores state externally, and makes it a poor fit for long-running background processing.

AT&T said it will activate its LTE-M network nationwide by the end of June to connect low-power Internet of Things devices. LTE-M uses minimal data and energy, can last up to 10 years on one charge, and penetrates walls better than standard cellular signals. Pepsi demonstrated connected soda fountains that track flavor preferences, while RM2 showed composite pallets with built-in radios to track pallets and freight. Capstone Metering demonstrated smart water meters that can detect continuous toilet flushing, leaks and other problems. AT&T said these devices use little data and remain largely disconnected, so they should not impede ordinary network use. Pricing has not been set, but AT&T is considering per-bit or per-device charges.

Detroit’s players and coach emphasize capitalizing on limited chances and the importance of power-play preparation against the Red Wings. They praise an opposing star’s maturity, offense, defense, and confidence, and reflect on recovering from a long injury, making changes after a losing stretch, and the competitiveness of the series against the same team that defeated them the previous year.

Apple Inc. reported unaudited results for its fiscal first quarter of 2016, ended December 26, 2015. Net sales increased 2% to $75.9 billion, while net income rose to $18.4 billion from $18.0 billion and diluted earnings per share increased to $3.28 from $3.06. Gross margin was 40.1%, up from 39.9%, but operating income declined slightly to $24.2 billion as operating expenses rose 14%, led by increased research and development spending.

Product sales were $51.6 billion for iPhone, up 1%; $7.1 billion for iPad, down 21%; $6.7 billion for Mac, down 3%; $6.1 billion for Services, up 26%; and $4.4 billion for Other Products, up 62%. Services growth included a $548 million payment from Samsung related to patent litigation. Regional net sales declined 4% in the Americas and 12% in Japan, while increasing 4% in Europe, 14% in Greater China, and 4% in the Rest of Asia Pacific. During the quarter, Apple released OS X El Capitan and tvOS and began shipping iPad Pro and the new Apple TV.

The effective tax rate declined to 25.3% from 26.2%. Unrecognized tax benefits totaled $7.4 billion, including $2.7 billion that could affect the effective tax rate. The European Commission was investigating alleged state aid to Apple through profit allocation in Ireland, but Apple could not estimate the potential impact as of quarter-end.

At December 26, 2015, Apple held $215.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, with $16.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Operating activities generated $27.5 billion, investing activities used $20.5 billion, and financing activities used $11.4 billion. Total assets were $293.3 billion, total liabilities were $165.0 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $128.3 billion. Commercial paper outstanding was $7.3 billion, and the principal amount of term debt was $55.5 billion.

Apple declared a quarterly dividend of $0.52 per share and had used $110 billion of its $140 billion share-repurchase authorization. The company expected 2016 capital expenditures of approximately $15 billion and anticipated second-quarter gross margin of 39% to 39.5%.

Apple disclosed risks from concentrated and outsourced supply chains, foreign-currency movements, competition, product transitions, and potential cost increases. It had $20.7 billion of manufacturing and component purchase commitments, $7.9 billion of other off-balance-sheet obligations, and $6.6 billion of future minimum operating lease payments. The company also adopted a standard classifying deferred tax assets and liabilities as noncurrent and evaluated forthcoming financial-instrument and revenue-recognition standards.

Tesla introduced standard versions of the Model Y SUV, priced just under $40,000, and the Model 3 sedan, starting around $37,000. The Model Y lacks features found on higher-end versions, costs about $5,000 less than the prior entry-level model, and has an estimated range of 321 miles. Tesla also released an updated supervised driver-assistance system as shares fell about 3% Tuesday following a 5% Monday gain. The lower prices may attract buyers after federal EV tax credits ended, amid intense competition. Tesla’s vehicle sales remain weak, with the Cybertruck the latest new model shipped. Investors are awaiting promised products including a redesigned Roadster, Cybercab, robotaxis and Optimus robots, none of which have entered production or reached the market. Tesla shares gained 40% in the third quarter and were up 12% for the year, aided by Elon Musk’s roughly $1 billion stock purchase.

Rock Springs City Council will hold a May 1 public hearing on amendments allowing seasonal outdoor dining decks at downtown restaurants. The proposal requires approval, inspections, six-foot sidewalk clearance, off-season equipment storage, fire-hydrant access, and restrictions on umbrellas and alcohol service.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said ace Tarik Skubal will not pitch in Game 4 of the ALDS against the Mariners despite Detroit facing elimination. Skubal completed his normal preparation for a potential Game 5 after delivering seven innings, allowing two runs and striking out nine in Game 2.

LEGO DC Super Villains was announced with a full trailer. Players create a villain and work with DC villains in a parallel universe without heroes. It launches October 16, 2018, for PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, with special editions featuring bonus characters.

Pakistan halted three China-Pakistan Economic Corridor road projects after China stopped funding, according to Dawn; work awaits renewed Chinese financing and approval. The parliamentary committee disputed claims the projects were shelved. Experts cited Sri Lanka’s Hambantota Port transfer to China, while tensions followed Pakistan’s rejection of CPEC funding and yuan trading.

Jarome is praised as one of the league’s best right wingers, with strong energy, discipline, work in difficult areas and playoff performance. His improvement is credited to assuming team leadership and reducing the pressure of being seen as the face of the team. The speaker says Jarome responds better to support and advice than harsh criticism.

Defensive deployment is also discussed, including using versatile players on either side, adjusting shifts rather than benching two players, and moving away from using older defensemen to shield younger ones. The team is said to be focusing on its own improvements rather than comparing itself with Detroit or San Jose. The speaker dismisses poor ice and a demanding playoff schedule as excuses, noting that the players maintained their competitive mindset.

An older defenseman is described as underrated, disciplined and effective against top opponents. The speaker also praises an official nicknamed “Scamp” for his speed, communication with players, informal authority and continued development in his role.

The author argues that national legislators should enact a permanent, gradually introduced inheritance tax on gifts, bequests, and devises. Rates should be low on moderate inheritances but rise sharply for large estates and potentially for beneficiaries more distant in kinship, placing an increasing burden on fortunes whose perpetuation is said not to benefit the country while encouraging thrift and ambition. Earlier federal inheritance taxes were enacted in 1797, 1862, and 1898, and the Supreme Court upheld the Civil War tax and the inheritance-tax provision of the 1898 act.

The passage distinguishes inheritance taxes from income taxes. Congress enacted an income-tax law in 1861, while the 1894 law was held unconstitutional by a one-vote majority; the divided decision suggests a constitutional income-tax law might still be devised. Legislation should first be attempted without amending the Constitution, but a constitutional amendment may ultimately be necessary if no workable alternative exists.

A retrospective cohort study analyzed 290 CABG patients treated from 2017–2021, most of whom underwent on-pump surgery, to assess complications and the roles of shunt number and internal thoracic artery use. Postoperative complications included arrhythmia, psychosis, stroke, myocardial infarction, hydrothorax, re-sternotomy, dyspnea, and sternal wound infection; hydrothorax was most frequent.

Older age was associated with more complications, longer ICU and total hospitalization, and greater risks of arrhythmia, psychosis, and stroke. Progressive angina and post-myocardial infarction myocardial sclerosis were also associated with more complications. Diabetes was linked to higher BMI and longer hospitalization, with diabetic complications more frequent among patients with higher BMI. Low BMI, prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass, and prolonged aortic cross-clamp time were associated with hydrothorax and longer hospitalization. Left ventricular aneurysm and CABG with aneurysm repair were associated with lower ejection fraction and longer bypass and cross-clamp times.

Complication counts were positively associated with age, CPB and cross-clamp times, and hospitalization duration. No statistically significant association was found between complication counts and the number of shunts or internal thoracic arteries used, or between complication counts and survival status. Two internal thoracic arteries were associated with longer CPB and cross-clamp times, while older patients received fewer.

The team matched up its four centers by having Tanner and Tyler play together. Kopy, a Selke nominee, was praised for his tenacious two-way play, playoff playmaking, and heavy minutes in crucial situations. Toffoli and Pearson were cited as role models. The team’s success was attributed to preparation, maturity, leadership, and collective effort rather than star status; despite being young and playoff-proven, it still has much to learn. Coach Sutter was praised for strong leadership and his work with young players. Slava was performing well in the Stanley Cup Final, while the team was described as fast and treating every game as an elimination game. The goalie was called a top league goalie and expected to play the next game.

The speaker credits the team’s early emphasis on being tough at home for its playoff success and confidence in handling adversity. He calls John a key contributor, praising his hard work, defense, and ability to step up after Holik left and when another teammate went down. Despite injuries, fatigue, and demanding travel, the team overcame a bumpy season, integrated new players, and won the Stanley Cup. He believes John deserves Conn Smythe recognition while acknowledging other contributors. Looking ahead, the team aims to develop its young players and pursue more championships, though he does not yet call it a dynasty.

The court held that a creditor’s action requiring assignees to account for a debtor’s assigned property and distribute the proceeds among creditors was not an action for money received in a fiduciary capacity under Code §179, subdivision 2. The proceeding sought an accounting and distribution, not merely recovery of money received. Accordingly, the plaintiff’s arrest was unauthorized, and the $100 false-imprisonment judgment was affirmed with costs.

America Saves Week 2017 will run February 27–March 4, promoting good savings behavior through daily focuses and engagement opportunities. Coordinated by America Saves and the American Savings Education Council, it offers participant recognition, resources and savings-planning tools.

In 2011, St. Olaf student Erik Brust founded JonnyPops to fulfill an idea he shared with cousin Jonathan Jeffrey before Jeffrey died from a drug overdose at 21. Brust and classmate Connor Wray developed additive-free fruit pops made with fruit, real cream, cane sugar, and salt. After campus taste tests, JonnyPops began selling at Twin Cities markets and the Minnesota Zoo in 2012, then expanded into several states by 2013. The co-founders entered grocery retail in Minnesota with about 50 partners in 2014, won the MN Cup Student Division, and later took full-time roles after graduating. Both were named to Forbes’ 2018 “30 Under 30” list, while JonnyPops reached 10,000 distribution points nationwide. Its Delights line introduced five new flavors in March. Through its Better Pop for a Better World mission, the company prints encouraging messages on pop sticks and partners with retailers to fund addiction treatment organizations including Hazelden and Betty Ford.

Nvidia will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees despite the Trump administration’s new $100,000 fee for new applicants, CEO Jensen Huang said, calling legal immigration essential to U.S. technology and innovation. Nvidia could pay an estimated $147.3 million if the fee applies to H-1B holders approved in 2025, based on USCIS data; it does not apply to renewals or current holders. Huang previously called the fee too high, while a Nvidia spokesperson declined to comment.

The speaker thanks citizens for his reelection, accepts the continuing obligation to deserve their confidence, and attributes the election’s unity less to personal merit than to the strength and stability of the Union. He reviews the recent war, which disrupted commerce, invaded frontiers, killed many citizens, and added $120 million to the public debt. In response, the government reduced its land force, pursued coastal fortifications and naval expansion under laws passed in 1815 and 1816, and maintained that these defenses were economical, protective, and intended to preserve peace.

On foreign affairs, the government maintained neutrality in the conflict between Spain and its South American colonies, treating it as a civil war and granting equal port, arms, trade, and commerce privileges to both sides. Piratical activity in neighboring seas and Florida was suppressed, while some offenders were pardoned when mitigating circumstances were shown. A ratified treaty with Spain addressed U.S. claims, established a western boundary, and ceded Florida, which provided access to the Atlantic, valuable harbors, protection from Indigenous attacks, and control over routes supporting western commerce. An 1818 British treaty renewed commercial arrangements and settled disputes over fisheries and other interests, though some restrictions remained. Negotiations with France continued, and naval forces in the Mediterranean and Pacific protected commerce and suppressed piracy and the slave trade.

The speaker cites the payment of nearly $67 million in public debt and substantial progress in defense and improvements as evidence of prosperity achieved without direct taxation. Falling prices had reduced revenue and led to loans, prompting consideration of restoring internal duties and excises to provide stable income and support domestic manufacturing. He also recommends ending recognized Indigenous sovereignty, securing individual land rights, and compensating tribes through permanent funds for civil government, education, farming, and immediate support.

Although Europe faced renewed danger of war, the United States expected to remain at peace, preserve neutrality, defend maritime rights, seek redress amicably, and prepare for emergencies during peacetime. Internally, the address praises the representative republican system for placing sovereignty in the people, resolving disputes through argument, and steadily improving. It also emphasizes territorial expansion, control of the Mississippi, Louisiana and Florida, admission of new states, and rapid population growth. The speaker concludes by taking office with confidence in his assistants, public support, and divine protection.

This protocol aims to evaluate the relationship between serial rt-PCR Ct values or other viral-burden measures and the likelihood and duration of replication-competent SARS-CoV-2 in solid-organ or hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipients. Searches will cover LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO COVID-19 database from November 2019 through December 31, 2021, without language restrictions. Four researchers will screen studies, with independent full-text review and third-reviewer arbitration of disagreements.

Eligible primary studies must report serial Ct or other respiratory viral-burden data and viral-culture results from the same pre- or post-transport samples. Postmortem-only and nonrespiratory samples, studies without viral culture, reviews, and posters or abstracts will be excluded. Data extraction will be independently checked.

Study quality will assess case definitions, population reporting, follow-up, replicability of PCR methods and standards, and appropriateness of viral-culture methods. Results will follow PRISMA and be summarized narratively and in tables, including a summary estimate of the relationship between viral burden and infectious virus. Pooling to establish a cutoff is not planned because laboratory methods and PCR controls vary; age and sex effects will be examined if data permit. The work is funded by the NIHR Evidence Synthesis Working Group and the University of Calgary, and competing interests are declared.

The passage mourns the President’s assassination, praises his courage, leadership, and achievements, and assures citizens that constitutional succession preserves governmental stability despite the tragedy. The new President vows to continue efforts to correct abuses, promote economy and prosperity, ensure domestic security, and maintain peaceful foreign relations. Lincolnshire County Council approved a new care leavers strategy after councillors heard that young people leaving care struggle with adult responsibilities and costs. The council provides support beyond age 18, including council tax discounts, advice and guidance to 25, help with university and driving-licence costs, and leaving-care services costing approximately £1.2 million.

A fossil of the 245-million-year-old marine reptile Dinocephalosaurus found in Yunnan, China, contains a developing embryo, showing that this fish-eating archosauromorph gave birth to live young rather than laying eggs. It is the first known viviparous member of a group that includes birds, crocodilians, dinosaurs and pterosaurs, changing understanding of vertebrate reproductive evolution. The approximately 13-foot reptile had a very long neck, paddle-like flippers and teeth suited to catching fish. Researchers identified the embryo by its curled posture and forward orientation, unlike swallowed prey. Viviparity allowed it to remain fully marine and avoid land egg-laying, while its offspring’s sex was genetically determined.

The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed a judgment for Farmers State Bank of Craig on a $3,000 promissory note against Samuel J. Lydick. Lydick alleged that the note and earlier obligations were given for stock in the Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company through fraudulent representations and sought damages from the bank and its officer, Everett J. Martin.

The jury found that the bank purchased the note for value, in good faith, without notice of defects, in the usual course of business, and before maturity. It also found that Martin had not made the alleged fraudulent representations. The court properly withdrew a later stock-purchase claim from the jury because there was insufficient evidence to support it.

The court rejected the argument that the bank, as the original payee of an unindorsed note, could not be a holder in due course. Applying the controlling Nebraska rule, it held that a payee who receives a negotiable instrument for value, in good faith, before maturity, and without notice is a holder in due course and is protected against fraud and failure-of-consideration defenses arising between the maker or drawer and the prior holder. The evidence sustained the verdict, the jury instructions were correct, and the judgment was affirmed.

James Schenck, president and CEO of PenFed Credit Union, accepted the Large Business Philanthropist of the Year award at the 20th annual Volunteer Alexandria Business Philanthropy Summit, citing PenFed’s 2,500 employees and its “People Helping People” philosophy. PenFed and the PenFed Foundation recently donated $300,000 to Serve our Willing Warriors, $125,000 to the Kennedy Center, $100,000 to DC Habitat for Humanity, $75,000 to the Military Officers Association of America, and $15,000 to Bunker Labs. The foundation also supported accessible homes through the Gary Sinise Foundation and launched the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program for veteran-owned startups.

The Alexandria-based PenFed Foundation has provided more than $30 million since 2001 to help military community members secure their financial futures. Schenck volunteers unpaid as its CEO and serves on several business and civic boards. He was named National Credit Union Hero of the Year in 2017 and, in 2015, one of HillVets’ 100 most influential and impactful U.S. veterans.

Established in 1935, PenFed is America’s second-largest federal credit union, serving more than 1.6 million members worldwide with $23 billion in assets.

Amazon Prime Day 2 runs October 7–8, with early deals already underway. WIRED’s updated September 30 roundup features discounts on hand-tested gear, including a 2025 A16 iPad for $299, an Anker MagGo 10K power bank for $70, an M4 MacBook Air for $799, an Arlo Pro 5S camera for $100, and a 2024 Kindle Scribe for $300.
