Over roughly two decades, China has modernized the PLA to strengthen its hard power, defend regional and maritime interests, protect sea lanes, support initiatives such as the AIIB and OBOR, and counter growing U.S. military presence in the Indo-Pacific. Since the late 1990s, the PLA has become a modern fighting force, accompanying a more assertive China increasingly willing to use military power to advance national interests. Its future development and use remain uncertain.

North Korea’s roughly $1 billion in syndicated loans have been in default since the 1980s without restructuring. In 1997, French bank BNP repackaged the debt into transferable securities through NK Debt Corporation. The Peterson Institute estimated total principal and accumulated interest at about $3 billion in 2013.

Trading was largely frozen after sanctions were imposed in early 2013, and Exotix Capital has seen no trades for three to four years. Prices had risen to 14–18 cents per dollar after Kim Jong-il’s death in 2011, anticipating economic opening under Kim Jong-un, before those hopes faded.

New U.N. sanctions banning exports including coal, iron and seafood could reduce North Korea’s $3 billion annual export revenue by a third, further discouraging investors. Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund reported holding $15.5 million in NK Debt Corporation zero-coupon bonds due March 2020 without assigning them a value.

Debt restructuring expert Charles Blitzer said North Korea is like Cuba in spades, with interest arrears estimated at four to five times the outstanding principal, and predicted no significant activity in the debt for a long time.

Latin American stocks rebounded Monday as U.S.-North Korea tensions eased, though Scotiabank warned renewed missile testing could revive risks. Mexico’s IPC index gained 1.1%, while Brazil’s Bovespa touched its highest level since May, led by Cia Paranaense de Energia. Currency trading was subdued; the Mexican peso strengthened ahead of NAFTA talks, while the Brazilian real fluctuated amid expected fiscal deficit revisions.

The study presents a modular, open-source framework for AI-assisted synchrotron experiments at NSLS-II, integrating the Bluesky suite, secure instrument controls, Tiled data access, human adjudicators, and configurable AI agents. Agents perform data processing, analysis, dimensionality reduction, and Bayesian-optimization-based measurement selection while preserving human control and facility safety. The system was demonstrated through synchronous XRD and XAFS mapping of identical Al–Ni–Pt combinatorial libraries on the PDF and BMM beamlines, enabling inter-beamline communication, real-time processing, and autonomous or grid-based acquisition. XAFS analysis mapped elemental composition, while XRD revealed spatially varying FCC and FCT phases, although overlapping peaks, texture, and anisotropic broadening limited determination of exact phase compositions and amounts.

A digital twin based on a simulated Al–Li–Fe oxide library enabled benchmarking of AI-driven, geometric-grid, and random-sampling campaigns. After collecting 5% of available measurements, AI-driven mapping reached 98.9% model accuracy, compared with 95.9% for geometric grids and 96.6% for random sampling. AI-driven campaigns better resolved phase boundaries, interfaces, and localized minor phases. The authors conclude that decentralized, human-AI workflows and offline simulation can improve beamline efficiency and facility throughput while supporting safer, flexible, and collaborative autonomous experimentation.

Let’s Grow Kids spent a decade advancing Vermont’s child care system before sunsetting in October 2025. Founded by Rick Davis and led by Aly Richards, the organization raised over $70 million, helped pass the 2023 Act 76 establishing near-universal child care, and supported the opening of more than 100 programs with over 1,000 spaces, 230 early-childhood jobs, and subsidies for an additional 4,000 children. Its planned sunset, which created urgency, accountability, and opportunities for staff to transition into permanent organizations, was considered central to its success. Implementation is now being carried forward by groups focused on financing, workforce, data, and advocacy, although 80%–90% of participating families qualify for subsidies and gaps remain.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 *Nevermind* album cover, depicting a naked baby underwater, is not child pornography and dismissed Spencer Elden’s lawsuit. The judge said the image, comparable to a family photo of a nude child bathing, lacked evidence of lasciviousness and did not satisfy statutory factors.

Four people were arrested after Joshua Bowen allegedly shot 39-year-old Jennifer Bartell outside her Portsmouth home on March 14. Bowen, his girlfriend Albany Pierce, her mother Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson face accessory charges stemming from a Facebook argument with Bartell's daughter that escalated to the home. Neighbors say the shooting was not random.

Florida Museum researchers found that vitamin-producing bacterial symbionts in lice parasitizing humans and other primates have been maintained continuously for at least 20–25 million years. Genome comparisons revealed extensive shrinking and remodeling of bacterial genomes, while retaining genes essential for vitamin synthesis and the symbiotic relationship. This parallel evolution provides new clues about primate and human history and offers a model for studying long-term mutualisms between insects and bacteria.

Researchers used deep learning to identify Martian dust devils in more than 50,000 satellite images from ESA’s CaSSIS and Mars Express HRSC cameras. Stereo images of about 300 dust Devils showed that they and the surrounding near-surface winds can reach 44 m/s (160 km/h) across Mars, exceeding earlier surface estimates. Because dust devils trace otherwise invisible airflow, they serve as markers of wind behavior. The findings indicate that strong, straight-line winds likely loft substantially more dust than previously assumed, influencing Mars’ dust cycle, weather, and long-term climate. The study provides globally scaled data spanning about two decades, which can improve atmospheric and surface-process models, assess risks for future landed missions, and inform research on dunes and slope streaks.

This study examined whether resting-state functional connectivity of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) predicts the course of ADHD symptoms and response to stimulant treatment. It included 54 adults newly diagnosed with ADHD, assessed at baseline and after approximately three years using the Wender-Reimherr Interview (WRI) and resting-state fMRI. All participants initially received methylphenidate; 20 discontinued treatment after an average of six months because of nonresponse, while 34 continued stimulants at follow-up.

Average WRI scores decreased from 14.5 at baseline to 6.06 at follow-up. Symptom improvement was greater among participants who continued medication (mean change −10.6) than among those who discontinued it (−5.10). Baseline ADHD severity was associated with lower connectivity between the NAc and right paracingulate gyrus. Across all participants, lower NAc connectivity with the right anterior insular cortex predicted greater symptom improvement.

Medication status altered the relationship between insular connectivity and outcomes. Among treated participants, higher NAc connectivity with the right posterior insula predicted improvement; among participants no longer receiving medication, higher connectivity predicted worse outcomes. No significant group differences in mean or maximum head motion were found.

The findings indicate that NAc connectivity with default-mode and salience-network regions correlates with ADHD severity, longitudinal symptom change, and medication response. The authors note limitations including the small sample, potential limitations of resting-state fMRI for delineating brain nuclei, absence of direct behavioral outcomes, and the need for larger, longer, randomized, and task-based studies. They propose that reward-network connectivity may warrant investigation as a potential marker of stimulant response and clinical prognosis.

Utah auditors found incorrect markup data on seven liquor products caused a $186 loss and $1,161 in customer overcharges. The agency plans refunds and added automated pricing checks. Auditors also found a delayed $4.6 million revenue transfer, later corrected.

In 1793, an unusually hot, dry summer, low water levels, abundant mosquitoes, and Caribbean refugees brought by yellow fever contributed to a devastating Philadelphia epidemic that killed about 5,000 people, over 10% of the population. Physicians initially failed to determine the cause; more than a century later, mosquitoes were identified as vectors. Public health measures then emphasized drainage, sanitation, and avoiding standing water and mosquito exposure.

Yellow fever’s last reported North American outbreak occurred in New Orleans in 1905. Since December 2016, Brazil has faced its worst human outbreak in decades, with at least 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths, raising fears of further spread. An effective vaccine, recommended by the WHO for residents of endemic areas and travelers to Brazil, is 99% effective and generally requires one dose. Researchers at Penn are also developing DNA- and mRNA-based Zika vaccines.

Rachael Caplan, 29, of Thornhill, Ont., developed Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) seven years ago while in her first year of law school at Queen's University. Once athletic and working toward family-law practice in Kingston, she is now essentially bedridden, confined to the upper floor of her parents' home and unable to go downstairs or go outside since August 2016.

According to pain specialist Dr. David Shulman of Wilderman Medical Clinic, CRPS begins like an autoimmune disease but after about six months progresses into a neurological disease involving injured nerves, causing tingling, burning, shooting or lightning-like pain. Symptoms include intense constant pain starting in a hand or foot and spreading, swelling, sweating, temperature and colour changes, hair and nail changes, and brittle bones; it can follow trauma, injury, a stroke, infection or a cast. The disease affects just over 9,000 people per year in Canada, with more than half in Ontario, said Helen Small, executive director and co-founder of advocacy group PARC, founded in 2002.

Caplan's symptoms intensified after a month of acupuncture in 2012, and it took about 18 months to receive a diagnosis, given by Shulman in June 2013 on her 26th birthday. Small stressed early detection is crucial: within the first three months there is an 80 to 90 per cent treatment success rate, but after six months reversal is unlikely. Constant pain can cause insomnia, memory loss, agitation and depression; most patients become disabled and unable to work, and chronic pain shortens lifespan.

Caplan's friends and family have run a social media campaign, including a Facebook page documenting her journey and an ice-water challenge using the hashtag #AceThisFire, which has drawn over 20,000 views. Physiotherapy and opioids have failed or worsened her condition, and she has seen about 60 providers, including trips to the U.S. Green light therapy recently helped her sleep up to nine hours a night. She hopes greater awareness will speed diagnoses, expand treatment options and eventually lead to remission.

The article presents Gulf Island Fabrication (GIFI) as a highly discounted but risky stock. Its offshore markets face severe oversupply, weak prospects for new platforms, and operational problems that included delayed vessel deliveries and a $23.9 million loss. However, the company is described as effectively debt-free, and most of its backlog is in shipyards, including vessel construction, engineering projects, and the SeaOne Caribbean fuel project. Potential offshore-wind contracts provide additional upside, though financing and margins remain uncertain.

The investment thesis is based mainly on valuation, not an expected turnaround. After shares fell 40% in two months, GIFI’s market capitalization was about $120 million. Its Texas facilities, recorded at roughly $100 million, are for sale; a $55 million agreement for the South Yard implies that the remaining shipbuilding, services, and Louisiana fabrication assets are worth about $30 million. The author considers the shares attractive if the sales are completed and book values prove valid, while acknowledging bleak results, possible equity issuance, and significant short-term volatility.

The paper introduces QoCGM, an open-source MATLAB tool for comprehensive analysis of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data. Tested with MATLAB R2021b, QoCGM accepts CSV files containing timestamps and glucose values in mg/dL or mmol/L. It removes duplicate timestamps, identifies missing periods using sampling-frequency and tolerance settings, and either interpolates gaps using PCHIP or removes them. Configurable options include the night/day boundary, unit conversion, plotting, and missing-data handling. Results are exported as CSV for statistical analysis.

QoCGM derives metrics covering descriptive statistics, time in ranges, glycemic risk, variability, glycemic control, and entropy/complexity. Descriptive and time-in-range metrics are calculated for the full day and separately for daytime and nighttime, with day-to-day variation also assessed. Included measures include TIR, TBR, TAR, GRI, GRADE, CONGA, MAGE, Mobility, DTpM, fasting-glucose proxy, GMI, hypoglycemia events, and multiscale entropy. Summary variables are averaged across days for each participant.

In a demonstration using the first seven days of data from insulin-treated participants with type 2 diabetes, 324 of 331 trial participants had available CGM data. Median glucose was 162 mg/dL, median TIR was 65%, and median CV was 24%. Coefficient-of-determination analysis showed substantial overlap among many metrics but identified relatively distinct information from day-to-day variability in mean glucose and TIR, MCI, Mobility, and DTpM. Daytime and nighttime TIR also differed substantially, supporting their separate analysis. The authors conclude that QoCGM may facilitate research and clinical use of CGM metrics, while further research is needed to establish clinical implications.

Postwar negotiations will focus on Germany’s economic recuperation. Slow demobilization could fuel insurrection, while rapid demobilization could cause economic crisis unless raw materials, transport, markets, and credit are available. Competition to allocate these resources, especially seaborne supplies for the Baltic–Balkans–Persian Gulf region, will be a major instrument of negotiation.

Germany is likely to retain dominance in the Near East and control strategic approaches across three continents, but the blockade and the region’s dependence on outside supplies and lost foreign markets make a self-contained Middle European economy impossible. Two German imperialist schools agree on eastern dominance and the need for access to external resources but disagree on how to secure it.

The Kühlmann–Helfferich group favors accommodation with the West, expecting overseas supplies, reduced armaments, and little postwar resistance; German Socialists support this pragmatic approach. The Fatherland Party instead advocates military and naval power and retaining Belgium. Belgium is therefore a policy pivot: it offers commercial and strategic advantages, could prevent England from again landing forces in France, and might be administratively divided, with the Flemish coast drawn toward German influence.

Dunkin’ Donuts will launch fall flavors Aug. 28, including returning pumpkin-spice offerings and new maple, pecan and bacon products. The limited-time lineup features pumpkin cream cheese, maple-pecan coffees and lattes, and a maple-sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. New and limited-time products have boosted sales amid seven straight quarters of better-than-expected earnings.

Sarasota County sought review of a Department of Administration declaratory statement concerning a proposed crude oil splitter in Manatee County. The Department concluded that Chapter 380’s DRI provisions applied only to projects presumed to be developments of regional impact under Florida Administrative Code Rule 22F-2, which did not include the splitter.

The majority held that Sarasota County lacked standing for judicial review because Chapter 380 assigned initiation of the DRI process to developers, local governments, regional planning agencies, and the state planning agency—not neighboring counties—and an unfavorable declaratory statement alone did not establish adverse effect or jurisdiction. Because no authorized entity had invoked the DRI process, the petition for certiorari was denied. The court suggested that the County could pursue its concerns through its regional planning agency or legal proceedings under the Florida Environmental Protection Act.

Judge Boardman concurred in the result while noting these alternative avenues and stating that the County was not necessarily precluded from relief. Judge Scheb dissented, arguing that the declaratory statement was final agency action subject to review and that the Department improperly restricted the state planning agency’s authority to determine whether an unlisted project could constitute a DRI. He would have granted the petition and ordered reconsideration.

The coach gave one player a day off and said the team focuses on day-to-day performance. After strong first periods in Boston, second-period lapses need improvement. Roberto and two teammates are playing better than their points, with goaltending and defense helping; the team will focus on one game at a time.

ICICI Bank said its mortgage portfolio crossed Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private-sector mortgage lender and half its roughly Rs 3 trillion retail loan book. It targets Rs 2 trillion by FY20 through growth in smaller towns, digital approvals and a 50% expansion of 1,050 processing centres; multiple agencies are probing the Videocon loan.

The study developed a mechanistic model of COVID-19 vaccine immunity and boosting by fitting vaccine-effectiveness data from England for AZD1222, BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273 against Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2. It estimated unobserved immunity levels using biphasic exponential waning and logistic relationships between immunity and protection against symptomatic mild disease, hospitalisation and death.

The model estimated a rapid initial immunity half-life of 33 days, followed by a slower half-life of 580 days, and a 6.5-fold reduction in vaccine-induced immunity against Omicron relative to Delta. At 180 days after boosting, estimated protection against Omicron hospitalisation was 49.5% for AZD1222, 69.8% for mRNA-1273 and 63.7% for BNT162b2. After one year, protection against hospitalisation declined to 38.9%, 60.0% and 53.3%, respectively.

Neutralising antibody titres from the Moderna bivalent vaccine were 1.61-fold higher than those induced by the original vaccine. Applying this difference to the model predicted similar short-term protection after a fourth dose, but better sustained protection from the bivalent vaccine. One year after the fourth dose, protection against hospitalisation was estimated at 77.9% with the bivalent vaccine versus 60.0% with the original vaccine. Over one year, roughly half the additional protection was attributed to receiving a fourth dose and half to switching to the bivalent formulation.

The authors noted limitations: infection-induced and vaccine-induced immunity could not be separated; direct immunological measurements were unavailable; the model may not capture long-term immune dynamics; and hospitalisation data could not distinguish COVID-19-related admissions from other causes. Predictions may also vary across countries because of differing levels of prior infection and with the emergence of Omicron subvariants.

A survey of 2,000 British adults found the average respondent wakes three times nightly; one in ten wakes seven to 10 times. Reported causes include needing the bathroom (47%), snoring (41%), being edged out in bed (25%), aches (19%), nightmares (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), a partner talking or using a phone (10% each), anxiety (6%), and a partner watching TV or reading (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep hygiene and sleep cycles are key. Consistent bedtimes, limiting food and drink, and avoiding screens in bed can help, while noise, snoring and discomfort may disrupt sleep; earplugs and a comfortable mattress may aid sleep.

Financial system liquidity remained negative as increased primary-market issuance and a CBN foreign-exchange auction drained N28.6 billion through OMO sales. Open buy-back and overnight rates fluctuated sharply but ended the week at 55.8% and 59.3%, respectively. Benchmark treasury-bill yields rose 61 basis points to 18.5% because of tight liquidity and bearish sentiment.

The CBN continued forex interventions, including a US$100 million SMIS auction. The naira remained broadly stable, with NAFEX, NIFEX and parallel-market rates nearing convergence, leading analysts to expect short- to medium-term stability.

Domestic bond performance was bearish, with average yields ending at 16.8%, while corporate Eurobond performance was mixed. Investors were positioning ahead of the August 23, 2017 bond auction.

The Federal Executive Council approved dollar-backed treasury instruments and extended their tenor from 91 and 364 days to two and three years. The government said this would ease debt-repayment pressure, reduce naira borrowing and borrowing costs, and lengthen repayment tenors. It also adopted a 2018–2020 fiscal framework targeting growth of 3.5%, 4.5% and 7%, with oil production projected at 2.3 million barrels per day.

The CBN’s importers’ and exporters’ forex window had attracted US$4 billion from foreign investors by the reporting date, including a US$240 million transaction on August 1, 2017. The Bankers’ Committee said the economy was recovering, while exchange rates continued converging.

The article backtests Larry Connors’ R3 mean-reversion strategy from his 2009 book *High Probability ETF Trading* through December 2020 using dividend-adjusted data without commissions or slippage. Entry requires a close above the 200-day moving average, a three-day consecutive decline in the two-day RSI beginning below 60, and a two-day RSI below 10; positions exit when RSI exceeds 70. The aggressive version involving adding a second unit was not tested.

The results could not be replicated exactly because the test generated fewer fills than Connors’ results. SPY had a 90% win ratio over 79 trades since 1993. A portfolio of all 25 ETFs from 2000 through December 2020, limited to five open positions and 20% of equity per position, recorded 992 trades, a 75% win ratio, 0.68% average gain per trade, a 2.08 profit factor, 6.47% CAGR, and a 16% maximum drawdown in August 2011. A 50/50 SPY-QQQ portfolio had a 3.37 profit factor and 2.69% CAGR, with only 4.5% exposure to the market. The authors conclude that R3 remained effective but works best in equity markets and does not suit every market.
The Eighth Circuit denied Earl Ringo’s petitions for rehearing en banc and by the panel. Judge Bye would have granted en banc rehearing; Judge Benton did not participate.

After conservative Texas politicians targeted faculty for teaching about gender identity, officials at six Texas public university systems ordered reviews of curricula, syllabi and course descriptions. Texas A&M launched an audit after criticism of a children’s literature lesson; the University of North Texas required expedited reviews, while the University of Texas, University of Houston and Texas Woman’s University also began reviews tied to laws and executive orders. Although these policies assert that only two sexes exist, no current state or federal law prohibits professors from teaching about transgender identity. It remains unclear whether courses will be censored or removed.

Publicly accessible syllabi have made faculty easier to identify. More than 500 institutions use Simple Syllabus, and some Texas universities allow public viewing, partly under Texas House Bill 2504. Lecturer Andrew Joseph Pegoda was targeted after a conservative site found his courses through the platform. Privacy controls are available, but faculty face added risks as institutions encourage more detailed syllabi following the Texas A&M incident.

This medRxiv preprint examined the metabolic effects of BNT162b2 COVID-19 mRNA vaccination in humans and mice. In a longitudinal, nonrandomized, unblinded study, healthy, pre-diabetic, and diabetic adults were assessed before and two weeks after a booster. SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, anti-spike IgG, and neutralizing activity increased significantly in all groups, with no significant differences between groups. However, pre-diabetic and diabetic participants showed increased HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and TyG index, while fasting glucose and insulin levels did not change significantly. HOMA-IR was positively correlated with post-vaccination immune markers.

In mice, repeated BNT162b2 vaccination impaired glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, elevated serum triglycerides, and reduced insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation in insulin-sensitive tissues without significant changes in fasting glucose, insulin, or body weight. Metformin improved glucose-tolerance and insulin-tolerance results and restored insulin signaling without altering measured vaccine-induced immune responses.

The authors proposed that persistent spike protein, signaling through TLR4 and estrogen receptors, and vaccine-induced immune responses may contribute to impaired insulin signaling. They recommended ongoing surveillance, additional glucose monitoring, and further research in people with prediabetes or diabetes.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is an offbeat, educational website featuring scientists’ and paleontologists’ reports, scientific papers, magazine articles, and diverse paleoart depicting dinosaurs, early mammals, and other prehistoric life. It also publishes humorous, often sharply critical reviews of children’s books, toys, films, and TV shows, plus reports and photos from museum dinosaur exhibits worldwide. Active since 2009, it posts nearly weekly and provides a monthly dinosaur-news roundup.

Olivia Munn had no breast cancer symptoms and negative mammogram, ultrasound, and genetic mutation tests. A two-minute lifetime risk assessment estimated her breast cancer risk at 37%, prompting an MRI that led to her stage 1 diagnosis at 43. Her mother, Kim Munn, later took the assessment and was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer in July 2025. Munn said such assessments should be standard care.

Hugh Jackman revealed he is undergoing another basal cell carcinoma treatment after at least four previous treatments since 2013. He said frequent checkups and doctors have kept him well, while Logan and The Greatest Showman remain on schedule.

At his Progressive Conservative leadership campaign launch, Doug Ford energized a packed Toronto Congress Centre with Survivor’s “Eye of the Tiger,” prompting chants of “Doug, Doug, Doug.” He embraced defeated candidate Christine Elliott, while rivals Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen showed support, presenting a unified front. Kory Teneycke was set to manage the campaign and Jeff Silverstein to handle communications. Ford criticized Premier Kathleen Wynne and Liberal spending, promising prosperity for all Ontarians. Allies predicted victory but acknowledged a difficult race, while the rally was likened to “FordFest” and celebrated the legacy of his late brother Rob.

Stan Lee, 95, was hospitalized after experiencing shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat at home. His condition remained stable, and he was released, though he must return periodically for monitoring. Lee attended the “Black Panther” premiere in Hollywood, appearing in good spirits, and said he felt great on Feb. 1.

Valeant and Pershing Square entered a litigation-management agreement for a putative California class action. Pershing Square agreed to forgo claims related to Allergan litigation, and the parties exchanged mutual releases. Specified legal costs would be split equally; absent a California settlement stipulation, the agreement would end November 1, 2017.

Hockey players discuss the importance of preparation, routine, and team play in the Stanley Cup Final, rejecting added pressure despite the stakes. They reflect on their difficult series win, gratitude to those who supported them, and one captain’s painful knee injury, which forced him to watch from the bench. The players also recognize veterans’ achievements, value loyal Pittsburgh support, and consider their return to the Final after last year’s loss a meaningful accomplishment.

Storms crossing the Southeast spawned tornadoes that damaged homes, downed trees, disrupted power and closed roads in northern Alabama, where at least three tornadoes were confirmed but no injuries were reported. Jacksonville State University had major roof damage. Forecasters warned of violent long-track tornadoes, 3-inch hail and 70-mph winds for more than 29 million people; schools dismissed early and officials urged sheltering.

A prospective study compared 101 patients with cardiomyopathy—43 with dilated cardiomyopathy and 58 with other forms—with 101 healthy controls. Blood samples were analyzed for inflammatory markers (CRP, TNF-α and IL-6), NT-proBNP, malondialdehyde (MDA), and glutathione peroxidase (GPX) activity.

Cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher CRP and TNF-α levels than controls and higher MDA and GPX levels. Within the cardiomyopathy group, TNF-α correlated positively with GPX and MDA; NT-proBNP correlated positively with MDA and GPX. The authors also reported relationships between GPX activity and inflammatory measures, including TNF-α, IL-6, white blood cell, neutrophil, and monocyte counts. These findings support an interaction between inflammation and oxidative stress in cardiomyopathy and suggest that the processes are linked to disease severity.

Premier Li Keqiang said China would further open its economy by expanding access to services and manufacturing, lowering import tariffs, and allowing domestic and foreign firms to compete on equal terms. He pledged no forced technology transfers and stronger intellectual-property protection as global trade-war concerns grew, including proposed US tariffs on Chinese goods and at a Buenos Aires meeting of major economies.

At Huntington University Hospital (HUH), cardiac surgery teams had substantially higher blood-product use than comparable hospitals. From 2011 to 2013, about 71% of the 500 annual patients undergoing aortic valve replacement or coronary artery bypass grafting received transfusions, compared with 48.9% nationally. The passage cites a 2006 study associating transfusion after these procedures with reduced survival. Bleeding-related complications at HUH generated nearly $8 million in direct costs in 2013, with cardiac surgery accounting for nearly half.

Dr. Frank Young was selected to lead a blood conservation project with the goal of reducing perioperative blood-product use by two-thirds within one year, lowering transfusion rates to the national average, saving $2.5 million annually, and potentially saving 125 lives over ten years. Implementing the project was challenging because Young lacked authority over many team members, cardiac teams operated across separate organizational and reporting structures, and surgeons were not required to approve transfusions before they occurred. Surgeons’ revenue-based compensation and resistance to disrupting established routines also complicated efforts.

A cardiac medicine committee found that 51% of center patients had bleeding-related complications and that 65% received transfusions in 2013. Young proposed blood-conservation techniques including autologous blood harvest and retrograde autologous priming, which could reduce dilution and preserve patients’ own clotting elements.

Supporters included anesthesiologist Anil Gupta, hospital administrators, nurses, perfusion staff, cardiologists, and some surgeons; approximately 40% of transfusions occurred in the intensive care unit. Veteran surgeons were skeptical because they saw no need to change procedures practiced for 20 years. Young ultimately had to determine how to explain the need for change, involve the appropriate staff, and ensure that new practices persisted.

A corrected DGAP voting-rights announcement for Amadeus FiRe AG disclosed a threshold event on 9 February 2017 involving BNP Paribas Investment Partners S.A. The resulting holding was 259,295 voting rights, or 4.99% (ISIN DE0005093108), down from a previously reported 5.003%, with no voting rights attributed to instruments. BNP Paribas Investment Partners Belgium S.A. was identified as the direct shareholder, and the notification listed a chain of controlled BNP Paribas entities.
Ajman reduced the tourism fee for hotels and tourism companies from 10% to 7%, effective immediately through December 31, to boost tourism and improve the emirate’s investment environment.

Meb Faber’s Three-Way Model allocates capital equally among stocks, bonds, and gold when each asset’s monthly three-month moving average exceeds its ten-month moving average, and exits when the condition no longer holds. Faber’s 1971–2015 test returned 13% annually. The momentum hypothesis cited in the passage holds that assets with strong trailing three- to 12-month returns may continue outperforming over the following three to 12 months.

Using GLD, SPY, and TLT from 2006, the updated backtest grew $100,000 to $422,000, producing an 8.9% CAGR, a 57% win rate, a 1.6 profit factor, and an 18% maximum drawdown. Performance after 2015 was weaker at 5.3% annually, though the strategy’s principal strength was its low drawdown. With 1.5× leverage, annual returns were 13.1% and maximum drawdown was 26%, although the article does not recommend leverage.

Nearby moving-average settings produced similar results, suggesting the strategy was not curve-fitted. The passage presents it as a simple, defensive momentum strategy intended for evaluation over long periods.

This statistical analysis plan addresses a multicenter pediatric trial comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg with placebo, with GlucaGen included as a reference. The primary comparison requires 20, 10, and 10 patients in the dasiglucagon, placebo, and GlucaGen groups, respectively, to provide 90% power under a two-sided 5% significance level with 45-minute follow-up.

The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as a first increase of at least 20 mg/dL without rescue IV glucose within 45 minutes. The primary analysis uses the full analysis set and a stratified log-rank test by age group and injection site, with Kaplan–Meier summaries and censoring at rescue treatment or 45 minutes. Sensitivity and supportive analyses include alternative censoring, interpolated recovery times, Wilcoxon testing, and conditional proportional hazards modeling. Secondary endpoints assess recovery and glucose changes at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes using stratified Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel tests and ANOVA. A hierarchical testing procedure controls multiplicity for dasiglucagon versus placebo.

Safety analyses use the safety set and cover treatment exposure, hypoglycemia induction, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, clinical laboratories, vital signs, ECGs, and descriptive immunogenicity analyses. Baseline characteristics, medical history, concomitant medications, and diabetes treatments will also be summarized. Pharmacokinetic analyses use noncompartmental methods in Phoenix WinNonlin, while pharmacodynamic assessment includes baseline-adjusted glucose area under the effect curve from 0–30 minutes. Analyses will use SAS, with missing efficacy data analyzed without imputation. Outputs will follow ICH conventions and undergo documented programming quality-control validation.

Soccer passing-direction terminology describes the path a ball is expected to take from a passer to a teammate. Directions are generally based on the player’s orientation and include forward, angled right, right, back and right, back, back and left, left, and angled left, whether passes are grounded or aerial. Forward terms include ahead, deep, downfield, down the line, long, parallel, short, straight, and upfield. Right- and left-side terms describe angled, diagonal, square, lateral, flat, centering, and wide passes, as well as passes toward the corner, post, or sideline. Back-pass terminology includes straight back, behind, reverse passes, and diagonals toward either rear side. Other terms cover the angle of a pass, backheel, center, near and far post, field axes, interface, outlet, passing angle, possession, reverse field, straight lines, and switching fields.

On January 31, 2017, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016. The filing included a press release and related data sheet as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. It stated that the information was not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference, except when expressly referenced in a filing.

Samsung unveiled the Galaxy J5 Prime in India at Rs 14,900, with a 5-inch HD display, 13MP rear and 5MP front cameras, 3GB RAM, 32GB expandable storage, dual-SIM 4G and a 2400mAh battery. Android 7.0 Nougat OTA began in the UAE; an official India rollout may take time. The update adds multitasking, notification, security, emoji, battery and performance improvements.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday, with the Dow dropping more than 650 points (2.5%) below 26,000; the S&P 500 fell 2.2% and the Nasdaq 2%, capping the Dow’s worst week in two years. Investors sold off after a stronger-than-expected January jobs report increased fears that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates more than expected. Wage growth accelerated to 2.9%, suggesting tighter monetary policy. The report showed 200,000 jobs added, above the 190,000 expected. Trump’s tax cuts and regulatory rollbacks had fueled a “Trump rally,” while Trump cited market gains and the jobs report on Twitter but did not address Friday’s downturn. Analysts attributed the decline to economic fundamentals, including earnings, interest rates, liquidity and valuation.

Peloton launched five AI-enabled fitness products, including refreshed bikes and treadmills and a new rowing machine, in a push to revive its post-pandemic business. Peloton IQ provides real-time form feedback, rep counting, and training suggestions. Prices rose, with the Tread+ reaching $6,695 and monthly membership increasing to $49.99. The launch followed layoffs, leadership changes, a $19 million treadmill-recall fine, and a 90% share decline since January 2021. Peloton stock closed down 3.67% Wednesday.

RaySearch and Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG, a leading European brachytherapy supplier, have signed a partnership agreement to integrate the RayStation® treatment planning system and RayCare oncology information system with Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG brachytherapy systems, enabling a complete brachytherapy solution covering treatment devices, planning, and information management. The partnership aligns with RaySearch's aim of supporting as many treatment systems and approaches as possible. Brachytherapy involves placing a small temporary or permanent radioactive implant in the patient's tissue, allowing a higher radiation dose to a smaller area and minimizing damage to surrounding tissue; it is most commonly used for prostate cancer but also for cancers of the brain, eye, lung, and skin. Dr. Harald Hasselmann, CEO of Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG, called the partnership a pathway to better integration of brachytherapy into modern radiation therapy workflows and an important step forward for future optimization. Johan Löf, CEO of RaySearch, is quoted.

During Prime Day, the 48-inch LG C4 OLED is priced at $800 on Amazon—the lowest WIRED has seen. It delivers natural colors, detailed shadows, minimal light bleed, good off-angle performance, and punchy HDR brightness, though it is dimmer than newer flagships such as the LG G4. It supports VRR up to 144Hz across all four HDMI inputs, runs LG’s webOS interface, includes a voice- and cursor-enabled magic remote, and has a slim center-mount pedestal. The 65-inch model is also reduced to $1,300.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture builds on Turing with major improvements to rendering, ray tracing, AI, memory, storage, and efficiency. ROPs moved from the memory controller and L2 cache into the GPC; the full GA102 has 112 ROPs, improving multisample anti-aliasing, fill rate, and blending. Each GA10x SM has four partitions with 64 KB register files and a shared 128 KB L1/shared-memory subsystem. Both datapaths support FP32, doubling Turing’s peak FP32 rate to 128 operations per clock while retaining concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution. Its four third-generation Tensor Cores are individually twice as powerful as Turing Tensor Cores, and its unified L1/shared-memory capacity is 33% larger, with twice the shared-memory bandwidth.

Second-generation RT Cores retain dedicated BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection hardware while doubling intersection throughput over Turing. New acceleration for moving and deforming geometry supports ray-traced motion blur, reportedly up to eight times faster than Turing, with up to five times faster motion-blur rendering measured on an RTX 3080 versus RTX 2080 Super. GA10x also supports concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, two simultaneous compute workloads, and workload prioritization.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, TF32, and BF16, but not FP64 acceleration. Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity skips zero-valued matrix elements, doubling sparse-operation throughput while retaining Turing-level dense throughput. The RTX 3080 is stated to deliver 2.7 times the peak FP16 Tensor throughput of the RTX 2080 Super with sparsity enabled. Enhanced DLSS uses a new 9x scaling factor to make 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible on the RTX 3090.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling and a Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding scheme. It supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, over 52% more than the TU102, while pseudo-independent channels assist BVH traversal. NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based lossless decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets directly from SSDs to the GPU, offloading substantial CPU work and improving loading, streaming, frame rates, and I/O performance.

The data-center A40 combines GA10x graphics and compute features with 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through two NVLink-connected GPUs. Compared with Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to five times the AI-training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity, and twice the PCIe bandwidth. It supports vGPU, Quadro Sync, and the EGX platform.

The RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X memory and is reported as 1.5 times faster than TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X while exceeding the preceding RTX 2080 Ti’s performance. The professional RTX A6000 provides 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB with two cards, plus hardware-accelerated ray tracing, motion blur, and AI denoising.

Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a for 8K at 60 Hz and HDMI 2.1 with 48 Gbps bandwidth for 8K60 and 4K120 output. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for major codecs and AV1, while seventh-generation NVENC provides low-CPU, high-quality H.264 and HEVC encoding up to 8K. GDDR6X interfaces also include Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed memory transmissions and retries them to improve overclocking reliability. At equivalent performance, Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power efficient than Turing GPUs.

Phlogopite was studied under electronic excitation using XTANT-3, a hybrid model combining transport Monte Carlo, Boltzmann collision integrals, and tight-binding molecular dynamics. The simulations capture nonequilibrium electronic and atomic dynamics, including electron–phonon coupling, nonthermal bond changes, phase transitions, and lattice disorder. A 396-atom cell was irradiated with 92 eV photons in 10 fs pulses at varying doses.

The calculated phlogopite band gap was 7.5 eV in the ideal crystal and about 6.5 eV at room temperature. At approximately 0.17 eV/atom, hydrogen bonds began breaking, causing hydrogen migration while the remaining lattice stayed stable. Electron–phonon coupling cooled the electronic system and delayed Mg and Si displacements compared with a Born–Oppenheimer simulation. At roughly 0.4 eV/atom, Mg became liquid-like, producing a two-superionic-subsystem state with Al, K, O, and Si still solid. Above approximately 0.5 eV/atom, the full atomic lattice disordered, with H and Mg moving fastest and Al and K slowest. Near 0.9 eV/atom, the bandgap collapsed, producing a metallic state. At around 2 eV/atom, nonthermal heating rapidly accelerated oxygen most strongly, followed by potassium and other elements, leading to complete disorder within hundreds of femtoseconds.

The predicted hydrogen-migration threshold of 0.17 eV/atom closely matched the experimental beta- and gamma-irradiation value of about 0.2 eV/atom (1000 kGy). Heavy-ion etching observations also qualitatively supported the prediction that hydrogen-containing regions damage before silicon-containing regions. Threshold photon fluences were additionally estimated for future irradiation experiments.

The lecture examines how utility derived from beliefs affects information seeking, self-deception, and decision-making. Anticipatory utility motivates people to expect positive future events, while ego utility encourages inflated beliefs about one’s abilities and traits. In a model where beliefs cannot affect future outcomes, believing oneself healthy may be preferable to realism because it increases current happiness. When beliefs guide treatment, retirement, travel, family, or other consequential decisions, however, realistic information may be preferable because overoptimism can distort behavior and choices. Optimal expectations balance immediate benefits against distorted decisions and potential future disappointment. Under a utility function \(f(p)\), concavity produces information aversion, while convexity produces information seeking.

Evidence shows systematic overoptimism about future events and personal traits. Weinstein’s studies found students predict more favorable outcomes for themselves than for the average student and consider themselves less likely to experience drinking problems, divorce, heart attacks, and similar negative events. Couples underestimate the likelihood that marriages end, small-business owners overestimate success, and smokers acknowledge general risks but deny personal vulnerability. Most drivers and many professors rate themselves above average. In an MIT survey, 31% of students described themselves as academically above average, while female students tended to be below average. Underconfidence may motivate effort and reduce disappointment, whereas frequent feedback can correct inflated or deflated beliefs.

Positive illusions may promote happiness, creativity, productivity, and mental health; “depressive realism” may be detrimental when it accurately emphasizes the world’s difficulties. Biases are generally greater for personally important prospects and traits, while clear objective feedback reduces them. Ambiguous feedback, perceived control, and a tendency to attribute luck to skill can strengthen overconfidence. Experts who receive reliable feedback, such as meteorologists, tend to be better calibrated.

Laboratory evidence shows motivated belief updating. In Eil and Rao’s study, participants updated approximately like Bayesians after favorable comparisons about IQ or attractiveness but discounted unfavorable information and paid more for information they expected to be favorable. Zimmermann’s research found no immediate asymmetric updating but greater recall of positive information a month later. Real-world evidence links overconfidence to excessive trading, lower returns, managerial hubris, and value-destroying mergers.

Bayesian learning is cognitively difficult. People usually identify whether evidence should raise or lower a probability, but often misjudge how much to update, especially across multiple signals, and consequently use heuristics. Documented deviations include the gambler’s fallacy, hot-hand fallacy, and base-rate neglect. The first two can reflect a mistaken belief that small samples should reflect underlying probabilities, producing either expectations of reversal or excessive inference of streaks. These errors affect decisions by judges, loan officers, and others. Base-rate neglect also distorts medical-test interpretations, especially when disease prevalence is low.

Heuristics include representativeness, illustrated by the Linda problem’s violation of the conjunction law, and availability, illustrated by overestimating homicide relative to suicide. Two-dimensional learning additionally requires evaluating both information and its source; research on fake news suggests inattentiveness may matter more than partisanship.

Policy responses depend on why people are misinformed. Salient information can help those who overlook facts or hold incorrect theories, whereas motivated beliefs may make people ignore corrective information or even worse off. Cognitive biases are more straightforward to address through correct information. When beliefs cannot alter serious outcomes and self-deception increases welfare, respecting a person’s preference for optimism may be appropriate.

The lecture examines sustainability-related real-estate decisions through two case studies: Boston’s Winthrop Center and New York’s 425 Park Avenue. It emphasizes stakeholder returns, development risk, information gaps, and the role of regulation in scaling innovation.

Winthrop Center, constructed from 2016 to 2018, faced weak market recognition of its Passive House features. A 2019 comparable transaction suggested no green premium, while State Street chose a competing building because of Winthrop’s less usable floor plate, luxury-condominium orientation, and rent premium. COVID-19 also disrupted an HSBC loan just before closing, halting construction for nearly three months. A Kuwait-based sovereign wealth fund later provided a $700 million loan. Cornell Tech’s equity involvement had helped reduce developer risk, while lessons from Cornell Tech and Winthrop showed that first-time projects can face construction premiums of 1–8 percent because of limited experience and information asymmetry. Winthrop’s premium was about 1 percent because of experienced development and consulting teams.

Tenants and the public were identified as likely beneficiaries rather than the developer in Winthrop’s first development cycle. Massachusetts building-code requirements, MEPA review, and city initiatives subsequently spread Passive House practices, including triple-glazed windows. Other Boston-area projects moved from LEED Platinum to Passive House, illustrating how sustainability advances from pilots among lower-risk corporate, municipal, university, school, and hospital clients to wider adoption. Massachusetts’s forthcoming stretch code was presented as a potential pathway toward net-zero buildings. The condominium portion used LEED Gold, while the cost of envelope improvements was identified as the largest construction-premium component.

425 Park Avenue was a roughly $1 billion, 670,000-square-foot office project with 18,000 square feet of retail. The developer faced a ground lease, a cash-negative property, an insolvent financial partner, financing uncertainty, and zoning changes requiring retention of 25 percent of an existing structure. That structural requirement was difficult and costly, contributing to an 8 percent cost premium, delayed the project by more than a year, and ultimately cost about $100 million. The project nevertheless had a strong Park Avenue location, while competitors included the 3 million-square-foot One World Trade Center and the 10 million-square-foot Hudson Yard.

The 425 Park Avenue concept was based on 2012 demand for healthier offices amid concerns about sick-building syndrome. Considered features included enhanced ventilation and MERV 15 filtration, WELL certification, Fitwell or CDC certification, and conventional LEED measures. Ventilation and filtration were projected to add $12.3 million in initial cost and $3.9 million annually, while adding certification and related costs could raise the total premium to roughly 2–6 percent. These costs were weighed against an assumed rent premium and potential savings from lower health-insurance costs, improved productivity, and reduced turnover and absenteeism, although much of the benefit analysis relied on assumptions.

The lecture applied the diffusion-of-innovation model, noting that early adopters bear first-mover risk and generate evidence needed to persuade the early majority, while regulation ultimately moves the market toward a new norm. The proposed strategy was to target large, whole-floor financial tenants, including hedge funds such as Citadel, whose investors might value wellness, prestige, and sustainability. Engagement would need to reach human-resources, payroll, finance, and investment stakeholders as well as facilities and leasing personnel.

Citadel ultimately signed a landmark lease and expanded its commitment, although about half the building remained unleased. The project entered financial distress in 2020 because of the structural-retention problems, which the speakers distinguished from the healthy-building decision. By 2021, higher-quality and ultra-healthy offices were gaining demand while lower-quality space was losing demand, supporting the lecture’s final question about whether an ambitious first-mover strategy can work in a broader market.

Topological insulators may enable more efficient, stable lasers by protecting light from defect-induced scattering. Conventional lasers are sensitive to dust, mirror misalignment, and other imperfections; increasing power can also introduce unwanted colors, destabilize output, and distort the beam profile.

In some insulating materials, surface electrons can conduct while protected from most scattering. Reversing an electron’s direction requires a spin flip, which is difficult because it demands a significant energy change. Replacing these electronic states with photons in a lattice of coupled optical waveguides creates a similar protected edge state. Carefully arranging the waveguides’ excitation and phase shifts confines amplified light to the edge and prevents nonprotected light from remaining in the crystal.

Researchers fabricated and compared lasers with protected and unprotected edge states. The protected laser continued operating when individual waveguides were removed, was more efficient, and developed no new colors as its power increased, unlike the unprotected laser. Accurate modeling and extremely precise fabrication were essential to preserving the energy gap between protected and unprotected states. Such lasers could support applications requiring a specific color and sharply defined wavelength, including 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

Authorities are coordinating a large security operation for Super Bowl LII between the Philadelphia Eagles and New England Patriots at US Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. The Minneapolis Police Department leads, supported by federal, state and local agencies and more than 400 Minnesota National Guard members. Preparations include threat assessments, credential checks for more than 30,000 workers, indoor prescreening away from the stadium, bag and item inspections, tactical officers, bomb-sniffing dogs, helicopters and fencing. The FBI leads counterterrorism efforts and is drawing lessons from attacks at mass events, while local authorities are considering past incidents involving malls, a mosque and Somalia’s Al-Shabaab. Homeland Security Investigations will monitor counterfeit goods. Extreme cold, expected around 3°F at game time, and surrounding businesses, residences, transit and pregame events complicate operations. Officials aim to make the event safe, smooth and enjoyable.

The speaker calls for a complete reorganization of Alaska’s government and notes its revenue, resource production, and potential as a land of homes. He supports Seattle’s Alaska Yukon Pacific Exposition, intended to develop Alaska and expand American Pacific commerce, benefiting the Pacific states and the nation through fair trade. He argues that national action should consider ethical principles as well as self-interest and that immigrants should be judged solely by their conduct, without discrimination based on religion or nationality. Specifically condemning anti-Japanese hostility, he praises Japan’s rapid military, industrial, artistic, and scientific development and recommends equal treatment for Japanese immigrants. He criticizes excluding Japanese students from public schools and emphasizes that Americans should treat Japanese people with the same courtesy they receive in Japan.

Researchers recorded medical problems among participants receiving at least one dose of a study vaccine and compared them across vaccine and placebo groups. In Phase 1, a few participants had temporary lymphocyte reductions 1–3 days after the first BNT162b1 or BNT162b2 dose; counts returned to normal by 6–8 days, with no low counts after Dose 2. Injection-site reactions and systemic events generally resolved quickly and were mild or moderate. Injection-site pain was most common, while tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events.

All tested 10-, 20-, and 30-µg doses of BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 were well tolerated, except the 100-µg BNT162b1 dose, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of injection-site reactions or systemic events. The 30-µg BNT162b2 dose was selected for Phase 2/3. No Phase 1 participant left because of medical problems, and most problems were mild or moderate.

In Phase 2/3, 30-µg BNT162b2 was well tolerated, with safety results similar to earlier phases. Few participants left the blinded phase because of medical problems: 32 of 21,926 in the BNT162b2 group and 36 of 21,921 in the placebo group. Most medical problems were mild or moderate, and most among BNT162b2 recipients involved injection-site reactions or systemic events. No single medical problem occurred in more than 1% of participants aged 12–15. Results for the first 360 Phase 2 participants were similar to those for all Phase 2/3 participants.

Serious medical problems were uncommon. In Phase 1, two occurred among BNT162b2 recipients, and researchers did not consider them vaccine-related. In Phase 2/3, no serious problems in participants aged 12–15 were considered vaccine-related. Among older participants initially receiving BNT162b2, three had one serious, temporary problem each that researchers considered possibly vaccine-related, including arm or leg numbness or tingling. Among those initially receiving placebo and later BNT162b2, three had one serious, temporary problem each that researchers considered possibly vaccine-related, including portal-vein blood-clot blockage and a mini-stroke. Serious problems after BNT162b2SA or booster doses were few; no single problem affected more than one participant, and researchers generally did not consider them vaccine-related. One serious problem occurred after a lower 5- or 10-µg booster, and one after an additional 30-µg booster; both were judged unrelated to vaccination.

No participant died in Phase 1 or among Phase 3 participants receiving BNT162b2SA. During Phase 2/3, deaths occurred in 85 of 23,141 initial BNT162b2 recipients, 62 of 21,371 placebo recipients who later received BNT162b2, and 23 of 23,141 placebo recipients who did not subsequently receive it. Causes varied, and researchers did not believe BNT162b2 caused the deaths.

Neutral-particle diagnostics can indirectly measure tokamak core-ion distributions, which cannot be obtained directly because ions are fully ionized and well confined. The approach creates neutral atoms through charge exchange, allowing them to escape and carry information about the core ions. Possible production mechanisms include charge exchange with edge neutrals and active neutral-beam injection. Radiative recombination is negligible because neutrals are rapidly reionized.

Escaping neutrals can be reionized by electron-impact ionization, ion-impact ionization, or further charge exchange, with charge exchange generally dominant. Transport is treated similarly to radiation transport, with survival probability expressed as an exponential involving integrated plasma density and collision coefficients. For example, 10-keV neutrals in a plasma at \(10^{20}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\) have a mean free path of about 10 cm, implying that neutral diagnostics require relatively low-density confinement devices and a line-integrated density below roughly \(10^{19}\,\mathrm{m^{-2}}\).

A passive diagnostic uses charge exchange with edge neutrals and measures escaping core neutrals with a stripping cell and velocity-selecting magnetic analyzer. It can reveal non-Maxwellian fast-ion tails, although its signal is line-integrated and difficult to interpret because cold edge neutrals also contribute. Neutral-beam injection can localize the measurement to the core. Charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy uses beam charge exchange with fully stripped impurities, whose emissions reveal impurity density, flow velocity, and temperature; beam modulation helps distinguish the weak signal from bremsstrahlung and other backgrounds. Beam-emission spectroscopy measures localized electron-density fluctuations through beam excitation and emitted spectral lines, with detailed analysis requiring models of nonequilibrium atomic processes and beam attenuation.

The motional Stark effect uses fast, unidirectional neutral-beam atoms: in their frame, the magnetic field produces an effective electric field proportional to \(V\times B\), causing larger spectral splitting than the Zeeman effect. Measuring this splitting determines the magnetic-field magnitude, while polarization measurements can determine field orientation, infer the poloidal field, and support reconstruction of the tokamak current distribution.

Current radiotheranostic therapies enable simultaneous diagnostic imaging and treatment but often use standardized doses and intervals, overlooking interpatient differences in pharmacokinetics, tumor burden, and radiosensitivity. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models within computational nuclear oncology and theranostic digital twins can integrate patient physiology, radiopharmaceutical properties, imaging, biofluid data, and radiobiology to predict biodistribution, tissue doses, tumor control, and normal-tissue complications.

PBPK models for radiopharmaceutical therapy combine computational, anatomical-physiological, radiopharmaceutical, and treatment-protocol components. They may be developed bottom-up from preclinical data, top-down from patient data, or middle-out by combining mechanistic knowledge with patient-specific calibration; the middle-out approach is particularly suited to sparse clinical datasets.

Rigorous verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (VVUQ) are essential for clinical translation. Verification checks model structure, implementation, mass balance, units, and expected behavior. Internal validation assesses goodness of fit, predictive performance, model selection using AIC/AICc, BIC, or F-tests, and local or global sensitivity analysis. External validation uses independent data, splitting, or resampling, while uncertainty quantification propagates parameter uncertainty through sampling and evaluates output confidence and accuracy using metrics such as relative deviation, RMSE, and MAPE.

Dynamic theranostic digital twins add bidirectional clinical-data exchange, repeated imaging and laboratory updates, spatial dosimetry, and adaptive treatment decisions. Their VVUQ must therefore be iterative and responsive to evolving disease, imaging variability, and sparse or noisy data. Fit-for-purpose regulatory standards and engagement with nuclear-medicine organizations are needed to advance PBPK models from research into clinical practice.

The case examines Toyota Motor Manufacturing Georgia’s difficulties with ChassisCo’s Athens, Georgia plant after the 2003 launch of the second-generation Suprima crossover. ChassisCo’s 120,000-square-foot plant, with more than 350 workers, welded approximately 200,000 rear suspension cradles annually and shipped them 27 times per day.

Toyota’s relationship with ChassisCo followed its supplier-development model. After outsourcing cradle production in 1993, Toyota supported the 1997 Suprima launch with engineering expertise, Japanese mentoring, and tightly controlled component specifications. ChassisCo subsequently launched the more automated 1999 Responsa successfully in St. Louis. This performance led Toyota to give ChassisCo greater responsibility for the 2003 Suprima, including project management, sourcing 85 component parts, incoming logistics, and inventory management.

The new cradle was more complex than the 1997 version. ChassisCo increased automation from 13 to 102 robots, doubled welding content, added riveting, compressed production into half its former factory space, and reduced cycle times. ChassisCo also expanded its quality staff, warehousing, and capacity to serve another Toyota plant. Despite these efforts, production and quality problems persisted.

The case identifies several capability and management gaps. ChassisCo lacked a parts-tracking system, stage-gate project-management process, effective quality-certification and inventory-management capabilities, and integrated support for its expanded responsibilities. Strong organizational silos prevented effective responses to Toyota’s requirements. Earlier experience from the Responsa launch was also weakened by ChassisCo’s 2000 decentralization, while simultaneous launches for other customers stretched engineering, tooling, materials, maintenance, and supplier-management personnel too thinly. The program lacked adequate tool-and-die staff, a supplier-management group, an executive escalation process, and clear separation of pre-launch and operating expenses.

Aggressive Toyota target prices compounded the problems. ChassisCo accepted low supplier bids, underestimated logistics costs, packed the new line into insufficient space, and failed to tell Toyota that the target price was unrealistic. Some suppliers lacked experience producing structural automotive parts. ChassisCo also lacked personnel skilled in auditing second-tier suppliers, while Toyota did not identify supplier problems until late. Toyota engineers tuned only a few critical parts, but most ChassisCo and North American supplier personnel were unfamiliar with this process, which relied heavily on tacit knowledge. Increased automation further complicated matters because robotic welding lacked the real-time visual feedback available to manual welders, making small part variations or misaligned equipment more likely to produce defective welds requiring inspection and rework.

Although the Suprima launched on time in September 2003, Athens had failed Toyota’s required one-hour high-volume production trial three times and was operating at roughly 60% of its target rate. Output reached only two-thirds of target after two months, while suppliers missed production requirements, causing overtime and cost overruns. The plant lacked standardized work, a defect-feedback system, and a second-tier supplier inspection system. Scrap, downtime, poor part quality, and extensive incoming inspection characterized the first production year.

Quality problems continued through 2004. A March audit found nonconforming assembly-critical welds, and a November arc-welding audit scored only 13 percent. External defects rose from 565 per week in July 2003 to 2,845 per week in July 2004. Left-cradle automated welding produced many final defects, while the right-cradle line introduced new riveting challenges. TMMGA personnel worked extensively at the plant, and Athens averaged about four hours of overtime per day plus Saturday shifts.

Toyota’s support followed its normal procedure for a struggling supplier: Walt Bernstein visited at least twice weekly, helped prioritize problems, and created improvement checklists. Nevertheless, progress remained inadequate because defects and downtime constrained output. The plant’s weak quality-information system and lack of a defect-flowout control process prevented TMMGA from reliably determining how many defective cradles had reached assembly. By late 2004, ChassisCo was losing money, requesting a price increase to cover added labor and inventory costs, and unable to solve the problems with its available resources. Bernstein emphasized that the issue was primarily quality rather than cost and warned that the vehicle program could be at risk.

The passage frames the crisis within the Toyota Production System, whose jidoka and Just-in-Time principles require built-in quality, problem detection, continuous flow, waste reduction, and coordination across the supply chain. Toyota develops suppliers as long-term partners through education, frequent communication, early escalation of problems, and respect for people. The case concludes with questions asking participants to identify the respective responsibilities of ChassisCo and Toyota, evaluate each party’s options, and recommend actions for resolving the crisis.

McGill University researchers developed DOLPHIN, an AI tool that analyzes exon and junction data to identify previously hidden disease markers in individual cells beyond conventional gene-level methods. In pancreatic cancer data, it found more than 800 markers missed by standard tools and distinguished aggressive, high-risk cancers from less severe cases. The researchers say the technology could support earlier diagnosis, better therapy selection, and virtual cell models that simulate disease progression and drug responses before laboratory or clinical trials.

Investing.com’s weekly chart review says the S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July, putting it up 7.8% year to date, before slipping 1.6% on August 1. Longer-term trends remain healthy, but short-term indicators are tenuous, with breadth rolling over from overbought levels, bearish divergence, and possible further downside. July was risk-on, with stocks up and bonds down; volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, investors are overweighting tech, and U.S. electricity demand reached a record. The site also promotes a stock screener and warns that trading risks are substantial and market data may not be real-time or accurate.

Both finalists are strong, similar hockey teams, while the opponent’s speed is concentrated mainly on one or two lines. He stresses rebounding consistently, keeping the puck deep, and playing simple, smart, patient team hockey. He praises Nieuwendyk’s shooting, the opponent’s multiple scoring threats and effective checking lines, and head coach Larry’s communication.
