A coach praised his players’ resilience, focus, trust, and collective play, crediting their ability to handle pressure, ignore outside noise, and support one another. He emphasized leadership, remaining grounded, and focusing only on the next game while respecting San Jose’s strength. He also highlighted Phil’s consistent two-way play and contributions.

Alibaba Group Holding (BABA) is downgraded from “Buy” to “Hold” as its shares approach fair value following a significant rally. AI and cloud computing are driving strong growth in revenue and profitability, while core China e-commerce and international operations continue posting solid revenue gains. Heavy reinvestment pressures overall profitability, making the stock’s discount to U.S. peers insufficient to justify a more bullish stance.

The paper examines how large language models (LLMs) can strategically influence human decisions through persuasion. It frames persuasion using Bayesian persuasion: an informed Sender commits to a signaling scheme, a Receiver observes a signal and updates beliefs, and the Receiver then chooses a utility-maximizing action. Persuasion is modeled as shifting the Receiver’s beliefs to locations where the Sender’s payoff is higher, often favoring partial rather than complete disclosure.

Motivated by heterogeneous effects in human persuasion and limitations in existing LLM evaluations, the paper proposes a scalable, theory-driven framework for measuring and training LLM persuasion. Repurposed human-persuasion datasets are converted into environments in which both Sender and Receiver are LLMs. A 45-participant human study supports the plausibility of these environments. Experiments show that stronger frontier models, including DeepSeek-R1, achieve greater persuasion gains and exhibit more sophisticated strategies such as adaptive information revelation.

The framework measures persuasive benefit through gains in Sender utility and assesses strategic disclosure using conditional mutual information between messages, underlying states, and interaction history. It also develops an opinion-change benchmark in which a Sender seeks to move a Receiver toward endorsing a target claim while the Receiver selects actions according to expected loss.

Finally, reinforcement learning is used to train Sender LLMs against Receiver LLMs. Even a small model, Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, can be trained to match large models in strategic persuasion, achieve significantly higher persuasion gains, and transfer its learned strategies across different Receiver architectures.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed an April 23, 2015 Form 8-K announcing its first-quarter 2015 financial results, with the press release and non-GAAP financial measure information included as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. Effective Q1 2015, Amazon reorganized its reportable segments into North America, International, and AWS. Exhibit 99.3 provides historical 2014 and 2013 segment results. The reorganization did not affect consolidated net sales, operating income or loss, or net income or loss.

The team resolved to stay focused, minimize mistakes, put the puck deep, play patient hockey and prioritize strong defense. Players emphasized that success depends on teamwork, communication and shared responsibility rather than individual performance. They credited Claude’s hard work and positive example for younger players and said Jason is stepping up as a leader. The line has improved defensively and feels confident in its approach, while the three players communicate using a mix of Czech and English.

A December 2, 1902 message to Congress urged the reduction of unnecessary government printing, recommended extending the merit system to the District of Columbia and establishing consular appointments and promotions on proven fitness, and described the White House’s restoration as a historic monument. The message also transmitted Executive Department reports.

Department of State circulars addressed passport issuance. Officers were instructed to apply 1899 regulations consistently so that effective expatriants would not receive U.S. protection while loyal citizens would not be denied it. Native-born and naturalized citizens were to receive equal treatment abroad, although prolonged residence in a naturalized citizen’s country of origin without an intention to return could indicate loss of protection. Such citizens were still entitled to full protection until they effectively abandoned their U.S. residence and domicile.

The Clock is a simple zone offense combining a 1-3-1 free-lance passing attack with clockwise and counterclockwise rotations. Effective against person-to-person and zone defenses, it relies on sharp ball movement to create open outside shots, basket cuts, and post rolls. Core options include corner passes, ball reversals, dribble clearing, and continuity. A wing-to-corner pass prompts a basket cut, while the corner can return the ball, feed the post, or reverse the attack. Against a 1-3-1 zone, the offense exploits baseline vulnerabilities; against a 1-2-2, it attacks the middle and corners. Traps or double teams are countered by immediately rotating into a 2-1-2 “Cat” alignment and passing sharply out of the trap. “Crunch Time” specials include the “Vegas” double-screen action and the “Back” weakside lob, both offering additional scoring and passing options before returning to basic Clock action.

The figures present perspective, front, rear, top, bottom, and side views of two exercise apparatus designs, with opposite sides shown as mirror images. A band has a symbolic break, and portions beyond the illustrated broken lines are not part of the claimed design.

Bitcoin and related cryptocurrencies and stocks have plunged amid fears of regulation, including new measures in India, South Korea, and China. Long Blockchain, formerly Long Island Iced Tea, abandoned a plan to buy bitcoin mining equipment and focused on a merger with Stater Blockchain; its shares have fallen nearly 55% since the pivot. Riot Blockchain, LongFin, and Nodechain have also suffered steep 2018 declines.

Jordan W. Cowman of Baker & McKenzie forwarded the firm’s October 15, 2001 Global Employment Law Alert, prepared by its Global Labour, Employment & Employee Benefits Practice Group. The web-based alert provides concise, linked updates on employment-law developments, organized into Global, Asia Pacific, Europe, Africa/Middle East, South America, and North America sections, with country and regional summaries and access to current and archived editions.

Highlighted topics include employee benefits and pensions in Japan and Italy; discrimination laws in the United Kingdom and Eagle Global Logistics’ US$9 million EEOC settlement; Amazon and eBay litigation; Vietnamese-Malaysian visa exemptions and South African immigration legislation; chocolate manufacturers’ plan to end African child labour by 2005; Australian cybercrime legislation; workplace privacy and Swedish drug testing; China’s proposed Trade Union Law revisions; and revisions to UK working-time rules. The alert also covers the employment effects of the September 11 attacks, including job cuts at General Motors and Fiat and Boeing’s forecast for airline-industry recovery, as well as union rights, strikes, labor-law reforms, court rulings, pensions, taxes, immigration, workplace safety, privacy, redundancy, and discrimination disputes worldwide.

The publication states that it summarizes selected recent legal developments, provides links to detailed sources, and should not be relied upon as legal advice.

On August 31, 2016, Tesla subsidiaries Tesla Finance LLC and Tesla 2014 Warehouse SPV LLC entered a loan and security agreement with Deutsche Bank AG, New York Branch. The facility supports Tesla’s direct vehicle leasing program and permits borrowing up to $300 million, with draws scheduled to end August 31, 2017 and outstanding principal due September 20, 2018, subject to possible acceleration or extension. No amounts were outstanding as of August 31, 2016.

The facility is secured by lease-contract proceeds and related leased vehicles. Drawn amounts bear LIBOR-based interest, currently approximately 2%, or certain prime-rate-based pricing. The agreement includes customary defaults, financial and portfolio-performance covenants, advance-rate and reserve requirements, concentration limits, and fees on the unused commitment. Tesla is not a guarantor or party. The facility reduces cash needs for direct leasing, potentially lowering public-market fundraising and related stockholder dilution.

DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation builds on Ada’s 2022 frame-generation technology, which inserted one AI-generated frame between traditionally rendered frames using optical flow, motion vectors, and an AI network. Blackwell’s fifth-generation Tensor Cores enable up to three additional frames per rendered frame. The new model runs once per rendered frame, is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and replaces hardware optical flow with an efficient AI model. Enhanced Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine for more precise timing, while doubled pixel processing supports higher resolutions and refresh rates.

DLSS 4 replaces the prior CNN-based architecture with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Transformers use self-attention to identify long-range patterns across larger pixel windows, scale to twice as many parameters, and improve temporal stability, lighting detail, motion detail, and anti-aliasing. Super Resolution produces higher-resolution frames from lower-resolution inputs; Ray Reconstruction generates additional pixels between sampled rays and reduces conventional denoiser artifacts; DLAA applies Super Resolution techniques at native resolution.

Blackwell is designed to advance neural shaders, which train AI models to approximate rendering calculations, decompress textures, predict indirect lighting, and approximate subsurface scattering. Cooperative Vectors for DX12 and Vulkan, together with Slang features, allow Tensor Cores to be accessed through pixel and ray-tracing shaders. Applications include RTX Neural Materials, which approximates complex multilayer materials; Neural Texture Compression, which can provide up-to-seven-to-one VRAM compression; Neural Radiance Cache, which infers many lighting bounces from path-traced rays after one bounce and trains on live game data; and Stochastic Texture Filtering, which reduces aliasing and moiré patterns. RTX Skin applies ray-traced subsurface scattering to translucent materials, while RTX Neural Faces uses an optimized real-time generative model to infer natural faces from rasterized faces and 3D pose data.

The Blackwell GPU family includes the flagship GB202, with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, used by the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, and 336 Tensor cores, and is used by the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, and 200 Tensor cores, and is used by the RTX 5070. The specifications are provided without warranties, and NVIDIA reserves the right to modify or discontinue products and specifications.

The disclosure, claiming priority to U.S. Patent Application Ser. No. 16/985,649 filed Aug. 5, 2020, describes systems, methods, and non-transitory computer-readable media for a variable multiplexer that supports vehicle communication bus compatibility across manufacturers using different connector pinout configurations.

Vehicles use communication buses such as CAN bus to connect sensors, electronic control units, actuators, and diagnostic devices through multi-pin data link connectors. Although connector hardware may be standardized, manufacturers can assign different functions to individual pins, requiring different external cables. A variable multiplexer can be electronically configured to connect or disable input and output lines so that connector pins are mapped to external-device pins performing the same functions, allowing one device and cable to support multiple vehicles.

The external device may include the variable multiplexer, a network gateway, connection detection, pinout determination, pinout modification, and data-storage components. Pinout determination can obtain a vehicle identifier such as a VIN and query a remote system maintaining a vehicle data index. Alternatively, it can monitor bus traffic, compare data received at each pin with known pinout configurations, identify matching sets of active and inactive pins, and analyze signals on pins whose functions differ among candidate configurations. Checksum values transmitted with bus data may also be used to verify candidate configurations.

The disclosed method detects connection to a communication bus, determines the connector’s pinout configuration, and commands the variable multiplexer to adopt the corresponding configuration. The passage also describes representative software layers and machine hardware capable of executing the disclosed methods.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. TU102 is the architecture’s highest-performing implementation; TU104 and TU106 use the same basic design at different scales for gaming, professional graphics, and data-center products.

The full TU102 has six Graphics Processing Clusters, 36 Texture Processing Clusters, and 72 Streaming Multiprocessors. Each SM contains 64 CUDA Cores, eight Tensor Cores, one RT Core, a 256 KB register file, four texture units, and 96 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. Its four processing blocks each contain 16 FP32 and 16 INT32 cores, two Tensor Cores, a scheduler, and a dispatch unit. Concurrent integer and floating-point execution can provide up to 36% greater effective floating-point throughput. Turing’s unified L1 cache and shared-memory design provides twice Pascal’s per-TPC hit bandwidth and can be configured between 32 and 64 KB for each use. TU102 also has 96 ROP units, a 384-bit GDDR6 interface, 6 MB of L2 cache, and 144 FP64 units whose throughput is one-thirty-second of FP32 throughput.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 operations. TU102 contains 576 Tensor Cores, with eight in each SM. They accelerate deep-learning training and inference as well as NVIDIA NGX neural services. NGX features include Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses neural networks trained against 64-times-supersampled references to enhance images with less shading work, while DLSS 2X renders at the target resolution and reconstructs an output approaching the reference quality. NGX also provides trained models for content removal, frame interpolation, and image or video upscaling.

Second-generation NVLink gives TU102 two x8 links, each rated at 25 GB/s per direction, for 100 GB/s aggregate bidirectional bandwidth. Connected GPUs can directly access one another’s memory and combine memory for larger datasets. TU104 has one x8 link.

Turing introduced GDDR6 memory, with redesigned interface circuitry operating at 14 Gbps and providing a reported 20% power-efficiency improvement over Pascal’s GDDR5X. Signal integrity work reduced crosstalk by 40%, while improved memory compression and higher raw bandwidth together increase effective bandwidth by approximately 50% over Pascal.

The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K output at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, USB-C output, HDR processing, and BT.2100 tone mapping. The enhanced NVENC encoder supports 8K HEVC encoding at 30 fps and reduces HEVC bitrates by up to 25% and H.264 bitrates by up to 15%. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit support.

Dedicated RT Cores make real-time hardware-accelerated ray tracing possible by performing Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests. This frees SMs to handle other shading and compute work. The passage reports performance above 10 billion rays per second, compared with approximately 1.1 billion for software ray tracing on Pascal, and characterizes Turing as roughly ten times faster. Hybrid rendering retains rasterization for operations where it is effective while using ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects. Advanced denoising reduces the number of rays required. Turing ray tracing supports NVIDIA RTX and OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API. Ray-traced shadows provide correct contact hardening, ray-traced ambient occlusion adds geometric definition, and ray-traced reflections provide physically correct results without the limitations of screen-space or static-probe techniques.

Several additional rendering technologies broaden Turing’s capabilities. Mesh shading adds cooperative Task and Mesh Shaders that can process many objects without individual CPU draw calls, select levels of detail dynamically, and implement geometry cutaways. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently from visibility in 16-by-16-pixel regions; applications include content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering, and shading rates can also be increased within MSAA limits. Texture Space Shading stores shading in texture space, allowing visibility and appearance sampling to use independent rates and grids, reusing shaded texels across frames, and accelerating stereo VR rendering. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views, with applications including stereo and wide-field-of-view VR displays, cascaded shadow maps, and multiple character instances. Turing also supports bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, co-located resource types, and Tier 2 resource heaps.

VirtualLink and USB Type-C provide power, display, and data through one connector for VR headsets. MVR, foveated shading, and RT Core acceleration of ray-traced audio further expand Turing’s VR capabilities.

TU104 contains six GPCs, 48 SMs, eight 32-bit memory controllers, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores. Its 256-bit memory interface supports 320 GB/s bandwidth. The Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with five GPCs, 20 TPCs, 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, and 320 Tensor Cores. It includes 16 GB of memory, a 70-watt base-clock design, INT8 and INT4 inference capabilities, enhanced video decoding, and Volta-derived Multi-Process Service. The passage reports up to 40 times higher inference performance and more than 50 times higher energy efficiency than CPU-based inference, along with up to twice the energy efficiency of Tesla P4.

TU106 contains three GPCs, 36 SMs, eight 32-bit memory controllers, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores. It supports RT Cores and Turing Tensor Cores but not NVLink or SLI, and was used in the GeForce RTX 2070.

RTX-OPS is presented as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering. It weights Tensor operations at 20% usage, CUDA cores at 80%, RT Cores at 40%, and INT32 pipes at 28%, rather than simply adding all peak throughputs. The passage ends with NVIDIA’s disclaimers concerning specification accuracy, warranties, liability, product suitability, intellectual-property rights, and reproduction of its materials.

The passage examines equality and equality of opportunity, particularly in education. Equality is presented as a moral and social ideal requiring nondiscrimination, while equality of opportunity means enabling all members of society to reach advantageous positions through their knowledge and talents rather than social origin. Education is identified as essential to achieving this principle by providing equitable resources and opportunities.

The literature defines education as a continuous, generally positive social process that develops individuals’ skills, attitudes, behaviors, and capacity for self-realization. Equality of opportunity in education has historical roots in Prussia’s compulsory education and later research, including Coleman’s 1968 report. It is defined as giving everyone nondiscriminatory access to educational services that allow talents to develop and individuals to reach attainable standards.

Five groups of barriers are identified: economic, geographical, political, individual, and social factors. In Turkey, education policy is primarily shaped by the Ministry of National Education, with National Education Councils advising on reforms. Problems include inadequate schools and equipment, economic difficulties, geographical access barriers, and culturally or socially related lack of student motivation.

The passage notes disagreement over whether equal opportunity means legal access, identical resources, or opportunities responsive to individual abilities and needs. Recommendations include early and independent assessment of children’s abilities, improved access and educational quality, reduced achievement gaps between regions and school types, expanded preschool provision, better teacher training and recruitment, improved learning environments and infrastructure, and scientifically based planning of school locations and capacity. Every school should be enabled to provide quality education equitably, while teacher candidates should be recruited according to subject-specific needs and practical preparation.

Bad Bunny’s selection to headline the Super Bowl LX halftime show triggered fierce backlash from right-wing influencers over his Spanish-language music and criticism of Donald Trump, immigration policies, and conservative values. His avoidance of touring in the continental United States because of ICE raid concerns intensified the controversy, while Homeland Security adviser Corey Lewandowski warned that undocumented immigrants could face detention and deportation around the event.

The article frames the dispute as part of America’s culture wars, with Bad Bunny’s Puerto Rican identity and activism making him a symbolic target for conservatives. The NFL selected the globally popular artist to attract younger and international audiences as part of its strategy to diversify aaging viewership, continuing its Roc Nation partnership’s effort to bring cultural relevance to the halftime show. Bad Bunny described the performance as a celebration of his people, culture, and history. Regardless of the performance’s content, the announcement has already exposed political divisions surrounding inclusion, representation, and cultural identity in the United States.

Reusable patterns and shared components are central to modern software development, enabling code reuse, consistent implementation, and faster identification of defects. Within containerized systems, splitting applications into focused containers supports resource isolation, team ownership, separation of concerns, modular reuse, independent deployment, and easier testing.

Three tightly coupled single-node patterns are described. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a co-scheduled container that augments it. Sidecars can add HTTPS to legacy services, synchronize dynamic configuration, expose process and resource information, or synchronize code from Git to build a simple PaaS. The ambassador pattern places a proxy between an application and the outside world, routing requests to shards, performing service discovery, or splitting traffic between production and experimental services. The adapter pattern translates heterogeneous application interfaces into standard forms, including monitoring metrics, logging output, and database health checks. These patterns avoid modifying third-party containers and promote reuse, but successful reusable containers require parameterization, stable APIs, and clear documentation.

Multi-node systems commonly use microservices, in which components communicate through APIs. This approach supports focused teams, independent releases and scaling, but increases architectural and debugging complexity. A basic distributed pattern is a replicated load-balanced service: identical stateless replicas sit behind a load balancer, with readiness probes indicating when they can serve traffic. Session tracking may use IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing to keep requests associated with the same replica. Replicated stateless systems can add a caching tier for performance and rate limiting, followed by an SSL-terminating proxy layer.

Sharded services divide requests among shards, each handling only a subset of traffic. They are generally used for stateful systems whose data cannot fit on one machine and can improve cache memory utilization by avoiding duplicate data. Shard failures can reduce hit rates and increase latency, so shards may themselves be replicated for resilience. Sharding functions commonly use a deterministic, uniform hash followed by modulo selection. The shard key must group requests with identical responses while separating requests whose responses materially differ.

Interviews note a gifted teammate who shoots more than he passes and a team struggling against a hard-playing, hungry opponent. The speaker says their effort comes in spurts and they must keep working without worrying about the outcome, adding that when they play "scared" and rely on every player doing his job rather than being individuals, they are most successful. Facing a big test one game away, they cite the opponent's speed across all four lines and two goals from their defense as signs of a team mirroring last year's hungry champions.

Blackwell’s GeForce architecture unifies FP32 and INT32 cores, enabling many integer instructions to run at up to twice Ada’s throughput, although cores operate in only one mode per clock cycle and not all integer operations achieve the increase. Blackwell SMs target neural shaders, while texture units increase from 512 in the RTX 4090 to 680 in the RTX 5090. The RTX 5090 provides 1,636.76 gigatexels/sec of bilinear-filtered output versus 1,290.2 on the RTX 4090, and doubles point-sampled texture performance per cycle.

GDDR7 memory uses PAM3 signaling, improved signal-to-noise ratio, twice as many independent channels, advanced equalization, new clocking, and enhanced I/O training. The RTX 5090 has 28 Gbps GDDR7 memory and 1.792 TB/sec peak bandwidth, while the RTX 5080 has 30 Gbps memory and 960 GB/sec bandwidth. ECC is built into GDDR7 dies, always enabled on GeForce GPUs, supports single-bit error correction without a performance penalty, and is accompanied by EDR technology.

Fifth-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8, FP4, and FP6 operations. FP4 uses less than half the memory of FP16, provides more than twice the prior-generation performance, and can retain nearly full quality with NVIDIA TensorRT Model Optimizer quantization. The FLUX.dev model, for example, falls from more than 23 GB of VRAM at FP16 to less than 10 GB at FP4, and RTX 5090 FP4 generation takes just over five seconds for 30 steps versus 15 seconds for RTX 4090 at FP16.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware for cluster-level geometry, Linear Swept Spheres, and Mega Geometry. Mega Geometry uses cluster-level acceleration structures of up to 256 triangles, reducing subsequent BVH-processing requirements by two orders of magnitude, and adds Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures that update only changed scene partitions. Its APIs cover clusters and PTLAS through DirectX 12 and NVAPI, Vulkan extensions, and OptiX 9.0, and it is supported on RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Linear Swept Spheres accelerate ray tracing of hair, fur, grass, and similar geometry, rendering common hair use cases about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth the VRAM.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 has twice the reorder-logic efficiency and greater precision, enabling application-controlled optimization for divergent ray-tracing workloads and neural shading. The AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts with lower latency than CPU-driven scheduling, coordinating graphics and AI workloads through a model aligned with Windows HAGS.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, offers an additional 5% through AV1 UHQ, and supports 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, increasing export speeds by more than 50% generation over generation and fourfold versus the RTX 3090. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding and adds 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps, including 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with DSC.

Blackwell’s Max-Q improvements include advanced clock, power, and rail gating, independently controlled GPU-core and memory voltage rails, and faster workload-responsive clock adjustment. Clocks adapt up to 1,000 times faster than on previous architectures, and the deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada. Combined efficiency measures can reduce power consumption by up to 50% in small-language-model inference examples.

DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation can add up to three frames for every traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the previous frame-generation method, while AI-based optical flow and enhanced Flip Metering reduce computation and improve frame pacing. DLSS 4 also replaces convolutional models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, supporting twice as many parameters and improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting detail, and denoising.

Cooperative Vectors for DirectX 12 and Vulkan allow graphics shaders to access Tensor Cores, enabling neural texture compression with up to 7:1 compression over block-compressed formats. Other neural rendering technologies include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Materials use neural approximations for complex layered materials; one demonstration reduced storage from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Neural Radiance Cache estimates multiple lighting bounces after one traced bounce and trains on live game data. RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to games, while Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model and rasterized face geometry with pose data to create more natural faces.

The GB202 flagship contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor and Texture Cores, and powers the RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor and Texture Cores, and powers the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. The GB205 configuration described for the RTX 5070 contains 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor and Texture Cores. The document closes with accuracy, warranty, liability, licensing, product-use, and trademark notices.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture advances GPU efficiency and performance for gaming, professional graphics, and deep-learning inference. It combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation through hardware accelerators and hybrid rendering. Improved streaming multiprocessors and GDDR6 support boost graphics performance, while Tensor Cores power Neural Services for graphics effects.

October 23–24, 2001 clippings centered on Enron’s financial and regulatory troubles. Enron said asset sales could fund repayment of about $3.3 billion in notes issued by affiliated investment vehicles and due over the next 20 months, avoiding new equity. Treasurer Ben Glisan said sales were expected to generate at least $2.2 billion by the end of 2002, including $1.55 billion from the planned sale of Portland General Electric, but warned Enron could issue as much as $1 billion in stock if proceeds were insufficient.

Enron reported a $618 million third-quarter loss tied to $1.01 billion in write-offs and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity after ending transactions with the Fastow-managed LJM2 partnership. The SEC opened an informal inquiry into LJM and LJM2 dealings, and shareholder lawsuits were also reported. Enron maintained that its transactions were proper.

During an investor conference call, Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay defended CFO Andrew Fastow, cited procedural safeguards intended to protect shareholders, and said Enron had adequate liquidity, but both executives declined to answer detailed questions about LJM2. Analysts challenged Enron’s limited disclosure and questioned the structure of guarantees associated with Marlin and other financing vehicles. Enron said auditors found no Marlin-related write-down was required, and it considered publishing balance sheets with earnings reports and financial statements for special-purpose entities.

Enron shares fell 86 cents to $19.79, were down more than 40% over the week and 75% for the year, and traded heavily. The company had $1.85 billion in commercial paper outstanding, backed by $3.35 billion in credit lines, and sought a $750 million Citigroup loan as protection against possible loss of access to money markets. High options volatility made Enron January straddle premiums unusually attractive, though sellers faced substantial risk.

Other reports covered a modest decline in major U.S. stock indexes; AES’s request for Indian government assistance; possible LNG-shipping oversupply; British Gas’s offer of Brazilian assets to ONGC for control of Indian oil fields bought from Enron; a House stimulus bill that would give Enron a projected $254 million tax refund; and shareholder-fraud investigations covering Enron securities purchases from January 2000 through October 17, 2001.

Tesla Motors, Inc. reported that Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja, who had served for seven years, intends to retire. He will remain until his successor is selected and an effective transition is completed. At Tesla’s June 9, 2015 annual meeting, stockholders elected Antonio J. Gracias and Kimbal Musk as Class II directors, ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla’s independent accounting firm for fiscal 2015, and rejected stockholder proposals from Mark Peters and Elizabeth Farrell Peters.

The Reverse Action Offense was introduced by Hall of Fame coach Pete Newell in the late 1950s. It is a continuity offense centered on guard-around action but requires precise footwork, timing, communication, and coordinated off-ball screening. The passer, screener, and receiver must function as one unit while recognizing defensive deployments. Its most recognizable option is the weakside wing’s rub cut off a post screen, alongside post play, guard-around isolation, and counters against defensive overplays.

Any pass or dribble can initiate the continuity. Players use weakside, strongside, dribble-clear, back-cut, and back-door entries, moving through guard-around cuts, rub cuts, post feeds, reversals, screens, and rolls. When a shot is unavailable, the ball can be reversed to continue the action.

Defensive reads shape specific counters. Guard-around defenders may chase over the screen, go under it, cheat early, switch, or show and recover, resulting in drives, kick-outs, pull-up jumpers, opposite drives, rolls, or slips. Sideline triangle actions include post splits, high-post splits, lob and high-post feeds, and one-on-one post isolation.

Post players counter high-side defense with power layups, baseline-side defense with baby hooks, a front with lob passes, behind-the-post defense with turn-and-face triple-threat moves, and double teams with releases to the elbow or short corner. Reverse Action spacing also creates immediate back-cut options against passing-lane overplays and denials, including lob passes, skip passes, and give-and-go cuts. Late-clock specials include weakside screen-and-roll, double screens, and back-screen lob actions.

Indian financial institutions led by IDBI were seeking buyers for the 85% of Dabhol Power Company held by Enron, Bechtel and General Electric. Tata Power and BSES began due diligence after signing confidentiality agreements. Lenders reportedly set a $700 million reserve price, although the bidders were said to consider no more than $400 million acceptable. A proposed restructuring package included a Rs 2.70-per-unit tariff, reductions in lender interest rates and equity values, conversion of foreign debt, MAT exemption, mega-power status, separation of the LNG facility from the power project, a long moratorium and guaranteed distribution rights. Lenders’ exposure to DPC exceeded Rs 6,000 crore.

Maharashtra State Electricity Board rejected the power-purchase agreement and refused to attend DPC’s November 19 board meeting in Houston. The Bombay High Court restrained DPC from issuing a final termination notice until December 3. DPC’s 740 MW first phase remained idle, while construction of the 90%-complete 1,444 MW second phase had stopped; DPC had also defaulted on Rs 57 crore in interest and guarantee fees. A London arbitration tribunal was scheduled to meet November 24 over DPC’s dispute concerning an unpaid December power bill.

Dynegy’s announced takeover of Enron was expected to take until the third quarter of 2002 to complete and was initially expected not immediately to affect negotiations over DPC. Separately, the Bombay High Court restrained authorities from encashing SBI guarantees for disputed customs duty on DPC equipment, involving a claimed total liability of Rs 290 crore.

SCI’s 20% interest in the LNG tanker LNG Laxmi was rescued by the Omani government’s acquisition of a 50% stake in the owning consortium and a 20-year charter. The article on Enron and Arthur Andersen questioned how the auditor failed to detect Enron’s overstated profits and cited earlier audit failures involving ZZZZ Best and savings-and-loan cases.

A football reverse play deceives the defense by moving the ball in one direction before transferring it to a player moving the opposite way. Timing, momentum, disguise, and a seal created by offensive linemen can produce large gains, while poor execution risks losing yards and momentum.

Examples described include:

- **Carolina Panthers, 2018:** Cam Newton tossed the ball to DJ Moore moving right, drawing the defense with him. Curtis Samuel collected the ball at full speed and ran left for 15 yards while blockers sealed off defenders, ultimately setting up a touchdown against man coverage.
- **Arizona Cardinals, 2020:** Kyler Murray faked a handoff and used Andy Isabella’s motion to draw both deep safeties away before running right behind a three-on-three blocking advantage.
- **Purdue, 2021:** A reverse screen returned the ball to the quarterback, who passed it to the original ball carrier. Six blockers formed a screen downfield, resulting in a touchdown.
- **Reverse pass:** A quarterback handed the ball to a motion receiver, then escaped a defender and ran down the sideline. The ball carrier passed back to him in stride for a touchdown.

Packers coach Mike McCarthy says cornerback Damarious Randall has had an outstanding offseason and stood out during OTAs and minicamp. After injuries, inconsistency and Sam Shields’ season-ending injury disrupted Randall’s second season, he is embracing the starting nickel role, with Davon House, Kevin King and LaDarius Gunter available on the perimeter.

Building a defensive wall requires defenders to stand shoulder-to-shoulder, at least 10 yards from a free kick, to obstruct the near side of the goal and reduce the goalkeeper’s workload. As players develop accurate, powerful free kicks—generally around age 12 on a full-sized field—coaches should introduce wall building. Defenders must anticipate the need for a wall and promptly build it, mark attackers, and prepare for a counterattack.

Law 13 requires defenders to remain at least 10 yards from the ball until it is in play and requires attackers to stay at least one yard from a wall of three or more players. Run-over deceptions are permitted, but defenders must move expeditiously. A kick taken with a defender inside 10 yards must generally be retaken unless advantage applies. Blocking or delaying the restart is unsporting conduct and may result in a yellow card.

The referee determines whether a free kick is direct or indirect, verifies the ball’s placement, and need not allow extra time for a wall. Attackers may take a quick free kick even while the wall is being formed. During a ceremonial free kick, attackers may request that an improperly positioned wall be moved back and must wait for the restart. The referee may also move the wall and use vanishing spray to mark the ball’s location and a temporary restraining line.

The goalkeeper alone decides whether to build a wall, based on the ball’s location and the goalkeeper’s training, experience, and confidence. Wall size and placement depend on the ball’s distance from the goal and its angle from the field’s midline; central, close free kicks require more players. The goalkeeper calls for a specific number of defenders, while other defenders mark attackers, establish an offside line, and prepare counterattacking options.

In a traditional wall, the “Anchor” or “Post-man,” usually a tall midfielder or striker, moves onto the imaginary line between the near post and the ball at 10 yards. The goalkeeper adjusts the Anchor’s position using left-or-right instructions and measured steps, then moves aside to protect the far side of the goal. Remaining wall players arrive in position, fill in shoulder-to-shoulder, and shift with the Anchor. Gaps are prohibited, and players should stand firmly facing the ball, hold any protected body parts against their bodies, avoid turning or rushing as the kick is taken, and jump only when doing so will not allow the ball to pass underneath.

An alternative uses a designated “Wall Setter” beyond the ball to position the Anchor. This frees the goalkeeper to see the ball, react to a quick kick, and take position near the far post while the Anchor remains facing the ball.

In the rare case of an indirect free kick less than 10 yards from goal, defenders must quickly form a wall on the goal line between the posts. There is no Anchor; the goalkeeper chooses its alignment, other players fill in shoulder-to-shoulder, and a designated “bullet player” may sprint directly at the ball once it moves. Coaches can use ropes to demonstrate wall angles and dummies to train goalkeepers against shots around a wall.

The Kansas Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for Farmway Credit Union. Melvin Douglas defaulted on his secured debt, and Farmway repossessed and sold collateral after Douglas’s death pursuant to a security agreement and a pre-death oral agreement with Douglas, his wife, and his heirs. The court held that an administrator’s statutory right to possess a decedent’s property is not absolute and does not override a secured creditor’s contractual right to peaceful self-help repossession. Farmway was not required to file a probate claim or foreclose before exhausting its security. The court did not address self-help repossession without an agreement permitting possession after default. Summary judgment was not premature because the relevant facts were uncontroverted and no further discovery could alter the legal determination.

Counter is a run play that fakes Power in one direction before running opposite. A guard pulls to kick out the playside edge defender, while a fullback inserts to block the linebacker. The play exploits aggressive defensive over-pursuit, creates favorable blocking angles, and gives the offense extra bodies at the point of attack. Its weaknesses include slower development, vulnerability to penetration in the open B-gap, and defensive “spill” tactics that force the ball carrier laterally.

Against a 3-4 front, the left tackle guides the B-gap defender toward the center before hinging to the C-gap; the right tackle and tight end combine against the backside linebacker. Against a 4-3 front, the left tackle protects the B-gap, the center and right tackle double-team the defensive tackle, and the tight end blocks the middle linebacker. In both schemes, the fullback fakes a counter step before inserting, the tailback redirects for the handoff, and the quarterback opens left before handing off right and booting left.

Variations include GT Counter, where the backside tackle replaces the fullback as the insert and the fullback secures the edge defender, and Gun Split GT Counter, which applies triple-option principles using the edge defender as the dive key and alley defender as the pitch key.

IDC’s December 2021 survey of 200 technology decision-makers at industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland examines simulation, modeling, data analytics, digital twins, and high-performance computing (HPC).

Cloud-based engineering workstations and visualization tools can give teams shared access to current data, improve collaboration, and support AR/VR-enabled development. Digital twins can digitally map products, plants, and processes, monitor operations, test scenarios, and enable new services such as Product-as-a-Service and outcome-based models.

Industrial simulations are becoming increasingly complex, while 42% of respondents report that their simulations are already outdated or inaccurate and half say calculations take too long. Industrial simulation increasingly depends on complex calculations, but limited computing capacity forces trade-offs between speed and accuracy and delays development. Forty-two percent of surveyed enterprises reported outdated or inaccurate simulations, while half said calculations take too long. HPC enables complex simulations, faster and higher-quality analysis, more iterations, new industrial use cases, and quicker development of digital products, services, and business models.

Most enterprises favor external HPC infrastructure: 87% of HPC users prefer or plan to use external services, while only 6% currently operate on-premises systems and 28% plan to. The paper develops a mathematical framework for analyzing cubic-to-tetragonal phase coexistence in ferroelectrics using high-resolution, three-dimensional X-ray reciprocal-space mapping. Pure cubic and tetragonal phases cannot form a mismatch-free planar interface unless their lattice parameters are equal, because the tetragonal distortion creates lateral strain. The adaptive-state (AS), or WLR, concept overcomes this mismatch by macroscopically averaging periodic assemblages of differently oriented tetragonal domains with a fixed volume ratio, producing an effective lower-symmetry lattice that can match the cubic phase.

Unlike conventional AS and WLR treatments, the framework does not require domains to be miniaturized. It derives the average lattice, mismatch-free habit-plane indices, orientation relationships among cubic, adaptive, and tetragonal lattices, and reciprocal-space separations of Bragg peaks. Three ferroelastic tetragonal variants form six permissible domain-wall pairings; two possible domain ratios for each pairing generate four connection variants, yielding 24 possible cubic–adaptive-state coexistence configurations. Analytical expressions for these configurations are summarized in tables. The model treats sufficiently large tetragonal domains as independently diffracting while retaining the orientation relationships imposed by the adaptive-state mechanism.

The formalism is tested against temperature-dependent high-resolution reciprocal-space maps of a PMN-35PT single crystal near its cubic-to-tetragonal transition at approximately 435 K. Phase coexistence spans about 4 K. The measured lattice relation gives a {110} habit plane and predicted tetragonal-domain fractions of 2/3 or 1/3. Predicted Bragg-peak separations agree strongly with observations, supporting an AS-like coexistence state without domain miniaturization. Peak-width analysis estimates domain dimensions of several hundred nanometers, while not excluding miniaturization near the transition. The results provide a basis for interpreting high-resolution X-ray and electron diffraction and may extend to other ferroelectric systems and coexisting rhombohedral–tetragonal phases.

The study examined antibody escape by SARS-CoV-2 BA.2.86 (Pirola) and its descendant JN.1. BA.2.86 carries 33 spike-protein mutations relative to BA.2, distributed across the NTD, RBD, and S1/S2–S2 regions; structural modeling showed them spread over the distal spike without clustering.

Using reverse mutational scanning, the authors created 33 BA.2.86 pseudoviruses, each reverting one mutation to its BA.2 amino acid, and tested neutralization with paired serum samples from healthcare workers before and after an XBB.1.5-adapted BNT162b2 booster. Before the booster, BA.2.86 and JN.1 were neutralized approximately 40-fold and 80-fold less efficiently than Wuhan-Hu-01, respectively. The booster substantially increased neutralization titers against both variants and eliminated the neutralization difference between them, although titers remained below those against Wuhan-Hu-01.

Individual-mutation testing identified contributions to immune escape from ins16MPLF, K356T, N460K, V483Δ, A484K, F486P, and P621S. After XBB.1.5 vaccination, removing the MPLF insertion, restoring Y144, K554E, or K484A improved neutralization toward BA.2 levels, whereas reverting P621S did not significantly increase neutralization. The findings indicate shared escape epitopes may account for residual resistance in BA.2.86 and JN.1.

Limitations include reliance on pseudoviruses rather than authentic virus, incomplete information about prior infections, a relatively young healthcare-worker cohort, and examination of single mutants rather than combinations.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed the confirmation of a South Bend local-improvement assessment roll. Changed circumstances required additional private contracting, raising the actual cost to $89,199.92, and assessments were increased accordingly.

The court held that the preliminary cost estimate guides the city council’s decision whether to initiate an improvement and need not limit later assessments. Because the increased assessment reflected the actual bona fide cost of the work, was authorized by statute, and was attributable to changed conditions, it was valid. The ordinance contained all material statutory provisions and was not void for indefiniteness, and the evidence supported the benefits assessed. The judgment was affirmed.

The document defines a standardized Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for interoperability between guest operating systems and hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. These features encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access or modification. VM exits are classified as Automatic Exits, which expose no guest register state, or Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), where the guest selectively shares state through the GHCB. The document also standardizes required NAEs, minimum exposed state, and guest-specific behaviors such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

The GHCB is a 4-KB decrypted memory area contained within one decrypted page. Its layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area through offset 0x3ff but includes only fields needed for VMGEXIT, limiting exposed guest state. Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, XSS MSR data for CPUID 0xd, shared SW_SCRATCH storage, and restricted APIC emulation for IPIs and timers.

The passage also covers GHCB establishment, negotiation, layout, secrets and EFI blob protocols, guest exits and VMGEXIT requests, SMP booting, NMIs, debug registers, SMM, nested virtualization, and SNP restricted injection. Revision notes describe 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, malformed-input error handling, VLEK GUID support, expanded SNP guest requests and certificate returns, APIC ID lists, multiple VMPL levels, page-state-change notifications, AP reset hold, and feature-advertisement updates.

The study examines elementary mathematics teachers’ perceptions of distance education (DE), obstacles encountered, and future preferences in the UAE. Following the UAE’s transition to DE during the COVID-19 pandemic, the research addresses how teachers view online mathematics instruction, what challenges they face, and whether they would prefer future DE use. The literature review emphasizes that technology can transform teaching but must be meaningfully integrated with content, pedagogy, teacher beliefs, and student needs; DE effectiveness also depends on course quality, instructor expertise, learner characteristics, and support.

A quantitative online survey was administered in spring 2020–2021 to 90 Grade 1–5 mathematics teachers in government and private schools in Al Ain. Participants were selected through convenience sampling; 75 were female and 15 male. The 37-item, five-point Likert questionnaire covered demographics, perceptions, obstacles, and future preferences. Experts reviewed its validity, 30 teachers pilot-tested it, and its overall Cronbach’s alpha was 0.79. Normality testing supported the use of parametric tests.

Teachers generally reported positive perceptions of online mathematics teaching, with an overall mean of 4.00. They were especially confident using digital technologies, adapting lessons to online instruction, representing mathematical ideas digitally, and supporting student learning. They also reported gaining technological skills and using more teaching methods. However, perceptions were mixed regarding student achievement and online teaching’s suitability for elementary mathematics. Teachers indicated that online instruction increased workload, preparation time, and stress, and many viewed face-to-face teaching as more effective.

Reported obstacles had an overall mean of 3.69. School resources, training, and flexible, understandable online tools were viewed favorably, while teachers reported increased preparation time, a need for new teaching methods, stress, weaker student communication and participation, reduced motivation, and concerns that students learned less mathematics online. Nevertheless, the reported difficulty of using online resources received the lowest obstacle score.

Future preferences favored institutional support and training: 87.8% reported receiving needed administrative support, and 85.6% reported receiving training for online teaching. Although 64.4% enjoyed teaching mathematics online, 76.7% preferred face-to-face instruction when given a choice. Statistical analyses found no significant differences in perceptions by educational level, gender, or experience; obstacles differed significantly by educational level, with graduate-level teachers reporting higher obstacle scores, while no significant obstacle differences were found by gender or experience.

The discussion concludes that teachers were generally confident in integrating digital tools into mathematics teaching but remained concerned about increased effort, student engagement, motivation, communication, and learning outcomes. The study recommends professional development in digital tools and online workload management, stronger technical and collaborative support, improved student engagement, suitable digital assessment and feedback, and testing of hybrid teaching models. Further research should include student perspectives, comparative and longitudinal studies, and investigation across subjects, grade levels, and cultural contexts. Limitations include the modest convenience sample, its restriction to teachers with abundant resources and support, and the mandatory pandemic context, which may not represent voluntary or hybrid teaching conditions.

The lecture introduces Langmuir probes as metal conductors inserted into a plasma to measure potential and current. A probe becomes negatively charged because electrons move faster than ions and initially dominate its collected current. Charging continues until electron collection is balanced by ion collection at the floating potential, which differs from the plasma potential because the probe and its sheath perturb the plasma. Potentials are referenced to the unperturbed plasma far from the probe.

Biasing a single probe produces a characteristic I–V curve with electron-saturation, transition, and ion-saturation regimes. Between the floating and plasma potentials, some electrons are repelled while ions are attracted; below the floating potential, electron collection is suppressed and the probe draws ion saturation current.

Quantitative interpretation requires sheath theory. The Debye length is the characteristic distance over which the probe’s potential perturbation is screened. When this is much smaller than the probe size, a quasi-planar, one-dimensional approximation can be used. The presented sheath model assumes cold ions, quasi-neutrality in the presheath, and Boltzmann-distributed electrons. For a sufficiently negative probe potential, the sheath-edge potential is \(V_s=-T_e/(2e)\). Ion continuity, energy conservation, and these assumptions relate the ion and electron densities and velocities at the probe to bulk plasma density and temperature. The resulting ion-current expression is approximately
\[
I_{\mathrm{si}}=eA n_\infty e^{-1/2}\sqrt{T_e/m_i},
\]
while the electron current contains a Maxwellian velocity factor and the factor \(1/4\) associated with random particle motion.

A single probe is normally swept near its floating potential. Fitting \(\ln(I-I_{\mathrm{si}})\) against probe voltage gives the electron temperature, after which the ion saturation current can be used to infer the plasma density. Operating near floating potential keeps currents low, avoids heating or melting the probe, and remains within the regime where the sheath approximation is valid. Limitations include the need to subtract ion saturation current, uncertainty in locating floating potential safely, and sweep time, which prevents resolving rapid fluctuations.

A double probe uses two connected tips biased relative to each other. Their currents are equal and opposite, so no net current is drawn from the plasma, and electron-saturation currents cannot be drawn accidentally. Its current follows a hyperbolic-tangent characteristic; the slope near zero bias gives the electron temperature, and the ion saturation current gives the density. It remains sweep-time limited.

A triple probe adds a floating probe that directly measures floating potential. With the double-probe bias fixed at several electron temperatures, the three probes sample three points on the exponential I–V characteristic, allowing density and temperature to be obtained without sweeping and with faster time resolution. This method depends strongly on the assumed characteristic’s validity and cannot reveal deviations with only three points. Closely spaced probes can also interfere through overlapping presheaths.

Magnetic fields alter particle orbits and presheath structure, while collisions modify particle flux and require corresponding changes to the sheath theory. Hutchinson’s textbook and Lieberman and Lichtenberg’s book on sheath theory are recommended for these and other detailed treatments.

Denver ended a 37-game drought without a 100-yard rusher by totaling 101 yards in a 28-3 Monday night win over Cincinnati. The Broncos outgained the Bengals 353 yards and evened their record at 2-2. Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 26, 2022 reported quarterly net sales of $97.278 billion, up 9% from $89.584 billion a year earlier. Product sales were $77.457 billion and services sales were $19.821 billion. Net income increased to $25.010 billion from $23.630 billion, while diluted EPS rose to $1.52 from $1.40. For the first six months, net sales were $221.223 billion, net income was $59.640 billion, and diluted EPS was $3.62.

Second-quarter sales increased 5% for iPhone to $50.570 billion, 15% for Mac to $10.435 billion, 12% for Wearables, Home and Accessories to $8.806 billion, and 17% for Services to $19.821 billion; iPad sales declined 2% to $7.646 billion. Six-month sales rose for iPhone, Mac, Wearables, Home and Accessories, and Services, while iPad sales declined.

Geographically, second-quarter sales rose 19% in the Americas to $40.882 billion, 5% in Europe to $23.287 billion, and 3% in Greater China to $18.343 billion. Japan sales were unchanged at $7.724 billion, while Rest of Asia Pacific sales fell 7% to $7.042 billion.

Gross margin was $42.559 billion, or 43.7%, compared with $38.079 billion, or 42.5%, in the prior-year quarter. Product gross margin was 36.4%, and services gross margin was 72.6%. Operating expenses rose to $12.580 billion from $10.576 billion, primarily reflecting higher research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses. Operating income was $29.979 billion.

At March 26, 2022, Apple reported $350.662 billion of assets, $283.263 billion of liabilities, and $67.399 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $28.098 billion, while current and non-current marketable securities totaled $164.632 billion. Commercial paper was $6.999 billion and term debt was $112.982 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $75.132 billion, compared with $62.744 billion in the prior-year period.

During the six months, Apple used $43.109 billion for share repurchases and paid $7.327 billion for dividends and dividend equivalents. It repurchased 266 million shares for $43.3 billion, including shares delivered under accelerated repurchase agreements. Remaining repurchase authorization was $17.6 billion at quarter-end. On April 28, 2022, the board added $90 billion to the authorization and raised the quarterly dividend from $0.22 to $0.23 per share beginning in the third quarter.

Deferred revenue was $12.5 billion, with 63% expected to be recognized within one year, 27% in one to two years, 8% in two to three years, and 2% after three years. The company used derivatives to partially offset foreign-exchange and interest-rate exposure, and hedge-related gains and losses were not material. Total deferred marketable securities restricted from general use were $15.4 billion.

The filing noted continuing COVID-19 effects, including remote work, limited retail-store operations, supplier disruptions, and potential shortages. The Epic Games litigation remained under appeal after a court found that certain App Store Review Guidelines violated California unfair-competition law; Apple’s cross-appeal was stayed. Disclosure controls were effective, and there were no material changes in risk factors or internal control over financial reporting during the quarter.

A Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found that more than one in four U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing support, contributing to lower job satisfaction. Two-thirds report insufficient teaching assistants, aides or paraprofessionals, while 62% report shortages of mental-health resources or special educators. Although 72% say they have the equipment needed to teach effectively, 24% lack adequate furniture, 25% lack laptops or computers, and 35% lack printing supplies; one-third describe ordering materials as difficult. Teachers with adequate resources are far more likely to report job satisfaction than those without (77% vs. 44%). Low-income schools more often reported technology and printing gaps, while staffing shortages persisted across income levels. About half of teachers said professional development is not grounded in students’ needs, and only one-third had opportunities to observe other teachers. The survey included roughly 2,000 teachers at three points from October 2024 to May 2025.

This medRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed, describes development and nurse evaluation of a Patient Report Template (PRT) intended to streamline electronic health record documentation and nursing handoffs. The PRT combines SBAR and I PASS the BATON with additional clinical information across nine sections: Patient Profile, Chief Complaint/Review of Systems, Situation, Safety, Background, Actions, Timing, Ownership, and Next. It provides an at-a-glance summary intended to reduce cognitive load, repeated EHR retrieval, information loss, and handoff-related safety risks. Large language models are proposed as a future mechanism for generating concise reports from unstructured clinical text.

An anonymous survey was emailed to 2,118 University of Iowa Health Care nurses, with 106 responding. Participants rated PRT component usefulness and their comfort, trust, and expected utility of AI-generated reports using five-point Likert scales. Most PRT components were considered useful. Patient Profile and Safety components received consistently strong ratings; Chief Complaint, Current Medications, Allergies, and Signs to Elevate were among the highest-rated items. Lower-rated components included Level of Uncertainty, Family History, Eyes, Integumentary, and Musculoskeletal sections.

Nurses reported relatively low comfort and trust in AI, with average scores of 2.38 and 2.50, respectively, while expected utility was moderate at 3.00. Limitations include restriction to one health system, possible selection and response biases, and reliance on perceived usefulness rather than hands-on testing. Future research should evaluate the PRT in clinical use, assess customization across specialties, and conduct usability and accuracy testing of AI-generated reports.

The article describes the “turn of the month” strategy as an extension of the end-of-month or Ultimo effect into the first three trading days of the new month. Its rules are to buy at the close of the fifth-to-last trading day and sell at the close of the third trading day of the next month, leaving the strategy invested about 33% of the time.

Backtests using compounded returns show that the strategy has performed strongly in the S&P 500 since at least 1960, reportedly producing a 7.1% CAGR with smaller, shorter drawdowns than buy and hold. The article also reports favorable results across emerging markets, healthcare, gold-mining stocks, high-yield funds, real estate stocks, Brazil, Japan, Bitcoin, commodities, utilities, energy, consumer staples, and India’s Nifty Fifty. The effect was weak or nonexistent in gold and more erratic in technology stocks.

The final calendar day averaged a 0.1% gain versus 0.04% for a random day, while the final trading day performed worst among the last seven trading days. Logging systems vary in output levels, destinations, and formats, complicating centralized collection, especially for containers expected to write to stdout. An adapter container can redirect logs to stdout and transform varied formats into a common structured representation for aggregation. This is cheaper and more reusable than maintaining patched versions of third-party application containers.

The passage reviews a peer quarterly comparison of eight oil majors—Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Royal Dutch Shell, BP, Statoil, Total, ENI and ConocoPhillips—arguing they can sustain profitable margins at roughly $50/bbl. Oil prices appear to have bottomed in 2016, and higher prices are driving revenues, operating cash flows, margins and return on sales. Aggregate revenues bottomed in 2016 and are rising on higher prices and production; aggregate oil production grew 5.3% (10.7 to 11.3 M b/d) from 2Q15 to 2Q17, natural gas output rose 9.7%, and combined boe production grew 7.2%, with five of eight majors expanding. Chevron and Statoil showed the most dramatic ROS improvement. Global supply and demand appear to be rebalancing, with inventories drawn down and demand growing about 1.2 M b/d; the author expects the positive trends to strengthen in the second half of 2017 and spill into 2018.
