Lenders described the outcome as positive, but no agreement was announced. IDBI denied that lenders had agreed to mothball the second phase, while DPC had proposed completing construction before reviewing the project; one source said completion required $500 million. DPC maintained that the power purchase agreement remained in force and said it could ultimately bill the state for second-phase electricity.

India’s prime minister expressed confidence that the dispute would be resolved, and the central government directed the Central Electricity Authority to seek additional buyers, but questioned who would purchase the costly power. Dabhol also planned to challenge a Maharashtra regulator’s order temporarily barring international arbitration. DPC’s lender discussions included the proposed plant load factor, unpaid contractor costs and possible additional buyers.

Chicago officials proposed an eight-year agreement under which Enron would supply 60% of electricity used by city buildings and municipal facilities, with ComEd providing the rest. Officials projected annual savings of about $3 million. City officials acknowledged concerns about California supply practices, while Enron said it was honoring contracts at agreed rates. The City Council also approved, 44-3, a ward-redistricting plan intended to preserve African-American voting strength despite growth in Hispanic-majority wards, and unanimously prohibited racial profiling by police and other law-enforcement officers.

California regulators were considering suspending direct access for large electricity users, a policy Enron had lobbied to preserve. The proposal could limit large customers’ ability to contract directly with suppliers such as Enron amid efforts to stabilize Southern California Edison.

Other reports examined opposition to possible steel import restrictions, noting warnings from steel-consuming businesses, including a coalition that included Enron, that tariffs could raise downstream costs and cost jobs. A profile of Pacific Hydro described its expansion plans for wind and hydroelectric power, strong share-price performance and high valuation. An analysis of India’s economic reforms highlighted stalled privatizations of Air-India, Maruti Udyog and VSNL alongside progress liberalizing insurance. A commentary criticized California Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s remark that convicted or unconvicted Kenneth Lay should share a prison cell with a violent, tattooed inmate, arguing that prison sexual assault should be treated and prevented as a crime.

Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the quarter ended March 31, 2022. The company operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments and reported that COVID-19 disruptions, semiconductor shortages, supplier delays, port congestion, inflation, and higher shipping, material, and labor costs continued to affect operations and pricing.

Total revenue for the quarter was $18.756 billion, compared with $10.389 billion a year earlier. Automotive revenue rose to $16.861 billion from $9.002 billion, comprising vehicle sales of $15.514 billion, regulatory credits of $679 million, and leasing revenue of $668 million. Energy generation and storage revenue was $616 million, while services and other revenue was $1.279 billion. Gross profit was $5.460 billion, operating income was $3.603 billion, and net income was $3.280 billion. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $3.318 billion, or $2.86 per diluted share, compared with $438 million, or $0.39 per diluted share, in the prior-year quarter.

At March 31, 2022, Tesla reported $17.505 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $66.038 billion of total assets, $30.632 billion of liabilities, and $34.085 billion of stockholders’ equity. Operating activities generated $3.995 billion of cash, while investing and financing activities used $2.167 billion and $1.914 billion, respectively. Total debt and finance leases declined to $4.812 billion from $6.834 billion at year-end 2021. The 2022 convertible notes were fully settled, the 2024 notes became convertible during the second quarter, and Tesla repaid $380 million of solar asset and loan-backed notes, recognizing an $11 million extinguishment charge.

Tesla held $1.26 billion of digital assets at carrying value, with a fair value of $1.96 billion, after purchasing an immaterial amount during the quarter. Construction in progress included work at Gigafactories Berlin, Texas, and Shanghai. Stock-based compensation expense was $418 million, including $48 million for the 2018 CEO Performance Award and $69 million for 2021 performance-based awards.

The company’s New York and Shanghai arrangements included investment, employment, capital expenditure, and tax-revenue commitments. Legal matters included the SolarCity acquisition litigation, challenges to the CEO award and a potential going-private transaction, a JPMorgan warrant dispute seeking approximately $162 million, and race-discrimination litigation and regulatory matters. Tesla stated that it could not reasonably estimate losses for certain stockholder proceedings and intended to defend the claims.

Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones said he stopped pursuing Trevor Lawrence on the Jaguars’ game-winning touchdown run because he believed the play was over, calling it a teaching moment and vowing it will not happen again. He said his social media accounts were deactivated before the game and that he welcomes criticism. The Chiefs next face Detroit’s top-scoring offense.

This medRxiv preprint examined whether the interval between COVID-19 infection and vaccination affects hybrid immunity. Two Oregon Health & Science University cohorts were studied using ELISA and live-virus neutralization assays against ancestral SARS-CoV-2 (WA1) and the Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.2 variants.

In a longitudinal cohort, 10 previously infected participants and 20 matched participants without prior infection received the two-dose BNT162b2 vaccine. Both groups developed neutralizing antibodies after vaccination, but previously infected participants had significantly higher titers against all tested strains. A cross-sectional cohort similarly found that 46 participants with hybrid immunity had greater antibody levels and variant-neutralizing titers than 20 vaccine-only participants. Hybrid immunity increased RBD-specific total antibodies 3.6-fold, IgG 3.7-fold, IgA 3.2-fold, and full-length spike antibodies 3.1-fold. Neutralizing titers increased 8.4-fold against WA1, 12.5-fold against Alpha, 22.7-fold against Beta, 9.6-fold against Delta, 19.0-fold against Omicron BA.1, and 13.3-fold against Omicron BA.2.

Across exposure intervals of 35–404 days, longer time between infection and vaccination was associated with higher full-length spike antibody levels and stronger neutralization. By day 400, estimated neutralizing increases ranged from 4.8-fold against Alpha to 17.6-fold against Omicron BA.1, with the largest gains against more vaccine-resistant variants. Cross-neutralization also improved with longer intervals for Beta, Delta, and Omicron, although neutralizing potency per antibody did not increase over time. These associations remained significant when infection-before-vaccination and vaccine-breakthrough groups were analyzed separately. Exposure interval was more strongly associated with antibody responses than age, sex, or time from final exposure to sample collection.

The findings indicate that hybrid immune responses continue developing for at least a year after initial antigen exposure and that longer intervals between infection and vaccination produce higher and broader variant-neutralizing responses. The authors state that the results support broader vaccine access, including delayed vaccination when appropriate, while cautioning that intentional SARS-CoV-2 infection is not a reasonable public-health strategy because of its risk of severe illness, complications, and death.

Castle Donington-based DPI (UK), which makes aluminium frames and lightboxes, received a Collaborate grant of more than £12,200 for an automated saw. It will cut larger aluminium panels and structures in the UK, reduce contract completion times, double output by retaining the existing saw for smaller work, and support future job creation in the workshop and sales office. DPI grew 37% last year. The ERDF-funded scheme, overseen by Leicester City Council, offers eligible businesses grants of £5,000–£25,000, specialist workshops and one-to-one advice.

Andrew W. Lo welcomes first-year MBA students to 15.401 Finance Theory, describing finance as the systematic study of financial transactions and “mathematics plus money.” He argues that finance is both intellectually rigorous and practical, and that its principles are essential to management decisions across business and personal life. The course is designed to develop financial reasoning through valuation, management, time, and risk.

Lo illustrates finance’s broad applicability through James Simons, whose quantitative hedge fund relies on advanced mathematics; Warren Buffett, who analyzes company statements and valuations using relatively simple arithmetic; and Jack Welch, who used financial judgment to guide investment and cost decisions at General Electric. All three succeeded through an understanding of finance despite their different backgrounds.

The course focuses on four components of the financial system: households, financial intermediaries, nonfinancial corporations, and capital markets. Its two fundamental challenges are valuing assets and managing them. Management means comparing alternatives and selecting the most valuable option, while valuation requires establishing what value means and how financial markets discover prices. In an auction demonstration, participants bid $45 for an unseen package that contained an iPod Nano worth about $149, illustrating price discovery despite limited information.

The financial-analysis framework begins with accounting and distinguishes stocks, or levels of assets, from flows, or rates of change. Balance sheets measure assets and liabilities, while income statements measure wealth generated or lost over time. Corporate cash-flow decisions concern financing, investment in real assets, reinvestment of operating cash, distributions to investors, and risk management, with the objective of maximizing shareholder wealth. Lo asks students to apply the same framework to their personal finances, including education, consumption, borrowing, savings, financial investments, and risk.

Time and risk are presented as the features that make finance distinct from ordinary microeconomic analysis. The course will first address the time value of money through discounting and net present value, then introduce risk and eventually combine the two in modern finance. Six basic principles will be introduced: no systematic free lunches; a preference for more money, earlier money, and less risk, other things equal; and agents acting in their self-interest. The final three principles and the limitations of the framework will be examined later.

Course sections cover introductory material, valuation and the pricing of stocks, bonds, futures, forwards, and options; risk; and applications to corporate finance. Grading consists of a written case study worth 10%, attendance and participation worth 10%, a midterm worth 25%, and a cumulative final worth 55%. Optional problem packages will include solutions, and more than half of exam points are expected to come from those problems. Lo emphasizes active participation, reviewing lectures, working through problems both individually and in groups, reading assigned material, and attending the “Practice of Finance” seminar.

President Trump’s description of the House-passed health care bill as “mean” has unsettled some House Republicans he had pressed to support it. Trump had praised the measure after its 217-213 passage but wants the Senate version to be “more generous.” Senate GOP efforts to revise the bill are slowed by disputes among conservatives and moderates over Medicaid expansion, coverage requirements and subsidies. GOP leaders target passage by the July 4 recess, though Sen. John Cornyn said late July may be needed.

ARDD praised Jordan’s government, legal aid providers and UNHCR for rapidly establishing legal services in refugee camps, including juvenile courts, family protection and free documentation support. The report said these services protect refugees’ rights and enable education and healthcare, but challenges remain, including changing needs, funding shortages, limited evaluation of legal aid and procedures for refugees seeking formal employment. A registration campaign has documented 25,000 additional refugees.

This application continues a series of U.S. patent applications incorporated by reference. The disclosure describes a hardware database privacy device and differentially private security system for executing analytical queries against private databases without exposing record-level information. The system supports sensitive data from disparate sources, including health, financial, telecom, proprietary, and contractually restricted records.

Clients submit queries and privacy parameters, such as ε and δ, while each client has a privacy budget that is reduced when a query is accepted. Database managers may also impose maximum disclosure thresholds. The security system includes a user interface, software library, account management, query handling, data integration, and privacy modules. It verifies query commands, transforms them into function and database-access commands, merges required data from one or more databases, and sends the resulting data and query instructions to the privacy system.

Privacy engines provide differentially private responses for counts, medians, means, variances, interquartile ranges, general linear models, random forests, histograms, classification-model testing, synthetic databases, and query validation. Techniques include perturbing counts and model outputs with Gaussian, Laplacian, or Cauchy noise; using smooth sensitivity for selected statistics; perturbing loss functions or gradient updates; and modifying random-forest leaf proportions. Histograms can be perturbed through count queries or private wavelet decomposition. Model testing recursively identifies decision thresholds and generates corresponding confusion matrices. Synthetic databases are generated through differential-privacy-preserving projection with fewer features while retaining approximate spatial relationships among entries. A validation engine tests whether submitted queries satisfy the specified differential-privacy definition and can reject noncompliant queries.

The overall process identifies the requested data and operations, accesses the data, modifies the operations according to the selected privacy level, executes them to produce a differentially private result set, and returns that result to the client for display. The described components may be implemented in software, firmware, hardware, or combinations thereof on processor-based systems.

Moody’s said India’s government could still meet its 3.3%-of-GDP fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019 by curbing capital spending, despite revenue and spending risks. A Moody’s-ICRA poll found most respondents in Singapore and Mumbai expected slippage and viewed higher oil prices as a major economic risk.
Sensors reveal how greater noctule bats snatch birds at night; a mist-netted bat held a passerine feather and bloodied mouth.

The MSPM0C1105/MSPM0C1106 data sheet warns that ESD can cause performance degradation or complete device failure and recommends appropriate handling precautions. Revision A, revised September 2025, updates power and package information, removes DGS32 package data, revises technical specifications, CPU features, ADC ENOB, and DEVICEID/USERID tables, and adds a debug section. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information covers package drawings, dimensions, thermal-pad soldering, optional vias, solder coverage, stencil design, tape orientation, lifecycle status, RoHS, moisture-sensitivity/reflow ratings, and part markings. TI provides technical resources without warranties, and users remain responsible for product selection, design validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements.

TyreWatch, a predictive tyre-management system, launched on 16 May at Harwell Innovation and Science Campus in Oxfordshire. Research cited in the passage found that three-quarters of tyre failures result from under-inflation or debris penetration.

TyreWatch monitors tyre pressure and temperature using wheel-rim sensors, transmitting data via cellular and satellite connections to a central server for real-time analysis, portal access and push notifications. Its only driver-facing display is a dashboard warning light. The server compares data against vehicle-specific baselines and recommends corrective action when concerning trends emerge.

Slow pressure loss generates maintenance alerts and continued monitoring, while rapid deterioration triggers critical alerts. The system also checks vehicles every 15 minutes after use, potentially detecting debris punctures before the next working day. It supports multi-brand fleets, integrates with manufacturer technology and third-party telematics, and is available as software or a complete retrofit.

Under testing, it reportedly prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns. It was developed by the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium, which received £1.2 million in Innovate UK funding for intelligent tyre telematics.

Attacking a box-and-one “horns” alignment uses double mid screens to free a star ballhandler, who can go either way, drive against an outnumbered defense, or pass to a rolling screener or corner shooters. If the drive is stopped, the star can drop-pass to a cutter; in screen-and-pop variations, one screener pops while the other rolls. A reversal pass can initiate single/double continuity when no shot is available. Success requires coordinated screens, post-ups, communication, timing, defensive recognition, and experience. Teams should scout and anticipate defensive reads and counters, vary alignments and entries, and move players against weaker defenders. In box-and-one defense, four defenders cover zone areas while a “Chaser” focuses on denying the ball and rebounds.

Japanese government bonds firmed after a strong two-year auction, with bids 5.51 times the offering versus 3.82 previously. The two-year yield fell 1.5 basis points to -0.210%, while the 10-year yield was unchanged at 0.015%. The BOJ was to detail May bond purchases after reducing shorter-dated purchases in April. Kuroda said the bank could meet its yield target with less buying and remained noncommittal on bond-buying guidance. The BOJ left policy unchanged and expressed optimism about an export-led recovery.

Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh said the government is considering skill-development courses and an optional curriculum paper to provide students with vocational and technical knowledge. He praised women students’ entrepreneurship initiatives and urged colleges to upgrade skills and product quality.

A fired Washington Walmart employee returned days later to retrieve a safe he had allegedly tried to steal. Loss prevention found heroin and Xanax inside. He admitted the drugs were his and was booked for unlawful possession of a controlled substance.

A retrospective histologic review of 30 adrenalectomy specimens examined adrenal vessels from normal glands, cortical adenomas, and pheochromocytomas using H&E and immunohistochemical stains. Normal adrenal central veins contained distinctive asymmetric longitudinal smooth-muscle bundles with gaps, disorganized elastic layers, and uneven smooth-muscle myosin expression; these changes were morphologically indistinguishable from FMD lesions in renal or carotid arteries. SAM-like changes were common in tumor-associated vessels, including arterial hyalinization, foamy macrophages, intimal fibroplasia, and myxoid or fibrinoid medial degeneration. Pheochromocytomas also showed thin-walled arteries, reduced muscular tissue, and “blood lakes” lacking discernible endothelium. Hemorrhage and vascular thrombosis were the most common complications. No FMD-like lesions occurred in vessels outside the adrenal glands, and nine examined fetuses had normal adrenal vessels without asymmetric bundles or FMD/SAM changes. The findings support considering FMD and SAM as parts of a single morphologic spectrum and suggest that local adrenal hormones or hormone-receptor signaling may influence vascular injury and provide directions for further investigation of FMD.

The address expresses gratitude for abundant harvests, peace, and preserved civil and religious liberty. It reports generally improved foreign relations: the Russo-Ottoman war is expected to remain limited; French indemnity claims remain unresolved but may receive favorable consideration; and the northeastern boundary dispute with Great Britain has been referred to the king of the Netherlands as umpire. Growing commerce with France and Britain is noted, while British colonial restrictions are criticized for harming British shipping and burdening both American producers and colonial consumers. A treaty with Austria is ready for signature, reflecting the longstanding American policy of liberal trade, reciprocity, and the abolition of discriminatory duties.

Relations with neighboring American nations remain generally friendly but unsettled. Treaties with Mexico are unfinished, civil war in Central America and political changes in Colombia and Peru have hindered commerce, and the peace between Buenos Aires and Brazil is welcomed, along with partial payment of American claims.

The nation’s finances are described as favorable. Estimated 1828 receipts were $24.09 million against expenditures of $25.64 million, leaving about $5.13 million in the Treasury on January 1, 1829. More than $12 million was applied to public debt, reducing annual interest payments by over $500,000. European harvest shortages created a temporary foreign market for American grain, and the revenue for 1829 was expected to equal or exceed that of 1828, permitting further debt reduction.

The address discusses British trade restrictions and the recent protective tariff, finding no clear revenue decline yet but stressing that any tariff burdening one section of the Union should be revised without weakening protection for domestic industry. It warns against conflict between federal and state authorities and calls for constitutional harmony.

Reports also cover military discipline, Indian affairs, fortifications, roads, canals, river and harbor improvements, and West Point. The government’s acquisition of Indian lands created obligations to provide subsistence, while successful efforts at education and Christianity produced communities asserting rival sovereignty; a remedy balancing justice with federal and state territorial rights is recommended. The Navy suppressed piracy, protected neutral commerce, improved shipbuilding and yards, and prepared a Pacific survey expedition. The Post Office expanded greatly since 1792. Congress is also urged to complete a penitentiary, resolve Ghent Treaty claims, extend land-payment terms, and improve the forthcoming census, including earlier enumeration, broader age categories, better manufacturing returns, and greater compensation for census workers.

Donna Adelson was convicted in the 2014 murder-for-hire plot that killed her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel. At sentencing, she denied participating, claimed there was no evidence against her, and said she would have stopped the plot had she known of it. Judge Stephen Everett said he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.” Adelson received life in prison for murder plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. Prosecutors alleged the family wanted Markel’s ex-wife and children to move to South Florida.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 26, 2021, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference except by specific reference. The filing also included an embedded Cover Page Interactive Data File and was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.
Ammunition found in a Litchfield High School bathroom prompted a soft lockdown. Students were dismissed around 10 a.m. as police secured the school.

IDC expects public-cloud HPC to become the leading architecture among manufacturing enterprises using or considering HPC, followed by hybrid-cloud systems that handle peak loads while retaining sensitive workloads on-premises. Prebuilt HPC systems may remain attractive because they are easier to deploy and less failure-prone than customized systems. Organizations must choose between building in-house infrastructure and purchasing HPC services.

In-house clusters offer control and performance but face high upfront and maintenance costs, limited expansion, underutilization, downtime, and restricted flexibility. Public-cloud HPCaaS shifts spending from capital expenditure to operational expenditure, provides scalable and on-demand capacity, and supports occasional users and newer adopters. Hybrid architectures can preserve required security by keeping sensitive data in-house while using the cloud for noncritical workloads or demand spikes. Cloud HPC still requires trained personnel to configure virtual clusters, run calculations, and interpret results.

Manufacturing respondents consider performance, agility, cost optimization, security, and resilience major priorities. HPCaaS also provides access to current hardware and analysis methods, facilitates collaboration through shared databases and cloud workstations, and supports new business models such as selling simulations, predictive-maintenance services, or insights from digital twins. Of respondents already using HPC, 81% intend to implement HPC-based business models, 49% view HPCaaS as complete infrastructure outsourcing, and 42% see it as a way to use HPC without building their own infrastructure.

IDC concludes that HPC, simulations, modeling, and data analytics are becoming essential to manufacturing innovation and digital transformation. Recommendations include establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, adopting a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, evaluating on-premises, HPCaaS, and hybrid operating models, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and using external expertise when internal capabilities are insufficient.

The findings come from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology-related decision makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

A Boeing-funded study observed passenger movement and tested airplane surfaces and air for cold and flu viruses across 10 flights. Researchers found no viruses and only one coughing passenger, limiting broad conclusions. Mathematical modeling estimated that an infectious aisle-seat passenger would infect only one of about 150 passengers on average. The 11 passengers closest to the infected person had the highest risk. Window-seat passengers moved least often, while about 80% of aisle-seat passengers moved at least once. Researchers said staying in a window seat may reduce exposure, but outside experts cautioned that the small study cannot establish general infection risks. The study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

The SuperTrend is a trend-following indicator created by Oliver Seban that identifies trend direction, continuation, and possible reversals using price action and volatility. It appears as a line above or below closing prices, with green and red phases representing upward and downward trends. A close crossing the prior SuperTrend value reverses the indicator’s direction.

Its calculation combines a candle’s median price, \((H+L)/2\), with Average True Range (ATR). The upper and lower bands are calculated as median price plus or minus a multiple of ATR. The displayed indicator alternates between these bands, with restrictions preventing the lower band from decreasing and the upper band from increasing. ATR measures volatility, so the line widens as volatility rises and tightens when volatility falls. The article identifies SuperTrend as a lagging indicator because its signals derive from historical prices.

The article’s 60-year, weekly, long-only backtest of the S&P 500 used a 10-period ATR and multiplier of 3, with all capital reinvested and no commission, slippage, or reinvested dividends. Across 38 trades, the reported win rate was 65.79%, described elsewhere as approximately 67%, while maximum drawdown was 24.6%, compared with 56.24% for buy and hold. One example trade gained 44.46%. These results were presented as evidence that the strategy captured market upswings while limiting downswings, although the authors note that performance depends on market direction, asset class, timeframe, and parameters.

SuperTrend can be applied intraday, daily, or weekly, with the article favoring weekly time frames for its backtest and recommending testing to determine suitability. It can also be adapted to ranging markets by adjusting its lookback period or multiplier and monitoring price crossovers, range boundaries, and reversal behavior. Potential benefits include clear signals, noise filtering, straightforward entry and exit guidance, and support for stop-loss and trailing-stop placement. It may be combined with moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, oscillators, price-action analysis, and risk-management methods for confirmation.

The article also acknowledges limitations: SuperTrend is lagging, can produce false signals or whipsaws in volatile or choppy markets, and may perform poorly on instruments lacking sustained directional trends. Its success rate can vary, making comprehensive backtesting across different conditions essential.

The passage examines baseball’s growing reliance on relievers and bullpens, with the Yankees as a leader. The team gave Aroldis Chapman a five-year contract as closer and paired him with Dellin Betances, continuing a practice dating to Joe Torre’s era. As bullpen use has increased, starting pitchers have averaged fewer pitches and often leave after about five innings, raising questions about whether costly starters earn their keep. Hall of Famer John Smoltz advocates pitching starters more, while MLB’s commissioner has considered reliever-use limits to reduce game delays and “dead time.”

Nathan Calvin, general counsel of the three-person AI policy nonprofit Encode, accused OpenAI of using subpoenas tied to its lawsuit against Elon Musk to intimidate critics of the company’s restructuring and California AI-safety work. Calvin, who says Encode is not Musk-funded, said an August subpoena demanded his private communications on SB 53; Encode was also served and refused to provide documents. Encode had filed a court brief supporting some of Musk’s arguments.

Calvin alleged that OpenAI sought to weaken SB 53 by favoring compliance credit for existing federal safety agreements or international frameworks such as the EU AI Code of Practice. The signed law requires frontier-model developers to publish safety frameworks and transparency reports, report critical safety incidents, and share catastrophic-risk assessments.

OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon said subpoenas are standard litigation tools and raised questions about Encode’s undisclosed funding and potential collaboration with commercially interested parties. The allegations drew support from former OpenAI personnel, AI safety researchers, and Tyler Johnston of The Midas Project, whose organization and he also received subpoenas. Calvin praised OpenAI’s safety research but said its alleged intimidation tactics conflicted with its mission.

The message reports that the country is at peace, national defense remains effective, industrial conflict has declined, and education, science, and public health have advanced. General and infant mortality rates declined through 1932. Private organizations and state and local authorities continued providing winter relief, while Reconstruction Finance Corporation loans to states were intended to prevent hunger and suffering from cold.

The worldwide economic depression continued, worsening after the European collapse and producing acute financial crises. Emergency measures and expanded federal credit through the Federal Reserve System and Reconstruction Finance Corporation were credited with averting economic disaster and beginning to improve conditions by July. The Corporation supported banks, railways, agriculture, industry, and borrowers, while assistance to Farm Loan Banks, Home Loan Banks, and Agricultural Credit Associations made funds available to the public. Federal spending for public works, agricultural and financial relief, and unemployment assistance increased substantially between 1930 and 1933.

The message identifies three priorities for restoring confidence and promoting recovery: reduce government expenditures and balance the federal budget; reorganize the banking system; and cooperate economically with foreign governments. The proposed budget would reduce appropriations by more than $830 million, although uncontrollable expenditures would rise by about $250 million. Federal construction spending was planned at $442.769 million, compared with $717.262 million for the current year, with greater reliance on self-liquidating projects financed through loans. The furlough system would continue, supplemented by a temporary 11 percent reduction on government salaries above a $1,000 exemption. Certain veterans’ payments would be eliminated, while uniform manufacturers’ excise taxes, except for necessary food and possibly some clothing, were proposed to broaden federal revenue. Executive orders would consolidate more than fifty agencies.

The banking system was criticized as inadequately organized and unable to respond effectively to the crisis. Bank failures increased sharply after 1930, contributing to currency hoarding, restricted credit, business failures, unemployment, and losses of savings, homes, and farms. Because failures had subsided and the acute phase had passed, comprehensive reform was urged. Such reform should improve regulation, organization, and safe practices without currency inflation or direct government operation of banks. Federal farm loan and joint stock land bank systems also required changes.

International economic cooperation, world disarmament, and organized world recovery were presented as essential to domestic prosperity. The message supported the World Disarmament Conference and World Economic Conference, sought greater trade and international monetary stability, and proposed methods for addressing temporary foreign exchange difficulties related to war-debt payments.

Additional legislative priorities included transportation and power regulation, antitrust laws for natural-resource industries, western range conservation, federal aid for child health, World Court membership, ratification of the Great Lakes–St. Lawrence Seaway Treaty, and revisions to bankruptcy laws and federal court procedure. The message concluded that government should preserve ordered liberty, maintain individual and local responsibility, regulate rather than compete in economic life, limit emergency intervention, and encourage voluntary private cooperation in responding to social and technological change.

Case Western Reserve University researchers estimate that the federal government spends about $55 billion annually on the effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence. Their study, published in The Journal of Family Violence, links such exposure to higher health-care costs, increased violent crime, and reduced productivity. An estimated 15.5 million children are exposed annually. By age 64, the average lifetime national economic cost associated with exposure approaches $50,000 per person. Researchers say quantifying these costs may help policymakers support more effective prevention and treatment.

The court denied plaintiffs’ request to enjoin NASD Regulation, Inc.’s Rule 8210 demands requiring on-the-record interviews of D.L. Cromwell Investments, Inc. and four employees. Plaintiffs argued that Regulation was acting as the government’s agent and was coercing them to testify despite Fifth Amendment protections, while also allegedly using grand jury materials in a private regulatory investigation.

Although Regulation’s Criminal Assistance Prosecution Unit cooperated with federal prosecutors and had inadequate physical and administrative separation from the Division of Enforcement, the court found no direct evidence that government officials encouraged or coerced the Rule 8210 demands. Crediting Regulation’s evidence, the court concluded that the demands arose from an independent DOE investigation into Cromwell and trading in Pallet Management Systems, Inc.

The court also found no credible evidence of a violation of Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 6(e). The two questioned documents were likely obtained through a federal search warrant, and plaintiffs failed to establish that they constituted matters occurring before a grand jury or were disclosed to unauthorized Regulation personnel. Accordingly, the Rule 8210 interviews would not be enjoined. The court nevertheless advised Regulation to strengthen controls separating CPAG from the DOE.

The Shepherd Express criticizes We Energies’ high rates, executive pay, and management of its regulated monopoly. It attributes rising rates to a compliant Public Service Commission approving requests tied to overbuilt power plants and shareholder returns of more than 10%. The passage contrasts We Energies with customer-owned municipal utilities that often charge less and credits former CEO Charlie McNeer with holding rates low through cost-control policies. We Energies has proposed a rate freeze through 2019, supported by the Metropolitan Milwaukee Association of Commerce, while the Citizens Utility Board and the new Initiative for Competitive Energy argue that rates should instead be rolled back.

Canadian Blood Services will open Canada’s largest donation clinic at Eau Claire Market on July 10, featuring 20 beds and replacing its 18-bed 13th Avenue clinic. With O-negative blood critically low, the agency is seeking 150,000 donations by July 1, short by 50,000, and plans a new Calgary operations facility for 2020.

F2 Logistics faces Generika-Ayala in the resumption of the 2018 Chooks to Go-PSL Grand Prix, aiming for a fourth straight victory and the No. 2 seed. Generika-Ayala earned its first win by defeating Smart in five sets over the weekend. Sta. Lucia meets winless Smart earlier, with both matches crucial to playoff positioning.

Prince’s catalog became available on Spotify despite his opposition, prompting debate among fans and artists reluctant to stream. Taylor Swift removed her 2014 album, arguing music has value; Garth Brooks keeps his music off Spotify and iTunes and will release his next album on his website. Thom Yorke condemns Spotify despite Radiohead’s presence, Beyoncé keeps “Lemonade” off Spotify because of Jay Z’s Tidal, and Joanna Newsom criticizes major labels.

Market Research Future published a global blowout preventer market report, segmented by type, well type and region, with forecasts through 2021. Rising oil and gas demand, unconventional-source exploration, offshore drilling and stricter safety standards are cited as growth drivers. The report analyzes market structure, pricing, supply chains, competitive forces, historical and forecast revenues across six regions, country and segment trends, and major players’ strategies and developments. It targets manufacturers, suppliers and R&D firms. The Middle East is expected to dominate due to increased onshore drilling, while Asia-Pacific is projected to grow rapidly.

Lake Lugano, just west of crowded Lake Como, offers a quieter alternative in Switzerland’s Italian-speaking canton of Ticino. Visitors can enjoy palm-lined promenades, cafés, art, markets, local cuisine, alpine scenery, and uncrowded hillside villages such as Gandria, Morcote, and Mont Bré. Recommended experiences include ferry trips, cruises, hiking on Monte San Salvatore and Monte Generoso, visiting parks and botanical gardens, and tasting Ticino’s merlot. The area’s appeal lies in its relaxed pace, cultural mix, and small moments rather than major attractions.

Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale expressed sorrow but no panic after a van attack in Toronto killed 10 people and injured 15. They said there was no apparent link to terrorism or national security, while stressing that the homicide investigation was still underway. Both praised first responders for their courage and professionalism, with all levels of government participating. Police arrested 25-year-old Alek Minassian, who was scheduled to appear in court.

The passage presents licensing terms for a proposed specification and the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 for SD Memory Cards.

If the proposed specification implements, incorporates, or references portions of versions 1.0 or 1.01 of the SD Specifications, adopters must obtain appropriate licenses from SD-3C, LLC. Host-device implementations require an SD Host Ancillary License Agreement, while memory-card implementations require an SD Memory Card License Agreement. The Simplified Specification/Addendum is a non-confidential subset of the SD Card Association’s specification, provided “AS-IS” without warranties. It disclaims responsibility for resulting damages or patent infringement, grants no implied patent or other rights, and creates no obligation to disclose confidential technical information.

The specification defines the physical interface, command protocol, operating environment, and handling of SD Memory Cards. Related documents cover audio and file-system applications, mechanical form factors, UHS-II, embedded devices, Mc-EX functionality, and SDIO cards. The SDIO specification is separate but maintains mechanical, electrical, power, signaling, software, and memory compatibility with SD Memory Cards. SDIO cards are intended to provide high-speed, low-power I/O and are ignored by hosts that do not support them.

SD Memory Cards support read/write or fixed-content ROM configurations, user and protected storage areas, and multiple capacity classes: SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC above 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC above 32 GB through 2 TB. Standard operating voltage is 2.7–3.6 V; UHS-II also specifies VDD2 at 1.70–1.95 V. Security features include SDMI-compliant content protection, mutual authentication, cipher-based protection, nonsecure access to user content, optional ISO-7816-based support, password locking, and permanent or temporary write protection.

The host controls communication through addressed and broadcast commands, responses, and data transfers over SD or SPI buses. Commands are 48 bits with CRC protection, while block data uses 16-bit CCITT CRC. Transfers may use single or multiple blocks and one or four data lines, with busy and status signaling on DAT0. Card registers include OCR, CID, CSD, RCA, optional DSR, SCR, SD status, and card status.

Bus modes include Default Speed, High Speed, SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, SDR104, DDR50, and UHS-II modes. UHS-I uses 1.8 V signaling for its higher speeds, requires four-bit operation, supports CMD6-based bus and driver selection, and uses CMD19 for sampling-point tuning where required. UHS-II initialization includes PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization, with support for FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624 modes. FD624 is also identified as the enhanced UHS-II mode, or UHS-III, and reaches 624 MB/s.

The card operates in identification and data-transfer modes. Identification uses CMD0 for reset, CMD8 to verify operating conditions, ACMD41 to establish operating voltage and capacity support, CMD2 to obtain the CID, and CMD3 to publish the RCA. Data-transfer operation includes selecting a card with CMD7, exchanging CSD information, configuring optional driver strength, reading and writing blocks, erasing, locking, switching functions, and stopping transfers with CMD12.

Additional features include speed, video speed, and application performance classes; cache; host- and card-initiated self-maintenance; command queue operation; extension functions for power management and performance enhancement; low-voltage initialization; and switch control over bus speed, command system, drive strength, and power limits. The document also covers card hardware, electrical characteristics, power-up sequences, ESD requirements, SPI transactions, and appendices covering terminology, tuning, power delivery, extension functions, application performance, and mechanical dimensions.

European stocks opened slightly higher Tuesday, lifted by energy shares as Brent crude reached a 30-month high after the leaking Forties pipeline was shut down. Investors awaited decisions from the Fed, Bank of England and ECB.

Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen said recent stock gains did not qualify as a bubble, but warned that asset valuations were elevated and urged investors to diversify. She called the U.S. economy and job market strong, noting unemployment at 4.1%, and expressed disappointment that she would not serve a second term.

In *Hogg’s Estate*, the majority affirmed the auditing judge and held that the unqualified term “grandchildren” in the testator’s will included all grandchildren, including the two children of a deceased afterborn child. The majority emphasized that positive testamentary language controls, disinheritance requires express words or necessary implication, and “per stirpes” determined shares without limiting the beneficiary class. It rejected the argument that the will should be confined to the children of the four named children and dismissed the exceptions, confirming the account absolutely.

Steakne, J., joined by Sinkler, J., dissented. The dissent argued that the testator’s intent at the time the will was executed governed, and that the will’s overall scheme contemplated only the issue of the four named children. Although the statute revoked the will partially in favor of three afterborn children, the dissent believed it should not also extend the testamentary gift to their issue. It would have sustained the exceptions, concluding that the majority’s construction produced an unjust distribution by allowing the claimants to receive half the trust while the three grandchildren of the named child received one-sixth each.

Dunas Capital Asset Management is a Madrid-based Spanish asset manager founded in 2016, serving local and international institutions with financial and real-estate investment strategies. It reported approximately €4.5 billion in assets under management as of July 2025, more than 80 professionals, and supervision by Spain’s CNMV and DGSFP.

The firm emphasizes capital preservation, absolute returns, multi-asset flexibility, bottom-up value investing and strict risk controls. Its risk-first approach uses volatility-based risk budgets to compare asset classes and adjust portfolios, while options and futures help mitigate tail risk.

Four non-indexed mutual funds share the same management team, philosophy and investment process but differ in risk and return targets: Dunas Valor Prudente, with about €1.5 billion under management, targets 12-month Euribor plus 100 basis points and 3% maximum volatility; Equilibrado targets plus 200 basis points and 6%; Flexible targets plus 400 basis points and 10%; and Audaz targets plus 600 basis points and 15%. The firm also offers alternative investments in infrastructure, renewable energy, transportation and agriculture.

Dunas cites independence, transparency, flexibility, innovation, experience and sustainability as its founding principles, with its capital held by independent partners. The passage also describes Pan Finance as a global financial-intelligence publication with more than 200,000 readers across 150 countries and includes numerous repeated business, finance and technology headlines.

The passage contains AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block Specification Agreement and technical specification. The agreement permits recipients to review the specification solely to design compatible products and optionally provide feedback, while prohibiting duplication, removal of notices, or transfer of rights. AMD provides the specification “AS IS,” disclaims warranties and liability, may use voluntary feedback without restriction or obligation, and requires compliance with applicable export laws. California law governs, with disputes to be brought in Santa Clara County.

The specification standardizes a 4 KB, page-aligned, decrypted GHCB for communication between SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. It defines Automatic and Non-Automatic Exits, guest and hypervisor responsibilities, required GHCB state, VALID_BITMAP handling, VMGEXIT processing, and a 4 KB GHCB MSR protocol for negotiation, CPUID data, GPA registration, feature advertisement, page operations, and other requests.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, malformed-input error codes, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page-state notifications, the Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC. It also covers SNP guest and extended requests, certificates, AP creation and SMP booting, termination requests, restricted injection doorbells, IPIs, and timers, plus SNP secrets and CPUID pages. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The budget proposes computing capital gains on transfers of unlisted shares using prescribed fair market value, likely calculated under the net asset value method. If consideration is below fair market value, the difference is deemed additional consideration, affecting startup and investor share sales.

The Dogs of the Dow (DOD) strategy selects the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks among the 30 components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Investors hold equal dollar amounts in those stocks and rebalance annually on the last trading day of each year. The strategy aims to beat the DJIA through high-yield, blue-chip stocks and has historically appealed to income investors.

The concept originated in 1951 through H. G. Schneider’s price/earnings-based stock-selection approach and later appeared in The Wall Street Journal. Michael B. O’Higgins named the strategy in his 1991 book, *Beating the Dow*. Investors can use individual stocks, ETFs such as SDOG, IDOG, and EDOG, or mutual funds; ETFs may offer a cheaper alternative to building the portfolio directly.

Backtests indicate recent underperformance. Since August 1998, a $10,000 investment with reinvested dividends grew to about $32,000 under DOD, versus $60,000 in the S&P 500, with CAGRs of 5% and 7.7%, respectively. From April 2014, $10,000 grew to $19,000 in SDOG, $11,600 in IDOG, $11,200 in EDOG, and $23,300 in SPY. SDOG performed best among the listed ETFs, but all underperformed the S&P 500. The passage recommends limiting DOD to a small portion of assets because of poor diversification.

Former Katsina State Governor Ibrahim Shehu Shema was remanded in Economic and Financial Crimes Commission custody over alleged N5.7 billion money laundering involving SURE-P funds. He pleaded not guilty to 26 charges. Justice Babagana Ashigar ordered his detention until April 27, 2018, when the court would hear his written bail application, which the prosecution opposed.

FULE logically erases the entire user area via CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 (arguments 00000002h). Hosts must check FULE_SUPPORT; if unsupported, they must not issue FULE and the card executes ERASE. Sequence errors set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR; other out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_RESET. FULE supports SDHC/SDXC, not SPI, and holds DAT0 low during operation.

The study developed COVIDFast, a laboratory-developed, RNA extraction-free RT-qPCR assay for rapid, high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 testing using anterior nares swabs (SwabFAST) or saliva (SalivaFAST). It combines specimen-specific preparation buffers, proteinase K treatment, and standardized collection kits to bypass the conventional extraction step, which is laborious, costly, susceptible to contamination and human error, and dependent on extraction supplies. Bar-coded 2 mL cryovials, automated decapping, and electronic pipetting support high-throughput processing. Swab samples use a TBE-based viral transport buffer, while saliva samples use a TCEP-containing preparation buffer. Viral transport buffer remained stable across tested storage conditions and durations.

Analytical testing found similar qualitative and quantitative results for extraction-free and extraction-based RT-qPCR. The detection limit for both specimen types was established at 4 copies/µL, with all 20 replicates testing positive. In split-sample clinical comparisons, swab assays showed 100% positive and negative agreement between methods; saliva assays showed 98.8% positive and 99.4% negative agreement.

Against SalivaDirect, SwabFAST had reported positive and negative agreements of 83.3% and 99.4%, respectively, while SalivaFAST had 95% positive and 100% negative agreement. By December 23, 2021, COVIDFast had processed 409,883 tests, with an overall positivity rate of 8.10%; SwabFAST accounted for 83.62% of tests and SalivaFAST 16.38%. The system produced results within 24 hours of sample receipt at volumes exceeding 5,000 tests per day. The authors proposed extending the extraction-free platform to other viruses, bacteria, and fungi.

A June 26, 2001 compilation of California energy coverage focused on Gov. Gray Davis’s response to the state’s electricity crisis. California opened confidential, FERC-ordered settlement talks in Washington seeking $8.9 billion in refunds for alleged overcharges between May 2000 and May 2001. Roughly 150 representatives of generators, utilities, municipalities and Western states attended. Generators denied overcharging, said prices reflected gas shortages and credit risks, and claimed California utilities owed them billions. FERC administrative law judge Curtis Wagner, who estimated refunds might reach only $2–$2.5 billion, urged compromise and said he would recommend a solution if no agreement was reached by July 10.

The negotiations also addressed the refund period, long-term power contracts, creditworthy electricity buyers, PG&E’s bankruptcy, natural-gas prices and pipeline capacity, and possible protection for generators from future liability. New FERC commissioners Patrick Wood and Nora Brownell met with Davis and state leaders, held hearings on natural-gas costs and promised a more cooperative federal approach. Other Western states reportedly sought up to $6 billion in additional refunds.

Former Duke Energy employees alleged that the company discarded spare parts and reduced output during Stage 3 alerts to manipulate supply and prices. Duke denied wrongdoing, said its actions followed orders from the Independent System Operator and supported spinning reserves, and another former employee corroborated some allegations. Davis praised the employees and asked federal regulators to investigate possible price gouging, natural-gas costs and the requested refunds.

State officials sought to suspend or restrict direct access to alternative electricity providers, warning that customers leaving traditional utilities could increase costs for remaining customers and jeopardize the state’s roughly $50 billion in electricity purchases and a planned $13.4 billion bond sale. Direct-access enrollment had fallen from more than 200,000 to about 88,000 by mid-May. Supporters argued that customer choice remained central to deregulation and proposed legislation using exit fees to protect the bond sale.

A review of 42 pending California power plants questioned whether all would be built or provide competitive prices, despite plans to obtain 70% of the state’s long-term purchased power from them. Concerns included price-cap loopholes, ownership concentration, alleged past pricing practices, political threats to projects, financing uncertainty and dependence on future natural-gas costs.

The compilation also examined solar-powered housing in San Diego. Falling photovoltaic costs, utility subsidies and high power bills were encouraging builders to integrate solar into subdivisions, lowering installation costs and household electricity use. Builders remained cautious because of buyer preferences, legal concerns, limited manufacturing capacity and uncertain federal policy. Net-metering restrictions and the state’s emphasis on natural gas were also described as obstacles to broader solar adoption.

In February 2018, the S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index rose 6.3% year over year, up from 6.1% in January. The 10-City and 20-City Composites increased 6.5% and 6.8%, respectively. Seattle led the 20 cities with a 12.7% annual gain, followed by Las Vegas at 11.6% and San Francisco at 10.1%.

Before seasonal adjustment, the National Index rose 0.4% month over month, while both composites gained 0.7%. Seasonally adjusted, the National Index increased 0.5%, and both composites rose 0.8%. All 20 cities recorded monthly gains on both bases.

National home prices had increased continuously for 70 months as of February, averaging 6% annually. The previous 182-month run, from January 1992 through February 2007, averaged 6.1% annually. David Blitzer said continued economic growth and employment gains were expected to support further price increases.

Seattle recorded the largest employment and home-price gains, while Chicago and Cleveland ranked near the bottom. Home-price growth in San Francisco and Los Angeles substantially exceeded that implied by employment gains, while Miami posted relatively modest price growth despite above-average employment gains.

The National Index stood at 197.01, 47.0% above its February 2012 trough and 6.7% below its July 2006 peak. The 20-City Index was 0.1% below its peak, while the 10-City Index was 2.5% below its peak. The indices are revised for the previous 24 months and are published monthly using non-seasonally adjusted headline data, with seasonally adjusted data also provided for analysis.

Coach Quenneville said his team was encouraged by its performance against Anaheim but remained focused on improving for the next game. He described the playoffs as difficult, noting a tough divisional race, hard series, and a seven-game conference-final loss, while praising the team’s resilience, preparation, consistency, and depth. He credited a core group that sets the tone for teammates, along with deadline acquisitions and contributions from newer players. He called Hossa a complete, consistent, speedy puck-control specialist whose understated style deserved more recognition, and praised Kimmo for his reliability, defense, support of the attack, and stability on the back end. Quenneville emphasized team accountability, communication, learning from experience, and adjusting as the game evolves without overthinking the outcome. Players should focus on each shift and the opponent rather than getting ahead of themselves. He said the team would maintain its routine, seek a strong start, and require every player to remain ready. He also identified forechecking, puck movement, speed, and pace as areas for continued improvement.

In *Betteys v. Ætna Life Insurance Co.*, Dr. William H. Betteys died after an injured hand developed an infection, and his wife sought death benefits and weekly disability indemnity under his accident policy. Ætna denied liability for the death benefit, claiming he died of disease, recalled its death-proof forms, and later rejected the proof submitted. The court held the company’s letters admissible on the issue of waiver of proof requirements. Its denial of liability excused timely proof of death and cause, but did not waive or estop it from enforcing the separate contractual deadline for filing suit. The plaintiff’s delay barred the death-benefit claim, warranting a directed verdict for Ætna. The weekly-indemnity claim required a new trial. The judgment was reversed, with costs awarded to Ætna.

Austria’s FMA raised its forecast for Heta Asset Resolution wind-down proceeds to €8.6 billion, citing strong asset sales. The €2.6 billion boost benefits the state and Carinthia; roughly half of Heta’s €8.1 billion cash balance was expected to be paid to creditors.

A preliminary inquiry into the alleged robbery-related 2017 murders of pensioners Phyllis Caesar and Constance Fraser continued before Principal Magistrate Judy Latchman. Imran “Christopher” Khan, Steven Andrews and Phillip Suffrien are charged. Four police witnesses testified and were cross-examined by Khan and Andrews; the inquiry continues Monday.

The paper proposes a hybrid deep learning framework, DNN-Transformer-AE, for corporate tax risk supervision and risk level assessment, addressing limitations of manual and rule-based supervision which struggle to scale and capture concealed, dynamic risk patterns. The model combines three modules: a DNN that models static enterprise attributes (firm size, industry, registered capital, ownership structure) through fully connected layers with nonlinear activations; a Transformer that embeds financial and taxation time series with positional encoding and multi-head self-attention to capture long-range temporal dependencies; and an Autoencoder that compresses concatenated features into a latent representation and reconstructs them, flagging anomalies when reconstruction error exceeds a threshold. Outputs are fused and mapped via fully connected layers to a risk score classified into high, medium, or low risk using predefined thresholds.

Prior work cited spans rule-based methods, machine-learning tax risk assessment, and deep-learning anomaly detection, including a two-layer deep-learning forecast of quarterly taxable-input risk, an optimized gated LSTM platform (97% accuracy), the MALDIVE network-mining framework for the Italian Revenue Agency, and an unsupervised pipeline for flagging under-reporting declarations without labels.

The dataset comprises real corporate tax declarations and financial records for approximately 12,000 enterprises across manufacturing, retail, and internet services, with expert-assigned risk labels, covering static features, quarterly time-series indicators, and tax behavior; it was preprocessed and split 70/15/15 with temporal stratification. Evaluation used Accuracy, Recall, and Macro F1, with emphasis on Macro F1 given limited and imbalanced high-risk samples. The hybrid model achieved 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 F1, outperforming logistic regression (0.79/0.68/0.70), random forest (0.84/0.75/0.77), XGBoost (0.86/0.77/0.79), and DNN-LSTM (0.89/0.82/0.85). Training and validation loss converged near 40 epochs at approximately 0.05, with validation loss consistently below training loss, indicating stable convergence and generalization.

The framework is presented as a tool for regulators to stratify firms, allocate supervisory resources, and give firms actionable feedback for self-remediation. Limitations noted are the restriction to financial and operational indicators without macroeconomic or inter-firm data, and computational complexity for resource-constrained tax offices; future work suggests adding macroeconomic and policy data and developing interpretable, lightweight models such as attention-based visualization or model compression.

The passage presents a theoretical framework for orbital degrees of freedom in strongly coupled magnon–phonon systems. It identifies ambiguities in conventional orbital angular momentum definitions for massless magnons and phonons and introduces orbital angular moment based on Bloch-wavefunction quantum geometry. In magnon–polarons, orbital contributions arise from global lattice rotation and the self-rotation of hybridized wavepackets, allowing orbital degrees of freedom to exist even when lattice rotation vanishes.

Using a two-dimensional Néel-ordered honeycomb antiferromagnet with magnetoelastic coupling, the study shows that hybridization breaks the combined inversion and time-reversal symmetry and couples magnon and phonon bands. This enables transfer of intra-band orbital angular momentum between magnon- and phonon-dominated states, while interband transitions produce an additional orbital contribution. Out-of-plane phonons can thereby acquire orbital angular momentum and spin moments despite their linear polarization.

The resulting magnetic-dipole transport generates electric polarization and a transverse voltage containing spin-Berry-curvature and orbital-moment contributions. For the MnPS₃ example, magnon–phonon coupling makes the orbital contribution dominant, enhances polarization by five to six orders of magnitude relative to the DMI-only case, and produces microvolt-scale voltages that increase with temperature and coupling strength and persist at zero temperature. The findings provide a basis for electrical control and detection of magnon–polarons and connect magnon and phonon orbitronics.

The specification defines SD memory-card tuning, transfer, storage-management, command, and error-handling behavior. CMD19 sends a fixed tuning block for sampling-point optimization, compensating for host/card-specific static timing delays. It is mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD, optional for HOST-SDR-FD, legal only in the unlocked Transfer State with 1.8 V signaling, and otherwise treated as illegal. A tuning sequence consists of consecutive CMD19 executions, with 40 executions completed within 150 ms.

During Card Identification Mode, the host remains at fOD; fPP may be used in Data Transfer Mode. CMD9 retrieves the CSD, optional CMD4 configures driver strength and switches the clock, and CMD7 selects one card for Transfer State. Selecting RCA 0x0000 returns all cards to Stand-by. Data communication is point-to-point with the selected card. Read and write transfers can be stopped with CMD12. Writes may enter Programming State, with DAT0 held low while busy. Block writes may be buffered, but CSD, protection, and erase operations are not buffered. CMD7 can disconnect a busy card without interrupting programming or erase, while CMD0 or CMD15 terminates pending programming and may destroy data.

Reads use CRC-protected blocks. CMD16 block length is limited to 512 bytes; CMD17 reads one block and CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12. Address, block-length, and misalignment errors abort transfers as specified. SDHC and SDXC cards use block addressing, fixed 512-byte blocks, and do not permit partial or misaligned access. A 2 GB card uses 1024-byte READ_BL_LEN/WRITE_BL_LEN values, while CMD16 remains limited to 512 bytes for compatibility.

Writes transfer CRC-protected blocks, reject invalid lengths, addresses, CRC failures, and write-protected areas, and may use ACMD23 to pre-erase blocks. ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks. CMD13 can poll write status, and separate CMD/DAT lines permit interleaved operations on multiple cards.

Erase ranges are selected with CMD32 and CMD33 and executed with CMD38. Out-of-sequence commands reset the erase sequence and set error status bits; protected sectors are skipped. Erased data may be either 0 or 1 as defined by the card. DISCARD is supported by SDHC/SDXC cards outside SPI, makes discarded content undefined, and has a 250 ms busy timeout. FULE logically erases the entire user area, has a one-second busy timeout, and falls back to ERASE when the full range is not specified.

Write protection may be mechanical, internal, or password-based. CMD42 sets, replaces, clears, locks, or unlocks passwords stored in nonvolatile PWD/PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP/FEP_LEN registers for Card Ownership Protection (COP). Locked cards accept only specified command classes and cannot access data. COP cards require CMD42[1Fh] after reset when FEP is set and then operate in CMD42 version 2.0 mode. Force Erase and FEP Force Erase erase user data and PWD information under specified password and card-state conditions; force erase does not erase the secure area and leaves the card locked until completion. Errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED, and lock-state changes are reported through CARD_IS_LOCKED. Locked cards reject ACMD6 bus-width changes.

CMD55 designates the immediately following command as an ACMD. Defined and undefined legal ACMDs are distinguished by the APP_CMD response bit, while illegal ACMDs generate an illegal-command error. Several ACMD numbers are reserved for proprietary use.

CMD6 switches functions through Mode 0 queries and Mode 1 setting operations. Six function groups contain selectable branches, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. The response status reports supported functions, resulting selections, busy states, and maximum current or power consumption. Invalid selections cancel the switch, while busy functions cannot be changed. CMD6 uses a predefined 512-bit status block, requires no block-length command, and permits new bus behavior after the specified clock delay. The default power limit is 0.72 W, with removable-card power capped at 1.80 W; UHS-II requires the power-limit function.

High-Speed mode optionally provides 25 MB/s using a 50 MHz clock and requires one card with one-to-one CLK/CMD/DAT connections. CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57 support optional command-system extensions selected through CMD6. CMD8 checks host voltage before ACMD41 and returns an R7 response echoing the voltage and check pattern when supported.

The host may reduce or stop the bus clock, subject to initialization and post-transaction clock requirements. CRC7 protects commands and most responses, while CRC16 protects each data block. A failed command CRC prevents execution and response; an illegal command also leaves card state unchanged. Read and write operations have defined timeout limits, including 100 ms minimum reads and 250 ms maximum busy time for High Capacity card writes.

The IMF urged Saudi Arabia to phase in fiscal consolidation and price increases gradually, warning that rapid reforms could hurt growth amid low crude prices. Despite three years of deficits totaling $200 billion, the IMF expects this year’s deficit to narrow to 9% of GDP from 17.2% in 2016. Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 aims to reduce oil dependence through measures including higher energy and water prices, excise taxes and expatriate labor fees. The government plans a 5% VAT next year and hopes to balance its budget by 2019, while the IMF recommends doing so by 2022.

The study couples a DFT-parameterized embedded cluster expansion (eCE) with canonical Monte Carlo simulations and a canonical-ensemble statistical-mechanics framework to compute finite-temperature equilibrium vacancy concentrations in concentrated refractory alloys. For a nine-component group 4/5/6 bcc alloy, the selected 4-eCE model reproduced DFT formation energies with an RMSE of about 7.7 meV/site. Its vacancy predictions agreed with grand-canonical Monte Carlo while requiring far fewer samples.

Vacancy concentrations depend strongly on composition, bonding, and short-range order. Group 5/6-only alloys have approximately \(10^{-7}\) vacancies near 2000 K, while adding group 4 elements can increase concentrations by roughly 10–100-fold. About 50–60% group 4 content is predicted to yield \(10^{-4}\)–\(10^{-5}\) vacancies at 1500°C. Hf and Zr preferentially occupy the first-neighbor shell around vacancies, while Mo favors the second. Unfavorable Cr-W-like bonds increase vacancy concentrations, whereas favorable Nb-W-like bonds reduce them; these binary ordering trends persist in concentrated alloys.

Single-special-quasi-random-structure calculations differed from Monte Carlo vacancy formation energies by approximately 0.2–0.3 eV and underestimated equilibrium concentrations by factors of 3 and 7 for Cr-Ti and HfNbTaTiZr. Some compositions also exhibit phase transitions or separation, requiring caution at lower temperatures. The framework enables alloy design for targeted vacancy concentrations but assumes dilute vacancies and neglects vibrational free-energy contributions and vacancy clusters.

Value area trading uses volume profiles to identify the price range in which 70% of total trading volume occurred during a specified period. These areas can indicate potential support and resistance and buying or selling opportunities. The strategy is commonly used in futures but can also apply to stocks, forex, and intraday, daily, weekly, or monthly charts.

Traders may use value-area levels to set stops and profit targets, confirm other signals, and identify breakouts above or below the area, rejections and reversals, or bullish and bearish divergence using stochastic, RSI, and MACD.

Risks include false signals, changes to the value area over time, and relying on it without other factors. Suggested risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, discipline, and avoiding emotional decisions. The passage introduces a backtest but provides no results and notes that meaningful testing requires explicit trading rules and settings.

The passage highlights a report that Iowa’s largest school district superintendent, described as a well-known state figure, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. It also presents a digest of The 74’s education journalism, including school integration and equity, college access, COVID-19 effects, Every Student Succeeds Act implementation, women in STEM, and school finance. Additional headlines cover vaping, meals, New Orleans schools after Katrina, Indigenous-language preservation, Supreme Court rulings, English-language policy, youth achievements, and featured documentaries. The page also promotes newsletters and a tax-exempt donation.

The court held that a conveyance by extent is subject to the same construction rules as a conveyance by deed. Because the debtor owned the land and buildings, the extent transferred the barn and blacksmith’s shop to the creditor regardless of whether they had permanent foundations. The execution returns described the land without reserving the buildings, so parol evidence that the creditor’s attorney intended to exclude them was inadmissible and properly rejected. Tenant-built structures associated with trade are exceptional to the rule that an owner’s buildings pass with the land. The court affirmed the verdict awarding the plaintiff the buildings’ value.

A Danish study found that children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis had higher risks of rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid disease, and epilepsy. Researchers recommend increased clinical attention to these children’s development.

Astronomers, students and citizen scientists are preparing for next week’s total solar eclipse, described as the best in the U.S. in nearly a century. Its narrow path will run from Oregon to South Carolina. Researchers will use telescopes, cameras, binoculars, three planes, more than 70 high-altitude balloons, the International Space Station and 11 satellites to study the sun’s corona, space weather and effects on Earth’s weather, animals and plants.

NASA and the National Science Foundation are spending about $7.7 million on eclipse projects. Citizen CATE has trained more than 200 volunteers using identical small telescopes at 68 sites, while other projects invite animal observations through iNaturalist, zoo behavior tracking and photos or videos for the Eclipse Megamovie 2017.

Scientists note that eclipses enabled the 1868 discovery of helium on Earth and provided the 1919 evidence supporting Einstein’s prediction that starlight bends around the sun.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 reported unaudited GAAP financial statements. Third-quarter revenue was $35.021 billion and net income was $10.752 billion, compared with $30.571 billion and $8.809 billion a year earlier. For the nine months, revenue was $104.982 billion, net income was $33.079 billion, and diluted EPS was $4.30. At March 31, total assets were $285.449 billion, including $137.626 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, while total debt was $66.610 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $42.002 billion, with $10.697 billion spent on property and equipment, $17.177 billion used for share repurchases, and $11.272 billion paid in dividends.

The three reportable segments generated nine-month revenue of $34.646 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $34.995 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $35.341 billion for More Personal Computing. Third-quarter commercial cloud revenue rose 39% to $13.3 billion, with reported growth of 25% for Office 365 Commercial, 47% for Dynamics 365, and 59% for Azure.

Microsoft described COVID-19’s net third-quarter revenue impact as minimal but said future effects remained uncertain. The notes addressed investments, derivatives, debt, leases, taxes, contingencies, unearned revenue, and upcoming accounting standards. Deloitte & Touche reviewed the interim financial information and identified no material modifications needed for GAAP conformity.

A study of 1,099 college students followed from age 18 found that continued energy drink consumption was associated with greater later use of cocaine or prescription stimulants for nonmedical purposes. Even occasional use was linked to increased stimulant use, while those who stopped consuming energy drinks were less likely to develop substance-abuse issues. Researchers said the findings suggest energy drinks may contribute to heightened substance-use risk but do not explain the link, which needs further study.

The passage describes a continuation application, with earlier disclosures incorporated by reference, concerning video coding and decoding. It explains intra-picture prediction, including the evolution of directional prediction from nine modes in H.264 to 33 in H.265 and up to 65 in JEM/VVC/BMS, and the coding of prediction modes, submode parameters, and directional information.

The disclosed methods and apparatuses encode or decode a block using intra prediction information. For a directional mode, the coding information indicates a nominal mode and an angular offset. The nominal mode supplies a nominal angle, while the offset can be calculated from an offset integer and a step size; their sum determines the prediction angle. The nominal mode, independently of the angular offset, maps to a transform-set mode identifying a set containing one or more non-separable transforms. A signaled non-separable transform index selects a transform from that set, which is used with the directional mode to reconstruct the block.
