The passage documents AMD AGESATM core software and its UEFI PEI/DXE integration. It defines early- and post-initialization PPIs, a memory-information HOB, post-reset PEIM duties, and reset coordination among chipset and processor PEIMs. Memory is not generally available until the standard EfiMemory PPI is posted. The CPU DXE driver calls AmdInitLate to generate data tables and publishes AgesaDxeProtocol, while a separate driver conditionally enables iGPU VGA decoding based on PciIo requests.

Build guidance covers reference and control files, platform options, IDS support, required environment variables, and indirect binary-module versus integrated source builds. It describes x86-64 stackless Cache-as-RAM routines, early silicon macros, and restrictions on modifying cache controls during CAR; AArch64 systems with PSP rely on the PSP for DRAM initialization.

The documented APIs include reset, early processor initialization, memory initialization, environment/HOB transfer, late table generation, and S3 save/resume routines. Utility interfaces support structure allocation and release, DIMM data-eye and FRU lookup, APIC and PCI address queries, execution-cache sizing, MMIO range allocation, and event-log access. Required host call-outs provide buffer allocation, deallocation, and lookup, cold or warm resets, SPD reads, and task execution on application processors.

Best Buy is discounting Lenovo’s Legion 7i Gen 10 by $220, reducing the price to $1,650. It features a color-accurate 2,560 × 1,600 OLED screen, a 115-watt RTX 5060, and an excellent keyboard and trackpad, but its high-power GPU provides under five hours of battery life.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on February 1, 2018, reporting its fourth-quarter and year-end 2017 financial results. The filing incorporates Exhibit 99.1, the results press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information on non-GAAP financial measures.

The Jerusalem Post seeks $5 monthly subscriptions as traditional business models are unsustainable. Benefits include an almost ad-free experience, Premium and Hebrew-learning content, Jerusalem Reporter stories, and an Israeli-style ePaper.

Alek Minassian, 25, made his first court appearance and was charged with 10 counts of first-degree murder for driving a rental van into pedestrians on Toronto’s Yonge Street, killing 10 people and injuring 15. Authorities said the attack did not change Canada’s threat level or preparations for June’s G7 summit. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau urged Canadians to remain united and safe as the motive was investigated. Memorials and tributes grew as victims were identified, the Canadian flag was lowered to half-staff, and the CN Tower went dark.

U.S. airlines recorded their best cancellation rate in 22 years of tracking in 2016, while mishandled baggage and involuntary passenger bumping fell to record lows. On-time arrivals rose to 81.4%, and Transportation Department complaints declined 11.3%.

Education for farmers should combine broad learning with practical agricultural knowledge, train productive citizens, foster cooperative action and respect for labor, and prepare students to shape public opinion. Farmers’ organizations provide economic and social benefits, while voluntary cooperation remains more effective than government assistance; however, the Department of Agriculture can support these organizations, coordinate state and federal programs, and expand practical education. Government-farmer cooperation has helped address the boll weevil and cattle fever tick, while irrigation and forest preservation have benefited the Rocky Mountains, Great Plains, White Mountains, and Southern Appalachians. Congress should fund preliminary work on an Arlington memorial amphitheater and assume authority over marriage and divorce to resolve conflicting state laws, protect family welfare, and address polygamy.

Oregon Health & Science University researchers reported limited success using somatic cell nuclear transfer with human cells, following the 2022 birth of three healthy mice from eggs created using adult skin-cell DNA. In a Nature Communications paper, the team described “mitomeiosis,” a process for reducing chromosome numbers to prevent embryos from having twice the normal complement. The technology requires further refinement before clinical testing but could eventually support infertility treatments, prevent heritable diseases, and enable same-sex couples to have genetically related children.

A small study of 19 mothers and their babies suggests dopamine supports mother-child bonding and caregiving. Mothers released more dopamine while watching their own babies, and higher dopamine responses were associated with sensitive, responsive care and adjustment to infants’ needs. Lower dopamine responses occurred among less-responsive mothers. Researchers said the process may continue throughout children’s lives and support nurturing relationships generally, but this remains unconfirmed. The findings may also help explain difficulties some mothers experience in caregiving. Researchers cautioned that the study’s small size limits generalization and cannot determine whether caregiving responsiveness causes stronger bonding or reflects mothers’ pre-existing tendencies. The study was published online in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

The article examines the prevalence and effects of trauma among postsecondary students and summarizes trauma-informed care (TIC) frameworks and educational practices for occupational therapy (OT) and other health professions education programs. Trauma includes direct and indirect experiences that may harm mental, physical, social, emotional, or spiritual well-being. Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are potentially traumatic events occurring before age 18. Estimates indicate that 50%–70% of postsecondary students have experienced at least one ACE, 30%–50% have experienced multiple ACEs, and 12%–20% have experienced four or more.

Trauma can affect attendance, concentration, memory, communication, engagement, self-efficacy, social relationships, and academic performance, while also increasing isolation and dropout risk. Indicators may include increased absences, fidgeting, aggression, dissociation, missed deadlines, risk avoidance, distrust, emotional dysregulation, and withdrawal. Environmental changes may also be triggering. Research involving OT students found that trauma affected daily routines, sleep, social participation, and education for 93% of participants, although many withheld their trauma histories from educators because of fear of stigma. Another study found generally low childhood-trauma scores among Canadian master’s-level OT students but identified possible minimization or denial in approximately 28%.

The review describes SAMHSA’s 2014 TIC framework, which seeks to restore safety, power, and self-worth and prevent retraumatization through organizational policies, procedures, and practices. Its six principles are safety; trustworthiness and transparency; peer support; collaboration and mutuality; empowerment, voice, and choice; and recognition of cultural, historical, and gender-specific issues. SAMHSA’s ten implementation domains address governance, workforce development, collaboration, financing, physical environment, engagement, screening and services, quality assurance, policy, and evaluation. Institutional leadership, faculty training, inclusive policies, safe learning environments, referral networks, survivor and student involvement, peer support, and ongoing evaluation are identified as essential elements.

Educational practices include trauma-sensitive curricula, self-assessment and self-care instruction, survivor-informed content, advance notice of potentially triggering material, classroom check-ins, predictable routines, transparent communication, equal participation, positive feedback, student choice in communication, culturally responsive and universally designed instruction, de-escalation techniques, and faculty reflective practice. Simulation-based PATH training improved OT students’ knowledge, self-efficacy, hope, and understanding of ACEs and TIC. Peer-delivered health and wellness coaching may also support stress management, resilience, and healthy coping.

The literature search covered peer-reviewed publications from 2015 onward, with selected older foundational sources, using PubMed, Google Scholar, and the American Journal of Occupational Therapy. The review concludes that OT curricula have limited trauma content and recommends that educators evaluate and strengthen trauma-informed practices to create supportive learning environments and improve student well-being, engagement, retention, and academic success.

National Journal’s June 8, 2001 CongressDailyAM reported on congressional spending, elections, legislation, and committee activity.

- **Appropriations:** House Appropriations subcommittees received $661.3 billion in proposed FY2002 discretionary spending, compared with President Bush’s $660.6 billion request. Allocations exceeded Bush’s requests for Labor-HHS by $3 billion, VA-HUD by $1.1 billion, and Energy and Water by $1.2 billion, while defense and transportation received less than requested. House leaders said they would support Bush’s roughly $7 billion FY2001 supplemental request, which includes $6.1 billion for defense offset by $505 million in cuts, despite demands for additional military spending. Senate officials indicated similar support, and the White House threatened a possible veto if Congress substantially raised the total.

- **House leadership and bipartisanship:** House Republicans said Democratic control of the Senate would give them more freedom to pass energy, prescription drug, campaign finance, patient-rights, trade-authority, and possibly tax-cut legislation before the August recess. Republican moderates reported greater White House sensitivity to diverse viewpoints. Democrats and some conservative Blue Dog Democrats continued to criticize House Republicans for limited consultation and cooperation.

- **House races:** Republican Rep. Steve Largent announced he would resign his Oklahoma seat on November 29 to run for governor and requested an early special election to avoid leaving the district unrepresented. The seat was described as strongly Republican, though Tulsa school board member Doug Dodd appeared likely to become the Democratic nominee.

- **Judiciary and legal liability:** Rep. Asa Hutchinson’s expected departure for the Drug Enforcement Administration left a prominent House sponsor of legislation limiting business liability and punitive damages. Senate Democrats’ control of the agenda was expected to complicate action on product-liability and class-action reforms, though bipartisan support among small businesses and future White House efforts could aid narrower measures.

- **Labor:** Labor Secretary Elaine Chao planned three public forums on workplace ergonomics and a September course of action. House Republicans praised the process, while Democrats and the AFL-CIO continued to seek a new protective rule after Congress overturned the Clinton administration’s regulations.

- **Health:** FDA officials told Congress that roughly two million packages of regulated personal-use products entered the United States annually by international mail, far exceeding inspection capacity. They warned that imported drugs could be contaminated, counterfeit, improperly stored, or otherwise unsafe, prompting bipartisan calls to tighten rather than loosen reimportation rules. Separately, the House Energy and Commerce Committee remained open to generic-drug patent reforms in a Medicare prescription-drug bill, despite concerns from brand-name drug makers and Republican Sens. Orrin Hatch and Edward Kennedy.

- **Trade:** European officials said Bush’s Section 201 steel-import investigation could disrupt the upcoming EU-U.S. summit and reflected growing concern about U.S. unilateralism. They also resisted linking steel problems to imports and described joint global-warming and Kyoto Protocol negotiations as especially difficult.

- **Senate organization:** Republican negotiators and Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle were close to agreement on an organizing resolution and assurances concerning the prompt consideration of Bush’s nominees. Democrats had not drafted the proposal directly but had negotiated its general concepts, and both sides described the process as smooth.

- **Other political developments:** Bush nominated Republican administrator Jo Anne Barnhart, subject to Senate confirmation, to lead the Social Security Administration. Republican members of the Census Monitoring Board released a report asserting the 2000 census was highly accurate and questioning statistical sampling. House Transportation Committee leaders scheduled a hearing on airline customer-service improvements and prepared to vote on limited antitrust immunity for airline scheduling. House Republicans introduced the National Monument Fairness Act, requiring public and state input for monuments larger than 50,000 acres and allowing such proclamations to expire if Congress did not approve them within two years.

- **Congressional schedule:** The newsletter listed hearings and events through Thursday on energy policy, transportation, drug access, government efficiency, foreign affairs, science legislation, fisheries, telecommunications, campaign finance, defense, and other subjects. The House held a pro forma session, and the Senate expected no votes.

AMC Entertainment’s management proposed doubling authorized shares to 1.1 billion, risking further shareholder dilution. Despite debt refinancing and adjustments, net debt exceeds $3 billion and Q3 box-office revenue was weak. Ongoing losses, negative equity, and persistent cash burn keep AMC’s valuation at a steep discount to peer CNK. The pandemic severely affected AMC as attendance plunged and releases were delayed. The passage also includes the author’s background, investment disclaimers, chart metadata, and entertainment-related headlines.

The passage reviews Robert Stuart’s investigation into BBC Panorama’s “Saving Syria’s Children,” which relied on footage of alleged casualties from an incendiary bombing at Urm al-Kubra school near Aleppo and treatment at Atareb hospital. Stuart’s presentation identifies disputed injuries, inconsistent victim totals ranging from 25 to 50, and major discrepancies in the reported timing of the attack. It also questions statements by BBC personnel and medical professionals, including Dr Saleyah Ahsan and Dr Rola Hallam, and discusses their military, political, and charitable affiliations. The author argues that the injuries, chronology, and account inconsistencies indicate possible staged events and broader BBC collusion. It concludes by asking how similar questionable narratives should be assessed when they support interventionist or anti-government agendas.

pfhrp2/3 gene deletions threaten malaria control by causing false-negative results with HRP2-based rapid diagnostic tests. This study used an individual-based P. falciparum transmission model, WHO Malaria Threat Maps data, and country-level risk factors to assess the global selection and spread of deleted parasites. The model tracks deleted and wild-type parasites through human and mosquito hosts and incorporates diagnosis, treatment seeking, adherence, RDT use, HRP3 cross-reactivity, and fitness costs.

Two risk maps were developed. The Innate Risk Score estimates how quickly deletions would spread after establishment, assuming HRP2-based diagnosis. The Prospective Risk Score models continued spread from current deletion frequencies and geographic connectivity. Model fitting to Eritrean and Ethiopian data estimated pfhrp2-deleted parasites’ relative fitness at 96.4% and the probability of an HRP2-based positive result despite pfhrp2 deletion at 29.0%. Globally, 63.5% of pfhrp2-deleted samples also had pfhrp3 deletions; in Africa, the estimate was 61.2%, with strong linkage between the deletions.

Malaria prevalence was the leading determinant of selection, with selection generally stronger below 20% prevalence. The Innate model predicted that 73 of 106 modeled countries would have at least one administrative region reach a 5% rate of clinically relevant false negatives within 20 years. High-risk regions included the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa, while highly transmissive Central and Western African regions were predicted to have slower spread. The prospective model predicted that 29 of 49 African countries had already reached or would reach the threshold within 20 years, with likely southward spread from the Horn of Africa and increases in Senegal and Mali.

Uncertainty was substantial, particularly because malaria prevalence and surveillance data were incomplete, international spread was modeled simplistically, and future prevalence and treatment assumptions were held constant. The maps are intended to guide surveillance, prioritization of alternative RDT deployment, and further research, while acknowledging that additional longitudinal data are needed.

Researchers combined somatic cell nuclear transfer (a cloning step) with fertilization and the chemical roscovitine to make human egg cells from adult skin cells (fibroblasts), reported September 30, 2025. Replacing an egg's nucleus with a skin-cell nucleus left the cell with 46 chromosomes; unlike mouse eggs, it did not shed half its chromosomes after fertilization, so roscovitine was added to trigger that division. Some fertilized eggs developed into early human embryos (blastocyst stage, about six days), but many failed and none had correct chromosome sets, so none were viable (one had 48). Amato called it proof-of-concept; the team is working to improve chromosome division. The technique could eventually help women without eggs and same-sex male couples, but is too inefficient and risky for clinical use, with trials perhaps a decade away and likely outside the U.S., which prohibits genetic modification of human embryos. It also requires donor eggs, though Hayashi called it a significant breakthrough in halving the human genome.

A July 31, 2001 IEP News compilation covers California’s electricity crisis and related policy disputes. Commentary by State Controller Kathleen Connell and economist Peter Navarro argued that the Davis administration’s $43 billion in long-term power contracts created billions in unnecessary “stranded costs,” following $8 billion in short-term state purchases and a planned $12.4 billion bond issue. They attributed improving conditions to cooler weather, conservation, reduced demand and federal price caps, and urged greater public oversight of energy decisions.

The SEC began a preliminary inquiry, requested by Secretary of State Bill Jones, into whether Davis administration consultants used inside information to trade in power-company stocks. Five consultants were fired over possible conflicts, and spokesman Steve Maviglio disclosed his $12,000 Calpine investment and Enron holdings. Consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo state compensation and leave the administration after working for Southern California Edison and facing conflict-of-interest litigation.

California’s proposed bailout of financially troubled Southern California Edison remained stalled because legislators could not agree on terms. Davis’s close ties to the utility, which claimed nearly $4 billion in debt and sought state help to avoid bankruptcy, drew criticism, while consumer advocates opposed a rescue. The state’s long-term contracts were also criticized for favoring fossil-fuel development.

San Francisco placed two public-power measures on the November ballot, including creation of a municipal utility district or citywide power agency. PG&E opposed the proposals, while supporters said locally governed public utilities would offer more control and potentially lower rates.

Federal regulators limited potential California electricity refunds to about $3.9 billion, less than half the $9 billion sought, and Davis planned to appeal. Elsewhere, Maryland regulators considered Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed separation from Constellation amid concerns about $2.4 billion in debt, while Texas began a limited electricity-deregulation pilot ahead of full implementation in January.

The lecture distinguishes the protein-folding problem—determining the 3D structure a protein adopts—from protein design, which seeks a sequence that produces a desired structure for applications such as drug development. A mechanical model treats a protein backbone as a chain or tree with fixed bond lengths and angles; motion consists of rotating connected segments around edges. Amino acids, energy, and biological folding forces are deliberately omitted.

Four geometric problems are examined:

- **Span:** Maximizing or minimizing endpoint distance. Minimum and maximum span among flat fixed-angle chains are NP-hard through reductions from partition. The complexity of general 3D versions remains open, although maximum span for orthogonal chains can be computed in linear time.
- **Flattening:** Determining whether a chain has a flat, non-self-intersecting configuration is NP-hard. Important special cases, including equal-length chains, remain unresolved.
- **Flat-state connectivity:** The configuration space of a fixed-angle chain may be disconnected, leaving flat states unable to reach one another. Whether every open chain is flat-state connected is open. Orthogonal and obtuse chains are connected, as are some acute chains with equal angles or particular length constraints. A partially rigid fixed-angle tree provides a disconnected counterexample, proved using topology.
- **Locked chains:** Additional constraints can prevent a linkage from moving. Fixed-angle chains can be locked, and models appear to provide equilateral, equiangular examples, though a formal proof was still pending. Producing a chain that is simultaneously equilateral, equiangular, and obtuse remained open.

Because proteins are produced through a ribosome tunnel and may fold while emerging, the lecture introduces a cone model of “producible” chains. New links emerge through a cone’s apex; outside it, chains may not self-intersect, intersect the cone, or reenter. For chains with suitably bounded turn angles, all producible configurations lie in one connected component, and all flat states are producible and flat-state connected.

Canonical configurations and reverse-production motions provide algorithmic paths between such states. The cone model is therefore proposed as a candidate mechanical algorithm for protein folding, although it does not explain the actual forces by which nature folds proteins.

Newark police seek public help locating nine suspects in seven unsolved crimes dating to June 2016. The cases include a Broad Street shooting, an armed grocery robbery involving three suspects, two other robberies, and a shooting that injured three people. Tips may be submitted through Crime Stopper hotlines, the department’s website, or its smartphone app; tips are confidential and may earn rewards.

Gas colic is common and generally less serious than other colic, but trapped gas can cause intestinal distension, severe pain, and complications such as displacement or twisting of the large colon. Gas is produced normally when microbes ferment plant fiber in the hindgut. It accumulates when large-colon motility is impaired.

Risk factors include inadequate forage, stall confinement, stress, ulcers, intestinal inflammation, insufficient exercise, dehydration, and abrupt feed or forage changes. Forage restriction can cause acid accumulation, rapid gorging, ulcers, and reduced hindgut motility, while confinement slows the muscular contractions needed to expel gas.

Prevention centers on making forage available continuously, providing pasture turnout or other regular movement, reducing stress, and changing feeds gradually. Hay transitions should take about a week, new fortified feeds two to three weeks, and bran should be introduced consistently and gradually. Slow feeders can promote calm, natural feeding and help horses self-regulate intake. The article also discusses prebiotics, B vitamins, yeast, and colostrum as possible supplements, and recommends limiting sugar, soy products, preservatives, and other inflammatory ingredients in commercial feeds. Juliet M. Getty, Ph.D., an independent equine nutritionist, provides additional equine nutrition resources through her website and publications.

Asus launched the Zenfone 5Z in India at Rs. 29,999, Rs. 32,999 and Rs. 36,999 for 6/64GB, 6/128GB and 8/256GB variants. It features a 6.2-inch notched FHD+ display, Snapdragon 845, Android Oreo, dual rear cameras and a 3,300mAh battery. It will be sold exclusively through Flipkart from July 15.

Richard Helzer was convicted by jury of two counts of gross indecency and, after the same jury considered the evidence, of being a sexually delinquent person. He received five peremptory challenges for the gross-indecency jury, although a sexual-delinquency conviction could result in imprisonment for life. The Court of Appeals ordered a new trial, and the Michigan Supreme Court reversed that order in part.

The Court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not an additional element of the principal offense or merely a penalty enhancement. Because the delinquency determination involves broad factual and expert findings and could expose the defendant to life imprisonment, it must be heard by a separate jury unless the defendant waives a jury trial. The second jury must be empaneled immediately after conviction on the principal charge and is entitled to 20 peremptory challenges; the initial jury receives only the challenges appropriate to the principal charge.

The sexual-delinquency charge must be included before trial on the principal charge begins, although the indictment or information may be amended before trial. The principal jury must not be informed of the delinquency charge; if it learns of it, that may justify a mistrial or reversal. The gross-indecency trial itself was error-free, so the Court affirmed those convictions and remanded only for a separate-jury hearing if the prosecution pursued the delinquency charge. If it did not, or if the defendant was acquitted on that charge, only the principal sentences would be imposed. Constitutional claims were left for later consideration. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, stating that the sexual-delinquency statute was unconstitutionally vague and that the procedural issues therefore need not have been reached.

On March 27, 2017, underwriters exercised their full option to purchase an additional $127.5 million principal amount of Tesla’s 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022. Tesla issued the option notes on March 30 under a supplemental indenture. Tesla also entered additional note hedge transactions, paying approximately $26.6 million, to reduce potential common-stock dilution and offset potential excess cash payments upon conversion. It issued additional warrants to hedge counterparties for proceeds of approximately $6.9 million, allowing purchase of up to approximately 0.8 million common shares at a $655 strike price, subject to adjustments. The warrants were sold under Securities Act Section 4(a)(2), are separate from the notes, and confer no rights on note holders.

The American Cancer Society’s updated guideline recommends regular colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults starting at age 45, using a high-sensitivity stool-based test or structural exam according to preference and availability. The qualified age-45 recommendation reflects rising incidence among younger adults, favorable modeling results, and expected screening performance similar to that among adults screened starting at 50. Screening at age 50 and older remains a strong recommendation. Options include annual FIT or HSgFOBT, mt-sDNA every three years, colonoscopy every 10 years, CT colonography every five years, and flexible sigmoidoscopy every five years, with no option prioritized. Positive non-colonoscopy tests require timely colonoscopy follow-up. Healthy average-risk adults with life expectancy over 10 years should continue screening through age 75; decisions at ages 76–85 should be individualized, and screening should be discouraged after 85.

European prompt power prices fell as wind supply increased and demand eased; 2019 forwards tracked lower coal prices. The outlook remained bearish amid improving French nuclear output and an expected demand drop. Carbon was flat, while gas and oil prices rose.

The University of Manchester Students’ Union launched Earth Week with a panel featuring Friends of the Earth campaigner Asad Rehman and Campaign Against Climate Change’s Martin Empson. Rehman emphasized climate change’s impact on developing countries and climate-related displacement, calling for legal protection and greater justice. Empson urged participation in environmental and migration movements through protests, petitions, contacting MPs, or donations to amplify their voices.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Turing introduced the first GPUs with GDDR6 memory, featuring redesigned high-speed interfaces, improved signal training, extensive clock gating, 14 Gbps signaling, and 20% greater power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X. Signal and power-integrity optimization reduced crosstalk by 40%. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice GP102’s 3 MB, and improved lossless memory compression. Together, GDDR6 and reduced memory traffic provide the RTX 2080 Ti with approximately 50% more effective bandwidth than the Pascal-based 1080 Ti.

Turing’s display engine supports higher resolutions and refresh rates, HDR, DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, 8K at 60 Hz, and two 8K displays with separate cables. It includes native HDR processing and BT.2100 tone mapping. The enhanced NVENC encoder supports H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps while saving HEVC and H.264 bitrates, and NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 HDR formats. Turing’s encoder is described as exceeding fast x264 quality with substantially lower CPU use.

Hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink allows a VR headset’s display, power, and tracking data to use one connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink rather than MIO or PCIe for SLI transfers. TU102 has two x8 links, while TU104 has one; each link provides 25 GB/s per direction. Two-way SLI is supported, while three- and four-way configurations are not.

RT Cores in each Streaming Multiprocessor accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing shader cores for other work. Turing supports hybrid rendering, using rasterization where effective and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other visually demanding effects. Denoising and advanced BVH structures reduce the rays required. With RT Core acceleration, Turing can exceed 10 Giga Rays per second and perform ray tracing about ten times faster than Pascal. The architecture supports NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, DirectX Ray Tracing, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API, and can accelerate physics, collision detection, particle simulation, audio, visibility queries, and path tracing.

NGX is Turing’s deep-learning stack, using DNNs and Tensor Cores for AI-enhanced graphics. Deep Learning Super Sampling produces TAA-like image quality with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X reconstructs target-resolution output approaching 64-times supersampling. Other NGX features include AI-based inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling. NGX is supported only on Turing and later architectures.

Mesh shading adds task and mesh shaders, replacing many individual CPU draw calls with parallel object-list processing. It supports dynamic level-of-detail selection and geometric cutaways and can increase the number of real-time objects by more than an order of magnitude. Variable Rate Shading independently controls shading by 16-by-16-pixel regions while retaining visibility sampling. Applications include content-adaptive shading for low-detail areas, motion-adaptive shading, foveated rendering, and increased shading rates with MSAA.

Texture Space Shading decouples appearance sampling from screen-space visibility, stores results in texture space, and reuses texels across frames or views. This provides temporal stability and can improve VR stereo rendering by reusing shading from one eye for the other. Multi-View Rendering supports four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views, expands Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection capabilities, and supports flexible view-dependent attributes. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, Tier 2 resource heaps, and mixed resource placement.

TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and a 256-bit memory interface. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, and supports neither NVLink nor SLI. The data-center Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, a 256-bit interface, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric that weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations according to their expected use in hybrid-rendering workloads. The document also explains ray casting, BVH construction and refitting, and denoising before closing with NVIDIA’s warranty, liability, licensing, trademark, and copyright notices.

American Girl will release its first male doll, Logan Everett, Thursday, as part of a new contemporary-character series. The $115 doll plays drums for Tenney Grant; Felicity Merriman returns, and filmmaker Z Yang and Nanea, a historical doll living in Hawaii during World War II, will debut in 2017.

Canada’s Privacy Commissioner is investigating Uber’s 2016 breach, which exposed data from more than 57 million riders and drivers. Uber concealed the breach and paid thieves $100,000 to delete the information. An Alberta class action is underway; the commissioner cannot fine companies but may seek Federal Court compliance orders.

Quantum spin relaxation in radical-pair systems is important for quantum computing, spintronics, quantum biophysics, and phenomena including organic semiconductors, molecular qubits, and avian magnetoreception. Major simulation challenges include ensemble averaging over randomly oriented room-temperature nuclear spins, exponential growth of Hilbert and Liouville spaces with the number of hyperfine-coupled nuclei, and stable propagation over nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales.

Existing full-quantum stochastic approaches face exponential scaling, while classical nuclear-spin treatments are generally accurate for high fields or systems with many nuclei but can be inadequate for significant non-Markovian hyperfine-mediated relaxation. Markovian models commonly integrate out ultrafast vibrational motion. Liouville-space methods avoid ensemble averaging and support arbitrary relaxation superoperators and Lindblad jumps.

The work introduces tensor-network approaches to radical-pair spin dynamics, including stochastic matrix product states, vectorised matrix product density operators, and locally purified matrix product states. Matrix product states reduce exponential state representations to polynomial scaling, while density-operator tensor networks reduce the number of matrix elements. Time-dependent variational principle methods permit evolution with long-range interactions, unlike TEBD, which is mainly suited to nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians.

The radical-pair model includes two electron spins coupled to surrounding nuclear spins and describes Zeeman, hyperfine, exchange, dipolar, and Haberkorn relaxation terms. Electronic singlet–triplet populations are the principal observables, with spin-selective reactions evaluated through a kinetic model using cumulative populations. The stated aims are to demonstrate achievable tensor-network simulations, clarify radical-pair modelling challenges for physicists, and highlight avian magnetoreception as a quantum-biological application.

A cave-rescue expert called the effort to extract 12 boys and their soccer coach from a flooded Thai cave one of the toughest he has seen. After rising floodwaters trapped them following practice, rescuers found them alive nine days later, 1.2 miles inside Tham Luang Nang Non.

He said the basic rule in flood rescues is to wait: if trapped people are alive and safe, rushing endangers rescuers, and if they have died, there is no justification for added risk. While waiting, teams can monitor water and weather, pump or divert water, search for other entrances, and use divers to make contact or deliver supplies.

The cave’s mid-70s temperatures would likely have caused hypothermia without preparation, while nine days without food left the group weak. Rescuers were introducing food gradually, and rebuilding their strength could take weeks.

Three main escape options were discussed: teaching the boys to dive out, which is extremely dangerous for novices; drilling a new entrance, which requires heavy equipment, detailed mapping or radiolocation and may miss the target; and waiting for monsoon floodwaters to recede, which could take weeks or months. If the group could remain safe from further flooding and receive food and care, they could stay underground; otherwise, risky diving might be the only option. Public pressure and fears of blame weighed heavily on rescuers.

Terry Rozier scored a career-high 31 points with seven rebounds, and Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 as the injury-depleted Boston Celtics beat the Atlanta Hawks 119-110. Rozier started for the second straight game with Kyrie Irving sidelined by a right quad contusion, following his first career start, a triple-double. Boston turned a 55-53 halftime deficit into a 19-point lead by outscoring Atlanta 41-20 in the third quarter. Jaylen Brown scored 19 and Al Horford added 17 points and seven assists for Boston, while Taruean Prince led Atlanta with 31 points and eight rebounds. Prince was also selected as an injury replacement for the Rising Stars game. Boston had not confirmed its reported signing of Greg Monroe.

President-elect Donald Trump drew attention on Twitter by calling the image of him on CNN’s book *Unprecedented: The Election That Changed Everything* “the worst cover photo of me,” while saying he hoped the book did well. The cover showed him pointing, and CNN also shared a commemorative 2017 edition featuring a different photograph. Reports described a growing list of Trump images he disliked, including photographs from his New Year’s Eve party. Other widely discussed posts included his brief follow of “Emergency Kittens,” his claim that canceled Hillary Clinton campaign fireworks signaled her loss, and a retweet of Ivanka Trump’s family photo montage. Twitter users mocked Trump’s complaint, called him vain, and urged him to focus on presidential matters.

Despite renewed economic growth and strong job availability, Bank of Japan sources say the bank is unlikely to quickly normalize its ultra-loose policy. Concern over a sharp yen appreciation, which could choke off the recovery and trigger political pressure, remains a major factor, while persistently low inflation makes tapering crisis-era stimulus premature. The BOJ may modestly raise yield targets and further slow asset purchases next year without starting a broad rate-hike cycle. Inflation must exceed 1% for many policymakers to consider hikes, and uncertainty over wages, inflation and Governor Kuroda’s April succession complicates timing. Prolonged easing could leave the BOJ with fewer tools against recession, while deeper negative rates or extreme intervention might be required if shocks emerge.

In an en banc decision issued March 5, 2013, the Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars a defendant from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered pursuant to a plea agreement that contemplated restitution up to a capped amount; any review must proceed through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings. The case arose from Frank Hoffman's prosecution for offenses arising from a traffic accident that injured another person. Hoffman pleaded no contest to DUI and agreed to pay restitution up to $53,653.45. The Tucson City Court adjudicated him guilty, imposed probation, and ordered fines, fees, and restitution to be set later but not to exceed the cap. About three months later, a contested restitution hearing produced an order requiring payment of $40,933.45. The superior court dismissed his appeal on the State's motion under § 13-4033(B) and Rule 17.1(e), and the court of appeals declined jurisdiction; the supreme court granted review to clarify the statute's scope.

Reasoning that statutes should be construed as a harmonious whole, the court treated the post-judgment restitution order as part of the "sentence" for purposes of § 13-4033(B). Doing so furthers the legislature's 1992 goal of reducing direct appeals arising from plea agreements, avoids a hybrid system of dual-track appellate review, and accords with the legislature's mandate of restitution for victims suffering economic loss. Subsection (A)(3) applies generally to post-judgment orders affecting substantial rights, while subsection (B) operates as an exception where such orders are entered pursuant to plea agreements. The court rejected Hoffman's arguments based on the State's ability to directly appeal such orders, the supposed redundancy of subsection (A)(3), his contention that contesting the amount took the order outside the plea agreement, and his concern that Rule 32 might not encompass such claims—noting that Rule 32 supplies the constitutionally guaranteed appellate review for pleading defendants. The court disapproved State v. Foy and State v. Unkefer to the extent they conflicted with this interpretation, and affirmed the dismissal of Hoffman's appeal.

This medRxiv preprint reports a blood-based test for detecting primary glial malignancy (GLI-M) in patients with intracranial space-occupying lesions. Peripheral blood samples undergo proprietary enrichment of viable circulating tumor or glial cells, followed by multiplex immunocytochemistry. Circulating glial cells are identified through co-expression of GFAP and OLIG2, with PanCK included in comparisons involving epithelial malignancies with brain metastases.

Analytical validation using spiked U87MG cells demonstrated a linear range of 5–1,280 cells per 5 mL, a detection limit of 1 cell per 5 mL, and an overall quantitation limit of 6 cells per 5 mL. Marker-specific sensitivities were 92.5% for GFAP and 95.0% for OLIG2, with 100% specificity. Drugs and elevated serum parameters did not significantly affect test sensitivity. Clinical samples could be stored at 2–8°C for up to 48 hours with no more than 15% cell loss.

In a blinded case-control test set of 57 samples, the test classified all 44 GLI-M and 23 benign brain tumor samples correctly. A second case-control study of 586 samples found all 40 GLI-M samples positive for circulating glial cells, while all 24 brain-metastasis samples were negative for these cells; benign brain tumor and healthy samples were also negative, yielding reported sensitivity and specificity of 100%. Two prospective cohorts of 68 and 31 patients reported sensitivities of 100% and 92.9%, respectively, with 100% specificity. FISH analysis of matched blood and tumor samples showed 100% concordance for EGFR copy status. Overall, the authors report greater than 99% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

The test reportedly detects common GLI-M subtypes regardless of age, sex, subtype, or grade, but does not detect CNS lymphoma or gliosarcoma and is not intended to determine subtype or grade. The study was funded entirely by Datar Cancer Genetics Private Limited, whose employees included many of the authors.

U.S. stock futures rose cautiously before the Fed’s rate decision, with economists expecting a 1–1.25 point increase and attention on Janet Yellen’s statement. Dow, Nasdaq-100, and S&P 500 futures gained 0.12%, 0.16%, and 0.06%. Apple confirmed autonomous-car plans; Tesla options volume rose; Micron rebounded after a bullish note.

Carleton University in Ottawa is hiring an Allan Slaight Chair to establish a research and teaching program in conjuring arts, with the possibility of tenure after a five-year renewable term. The chair will investigate how magic, perception and deception work, create a digital archive of information on magic, and develop graduate study and travel to magic archives worldwide. The position is supported by a $2 million grant from the Slaight Family Foundation, which Carleton is matching; about 80 applicants have applied, and an appointment is expected this summer.

A University of London experiment involving 120 participants examined how people explain a card trick. When the magician openly displayed an empty hand, only 60% identified the duplicate-card method, compared with 87% when the apparent swipe was not shown. Researchers suggested that constructing an initial explanation can make people less willing to abandon it, while magicians Michael Close and study leader Gustav Kuhn linked rationalization of puzzling tricks to how myths develop around misunderstood phenomena.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on July 31, 2018, reporting its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018. Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021 reported:

Gross margin was $54.243 billion, operating income was $41.488 billion, net income was $34.630 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.10, compared with $28.755 billion and $1.68 in the prior-year quarter. - Revenue by category was: iPhone $71.628 billion, up 9%; Mac $10.852 billion, up 25%; iPad $7.248 billion, down 14%; Wearables, Home and Accessories $14.701 billion, up 13%; and Services $19.516 billion, up 24%. Apple released MacBook Pro models with M1 Pro and M1 Max chips, third-generation AirPods and Apple Watch Series 7 during the quarter.
- Geographic net sales were: Americas $51.496 billion, up 11%; Europe $29.749 billion, up 9%; Greater China $25.783 billion, up 21%; Japan $7.107 billion, down 14%; and Rest of Asia Pacific $9.810 billion, up 19%. Segment operating income totaled $49.657 billion.

Adam Henrique and Travis Zajac said their opponent is a large, physical, deep team with puck-moving defensemen, four contributing lines, and strong puck-playing goaltending. Their team began nervously and tentatively, struggled to retain pucks, forecheck, win battles, and execute on dumps and routes, but improved later in the game. Both expect better execution and more success in the next game. Henrique’s return after missing most of the year has added leadership, depth, and four-line capability. They plan to focus on getting pucks behind the opposing defense, sustaining the forecheck, and generating offense through cycles, traffic, and shots.

U.S. stocks rallied after Donald Trump’s election on expectations of tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation, but gains in four “Trump trades” slowed after his inauguration. Hospital stocks, tied to repeal of Obamacare, fell 7.1% from election to inauguration, then recovered 4.1% as Republican healthcare efforts advanced unevenly. Six infrastructure stocks rose 13%, then gained 2.4% as no spending package materialized. The S&P 500 banks index jumped 20.8%, then added 3.1%, with slowing loan growth and doubts about deregulation weighing on the sector. The Russell 2000 gained 12.6%, then 5.3%, amid proposed tax reforms and concerns over Trump’s legislative ability and foreign-policy distractions.

The speaker credits his father, Patrick Kane, and coaches Don Harkins, John Hines, Dale Hunter and Dave Gagner for their support. He chose the OHL route, will play either wing or center as needed, and hopes Buffalo will soon win its first Cup. He admires Brière.

Former U.S. Senator and Anchorage mayor Mark Begich entered Alaska’s governor race as the sole Democratic candidate, prompting concerns that he and independent Gov. Bill Walker could split the vote and help Republicans. Begich said he would not run unless he believed he could win, while Democratic leaders maintain the party can win a three-way race.

The general election is expected to pit Begich, Walker and the Republican nominee. Conservative state Sen. Mike Dunleavy was an early GOP favorite before the Aug. 21 primary, while Libertarian William “Billy” Toien is also running. Walker and running mate Byron Mallott bypassed the primary to keep control of their ticket.

Dunleavy supports deeper deficit cuts, school choice and full oil-wealth fund dividends. Begich criticized Walker and lawmakers for budget gridlock and supports a constitutional formula for fund payouts. Walker reduced annual oil-fund payments in 2016, and the Alaska Supreme Court has allowed independents to participate in party primaries.

The Sixth Circuit affirmed Howard W. Ellzey’s conviction for conspiracy to illegally distribute controlled substances and eleven substantive counts of illegal distribution. Ellzey, a Memphis physician, routinely gave diet patients brief vitamin B-12 injections and amphetamine prescriptions, sometimes allowing patients to obtain prescriptions at both offices. A DEA survey showed that Ellzey wrote 29,000 of 39,000 Schedule II prescriptions, nearly all for amphetamine-type drugs. The court found substantial evidence supporting the convictions and rejected his challenges to the admission of his prescriptions, the indictment’s use of “distributing” rather than “dispensing,” the testimony, jury instructions, and juror examination. It concluded that he distributed illegal prescriptions on a large scale outside accepted medical practice.

The November 23, 2001 Energy Central Direct daily edition presents 85 electric-power articles, along with selected gas-industry and restructuring news. Leading stories cover Los Angeles retaining its share of a Nevada power plant, E.ON planning U.S. acquisitions, federal regulators restricting Southern Co. from charging unregulated wholesale rates, and FERC preparing a workshop to expedite 51 hydroelectric relicensing applications.

California coverage includes federal orders against preferential treatment of electricity buyers, assessments that supply may be sufficient but fiscal problems are worsening, developments in Pacific Gas & Electric’s bankruptcy, concern over possible cuts to the CARE discount program, and SMUD’s creation of its own transmission-control area.

At the first triple-header T20 Cayley Cup Finals Day at North Marine Road, Ebberston, Mulgrave and Ganton won the Premier, Division One and Division Two finals respectively. Ganton restricted Kirkbymoorside to 97-8 before reaching 103-1 in 10 overs; Ian Cousins made an unbeaten 40 and Robbie Milner scored 34. The author describes panic attacks beginning at age 19, a later panic disorder diagnosis, treatment through therapy and medication, and occasional recurring attacks. Experts clarify that “panic attack” is the clinical term for a sudden burst of intense fear lasting fewer than 30 minutes, while “anxiety attack” is informal; panic attacks associated with panic disorder typically have no obvious trigger, although specific fears can also provoke them.

Recognizing symptoms—including palpitations, sweating, shaking, shortness of breath, choking sensations, chest pain, nausea, dizziness, chills, tingling, derealization, detachment, and fears of losing control or dying—can reduce fear. A physical exam is recommended to rule out other problems.

Recommended coping strategies include recording reminders that panic attacks are not life-threatening and have been survived before, preparing positive and realistic rebuttals to catastrophic thoughts, visualizing panic as a wave that rises and fades, using smartphone games, music, or guided relaxation as distractions, and practicing slow, deep full-body breathing daily so it can be used during an attack to slow the heart rate and calm the body.

An exploratory analysis of the 2019 NSECE Household Survey examined information sources used by 1,190 households searching for child care and early education for a focal child under age 6 within the previous 24 months. Latent class analysis of the first two reported sources identified five search types: CCR&R/local organizations or friends and family (9%); internet search or social media (28%); known providers or friends and family (8%); social media or friends and family (20%); and friends and family or internet search (37%). Overall, 49% of families reported two sources and 51% reported one; friends and family were the most common source, followed by internet search.

Regression analyses found that only the search for information about type of care differed significantly across types. Families searching for a child with a condition affecting care provision were more likely to use the CCR&R/local organizations or known providers search types. Search types also varied geographically: known providers or friends and family searches were more common in the West, while friends and family or internet searches were more common in the Northeast. No relationships were found with the other search topics or most family and child characteristics.

Limitations include recording only the first two sources, excluding 79% of households that reported no recent search or considered only one provider, and an analytic sample that was higher-income, more often had two working parents, and was more often English-only than the full survey population.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses 40 GB of HBM2 memory organized across five active stacks, delivering 1,555 GB/s bandwidth—more than 1.7 times that of the Tesla V100. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L1 and L2 caches, and register files. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than the V100’s, is divided into two partitions and 40 slices, and provides 2.3 times greater L2 bandwidth. Cache-residency controls and Compute Data Compression improve data reuse and can reduce DRAM traffic while increasing effective bandwidth and cache capacity.

A100 has 108 Streaming Multiprocessors, compared with 80 in V100, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting peak mixed-precision performance 16 times that of standard FP32 operations. Improvements include greater data sharing across warps, larger matrix operations, fewer issued instructions, fewer register-file accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and larger shared-memory allocation. These features are intended to improve strong scaling and data-delivery efficiency for deep-learning and HPC workloads. A100 does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory controllers, and portions of frame-buffer memory. GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances that support simultaneous contexts and Volta-style Multi-Process Service. MIG provides quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, and predictable performance for separate clients, while migration allows virtual GPUs to move between instances or physical GPUs.

Third-generation NVLink provides A100 with twelve links and 600 GB/s of aggregate bandwidth, compared with 300 GB/s for V100. It supports faster peer-memory access, improved error detection and recovery, and requester-side synchronization. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, providing 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections, and SR-IOV for sharing and virtualizing a GPU.

Additional error-handling features improve fault attribution, isolation, and containment, including remote page-fault reporting over NVLink. A100 also includes a five-core NVJPG hardware JPEG decoder, a GA100 Optical Flow Accelerator for optical-flow and stereo-disparity estimation, improved global-memory atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units for video decoding.

CUDA 11 supports third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, and L2 residency controls. Task Graphs reduce repeated CPU launch and inter-kernel overhead, while A100-specific launch and dependency optimizations accelerate graph execution. CUDA asynchronous copy directly transfers global memory to shared memory while bypassing the register file and optionally L1. Hardware asynchronous barriers support fine-grained synchronization and pipelining. L2 persistence can reserve cache space in 2.5 MB increments, although this feature is disabled in MIG mode. Cooperative Groups adds group-wide asynchronous copies, multi-stage pipelines, hardware-accelerated reductions, and lower grid-synchronization overhead.

DGX A100 contains eight A100 GPUs connected through six NVSwitches, provides up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and supports 4.8 TB/s of total bidirectional NVLink bandwidth. Slicing its GPUs with MIG can create up to 56 isolated accelerators. The system also includes eight 200 Gb/s Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters and an optimized software stack for deep learning, analytics, and HPC.

The document also explains neural-network pruning and fine-grained structured sparsity. A100 supports 2:4 sparsity to reduce computation, memory traffic, and latency while maintaining balanced workloads; NVIDIA reports virtually no accuracy loss in its cited evaluations. The publication concludes with NVIDIA’s disclaimers concerning specification accuracy, warranties, liability, intellectual property, product suitability, and trademarks.

The lecture demonstrates common web-security failures and their defenses. A Shellshock exploit sends a crafted HTTP header that a CGI server converts into a Bash environment variable; malformed syntax then confuses Bash into executing attacker-controlled commands. This illustrates how insecure input handling across multiple languages, operating systems, and web components can produce server-side compromise.

Cross-site scripting (XSS) is demonstrated with a CGI server that inserts untrusted query data directly into HTML. Although browser filters block a straightforward script injection, malformed HTML and CSS can confuse parsers and allow attacker code to run, potentially exposing cookies or performing other actions in the site’s origin. XSS is especially relevant because dynamic sites commonly display untrusted user content, cross-domain content, comments, documents, and profiles.

Browser XSS filters use heuristics and are incomplete. HTTP-only cookies prevent client-side scripts from reading cookies but do not stop cross-site request forgery. Privilege separation, such as serving untrusted content from a separate domain, limits damage but does not eliminate it. Content sanitization encodes untrusted data so it cannot escape its intended context; Django templates illustrate this by escaping HTML metacharacters. Sanitization remains imperfect because HTML, CSS, and JavaScript have complex, inconsistently implemented grammars that browsers tolerate by repairing malformed code. Less expressive languages such as Markdown can simplify sanitization, provided unrestricted inline HTML is disabled.

Content Security Policy (CSP) lets servers restrict permitted content sources, block inline scripts, and restrict dynamic code mechanisms such as `eval`. It offers stronger isolation but is not provably complete, and browsers may implement its requirements inconsistently. The `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` header separately prevents browsers from overriding a declared content type based on file contents.

SQL injection is shown to arise when untrusted values are concatenated into database queries, potentially enabling commands such as table deletion. Quoting alone is insufficient because attackers can include quotes; rigorous encoding and parameterized, framework-provided database interfaces are needed. Similar unsanitized path input can enable directory traversal, so dangerous sequences must be detected or escaped.

Cookies commonly store session identifiers, making them sensitive targets. Sharing domains or subdomains with untrusted parties can expose or overwrite session cookies. Alternatives include stateless authentication using keyed message-authentication codes over each request, as used by AWS; DOM storage, which is more strictly origin-bound than cookies but accessible to application JavaScript; and client certificates, which lack a direct JavaScript interface but have revocation and usability difficulties. Stateless systems also face key-distribution, request-replay, expiration, logout, and revocation challenges.

Protocol-level ambiguity is illustrated by components parsing the same URL as having different origins, enabling one component to obtain code or authority from another origin. The GIFAR attack combines an image with an embedded JAR file: the file passes image validation, while an applet loader can execute its hidden Java code. Combined with XSS, this allows attacker-supplied Java to run with a victim site’s authority. Strict resource-length checking and similar parser fixes closed such vulnerabilities.

Finally, covert channels can reveal browsing history. JavaScript may infer visited sites from link colors, though browsers can mitigate this by reporting all links as unvisited. Cache and DNS response timings can reveal previously accessed resources even when browser caching is disabled. Rendering-speed differences can expose cached or previously visited content through cross-origin iframe behavior, and screen-sharing APIs may allow pixel-based inspection. None of these approaches is presented as a complete solution.

A.J. Brown expressed frustration with receiving few targets and limited production, saying he wants the ball when the offense struggles and the game is on the line. His only game above 30 receiving yards produced six catches for 109 yards and a touchdown. UK scientists found that bumblebee queens exposed to field-like levels of the neonicotinoid thiamethoxam were 26% less likely to lay eggs than unexposed queens. Researchers warn this could drive wild bumblebee populations into decline, though field effects remain uncertain alongside limited nutrition and parasites. The findings may strengthen pressure to make the EU’s 2013 neonicotinoid moratorium permanent, despite concerns about lower canola yields and increased use of other pesticides.

Swarthmore students face high expectations for academics, accountability, and personal conduct, but mistakes are not life-changing and often teach more than successes. Students should laugh at themselves, recognize the college’s unique and intense environment, and give themselves and others room to err. When others say offensive or outrageous things, students should seek clarification, assume good intentions, and forgive mistakes. Laughter cannot solve every problem, but it can help people manage discomfort and feel better.

A Spring Valley woman is San Diego County’s first confirmed West Nile virus case this year. The virus is transmitted by infected mosquitoes and can cause symptoms including headache, fever, nausea, rash, fatigue and swollen glands, though many infected people have no symptoms. County officials urge residents to use insect repellent, wear long sleeves outdoors, remove standing water and report mosquito activity, dead birds or breeding sites to Vector Control.

This retrospective multicentric study developed and evaluated MRI-based deep-learning measures of brain ageing and multiple sclerosis–specific damage in 4,392 patients with multiple sclerosis or clinically isolated syndrome from 15 European centres. A longitudinal early-disease cohort of 252 patients (749 sessions; mean follow-up 4.5 years) was used for clinical validation.

Three models were compared using T1-weighted MRI: a conventional brain-age gap (BAG), a brain-predicted disease-duration gap, and an MS-specific age gap. The disease-duration model used a 3D DenseNet264 and achieved a test-set mean absolute error of 5.63 years and R² of 0.34, compared with R² values of 0.10 and 0.14 for total lesion and thalamic volumes. The MS-age model achieved an MAE of 3.78 years and R² of 0.80. Disease-duration gap and BAG were nearly independent (r=0.06), whereas MS-age gap correlated moderately with BAG (r=0.35). Model interpretation showed reliance on distributed brain-volume changes, particularly cerebrospinal-fluid-space widening.

All three gap measures were positively associated with disability measured by the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS). Disease-duration gap added significant explanatory value beyond BAG (ΔR²=0.012), whereas MS-age gap did not. During longitudinal follow-up, EDSS and BAG increased significantly, while disease-duration and MS-age gaps showed no significant group-level increase. Annualized EDSS worsening correlated with changes in BAG (r=0.48) and disease-duration gap (r=0.50), but not MS-age gap; adding longitudinal disease-duration gap to BAG significantly improved the model (ΔR²=0.064).

The authors concluded that disease-duration gap is a complementary biomarker of multiple sclerosis–specific brain damage, severity, and progression. Limitations included the noisy, retrospectively defined clinical-onset date, possible treatment effects, disease-duration-dependent prediction bias, and the need for validation in additional outcomes and clinical populations.

The paper applies non-Markovian Situation Calculus to an existing deontic account of obligations to formalize a taxonomy of obligation types, motivated partly by smart contracts and their need for explicit obligations. Situation Calculus models changing systems through actions, situations, fluents, action preconditions, and successor state axioms, which address the frame problem by specifying what changes and remains unchanged. Markovian theories determine preconditions and effects solely from the current situation, while non-Markovian theories allow dependence on prior situations through bounded formulas.

The underlying many-sorted second-order language covers actions, situations, time, and other objects. It includes action terms, action histories represented by `do(a,s)`, predicate and functional fluents, `Poss`, a reachability relation, unique-name axioms, initial-situation axioms, and foundational axioms. A running door-opening example defines relevant actions, fluents, preconditions, and successor-state axioms.

For obligations, the paper summarizes a deontic embedding where `O(s′,s)` means that `s′` is deontically accessible from `s`; `Oblg(φ,s)` requires `φ` to hold in every deontically accessible situation. This builds on prior work combining deontic modalities with time and extending regression to obligation-changing actions. Subsequent sections formalize the obligation taxonomy, establish properties, and examine obligation violation and compensation.

Archaeologists’ confirmation that Richard III’s remains lay beneath a Leicester car park profoundly affected several people connected to the discovery. Dominic Smee, a 30-year-old with scoliosis curved almost identically to the king’s, trained in foot combat and horse riding, then portrayed Richard’s final moments in a Channel 4 documentary. The experience, including the positive response to his openness about his condition, increased his confidence.

Michael Ibsen, a descendant of Richard’s sister Anne, supplied a DNA sample before excavation began. His contribution later helped confirm the remains beyond reasonable doubt, and he subsequently made Richard’s coffin and received widespread public attention.

Mike Mistry, who had worked as a car park attendant for over 15 years, witnessed the excavation and fielded questions from international visitors. He had unknowingly marked the discovery site with a large “R” while maintaining a reserved parking space. He was made redundant in 2016 and had not found another attendant’s job.

Musician Ian Churchward was likewise transformed by the discovery, which inspired Richard-themed songs and albums with his band, The Legendary Ten Seconds. Their output grew to five albums, with a sixth and a narrated concept album also underway, bringing invitations to perform at festivals, battlefields and Richard III Society events.

The instructor reviews Problem Set 8, noting that its problems are new and intended as a shakedown. Chapter 11 introduces binary Hadamard-transform realizations of Reed–Muller codes. The universal matrix \(U_m\) is the \(m\)-fold tensor product of a lower-triangular \(2\times2\) generator matrix. It is self-inverse, so the \(2^m\times2^m\) Hadamard transform is its own inverse. Reed–Muller codes are generated by selecting appropriate rows of \(U_m\). Row weights are related to the Hamming weights of binary row indices: indices of weights \(0,1,2,\) and \(3\) correspond to row weights \(1,2,4,\) and \(8\), respectively. This relationship is the key hint for Problem 8.1.

A graphical realization begins with a simple controlled-NOT-style \(2\times2\) block and recursively combines blocks into butterfly networks resembling fast Fourier transform structures. For the \((8,4,4)\) Reed–Muller code, four internal variables are free and four are fixed to zero, producing 16 valid trajectories whose external tuples are the codewords. Graph reductions yield a realization with 12 simple binary constraints and cycles. Agglomerating the cycles produces a more complicated, cycle-free trellis-like realization using \((6,3)\) constraints and higher branch complexity. A two-state tail-biting realization is another cyclic alternative. These illustrate the trade-off between simple cyclic graphs and more complex cycle-free graphs: exact decoding is possible on cycle-free graphs, while decoding on graphs with cycles is approximate and may be suboptimum.

In general, agglomerated Hadamard-transform realizations provide cycle-free four-section Reed–Muller realizations whose state dimensions meet the cut-set bound and yield minimal trellis complexity. The instructor also briefly compares factor graphs, Markov graphs and random fields, and Bayesian networks, which use differing conventions for variables, constraints, and directionality.

The lecture then introduces a posteriori probability decoding and the sum-product algorithm. On cycle-free graphs, sum-product decoding is exact and terminates in time related to the graph’s diameter; on a trellis, it corresponds to the BCJR algorithm. On graphs with cycles, it becomes iterative and approximate, raising questions about initialization, convergence, and stopping criteria. Graphs with large girth are preferred because short cycles degrade performance.

A posteriori probability decoding computes, for every external and internal variable, its probability conditioned on the received sequence. Bitwise maximum-a posteriori decisions minimize bit-error probability but may not produce a valid codeword, whereas maximum-likelihood sequence decoding minimizes block or word-error probability. A posteriori probabilities are especially useful for passing soft information between component decoders in turbo and other capacity-approaching codes.

The relevant probability is expressed as a sum over compatible codewords of products of channel likelihoods, giving the algorithm its name. Direct symbol likelihood is termed intrinsic information, while likelihood contributions from other received symbols are termed extrinsic information. The algorithm requires a past–future decomposition, sum-product update rules, and a scheduling procedure. In cycle-free graphs, each edge is a cut separating past from future, allowing posterior probabilities to factor into past and future components and be combined efficiently. The lecture ends before completing the full algorithm or reaching the BCJR discussion.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and suit buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Duty-cycle limits are programmed through DCL: TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP support 100% operation with DCL connected to VLDO and 75% maximum duty cycle with DCL floating; TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP also support 50% with DCL connected to AVSS. TPS7H5004-SP requires the 50% configuration.

CS_ILIM senses transformer primary current for PWM control and overcurrent protection, comparing it against COMP/2. At a nominal 1.05 V threshold, the controller enters cycle-by-cycle current limiting and charges CHICC; reaching 0.6 V stops switching and initiates a hiccup restart sequence when CHICC falls to 0.3 V. A minimum CHICC value of 3.3 nF is recommended. The FAULT pin supports externally generated protection signals, shutting down above a typical 0.6 V and restarting after the signal falls below 0.5 V and a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles. RSC provides slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, with 1 times recommended. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported, and thermal shutdown occurs at a typical junction temperature of 175°C, with restart below 160°C.

A 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses a 5-V output, 205-kΩ RT resistor, 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms, a 40-µH transformer primary, 0.47-µH output inductor, 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, and Type 2A compensation with a 10-kHz crossover. It uses 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous rectifiers, seven 330-µF output capacitors totaling 2.3 mF, and a 102-kΩ RSC resistor. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require close, low-impedance bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and control traces from switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide current paths, and placing filter, bypass, compensation, and sensing components near their associated pins.

Top 2026 recruit Junior County, a 6-foot-4 combo guard from Wasatch Academy, committed to UConn. The No. 43 player in the SC Next 100 and No. 4 shooting guard, County chose the Huskies after touring his other finalists and visiting UConn. He cited the intensity of practice, his relationship with coach Dan Hurley and the campus atmosphere, and said he believes UConn will help him develop and make winning plays on and off the ball.

County averaged 13.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.4 assists for the Utah Prospects on the Nike EYBL circuit, including two 20-point games and two outings with four three-pointers. UConn landed a top-five 2025 class featuring Braylon Mullins and Eric Reibe and has produced three consecutive top-10 recruiting classes, including back-to-back national championships.

A Fox News Halftime Report editorial argues that weakening political parties contributes to ideological polarization, voter alienation and partisan gridlock. It cites preliminary California data showing registered independents now outnumber registered Republicans, and discusses the state’s open top-two primary system, which reformers hoped would reduce extremism. The piece argues that national media have sorted voters into more ideologically homogeneous parties, while primaries reveal rather than cause these trends. It predicts unaffiliated voters may eventually outnumber Democrats but cautions that replacing two major parties with many narrow-interest groups would create greater factionalism, not a centrist alternative. Campaign-finance rules, outside political spending and partisan gerrymandering are identified as problems, while further weakening the two-party system is rejected as a solution.

Researchers led by OIST combined fossil evidence, molecular-clock analysis, and 17 rare horizontal gene transfers between fungal lineages to better date fungal evolution. Because fungi rarely fossilize well and complex multicellularity evolved repeatedly in them, their origins have been difficult to establish. The gene transfers provided relative ancestry clues, while fossils calibrated the timeline. The analysis estimates that the common ancestor of living fungi lived roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, hundreds of millions of years before land plants. The findings support a prolonged period of fungi-algae interactions in which fungi recycled nutrients, broke down rock, and created primitive soils, potentially preparing Earth’s terrestrial environments for plants.

The passage argues that U.S. strategic superiority led the Soviet Union to withdraw Cuban missiles in 1962 without war and that strength, rather than bluster, best preserves peace. It criticizes U.S. defense officials and the Carter administration for discounting Soviet military buildup, reducing defenses, and responding with weakness and indecision. It cites continued Soviet forces in Cuba and Afghanistan, as well as conflicting U.S. threats and claims of military capability, as evidence that U.S. credibility and alliances are weakening. The passage calls for prudently restoring U.S. superiority in conventional arms, troop deployments, and strategic deterrence; firmly combating terrorism; consulting allies; and reaffirming American principles. It maintains that renewed strength and alliance cohesion are the best means of achieving world peace.

Beijing ordered 15 property portals to remove false ads, price-gain promises, rumors, feng shui and financing advice, and help with residence permits or school enrollment. The restrictions accompany tighter mortgage rules and a third-home ban aimed at cooling rising housing prices.

MusConv is software for transferring playlists between streaming platforms. United Airlines promoted its premium positioning during an earnings call, highlighting uncrowded airport lounges and seatback entertainment installed on more than 146,000 seats across 765 aircraft. The speaker describes wearing a hoody and headphones before games to block distractions and focus on preparation. Ohio education regulators are reviewing a whistleblower’s claim that the Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow manipulated attendance data with ActivTrak software to increase state funding. A former technology employee said school officials ordered staff to adjust student data to meet enrollment and payment targets. ActivTrak was installed after the state challenged ECOT’s reporting of learning hours.

The state previously found that ECOT significantly overreported full-time-equivalent students, required it to return $60 million in 2015-2016 overpayments, and assessed a $19 million penalty for 2016-2017.
