In his final Oval Office address, the outgoing president thanks Americans, Vice President Gore, his Cabinet, and others for eight years of service. He credits the public with economic gains—including more than 22 million new jobs, low unemployment, record homeownership, reduced crime, greater educational opportunity and health coverage, and lower poverty—while also citing safer food and water and increased environmental protection.

He urges Americans to preserve three priorities: continued fiscal responsibility and debt reduction; active global leadership to expand freedom, prosperity, and trade while confronting terrorism, organized crime, weapons, disease, environmental degradation, and global poverty; and greater unity at home, treating all people fairly and humanely regardless of race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or nationality.

He concludes by wishing President-elect George W. Bush and his family success, expressing confidence in America’s future, and saying he will remain a citizen and servant after leaving office.

The paper examines blockchain education in US universities with AACSB-accredited business schools, emphasizing the enterprise knowledge gap and the need for interdisciplinary skills beyond technical expertise. Blockchain integration requires coordination among management and finance, supply chain management, IT and cybersecurity, law and compliance, procurement, and sales, supported by social, methodological, and personal competences.

In March 2024, researchers screened 533 universities and found 151 offering at least one blockchain course, totaling 361 courses. Courses were classified by topic, academic field, and references to AI, IoT, and cybersecurity through independent review and consensus reconciliation. Most courses were undergraduate-level, and larger undergraduate populations were more likely to have blockchain offerings. Computer science and information systems departments hosted the most courses, followed by finance, although courses also appeared in biology, literature, political science, and other disciplines.

The largest course category was blockchain fundamentals, followed by digital assets and cryptocurrencies and technical development. AI and machine learning were the most frequently referenced related technologies, ahead of IoT and non-fungible tokens. The findings indicate that blockchain curricula are interdisciplinary but unevenly distributed. Future research should assess evolving course content, competency requirements by discipline and job level, alignment with industry needs, and changes over time.

After his grandfather died from heart disease, seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg founded “Heart Cents,” collecting pennies and donations for St. Joseph’s heart patients. He raised more than $200 in Savannah and Richmond Hill; another family matched his total, and an anonymous $250 donation brought the amount to $672. The funds will cover patients’ transportation and co-pays, and Joseph plans to continue fundraising.

Read operations support legacy SPI-compatible single- and dual-SDO protocols and a source-synchronous protocol. After power-up or asynchronous reset, SPI-00-S supports reads and writes. Another SPI protocol is selected using SDI_MODE[1:0], with SDO_MODE[1:0]=00b; RVS remains low during transfers. Short frames read only required MSBs, while SDO_CNTL_REG[7:0]=00h enables daisy chaining. Optional dual SDO mode uses SDO1_CONFIG[1:0]=11b and launches two bits per SCLK edge. The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitors and methods that combine raw or minimally processed optical-sensor data from multiple patient measurement sites to generate a single physiological measurement. Sensors may include multiple wavelength-specific light emitters and photodetectors, with outputs supplied through sensor interfaces to a signal processor. The processor can combine signal features such as amplitude, phase, DC values, wavelength ratios, and measurement-site or tissue information, or separately calculate site-specific measurements.

Photodetectors may be spatially distributed in a three-dimensional configuration conforming to the anatomy of a measurement site. This arrangement provides varied light-path lengths, improves measurement robustness, and supplies topology information that can help determine whether a sensor is correctly positioned. Clip-style and adhesive-tape sensors are contemplated for sites such as fingers, hands, feet, faces, noses, earlobes, and foreheads.

Multiple-site monitoring can combine cephalic and peripheral measurements, such as a nose and fingertip, and may provide more informative results, cross-checking, and reduced sensor-specific errors or noise. Physiological measurements may include oxygen saturation, pulse rate, plethysmograph waveform, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, glucose, and other relevant patient characteristics.

This continuation application concerns torque sensing in surgical robotic wrists. It describes a surgical robot arm with an articulated wrist comprising a proximal roll joint, crossed-axis pitch joints forming a universal joint, and a terminal roll joint. The wrist may be positioned at the arm’s distal end or within a surgical instrument and can carry a surgical instrument or end effector. Torque sensors associated with the wrist joints measure applied torque about multiple axes; possible sensors include resistance-based strain gauges, piezoelectric strain gauges, and magnetostrictive gauges. A processor uses sensor outputs and motor inputs to distinguish externally applied torque from torque produced by motor-driven joint motion. The sensed forces may be converted into haptic feedback for the surgeon.

The disclosed arm arrangements use alternating roll and pitch joints, offset joint axes, and a compact wrist to provide substantial end-effector mobility while remaining relatively slim and lightweight. The arrangement is intended to reduce kinematic singularities, permit multiple robot arms to operate closely together, support instrument motion resembling a human wrist, and facilitate measurement of forces applied to surgical instruments or end effectors. During surgery, the arm can align and insert an instrument through an incision, manipulate the end effector, withdraw the instrument, and rotate the shaft about the incision to move the end effector without enlarging the wound.

CoreLogic reported year-over-year home-price gains of 8.3% in Los Angeles County, 8.2% in Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and 6.2% in Orange County in May. The book aims to regularize distributed-system design through reusable patterns, beginning with single-node containers because co-located containers form the atomic elements of distributed-system patterns. Containers establish resource boundaries, clarify team ownership, and separate concerns, allowing components on one machine to have distinct requirements and priorities. Separating a user-facing server from a best-effort background loader isolates resources, protects service quality, and lets the loader use spare capacity while prioritizing critical services during contention. Multi-container decomposition also supports small, focused teams, reusable modules, and independent testing, deployment, updates, rollouts, and rollbacks, improving reliability and agility. Single-node patterns assume tightly coupled containers reliably scheduled onto one machine that may share volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, and memory. In Kubernetes, this grouping is called a pod, though the concept applies more broadly.

Kesha supported Taylor Swift in 2017 after David Mueller sued Swift, alleging he was groped in 2014 and fired over her account. Mueller’s suit was dismissed; Swift’s $1 countersuit remained pending. The Combo defense uses three perimeter defenders in person-to-person pass denial and two interior defenders zoning for support against spread offenses. X1 protects the middle and forces the ball toward the sideline; X2 and X3 deny passes, while X4 and X5 guard the baseline. Rotations trap penetration, close out to shooters, and prevent return passes, while caught dribblers are smothered into difficult passes. If X4 and X5 handle and shoot well, use a quarter-court 1-3-1 trap.

The passage documents AGESA host-environment interfaces for pre-memory stack management, structure allocation, processor and memory initialization, platform configuration, suspend/resume handling, utility services, and host-implemented call-outs.

`AMD_ENABLE_STACK` is a stackless native-assembler procedure using register-based parameters. It divides the available pre-memory stack among processor cores, maps it into global address space, configures x86-64 MTRRs, establishes ESP or real-mode SS:ESP, and creates a `UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF` structure. Protected mode requires the host to supply an SS descriptor with a zero base address. The procedure must run on all cores and reports success, stack reentry, or an unknown processor family. A corresponding routine removes the pre-memory stack after memory becomes available, disables Cache-as-RAM mode, flushes caches, and leaves processor cache enabled for the BSP. AArch64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor use PSP-initialized DRAM instead of these stack facilities.

`AmdCreateStruct` allocates and initializes AGESA parameter structures using pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage; `AmdReleaseStruct` releases them. Other services return DIMM data-eye results, APIC addresses, available execution-cache size, PCI addresses, current socket/die/core identity, and detailed DIMM locations. Additional interfaces update MMIO ranges, read event-log entries from a circular buffer, and map memory addresses to FRU and error-location information.

The initialization sequence provides minimal reset-time processor setup, full processor initialization, and main-memory initialization. The reset routine separates BSP and AP behavior, performs HyperTransport initialization, and allocates up to three execution-cache regions under alignment, size, address, and boundary restrictions. The early routine completes coherent and non-coherent link setup, configures power-management capabilities, and can request a warm reset. The post-memory routine locates, initializes, and enables system memory, applies extensive configurable memory options, transfers HOBs and artifact data into main memory, disables the pre-memory stack, and prepares processors for host control. Later routines move artifact data into protected host memory, configure graphics hardware, and generate ACPI, DMI, P-state, CRAT, CDIT, and related tables before operating-system handoff.

Ready-to-boot routines save critical processor and silicon state for suspend without initiating suspend. Resume routines restart memory from non-volatile context data, restore silicon registers after PCI control structures are re-established, perform final reinitialization, and prepare the system for operating-system restart.

Required host call-outs include buffer allocation, deallocation, and lookup; cold or warm reset initiation; DIMM SPD reading over SMBus; and dispatching tasks to application processors through `AmdLateRunApTask`. Optional call-outs support IDS data retrieval, heap rebase, DRAM and training hooks, external Vref and voltage adjustment, FCH customization, PCIe clock requests, AP idle handling, and platform-specific controls. Most AGESA procedures require the host to establish a stack before invocation. Platform customization is supported through build-configuration settings, including platform-specific limits and user-defined register-setting tables.

Johnson & Johnson’s first-quarter trading update was mixed. Adjusted earnings per share met consensus, but sales were slightly below estimates. The company raised 2017 sales guidance to $75.4–$76.1 billion and adjusted earnings guidance to $7.00–$7.15 per share, incorporating the estimated impact of its $30 billion Actelion transaction. Remicade sales fell 6% year over year to $1.67 billion, while baby care, oral care and wound care sales declined. Reported EPS was $1.61, or $1.57 excluding buybacks.

At roughly $125 per share, JNJ traded at 19 times forward earnings and 11.9 times enterprise value to EBITDA. Analysts saw limited upside after a rally from $111 in late January to $129 in mid-March. Potential influences included investor preference for defensive stocks, Actelion’s growth and reinvestment, clinical results, and pharmaceutical competition.

Regulatory risks included President Trump’s calls for greater U.S. drug production, lower prices and faster FDA approvals, while delayed tax reform also reflected healthcare-related setbacks. Falling rates have increased the value of JNJ’s long-term debt, including its 3.7% 2046 bond, though projected rate increases create fixed-income risk. The author found JNJ’s fundamentals solid but concluded that the quarterly update warranted seeking value elsewhere.

The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed the dismissal of United Distributors’ suit against Alfred R. Willis for his alleged liability on a personal guarantee. Willis had signed credit documents and a guarantee contemplating his purchase of 50 percent of Airco Appliance & Hardware, Inc. Two days later, he abandoned the venture, and United Distributors was informed that he would not participate. Its salesman returned Willis’s other documents but inadvertently retained the guarantee.

Burke continued operating Airco, which later purchased air-conditioning units from United Distributors and issued an unpaid $3,107.82 note. Willis argued that the guarantee lacked consideration because he never became a shareholder and alternatively asserted revocation and estoppel. The court found that Willis’s intended stock ownership and participation were the sole consideration for the guarantee. Because that purpose failed and United Distributors knew Willis would not join, the guarantee became ineffective under Revised Civil Code Articles 1825–1827. Burke’s and the corporation’s liability were not contested.

ConocoPhillips agreed to sell its San Juan Basin assets to a Hilcorp Energy affiliate for $2.7 billion in cash plus contingent payments of up to $300 million over six years. Payments depend on Henry Hub natural gas prices, with full payment available if the price meets or exceeds $3.20 per MMBTU during at least 59.5% of qualifying months. The sale follows a $13.3 billion divestiture of Canadian assets and further reduces ConocoPhillips’s exposure to natural gas. The San Juan assets represent 0.6 billion barrels of oil equivalent, including 78% natural gas, 20% natural gas liquids and 2% oil.

The transaction will reduce annual production by about 115,000 barrels per day and, combined with the Canadian sale, lower projected production by 25.4%. Operating cash flow is expected to decline by $0.3 billion, and ConocoPhillips will record a likely noncash impairment of approximately $2.9 billion, potentially creating future tax benefits. Despite plans to maintain roughly $5 billion in capital expenditures, production and cash flow could remain under pressure.

Management said the $2.7 billion proceeds are for general corporate purposes, making their eventual allocation uncertain. The analysis concludes that the sale is reasonable and could create value, particularly if the proceeds fund accretive asset purchases, although reserve valuation and future production remain key considerations.

The Inquiry would assess the strength and weakness of doubtful Russian regions, the Balkans, and Turkey; develop possible economic arrangements for numerous European, African, Asian, and Latin American territories; and consider safeguards for minorities and weak peoples in Turkey, Tropical and South Africa, and potentially several other regions.

VIX futures, introduced in 2004, are contracts based on the VIX Index, which measures expected 30-day implied volatility in the U.S. equity market and is widely used as a market-sentiment indicator. Traded on Cboe Futures Exchange, they allow investors to hedge equity risk, diversify portfolios, and speculate on volatility. Strategies may use technical or fundamental analysis, precise entry and exit signals, risk management, position sizing, and arbitrage.

VIX futures do not precisely track spot VIX. The S&P 500 VIX Short-Term Futures Index captures only about half of spot movements, and rolling contracts creates performance drag, making futures relatively costly as a long-term hedge. A backtest presented did not find a valuable futures strategy, but a spot-VIX-based stock strategy showed a 0.64% average gain per trade, 44.06% risk-adjusted return, and a 23% maximum drawdown versus 55% for buy-and-hold.

VIX prices are primarily influenced by bull and bear market cycles and by contango and backwardation. Futures trade at a premium when spot VIX is low and a discount when it is extremely high. The index reportedly performs better in summer and fall, is stagnant in winter, and declines in spring.

There are full and mini contracts worth the index multiplied by $1,000 and $100, respectively. The minimum fluctuation is 0.05 index points, worth $50 per full contract. Monthly contracts are financially settled using a Special Opening Quotation. The futures symbol is VX, while the index symbol is VIX. Trading requires a funded futures-broker account; CFDs are another option but are broker contracts without expiration dates. Leverage is the primary trading risk because adverse movements can magnify losses. Reported records include a VIX futures high of 80.850 in March 2020, a spot VIX high of 89.53 in October 2008, and a spot VIX low of 8.56 in November 2017.

A simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography method was developed to map NCM111 cathode structure, chemical composition, and transition-metal valence states in 3D during a single low-dose STEM acquisition. This reduced beam damage and ensured spatial alignment across modalities. Applied to pristine, 50-, 100-, and 200-cycle particles, the method showed layered-to-spinel-like and then rock-salt structural transformations, alongside capacity losses of 34.3%, 52.2%, and 100% at 50, 100, and 200 cycles, respectively.

Chemical composition changed largely uniformly throughout particle volumes. Oxygen content remained near 66–67% through 100 cycles before falling to 61% at 200 cycles, when 33.7% of the particle volume had converted to rock-salt structure. Local transition-metal segregation was more surface-dependent and increased with cycling, with Co showing the greatest segregation, followed by Ni and Mn.

Valence-state distributions showed strong depth dependence. Mn4+ and Co3+ dominated pristine material, but by 200 cycles Mn4+ fell from 80.7% to 53.4%, Mn2+ rose from 12.1% to 42.0%, Co3+ fell from 77.5% to 11.0%, and Co2+ rose from 22.5% to 89.0%. Surface-localized transition-metal clustering in pristine particles was linked to these depth-dependent valence variations.

Overall, degradation reflected interacting phase transitions, transition-metal migration, and dissolution-driven segregation, with compositional changes affecting the whole particle and valence-state and segregation changes concentrated near its surface.

The Cleveland Guardians defeated the Detroit Tigers in AL Wild Card Series Game 2 with a five-run eighth inning, forcing a decisive Game 3 on Thursday. Brayan Rocchio’s solo homer off Troy Melton broke the 1-1 tie; his 99.9-mph four-seam fastball was nearly impossible to hit under the windy, shadowy conditions. Detroit stranded a playoff-record 15 baserunners, while Cleveland had only two hits through seven innings. The win continued Cleveland’s improbable season after Rocchio spent six weeks in Triple-A and the Guardians once trailed Detroit by 15½ games in the AL Central. The Tigers now face elimination, while Cleveland hopes to extend its habit of overcoming adversity.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s determination that Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. owed sales or use taxes on certain drilling-equipment purchases. Mumma qualified as a contractor because it incorporated tangible personal property into improvements to land under Indiana Code § 6-2-1-38(k). The court rejected Mumma’s claim that the purchases were exempt as manufacturing equipment directly used to extract tangible personal property, finding that “manufacturing” implies extraction for resale, while the ultimate users consumed the water for business, household, or farming purposes. The earlier statute-of-limitations ruling was reaffirmed.

Elliott Wave theory is a technical-analysis principle developed by Ralph Nelson Elliott in the 1920s after studying 75 years of stock data. It asserts that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns that may help identify future price direction, though not with certainty. Impulse waves move with the market trend and contain five subwaves: waves 1, 3, and 5 are motive waves, while waves 2 and 4 are corrective. Corrective waves move against the trend and consist of three subwaves: A and C move in the pullback direction, while B moves in the main trend direction.

Traders apply the theory in stock, forex, and commodity markets, including day, swing, and long-term trading. It may be used alone or alongside trendlines, moving averages, momentum indicators such as RSI and the stochastic, and other technical analysis. A suggested approach is to identify the trend first, track price swings, and trade the next impulse wave after a corrective wave loses momentum.

The theory is complex and subjective, particularly regarding wave counts, entries, and exits, making it extremely difficult to backtest and vulnerable to curve fitting. There is no single best timeframe: intraday charts suit day traders, while swing traders generally use daily charts. Elliott recommended combining the theory with other technical analysis rather than relying on it alone.

In a Supreme Court hearing on Holsey Ellingburg’s sentence, the government agreed that the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act cannot retroactively increase punishment if restitution constitutes a criminal penalty under the Ex Post Facto Clause. Justices divided over whether victim restitution is criminal, civil, or both. Justice Alito emphasized the statute’s victim-remedy purposes, while Justices Kagan and Jackson viewed its integration into criminal sentencing as inherently penal. The author predicted the Court would reject applying the later-adopted statute to Ellingburg, likely without lengthy separate opinions.

Verizon Communications (VZ) fell $0.37 to close at $48.81, recording $56.85 million in net trading inflows. Analysts maintain an average “Hold” rating and $52.86 price target. Quarterly results included $0.96 EPS, matching estimates, and $30.55 billion in revenue, exceeding expectations. Call-option trading was approximately 524% above typical volume. Verizon declared a $0.59 quarterly dividend with a 4.84% yield. EVP Craig Silliman sold 610 shares, while several institutional investors established or increased positions. Hedge funds and institutions own 62.24% of the stock. Verizon provides wireless and wireline communications through its Wireless and Wireline segments.

This preprint examines microtubule (MT) dynamics as a basis for predicting and overcoming treatment resistance in advanced prostate cancer. Approximately one-third of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers (mCRPC) are intrinsically refractory to systemic therapy, while acquired resistance and limited treatment options create a need for biomarkers that guide taxane selection.

AR splice variants differentially affect MT organization and drug response. ARv7 is constitutively active, associated with taxane resistance, and increases MT growth speed by more than 40% in M12 cells, whereas wild-type AR has little effect on overall speed but slows MT growth near the cell edge. Taxanes inhibit nuclear accumulation of ARv567 but not ARv7, supporting a link between MT dynamics, AR signaling, and resistance.

The study describes an automated live-cell imaging method that tracks fluorescent EB1/EB3 comets at growing MT tips, using difference-of-Gaussians detection, Kalman filtering, and Hungarian-algorithm assignment of interrupted tracks. It also describes patient-derived prostate organoids and methods to improve tumor-cell selection, including use of the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632.

Several additional findings connect cytoskeletal remodeling with resistance. mCRPC circulating tumor cells can be smaller than leukocyte-based detection thresholds and may be missed unless PSMA-based methods are used. Op18 upregulation is associated with reduced MT polymerization and potentially small, therapy-resistant cells. ERG-positive cells show reduced taxane-induced MT bundling, while paclitaxel suppresses MT growth rates. Both unusually fast and slow MT turnover may characterize drug resistance. The pVHL–GSK3β axis regulates MT turnover, catastrophe events, and primary cilia; GSK3β-mediated pVHL phosphorylation during quiescence destabilizes MTs. GPX4 inhibitors RSL3 and ML210 are proposed for eliminating drug-tolerant persister cells through ferroptosis, and NAD+ is discussed as a possible compound for restoring normal MT regulation and drug sensitivity.

A circular Hough transform was used to quantify paclitaxel-induced circular MT bundles. Taxane-sensitive A549 cells formed bundles more frequently and brightly than BRCA1-knockdown cells, which exhibited resistance. Planned validation includes correlating organoid MT dynamics with patient gene-expression and clinical-response data, testing candidate MT regulators in knockdown and xenograft models, evaluating cultured tissue slices, and screening small molecules in patient-derived tumor organoids with expanded immune cells. Overall, the work proposes image-based, patient-specific assessment of MT dynamics to anticipate resistance, inform drug and dose selection, and identify sensitizing targets such as the tubulin transcriptome and GSK3 pathways.

Faster SSDs have exposed bottlenecks in traditional game storage systems, where CPU-based decompression can consume dozens of cores. NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft DirectStorage to keep data compressed and move it directly from NVMe storage to an RTX GPU for GPU-based lossless decompression. NVIDIA claims RTX IO can accelerate I/O by up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs, improving loading times, frame rates, texture streaming, and object pop-in while reducing CPU utilization. It also supports professional workloads involving large CAD, rendering, scientific, and virtual-reality datasets.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU uses the GA10x Ampere architecture and offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput of the Quadro RTX 6000, along with up to five times the AI-training throughput, or ten times with sparsity. Its PCIe Gen4 interface provides up to twice the bandwidth of Turing-based GPUs. Each A40 has 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB by linking two GPUs with third-generation NVLink. It includes three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, vGPU virtualization, Quadro Sync support, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K displays at 120 Hz and 8K displays at 60 Hz. Their display features include DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth, plus HDCP 2.3 support.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x GPUs provide the first hardware AV1 decode support described by NVIDIA. AV1 can reduce bitrates by 50–55% compared with H.264, while hardware decoding can play 8K60 HDR content with substantially lower CPU usage than software decoding.

Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-based encoding independent of graphics performance, freeing the graphics engine and CPU for other tasks. It supports high-quality, low-latency streaming and archiving, including H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K. NVIDIA reports that GA10x hardware encoding exceeds x264 Fast quality and approaches x264 Medium quality with common streaming settings.

GA10x Ampere provides up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection performance and adds ray-traced motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Its third-generation Tensor Core supports structural sparsity for up to twice the effective Tensor Core throughput. GA10x is also the first GPU architecture to support GDDR6X; the GeForce RTX 3090 reaches 19.5 Gbps memory rates and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU, has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores, and is reported as 1.5 times faster than the Titan RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, supports GDDR6X but uses GDDR6, omits NVLink, and is described as faster than the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti.

New GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay technology detects memory-transmission errors and retries failed transactions. Performance plateauing under memory overclocking indicates reduced useful bandwidth from repeated errors and the practical memory limit, although continued overclocking can still cause crashes and EDR cannot prevent every crash.

The RTX A6000 workstation GPU uses GA102 with 10,752 CUDA cores, second- and next-generation RT Cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6. It supports hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and two linked cards provide 96 GB of combined memory. The publication includes rendering, visualization, HPC, and deep-learning performance comparisons with the RTX 6000. It states that the specifications are believed accurate as of the publication date but are supplied without warranties and may be changed or discontinued.

The Eleventh Circuit affirmed the district court's 51-month sentence for Alexis Perez, who pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail fraud. Perez argued that his offense level should have been reduced three levels under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) for an incomplete conspiracy and that he should have received a minor-role reduction under § 3B1.203.

As to the incomplete-conspiracy claim, the court distinguished United States v. Khawaja and United States v. Puche, which involved conspirators who had not taken "crucial steps" toward completing the substantive offense. Because Perez and his co-conspirators had established a detailed plan, had the means to execute it, and were on the verge of executing it when law enforcement intervened, the district court correctly declined the three-level reduction.

As to the minor-role claim, the court noted that the defendant bears the burden of proving his role by a preponderance of the evidence and that the determination should consider both his role in the relevant conduct and his culpability relative to other participants. The record supported the district court's finding that Perez played an "important" role, being involved in planning and preparation, knowing how the fraud would be implemented, and being paid for his services; Perez also failed to show he was less culpable than most other conspirators.

The court also declined to enforce the sentence appeal waiver, because the district court did not specifically question Perez about it, and it rejected his attempt to adopt his codefendants' arguments, since his appeal was not consolidated and he filed no motion for adoption. The judgment was affirmed.

Price-action trading is a form of technical analysis that uses historical price movements—swing highs and lows, chart patterns, candlestick patterns, trends, and support/resistance—to identify trade entries and exits. Intraday strategies include trend following, breakouts, reversals, and scalping. Pure price-action traders avoid indicators, though some combine price analysis with moving averages, VIX, or RSI. Because price-action strategies are difficult to codify and backtest, especially at the intraday level, the passage emphasizes translating them into specific rules, testing them historically and out of sample, and optimizing them. It warns that anecdotal charts can make random strategies appear profitable and recommends testing across different markets and strategies for diversification.

Cut credit card use, establish a spending plan and emergency fund, and pay as much as possible monthly toward debt, including extra earnings. Distinguish necessities from discretionary spending and cut unnecessary expenses so savings accumulate. Prioritize debts with the highest interest rates, then redirect payments from paid-off cards to the next balance. Make gradual lifestyle changes to avoid becoming overwhelmed.

Google celebrated what would have been Max Born’s 135th birthday with a colorful Doodle. Born, a German physicist and mathematician, was born Dec. 11, 1882, in Breslau (now Wrocław, Poland), into a Jewish academic family. He spent 12 years teaching theoretical physics at the University of Göttingen, mentoring scientists including Werner Heisenberg, Enrico Fermi, J. Robert Oppenheimer and Maria Goeppert-Mayer. Born and Albert Einstein maintained a friendship of more than 40 years despite differing scientific approaches. After Hitler’s rise, Jewish academics including Born were barred from university work; in 1933, Born emigrated to England. He received the 1954 Nobel Prize for the Born Rule, which uses mathematical probability to predict quantum measurement outcomes and forms the basis of most quantum-physics predictions. Born died on Jan. 5, 1970, at age 87.

Spanish police dismantled a network that recruited Venezuelan transsexuals through fake “Miss Trans” competitions before exploiting them in prostitution and drug dealing. Over 20 victims were freed; 14 suspected organizers were arrested.

The bill would allow district and charter schools to create innovation plans and seek State Board rule waivers. LEAs could use some restricted state funding and accept private support, and approved plans could be incorporated into charter agreements. The State Board could terminate plans and annually report by November 30 on plans, waivers, funding, statutory barriers, and recommendations. With no LEA applications or approved plans reported, the State Board is recommended to promote the program through a website, optional forms, and existing communications.

UK employment rose by 109,000 in the three months to April, lifting the rate to a joint-record 74.8%, with hiring continuing into May. However, regular pay growth slowed to 1.7%, while annual inflation reached 2.9%, pushing real pay lower and squeezing household spending. Post-election uncertainty may weaken business confidence and leave growth reliant on exports, services and investment. Moderating input-cost growth suggests consumer inflation may peak and ease later in the year, though wages are unlikely to improve significantly and the labour market could weaken. The Bank of England is therefore likely to keep interest rates on hold until the outlook improves.

In Document 29, Minister Schoenfeld told Finnish Foreign Minister Witting that his advice about favorable American attitudes toward Finland conflicted with Schoenfeld’s knowledge. Witting acknowledged that he and Procopé had overstated American friendliness and that Procopé remained pessimistic about Finland’s long-term outlook. Schoenfeld stressed that Finland still supported the U.S. position and instructions from the previous fall, questioned security based on strategic lines rather than sound political foundations, and challenged Witting’s comparison of German and British positions on small nations. Witting said Finnish realism rested on historical experience with Russia and survival against great odds. He also relayed Procopé’s private view that small European nations might face postwar Anglo-Russian control and Germany’s war industry should be eliminated. Schoenfeld found Witting grave but at a loss over what Finland could do, believing its government increasingly controlled by outside forces.

In Document 30, the Secretary of State clarified that his inquiries applied to American citizens serving in the Finnish Legation and Finnish consulates. He said the Finnish minister could require their compliance or end their official ties, but modified the request so consular personnel needed permission to make such inquiries only when leaving the city containing their office.

The passage documents the AMD AGESA/AGESATM host-environment interface and UEFI integration. Host BIOS code accesses AGESA through a bridge and dispatcher, passing configuration blocks and standard headers; AGESA returns status codes and uses a call-out port and host router for reverse calls. Calls require a valid stack, and only published entry points should be used. Entry-point identifiers are provided in AMD.H, with AmdBridge32.asm supplied as an example bridge implementation.

UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases across 16-, 32-, and 64-bit modes. The passage describes AGESA libraries, build targets, assembler/compiler toolchains, platform option and control files, environment variables, and reference files for binary-module or source-integration builds. PEI components initialize processors, memory, and resets; publish PPIs and HOBs; coordinate multicore execution; and support DXE table generation, an AGESA protocol, and iGPU VGA-resource decoding.

Host procedures provide stack creation and removal, structure allocation and release, DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, processor identification, execution-cache sizing, address-to-DIMM FRU mapping, MMIO range merging, and event-log reading. Published initialization procedures progress from reset and cache setup through early processor initialization, memory initialization, artifact transfer, graphics configuration, late ACPI/DMI table generation, and suspend/resume save-and-restore operations. Responsibilities differ between the boot processor and application processors, and procedures document dependencies, parameters, status codes, and architectural limitations. The host must provide required call-outs, preserve initialization artifacts, supply memory and storage, establish stacks, and avoid interfering with parallel core communication, cache controls, or APIC registers.

On December 21, 2015, Apple Inc.’s Board adopted amended bylaws implementing proxy access. A shareholder or group of up to 20 shareholders owning at least 3% of Apple’s common stock for at least three years may nominate directors comprising up to 20% of the Board, subject to stated requirements. The bylaws also revised advance-notice provisions and made minor conforming changes.

NEMA South East coordinator Walson Ibarakumo warned of possible floods in Enugu, Anambra and Ebonyi states, based on NIHSA and NiMET forecasts. He attributed the heavy rain, storms and wind to climate change, urged residents to conserve energy and prepare early, and identified likely flood-risk areas in each state.

DBS expects Indian government bond yields to keep rising, though more modestly after the bulk of a six-month sell-off, and favors shorter-term bonds while remaining neutral-to-negative on longer-term maturities. Easier CPI supports this view, and better entry points may emerge as increased issuance is absorbed. The rupee, down 2% YTD against the dollar, remains vulnerable to financing needs, a widened savings-investment gap and rising US rates; DBS forecasts depreciation toward 67.

Al-Qaida-linked Syrian militants shot down a Russian Su-25 fighter near Saraqeb in Idlib, according to Syrian monitors and Russia’s Defense Ministry, which said the pilot was killed after fighting militants. The pilot reportedly resisted capture and opened fire before being shot. A social-media video purportedly showing his body could not be independently verified.

Russian and Syrian aircraft and helicopter gunships struck rebel-held Saraqeb and nearby Tel Mardeekh as government forces advanced in Idlib. The U.N. reported that more than 270,000 people had been displaced since Dec. 15.

In northern Syria, Turkish forces and allied Syrian opposition fighters clashed with the U.S.-backed YPG in Afrin. Turkey said three soldiers had been killed, while eight Turkish soldiers and at least 24 allied fighters had died since the Jan. 20 offensive began. Turkish spokesman Ibrahim Kalin demanded that the YPG withdraw east of the Euphrates and leave Manbij, called on the U.S. to disengage, and hinted that the operation might expand eastward.

Mentoring relationships with adults and peers—including school staff, volunteers, family members, community leaders, and cross-age peers—can improve students’ academic achievement, attendance, school connectedness, engagement, behavior, graduation, and college attainment. Such relationships occur through in-school and after-school programs, as well as naturally in communities. Their availability is uneven: youth of color, low-income youth, and youth with less-educated parents generally have fewer mentoring relationships.

The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted students’ learning and relationships with caring adults, with disproportionate effects on low-income students, students of color, students with disabilities, and marginalized youth. By the end of the 2020–21 school year, the average student was reported to be five months behind in mathematics and four months behind in reading. Surveys also found low levels of adult availability and school belonging, while nearly half of students identified depression and anxiety as obstacles to learning.

Meta-analyses and research syntheses conclude that well-designed mentoring programs generally improve educational outcomes, including attendance, grades, test scores, classroom behavior, school connectedness, and educational self-confidence. Effects are often moderate to large when programs use evidence-based practices, address cultural and social barriers, and teach skills such as managing academic stress and setting educational goals. Cross-age peer mentoring can improve belonging and attendance while benefiting both younger students and older mentors’ leadership and engagement.

Representative studies found that school-based programs such as Big Brothers Big Sisters, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, and Check and Connect improved academic performance, attendance, credits, graduation prospects, or disciplinary behavior. After-school programs, including Quantum Opportunities, Village Model of Care, and Canada’s Pathways to Education, were associated with stronger grades, graduation, college acceptance or enrollment, and other positive outcomes.

Natural mentoring by teachers and other school personnel is likewise associated with stronger school attachment, motivation, academic performance, graduation, and educational attainment, with particular benefits reported for students of color. The passage calls for expanded access to mentoring through private and public investment and local, state, and federal action.

Xiaomi’s Redmi 5 went on sale in India at noon through Amazon India, Mi.com, and Mi Home stores, starting at Rs 7,999. Its three variants are 2GB/16GB at Rs 7,999, 3GB/32GB at Rs 8,999, and 4GB/64GB at Rs 10,999. The smartphone has a 5.7-inch HD+ 18:9 display, metal unibody, rear fingerprint scanner, Snapdragon 450 processor, 3300mAh battery, 12MP rear and 5MP front cameras, microSD expansion, and 4G connectivity. He declined to seek Senate ratification of the 1853 U.S.–Mexico convention on a transit way across the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, citing its potentially indefinite guarantees for a private company’s contract, personnel, property, and capital. These obligations were especially burdensome because Mexico was susceptible to civil wars and public vicissitudes, and withdrawal required a year’s notice. He also maintained that ratification would violate obligations under the 1850 U.S.–Great Britain convention, which covered interoceanic communication through the isthmus.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 25, 2015 describes a fabless visual-computing business with two reporting segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, serving Gaming, Enterprise, High Performance Computing and Cloud, and Automotive markets. Its business model includes branded products and services, processor sales to original equipment manufacturers, and intellectual-property licensing. Major GPU brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, and GRID, while Tegra processors support SHIELD and DRIVE products and are also sold to OEMs. CUDA enables GPUs to accelerate general-purpose computing. NVIDIA reported investing more than $10 billion in research and development since inception and holding about 7,000 patent assets.

NVIDIA uses third-party foundries, including TSMC and Samsung, to manufacture wafers and independent subcontractors to assemble, test, and package products. It maintains substantial inventories to support short semiconductor lead times. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $4.62 billion at fiscal year-end, which management said was sufficient for operating, acquisition, capital-purchase, and shareholder-return needs for at least 12 months. The company had 9,228 employees, including 6,658 in research and development, and spent $1.36 billion on R&D in fiscal 2015. Its largest customer represented 11% of fiscal 2015 revenue, and revenue from customers outside the United States and Other Americas represented 75%.

The filing identifies risks including intense competition, dependence on design wins and customer purchasing decisions, product defects, cybersecurity incidents, reliance on third-party manufacturers, manufacturing-yield and supply constraints, natural disasters and geographic concentration, customer concentration, demand-forecasting errors, margin pressure, international operations, acquisitions, intellectual-property litigation, fluctuating results, indebtedness and potential dilution, and provisions that could impede a change in control. NVIDIA also discloses litigation filed against Qualcomm and Samsung entities over GPU patents and a subsequent Samsung complaint against NVIDIA and Velocity Micro.

For fiscal 2015, NVIDIA reported revenue of $4.68 billion, operating income of $759.0 million, net income of $630.6 million, diluted earnings per share of $1.12, total assets of $7.20 billion, long-term debt of $1.38 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $4.42 billion. During the year it repurchased 44.4 million shares for $813.6 million and paid $186.5 million in dividends, returning $1.0 billion to shareholders. The quarterly dividend was $0.085 per share, or $0.34 annually, and $434.8 million remained authorized for repurchases through January 2016. NVIDIA announced plans to return approximately $600 million to shareholders in fiscal 2016.

Fiscal 2015 developments included shipping Maxwell-based GeForce GPUs, surpassing 50 million GeForce Experience installations, introducing Tesla K80, announcing Pascal architecture details, expanding VMware GRID support, launching Tegra X1 and Jetson TK1, adding SHIELD devices, and introducing DRIVE automotive computers. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements depend on assumptions and are subject to risks that could cause actual results to differ materially.

COVID-19 outbreaks in nursing homes caused substantial morbidity and mortality, and vaccination reduced infections and severe outcomes, although the durability of immune responses remained uncertain. A longitudinal public-health surveillance evaluation studied SARS-CoV-2 infection and Pfizer-BioNTech vaccination among residents of a 149-bed Georgia nursing home from October 2020 through April 2021. Visits occurred every other day for the first four visits and monthly thereafter, with symptom questionnaires, medical-record review, nasal testing by BinaxNOW and RT-PCR, viral culture, and serum antibody testing for pan-immunoglobulin, IgG, IgA, and IgM.

Of 12 enrolled residents, 11 were analyzed; one died before the second follow-up. Participants had a median age of 74, substantial comorbidities, and generally severe or medically complex conditions. Four had severe COVID-19 and were hospitalized, one died during follow-up, and two were asymptomatic. Ten participants received two vaccine doses and one declined vaccination. The analysis included 166 nasal and 61 blood specimens.

Post-infection, 9 of 10 participants with post-infection serology developed detectable pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA, while 8 developed IgM. Median detection times were 13 days for pan-Ig and IgG, 16 days for IgA, and 15 days for IgM. At first antibody detection, 6 of 9 remained RT-PCR positive, but none had positive viral cultures; antibody detection did not correspond to negative RT-PCR or BinaxNOW results. Pan-Ig and IgG titers rose and remained elevated, whereas IgM and IgA began declining after 30 days and sometimes became undetectable by 50 days. One unvaccinated participant retained detectable pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA for at least 150 days.

After vaccination, all 10 vaccinated participants had detectable pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA, and six had detectable IgM. Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers exceeded pre-vaccination levels, with peak post-vaccination-to-post-infection geometric mean ratios of 142.3 for pan-Ig, 200.5 for IgG, and 4.4 for IgA. Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers began decreasing during 61–90 days after vaccination, while all post-vaccination IgM titers were undetectable during that interval. Using cited criteria, all vaccinated participants surpassed an IgG threshold associated with 80% vaccine efficacy two weeks after the second dose.

The findings indicate that infected nursing home residents developed diverse, durable binding-antibody responses and that vaccination augmented pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA responses. Seroconversion may mark absence of culturable virus before vaccination. Limitations included the small sample, use of only Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, infrequent or missed specimen collection, uncertain illness-severity classification, limited observation of antibody duration, and data collected before the Delta and Omicron variants emerged.

Indianapolis blew six leads, including four double-digit second-half advantages, before losing 13-7 in overtime. A late flag negated Jacoby Brissett’s apparent go-ahead touchdown pass, forcing Adam Vinatieri to make a 43-yard extra point in a blizzard to tie the game. The four-game losing streak is the longest in Frank Pagano’s six-year tenure; Indianapolis is eliminated from playoff contention, and attention has turned to Pagano’s future. Cold weather left players fatigued before Thursday’s game against Denver. Kelly and Rashaan Melvin practiced, while Donte Moncrief is week-to-week with an ankle injury.

The passage argues that Oclaro (OCLR) is reasonably valued and well positioned among optical-network companies because it has less legacy business and greater exposure to newer, high-growth products. Fiscal 2017 revenue rose 47%, margins expanded 11 points to 39%, and EPS reached $0.79, up 460%.

Demand for 100G products is strong: 100G represented 81% of Q4 revenue, QSFP28 sales doubled sequentially, and datacenters drove growth. Legacy CFP and 40G products declined as customers transitioned. Chinese demand remained mixed, with Q4 revenue down 11% sequentially, China’s revenue share falling from 36% to 32%, and further declines expected. Management nevertheless expects growth in 25G and 100G transceivers for 5G front-haul deployments.

Longer-term demand drivers include streaming, cloud computing, virtualization, IoT, 4G/5G, and AI. Oclaro is also beginning to generate modest 400G revenue and expects related products to grow. Its high-speed focus is presented as reducing legacy revenue losses, supporting higher margins, and providing exposure to high-growth segments.

Oclaro had no debt, $258 million in cash and short-term investments, $46 million in operating cash flow, and $11.5 million in free cash flow, with a P/E below 11. Q1 guidance called for revenue of $151 million–$159 million, gross margin of 38%–41%, and operating income of $30 million–$34 million. The author sees limited reasons for further decline absent broad market weakness and considers a major cyclical downturn unlikely, while noting geopolitical and broader market risks.

The court affirmed the Commissioner of Patents’ dismissal of Lever Brothers’ opposition to Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners’ service mark for dry-cleaning and pressing services. Although Lever Brothers had extensively used and advertised “Lux” for soap products, the court held that “Thrift-D-Lux” conveys thrift combined with de luxe quality, rather than “Thrifty Lux.” Because “de luxe” was commonly used in trademarks and trade names, restricting it would improperly limit a public-domain term. The cited precedents were distinguishable because they involved identical suffixes or closely related goods sold through similar channels. Although some affiliated “Lux Laundries” also performed dry cleaning, the record contained no evidence sufficient to establish likely confusion or damage from registration of the service mark.

An outside day is a two-bar pattern in which the current bar has a higher high and lower low than the previous bar, with its open and close extending beyond the prior bar. It consumes the previous bar’s full range, signals rising volatility, and can indicate buyer or seller control.

Outside days have four configurations based on whether the first and second bars are up or down. When both bars move in opposite directions, the pattern is an outside reversal. Outside days may act as continuation patterns when aligned with the prevailing trend or as reversal patterns when opposed to it. Bullish and bearish outside days resemble stronger versions of bullish and bearish engulfing patterns.

Because interpretation depends heavily on context, outside bars should not be traded alone. Analysts are advised to combine them with trend, support and resistance, pivot, and Fibonacci analysis.

Backtests found little usefulness for day trading. In his inaugural address, the speaker thanks President Reagan, honors George Washington and the nation’s democratic continuity, and begins his presidency with a prayer emphasizing that power should serve people. James Horne, a plastic surgeon, sued the New York State Department of Health under Executive Law § 296, alleging disability discrimination in the revocation of his medical license based on adult ADD. The court held that his action was an untimely CPLR article 78 challenge to that revocation. The Appellate Division affirmed because his relief required reversal of the Administrative Review Board’s decision. It rejected the contention that an independent action was permissible merely because the statute said “may,” and did not reach the res judicata or collateral estoppel issues. The dismissal was affirmed without costs.

The Thompson Oil Company recovered a Pennsylvania judgment against Snow and others, then assigned it for value to Pennsylvania residents before a New York creditor obtained a foreign attachment against the debtors. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court held the assignment valid and effective everywhere, transferring all of Thompson’s interest and leaving it without an attachable interest in the judgment. The assignees nevertheless took the judgment subject to existing equities and any payments made before notice of the assignment.

A later New York judgment against the attached debtors did not defeat the assignees’ rights because they were neither parties nor privies to the New York proceeding, and the New York court lacked jurisdiction over them or the assigned property. Although the Full Faith and Credit Clause requires recognition of sister-state judgments, it permits inquiry into whether the rendering court had jurisdiction. The garnishees’ payment did not bar recovery by the assignees.

The issue concerning production of the New York record was treated as waived after the parties submitted a supplemental record. The judgment entered for the assignees on the demurrer was affirmed.

Northern Ireland’s health service, the only UK region without a minister, faces an ageing population, complex care needs, GP staffing problems, rising drug costs and long hospital waiting lists, despite an extra £30m. Prosecutors argued Copeland stabbed Thomas with a steak knife during a brawl that followed online taunts and insults. Copeland’s attorney said she carried but did not use the knife and that blood would have splattered onto her clothes if she had.

William Green concludes the course by reviewing stochastic simulation methods and how to select among them. He explains that Bayesian analysis combines a likelihood with prior information to form a weighting function \(w(\theta)\). Multidimensional integrals weighted by this function can yield expected values, distributions, and parameter correlations using Metropolis Monte Carlo. Its efficiency depends strongly on the step size in each dimension: overly large steps produce mostly rejected transitions, while overly small steps explore the space too slowly. Adaptive step sizing can help, with acceptance ratios around 0.2–0.8 cited as a rule of thumb. Reliable results require sampling all accessible regions, testing sensitivity to initial states, and checking answers against expected magnitudes before calculation. Irrelevant dimensions should also be eliminated. Monte Carlo initially provides reasonable estimates but scales as \(1/\sqrt{n}\), so each additional significant figure can require roughly 100 times more sampling.

For nonstationary systems described by differential equations, Green introduces Kinetic Monte Carlo using the Gillespie algorithm. He illustrates this with a catalytic surface containing 100 sites, each of which may be empty or occupied by A, B, or coke. The resulting \(4^{100}\) possible states make explicit probability vectors and transition matrices impossible to store or exhaustively sample. A Gillespie trajectory uses one random number to select a waiting time and another to select an event. Time must be calculated when kinetic information matters; otherwise, only the sequence of states is needed. Initial surface populations can be sampled from Poisson distributions based on known averages. Because many trajectories are required, relevant averages and diagnostics should be computed during simulation rather than storing every trajectory.

Kinetic Monte Carlo can be accelerated by treating fast diffusion as instantaneous or deliberately slowing it, removing rare processes that cannot be sampled, and limiting the state space. The accuracy of rare events is limited by large statistical margins of error, while very fast processes can make trajectories computationally expensive.

Green also reviews molecular dynamics, which solves atomic equations of motion using force fields, optional quantum effects, velocity-Verlet integration, and thermostats. It provides real-time information and can reproduce picosecond- or nanosecond-scale processes, but its very small time steps limit accessible durations and make it unsuitable for many slower equilibrium or conformational transitions. Initial configurations may therefore require separate sampling.

Finally, he discusses choosing efficient Monte Carlo weighting functions by rewriting an integrand as \(p f\), seeking a nearly constant \(f\) and sharply focused \(p\). Unimportant parameters can be removed through marginal integration, and velocities are sometimes integrated out in Boltzmann calculations. Green concludes that Metropolis Monte Carlo, Kinetic Monte Carlo, and molecular dynamics suit different problems, so the method should be chosen according to whether equilibrium, kinetics, or time-dependent behavior is needed.

Rangers players Marian Gaborik and Dwight King addressed the media ahead of tomorrow's playoff game at Madison Square Garden. Having lost their last three games by two-goal deficits, they emphasized needing better starts, with Gaborik noting that scoring first jump-starts their offense and that three straight losses and extra periods have been tough. King said the team's days off should be used for physical recovery, sleep, and relaxation, and that players must work within rules protecting goaltenders by creating traffic. King added that home ice, momentum, and quick shifts in a series' tide matter in the playoffs and that opponents will be ready at their home building.

Gaborik, appearing in his first Stanley Cup Final and visiting the renovated Garden for the first time since being traded, said the building's history gives teams extra energy and that its fans will support a strong effort. Both said the Rangers have vocal leaders, a calm mindset, and confidence in themselves and their teammates, and they intend to bring a better performance to the table.

Zeta Global has agreed to acquire Marigold’s enterprise software business for $325 million, its largest acquisition to date and its 17th. The deal includes Marigold’s Loyalty brand, Cheetah Digital and Sailthru email platforms, and Selligent marketing automation. Marigold will continue operating its small- and midsize-focused business, including Campaign Monitor, Emma, and Vuture. Zeta expects the acquisition to expand its Fortune 500 customer base, strengthen its presence in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, and add loyalty data to improve targeting and advertising algorithms. It will pay $100 million in cash and $100 million in shares upfront, with the remaining $125 million due through a seller note within three months after closing.

The patent application concerns methods, compositions, kits, and systems for detecting premalignant or malignant gastric neoplasia through DNA methylation analysis. It identifies 123 candidate methylation markers using reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing and case-control comparisons of gastric cancer tissue with normal stomach, colon, blood, and plasma DNA. Validation produced panels of 10, 30, and 12 gastric-cancer markers, including ELMO1, ZNF569, C13ORF18, CD1D, ARHGEF4, SFMBT2, ABCB1, CLEC11A, ST8SIA1, CYP26C1, and PPP2R5C.

The methods assess methylation in differentially methylated regions designated DMR 1-274 and compare results with non-neoplastic controls. Suitable samples include gastric tissue, plasma, stool, other blood samples, and urine. Methylation may be measured using bisulfite treatment, methylation-specific PCR, quantitative allele-specific real-time target and signal amplification, sequencing, mass spectrometry, methylation-sensitive restriction enzymes, target capture, and related methods. Methylation percentages can be calculated from methylated and unmethylated DNA quantities, with standard curves and Ct values.

Provided embodiments include oligonucleotides, primers, probes, reaction mixtures, master mixes, kits, controls, and sample-collection materials. Computer-based systems can compare methylation states, calculate statistics, ROC curves, AUC values, and composite cancer-risk scores, and issue alerts. In reported plasma testing, a three-marker panel comprising ELMO1, ZNF569, and C13ORF18 detected gastric cancer with 86% sensitivity at 100% specificity, while methylated ELMO1 levels increased with cancer stage.

A study presented at the International Astronautical Congress identified 50 objects in low Earth orbit most likely to create additional debris through collisions. Traveling at nearly 5 miles per second, 76% were deposited before 2000 and 88% are rocket bodies. Russia and the Soviet Union account for 34 objects, followed by China with 10, the United States with three, Europe with two, and Japan with one. Removing all 50 would reduce the orbit’s overall debris-generating potential by 50%, while removing the top 10 would reduce it by 30%.

Since January 2024, 26 hazardous rocket bodies have been abandoned, 21 from Chinese launches. Upper stages used for China’s Guowang and Thousand Sails megaconstellations have remained in orbit, violating 25-year reentry guidelines. Continued deployment could leave more than 100 additional rocket bodies.

Some Chinese rockets cannot restart in orbit, while deorbit burns reduce payload capacity, although the Long March 5’s YZ-2 stage can deorbit itself. China is researching debris removal, though cleanup technologies may have military applications. Limited cleanup projects and demonstrations are underway in Europe and Japan.

East Dunbartonshire Council faces worsening industrial relations, with GMB, Unison and Unite strike action scheduled for July 12–15, affecting refuse collections and depot operations. Action short of strikes continues, service impacts are being assessed, and union discussions remain scheduled.

Petitioner Buchanan was convicted of murdering his wife by poison. He sought a federal writ of error, alleging that his conviction violated due process and the right to an impartial jury because juror Paradise became ill and mentally incapacitated during deliberations. After being treated, Paradise rejoined the jury; the jury was instructed to confer again and returned a guilty verdict. Conflicting medical evidence was presented concerning whether Paradise had suffered epilepsy or another mental disorder or merely nervous exhaustion and hysteria. The trial court found no juror incompetency or prejudice from the jurors’ temporary separation and denied a new trial; the New York Court of Appeals affirmed.

The U.S. Supreme Court held that, even assuming Buchanan’s federal claim was sufficiently presented, the juror’s physical and mental condition and competency to participate in the verdict were questions of fact. A federal court reviewing a state court’s judgment on writ of error could not overturn the state court’s determination on those issues. The application was therefore denied.

Cerebras Systems withdrew its proposed IPO, saying in an SEC filing that it does not intend to conduct the offering “at this time.” The announcement came days after the AI chipmaker raised $1.1 billion at an $8.1 billion valuation and more than a year after filing to go public on the Nasdaq. A spokesperson said Cerebras still hopes to go public soon and that the government shutdown did not influence the decision. The company has shifted toward cloud services using its chips, while CEO Andrew Feldman said the original prospectus was outdated because of developments in AI.

The UN World Water Development Report 2018 praised community-led, nature-based water solutions as population growth, economic development, changing consumption and climate change increase global water demand. It warned that five billion people could live in areas with poor water access by 2050, while 3.6 billion already face seasonal scarcity. In Rajasthan, Tarun Bharat Sangh’s restoration of soils, forests and water-harvesting structures increased forest cover by 30%, raised groundwater levels and improved farmland productivity. Similar efforts increased groundwater levels by an estimated six metres, productive farmland from 20% to 80%, and forest cover by 33%, with women playing key roles in securing safe freshwater. The report also cited China’s rainwater recycling, India’s forest regeneration and Ukraine’s artificial wetlands. It highlighted SDG 6’s goal of universal access to safe drinking water and adequate sanitation and hygiene by 2030.

Six-year-old Ryan stars in “Ryan ToysReview,” which his parents began filming when he was three. The family posts daily videos of him opening, reviewing, and playing with toys. It lacks Pixel Screenshots and Call Notes, while the $999-class Pixel 10 adds a brighter display, Tensor G5 chip, louder speakers, Qi2 charging, sharper selfies and a 5X optical telephoto camera. The Pixel 10 Pro and Pro XL are the highest-end slab phones, with 16GB of RAM, vapor-chamber cooling, brighter LTPO displays, larger camera sensors, Wi-Fi 7, Pro Res Zoom up to 100X and cloud-processed Video Boost that can upscale footage to 8K. Safety and accessibility features include cough and snore detection, audio-guided selfies, theft protection, identity checks, Private Space, satellite emergency SOS, crash detection, Find Hub, Circle to Search, external-display support and adaptive vibration.

In Lewis v. Bayer AG, the court considered certification of four proposed classes arising from alleged injuries associated with Baycol (cerivastatin), a cholesterol-lowering drug withdrawn from the market in August 2001. Plaintiffs alleged that Baycol and other statins can cause rhabdomyolysis and deplete coenzyme Q10, potentially causing heart failure and other conditions.

The court granted certification in part and denied it in part. It certified a Pennsylvania class of persons who were prescribed and ingested Baycol and have not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart disease. The class seeks medical monitoring, including tests for CoQ10 depletion, elevated CK levels, and chest X-rays, together with a court-supervised monitoring program, epidemiological research, and equitable relief. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were appointed as class representatives, and plaintiffs’ counsel was appointed as class counsel.

Certification was denied for the nationwide medical-monitoring and personal-injury classes and the Pennsylvania personal-injury class because individualized causation, medical history, dosage, treatment duration, warnings, and state-law differences defeated commonality. The court also rejected certification of claims under Pennsylvania’s Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law because reliance and causation require individual proof. Although a limited unjust-enrichment subclass presented common issues, the court found insufficient evidence that the named plaintiffs were typical of that subclass. The parties were ordered to submit proposed class-notification procedures and forms within 30 days.

This continuation patent application concerns wireless-communication downlink assignments for downlink control channels and incorporates by reference U.S. patent applications Ser. Nos. 17/718,018 and 16/536,803 and provisional application Ser. No. 62/716,894.

Disclosed methods and apparatuses enable a UE to monitor PDCCH candidates associated with different control resource sets, receive downlink assignments, determine PDSCH resource allocations and DMRS symbol locations from the assignments and the control resource sets’ OFDM-symbol spans, and decode the corresponding PDSCHs. When control resource sets have different durations or overlap a PDSCH allocation, the first DMRS symbol may be placed immediately after the control resource set ending in the later OFDM symbol. The disclosure also addresses overlapping assignments, resource-block numbering, and selection of a common PUCCH acknowledgment resource.

A UE may receive identities of associated search spaces, determine their monitoring occasions, and monitor candidates across common or associated slots when the candidates are expected to carry identical DCI. This supports multi-TRP transmission of multiple PDCCHs carrying the same DCI and multiple PDSCHs carrying the same transport block, enabling blind decoding, soft combining, early termination after successful PDSCH decoding, and a single HARQ-ACK per transport block.

PDSCH repetition across consecutive TTIs is also described, including higher-layer aggregation configuration, repetition-window timing, beam and TCI consistency, soft combining, and restrictions on changing TCI interpretations during reception windows. TCI states provide quasi-colocation relationships between downlink reference signals and DMRS ports, with MAC control element activation, deactivation, codepoint mapping, and timing rules. When scheduling DCI may be received in multiple control resource sets, specified alternatives determine which control resource set governs PDSCH reception parameters and acknowledgment resources. The embodiments may be implemented in hardware, software, or combinations thereof and are illustrated by system, apparatus, search-space, and method diagrams.

A defensive switch occurs when a first defender controlling an opponent is beaten and a properly positioned support defender takes over the ball carrier while the first defender takes over the support defender’s previous opponent. The support defender should be goalside, behind and inside the first defender, while adjusting to the attacker’s movements without overrunning play and announcing their arrival. They may signal “support,” instruct the first defender to “jockey,” “contain,” or “challenge,” and call “switch” when the first defender is beaten. The resulting movement usually creates a crossing pattern led by the support defender. Defenders may also switch assignments to prevent open space or collisions, even without a dribbler, and return to their original assignments with a “switch back” or “return” call once the immediate play ends. Training progresses from stationary positioning to relative movement, communication, half-speed and full-speed scenarios, including switches down the sideline, outside, inside, and in midfield.

The study examines how the COVID-19 pandemic affected special education due process hearings involving city local education agencies (LEAs) in Pennsylvania. It compares published hearing officer decisions from the two years before and after March 16, 2020, when pandemic-related office closures occurred. The research questions address whether city LEAs appeared in more hearings after the pandemic, whether ruling outcomes differed between periods, and what remedies LEAs owed.

Pennsylvania requires LEAs to provide a free appropriate public education despite pandemic-related service changes. During closures, limited internet access and technology impeded IEP accommodations, while procedural requirements such as parental notice, Notice of Recommended Educational Placements, and timely IEP meetings remained in effect. Failure to provide FAPE was the most common post-pandemic issue nationally, and hearing officers were more likely to rule against schools. Pennsylvania also experienced substantial IDEA dispute activity, with the School District of Philadelphia generating the most hearings.

Using an ex post facto, quasi-experimental design, the researcher will review 323 unique ODR decisions published from March 16, 2018, through March 15, 2022. Non-city LEAs will be excluded, and remaining decisions will be coded into five ruling outcomes: full student, mostly student, in part for both parties or inconclusive, mostly LEA, and full LEA. Frequency distributions, chi-square testing, and remedy review will address the research questions. Remedies include independent educational evaluations, compensatory education, and financial reimbursement. The findings may identify training and support needs for Pennsylvania city LEAs.

The passage examines how the Air Force must adapt to rapidly changing cyber threats by embracing flexible training, organization, procurement and innovation. Adm. Michael Rogers argues that fixed structures, operational practices and skill sets are increasingly flawed, and that cyber forces must integrate diverse perspectives and organizations. The Air Force has begun cross-training active-duty cyber defense specialists in offensive tactics, and vice versa.

The Maryland Air National Guard’s 175th Cyberspace Operations Group is presented as a model for combining military experience with civilian expertise. Formed from 35 Airmen in 2013 and activated in 2016, the group grew to more than 200 Airmen in four squadrons responsible for offensive cyber engagement, defensive operations and operational support. Its missions included protecting Maryland government networks during the Baltimore riots, training with Estonia, supporting presidential inauguration security, and assisting the FBI, Secret Service, Homeland Security, 24th Air Force, NSA and U.S. Cyber Command.

Tech. Sgt. Kyle Hanslovan credits his self-taught, initially illicit interest in coding and gaining online access with preparing him for defensive Air Force duties, later work as a Defense Department contractor and CEO of a cybersecurity startup. He said civilian experience helps ANG Airmen anticipate attacks and strengthens offensive operations. The group also draws on personnel with backgrounds in software development, system architecture, training, information technology and other fields, creating broader operational choices than those available to commanders working only with traditionally trained personnel.

The group’s organizational culture emphasizes transparency, open criticism across ranks and the rapid exchange of ideas. Members apply lessons from civilian and military cyber competitions, including DEFCON Capture the Flag events, to operational work. The National Guard’s 2017 Innovations Program encourages Airmen to propose and rapidly implement new ideas rather than waiting years for formal policies and solutions.

Col. Kevin George said cyber personnel require continual intelligence on vulnerabilities, threats, tools and patches. Combining private-sector knowledge with Air Force training creates a “force multiplier,” while ANG personnel’s continuity may help develop specialized capabilities such as software tools, data analytics and artificial intelligence that are difficult to sustain amid active-duty personnel rotations.

Robinson and Hanslovan also identified personnel challenges. The Air Force must balance promotion opportunities for technical leaders with members who prefer hands-on keyboard work, expand recruitment, and retain scarce expertise. Hanslovan noted that civilian firms can hire within weeks, compared with months in the Air Force, and that ANG service arrangements make retaining full-time specialists difficult. Despite these concerns, they viewed the Air Force as encouraging needed innovation and dialogue, while Robinson has since been named vice commander of the 175th Wing.

Apple is reportedly debuting a “blush gold” iPhone 8 in September. Leaks from Benjamin Geskin show alleged 64GB and 128GB models; the phone is also rumored to feature an edge-to-edge screen, no home button, and wireless charging. Its final color name remains uncertain.

WHO data show Delhi’s average PM2.5 concentration at 150 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with London’s 16.
