After hours, Amazon rose over 6%, Alphabet fell nearly 3% and Apple fell about 1%.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority has designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status, granting it greater regulatory powers over Google’s “substantial and entrenched market power.” Possible measures include allowing users to choose rival search engines, enforcing fair-ranking principles, increasing data portability, and requiring permission to use publishers’ content in AI Overviews. The CMA says Google handles over 90% of UK general searches, while UK firms spent more than £10 billion on Google search advertising in 2024. Google warned that interventions could inhibit innovation, harm businesses and raise prices. Google News and Gemini are excluded, but the Search News tab, Top Stories carousel and Google Discover are affected.

**Summary**

Giuriato and Lovecchio (2025) examined whether increasing physical education (PE) hours, using cognitively engaging activities, improves attention in middle school students. Sixty-five... (corrected) A total of 75 students (36 girls, 48%) from two secondary classes participated: Class 6 received four PE hours per week and Class 7 received two hours, with 41 students in the experimental group and 34 in the control group; randomization was applied at class level because individual reassignment was not feasible. Attention was assessed with the validated Bells Test (Biancardi and Stoppa, 1997), administered in October and December, producing three measures: Processing Speed Score (bells identified in the first 30 seconds), Total Detection Score (bells over 120 seconds), and Error Rate. The PE curriculum featured agility drills, coordination circuits, and strategic team games such as volleyball and badminton. Normality was checked with the Shapiro-Wilk test and a one-way ANOVA assessed group differences; Classes 6 and 7 were analysed separately because attention depends on cognitive maturation, and no gender comparisons were made.

Results showed significant improvements in 30-second bell counts for the experimental groups in both Class 6 and Class 7 (p < 0.001), while control groups showed no significant change. Sustained attention (120 seconds) improved significantly only in Class 6 (p = 0.012), with no notable change in Class 7. Authors noted that four PE hours per week produced greater benefits than two, suggesting 120 minutes weekly may be insufficient. Benefits for accuracy and prolonged attention were less consistent, so caution is advised in generalizing. Cognitive load from activities may have contributed, but this was not directly evidenced. Greater improvement in short-duration tests may reflect contemporary shorter attention spans amid digital media use; extending motor activity duration is recommended to train sustained attention.

Limitations include contextual factors (schedules, fatigue, extracurricular activities), limited generalizability to other age groups, and untested differences between activity types. The study concludes that increased PE hours with strategically designed activities can improve short-term attention, with activities preferably placed at the start of the school day; further research is needed on long-term and content-specific effects.

Rockwood School District in Missouri keeps students together for grade-level instruction and uses flexible, needs-based groups within each grade for reteaching or enrichment. All students receive daily phonics and comprehension lessons, while multilingual learners, struggling readers, and advanced readers receive scaffolds or more complex work. The approach also includes independent and partner reading, targeted specialist interventions, shared reading, and movement-based learning activities.

The author argues against grouping students across grades by reading ability, citing research involving nearly 12,000 students that found children in the lowest kindergarten reading groups rarely caught up with peers. Removing students from grade-level classrooms may also reduce their access to complex vocabulary, shared texts, and academic discussion.

According to Rockwood’s 2024–25 data, kindergarteners exceeded national proficiency averages in every skill group, sometimes by more than 17 percentage points, while first and second graders exceeded national averages in nearly every domain. The author says this model builds literacy, confidence, stamina, and joy without claiming it will work equally well in every district or classroom.

The application describes hardware for implementing deep neural networks, particularly convolutional neural networks, with configurable activation modules. After neural-network optimization, calibration data is processed by actual or simulated hardware while inputs to each activation module are monitored to determine its likely operating range. The range may be based on observed extrema, a histogram, or selected distribution percentiles. Lookup data approximating each required activation function—such as data points, gradient and offset pairs, or linear or quadratic curve segments—is then generated over that range and loaded into a programmable lookup table.

The activation modules support offsets to center inputs, clamping or extrapolation for out-of-range values, and interpolation between adjacent lookup-table entries using input MSBs for addressing and LSBs for interpolation. Even and odd table entries may be stored separately for simultaneous access, and multiple table sets may permit new data to be loaded while another set is in use. Lookup data may be generated separately for each activation function, hardware pass, or module.

A configurable CNN implementation includes memory and buffer controllers, convolution engines, accumulators, activation, normalization, pooling, and shared-buffer components. An activation module may combine a lookup-table path with a ReLU path, bypassing or disabling the unused path to reduce power and using ReLU logic for clamping.

The methods and hardware may be implemented in software, firmware, fixed logic, or integrated circuits, with corresponding computer-readable code, storage media, and integrated-circuit manufacturing systems.

China announced it will close its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017, targeting the world’s largest ivory market, where most ivory is carved into decorative objects. African elephant populations have fallen sharply despite a 1989 international ivory-trade ban because pre-ban ivory remained legal, allowing newly poached ivory to be passed off as older. Conservationists said China’s action could reduce demand and inspire similar measures elsewhere.
A global study of 198 honey samples found 75% contained neonicotinoid pesticides; 45% contained multiple compounds. Rates were highest in North America (86%), followed by Asia (80%) and Europe (79%).

Platinum is a rare, silver-white, soft and ductile metal in the platinum group metals. Its high melting point, corrosion resistance, catalytic properties, and uses in jewelry and automotive catalytic converters underpin its value and demand.

Platinum futures are standardized, legally binding contracts on the CME Globex platform for the physical delivery of 50 troy ounces of platinum on a specified future date. Prices are quoted in U.S. dollars and cents per troy ounce; the minimum fluctuation is $0.10, or $5 per contract. Trading runs Sunday through Friday, with a daily one-hour halt from 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. Central Time. Trading ends on the third-last business day of the contract month. Investors can also gain exposure through CFDs, ETFs, options, stocks, or physical platinum.

A platinum futures strategy typically combines technical and fundamental analysis with market timing, position sizing, risk management, and precise entry and exit rules. It may be used to speculate on prices, diversify a portfolio, hedge inflation or industry exposure, or manage commodity-related risk. The article emphasizes backtesting with defined rules and recommends evaluating statistical expectancy, correlation with existing strategies, risk tolerance, goals, experience, and trading costs. It considers gold a stronger long-term store of value and platinum more of an industrial commodity.

One backtest combined long and short monthly signals across 473 trades, producing a 64% win rate, 0.57% average unleveraged gain, and 1.7 profit factor, with returns described as uncorrelated to the stock market. A second seasonal strategy, trading on a specified day with a volume requirement, produced 60 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.66% average gain, and 2.3 profit factor. The passage states that platinum futures historically perform better in winter and spring than in summer and fall.

Platinum prices are affected by supply and demand, production costs, economic and political events, mining-country instability, automotive and jewelry demand, and substitute materials. South Africa is cited as producing about 80% of global supply and holding 90% of proven reserves. Major risks include leveraged losses, volatile markets, physical-delivery obligations, and the difficulty of developing a consistent edge in commodities. As of December 14, 2022, platinum futures traded at $1,036.90; the cited all-time high was $2,308.80 in March 2008, and the low was $267.10 in July 1985.

Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship demonstrates that high-dosage virtual tutoring can improve achievement, support educators, and recruit future teachers. Over five years, Ignite reached more than 40 communities, hundreds of schools, and over 5,500 trained virtual tutors; in the latest school year, more than 2,000 fellows delivered nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning. Middle-school math scores grew at up to 2.5 times the expected rate, while elementary readers improved up to three times faster than average.

The program emphasizes structured tutor training and coaching, using technology to expand relationships rather than replace them, and treating tutoring as a teacher-pipeline strategy. Cited research found that serving as an Ignite tutor nearly tripled the likelihood of applying to Teach For America’s teaching program, with the strongest effects among men, people of color, and non-education majors. Since launch, 550 fellows have joined TFA’s teaching corps. The author argues that tutoring should be a funded, long-term instructional strategy—not merely pandemic remediation—because it can advance student learning and strengthen the next generation of educators.

This review section from the *International Journal of Reviews* (Vol. 2, Issue 1, pp. 100–124, Feb. 2024) summarizes 41 publications (2020–2024) on higher education quality, online teaching, and quality assurance.

Ramírez-Hurtado et al. (2021) assess online teaching service quality during COVID-19 using SERVQUAL dimensions (tangibles, reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy) and a mixed-methods design, finding technological infrastructure, instructor competence, and institutional support central to quality. Karsono et al. (2022) examine leadership spirituality in Indonesian higher education, reporting positive links with student engagement, faculty satisfaction, and academic performance, and highlighting visionary, ethical leadership and spiritually grounded development programmes. Anastasiadou and Taraza (2020), using qualitative literature review and case studies, identify resistance to change—fear of the unknown, loss of control, weak buy-in, entrenched culture—as an obstacle to quality, emphasizing leadership, supportive climates, and systemic change management. Elumalai et al. (2021) examine e-learning quality from students' perspectives, stressing technological infrastructure and digital literacy, instructional design, social interaction and peer support, timely feedback, and academic advising. Tight (2020) reviews quality assurance and management research, covering accreditation, internal audits and peer review, methodological approaches, and critical concerns including standardization, bureaucratization, performativity and commodification.

Shahzad et al. (2021) compare male and female students' COVID-19 e-learning experiences, noting additional challenges for female students from household and caregiving duties and gender norms, and advocating gender-sensitive design. Dagiene et al. (2022) report higher education leaders' views, identifying organizational resilience, technological readiness, pedagogical innovation, stakeholder engagement, financial stability and crisis management as critical factors, with the pandemic seen as a catalyst for transformative change. Naim and Alahmari (2020) present a reference model for e-learning interoperability and quality; Del Río-Rama et al. (2021) link perceived service quality to student loyalty; Khodadad Hoseiny et al. (2023) apply flow theory, TAM and e-service quality to e-learning acceptance; and Cavallone et al. (2022) examine convergences and divergences in quality expectations between students and faculty.

A large group of Kayyali papers addresses university rankings and their relationship to academic quality, their pros and cons, their importance in academia, their use in combating diploma mills and in accreditation processes, and their critiques and limitations; other chapters cover the post-COVID-19 era in higher education, the rise and worthiness of online learning, EEDI as key performance indicators, high technology's positive impact, quality assurance concepts and frameworks, the evolution of quality assurance systems, the UN SDGs as ranking indicators, ISO 21001 with globalization and internationalization, universities as agents of change, career development, virtual universities, ICT-based governance and entrepreneurship, AI's future possibilities and challenges, big data in management, recognition of non-formal and informal learning, academic freedom challenges, and faculty development. Additional works include Lukita et al. (2020) on Curriculum 4.0 and Industry 4.0, De Wit and Altbach (2021) on internationalization, Bovill (2020) on whole-class co-creation, Sotivoldievich and Rakhimdjanovich (2021) on demonstration as a pedagogical method, and Pedro and Kumar (2020) on institutional support for online teaching. The latter entries are largely described in tentative terms ("likely," "may"), reflecting summarized content.

The conclusion states that higher education publishing is undergoing dynamic shifts driven by new models and technologies, including open access and collaborative digital platforms, with growing emphasis on inclusivity, accessibility, and agility in scholarly communication.

The study introduces GeoSQL-Eval, an end-to-end automated framework for evaluating large language models that generate natural-language-to-PostGIS queries, and GeoSQL-Bench, a corresponding benchmark. GeoSQL-Bench contains 14,178 questions across conceptual multiple-choice/true-false tasks, syntax-level SQL generation, and table-schema retrieval. Sources include the PostGIS 3.5 manual and UN-GGIM/ISO geospatial themes; GPT-4o assisted with formatting and generalization, while three experts reviewed and validated the questions.

The framework evaluates conceptual understanding, structured SQL generation, semantic alignment and function invocation, execution and result accuracy, and robustness across five capability levels and 20 task categories. It uses AST parsing, real PostGIS execution, schema and function matching, type-aware geometric comparisons, repeated generations, pass@n, stability-adjusted accuracy, entropy weighting, resource tracking, and error logging. Twenty-four models across six categories were tested.

Results show that general reasoning-enhanced and non-reasoning models generally perform best, with GPT-5, o4-mini, and DeepSeek-R1-0528 ranking highly. Conceptual knowledge is relatively strong, but semantic alignment—especially function selection and argument matching—is a major bottleneck. Syntactically valid SQL often fails to execute, and schema-retrieval tasks are harder than isolated syntax tasks. PostGIS-function and SQL-syntax errors dominate, together accounting for roughly 70% of errors. Reasoning models improve multi-attempt success but remain vulnerable to underspecified prompts; o4-mini provides the strongest balance of accuracy and efficiency. SpatialSQL performs competitively on schema retrieval.

Limitations include emphasis on PostGIS vector functions, exclusion of raster, network, and advanced spatial modules, focus on PostGIS rather than other spatial platforms, and incomplete model coverage.

The author returns House Bill 7864 without approval because it would radically restrict U.S. immigration. Its first section would exclude immigrants over 16 who cannot read or write English or another language, while allowing certain illiterate parents, grandparents, wives, and minor children to accompany qualified immigrants. Applicants would have to read and write 20–25 words of the Constitution, and those failing would be returned at their carriers’ expense.

The author argues that recent immigration problems do not justify abandoning the nation’s longstanding policy of welcoming immigrants capable of contributing through labor. Claims of urban overcrowding and unemployment were not shown to result primarily from immigration; unemployment was attributed largely to economic depression. Literacy would not effectively prevent disorder, which the author says is more often incited by educated agitators than by illiterate laborers. The family exceptions are also criticized as incomplete, burdensome, and uncertain.

The bill would also prohibit certain male aliens from working on federal public works or repeatedly entering the country for private wage labor, and would make employing such aliens unlawful. The author considers these provisions illiberal and potentially harmful to U.S. border communities, where cross-border labor exchanges benefit citizens. Their vague terms could also create uncertainty in enforcement. Overall, the bill is characterized as unnecessarily harsh, oppressive, poorly constructed, and harmful to American citizens.

Kyle Busch won his third straight NASCAR Cup race at Richmond, matching Kevin Harvick’s streak, but worried his momentum is peaking early in the 2018 regular season. He credited his success to short-track strength and experience running his super late model teams, while saying a fourth win at Talladega would be difficult because restrictor-plate racing is unpredictable.

Representatives of the United States, Great Britain, and China informally discussed the League of Nations’ dissolution and transition to the United Nations at Dumbarton Oaks on October 7, 1944. The League’s Supervisory Committee formed a three-member Conciliation Committee in December to confer with a group designated by the United Nations Conference, but no meeting plans were made because no conference date had been set. The recommended U.S. procedure was to take no initiative and leave the matter to the conference unless the United Kingdom or China acted.

At a January 31, 1945 meeting in Washington, diplomats discussed progress on the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals before the Mexico City Conference. Following Chile’s objection to the December 29 minutes, Mora and Pasvolsky were asked to draft language concerning “assuring respect for international treaties,” although Mora said recording his remarks might suffice.

Researchers simulated biosecurity screening tests using about 76,000 AI-generated protein blueprints based on 72 harmful proteins. While screens flagged nearly all original versions, many AI-modified variants evaded detection. Software patches improved detection, including when genes were fragmented, though about 3% of variants still went unflagged. The work was entirely computational; no physical proteins were made, and it remains unclear whether the variants retained their function. Experts noted that malicious attempts to produce harmful proteins remain extremely rare.

After Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans, especially the predominantly Black, lower-income Lower Ninth Ward, many residents struggled to return and rebuild amid redevelopment and gentrification. The city and Louisiana have since adapted to increasingly severe weather and flooding through evacuation centers, raised homes, solar panels, rain gardens, elevated planting beds in contaminated soil, and green infrastructure.

New Orleans architects developed the Greater New Orleans Urban Water Plan to address heavy rainfall and land subsidence, including parks, tree-lined streets, ponds, and the 25-acre Mirabeau Water Garden. Louisiana’s 2017 Coastal Master Plan identifies $50 billion in projects to rebuild wetlands and barrier islands, restore marshes, construct flood protections, elevate homes, and relocate some residents. The state is losing wetlands at roughly a football field per hour.

Oil and gas extraction contributes to coastal subsidence, while rising seas—projected to average about 1 cm annually by 2050—threaten infrastructure and communities. Experts say Louisiana’s adaptation efforts offer valuable lessons as extreme weather intensifies, though unequal resources make resilience more difficult for poorer neighborhoods.

The cup and handle is a bullish continuation chart pattern consisting of a U-shaped cup and a smaller trading-range handle. The cup forms after a rally as prices consolidate and recover toward the prior peak; the handle forms on the cup’s right side through a slight downward drift. Qualification criteria include an existing uptrend, a 30–50% cup retracement, a handle that does not fall below the cup’s halfway point, and an upside breakout above the handle’s resistance, preferably on increased volume. Traders may enter long after breakout or wait for the price to exceed the cup’s swing high. The projected target is measured by adding the cup’s depth to the breakout price.

Volume typically declines as the cup forms, increases during its recovery, declines during the handle, and rises significantly at breakout. Stops may be placed below the handle’s low or the cup’s bottom. Because no pattern is infallible, a break below the cup’s support invalidates the formation.

The inverted cup and handle is a bearish continuation pattern. Its dome-shaped cup forms after a decline in a downtrend, followed by an upward-drifting handle and a downward breakout. It can also occur across stocks, forex, and commodities over short- or long-term charts.

Psychologically, the cup reflects a transition from pessimism and selling to renewed optimism and buying, while the handle represents profit-taking, hesitation, and a final test of investor conviction. High volatility can disrupt the formation, create false signals, and reduce reliability; lower volatility generally produces clearer patterns.

Traders are advised to consider overall market conditions, volume, other technical indicators, and fundamental analysis rather than rely on the pattern alone. Backtesting is difficult because strict entry and exit rules are subjective. Reported studies include an S&P 500 test from 2016–2018 that underperformed the index but showed favorable metrics at low market exposure, and a five-year study of 500 stocks showing a 26% failure rate, falling to 10% when trades waited for an upside breakout, with an average gain of 38%.

A higher-order self-energy correction produces a loop integral proportional to \(q^3/q^4\), which diverges logarithmically when integrated from zero to infinity. Introducing a cutoff scale keeps the calculation physically sensible and Lorentz invariant, although the correction remains infinite at arbitrarily high scales. Masses and couplings can then be redefined or renormalized as bare values plus corrections, with physical quantities evaluated at specific experimental scales. The electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings vary with energy and may not converge at high scales. Introducing new particles can alter this scale evolution and could enable a unified theory at a particular scale.

The lecture reviews the graph removal lemma and introduces its induced variant: for every graph \(H\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a \(\delta>0\) such that any graph with sufficiently few induced copies of \(H\) can be made induced-\(H\)-free by adding or deleting fewer than \(\varepsilon n^2\) edges. A colorful formulation generalizes this to edge colorings.

The usual regularity-lemma proof encounters an obstacle because induced subgraphs depend on both edges and nonedges, while irregular vertex pairs cannot simply be discarded. To address this, the lecture develops a strong regularity lemma, which produces nested partitions \(P\) and \(Q\), where \(P\) is regular, \(Q\) is extremely regular and has bounded size, and their energy difference is small. Its proof repeatedly applies Szemerédi’s regularity lemma and uses the boundedness of energy to limit the number of iterations.

A corollary yields an equitable partition with large subsets \(W_i\) that are pairwise regular, including internally regular, while their edge densities mostly resemble those of the ambient parts. This enables the induced removal proof: partition the graph, add or remove edges to make densities uniformly low or high, and use an induced counting lemma. Any surviving induced \(H\) would imply many induced copies in the original graph, contradicting the hypothesis.

The lecture also states an infinite removal lemma for possibly infinite families of finite graphs and discusses property testing. Randomly sampling vertex triples yields a constant-time oblivious tester that distinguishes triangle-free graphs from graphs \(\varepsilon n^2\)-far from triangle-free with high probability. More generally, the infinite removal lemma implies that every hereditary graph property is testable by an oblivious tester with one-sided error.

The article compares lump-sum investing with dollar-cost averaging and backtests a lump-sum buy-and-hold portfolio using five equally weighted asset classes: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. It examines portfolio equity, drawdowns, monthly and annual returns, and performance statistics around financial crises. The analysis states that investing earlier generally produces greater average profits and that crises have less impact over long-term horizons. Lump-sum investing provides immediate market exposure and may yield higher long-term returns, while dollar-cost averaging reduces exposure to short-term volatility and timing risk but may earn less.

NeoWorld is a deep-learning framework for constructing an infinitely expandable, interactive 3D world from a single image, inspired by the on-demand rendering concept in *Simulacron-3*. It uses a hybrid representation: lightweight object-centric 2.5D Gaussian layers for backgrounds and progressively reconstructed full-3D objects for interaction-relevant foreground elements. This balances rendering quality, physical consistency, and computational efficiency.

The 2.5D representation uses foreground/background Gaussian layers enriched with compact, learnable instance-semantic attributes. A fixed low-dimensional codebook reduces memory and computation while supporting scalable object identification, cross-view label propagation, KNN smoothing, and joint optimization with image reconstruction and semantic losses. Objects selected by proximity or user prompts are converted from 2.5D to 3D using image-to-3D reconstruction. Coarse pose and geometry alignment uses a learned pose token with negligible overhead, followed by fine alignment through depth and silhouette losses. Unreliable reconstructions are detected using DINOv2 similarity and reverted to 2.5D.

A large language model interprets natural-language commands, identifies target objects, and specifies transformations, animation sequences, or physical parameters. The framework therefore supports navigation, 3D-consistent exploration, object translation and rotation, text-driven dynamics, and physics-based manipulation.

Experiments used a benchmark of 28 curated images and 112 procedurally generated scenes. NeoWorld outperformed WonderJourney and WonderWorld on human-rated 3D consistency and scene quality, receiving more than 45% of participant preferences, while also surpassing them on CIQA+ and Q-Align. Its segmentation IoU of 70.53 substantially exceeded OmniSeg3DGS and GaussianGrouping, and its prompt-alignment and VideoCLIP scores exceeded those of tested video-generation baselines. Ablations showed that the compact codebook provided a strong efficiency–accuracy balance, while coarse and fine alignment improved plausibility and coherence at substantially lower runtime than Flash Sculptor.

Limitations arise because NeoWorld is a cascade of pretrained modules, so upstream errors can propagate. Reported failures include 3D alignment errors, LLM misinterpretation of ambiguous prompts, reconstruction failures under severe occlusion or complex reflective textures, and under- or over-segmentation that corrupts object masks.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to resolve delayed performance-based bonuses for public school teachers, calling the recurring delays unacceptable and recommending streamlined clearance processing. Teachers’ bonuses for 2016–2017 remained unpaid as delays extended into the next fiscal year.

A June 5, 2001 media compilation focused primarily on California’s electricity and natural-gas crises and their effects on consumers, utilities, regulators and energy traders. High demand, transmission constraints, inadequate pipeline capacity, reduced hydroelectric imports and power-plant outages contributed to shortages and sharply higher wholesale prices. About half of California’s electricity was generated by gas-fired plants, while 85% of the state’s gas came from outside California. Critics blamed deregulation, financial trading, inadequate storage and alleged market manipulation, while El Paso and Southern California Gas denied contributing to higher prices. Southern California Edison attributed $3.7 billion in excess energy prices to the two companies. Federal regulators considered transaction-disclosure requirements, restored price caps and examined bundled gas and pipeline-capacity sales.

FERC introduced a new price-mitigation plan using production costs as a benchmark during periods of tight supply, with possible refunds for higher-priced sales. The plan also required generators to offer available capacity around the clock, required weekly state reports on bids and outages, and opened an investigation into Western electricity trading. Supporters called it more comprehensive than earlier controls, but critics said it applied to too few hours, excluded out-of-state sales and left loopholes such as “megawatt laundering.” A prior FERC “soft cap” had produced tentative refund orders exceeding $100 million.

California’s Senate Rules Committee approved subpoenas for pricing, bidding and sales documents from Reliant Energy, Dynegy, Williams Energy, Enron, NRG Energy, Duke Energy, Mirant and AES. The inquiry was examining whether out-of-state generators illegally profited from the crisis. The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and state Department of Water Resources also faced possible subpoenas. Utility executives denied wrongdoing. Separately, PG&E filed for bankruptcy protection, the state began purchasing power for utilities serving nearly nine million customers, and regulators approved residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural rate increases ranging from 15% to 49%.

PBS and The New York Times presented the Frontline documentary “Blackout,” which examined deregulation, alleged price manipulation, corporate influence and the wealth transferred to power sellers and traders such as Enron. Enron CEO Jeff Skilling defended competition and open markets, while Chairman Kenneth Lay defended the Bush administration’s energy policies. Reviews noted that the documentary presented competing claims but intensified the blame game. KUHT delayed “Blackout” by one hour because of its Houston relevance while substituting the first hour of the Tony Awards during a pledge drive.

Enron’s Indian and international lenders met in Singapore to try to preserve the $2.9 billion Dabhol power project after Dabhol Power and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board disputed tariffs and unpaid bills. The project was 65%-owned by Enron; Indian lenders had substantial exposure, and Dabhol had issued a preliminary termination notice. Enron denied renegotiating its contract, while lenders sought an affordable tariff, payment of defaults and additional electricity buyers.

Other reports said Marathon replaced Enron’s 20% stake in the Red Sea Consortium, part of a $25 billion Saudi Arabian natural-gas venture. Enron and the Connecticut Resources Recovery Authority sought $125 million from a ratepayer conservation fund for a FuelCell Energy project, drawing objections that the money would be diverted from proven conservation programs. Domtar agreed to buy four Georgia-Pacific pulp and paper mills for $1.65 billion, becoming North America’s second-largest uncoated-freesheet producer. Weak newsprint demand and excess inventories were expected to push prices lower despite production cuts, with Enron offering publishers an alternative supply source.

Additional items included an Alliance for Retail Energy Markets statement endorsing aspects of California’s proposed “Fair Plan” while seeking retail access for residential customers and fair cost allocations; Enron’s ¥50 billion two-tranche securities offering; and a dispute over delays in ethics approval for Karl Rove to divest stocks, including Enron holdings.

Robert Mugabe returned to Zimbabwe after receiving medical treatment in Singapore, amid allegations linking his G40 allies to the June 24 bomb attack at White City Stadium in Bulawayo. The blast killed two and injured more than 40, including Vice President Kembo Mohadi and Environment, Water and Climate Minister Oppah Muchinguri-Kashiri. President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s government called it an attempt on his life, while Mnangagwa claimed without evidence that G40 was responsible. Mugabe considers Mnangagwa’s administration illegitimate, demands constitutionalism and has reportedly warmed to the MDC Alliance ahead of July 30 polls. Mugabe’s nephew Patrick Zhuwao warned British Prime Minister Theresa May that Mnangagwa might use the blast to target his enemies, while G40 functionary Jonathan Moyo criticized the cancellation of Mnangagwa’s rallies in Matabeleland.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition ADC with per-channel PGAs, selectable bipolar input ranges, programmable antialias filters, input clamp protection, and common-mode operation up to ±12 V. Inputs can be differential or single-ended. Internal clamps allow input swings to ±18 V; input current should remain within ±10 mA, with a series resistor recommended for current limiting and optional filtering. The device supports straight-binary or two’s-complement output, with LSB size determined by the selected input range.

Normal operation requires a free-running differential or single-ended sampling clock. SMPL_SYNC enables simultaneous sampling and frame alignment across multiple devices. The low-drift internal reference requires a recommended 10-µF bypass capacitor at REFIO, or an external reference can be used. The source-synchronous data interface supports two- or four-lane SDR/DDR modes and outputs 20-bit results MSB-first in 24-bit packets. Optional output randomization reduces interference between data transmission and analog performance. Simple and moving averaging improve SNR, while fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns support interface debugging.

Reset, power-down, and initialization are register-controlled. Speed-boost mode converts a selected channel pair at up to 8 MSPS. Configuration registers are organized into three banks and support SPI reads, writes, and daisy chaining. Application guidance covers PMU signal-chain use, calibrated TUE, bandwidth and settling performance, power supplies, PCB layout, development resources, and ESD handling.

The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt and were issued under the 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee, pursuant to Apple’s Form S-3 registration statement. The study developed and validated a whole-body human PBPK model predicting rifampicin, ethambutol, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide concentrations at extrapulmonary TB sites. The 17-compartment model includes pleural fluid and lymph nodes, incorporates oral absorption and first-order elimination, and considers slow and fast isoniazid acetylators. Model parameters were calibrated using plasma and lung data and independently validated against separate datasets.

Predictions showed that rifampicin and isoniazid generally exceeded their critical concentrations, although rapid isoniazid acetylators maintained effective levels less often than slow acetylators. Ethambutol failed to exceed its critical concentration in the brain, kidney, bone, and skin, while pyrazinamide remained below critical concentrations in all simulated compartments. In pleural fluid, ethambutol and pyrazinamide were below critical concentrations, whereas rifampicin and isoniazid were above them; rifampicin pleural exposure was overpredicted.

Limitations included representing all lymph nodes as one compartment, omitting rifampicin autoinduction, and not accounting for drug synergy, immune effects, age-dependent pharmacokinetics, or significant drug interactions. The authors positioned the model as a starting point for improving and validating extrapulmonary TB treatment regimens.

The Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage points to 1%–1.25%, marking its second hike in six months and third since ending a seven-year post-crisis rate freeze.

The study harmonized prospectively collected data from South Korea’s CRCS-K registry and Taiwan’s TREAT-AIS registry, creating a unified dataset of 9,941 EVT-treated acute ischemic stroke patients: 7,835 from Korea and 2,106 from Taiwan. Approximately 200 common fields covered demographics, premorbid status, risk factors, stroke characteristics, treatment timelines, recanalization, complications, and 90-day outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines assessed age and other predictors.

Compared with Korean patients, Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors and severe strokes, were less likely to be functionally independent before stroke, and had longer treatment delays and lower intravenous thrombolysis rates. Successful recanalization rates were similar, but Taiwan had lower 90-day functional independence and Korea had higher 90-day mortality.

Age strongly predicted outcomes after EVT. Patients aged 80 or older had less favorable functional recovery, higher mortality, and lower successful recanalization than younger patients, while symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage rates did not differ significantly by age. The age effect was nonlinear and most pronounced between ages 75 and 85. Among older patients, premorbid functional independence, baseline stroke severity, and bridging thrombolysis were important outcome modifiers. The findings do not support excluding elderly patients categorically from EVT; carefully selected older patients may benefit. Study limitations included differing registry definitions and inclusion periods, retrospective analysis, and unavailable detailed imaging and post-discharge data.

GBMC neonatologist Dr. Maria Pane cares for the sickest, tiniest patients, includes parents in rounds, and values team collaboration. She supports the Father’s Day 5K fundraiser for the neonatal intensive care unit.

Kalai introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs), in which a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier queries randomly selected bits of a proof rather than reading the entire proof. Completeness requires every true instance to have a proof accepted with probability at least \(c\); soundness requires every proof for a false instance to be accepted with probability at most \(s\). In ordinary PCPs, the verifier reads all of the instance \(x\). Query indices are chosen randomly and commonly in advance, making the verifier nonadaptive. For cryptographic applications, proof generation from an instance and witness must also be efficient.

The lecture’s stated goal is a PCP for every NP language with completeness 1, soundness \(1/2\), and polylogarithmic randomness and query complexity. Known PCPs can do better—constant-query, \(O(\log n)\)-randomness constructions exist—but the lecture covers only the polylogarithmic version.

For the construction, an NP problem is reduced to 3SAT and then to a bounded-depth, logspace-uniform verification circuit with efficiently computable addition and multiplication selectors. Using the GKR protocol, the prover computes low-degree extensions of the witness and of every circuit layer. To turn the interactive protocol into a PCP, the oracle contains the possible prover responses for every possible sumcheck randomness and partial transcript. GKR’s ability to forget earlier randomness avoids writing out the full exponential transcript tree while still producing a polynomial-sized proof.

With layer size \(s=|H|^m\), circuit depth \(d=\operatorname{polylog}n\), and a field \(F\) chosen so the relevant field powers remain polynomial in \(s\), the \(2d\) parallel sumchecks each have \(3m\) variables. Each has soundness error \(3m|H|/|F|\), and a union bound gives total error \(2d\cdot3m|H|/|F|\). Choosing \(F\) sufficiently large, but still polylogarithmic in \(s\), yields soundness \(1/2\). Completeness is 1, and the verifier uses polylogarithmically many random bits and queries. A low-degree test is required for the prover-supplied extension of the witness. The segment ends with plans to cover that test and then introduce computational soundness and cryptography.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2022 reported Q2 net sales of $121.2 billion, up 7%, but operating income of $3.3 billion and a net loss of $2.0 billion, or $0.20 per diluted share, versus $7.7 billion of operating income and $7.8 billion of net income in Q2 2021. Six-month net sales were $237.7 billion, while operating income fell to $7.0 billion and net loss reached $5.9 billion. Results were affected by inflation, supply-chain and labor constraints, higher transportation and fulfillment costs, fulfillment inefficiencies, and a $5.5 billion Q2 other expense, including a $3.9 billion Rivian investment valuation loss.

North America sales rose 10% to $74.4 billion but produced a $627 million operating loss. International sales fell 12% to $27.1 billion, with a $1.8 billion operating loss. AWS sales increased 33% to $19.7 billion and operating income rose to $5.7 billion. Q2 operating cash flow was $9.0 billion, investing activities used $12.1 billion, and financing activities provided $4.6 billion. At June 30, cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $60.7 billion, total assets were $419.7 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $131.4 billion.

The company effected a 20-for-1 stock split in May 2022 and changed estimated useful lives for servers and networking equipment, reducing Q2 depreciation and amortization by $928 million. Amazon acquired MGM Holdings for approximately $6.1 billion net of cash and agreed in July to acquire 1Life Healthcare for approximately $3.9 billion. It repurchased $6.0 billion of stock, had $62.5 billion of senior notes outstanding, and reported total contractual commitments of $278.7 billion. Management stated that operating cash flow, marketable securities, and borrowing arrangements should meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least the next twelve months.

The Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed Robert Pearl Bryson’s convictions for aggravated sodomy, child molestation, and failure to register as a sex offender. The evidence showed that Bryson befriended two boys, eight-year-old B. S. and ten-year-old K. S., and sexually abused them. The court found the evidence sufficient to establish aggravated sodomy because Georgia law requires only sexual contact, not penetration. It also found that Bryson’s kiss of K. S. on the lips, considered with the surrounding circumstances, supported the required sexual intent for child molestation. His departure from Georgia for more than a year without notifying the Stephens County sheriff of his changed residence address supported the registration charge.

The court found no error in denying Bryson’s motions to quash the indictment or Count 8, denying counsel’s withdrawal shortly before trial, or refusing to sever the connected charges. The withdrawal request would have delayed trial, and severance was unnecessary because the offenses and evidence were connected. Bryson’s North Carolina no-contest plea was admissible to establish a conviction requiring sex-offender registration, and the jury was properly instructed on its permissible use.

The court also held that Bryson knowingly waived his ineffective-assistance claim by declining to pursue it at his first opportunity in the trial court. Bryson’s conviction on Count 9 had been merged into Count 8 for sentencing, so the court did not address its sufficiency.

Image registration aligns a moving image to a fixed image by optimizing a coordinate transform, commonly combining affine and deformable components. It is important for multimodal fusion, cross-subject comparison, morphometry, atlases, anatomical-variability studies, pathology detection, and precision medicine. Increasing imaging resolution exposes a major gap: existing methods require substantial compute and memory, often exceed GPU capacity, and frequently rely on downsampling or patch-based approximations.

The paper identifies grid sampling, cross-correlation, and mutual-information computation as key bottlenecks. It introduces fused CUDA implementations for a composite implicit grid sampler, implicit Parzen-windowing for mutual information, and implicit fused LNCC. These reduce additional high-bandwidth-memory usage from O(N) to O(1) for grid sampling and mutual information while substantially reducing LNCC memory. The kernels enable problems up to 64 times larger on a single GPU and accelerate existing optimization and deep-learning pipelines.

The proposed Flash Fused Distributed Primitives framework extends registration across multiple GPUs. Grid Parallel shards images, displacement fields, and optimizer state while synchronizing shard boundaries for convolutional operations. A distributed ring sampler computes cross-shard interpolation without gathering the full moving image, and distributed MSE, LNCC, and mutual-information losses combine shard-level results correctly.

Experiments show reduced memory use and substantial runtime improvements for TransMorph and FireANTs. On a simulated 250-micron brain MRI dataset, the proposed method achieves an average Dice score of 0.895, inverse Dice of 0.597, and average HD90 of 0.216, outperforming baselines that generally degrade at higher resolutions. The method is Pareto-efficient across accuracy and computational cost and can require up to 500 times fewer GPU-hours than alternatives.

A demonstration registers a 250-micron in-vivo MRI to a 100-micron ex-vivo human brain volume, involving more than 11 billion transform parameters. The multimodal deformable registration completes in approximately one minute on eight NVIDIA A6000 GPUs and aligns fine structures such as cerebellar white matter.

The study examines from a managerial perspective how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA) interact within digital business platforms and enterprise transformation. It uses an iterative taxonomy-development approach combining conceptual and empirical research, drawing on literature from 2010–2019 and semi-structured interviews with Russian National Technology Initiative members, founders, and CTOs. The resulting framework maps AI innovation across a value chain that includes data acquisition, curation and quality measurement, storage, interpretation and reporting, and data-driven decision-making. It also examines seven overlapping technology platforms: information systems, customer experience, data and analytics, IoT, ecosystems, trust, and integration. A five-level maturity framework progresses from human-led initial analytics to machine-controlled advanced analytics, with each level linked to increasing AI/BD/AA value-chain coverage. The study’s main contribution is a multidimensional, data-driven AI innovation taxonomy that supports assessment of human–machine relationships, organizational readiness, automation opportunities, and AI maturity. The framework is intended to help managers identify appropriate AI use cases, plan investment and transformation, communicate AI’s business value, and evaluate legal, ethical, and societal implications.

This study evaluated the effect of pharmacological mydriasis on retinal image quality and AI-based diabetic retinopathy screening using a portable, smartphone-linked fundus camera. Patients were imaged before and after 0.5% tropicamide dilation, with two images per eye. Among 327 participants, masked ophthalmologists graded images and labeled diabetic retinopathy lesions, while a ResNet-200d model trained on the mBRSET dataset was validated on 597 paired mydriatic and non-mydriatic images.

Mydriatic images were gradable more often than non-mydriatic images (82.1% versus 55.6%; P<0.001). In non-mydriatic imaging, older age, longer diabetes duration, male sex, and systemic hypertension were associated with reduced image quality; Indigenous race was also significantly associated with lower quality, while Black and mixed-race categories were not.

AI performance numerically favored mydriatic images: accuracy was 82.91% versus 79.23%, F1 score was 0.83 versus 0.79, and AUC was 0.94 versus 0.93. Mydriatic images also produced fewer false positives (13.9% versus 17.8%), while false-negative rates were similar (3.2% versus 3.0%). However, the overall between-group difference was not statistically significant (P=0.3279).

The findings indicate that dilation can improve image gradability and reduce false-positive DR classifications, but non-mydriatic imaging may remain necessary where dilating agents, trained personnel, or follow-up care are limited. Limitations included image acquisition by non-specialists, selection bias from analyzing paired images, use of one camera and dataset, and lack of detailed analysis across referral-grade DR categories.

The AMD Geode CS5535 specification update documents several device limitations and workarounds:

- An SSMI coincident with an interrupt request may not be signaled before the associated I/O completes; the Geode GX processor can instead generate required SSMIs.
- UDMA fails if IDE bus mastering is enabled before the PIO command packet. The required order is command packet first, then bus-master enable.
- GPIO[27:24] cannot wake the system from ACPI S3; use PWRBTN#, optionally combining events with external circuitry powered by VIO_STB and VMEM.
- An extended CMOS RAM write followed by a legacy-port read may return incorrect data unless an address-port write intervenes; no resolution is provided.
- Block- and demand-mode legacy DMA to LPC can block I/O and return invalid data; use single-transfer mode.
- USB clock gating can cause register-read failures and should be disabled.
- An unexpected IDE interrupt after bus mastering begins can reset the bus-master engine and stop the transfer; affected CD-ROM firmware has reportedly been revised.
- Reading Port 60h can incorrectly clear AuxOutputFull; interrupts should manage USB keyboard and mouse traffic in PS/2 emulation.
- The tACK bits do not affect UDMA timing because IDE_DACK setup is fixed at 30 ns, which satisfies all UDMA modes.
- ATAC can hang with WORD-aligned PRDs; ATAC drivers should use DWORD alignment.
- LPC may abort transactions when valid SYNC patterns arrive late, discarding writes or returning all ones; a PLD-based workaround is described.
- SMB NEGACK may be set late; clearing it requires two SMB_STS writes: first writing 1 to NEGACK, then writing 0x00.
- The GLPCI retry counter includes unrelated PCI retries and may exhaust its limit early.
- After suspend, atomic GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Register writes clear nonselected bits; use a full-register read-modify-write.
- SMBus data hold time is shorter than expected, and LOWBAT_FLAG may not be set after abnormal standby.
- Premature delay-counter resets can leave SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y asserted and PCI/IDE inputs disabled; program the relevant counters below the PM_SED delay value.

The Mississippi Supreme Court affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy’s second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence for a collision that killed Daniel Palmer and two passengers. The court found sufficient evidence for the jury to conclude that Gandy was intoxicated and drove into the wrong traffic lane, causally connected to the deaths. It rejected Gandy’s challenges to the refusal of a peremptory instruction, the refusal of proposed jury instruction D-13 concerning intoxication, and the admission of three post-accident scene sketches. The court found the jury had been adequately instructed on intoxication and the sketches were relevant, properly founded, and did not reconstruct the vehicles’ positions at impact. It also rejected Gandy’s claim that jurors should have received a food or refreshment recess.

The study developed an age-structured, region-level metapopulation SIR model linking SARS-CoV-2 transmissibility to Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMRs). Changes in grocery/pharmacy, retail/recreation, transit, and workplace activity were modeled as additive contributions, assuming linear relationships between activity and transmission-relevant contacts; residential and park categories were excluded. Weekly regional residual terms accounted for transmission outside these settings. Temperature, used as a proxy for seasonality, and the prevalence of Alpha and Delta variants acted multiplicatively on infection probability per contact. Bayesian fitting to weekly hospitalization data incorporated age-specific susceptibility, vaccination, variant-related hospitalization risk, imported cases, and delays to hospitalization.

The model was applied from February 2020 to July 2021 in 11 Norwegian and 21 Swedish regions and from February to December 2020 in Bavaria and Berlin. It fit Scandinavian hospitalization data well. A 20°C temperature increase reduced transmissibility by about 40%; Delta roughly doubled transmissibility, with substantial uncertainty, while Alpha increased it by about 20% in Norway but showed no clear increase in Sweden. The four GCMR settings accounted for 60.0% of infections in Sweden and 38.7% in Norway, with substantial regional variation. At pre-pandemic activity levels, transit and workplaces had the largest estimated contributions, followed by retail/recreation and grocery/pharmacy. In Germany, the GCMR categories captured 64.5% of Bavaria’s and 69.7% of Berlin’s daily infectious contacts; retail/recreation was most important, followed by transit and workplaces.

Overall, GCMRs were associated with infection dynamics and could support real-time monitoring, but their interpretation required strong assumptions and a complex model. Limitations included constant linear activity–contact relationships, common seasonal and variant effects across settings, all-or-nothing vaccine protection, reliance on literature parameters, and possible GCMR measurement error, limiting causal interpretation.

The speaker accepts his party’s nomination for president of the United States, thanking Texas and Dallas for their hospitality. He frames the election as a choice between two fundamentally different futures: one based on pessimism, fear, and government expansion, and another based on hope, confidence, growth, and individual opportunity.

He criticizes opposition policies for producing inflation, high interest rates, tax increases, federal deficits, and dependence on government programs. Crediting his administration with spending restraint, tax cuts, indexing, deregulation, economic growth, low inflation, job creation, and reduced poverty, he calls for a balanced-budget amendment, presidential line-item veto authority, simpler and lower taxes, tuition tax credits, enterprise zones, and passage of an anticrime bill. He also advocates voluntary school prayer.

On foreign policy, he emphasizes stronger armed forces, improved alliances, diplomatic progress in Asia, continued support for Israel, and assistance to free Latin American countries. He defends the Grenada mission as a rescue operation and rejects comparisons with Soviet actions in Afghanistan. At the same time, he urges renewed negotiations with the Soviet Union to reduce nuclear arms, arguing that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

The speaker presents his governing philosophy as protecting individual liberty, human dignity, opportunity, religious freedom, and opposition to prejudice and statism. He says he began as a Democratic voter but believes the party’s leadership abandoned its original principles, while welcoming Democrats who share his views.

Reflecting on four years of change and accomplishment, he presents his party as ready to continue economic recovery, preserve freedom, strengthen defense and alliances, and pursue peace. He closes by describing the Olympic torch relay across the United States and the restored torch atop the Statue of Liberty as symbols of national unity, opportunity, and a bright future.

Grief is a highly personal emotional response to losing someone or something important. It can also follow significant life changes, such as becoming a carer, a relative’s retirement, declining health, or moving home. Its effects, duration, and coping patterns vary according to life experience, circumstances, and personality; there is no right or wrong way to grieve. Grief may occur before an expected loss, allowing time to prepare and say goodbye, and it can span generations as relatives face one another’s health changes.

After a death, people may move repeatedly between emotions rather than follow fixed stages. Common reactions include numbness, denial, acceptance or relief, intense yearning, repeatedly reviewing the death, restlessness, disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness or depression. Moving home may cause additional grief, particularly when filled with memories or when support networks are disrupted, so major decisions should be considered carefully.

Grief can last for a long time, but most people eventually experience more good days than bad. Friends, family, bereavement organizations, a GP, or specialist support can provide help when needed.

The ADS9803 supports simple and moving averaging to improve signal-to-noise ratio. Simple averaging halves the output data rate, while moving averaging leaves it unchanged. Host-accessible test patterns for debugging and interface verification can replace ADC outputs for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. Supported patterns include fixed values, digital ramps with programmable increments of N+1, and alternating fixed patterns.

The device can be reset by pulling RESET low or setting the RESET field at address 0x00 in register bank 0. Power-down is controlled through the PWDN pin or the PD_CH field at address 0xC0 in bank 1. After power-up or reset, registers receive default values and require an initialization sequence; a free-running sampling clock must be connected before initialization. User configuration can change analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, and data-interface settings.

Speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS for a selected analog channel pair while the other six channels remain idle. The sampling rate equals the sampling-clock frequency, and output-interface specifications remain unchanged.

The 16-bit configuration registers occupy three banks and use 8-bit addresses. SPI writes require SPI_RD_EN = 0; bank 1 or 2 is selected by writing address 0x03, while bank 0 is always accessible. SPI reads require SPI_RD_EN = 1 and SPI_MODE = 1 and use separate frames for bank selection, read enable, and data retrieval. Daisy-chain configurations share CS and SCLK, connect each ADC’s SDO output to the next ADC’s SDI input, and use DAISY_CHAIN_LEN to specify the chain. A write to N devices requires N × 24 SCLK cycles.

The ADS9803 is described as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. For calibrated operation, its total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. It can receive separate PMU outputs or multiplexed PMU signals and offers low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz; in wide-bandwidth mode, multiplexed signals settle to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. It uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies, with no mandatory power-up sequence. Recommended layout includes nearby 0.1-µF bypass capacitors, reference decoupling near REFIO and REFM, separation of analog and digital paths, and short ground-plane connections.

The Patriots struggled offensively against Miami but remained in contention late. Stephen Gostkowski’s onside kick attempt failed, allowing the Dolphins to recover and win. Jon Gruden called it “the most bizarre onside kick” he had seen.

Researchers led by Vanderbilt University’s Joshua Caldwell reported a major advance in hyperlensing in Nature Materials. By producing hexagonal boron nitride crystals from 99% isotopically pure boron, the team greatly reduced optical losses, tripled polariton lifetime and travel distance, and improved imaging resolution by about tenfold over previous hBN hyperlenses. Their calculations indicate that lenses using the purified crystal could, in principle, image objects as small as 30 nanometers—small enough to resolve some viruses.

Unlike electron-based and atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses could image living organisms in natural, solution-based environments without high vacuum, harmful radiation or lethal preparation. Infrared imaging could also provide spectroscopic “fingerprints” of materials, with potential applications in biology, medicine, communications and nanoscale optical components. Researchers suggested that larger purified crystals could yield further improvements, potentially another tenfold.

Attackers can counter an offside trap by recognizing that defenders are moving up rather than retreating, remaining onside when the ball is played, timing their runs, and exploiting space behind the defense. If forced offside, attackers should stop or run back with defenders without interfering with play.

Methods include faking or self-passing to dribble into open space, timed through passes, horizontal or lateral runs, checking runs, short passes, deep-lying and bending runs, back passes, delayed runs, and using a designated “non-runner” during free kicks. Fakes can reveal whether defenders are executing the trap, allowing attackers to capitalize when a defender fails to move up. Successfully beating the trap can leave a striker one-on-one with the goalkeeper.

The articles summarize Enron-related developments in California and India in July 2001.

California records showed that numerous public and private suppliers charged the state high wholesale electricity prices during the first-quarter energy crisis. Enron averaged $181 per megawatt-hour and Mirant $225, while TransAlta and Sacramento Municipal Utility District averaged $335 and $330, respectively. California’s average purchase price fell from $316 per megawatt-hour in January to $243 in May, and prices declined further in June and July. The state spent nearly $8 billion on power during the first five months and bought about 10% more electricity in April and May than projected.

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission mediation over alleged California overcharges ended without agreement. Power companies offered $716.1 million in refunds, while California sought $8.9 billion. An administrative law judge recommended a plan potentially producing hundreds of millions, perhaps $1 billion, in refunds for sales from October 2000 through May, with further hearings to determine amounts. California officials said they might pursue further litigation.

A California Senate committee investigating price gouging accused Duke Energy of withholding confidential bidding data from its Chula Vista plant. Duke said it was complying and that grid operators ordered the plant’s output changes during the January emergency. The committee was considering contempt citations. Separately, a judge ruled that California prosecutors could share documents subpoenaed from Reliant Energy, Mirant and Dynegy with Oregon and Washington; the companies planned to appeal.

In India, Dabhol Power CEO Neil McGregor resigned after his contract expired, with Enron India managing director K. Wade Cline assuming added responsibility. The Maharashtra State Electricity Board’s payment defaults, totaling $48 million, prompted it to stop buying power from the operating first phase and halted financing for the 85%-complete second phase. Chairman Kenneth Lay met Indian ministers, state officials, lenders and business leaders to discuss solutions but reached no immediate conclusions. He said Enron had no plan to leave India and remained committed to the project. Options discussed included finding a buyer, reducing tariffs or greater central involvement.

Enron Broadband Services and Anschutz Investment were identified as key investors in Tropic Networks’ $60 million financing. Separately, analysts continued to rate Enron a “buy,” citing its strong trading business and projected earnings growth despite California scrutiny, India-related difficulties and a $35 million quarterly loss in broadband services. Independent power producers generally were expected to meet second-quarter earnings targets as higher April and May prices and increased output offset declining June prices.

Periwinkle sea snails exposed to predicted 2100 ocean conditions adapted to acidification by accelerating shell formation, producing less-dense inner shells, and developing less-soluble, more resistant shells despite reduced metabolism.
Roldán’s case was nearly identical to People v. Soldán, No. 2037, except for the loan amount. Following that decision, the court reversed the judgment and acquitted Roldán.

Barron’s Jack Hough warns that Netflix could lose more than half its value due to competition from Disney, Facebook, and Amazon, cash burn, debt, and accounting practices. The passage disputes this bearish case, arguing that Netflix has consistently grown despite Amazon and YouTube, while Disney and Facebook may not offer stronger offerings. Netflix has raised U.S. prices twice since early 2014, increasing its most popular plan by 25% without disrupting subscriber growth, and has announced increases in Australia and Canada. Its 104 million streaming accounts provide scale, help control costs, and attract content creators. Although Netflix stock is expensive and likely to correct at some point, the passage concludes that betting against the company is risky because of its demonstrated growth, pricing power, and revenue diversification.

China’s Ministry of Commerce blacklisted Canadian research firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries on its “unreliable entity list,” accusing them of violating national interests after TechInsights analyzed Huawei’s advanced AI chips. The restrictions prohibit Chinese organizations from collaborating with or supplying data to the firm and limit its access to Chinese clients. TechInsights is known for semiconductor reverse-engineering and teardown analysis used to monitor export controls and rival technologies. Analysts said the ban reflects tighter Chinese control over technology information flows and escalating semiconductor tensions, potentially reducing transparency in global supply chains.

Ryan Kerr, 26, was remanded in custody pending sentencing after admitting a series of attacks, including punching a woman and leaving a man unconscious in a pub toilet. The judge heard Kerr showed no remorse and had previous battery and assault convictions. His lawyer requested psychiatric reports and argued he was a viable prospect for rehabilitation.

Peterborough City Council has pledged £4 million for new homes on Midland Road and Bretton Court and is working with St Michael’s Gate residents on accommodation concerns. Its Empty Homes Strategy returned 179 of 574 long-empty properties to use last year; over five years, the council helped bring 663 empty homes back into use, earning more than £3 million through the government’s New Homes Bonus.

The council published Phase Two budget proposals for consultation, warning that government grants have fallen 80% in eight years, from £55 million to £10 million. It says this reflects outdated population figures and launched the Stand Up for Peterborough campaign to seek protection from future funding shortfalls.

Two Public Space Protection Orders introduced six months ago are showing reduced littering fines and a sharp fall in unauthorised cycling. The council also launched CHUMS, a service supporting children and young people with anxiety, depression and other mild-to-moderate mental health needs, including prevention interventions for self-harm.

A study of national hospital and field-investigation data found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 children under 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window-blind injuries. Most injuries were minor and did not require hospitalization, but cord entanglement represented 11.9% of cases and was linked to nearly 80% of 726 hospitalizations and more than 94% of 271 deaths. Most entanglements occurred at home while children were unsupervised, often briefly; toddlers and preschoolers were especially at risk.

Researchers said voluntary safety standards and recalls had not adequately prevented injuries and called for mandatory standards requiring unexposed or inaccessible cords. The Consumer Product Safety Commission began rulemaking for a mandatory standard, while manufacturers proposed that stock coverings sold in stores or online be cordless or have inaccessible cords. Safety advocates said supervision, cord tying and safety kits were insufficient and urged cord-free or inaccessible-cord coverings.

Chef and cookbook author Shannon Bard announced that Zapoteca, the Portland restaurant she and her husband Tom owned, has closed permanently. The couple prioritized spending more time with their five children while retaining Toroso, Salud, a cooking school and catering company. Bard also wrote a cookbook and appeared on Food Network programs.

The protocol and informed consent documentation were reviewed and approved by independent ethics committees at participating centers before study initiation, and investigators had to report serious or unexpected adverse events.
