Hospitalized COVID-19 care is mainly supportive, with mortality benefits reported for dexamethasone and tocilizumab in oxygen-requiring patients, while remdesivir showed little benefit. Convalescent plasma studies had inconsistent findings, possibly due to administration timing, transfusion volume, or antibody titers. The study hypothesized that early, high-volume convalescent plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation. Its primary objective was to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus supportive care alone; secondary objectives assessed severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, tracks member firms’ average exposure to U.S. equity markets. It is calculated from weekly surveys of members’ equity exposure as of each Wednesday, with the published indicator shown as a two-week moving average of responses. High readings indicate bullish sentiment and low readings bearish sentiment, potentially serving as contrarian signals of market tops and bottoms. However, the index is not predictive, and backtests found the tested strategies performed poorly. Extreme readings and varying the moving-average period did not improve results; low readings performed better than high readings, with reported annual returns of 4.4% and 2.5%, respectively, excluding dividends. The authors conclude that other contrarian indicators, such as the VIX, may be more useful.

Lubrizol will invest US$80 million to expand TPU production across North America, Europe and Asia, including new North American capabilities, Songjiang compounding and extrusion lines, and European elastomer, aliphatic and adhesive capacity. Further Asian and major European expansions are planned for 2019.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane on Wednesday, seeking to reinforce his disputed unanimous decision over Manny Pacquiao last July. A victory could lead to a bout with Terence Crawford in 2018 and a possible Pacquiao return, while defeat could send Horn back into obscurity. Horn, unbeaten in 18 bouts, faces 17-1 underdog Corcoran, who is fighting abroad for his first world title. Promoter Bob Arum said Crawford could become mandatory for a 2018 fight. Pre-fight tension centered on accusations that Horn head-butted Pacquiao and claims Corcoran might bite. Both boxers expect an aggressive contest, and Corcoran’s trainer said he would not be intimidated.

President Trump announced a deal under which Pfizer will offer lower drug prices to Medicaid and patients, launch new medicines at prices matching other countries, and avoid certain tariffs on imported drugs if it continues U.S. manufacturing. It is the administration’s first publicly announced drug-pricing agreement, with more companies expected. Experts remain skeptical about effects on affordability and Medicaid budgets because enrollees already pay little or nothing, and federal law requires drugmakers to provide Medicaid the lowest U.S. prices and increased rebates when prices rise faster than inflation. The newsletter also notes that Sanofi is under European Commission investigation for potentially anticompetitive activity.

Manchester City face Burnley at the Etihad on Jan. 2, seeking an early goal and another win as Pep Guardiola targets an unbeaten run in 2017. Burnley, just above the relegation zone, need points and pose a physical threat. Sergio Agüero returns for City, while Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva are key; Andre Gray and Sam Vokes lead Burnley’s scoring threat.

A non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint investigated neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS) using EEG responses to single-pulse median nerve stimulation. Nineteen adults with TS were compared with 19 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Neural noise was operationalized as trial-to-trial variability in the magnitude or timing of EEG responses. Most early and mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential components showed no group differences in amplitude, timing, variability, or scalp topography, although the P2/P100 component was larger in TS and its amplitude correlated with tic impairment. Trial-by-trial variability was consistently greater in the TS group, including at rest. However, coefficient of variation decreased substantially after stimulation in both groups at comparable rates, suggesting that the elevated variability normalized with stimulation. TS participants also had greater high-beta and gamma power, flatter 1/f spectral slopes, and a slower initial rise in inter-trial phase coherence, consistent with reduced or delayed neural synchronization. Beta-band coherence was briefly higher in TS around the P100 response. Greater premonitory-urge severity was associated with larger reductions in coefficient of variation and smaller gamma-coherence increases, while motor-tic severity was associated with larger alpha-coherence increases. Overall, the findings suggest that sensorimotor neuronal recruitment is less stable at rest in TS but may normalize following somatosensory stimulation, with altered central tactile processing potentially contributing to heightened sensory awareness.

Facebook published an expanded, roughly 8,000-word rule book detailing permitted content on its platform, including rules on drug use, sex work, bullying, hate speech, violence and hacked material. The company also introduced appeals for removed individual posts and provided specific removal reasons in more cases. Facebook uses automated software and 7,500 moderators to enforce its standards, which it reviews every two weeks with input from more than 100 outside organizations and plans to discuss further through public forums. Government requests to remove locally prohibited content require formal written requests and legal review; such content can be blocked only in the relevant country. The standards do not prohibit false information, though Facebook seeks to reduce its distribution. The release followed criticism from governments and rights groups over hate speech, terrorism and content removals.

Apple Inc. reported that on June 20, 2017, it completed the issuance and sale of $1 billion of 3.000% senior unsecured notes due June 20, 2027. Interest is payable semiannually in arrears on June 20 and December 20, beginning December 20, 2017. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The offering was made under an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith, and pursuant to Apple’s April 29, 2013 indenture and April 28, 2016 Form S-3 registration statement. The filing included the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, form of global note, legality opinion from Hogan Lovells US LLP and related consent as exhibits.

A federal jury unanimously cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive-force claims involving Jon “Chris” Erwin’s October 2011 arrest outside Ferneau. Video showed Hudson punching Erwin seven times and throwing him to the ground. After two days of testimony, jurors decided the force was reasonable from Hudson’s perspective.

Hudson testified that Erwin repeatedly demanded to know who complained, resisted arrest, touched Hudson, and moved toward him. Hudson said he punched Erwin to gain compliance, then took him down and handcuffed him after continued resistance. He said he followed department use-of-force policy; former police chief Stuart Thomas testified that repeated face punches were permitted when necessary and reasonable. Party workers and witnesses described the group as intoxicated, while Erwin denied drinking much.

Erwin sustained cuts, swelling and three stitches and later sought therapy for a sore back. He said the case was about police accountability, not money, and maintained that the force was excessive. His attorneys presented no medical evidence supporting his alleged post-traumatic stress disorder. Erwin and friend Blake Mitchell had misdemeanor charges dropped for procedural reasons, but jurors did not hear about the dismissal. A settlement with the city and restaurant company meant Hudson would have personally paid any damages awarded. Hudson said he felt vindicated.

The Texas Monthly article “How Enron Blew It,” by Mimi Swartz, examines Enron’s rapid rise and decline through the leadership and culture established by Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Beginning as a pipeline company after a 1985 takeover maneuver, Enron became a Wall Street darling under Skilling’s vision of trading energy as aggressively as financial assets. His “Gas Bank” allowed Enron to contractually guarantee gas supply and prices, creating a trading business that quickly grew to dominate 20 percent of North America’s natural-gas market by 1995.

Enron expanded the model into electricity, bandwidth trading, online commodity transactions, and other unconventional businesses. EnronOnline processed $335 billion in commodity trades in 2000, while the company pursued broadband capacity, movies on demand, and other technology-related ventures. Growth was accompanied by aggressive recruiting of highly educated employees, uncapped performance bonuses, extensive employee services, and intense pressure to produce immediate results. Skilling became CEO in February 2001 after Lay promoted him.

The article describes a culture built around risk, rapid profit, intellectual capital, and an “us versus them” attitude toward established business practices. Enron marketed itself to Wall Street as a technology company, abandoned long-term assets and projects, and often took large profits upfront through aggressive mark-to-market accounting. Customers became “counterparties,” and even corporate philanthropy was expected to generate profit.

Internal practices also grew increasingly harsh. Enron’s Performance Review Committee used forced rankings, regularly terminating the highest-rated employees and turning over roughly 15 percent of Capital and Trade Resources employees each year. Work became intensely competitive and isolating; email was monitored, contracts imposed broad confidentiality restrictions, and employees reported paranoia, burnout, and declining morale. Skilling’s own relentless work schedule damaged his personal and family life, and he later said he had sacrificed nearly everything for Enron.

Enron also sought to replace its remaining asset-based culture. Rebecca Mark was removed from her leadership role and assigned the water company Azurix, created through Enron’s purchase of a British utility for more than $2 billion. Azurix struggled, its stock fell from $19 to $5, and the division was folded back into Enron after Mark resigned.

Problems intensified in 2001. Enron became a target during California’s electricity crisis, while its costly Indian power project, questions about its accounting, executive stock sales, and the collapse of its highly valued telecommunications division damaged investor confidence. The economic downturn also contributed, but the article emphasizes Enron’s culture of aggressive risk, short-term gains, internal competition, and limited contrition as central factors in its decline. Its stock fell from $80 in January to below $40 by late August.

Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, and Lay returned as chief executive. Lay promised a less aggressive Enron focused more closely on its core business, acknowledged problems with the Performance Review Committee, and said the company would no longer trade indiscriminately. Skilling, whose net worth remained heavily tied to Enron stock, looked toward new technology ventures and expressed little concern about the company’s future.

The study surveys ontologies and ontology design patterns (ODPs) for process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE), addressing interoperability, reuse, and the limited adoption of reusable ODPs. Three domain-specific requirements were defined with input from nine experts: modeling process structure and execution order; representing data, resources, and experimental parameters; and capturing project goals, stages, participants, and roles.

Relevant ontologies were reviewed, including PMDcore, the General Process Ontology, WILD, P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, and OPMW. Manual analysis identified process, resource, and project patterns based on their support for these requirements. PMDcore supported all three pattern categories, P-PLAN supported process and resource patterns, Metadata4Ing supported resource and project patterns, and OPMW and GPO supported process and resource patterns; WILD provided process structures but lacked sufficient input/output and project constructs.

A baseline automated method aligns natural-language requirements with ontology classes and properties using sentence-transformer embeddings and cosine similarity. Selected terms were converted into reusable modules with ROBOT. Four extraction methods and intermediate-class configurations were tested, with STAR and no intermediate classes selected as the most compact and semantically coherent default.

Evaluation against curated ground truth showed that P-PLAN achieved the highest F1 scores for process (0.59) and resource (0.53) patterns. PMDcore supported all three categories, scoring 0.36 for process, 0.21 for resource, and 0.25 for project patterns, with strong project recall. Metadata4Ing performed moderately for resource and project patterns but weakly for process patterns. The approach was affected by annotation quality and requirement wording, and processing ontologies independently limited identification of shared patterns. Future work will expand coverage, incorporate ontology mappings and structural features, use controlled vocabularies and multi-expert validation, and develop a platform for publishing the extracted patterns with usage scenarios and community feedback.

Operating income nearly doubled to $1.927 billion from $1.005 billion, and net income increased to $1.629 billion from $724 million. Diluted earnings per share were $3.27, compared with $1.48.

Sales and operating results by segment were:

- North America: sales of $30.725 billion, up 46%, and operating income of $1.149 billion, compared with $596 million.
- International: sales of $14.875 billion, up 34%, and an operating loss of $622 million, compared with $481 million.
- AWS: sales of $5.442 billion, up 49%, and operating income of $1.400 billion, compared with $890 million.

Revenue categories included $26.939 billion from online stores, $4.263 billion from physical stores, $9.265 billion from third-party seller services, $3.102 billion from subscriptions, $5.442 billion from AWS, and $2.031 billion from other services. In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated an outbreak of Salmonella Typhimurium gastroenteritis linked to an Eid al-Adha barbecue in Cardiff. Twenty-two symptomatic cases were identified, with 12 seeking emergency care, six admitted overnight, and one requiring intensive care. A cohort study of attendees and a nested case-control analysis using Firth logistic regression identified the traditional raw sheep-liver dish “marara” as the most likely transmission vehicle (adjusted odds ratio 49.99; 95% CI 1.71–1461.54; p=0.02). No dose-response was found for raw liver, while lamb and spicy sauce confounded its apparent effect.

Five cultured cases were genetically indistinguishable by whole-genome sequencing. Raw lamb samples and samples from two local butchers and their supplying abattoir also matched the outbreak isolates, indicating widespread contamination but not establishing the exact point where contamination occurred. Possible cross-contamination included reuse of raw-liver marinade and its serving plate, undercooking, and prolonged unchilled storage.

The outbreak was part of a wider Salmonella Typhimurium cluster reported across several UK regions since 2018; investigations into its food-supply chains continued. Public Health Wales also developed culturally sensitive, multilingual food-safety communication with community partners. The authors identified raw offal as a new outbreak vehicle and recommended that investigations of culturally significant events consider foods beyond routine questionnaires, alongside improved messaging about raw and undercooked meat and offal.

A federal appeals court ruled that the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service lacked authority under the Lacey Act to restrict interstate trade in Burmese pythons and other listed giant snakes within the contiguous United States. Wildlife officials had banned several python and anaconda species to prevent invasive spread, particularly in South Florida. The court did not address the scientific evidence supporting the bans. Reptile keepers say the decision restores owners’ rights to travel with their pets, attend trade shows and seek veterinary care, while conservation advocates warn it could affect other invasive species.

Morgan “Dr. Noc” McSweeney, a biotech scientist and social media educator, discussed using “edutainment” to translate academic research into engaging, actionable public-health content. He prioritizes confused, undecided audiences over committed opponents, emphasizing nuance and evidence because contentious content may gain reach without informing or changing minds. He selects topics from comments, messages, and news, often examining the studies and uncertainties behind major health claims.

McSweeney said personal relatability can build trust in ways institutional communication often cannot; briefly sharing everyday details may make audiences more receptive to his scientific messages. He avoids directly confronting committed anti-science viewers because he finds it emotionally exhausting and rarely persuasive.

He attributes the dominance of questionable health content online partly to underinvestment by institutions such as the NIH, CDC, FDA, and WHO, along with bureaucratic review processes and the difficulty of producing consistently effective social media. While working full time in biotech, he keeps his job separate from his content, though his experience informs his credibility and subject choices. He also describes ignoring or blocking hostile comments to avoid amplifying them and says he may eventually pursue science communication full time.

The Coppock Curve is a long-term smoothed momentum indicator for stocks and indices, devised by E.S.C. Coppock in 1965. It uses a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11- and 14-month rates of change. On a monthly chart, it signals entry when the curve crosses above zero and exit when it crosses below. An S&P 500 backtest since 1960 produced 12 trades over 63 years, all profitable, with reduced drawdown, less market exposure, and better risk-adjusted returns than buy-and-hold. Two example trades each lasted just over six years and returned approximately 80% and 65%.

The excerpt references detailed L4 Fast and L4 Slow peripheral memory maps, including regions decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 subsystem that are reserved for other masters. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB extended address range through a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views. This full range is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems; other masters can access individual views through the 512-MB TILER region in the base 4-GB map.

Package pin assignments and terminal-function tables identify signal names, multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, pin types, internal pull states, supply voltages, and pin functions. MUXED entries also identify the controlling PINCNTLx register, de-selected input states, and multi-mux options.

Boot-configuration pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot modes and GPMC functions. BTMODE bits configure GPMC CS0 wait, address/data multiplexing and bus width, RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior, XIP-on-GPMC options, Ethernet PHY mode, and boot configuration, after which the pins operate as GPMC data/address signals.

The president congratulated the 100th Congress during the Constitution’s bicentennial, emphasizing that the document’s enduring principles should guide the nation. He welcomed House Speaker Jim Wright and Senate Majority Leader Robert Byrd and expressed optimism that congressional leaders could work together in the national interest.

He reported economic progress, including the lowest inflation in 25 years, falling interest rates, increased housing construction, nearly 13 million new jobs, and record employment. He called for a constitutional balanced-budget amendment, a line-item veto, continued deficit-reduction efforts, welfare reform, and legislation protecting older Americans from catastrophic medical costs.

The president accepted responsibility for the failed Iran rescue mission, acknowledging serious mistakes while defending its humanitarian and strategic goals. He urged continued support for freedom and peace rather than allowing setbacks to prevent future action. He requested a larger defense and foreign-affairs budget, citing Soviet military spending and reductions in U.S. security assistance. He supported a political settlement in Afghanistan requiring Soviet withdrawal and Afghan self-determination and defended the Monroe Doctrine by promising continued support for Nicaragua’s freedom fighters.

He urged constructive relations and arms reductions with the Soviet Union while maintaining the Strategic Defense Initiative, human-rights commitments, and U.S. negotiating leverage. He also promoted expanded trade through the Uruguay Round and the proposed U.S.-Canada free trade agreement, while opposing protectionism.

Addressing domestic policy, he called for renewed national competitiveness through science, technology, research, regulatory reform, fair trade, agriculture, worker retraining, and job mobility. He proposed higher literacy, stronger education in mathematics, science, and constitutional documents, drug-free schools, and voluntary prayer in public classrooms.

The president concluded that the Constitution distinguishes America from other nations through “We the people,” because citizens, rather than government, hold authority. He described Americans as soldiers, volunteers, farmers, workers, entrepreneurs, and ordinary citizens committed to freedom, and quoted Benjamin Franklin’s hope that the constitutional era represented a rising rather than setting sun. He ended by affirming that America was unfinished and that its best days had just begun.

The lecture frames sustainable real estate as an asset class and examines how sustainable buildings affect real-estate economics, capital markets, mortgages, and private equity. Tenant demand for green, healthy, and climate-resilient buildings can support rent premiums when occupants value lower operating costs and better indoor conditions. These premiums can increase property values and developer returns, while capital is required to build, buy, or invest in sustainable real estate.

The lecture situates real estate within the emerging field of sustainable finance. Larry Fink’s 2020 letter to CEOs helped emphasize that climate risk is a financial risk and that asset managers acting as fiduciaries must identify and manage future risks. A simplified “sandwich” model connects end users’ choices in the physical space market with capital providers in financial markets. Sustainable preferences can redirect capital toward greener properties.

Real estate connects space and capital markets through asset cash flows, discount rates, and net present value. Investors combine equity and debt from multiple sources and calculate a weighted average cost of capital. An investment proceeds when expected asset returns exceed financing costs or when discounted cash flows produce a positive NPV. Portfolio theory adds bonds, stocks, and real estate to an efficient frontier of risk and return. A genuinely sustainable building can offer higher NOI and lower risk than a conventional building because of regulation, tenant preferences, and investors’ willingness to accept lower required returns, raising its value and shifting its risk-return position. Conversely, penalties, climate-related losses, tenant departures, and risk premiums lower conventional building values. Information asymmetry, market frictions, and limited supply allow inferior buildings to remain in portfolios temporarily. Early investors benefit from information advantages, although increased capital inflows eventually reduce green-building returns while leaving them superior.

The focus then shifts to private-sector debt and mortgages. Mortgage analysis includes delinquency, default, prepayment, and climate risk. Flooding, wildfire, hurricanes, declining communities, and falling property values can cause rational defaults and losses for lenders. Research cited on California wildfires found defaults increased by 1% in properties within fire zones. Because mortgage-backed securities and government-backed mortgage programs are affected by widespread defaults, federal support for mortgages and flood insurance has become a major issue, especially for lower-income households in high-risk locations. The National Flood Insurance Program has lacked sufficient funds, contributing to uninsured properties. A Fannie Mae collaboration aims to incorporate climate risk into property appraisals and train appraisers, although accurate climate-risk pricing could raise borrowing costs and create social-justice and political challenges.

Green mortgages offer energy-efficient homeowners lower rates or larger loans. In the example, a household earning $5,000 monthly could receive a $207,000 conventional loan under a 29% monthly-payment limit, or a $235,000 loan at 33% by presenting a HERS energy-efficiency report. Banks may lend more because energy-efficient property has higher value and a lower loan-to-value ratio, while lower energy bills free household income for mortgage payments. Research using 71,000 CoreLogic loans found energy-efficient homes were one-third less likely to default; later work found stronger effects for lower-income households and similarly lower default risk for commercial properties with Energy Star or LEED ratings.

Green renovation financing allows lenders to advance more money based on expected post-renovation appreciation. For a property worth $100,000, a bank might provide $80,000 conventionally; if renovation is expected to raise its value to $110,000, the bank may provide $88,000, with $8,000 used for renovation.

Finally, the lecture introduces private-equity real-estate financing, distinguishing direct and indirect investing and emphasizing commingled funds. A general partner typically contributes 5–10% and manages investments, while limited partners supply passive capital. Private-equity firms are incorporating ESG into investment memoranda because they expect sustainable real estate to generate stronger business returns. Due diligence and later management or disposition actions address physical and transition risks.

Italian- and Spanish-language Wikipedia blocked all articles on 3 July to protest proposed EU copyright legislation, particularly Articles 11 and 13. The European Committee on Legal Affairs had approved the directive, with a full parliamentary vote scheduled for 5 July. The provisions require content-filtering systems and include a proposed “link tax.” Critics warned that vague rules, differing national implementations and imperfect filters could restrict sharing and search results, potentially endangering Wikipedia’s openness and operation. A football blitz sends five or more defenders directly at the quarterback, rather than the typical four-man rush. Its goal is to pressure or sack the quarterback and disrupt the offense, but additional rushers leave fewer defenders covering receivers and create exploitable gaps.

Defensive coordinators determine when and how to use blitzes. Conventional blitzes maintain defensive-back coverage, while zone blitzes substitute a linebacker for a rushing defensive lineman who drops into coverage, creating deception. Safety and cornerback blitzes bring a deeper defender forward to create surprise, but leave space behind the rush. Zero blitzes leave no deep safety and are used when a run is likely, such as third-and-one. Run blitzes send extra defenders toward the point of attack to stop the run.

Offenses can counter blitzes with quick passes, often targeting a nearby running back, or by using a mobile quarterback to escape the rush. Max-protection audibles keep extra players in to block, slowing the blitz and allowing receivers time to beat their coverage.

Market sentiment reflects the aggregate mood of investors and traders as bullish, neutral, or bearish. Sentiment indicators measure this mood and may identify potential reversals: extreme bullishness can limit further gains because participants may already be positioned for rising prices, while extreme bearishness can precede a turnaround on positive news.

The AAII sentiment index, published weekly since the 1980s by the American Association of Individual Investors, surveys members’ expectations for the stock market over the next six months. Other sentiment indicators include Investors Intelligence Bulls & Bears, the VIX, and 52-week market breadth measures.

Spreadsheet backtests using weekly AAII data since 1987 examined four-week returns. A strategy buying when the bull-bear spread turned negative returned 70% cumulatively, or 0.68% per trade, with lower drawdown than holding the S&P 500 but weak performance during 2000–2010. Buying when the spread was below −20 produced an average gain of 1.03%. Bullish readings above 20 averaged 0.52% gains, while readings above 40 averaged a 0.33% loss. Overall, bearish readings were followed by stronger returns than bullish readings, but the passage concludes that other indicators may be better for short-term trading.

Rapid technological, informational, and social change has made initial LIS degrees insufficient for meeting specialised employment requirements, making lifelong learning essential for Romanian librarians. The paper develops a formal model of information design that combines Bayesian persuasion with behavioral framing effects. A sender observes the world state, while a receiver chooses an action using their beliefs. In addition to a Bayesian signaling or recommendation scheme, the sender may select a framing from a potentially vast natural-language space, represented by a belief oracle mapping each framing to the receiver’s induced belief. Three optimization settings are considered: recommendation-only, framing-only with a fixed recommendation scheme, and joint optimization of framing and recommendations.

The theoretical analysis shows that framing-only optimization is generally difficult: sender utility can be discontinuous in the framing-induced belief, making small oracle errors consequential, and finding the optimal framing is NP-hard even to approximate. Joint optimization is more tractable. When framing and the optimal recommendation strategy are optimized together, sender utility is continuous in the induced belief, making the approach more robust to oracle errors. The authors also provide a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme for this joint problem.

For practical use, the paper proposes a hill-climbing method in which LLMs generate and evaluate framings, serve as belief oracles, and combine with analytical optimization of recommendation strategies. Two case studies examine a realtor framing recommendations to buyers and a clothing brand selecting campaign text and discount strategies. LLM evaluations show strong effectiveness, while human subjects exhibit weaker and more variable responses; nevertheless, the predictions are directionally correct and approximately match the effect size.

The work positions LLM-assisted joint optimization as a scalable alternative to manual framing design and heuristics, while emphasizing the remaining computational difficulties of framing-only optimization. It also identifies opportunities to extend such methods to non-textual media such as images and video.

The passage describes container and distributed-system patterns through Kubernetes examples. In the single-node adapter pattern, a separate adapter container standardizes an application’s monitoring, logging, or health-check interface without modifying the application image. Examples include Prometheus exporters for Redis, Fluentd-based normalization of Redis and Storm logs, and an HTTP health-check adapter for MySQL. This separation improves modularity, reuse, upgradeability, and resource isolation.

Microservices are presented as multi-node architectures in which independently developed services communicate through APIs. They support focused teams, autonomous releases, and independent scaling, but make dependencies, debugging, and system design more difficult. Distributed patterns help manage these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer, with readiness probes indicating when instances can accept traffic. Session affinity can route users consistently by IP address or application-level identifiers, while consistent hashing reduces remapping during scaling. The stateless pattern can be extended with separate replicated Varnish caches for performance, rate limiting, and denial-of-service protection, plus replicated nginx servers for SSL termination. The resulting deployment separates HTTPS, caching, and application-serving responsibilities.

Sharded services assign subsets of requests or data to shards through a routing root. They are typically stateful and allow capacity to scale with data size. In caches, sharding stores distinct data across nodes and uses memory more efficiently than replication, while cache hit rates affect throughput and latency. Individual shards may be replicated for resilience and rollout safety and scaled independently when traffic becomes uneven. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform; keys must reflect properties that affect responses, and consistent hashing minimizes data movement when shard counts change. Requests may reach shards through per-pod ambassadors or shared, load-balanced routing services.

Scatter/gather distributes each request simultaneously to multiple leaf nodes, which perform partial processing before a root combines their results. This parallelizes work and reduces latency, while leaf sharding allows datasets too large for one machine. However, communication overhead and slow “straggler” nodes increase tail latency and can reduce availability because the root waits for every leaf. Replicating each shard allows failures and upgrades to occur without user-visible outages.

Function-as-a-service and event-driven processing are presented as lightweight, stateless execution models that automatically scale and restart functions. They simplify deployment and suit asynchronous, independent events, but introduce operational complexity, limited observability, no local in-memory state, poor support for long-running background work, and potentially high costs for sustained workloads. FaaS decorator functions can transform requests or responses, such as supplying API defaults, while event handlers can perform asynchronous tasks like sending two-factor authentication codes.

Lecture five extends the one-way wave equation to the two-way, second-order equation \(u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}\), also written as a symmetric first-order system whose eigenvalues are \(c\) and \(-c\), representing waves traveling in opposite directions. The continuous solution has the form \(u(x,t)=F(x-ct)+G(x+ct)\), with \(F\) and \(G\) determined by initial displacement and velocity. The lecturer also discusses how variable coefficients, forcing, high-frequency oscillations, and finite boundaries complicate practical wave problems.

The numerical analysis begins with Fourier/exponential substitutions. In the semidiscrete method of lines, space is discretized while time remains continuous. Centered second differences introduce dispersion: the discrete wave number is \(c\sin(k\Delta x/2)/\Delta x\), which approximates \(ck\) for small \(k\Delta x\).

The fully discrete scheme uses centered differences in time and space, producing the leapfrog method. Its stability analysis introduces the Courant number \(r=c\Delta t/\Delta x\); stability requires \(r\leq1\), while larger values cause instability. The next topic is a staggered-grid formulation.

The study demonstrates controlled defect engineering in CVD-grown monolayer MoS₂ using 1 MeV electron irradiation at a flux of approximately \(3\times10^6\) electrons/s for 30–120 seconds. Raman measurements indicated irradiation-induced sulfur vacancies and lattice disorder, while XPS and KPFM showed increasing Mo oxidation and Mo–O bonding, a work-function rise from 4.8 to 5.24 eV, and p-type behavior.

Photoluminescence measurements revealed exciton blueshifts, reduced free-exciton intensity, and increasingly strong defect-bound emission 200–300 meV below the A exciton. Two defect states emerged after prolonged irradiation. Power-dependent PL confirmed defect-state saturation and enhanced defect-mediated recombination. Circularly polarized PL showed that defect emission remained unpolarized and that the A-exciton valley polarization decreased from 62% in as-grown MoS₂ to 38% after 120 seconds of irradiation.

First-principles calculations indicated that sulfur vacancies introduce donor states, while oxygen interaction at vacancy sites creates acceptor states near the valence band. Transitions from the conduction band to these acceptor levels explain the defect emission, and reduced Γ–K valley separation may contribute to irradiation-induced valley depolarization. Overall, the results establish high-energy electron irradiation as a tunable method for introducing defects in monolayer MoS₂, with potential application to other transition-metal dichalcogenides after parameter optimization.

Gold has a long history as currency, jewelry material, and more recently as a commodity speculation vehicle and inflation hedge. The article develops and backtests a strategy trading gold only near all-time highs, using monthly closing prices from the World Bank's Commodities Markets Database. Results show a decent equity curve without major drawdowns: lower returns, but time in the market cut to about a third and maximum drawdown nearly halved. The strategy can help identify bull regimes in gold.

The Wing-T is a football offense built around misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse running game. It makes different plays appear similar, forcing defenses to react rather than attack confidently. Developed by Harold “Tubby” Raymond at the University of Delaware from 1966 to 2001, it is also known as the Delaware Wing-T.

Running the traditional system requires at least two running backs, including a fullback who can run inside, catch passes, and lead blockers. The quarterback must be athletic enough to run or execute waggle passes but need not be an elite passer. Smaller, quick offensive linemen adept at pulling and trapping can be especially effective.

The offense’s strengths include play-action passes, quick motions, deception, and its ability to slow aggressive defenses. Its main weakness is the absence of a traditional dropback passing game, though teams can supplement Wing-T sets with shotgun formations. Common formations include the Wing (100/900), Wing-Slot (Red or Doubles 100), and unbalanced formations.

Common running plays include the Buck Sweep, Down or Belly G, and Trap. Common passing concepts include the Waggle, Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical Pass. The Waggle disguises itself as a Buck Sweep, while play-action passes freeze defenders before quick throws over the middle.

The traditional Wing-T is now primarily a high-school offense and has largely disappeared from major college football. Its principles have nevertheless influenced modern spread offenses, including Gus Malzahn’s attacks at Auburn and UCF.
