The ADS868xW operates in ACQ and CONV states. It enters ACQ at power-up, after an asynchronous reset, or after a conversion. A falling RST edge selects the RESET state, while a rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion. Conversions use an internal clock, and further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored until completion. The host can detect conversion completion through a low-to-high RVS transition or wait for tconv_max. A programmable low-power NAP mode is available during ACQ.

The device has nine configuration registers and supports host writes for configuration and host reads for data retrieval. A data-transfer frame begins on the falling CONVST/CS edge, when RVS goes low, the output word loads into a 32-bit output shift register, and the internal command defaults to NOP. SCLK clocks shift SDI data into the input register and output data from the MSB on selected SDO pins. Pulling CONVST/CS high ends the frame, transfers the input word for command decoding, and begins conversion.

A 32-clock frame is optimal and its input word is valid. Shorter frames cannot contain a valid write and are treated as NOP, although their output data remains valid. In longer frames, the final 32 input bits form the command. Write commands must be 32 bits and execute on the rising CONVST/CS edge. Byte and half-word reads or writes are supported; half-word commands ignore the address LSB.

The next frame’s output contains the command-dependent result: a fixed test pattern, 8- or 16-bit register data followed by zeros, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional appended fields include device address, input-range flags, AVDD alarm flags, input alarm flags, and parity, with unused bits set to zero.

The multiSPI interface provides four legacy SPI-compatible configurations for writes. Reads can use single- or dual-SDO SPI modes or a source-synchronous mode with internal or external clocking and optional dual SDO. SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or asynchronous reset. Changing the selected SPI mode requires the first write to use SPI-00-S, after which subsequent frames use the new protocol. Dual-SDO mode launches two bits per clock edge and requires half as many cycles as single-SDO mode. In source-synchronous operation, RVS supplies the output clock.

The register map includes DEVICE_ID, RST_PWRCTL, SDI_CTL, SDO_CTL, DATAOUT_CTL, RANGE_SEL, ALARM, ALARM_H_TH, and ALARM_L_TH registers. They control identification, reset and power behavior, SPI configuration, output protocol, output flags and test patterns, reference and nine input ranges, alarm status, and alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Writes to protected power-control bits require the key 69h.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit SAR data-acquisition device with an integrated analog front end, ADC driver, programmable gain, and buffered reference. An example industrial module combines an ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to provide eight software-configurable voltage or current channels. It supports standard industrial voltage and current ranges, reaches 1% accuracy in under 5 µs, and includes input overvoltage protection and configurable input and AVDD alarms. Programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis support thermistor temperature monitoring while reducing false triggering from noise.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies. Recommended decoupling includes a 1 µF capacitor near each supply, a minimum 10 µF capacitor for AVDD, and close placement of bypass capacitors. PCB analog and digital sections should be separated, with short ground paths and no vias between supply pins and their bypass capacitors.

NAP mode reduces consumption between conversions. It is enabled through RST_PWRCTL after unlocking the register, and the device remains in NAP while CONVST/CS is high. A falling edge exits NAP, followed by the required tNAP_WKUP delay. Power-down mode disables analog blocks while retaining the interface and register contents. It is entered on a rising CONVST/CS edge after setting PWRDN, and exiting requires clearing PWRDN and waiting tPWRUP.

Corning Incorporated’s Growth and Strategy Council (GSC) provides centralized oversight of innovation across the company’s business segments. Founded as a glassmaker in 1851, Corning repeatedly reinvented itself through products such as Pyrex, television bulbs, fiber optics, ceramic substrates, and scientific consumables. Under CEO Roger Ackerman, it shifted resources from consumer products toward optical fiber and photonics during the telecommunications boom, increasing its market value from $9 billion in 1996 to $50 billion in 2000. The subsequent telecom crash cut annual revenue from $6.3 billion in 2001 to $3.1 billion in 2002, reduced the stock from $100 to $1.50, produced a $5.4 billion loss, and resulted in more than 12,000 layoffs. Despite the downturn, Corning maintained its research spending and chose to preserve its core identity. Management subsequently emphasized balanced growth, disciplined risk management, and continued investment in promising businesses.

By 2008, Corning had 24,800 employees and four segments: Display Technologies, Telecommunications, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences. All were based on a common model of inventing an enabling component, protecting it through intellectual property, and developing large-scale manufacturing capabilities. Business units managed product development, manufacturing, sales, and marketing, while long-term research was centralized at the Sullivan Park R&D facility. This arrangement allowed expertise and technologies to be shared across otherwise distinct markets.

Corning’s innovation governance divided projects between the Technology Council and the GSC. The Technology Council evaluated early-stage opportunities, assessed market size, strategic fit, differentiation, required resources, and other criteria, and decided when projects should advance. The GSC focused on high-potential projects in later stages, advising businesses and controlling the pacing, investment, and resource allocation of major innovation programs. Its principal objective was to maintain a balanced, robust innovation portfolio across existing and developing businesses rather than favor only currently profitable operations.

The GSC began in 2001 and was later led by CEO Wendell Weeks, COO Peter Volanakis, and CTO Joe Miller. It met several times monthly, generally with 18–20 participants and three major topics per meeting. Presenters provided prepared analyses, answered questions, and then left while the core members deliberated; the Director of Strategic Planning subsequently gave written feedback. In September, the council reviewed each business’s technology portfolio using zero-based project budgeting. Its culture emphasized frank, respectful challenge, although some managers found the large meetings intimidating and believed too many attendees diluted discussion.

Corning’s innovation process began with deep technological knowledge, a difficult customer problem, and a unique combination of materials and processes that produced a “keystone” component. Projects advanced through stage gates with commercial, technology, and manufacturing leaders, while decisions examined market, product, process, and business-case questions. Its innovation philosophy emphasized generating many ideas, applying capabilities from failed projects elsewhere, and making sustained long-term investments. Display became profitable after 14 years, and optical fiber required 20 years. Corning also approved a $250 million diesel factory during the telecom downturn.

The GSC supported major opportunities, including an accelerated diesel-filter program for Volkswagen in 2005 and Corning’s 2003 response to Verizon’s fiber-to-the-home initiative. However, planned growth in new businesses created challenges: the council would need to prioritize a larger portfolio, preserve candid discussion as participation expanded, focus on strategic rather than routine problem-solving, and understand unfamiliar business models. Its effectiveness would also depend on program managers supplying balanced and candid information.

The article presents a long-only strategy for the Global X Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), using a three-period Donchian Channel and a 200-period exponential moving average (EMA) to filter false signals. Optimization emphasizes robustness across varied settings rather than selecting the best-performing inputs.

Daily backtesting from September 13, 2016 produced 87 trades and outperformed buy-and-hold with lower volatility. A two-hour version also showed a smooth equity curve and results close to the daily strategy. However, BOTZ’s short history, low trade count, and potential curve fitting limit the statistical reliability of the results. The authors recommend out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period before considering the strategy viable for live trading.
The team lost despite starting well and attributed the loss to turnovers, poor puck management, and making plays too easy for opponents.

A Tennessee judge sentenced Christopher Drone Bassett to life plus 35 years, Richard Gregory Williams III to 143 years and Kipling Deshawn Colbert to 109 years for the 2015 death of 15-year-old Zaevion Dobson, who shielded friends from gunfire. Bassett was convicted of first-degree murder and Williams and Colbert of facilitating murder; their terms include charges unrelated to Dobson’s death.

The S&P 500 Financial Services sector includes banks, investment houses, insurers, and fintech companies serving individuals, SMEs, and corporations. Its capitalization-weighted index is tracked by Vanguard Financials ETF (VFH) and Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF). As of July 21, 2022, its largest stocks included Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs.

After falling 85% from its 2007 peak during the 2008–09 crisis, the sector changed and consolidated substantially. Its high volatility makes it suitable for trading, although it is highly correlated with the broader market. A backtested XLF strategy using monthly volatility-based trading edges recorded 198 trades, a 1.05% average gain, a 73% win rate, a 21% maximum drawdown, and a 2.25 profit factor. The strategy reportedly works across most stock indices but not commodities.

Amazon is developing a top-secret domestic robot, codenamed “Vesta,” through its Lab126 division. The project is ramping up hiring, with employee trials potentially beginning this year and consumer release as early as 2019, though neither timeline nor capabilities are certain. Prototypes can navigate homes using cameras and computer vision and may serve as mobile Alexa devices. Advances in AI, sensors, and voice activation, along with Amazon’s history of hardware subsidies, could support a mass-market launch. Previous consumer robots have had limited success, and Amazon declined to comment on the project.

SMPFC delayed its P100–150 billion follow-on offering to the third or fourth quarter, citing stock rights offerings and market volatility. San Miguel Food and Beverage would have a 4.3% float, requiring an offering to meet the 15% ownership minimum. Planned capital spending is P56–60 billion over three years. In 2017, net income rose 16% to P6.9 billion and revenue rose 5% to P117 billion.

The disclosure describes computer-implemented systems, methods, and program products for customizable digital twin simulations of physical assets. A digital twin is a virtual counterpart whose real-time data is supplied by sensors, IoT devices, and recording systems, enabling remote monitoring, diagnosis, and performance prediction.

A digital twin module creates and stores a base model and successive versions reflecting reported or detected asset changes, using timestamped timelines and logs. Collected performance data can identify configuration or operating deviations that trigger creation of updated versions. Users can select the current model, an earlier version, or a hybrid model assembled from components of two or more versions, with component mapping supported by a graphical interface or augmented reality.

The simulation engine lets users focus on selected components, bypass others, substitute alternatives, and provide overriding values for nonsimulated upstream portions. It can run multiple simulations with different substitutions, pass intermediate results between downstream components, and produce final results. A reporting engine displays, formats, archives, retrieves, and shares results, supporting comparison, reruns, and parameter revisions.

Embodiments may operate across networked host systems, clients, repositories, sensors, IoT devices, and recording systems in cloud or other computing environments, including containerized digital twin modules.

Nigeria is experiencing growth in large shopping malls, driven by demand for one-stop shopping, convenience, and increasingly brand-conscious consumers. More than five upscale malls have reportedly opened, while retailers such as Shoprite and Spar have expanded. The malls are viewed as signs of investor confidence, offering convenient shopping and entertainment while creating jobs and boosting government tax revenues.

Paul Tisdale said Exeter City could be proud of their performance in a 1-0 defeat to table-toppers Luton Town, with the Grecians fielding six missing players and giving 20-year-old Jordan Storey his first league start in defence. The only goal came from Harry Cornick's deflected strike, and although Tisdale conceded Luton deserved to win, he praised his side's effort and the way they defended, finishing with Kane Wilson, Dean Moxey and Storey at the back. Liam McAlinden's late equaliser was ruled out for a foul by Robbie Simpson on goalkeeper Marek Stech, a decision Tisdale disputed. He credited Matt Taylor and Andy Tillson for developing Storey, now a starting centre-back. City next host promotion rivals Wycombe Wanderers, and Tisdale said their form remains strong despite the defeat.

Fabry–Perot cavities provide high quality factors and frequency stability, but conventional polished mirrors are large, difficult to scale, and have large radii of curvature that increase mode volume. Microfabricated alternatives offer compact integration but can have lower finesse or require complex coupling. At visible wavelengths, high finesse is especially challenging because surface-scattering loss increases as the inverse square of wavelength.

The work presents a scalable method for producing buckled dielectric membrane micromirrors. A double-side-polished silicon wafer is smoothed through repeated wet oxidation and hydrofluoric-acid removal, reducing RMS roughness from about 0.3 nm to 33–50 pm. A roughly 5 μm SiO₂/Ta₂O₅ quarter-wave stack with a protective SiO₂ cap is deposited, followed by photolithographic patterning and a Bosch etch that suspends the coated regions. Compressive strain in the dielectric causes the membranes to buckle into concave mirrors. Arrays of 600 μm mirrors were fabricated with radii of curvature from 0.9 to 21 mm. Simulations matched measured profiles with an R² of 99.98%, and optical profiling showed rotationally symmetric mirror surfaces.

Two mirrors were aligned on translation stages and characterized using a swept ring-down method near 780.24 nm while monitoring the TEM₀₀ mode. The highest measured finesse was \(0.89\times10^6\), with \(\kappa=(2\pi)(233\pm1)\) kHz, and the highest quality factor was \(2.3\times10^9\), with \(\kappa=(2\pi)(124\pm0.5)\) kHz. Finesse decreased with cavity length because of diffraction, shape deviations, and other imperfections; quality factor initially increased, plateaued, and eventually fell when cavity lengths substantially exceeded the mirror curvature.

The measured finesse bounded combined absorption and scattering loss at no more than 2.20 ppm. Assuming zero absorption gave an upper roughness limit of 90 pm. The coating’s estimated absorption of 1.5–2 ppm indicates that scattering was comparable to or lower than state-of-the-art visible dielectric coatings. Extrapolation to telecommunications wavelengths predicted a finesse of \(3.5\times10^6\).

The process also produced compact glued cavity assemblies from 1.7 mm-diameter silicon chip cutouts, including 45 μm and 1 mm cavity lengths. A fiber-coupled 45 μm cavity had a linewidth of \(\kappa=(2\pi)(5.16\pm0.14)\) MHz and an FSR of 3.18 THz. The resulting mirrors, arrays, and assemblies are intended for visible lasers, sensing, quantum networking, compact filters, transfer cavities, and external laser cavities.

At reset de-assertion, BTMODE states are latched into CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC bus width, wait enable, and multiplexing; BTMODE[4:0] defines primary and fallback boot order. Bits [7:5] are reserved and pulled down. For EMAC, bits [9:8] select PHY mode; for XIP, bit [10] selects GPMC muxing.

Messaging interfaces are expected to remain stable while apps expand into broader ecosystems. WeChat already supports ordering food or cabs, gaming, and dating. In India, WhatsApp has about 94% reach and is adding services such as voice/video calls and payments. Competition is shifting toward user engagement through content, professionally produced media, and gaming. Hike could combine payments with Airtel TV and Wynk content. As India’s internet market consolidates around large conglomerates, chat platforms are becoming a strategic battleground.

The passage describes a network security appliance with a local touchscreen or similar interface for administering packet-filtering and network configuration when remote access is unavailable or disrupted by denial-of-service attacks. Local interface commands may receive priority processing and reserved memory, enabling administrators to close ports, block packet sources, modify filters, prioritize rules, and pause selected traffic during attacks.

Complex packet rules may be matched through geoprocessing techniques using multidimensional minimum bounding rectangles and spatial indexes such as R-trees, which can accelerate searches compared with conventional B-tree queries. A management server may distribute mandatory rules for known threats to all appliances and potential-threat rules to selected subsets according to assigned likelihoods or weights, reducing memory, processing, and bandwidth demands while allowing attack reports to increase a rule’s distribution.

The appliance may also buffer packets from unrecognized devices until a nearby administrator authorizes or rejects them through the local interface, after which packets may be processed, forwarded, modified, or discarded. Administrative requests can require authentication, and attack or device events may generate logs and visible or audible notifications.

At Apple Inc.’s March 10, 2015 annual meeting, shareholders elected Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner as directors. They approved Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent accounting firm for 2015, an advisory vote on executive compensation, and an amendment adding 50 million shares to the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Shareholder proposals titled “Risk Report” and “Proxy Access for Shareholders” were not approved. The amended plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Environmental Defence criticized Canada’s finding that studied phthalates posed no human-health risk, noting the EU identified at least four as risky. The group urged Canada to require manufacturers to prove products safe; the government is considering a 2018 plan to modernize chemical regulations.

The passage argues that standardized-testing monopolies constrain educational freedom by narrowing curriculum, encouraging teaching to tests, and extending public-school testing mandates into private school-choice programs. Studies cited show that educators alter instruction in response to high-stakes exams, while several states require particular tests for graduation, scholarships, or college admissions. The author also claims that SAT and ACT standards have weakened, citing declining reading performance and a reported drop in SAT math rigor.

Rather than banning standardized testing, the passage advocates allowing schools or students to choose among assessments. The Classic Learning Test is presented as an alternative for grades 3–12 and college entry that measures literacy and numeracy through classic works, while a cited study found a 0.89 correlation between CLT and SAT scores. The author recommends that states offer school-choice programs multiple testing options and accept all such options for public-college admissions and scholarships, noting that Arkansas and Florida have already adopted such reforms.

The Supreme Court is considering whether Colorado’s 2019 Minor Conversion Therapy Law, which prohibits licensed mental-health professionals from providing conversion therapy to minors, violates the First Amendment as applied to Christian therapist Kaley Chiles. The 10th Circuit upheld the law as a regulation of professional conduct incidental to speech, applying rational-basis review; Judge Harris Hartz dissented, saying the majority improperly treated speech as conduct.

Chiles and the federal government argue that talk therapy is inseparable from the message conveyed, making the law content- and viewpoint-based and subject to strict scrutiny. They contend Colorado lacks evidence that counseling causes harm, the ban is not narrowly tailored, and it selectively prevents licensed counselors from discussing certain desired changes while allowing similar conversations by unlicensed people and with adults. The solicitor general also says Colorado appears unlikely to satisfy strict scrutiny.

Colorado responds that the law narrowly prohibits a specific unsafe and ineffective medical treatment, not general discussion, and is a permissible regulation of healthcare and the standard of care. It argues rational-basis review applies and, alternatively, that the law satisfies strict scrutiny because protecting minors from harmful or ineffective treatment is compelling and the ban is narrowly tailored.

A Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians analysis concludes that expanding palliative and hospice care would improve care while reducing costs. Hospital-based palliative care saves an estimated $7,000–$8,000 per patient compared with acute care, while outpatient, home-based, and hospice programs can reduce costly hospital use, improve satisfaction and quality of life, and potentially extend survival. An Ontario study projected that expanded home care could avoid $191 million–$385 million in costs. The society recommends that governments expand, monitor, and evaluate access to a mix of palliative-care programs as Canada’s population ages.

Gardaí in Louth appealed for information about 18-year-old Cameron Conor’s murder in Dunleer and are seeking his iPhone for vital clues. Separately, Dublin officers arrested two people and seized a shotgun, €1m in drugs and cash, preventing a likely gangland attack.

AMP chairman David Murray blamed ASX governance principles for weakening financial-sector governance standards and creating a “trust deficit.” He urged institutions to redesign governance mechanisms, arguing broad principles had become prescriptive “one-size-fits-all” regulations that institutions follow by default.

The seventh Johnston Press South Business Awards were held at Brighton’s Grand Hotel and presented by TV personality Nick Wallis. Guardian Angel Carers of Chichester won Overall Business of the Year and Large Business of the Year. Olive and Vine in Midhurst received the Place to Eat or Drink award, Brandon Relph of Go Creative won Young Achiever, and Southsea Bathing Hut was named Retailer of the Year. Talks at Six, a Chichester forum that hosts charitable talks, received the Outstanding Contribution to the Community award after raising over £7,500 in 15 months. Winners were also recognized across customer service, innovation, green business, training, hospitality, manufacturing, employer, employee and lifetime achievement categories.

The Missouri Supreme Court affirmed a verdict for the defendants. The court held that the jury charge sufficiently presented the plaintiff’s allegation that the defendants negligently failed to sound their horn or give warning when approaching the intersection. Because the petition did not allege a right-of-way violation or failure to reduce speed, and no specific requests were made, the court’s omission of instructions on those issues was not error. A charge concerning violations of state law and city ordinance did not prevent the jury from considering other negligence allegations. The court could instruct on comparative negligence because the evidence supported findings that both parties were negligent. Any error concerning damages was harmless because the jury found for the defendants. Conflicting evidence authorized the verdict, and no legal error appeared.
CBN introduced Form X for SME forex applications, requiring basic documents to ease access for genuine forex needs of $10,000 or less.

The passage describes embodiments for enhancing fast-forward and rewind (“trick-play”) during video streaming. A media guidance application and streaming client maintain a normal buffer of continuous content and separately buffer selected frames—often key frames—outside that window for use during faster-than-real-time playback. Frame-address metadata or indexes identify frame locations, allowing ranged requests for individual frames without downloading intervening ranges. A trick-play optimizer selects frames, sampling intervals, buffer sizes, and source streams based on playback rate, streaming performance metrics, anticipated jump points, and user requests. The video player uses the buffered frames to provide frequent visual updates and approximate requested trick-play speeds.

The streaming client assembles content from multiple bitrate streams, adaptively selects streams, monitors network conditions, and later fills omitted frame ranges to restore continuous normal playback. A proxy server can generate indexes, metadata, and specialized audio-only, video-only, key-frame, or trick-play streams for conventional servers lacking such support. The disclosed system may include a video repository, streaming and proxy servers, a video player, a performance monitor, and a trick-play optimizer, with HLS-compatible implementations described.

NVIDIA appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer effective June 17, 2019, reporting to Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress. Robertson succeeds Michael Byron, who moved into a new NVIDIA finance role covering merger and acquisition integration and financial systems. Robertson previously held accounting leadership positions at Western Digital and SanDisk and is a certified public accountant. His at-will offer includes a $650,000 annual salary, a $600,000 sign-on bonus subject to repayment if he leaves before his first anniversary, and 15,000 restricted stock units vesting over four years, contingent on continued employment. He is also eligible for NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and comprehensive benefits.

Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months in a young offender institution after pleading guilty to stabbing Liam Brown in the abdomen with a flick knife during an argument over a spilled drink at Plymouth’s Newmarket Tavern. He also admitted carrying an offensive weapon, possessing cannabis and breaching a suspended sentence for affray. The judge cited Haydon’s violent record, drinking and drug use. Brown required overnight hospital observation but was not thought to have suffered lasting damage.

SPYR announced that shareholders of record on May 19, 2017, would receive a one-for-one stock dividend in a new publicly traded spin-off company separating its restaurant division. The spin-off plans to license or franchise the Eat at Joe’s brand, manufacture and distribute branded foods, and potentially acquire food-concept companies. The release estimated potential share values using historical Eat at Joe’s trading prices and described the new company as a low-float stock. Stock Market Media Group disclosed that SPYR compensated it with $5,000 monthly and 250,000 restricted shares under a one-year publishing contract, subject to securities-law and trading-volume restrictions.

Around 56,000 new breast cancer cases occur annually in the UK. Lumps may be pea-sized or large, hard and irregular, and can occur anywhere in the breast or armpit. Self-examination should include checking for swelling, dimpling, changes in breast shape or size, dryness, redness, rashes, nipple discharge or inversion, and unusual pain.

Checks can be visual while standing before a mirror with arms raised, followed by feeling the breasts and armpits while lying down and sitting up. Palpate with slight pressure in a circular motion from the collarbone toward the nipple, including beneath the breast. Familiarity with normal breast appearance and feel helps identify changes, which may be easier to detect when skin is moist. Checks are recommended every two weeks to monthly, on the same day each month, around a week after menstruation for those who menstruate.

Any persistent lump or concerning change should be assessed by a doctor, who may review medical and family history, medicines, lifestyle, and refer for examination. Screening can detect cancer when no lump is noticed. Risk factors include BRCA1/2 mutations, early menstruation, later menopause, never giving birth, giving birth first after age 30, and long-term combined HRT. An active lifestyle and breastfeeding may reduce risk.

Men can rarely develop breast cancer, usually after age 60; a lump is the main symptom, but nipple changes can also occur. Early diagnosis improves the likelihood of successful treatment, and over three-quarters of women diagnosed remain alive ten years later.

A 167-million-year-old fossil from Scotland’s Isle of Skye revealed a new lizard species, *Breugnathair elgolensis*, with python-like hooked teeth and snake-like jaws combined with a short, fully limbed body. CT and synchrotron X-ray analysis showed that the specimen possessed both snake-like and gecko-like features and belonged to the predatory squamate group Parviraptoridae. Its unusual anatomy suggests that either early snake ancestors differed from expectations or snake-like features evolved independently in a primitive lineage. Its exact relationship to snake origins remains uncertain.

A100 includes a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7 times larger than V100’s, divided into two partitions and 40 slices. It delivers 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth and 5120 bytes/clk reads. The larger cache benefits HPC and AI workloads, while Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM read/write and L2 read bandwidth by up to fourfold.

Chicago is bolstering security for three major events expected to draw about 1.7 million marathon spectators, 45,000 baseball fans, and more than 60,000 football fans. Concern has heightened following the Las Vegas massacre and reports that a gunman had reserved rooms overlooking the Lollapalooza festival, raising fears of an attack from a nearby high-rise.

Police will deploy 1,000 more officers than usual Sunday and increase undercover officers around the marathon. Security measures include bag checks, restrictions on unattended items and access to the marathon start and finish, coordination with downtown building personnel, and public vigilance for suspicious behavior. Mayor Rahm Emanuel said he was “100 percent” confident the events were secure, while security experts emphasized layered defenses and noted that copycat attacks are rare.

These precautions echo those adopted after the 2004 Boston Marathon bombings. Several runners said the Las Vegas attack increased their concerns but did not cause them to withdraw.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 support a 32 kHz RTC_B with calendar counters, binary or BCD format, leap-year correction for 1901–2099, customizable calendar alarms, interval and periodic wake-up interrupts, operation in STANDBY, crystal-offset and temperature-drift calibration up to ±240 ppm total, and an RTC calibration output on GPIO. The LFSS also includes an independent watchdog timer driven by the fixed 32 kHz LFOSC, with a programmable divider, eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours, and a POR reset if the watchdog is not serviced. The windowed watchdog timer supports eight selectable periods, reset or interrupt generation, automatic stopping during sleep, and interval-timer operation.

TIMGx general-purpose timers and TIMAx advanced timers provide compatible common features. TIMGx supports 16- or 32-bit counting modes, an 8-bit prescaler, repeat-reload operation, selected shadow registers, QEI and Hall-sensor inputs on specified instances, synchronization and cross-triggering, and interrupt, DMA, and cross-peripheral triggers. TIMAx adds a 16-bit up/down or up-down counter, repeat counter, additional capture/compare channels, complementary PWM outputs with programmable dead time, and configurable fault handling, including fast responses and safe output states.

DAC_OUT connects to PA15, so external signals on PA15 are not recommended when DAC_OUT is enabled. The IOMUX selects peripheral functions on digital I/O and controls output drivers, input paths, and SHUTDOWN wake-up logic; pin features vary by device and should be checked in the device data sheet.

The device provides a two-wire ARM-compatible SWD interface. Its boot strap loader supports device configuration and programming through UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, and can be disabled. It can be invoked during boot through BSL_invoke conditions, automatically on an unprogrammed device, or by a runtime SYSRST command. A memory-mapped FACTORY region contains read-only capability information, factory trim data, and hardware revision and identification values, which are also included in package markings.

Recommended typical-application connections include 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 10 nF pulldown, a 100 kΩ, 0.1% ROSC-to-VSS resistor when SYSOSC frequency correction is enabled, and a 0.47 µF capacitor at VCORE. Open-drain I/O requires an external pullup for high-level I2C or UART output.

TI provides development resources including the MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, Resource Explorer, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm Embedded, IAR Embedded Workbench, and Keil MDK. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental X-prefixed devices from fully qualified MSP-prefixed production devices. Documentation and support include the technical reference manual, data sheet, boot strap loader guide, E2E forums, revision history, and device-specific errata.

The April 2025 revision updated device variants, electrical and timing specifications, ADC, comparator, SPI, DMA, flash, SRAM, security, LFSS, UART, timer, and timer cross-trigger information. Mechanical, packaging, orderable-part, material, RoHS, moisture-sensitivity, marking, and automotive-qualified-version information are also provided.
AI models generated bacteriophage genomes from scratch; some outperformed a well-studied strain in laboratory tests.

Saudi Aramco plans to change its Asian crude official selling price formula from October, the first benchmark change since the mid-1980s, according to trade sources. The new formula will combine DME Oman futures prices with Platts’ Dubai cash assessment. The change could boost DME Oman liquidity and related hedging instruments. Aramco’s pricing influences other regional producers and more than 12 million barrels per day of crude bound for Asia, though other producers have not decided whether to change benchmarks.

The speaker welcomes the visiting Native American delegation, affirms friendship and a desire for permanent peace, and pledges that the seventeen states will respect Native lands and punish encroachment. Responding to a request to purchase land for payment of trade debts, the speaker says Mississippi lands are favored for boat stops, provisions, and care for sick travelers, while Tombigbee lands are not discussed in detail. Negotiators familiar with the territory will determine the boundary and an equitable price. The speaker states that previously ceded lands were paid for when purchased, so no repayment is owed. Native people are encouraged to farm, raise livestock, and spin and weave rather than rely on hunting, with assistance offered in adopting those practices. Clothing and supplies sent previously were gifts, and the land on which a requested store was placed would remain Native-owned. The Secretary of War will address remaining matters and honor any promises made. The delegation will receive carriages, care, and a safe return journey by land, and the speaker expresses hope for the nation’s protection and prosperity.

The Florida Second District Court of Appeal reversed the denial of Genel Altimeaux’s unemployment benefits and directed reinstatement of his award. After a dispute over Haitian workers’ pay, Altimeaux was told he was no longer employed by Ocean Construction. A referee, at a hearing Altimeaux did not attend, found that he voluntarily quit based on supervisor Bruce Milliken’s testimony. On remand, the referee found Altimeaux received no notice and held a second hearing.

At the second hearing, Altimeaux denied saying he would quit. Supervisor William Tranowski said the crew quit but acknowledged he never personally heard Altimeaux say he was quitting. The referee nevertheless relied on Milliken’s earlier, uncross-examined testimony to find a voluntary quit. The court held that this was not competent, substantial evidence because Altimeaux had not been permitted to cross-examine Milliken, and the remaining testimony did not support the finding.

Parents have raised concerns about transparency in Township High School District 113’s search for a new Highland Park High School principal, including why only two parents serve on the stakeholder interview committee. Superintendent Christopher Dignam said the process mirrors last year’s Deerfield search. Ray and Associates is screening candidates to replace Tom Koulentes, who is leaving June 30. An 18-member committee will interview two or three finalists April 25, when the district aims to select a principal.

Pin and Pull is a perimeter run concept that creates favorable down-block angles and sends lead blockers into space. Its strengths include getting extra blockers to the point of attack, using pre-snap alignments to set up pulls, and allowing the tailback to run from the C-gap to the sideline. The concept requires at least two guards capable of pulling and is best suited to speed backs who can stress defenders horizontally and cut vertically, though power backs can also succeed.

Unlike the traditional Buck Sweep, which includes an inside run threat, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. Detailed assignments are provided against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, including pull, kickout, log, down, back, and combination blocks, along with tailback and quarterback exchange rules. Two variations use a toss instead of a handoff: Pin and Pull Toss, featuring motion toward the formation’s core, and TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss, which adds a tight end and wing to create a four-man blocking surface and advantageous angles.

Researchers equipped greater noctule bats with motion sensors and microphones to document their nighttime hunts. The bats ascended above migrating songbirds, then dived steeply while emitting feeding buzzes before capturing and consuming birds in flight. Recordings captured one robin’s distress call and a 23-minute airborne meal; one other bird escaped near the ground. Wing injuries, DNA analysis, and feathers and blood on captured bats further confirmed the attacks. The study provides the first tracking of a greater noctule pursuing and catching a songbird in flight.

An Investing.com article argues that gold’s strong Friday rally lacked confirmation from silver, platinum, and mining stocks. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF closed below its April high for a third consecutive session, which the author views as bearish and indicative of an early stage in a larger decline. Gold remains below a rising resistance line, while the U.S. dollar index retested the neck of an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, suggesting a possible rally to at least 101.3. After sharp equity losses, stocks paused above 6,250 but remained below rising support; the author says bearish signals persist and compares the broader setup to 2008. The page also promotes a stock screener, provides trading risk disclosures, and includes a reader criticizing the technical-analysis interpretation.

Verizon and AST SpaceMobile announced a commercial agreement to provide space-based cellular broadband across the continental U.S., expanding Verizon’s coverage. The author rates Verizon a “strong buy,” citing modestly improved growth prospects and competitive positioning, along with expected revenue and earnings growth, low trading multiples, and favorable analyst sentiment. AST SpaceMobile is rated “sell” because minimal revenue, heavy dilution, and a high valuation make it highly speculative. After the announcement, Verizon shares rose over 9%, while ASTS were nearly flat.

Former Nepalese prime minister K.P. Oli won his parliamentary seat, while his Communist UML party and Maoist allies appeared headed for a majority. Oli pledged a full five-year term, infrastructure development, and a geopolitical balance between China and India; final results were pending.

Brock University research found that rosemary extract inhibited A549 lung cancer cell growth and survival, enhanced apoptosis, and blocked Akt signaling and related protein activation. Published in *Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy*, the study suggests potential anti-tumour and chemopreventive properties but requires further investigation. Researchers are examining whether carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid are responsible and caution against recommending increased rosemary consumption for lung cancer prevention or treatment.

Displayed plans cover a 32-mile M4 smart-motorway upgrade between junctions 3 and 12. Starting in September, the £862.4m project includes four-lane widening, rebuilding 11 bridges, widening four others, and variable-speed technology; completion is due by March 2022.

The passage compiles articles published January 16–17, 2002, about Enron’s bankruptcy and the resulting investigations into its accounting, advisers, directors, auditors, and political relationships.

Enron’s 2000 partnership with Blockbuster was intended to deliver movies through its fiber-optic network, but the companies split after eight months. Enron then created the off-balance-sheet Project Braveheart, also known as EBS Content Systems, without Blockbuster’s knowledge. Enron assigned the partnership a $124.8 million valuation, obtained $115.2 million from CIBC in exchange for 93% of its cash flow for ten years, and structured nominally outside ownership through nCube and another partnership. Arthur Andersen approved the structure and valuation. Enron reported $53 million in profits for the fourth quarter of 2000 and $57.9 million for the first quarter of 2001 even though the Blockbuster pilot had few customers and was not profitable. Those $110.9 million in claimed profits were reversed after the venture ended, contributing to a $618 million third-quarter loss.

Enron used numerous partnerships to move debt off its balance sheet, obtain financing and support expansion into broadband and other businesses. CFO Andrew Fastow headed the LJM and LJM2 partnerships, and Enron’s board twice waived its ethics code to permit his participation despite his financial conflicts. Enron later estimated that Fastow made more than $30 million from those partnerships. Enron subsequently restated earnings by $586 million, or 20%, and its disclosures of the partnerships contributed to falling investor confidence, the collapse of its stock, and its December 2, 2002 bankruptcy filing.

Arthur Andersen records showed that its executives discussed LJM, off-balance-sheet accounting, Fastow’s conflicts and Enron’s aggressive transaction structures in February 2001, yet decided to retain Enron as a client. Internal memoranda also recorded Sherron Watkins’s August 2001 warning to Andersen about accounting irregularities and possible conflicts of interest. Andersen fired audit partner David Duncan, who had overseen the Enron account, for ordering the destruction of Enron-related documents after regulators began examining the company’s books. Duncan was questioned by congressional investigators, who said his limited recollection and the document destruction raised concerns about possible illegal conduct.

Pricewaterhouse advised on asset transfers involving LJM and LJM2, while KPMG issued independent reports on the partnerships. Deloitte’s peer review of Andersen noted minor shortcomings but recommended no action. McKinsey had advised Enron on strategy and operations for years and helped it develop its asset-light model, but denied advising on financial reporting, financing, partnerships or off-balance-sheet vehicles and denied participating in investment decisions.

Enron directors’ waiver of the ethics code raised questions about potential liability amid nearly 50 shareholder suits and possible efforts by insurers to cancel or rescind directors-and-officers coverage. SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt’s prior representation of Andersen and other accounting firms prompted demands that he recuse himself from the Enron inquiry. Pitt declined, saying the SEC chairman does not manage investigations, while critics questioned the appearance of conflicts.

The articles also examined Enron’s political relationships. Enron representatives met Vice President Dick Cheney’s energy task force six times, and a congressional report said numerous energy policies benefited Enron. Enron and its executives also gave millions to political campaigns and maintained ties to figures in both parties. White House economic advisers monitored Enron’s worsening financial and market effects in October 2001 but did not inform President Bush, according to the White House, and rejected Enron’s requests for assistance. Former Senator Joseph Lieberman’s chief of staff lobbied his staff for Enron shortly before becoming Enron’s lobbyist, although Lieberman said the contacts would not affect his investigation.

Following losses to employees whose retirement funds were heavily invested in Enron stock, the Labor, Treasury and Commerce departments formed a task force to study diversification, employer restrictions on selling company shares, investment advice, pension rules and possible limits on company stock in 401(k) plans. Consumer advocates argued that stronger laws were needed.

Enron Europe said its core power and gas trading business was sound but that the collapse destroyed confidence and financing, sharply reducing European market liquidity. The IntercontinentalExchange reported a 30% increase in January trading volume and planned clearing services to reduce counterparty risk. American Electric Power also acquired Enron Nordic Energy, adding personnel and trading capabilities in the Nordic region.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture and related GeForce RTX, NVIDIA A40, and RTX A6000 products. GDDR6X memory supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, more than 52% above the TU102 GPU in the RTX 2080 Ti. Its pseudo-independent memory channels assist BVH ray traversal, while an Error Detection and Replay feature detects failed memory transmissions and retries them to help identify overclocking limits.

NVIDIA RTX IO provides APIs for loading and streaming assets directly from NVMe SSDs to GPU memory. Combined with Microsoft DirectStorage, it moves compressed data to the GPU for lossless decompression, reducing CPU demands that can otherwise consume multiple processor cores during game loading. The passage claims improvements of up to 100 times over hard drives and traditional storage APIs, along with faster game loading, improved frame rates, reduced object pop-in and stutter, and efficient texture streaming. RTX IO also supports professional workflows involving large datasets, rendering, CAD, scientific visualization, and virtual reality.

The NVIDIA A40 data-center GPU is based on GA10x and is positioned for visual computing, AI, simulation, and data science. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to five times AI-training throughput—or ten times with sparsity—and twice the PCIe Gen4 bandwidth. It has 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB by linking two A40 GPUs with NVLink, and supports vGPU, Quadro Sync, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

The RTX A6000 includes a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA cores, second- and next-generation RT Cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory; two boards can provide 96 GB of combined memory through NVLink. It targets professional rendering, simulation, virtual production, engineering, and deep-learning workloads.

GA10x GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including Display Stream Compression and dynamic HDR. Their fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports hardware-accelerated decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. AV1 playback can be offloaded from the CPU, with the passage citing 8K60 HDR playback at roughly 4% CPU usage versus above 85% for software decoding. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC and is described as exceeding software x264 Fast quality while matching x264 Medium quality in common streaming settings.

The architecture provides up to twice the performance of the prior generation in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Second-generation RT Cores improve ray-triangle intersection performance and support motion blur and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute, while third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU, has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, and supports 8K HDR rendering through DLSS. The RTX 3070 uses the GA104 GPU, exceeds the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti in performance, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

COTUTOR is a generative AI educational model that combines Bayesian knowledge tracing, signal processing, and convex optimization to deliver real-time, personalized instruction. Unlike systems based primarily on end-to-end generative inference or retrieval-augmented prompts, it maintains an explicit, interpretable model of each student’s learning trajectory.

The model operates as an iterative flywheel. It collects submission and grading data, participation logs, and student queries and feedback; preprocesses these multichannel time-series signals; estimates knowledge states probabilistically; predicts next steps; and recommends resources or activities. Student responses continuously update mastery probabilities, latent states, and policy parameters. Convex optimization provides transparent decision boundaries, globally optimal state updates, and lower inference costs than autoregressive LLMs.

COTUTOR was implemented with online judge data from an introductory C programming course. Submission histories include timestamps, attempts, scores, verdicts, error types, resource usage, and problem difficulty. Exponential smoothing captures recent context, while Bayesian updates estimate skill mastery after each correct or incorrect submission. Recommendations can include harder exercises, review sessions, or targeted interventions.

Interactive copilots were integrated into My Code Weapon and Nemobot to provide deadline reminders, question handling, and links to recommended materials. The system distinguishes itself through persistent student modeling, optimization-based personalization, support for experimentation, standardized responses, and instructor review of chatbot outputs.

A case study formulates resource allocation across educational sessions as a convex optimization problem constrained by normalized resources, priorities, and dependencies between theoretical and application content. It models student sentiment, emotional volatility, and resource influence, and evaluates individual and collective allocation for 30 sessions using theory and application resources. The proposed evaluation tests improved knowledge-state estimation and learning outcomes against unassisted learning, BKT, DKT, and code-DKT; the paper reports stronger performance and improved real-world learning effectiveness.

BioNTech SE’s InstaDeep special-call slide deck appears on Seeking Alpha with transcript-team information, stock-analysis headlines, and a chart spanning September 26–October 1, 2025, with values from 96.98 to 102.72.

A November 26, 2001 email compilation reviewed press coverage of Enron’s financial crisis, its proposed acquisition by Dynegy, accounting concerns, and related developments. Dynegy’s roughly $9.3 billion stock deal, plus about $13 billion in assumed debt, offered $10.85 per Enron share, but Enron’s shares fell to about $4.71 as investors questioned completion. Both companies continued to support the merger, which required shareholder approval. Dynegy retained broad walk-away rights involving material adverse changes, untrue representations, or litigation liabilities, including a $3.5 billion liability threshold, with possible $350 million termination fees.

ChevronTexaco, which owned 26% of Dynegy, supplied Enron with $1.5 billion in cash and planned to invest $2.5 billion in the combined company while potentially increasing its stake. The proposed merger would give Dynegy more than $200 billion in revenue, $90 billion in assets, and an estimated 20% to 25% of the energy-trading market. Dynegy also had rights to Enron’s Northern Natural Gas pipeline if the merger failed. Regulators and California officials raised antitrust and market-power concerns about the combination.

Enron sought $500 million to $1 billion from outside investors while relying on a $500 million to $1 billion contribution from JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup that depended on an unofficial pact among lenders, rating agencies, Enron, and Dynegy. A $690 million note repayment was postponed and a $1 billion credit line was established, but Enron’s shares and bonds continued to decline. If Dynegy withdrew, Enron faced a possible junk-rating downgrade and debt demands across partnerships and off-balance-sheet vehicles.

Enron disclosed that earnings had been overstated, restated results from 1997 onward, reduced reported profits by roughly $591 million to $600 million, and increased debt. The SEC was investigating transactions that moved assets off Enron’s balance sheet and benefited company officials. More than a dozen shareholder suits alleged breaches of fiduciary duty and misleading reporting. Dynegy’s management maintained that Enron’s core trading business remained strong, while analysts questioned whether additional liabilities or accounting problems could emerge.

BusinessWeek’s broader accounting coverage said corporate write-offs were expected to reach a record $125 billion in 2001. It described inconsistent “pro forma” and “operating earnings” measures, large gaps between those figures and GAAP, and concerns that “special charges” could obscure performance or smooth future results. S&P proposed standardized operating-earnings rules, while the FASB and International Accounting Standards Board were also considering the issue.

Other coverage noted slight declines in major volatility indexes, unusually heavy trading in Enron call options, and renewed interest in Eli Lilly puts. Charles Schwab advised investors to diversify and avoid letting fear or greed drive decisions. A profile described former Enron executive Rebecca Mark’s post-Enron advisory and investment activities. Separately, India’s Aditya Birla Group denied pursuing Enron’s 65% stake in the Dabhol power project, although India’s power minister welcomed potential added competition. The compilation also included analysis attributing Enron’s crisis to off-balance-sheet investments, accounting failures, inadequate scrutiny by auditors and analysts, and broader risks in trading practices.

Jamie Dimon said AI is real, transformative and worth using, while rejecting the idea that all AI is a bubble, though he believes some assets and projects may be in “bubble territory.” Drawing on the internet’s early years, he said AI investments should be assessed case by case and will likely pay off overall. He warned that rapid adoption could eliminate jobs too quickly and urged governments, businesses and society to prepare through retraining, alternative income, early retirement and other safeguards.

At JPMorgan, AI is used in fraud prevention, risk, marketing, customer service and legal-document analysis. The bank has invested billions since 2012 and employs more than 2,000 AI staff. Dimon distinguished these targeted applications from generative AI, whose efficiency benefits remain uncertain, saying data preparation should come first and efficiency gains would follow. He recommended employee training, ongoing adaptation, thoughtful regulation and safety nets. Dimon also expressed market caution, including a 30% chance of a stock-market correction.

A WIRED podcast episode examines renewed interest in autonomous delivery robots. DoorDash introduced Dot, a nearly five-foot-tall red robot with nine cameras, seven other sensors, and a Pac-Man-style delivery compartment. Intended for sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes, Dot is part of DoorDash’s proposed “hybrid” delivery model combining human couriers, drones, and autonomous vehicles.

DoorDash is also partnering with Los Angeles-based Coco Robotics, whose smaller sidewalk robots still rely partly on remote operators. Experts say delivery robots remain technically difficult because of uneven sidewalks, pedestrians, bicycles, obstacles, and changing environments. Companies are focusing deployments on controlled settings such as college campuses, while Starship Technologies has pursued university markets. Investment has fluctuated since pandemic-era enthusiasm; Amazon and FedEx reportedly scaled back, though Coco, Serve Robotics, Starship, and DoorDash continue developing the technology.

Dot’s planned use of bike lanes could worsen congestion and raise regulatory questions, especially where bike access is already limited and e-bikes or other devices are restricted. Labor may be reshaped rather than eliminated: robots still require people to load, retrieve, maintain, and handle deliveries, while human couriers remain better suited to stairs, gates, codes, and other access tasks. In China, some hotel deliveries use robots for elevators while couriers complete room deliveries, allowing couriers to serve more customers. A Carnegie Mellon study cited in the episode found that sidewalk robots displaced work onto other workers.

The episode also recommends the JBL Clip 5 Bluetooth speaker, journaling with an unlined notebook, and Google Photos’ Gemini-powered “Ask Photos” editing feature on compatible Android phones.

Jane Goodall’s legacy includes a unique collection of chimpanzee skeletons assembled from Gombe chimps whose sex, age, weight and life histories were known. By retrieving recently deceased animals and using insects to clean the remains, Goodall’s team created opportunities to study how individual development and experience shape skeletons, potentially informing research on ancient hominins. Goodall maintained that the implications remained uncertain—“We just don’t know”—but emphasized that field researchers should not waste anything. The collection revealed complexities such as Flo’s unusually large skeleton despite her lower weight than a smaller male, a bone-loss pattern unlike osteoporosis in human females, and evidence consistent with reproduction shortly before her death near age 50. The skeletons continued producing scientific insights after Goodall shifted from fieldwork to environmental activism and writing.

Gold is forecast to reach a four-year high of $1,400 an ounce by year-end amid U.S.-North Korea tensions, political risks, and strong demand from China and India, said VTB Capital’s Evgeny Ananiev. Gold traded at $1,281.86, up 12 percent this year, as subdued U.S. inflation reduced the prospect of further rate increases. Indian gold imports are projected to rise 30 percent to as much as 800 metric tons in 2017, while Chinese gold-bar demand more than doubled in the first half of the year.

This U.S. continuation application describes multi-camera imaging systems for detecting faint objects in space and other low-light or low-contrast environments using cameras that may be inadequate individually but economical and scalable when combined. Three configurations are disclosed: a common field array, in which cameras share an overlapping field of view; a hybrid array, in which multiple common-field arrays are stitched together for a wider composite view; and an adaptive array, in which cameras detect a target over a broad field and then automatically reposition to focus on it.

A computing system co-registers captured images, aligns common objects or spatial features, and combines corresponding pixel data. Combining N images can increase signal-to-noise ratio by approximately √N, increase effective bit depth by approximately log₂N, and reduce cosmic-ray artifacts. These systems can improve sensitivity, deconvolution capability, scalability, and flexibility while reducing camera, operating, and maintenance costs.

Calibration may include dark-frame, flat-frame, bias-frame, barrel-distortion, and field calibration. Data collection uses star-based pixel mapping and registration, while data reduction can remove stellar backgrounds, detect object streaks using a Hough transform, characterize the streaks, calculate orbital parameters, and compare them with a space-object catalog to identify correlated or uncorrelated targets. Potential applications include astrophotography, deep-space searches, satellite detection and tracking, tactical sensing, and night vision. The invention was made in part with government support, and the government retains certain rights.

University of Washington researchers and partner companies conducted the first large-scale field test of poplar trees inoculated with a probiotic bacterium at a California Superfund site contaminated with trichloroethylene (TCE). Inoculated trees grew larger and healthier than untreated trees, retained high TCE-degrading activity after three years, and contained greatly reduced TCE. Groundwater downstream from the planting site also had lower toxin levels, while increased chloride around the roots indicated TCE degradation. The experiment demonstrates that combining trees’ phytoremediation with selected microbes can improve tree survival and pollutant removal. The approach could enable faster, more effective, sustainable, and potentially less expensive cleanup of TCE-contaminated sites. Results were published in *Environmental Science & Technology* on Aug. 11.

Natural zircon undergoes a pressure-induced transformation to scheelite-structured reidite. The transition pressure varies with temperature and compression conditions, and both martensitic and reconstructive mechanisms have been considered. Static-compression studies showed that reconstructive transformation can occur in crystalline zircon through an intermediate phase. Reidite occurs in meteorites and impact-metamorphic rocks, can persist over geological time, and provides constraints on the minimum pressure experienced by those rocks.

Natural zircon single-crystal plates from Australia were shock-compressed near the [100] direction to maximum pressures of 13.6 and 51.3 GPa. Hydrodynamic calculations, performed without accounting for the phase transition above 30 GPa, estimated pore-free heating of 24°C and 265°C and residual heating of 21°C and 182°C, respectively; temperatures near pores were much higher. Recovered samples were examined by X-ray diffraction, Raman and infrared spectroscopy, cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence, and electron microscopy.

At 13.6 GPa, zircon remained the dominant phase, although it was strongly fractured and locally brecciated. Some fracture-filling material was disoriented, but most fragments retained their original orientation. Red-tinted cathodoluminescent patches near fractures had lower intensity and weak or absent Dy³⁺ peaks, indicating radiation-promoting structural defects. Partial formation of an intermediate high-pressure phase and retrograde transformation could not be excluded.

At 51.3 GPa, the material became predominantly mosaic reidite, with minor residual zircon. Its crystallographic orientation followed the known (112)reidite || (200)zircon relation. Raman, infrared, and X-ray data confirmed reidite, while residual zircon was broadened and shifted by residual lattice stress and occurred preferentially near fractures. Electron microscopy showed strong fracturing, including thin fractures parallel to the shock plane and zircon (001), and contrasting domains attributable to the approximately 9% density difference between reidite and residual zircon.

Cathodoluminescence changed markedly with pressure. The reidite sample was about six times less luminous than the starting zircon, with a blue band near 430 nm and prominent Dy³⁺, Sm³⁺, Pr³⁺, Eu³⁺, Er³⁺, and Tb³⁺ emissions. Dy³⁺ line splitting and intensity changes indicated at least two locally distinct sites. Numerous 2–10 μm yellow luminescent speckles were associated with enhanced rare-earth-element emission and were commonly confined to crystallographic planes.

The authors concluded that shock-induced transformation causes some trace cations, including rare-earth elements, to segregate rapidly onto planar defects, dislocations, and related structures without prolonged annealing. Reconstructive rearrangement of the zircon-to-reidite structure may release substituting ions into interstitial positions, after which rapid transport through vacancies, dislocations, or grain boundaries could produce the observed segregation within tens of seconds. Partial zircon decomposition to ZrO₂ and SiO₂ could not be excluded, although no baddeleyite or orthorhombic ZrO₂ was detected. Zircon and reidite may retain broadly similar isotopic characteristics and trace-element ratios, while transformation-related material flow can partly close fractures formed during shock loading.

This continuation patent application describes improved ladar transmitter systems for computer-vision applications. Ladar combines the resolution of optical sensing with radar-like depth information, but conventional systems are described as costly, large, heavy, power-intensive, and bandwidth-intensive; flash-ladar systems also face high pulse energy, eye-safety, readout noise, low signal-to-noise ratio, and short-range limitations.

The disclosed transmitter architecture includes a laser source, laser optics, a controllable beam scanner, transmission optics, and a receiver that determines range and intensity. Range-point selection and pre-scan compression can reduce bandwidth by directing pulses toward selected points. Scanning mirrors may include dual MEMS mirrors, galvo meters, acousto-optic deflectors, photonic steering devices, phased arrays, or other arrangements.

An optical field splitter/inverter is disclosed to improve gaze on desired portions of a scan area. Resonant scanning is fastest near the field center and slowest at its edges, which can leave insufficient firing time for central points, line skips, or detours. W-shaped reflectors or a triangular-prism assembly can split and invert the field so that slower scanning occurs in the center. Overlapping the split fields can further increase centerline revisits, while hinged mirrors permit real-time adjustment of overlap and field of view.

The application also describes Lissajous scanning using sinusoidal motion on two axes. Standard patterns produce larger gaps and fewer revisits near the center than at the edges. Induced periodic phase drift, generated by slightly varying a mirror’s phase off resonance, can redirect gaps and increase dwell in selected gaze regions. A total-least-squares process using singular-value decomposition selects drift parameters in real time to reduce or eliminate gaps without sacrificing pattern periodicity.

Finally, an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector reimaging assembly is disclosed for compact two-mirror scanners. Placing scan mirrors at the ellipsoid’s foci and positioning a reflector between them reimages the beam spot onto the second mirror, permitting smaller, similarly sized mirrors. A specified coplanar angle keeps the reflected ray fan planar and limits scan-field distortion, while an optional first-mirror tilt provides additional design flexibility.

The White House blocked congressional funding for a federal inspectors general oversight office, effectively closing it after Tuesday. Republican senators condemned the move and called for its reversal.

Short Tata Steel at 575 (stop 580, target 567) and Ambuja Cements at 231 (stop 233, target 226); long PowerGrid at 194 (stop 192, target 196). Nifty may reach 10,000–10,250; Bank Nifty 24,000–24,650 amid possible short-covering.

A June 2001 email circulated reports on California’s electricity crisis, driven by high demand, transmission constraints, scarce hydropower, aging plants, high wholesale prices and a flawed deregulated market. PG&E and Southern California Edison accumulated nearly $14 billion in unrecoverable power costs, leading to PG&E’s bankruptcy and state purchases of electricity for utilities and consumers. Plant restarts and conservation reduced demand, but experts said generation remained insufficient and summer blackouts likely.

Political debate centered on federal price limits versus increased supply and market-based pricing. Economists argued that cost-based caps could restrain prices in an uncompetitive market, while the Bush administration favored production increases. A poll found 56% favored wholesale price limits. Davis and Bush each blamed the other and energy interests, with critics saying partisan stereotypes obscured the crisis.

State investigators sought pricing and bidding records from eight out-of-state generators, including Enron, and from state agencies. FERC was criticized for inadequate staffing, data gathering and market oversight. Separate reports examined possible natural-gas market manipulation, pipeline and storage constraints, Chevron’s threat to reduce refinery output, PG&E’s executive bonuses and reimbursement lawsuit, utility rate proposals, Calpine’s city deal, and Edison’s shareholder lobbying campaign. New power contracts and generating-unit restorations were announced, including a 430-megawatt GWF agreement with the state.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 27, 2021, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2021. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” or incorporated by reference except by specific reference. The filing was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

NASA researchers developed a theoretical plan called the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) to deflect threatening asteroids. Their work focuses on Bennu, which has a small chance of striking Earth on September 22, 2135, with odds estimated at 1 in 2,700. Possible methods include using a nearly nine-tonne impactor or a nuclear device. Although Bennu is not large enough to cause dinosaur-like extinction, NASA hopes the design studies will improve preparations for future threats. Bennu’s well-observed characteristics make it useful for testing mitigation calculations. NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft is en route to map the asteroid, determine its composition and collect a sample for return to Earth. A later, more powerful craft could be sent if Bennu becomes a greater threat.

The Motley Fool Money highlights the Citi Simplicity Card as a top pick for paying off credit card debt, citing a 21-month 0% introductory APR on balance transfers and 0% intro APR on purchases for 12 months. The card has no annual fee, late fees, or penalty APR. Afterward, the variable APR is 17.99%–28.74%, based on creditworthiness. Balance transfers must occur within four months of account opening, with fees of 3% (minimum $5) during the first four months and 5% (minimum $5) afterward. It also offers flexible payment dates. The recommended credit score is Good/Excellent (670–850), though approval is not guaranteed. Citi is an advertising partner of Motley Fool Money, which states that compensation does not influence its product ratings.

Party-list Rep. Lito Atienza filed House Bill 4758 to replace the MMDA with a Metropolitan Manila government led by an elected governor. He argued that the MMDA’s appointed-chairman structure lacks accountability and has failed to address congestion, flooding, peace and order, and garbage problems. Atienza also cited elected governors in New York and Tokyo as models.

The proposed government would include an elected governor, vice governor, and Metro Manila Council. The governor and vice governor would be elected by residents, while council members would be elected from each congressional district covering Metro Manila’s 16 cities and the town of Pateros.

Manchester City beat Burnley 2-1 at the Etihad despite Fernandinho’s first-half red card. Gael Clichy scored before substitute Sergio Agüero added the winner from a tight angle; Ben Mee hit the bar and Burnley failed to equalize. The victory moved City third and within two points of Liverpool, renewing their title hopes. Fernandinho received a four-match ban, while Agüero’s impact prompted calls for his immediate recall.

Eric Fung, a 37-year-old American entrepreneur and CEO of Colega AI, left Silicon Valley and moved to Tokyo with his wife, Shana, to found the US-registered startup. The remote-first company has seven staff, including three in Tokyo and others across Asia. Fung previously worked in advertising and startups, co-founded a company that exited during the pandemic, and operated three California restaurants. He chose Japan partly for its safety, cleanliness, energy, lower costs, and large base of small businesses, which he saw as a promising market for his AI business. Although he does not speak Japanese, he partnered with a local contact to navigate business relationships. He also describes challenges adapting to long working hours, seniority hierarchies, language barriers, and slower friendship formation while maintaining a flexible startup culture. He and his wife rent a 500-square-foot studio near Shibuya for about $1,350 a month, compared with roughly $3,000 for a similar San Francisco space.

Newspaper clippings dated Dec. 31, 2001, focus on Enron’s Chapter 11 collapse and its effects on investors, regulators, creditors, employees, and the energy market. Enron’s stock fell 99%, while the SEC and Congress began investigations. SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt assigned investigators to Enron’s books but could face a conflict because his former law firm represented Arthur Andersen, Enron’s auditor. Credit Suisse First Boston briefly joined and then left Enron’s unsecured creditors committee, citing the time commitment and its relatively limited exposure. American Electric Power separately acquired Enron Wind’s 160-megawatt Indian Mesa project for $175 million.

Several reports examined why corporate distress was often overlooked. Enron and Nortel expanded aggressively to meet unrealistic analyst expectations, sometimes manipulating information when results fell short. Analysts urged managers to resist earnings guidance, disclose segment budgets and value drivers, report auditable metrics, and state when their stock is overvalued. Articles also argued that unusual write-offs can reveal future problems rather than safely being dismissed as one-time events. Bethlehem Steel’s deferred-tax write-off preceded bankruptcy; At Home’s large goodwill write-down foreshadowed its collapse; and charges at Lucent and Providian exposed weakening business conditions. Among S&P 500 companies, unusual charges exceeded $165 billion during 2001, and firms with the largest charges relative to sales subsequently performed worse than firms with minimal charges.

Suggested early-warning signs of bankruptcy included widening credit-default-swap spreads, falling bond prices, withdrawal of credit lines, covenant violations, large upcoming interest payments, and the hiring of bankruptcy counsel or restructuring advisers. Enron’s credit-default-swap spreads rose sharply well before its stock price fully reflected the danger. Separately, a report concluded that bandwidth trading had effectively collapsed after Enron because fiber capacity was abundant, prices were low, Internet growth was slower than expected, and some trading had been largely financial maneuvering.

Other coverage addressed broader financial and economic concerns. A Vanguard survey of 500 401(k) participants found muted near-term stock-return expectations but unrealistic long-term forecasts; many participants also underestimated the risk of holding employer stock. California’s regulator said the state’s 1996 electricity deregulation plan lacked safeguards and that litigation delayed its market-manipulation investigation. Meanwhile, power producers including Mirant, NRG Energy, and Dynegy cut or delayed projects because of lower prices and investor concerns, raising the possibility of tighter electricity supply as the economy recovered, though transmission constraints were viewed as a greater immediate risk.

Polaroid sought bankruptcy-court approval for retention bonuses worth as much as $1.7 million for its chief executive and payments to 45 senior executives, prompting anger from former workers and retirees who lost benefits. A commentary argued that University of California managers should have sold their Enron holdings and advocated broad index funds, tighter loss-cutting discipline, and compensation for Enron employees who lost retirement savings.

A year-end stock-awards column noted Enron and Providian as major losers, real-estate trusts entering the S&P 500, asbestos-related bankruptcies, resilient retailers and security-software companies, and strong gains by video-rental chains.

The Consumer Mortgage Coalition asked Treasury to let qualified mortgage lenders use the Health and Human Services’ National Directory of New Hires to verify applicants’ income, citing problems with the IRS’s IVES system that could delay spring closings. The proposal requires consumer consent and encrypted transmission to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; the group also urged Congress to fund upgrades to IVES.

The passage explains that variable APRs generally track the prime rate, while fixed APRs remain relatively stable and require advance notice before changes. It says issuers commonly offer 6- or 21-month introductory periods at 0%–3.99%, after which the regular APR may apply.
