ESPN: Cubs' 'Korean corn dog' tops 2025 ballpark grub; Bananas selection show Oct. 9 on ESPN2; Smith urges Yankees momentum; ESPN BET gambling disclaimers.

Sirius XM has roughly 4.3% fixed-rate debt, 11–12% ROIC, and a 6% WACC. Satellite spending cuts are expected to increase free cash flow by about 20% by 2026, while share retirements could improve per-share value and ROIC. At about 7.6× EV/EBITDA versus a historical 15×, an unlevered DCF suggests 2–3× upside. The author discloses a beneficial long position.

The passage details NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture, centered on the GA102 GPU, and its improvements over Turing across graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, storage, and video workloads.

Second-generation RT Cores deliver up to twice the ray-tracing performance of Turing RT Cores by doubling ray/triangle intersection testing and supporting concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads. Each SM can run two compute workloads simultaneously, including denoising alongside ray tracing. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur involving moving or deforming geometry, enabling rendering up to eight times faster than Turing; one measured Blender Cycles comparison showed up to a fivefold gain.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and a Sparsity feature based on a 2-out-of-4 nonzero weight pattern. Sparsity doubles Tensor Core throughput and reduces weight storage and bandwidth requirements by half. TF32 provides up to five times the prior-generation training throughput without code changes. The cores accelerate applications including DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, Canvas, and NGX services. Enhanced DLSS supports 8K output through 9x scaling, enabling 60 fps 8K ray-traced gaming in many titles on the RTX 3090.

The GA10x SM provides 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, four texture units, and a unified 128 KB L1 cache/shared-memory subsystem. Its dual datapaths can execute 32 FP32 operations per clock per partition, doubling Turing’s aggregate FP32 rate, or 32 FP32 and 32 INT32 operations. L1 capacity is 33% larger than Turing, while shared-memory bandwidth doubles. Full GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Moving ROPs into each GPC improves raster throughput, multisample anti-aliasing, fill rate, and blending.

The architecture supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding. Speeds reach 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth reaches 936 GB/sec on the RTX 3090. The RTX 3080 uses a 320-bit interface and has 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. Professional RTX A6000 and A40 GPUs each provide 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96 GB through third-generation NVLink. PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth over PCIe Gen 3, supporting up to 64 GB/sec on a x16 slot. Ampere GPUs are described as up to 1.9 times more power efficient than Turing at equivalent performance.

GA10x GDDR6X also adds Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed memory transactions and retries them until successful. Performance plateauing under memory overclocking indicates the memory limit, although continued overclocking can still cause crashes.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based lossless decompression and Microsoft DirectStorage to accelerate asset loading and streaming, claiming up to 100 times the throughput of hard drives and traditional storage APIs. It offloads work that could consume dozens of CPU cores, enables near-instantaneous loading, reduces stutter and object pop-in, and supports compressed data and high-quality texture streaming.

The RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X, and is reported as 1.5 times faster than TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, retains most GA10x features except NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

For data centers, the A40 provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI-training throughput of Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB expandable to 96 GB, PCIe Gen 4, display outputs, virtualization support, and compatibility with NVIDIA EGX. The RTX A6000 targets professional workstations with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB with NVLink.

GA10x supports 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz, including two 8K displays through separate DisplayPort 1.4a connections. It supports HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth and Display Stream Compression. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 AV1 playback at low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC while substantially reducing CPU utilization.

An analysis of the 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic found that about 3% of patients were superspreaders responsible for roughly 61% of infections, with each patient infecting 2.39 others on average. Transmission was limited after patients reached hospitals, while delayed recognition, limited access or fear of care, and traditional funeral handling of infectious bodies fueled spread. Close caregiving involving very young or very old patients also increased superspreading risk. The epidemic was stopped through public health efforts focused on safe burials and rapid hospitalization, and researchers said identifying high-risk behaviors and demographics could improve future epidemic control.

The global automated fare collection (AFC) system market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024, with a 13.3% CAGR from 2017 to 2024. AFC automates public-transport ticketing, supports integrated and contactless payment across transit modes, reduces queues and errors, and improves transaction efficiency and security. Growth drivers include technology adoption, new AFC applications, and government investment, while low awareness and limited smart-card use are restraints. The market is segmented by component, application, technology platform, and geography. Key players include Advanced Card Systems, Atos, Cubic Transportation Systems, LG CNS, NXP Semiconductors, Omron, Samsung SDS, Scheidt & Bachmann, Thales, and LECIP Group.

Subject to TSX-V approval, Bayhorse Silver increased its non-brokered private placement to 3 million units at C$0.10 each, for gross proceeds of C$300,000. Each unit includes one common share and a half-warrant exercisable at C$0.15 for 24 months. Existing shareholders may participate; funds will fund mine equipment, working capital and general costs.

Massachusetts’s House and Senate passed a supplemental budget bill allocating $15 million to districts serving students who fled Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. Aid would follow the existing enrollment-based formula. More than 2,300 students have arrived since September, and minor legislative differences remain to be negotiated before the bill reaches Baker’s desk.

The author recounts passing the online “Jeopardy!” contestant test and reflects on the unresolved scientific search for how learning and memory are stored in the brain. Research supports both localized and distributed memory models, while experiments in snails and planarians suggest RNA may transfer memories, though results remain unsettled. The author also describes failed attempts to replicate James McConnell’s flatworm experiments and jokes that a future “Jeopardy!” opponent’s recall might warrant an RNA drug test.

The patent application, a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 17/051,195, describes non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) transmissions and small-data transmission in new radio (NR). In LTE, conventional small-data transmission requires establishing and releasing an RRC connection, creating signaling overhead. Control-plane approaches can carry small data in NAS messages, while user-plane approaches preserve RRC and security contexts to resume a suspended connection. The application also discusses LTE downlink multi-user superposition transmission and its potential capacity, throughput, and cell-edge benefits.

The disclosed NR techniques allow a user equipment (UE) in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE state to transmit small uplink data while reducing state-transition overhead, latency, and power consumption. A gNB may configure contention-based physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) resources as a configured-grant PUSCH and broadcast their configuration through remaining system information or other system information. The broadcast information may include demodulation reference signal (DMRS) ports, multiple-access signatures, interleavers, and other NOMA parameters. If no NOMA parameters are specified, orthogonal multiple access may be used.

For RRC-IDLE operation, a UE may send small data through a configured grant, either by briefly transitioning to RRC-connected state or by first performing random access and contention resolution. The data may be carried with or without a NAS PDU and forwarded through the AMF for authentication and delivery to a gateway. Payload headers may contain a UE identity, a small-data indicator, and a last-packet indicator. The last-packet indicator can indicate that no further uplink data, or only limited subsequent downlink data, is expected. An IdleStateConfiguredGrantData message may contain UE identity, small-data indicator, last-packet indicator, and data.

The application describes UE-specific reference bits generated from a UE-specific identity and, optionally, a multiple-access identity. Reference bits may use low-correlation M-sequences, Gold sequences, or sparse sequences and may be jointly encoded with information bits using a systematic LDPC encoder. The resulting codeword contains the known reference bits and information-plus-parity bits. Reference bits may be separated and reused as a preamble or DMRS, while information and parity bits undergo UE-specific interleaving, rate matching, modulation, optional spreading, and resource-element mapping. Front-loaded preamble or DMRS symbols may support UE activity detection and channel estimation; detecting the UE-specific sequence may also assist data decoding.

Configured-grant resources may be specified through time-domain and frequency-domain allocations, transmission periodicity, DMRS configuration, cyclic-prefix settings, guard bands, and NOMA signatures. Multiple grants with different periodicities or payload capacities may be configured, with resource selection based on message size. Guard bands, extended cyclic prefixes, zero-padding periods, and sparse subcarrier activation can mitigate inter-carrier and inter-symbol interference in asynchronous transmissions. DMRS ports may be mapped to multiple-access signatures to reduce collisions and support activity detection and decoding.

Grant-free or configured-grant PUSCH data may be processed using CRC attachment followed by LDPC or Polar encoding, cell- or UE-specific interleaving, rate matching, QPSK or higher-order modulation, optional superposition coding, spreading, and resource mapping. A preamble may be multiplexed with configured-grant PUSCH through time, frequency, or combined division multiplexing. A UE may monitor a response window for downlink control information identified by a configured-grant RNTI, decode a response PDSCH, or treat an absent or invalid response as a negative acknowledgment and prepare retransmission.

In RRC-INACTIVE state, stored AS security and RRC context may allow a UE to transmit small data immediately through a configured grant without necessarily entering RRC-connected state. Such transmission may combine the data with the UE’s I-RNTI, logical-channel group, and buffer-status report; small-data and last-packet indicators may be unnecessary because a buffer-status report is available. An InactiveStateConfiguredGrantData message may contain I-RNTI, a requested cause such as RRCConnectionResume, and the data unit. Timing re-alignment may be required if the time-alignment timer has expired. UE-specific DMRS ports and multiple-access signatures may be assigned in the inactive state to avoid collisions, and a negative acknowledgment may cause the network to direct the UE to RRC-connected state for retransmission.

Random-access preamble collisions may congest PRACH and delay the four-step procedure. NOMA may be applied to the PUSCH transmission so colliding UEs can use different multiple-access signatures, reducing collision effects and improving detection. The random-access response may provide DMRS and multiple-access information or enable NOMA through downlink control signaling. PUSCH transform precoding and subcarrier spacing may be controlled by RRC parameters.

The application also describes DRX paging in RRC-IDLE and RRC-INACTIVE states, including paging occasions, P-RNTI monitoring, and use of paging DCI to activate or deactivate type-2 configured grants. An asynchronous NOMA scheme based on OFDM index modulation may use sparse subcarrier activation patterns and k-sparse codebook columns as multiple-access signatures.

The disclosure provides embodiments in communications systems comprising UEs or other wireless devices, base stations, remote radio heads, transmission and reception points, roadside units, radio access networks, core networks, and other network elements. It also describes display interfaces capable of presenting flows, state transitions, message progress, device topology, or other information associated with the disclosed small-data and NOMA methods.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill approved recommendations allowing people 6 months and older to receive an updated Covid-19 vaccine after discussing risks and benefits with a provider. Insurance coverage remains, but the recommendations do not clarify prescription requirements. O’Neill also approved separate MMR and chickenpox shots for children under 4, replacing the combined vaccine. His sign-off enables states to order updated Covid vaccines through the Vaccines for Children program; a delay had left roughly half of participating U.S. children without access. A revised childhood vaccine schedule was also expected.

The Tax Court granted summary judgment for the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, upholding the decision to proceed with levy collection for unpaid 1994 and 1996 federal income taxes. Robert Eugene Poindexter, a songwriter, requested a collection due process hearing, claiming his returns were inaccurate because of disputed royalties from record companies. The Appeals officer concluded that the underlying tax liabilities were not properly at issue because Poindexter had reported them on his returns and declined to file amended returns.

The court rejected the Commissioner’s argument that a taxpayer may challenge a self-reported liability only when the Commissioner asserts a different amount. Poindexter was entitled to challenge the existence or amount of his liabilities because he had received no deficiency notice or other opportunity to dispute them. However, his petition failed to comply with Tax Court Rule 331 because it did not identify the specific income, deductions, credits, or computations he disputed. He also provided no evidence establishing the royalties owed, copyright violations, or any authority for the IRS to subpoena record companies. His other claims concerning assessment procedures and levy execution were unsupported, and no levies had yet occurred.

Agent Mutual, owner of OnTheMarket.com, plans to float on London’s AIM and raise £50 million to compete with Rightmove and Zoopla. The UK’s third-largest property portal will invest in marketing, sales, customer relations and technology, including a major TV, digital and print campaign. Following the abandonment of its mutual status, the company signed long-term listing agreements with estate agents and property service firms. CEO Ian Springett said the flotation would strengthen its market position. Analyst George Salmon acknowledged the logic of scaling up but said OnTheMarket remained far behind its rivals. The portal also won a case supporting its rule that agents listing with it can use only one of Rightmove or Zoopla.

A father was allegedly spat at, punched and kicked by two men while walking with his children in Coed Bach Park, Pontarddulais, Swansea, on 29 June. Police said the attack followed his challenge to an erratic moped rider and appealed for witnesses.

The appeal concerned whether Pelitsie substantially complied with burglary policies requiring insured records sufficient for the insurers to accurately determine the amount of loss. Pelitsie maintained a cash fund for cashing customers’ payroll checks and recorded the combined total of cash and checks on a scratch pad. Before the February 10, 1954 burglary, he had recorded $2,922, but did not separately identify the cash and checks or document individual checks. Testimony conflicted over what notation remained after the claims adjuster visited. The jury awarded $2,740, reflecting recovery of $182 on two checks whose details Pelitsie remembered.

The court stated that recordkeeping clauses require reasonable, substantial compliance, but records must permit determination of the loss with reasonable accuracy without supplying essential facts from an interested party’s memory. Because the stolen fund included negotiable payroll checks as well as cash, adequate records needed to identify each check and provide information permitting claims against its drawer, such as the drawer’s name and either the payee’s name or check number. Pelitsie’s records did not meet that standard, and his recovery of two checks through memory demonstrated the deficiency. The court therefore held that the recordkeeping condition precedent had been breached, reversed the judgment, and remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the Tax Court’s judgment that Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Co. was liable for federal income tax deficiencies for 1975 and 1976. The Delaware corporation manufactured jewelry in American Samoa and excluded sales proceeds paid by its Hawaii parent under 26 U.S.C. § 931(a). The court held that § 931(b) nevertheless required the proceeds to be included in gross income because the parent’s checks were deposited into the taxpayer’s bank account in Honolulu, where the taxpayer obtained custody and control of the funds. Giving “received” its ordinary meaning, the court treated the place of physical receipt as controlling. It rejected the taxpayer’s argument that receipt should be determined by the corporation’s primary physical presence, as that interpretation would largely nullify § 931(b).

This work evaluates global variance reduction techniques (VRTs) and population control techniques (PCTs) for time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations. It reviews implicit capture, weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper–Larsen methods, as well as uniform and weight-based combing, and examines their interactions in the Shift and MC/DC codes.

In a pulsed slab problem using Shift, FW-CADIS achieved the best figure of merit among the tested VRTs, though its deterministic-solve costs limited the overall improvement. Static weight windows and always-active weight-based combing were identified as possible limitations.

For the supercritical AZURV1 benchmark using MC/DC, Cooper–Larsen weight windows with uniform combing substantially improved efficiency, and time-dependent weight windows performed better than static windows. Combining Cooper–Larsen windows with weight-based combing exhausted available memory because combing reset particle weights, causing excessive splitting at the pulse edge. Implicit capture provided no efficiency improvement in the supercritical case and interacted poorly with uniform combing.

In the 1D SCRAM problem, uniform combing was important for controlling particle populations, memory, and runtime. Cooper–Larsen windows with uniform combing performed best, while weight-based combing again failed with Cooper–Larsen windows because of excessive splitting, and implicit capture underperformed with uniform combing.

The results show that suitable combinations of VRTs and PCTs can make time-dependent simulations substantially more efficient, whereas incompatible combinations can reduce performance or exhaust memory. Time-dependent adaptations of steady-state VRTs were identified as promising for future large-scale parallel simulations.

The article argues that language education should foreground its essential purpose: connecting people with languages, cultures, and communities. This focus is especially important as low enrollment has led to language programs being reduced or eliminated, particularly in German and French. Educators can make language learning more meaningful and support recruitment, retention, and program survival by fostering “imagined communities”—groups connected through imagination rather than direct contact.

The proposed approach uses task-based instruction, with meaningful, authentic scenarios serving as the vehicle for imagined communities. Teachers must intentionally develop scenarios aligned with curriculum, activities, assignments, and assessments; provide authentic materials, just-in-time instruction, and scaffolding; and give students autonomy to connect personally with the tasks. Examples include planning a move to a target-language-speaking city, searching for and furnishing an apartment, navigating transportation, buying groceries, researching restaurants, applying for jobs, and planning study abroad.

A yearlong study in two eighth-grade German classrooms found positive results, including deeper study of language and culture, increased feelings of connection and membership, continued language study beyond required years, and sustained student interest. For sustainability, instructors should document and revise materials, collaborate with colleagues, and continually adjust activities to students’ needs. The article concludes that imagined-communities-based learning can be implemented across educational levels, contexts, and languages.

- A May 3, 2001 news compilation reported that Pompano Beach officials scheduled a public meeting on Enron’s proposed power plant before the City Commission’s zoning-variance vote.

- California lawmakers considered giving the state authority to refuse electricity purchases above specified prices during shortages. Supporters argued that a buying boycott could weaken wholesale power suppliers, while economists and business representatives warned that prolonged blackouts could cost far more than high electricity prices. California had spent $5.7 billion buying power in three and a half months, and spending was reaching $90 million per day. Economists estimated that statewide blackouts could reduce economic output by $2 billion to $16 billion.

- Enron’s Indian unit, Dabhol Power Co., remained in a dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over power prices and unpaid bills. MSEB owed about $48 million, while DPC’s board had authorized management to halt power sales if the dispute was unresolved. Indian lenders asked the government to intervene. DPC agreed to meet a state renegotiation panel, but said the meeting would not constitute an offer to revise the contract; the first meeting was postponed to May 11.

- The Democratic National Committee criticized the Bush administration’s energy policy as favoring oil and gas interests over conservation, citing campaign contributions, industry representation on transition teams, proposed drilling, regulatory rollbacks, and the administration’s response to California’s electricity crisis. The release identified Enron as a major Bush campaign contributor.

- British utility Innogy began wholesale electricity trading between France and Italy and was preparing to enter Germany. It planned to expand its continental trading team and focus on trading services rather than acquiring physical energy assets. France had become a more important market than expected because of access to the UK-France undersea interconnector.

- Mosaic Group reported first-quarter revenue of $171.8 million, up 89% from a year earlier and marking its 18th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. Its Paradigm unit expanded a customer-acquisition contract with Enron-created New Power and secured new business worth an estimated $20 million to $25 million annually.

- European telecommunications companies’ debt outlook improved as asset sales and planned equity offerings reduced concerns about repayment. Spreads on bonds and bankruptcy swaps for British Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, Royal KPN, France Telecom and Telecom Italia declined, although British Telecom’s credit ratings remained under review.

- European corporations were increasingly using credit derivatives to hedge debtor default and country risk. Siemens Financial Services used credit default swaps to manage receivables, while market participants expected corporate use to grow. They cited flexibility and lower costs, but noted documentation, complexity, limited experience and court disputes as obstacles.

- Allegheny Energy completed its purchase of 1,710 megawatts of natural-gas-fired generation from Enron North America in Tennessee, Indiana and Illinois. The transaction was financed with debt and equity, including more than 14 million Allegheny shares, and increased Allegheny’s planned generation fleet to more than 14,000 megawatts by 2005.

- Salomon Smith Barney cut its U.S. power-profit forecast for 2002 and beyond, expecting electricity prices to fall faster than natural-gas prices. It projected a 2003 natural-gas generation margin of $3.98 per megawatt-hour, down from $8.73 previously, and expected energy-trading companies such as Enron to benefit from greater trading volume and volatility outside the summer.

- Fitch affirmed Northern Border Partners’ BBB+ senior-debt rating and Northern Border Pipeline’s A- rating, changing both outlooks to stable after reviewing acquisitions, financing plans and operating strategies. Enron held a 10% economic stake in Northern Border Partners and controlled 82.5% of its management committee allocation.

- EnergieKontor signed a framework agreement with Enron Wind for 200 megawatts of 1.5-megawatt turbines for projects in Germany and Spain. It also began exclusive negotiations for as many as 15 wind farms totaling 700 megawatts in Spain’s Castilla-La Mancha region.

- Scottish Power reported lower fiscal-year pretax profit and adjusted earnings and sought to restructure into three divisions focused on generation, supply and infrastructure, with expansion in the United States. It was considering selling Southern Water but remained supportive of its loss-making Thus telecom stake, contributing to investor concerns about strategic focus.

The National Endowment for the Humanities and First Nations Development Institute will each contribute about $2 million to tribal Native-language education, funding about 15 programs yearly. Funding will be competitive, with preference for successful immersion programs and language-retention or restoration efforts.

Rep. Garret Graves said the shooting of Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise and three others by Bernie Sanders supporter James T. Hodgkinson reflects a divisive political climate and that rhetoric has consequences, while blaming misinformation and sensationalism in part. Scalise remains in critical condition; police have not stated a motive, though the shooter’s anti-Republican views and Sanders campaign volunteering prompted suggestions of political motivation. Sanders condemned the attack and violence. Some Republicans cited heightened threats and backlash against President Trump, while Trump urged unity and peace.

The application is a continuation of prior applications and patents involving cannabinoid biosynthesis. The invention was made with National Science Foundation support under Grants 1330914 and 1442724, and an XML sequence listing, B16-072-8SeqList, is incorporated by reference.

The disclosure provides methods, polypeptides, encoding nucleic acids, vectors, and genetically modified host cells for producing cannabinoids, cannabinoid precursors, cannabinoid derivatives, and cannabinoid precursor derivatives in vivo or in cell-free systems. Biosynthetic pathways use TKS and OAC polypeptides to form olivetolic acid or derivatives, GOT polypeptides to produce cannabigerolic acid from geranyl pyrophosphate (GPP) and olivetolic acid, and THCA or CBDA synthases to generate additional cannabinoids.

New GOT polypeptides, including full-length CsPT4 and truncated CsPT4t, were identified and characterized. CsPT4 has SEQ ID NO:110, while CsPT4t lacks N-terminal amino acids 1–76 and has SEQ ID NO:100. These polypeptides reportedly catalyze CBGA production at least tenfold more than CsPT1 (SEQ ID NO:82), can be readily reconstituted in genetically modified hosts, and exhibit broad substrate specificity. Other truncations of CsPT4 lacking 112 or more N-terminal residues lacked detectable CBGA-producing activity. Corresponding nucleic acid sequences, conservatively substituted variants, sequence-identity ranges, hybridizing nucleic acids, cDNA, and expression vectors are also described.

Host cells may express enzymes from the mevalonate or DXP pathways to generate GPP and enzymes that generate hexanoyl-CoA, acyl-CoA compounds, malonyl-CoA, or acetoacetyl-CoA. Suitable hosts include eukaryotic cells, including plant cells and Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and prokaryotic cells. Heterologous nucleic acids may be chromosomally integrated, maintained extrachromosomally, or combined in expression vectors with inducible or constitutive promoters.

Methods involve culturing modified cells and recovering cannabinoids or derivatives, optionally using media containing carboxylic acids, olivetolic acid or its derivatives, fermentable sugars, cellulosic feedstock, or non-fermentable carbon sources such as ethanol. These pathways are presented as enabling rapid microbial production of naturally occurring and non-naturally occurring cannabinoids with defined stereochemistry. Figures depict pathway schemes, expression constructs for numerous engineered strains, and LC-MS evidence for CBGA, THCA, and CBDA production.

An Ilorin Magistrates’ Court remanded Shehu Abubakar and Abdulkareem Maikudi, accused of killing colleague Musa Kareem after a dispute over a cell phone. They face conspiracy and culpable homicide charges. Bail was opposed because the alleged offence was capital, and the accused were remanded to Okekura Prisons pending further investigation, with the case adjourned to July 12.

The speaker felt energized throughout the game, crediting the team’s four scoring lines for stepping up when one struggles. Both teams played aggressive penalty killing, including blocking shots, while the rink was hot and chippy. After emphasizing composure and finding openings, the speaker took a shot from the right side through an open lane created by Sergei.

A New York Times survey found broad dissatisfaction among federal judges with the Supreme Court’s use of emergency dockets since President Trump returned to office. Of 65 respondents, 12 said the Court used emergency orders appropriately, while 47 disagreed and six were neutral. Twelve said lower courts received sufficient guidance, compared with 48 who disagreed and five neutral. Of 54 judges addressing public perception, 42 said emergency orders harmed it, 10 saw no effect, and two saw improvement. Some judges described the orders as opaque, demoralizing and damaging to district courts; one Trump appointee said they exposed anti-democratic rulings. The orders have largely benefited the Trump administration and have enabled major policy actions, though some lacked explanations. The Times cautioned that respondents may not represent the judiciary, while the Volokh Conspiracy criticized possible response and sampling biases.

The Jan. 15, 2002, Energy Central Direct daily edition compiles 75 selected articles, with Enron’s collapse and aftermath dominating coverage. Reports include calls involving Enron Chairman Ken Lay, UBS sharing profits from its acquisition of Enron’s trading unit, a planned Feb. 12 Senate hearing, document-destruction allegations involving Arthur Andersen, political contributions, worker losses, a New York bankruptcy trial, Texas Attorney General recusal, and Enron’s effects on creditors and customers in the United States, Britain, and Spain.

Other stories cover imminent U.S. approval of National Grid’s $3 billion NiMo acquisition, the possible end of new U.S. utility stranded-cost bonds, California regulatory and bankruptcy disputes, electricity deregulation and customer switching, merger activity, power contracts, weather-driven prices and outages. Additional coverage addresses Australian retail competition, nuclear safety and Yucca Mountain, wind and solar investment, environmental policy, emissions trading, and international electricity markets. The edition also lists top utility stock gainers and most-requested stories.

Nigeria launched its National Cancer Control Plan 2018–2022 to improve access to affordable, equitable cancer diagnostics, treatment, and medicines. At the Abuja launch, Health Minister Isaac Adewole highlighted BVGH’s Access Accelerated Initiative (AAI), which works with Nigerian hospitals to coordinate drugs, technologies, and training. Led by BVGH with AORTIC, IFPMA/Access Accelerated, Pfizer, and Takeda, AAI seeks to expand access to cancer medicines and technologies, strengthen healthcare infrastructure, and build clinical and research capacity across Africa. Its first phase includes Nigeria, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, and Rwanda. BVGH has assessed eight Nigerian hospitals and is conducting eight more to identify patient needs, staffing, capacity, and medication-access gaps. Future work will follow the NCCP and assessment findings, with potential participation by additional pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and the AC 3 T clinical trials program.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 reported net sales of $70.0 billion, up 24% from $56.6 billion in Q3 2018. Product sales were $39.7 billion and service sales were $30.3 billion. Operating income declined to $3.2 billion from $3.7 billion, while net income fell to $2.1 billion from $2.9 billion and diluted earnings per share fell to $4.23 from $5.75. For the nine months, net sales rose 20% to $193.1 billion, operating income increased to $10.7 billion from $8.6 billion, net income rose to $8.3 billion from $7.0 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased to $16.53 from $14.10.

Q3 segment results were: North America sales of $42.6 billion and operating income of $1.3 billion; International sales of $18.3 billion and an operating loss of $386 million; and AWS sales of $9.0 billion and operating income of $2.3 billion. Sales growth reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller sales, inventory availability and selection in North America and International, and greater customer usage in AWS. North American operating income was pressured by higher shipping and marketing costs, International’s loss was affected by marketing spending, and AWS productivity gains were partly offset by price reductions and infrastructure and payroll investment.

Q3 operating cash flow was $7.9 billion, compared with $8.6 billion a year earlier; nine-month operating cash flow was $18.9 billion, compared with $14.2 billion. Nine-month investing cash outflow increased to $20.7 billion, and financing cash outflow was $6.5 billion. At September 30, 2019, cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities totaled $43.4 billion at fair value. Total assets were $199.1 billion and stockholders’ equity was $56.5 billion. Management stated that operating cash flows, liquid balances and borrowing arrangements were expected to meet operating cash needs for at least the next 12 months.

Amazon adopted new lease accounting in January 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities without retrospectively adjusting prior periods. New film-cost guidance resulted in $631 million of incremental capitalized production costs during the first nine months of 2019. Present-value lease liabilities totaled $49.3 billion, and contractual commitments totaled $137.3 billion. Face-value debt was $25.4 billion, including $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes; $603 million was outstanding under the secured Credit Facility, while no amounts were outstanding under the commercial paper program or the $7.0 billion Credit Agreement. Amazon made no stock repurchases in the first nine months of 2018 or 2019.

The filing also disclosed approximately $3.8 billion of tax contingencies and various legal matters, including transfer-pricing proceedings, a European Commission state-aid decision, an appealed South Carolina sales-tax assessment and an ongoing review of sanctions-related orders. It identified inventory valuation and income taxes as critical accounting judgments and cautioned that forward-looking results were inherently uncertain.

The court affirmed the denial of unemployment insurance benefits, finding substantial evidence that the warehouse worker resigned in lieu of discharge for misconduct after pulling a box cutter on his supervisor.

President Trump’s criticism of FBI raids on attorney Michael Cohen’s home and office, followed by his full pardon of Scooter Libby, intensified debate over presidential pardon power. Libby was convicted of perjury and obstruction of justice. Critics argued the pardon signaled support for Trump associates targeted by Special Counsel Robert Mueller; the White House denied this and said the pardon corrected an injustice, but did not rule out a future pardon for Cohen.

Legal experts agree presidents have broad pardon authority but disagree over whether self-serving or corrupt motives invalidate pardons, whether public interest is required, and whether a president may pardon himself. Pardons do not protect a president from impeachment. Historical precedents include George H.W. Bush’s pardon of Caspar Weinberger during Iran-Contra and Bill Clinton’s pardon of Marc Rich after donations to Clinton interests. Richard Nixon reportedly considered a self-pardon before resigning.

Rep. Adam Schiff introduced the Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act, which would require disclosure of evidence against recipients of pardons connected to investigations involving the president or his family. New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman also sought to close what he called a double-jeopardy loophole, although New York currently recognizes presidential pardons.

Legal analysts said a pardon need not end an investigation: recipients lose Fifth Amendment protection for the pardoned offense and must testify truthfully, potentially facing charges for false testimony or obstruction.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero Energy from Overweight to Neutral while raising its price target from $75 to $78. It said improved capital discipline had already boosted the stock’s multiple, but industry cyclicality could delay further gains. Free cash flow should cover the dividend, though buybacks could be cut to zero; estimated total return is 6% versus 7% for the group.

The paper investigates whether LLM agents exhibit egoistic or altruistic behavior in large-scale social dilemmas. It proposes a Schelling-variant urban migration model in which 225 agents occupy nine residential blocks of capacity 50. Individual utility depends on block density and peaks at density 0.5, creating incentives for personal gains that can prevent the group from reaching the socially optimal distribution. Agents can migrate, post anonymous messages, and like messages on a shared message board. Three guidance levels vary whether agents consider only themselves, other agents, or how their actions influence others.

Six models are evaluated: o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B, Deepseek-V3.1, Deepseek-R1, and Gemini-2.5-pro. Evaluation combines collective-welfare, population-inequality, convergence, and individual-action metrics with qualitative analysis of reasoning logs and messages using Gemini-2.5-pro as an LLM judge.

The results identify two behavioral archetypes. “Adaptive Egoists” generally prioritize personal utility and reach sub-optimal, unequal equilibria without communication, but become more altruistic when exposed to message-board norms. For example, Qwen2.5-7B’s altruistic actions rose from 0% to 22.7%, while o1-mini and o3-mini showed reduced egoistic behavior. “Altruistic Optimizers,” including Gemini-2.5-pro and both Deepseek models, consistently reach optimal collective welfare and an equal population distribution, with or without the message board, despite sometimes sacrificing personal utility.

The paper argues that selecting an LLM for social simulation is therefore a theoretical choice about the social actor being modeled, not merely a technical performance decision. Adaptive Egoists may better represent socially influenced, bounded-rational human dynamics, while Altruistic Optimizers may suit models of idealized pro-social actors, collective action, or common-good resource allocation. Limitations include the simplified migration environment and homogeneous agents; proposed future work includes human-participant comparisons and simulations using heterogeneous, real-world demographic profiles.

Texas Instruments provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for the TLV3211, TLV3212, TLV3214, TLV3221, and TLV3222, subject to change without notice. Its tape drawing specifies carrier dimensions and pin-1 quadrant assignments, with notes on tolerancing, flash limits, solder-mask tolerances, and stencil recommendations. TI supplies design resources “as is,” disclaims warranties, and assigns developers responsibility for product selection, validation, testing, and compliance. Resource use is limited to applications using the described TI products; products remain subject to TI’s applicable terms.

A retrospective MIMIC-IV study evaluated resting heart rate (RHR) as a predictor of all-cause mortality among 1,918 adults with intracerebral hemorrhage in the ICU from 2011–2019. Patients were grouped into four RHR quartiles, and mortality in the ICU and at 30 days, 90 days, and one year was assessed using survival analyses and adjusted Cox regression.

Patients in the two highest RHR quartiles had more intraventricular hemorrhage, mechanical ventilation, and mortality. RHR was not significantly associated with mortality in the lowest two quartiles, but above 78.5 bpm, each quartile increase was associated with approximately 50%–100% higher mortality than the lowest quartile. Restricted cubic splines identified a nonlinear association and a threshold of 90.3 bpm: RHR below this level may be protective, while RHR above it was independently associated with increased mortality. Associations were stronger among patients older than 60 and were significant at 90 days and one year, but not 30 days, in the intraventricular hemorrhage subgroup. RHR above 90.3 bpm had limited predictive value, with an AUC greater than 0.5. Limitations included excluding blood-pressure measures as confounders and the need for further studies to clarify RHR’s predictive role. The authors concluded that stratifying patients with intracerebral hemorrhage by RHR may support risk assessment and heart-rate management.

Sigi Zheng explains how hedonic pricing models can quantify the economic benefits of green buildings, healthy buildings, and urban amenities. He recaps research indicating an average green-building rent premium of about 6% and a price premium of 7.6%, then introduces willingness to pay, stated preference, and revealed preference. Housing transactions reveal preferences through observed prices and rents, allowing researchers to decompose a property’s value into physical attributes, location, environmental features, and an unobserved residual.

Hedonic regressions estimate each attribute’s contribution using large transaction datasets, such as Zillow sales in Boston. With log-price models, coefficients are interpreted as percentage price changes; dummy-variable coefficients estimate effects such as a 6% premium for LEED certification. Regression fit indicates how much price variation the included variables explain, while omitted characteristics remain in the residual.

A central challenge is causal inference: observed green and nongreen buildings may differ in age, quality, neighborhood, developer, or other attributes, producing an “apples-to-oranges” comparison. Zheng defines the unobservable counterfactual and discusses endogeneity arising from omitted variables, reverse causality, and selection bias. Approaches discussed include ordinary least squares with controls and fixed effects, randomized controlled trials, quasi-experiments, geographic and propensity-score matching, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables, and difference-in-differences. Geographic matching, which compares green buildings with nearby nongreen properties, can produce more credible estimates; one cited study reports a 2.6% green-rating premium and a 13.3% sale-price premium after matching.

The lecture illustrates applications through Winthrop Center, where hedonic analysis can compare the market value of energy efficiency with views and other attributes. It also describes using housing data to value amenities such as parks, schools, subway stations, clean air, walkability, and transit proximity. Examples include an estimated 8% school-district price premium, High Line Park’s redevelopment and resulting property appreciation, and a transit-oriented development project where estimated station-area premiums informed investment decisions.

Finally, Zheng emphasizes that green improvements can also produce gentrification: higher-income residents and businesses may bid up housing and displace existing residents and local businesses. Quantitative modeling should therefore inform both the potential economic benefits and the distributional consequences of urban environmental investments.

After the Trump administration canceled a $34.9 million grant, Purdue ended its GEAR UP college-prep program, serving over 13,000 low-income Indiana students. The Education Department cited merit, fairness, civil-rights concerns, and DEI training. Purdue did not appeal; at least nine GEAR UP grants were canceled.

Edinburgh has experienced increased haar this spring, obscuring landmarks and bridges. The Met Office attributes this to reduced Atlantic temperature contrasts, which weakened the jet stream’s influence on Scotland. Persistent easterlies replaced prevailing westerlies, making eastern Scotland more prone to haar and creating sharp weather differences between east and west.
ID Buzz production is uncertain, though shared underpinnings could enable it. The regular ID targets Golf buyers, while the Crozz’s 302-hp all-wheel drive may suit a large U.S. launch.

DWH Deutsche Werte Holding AG joined Vienna’s mid-market segment on 23 April 2018, increasing transparency, quality and publicity requirements. The government plans to restore trading of Austrian bearer shares on the Third Market.

The Supreme Court denied review in several disputes, including Ghislaine Maxwell’s challenge to her prosecution, a state gun-enforcement law, a police drug-sniffing appeal, and Laura Loomer’s social media censorship suit; Justice Alito recused from Loomer’s case. It also denied rehearing of a Native American challenge to an Arizona forest land transfer, with Gorsuch saying he would have granted rehearing and Alito not participating. The court invited the solicitor general’s views on nuclear safety, trademark law, arbitration, and foreign sovereign immunity.

The Turtle Trading Strategy originated in a 1983 experiment led by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt to test whether trading skills could be taught. Dennis recruited 14 novice traders, trained them for two weeks, funded their accounts with $500,000 to $2 million, and required strict adherence to predefined rules. Many became successful, supporting Dennis’s view that trading could be learned.

The strategy is mechanical trend following: traders enter when prices break established ranges, trade in the direction of the trend, add to winning positions, and exit when the trend reverses. The original rules emphasized volatility-based position sizing using average true range, pyramiding, predetermined stop-loss orders, and exit criteria. Turtles entered longs after a 20-day high breakout, could add positions at a 55-day high breakout, and exited or reversed after a 20-day low breakdown. They traded a diversified basket of futures, including bonds, commodities, equity-index futures, and currencies.

Position sizes were larger in less volatile markets and smaller in more volatile ones to maintain consistent risk per dollar. Pyramiding increased exposure as trades progressed, while stop-loss orders limited losses and waiting for opposite breakouts determined exits. These methods could produce substantial gains but also involved leverage, whipsaws, long drawdowns, and a low win rate. Traders who strictly followed the rules generally survived and prospered, while those who struggled with exits were removed.

Although the strategy is considered less profitable than in the 1980s, it remains relevant and continues to work in markets with persistent trends. Modern traders often add technical indicators to identify trends. Evidence includes the Mt. Lucas Management Index, the Barclay CTA Index, and the success of systematic funds such as Swedish Lynx. Turtle-style systems also performed well in bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies through 2022, although weakening crypto trends have made them more difficult.

Backtests indicate that the rules can work over the long term but may be less effective since 2007. Their returns are uneven, with profits often concentrated in relatively short periods and prolonged drawdowns testing adherence. Real-world execution is harder than backtesting, particularly regarding exits, risk management, and disciplined rule-following. Dennis lost more than half his assets in 1987–1988 and stopped trading, while Eckhardt later founded a successful commodity trading adviser and publicly acknowledged that the mechanical program disproved his belief that successful traders required an innate, unencapsulable talent.

Preliminary data from the BC Coroners Service reported 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths in 2017, up 43% from 993 in 2016. The death rate rose for a second consecutive year to 30 per 100,000. Fentanyl was detected in 81% of deaths, usually combined with other drugs, and carfentanil was detected in 64 deaths from June through December. Deaths declined during the final four months of 2017. Most occurred indoors, often in private residences, and none occurred at supervised consumption or overdose prevention sites. More than half involved people aged 30–49, about four-fifths were male, and Vancouver Coastal Health had the highest regional death rate. Officials called the epidemic a continuing public-health crisis and emphasized naloxone, drug-checking services, outreach and treatment access.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit SAR ADC with an analog front end, programmable-gain amplifier, ADC driver, buffered precision reference, alarm monitoring, and a configurable multiSPI digital interface. Its PGA output includes a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter typically set to a 500 kHz −3 dB cutoff frequency.

The internal reference provides a nominal 4.096 V output and is selected by programming INTREF_DIS in RANGE_SEL_REG. It requires at least 4.7 µF of decoupling at REFIO and should not directly drive external loads. Although factory-trimmed, the reference can shift due to mechanical stress and solder reflow; repeated reflows can cause additional shifts. It is temperature-compensated from −40°C to +125°C. Alternatively, an external 4.096 V reference can drive REFIO while the internal buffer drives REFCAP, which requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1 µF decoupling capacitor. Typical reference-buffer temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C, with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs and uses straight-binary output. Full scale is the difference between positive and negative full-scale voltages, and LSB size is FSR/2^16. Input alarms provide programmable high and low thresholds with common programmable hysteresis. Separate AVDD alarms trigger at typical low and high thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped alarm flags are available through ALARM_REG, the multifunction alarm pin, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI read and write operations, single- or dual-SDO output, source-synchronous data transfer, single-device connections, and daisy-chained devices. Devices support RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, with programmable application reset or power-on reset behavior. Data-transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on its rising edge. A 32-clock frame is optimal; short frames cannot write registers, while long frames use the last 32 shifted bits as the command. Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, data formatting, range and reference selection, alarms, and alarm thresholds.

An application example combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 to digitize standard industrial voltage and current inputs. The ADS868xW settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and includes input and supply alarms for monitoring abnormal conditions, including thermistor-based temperature sensing.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires close decoupling to improve power-supply rejection. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce power consumption at lower throughput. Recommended PCB layouts separate analog and digital circuitry, use short ground paths, avoid vias between supply pins and bypass capacitors, and place specified reference-decoupling capacitors directly beside the device pins.
A Harvard Business School study found that several AI companions use emotional tricks to keep conversations from ending.

The study investigated mixed natural dyes from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) for dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs). MP and GJL extracts were mixed at volume ratios from 3:1 to 1:3 and applied to TiO₂-coated ITO substrates; cells were completed with an iodide/iodine electrolyte and graphite counter electrodes. UV–Vis analysis showed that blending the dyes broadened light absorption by combining anthocyanin, α-mangostin, and chlorophyll absorption bands. Microscopy indicated improved film uniformity for mixed dyes, while MP-rich formulations showed cracking and pure GJL produced a porous, microcracked surface.

The 1:3 MP:GJL mixture achieved the highest power conversion efficiency, 3.50%, compared with 2.75% for MP alone and 2.12% for GJL alone. Its improved performance was attributed to complementary absorption, enhanced current, and more efficient charge collection. Over ten cycles, GJL-rich mixtures generally retained more of their initial efficiency, while the 1:1 mixture declined rapidly; MP-dominant mixtures showed intermediate, steadier decay. The results support natural-dye combinations as low-cost, environmentally friendly DSSC sensitizers, but further work is needed to improve long-term stability. Reported efficiencies reflect relative performance under consistent halogen-lamp conditions rather than direct AM1.5G comparisons.

Eighteen-year-old Luca Speight received the Outstanding Achievement Award and was named Isle of Wight College Student of the Year 2018. Despite a life-threatening illness, surgery and three months away, he returned to catering studies, caught up on missed work, volunteered at college events and excelled in his work placement while pursuing his goal of becoming a chef.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, is preparing for the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse, the first to cross the continental United States in 99 years and the first visible in the lower 48 states since 1979. The town, where totality will last a little over two minutes, expects thousands to hundreds of thousands of visitors; hotels and campgrounds have been sold out for months. Drawing on its earthquake and tsunami preparations, the city has added trash cans, portable restrooms and free protective glasses, advised residents to stock essentials, and planned for gridlock on Highway 101, its sole access route. Three fire stations will operate during the four-day event, with authorities keeping lanes clear for emergency vehicles. The Coast Guard will monitor the harbor and inspect boats, while local operators have reserved boats for eclipse viewing and offshore fishing trips.

Figma shares rose 7% Monday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman demonstrated Figma integration with ChatGPT at DevDay. The integration allows users to request Figma by name or receive app suggestions, enabling third-party apps to complete tasks through OpenAI’s Apps SDK. Figma shares spiked as much as 16% during trading. Altman said developers can submit apps for review later in 2025 and that OpenAI plans to monetize third-party integrations.

Traditional game storage can bottleneck modern systems because faster SSDs leave CPU-based decompression as the limiting factor. NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft DirectStorage to keep data compressed while transferring it from NVMe SSDs to an RTX GPU, where lossless decompression is performed asynchronously. This offloads work that may require dozens of CPU cores, delivers up to 100 times the I/O performance of hard drives and traditional storage APIs, and can improve frame rates, loading times, texture streaming, pop-in, and stutter. Lossless compression can also reduce download and installation sizes. RTX IO is also positioned for CAD, scientific visualization, virtual reality, and production rendering workloads.

The GA10x Ampere architecture supports up to twice the performance of the prior architecture in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance and adds ray-traced motion blur and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Its third-generation Tensor Core adds structural sparsity. Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including HDR support, and include updated HDCP capabilities.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x GPUs are the first to provide hardware AV1 decoding, which can reduce bitrate by 50–55% versus H.264. In a cited test, AV1 playback of 8K60 HDR content used about 4% CPU through NVDEC, compared with 28 FPS and more than 85% CPU utilization using software decoding. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated H.264 encoding up to 4K and HEVC encoding up to 8K while reducing CPU utilization.

The NVIDIA A40 data-center GPU offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI throughput of the Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB through two A40 GPUs connected with NVLink, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, vGPU support, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU, 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores. Its GDDR6X memory reaches 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s peak bandwidth. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, exceeds the previous RTX 2080 Ti in performance, uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X, and lacks NVLink. GDDR6X memory also gains Error Detection and Replay, which detects and retries faulty transmissions to identify memory-overclocking limits, though it cannot prevent every crash.

The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes a GA102 GPU, 10,752 CUDA cores, 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, hardware-accelerated ray tracing and motion blur, and AI denoising. Two cards can be linked with NVLink for 96 GB of combined memory. The document also provides performance comparisons for rendering, HPC, and deep-learning workloads, along with warranty, liability, intended-use, and product-change disclaimers.

Benjamin David Sherwood, a Wisconsin man who traveled to Houston seeking sex with a child he believed was 4, pleaded guilty to interstate illicit contact with a child and enticing a minor into sexual contact. A Houston judge sentenced him to 11 years, ordered concurrent terms, lifelong supervision, sex-offender registration, and child and internet restrictions. Federal agents arrested him at a hotel after a federal investigation.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018. For the three months, revenue was $26.819 billion, compared with $23.212 billion a year earlier, as product revenue rose to $15.114 billion and service and other revenue increased to $11.705 billion. Gross margin was $17.550 billion, operating income was $8.292 billion, net income was $7.424 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $0.95, versus $5.486 billion and $0.70 in the prior-year quarter.

For the nine months ended March 31, revenue was $80.275 billion, up from $70.966 billion, and operating income was $24.679 billion, up from $21.343 billion. Net income declined to $7.698 billion from $17.420 billion, and diluted earnings per share declined to $0.99 from $2.22, primarily because of a second-quarter tax charge related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

At March 31, 2018, Microsoft held $9.221 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $123.049 billion of short-term investments. Total assets were $245.497 billion, total liabilities were $166.258 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $79.239 billion. For the first nine months, operating activities generated $32.466 billion of cash; financing and investing activities used $27.551 billion and $3.391 billion, respectively. The company paid $9.473 billion in common-stock cash dividends and reported 7.683 billion shares outstanding as of April 20, 2018.

The unaudited interim statements were prepared under U.S. GAAP. Revenue is recognized when control of products or services transfers to customers. On-premises licenses generally are recognized when made available, subscription-based cloud revenue generally is recognized ratably, consumption-based cloud revenue follows customer utilization, consulting revenue is recognized as services are provided, and search advertising is recognized when the advertisement appears or the required action is completed. Products and services are treated as separate performance obligations when distinct; Office 365 is generally accounted for as a single performance obligation because of the integration of its desktop and cloud components.

Microsoft adopted the revenue recognition and lease standards on July 1, 2017, using full retrospective and modified retrospective methods, respectively. The changes primarily affected the timing of Windows 10 and certain commercial software-license revenue and resulted in the recognition of operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities. Prior-period amounts were restated, with no effect on operating, financing, or investing cash flows. Standards not yet adopted include guidance on hedging, intra-entity asset transfers, credit losses, and financial-instrument recognition and measurement.

The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act reduced the U.S. federal statutory rate to 21% and required a transition tax on deferred foreign income. Microsoft recorded a provisional $13.8 billion net charge in the second quarter, comprising a $17.8 billion transition-tax charge, partly offset by a $4.0 billion tax-rate benefit, including an estimated $454 million GILTI benefit. The company had not completed its accounting for the legislation and said the estimates remained subject to revision.

Microsoft’s investment portfolio included government securities, corporate and foreign bonds, commercial paper, certificates of deposit, and equity investments. It used derivatives to manage foreign-currency, equity-price, interest-rate, and credit risks. Fair-value measurements were classified into three levels based on the observability of inputs, and Level 3 changes were immaterial during the reported periods.

Long-term debt, including the current portion, had a carrying value of $76.9 billion and an estimated fair value of $78.9 billion. Commercial paper outstanding totaled $231 million, supported by two $5.0 billion credit facilities that remained undrawn. Microsoft had $7.133 billion of operating lease liabilities and $4.331 billion of finance lease liabilities.

The company had accrued $371 million of aggregate legal liabilities and estimated that reasonably possible adverse outcomes beyond recorded amounts could reach approximately $1.3 billion. Matters included patent and antitrust litigation, cell-phone health-effect claims, and an employment gender-discrimination class action. Microsoft and IPCom settled all IPCom claims in April 2018.

As of March 31, 2018, $30.3 billion remained under Microsoft’s $40.0 billion share-repurchase authorization. During the first three quarters of fiscal 2018, the company repurchased 78 million shares for $6.5 billion under the repurchase programs, excluding shares used to settle employee tax withholding.

BMW and Brilliance Automotive launched the China-only 1 Series sedan in July 2016. BMW is considering an Indian launch but has not decided; India has shown interest in the affordable sedan. The car uses the UKL1 platform, is front-wheel drive, and may offer 125i and 120i petrol engines with diesel options.

The Portland Thorns (14-5-5) host the third-place Orlando Pride (11-6-7) in Saturday’s first NWSL playoff semifinal, seeking to avoid last season’s 4-3 home semifinal loss to the Western New York Flash, now the North Carolina Courage. The Courage (16-7-1) won the Supporters’ Shield and host the Chicago Red Stars in Sunday’s other semifinal; the winners meet Oct. 14 in Orlando for the championship. Portland has never lost to Orlando (3-0-1), but Pride midfielder Camila has an ACL tear. The Thorns opened the season by beating Orlando 2-0 and posted a league-record 10 home wins. Sam Kerr won the Golden Boot with a record 17 goals, and the fifth season was the first with a national U.S. broadcast deal, with Lifetime airing both semifinals.

Forecast rain over the next 10 days is expected to pose less risk to Oroville Dam than the February storm. The Feather River basin is forecast to receive 7.5 inches, versus 13.6 inches from Feb. 5-11, with rain spread out and temperatures colder. Snow at elevations as low as 3,500 feet should reduce immediate runoff, and inflows may be about one-quarter of the prior storm, whose peak reached 190,000 cubic feet per second. River flows have dropped, upstream dams are retaining water, and reservoir releases are lowering the lake about four inches per hour. As of Tuesday afternoon, it stood 15 feet below the emergency spillway lip and could fall another 24 feet by Friday. However, record snowpack remains a threat if abruptly warmed.

The lecture reviews the LSZ theorem for obtaining scattering amplitudes from time-ordered momentum-space correlation functions. In the on-shell limit, an \(n\)-point correlation function yields the product of external propagators times the scattering amplitude. Fourier transformation and operator ordering explain the sign convention: initial-state momenta approach the negative-energy root, while final-state momenta approach the positive-energy root. Scattering amplitudes are calculated using connected diagrams with external propagators truncated. Diagrams that only correct external propagators are absorbed into a factor \(Z\), which is independent of momentum, may differ by particle type, and contributes only beyond leading order; correlation functions retain these corrections, whereas scattering amplitudes omit them.

The lecture then transitions from interacting scalar theories to fermions. The Klein–Gordon equation, despite its relativistic plane-wave solutions, does not provide positive-definite probability and includes negative-energy states. Dirac sought a first-order, Lorentz-covariant equation and replaced constant coefficients with Hermitian matrices. Conditions on the spatial matrices ensure that squaring the equation reproduces the Klein–Gordon equation, requiring matrices of at least \(4\times4\) size and a four-component spinor.

Defining gamma matrices from these coefficients yields the Clifford-algebra relation
\[
\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}.
\]
Different solutions are related by similarity transformations and are physically equivalent, although particular forms can be convenient in different regimes. For a massless particle, the equation reduces to a two-component description using Pauli matrices, whereas a massive particle requires four components. The spinor is not a Lorentz four-vector. The Dirac equation also yields a conserved current with a classically positive-definite time component. Lorentz covariance remains to be demonstrated in the next lecture, following a recap of the scalar-field case.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017 reported net sales of $35.7 billion, up 23% from $29.1 billion a year earlier. Product sales were $23.7 billion and service sales were $12.0 billion. Operating income declined to $1.0 billion from $1.1 billion, while net income rose to $724 million from $513 million and diluted EPS increased to $1.48 from $1.07.

North America net sales rose 24% to $21.0 billion, with operating income of $596 million. International sales increased 16% to $11.1 billion, while the segment recorded a $481 million operating loss. AWS sales increased 43% to $3.7 billion, and AWS operating income rose to $890 million. Higher fulfillment, marketing, technology and content, and general and administrative expenses contributed to the consolidated operating-income decline.

Cash and cash equivalents totaled $15.4 billion, while cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities had a fair value of $21.5 billion. Quarterly operating cash flow was negative $1.6 billion, and trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow and free cash flow were $17.6 billion and $10.2 billion, respectively. Amazon had $45.9 billion of contractual commitments, $8.8 billion of long-term debt, and agreed to acquire Souq Group Ltd. for $580 million in cash, subject to adjustments. A $5 billion share-repurchase authorization was outstanding, but no shares were repurchased in either first quarter.

The filing described material uncertainties involving tax audits, legal proceedings, foreign exchange rates, and interest rates, including potential IRS transfer-pricing adjustments and an ongoing review of sanctions-related orders. Amazon also adopted new inventory and stock-compensation accounting guidance and was evaluating revenue-recognition, lease, tax, and restricted-cash standards. Second-quarter 2017 guidance called for net sales of $35.25 billion to $37.75 billion and operating income of $425 million to $1.075 billion, including an anticipated $720 million unfavorable foreign-exchange impact.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards to return to patrol the province’s beaches by April 1, following a March 21 meeting about the ongoing lifeguard crisis. Local administrative offices must cover beaches in Muang Phuket and Kathu districts, while a contractor is expected to serve five Thalang district beaches. Authorities without six months’ funding from April must seek support from the Phuket Provincial Administration Organisation (PPAO), and local offices are expected to fund lifeguards in their next budget year.

NNT reported that 37 lifeguards previously covered 15 points across six beaches from December 28 to February 26. The report also raised confusion because, on December 12, the governor had said the PPAO would no longer be involved in providing lifeguards, contrary to the later financial-support arrangement. The governor did not explain this apparent change, and questions from The Phuket News remained unanswered.

Schmidt Sciences, created by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and his wife Wendy, announced $45 million in five-year funding for global carbon-cycle research, including a Southern Ocean project led by Galen McKinley. Four remotely piloted drone boats will collect data for five years, including during Antarctic winters, from remote areas beyond commercial shipping routes. They will measure seawater CO₂ partial pressure, use machine learning to optimize data collection, and make the results publicly available. The project is structured as a public-private partnership, with Schmidt Sciences purchasing data from vessel operators contracted through NOAA. Scientists said the initiative could address limited observations of the Southern Ocean, an important carbon sink, while private funding has become more important amid proposed cuts to NOAA, the National Science Foundation, and other federal research programs.

The passage documents AGESA host-environment services. Native assembler procedures initialize a pre-memory stack on all processor cores by dividing the available stack region, mapping it to global address space, configuring MTRRs, setting SS:ESP for protected or real mode, and creating a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF. A corresponding BSP-only procedure disables cache-as-RAM mode once memory is available, leaves MTRR settings unchanged, flushes caches, and leaves the BSP’s cache enabled. AARCH64 systems with a PSP do not use these stack and early macros because the PSP initializes DRAM.

AmdCreateStruct allocates and initializes a named structure using a pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage. Host-allocated storage must be sufficient, and successful initialization may overwrite the parameter block. It requires an established stack and must be paired with AmdReleaseStruct.

Other services return a DIMM data-eye bitmap, an APIC address, pre-memory execution-cache capacity, a processor die’s base PCI address, and identifiers for the current socket, die, and core. Another service maps a memory address to its FRU DIMM and reports socket, channel, DIMM, chip-select, bank, row, and column locations for memory-failure diagnosis.

Scientists are investigating whether electrical sparks from tiny bubbles could explain will-o’-the-wisps, the bluish lights reported over swamps and cemeteries. Researchers believe methane released by decaying plants or animals can burn with a cool blue flame, but what ignites it remains uncertain.

A team led by Yu Xia used a 3-D-printed nozzle to create tiny bubbles in water, then detected emitted photons and captured microscopic lightning with a high-speed camera. Crowded bubbles produced electrical zaps, while methane-and-air mixtures released more photons and heated the water. The findings suggest that microbubbles could ignite methane and possibly create will-o’-the-wisps, though experts note that the experiments occurred underwater and natural swamps differ from laboratory conditions. The researchers also say such sparks may offer environmentally friendly ways to trigger chemical reactions, break down pollutants, and advance research into triboelectricity.

In a daisy chain, all devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, while each device’s SDO-0 feeds the next device’s SDI; the last feeds the host. The host programs identical configuration values and sets SDO_CTL_REG bits 7–0 to 00h. Data shift MSB-first, with the host receiving device N through device 1; the optimal frame has 32 × N SCLK capture edges.

The Solawave 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is on sale for a little over $100 during Prime Day. It targets specific areas, vibrates and provides warmth, and requires three minutes of manual facial massage. WIRED testers reported skin-tightening results, particularly around the eyes. Solawave’s flexible red-light face mask is also on sale for $227, $122 off.

On February 10, 2016, Amazon.com, Inc.’s Board elected Wendell P. Weeks as a director and appointed him to its Audit Committee. Weeks, Corning Incorporated’s CEO, president and chairman, received a restricted stock unit award for 1,365 Amazon shares vesting in three annual installments beginning February 15, 2017, subject to continued service, and entered Amazon’s standard director indemnification agreement.

The Board approved a two-year leave of absence for Senior Vice President Diego Piacentini, effective August 2016, during which forfeiture of his restricted stock unit awards would be suspended. Russ Grandinetti will oversee Amazon’s international consumer business and report to Jeffrey A. Wilke.

The Board also authorized Amazon to repurchase up to $5 billion of common stock, replacing its prior $2 billion authorization. The program has no fixed expiration and permits opportunistic purchases through various transaction methods.

The message urges Congress to reform federal land and natural-resource policies to conserve public lands while encouraging productive private development and preventing monopolies and abuse. The public domain declined from 1,055,911,288 acres in 1860 to 731,354,081 acres, with an additional 368,035,975 acres in Alaska. Earlier land statutes and lax distribution enabled fraud, transferred valuable resources to irresponsible owners, and made recovery of some lands impossible through statutes of limitation.

Congress is urged to classify public lands and resources through the Geological Survey, validate existing withdrawals, and clarify the Interior Secretary’s authority to temporarily withdraw lands pending legislation. Agricultural land titles could be separated from mining rights, allowing surface lands to be sold while coal, oil, asphaltum, natural gas, and phosphate deposits are leased for royalties, required development, and anti-monopoly forfeiture provisions. Similar protections should apply in Alaska. Government control of water-power sites should be retained, and any private leases should limit use, rents, renewals, and consolidation in ways that preserve competition.

Soil conservation is presented as the foremost resource issue, requiring scientific management of soils and state action alongside the Department of Agriculture. Enlarged homesteads in semiarid areas have promoted dry farming, while millions of arid acres could become productive through irrigation and reservoirs. To complete existing reclamation projects and provide relief for settlers, the message recommends authority to issue up to $30 million in bonds, repayable over ten years or more from land proceeds and water-rental returns, as well as consideration of proposed amendments to the reclamation act.

Congress is also urged to repeal the June 3, 1878 timber-land act and dispose of public timber by sale, with the cleared lands subject to agricultural or mineral laws. Federal forest reserves of about 190 million acres should be preserved and scientifically managed, and moderate annual reforestation spending should continue for five or ten years. Regulation of privately owned forests is primarily a state responsibility.

For inland waterways, Congress should finance only projects with definite plans, costs, and probable traffic.
