It should continue the Ohio River project, which requires 54 dams to maintain a nine-foot channel, with seven completed, six under construction, and $63 million remaining. Congress should also continue improvements to the upper Mississippi and Missouri and deepen the lower Mississippi if increased traffic warrants. The message concludes that Congress should promptly enact the proposed land, reclamation, and conservation measures without awaiting the ordered investigation of the Interior Department and Forest Service.

NVIDIA’s RTX IO accelerates professional visualization and rendering workflows by transferring data directly from NVMe storage to compatible GPUs. Working with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, RTX IO enables GPU-based lossless decompression of compressed assets, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance for rendering, large CAD datasets, and high-resolution virtual reality.

The NVIDIA A40, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, targets data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to five times the AI-training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity, and twice the PCIe Gen4 bandwidth. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, virtualization support, Quadro Sync, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including HDR support with higher interface bandwidth. Their fifth-generation NVDEC decoder offloads playback and transcoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs provide the first hardware AV1 decoding, capable of 8K60 HDR playback with about 4% CPU usage in the cited test. Their seventh-generation NVENC encoder supports H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K while reducing CPU use.

GA10x provides up to twofold improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection performance and supports concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. The third-generation Tensor Core adds structural sparsity, while GDDR6X support enables data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth on the GeForce RTX 3090.

The GeForce RTX 3090 has 24 GB of memory, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores and is described as 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and is reported as faster than the preceding RTX 2080 Ti. GDDR6X memory also gains Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transmissions and retries them, helping identify memory-overclocking limits, though it cannot prevent every crash.

The RTX A6000 includes a GA102 GPU, 10,752 CUDA cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB with two NVLink-connected boards. It provides real-time and final-frame ray tracing, hardware-accelerated motion blur, AI denoising, and support for large 3D datasets and professional rendering, simulation, virtual-production, and deep-learning workloads.

EUR/USD’s channel targets wave 3’s 161.8% level; slowing momentum and a resistance breakout may invalidate it or suggest a bullish ABC. GBP/USD’s breakout could target resistance or 1.05, while a breakdown invalidates the bullish setup. USD/JPY’s bull flag targets wave 3; a support break could prompt a bearish ABC retracement.

Consumer confidence measures consumers’ optimism about the economy and influences spending, saving, production, hiring, lending, and market sentiment. The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index is based on a monthly survey of 5,000 U.S. households, while the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index uses monthly telephone interviews covering personal finances and short- and long-term economic expectations. Changes below 5% are generally considered insignificant, while larger changes may indicate shifts in economic momentum.

Using monthly U.S. consumer-confidence data from the OECD, the article backtests S&P 500 performance against confidence relative to its 12-month moving average. An initial $10,000 investment in 1993 grew to $159,000 under buy-and-hold, compared with $99,000 for a strategy invested in stocks only when confidence exceeded its moving average. The buy-and-hold strategy’s CAGR was 10.4%, versus 8.4% for the confidence strategy, but the latter had a lower maximum drawdown of 23% versus 55% and was invested only 55% of the time. The inverse strategy, invested in stocks only when confidence was below its moving average, grew to just $15,000 over 28 years, a 1.58% annual return.

The first strategy calculates a 12-month simple moving average of consumer confidence: when the monthly reading is above it, the strategy holds the S&P 500 for the next month; when below, it switches to cash. The backtests indicate that bullish confidence is associated with stronger subsequent stock performance, while bearish confidence is associated with weaker performance.

The passage defines the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), which lets guests selectively expose register state during non-automatic exits. Automatic exits expose no guest state, while non-automatic exits generate a VMM Communication exception, allowing the guest to copy required data into the GHCB and issue VMGEXIT. The 4 KB, page-aligned GHCB must be mapped decrypted or shared and mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state layout.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and a 52-bit hypervisor feature bitmap. Supported enhancements include 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, additional VMGEXIT error reporting, a VLEK GUID, APIC ID discovery, multiple VMPL levels, page-state changes, the SEV-SNP EFI confidential-computing blob protocol, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC. A feature bitmap advertises optional capabilities, while core support is mandatory.

The GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 for requests and the upper bits for the GHCB address and related data. Hypervisors must not intercept this MSR. Defined requests cover protocol and feature negotiation, CPUID data, AP reset hold, preferred or registered GHCB addresses, page-state changes, VMPL changes, unregistering a GHCB, and termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB address for each vCPU before using it for VMGEXIT.

Non-automatic exit processing requires the guest to mark valid GHCB fields and supply SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2. Defined events include protected I/O and MSR accesses, VMMCALL, MMIO transfers, page-state changes, SNP guest requests, extended requests returning VCEK or VLEK certificates, AP creation and removal, restricted-injection doorbell management, IPIs, timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL changes, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, and guest-requested termination. Hypervisors report malformed input and other failures through the exit-information fields. MMIO and other multi-step operations can use the shared buffer and be resumed or split across multiple VMGEXIT calls.

SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages and synchronous firmware operations. Extended requests can return certificates with the attestation report. SEV-TIO requests support device binding and return measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports. Page-state changes support private, shared, smash, and unsmash operations and record progress so interrupted requests can resume.

The document also covers guest identification through CPUID, SMP application-processor booting through reset-hold mechanisms, jump tables, or SNP AP creation with VM Save Areas, and associated hotplug support. NMI handling requires the hypervisor to avoid intercepting IRET and intercept #DB, with the guest issuing an “NMI Complete” message when another NMI can safely be accepted. Hardware debug-register virtualization may be supported; SMM and nested virtualization are not supported in this version.

For restricted injection, the host communicates essential notifications through a shared #HV doorbell page containing a 16-bit PendingEvent field and a NoEoiRequired field. The host must emulate APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and end-of-interrupt behavior, present the highest-priority ready interrupt, and use the doorbell’s signal-suppression and EOI fields consistently.

Natalie Grabow, 80, set the world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing the course in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds in Hawaii. The New Jersey grandmother of four began triathlons at 60 after learning to swim at 59, progressing from sprint races to half-distance Ironmans and qualifying for Kona at 61. Despite limited sports opportunities for women growing up, she stayed active through cheerleading, skiing, running, and shorter races. She trains for months before competitions, exercising about two hours daily, and plans to compete for as long as possible.

Lenovo unveiled the limited-edition ThinkPad 25, combining T470 hardware with retro styling inspired by the 1992 ThinkPad 700C. It features a 14-inch Full HD touchscreen, Core i7-7500U, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD, and claimed 18-hour battery life. Limited quantities are available in select countries starting at $1,899.

The document describes NVIDIA’s GA10x-class Ampere architecture and related data-center, professional, and GeForce GPUs, emphasizing visual computing, AI, high-performance computing, virtualization, and hardware-accelerated media processing.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x Ampere, is presented as a data-center GPU for visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. Its PCIe Gen4 interface provides up to twice the bandwidth of Turing-based GPUs. Each A40 has 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB by connecting two GPUs with third-generation NVLink. It includes three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs and supports NVIDIA vGPU software and Quadro Sync; its display outputs are disabled by default for virtualization. The A40 is also compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz, including two 8K displays at 60 Hz. DisplayPort 1.4a uses DSC 1.2a for visually lossless compression, while HDMI 2.1 increases maximum bandwidth to 48 Gbps and supports formats such as 8K60, 4K120, and dynamic HDR. The architecture also supports HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux, freeing the graphics engine and CPU for other work. GA10x GPUs provide the first hardware AV1 decode implementation; one test reported 8K60 HDR playback with about 4% CPU usage, compared with 28 FPS and more than 85% CPU usage for software decoding. Supported AV1 features include 8- and 10-bit Profile 0 decoding, resolutions from 128×128 to 8192×8192, histogram collection, film-grain synthesis, and sub-sample maps.

Seventh-generation NVENC offloads encoding from the CPU. The document says it can exceed software x264 Fast quality, approach x264 Medium quality, reduce CPU utilization, and support up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding. GA10x also provides up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance and adds motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing, while its third-generation Tensor Core supports structural sparsity for doubled effective throughput.

The architecture supports GDDR6X memory, including data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth in the GeForce RTX 3090. RTX IO provides APIs for faster SSD-to-GPU loading and streaming and, with Microsoft DirectStorage, offloads work from CPU cores to the GPU.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU, has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores, and is described as 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 without NVLink and is presented as faster than the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti; it uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

GA10x GDDR6X memory interfaces include Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transmissions and retries them. Retries reduce useful bandwidth as memory overclocking reaches its limits, providing an indication to stop increasing clock frequency, though crashes remain possible.

The RTX A6000 contains a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA cores and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, supports real-time and final-frame ray tracing, accelerated AI denoising, and large 3D datasets, and can combine two boards through NVLink for 96 GB. The document also provides benchmark setups and figures comparing its professional rendering, HPC, and deep-learning performance with the RTX 6000.

The specification states that information is believed accurate as of its publication date but may be corrected or changed, that customers should verify current specifications, and that products are sold under NVIDIA’s standard terms. NVIDIA disclaims warranties, grants no implied intellectual-property license, and states that its products are not warranted for medical, military, aircraft, space, life-support, or other safety-critical applications.

COPD is caused almost exclusively by smoking. Symptoms include chronic coughing, shortness of breath, and difficulty exhaling. Doctors review smoking history, conduct breathing tests, and may recommend inhalers, oxygen, or rehabilitation. There is no cure; quitting smoking is the best way to prevent or slow progression.

Distance education developed from early correspondence instruction into technology-supported, institution-based learning in which teachers and students are physically separated and communicate through print, electronic, or mechanical tools. Its growth accelerated during the COVID-19 pandemic, when it became essential for continuing higher education. The study aimed to evaluate distance education practices in Turkish sports higher education during the pandemic and recommend ways to improve them.

A qualitative case study using descriptive analysis examined 14 sports lecturers selected by criterion sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews between December 2020 and November 2021 and analyzed by two experts using MAXQDA 20; coding reliability was 82%. Participation was voluntary, and participants’ identities were confidential.

Lecturers identified benefits including flexibility independent of time and place, reduced costs, access to varied resources and information, repeated access to recorded lessons, greater use of information technologies, reduced pandemic transmission, and expanded instructional diversity. Reported disadvantages included weakened interaction and socialization, unequal access to equipment and connectivity, participation and motivation problems, inadequate assessment, exam integrity concerns, and limited effectiveness of theoretical and especially applied sports lessons. Major challenges involved infrastructure and connection failures, insufficient institutional and technical capacity, non-user-friendly platforms, communication difficulties, intensive workloads, and assessment and evaluation problems.

Although participants considered distance education practical and necessary during disruptions, they regarded its management as generally ineffective. Responsibilities were dispersed among authorities, universities, departments, and lecturers, contributing to delayed decisions, weak coordination, inadequate lecturer training, and technical problems. The discussion also emphasized personal-data security when recording, storing, transferring, and granting access to course and examination data.

The study concluded that distance education can provide continuity when formal education is disrupted, but sports programs require field-specific designs aligned with course outcomes and student access. Limited provision of practical instruction may cause learning losses, and further research is needed to establish its effectiveness, advantages, and disadvantages.

First-principles scattering and Landauer–Büttiker calculations were used to study tunnel magnetoresistance in an all-antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn(01¯10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junction. Mn3Sn has an inverse triangular magnetic order that breaks macroscopic time-reversal symmetry and produces momentum-dependent spin splitting. Calculations for parallel and antiparallel configurations show that transmission decreases exponentially with MgO thickness, confirming tunneling transport. With 12 MgO monolayers, the TMR ratio exceeds 1000%, while the resistance-area product is approximately 1–10 kΩ·µm², considered reasonable for practical devices. Symmetry and Fermi-surface analyses show that spin polarization along the cluster-octupole easy axis dominates the TMR, while the perpendicular z component largely cancels across opposite momenta. Transmission differences are strongest near zero in-plane momentum. MgO complex-band calculations show correspondingly smaller electron decay rates near this momentum, demonstrating that barrier filtering contributes alongside Mn3Sn’s spin splitting. The results support Mn3Sn as a promising electrode for electrically readable antiferromagnetic MTJ devices, using an orientation compatible with spin-orbit-torque switching.

MD simulations enable nanoscale thermal studies; thermal conductivity κ is obtained by Green-Kubo (GK), which uses the equilibrium heat-flux autocorrelation and fluctuation-dissipation theorem, or non-equilibrium MD (NEMD), which imposes a temperature gradient via thermal reservoirs and Fourier's law (κ = −J/∇T). NEMD heat flux comes from thermostat energy exchange; GK heat flux is averaged over the volume from velocities and forces. The interfacial heat current Q1→2 yields interfacial thermal conductance and enables spectral decomposition (SDHC) by phonon mode energy, which for many-body potentials requires defining interatomic mechanical power across the interface—trivial only for pair potentials.

LAMMPS supports both methods, but its GK heat flux uses a stress-tensor formula valid only for pair potentials, giving incorrect κ otherwise. Torii et al. derived exact control-volume and control-surface heat flux formulas for arbitrary many-body potentials and energy partitioning; exact implementations exist only for specific systems (bond/angle/torsion models, Tersoff carbon, machine-learning potentials), while control-surface Q1→2 and SDHC were limited to pairwise potentials or the harmonic approximation. This work implements the Torii formulas in LAMMPS for arbitrary many-body potentials.

The methods section gives Hardy's and Torii's control-volume heat flux formulas, noting that partitioning many-body energy U = Σj Uj among atoms is arbitrary and non-unique without affecting κ. Comparative GK/NEMD tests against LAMMPS use 2D and 3D solids with Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials, plus SDHC results for monolayer graphene and MoS2; details are in supplementary material.

Jeff Bezos proposed building future data centres in space as demand for cloud services and AI computing strains terrestrial infrastructure. He said orbital facilities could ease constraints on land, energy and water, use solar power, and provide resilience against terrestrial disruptions. Major hurdles remain, including radiation shielding, power storage, vacuum cooling, reliable low-latency communications, and launch and maintenance costs. Falling launch costs and advances in miniaturised hardware are encouraging aerospace and technology firms to explore orbital and lunar infrastructure. The concept remains speculative, but reflects growing pressure on computing capacity and the search for alternatives to conventional data centres.

A Journal of Neuroscience study found that barn owls, despite simpler brains than humans and other primates, group visual elements moving in the same direction to distinguish targets from shifting backgrounds. Researchers showed owls moving black dots and tracked their head turns; detection improved when background dots moved uniformly. Activity in the ocular tectum varied with dot motion, suggesting this brain area supports the visual task.
Strong U.S. job and wage gains fueled Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations, lifting the dollar and 10-year Treasury yield to 2.84% while stocks fell.

Gold edged lower as the dollar gained against the euro ahead of U.S. January nonfarm payrolls, expected to show job growth above the prior month. Spot gold fell 0.3% to $1,345.22 an ounce, while June futures were flat at $1,353.10. Strong payrolls could prompt faster Federal Reserve rate hikes and weigh on non-yielding bullion. The Fed held rates steady but raised its inflation outlook and signaled gradual increases. Global stocks headed for their biggest weekly drop since late 2016 amid tightening-policy and inflation concerns. Silver and platinum fell, while palladium faced its biggest weekly decline since early September.

Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retired after five years as superintendent and 30 years in the district, with Dr. Jesus Jara named as his successor. Skorkowsky cited increases in graduation rates from 60% to 83% and more than 10,000 added magnet-school seats. He said the district still faces a $60 million budget shortfall and urged state leaders to direct marijuana revenue to Clark County education. Other concerns included program and teacher-pay funding and school safety following the Santa Fe High School shooting. He recommended single-point entry at all schools and more mental-health professionals. Skorkowsky advised Jara to listen to the community and said they would work together for several weeks.

At RSA Conference 2017, speakers warned that attackers are corrupting data used in decision-making, including small inputs underlying big-data models, to produce faulty outcomes and economic losses. Intel Security’s Chris Young also identified insecure home networks and IoT devices as risks to corporate systems, citing the Mirai botnet. Microsoft President Brad Smith urged global cooperation, arguing for defense-only principles, protection of customers and civilian infrastructure, and international agreements governing cyber conflict. He proposed a “digital Geneva Convention,” government disclosure rather than stockpiling of software vulnerabilities, and an international agency to monitor and attribute nation-state attacks. Smith also said private-sector security practitioners must help restore trust in cyberspace.

Lifeline Fiji said suicide remains taboo in Fiji and called for greater awareness of support services and emotional wellbeing. NSAAC recorded 124 suicides and 107 attempts in 2015, and 102 suicides and 104 attempts in 2016. From 2011 to March this year, 627 suicides and 694 attempts were recorded, including 56 suicides and 97 attempts among children. Program director Jeremiah Merekula cited low help-seeking, limited community support and poor awareness of warning signs. Lifeline is expanding school and parent education programs and operates a 24/7 helpline.

The disclosure describes a geographically based map GUI for a social networking application that displays users’ and friends’ approximate locations using avatars, profile pictures, or default icons. Users may control whether their location is shared, select audiences such as “Best Friends,” “Friends,” or “Custom,” select friends on the map, and initiate chats without leaving it.

The system predicts a user’s presumed destination by receiving location data from the user’s device, determining the user’s current trajectory, and correlating it with historical location information. Candidate habitual places are evaluated using factors including distance trends, likelihood of arrival within a set time, expected stay duration, and similarity to habitual behavior. The system also extracts recurring trajectory patterns from historical trajectories, clusters similar trajectories, and averages each cluster into a pattern. If the current trajectory correlates strongly with a pattern, the pattern’s arrival point is selected as the presumed destination.

Friends’ map GUIs can display an icon representing the presumed destination, an illustration of a matched trajectory, estimated arrival time, and the user’s speed or other status. Predictions and arrival estimates may be updated as new information arrives or removed if confidence falls below a threshold. If device updates cease, the system may project the user’s position along an identified trajectory pattern and use available schedule or delay information to refine arrival estimates. The disclosure also describes the related client-server architecture, databases, processing components, and methods for extracting trajectory patterns.

Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open the Radyr Tap, a micropub in an empty Station Road unit, ending Radyr’s 15-year pub drought since the Radyr Arms closed in 2003. The proposal follows resident Jamie Grundy’s Twitter campaign. Consultation ends June 19, before Cardiff Council decides. It would serve local and craft beers, wines, spirits and artisan snacks, but no cooked food.

MIT became the first of nine invited universities to reject the Trump administration’s proposed Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education, which sought sweeping campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding treatment. President Sally Kornbluth said the compact would restrict free expression and institutional independence and conflict with MIT’s support for merit-based funding.

Most other invited institutions said they were reviewing the proposal, though the University of Texas showed enthusiasm. Dartmouth defended academic freedom and self-governance while confirming that deliberations continued. California and Virginia officials threatened reduced state funding for universities that sign, and Pennsylvania lawmakers also opposed the compact.

MIT’s rejection was praised by academic and political figures as courageous and potentially precedent-setting. Higher education professor Brendan Cantwell said accepting universities would need to explain that they were not surrendering academic freedom or institutional independence. Former Education Department official Kenneth Marcus suggested possible retaliation and referenced a pending lawsuit. The White House and Department of Education did not respond to comment requests.

The passage describes the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontroller system architecture and peripherals. The CPU subsystem includes a 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ processor operating from 32 kHz to 80 MHz, instruction prefetch and I-cache, SysTick, an eight-region MPU, and an NVIC with four priority levels and interrupt grouping.

Five power modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—support configurable performance and power policies. PD1 powers the CPU, memories, and high-performance peripherals, while PD0 powers low-power peripherals. Both domains are disabled in SHUTDOWN, which can be exited through NRST, SWD, or designated I/O conditions. The PMU provides regulated core supplies, VDD supervision, brown-out reset, and protected power-on trim. The clock module supports internal and external low- and high-frequency oscillators, a system PLL, and multiple distributed clock sources.

The DMA controller provides 12 channels, multiple transfer widths, up to 64,000 transfers per block, configurable triggers, interrupts, channel cascading, and stride mode. The event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals through static and programmable event fabrics.

Memory includes dual-bank nonvolatile flash with ECC, 1 kB erase sectors, selectable high-endurance sectors, and address swapping for OTA updates. Up to 128 kB of zero-wait-state SRAM is divided into protected and unprotected banks, with configurable availability and write-execute partitioning.

GPIO and IOMUX provide programmable multiplexing, drive strength, pulls, speed, input paths, and wake logic. Analog peripherals include two 12-bit ADCs with simultaneous sampling, internal temperature and supply channels, hardware averaging, a temperature sensor, configurable internal or external voltage references, comparators, and a buffered 12-bit DAC.

Security and processing features include AES-128/256 acceleration, flexible firewalls, secure storage for up to four AES keys, CRC modules, a true random number generator, a separate AES accelerator, a keystore, and a math accelerator.

Communications peripherals include UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD controllers. The low-frequency subsystem contains an RTC with calendar, alarm, periodic-interrupt, calibration, and clock-output capabilities, plus an independent watchdog timer. The windowed watchdog timer can reset or interrupt the device when not serviced, and general-purpose and advanced timers support counting, capture/compare, PWM, dead-band insertion, fault handling, encoder and Hall inputs, and cross-triggering.

The devices also provide a two-wire serial wire debug interface, a password-protected UART/I2C boot strap loader, and memory-mapped factory identification and trim data. Recommended layout includes VDD decoupling, NRST pull-up and capacitor circuitry, an optional SYSOSC correction resistor, and a VCORE tank capacitor. TI development resources include Code Composer Studio, SysConfig, SDKs, debug tools, and other IDE and cloud-based resources. Mechanical, packaging, orderable, revision, documentation, support, and trademark information are also provided.

At Leicester Crown Court, 68-year-old spiritual healer Komar Uddin denies raping a 19-year-old woman during an exorcism-like ritual at her family home in Leicester. The prosecution alleges that, while her family remained downstairs, he applied oil, sexually touched her and raped her twice. The woman said she initially believed the conduct was part of the ritual but became frightened, was unsure whether to object and was told not to tell anyone. She also said Uddin announced she was pregnant and offered to make the baby “go away” for £200. An internal swab contained Uddin’s DNA. His defence claimed the woman initiated sexual contact, which he refused, and that no sexual activity occurred. Uddin was released on bail in 2015, left the country and was extradited from Germany last November. The trial continues.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020 identifies the company as a large accelerated filer, with common stock trading on Nasdaq under “AMZN.” It reported 503,564,743 shares outstanding as of January 20, 2021, and a non-affiliate market value of $1.174 trillion as of June 30, 2020.

Amazon operates through North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. It serves consumers through online and physical stores, Amazon Prime, devices such as Kindle, Fire, Echo, and Ring, and media content; sellers through store and fulfillment programs; developers and enterprises through AWS cloud services; and content creators through publishing and distribution programs. It also offers advertising services. The company employed approximately 1,298,000 people at year-end and emphasizes customer experience, low prices, selection, convenience, fast delivery, and long-term sustainable free cash flow.

The filing identifies risks from intense competition, international expansion, inventory and demand fluctuations, seller misconduct, intellectual-property claims, foreign exchange, growth-related resource strain, fulfillment and data-center operations, data and system disruptions, personnel and supplier dependence, acquisitions, payment regulation, stock-price volatility, legal proceedings, product liability, taxes, and government-contract requirements. COVID-19 affected Amazon and its business partners; the company modified operations, hired more than 400,000 workers since February 2020, and incurred more than $11.5 billion in related costs during 2020, including $4.0 billion in the fourth quarter.

For 2020, Amazon reported net sales of $386.064 billion, operating income of $22.899 billion, net income of $21.331 billion, diluted earnings per share of $41.83, and operating cash flow of $66.064 billion. Total assets were $321.195 billion and long-term obligations were $101.406 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $84.4 billion, including $23.5 billion held in foreign currencies. Amazon reported $59.6 billion of investing cash outflows, including $35.0 billion of cash capital expenditures, and $1.1 billion of financing cash outflows. At year-end, foreign subsidiaries held $17.2 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities.

Cellphone videos released by prosecutors show Nikolas Cruz announcing plans to become a school shooter, kill at least 20 people with an AR-15, and attack Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School. The undated videos also described his planned route and expressed loneliness, anger and hatred. Surveillance footage showed that Cruz largely followed the plan during the Feb. 14, 2018 shooting, which killed 17 and injured 17, though he arrived earlier than stated.

Cruz, 19, is charged with 17 counts of murder and 17 attempted murder. His attorneys say he would plead guilty if guaranteed life without parole, but prosecutors refuse to waive the death penalty. The videos became public under Florida discovery rules. Cruz previously attended a school for children with emotional disabilities before transferring to Stoneman Douglas, where he was later kicked out. His mother repeatedly called police on him, and he had a history of killing animals and keeping body parts.

The Navy needs 1,000 more officers to man ships operating and under construction, expanded Naval School classes, retirement of impaired senior officers, and continued promotion to maintain efficiency. Lieutenants and junior officers have faced exceptional workloads because of shortages and untrained recruits, though their service has been creditable. Although no immediate foreign conflict is apparent, an efficient navy is essential to preserve peace and avoid disaster.

Post-Office receipts reached $121,848,047.26, a record increase of $10,216,853.87. Rural free delivery had become established policy, with 11,650 routes operating by November 1, 1902, and requests for 10,748 additional routes. Its financial and practical benefits justify further congressional support and expansion.

National irrigation in the arid West had begun, increasing the need for scientific forest protection. Legislation should protect game and wildlife on forest reserves and end the slaughter of animals, including elk.

The passage argues that President Donald Trump is pursuing an energy-based grand strategy to replace the post–World War II liberal order. Rather than organizing world politics around democracies versus autocracies or competing civilizations, Trump appears to favor dividing states into fossil-fuel “carbonites” and post-carbon green powers, with the United States, Russia, and Saudi Arabia leading the former and Germany and China facing marginalization.

Domestically, Trump seeks to restrict renewable energy, withdraw from the Paris climate agreement, revive coal production, reduce vehicle-efficiency requirements, and expand drilling for oil and natural gas. Abroad, his steps have included strengthening ties with Saudi Arabia, weakening NATO and the European Union, and pursuing closer relations with Russia. His Saudi visit produced a $110 billion arms agreement, with potential sales reaching $350 billion, deeper energy cooperation, and joint efforts to counter Iran; the passage also links Saudi military operations in Yemen to civilian deaths, disease, and famine risk. At NATO, Trump initially refused to reaffirm Article 5 and pressed allies to increase defense spending. He later rejected European appeals to remain in the Paris agreement, prioritizing economic benefits to the United States.

The proposed U.S.–Saudi–Russian alliance would coordinate energy, diplomatic, and military relations and oppose common rivals such as Iran. The three countries control about 38% of global oil and 41% of natural-gas production; with associated hydrocarbon states, their network would control roughly 57% of oil output and 59% of gas production. Cooperation between Russia and Saudi Arabia suggests potential progress, although their conflicts over Syria and Iran remain obstacles, while allegations of Russian interference complicate Trump’s effort to improve bilateral relations.

Researchers led by Hebrew University’s Omri Yosef and Michael Berger, with international collaborators, found that blocking the protein Ant2 reprograms T-cell metabolism. The change affected mitochondrial energy pathways, making T cells more active, resilient, faster-replicating and better at recognizing and killing tumor cells in mice. Ant2 could be disabled genetically or with drugs, potentially enabling treatments that strengthen anti-tumor immunity, though further studies and clinical trials are needed.

This study assessed Belgian medical students’ knowledge, attitudes, career aspirations, and exposure to global surgery and explored approaches to curriculum development. An anonymous online survey, developed through a literature review and reviewed by surgeons, students, and InciSioN Belgium, was distributed across seven Belgian universities. Analyses included 304 responses from four universities and examined associations by gender and stage of education using descriptive statistics and odds ratios.

Although 75.3% of respondents wanted greater exposure to global surgery, only 24.7% had previously encountered it, usually through social media. Most were unfamiliar with the field, and global surgery was rarely or never included in required curricula. Nevertheless, 94.3% considered it relevant, and 70% supported more compulsory teaching. Preferred educational opportunities included optional teaching programs, events, clinical internships, and required courses; respondents most wanted to learn about clinical aspects. Knowledge was generally poor: 23.9% correctly identified that five billion people lack access to safe, affordable surgical care, 21.7% knew that approximately 150 million additional procedures were needed annually, and only 12.8% identified the three Bellwether procedures. While 53.3% were interested in surgery, 35.9% in global surgery, and 37.5% in global health, most had little familiarity with global surgery as a career. Leading obstacles included personal or family responsibilities, language barriers, absent career pathways, financial constraints, and insufficient role models and mentorship.

The authors described the findings as the first quantitative assessment of medical students’ knowledge, attitudes, and exposure to global surgery in a European setting. They concluded that curricula should combine pre-clinical seminars, particularly for bachelor’s students, with equitable, bidirectional international clinical internships, pre-departure training, career pathways, and logistical, financial, and mentorship support. Limitations included a non-random sample, participation from only four institutions, possible selection bias, an unvalidated questionnaire, and limited generalizability outside Europe.

Facebook took over two hours to remove live footage of Robert Godwin’s shooting death. Border Angels worker Hugo Castro went missing in Mexico after a Facebook Live plea for help. Georgia congressional candidate Jon Ossoff gained national attention and raised $8.3 million.

Paul Ehrlich’s 1968 *The Population Bomb* framed overpopulation through images of crowded Delhi, raising questions about whether Western fears of developing-world megacities reflect racism as well as demographic reality. Urbanization itself is not driving population growth: city dwellers generally have fewer children than rural residents, while rural-to-urban migration drives urban growth. However, cities create a “consumption bomb,” disproportionately using global materials, food, water and other resources while generating substantial sewage and household waste. Their environmental impacts extend beyond city limits through their dependence on surrounding regions for resources and labor.

WebRTC can expose users’ real IP addresses despite VPNs. On March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPN and proxy providers: 20 leaked users’ IPs (16.13%) and 101 concealed them. The passage lists leaking providers, recommends testing for leaks, and advises disabling WebRTC manually or with an add-on if detected. It also ranks VPN services for WebRTC privacy and notes that most browsers enable WebRTC by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer.

Global equities declined Monday as the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reached 2.998%, nearing a level investors see as a potential tipping point amid concerns about government debt supply and inflation. Falling commodity prices after the U.S. hinted it might ease sanctions on Rusal weighed on materials stocks, with aluminum down 8.7%, Alcoa down 13.51%, and gold down 0.8%. The dollar rose to a seven-week high, while the euro and yen weakened. U.S. indexes were nearly flat ahead of earnings from more than 180 S&P 500 companies expected to report their strongest first-quarter profit gains in seven years.

Caterpillar’s board kept its quarterly dividend at $0.77 per share, marking the seventh consecutive quarter without an increase. Its 3.25% yield remains above the S&P 500 and 10-year Treasury yields, while dividends have increased for 23 consecutive years. Goldman Sachs added the stock to its “conviction buy” list, citing increased mining capital spending, and set a $120 target, 26% above its roughly $95 share price.

Caterpillar shares have gained nearly 20% over nine months amid expectations that U.S. infrastructure spending, economic improvement, higher oil prices, and easing Asian growth concerns could benefit the company. However, optimism is already reflected in a valuation near its 52-week high, while a federal tax investigation, China’s slowdown, and possible failure of Trump’s infrastructure plan pose risks. In 2016, revenue and EBITDA fell 18% and 39%, while excess cash flow after capital spending and dividends declined to $881 million. Caterpillar expects further revenue and profit declines and advises “prudently cautious” guidance; the author urges investors to exercise caution.

EchoingECG is a probabilistic student–teacher framework for learning ECHO-informed ECG representations. It addresses the complexity and temporal variability of ECG signals, limited one-to-one mappings in deterministic contrastive learning, and scarcity of ECG data labeled with ECHO outcomes. Using PCME++, the model learns mean and variance in latent embeddings to support uncertainty-aware, many-to-many alignment among ECG windows, text, and ECHO frames. ECHO-CLIP serves as a teacher, distilling cardiac information from ECHO data into ECG representations through ECHO–ECG and ECG–text bindings. The approach captures structural and functional ECHO insights, reduces reliance on large annotated datasets, and enables uncertainty-aware evaluation of downstream tasks.

Henry L. Stimson argued that raising Pacific territorial adjustments, including trusteeships, would provoke distrust, draw attention to U.S. aims, and poison discussions. He recommended deferring and avoiding the issue until the war progressed further and Russia participated in the Pacific war, while noting that trusteeships could not be discussed satisfactorily without fuller knowledge of the territories involved. The passage cites the Cairo Declaration’s pledge that the Allies sought no territorial gain and that Japan would be stripped of Pacific islands seized or occupied since 1914.

At an informal meeting of American diplomatic chiefs on January 26, 1945, Under Secretary Grew urged careful study of international organization and the inter-American system before the Mexico City conference. He called for exchanging views on the Dumbarton Oaks proposals, explaining U.S. reasoning, and considering ways to strengthen the inter-American system after the war. Grew said Dumbarton Oaks was promising but incomplete, and that history showed superficial efforts to preserve peace had failed, sometimes requiring all available measures, including force.

On April 20, 2022, Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2022. The results were furnished through the First Quarter 2022 Update, attached as Exhibit 99.1, and were not deemed filed for specified securities laws. Exhibit 104 contains the inline XBRL cover-page data file. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Chris King, 57, watched Leeds Rhinos beat Widnes Vikings 42–22 on his first visit to Headingley Carnegie Stadium, where he was applauded at half-time. After losing both hands in an industrial accident, he received the UK’s first bilateral hand transplant from Professor Simon Kay at Leeds General Infirmary.
Crocs’ design patent for its molded-clog shoe was rejected because another company filed a similar patent first. The company plans to appeal while closing 160 stores amid revenue declines.

The study developed and tested a streamlined clinical workflow for analyzing and reporting optical genome mapping (OGM) data in myeloid neoplasms using Bionano Access, Solve, and Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA). Ten retrospective cases—nine acute myeloid leukemia and one myelodysplastic syndrome/neoplasm—were each reviewed 5–6 times by independent technologist-director teams. Technologists used automated decision-tree analysis, guideline-based panels, custom views, and copy-number and allelic-imbalance tracks; directors finalized classifications, selected reportable findings, and generated ISCN summaries and reports.

OGM detected all standard-of-care findings. Six cases were positive by both methods and four were negative by both. Sentinel AML variants were consistently classified as Tier 1A. OGM identified additional findings in five of six positive cases, including large copy-number losses, trisomy 8, small deletions involving IKZF1 and SETD2, and a KMT2A::MLLT10 fusion. Variation remained in the tiering and reporting of nonsentinel variants. Average technologist review time was 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases. The authors concluded that OGM with VIA can improve cytogenomic resolution, streamline reporting, reduce labor, and support more standardized interpretation.

Digital accessibility encompasses inclusive access to digital infrastructure, content, services, and devices for people with differing abilities and needs, with the goal of equal opportunities in education, employment, and information exchange. The study conducts a bibliometric analysis of research on digital accessibility, particularly in education, to identify trends, gaps, collaborations, influential works, and future research priorities.

Using the queries “Digital Accessibility” and “Digital Accessibility” AND Education across Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC for 2013–2024, the researchers obtained 1,544 and 924 records, respectively, and analyzed the data with VOSviewer 1.6.20. Publications on digital accessibility increased from 12 in 2013 to 502 in 2024, with rapid growth after 2019 and during the post-pandemic period. Education-related publications rose from four in 2013 to 339 in 2024. Scopus contained most records across the analyses.

Journal articles were the most common publication type, followed by conference papers and book chapters. The leading research areas were Digital Accessibility and Inclusion, Education and Social Sciences, and Computer Science and Engineering Sciences. English dominated the education-related literature, while higher education accounted for most studies classified by educational level. The United States, United Kingdom, and Spain produced the most publications.

Citation analysis identified Gorriz (2023), Kuc-Czarnecka (2020), and Bong (2024) as highly cited documents, while Chen Weiqin was the most cited author and had the strongest author-network links. The United States and England led country-level citations, although countries such as Poland showed high citation impact relative to their output. The findings indicate that a small number of documents, authors, and countries strongly shape the field, while broader international collaboration remains limited.

The authors conclude that digital transformation and COVID-19 increased the importance of accessible education and positioned digital accessibility as an issue of inclusion and equality. Future work should strengthen cooperation, produce higher-quality research, support legal frameworks, and prioritize computer literacy and motivation for students with disabilities. Ethics approval was granted by Gazi University.

A community backed St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School headteacher Mark Ryan after the Gazette inaccurately reported that he took a two-week term-time holiday to attend a wedding abroad. Ryan had governors’ approval for a three-day leave under the school’s exceptional-circumstances policy and had not spoken to the parent who made the allegation. The report also wrongly claimed he said a pupil’s mother would be fined for taking her child out during term time. Ryan said the misinformation caused distress, while governors, staff, parents and others rallied to support him. Chair of governors Gary Wilson praised Ryan’s commitment to the school and children, and parish priest Michael Keogh said the community’s support reflected its esteem for Ryan and his family.

The Shippers Group celebrated the September 15 ribbon cutting of its new 540,000-square-foot distribution facility in Austell, Georgia. The multi-client warehouse serves food, consumer goods, automotive and contract packaging businesses, offering warehousing, transportation, packaging and e-commerce fulfillment. Founded in 1901 and headquartered in Dallas, the company has expanded to 11 U.S. locations since 1970. The opening increased its Georgia warehouse space to 1.5 million square feet.
Apple nears $1 trillion in market value as Amazon closes the gap, now about 10%, or $85 billion, after Amazon’s value rose $260 billion in 2018.

After missing the playoffs, the Mets are overhauling their coaching staff despite a $429 million payroll. Manager Carlos Mendoza will return, but pitching coach Jeremy Hefner will be replaced. Hitting coaches Jeremy Barnes and Eric Chavez and third-base coach Mike Sarbaugh are leaving; bench coach John Gibbons resigned, and catching coach Glenn Sherlock is retiring. Pitching and defense were the Mets’ biggest problems as they went 38-55 over their final 93 games after being 45-24 in June. The offense also drew criticism following a $765 million, 15-year offseason signing. Assistant pitching coach Desi Druschel and bullpen coach José Rosado can speak with other teams, while first-base coach Antoan Richardson, strategy coach Danny Barnes and assistant Rafael Fernandez have been invited back. Additional headlines preview MLB playoff matchups, odds and fantasy rankings.

Global stocks fell Tuesday, reversing early gains after the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield crossed 3% for the first time in four years; the two-year yield hit 2.5% for the first time since September 2008. The Dow lost 0.19%, the S&P 500 0.24% and the Nasdaq 0.73%. Alphabet fell 4.93% on surging costs despite strong ad sales, and chipmaker AMS slumped 9.64%. U.S. earnings began strongly, with 77.1% of 118 S&P 500 reporters beating expectations. Brent crude rose above $75 a barrel, its highest since November 2014, on OPEC cuts, strong demand and possible U.S. sanctions on Iran.

The Best 6 Months Timing Model is an active strategy created by Yale Hirsch that can be applied across asset classes. It follows model-generated entry and exit signals rather than remaining continuously invested, aiming to reduce market exposure and risk. A 16-year backtest uses an equally weighted portfolio of stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities, represented by diversified, liquid ETFs with long histories. Stocks have historically delivered the highest returns; bonds reduce volatility and drawdowns; REITs and commodities provide diversification through lower correlations with traditional assets. The strategy’s maximum drawdown was -27.27%, compared with -47.77% for buy-and-hold. Hirsch founded the Hirsch Organization and created the Stock Trader’s Almanac, which has documented seasonal market trends and phenomena since 1968.

Home Capital Group is negotiating with Canadian and international banks for a roughly C$2 billion syndicated loan to replace a costly emergency credit line. RBC, BMO and TD are among potential lenders, though not all six major Canadian banks are expected to participate. The company has faced 95% withdrawals from high-interest savings accounts since March 27, accelerating after the Ontario Securities Commission accused it of misleading investors about its mortgage underwriting; Home Capital denies the allegations. Withdrawals have slowed since mid-May, and the loan terms under discussion remain uncertain.

The speaker condemns the Carter Administration’s neglect of American military strength and Secretary of State Muskie’s warning that rearmament could trigger an arms race. He argues that Soviet military spending and strategic forces exceed America’s, while Soviet and Cuban influence in Africa, Soviet advances in Afghanistan, and Soviet-backed conflict in Central America threaten U.S. resource security and place Soviet forces near the Arabian Gulf. Given that the U.S. is self-sufficient in only five of 27 strategically important minerals, he considers a strong military margin of safety essential to deterrence and peace.

He insists that peace must not require surrender, humiliation, or the loss of freedom and justice, citing Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, and Soviet-dominated Czechoslovakia. He defends America’s role in Vietnam, honors its veterans, and warns that fighting without the means and determination to prevail creates “no-win” wars and erodes credibility. He credits post–World War II U.S. military superiority with deterring aggression, supporting allied recovery, turning former enemies into allies, and preserving peace from Berlin to Cuba.

The Dodgers opened their NL Division Series with a 9-5 win over the Arizona Diamondbacks in Los Angeles. Justin Turner hit a three-run homer and drove in five runs, tying a Dodgers postseason record, while Yasiel Puig and Corey Seager each drove in two runs. Clayton Kershaw allowed four homers but earned his first playoff victory at Dodger Stadium, striking out seven over 6 1/3 innings. Arizona starter Taijuan Walker lasted one inning as the Dodgers’ first five batters reached base. A.J. Pollock, J.D. Martinez, Ketel Marte and Jeff Mathis homered for the Diamondbacks. Los Angeles leads the series 1-0 after posting 104 wins and a fifth consecutive NL West title. Game 2 pits Rich Hill against Robbie Ray.

The paper examines the normative assumption that educational disparities caused by social background should be corrected because they are unfair. It argues that luck egalitarianism justifies this aim by distinguishing brute luck—circumstances beyond individual control—from option luck arising from individual choices. The theory seeks to reduce brute-luck inequalities while retaining individual responsibility.

Two critiques of luck egalitarianism are considered. Anderson’s harshness objection holds that its strict distinction between brute and option luck can leave individuals bearing severe consequences for their choices, as in the case of a musician prevented from returning to education by poverty. The humiliation objection argues that compensation policies may undermine dignity by labeling recipients as deficient or requiring humiliating disclosures.

The paper responds to the harshness objection through fresh start and sufficiency. Fresh-start theories support opportunities for people to reconsider past choices, although concerns include moral hazard and redistribution costs. Dynamic luck egalitarianism suggests that responsibility can diminish over time, which may counter the Matthew effect by which educational inequalities widen. Sufficiency requires basic resources or educational thresholds to be secured regardless of responsibility, but determining the threshold is controversial and may leave achievement gaps above it. A combined approach would first meet basic needs and then apply luck egalitarianism to remaining inequalities.

To address humiliation, the paper adds respect as a value beyond fairness, noting that eligibility assessments and support practices can stigmatize disadvantaged learners. It recommends empirical attention to classroom humiliation and possible practices such as proficiency-based classes.

The paper concludes that research on educational disparities should assess not only fairness but also opportunities for fresh starts, educational sufficiency, respect, relational capacities, and the practical effects of educational practices on students’ dignity.

Local social influencers can help businesses overcome limited social-media reach by creating or sharing content about them. Credible local influencers include food bloggers or critics, food and pizza enthusiasts, community leaders, local media personalities, entertainers, and attraction representatives.

The bankruptcy court denied East Tennessee Equity, Ltd.’ and Theodore A. Erck’s motion to dismiss Thomas E. DuVoisin’s fraudulent-conveyance action under 11 U.S.C. § 548. Southern Industrial Banking Corporation’s Chapter 11 reorganization plan transferred approximately $26 million in loans and preference and fraudulent-transfer claims to a Creditors’ Liquidation Trust, whose trustee was authorized to enforce them.

The court rejected the argument that recoveries would not benefit SIBC’s creditors because impaired unsecured creditors received stock or rights to purchase stock in the federally insured successor-in-interest. Recovering fraudulent transfers would strengthen the successor and increase the value of those creditor ownership rights. The court also relied on § 1123(b), which permits plans to authorize a debtor, trustee, or estate representative to retain and enforce claims.

Applying *Centennial Industries*, the court held that preference or fraudulent-transfer recovery is permissible when creditors benefit in any respect, even if their fixed distributions do not increase. It distinguished *Texas Consumer Financial*, *Sapolin Paints*, and *Whiteford Plastics* as inapplicable because those cases did not involve the plan-authorized enforcement at issue or concerned benefits sought solely for a stranger to the bankruptcy. Permitting the action would benefit impaired creditors, while rejecting it would give defendants a windfall. The court also noted that the district court had already held SIBC eligible for Chapter 11 and that subsequent changes did not bar the trustee from pursuing preference claims belonging to the trust.

The IMF urged China to prioritize financial stability over regional growth and employment objectives, which it said had contributed to rapid credit growth and local-government debt. It recommended stronger regulatory coordination, a financial stability sub-committee involving the central bank and three regulators, and more resources for the banking watchdog. The IMF also warned that high credit levels and rapidly expanding wealth-management products could become systemic risks. Although Chinese banks met Basel requirements, the IMF said they should hold more liquid assets and increase capital buffers. Stress tests of 33 banks under severe domestic and external shocks projected nonperforming loans rising to 9.1% from 1.5% and a capital shortfall equal to 2.5% of GDP, with joint-stock and city commercial banks widely undercapitalized. The central bank disputed the tests’ comprehensiveness but maintained that China was capable of managing financial risks.

**Hardin v. White** (Iowa; appeal from Keokuk Circuit Court). Action to enjoin an execution sale of real estate in Keokuk; decree for plaintiff; defendant, White, the execution creditor, appeals.

Two questions were decided:

1. **Injunction bond.** Under Code §§ 3396, 3397, an injunction restraining collection of a judgment requires a bond for double the judgment. This rule does not apply where the injunction seeks only to restrain the sale of specific property under a general execution. Here the execution was general and the action sought merely to enjoin the sale of a particular parcel, so the court properly overruled the motion to increase the bond.

2. **Sale of the right of redemption.** A foreclosure decree of $3,690.31 (10 percent interest) and $743.18 (8 percent) covered liens on White's property, with a single special execution awarded. White took execution for only the 10 percent item, sold and bid in the property, and then took a general execution for the balance, levied upon the statutory right of redemption. The court held he had exhausted his remedy under that decree as to the property, since the debtor's protection lies in the right of redemption, which successive levies, sales, and costs would render nearly worthless. *Barnes v. Cavanagh*, 53 Iowa 27, was distinguished; *Clayton v. Ellis*, 50 Iowa 590, and *Hayden v. Smith*, 58 Iowa 285, cited.

**On rehearing:** the property had in fact been sold to one Dickerson rather than bid in by the creditor, which was immaterial. White held two decrees—one from a chattel mortgage foreclosure, one from a real estate mortgage foreclosure—both recognizing the same claim purchased from Minnie E. Hardin. The court treated the two decrees as identical for the same indebtedness, since form cannot outweigh substance: the debt may be collected but once, and satisfaction of one satisfies both. A small difference in balances (insurance paid) was immaterial.

The judgment of the circuit court was **affirmed**.

Chrissy Teigen spoke openly about living with anxiety and postpartum depression, including feeling shaky and believing everyone was watching her. She was diagnosed shortly after the birth of her daughter, Luna, and experienced PPD for four months, from September to December 2016. PPD can involve depressive symptoms lasting more than two weeks, including insomnia, appetite loss, irritability, and difficulty bonding with a baby. Teigen takes an antidepressant and, despite difficult days, wants to expand her family. The article encourages those affected to seek support from health-care or mental-health resources.

They criticize students’ silence and adults’ failure to intervene, noting that bullying can escalate on social media through abusive messages. A March 19, 2001 email assembled reports on California’s electricity crisis and related energy issues. San Diego’s air-pollution board allowed the former Encina/Cabrillo power plant to increase nitrogen-oxide emissions, though greater use of fuel oil could worsen ozone pollution. FERC ordered six wholesalers to justify or refund $55 million in February sales above $430 per megawatt-hour during Stage 3 shortages, following a $69 million January order. Suppliers defended their rates, while state officials and consumer advocates said the action was inadequate.

The state Department of Water Resources bought electricity on behalf of cash-strapped utilities, spending about $350 million weekly, while critics questioned its inexperienced traders and secretive contracts. PG&E and Southern California Edison accumulated $13.8 billion in debts, and creditors threatened involuntary bankruptcy proceedings, complicating state plans to purchase their transmission grids. PG&E also reassigned customers in its blackout-exempt “Block 50,” moving 810,000 out and 690,000 in. Automakers, manufacturers, and the Westlands Water District invoked the energy crisis in policy disputes involving electric vehicles, overtime rules, and Trinity River flows. An editorial criticized political focus on out-of-state generators, arguing that California should prevent market gouging while participating in a Western power market and purchasing power based on price rather than corporate headquarters.

After returning to school part-time for journalism in their 40s, the author completed a bachelor’s degree by transferring credits from an earlier associate degree. They embraced journalism’s shift toward digital storytelling, gained new technology skills, and remained open to changing career possibilities. Academically, they rediscovered a love of learning and confidence in their abilities, including passing a statistics course. Participation in the school paper, magazine, blog, radio station, Honors Society, and campus events enriched their experience. The author also described earning the degree as reclaiming potential lost after bullying in junior high and healing an old wound. They are now pursuing graduate study in digital storytelling and working as a research assistant to respected professors.

Sickle cell disease (SCD), or sickle cell anemia, is an inherited disorder that causes abnormal, sickle-shaped red blood cells. These cells contain abnormal hemoglobin, do not last as long as healthy cells, and can block blood flow. SCD affects people of all backgrounds, although prevalence is highest among people of sub-Saharan African descent, and it affects approximately 100,000 people in the United States. Symptoms include pain crises, acute chest syndrome, anemia, jaundice, swollen hands and feet, organ problems, serious infections, leg sores, strokes, and eye, bone, joint, heart, and lung complications. Diagnosis relies on blood testing and newborn screening in the United States; prenatal testing can determine whether a fetus has SCD. Management includes regular screenings and checkups, vaccinations and preventive antibiotics for children, pain treatment, medications that increase fetal hemoglobin, and blood transfusions for some complications. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only permanent treatment but is generally reserved for severe cases because of its risks. Quitting smoking and avoiding secondhand smoke are important because smoking increases pain episodes and acute chest syndrome. A balanced diet, limited alcohol, adequate rest, and regular exercise may also improve health and quality of life.

Coach Quenneville described the playoff series as a relentless battle and praised both teams’ effort. He said he hopes Toews will be ready for the next game and noted that chemistry among Toews, Bicks and other teammates has produced important goals. The coach said the team will manage minutes, keep all four lines fresh and approach each game as if it could last 60 minutes. He praised the veteran leadership group’s businesslike approach and the coaching staff’s trust that players would respond well in high-pressure games. AppLovin shares plunged after Bloomberg reported that the SEC is investigating whether the mobile advertising company violated agreements governing targeted ads. University of Exeter researchers found that the Fal oyster fishery’s centuries-old, sail-powered methods are inefficient but crucial to preventing overfishing and sustaining stocks. Motorizing the fleet could increase fishing activity ninefold. GPS tracking and onboard observations showed sail-hauled dredging is less effective than mechanized methods. Disease and motorization threaten the fishery, while pollution, overfishing, and non-native Pacific oysters threaten the native European flat oyster.

Gallup found 44% of Americans believed Donald Trump could prevent major scandals, versus 74% for Barack Obama and 77% for George W. Bush upon taking office. Trump’s confidence deficits across all categories ranged from 15 to 32 percentage points, amid low government trust.

The passage argues that wealth-building portfolios should emphasize stocks because they offer the highest long-term returns among major asset classes. Citing Jeremy Siegel’s 1801–2021 study, it reports that $1 invested in stocks grew to $2,334,920, versus $2,163 in bonds; bills and gold performed worse. It selects liquid, diversified stock ETFs with long histories, ranks them by return-to-drawdown ratio, and proposes a moderately aggressive allocation intended to limit crisis drawdowns. The article stresses that drawdowns are not necessarily permanent losses and advises patience rather than selling during declines. A backtest examines the portfolio’s equity, underwater, monthly, annual, and overall performance.

Candidates need at least two years of commercial newsroom weather reporting or multimedia journalism, strong forecasting, editing, shooting, digital and social-media skills, and an energetic, engaging personality. Heikin Ashi is a Japanese-derived candlestick charting technique that smooths price movements to highlight trends or consolidation phases. Unlike standard candlesticks, which show actual open, high, low, and close prices, Heikin Ashi uses artificial values: haClose is the candle’s total average price, haOpen is a three-period exponential moving average of the prior haClose, and haHigh and haLow are calculated from the actual high and low relative to haOpen. The resulting bars omit price gaps, reduce apparent color changes, and are delayed, making them unsuitable for direct execution at their displayed prices.

The passage presents a long-only, monthly S&P 500 trend-following strategy backtested from 1960 onward. It buys when haClose crosses above haOpen and sells when it crosses below. The reported win rate is 49.4%, with a favorable asymmetric profit/loss distribution and generally strong performance metrics. An ADX-filtered mean-reversion variant produced a 5.27% CAGR with 5% market exposure; consumer staples performed better, but average profit per trade was only 0.22%.

Heikin Ashi can be customized by changing the open-price averaging period to filter more or less noise. Overall, it is presented as a useful lagging indicator for trend following, particularly on longer time frames, rather than as a predictive price representation or a direct replacement for standard candlesticks.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended December 30, 2017 reported net sales of $88.293 billion, up 13% from $78.351 billion in the prior-year quarter. Gross margin was $33.912 billion, or 38.4%, versus 38.5% previously, and operating income was $26.274 billion. Net income rose to $20.065 billion from $17.891 billion, while diluted earnings per share increased to $3.89 from $3.36.

Sales increased across all geographic segments: Americas rose 10%, Europe 14%, Greater China 11%, Japan 26%, and Rest of Asia Pacific 17%. By product, iPhone sales increased 13% to $61.576 billion, iPad sales rose 6%, Services increased 18% to $8.471 billion, and Other Products rose 36%; Mac sales declined 5%. The company attributed iPhone and iPad growth primarily to higher average selling prices, Services growth to licensing and App Store sales, and Mac’s decline to lower unit sales.

At December 30, 2017, Apple reported $406.794 billion of assets, $266.595 billion of liabilities, and $140.199 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $27.491 billion, with short- and long-term marketable securities of $49.662 billion and $207.944 billion, respectively. Operating activities generated $28.293 billion of cash, while investing and financing activities used $13.590 billion and $7.501 billion. Apple repurchased $10.095 billion of stock, paid $3.339 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents, and issued $7.0 billion of term debt.

The U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act lowered the federal statutory rate from 35% to 21% effective January 1, 2018. Apple recorded a provisional $2.6 billion tax estimate and replaced a $36.1 billion deferred foreign-income tax liability with a provisional $38.0 billion tax payable related to deemed repatriation. The first-quarter effective tax rate was 25.8%.

Apple also disclosed €13 billion plus €1 billion of potential interest under the European Commission’s Irish State Aid Decision, which it is contesting and anticipates funding through escrow in 2018 pending appeals. Other disclosures addressed derivative hedges, debt, share-based compensation, supply and manufacturing concentration, lease and purchase obligations, and the Samsung litigation, for which a new damages trial was ordered.

An October 22, 2001 compilation reported that Enron’s shares fell 21% to $20.65 after the company disclosed that the SEC requested information about related-party transactions involving LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, partnerships organized and formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron said it was cooperating, described the request as an informal inquiry, and maintained that auditors, attorneys and the board had reviewed and approved the arrangements and disclosed them in SEC filings.

Enron reported roughly $35 million in partnership-related costs, plans to repurchase 55 million shares, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. It also recorded a third-quarter loss of approximately $618 million to $638 million following $1.01 billion in charges and write-downs. Investors expressed concerns about conflicts of interest, Enron’s credibility, credit ratings, and the potential cost or dilution from unwinding affiliated entities. Fastow reportedly received more than $7 million in management fees and about $4 million in capital increases in 2000 from an investment of nearly $3 million.

A shareholder filed a derivative lawsuit alleging that Enron’s board breached its fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to operate the partnerships. A separate securities class action covering purchasers from July 13 through October 16 alleged that Enron and certain officers and directors misrepresented and concealed material facts, artificially inflating Enron’s stock price.

Broader market coverage showed major indexes rising on strong earnings despite anthrax concerns, while U.S. leading economic indicators declined 0.5% in September. A separate article reported that UniPrime signed a letter of intent for a partial interest in an Enron Wind ground lease covering more than 3,000 acres in California’s Tehachapi Valley, with projected annual revenue of $96 million.

Bonds were mixed, the dollar strengthened, and the Conference Board’s leading-indicators index fell 0.5% in September, its largest monthly decline since January 1996.

Enron shares fell 21% to $20.65 after the company disclosed that the SEC had requested information about related-party transactions involving limited partnerships organized by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron said the SEC inquiry was informal, that it was cooperating, and that auditors, attorneys and the board had reviewed and approved the arrangements, which were disclosed in SEC filings. The article argues that gold’s strong Friday rally and the dollar’s decline were not matched by meaningful gains in silver, platinum, or mining stocks. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF closed below its April high for a third consecutive day, confirming what the author calls a bearish setup and diverging from the usual pattern of gold stocks outperforming early in precious-metals rallies. For FHA loans, married couples are assessed jointly: lenders pull both spouses’ credit and count a non-borrowing spouse’s debt in the borrower’s debt-to-income ratio, whether buying or refinancing. This can reduce borrowing capacity. The rule begins upon legal marriage, not while single or engaged. One spouse must sign a quitclaim deed at escrow when the other applies for an FHA loan on a sole and separate property. A conventional loan may avoid the credit requirement.

Mack, arrested April 20 on sex-trafficking and forced-labor charges, describes JNess as her most gratifying work and says no one is punished or told they are bad.
