Additional suggestions include focusing on real-world subjects, avoiding conclusions that merely restate the thesis, checking spelling, using readability and mind-mapping tools, and recognizing that lack of interest, time, energy, or a suitable environment can hinder writing.

The Trap play is a quick-hitting downhill running scheme that kicks out an interior defensive lineman. It can work with either a powerful fullback or a smaller, dynamic tailback, especially when combined with Wing-T deception. Its speed gives defenders little time to identify the ball carrier, while angle blocks make it suitable for smaller offensive linemen. Its main weakness is that defenses squeezing the interior gaps can limit the offensive line’s ability to climb to linebackers. The passage details assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts and two variations: Gun Trey Same-Side Trap RPO, giving the quarterback a passing option, and Wing-T Trap, which uses Buck Sweep action to pressure defenders.
Hillview Middle School will host an all-ages outdoor family movie night April 27 at 7:30 p.m., showing “Sing.” Proceeds benefit LLS and JDRF.

The President reviewed U.S. foreign policy, emphasizing national unity, cooperation with Congress, stronger alliances, continued support for friends and commitments, and sustained military strength. He acknowledged earlier foreign-policy setbacks while citing improved relations with Europe, Japan, China, and the Soviet Union, as well as diplomatic initiatives in the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa.

The most urgent issue was the collapse of the 1973 Paris accords and renewed North Vietnamese offensive in South Vietnam. The President called on Hanoi to halt military operations and honor the agreement, and urged all signatories to enforce the accords. He requested $722 million in emergency military assistance and $250 million for economic and humanitarian aid, with congressional action by April 19. He also sought authority to use U.S. forces to protect and evacuate Americans and endangered Vietnamese. In Cambodia, he described the government’s request for food, ammunition, and weapons while warning that assistance might soon be too late.

The President also reaffirmed U.S. commitments to Japan and South Korea, sought stronger cooperation among NATO allies, and called on Congress to lift the arms embargo against Turkey and consider assistance to Greece. He requested changes to trade restrictions that harmed OPEC members including Ecuador, Venezuela, Nigeria, and Indonesia. In the Middle East, he pledged to continue U.S. mediation efforts, support negotiations between Israel and Egypt, and reconvene the Geneva conference.

Regarding the Soviet Union, he advocated firmness, restraint, and continued strategic-arms negotiations while seeking revision of the 1974 trade law because its effects on Soviet relations and emigration had been counterproductive. He affirmed the Shanghai Communiqué with China and planned a visit to reinforce their developing relationship.

Finally, he identified hunger, world trade and resources, oceans, technology, the environment, energy, intelligence, and defense as major challenges. He urged domestic action to reduce dependence on imported energy, called for discreet congressional oversight of intelligence activities, and warned that significant defense-budget reductions would endanger national security.

Gary Kleck and Marc Gertz’s 1993 survey, published in 1995, estimated that Americans used guns defensively more than 2.2 million times annually. The passage says three subsequent CDC studies produced similar results, estimating about 2.5 million past-year defensive gun uses and suggesting defensive uses occurred roughly 3.6 times as often as offensive gun use. According to the author, the CDC never published these findings. Former Department of Defense researcher Dean Weingarten noted that the surveys were conducted during the Clinton administration, when their results could have conflicted with the administration’s gun-control agenda; Kleck did not accuse the CDC of misconduct. The passage argues that the episode challenges government transparency, weakens a common anti-gun argument, and underscores the importance of educating the public about gun-control and gun-ownership issues, including through John Birch Society programs.

Studies cited by Cosmos found evidence on biodegradable plastic bags’ manufacture, end-of-life and environmental value inconsistent and often poorly defined, suggesting little support for them as environmentally helpful alternatives to conventional carrier bags.

The passage documents AGESA/AGESATM host-BIOS integration and UEFI porting requirements. The 16-bit real-mode binary module is deprecated but retained for 32-bit protected-mode, flat-address operation. Host code enters the module through a Bridge and function-number Dispatcher; reverse call-outs use a Call-Out port and Router to invoke host BIOS procedures. The host must establish a valid stack, populate the standard header and configuration block, and use published entry identifiers from AMD.H. AGESA retains the 16 most recent events in a circular log; all reported errors except SUCCESS and BOUNDS_CHK generate logged events.

UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases using 16-, 32-, and 64-bit execution. AGESA core code is organized into libraries and build targets using MASM, Microsoft Macro Assembler, and Microsoft C/C++ tools. Platform options are customized through `<plat>Options.c`; build integration uses UEFI control files and environment variables such as `AGESA_ROOT` and `AGESA_OptsDir`. Addendum files are reference examples rather than build inputs.

UEFI PEI modules perform early processor initialization, post-reset and memory initialization, and warm-reset coordination while publishing processor, memory, and reset-status PPIs and HOBs. DXE performs late initialization, generates platform data tables, and publishes `AgesaDxeProtocol`. A separate driver controls processor-GPU VGA decoding. Build methods include indirect binary modules and integrated source builds.

Host services include structure creation and release, event-log retrieval, MMIO range mapping, DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI address queries, execution-cache sizing, current-core identification, and mapping addresses to DIMM locations. Initialization entry points perform minimal reset initialization and cache allocation, full processor setup, memory initialization and transition to post-memory operation, artifact relocation into host-controlled memory, graphics configuration, and late ACPI/DMI table generation. S3 procedures save silicon and processor state before suspend and restore or reinitialize components during resume. All applicable calls require an established stack. x86-64 CAR procedures allocate per-core pre-memory stacks, configure MTRRs, and later disable CAR; host code must not alter relevant stack, cache-control, SS, or ESP state during CAR use. AArch64 systems using the PSP do not use these stack and early macros.

Mitsui & Co’s April-December net profit rose 64% to a record ¥376.8 billion, prompting it to raise its full-year forecast to ¥440 billion amid higher iron ore and coking coal prices. Itochu’s profit rose 19%, but its forecast remained unchanged. Sojitz increased its forecast 12% to ¥56 billion.

At Norfolk General Hospital, a man says his wife waited from 5:15 p.m. until 11:45 p.m. to see a doctor. He criticizes administrators—not doctors or nurses—for not calling in more help despite empty beds. Election-related letters question the timing of new long-term-care bed funding, argue seniors in long-term care should pay no medication fees, and credit Brant County’s development to independent farmers now in or awaiting care.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for dynamically replacing video content while retaining or reproducing overlays generated by an intermediate device, such as a set-top box. A client device identifies the set-top box using EDID data, user input, IP-address lookup, or menu matching and stores the resulting device identifier.

The client device fingerprints regions of received video and queries a video identification system containing reference fingerprints. The system matches query and reference fingerprints using quantized indexes, distance measurements, and varying fingerprint block sizes to identify the underlying content. The client can then retrieve replacement content, such as local commercials, alternative programming, or a version with different content ratings.

Templates associated with identified set-top boxes define how their overlays are displayed. These include picture-in-picture windows, cropped regions, superimposed menus, blended areas, position and size, transparency, and playback speed. Templates may be created manually or programmatically by identifying known and unknown video regions and analyzing changes across frames. The client matches incoming frames against templates using pixel comparisons, color-distance calculations, cross-correlation, optical character recognition, or other techniques.

A video overlay module uses matching results and masks to pass through selected set-top-box information while replacing other portions with replacement video. Replacement footage may be cropped, resized, repositioned, alpha-blended, or played at a rate matching the incoming stream. Semi-transparent overlays may be reconstructed from pixel differences between the received and original video, transferred to replacement content, or reproduced using stored transparency, color, and text information. Background pixels may be filtered while foreground text or icons are preserved.

The system detects channel or content-source changes by comparing fingerprints and templates, temporarily stops replacement when other content is selected, and resumes replacement when the original content returns. Playback speed can be inferred from overlay symbols or fingerprint sequences and applied to the replacement stream. A replacement content server supplies video and templates, while databases map set-top-box identifiers to template types, images, bitmaps, and coordinates for picture-in-picture, menu-overlay, and blended-menu regions.

The hockey team remains confident it can win Saturday and turn the series, crediting coach Peter DeBoer’s leadership and a rookie’s strong performance. After struggling to establish momentum or score a first goal in three games, they finally earned a win and hope to build on it. Their power play generated opportunities, but the opponent’s goaltending and penalty killing were strong. The veteran team believes it can continue competing for the Stanley Cup, but must end the opponent’s streak to avoid elimination.

KDKA-TV and WPXI-TV initially reported, citing police sources, that surveillance video showed Antwon Rose II firing a gun before he was shot and killed by East Pittsburgh police officer Michael Rosfeld on June 19, and that gunshot residue was found on his hands. Allegheny County Police Superintendent Coleman McDonough said the video did not show Rose firing and the residue claim was false. WTAE-TV did not report the claims.

When prosecutors announced homicide charges against Rosfeld on June 27, a district attorney spokesman accused local media of defying an earlier correction and spreading wrong information. KDKA retracted its report and apologized, citing incorrect sources. WPXI initially denied intentionally spreading false information and did not apologize on-air, but issued a written apology June 28, saying the video did not show Rose firing and acknowledging harm to his family and community.

The New Pittsburgh Courier criticized both stations’ failures and questioned the unverified sources, the alleged video, and their possible connection to Rosfeld or East Pittsburgh police.

Kinder Morgan rose after Canada agreed to buy a $3.4 billion pipeline. Bank of America fell as interest rates dropped, while Petrobras fell amid diesel subsidies during a truckers’ strike. ZTO, Booz Allen, American Woodmark, KB Home and American Water Works rose.

Costa has helped drive Britain’s coffee-shop boom and grown into the world’s second-largest coffee chain behind Starbucks. Its sales reached £3.4 billion in 2016, it operates more than 2,000 UK shops, and further expansion could add 6,000 worldwide stores over the next 30 years.

Costa’s new Basildon, Essex, roastery was selected for its proximity to Tilbury Docks and London. It quadruples annual roasting capacity from 11,000 to 45,000 tonnes, enough to produce 2.1 billion cups. Robotic packing is expected to improve productivity by 25%, while the facility can train 3,000 baristas annually and has room for further expansion.

The environmentally focused site uses solar panels, rainwater harvesting and LED lighting, and all Costa-sourced coffee is Rainforest Alliance Certified. Costa imports beans globally, including bitter robusta beans from Vietnam, which form part of its arabica-and-robusta blend.

Quality control begins with sampling every incoming bag, inspecting beans for impurities and roasting samples for taste tests. Infrared equipment monitors colour, specialist machines measure moisture, and around 8% of beans are typically rejected annually. Costa’s Master of Coffee, Gennaro Pellicia, oversees the process and has a £10 million insured tongue.

YouTube Red will debut four family-focused Original series in spring: “Hyperlinked,” starring L2M; “DanTDM Creates A Big Scene”; “The Kings of Atlantis,” featuring Cody and Joe; and “Fruit Ninja: Frenzy Force.” More shows are planned for 2017, and the YouTube Kids app is coming to LG and Samsung Smart TVs.

An MIT OpenCourseWare lecture examines multi-stakeholder engagement through a case involving Golden Aggregate Resources (GAR), a palm-oil supplier, and stakeholders including Nestlé, Unilever, Greenpeace, the RSPO, and Indonesia’s ISPO. Students compare three strategies: applying public pressure through Greenpeace, pursuing industry self-regulation, and using market premiums for certified sustainable palm oil.

Stakeholders identified include growers and small farmers, mills and intermediaries, corporate customers, consumers, investors, local and international communities, the Indonesian government, certifying bodies, competitors, and environmental organizations. The discussion emphasizes the palm-oil sector’s limited supply-chain transparency, the difficulty of tracing oil to its source, and concerns that RSPO certification may include noncertified plantations. Mandatory ISPO standards and voluntary RSPO certification offer different incentives, while certification costs, uncertain data, limited premium sales, and the burden on small farmers complicate wider adoption. Proposed responses include financial incentives, productivity support, education and training, third-party audits, forest protections, greater disclosure, and partnerships with NGOs that can provide expertise or funding.

Participants also discussed communication strategies, including sustainability reports, corporate websites, celebrity advocacy, NGO partnerships, product labels, and working with Greenpeace. Corporate customers and consumer pressure were identified as key forces motivating sustainable sourcing, while broader strategic choices included maintaining high standards and leading industry innovation or lowering standards for price competitiveness.

The lecture broadened the case through examples of NGO campaigns and collaborations involving Chiquita, Dell, Walmart, Starbucks, and organizations such as the RSPO, Sustainability Consortium, EICC, and Sustainable Apparel Coalition. It highlighted the need to define objectives, select appropriate partners, assign company contacts, and establish measurable outcomes, as well as inconsistencies in the rigor and regulation of sustainability labels. An Environmental Defense Fund session and a project deliverable due one week later were announced.

The Kiss of Death is an S&P 500 sell signal triggered when the index falls from an all-time high below its monthly 21-day exponential moving average, rebounds above it, and then drops below its recent low. Since 1960, the signal has occurred in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, and 2008, preceding major crashes and bear markets. A September 2022 signal was a false signal, as the index subsequently rose. The strategy sells when triggered and buys back when the S&P 500 closes above its 10-month EMA; no universal re-entry condition exists. A backtest using non-dividend-adjusted data from 1967 found that the strategy improved buy-and-hold performance, increasing CAGR and reducing maximum drawdown to almost half, partly by avoiding severe downturns.

Fair Isaac introduced a pricing model allowing lenders to license FICO credit scores directly through mortgage resellers and distribute them to borrowers, with two pricing options available. Its shares rose more than 20%, their largest gain since Nov. 22, while Experian, TransUnion and Equifax fell 4%–10%. Fair Isaac plans to offer both pricing models to credit bureaus on equal terms, potentially reducing their markup on FICO scores. FHFA director Bill Pulte encouraged bureaus to pursue similar competitive measures.

Pekkala reported growing Finnish support for a separate peace with the Soviet Union, including within the army and among Social Democrats, the Swedish Party, and Progressives; Agrarians continued to favor crushing Russia. He emphasized the urgency of translating these views into official action. Foreign Minister Witting said Finland depended on German goodwill for 93% of its imports and, fearing starvation if imports were interrupted, showed little disposition to challenge German control. In Sweden, the Finnish military situation was rapidly deteriorating. A further Russian advance could create demands for Swedish assistance, strengthen pro-German and anti-Allied elements, and threaten Sweden’s coalition government and the democratic cause. Soviet Minister Kollontay reportedly shared these concerns and was exploring ways to secure a simple cessation of fighting.

MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs based on Arm Cortex-M0+, operating up to 32 MHz. They provide 64 KB flash, 8 KB SRAM, analog and digital peripherals, and UART, SPI, and I²C interfaces with multiple protocol supports, operating from 1.62–3.6 V and −40°C to 125°C.

Tesla Motors’ March 11, 2016 Form 8-K reported an immaterial error in its 2015 Form 10-K. The Supercharger network’s net book value as of December 31, 2015, should have been $166.6 million; the error affected only the MD&A section and did not impact the consolidated financial statements or notes. Chief Financial Officer Jason Wheeler signed the filing.

Researchers have developed a molecular sensor designed to detect influenza by releasing thymol, a strong herbal taste found in thyme. The sensor uses a synthetic neuraminidase substrate linked to thymol; when influenza neuraminidase is present, it detaches the thymol, producing a taste detectable by the tongue. If incorporated into gum or lozenges, the technology could provide rapid, accessible first-line screening and potentially identify infections before symptoms develop. Laboratory tests found that the sensor released free thymol within 30 minutes in saliva from people diagnosed with influenza and did not alter human or mouse cell function. Researchers hope to begin human clinical trials in about two years to confirm taste sensations in people with pre- and post-symptomatic influenza. The authors have registered a European patent and acknowledged German federal research funding.

At a forum for Baltimore County executive candidates, Vicki Almond, Jim Brochin, Johnny Olszewski Jr. and Al Redmer Jr. discussed development policy before real estate, building and mortgage professionals. All supported smart growth and smoother approvals, but did not back impact fees; Brochin proposed housing standards for overcrowded schools, while others questioned the fees’ relevance. Candidates described the permit process as cumbersome and discussed waiving some requirements to speed housing construction. They also sought more predictable rezoning tied to the county master plan, with Olszewski and Redmer opposing unilateral downzoning and Redmer advocating appeals. Brochin continued his “end pay-to-play politics” pledge, while others emphasized development’s economic and tax benefits. The June 26 primary also includes Kevin Marron and Pat McDonough; candidates are seeking to succeed Kevin Kamenetz.

The 12th Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards are accepting entries until noon on Monday, March 13, with businesses allowed to enter multiple categories. The black-tie ceremony will be held for the first time at the restored Royal Hall on Thursday, April 27. The awards cover 10 categories, including rural, tourism, family-run, employer, company size, website, personality and lifetime achievement. Verity Frearson is the main sponsor, with each category separately sponsored.

The author argues that Robert Oscar Lopez’s experience and other campus disputes show that academic freedom is neither an absolute virtue nor a practical reality, since tenure protects a select few while ideological double standards persist. Calling for truth as the standard for curricula, the author urges cutting college funding, expanding trade schools and apprenticeships, reducing debt and credential inflation, and purging academia’s moral and intellectual dysfunction.

The paper studies repeated bilateral trade from a broker’s perspective, seeking to maximize profit while preserving dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality. Using online learning, it compares the learned broker’s profit with that of the best mechanism in hindsight, rather than restricting the benchmark to fixed-price or other parametric mechanisms.

In the stochastic i.i.d. setting, where valuations may be correlated and come from an unknown fixed distribution, the paper presents a polynomial-time algorithm with nearly optimal \(\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})\) regret. A matching \(\Omega(\sqrt{T})\) lower bound establishes optimality up to polylogarithmic factors. The results also imply that learning an expected \(\varepsilon\)-optimal mechanism requires approximately \(1/\varepsilon^2\) samples.

In the adversarial setting, the paper proves that no learning algorithm can achieve sublinear regret relative to a \(2/3+\varepsilon\) fraction of the optimal profit, demonstrating a separation between stochastic and adversarial data generation.

A correspondence between bilateral trade and non-excludable mechanism design is also used to improve regret for the joint ads problem from \(O(T^{3/4})\) to \(\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})\).

DSIC and IR mechanisms admit a geometric representation in the unit square, but the mechanism space remains non-parametric and the profit function may be irregular, making standard discretization insufficient. The paper leaves intermediate models, such as a \(\sigma\)-smooth adversary, as an open direction.

The passage examines the first trading day of the month effect in the S&P 500, using SPY since 1993. Holding from the previous month’s final close to the first trading day’s close averaged a 0.24% gain, compared with 0.04% on a typical day, but the unfiltered strategy was unstable and performed less well after the 2008/09 financial crisis. February and July had the strongest first-day results. Adding a simple filter reduced trades by one-third, increased average gains to 0.35%, and produced a 3% CAGR, 67% win rate, 2.5 profit factor, and 5% maximum drawdown. Exiting at the first day’s open retained a 0.22% average gain and reduced drawdown to 3%. A separate filtered strategy generated 61 trades, averaged 1.1% per trade, and returned 2.2% annually. The article identifies monthly capital inflows as a possible cause but emphasizes that the underlying effect is factual.
Figures show the cooling fan design in elevation, plan, and perspective views, including an alternative position; broken lines mark unclaimed portions.

Mediation analysis clarifies how interventions influence outcomes through intervening mechanisms, supports intervention refinement, and may provide early indicators of treatment success. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is commonly used to address measurement error and correlated indicators of latent constructs, but its causal mediation analysis requires sequential ignorability—an assumption that is rarely achievable because relevant confounders may be unmeasured or difficult to assess. Rank-preserving models based on g-estimation offer an alternative that permits omitted covariates under a no-effect-modifier assumption, provided they do not interact with treatment or the mediator. The paper introduces the Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), which integrates rank-preserving modeling, factor score regression, and interaction corrections to allow latent variables while retaining this relaxed assumption. RAPSEM is intended to address both measurement error and omitted mediator–outcome confounding. For randomized binary treatment, the paper defines the controlled direct effect of treatment on the outcome and the controlled mediation effect of the mediator on the outcome while holding the other variable fixed and adjusting for latent covariates. RAPSEM is mathematically equivalent to a standard SEM with measurement and structural components; the mediator, covariates, and outcome are modeled as latent factors measured by observed indicators. The paper will present estimation, identification assumptions, simulation evaluations, and discussion of the method’s strengths and limitations.

The team credits fun during hard practices for its success. A fearless defenseman blocks shots, rises, and motivates teammates. Media hype builds before games, while a smooth, understated player earns a top-defenseman nomination.

The team credits strong play and capitalizing on chances for its latest victory, giving it another chance to even the series. With both Conks and Markkanen having had trying seasons, the coaching staff praises the veteran goalie who played well and says he must get hot for the remaining three games. Ryan Smyth is singled out as a highly skilled, hard-working leader and role model whose big plays have helped the team. The opponent pressures the power play, blocks shots, and pressures hard against diamond formations, making puck commitment and confidence crucial. The team’s structure and adjustments, particularly on shorthanded situations and limiting pressure, helped it beat Detroit and succeed against San Jose. Coaches believe maintaining focus and raising the team’s level could be enough to take over the series. They also value the franchise’s tradition and the presence of former players in the building.

The study investigates whether transformers can learn transitive relations—equivalently, directed-graph connectivity—from individual node-pair training examples rather than graph edges supplied in prompts. The connectivity task labels a start–goal node pair as “Y” if a directed path exists and “N” otherwise, and is shown to correspond to transitive-relation inference and deductive reasoning in implicational logic.

Experiments compare low-dimensional grid graphs with disconnected chain graphs using four-layer transformers, learned token embeddings, and connectivity labels. Transformers achieve near-perfect generalization on grid graphs but often fail to generalize on disconnected chain graphs, which cannot be represented as easily through simple low-dimensional embeddings.

Increasing model size improves connectivity performance on grid graphs but does not yield comparable gains on disconnected chain graphs. Increasing graph size leaves grid-graph performance consistent while improving chain-graph performance when the number of chains is fixed, because longer chains provide more connected-node training examples. Lower-dimensional grids are learned more accurately than higher-dimensional grids; for higher dimensions, adding nodes is more effective than increasing model size. Similarly, graphs with fewer chains perform better, and model scaling does not resolve poor performance with many chains, whereas increasing graph size does.

Overall, the results indicate that model scaling benefits grid-graph connectivity more than chain-graph connectivity, while data scaling is more effective for higher-dimensional grids and disconnected graphs with many chains. The study identifies evaluating real-world graphs, including knowledge and causal graphs, as future work.

Hawkin’s Bazaar will close its Plymouth shop on February 4, with a clearance sale offering up to 75% off. The business previously spent six years in the West End and has not responded to requests for comment.

Visceral leishmaniasis (VL), or Kala-azar, is caused by parasites of the *Leishmania donovani* complex and transmitted by sand flies. It is endemic in 75 countries, with about 90% of cases concentrated in seven. Ethiopia has reported cases from six regions and an estimated 4,500–7,400 annual cases. In Somali Regional State, outbreaks were first reported in 2001, and broad areas were identified as high risk.

A cross-sectional study was conducted from April to August 2021 in Denan district, southeastern Ethiopia. Permanent residents from six kebeles were selected through single-stage random household sampling; 187 of 204 planned participants provided blood samples. Sera were tested using the Direct Agglutination Test, with a positivity threshold of 1:800. Questionnaires assessed sociodemographic characteristics, housing, sleeping and other practices, and knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding VL and sand flies. Sand flies were collected over 12 nights from indoor, peri-domestic, forest and termite-mound habitats in four kebeles using light and sticky traps.

VL seroprevalence was 9.63% (18/187), with no significant difference by sex. Multivariable analysis identified age 19–36, damp floors, outdoor sleeping and sleeping near animal shelters as factors associated with infection. Among participants, 53.48% had heard of VL, 42% identified sand-fly bites as the transmission route, and 89% knew at least one symptom. Only 36% considered VL preventable, while 44% believed untreated VL would be fatal. Reported prevention practices included bed-net use (42%), insecticide spraying (32%), smoking plant parts (14%) and environmental cleaning (8%).

A total of 823 sand flies representing 12 species were collected. Five belonged to *Phlebotomus* and seven to *Sergentomyia*. *P. orientalis* was the dominant *Phlebotomus* species, accounting for 94 specimens, and was captured mainly in termite mounds and forest but not indoors. *S. clydie* was the most abundant species overall. The authors concluded that VL seroprevalence was relatively high in this pastoral community, knowledge and prevention practices needed improvement, and further epidemiological and vector-bionomics studies were warranted.

The North Carolina Supreme Court reversed the defendant’s assault conviction and ordered a new trial. After withdrawing a guilty plea, the defendant requested time to obtain witnesses from Florida and West Virginia and for appointed counsel to prepare his defense, but the court tried him the next day and denied both continuance requests. The court held that, under the circumstances, the defendant was not given reasonable time to prepare and was prejudiced by the jury’s likely recollection of his original guilty plea.

Cincinnati snapped No. 14 Iowa State’s unbeaten season with a 17-point first-quarter lead and a 31-7 advantage late in the second quarter. The Cyclones rallied to within eight points before Cincinnati recovered an onside kick to secure its first home win over a ranked opponent since beating Houston in 2021. Pryor ran for 111 yards and two touchdowns, while Iowa State quarterback Rocco Becht passed for 314 yards and two scores. The Cyclones were missing 16 injured players, including all their All-Big 12 defensive backs and top two kickers.

MADSEN Cycles manufactures brightly colored bucket bikes with large rear buckets that carry up to four children and cargo. The bucket includes two removable bench seats and four seat belts. Accessories include custom-made rain covers, frame-mounted front racks, and a padded middle seat for pets, diaper changes, or drinks.

Jerome “Jay” Powell, a former investment banker and Fed governor, succeeds Janet Yellen on Monday as chair of the US Federal Reserve. Yellen departs with unemployment at 4.1%, low inflation, nearly four years of growth, and a more normalized monetary policy after steering the Fed out of large-scale bond buying. Powell inherits a synchronized global expansion, fiscal stimulus from tax reform, solid job growth and rising wages. The Fed has raised rates five times under Yellen and projected three increases in 2018, with March widely expected to be the first. Policy debates center on how quickly to tighten amid low inflation, limited labor availability and concerns that faster increases could unsettle markets.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in Barrett's case, which asks whether 18 U.S.C. § 924(j) creates a separate crime carrying separate punishment from § 924(c) under double jeopardy principles. Barrett was convicted in 2013 of several armed robberies and other offenses after a coconspirator fatally shot a victim who tried to thwart a robbery.

Section 924(c) makes possessing, carrying, or using a firearm to advance a federal crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense a "compound crime" with aggravating sentencing factors, while § 924(j) applies to defendants who "cause[] the death of a person through the use of a firearm." Under the Court's nearly century-old test, separate punishments are presumed permitted when each offense requires proof of a fact the other does not, but presumed barred when one offense's elements are a subset of the other's, absent clear legislative intent. Section 924(c) mandates consecutive sentences, and the Court previously held that its consecutive-sentence and mandatory minimum provisions do not apply to § 924(j) charged alone, leaving double jeopardy unaddressed.

Because the government and Barrett agree separate sentences are not permitted for the same conduct, the Court appointed amicus McCloud, a former assistant solicitor general, to defend the Second Circuit's judgment permitting separate convictions under both provisions. Barrett and the government argue neither statute addresses cumulative punishment; McCloud counters that § 924(c)(1)(D)(ii)'s consecutive-sentence mandate suffices.

In vocational education and training (VET), formative assessment requires active teacher–student participation, immediate feedback, guided next steps, and student self-evaluation. Teachers must use professional judgment, accommodate spontaneous teachable moments, and prepare for the additional workload. Formative methods identify learning difficulties and missed opportunities through clear expectations, descriptive feedback, multiple attempts, peer review, self-assessment, and workplace-like methods. They can increase motivation, deepen learning, and prepare students for workplace feedback.

VET teachers must balance vocation-based formative assessment with academic summative assessment. Many school-based tools, especially written tests, are poorly suited to VET and may prioritize documentation or arbitrary standards over competence. Academic testing should therefore be balanced with technical-skill and vocational-competency assessments. Competence-based education links classroom theory to industry-standard workplace performance through essential tasks, clear standards, and authentic practicum evaluations by supervisors or managers, potentially improving motivation and engagement.

Authentic assessment emphasizes workplace-like performance rather than isolated skills or standardized testing. Teachers can balance authenticity and reliability through clear procedures, communicated expectations, workplace-connected tasks, rubrics, professional calibration, and workplace supervisor feedback. It also addresses the social dimension of performance and can strengthen industry relationships.

A comprehensive VET assessment program combines written tests, technical-skills assessments, workplace evaluations, process and product assessment, and formative and summative methods before, during, and after learning. It evaluates all levels of vocational knowledge: “knows,” “knows how,” “shows how,” and “does.” Clearly communicated outcomes, competencies, portfolios, and workplace evaluations support deeper learning and student engagement.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court’s grant of summary judgment to Reisdorf Brothers, Inc. on the Georges’ Clean Water Act and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act claims. The Clean Water Act requires a continuous or intermittent discharge, but the evidence showed only a discrete March 2009 spill or speculative theories concerning fertilizer, pesticides, and molasses; it did not create a triable issue. The consent orders likewise established no ongoing violation, and the plaintiffs’ expert report did not alter the result. The plaintiffs also failed to allege or prove violations of the regulatory criteria defining an open dump under RCRA.

The court found no abuse of discretion in dismissing the plaintiffs’ state-law adverse-possession claim without prejudice to renewal in state court. It likewise upheld the denial of attorney’s fees because the unsuccessful pollution claims had an arguable basis and appeared to have been litigated in good faith. The plaintiffs’ newly raised stormwater claim was not considered because it was raised late and the complaint did not provide sufficient notice of that claim.

The Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Washington Capitals 7-4 Friday, extending their winning streak to four and pulling within four points of Washington in the Metropolitan Division. Phil Kessel scored twice, while Evgeni Malkin had two goals and two assists; Bryan Rust, Carl Hagelin and Patric Hornqvist also scored. Sidney Crosby recorded two assists, extending his NHL-leading active scoring streak to 11 games. Alex Ovechkin scored twice for Washington, bringing his season total to an NHL-best 32. Goaltender Matt Murray made 29 saves as Pittsburgh won its seventh straight home game.

This study used longitudinal PREVEND cohort data from 8,569 participants to model transitions among low, intermediate, and high/very-high KDIGO kidney-risk stages before new-onset heart failure (HF) or death. Kidney function was assessed using urinary albumin excretion (UAE) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at four examinations, with a multi-state model accounting for age, sex, and potential misclassification.

During median follow-up of 12.6 years, 373 participants developed new-onset HF and 710 died before HF. Forward transitions to higher kidney-risk stages were uncommon before age 50, increased with age, and were generally more frequent in men than women. Women and younger participants were more likely to transition backward from intermediate to low risk. HF transition rates increased exponentially with age and were lower in women.

Compared with low-risk participants, those at intermediate or high/very-high risk had greater HF risk. Relative risk was highest in younger adults and declined with age, whereas absolute risk differences increased with age. In projections for people starting at low risk at age 50, progression to intermediate risk was most common between ages 60 and 70, while progression to high/very-high risk occurred mainly after age 70. By age 90, projected HF prevalence was 24% in men and 21% in women.

Model calibration was excellent, and sensitivity analyses using cystatin C-based eGFR were broadly consistent. Limitations included an albumin-enriched, predominantly Caucasian cohort and the Markov assumption that transition rates depend only on current risk stage and age. The findings indicate that more advanced KDIGO status is associated with increased new-onset HF risk and suggest that slowing kidney-risk progression in middle-aged people could reduce HF incidence.

This descriptive survey study developed and evaluated a scale for measuring prospective teachers’ attitudes toward values education through distance education. The sample comprised 341 prospective teachers from Gazi University’s Faculty of Education, most of whom were female. A literature review, compositions from 20 candidates, expert review, and a pilot study with 30 candidates produced 40 five-point Likert items. Exploratory factor analysis of the main sample eliminated four items, yielding a final 36-item scale with 21 positive and 15 negative items.

The analysis identified two factors: “Necessity and Usefulness,” with 21 items and 35.029% of the variance, and “Feasibility,” with 15 items and 28.257%. Together, the factors explained 63.286% of the total variance. Cronbach’s alpha coefficients were .969 and .961 for the two factors, while split-half reliability coefficients were .934 and .930. The scale lacked additivity, so its subfactors should be evaluated separately. Item-total correlations and significant differences between the upper and lower 27% groups confirmed the items’ distinctiveness. Scores range from 21 to 105 for necessity and usefulness and from 15 to 75 for feasibility, with negative items reverse-scored. Limitations include the predominantly female sample, restriction to one university, and the absence of an external scale for comparison.

Investors can access Australian markets through US-listed ETFs, American Depository Receipts, international brokers offering direct ASX access, or Australian CFDs. The ASX, based in Sydney, provides listings, trading, clearing, settlements, and futures services; the SSX is another exchange. Australian markets open weekdays, excluding national holidays, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Australian Eastern Daylight Time (GMT+11), or 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. GMT. The AUD can be traded against major currencies.

Backtests using EWA found that moving-average and Golden Cross strategies were unsuccessful, while mean reversion performed less consistently than the comparable SPY strategy, partly amid Australia’s greater commodity exposure. A seasonal “Santa Claus effect” strategy reported only two negative years since 1996, a 92% win rate, and a 2.4% average gain per trade, but its limited annual investment produced 1.87% returns versus 7.34% for buy-and-hold. The passage notes that backtesting helps assess strategy risk and profitability but is imperfect.

On April 26, 2001, the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) board authorized management to issue a preliminary termination notice to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over the disputed power purchase agreement. The vote was 6–1, with IDBI opposed; MSEB representatives were not permitted to vote. The authorization did not mean termination was imminent. Lender consent was required, and a preliminary notice would trigger a six-month consultation period before further action.

International lenders favored ending the project and withholding some Phase II funding, while IDBI and other Indian lenders sought renegotiation. Maharashtra and central governments also opposed termination and planned to form a joint committee to negotiate lower tariffs and resolve outstanding dues. Potential government liabilities were variously estimated, including one year’s electricity payments and a $300 million termination fee.

The dispute involved overdue bills, MSEB’s Rs 401 crore penalty against DPC, and DPC’s use of political-force-majeure, conciliation and arbitration procedures. MSEB made a Rs 134 crore “protest payment” toward its disputed Rs 146.64 crore March bill. Enron held 65% of DPC, GE and Bechtel 10% each, and MSEB 15%.

Post defense against tall, physical players requires coordinated team adjustments: active pressure on the passer, backside help, and post traps. Defenders should deny entry, influence the ball toward the post player’s weak side, and disrupt preferred moves. Options include full-court pressing, a 2-3 zone, and Diamond & One.

Law enforcement officials said Stephen Paddock bought 1,000 tracer rounds, though it was unclear whether he used them during the Las Vegas attack that killed 58 and injured nearly 500. He stockpiled 23 guns, modified some to fire continuously, positioned cameras, and booked rooms overlooking other events. Authorities also investigated possible additional attacks after finding ammunition, fertilizer and Tannerite in his car.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2017 reported Q2 net sales of $38.0 billion, up 25% from $30.4 billion, and six-month net sales of $73.7 billion, up 24% from $59.5 billion. Q2 operating income fell from $1.3 billion to $628 million, while six-month operating income declined from $2.4 billion to $1.6 billion. Net income fell from $857 million to $197 million in Q2 and from $1.37 billion to $921 million for the six months. Diluted earnings per share were $0.40 in Q2, down from $1.78, and $1.87 for the six months, down from $2.84.

North America sales increased 27% in Q2 to $22.4 billion, while segment operating income declined to $436 million from $702 million. International sales increased 17% to $11.5 billion, and the segment’s operating loss widened to $724 million from $135 million. AWS sales increased 42% to $4.1 billion, and operating income rose to $916 million from $718 million. For the six months, sales increased 25% in North America, 16% internationally, and 42% in AWS. Sales growth was attributed largely to higher unit sales, third-party seller activity, lower customer prices, shipping offers, greater inventory availability and selection, and increased AWS usage.

Operating expenses increased as Amazon expanded its fulfillment network and spending on technology, content, marketing and personnel. Q2 shipping costs rose to $4.6 billion from $3.4 billion, and six-month shipping costs reached $9.0 billion. Capital expenditures were $2.5 billion in Q2 and $4.4 billion for the six months, primarily supporting fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure, including AWS. Property and equipment acquired under capital leases was $2.7 billion in Q2 and $4.6 billion for the first six months.

At June 30, 2017, Amazon held $13.2 billion in cash, $8.2 billion in marketable securities and had total assets of $87.8 billion. Stockholders’ equity was $23.2 billion, compared with $19.3 billion at December 31, 2016. Q2 operating cash flow was $3.8 billion, investing activities used $5.1 billion and financing activities used $1.3 billion. For the six months, operating cash flow was $2.2 billion, investing activities used $6.7 billion and financing activities used $2.2 billion.

Amazon entered into an agreement to acquire Whole Foods Market for approximately $13.7 billion, including its net debt, expected to be funded with debt and cash on hand and to close in 2017. It secured a commitment for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility of up to $13.7 billion to fund the acquisition. Amazon also acquired Souq Group in May 2017 for approximately $586 million, net of cash acquired, and other companies for $86 million. It had contractual commitments of $49.2 billion and purchase obligations and open purchase orders of $12.9 billion.

The company adopted accounting standards for inventory valuation and stock-based compensation in the first quarter of 2017. The stock-compensation guidance increased retained earnings by $687 million and required certain 2016 excess tax benefits to be reclassified from financing to operating cash flow. Future standards covering revenue recognition, leases, income taxes and restricted cash were expected to affect reported results, with revenue recognition planned for adoption in the first quarter of 2018.

Amazon reported $1.9 billion of tax contingencies and recorded a $600 million valuation allowance against Luxembourg deferred tax assets. The IRS sought approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax for 2005 and 2006 transfer-pricing adjustments, although the U.S. Tax Court adopted Amazon’s approach with adjustments, subject to appeal. Amazon also contested a €196 million French tax assessment and remained subject to a European Commission state-aid investigation.

Disclosures also covered potential sanctions penalties involving orders processed for customers in Iran, disputed indirect-tax assessments, and patent litigation involving Eolas Technologies and the University of Tennessee Research Foundation. Amazon said it disputed these matters and intended to defend itself vigorously, while noting that legal outcomes and other contingencies could materially affect results. The filing reported 480,379,517 common shares outstanding as of July 18, 2017.

A live Sporting News update shows No. 22 Aledo leading the Ryan Raiders 2-0 in Denton, Texas. Ryan was called for intentional grounding in its own end zone, resulting in a safety for Aledo. Aledo is also ranked No. 16 in the Massey Ratings.

Key sources for *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988, Volume IV* include Reagan Library White House and NSC records, relevant State Department executive-secretariat lots and country-office files, and cables between the Moscow Embassy and Washington; declassified NSDDs and other documents are also online. The volume includes a note on the development of U.S. covert-action procedures. In December 1947, NSC 4–A authorized peacetime covert operations and assigned responsibility for psychological warfare to the CIA, whose access to unvouchered funds reduced the risk of exposure. Opposition from State and Defense officials led NSC 10/2 to supersede the directive on June 18, 1948. It broadened the CIA’s mandate to covert operations and defined them as activities planned so U.S. responsibility was not evident to unauthorized persons and could be plausibly disclaimed if uncovered.

On March 30, 2018, a Federal High Court judge in Abuja admitted EFCC documents against Chinese national Li Ya Ping, charged with concealing $300,000 (N108 million) while trying to board a Dubai flight under the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, 2011. EFCC's fourth witness, detective Hassan Mohammed Misau, testified that customs officers arrested the defendant on March 15, 2018 at Nnamdi Azikwe Airport and handed over the cash and related documents.

Parental obesity is associated with increased childhood obesity risk. Maternal pre-conception BMI is most closely linked to obesity in young children, while paternal obesity also contributes; two obese parents further increase risk. Research indicates that eggs and sperm transmit more than DNA: obesity-related changes in sperm non-coding RNA and egg components can alter embryonic metabolism and obesity susceptibility. Defective mitochondria in eggs of obese females may be inherited, affecting offspring metabolism and increasing lifelong risk of obesity and diabetes. Animal studies suggest that diabetes treatment, exercise, and dietary interventions can improve egg or sperm quality and prevent transmission of obesity, although human evidence remains limited. Children conceived after maternal gastric banding were less obese than earlier siblings. Researchers are developing interventions for obese mothers before pregnancy and advocate extending them to fathers. Preventing obesity before reproduction may shape community obesity rates.

VentureWire’s October 19, 2000 issue reported private-company financing, product launches, transactions, and venture-capital developments.

- St. Paul Venture Capital closed its sixth fund with $1.3 billion, bringing assets under management to $3 billion, focused on early-stage Internet, communications, consumer technology, and healthcare investments. Idealab! postponed its IPO because of market volatility, while Constellation Ventures closed a $350 million fund targeting digitally delivered content and enabling technologies. Football is increasingly offense-driven, making cornerbacks vital for shutting down passing attacks. Cornerbacks cover opposing wide receivers in man or zone coverage, often in one-on-one situations. In man coverage, they must mirror receivers’ routes while reacting to their movements, requiring speed, agility, sharp turns, and the ability to transition from backpedaling into a sprint. They primarily protect the outside thirds of the field, but also contain outside runs and tackle or force runners inward. Teams usually deploy two cornerbacks, sometimes adding a third to cover a slot receiver. Excellent corners, called “lockdown corners,” can erase a receiver’s threat and prevent quarterbacks from exploiting defensive weaknesses. The position’s celebrated players include Deion Sanders, Charles Woodson, Mel Blount, Champ Bailey, Ty Law, and Darrell Revis, whose dominance inspired “Revis Island.”

Defending soccer goal kicks requires positioning, pressing, and quickly transitioning to attack. The primary aims are to win possession in a dangerous area or prevent the opponent from building comfortably or launching a successful long kick. Defenders should cover potential receivers using man-to-man and zone marking. Typically, the center striker pressures the kicker at the top of the penalty area, wing strikers close-mark opposing wingbacks, the center midfielder occupies the center mark, wide midfielders cover the flanks, and the center back and wing backs provide central and wide defensive support.

The first striker moves toward the ball while secondary strikers cut off short passes and pressure the goalkeeper. Midfielders contest lofted balls and must be positioned to challenge for them. If possession is won, the team should attack immediately; if not, it should apply a coordinated high press, retain the ball in the opponent’s half, and offer counterattack and back-pass options. Flick headers in the wide areas should be recognized and the intended receiver tightly marked.

Under Law 16, a goal kick is taken from anywhere in the goal area after an attacker sends the ball over the defending end line. The ball must be stationary before the kick and becomes live once kicked and visibly moves. Any attacking player may take it, but the original kicker cannot touch it afterward. Defenders are expected to remain outside the penalty area unless the kicking team has not allowed enough time for them to retreat. A kick may proceed with opponents still inside the area, but a retake is required if an opponent enters early and interferes before play begins.

For young players, local rules often reduce field size and introduce a build-out line parallel to the goal line. Defenders who win the ball must retreat behind this line before challenging, and the attacking team must build up rather than kick long. Basic plays use a designated kicker placing the ball at the outer corner of the goal area and playing to a nearby dribbler or a target receiver, with secondary options farther upfield. Coaches should teach players to keep the ball wide and upfield, never send it across their own goal, track the ball, and allow defenders time to retreat.

For players aged 11 and above, coaches can progressively use two wide targets and then a supporting midfielder as additional options, selecting an uncovered receiver or kicking short to the farther target so the receiver can meet the ball. Players must prepare for kicks from either side and attack the ball forcefully. Adult teams may use short, deep, or lofted kicks, usually taken by the goalkeeper, with teammates running toward predetermined receiving points.

Goal kicks are direct restarts and may result in a goal without another player touching the ball. Players should react immediately, account for wind and field conditions, never lose sight of the ball, scout the opposition’s strongest kicker, and drill against every available attacking option.

The article backtests Larry Connors’ 3-day high/low ETF strategy, introduced in *High Probability ETF Trading* (2009). The strategy buys an ETF after three consecutive days of lower highs and lower lows, with criteria including a close above the 200-day moving average and below the 5-day moving average. Connors emphasized ETF-only trading, high win ratios of at least 65%, and quantifiable rules. Although 13 of the original 20 ETFs performed worse than in Connors’ pre-2009 tests, the strategy still showed promise. A portfolio test using 25 ETFs, up to five simultaneous positions, and 20% equity per position also found that the method had deteriorated somewhat. Its worst drawdown occurred during the EU debt crisis in July 2011.

NewMarket generates most revenue, profit, and cash flow from Afton Chemical, which makes petroleum-fuel and lubricant additives. The company has strong EBITDA margins, cash flow, and capital returns, but North American and European growth faces headwinds as improved vehicle and engine efficiency reduces additive demand. NewMarket’s growth prospects depend increasingly on expanding in emerging markets, particularly Asia. Its new Singapore plant and $183 million acquisition of Aditivos Mexicanos support that strategy and increase exposure to diesel additives, though the acquisition is not large enough to materially shift its gasoline-heavy mix.

The passage estimates roughly 3% long-term revenue growth, driven by rising vehicle volumes in China, India, Indonesia, and Vietnam. Free cash flow should improve after the Singapore plant is completed, potentially reaching low-double-digit margins, with capital expected to support dividends, acquisitions, and buybacks. NewMarket’s R&D focus and OEM relationships may help it develop accepted products and enter additional diesel-market segments.

Despite its quality, the shares are not viewed as undervalued: the price already anticipates high-single-digit free-cash-flow growth and trades above 12 times estimated 2017 EBITDA. Without diversification, NewMarket may struggle to generate substantially faster growth.

The agreement charges voyage expenses resulting from misconduct, desertion, disobedience, or mutiny to those responsible. After a fair trial, the master may replace an officer or seaman judged incompetent or indisposed, with pay adjusted to the duty performed and increased at final settlement for anyone promoted. If sickness or death prevents completion of the voyage, legal representatives receive the proportional share earned for time served. Crew members must account for entrusted vessel property, reimburse owners for losses caused by negligence, and safely handle assigned cargo and stores.

Crew members who properly perform their duties and comply with the regulations are paid in San Francisco upon return: whale oil at 20 cents per gallon, sperm oil at 40 cents, and whalebone at $1.25 per pound if the fleet’s seasonal catch exceeds 200 whales, or $1.50 if it does not. Distilled liquor may be carried only for medical use; violators forfeit their entire voyage share to the owners. The $760 million Bifrost subsea cable, a 20,000-kilometre system linking Singapore and the U.S. West Coast, is ready for commercial operations. Keppel invested about $350 million and holds five of its twelve fibre pairs. Following weather and regulatory delays, Bifrost is expected to support growing cloud, AI and content-delivery demand while strengthening Singapore’s digital-hub position.

The study examined how second-year engineering and technical management students at a Hungarian university prioritized employability skills, expected from higher education, and valued international study. A cross-sectional questionnaire used purposive, non-probability sampling. Of 165 respondents, 147 responses were analyzed: 65.3% studied Mechanical and Safety Engineering and 34.7% Technical Management. Surveys were conducted in 2019 and 2021 using paper and online formats. Questions were informed by literature, World Economic Forum job-skill research, and 22 interviews with Hungarian industry representatives. Data were examined descriptively and through chi-square tests and CHAID decision-tree analysis; the four-point Likert question group had a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.726.

Both faculties ranked problem-solving first and specialization-related knowledge highly. Significant differences showed that engineering students prioritized specialization and technical-mathematical knowledge more, while technical management students prioritized decision-making and analytical skills more. Thus, the first hypothesis was accepted.

Foreign study was considered most beneficial for language skills and communication (84.6%), followed by networking (53.1%) and adaptation to international norms (45.5%). Engineering students placed greater importance on new approaches to learning and opportunities for projects or research, whereas technical management students emphasized networking and adaptation. The groups otherwise showed strongly correlated rankings of international-study benefits.

Both groups viewed individual talents and skills, professional devotion, and professional networks as leading determinants of graduate career success. No significant faculty difference was detected for these perceptions, so the second hypothesis was not accepted. More than half of students said higher education fully contributed to knowledge related to future work, digital literacy, and understanding other people, while responses on communication, quantitative analysis, teamwork, and self-understanding were more divided. Significant faculty differences occurred for future-work knowledge, quantitative analysis, teamwork, and self-understanding. The third hypothesis was therefore only partly accepted. A CHAID model, 77.6% accurate, identified future-work knowledge, decision-making training, and approaches to learning gained abroad as key differentiating factors.

The findings support combining technical and soft-skills development in university curricula. Engineering students additionally require technical and IT preparation, while technical management students emphasize decision-making, foreign languages, and networking. Limitations include the small, non-probability sample, which prevents generalization, and the absence of earlier comparable research at the two faculties. Future research should use larger samples, additional faculties and universities, interviews, and greater involvement of Industry 4.0 participants.

The passage examines racial economic disparities in Durham and the United States. In 2014, median family income was $71,300 for whites and $43,300 for blacks; in 2015, median family wealth was $171,000 versus $17,600, a 10-to-1 gap that some studies place as high as 20-to-1. Cited causes include education, age, labor-force experience, and current and past discrimination, with racial differences in homeownership and home equity playing a major role. In Durham, 73 percent of whites owned a primary residence compared with 45 percent of blacks, while 19 percent of black families had zero or negative net worth versus 9 percent of white families. The author argues that affordable-housing policies often create expensive rental units without resident equity and that demolitions reduce the housing stock. Alternatives include Habitat for Humanity, Rebuilding Together, Preservation Durham’s Preservation Equity Program, and property-tax deferrals to help existing homeowners maintain their homes, retain or gain equity, and potentially benefit from gentrification.

This conceptual survey examines the largely overlooked relationship among slavery, pedagogy, surveillance, and digital technology. Using Foucault’s panopticism and surveillance textualism, it argues that surveillance is inherent to teaching: examinations, records, writing, and discourse turn human experience into texts that enable categorization, normalization, behavioral control, and self-discipline. Race structures these processes, allowing racial surveillance to reproduce inequality. Although Foucault’s work has been criticized for neglecting race and slavery, his framework remains useful for understanding surveillance as an instrument of power.

The survey traces pedagogy’s origins to Ancient Greece, where pedagogues were often enslaved people responsible for guiding children’s learning while also teaching them relations of power. Later, racial chattel slavery made surveillance, restricted literacy, documentation, measurement, and violence central to controlling Black labor and education. Givens’s concept of “fugitive pedagogy” identifies the resistant practices through which Black educators challenged the suppression and criminalization of Black learning.

Extending this history, the article develops “surveillance pedagogy” to describe observation, monitoring, data extraction, textualization, and differentiation practiced by those exercising authority over formal and informal learning. Digitalization and surveillance capitalism expand these processes by enabling platforms and learning-management systems to mine student data, influence instruction, and monetize behavior, often with limited oversight. Examples include Google Classroom and AI language models. The article concludes that digital surveillance rearticulates older practices of slave masters and schoolmasters, perpetuating inequalities between masters and slaves, teachers and students, and capital and labor, while offering a framework for examining the pedagogical, political, and economic values embedded in digital texts.

News clippings compiled May 30, 2001 on the Dabhol Power Company (DPC)–Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) dispute over the $2.9-billion, 2,184 MW Dabhol project (DPC 65% owned by Enron):

- MSEB stopped buying power from DPC from noon on May 29, following its May 23 rescission ("avoidance") notice cancelling the power purchase agreement over payment differences, including the unpaid December 2000 bill of Rs 102 crore and a Rs 402-crore availability penalty. MSEB said DPC failed to supply power within the stipulated ramp-up time and had rejected a Rs 136-crore cheque "under protest." Phase II block B (722 MW), due for commissioning June 7, was left without a buyer, and the plant was to be shut down pending resolution.

- MERC granted ad-interim relief restraining DPC from activating the roughly Rs 5,000-crore annual escrow account (Canara Bank as receptor) and from proceeding with international arbitration under clause 20.3 of the PPA, until the June 14 hearing, finding it had jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes between utilities under the 1998 Electricity Regulatory Commission Act. DPC's counsel contested jurisdiction, sought two weeks, and gave no assurance the escrow would remain untouched; DPC is expected to challenge the order in the Mumbai High Court. The state Cabinet decided to settle disputes through MERC rather than London arbitration, arguing PPA arbitration clauses were superseded by the 1998 Act. MSEB's advocate general said DPC misdeclared availability on January 28, February 13 and March 29, entitling a rebate of Rs 401 crore.

- The Centre said it would play an "active role" but would not buy power from Dabhol. Power Minister Suresh Prabhu rejected Maharashtra's request that NTPC and the Power Trading Corporation buy phase-II power, describing the Centre as a facilitator only. At the second round of the Godbole renegotiation committee, the Centre tabled a set of proposals (reportedly around 36) but declined to give specifics; no date was set for the next meeting. DPC maintained its 10% tariff reduction proposal from May 11 and agreed to discuss methodology with MSEB officials, subject to lender and shareholder approval, but submitted no concrete proposal.

- The Centre also asked DPC to extend the conciliation period 60 days beyond the June 7 deadline in the December-bill dispute; David AR Williams QC was agreed as third conciliator, alongside DPC's Laurence Street and the Centre's B.P. Jeevan Reddy, with conciliation begun April 9.

- Foreign lenders are weighing invoking domestic financial institutions' guarantees to curb DPC exposure. Domestic lenders with about Rs 6,000 crore exposure, led by IDBI (Rs 2,158 crore exposure, Rs 1,528 crore guarantee), met May 30 to urge offshore restraint ahead of a foreign lender meeting in Singapore on June 5–6; RBI rules excluding forex loans from foreign banks' Tier-1 capital from fiscal 2002 may accelerate the decision.

A quantitative cross-sectional study assessed lung function decline among adults with heroin use disorder receiving methadone at the Muhimbili National Hospital medication-assisted therapy clinic in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Systematic sampling enrolled 310 participants between May 2022 and July 2023; 302 completed spirometry. Participants had a mean age of 42.78 years, and 95.7% were male. Most smoked cigarettes, and 20.9% were underweight.

Lung function decline was identified in 28.5% of participants, with a mean age at onset of 44 years. Restrictive abnormalities were most common (13.2%), followed by obstructive abnormalities (11%) and mixed abnormalities (4.3%). Respiratory symptoms were reported by 37.7% of participants.

Binary logistic regression identified underweight (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.73), HIV infection (aOR 2.61), and a history of pulmonary tuberculosis (aOR 2.48) as independent factors associated with lung function decline. Other examined demographic and substance-use variables were not statistically significant. The authors recommended routine lung-function screening in medication-assisted therapy settings to identify undiagnosed or underdiagnosed lung disease. A limitation was the inability to perform bronchodilator reversibility testing to distinguish asthma from COPD among participants with obstructive abnormalities.

The Pennsylvania Superior Court affirmed Clay Williams’s judgment and sentence for the 2005 shooting death of Mizael Velez during an attempted cell-phone robbery at a Philadelphia Chinese store. A jury convicted Williams of first-degree murder, robbery, two firearms offenses, and possessing instruments of crime. He received life imprisonment without parole for murder and concurrent sentences for robbery and carrying a firearm without a license.

Williams raised suppression, sufficiency, evidentiary, juror, and ineffective-assistance claims. The court found his Rule 1925(b) statement timely because the record did not establish proper notice of an extension order, but deemed the suppression and sufficiency claims waived because they did not specifically identify the alleged error or unproved elements. It also found the cumulative-evidence claim waived because Williams neither developed the argument nor cited supporting authority. The court declined to address three ineffective-assistance claims on direct appeal because no hearing or dedicated record had been developed, dismissing them without prejudice for post-conviction review. It denied Williams’s petition to remand to develop the record on the juror disclosure, noting that counsel had raised no objection at trial.

The passage introduces BALLAST (Bayesian Active Learning with Lookahead Amendment for Sea-drifter Trajectories), a method for placing Lagrangian ocean-drifter observers. Ocean currents, important for mapping heat, nutrients, pollutants and sediments, are inferred from buoys, satellites and free-floating drifters; drifters are increasingly used because they sample spatial and temporal flow properties at relatively low cost and represent the Lagrangian specification of flows. Existing placement campaigns use space-filling designs, ad-hoc expert judgement, or hand-crafted criteria under Lagrangian data assimilation; an explicit active-learning placement strategy has not previously been presented. BALLAST treats placement as sequential experimental design, selecting at each predetermined measurement time the location maximising expected information gain (negative posterior entropy) of a spatio-temporal vector-output Gaussian process (GP) surrogate for the time-dependent vector field. The surrogate uses a vector-output Helmholtz kernel with a separable Matérn 3/2 temporal kernel, over a finite time interval and rectangular spatial domain discretised in time and space. BALLAST accounts for the Lagrangian data structure by simulating hypothetical trajectories, uses an information-theoretic utility, and applies the GP SPDE approach for efficiency, together with a new posterior sampling method combining standard GP regression and the SPDE approach. Contributions are introducing active learning to Lagrangian observer placement, the BALLAST amendment itself, and the new sampling method; results indicate noticeable benefits on synthetic and high-fidelity ocean current models.

An ETFO-commissioned report finds that Ontario’s 1997 funding formula has created an “upside-down equity”: wealthier school boards raise nearly $200 million more through school-based fundraising than the government provides to lower-income communities. Needy schools receive about $179 per student through learning opportunities grants, while fundraising averages $280 per student; disparities are wider at the school level. Ontario spends $23 billion, or $12,107 per inflation-adjusted student, ranking fifth nationally, but special education, ESL and maintenance remain underfunded. ETFO recommends increased funding and staffing for special-needs and mental-health services, external reviews and funding evaluations every five years. The province recently added $219 million for 875 teachers and 1,600 education workers. School-generated funds support enrichment programs, computers and equipment.

A cross-sectional analysis of 1,284 Kailuan cohort participants evaluated 2006–2022 blood pressure measurements alongside 2020–2022 MRI findings. Long-term visit-to-visit variability in systolic BP, diastolic BP, and pulse pressure was assessed, with variability independent of the mean as the primary measure. MRI markers included white matter hyperintensities, lacunae, cerebral microbleeds, and visible perivascular spaces; their combined burden was categorized from none to severe.

Cerebral small vessel disease was present in 69.3% of participants. High systolic BP variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and perivascular spaces, while high diastolic BP variability was associated with lacunae. High pulse pressure variability was associated with moderate and severe cSVD burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces. Associations varied by age and hypertension status: among participants under 60, high pulse pressure variability was associated with severe cSVD, lacunae, and perivascular spaces, whereas significant effects of systolic and pulse pressure variability on overall burden were confined to participants with hypertension. Results were unchanged in sensitivity analyses. No significant associations with white matter hyperintensities or cerebral microbleeds remained after adjustment for mean BP. Limitations included a single MRI assessment, possible reverse causation, and selection bias.

The lecture examines payment-system problems: excessive intermediaries and parallel ledgers, high costs, delayed merchant settlement, limited financial inclusion, slow cross-border currency conversion, chargebacks and lack of finality, privacy concerns, cyberattacks, and identity theft. Blockchain may reduce networking and verification costs, support shared ledgers, and enable programmable payments through smart contracts. Its challenges include scalability, transaction costs, processing speed, interoperability, error resolution, governance, regulation, liquidity, and the tension between immutability and consumer recourse.

Participants debate whether blockchain is necessary, could improve existing systems, or merely catalyze incumbents to innovate. India’s non-blockchain payment infrastructure illustrates how established rails can address inclusion, while blockchain may be especially valuable where legal and financial infrastructure is weak. Discussion also covers censorship resistance, smart-contract limitations, crypto payment providers, institutional blockchain projects, and incumbent patent activity.

Finally, the class evaluates using crypto as a bridge between fiat currencies in cross-border payments. Such systems could reduce intermediaries, shorten settlement, and lower costs for small transfers, but introduce extra conversions, bid-ask spreads, volatility, reserve, liquidity, arbitrage, and adoption risks.

Password protection lets the host lock a card; password data stays in nonvolatile registers. Locked cards permit basic commands but deny data access and relock automatically after power-on if previously set. Lock/unlock requires transfer state and card selection and resembles a single-block write.

The article explains Bollinger Bands—typically a 20-period moving average with bands two standard deviations above and below—and asks ChatGPT to create and backtest two strategies using Python. It tests a squeeze strategy on SPY data from 1993, identifying a squeeze when Bollinger Bands fall inside Keltner Channels based on two times the average true range. The strategy buys and holds while both Bollinger Bands remain within the Keltner Channels and sells otherwise. Results showed low, erratic compounded returns and a sizable drawdown; risk-adjusted improvements did not make the strategy notably profitable. The authors conclude that ChatGPT completed the backtest effectively but generated a strategy unsuitable for live trading.

Official certifications from 1891 and 1900 authenticate the crew list and attached documents for the bark *Cape Horn Pigeon*, of New Bedford under Thomas Scullan. The shipping agreement covers a voyage from San Francisco of up to 12 months to the North Pacific and Arctic oceans or elsewhere, for whaling, walrusing, and trade. Officers and crew agreed to share freight on cargo shipped by other vessels, refrain from trading, and remain aboard eight days after discharge, paying $2 daily for absence. Advances bear 15% annual interest. Crew members must obey officers, seek whale oil, preserve vessel and cargo, and remain aboard without leave until discharge. The master must maintain logbook records concerning discipline, drunkenness, unauthorized absence, women aboard, and disability. Watch officers must prevent unauthorized women from boarding, with specified pay forfeitures for failures, misconduct, and related offenses.
