The paper introduces RADAR, a black-box routing framework that selects the reasoning language model and reasoning budget for each query according to a user’s performance–cost preference. RADAR combines a two-parameter item response theory model, which estimates query difficulty and discrimination from frozen embeddings and scalar ability for each model configuration, with multi-objective optimization using linear or Chebyshev scalarization. New configurations can be added through adaptive calibration on a small, dynamically selected query set. The router operates before model inference, adds about seven milliseconds of latency, requires no fine-tuning or mid-generation model switching, and supports standard API use. Experiments show strong performance–cost tradeoffs, including matching 90% of OpenAI o4-mini’s high-reasoning performance on MATH-500 at 1.31% of its cost and on FRAMES at 10% of its cost, while generalizing to out-of-domain queries and new configurations.

Forecasters monitored a slowing outflow boundary, storms near Gulf moisture in southeast Missouri, and an MCV that could trigger a severe bow over part of the Tri-State, though duration and intensity were uncertain.

Milwaukee's score in the Campaign for Black Male Achievement's "Promise of Place" report, which measured 50 cities, rose from 63 to 71 since 2015, ranking 13th. Cited supports include city commitment, My Brother's Keeper initiatives, the Department of Black and Latino Male Achievement and the MyBlackStory.us website. CBMA, launched a decade ago as a three-year campaign tied to Obama's My Brother's Keeper initiative, is directing added resources to five cities with wide racial disparities and facilitated an exchange with Oakland's African-American Male Achievement Initiative. Ald. Khalif Rainey said the Black Male Achievement Advisory Council is in limbo since Community Engagement and Achievement Collaborative director Mike Williams was fired, and that increased engagement has yet to produce lower crime or higher black male graduation rates; MPS four-year graduation rates are 49 percent for African-American males and 57 percent for Latino males. Department strategies include improved school climate, positive media narratives, expanded manhood academies and hiring more male teachers of color.

Reckitt Benckiser’s shares trade roughly 15% below their 52-week highs across London and unlisted U.S. tickers, with a P/E ratio of 22.79 versus 24.62 for household-products companies and 25.03 for the S&P 500. The article attributes the discount partly to the South Korean dehumidifier controversy, which caused at least 92 deaths and further injuries, and the $17.9 billion Mead Johnson acquisition, which moved the company into a sector where it has limited expertise. It counters that the dehumidifier incident was a one-time event confined to South Korea, while Reckitt Benckiser’s established health and hygiene brands remain profitable.

Debt rose sharply, but the company holds £765 million in cash and received $4.2 billion from selling its food business, easing concern about servicing debt. The sale also sharpens its focus on health and hygiene products, which represent 83% of its portfolio, and on developing markets, particularly China, where Mead Johnson is established. The article highlights a 2.37% dividend yield, a decade of dividend stability, and a 53% payout ratio, and concludes that the discounted valuation represents an attractive entry point.

Protesters rallied at Laguna’s Main Beach on Feb. 3 against the Trump administration’s proposed expansion of offshore oil and gas drilling. The plan would lease 47 areas from 2019–2024, including seven in the Pacific, and would offer California’s first new offshore drilling leases since 1984.

Baylor NAACP created the hashtag #myblackhistory, which enables African-American students to share diverse perspectives on their experiences. Maryse Bombito, the organization's press and publicity chair, came up with the idea and films students discussing what they love about being black, aiming to celebrate the present as well as the past. Participant Danielle Sherman said black culture should be celebrated year-round, not just in February. The group also marked the NAACP's 108th founders day with a screening of "A Raisin in the Sun." President Reginald Singletary said the organization gives students a platform for continued work. Upcoming supported events include a Black Heritage Banquet, an All For One Soiree and an Asian Student Association fashion show, open to all students.

Healthy U is a six-week interactive small-group workshop offered by the Area Agency on Aging and Preble County Council on Aging to help people manage chronic conditions. It covers chronic pain, nutrition, exercise, medication use, emotions, and communication with doctors and family through action planning, problem-solving, decision-making, and social support. The workshops meet Tuesdays, March 6–April 10, from 9:30 a.m. to noon at 800 East St. Clair Street in Eaton. Advance registration is required by calling 937-456-4947 or emailing hsteele@prebleseniorcenter.org or scopes@prebleseniorcenter.org.

Constable Godknows Dube, 36, who faced rape charges in Gwanda, was found hanging from a tree at Gungwe Police Base, allegedly by suicide, around 6AM on Wednesday. He was due in court on October 26. No suicide note was found, but a source said the allegations may have caused him psychological pressure.

The Third Circuit affirmed the district court’s ruling that Vigilant’s policy provided primary coverage for the $87,500 settlement paid by Essex. Travelers’ Endorsement 0192 expressly made its coverage excess over valid, collectible insurance available to Essex as an additional insured, and no other provision contradicted that subordination. Because the policy was unambiguous, the dispute over resolving ambiguity was moot.

University of Bonn biologists found that male cichlids exposed to conspecific alarm substances grew faster, developed larger eyes and longer dorsal-fin spines, and delayed conspicuous breeding coloration. These changes may reduce predation by making the fish harder to catch or swallow and helping them detect predators sooner. The differences occurred only in males, which remain outside breeding caves and are more exposed than females. By about one year, fish in both groups displayed similarly conspicuous coloration, a social signal used in dominance and mate attraction.

Write blocks should be erased in groups using CMD32, CMD33, then CMD38. Out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET and reset the sequence; protected sectors remain intact with WP_ERASE_SKIP set. DAT0 stays low during erasing, and final data is vendor-dependent.

UBS's Ermotti is seen as stronger than Barclays' Staley, who disregarded whistleblowing rules. UBS trades at 1.3 times tangible book value versus Barclays' 0.7, though Barclays' 9% return on tangible equity (excluding an African goodwill writedown) nears UBS's 10.9%. Both lagged U.S. peers in capital markets; UBS's wealth premium faces outflows and passive-investing shifts, suggesting Barclays' discount is too large.

Several Moffat County students are graduating after pursuing nontraditional education. Casey Copeland graduates from Monte Vista Online Academy, where he joined the National Honor Society and earned honor-roll recognition. Isaiah Harmon, Jessica Johnson and Macie Schrimsher graduate from G.O.A.L. Academy. Colin Jensen graduates through homeschooling and was accepted to Western State. John Cutler also homeschools and recently earned an automotive certificate from Colorado Northwestern Community College. Parents expressed pride in the students. The former Gympie nursing home Winston House has been redeveloped as a hybrid medical-care and short-term accommodation facility, with over $500,000 budgeted and the eastern wing designated for patient services. Century 21 manages 18 self-contained units, 95% occupied, with plans to expand to 30 by December. Medical-service completion awaits council approvals.

A Phase 2/3 trial found two 30-µg doses of BNT162b2 95% effective versus placebo at preventing COVID-19 in participants aged 16 and older, from seven days after Dose 2. Results were similar regardless of prior infection.

After the league’s four-game decision on Nathan Horton, a team spokesperson said it was final and the team would miss him. The team dedicated a playoff win to Horton, who had helped them reach the series. Since he had previously presented the team jacket, no one else presented it in his absence. With Claude’s plans unclear, the speaker was ready to step up if needed. He called the game chippy and hot, expected similar conditions, and urged smart puck decisions due to unpredictable bounces.

Moyale Barracks will host defending champions Be Forward Wanderers in an Independence Day friendly on July 6. A government watchdog urged the Education Department to resume forgiving student loans for Americans defrauded by for-profit colleges. The Office of Inspector General recommended restarting the review and discharge process, setting timeframes and controls, and noted the claims unit's staffing fell from 19 to six. Secretary DeVos has been criticized for stalling more than 95,000 claims; Senator Murray said the report confirms she shut down the borrower defense program.

The court held, on stipulated facts, that export value under Tariff Act of 1930 § 402(d) was the proper valuation basis. Appraised values excluded importer additions on entry resulting from the appraiser’s advances in similar cases.

The message reports that the presidential election occurred without extraordinary political disturbance, amid peace, prosperity, an abundant harvest, and the easing of pestilence. It mourns the death of Secretary of State Daniel Webster, praising his talents, patriotism, public service, and lasting place in national history.

In foreign relations, the administration seeks negotiations with Great Britain over disputed North Atlantic fishing rights and commercial intercourse with the British North American provinces, potentially through separate conventions. An earlier British notice concerning fisheries proved less threatening than first feared, but the disagreement over the 1818 convention remains unresolved. Tensions with Cuba have disrupted trade and mail service and prompted a formal remonstrance with Spain, although U.S. representatives were courteously received in Havana and no permanent arrangement was made. The United States declined a French and British proposal for a tripartite agreement concerning Cuba because it was viewed as constitutionally doubtful, impolitic, and ineffective. The administration maintained that it had no designs on Cuba and that annexation would be hazardous because of the island’s population, language, and potentially disruptive economic and sectional effects.

Mexico’s rejection of a transit convention and continuing negotiations over Nicaragua and Costa Rica created obstacles to an interoceanic canal and the resolution of the San Juan de Nicaragua dispute. Venezuela acknowledged longstanding U.S. citizens’ claims, though payment still required congressional action. U.S. ministers were authorized to negotiate commercial treaties with the new Argentine Confederation, and a treaty with Uruguay was concluded for Senate consideration. Further investigation removed doubts about Peru’s title to the Lobos Islands, leading the United States to acknowledge Peruvian sovereignty and arrange guano shipments on Peruvian terms.

A naval expedition to Japan was ordered to seek more open relations, protect American shipwrecked mariners from cruel treatment, and expand peaceful commerce and access to Asian markets. The Netherlands assisted the preparations.

The message recommends transferring remaining domestic duties from the State Department and constructing fireproof government buildings to protect important archives. Treasury figures showed receipts exceeding expenditures, a substantial balance, continued debt reduction, and significant imports and exports. The administration reaffirmed support for protective duties to preserve domestic manufacturing, employment, and farm markets, while also recommending specific duties or home valuation where feasible to prevent invoice fraud and unfair competition. It also opposed tariffs that charged more on raw materials than on goods manufactured from them.

Unresolved treaties left California and Oregon tribes without recognized land rights, prompting requests for legislation either removing them or assigning them lands. Sioux treaty amendments received tribal assent and opened territory for settlement, while Seminole leaders acknowledged their obligation to leave Florida and began preliminary removal arrangements. The government also reported expanded surveying and disposition of public lands, completion of most census work, a proposed analytical publication of patents, and progress on an asylum for the District of Columbia and military insane.

Congress was urged to resolve a restriction on Mexican boundary surveying expenditure, complete the Rio Grande survey, and fulfill treaty obligations. Washington’s water supply, bridges, streets, and public grounds also required attention. Federal forces had largely restrained Indian incursions, but the government urged Texas to reserve land for tribes within its borders to prevent conflict. Appropriations were recommended for coastal fortifications and nationally significant river and harbor improvements.

The Navy was active in preparations for the Japan expedition, surveys in Asian and African waters, and exploration of the Amazon and La Plata regions. The administration supported a permanent corps of seamen, Naval Academy reorganization, and an apprenticeship system for training recruits. Postal receipts had fallen after rate reductions, but the message urged continued cheap postage in expectation that correspondence would increase with population and business. Additional legislation was recommended on foreign consuls, military expeditions, archives, public lands, roads, agriculture, pensions, military organization, statutory revision, private claims, and stronger penalties for bribery and corruption.

The message affirmed a policy of nonintervention in other nations’ domestic affairs, arguing that revolutions without preparation for self-government could produce anarchy and renewed despotism. It supported national progress through industry, transportation, education, and constitutional government while warning against both reckless constitutional changes and aggressive interference abroad. The president closed by citing peaceful and prosperous conditions, friendly foreign relations, and the nation’s ability to provide refuge for newcomers from Europe, and retired from office with gratitude for his public service.

The Big Ten is discussing a private capital deal that could inject at least $2 billion into the league and its schools. The proposal includes extending the conference’s grant of rights for 10 years to 2046 and creating a commercial entity, tentatively named Big Ten Enterprises, to manage media rights, sponsorships and other revenue streams. An outside investor would receive annual distributions based on its stake without control over conference decisions or board seats. Immediate, tiered payments of at least nine figures per school are being considered, with larger-branded schools potentially receiving more. The plan has support from nearly every member, but some major brands remain uncommitted and unanimous approval is required. Three private capital entities are under consideration, no vote has occurred, and a decision is expected in coming weeks, though it is neither imminent nor certain.

A cousin’s planned move from New York City to Nevada prompts discussion of seasonal affective disorder (SAD), a recurring depression associated with seasonal changes, particularly winter. Winter depression is most common, while summer depression is rare. SAD affects an estimated 1–10% of the global population, especially people far from the equator and women, and roughly 10 million Americans. Although seasonal illness has long been documented, its cause remains uncertain. Reduced sunlight may disrupt serotonin and melatonin levels, though some scientists question whether SAD exists.

Symptoms include fatigue, difficulty waking, cravings, weight changes, poor concentration, depression, social withdrawal, and aches; summer SAD may cause insomnia, appetite loss, and anxiety. Untreated SAD can worsen and contribute to eating disorders or suicidal thoughts. Treatments include bright-light therapy, medication, psychotherapy, meditation, and relaxation. Because other conditions can resemble SAD, medical consultation is recommended. Preventive measures include exercise, outdoor time, social activity, adequate sleep, a balanced diet, stress reduction, full-spectrum lighting, plants, and colorful surroundings.

The Arms Index, or TRIN, is a market-sentiment oscillator created by Richard W. Arms in 1967 to assess market strength through advances and declines in stock prices and volume. It is calculated as (Increasing Volume ÷ Decreasing Volume) ÷ (Increasing Stocks ÷ Decreasing Stocks). A reading of 1.0 indicates balance; readings below 1.0 are generally viewed as bullish, while readings above 1.0 indicate bearish bias. Readings above 3.0 may signal an oversold market and potential bullish reversal, while readings below 0.50 may signal an overbought market and potential decline.

The AD Volume Line tracks net advancing volume to measure buying and selling pressure. It confirms index moves when moving in the same direction and can signal bullish or bearish divergence. Market breadth reveals how many stocks contribute to an index’s performance and can show that most stocks are weakening despite a rising index.

TRIN should not be used alone and requires backtesting and confirmation from other indicators or chart patterns. In the cited backtests, an initial strategy produced 522 trades and an average gain of 0.39% per trade but was considered untradable. Adding a second indicator while requiring TRIN above 100 increased the average gain to 0.66%, with a 77% win rate and a 2.4 profit factor; the second indicator alone averaged a 0.42% gain.

Pitt students Trisha Klan, Bethany Peng, and Madeline Borsos describe the demands of holiday hospital work. Klan, a patient care technician at Jefferson Hospital, works Christmas and has observed increased emergency-room visits. Workers cite possible nursing-home admissions for elderly patients and holiday isolation leading to depression and suicidal ideation, which Klan monitors to prevent self-harm. Seasonal car accidents also increase ER volume. Peng, a registered nurse at Allegheny General facing her first Christmas shift, expects a busy, unpredictable workload caring for patients too ill to go home, with little time for breaks or meals. Nurses may alternate years off but receive overtime holiday pay. Borsos, a UPMC clinical and on-call research assistant, handles overnight shifts, trauma and acutely ill patients, and ICU and operating-room follow-ups. Holiday decorations throughout the units help make hospitals feel more like home.

The paper proposes the Pilot-and-Adaptive Stable Trading (PAST) framework for edge-assisted UAV networks with dynamic UAV demands, mobility, and edge-server resources. PAST operates in two stages. PilotAO establishes pre-signed, overbooking-enabled trading agreements between UAV buyers and edge-server sellers through risk-aware many-to-many matching, considering expected utilities, service costs, penalties, compensation, and overbooking risks. It is based on a Gale–Shapley-style procedure and is designed to provide individual rationality, strong stability, competitive equilibrium, and weak Pareto optimality. AdaptAO then monitors agreement fulfillment and market conditions, using a double deep Q-network within a Markov decision process to decide whether and how to renew agreements and overbooking rates.

The model divides time into broader trading units representing complete UAV missions and smaller trading units representing individual service transactions. UAV mobility follows a Markov process, while edge servers’ resources vary partly because of Poisson-distributed demand from other users. Evaluations use the Chicago taxi dataset, 100 simulation runs, and comparisons with online spot trading, static futures trading with and without overbooking, greedy matching, and random matching. PAST substantially reduces decision and completion latency relative to online spot trading and improves social welfare, task completion, and resource utilization over static futures methods. Online spot trading retains the highest social welfare and average resource utilization but incurs the greatest overhead; greedy and random methods have lower overhead but substantially poorer welfare. The results also confirm that UAV payments do not exceed received value and edge-server service costs do not exceed payments.

Future work will address privacy-preserving mechanisms, machine-learning-based task specification such as target detection, and extensions to heterogeneous multi-UAV, multi-edge-server networks.

USDA predictions of record U.S. meat consumption in 2018 obscured a decades-long shift in diets. Per capita beef consumption peaked in the 1970s and fell about one-third, pork remained relatively steady, and chicken consumption more than doubled. Health concerns, greater workforce participation by women, convenient chicken products, increased production efficiency and lower chicken prices helped drive this shift. High meat prices contributed to declining consumption from 2005 to 2014, though meat use has since rebounded.

Beef remains far more environmentally intensive than chicken and plant-based foods, and its consumption continued to rise globally. Researchers say further reductions in high-consuming countries are needed to limit warming to 2°C. WRI will model how national and global diets must shift toward plant-based foods by 2050 to support nearly 10 billion people within environmental limits.

The lecture surveys empirical research on price discrimination, asking whether firms discriminate, whether observed prices are consistent with profit-maximizing models, and how discrimination affects profits, consumer surplus, and welfare. It emphasizes that online information may expand opportunities for targeting without necessarily producing large economic gains.

Early studies examined price differences between products and customer groups. Severin Borenstein used detailed cost accounting to argue that the large price gap between leaded and unleaded gasoline reflected discrimination rather than production costs. Andrea Shepard compared Massachusetts gas stations offering self-service, full-service, or both and found markups consistent with second-degree discrimination through higher-priced full service. Audit studies of automobile bargaining produced different estimates of racial and gender discrimination: Ayres and Siegelman reported substantially higher initial offers for Black and female buyers, while Penny Goldberg’s survey-based study found no racial price difference. Katy Graddy’s observations at New York’s Fulton Street Fish Market found Asian buyers receiving prices 7% below white buyers for the same fish. The lecturer notes limitations from small samples, vehicle heterogeneity, and reliance on remembered purchase prices.

Morton, Zettelmeyer, and Silva-Risso combined two million Autobytel requests with transaction-level J.D. Power data covering 671,000 purchases from 3,562 dealerships. Controlling for vehicles, accessory costs, location, timing, and other factors, they found much smaller pricing differences than earlier audits: buyers in predominantly Black areas paid about 1.5% more, those in Hispanic areas 1.1% more, and those in Asian areas 0.4% less; women paid about 0.2% more. Buyers from more educated or homeowner-heavy areas paid less, suggesting advantages associated with search sophistication, information, or bargaining ability. Race premiums roughly halved among customers trading in cars, consistent with greater ability to comparison shop, and largely disappeared among Autobytel users, who paid about 0.9% less overall than traditional buyers. Because the data lacked exogenous price variation, the study could not directly estimate elasticities; the lecturer presents search costs, differential preferences, and profit-maximizing discrimination as possible explanations and notes that banning mean discrimination would likely have little effect on dealer profits.

Shiller studied online price discrimination using ComScore browsing data for 61,000 users. Netflix’s DVD-by-mail service provided a large identifiable subscriber population, observable demand indicators, and costs that could be estimated from accounting data. Under a profit-maximizing monopolist assumption, known costs and prices allowed demand elasticities to be inferred without observed price variation. A logit demand model used demographics, internet-use measures, and visits to 4,600 websites, with a Lasso-like maximum-likelihood procedure retaining roughly 900 variables. Demographic targeting was estimated to raise Netflix profits by 0.3% and consumer surplus by 0.05%, whereas web-based targeting could raise profits by 13% while lowering consumer surplus by about 0.5%. The lecturer describes second-degree discrimination through different subscription plans as potentially more powerful and notes limits arising from maintained demand assumptions, uncertain welfare properties, privacy practices, and consumers’ ability to obscure browsing behavior.

Dubé and Misra used internal access to ZipRecruiter to randomize monthly subscription prices among 7,867 small firms. Firms entering information associated with fewer than 50 employees and one to three planned hires received offers from $19 to $399 rather than the standard $99. The researchers estimated heterogeneous valuations and price sensitivities from 133 firm characteristics using maximum likelihood, Lasso, and a Weighted Likelihood Bootstrap Lasso; the latter performed best out of sample. ZipRecruiter’s $99 price was below the estimated short-run profit-maximizing price of $327, and the company subsequently raised its standard price to $249. Estimated personalized prices ranged widely, and a practical scheme capped at $499 was predicted to increase profits by 8.2% over uniform pricing. The model’s unrestricted personalized prices were also predicted to reduce consumer surplus by about 25% and total welfare.

A follow-up randomized experiment assigned firms to $99, $249, or personalized prices between $129 and $499. Model predictions of signup rates and revenue closely matched observed outcomes, supporting an approximately 8% short-run profit gain from personalization; nevertheless, ZipRecruiter retained the $249 uniform price. The lecturer emphasizes that these experiments identify only short-run individual responses and omit word-of-mouth effects, general-equilibrium changes, network effects from reducing job postings, and possible reputational or political costs of discriminatory pricing. Overall, the research suggests that rich behavioral data can improve customer segmentation, but demographic targeting has limited value, broader targeting may yield modest profit gains, and the welfare consequences can be adverse.

This article, authored by Michelle Barker, Jeremy Cohen, Pedro Hernández Serrano, Daniel S. Katz, Kim Martin, Dan Rudmann and Hugh Shanahan, outlines the work of the Policies in Research Organisations for Research Software (PRO4RS) Working Group (WG), a joint Research Software Alliance (ReSA) and Research Data Alliance (RDA) initiative that ran from 2023 to 2025. Led by eight co-chairs with more than 100 participants over 18 months, the WG aimed to help research performing organisations (RPOs) create, share, manage and re-use research software and develop, align and implement related policies as part of FAIR and open science. It adopted the FAIR for Research Software Principles definition of research software.

The WG produced four outputs: a global list of publicly available institutional research software policies; a report summarising resources for stakeholders on enabling institutional policy change; a report identifying policy gaps; and case studies of four research organisations' implementation efforts. Analysis showed that while many institutions mention research software in infrastructure, licensing or open science policies, few address it substantively in research assessment reform, and policies often lack operational detail, with some possibly existing but not publicly accessible. Existing metrics such as downloads and GitHub stars were found unreliable for assessing software importance.

The article reviews broader initiatives — including DORA, CoARA, Science Europe, OpenAIRE, OPUS, the RDA SHARC Interest Group, the ADORE.software Toolkit and the Amsterdam Declaration on Funding Research Software Sustainability — and institutional examples from Monash University Business School and the Helmholtz Association, including the Helmholtz Research Software Directory.

The WG proposes a layered framework: an optional central research software policy, a middle layer aligning other policies (open science, legal and ethical use, intellectual property, community interaction, recognition in hiring, evaluation and promotion), and an outer layer of guidelines and frameworks enabling implementation. Three recommendations are offered: document institutional research software volume (e.g. via GitHub organisations or software directories), advocate for recognition of software's role, and engage key institutional stakeholders. The article concludes that institutions with formal research software policies remain few, and that such policies promote best practices, training, reproducibility and institutional impact. The WG was supported by EU Horizon Europe grant 101094406 via the RDA TIGER programme.

The Treasury Department is considering a draft $1 commemorative coin for the nation’s 250th anniversary featuring President Donald Trump on both sides. One side shows his profile with “IN GOD WE TRUST” and the dates 1776 and 2026; the other depicts him raising a fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, surrounded by “FIGHT FIGHT FIGHT.” Treasury said no final design has been selected. Although a law signed by Trump in 2021 authorizes $1 semiquincentennial coins, it bars portraits of living people on the reverse, raising questions about the draft’s legality. It remains unclear whether any previous commemorative coin has depicted a living president.

Following President Tyler’s December 1842 recommendation, Congress funded a diplomatic post in the Sandwich Islands. George Brown, appointed in March 1843, sought impartial treatment for Americans; the King promised them equal privileges with the most favored nation. Disputes over John Wiley’s denied jury trial, discriminatory treaty terms, and advice from Attorney General John Ricord prompted the King to request Brown’s recall, though the U.S. government approved his conduct. The United States recognized Hawaiian independence in 1844. In 1846, France and Great Britain modified jury and liquor provisions without fully recognizing Hawaiian independence, while a Danish treaty first fully acknowledged it. Ten Eyck continued pressing for the objectionable British-style jury clause despite Buchanan’s warning. Stalled negotiations and disputes over Americans’ rights and foreign factions marked his hostile tenure. Criticized by Buchanan, he resigned in September 1848; Charles Fames succeeded him in January 1849.

## Summary

This passage is an excerpt from NVIDIA's A100 Tensor Core GPU whitepaper, describing the eighth-generation data center GPU built on the Ampere GA100 architecture (TSMC 7nm N7, 54.2 billion transistors, 826 mm² die), its predecessor generations (Tesla V100's 2017 introduction of Tensor Cores; Turing T4), and its deployment across AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

**Architecture and hardware.** The A100 configuration includes 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, five HBM2 stacks, and ten 512-bit memory controllers (the full GA100 has 128 SMs). Each SM has 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory (1.5x V100's 128 KB), with maximum shared memory allocation raised 1.7x to 164 KB. The GPU has 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth (1.7x V100) and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) with 2.3x the read bandwidth. L2 is divided into two partitions of 40 slices each, with SECDED ECC protecting HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files. Compute Data Compression yields up to 4x DRAM read/write bandwidth, 4x L2 read bandwidth, and 2x L2 capacity.

**Tensor Cores and sparsity.** Third-generation Tensor Cores perform 256 FP16 FMAs per clock each (four per SM, doubling Volta/Turing SM throughput), supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary. Versus V100: TF32 is 10x faster than FP32 FMA (20x with sparsity); FP16/FP32 mixed precision is 2.5x faster (5x with sparsity); BF16 matches FP16 rates; FP64 reaches 2.5x V100 performance (19.5 TFLOPS peak); sparse INT8 runs up to 20x faster. Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a 2:4 non-zero pattern, doubling Tensor Core throughput and halving data footprint; NVIDIA's recipe (dense training → pruning → fine-tuning) showed virtually no inference accuracy loss across dozens of networks. TF32 was the fastest and most robust mode in cuSOLVER's TCAIRS iterative refinement solver tests (geomean 2.0x over the FP64 solver), with up to 4x speedups on large complex matrices.

**MIG.** Multi-Instance GPU partitions an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with fully isolated paths through crossbar ports, L2 banks, memory controllers, and DRAM busses, delivering up to 7x more instances for CSPs at no additional cost. Each instance has dedicated GPCs, L2 slice groups, memory controllers, and frame buffer; instances are built from seven GPU slices (one Sys Pipe, one GPC, one 10-slice L2 group each). Compute Instances within a GPU Instance permit independent context switching and support Volta-style MPS. MIG is compute-mode only, and L2 set-aside is disabled in MIG mode. Key use cases include multi-tenant vGPU rental, single-tenant/single-user, and single-tenant/multi-user; vGPU migration between instances and GPUs reduces fragmentation and enables servicing without killing jobs.

**Interconnect and other features.** Third-generation NVLink delivers 50 Gbit/s per signal pair (vs 25.78 in V100), with 12 links (vs 6) totaling 600 GB/s, plus non-posted writes and improved error attribution/recovery. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 (31.5 GB/s x16) and SR-IOV. Additional features include a 5-core NVJPG hardware JPEG decoder, an optical flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved atomics (11x FP16, 2.7x FP32 over V100), five NVDEC units (vs one), and new error/fault detection, isolation, and containment technology.

**CUDA 11 advances.** CUDA 11 supports third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 residency controls. Task graphs provide define-once/run-repeatedly execution, with A100 launch optimizations (single submission of multiple work items, faster kernel upload) and execution dependency optimizations (multi-dependency forks executed at lowest latency, grid-to-grid latency speedups). Async copy loads global memory directly into shared memory bypassing the register file, in BYPASS and ACCESS variants. Asynchronous barriers separate arrival from wait, enabling producer-consumer models and overlap of copies with compute, with synchronization at any thread subset granularity. L2 residency controls let programs mark data as persisting or streaming, with set-aside in 2.5 MB increments, useful for LSTM recurrent weights and large global-memory histograms (2.5x faster than V100). Cooperative Groups adds a group-wide async-copy collective and a hardware-accelerated reduce API (single-step warp reductions), cutting grid synchronization overhead by up to 30%.

**DGX A100.** The third-generation DGX A100 system packs eight A100 GPUs (six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth) into a 6U form factor delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, up to 6x the V100-based DGX-1 for AI training, with eight ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters at 200 Gb/s and support for the Magnum IO SDK and NVIDIA DeepOps. MIG can yield up to 56 isolated accelerators per system. Its software stack centers on a minimal OS/driver install with application and SDK software provisioned through the NGC Private Registry.

The paper examines how an inquiry-based community oral history project affects elementary preservice teachers' (PSTs') learning and teaching of citizenship, and whether it could become a permanent assignment in social studies methods courses. Citizenship education, positioned as central to U.S. social studies, is under-taught in elementary and middle schools, which have marginalized social studies in favor of tested subjects; NAEP (2024) reported nearly 80% of students lacking proficiency in states requiring an 8th-grade civics exam. Literature reviewed indicates PSTs enter teacher preparation with little citizenship experience, often equating citizenship with patriotism or character education, and lack skills in questioning, inquiry, controversial topics, emotions, historical thinking, multicultural education, and community engagement. Drawing on Dewey, Rugg, Freire, Vygotsky, and others, the author argues oral histories offer experiential, perspectival, inquiry-based learning that connects teaching to real-life issues and community collaboration.

Methodologically, the study used a qualitative case design at a South Florida university, involving 38 of 71 elementary PSTs across four K-6 social studies methods courses. Participants selected citizenship topics, secured anonymous community interviewees, wrote ten open-ended questions, recorded and transcribed interviews using technology, and completed a post-survey. Data were thematically coded by the researcher, verified by external reviewers, and triangulated. Limitations include no pre-survey and only four course sections.

Findings: Topics ranged widely (immigration, military, entrepreneurship, poverty, civil rights, natural disasters, Cold War, incarceration, 9/11, among others). PSTs learned personal experiences beyond textbook and media portrayals, saw controversial issues magnified, felt interviewees' emotions, grew more appreciative of citizenship and elders, gained confidence teaching difficult topics, and planned to have students conduct oral histories and bring community members into classrooms. Some struggled with question preparation and securing interviewees. The study concludes oral histories deepen PSTs' understanding of citizenship's link to democracy, inspire civic engagement, and build foundations for citizenship for future students; proposed future research includes professional development workshops, pre-surveys, and studies of classroom implementation.

On January 27, 2017, NVIDIA Land Development, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of NVIDIA Corporation, entered into an amendment to its June 19, 2015 Participation Agreement with Wachovia Service Corporation, Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and a syndicate of other institutions, related to construction and lease of the company's new Santa Clara, California headquarters. The amendment conformed certain representations, warranties and covenants to NVIDIA's October 7, 2016 Credit Agreement, increasing the maximum total leverage ratio to 3.5:1.0 (from 3.0:1.0) and deleting the minimum interest coverage ratio requirement (previously 3.5:1.0). The Participation Agreement was filed as Exhibit 10.1 to NVIDIA's Form 10-Q for the period ended July 26, 2015; the Credit Agreement was filed as Exhibit 1.1 to its Form 8-K filed October 13, 2016. The amendment will be filed as an exhibit to NVIDIA's Form 10-K for fiscal year 2017. The report was signed on February 2, 2017 by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

A doctor who treated 12 Grenfell Tower casualties said staff prepared cyanide-poisoning kits because older, untreated polyurethane foam in furniture can emit deadly hydrogen cyanide when burned, particularly in an enclosed fire. Such foam can exceed 760°C within minutes, and one breath of its superheated toxic gas can incapacitate someone. Around 60 people were taken to six London hospitals, with scores initially reported missing. Fire crews searched most flats but expected no further survivors; drones were used because the tower’s structural integrity was uncertain. The cause remained unknown, and officials promised a full investigation into how the fire started and spread so rapidly. Grenfell Tower had been refurbished in 2016, and the contractor said the work met all relevant building, fire, and safety standards.

PITB’s Plan9 Technology Incubator 10th Launchpad will take place in Lahore July 17–23, opening with a two-day Makeathon and continuing with startup training, workshops and a pitch competition. Applications from Pakistani founders aged 18 or older are due June 20; teams must have one product-based technology idea, and selected non-Lahore teams must relocate for six months. Plan9 has graduated over 130 startups.

The president describes the Afghanistan surge of 30,000 additional U.S. troops, announced to refocus efforts on al Qaeda, reverse Taliban gains, and train Afghan security forces. He says U.S. and coalition forces have weakened al Qaeda and the Taliban, killed Osama bin Laden, and expanded Afghan security forces by more than 100,000. Beginning the following month, 10,000 troops will withdraw by year’s end, with 33,000 returning by the following summer. The mission will shift from combat to support, with Afghan forces assuming greater responsibility and the transition targeted for completion by 2014.

The president says political reconciliation is necessary for peace. Talks must be led by the Afghan government, and participants must break from al Qaeda, abandon violence, and follow the Afghan constitution. The United States will also continue pressing Pakistan to combat violent extremism and prevent terrorist safe havens.

He notes that the combat mission in Iraq has ended and 100,000 American troops have already withdrawn, while acknowledging continued challenges and U.S. military losses—nearly 4,500 in Iraq and more than 1,500 in Afghanistan. Calling for a pragmatic foreign policy, he advocates targeted force when necessary, international action when appropriate, and support for self-determination. In Libya, the United States is assisting allies without deploying ground troops.

Turning to domestic priorities, the president says the nation must invest in its people, encourage innovation and job creation, rebuild infrastructure, develop clean energy, and restore a shared national purpose after a decade of war. He pledges continued care, benefits, and opportunities for troops, veterans, and their families, and concludes by emphasizing unity, responsible war endings, and the promise of America.

House Republicans will meet Monday on an unfinished spending bill needed to fund the government by midnight Friday. Unresolved issues include Affordable Care Act marketplace stabilization, abortion restrictions, sexual-harassment reporting reforms, DACA and border-wall funding, and tax corrections; controversial provisions may be dropped to avert a shutdown.

Tom Barrett is a corporate growth and change agent with more than 30 years in the landscape industry. He drives revenue through innovation, coaches executives and has served for 20 years as principal of Green Water Infrastructure. His strategic, collaborative leadership emphasizes relationships, identifying patterns and helping companies achieve breakthroughs. Barrett cites Warren Buffett as a role model, reads Seth Godin, Chris Brogan and Jay Baer, and believes individual leadership remains essential despite the web’s transformation of relationships. Inspired by Marianne Williamson, he says people can achieve more than they realize. Preparations continued for joint Anglo-American negotiations with Belgian authorities over Congo purchases and supplies. Belgium was to submit lists of materials it could provide and its total requirements from the UK and US. US experts were to assess mining and Belgian material needs in the Congo, with UK representatives urged to cooperate on-site. The Department requested immediate consultations, direct Belgian government participation, and full reporting; Belgium’s Colonial Minister postponed a Washington trip and was to remain in London.

A tripartite Anglo-American-Belgian supply arrangement was proposed instead of separate bilateral agreements. The prior Anglo-Belgian purchasing agreement covering September 1, 1941–August 31, 1942 remained unsigned but was considered necessary because of the January 21, 1941 financial agreement. It was expected to be signed after the joint meeting, while the tripartite arrangement would tentatively begin September 1, 1942 to avoid overlap; the Department’s comments were requested.

Professor David Nutt developed “alcosynth,” a synthetic alcohol intended to mimic alcohol’s effects with fewer health risks and without the acetaldehyde buildup associated with hangovers. His team tested about 80 substances and narrowed them to five, with one planned for submission to Britain’s Food Standards Agency as a novel food ingredient. Nutt sought $11.8 million for final safety checks and envisioned sales in more than 100 bars by 2020 and eventual replacement of conventional alcohol by 2050.

NerdWallet ranked home affordability for 172 metro areas in the first quarter of 2018 by comparing median annual household income with the monthly principal-and-interest payment on a median-priced single-family home, assuming a 20 percent down payment and a 4.45 percent rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage, using National Association of Realtors, Census Bureau and Realtor.com data.

Decatur, Illinois, topped the most-affordable list ($73,000 median home price, $46,198 median income, $294 payment, 7.6 percent of monthly income), followed by Cumberland, Md.-W.Va., Elmira, N.Y., Binghamton, N.Y., and Peoria, Ill. San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara, Calif., was least affordable ($1.37 million median home, $110,040 income, $5,533 payment, 60.3 percent of income), ahead of Honolulu, San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward, San Diego-Carlsbad and Los Angeles-Long Beach; California holds four of the five least-affordable spots. Decatur homes cost about 1.5 times annual income versus roughly 12 times in San Jose. San Jose listings spent a median 17 days on the market, while Peoria was the quickest-selling of the most-affordable group at 77.25 days.

The passage contrasts the Duchess of Cambridge’s $8,900 delivery at London’s Lindo Wing with the high costs and poorer outcomes of maternity care in the United States. It says American delivery costs average $12,290, with cesarean sections and emergency care producing bills above $30,000, while some premature triplets incur costs exceeding $870,000.

It reports that the United States has among the OECD’s highest maternal and infant mortality rates, the shortest average life expectancy, and the highest health spending—$3.3 trillion in 2016. Americans use health services at roughly the same rate as Europeans but pay substantially more. High insurance premiums, deductibles, copayments, and coverage gaps leave many patients with large expenses, including cancer treatment and laboratory bills, while tens of thousands use crowdfunding to cover care.

The passage emphasizes the burden on young families, noting that U.S. parents may spend about 10 percent of their wealth on uncovered maternity costs, compared with costs largely borne by Britain’s National Health Service. It concludes that every mother should have access to safe, clean, comfortable delivery care and competent medical assistance without parents having to worry about paying their newborn’s medical bills.

A May 3, 2001 Enron news digest covered corporate developments, energy markets, policy issues and financial news:

- Pompano Beach scheduled a public meeting on Enron’s proposed power plant, while the city commission was set to vote on a zoning variance.
- California lawmakers considered authorizing the state to refuse electricity purchases above specified prices. Supporters argued the boycott could restrain wholesale suppliers, while economists warned that blackouts would impose greater economic costs and hardship on businesses and vulnerable consumers.
- Enron’s Indian unit, Dabhol Power, remained in a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, which owed about $48 million. Indian lenders urged government intervention, while Dabhol prepared to meet a state panel on May 11 without offering contract concessions. Enron had authorized a possible halt to power sales, raising concerns about withdrawing from or selling the $2.9 billion project.
- A Democratic National Committee release criticized the Bush administration’s energy policy as reflecting oil and gas interests, citing campaign donations, regulatory rollbacks, proposed drilling and the industry’s role on transition teams.
- Innogy began wholesale electricity trading between France and Italy and prepared to enter Germany. The company planned to emphasize trading services rather than acquiring physical assets, with France expected to be a key market.
- Mosaic Group reported first-quarter revenue of $171.8 million, up 89%, and an 18th consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth. Its Paradigm unit expanded customer-acquisition work for Enron-formed New Power.
- European telecommunications companies’ debt prospects improved as asset sales and equity plans reduced borrowing concerns, narrowing bond spreads and lowering bankruptcy-swap costs. Major telecom companies sold $100 billion in bonds the previous year.
- European corporations increasingly used credit derivatives to hedge receivables and facilitate business, though documentation designed for bonds did not directly cover private debt and required costly amendments.
- Allegheny Energy completed its purchase of three Enron gas-fired plants with 1,710 megawatts of capacity in Tennessee, Indiana and Illinois. The transaction increased Allegheny’s planned generating capacity to more than 14,000 megawatts by 2005.
- Salomon Smith Barney sharply reduced forecasts for U.S. power-generation profitability because electricity prices were expected to fall faster than natural-gas prices, while anticipating stronger trading conditions for energy merchants such as Enron.
- Fitch affirmed Northern Border Partners’ BBB+ rating and its pipeline affiliate’s A- rating, changing both outlooks to stable after reviewing acquisitions, financing plans and commodity-risk management.
- EnergieKontor signed a framework agreement with Enron Wind for 200 megawatts of turbines in Germany and Spain.
- Scottish Power reported lower annual profits and earnings and announced restructuring into three divisions focused on generation, supply and infrastructure. Potential sales of Southern Water and Thus, possible U.S. expansion and interest in Enron’s Portland General remained unresolved.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023 describes its business, operating risks, legal proceedings, properties, and share repurchase activity. The company is incorporated in California and headquartered in Cupertino. Its common stock trades on Nasdaq under “AAPL,” and nine series of notes due between 2024 and 2042 are also registered on Nasdaq. Apple is classified as a large accelerated filer. The aggregate market value of voting and non-voting stock held by non-affiliates was approximately $2.591 trillion as of March 31, 2023, and 15,552,752,000 common shares were outstanding as of October 20, 2023.

Apple designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, accessories, and related services. Its principal product lines include iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Wearables, Home and Accessories. Services include advertising, AppleCare, cloud services, digital content through platforms such as the App Store and subscription offerings, and payment services such as Apple Card and Apple Pay. The company manages five geographic reportable segments: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific. Direct channels generated 37% of 2023 net sales and indirect channels generated 63%.

The business operates in highly competitive markets characterized by pricing pressure, short product cycles, rapid technological change, and competitors with substantial resources. Apple depends on innovation, research and development, intellectual property, third-party developers, digital-content providers, resellers, and outsourced manufacturing and logistics. Risks include adverse macroeconomic and trade conditions, geopolitical or public-health disruptions, product-transition failures, component shortages, reliance on single or limited suppliers, design and manufacturing defects, inventory and asset write-downs, unavailable third-party intellectual property, cybersecurity and system failures, acquisitions, retail-store operations, legal and regulatory compliance, privacy and data-protection requirements, App Store litigation and regulatory changes, fluctuating margins, foreign exchange, credit and investment risks, tax changes, and stock-price volatility.

As of September 30, 2023, Apple had approximately 161,000 full-time equivalent employees. Its headquarters are in Cupertino, and it owned or leased facilities and land for corporate, research, data-center, retail, and other purposes in the United States and other countries.

Two significant legal matters are detailed. In the Epic case concerning App Store antitrust and unfair-competition claims, a district court ruled for Apple on nine of ten counts but required Apple to permit external purchase links. The Ninth Circuit affirmed the decision, denied further review, and stayed enforcement pending Apple’s appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court. In the Masimo matter, the International Trade Commission entered a limited exclusion order on October 26, 2023, concerning certain Apple Watch models with blood-oxygen functionality, including Series 9 and Ultra 2. The order was scheduled to take effect after an administrative review period expected to end December 25, 2023, and Apple intends to seek a stay and appeal.

Apple had 23,763 shareholders of record as of October 20, 2023. During the three months ended September 30, 2023, it repurchased 106.595 million shares for approximately $74.069 billion. At September 30, $15.9 billion had been used under the $90 billion authorization announced in May 2023, while the final $4.6 billion was used during the fourth quarter under the prior program.

This continuation application, titled “Multi-Modal Interfaces,” discloses methods, computer-readable media, and electronic devices for digital-assistant interfaces that support multiple interaction modes. Digital assistants interpret spoken or textual natural-language input, infer user intent, execute tasks through device services, and provide audible, visual, or tactile outputs.

Four disclosed method groups involve:

- Displaying received words on a touch-sensitive display, selecting a word using a different input type, modifying it based on further input, and displaying the modification.
- Using device context information to determine whether criteria for disabling an output type are met and disabling that output when they are.
- Performing a requested task, determining whether it could instead be performed using a second input type, and indicating that alternative input through an output.
- Determining whether additional input is required for a task, requesting it using a second input type, receiving it, and completing the task.

The disclosure describes client-server digital-assistant systems, including devices acting as proxies for server communication, natural-language task processing, contextual data, and user-specific data and models. Implementations may use portable multifunctional devices, multifunction devices, or personal electronic devices with touch displays or separate touch surfaces, audio components, radio circuitry, optical, proximity, motion, and contact-intensity sensors, tactile output generators, and supporting input controls.

Software components described include an operating system, contact and motion detection, graphics, text input, GPS, digital-assistant client functions, event handling, and applications for communications, media, camera, maps, calendars, web browsing, and other tasks. Event handling routes input to application views, recognizes gestures and other predefined events, and invokes data, object, or graphical updates. Supported inputs include touch, gestures, mouse, keyboard, stylus, device movement, speech, eye movement, and biometrics. The stated objectives include more intuitive and efficient interaction, context-appropriate outputs, reduced unnecessary output, and lower power use and improved battery life.
Judgment reduced by $914.36 plus interest and affirmed without costs.

The study examines whether vision-language models and multimodal large language models can support marine species recognition and conservation. Zero-shot evaluations reveal major gaps in fine-grained marine taxonomy and perception, motivating the introduction of FishNet++, a multimodal benchmark containing 99,556 images of 17,393 fish species, 35,133 species descriptions, 119,399 bounding boxes, and 706,426 key-point annotations. Descriptions were synthesized with GPT-4o from FishBase, iNaturalist, WoRMS, and NOAA information, then expert- and user-validated. Annotations cover six body-part locations and whether fish are above or below water. The dataset also includes taxonomic corrections for 266 outdated species names, 36 images of potentially unknown species, and 5,024 added images that increased the number of species with at least ten images from 495 to 804.

All evaluated models performed poorly on open-vocabulary species recognition. Qwen2.5-VL achieved 6.2% accuracy for frequent species and 0.2% for rare species, while GPT-4o reached 17.9% and 1.2%. Accuracy improved at genus and family levels, indicating that models often identify related taxa but struggle with species-level distinctions.

Diagnostic tests show that failures reflect both missing domain knowledge and weak fine-grained visual perception. Qwen2.5-VL achieved only 3.6% on bidirectional common-to-scientific name translation and performed below random chance when rejecting visually similar incorrect species. It localized whole fish comparatively well, trailing a YOLO-12 baseline, but performed substantially worse on key-part localization, where subtle features such as fin structure, eye coloration, and tail shape are important.

Retrieval-augmented generation produced modest gains, while LoRA supervised fine-tuning raised Qwen2.5-VL’s frequent-species accuracy from 6.2% to 37.0%. Explainable fine-tuning retained similar accuracy while generating supporting rationales for predictions. Overall, the results identify domain-specific training and fine-grained ecological benchmarks as necessary for improving marine species recognition.

In this final State of the Union address to the 95th Congress, President Carter reports that the state of the Union is good, though improvements are still needed, and notes that his report is the first of many in the nation's third century of independence. He congratulates President-elect Carter and the new Congress and stresses the orderly transfer of power that characterizes the American system.

Recalling the crisis of August 1974—when the Vice President and President had resigned in disgrace, the Vietnam War's after-effects lingered, the economy was unstable, inflation was soaring, and Congress and the Executive were at odds—Carter describes the recovery since then: an economy moving toward sound growth, inflation cut by more than half (from 12.2 percent to 5 percent), and more than four million jobs created since spring 1975, with over 88 million people in productive work, though unemployment remains his greatest regret. He urges passage of tax measures, including a $10 billion income tax cut, higher personal exemptions, accelerated depreciation, a lower corporate rate, and elimination of double taxation of dividends, to create productive jobs.

On crime, he reports that its growth rate fell from 18 percent annually to 2 percent, though crime remains a serious problem. On energy, he concedes unsatisfactory progress toward independence, noting reliance on foreign oil has risen from 36 to 40 percent with a $34 billion import bill this year, and urges Congress and the new administration to act on conservation, resource development, a 500-million-barrel petroleum stockpile, nuclear power, and an energy independence authority.

In foreign affairs, he cites peace, strengthened alliances with Western Europe, Japan, and Canada, the Vladivostok Accord with Brezhnev capping strategic weapons, progress toward Middle East peace, opening relations with the People's Republic of China, a new Asia-Pacific partnership, an emerging dialogue between industrial and developing nations, trade and monetary progress, new maturity in Latin American relations, and U.S. engagement in Africa favoring peace and majority rule. He urges Congress to support the new President and to guard but not obstruct its constitutional foreign policy powers, noting there can be only one Commander in Chief.

He also reports difficulties reducing the size and cost of federal government, a shortage of federal judges and excessive litigation, and urges congressional cooperation on reform and block grants. On national defense, he reports reversing the decline in real defense resources, stresses sustained long-term effort, and advocates the Trident submarine, the B-1 bomber, an advanced ICBM, and strong conventional forces to deter Soviet buildup and maintain strategic balance.

Closing, he reflects on the separation of powers, the Constitution, and his years in the House, Senate, and presidency, thanks the members of Congress, and offers his prayers that the nation's third century be illuminated by liberty and blessed with brotherhood.

The passage describes the power, reset, clock, interrupt, and peripheral characteristics of the TMS320DM814x DaVinci device. SRAM in switchable power domains automatically enters SHUTDOWN when its domain is turned off, losing its data, and returns to ACTIVE when the domain is restored; specified ALWAYS_ON SRAM can also be shut down through x_MEM_PWRDN registers. I/O supply groups independently support 1.8 V or 3.3 V, while each DDR interface separately supports 1.5 V or 1.8 V. PHYs must enter power-down mode before their domains are turned off. Low-Power Standby requires switchable domains off, the Cortex-A8 running an IDLE loop at its lowest frequency, and unnecessary blocks clock-gated.

The device uses four supply-sequencing groups, and specified power-up and power-down sequences must be followed. The 3.3-V supplies must never exceed the 1.8-V supplies by more than 2 V. PLL and analog supplies should use nearby ferrite-bead and capacitor filtering. Decoupling recommendations include 0.1-µF capacitors no larger than 0402, at least one capacitor for every two power pins, and a bulk capacitor of at least 10 µF for approximately every ten power pins. Capacitance must not delay startup enough to alter the supply sequence, and reset must remain asserted until supplies are stable.

System-level resets include power-on, external warm, emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold and warm, test, and local resets. POR resets the full chip, including test, emulation, and EMAC Switch logic; warm resets generally exclude test and emulation logic and can optionally preserve the EMAC Switch. Software cold and warm resets are initiated through PRCM registers. When reset requests occur simultaneously, only the highest-priority request is processed, and the PRM_RSTST register records the last reset. Most I/O pins enter a high-impedance state after reset, with specified exceptions for emulation pins, isolated EMAC Switch pins, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT. RSTOUT_WD_OUT is always asserted for watchdog resets and is three-stated during POR or RESET assertion. Reset isolation is supported for the PCIe subsystem and EMAC Switch, allowing them to remain operational during applicable resets.

The device accepts DEV and AUX clock sources from external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS-compatible inputs. DEV is generally 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under stated conditions; AUX is optional and supports the same range. Crystal oscillators require fundamental parallel resonance and do not support overtones. The device contains 12 top-level PLLs and four embedded PLLs; PLLs start in bypass mode and must be programmed within reference, internal, output, and module-frequency limits. PLL_USB must operate at 960 MHz when USB is used. The ARM interrupt controller supports up to 128 prioritized requests, while the C674x controller combines 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts and supports multiplexed event sources.

AC timing measurements use a 1.5-V reference for 3.3-V signals and a 4-V/ns input slew rate. Board-routing delays must be considered, and IBIS models are recommended for accurate analysis. The two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0, message-object masking, FIFO and loopback modes, automatic bus-off recovery, test-mode message-RAM access, configurable CAN pins, and interrupts. EDMA supports up to 64 channels and maps synchronization events to any of 512 parameter entries.

Advanced Event Triggering provides hardware breakpoints, data watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing. The device also supports real-time Cortex-A8 and system trace, IEEE 1149.1 JTAG, and a JTAG ID register value of 0x0B8F202F. The three-port gigabit EMAC Switch has one internal and two external ports, supports 10/100/1,000-Mbps Ethernet and MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII, and uses an MDIO interface that polls 32 PHY addresses. Its CPPI block contains 2,048 words of buffer-descriptor memory for up to 512 descriptors.

Four 32-channel GPIO modules provide configurable inputs, outputs, set/clear controls, interrupts, and open-drain operation. The GPMC provides a glueless 8- or 16-bit interface for NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom devices, with up to eight chip selects and 512 MB addressing. The ELM locates 4-, 8-, or 16-bit BCH errors in NAND data. The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports video, multichannel L-PCM audio, CEC, DDC, and specified display formats; PCB guidance requires controlled TMDS impedance, paired vias, pullups or integrated ESD protection, and HDMI protection capacitance no greater than 5 pF. The HDVPSS provides video input and output interfaces, two processing pipelines, scaling, de-interlacing, alpha blending, color-space and pixel-format conversion, picture-in-picture, multiple graphics layers, and an HDMI transmitter.

The lecture reviews relativistic kinematics for particle and nuclear physics. It defines \(\beta=v/c\), the Lorentz factor \(\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-\beta^2}\), and the energy and momentum relations \(E=\gamma mc^2\), \(p=\gamma mv\), and \(E^2=p^2+m^2\). It explains that energy and momentum transform like space and time under Lorentz transformations, while the invariant mass-squared \(m^2s\) remains unchanged. Total energy and momentum are conserved in reactions but are not Lorentz invariant.

The invariant mass of decay products can be used in any frame to identify a parent particle, as in measuring two photons from Higgs-boson decay. The lecture contrasts fixed-target collisions with colliding-beam experiments and introduces exercises involving Z-boson production, Higgs-Strahlung, deuteron binding energy, photon reabsorption, antiproton and pion production, pion decay, and Compton scattering. These exercises apply relativistic kinematics to determine collision energies, particle speeds, momenta, and photon wavelengths without analyzing the underlying dynamics.

NVIDIA’s GA10x-class Ampere architecture introduces second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, structural sparsity, and GDDR6X support. The architecture provides up to twice the performance of the prior Turing generation in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its Tensor Cores can double effective throughput through sparsity, while its RT Cores improve ray/triangle intersections and support concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 is positioned for data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. Its PCIe Gen4 interface provides up to twice the bandwidth of Turing-based GPUs. Each A40 has 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB by linking two GPUs with third-generation NVLink. It includes three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, supports vGPU software and Quadro Sync, defaults to virtualization with display outputs disabled, and is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz, including two 8K displays with separate cables. They support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with Display Stream Compression 1.2a, and HDMI 2.1 adds 48 Gbps bandwidth and dynamic HDR support. The architecture also supports HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x GPUs provide the first listed hardware AV1 decoding implementation, with claimed bitrate savings of 50–55% over H.264. In the cited test, NVDEC played 8K60 HDR AV1 content with about 4% CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding for high-quality, low-latency streaming and archiving, including H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K, while reducing CPU utilization.

For GeForce, the GA102-based RTX 3090 has 24 GB of memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores; the passage states it is 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. GA10x supports GDDR6X rates up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth in the RTX 3090. RTX IO APIs and DirectStorage support faster asset loading, GPU-based decompression, and reduced CPU workloads. The GA104-based RTX 3070 is described as faster than the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti; it lacks NVLink and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

A new GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay feature detects failed memory transmissions and retries them, helping users identify memory-overclocking limits through declining useful bandwidth, though it cannot prevent every crash.

The GA102-based RTX A6000 includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, hardware-accelerated ray tracing and motion blur, and AI denoising. Two boards can be linked with NVLink for 96 GB of combined memory. The closing specification states that NVIDIA does not warrant the information’s completeness or accuracy, may revise or discontinue products, and disclaims suitability for applications where failure could cause injury, death, or property or environmental damage.

Forecasters expect high pressure to bring drier, brighter and potentially warmer weather to much of Britain from mid-next week, with the best chance of warm spells in the south. Temperatures could reach the low 20s C on Saturday and about 25C in the southeast from Sunday to Monday, although models disagree. Tropical Storm Gert may disrupt the pattern but is unlikely to make landfall and is expected to weaken before reaching the UK. The Met Office said there was only a small chance of settled weather.

Andrew Kahn lists 10 college basketball conference games to watch, with statistics and records current through Dec. 27. The schedule includes Villanova at Butler on Jan. 4, Kansas at West Virginia on Jan. 24, Kentucky at Florida on Feb. 4, Indiana at Wisconsin on Feb. 5, Louisville at Virginia on Feb. 6, North Carolina at Duke and Oregon at UCLA on Feb. 9, Gonzaga at Saint Mary’s on Feb. 11, Kansas at Baylor on Feb. 18, and Indiana at Purdue on Feb. 28. Kansas seeks to continue its dominance against West Virginia and Baylor, while Butler, Florida, Gonzaga, and others are positioned as credible challengers. U.S. colleges celebrated Valentine’s Day with campus serenades, treats, e-cards, relationship stories, rallies, and date-night guides. Arizona State students shared holiday customs from their home countries; Cal’s gymnastics team distributed valentines, and Marshall University received a tuba performance. Other schools featured relationship hashtags, campus surprises, playful rival taunts, and stories of couples who met there, including an estimated 9,030 at Boston University.

A July 2001 news compilation reported that Fortune ranked Enron No. 16 in its Global 500 list and highlighted the company amid broader market developments:

- Corporate earnings fell sharply in the second quarter: BusinessWeek reported a 34% decline in net income among 90 major companies despite an 8% sales increase, largely reflecting Enron’s 196% revenue growth.
- Falling Western electricity prices and federal price controls prompted cancellations of planned generators, reducing projected Northwest peak capacity by up to 1,000 megawatts and raising concerns about winter supply. Portland General Electric halted a 45-megawatt turbine project, while NRG abandoned plans for 300 megawatts in Washington. Industry participants disagreed over whether price controls, weak demand, conservation, or new capacity were responsible.
- Following the Bonn climate conference, governments moved toward implementing the Kyoto Protocol, including emissions trading and projects in developing countries. Companies began incorporating carbon costs into investments, creating opportunities for energy traders, including Enron, as well as gas, nuclear, wind, and other low-emission industries.
- Kobe Steel announced plans to raise 165 billion yen to enter Japan’s wholesale electricity market, which Enron was also pursuing.
- Enron canceled its Miami-Dade power-plant option and focused on Deerfield Beach, where its project was stalled by a county moratorium. The cancellation also allowed officials to proceed with closing a construction landfill.
- White House adviser Karl Rove delayed selling stock in companies including Enron and met with their representatives, prompting conflict-of-interest scrutiny. The White House defended the meetings as broad policy discussions, and Rove sold his holdings in June.
- Enron executives Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling sold substantial shares while publicly describing Enron stock as undervalued. Company officials characterized the transactions as routine equity-compensation sales, while analysts questioned the mixed message; both executives retained large positions.
- Enron abandoned much of the valuation associated with its broadband venture after recording a $109 million loss, scaling back spending, and delaying recovery expectations. Analysts assigned the business little or no value, while noting that Enron’s core wholesale energy operations remained sound.

While tuna fishing about 120 kilometres off Tofino, a group including former Canuck Willie Mitchell encountered a large shark initially mistaken for a great white. Underwater footage helped identify it as an 8–9-foot salmon shark, a Pacific species that eats salmon, resembles great whites and generally avoids mammals. Such sightings are rare and considered signs of a healthy ecosystem, while warming waters may expand the ranges of southern shark species northward.

Sean Combs was sentenced Friday to 50 months in prison, closing his criminal case; he has denied accusations of sexual assault. He still faces dozens of civil suits, with more expected, which could bring settlements or payouts, legal fees, and further reputational damage.

Combs said he had lost his businesses, career, and reputation. His nearly $1 billion empire has contracted: Diageo ended its Cîroc and DeLeón relationships, Macy’s pulled Sean John, he left Revolt’s chairman role and sold his stake, and his music catalog and song values have declined.

Although he retains mansions and a private jet for sale, reputation strategist Eric Schiffer said Combs is unlikely to regain his former status. Combs said he does not care about fame, records, money, or performing after his release.

President Hayes returned Senate Bill 71 with objections, arguing that the 1880 treaty with China permitted the United States to regulate, limit, or suspend Chinese labor immigration but not absolutely prohibit it. He concluded that the bill’s 20-year suspension was unreasonable and violated the nation’s treaty obligations. Accepting the need for immigration legislation and Congress’s concern about Chinese labor, he urged a shorter experimental period and rules adapted to local economic and public-order conditions.

Hayes also questioned passport and registration requirements for Chinese persons protected by the Burlingame Treaty, noted the bill’s omission of provisions for Chinese transit across the United States, and advocated treating protected Chinese immigrants as nearly like U.S. citizens as possible. He acknowledged that Chinese labor had helped build railroads and develop the Pacific states but warned that broad exclusion could drive Asian trade elsewhere, recommending instead a limited trial and alternative regulation consistent with treaty rights and American interests.

German MP Norbert Röttgen urged suspending EU membership talks with Turkey, citing Erdoğan’s growing authoritarianism. Erdoğan dismissed the threat as unimportant and accused German and Dutch leaders of “Nazi practices.”

Academics in Zimbabwe and South Africa criticized Grace Mugabe’s University of Zimbabwe sociology PhD as plagiarized, theoretically shallow and below doctoral standards. Some cited post-graduation references, while others said the thesis relied mainly on pre-1999 literature. UZ academics petitioned an anti-corruption commission, which said no investigation was underway.
