Wall Street indexes closed higher Monday, led by technology and energy stocks as Apple provided a major boost and oil prices rose after a North Sea pipeline shutdown. Investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s two-day rate-setting meeting, with traders assigning an 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike and 15% chance of a 50-point increase. The Dow rose 0.23%, the S&P 500 0.32%, and the Nasdaq 0.51%. Bluebird Bio jumped 17.9% after positive myeloma study results, while bitcoin-related stocks surged. The market largely ignored an apparent terrorist attack at a New York commuter hub that wounded four people.

The Arkansas chancery court held that Eugene A. Causey acquired fee simple title to lands in section 16 through Isaac Adair’s oral promise to give him the land, his possession and valuable improvements, and a prior decree quieting his title. The decree bound his children, including those not yet born at the time, and Causey’s conveyance to T. F. Tillar therefore conveyed the same fee simple title.

For the woodland in section 15, however, Adair’s will gave Causey only a life estate, with the remainder in fee to his children; Tillar acquired only that life estate. A life tenant may remove timber only as reasonably necessary for proper enjoyment and good husbandry. Because 25 percent of the standing timber should have remained for farm upkeep, the appellants’ damages could not exceed one-fourth of the timber’s actual value. The timber was valued at $619.38, and the court awarded $154.84 for waste. The decree was affirmed.

The passage examines how sex scandals involving women differ from those involving men, using Nikki Haley’s disputed affair rumors and Megan Barry’s admitted affair as central examples. Barry, Nashville’s mayor, acknowledged a long-running, consensual extramarital relationship with subordinate and security-detail officer Robert Forrest Jr., who retired. Her apology emphasized shame, faith, brevity and consensuality while avoiding details and deflecting questions about other relationships.

The article contrasts Barry’s handling with media commentary defending Haley against Michael Wolff’s allegations and with broader feminist critiques of how powerful women are judged for infidelity. It describes a perceived “female sex scandal playbook” centered on apology, religion, humiliation and refusing to acknowledge sexual pleasure, while noting that male infidelity often receives less criticism. Despite the scandal, Barry remained mayor, and the passage predicts she may use selective #MeToo-style empowerment to avoid greater punishment.

MIT CSAIL researchers developed “Pensieve,” a neural-network system that selects streaming algorithms based on network conditions. In tests, it reduced rebuffering by 10–30% and improved quality by 10–25%. Its reward-based optimization could prioritize quality, speed, or data conservation. The team plans to open-source the code at SIGCOMM, test VR video, and expects larger-dataset training to yield further gains.
Two years after his trade from Toronto to Pittsburgh, two-time Stanley Cup champion Phil Kessel celebrated by golfing and filling the Cup with hot dogs, referencing an earlier fat-shaming column.

Ambient-pressure CVD was used to grow single-orientation graphene flakes on atomically smooth, 700-nm single-crystal Cu(111)/sapphire. SEM and AFM showed that some aligned flakes merged seamlessly, while others exhibited merging lines with increased contact potential difference, indicating non-seamless junctions. Conductive AFM and FFT analysis confirmed that similar merging lines occurred between both aligned and misaligned flakes. Wet oxidation in 90 °C water revealed copper oxidation beneath defective merges, demonstrating nanoscale water-permeable pathways. STM at 4 K in ultrahigh vacuum identified many merging lines as overlapped junctions in which one graphene flake terminates at a copper step and another overgrows it, forming a bilayer region approximately 10–50 nm wide. Tearing and folding experiments further confirmed this structure. Among 122 merging regions, 55 (about 45%) showed oxidation consistent with defective structures, while 67 (about 55%) were likely seamless. The authors classified merging behavior as seamless stitching, defective stitching involving structural defects or grain boundaries, and overlapped junctions. These findings show that aligned graphene films are not uniformly defect-free or impermeable and may support uses in nanofiltration, desalination, and molecular sieving.

Singer Meghan Linsey was bitten by a brown recluse spider while sleeping in Nashville, waking with facial pain and the dead spider in her hand. She sought urgent care and experienced severe pain, swelling, rash, spasms, and a wound that developed necrosis, or dead tissue. Brown recluse bites are rare and rarely fatal, but symptoms can worsen and wounds may take weeks or months to heal. There is no antidote; treatment focuses on symptoms and wound care. Linsey underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy, which helped remove dead tissue and form new skin. More than two months later, her wound was healing well, her scar was nearly invisible, and she had returned to performing. She hopes sharing her experience raises awareness of brown recluse bites.

Wealth and material well-being are widely distributed, with increased farm ownership, savings, and wage employment, while large fortunes remain small relative to overall national wealth. A Nature Climate Change study found that human-caused climate change could become the leading driver of extreme summer heat waves across much of the western U.S. within years, versus the 2030s in the Great Lakes and 30–50 years in the Great Plains. Population growth may worsen impacts, prompting calls for mitigation and adaptation plans.

Vision-language models (VLMs) and vision-language-action models power image captioning, VQA, multimodal dialogue, and embodied driving, but tokenizing high-resolution images or video produces long visual sequences that create memory and latency bottlenecks, making token pruning important for real-time use. Training-free pruning avoids retraining, yet most existing methods rely on fixed pruning schedules or layer-specific heuristics that lack adaptability, cannot reliably respect a token or FLOPs budget without manual tuning, and show limited generalizability. The authors' experiments show that token importance varies with both the input image and the posed query, and across decoder layers.

Inspired by neuroscience—where simple descriptions engage the ventral visual stream with sustained fixation while ambiguous ones engage dorsolateral prefrontal and parietal networks with competing hypotheses and iterative gaze shifts—the authors find that simple inputs cause rapid collapse of cross-modal attention in early layers, whereas complex inputs sustain diffuse attention and inter-layer saliency fluctuations.

They propose AutoPrune, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that estimates sample complexity via mutual information between early-layer visual and textual tokens (high = simple, low = complex). This score modulates logistic retention curves mimicking the human explore-commit-stabilize pattern, yielding front-loaded aggressive pruning for simple inputs and conservative late-onset pruning for complex ones; each curve is analytically rescaled so its area matches a user-specified token or FLOPs budget.

AutoPrune integrates with LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Senna, outperforming existing training-free methods across benchmarks and pruning ratios. On LLaVA-1.5-7B it prunes 89% of visual tokens, reduces inference FLOPs by 76.8%, retains 96.7% of original average accuracy, a 9.1% gain over PDrop (CVPR 2025).

The passage describes the device’s interrupt architecture, peripheral capabilities, electrical timing, and PCB routing requirements. The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller prioritizes up to 128 peripheral requests and generates IRQs or FIQs, while the C674x DSP controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts and also controls exceptions, NMI, and emulation interrupts. The EDMA controller supports up to 64 channels, with each synchronization event assignable to any of 512 parameter entries.

Timing specifications are referenced to device pins and use a 4 V/ns input edge rate; a 2 ns transmission line may represent the load without changing the stated data-sheet timing. For 3.3-V signals, Vref is 1.5 V. Board-routing delays are not included and must be considered, generally using IBIS models, external buffers when necessary, or the specified DDR2 routing rules.

Two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0, programmable FIFO and loopback modes, automatic bus-on recovery, message-RAM test access, configurable CAN pins, and dedicated interrupt lines. Debug support includes Advanced Event Triggering for hardware breakpoints, data watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing; real-time Cortex-A8 and system trace; and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG emulation and boundary scan. The JTAG ID register is located at 0x4814 0600 and has the device value 0x0B8F 202F.

The Ethernet subsystem includes a three-port gigabit switch with two external ports, hardware flow control, QoS, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII modes, and IEEE 802.3-compatible behavior. Its MDIO interface polls 32 addresses and controls multiple PHY devices for configuration and status monitoring. CPPI uses 512 32-bit buffer descriptors to improve host communication with communications modules. GPIO provides four 32-channel modules, configurable inputs or outputs, set/clear registers, and edge- or level-triggered interrupts.

The GPMC provides a glueless asynchronous interface for NOR flash, NAND flash, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic, with an 8-/16-bit multiplexed bus, up to eight chip selects, and 512 MB of addressing. The ELM locates BCH errors in NAND data. The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports TMDS video, multichannel L-PCM audio, CEC, DDC, and multiple color depths and resolutions. Its PCB guidance requires controlled differential impedance, paired vias, suitable pullups, and an ESD protection device with no more than 5 pF capacitance.

The HDVPSS provides video input and output interfaces, HD/SD encoding, two display pipelines, picture-in-picture composition, format and color conversion, graphics layers, and an HDMI transmitter. Video DAC outputs support normal and bypass modes, with detailed 75-Ω routing and short, isolated analog trace requirements. Four I2C modules support Philips I2C 2.1, standard and fast modes, 7- and 10-bit addressing, multimaster operation, and a 32-byte FIFO.

The Imaging Subsystem accepts parallel-camera or CSI-2 input, uses the Image Signal Processor, and provides flash-strobe and shutter control, extensive image correction, color processing, compression, and data collection for autofocus functions. Dedicated DDR2 and DDR3 interfaces support 16- or 32-bit paths, multiple device capacities, two chip selects, and two PHYs. Their PCB guidance specifies stackups, placement, keepout regions, signal routing, reference planes, VREF generation, termination, bulk bypassing, and extensive high-speed bypass-capacitor and return-current requirements.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 12, 2017, reporting that its Letter to Shareholders accompanying the 2016 Annual Report was attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky.

The 1-4 “Slice” zone offense uses a high alignment that challenges zone defenses and allows quick entries to four receivers. It features strong post play, spot-up shooters, rapid reversals, and rotations that force zones to shift. O1’s basic cut feeds a popping post; O5 slices over defenders playing off or straight up and curls behind defenders playing inside. Missed cuts lead to strong post-ups, high/low or baseline feeds, and cross-court skips against a fronted post. Closed-out defenders can be exploited by an extra pass for an open three. Ball movement includes weakside give-and-go actions, cross-court skips, high-post feeds, and wing entries that trigger cuts. Against post or wing overplays, O1 can pump fake to create a lob or use the opposite wing. If no shot or post feed is available, O1 starts continuity with a cross-court skip or high-post pass.

Mayor Bill de Blasio urged Albany to extend and expand the expiring school-zone speed camera program and announced a Ninth Street safety redesign after two children were killed by a driver running a red light. Siqi Zheng frames policy as a “game changer” for sustainable real estate by reconciling the three bottom lines: environmental benefits, social benefits, and profit. Market failures prevent these goals from intersecting. Information asymmetry can be addressed through certifications such as LEED and WELL, while split incentives between landlords and tenants can be addressed through green leases that share energy-efficiency costs and benefits.

The lecture focuses on externalities. Green buildings create positive externalities when benefits such as reduced carbon emissions accrue to society rather than developers, leading to undersupply. Incentives, including tax rebates, subsidies, and development bonuses, can internalize these benefits and turn a project’s net present value positive. Conversely, brown buildings and polluting factories create negative externalities through social costs not captured by developers. Carbon taxes, penalties, disclosure requirements, and building codes can raise private costs and encourage cleaner construction or retrofits. The formal terms are “carrots” for incentives and “sticks” for enforcement.

Policy examples include EU funding for building renovations, Mass Save assistance and heat-pump subsidies, and Arlington, Virginia’s density bonuses tied to LEED certification. Large commercial owners are often regulated through disclosure and penalties, while households and smaller organizations are more often offered rebates. Cambridge’s BEUDO uses each building’s 2018–2019 energy baseline, while Boston’s BERDO uses absolute emissions limits. MIT is pursuing a 2026 net-zero goal, initially relying on carbon offsets, with a broader campus target for 2050.

Zheng also describes MIT research on balancing sustainability and housing affordability in Massachusetts. Stricter energy codes may lower utility costs but increase development costs that builders pass to buyers and tenants, potentially pushing some households above the 30 percent housing-cost-to-income affordability threshold. The findings support combining “sticks” with carrots such as zoning bonuses, tax rebates, and faster permitting rather than imposing standards alone.

The final section examines climate-resilience investment in coastal areas despite continued migration and development in high-risk locations. Resiliency measures are costly and can generate a positive feedback loop in wealthy cities such as Miami, where investment attracts residents and businesses, but a negative loop in poor communities such as Fair Bluff, North Carolina, where population loss weakens the tax base. Federal coastal-resilience funding raises moral-hazard and distributional concerns, especially where local matching funds are unavailable. Whether to rebuild vulnerable communities or pursue organized “managed retreat” remains politically and economically contested.

With LeBron James and Stephen Curry still dominating the league’s popularity, ESPN examines who could become the NBA’s next “face of the league.” Victor Wembanyama is the leading candidate because of his exceptional skills, basketball intelligence and potential global appeal, though questions remain about positional bias and his being the first international player to attain that status. Anthony Edwards fits the Jordan-Kobe model as a charismatic, elite-scoring guard. Luka Dončić is another strong candidate, particularly if he leads the Lakers to another championship. Other possibilities include Zion Williamson, LaMelo Ball, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Cooper Flagg and an All-NBA, All-Defensive third-season standout. Ultimately, talent and achievements alone are insufficient; market, media exposure, geography, style and organic rivalries also shape the league’s most recognizable star.

This continuation patent application describes electronic devices with glass enclosures defining multiple major and peripheral surfaces, including substantially transparent enclosures that may appear seamless even when formed from multiple joined glass members. Displays positioned within the enclosures can be viewed through multiple sides, using flexible or assembled display components, while touch and force-sensing systems allow the surfaces to function as interactive inputs.

Graphical content may be divided into physically distinct main, peripheral, and corner regions or combined into unified, continuously scrollable displays spanning multiple surfaces. Either major side may dynamically serve as the primary interface, and symmetrical arrangements of speakers, microphones, cameras, and other sensors may support operation independent of device orientation.

The disclosed embodiments include varied glass thicknesses, tapered and curved overlapping edges, hidden seams, interlocking joints, glass-frit, adhesive, fusion, and ultrasonic bonding, as well as additive manufacturing. Enclosure shapes include cuboids, cylinders, elliptic cylinders, and octagonal prisms. Openings and removable or fixed caps may accommodate speakers, microphones, charging or communication interfaces, and SIM or memory cards. Displays may also support wireless charging, acoustic actuation through the enclosure, and optical access to internal components. The devices include processing units, memory, displays, touch and force sensors, communication systems, microphones, speakers, cameras, batteries, and other sensors for coordinated operation.

Russia agreed to Geneva talks with the UN and US on April 24, awaiting confirmation, to revive peace efforts in Syria, said deputy foreign minister Mikhail Bogdanov. UN envoy Staffan de Mistura may attend. The move follows US missile strikes on a Syrian air base blamed for a nerve gas attack that killed 87.

About 666 pilot whales stranded in two pods at Farewell Spit, New Zealand, were removed after most died, while survivors were successfully re-floated. Workers in bio-hazard suits punctured decaying carcasses to prevent gas buildup and explosions, and trucked more than 300 to an inaccessible site. The beach was closed as a health precaution.

The passage examines the paradox of moral education through the concepts of free will, autonomy, authenticity, and moral responsibility. It argues that philosophy of education often relies uncritically on libertarian assumptions: free will requires both alternative possibilities and self-initiated action. Autonomy is presented as a central educational aim and as a condition for critical thinking, well-being, responsibility, and authentic life, yet these assumptions conflict with causal determinism.

A dilemma attributed to Fischer and James shows that neither determinism nor indeterminism adequately grounds moral responsibility. If determinism is true, people cannot act differently; if it is false, actions may appear disconnected from the conditions that meaningfully ground them. Indeterminism permits different choices but does not establish control over them. Consequently, both positions threaten the conventional concepts of freedom and autonomy on which educational and moral theories rely.

The paper proposes Frankfurt’s hierarchical theory of the will as an alternative. Frankfurt’s thought experiment describes a neuroscientist who ensures that a person acts as intended while preventing any alternative action. Frankfurt argues that responsibility concerns the actual scenario: a person may be responsible even if unable to act differently, provided the action expresses the will they genuinely want and endorse. Responsibility therefore does not require alternative possibilities.

Frankfurt’s theory distinguishes first-order desires from second-order desires, or desires about desires. Through reflexive self-assessment, people identify with certain desires and wish them to motivate their actions. A will is free when first- and second-order desires are in harmony. Moral responsibility rests on volitional control—identification with and endorsement of one’s effective desires—rather than control over all determining conditions or unchosen alternatives. This criterion can operate under both determinism and indeterminism, while people unable to form second-order desires or identify with their desires are excluded from responsibility.

For moral education, the paper recommends emphasizing the actual scenario, the quality and authorship of the will, and responsibility for actions, omissions, non-action, and consequences. Young people should learn that they can remain responsible and authentic even when unable to act differently, because their attitude toward and identification with their will can reveal preferences, values, and moral character. The hierarchical interpretation thus redefines autonomy through endorsement and volitional control, makes the metaphysical status of the world less decisive, and resolves the paradox of moral education by showing that it stems from the libertarian position.

In Arthur C. C. Hill v. Jacob Levine (Massachusetts, 1925), the court held that a deed requiring subdivided lots to have at least fifty feet of frontage was subject to the stated twenty-year restriction period and expired on August 20, 1916. The restriction was a personal agreement between grantor and grantee, not an equitable easement benefiting other lots, as it was omitted from later deeds and the Land Court decree. Because this raised no reasonable doubt about title or threat of adverse claims, the court reversed the dismissal of Hill’s bill and ordered specific performance of Levine’s agreement to purchase the land, with Hill permitted to seek damages.

California and controlling U.S. federal law govern the parties’ software-use agreement; invalid terms are severable, and the CISG is excluded. Exclusive venue is in Santa Clara County courts. U.S. export restrictions and required licenses apply, amendments require written authorized signatures, and licensors are third-party beneficiaries.

President Yameen Abdul Gayoom said he was willing to hold an early presidential election, months before his term ends in November, as unrest grew after the Maldives' Supreme Court ordered the release and retrial of political prisoners, including exiled former President Mohammed Nasheed, whose convictions the court said were politically influenced. The court also reinstated 12 opposition-aligned lawmakers, costing Yameen's Progressive Party its majority in the 85-member parliament; its February 5 opening was postponed indefinitely. Yameen fired national police chief Ahmed Saudhee for the second time since the order, naming Abdulla Nawaz interim chief. Protesters demanding release were dispersed by police using tear gas and batons. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged respect for the ruling and all-party talks. Nasheed said he would challenge Yameen again.

Manchester United reportedly received approval to bid £50 million for Fulham’s 17-year-old left-back Ryan Sessegnon, who can also play forward, ahead of January. Fulham are seeking a replacement as United and Tottenham monitor him. Jose Mourinho has discussed Marouane Fellaini’s contract extension but says talks are between the player and the club.

Microsoft announced upcoming Windows 10 accessibility updates, including reorganized Ease of Access settings, larger and brighter display options, improved Narrator, Edge page-loading information, vocal text styling, and enhanced eye control.

Marine heatwaves — prolonged periods of unusually warm water for the time of year, occurring in any season — can kill kelp forests and corals and disrupt marine ecosystems, fisheries and aquaculture. A 2015 working group of scientists defined the phenomenon, enabling analysis of more than a century of sea surface temperature data from ships, shore stations and satellites. This showed marine heatwaves have grown longer and more frequent worldwide: heatwave days rose 54% from 1925 to 2016, accelerating since 1982, with frequency up 34% and duration up 17% across 1925–1954 and 1987–2016, trends attributed to rising ocean temperatures.

Recent events illustrate impacts: a 2011 heatwave off western Australia replaced kelp with turf seaweed and killed Shark Bay seagrass, while a 2012 Gulf of Maine heatwave disrupted the lobster fishery. "The Blob" (2014–2016) in the North Pacific caused fishery closures, marine mammal strandings, algal blooms and altered weather patterns. Human-caused climate change made the 2016 Great Barrier Reef bleaching heatwave 53 times more likely and the 2015–16 Tasman Sea heatwave more than 300 times more likely. Scientists now seek forecasts under warming scenarios to guide fishery, aquaculture and conservation decisions, alongside urgent emissions reductions.

Scientists used stored sperm from Sudan, the last male northern white rhino, to fertilize southern white rhino eggs, creating two hybrid embryos that were frozen and could eventually be implanted once rhino embryo-transfer procedures are developed. Researchers hope to produce pure northern embryos by obtaining eggs from the two remaining females, Fatu and Najin, in Kenya, or through inbreeding or stem-cell-based methods. A northern white rhino calf could be born within three years, but biological uncertainties remain, and conservationists warn that reproductive technology should not replace broader conservation efforts.

An MIT study of three million Manhattan taxi rides found that 3,000 pooled four-person sedans could meet 98% of demand. Shared rides could reduce congestion and pollution but add average waits of 2.8 minutes and trip delays of 3.5 minutes. Riders and drivers resist shared rides, and switching could displace thousands of drivers; autonomous vehicles could further reduce driving work.

Carolina’s 2016 season ended with a 17–16 loss to Tampa Bay and a 6–10 record. After trailing 17–3, the Panthers made a late push, but a failed two-point conversion ended their chances when Greg Olsen slipped and Cam Newton’s pass fell incomplete. Newton completed 56% of his passes and threw three interceptions. Graham Gano, playing with a broken bone in his plant foot, missed three field goals, though the defense allowed 300 yards. Several younger or seldom-used players provided positive moments. Carolina will select eighth in the NFL Draft, its first top-10 pick since 2012.

Kerberos is a cryptographic protocol for authenticating clients, applications, and services over an untrusted network. Its trust model centers on a Key Distribution Center (KDC), which maps string-based principals to shared keys and manages authentication. Users must trust their workstations, while separate servers do not inherently need to trust one another. Kerberos authenticates principals but does not perform authorization; individual services enforce access through controls such as ACLs.

Clients initially derive a key from their password and request a Ticket Granting Service (TGS) ticket from the KDC. The password itself is not sent over the network, and the client can discard it after decrypting the response. The client then uses the TGS ticket and an authenticator to request tickets for specific services. A ticket contains client and server names, a client IP address, timestamps, a lifetime, and a session key. Tickets bound stolen credentials to limited validity periods, while authenticators and server caches are intended to detect replayed requests.

Kerberos 4 has several weaknesses: it treats successful decryption as proof of message authenticity, permits offline password guessing, uses only 56-bit DES, does not bind authenticators to application requests, and uses the same key in both directions, permitting reflection attacks. Kerberos 5 adds explicit message authentication, supports stronger encryption such as AES, connects authenticators to requests, and uses separate directional keys.

The KDC is a critical security target because compromise allows an attacker to issue tickets for arbitrary principals. Existing sessions can continue if the KDC fails, and read-only replicas can handle login and ticket requests. Compromised service keys must be rotated because an attacker retaining an old key can decrypt traffic and forge tickets for that service.

Password changes use a dedicated service that requires a ticket obtained directly through the password-derived key rather than a TGS-issued ticket, preventing a stolen ticket alone from changing the password. Kerberos 4 can expose a chain of later password changes if an old password is disclosed; Kerberos 5 instead uses Diffie-Hellman key exchange to derive a new secret for the exchange. Password-only remote logins also require an additional KDC-verified exchange to prevent a forged KDC response from granting access.

The passage defines SD memory card locking, erase, command, switching, transfer, status, and performance behavior. Force erase does not erase the secure area. A card remains locked during the user-area erase and becomes unlocked afterward; temporary and group write protection are also cleared after completion. If an erase error occurs, force erase may continue when the data is treated as “don’t care.” ACMD6 is rejected while the card is locked, and bus width can be changed only while unlocked. Locked cards accept only specified commands; other commands, including security commands, are illegal. CMD11 and CMD40 are newly accepted in the locked state, with CMD40 reserved for security use. The CARD_IS_LOCKED status identifies the lock state, and force erase completion changes it from 1 to 0. Lock/unlock implementations include Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 (COP) cards, with compatibility requirements tied to Physical Layer specification versions.

CMD55 (APP_CMD) causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command. An undefined ACMD is treated as a normal command, while the APP_CMD status bit indicates whether a command was interpreted as an ACMD. Illegal ACMDs produce an Illegal Command Error. Only the command immediately following CMD55 is interpreted as an ACMD, although consecutive CMD55 commands are permitted. ACMD41 is an exception because its response does not include APP_CMD status. Several ACMD numbers are reserved for proprietary SD memory card applications.

CMD6 switches or expands card functions through function groups for access or bus speed mode, command-system extension, driver strength, and power limit. Later status structures also reserve groups 5 and 6. Each group has 16 possible branches, with Function 0 as the default and 0xF used to retain the current function. CMD6 mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum current or power, while mode 1 selects functions. A busy function cannot be changed, and mode 0 should be used to check busy status because it does not alter function behavior. Invalid mode 1 selections cause the requested changes to be ignored.

The power-limit function applies across bus modes and defaults to 0.72 W. Total card power includes VDD1 and VDD2. Removable cards may consume up to 1.80 W, and higher UHS-I or UHS-II performance requires an appropriate power-limit setting. Functions without sufficient power fail initialization and are disabled. In UHS-II mode, the access-mode and driver-strength groups are unused, command-system support is optional, and power-limit support is mandatory. CMD6 returns an R1 response and a 512-bit status block representing a single-block read transaction with a 100 ms timeout. Selected functions return to defaults after a power cycle, CMD6 with Function 0 for each group, or CMD0.

High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface by increasing the clock to 50 MHz. It is optional, and a host must not control two cards simultaneously when they use different timing modes. CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57 are reserved for the optional command-system group. Their behavior depends on the selected function: the standard function treats them as illegal, the vendor-specific function gives vendor-defined behavior, and the mobile-commerce function follows the Mobile Commerce Extension Specification.

CMD8 is issued while the card is in the Idle state to check whether the host’s supplied voltage is supported. The host must issue it before ACMD41. A compatible card returns an R7 response echoing the voltage range and check pattern; an incompatible card does not respond and remains in the Idle state.

The CCS value returned by ACMD41 identifies SDSC, SDHC, or SDXC cards. SDHC and SDXC use block addressing and a fixed 512-byte block length, disable partial and misaligned access, and do not support write-protected groups or CMD28–30. SDSC uses byte addressing and a block length set by CMD16. The host may lower or stop the bus clock to control data flow or save power, subject to timing limits. ACMD41 has special clock requirements, and eight clock cycles must be supplied after specified bus transactions. A clock edge is required to terminate a busy signal after the clock has been stopped.

CRC7 protects commands, most responses, and the CID and CSD registers. CRC16 protects transferred data blocks and is calculated separately on each DAT line in wide-bus mode. A CRC failure causes the card not to respond or execute the command, leaves its state unchanged, and sets COM_CRC_ERROR. Illegal commands likewise produce no response or state change and set ILLEGAL_COMMAND. Read, write, and erase operations have specified timeout rules; high-capacity cards generally require fixed minimum timeouts, while some SDXC and UHS-II operations permit longer busy periods.

SD commands use a 48-bit format and are organized into command classes recorded in the card’s CCC field. Mandatory and optional classes depend on card type, capacity, version, and supported functions. The passage catalogs normal, block-oriented, write-protection, erase, application-specific, switch-function, function-extension, and I/O commands. Command legality depends on both the current card state and the supported command classes.

Responses are transmitted over the CMD line and include R1, R2, R3, R6, and R7 formats; SDIO also defines R4 and R5. Card status provides command error and state information. SD Status is a 512-bit block obtained through ACMD13 in the transfer state and reports features such as speed class, UHS speed grade, video speed class, application performance class, erase timing, and command-queue support. Task Status reports queued-task information when selected through CMD13.

Speed-class methods are optional and include Speed Class 2, 4, 6, and 10; UHS Speed Grade 1 and 3; and Video Speed Class 6, 10, 30, 60, and 90. The user area is divided into Allocation Units, which are further divided into Recording Units in multiples of 16 KB. SDSC and SDHC performance definitions account for fragmented AUs, internal data movement, random reads, and FAT-update overhead. Class 10 performance is defined only for entirely free AUs. SDXC uses larger AUs, exFAT-related updates, and no performance-move operation; it permits only sequential writes to completely free AUs. Speed Class Control command CMD20 is optional for SDHC and introduced for SDXC to optimize operation for capacities up to 2 TB and larger AU sizes.

The disclosure describes methods and systems for detecting, processing, and responding to speech commands across networked data modules such as loudspeakers. Modules detect and score a user-generated activation command, or “Hot Word,” using signal power, detector confidence, source location, and audio processing. In a centralized arrangement, a Player or group leader collects scores, selects the highest-scoring modules, activates their microphones, combines recorded speech, sends it to a server for interpretation, and distributes the requested action and optional audible confirmation. In a decentralized arrangement, modules broadcast scores and server-response confidence levels, and modules with leading values act. The system can also combine the best audio segment from different modules for each part of a command and compare signal-to-noise ratios using synchronized clocks. The broader content-management architecture dynamically groups modules into Player, Follower, and Renderer roles for synchronized media playback; leader selection may consider processor capability, codec support, and bandwidth or latency. This application continues several earlier U.S. applications whose disclosures are incorporated by reference.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 15, 2017, announcing the pricing of a private placement offering of $16.0 billion in senior unsecured notes. The related press release was included as Exhibit 99.1.

The United Nations Conference on International Organization met in San Francisco from April 25 to June 26, 1945, to draft a charter for a world security organization. Delegates from 50 governments unanimously approved the UN Charter, the Statute of the International Court of Justice, and Interim Arrangements for the Preparatory Commission on June 25. The Charter was signed by 153 delegates the next day, with space reserved for Poland.

The U.S. Senate consented to ratification on July 28, and President Truman ratified the Charter on August 8. He signed the United Nations Participation Act on December 20. The Charter entered into force on October 24, after ratification by the five major powers and 24 other states.

The Conference included four commissions, 12 technical committees, and four general committees. Technical committees drafted the Charter in closed meetings before submitting recommendations to commissions and the plenary session. Approximately 500,000 sheets of documentation were reproduced daily. The principal records were published in a 22-volume series, with final documents available in Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish.

A year after overruling Chevron in Loper Bright, the Supreme Court’s administrative-law framework remains unsettled. Three developments merit attention: courts increasingly use independent textualist interpretation rather than deferring to agencies; Skidmore deference appears to survive indirectly as courts interpret statutes independently but cite longstanding agency positions as evidence supporting their conclusions; and the major questions doctrine continues to limit delegations of vast economic or political significance.

Lower courts are divided over the declining use of Skidmore, which may serve as a legitimating tool for technical decisions or simply become one interpretive tool among several. The Supreme Court’s stricter textualism could eventually displace it.

In a separate concurrence, Justice Kavanaugh suggested that the major questions doctrine may not apply to national security and foreign policy because Congress often grants presidential discretion in those areas and nondelegation doctrine has played a limited role there. The Court had not adopted this proposed exception, but it could affect a pending challenge to tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Danica Patrick drew criticism after confronting booing fans at Pocono Raceway, saying her job is to drive rather than sign autographs and that the boos hurt her feelings. The incident triggered debate among drivers: Kevin Harvick and Dale Earnhardt Jr. said signing autographs is part of the job, while Ryan Blaney said it isn't required but that he enjoys it and prioritizes signing for kids. Earnhardt, who dislikes that Patrick's remarks paint her badly, noted cameras are always rolling and said talking with fans can provide welcome reinforcement after a poor performance.

At the World Economic Forum, President Trump presented “America first” as a call for national strength alongside cooperation among sovereign nations. He claimed strong U.S. economic growth, record stock-market levels, $7 trillion in added wealth, 2.4 million jobs since his election, and historically low unemployment for several groups. He highlighted tax reform, including a corporate rate reduction from 35% to 21%, employer bonuses, regulatory reductions, and increased investment, including Apple’s announced $350 billion in U.S. investment.

Trump advocated fair, reciprocal trade and said the United States would address intellectual-property theft, industrial subsidies, and state-led economic practices while remaining open to bilateral agreements, including with TPP members. He also promoted expanded domestic energy production, military investment, and allied contributions to collective security.

On international issues, he described pressure on North Korea, opposition to Iran’s support for terrorism and nuclear weapons, cooperation against ISIS, and efforts to prevent Afghanistan from becoming a terrorist haven. He said coalition forces had retaken nearly all ISIS-held territory in Iraq and Syria. Domestically, he called for stronger border and immigration enforcement, merit-based immigration, and workforce development to reduce dependence.

In a question-and-answer session, Trump described tax reform as politically difficult but successful, said unexpected employer bonuses were increasing workers’ pay, and credited his business experience with preparing him to challenge excessive regulation. He argued that America’s tax cuts, regulatory reductions, business investment, and national spirit were producing economic gains and encouraged global leaders to invest in the United States.

Live third-quarter updates from No. 16 Vanderbilt vs. No. 10 Alabama showed the teams exchanging touchdowns and turnovers. Ty Simpson threw Vanderbilt touchdown passes to Germie Bernard and Ryan Williams, while Diego Pavia connected with Sedrick Alexander, who later scored on a 65-yard run. Conor Talty made a 30-yard field goal but missed a 47-yard attempt; both quarterbacks also threw interceptions.

The preview said Vanderbilt entered 5-0, while Alabama was coming off a road win over Georgia and remained a top-10 team despite an opening loss to Florida State. Vanderbilt’s 2024 upset of then-No. 1 Alabama, 35-4, was highlighted, with the outcome framed as significant for College Football Playoff positioning. Pavia ranked among the nation’s top 10 in non-play-action passing statistics. Simpson entered with a 69% completion rate, nearly 1,200 yards, 11 touchdowns and no interceptions, while ranking second in early Heisman tracking. Key matchups included Vanderbilt’s pass rush against Simpson and Alabama’s offensive line against Vanderbilt’s improved front and pass coverage.

The passage explains the scale-in trading strategy: gradually increasing position size as the market presents additional entry opportunities, as part of a planned trading approach rather than a reactive attempt to salvage a losing trade.

For retail investors, scaling in means buying more shares as prices fall, assuming the decline is temporary and the stock will rebound. This form of dollar-cost averaging lowers the average purchase price and offers greater flexibility in market timing, but requires discipline, goes against the grain, and risks an incomplete position or a loss if the price does not recover. It is also useful for large purchases in illiquid stocks, where buying all at once would move the price, though exit liquidity remains an issue.

Day traders scale in differently: they test the market with a small trade size and add only to a winning position as it moves favorably, using floating profit to risk additional positions. The risk is that a sudden reversal can wipe out floating profits and produce an overall loss.

Institutional traders scale in to fill large orders gradually without moving the market or attracting front-runners; the passage cites hedge funds such as Jim Simons' Medallion Fund as users.

Scale-in is distinguished from double-down and Martingale strategies, which add to losing positions (Martingale doubling the position size) in a desperate attempt to reach breakeven. Swing traders may scale in at potential reversal levels under mean-reversion strategies, or add to winning positions under trend-following approaches.

Scale-out is presented as the counterpart: exiting in pieces by taking partial profit while leaving part of the position running, then moving stops to break even.

A backtest investing 100% of equity on the first signal showed the scale-in version had a lower CAGR (equity dropping from 1.4 million to 1.06), but the authors judged it improved overall, achieving better risk-adjusted returns by spending less time in the market for similar returns. Strategy code and logic are offered to Silver members. The passage concludes that scaling in may be an alternative for many trading strategies, since picking tops and bottoms is futile.

A retrospective single-center study evaluated rebleeding predictors in 226 adults with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage at Rennes University Hospital from 2020–2022. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%). Established risk factors did not differ significantly between patients with and without rebleeding. Each additional hour from symptom onset independently increased rebleeding odds by 0.7% (OR 1.007), while higher WFNS scores were also independently associated with rebleeding (OR 2.444). Two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred after 24 hours; patients whose aneurysms were secured within 24 hours had less rebleeding before securing than those treated later (9% vs. 21%, p=0.021). One- and six-month outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, although good-outcome scores were more frequent at six months among patients without rebleeding. The authors concluded that time since symptom onset is a significant rebleeding risk factor and emphasized securing aneurysms as early as possible. Limitations included the retrospective design, small number of events, and a pragmatic rebleeding definition.

A prospective multicenter study evaluated the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) for assessing hearing-related quality of life in 97 consecutive patients with unilateral Menière’s disease. Participants underwent comprehensive vestibular assessment, MRI, pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, and SSQ17 testing. Most had definite Menière’s disease; mean age was 56.2 years, 56.7% were female, and 51.6% used hearing aids.

Hearing loss was asymmetric, with mean four-frequency pure-tone averages of 51.9 dB HL in affected ears versus 19.3 dB HL in unaffected ears. Monosyllable recognition was 33.9% in affected ears and 86.6% in unaffected ears. Mean SSQ17 scores were 6.0 overall and 5.3, 5.1, and 7.2 for speech, spatial, and qualities of hearing, respectively. Scores did not differ significantly by diagnostic category.

The SSQ17 demonstrated excellent internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha of 0.960 overall and 0.904–0.956 for subscales. Subscale and listening-effort scores correlated negatively with affected-ear pure-tone thresholds and positively with speech recognition. The findings support SSQ17 as a reliable tool for assessing hearing disability and advanced listening difficulties in Menière’s disease, complementing audiometric assessment. It does not capture the major burden of vertigo, and factor analysis of listening effort was deferred to future registry analyses.

The article backtests calendar effects in the TLT ETF, which tracks 20-year Treasury bonds, from 2004 through August 2021. Results show strong negative returns during the first seven trading days of each month and solid gains during the rest of the month. A combined strategy produced an annual return of 10.2% versus 3.8% for buy-and-hold, with a 24% maximum drawdown compared with 48%. A short strategy from the prior month-end close through the seventh trading day’s close averaged 0.6% per trade, with a 5.5% unleveraged CAGR and a profit factor of 2. Investing from the seventh trading day’s close through month-end reportedly doubled buy-and-hold returns while remaining invested two-thirds of the time. The article also explains that TLT prices and interest rates move inversely and includes Python code for the strategies.

News reports from November 29, 2001, described Enron nearing bankruptcy after Dynegy abandoned its acquisition following disclosures of worsening operations and three credit-rating agencies downgraded Enron to junk status. Enron had more than $15 billion in debt, less than $2 billion in cash, and over $61 billion in assets. Bloomberg reported that a Chapter 11 filing could become the largest corporate bankruptcy reorganization, while Enron’s European operation entered administration and was being separated from U.S. operations.

NYMEX restricted Enron’s trading and raised margins on natural-gas and crude-oil futures. Enron reopened EnronOnline solely to allow counterparties to unwind positions. U.S. power and gas trading remained broadly orderly, though physical gas prices were volatile and European electricity markets experienced price swings as contracts and deliveries were reassessed. ICE’s electronic trading volume rose 65% from October as users sought alternatives to EnronOnline.

Enron’s roughly $18.7 billion in derivatives liabilities raised concern about an unprecedented over-the-counter unwinding that could take weeks or months to value. Banks and investors faced significant potential losses: Credit Suisse First Boston estimated direct Enron exposure of about $500 million each at Bank of America, Citigroup, and J.P. Morgan, $300 million at Bank One, and $50 million at Wachovia. Reliant Resources reported approximately $80 million of exposure, while Williams expected less than $100 million. Enron bonds traded near 20 cents on the dollar, indicating expectations of bankruptcy, and several Japanese investment funds fell below par value amid investor redemptions.

Enron’s metals unit was reportedly close to a sale, while its extensive overseas power, pipeline, and industrial holdings complicated potential asset claims. In Houston, a $108 million office project was delayed partly because Enron’s expected departure from 3 million square feet of space could increase vacancies and pressure rents. NewPower said it had enough cash and credit through the second quarter, while Reliant described its exposure as manageable. Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle called for congressional investigation into Enron’s collapse and any broader implications for the energy industry.

Digital laggards struggle to connect goals with strategy, leading employees to deprioritize poorly understood objectives and creating company-wide misalignment. A data-driven culture supports vertical alignment through shared metrics and objectives and horizontal alignment through common data models and transparent data access. Digital leaders emphasize learning, transparency, clear metrics, and a culture that coordinates beliefs, values, and daily behavior. Their employees generally understand expected actions, while digital laggards face gaps between stated values and actual practices because of entrenched habits, skills shortages, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors remains a central transformation challenge, but laggards can improve. Strong data cultures reflect beliefs about learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement in company values and everyday practices. Organizations fall into four maturity patterns: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant, with each able to build on existing strengths through targeted action.

This medRxiv preprint scoping review examines the current state of inflammation research in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of depression and the existing frameworks for guiding future work, with a proposed role for artificial intelligence (AI) in managing anti-inflammatory-based treatment.

**Background and rationale.** Inflammation is closely associated with depression pathogenesis; depressed patients show elevated cytokines and chemokines that may affect neurotransmitter metabolism, neuroplasticity, neuronal signalling, and dopamine production. NSAIDs, Omega-3 fatty acids, and steroids are already used clinically and have shown antidepressant effects. The authors argue that reducing inflammation should be a treatment goal, while noting a crisis in translating mechanistic discoveries into clinical practice.

**Literature review.** A search yielded 118 articles on animal research, 61 available in full text; 21 were excluded for comorbidities and 9 for focusing on inflammation-associated depression mechanisms, leaving 31 animal studies. These covered pharmacological interventions (SGLT2 inhibitors, vitamin D analogues, natural extracts) and non-pharmacological ones (acupuncture, exercise, light therapy). Key findings: empagliflozin acts via AMPK activation to regulate autophagy/inflammation and neurogenesis and inhibit NLRP3; calcitriol and vitamin D analogues inhibit the P2X7R/NLRP3/caspase-1 pathway; brexpiprazole plus fluoxetine produces rapid effects via BDNF-TrkB and dendritic spine density; antiretroviral therapy and p53 knockdown suppress microglial immunoinflammatory responses; leukotrienes enhance depressive-like behaviour with sex-selective effects on IL-6 and TNF-α; progesterone attenuates neuroinflammation and oxidative stress; a selenium compound (CMI), liver-sparing granules, propolis, n-3 PUFAs, and glycine also improved depression-like behaviour. Fourteen natural-extract studies (including Loganin, Berberine, Cinnamic Acid, Nootkatone, Thymoquinone, Baicalein, Baicalin, Sinomenine, Salvianolic acid B, and clove oil) modulated oxidative stress, neuroinflammatory markers, and related pathways. Non-pharmacologically, acupuncture modulated oxidative stress, neuroinflammation and apoptosis; swimming exercise raised hippocampal neuroplasticity proteins; brain-gut photobiomodulation modulated gut microbiota, restored hippocampal Sirt1 and improved cognition. Major debates concern single-target versus multi-target modulation and pharmacological versus non-pharmacological strategies. Most studies are short-term and small-scale, with limited clinical relevance, prompting calls for long-term follow-up, study of individual differences (polymorphisms, lifestyle, gut flora), combined interventions, optimised animal models, and fuller reporting of data beyond P-values.

**Methods.** The review followed Arksey and O'Malley's framework, expanded by Levac et al. and JBI, reported per PRISMA scoping review guidance, with the protocol on OSF. PubMed was the sole database searched (no date restrictions); only RCTs were eligible. Two reviewers screened in duplicate after calibration on the first fifty articles; two independently extracted data using a form informed by GRIPP2; synthesis followed the six-step Thomas/Harden approach as implemented by Ryan et al. Ethical approval was not required.

**Results.** 1057 articles were screened; 11 were included, published 2008–2024, from the UK (n=3), China (n=3), and other countries. Together they encompassed 907 patients, mostly with major depression (n=8), DSM-IV as the commonest criterion (n=7), largely middle-aged samples. Drugs included fluoxetine, infliximab, ketamine, minocycline, votioxetine plus celecoxib, SSRIs, and lacquer tree. Treatment cycles ran 2–18 weeks; most markers were undetectable, but CRP, hs-CRP, sTNFR1/2, IL-2, IL-6 and TNF-α were reasonably detectable. Benefits included glycopyrrolate adjunct to SSRI improving remission rates at 2 and 4 weeks, and lacquer tree plus calorie restriction reducing weight, BMI, body and visceral fat, MDA, and hs-CRP. Challenges included inter-patient variability (minocycline response favouring baseline hsCRP ≥3 mg/L), drug safety concerns (celecoxib non-inferior to placebo but with side effects), and the cost of biomarker testing (1000–1500 RMB versus about 1000 RMB for a full treatment course in China). Infliximab response correlated with baseline CRP and TNF-α levels, and escitalopram produced larger reductions in IL-2, IL-6 and TNF-α than fluoxetine, correlating with symptom improvement. Five research questions were posed.

**Discussion.** The authors state that immune mechanisms from cellular and animal models do not translate to human depression, that anti-inflammatory pathways cost more than conventional treatment, and that inflammation indicators are not rationally set (one trial found most cytokines below detection). They propose a staged method: transcriptomics/single-cell sequencing to identify candidate markers, blood-level re-analysis, establishing healthy-adult reference ranges, and final indicators that might become a gold standard judged by psychiatrists and psychologists rather than rating scales. AI is proposed to integrate patient data into personalised health assessments, monitor medication response and issue early warnings; a Harbin Institute of Technology micro-robot that mimics white blood cells could carry medication and report real-time internal data, potentially reducing monitoring costs.

**Conclusion.** Anti-inflammatory pharmacological strategies for depression currently have limited research value and poor feasibility. The authors recommend shifting focus toward non-pharmacological approaches such as positive thinking and exercise, and toward public-interest studies with low costs and broad generalisability. No conflicts of interest were declared; funding was provided by Youwei Wang and Ren Sha, with registration at osf.io/k9pue.

A Seattle Public Utilities study found that Seattle’s typical drizzle and short showers remain largely unchanged, but extreme rainstorms have become more frequent and intense. Based on four decades of data from 17 gauges, SPU updated its rainfall standards: a 24-hour storm once expected every 100 years now produces more than 5 inches and can occur every 25 years; a six-hour, 1.86-inch storm has similar frequency. Rare flash storms are not necessarily worsening.

SPU will use the data to design drainage, sewage and flood-control projects. The agency is building a Lake Washington Ship Canal storage tunnel expected to keep nearly 60 million gallons of polluted water from the canal annually, and future infrastructure will be sized for heavier rainfall. SPU scientists expect climate change to continue increasing extreme storms, while local officials cited the findings to support greater flood preparedness and climate action.

The 1942 *Foreign Relations* series comprises six numbered volumes covering the British Commonwealth, Far East, Europe, Near East, Africa, and American Republics, plus a previously published unnumbered volume on China. Its Belgium section includes U.S.–Belgian mutual-aid and military-service agreements and records of tripartite U.S.–British–Belgian negotiations concerning Belgian Congo trade. The documents report delays in renewing the expired Anglo-Belgian economic agreement due to interruptions, changes in negotiators, and price disputes. Belgium sought British products, especially mining machinery, but had not defined its overall needs. Far East developments increased the urgency of Congolese products, while Britain sought to coordinate its policy with the United States.

NVIDIA Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the second quarter of fiscal 2016, ended July 26, 2015, reported quarterly revenue of $1.153 billion, up 5% from $1.103 billion a year earlier. Gross profit was $634 million, while operating income fell to $76 million from $163 million and net income declined to $26 million from $128 million; diluted EPS was $0.05 versus $0.22. For the first six months, revenue rose 4% to $2.304 billion, but net income fell to $160 million from $265 million and diluted EPS to $0.28 from $0.46. Quarterly gross margin was 55.0%, compared with 56.1%, and the effective tax rate was 64.0%, including a $27 million deferred-tax-asset write-down related to Icera, partly offset by a $13 million restructuring tax benefit.

GPU revenue increased 9% to $959 million in the quarter and 7% to $1.899 billion for the half, driven primarily by high-end GeForce gaming products, while GPU operating income rose to $273 million. Tegra Processor revenue fell 19% to $128 million for the quarter and 8% to $273 million for the half, with OEM smartphone and tablet sales declining more than 80%, partly offset by automotive growth; the segment reported operating losses of $41 million and $99 million, respectively. “All Other” revenue remained $66 million quarterly and $132 million for the half, primarily from Intel patent licensing.

At July 26, 2015, NVIDIA held $435 million in cash, $4.070 billion in marketable securities, $6.979 billion in total assets, $1.399 billion in long-term debt, and $4.185 billion in shareholders’ equity. Six-month operating cash flow was $409 million. The company repurchased $452 million of stock and paid $99 million in dividends during the half.

NVIDIA began winding down Icera modem operations after failing to find a viable buyer, recording $89 million of restructuring charges and expecting another $15 million to $25 million during the remainder of fiscal 2016. It also announced a recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets due to battery fire risk and recorded $21 million in related costs during the half.
