The patent describes a vehicle driving-assistance system using exterior cameras, preferably CMOS cameras, and optionally radar, lidar, LADAR, ultrasonic, and vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-to-infrastructure communications to detect surrounding vehicles, objects, lanes, speeds, and free space. An image processor or electronic control unit detects vehicles and other objects, may display or highlight them, and can issue visual, audible, or haptic alerts.

When a faster vehicle approaches from behind, the system may warn the driver or automatically accelerate the ego vehicle to match the approaching vehicle’s speed and/or change lanes to avoid a collision and allow the faster vehicle to pass. It may later slow down and return to the original lane after passing a slower lead vehicle. Maneuver decisions can account for relative distance and speed, available space, closing time, following vehicles, lane splits, speed limits, discomfort, safety, and emergency vehicles, using decision logic, lookup tables, AI, optimal control, or influence mapping. The system supports SAE Level 2 assistance through SAE Level 3 or higher automation. Adaptive cruise speeds may also be limited by lane, vehicle, trailer, and driver-license restrictions.

Mapbox announced partnerships with Microsoft, ARM and Intel’s Mobileye to expand its self-driving mapping tools. Its software will integrate with Microsoft Azure to process camera data and improve navigation algorithms, optimize road-feature recognition with ARM chips, and deliver Mobileye’s cloud-based road data about 200 meters ahead without excessive bandwidth use.

### Mega Geometry and acceleration structures
Mega Geometry treats clusters of triangles as primitives. It can generate Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) from spatially compact batches of up to 256 triangles, cache them on demand, and use them to build final BVHs. Because each CLAS contains roughly 100 triangles, subsequent BVH construction requires about two orders of magnitude less processing than classic triangle-based builds, enabling more BVH updates per frame and rapid cluster-LOD reconstruction.

All Mega Geometry APIs are fully batched and driven from GPU memory, allowing LOD selection, animation, and culling to run on the GPU while minimizing CPU communication and BVH-management overhead. For scenes with many objects, the Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) preserves static partitions across frames and rebuilds only changed partitions, while dynamic objects can remain in a global partition rebuilt each frame.

Mega Geometry also accelerates BVH construction for animated, displaced subdivision surfaces by mapping tessellation directly to cluster generation and building BVHs from the resulting CLAS. It supports clusters and PTLAS in DirectX 12 through NVAPI and Vulkan extensions, native cluster support in OptiX 9.0, and all RTX GPUs from Turing onward.

### Blackwell ray-tracing and scheduling
Blackwell’s fourth-generation RT Cores include cluster engines and new geometry and BVH compression schemes. They deliver up to twice the ray-triangle intersection rate of third-generation RT Cores and can reduce VRAM use by several hundred megabytes in typical cases.

Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) provide hardware ray-intersection support for strand-like geometry. LSS segments sweep spheres through space and may vary their radii between endpoints; standalone spheres are also supported. Common hair-rendering cases are about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth as much geometry memory.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves GPU thread scheduling for divergent ray-tracing workloads and routes coherent neural work to Tensor Cores. Blackwell’s core reordering logic is twice as efficient and more precise, while the API allows application-specific ordering and flexible ray-shader invocation. Existing SER applications benefit without code changes.

The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a programmable GPU context scheduler implemented with a dedicated RISC-V processor. It offloads GPU-context scheduling from the CPU, follows the Windows HAGS scheduling model, and coordinates AI and graphics workloads with lower latency. AMP can reduce CPU overhead, improve multitasking and frame pacing, shorten LLM first-response times, and help prevent game stuttering.

### Video, display, and power efficiency
Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled H.264 and HEVC. YUV 4:2:2 retains full luminance and half the original chrominance information, requiring two-thirds the data of uncompressed 4:4:4 while providing twice the color resolution of 4:2:0.

The ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, supports 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding, and adds an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode worth another 5% improvement. Together, these changes can produce up to 15% BD-BR PSNR gains. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, providing more than 50% higher generation-to-generation export speeds and four times the export speed of an RTX 3090 with one encoder. The sixth-generation NVDEC provides twice as fast H.264 decoding, matching HEVC and AV1 speeds, and supports 4:2:2 decoding.

DisplayPort 2.1b supports 80 Gbps using UHBR 20, including 8K at 165 Hz and 4K at 480 Hz with DSC, provided a DP80LL-certified cable is used.

Blackwell’s Max-Q improvements include finer-grained clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, including memory-clock gating and separate GPU-core and memory rails. Clock frequencies adapt to dynamic workloads 1,000 times faster than previous architectures. The deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada, and one small-language-model inference example achieved up to 50% power savings.

### DLSS 4 and neural rendering
DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation can create up to three additional frames for every traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the previous frame-generation method, while AI-based optical flow reduces computation. Enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine, whose doubled pixel-processing capacity supports higher resolutions and refresh rates.

DLSS 4 replaces CNN-based Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing models with transformer-based models containing twice as many parameters. The models improve temporal stability, motion detail, anti-aliasing, and ray-traced image quality, particularly under challenging lighting.

The new Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan, combined with Slang, exposes Tensor Cores to pixel and ray-tracing shaders. This enables neural texture compression with up to seven-to-one compression over block-compressed formats and supports RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

RTX Neural Materials uses neural approximations of complex multilayer optical materials. In its demonstration, neural materials reduced storage from 1,110 MB to 333 MB while providing higher visual quality. Neural Texture Compression uses neural networks for texture compression and decompression, while Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré and supports higher-order filtering. Blackwell’s doubled point-sampled texture-filtering rate accelerates this technique.

Neural Radiance Cache trains small networks on live game data to infer lighting from many additional bounces after an initial path-traced bounce, reducing ray-tracing work while improving indirect lighting. RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to games. RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model, trained on thousands of offline images, to infer a more natural face from a rasterized face and 3D pose data.

### GPU configurations
GB202, used by the GeForce RTX 5090, has 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, 768 texture units, 192 ROPs, and a 512-bit memory interface. GB203, used by the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, 336 texture units, 112 ROPs, and a 256-bit interface. GB205, used by the RTX 5070, has 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, 200 texture units, 80 ROPs, and a 192-bit memory interface.

NVIDIA states that the specifications are subject to correction or discontinuation, provides the materials “as is,” disclaims fitness warranties, places responsibility for suitability and testing on customers, and excludes NVIDIA products from being warranted for medical, military, aircraft, space, life-support, or other safety-critical applications.

The Seventh Circuit reversed the district court’s dismissal and remanded the case. Six former detainees challenged Illinois counties’ practice of charging fees, in addition to bail, for pretrial release under a state statute authorizing fees of $1 to $45.

The named plaintiffs adequately alleged individual claims against Kane and DuPage Counties, the only counties that directly charged them. Their monetary injuries satisfied standing requirements, and dismissal of those claims was unwarranted. The court reinstated the individual actions and reversed the dismissal of putative class claims against Kane and DuPage, leaving Rule 23 certification for further proceedings.

The plaintiffs had not properly or timely sought certification of a defendant class encompassing the other 17 counties. Nevertheless, because all counties implemented the same statutory fee and therefore were “juridically linked,” the plaintiffs might represent a class capable of suing all 19 counties if they satisfy Rule 23’s requirements. The district court must develop the record and evaluate typicality, numerosity, commonality, adequacy of representation, and the applicable Rule 23(b) category.

Once a class is properly certified, standing is assessed for the class as a whole, although the named plaintiffs must have personally suffered the same type of injury under the same statute. On remand, the court must also consider the effects of related Coleman and Ringswald litigation, including any claim-preclusion and class opt-out issues.

The study demonstrates solid-state near-infrared-to-visible photon upconversion using a DIB-SQ:PCBM bulk-heterojunction sensitizer coupled to a rubrene annihilator layer, optionally doped with DBP. Under 690 nm excitation, charge separation and recombination at the DIB-SQ–PCBM interface generate charge-transfer states, including long-lived triplet charge-transfer states. These transfer triplet energy directly or through PCBM molecular triplets to rubrene. Annihilation of two rubrene triplets then regenerates a singlet, producing upconverted emission in the 550–650 nm range.

A DIB-SQ:PCBM ratio of 1:3 maximized rubrene triplet population and overall light output while reducing squaraine aggregation. Devices with neat DIB-SQ or PCBM showed little or no upconversion, while the blend operated under low-intensity incoherent excitation. Transient absorption, time-resolved photoluminescence, and magnetic-field measurements supported the proposed charge-transfer-mediated triplet-energy-transfer and triplet-triplet-annihilation mechanism.

DBP doping increased the rubrene:DBP photoluminescence quantum yield to 47.5 ± 2.4% and shifted the upconverted emission peak from 562 to 605 nm. The DIB-SQ:PCBM (1:3)/rubrene:DBP device reached a saturated upconversion quantum yield of 1.36% above 69.7 mW/cm² and a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm². The work repurposes charge-transfer formation, commonly treated as a loss mechanism, as a triplet-sensitization pathway for efficient solid-state upconversion.

The £1,100 Marin Nail Trail 6 is a 29-inch trail hardtail built on a 6061 hydroformed aluminium frame. It features a 120mm RockShox Recon fork, SRAM GX 1×11 drivetrain with an 11–42 Sunrace cassette, Marin 30mm rims, Schwalbe tyres, and Shimano Deore hydraulic brakes. Offered in four sizes, it includes 27.5- and 29-inch wheel options, internal dropper-post routing, and twin bottle-cage mounts. The reviewer found its frame roomy, comfortable, and stable, with predictable, enjoyable handling. Its component selection was praised as durable and suitable for future upgrades, while its versatility made it a regular trail bike for commuting, exploring, and more energetic riding.

The Louisiana Supreme Court denied the plaintiffs’ motion to dismiss the defendants’ devolutive appeal. Three transcripts filed under the same docket number collectively contained the complete lower-court record, making a new transcript unnecessary. Appellants need not name every appellee if they request that the clerk issue citations, and failure to include a deceased defendant’s representatives did not prejudice appellants. Four appellants’ acquiescence in the $15,000 judgment did not affect the remaining appellants’ rights, although the court would not adjudicate against those who had acquiesced. The delay period for a devolutive appeal had not expired, and appellants stated that the deceased defendant’s heirs had no interest because they had acquiesced in and executed the judgment.

Victor Wembanyama’s transformative offseason was shaped by a life-threatening shoulder diagnosis. He trained at a Shaolin temple, studied with Kevin Garnett and Hakeem Olajuwon, developed new physical and mental skills, and created a fan environment modeled on PSG ultras. He also supported flood-affected communities through school events. Returning to Spurs training camp, he emphasized growth, versatility and readiness for the upcoming season.

In 2017, the Woodland Trust recorded 42 spring indicators at over 1,000 UK sites, including snowdrops, hazel catkins and singing song thrushes. Colder January weather delayed signs, though warming was expected to bring more.

Kimberly Kirkwood forwarded a chain email to numerous colleagues, calling it a fun holiday wish. Titled “THIS IS SCARY!!! DO IT!!,” the message claims that making a wish while reading it will make the wish come true within a number of minutes equal to the reader’s age. It includes anecdotes about a 13-year-old whose father returned from the Army and a 20-year-old whose boss was promoted, and warns that failing to forward it to 15 people within five minutes will bring years of bad luck.

The San Diego Unified School District's resolution to invite U.S. Education Secretary Betsy DeVos was rescinded after the city's teachers' union objected. Sponsored by board president Richard Barrera and Trustee John Lee Evans, it drew opposition from the San Diego Education Association, parents and community partners citing DeVos's support for vouchers and lightly regulated charter management; Barrera withdrew his backing. Protesters also tried to block DeVos from entering a Washington, D.C., school, drawing a rebuke from AFT president Randi Weingarten, who said she should visit public schools. DeVos's nomination drew bipartisan opposition and was confirmed by Vice President Pence's tie-breaking Senate vote. At a White House parent-teacher session, Trump praised DeVos and promoted school choice; DeVos said she was eager to learn from parents and educators across school settings.

Denby reported that the Korea situation was critical, hostilities were imminent, and China sought a peaceful solution through British and Russian mediation. At O’Conor’s request, Denby considered asking Washington to unite the powers in protesting Japan, but declined until China’s Tsung-li-Yamén formally requested it. He later relayed Viceroy Li’s request for the United States to lead powers in demanding Japanese troop withdrawal.

Sill reported the admiral’s departure, expected arrival of the Monocacy, concern for the king’s safety, and Washington’s advice that Korea protest Japanese demands and notify foreign powers; Gresham replied that the United States would not intervene forcibly. No fighting had occurred because no additional Chinese troops had been sent. Japanese merchant vessels were being used as transports, and Japanese conduct had won some Korean goodwill, though interference with Britain’s representative and reform demands were noted.

Tesla’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2017 describes a vertically integrated sustainable-energy business operating through two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Its automotive products include the Model S, Model X, and lower-priced Model 3, with plans for additional vehicles such as the Tesla Semi, Model Y, and a new Roadster. Tesla also develops and sells Powerwall 2 residential batteries, Powerpack 2 commercial and utility-scale storage systems, Solar Roof, traditional solar systems, and renewable electricity. It manufactures vehicles in California and the Netherlands, battery and storage products at Gigafactory 1 in Nevada, and solar products at Gigafactory 2 in New York.

The company sells vehicles directly through company-owned stores, galleries, service centers, and online reservations, and supports them through a global Supercharger and Destination Charger network, used-vehicle sales, vehicle financing and leasing, warranties, maintenance, and service. Its core technologies include electric powertrains, battery packs, power electronics, control and infotainment software, and autopilot hardware designed to support future self-driving capability. Tesla reported 37,543 full-time employees as of December 31, 2017.

The filing identifies major risks involving Model 3 production and delivery targets, Gigafactory 1 expansion, supplier concentration, battery-cell availability, material costs, manufacturing and service scalability, international expansion, consumer demand, product defects and software failures, lithium-ion battery safety, product liability, evolving vehicle and energy regulations, dealer-licensing restrictions, and intensifying competition in automotive, solar, and energy-storage markets. It also notes that forward-looking plans are subject to risks and uncertainties and actual results may differ materially.

The May 23, 2001 State Bar of Michigan e-Journal contains case summaries across bankruptcy, civil rights, constitutional law, criminal law, employment, family law, insurance, litigation, municipal law, negligence, and real property, along with practice-area directories, classified advertisements, bar events, news, and archived issues. It is available to State Bar members at no additional charge, with support from advertisers.

In In re Hood, the Sixth Circuit held that the Tennessee Student Assistance Corporation lacked sovereign immunity in a student-loan dischargeability action because states ceded sovereignty over bankruptcy discharge matters. In Thakur v. Department of Corrections, the court affirmed summary disposition for defendants because the plaintiff did not refute their stated reason for not interviewing him or connect statistical racial evidence to a facially neutral employment practice.

Most criminal cases were affirmed. People v. Bridgewater involved waiver of an omitted negligent-homicide instruction; People v. Byars was reversed because dismissal with prejudice was an excessive remedy for delayed discovery; People v. Ferguson involved a claim of ineffective counsel; People v. Knott concerned destruction of a videotape under police policy; People v. Minge upheld a vehicle stop; and People v. Williams involved an informed waiver of separate counsel. Parental-rights terminations in In re Guy, In re Jones, and In re Pittao were affirmed. In Slawick v. Detroit Newspaper Agency, a former employee’s defamation claim was not preempted by federal labor law, and the court affirmed jury awards totaling $106,000.

Other decisions included reversing summary disposition for the plaintiffs in Van Reken v. Michigan Basic Property Insurance Association, affirming the striking of a supplemental witness list in Moton v. Oakwood Healthcare, and reinstating a zoning board’s denial of a variance in Domine v. Township of Grosse Ile because the hardship was self-created. In Berry v. John Carlo, Inc., the fireman’s rule barred a police officer’s negligence claim. Affirmances also issued in Garrison v. Mount Clemens General Hospital and Girard v. Dearborn Cinemas.

Each Core Logic Voltage Domain can operate at an independently selected operating performance point (OPP) that defines maximum module frequencies and an associated voltage range. Lower-frequency OPPs use lower voltages, and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling allows real-time OPP changes without reset. Not all OPP combinations are supported, and DDR access must be suspended before changing the DDR frequency. Adaptive Voltage Scaling is marked as unsupported. Switchable SRAM automatically enters shutdown when its power domain turns off, while selected always-on SRAM can be shut down through `x_MEM_PWRDN` registers; shutdown removes power and loses stored data.

Several I/O groups independently support 1.8 V or 3.3 V, and each DDR interface can separately use 1.5 V or 1.8 V. PHYs must enter power-down mode before their associated domain is turned off. Low-Power Standby Mode requires switchable domains to be off, the ARM Cortex-A8 to run an IDLE loop at its lowest frequency, and unused functional blocks to be clock-gated. Supplies are divided into four sequencing groups and must follow specified power-up and power-down orders; the 3.3 V supplies must never exceed the 1.8 V supplies by more than 2 V. PLL and analog supplies require filtering near the pins, and power pins require small decoupling capacitors and periodic bulk capacitance without excessively delaying supply ramps. The main reset must remain low until supplies reach the correct voltages and are stable.

The device supports power-on, external warm, emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold and warm, test, and local resets. A power-on reset resets the chip and latches `BTMODE` before the ARM Cortex-A8 starts executing from Boot ROM. Warm resets generally preserve emulation activity and may optionally preserve the EMAC switch. Simultaneous reset requests are handled according to priority. Reset isolation permits the PCIe subsystem and EMAC switch to be preserved or reset independently, with required idle and bus re-enumeration procedures for PCIe. `RSTOUT_WD_OUT` reflects reset status and is always asserted for watchdog resets. Most I/O pins enter a high-impedance state during reset, with specified exceptions for emulation pins, EMAC switch pins, and `RSTOUT_WD_OUT`.

Device clocks derive from DEV and AUX reference inputs that may use internal oscillators with external crystals or external 1.8 V LVCMOS sources. The DEV clock is generally 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under stated exceptions; the optional AUX clock also supports 20–30 MHz. Oscillator components must be placed close to their associated pins, and supported crystals must operate in fundamental parallel-resonant mode. The SERDES input requires a low-jitter differential clock with nearby AC-coupling capacitors. Optional external clocks include AUD_CLKIN0–2, a 32.768 kHz clock, and two programmable clock outputs. The device has 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs; they start in bypass mode, have programmable frequency limits, and use the DEV clock as the usual reference. PLL_USB must be set to 960 MHz when USB is used. PRCM-generated SYSCLKs and module clocks must remain within their specified maximum frequencies.

The ARM interrupt controller prioritizes up to 128 requests and generates IRQ or FIQ signals, while the C674x DSP controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts and supports multiplexed event sources. Timing specifications exclude board-routing delays, so routing must be considered separately, using IBIS models where appropriate. Monotonic clock and control-signal transitions are required.

Additional peripherals include two DCAN interfaces, a 64-channel EDMA controller with 512 selectable parameter entries, Advanced Event Triggering, real-time Cortex-A8 and system trace, and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG emulation and boundary scan. The EMAC subsystem is a three-port gigabit switch with two external PHYs, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII modes, hardware flow control, QoS, and MDIO PHY management across 32 addresses. It operates with 3.3 V PHYs. The GPIO peripheral provides four 32-channel modules and up to 128 configurable 1.8/3.3 V pins. The GPMC supports glueless external-memory interfaces, including NOR and NAND flash, SRAM, and custom asynchronous devices, while the ELM locates BCH errors. The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports video, multichannel L-PCM audio, CEC, and DDC. Its PCB layout requires controlled TMDS impedance, paired vias, DDC pullups, and ESD protection with no more than 5 pF capacitance.

Bracero, an independent contractor hired to haul rice from the defendant’s Ponce branch, was injured when 25 to 30 bags from a tall pile fell on him during a second loading trip. The defendant argued that Bracero was an employee covered by the Workmen’s Compensation Act and denied ownership or control of the branch. The trial court found Bracero to be an independent contractor, found that the defendant maintained a Ponce branch, and awarded damages for negligently constructed rice piles and failure to warn him. Justice Wolf’s majority reversed, holding that res ipsa loquitur did not apply because Bracero and other workers were removing bags from the pile and that the record showed no negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident. Justice Del Toro, joined by Justice Hutchison, dissented, stating that evidence of a prior warning about the defective pile and the defendant’s failure to rebuild it or warn Bracero supported the judgment and warranted affirmance.

Akamai, a leading content delivery network, provided customers such as Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, Samsung, Netflix, and government agencies with content delivery, cloud infrastructure, streaming, storage, analytics, security, networking, and support services. By 2011, it operated more than 100,000 servers across 1,976 networks in 78 countries. Its innovative decentralized model placed servers at internet service providers near end users, enabling faster delivery and superior user experiences.

As Akamai expanded internationally, its market share declined with distance from the United States. Local competitors were taking customers in important markets, while global customers such as Amazon developed competing services and Microsoft and other large firms built internal delivery capabilities. Telecommunications firms also formed alternatives through acquisitions and federated networks. In 2009, engineering vice president Charley Dublin warned senior management that Akamai needed to adopt a local perspective to preserve its global leadership; the CEO subsequently asked Dublin and the international leadership team to develop a localization proposal.

Akamai’s products and prices were developed centrally in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and introduced to overseas markets with limited assessment of local demand, competition, working conditions, or purchasing power. Headquarters sometimes imposed sales targets that local teams struggled to meet, while local managers lacked authority over products, pricing, and customer ownership. Examples included unsuitable products and targets in Japan, structural limits in France’s consolidated ISP market, and globally set prices that local competitors undercut in South Korea. Akamai also lacked awareness of relevant local technologies and had weak brand recognition in some countries, including China.

A 2011 reorganization created product-focused business units and three geographic operating theaters to improve efficiency, coordination, and customer accountability. It also enabled more local resolution of field conflicts, although product and pricing authority remained centralized.

Dublin still had to determine where, how quickly, and to what extent Akamai should become local. The proposal had to balance local customer needs, support, competition, and revenue opportunities against the cost of investment while retaining global processes and infrastructure needed by multinational customers and the company’s global core.

The team is proud to reach the Stanley Cup Finals with home-ice advantage, believes it is tough to beat when playing its best, and is confident that preparation and strong leadership will guide them in the finals.

The paper introduces a two-timescale evolutionary hypergame framework for the voluntary prisoner’s dilemma with cooperation (C), defection (D), and opting out (L). Players have heterogeneous subsets of these strategies, reflecting differences in knowledge, experience, and cognitive access. On the fast timescale, players adopt available strategies through Fermi-weighted payoffs based on introspection; on the slow timescale, strategy sets evolve according to relative success.

Pairwise tournaments, Markov-chain stationary distributions, and expected payoffs are analyzed for three two-strategy sets and all seven nonempty strategy subsets. Greater introspection strengthens self-reciprocity within {C,L} players and improves their ability to avoid exploitation by defectors. Weak introspection favors {D,L} or {L}, whereas stronger introspection and higher cooperation benefit-to-cost ratios generally make {C,L} dominant.

In well-mixed replicator dynamics, weak introspection produces low-payoff populations dominated by {D,L}, while strong introspection leads to high-payoff populations dominated by {C,L}. In spatial populations with asynchronous payoff-based updating, {D,L} dominates at low introspection among three sets, but {C,L} eventually replaces it. With all seven sets, {L} dominates under weak introspection, mixed and {C}-dominated states occur at intermediate levels, and {C,L} dominates at high introspection. Overall, the framework shows how heterogeneous strategy access and introspection jointly shape the evolution and stabilization of cooperation.

Gold prices are holding near record highs after rising more than 50% over the past year amid recession fears and macroeconomic uncertainty, and are forecast to keep rising; stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 snapped a seven-day winning streak. UBS expects gold inflows of 830 metric tons this year, nearly double its initial 450-ton forecast, citing lower interest rates, dollar weakness and political uncertainty, and expects central-bank buying to continue for three more years, with roughly 95% of central banks anticipating higher holdings. Other analysts forecast a 6% climb to $4,000 per troy ounce by mid-2026.

Rising costs and tariffs are pressuring jewelry companies, which are raising prices or altering products. Mejuri announced price increases, is streamlining supply chain and sourcing, and is introducing 10-karat solid gold; Signet cited an 80-basis-point hit and more than a 30% increase in gold costs; BaubleBar has leaned into "demi-fine" 18k gold-plated pieces priced from $50 to $150; Alexis Bittor is emphasizing gold-plated products and slight price increases without repricing existing items; and Rowan, which uses 14k gold to coat steel or titanium for piercings, raised prices on some pieces. Executives noted cautious consumers who appear more sensitive to solid gold, and warned that gold's surge reflects hoarding tied to dollar uncertainty and signals broader economic concerns, especially for brands selling to price-sensitive customers.

Following Category 4 Hurricane Maria, Elon Musk said Tesla could rebuild Puerto Rico’s power grid, citing work on smaller islands and arguing there was no scalability limit. He said the decision would rest with Puerto Rico’s government, utility regulators, commercial stakeholders and residents. Gov. Ricardo Rossello invited Musk to discuss making the island a flagship Tesla project, and Musk agreed to talk. At the time, only about 10% of island residents had power. Researchers assessed ex vivo drug susceptibility and resistance-associated genotypes of Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum. From July 2019 to June 2024, isolates were collected from uncomplicated malaria cases at three eastern and two northern Ugandan sites; analyses also included samples collected since 2016. Susceptibility to nine antimalarials was measured using 72-hour growth-inhibition assays, and parasites were genotyped by deep sequencing of 80 candidate resistance genes.

Most drugs retained potent activity at low nanomolar concentrations, although quinine was less potent and pyrimethamine resistance was established. From 2016–2024, chloroquine susceptibility increased, while dihydroartemisinin (DHA), lumefantrine, and mefloquine susceptibility declined. Many isolates exceeded previously established artemisinin-resistance survival cutoffs, and ring-stage survival after DHA exposure increased over time.

PfCRT K76T and PfMDR1 N86Y became uncommon, while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance markers remained prevalent. PfK13 C469Y and A675V were associated with reduced DHA and lumefantrine activity, as were PfCARL D611N for lumefantrine and PfMDR1 Y500N for DHA. Overall, common antimalarials generally remained active, but modest declines in DHA and lumefantrine susceptibility indicate a potential threat to first-line therapy, supporting continued parasitological and genomic surveillance and policies to limit resistance selection and treatment failure.

The paper introduces InVirtuoGen, a continuous-time discrete flow model for molecular generation using fragmented SMILES. Unlike autoregressive models, which emit tokens sequentially, and masked diffusion models, which progressively unmask and fix tokens, InVirtuoGen jointly refines all positions at each denoising step, enabling coordinated molecular updates and decoupling sampling steps from sequence length. A bidirectional diffusion transformer predicts token distributions, while sequence length is modeled separately. Molecules are decomposed using revised BRICS, represented as shuffled fragment blocks with numbered attachment points, and tokenized into a 204-token vocabulary.

The model is pretrained on ZINC and UniChem, comprising roughly one billion molecules, and evaluated on de novo generation, fragment-constrained design, PMO property optimization, and lead optimization. It achieves a superior quality–diversity frontier for de novo generation and competitive performance across five fragment-constrained tasks. Prescribed fragments must be overwritten at every step, limiting this task to masked completion. For property optimization, the authors combine a fragment-recombination genetic algorithm with PPO adapted to discrete flows through Monte Carlo-estimated sequence log-probabilities, reporting state-of-the-art PMO and improved lead-optimization results.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture advances GPU ray tracing with fourth-generation RT Cores, dedicated BVH traversal and intersection hardware, an Opacity Micromap Engine, and a Triangle Cluster Intersection Engine. Blackwell doubles ray-triangle intersection throughput over third-generation RT Cores. Mega Geometry enables full-fidelity ray tracing of high-detail, cluster-based level-of-detail meshes by treating clusters of up to 256 triangles as acceleration-structure primitives. This reduces subsequent BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude, supports fully batched GPU-driven workflows, and introduces persistent Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures that update only changed scene partitions. The technology also accelerates ray tracing of displaced subdivision surfaces and is supported through DirectX 12, Vulkan, OptiX 9.0, and RTX GPUs from Turing onward.

Blackwell adds hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres for fine strand-like geometry such as hair. Compared with Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips, common hair-rendering use cases are about twice as fast and require roughly one-fifth the VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 provides more precise and efficient workload reordering, including neural workloads sent to Tensor Cores, while the programmable AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts with lower latency and reduced CPU dependency.

Blackwell GPUs add 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding and decoding. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, with an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode adding another 5%, while the sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. The GeForce RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps through UHBR 20, supporting 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with DSC.

Max-Q power improvements include advanced clock and unit gating, separate GPU-core and memory voltage rails, frequency switching up to 1,000 times faster than earlier architectures, and a deepest sleep state reached ten times faster than Ada. In a small-language-model inference example, these changes produced power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the previous method, while enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine. DLSS also moves its Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing models from CNNs to transformer architectures, enabling twice as many parameters, greater temporal stability, improved detail in motion, and stronger ray-reconstruction quality.

Cooperative Vectors for DirectX 12 and Vulkan makes Tensor Cores accessible to pixel, ray-tracing, and other shaders. Blackwell neural-rendering technologies include RTX Neural Materials for complex layered materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache for estimating indirect lighting, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces for generating faces from rasterized geometry and pose data. Neural Texture Compression can provide up to seven-to-one VRAM compression over block-compressed formats, while the Neural Radiance Cache infers multiple lighting bounces from limited ray tracing.

The Blackwell GPU family includes the 92.2-billion-transistor GB202 used in the GeForce RTX 5090, with 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores; the 45.6-billion-transistor GB203 used in the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores; and the 31-billion-transistor GB205 used in the RTX 5070, with 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores. The author argues that Nigeria’s political problems stem from inadequate understanding of its ethnic, regional, and colonial history. Nigeria is a nation of distinct ethnicities rather than a simple North–South binary created by colonial administration. The North’s greater cultural, linguistic, and religious cohesion reflects Usman Dan Fodio’s conquests and the subsequent emirate and Sharia system, while the South historically comprised diverse peoples brought together under one colonial administration.

The foundational political figures interpreted Nigeria differently: Nnamdi Azikiwe favored a strong central government and a new national identity beyond ethnicity; Obafemi Awolowo advocated federalism with equal regional and central authority and space for ethnic communities; Ahmadu Bello favored stronger regions, pursued Northern unity, and formed the Northern Peoples Congress around alliances with emirs and Islamic leadership. The author contends that Bello’s positions were shaped by political strategy and rivalry with Aminu Kano’s NEPU, and that Zik’s and Awolowo’s contrasting approaches were subsequently reflected in the regionalism of Zik, Awolowo, and Bello.

Historical alliances between Northern and Southern politicians, including Zik’s coalition with the NPC and the Niger Delta Congress, helped shape independence-era government. The 1966 coup and killing of Ahmadu Bello and Tafawa Balewa were interpreted by many Northerners as ethnically targeted, although the author disputes that explanation, arguing that the event intensified Northern concern about national power and vulnerability.

The author identifies several Northern political traditions, including Ahmadu Bello’s conservative and nationalist blocs, Aminu Kano’s radicals, and Middle Belt nationalism. Awolowo’s demand that regional minorities receive distinct states produced only the Midwest Region before Gowon divided the regions into states. In the Second Republic, the nationalist NPN represented multiple ethnicities, but the author says some Northern elites displaced Shagari in 1983 and later used ANPP opposition to Obasanjo to elevate Buhari, whom he identifies as the product of a persistent Northern oligarchy rather than a unified Northern position.

Rejecting both an exclusively Southern opposition and superficial appeals to unity, the author supports a broad, mass-based coalition against Buhari’s government that includes principled Northern allies. He cites attacks on the emirs of Kano and Zaria and on Sule Lamido and Ghali Umar Na’aba as evidence that northern opposition figures have suffered for supporting the PDP and Goodluck Jonathan. He concludes that meaningful opposition must be nationally assembled, informed by historical differences, and suspicious of political actors who invoke Nigerian unity without understanding its diversity.

The lecture reviews stopping trials and Wald’s equality. For IID random variables with mean \(\bar X\), a stopping trial \(J\) with finite expectation satisfies \(E[S_J]=\bar X E[J]\). The elementary renewal theorem follows by taking \(J=N(t)+1\), bounding the expected first arrival after \(t\), and using truncation: \(\lim_{t\to\infty}E[N(t)]/t=1/\bar X\).

Stopping trials are generalized to paired arrival and service variables for G/G/1 queues, where interarrival and service times are independently IID. The first arrival to an empty system is a generalized stopping trial; subsequent arrivals and service times are independent of the past, so busy periods form an embedded renewal process. The departure process itself is not a renewal process because it includes idle periods.

Using renewal-reward arguments, the lecture derives Little’s theorem: the time-average number of customers in the system equals the arrival rate \(\lambda\) times the average customer delay, \(L=\lambda W\).

Finally, for an M/G/1 queue with finite service-time moments and \(\rho=\lambda\bar V<1\), the Pollaczek–Khinchin formula gives the expected queueing time
\[
E[W_q]=\frac{\lambda E[V^2]}{2(1-\rho)}.
\]
The corresponding expected number in the system is \(\lambda E[W_q]\). The derivation uses the average residual service time \(E[V^2]/2\) and shows how service-time variability, including heavy tails, increases waiting times.

Youth suicide remains a major public health concern in China despite declining national rates, with studies reporting high rates of suicidal thoughts, planning, attempts, and ideation among adolescents. School staff and families are important gatekeepers, yet evidence that gatekeeper training reduces suicidal behavior or changes behavior is inconclusive. Existing Chinese research has focused on university students, while programs for secondary-school teachers or parents remain limited. Western programs may require localization because of sociocultural factors, parental migration among left-behind children, limited access to qualified school counselors, and gaps in standardized training and evaluation.

The study therefore used a two-round Delphi process to develop China’s first evidence-based, localized school-based suicide-prevention gatekeeper training program for teachers and parents. Program content was informed by a literature review, consultations with school counselors and suicide-prevention experts, and working-group revisions. Eight sections addressed adolescent suicide severity, understanding suicide, risk factors, warning signs, communication, risk assessment, safety planning, teacher–parent communication or parent support and help-seeking, and barriers to obtaining or providing help. The teacher- and parent-specific modules supported school–family collaboration, while the barriers module incorporated the theory of planned behavior.

An expert panel included Chinese mental-health and crisis-intervention professionals, qualifying psychiatrists and psychotherapists, psychology professors, school counselors, and experienced crisis-line operators. Participants independently rated statements on a five-point scale for importance, feasibility, and material appropriateness, received feedback after Round 1, and re-rated them in Round 2. Statements with substantial consensus were retained as program content, while those with low or conflicting ratings were discarded. The study received institutional review-board approval from Tsinghua University.

The passage reviews magnetic monopoles and the topological magnetoelectric effect, noting that no fundamental monopole particle has yet been directly observed. In three-dimensional topological insulators, a radially distributed electric field can generate circulating surface currents at interfaces where the topological parameter θ changes, producing fields equivalent to a pair of opposite magnetic monopoles.

Using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, the authors measured image potential states on Bi grown on Si(111): the topologically trivial √3×√3-Bi phase, the two-dimensional topological insulator Bi(110), and the three-dimensional high-order topological insulator Bi(111). Image potential states appeared as discrete Rydberg-like peaks above 4 eV. On √3-Bi and Bi(110), the peaks followed Gaussian profiles and narrowed as the principal quantum number increased.

On 5–6 nm-thick Bi(111), image potential states with n>1 became asymmetric and split into multiple components; the n=2 peak separated into two distinct peaks. The splitting showed no dependence on film thickness or terrace location, and similar splitting was observed in seven-quintuple-layer Bi2Se3. The authors considered and discounted symmetric/antisymmetric states, quantum-well states, and quantum-dot confinement as explanations.

A model treating image potential states on Bi(111) as electron–dyon excitons predicts that a monopole-generated magnetic field couples to orbital magnetic moments, reducing degeneracy and producing Zeeman splitting. The observed splitting followed the predicted scaling with principal quantum number; the measured n=2 splitting was about 400 meV versus a theoretical estimate of 204 meV. Varying the tunneling current and therefore the STM tip’s electric field continuously tuned the splitting according to the predicted field dependence. These results are presented as evidence for generating and detecting field-induced magnetic monopoles on the surface of a three-dimensional topological insulator.

This continuation application describes image encoding and decoding methods, apparatuses, and recording media that improve compression efficiency through motion-vector refinement for inter prediction. During decoding, initial L0 and L1 motion vectors for a current block are derived and refined using either merge-mode-based or prediction-block-based refinement, then used to generate a prediction block. Encoding similarly entropy-encodes motion-compensation information using the refined vector.

Merge-mode refinement applies search-area offsets and, based on POC differences between the L0 and L1 reference pictures and the decoding target, adds, mirrors, or scales differences from the opposite list. It may entropy-decode information identifying the initial vector and the refined vector’s magnitude, direction, and integer- or sub-pixel magnitude unit.

Prediction-block refinement is performed only under specified conditions, including bidirectional prediction merge mode, equal L0 and L1 POC differences, a vertical block size of at least 8, and an area of at least 64. It searches integer-pixel positions from −2 to +2 around each initial vector, may operate on 16×16 subblocks for larger blocks, and selects a refined vector using distortion measured by SAD, SATD, SSE, or MSE. The document also describes encoder and decoder components, coding-tree partitioning, and merge and motion-vector candidate derivation.

An inside day occurs when a bar’s high is below the previous bar’s high and its low is above the previous bar’s low, placing all price action within the prior range. An outside day has both a higher high and a lower low. Inside days are frequent across time frames, though frequency varies by market and trading session; SPY had 779 inside days since 1993, about 10% of the time.

Backtests found inside days to be poor standalone trading signals with no consistent bullish or bearish indication. Buying all inside days in the S&P 500 and selling at the next open produced only a modest average gain. Adding a five-day RSI-below-50 filter raised the average gain to 0.1% but sharply reduced trades and remained untradeable. A modified swing strategy generated 89 trades since 1993, averaging 0.45% with a 2.1 profit factor; it worked in equities but performed oppositely in gold. Testing two consecutive inside days produced only 22 trades. Additional variables are generally needed to improve inside-day strategies.

The passage explains that damages for unlawfully detaining a whaling ship compensate owners, officers, and crew for direct losses from the vessel’s unavailability during the brief whaling season, rather than constitute indirect or speculative profits. Strength training can build muscle mass, strength and endurance, but correct technique, warm-ups, cool-downs and gradual progression are important for preventing injury. Common strength-training injuries include rotator cuff tears and tendinopathy, hamstring strains, herniated discs, tendonitis, tennis elbow and golfer’s elbow. They may result from repetitive movements, sudden movements, poor form, excessive exercise or lifting weights beyond one’s ability. Symptoms can include pain, weakness, numbness, tingling and swelling.

Prevention measures include maintaining good shoulder-blade posture, stretching gently, warming up properly, limiting forceful repetitions, adjusting exercises that cause strain, and not pushing through persistent pain. Rest and seeking medical advice are recommended when discomfort continues. Hamstring rehabilitation may take days for minor pulls or weeks to months for more severe tears, while herniated discs usually improve slowly with rest, gentle exercise and sometimes pain medication.

Warm-ups increase heart rate and blood flow, delivering oxygen to muscles and reducing injury risk. Cooling down helps blood flow return gradually after exercise. Dynamic, full-range movements are useful before training, whereas static exercises are better suited to the end. Recovery also benefits from rest, a good diet and hydration; ice, compression and elevation may help initial treatment of sports injuries.

A doctor can assess injuries and may recommend imaging, physiotherapy, injections or surgery depending on severity. Consulting a doctor or qualified fitness instructor before starting a new strength-training routine can help ensure exercises are appropriate and performed correctly.

The document describes NVIDIA’s GA10x family of Ampere-architecture GPUs, including the GA102 and GA104, which build on Turing. GA102 is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N process and contains 28.3 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. GA104 powers the GeForce RTX 3070. NVIDIA reports that Ampere delivers up to 1.7 times the raster-graphics performance and twice the ray-tracing performance of Turing, while improving power efficiency by as much as 1.9 times.

GA10x streaming multiprocessors support FP32 processing on both datapaths, doubling peak FP32 throughput. They also provide 128 KB of configurable L1 cache and shared memory per SM, twice the shared-memory bandwidth of Turing, and redesigned raster operations with 112 ROPs. Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and can operate concurrently with graphics or compute workloads. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur for moving or deforming geometry, enabling motion-blur rendering up to eight times faster than Turing.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support, fine-grained structured sparsity, and improved AI performance. Sparsity doubles Tensor Core throughput for supported sparse matrices, while TF32 enables Tensor Core acceleration of FP32-based training. These features support applications including DLSS, AI denoising, RTX Voice, Broadcast, and Canvas. Enhanced DLSS adds a 9× super-resolution mode, allowing the RTX 3090 to run many games at 8K/60 fps with ray tracing.

The GeForce RTX 3090 includes 10,496 CUDA Cores and 24 GB of GDDR6X for 8K HDR gaming, while the RTX 3080 reportedly delivers up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance and 1.5 times its memory bandwidth. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and offers performance comparable to the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti. Professional products include the RTX A6000, with 48 GB of GDDR6 and NVLink expansion to 96 GB, and the A40 data-center GPU, designed for visual computing, virtualization, AI, and professional workloads.

GA10x supports third-generation NVLink and PCIe 4.0. Two GPUs can communicate with 112.5 GB/s total bandwidth and share a 96 GB memory pool. PCIe 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth and provides up to 64 GB/s on a x16 slot. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling, MTA encoding, and rates up to 19.5 Gbps, delivering up to 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth on the RTX 3090.

NVIDIA RTX IO is presented as a storage architecture that works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets directly to the GPU for GPU-based decompression. The document reports throughput improvements of up to 100 times and CPU utilization reductions of up to 20 times, with benefits for game loading, streaming, rendering, and large professional datasets.

GA10x also adds DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 support for 8K60 and 4K120 displays. Its fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 HDR AV1 playback with substantially reduced CPU use. Its seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated H.264 encoding up to 4K and HEVC encoding up to 8K. GDDR6X’s new Error Detection and Replay technology detects failed memory transmissions and retries them, helping identify memory-overclocking limits and reduce instability.

Blackhawks players discussed offensive production, defensive responsibility, and preparations for returning home for Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final. Jonathan Toews said the team cares only that goals originate from its own players, regardless of which line produces them. Patrick Kane praised the team’s depth and flexibility, while noting that forward combinations such as Teuvo Teravainen, Patrick Kane, and Jonathan Toews can create offensive opportunities when playing smart two-way hockey. Toews also praised teammates’ scoring ability, patience, and willingness to absorb responsibility.

The players said the visiting team has been defensively disciplined, effective at skating on the puck, and capable of creating chances despite limiting possession. They emphasized staying patient, confident, and attentive to defensive details rather than focusing solely on scoring. The Blackhawks aim to keep possession low in the opponent’s zone, reduce turnovers, and continue improving as the series progresses.

Returning to their home arena was described as an advantage, with an enthusiastic crowd expected to support the team. The speakers expressed confidence in the Blackhawks’ experience and collective support for teammates, including goaltender Corey Crawford, who has taken significant blame after allowing several goals. Kane stressed making the correct play rather than worrying about individual shot totals.

The paper extends a previously developed ab initio method for spin diffusion length and spin lifetime to include drift caused by an electric field along a periodic direction. The approach uses a Wigner-transformed quantum master equation with diffusion, coherent, drift, and electron–phonon scattering terms, and derives a linearized steady-state formulation for device-relevant conditions. Covariant derivatives represent the field-induced drift. A Wannier-representation finite-difference technique computes these derivatives accurately while avoiding problems caused by arbitrary eigenstate phases, band degeneracies, and crossings.

The motivation is that longitudinal electric fields can substantially alter spin diffusion through the spin-drift effect, while conventional drift-diffusion models may give significant errors when spatial spin precession is important, as in graphene–h-BN and wurtzite GaN. The paper also introduces a Rayleigh–Ritz-based spin-diffusion-length formula applicable beyond the effective-mass approximation. Results are presented for monolayer WSe₂, bulk GaAs, bulk GaN, and graphene–h-BN and compared with estimates from several model formulas.

The Georgia Court of Appeals reversed and remanded Carley Bottoms’s sentence. She had pleaded guilty to several theft-by-receiving counts and financial transaction card theft and received ten years’ probation with restitution. The court found no abuse of discretion in continuing the restitution hearing to secure the victims’ presence. However, the trial court could not require restitution for all property taken during the victims’ burglaries because Bottoms was charged only with receiving certain items, not with committing the burglaries. Restriction was limited to damages caused by her charged offenses. Her remaining enumeration of error was moot.

On June 4, 2018, Microsoft Corporation announced a definitive agreement to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion. The acquisition press release was filed as Exhibit 99.1, and investor presentation slides as Exhibit 99.2. The Form 8-K stated that the Regulation FD materials were not deemed filed or incorporated by reference except when expressly referenced.

A Middlebury College Public Safety officer falsely identified former student Addis Fouche-Channer as participating in the March 2, 2017 protest that disrupted Charles Murray’s planned lecture. The officer named Fouche-Channer but provided no other evidence that she was present. After Fouche-Channer contested the allegation and supplied Wi-Fi logs, witness statements, emails, blog posts, and phone activity, the judicial dean ended the disciplinary proceeding without a hearing, finding no reason to proceed.

Fouche-Channer then requested an apology and a formal investigation into whether the officer had racially profiled her because she is Black. The college’s investigation into whether the officer violated its anti-discrimination policy was reported complete on Sept. 14, but no determination had been announced because the decision was delayed. The officer and other college officials did not respond to requests for comment, while a college spokesman declined to provide details.

The paper investigates the feasibility of Vehicular Cloud Computing in 5G-enabled urban environments, focusing on latency, energy, emissions, and stakeholder incentives. It proposes a centralized architecture comprising end users, a 5G base station and controller, vehicles, and a cloud backup. Vehicles periodically report location, speed, available computing capacity, energy use, and task status via ETSI CAM beacons; the controller ranks candidate executors by expected dwell time, energy availability, and capacity, then assigns tasks to suitable nodes.

The delay model includes UE–controller and controller–executor transmissions, propagation, network and switching delays, computation, queuing, and allocation time. Energy models cover the network operator’s transmission and allocation overhead and the executors’ computation and result transmission; UE uplink and beacon energy are excluded because they are external to allocation decisions or already embedded in CAM messages. Task assignment maximizes utility based on nominal estimates while requiring deadline compliance and respecting executor capacity.

Uncertain execution times, energy use, and network conditions are modeled stochastically. Revenue is distributed through a coalitional game with transferable payoffs, efficient and coalitionally rational allocations, and a non-empty robust core; actual post-execution energy and timing data inform distribution, and revenue is paid only for tasks completed by their deadlines. The framework also evaluates CO₂ savings relative to traditional edge infrastructure and examines incentives for sustained vehicle participation.

Chamomile includes several species, notably Matricaria recutita (German chamomile) and Chamaemelum nobile (Roman chamomile), grown worldwide. German chamomile has long been used in teas for fevers, flu, digestive disorders, and skin ailments. Its flower essential oil, called blue oil, is obtained by steam distillation in yields of 0.2–0.4%. The oil is used for relaxation, insomnia, mood enhancement, anxiety relief, joint and muscle soreness, digestive problems, conjunctivitis, and skin care, and also appears in soaps, beverages, detergents, perfumes, foods, and cosmetics.

America’s science education crisis is reflected in low eighth-grade proficiency, declining student interest, and growing demand for STEM workers. Although 49 states have adopted standards emphasizing inquiry, many middle and high school courses still prioritize memorization and disconnect science from mathematics, technology, and ethics.

Drawing on the literacy field’s research-based approach, the passage calls for a “science of science education” built on high-quality instructional materials and sustained, curriculum-based professional learning. Teachers should engage with the same inquiry materials as students, experience productive struggle, collaborate, and deepen their content knowledge. This shifts instruction from delivering content and answers to guiding investigation, data analysis, explanation, and problem-solving.

Teachers report stronger student engagement, persistence, real-world connections, and participation by all students. District and school leaders are urged to provide appropriate materials, planning time, ongoing certified support, and principal backing for new teaching practices. Science education is presented as essential to economic prosperity and civic health.

On May 25, 2016, Microsoft Corporation announced plans to streamline its smartphone hardware business, reducing up to 1,850 positions, including 1,350 at Microsoft Mobile Oy in Finland. For the quarter ending June 30, 2016, Microsoft expected to record approximately $950 million in impairment and restructuring charges, including about $200 million for severance payments. The actions were expected to be substantially complete by the end of 2016 and fully completed by July 2017. The Form 8-K included Microsoft’s press release as Exhibit 99.1 and noted that forward-looking statements were subject to risks and uncertainties.

Exxon Mobil reported December-quarter earnings of $0.88 per share, matching the previous three quarters’ average but below the analyst estimate of $1.04. Shares fell 3% in premarket trading, and the disappointment erased about $10 billion in market value. Full-year earnings were $19.7 billion on revenue of $244.36 billion. The company also reported a $5.9 billion tax-cut gain and plans $50 billion in U.S. investment over five years. Its unchanged 77-cent dividend increased the yield to 3.55%.

Exxon aims to triple Permian Basin production to 600,000 barrels per day and expects stronger 2018 earnings if output increases and oil prices remain stable. Falling oil prices are a risk, though Goldman Sachs expects prices above $82 per barrel amid tight inventories, strong demand, Venezuelan production losses, and OPEC compliance.

This protocol describes the Canadian Social Determinants Urban Laboratory (CSDUL), a multilevel, longitudinal virtual research environment designed to examine how social, economic, political, environmental, and health-system factors influence health inequalities in Canadian cities and towns. Its backbone is Statistics Canada’s linked Canadian Population Health Survey, including survey, administrative, registry, cancer, mortality, and tax data, supplemented by area-level environmental, socioeconomic, governmental, and spatial datasets. The initial data window is expected to include roughly 500,000 participants.

A central Hub at the University of Saskatchewan and Urban Public Health Network will coordinate the project with five Nodes covering political and economic context, environmental context, socioeconomic context, material circumstances, and health systems. These teams will develop and validate contextual indicators, document the strengths and limitations of the data, and derive appropriate variables.

The primary outcome for a twofold Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition analysis will be self-reported health, categorized as at least “fair,” with additional analyses for mental health and life satisfaction. Pooled multilevel logistic models will estimate the relative contributions of individual and contextual determinants to income-related health inequalities. The analysis will account for survey weights and complex design, examine interactions and effect modification involving gender and racial identities, and compare results across socioeconomic levels.

The three-year project will integrate and disseminate CSDUL within Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, then replicate and extend the WHO/Europe decomposition analysis for urban Canada. Its intended contributions include identifying the factors most strongly associated with health outcomes, supporting tailored multisectoral interventions, and providing reusable data, methods, and tools for collaborative population-health and health-equity research.
Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated November 7, 2018, reporting under Item 8.01 that it had published a blog post on its website. The blog post was filed as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference.

A meta-analysis of 333,247 adults found that moderate alcohol consumption was associated with lower all-cause mortality than abstinence or heavy drinking. During roughly eight years of follow-up, moderate drinkers had no greater risk of cancer death than abstainers and were about 25% less likely to die of heart disease or stroke. Heavy drinkers had slightly higher all-cause mortality, with cancer-death odds about 45% higher than among moderate drinkers. Weekly binge drinking was associated with about 16% higher odds of death, largely through increased cancer rates.

Moderate intake is defined as no more than 14 servings weekly for men and seven for women. Associations varied by demographics: moderate drinking appeared beneficial among non-Latino whites and adults 60 and older, but not among non-Latino blacks or adults 18–39. Heavy drinking increased mortality among men, but not women. Possible benefits include lower blood pressure and improved blood-vessel function, while excessive consumption increases accident, violence and cancer risks. The World Health Organization recommends no alcohol consumption, citing 3.3 million alcohol-attributed deaths, or 5.9% of global deaths, in 2012.

IWM is the iShares Russell 2000 ETF, a major ETF providing exposure to small-cap U.S. stocks by tracking the Russell 2000 index. The index measures the 2,000 smallest companies in the Russell 3000, represents about 10% of its market capitalization, and is widely regarded as a benchmark for small-cap stocks and a bellwether for the U.S. economy. Launched in 1984, it is managed by FTSE Russell and rebalanced annually in June, potentially changing its components. A strategy trading IWM and RTY around the annual rebalancing reportedly produced solid performance and Russell outperformance, although broader market gains also contributed. The position can be hedged against the S&P 500 as a pair trade, and IWM may aid diversification because small-cap stocks can diverge from the broader market over time.

Diplomatic reports from January 1917 recorded Italy’s defense of government coal-price controls as necessary to sustain the war and continued press criticism of the Balfour Note and Allied territorial ambitions. The British minister in Greece considered peace negotiations satisfactory, with only minor differences remaining, while the Dutch minister forwarded a newspaper extract concerning peace proposals. In his Senate address, President Wilson explained that he had asked the belligerents to define the terms on which they would consider peace. He said the Central Powers offered only a conference, whereas the Entente powers outlined more definite conditions for a settlement. Wilson maintained that any lasting peace would require an international concert of power strong enough to prevent another such catastrophic war.

Marcus Lemonis bought the bankrupt Gander Mountain chain, renamed it Gander Outdoors, and began reopening 69 stores. He canceled national Good Sam Club rallies and repurposed its Good Sam Man mascot for Gander Outdoors.

Apple has reportedly stopped developing a cheaper, lighter Vision Pro to focus on lightweight AI smart glasses similar to Meta’s offerings. The $3,500 Vision Pro, launched in February 2024, has struggled due to its high price, bulk, limited use cases, and weak developer ecosystem, though an updated model with a better chip is still planned. Demand for face-worn computers remains largely unproven: Meta’s earlier Ray-Ban glasses sold modestly, while newer display-equipped models and potential enterprise applications offer possible paths forward. No company has clearly won the market.

Doug Weight has played well throughout the playoffs and will be missed if he does not play, though other centermen can fill in. The team aims to improve its net attacks, create more traffic, and pressure the opposing goalie when he exits the net. After a tough loss, the resilient group will use the extra rest to refocus and aim to close the series Saturday.

The athlete calls winning the Stanley Cup his greatest career accomplishment so far, while emphasizing that players must continually prove themselves. He says returning from Finland was a difficult but rewarding decision and that he focused on one game at a time. After scoring a game-winning goal, he tried to remain composed; during the final, Vancouver’s early pressure made him nervous, though he says he faked composure until winning the Cup. He also describes the Conn Smythe Trophy as a great honor and names Patrick, Ron Hextall, and Ken Dryden as fellow honored goalies.

Taylor Swift is credited as the sole writer of 67 songs, composing the lyrics and melodies alone. The passage lists these tracks in roughly chronological order, spanning her debut album through “The Tortured Poets Department: The Anthology” (2024). Though she has collaborated with producers and co-writers—including Max Martin and Shellback on “Midnights”—she is credited as lead writer on every released song. Swift began playing guitar at 10 and signed as the youngest songwriter at 15, later describing her storytelling as her defining specialty.

Texas public university officials have directed faculty to review syllabi and course content for compliance with laws and executive orders, but vague and conflicting instructions have created confusion and concern. San Jacinto College said faculty were asked to align courses with state manuals, although a faculty member reported verbal instructions to teach only a male-female binary outside transgender identity. At Texas Tech’s Angelo State University, conflicting directives were followed by an email stating employees could not teach, discuss, or acknowledge transgender identity; faculty were also told to remove unspecified “noncompliant” language. Texas A&M began a similar compliance review after two administrators were demoted and a professor fired over a gender-identity lecture video. A FIRE senior attorney called the directives an unsupported, voluntary effort to censor speech that contradicted the First Amendment. The passage states that no federal or state law prohibits public-university professors from teaching about transgender identity. The Texas AAUP encouraged faculty to report censorship, while similar efforts at other Texas public universities remained unconfirmed.

Joe Hadzima opens the first of six sessions of MIT’s “Nuts and Bolts of New Ventures and Business Plans.” The course treats business planning as an iterative process for understanding, launching, and executing new ventures rather than as producing a fixed document. Its concepts can apply to commercial, nonprofit, social, and governmental projects. Hadzima describes how the course was created after students requested practical entrepreneurship instruction. Its rapid organization succeeded by identifying a clear need, recruiting capable people, communicating the task, and allowing experts to contribute. He argues that venture success ultimately requires creating value and then capturing enough of it to remain sustainable.

The session introduces the diverse participant group, teaching team, Virtual Ink case study, and business-plan fundamentals. Virtual Ink, founded by Yonald Chery, is presented as an instructive historical case rather than a model to copy. The course’s central planning model resembles a pyramid: a mission statement supported by an elevator pitch, executive summary, presentation, full business plan, and underlying topic analysis. The entrepreneur or team must own the plan and be able to defend it. A business plan should be professional, credible, and useful for attracting investors, partners, employees, and customers, but it should not be a hype document.

Hadzima explains that investors typically want to know three things: why the proposed venture matters, why the timing is right, and why this team is capable. A persuasive plan should also anticipate objections, including why the venture might fail. The executive summary serves as a concise resume of the venture, explaining the opportunity, market, resources required, financial needs, sustainable advantage, and reasons for success within two to five pages.

Other planning topics include identifying the opportunity and market, determining customers and payers, explaining why the opportunity exists now, anticipating incumbent reactions, and providing evidence that customers will buy the offering. Development plans must break a broad project into achievable steps. “Credibility testers” are identified to reduce major risks, such as proving technical feasibility, securing access, or resolving regulatory requirements. Plans should sequence work against available resources, avoid excessive dependencies, and demonstrate that the team can execute and deliver value.

Presented as a financing document, a plan is read at three levels: an initial screening, an assessment of investment potential, and a commitment by investors and entrepreneurs. Initial screening is weakened by small markets, unrealistic financing needs, noncredible technology, misunderstood regulations, insufficient evidence of demand, weak or overly optimistic assumptions, poor presentation, and basic errors such as misspellings.

Hadzima also introduces the formula “H = R/E,” meaning happiness equals reality divided by expectations, encouraging participants to lower expectations and over-deliver. Participants are asked to form teams, and the evening concludes with a break before a session on making an effective pitch.

Charles Robert Jenkins, a 24-year-old U.S. Army sergeant, deserted to North Korea in 1965, saying he feared hazardous duty in South Korea and combat in Vietnam. He later taught English, appeared in propaganda films, and married Japanese abductee Hitomi Soga. After Soga returned to Japan in 2002, Jenkins followed with their two daughters in 2004. He received a 30-day desertion sentence, settled on Sado Island, worked at a gift shop, and wrote about his experiences. Jenkins died in Japan at 77.

The lecture reviews countable-state Markov processes defined through an embedded Markov chain and exponential exit rates \(\nu_j\). For a positive-recurrent embedded chain with stationary transition probabilities \(\pi_j\), the normalized long-run fraction of time in state \(j\) is

\[
p_j=\frac{\pi_j/\nu_j}{\sum_k \pi_k/\nu_k}.
\]

The overall transition rate is the reciprocal of the denominator and, almost surely, does not depend on the initial state. When this denominator is finite, the stationary probabilities satisfy flow balance between arrivals to and departures from each state; birth-death processes are handled by equating overall upward and downward transition rates. When the denominator is infinite, transitions may slow toward zero and no meaningful steady state exists, as illustrated by “rattled server” and discouraged-arrival examples.

The lecture also examines a hyperactive birth-death chain whose transition rates grow rapidly with state. Formal balance equations produce misleading occupancy formulas, while truncations place progressively more time in high states and yield unbounded transition rates. The embedded chain in this example lacks a meaningful steady state, illustrating why simulation results for a process should be checked against its embedded chain.

For reversibility, exponential memorylessness means that a state’s exit rate is identical when time is reversed. With backward rates \(q^*_{ij}=\nu_iP^*_{ij}\), a process is reversible when \(q^*_{ij}=q_{ji}\) for all states. Under positive recurrence and the stated stability condition, a Markov process is reversible if and only if its embedded chain is reversible. A “guessing theorem” says that, for an irreducible process, finding positive normalized probabilities satisfying detailed balance and stability establishes the state-time fractions, process reversibility, and positive recurrence of the embedded chain. This applies to qualifying birth-death processes and Markov trees.

Burke’s theorem is presented for a stable M/M/1 queue with arrival rate \(\lambda<\mu\). Its departures form an unconditional Poisson process of rate \(\lambda\); the state at time \(t\) is independent of earlier departures; and, under first-come-first-served service, a customer’s arrival time conditional on departing at \(t\) is independent of earlier departures. In tandem M/M/1 queues, the first queue’s output is Poisson but is not Poisson conditional on that queue’s arrival or service behavior. The output serves as the second queue’s Poisson input and is independent of the second queue’s service times.

The lecture then introduces random walks, where \(s_n=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\) for i.i.d. increments. Central questions concern crossing upper or lower thresholds, hitting times, which threshold is crossed, and overshoots. These problems arise in communications, queue overflow, sequential hypothesis testing, and ruin analysis. Simple random walks use increments \(+1\) or \(-1\), can be viewed as Markov chains, and have probability \(p/(1-p)^k\) of ever reaching integer \(k\). Integer random walks allow integer-valued increments, while renewal processes are the nonnegative-increment special case.
