For a G/G/1 queue with interarrival times \(X_n\), service times \(Y_n\), and queueing delays \(W_n\), a sample-path argument gives

\[
W_n=\max\{0,\;W_{n-1}+Y_{n-1}-X_n\}.
\]

Without the reflection at zero, this is a random walk driven by \(Y_{n-1}-X_n\); reflection prevents negative delays and divides the path into regenerative segments.

Finally, the lecture motivates detection, decisions, and binary hypothesis testing. It defines a binary hypothesis \(H\in\{0,1\}\), multiple observations that are i.i.d. conditional on each hypothesis, their product densities, and Bayesian posterior probabilities using prior probabilities. Comparing the two hypotheses yields a likelihood ratio involving the prior odds and the ratio of the conditional observation densities.

India’s government menstrual hygiene scheme, launched in 2011 for girls aged 10–19, covers rural areas in 107 districts across 17 states and was merged with RKSK in 2014. Sanitary-napkin use rose from 50.7% to 54% between 2014 and 2015, while expenditure increased from Rs 24.33 billion in 2014–15 to Rs 37.03 billion in 2016–17. National fund utilization remained low and uneven, although higher in 10 focus states.

The scheme faces poor-quality products, stockouts, delays of up to three months, limited awareness and inadequate ASHA training. Monthly meetings were often not held, and peer education was implemented only in Tamil Nadu. Implementation is also uneven; it had not been rolled out in West Bengal, and several states reported weak uptake or irregular supplies.

NFHS-4 found that 48% of rural women aged 15–24 practised menstrual hygiene. A Rutgers study reported that 89% of Indian women used cloth, while 14% of girls reported menstrual infections. Unsafe disposal of non-biodegradable napkins is an environmental concern; funding for disposal facilities was underused. The health minister did not respond to IndiaSpend’s requests for comment.

In macOS High Sierra, disable automatic screenshot drop shadows by running `defaults write com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow true`, followed by `killall SystemUIServer`, in Terminal. Restart the Mac if needed. To restore shadows, replace `true` with `false` and run the kill command again.

Archival notes trace U.S.-Soviet memoranda and meetings in February–March 1983. The February 4 memorandum was unsigned; Reagan initialed it and a February 7 memorandum. Clark said the latter provided a basis for discussing “next steps.” On February 15, Shultz brought Soviet Ambassador Dobrynin to the White House Residence. Reagan and Shultz met him for two hours; Reagan wanted Shultz to be a direct channel to Andropov without bureaucracy. Dobrynin afterward called the meeting potentially historic. Shultz and Dobrynin met again that evening, and Clark later sent Reagan their conversation memorandum.

Clark expressed skepticism that the Soviets intended to permit Pentecostalists to leave. Later records concern a March 3 memorandum hand-carried to the White House in San Francisco, a March 8 Pentagon meeting, and March 9 and 16 memoranda, with drafting, clearance, and forwarding details.

The passage compares mental fitness to physical fitness, emphasizing that minds need regular exercise and daily attention. It presents a seven-step routine for processing emotions and promoting happiness: identify and label your feelings; breathe slowly using five-count belly breaths; write down the source of an emotion and tear up the paper; list things you appreciate; perform a short mindful activity such as drawing, solving a puzzle, or listening to music; complete a compassion exercise involving forgiveness, support, appreciation, or self-love; and send someone a positive message. It stresses that all emotions are temporary and that accepting changing moods, releasing worries, gaining perspective, and valuing happiness over perfection can reduce stress and improve well-being.

The author disputes claims that the Government edited or doctored the electoral-reform Bill, attributing them to misinformation. A Bill is a draft law, generally prepared by a government department under a minister and approved by Cabinet. The Law Commission makes recommendations on Malawi’s laws; these pass through the Executive before a Bill is tabled in Parliament, which then debates and shapes it. The author says “doctoring” would make sense only if the Law Commission submitted an unalterable package, and urges citizens to remain attentive rather than worry.

The passage presents a theoretical framework for explaining why spatial averaging can make populations of nonlinear dynamical systems exhibit linear macroscopic dynamics. It is motivated by empirical findings that linear models effectively capture large-scale brain dynamics despite strongly nonlinear individual neurons. Earlier simulations and proofs suggested spatial averaging as the source of this linearity, but assumed homogeneous, independent, and disconnected subsystems. The new work extends the analysis to heterogeneous, interconnected, and spatially correlated systems, including fixed or random Euclidean embeddings.

The stated contributions are fourfold: extending mixing-process theory through a multivariate central limit theorem for ρ-mixing sequences, defining residual factors, and extending ρ-mixing to spatially embedded ρ*-mixing sequences; proving asymptotic linearity of spatially averaged state dynamics under relatively mild restrictions, with limits generally linear time-varying (LTV); proving linear time-invariant (LTI) limits under additional stationarity assumptions; and analyzing finite-sample convergence rates. Convergence is parametric, \(O(1/\sqrt N)\), for independent subsystems, slows as correlations increase, and fails under perfect correlation.

The preliminaries define ρ-mixing sequences, in which statistical dependence decays as separation increases, as a generalization of independent sequences. A central limit theorem is stated for zero-mean, finite-variance ρ-mixing variables with bounded shifted partial-sum variance and slowly varying cumulative-variance growth.

The central problem considers \(N\) heterogeneous discrete-time nonlinear subsystems with noise and finite-range neighborhood interactions, and asks whether their centered, normalized population average becomes asymptotically linear as \(N\) grows. To support this result, the passage extends ρ-mixing to random vectors and introduces a residual factor \(h(N)\) for a cumulative sum when \(\operatorname{Cov}(S_N)/(Nh(N))\) has a finite limit. Under uniformly bounded variances, \(h(N)=N\) is a residual factor, although factors matching the covariance growth rate are more useful. Specific relationships are established between correlation decay and residual-factor growth: decay proportional to \(1/n\) gives \(h(N)=\log N\), decay proportional to \(1/\log(1+n)\) gives \(h(N)=N/\log N\), and decay proportional to \(1/n^p\) gives \(h(N)=N^{1-p}\). Slowly varying residual factors are identified as critical for central-limit and asymptotic-linearity results.

Business Insider held a virtual event, "Beyond the Bell: Navigating the Path to Public," on September 30, sponsored by Fidelity Investments, featuring experts from Hinge Health, Fidelity Investments, and AuditBoard. Panelists — Melike Atil, Emily Cervino, Bianca Buck, and Raul Villar Jr. — advised companies preparing for an IPO on shifting investor expectations, new regulatory demands, and preserving culture, noting that staying private longer gives companies more runway to prepare. Recommended practices included bringing in outside experts to handle the IPO process, running quarterly reviews to understand the business externally, building multi-year timeframes, and proactively meeting with investors. Panelists also discussed regulatory reporting, shareholder and disclosure requirements, employee compensation and talent retention, the importance of surrounding themselves with the right investors, the 18-to-24 month timeline, and the need for a suitable broker to unlock liquidity. Villar emphasized communicating with employees after quarterly public calls, while Cervino noted IPOs create wealth opportunities requiring financial, tax, and charitable giving support for employees.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting its second-quarter 2020 financial results, announced July 30, 2020. Exhibit 99.1 contains the results press release, and Exhibit 99.2 provides information on non-GAAP financial measures; both are incorporated by reference. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card Physical Layer Version 6.00 behavior, emphasizing UHS-II. UHS-II-capable hosts support both Legacy SD Bus and UHS-II interfaces, and removable UHS-II slots connect to both. After power-up, the host provides RCLK and STB.L on D0 and checks whether D1 changes from EIDL to STB.L. Detection initiates UHS-II initialization; failure within the card-defined 200 µs detection period causes initialization through SD Bus. UHS-II initialization proceeds through PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration by Device ID, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization, which carries emulated SD commands in packets. CMD0 restarts SD-TRAN initialization.

The specification also defines UHS-II and UHS-III bus ranges, introduces FD624 at up to 624 MB/s, and describes performance classes, cache, self-maintenance, command queueing, and 1.8 V low-voltage operation. Cache data can be lost if not flushed before power-off. The command queue supports voluntary reordering or sequential execution.

The host controls all communication through broadcast and addressed commands. Card identification uses CMD only and covers reset, voltage verification with CMD8, initialization with CMD55/ACMD41, CID retrieval with CMD2, and RCA publication with CMD3. CMD8 must precede ACMD41 for SDHC and SDXC initialization. ACMD41 communicates the desired voltage range and host capacity support, may query OCR, and must reach readiness within one second. UHS-I initialization also covers 1.8 V switching through CMD11 and sampling-point tuning through repeated CMD19.

In data-transfer mode, CMD7 selects one card, CMD4 configures driver strength, and the clock may advance from identification frequency to the operating range. Block transfers use CRC protection and normally have a maximum block size of 512 bytes. Reads and writes can be stopped with CMD12; write buffering may keep DAT0 busy while programming continues. Misalignment, length, address, CRC, and write-protection errors are reported. ACMD23 supports pre-erasing, ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks, and CMD32/CMD33/CMD38 perform erase, discard, or full-user-area logical erase. Discard makes affected data undefined, while FULE logically erases the entire user area.

Three write-protection methods are described: a mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking. Locked cards permit basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and CMD42, but not data access. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, and force erase. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password and COP Unlock command; when the FEP is set, a COP card remains inaccessible after reset until unlocked. FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP, erases all card content and the normal password, and leaves the FEP unchanged.

CMD55 causes the next command to be interpreted as an ACMD. CMD6 provides check and set modes for access mode, command-system extensions, driver strength, and power-limit functions, returning a 512-bit status block. UHS-II mode requires Power Limit support, while the total card power is the sum of VDD1 and VDD2 consumption. The default limit is 0.72 W, speed-grade performance is defined at 1.44 W, and stated maxima are 1.80 W for removable cards and 2.88 W for embedded devices.

The lecture derives perturbative path-integral methods for interacting quantum field theories. It begins with a general master formula expressing a time-ordered operator as a path integral. The action is separated into free and interaction parts, \(S=S_0+S_i\), with the assumption that the interaction contains no time derivatives. Treating \(S_i\) as small produces an exact expression for interacting correlation functions as a ratio of free-theory correlation functions containing time-ordered exponentials of \(iS_i\).

Expanding this ratio in powers of \(S_i\) gives the perturbative series. The zeroth-order term is the free-theory \(n\)-point function, while higher orders contain time-ordered products of external fields and interaction Hamiltonians. By Wick’s theorem, these correlation functions factorize into products of free-theory two-point functions.

The lecture applies this procedure to an interaction
\[
\mathcal L_i=-\frac{\lambda}{4!}\phi^4
\]
and computes the interacting two-point function. At first and second order in \(\lambda\), Wick contractions are enumerated and combined. Some terms cancel, leaving contributions represented by diagrams with four-legged interaction vertices.

These contractions are organized using Feynman diagrams, which provide a more intuitive and less tedious alternative to counting contractions directly. The coordinate-space Feynman rules assign a free Feynman propagator to each internal line, a factor \(-i\lambda\) and a spacetime integration to each interaction vertex, and a factor of one to each external point. Each diagram must also be divided by its appropriate symmetry factor. Factorials from the perturbative expansion and from identical fields at a vertex cancel when vertex and leg permutations are accounted for.

Finally, the lecture introduces momentum-space Feynman rules using Fourier transforms. Translation invariance produces overall momentum-conservation delta functions, while momentum conservation is imposed separately at every vertex. Each internal line carries a momentum and a momentum-space free propagator, each vertex contributes \(-i\lambda\) and a four-dimensional delta function enforcing conservation, undetermined loop momenta are integrated over, and diagram symmetry factors are applied. An example with two four-legged vertices is translated into its momentum-space expression.

The column reviews Netflix’s documentary “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish,” about Michigan junior high student Lauryn Licari and her boyfriend, Owen McKenny, who received escalating abusive, sexually graphic, and threatening messages from someone with intimate knowledge of their lives. After 18 months and a stalled local investigation, the FBI received hundreds of pages of messages and sought Owen’s phone for forensic examination.

The reviewer finds the documentary sad and thought-provoking but criticizes its limited explanation of cellphone forensics, including the distinction between information on a device and cellular-provider records. The case illustrates how constant cellphone access can facilitate cybercrime, generate numerous suspects, and harm both victims and those involved in investigations. The column also discusses Oklahoma’s one-year “bell to bell” school policy restricting phones and internet-connected devices, noting backlash from some parents and students.

SOS Defensive Do’s direct ballhandlers toward side, corner, or baseline checkpoints using SET, ON, and SMOTHER positions. Defenders use contact SNUGGLE denial one pass away, FRONT deep posts, Go Base post traps, and wing box pressure while denying middle drives. Checkpoints include the corners, extended free-throw line, baseline, and half court.

Weakside defenders use Double or Triple Helpside “I” alignments to provide help, deny cuts, trap, and rotate. During sideline and baseline traps, the three uninvolved defenders form a Helpside Triangle “I.” After a pass leaves the trap, defenders rotate immediately and close out on the nearest opponent.

When a wing ballhandler drives middle, the defender turns the dribble toward the nearest sideline checkpoint; if the ballhandler reaches the free-throw-line area, X2 cross-switches with X3. Defenders switch on contact against off-ball screens using “Screen/Over/Switch” calls. Contact traps apply to side screen-and-roll, mid-screen, baseline penetration, mismatch, and corner situations, while near-player rotations address unstructured offenses. On every shot attempt, all five defenders must box out and “flood the boards” for the rebound.

On June 22, 2016, Apple Inc. completed the issuance and sale of $1.377 billion in 4.15% notes due June 22, 2046. Deutsche Bank AG, Taipei Branch and KGI Securities Co. Ltd. served as managers under a June 7, 2016 subscription agreement. The notes were issued under Apple’s April 29, 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee, and a registration statement filed April 28, 2016. Interest is payable semiannually on June 22 and December 22, beginning December 22, 2016. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Apple furnished the subscription agreement, officer’s certificate and form of global note as exhibits, along with a legal opinion and consent from Shearman & Sterling LLP.

The paper investigates how large language models (LLMs) can generate 100% chemically valid molecules using SMILES or SELFIES representations. Experiments on ChEBI-20 text-based molecule generation and captioning show that LLMs perform worse with SELFIES than with SMILES, despite SELFIES guaranteeing valid molecular strings. Invalid SELFIES Editing removes non-alphabet symbols to ensure validity, but substantially reduces other performance metrics.

Using LLMs as iterative post-hoc correctors improves SMILES validity, but correction rates vary by model and error type, and improvements are accompanied by significant declines in BLEU, Levenshtein, and other metrics. The most common errors are parentheses and valence errors.

The proposed SmiSelf framework converts invalid SMILES into a molecular graph, transforms it into SELFIES, and converts it back into SMILES, using graph intermediaries to eliminate syntactic and semantic errors. SmiSelf guarantees 100% validity, generally causes smaller performance degradation than existing correction approaches, preserves molecular characteristics, and improves validity, diversity, and class membership in class-specific molecule generation. Its main limitation is slight distortion when correcting molecules for one-to-one text-based generation, which can reduce alignment with descriptions and ground truth.

The study reports strain-induced, field-free superconducting diode effects (SDEs) in centrosymmetric NbSe₂. Devices were fabricated by placing exfoliated NbSe₂ on h-BN supported by a curved aluminum nanoridge, which applied local uniaxial stress. SDEs appeared in stressed regions but not in unstressed areas of the same devices. For one device, the superconducting transition temperature was 6.4 K, while the maximum zero-field critical-current difference and diode efficiency were 286 μA and 6.76%, respectively. Both declined with increasing temperature and magnetic field.

Different devices exhibited three field dependences: even, odd, and mixed even–odd symmetry of ΔI_c. The proposed explanation involves two independent, spatially orthogonal nonreciprocal channels. Uniaxial stress breaks inversion symmetry and creates real-space structural polarity, producing a B-even SDE along the armchair direction. An external magnetic field breaks time-reversal symmetry and induces valley polarization and finite Cooper-pair momentum, producing a B-odd SDE along the zigzag direction. Reversing the magnetic field reverses this field-driven nonreciprocity.

The work establishes a method for generating and studying zero-field SDEs in superconducting materials and proposes a platform for investigating stress effects and developing superconducting quantum devices.

Mike Peca’s Selke Trophy win and repeated nominations reflect his consistency and merit. A player held different positions during nine years with the North Stars and Dallas Stars while pursuing the Stanley Cup and remaining competitive annually. The speaker supports unrestricted free agency as a roster-building tool alongside drafting and trades and says signings generally worked for both teams and players.

Tasmania’s Meander Valley Council will auction the Beerepoot family’s Mole Creek home, the Blue Wren Hideaway, on September 1 unless overdue council rates are paid. The family has withheld rates since 2010, saying the land belongs to God and they cannot submit to council authority. Two other family properties had their rates paid in June. Councilors approved selling all three properties in March when $9,332 was outstanding; prior legal action led police to seize and sell an old vehicle for the family.

Fitch Ratings affirmed Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc.'s (MMC) Long-Term Issuer Default Rating and existing senior unsecured debt ratings at 'A-' and short-term ratings at 'F2', and revised the Rating Outlook to Positive from Stable. The affirmation reflects MMC's multi-year trend of improved operating performance and stronger credit metrics, both absolutely and relative to peers, in line with Fitch's upgrade triggers. Fitch cited MMC's strong balance sheet, financial flexibility, excellent cash flow generation and top-tier competitive position as one of the world's largest diversified services firms, with major insurance brokerage and consulting operations. Partially offsetting factors are contingent risks to reputation and potential litigation and regulatory actions, which Fitch views as manageable. Liquidity remained strong, with $1 billion of cash and equivalents at Dec. 31, 2016 and a $1.5 billion multi-currency unsecured revolving credit facility expiring November 2020. Fitch expects continued free cash flow growth from expense reductions and earnings growth, with restructuring expenses immaterial and share repurchases treated as discretionary ($800 million in 2016 versus $1.4 billion in 2015). Key metrics were strong: a 20% Fitch-calculated consolidated EBIT operating margin in 2016 (up from 19%), debt-to-EBITDA of 1.5x (roughly 1.8x pro forma for the January 2017 debt issuance and refinancing, expected to normalize lower), and EBITDA-to-interest coverage above 16x. Both the RIS and Consulting segments posted organic revenue growth and margin expansion, with expected 2017–2018 earnings growth keeping metrics within rating guidelines. Upgrade triggers include EBIT operating margins of 18% or better, debt-to-EBITDA near 1.5x, and EBITDA-to-interest above 14x; a return to Stable Outlook could follow failure to reduce debt-to-EBITDA to near 1.5x, coverage below 10x, material litigation or regulatory charges, or a material goodwill impairment. A full list of affirmed ratings covering commercial paper and senior debt and notes maturing 2018 through 2047 was included.

OpenAI and Stripe introduced ChatGPT’s Instant Checkout, powered by the open-source Agentic Commerce Protocol, built on Anthropic’s MCP standard. The U.S.-launch will expand to more than a million merchants, including Glossier, Skims, Spanx, and Vuori. Because ACP is open source, other AI assistants could adopt it, potentially shifting shopping away from Google and Amazon. OpenAI says broad adoption will simplify merchant integrations, though it may cost retailers customer-data control and incur Stripe transaction fees. Merchants must provide detailed, current product feeds for ChatGPT to recommend their products, prompting the emergence of “AIO,” a possible successor to SEO. The approach could make ChatGPT a major product arbiter while raising questions about recommendation transparency and paid placement.

Researchers found that brown recluse spiders use large spinnerets to draw silk into loops and smaller spinnerets to clamp and release them, creating a web of micro-loops. The silk is unusually thin, flat, sticky and tough; its loops strengthen the material, add flexibility and prevent the web from collapsing. This ground-dwelling species uses its fly-paper-like web to trap prey. Because earlier attempts to loop synthetic fibers caused them to break, researchers propose using thin, flat, nanoscale ribbons instead. They have developed mathematical models, begun creating a synthetic version and filed a patent application. Potential uses include protective structures in space, energy-absorbing bungee cords for stunts and improved parachute cords. More broadly, the spider-inspired material could produce strong, lightweight, flexible fabrics and cords without petroleum, toxic substances, high temperatures or substantial energy.

The third Hero Indian Super League’s 2016 finale drew 54,000 stadium attendees and 41 million television viewers. Overall viewership rose 41% from 2015 to 216 million, including 101 million rural viewers. Mumbai, Chennai and Tamil Nadu also registered strong growth. Jio-platform watchtime reached 2.3 times the previous year, while average stadium occupancy exceeded 84%. In Kerala, ISL was 2016’s most-viewed televised sporting event.

Researchers have documented about 150 petroglyphs at Jebel Misma and nearby Jebel Arnaan and Jebel Mleiha in the now-arid Nefud region of Arabia. Dating to 12,800–11,400 years ago, the engravings span four phases, from stylized human figures to naturalistic animals as long as 3 meters and later cartoonlike depictions. Researchers think the artists were among the first nomads to enter the region as it became wetter following an arid period that ended about 19,000 years ago. Temporary lakes supported wildlife, and the engravings may have marked territory or water sources. Nearby excavations yielded stone tools and objects indicating links with prehistoric peoples in the Eastern Mediterranean, while the engravings’ scale and style reflect a distinct artistic tradition. Arabia’s last lush era ended about 6,000 years ago, leaving the Nefud among Earth’s driest places.

Research by University of Washington astronomer Rory Barnes suggests many exoplanets discovered by powerful telescopes may be tidally locked, with one side permanently facing their star. By expanding models to include larger planets, eccentric orbits, and varied initial rotation periods, Barnes found tidal locking could be much more common than previously assumed. He estimates every potentially habitable planet detected by NASA’s TESS mission will likely be tidally locked. His paper, “Tidal Locking of Habitable Exoplanets,” was accepted by *Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy*.

Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said North Korea’s missile and nuclear developments could destabilize the yen despite its safe-haven reputation. He said currencies should be market-set and urged the 11 remaining TPP countries to proceed without the United States, believing Washington would eventually rejoin.

The passage is dominated by a list of financial and business headlines — repeated several times — covering Fifth Third's $10.9 billion acquisition of Comerica, the Santander UK CEO's departure ahead of the TSB merger, JPMorgan Chase's AI integration, the Bank of England's largest six-month repo allotment since 2020, AMD's stock surge on an OpenAI chip deal, London's IPO revival hopes, Tesla's record Q3 deliveries and a teaser for a new affordable EV, a possible Wall Street-style equity tool under consideration by the Trump team, U.S. stock gains ahead of a shutdown threat, the Bifrost subsea cable launch, Poland's $5.5 billion NATO fuel network investment, frozen New York City infrastructure funds, Danantara's Indonesian waste-to-power projects, South Korea's post-data-centre-fire service restoration, Bezos's space-based data centre plans, OpenAI's $500 billion employee share valuation and new parental controls, Opera's Neon AI browser, and items on Chinese soybean purchase halts and a print/online finance publication's global reach.

The one fully reported story concerns oil: prices rose roughly 1.5% on Monday after OPEC+ approved a smaller-than-expected output increase of 137,000 barrels per day from November, matching October's increment. Brent reached about $65.44 and U.S. West Texas Intermediate near $61.77. Members had debated a larger hike to defend market share against restraint; the group prioritised price stability, with the move seen as stabilising after weeks of volatility. Analysts warned gains may be short-lived given uneven demand, seasonal refinery maintenance, rising inventories and slower consumption, leaving the market balanced between cautious optimism and oversupply risk ahead of the next meeting and into 2026.

Euclidean regularity at black-hole and Rindler horizons requires periodic identification of Euclidean time, yielding a temperature that depends on the observer’s chosen time coordinate and, for black holes, on the surface gravity.

Vacuum states in curved spacetime are not unique because different time foliations produce different quantizations. For a black hole, canonical quantization in Schwarzschild time yields the Schwarzschild or Boulware vacuum, whereas periodic Euclidean time yields the Hartle-Hawking vacuum. The Schwarzschild vacuum has a singular horizon and divergent stress-energy beyond it, while the Hartle-Hawking vacuum gives regular observables. Assuming the horizon is physically smooth therefore favors the Hartle-Hawking vacuum, though the distinction cannot currently be tested experimentally. These vacua are physically inequivalent states related by a Bogoliubov transformation; each appears highly excited relative to the other.

For Rindler spacetime, periodic Euclidean angular identification produces the standard Minkowski vacuum restricted to the Rindler patch. Consequently, the Minkowski vacuum appears thermal to a Rindler observer. This is demonstrated by treating a thermal density matrix as the reduced state of an entangled pure state in two identical systems. The corresponding oscillator state is a squeezed state and is invariant under the difference of the two Hamiltonians.

In the Schrödinger representation of quantum field theory, the Minkowski Hilbert space factors into left- and right-Rindler spaces. Expanding the Minkowski vacuum in right-Rindler modes and tracing out the inaccessible left region yields the Rindler thermal density matrix, proportional to \(e^{-\beta H_R}\), with \(\beta=2\pi\) in Rindler-time units. Thus, Rindler temperature reflects the observer’s limited access to the other spacetime region; an analogous black-hole interpretation is deferred.

IDC finds that simulation, modeling, and data analytics are increasingly central to industrial innovation, product quality, cost reduction, faster development, and more reliable decision-making. In a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers at industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, three-quarters prioritized innovation potential, while 57% viewed these technologies as important for improving quality and preventing defects and negative user experiences. About half already used them in product development, production and process planning, or quality management, with deployment expected to reach as high as 90% within two years.

Industrial enterprises are adopting 3D visualization, virtual prototyping, simulation-based digital twins, IoT feedback, AR/VR, and cloud-based engineering workstations. These technologies can reduce physical prototyping and testing, accelerate development, optimize materials and processes, and support new products, services, and business models, including “Product as a Service” and outcome-based services. However, fragmented data silos remain a major obstacle; IDC recommends a holistic data strategy and a unified “single source of truth” across the product life cycle and value-creation chain.

High-performance computing is viewed by four out of five surveyed industry decision makers as a game changer for product and process innovation. HPC enables complex calculations, faster and more frequent simulations, broader use scenarios, and greater agility, while demand is expected to rise from 8% currently identifying high demand to almost half within two years. More than a quarter of enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, and another 39% are planning or piloting deployment.

Current HPC use faces inadequate capacity, outdated infrastructure, high investment and licensing costs, downtime, security threats, energy consumption, and shortages of expertise. Security is a leading concern for 72% of respondents, sustainability for 58%, and lack of expertise for 42%. Enterprises therefore show strong interest in external infrastructure: 87% of HPC users prefer or plan to use cloud providers, while 74% operate or plan own infrastructure in colocation data centers.

IDC expects the public cloud to become the leading HPC architecture, followed by hybrid cloud, with HPC-as-a-Service offering scalability, flexible performance, faster access to current hardware and methods, and a shift from capital to operating expenditure. Recommendations include selecting an HPC operating model according to utilization, budget, performance, security, and skills needs; ensuring scalability, security, and energy efficiency; and using external expertise and ecosystem partners where internal capabilities are insufficient.

A prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III study evaluated a single heterologous booster dose of Biological E’s recombinant RBD-based CORBEVAX™ vaccine in India. The trial enrolled 416 adults aged 18–80 years who were SARS-CoV-2-negative and had received two doses of COVAXIN or COVISHIELD™ at least six months earlier. Within each primary-vaccine cohort, 156 participants received CORBEVAX™ and 52 received placebo. The primary endpoint was neutralizing-antibody response 28 days after boosting; safety, reactogenicity, humoral responses to ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron, and cellular immunity were also assessed.

CORBEVAX™ was safe and well tolerated. Adverse events were mild to moderate, resolved without sequelae, and led to no discontinuations; no serious or grade 3 adverse events, deaths, or adverse events of special interest were reported. Compared with placebo, CORBEVAX™ produced statistically superior neutralizing-antibody and anti-RBD IgG responses, including greater proportions with at least twofold increases. Omicron-neutralizing responses increased from 43% to 91% in COVISHIELD™-primed recipients and from 33% to 75% in COVAXIN-primed recipients. The booster also enhanced interferon-gamma–producing PBMC responses, while IL-4 levels were unchanged. Overall, the vaccine elicited effective humoral and cellular immune responses after either primary series. A limitation was that immune-response findings were reported only through day 28; longer-term safety and immunogenicity follow-up was ongoing.

UK median disposable household income reached £27,300 in the year ending 2017, up 2.3% from the previous year after inflation and £1,600 above pre-downturn levels. Poorer households benefited most: average income for the poorest fifth rose £1,800 since the banking crisis, compared with £200 for the richest fifth, modestly reducing inequality. However, average annual disposable income remained £12,748 for the poorest fifth versus £65,542 for the richest. The richest fifth paid an average £21,400 in direct taxes, while the poorest paid £1,900. Retired households had median disposable income of £22,300, compared with £29,900 for non-retired households, and their income growth was slower.

Insurance-industry research found British building fire-safety tests unrepresentative, using wood and sealed cladding without real-world gaps or penetrations. Following Grenfell Tower, the ABI called for non-combustible materials, testing reform, and mandatory sprinklers in new schools, care homes and warehouses over 2,000 square metres.

The study examines how Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine affected foreign co-funding, international authorship patterns, and citation impact in research funded by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MESU), the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU), and the National Research Foundation of Ukraine (NRFU). It also describes Ukraine’s Soviet-inherited research structures, long-standing underfunding, publication requirements that prioritized Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed journals, and wartime budget reductions. Public R&D expenditure fell from 0.75% of GDP in 2010 to 0.33% in 2023, while researchers faced displacement, military service, infrastructure damage, and declining institutional capacity.

The analysis covered all 61,698 Scopus-indexed articles published in 2020–2023 with at least one Ukrainian-affiliated author. Funding was identified through Scopus metadata, acknowledgement text, and the UKRNTI registry; 15,179 articles, or 25%, were classified as funded. The study distinguished Ukrainian-only, foreign-only, and joint Ukrainian–foreign funding; foreign co-authorship and co-affiliation; and calculated field-normalised citation impact (FNCI), supplemented by negative binomial regression.

The proportion of Ukrainian articles acknowledging funding rose from 21.7% in 2020–2021 to 28.5% in 2022–2023, although total output fell 3.6%. The combined share funded by MESU, NASU, and NRFU increased from 8.6% to 11.9%. MESU’s share rose from 4.3% to 5.0%, NASU’s from 4.0% to 4.8%, and NRFU’s from 0.9% to 3.0%.

Foreign funding was associated with greater international collaboration. The numbers of articles with foreign co-authorship and foreign co-affiliations increased across the three agencies, while foreign co-funding remained especially prominent in NASU-funded research. Poland led foreign co-affiliations for MESU- and NRFU-funded articles, while the Netherlands led for NASU-funded articles. Germany, the USA, and Poland remained central collaborators and co-funders. Russia disappeared from the leading country lists after the full-scale invasion, while Slovakia, Lithuania, Kazakhstan, and Finland gained prominence in some categories. The average number of foreign co-funders per article declined from 20.9 to 18.4 for NASU-funded research and from 11.1 to 2.1 for NRFU-funded research.

Foreign-only funded articles had the highest FNCI, declining from 1.70 to 1.49 across the periods. Ukrainian-only articles generally had the lowest impact, although MESU-funded articles rose from 0.58 to 1.14 because of a small number of highly cited articles. NASU-funded impact remained nearly unchanged at 0.36 to 0.35, NRFU-funded impact declined from 0.70 to 0.61, and unfunded articles improved from 0.29 to 0.37. Internationally co-authored articles and those involving foreign co-affiliations consistently outperformed articles by Ukraine-only affiliated researchers. MESU articles with foreign co-affiliations showed a particularly large FNCI increase, from 0.85 to 3.84, driven by highly cited outliers. NASU-funded articles without foreign co-funding were statistically indistinguishable from unfunded articles in 2022–2023.

Regression results showed positive associations between foreign co-funding and citation impact for NASU-funded articles in both periods and, more weakly, for NRFU-funded articles. The MESU relationship changed between periods. Most models explained little variance, limiting strong causal or predictive conclusions.

The findings indicate that funded research generally had greater citation impact, but international collaboration was more consistently associated with visibility than domestic funding alone. The authors identify concerns about current allocation mechanisms and recommend greater transparency, strategic use of joint foreign funding, support for international engagement, and a centralized national database documenting grants, funded researchers, and research outputs.

Taxpayers are generally due to file by April 17 and can request an extension to avoid penalties. Late filings may incur fees, while failure to file can mean forfeiting refunds or, in serious cases, jail time. Refunds generally must be claimed within three years; as of March 8, the IRS reported $1.1 billion in unclaimed 2014 refunds for about one million taxpayers. Even people not required to file may have withholding refunds or qualify for credits such as the EITC. IRS-created substitute returns may overstate taxes because credits and deductions are not considered. Taxpayers owing money receive notices with penalties and interest and may set up installment payments; continued nonpayment can lead to asset seizures. The passage urges timely filing and communication with the IRS.

Automation Anywhere’s Bot Store, an online marketplace for off-the-shelf plug-and-play bots, doubled its bot count in two months. AI is the largest category with 24 bots, speech-to-text leads downloads, finance and accounting is the leading business process, and SAP has 31 listings. The addition of Automation Anywhere IQ Bot enables computer vision, natural language processing and machine learning capabilities, including automation of utility bills, bank statements, settlement instructions, benefits explanations and 1040 and W4 forms.

Colorado Gov. John Hickenlooper will testify before a California legislative committee on February 14 about the state’s experience regulating recreational cannabis. The hearing will address cannabis taxes, regulatory timelines, tax compliance and implementation of a track-and-trace system. California officials face a January 1, 2018 deadline under Proposition 64, and Sen. Mike McGuire expressed concern that the timeline was unrealistic. Other California officials, industry professionals and state agency leaders will also speak, and the hearing will be live-streamed.

Arsenal visit Tottenham on Sunday in the 50th North London derby of Arsene Wenger's reign; Arsenal won 18, drew 21 and lost 10 of the previous 49 meetings. Spurs fans expect a tight 2-1 win, see Arsenal possibly playing deep and on the counter as against Manchester City in the FA Cup semi-final, and call the North London derby the biggest in British football with a poisonous atmosphere. Arsenal fans, buoyed by cup and league wins and a new formation, say the match is about returning to the top four, building confidence before the cup final and preventing Spurs from winning the title; one predicts 2-1, another 1-1. They also note Spurs finishing above Arsenal for the first time in over twenty years and that most fans still want Wenger replaced.

Tony James is backing a newly launched life sciences investment firm led by a former Flagship associate, according to STAT. The newsletter also lists updates on pharma tariffs, drug pricing, biotech deals, clinical trials, FDA actions, AI-driven digital health M&A, and healthcare policy.

Developmental research cited in the passage indicates that children’s fantastical beliefs, including belief in Santa, are not harmful and may support counterfactual reasoning and emotional development. Most children believe in Santa and abandon that belief by about age eight, with their questions reflecting growing cognitive understanding.

Parents can respond by offering plausible explanations or evidence to extend belief, redirecting questions so children develop their own explanations, or presenting disconfirming evidence to establish Santa as a fantasy. Studies suggest children generally react positively when they discover the truth, evaluate information from trusted sources, and are unlikely to suffer irreparable harm from a single well-intentioned lie. Modest gifts from Santa can preserve a positive holiday experience even after belief has ended, while larger gifts can come from parents.

Jacques Dubochet, Joachim Frank and Richard Henderson won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing cryo-electron microscopy, which freezes biomolecules and produces detailed images of biological structures down to individual atoms. Dubochet rapidly vitrified sample water to prevent electron-beam diffraction; Frank developed mathematical models to sharpen images; and Henderson generated a 3-D protein image at atom-level resolution in 1990. The academy said the method advances understanding of life’s chemistry and pharmaceutical development. The 9-million-kronor prize is shared among the three scientists based in Switzerland, the U.S. and Britain.

Stephen Hawking and Thomas Hertog submitted “A Smooth Exit from Eternal Inflation?”, an alternate multiverse model proposing infinitely many parallel universes alongside ours. Submitted days before Hawking’s death at 76, it also predicts our universe will die out as stars lose energy and was under consideration by a leading journal.

The passage defines a standardized Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperating between SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and supporting hypervisors. The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted guest page whose layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save area while exposing only state required for communication. Protocol version negotiation, hypervisor feature advertisement, CPUID and SEV-information requests, GHCB GPA registration, AP reset hold, and guest termination are handled through GHCB MSR protocols.

The specification defines standard handling for non-automatic exits, including use of the VALID_BITMAP, required guest and hypervisor state, VMGEXIT error reporting, and protection of GHCB access from interrupts and preemption. Supported events include MSR and MMIO protection, VMMCALLs, page-state changes, SNP guest requests and extended certificate requests, AP creation, doorbell-page management, restricted-injection IPIs and timers, APIC ID discovery, execution at different VMPL levels, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, and termination requests.

Additional sections cover the SEV-SNP secrets page and EFI Confidential Computing Blob, AP booting through AP reset hold or SNP AP creation, AP jump tables, NMI handling, and hardware debug virtualization. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. The document also defines the shared #HV doorbell page used with restricted injection, including PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, host interrupt presentation and acknowledgment, guest EOI processing, and associated VMGEXIT configuration requests.

This continuation application describes a linear surgical stapler used to clamp, cut, and staple tissue. The stapler includes a cartridge half supporting a reload and a pivoting firing assembly, and an anvil half supporting an anvil plate with staple-forming pockets. A clamp lever captures a distal anvil latch pin to clamp the halves together. A proximal retaining assembly captures a proximal anvil pin to couple the halves and retains the firing assembly before and after firing; during firing, it also prevents the clamp lever from opening. The firing assembly uses side beams and cam ramps to drive staples and a center knife to cut tissue simultaneously. A tissue-gap post establishes a predetermined gap between the cartridge and anvil, and shrouds improve grip and manipulation.

Exemplary operation involves placing tissue between the stapler halves, aligning and coupling their proximal ends, rotating the anvil half toward the cartridge half, closing the clamp lever, and actuating a firing knob. After firing, the firing assembly is returned to its home position, the clamp lever is released and opened, and the proximal coupling is disengaged to separate the stapled and cut tissue.

The disclosure focuses on multiple pin-trap mechanisms that releasably retain the proximal pivot pin while the stapler is open, including a “hang open” or “open aperture” state. These mechanisms allow one-handed manipulation, resist unintended separation, and provide controlled release.

Described embodiments include: a cartridge-half slide with an aperture and detents that captures the proximal anvil pin in a locked position; a spring-biased pin on the anvil half that engages cartridge camming surfaces to bias the halves toward clamping and permits separation after sufficient rotation; a spring-biased cartridge-half hook slide that captures the anvil pin and is released with a button; and a proximally biased anvil-half hook slide that captures a cartridge pin. Further embodiments use a C-clip with either a pivotable ejector lever or a slidable ejector slide, as well as proximally biased slides incorporating camming surfaces for automatic release, assisted separation, or both during approximation.

Other disclosed configurations include opposing spring-biased slides whose hooks cooperate to trap a pivot pin, and a rotatable latch assembly having a torque arm. In that configuration, further opening of the anvil half causes its proximal channel extension to depress the torque arm, rotate the latch finger away from the pin, and establish a second pivot axis that permits the stapler halves to separate.

The stated combinations broadly cover staplers having opposed anvil and staple-deploying halves, a lateral proximal pivot projection, and a longitudinally translating locking member or slide that captures and releases the projection. Optional features include spring biases, accessible buttons, notches and hooks, camming surfaces, non-circular pins, and configurations that retain the proximal coupling throughout movement between open and clamped states.

The passage describes a patent application for a laser diode proximity sensor packaged in a single integrated module. Prior art proximity sensors, used in cell phones, tablets and personal computing devices to detect nearby objects (and optionally measure distance and ambient light), employ a plastic housing and cap, glass lenses, and a central barrier joined with adhesive. Such assemblies require many tiny parts in a 2.5–2.8 mm footprint, present lens alignment and reflection problems, and are subject to glue voids, bubbles and overflow that can cover the light sensing circuit.

The invention replaces the plastic cap and glass lenses with drops of viscous, curable optical resin dispensed over the light-emitting diode and the light sensor chip to form rounded lenses. The resin may be transparent or tinted for color filtering and entrains light more completely than the prior art. The chips, diode and lenses are then fully encapsulated in opaque molding compound, which blocks all cross-talk between source and sensor and eliminates the need for the cap, the central barrier and associated glue. The assembly is polished to expose the lenses, covered by a baffle, metal cap or etched silicon carbide layer, and diced into individual packages, allowing array-level mass assembly. Advantages cited include lower cost, greater ruggedness and reliability, simplified manufacturing and higher yields.

Alternative embodiments include an added glass lens over the resin with an air gap for independent lens shaping and filtering, a central black-glue stopper protecting the die surface, a package with the LED on its own conductive lead alongside data and reference light sensors for calibration, and a flat laminated-substrate package with optical overmold covering wire bonds.

Further embodiments describe a sensor stick in a memory-stick form factor containing environmental sensors (methane, CO, CO₂, IR, UV, humidity, temperature, pressure), ambient light, proximity and ranging sensors, a mini-projector, motion sensors (magnetometer, gyroscope, accelerometer) and wireless chips (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, NFC, IR), connected via wired contacts and wirelessly while powered by the host device, along with its manufacturing sequence.

The speaker says the team became more relaxed as the playoffs progressed, aided by experience from prior playoff runs, overtime games, comebacks, and a mostly familiar core. Although not oversized, the team is strong, reasonably physical, and expects to both give and absorb hits. The opponent has highly skilled, quick forwards, but the speaker sees no clear speed advantage and considers his own team a good skating club. Reaching the Finals was exciting but less fulfilling than winning there; beating Colorado was a major triumph, while a previous Finals loss to New Jersey provided valuable lessons.

The article explains and implements in Python a trading strategy combining the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Simple Moving Average (SMA). RSI conditions above 70 indicate overbought markets, while conditions below 30 indicate oversold markets. The strategy buys when the 14-day RSI is below 30 and the closing price is above the 5-day SMA, and sells when RSI exceeds 70 and the closing price is below the SMA.

Using yfinance, the article downloads daily Walmart data from January 3, 2020, to January 10, 2022, then calculates average gains and losses, RSI, and a rolling five-day SMA based on closing prices. It demonstrates how to generate Boolean buy and sell signals, manage long positions, record trades and daily returns, and plot the strategy’s equity curve. The same code can be applied to SPY and QQQ for additional backtesting. Proposed performance metrics include annual return, average gain per trade, win ratio, time invested, maximum drawdown, and risk-adjusted return.

Sebastian Vettel won the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix, resisting a late charge from Mercedes’s Valtteri Bottas to finish 0.699 seconds ahead. Starting from pole in his 200th Grand Prix, Vettel adopted a one-stop strategy and conserved his worn soft tyres as Bottas closed rapidly with fresher rubber. Ferrari’s attempt to stop Kimi Raikkonen ended in retirement when Bottas left his pit box before the stop was completed. Daniel Ricciardo retired with an electrical failure, while Max Verstappen punctured his car in an opening-lap collision with Lewis Hamilton and retired on lap five. Hamilton finished third despite radio issues and tyre disadvantage. Pierre Gasly took fourth, Kevin Magnussen fifth, and Fernando Alonso and Stoffel Vandoorne scored for McLaren. Marcus Ericsson scored Sauber’s first points since 2018’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix, and Esteban Ocon gave Force India its first point of the season.

The Stochastic Indicator Strategy is a momentum-based technical analysis tool that compares an asset’s closing price with its price range over a specified period, typically 14 periods. It generates two lines: %K, showing the closing price’s position within the highest-high/lowest-low range, and %D, a moving average of %K, typically over three periods. %K values near 0 indicate oversold conditions, while values near 100 indicate overbought conditions. Common thresholds are 20 and 80.

Traders interpret %K/%D crossovers as potential momentum signals: %K above %D suggests bullish momentum, while %K below %D suggests bearish momentum. Crossovers in overbought or oversold territory may be used for confirmation. Bullish divergence occurs when price makes a lower low and the indicator makes a higher low; bearish divergence occurs when price makes a higher high and the indicator makes a lower high. Divergence may signal weakening momentum or a possible reversal but should be combined with other analysis.

The strategy can be used for short-term mean reversion or %K/%D crossovers and adapted to intraday, swing, or longer-term analysis. Common intraday timeframes include 5-, 15-, and 30-minute charts, while hourly, daily, or weekly charts may suit swing trading. It can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, cryptocurrencies, and other markets.

In an Amibroker backtest using SPY as an S&P 500 proxy from 1993 onward, the overbought/oversold rules produced 556 trades, an average return of 0.57% per trade, a 2.2 profit factor, and a 19.8% maximum drawdown. Short lookback periods performed best with similarly low smoothing periods and thresholds. Tested crossover strategies, including optimized versions, did not approach the overbought/oversold results.

Sensitivity can be adjusted by changing moving-average lengths, lookback periods, or overbought/oversold thresholds. Combining the indicator with tools such as moving averages, RSI, MACD, support and resistance levels, or chart patterns can confirm signals, filter noise, and provide a broader view of momentum and trends.

The strategy may produce false signals in low-volatility or ranging markets, lag in strong trends, generate conflicting signals during extreme volatility, and react with whipsaws after sudden price movements. Overbought or oversold readings alone are not reliable trade entries, particularly because strong trends can persist at those levels. Traders should account for broader market context, use appropriate settings, and avoid over-optimization.

Recommended risk management includes setting maximum trade-risk limits and stop-loss orders, diversifying across trades or assets, sizing positions according to account size and risk-reward considerations, and continuously monitoring and adjusting exposure, stops, and positions as market conditions change.

KeyBanc downgraded Fortinet from Overweight to Sector Weight with no price target, citing a full valuation after strong share gains. While praising its network security position and cloud opportunity, the analyst said fading operating-margin targets and possible increased spending could disappoint investors. Shares fell 2.5% Monday.

The page lists and previews trading articles on commodities, gold, crude oil, agricultural products, metals, technical indicators, and currency strategies. It describes approaches including trend following, mean reversion, spread trading, fundamental analysis, arbitrage, and options, noting that traders often combine and adapt them to market conditions. Featured posts provide strategy rules, settings, futures examples, Python code, performance data, and backtests for gold, copper, crude oil, coffee, cotton, sugar, corn, cocoa, lumber, and other markets. Additional topics include the True Strength Index, Relative Vigor Index, Polarized Fractal Efficiency, CHFJPY trading, and portfolio diversification. The site is managed by independent traders Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette and their team.

Indices traded higher Thursday: Nifty rose 26 points to 10,641 and Sensex 88 points to 34,994. Banking, telecom, oil and gas, and metal stocks advanced; 38 stocks reached 52-week lows. Reliance Industries was Independent Media Trust’s sole beneficiary.

Thousands of schools nationwide closed Monday because of snow. Continued icy weather left numerous schools in and around Warwick District and Rugby Borough closed Tuesday; the listed closures may be updated if more schools announce closures.

Saudi Aramco cut May official selling prices for lighter crude grades shipped to Asia, marking a second consecutive monthly reduction despite its role in OPEC-led output cuts. Arab Light fell 30 cents per barrel to a $0.45 discount to Oman-Dubai, Arab Extra Light dropped 35 cents, and Super Light fell 20 cents; medium and heavy grades were unchanged. The reductions appeared aimed at competing with light crude from the U.S., West Africa and other producers outside OPEC and its allies amid plentiful Asian supply. Middle Eastern exporters’ share of Asian crude imports fell to 61.5% in March from 65.9% in January, while Western exporters’ share rose to 19.7% from 17.9%. Continued reductions in heavy-grade shipments could create a lighter-crude surplus, heavier-grade deficit and potentially push Brent-Dubai swaps into a discount.

Welles told the Finnish minister that the United States could not maintain normal relations with any country actively assisting the Axis. He said Finnish operations against the Soviet Union would constitute active assistance to Germany and warned that major offensives would create a regrettable situation. The minister sought clarity on Finland’s military limits and information about Stalin-Eden conversations, which Welles declined to provide. The United States proposed that Swedish officials urge Finland to halt further Soviet offensives and seek a peaceful settlement or cease-fire. A subsequent telegram reported a German-Finnish trade agreement under which Germany pledged continued economic support, while Finland would supply Germany with forestry and industrial products; a separate agreement covered Finnish-Norwegian goods exchanges.

Jane Goodall says conservation is urgently needed, with climate change posing the greatest long-term threat alongside poaching and deforestation. Despite cautious optimism, she urges immediate action, ahead of the documentary *Jane*.

A retrospective TriNetX cohort study evaluated whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve cardiovascular outcomes in adults with cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). The study included patients treated with potentially cardiotoxic antineoplastic therapies between 2012 and 2023, excluded those with prior acute coronary syndromes, CABG, or PCI, and compared patients receiving GLP-1 RAs with those who did not while both groups received guideline-directed medical therapy. Propensity-score matching produced 1,223 patients per cohort.

Over one-year follow-up, the composite of heart failure exacerbation, death, and hospital or emergency department admission occurred in 55.7% of the GLP-1 RA group versus 68.9% of the untreated group (OR 0.566; HR 0.701; both p<0.001). GLP-1 RA use was also associated with lower mortality, heart failure, and all-cause hospital admission. Atrial fibrillation/flutter and ventricular tachycardia showed nonsignificant downward trends, while gastroenteritis incidence did not differ significantly.

The authors identified anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanisms as possible sources of cardioprotection and considered GLP-1 RAs a promising therapy for CTRCD. However, the observational design cannot establish causality, and residual confounding, reliance on electronic records, unavailable adherence and combination-regimen data, limited demographic representation, and short follow-up restrict interpretation. Randomized controlled trials are needed to validate the findings.

A Tennessee mother's Facebook video of her tearful son Keaton recounting middle school bullying — being called ugly, mocked for his nose, told he has no friends, with milk poured on him and ham stuffed down his clothes — drew more than 18 million views by Sunday and prompted support from athletes and entertainers. A crowdsourcing page for Keaton's education raised over $29,000. In the video, Keaton asked why students bully, saying people who are different shouldn't be criticized and that one shouldn't let mockery bother them. His mother, Kimberly Jones, said only a select few know what it feels like to not belong anywhere. Tennessee Titans tight end Delanie Walker invited the family to a game, University of Tennessee receiver Tyler Byrd and teammates plan to visit him at school, country singer Kelsea Ballerini said she wants to see the bullies apologize, Dale Earnhardt Jr. offered friendship, and Snoop Dogg said Keaton has a friend for life.
Kirigami-inspired, perforated Mylar parachutes unfold while falling, lowering water bottles for aid drops or package delivery.

Analysis of the JAVELIN Merkel 200 Phase II trial found that, in patients with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, tumor reduction and non-progression during avelumab treatment correlated with improved health-related quality of life measured by generic and skin cancer-specific instruments.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon and placed Fastow on leave after an SEC inquiry into partnerships he managed, citing the need to restore investor confidence. McMahon, formerly Enron’s treasurer and later head of industrial markets, had reportedly raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest. The LJM partnerships were dissolved after Enron recorded a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to ending related transactions. Enron denied wrongdoing and said its operations were normal.

Enron’s shares fell 17% to $16.41, nearly 50% below their October 16 level, while other energy traders also declined. Analysts welcomed the leadership change but questioned whether it resolved concerns about unclear disclosures, related-party financing, liquidity, credit ratings, possible asset sales or share issuance, and additional losses. Moody’s placed Enron’s long-term debt on watch for a possible downgrade. Shareholder lawsuits alleged inflated asset values, concealed partnership obligations, and insider trading.

The compilation also included commentary sharply criticizing Enron’s governance and transparency, along with brief reports on small-cap stocks, corporate-director ratings, utility shares, and mixed European and U.S. markets.

A Washington Capitals coach reflects on reaching the Stanley Cup Finals against the defending champion Detroit Red Wings, saying the experience has not felt as draining as expected and that winning has energized the team. He describes Detroit as patient, difficult to fluster, and stronger after its previous playoff series against Anaheim. Washington has a different team and system with four distinct lines, while its experienced players are not intimidated by Detroit’s reputation, though they respect the Red Wings.

The coach praises Detroit coach Scotty Bowman for adapting his teams to different players and eras, noting Bowman’s record of seven championships. He values the leadership, character, and experience of Brian Bellows and Tikkanen, who have helped players relax and believe in themselves during tense games. He credits strong organizational support, his family’s enthusiasm, and a locker-room culture built on open communication, humor, and team play.

Players have dedicated games to parents, children, pregnant wives, and other supporters, strengthening the team’s sense of unity. The coach says Washington will make flexible line and individual matchup adjustments as needed. He expects a close contest featuring two of the league’s leading goaltenders, Olaf Kolzig and Chris Osgood, and says neither has won a championship alone.

CeeDee Lamb is progressing in his rehabilitation from a high left ankle sprain, doing resistance-band work at practice for a second consecutive day. After missing two games, the Cowboys star is unlikely to play in Week 6, but Todd Archer believes he could return in Week 7 against Washington.

The disclosure describes a respiratory assistance system that delivers heated, humidified respiratory gases through a humidification chamber, inspiratory conduit, and patient interface. It aims to provide gas conditions approaching those produced naturally during unassisted breathing—100% relative humidity at 37°C—and improve patient comfort and system performance across invasive ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, high-flow therapy, and positive airway pressure therapy.

A control system automatically or semi-automatically determines whether the gas source entrains ambient air or supplies dry gas from a wall source, tank, or bottle. Detection uses sensor measurements and system configuration, including mean and bias flow, breathing patterns, rebreathing, inlet temperature, humidity, and the presence or electrical characteristics of an expiratory heater wire or conduit. Rebreathing can be identified by comparing inlet and outlet flow profiles, detecting breath phases and double peaks, correlating signals, or comparing inspiratory and expiratory phase durations.

Based on the detected gas source and therapy, the controller adjusts chamber-heater temperature set points and power, and may also control conduit heating. Ambient-air systems generally use a lower set point because incoming air contains more humidity, while dry-gas systems may retain or increase the set point to add humidity. Temperature and flow sensors, optional humidity sensors, pressure data, ambient readings, and user inputs can also influence heating control. The system may estimate heat loss through unheated components and provide indicators of source type, set point, operating condition, and breathing rate.

The control system can validate user-selected configurations against measured system behavior, present automatic gas-source detections for acceptance or rejection, and issue audible or visual alerts when inputs conflict. It can also identify optional components and conduit types, select a default or safety mode before configuration is confirmed, and automatically determine operational settings.

A cross-sectional study in Nigeria recruited 128 HIV-positive and 120 HIV-negative adults, grouped by HIV status and occupational chemical exposure. Serum p53, bcl2, superoxide dismutase (SOD), 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine (8OHdG), malondialdehyde (MDA), and CD4 counts were measured. HIV-positive exposed participants had significantly lower p53 and bcl2 levels than HIV-negative unexposed participants and significantly higher MDA levels than HIV-negative exposed and unexposed groups; other group differences were nonsignificant. HIV-positive participants had lower CD4 counts regardless of occupational exposure, and CD4 counts correlated negatively with MDA. After adjustment for sex, age, BMI, and smoking, HIV status and SOD activity were associated with p53 and bcl2, while occupational exposure was not independently significant. The authors interpreted the findings as suggesting that combined HIV infection and chemical exposure may contribute to oxidative stress, impaired antioxidant defense, disrupted apoptosis, and increased cancer risk. The cross-sectional design prevented causal conclusions, and specific cancers and long-term outcomes were not assessed.

At a UN youth forum in New York, Solomon Dalung said President Muhammadu Buhari’s 2015 victory demonstrated that Nigerian elections could be won without money and represented a revolution against political “god-fatherism.” He credited the “Not Too Young to Run” advocacy with challenging entrenched political leaders and urged young Nigerians to understand and strategically engage the political system. Dalung accused “urban gorillas” of manipulating politics and said Nigeria was progressing in infrastructure, economy, and security. He also called for unity and engagement with neighboring countries to curb armed herdsmen. Nigerian Ambassador Samson Itegboje praised the government’s anti-corruption and security efforts and pledged continued international engagement.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 include a temperature sensor with ADC conversion and factory calibration, a low-frequency subsystem containing a real-time clock and asynchronous IWDT, selectable 1.4 V or 2.5 V internal references with external-reference support, and a comparator with programmable inputs, blanking, wakeup, timer fault handling, and an 8-bit reference DAC. Security features include flexible firewalls and CRC-16 with customizable polynomials. The CRC module supports CRC16-CCITT and bit reversal.

Communications peripherals include three UARTs with configurable framing, baud rates, LIN mode, DMA-capable FIFOs, and loopback; I²C controllers and targets supporting 7- and 10-bit addressing, clock stretching, SMBus 3.0, DMA, glitch filtering, and speeds up to 1 Mbps; and SPI controllers or peripherals supporting up to 16 Mbit/s, programmable frame sizes, DMA, and TI, Motorola, and National Micowire formats.

The independent watchdog timer monitors execution using its own power and 32 kHz clock source and generates a power-on reset after a programmed timeout. The windowed watchdog can reset or interrupt the device and can stop during sleep. The RTC_B provides calendar and clock counters, customizable alarms, periodic wakeups, binary or BCD formats, leap-year correction, crystal-offset and temperature-drift calibration, and clock output. General-purpose and advanced timers provide programmable counters, prescalers, QEI support, cross-triggering, PWM with dead-band insertion, and fault handling.

IOMUX controls digital pin functions, drivers, input paths, and shutdown wakeup. A two-wire SWD interface and DEBUGSS provide processor and device-state debugging, peripheral control, mailbox communication, and security options including lockout and password-authenticated debugging. Factory-constant memory stores device identification, capabilities, and trim information.

The recommended application schematic uses 10 µF and 0.1 µF ceramic decoupling capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000 pF pulldown, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O. The document also covers TI development tools, device nomenclature distinguishing experimental X devices from qualified MSP production devices, support resources, ESD precautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Researchers proposed deploying 10 million wind-powered pumps across 10% of the Arctic Ocean to spray seawater onto the ice, potentially adding one meter of ice and reducing the risk of complete summer ice loss. A paper in *Earth’s Future* estimated that extending the system across the entire Arctic would require 100 million pumps, about 10,000 kilograms of steel per device, and roughly $500 billion. The proposal aims to preserve sea ice, ecosystems, and Earth’s capacity to reflect solar radiation as the Arctic warms rapidly. The passage also reviews earlier geoengineering ideas involving reflective aerosols and artificial clouds. Researchers cited links between Arctic warming, disrupted jet-stream patterns, and extreme weather, while warning that current emissions-reduction policies may be insufficient. The project’s scale makes implementation in its present form highly uncertain.

Germany’s Federal Cartel Office is investigating online retailer Temu over suspicions that its policies and pricing tools constrain independent merchants, distort competition and encourage uniform or higher pricing. Led by Andreas Mundt, the probe will examine whether Temu’s control over third-party listings breaches competition law. Dublin-based operator Whaleco says Temu complies with EU law and is cooperating. Confirmed violations could bring penalties or required changes to merchant terms.
The Third Circuit found no error and affirmed the district court’s judgment.

This retrospective study examined the sequential replacement of SARS-CoV-2 lineages in Connecticut from January 2022 to January 2023 using genomic surveillance data covering approximately 5–10% of reported cases, linked laboratory and patient metadata, GISAID data, and covidestim modeling. BA.1 replaced Delta, BA.2 replaced BA.1 in March 2022, BA.4 and BA.5 co-circulated after May, and XBB-based lineages displaced late BA.5 sublineages. Estimated infections were approximately 1.5 million for BA.1, 2.1 million combined for BA.2, BA.4, and BA.5, and 0.4 million for XBB through January 2023.

BA.1 had the fastest rise, increasing from 5% to 50% of cases in 10 days, while later replacements took 20–59 days. Relative fitness advantages varied: BA.1 was 78.4% more transmissible than Delta, BA.2 76% more transmissible than BA.1, BA.4 and BA.5 27.9% and 48.5% more transmissible than BA.2, and XBB 28.5% more transmissible than late-stage BA.5. RT-qPCR cycle-threshold values, used as a proxy for intrinsic transmissibility, varied over time and only partly explained replacement patterns.

Vaccination-adjusted models found increased odds of BA.1 infection among vaccinated people more than five months from their last dose, supporting immune escape as a driver. BA.2 was not overrepresented among breakthrough infections, while trends for BA.5 and XBB were not statistically significant. A conceptual SIR model proposed that BA.2’s greater transmissibility helped it reach remaining Omicron-naive hosts; BA.4 and BA.5 combined lower transmissibility with escape from prior immunity; and XBB combined immune escape with higher transmissibility. Overall, lineage fitness reflected changing combinations of transmissibility and immune escape shaped by population antigen exposure. The authors noted limitations concerning generalizability to populations with different immunity, vaccination, and policy profiles and the interpretation of cycle-threshold values.

Tesla introduced lower-priced Model Y and Model 3 Standard versions at $39,990 and $36,990—about $5,000 below Premium models but short of replacing the canceled $7,500 EV tax credit. The Model Y Standard features smaller wheels, fewer colors, reduced luxury materials, no rear touchscreen, lower performance, and an estimated 321 miles of range versus 363 for the Premium. The Model 3 Standard retains its glass roof but also lacks a rear touchscreen and some luxury features. Both include supervised Full Self-Driving, which requires constant driver oversight and costs $8,000. Analyst Joseph questioned whether the roughly 10% price cut would significantly boost sales, while a vehicle closer to $30,000 might attract EV-skeptical buyers. As Tesla emphasizes autonomy and humanoid robotics, its global sales are down 6% from last year.

The passage reviews Subjective Survival Probabilities (SSP), or subjective life expectancy, and distinguishes them from self-rated health. SSP is associated with mortality, may reflect personal, family, socioeconomic, and life-situation factors, and predicts mortality independently of self-rated health. Evidence also suggests gender differences and links between SSP and lifetime socioeconomic position.

The study focuses on people aged 50 and over in Japan, distinguishing employment status within the labor market from the nature of the work performed. It reviews pension and employment reforms, including the gradual increase in pension eligibility from age 60 to 65 and measures encouraging companies to raise, clarify, or abolish mandatory retirement. It also describes common late-career reemployment arrangements and possible health implications. Employment categories discussed include unemployment, self-employment, domestic work, part-time work, and non-regular contract employment.

Working time and job satisfaction are also examined. Job satisfaction is related to health and is influenced by scheduling control, work-life balance, age discrimination, workplace support, earnings, and non-financial factors. In Japan, long working hours have been associated with poorer health particularly among workers reporting low job satisfaction. The review identifies gaps concerning distinctions between work and employment, inconsistent definitions of job satisfaction, and limited research on employment category, job satisfaction, and SSP in Japan.

Using four waves of Japanese Study of Retirement and Aging data from 2007–2013, the study asks whether SSP differs by employment status, varies with job satisfaction and working time, how job satisfaction and employment category relate to SSP, and whether demographic, socioeconomic, and health adjustments alter these relationships. The dataset includes 16,932 observations from 7,082 respondents across ten Japanese cities and repeated self-rated probabilities of surviving to specified ages.

Frank Schilbach introduces MIT’s 14.13 course on Psychology and Economics, also called Behavioral Economics. His research combines development economics and psychology, focusing on poverty, financial constraints, sleep deprivation, pain, substance abuse, depression, loneliness, and how such conditions affect decision-making, productivity, and labor-market behavior.

Behavioral economics studies how psychological and economic factors jointly influence behavior.
