It incorporates insights from fields including anthropology, sociology, medicine, and psychiatry to make economic models more realistic, predictive, and useful for policy. The course examines deviations from the standard economic model, whose assumptions include stable and well-defined preferences, rational utility maximization, narrow self-interest, self-control, constant discounting, risk aversion, preferences over final outcomes, perfect Bayesian information processing, and no desire for beliefs or information as such.

Schilbach describes numerous ways real behavior may violate these assumptions. People may have unstable or context-dependent preferences, discount future outcomes inconsistently, prefer changes to final outcomes, or limit their choices to avoid future temptation. They often update beliefs imperfectly, experience limited attention, care about others and peer influences, and derive utility from certain beliefs. Examples include ignoring information about climate change, overconfidence in multitasking, using reminders for medication, opting into charity, and refusing genetic information when its implications are severe. Default organ-donation rules can produce substantially different participation rates even when preferences and decision costs are otherwise similar.

A central principle is that behavioral economics seeks realistic yet simple, tractable, insightful, generalizable, falsifiable, empirically consistent, and predictive models. It does not replace standard economics: decision makers may be sophisticated, and markets, prices, and incentives remain important. Researchers should identify deviations that materially affect behavior rather than incorporate every possible bias. The course will approach topics through intuitive examples, empirical and experimental evidence, explicit modeling, and policy implications.

Laptops in class illustrate this framework. Standard economic considerations include note-taking benefits, accessibility, student autonomy, and distraction of others. Psychological considerations include temptation, limited self-control, the effort required to resist distractions, and mistaken beliefs about multitasking. Evidence cited indicates that unrestricted laptops and flat tablets reduced test scores in a randomized economics course. The course therefore uses an opt-in laptop section in the front of the room, where teaching assistants can discourage nonacademic use, while acknowledging possible limitations of existing studies.

Planned topics include time, risk, and reference-dependent preferences; social preferences; beliefs, information, and learning; emotions and projection bias; limited attention; mental accounting; malleable preferences; happiness and mental health; gender and racial discrimination; framing, defaults, nudges, and paternalism; and psychological approaches to poverty. Students are asked to read sections one and two of Matthew Rabin’s paper on psychology and economics.

GAO’s January 2024 report examined comprehensive support and improvement (CSI) schools, CSI plans, and Department of Education monitoring of state compliance with the Elementary and Secondary Education Act. Using 2019–20 data, GAO found about 5,200 CSI schools served 2.5 million students, or 5% of all public-school students. Compared with Title I and other public schools, CSI schools had higher concentrations of low-income and Black students, were more often urban, had much lower math and reading proficiency, and had slightly higher student-teacher ratios.

In a nationally generalizable sample of CSI plans available as of June 2022, 42% appeared to address all three selected required elements—school-level needs assessments, resource inequities, and interventions—while 30% addressed two and 28% addressed one or none. An estimated 73% appeared based on a needs assessment, 52% identified resource inequities, and 86% included at least one intervention; 58% included an intervention supported by a high-quality study reviewed by What Works Clearinghouse, while 18% included interventions shown to be ineffective. GAO did not independently determine whether plans complied with ESEA requirements or whether interventions met the statutory definition of evidence-based.

Interviews and discussion groups identified challenges assessing needs, identifying resource inequities, and selecting evidence-based interventions, particularly because school officials were generally unaware of What Works Clearinghouse. These interviews were not generalizable, but were consistent with a 2019 survey in which most states reported difficulty supporting resource-inequity reviews and intervention selection.

Education’s monitoring identified compliance problems in CSI planning and funding. GAO recommended that Education update monitoring protocols so staff independently select CSI plans for review rather than relying on states and districts. Education agreed and said implementation would begin in spring 2024.

The lecture examines entry as a departure from models with a fixed number of firms. A two-stage framework has potential entrants pay a sunk fixed cost and then compete through Bertrand, Cournot, search, or price competition. Solving by backward induction, competition determines equilibrium prices and variable profits, while entry costs determine the number of entrants. Lower fixed costs generally increase entry, and equilibrium profits may be small because markups must offset entry costs. Market expansion also tends to increase firm size; in the Cournot example, profits decline with the number of firms and firm size rises with the square root of market size.

For homogeneous goods, the efficient allocation would have one firm price at marginal cost, but the relevant second-best allocation maximizes welfare while retaining the market’s equilibrium competition. Entry is generally excessive, apart from a possible integer “rounding” exception illustrated by Bertrand competition. The reason is the business-stealing effect: an entrant’s private benefit includes sales taken from incumbent firms, while the social benefit is only the additional output’s gain, \( \Delta q(p-c) \). In the Cournot example, the entrant’s incentive is roughly \(N\) times its social benefit.

With heterogeneous goods, entry can be either excessive or insufficient. Entry is insufficient when increased consumer surplus from better product matching outweighs the losses incumbent firms suffer from business stealing. Most standard models still predict excessive entry. In a circular Hotelling example, equilibrium entry is \(N^*=\sqrt{mt/K}\), while the socially optimal number is half as large; although additional firms improve matching, all of the entrant’s demand is taken from existing firms. Underentry becomes more plausible when utility rises sharply near consumers’ ideal products and entry primarily serves new customers rather than stealing business.

In vertical differentiation, the Shaked-Sutton natural-oligopoly case has a finite number of firms because all consumers optimally buy the highest-quality product, preventing prices from falling to marginal cost as entry expands. In the specialization case, different consumers have different efficient qualities, allowing the number of products and firms to grow without bound as entry costs fall.

The lecture also reviews Jovanovic’s model of entry, exit, and growth under asymmetric information. Firms learn their unknown cost types through noisy operating results, with Bayesian learning determining output, growth, and exit. Young, uncertain firms produce little, may grow rapidly, and fail frequently; established low-cost firms become large and profitable. Concentration is correlated with both profit levels and profit dispersion because it reflects underlying cost heterogeneity rather than competition causing profits. US Census of Manufacturers data provide evidence of substantial entry, exit, growth, and shrinkage.

Finally, Vellodi extends this framework to rating intermediaries such as Amazon and Yelp. Because new firms receive few reviews, consumers cannot readily learn their quality, limiting entry and causing many firms to exit after bad reviews. The model’s consumer-optimal policy selectively withholds reviews once a firm reaches a quality threshold, making reputation gains flatter and encouraging firms to price below cost temporarily to attract customers and reveal their quality.

This study investigated sodium homeostasis in structural connectivity hubs in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Twenty-three patients undergoing presurgical SEEG and 21 matched controls completed 7T anatomical, diffusion-weighted, and sodium MRI. SEEG classified brain parcels as epileptogenic, propagation, or non-involved zones, while tractography and graph metrics identified hubs.

Patients had higher mean total sodium concentration (TSC) than controls (54.6 vs. 51.3 mM), with increases across both epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic regions and a positive correlation between TSC and epileptogenic-network extent. Sodium signal fraction was elevated specifically in the epileptogenic zone and reduced in other regions. Both groups had higher TSC in hubs than non-hubs, without a corresponding difference in signal fraction. Epilepsy-related sodium changes did not differ significantly by hub status, and hub–epileptogenic-zone overlap showed only nonsignificant trends in seizure recurrence.

The authors concluded that elevated TSC in hubs more likely reflects nonspecific microstructural or tissue-integrity differences than epilepsy-specific hub vulnerability, whereas sodium signal fraction may be more closely associated with regional homeostasis and susceptibility to abnormal rhythms.

Telltale Games confirmed it has an original new IP in development, though it may not arrive soon and has no announced genre or story. Communications head Job Stauffer also discussed the potential of VR and streaming services. Telltale is exploring platforms beyond consoles, mobile, and PC, including set-top boxes and possibly Netflix, with details planned for summer. A catastrophic injury that could keep a player out for up to six months forced the team to evaluate young players at different positions and learn its organizational depth. That knowledge helped identify roster needs before the trade deadline and enabled useful acquisitions. The team had started strongly from training camp, including wins in Los Angeles and Anaheim, but the injury changed its outlook.

DeBoer said the veteran group did not need inspirational speeches before the Stanley Cup Finals; he focused on energy, execution, and keeping the game on track. He described special teams as developing in waves and emphasized drawing penalties, attacking open space, and gaining rhythm through frequent opportunities. He praised Melker’s intelligence, competitiveness, honesty, two-way play, and offensive confidence, noting that injuries had given him a higher lineup position and more opportunities.

Leadership was handled inclusively, with non-captains such as Vlasic, Marleau, Burns, and Ward involved. DeBoer said the group set aside egos and internal drama to focus on hockey. He also described the team as resilient on the road, with veterans rarely complaining about travel or practice, and rejected claims that Eastern teams lacked character or leadership. The passage closed with praise for DeBoer’s professionalism, work ethic, relaxed demeanor, and ability to include players, along with a humorous account of watching *Downton Abbey* and films during long flights.

Periyar University published its 2017 UG and PG examination results. The passage combines three warnings amid unrest involving Japan and Korea. Japanese Consul Sugimura reports that the Tong Hâk have left Chulla Do and Kyung-sang Do and are approaching Seoul. He advises Japanese subjects to prepare immediately to remove women and children from Seoul, noting that the king may arrange their safe departure to Chemulpo.

Britain’s first carbon-neutral new-build church, the Roman Catholic Church of the Annunciation in Walsingham, opened in 2006 with rooftop solar, deep-bore heating, and reused stones. Sheffield’s planned PassivHaus church stalled over funding, though projects are under way in the US and Canada.

Via Browser is a lightweight, fast, customizable Android browser with full-featured capabilities, active bug fixes, and regular updates. Local bus clock gating may prevent edge-configured PIC inputs from reaching Idle, blocking clock restart and potentially hanging the system. Recovery requires the clock to be on or turn on while the source is low; otherwise, interrupts may be missed.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its fiscal 2019 Form 10-K for the year ended January 27, 2019. Its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “NVDA.” The company reported 606 million shares outstanding as of February 15, 2019, and a non-affiliate market value of approximately $146.66 billion as of July 27, 2018.

NVIDIA reports two segments—GPU and Tegra Processor—based on a unified architecture using GPUs and CUDA. Its four principal markets are gaming, professional visualization, datacenter, and automotive. Product brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, DGX, GRID, DRIVE, Clara, SHIELD, and Jetson. The company says its GPU and software platforms support gaming and virtual reality, professional design and visualization, AI and high-performance computing, cloud graphics, robotics, and autonomous vehicles. It has invested more than $17 billion in research and development since its inception and supports products from major server makers and cloud providers.

Business strategies include advancing GPU computing, extending NVIDIA’s AI platform, maintaining visual-computing leadership, advancing autonomous vehicles, and leveraging intellectual property. NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries, assembly and packaging subcontractors, contract manufacturers, and component suppliers. It maintains substantial inventory to support short lead times and manages demand through customer and partner forecasts.

The company faces intense competition based on factors including performance, product breadth, customer access, software support, standards, manufacturing capability, pricing, and system cost. Competitors include AMD, Intel, Xilinx, Qualcomm, Broadcom, Samsung, and others. NVIDIA protects its intellectual property through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements.

Principal risks include rapidly changing markets and customer requirements; competition; cybersecurity breaches and product defects; reliance on third-party manufacturers without long-term supply commitments; insufficient design wins; business disruptions and geopolitical or trade restrictions; inaccurate demand forecasts and inventory write-downs; international operations; difficulty retaining key personnel; unsuccessful acquisitions; intellectual-property disputes; operating-result volatility; privacy and data-protection compliance; tax liabilities; litigation and regulatory proceedings; and anti-takeover provisions that could delay a change in control. Revenue from sales outside the United States represented 87% of total revenue in fiscal years 2019, 2018, and 2017, while billings to China, including Hong Kong, represented 24% of fiscal 2019 revenue.

As of January 27, 2019, NVIDIA had 13,277 employees, including 9,486 in research and development. Its headquarters are in Santa Clara, California, where it owns and leases facilities; it also owns a research and development building in Hyderabad, India, and leases facilities in the United States and internationally. The company reported $7.42 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities at fiscal year-end, up 4% from the prior year.

Since its repurchase program began in 2004, NVIDIA had repurchased 260 million shares for $7.08 billion through January 27, 2019. In November 2018, the board added $7 billion of authorization and extended the program through December 2022, leaving $7.24 billion available. The company intended to return $3 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal 2020 and repurchased 5.2 million shares for approximately $746 million during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2019.

On April 16, 2020, China’s Anti-Monopoly Bureau approved NVIDIA’s proposed acquisition of Mellanox Technologies through NVIDIA International Holdings Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary. The deal had also received antitrust clearance from the European Commission and Mexico. The U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired May 23, 2019, and the transaction was expected to close on or about April 27, 2020, subject to customary closing conditions.

The Rancho Bernardo Kiwanis Club marked 50 years of community service at a dinner at StoneRidge Country Club. Organized in 1967 as the Kiwanis Club of Los Rancheros, it was founded largely by Franklin Lenfesty and 30 charter members; his $160,000 gift established its nonprofit foundation. The Executive reports that, at the beginning of the presidential term, federal authority was generally suspended in South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Florida. Federal forts, arsenals, dockyards, customhouses, revenue, weapons, and other property had been seized, while surviving federal positions were besieged or threatened. Secession ordinances had been adopted in all six states, and an organization calling itself the Confederate States sought foreign recognition and assistance.

Although the administration initially relied on peaceful measures, military assessments concluded that Fort Sumter could not be relieved before its provisions were exhausted. An order to reinforce Fort Pickens was delayed when troops were refused permission to land. After an expedition to provision Fort Sumter was announced, the fort was attacked and bombarded before the expedition arrived. The Executive characterized the assault as an deliberate initiation of armed conflict that forced the choice between the Union’s immediate dissolution and war.

The Government called out military forces, instituted a blockade, requested volunteers and larger regular forces, and authorized the qualified suspension of habeas corpus. The Executive defended the latter as necessary during rebellion and submitted its legality to Congress. State responses varied: the seceded states supplied no troops, while Virginia reversed its position after Fort Sumter’s fall, seized federal facilities, allied with the Confederacy, and transferred its government to Richmond. The Executive also opposed proposed “armed neutrality,” arguing that it would aid secession while restricting Union operations.

Concluding that secession was not lawful under the Constitution, the Executive argued that states could not unilaterally destroy the Union or escape associated debts. He described the struggle as a contest between free government and its suppression through rebellion, emphasized the loyalty of ordinary soldiers and sailors, and stated that the Government’s postwar purpose would remain preservation of the Constitution and the rights of loyal citizens rather than conquest or subjugation.

The Executive requested legal authorization for at least 400,000 men and $400 million to make the conflict short and decisive, while noting abundant domestic resources and foreign powers’ practical respect for U.S. sovereignty.

A retrospective, single-center CMR study evaluated 15 adults with excessive left ventricular trabeculation who met the Jacquier criterion. Using threshold-based labeling, the investigators separately measured the compact myocardium, central cavity, trabeculations, and intertrabecular recesses at end-diastole and end-systole. Results were compared across three approaches: adding trabeculations to the blood pool, excluding recesses from the cavity, and explicitly contouring trabeculations. Four-chamber images from 15 additional publicly available cases and theoretical volume models were also analyzed.

Intertrabecular recesses had higher ejection fraction than the central cavity (61% vs. 44%, P<0.001) and showed greater systolic area reduction. Contoured total LVEF correlated positively with global longitudinal shortening and mitral annular plane systolic excursion. Including trabeculations in the cavity increased end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes and reduced EF, whereas excluding recesses reduced measured volumes, stroke volume, and EF. Explicit contouring produced the highest EF, halved the number of patients classified with EF below 40%, and doubled the number above 50%. Theoretical calculations showed that measured EF depends on the amount and functional ejection fraction of trabecular tissue and on differences between systolic and diastolic tissue-volume measurements. Trabecular extent was not significantly correlated with total EF.

The authors concluded that the trabecular layer has a high EF and that contouring trabeculations may provide more accurate LV volume and EF assessments, potentially reducing inappropriate classification and treatment. Limitations included manual labeling, technical variation, a small single-center population, and the need for validation in larger prospective studies.

Lois Riess, 56, is in custody in Texas awaiting trial in either Florida or Minnesota. Authorities allege that after shooting her husband, David Riess, multiple times at their Minnesota home in March, she forged checks and took $11,000 from his account. They also allege that she befriended Pamela Hutchinson in Florida because they resembled each other, killed her and intended to assume her identity. Riess was arrested after being recognized at a South Padre Island restaurant.

Minnesota has charged her with felony theft, and authorities say a second-degree murder charge is pending. Florida prosecutors could seek the death penalty only if a grand jury indicts first-degree murder; conviction would not automatically result in execution because aggravating and mitigating factors must be considered. Riess’s history of theft and gambling, including taking guardianship funds from her disabled sister, was also detailed.

The paper examines how blockchain companies create and capture value through digital business models. It describes blockchain as a distributed, cryptographically secured ledger governed by consensus, with immutable transaction records, smart contracts, and either permissioned or permissionless networks. Although blockchain is often presented as disruptive, some scholarship views it as a foundational technology that improves existing socioeconomic systems. Using digital business model and value configuration theories, the study focuses on value creation logic and value-capturing mechanisms.

An exploratory multiple-case study examines five Chinese blockchain companies selected with recommendations from the People’s Bank of China and the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. The cases use permissioned consortium blockchains without tokens. Data came from 43 interviews with 31 informants, site visits, company archives, case narratives, and thematic analysis.

The analysis identifies five blockchain-inspired business models. ChainArchitect follows a platformer strategy by offering its proprietary Ledger1.0 architecture as an open foundation for third-party applications; compatibility with existing infrastructure and standards is its main challenge. ChainFinance is a disintermediator that uses blockchain-enabled RMB interbank transfers to replace conventional clearing processes and reduce costs, but faces institutional resistance and organizational inertia. ChainNova is a transformer that develops customized applications, such as rice traceability, for traditional industries and attempts to replicate successful practices elsewhere; industry-specific differences limit transferability. ChainSecurity is a mediator that applies blockchain to asset-backed securities to improve transaction verification, risk assessment, documentation, and issuance, but must obtain broad industry participation and address confidentiality and governance issues. ChainDraft is a co-innovator that develops organization-specific solutions on its proprietary Draftchain platform and captures value through licensing and co-development agreements; limited adoption, small-scale deployments, and development and maintenance costs constrain returns.

The findings provide a typology of five models spanning ecosystems, conventional value chains, and individual organizations, while identifying distinct mechanisms for value creation, capture, and associated implementation barriers. The study notes limitations in generalizability from analyzing only five Chinese companies and calls for research involving additional cases, including companies outside mainland China.

After the Trump administration fired most members of the National Council on the Humanities, four remained, all appointed by Trump. The 26-member council advises the NEH on grants, policy and funding and was scheduled to review the National Garden of American Heroes program.

President Biden said the United States had made substantial progress against COVID-19 despite the Delta variant: more than 175 million Americans were fully vaccinated, weekly deaths had fallen 70% from a pre-inauguration week, and job growth had accelerated. However, he said nearly 80 million eligible Americans remained unvaccinated, driving hospitalizations and deaths and placing strain on hospitals.

He announced a six-part pandemic plan:

1. **Increase vaccination:** Require large employers to ensure workers are vaccinated or test negative weekly; extend requirements to medical workers, federal employees, and contractors; provide paid time off for vaccination; and prepare booster distribution, subject to FDA and CDC decisions.
2. **Protect children and keep schools open:** Vaccinate eligible adolescents, vaccinate household members to protect younger children, support scientific review of vaccines for children under 12, require Head Start educators to be vaccinated, call on governors and school officials to use testing, masking, ventilation, distancing, and vaccination, and provide federal support for educators.
3. **Expand testing and enforce masking:** Increase rapid-test production through the Defense Production Act, sell at-home tests at cost through major retailers, expand free testing at pharmacies, purchase nearly 300 million tests for community sites, and double TSA fines for refusing to mask.
4. **Support economic recovery:** Expand low-interest disaster loans so small businesses can borrow up to $2 million.
5. **Improve COVID-19 care:** Deploy additional medical and military surge teams and increase shipments of monoclonal antibody treatments.
6. **Maintain equity and global assistance:** Prioritize equitable vaccine access and continue donating vaccines overseas, including 500 million Pfizer doses for lower-income countries.

He urged unvaccinated Americans and healthcare professionals to promote vaccination and called on the country to use available tools collectively to finish the pandemic response.

This cohort study evaluated two-dose BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 vaccine effectiveness against unvaccinated individuals across 12 four-week periods, extending follow-up to as long as 50 weeks after the second dose or 31 March 2022. Participants were eligible English primary care adults without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, grouped by age and clinical vulnerability.

Third-dose uptake reached at least 90% among those aged 65+, clinically vulnerable adults aged 18–64, and adults aged 40–64. In these groups, people remaining with two doses were disproportionately likely to have delayed vaccination because of recent infection, serious illness, or frailty, indicated by elevated non-COVID-19 mortality. Consequently, two-dose effectiveness estimates beyond 26 weeks were considered unlikely to be meaningful, and the effects of third-dose uptake and Omicron could not be separated.

Among adults aged 18–39, third-dose uptake reached 73%, without evidence of selection based on non-COVID-19 death. Protection against COVID-19 hospitalisation waned approximately log-linearly and was negligible by weeks 35–38. Protection against positive SARS-CoV-2 testing also waned, but differential testing behaviour and changes in testing policy may have confounded estimates. Waning in this age group did not appear affected by Omicron’s emergence. The authors concluded that long-term and Omicron-era effectiveness estimates require careful consideration of booster uptake, delayed vaccination, testing behaviour, and healthy-participant selection.

Halimat Oniru, founder of Haleem Group, is praised for creating tens of thousands of jobs across Lagos, Delta, Bayelsa, and Cross River. The Abuja-based company is described as a leading West African dredging firm and major player in Nigeria’s road construction sector. Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2021 reported net sales of $113.08 billion, up 27% from $88.91 billion in Q2 2020. Net income rose to $7.78 billion from $5.24 billion, operating income increased to $7.70 billion from $5.84 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $15.12 versus $10.30. For the first six months, net sales were $221.60 billion, up 35%, with net income of $15.89 billion and operating income of $16.57 billion.

Q2 2021 segment results were: North America sales of $67.55 billion and operating income of $3.15 billion; International sales of $30.72 billion and operating income of $362 million; and AWS sales of $14.81 billion and operating income of $4.19 billion. Sales grew 22%, 36%, and 37%, respectively.

At June 30, 2021, Amazon had $40.38 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $49.51 billion of marketable securities, $360.32 billion of total assets, and $50.28 billion of long-term debt. It also disclosed a €746 million Luxembourg data-protection fine, which it disputed, along with tax contingencies of approximately $2.8 billion and various antitrust and consumer-protection litigation.

The patent document is a continuation application related to prior ClimaCell applications and patents on real-time weather data pipelines and fast weather forecasting; identified patents, applications, and provisional applications are incorporated by reference. Copyright is attributed to ClimaCell, Inc. for 2018.

The disclosed technology collects and processes real-time, high-frequency, and historical weather data to determine current conditions and generate rapid forecasts. It applies to precipitation, atmospheric water vapor, liquid water content, fog inference, visibility, and runway visual range (RVR), with applications including signal processing and transportation planning. The background identifies limitations in existing fog detection and forecasting: direct observation has limited range, RF attenuation cannot always distinguish fog from rain or other atmospheric conditions, satellite microwave-link processing is computationally demanding, machine-learning fog models have not been integrated with real-time microwave attenuation data, and conventional systems struggle to process large volumes of rapidly collected vehicle and sensor readings.

The system uses asynchronous collection and preprocessing, parallel forecasting, and short cadence intervals that can support forecast cycles of about one minute. Preprocessing converts weather and non-weather observations, including vehicle sensor reports and terrestrial or satellite microwave-link attenuation, into precipitation, water-vapor, LWC, and fog estimates. Blending multiple data sources is stated to improve forecast accuracy by 30–70% and forecast speed by as much as 50%.

An illustrative architecture has four functional components: an information collection and normalization server; an offline and background processing server; a modeling and prediction server; and an information distribution and alerting server. These components respectively collect, clean, normalize, and store data; train models and prepare filters and transforms; execute cadence-based forecasting and data blending; and produce maps, reports, alerts, and user-interface or API outputs. A shared system database organizes radar, sensor, microwave-link, NWP, precipitation, RVR, fog, mapping, and forecast data.

The system processes repeating cadence cycles comprising collection, post-processing, forecast preprocessing, iterative forecast generation, and post-forecast processing. Each cadence instance acts as a control record and organizes collected, processed, generated, and forecast data into timestamped tile layers and tile stacks. Associations among data, cadence instances, processing stages, and tile layers can be added, replaced, shared, or pruned. Cadence timing, forecast limits, and processing stages are configurable for short- or long-term forecasts.

Forecast preprocessing and iterative forecast programs generate precipitation, wind, convective potential energy, fog, RVR, and related products, including forecast accumulation. A cadence manager compares collected data with prior forecasts to determine whether forecasts should be fully recalculated, partially updated, or propagated unchanged. Changed tiles are selectively recalculated and propagated through dependent forecast and product layers, avoiding unnecessary processing. Forecasts can also reference future observations and current sensor readings for targeted reprocessing, supporting rapid updates when observed conditions differ from predictions.

Two Oceans Restaurant has depleted its West Coast Rock Lobster stocks and will not sell the species until its population recovers. SASSI red-listed the lobster as unsustainable and reported that less than 2% remains, while SANParks supports the conservation initiative.

Linda Ronstadt, diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 2013 after losing her ability to sing, continues public appearances through “A Conversation With Linda,” featuring an audiovisual career retrospective based on her memoir and a question-and-answer session. She described daily difficulties with speaking, traveling, and brushing her teeth, while selectively maintaining work and exercising daily.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 support several watchdog and timer peripherals. The independent watchdog uses a 32 kHz LFOSC path, provides eight selectable periods from 2 ms to 2 hours, and generates a power-on reset if not serviced in time. The windowed watchdog provides eight selectable periods, can generate a reset or interrupt, can stop automatically during sleep, and can operate as an interval timer. General-purpose timers support 16- or 32-bit counting modes, prescaling, repeat-reload operation, QEI and Hall-sensor inputs on specified instances, synchronization and cross-triggering, and interrupt, DMA, and peripheral triggers. Advanced timers add repeat counters, complementary PWM outputs with programmable dead bands, fault handling with responses under 40 ns, safe-state fault outputs, and additional capture/compare channels.

The IOMUX selects peripheral functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wake-up logic. Available pin features vary by device and pin. DAC_OUT uses PA15, so external signals on that pin are not recommended when DAC_OUT is enabled.

An Arm-compatible two-wire SWD interface provides device debugging. The boot strap loader supports configuration and memory programming through UART or I²C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, and can be disabled. It is enabled by default for production programming and may be invoked through the BSL_invoke pin, an unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or a runtime SYSRST command.

A memory-mapped FACTORY region contains read-only capability descriptions, factory trim data, revision information, and device identifiers. DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008; identification and revision information also appear in package markings.

Recommended application connections include 10 µF and 0.1 µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 10 nF pulldown, a 100 kΩ precision resistor between ROSC and VSS when SYSOSC frequency correction is used, and a 0.47 µF VCORE capacitor. Open-drain I/O requires pullup resistors to output high.

TI identifies experimental X-prefixed devices and fully qualified MSP production devices and provides development resources including SysConfig, the MSP SDK and Resource Explorer, Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain, GUI Composer, MSP Academy, LaunchPad boards, and BoosterPack modules. The April 2025 revision updates numerous electrical, timing, memory, security, and peripheral specifications. Mechanical, package, orderable, lifecycle-status, and automotive-qualified version information is also provided.

The application describes blockchain-based digital certificate management methods, apparatuses, and systems. A certificate authority issues certificates and submits transaction requests to the blockchain, but cannot directly store or chain them. Before a certificate is recorded, blockchain nodes perform consensus verification using criteria such as validity period, serial-number requirements, or customized certificate information. Nodes broadcast their verification results, and consensus is determined through predetermined thresholds, participant counts, proportions, or time-based procedures.

The blockchain also consensus-verifies certificate revocation lists, revocation records, and revocation-list updates before storing them. Nodes distribute and maintain these lists in local ledgers, allowing transaction certificates to be checked against revoked certificates and transactions to be approved or rejected without remotely requesting verification from the certificate authority.

The disclosed apparatuses include receiving, determining, response, update, and transaction units, with corresponding processor-based implementations, storage media, and systems. The stated benefits include reducing certificate-verification costs, improving transaction efficiency, limiting the impact of a hacked or malicious certificate authority, and improving blockchain security.

A longitudinal study using data from the UK LOCOMOTION consortium further validated the 17-item COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale modified (C19-YRSm), a patient-reported measure for Long Covid. Of 1,314 patients completing the scale at least once, 263 completed it at baseline and approximately 30 days later. The instrument assesses symptom severity, functional disability, overall health, and additional symptoms.

The C19-YRSm demonstrated good convergent validity, with expected associations with the FACIT-Fatigue scale, and discriminated between groups by symptom burden, COVID-19 hospitalization, and intensive-care admission. Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were good; test-retest coefficients were 0.86 for symptom severity and 0.78 for functional disability. All three principal subscales were responsive to change over time, with effect sizes of 0.22–0.50, compared with 0.14–0.18 for EQ-5D measures. Initial minimally important differences were estimated as 2 points for symptom severity, 2 for functional disability, and 1 for overall health; clinically important differences were estimated at 4 points for symptom severity and functional disability. Confirmatory factor analysis supported separate symptom-severity and functional-disability factors, although not all fit thresholds were met.

Overall, the findings support C19-YRSm as a valid, reliable, responsive, and brief measure for monitoring Long Covid and assessing interventions in clinical and research settings, while further anchor-based validation of change thresholds was recommended.

Kyle Busch won the Overton’s 400 for Joe Gibbs Racing in the No. 18 Skittles America Mix Toyota, leading 59 laps. Starting 16th, he finished 12th in Stage 1 and 11th in Stage 2. After starting Stage 3 in 10th, Busch advanced to second by lap 193 and took the lead off pit road on lap 210. He held off Kyle Larson on the final lap to win by 1.162 seconds.

Busch struggled throughout with handling that was initially too tight and later too loose, prompting chassis, air-pressure and trackbar adjustments. Fast pit stops were key to his late-race gains. Aric Almirola won Stage 1, and Kevin Harvick won Stage 2.

The victory was Busch’s fifth of the season and 48th Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series win, tying Buck Baker for 14th on the all-time list. He also reached 190 career wins across NASCAR’s top three divisions. The next Cup Series race is the Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona International Speedway on July 7.

President Donald Trump said the Monday underground explosion near Manhattan’s Port Authority Bus Terminal underscored the need for congressional immigration reforms. Police identified the suspect as Akayed Ullah, a 27-year-old Bangladeshi-descent permanent resident who entered in 2011 on an F43 family visa and, according to DHS, benefited from family chain migration. Trump called for ending chain migration, increasing ICE officers and immigration enforcement authorities, and combating fraud and abuse. He also said convicted terrorists should face the strongest penalties, including death where appropriate.

The push-pull converter design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, and 6% magnetizing current. Although the calculated transformer primary inductance was 33 μH, 40 μH was used. Primary GaN FETs were rated at 170 V for a 36 V maximum input, while secondary synchronous rectifier FETs were rated at 80 V against approximately 20 V expected stress; a parallel Schottky diode is recommended to reduce soft-start current, dead-time conduction loss, and reverse-conduction loss. An RCD clamp limits switch-node overshoot and requires resistor and capacitor values to be optimized through testing.

The output inductor is 0.47 μH with a targeted 40% ripple current. Calculations require at least 1.3 mF of output capacitance; the design uses 2.3 mF total, provided by seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors, partly to mitigate radiation-induced single-event transients. An optional output filter places ceramic capacitance after the main output inductor and an additional inductor before the bulk capacitance; resistor damping may be needed for high-frequency peaking.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load. Primary current is sensed through a 1:100 current-sense transformer, and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor was selected. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation uses a 10-kHz crossover and selected values of 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF. Slope compensation uses a 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS.

The controller supply range is 4 V to 14 V and requires at least a 0.1-μF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably X5R or better ceramic capacitance placed close to the controller. Layout guidelines emphasize separating feedback and control signals from switching nodes and power magnetics, minimizing high-d/dt and high-dv/dt loops and switch-node copper, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing filtering and compensation components near their associated pins, and filtering the CS_ILIM signal when required.

The Department of Transport has warned that some commercial State companies believe government-set CEO salaries are too low to retain or attract candidates. The department also reported discontent among CEOs over prohibited performance-related bonuses; several threatened legal action, and the Dún Laoghaire Harbour Company CEO referred unpaid bonuses to the High Court. Policies introduced in 2011 lowered CEO pay and removed benefits such as car allowances from new and renewed contracts. The department oversees about 15 commercial State companies, while senior management pay at Bus Éireann is to fall 10%.

At the San Diego County Fair’s “Where the West is Fun” exhibit, Kumeyaay Nation members share their culture through songs in their native language at 12:30 p.m. each Wednesday, with craft projects planned for Kids’ Day. Displays include a map of where Kumeyaay people live today, member photos, and information about the yucca festival. The exhibit also explores myths about cowboy life and Hollywood portrayals, alongside daily shows and variety performances.

Edmonton police seized $3.2 million worth of carfentanil, the department’s largest such haul, after firefighters found suspicious powder in a southwest basement. Testing confirmed blue and pink powder was carfentanil; white powder was believed to be caffeine used as a cutting agent. Police estimated the 16 kilograms represented about 161,000 doses intended for the black market. No arrests have been made, the building has been condemned, and the investigation continues.

Ruth Negga, who grew up in Limerick, said she resented how teachers spoke to her and could not wait for school to end. She compared acting’s rigid schedule with the freedom of touring and credits luck for her success. Negga received her first Oscar nomination for playing Mildred Loving in *Loving*, about an interracial couple whose convictions were overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court.

VentureWire’s May 30, 2001 “People” newsletter reported numerous technology-sector executive appointments. Solsoft named Robert de Monts chairman and CEO; Real Media co-founder David Morgan planned to leave to start an audience-data software company; Gluon Networks appointed Jo Anne Heywood Miller president and CEO; and InfoImage named Thomas Niccoli president and first COO. QED Solutions, Corechange, and DigitalMoJo also made senior leadership changes.

Other appointments included Kevin Carrington at Partech; Donna Ronayne at BitFlash; Matt Camp at Pelago Networks; Veronica O’Shea at Octopus; Jim Charlton and Mike Wells at Riptech; Peter Slade at Axerra; Gavin Stener at Elagent; and Bonnie Crater at PurpleYogi. Operations leaders were appointed at OptiMight, World Wide Packets, and ChipData, while finance executives joined CryoCor, OutStart, Delphi Communication Systems, and Isovia. Product and technology roles were filled at Nerve Wireless, NetByTel, and CommerceFlow, and Converge named Sally Conkright vice president of human resources.

The newsletter also listed openings in analytics, marketing, sales, finance, product management, engineering, and venture capital, including Google’s director of UK advertising sales. A “Who’s Hiring” feature said Proteus, an Internet professional-services firm focused on wireless and interactive television, was seeking its first vice president of sales and marketing to build its sales team.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2016 describes a visual-computing platform company serving Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive markets through two reportable segments: GPU and Tegra Processor. Its brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, Tegra, DRIVE, and SHIELD. The company reported investing $12 billion in research and development since inception and holding approximately 7,300 patent assets. CUDA and virtualized GPU technologies support parallel processing in general-purpose, cloud, deep-learning, and scientific applications, while NVIDIA products are used in more than 10 million vehicles.

NVIDIA sells through OEMs, ODMs, system builders, distributors, retailers, and other channel partners. ASUSTeK represented 11% of fiscal 2016 revenue, consumer products generally generated stronger revenue in the second half of the fiscal year, and the company maintained substantial inventory to support short lead times. It used a fabless manufacturing model, relying on TSMC and Samsung for wafers and independent contractors for assembly, testing, and packaging, without long-term supply commitments. It had 9,227 employees at year-end, including 6,566 in research and development, and spent $1.33 billion on research and development in fiscal 2016. Cash and marketable securities rose 9% to approximately $5.04 billion.

The filing identified material risks involving intense competition, manufacturing yields and defects, cybersecurity, dependence on third-party suppliers, failure to secure design wins, natural disasters and geographically concentrated operations, customer concentration, demand forecasting, product margins, international operations, acquisitions, intellectual-property litigation, privacy, headquarters construction, convertible debt, and anti-takeover provisions. Revenue generated outside the United States and Other Americas represented 79% of fiscal 2016 revenue. Competition came from GPU and mobile-SoC suppliers, including AMD, Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, Samsung, and others. NVIDIA also depended on Intel licensing revenue, including a final $200 million payment received in January 2016 under a six-year, $1.5 billion agreement.

NVIDIA’s common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “NVDA.” The board increased the quarterly dividend twice during fiscal 2016, ultimately to $0.115 per share, or $0.46 annually, and the company paid $213 million in cash dividends. It had $1.47 billion of remaining repurchase authorization through December 2018 and intended to return approximately $1 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2017 through dividends and repurchases. Historical total-return comparisons showed $100 invested in NVIDIA stock on January 30, 2011 grew to $127.99 by January 31, 2016, compared with $167.81 for the S&P 500 and $139.35 for the S&P Semiconductors Index.

For fiscal 2016, NVIDIA reported revenue of $5.010 billion, operating income of $747 million, net income of $614 million, diluted earnings per share of $1.08, total assets of $7.370 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $4.469 billion. Fiscal 2016 was a 53-week year. The results included $131 million of restructuring and other charges tied to the wind-down of Icera modem operations, with an after-tax impact of $86 million.

Dwight D. Eisenhower accepts the Republican presidential nomination in 1956, praising Richard Nixon and arguing that the Republican Party is the “Party of the Future.” He urges Republicans, independents, and supportive Democrats to communicate the party’s record and platform, register voters, and ensure turnout, noting that registration has fallen below previous levels.

Eisenhower presents five reasons for the party’s future orientation: commitment to long-range principles rather than expediency; focus on present and future issues rather than Depression-era concerns; unity across groups; reliance on individual initiative and private organizations to address remaining social and economic injustices; and dedication to peace. His policy examples include soil conservation and farm income, free collective bargaining, balance between federal and state authority, urban development, education, housing, health, power, and peaceful uses of atomic energy.

His peace program has three requirements: maintaining American moral, economic, and military strength; collective security through cooperation among free nations; and, without weakening defenses, cautiously expanding contact with peoples under communist rule. He also supports disarmament and the international sharing of nuclear technology.

Concluding that this better era will come not through revolution or division but through coordinated action by free Americans, Eisenhower expresses confidence in the Republican Party’s future and accepts the nomination with “humbly but confidently.”
