The post closes with “What Is a Vet,” describing veterans as ordinary people marked by service, sacrifice, courage, and injuries whose effects may be hidden. It portrays veterans as troops, nurses, prisoners of war, drill instructors, medics, and survivors who gave years of their lives so others could retain their freedoms. It asks readers to thank veterans and notes that November 11 is Veterans Day. A quotation attributed to Father Dennis Edward O’Brien, USMC, states that soldiers protect freedoms of speech, the press, and demonstration.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 26, 2022, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2022. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” for Section 18 liability or incorporated by reference absent express reference. The filing identified common stock and two note series registered on NASDAQ and was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

The paper examines statistical independence (SI) in Bell’s theorem and argues that SI is best understood through a frequency interpretation: random sampling should yield samples representative of the population from which they are drawn. A theory that systematically violates this requirement is superdeterministic.

Contrary to the common view that superdeterminism requires determinism and atypical, fine-tuned initial conditions, the authors identify three forms: deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions; statistical flukes in deterministic or indeterministic theories; and nomic exclusion, in which certain combinations of hidden variables and measurement settings are physically impossible. The discussion examines Leibnizian Quantum Mechanics, coin-flip and Everett-style branching examples, “goblin” models, and several proposed literature models. These examples are presented as showing that fine-tuning, determinism, and statistical flukes are not individually necessary for violating SI.

The authors also argue that retrocausal and invariant-set theories need not be superdeterministic. For retrocausal theories, they distinguish causal-order from temporal-order interpretations and favor the former, under which SI may remain intact. Philosophical issues addressed include superdeterminism’s relation to free will, conspiracy, and scientific status. The introduction states the position that some compatibilist accounts of free will are restricted by superdeterminism, that superdeterministic theories involve a conspiratorial element, and that superdeterminism should be regarded as pre-scientific rather than as necessarily undermining the scientific method.

A Regina father urged police to raise awareness of drivers who splash pedestrians after his wife and infant son were drenched with slush. Regina and Saskatoon prohibit such splashing, but police say enforcement is difficult because victims often cannot identify the driver or vehicle.

The World Bank raised China’s 2025 GDP growth forecast to 4.8% from 4.5%, citing government stimulus, infrastructure investment, manufacturing support, improving consumer sentiment, and stronger exports. It expects growth to slow in 2026 as fiscal constraints and global trade headwinds weigh on demand. Property weakness, subdued private consumption, high local-government debt, demographic pressures, and declining productivity remain structural risks. The bank anticipates a gradual shift toward consumption, green industries, and digital innovation, while analysts say reforms in innovation, productivity, and services are needed to sustain growth.

Will Ma explains independent chip model (ICM) theory in tournament poker. Unlike cash games, chips have nonlinear monetary value in tournaments because players seek to survive and reach escalating payouts. Maximizing chip EV remains a reasonable approximation, but ICM can materially affect decisions in extreme situations. ICM estimates a stack’s prize equity by assuming each player’s chance of winning is proportional to their stack, then recursively calculating placement probabilities and payouts. In a three-player example with $5, $3, and $2 payouts and matching stacks, the shortest player has a 20% chance of winning, about a 29% chance of finishing second, and an equity of $2.89 rather than $2.

ICM is irrelevant in cash games, winner-takes-all tournaments, and heads-up play. It matters most at the payout bubble, on the final table, and in satellites or extreme survival situations. Large stacks generally have lower money EV than chip EV and can pressure smaller stacks, while small stacks have higher money EV than chip EV and benefit from avoiding elimination. Early in tournaments, accumulating chips remains the priority.

Ma demonstrates how ICM changes final-table play: players may shove more when acting first, call all-ins less, avoid large pots with covering or short stacks, and sometimes make “hero folds” with strong hands. In one hand, the chip-EV calling threshold is about 33%, but ICM raises it to 39.6%; plausible opponent ranges give Ma 34–37% equity, so he folds after bluffing. He also discusses stop-and-go plays, reverse implied odds, exploitative adjustments, and how chip movement among differently sized stacks affects ICM.

In satellites with equal stacks, Ma describes a “traffic light” or “traffic intersection” game: the first player to shove can make rational opponents fold even with strong hands because qualification and first-place prizes are equal. With unequal stacks, a short stack needs a strong hand and positive chip EV to shove. He notes that folding pocket aces can also be rational in an extreme normal-tournament bubble spot with one chip and a guaranteed payout.

Ma then provides a hand-by-hand final-table and heads-up tournament example, discussing ranges, pressure, bluffing, position, ICM pressure, and exploitative play. He acknowledges selection bias in the chosen tournament and briefly describes cooperative or collusive play aimed at busting a short stack, plus historical high-blind “angle shoot” setups. He concludes by previewing the remaining theory and cash-game lessons.

Researchers led by University of South Florida’s Dr. Davide Tanasi chemically analyzed residues in pottery fragments found in the 1990s at Castelluccio, Sicily, identifying oleic and linoleic acids as evidence of olive oil. Dating to the end of the 3rd and beginning of the 2nd century BC, it is the oldest olive oil recovered in Italy and indicates systematic olive-oil production at least 700 years earlier than previously believed. Other finds included a three-handled storage container, terracotta plate, and pottery septum.

“Mad Money” host Jim Cramer has turned cautious on Snap after initially comparing it to early Facebook and praising its 72% year-over-year revenue growth. He blames the unpopular app redesign, celebrity backlash, and possible declines in user engagement and advertising. Cramer says the stock remains too expensive and risky but would consider buying it at a lower price.

Running backs are vital offensive football players whose primary role is to run the ball efficiently, gain positive yards, and protect the football. They line up in the backfield behind the offensive line and may also pass block and catch passes. Elite running backs combine speed, agility, strength, vision, toughness, and ball security. They are typically well built, often 5'9"–6'2" and 190–235 pounds, though body types vary. Teams value different skill sets: short-yardage backs gain tough yards, while all-purpose backs contribute as receiving threats. Versatile running backs can turn negative plays into major gains and make offenses more productive. The passage also identifies Barry Sanders, Emmitt Smith, Walter Payton, Jim Brown, and Ladanian Tomlinson among notable running backs, citing their rushing, receiving, scoring, and championship achievements.

During puberty and early adolescence, children develop identities apart from their parents, give peers greater influence, and may feel insecure amid physical and emotional changes. Exclusion can cause loneliness, poor school performance, and depression. Parents should listen patiently, provide reassurance and support, and seek professional help when clear signs of depression appear.

Experts recommend selling unwanted gifts through different channels based on the item. Collectibles and valuables suit eBay or auction houses, while inexpensive household goods can be sold cheaply at garage sales. Kijiji is useful for bulky items because buyers can collect them and for high-demand electronics such as televisions, consoles, laptops, smartphones and speakers. Bunz supports no-money trades in clothing, perfume, makeup, furniture and decor.

Clear photos, good lighting, multiple angles, condition labels such as BNIB or EUC, holiday hashtags and engaging descriptions can improve visibility. Sellers should check eBay’s completed listings, consider condition and depreciation, and avoid unusually high or low prices. Kijiji searches peak around Jan. 8, particularly on Sundays, while furniture and decor sell well in August and September. Gift cards sell through Bunz, Kijiji and Craigslist, or can be exchanged for less than face value through card-buying services.

Regifting is acceptable only for brand-new, originally packaged items the recipient would love, provided they do not know the original giver. Handmade, personalized or thoughtfully selected gifts should not be regifted.

Chelsea manager Antonio Conte says he faces harsher media scrutiny after defeats than rival Premier League managers. Having won the league and reached the FA Cup final in his first English season, he has struggled this term, with Chelsea 18 points behind Manchester City and seeking a top-four finish. Despite exit rumours and links to Italy, he wants another season in England and intends to honor his remaining 18-month contract. Chelsea visit Watford on Monday after a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth.

David Luiz is holidaying in Dubai, where he went flyboarding above the ocean. After a difficult Chelsea season affected by knee and ankle injuries, he was dropped from Brazil’s World Cup squad, and his Stamford Bridge future remains unclear. Chelsea finished fifth but won the FA Cup.

The paper addresses ill-posed inverse problems that reconstruct PDE-governed physical fields on irregular geometries from sparse, noisy sensor observations. It introduces GeoFunFlow, a geometry-aware framework combining operator learning and generative modeling. Its geometric function autoencoder, GeoFAE, uses a Perceiver module to process unstructured meshes of varying sizes and continuously reconstruct solution fields. GeoFAE is coupled with a latent diffusion model using rectified flow, enabling conditional posterior sampling without explicit likelihood evaluation or MCMC. Given well-trained components, the framework has theoretical guarantees for accurate posterior approximations. Experiments on complex-geometry benchmarks, including Airfoil, Cylinder, and Ahmed body datasets, report state-of-the-art accuracy and efficient inference, outperforming representative baselines. The work highlights that existing neural operator and diffusion approaches largely focus on regular domains or forward tasks, leaving inverse problems on irregular geometries underexplored.

Researchers at Karolinska Institutet in Sweden, with colleagues in Finland, developed the CORE model, a tool that uses five factors—age, sex and levels of three common liver enzymes (AST, ALT and GGT)—from routine blood tests to predict the risk of severe liver disease within 10 years. Unlike the FIB-4 method, which is not suited to the general population, CORE proved highly accurate, correctly differentiating between those who did and did not develop severe liver disease in 88% of cases.

The study used data from more than 480,000 people in Stockholm who underwent health checks between 1985 and 1996; following them for up to 30 years, about 1.5% developed cirrhosis, liver cancer or required a liver transplant. The model was also tested in population groups in Finland and the UK, again showing high accuracy.

Researchers aim to make CORE usable in primary care, where most patients first seek help; a web-based calculator is already available for doctors and nurses. They note it still needs testing in high-risk groups such as people with type 2 diabetes or obesity, and integration into medical record systems. The work was funded by the Swedish Research Council, Region Stockholm (CIMED) and the Swedish Cancer Society, and Hannes Hagström disclosed pharma collaborations unrelated to the study.

NASA launched Voyagers 1 and 2 in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn. Voyager 2 subsequently flew by Uranus and Neptune, becoming the only human-made object to fly by all four giant planets. Both probes remain functional, carry Golden Records, and follow trajectories out of the solar system; Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012.

A new Chicago ordinance requires hotels to provide "panic buttons" to protect housekeeping staff and other workers alone in guest rooms from sexual harassment and other crimes. Buttons alert a supervisor, manager and HR, and provide the worker's name and location. A Unite Here Local 1 survey of 500 workers found 58 percent experienced guest sexual harassment—most often guests answering the door naked—and only one-third of those who experienced it reported it to a manager. Unite Here Local 1 president Karen Kent called it "a new day for women working in Chicago hotels." Some Las Vegas hotels have followed suit, though hospitality workers there continue negotiating for panic buttons with individual properties.

An Option Investor Newsletter forwarded by Enron’s ECT Legal summarized U.S. market activity for January 19, 1999. The Dow gained 14.67 points to 9,355.22, the Nasdaq gained 59.97 to 2,408.17, and the S&P 500 gained 8.74 to 1,252. Internet and technology stocks led the advance. AtHome agreed to acquire Excite/XCIT for $7 billion, Microsoft reported quarterly earnings of $0.73 per share versus a $0.59 estimate, and rumors of a major Compaq Internet acquisition were reported. The put/call ratio was 0.42, while market breadth remained mixed.

The newsletter said Microsoft’s results and other after-hours announcements lifted futures, although Alan Greenspan’s forthcoming testimony and President Clinton’s State of the Union address could affect trading. Clinton was expected to support allowing Social Security funds to be invested in retirement savings accounts, with estimates of $500–700 billion potentially entering markets if approved. Pinnacle Capital Advisors described option activity as quiet ahead of the speeches and a new expiration period, noting excessive bullish sentiment—60% bullish and 30% bearish—along with bearish short-term indicators and a recommendation to protect long positions tightly.

Market posture was bullish for the Nasdaq 100, hardware, and software but neutral for most broad indices and other sectors; oil and gas was rated bearish. Technology strength included gains in Microsoft, Qualcomm, Dell, Cisco, ATI, Sun Microsystems, Nokia, Micron, and Yahoo. Microsoft and Qualcomm exceeded earnings estimates, while Dell reported substantial workstation market-share growth. The newsletter expected continued strength but warned that weak broader-market internals, profit taking, and concentrated Dow gains created risk.

The newsletter dropped put plays on XCIT following its acquisition-related gap and on BMCS after it broke above a key benchmark. It provided updates on numerous existing call and put positions, emphasizing technical levels, earnings dates, stop-loss levels, merger speculation, and possible stock splits. Ford was added as a new call play ahead of earnings, while speculative call-spread plays were presented for Premiere Technologies, Omnipoint, Secure Computing, and R.H. Donnelley based on Internet IPO speculation, telecom takeover interest, expected earnings and split rumors, and Internet yellow-pages expansion.

The publication stated that its stock and option selections were educational information rather than recommendations, advised investors to consult qualified professionals, and noted that information came from sources believed reliable but was not guaranteed accurate or complete.

In his final address to the U.N. General Assembly as president, the speaker reflects on five decades of public service and historical progress, including the end of the Cold War and Vietnam War, the fall of apartheid, and U.S. action against terrorism and in Afghanistan. He emphasizes that these developments demonstrate optimism and the possibility of reconciliation despite global crises.

He urges sustained support for Ukraine until it reaches a just and durable peace based on the U.N. Charter, responsible management of competition with China, and continued cooperation on issues such as synthetic narcotics. Calling for a ceasefire, hostage releases, Israeli security, and a two-state solution, he also urges action against terrorism, Iran’s nuclear ambitions, and Sudan’s civil war and famine.

He highlights U.S. investments in food security, global health, climate action, COVID-19 vaccination, infrastructure, and clean energy, while calling for U.N. Security Council reform and a more effective, inclusive United Nations. He says international cooperation is essential to address hunger, disease, displacement, climate change, and democracy’s decline.

He also warns that artificial intelligence could transform society while creating risks from disinformation and bioweapons. Calling for global rules that ensure safety, trust, equitable benefits, and human dignity, he concludes that democracies must remain focused on serving their people and that stronger international cooperation is necessary to overcome seemingly impossible challenges. He says he is stepping aside after 50 years of public service so a new generation can lead.

A May 10, 2001 compilation of news reports describes California’s worsening electricity crisis. Rolling blackouts began earlier than expected amid extreme heat, power-plant maintenance, transmission constraints, and inadequate supply, with forecasts of at least 30 more blackout days and severe shortages. PG&E entered bankruptcy after accumulating roughly $14 billion in costs that deregulation prevented it from passing to customers. The Western power grid remains fragmented and overworked, with no immediate solution to transmission bottlenecks.

The Public Utilities Commission approved a $5 billion rate increase, with charges beginning in June. Under a proposal from commission President Loretta Lynch, about half of residential customers would see no increase if consumption remained within 130% of baseline usage, while heavy users could face increases of up to about 60% and commercial and industrial customers more than 50%. Consumer, business, and agricultural groups criticized the proposal.

Gov. Gray Davis asked power generators to accept 70 cents on each dollar owed by Southern California Edison, a 30% reduction, and sought their support for the state’s planned purchase of Edison’s transmission system. Generator representatives gave mixed reactions. The Legislature approved $13.4 billion in bonds to finance state-purchased electricity, but the sale was delayed until August after more than $6 billion had already been spent.

California’s budget surplus was projected to shrink by $3.4 billion because of weaker technology-sector revenue and rising energy costs, raising the prospect of spending cuts. Congress debated emergency California assistance, price controls, conservation requirements, emissions waivers, and federal aid, while the Bush administration emphasized longer-term transmission and conservation measures.

Bernstorff reported that Wilson, through House, offered confidential peace mediation based on his Senate message and requested disclosure of German peace conditions. Bernstorff believed the Entente note was a bluff and advised delaying unrestricted U-boat warfare, arguing that conferences could produce a better peace and that Wilson would find war against Germany difficult if his proposal was accepted. He asked for immediate wireless confirmation whether the planned February 1 dispatch would proceed.

Sharp reported that 80–90 French Socialist deputies approved Wilson’s address, supporting peace based on the free will of peoples rather than force. They urged the French government and all belligerents to support the proposed peace effort. The French press broadly endorsed Wilson’s principles, although many writers maintained that peace should follow an Allied victory.

Amanda Nunes retained her UFC title by defeating Ronda Rousey at UFC 207, then criticized Rousey’s coach, Edmond Tarverdyan, for promoting boxing over her successful judo. Rousey suffered her second consecutive loss, again exposing the striking weakness Holly Holm had revealed a year earlier. Nunes had said she would grant Rousey a rematch if she won. Rousey announced she would reflect on her career amid calls to continue fighting and suggestions that she change fight camps.

Healthcare fraud and overutilization place substantial burdens on Medicare, yet detection relies largely on manual audits and known-fraud datasets that emphasize blatant conduct and rarely capture subtle overuse. This study developed a physician- and medical-biller-labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists—200 labeled as overutilizers and 463 as non-fraudulent—to predict Medicare overutilization using detailed billing patterns.

Using CMS Medicare Provider Utilization and Payment Data from 2013–2021, the researchers created a 1,028-feature representation of each provider based on 513 ophthalmology HCPCS codes, service and beneficiary counts, payments, and derived ratios. They compared KNN, logistic regression, SVM, XGBoost, multilayer perceptron, and stacked ensemble models using repeated nested cross-validation. Stacking performed best, with an AUROC of 0.907 and Brier score of 0.109; XGBoost had the next-highest AUROC at 0.898 but poorer calibration and predictive accuracy.

Applied to 2021 data for 17,013 Medicare ophthalmologists, the stacking model classified 1,457 as probable overutilizers, an estimated rate of 8.6%. These providers had higher average Medicare payment per patient than non-fraudulent providers. Comparing their combined payments with those expected at the non-fraudulent average produced an estimated ophthalmology loss of $437.1 million for 2021. Extrapolating from ophthalmology’s reported 0.89% share of the Medicare budget, the authors estimated Medicare-wide losses of approximately $49.1 billion annually, or 5.5% of the 2021 budget. Predicted rates varied by jurisdiction, from 14.01% in JE to 4.11% in J15, while JN had the highest estimated loss at $63.6 million.

SHAP analysis identified the payment-per-patient ratio as the strongest feature, with higher values associated with increased overutilization predictions. Excessive use of specific HCPCS codes was also influential, although the authors cautioned that high utilization alone does not establish fraud and must be interpreted alongside subspecialties, patient complexity, and patterns across codes.

The study is limited by its small, labor-intensive labeled dataset, reliance on model-based estimates requiring manual validation, and use of annual provider-level patterns rather than patient records to assess clinical necessity. Applying the approach to other specialties would require new specialty-specific labeled datasets and continued domain-expert involvement.

The case examines DeBeers’s response to rapidly growing laboratory-grown diamond sales. Chemically identical to mined diamonds and produced in days rather than millions of years, synthetics offered consumers lower prices, less environmental disruption and no risk of financing conflict. Their expanding market nevertheless posed a strategic dilemma for DeBeers: enter the synthetic-diamond market or assume consumers would continue preferring natural stones.

The global diamond industry generated an estimated $13 billion in annual rough-stone sales and $62 billion in jewelry sales. Seven countries accounted for most production, while India dominated processing and cutting. Southern African countries increasingly sought to retain more diamond-processing value domestically, and retailers and miners expanded forward and backward integration. The United States remained the largest market, accounting for 46% of demand, while India and China were the fastest-growing jewelry markets.

DeBeers had dominated rough-diamond distribution in the early 1990s, producing 45% of global supply and selling 80%. Its position weakened as Russian production entered the open market, Australia’s Argyle mine ended its contract, and Canadian supply expanded outside DeBeers’s control. The resulting stockpiles, falling share price and antitrust scrutiny—including a 2004 guilty plea and $10 million fine—combined with criticism of DeBeers’s role in the conflict-diamond trade to create major financial and reputational pressures.

In 1998, following advice from Bain and Company, DeBeers shifted from buying surplus diamonds to a demand-driven, brand-focused strategy. It ended open-market purchasing and stockpiling, reduced its sightholder network, introduced the “Supplier of Choice” program and Forevermark branding, renamed its selling organization the Diamond Trading Company, and expanded marketing beyond engagement rings. After privatization in 2001, the company also supported African beneficiation through joint ventures in Botswana and Namibia and settlements involving consumers and regulators.

Synthetic diamonds were chemically identical to natural stones but could be manufactured through high-pressure, high-temperature or chemical vapor deposition processes. By 2006, U.S. production had reached 400,000 carats, annual sales were nearly $50 million, and analysts projected sales above $2 billion by 2015. Synthetic diamonds generally cost 15%–40% less than mined stones, with especially large price differences for colored diamonds. Producers emphasized their environmental and political advantages, although the Kimberley Process had reduced conflict diamonds to about 1% of trade by 2006. Debate also continued over whether mined diamonds supported African communities, while synthetic products remained limited to one carat in the jewelry market.

The GIA began grading synthetic diamonds using the same four Cs applied to natural stones and required disclosure that they were laboratory-grown. Synthetic diamonds also had expanding industrial uses in semiconductors, heat management, optics, data storage and medical implants, accounting for 90% of the industrial diamond market.

DeBeers defended natural diamonds by providing gem laboratories with detection equipment, spending $17 million on identification research and conducting consumer campaigns emphasizing natural stones’ age, uniqueness and support for mining communities. It largely assumed synthetics would not displace natural diamonds and sought additional natural sources through new deposits and marketing agreements. Its central unresolved decision was whether to enter the synthetic market, distinguish synthetics more aggressively or continue relying on consumers’ preference for natural diamonds.

Tesla, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and solar energy and storage products through two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of March 31, 2019, total assets were $28.91 billion, total liabilities were $22.87 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $4.61 billion.

First-quarter revenue was $4.54 billion, including $3.72 billion from automotive and $325 million from energy generation and storage. Gross profit was $566 million, compared with $457 million a year earlier. Tesla reported a $522 million operating loss, a $668 million net loss and a $702 million net loss attributable to common stockholders, or $4.10 per diluted share. Net cash used in operating activities was $640 million, and cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash declined by $1.59 billion to $2.68 billion.

Pricing adjustments increased the reserve for vehicles previously sold subject to buyback options, reducing automotive revenue by $500.5 million and automotive cost of sales by $408.8 million, for a $91.7 million reduction in gross profit. Inventory rose to $3.84 billion, partly because Tesla delivered Model 3 vehicles outside North America for the first time and production and shipping lead times increased.

Tesla adopted ASC 842 on January 1, 2019 without recasting prior periods. The adoption recognized $1.29 billion of operating lease right-of-use assets and $1.24 billion of liabilities, derecognized $1.62 billion of build-to-suit assets and $1.74 billion of related liabilities, and reduced beginning accumulated deficit by $96.7 million after deferred taxes. New solar energy system sales and power purchase agreements are accounted for under ASC 606.

At March 31, 2019, total debt was $10.33 billion. Tesla repaid $920 million of 2019 convertible notes during the quarter, increased its asset-based revolving credit commitments by $500 million to $2.425 billion, entered a non-recourse facility of up to RMB 3.5 billion for Gigafactory Shanghai, and extended the 2019 term-loan maturity to June 2019. Tesla reported compliance with its financial covenants.

The accrued warranty reserve was $843.9 million. Tesla also disclosed that it would abandon development of acquired in-process research and development and impair the remaining $47 million in the quarter ending June 30, 2019.

Legal proceedings included challenges to the SolarCity acquisition, Model 3 production disclosures and the 2018 CEO Performance Award, plus nine stockholder actions concerning Elon Musk’s potential 2018 take-private proposal. The Model 3 production complaint was dismissed with prejudice and was appealed, while other matters remained pending. The filing cautioned that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties and actual results could differ materially.

BSEB declared BETET/BSITET 2011 results for the 2016 special exam, covering classes 1–5, 6–8, 9–10, and 11–12. Candidates can check Paper I and II results and download answer keys via biharboard.ac.in.

The statistical analysis plan covers demographic and baseline characteristics, concomitant medications, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety for a multicenter study with approximately five centers comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg, placebo, and GlucaGen.

Demographics and baseline characteristics will be summarized by treatment group for the safety analysis set and full analysis set (FAS), with a statement of equivalence if the sets are identical. Variables include age, age group (6–11 or 12–17 years), sex, childbearing potential, ethnicity, race, diabetes history, medical history, height, weight, and BMI. Diabetes duration will be calculated from the diabetes diagnosis date, with incomplete dates handled using available month and year information. Medical history terms will be coded using MedDRA version 22.0. BMI will be classified and summarized by BMI class, country, and US versus non-US status.

Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment will be coded using WHODrug Global, version March 2018, and summarized by WHO ATC level 2 and preferred name, with ATC level 4 listings. Prior medication is medication stopped before first IMP administration; concomitant medication includes medication started before or after first study-drug intake that continued or stopped at that time, as well as later medication. Medications with dates insufficient for classification will be treated as concomitant.

The primary efficacy population is the FAS, with supportive sensitivity analyses in the per-protocol set (PPS) without inferential intent. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp without rescue IV glucose, assessed within 45 minutes. Missing data will not be imputed, and there are no planned interim analyses.

Confirmatory testing will compare dasiglucagon with placebo using a hierarchical procedure at a two-sided 0.05 significance level, proceeding until the first failure to reject a null hypothesis. The order comprises time to recovery, recovery at 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes, and changes from baseline at those times. GlucaGen comparisons are supportive and outside the confirmatory hierarchy. The primary analysis will use Kaplan–Meier estimates and a log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site; center will not be included. Patients receiving rescue IV glucose or not recovering by 45 minutes will be censored at 45 minutes in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses will address alternative rescue-glucose censoring. Supportive analyses include a stratified Wilcoxon test, recovery histograms, and a discrete-time Cox proportional-hazards model when specified assumptions are met. Linear interpolation of recovery times and exact tied-time methods will be used supportively.

Secondary recovery rates will be assessed at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes using Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel tests stratified by age group and injection site, with 95% confidence intervals and a non-stratified Fisher test fallback for small or zero cell counts. Glucose changes from baseline will be analyzed by ANOVA using treatment, age group, and injection site, with adjusted means, confidence intervals, and treatment differences. Patients receiving rescue glucose before an assessment are treated as not recovered for recovery endpoints and use the rescue-time glucose value for change analyses.

Plasma dasiglucagon and GlucaGen will be measured from pre-dose through 300 minutes and analyzed by non-compartmental analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin version 6.4 by Synteract. Summary tables, concentration-time figures, and PK metrics will be reported by treatment group, including original and logarithmic scales and individual profiles. Plasma glucose will be measured at specified intervals through 45 minutes, and at 60 minutes for patients weighing at least 21 kg. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is baseline-adjusted glucose area under the effect curve from 0 to 30 minutes, calculated with SAS.

Safety analyses will use the safety set and cover insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial-medication administration, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity. Treatment-emergent adverse events will be coded with MedDRA version 21.0 or higher and summarized by treatment group, system organ class, preferred term, causality, severity, seriousness, special-interest categories, and injection-site reactions. Missing causality will be queried and classified as related if unresolved, while missing severity will remain missing. ADA incidence will be described without statistical testing, including treatment-induced ADA and treatment-boosted ADA.

The SAP also specifies output formatting, derivation rules, SAS quality-control and validation requirements, and planned tables, figures, and listings. Changes from the protocol include rewording the primary efficacy analysis and adding sensitivity/supportive analyses, and changing secondary terminology from “within” to “at” specified minutes.

North Carolina child care academies offer low-cost, accelerated routes into early childhood education, with programs in at least 11 counties lasting two to six weeks and requiring 20 to 64 class hours. They are locally customized and typically run by Smart Start partnerships, community colleges, or child care resource and referral organizations.

Two models are emerging. The classroom-ready model qualifies graduates to work in licensed child care facilities but not as lead teachers. The teaching credential model adds the EDU 119 curriculum; graduates earn transferable EDU 3119 credit, enabling them to qualify as lead teachers, work as elementary teaching assistants, and continue toward an associate degree.

The article reports that 60% of licensed child care providers were experiencing staffing shortages. More than a dozen community colleges are preparing or interested in offering academies. A $1.476 million state-funded pilot passed the North Carolina House but was omitted from the final budget. Separately, DCDEE is offering grants of up to $50,000 to as many as 10 UNC institutions to operate academies through July 31, 2026.

Local examples include Wayne and Johnston counties, where Camber Foundation funding covered training for 89 graduates; Stanly County, where 13 students completed a classroom-ready program; McDowell County, where six earned lead-teacher credentials; and Durham County, where a bilingual six-week program received 140 applications for 20 slots. Programs also connect students with employers, career resources, tuition assistance, and pathways to higher education and higher earnings.

Sheffield council contractor Amey plans to fell 31 lime trees along Rivelin Valley Road as part of a citywide tree-removal and road-resurfacing programme. The 1907 avenue contains 700 limes and is described as the UK’s second longest. Residents and campaigners oppose the felling, citing visual damage and possible root damage, and believe the trees are targeted to simplify resurfacing. An independent panel’s report on their future is awaited.

The passage argues that Ontario election candidates should prioritize gender equity and sexual violence. It cites Elisabeth Salm’s death following an assault at her Ottawa workplace, the Gagnon family killings, and approximately 19 women reportedly murdered since January as evidence of domestic violence. It criticizes the eventual premier’s focus on memes and dismissive remarks about women leaders. All major parties except the Progressive Conservatives answered Ontario Thrive’s survey. Safe workplaces, affordable child care, safe transit, a livable minimum wage, and education on consent and gender-based violence are identified as priorities for women’s safety and economic security.

Investing.com highlights seasonal market weakness, thin liquidity, institutional tax-loss selling, and rebalancing ahead of month-end. Analysts see potential for further yield declines, with TLT potentially clearing resistance and SPY continuing higher, while a weakening dollar supports commodities. Technical charts also indicate bullish divergence in TLT, rising gold prices, and widening growth–value performance. The site promotes its Stock Screener and includes risk disclosures for financial and cryptocurrency trading.

Former Infosys CFO V. Balakrishnan said Sebi should decide Infosys’ settlement plea on legal merits, not the whistleblower’s emotions. The whistleblower alleged governance lapses and a “backdoor” severance settlement connected to the Panaya deal and Rajiv Bansal’s severance payment. Infosys sought to resolve allegations that Bansal’s 2015 severance was approved without prior committee consent; it paid Rs5 crore of Rs17.38 crore and withheld Rs12 crore. Balakrishnan and former CFO T.V. Mohandas Pai opposed the settlement.

STAT’s Health Care Inc. newsletter seeks question ideas from current and former Medicaid directors and announces a week off. The government shutdown continues amid disagreement over extending enhanced ACA premium tax credits, which increase aid for eligible people and broaden eligibility to higher earners.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that, effective February 1, 2017, it amended its certificate of incorporation and bylaws solely to change its corporate name from Tesla Motors, Inc. to Tesla, Inc. The filing includes the certificate of amendment and amended and restated bylaws as exhibits.

The dollar has rebounded sharply as December rate-hike prospects grow and the U.S. economy strengthens. After falling over 10% through early September, the Bloomberg U.S. Dollar Index rallied nearly 4% in under a month, breaking above its 50-day moving average and its yearlong downtrend range, though it remains down over 7% for the year. The rally has also pressured crude oil below $50 after it approached $53 in late September.

Kerala’s budget allocates ₹970 crore for general education and ₹789 crore for higher education. It includes ₹614 crore to turn 138 schools into centres of excellence, ₹50 lakh–₹1 crore for infrastructure at schools with over 500 students, ₹33 crore through KITE for classroom digitisation, and ₹300 crore from KIIFB for computer labs in all primary and upper-primary schools. Older schools will receive special allocations. Higher education funding includes ₹248 crore for technical education, ₹28 crore for skills acquisition, and ₹13 crore for upgrading libraries, laboratories, and courses.

In SCET, an \(e^+e^-\) collision producing a virtual photon or \(Z\) and two back-to-back jets is organized into hard, collinear, and ultrasoft modes. The hard scale is set by \(q^2\); the jet scale is of order the measured hemisphere mass \(m\), with power-counting parameter \(m/q\); and the ultrasoft scale is \(m^2/q\). A separate \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\) scale distinguishes two regimes. In the “peak” region, where \(m^2/q\sim\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\), power corrections are not parametrically small and a nonperturbative soft function is required. In the “tail” region, where \(m^2/q\gg\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\), ultrasoft radiation is perturbative, with leading power corrections proportional to \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}/(m^2/q)\).

Hemisphere invariant masses are obtained by summing the final-state momenta in each of two hemispheres and squaring them. Requiring both \(m_A^2\) and \(m_B^2\ll q^2\) selects a dijet configuration; a trijet would retain a hemisphere mass of order \(q^2\). Matching the QCD current onto SCET produces two Wilson lines, and the collinear and ultrasoft degrees of freedom factorize. Momentum conservation fixes the collinear labels and allows the measurement to be represented by delta functions associated separately with the collinear and soft sectors.

After Fourier transformation and use of the multipole expansion, the cross section factorizes into a hard function, two jet functions, and a soft function. The hard function is the squared Wilson coefficient; the jet functions describe the two collinear jets; and the soft function encodes the ultrasoft hemisphere momenta, the \(m^2/q\) scale, and nonperturbative physics. Charge conjugation gives the same jet function for the quark and antiquark sectors.

Each factor has a preferred perturbative scale: \(q\) for the hard function, \(m\) for the jet functions, and \(m^2/q\) for the soft function. A common factorization scale can be introduced, after which renormalization-group evolution moves each function to its preferred scale and resums large logarithms involving \(m^2/q^2\). A soft-function operator product expansion can separate perturbative contributions, which have a power-law tail, from nonperturbative contributions concentrated near the \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\) scale and having an exponential tail.

Thrust is introduced as a one-variable dijet observable. Its conventional thrust \(t\) approaches one in the dijet limit, while \(\tau=1-t\) approaches zero. In the dijet region, \(\tau\) is related to the sum of the two hemisphere invariant masses, so requiring small \(\tau\) requires both masses to be small. Projecting the two-variable factorization onto this symmetric variable produces a factorization involving hard, jet, and soft functions of \(\tau\). The resulting thrust distribution has a nonperturbative peak near the soft scale and a perturbative tail; outside the dijet region, additional jet configurations must be considered.

The perturbative ingredients are obtained through one-loop calculations. The hard function is related by matching to the quark form factor. Jet functions arise from cut vacuum matrix elements and contain delta functions and plus distributions, while their anomalous dimensions contain delta-function and plus-function structures. The one-loop soft function contains delta functions and logarithmic plus distributions for each hemisphere momentum. The hard function has a multiplicative renormalization-group evolution, whereas the jet and soft sectors are linked by convolutions. The factorization derivation itself is based on the SCET Lagrangian and operator factorization rather than perturbative diagrams and is intended to hold to all orders in perturbation theory while making the power expansion explicit.

The passage describes the On-Site Analysis (OSA) systems for the MAGIC and LST-1 Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma. Both systems automatically process daily observations through a common sequence from calibrated pixel data (DL1) to reconstructed event parameters (DL2) and photon-candidate event lists with instrument response functions (DL3).

The pipelines use Python-based, crontab-launched workflows, with parallel batch processing through Torque for MAGIC and SLURM for LST-1. They incorporate supervision through status webpages, email notifications, automatic retries, limited error recovery, and vetoing of persistently failing jobs. MAGIC’s pipeline additionally produces detection significance, spectra, light curves, and sky maps, while LST-1 is adding similar final analysis steps.

After processing, files are merged, organized, and transferred to off-site data centres for user access and rapid analyses. The next-day pipelines provide high-quality results, normally before 14:00, complementing faster real-time analyses.

The authors conclude that complete next-day analysis is necessary for rapid transient-event responses and identifying hardware or software problems. They recommend tightly coordinating pipelines with observatory databases and simulation tools, retaining easy human intervention, and designing comprehensive error detection and recovery from the outset. The systems can serve as a prototype and test bed for future CTAO on-site pipelines.

Apple discontinued the nano, shuffle and classic iPods; their lack of Apple Music support sealed their decline. The name survives, but the iPod’s influence endures in the iPhone and Apple’s hardware, software and services ecosystem.

OpenAI introduced ChatGPT parental controls after a lawsuit concerning a California teenager’s death and allegations that the chatbot provided harmful advice and helped draft a suicide note. Linked parent and teen accounts enable restrictions on sensitive content, voice and image functions, quiet hours, chat storage, and risk alerts without exposing transcripts. OpenAI is also developing age prediction to automatically apply stricter safety settings to users under 18.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 16, 2020. The filing reported that its 2019 Letter to Shareholders, accompanying its annual report for the year ended December 31, 2019, was attached as Exhibit 99.1. The Form 8-K cover page, formatted in Inline XBRL, was included as Exhibit 101. The filing was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky.

Plymouth Studio School, a £4.2 million studio school near Plymouth Marjon University, is expected to close in September 2018 after an Ofsted inspection rated it “inadequate.” A final decision was due from the schools minister in July 2018. The school opened in 2015 and welcomed its first students at its purpose-built Derriford campus in November 2016. It planned for 300 pupils aged 14–19, combining academic qualifications with sports coaching and athlete development. Closure followed viability concerns and insufficient progress on Ofsted’s identified improvement areas. Plymouth City Council is finding alternative school places and supporting families, while the school, council and Careers South West are providing information, advice and career guidance. Staff options are also being discussed. The closure would make Plymouth Studio School the 19th studio school to close since the model’s inception.

The HHLL strategy is a price-action reversal system. In a downtrend, a lower low followed by a higher high signals a potential bullish reversal, with a buy entry on a pullback to the previous low. In an uptrend, a higher high followed by a lower low signals a potential bearish reversal, with a sell entry on a pullback to the previous high. The simplified backtest uses an outside day as a trade criterion. Backtesting is difficult because identifying tops and bottoms involves discretion, while the forward-looking ZigZag indicator is unsuitable. A Philip Morris backtest recorded 118 trades, 9.8% CAGR, a 1.26% average gain per trade, and a 2.2 profit factor.

Designs in Mind has permanently leased the former Chrissie’s in Cross Street, Oswestry, where it opened its Jolt shop after a successful pop-up trial. Jolt sells brightly coloured homeware and prints and runs screen-printing and lino-printing workshops. The Community Interest Company aims to reduce stigma around mental health by generating public interest in work by members referred through its mental health scheme.

An informal meeting discussed a draft tripartite agreement governing Congo commodity purchases and supplies. Belgium proposed earlier revision if Belgian territory were liberated, allowing Congo products to meet Belgian needs. Article 3 discussion favored excluding actual prices, preserving existing special agreements, and setting prices later through subsidiary arrangements. Article 4 addressed Belgium’s dollar shortage and U.S. purchases; a British representative cited the 1941 UK-Belgian agreement under which the Treasury would provide necessary foreign exchange. Belgians sought an express shipping assurance, noting that Belgian ships in the pooled fleet had not been made available. British participants advised pursuing the issue with the Ministry of War Transport, while contact with the Harriman Mission’s American shipping representative was suggested. Participants also proposed that the new agreement begin afresh, with unfinished transactions under the old agreement lapsing and being assimilated to the new one. The observations were informal. Draft Article 1 provides that, from September 1, 1942, through December 31, 1943, Belgium would make specified Congo export quantities available to U.K. and U.S. buyers and government agencies.

A new directive defined covert activities to include propaganda, economic warfare, sabotage, subversion, and support for resistance and anti-Communist groups, while excluding armed conflict by recognized military forces, espionage, counterespionage, and military deception. The CIA’s Office of Policy Coordination, established in 1948, organized covert actions and initially received policy guidance from State in peacetime and the military in wartime. Its rapid growth during the Korean War prompted closer policy control. Truman created the Psychological Strategy Board in 1951, while NSC 10/5 reaffirmed the CIA’s covert-action mandate and expanded its authority over guerrilla warfare.

Under Eisenhower, NSC directives required coordination and advance approval of major covert programs and created the Special Group as an executive body reviewing CIA initiatives. After the Bay of Pigs, the Taylor Report led to increased Special Group oversight. By 1963, informal criteria—including risk, likely success, exposure, political sensitivity, and cost—governed which projects required review.

Actor-turned-politician Shatrughan Sinha criticized the BJP after its Rajasthan bypoll losses, saying the results showed that the common man had begun to speak and opponents had won by record margins. Having recently joined Yashwant Sinha’s Rashtra Manch, Sinha said he had long differed with BJP leadership and felt treated like a stepson. Union Minister Babul Supriyo responded by telling Sinha to leave the BJP.

Fullbacks serve primarily as additional blockers in two-back formations, helping offenses create running lanes and seal linebackers at the second level. Though less athletic than running backs, they compensate with toughness, hard-nosed physical play, and blocking ability. They occasionally touch the ball on fullback dives or short passes but rarely contribute major statistics. Traditional, pro-style offenses rely on them more, while the spread offense has reduced their use. Fullbacks are generally thick-built, estimated at 5'11"–6'1" and 235–250 pounds. The position’s name reflects historical field depth and alignment. Mike Alstott and Larry Csonka are highlighted among the best fullbacks, both benefiting from eras when fullbacks received more carries.

Readers responded to an opinion piece on overcrowded Ontario hospital emergency departments, citing long waits, insufficient beds, exhausted staff, nonurgent use and broader health-system problems. They questioned whether reduced access to family doctors and community clinics contributes to ER overcrowding; one called ERs a “dumping ground,” while another described conditions as frightening. A reader also criticized Ottawa’s recycling collection for scattering waste and proposed clear plastic bags, as used in Smiths Falls. The Citizen invited nominations of local “Capital Builders” in letters of 200 words or fewer.

The coach remained confident that the team could split the two-game series despite a brief lapse in the opener. He said the opponent’s four lines demonstrated that the team must also get scoring from its third and fourth lines, avoid mistakes and large deficits, and continue giving full effort every night.

The author recounts a failed May 2012 Brooklyn strike that sought to halt work, school, shopping, and banking to press for economic justice. Although thousands participated elsewhere, local organizing was too weak to disrupt business as usual.

New strikes are being organized in response to the Trump administration. A February 17 strike calls for no work or spending and demands that Congress defend the U.S. Constitution. A March 8 international women’s strike, led by women of color, plans demonstrations, walkouts, sex strikes, boycotts, road blockades, and other locally adapted actions while including trans women and their supporters. A May 1 strike is also being considered.

The passage cites European precedents: unions and other groups held 63 general strikes from 2000 to 2016, and governments changed or withdrew the policies that prompted them 42 percent of the time. A mass boycott of work and school in Poland helped force the government to abandon a restrictive anti-abortion bill.

American organizers acknowledge that anti-striking laws, weak union density, and the history of harsh government reactions make a traditional general strike unrealistic. They therefore describe the March 8 action as an inclusive “mass strike,” supported by groups including the National Organization for Women, the Chicago Teachers Union, Black Lives Matter, and Palestinian rights organizations. The author concludes that the strikes may not succeed, but they could help Americans practice collective resistance and build political capacity.

The message announced that Texas had accepted congressional proposals establishing its northern and western boundaries, relinquishing claims to territory outside them and to the United States, and providing for a territorial government for New Mexico. An authenticated Texas law approving the agreement was received and transmitted to the President and Congress. The message praised widespread approval of the settlement in Texas and described it as overcoming dangers associated with the Mexican treaty. Territorial governments had been established in the remaining acquired territories, while further congressional action was considered necessary to govern them and complete the acquisition peacefully.

A message transmits the International American Conference report recommending reciprocal commercial treaties between the United States and other American republics. More than 87 percent of Latin American products already enter U.S. markets free; adding sugar would leave wool as the major exception and complicate reciprocity. Better steam and financial services and rebates on imported raw materials could enable U.S. merchants to compete. After congressional tariff action, trade could expand under treaty powers if mutually advantageous.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018 describes its strategy, operations, competitive environment, and principal risks. Microsoft develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions, including operating systems, productivity applications, business applications, cloud services, AI tools, Surface devices, Xbox gaming products, and online advertising. Its strategy centers on reinventing productivity and business processes, building an intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing through workplace applications, Azure, AI, Windows, devices, and gaming.

The company reports through three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, comprising Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics; Intelligent Cloud, comprising server products, Azure, and enterprise services; and More Personal Computing, comprising Windows, devices, gaming, and search. Microsoft distributes products through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, and digital channels, with licensing programs for cloud and on-premises software. It continued substantial investments in cloud, AI, devices, digital work, and entertainment. R&D expense was $14.7 billion in fiscal 2018, 13% of revenue, and the company employed approximately 131,000 people.

Embodiments include an optical substrate, light source, light coupler, light extractor, and debanding optic. The coupler launches light into total internal reflection (TIR), with each incidence angle defining a unique TIR angle, while the extractor produces output illumination. Banding arises when successive light extractions have gaps or overlaps, creating an illumination ripple. Debanding optics shift the pupil or otherwise vary diffraction efficiency, transmission, polarization, or birefringence to produce a substantially flat output profile, with spatial non-uniformity below 20% and preferably below 10%.

Disclosed debanding implementations include an effective input aperture based on the 2D tan(U) relationship; multiple, passive, multiplexed, switchable, or rolled-K-vector gratings; index and gradient-index layers; partially reflecting or polarization-modifying layers; crossed-slant gratings; variable-numerical-aperture microdisplays; tilted microdisplays; coupling prisms; and edge light-absorbing films. Switchable Bragg gratings may use voltage-controlled holographic polymer-dispersed liquid crystal layers to shift pupils.

A color waveguide uses stacked optical substrates with input stops containing outer dichroic portions for pupil shifting and color-band mitigation, plus inner phase-compensation coatings. A corresponding method couples source light into a substrate for TIR, extracts it through a light extractor, and applies a debanding optic to reduce output-illumination banding.

This excerpt from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification (Version 6.00) covers UHS-II operation, card states, data read/write and erase procedures, write protection and lock/unlock (including Card Ownership Protection), and switch function, clock and CRC behavior.

**UHS-II and card selection.** The broadcast command SET_DSR (CMD4) configures driver stages of all identified cards, programming their DSR registers for the application bus layout, number of cards on the bus and data transfer frequency, and switching the clock rate from fOD to fPP. CMD7 selects one card and places it in the Transfer State; only one card may be in that state at a time, and a previously selected card returns to Stand-by State. CMD7 with reserved RCA 0x0000 returns all cards to Stand-by; the host must reserve RCA=0 for de-selection. Cards already having an RCA do not respond to identification commands (ACMD41, CMD2). CMD48, CMD49, CMD58 and CMD59 are also available in UHS-II mode.

**Data transfer mode.** Communication is point-to-point between host and selected card using addressed commands. Read and write commands can be aborted with CMD12; write commands must be stopped before deselection with CMD7. On completion of transfer, the card leaves the write state for either the Programming State (success) or Transfer State (failure); if a block write is stopped with valid block length and CRC, the data is programmed. Block write may be buffered, with DAT0 held low (BUSY) while in Programming State; no buffering exists for write CSD, write protection and erase, and while busy no other data transfer commands are accepted. Parameter set commands (CMD16, CMD32, CMD33) and read commands are not allowed while programming. Selecting another card moves the card to Disconnect State and releases the DAT line; reselection returns it to Programming State and reactivates the busy indication. Reset (CMD0 or CMD15) terminates pending or active programming and may destroy data. CMD34-37, CMD50 and CMD57 are reserved for command system expansion.

**Bus width and card capacity.** ACMD6 selects/deselects 4-bit mode; the default after power up or CMD0 is 1-bit. A locked card responds to ACMD6 with an illegal command. For a 2GB card, READ_BL_LEN/WRITE_BL_LEN are 1024 bytes while CMD16 block length stays at up to 512 bytes.

**Data read.** The DAT line is held high by pull-up when idle; a block consists of 1 or 4 start bits (LOW), a continuous data stream with payload and optional off-card ECC bits, and 1 or 4 end bits (HIGH), transmitted synchronously to the clock and protected by CRC. Data is not destroyed by power-off except during host-issued write or erase. The basic transfer unit is a block of at most 512 bytes; CMD16 may set block length up to 512 bytes regardless of READ_BL_LEN, and each block ends with a CRC. CMD17 performs a single block read and returns the card to Transfer State; CMD18 transfers consecutive blocks until CMD12 (which has an execution delay), and the host should ignore OUT_OF_RANGE at the last block of the user area. Block misalignment is detected at the first misaligned block, setting ADDRESS_ERROR, aborting transmission and waiting in the Data State for CMD12.

**Data write.** CRC bits are appended per block and checked by the card before writing; CRC failure is signaled on DAT, the data is discarded and further blocks are also rejected. Writes are rejected with no data on BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR. Block length set by CMD16 must be 512 bytes for block writes regardless of WRITE_BL_LEN; with WRITE_BL_PARTIAL=1 smaller blocks down to one byte are allowed. Misalignment aborts programming before the first misaligned block, sets ADDRESS_ERROR and waits in Receive-data-State for a stop command; writing to a write-protected area sets WP_VIOLATION. CSD programming needs no prior block length, is CRC protected, and errors without register change if a ROM-stored part mismatches the received buffer. While the write buffer is full, DAT0 is held low; the host may poll status with CMD13, and READY_FOR_DATA indicates readiness. CMD7 deselection moves the card to Disconnect State without interrupting the write, and reselection restores the busy indication, allowing interleaved writes to several cards by disconnecting busy cards. ACMD23 pre-erase speeds a following multiple block write; early termination leaves remaining blocks undefined, excess blocks are erased as data arrives, the count resets to 1 afterwards, and it may be cleared by intervening commands. ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks for pipeline systems.

**Erase, Discard and FULE.** Erase uses CMD32, CMD33 and CMD38; out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET and reset the sequence, write-protected sectors are left intact with WP_ERASE_SKIP set, and erase progress is shown by DAT0 low. Post-erase data is '0' or '1' per SCR bit DATA_STAT_AFTER_ERASE (bit 55). DISCARD (CMD38 argument 00000001h) de-allocates blocks whose content becomes 'don't care', is supported on SDHC/SDXC only, not via SPI, uses a 250 ms busy timeout, and is forgotten on power cycle. FULE (CMD38 argument 00000002h) logically erases the entire user area, also SDHC/SDXC only, with a 1 second busy timeout; if the host does not specify the full user area the card executes ERASE instead.

**Write protection and lock/unlock.** Three methods exist: a mechanical write-protect switch (host responsibility), card-internal protection, and password protection. Password and size reside in 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP/FEP_LEN for Card Ownership Protection (COP); these registers are non-volatile. Locked cards accept class 0 commands, ACMD41, CMD16 and lock card commands but cannot access data. CMD42 is available in Transfer State only and uses a single block write structure, with password length up to 16 bytes and up to 32 bytes total for a password change; the block length must be at least the required data structure and is rounded up to an even size in DDR50 mode.

**COP.** COP prevents re-use of a COP card without the password; setting FEP disables Force Erase and Clear PWD, and COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) is required after power-up/reset when FEP is set. COP cards start in CMD42 Ver.1.0 compatible mode; with FEP=0 functions are compatible except argument 1Fh, while with FEP set the card is COP Locked, returns CARD_IS_LOCKED and LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED, and rejects all CMD42 functions except CMD42[1Fh]. That command moves the card to CMD42 Ver.2.0 mode, adding FEP management (Reset/Set/Replace FEP), two Force Erase variants (CMD42[08h] with no password, enabled when FEP=0; CMD42[18h] with password, enabled when FEP=set) and Reset PWD inhibit. Force Erase erases all card content including PWD and unlocks the card, is disabled when FEP is set, fails on an unlocked card, and leaves the secure area intact. Errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED (bit 24); CARD_IS_LOCKED (bit 25) reflects card state. ACMD6 is rejected while locked. Cards are classified as Type 1, Type 2 and Type 3 (COP).

**APP_CMD, CMD6, and other commands.** APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the next command an ACMD; undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands, and illegal ones raise an illegal command error. ACMD6, ACMD13, ACMD17-26, ACMD38-49 and ACMD51 are reserved for proprietary use; ACMD41 responses carry no APP_CMD status. CMD6 supports six function groups of 16 functions each (access mode/bus speed, command system, driver strength, power limit), with function 0 default, Mode 0 for checking and Mode 1 for setting; it returns R1 plus 512 bits of status with a 100 ms timeout, and functions revert to default on CMD0 or power cycle. The status block carries maximum current/power consumption, support bits, function selection and busy status per group, with data structure version 01h making busy status effective; busy functions cannot be switched. The Power Limit default is 0.72W, with total card power being the sum of VDD1 and VDD2; in UHS-II mode function groups 1 and 3 are unused, group 2 is optional and group 4 mandatory. High-Speed mode (25 MB/s, 50 MHz clock) is optional and set via CMD6; because timing modes cannot be mixed, the host shall drive only one card with 1-to-1 CLK/CMD/DAT connections. CMD34-37, CMD50 and CMD57 are illegal by default (function 0x0), vendor-specific at 0xE and governed by the Mobile Commerce Extension at 0x1. CMD8 initializes cards compliant with Version 2.00 or later, is issued in Idle state before ACMD41, echoes voltage and check pattern in R7, and leaves the card in Idle if the voltage is unsupported. SDSC (CCS=0) uses byte addressing with CMD16-determined block length, while SDHC/SDXC (CCS=1) use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte length regardless of CMD16, disable partial and misaligned access, and do not support write-protected groups; CMD42 is not a memory access command and a block length above 512 bytes sets BLOCK_LEN_ERROR.

**Clock and CRC.** The host may lower or shut down the bus clock; after ACMD41 it must supply continuous 100–400 kHz clock and provide 8 clocks after the last bus transaction, and it may stop the clock of a busy card, though a clock edge is needed to release the busy signal. CRC7 (x7+x3+1) protects commands, responses except R3, and CID/CSD; CRC16 (x16+x12+x5+1, CCITT) protects data blocks with minimum distance d=4 for payloads up to 2048 bytes, applied per line in wide bus mode. CRC failure causes no response and sets COM_CRC_ERROR; illegal commands leave state unchanged and set ILLEGAL_COMMAND.

**Timeouts.** Read timeout is the lower of 100 times the typical access time (TAAC+NSAC) or 100 ms; SDHC/SDXC indicate fixed values and hosts should use at least 100 ms. Write timeout is the lower of 100 times the typical program time (based on R2W_FACTOR) or 250 ms. SDHC busy is limited to 250 ms; SDXC may indicate up to 500 ms in listed scenarios, while speed class writes keep busy to 250 ms. CMD12 during a busy period resets the host timeout counter. In UHS-II mode data is transferred in Data Bursts, busy is indicated per burst rather than per block, and maximum busy after a burst is 1 second. Hosts are advised to use a fixed write timeout exceeding 500 ms.

The passage provides clocking, interrupt, timing, peripheral, and PCB-layout guidance for the TMS320DM814x DaVinci device. The SERDES interface requires a low-jitter differential clock with AC coupling near the processor and compliance with PCI Express REFCLK specifications. Optional external clocks include three AUD_CLKIN inputs up to 50 MHz and a 32,768-Hz CLKIN32 input. The device has 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs that start in bypass mode, with programmable multipliers and dividers constrained by REFCLK, CLKDCO, CLKOUT, SYSCLK, and module-frequency limits; PLL_USB must operate at 960 MHz. The ARM Cortex-A8 interrupt controller supports up to 128 prioritized requests, while the C674x controller combines 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts with event multiplexing.

Timing specifications are measured at device pins and exclude PCB routing delays; board timing must be analyzed using IBIS models. Clock and control signals must transition monotonically. The device includes two CAN 2.0 interfaces, an EDMA controller with up to 64 channels and 512 remappable parameter entries, Advanced Event Triggering with breakpoints, watchpoints, counters and state sequencing, real-time Cortex-A8/system trace, and JTAG emulation and boundary scan with JTAG ID 0x0B8F202F.

The three-port gigabit EMAC switch supports MII, GMII, RMII and RGMII, external Ethernet PHYs and MDIO management. Four GPIO modules provide up to 128 configurable pins. The GPMC supports glueless NOR, NAND, SRAM and custom-logic interfaces, while the ELM identifies BCH errors. HDMI supports 1.3a-compliant video and audio and specifies TMDS impedance, routing and ESD-protection requirements. The HDVPSS provides two display pipelines, video capture and output, graphics layers and format conversion. Video DAC guidance covers normal and bypass modes with 75-ohm routing. Four I2C modules support 10–400 Kbps operation and 7- or 10-bit addressing. The imaging subsystem supports parallel and serial camera inputs, ISP processing, flash strobe and shutter control. DDR2/DDR3 controllers support 16- or 32-bit data paths, two chip selects and two interfaces, with detailed schematics, placement, bypass, termination, VREF and signal-routing requirements; the minimum DDR2 stackup is six layers, and DDR3 support generally includes x8 or x16 DDR3-1600 devices.

High-performance computing (HPC) lets manufacturers perform complex simulations, modeling, analysis, and optimization faster and at higher quality. The passage describes NVIDIA’s Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing (DLAA), which uses the same super-resolution technology as DLSS to produce more realistic native-resolution images with greater temporal stability and detail in motion. It explains that Blackwell was designed to support neural shaders, GPU programs that calculate and control rendering effects. Shader development progressed from fixed-function pipelines to programmable vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, tessellation, primitive, mesh, and ray-tracing shaders.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders that train AI models to approximate computations traditionally performed by shader code. They can efficiently approximate light interactions, decompress textures, predict indirect lighting, and estimate subsurface scattering. NVIDIA and Microsoft’s Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan makes Tensor Cores accessible to pixel, ray-tracing, and other shaders, while Slang features support applications including neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

RTX Neural Materials replaces complex mathematical material models with neural approximations, enabling real-time rendering of multilayer, film-quality assets. RTX Neural Texture Compression uses neural networks for more efficient texture compression and decompression; in the cited demo, memory use fell from 1,110 MB to 333 MB while visual quality increased. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré artifacts and supports higher-order filtering with a single point sample, with Blackwell providing a twofold improvement in point-sampled texture-filtering rates. Neural Radiance Cache infers many lighting bounces from path-traced rays after one bounce, reducing GPU workload while improving indirect lighting. RTX Skin applies ray-traced subsurface scattering to translucent materials, and RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model to improve rasterized faces using pose data and training images covering angles, lighting, emotion, and occlusion.

The Blackwell family includes the flagship GB202, used by the GeForce RTX 5090, with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, and 336 Tensor cores, and is used by the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, and 200 Tensor cores, and is used by the RTX 5070.

NVIDIA states that the specifications are believed accurate as of the publication date but are provided without warranties. It reserves the right to change or discontinue products, disclaims suitability for medical, military, aircraft, space, life-support, or other high-risk applications, provides materials as-is, and grants no intellectual-property licenses beyond the stated terms. NVIDIA, GeForce, and GeForce RTX are identified as NVIDIA trademarks.

On Nov. 27, 2001, Dynegy confirmed negotiations with Enron to restructure a two-week-old, roughly $9 billion all-stock acquisition. Sources said the exchange ratio could fall from 0.2685 to below 0.15 Dynegy shares per Enron share, valuing Enron at about $5 billion. The companies were also considering additional cash funding, debt extensions or refinancing, and protections related to litigation to restore confidence and ease Enron’s liquidity crisis. No final agreement had been reached, and the deal remained vulnerable to termination under a “material adverse change” clause.

Enron’s credit concerns had sharply reduced trading activity. Many energy companies had stopped selling to it and would only buy short-term gas and power; some suspended spot-market transactions after Enron’s quarterly filing raised fears it could not pay upcoming bills. A broker estimated Enron’s over-the-counter volume at about 25 percent of the prior month’s level, while Enron reported a $2.8 billion 30-day rolling average in transaction value and disputed the more severe estimate. Enron’s equity trading unit was reportedly being closed, affecting about 60 employees.

Financing efforts also faced resistance. J.P. Morgan and Citigroup planned to provide $250 million each, while Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal, Carlyle, Blackstone and other investors declined to invest. Moody’s left Enron’s rating at Baa3, the lowest investment-grade level, while noting a possible downgrade. Enron was seeking at least $500 million in new cash, restructuring debt, and extending maturities. Dynegy’s ownership rights to Northern Natural Gas could also become contested if the merger failed.

Enron shares closed at $4.14 after recovering from an intraday decline below $4, while its bonds rebounded. Analysts and arbitrageurs remained cautious because of possible bankruptcy, litigation, liabilities and the deteriorating trading franchise. Forbes separately highlighted Enron’s financial restatement, executive departures, debt burden, lawsuits and declining market value.

Matrimonial websites have transformed traditional arranged matchmaking by allowing families and individuals to find partners online without commission. They offer extensive databases and filters for specific backgrounds or qualities, saving time, money, and travel while expanding choices beyond personal networks. Accessible via websites and mobile apps, they facilitate profile sharing, live text or video chats, and detailed partner information. Many also provide wedding and relationship counseling, private profiles for anonymity, and membership screening and profile verification to reduce fake profiles and enhance safety.

Larry Connors’ %b strategy, outlined in Chapter 5 of *High Probability Trading*, is a mean-reversion strategy based on Bollinger Bands. A buy signal occurs when the close is above the 200-day moving average and %b remains below 0.2 for three consecutive days; the exit signal occurs when %b closes above 0.8. Because Connors omitted the Bollinger Band parameters, the researchers used a five-day lookback and two standard deviations, preventing replication of his exact results. Results for QQQ and SPY were strong but had few fills. A simulated 25-ETF portfolio from 2000 through December 2020 recorded 677 trades, a 75% win rate, 4.84% CAGR, 16% maximum drawdown, and 17% market exposure. Using a ten-day lookback raised CAGR to 8.2% but increased drawdown to 24%. Another parameter set produced only 56 trades, a 5.1% CAGR, and an 11% drawdown. No optimization or combination with Connors’ other strategies was tested.
