The study develops a coarse-grained rod–sphere model for polymer-grafted nanoparticles. A nanosphere is represented by a sphere, while its crystallized polymer bundle is represented by a rigid five-bead rod tethered to the sphere. Three rod-interaction types are considered: lock-and-key, symmetric, and unspecific. Molecular-dynamics simulations vary temperature, sphere-to-rod radius ratio, and interaction type to characterize self-assembly.

Mesostructures are classified by first grouping rods into ordered and disordered clusters and then determining cluster dimensionality from the gyration tensor. A dimensionality parameter \(D\) ranges from zero to three, while a degree-of-order parameter \(O\) measures the fraction of aligned rod–sphere particles. The observed structures include three-dimensional bulk assemblies, monolayers and bilayers, one-dimensional ribbons, fibers, and worms, and zero-dimensional stars and spherical clusters, as well as gels, dispersions, and liquid phases.

Temperature and geometric frustration strongly control morphology. Increasing the sphere-to-rod radius ratio generally lowers dimensionality because the sphere hinders rod growth; larger spheres produce structures ranging from bulk assemblies to ribbons and stars. Interaction type also changes the phase behavior: symmetric rods can form fibers under conditions where lock-and-key rods cannot, while unspecific interactions permit ordered assemblies at higher temperatures.

Assembly trajectories proceed through rapid aggregation, growth, and slower consolidation. Dimensionality increases mainly during growth, whereas order rises during aggregation and consolidation. Simulations of straight ribbons show spontaneous formation of double helices. The system is achiral, so left- and right-handed helices occur equally, handedness can switch at defects, and increasing sphere radius decreases helix pitch.

The model reproduces experimentally observed aggregates and fibers formed by PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles and offers guidance for designing nanobuilding blocks. Limitations include representing polymers as preformed bundles, using a relatively high volume fraction, reaching timescales shorter than experiments, and tethering only one rod per sphere.

The Yankees and Red Sox open a best-of-three AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday, Sept. 30, with first pitch at 6:08 p.m. ET. Boston finished 89-73 and held a 9-4 regular-season head-to-head edge, while New York finished 94-73 on an eight-game winning streak. The winner advances to the ALDS against Toronto. SiriusXM carries New York on channel 89 and Boston on channel 178.

This medRxiv preprint reports the first transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) of whole-blood RNA sequencing from 194 virally non-detectable people living with HIV (PLWH) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) versus 361 HIV-1 seronegative individuals in the Vancouver People Who Inject Drugs Study (ACCESS and VIDUS cohorts).

Of 20,211 genes tested, 566 were differentially expressed (274 up-, 292 downregulated), enriched for 77 GO biological process terms and eight KEGG canonical pathways involving immune functions (cell migration, adhesion, T-cell biology, calcium and PI3K signaling) and cancer pathways (pathways in cancer, chronic myeloid leukemia, non-small cell lung cancer), including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, p53, and TGF-β signaling. Cell-type deconvolution found five cell types differing by HIV status (higher CD8+ T cells and follicular helper T cells; lower naïve CD4+, resting CD4+ memory T cells, and resting mast cells), with DICE data indicating dysregulation spans innate and adaptive immune cell types (e.g., KLRD1 enriched in NK cells, CD40LG in T cell subsets).

Using genes from Massanella et al., 234 HIV-associated DEGs were classified as ART-affected and 332 as ART-unaffected; ART-affected genes showed mostly opposite direction of effect to the pre/post-ART study, suggesting ART shifts expression toward the uninfected state without fully restoring it, and ART-unaffected genes also contribute to enriched pathways.

Partitioned heritability testing (30 GWAS traits) showed enrichment for blood cell counts and inflammatory diseases (asthma, Crohn's disease, rheumatoid arthritis, primary biliary cirrhosis, primary sclerosing cholangitis), but none for cancer traits or HIV acquisition. Cis-eQTL mapping identified 22,475 eQTL for 258 eGenes, with colocalization (posterior probability >0.75) for 17 traits and 26 eGenes, including pancreatic cancer with FAM135B and RP11-826N14.7 and lymphocytic leukemia with CMTM8, plus pleiotropic genes (ANKRD55, CCR6, FUT11, IKZF3, ITGA4, LIME1, SESN1). Drug-target databases showed 111 DEGs are targets of at least one compound (55 ART-affected; 42 targets of approved drugs), e.g., PRKCA targeted by midostaurin and bryostatin 1.

Authors conclude widespread gene dysregulation in suppressed PLWH is not strongly driven by shared genetic susceptibility and may be modifiable with treatment, offering potential drug targets for co-occurring conditions, while noting limitations such as whole-blood data and confounding of infection with ART.

This case-control study examined lipid abnormalities in simple dysmood disorder (SDMD) and first-episode SDMD (FE-SDMD). It recruited 108 Thai university students at Chulalongkorn University, including 64 depressed and 44 control participants matched on age, sex, BMI, and education; three were excluded. Participants with metabolic syndrome and several medical or psychiatric conditions were excluded. Depression severity, suicidal behavior, brooding, and a combined depression phenome were assessed using validated clinical scales, while serum lipids, apolipoproteins, free cholesterol, ApoE, and an LCAT activity index were measured.

Compared with controls, SDMD and FE-SDMD participants had significantly higher free cholesterol and ApoE and lower LCAT activity. SDMD also showed higher composite atherogenicity and Athero/LCAT and Athero/RCT indices, but no substantial changes in HDL cholesterol, ApoA1, reverse cholesterol transport, ApoB, or triglycerides. Clinical severity, suicidal behavior, and phenome scores correlated positively with free cholesterol and inversely with LCAT; atherogenicity indices correlated positively with several clinical measures.

Regression and partial least-squares analyses indicated that LCAT’s association with the depression phenome was mediated through free cholesterol and brooding, without a direct effect. Brooding and lipid measures together explained substantial variation in illness severity and suicidal behavior. Subclinical metabolic syndrome was associated with lower HDL cholesterol and reverse cholesterol transport, higher triglycerides, ApoE, ApoB/ApoA, and Athero/RCT, and interacted with SDMD to intensify these abnormalities. Free cholesterol remained elevated and LCAT reduced across subclinical metabolic syndrome stages.

The authors characterized SDMD and FE-SDMD as pre-proatherogenic states and recommended lipid screening for free cholesterol, LCAT, and ApoE. Limitations included unmeasured oxysterols, omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, and vitamin E, and they called for longitudinal and genetic studies.

The speaker accepts the presidential responsibility with humility, relying on the support of fellow citizens, government associates, patriotic leadership, and Providence. He praises the Constitution’s compromise between former sovereign states, its protection of state and popular authority, and its successful balance of federal and local powers.

Reviewing national development, he argues that America’s institutions have withstood predicted threats involving taxation, war, factional conflict, rapid territorial expansion, and disputes between federal and state authority. He credits the people’s willingness to bear necessary burdens, maintain self-government, and preserve the Union for the nation’s prosperity and growing power.

On slavery, he firmly opposes congressional abolition in the District of Columbia against the wishes of slaveholding states and any federal interference with slavery where it exists. He nevertheless maintains that agitation over slavery has failed to undermine the Union and urges continued restraint and fraternal sentiment.

He pledges strict adherence to the Constitution, faithful performance of federal duties, and no action beyond the limits of federal authority. His foreign policy will favor friendship, equal commercial relations, openness, neutrality, and noninterference in other countries’ affairs while resisting invasions of American rights. He concludes by pledging faithful service and praying for the country’s continued peace and prosperity.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 presents unaudited financial statements covering automotive and energy generation and storage operations. At September 30, Tesla reported $28.11 billion of assets, $21.93 billion of liabilities, $4.71 billion of stockholders’ equity and $3.53 billion of cash and cash equivalents. Third-quarter revenue was $2.98 billion versus $2.30 billion a year earlier, while the company recorded a $619.4 million net loss attributable to common stockholders rather than $21.9 million of income. For the nine months, revenue was $8.47 billion and the net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.29 billion. Gross profit declined to $449.1 million from $636.7 million, and operating results moved from $85.6 million of income to a $535.5 million loss.

Nine-month operating activities used $570.5 million of cash, investing activities used $3.46 billion, and financing activities provided $4.13 billion. Ending cash and cash equivalents increased by $136.8 million to $3.53 billion. The company added $977.5 million of 2.375% convertible notes due 2022, entered related hedging and warrant transactions, and issued $1.8 billion of 5.30% senior notes due 2025. Total debt principal was $9.99 billion, and Tesla reported compliance with its debt covenants.

The notes describe accounting for vehicle resale guarantees as operating leases or collateralized borrowings, the January 2017 cash acquisition of Grohmann for $109.5 million, and ongoing purchase-accounting adjustments for the 2016 SolarCity acquisition. Tesla expected to adopt the new revenue-recognition standard on January 1, 2018 and estimated an equity increase of $550 million to $750 million. It also planned to adopt the new lease standard on January 1, 2019.

Commitments and legal proceedings include the Gigafactory 2 build-to-suit arrangement, under which failure to meet investment and employment requirements could trigger annual payments of $41.2 million. The filing discusses securities litigation involving SolarCity and Tesla, stockholder challenges to the SolarCity acquisition, and a U.S. Treasury settlement under which SolarCity agreed to return $29.5 million without admitting wrongdoing.

More than 250 small earthquakes struck near the California-Mexico border beginning New Year’s Eve, unsettling Brawley residents. The largest was a magnitude-3.9 quake beneath Brawley in the southern Brawley Seismic Zone. Scientists monitored the swarm because it could trigger a larger earthquake, though that risk had largely receded by Sunday night. The zone connects the San Andreas and Imperial faults. A 1979 magnitude-6.5 quake near El Centro injured 91 and damaged major infrastructure, while a 1940 magnitude-7.1 quake killed nine. Brawley’s last major quake was magnitude 5.4 in 2012.

Real Madrid drew 1–1 with Levante at the Bernabéu after Sergio Ramos opened the scoring, Emmanuel Boateng equalized, Isco scored in the 81st minute, and Giampaolo Pazzini’s 89th-minute debut goal earned Levante a point. The result leaves Madrid fourth, 18 points behind Barcelona.

Investing.com reports that the S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date before slipping 1.6% on the first day of August. Medium- and long-term trends remain healthy, but short-term charts show mounting pressure: volatility and credit spreads are rising, market breadth is rolling over with bearish divergence, and August began poorly. July was broadly risk-on, with stocks up and bonds down; technology weighting increased, while U.S. electricity demand reached an all-time high. The page also promotes AI-selected stock strategies, updated gold and silver forecasts, and other investment ideas, alongside warnings about trading and data risks.

Enron disclosed that the SEC had informally requested information about certain related-party transactions, including dealings with the LJM Cayman and LJM2 partnerships formerly managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron called the request voluntary and said it would cooperate; the SEC declined to comment and had not announced a formal investigation. The disclosure followed an unexpectedly reported $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, disclosed only briefly during an analyst call rather than in Enron’s earnings release.

Enron’s shares fell about 21% to $20.65, reducing its market capitalization by roughly $4 billion. The company also reported a $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off, including $35 million connected with terminating the LJM partnerships, producing a $618 million loss. Analysts questioned the valuation, accounting treatment and disclosure of the transactions. Fastow resigned from the partnerships amid conflict-of-interest concerns, while Enron maintained that the arrangements had been reviewed by auditors and attorneys, approved by its board and properly disclosed.

Investors also expressed concern about other off-balance-sheet financing vehicles, particularly the $1 billion Marlin Water Trust II and the $2.4 billion Whitewing trust. Enron could face costly unwinding, requiring asset sales or new share issuance that might dilute shareholders if credit-rating and stock-price triggers were met. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt under review for a possible downgrade, though it remained investment grade.

Shareholder lawsuits challenged Enron’s board and alleged misleading disclosures. Meanwhile, broader U.S. markets rallied late in the session, with the Dow rising 1.88% and the Nasdaq gaining 2.2%, led by semiconductor and other technology-related stocks.

The professor introduces standard experimental games for measuring social preferences and has students participate with candy, apples, and money. In the Dictator game, one participant receives a fixed amount and chooses how much to share with a randomly assigned receiver, who takes no action. The class tests different stakes, public versus less-public decisions, and conditions with and without communication.

In the Ultimatum game, a proposer offers a division of a fixed amount, and a responder accepts or rejects it; rejection gives neither player anything. Students play in both roles, sometimes with communication and varying degrees of publicity. The professor then explains the strategy method: participants specify contingent choices for both roles, including what they would offer as proposer and the minimum offer they would accept as responder. One randomly selected plan is implemented, allowing researchers to collect more information efficiently.

The class also plays the Trust game, in which an investor sends money or candy to a responder, the amount is multiplied, and the responder may return some of it. Communication is allowed in one version. The professor closes by noting that future classes will examine these games more rigorously, including their procedures, interpretations, and relevance to real-world behavior, and invites students to share anonymous observations through the course forum.

The flea flicker is a football trick play designed to resemble a run: the quarterback hands off, the ball is tossed back, and the quarterback throws downfield. It can force defenders to commit to stopping the run, potentially leaving receivers open. Illinois coach Bob Zuppke is credited with the play; he called it against Penn in 1925 and said he first used it in 1910 at Oak Park High School. He compared its action to a dog shaking off fleas. Because the quarterback relinquished possession before receiving the ball back, he cannot intentionally ground it and must throw toward an eligible receiver. Michigan used a flea flicker against TCU in the 2022 College Football Playoff for a touchdown to Ronnie Bell. Related versions include a reverse flea flicker, featuring multiple changes of direction and motion, and a fake flea flicker, which threatens the return pass before the runner continues up the middle.

OFB completed user evaluation of an indigenous upgrade of 130-mm field guns to 155-mm capability at its Nalanda facility and expects an Army order for 300 upgrades. At Rs 1 crore each, the upgrade is cheaper than a new Rs 15-crore gun and increases range from about 27 km to 36 km. OFB also cited IIT-assisted development of new weapon platforms.

The lecture examines direct elimination for large sparse systems \(Ax=b\), emphasizing that elimination can turn zeros into nonzeros, creating “fill-in.” The order of elimination therefore matters greatly: permutations of the unknowns reorder rows and columns compatibly and can produce substantially different amounts of fill.

A graph represents the matrix structure, with one node per row and edges corresponding to nonzero positions. Eliminating a pivot removes its edges and may add edges between nodes previously connected to that pivot. Red-black ordering separates adjacent nodes into two groups, while approximate minimum degree chooses at each stage the node with the fewest current connections. Perfect minimum degree is also discussed, though approximate minimum degree is presented as often performing as well or better.

Examples show that minimizing bandwidth is not necessarily an effective objective: a matrix with large bandwidth can admit an ordering with no fill, whereas a bandwidth-reducing permutation can introduce fill. Block-structured matrices can arise in constrained optimization through Lagrange multipliers.

Fill-in can be observed in the nonzero entries of the \(L\) and \(U\) factors produced by elimination. MATLAB’s `spye` visualizes sparsity, and `nnz` counts nonzeros, allowing experimental comparison of orderings and their fill and operation counts. For symmetric positive-definite matrices, Cholesky factorization provides a special case.

Graph-separator methods instead partition a graph into two groups connected through a separator, which is ordered last to preserve zero blocks. Nested dissection recursively applies this strategy and may be especially useful for three-dimensional or very large sparse problems.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit successive-approximation ADC data-acquisition device with a differential analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, integrated ADC driver, precision reference buffer, alarm functions, and multiSPI digital interface.

Each analog input includes an internal overvoltage-protection circuit using current-limiting input resistors and antiparallel diodes. External surge, ESD, and EFT protection is still required. With AVDD at 5 V, the internal circuit withstands inputs up to ±20 V, although excessive energization can saturate the ADC and potentially damage the device. Protection also operates when AVDD is floating, with an approximately ±15 V boundary. Higher source impedance reduces protection-diode current but can increase gain errors and system noise.

The PGA converts single-ended or differential inputs into signals for the SAR ADC and adjusts their common-mode level to maximize ADC dynamic range. The RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits select input ranges; the power-on setting of 0000 corresponds to ±3 V × VREF. A trimmed, precisely matched resistor network minimizes gain error. A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter at the PGA output typically has a 500 kHz −3 dB cutoff and is consistent across input ranges.

The internal 4.096 V reference is selected by default through INTREF_DIS = 0 and appears at REFIO. REFIO requires at least 4.7 µF of decoupling and cannot directly drive external loads without an acceptable buffer. Factory calibration establishes initial accuracy, but mechanical and thermal stress, particularly solder reflow, can shift the reference voltage; multiple reflows cause additional shifts. The reference is temperature compensated from −40°C to +125°C. For external-reference mode, INTREF_DIS is set to 1, a filtered external 4.096 V source drives REFIO, and the internal buffer drives REFCAP. REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a closely placed 1 µF for high-frequency decoupling. Typical reference-buffer temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C, with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar and unipolar inputs with straight-binary output. For each range, FSR equals PFS minus NFS and LSB equals FSR/2^16. The active-high ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin can provide alarm output when configured accordingly. Input alarms use programmable high and low thresholds with hysteresis, while the AVDD alarm trips at typical low and high thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped flags are stored in ALARM_REG; active flags clear at the end of each conversion, whereas tripped flags remain set until the register is read. Alarm information can be read through the alarm pin, the alarm register, or appended to output data.

The multiSPI interface uses input and output shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol processor. It supports standard SPI writes and several read configurations, including single- or dual-SDO legacy SPI and source-synchronous modes. The interface may be connected to a single device or multiple devices in a daisy chain. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, SDO-0 of one device feeds SDI of the next, and an optimal frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges; received data appears from device N back toward device 1.

The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST input can request either an application reset, which restores configuration registers, or a power-on reset, which also resets the PGA, ADC driver, and reference. ACQ acquires the analog input, and CONV performs a conversion after a rising CONVST/CS edge. Further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored until conversion completes. RVS can signal completion, or the host can wait for the maximum conversion time. NAP and power-down modes reduce power use.

A data-transfer frame begins with a falling CONVST/CS edge and ends with its rising edge. During the frame, SCLK shifts commands into the device and output data out. A 32-clock frame is optimal and executes the received command; a shorter frame cannot perform a valid write but can provide requested output bits, while the last 32 bits of a longer frame form the command. Output data can contain the latest conversion result, fixed test patterns, or requested register data, with optional device-address, input-range, AVDD-alarm, input-alarm, and parity fields.

After power-up or reset, SPI-00-S is used by default. SDI_MODE selects one of four SPI clock configurations, and SDO_MODE selects SPI-compatible or source-synchronous output. Source-synchronous mode supplies a synchronous clock on RVS and permits internal or external clock sourcing. Dual-SDO operation assigns SDO-1 to the multifunction pin and outputs two bits per clock edge. The default SPI-00-S protocol applies to the first write used to change SDI_MODE.

The nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power functions, SPI input and output protocols, output data formatting, reference and input-range selection, alarm status, and alarm thresholds. RST_PWRCTL_REG writes require first writing 69h to address 05h as an unlock key. The DEVICE_ID_REG supports identification of as many as 16 devices in a daisy chain.

A reference design combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 to provide eight software-configurable differential channels for industrial voltage, current, or temperature sensing. It supports standard industrial ranges and reaches 1% settling accuracy in under 5 µs. A thermistor example illustrates programmable input alarms and hysteresis for avoiding false trips near temperature thresholds.

AVDD and DVDD are separate, independently adjustable supplies. Each requires at least 10 µF and 1 µF decoupling, with the 1 µF capacitor placed close to the supply pins. NAP mode is enabled through RST_PWRCTL_REG and entered when CONVST/CS remains high after conversion. Power-down mode shuts down analog blocks while retaining the interface and registers; recovery requires clearing PWRDN and waiting the specified power-up interval. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital regions, minimizes supply vias, uses short ground paths, places 1 µF and 10 µF ceramic capacitors directly across REFCAP, and decouples REFIO by at least 4.7 µF when the internal reference is used.

The document also provides related component references, support resources, ESD cautions, revision information noting production-data status for the ADS8685W and ADS8689W, package and orderable information, and legal disclaimers.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated September 11, 2015, announcing that Bradford L. Smith was appointed President and Chief Legal Officer effective that date. Smith, age 56, previously served as General Counsel & Executive Vice President, Legal and Corporate Affairs. He joined Microsoft in 1993 and has served as General Counsel since 2002. The report was signed by John A. Seethoff, Assistant Secretary.

The D.C. Circuit held that the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission had jurisdiction to review an ALJ's Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA) fee award, rejecting the petitioner's contrary argument; 5 U.S.C. § 504(a)(3) permits normal agency review of an ALJ's decision, and Chevron deference does not apply. On the merits, the court reversed the Commission's 3-to-2 decision vacating the fee award, holding that the Secretary of Labor's position was not substantially justified.

In the underlying proceeding, MSHA cited CSG and its general manager for using equipment frames as grounding conductors, claiming frame grounding was prohibited and constituted an "unwarrantable failure" to comply with 30 C.F.R. § 56.12025. No regulation forbade frame grounding, the regulatory definition (30 C.F.R. § 56.2) merely required connecting with ground to make earth part of the circuit, and MSHA inspectors never tested CSG's compliance. A closure order forced CSG to install fourth-wire grounding, and MSHA assessed civil penalties of $7,000 against CSG and $6,000 against the individual manager. The Secretary initially alleged frame grounding violated MSHA standards and the National Electrical Code, then shifted to claiming the motors lacked a ground lead. CSG moved for summary judgment with uncontested evidence of compliance, and the ALJ granted it; the Secretary did not appeal. The ALJ then awarded CSG EAJA fees, which the Commission vacated.

The court found the Commission's legal analysis erroneous: it relied on the objective of mine safety to justify enforcement of requirements never adopted through rulemaking, a recurring error the court had previously rejected in a case involving trash accumulations outside mine workings. The Secretary's claim that frame grounding had been forbidden for fifteen years was unsupported, and prior ALJs had repeatedly rejected the same theory, advising that the Secretary should use rulemaking instead. The Commission also erred in finding a reasonable basis in fact, since no testing was performed and frame grounding was not a per se violation. The court therefore restored the ALJ's award and remanded to determine fees for pursuing the petition for review.

Although the establishment survey reported 33,000 lost September jobs, the household survey showed employment up 906,000 to a record 154.3 million, unemployment down 331,000 to 4.2%, and labor force participation and wages rising. Beth Ann Bovino attributed the discrepancy partly to hurricane-affected businesses’ inability to respond, while noting payroll revisions and expected weather-driven rebounds. Markets were largely unmoved, and private payroll data showed 135,000 added jobs.

Starting investing young helps build lasting habits and gives money more time to grow. Investing €50 monthly from age 20 at 5% annually could yield €75,000 by 60, while starting at 40 would require saving €185 monthly for the same result. The article recommends contributing regularly, separating savings from spending, and investing promptly to benefit from compounding—earning interest on interest or reinvesting dividends. More frequent compounding over longer periods can accelerate growth. It also advises creating a budget based on take-home pay, distinguishing fixed and variable expenses, and redirecting discretionary spending toward investing as income grows.

Malik Nabers will undergo knee surgery this week and is out for the season after tearing his right ACL and meniscus while leaping for a pass. His injury renewed criticism of MetLife Stadium’s FieldTurf, which has been linked to at least 15 knee ligament or Achilles tears since 2020. The stadium installed FieldTurf Core in 2023 to reduce injuries, and NFL data showed fewer ACL injuries on synthetic turf than grass last year. More than 90% of players have recently said they prefer grass, but the NFL has no plans to replace MetLife’s surface. The NFLPA had also raised concerns after Joe Burrow suffered turf toe at another FieldTurf venue.

Philosophy of education is often treated as peripheral to educational research because research is commonly identified with empirical data collection and analysis. Students may question whether it is research, while some scholars misconstrue it as qualitative research. Economic precarity, competitive academic funding systems, and preferences for high-impact publications further marginalize the field.

Scientistic standards privilege large-scale, quantitative, experimental, and generalizable research as evidence-based and predictive, despite limitations involving generalizability, ethical questions, and local impact. Historically, philosophy of education has faced criticism as both irrelevant and methodologically weak, while its identity, methods, foundations, and future direction remain internally contested. Narratives of a “golden age” and a uniquely new precarity are characterized as partial and nostalgic.

Proposed responses include critically examining evidence, impact, and generalizability; appealing to justice and educational values; and defending philosophy’s distinctive contributions. The essay concludes that philosophy of education should be repositioned as an essential site of pluralism, community-based deliberation, reflexivity, responsiveness, and criticality, while rejecting the assumption that educational research must be empirical.

The Soviet representative discussed trusteeship for detached territories, noting Soviet responsibilities regarding Italian colonies and potentially Japanese territories, and agreed that League members should lead the League’s liquidation. He maintained that all Soviet republics should be initial members, while associated nations and neutral states should be excluded. After briefly considering possible locations for the organization, he reviewed Latin American proposals. He accepted principles including political independence, territorial integrity, peaceful change, treaty revision, and international law, but opposed strengthening the Assembly and Court at the Council’s expense. Compulsory jurisdiction was explained to him. He also regarded smaller states’ opposition to permanent-member voting as unrealistic but agreed to consider the proposed voting formula and requested an analysis of the Council’s functions. The conversations ended on a friendly note.

ETH Zurich researchers found that cancer cells transfer mitochondria through threadlike nanotubes into neighboring fibroblasts. Within 24 hours, these fibroblasts grew faster and showed increased activity of cancer-related genes; when injected with cancer cells into mouse ears, they promoted tumor formation. The protein MIRO2 is essential for delivering mitochondria to nanotubes and transferring them to fibroblasts, making it a possible therapeutic target, though research remains early. Earlier work also suggests cancer cells can transfer mitochondria to immune cells, weakening their cancer-fighting abilities. Questions remain about the transfer’s triggers, driving forces, and mechanisms.

The speaker sees little carryover from the previous season and no meaningful rivalries, saying the team is focused on its own play regardless of a potential opponent’s return. Despite disappointing results in the first games, they believe both teams played well enough to win and failed to capitalize on opportunities. Home-crowd advantage helps, and they remain confident of securing at least one road win.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2020 reported net sales of $88.9 billion, up 40% from $63.4 billion in Q2 2019. Operating income rose to $5.8 billion from $3.1 billion, net income increased to $5.2 billion from $2.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $10.30, up from $5.22. For the first six months, net sales were $164.4 billion, operating income was $9.8 billion, and net income was $7.8 billion.

Q2 North America sales were $55.4 billion with $2.1 billion of operating income; International sales were $22.7 billion with $345 million of operating income, versus a $601 million loss a year earlier; and AWS sales were $10.8 billion with $3.4 billion of operating income. Six-month North America operating income declined, while International’s loss narrowed to $52 million and AWS operating income rose to $6.4 billion.

COVID-19 increased demand for staples, essential goods, and home products but also created fulfillment and supply-chain constraints. Amazon lengthened delivery promises on some products, moderated other orders, reduced marketing spending, hired 175,000 additional employees, and incurred more than $4 billion of pandemic-related costs in Q2. Management expected capacity constraints and elevated sales, fulfillment, and workplace-safety costs to continue affecting results through at least Q3.

Q2 operating cash flow was $20.6 billion, compared with $9.1 billion a year earlier; six-month operating cash flow was $23.7 billion, compared with $11.0 billion. Investing activities used $17.8 billion and financing activities provided $7.4 billion in Q2. Cash capital expenditures were $6.6 billion in Q2 and $12.0 billion for six months, primarily supporting fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure, including AWS. At June 30, Amazon had $37.5 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $33.9 billion of marketable securities, $33.1 billion of long-term debt, $258.3 billion of total assets, and $73.7 billion of stockholders’ equity.

Effective January 1, 2020, Amazon extended servers’ estimated useful lives from three to four years. The change reduced Q2 depreciation and amortization by $696 million and increased net income by $534 million; for six months, it reduced depreciation and amortization by $1.5 billion and increased net income by $1.1 billion. The inventory valuation allowance was $1.7 billion at quarter-end, with each additional 1% potentially adding about $220 million to cost of sales.

Amazon had $33.2 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, including $10 billion issued in June 2020, $730 million of commercial paper borrowings, and $573 million under its secured credit facility. Total contractual commitments were $171.9 billion. The company also disclosed tax contingencies of approximately $3.7 billion and new class-action litigation alleging price-fixing, monopolization, consumer-protection, and unjust-enrichment claims, which Amazon disputes.

The president argues that the public inauguration, though not constitutionally required, creates a solemn mutual covenant to uphold the Constitution, obey the laws, and secure equal rights. Marking the nation’s entry into its second century under the Constitution, he contrasts the weak original republic with a nation of thirty-eight prosperous states whose population, wealth, education, material welfare, religion, charity, and civic virtues have greatly advanced.

He supports a protective tariff as a continuation of the policy that made the early republic economically independent and, following emancipation, removed sectional divisions from tariff debates. He urges Southern manufacturers and miners to include Black workers as allies and calls protective policy a means of achieving national unity, while insisting that the executive enforce all laws uniformly and without regard to sectional or private interests. Corporations and communities must respect legal limits, and naturalization laws should more carefully examine applicants’ character and fitness.

On foreign affairs, he advocates peaceful diplomacy, friendly relations with European powers, and protection of American citizens and commercial rights abroad, while opposing European domination of an American canal or control of independent American states. He supports improved naval strength, American steamship lines, more adequate pensions for Union veterans and their families, and admission of the Dakota, Montana, and Washington territories as states, with prompt confirmation of settlers’ land titles.

The president calls for careful, merit-based appointments, full enforcement of civil-service laws, and continued reform toward a nonpartisan civil service. He warns that large annual surpluses are harmful but supports reducing revenue when possible, applying small excesses to the public debt, and maintaining modern warships. He also urges stronger election safeguards, education where suffrage is threatened, fair treatment of opposing political views, and patriotism exercised through fraternity and justice rather than partisan or unlawful methods. He expresses confidence in the nation’s future while insisting that power, wealth, and opportunity remain conditioned on justice, mercy, education, virtue, and respect for the law.

Penn State is renovating the White Building’s lobby, entrance, pathway, registration desks, stairwell, and elevator to improve traffic flow, safety, and usage tracking. Completion is expected by the end of March, but gym upgrades are not planned.

The global visceral pain market is projected to reach USD 14.22 billion by 2024, driven by population aging, rising prevalence and awareness, and increased healthcare spending and infrastructure. North America led in 2016, while Asia Pacific is expected to grow fastest at 6.2% CAGR. Analgesics dominated with 60.4% share, and Crohn’s disease was the largest indication at 41.4%. Pharmaceutical R&D and government initiatives are cited as growth supports.

Superannuation tax changes take effect in July and are expected to boost self-managed funds, with more than two million Australians projected to hold SMSFs within 15 years. Measures include a $1.6 million transfer-balance cap, lower contribution caps and removal of the work test for over-65s. SMSF interest is rising among younger Australians and business owners, although total numbers are declining.

The Finance Ministry amended Rule 80 governing advances to families of government employees who die in service, retaining existing provisions. The maximum advance is ₹25,000. The order takes effect upon issuance, does not require reopening sanctioned cases, and applies to Indian Audit and Accounts Department personnel in consultation with the CAG.

Injuries and a demanding hockey schedule have taken a toll, but the team remains confident and focused on avoiding outside noise. After a loss they cited a broken play, emphasized a must-win mentality, and said they typically rebound from poor games while aiming to avoid consecutive bad performances.

The paper argues that rapid AI adoption in financial markets—driven by algorithmic trading, high-frequency trading, machine learning, and growing bank investment—has increased operational, systemic, and manipulation risks amid fragmented regulation and limited incident transparency. Confidential regulator reporting, information withholding, and the specialized nature of financial data mean existing crowdsourced AI incident databases omit many algorithmic-trading incidents. Post-2008 reporting regimes provide useful infrastructure, but current frameworks do not comprehensively address AI-specific risks or support coordinated global oversight.

Drawing lessons from healthcare and aviation, the paper proposes a semi-public, regulator-reported global database of significant AI incidents. Adapted from MiFID II structures, it uses standardized fields covering market context, volume, price impact, regulatory indicators, and AI system details. Percentage-based metrics, high-level categorizations, and the deliberate omission of timestamps and execution dates would permit cross-jurisdictional analysis while protecting commercially sensitive information. Only incidents causing more than a 5% price deviation or a 20% volume anomaly against the 30-day average would be reported.

A search of regulatory websites identified 20 AI-related algorithmic-trading incidents, none of which appeared in four prominent incident databases. The authors generated 2,999 synthetic records using Gretel.ai’s ACTGAN model for proof-of-concept testing. ANOVA results indicated that AI system type affected trading behavior more than geography, while systemic risks showed no significant regional variation, supporting globally coordinated responses. The model achieved 92% precision in detecting systematic risk patterns despite modest explanatory power.

K-means clustering and PCA identified five trading zones associated with stable activity, anomalies, transitions, irregular behavior, and strategic trading, supporting detection of spoofing, momentum ignition, layering, and cross-market manipulation. The framework could assist regulators, central banks, surveillance teams, and global risk bodies through standardized monitoring, dashboards, circuit breakers, alerts, and coordinated intervention. Limitations include uneven reporting practices, reliance on synthetic and English-language data, the inability to capture all trading-floor dynamics, and the effect of temporal omission on Granger causality analysis.

Sweden’s unemployment rate remained at 7.3% in July 2017, unchanged from a year earlier, but varied sharply by birthplace: 3.9% for the Sweden-born and 21.8% for the foreign-born. Record numbers of foreign-born job seekers were registered in the Introduction Programme, rising from 59,362 to 76,561 as asylum backlogs were processed. Long-term unemployment increased from 142,499 to 145,896, mainly because programme participants are included. Arbetsförmedlingen requested 600 million kronor more for 2018 and 900 million more for 2019.

Version 2 expands SEV-ES support and introduces initial SEV-SNP support, including a 52-bit hypervisor feature bitmap for advertising optional capabilities. Revisions add 64-bit SNP guest-request sequence numbers, the VLEK GUID, expanded error reporting, guest APIC ID discovery, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, the SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and additional GHCB MSR functionality. Full Version 2 support is mandatory except for features identified as optional through the bitmap.

The specification defines the GHCB page, its alignment and shared-memory requirements, access through MSR 0xc001_0130, protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, SNP GHCB GPA registration, and requests for preferred GHCB addresses, page-state changes, VMPL changes, and unregistration. SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use. The SNP Secrets Page reserved area can communicate VMPL message sequence numbers, and the EFI protocol supplies the Secrets and CPUID pages to the operating system.

Guest non-automatic exits generate a #VC exception. The guest copies required state into the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and processes the hypervisor’s response after resumption. The VALID_BITMAP identifies supplied fields, while SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 convey responses and errors. Supported events cover I/O and MMIO access, MSR protection, hypercalls, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended requests, certificate return, AP creation, APIC ID lists, VMPL execution, Secure AVIC, SEV-TIO, termination, and unsupported events. SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages and require firmware sequence-number synchronization; extended requests may also return certificates. Page-state processing records progress in shared memory so interrupted requests can resume.

SEV-ES application-processor startup uses AP reset-hold requests and an AP jump table, while SEV-SNP AP Creation can create or update VMSA-backed processors and enable hotplug. Restricted Injection requires SNP AP Creation and provides a host-owned doorbell page, #HV notifications, host-emulated APIC behavior, guest IPI delivery, and emulated timer support. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. Hardware debug behavior is also specified for SEV-ES guests.

Derivatives are financial contracts whose value derives from an underlying asset, such as a commodity, stock, currency, index, or interest rate. Major types include forwards, futures, options, swaps, and CFDs. Futures are standardized exchange-traded contracts requiring delivery at a predetermined price and date; forwards are privately agreed; swaps exchange cash flows; CFDs are broker contracts settling the price difference between opening and closing a trade. Options give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at an agreed strike price before expiration.

Derivatives serve three main purposes: hedging against price movements, speculating on price movements, and gaining access to otherwise difficult-to-trade assets or markets. Hedging examples include farmers selling wheat futures and investors buying index put options to protect portfolios. Most retail trading is speculative, but the market is zero-sum, and consistent profitability is difficult due to market changes, behavioral biases, leverage, and poorly structured products.

Options strategies include buying calls in expectation of rising prices and spreads involving multiple options with different strikes or expirations. Options profits depend on underlying price movements, strike prices, time remaining, and expiration. One examined put-selling strategy produced a 10.1% backtested return versus 9.8% for the S&P 500, with substantially lower volatility, although commissions, slippage, and taxes reduce such differences.

The passage recommends trading only for hedging or with a specific, backtested plan, using conservative leverage and adequate margin, fully understanding the instruments, and never risking capital without a demonstrated edge.

The study addresses mapping messy point-of-sale transaction text to merchant IDs, a task limited by noisy formats, aggregators, transaction numbers, scale, latency, and cost. It compares pretrained SBERT, Llama3-8B, and Flan-T5 with small proprietary encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder Transformer models trained on transaction and merchant data.

Out-of-the-box models performed poorly, while fine-tuning improved Llama3 and Flan-T5 but reduced SBERT performance. Proprietary models matched or exceeded the pretrained models with fewer parameters and lower training and inference costs. The proprietary decoder-only model achieved 72.07% weighted accuracy versus Llama3’s 72.89%, while reducing inference time from 735 milliseconds to 95.02 milliseconds. Proprietary encoder-decoder and encoder-only models also outperformed Flan-T5 and SBERT, respectively. Experiments showed that tokenizer, vocabulary size, embedding dimension, and depth materially affect performance; larger models and vocabularies are not always better.

The proprietary decoder-only model was deployed for previously unhandled raw transactions, while retaining existing rule-based and string-distance matching. Confidence and name-similarity filters excluded potentially incorrect matches, and monthly manual review supported further fine-tuning. Deployment raised overall transaction coverage from 80% to 94% and produced estimated annual savings of approximately $13.2 million.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on July 21, 2015, reporting its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2015. The related press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference absent express reference.

IHE editors discuss White House and Hill developments affecting higher education, including minority-serving institution funding cuts, international-student restrictions, student borrowing, and the “Compact for Academic Excellence,” while previewing federal policy priorities.

David Moyes named his team to face Liverpool, with Donald Love replacing the suspended Billy Jones and Jack Rodwell returning to midfield. Injuries to Lamine Kone and Victor Anichebe forced changes, while four unfamiliar names joined the bench. Moyes, with limited resources, plans to bolster his squad in January.

During GOG’s 2017 Piñata Madness event, players could buy $3 piñatas containing random games valued at $6–$45. GOG said players were likely to receive a title they did not own; anyone owning every game in the pool would receive one to give away. Confirmed titles included Heroes of Might and Magic V, Pillars of Eternity, and Shadow Warrior 2, and new games might be added without advance notice. Contents were generated at purchase, delaying openings offered no advantage. The promotion applied loot-box mechanics to game purchases, raising concerns about gambling-based profits. The event ran through August 21, with purchased piñatas openable until August 28.

The passage reviews chess’s origins, characteristics, educational benefits, and the strength of supporting research. Chess first appeared in India about 1,500 years ago and later spread worldwide. It is described as a strategy and mind sport requiring tactical skill, decision-making, memory, logic, planning, creativity, concentration, and the prediction of outcomes, as well as a science and art.

Studies cited associate chess with improved spatial abilities, mathematical achievement, logical thinking, IQ, focus, visualization, analysis, abstract reasoning, critical thinking, metacognition, and problem-solving. Reported personal and social benefits include self-confidence, self-control, perseverance, motivation, independence, emotional regulation, sportsmanship, communication, and friendship formation. Chess players are also described as more academically successful, adaptable, optimistic, confident, and compatible with their schools and teachers.

Chess may support education because players consider alternatives, anticipate consequences, receive immediate feedback, and continually adjust their strategies. These processes can transfer to mathematics and other subjects, where students similarly set goals, evaluate possible solutions, and reflect on decisions. Chess has been linked to improved numerical reasoning, visualization of texts, and reading comprehension, although some relationships, including the proposed reading benefits, remain speculative. Chess training may also improve concentration, patience, creativity, observation, research skills, and the ability to work independently.

Children and adults learn through similar processes, but children reportedly adapt more readily, tolerate mistakes, and use feedback to correct their play. Early training may be more effective because children’s mental schemas change more quickly. However, children may quit after early failures, and the resulting selection of successful participants limits research samples.

Chess expertise develops from knowledge and rule recognition through pattern recognition, intuition, and automatic play, requiring sustained practice, analysis, and experience. Playing for many years is important, but researchers disagree about whether experience alone determines expertise, and intelligence alone cannot reliably explain chess ability. The relationship between chess and intelligence remains difficult to measure because both are multidimensional and are influenced by practice and other factors.

Reported outcomes may partly reflect the Pygmalion effect, in which extra attention and teacher expectations improve performance independently of chess itself. A meta-analysis of 24 studies found that chess instruction benefited mathematics, reading, and cognitive skills, more strongly in mathematics than reading, but reported a modest average effect and noted that instructor effort may have contributed. Other studies question whether chess improves attention, creativity, intelligence, or academic performance, and its initial benefits may decline as playing skill increases.

Methodological weaknesses—including inadequate pre- and post-testing, incomplete randomization, absent active control groups, small or biased samples, and difficult measurement of abstract concepts—limit conclusions. Recommended research includes larger, longitudinal, quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies, active controls, structural equation modeling, and direct examination of cognitive and academic changes.

The passage recommends expanding chess opportunities in schools through extracurricular activities, lessons, tournaments, online play, and integration with mathematics and geometry. Beginning around ages four or five is proposed as ideal, with age-appropriate programs, instructional materials, competitions, and possible use in special education.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by a quarter-point to 1%–1.25%, its third increase in six months, citing a slow-growing but durable economy. It also plans to gradually reduce its $4.5 trillion bond portfolio. The Fed forecasts one more increase this year. Solid hiring and expectations of higher inflation support continued rate rises, but chronically low inflation and political uncertainty may keep increases modest. Three vacancies on the Fed’s seven-member board could alter policy, with possible nominees including Randal Quarles, Marvin Goodfriend and Robert Jones. Chairwoman Janet Yellen’s term ends in February, and President Trump has given conflicting signals about renominating her.

The Horns offense is a high-post screen-and-roll system using two high-post screeners. This gives the ball handler screens in both directions, limits baseline help on drives, and creates open shots when defenders sag. Its 1-4 high alignment is suited to pressure defenses. The primary action has O1 driving off O5’s high-post screen, with options to turn the corner, pull up, return the ball if the defense switches, or kick out to wings. If the initial action does not produce a shot, the offense reverses the ball for post isolation.

Counters include driving against a chasing defender, passing to a shooter when help sags, pulling up against a defender going under the screen, and feeding a roll or post mismatch after a switch. Against anticipated switches, the screener can slip; against show-and-recover, the ball handler can dribble away and use a roll or pop. The ball handler may drive opposite an early cheat, back-cut for a lob when a post is overplayed, or move the ball immediately with sharp passes against a trap. The off-screener pops or cuts opposite the primary screener as appropriate.

Variations include Loop, Base Split, Picked Fence, Twin Sides, High Post Rub, and Hand Back Lob, using combinations of mid, down, back, and side screens, flex actions, inside-triangle motion, ball reversals, posting, and lob passes.

Successful execution requires coordinated footwork, timing, nonverbal communication, and experience among the ball handler, screener, and receiver. Installation emphasizes repeated breakdown drills, two- and three-player actions, and scrimmages. Game strategies include scouting opponents, recognizing defensive adjustments, varying alignments and entries, moving players against weaker defenders, and developing individual fundamentals. The passage also recommends preparing to defend the Horns because it is among the game’s most-used offenses.

California's 2016 gun violence restraining order law, which served as a model for national legislation proposed by Sen. Marco Rubio after the Florida mass shooting, resulted in 190 orders in 2016-17 allowing police to temporarily remove firearms from people deemed dangerous to themselves or others. The process lets law enforcement, family members, or household members petition a judge, who must find that alternatives were tried and found inadequate; orders last a 21-day cooling-off period before a hearing on extension of up to one year, with the target given a chance to respond. According to the California Department of Justice, most of the 190 orders did not extend beyond the initial 21 days, only 17 lasting a full year, and the vast majority were initiated by law enforcement rather than family members. State data also showed law enforcement failed to serve 31 orders. Author Sen. Nancy Skinner (D-Berkeley), who introduced the law after the 2014 Isla Vista shooting, said the tool can help prevent deaths and that loved ones are often the first to notice threats. A state website provides information on seeking such orders.

Taco Cabana is offering two free breakfast tacos via Favor today from 9–11 a.m., while supplies last, to users in Favor’s Dallas delivery zone. Friday visitors can receive a limited coupon for one breakfast taco.

Blackwell’s accelerated frequency switching enables full GPU performance within a power budget, saves power during short idle periods, and permits higher clock speeds during active work. Its low-latency sleep states enter 10 times faster than Ada and use Advanced Power Gating to reduce power more quickly. For small-language-model inference, shorter active periods, lower-power transitional states, and faster deepest sleep can save up to 50% power.

DLSS 4 uses AI to improve frame rate, latency, and image quality. Multi Frame Generation can produce up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using fifth-generation Tensor Cores. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster than the previous method, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame; an efficient AI model also replaces hardware optical flow for generating flow fields. Enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine, whose doubled pixel-processing capacity supports higher resolutions and refresh rates.

DLSS 4 replaces the CNN architecture used since DLSS 2 with transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. Transformers use self-attention to identify longer-range patterns, ingest twice as many parameters, and improve temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ray-traced image quality. Super Resolution produces more stable frames with less ghosting, Ray Reconstruction reduces denoiser artifacts, and DLAA constructs higher-quality native-resolution images.

Blackwell advances GPU shading from fixed-function and earlier programmable shader stages toward neural shaders. Cooperative Vectors for DX12 and Vulkan allow Tensor Cores to be accessed from any shader, while Slang features support neural rendering techniques. Potential applications include neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

RTX Neural Texture Compression can provide up to seven-to-one VRAM compression over block-compressed formats. In the cited demo, neural materials reduced memory use from 1,110 MB to 333 MB while improving visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns, with Blackwell providing twice the point-sampled texture-filtering rate. Neural Radiance Cache infers multi-bounce indirect lighting from path-traced rays after one bounce and trains small neural networks on live game data. RTX Skin brings subsurface scattering to real-time game rendering, while RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model, trained on thousands of offline images, to improve faces from rasterized geometry and 3D pose data.

The Blackwell GPU family includes three described chips. GB202 has 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; it powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and a 256-bit memory interface; it powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, 200 Tensor Cores, and a 192-bit memory interface; it powers the RTX 5070.

AMD’s Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) provides signed, nonpersistent runtime updates to selected firmware and settings without a BIOS reflash or system reset. It targets high-benefit, low-risk runtime concerns in AMD-provided binary firmware included in AGESA releases, such as ASP firmware, modules, and register settings, and may update firmware on other microprocessors. SFS does not patch customer BIOS or other x86 code, including SMM, AGESA, and UEFI, or run-once code such as the AGESA boot loader.

Each SFS package targets a specific PI release, base patch, and firmware level and includes release notes. Packages are nonpersistent and intended as interim steps between BIOS releases, allowing additional customer validation of new BIOS firmware while potentially reducing security issues and unplanned maintenance.

Customers are responsible for deciding whether to deploy packages, testing and validating them, and operating an SFS Deployment Agent that communicates with AMD’s PSP/ASP through the appropriate driver. AMD identifies eligible fixes and distributes them as SFS packages. Updates are applied at runtime, must be reapplied after reboots, and, in multi-socket systems, are distributed to the appropriate sockets.

SFS uses three version levels. The monotonically increasing SFS Patch Level identifies the installed package and prevents rollback. Individual firmware components maintain firmware and Security Patch Level versions, whose functionality may later be reverted. The monotonically increasing System Patch Level tracks run-once code executed since the last reboot, preserving its execution history even if its effects are reverted. The host OS can query these levels.

AMD cryptographically signs every package, and the ASP verifies AMD’s signature before execution. Customers may optionally co-sign packages to retain approval authority over deployments; the ASP then verifies the customer signature before AMD’s. Co-signing requires the customer to provide an RSA public key during early boot, before BOOT_DONE, after which the key cannot be changed. BIOS developers must explicitly enable SFS and, optionally, require co-signing; both options are disabled by default.

Packages may modify registers or other values, replace a complete microprocessor firmware image, or update portions such as drivers. SEV updates are committed to prevent rollback and require a reboot to revert, while SNP packages require the relevant pages to be HV-FIXED. Attestation evidence is obtained through interfaces such as SPDM or DPE. Packages verify firmware dependencies before updating and should not be applied if any portion cannot complete, avoiding forced resets.

A customer deployment agent builds a 2MB-aligned command buffer containing any co-signing header, the signed AMD package, and optional customer signature, then submits it through the TEE mailbox interface. The ASP protects the buffer from x86 access, verifies signatures, validates and executes the patch, updates version information, and returns status. Packages can be applied during OS boot, immediately afterward, or during operation, and must be deployed sequentially. They are matched to exact firmware and patch-level combinations and run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines may need to stop and restart during an SEV firmware update, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

Pharmaceutical dosage form testing systems assess tablets’ chemical, physical, and bioavailability properties through QC tests covering weight, uniformity, dimensions, hardness, friability, disintegration, dissolution, stability, and degradation. Regulatory requirements, quality assurance, and technological advances drive market growth, while high prices and shortages of skilled personnel are restraints. North America is expected to lead, followed by Europe, while APECJ and China are emerging markets.
