Before taking action, the Executive sought approval of the Senate and Congress, including confirmation of nominees and funding. The United States intended to promote liberal commercial relations, oppose discriminatory trade practices favoring European powers, support maritime neutrality, recognize that free ships make free goods, limit blockades, discourage future European colonization, and encourage religious liberty. It also expressed an interest in peacefully influencing the ongoing southern American wars without forming alliances or taking belligerent actions. Richard C. Anderson and John Sergeant were nominated as envoys extraordinary and ministers plenipotentiary, with William B. Rochester as secretary to the mission.

Hollywood Bowl Group’s full-year results were well received, with shares up nearly 8%. Revenue rose almost 9%, like-for-like sales 3.5%, net cash from operations more than 16%, and adjusted underlying post-tax earnings 30%; adjusted diluted EPS fell 8% because of a higher share count. It declared a first meaningful annual dividend yielding just over 1.9%, plus a special dividend taking the yield above 3.5% at about 205p. The firm operates 58 UK bowling centres under three brands. It opened three during the period and a fourth since year-end, while refurbishment, rebranding and selective openings and acquisitions support expansion. Customers prepay, enabling immediate reinvestment.

By contrast, UK Oil & Gas Investments raised £16.5m for four wells in 2018 and aims for stable production by early 2019 from the Kimmeridge and Horse Hill discoveries. Results and cash inflows remain uncertain, and its shares fell from 9p in September to around 3.5p. The author favors Hollywood Bowl’s consistent cash flow over UKOG’s speculative prospects.

FMI projects the global surface protection films market to grow at a 5.7% CAGR from 2017–2027, reaching US$2,081.6 million by 2027. The 50–100-micron segment holds nearly 38% of market value, while PE leads base materials with over 40% share; PET has the highest projected CAGR at 6.3%. Construction and interior is expected to represent about 56% of the market by 2027. Western Europe led in 2017 with 30.4%, while Latin America is projected to grow 4.7% annually.

## Summary

This paper documents the **Voice Reasoning Gap (VRG)** — a large, consistent drop in reasoning performance when language models operate through a voice interface rather than text. The gap is most severe on complex, multi-step reasoning: GPT-realtime scores 6.1% on mathematical problems versus 74.8% for GPT-5 (a 68.7-point difference), with voice models scoring 42% lower on average (a 40.4-point macro-average drop). Because voice models already perform well at audio understanding, the authors hypothesize the gap stems from an architectural tension: real-time streaming requires an irreversible, low-latency audio commitment, while deep reasoning depends on iterative, revisable computation.

The authors introduce **VERA (Voice Evaluation of Reasoning Ability)**, a benchmark measuring reasoning under real-time constraints. It contains 2,931 episodes across five tracks adapted from existing text benchmarks: Math (115 AIME problems), Web (1,107 BrowseComp), Science (161 GPQA Diamond), Context (548 MRCR, up to 100K characters), and Factual (1,000 SimpleQA). A four-stage pipeline filters ~22,000 source items for voice suitability, rewrites them in TTS-aware speakable form, validates quality (mean accepted score 9.0/10), and renders audio at 24kHz using Higgs-Audio v2, which varies timbre, tone, and emotion. A 200-episode manual audit confirmed semantic preservation, and speaker-embedding analysis confirmed acoustic diversity.

Evaluation uses WER for speech fidelity and GPT-4o as an LLM judge (three runs, majority vote), calibrated against 1,000 human-rated predictions (97.8% agreement; Gemini-2.5-Flash reached 98.7%). Failures are classified by GPT-5 into 16 error categories. Twelve voice systems (commercial APIs, open models, end-to-end speech generators) were compared with text baselines and a cascade baseline, LiveAnswer, which pairs GPT-5 reasoning with a faster Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct narration model.

Findings show the gap scales with task complexity (Factual: 48.3% vs. 27.4%; Math: 74.8% vs. 6.1%; McNemar's test p < 0.001), and across all voice architectures; within-voice variance across Math scores was 171× smaller than between-modality variance. Diagnostics rule out simple engineering causes: extended thinking mode raised latency 530% yet reduced accuracy (1.7%→1.5%), the LiveAnswer cascade retained a 15.7-point Math gap and failed almost entirely on Context (0.2%) with 10.5s time-to-first-response, and reasoning stayed poor across WERs from 7.9% to 19.8%. Failure signatures differ by architecture: native streaming models produce fluent but incorrect completions, cascades show grounding and logical inconsistencies (e.g., UNSUPPORTED FACT +0.27), and end-to-end models diverge most (Moshi OFF TARGET +0.52; Qwen2.5-Omni NO FINAL ANSWER +0.36). The authors conclude that bridging the gap requires architectures that decouple thinking from speaking through an editable internal state, with research directions including asynchronous reasoning, chunked parallel processing, confidence-gated ASR handoff, answer-first narration, and cross-stage consistency.

Reuters interviews with Rohingya fighters and refugees described ARSA’s Aug. 25, 2017 attacks on dozens of Myanmar police posts in Rakhine state as poorly organized and under-equipped. Hundreds of largely untrained villagers reportedly used knives, sticks, homemade explosives and a few guns; some said they were promised AK-47s but received none. Recruitment involved religious teachers and WhatsApp groups, including some administered overseas, while refugees in Bangladesh expressed support and raised funds for the movement.

The attacks followed a Myanmar military counteroffensive that prompted more than half a million Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. Fighters remained determined to continue despite losses, while other refugees condemned the violence. Myanmar spokesman Zaw Htay said ARSA killed Muslims who cooperated with authorities and that religious scholars recruited followers; ARSA denied killing civilians. Myanmar portrays ARSA as an Islamist movement seeking an Islamic republic, while ARSA says it is fighting for Rohingya rights. Analysts warned that refugee desperation could strengthen the insurgency and facilitate radicalization. It remained unclear how ARSA would rebuild after commanders ordered fighters to abandon their villages and communication groups fell silent.

Seattle overcame an 11-point deficit to beat San Francisco 25-23 in the regular-season finale, finishing 10-5-1 and securing the NFC’s third seed after Atlanta beat New Orleans 38-32. Russell Wilson threw for 258 yards and a touchdown before Pete Carroll pulled him and other key players in the fourth quarter to keep them fresh for the playoffs. Seattle will host Detroit. The loss left the 49ers 2-14, matching the franchise record for season losses. It was Chip Kelly’s final game, and hours later the 49ers announced Kelly and general manager Trent Baalke had been fired.

Ronny Jackson’s confirmation hearing for secretary of veterans affairs was postponed as the Senate reviews allegations of a hostile work environment, improper prescriptions of Ambien and repeated drunkenness on duty. Jackson denied wrongdoing and sought to reschedule the hearing. Trump met with him, defended him and said the nomination was his decision. The White House said Jackson would not withdraw, while some Republicans requested more time and critics questioned the administration’s vetting process.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, the head of its industrial markets group and a former treasurer, and placed Fastow on leave. Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said the change was necessary to restore investor confidence following discussions with the financial community. Fastow had managed the LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment partnerships, which conducted complex financing and hedging arrangements with Enron. The partnerships were dissolved; unwinding them produced a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity.

The SEC began an informal inquiry into the related-party transactions. Enron said it was cooperating, had received no subpoenas, and denied wrongdoing. An earlier analyst conference failed to resolve concerns about the partnerships and Enron’s complex off-balance-sheet financing. Investors also worried that Enron could need to sell assets or issue shares, potentially diluting shareholders and weakening its credit standing. Enron maintained that its operations were normal and that it remained financially strong and liquid.

Enron shares closed at $16.41, down $3.38, or 17%, on October 24 and had fallen roughly 50% since October 16. Other energy-trading companies also declined amid concern that Enron’s troubles could destabilize the market. Analysts gave mixed assessments of the CFO change, viewing it as either a necessary confidence-building step or an admission of concern, while emphasizing the need for greater disclosure. Ratings were cut, including Prudential’s downgrade to “sell,” and shareholder lawsuits alleged asset overvaluation, concealed related-party dealings, potential dilution, and insider trading.

NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x architecture builds on Turing and is designed to improve graphics, ray tracing, AI, compute, and energy efficiency. GA102 and GA104 are its first GA10x GPUs: GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090 and 3080, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and A40, while GA104 powers the RTX 3070. Compared with Turing, Ampere is described as up to 1.7 times faster in raster graphics, up to two times faster in ray tracing, and up to 1.9 times more power-efficient at equivalent performance.

The full GA102 is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process and contains 28.3 billion transistors. It has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, and 112 ROPs. Its 384-bit memory subsystem includes 6,144 KB of L2 cache. GA10x SMs provide dual-datapath FP32 processing, doubling FP32 throughput, along with larger configurable L1/shared memory and twice the shared-memory bandwidth of Turing.

Second-generation RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, run concurrently with graphics or compute workloads, and include an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support structured sparsity, TF32, and BF16. Sparsity can double matrix-operation throughput by skipping zero values, while TF32 provides up to five times the prior generation’s training throughput without code changes.

The RTX 3090 includes 10,496 CUDA Cores, 24 GB of GDDR6X, and DLSS 8K support for 8K HDR gaming. The RTX 3080 is claimed to deliver up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance, while the RTX 3070 rivals the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 and A40 provide 48 GB of GDDR6 each and can be linked with NVLink for 96 GB of combined memory. The A40 is aimed at data-center visual computing, supporting virtualization and combining professional graphics with compute and AI acceleration.

GA10x supports third-generation NVLink and PCIe 4.0. Its GDDR6X implementation uses PAM4 signaling, supporting rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/sec. GDDR6X memory also adds Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transactions and retries them.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based lossless decompression and Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets directly from storage to the GPU. The passage reports up to 100 times better I/O throughput and substantially lower CPU utilization than traditional storage approaches, benefiting game loading and professional datasets.

GA10x also adds DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 support, including 8K at 60 Hz and 4K at 120 Hz. Its fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, while the seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. Enhanced DLSS uses a 9x scaling factor, making 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible on the RTX 3090.

Delta College President Gavin will resign in January to lead a national coalition defending equity in higher education. A prominent defender of community-college DEI work, he cited his career’s focus on equity and concern about partisan interference. Trustees will begin selecting a successor.

The Southern Poverty Law Center released “The Alt-Right on Campus: What Students Need to Know” to help students identify and counter the alt-right, which it says is closely linked to white nationalism. Released before the Charlottesville “Unite the Right” rally, the guide explains prominent movement figures and recommends advance preparation, including informing classmates, using videos or pamphlets, enlisting campus leaders, and avoiding direct engagement, violence, or “spectacle” that would give speakers attention. Distributed to more than 2,000 schools, the guide describes the alt-right, “identarians,” and “race realists” as rebranding of white supremacy and says white-nationalist organizing on campuses grew around 2012.

President Donald Trump’s attendance at the opening of the Mississippi Civil Rights Museum in Jackson drew criticism over his administration’s ties to white supremacy and his failure to condemn Charlottesville’s white supremacists. Some civil rights leaders threatened to boycott. Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba said the museum recognized historical struggles but stressed the need to confront threats to human and civil rights. Trump spoke at a separate, smaller event.

Lumumba is pursuing a “most radical city” agenda centered on people’s assemblies, participatory democracy, Black self-determination and expanded public access. The movement grew from post-Hurricane Katrina activist organizing in the Mississippi Delta and took over city government when his father became mayor. After his father’s death, Lumumba ran for office and became mayor in 2017. The assemblies are presented as an alternative to Trumpian authoritarianism.

During Larry Nassar’s final sentencing hearing, Randall Margraves rushed toward the former sports doctor after Judge Janice Cunningham denied his request for private time with him. Margraves, whose three daughters were sexually abused by Nassar, was blocked, tackled and removed from the Michigan courtroom. He later apologized, saying he had lost control and wanted to help his daughters heal. The judge said she would not fine or jail him for contempt. Nassar admitted sexually assaulting girls under the guise of medical treatment and received sentences ranging from 40 to 175 years for assaults and 60 years for child pornography. More than 200 accusers submitted statements or spoke in two Michigan counties.

The TLV32xx comparator inputs may operate from 200 mV below V− to 200 mV above V+, with input clamp current limited to 10 mA or less. Series input resistance is recommended for transient and fault protection, and signals should not be applied without supply voltage. Unused inputs must not be tied together because internal noise can cause chatter; instead, they should be connected within the valid input range with at least 50 mV differential voltage.

The family provides 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis based on threshold voltage, input offset, and hysteresis voltage. TLV321x devices use push-pull outputs that source and sink current, while TLV322x devices use open-drain outputs that support wired logic, level translation, and external pull-ups from 0 to 5.5 V. Recommended open-drain pull-up current is 100 µA to 1 mA. Outputs must not be connected together or shorted to supply rails; current-limiting series resistors may be needed. Unused push-pull outputs should remain floating, while unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−. Internal ESD protection clamps input voltages to 0.2 V beyond the rails.

TLV321x devices include a power-on reset that holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses 1.65 V. Afterward, the output reflects the differential input state. In basic comparator operation, VIN below VREF produces a low output, and VIN above VREF produces a high output; swapping inputs reverses polarity. Propagation delay depends on transition direction and overdrive, with delays increasing at low overdrive, particularly below 100 mV.

External hysteresis can reduce chatter near the switching threshold and adds to the internal hysteresis. The passage describes three-resistor inverting and two-resistor non-inverting configurations and their trip-voltage calculations. A low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier and comparator to generate a high alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Proper layout requires a low-ESR 0.1 µF supply bypass capacitor, short supply and ground connections, minimal input/output coupling, closely placed input resistors, and, where needed, output damping or controlled-impedance routing for high-speed signals.

In a Supreme Court hearing, the justices considered whether federal prisoner Michael Bowe may challenge the rejection of his request to file a successive habeas petition challenging his firearm conviction. The threshold issue is whether 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3)(E), which bars review of grants or denials of authorization to file successive petitions, applies. Bowe argued that the dismissal was not a denial of authorization and, alternatively, that the provision does not apply to federal prisoners. The government argued that dismissal counts as denial, while an amicus urged that § 2244’s cross-reference makes § 2244(b)(1) applicable to federal inmates. If the Court reaches the merits, Bowe and the government contend that § 2244(b)(1), which expressly references § 2254 proceedings for state inmates, does not apply to his federal habeas claim. The justices gave little indication of their view, and there appeared to be fewer than five votes for applying § 2244(b)(1) to federal inmates.

Python is an open-source, high-level, dynamically typed programming language widely used for algorithmic trading, data analysis, and backtesting. Its readable syntax, scientific libraries, commercial-use packages, and large developer community make it popular for building trading algorithms, statistical models, and execution, risk, and order-management systems. Trading algorithms analyze markets, identify opportunities, execute trades, and manage positions according to predefined rules.

Backtesting applies a coded strategy to historical price data to assess its performance, identify bugs, and gain confidence before live use. It does not guarantee future success, and traders should account for real trading fees that are often omitted from tests. A typical backtest requires importing a framework and obtaining OHLCV data, separating in-sample and out-of-sample data, running and optimizing the strategy, and analyzing results.

Popular Python backtesting tools include PyAlgoTrade, Bt, Backtrader, Fastquant, LEAN, and Zipline. QuantConnect and Backtrader are highlighted for their features: QuantConnect supports multiple languages and fast backtesting but may challenge non-native C# users; Backtrader is beginner-friendly, supports backtesting and live trading, provides performance analyzers, and may struggle with very large datasets. Other frameworks offer features such as paper and live trading, multiple data sources and order types, portfolio rebalancing, browser-based research, and rapid implementation.

Popular Python strategies include trend following, momentum, RSI, and moving-average approaches. The passage also argues that beginners may benefit more from established trading software than from building custom platforms, emphasizing market interpretation, backtesting, and sound strategies over coding.

The team is pleased with a close series victory, though Philadelphia rallied and applied sustained pressure. With another win potentially putting them ahead, Game 3 is considered crucial, but they have a day to rest and prepare. The speaker praises a teammate as a good, upbeat person and an intense, physically strong, hard-nosing winger whose emotion and natural scoring ability provide a needed contribution.

The team has received goals from multiple players, allowing it to play freely, remain composed and emphasize sound defense, positioning, goaltending and shot-blocking. Philadelphia briefly gained momentum through consecutive penalties and power-play goals, including one by Brind’Amour, before the team regained control.

Philadelphia is described as an excellent road team likely to play strongly in Game 3, making disciplined hockey and proper preparation essential. The speaker credits the team’s experience from lengthy playoff runs over the past two years for its composure. He also acknowledges that the team must improve its penalty killing after allowing two power-play goals on strong shots and deflections.

The Kentucky Supreme Court held that Bunch had 55% active occupational disability immediately before his 1977 work-related injury, so the Special Fund was not liable for that portion. The Board had assigned 15% of his total disability to the employer and 30% to the Special Fund, finding that the 1977 injury alone would not have caused his complete disability. The Court affirmed the Board’s decision, reversed the Court of Appeals, and overruled contrary language in the cited cases.

Electronic Arts announced it will go private in a $55 billion all-cash deal — the largest leveraged buyout in history — backed by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, with shareholders receiving a roughly 25% premium. CEO and chairman Andrew Wilson, who joined EA in 2000 and has led it since 2013, will remain CEO. Observers called the price fair given few alternative buyers and a difficult antitrust landscape. Going private relieves Wilson of shareholder pressure, which followed a nearly 17% single-day share decline after EA cut its fiscal-year outlook amid challenges with "EA Sports FC," but his new owners could apply their own pressure. EA's shares rallied ahead of the October 10 release of "Battlefield 6," while "Grand Theft Auto VI" was postponed to May 2026. Analysts cited EA's reliance on aging franchises like "The Sims" and "Madden NFL" and struggles in mobile gaming, while Wilson pointed to generative AI and potential esports expansion in Saudi Arabia.

The lecture extends data-structure analysis beyond the flat RAM model to realistic memory hierarchies consisting of caches, main memory, disks, and slower levels. Data structures should maximize work in fast cache and minimize transfers to deeper levels.

The external memory, or I/O, model abstracts the hierarchy into an infinitely large, slow disk and an infinitely fast cache. Computation and cache access are free; the cost is the number of block transfers between disk and cache. Disk and cache are divided into blocks of size \(B\), and the cache has total size \(M\). Scanning \(N\) items costs \(\lceil N/B\rceil\) transfers. B-trees with branching factor \(B+1\) support search in optimal comparison-model time \(\Theta(\log_{B+1} N)\), as each block yields at most \(\log(B+1)\) bits of information. Their insertion and deletion bounds are not optimal. The optimal comparison-model sorting bound is \(O((N/B)\log_{M/B}(N/B))\). Optimal permutation takes the minimum of the sorting bound and \(N\), under the indivisible-word assumption. Buffer trees attain the sorting bound divided by \(N\) per amortized operation, supporting batched updates, delayed queries, flushing, and priority queues with constant-time find-min.

The cache-oblivious model assumes an algorithm does not know the block size \(B\) or cache size \(M\). It writes like a RAM algorithm, while the cache and replacement policy are managed automatically. Analysis may assume optimal offline replacement; LRU and FIFO are within constant factors under suitable cache-size comparisons. A cache-oblivious algorithm is efficient simultaneously for all \(B\) and \(M\), including multilevel and changing hierarchies.

Cache-oblivious scans still cost \(O(\lceil N/B\rceil)\), and searches, insertions, and deletions can achieve \(O(\log_{B+1} N)\) without knowing \(B\). Cache-oblivious permutation cannot attain the minimum of the sorting bound and \(N\), because choosing between them requires knowing the relationship among \(B\), \(M\), and \(N\). A lower bound gives a best search-tree constant factor of \(\log_2 e\approx1.44\), while the lecture’s construction achieves 4. Cache-oblivious priority queues attain the optimal external-memory bound under the tall-cache assumption, which requires \(M\) to grow faster than \(B^{1+\epsilon}\).

For static search, the lecture lays out a perfect balanced binary search tree in van Emde Boas order. The tree is recursively divided at its middle level, each resulting subtree is recursively laid out, and the layouts are concatenated. Any root-to-leaf path visits \(O(\log_B N)\) blocks for every block size. In the analysis, recursive subtrees smaller than \(B\) occupy at most two blocks, while each recursion level makes \(\Theta(\log B)\) vertical progress, yielding at most \(4\log_B N\) transfers for \(B>1\).

Dynamic cache-oblivious search uses order file maintenance as a deferred black box. Order file maintenance stores ordered elements in a linear array with constant-sized gaps, supporting insertion and deletion through shifts in amortized \(O(\log^2 N)\) time, conjectured to be optimal. The lecture combines this structure with a van Emde Boas layout and cross-links; internal nodes store subtree maxima. Search uses the static tree’s \(O(\log_B N)\) bound, while updates modify the ordered file and propagate new maxima in postorder.

Initially this gives an update bound of \(O(\log_B N+\log^2 N/B)\). Postorder traversal lets alternating small subtrees share cached blocks, and only ancestors of the updated region require additional transfers. A final indirection layer stores representative elements in the upper tree and groups the remaining items into chunks of roughly \(\log N\). Chunks are scanned, split, and merged as in a B-tree. Because upper-level updates occur only after many lower-level changes, the \(\log^2 N\) update term is amortized away, yielding cache-oblivious search, insertion, and deletion bounds of \(O(\log_B N)\).

Colorado Boy Scout Troop 1532, formed in 2014 by Dr. P.J. Parmar through his Denver-area refugee clinic, is composed almost entirely of refugees from places including Africa, Burma, Rwanda and Nepal. The troop helps children adjust to American culture, learn skills, and find a safe place where they can be themselves while building discipline, respect and resilience. Because many families lack transportation and parents work long, irregular hours, the group mainly meets for camping trips.

Maintaining adult leaders and membership, earning merit badges and advancing in rank remain difficult. Some scouts have faced discipline issues, including smoking and alleged theft, and leaders say refugees receive less benefit of the doubt. The program is viewed as a model for other Boy Scout groups. Jean Tuyishime and his brother Moise, born in a Rwandan refugee camp before moving to the Denver area in 2014, said their leaders have taught them discipline and respect; Jean wants to become a leader and help other children.

The Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the European Central Bank (ECB) are assessing the feasibility of connecting their instant payment systems — the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) network and the Eurosystem's TIPS platform — to enable cross-border transfers between the two currency areas in seconds. An exploratory phase running through 2026 will examine legal and compliance issues, operational frameworks, settlement risk, and liquidity management, with cybersecurity and regulatory alignment among the key challenges. The SNB says the link would reduce reliance on slower, more costly correspondent banking, ease cross-currency payment friction, and support G20 goals of faster, more transparent global payments; for Switzerland it would mean closer integration with EU payment infrastructure without adopting the euro. The ECB views the project as consistent with its strategy of improving cross-border payment interoperability and expanding TIPS' global reach. If successful, it could set a precedent for further links between central bank instant payment systems. The passage also lists related news headlines covering markets, energy, technology and regulation (e.g., BRICS rupee bond, BBVA's Sabadell bid, U.S. stocks, Iran-Russia nuclear deal, OpenAI parental controls) and describes the publication as a global financial intelligence source with offices in London, Lagos, Barcelona, Miami and Sharjah.

The November 17, 2001 Commissioner.COM fantasy football report contains SportsLine promotions and links, a “Luccis Losers” roster with eight active and seven reserve players, and an injury update on Cameron Cleeland, Rob Johnson, and Kurt Warner. It provides extensive NFL player news on suspensions, injuries, expected starters, returns, and performance, along with fantasy start/bench advice. Notable updates include Correll Buckhalter and Jamal Lewis serving suspensions, Edgerrin James being ruled out for the season with a torn ACL, and Emmitt Smith, Steve McNair, Chris Weinke, and Tyrone Wheatley facing injury-related uncertainty.

Vancouver’s coach expressed confidence in the team’s core, leadership and accountability heading into another Stanley Cup Final game in Boston. He praised Boston as a strong opponent and said Vancouver’s offensive struggles were a team-wide execution issue, not a goaltending problem. He noted Boston’s aggressive goalie and discussed generating more pucks, traffic and net preference, while emphasizing that his top players must perform to their standards. The coach said both teams had faced adversity and described Vancouver’s previous Boston games as increasingly emotional as the outcome shifted. He also explained that a goalie change against Chicago was intended to change momentum after two playoff losses, praised Roberto’s play, and maintained confidence in the power play.

ChatGPT is a conversational AI system from OpenAI that can support trading by analyzing market data, brainstorming strategies, and generating Python code for backtests. Its outputs may be incomplete or incorrect, so users should provide clear context, request refinements, and independently verify results.

In one example, ChatGPT generated and backtested a Bollinger Bands mean-reversion strategy using pandas, NumPy, yfinance, and Matplotlib. The unmodified code was run on adjusted SPY data since inception. Reported results included a 3.20% CAGR, 326 trades, and 45.63% time in the market.

The article cautions that ChatGPT is not a trading platform, does not provide financial advice or make investment decisions, and cannot guarantee profitable strategies. It is best used as a starting point for developing and refining traders’ own models and strategies.

Leeds United lost 1-0 to Wolves at Elland Road and slipped to seventh in the play-off standings. Nouha Dicko scored in the 39th minute after Leeds defender Pontus Jansson’s forward charge left the team exposed. Although Leeds improved after half-time and applied pressure, they managed only one effort on target and failed to equalise despite several chances. Goalkeeper Rob Green made important saves, while Wolves’ late time-wearing disrupted Leeds’ momentum. Leeds may now need to win their remaining three matches to secure a play-off place.

The team plans to focus on generating more rebounds and shots while staying disciplined despite mistakes. Coaches believe the team played well and can build on that performance, emphasizing moving forward, preparing for St. Louis, and relying on established chemistry, lineup continuity, and a shared system.

Gold climbed above $4,000 per ounce as weak U.S. retail and manufacturing data fueled expectations of Federal Reserve easing, with traders anticipating possible rate cuts by early 2026. Falling yields, a softer dollar, slower global growth, geopolitical tensions, fiscal pressures and central-bank buying strengthened demand for gold as a safe store of value. Analysts warned that hawkish Fed signals or stronger U.S. growth could trigger short-term corrections, but a sustained rally could reshape 2025 asset allocation.

Michael Bowe, sentenced to 24 years for a 2008 armored-car robbery and related federal offenses, seeks habeas relief from his Section 924(c) firearm conviction. He argues that later Supreme Court rulings excluding conspiracy and attempted Hobbs Act robbery from “crimes of violence” require vacating that conviction.

Bowe must overcome two procedural barriers. First, he argues that 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3)(E), which bars Supreme Court review of decisions permitting successive habeas petitions, applies only to state inmates; the government says Section 2255(h) incorporates its gatekeeping requirements for federal inmates as well. Bowe also raises an exceptions-clause challenge, noting that the Supreme Court earlier rejected his attempt to invoke original habeas jurisdiction. Second, he challenges the 11th Circuit’s application of Section 2244(b)(1), which restricts repeated claims by state inmates. The government agrees that the provision applies only to state inmates but suggests that the abuse-of-the-writ doctrine could similarly limit repetitive federal petitions. The Supreme Court appointed an amicus to defend the appeals court’s position.

After the Browns traded Joe Flacco, Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders remained the team’s only active quarterbacks. Coach Kevin Stefanski had not decided on a backup, saying he would let the week play out. Sanders, the inactive emergency quarterback for the first five games, said he was thankful for whatever role he received and saw “light at the end of the tunnel.” He praised Gabriel’s preparation and remained positive after critical comments from ESPN analyst Rex Ryan. Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees also praised Sanders’ growth, preparation, and understanding of Cleveland’s offense. Sanders said he was mindful that his playful personality could be misinterpreted.

Dean Smith’s “Four Corner” offense, a recognizable spread offense for North Carolina, requires a skilled ballhandler capable of one-on-one play. Spreading players across the corners creates isolation opportunities, lets one player control the game, reduces turnovers and opponents’ possessions, and provides options through drives, kick-outs, return passes, back cuts, and drop passes. When return passes to O1 are denied, O2 or O3 exchanges positions with O1 and attacks the basket.

Air Canada apologized and offered compensation after bumping 10-year-old Brett Doyle from an oversold flight from Charlottetown to Montreal, his father said. The family ultimately reached Montreal and continued to Costa Rica. Air Canada gave them a C$2,500 voucher after a newspaper reported the case and said it was investigating what went wrong. The incident drew attention amid outrage over airline overbooking following the forceful removal of a 69-year-old United passenger in Chicago.

The passage praises the Army’s and civil authorities’ constructive statesmanship in the Philippine Islands and the many Filipinos who accepted new conditions and cooperated for the islands’ welfare. It argues that although the Army has been reduced to the legal minimum, it must remain highly efficient, with continued small-unit maneuvers, rigorous individual and collective training, and special attention to marksmanship, since modern warfare depends on the individual soldier. It urges passage of legislation establishing a general staff and reorganizing supply departments, continued development of West Point officers through training and merit, and prompt action on militia reorganization, including defining the National Guard’s relationship to other military forces and replacing obsolete laws. Worn cavalry and artillery horses should be used for light work and humanely euthanized when necessary.

The passage also calls for improved naval marksmanship and gunnery, adequate practice funding, annual additions to the Navy, and highly efficient ships and personnel. A strong navy is presented as necessary to support American foreign policies, make the isthmian canal effective, and back the Monroe Doctrine, while serving as a guaranty of peace. It warns that ships and trained crews cannot be improvised after war begins, emphasizing the need for sufficient numbers of highly skilled sailors and sea mechanics.

Coaches should evaluate players’ abilities, skills, temperaments, and preferences before assigning positions, using observation, drills, experimentation, player discussions, outside reviews, scrimmages, and progress monitoring. Basic requirements include hand skills and willingness for goalkeepers; marking and goal-side awareness for defenders; offensive and defensive readiness and stamina for midfielders; and scoring ability and an attacking mindset for forwards.

After selecting a formation and naming its positions, coaches should diagram the formation, indicate attack and defensive goals, teach players the names and relative locations, and place them in position during practice. Teams should move collectively between attack and defense while maintaining their shape. Functional training should clarify the responsibilities of each role.

Players should not be typecast or restricted to one position; all should be exposed to all roles and learn every position. Coaches must balance competitive needs with equal playing time, position exposure, skill development, and small-sided games. Playing-time charts can help ensure equality, though coaches may sometimes place less-skilled players at positions such as right back or left wing. Players’ long-term potential may not be immediately apparent.

Rush Bowls, a Colorado chain, opened its first St. Louis-area shop in the Central West End. Customers order smoothies and fruit bowls at the counter. Seventeen basic smoothies cost $6.50, while four bowl categories—Enlightened, acai, seasonal, and Comfort Bowls—cost $7.95. Bowls can include granola, honey, peanut butter, jelly, and other toppings. The shop is very loud because of its blenders and has limited seating. Rush Bowls is aimed at customers seeking a healthy meal before or after exercise, with convenient access to Forest Park, Steel Wheels, and LimeBike.

EUR/USD extended its monthly decline as weaker-than-expected Eurozone data weighed on the euro. Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s hawkish testimony, supporting interest-rate increases and balance-sheet reduction as rates normalize, boosted the dollar. After falling below its 50-day moving average, EUR/USD approached 1.0500 support; further downside could target December–January lows near 1.0350.

The study examines digital transformation in Ethiopian higher education within the context of global efforts to expand equitable, quality education through ICT. It highlights substantial digital-access disparities between developed countries and least developed countries, along with inadequate internet and ICT infrastructure in many African higher education institutions. Ethiopia has ambitious national development and digitalization strategies, but its internet penetration, telecommunications services, electricity access, and institutional digital infrastructure remain limited.

Using a qualitative document and thematic analysis methodology, the study reviews continental, national, and institutional policies and strategies, publicly available reports, and the author’s professional experience. Deductive thematic analysis identified policies and initiatives supporting digital transformation, current digitalization practices, and barriers to implementation.

Ethiopian development plans, including the Growth and Transformation Plan II, Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda, Digital Ethiopia 2025, and Ten-Year Development Plan, identify ICT as important for economic growth and inclusion. Before 2018, no policies directly addressed digital transformation in higher education. The subsequent Ministry of Science and Higher Education developed national ICT policies and strategies for higher education and TVET, a digital skills action plan, infrastructure targets, and an institutional ICT policy for universities to customize. Following the ministry’s 2021 merger back into the Ministry of Education, the future direction of digitalization became less predictable.

Major initiatives include the Ethiopian Education and Research Network, the National Academic Digital Repository of Ethiopia, and the National Academic Digital Library of Ethiopia. Their services and coverage remain limited. University digitalization has primarily supported routine administration and service delivery through computers and information systems, while innovation in digital teaching, learning, and research remains in its infancy. COVID-19 exposed inadequate readiness for online learning. Subsequent measures included authorization for fully online degrees, efforts to improve learning management systems, implementation of a higher education management information system, and an introductory emerging-technologies course.

Major barriers include poor, expensive, and unreliable internet connectivity; insufficient campus bandwidth; electricity disruptions; weak ICT infrastructure; shortages of skilled ICT personnel, educators, and students; inadequate training opportunities; and resistance to poorly contextualized change. The findings conclude that policies alone are insufficient. Successful digitalization requires reliable and affordable internet, robust infrastructure, professional digital-skills development, effective leadership and governance, and sustained implementation of national and institutional strategies.

WTI crude futures fell 46 cents to $52.72 a barrel as rising US shale output and easing geopolitical tensions pressured an oversupplied market. US drillers added 11 oil rigs, while crude production reached 9.24 million barrels per day. Reduced Libyan output and hopes of extending OPEC production cuts offered some support.

Dita Von Teese unveiled her Scandalwood fragrance at Bergdorf Goodman. Other stories covered Bergdorf’s scalp-facial salon, New York holiday windows, Neiman Marcus’s first comparable-store sales increase in eight quarters, lenders’ concerns about luxury retailers, Linda Fargo, Saks Fifth Avenue’s $11 million lawsuit against John Barrett, and Barbara Taylor Bradford.
