Tomas Gajowniczek, 37, is on trial for the attempted murder of Alicja Kalinowska, 30, and intentionally or recklessly causing her serious harm at their Dublin home on June 16, 2016. He denies guilt, and the jury must decide whether he is not guilty by reason of insanity.

The prosecution said Gajowniczek intended to kill Kalinowska, whom he accused of cheating on him, after stuffing underwear in her mouth, pinching her nose and beating her with a hammer. It argued that his cannabis use and resulting intoxication did not constitute a mental disorder under the Criminal Law (Insanity) Act 2006.

The defence argued that he had psychosis and a disease of the mind, believing Kalinowska was drugging him and their baby and fearing tax fraud. Defence psychiatrist Dr Conor O’Neill disputed the prosecution’s drug-induced psychosis account. The jury of six men and six women will receive Justice Patrick McCarthy’s final directions.

MCW’s “Spring Fever” on April 22 at MCW Arena in Joppa, Maryland, features a 4 p.m. meet-and-greet, 7:30 p.m. action, and Rey Mysterio. Matches include vacant tag titles, Sean Studd and Andy Vineberg versus Bruiser, Dante Caballero’s scramble defense, and several singles and tag bouts.

In 1850, Hawaiian commissioners Prince Alexander and Lott Kamehameha met British Prime Minister Lord Palmerston in England. Palmerston urged Hawaiians to maintain proper government and preserve independence but suggested a U.S. protectorate or annexation if they could not, citing their proximity to California and Oregon, economic dependence on U.S. markets, and likely replacement of the native population by U.S. immigrants.

Hawaiian sovereignty was temporarily seized by Britain in 1843, then restored; Britain and France subsequently recognized Hawaiian independence, though the United States declined to join the agreement. French forces occupied government buildings in Honolulu in 1849 and returned in 1851, threatening bombardment. Fearing French rule, King Kamehameha III then ceded Hawaiian sovereignty to the United States, conditional on formal U.S. possession after the first hostile French shot. The French withdrew, and later relations became conciliatory. The cession document was returned to Hawaii in 1851. U.S. negotiations in 1854 produced only a proposed protectorate, which Secretary of State William Marcy rejected.

Pierce enclosed a 1870 review of Hawaiian agriculture and commerce and referred to an 1867 map. He added that continued failure of annexation sustained consideration of reciprocity, but U.S. sugar-state interests obstructed a treaty. In 1873, Secretary Hamilton Fish turned from reciprocity toward annexation.

Empirical studies from 2000–2020 and a 1973–2014 CFA report found that stocks with high short interest tend to have weaker future returns than stocks with low short interest. Short interest is the percentage of outstanding shares sold short, while the short-interest ratio estimates the average days needed to cover short positions. Broker-dealers report short positions twice monthly to FINRA, and data are available through sources such as Seeking Alpha and NYSE files.

A short squeeze occurs when short sellers must buy shares back as prices rise, potentially creating explosive demand. GameStop’s 2021 squeeze is cited as a dramatic example. Although traders can profit from squeezes, they are rare, random, and difficult to predict; high short interest does not necessarily trigger one. Short selling is therefore considered difficult and generally unfavorable over the long term, though it may support strategies such as pairs trading and portfolio risk mitigation.

The disclosure describes a waveguide display for virtual, augmented, mixed-reality, or combined near-eye displays. A display assembly generates image light with a source assembly, conditions and optionally scans the light through an optics system, and directs it into an output waveguide for presentation to the user. Embodiments may use a narrow source waveguide that expands the image light in one dimension and is rotated by an actuator assembly. Coupling and decoupling elements, such as diffraction or holographic gratings, transfer image light into and out of the waveguides using total internal reflection.

The light source may use MicroLEDs or other LEDs in linear, curved, stacked, dense two-dimensional, or sparse two-dimensional arrays. Elements may emit the same or different wavelength ranges. Optical isolators and spacing between elements reduce optical interference and crosstalk. A controller divides display content into sections, sequentially activates source elements, and controls scanning mirrors or source-waveguide rotation so the user’s eye integrates the sections into an image. The disclosed designs address brightness, resolution, field of view, compactness, and scanning constraints associated with near-eye MicroLED displays.

The paper argues that single-reward formulations inadequately represent agents with multiple, conflicting objectives and that independent multi-objective solutions fail to capture strategic interactions among agents. It introduces Multi-Objective Markov Games (MOMG) with vectorial rewards and the Pareto-Nash Equilibrium (PNE), combining Nash stability with Pareto optimality, and proves that PNEs exist in finite MOMGs. It also establishes equivalence between MOMG PNEs and the union of Nash equilibria from linearly scalarized games, enabling use of existing single-objective solvers. Finally, it examines weaker concepts, including Weak PNE and Pareto Correlated Equilibrium, and develops a decentralized online learning algorithm with provable convergence to a PCE.

A hockey player discusses being disappointed to leave the lineup, accepting the coach’s decision, and focusing on solid all-around play and strong defense. He expects a tough game against a disciplined, hard-working team and says reaching the Stanley Cup has made the opportunity less frustrating.

Colorado’s aggressive counterattacking and pressure on breakouts created difficulties, while the speaker’s team struggled with poor ice, lacked crisp play, and failed to adapt despite a late scoring opportunity.

Indian shares rose Monday, ending a five-day losing streak, as global market gains and weak U.S. inflation data eased rate-hike concerns. The NSE index gained 0.83%, BSE 0.82%, and Nifty Bank 0.74%. DLF surged up to 13.7% amid rental-unit deal talks, while Sun Pharma and BPCL fell after disappointing quarterly results.

Jason Keidel weighs concerns that Cleveland may be “pseudo-tanking” as the NBA playoffs begin, citing the Cavaliers’ 109–108 win over Indiana, declining results after strong January starts, and 22nd-ranked defense. He points to alleged roster discord, Kyrie Irving’s reduced production, Kevin Love’s outsider status, Tyronn Lue’s perceived lack of authority, and LeBron James’s heavy workload and exhaustion.

Despite these concerns, Keidel argues Cleveland should not be underestimated. The team is atypically healthy, and LeBron has reached the NBA Finals in all five postseason appearances as the No. 2 seed, including six straight Finals trips overall. Another appearance would make him the first to reach seven consecutive Finals since Bill Russell. His history of advancing weaker teams, 18 consecutive first-round playoff victories, and the Cavaliers’ likely matchup with last year’s defeated opponent, the Warriors, make them dangerous through June.

German consumer inflation unexpectedly rose 2.2% year over year in May, above the 1.9% forecast and the highest since February 2017. Energy prices, up 5.2%, were the main driver; food rose 3.5% and services 1.9%, suggesting subdued core inflation. The ECB is expected to maintain policy, with asset purchases likely extended through year-end at its June meeting amid eurozone slowdown concerns and Italian political uncertainty.

Tesla’s stock has risen more than 1,000% over five years as the company advances toward making electric vehicles and solar energy affordable to average consumers. The Model 3 generated more than 400,000 preorders and 1,800 daily orders, while revenue rose 119.7% year over year, automotive revenue increased 93%, and losses narrowed. Tesla also held $3 billion in cash, began producing battery packs at its Nevada Gigafactory, and projected increasing annual vehicle production from 100,000 to 500,000.

However, Tesla remained unprofitable, paid no dividend, and had a $56.9 billion valuation despite far lower revenue and earnings than Ford, General Motors, and BMW. Its planned $1.8 billion bond offering would bring long-term debt to roughly $9 billion, while established automakers offered competing electric vehicles and greater resources.

The passage argues that Tesla should be evaluated as a renewable-energy technology company rather than solely against automakers, with its trajectory and potential economies of scale more important than current valuations. Nevertheless, delays, competition, or other setbacks could hurt the company. The conclusion is cautiously optimistic but warns that Tesla is no longer an obvious value and could experience a stock-price pullback.

Star Bulk Carriers (SBLK) is a dry bulk shipping company whose fleet is weighted toward Capesize and Panamax vessels. After weakness caused by slower Brazilian iron ore exports, Capesize rates more than doubled over 10 days in April 2018. SBLK recently acquired 16 vessels built between 2010 and 2017 by assuming $310 million of debt and issuing 10.5 million shares, effectively paying $433 million for a fleet valued at $441 million. The transaction expanded its fleet from 74 to 90 ships, increased cargo capacity by 24%, reduced average fleet age from eight years to seven, and diluted equity by 14%. The analyst described the acquisition as accretive. SBLK’s estimated NAV is $12.60 per share and could rise to $15.40 if fleet values increase by 10%. Value Investor’s Edge considers SBLK one of its largest positions and has a $15 per-share fair-value target, representing 24% upside, citing the company’s Capesize exposure, larger publicly traded dry bulk fleet, and potential industry leadership.

The incoming president accepts the responsibilities of office with humility and invokes divine guidance. He pledges to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution, which he identifies as the guide for government. Because federal power is limited, he vows to exercise only delegated or clearly implied powers, while states must likewise respect the limits of their reserved authority. He supports majorities ruling within constitutional limits, protecting minorities’ rights, and using the qualified presidential veto to guard against unconstitutional legislation.

He regards the federal Union as a source of liberty, equality, prosperity, peace, and individual opportunity. To preserve it, he calls for observance of the constitutional compromises, rejection of sectional jealousies, just laws, and strict limits on federal power. He opposes institutions that would place government at the service of sections, classes, or individuals and advocates economy in public spending, repayment of public debt, and restoration of state and federal credit.

On taxation, he supports tariffs primarily for revenue, with only moderate discrimination providing incidental protection to domestic interests. He rejects taxing one industry or class for another’s benefit and urges equitable taxation of luxuries and necessities. Mutual concession among competing interests should guide revenue legislation.

He supports the proposed annexation of Texas as a peaceful agreement between independent powers, arguing that it would promote trade, security, peace, and development without burdening existing states with Texas’s local institutions. He also asserts a clear U.S. title to Oregon and supports extending republican institutions and legal protection to American settlers there while respecting treaty obligations.

In foreign relations, he intends to respect other nations’ rights, pursue exact justice, avoid harmful alliances, and expand commerce through peaceful relations. He demands strict accountability from public officers, especially those handling government revenue, and vows to govern impartially as president of all Americans while respecting dissenting opinions.

U.S. stocks opened nearly flat after an explosion at New York’s Port Authority; police detained one suspect, and authorities said a possible pipe bomb had detonated underground. Crypto-linked shares rose 10%–24%, while bitcoin futures jumped over 20% in their U.S. debut. November’s addition of 228,000 jobs supported expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, though sluggish wages raised doubts about three hikes in 2018. Bluebird Bio gained 19.2% after positive early-stage results for an experimental gene-modifying immunotherapy; Celgene rose 2.4%.

Carbon-related spin defects were created in hBN by ^13C ion implantation and high-temperature annealing. Confocal photoluminescence showed isolated emitters with a peak near 600 nm, while photon correlation (g²(0) = 0.21) confirmed single-defect emission. One electron spin in each defect pair couples strongly to a ^13C nuclear spin, forming a four-level, two-qubit subsystem controlled by microwave and radiofrequency pulses. ODMR showed hyperfine-split resonances separated by about 290 MHz, while ODNMR identified nuclear transitions at 141 and 145 MHz and nuclear Rabi oscillations near 0.8 MHz at 73.5 mT.

CPMG dynamical decoupling extended coherence from a Hahn-echo T₂ of 148 ± 8 ns to 38 ± 10 µs with 1024 refocusing pulses, following a power-law dependence with exponent 0.77 ± 0.09.

Calibrated selective microwave and radiofrequency drives enabled local and nonlocal electron–nuclear gates. Following optical initialization, a SWAP sequence transferred polarization to the nucleus. Nonlocal gates then generated all four Bell states, whose reconstructed density matrices supported successful state preparation and characterization.

STAT’s Health Care Inc. newsletter covers pressure on doctors not to test or report infections, hospitals penalized for reporting infections, and a judge siding with Humana against a 2023 Medicare Advantage audit rule. Headlines also address drug tariffs, vaccines, FDA weight-loss policy, and Huntington’s treatments.

MOMO shares rose more than 15% after beating Q1 sales and profit estimates and projecting 51%–55% Q2 revenue growth. Up nearly 85% in 2018, the stock has formed a cup-shaped base and shown a constructive breakout from a handle. The author favors a modified fence strategy: buying the July $45/$50 call spread and selling the July $40/$35 put spread for a $1.10 debit. At a $44.85 share price, the strategy offers limited risk, potential accumulation at lower prices, and a projected $3.90 profit if MOMO exceeds $50 at July expiration. Accounts managed by Christopher Tyler hold MOMO stock and derivatives; the analysis is educational, and trading risks remain the individual investor’s responsibility.

The Santa Barbara Public Library System will offer free spelling workshops in July and August, with daytime classes for students entering seventh grade and adults and evening classes for adults. Preregistration is encouraged; walk-ins are welcome.

Quinstreet Inc. (QNST) rose 38.91% in its latest session. Analysts’ mean 52-week target is $9.88, based on three opinions, with targets ranging from $8.50 to $12.50 versus a $12.96 close. Brokerage recommendations include one Buy, one Outperform, and one Underperform; its ABR is 2, ranking 169th among 265 companies in its industry. Its ATR-14 is 0.67, weekly volatility is 9.10%, monthly volatility is 6.30%, and RSI is 83.22. Market capitalization is $575.55 million, with 44.41 million shares outstanding. Previous-session volume was 3.69 million shares, compared with an average of 433.51 million.

The lecture introduces batch arguments (BARGs), also called SNARGs for BatchNP, which let a prover convince a verifier that multiple NP statements are true using one proof. A BARG consists of generator, prover, and verifier algorithms; it is succinct when its proof is smaller than the combined witnesses. It must satisfy completeness and soundness against non-uniform cheating provers.

The lecture motivates BARGs as building blocks for SNARGs for all P, analogous to aggregated signatures and batch interactive proofs. It also discusses the Gentry–Wichs lower bound: under falsifiable assumptions, SNARGs for time-hard languages cannot have proofs significantly shorter than the logarithm of the decision time, making highly succinct SNARGs for general NP difficult.

The main result is a BARG construction from learning with errors. Its proof size depends polynomially on the relation-circuit size, while verification is roughly linear in the total instance length plus terms depending on the circuit size, security parameter, and logarithm of the batch size.

Construction begins with a simplified Kilian protocol. The prover creates a PCP proof for each statement, arranges them as a matrix, hashes every column, and lets the verifier issue one PCP query before opening the queried columns across all proofs. To make the protocol non-interactive, the lecture introduces correlation-intractable hashes and rewrites the verifier’s query as the hash of the column-hash vector, requiring a public-coin PCP.

Because compressing hashes may have many preimages, the proof uses a somewhere-statistically-binding hash built from fully homomorphic encryption. Its key hides a selected index, equal hashes bind the input at that index, and a trapdoor enables extraction. In the soundness hybrid, the selected row is fixed to a false statement; key indistinguishability permits changing the CRS, and extraction recovers that row’s PCP. Acceptance then yields an input/output pair forbidden by the correlation-intractable hash, contradicting soundness.

Tesla, Inc. reported in a Form 8-K that it published a press release on July 2, 2022, furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The release was attached as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” for Section 18 purposes. CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report on July 5, 2022.

AAPL is Apple Inc.’s Nasdaq ticker symbol. Apple began trading on Nasdaq on December 12, 1980, and is known for products including the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, Apple TV, HomePod, software, and services. AAPL shares can be bought through online or full-service brokers, but investors should research the stock, understand market risks, and consider the broker’s risk profile.

AAPL’s average return over the past five years is reported as approximately 16.1%. It pays an annual dividend of $0.82 per share, subject to change by Apple’s board. The passage lists an all-time high of $233.47, reached on October 3, 2018. Shares do not expire and may be held indefinitely. AAPL is subject to capital-gains tax when sold; in the U.S., short-term gains are taxed at the ordinary income rate and long-term gains at a lower rate. Foreign investors may have 15–35% withheld from dividends, depending on tax agreements and local law.

Regular trading hours are 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET, although AAPL also trades actively before and after the official session. It cannot be traded 24 hours a day. AAPL options are available, but the options market is described as highly competitive and zero-sum. A related volatility index, VXAPL, is available through CBOE.

Day, swing, and scalping are possible; swing trades may last days or weeks, while scalping targets minute- or second-level movements. The passage does not recommend scalping. Effective trading requires market knowledge, quick analysis, awareness of news and events, a trading plan, disciplined risk management, and backtesting. Strategies and time frames should suit each trader’s abilities and risk tolerance.

AAPL’s popularity is attributed to Apple’s strong fundamentals, recognizable products, long record of shareholder returns, and historical upward performance. Becoming a millionaire through AAPL is possible but highly unlikely, and most traders fail. Successful traders are described as systematic, patient, rational, disciplined, and comfortable making decisions. When selling AAPL, investors should consider financial goals, valuation, diversification, fundamentals, market conditions, taxes, personal circumstances, psychology, performance, and risk tolerance.

The passage presents a backtested “Stay Rich Portfolio” for people who have achieved financial independence and want to preserve their wealth, emphasizing that preservation requires different strategies than wealth creation. Drawdowns are not necessarily permanent losses, and all asset classes experienced significant declines from 1926–2019. US and foreign stocks offered the strongest long-term return-to-drawdown ratios, while global diversification reduced maximum drawdowns only modestly. The moderately conservative portfolio uses liquid, diversified ETFs across asset classes, including stocks, inflation-protected Treasury securities, and corporate bonds. Approximately 75% is invested in the US and 25% in foreign markets, with additional indirect foreign exposure through US companies.

The passage argues that revolutionary Communist regimes produce large refugee flows by imposing sweeping social changes that conflict with established values and habits. It cites the hardship of more than one million Chinese residents in Vietnam and reports that over six million people had fled Marxist-governed countries by the end of 1978. Compared with refugees leaving other autocracies, the passage presents communist revolution as a particularly severe driver of displacement.

It contends that radical totalitarian governments are unlikely to reform themselves, while liberalization and democratization appear more plausible in countries such as Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Taiwan, South Korea, and Zaire. It recommends U.S. support for gradual political opening, informed by historical experience and directed toward governments not fighting armed adversaries.

The passage warns that victorious Marxist insurgencies are unlikely to become democratic and instead risk producing totalitarian rule. It distinguishes authentic democratic revolutionaries by their commitment to consent, popular participation, and elections, contrasting them with leaders who postpone elections. Finally, it treats revolutionary leaders’ characterization of the United States as imperialism, racism, and genocide as evidence that they are not democratic allies.

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will start against the Chargers on Sunday after missing two games with a sprained left knee. Daniels practiced in full with a nonrestrictive black brace and was medically cleared Wednesday. The Chargers have allowed the NFL’s third-most scramble yards this season, while Daniels recorded 570 scramble yards as a rookie in 2024. Backup Mariota compiled 729 passing yards, seven touchdowns and one interception in four relief games over the past two seasons. Daniels said he will be smarter after being hit in the knee but remains committed to winning.

The lecture reviews transport operations needed to define tensorial derivatives on curved manifolds. Requiring transport to preserve the metric leads to the covariant derivative, while sliding vectors along a vector field defines the Lie derivative. Connection terms cancel in the Lie derivative, making it tensorial despite its expression using partial derivatives. A Killing vector is one whose flow leaves the metric invariant; its existence corresponds to metric symmetry, such as independence from a time coordinate.

Tensor densities are then introduced. The Levi-Civita symbol is a tensor density of weight \(+1\), while the metric determinant is a density of weight \(-2\). A density of weight \(W\) can be converted into a proper tensor by multiplying by \(|G|^{W/2}\), where \(G\) is the metric determinant. This construction produces proper volume elements; in three-dimensional spherical coordinates, the volume element is proportional to \(r^2\sin\theta\,dr\,d\theta\,d\phi\).

A matrix variation identity for the logarithm of a determinant yields the useful relation
\[
\Gamma^\mu{}_{\mu\alpha}
=\frac12 g^{\mu\beta}\partial_\alpha g_{\mu\beta}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|G|}}\partial_\alpha\sqrt{|G|}.
\]
This gives a shortcut for computing contracted Christoffel symbols and simplifies the covariant divergence of a vector field. It also enables a curved-spacetime form of Gauss’s theorem. Such simplifications generally do not extend to the divergence of arbitrary tensors, although antisymmetric tensors are an exception. In particular, the covariant divergence of the stress-energy tensor expresses local conservation of energy and momentum, but promoting it to a global conservation law is ambiguous because transporting vectors over extended regions is path-dependent and affected by spacetime curvature.

The lecture then develops the kinematics of freely falling test bodies. In a locally Lorentz frame, an uncharged, structureless, nonrotating body follows an inertial path, so its tangent vector is parallel transported. This gives the geodesic equation,
\[
\frac{du^\mu}{d\lambda}+\Gamma^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}u^\alpha u^\beta=0.
\]
Charged particles and extended or spinning bodies require additional force and curvature-coupling terms.

Geodesics may use affine parameters, for which the tangent is parallel transported with zero right-hand side; for timelike motion, proper time is an affine parameter. Reparameterizing a geodesic appropriately always restores affine form. A second derivation varies an action defined from accumulated proper time. Requiring stationary action reproduces the geodesic equation and shows that a timelike geodesic maximizes the proper time accumulated between two events among timelike paths. Future lectures will extend the analysis to null trajectories and combine Killing vectors with geodesics to obtain conserved quantities, including energy in time-independent spacetimes.

STAT’s Morning Rounds newsletter highlights several health policy and research developments. The NIH named 13 teams to study autism, emphasizing environmental influences during pregnancy and the challenges of measuring cumulative exposures through the “exposome.” The agency also launched an $87 million initiative to develop organoids and other methods that could reduce animal use in biomedical research.

The FDA approved Evita Solutions’ low-cost generic mifepristone for pregnancies up to 10 weeks, drawing pushback from anti-abortion groups and Trump administration officials. Its application had been pending for four years, compared with the FDA’s typical 10-month review period. The administration also postponed for a year proposed restrictions on a Medicare drug-price negotiation loophole.

In an opinion, Boston University professor Shoumita Dasgupta said Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s framing of autism as an epidemic and policies involving pregnancy acetaminophen, childhood vaccines and autism genetics echo eugenic thinking and dehumanize autistic people. Other coverage addresses cholesterol treatment, telemedicine coverage, health-sector AI, drug tariffs and medical costs.

In his first interview after being sacked as White House communications director over comments about Reince Priebus, Scaramucci told ABC News that "elements" in Washington and the White House are trying to eject Trump. He was fired after a recorded call with journalist Ryan Lizza became public.

The Double Seven strategy, revealed by Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez in their 2010 book "Short Term Trading Strategies That Work," is a mean-reversion system: it buys when the close is at a seven-day low and the close is above the 200-day moving average, and sells when the close is at a seven-day high. It has no stop loss and few parameters.

Backtests using AmiBroker covered 21 years from 2000 across liquid ETFs. Since SPY's 1993 inception, the strategy on SPY produced 154 trades with an average gain of 1.18%, an 82.5% win ratio, a profit factor of 2.58, and a Sharpe ratio of 1.4; maximum drawdown was 33% versus 55% for buy and hold, with 26% market exposure and a 6.3% CAGR compared to 10.1% for buy and hold. A combined ETF portfolio (20% per position, maximum five positions) generated 1,189 trades averaging 0.63% and a 6.3% CAGR, with nearly all gains occurring before 2010. A portfolio of only SPY and QQQ failed due to too many overlapping trades. Performance was reasonable on lookbacks from 2 to 15 days, and using the lowest close instead of the lowest low returned slightly less. Flipping the strategy to short performed badly because of the market's long-term upward bias.

The authors conclude the strategy still works on main stock indices but consider Connors' other strategies better for mean reversion, and note that "twists" can improve results.

Recruitment of a Dutch-speaking Mechanical Engineer for a 12-month assignment in Genk/Brussels, starting within 1-4 weeks, requiring modelling (MATLAB, Modelica or Dymola), thermal and mechanical experience; chemical processing preferred. Applications by CV or phone, with a referral scheme available.

Biogetica partnered with Research Needs for clinical trials and research projects using an evidence-based, system-agnostic approach to natural medicine. Their 2018 plans included clinical trials and observational studies for HPV, herpes, trigeminal neuralgia, vertigo, tinnitus, and cataracts, evaluating plant medicines and Biogetica’s combination of nutraceuticals, herbs, and resonance homeopathy while validating multidisciplinary protocols.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card behavior for card selection, data transfer, erase operations, write protection, command extensions, switching functions, initialization, clock control, CRC protection, and timeouts.

- In UHS-II Card Identification Mode, the host remains at fOD because cards may restrict operating frequencies. In Data Transfer Mode, it may use fPP. CMD9 retrieves the CSD, while broadcast CMD4 configures all identified cards’ driver stages, bus layout, card count, and transfer frequency. CMD7 selects one card for the Transfer State; selecting another card releases the previous card to Standby. CMD7 with RCA 0x0000 deselects all cards. Data communication is point-to-point between the host and the selected card.
- Read and write transfers can be stopped with CMD12. Writes must be stopped before deselection. During programming, DAT0 indicates busy status; block writes may use buffering, while CSD programming, write protection, and erase do not support concurrent transfers. Parameter-setting and read commands are not permitted while programming. Selecting another card does not terminate an active erase or programming operation, because the busy card enters Disconnect State and can later be reselected. CMD0 or CMD15 can terminate pending programming and may destroy card data.
- Standard-capacity reads use a maximum block size of 512 bytes, with CRC protection for each block. CMD17 reads one block, and CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12. Address and block-length errors prevent transfers. For writes, CMD24 and CMD25 transfer blocks with CRC, and invalid length, address, CRC, write protection, or misalignment causes rejection or abortion. Busy status can be checked with CMD13, and disconnected cards can be accessed while other cards remain busy. ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks before multiple-block writes, and ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks.
- Erasing requires CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 in sequence. Sequence errors reset the erase operation, protected sectors remain unchanged, and the ERASE_SEQ_ERROR, ERASE_RESET, and WP_ERASE_SKIP status bits report relevant conditions. DISCARD uses CMD38 argument 0x0001 and may leave discarded contents undefined; FULE uses argument 0x0002 to logically erase the full user area. DISCARD and FULE are supported only by SDHC and SDXC cards over non-SPI interfaces, with unsupported cards executing ERASE instead.
- Write protection can be provided mechanically, optionally by the card, or through password locking. PWD and PWD_LEN store the password and its length; optional FEP and FEP_LEN store a Force Erase Password. Locked cards permit basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock-related commands but deny data access. CMD42 operates in Transfer State and carries mode, password length, password data, and CRC.
- Card Ownership Protection adds FEP management, FEP Force Erase, and restrictions on resetting a password. When FEP is set, COP Unlock is required after reset, Force Erase and PWD reset are disabled, and only a matching FEP permits FEP Force Erase. Force Erase clears user-area data and the password while preserving the card’s locked state until completion. FEP Force Erase performs the same erasure but retains FEP. COP status and failures are reported through CARD_IS_LOCKED and LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED.
- CMD55 makes the next command an application-specific command. Defined ACMDs retain their special interpretation; undefined but legal ACMDs are treated as regular commands, while illegal commands return an error. CMD6 switches among six function groups for access mode, command systems, driver strength, and power limits, with additional groups represented in status data. Mode 0 queries supported functions and power consumption; Mode 1 changes functions. Invalid selections are ignored, busy functions cannot be changed, and selected functions remain active until a power cycle, CMD0, or reset restores defaults. The default power limit is 0.72 W.
- Optional High-Speed mode uses a 50 MHz clock for a 25 MB/s interface. Because differently timed cards cannot be controlled together in this mode, the host must drive only one card with one-to-one CLK, CMD, and DAT connections.
- CMD8 checks the host’s supplied voltage during Idle state. A compatible card returns R7 and echoes the voltage range and check pattern; an incompatible card remains in Idle state without responding. ACMD41 determines capacity type through CCS: CCS=0 denotes SDSC, while CCS=1 denotes SDHC or SDXC.
- SDSC uses byte addressing and a CMD16-selected block length; SDHC and SDXC use block addressing, fixed 512-byte memory blocks, and do not support partial or boundary-crossing access. For a 2 GB card, maximum block length is 1024 bytes, although CMD16 remains limited to 512 bytes. CMD42 is exempt from the fixed SDHC/SDXC memory-block rule.
- The host may reduce or stop the bus clock, subject to frequency and identification restrictions. Following ACMD41, the clock must run continuously at 100–400 kHz or be polled with ACMD41 at intervals below 50 ms. Eight clock cycles are required after specified bus transactions. A busy card may continue programming without a clock, but one clock edge is needed to release its busy signal.
- CRC7 protects commands, most responses, CID, and CSD data; CRC16 protects each transferred data block and is calculated separately on each DAT line in wide-bus mode. Failed CRC or illegal commands do not change card state and set COM_CRC_ERROR or ILLEGAL_COMMAND. Read operations use at least a 100 ms timeout. Write timeouts are generally at least 250 ms; SDXC operations may require up to 500 ms, while UHS-II busy indications after a Data Burst may last up to one second.

This medRxiv preprint analyzes 13,152 genomes from Tennessee’s Biorepository and Integrative Genomics (BIG) Initiative, which links genomic, phenotypic, clinical, and environmental data from underrepresented Mid-South populations. BIG has enrolled more than 42,000 participants, collected over 15,000 biosamples, and is predominantly pediatric, with 87% of participants under age 18.

Ancestry analysis using 1000 Genomes and HGDP references found 20% of participants with ancestry resembling African reference populations and 30% with admixed ancestry. Ancestry was geographically stratified, with African ancestry more common in urban areas and European ancestry more common in suburban areas, making geography a potential confounder. Disease analyses found high pediatric asthma and diabetes burdens, higher odds of asthma and obesity among participants identifying as non-White, and geographic variation in prevalence; asthma affected about 20% of individuals in three Memphis suburbs versus 12.8% cohort-wide.

The cohort captured substantial genetic diversity and admixture. African and admixed African participants averaged approximately 85,000 more variable sites than other groups. The study identified 771,717 novel single-nucleotide variants, comprising 11.2% of all variants, including rare ancestry-specific variants with potential functional or clinical effects. Rare deleterious-to-synonymous variant ratios varied by ancestry, although the authors cautioned that sample size, population stratification, and demography require further investigation.

Self-reported race did not consistently correspond to inferred ancestry: participants reporting as Black or African American were distributed across African and African-European ancestry categories, and genetically related individuals sometimes reported different races. The findings indicate that race should be used cautiously as a genetic covariate. Community programs including MEMGEN and advisory boards support trust and participation. Future priorities include expanding enrollment across age groups toward 100,000 participants, continuing community education, and adopting pangenomic analyses to improve representation of cohort diversity and support equitable precision medicine.

SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy targets a February 6 launch at 1:30 p.m. EST, with February 7 as a backup, after a successful engine test. The company plans to attempt landings of all three first stages: two at Cape Canaveral and one on the Atlantic drone ship Of Course I Still Love You. Designed for human spaceflight and heavy cargo, the rocket has suffered previous explosions. Despite an FAA license, Musk considers avoiding orbit or launch-pad destruction a potential “win,” while a government shutdown could delay launch.

This PRISMA-guided systematic review examines empirically studied educational applications of large language models (LLMs), their evaluation methods, associated risks, and proposed mitigations. A search of five computing and education databases from 2015–2025 yielded 70 included studies, grouped into operational effectiveness, personalized applications, and interactive learning tools. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were the most frequently studied systems.

Across these applications, LLMs showed efficiency and competence in tasks such as generating feedback, answering domain questions, analyzing educational data, and supporting writing or programming. However, technical risks included toxicity, misinformation, bias, hallucinations, privacy violations, opacity, and inconsistent performance. Pedagogical risks included superficial understanding, reduced cognitive and metacognitive engagement, weaker critical thinking, memory erosion, over-reliance, diminished student agency, compromised academic integrity, and reduced motivation. Societal risks included unequal access, data colonialism, environmental harm, and regulatory gaps, with many risks overlapping across domains.

Personalized applications showed demographic bias in grading, content generation, progress prediction, and recommendations. Interactive learning tools sometimes improved efficiency, writing quality, or assignment performance, but could also reduce revision effort, creativity, research skills, independent learning, and meaningful engagement. LLMs were frequently unable to detect their own bias, and transparency strongly affected students’ perceived fairness.

Recommended responses include human oversight, educator training, clear usage guidelines, revised assessments, diverse training data, continuous audits, bias reduction, explainable and learner-centred design, improved detection tools, student verification and disclosure practices, and stronger data governance. The review introduces an Interaction–Monitoring–Outcome model showing how risks accumulate across the learning cycle. Limitations include the English-only search, rapidly changing models, search coverage, and reliance on mostly short-term studies; future work should include longitudinal, cross-cultural, and design-oriented research.

A commodity trading advisor (CTA) is a registered individual or organization that advises on or manages accounts trading futures, commodity options, currency swaps, and other derivatives. CTA funds generally operate as managed-futures hedge funds, investing across global asset classes such as foreign exchange, energies, metals, interest rates, equity indices, and commodities. CTAs typically charge management and incentive fees and must register with the CFTC and join the NFA.

Most CTAs use systematic strategies based on quantitative models and trading algorithms, although some trade discretionarily. Signals may reflect technical analysis, trend following, momentum, or economic fundamentals. Trend following is the predominant CTA strategy and seeks to identify medium- to long-term trends through signal generation and exposure sizing. Many CTAs also use cross-sectional momentum by ranking assets and buying winners while shorting losers.

A simple example goes long the S&P 500 when it closes above its 200-day moving average and remains out of the market otherwise. The cited backtest produced a 28% maximum drawdown and 6.73% CAGR, versus 7.16% for buy-and-hold without dividends. The article stresses that professional CTAs prioritize multiple uncorrelated, complementary strategies and lower volatility rather than the highest standalone return.

Unlike hedge funds, which can trade a broader range of securities, CTAs are generally limited to futures, options, and currency swaps. CTA strategies can trade commodities, stocks, currencies, and futures, while potentially reducing risk through diversification. However, they remain exposed to losses, market volatility, inaccurate data, capital requirements, and the need for market expertise; added complexity does not necessarily improve results.

Andropov has internal incentives to pursue an arms control agreement: retaining military support while limiting military spending, relieving economic pressures, and gaining political advantage over Chernenko and others favoring détente. The passage recommends prioritizing INF negotiations over START and opening a private channel, which suits Andropov’s preference for secrecy and may avoid leaks from officials opposed to arms control. An initial short letter should express concern about renewed confrontation, emphasize the shared interest in peace, and invite Andropov to make progress toward reducing nuclear arms without presenting a full proposal. Negotiators should remain tough, sustain the U.S. defense buildup, and avoid assuming that past SALT-era failures will recur.

The study proposes a meta-learning framework using a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to approximate the inverse Hessian operator in 4D-Var data assimilation. The FNO maps the adjoint-model output \(f\) to an estimated initial state, with sparse observations embedded implicitly in \(f\). Although the standalone FNO is less accurate than conjugate gradient (CG), its prediction provides a useful initialization for CG.

Experiments use a linear advection equation on a periodic domain, generating training and test datasets of 5,400 samples each with varied background states, covariance scales, and observation configurations. Compared with standard CG, FNO-CG reduces average relative error from \(4.26\times10^{-2}\) to \(1.61\times10^{-2}\) and average iterations from 127 to 105—a 62% error reduction and 17% iteration reduction. Improvements are most pronounced for poorly conditioned Hessian problems, while gains are limited for well-conditioned cases where CG already performs well. The results indicate that FNOs can approximate operators beyond PDE solvers and can accelerate variational data assimilation by reducing expensive iterative computation. Future work will extend the approach to nonlinear PDEs, including the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.

The passage (© CoachingAmericanSoccer.com) urges soccer coaches to engage in contingency planning rather than reacting "on the fly," suggesting coaches work through a series of "what if" questions, with answers for applicable items developed collegially among coaches, players and/or parents, documented, and communicated as a true Contingency Plan.

The questions are grouped into categories:

- **Communications:** normal and emergency communication processes, electronic system failures and backups, procedures for cancelling practices/games due to field conditions, appointing and informing a back-up (including access to equipment and documents), relocating practices/games, and learning of last-minute player absences.
- **Players/Practices:** knowing which players wear contact lenses or have allergies (particularly bee stings); who cares for injured players and who takes over the practice; handling multiple injuries, financial hardship, unpaid fees and registration forms; player eligibility criteria and mid-season ineligibility; responses to drills or tactics that don't work, disruptive players, poor teammates, players' attitudes and reactions to criticism; dealing with losing, problem parents and cuts (how to tell players and parents why); preparation for varied field conditions; restroom emergencies.
- **Pre-Game:** forgotten or dead cell phones and lack of service, hard-copy phone numbers, missing referees, unplayable surfaces and who decides to cancel and reports to, fields lacking lines/nets/flags, local rules, officiating and lines-persons, player passes, completeness of kits (water, first aid, coach's kit, balls, backup equipment), lost equipment, missing uniforms/shinguards/shoes, medical authorization forms, insufficient players or cancellation/forfeiture with rides already left, coin toss, uniform conflicts, and repairing nets or supplying backup jerseys/shorts for blood incidents.
- **Within Game:** lost contact lenses, injury treatment and 911 access, hospital transport when no guardian is present, tactical responses to ejection and yellow cards, weather such as lightning (no one under trees), suspension or termination of games, fighting among players or fans, referee misconduct or medical emergency, unexpected opponent lineup changes, multi-player events like vehicle breakdowns or food poisoning, multiple injuries, coach incapacitation, response to poor referee calls, and warming up substitutes.
- **Post-Practice/Post-Game:** players not picked up and vehicle breakdowns.
- **Extended or Total Absence:** long-term medical conditions, family needs, extended travel, permanent departure due to job change or move, a child quitting, succession planning with the club.

The closing tips: create checklists; recognize the list is not comprehensive and ask what can go wrong and what the response will be; delegate; accept that some things cannot be controlled or anticipated and that ready help is needed; instill contingency planning in assistant coaches, players and parents; and teach players to be prepared for contingencies.

A collection of October 25, 2001 reports chronicled Enron’s worsening financial and credibility problems after it recorded a $1.01 billion third-quarter charge related to broadband, water trading and limited partnerships overseen by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron reported a $618 million quarterly loss, compared with a $292 million profit a year earlier; excluding the charge, it would have earned $393 million. Standard & Poor’s affirmed Enron’s ratings but assigned a negative outlook, citing reduced financial flexibility and the challenge of selling assets and reducing leverage. Fitch also placed Enron’s securities on negative watch, while Moody’s had its credit under review. Fitch highlighted $3.2 billion of combined debt at two affiliates and questioned whether their underlying assets could cover it. Enron said it had roughly $3.4 billion in bank credit available, sought a $750 million loan arrangement and planned to use asset-sale proceeds to repair its balance sheet.

Energy trading partners continued doing business with Enron and had generally left their credit policies unchanged, though some firms were monitoring exposures, seeking more information or limiting credit. EnronOnline remained highly active, recording 8,000 transactions worth $4 billion on Wednesday, above its $3.5 billion daily average. Fastow was placed on leave and replaced by Jeff McMahon after the SEC began questioning transactions involving partnerships managed by Fastow. The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit ADC and data-acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. It supports 2-lane and 4-lane SDR or DDR output interfaces, producing data on D[3:0], a data clock on DCLKOUT, and a frame clock on FCLKOUT. The 20-bit conversion result is transmitted MSB first with six trailing zero bits. Its source-synchronous interface frequency depends on sampling-clock speed, data rate, and lane count; the frame-clock frequency is one-fourth the sampling-clock frequency.

An optional output randomizer XORs conversion data with either the conversion-result LSB or an appended PRBS bit, reducing correlation between ground bounce and analog input voltage. Two averaging modes are available: simple averaging halves the output data rate, while moving averaging does not. Configurable fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns can replace ADC data for channel groups 1–4 and 5–8.

The device can be reset or powered down through pins or register fields, after which its registers require a specified initialization sequence and a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS for one selected analog-input pair while leaving the other six channels idle.

The 16-bit configuration registers are divided into three banks with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible; other banks are selected through address 0x03. SPI writes and reads require specified frame sequences. Multiple devices can be daisy-chained by connecting their CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO pins in series. The chain length is configured in DAISY_CHAIN_LEN, and each chained register write requires 24 SCLKs per ADC. The register map also includes controls for averaging, XOR randomization, test patterns, speed boost, lane selection, analog bandwidth and common-mode range, power-down, initialization, gain-error correction, and user-defined output bits.

For ATE applications, the ADS9803 provides calibrated total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. It offers low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz; in wide-bandwidth mode, multiplexed signals settle to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. It uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies with no required power-up sequence. Recommended layout includes close-proximity 0.1-µF supply bypass capacitors, reference-capacitor placement near REFIO and REFM, short ground-plane connections, and separation of analog and reference paths from digital signals and noise sources. TI also provides documentation-update notifications, development resources, and E2E support forums.

The article explains that low-volatility investing focuses on stocks or sectors with relatively stable prices, lower price fluctuations, and a beta below 1, such as utilities, consumer staples, and healthcare stocks. The strategy aims to reduce portfolio volatility, limit large declines, and provide more consistent returns, potentially appealing to investors with lower risk tolerance or nearing retirement. However, it may produce lower returns than high-volatility stocks in some periods and can experience long stretches of underperformance.

Implementation options include low-volatility ETFs or mutual funds, such as SPLV, or selecting stocks through historical price analysis, technical and fundamental research, stable earnings, consistent dividends, low debt, and low beta. Portfolios should be diversified across sectors and reviewed and rebalanced periodically, generally annually or less. The strategy requires a long horizon of years or decades.

Historical research cited indicates that the most volatile stocks performed poorly during major market declines, the three lowest-volatility deciles had not produced negative returns over any ten-year period since 1974, and the low-volatility effect appeared across 21 developed and 12 emerging-market exchanges. Berkshire Hathaway was also cited as evidence that cheap, safe, high-quality stocks can perform well. Backtesting with historical data can estimate past performance but cannot reliably predict future results.

The Triple RSI strategy is a modified RSI-based mean-reversion system inspired by Larry Connors’ R3 strategy. It uses four key variables—three based on RSI—along with the 200-day moving average and entry and exit signals. A backtest of SPY since 1993 produced 83 trades, an average gain of 1.4% per trade, a reported win rate of about 90%–91%, and a profit factor of 5. The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update (March 2006) documents known hardware deviations, limitations, and workarounds affecting the PIT, PIC, DMA controllers, GLIU, PMC, ACPI, KEL, USB, UART, ATA/UDMA, LPC, SMBus, GPIO, RTC, and power-management functions.

Issues include incorrect PIT command cancellation and count-mode loading; PIC AEOI and edge-interrupt failures; incorrect DMA request rotation; GLIU debug and error-reporting failures; incomplete thermal-alarm recovery during standby; malformed ACPI register accesses and PMC write corruption; KEL port-reporting and Snoop-mode errors; UART access during DMA; failed USB clock gating and USB over-voltage tolerance; ATA PRD alignment and prefetch hazards; UDMA CRC corruption after host termination; failed reverse-order UDMA startup; unreliable ATAPI transfers; LPC failures during legacy DMA, back-to-back PCI reads, and synchronization with ISA bridges; SMBus NEGACK and hold-time problems; GPIO corruption after suspend; and wake-event failures in ACPI S3.

Recommended workarounds include using supported command sequences, single-transfer DMA, DWORD-aligned PRD tables, UDMA host-termination blocking, normal PIO-before-bus-master ordering, ACPI SMI traps for narrow accesses, disabling affected clock-gating features, using PWRBTN# for S3 wake, restoring KEL state around Snoop mode, adding USB over-voltage protection, using read-modify-write for GPIO registers after suspend, programming sleep-delay counters below PM_SED, and applying an LPC-bus PLD workaround. Some listed defects are limited to debug or diagnostic functions and have no operational impact.

Defensive tackles line up in the interior of the defensive line and are essential to stopping the run and pressuring quarterbacks. NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to twice the programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI performance of Turing. Its second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance and add motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute, while third-generation Tensor Cores support structural sparsity for greater effective throughput.

DLSS uses a neural network to combine scene details from multiple frames for high-quality, native-resolution-like images with improved performance. On Ampere, DLSS adds a 9x scaling factor, enabling the GeForce RTX 3090 to support 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps in many titles.

GA10x supports GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron Technology. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to transfer two bits per clock edge, supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, and delivers up to 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth on the RTX 3090—over 52% more than the RTX 2080 Ti’s TU102 GPU. MTA encoding, interface training, equalization, and careful package and PCB design address signal-integrity challenges introduced by PAM4. GDDR6X also includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed memory transactions and retries them, indicating when memory overclocking has reached its practical limit.

As game sizes and SSD speeds increase, traditional storage APIs and CPU-based decompression can become bottlenecks. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, loads and decompresses assets directly on the GPU, reducing CPU work and improving I/O performance by up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional APIs. GPU-based lossless decompression uses asynchronous compute kernels and the DMA and copy engines of Turing and Ampere, enabling rapid loading and streaming, reduced pop-in and stutter, and greater SSD storage efficiency. RTX IO also benefits professional workloads involving large CAD models, scientific visualization, and rendering.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC and HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth. They also support HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x. The fifth-generation NVDEC decoder accelerates decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x provides the first hardware AV1 decoding support, including 8K60 HDR playback with substantially lower CPU use. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder handles high-quality, low-latency streaming and archiving with low CPU use and power consumption, supporting up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB by linking two A40 GPUs with third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen4 connectivity, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU and has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores; NVIDIA states it is 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, supports GDDR6X in the architecture but uses GDDR6 in this product, omits NVLink, and is described as faster than the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti.

The RTX A6000 is a professional GA102-based workstation GPU with 48 GB of GDDR6, second-generation ray-tracing hardware, and support for large 3D datasets and hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising. Two linked cards provide 96 GB of combined memory. The passage also presents generational performance comparisons for its rendering, HPC, and deep-learning workloads.

The specifications are presented as accurate and reliable as of the publication date, although NVIDIA reserves the right to revise them and provides the materials and products under its stated sales terms, warranties, disclaimers, and liability limitations.

Current machine-learning force fields approximate density functional theory for efficient crystal structure relaxation and property prediction, but their performance depends strongly on crystal representations. Existing approaches—including multi-edge graph models, atomic angular embeddings, periodic-vector systems, and transformers—use local encodings that may map distinct structures to identical representations and fail to capture long-term interactions in infinite periodic crystals.

The paper presents reciprocal-space diffraction as an alternative because it uniquely encodes the complete electron distribution and periodic real-space arrangement of a crystal. Conventional X-ray, electron, and neutron diffraction has limitations: X-rays and electrons primarily reflect electron clouds and struggle to distinguish atoms with similar charge, while neutrons provide weak contrast between heavy atoms of similar mass. Traditional X-ray form factors are fixed tabulated values and cannot account for local chemical environments.

To address these issues, the authors introduce PRDNet, a multimodal architecture combining graph embeddings with a learned pseudo-particle diffraction module. The pseudo-particle has learned, environment-dependent attributes, enabling it to act as a distinct probe and generate synthetic diffraction patterns that distinguish atomic arrangements and local chemical environments. The framework incorporates symmetry-preserving properties and is designed to be invariant to crystal rotations, reflections, and translations.

The authors formally describe crystal structures through atomic types, atomic positions, and a periodic lattice, and explain diffraction using structure factors and atomic form factors. Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench report state-of-the-art performance across multiple crystal-property prediction tasks.
