The Higgs field can also provide masses to fermions.

The passage examines education groups in China as a response to unequal access to high-quality basic education and the “siphon” effect, in which teachers and students move from disadvantaged areas to schools with superior resources. A group typically centers on a prestigious “core school” and ordinary branch schools, with core-school administrators and anchor teachers providing guidance, training, cooperative research, and teacher exchanges.

Education groups promote resource sharing, instructional coordination, curriculum development, standardized assessment, and regional balance. They improve teachers’ professional competence, confidence, collaboration, and job satisfaction while expanding students’ access to courses, activities, advanced teaching methods, and diverse learning experiences. Such groups have also reduced public anxiety over school choice and, in Hangzhou’s Xiacheng District, benefited 90% of students.

Challenges include mechanically imposing core-school culture on branch schools, which can erase distinctive traditions; transferring core-school theories and methods without adapting them to ordinary schools’ circumstances and capacities; and burdening core-school management and resources through expansion. Recommendations include establishing democratic, shared governance among member schools; strengthening teacher rotation, training, incentives, and online resource platforms; and securing government funding, policy support, and recognition for teachers and principals who support less-advantaged schools. The passage concludes that education groups represent deeper, contractual cooperation than earlier inter-school arrangements, but their continued development requires further study.

Fire departments promote Fire Prevention Month’s “Every Second Counts—Know Two Ways Out” theme, urging families to maintain multiple exits, keep windows usable, stay outside after alarms, and practice home fire drills.

Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days feature discounts on nearly the entire Kindle lineup ahead of the holiday season. The Colorsoft is recommended for colorful libraries, comics, and graphic novels, while its Signature Edition adds wireless charging, an auto-adjusting front light, and more storage. The second-generation Kindle Scribe is favored as an e-reader and digital notebook with three-month battery life. The 2024 Paperwhite is the all-around recommendation, with a larger screen and warm light; its Signature Edition adds an ad-free lock screen and wireless charging. The basic Kindle remains a budget-friendly option with fast performance, dark mode, and a front light. Kids bundles include covers and Kids+ content.
John Whitfield’s application for a writ of error coram nobis was denied because he failed to establish that he was denied effective assistance of appellate counsel.

- The passage describes SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest–hypervisor communication through the GHCB and VMGEXIT protocols. The hypervisor exposes the GHCB guest physical address through VMCB offset 0x00a0 and the GHCB MSR. During negotiation, intercepted CPUID requests cause a #VC exception, allowing the guest to obtain the supported GHCB protocol versions and SEV page-table encryption-bit position. Examples use GHCBInfo 0x001 with protocol version 1 and encryption bit 47 for SEV-ES, or up to version 2 and encryption bit 51 for SEV-SNP. The guest configures long mode and encrypted page tables, allocates a shared GHCB page, and writes its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130 before using it.

- For a #VC exception, the guest determines the cause, places the required state in the GHCB, and invokes VMGEXIT. The hypervisor processes the exit, updates the GHCB save state, and resumes the guest, which copies returned values into its register state. Guest and hypervisor reset the GHCB VALID_BITMAP before setting required fields. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while updating or accessing the GHCB.

- The specified non-automatic exit events include IOIO protection, MSR protection, hypercalls, MMIO accesses protected through nested-page-table reserved bits, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended guest requests, SEV-TIO requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell management, IPI delivery, timer access, APIC ID discovery, VMPL changes, Secure AVIC backing-page management, and guest termination. Unsupported events use an unsupported-event exit code.

- MMIO and string operations may require decrypted data buffers in the GHCB shared buffer area. The guest supplies the buffer address through SW_SCRATCH and may divide transfers across multiple VMGEXIT calls. Hypervisor error conditions are reported through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2, including requested exception injection and malformed or invalid VMGEXIT input.

- Page-state-change requests use structures in the shared buffer, which can hold up to 253 entries. Requests can make pages private or shared and, for SEV-SNP, update the RMP table. PSMASH and UNSMASH requests provide RMP update hints. Progress is recorded in cur_entry and cur_page so an interrupted request can resume, with failure or incomplete status reported through SW_EXITINFO2.

- SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages. The hypervisor translates and validates them, assigns the response page to firmware, processes the request, and reclaims the page afterward. It returns the firmware result in SW_EXITINFO2. Because the message sequence number is used in the AES-GCM IV, failed requests must be retried before another request is allowed; repeated requests may be rate-limited. Extended guest requests can return VCEK or VLEK certificates in a GUID-indexed table. TIO requests similarly use shared data pages to return measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report, and may provide a nonce for fresh device measurements.

- For SEV-SNP, the hypervisor supplies secrets and CPUID pages during launch. Part of the secrets page is reserved for guest communication, including per-VMPL guest-message sequence numbers. EFI firmware can provide the secrets and CPUID pages through an EFI configuration table. Guest termination requests provide a reason code and 64 bits of termination information.

- SNP AP creation allows a guest to create, update, or remove an AP vCPU by supplying a VM Save Area page. It supports deferred initialization until INIT-SIPI or immediate activation and permits vCPU hotplug. Secure AVIC uses a private, guest-owned APIC backing page per vCPU that is registered with and kept mapped by the hypervisor while the vCPU runs.

- The #HV doorbell mechanism supports Restricted Injection by allowing a host to notify a guest of pending interrupts and non-maskable events. The shared doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and end-of-interrupt behavior. The guest acknowledges events and EOI assistance through atomic exchanges, using an explicit X2APIC EOI write when necessary. Interrupt-shadow rules differ from normal execution: the guest executes HLT with interrupts disabled, while the host immediately re-enters the guest if events remain pending.

- SEV-ES guests identify hypervisor and SEV support through additional CPUID properties, including the encryption-bit position and physical-address-space reduction. AP booting requires special handling because measured, encrypted register state cannot be changed normally; the passage describes reset-hold procedures, AP jump tables, and SNP AP creation as alternatives. NMI handling requires intercepting #DB rather than IRET and using an “NMI Complete” message. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when advertised; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Adidas and Refinery29 created “Boost the Nation,” one custom UltraBOOST X shoe for each of the 50 states, designed by female artists and auctioned to benefit Women Win. Georgia’s peach-themed shoe, designed by Lizzie Darden, was a women’s size 8 with a $350 bid; Ohio’s reached $1,000.

The court affirmed Vu Ngo’s conviction for three counts of first-degree robbery. His peremptory-challenge discrimination claim was unpreserved, and the court declined discretionary review. His hospital questioning and brief detention did not constitute a forcible seizure warranting suppression, and officers had reasonable suspicion to continue detention for a showup identification and questioning after investigating a nearby robbery and homicide.

Britain’s FTSE 100 closed 0.4% higher after a choppy session following the formal trigger of Brexit, as sterling’s decline boosted export-heavy companies. The mid-cap index gained 0.1%. 3I rose 5.7% on an upgrade, while LSE gained 2.7% despite EU regulators blocking its proposed Deutsche Boerse merger. Copper miners advanced, gold-related stocks fell, and AA dropped 3.9%.

A delivery-failure notice returned Jeff Dasovich’s February 16, 2001 email, “Ken Lay’s email to Sen. Brulte,” because one recipient’s address was unknown. The original message circulated confidential materials sent to Ken Lay’s office for delivery to Sen. Brulte and discussed Enron’s California legislative and public-relations strategy, including coordinated public release, a one-page summary, coalition-building, and PR activation. The enclosed materials addressed barriers to distributed generation, DWR power-purchase credit risks under AB1X, and a projected California summer 2001 supply shortfall of about 5,000 MW, with blackouts considered likely. Enron’s legislative package proposed increasing supply through SB28X, reducing demand through AB31X, establishing a competitive retail market through SB27X, and restoring investor-owned utilities’ solvency through AB18X. Recommended DWR fixes included amending AB1X, using a PUC order and contract terms, or accepting other credit support. Attachments included PUC talking points and proposed AB1X amendments.

This cross-sectional study investigated whether perivascular spaces (PVS), a component of the brain’s glymphatic system, are enlarged in epilepsy. Researchers compared 467 patients with temporal lobe epilepsy and hippocampal sclerosis, MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy, extratemporal focal epilepsy, or idiopathic generalized epilepsy against 473 healthy controls. Participants underwent 3T T1-weighted MRI, and PVS were segmented using the PINGU algorithm and assessed in white matter and basal ganglia, with age and sex included as covariates.

All epilepsy groups had substantially greater basal ganglia PVS volume fractions than controls—approximately 101–140% higher—with large effect sizes. Basal ganglia PVS numbers were also higher, and extratemporal focal epilepsy had greater PVS burden than temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis. After age and sex adjustment, white-matter PVS did not differ significantly between groups. Patients with hippocampal sclerosis showed an asymmetry with larger PVS on the contralateral side, but no significant between-group white-matter asymmetry was established. PVS measures were not associated with illness duration.

The findings indicate that basal ganglia PVS are enlarged across the epilepsy subtypes studied. Because the study was cross-sectional, it cannot determine whether PVS enlargement precedes seizures or results from recurrent seizures; longitudinal research is needed.

NVIDIA reported that David M. Shannon, 60, Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary, will retire at the end of 2016. Shannon joined NVIDIA in August 2002 and oversaw its legal and human resources functions. Upon his retirement, Senior Vice President and General Counsel Brian E. Cabrera will lead the legal team, while NVIDIA will recruit a leader for human resources.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN) on May 29, 2018, to pursue his presidential ambition in the 2019 election. ANN had been adopted by the Nigerian Intervention Movement, which includes his YesWeFit movement. After leaving the NCP citing over-taxation, he urged supporters and other aspirants to unite under ANN as a “Third Force.”

The passage presents a formally specified, correct-by-construction voter unit for synchronous N-modular redundant measurement systems used in avionics control applications. Each cycle, the voter receives a measurement and self-reported health status from every input unit. Faults are either self-identifying or deviations greater than a noise threshold δ. Faulty behavior lasting fewer than a configurable persistence limit is transient; reaching that limit constitutes a permanent fault. Assumptions bound simultaneous new faults and specify the minimum number of units needed to remain operational.

The voter uses mutual measurement comparisons to classify units as miscomparing, not miscomparing, or maybe miscomparing. Formal requirements define soundness and completeness limits for this identification, including conditions under which complete classification is impossible. The proposed rules achieve complete classification under the minimum-surviving-units assumption while preserving soundness and enabling partial fault identification in other cases. Consecutive suspicious behavior is tracked with a risky count, and persistently faulty units are isolated permanently.

Each cycle, the voter selects a prime unit and produces the selected reading and unit identifier, output age, validity status, and preserved historical data. It always outputs healthy data, retains the previous output during transient failures, and switches prime units only when the prior prime has been isolated. The status can be valid, unidentifiable, or invalid; the unidentifiable state permits bounded use of retained output when enough non-isolated units remain but no healthy unit can yet be identified. Output age is bounded under the stated fault assumptions.

The voter is modeled as a five-state transition system parameterized by the number of units, noise threshold, persistence limit, and maximum simultaneous faults. In Rocq, the state and transition definitions embed proof terms establishing the required invariants, and requirements R1–R16 and their consistency are machine-verified. The verified implementation can be extracted to OCaml, Haskell, or Scheme; the extracted OCaml contains 362 lines and processes one state transition in about 3 milliseconds, while verification takes approximately 23 seconds on the stated laptop. Proposed future work includes hierarchical redundancy management and verified fault handling for asynchronous or distributed voting units.

Doctors urged awareness of eye-cancer types and symptoms because cases in India are often detected late, complicating treatment. Specialized facilities and trained ocular oncologists are scarce. Retinoblastoma, the most common eye cancer in children under five, may cause squinting or a white pupil; early detection can preserve sight and save lives.

The paper distinguishes formal, non-formal, informal, and random education and examines how digitalization has expanded conventional, distance, and online learning through multimedia resources, intelligent and hybrid environments, and synchronous and asynchronous instruction. In design education, digital tools, algorithms, machine learning, learning-management systems, and virtual simulations support rapid iteration, computational and parametric design, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

The study asks how diversified informal online learning platforms can contribute personalized learning to formal design education. Using a literature review and case studies, it analyzes two synchronous computational-design programs: “Introduction to Computational Design,” a five-day Rhino and Grasshopper workshop, and “Sustainability through Computational Design,” a 21-day course integrating climate data, environmental analysis, and computational design.

Findings indicate that these programs provide hands-on, interactive, and discussion-based learning; accelerate software skill acquisition; support personalized and multidisciplinary development; and strengthen creativity, self-confidence, critical thinking, and environmental awareness. The course also offers practical assignments, a model project, jury evaluation, networking, and possible professional benefits.

Limitations include limited personal interaction, isolation, technical and connectivity issues, financial and resource barriers, unequal access, trainer-dependent quality, and competition between participants. Informal programs also remain outside formal curricula and transcripts. The paper concludes that online informal education enables personalized, collaborative, and accessible learning that can complement conventional design education, while noting that varied training approaches limit the objectivity of current findings.

The guide defines optional extensions to AMD SEV and SEV-SNP that facilitate page migration, the copying of page contents while updating virtual-to-physical mappings. AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine offloads this work, including migration of pages subject to concurrent DMA and SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor or operating system. TMPM support is indicated by the ENGINE_READY bit, and IOMMU enablement is required.

TMPM supports tiered-memory optimization by allowing frequently accessed data to move to faster memory. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates DMA-mapped system physical pages between physical locations and coordinates with IOMMU host page table entries. It can suspend DMA while copying data and updating mappings, directly modifies IOMMU host page table entries, and permits migration of hypervisor-owned pages in SNP systems or default pages in non-SNP systems. The CPU must be prevented from accessing the source pages during migration.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages while preserving the guest physical address. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, and destination pages must be in the newly defined Pre-Migration state. After migration, source pages return to Pre-Migration state while destination pages inherit the source states. Pre-Migration entries use the platform-specific PS_ASID_VAL, ignore the GPA, cannot be validated by a guest, and must be converted to Hypervisor state through RMPUpdate. Concurrent DMA is unsupported for guest-page migration.

A command can contain 1–128 migration entries for noncontiguous pages and may reference multiple guests. Entries have no order dependency and receive individual statuses. PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking per-page results, while other command-level results indicate that no migrations executed. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE identifies a potentially retryable conflict. Migration lists must begin on a 4KB system physical boundary.

Performance is highest with 128-page commands, while commands with at least 16 pages have substantially greater bandwidth than smaller batches. Keeping the command ring buffer supplied and batching completion interrupts are recommended. The ring buffer is separate from the SEV/SNP buffer and can hold 256 16-byte commands per page. Software controls the write pointer, firmware controls the read pointer, and command execution order is not guaranteed.

IOMMU data structures accessed through SPAs, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages cannot be migrated. Migrated page addresses must be 4KB aligned; host page table entry addresses are 8-byte aligned. Two-megabyte IO migrations must be split into 4KB pages, while guest migrations may use aligned, physically contiguous 2MB pages. SPAs may be 46 or 52 bits depending on system-encryption mode, with encrypted-memory use indicated by the C bit.

The driver exposes the TMPM device, configures the ring buffer, enables PAGEMIGRATION_EN in all IOMMUs, and supports initialization, pause/resume, shutdown, completion detection, and shared interrupt handling for queue errors, empty or low-water conditions, command errors, and command completion. Firmware reload requires operations to be paused and the ring buffer torn down, uses the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol, and requires firmware of the same or a newer version. Clients must verify ENGINE_READY after reload.

Command and migration-entry errors are reported through command and per-page status fields; ring-buffer errors appear in PM_Status, while hardware failures may also generate Machine Check Architecture reports. A timeout should be logged and handled by the client, potentially including preserving state or terminating VMs. A hardware failure during a batch can render all pages in that command unrecoverable, and the system may ultimately require a reboot.

The Supreme Court’s Constitution Bench held that re-promulgating ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic legislative processes. A majority ruled that ordinances must be laid before the legislature, making this a mandatory obligation, and that noncompliance is a serious constitutional infraction. Presidential and gubernatorial satisfaction under Articles 123 and 213 is subject to judicial review for fraud or oblique motives. Ordinances must cease six weeks after the legislature reassembles, or earlier if disapproved. In the Bihar teachers’ case, the Court held that salaries already paid need not be recovered.

University of Surrey researchers report that solar photovoltaic power is now the cheapest option for large-scale generation, costing as little as £0.02 per unit in sunniest countries and less than coal, gas, or wind. Global installed solar capacity exceeded 1.5 terawatts in 2024, double its 2020 level. Lithium-ion battery prices have fallen 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems as cost-effective as gas plants and allowing solar power to be dispatched when needed. Major obstacles include grid congestion and integrating growing solar generation into electricity networks. Researchers recommend smart grids, AI forecasting, stronger regional connections, and continued long-term policies to support investment, innovation, and a reliable clean-energy transition. Innovations such as perovskite solar cells could increase output by up to 50% without expanding land use.

The first document extols Eastern traditions of propriety, rectitude, ancestral sacrifice, patriotism, and good government while condemning foreign doctrines, especially “universal love,” as delusive. It urges adherence to ancestral teachings and the burning of offending books. A second anonymous 1893 notice attacks Christian worshippers and preachers as insincere, unfilial, greedy, and exploitative, orders them to leave, and threatens an attack by patriots. Mr. Heard reports that Confucian followers in Seoul petitioned the king, alleging that Tong Hâk’s doctrines corrupted the people and demanding reform or extermination. The king said the government would address the matter and advised the petitioners to study their professed principles.
A non-inverting hysteresis circuit uses two resistors and VREF. Output switches low-to-high when VIN exceeds VIN1 and high-to-low when VIN drops below VIN2. Hysteresis is VIN1 minus VIN2.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2015, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014. The filing furnished a January 26 press release as Exhibit 99.1, which was not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act or incorporated by reference except by specific reference. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President of Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer.

The passage presents an S&P 500 timing strategy based on a bull-market signal: 18 consecutive closes above the 200-day SMA during a bear market. Its rules are to sell when the index falls 20% from its all-time high and buy after the signal, holding until the next bear market.

Backtested from 1927 to the present without dividend- or split-adjusted data, the strategy produced 12 signals, a 7.24% CAGR, 15.26 standard deviation, 0.24 Sharpe ratio, 60% maximum drawdown, 87.38% time in the market, and 8.28% risk-adjusted return. Excluding the 1929 crash, maximum drawdown was about 25%.

Average S&P 500 returns after the signal were 9.54% at six months and 21.84% at one year; the index was higher 100% of the time after 12 months. The strategy outperformed a golden-cross model on returns but not risk-adjusted performance and generated 12 signals versus 49. The signal was last triggered on February 15, 2023.

St. George welcomed an 11-member delegation from Ibigawa, Japan, continuing a sister-city cultural exchange dating nearly three decades. The visitors, received by Mayor Jon Pike and other officials, included Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji and four marathon entrants: Kenji Miyazaki, Mitsue Tomita, Nobuchika Tsuboi and Mina Tusboi. Miyazaki and Tomita were listed among the marathon’s top 20 elite runners in their divisions. The group was recognized by the City Council, stayed with host families and attended an international luncheon where Pike and Isaji exchanged ceremonial gifts. St. George plans to send officials and runners to Ibigawa’s Nov. 12 marathon. The delegates also toured local attractions, Springdale and Zion National Park during their five-day visit.

The study investigates integrating environmental education into expanded-opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Educational Service Area 2, Thailand. Such schools extend primary education to junior-high level for students in remote areas and are presented as supporting inclusive, sustainable education under SDG 4. The research addresses students’ limited environmental knowledge and the limited integration of environmental issues into school curricula.

The three-phase study included questionnaire surveys, environmental assessments, interviews, observation, SWOT analysis, and action and developmental research. Participants included 364 students sampled from 3,951 students across 22 schools, 44 teachers, and three school directors; a separate group of 30 students from three schools evaluated the instructional model.

Community assessments identified agricultural activities, especially rice cultivation, as a major source of chemical-related soil pollution. Agricultural chemicals were also identified as causes of water and air pollution. Other concerns included household wastewater discharged into drains, chemical contamination, indiscriminate garbage disposal, and cultural problems associated with technological change.

Students’ mean environmental-education scores were 3.79 for awareness, 4.00 for knowledge, 4.09 for attitude, 3.96 for skills, 3.90 for participation, and 3.99 for evaluation ability. Teachers’ overall mean was higher at 4.48. SWOT analysis identified community interest, cooperation, environmental awareness, and technological access as strengths; pollution, continuity of environmental instruction, and waste management as weaknesses; support for the SDGs and potential use of IT and AI as opportunities; and industrial growth, climate-related changes, and resource decline as threats.

The researchers developed an integrated environmental-education model based on nine forms of multiple intelligence, emphasizing practical and collaborative learning and the integration of environmental content across subjects. The model achieved effectiveness values of 81.51/82.11, exceeding the criterion of 80/80. Experts rated its content validity at 4.60 and construct validity at 3.97. Among the 30 evaluation students, mean post-instruction achievement increased from 5.90 to 24.63, a statistically significant difference at the 0.05 level, and satisfaction was high at 3.83.

The study concludes that the model is practical for teachers and can improve students’ environmental knowledge, participation, skills, and awareness. Recommendations call for holistic, real-world environmental learning, systematic integration across subjects, learner-centered and collaborative activities, and development of standards and curricula for environmental management education in schools.

App-based taxi drivers in Delhi-NCR threatened a one-day strike against Ola and Uber, citing fares of Rs 6 per km and 25% company commissions while demanding fares near Rs 20 per km. The Delhi High Court permanently barred two driver unions and associates from blocking the cabs. The Sarvodaya Drivers’ Association planned a protest and warned of an indefinite strike if demands were unmet, though autorickshaw and yellow-black taxi unions declined to participate.

Rain Bird’s waterproof 9V WPX battery controller suits locations without mains power. It supports 1–6 zones, multiple run times and zone stacking, with about one year’s operation on one battery or up to two years on two.

A study analyzing roughly 300 billion data points from about 11,500 living and fossil species reconstructed animal habitats and temperature fluctuations over 270 million years. It found that birds and mammals adapt to temperature changes two to three times faster than reptiles and amphibians, partly because they regulate body temperature and use body heat to protect developing offspring. This advantage helped them colonize colder latitudes, but researchers cautioned that rapid climate change may leave some species unable to adapt in time. Pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species also contribute to extinction pressures. It remains unclear whether past adaptive advantages will help birds and mammals under current conditions.
The speaker describes a goal sequence involving Matt and Teemu after a line change and credits disciplined third-period play for the game-sealing score.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor interfaces for VMPL changes, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, termination, guest identification, multiprocessor startup, interrupt handling, and host notifications.

SNP guests may request a vCPU run at another VMPL level using a unique VMSA per level. Requesting an unsupported VMPL produces an error, and VMPL changes require updating the VMSA system physical address and associated GHCB. The SEV-TIO extension lets guests bind trusted devices to their private address space. SNP guests discover support through PCIe capabilities; the device is bound on the first TIO guest request. Unenlightened guests rely on VMPL0 firmware for setup, while other guests fetch device information, validate the interface report, and configure MMIO and IOMMU.

The SNP TIO Guest Request supplies a guest PCI ID, an MMIO range and desired validation state, and TDISP status. Optional, guest-contiguous, hypervisor-assigned data pages carry guest data and returned measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports. The hypervisor validates that enough pages are available and reports the required count if not. For TDI information requests, a nonzero 32-byte nonce causes firmware to obtain fresh device measurements before processing the request. Returned data is described by GUID, offset, and length entries.

Secure AVIC uses a private guest-owned backing page per vCPU that must remain present in the nested paging table while the vCPU runs. Guests register or unregister the page by APIC ID; no separate feature bit advertises this event. The termination request follows the MSR termination format, can include 64-bit termination information, and defines reason code 0x01 for unsupported SEV-ES/GHCB protocol features. Unnegotiated NAE events must exit with the “Unsupported Event” code.

SEV-ES guests receive CPUID properties identifying hypervisor operation, SEV support, the encryption bit position, and reduced physical-address bits. Because measured and encrypted AP register state cannot be updated conventionally, SMP startup uses initially measured values, reset-hold requests, and an encrypted, page-aligned AP jump table. This model does not support vCPU hotplug. The SNP AP Creation feature instead lets guests mark a page as a VMSA and create or update AP state through VMGEXIT, enabling hotplug.

For NMI injection, the hypervisor intercepts #DB rather than IRET and uses the guest’s “NMI Complete” message to control subsequent injection. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when indicated by SEV_FEATURES; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

The #HV doorbell page provides host notifications using a shared, host-owned page accessed with C=0. Its PendingEvent field identifies maskable interrupt vectors, NMIs, virtual #MC events, and whether further signals are needed; NoEoiRequired indicates whether an explicit end-of-interrupt is unnecessary. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics. Guests atomically exchange pending-event data, validate observed vectors, and issue either an implicit or explicit EOI. Guests halt with interrupts disabled and recheck pending events immediately after resumption. Doorbell configuration uses VMGEXIT code 0x8000_0014 with SET and QUERY actions.

Kuwait said cleanup of a crude spill in southern Gulf waters would finish this week, with no new oil patches found and the cause still unknown. Saudi-Kuwaiti facilities were reported safe, and an aerial survey was planned.

The invention describes an augmented-reality tracking system for image-guided surgery. A healthcare professional wears a head-mounted device with a display and tracking device, such as a high-speed camera, that tracks patient and tool markers to determine the position and orientation of the head-mounted device, the patient’s anatomy, and the surgical tool. A uniquely patterned patient marker permits tracking without triangulation. The processor overlays a virtual tool and patient anatomy on the display, optionally alongside a transparent view of the actual patient.

When the primary tracking device loses sight of either marker, data from an additional tracking device—such as one on a second head-mounted device or a stationary operating-room device—may be used alone or combined with the primary data. If the patient marker is obscured, an inertial measurement unit and the last known marker position can maintain patient tracking. Tracking algorithms such as a Kalman filter may continue tracking partially obscured markers. The system may generate two-dimensional or three-dimensional images and can continue displaying virtual tool and anatomy information when accurate alignment with the actual patient cannot be maintained.

Investors initially ignored geopolitical and economic risks, focusing on strong growth, corporate profits and President Trump’s tax and deregulation policies, which helped propel stocks into a ninth-year boom. A jobs report then raised fears of wage-driven inflation, while investors worried that central banks’ cheap-money policies might end. Stocks tumbled more than 2%, posting their worst week in two years, as Treasury yields surged and markets worldwide sold off.

Fewer than one in five market corrections become bear markets, and 80% don't. A correction is a drop of at least 10% but no more than 20%, while a bear market is a drop exceeding 20%; corrections have occurred, on average, every year since 1900. The average correction was a 13.5% decline lasting 54 days. Bear markets, by contrast, saw the S&P 500 fall an average of 33%, dropping over 40% in more than a third of cases. The 14 U.S. bear markets of the last 70 years ranged from 45 to 694 days, averaging about a year, and bear markets don't last. From 1980 through 2015, the S&P 500 posted positive returns in 27 of 36 years despite two Gulf wars, 9/11, wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression. Buffett's 2015 Berkshire Hathaway report credited population growth and productivity gains with creating enormous future wealth, calling it "a terrible mistake to bet against America." Rather than panic-selling, investors should understand how markets behave and take responsibility for their own decisions.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters operating from 4 V to 14 V and switching up to 2 MHz. Supported topologies include buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters; external gate drivers are recommended.

Primary outputs include OUTA alone or OUTA/OUTB, while synchronous-rectifier outputs include SRA alone or SRA/SRB, depending on the device. Each output has roughly 150 mA peak-current capability. OUTB and SRB operate only with the 50% duty-cycle limit, supported by the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. Synchronous-rectifier outputs remain off during soft start and begin switching when the soft-start voltage exceeds 1 V.

The TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP provide independent programmable dead times through PS and SP resistors; the TPS7H5003-SP uses a typical fixed 50 ns dead time. Leading-edge blank time is fixed at a typical 50 ns for the TPS7H5003-SP and resistor-programmable for the other devices. Recommended resistor values are 10–300 kΩ. Pulse skipping is used when COMP is below 0.3 V at the rising clock edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%, reducing startup-current problems and maintaining the required output voltage. With both primary outputs active at a 50% duty-cycle limit, equal pulses are skipped to preserve transformer volt-second balance.

Maximum duty cycle is programmable on the TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP: connecting DCL to VLDO permits 100%, leaving it floating permits 75%, and connecting it to AVSS permits 50%. Only the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP support the 50% limit; the TPS7H5004-SP requires that setting.

CS_ILIM senses primary current for PWM control and overcurrent protection. Primary outputs turn on with the internal clock and turn off when sensed peak current reaches the COMP/2 comparison level, including a 150 mV offset. A 1.05 V nominal CS_ILIM threshold initiates hiccup operation. During an overcurrent, cycle-by-cycle limiting charges CHICC with an 80 µA pulsed current until it reaches 0.6 V. Switching then stops, CHICC is discharged from 1 V to 0.3 V, and soft start restarts. A minimum CHICC value of 3.3 nF is recommended.

The FAULT pin supports external fault detection. A typical threshold above 0.6 V sustained for the specified 0.4–1.4 µs pulse width shuts down switching and discharges SS. After FAULT falls below 0.5 V, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles before restarting soft start.

Slope compensation through RSC mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; the minimum stability value is 0.5 times the inductor falling-current slope, and the recommended value is equal to that slope. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be used, with Type 2A including an additional CHF capacitor. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and permits restart below 160°C.

A 500 kHz, 5 V synchronous push-pull example using the TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs selects a 205 kΩ frequency resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns, a 49.9 kΩ LEB resistor, and a 33 nF soft-start capacitor giving approximately 7.5 ms start-up. The example uses a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary FETs, 80 V synchronous rectifiers, a 0.47 µH output inductor, and 2.3 mF total output capacitance for radiation-induced transient mitigation. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5 Ω sense resistor provide cycle-by-cycle limiting near 35 A. Type 2A compensation uses 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF, while RSC uses 102 kΩ.

Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching-node and gate-drive traces, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, joining analog and power grounds at one point, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and using adequately wide high-current traces. VIN requires at least 0.1 µF of ceramic bypass capacitance, with additional bulk capacitance recommended when the supply is remote.

The passage urges Congress to pursue moderate reforms through regulation rather than government ownership of industry. It argues that combinations of capital, like those of labor, are necessary and cannot be wholly prevented, while laws forbidding all combinations are ineffective and harmful because they force honest businesses into technical violations. Harmful combinations should instead be rigorously supervised, and railroad agreements should be permitted when sanctioned by the Interstate Commerce Commission and published. It recommends early consideration of amending existing law to address these problems.

On taxation, it maintains that some taxes, including real-estate and state franchise taxes, are best levied locally, while others are better imposed nationally to prevent burdens from shifting among states. It supports adding graduated federal inheritance and, if possible, income taxes. Tax reform should distribute governmental burdens more equitably and treat rich and poor equally with justice and moderation.
After a Frankston police pursuit, a 17-year-old girl and 18-year-old man were arrested over a stolen-plated car; a third person remains on the run.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018 reported unaudited net sales of $61.137 billion, up 16% from $52.896 billion a year earlier. Gross margin was $23.422 billion, or 38.3% of sales, versus $20.591 billion, or 38.9%. Operating income increased to $15.894 billion from $14.097 billion, and net income rose to $13.822 billion from $11.029 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.73, compared with $2.10. For the first six months, net sales were $149.430 billion, operating income was $42.168 billion, net income was $33.887 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $6.63.

Second-quarter sales increased across all geographic segments and for most product categories. iPhone sales rose 14% to $38.032 billion, iPad sales increased 6% to $4.113 billion, Services sales grew 31% to $9.190 billion, and Other Products sales rose 38% to $3.954 billion. Mac sales were unchanged at $5.848 billion. Geographic sales were $24.841 billion in the Americas, $13.846 billion in Europe, $13.024 billion in Greater China, $5.468 billion in Japan, and $3.958 billion in the rest of Asia Pacific. Stronger foreign currencies favorably affected sales and gross margin. Apple began shipping HomePod in February 2018 and introduced a new 9.7-inch iPad compatible with Apple Pencil during March.

At March 31, 2018, Apple reported $367.502 billion of assets, $240.624 billion of liabilities, and $126.878 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $45.059 billion, while short- and long-term marketable securities totaled $222.167 billion. During the first six months, Apple generated $43.423 billion of operating cash and $15.120 billion from investing activities, while financing activities used $33.773 billion. The company repurchased $32.851 billion of common stock and paid $6.529 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

Apple adopted accounting standards governing excess tax benefits on equity awards and the reclassification of tax effects from accumulated other comprehensive income. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act reduced the U.S. statutory rate from 35% to 21% and resulted in a provisional $38.0 billion deemed repatriation tax payable. First-half tax expense was $9.311 billion, and the effective tax rates were 14.5% for the quarter and 21.6% for the six months. The company also disclosed $9.5 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits and continued to appeal the European Commission’s €13 billion Irish state-aid assessment, plus €1 billion in interest.

The company had $12.0 billion of commercial paper and $111.137 billion of term debt outstanding. It used derivatives to manage foreign-currency and interest-rate exposure and held marketable securities with $3.705 billion of unrealized losses, none of which were considered other-than-temporarily impaired. Apple’s existing repurchase authorization totaled $210 billion, of which $199.6 billion had been used, and the board authorized an additional $100 billion program on May 1, 2018. The company also reported 112.384 million outstanding restricted stock units and $11.4 billion of unrecognized share-based compensation cost expected to be recognized over 2.8 years.

Risk disclosures included concentrated and limited-source component supply, reliance on a small number of Asian manufacturing partners, foreign-exchange exposure, product pricing pressure, and potential gross-margin pressure. Apple reported future minimum lease payments of $9.8 billion and noncancelable purchase obligations exceeding one year of $8.3 billion. In the VirnetX litigation, verdicts awarded damages of $440 million and $503 million in two cases, both subject to ongoing appeals or proceedings. Apple anticipated third-quarter fiscal 2018 gross margin of 38.0% to 38.5%.

A May 18, 2001 Dow Jones column said California’s $43 billion in long-term electricity contracts had lost about $6.5 billion in value as western power prices fell and demand declined. Sellers were unlikely to cancel because prices remained favorable, but the column argued the state should address supply-demand imbalances before buying power and had missed an opportunity to purchase summer electricity at $325 per megawatt-hour.

Options volatility fell to near an eight-month low for technology stocks as investors anticipated range-bound markets and sold options for upfront income, particularly through covered-call strategies. Activity included Ericsson and Microsoft options, bullish trading in Cree, and an Enron spread indicating expectations that its stock would remain above $50 by mid-June. Analysts noted risks from both sudden market declines and periods of heightened volatility.

Saudi Arabia selected eight international oil companies for three natural-gas projects requiring about $25 billion in initial investment. ExxonMobil, Shell, BP and Phillips were selected for the approximately $15 billion South Ghawar project, with no leader yet named. ExxonMobil would lead the Red Sea project with stakes for Occidental Petroleum and Enron. Shell, TotalFinaElf and Conoco were selected for the Shaybah project, whose leader also remained undecided.

Saudi Arabia was expected to sign memoranda of understanding in early June and announce leaders for South Ghawar and Shaybah by June 5. Company stakes, management arrangements and financial terms were still unresolved. Saudi Aramco was expected to hold equity and oversee the projects while consortia operated downstream segments; the Saudis would retain final approval authority. The awards represented a major reopening of the kingdom’s energy sector to foreign investment. Shell and the U.S. government welcomed the selections, while Chevron, Eni and Marathon were not chosen. Analysts expected the projects to offer returns of 10% to 15% and potentially improve foreign companies’ prospects for future access to Saudi oil.

Penn State will end student-led outdoor trips next semester after determining that the Outing, Caving and SCUBA clubs’ activities were too risky due to remote locations, poor cell service and distance from emergency services. Student leaders said they were not consulted. The university will replace them with a university-operated program, which students say costs more.

The case study traces FTX’s rise and collapse through the experiences of founder Sam Bankman-Fried, Nishad Singh, Gary Wang, and Caroline Ellison. Singh, who had been an honors student, competitive ultra-marathon runner, and electrical engineering graduate, joined Alameda Research and eventually led engineering at FTX. By early 2022, FTX was the world’s second-largest cryptocurrency exchange, reportedly reporting $1.02 billion in 2021 revenue, nine million customer accounts, and a $32 billion valuation.

Bankman-Fried studied mathematics and physics at MIT, worked at Jane Street, and adopted effective altruism and its “earning to give” philosophy. He and Tara Mac Aulay co-founded Alameda in 2017, with Wang as CTO and Singh as director of engineering. Alameda initially traded crypto arbitrage profits before moving to Hong Kong. In 2018, most of Alameda’s management and employees resigned after trading losses and Bankman-Fried’s failure to account for more than $4 million in XRP; Wang, Singh, and new employee Ellison remained. Bankman-Fried continued to hold a 90% stake in Alameda.

Bankman-Fried and Wang founded FTX in May 2019. Headquartered in the Bahamas and incorporated in Antigua and Barbuda, FTX specialized in derivatives and leveraged crypto trading, which was prohibited in the United States. FTX introduced its own FTT token, which provided trading discounts, could earn interest or serve as collateral, and was traded on secondary markets. Alameda held most FTTs and used them to obtain loans totaling $9.4 billion. Unlike Coinbase’s custody-based model, FTX and Binance emphasized derivatives and leverage, creating greater liquidity and risk-management challenges.

Crypto regulation varied by country and remained unsettled in the United States. The SEC treated cryptocurrencies as securities requiring registration, while the CFTC treated them as commodities. Bankman-Fried favored CFTC oversight, which the passage describes as less aggressive than SEC regulation. FTX operated offshore beyond direct U.S. regulatory jurisdiction, although separate FTX U.S. entities complied with stricter American trading rules.

During the 2022 crypto-market decline, Alameda and FTX spent heavily to support other crypto companies, including Voyager Digital and BlockFi, as Bankman-Fried was promoted as an industry “white knight.” Alameda’s large exposure to FTT made its finances dependent on FTX’s own condition. When CoinDesk leaked Alameda’s balance sheet on November 2, 2022, it showed $14.6 billion in assets, 40% consisting of FTT. Alameda and FTX together held roughly 90% of the tokens, making their stated valuations difficult to validate through the limited market.

Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao announced on November 6 that he would sell his FTT holdings. FTT fell 80% over the next two days, triggering a run on FTX and more than $6 billion in customer withdrawals within 72 hours. A balance sheet shared by Bankman-Fried showed approximately $8.9 billion in liabilities against only about $890 million in liquid assets. Unable to secure emergency financing, Bankman-Fried sought help from Zhao, but Binance declined to acquire FTX. The Bahamian government froze FTX’s assets on November 10, and FTX and 100 related entities filed for bankruptcy on November 11. Bankman-Fried resigned, and more than one million creditors were identified.

Bankman-Fried was arrested in the Bahamas and charged in the United States on December 12 with eight counts involving fraud, money laundering, wire and commodities fraud, securities fraud, and campaign-finance violations. He pleaded not guilty, was extradited to the United States, and initially received $250 million bail. His bail was revoked in August 2023, and he remained detained pending trial. Wang and Ellison pleaded guilty and cooperated with prosecutors. Ellison acknowledged that she, Bankman-Fried, and Wang knew Alameda had used FTX customer funds to meet its liabilities.

Singh pleaded guilty in February 2023 to six counts, including conspiracy to commit securities fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and campaign-finance violations. He admitted writing code that enabled the diversion of FTX customer funds to Alameda, making illegal political contributions, concealing the source of those contributions, and inflating FTX’s 2021 revenue by roughly $50 million through fabricated and backdated transactions. Singh said he learned in September 2022 that billions in customer deposits had been transferred to Alameda. Although he remained at FTX after acknowledging his own role in granting Alameda special privileges, he did not report the conduct or resign.

The SEC’s civil complaint alleged that FTX and Alameda diverted customer funds, commingled them with Alameda assets, concealed Alameda’s debt from lenders, and used the funds for trading, technology investments, real estate, political contributions, and personal spending. FTX allegedly gave Alameda a customer-funded line of credit that reached $65 billion, allowed its FTT collateral to fall below required margins, and used altered code to permit negative balances. The complaint also said FTX and Alameda overstated the value of illiquid FTT holdings and misrepresented asset segregation and customer protections to investors and customers. Four executives, including Bankman-Fried, received $4.1 billion in loans from Alameda.

The collapse prompted scrutiny of FTX’s investors, auditors, regulators, customers, executives, and celebrity endorsers. Investors had provided $1.8 billion without demanding stronger governance or financial audits. FTX’s outside auditors did not examine its internal controls, while the company lacked an independent board, accounting department, and CFO. Questions also arose over whether offshore regulation, weak enforcement, celebrity promotions, and employees’ failure to report misconduct contributed to the losses.

Android 8.0 Oreo introduces refinements including Picture-in-Picture (PiP), Notification Dots, Smart Text Selection, notification snoozing, and an Autofill Framework. PiP extends multitasking beyond split-screen by allowing supported apps to continue playing in a movable floating window. Listed compatible apps include Chrome, Duo, Play Movies & TV, Play Services, Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC, though YouTube requires YouTube Red. The guide demonstrates PiP in Chrome by playing a YouTube video, entering fullscreen, and pressing Home. The floating window can be moved, paused, closed, restored to fullscreen, or dismissed by dragging it to the bottom. PiP support must also be enabled in the app’s special-access settings.

In this trespass-to-try-title and partition action over an undivided half-interest in the Mastin Latham league, the Texas Supreme Court held that Latham’s 1839 instrument to William F. Henderson was an absolute deed, not an executory contract. The recital that Henderson had cleared, located, surveyed, and paid government dues referred to completed acts, as Latham’s land grant had issued in 1835 and Henderson testified that the services had already been rendered or paid. The partition clause merely provided for an equal division and Latham’s selection of halves. Even if it created a condition subsequent, no forfeiture occurred because Latham never elected to enforce it or take legal action, and an assignee could not invoke the condition.

The defenses of stale demand and the three-, five-, and ten-year limitation periods therefore failed. The possession did not satisfy the ten-year period, no evidence showed payment of taxes for the five-year defense, and the occupants held as Latham’s tenants in opposition to Beaton’s later chain of title, leaving no title or color of title for the three-year defense. Beaton also lacked the required privity for the ten-year defense, and the Wood heirs’ deed failed to convey title because authority and proper acknowledgment for a married grantor were not proven. The court reversed the judgment for the defendants and remanded the case, declining to render judgment for Henderson because the parties’ respective rights to partition required further determination.
Annual Fund gifts support protecting the rule of law, building independent courts, expanding access to justice, and ensuring fair representation; donors get stickers and magnets.

Ukraine and Bitfury signed a memorandum to place the government’s electronic data on a blockchain platform. Bitfury CEO Valery Vavilov described it as the largest government blockchain deal yet. A pilot covering state registers, public services, social security, public health, and energy is expected to launch late this year, followed by expansion across all government areas, including cybersecurity.

Five themes are likely to shape investor and trader thinking next week. The Bank of England is expected to hold rates while publishing meeting minutes and its quarterly inflation report; investors will focus on the growth and inflation outlook, sterling’s recovery, oil prices and global growth. Australia and New Zealand central banks may delay rate hikes as housing markets cool, inflation eases and currencies strengthen. China’s monthly data, including slowing inflation and its US trade surplus, will also be watched amid protectionist rhetoric. The US trade deficit is expected to widen to $51.7 billion from $50.5 billion on record imports and strong demand, while another government shutdown looms. Earnings expectations now exceed those for European companies, which have been hurt by the weak dollar, though their valuations average 9% below US peers. Results from oil majors, banks and drugmakers are due. Among emerging markets, Russia may cut rates, Mexico and Romania may hike, and India is expected to hold at 6% amid budget-related inflation concerns.

The executive reports to Congress that efforts to induce Britain and France to revoke decrees against U.S. commerce failed. Ministers were instructed to offer a targeted suspension of the embargo: rescission by Britain would reopen American trade with Britain while leaving it shut to France if France refused. Britain rejected the proposal, and France did not respond. Because no statutory basis for further suspension existed, the embargo continued as originally authorized. The administration said it had protected mariners and property, provided time for defense, and frustrated violations of neutral rights; Congress must decide how to respond to continuing belligerent measures.

No British redress has been taken for the attack on the frigate Chesapeake, and Britain continues to insist on a disputed preliminary. Other European relations are materially unchanged, though Spanish negotiations have paused amid Spain’s internal crisis. Relations with the Barbary powers are generally harmonious except for the dey of Algiers’s action toward the American consul.

Peace has been maintained with Indian neighbors. Tribes have delivered or sought offenders accused of murdering Americans; tribal attachment, agriculture, and household manufactures are advancing, and one Cherokee division is considering U.S. citizenship. Harbor defenses have been erected, 103 gunboats will be built, additional troops are being recruited, and detachments have enforced the embargo. No general militia or volunteer call was made last season, but units should be ready next season; domestic arms production is expanding.

The embargo has encouraged domestic manufacturing and internal trade. Treasury receipts reached nearly $18 million; after expenses and interest, $2.3 million in debt principal was repaid, leaving nearly $14 million. Total principal discharged reached $33.58 million, reducing annual interest by about $2 million. Congress is urged to consider using future surpluses for roads, canals, rivers, education, and other improvements. In closing, the executive thanks Congress and the public, acknowledges possible errors, and expresses confidence in the republic’s permanence.

The Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for the Village of Orland Park and three police officers in Joseph McGreal’s retaliation and intentional-infliction-of-emotional-distress claims. McGreal alleged he was fired for proposing alternatives to layoffs at a village board meeting, but presented no admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his speech or that it motivated his termination. He also failed to show that the defendants’ stated reasons for firing him—perjury, insubordination, and reckless conduct—were pretextual. Documents he cited predated the meeting, were unrelated, or lacked admissibility, and suspicious timing alone could not defeat summary judgment. For the emotional-distress claim, McGreal offered no evidence of extreme or outrageous conduct or severe distress and acknowledged that his distress was probably garden-variety, which is insufficient under Illinois law.

HoopTactics’ out-of-bounds plays aim to create high-percentage shots with two or three options and predetermined continuations that prevent rushed shots. Teams should prepare for rare full-court pressure situations, often creating a 5-on-4 disadvantage. When leading, a baseline inbound can safely gain possession; use the best available players and shooters, make substitutions, and scout the expected defense. At the end of a game, advance the ball and call timeout if time permits, or inbound safely from the baseline with strong free-throw shooters on the court.

Kyle Freeland pitched 5⅓ innings and hit a two-run double, leading Colorado to an 11-4 win over San Francisco. Every Rockies starter had a hit, with David Dahl, Trevor Story, Nolan Arenado, Gerardo Parra and Ian Desmond contributing extra runs.

The Giants lost starter Jeff Samardzija to shoulder tightness after one inning and rookie reliever Dereck Rodriguez after 3⅓ innings when a Desmond line drive struck his shin and caused cramping. Rodriguez allowed four runs, one earned. Evan Longoria hit two solo homers for San Francisco, and Buster Posey also went deep.

Maddie Sabourin, 18, a high school senior at Darlington School in Rome, Georgia, found a kidney match for her grandfather, Sam Senseney, 63, who has been on the transplant list for six years and receives dialysis three times a week. Although family and friends had been tested without success — with 2,000 others on the Georgia transplant list — Maddie, who competed in the Miss Georgia Outstanding Teen Pageant and raised $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund, learned the day after her 18th birthday that she was a match. Doctors initially said she was too young, but she persuaded them to let her donate. Maddie and her grandfather plan to meet doctors next week to schedule surgery, hoped for within the month; she will miss three weeks of school.

Astronomers at Trinity College Dublin used the James Webb Space Telescope to study the atmosphere and weather of starless rogue planet SIMP-0136. Tracking minute brightness changes as it rotated revealed strong auroras, temperature shifts below 5°C, chemical changes suggesting rotating storms, and constant cloud coverage. At temperatures above 1,500°C, the planet’s clouds consist of sand-like silicate grains.

The observations are described as the most precise measurements yet made of an extrasolar atmosphere and the first direct measurement of changes in atmospheric properties. Multiwavelength data and atmospheric models enabled researchers to estimate temperature, chemical composition, and cloud position. The findings advance understanding of weather beyond the solar system, while future observations with the Extremely Large Telescope and Habitable Worlds Observatory could extend atmospheric studies to diverse exoplanets.

The patent disclosure describes enhanced 5G core architecture and network-slicing mechanisms, particularly Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) selection for isolated network slices. It reviews 5G network functions, including the AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, NEF, NRF, UDM/UDR, NSSF, N3IWF, and AF, along with registration, connection management, PDU sessions, QoS, edge computing, and network-slice selection.

During UE registration, the UE may provide requested S-NSSAI information, a DNN, UE identifiers, PDU-session information, and network-slice isolation information. Three isolation levels are defined: fully isolated slices, which share neither radio access network nor core-network functions; partly isolated slices with a shared radio access network; and partly isolated slices with shared radio access network and AMF.

Accordingly, an NRF, NSSF, or UDM may select an AMF according to requested and subscribed S-NSSAI information, isolation level, UE identity, DNN, local operator policies, and subscription data. The selected AMF may be returned to the radio access network by IP address or fully qualified domain name. The disclosure also describes allowed and configured NSSAI, primary and secondary slices, slice-selection policies, and procedures for simultaneous access to multiple network slices.

In an action by the assignee of W. W. Montague & Co., the plaintiff sought to set aside two deeds of gift made by Louis Helbing to his wife, Louise, on May 15, 1893. The deeds were not recorded until December 11, 1895. Before their recordation, Helbing represented that he owned the conveyed property and obtained approximately $1,000 in credit from Montague & Co. He was solvent when the deeds were executed and retained other property worth about $1,200.

The trial court found that the conveyances were made for love and affection, without intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors, and that Helbing’s apparent ownership resulted from the deeds’ nonrecordation rather than any conduct by his wife. The plaintiff bore the burden of proving fraudulent intent. Although the delayed recordation cast suspicion on the transaction, it was insufficient alone to establish fraud. The court concluded that Helbing’s intent, assessed from all the facts and circumstances, was a question for the trial court, which was required to find no fraudulent intent absent clear evidence to the contrary. The wife’s lack of knowledge was relevant, though her knowledge was not essential if the husband had intended fraud.

The court also upheld the exclusion of evidence concerning goods allegedly concealed under the conveyed house and the wife’s later ownership claim to them. These events occurred nearly four years after the deeds and concerned unrelated personal property; even if erroneously excluded, they could not justify reversal. The judgment and order denying a new trial were affirmed.

Tropical Storm Nate, the Atlantic season’s 15th system, moved toward Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula and threatened the U.S. Gulf Coast, with forecast landfall in southeast Louisiana as a Category 1 hurricane. Louisiana declared an emergency, mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops and ordered coastal evacuations. Nate had killed at least 22 people in Latin America, including 15 in Nicaragua and seven in Costa Rica, where flooding forced 5,000 residents into shelters. September was the most active month on record for Atlantic Accumulated Cyclone Energy, surpassing September 2004, as Harvey, Irma and Maria caused widespread devastation.

A retrospective cross-sectional study examined delayed discharges from the 23-bed Complex Discharge Unit at St James’s Hospital, Dublin, during March 2020–February 2021. Data for 390 adults were obtained from electronic patient records, with prolonged length of stay (LOS) defined as more than 15 days. Kaplan–Meier and stratified Cox regression analyses assessed factors associated with discharge delays.

Most patients were over 65, female, and had multimorbidity. The median CDU LOS was 19.4 days, and infection or sepsis was the most common admission diagnosis. Longer LOS was associated with age, female sex, more than four comorbidities, complications of primary diagnoses, and patient-centred needs. In multivariable analysis, complications arising from primary diagnoses and patient-centred needs—including cognitive, psychosocial, and carer needs—were significant factors across strata. Univariate analysis did not identify healthcare-associated infection, frailty or falls requiring rehabilitation, community-service issues, or complications arising directly from comorbidities as prolonging LOS.

The study concluded that reducing LOS requires addressing diagnostic complications and patient-centred needs. Its findings may support clinical decisions and contingency planning, but interpretation is limited by its single-centre design, sample size, focus on CDU admissions rather than all hospital admissions and readmissions, and incomplete assessment of mortality and readmission.

The article tests a pair-trading strategy involving the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and long-term Treasury ETF (TLT). When SPY falls and TLT rises by more than 1.25 times their respective 50-day average high-low ranges on the same day, the strategy goes long SPY and short TLT, then closes the positions after a specified number of days.

Using data from 2003 through June 2021, the strategy produced an erratic equity curve, a 1.93% CAGR, a 60% win rate, and an average round-trip gain of 0.18%, before commissions and slippage. Performance weakened in later years. The best average result, 0.26%, occurred when positions were closed at the end of the third day; results generally worsened with holding periods longer than five days. Changing the movement threshold above or below 1.25 did not materially improve performance. The article concludes that the strategy is not consistently profitable or tradeable.

OpenAI plans a TikTok-like social app powered by Sora 2, featuring AI-generated videos in a swipeable vertical feed and a recommendation-driven “For You” page, with options to like, comment, or remix.

The Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10) is a passive investment strategy allocating 90% of funds to low-cost, passively managed S&P 500 index ETFs (such as VOO or IVV) and 10% to government or short-term U.S. Treasury bond funds (such as SHY or VGSH). It derives from Warren Buffett's 2013 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, in which he instructed that 90% of his wife's inheritance be placed in a very low-fee stock index fund and 10% in short-term government bonds. The equity portion captures historical growth of the 500 largest U.S. companies, while the bond allocation cushions market volatility and reduces fees relative to actively managed portfolios. Key principles include long-term investing, avoiding market timing and high-fee funds, and rebalancing as the portfolio ages. The portfolio suits beginners and can be built via a lump-sum investment or dollar-cost averaging; optimal choices depend on goals, risk tolerance, and time horizon. Risks include market conditions, economic changes, and geopolitical events, and past performance does not guarantee future results. Capital gains and dividends may be taxed at federal and state levels depending on tax bracket, ETF type, account type, and holding period. Backtests comparing SPY with 10% allocations to SHY, IEI, and TLT showed the SHY version performing slightly worse than SPY, IEI slightly better than SHY, and TLT nearly matching SPY; longer bond maturity adds risk that is generally compensated over time, and underperformance was attributed to the weak 2022 bond market.

Bank of England research suggests that a central bank digital currency (CBDC), designed as a close substitute for bank deposits, could improve monetary policy transmission and quantitative easing. An interest-bearing CBDC offering payment services could strengthen the Bank’s control over policy and accelerate commercial banks’ responses to interest-rate changes. It could also let the central bank purchase assets directly from non-banks, bypassing banks. Researchers say careful design could avoid disruption and protect commercial banks from runs. The Bank is not currently planning to issue a CBDC.

Consuls report that Americans in Cuba lack food and medicines, especially in rural central and eastern areas. Displaced farmers lack work, and local authorities cannot help. Lee estimates 600–800 need support; at least $50,000 is recommended for relief and transportation home.

**People v Schaub** (Mich. Ct. App., Docket No. 231009, decided Nov. 15, 2002) concerned whether sufficient evidence existed at a preliminary examination to bind over Lawrence B. Schaub for trial on a charge of child abandonment under MCL 750.135.

The charge arose from allegations that Schaub transferred possession of his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer posing as a prospective buyer. Schaub's daycare provider testified that he asked her about persons wanting to buy his child. Schaub agreed to sell the child for $10,000 in cash plus a $50,000 promise, relinquishing parental rights and reducing the terms to writing. The officer testified the child was never without care, having been transferred directly from Schaub to the buyer's "son," and that Schaub provided feeding instructions.

The district court dismissed the charge, finding the prosecution had not proven the elements of child abandonment because the child was never placed in a situation where she was without care. The circuit court reversed, reinstated the charge, and bound Schaub over, holding that the evidence showed the intent to wholly abandon and that exposure was established by his failure to inquire into the prospective parents' fitness. The Court of Appeals denied interlocutory leave; the Supreme Court remanded the case for consideration as on leave granted.

Writing for the majority (Hoekstra, J., with Griffin, J., concurring), the court reviewed the statutory-interpretation question de novo and agreed with Schaub. Under Shannon v People (1858), the controlling precedent, the elements of child abandonment are exposure of the child and intent to wholly abandon it, and exposure requires circumstances that subject the child to the hazard of personal injury; leaving a child where it would be certain to be cared for does not constitute exposure. Because Schaub handed the child to a person to care for her, the evidence did not establish exposure, notwithstanding his "repugnant" conduct. The circuit court's order was reversed and the matter remanded.

The court noted that the Legislature responded to the case's publicity by enacting MCL 750.136c, barring the sale or purchase of people, but ex post facto protections preclude applying it to Schaub. The court also stated that Schaub may have committed a common-law felony by attempting to sell his child, but, because no such charge was filed and the prosecutor did not raise the issue, it expressed no opinion; the reversal was without prejudice to such charges.

Judge O'Connell, P.J., dissented, concluding that delivering an infant to total strangers who might be pedophiles or child pornographers constituted exposure, that Shannon's definition of "expose" was dicta, and that under modern societal conditions and caregiver licensing requirements, exposure was a question of fact for the jury; he would have affirmed the circuit court.

Walmart executive Greg Cathey said the retailer plans to make drone delivery available in “most areas that we operate in,” though he provided no timeline. After more than five years of testing, delivery is available at only a handful of Walmart’s 4,600 U.S. locations. The company plans to expand its partnership with Alphabet’s Wing from 100 stores in Atlanta, Charlotte, Houston, Orlando and Tampa to additional locations in Bentonville and Rogers, Arkansas, calling drones a key part of its last-mile strategy.

Cathey said the regulatory environment has made the business viable. The FAA has proposed rules permitting flights beyond visual line of sight, but they remain in a public-comment period and are not expected to take effect until next year. Technical, regulatory, financial, infrastructure and customer-acceptance hurdles mean widespread delivery is likely several years away.

Walmart is working with Wing, one of the few companies permitted to conduct package deliveries beyond visual line of sight in Dallas. The retailer has surpassed 300,000 drone deliveries, twice the 150,000 announced in June, and has also experimented with Zipline and DroneUp.

The editor acknowledges assistance from Reagan Library and Library of Congress staff, the Estate of Secretary Haig, the CIA, and the Estate of Jeane Kirkpatrick, as well as document recommendations by Office of Historian staff. The editor conducted the research and selected and annotated the documentation under Adam M. Howard’s direction; Kathleen B. Rasmussen reviewed the volume, Chris Tudda coordinated declassification, and Kerry Hite performed copy and technical editing.

Sources included public publications such as the Public Papers of the Presidents, Department of State Bulletin, Congressional Record, Documents on Disarmament, Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents, and congressional reports. Reagan Library materials included Reagan’s pre-presidential and presidential speeches, 1980 campaign and transition files, and White House speech and subject files. Classified sources included presidential papers, White House staff files, George Shultz’s donated papers, State Department Policy Planning and Directors’ files, Haig memoranda, and Central Foreign Policy File reels containing cables, memoranda, letters, briefing papers, and airgrams. These State Department collections are expected eventually to become part of Record Group 59 at the National Archives’ College Park facility.

The Golden Cross strategy uses 50-day and 200-day moving averages, buying when the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day and selling when it crosses below. A daily-bar S&P 500 backtest since 1960 produced 33 trades, averaging about 350 days; $100,000 grew to $7.2 million excluding reinvested dividends. The strategy had a 79% win rate, 15.8% average trade gain, and 6.8% annual return versus 7.2% for buy-and-hold. Invested 70% of the time, it recorded a 33% drawdown versus 56% for buy-and-hold and a stated 9.6% risk-adjusted return. The strategy aims to capture long-term bullish trends and reduce bear-market losses, though it is prone to whipsaws.

A cross-sectional quantitative study assessed antiretroviral therapy (ART) non-adherence among HIV patients in the catchment area of Kibungo Referral Hospital, Rwanda. The target population was 3,508 adults receiving ART, with 424 participants recruited from 13 health centers and the referral hospital between March 25 and April 30, 2024. Data were collected using a structured, context-modified questionnaire with acceptable reliability and validity.

Overall, 13% of participants were non-adherent to ART and 87% were adherent. Bivariate analyses found significant associations between non-adherence and age, education, household size, multiple sexual partners, travel and waiting times, smoking, HIV-status disclosure, and several psychological and behavioral factors. Multivariate analysis identified age under 31 years, lack of tertiary education, stigma, perception that ART was ineffective, and failure to integrate ART into daily routines as significant factors associated with non-adherence. Setting an alarm as a medication reminder was not significantly associated with adherence.

Kibungo’s 13% non-adherence rate was lower than rates reported in Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda, South Africa, and the United States and Europe, but slightly higher than the 10.2% reported at Ruhengeri Referral Hospital. The study recommends targeted education, stigma-reduction efforts, routine integration of ART, and broader support systems. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, reliance on self-reported data, and limited generalizability beyond the study setting.

In *Milan v. Duckworth*, the court granted summary judgment for the prison defendants, who denied Milan a visit with Judy Ballard following his escape attempt.
