The paper examines technical-information management in industrial plant lifecycles, where large, heterogeneous equipment bases and proprietary back-end systems make information exchange labor-intensive, error-prone, and costly. Existing standards for business documents, invoices, equipment integration, and technical data address only parts of the problem, while manual methods such as spreadsheets, email, and physical media remain common. The research asks what architecture can enable digitally structured technical-information exchange across business partners and how it can scale to networks with heterogeneous systems.

The proposed architecture combines an open consortium with a network of information mediators. The consortium creates and maintains common business practices and information structures, extending existing standards where necessary. Mediators use agreed APIs, routing, business-process coordination, and matchmaking features to connect multiple business roles. Each party needs only one adapter, which maps its proprietary systems to the common format and shields partners from internal system changes. The approach also recognizes hierarchical plant information, device- and product-level data, engineering designs, and attachments.

A prototype implemented the mediator as a web application platform. Because no open APIs or agreed formats yet existed, spreadsheet import and export applications used XML mappings to transfer equipment information between dedicated storage silos. Tasks represented maintenance requests and equipment orders, allowing parties to review, validate, enrich, and exchange data. Experiments with two equipment suppliers and two plant operators successfully delivered valve and pump information for maintenance and production-unit renewal cases, sometimes including export to recipients’ back-end systems.

The prototype demonstrated practical utility but lacked an open consortium, standardized APIs, actual back-end adapters, and a multi-mediator network. Future work includes forming the consortium, developing adapters and mediator networking, expanding support to engineering-design information and additional business processes, and extending the approach to financing, logistics, manufacturing, and marine industries. The authors identify ecosystem organization as the main challenge and identify semantic technologies as a possible aid to data conversion.

In *Meech v. City of Buffalo*, property owners challenged a second assessment for a sewer improvement. Buffalo initially assessed $1,058.63 and contracted with Robert J. Randolph for that amount. Randolph encountered extensive, unforeseen quicksand that made completion impossible at the agreed price, so the common council allowed an additional $588.13 and assessed it on benefited property to complete the sewer. The court held that Buffalo’s charter authorized a further assessment when the original assessment proved insufficient and that the unforeseen obstruction created such a deficiency. It also held that the city could modify the contractor’s agreement when circumstances justified doing so and need not first exhaust remedies against the contractor. The order granting a new trial was affirmed, and judgment was entered against the plaintiffs.

This qualitative case study examined how physical education teacher education students developed 21st-century competencies through peer mentoring in a 14-week first-year movement education course in Türkiye. Participants included three peer mentors, 25 peer learners, and the course lecturer. Lessons combined basic movement skills, storytelling, gamification, social media, group work, and reflective meetings; peer learners later designed and delivered their own teaching activities.

Three themes emerged. Peer learners excluded members who did not contribute, although they supported peers who showed effort, while peer mentors divided responsibilities, adapted, and completed tasks despite disagreements. Storytelling course content made learning more permanent and strengthened participants’ awareness of their teacher roles. Connecting movement skills to familiar stories, games, films, and television programs helped students retain knowledge, relate it to daily life, and recognize skills in new contexts.

The findings indicate that peer mentoring provides realistic teaching experience, develops communication, cooperation, responsibility, leadership, creativity, technology, and problem-solving skills, and can bridge students and teaching staff. The study recommends integrating this approach throughout teacher preparation, sustaining peer mentoring at all grade levels, and conducting long-term research on storytelling-based course design.

The Korean diet emphasizes whole, unprocessed foods, including vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fermented foods, and broth-based dishes. It is generally low in sugar, calories, and saturated fat, while limiting processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Its plant-based, high-fiber foods and probiotics may support digestion and overall wellbeing, and its smaller portions and emphasis on physical activity can contribute to weight loss. Potential drawbacks include high sodium from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium, digestive irritation from spicy ingredients, and the need to control carbohydrate-heavy portions. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low-carbohydrate, and gluten-free needs.

Week 6’s reshuffled college football Power Rankings focus on offenses as the 2025 season nears the midpoint. Penn State and Texas fell out of the Top 25 following losses to UCLA and Florida, respectively, while three teams joined the rankings. Ohio State’s defense held opponents to five points per game, Oregon relied on Dante Moore and freshman running backs, and Miami improved to 5-0 after Carson Beck threw for 241 yards and four touchdowns in a 28-22 win over Florida State. Texas A&M rose to the top five after a 31-9 win and a dominant defensive showing, while Oklahoma continued to seek a reliable running game. Indiana averaged 47.8 points per game but converted only two of eight fourth downs. Texas Tech reached 5-0 with five wins by more than 20 points, Alabama produced 486 yards against Vanderbilt, and Cincinnati totaled 1,082 yards over two games. Michigan scored 17 rushing touchdowns, while LSU’s run game, Iowa State’s defense, Georgia’s offensive-line continuity and Texas’s turnover and sack problems were cited as concerns.

The Citi Simplicity® Card advertises a 21-month 0% intro APR on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases, with no annual fee, late fees, or penalty rate. Balance transfers completed within four months of account opening incur a 3% fee (minimum $5); later transfers cost 5%. The variable APR afterward is 17.99%–28.74%, based on creditworthiness, and applicants need an application and a good-to-excellent recommended credit score of 670–850. The advertisement estimates savings of $2,428 on a $5,000 balance transfer from a card charging 24% APR, though approval is not guaranteed and intro APR periods may change. Citi and Citigroup are advertising partners of Motley Fool Money, which states that compensation does not affect product ratings or editorial opinions.

The passage characterizes the Russian cruiser commander’s seizure of American seamen from the Cape Horn Pigeon and their forced, under-protest service aboard a Russian vessel as an unlawful violation of their nationality, personal liberty, and natural rights. It states that the crew’s acceptance at Vladivostok of compensation for their labor did not waive claims for services, injury to national pride, and violations of personal liberty. Their abandonment without food or shelter and inadequate housing in a jail created further claims for indemnity. Numerous arbitration precedents are cited to support awarding interest, and full damages and interest are expected.

The passage then estimates the vessel’s loss of use through its average whale catch. Captain Scullun’s estimate of eight whales, supported by affidavits estimating six to ten, and his average yield of 1,250 pounds of bone per whale are considered reasonable; testimony establishes 100 barrels of oil per whale. Bone was valued at $5 per pound in August, the applicable price for the September 10 seizure, and oil at $13 per barrel. An average catch of eight whales supported Scullun’s $1,800 deduction.

Google launched three experimental photography apps across Android and iOS, using advances in phone hardware and computer vision. Storyboard turns videos into on-device comic layouts with selected frames and six visual styles. Selfissimo! automates black-and-white selfies, capturing images when users stop moving. Scrubbies, for iOS, enables finger-controlled video speed and direction to create shareable loops. Google says the technologies remain under active research and performance may vary.

- Version 2 adds a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap through the GHCB MSR protocol so guests can discover optional hypervisor capabilities. Advertised features include base SEV-SNP support, AP VMSA creation, restricted injection and its timer, APIC ID lists, multiple VMPLs, SEV-ES page-state changes, TDISP trusted I/O, and GHCB GPA unregistration. Full specification support is otherwise mandatory, and some features may depend on others.

- The guest selects a 4K-aligned GHCB location and exposes it to the hypervisor as decrypted shared memory. Hardware saves and restores its guest physical address through VMCB offset 0xa0, while the guest accesses it through MSR 0xc001_0130, which the hypervisor must not intercept. The lower 12 bits of that MSR encode guest requests and hypervisor responses.

- The SEV Information request supplies minimum and maximum GHCB protocol versions and the SEV page-table encryption bit number before the GHCB address is established. Guests must select a supported version and terminate if none is acceptable. A separate CPUID request protocol returns one register value per VMGEXIT; it does not support functions requiring nonzero subleaves or function 0x0000_000d.

- SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first using it for VMGEXIT. The protocol can obtain a hypervisor-preferred GPA or register a guest-selected GPA, automatically replacing any prior registration. Registration failure or a mismatch requires hypervisor termination, and each VMPL may register its own GPA when multi-VMPL is advertised. Guests may also unregister the current GPA.

- Negotiation examples show guests handling intercepted CPUID operations through #VC exceptions, obtaining the encryption bit, configuring page tables, allocating and sharing the GHCB page, and writing its GPA to the MSR. SNP guests additionally register the GHCB GPA.

- The SNP Secrets Page reserves 96 bytes for guest use, including per-VMPL guest-message sequence numbers, an AP jump-table address, and guest-defined storage. Firmware may pass the Secrets and CPUID pages to an operating system through the EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table.

- Non-automatic exits generate a #VC exception whose error code matches the underlying VMEXIT code. Guests populate the GHCB, invoke VMGEXIT, and resume after it to consume hypervisor results. VALID_BITMAP identifies supplied fields; guests provide SW_EXITCODE and two information fields, while hypervisors return the information fields. The protocol covers protected I/O, MSR accesses, hypercalls, nested-page MMIO, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL changes, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC, and termination.

- Page-state requests use a shared-buffer structure supporting up to 253 entries and private, shared, PSMASH, and UNSMASH operations. Progress is recorded so interrupted requests can resume. SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages, require firmware sequencing, and may use rate limiting to protect against excessive requests. Extended requests can return certificates and attestation data.

- SEV-SNP AP creation lets a guest create, update, or remove an AP’s vCPU state at a specified VMPL after using RMPADJUST to designate a VMSA page. Secure AVIC supports a private backing page per vCPU. Restricted injection provides doorbell, IPI, and emulated APIC timer operations.

- Under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, measured AP register state cannot be changed for later resets, so initial boots use the original measured values and subsequent boots use reset-hold procedures, an AP jump table, or SNP AP creation. AP jump tables are encrypted, page-aligned, 4K pages. Restricted Injection requires AP creation, which also permits vCPU hotplug; otherwise hotplug is unsupported.

- NMI delivery requires the hypervisor to avoid intercepting IRET and to intercept #DB, using an “NMI Complete” message to control further injection. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled in SEV_FEATURES; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

- Restricted Injection uses a shared host-owned #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host emulates APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior, while the guest atomically exchanges these fields when acknowledging interrupts or completing EOIs. The specified HLT convention prevents missed or premature interrupt delivery. A noncooperative host may cause denial of service but is not permitted to corrupt host integrity.

Pumpkin is a nutrient-rich fruit in the Cucurbitaceae family. One cup of cooked pumpkin provides 52 calories, 3 grams of fiber, 13 grams of carbohydrate, iron, potassium, vitamin E, and the carotenoids alpha- and beta-carotene, lutein, and zeaxanthin. The passage highlights pumpkin’s potential benefits for cardiovascular health, immunity, eye health, dementia and cognition, and blood pressure. Potassium supports blood-pressure control and cardiovascular health, while carotenoids have anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties; lutein may reduce macular-degeneration risk, and beta-carotene may help protect against cataracts. Pumpkin’s phytonutrients are also presented as supporting immune and brain health. It can be used in salads, soups, desserts, preserves, muffins, quick breads, or seasoned and baked like sweet potato. The passage concludes with the credentials of registered dietitian and nutritionist Doug Cook, coauthor of several nutrition books.

A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and computational taxonomy map the social-science literature on large language models (LLMs). A search of seven databases through September 19, 2025 identified 64,717 records and included 270 eligible English-language studies from 2020–2025. The corpus spans journals, preprints, and conference papers, with most studies published from 2023 onward and across computer science, psychology, sociology, HCI, economics, education, and general science.

Study 1 embedded titles and abstracts with Sentence-BERT, applied K-means clustering and UMAP visualization, and used latent Dirichlet allocation to interpret each cluster. Internal validation, resampling stability, and topic modeling supported three stable domains:

- **LLM as Social Minds** (111 studies): theory-of-mind and other mind-like capacities, moral and social reasoning, bias, self-regulation and ideological consistency, strategic deception, and resulting trust risks. Evidence increasingly emphasizes robustness to prompt perturbations, removal of superficial cues, and distinctions between genuine inference and prompt-driven performance.
- **LLM Societies** (99 studies): interactions among LLM agents, generative-agent simulations, cooperation and games, collective learning and polarization, institutional design, collective decision-making, and deception within multi-agent systems. Research shows that memory, roles, rules, sanctions, and other institutional scaffolds can produce population-level norms and coordination.
- **LLM–Human Interactions** (60 studies): perception and trust, anthropomorphism, affect and communication, collaboration and creativity, learning, productivity, inequality, social engineering, and governance. The literature treats this interface as a joint human–LLM system shaped by user beliefs, framings, interfaces, and institutions.

Study 2 compared these partitions with classifications independently produced and reconciled by two experts. Agreement was strong: cross-validated Macro-F1 was **0.954 ± 0.018**, NMI was **0.811**, and ARI was **0.867**. Low-silhouette and discrepant studies marked conceptual boundaries, such as work combining individual mind attribution with multi-agent interaction, collective decision-making without explicit agent interaction, and human interaction studies framed around either individual cognition or societal processes.

The authors present the taxonomy as a reproducible framework of complementary levels of analysis rather than competing schools. It provides distinct evidentiary standards for individual-level behavioral claims, society-level institutional claims, and human-facing interactional claims. Proposed priorities include anti-shortcut testing of cognitive attributes, mechanism-focused agent simulations, and interventions that calibrate trust, transparency, verification, and reliance.

Limitations include restriction to English-language literature, a September 2025 cutoff, sensitivity to representation and clustering choices, narrative rather than pooled-effect synthesis because of heterogeneity, and the inability of semantic agreement metrics to establish causal structure. The paper concludes that LLM sociality should be evaluated primarily through situated performance and institutional adequacy rather than anthropomorphic resemblance to persons.

The 2017 report analyzes the global smart service robots market from 2012 to 2022 using SWOT analysis and covers production, consumption, revenue, pricing, capacity, market share, and CAGR. It examines personal and professional service robots across commercial and home applications in North America, Europe, China, Japan, Southeast Asia, and India. Manufacturer profiles include company information, products, competitors, capacity, production, revenue, price, gross margin, and business overviews for 14 named key players.

Lincoln County’s Lady Lynx defeated Laughlin 3-2 in Thursday’s Homecoming match after winning the first two sets and nearly finishing in four. Mental lapses during Laughlin’s serve runs prompted Coach Chantel Holt to stress staying focused and choosing to win. Lincoln won the deciding set, reaching 15 while holding the Cougars under 10 points. Holt said substitutions and changes built camaraderie and gave players opportunities. The Lady Lynx next host Calvary at 3 and 4 p.m.

The passage describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an AMD-created optional extension to SEV and SNP firmware ABIs that facilitates page migration — copying page content while updating virtual-to-physical mappings. Support is detected via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register, and TMPM requires IOMMU enablement. In tiered memory systems, software monitors access patterns and migrates frequently accessed data to faster tiers. TMPM's two key capabilities are pausing DMA traffic to a page while it is copied and its IOMMU page table entry updated (enabling safe migration of pages under active I/O use), and acting as a trusted agent that can migrate pages owned by SEV/SNP-protected guests.

Two commands are described: PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, which migrates pages that are concurrent DMA targets and requires the location of the relevant IOMMU host page table entry (hPTE), with source pages DMA-mapped via IOMMU host page tables (only one such table per migrated physical page) and an IOMMU host page table constructed to map the memory containing those tables (the host page table virtual address, HPTVA); and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, which migrates guest pages in SNP systems, replacing the SNP PAGE_MOVE command, with source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destination pages in the new Pre-Migration state. The Pre-Migration state resembles Guest-Invalid but holds a Platform Specific ASID value (PS_ASID_VAL, never associated with a guest, GPA ignored); the HV/OS supplies PS_ASID_VAL as input to RMPUpdate, and software uses RMPUpdate to return such a page to Hypervisor state. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO also supports migrating hypervisor state pages in SNP systems, with source and destination pages returned to Hypervisor state.

Commands may move multiple pages — up to 128 — described by a Page Migration List of up to 128 entries that need not be adjacent, may reference multiple guests, and have no order-dependence within or between commands. The list must begin at a 4KB system physical address. Entries are updated with per-page Page Migration Status: PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires inspecting individual entries, and any other code means no migrations executed. A status may indicate a page was not migrated without error (for example when its RMP entry is unavailable due to a concurrent RMPUPDATE), which software may retry — the retryable code is PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE.

Performance guidance includes that commands with 16 or more pages have significantly higher bandwidth, with maximum performance at 128 pages per command; the ring buffer command input queue should stay ahead of the engine, interrupts are better requested at the end of a command sequence (via NOP or Interrupt on Complete) rather than per command, and TMPM can interrupt on a low-water mark to allow refilling. Data structures that cannot be migrated include IOMMU data structures accessed via SPA (host page tables, command buffer, event log), IOMMU page tables mapping the vIOMMU Private Address Space, vIOMMU pinned backing storage buffers, and the ring buffer and argument pages; the HV/OS is responsible for not issuing migrations of these. Because the engine may modify IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically and set host Access and Dirty bits, host software must avoid concurrent hPTE modifications, achievable by pausing ring buffer processing or careful command creation.

Firmware can be reloaded, but only with no operations in flight: the HV/OS pauses operations, tears down the ring buffer, and issues a reload command via the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol (publication #57299), disabling the IOMMUs' PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits as best practice. Reloading with the ring buffer still initialized returns PM_MX_INVALID_RELOAD_REQUEST; the reload firmware must be the same or a greater version; and software must always check ENGINE_READY before communicating with the firmware. Reload methodology varies by EPYC family, determined by executing PM_GET_CAPABILITIES and reading the FW_VER_Major field, which represents the family (not 1:1); EPYC Family 19h is indicated by 71 decimal, and failure of this command means TMPM update is unavailable. For 19h, the client places the firmware image in system memory and builds a reload firmware header (MBOX_BUFFER currently 20/0x14 bytes, including Image_addr_lo and Image_addr_hi fields), and accesses ASP registers via a PCI driver: poll the Command/Status Ready flag to 1, write the header physical address into CmdRspBufAddr_Lo/Hi, write 0x70 to the Command ID field with other fields zero and update the register, loop while Ready is 0, then read the header's Status field together with the Command/Status register status.

Finally, because commands are processed asynchronously, developers may send single commands of 1–X migration entries; in that case the Tail pointer should not advance more than one command entry beyond the Head pointer so processing pauses when the queue empties, optionally with a queue-empty interrupt. The TMPM hardware can only move data from one 4KB-aligned page to another, so all system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned.

The passage is a collection of ESPN NFL headlines and a story about the 49ers' injury report before their Thursday night game against the Rams. The Niners ruled out quarterback Brock Purdy (toe soreness), receiver Ricky Pearsall (right knee) and receiver Jauan Jennings (ribs); Purdy said the short Sunday-to-Thursday turnaround would make it tough to heal. Mac Jones is expected to make his third start in the first five games; he won in Weeks 2 and 3 against Arizona and Jacksonville, is back to full strength after a sprained knee, and called the Rams defense the best in the NFL, noting their multiple schemes (9th in yards allowed per game at 284.5, fifth in defensive EPA at 13.78, tied for second in sacks at 14). With only two practice squad receivers healthy and one open spot at receiver, the 49ers are expected to start Robinson and Bourne, and a tight end was also ruled out. After Thursday, the Niners travel to Tampa Bay in Week 6. Other headlines cover Week 5 power rankings, playoff and 2026 draft projections, trades, betting odds, the Browns benching Flacco for Gabriel, and Ravens quarterback injury rumors. The remainder is ESPN legal, privacy and gambling boilerplate.

A community-based commentary examines how Citizenship educators in England can create safe, empowering, rights-respecting classrooms that support transgender students amid rising hostility and media debate about trans rights. It considers teachers’ legal and professional responsibilities through the Equality Act 2010, Human Rights Act 1998, UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, Yogyakarta Principles+10, UNESCO guidance, and Plan International’s comprehensive sexuality education principles.

A year-long knowledge exchange project, from October 2023 to June 2024, involved UCL’s Institute of Education and the LGBTQ+ anti-bullying charity Diversity Role Models. Three workshops helped student teachers incorporate trans-inclusive practices into Citizenship teaching, apply them during school placements, and reflect on rights and identities. Student presentations found that “actualising” LGBTQ+ issues was concentrated on sexual orientation, while trans identities were rarely addressed. Teachers attributed this gap to uncertainty surrounding proposed Department for Education guidance and low confidence discussing gender identity.

Draft guidance on supporting “gender-questioning children” prompted criticism that it could encourage pupils to be outed, while later draft Relationships, Sex and Health Education guidance proposed excluding discussion of the broader concept of gender identity. Participants questioned whether teachers could explain transgender people’s legal rights without doing so. Existing statutory requirements remained in force, including teaching the facts and law concerning sexual orientation and gender identity, integrating LGBTQ+ identities across the curriculum, and protecting transgender students under the Equality Act 2010.

Personal stories and diverse role models were identified as ways to make abstract rights issues concrete, humanize discrimination, build empathy, and encourage allyship. Citizenship lessons grounded in equality and human rights legislation similarly framed transgender young people as rights holders and promoted behaviours that challenge discrimination and bullying. International frameworks were presented as supporting comprehensive, accurate teaching and sustained teacher training.

The project also emphasized whole-school inclusion through positive representation, clear and consistently applied anti-bullying policies, restorative approaches, bystander and upstander training, and Pride groups as spaces for safety and equality activism. Participants called for specialist training for Citizenship educators and other staff, continued partnership with civil society organisations, and further development of inclusive teaching materials.

King Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met in Riyadh to review bilateral ties and regional and international developments. Senior officials attended discussions focused on peace, security, and combating terrorism.

The president urges Congress to grant Cuba tariff reciprocity by substantially reducing duties on Cuban imports while preserving the protective system and leaving other countries’ rates unchanged. He cites moral and national interests, Cuba’s constitutional pledge to maintain closer relations with the United States, an urgent appeal for financial relief, and McKinley’s support for close, reciprocal relations and Cuban prosperity.

The existing tariff law permits reductions of up to 20 percent for a particular country. The president says safeguards can ensure Cuban sugar producers benefit rather than American refiners and rejects tariff schedules unrelated to Cuba as irrelevant. He disputes claims that reduced duties would harm American industry, citing Hawaii’s experience and predicting benefits to American producers seeking access to Cuba’s growing market.

He argues that post–Spanish-American War conditions and the prospective Isthmian Canal make U.S. engagement with Cuba and the Caribbean increasingly important. Because Cuba is independent but has assumed special international obligations in response to U.S. requests, he requests economic concessions that would advance both countries and help the young republic develop self-government.

Phase 3 tables report common medical problems after 5- or 10-µg lower boosters; Phase 2/3 tables cover problems after 30-µg booster or additional booster doses. Serious problems were life-threatening, required hospital care, or caused lasting effects. In Phase 1, one participant each (1 of 24, 4%) in the 20- and 30-µg BNT162b2 groups had appendicitis and inflamed nerves, respectively.
Taiwan health authorities warn against raw or undercooked eggs amid rising avian flu, urging cooking to 70°C, handwashing, mask use, and medical care for fever.

Malaysia’s central bank will allow all resident entities to short-sell Malaysian government securities from May 2, expanding access beyond licensed banks and investment banks. BNM also plans broader hedging options, considers short-selling Islamic government bonds, and is updating financial-market conduct rules to improve liquidity, market stability and onshore ringgit trading.

The court reversed a jury verdict awarding Charles Jones $16,369.69 against Orin S. Bacon, executor of James McKechnie, and ordered a new trial. Jones claimed McKechnie agreed to indemnify him for endorsing notes and mortgages for Sherman Kingsbury, McKechnie’s business associate and Jones’s son-in-law.

Although Kingsbury was the only surviving witness to the alleged agreements, the court considered his testimony suspicious because he was an interested witness and corroborating evidence was weak. Jones’s subsequent execution of mortgages for substantial collateral also appeared difficult to reconcile with his claim that he had merely received an unconditional promise of protection.

The decisive error was the admission of evidence concerning McKechnie and Denbow’s hop speculation with Kingsbury, including McKechnie’s refusal to sell hops at forty cents per pound despite an offer that might have satisfied Kingsbury’s debts. The timing of that offer was uncertain, and the evidence was unrelated to whether McKechnie had promised to indemnify Jones. Its purpose was to evoke jury sympathy for Kingsbury and Jones and prejudice the defense. The judgment was therefore reversed and a new trial granted, with costs to abide the event.

Kinlochleven has received three defibrillators through community fundraising. Lucky2BHere presented two along with cabinets and training, while Marcus and Martine Spence donated the third. The first responders group has raised £2,900 of its £3,500 target.

Magda Enriquez secretly joined Nicaragua’s Sandinistas in 1976 after founding a school for children with special needs and discovering that malnutrition caused many of their conditions. Influenced by liberation theology, she became a founding member of the movement’s women’s association, AMNLAE. A 1978 peasant land sit-in, during which police jailed protesters and a plane sprayed poison that killed ten children before treatment, prompted her to seek military training. Enriquez later served on Nicaragua’s Council of State and in delegations preparing for elections, while remaining active in the Sandinista government. She defended young militia members as proud of a revolution they had helped build, but was deeply involved in her own six children and relied on party and community support while working away from them. She said the Revolution had created opportunities to address women’s problems without immediately transforming social attitudes. Her life, she argued, challenged the idea that women must choose between family and public life.

England beat Colombia 4–3 on penalties after Yerry Mina’s late equaliser to reach the World Cup quarter-finals. Harry Kane scored the opener and his shootout kick, while Eric Dier netted the winner. England face Sweden on Saturday, and Kane leads the tournament’s scorers with six goals. Radamel Falcao accused the referee of favouring England, while Diego Maradona called the result a “monumental theft.”

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2016 (Commission File No. 000-22513), classifying as a large accelerated filer; 475,166,527 shares of common stock were outstanding as of October 19, 2016.

Results: Q3 2016 net sales were $32.71 billion (product sales $22.34 billion; service sales $10.38 billion), up 29% from $25.36 billion in Q3 2015; operating income was $575 million vs. $406 million; net income $252 million vs. $79 million; diluted EPS $0.52 vs. $0.17. For the nine months ended September 30, 2016: net sales $92.25 billion vs. $71.26 billion, operating income $2.93 billion vs. $1.12 billion, net income $1.62 billion vs. $114 million, and diluted EPS $3.36 vs. $0.24.

Segments (Q3 2016): North America sales $18.87 billion with operating income of $255 million; International sales $10.61 billion with an operating loss of $541 million; AWS sales $3.23 billion with operating income of $861 million. Nine-month figures: North America $53.54 billion/$1.55 billion; International $30.02 billion/$(796) million; AWS $8.68 billion/$2.18 billion. AWS growth was attributed to increased customer usage partly offset by price reductions; North America and International growth reflected increased unit sales (including marketplace sellers), price reductions, faster-growing categories such as electronics and general merchandise, greater in-stock availability, and wider selection.

Cash flow and balance sheet: Operating cash flow was $4.49 billion in Q3 2016 and $5.79 billion for nine months (trailing twelve months $14.60 billion); investing outflows were $2.57 billion and $5.70 billion; financing outflows $827 million and $2.66 billion. Cash capital expenditures were $1.84 billion in Q3 and $4.73 billion for nine months, primarily technology infrastructure supporting AWS and fulfillment capacity. Cash and equivalents ended at $13.66 billion (vs. $15.89 billion at December 31, 2015); cash, equivalents and marketable securities totaled $18.3 billion. Total assets were $70.90 billion vs. $64.75 billion; stockholders' equity $17.78 billion vs. $13.38 billion; long-term debt $8.21 billion. Interest expense was $118 million in Q3 and $351 million for nine months. Q3 shipping revenue of $2.15 billion versus shipping costs of $3.90 billion produced a net shipping cost of $1.74 billion (vs. $1.23 billion); inventory turnover was 9.

Debt and equity: $8.3 billion of unsecured senior notes were outstanding. A $3.0 billion unsecured revolving credit facility was entered May 2016 with no borrowings outstanding, and a $500 million secured revolving facility was entered October 13, 2016. In February 2016 the Board authorized repurchases of up to $5.0 billion of stock (replacing a prior $2.0 billion authorization); no repurchases occurred in Q3 2016 or Q3 2015. Unrecognized stock-based compensation cost was $4.6 billion, with 20.8 million restricted stock units outstanding.

Commitments: Total contractual commitments were $39.86 billion (debt principal and interest $12.48 billion, capital leases $8.48 billion, finance leases $3.20 billion, operating leases $9.04 billion, unconditional purchase obligations $1.90 billion, other $4.77 billion); purchase obligations and open purchase orders were $10.6 billion, and $588 million of cash, securities and certain property were pledged as collateral.

Taxes and legal matters: The tax provision was $229 million in Q3 and $1.01 billion for nine months (vs. $161 million and $498 million); tax contingencies were $1.7 billion vs. $1.2 billion and are expected to grow. The IRS seeks approximately $1.5 billion of additional federal tax on 2005–2006 transfer pricing, contested in U.S. Tax Court; a French Tax Administration assessment of €196 million is being contested; and an EU state aid investigation into Luxembourg tax decisions remains open. The company disclosed that it processed and delivered orders for certain consumers in Iran potentially covered by U.S. sanctions laws, voluntarily reported the matter to OFAC and BIS, and continues its review, which may result in penalties. In September 2016 Broadcom and Avago filed a patent complaint against Amazon.com and AWS alleging infringement by Fire and Kindle devices, the Dash Button, Amazon Echo, Elastic Transcoder, CloudFront and Elastic Compute Cloud; Amazon disputes the allegations.

Accounting: Statements are unaudited; prior periods were reclassified for stock-based compensation and other operating expense allocated to segments and capitalized debt issuance costs moved to long-term debt. The ASU requiring non-current classification of deferred taxes was adopted in Q1 2016 retrospectively; the company is evaluating new guidance on leases, stock-based compensation excess tax benefits, intercompany asset transfers and revenue recognition. Critical estimates include inventories (FIFO, lower of cost or market; each 1% additional allowance ≈ $120 million of cost of sales), goodwill (April 1, 2016 test showed no impairment; a 10% fair-value decline had no impact), and a 28% stock-compensation forfeiture rate (a 1% change ≈ $70 million effect on Q3 operating income).

Between weeks 24 and 48, adverse events occurred in 33.8%–40.8% of subjects across groups; bleeding occurred in 3.2%–4.1%, with two fatal cases. There were 24 deaths, no pregnancies, and no concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signal. Apixaban adherence and persistence sustained through 48 weeks, without added benefit from the educational program.

Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars for outstanding academic achievement. Scholars rank among the top 10% of Illinois graduating seniors and are selected using ACT and SAT scores, unweighted GPA, and junior-year class size. The passage lists the honorees.

Retirees and FIRE participants face substantial sequence-of-returns risk, especially when withdrawals continue during prolonged market declines. Poor diversification and excessive withdrawal rates can cause portfolios to fail; conservative spending, lower withdrawal rates, diversification, and a large margin of safety improve survival prospects.

After Andrea collapsed from a rare, undetected heart defect, Luke Benrud performed CPR for seven minutes, saving her life. Featured by People Magazine, the CPR-trained couple and family hope their story encourages others to learn CPR.

Analysts expect the ECB to keep interest rates at historic lows and maintain its €30 billion monthly QE bond-buying scheme through September, tempering expectations for a rapid exit from stimulus. Inflation remains below target and downside growth risks have re-emerged, despite a 2.4% eurozone growth forecast for 2018. Business activity is still expanding but has slowed, while U.S. tariff threats and delayed eurozone reform add uncertainty.

Body-camera footage shows that, during an August 19 armed-robbery response in Grand Rapids, officers mistakenly detained an intoxicated man who refused to cooperate. After tasing and bringing him to the ground, Officer Kevin Penn pressed an AR-15’s muzzle against his head; Officer James Smith pushed the rifle away. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker called the conduct a glaring violation of the man’s rights but said the circumstances did not warrant criminal charges. Penn was allowed to resign. The suspect was arrested for resisting arrest and released on his own recognizance. The video’s release could prompt an attorney to pursue a civil case.

Companies use exhibitions to build brand image and gather direct customer feedback, requiring skilled hosts, models, registration staff, and moderators. Traditional recruitment agencies can be costly and have limited databases. Professionate offers an online staffing portal where companies can search candidate profiles, ratings, and reviews, while recruiters and temporary-job seekers can post profiles, find vacancies, and apply.

Police charged a 33-year-old Manheim Township man with drug manufacturing and possession, drug paraphernalia possession, and child endangerment after a search of his home found two marijuana plants, other controlled substances and smoking devices. He was released on $20,000 unsecured bail. Other recent charges involved alleged indecent assault, corruption of minors, and a domestic dispute in which a man allegedly assaulted a victim, removed a necklace and threatened occupants.

UNICEF warned that two years of war and unpaid salaries affecting over three-quarters of Yemen’s teachers could keep up to 4.5 million children from finishing school, increasing risks of early marriage and child-soldier recruitment.

A Channel 4 documentary follows five women who report experiencing as many as 100 orgasms in one sexual encounter. Experiments measured arousal, brain-wave activity, and blood flow, suggesting possible neurological differences in women who experience multiple orgasms. However, the documentary’s research was not scientific because it involved few participants and no control group. Experts interviewed by SELF rejected “super orgasm” as a meaningful distinction, describing the women as unusual outliers and emphasizing that orgasm varies widely. They also disputed the documentary’s suggestion that most women could achieve 100 orgasms with practice.

This study examined whether sex and trauma type affected agreement between the self-reported PTSD Checklist (PCL-5) and clinician-administered CAPS-5 among 100 adults (56 male, 44 female). Participants completed the PCL-5 before the CAPS-5. CAPS-5 scores did not differ significantly by sex or military versus civilian trauma. Overall PCL-5 and CAPS-5 scores correlated strongly (ρ=.815), but correlation was stronger for females (ρ=.907) than males (ρ=.655). Males’ scores also deviated significantly from the regression line defined by the diagnostic thresholds, while females’ scores did not. Using PCL-5 alone misclassified PTSD status relative to CAPS-5 in 26.8% of males and 11.4% of females, with most male misclassifications being PCL-5-positive/CAPS-5-negative cases. Correlation was stronger for civilian trauma (ρ=.885) than military trauma (ρ=.523), with the same pattern within each sex. Findings suggest that PCL-5 should be interpreted cautiously for males and military populations, particularly when used alone to determine PTSD diagnosis or severity. Limitations included the small sample, few females with military trauma, and recruitment from one southeastern region; causal explanations were not established.

For a function \(f:S\to\mathbb R\), continuity at \(c\in S\) means that \(f(x)\) approaches \(f(c)\) as \(x\) approaches \(c\). If \(c\) is not a cluster point of \(S\), every such function is automatically continuous at \(c\). If \(c\) is a cluster point, continuity is equivalent both to \(\lim_{x\to c}f(x)=f(c)\) and to the condition that \(f(x_n)\to f(c)\) for every sequence \(x_n\in S\) converging to \(c\).

The sequence characterization was proved in both directions and used to establish closure properties: sums and products of functions continuous at a point are continuous there, as are quotients when the denominator is nonzero. If \(g\) is continuous at \(c\) and \(f\) is continuous at \(g(c)\), then \(f\circ g\) is continuous at \(c\).

Sine was proved continuous directly from the epsilon–delta definition using trigonometric identities and the bound \(|\sin x|\le |x|\); cosine was then shown continuous using \(\cos x=\sin(x+\pi/2)\). The sequence criterion also proved that the function equal to \(1\) on rationals and \(0\) on irrationals is discontinuous at every real number, answering that a function with domain \(\mathbb R\) need not have any continuity point. Repeated products and sums establish that natural-number powers and polynomials are continuous, and the same principles show, for example, that \(1/(3+\sin^4 x)\) is continuous. The lecture concludes by previewing the extreme value and intermediate value theorems.

A STAT biotech newsletter reports that FDA approved a second generic version of mifepristone. Amgen’s 12,000-patient Repatha trial found its cholesterol-lowering injection reduced the combined risk of heart-disease death, heart attacks and strokes, supporting broader use of PCSK9 inhibitors. It also mentions a new NIH office focused on reducing animal testing and lists other biotech and drug-policy headlines.

Cover 3 is a zone defense using four underneath defenders and three deep defenders. The free safety covers the middle deep third, while the two cornerbacks cover the outside thirds, typically by bailing or backpedaling to prevent deep passes. Three linebackers and the strong safety handle the underneath hook, curl, and flat zones, with responsibility for stopping the run and forcing short passes.

Compared with Cover 2, Cover 3 adds a third deep defender while allowing a safety to move closer to the line of scrimmage. This creates favorable numbers against the run and balances coverage against both run and pass plays. Its weaknesses are the flats, where receivers can catch short hitch, out, or arrow routes; the seams, which can be attacked with four verticals; and the perimeter against outside runs. Defenders must adjust when one player is responsible for a seam route or when linebackers are caught out of position.

Variations include flipping the safeties’ assignments, using a fire-zone blitz, and Cover 3 Buzz, in which a rolled-down safety plays the middle hook-to-curl area while outside linebackers or a nickel back cover the curl flats. Defenses can also use pattern-reading coverage, such as Rip/Liz, to combine zone principles with man-like route responsibility.

The president transmitted to the House of Representatives the Secretary of State’s report and documents concerning the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo and the Senate’s amendments, including instructions previously withheld on grounds of public interest but now deemed necessary for understanding the treaty proceedings.

The instructions directed U.S. commissioners to obtain Mexico’s ratification of the Senate-amended treaty without renegotiating or modifying it. They were authorized to explain the amendments personally to Mexican representatives but were not to negotiate any new treaty.

The Secretary of State explained the amendments to Mexico before the Mexican Congress acted. On May 25, 1848, the Mexican Congress approved the treaty without alteration, before the U.S. commissioners were officially received. The commissioners subsequently met with Mexican officials and exchanged ratifications. A later protocol recording those conversations did not amend the treaty because it followed congressional ratification and was never submitted to or approved by the Mexican Congress. The treaty was received in Washington, proclaimed as the supreme law of the land, and substantially executed while peace had already been restored; unilateral abrogation would have required a declaration of war.

The protocol gave three explanations of the Senate’s amendments. First, replacing the treaty’s ninth article did not diminish the civil, political, property, or religious protections promised to inhabitants of ceded territories. The amended article guaranteed their liberty and property and unrestricted religious exercise. Second, removing the tenth article did not invalidate legitimate pre-existing Mexican land titles, though it did not revive grants that had already become void. Valid property rights were independently protected by U.S. law and Article 8. Third, eliminating provisions for transferable government certificates did not prevent Mexico from assigning its $12 million payment obligation. An assignee, however, would receive no greater rights than Mexico and could not demand payment if the stated consideration failed.

Because these explanations were consistent with the amended treaty, the president concluded that no further action was necessary.

American Surety Company filed an involuntary bankruptcy petition against John Jacob Beechwood. Beechwood denied insolvency and the alleged acts of bankruptcy and claimed exemption as a farmer under the Bankruptcy Act. A jury found that he was insolvent and had committed the alleged acts, leaving the court to determine whether he was a farmer when he conveyed his farm to his wife on September 20, 1940, and transferred his steamship stock interest on October 10, 1940.

Although Beechwood resided on a genuine farm operated by a practical farmer, participated in agricultural work during leisure time, and later worked there full-time, most of his income came from his legal and business employment. On the relevant dates, he was addressing the consequences of his employer’s losses, resigning, pursuing business opportunities, and handling criminal charges and legal matters. Applying the statute’s requirement that a farmer be personally engaged in agriculture and derive the principal part of his income from farming at the time of the bankruptcy act, the court held that Beechwood did not qualify for the farmer exemption. His defense was rejected, and the court directed that an order adjudicating him a bankrupt be entered.

The Times reported that Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort was aware of calls involving Russian intelligence officers; Manafort denied knowingly speaking to them or involvement with the Russian government. U.S. intelligence suspected Russia sought to help Trump win, while Russia denied involvement. National security adviser Michael Flynn resigned over calls with Russia’s U.S. ambassador. Press Secretary Sean Spicer said Trump’s January denial of pre-election campaign contacts with Russia had not changed.

A memorandum outlines the Inquiry’s potential role in peace conferences, including coordinated subcommittees and commissions; data on conflict-prone areas, major nations, national aspirations, international administration, world organization, laws of war, reparations, trade routes, business, and diplomacy. It identifies practical tasks: establishing boundaries and governments, assessing states’ strength, arranging economies, protecting minorities and weak peoples, ensuring equal economic opportunity, revising international law, and considering diplomatic history. Boundary settlement is especially needed in Poland, Alsace-Lorraine, Trentino, Trieste, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, and Turkey; government establishment is required in Poland and Austria-Hungary. Other potential areas include Russian territories, Slesvig, Belgium, Luxemburg, Turkey, Africa, the Far East, Pacific islands, Latin America, Persia, Afghanistan, and Spitsbergen, with proposed measures tailored to each region’s needs.

Amazon reportedly plans to cut up to 15% of its human resources staff, with additional layoffs possible in its core consumer business and other divisions; the total number affected and timing are unknown. The HR division, known as PXT or People eXperience Technology, has more than 10,000 employees worldwide. The cuts come as Amazon reduces corporate costs while investing heavily in AI products, infrastructure and datacenters, with capital spending expected to exceed $100 billion this year. CEO Andy Jassy said extensive AI use will reduce Amazon’s corporate workforce. Amazon recently made smaller layoffs but is separately hiring 250,000 seasonal warehouse and logistics workers.

Vice President Biden affirms the enduring principles of the Constitution and democracy, arguing that equal rights require collective action while preserving individual freedom, initiative, personal responsibility, and skepticism toward centralized power.

He says successive generations ended slavery, built infrastructure and education, promoted fair markets, and protected vulnerable people. He calls for government, tax, and school reforms; worker training; broad prosperity based on a rising middle class; and policies that preserve basic security and dignity through Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security.

Biden urges action on climate change and American leadership in sustainable energy. On national security, he supports strong defenses, alliances, diplomacy, democracy, and peace while advancing freedom, opportunity, human dignity, and justice.

He says the current generation must make equality real through equal opportunity for women, equal treatment of gay people under law, easier voting, welcome for immigrants, retention of young talent, and protection of children. Rejecting delay, absolutism, and spectacle, he urges citizens to act now and use both their votes and voices to defend enduring ideals, carrying freedom into an uncertain future through common effort.

A Brazilian mouse study examined Bt/Cry toxins used in most GMO food crops and reported effects on mammalian blood cells, including the erythroid lineage. Findings included anemia, bone-marrow suppression, and abnormal lymphocyte patterns associated with leukemia. Cry1Ab at the lowest tested dose of 27 mg/kg induced hypochromic anemia, while effects became more pronounced after 72 hours. Contrary to earlier beliefs, Cry toxins produced hematotoxicity in distilled water without requiring alkaline activation. The authors concluded that these toxins may pose hematological risks to vertebrates and require further study before their safety in mammals can be established.

The passage also cites a French rat study linking GM corn and Roundup to cancer, raises concerns about combined Cry-toxin and glyphosate-residue exposure, and criticizes industry-funded GMO safety research. It advocates precaution and GMO bans and promotes the March Against Monsanto.

Founded by Herbert Henry Martyn in Cheltenham in 1888, H.H. Martyn & Co. became a prolific art-craft and engineering firm. It moved to a 12.5-acre Sunningend site, where its large foundry produced the 40-ton iron gates for London’s Marble Arch. Royal Warrant work at Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle was followed by international commissions, while Martyn’s created the Selfridges frontage, the House of Commons Speaker’s Chair and dispatch boxes, and the Whitehall Cenotaph. By 1910, it employed more than 1,000 people.

The firm also fitted out over 100 ocean liners, including the Titanic, Lusitania, Queen Mary, Queen Elizabeth and QE2. During the First World War, it began manufacturing military aircraft, leading to Gloster Aircraft Company, which later contested the Schneider Trophy. Martyn’s also contributed to Sir Henry Segrave’s Golden Arrow land-speed car, made Wolseley cars and designed the Unibus scooter.

Between 1920 and 1937, it supplied 75% of Britain’s orders for statues, ornamental screens, decorative doors, gates and related art metalwork. Bought by Maples in the mid-1930s, it continued major commissions into the 1960s but closed in 1971 after Britain’s shipbuilding decline led Maples to sell its assets.

December deals include a $5,000 Kia Optima Hybrid discount in Western states ($4,000 elsewhere), or 0% APR for 60 months if $3,000 in bonus cash is forgone. The Optima Plug-In lease is $249 monthly for 36 months with $1,999 down and $12,249 in lease discounts, plus federal and California incentives. The Chevrolet Volt lease is $273 monthly for 39 months with $500 down and a $7,500 federal credit. Following May 1825 orders, Commodore Thomas ap Catesby Jones reached Honolulu aboard the Peacock in 1826. His friendly inspection addressed American deserters and citizens’ claims and produced a friendship, commerce, and navigation treaty signed by the king on December 23. It was Hawaii’s first formally negotiated treaty with a foreign power; although unratified by the United States, some provisions were considered morally binding. U.S. naval vessels thereafter intervened in Hawaiian affairs, including Commodore Downs’s protection of persecuted Catholic converts and a 1829 letter conveying the President’s desire for peace, kindness, and justice toward American visitors. In 1839, Laplace’s threatened intervention led to a treaty protecting Catholics, averting violence but introducing intoxicating liquors. Britain had already obtained a treaty in 1836 under naval threat. In February 1843, Lord George Paulet seized the islands, forced Kamehameha III to cede them, and established a commission that governed Hawaii and formed the Hawaiian-armed “Queen’s Own.” After Judd resigned in protest, the commission continued. Commodore Kearney protested the cession and harm to American rights; Rear Admiral Thomas’s subsequent negotiations restored the Hawaiian flag on July 31 and disavowed Paulet’s seizure.

It covers market status, growth, revenues, drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, Five Forces, applications, regional markets, and competitive landscape. The report also provides SWOT, investment feasibility and return, marketing, price, and margin analyses and profiles companies including Chr. Hansen, Danisco, Kerry, Lallemand, BIOTEC, and Sacco System.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported that on September 9, 2020, its Board elected retired General Keith B. Alexander as a director and appointed him to the Audit Committee. Alexander is Co-Chief Executive Officer, President, and Chairman of IronNet Cybersecurity, Inc., which he founded in 2014. He previously commanded U.S. Cyber Command and served as Director of the National Security Agency and Chief of the Central Security Service. Amazon granted him 288 restricted stock units vesting in three equal annual installments beginning November 15, 2021, subject to continued service, and he entered into the company’s standard director indemnification agreement.

The paper proposes a Bayesian, top-down recursive bipartitioning framework for community detection that does not require prespecifying the number of communities. The network is repeatedly divided using Gibbs sampling, while a Bayes factor compares models with and without community structure to determine when further division should stop. The framework accommodates stochastic block models, edge exchangeable models for directed interactions, and latent space models with Gaussian-mixture community structure, allowing network properties to be incorporated through likelihoods. The paper defines strong and weak consistency for community labels and establishes that, under stochastic block model conditions favoring within-community connections, recursive bipartitioning using Erdős–Rényi modularity is strongly consistent when the expected subnetwork degree grows faster than its logarithm divided by its number of nodes, and weakly consistent under a weaker degree condition. No theoretical consistency guarantees are given for the other two model classes. Simulation studies and an application to stroke patient transfer data are planned to evaluate the framework.

Progress Software’s Q3 2025 earnings call began September 29, 2025, with CEO Yogesh Gupta, CFO Anthony Folger, and Senior Vice President of Investor Relations Michael Micciche. The call’s outlook would cover financial and operating performance, strategy, product plans, cost initiatives, and ShareFile integration. Forward-looking statements were subject to risks and uncertainties, with no obligation to update. Financial figures would be non-GAAP unless otherwise indicated. The passage also listed participating analysts, promotional links, and stock-chart metadata.

A study detected water molecules in hot-Jupiter WASP-121b’s atmosphere, indicating that temperature rises with altitude and revealing a warm stratosphere. The planet is about 880 light-years away and reaches roughly 2,500°C (4,500°F) at the top of its atmosphere. Researchers used Hubble infrared transit observations to measure its spectrum, calling this the strongest evidence yet for an exoplanet stratosphere and a milestone for analyzing distant atmospheres. Current technology favors studying large, hot gas giants, but future observatories may enable analysis of smaller, Earth-like planets, including searches for signs of life. The study was published online Aug. 2 in Nature.

Winthrop University will receive $1.1 million from a highly competitive $20 million National Science Foundation award shared by 10 South Carolina institutions over five years. The funding supports research on complex, intelligently designed materials; 36 summer student research experiences; $330,000 in equipment and facility upgrades; faculty development; conference travel; and two-week summer teacher workshops. Winthrop researchers will study electronic, optical, biomaterial, nanoparticle, supercapacitor, photocatalytic, and computational materials research. The broader MADE in SC initiative is managed by South Carolina’s Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research.

The NHS Constitution, also called the Patient Charter, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS commitments beyond legal requirements, and patients’ responsibilities. It guarantees access to free care at the point of use, subject to exceptions, with equal treatment, waiting-time standards, explanations and alternatives when standards are missed, and services planned around community needs. It covers safe, high-quality care by qualified staff, privacy, consent, clear information, treatment choices, GP selection, involvement in decisions, and disclosure of errors. Patients are entitled to NICE-recommended medicines and treatments, routine vaccinations, rational and explained local funding decisions, and support for complaints, judicial review, and compensation for negligence. Patients are expected to look after their health, respect staff and others, follow treatment plans, attend appointments, and participate in vaccination and screening. The Charter promotes fairness, transparency, accountability, trust, and shared responsibility within the NHS.

The coach described the Chicago series as emotionally and physically demanding, with seven games, three overtimes, late-night travel, media duties and an unusual practice schedule. He said roster changes and several players’ first Stanley Cup Final affected the team, while praising Kyle’s energy and both teams’ resilience. He emphasized that strong relationships, defined roles and a winning record help players accept assignments, noting Mike Richards is focused simply on winning. He praised Jonathan’s focus and penalty-killing and advised young players to improve ice-time management, shot selection, preparation, nutrition and game-day routines. He also discussed Madison Square Garden’s distinctive atmosphere, defensive changes and efforts to manage players’ performance.

The article explains Average True Range (ATR), a volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr. It demonstrates calculating ATR in Python with pandas_ta and backtesting a simple 14-day ATR strategy on SPY: hold when volatility is high and sell when it is low. ATR is commonly used for stop-loss placement, position sizing, and identifying possible breakouts. The strategy’s results were not very promising; although risk-adjusted performance was better, its drawdown was nearly identical to buy and hold. Combining ATR with other indicators might improve results.

A University of Bristol-led study found that chloroplast lineages diverged from their closest cyanobacterial ancestor more than 2.1 billion years ago in low-salinity habitats, followed about 200 million years later by a symbiotic relationship with eukaryotic hosts. Marine algae diversified around 800–750 million years ago. The researchers conclude that complex algae evolved in freshwater before colonizing marine environments, with implications for understanding the carbon cycle and early life.

After the Daily Stormer published an article mocking Heather Heyer, killed in the Charlottesville car attack, GoDaddy terminated the white supremacist site’s domain registration, citing concerns that the article could incite violence. The site moved to Google Domains, which canceled its registration the following day. Neither company hosts the site; Cloudflare obscures its host and has faced criticism for sharing complainants’ information with founder Andrew Anglin.

A post claiming Anonymous had hacked the Daily Stormer and would release private data appeared before Anglin said he had regained control. Separately, the Southern Poverty Law Center is suing Anglin over an alleged coordinated harassment campaign against Tanya Gersh’s family. Anglin has not participated in the case and claims to have left the United States, although Reveal reported that evidence supporting his claim he was living in Nigeria was falsified. If the lawsuit succeeds, his assets could be seized, potentially shutting down the website.

NASA coverage of an ISS spacewalk begins at 10 a.m. EDT on August 17. Expedition 52 Commander Fyodor Yurchikhin and Flight Engineer Sergey Ryazanskiy will exit through the Pirs airlock for a six-hour mission, deploying five nanosatellites, scraping exterior residue samples for analysis, and installing handrails and struts. It is the only spacewalk planned during Expedition 52.

Anne-Marie D’Amico, an Invesco employee, was identified as one of 10 people killed when a van struck pedestrians on Yonge Street near Finch Avenue on Monday. Fifteen others were injured. Police arrested 25-year-old Alex Minassian, who is accused of renting the van and driving into the crowd. Toronto Police Chief Mark Saunders said the attack appeared deliberate, but its motive remains unknown.

A retrospective records-review study at Mulago National Referral Hospital assessed outcomes and health-system costs for children admitted with clinical measles in 2018. Of 570 admissions, 553 charts were retrieved, 16 were excluded, and 267 cases were systematically sampled. The median patient age was 1.0 year, median hospital stay was four days, and 30 patients (11.3%) died. Complications developed in 185 patients (69.3%), with severe pneumonia most common. Among deaths, 44% were unvaccinated and 70% were aged zero to one year.

Average direct health-care costs were $33.13 per patient, comprising treatment ($21.98), blood tests ($11.73), and radiology ($3.48). Average overhead costs were $81.37, mainly human resources, giving a reported total direct cost of $114.50 per case. Costs were significantly higher among males, patients with comorbidities, those hospitalized longer than 15 days, and those who died. Longer stays were associated with substantially higher average costs.

The findings indicate high measles mortality, frequent complications, and substantial treatment costs at a national referral hospital, supporting greater vaccination promotion to reduce mortality and health-service expenditure. Limitations included reliance on a single public hospital, retrospective data, clinical rather than laboratory confirmation of measles, inability to determine whether all documented treatments were received, and exclusion of family and societal costs.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture and TSMC’s 7nm N7 process to improve AI and high-performance computing performance, power efficiency, fault isolation, and multi-GPU scaling. The A100 implementation contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and 40 GB of HBM2 memory. A full GA100 configuration contains 128 SMs and 8,192 FP32 cores.

Each A100 SM has four third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. A100 provides up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 performance. Relative to V100, its FP16/FP32 Tensor Core operations are 2.5 times faster, TF32 operations can reach 10 times the speed of standard V100 FP32 operations, FP64 performance is 2.5 times higher, and sparse INT8 performance can be up to 20 times higher. Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity skips zero-valued matrix entries, doubling Tensor Core throughput while reducing storage and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA’s pruning and fine-tuning recipe produced virtually no inference-accuracy loss across the evaluated networks.

A100 includes 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. New asynchronous-copy instructions transfer data directly from global memory to shared memory, optionally bypassing L1 and avoiding intermediate register-file use. Hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers separate arrival from waiting, support synchronization of arbitrary thread subsets, and allow copies to overlap with computation. CUDA Task Graphs support define-once, repeated execution of dependency-connected operations, with A100 adding faster launch and inter-grid paths.

The GPU has 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth. HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files use SECDED ECC. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM read/write bandwidth and L2 read bandwidth by up to four times and L2 capacity by up to two times. CUDA 11 adds L2 residency controls, including persistent-access set-asides and address-based controls.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, L2, and memory resources. GPU and Compute Instances support separate contexts and Volta-style MPS, predictable quality of service, fault isolation, and workload migration. This enables multiple VMs, containers, or processes to share one physical GPU.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per GPU, compared with six links and 300 GB/s on V100. It includes error detection, packet replay, and remote page-fault reporting. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and SR-IOV for sharing a GPU among processes or VMs.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved global-memory atomics, and five NVDEC units. Enhanced fault attribution, isolation, containment, and recovery are designed to maintain availability in multi-GPU and multi-tenant systems.

CUDA 11 supports the A100’s Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, task graphs, asynchronous copies and barriers, L2 residency controls, and new warp-level reductions through Cooperative Groups. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system, provides 4.8 TB/s aggregate interconnect bandwidth, and can expose as many as 56 isolated accelerators through MIG. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and optimized containers for deep learning, analytics, and HPC through the NVIDIA GPU Cloud registry.

**Summary**

This patent application (a continuation of PCT/CN2019/128475, priority CN 201811653380.3 filed December 29, 2018) concerns a big-data recommendation model training method and related apparatus.

**Background.** In machine learning recommendation systems, sampling improves training quality, reduces computing resource consumption, improves training efficiency, and addresses data imbalance. Without sampling, tens of billions of daily data items (as in HUAWEI APPGALLERY) can cause rapid overfitting from homogeneous data, excessive hardware consumption and slow or infrequent model updates, reduced prediction accuracy, and severe imbalance between negative and positive samples. How to account for top-N ranking performance when sampling is an open technical problem.

**Training method.** A positive sample is selected from a sample set and added to a training set; each sample carries n features including a label indicating positive/negative status. Sampling probabilities for the negative samples are computed with a preset algorithm derived from one or more of three rules: (1) probability is negatively correlated with the score difference between a positive sample's and a negative sample's estimated score; (2) probability is negatively correlated with the vector distance between the eigenvectors of the positive and negative samples; (3) probability is positively correlated with the variation of a ranking indicator (e.g., NDCG@5, NDCG@10, P@5, P@10) generated after the rankings of the positive and negative samples are exchanged. Negative samples are then selected per these probabilities, added to the training set, and used to train the recommendation model (e.g., via FTRL, LR, or FFM algorithms), optionally storing the model.

Four formula implementations are given (combining the three rules, first+third, a first+third variant using |Δz_ij|(s_j−s_i), and first+second). Stated conclusions: a negative sample with a higher estimated score/ranking receives a higher sampling probability; the pairwise relation improves final ranking performance; a larger vector distance raises probability; and |Δz_ij| raises probability for negative samples farther away in ranking. Example: NDCG@5 of 1.0 versus 0.8 yields |Δz_ij| = 0.2.

**Sampling options.** Negative samples may be collected in descending order of sampling probability up to a preset quantity, or selected by comparing (optionally normalized by the maximum probability) sampling probabilities against random numbers from 0 to 1. Normalization maximizes each probability without altering their relative distribution and speeds sampling.

**Iteration and recommendation.** The trained model also generates estimated scores used by the next round of sampling, so training and sampling mutually influence each other, enabling rapid convergence. A recommendation method computes estimated scores for to-be-recommended objects using user and/or object features, ranks objects in descending score order, and recommends the top M objects (M preset, e.g., 10) to the target user.

**Apparatus and embodiments.** The application also discloses a training apparatus (first/second sampling units and a training unit), processor-and-memory based training and recommendation devices, computer-readable storage media, and computer program products. A system architecture includes a data collection device, training device, execution device, data storage system, and client device. Samples comprise user features (gender, age, occupation, hobby, etc.), object features (ID, name, type, size, label, comment, etc.), and a sample type identifier (e.g., 1 = download = positive; 0 = browse = negative). Objects in one sample set are those shown in one ranking list.

**Testing.** Using a HUAWEI APPGALLERY data set, the method outperformed training without sampling, random sampling, dynamic negative sampling (DNS), and optimized LR sampling on NDCG@5, NDCG@10, P@5, and P@10; NDCG@5 improved by 0.0026 over non-sampling, 0.0015 over random sampling, 0.044 over DNS, and 0.0026 over optimized LR sampling.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA, SoftBank Group Capital Limited, and SVF Holdco (UK) Limited mutually terminated their September 2020 agreement to acquire Arm due to significant regulatory challenges. The sellers will retain NVIDIA’s $1.25 billion prepayment, while NVIDIA will retain its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA plans to record a $1.36 billion termination charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2023.

The passage specifies the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for guest–hypervisor communication in SEV-ES and SEV-SNP environments. GHCB MSR requests include CPUID retrieval, AP reset hold, preferred or registered GHCB GPA selection, page-state changes, SNP VMPL execution, hypervisor-feature discovery, and termination. CPUID requests return one register per VMGEXIT and do not support functions requiring non-zero sub-leaves or CPUID function 0x0000000d. Termination requests carry reason codes, including an unsupported-protocol code.

For SEV-SNP guests, each vCPU must register a GHCB GPA before first use. A guest may request the hypervisor’s preferred GPA, but the hypervisor must ensure the GPA cannot otherwise be mapped by the guest and make the page hypervisor-owned and shared. Registering a GPA replaces any previously registered GPA; a mismatched GPA causes guest termination. The hypervisor must permit separate registrations per VMPL when Multi-VMPL is advertised. Guests may unregister a GHCB GPA.

Negotiation examples show the hypervisor placing protocol-version information in VMCB offset 0x00a0. Guests use CPUID interception and #VC handling to obtain protocol versions and the SEV page-table encryption-bit position, configure encrypted page tables, establish long mode, allocate and share a GHCB page, register its GPA when required, and write its GPA to MSR 0xc0010130 before VMGEXIT use. SEV-ES guests must establish the encryption bit before relying on the GHCB because early guest memory is encrypted.

NAE events are handled through #VC exceptions and VMGEXIT. The guest supplies SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2, and state identified by the GHCB VALID_BITMAP; the hypervisor returns results in designated fields. Nonzero SW_EXITINFO1 denotes an error, including malformed VMGEXIT input, an unregistered GHCB, invalid scratch data, missing valid fields, or invalid event input. Guests and hypervisors reset VALID_BITMAP before each exchange, and software disables interrupts and preemption while accessing or updating a GHCB.

Defined events include IOIO and MSR protection, MMIO transfers through a decrypted shared buffer, page-state changes, SNP guest requests, extended SNP requests with certificates, AP creation, #HV doorbell-page management, #HV IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, SNP VMPL changes, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing-page registration, and termination. Page-state changes support making pages private or shared, PSMASH and UNSMASH hints, resumable shared-memory tracking, and SNP RMP updates. SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages and forward guest messages to firmware. Extended requests can return certificates identified by GUIDs. AP creation can add, update, or remove a vCPU and its VMSA at a selected VMPL.

SEV-ES AP startup uses AP reset hold followed by INIT-SIPI-SIPI handling because measured registers cannot be changed normally. SEV-SNP can instead use the AP Creation event, which supports vCPU hotplug. An AP jump table communicates reset-vector information between environments. Restricted Injection disables AP Reset Hold and requires AP Creation for AP startup.

The SNP secrets page includes a guest-reserved area for VMPL message sequence numbers, an AP jump-table address, and guest-defined data. EFI platforms may pass secrets and CPUID pages through an EFI SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table.
