SEV-ES guests identify support through CPUID properties that indicate hypervisor operation, SEV support, the encryption-bit position, and reduced physical-address space. NMI handling requires non-intercepted IRET, intercepted #DB, and an “NMI Complete” message. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported conditionally; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

The #HV doorbell page provides common host-notification data in an APIC-like format. PendingEvent contains the interrupt vector and non-maskable-event indicators, while NoEoiRequired can avoid an explicit EOI. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics and may replace an unacknowledged vector with a higher-priority one. The guest must atomically exchange PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, validate observed vectors, handle non-maskable events even with interrupts disabled, and use an explicit APIC EOI when atomic EOI assistance is unavailable.

The High/Low Zone Offense combines an outside three-player passing attack with an inside high-low rotation. It can begin from many alignments, is relatively simple to learn, and uses continuous movement by two interior players to create matchup problems against zone defenses. When zones collapse toward the middle, spot-up shooters receive open outside shots. Quick weakside attacks force full-court defense, while sharp, accurate ball movement is central to the offense.

Basic continuity begins with the point player entering a wing and going opposite. The wing looks to feed a rolling or posting interior player in the basket or short corner, or a player flashing into the middle or side post. If the interior player does not receive the ball, they step out to initiate a reversal and weakside attack. The same patterns continue from either wing, with options for shooting, post feeds, kick-out passes, baseline cuts, and high-post actions.

Common entries include Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns. These use back cuts, slice cuts, screens, reversals, rolls, and flash cuts to initiate or continue high-low action.

The offense can also flow into quick-hitting sets to avoid rushed late-clock shots or to organize play after a timeout. The featured specials are Pin Down, Weakside Double, and Vegas, which incorporate down screens, double screens, reversals, flash cuts, lob passes, and cross-court skip passes.

The paper presents a proof-of-concept system for analyzing instant messaging data from seized smartphones in criminal investigations. The work is part of a national Italian project and was developed with investigators using data from two investigations involving fraud and corruption. It addresses the difficulty of manually analyzing thousands of chats and the time and resources required to process audio messages.

The proposed architecture imports chat content and metadata, including participants, timestamps, senders, and attachments, into a Neo4j property-graph knowledge graph. Whisper speech-to-text transcribes audio messages, while future extensions are planned for images and videos. A Named Entity Extraction and Linking pipeline annotates chat content and updates the graph with extracted entities. It uses transformer-based named entity recognition, BLINK for entity linking, logistic regression for NIL prediction, and supervised similarity scoring with Louvain community detection for entity clustering. Person mentions are linked to chat participants, while organizations and locations are linked to Italian Wikipedia.

Two interfaces support investigation: Neo4j provides graph queries and visualizations, while DAVE offers keyword and faceted search, entity-based filtering, document exploration, and manual correction of annotations. The design emphasizes human decision-making, traceability, and verification against original evidence.

In the second investigation, the system processed 1,442 chats, 364,690 messages, and 63,224 attachments. The NEEL pipeline processed 1,296 chats, and audio transcripts contained on average four times as many entities as text messages. Initial NER evaluation produced an F1 score of 28.8 for strong matches and 47.0 for partial matches, indicating that domain-specific fine-tuning and a larger gold standard are needed. Investigators found graph visualizations, combined textual and relational search, speech-to-text, and semantic browsing useful, while requesting simpler query methods and direct audio playback.

Current limitations include weak out-of-domain NER performance, the expertise required for Cypher queries, and errors caused by extremely long chats. Planned work includes in-domain fine-tuning, further interface development—including early Python and retrieval-augmented conversational search prototypes—and image and video enrichment. Data are stored on local servers with restricted VPN and password access, and the system avoids external APIs to protect private information.

AQTWM, Inc. (Aqua Terra) filed a preliminary long form prospectus with Canadian securities commissions (all provinces except Québec) for an IPO of common shares, through a syndicate co-led by TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity and RBC Capital Markets. Share count and price are undetermined and depend on market conditions; completion is not assured, and the offering will not occur in the United States. Aqua Terra provides oilfield water disposal services to Canadian and U.S. onshore producers.

Charlie Tillett, introduced by Joe Hadzima, gives an MIT lecture on business-plan financials. Tillett, a 1991 Sloan graduate and third-place finisher in the MIT $10K (now $100K) Contest, built the financial template he teaches while working with a team; he later served as CFO of NetScout Systems (publicly traded in 1999) and Reveal Imaging, a bomb-detection-equipment company founded in 2003, raising $125 million across more than ten transactions. He presents a downloadable Excel template and argues that the financials are the "scoreboard" of a company: they reveal key assumptions and drivers, and the CEO's main job is maintaining cash. He acknowledges that investors do not expect founders to be accountants but do expect them to understand key metrics, and he reviews business plans by looking first at the top line, then at year four (critical mass, gross margins, and large expenses such as sales and marketing), and finally at operating profit over four years as a rough proxy for capital needed (within 20–30%).

Using Reveal Imaging as a case study, he describes raising a $1 million angel round within 90 days and then a venture round structured as two $5 million tranches released on milestones, which avoided immediately needing to raise the second half; a $500,000 bank equipment line extended runway by about three months. He then details the venture capitalist's perspective: 3x–5x returns, a five-to-seven-year horizon, pressure starting the day funds arrive, and a desire for significant ownership. Equity percentage equals money invested divided by pre-money value plus investment, so $5 million on a $5 million pre-money gives 50%, and a $10 million Series B on a $15 million pre-money gives 40%, diluting Series A holders to 30%. In an example, four founders' four million shares are diluted to 80% by a $500,000 angel round at a $4.5 million pre-money, to 50% after a 50%-owning Series A (with a 12% option pool), and the founding team ends at 18.2%. Investors also receive preferred shares, anti-dilution and ratchet provisions, and board seats, with a mutually agreed fifth board member. If too much capital is raised for a small opportunity, the outcome is poor: a company at $5–10 million in revenue is "walking dead," and Reveal, at $50 million revenue, sold for $125 million (about 1.5x revenue).

Treating the business model as an income statement expressed in percentages, he walks through revenue, cost of goods sold (materials, labor, facilities, warranty and support, shipping, but not R&D), sales and marketing, R&D, G&A, and operating profit/EBITDA, advising against depreciation and allocating G&A across departments. Benchmark examples include Walmart (24% gross margin, $344 billion revenue), Target (34%), restaurants (68% COGS, $45,000 revenue per employee), Cisco (64% gross margin, 13% R&D, 25% operating profit, $573,000 per employee), Microsoft, Oracle and SAP ($250,000–$300,000 per employee), Apple ($2 million per employee), Google ($1 million, increasing as it grew), Dell (minimal R&D), and Apple and Pandora (lowest gross margins). He notes retail revenue per employee of $150,000–$200,000 and that business models evolve slowly once critical mass is reached.

On pricing, he says a claimed $10,000 customer value should probably be priced at $2,000–$3,000 so customers capture most savings. Distribution strategy affects everything from revenue to operating profit: in his example, direct sales at $100 million revenue gives $23 million sales and marketing and $20 million operating profit (20%), while a distributor taking 20% cuts revenue to $80 million and sales and marketing to $8 million, leaving $16 million operating profit. He advises against business-planning software ("TurboTax"-like), building sales projections bottom-up (salespeople, territories, reps, closure rates) rather than from total market share, avoiding multiple best/worst case models, and modeling quarterly. Rules of thumb include staffing at 50–66% of expenses, average salaries near $90,000, benefits adding about 15% (7% FICA, 8% health), roughly 2% quarterly raises, heavy use of formulas, and sales salaries ranging from $40,000–$50,000 for simple products to $150,000–$250,000 for complex software. Cash flow statements are error-prone, so cumulative operating losses plus capital expenses serve as a proxy; founder compensation should be benchmarked to peers or prior earnings.

Finally, on equity, he urges vesting for everyone over three to four years with quarterly vesting (or 20% vested after one year), notes typical post-dilution grants (CEO 5–10%, VPs 1–2.5%, senior managers 0.25%, senior individual contributors 0.10%, founders two to three times that), and says angel investors negotiate as hard as VCs — a 10% angel stake can dilute to 2.3% — while friends and family should receive a fair deal. In Q&A he explains that departing founders keep vested shares, and that while the CEO makes decisions, a CFO becomes worthwhile once venture money is taken, perhaps initially via a mentor advisor and controller, since an experienced CFO can save several percentage points of dilution.

The lecture reviews Chapter 14 on coding for bandwidth-limited additive white Gaussian noise channels, contrasting them with power-limited channels where binary codes are nearly optimal. The final is closed-book, calculators are optional, and five sheets of notes are permitted; Problem Set 10 solutions are available online, and a review session is scheduled for the following day.

For bandwidth-limited channels, constellations must be multilevel and assessed using Euclidean rather than Hamming distance. A lattice constellation is formed by selecting a finite set of points from a lattice and a shaping region. A union-bound approximation based on nearest-neighbor error events gives an error expression that separates coding gain from shaping gain and, after normalization by spectral efficiency, is independent of rate and constellation size. Integer lattices shaped by cubes have unit coding and shaping gains and share a baseline error curve applicable to m-PAM and its Cartesian products. At an error probability near \(10^{-5}\), this baseline is roughly 9 dB from the Shannon limit.

Shaping minimizes the normalized second moment of the constellation region. The optimal region is an n-sphere, providing about 0.2 dB in two dimensions and at most \(\pi e/6\), or approximately 1.53 dB, as the dimension tends to infinity. A 16-dimensional spherical region yields about 1 dB. Shell mapping, used in V.34 modems, provides roughly 0.8 dB, while trellis shaping is described as more elegant. Uniformly distributing points over a high-dimensional sphere also produces Gaussian-like projections in one or two dimensions. Although shaping cannot provide more than about 1.5 dB, it is necessary for approaching the Shannon limit.

The lecture then examines dense lattices. The hexagonal \(A_2\) lattice provides about 0.6 dB of coding gain in two dimensions, while \(D_4\), \(E_8\), \(\Lambda_{16}\), and higher-dimensional Barnes-Wall lattices provide progressively larger nominal gains. These gains become limited in practice because highly symmetric lattices have very large numbers of near neighbors, so effective gains level off around 4 dB. Barnes-Wall lattices are constructed by a nested \(u,u+v\) process analogous to the construction of Reed-Muller codes; each stage doubles both distance and dimension. The 24-dimensional Leech lattice has a nominal 6-dB gain but about 195,560 near neighbors, and is related to the Golay code.

Trellis codes, introduced by Ungerboeck in 1982, expand the constellation rather than the bandwidth and use redundancy to encode the constellation’s set partition. In a basic four-state, two-dimensional scheme, a rate-1/2 convolutional code selects among four subsets of an expanded QAM constellation. The code protects against errors between subsets, while within-subset errors remain uncoded and limit the overall minimum squared distance to 4. The resulting code has four nearest neighbors per two dimensions, yields about 3 dB of coding gain, and can be decoded with a four-state Viterbi algorithm by first selecting the closest point in each subset.

An eight-way partition permits a larger minimum squared distance and nominal coding gains up to about 6 dB, with 256- or 512-state decoders. In four dimensions, Wei’s multidimensional partition reduces constellation redundancy per two dimensions. Its eight- and sixteen-state versions provide about 4.2 and 4.5 dB, respectively, and similar codes were adopted in V.34 and ADSL. Reasonable-size trellis codes generally saturate around 5–6 dB of coding gain; adding roughly 1–1.5 dB from shaping still leaves an estimated 2–3 dB gap to the Shannon limit.

Higher-performance approaches include turbo codes, reported to approach within 1 dB of the limit, and sequential decoding, reported to approach within about 1.5 dB. Multilevel coding treats each partitioning level as a separate effective binary channel; independently coding these levels can achieve the aggregate channel capacity. Capacity-approaching codes are needed mainly on the least reliable levels, while high-rate algebraic codes may suffice on more reliable ones. The only widely used practical approach discussed is bit-interleaved coded modulation, which interleaves bits from a capacity-approaching binary code across constellation levels so existing binary-channel chips can be reused; it is used on wireless cellular channels.

The lecture concludes that coding for traditional AWGN channels is mature and already close to the Shannon limit. Remaining theoretical questions concern iterative-decoding convergence, statistical-physics connections, graph-theoretic properties, and algebraic construction of capacity-approaching codes. Research attention has increasingly shifted toward networks, multi-user systems, and data compression, while wireless-system calculations commonly assume operation at the channel’s mutual information.

STAT’s Pharmalittle highlights a December “Future of Pharmaceuticals” summit hosted by BlinkRx, where top drugmakers are expected to meet Donald Trump Jr. and administration officials. The event has raised concerns about the White House’s preference for BlinkRx because of its Trump-family ties, while direct-to-consumer sales and the planned TrumpRx website could benefit the company. Pfizer’s agreement with the administration to lower drug prices has prompted other drugmakers to pursue similar deals, though their ability to reduce prices remains uncertain. The newsletter also notes a setback for Sarepta after a New York panel recommended pausing Medicaid coverage of a Duchenne drug.

The fourth and final case study examines ongoing thesis research on manufacturing polymer microfluidic devices through hot embossing. Polymers are attractive because they are inexpensive, transparent, and mechanically tough, while embossing can be rapid and applied to individual chips or continuous polymer film. The process uses a microfabricated stamp, heated plates, and applied pressure to form a thermoplastic above its glass-transition temperature. The polymer is loaded and held to fill the stamp cavities, cooled under load, and demolded. Critical variables include temperature, load, loading rate, holding time, material properties, and pattern geometry. Differential thermal contraction makes demolding particularly difficult.

Thermal nanoimprint lithography applies similar principles to submicrometer polymer films and can transfer features without the wavelength limits of optical lithography. Its effectiveness depends on uniform residual polymer layers, while its mechanics differ from those of micro-scale embossing. Stamps can be produced by deep reactive-ion etching, electroplating, or electron-beam lithography.

The research seeks computationally efficient models that predict feature replication while minimizing time, energy, and cost. Effects occur at substrate, device, and individual-feature scales, including uneven pressure, pattern-density interactions, and difficulty filling narrow gaps. Experiments with PMMA showed that a simple elastic model using a fitted Young’s modulus could approximate embossed topography and interactions among patterns of different densities. The speaker estimated that this model supplied about 95% of the topographic information of a full finite-element simulation while running in roughly 20 seconds in Matlab. Adding a dashpot-based scaling term reasonably captured time-dependent plastic flow in longer embossing cycles.

Carefully designed test patterns were also used to estimate material properties, including temperature-dependent modulus, and to detect anisotropy. Tests of TOPAS revealed strong orientation-dependent filling, while fractional-factorial experiments indicated that temperature, force, and holding time were significant; the importance of loading rate remained uncertain. Comparisons involving PMMA, ZEONOR, and TOPAS examined how material softening temperature, viscosity, pattern dimensions, and processing conditions affect replication.

Demolding and cooling were identified as major obstacles to microscale imprinting because thermal contraction, lateral forces, mechanical locking, and stamp damage can produce ridges, distortion, shearing, or broken stamps. Mold lubricants and Teflon coatings may ease removal but do not eliminate thermal forces. Carefully controlling the demolding temperature produced flatter features in some cases, although production temperature control could be costly and operation above the glass-transition temperature risked bowing and other defects. The lecture concluded with course presentation scheduling and discussion of multiobjective optimization and one-factor-at-a-time experimental strategies.

UNC Chapel Hill reinstated professor Dwayne Dixon after a threat assessment found no basis to conclude he posed a threat or violated university policy. He had been placed on leave following allegations; his activism included counterprotests, gun-rights advocacy and former membership in Redneck Revolt.

Hetzner now directly peers with NAP Africa in Isando via a 10Gbps circuit, adding to its NAP Africa Cape Town and JINX connections. With JINX, more than 65% of Hetzner’s local traffic is routed through Internet exchange points rather than costly transit links; Hetzner contributes over 4Gbps, with traffic continuing to grow weekly. The company advocates settlement-free peering to reduce connectivity costs and latency while improving resilience. It peers with major South African network operators and content providers and encourages other operators to peer through exchange points or directly. Hetzner’s Samrand data centre has redundant transit and peering connections on 10Gbps interfaces, near major fibre routes, while providing international access through four cable systems. The company hosts more than 330,000 active domains. NAP Africa is a neutral, layer-2 IXP available throughout Teraco’s South African data centres, supporting IPv4, IPv6, scalable connectivity, and online peering tools.

The gold/silver ratio measures the relative prices of gold and silver by dividing gold’s price by silver’s price using the same currency and weight. A 60:1 ratio means 60 ounces of silver equal the value of one ounce of gold. Traders generally use the ratio for mean-reversion strategies: when it is high, they may buy silver and short gold; when it is low, they may buy gold and short silver. The ratio can be traded through futures, options, and related ETFs, with thresholds determined through backtesting.

Governments historically fixed the ratio for monetary stability, including at 12:1 in the Roman Empire and 15:1 in the United States under the Coinage Act of 1792. Its 20th-century average was 47:1; in the 21st century it has generally ranged from 50:1 to 70:1, reaching 114.77 in 2020 and a low of 35:1 in 2011. Traders commonly regard 35 as low and values above 80 as high, although the 2018–2020 spike showed that higher levels can occur.

Backtests described found that a simple GLD strategy had positive expectancy but an erratic, untradable equity curve, while the same strategy performed poorly on SLV. A pair trade based on the five-day RSI also produced flat results. Broader risk-on/off tests found no meaningful profitable strategy, and the passage concludes that no robust gold/silver ratio strategy was identified, noting that metals and commodities are difficult markets. Some commentators also argue that the ratio can gauge stock-market risk appetite.

A letter to Delta’s mayor and council opposes the proposed 35-storey development at Scott Road and 75A Avenue, arguing it conflicts with the North Delta Area Plan and Cougar Creek ISMP. The writer says it exceeds the six-storey limit, inadequately preserves trees and amenities, and would largely prevent rainwater infiltration by using the lot for parking. They dispute that it qualifies for Scott Road Revitalization Bylaw incentives, citing permanent losses of tree cover and infiltration capacity and increased flood and drought vulnerability. The writer says approval could encourage upzoning, speculation, and higher housing prices, while high-rise units have not necessarily expanded housing supply. The only acceptable change identified is a reduced underground footprint and at least 15% permeable open space for large trees and runoff infiltration. They recommend imposing this minimum on all multi-family developments to support the urban forest, groundwater, and climate resilience.

AMD’s Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification directs OS or platform software to obtain attestation measurements through interfaces such as SPDM or DPE. Some attestation schemes restrict firmware modifications, which AMD will not attempt. Update packages must ensure dependent firmware versions are present and must not be applied unless every portion can be fully updated, avoiding a forced reset.

Because patches do not persist across reboots, customers may apply them during OS boot, immediately after boot, or during operation. Issuing SFS commands requires a customer deployment agent, a 2MB-aligned DRAM command buffer, specified buffer offsets, an optional customer co-signing header, and the AMD-signed update package. The agent submits the command through the TEE mailbox and passes the buffer’s physical address to ASP firmware.

ASP verifies memory protection and applicable signatures, loads and executes the validated patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Commands can report firmware versions and patch levels, while update commands validate the entire package before applying changes. Packages follow a defined naming format and must match the system’s specific firmware and patch-level combination. Updates run concurrently with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV/ES virtual machines may need to stop and restart for relevant updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

The paper introduces EqDiff-CT, a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model for synthesizing CT-like images from CBCT. CBCT supports daily image-guided radiotherapy but suffers from scatter, truncated projections, and inconsistent Hounsfield unit calibration, while planning CT offers better soft-tissue contrast and dosimetric accuracy but cannot capture daily anatomical changes. Synthetic CT generation can improve dose calculation, segmentation, treatment adaptation, workflow efficiency, and patient comfort, although accurate HU mapping is clinically essential.

Earlier approaches included deformable registration, analytical intensity correction, GANs, CNNs, transformers, and hybrid models. Registration methods require prior CT anatomy and cannot recover high-frequency structures; GANs may be unstable and hallucinate anatomy; CNN and transformer approaches improve spatial consistency but can remain computationally costly, insufficiently interpretable, or poorly generalized. Diffusion models offer greater training stability and theoretically grounded generation, but their computational demands and cross-site generalization remain concerns.

EqDiff-CT learns CBCT-to-CT mappings without deformable priors or adversarial training. It uses a time-conditioned U-Net denoiser with C4 rotational equivariance through e2cnn, self-attention for long-range dependencies, and CBCT concatenation at every diffusion timestep. Training uses a non-adversarial combination of MSE and SSIM losses on predicted noise, while inference applies variance-corrected reverse diffusion. During training, reference CT images are progressively corrupted by a fixed Gaussian forward process, and the model learns to recover them using paired CBCT conditioning. An HU-preserving preprocessing and postprocessing pipeline is included.

Evaluation used the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset with an 80/20 patient-wise split and both slice-wise and volume-wise metrics. The proposed model outperformed an attention-free diffusion baseline and a CycleGAN baseline in SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE while preserving the mandible, airway, and cervical spine. The clinical procedures were approved by the LMU University Hospital Munich ethics committee under study number 24-0195.

Colorado’s coach said the team would focus on preparation rather than past results as Dallas prepared to play at its best after a strong record following an opening loss. Dallas had become more aggressive, physical, and effective on the forecheck against Colorado, so the emphasis was on applying pressure, minimizing time for Dallas’s skilled players, and coordinating defense with the forwards.

Each game was considered important, especially because a road victory could force Dallas to return home needing a series split. The coach stressed that Colorado had previously disappeared after strong starts and needed consistency throughout the playoffs. Although Colorado’s puck decisions were poor and Dallas played more aggressively, the close score was encouraging because neither team had played its best.

Modano was described as dangerous with the puck, Hull as an elite shooter, and Nieuwendyk as a major offensive presence. Hull’s apparent offside goal was noted but dismissed as the reason for the loss. With the series tied 1–1, Colorado needed to improve in Dallas. Madden was the only significant injury, while Brian was playing well despite sometimes trying too much and turning the puck over.

A CDC report says mosquito-, tick- and flea-borne illnesses have tripled in the U.S. since 2004. Venice is vulnerable because still waters in its canals and Ballona Wetlands can support mosquito breeding, and West Nile virus is endemic in Los Angeles County. The virus spreads from infected birds to humans and animals through mosquitoes; about 80% of infected people show no symptoms, while fewer than 1% develop severe neuroinvasive disease. Los Angeles County recorded 300 human cases in 2015, its highest recent total. Residents are advised to eliminate standing water held for more than five days and use insect repellent when outdoors between dusk and dawn, including products containing 5%–30% DEET, picaridin, IR3535 or citronella.
Weston’s library will hold free-viewer distribution, a pinhole-projector craft, and a NASA livestream for the Aug. 21 eclipse, when Weston expects about 70% coverage.

The study examines potential sources of influenza A H5 RNA detected in wastewater and developed a mass-balance model to interpret these detections. H5 RNA was detected in U.S. wastewater beginning in March 2024 alongside H5N1 outbreaks in cattle, with humans, cow’s milk, poultry feces, and wildfowl feces identified as plausible contributors.

Researchers retrospectively tested 110 archived wastewater-solids samples collected from September 2023 to May 2024 at the Southeast San Francisco treatment plant, which serves 750,000 people and has combined stormwater and sanitary sewers. Multiplex droplet digital RT-PCR measured total IAV and H1, H3, and H5 subtype RNA. H1 and H3 assays were designed using sequence alignment and evaluated in silico and against respiratory-pathogen panels.

The source model assumes measured H5 RNA comes from humans, poultry, wild birds, or milk. It partitions RNA between liquid and solid wastewater phases using a Freundlich isotherm and calculates daily H5 RNA flux from wastewater flow and total suspended solids.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018 reported third-quarter net sales of $53.265 billion, up 17% from $45.408 billion a year earlier. Gross margin was $20.421 billion, or 38.3%, compared with 38.5% in the prior-year quarter. Operating expenses increased to $7.809 billion, including $3.701 billion of research and development and $4.108 billion of selling, general and administrative expense. Operating income rose to $12.612 billion, net income to $11.519 billion, and diluted earnings per share to $2.34 from $1.67. For the nine months, net sales were $202.695 billion, net income was $45.406 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $8.99.

Third-quarter product sales included $29.906 billion from iPhone, up 20%; $9.548 billion from Services, up 31%; $3.740 billion from Other Products, up 37%; $4.741 billion from iPad, down 5%; and $5.330 billion from Mac, down 5%. iPhone growth primarily reflected a product mix with higher average selling prices, while lower Mac unit sales drove its decline. Services results included a favorable one-time $236 million item related to the resolution of lawsuits. Net sales increased in every geographic segment: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific.

At June 30, 2018, Apple reported $349.197 billion of assets, $234.248 billion of liabilities, and $114.949 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $31.971 billion, while short- and long-term marketable securities totaled $211.772 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $57.911 billion, investing activities generated $19.067 billion, and financing activities used $65.296 billion, including $53.634 billion for share repurchases and $10.182 billion for dividends and dividend equivalents.

During the third quarter, Apple repurchased 112.8 million shares for $20.0 billion, completing its prior $210 billion repurchase program and using $9.6 billion of a newly authorized $100 billion program. Apple had $12.0 billion of commercial paper outstanding and $104.1 billion of term debt principal. Its quarterly gross margin percentage was slightly below the prior year due primarily to higher product costs, partially offset by product mix and Services growth; Apple anticipated a fourth-quarter gross margin percentage of 38.0% to 38.5%.

The U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act reduced Apple’s federal statutory rate from 35% to 21%. Apple reduced its provisional transition-tax estimate from $2.6 billion to $900 million during the quarter and reported a 13.3% effective tax rate, compared with 22.9% in the prior-year quarter. Its provisional deemed repatriation tax payable was $37.0 billion.

The European Commission’s State Aid Decision calculated recoverable taxes of €13 billion, plus €1 billion of interest. Apple and Ireland appealed the decision. Apple had €4.5 billion in escrow as of June 30 and funded another €4.5 billion after quarter-end. Total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities included $8.8 billion restricted from general use.

The filing identified material legal matters involving VirnetX, with judgments totaling $440 million and $503 million in two cases, and a dispute with Qualcomm concerning device royalties, for which Apple had accrued its estimated loss. It also disclosed supply-chain and manufacturing concentration risks, future noncancelable lease payments of $9.6 billion, and unconditional purchase obligations of $8.5 billion.

The SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds, rated 9/10 by WIRED, are discounted to $128 on Amazon, saving nearly $75. They support Xbox or PlayStation, Switch, PC, and smartphones, with low-latency 2.4GHz and Bluetooth via a USB-C dongle. Battery life is about 10 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case. The SteelSeries app offers noise cancellation and game-specific equalizer presets, while the earbuds are praised for portability, comfort, isolation, and physical controls.

James Harden scored 60 points with 10 rebounds and 11 assists, leading the Houston Rockets to a 114-107 win over the Orlando Magic and becoming the first NBA player to record a 60-point triple-double. He broke Houston’s scoring record of 57 points set by Calvin Murphy in 1978. Harden made 17 of 18 free throws and scored Houston’s final six points after a 107-107 tie. The short-handed Rockets received 12 points and 13 rebounds from Clint Capela. Mario Hezonja and Marreese Speights each scored 17 for Orlando, which lost its third straight.

The disclosure describes networked exercise systems and methods that provide live instructor-led and recorded exercise classes to remote or local users. Exercise equipment, including treadmills, can integrate displays, cameras, microphones, speakers, controllers, and network communications to support multimedia classes, real-time instructor and participant interaction, performance-data sharing, competitions, leaderboards, and gamification. Backend systems manage content, communications, databases, live broadcasts, archived classes, and synchronized participant data.

Example treadmill embodiments include a deck with continuous tracks and slats, motors for belt movement and deck inclination, posts, arms, crossbars, and separate rotary controls assigned to different treadmill functions. Rotary controls may include grips, detents, illuminated indicators, tactile and audible feedback, and central input devices for starting or stopping the belt, selecting classes, or changing operating modes. Alternative capacitive, substantially linear controls are also described. Sensors measure machine and user metrics, including incline, speed, power, distance, heart rate, respiration, hydration, and calories, and may provide data to users, instructors, or other participants. A magnetic emergency-stop arrangement can stop the belt when a user-worn clip is removed.

Displays provide touch or voice-operated interfaces for live and archived classes, featured content, class libraries, schedules, “just run” content, performance trends, scorecards, leaderboards, user feedback, profiles, and account settings.

This study develops hydrogen-bonded metal inorganic-organic complex (MIOC) crystals and glasses through ligand tuning of ZIFs. Slow evaporation produced MIOC-4 (ZnCl₂HIm₂) and MIOC-7 (ZnCl₂HbIm₂), whose supramolecular structures are stabilized mainly by hydrogen bonds, with additional π–π interactions in MIOC-7. MIOC-4 has a stacked structure and melts at 440 K, while the interdigitated MIOC-7 is more thermally stable and melts at 508 K. Their glass-transition temperatures are approximately 282 and 360 K, respectively.

In situ X-ray diffraction showed that melting begins with slippage and distortion of hydrogen-bonded chains, followed by hydrogen-bond rupture and disordering. During quenching, stronger N–H···Cl bonds reform into a disordered network, while weaker C–H···Cl interactions diminish. Metal-ligand bonds and short-range Zn–N, Zn–Cl, and Zn–C correlations remain intact, whereas medium- and long-range intermolecular order disappears.

Mixed-ligand synthesis produced physical mixtures of MIOC-4 and MIOC-7 with reduced melting points and compositionally tunable glass-transition temperatures. Increasing HbIm content raised Tg from 282 to 360 K, while the lowest melting point was 415 K. Extending the strategy to Cu/Co metal nodes and SCN⁻ anions yielded additional MIOC systems, indicating that hydrogen-bond strength and network topology are more important determinants of thermal behavior than the metal node.

MIOC-7 glass exhibited enhanced, excitation-dependent visible photoluminescence, with emission color shifting from blue toward yellow through a red-edge effect associated with slow molecular relaxation and frozen conformations. Its internal photoluminescence quantum yield was 3.4%, compared with 1.2% for MIOC-7 crystals, supporting potential anti-counterfeiting applications.

Successful early offense depends on precise execution, coordination, spacing, timing, footwork, and game-speed practice. Coaches should prepare players beforehand and use the “Whole-Part-Whole” method: explain roles and defensive reads, walk through options, progress through one- to five-player breakdown drills, then go live against strong defense. Training should build confidence against presses, promote press breaking on every possession, force full-court defense, develop quick ball advancement and outlet passes, address outnumbered situations and double teams, transition into early offense, and pursue missed shots. Strategies include disruptive defense, opponent scouting, and moving directly from push to flow to continuity. Immediate defensive pressure can disrupt fast breaks and create steals and baskets.

A player handled his first major adversity by responding outstandingly after an early loss, remaining calm and mentally strong despite conceding goals. The speaker compares two teams and centers—Bergeron and Ryan O’Reilly—as skilled faceoff players who work hard, forecheck, and play a physical, team-oriented style. Both teams are difficult to play against and have mobile, puck-moving defensemen, though their size differs. The speaker emphasizes clean physical play, discipline after whistles, and putting the team first. He also says two strong goaltenders are necessary given demanding schedules and travel.

After the Diocese of Covington barred speeches at Holy Cross High School’s graduation as political and inconsistent with Catholic teaching, valedictorian Christian Bales and student council president Katherine Frantz delivered commencement addresses outside using a bullhorn. Bales, who is gay, said the restriction amplified his voice and gave him a wider audience. His four-minute speech praised Florida students’ gun-law activism and urged young people to speak candidly, resist institutions that silence them, and use opposition as empowerment. The speeches drew national media attention and broad support.

The Trump administration has called for hiring more than 400 additional assistant U.S. attorneys, but recruiting is off to a slow start. Incomplete LinkedIn data show 42 prosecutor hires from January through August, more than half fewer than in each of the previous four comparable periods. Current and former prosecutors attribute the decline to hiring freezes, higher costs, vacancies, low morale, ethical concerns, public skepticism, rising wages, and departures linked to administration initiatives.

Some U.S. Attorneys’ Offices are still recruiting; Philadelphia seeks 20 frontline prosecutors, while Southern Florida lists several criminal, civil, and appellate positions. New hires generally have strong credentials, and the Justice Department does not appear to be lowering standards, though qualified applicants are reportedly harder to find. Veteran prosecutors say office leadership is qualified and experienced lawyers remain to train recruits, but they are divided on whether to recommend government service because of its high-stakes work, political interference, and potential exposure to DOJ controversies.

Socket 940 uses an LCP base and cover rated UL 94 V-0, with a black base and natural or ivory cover. Support structures provide a package-substrate seating plane without damaging pins. Cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm, including a 0.30 mm pocket recess, and cover and seating-plane flatness must remain within 0.25 mm before and after PCB reflow and after environmental and mechanical testing. A removable overlay aids vacuum pick-and-place but cannot outgas during reflow or leave residue.

Required markings include “SOCKET 940,” locked and unlocked indicators, an A01 orientation triangle, and the supplier’s UL symbol; lot traceability must remain visible after PCB mounting. Contacts are high-strength copper alloy with minimum 1.27 µm nickel plating and 0.76 µm gold over nickel on mating surfaces. SMT attachment uses 0.64 mm PCB pads and 0.76 mm tin/lead solder balls, with solder barriers and 0.20 mm ball-field coplanarity.

A stainless-steel lever actuates and latches the contacts, requires less than 3.6 kgf, limits pin displacement to under 1.0 mm, and must preserve integrity for 50 cycles. Actual insertion and extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction requires at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact, LLCR no greater than 25 mΩ initially and after testing, specified inductance, capacitance, impedance, skew and crosstalk limits, 650 Vac dielectric withstand, and 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

Welles Wilder introduced the ADX in 1978. It is a lagging indicator that measures trend strength rather than direction, with readings from 0 to 100; higher values indicate stronger trends, while lower values indicate non-trending markets. Wilder considered readings below 15 non-trending and above 20 trending. The DI+ and DI- lines show bullish and bearish momentum, but not trend direction. ADX readings vary by timeframe and market, generally rising more sharply on shorter periods.

Backtests of stand-alone ADX strategies produced modest results. A ten-day DI crossover on the S&P 500 returned a 5.4% CAGR and 1.71 profit factor. An optimized ADX breakout strategy had a smaller 13.76% drawdown than buy-and-hold but a much lower 3.03% CAGR versus 9.9%.

The article found ADX more valuable when used as a filter with another indicator. On SPY, adding a five-to-ten-day ADX threshold of roughly 30–40 reduced market exposure to 7%, produced a 7.3% CAGR, and increased the profit factor to 2.6. On QQQ, the filtered strategy returned a 12.5% CAGR with 8% exposure. Overall, ADX performed reasonably alone but was more effective as a supplement to other indicators and as a mean-reverting tool.

A speaker describes an overtime power-play goal, praising the extra-man support, a defenseman opening space, and the deciding shot. They emphasize competing, staying disciplined, and avoiding penalties against an elite opponent. The speaker also praises the team’s depth, ability to replace key players, and a supportive hometown hockey fan base.

A Stanford, Harvard and Census Bureau study of de-identified data from 20 million U.S. children and their parents found that black boys earn less in adulthood than white boys from similar socioeconomic backgrounds in 99% of U.S. neighborhoods. Black and Native American children had the lowest rates of upward mobility, while white and Asian children had the highest. Among children raised in the bottom income fifth, 11% of white children and 2.5% of Black children reached the top fifth. Black children of parents averaging $1.1 million in income still earned 12.4% less than white children with similar family incomes.

The study also found that the Black-white earnings gap is driven largely by men: white men out-earned Black men even with similar parental incomes, while Black women earned slightly more than white women. Neighborhoods continued to affect adult earnings across racial groups, with particularly large Black-white gaps in affluent areas. Some Washington, D.C., suburbs showed relatively low racial bias and high community shares of Black fathers and greater adult parity, though the findings did not establish causation. Researchers suggested that differing historical experiences may help explain persistent disparities for Black and Native American communities.

On October 7, 2016, NVIDIA entered a five-year unsecured senior revolving credit agreement with Wells Fargo Bank and other lenders. The agreement permits borrowing, repayment, and re-borrowing of up to $575 million for working capital and general corporate purposes, with an additional $425 million available for revolving commitments or letters of credit subject to specified conditions. Loans may bear interest at NVIDIA’s election at the Adjusted LIBO Rate or Alternate Base Rate plus an applicable rate. The agreement expires October 7, 2021, and includes customary representations, covenants, default and acceleration provisions, including a debt-to-adjusted-EBITDA maintenance covenant. NVIDIA filed the related Form 8-K on October 13, 2016.

Future Electronics and NXP will host a free July 4, 2018 seminar in San Sebastian, Spain, introducing the i.MX RT Series crossover processor through presentations and hands-on exercises. The i.MX RT 105x processors feature an Arm Cortex-M7 core, real-time performance, MCU usability, and no flash memory, allowing flexible implementation at an affordable price. Registration is available via the provided link. Future Electronics is described as a global electronics distributor with 5,500 employees in 169 offices across 44 countries.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture expands concurrent GPU processing: each streaming multiprocessor can run RT Core work alongside graphics or compute and can execute two compute workloads simultaneously, with software controls for workload priorities. Dedicated RT Cores leave more SM capacity available than architectures that perform ray tracing on standard cores.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput over Turing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for accelerated ray-traced motion blur involving moving or deforming geometry. The new unit can make motion-blur rendering up to eight times faster than Turing, while a measured RTX 3080 Blender Cycles test was up to five times faster than an RTX 2080 Super. OptiX 7 supports timestamped rays and geometry motion paths. In a Wolfenstein: Youngblood frame, an RTX 2080 Super improved from 51 ms with shader cores alone to 20 ms with RT Cores and 12 ms with DLSS and Tensor Cores; an RTX 3080 rendered the frame in 6.7 ms.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BFloat16 support, 2:4 structured sparsity, and up to twice the matrix-multiplication throughput of Turing Tensor Cores. Sparse operations skip zero-valued weights, reduce data footprint and bandwidth by half, and reportedly cause virtually no inference-accuracy loss after fine-tuning. FP16 and BFloat16 provide four times the throughput of standard FP32, while TF32 provides twice the FP32 throughput. Enhanced DLSS uses a new 9x scaling factor, enabling reported 8K gaming at 60 fps on the RTX 3090.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, which transfers two bits per clock edge through four voltage levels. Supporting data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, GDDR6X delivers up to 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth on the RTX 3090, more than 52% above the TU102 in the RTX 2080 Ti. MTA encoding, interface training, equalization, and signal-integrity design address PAM4 noise, while pseudo-independent memory channels assist BVH traversal.

NVIDIA RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to keep assets compressed during transfer and perform lossless decompression on the GPU. The document reports I/O acceleration up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs, substantially reduced CPU use, faster loading, reduced stutter and object pop-in, and improved streaming of detailed assets. It also applies to professional datasets and render-queue data.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, NVIDIA reports up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB with two GPUs over third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen4, virtual-GPU support, Quadro Sync, and EGX compatibility. The RTX A6000 provides a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48 GB of GDDR6, hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and 96 GB of combined memory when paired over NVLink.

Ampere supports 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs were the first to support AV1 hardware decode; in the cited test, 8K60 HDR AV1 playback used about 4% CPU compared with over 85% for software decoding. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC while freeing CPU and graphics resources.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 and provides 24 GB of memory, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA Cores. The GA104-based RTX 3070 lacks NVLink and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X. GDDR6X memory also adds Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transactions and replays them, indicating when further memory overclocking is causing performance to plateau.

Across GeForce RTX 30-series products, NVIDIA reports up to twice the programmable-shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of the prior generation. The passage notes that specifications are supplied as-is, may be changed without notice, and are provided with limited warranties and suitability guarantees.

President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Pfizer to lower U.S. drug prices, including offering existing drugs to Medicaid patients at the lowest prices charged in other developed nations and applying the same “most-favored-nation” pricing to new drugs for Medicare, Medicaid and commercial payers. Discounted medications will be available through TrumpRx.gov.

Pfizer also received a three-year exemption from pharmaceutical-specific tariffs, contingent on continued U.S. investment. The company plans to invest $70 billion in domestic drug manufacturing and research facilities. Trump is pursuing similar agreements with other drugmakers, including ongoing negotiations with Eli Lilly, while Pfizer and 16 other companies face a deadline to reduce prices. Trump separately announced a 100% tariff on imported branded or patented pharmaceuticals beginning Oct. 1, exempting companies building U.S. plants. Pfizer shares rose more than 4% after the announcement.

On January 18, 2017, NVIDIA appointed Tim Teter as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary, effective when his employment is expected to begin January 23, 2017. Teter, formerly a Cooley LLP partner focused on patent and technology litigation, will lead NVIDIA’s legal department as David M. Shannon shifts to leading human resources and assists with legal matters until his planned retirement.

Teter’s at-will offer includes an $850,000 annual base salary, target annual incentive compensation of $250,000 beginning with fiscal 2018, a $450,000 first-anniversary bonus subject to repayment if he leaves before his second anniversary, and restricted stock units targeted at $5.8 million vesting over four years. He will also be eligible for NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and comprehensive benefits and is expected to sign the company’s standard officer indemnity agreement.

Speaking at the Brandenburg Gate, the speaker celebrates Berlin’s reunification and the fall of the Wall, honoring the courage of Berliners who resisted division and pledging a new U.S. embassy in Berlin. He argues that freedom now requires the “civil courage to build”: a Europe of independent democracies, borderless free markets and prosperity, security through bridges rather than walls, equal opportunity, and peace. He urges Germans, Americans, and young people to reject division and hatred based on race, ethnicity, or religion while accepting the discipline and responsibility of maintaining freedom. He cites democratic growth, economic reform in formerly unfree lands, and NATO’s Partnership for Peace as signs of a promising future. Reaffirming that American forces will remain in Europe, he describes the Brandenburg Gate as a gateway to a united, peaceful, free, and progressive Europe, declaring, “Berlin is free.”

The author’s dividend-focused retirement portfolio returned 15% in 2016, outperforming the dividend-inclusive S&P 500’s 11.66% return every month. The portfolio, held in Roth IRAs, workplace 403(b)s, and share-builder accounts, included only dividends and capital gains and did not count new contributions. The author’s target annual return is 6%–8%; the portfolio returned 5.39% in 2015.

Beginning with 27 positions and ending with 35, the portfolio’s top 2016 performers were Chevron (+30.84%), JPMorgan (+30.68%), AT&T (+23.60%), 3M (+18.54%), and Aflac (+16.19%). Its largest losses were Gilead Sciences (−29.23%), CVS Health (−19.29%), Starbucks (−7.51%), Coca-Cola (−3.49%), and Target (−0.52%). The author withheld additional investment in Gilead pending a strong quarter or acquisition and viewed Starbucks’ decline as a potential buying opportunity.

The portfolio added Visa, Cisco, Pepsi, Cummins, Honeywell, Qualcomm, Disney, and V.F. Corp., while making one sale: exchanging Baxalta for Visa in January. Boeing, Cisco, and Microsoft were the strongest 2016 purchases, gaining approximately 34%, 29%, and 25%, respectively; both CVS Health purchases remained below their purchase prices. Six stocks were held in two share-builder accounts and purchased monthly.

Despite acknowledging that unusually strong returns may not recur, the author intends to continue buying dividend-paying and dividend-raising companies when shares appear fairly valued. The article states that the authors are not investment professionals and advises readers to conduct their own research.

The paper frames multi-agent reinforcement learning through repeated-game theory and asks when decentralized “win-stay, lose-shift” updates can reach equilibrium. It formalizes ε-satisficing paths and introduces grouped satisficing paths, where all members of a player group retain their strategies when every member is a best responder. It also defines the ε-best-response group count and studies its local extrema topologically.

For finite-player pure-strategy games with convex compact strategy sets, continuous partially analytic payoffs, and an equilibrium in every subgame, Theorem 2 proves that every initial joint strategy admits a finite grouped satisficing path ending at equilibrium. Theorem 1 shows that, under the first two assumptions, groups achieving best responses at a state continue doing so along all admissible successors, enabling reduction to a subgame.

Corollaries establish finite satisficing paths from arbitrary initial mixed strategies to mixed equilibria in N-player games with finite strategy sets and in stationary or k-step finite-state Markov games. These results do not restrict update functions and support stochastic update approaches. Open questions concern necessary and sufficient conditions, extension to ε > 0, and restrictions on non-best-responding players’ strategy changes.

The lecture examines two algorithmic geometry topics. For protein folding, it focuses on the HP lattice model, which represents amino acids as hydrophobic (H) or polar/hydrophilic (P) and maximizes nonconsecutive H-H adjacencies. Optimal folding is NP-hard in both two and three dimensions. A parity-based approximation algorithm guarantees at least one-third of the optimal score, the best known approximation discussed. Unique optimal foldings exist for certain closed and open chain lengths, while related uniqueness and protein-design questions remain open.

For interlocked 3D chains, the lecture classifies which pairs of short universal-joint chains can separate: two-bar chains are always separable, as are pairs of three-bar chains, while three- and four-bar chains can interlock. It also discusses Lubiw’s problem of determining how many vertices must be cut to unlock a chain, with known lower and upper bounds of roughly \((n-1)/4\) and \((n-3)/2\). Interlocked chains are also used in constructions proving that deciding whether one chain configuration can move to another is PSPACE-complete; whether arbitrary chains can be unfolded from a straight configuration remains open.

E-mini futures are electronically traded contracts representing one-fifth the size of standard futures contracts. First launched by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange in 1997 for the S&P 500, they now cover stock indexes, commodities, currencies, and individual stocks. They provide retail investors with lower capital requirements, leverage, high liquidity, nearly continuous trading, and the ability to hedge or speculate. Their leverage can also magnify losses, and their limited scope and volatility create additional risk.

Trading requirements and costs depend on the contract and broker. For example, the S&P 500 e-mini’s value is $50 multiplied by the index, with a $10,000 minimum margin at an index level of 4,000. The article suggests keeping roughly $13,000–$15,000 to cover margin and potential losses. General e-mini margins are described as approximately $400–$900, while commissions generally range from $0.50 to $2.50 per contract, plus exchange, broker, and clearing fees.

A Rubber Band-style strategy was backtested on the S&P 500 e-mini from January 2000 through 2021 and tested out-of-sample on 2022 data. It produced 163 trades, an average gain of 0.89%, a 79% win rate, and a profit factor of 2. Its 13 trades in 2022 averaged a 0.18% gain, compared with a 15% S&P 500 decline.

The FAQ notes that traders need a futures broker account and should understand margin, order types, expiration, and risk management. Strategies should be backtested because approaches differ by asset. Although no legal limit exists on daily e-mini trades, brokers may impose pattern-day-trader restrictions, higher margin, or increased monitoring. Positions must be settled or offset at expiration. Because most retail traders fail, the article emphasizes discipline, detailed records, and a written, statistically supported trading plan. It also warns that scalping is highly competitive and burdened by commissions and slippage.

WIRED selected tested Amazon Big Deal Days offers for Prime members during the October 7–8 event. Discounts cover streaming and smart-home devices, headphones, chargers, routers, cameras, gaming gear, trackers, and home security products. Home and kitchen deals include desks, a Ninja Blast blender, Instant Pot air fryers, cookware, cleaning tools, dehumidifiers, humidifiers, bedding, and pillows. Pet selections include cameras, feeders, fountains, and a smart bird feeder. Other offers feature antivirus, grooming devices, toys, and games. Notable prices include a Roku Streaming Stick 4K for $30, SteelSeries Rival 3 Gen 2 mouse for $45, Eufy S350 camera for $80, and Bissell Little Green Machine for $100. WIRED states that editors independently select the products and may receive compensation from retailers or linked purchases.

The bibliometric analysis examines the competencies required of future leaders in digital education transformation within Thailand’s Digital Thailand 4.0 and Education 4.0 agendas. It reviewed eligible full papers published in open-access journals or academic conferences since 2019 during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on digital disruption, digital literacy, Education 4.0, and digital transformation leadership.

The analysis identifies five core areas. Digital Literacy is the foundation for accessing and using technology, understanding information, maintaining cybersecurity, creating digital media, and collaborating online. Digital Readiness requires organizational vision, strategy, mindset change, digital skills, secure infrastructure, and digitized processes and documentation. Digital Culture involves embracing technology, hybrid learning, digital data management, collaboration, innovation, and data-driven decision-making while protecting data security. Digital Mindset requires accepting inevitable change, applying design thinking, and moving beyond traditional educational practices. Digital Leadership depends on professional growth, rethinking and reinventing roles, adaptability, clear executive vision, effective communication, teamwork, and the knowledge, skills, abilities, and infrastructure needed to guide transformation.

The passage also describes the shift from teacher-centered education toward project-based, remote, and online learning, with educators assuming expanded roles in digital guidance and supervision. It concludes that effective digital transformation requires coordinated adaptation by leaders, educators, teams, institutions, and students. Technology may support transformation, but good teachers remain essential, and digital changes should be adapted to benefit students and society.

This study examines Songyang Academy’s history, educational philosophy, and relationship to modern general education using documentary research, field studies, interviews, observations, and historical materials. Founded as a Buddhist temple in 484 CE and later organized as Taiyi School, the academy flourished during the Northern Song through imperial support and lectures by prominent Neo-Confucian scholars. It later declined amid political unrest, briefly revived during the early Qing, and ultimately collapsed after the imperial examination system was abolished.

Songyang Academy emphasized moral education, personality cultivation, practical learning, and the unity of knowledge and action. It welcomed students regardless of region or status and promoted autonomous learning, questioning, debate, and critical thinking, with teachers serving as guides. Its management system combined hierarchical administration with student participation.

The article concludes that the academy’s emphasis on holistic development, responsibility, ethical conduct, and academic inquiry aligns with general education’s aim of developing morality, wisdom, physical fitness, and comprehensive literacy. Reviving and adapting its educational model could offer contemporary education valuable approaches for cultivating well-rounded social talents.

Virtual education can provide flexible scheduling, individualized or self-paced instruction, expanded course access, credit recovery and retaking, accommodations and progress monitoring for students with special needs, greater comfort for students with physical limitations, increased parental engagement, and preparation for postsecondary learning. Challenges include limited internet access, technology requirements, increased family responsibilities, students’ need for motivation and self-direction, delayed feedback, isolation, and difficulties maintaining engagement and instructional quality.

The study examined Indiana public-school districts during the 2020–21 school year using surveys of all 290 superintendents and 77 virtual-program administrators, followed by volunteer, semistructured interviews. Survey response rates were 33.1% for superintendents and 47% for program administrators. Interviews, conducted virtually and lasting about twenty minutes, were transcribed and coded into themes concerning pandemic effects on districts, teachers, and students. Most survey respondents represented rural districts or districts with fewer than 2,500 students.

Pandemic-related parental concerns were a leading reason for adopting or maintaining virtual programs: 79.2% of superintendents and 84.8% of program administrators rated or identified this factor as highly important. Credit recovery was also prominent, cited by 48% of superintendents and 77.1% of administrators. The most frequently identified benefits were maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, credit recovery, and learner convenience and flexibility. The leading challenges were student engagement, identified by 80.5% of superintendents and 97.1% of administrators, and ensuring curriculum and instructional quality, identified by 79.2% and 85.3%, respectively. Staffing, professional development, student retention, and excessive cost were additional concerns.

Interviewees described enrollment and revenue pressures, rapidly changing technology plans, expanded grade-level offerings, and greater demand for school-choice options. Teachers experienced stress, limited control over their work, inadequate training, and difficulty using multiple platforms, although they also developed stronger technology skills. Students faced challenges involving attendance, engagement, time management, independent learning, parental support, mental health, and social connections. Some students who had struggled in traditional settings succeeded virtually. Participants generally characterized the programs as successful for maintaining student enrollment and engagement during the pandemic, while noting that virtual education did not fully replace face-to-face relationships and support.

The findings and cited research indicate that the pandemic accelerated existing uses of virtual education rather than creating entirely new benefits and challenges. Districts were encouraged to understand local demand, design programs around engagement and instructional quality, provide effective professional development, support teachers, and promote parental and social-emotional support. Future research should examine post-pandemic program changes, the characteristics of successful virtual students and educators, and ways to improve virtual teaching and learning.

The passage provides TI E2E support resources, trademark ownership, and an ESD warning that improper handling can degrade performance or cause complete device failure. The revision history for MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G1518, and MSPM0G1519 lists updates to device variants, timers, communication interfaces, electrical specifications, power characteristics, flash endurance, DMA, SRAM, security, and operating modes from November 2024 to April 2025. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information follows, including package drawings, soldering and thermal-pad guidance, product-status notes, RoHS and moisture-sensitivity information, part-marking details, and automotive-qualified Q1 variants. TI disclaims warranties for its technical resources and states that developers are responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements.

Kobe University researchers found that dustlike orchid seeds germinate only near decaying logs, where seedlings form exclusive partnerships with wood-decaying fungi that supply needed carbon. These fungi closely match those associated with adults of the same species that have coral-shaped rhizomes. The findings reveal a hidden carbon pathway from deadwood to green plants and suggest that maintaining fungal associations may have facilitated the evolution of fully mycoheterotrophic orchids. Protecting wild orchids therefore requires safeguarding deadwood and its fungi, particularly in warm, humid forests.

The study assessed elementary teachers’ attitudes toward inclusive education for learners with special education needs in Liloan District, Cebu, and examined whether teacher demographics influenced those attitudes. It used a descriptive correlational design involving 30 purposively selected teachers from four public schools. Data were collected through a demographic questionnaire and a Modified Scale of Teachers’ Attitudes Toward Inclusion (STATIC), covering perceived advantages and disadvantages, professional issues, philosophical issues, and logistical concerns. Responses were analyzed in SPSS using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and ANOVA, following an Input–Process–Output model informed by theories of planned behavior, ecological systems, social learning, and relevant Philippine laws and DepEd policies.

Most respondents were female, married, aged 34–43, and had completed master’s-level units. Teachers generally had positive attitudes, particularly regarding inclusion’s philosophical and professional dimensions, and reported low burnout. They recognized social benefits and supported equal access and differentiated instruction. However, they expressed uncertainty about academic outcomes and concerns about large classes, limited preparation time, insufficient resources and specialist support, scheduling, materials, assistive technology, and teacher-to-learner ratios. Most teachers had limited experience teaching learners with special needs and had attended only one or two inclusion-training sessions.

No statistically significant relationships were found between demographic characteristics and attitudes toward inclusion. The study recommended an evidence-based Teacher Inclusion Support Plan centered on sustained, tailored professional development; practical classroom experience and mentorship; stronger pre-service preparation; smaller classes; additional qualified personnel; improved coordination with special education specialists; assistive technologies and instructional materials; adequate budgets; and parent–teacher partnerships. Continued monitoring, refinement, and pre- and post-implementation evaluation were also recommended to sustain inclusive practices and reduce teacher burnout.

Classes resumed at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, two weeks after a student’s AR-15 shooting killed 17 students and teachers. About 50 officers secured the campus, where counselors, therapy animals and memorial tributes greeted students. The schedule began with fourth period, allowing students and teachers to reunite with those present during the shooting; the freshman building remained cordoned off.

Students described emotional trauma and nervousness while continuing their advocacy for stricter gun laws. Dick’s Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and prohibit gun sales to anyone under 21.

After relatives gave emotional testimony, a Florida House committee approved a bill raising the long-gun purchase age to 21 and allowing trained, deputized teachers to carry concealed weapons if districts permit it. The superintendent and student activist David Hogg opposed arming teachers. The Senate approved a similar bill in committee, while Gov. Rick Scott said he wanted school-safety legislation passed but did not say whether he would veto the package if it included teacher arming.

The speaker valued the honor despite not receiving a rookie nomination. They stayed in Europe an extra year to prepare mentally and physically, trained hard, and drew motivation from veteran Flyers teammates. After a poor five-game start, their confidence rose and performance improved.

The passage describes the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontroller features and support resources. SRAM provides up to 128KB of zero-wait-state volatile memory in two 64KB banks: ECC- or parity-protected Bank 0 remains available in run, sleep, stop, and standby modes, while unprotected Bank 1 has configurable availability in run, sleep, and stop and can be powered down during stop. Boundary registers divide SRAM into two read-write edge regions and a central read-execute region to protect code from unintended modification. The devices support up to 93 GPIO pins with multi-bit operations and low-power wake functions, while IOMUX provides programmable pad settings and peripheral signal routing.

Two 12-bit ADCs support single-ended inputs, simultaneous sampling, 4Msps conversion, hardware averaging, internal temperature and supply monitoring, and internal or external references. The temperature sensor has factory calibration data. VREF offers selectable 1.4V and 2.5V internal references or an external reference, while comparators provide blanking, low-power wake, selectable inputs, and timer fault handling. A buffered 12-bit DAC supports 8- or 12-bit output, calibration, multiple data formats, FIFO/DMA operation, and hardware triggering.

Security and processing features include AES accelerators, firewalls, secure storage for up to four AES keys, CRC modules, a 32-bit true random number generator, and a hardware math accelerator. Communication peripherals include UART, I²C, SPI, and CAN-FD. The low-frequency subsystem contains a 32kHz RTC and independent watchdog; the device also includes a windowed watchdog and general-purpose and advanced timers.

A two-wire serial wire debug interface and password-protected UART- or I²C-capable boot strap loader are provided. The factory region contains read-only device capabilities, identification data, and trim information. Recommended layout includes VDD/VSS ceramic decoupling, an RC network on NRST, an optional precision ROSC resistor for frequency correction, a dedicated VCORE capacitor, and pullups for open-drain I/O.

The document also lists TI development tools and documentation, MSP versus X device nomenclature, ESD precautions, the April 2025 revision history, mechanical and orderable information, package details, and automotive-qualified variants.

An economic analysis estimated that keeping the NIH’s 1980–2007 budget 40 percent smaller could have prevented some drugs approved between 2000 and 2023. Of 557 approvals, 59 percent had patents citing NIH-supported research, and 65 had patents in which more than one-quarter of citations referenced NIH-funded work. Drugs linked to at-risk grants more often received FDA priority review—60 percent versus 41 percent—and had higher average market value. Researchers said the findings suggest substantial cuts would have reduced medical innovation, while emphasizing that the analysis cannot establish whether particular drugs would have been invented and that indirect research effects may be larger than measured.

The author refers to his 21-year-old college daughter as “The Girl” to protect her privacy and says she has the abilities of a literature professor: she reads and writes insightfully, performs confidently before audiences, defends her views with evidence, and is very funny. Yet he considers full-time literature-teaching positions extremely scarce and does not want her to pursue one despite her promise. He describes a worsening academic job market shaped by rising costs, demographics, generative AI, political hostility, and reduced faculty hiring. Journalism and publishing have also contracted, while web publications failed to replace lost midlist jobs. He encourages his daughter’s interest in librarianship, hopes libraries remain viable, and asks readers for advice for talented prospective professors while continuing to root for her.

Brian O'Loughlin sued the Patrolmen's Benevolent Association of New York and its president, Phil Caruso, for defamation over a letter published in the PBA's magazine New York's Finest. The letter concerned a $20 contribution deducted from members' paychecks that the PBA donated to build a memorial for officers killed in the line of duty. O'Loughlin suggested the money be spent on bullet-proof vests and other equipment and requested a refund; Caruso ignored these suggestions, calling O'Loughlin and eight other refund-seeking officers persons who "have no feelings" and "are a disgrace" to the police force. Defendants moved to dismiss under CPLR 3211(a)(7), and the Bronx County Supreme Court (Barry Salman, J.) granted the motion. The Appellate Division affirmed unanimously without costs. Applying the standard of Silsdorf v Levine, the court held the challenged statements were indefinite, ambiguous, not objectively verifiable, and expressed pure opinion in context, rather than actionable "mixed opinion," and that O'Loughlin's alternative proposed uses of the money did not render them false; accordingly the complaint failed to state a cause of action.

Growing population and food consumption are increasing cereal production and pesticide use. The grain and cereal crop protection market includes insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides; herbicides dominate due to low costs, increased R&D, and new active ingredients. Crop rotation supports crop protection, soil nutrients, erosion control, and yields, while chemical use can harm the environment and human health. North America leads the market, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, and Asia Pacific is expected to grow rapidly.

Tesla, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022. Its common stock trades on Nasdaq under “TSLA,” and 3,157,752,449 shares were outstanding as of October 18, 2022. Tesla reported two operating segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties, including those related to COVID-19, supply chains, competition, demand, operations, costs and financial performance.

At September 30, 2022, Tesla had total assets of $74.426 billion, total liabilities of $33.302 billion and stockholders’ equity of $39.851 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $19.532 billion, short-term marketable securities were $1.575 billion, inventory was $10.327 billion and property, plant and equipment, net, was $21.926 billion.

For the third quarter, revenue was $21.454 billion, compared with $13.757 billion a year earlier. Automotive revenue was $18.692 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $1.117 billion, and services and other revenue was $1.645 billion. Gross profit was $5.382 billion, operating income was $3.688 billion and net income was $3.331 billion, compared with $3.660 billion, $2.004 billion and $1.659 billion, respectively. Diluted earnings per share were $0.95, compared with $0.48.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2022, revenue was $57.144 billion, compared with $36.104 billion in 2021. Automotive revenue increased to $50.155 billion from $31.265 billion, energy generation and storage revenue to $2.599 billion from $2.101 billion, and services and other revenue to $4.390 billion from $2.738 billion. Gross profit was $15.076 billion, operating income was $9.755 billion and net income was $8.880 billion, compared with $8.759 billion, $3.910 billion and $3.301 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.55, compared with $0.95.

For the first nine months, net cash provided by operating activities was $11.446 billion.
