Investing activities used $5.842 billion, including $5.300 billion for property and equipment purchases, while financing activities used $3.032 billion, including $3.0 billion of debt repayments. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash ended the period at $20.149 billion.

Tesla completed a three-for-one stock split in August 2022 and retroactively adjusted all share and per-share information. The filing said COVID-19 continued to cause supply-chain constraints, port congestion, supplier delays and semiconductor shortages. Inflation and higher shipping, raw-material and labor costs led Tesla to adjust product pricing while continuing efforts to reduce manufacturing costs.

Automotive sales revenue is recognized when control transfers to customers upon delivery, while regulatory-credit revenue is recognized when control of the credits transfers. Automotive deferred revenue, primarily associated with Full Self-Driving features, connectivity, Supercharger access and software updates, totaled $2.80 billion; Tesla expected to recognize $1.09 billion within 12 months. Energy-generation and storage deferred revenue totaled $665 million, with $12 million expected to be recognized within 12 months and the remainder over periods extending to 25 years.

Digital assets had a carrying value of $218 million and fair value of $226 million at September 30, 2022. During the first nine months of 2022, Tesla converted approximately 75% of its digital-asset purchases into fiat currency, recorded $170 million of impairment losses and realized $64 million of gains. Inventory write-downs totaled $91 million for the nine months. The accrued warranty reserve was $2.771 billion at quarter-end.

Debt and finance leases totaled $3.553 billion, consisting of $1.457 billion current and $2.096 billion long-term. The company had $2.266 billion of unused committed credit facilities and was in material compliance with its debt covenants. Tesla early repaid $819 million of Solar Asset and Loan-backed Notes, recording a $24 million extinguishment charge, and fully settled its 2022 convertible notes.

Under its Buffalo, New York agreement, Tesla must meet employment and investment requirements, including spending or incurring $5 billion in New York through December 31, 2029. Tesla reported that it was in excess of applicable targets. Its Shanghai land-use arrangement requires RMB 14.08 billion of capital expenditures by the end of 2023 and RMB 2.23 billion of annual tax revenue beginning at the end of 2023; Tesla said it expected to meet the requirements.

Legal proceedings included the SolarCity acquisition litigation, the 2018 CEO Performance Award litigation and litigation concerning directors’ compensation. In the SolarCity case, the Delaware Court of Chancery entered judgment for Elon Musk on all counts on April 27, 2022, and the plaintiff appealed. The CEO award case was proceeding as a derivative action with trial scheduled for November 2022.

Kayleigh Gray, whose premature daughter Emilia was born at 27 weeks and treated for months at Royal Preston Hospital’s Neo Natal Unit, designed 25 pairs of acrylic turtle doves. Her employer, Sign Build, produced them for donation, with one dove staying with each baby and the other taken home by parents.

The team maintains the same focused mentality it has had throughout the series and is excited to be one win from the Stanley Cup. They praise Marian for his smart, hard, simple style, leadership, and contributions on and off the ice, noting that his previous Cup-final losses only make this opportunity more meaningful. Reaching the final has been a lifelong dream for many players, inspired by Pittsburgh’s comeback last year. The team emphasizes discipline, composure, contributions from players throughout the lineup, and the importance of avoiding frustration when facing calls. Support from fans has helped during the last three games, but the players are focused on delivering their best performance in the next game. Despite unexpected success in only their third professional season, they are enjoying the journey and whatever lies ahead.

Vertical farming grows crops without soil in controlled environments, stacking them in layers and using hydroponic, aeroponic and other systems. The global market is projected to reach USD 6 billion by 2022, with a 21% CAGR during 2016–2022. Drivers include food quality and demand, population growth, reduced water and soil dependence, technology, artificial lighting and zero pesticide/fertilizer use. High initial costs, lighting energy use and high-value crop production hinder growth. North America leads; Asia-Pacific is expected to grow rapidly.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated August 15, 2019, announcing results for the quarter ended July 28, 2019. The filing furnished a press release and CFO Commentary by Colette M. Kress as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. These materials were not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act and were not subject to specified Securities Act liabilities.

Only 18% of U.S. workers are very confident their retirement savings are secure. The passage recommends estimating retirement income from savings and Social Security, reviewing investment fees, and maintaining an age-appropriate asset allocation. It warns that saving 10% may be insufficient and that replacing at least current income may require increased savings. It also promotes strategies that could increase annual Social Security income by up to $16,122.

An analysis by Notre Dame Law professor Derek Muller found that attorneys and staff at 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms made about $52 million in Democratic-affiliated contributions and $4 million in Republican-affiliated contributions in 2023–2024. Democrats received 92.45% of contributions, compared with an approximately 6-to-1 ratio in 2017–2020. Cleary Gottlieb led top-grossing firms in Democratic support at 99.7%, while Nelson Mullins had the lowest share at 66.4%.

E-mini Russell 2000 futures are derivative contracts that allow traders to speculate on or hedge U.S. small-cap performance. The underlying Russell 2000 is a market-cap-weighted index tracking the 2,000 smallest companies in the Russell 3000; it was created by Frank Russell in 1984 and is maintained by FTSE Russell. The E-mini contract trades on CME Globex and has a value equal to $50 times the index. CME also offers Micro E-mini versions.

Trading occurs Sunday through Friday, generally from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily maintenance break. Quarterly March, June, September, and December contracts are listed for five consecutive quarters. Contracts are cash-settled using special opening quotes, normally on the third Friday of the contract month at 9:30 a.m. ET. At an index value of 1,841.2, one contract was worth $92,060. The standard tick value is $5, and the minimum price fluctuation is 0.10 index points.

A futures strategy may combine technical and fundamental analysis with defined entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management for speculation, hedging, arbitrage, or spread trading. The passage presents a Russell 2000 rebalance strategy that buys at the close on the first trading day after June 23 and sells at the close on the first trading day of July. Its reported backtest produced an unleveraged gain of 1.34% per trade, a 76% win rate, and average winners larger than average losers. The index tends to perform better in spring than summer, with August and December also stronger within their respective seasons.

Traders can access the contracts through a funded futures broker or trade tracking CFDs, which do not expire. The passage reports a November 30, 2022 price of $1,841.2 and an all-time futures high of 2,460.8 in November 2021; it gives the underlying index’s all-time low as 106.07 in October 1987. Charts are available through CME, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, and paid platforms such as MultiCharts.

Principal risks involve leveraged losses from adverse price movements. Prices may be influenced by heavily weighted component stocks, interest rates, economic news, and the U.S. dollar.

WiseGuyReports published a research report on the US data center UPS market, forecasting a 4.01% CAGR from 2016 to 2020. It explains that UPS systems automatically supply power during outages and voltage fluctuations until generators take over, typically for seconds to minutes. Their core components are a rectifier, inverter, and battery or flywheel; these support data center availability, efficiency, scalability, and protection from damage.

The report covers the market’s current situation and growth prospects through 2020, including market size, segmentation, drivers, challenges, trends, opportunities, threats, and vendor strengths and weaknesses. It divides systems by topology—standby, line-interactive, and double-conversion online—and by placement: centralized, zone, and rackmount.

Key vendors include ABB, Eaton, Emerson Network Power, GE Industrial Solutions, Schneider Electric, and Tripp Lite. Increased data center power outages is identified as a market driver, UPS battery failure as a challenge, and advances in data center infrastructure management as a trend.

New York’s Board of Regents unanimously approved an emergency pathway allowing special-education students to earn local high-school diplomas through occupational assessments instead of minimum Regents exam scores in English and math. The 16-member committee’s vote virtually assures full-board approval and applies to students graduating as early as January. Under the plan, students can qualify by meeting Career Development and Occupational Studies requirements and having district superintendents verify academic proficiency; graduating students in 2017-18 or 2018-19 may instead have principals certify entry-level employment skills. The change follows lobbying by parents and could affect many students: in 2016, over 15,000 students with disabilities statewide failed to graduate within four years. Critics warned the rushed policy could revive separate academic tracks and said the prior flexibility for students with disabilities needed more time to evaluate.

Turkey secured a €974 million loan from international lenders for a central Anatolian highway linking provincial centres, trade routes and export corridors. The project is intended to reduce travel times, support logistics, investment and employment, and strengthen connectivity between Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Environmental and social standards apply, though rugged terrain, land disputes, borrowing costs and lira volatility could create delays and increase financing pressures.

Jawed Zia resigned from Novartis India 15 days after taking charge and may join Abbott India. Novartis named no successor. The firms compete in diabetes and cardiovascular drugs, share tie-ups and face price-collusion scrutiny.

SARS-CoV-2 causes COVID-19; no coronavirus therapies are approved. The DAWN protocol studies drugs or convalescent plasma, whose potential benefits and risks require randomized controlled testing in hospitalized infected adults.

A hockey team discusses needing four goals to win, calling one goal "huge" and a second-effort score. As the lower seed, they knew they had to win games on the road. The goalie made two or three big saves before the opponent scored on a play they had known about. They used four lines with five days off, credited the Clark line with playing well on the road, and said road success comes from style and system, not lineup. They also felt they need a better first period, as the score didn't reflect the play.

The passage defines swing trading as holding financial instruments for a few days to several weeks to capture short- to medium-term price movements. It presents 10 free swing-trading strategies developed and backtested in Amibroker, including:

- Monday reversal and new-intraday-high strategies in the S&P 500  
- An overnight S&P 500 strategy  
- Monday/Tuesday trading in Nasdaq  
- Rotation between SPY and TLT, and among SPY, GLD, and TLT  
- An XLP mean-reversion strategy  
- A MACD-histogram strategy  
- Turn-of-the-month trading in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq  
- A trend-following strategy using the 200-day and 12-month moving averages  

Several strategies have been tested over long periods, including out-of-sample testing. The passage reports that a 200-day moving-average strategy reduced the S&P 500’s maximum drawdown to 28% versus 55% for buy and hold, while a Nasdaq-related strategy produced a 7.2% CAGR and a 51% drawdown versus 83% for its index.

Backtesting is presented as a way to estimate potential results, but the strategies are described only as ideas that require independent verification. Traders are advised to start small, risk only manageable money, use mechanical or automated execution, and conduct their own research. Most swing traders are said to be unsuccessful, while successful traders are characterized as using quantified, backtested, mechanical systems with out-of-sample validation.

Realistic annual swing-trading returns are stated as 5%–20%, with emphasis on risk-adjusted returns and drawdowns rather than unrealistic triple-digit gains. Buying and holding is described as a long-term foundation, citing an approximate 10% annual CAGR over the last 100 years, and combining it with systematic swing trading is suggested. Some complete strategy materials and code require paid membership.

The Florida First District Court of Appeal affirmed AHCA’s final order dismissing Glenwood Nursing Center’s request for an administrative hearing with prejudice. Glenwood missed the June 14, 2010 deadline to request a hearing after AHCA filed deficiencies and sought revocation of its nursing home license and penalties.

The court found no equitable tolling. Although AHCA’s counsel agreed after the deadline to accept Glenwood’s late request, Glenwood knew the deadline had expired, no extension was granted before it passed, and Glenwood cited no extraordinary circumstances, misleading conduct, or mistake in filing with the wrong forum. The court distinguished Foley and found Watson more persuasive because Glenwood failed to comply with the clear, written 21-day filing directive.

The court also rejected Glenwood’s claim that its June 15 request amended or related back to an April 16 letter sent to CMS stating that it disputed state deficiencies. Florida law requires hearing requests to be filed with the state agency, and Glenwood cited no authority permitting a CMS filing to serve as an AHCA hearing request. Even assuming the CMS letter could qualify, sending a copy to an AHCA field office manager did not satisfy the requirement that Glenwood file the request with the agency clerk.

The disclosure describes wood-type golf club heads, particularly drivers, featuring raised or bi-level soles that increase sole curvature, stiffness, mass savings, and acoustic performance while reducing the need for reinforcing ribs. Some embodiments elevate most of the sole above front and rear sit pads, use separate toe- and heel-side raised portions, or incorporate downward-extending cantilevered ledges and sloped transitions.

The club-head body may include a front channel, sole and crown openings, lightweight composite or polymer sole and crown inserts, thick/thin sole regions, internal ribs, adjustable head-shaft connections, and sliding or threaded weights. Adjustable weights can shift the center of gravity and moment of inertia to alter ball flight, spin, and forgiveness. Metallic bodies may be combined with composite inserts to reduce mass while retaining structural strength.

The disclosure also describes curvature measurements, dimensional ranges, mass, volume, center-of-gravity and moment-of-inertia targets, forgiveness ratios, and methods for manufacturing the heads using metallic frames and composite or thermoplastic components.

The tutorial demonstrates how to deploy Mattermost 4.9.0 on CentOS 7 using MariaDB and Nginx as an SSL reverse proxy. It covers prerequisites, including a domain, Nginx, and an SSL certificate; creation of a Mattermost database and system user; downloading and configuring the server; and testing it locally on port 8065. It then creates and enables a systemd service for automatic startup. Nginx is configured to redirect HTTP to HTTPS, proxy requests and WebSocket connections to Mattermost, and cache content. After reloading Nginx, the browser-based setup creates the initial administrator account and first team. Final configuration includes setting the site URL, enabling email notifications with SMTP details, and restarting Mattermost to apply the changes.

The SEC fined Altaba, formerly Yahoo, $35 million for failing to investigate and disclose a breach affecting hundreds of millions of accounts. Yahoo publicly reported the breach in 2016, two years after learning of it.

U.S. Treasury yields rose Monday, rebounding from recent lows as easing tensions with North Korea prompted investors to reduce safe-haven debt holdings and move toward stocks and other risky assets. The 10-year yield climbed over 3 basis points to 2.222%, while the two-year yield rose 2 basis points to 1.314%. Friday’s lows followed softer July inflation data and reduced expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters up to 2 MHz. They require external gate drivers and support buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. External current sensing is compared with the COMP voltage to determine power-switch turn-off.

Hiccup operation begins when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, initiating cycle-by-cycle current limiting while CHICC is charged by an 80-µA pulsed current. At 0.6 V, switching stops and the soft-start pin is discharged. CHICC is then recharged to 1 V and discharged with a 1-µA restart current until it reaches 0.3 V, triggering soft start again. CHICC controls both intervals, and a minimum value of 3.3 nF is recommended. The FAULT pin supports additional external protection: exceeding a typical 0.6 V for the specified 0.4–1.4-µs pulse width causes shutdown. Shutdown persists until FAULT falls below 0.5 V, followed by a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles and another soft-start attempt.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The minimum is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, although 1 times that slope is recommended. Its value is set with a resistor from RSC to AVSS. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be used; Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Thermal shutdown stops switching at a typical junction temperature of 175°C and permits restart below 160°C.

A 5-V, 500-kHz synchronous push-pull design using GaN FETs illustrates component selection. It uses a 205-kΩ timing resistor, a 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 25-ns dead time, a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms of soft start. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-µH primary inductance. Selected devices include 170-V primary GaN FETs and an 80-V synchronous rectifier. The output stage uses a 0.47-µH inductor and 2.3 mF total output capacitance; an optional LC filter can further reduce output noise and mitigate radiation-induced transient effects. Type 2A compensation targets 10 kHz crossover and uses 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF components. The example also selects 3.3 nF for CHICC, 102 kΩ for RSC, and 7.5 Ω for current sensing with a 1:100 current-sense transformer.

The controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control signals from switching nodes, minimizing high-di/dt and high-dv/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, keeping high-current traces short and wide, and placing filtering, compensation, and bypass components close to their associated pins.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint compares six machine-learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner—for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using synthetic clinical data. Predictors included demographics, obesity, genetic mutations, diabetes history, weight loss, abdominal pain, and jaundice. After preprocessing, the data were split 80% for training and 20% for testing without resampling.

All models produced similar accuracy (76.05%–76.35%) but had very low sensitivity because of class imbalance. Random Forest and Decision Tree detected no true positives. SVM had the highest sensitivity (1.90%), followed by Logistic Regression and Neural Network (1.47% each). SuperLearner achieved the highest precision (66.67%) but only 0.42% sensitivity. Overall, the results were considered insufficient for clinical diagnosis.

The study recommends resampling methods such as SMOTE and ADASYN, cost-sensitive learning, lower classification thresholds, feature engineering informed by PCA and clustering, ensemble methods, and explainability tools such as SHAP and LIME. Gene-expression analyses of metastasized cancer and normal colon tissues showed distinct clustering and separation and were proposed as potential feature sources. Future work should incorporate real-world clinical data, imaging and genomic information, longitudinal records, external validation, and collaboration between data scientists and clinicians.

An 11Alive study reported that the CDC cut over $700,000 from HIV prevention in 2016 while funding a failed project. Atlanta ranks among the nation’s highest-HIV areas, with prevention limited by expensive PrEP medication, inadequate healthcare access, stigma, and fear of disclosure or a positive diagnosis. Georgia laws criminalizing certain conduct by people with HIV may further discourage testing, often resulting in diagnoses at advanced stages. Georgia State launched a student testing campaign; Georgia ranks fifth nationally for new diagnoses, and two-thirds of residents living with HIV live in Atlanta. House Bill 65 would add HIV/AIDS to conditions eligible for medical marijuana.

RTX Neural Faces uses generative AI to infer a natural-looking face in real time from a rasterized face and 3D pose data. It is trained on thousands of offline-generated images varying angles, lighting, emotion, and occlusion, then optimized with TensorRT.

Salesforce announced it would invest more than $2.2 billion in its French business over five years, citing rapid growth and plans to expand staffing, real estate and data-center capacity during Macron’s state visit to Washington.

Churchill’s population of 900 has been shrinking since the rail line washed out in spring 2017, with 30 families leaving amid low employment and rising costs. School enrollment is down about 40 students from last June, potentially affecting teaching jobs, while no timeline exists for rail repairs.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017, reporting 7.72 billion common shares outstanding as of April 21, 2017. For the three months, revenue was $22.09 billion, up from $20.53 billion, as service and other revenue increased to $8.70 billion from $6.21 billion while product revenue declined to $13.39 billion from $14.32 billion. Gross margin was $14.03 billion, operating income was $5.59 billion, net income was $4.80 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $0.61, compared with $3.76 billion and $0.47 in the prior-year quarter. For the nine months, revenue was $66.63 billion, operating income was $16.996 billion, net income was $14.69 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $1.87.

At March 31, 2017, Microsoft reported $225.02 billion of assets, $155.29 billion of liabilities, and $69.73 billion of stockholders’ equity. Cash and short-term investments totaled $126.02 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $28.50 billion, investing used $39.41 billion, and financing provided $11.11 billion.

Third-quarter highlights included a commercial cloud annualized revenue run rate above $15.2 billion, 45% growth in Office 365 commercial revenue, 26.2 million Office 365 consumer subscribers, 81% growth in Dynamics 365 revenue, 93% growth in Azure revenue, 5% growth in Windows OEM revenue, and 4% growth in gaming revenue. Surface revenue declined 26%.

Microsoft completed its $27.0 billion LinkedIn acquisition on December 8, 2016, primarily for $26.4 billion in cash. The preliminary allocation included $16.69 billion of goodwill and $7.89 billion of intangible assets. LinkedIn contributed $975 million of quarterly revenue and a $386 million operating loss.

Microsoft planned to adopt the new lease and revenue recognition standards on July 1, 2017. It estimated that lease accounting would add approximately $5 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities and that fiscal 2016 revenue under the new revenue standard would have been approximately $6 billion higher, primarily from Windows 10 revenue recognition.

The filing also reported $14.4 billion of tax contingencies, $443 million of accrued legal liabilities, and approximately $1.5 billion of reasonably possible adverse legal outcomes beyond recorded amounts. Microsoft repurchased $1.6 billion of shares in the quarter, had $38.4 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization, and declared a $0.39 quarterly dividend. Deloitte & Touche reviewed the unaudited interim statements and reported no material modifications needed for compliance with U.S. GAAP.

Research by the Cinnamon Network found that more than 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers support NHS health and social care initiatives, filling gaps left by funding cuts and limited resources. Its study of 32 church-led projects addressing mental health, obesity and social isolation found them to be cost-effective; 2016 research valued the annual contribution of UK church and faith groups to communities at £3bn.

Parish nursing is a growing example. Retired and NHS-employed nurses work voluntarily or paid to support community patients through preventative care, monitoring and non-task-focused assistance. More than 100 parish nurses work with 85 UK churches, with another 100 planned within 18 months. Parish nurses complement rather than replace NHS staff as healthcare shifts into communities and demand increases.

Columbiana defeated Lisbon 49-47 with a late comeback. Alexis Cross tied the game with 23 seconds remaining, and Kayla Muslovski made a steal and layup 10 seconds later for the winning points. The Clippers moved to 5-0 overall and 3-0 in league play, while the Devils fell to 3-2 overall and 2-1 in league play. Cross and Muslovski each scored 14 points. Lisbon’s Izzy Perez led all scorers with 17 points, and Maddie Liberati added 12. Columbiana also won the junior varsity game 33-23, led by Annaliese Quibley’s 11 points.

An IDC white paper examines how industrial simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC) can support manufacturing innovation, productivity, competitiveness, and digital transformation amid geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy prices, material and labor shortages, supply-chain disruptions, and sustainability concerns. Findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers at discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Simulation, modeling, and analytics are increasingly used to accelerate product development, reduce costs, improve quality, avoid defects, and support decision-making. Three-quarters of respondents consider innovation the most important objective, while 57% view these technologies as important for improving product and service quality. Around half already use them in product development, production and process planning, and quality management; most plan broader deployment and investment within two years. However, fragmented data and departmental “silos” can produce inconsistent analyses. IDC identifies integrated data sources and a unified “single source of truth” as essential for efficient, cross-departmental value chains and collaboration with external partners and innovation ecosystems.

IT advances have expanded use cases through virtual prototyping, design optimization, digital verification, IoT-enabled feedback loops, and digital twins. More than half of respondents use virtual testing, 39% seek to simulate as many physical processes as possible, and 42% already use high-performance data analytics. Digital twins can monitor products and processes, test hypothetical scenarios, integrate ecosystem data, and support new services and business models such as Product-as-a-Service and Outcome-based Service.

Increasing calculation complexity and limited infrastructure have created trade-offs between speed and accuracy; 42% report that their simulations are already outdated or inaccurate, and half say calculations take too long. HPC is viewed by four out of five decision-makers as a game changer for product and process innovation because parallel systems enable complex calculations, faster iteration, higher-quality results, and new industrial applications. More than a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, another 39% are planning or piloting it, and only 15% are not yet engaging with HPC, citing investment costs, limited awareness of opportunities, and the topic’s relative newness.

Reddit has overtaken Facebook to become the third most visited website in the US, according to Alexa rankings reported by The Next Web. Google ranks first, followed by YouTube, Reddit, Facebook and Amazon. Users spend an average of 15 minutes 10 seconds daily on Reddit versus 10 minutes 50 seconds on Facebook, with 9.73 page views per visitor. The shift comes amid Facebook's Cambridge Analytica data scandal and its GDPR-related changes, including measures to make the platform safer. Statista data show nearly 1.69 billion users accessed Reddit in the most recent period, while Facebook had 2.19 billion monthly active users as of the first quarter of 2018. The US accounts for over 40 percent of Reddit's desktop traffic, followed by the UK and Canada.

The ICC Board may discuss a proposal to replace the 2021 Champions Trophy in India with a World T20 during its Kolkata meetings. BCCI treasurer Anirudh Chaudhry said the change would cost the board about $30 million and would likely be unacceptable without General Body approval. The proposal conflicts with the 2019–2023 FTP cycle, which awarded India the 2021 Champions Trophy and 2023 World Cup after an ICC meeting in Auckland. Chaudhry also criticised ICC chairman Shashank Manohar’s communication with the board.

Auckland had also agreed to nine-team Test and 13-team ODI leagues. The BCCI moved the 2019 IPL to March 29–May 19 to provide a 15-day break before the World Cup, following a Supreme Court directive. India’s first World Cup match is against South Africa on June 5, followed by Pakistan on June 16.

Suspected jihadists killed at least 18 people and wounded several in an overnight raid on a restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Security forces killed both attackers and rescued trapped diners; the communications minister called it a terrorist attack and said the death toll was provisional.

The paper introduces iMOOE, a physics-guided framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution forecasting of two-dimensional PDE dynamics without test-time adaptation. It defines two levels of PDE invariance: invariant spatial operators representing distinct physical processes and invariant compositional relationships linking those operators with parameters and forcing terms. The proposed mixture-of-operator-experts architecture uses parallel neural operator specialists, adaptive derivative masks, and a parameter-conditioned fusion network. Training combines prediction loss, cross-environment risk equality, frequency-enrichment, and mask-diversity losses to capture predictive, invariant, and high-frequency structure. Experiments on diffusion-reaction, Navier–Stokes, Burgers, shallow-water, heat-conduction, and real-world sea-surface-temperature dynamics report state-of-the-art zero-shot OOD results, with average OOD improvements of 40.21% in nMSE and 30.78% in fRMSE over the simulated benchmarks. Temporal extrapolation and compatibility studies show that iMOOE improves several neural operator backbones. A sensitivity study found three experts performed best. The authors note validation on limited dynamical-system diversity and propose future work on irregular grids and earth-system forecasting.

Severe storms threatened 29 million people across the Southeast Monday, with damaging hail, high winds and tornadoes possible. The Storm Prediction Center identified tornado threats across much of Alabama, Georgia and Tennessee and part of northeast Mississippi, especially in northern Alabama. Hail was reported near Ripley and along a 50-mile path from Holly Springs to Booneville, Mississippi; social media showed several inches of pea-sized hail. Northern Alabama schools closed early, and Birmingham offices closed at noon. Tennis-ball-size hail and 70 mph winds were possible.

Indian stocks opened the week upbeat but erased most gains by Friday: the Nifty fell 0.3%, while mid- and small-cap indexes gained about 1.5%. Sentiment was hurt by U.S. tariff threats, global rate-hike fears, political uncertainty, the RBI ending LoUs and LCs as trade-credit instruments, and the RBI–finance ministry dispute. The rupee strengthened to 64.93 per dollar from 65.16, while oil was nearly flat. TCS’s stake sale was criticized, some A320neo aircraft were ordered grounded, and Punjab National Bank found another 90 million rupees in fraud. Three major IPOs came to market, WPI inflation slowed as expected, industrial output rose 7.5%, and retail inflation eased to 4.44%.

Crude sulfate turpentine, also called sulfate wood turpentine, is a flammable, water-insoluble byproduct of the Kraft process. Distilled from tree resin, particularly pine, it contains terpene hydrocarbons and sulfur compounds. Its primary constituents are alpha-pinene and beta-pinene, with smaller amounts of limonene, camphene, carene, and terpinene.

It is mainly used in fragrances and flavors, including cosmetics and food and beverage products. It also serves as a solvent for thinning oil-based paints, in varnish production, and as a raw material for organic synthesis of aromatic chemicals.

Market growth is constrained by high distillation investment requirements and limited black-liquor retrieval through the Kraft process. Alpha-pinene is used as an anti-inflammatory agent and in a broad-spectrum antibiotic. Beta-pinene is primarily used in perfumery for its woody-green, pine-like scent, while carene contributes pine-like, sweet, woody, cedar, and pungent fragrances.

The lecture introduces interacting quantum gases, emphasizing how approximations reduce unsolvable Hamiltonians to tractable forms. For a homogeneous Bose-Einstein condensate, the Bogoliubov approximation replaces the zero-momentum condensate operator with a macroscopic number and diagonalizes the resulting bilinear Hamiltonian, describing noninteracting quasiparticles. Their dispersion is linear at low momentum and free-particle-like at high momentum. The dimensionless gas parameter \(Na^3\) controls interaction strength and quantum depletion; depletion is about 1% in dilute atomic condensates but about 90% in liquid helium.

Experiments can create sound waves with a blue-detuned repulsive laser and probe quasiparticle excitations through stimulated light scattering, a method called BEC spectroscopy. For trapped, inhomogeneous condensates, a position-space Bogoliubov treatment produces the nonlinear Gross–Pitaevskii equation, including a mean-field repulsion term proportional to density. Its solutions feature a healing length near boundaries and, in the Thomas–Fermi approximation, an inverted trapping-potential density profile. The equation quantitatively describes condensate expansion and shape changes. Rotating condensates form vortices rather than rotating rigidly; multiply charged vortices are unstable and split into repelling singly charged vortices that can form a hexagonal lattice.

The lecture then extends these ideas to optical lattices. In the tight-binding regime, atoms occupy localized Wannier states and are described by a Bose–Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor tunneling \(j\) and on-site interaction \(U\). When \(U\gg j\), tunneling and transport vanish, producing a Mott insulator with fixed occupation per site; when \(j\gg U\), the system behaves as a superfluid and condenses into the lowest quasimomentum state. A mean-field decoupling and perturbative treatment of tunneling in the insulating state yields an energy functional whose transition from a single-well to a double-well shape identifies the superfluid–Mott-insulator transition and produces phase diagrams with insulating lobes at integer fillings. Time-of-flight diffraction reveals superfluid coherence, while quantum gas microscopy directly resolves site occupation.

This medRxiv preprint presents a Learning Health System (LHS) protocol for evaluating Ambient AI, a generative AI tool for clinical documentation embedded in Epic at UW Health. The pragmatic trial Operations (PTOps) playbook combines shared governance, user experience, technical integration, documentation sustainment, and outcomes analytics. An alpha phase used iterative Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles to assess safety, usability, compliance, and clinical impact, while the beta phase uses a 24-week, multisite, individually randomized stepped-wedge trial to assess provider well-being using the Professional Fulfillment Index.

The alpha phase ran from June 24 to October 10, 2024, evaluating 20 providers across five specialties, 12 clinic locations, and 8,527 encounters. Provider interviews identified organizational characteristics, provider and patient readiness, documentation preferences, service setting, and clinical task needs as influences on adoption. Recommended adaptations included standardized workflows, tailored training, technical support, compliance reminders, and monitoring tools. Median weighted daily Ambient AI utilization was 65.4%, with a lower utilization control limit of 48%.

Manual review identified discrepancies between provider-entered diagnoses and supporting documentation. Diagnosis-code accuracy fell from 79% before Ambient AI implementation to 35% after an interim note-template change, then returned to pre-intervention levels after the diagnoses were moved to the attestation section. A two-week difference-in-differences analysis showed average changes of −6.84 percentage points in utilization, +0.33 hours in work outside work, and +0.43 hours in time spent on notes. A validated LLM-based coding-review tool achieved a mean Jaccard score of 0.54 and was used to flag notes for coder review.

The beta trial randomized 66 providers across eight specialties in Wisconsin and Illinois into three waves at six-week intervals. Operational staff coordinated recruitment, training, onboarding, and technical deployment, while governance committees monitored safety, deviations, resources, and implementation changes. A real-time dashboard tracked utilization, documentation efficiency, consent compliance, provider feedback, and performance drift, and was transferred to operational ownership after implementation. The report concludes that the LHS-based governance and evaluation framework provides a scalable model for integrating rigorous research with operational implementation of rapidly evolving GenAI tools.
Players should focus on the next shift, not the final result, and execute each period. Many have never won the Cup and may never get another chance.

A newlywed Northamptonshire couple walked home after police stopped their uninsured driver for speeding in a 30mph zone. PC Dave Lee said police had no discretion to let the vehicle continue, but the couple remained cheerful and took a selfie with him before walking the rest of the way.

Baumann appeals the district court's grant of summary judgment in her malpractice action against The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler. Pro se after her attorney withdrew, she alleged that Dr. Tayler breached the standard of care in prescribing her medications and that Kroger breached its standard of care, violated the Utah Pharmacy Practice Act, and failed to comply with its assumed duties and written assurances. Her 2007 complaint had been dismissed by stipulation; she refiled in February 2013 under Utah's one-year savings statute.

Under a stipulated discovery schedule, Baumann was to disclose expert witnesses by June 6, 2014, with expert discovery closing September 5, 2014. She made no disclosures and, on the day of the summary judgment hearing, filed an expert report addressing only Kroger without seeking leave of court. At the hearing, the court denied her husband's request to speak for her, continued the hearing, and refused to consider filings submitted after October 8, 2014. At the rescheduled hearing, still unrepresented, Baumann argued summary judgment was improper because Defendants' basis was procedural rather than evidentiary. The district court granted summary judgment, finding no good cause for the disclosure failure, precluding her from using any undisclosed witness, document, or material under Rule 26(d)(4), and concluding expert testimony was required because the applicable standards of care were not within laypersons' common knowledge.

The Court of Appeals affirmed. It declined to review Baumann's argument concerning an expert report for Dr. Tayler as unpreserved, and rejected her contention that Rule 16(d) rather than Rule 26(d)(4) governed, reasoning consistently with Sleepy Holdings LLC v. Mountain West Title that Rule 26 addresses disclosure failures, and relying on Bodell Construction Co. v. Robbins to characterize her late filing as a failure to disclose. The district court did not abuse its discretion.

The document details NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture, centered on the GA102 and GA104 GPUs. Fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N process, GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors in a 628.4 mm² die. A full GA102 configuration has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, 112 ROPs, and a 384-bit memory interface. GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3080, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40, while GA104 powers the GeForce RTX 3070.

Compared with Turing, Ampere provides up to 1.7 times the raster-graphics performance and twice the ray-tracing performance, while offering up to 1.9 times greater power efficiency at equivalent performance. Its SM design doubles FP32 throughput by allowing both datapaths in each processing partition to execute floating-point operations. Each GA10x SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, a 256 KB register file, and 128 KB of configurable L1 cache/shared memory. The unified cache system provides 64 KB for L1 and texture caching, 48 KB for shared memory, and 16 KB for graphics operations in graphics and asynchronous-compute configurations. Shared-memory bandwidth is twice that of Turing. GA10x also relocates ROPs into graphics processing clusters, increasing the full GA102’s ROP count from 96 in TU102 to 112.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and allow ray tracing to run concurrently with graphics or compute operations. They also add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for ray-traced motion blur involving moving or deforming geometry, enabling motion-blur rendering up to eight times faster than on Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32 and BF16 in addition to FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary precision. Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a 2-out-of-4 nonzero pattern to double Tensor Core throughput and reduce data footprint. The RTX 3080 delivers 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS, or 238 with sparsity, and 2.7 times the dense FP16 Tensor throughput of the RTX 2080 Super with sparsity enabled.

GA10x supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling. At speeds up to 19.5 Gbps, the RTX 3090 reaches 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth, more than 52 percent above TU102. Professional GA102 products use 48 GB of GDDR6. Third-generation NVLink provides four links totaling 112.5 GB/s between two GPUs and allows two A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs to combine 48 GB of memory into 96 GB. PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth and provides up to 64 GB/s over an x16 connection.

The GeForce RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming with 10,496 CUDA Cores, 24 GB of GDDR6X, and DLSS 8K mode. The RTX 3080 offers up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance, while the RTX 3070 rivals the previous RTX 2080 Ti; the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and does not support NVLink. The RTX A6000 targets professional workstations with 48 GB of GDDR6 and NVLink scaling. The data-center-oriented A40 offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput of the Quadro RTX 6000 and up to five times its AI-training throughput, or ten times with sparsity.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to move assets directly from SSDs to GPUs. NVIDIA states that it can improve I/O performance by up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs while reducing CPU utilization by as much as 20 times, enabling rapid game loading and reducing stutter and object pop-in.

GA10x supports DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 8K at 60 Hz and 4K at 120 Hz. Its fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x is described as the first GPU generation with hardware AV1 decoding, capable of playing 8K60 HDR content with about 4 percent CPU usage in the cited test. Its seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

GA10x GDDR6X memory also includes Error Detection and Replay. CRC checks detect transmission errors, after which failed memory transactions are retried until successful. The resulting reduction in useful bandwidth indicates when memory overclocking has reached its practical limit, although continued overclocking can still cause crashes.

The president returned the bill to the House because Section 5 would restrict national banks, after July 1, 1881, to depositing 3 percent U.S. bonds as collateral, preventing new banks and capital expansion, disadvantaging existing banks, and potentially destroying the national banking system. He supported prompt debt refinancing to reduce interest costs but argued that the banking restrictions were unnecessary and would harm commerce and national prosperity.

The paper presents DSCHECKER, an LLM-based method for detecting and repairing misuse of Python data-science APIs. It prompts models with code, relevant API directives, and dynamic information about processed variables, requiring a correctness judgment, unified-diff patch, and explanation. A function-calling variant, DSCHECKERagent, retrieves documentation and variable information on demand when the misused API is unknown.

Evaluation used DSMISUSES, derived from 49 reported misuses in NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, and seaborn. Eight unreproducible cases and three duplicates were removed, leaving 38 misuses; adding a corrected version of each produced 76 snippets. Three models—GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, and Llama 3.1 405B—were tested with varying prompt information.

Providing both directives and data information produced the best overall results for GPT-4o and Llama. Llama achieved the highest detection F1-score, 61.18%, and fix rate, 51.28%. Directives significantly improved detection for GPT-4o and Llama, while combined context particularly improved detection of data-dependent misuses. Added context sometimes reduced GPT-4o-mini’s performance. Few-shot prompting produced mixed results: it significantly improved GPT-4o’s detection and fixing but slightly reduced Llama’s detection and did not significantly change its fixing performance.

On 15 reproduced deep-learning misuses, DSCHECKER achieved a 48% detection F1-score and 26.67% fix rate; detection reached 66.67% for cases with explicit directives. It also detected and fixed a misuse missed by LLMAPIDET. On DSMISUSES, DSCHECKER detected substantially more misuses than LLMAPIDET, whose generated rules failed to transfer to non-deep-learning APIs and whose fixes were unsuccessful.

DSCHECKERagent achieved a 48.65% detection F1-score and 39.47% fix rate with GPT-4o. Although weaker than the context-supplied version, it demonstrated potential for practical settings where relevant API and data information is not preidentified. The study concludes that directives and dynamic variable information improve LLM-based misuse detection and repair, while highlighting the need for more effective agent information retrieval and machine-readable documentation.

The speaker says his team lost despite taking three good shots and needs crisper play, better positioning, and fewer mistakes. He expects an energetic crowd and stresses that scoring first is crucial, noting that his team recently overcame a deficit to win in overtime. He plans to keep playing his own game and be ready defensively. He also describes sharing a hotel bed with his young son and sleeping in. Calling Dominik one of the NHL’s best goalies, he says one of the two European finalists could become the first European goalie to win the Cup.

Researchers at King’s College London analyzed 2,066 millennial twins in England and Wales, assessing their relationships, loneliness, and health. At age 18, 7% often felt lonely, while 23–31% felt excluded or lacked companionship. Loneliness was associated with twice the risk of depression and anxiety, a 38% increased risk of unemployment, and more smoking and inactivity.

Loneliness is greatest among teenagers and young adults. Social media’s role varies: keeping contact may help, while aimless scrolling and jealousy may increase FOMO and loneliness. Loneliness can also be socially contagious, as lonely people may withdraw and cause close connections to feel lonely. Researchers suggest early intervention for lonely young adults, while Mind notes that loneliness is strongly connected to poor mental health and that social connection can support well-being.

Since 1988, Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science (HMNS) have partnered on space-science outreach through teacher research programs, university courses, planetarium projects, educational technology, and public events. Their Heliophysics “Big Year” outreach used NASA-supported eclipse animations, a “Totality” fulldome planetarium show, teacher workshops, classroom activities, safety resources, websites, media, and public observing events. The animations, including three added in 2021, were freely distributed to educators and planetariums; 186 educators in 33 countries and 33 U.S. states requested them, and their YouTube versions received more than 19,000 views. “Totality” was distributed to 147 planetariums, with a Texas version sent to 53 schools and planetariums, contributing to a reported impact exceeding 180,000 viewers.

Rice and HMNS also supported Citizen CATE 2024, a community-led project using 35 uniform observing sites to capture continuous, polarized coronal imagery during the April 8, 2024 total solar eclipse. More than 250 participants took part, including students, educators, citizens, and amateur astronomers; over 80% of teams obtained at least some totality observations, and analysis was ongoing.

The project documented more than 250,000 leveraged views, distributed nearly one million eclipse viewers, confirmed 5,405 teacher users, and achieved a total estimated reach of more than 1.5 million people. Teachers reported sharing the materials with an average of about 500 students each. The organizations also used MMS-supported space-weather forecasts to issue alerts, including during major geomagnetic storms that produced visible auroras.

Sean McVay said Todd Gurley and other starters will receive “progressive work” through the Rams’ third preseason game against the Chargers, aiming to have Gurley ready for the Sept. 10 opener against Indianapolis. Gurley had four carries for two yards and a 10-yard reception in the Rams’ 13-10 win over Dallas, matching his 2016 preseason workload. McVay said coaches will monitor his reps to balance preparation and injury risk.

Camera-trap footage from a Malaysian durian orchard shows that island flying foxes feed on nectar without damaging flowers and positively affect durian reproduction. Published in Ecology and Evolution, the study challenges the belief that flying foxes harm durian and provides evidence that they are important pollinators of this valuable Southeast Asian crop. The findings highlight bats’ ecosystem services amid declining pollinator populations. Island flying foxes are threatened by hunting and habitat loss and are endangered in Malaysia.

A compilation of March 2001 reports details California’s electricity crisis and proposed responses. Gov. Gray Davis sought federal support for acquiring utility transmission lines and using state bonds to assist financially distressed utilities. A tentative agreement would sell Southern California Edison’s grid to the state for about $2.7–$2.8 billion, while negotiations continued with PG&E and San Diego Gas & Electric. FERC approval was likely required; its chairman opposed the proposal, while Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham was described as open to reviewing it. Davis cited a 1946 Nebraska case as possible precedent for avoiding federal approval.

The state’s utilities faced roughly $13 billion in debt, frozen retail rates and unpaid power bills, raising bankruptcy concerns. PG&E announced it would pay creditors about $228 million of approximately $1.4 billion owed, prompting objections from smaller suppliers. PG&E also faced lawsuits alleging nearly $3 billion in financial mismanagement and default on more than $730 million in short-term payments.

The California Independent System Operator projected substantial summer shortages, including 6,815 megawatts in June, even after accounting for new plants and Davis’s conservation goal. Davis said the state was on the “back side” of the crisis, but industry experts and the ISO expected severe shortages if demand rose with summer temperatures.

Cal-ISO reported that wholesale suppliers appeared to have charged $562 million above reasonable prices in December and January, and asked FERC to investigate possible refunds. Generators denied overcharging and cited legitimate operating and credit risks. FERC had imposed a $150-per-megawatt-hour soft price cap, while former federal regulator Elizabeth Moler urged temporary federal price controls. Davis, Sen. Dianne Feinstein and consumer advocates also favored caps, but FERC chairman Curtis Hebert opposed them.

Public Utilities Commission President Loretta Lynch defended the agency’s crisis response while acknowledging that deregulation had failed. The PUC was reviewing residential electricity baselines, a temporary 9% rate increase for Edison customers and larger increases for business customers.

The state pursued long-term supply contracts as an alternative to emergency purchases. Calpine signed two contracts worth up to $8.3 billion for 1,500 megawatts over 10–20 years, following a separate $4.6 billion contract, while Mirant shifted contracts for about 1,000 megawatts to the state.

Lawmakers and consumer advocates urged generators to forgive utility debts, arguing that unsecured creditors could recover more through a bailout than bankruptcy. Most suppliers rejected forgiveness; Enron executive Steven Kean said there was “no reason” to forgive debts, and Reliant called the issue nonnegotiable, although Davis’s office reported unsolicited offers from some generators. Critics also warned that state ownership of transmission lines and power plants could displace private investment, introduce political control and produce higher long-term costs.

A European study of 2,480 men aged 42–60 found that, after 22 years, the highest blood linoleic acid levels were associated with a 43% lower risk of premature death from all causes than the lowest levels. Higher levels were also linked to lower cardiovascular-death risk, but not cancer-death risk. Vegetable oils, plant-based spreads, nuts and seeds raise linoleic acid levels.

This final videotaped lecture of MIT course 18.086 begins by returning to the previous lecture's least-squares example: projecting b onto the subspace spanned by Ax and onto the perpendicular direction w. The lecturer restates weak duality (the two squared distances sum to at least |b|²), identifies the missing term that measures the loss away from the optimum, and notes that its vanishing (b = Ax + w) characterizes optimality. He connects the primal and dual problems through the condition Aᵀw = 0, derived by expanding (b − Ax)ᵀ(b − Ax), and poses as an open problem for students the geometric identity a² + c² = b² + d² for a point joined to the four corners of a rectangle, provable algebraically but also expected to follow from Pythagoras. He briefly notes that the stationarity condition c = α/x in the barrier problem leads to Newton's method, then turns to inverse problems.

Examples given include finding velocities from positions (differentiation amplifies small high-frequency noise, making the problem ill posed); finding earth density from seismic travel times via back projection, as in oil exploration; CT, MRI and PET; finding earth's density from gravitational measurements; recovering an obstacle's shape from scattering data (radar); the inverse of a Laplace or Poisson equation (find the coefficient c given u and f); and recovering the matrix A from b and x. Many such problems are first-kind integral equations (Volterra, Fredholm), which are ill posed; adding αI to A, giving a second-kind equation, improves the conditioning.

The main remedy discussed is Tikhonov regularization: minimize ‖Ax − b‖² + α‖x‖², yielding (AᵀA + αI)u = b. With noise δ in b, the error is of size δ/√α, so α must be balanced; α = δ^(2/3) gives error δ^(2/3) as noise decreases. Iterative methods such as conjugate gradients must be stopped before yielding unrealistic solutions, and refining discretizations of integral equations makes them more ill posed. A final application: genomics, estimating the importance of individual genes (eye color, sex) from gene expression, i.e., estimating derivatives in high dimension from few samples, again ill posed and requiring regularization. The lecturer closes by noting presentations begin Monday, soliciting volunteers, and leaving the rectangle-corner geometry problem for the weekend.

Opioid misuse is a worldwide epidemic; the mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is targeted by fentanyl, heroin, methadone and buprenorphine, and MOR agonists risk respiratory depression. Naloxone is a short-acting antagonist used to reverse opioids and combined with buprenorphine for OUD. MORs occur in the CNS, peripheral organs and immune system, yet [11C]carfentanil ([11C]CFN) PET studies have largely been restricted to brain. Reported sex differences include MOR availability rising with age in neocortical areas and putamen, higher availability in women, and lower availability in postmenopausal women than men in thalamus and amygdala. Long axial field-of-view instruments (PennPET Explorer) now allow whole-body imaging; the authors present the first human whole-body [11C]CFN neuroreceptor PET study, evaluating extra-CNS reference regions (aorta, muscle).

Methods: IRB-approved and registered (NCT05528848); healthy English-speaking adults aged 18–45 consented, were screened with the MINI, and underwent urine drug testing; T1-weighted 3-T MRI was acquired. [11C]CFN was synthesized from [11C]CO2 via [11C]CH4 and [11C]CH3I into desmethylcarfentanil, purified, and checked by HPLC. Scans used low-dose CT and a 90-min dynamic acquisition (168.5±58.6 MBq) reconstructed with TOF OSEM. PMOD analysis included MNI normalization, five bilateral VOIs (amygdala, caudate, putamen, thalamus, ventral tegmentum), Logan DVR with visual cortex as reference (k2′=0.1237 min−1), and percent receptor occupancy for naloxone pretreatment.

Mitch Larkin won the 400m individual medley at the Queensland titles in 4:20.45 and is considering adding it to his program for February’s Commonwealth Games trials. The dual backstroke world champion wants more race opportunities but prioritizes returning his backstroke to world-class form. After winning 100m and 200m backstroke titles at the 2015 world championships, he won Rio silver in the 200m and missed the 100m podium. Following a difficult year and coaching changes, Larkin says his desire for Olympic redemption has returned.

The Aug. 21 total solar eclipse will cross the contiguous United States from Oregon to South Carolina, the first coast-to-coast total eclipse in 99 years. Its path of totality spans 8,600 miles through 14 states, with darkness lasting up to 2 minutes 44 seconds in Illinois. The lunar shadow, 60 to 70 miles wide, will sweep across the country for about 1½ hours.

NASA will provide TV and internet coverage while balloons, satellites, telescopes, aircraft, ships and International Space Station cameras observe the event. Researchers will study the corona, temperature changes and reactions among animals and plants. Festivals, sports events, parties and other celebrations are planned throughout the path, where large crowds are expected. Eye protection is required before and after totality.

A partial eclipse will be visible across much of Canada, Central America and northern South America. The passage also previews the April 8, 2024 total eclipse, which will cross Mexico, Texas, the Midwest, Maine and New Brunswick, Canada, producing up to four minutes of darkness.
Ventura police will review procedures after a homeless man fatally stabbed a patron; the chief says officers should have responded to reports in person. Jackson is charged with murder.

Canon’s EOS M6 replaces the M3 as an entry-level mirrorless camera, with an optional viewfinder, revised controls, popup flash, and a tilting 3.2-inch touchscreen. It was due in April 2017, starting at $780. The passage says cheaper Sony A5100 and A6000 models offer similar specifications, a built-in viewfinder, and more compact power-zoom lens options.

For sets \(A,B\) in an arbitrary Abelian group, additive energy \(E(A,B)\) counts quadruples satisfying \(a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2\), and it equals the sum of squared representation counts. Small doubling implies large energy: if \(|A+A|\le k|A|\), then \(E(A)\ge |A|^3/k\). The converse fails, since a highly structured subset combined with unstructured elements can yield cubic energy and a quadratic-sized sumset.

The Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers theorem states that large energy forces a substantial subset with small doubling, up to polynomial losses. A stronger two-set version produces substantial subsets \(A'\subset A\) and \(B'\subset B\) with controlled sumset; the Ruzsa triangle inequality and Plunnecke–Ruzsa lemma connect it to the one-set version.

The proof uses a bipartite graph analogue involving restricted sumsets across graph edges. Popular sums contribute most of the energy, yielding a dense graph suitable for the graphical theorem. Dependent random choice establishes a path-of-length-2 lemma, which is strengthened to a path-of-length-3 lemma finding large subsets with many length-3 paths between every pair. These paths bound the complete sumset \(A'+B'\) by the cube of the restricted sumset, completing the proof.

This IDC white paper examines how manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland use simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC) to improve innovation, quality, cost, speed, agility, and sustainability amid geopolitical, energy, material, supply-chain, labor, and sustainability pressures. It reports a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers from discrete and process manufacturers with more than 500 employees.

Simulation, modeling, and analytics are linked primarily to innovation, considered important by three-quarters of respondents, and product and service quality, cited by 57%. Around half already use them in product development, production and process planning, or quality management, with deployment expected to reach as high as 90% within two years; 64% plan relevant investments. Persistent data silos and inconsistent departmental data require integrated sources and a “single source of truth,” while external data sharing and cross-industry collaboration create potential for new products, services, and business models. Current uses include virtual prototyping, design optimization, digital verification and validation, AI/ML analytics, IoT-enabled feedback loops, and digital twins.

The paper presents HPC as a major enabler of complex, faster, and more accurate calculations and of new product and process innovation. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise from 8% reporting high demand to almost half within two years; half say calculations take too long, and 42% report that some simulations are outdated or inaccurate. While 81% view HPC as a game changer, adoption faces security, energy and sustainability, expertise, cost, performance, availability, scalability, and infrastructure-complexity concerns. Enterprises favor external cloud or colocation infrastructure, and public and hybrid cloud architectures are expected to become more important because of their scalability and flexibility compared with customized on-premises systems.

Deion Sanders underwent a medical procedure Tuesday for recurring blood clots and hopes to return to practice the next day and coach against Iowa State on Saturday. Sanders, who experienced pain and limping during the Buffaloes’ 35-21 loss at TCU, said the condition is hereditary. He previously underwent procedures to remove blood clots, including amputation of two left-foot toes in 2021, and received treatment for aggressive bladder cancer that required reconstructing part of his intestine to function as a bladder.
