Douglas Haig, an Arizona man, was charged with conspiring to manufacture and sell unlicensed armor-piercing ammunition, allegedly sold to Stephen Paddock, who killed 58 concertgoers and wounded hundreds at the 2017 Las Vegas country music festival before taking his own life. Haig was released on bail. Investigators found Haig’s fingerprints on reloaded cartridges and tool marks matching his equipment on ammunition recovered from Paddock’s hotel rooms.

Rockefeller University researchers kept a sliver of gerbil cochlea alive and functional outside the body for the first time using a chamber that maintained native fluids, temperature, and voltage. By playing sounds and observing the tissue at the subcellular level, they captured how cochlear hair bundles and outer hair cells amplify vibrations. The experiments directly confirmed that mammalian hearing relies on a Hopf bifurcation, a mechanical tipping point that enables signal amplification, supporting its role across the animal kingdom. Researchers said the system could allow targeted testing of how hearing works and fails, potentially aiding development of treatments for sensorineural hearing loss.

This reissue of U.S. Patent No. 10,607,995 pertains to memory arrays and derives from U.S. patent application Ser. No. 15/973,697 and Provisional Patent Application Ser. No. 62/502,999, “Memory Arrays,” naming Martin C. Roberts, Sanh D. Tang, and Fred D. Fishburn as inventors.

Described embodiments form a memory array above a base substrate using vertically alternating tiers of insulative material and memory cells. Each memory cell includes a transistor and capacitor. The transistor has first and second source/drain regions, a channel region, and a gate positioned near the channel. At least part of the channel is horizontally oriented to permit current flow between the source/drain regions. The capacitor has first and second electrodes separated by a capacitor insulator, with its first electrode electrically coupled to the first source/drain region. Insulator and gate materials may include silicon dioxide, silicon nitride, high-k materials, or ferroelectric material.

Vertically extending capacitor-electrode structures couple second capacitor electrodes across memory-cell tiers, while vertically extending sense-line structures couple second source/drain regions across tiers. Access lines interconnect transistor gates along rows or columns. Staircase regions containing staggered contact openings and conductive vias provide connections to gates in individual tiers.

Alternative embodiments include vertically stacked memory cells within a single tier, segmented channel regions, single-gate transistors with single-sided capacitors, and independently accessed gates. Another variation electrically connects source/drain regions of vertically stacked transistors along the sense-line structure.

A fabrication method deposits and selectively etches alternating semiconductor, conductive, and insulating layers to form openings, channel regions, capacitor structures, access lines, sense-line structures, and conductive vias. Example materials include doped polysilicon, silicon nitride, silicon dioxide, titanium nitride, and tungsten, with TMAH, dilute HF, hot phosphoric acid, and sulfuric-acid/hydrogen-peroxide solutions used for selected etching steps.

NVIDIA Ampere adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 Tensor Core formats. FP16 and BF16 enable mixed-precision training matching FP32 results and provide 16× greater math throughput; TF32 enables default tensor-core acceleration while preserving FP32 range and producing FP32 output.

President Biden praised union workers in Pittsburgh, emphasized his support for unions and the middle class, and said he had returned to outline a plan to “rebuild the backbone of America.” He cited 547,296 American deaths from COVID-19, widespread job losses, and increased inequality, while crediting the American Rescue Plan with saving jobs, businesses, and lives. He said the administration was approaching 200 million vaccine doses in its first 100 days and that economists were forecasting 6 percent economic growth.

Biden introduced the American Jobs Plan as the first of two proposed plans, with the American Families Plan to follow. He described it as the largest American jobs investment since World War II, intended to create millions of good-paying jobs and strengthen the economy. Its provisions include modernizing 20,000 miles of highways, roads, and main streets; replacing 10 economically significant bridges; repairing 10,000 other bridges; building rail and transit lines; and improving ports and airports.

The plan would also support climate resilience and clean energy through infrastructure upgrades, 500,000 charging stations, and American-made electric and hydrogen vehicles. It would replace all lead pipes and service lines, expand affordable high-speed internet access, modernize the electric grid, cap orphaned oil and gas wells, weatherize housing and commercial buildings, and extend affordable community-based care for seniors and people with disabilities. Biden also proposed the largest increase in federal non-defense research and development spending on record, focusing on areas including battery technology, biotechnology, computer chips, and clean energy.

Biden said the proposal would protect organizing and collective bargaining rights and direct investment toward marginalized, rural, and historically underserved communities. He estimated it would create more than 18 million jobs over four years and required roughly $2 trillion in investment spread largely over eight years. He argued that delaying would worsen debt, infrastructure deficiencies, and international competitiveness, particularly with China.

To finance the proposal, Biden said no one earning under $400,000 would face a federal tax increase. He proposed raising the corporate tax rate from 21 percent to as much as 28 percent, establishing a 21 percent global minimum tax for U.S. corporations, ending deductions for offshoring jobs and assets, and increasing IRS enforcement. He also proposed tax credits for companies that locate manufacturing in the United States. He said he would consider alternative funding ideas if they met his income threshold.

Concluding, Biden cited Abraham Lincoln and Dwight Eisenhower as examples of bipartisan infrastructure leadership and called for cooperation among Republicans, businesses, and the public. He framed the investment as a choice between democratic capacity and autocratic competition and said the country needed to act together.
XPIC’s delayed IRR clearing causes AEOI to send two interrupts instead of one. AEOI is master-PIC-only and unsuitable where nested interrupts are required.

The passage describes automated storage, retrieval, and processing systems in which conveyance systems deliver storage and destination bins to a processing station, where robotic devices grasp objects and distribute them according to a manifest. Perception data supports grasp selection by evaluating obstruction, center of mass, surface shape, fiducials, and approach direction, while machine learning can identify good and bad grasp locations. Embodiments include separate, shared, multiple, and multi-floor bin areas controlled by computer systems that track bin locations and direct all movements.

The speaker credits his team’s persistence after generating traffic, pucks toward the net and rebound opportunities but failing to find a third goal. Although the team was unsettled early, it quickly settled in and showed energy, speed, puck possession, territorial control and strong scoring chances. He notes that an elimination game against another strong team requires their best effort, while praising the team’s efforts to prevent clean opportunities from below the goal line, where the opponent uses its size and skill.

He identifies Burns as an important offensive presence who generates chances from the blue line and rushes the puck. The team plans to account for him and choose advantageous matchups, particularly defensive pairings, without being overly concerned about the opponent’s lineup choices.

The speaker trusts the team’s leadership to channel emotion and energy properly. He describes Sid as a consistent threat, Sergei as invaluable to the defense because of his experience, insights and relationships with players, and Geno as an elite player whose improving two-way play and recent goal and setup make the team more difficult to oppose. Matt’s on-ice performance, experience, composure and positive influence on the locker room are also praised, with the speaker viewing him as an extension of the coaching staff.

Rejecting superstition, the speaker emphasizes trusted routines, controlled thoughts, discipline and staying in the moment. He says the players have maintained that focus throughout the postseason and will continue doing so until the series ends.

PINCMx registers map digital I/Os, and PF bits configure pin functions. IOMUX allows one digital function per pin; non-IOMUX signals can coexist without contention, with PF/PC recommended at zero and designers verifying no contention.

Bear markets have no official definition but are commonly associated with declines of at least 20%. They are longer and steeper than corrections and feature high volatility, sharp selloffs and rallies. Markets spend roughly 80% of their time in bull markets and 20% in bear markets, which tend to be shorter than bull markets but take much longer to recover. Bear markets may help remove economic excesses and encourage innovation, although fiscal stimulus and monetary intervention may not prevent future recessions and asset-price declines.

During the 2000–2003 bear market, the dividend-adjusted S&P 500 fell 45%, bottoming on March 12, 2003, and did not regain its late-2000 high until late 2006. The Nasdaq peaked in March 2000, fell more than 80%, bottomed in October 2002, and took 15 years to fully recover.

Long-term investors can benefit from buying stocks at lower prices and adding to positions as risk premiums and expected future returns rise. Traders benefit from increased volatility, which creates opportunities for both long and short strategies. A QQQ mean-reversion strategy using RSI and another indicator produced average gains above 2% and win rates of 68% during 2000–2002 and 73% during 2007–2009. Traders generally need not change automated strategies, while investors should remain cautious if they are near retirement or need to withdraw funds.

The President reported that 653 troops, excluding marines at the navy-yard, were deployed in Washington as a posse comitatus under civil authority to maintain peace and order around the President-elect’s inauguration. A House committee found no proof of a secret organization threatening the capital or government operations, but the House overwhelmingly favored removing the troops. The President said he retained them because revolutionary unrest, rumors, and fears warranted protecting public property, archives, the city, and the inauguration. He added that alarm quickly subsided after the first company arrived, restoring relative peace and security.

Louisiana’s Supreme Court declined to consider Rhodes’s untimely writ and ruled that he had exhausted state post-conviction relief absent a statutory exception for successive applications; the district court was ordered to enter a minute entry.

The study examines how uniform strain and nonuniform strain gradients affect thermal transport in β-Ga₂O₃, a wide-bandgap semiconductor with low thermal conductivity and applications in high-power electronics, UV photodetectors, and flexible devices. A first-principles-trained neuroevolution potential combined with the Boltzmann transport equation and a strain-gradient model was used to analyze bulk material, 10- and 100-nm films, and nanowires at 300 K. The trained potential reproduced DFT energies, forces, virials, phonon dispersions, and known thermal conductivities accurately.

Uniform uniaxial and biaxial strain substantially and anisotropically modified thermal conductivity, with b-axis-related strains producing the largest changes. Heat capacity and phonon velocity remained comparatively stable, while intrinsic phonon lifetime tracked conductivity changes closely, indicating that uniform strain primarily alters three-phonon scattering rates.

Strain gradients monotonically suppressed conductivity and were more effective than equivalent uniform strains in thin films. At a uniaxial gradient of 0.6%/nm, a 10-nm film experienced conductivity reductions of 31.8%, 35.3%, and 36.6% along the a, b, and c axes, compared with 16.1%, 27.0%, and 23.4% under 3% uniform b-axis strain. A biaxial gradient of 0.6%/nm reduced the three components by 42.4%, 43.3%, and 41.6%, approximately 1.5 times the suppression from the corresponding uniform biaxial strain. Ten-nanometer nanowires showed reductions of up to 30.5%.

The enhanced suppression was attributed to symmetry breaking, phonon spectral broadening, altered mode-frequency gaps, and activation of previously forbidden scattering channels, which expanded the phonon-scattering phase space. Gradient-induced scattering dominated across the heat-carrying 0–10 THz range. Unlike uniform strain, which strongly altered thermal anisotropy ratios, strain gradients strongly reduced conductivity while leaving anisotropy comparatively stable. The findings identify strain gradients as essential considerations for accurate β-Ga₂O₃ thermal modeling and for thermal management in flexible and nanostructured devices.

Investors assess startup opportunities through potential returns, the founder’s presentation and team, market opportunities, and strategy. Founders should consider equity flexibility and investor mentorship, communicate confidently while accepting feedback, and demonstrate an experienced, proactive team. Market traction can be shown through revenue, customer satisfaction, or identifiable gaps for innovation, supported by practical solutions to challenges. A coherent business plan should include evidence-based projections, analysis of competition and threats, and awareness of financial consequences if forecasts are missed.

UCLA researchers found that increasing lactate production activates normally inactive hair follicle stem cells and accelerates hair growth in mice, while blocking lactate prevents activation. Two skin-applied drugs—RCGD423 and UK5099—promoted lactate production through different mechanisms and increased hair growth in mice. The findings may support future treatments for baldness or alopecia, but the experimental drugs have not been tested in humans or approved by the FDA.

Colgate-Palmolive’s recent decline has paused, with improving revenue and profit growth prompting analysts to become more bullish. Argus set a $72 price target, implying about 12% upside, while the stock’s forward P/E ratio fell below 20. Analysts expect revenue growth over the next two fiscal years and mid- to high-single-digit profit growth over three years. Colgate is also a dividend aristocrat, raising its dividend annually since 1964 and yielding about 2.6%.

Despite these improvements, the author considers Colgate’s valuation excessive. Its products are easily copied, and e-commerce has weakened large manufacturers’ control of shelf space by enabling smaller and niche competitors to attract customers. Although Colgate retains a loyal customer base and stable dividend, the author believes 20 times earnings is too high for a business lacking a durable competitive moat.

Jean-Claude Juncker said India’s 5.7% GDP growth was better than Europe’s 2% and was not considered a slowdown outside India. World Bank President Jim Yong Kim attributed the decline to temporary GST-related disruption.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 support ARM Serial Wire Debug through DEBUGSS, including SWDIO/SWCLK pullup and pulldown resistors, optional use of SWD pins as GPIO, configurable peripheral behavior during debug, PMCU reset and mode-change requests, a DSSM mailbox for communication with boot ROM and application software, and security features such as SWD lockout and password-authenticated debugging.

A memory-mapped, read-only FACTORY region stores device capability information and factory trim data. DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004, with PARTNUM in bits 12–27 and MANUFACTURER in bits 1–11. USERID is at 0x41C4.0008, with PART in bits 0–15 and VARIANT in bits 16–23. Revision and identification information also appears in package markings.

The recommended application circuit uses 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS. The NRST pin requires a 47 kΩ pullup and 1000 pF pulldown; external crystals require bypass capacitors; and 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O pins require pullup resistors, including when used for I²C or UART.

TI provides development tools including SysConfig, the TI Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, and the TI Arm-Clang compiler. Device prefixes identify lifecycle stage: “X” denotes experimental devices for internal evaluation, while “MSP” denotes fully qualified production devices.

Mechanical drawings provide package, stencil, solder-coverage, and orderable-part information. Thermal pads must be soldered to the PCB for thermal and mechanical performance, and actual packages may differ from generic representations. Officials raised the AJC Peachtree Road Race alert to Code Red–Dangerous, advising runners to slow down, follow course changes and official instructions, and consider stopping if necessary. Forecasters predicted a dry Fourth of July morning with temperatures in the upper 80s. The shallow cross concept combines a basic route and shallow drag route in opposite directions to stress linebackers, attack the middle, and create triangle or secondary-read opportunities. It can quickly release the ball against blitzes or find voids over the middle against zone coverage. The concept is effective against man coverage, Tampa 2, and Cover 4, but Cover 3’s numbers advantage makes it less effective for big gains.

The tight end runs the basic route to a 10–12-yard landmark, while the slot receiver runs a shallow drag at 3–4 yards. Both stay on the move against man coverage and settle in zone voids against zone coverage. The quarterback reads downfield routes first, then transitions to the post, drag, basic route, and running-back checkdown progression. Against immediate pressure, the quarterback quickly targets the drag-basic combination.

Two variations are highlighted: a bunch-X shallow cross with a high-to-low post-out progression against two-high defenses, and an empty formation using a post-wheel combination before returning to the drag-basic read.

The lecture reviews digital communication as a system with a binary interface between source and channel coding, even when sources and channels are analog. Standardization reduces the number of coder and decoder implementations, lowers chip costs, and simplifies conceptual organization; Shannon’s result indicates that a binary interface need not sacrifice performance.

Source coding is divided into three stages. Waveforms, images, or videos are sampled or expanded into sequences of real or complex numbers. A quantizer converts these continuous values into a finite alphabet, necessarily introducing distortion. A discrete coder then maps the symbol sequence to bits for transmission over a reliable, error-free binary channel. The course focuses primarily on waveform sources such as voice and music.

Discrete source coding maps symbols to binary strings so that the original sequence can be recovered uniquely. For an alphabet of size \(m\), a fixed-length code requires \(l=\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\) bits per symbol; only the number of possible symbols matters, not their meanings. Grouping \(n\) symbols creates \(m^n\) possible blocks and requires \(\lceil\log_2(m^n)\rceil\) bits per block, yielding a rate approaching \(\log_2 m\) bits per source symbol as block length increases.

Variable-length coding can assign shorter words to common symbols and longer words to uncommon ones. Its concatenated output has no delimiters, so buffering may be needed when symbol and bit rates differ. Distinct codewords alone are insufficient for decoding: for example, assigning \(a=0\), \(b=1\), and \(c=10\) makes the sequence \(ba\) indistinguishable from \(c\). Unique decodability requires different source strings to produce different concatenated bit strings.

A prefix-free code has no codeword that is a prefix of another. Such codes are uniquely and instantaneously decodable and can be represented by binary trees. Kraft’s inequality states that codeword lengths \(l_i\) can form a prefix-free code exactly when \(\sum_i 2^{-l_i}\leq 1\). The inequality follows by associating each codeword with a binary-expansion interval of size \(2^{-l_i}\); prefix-free intervals must be disjoint. Equality corresponds to a full code with no unused leaves. All uniquely decodable codes also satisfy the inequality, although some uniquely decodable codes are not prefix-free.

The lecture then introduces discrete memoryless sources: sequences drawn independently from a finite alphabet according to a common probability distribution. This simplified framework provides a foundation for later work on optimal code lengths, entropy, block coding, and more complex sources with dependencies.

The lecture introduces the economics of green buildings through the “triple bottom line” of environmental performance, social well-being, and profit. Because private-sector actors supply more than 80% of urban building stock, sustainability initiatives must offer a viable business case rather than rely solely on social or environmental goals. The lecture’s market model links tenants, owners, and developers: tenant demand and willingness to pay can increase owner revenues and property values, which can then support developers’ construction and sales decisions.

Millennium Partners illustrates how developers rationally adapt their positioning to market conditions. Its San Francisco Millennium Tower focused on luxury condominium sales, but foundation and structural problems later caused the building to tilt and sink, resulting in lawsuits. Millennium Place in Boston was presented to city officials as supporting job creation and downtown revitalization, which helped secure approval. The Boston Millennium Tower was pitched both as a solution to an abandoned downtown site and as offering residents exclusive wellness amenities. Winthrop Center, by contrast, prominently marketed sustainability through Passive House design and LEED certifications to environmentally conscious, affluent buyers. The cases suggest that sustainability has not always been the developer’s first priority. Students are encouraged to question corporate sustainability narratives and ask how social and business value are aligned and which takes priority when they conflict.

Green buildings may benefit tenants through lower energy and operating costs, improved health and indoor environmental quality, greater productivity, fewer sick days, improved recruitment and retention, and greater comfort and safety. Tenants may therefore have a higher willingness to pay higher rents. Benefits to owners can include higher rents, occupancy and market value; lower vacancy, operating and maintenance costs; potentially lower capital expenditures and depreciation; and lower risk. Relevant risks include policy and regulatory changes, difficulty selling an undesirable property, and physical risks such as flooding. For developers, green buildings may command higher sale prices and sell faster, but passive design, advanced HVAC, insulation, lighting, and other technologies can increase construction or retrofit costs.

These effects are evaluated dynamically over a property’s holding period using discounted cash flow and NPV. Green-building changes can increase potential rental income, reduce vacancy and operating expenses, improve resale value, and potentially lower the discount rate, producing a higher NPV and purchase price. Tenant operating savings do not automatically accrue to owners because lease structures determine who pays which costs; instead, tenant savings may be reflected in higher willingness to pay and rent. Empirical findings cited in the lecture indicate an average green-building rent premium of roughly 6%, with substantial variation: rental premiums range from 0% to 23%, operational-cost effects from negative 14% to positive 25%, and sales-price effects from 0% to 43%. New-building cost premiums range from 0% to 12.5% and may be higher for retrofits. Premiums can decline as technologies mature, contractors gain expertise, passive design substitutes for mechanical systems, and supply chains improve. Consequently, green-building outcomes vary by property and should be assessed as ranges rather than deterministic gains.

The lecture then introduces market failure. Even energy-efficiency investments with positive NPVs may not be adopted when environmental, social, and financial objectives diverge. Three market failures are identified for discussion: information asymmetry, split incentives between tenants and landlords, and externalities requiring government intervention. The lecture concentrates on information asymmetry. Green buildings are partly experience or credence goods, and buyers cannot always judge their energy performance or indoor quality from marketing materials, creating opportunities for greenwashing.

Research described from China’s immature residential green-building market found that residents of green buildings recognized benefits and expressed willingness to pay approximately 300 RMB per square meter, while residents of comparable non-green buildings initially lacked understanding. Providing information about energy bills, lighting, and indoor air quality increased the latter group’s stated willingness to pay, although the findings relied on hypothetical purchase questions. Before effective certification systems existed, developers could make unsupported sustainability claims in presales, leaving early buyers with unexpectedly high energy costs or poor indoor conditions and no resale premium.

The economic problem is illustrated through adverse selection: without credible signals, buyers may treat green and non-green buildings alike, reducing developers’ ability to recover green-building costs and crowding out higher-quality developers. Certification such as LEED Platinum or LEED Gold provides a signal that helps distinguish genuine performance from greenwashing, sustains a differentiated market, and addresses information asymmetry. The lecture ends after introducing this first market failure and its potential remedies.

On Aug. 21, Columbia will be directly in the path of totality, where the moon fully covers the sun, creating daytime darkness. Hundreds of thousands are expected in the Midlands, and WIS News 10’s special airs at 7:30 p.m.

Noncredit continuing education includes professional competency education, career development, and personal enrichment. Although learning assessment is well established in credit-bearing courses and programs, noncredit offerings rarely assess learning outcomes; satisfaction surveys remain more common than direct assessment. Short course durations, varied learner motivations, and limited institutional resources may contribute to this gap.

Noncredit programs should establish realistic, clear, measurable outcomes suited to course length and learners’ prior knowledge. SMART outcomes should be linked directly to assessment methods and communicated in advance. Coordinators should collaborate with instructors and, where practical, involve learners in developing or reviewing outcomes.

Outcome-focused surveys can provide an efficient first step by asking learners to self-rate achievement or perceived learning gains. Low reported achievement can prompt review of instruction, curriculum, and learner information, while repeated surveys can monitor teaching effectiveness. Retrospective pre-post surveys are useful where course time is limited. These methods assess learners’ perceptions rather than learning directly.

For short programs, direct assessment can include one to three knowledge or skill questions within an end-of-course survey. For medium-duration programs, instructors can evaluate observed performance or learner products aligned with specific outcomes. Assessment activities should be valid, fair, practical, and beneficial to learners. Expert guidance can strengthen question design, scoring, analysis, and interpretation, while transparent alignment among curriculum, outcomes, and assessments supports fairness.

Overall, well-crafted outcomes, outcome-focused surveys, and direct assessment can guide course improvements, provide evidence of program quality, support resource requests, and align digital credentials with demonstrated competencies.

Brea’s police department is using a $21,000 all-electric Polaris Gem Global Motorcar to patrol The Tracks and the downtown entertainment district. The two-seat vehicle reaches 25 mph, travels 98 miles per charge and has off-road capabilities. Air Quality Management District funds paid for it.

The lecture concludes the discussion of Markov chains by reviewing eigenvalues and eigenvectors. For a transition matrix with transient and recurrent blocks, the determinant factors into the determinants of the blocks, so the matrix’s eigenvalues are the combined eigenvalues of its transient and recurrent submatrices. The transition probabilities from transient states to recurrent states affect row sums but not these eigenvalues. Left eigenvectors of a recurrent block can be extended with zeros to form left eigenvectors of the full matrix, and the same reasoning applies to chains with multiple recurrent classes.

The lecture then introduces state-dependent rewards or costs. It derives formulas for expected one-step and aggregate rewards and explains that, for an ergodic Markov chain with one recurrent class, the long-run expected gain per step becomes the steady-state value \(\sum_j \pi_j r_j\), independent of the initial state after a transient period. Rewards attached to transitions can also be converted into state-based rewards.

Expected first-passage time is presented as a reward problem. A target state is made absorbing, with zero reward there and unit rewards in all other states, so the accumulated reward equals the time until the target is first reached. The expected hitting times are then obtained from the linear equations \(v_1=0\) and \(v_i=1+\sum_j p_{ij}v_j\). This works when every state can reach the target; in a chain with multiple recurrent classes, states that cannot reach the target have infinite expected hitting time.

Finally, the lecture formulates a controlled finite-horizon Markov process. At each time, a decision maker observes the current state and chooses among finite alternatives, each specifying an immediate reward and transition probabilities. Dynamic programming works backward from a terminal reward, computing for each state and remaining horizon the alternative maximizing the immediate reward plus the expected optimal future reward. This produces both optimal state-dependent decisions and expected total rewards. The lecture contrasts these finite-horizon dynamic policies with stationary policies for indefinite operation and credits Bellman with formulating the problem that yields this simple backward-induction algorithm.

BG Group agreed to buy Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, including stakes in the Tapti and Panna/Mukta fields and the CB-OS/1 exploration block, with reserves exceeding 170 million barrels of oil equivalent. Analysts considered the price, under $2.30 per barrel, attractive. The transaction required Indian government approval and agreement among partners for BG to operate the fields; ONGC contested the operatorship, creating uncertainty. BG planned further investment and expansion, consistent with its strategy of developing India as a core gas market.

The sale marked Enron’s retreat from owning large physical assets as it focused more on trading. Enron separately sought to exit its 65% stake in the troubled Dabhol power project, whose operator defaulted on a $24 million interest payment and faced payment disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board.

Technology stocks led a major U.S. market rally, with the Nasdaq gaining 5.93% and Cisco rising 22%. Separately, Southern California Edison reached a settlement with state regulators that kept rates elevated to help repay debt and avoid bankruptcy, drawing consumer advocates’ criticism. Former Enron executive Thomas White was appointed the Pentagon’s liaison for homeland security.

The Power Play is a flexible gap-running scheme featuring a pulling guard, kick-out block, double teams, and back blocks that create angles at the point of attack. It can be run from numerous formations and personnel groups. Its concentration of blockers can produce yardage and help smaller offensive lines succeed through proper leverage and blocking angles. Double teams may be taught vertically for powerful lines or horizontally for undersized lines. Its primary weakness is backside pursuit and penetration, especially through the open gap created by the pulling guard; against odd fronts, an incorrect point call can leave a backside rusher unblocked. Common blocking assignments are outlined for 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, including adjustments to tight-end and fullback responsibilities. Fullhouse Power changes the formation’s F and U responsibilities, while gun same-side RPO allows the quarterback to throw based on box count or safety movement.

This continuation application addresses maximum power exposure (MPE) and maximum power reduction (MPR) in high-frequency 5G and millimeter-wave communications, where power reduction may vary by uplink beam or antenna panel and cannot be readily applied through base-station scheduling. A first communication node, such as a user equipment, sends report information to a second communication node, such as a base station. The report includes at least first-type power-parameter information or uplink channel-state information, enabling the second node to determine maximum power reduction and schedule the first node, including selecting a beam with lower MPE, to reduce human-body exposure and improve uplink performance.

Power-parameter information may include MPR, remaining or accumulated energy, uplink duty cycle, alert information, power backoff, and real or virtual power headroom. Channel-state information may include reference-signal indices, antenna groups or panels, uplink path loss, quasi-co-location information, and corrected uplink values. These data may be associated with beams, antenna groups, reference signals, spatial relations, transmission occasions, and time windows. Virtual power-headroom reporting can identify candidate spatial relations or reference signals associated with lower MPE using configured uplink power-control parameters. Reports may be periodic, semi-persistent, or aperiodic and triggered by thresholds, parameter changes, timers, or signaling. The application also provides sending and receiving apparatuses, processor-based communication nodes, and a storage medium implementing the methods.

Dairylea Cooperative appealed an order denying its motion to quash a New York Attorney General’s subpoena for corporate records in a grand jury investigation. It argued that the Attorney General lacked authority and that the subpoena was unduly burdensome. Special Term found the burden argument meritorious while noting the subpoena’s narrowed scope. The appellate court found statutory authority under Executive Law § 63(3), supported by a request from the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets, and affirmed the order without costs.

Purswell appealed his conviction for transporting intoxicating liquor. Sheriff’s officers concealed themselves near a gathering at McElvain’s home and arrested Purswell after observing him carry a jug containing whiskey. The court held that Purswell could not challenge the search of premises not owned or possessed by him, and that the evidence was properly admitted because his arrest was based on probable cause. It also rejected his general objection to the jury charge as insufficiently specific. On rehearing, the court found no evidentiary support for his allegation that the jury improperly considered his failure to testify and presumed that evidence heard on his motion for a new trial justified the ruling. The judgment was affirmed, and rehearing was denied.
The South Dakota Board of Regents directed central staff and officials from the state’s two largest universities to develop a plan to close the jointly operated Capital University Center in Pierre.

The article traces Enron’s transformation from a heavily indebted pipeline company into an energy-trading giant and its abrupt decline by 2001. Under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, Enron shifted from owning physical assets to creating and trading markets in gas, electricity, and other commodities. Skilling’s “Gas Bank” guaranteed gas supply and prices, allowing Enron to assume trading risks; the company soon dominated the market it had created.

Enron expanded into electricity, broadband, online commodity trading, and markets for products including coal, paper, steel, and weather. EnronOnline processed $335 billion in commodity trades in 2000, while the company’s growth helped its stock rise 1,700 percent from 1985 to 2000 and increased annual revenues from $40 billion to $100 billion.

The company recruited elite, aggressive employees and offered high salaries, uncapped performance bonuses, extensive perks, and rapid advancement opportunities. Its culture emphasized intellectual ability, urgency, risk, and individual financial reward. As competition intensified, forced rankings replaced employees rated poorly, roughly 15 percent of one division’s workforce was turned over annually, and workaholism, surveillance, restrictive confidentiality agreements, and internal distrust spread.

Enron increasingly used aggressive accounting and short-term trading strategies. It recorded much of the projected profit from long-term deals immediately, set its own market prices and deal terms, and sometimes abandoned projects when expected margins declined. Employees were treated as replaceable commodities, and senior executives frequently received large bonuses despite broader corporate problems. Skilling also sought to remove long-term, asset-heavy operations, prompting Rebecca Mark’s departure from Enron and her placement in charge of the water company Azurix. Azurix’s difficulties and eventual absorption into Enron reinforced criticism of the company’s rejection of slower, tangible businesses.

Enron’s prominence made it a target during California’s electricity crisis, while its India power project remained costly and its telecommunications investments collapsed with the technology-market downturn. Questions also arose about Enron’s accounting and profits, and the stock fell from $80 in January 2001 to around $35 by October. Although the article notes that the broader economic downturn contributed, it emphasizes the company’s aggressive culture, short-term incentives, and deteriorating internal morale.

Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, and Lay returned to promise a less aggressive company focused more closely on its core business and less reliance on forced performance rankings. Skilling defended his decisions and said his interests were aligned with shareholders, while looking toward future technology and commodity-trading ventures in Houston.

Firefly Aerospace shares fell nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test flight at its Briggs, Texas, facility. The company said safety protocols were followed, all personnel were safe and no other facilities were affected. Firefly debuted on the Nasdaq last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, but its shares have since fallen more than 50%. The company makes rockets, space tugs and lunar landers, including the Blue Ghost lander, which successfully landed on the moon earlier this year. Firefly plans to continue Alpha testing after its sixth rocket failed in April.

The passage reviews 3GPP LTE/LTE-A architecture, carrier aggregation, protocol layers, scheduling, semi-persistent scheduling, LTE Device-to-Device Proximity Services, and vehicular V2X communication. It describes two sidelink resource-allocation modes: Mode 1, in which an eNodeB allocates resources, and Mode 2, in which a UE autonomously selects time-frequency resources from configured pools.

The disclosure proposes improved Mode 2 resource selection for periodic or non-periodic data transmitted via the PC5 sidelink interface. A transmitting UE continuously senses future resources, including scheduling-assignment reservations and optionally received-signal energy. When data becomes available, the UE defines a transmission window based on delay requirements and uses information gathered during a preceding sensing window to select resources.

Because a half-duplex UE cannot sense while transmitting, transmission-window subframes are classified as primary when all corresponding sensing opportunities were sensed and secondary when sensing information is incomplete. Resources in primary subframes are preferred over those in secondary subframes. Candidates within each category are ranked separately, favoring shorter transmission delays and lower predicted energy; if the highest-ranked candidate is unavailable, lower-ranked candidates may be used. Energy prediction may use measurements aligned with possible data periodicities of 100 to 1,000 milliseconds.

The same selection principles apply to scheduling-assignment transmission. A scheduling assignment can identify reserved resources for subsequent scheduling assignments or data, with data and scheduling-assignment reservations managed separately or together. An optional preemption procedure addresses cases where no suitable candidate remains by selecting reserved resources based on random choice, predicted signal strength, or indicated priority. Vehicular communication, including periodic Cooperative Awareness Messages, is presented as an exemplary application.

The passage presents the Arctic as a rapidly changing, interconnected security system in which environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors interact. Decisions in one area can cascade across the others; for example, the Nome port expansion, motivated by shipping, resource development, and military objectives, may produce environmental disruption, cultural tensions, geopolitical shifts, and operational challenges. Traditional siloed, linear approaches are therefore inadequate for understanding or governing Arctic security.

The proposed alternative is systems thinking, which examines whole systems, interactions, feedback loops, recurring patterns, underlying structures, and leverage points where small interventions can produce significant effects. Arctic security education should emphasize interdisciplinary learning, strategic foresight, adaptive decision-making, and the analysis of second- and third-order consequences. Relevant leverage points include shifting conventional mental models, improving information sharing, strengthening policy and governance, encouraging behavioral and operational adaptation, and integrating economic and technological advances.

The Systems Thinking Education Model has three components: core systems-thinking principles, educational leverage points, and learning and assessment strategies. An integrated curriculum should bring together international relations, climate science, security studies, economics, and Indigenous knowledge rather than teaching them separately. Active methods—including concept mapping, simulations, wargaming, role-playing, stakeholder exercises, hypothetical cases, and interactive case studies—allow learners to manage competing interests and respond to dynamic security dilemmas.

Assessment should measure applied systems-thinking competencies through scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis and metacognition, and competency-based metrics. These approaches emphasize reasoning, interdisciplinary synthesis, adaptability, strategic foresight, and real-world performance rather than theoretical knowledge alone.

The model is presented as well suited to online graduate education because asynchronous scenarios, digital simulations, multimedia cases, concept-mapping tools, discussion forums, collaborative projects, journaling, and peer evaluation can support flexible, interdisciplinary experiential learning. Overall, the passage argues that systems-thinking education can prepare Arctic security professionals to anticipate cascading effects, bridge theory and practice, and develop sustainable, adaptive strategies amid the region’s evolving legal, geopolitical, environmental, economic, and Indigenous governance challenges.

On October 29, 2001, Enron’s shares fell to multiyear lows, losing more than half their value in two weeks and roughly $14 billion–$15.6 billion in market capitalization. The sell-off followed disclosures of complex off-balance-sheet partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, a $618 million third-quarter loss and $1.01 billion in write-offs, and an SEC inquiry into possible conflicts of interest.

Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured debt from Baa1 to Baa2, two notches above junk, and placed its ratings and Prime-2 commercial-paper rating under review for further downgrade. Moody’s also warned that deteriorating U.S. corporate credit could persist, with downgrade reviews substantially outpacing upgrades.

Enron was negotiating with banks for a new $1 billion–$2 billion credit line after drawing about $3 billion–$3.3 billion from existing facilities to repay commercial paper. Although Enron reported a net cash position above $1 billion, analysts said lenders were likely to demand higher interest rates, additional collateral and other stricter terms. Enron was selling assets, including a planned $2.9 billion sale of Portland General Electric, to raise cash. European energy companies were limiting or freezing trades with Enron, while those continuing to trade sought restrictive arrangements such as letters of credit.

Analysts questioned whether Enron’s asset-light trading model remained viable because its credibility and financial transparency were central to counterparties’ willingness to trade with it. They noted declining trading margins, asset write-downs, senior-management departures and nearly worthless employee stock options, while suggesting Enron might need to place greater emphasis on physical assets.

Shareholder litigation was also expanding. At least five class-action suits had been filed by 14 law firms, with another suit targeting directors. The cases focused on Fastow-managed partnerships, underperforming investments and transactions in broadband, water and other assets, including purported broadband hedging deals. Potential damages were described as potentially reaching billions of dollars.

Lorna Gibson introduces a course on cellular materials: highly porous solids with low solid volume fractions, typically below 30%. Engineering examples include two-dimensional honeycombs, three-dimensional foams, and regular 3D lattices or trusses. The course will examine deformation and failure, derive bulk properties such as stiffness, strength, fracture, and toughness, and consider how microstructure and material selection can produce desired engineering performance. Honeycomb and foam applications include lightweight sandwich panels, low-stress energy absorbers, thermal insulation, and catalytic-converter substrates. Open- and closed-cell foams, anisotropic cells, and the effects of solid fraction and cell shape will be considered.

Medical topics include trabecular bone, osteoporosis, porous coatings for orthopedic implants, and tissue-engineering scaffolds. Bone loss through strut thinning and resorption lowers relative density and strength. Scaffold mechanics can affect cell contraction, attachment, and migration. Natural cellular materials include wood, cork, plant parenchyma, glass sponges, leaves and skulls with sandwich structures, density-graded palm stems and bamboo, and plant stems and animal quills with compliant cellular cores. Cork’s corrugated cells give it a near-zero Poisson’s ratio, while wood fails through cell-wall buckling.

Students will complete open-ended projects in pairs. Examples include negative-Poisson-ratio honeycombs, elephant skull acoustics, osteoporosis, tissue scaffolds, and food foams such as bread. The elephant-skull project compared the vibration response of porous elephant skulls with a nonporous dolphin skull using CT images, 3D-printed models, and accelerometers. Historical examples include John Evelyn’s seventeenth-century paper on bread making and Robert Hooke’s drawings of cork cells.

Honeycomb fabrication methods include expansion of glued sheets, corrugation and bonding, ceramic extrusion, casting, rapid prototyping, selective laser scanning, and wood-derived bio-carbon templates. Wood can be pyrolyzed at about 800°C to preserve its cellular structure, then infiltrated with silicon to produce silicon-carbide replicas for high-temperature filters or catalyst carriers.

Polymer foams are produced by introducing and stabilizing bubbles through mechanical mixing or physical and chemical blowing agents. Whether cells are open or closed depends on polymer viscosity and surface tension. Other approaches include bonding hollow spheres into syntactic foams and forming thick surface skins to create structural sandwich panels. Metal foams can be made by stirring gas into molten aluminum with stabilizing particles, using titanium hydride to release hydrogen in aluminum powder or molten metal, replicating a polymer foam, vapor-depositing nickel, expanding trapped gas under pressure, bonding hollow spheres, or infiltrating a mold with metal and leaching away a salt phase. Gibson closes by describing her civil-engineering education, PhD work on cellular solids at Cambridge, work in Calgary and Vancouver, and subsequent appointments at MIT’s civil engineering and materials science departments.

Goals in soccer are scored at higher rates during specific five-minute periods: the start of the match and second half, after goals or penalty kicks, after dangerous fouls, near halftime, during the match’s final minutes, and around extra time. Coaches should prepare players to exploit or defend against these periods. The pattern is attributed to psychological factors such as excitement, unreadiness, overconfidence or depression after goals, retaliation, and urgency as time expires. Post-goal “let-down” is identified as the most important factor, with “No letdown!” recommended as a team reminder.

Q3 2025 commentary notes municipals remain an extremely safe, flight-to-quality asset class, describes the Fed's September short-term rate cut amid slowing job growth and mixed inflation, cites upgrades for well-funded municipal reserves, and suggests muni credit quality may begin to turn as government-shutdown challenges arrive. A biography outlines David Kotok's co-founding of and CIO role at Cumberland Advisors (1973–December 2024), publications in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Barron's and Bloomberg, five books, three University of Pennsylvania degrees, and various GIC and public-service roles. Listed headlines cover AI ETFs, Micron, Kayne Anderson BDC, Nebius, LNG royalties, Tesla, MercadoLibre, REITs, and three municipal bond ETFs.

Newcomers can prepare for Canadian job searches by researching jobs online before arrival, attending free career workshops, and pursuing internships or volunteer opportunities to build experience and networks. They should check credential requirements, update skills as needed, and improve English or French proficiency, including business skills, through courses and associations.

Trump described Canada-US trade problems as less severe than those with Mexico and indicated tweaks rather than an overhaul; USD/CAD fell to 1.3060, easing a key CAD risk and paving the way for another test of 1.3000. Markets also awaited Yellen’s testimony, China’s January inflation data, and a Kuroda speech.

At Supreme Court oral argument on whether Delaware's medical malpractice filing requirements apply in federal court, several justices appeared skeptical of applying them. Justice Kagan argued the Delaware rules conflict with the Federal Rules' notice-pleading system by forcing a plaintiff to prove her case before the case begins; Justice Jackson emphasized that under federal law an action commences by filing a complaint; and Justice Sotomayor noted the federal 20-day answer requirement versus Delaware's delay until an affidavit is filed. Justice Gorsuch faulted the defendants' suggestion that courts could pick and choose among Delaware statute provisions, calling it a "Frankenstein" with no authority to rewrite state law. Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Thomas and Alito, who might favor Delaware's concerns, said little, making the court's eventual outcome unclear.

Built in 1992, Treetops provides dementia accommodation for older people within walking distance of Keynsham town centre. It has one of three family-sized units, communal and quiet meeting areas, named carers, family involvement in care planning, and indoor and outdoor activities.

DAWN-PLASMA was a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial comparing standard supportive care plus convalescent plasma with supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with confirmed COVID-19. The study was adapted from a WHO master protocol. The primary objective was to assess the clinical efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma; the hypothesis was that early administration of high-volume, high-titer plasma would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation.

Participants were randomized 2:1 by a computerized system to receive convalescent plasma plus standard care or standard care alone. Patients received 800–1,000 mL of plasma in four doses, with the first two units given within 12 hours of randomization and the next two 24–36 hours later. Plasma required neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. Prior, concomitant, and post-intervention therapies were unrestricted, while standard care followed evolving national and international guidance.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status at Days 15 and 30, time to sustained clinical improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death within 30 and 90 days, thromboembolism, transfusion effects, antibody-titer correlations, safety, quality of life, adverse events, laboratory data, and vital signs. Exploratory assessments included SARS-CoV-2 PCR, NT50 measurements, and comparisons by pre-existing COVID-19 antibodies.

Eligible patients were non-pregnant adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and radiographic infiltrates or clinical findings including rales and oxygen saturation of 94% or lower. Exclusions included pre-existing mechanical ventilation and specified safety risks. Five patients withdrew before intervention and one was a screen failure; six replacements were randomized, and no patients were lost to follow-up afterward.

The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Ethics committees approved the protocol and consent documentation, and informed consent was obtained before enrollment. Sponsor monitoring reviewed protocol adherence, GCP compliance, and data quality. Investigators verified CRF data, central laboratories performed specified assays, and no quality audits or predefined QTLs were conducted.

The creed urges players to maintain ball awareness, communicate with teammates and coaches, report injuries or suspected concussions, avoid errors, create passing options, protect the ball, and move for the team’s benefit. Players should play aggressively without reckless fouls, avoid retaliation, listen to opponents, keep opponents contested, follow the referee and game laws, learn from mistakes, and practice fair play and sportsmanship.

The paper explores how website usability affects customer experience in Saudi Arabia’s emerging e-business market. A cross-sectional evaluation involved 65 trained student evaluators in two cohorts: 26 assessed four retail sites and 39 assessed four booking sites. Participants used selected websites for 30 minutes and completed Likert-scale questionnaires covering navigation, design, and content; results were analyzed in Excel.

Overall ratings were positive, but both groups identified similar weaknesses. These included disappearing menu links, orphan pages, poor sitemap and within-page navigation, inconsistent Arabic-English interfaces, and design issues involving layouts, font sizes, menus, and icon labels. Content problems included weak ordering, blank pages, spelling and grammar errors, missing contact information, and absent last-update dates. Cronbach’s alpha values were 0.66 and 0.79, with results converging across groups.

The study recommends user-centered and participatory design, task analysis, ethnographic research, and professional content review to improve portals. It notes that the small sample of evaluators and websites limits generalizability and calls for longitudinal research on usability improvements and customer behavior.

Blair voters rejected a $250,000 transportation bond issue, 111-80 (58.76%), below the 60% supermajority required by state law. The proposal would have purchased three 72-passenger buses to replace leased vehicles. Area voters also chose municipal council and school board candidates, with results reported for Altus, Walters, and school districts in Caddo, Comanche, and Cotton counties.

Senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins told a parliamentary committee that the Bank of Canada is seeing slower credit growth in mortgages and other household debt alongside rising labour income, and expects the household debt-to-disposable-income ratio to stabilize over the coming years. The ratio reached a record 170.4 per cent in the final three months of 2017, slightly down from a peak of 170.5 per cent, up from 90 per cent in 1990. Wilkins noted the buildup included asset purchases like housing, raising net worth, and said the decline will take time because accumulation was lengthy. Some experts say the ratio is only one metric and that debt composition and risk levels also matter. The Bank of Canada has raised rates three times since July, calls household debt a top concern, and governor Stephen Poloz said high debt loads have made households 50 per cent more sensitive to interest rate changes.

Players are responsible for getting into scoring areas and generating shots against a large goaltender. After two days off and a disappointing loss, the team practiced, regrouped, and is ready to score first.

In a 1980 interview, Ronald Reagan questioned whether President Carter was downplaying U.S. responsibility following a failed Iran mission. He noted Khomeini’s apparent opposition to Soviet influence but cited Soviet propaganda and the Iranian Communist Party as factors. Reagan called direct Iranian alignment with the Soviet Union a potentially grave threat to the Middle East and U.S. security; reporters also raised the possibility of covert or overt U.S. action.

After accepting the Republican presidential nomination on July 17, 1980, Reagan declared that protecting Americans and maintaining world peace and freedom were his administration’s top priorities. He described Americans as peaceful but unwilling to resort to force except when absolutely necessary, emphasized good-faith negotiation, and maintained that national strength was essential to deter aggression and preserve freedom.

In a subsequent address, Reagan told veterans that experience of war showed peace cannot be secured through wishful thinking or weakness. He warned that America’s margin of safety was shrinking, defended military preparedness as necessary rather than warlike, and quoted Will Rogers: “I’ve never seen anyone insult Jack Dempsey.”

This basketball guide outlines offensive strategies for breaking full- and half-court presses. Teams should anticipate pressure, analyze the press, exploit weaknesses and weak defenders, spread the floor, maintain defensive balance, and use a slow-to-quick tempo. Ballhandlers should advance quickly through teamwork using short, crisp passes, close distance before passing, work the ball into the middle, dribble sparingly, use jump stops, avoid passing off the dribble, and “eat the ball” rather than commit turnovers. Receivers should create leads, meet passes, and catch with their backs to the sideline in a triple-threat stance; long passes should lead receivers toward the elbow.

Five-player attacking formations such as 2-1-2 are preferred over set plays. Clearing out is useful against person-to-person presses but dangerous against zones. Outlet and inbound pass priorities are long, then short, then to the middle. The trailer should preserve defensive balance and wait for the early push to be stopped. Teams should practice attacking outnumbered situations, particularly two-on-one and three-on-two, and reverse the ball to the inbounder or trailer against double teams. Players should avoid receiving with their backs to the basket, dribbling along the sideline, one-handed or bounce passes, telegraphed passes, picking up the dribble, and making inbound passes before teammates are ready.

Successful press breaks require designated roles, precise coordination, and proper spacing, timing, and footwork. Coaches should teach before games, use the Whole-Part-Whole method with progressive breakdown drills, and then practice at game speed against strong defense. Press breaks should be used on every possession and incorporated into every practice. The goals are to build poise, advance the ball under control, attack outnumbered situations, counter double teams, transition into early offense, and pursue offensive rebounds. Defensively, teams should scout opponents, apply immediate pressure, disrupt fast breaks and early offense, and move directly from push to flow to continuity.

The study demonstrates coherent control of the three nearest-neighbor ^15N nuclear spins surrounding negatively charged boron vacancies (V_B^−) in isotopically enriched h^10B^15N. Optical detected magnetic resonance at 212 mT resolved the four hyperfine states of the electron–nuclear system, and pulsed electron–nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) enabled selective initialization and manipulation of multinuclear configurations.

Hyperfine-mediated mixing between electronic and nuclear spin states lifts transition degeneracies, producing three distinct nuclear transitions whose energies depend on magnetic field. Measurements from 169–240 mT agreed with simulations and yielded fitted hyperfine couplings of A_x = −61.3 MHz, A_y = −121.6 MHz, and A_z = −63.7 MHz. Simulations extended to 0–500 mT predicted substantial shifts near the ground-state level avoided crossing and showed that nuclear-state control is also possible in the predominantly m_S = 0 branch.

Rabi oscillations were measured for selected nuclear transitions at 212 mT. Hyperfine mixing enhanced the effective nuclear g-factor by approximately 116 relative to isolated ^15N spins, enabling faster nuclear driving than expected. The Rabi coherence time was about 12 μs, one to two orders of magnitude longer than the electron-spin T_2, while ENDOR linewidths reached 1.2 MHz. The theoretical enhancement was 416, with the difference attributed to uncertain microwave and radio-frequency powers and neglected nuclear spins.

Continuous optical pumping unexpectedly depolarized the nuclear spins within about 1 μs. The authors tentatively associated this relaxation with the triplet optical excited state, while noting that the detailed mechanism remained unresolved.

Isotopically enriched hBN flakes were fabricated, implanted with helium ions to create V_B^− ensembles, and measured under ambient conditions using a 488 nm laser and coplanar-waveguide microwave and radio-frequency pulses. Numerical simulations used the four-spin Hamiltonian and ab initio hyperfine parameters. The results indicate that strongly coupled nuclear spins around V_B^− centers could support quantum memories, nuclear-assisted dynamics, enhanced sensing, and integration with van der Waals heterostructures.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court’s judgment that Pennsylvania’s Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act (Act 109) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. It rejected four arguments by the Department of Education.

First, the U.S. Supreme Court’s decisions in Lemon v. Kurtzman invalidated Act 109 only as applied to sectarian schools because of excessive government entanglement, including teacher-role restrictions, accounting supervision, and continuing direct aid. Those decisions did not resolve the statute’s validity for nonsectarian schools.

Second, Act 109 is severable. Pennsylvania law favors severability, the statute contains an express severability clause, and its provisions can operate independently for sectarian and nonsectarian schools. Application to nonsectarian schools fulfills the legislature’s secular-education purpose.

Third, Act 109 was not impliedly repealed by later statutes concerning nonpublic education. Valid later laws did not establish an irreconcilable, comprehensive system covering the entire subject of Act 109, while unconstitutional statutes could not impliedly repeal it.

Finally, requiring the Department to determine whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian would not create excessive constitutional entanglement. The inquiry would be limited, comparable to tax-exempt status review, and would satisfy the Establishment Clause test.

The Commonwealth Court’s order was affirmed. Justice Eagen dissented.

As Jake Browning struggles for the Bengals, former Cincinnati starter Andy Dalton has resurfaced as a potential outside target. The Panthers backup is familiar with coach Zac Taylor and showed flashes of his former form, while speculation suggests Cincinnati could acquire him for about $3 million.

- Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 covers two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. It reported 169,793,685 common shares outstanding as of April 30, 2018.

- Quarterly revenue was $3.409 billion, comprising $2.735 billion of automotive revenue, $410.0 million from energy generation and storage, and $263.4 million from services and other activities. Gross profit was $456.5 million, operating expenses were $1.054 billion, and the operating loss was $597.0 million. The consolidated net loss was $784.6 million, including a $709.6 million loss attributable to common stockholders, or $4.19 per diluted share. Comparable 2017 figures were $2.696 billion of revenue, $667.9 million of gross profit, and a $397.2 million net loss.

- At March 31, 2018, assets totaled $27.271 billion and liabilities totaled $21.551 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.666 billion, while total cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash was $3.220 billion. Inventory was $2.566 billion, solar energy systems $6.346 billion, property, plant and equipment $10.519 billion, and operating lease vehicles $2.315 billion. During the quarter, Tesla used $398.4 million in operating cash, $728.6 million in investing cash, and received $371.7 million from financing activities.

- Tesla adopted the new revenue standard on January 1, 2018 using the modified retrospective method, reducing opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. Relative to the former treatment, first-quarter automotive sales revenue increased by $299.0 million, automotive leasing revenue decreased by $164.9 million, and the loss attributable to common stockholders improved by $33.3 million. Vehicle sales generally are recognized upon delivery; connected services, monitoring, maintenance and certain other obligations generally are recognized over relevant service periods. Solar and storage project revenue is recognized using control-transfer or percentage-of-completion methods, while lease revenue generally is recognized straight-line.

- Total debt had $10.466 billion of unpaid contractual balances, with $1.756 billion of current and $8.220 billion of long-term net carrying values. Tesla was in compliance with all debt covenants. It also adopted retrospective presentation of restricted cash in cash-flow statements and expected to adopt the new lease standard on January 1, 2019, which was expected to materially affect reported assets, liabilities and results.

- Stockholders approved a March 2018 CEO award of 20,264,042 options, structured in 12 tranches requiring both market-capitalization and operating milestones. Tesla recorded $6.7 million of related expense in the quarter; $766.2 million of compensation remained unrecognized for milestones considered probable and $1.51 billion for milestones considered not probable. The report also identified dependence on single-source suppliers and uncertainty in warranty-cost estimates as significant risks.

The socket uses a black Liquid Crystal Polymer base and natural or ivory LCP cover with a UL 94 V-0 rating. Cover thickness, including the 0.30 mm pocket recess, must not exceed 1.17 mm, and flatness must remain below 0.25 mm after reflow and environmental/mechanical testing. A removable overlay covers the pin holes, facilitates vacuum pick-and-place, and must not outgas during reflow or leave residue. Molded markings include “SOCKET 940,” locked/unlocked indicators, A01 orientation, and the supplier’s UL symbol; lot traceability markings must remain visible after PCB mounting.

Contacts are made from high-strength copper alloy with nickel plating and gold-plated mating areas. SMT attachment uses 63/37 ±5% tin/lead solder balls, a 0.20 mm coplanarity requirement, and solder-barrier features. The stainless-steel lever enables toolless actuation, requires less than 3.6 kgf operating force, limits pin displacement to under 1.0 mm, and must maintain integrity through 50 actuations. Inspections require intact solder balls, contacts, cover, base, tabs, and lever.

Each contact is rated for 1.5 A with less than 30°C temperature rise. Initial and post-test LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact with Kovar pins. Requirements also cover inductance, capacitance, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, propagation-delay skew, crosstalk, 650 Vac minimum dielectric withstand, and 1000 MΩ minimum insulation resistance.

The U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian released a May 2018 electronic edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1906, Part I*. The portable edition reproduces the full volumes, supports full-text search, bookmarking, and note-taking, and can be used offline. Readers are advised to cite persistent document numbers rather than printed page numbers; older cross-references include corresponding document numbers in brackets.

The President’s annual message described unprecedented national prosperity that could be harmed by reckless speculation and disregard for legitimate business methods. It urged Congress to complete unfinished legislative business, recommended prohibiting corporations from contributing to political campaigns while allowing individual contributions, and advocated granting the government the right to appeal criminal cases involving questions of law. The President said such appeals would not overturn acquittals on the merits but would resolve conflicting lower-court rulings, including cases involving rebate conspiracies. He argued that the appeal right was needed to obtain justice against wealthy wrongdoers and protect wage workers, citing a decision that left railway employees without a remedy under a labor statute and asserting the Supreme Court should determine the statute’s constitutionality.

Tesla Motors, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016 reported unaudited second-quarter revenue of $1.27 billion, up from $955.0 million a year earlier. Automotive revenue was $1.18 billion and services and other revenue was $88.2 million. Gross profit was $274.8 million, representing a 21.6% margin, while the operating loss was $238.0 million and the net loss was $293.2 million, or $2.09 per share. For the first six months, revenue was $2.42 billion and the net loss was $575.5 million, or $4.22 per share.

At June 30, 2016, Tesla reported $11.87 billion of assets, $9.31 billion of liabilities, $2.52 billion of stockholders’ equity and $3.25 billion of cash and cash equivalents. First-half operating and investing activities used $99.3 million and $553.7 million of cash, respectively, while financing activities provided $2.69 billion, including $1.70 billion from a May public stock offering and $1.11 billion from debt issuance.

Tesla was producing the Model S and Model X, continued ramping Model X production, and planned approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016. It expected Model 3 volume production and deliveries in late 2017 and targeted 500,000 vehicles in 2018. The company was developing the Gigafactory for integrated battery and energy-product production. Following quarter-end, Tesla entered an agreement to acquire SolarCity through an exchange ratio of 0.110 Tesla shares per SolarCity share, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The filing also detailed Tesla’s accounting policies, lease and resale-value guarantees, debt, stock compensation, derivatives, contingencies and legal proceedings.

North Carolina’s 38–10 loss to Clemson exposed defensive and offensive shortcomings, including 399 passing yards allowed and 2-of-11 third-down conversion. Head coach Bill Belichick accepted responsibility for penalties and defensive lapses, declined to assess the program rebuild, and praised his team’s effort while emphasizing improvement.

Moscow denies responsibility for the Skripal poisoning and says it destroyed its chemical weapons in 1992. Britain says it has evidence that Russia continued producing and stockpiling Novichok and investigated nerve-agent delivery for assassinations. The passage calls for stronger sanctions and tighter laws to identify and seize Russian assets hidden in the West.

The ADS868xW uses separate AVDD and DVDD power supplies, which can be set independently within their permissible ranges. Decoupling with 1 µF and minimum 10 µF capacitors is recommended; the 1 µF capacitor should be placed closest to the supply pins. Decoupling improves power-supply rejection ratio, particularly for high-frequency digital switching current.

The device provides two programmable low-power modes for reduced-throughput operation. In NAP mode, write 69h to register address 05h, set the NAP_EN bit, and hold CONVST/CS high after conversion. The device remains in NAP while the pin is high and exits on its falling edge; a new conversion must wait until tNAP_WKUP elapses. In power-down mode, set the PWRDN bit after unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG. The device enters PD on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, powers down analog blocks, and retains interface operation and register contents. Clearing PWRDN initiates recovery; RVS goes high, and a new conversion must wait until tPWRUP elapses.

PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital sections, routing analog signals away from digital lines, using clean and well-bypassed supplies, and providing low-impedance ground connections. AVDD and DVDD require nearby 1 µF X7R, 0603 ceramic capacitors rated at least 10 V. REFCAP requires 1 µF and 10 µF ceramic capacitors connected without intervening vias, with the 10 µF capacitor having ESR below 0.2 Ω. REFIO requires at least 4.7 µF when the internal reference is used.

The document also identifies TI support resources, documentation-update notifications, ESD handling precautions, revision information, mechanical and orderable data, and associated legal disclaimers.

Since becoming chief executive in summer 2015, Russell Down has led Speedy’s turnaround by refocusing on customers, changing an inward-looking culture, controlling operating costs and improving equipment availability and asset utilisation. He addressed unreliable asset data following an IT upgrade, declining attention to smaller customers and a cost-saving strategy that centralised equipment testing, created backlogs and left more than half of products unavailable in September 2015.

For the six months ending September, profits rose 58.8% to £10.8m, net debt fell and ROCE improved. Customer surveys and an annual staff survey accompanied gains in staff engagement. Speedy has also acquired powered-access businesses Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited, expanding its product range and expected revenue and cost synergies. Down believes the company is financially strong and positioned for sustainable, profitable growth.

The article introduces a periodically modulated multi-chain SSH platform for generating non-Abelian quantum interference and entanglement through braiding topological edge states. Protection is provided by time-independent inversion symmetry and time-dependent interchain symmetry.

In a double-coupled SSH chain, four edge states form two branches with a twisted energy spectrum. Their symmetry eigenvalues swap over one period, producing an Abelian braid and exchanging states between chains. Symmetry-protected adiabatic evolution preserves parity and transfers an end-localized particle from one chain to the two ends of another, with the final partition continuously tunable by the accumulated relative dynamical phase. Numerical results agree with the analytical predictions, with a reported fidelity of 0.998. Protection by time-dependent symmetry requires a sufficiently long, though finite, evolution period.

The analysis is extended to three coupled SSH chains containing six edge states in three branches. Their symmetry eigenvalues undergo cyclic swaps, and different braid sequences produce different final states. Consequently, the recipient chain for topological transport depends on the order of braiding operations, while the accumulated phase controls how the transferred state is partitioned between the recipient chain’s two ends.

For two identical bosons initially placed at opposite ends of one chain, adiabatic evolution at selected phase differences produces a spatial two-particle NOON state through Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The braiding sequence determines whether the entangled state and associated bunching correlations appear on one chain or another, with reported fidelity of 0.995. The results demonstrate order-dependent edge-state swapping, transport, and interference as signatures of non-Abelian braiding. The authors also identify slowly modulated photonic waveguide arrays as a viable experimental platform and note that the symmetry-protected braiding approach may extend to bulk states.
