Clark County schools are deciding how to allocate new state “weighted funding” for students who score in the bottom 25% on state tests and either are learning English or live in poverty. The formula provides $1,200 per eligible student at schools not already receiving Zoom or Victory funding. Clark County received more than $34 million of the $36 million allocated statewide.

At Garside Junior High in Las Vegas, 378 students qualify, and the school expects more than $450,000. English-language teacher Kimberly Ivanick proposed expanding after-school tutoring and providing technology. Spending will be tracked separately and evaluated for its effect on student achievement.

Bovine mastitis costs dairy farmers more than $400 per clinical case and damages mammary tissue, reducing milk production and quality. Although antibiotics eliminate bacteria, they do not restore damaged tissue. Cornell researchers characterized secretions from bovine mammary stem cells, finding that they promote blood-vessel formation and cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and include antimicrobial peptides, particularly effective against gram-negative bacterial toxins. The researchers propose that these secretions could complement approved intramammary antimicrobials and support tissue regeneration, but their effectiveness in cows with mastitis still requires testing.

Hyundai Motor and Kia Motors have installed a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) system on a 14-kilometer Hwaseong road with seven intersections to support autonomous driving. The system enables real-time information exchange among vehicles, roads, traffic signals and pedestrians, and the automakers plan further testing and development.

The Executive transmits to the Senate a February 14, 1893 annexation treaty between U.S. Secretary of State John W. Foster and Hawaiian government commissioners, seeking ratification. The treaty leaves detailed annexation questions for future adjustment. The message argues that Queen Liliuokalani’s restoration would be undesirable or impossible and that annexation was preferable to a U.S. protectorate because it would protect Hawaiian and American interests and prevent another power from gaining the islands. It reports no foreign-government protests and urges prompt Senate action, with existing laws maintaining peace and order until Congress establishes a permanent government protecting residents’ rights.

International star Caitlin Bassett says the hype and intense preparation for Saturday’s Super Netball grand final are unlike anything she has experienced. Sunshine Coast Lightning face Greater Western Sydney in Brisbane, with Bassett helping prepare goalkeeper Geva Mentor to contain the Giants’ dangerous attack, including 196cm shooter Kristina Brice.

The passage outlines how to introduce corner-kick offense to young soccer players. A corner kick restarts play when a defender touches the ball completely over the own end line; the attacking team takes the ball to the nearest corner arc. Because corner kicks provide set-play opportunities near goal, coaches should teach Law 17 carefully, including ball placement, proper run-up, instep-drive kicking, defender distance, and the rule that the kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does.

Teaching should progress from basic demonstrations to designated positions: corner taker, receiver, and cover man. In the basic play, the corner taker passes to a receiver five yards into the field. The receiver turns toward goal while the taker and cover man run behind for a possible pass. The cover man begins near the end line to prevent a missed kick from going out of bounds. Players should rotate through all positions, practice right- and left-footed kicks from both corner arcs, and eventually have specific players assigned to each role. Passive and active defenders, passing options, offside instruction, and additional plays can be introduced as players improve. During games, the referee indicates the correct arc, and the corner taker must wait for the referee’s acknowledgment before kicking.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), introduced by Welles Wilder in 1978, is an oscillator that measures the magnitude of gains and losses over a chosen number of days on a scale from 0 to 100. It is commonly used to identify overbought and oversold conditions, with readings above 70 or 85 generally indicating overbought conditions and readings below 30 or 15 indicating oversold conditions.

The article’s backtests indicate that RSI works best as a mean-reverting strategy on stocks and performs less effectively on other assets, including forex and commodity-related stocks. It generally requires additional filters, variables, or a second indicator. Daily bars and short lookback periods—preferably under five days—favorably balance performance and drawdown, while shorter intraday periods are less useful. A two-day strategy buying below 15 and selling above 85 slightly underperformed buy-and-hold on SPY from 1993 to 2020 but had lower drawdown and less market exposure. A QQQ test reported a 71% win rate, 0.82% average gain per trade, and 23% worst drawdown. Backtesting is essential because results vary by market, asset, timeframe, thresholds, and transaction costs.

Combining a 30-day RSI above 50 with a two-day RSI below 15 and exiting above 85 reduced SPY exposure to 27% but performed worse than the single-timeframe strategy. Price-RSI divergence is widely treated as a reversal signal, although the article notes that divergences are recognized in hindsight and are difficult to quantify.

RSI performs best when paired with tools such as volume, trend information, relative performance, or the Internal Bar Strength Indicator. RSI-14 provides faster, more sensitive signals, while RSI-21 offers smoother readings suited to longer-term analysis. Variants include ConnorsRSI and Cutler’s RSI.

The passage criticizes commentary portraying Supreme Court religious-freedom cases as polarized, partisan “culture wars” or efforts to advantage conservative Christians. It focuses on *Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety*. Rastafarian prisoner Damon Landor was forcibly shaved by Louisiana officials, violating the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA). Although a lower court ruled that RLUIPA does not permit money damages, the Supreme Court agreed to review the case. The author, who filed a supporting brief, argues that Landor should win because denying damages would leave deliberate violations of prisoners’ religious rights without meaningful relief.

The passage emphasizes that many important religious-liberty decisions have been unanimous or nearly unanimous and have protected diverse groups, including religious minorities and non-Christian practitioners. It says most disputes involve practical accommodations—such as Amish buggies, religious dress in identification photos, or halal and kosher meals—rather than contested social issues. Ultimately, the author argues that religious freedom is a fundamental right belonging to everyone, not a partisan or theocratic objective.
Police pursued a wanted shooting suspect in City Heights after a traffic stop. He crashed through school and fire-station fences, then fled armed before being arrested nearby.

A retrospective study of 671 patients treated from July 2017 to December 2018 examined traumatic brain injury risk factors. Participants averaged 46.016 years; 459 were male and 212 female. Domestic accidents were the most frequently reported cause in both sexes, followed overall by alcohol-related injury, motor vehicle injury, and criminal injury. Nearly all patients received conservative therapy, while 198 required surgery, most commonly wound debridement. Men developed TBI at younger ages than women and had longer hospital stays. Hospitalization duration was positively associated with age in both sexes. Village residents were reported to have greater TBI risk than urban residents, while urban TBI patients were older. Cause-specific mean ages and hospitalization durations varied by injury type and sex. The authors identified alcohol consumption and poor hygiene or harmful habits as potentially avoidable risk factors and concluded that domestic accidents, residence, age, and gender were important in TBI occurrence and outcomes. The study lacked a control group, limiting comparisons of incidence between men and women.

In 1945, President Truman reorganized U.S. foreign-policy institutions. Edward R. Stettinius Jr. resigned as secretary of state; James F. Byrnes succeeded him, while Dean Acheson replaced Joseph C. Grew as under secretary. Patrick J. Hurley resigned as ambassador to China, and George C. Marshall was appointed Truman’s personal envoy to China with ambassadorial rank. Cordell Hull received the Nobel Peace Prize.

International-information functions of the Office of War Information and Office of Inter-American Affairs were transferred to the Department of State. Research and Analysis and Presentation branches of the Office of Strategic Services were also transferred to State; the OSS was abolished and its remaining activities assigned to the War Department. Truman directed State to lead a coordinated foreign-intelligence program and preserve wartime experience for addressing postwar problems. The passage cites presidential statements on China, national defense, and displaced persons, along with contemporary Department of State publications and Franklin’s 1947 study of diplomatic and consular practice.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a water-soluble hydrotrope with hydrophilic and hydrophobic parts. Available in powder and liquid forms, it improves the solubility of poorly soluble organic matter, lowers cloud points, promotes ingredient compatibility, and moderates viscosity. It is used in detergents, cleaners, drilling fluids, metal processing, and anti-caking agents. Industrialization and household detergent use may drive demand, while raw-material volatility and declining R&D may hinder growth. Liquid forms and household applications are expected to dominate; heavy exposure may irritate the eyes and respiratory tract.

U.S. stocks fell about 2% Monday, led by a 7.1% drop in Facebook after reports that a Trump campaign consultancy improperly accessed data from more than 50 million users. The Nasdaq lost 2.09%, the S&P technology index dropped 2.5%, and all 11 S&P sectors declined. Tech scrutiny, trade-war concerns, political uncertainty and an expected Federal Reserve rate increase fueled the broad selloff.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January, forming FBT Gibbons with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. Robert Sartin will be chairman, and Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo will be co-managing partners. Leaders say the merger expands FBT’s Northeast footprint, helps serve financial-services clients and supports national growth, with integration the first priority. Law.com ranked FBT No. 128 and reported $336.5 million in gross revenue, compared with Gibbons’ $115 million.

Stephen Hawking, the theoretical physicist and author of the international bestseller *A Brief History of Time*, died after living with ALS for more than 50 years. His children described him as a great scientist and extraordinary man. Despite paralysis and the loss of his voice, Hawking continued his scientific work, sought a unified theory linking relativity and quantum mechanics, wrote *The Universe in a Nutshell*, appeared on television, and served as Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge University. He became a highly recognizable public figure, inspired renewed interest in science, and was portrayed by Eddie Redmayne in *The Theory of Everything*. His longevity and achievements helped demonstrate that severe disabilities need not stop people from living.

Blackwell adds fine-grained clock, power, and voltage gating to reduce dynamic power, leakage, and latency when entering or leaving deep power states. Its clock gating can shut down entire clock trees quickly, including the full memory clock tree for the first time using GDDR7’s fast-wakeup architecture. Separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory enable workload-specific voltage control and frame-granular shutdown of unused chip areas, improving efficiency in battery-powered systems and laptops.

Blackwell’s clock architecture allows clocks to adapt to changing workloads 1,000 times faster than previous GPU architectures, permitting higher clocks during active periods and lower power during brief idle gaps. Its deepest sleep state is entered 10 times faster than on Ada. In an example involving small-language-model inference, reduced active periods, gated transitional states, and faster sleep produced power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can create as many as three additional frames for every traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model runs 40% faster than the previous generation, uses 30% less VRAM, and replaces hardware optical flow with an efficient AI model. Blackwell’s enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine, while doubled pixel-processing capability supports higher resolutions and refresh rates. Fifth-generation Tensor Cores accelerate the AI models, and the AI Management Processor schedules DLSS processing, rendering, and pacing.

DLSS 4 also replaces CNN-based models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. Transformers use self-attention to identify longer-range patterns and support models with twice as many parameters. Super Resolution provides greater temporal stability, less ghosting, and more detail in motion; Ray Reconstruction improves ray-traced scenes and reduces typical denoiser artifacts; DLAA uses Super Resolution technology to produce a more realistic native-resolution image.

Blackwell expands access to Tensor Cores through Microsoft’s Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, allowing neural techniques in pixel and ray-tracing shaders when combined with Slang features. Neural shaders can approximate complex lighting algorithms, compress textures, predict indirect illumination, and simulate subsurface scattering. Associated technologies include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression can provide up to seven-to-one VRAM savings over block-compressed formats; the cited materials demo uses 333 MB instead of 1,110 MB. Neural Radiance Cache trains small networks on live game data to infer multiple lighting bounces after one traced bounce. RTX Skin applies ray-traced subsurface scattering, while Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model to improve a rasterized face using pose data and training images covering varied angles, lighting, emotions, and occlusions.

The GPU family includes GB202, a flagship chip with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface. It powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and a 256-bit memory interface; it powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 is described as the entry point to Blackwell’s new features, with 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor Cores, and a 192-bit memory interface; it powers the RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and that products are not warranted for medical, military, aircraft, space, life-support, or other safety-critical applications.

An earlier annexation treaty providing annuities triple Marcy's offer and admitting Hawaii as a state drew U.S. objections and collapsed when Kamehameha III died in February 1855; the succeeding prince opposed it. A reciprocity treaty signed at Washington on July 20, 1855, also went unratified. After the diplomatic post was upgraded to minister resident in 1863 (James McBride appointed), the Civil War deferred reciprocity talks. In 1867 McCook was instructed to revive the 1855 treaty on more liberal terms; a treaty concluded at San Francisco on May 21 won presidential approval, and Hawaii ratified it July 30, 1867, but the Senate rejected it June 1, 1870. Seward authorized annexation overtures through Minister Harris and held annexation preferable to reciprocity. The presence of the U.S.S. Lackawanna delayed the King's ratification.

Taking the presidential oath, the speaker invokes divine wisdom, pledges faithful service to the Constitution and Union, and notes that the recent election’s intense divisions quickly gave way to calm acceptance of the majority’s decision. Declining to seek reelection, he says his sole motive will be to serve the country.

On slavery in the territories, he supports popular sovereignty: Congress should neither impose nor prohibit slavery but allow territorial residents to determine their own institutions, subject to the Constitution. He considers the timing of Kansas’s decision a judicial matter pending before the Supreme Court, while personally favoring action by actual residents. He pledges protection of every resident’s right to an independent vote and urges an end to agitation over slavery, warning that its continuation threatens domestic security, alienates the states, and endangers the Union. He also rejects measuring the Union solely through material interests, emphasizing instead the prosperity, peace, and liberty preserved by free trade and continued union.

The speaker identifies corruption as a major threat to republican government. He attributes it partly to an unprecedented treasury surplus, which encourages wasteful spending and speculative schemes. He proposes using the surplus for national purposes, including reducing the public debt, strengthening the Navy, and defending the coasts, while maintaining tariffs sufficient for economical government but avoiding preferential treatment. He advocates reserving public lands primarily for actual settlers at moderate prices while recognizing immigrants as equal citizens after naturalization.

Affirming a strict construction of federal power, he nevertheless finds congressional authority under the war-making power to construct a military road when absolutely necessary to defend the Union, particularly California and the Pacific possessions.

Finally, he calls for peace, commerce, friendship, respect for other nations’ independence, avoidance of entangling alliances, and fair treatment in international dealings. He supports territorial expansion only through justice and honor, emphasizing that prior acquisitions brought civil and religious liberty and equal laws to their inhabitants.

On February 16, 2016, Apple Inc. entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated for nine series of notes: $500 million each of floating-rate notes due 2019 and 2021; and fixed-rate notes of $500 million at 1.300% due 2018, $1 billion at 1.700% due 2019, $2.25 billion at 2.250% due 2021, $1.5 billion at 2.850% due 2023, $2 billion at 3.250% due 2026, $1.25 billion at 4.500% due 2036, and $2.5 billion at 4.650% due 2046. The notes were issued under Apple’s April 29, 2013 indenture and registration statement. Floating-rate interest is payable quarterly; fixed-rate interest is payable semiannually. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of notes, legal opinion, and earnings-to-fixed-charges computation.

Synaptics announced plans to mass-produce Clear ID, an optical in-display fingerprint sensor for bezel-less smartphones. The company says it unlocks twice as fast as 3D facial recognition, works from any angle, and requires one touch, though no smartphone release date was given.

Bemidji’s Lumberjacks defeated Thief River Falls 77-45 after leading 45-25 at halftime. Caden Rolfes scored 18, Linaes Whiting 17, Caleb Carlson 14, and Jeremy Beberg 10. Coach Travis Peterson called the 32-point win a major step forward before Saturday’s matchup with top-ranked Section 8AAA team Fergus Falls.

The passage explains how to design modular, reusable containers and major distributed-system patterns. A container’s API includes its parameters, service calls, and HTTP or other interfaces; stable APIs and image documentation through Dockerfile `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL` directives help prevent subtle breaking changes and support reuse.

Single-node patterns include sidecars, which augment applications; ambassadors, which broker external interactions, route requests to shards, perform service discovery, and split traffic; and adapters, which normalize monitoring, logging, and health-check interfaces for heterogeneous applications without modifying third-party containers. Kubernetes examples demonstrate these patterns with Redis, Prometheus, Fluentd, MySQL, nginx, StatefulSets, Services, and ConfigMaps.

Microservices are presented as loosely coupled components communicating through stable APIs, enabling independent team workflows and scaling but making debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns include replicated stateless services behind load balancers, using readiness probes, session tracking, caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services divide data among shards routed by deterministic, uniform hashing; careful shard-key selection and consistent hashing minimize remapping, while replicated shards and autoscaling address failures and hot traffic. Scatter/gather distributes requests across leaves for parallel processing and combines partial results, though overhead, stragglers, and failure probabilities limit scaling, motivating replication of each shard. The passage concludes by introducing event-driven, function-as-a-service, and serverless architectures.

FSU President John Thrasher appointed a 15-member advisory panel to review university policies on campus names, markers and statues and recommend changes. Renisha Gibbs and the chief diversity officer will co-chair. The committee will seek community input and hold open public meetings. Its work follows calls to remove Confederate designations and includes scrutiny of Francis Eppes, whom SDS supporters say should not be honored because he supported slavery and the Confederacy.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is NVIDIA’s eighth-generation data center accelerator, built on the Ampere GA100 architecture for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Manufactured using TSMC’s 7nm N7 process, GA100 contains 54.2 billion transistors in a die size of 826 mm². The A100 implementation has 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, IEEE-compliant FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data. A100 delivers up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance. Compared with Tesla V100, TF32 operations are up to 10 times faster, or 20 times faster with sparsity; FP16/FP32 operations are 2.5 times faster, or 5 times faster with sparsity; BF16/FP32 runs at the FP16/FP32 rate; sparse INT8 is up to 20 times faster; and FP64 performance is 2.5 times higher.

A100 introduces fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that permits two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse matrix operations skip zero entries, doubling Tensor Core throughput while compressing weight storage and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA describes a process of dense training, structured pruning, and fine-tuning that produces virtually no inference-accuracy loss across numerous evaluated networks.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s read bandwidth, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. Asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and Compute Data Compression improve data movement, latency, power consumption, and memory bandwidth.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, quality-of-service guarantees, and fault isolation. MIG supports multi-tenant cloud deployments, multiple Compute Instances and MPS clients, and migration of compatible virtual GPUs between instances.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate GPU-to-GPU bandwidth. A100 systems can scale through NVSwitch, Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet, and other high-speed interconnects. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s bandwidth, while SR-IOV permits PCIe sharing and virtualization. Additional hardware includes fault detection and containment, hardware JPEG decoding, an optical-flow accelerator, improved atomic operations, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, asynchronous copy and barriers, and L2 cache controls. CUDA Task Graphs support define-once, repeated execution and reduce launch overhead. NVIDIA also provides CUDA-X libraries, GPU-optimized containers through NVIDIA GPU Cloud, and Kubernetes support for scaling training and inference deployments.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and as many as 56 isolated MIG accelerators. It is intended for large-scale AI infrastructure and includes an NGC-based software stack with containers, frameworks, models, Helm charts, and SDKs for deep learning, analytics, and HPC.

Essential FAA and TSA employees are working without pay during the government shutdown, worsening staffing shortages and strain across air traffic systems, maintenance, and airport operations. Workers remain confident aviation is safe but expect prolonged disruption, delays, and cancellations. The FAA says it will slow traffic when staffing constraints arise and that safety-critical positions, including controllers, are exempt from mass firings, though Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has threatened employees who do not report to work. Workers also fear political retaliation, weakened unions, and consequences for missing work because unpaid employees may lack commuting funds. The shutdown has halted some projects and may lead to furloughs among aviation contractors.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna expects nearly 3,000 participants for marathon, half marathon, 10K and newly timed 5K events along Okanagan Lake. Saturday includes a free 3K friendship run and a children’s 1K event; the longer races occur Sunday. The event features a team supporting transplant recipient Andrew Brownell, Olympic race walker Mat Bilodeau and fundraising for the Sunshine Foundation of Canada.

The disclosure describes robotic- and navigation-assisted surgical tool assemblies and methods for preparing vertebral anatomy and placing pedicle screws. It addresses limitations of manually placed K-wires and current robotic systems, including instrument interchange, advancement within bone, and tracking errors caused by vertebral movement during discectomy and cage placement.

Removable drive couplers connect interchangeable working tools—including scalpels, depth probes, dilators, burs, drills, tap drills, and tap inserters—to manual, powered, freehand, or robotic input devices. One coupler transfers torque and uses complementary mating and locking features so tools can be exchanged without disconnecting the coupler; another permits semimanual axial or rotational movement while a manipulator constrains other motion. Depth markings indicate insertion depth.

Working tools may be carried within a stiff elongate sleeve that dilates and retracts overlying tissue. A closed, tapered or flexible-tab distal end limits tissue ingress and opens when the tool advances. Bone-penetrating spikes can anchor the sleeve in vertebral bone, supporting subsequent drilling and tap-marker placement while limiting lateral tool movement. A drive coupler may be removed while a working tool remains secured in bone.

Navigation features include touch-off points and removable trackers with detectable markers for determining tool position and orientation and relocalizing vertebrae after movement. A tracker may magnetically couple to a tap marker and use a ratcheting mechanism for unidirectional rotation. In the described screw-placement methods, controllers align a screw and coaxial sleeve with a planned trajectory, advance both through soft tissue, and then advance the screw relative to the sleeve into the vertebral body; screw advancement can open the sleeve’s flexible distal feature.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 27, 2022, reporting its issuance of a press release covering financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021. The press release was included as Exhibit 99.1. The report stated that its contents were not deemed filed under Section 18 or incorporated by reference except by specific reference. It was signed by Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural deaths involving tourists from Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Pravin Sundaram, 28, collapsed after a rave party near Vagator; Abdul died after being brought to hospital by an unknown person. Both bodies were sent for autopsy, with viscera preserved to determine the causes. Police have not ruled out drug overdose. A minister urged authorities to curb outdoor parties and drug-related activity.

A New York Medicaid advisory board unanimously recommended pausing coverage of Sarepta’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy drug Elevidys amid safety concerns. It advised waiting for the FDA to add safety and clinical-trial data to the labeling and evaluating a forthcoming regimen intended to reduce liver-failure risk. Some patients under 21 may still receive case-by-case coverage when medically necessary.

The team remains confident after a 5–3 playoff loss and is focusing on Wednesday’s decisive game. They praised their goaltender and plan to rely on their successful road approach: forechecking, putting pucks deep, closing gaps, and staying consistent. Players are excited but businesslike, preparing on the ice while looking forward to playing before their home crowd.

The St. John’s Edge defeated the London Lightning 123–110 in Game 4 of the NBL Canada Central Division final, tying the best-of-seven series 2–2. Game 5 is Thursday in St. John’s, with Game 6 scheduled for Sunday in London. The Edge played with greater intensity and won the battle in the paint 50–38, while London committed 13 missed free throws. Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams scored 28 points each for St. John’s, Ryan Reid added 22, and Alex Johnson’s insertion at guard provided quickness and distribution. London was led by Royce White with 32 points and Ryan Anderson with 21.

Lightning coach Keith Vassell accepted responsibility for his team’s preparation and said he would reconsider limiting the bench. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap made adjustments and expected the series to last seven games. White and Anderson also briefly tugged at each other after a dispute. Separately, the league investigated a complaint alleging White used a homophobic slur during Game 3; reports differed on what was said, and officials said they heard nothing.

A Carpool Karaoke-style video of mothers and children with Down’s syndrome signing in Makaton to Christina Perri’s “A Thousand Years” drew praise from Perri and James Corden and more than 600,000 views. Created for World Down’s Syndrome Day, it aimed to change perceptions of people with the condition.

This qualitative case study examined Turkish teachers’ experiences with pandemic-era distance education and technological tools used in Turkish-language courses. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 Turkish teachers serving grades 5–8 in Hazro, Diyarbakır, and responses were analyzed descriptively.

Teachers reported that education continued despite Turkey’s initial lack of preparedness, and EBA and EBA TV were viewed as useful resources. Nevertheless, none of the participants considered distance education fully efficient; most described it as insufficiently effective compared with face-to-face instruction. Target behaviors and achievements were partially achieved primarily because students lacked internet access, devices, materials, or regular attendance. Additional difficulties included parents supervising multiple school-age children, disconnections during lessons, infrastructure gaps in rural areas, and limited time for completing planned activities.

For Turkish lessons, teachers emphasized access to reading books and dictionaries, technological materials, and activities supporting reading, writing, listening, and speaking. Phones were the most-used communication tools, followed by WhatsApp, Zoom, and EBA. Recommended teacher competencies included subject knowledge, activity-based planning, communication skills, attention to individual differences, and effective technology use.

Recommendations included resolving infrastructure and material shortages, ensuring equal educational access, updating EBA content, supporting reading activities, expanding teacher professional development, redesigning learning targets, and retaining distance education as an auxiliary to face-to-face teaching. Cooperation among teachers, students, and parents was considered essential.

Topshop recalled all till display stands nationwide after 10-year-old Kaden Reddick suffered fatal head injuries in an incident involving a display barrier at its Reading store. Police continue investigating, with Reading Borough Council assisting.

The speaker calls the transfer of power a moment of unity and urges Americans to seize an opportunity to become peacemakers. Reflecting on national achievements in science, industry, education, prosperity, and freedom, he contrasts material abundance with a spiritual crisis marked by war, division, discord, and empty lives. He advocates simpler virtues such as kindness, decency, love, and lower voices, along with government action and widespread citizen participation to address social needs, including housing, employment, education, environmental protection, and economic security.

He emphasizes that progress requires black and white Americans to advance together and that laws must be matched by equal dignity and opportunity. Abroad, he promotes negotiation, open communication, peaceful competition, reduced arms burdens, cooperation, and sustained diplomacy, while maintaining necessary strength. Concluding with the Apollo astronauts’ view of Earth as a shared home, he frames humanity’s future as a common responsibility and presents the dawning era as an opportunity for collective action, peace, and moral renewal.

The FDA announced a nationwide crackdown on illegal Juul sales to minors, including undercover inspections of stores and online retailers. Since March, compliance checks found 40 violations, prompting 40 warning letters, with more actions planned. The FDA contacted eBay, which removed Juul listings, and requested documents from Juul and similar manufacturers to determine why their products appeal to youth; noncompliance could bring enforcement. The agency also plans action against misleading marketing, youth education campaigns, and research into making tobacco products less toxic, addictive, and appealing.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger and her husband, Christian, bought a 160-acre property near Merrickville in the 1970s and created the Carrigliath arboretum and organic garden, filled with rare plants and trees. After losing her family at age 11, she was raised with old Irish teachings about nature and later studied botany, biochemistry, and related sciences. The couple’s “expotitions” catalog and preserve rare local species threatened by development. A noted author and international speaker, Beresford-Kroeger wrote and narrated the Canadian-made documentary “Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees,” which examines deforestation and climate change. Her Bioplan proposes that each person plant one tree annually for six years, potentially reducing atmospheric carbon dioxide from 400 to 300 parts per million. The film has drawn large audiences, received award nominations, and was scheduled for European premieres.

Ravita Meghwar, now Gulnaz Shah, says she voluntarily eloped, converted to Islam, and married a Muslim man. Her family alleges that kidnappers drugged and abducted her and forced her conversion. Her case reflects concerns among Hindus in Sindh, where activists and families report an organized pattern of minor girls being abducted, coerced into converting, and married to Muslim men. Muslim religious leaders counter that these conversions are voluntary and blessed, often supported by shrines, seminaries, clerics, and local politicians.

Forced conversions became a national issue in 2012 after three Hindu girls were reportedly converted and married; the Supreme Court allowed them to remain with their husbands. Sindh passed a 2016 law against forced conversion and conversion before age 18, but opposition from hardline religious groups led the governor to withhold approval. Lawyers are instead using Sindh’s ban on underage marriage in cases involving girls, though judges have generally allowed them to live with their husbands without examining alleged coercion.

The issue has intensified Hindu unease about their place in Pakistan, a Muslim state where minorities have limited influence and Islamic nationalist groups are powerful. Some Hindus are moving from villages to cities or emigrating to India, although migration figures are largely anecdotal; one estimate puts emigration at 5,000 annually. Mass conversions also involve Hindu families, particularly lower-caste and low-income Hindus. Activists attribute the growing movement partly to the legacy of General Zia-ul-Haq’s Islamicization policies, while its precise origins remain unclear.

The author argues that expanding employment, internships, and apprenticeship opportunities for disconnected and “opportunity” youth can improve academic, social, and economic outcomes and benefit communities. Recalling his own high-school disengagement, he says a lifeguard job helped him maintain a 4.0 GPA, connect classroom learning to real life, develop responsibility, and gain confidence and purpose. Citing research, the passage says youth employment can reduce delinquency, improve academic performance and college enrollment, strengthen social development, and reduce interaction with the criminal justice system.

The author notes that many young people, including African American peers, struggle to find work or internships, while transportation and scheduling create additional barriers. He urges governments and policymakers to provide incentives for businesses, highlights state tax-credit and transportation initiatives, and criticizes Nevada’s failure to advance funding for NEETs.

The speaker says the coach has the character to become a head coach, is tough but honest and clear, and demands hard work. He calls the opposition’s defense and depth a serious but familiar challenge, while expressing excitement about his team’s long-awaited opportunity and shared goal, tempered by the work ahead. He praises Canadian fan support and expects Ottawa’s arena to create an intense atmosphere like Edmonton’s. He commends modern players’ play-reading and athletic goalies, and highlights his team’s forward depth, especially its productive younger lines and Pohlsner’s line. On age and recognition, he says he feels similar to younger teammates and attributes “Giggy’s” limited exposure to the smaller market.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on August 1, 2017, reporting financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended July 1, 2017. The filing attached Apple’s press release and related data sheet as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The information was furnished, not deemed filed, and not incorporated by reference except when expressly cited. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

Saturday-night entertainment has long been a major ratings battle between BBC1 and ITV, but launching successful new shows in the slot is extremely difficult. Established favourites such as Casualty, Strictly and The X Factor dominate, while most new programmes fail; The Voice UK is a recent moderate success. The BBC and ITV have repeatedly revived Saturday-night audiences by replacing declining shows with new formats. Although ratings are not easily achieved, the rewards can be substantial, as demonstrated by Strictly’s success and international production. Ultimately, formats and hosts can become stale, audiences gradually leave, and channel controllers must rely on instinct, producers’ track records and hope to find the next hit.
