Combination defenses aim to deny touches to outstanding offensive players and serve as surprise tactics, with timing and surprise being key to their success. The most common is the "Box and One," in which four defenders play a box zone while one "Chaser" applies full pass denial to the opponent's top scorer. The "Diamond and One" uses a diamond zone alignment matched to a single guard front; it effectively takes away the middle but gives up the corners. Less common but devastating to unprepared teams, the "Triangle and Two" works against two outstanding scorers, can change up the defense to catch opponents off guard, and can be used at the end of a game to hold the ball.

Researchers found pre-existing psychiatric or substance use disorders, psychoactive medication use, and harmful opioid-related outcomes predicted greater risk of long-term opioid use. Among 10.3 million patients with opioid claims, 1.7% became long-term users; risk reached nearly ninefold among those with prior opioid use disorders.

Facing AfD gains in Bavaria and pressure from Interior Minister Horst Seehofer, Chancellor Angela Merkel agreed to establish transit camps along the German-Austrian border. Rejected asylum seekers would be returned to their countries of origin or, absent an agreement, to Austria, though Austria has opposed accepting them. The move has unsettled coalition partner the SPD, which had previously rejected similar proposals. Merkel’s three-party coalition with the SPD and CDU/CSU was nevertheless renewed. The dispute reflects broader European divisions over migration, with several countries refusing to accept migrants and Austria threatening reciprocal expulsions that could undermine the EU’s open-border system.

Dallas’s coach attributes the loss to the team’s own third-period mistakes, especially poor puck support that led to odd-man rushes. He says Dallas played two strong periods but became frustrated as the game tightened, taking unnecessary risks with long passes and attempts to score quickly. He believes the errors are correctable, expects the players and leaders to respond, and says the immediate focus is winning the next game rather than considering three consecutive victories.

New Jersey is described as fast, physically strong, committed to structured defense, and supported by a smart, composed goaltender. The coach notes that the Devils won two close games by sustaining their defensive intensity and capitalizing on Dallas mistakes. He also observes that Dallas was fortunate to win their earlier overtime meeting and that this situation differs from previous comeback series because the opposing goaltender has performed well.

The coach emphasizes that scoring chances matter more than shot totals and that Dallas must remain disciplined, make short passes, stay within the team system, and eliminate odd-man rushes. He says defensive consistency has deteriorated when the playoff intensity rises and compares this series with the Colorado series, where Dallas became too passive while protecting a large lead. Players such as Modano and Carbonneau are urged to remain within their roles rather than chase an immediate goal.

He believes the team must raise its level, accept the physical and mental demands of playoff hockey, and draw passion from its captains and dressing room. He praises the players’ desire to continue, expresses confidence in a strong response, and describes the current challenge as difficult but manageable.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data-center accelerator built on the Ampere GA100 architecture using TSMC’s 7nm N7 process. The GA100 contains 54.2 billion transistors in a 826 mm² die. The A100 implementation has 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. It targets AI, high-performance computing, and data-analytics workloads across workstations, servers, clusters, edge systems, and supercomputers.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, IEEE FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. A100 provides up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance, 2.5 times V100’s mixed-precision throughput and five times when sparsity is enabled. TF32 operations run up to 10 times faster than V100 FP32 operations, while FP64 performance is 2.5 times V100’s and sparse INT8 performance is up to 20 times greater. A100’s 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity skips zero-valued matrix entries, doubling Tensor Core throughput and halving weight storage and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA provides a pruning and fine-tuning process for sparse inference that reportedly causes virtually no accuracy loss across numerous tested networks.

A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s read bandwidth, and ECC protection across major memory structures. Its SMs provide 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory, separate FP32 and INT32 pipelines, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, warp-level reduction instructions, and L2 cache residency controls. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to four times and L2 capacity by up to two times.

Multi-Instance GPU technology can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute, cache, and memory resources. These provide quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, and security for containers, virtual machines, and processes. GPU instances can contain multiple compute instances supporting simultaneous contexts and MPS, and virtual GPUs can be migrated between compatible instances or physical GPUs.

For multi-GPU scaling, A100 provides 12 third-generation NVLink links totaling 600 GB/s, plus PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s x16 bandwidth and SR-IOV support. It is compatible with NVSwitch, NVIDIA Magnum IO, and Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet networking. CUDA 11 adds support for task graphs, asynchronous copies, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, sparsity, MIG, and expanded Cooperative Groups operations. A100 also includes a five-core NVJPG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator, improved atomic operations, and five NVDEC units.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, 4.8 TB/s bidirectional internal bandwidth, and eight 200 Gb/s Mellanox ConnectX-6 adapters. It can expose up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators and scale to thousands of systems using NVIDIA networking and software, including NGC, DeepOps, Kubernetes, and Slurm.

The lecture presents detection through a deliberately simplified binary communication system: one bit is encoded, modulated, corrupted by noise, demodulated, sampled, and classified as zero or one. This one-shot model ignores sequences of bits and intersymbol interference. Shannon’s approach is illustrated as the basis for the method: solve simple theoretical “toy problems” first, then add practical constraints while retaining understanding of the underlying solution. This makes theoretical analysis the foundation for practical engineering.

For a known probabilistic model, the optimal equal-cost detector uses maximum a posteriori probability decoding: after observing \(v\), it selects the hypothesis with the largest posterior probability. With binary hypotheses, this is a threshold test based on the likelihood ratio
\[
\Lambda(v)=\frac{p(v\mid H=0)}{p(v\mid H=1)}.
\]
Comparing \(\Lambda(v)\) with the prior-probability threshold \(\eta=p_1/p_0\) minimizes error probability. The likelihood ratio is a sufficient statistic: once calculated, the original likelihoods need not be retained.

For binary antipodal signaling in Gaussian noise, zero and one are represented by \(+a\) and \(-a\), with noise variance \(N_0/2\). The likelihood ratio becomes \(e^{4av/N_0}\), so MAP detection reduces to comparing \(v\) with \(N_0\ln(\eta)/(4a)\). With equally likely symbols, the threshold is zero, and the error probability is
\[
Q\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{2E_b}{N_0}}\right).
\]
For non-antipodal signals, error probability depends only on the separation of the two signal points; shifting them away from their mean increases energy per bit without improving error probability. Such an offset or pilot signal can therefore waste energy, with the example given costing 3 dB.

The lecture then extends antipodal detection to vectors in white Gaussian noise. The sufficient statistic becomes the inner product between the received vector and the transmitted signal vector. A matched filter computes this inner product for waveforms, after which the scalar binary threshold rule is applied. Geometrically, the MAP or maximum-likelihood decision boundary is a plane perpendicular to the line between the two antipodal signal vectors, and the earlier scalar Gaussian error analysis applies after projection.

The NPD Group has identified five trends shaping Britain's £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018: click & collect, staff investment, personalized VIP loyalty schemes, reliable brand promises, and tailored recommendations. Click & collect via smartphones is expected to drive adoption among tech-savvy millennials and Generation-Z consumers, cutting order and wait times while boosting sales, profits and customer data, and requiring efficient fulfillment, possible layout changes and staff training, plus use to drive off-peak traffic. Operators that nurture, train and retain staff gain customer satisfaction, loyalty and commercial advantage. Customers now expect tiered, exclusive loyalty offers and occasional surprises. Operators must align product quality, service and marketing with promises to protect repeat business and avoid social media complaints. Staff recommendations combined with customer data can tailor suggestions to mood, diet or occasion. Cyril Lavenant, NPD Group's UK Foodservice Director, emphasized innovation and never over-promising or under-delivering.

Three chemists, including a UC Berkeley chemist, Susumu Kitagawa and Richard Robson, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks. The room-like structures can harvest water or store toxic gases; more than 100,000 have since been created.

Horse dealers Koster et al. sued Koedding for a horse’s price. The trial court found that he had received and accepted the horse, rejecting his claim that a 30-day trial had been agreed and that the statute of frauds applied. His warranty-breach defense also failed. The horse was used and returned before dying shortly afterward. Judgment for the plaintiffs was affirmed with costs.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020 reported Q3 net sales of $96.145 billion, up from $69.981 billion, including $52.774 billion in product sales and $43.371 billion in service sales. Operating income rose to $6.194 billion from $3.157 billion, and net income increased to $6.331 billion from $2.134 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $12.37, compared with $4.23. For the first nine months, net sales were $260.509 billion, operating income was $16.026 billion, and net income was $14.109 billion.

Cash provided by operating activities was $11.964 billion in Q3 and $35.633 billion for the first nine months. Investing activities used $15.876 billion and $42.574 billion, respectively, while financing activities used $4.105 billion in Q3 and provided $712 million for the nine months. At September 30, 2020, Amazon had $29.930 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $38.472 billion of marketable securities, $282.179 billion of total assets, $32.929 billion of long-term debt, and $82.775 billion of stockholders’ equity.

Amazon changed the estimated useful life of its servers from three to four years effective January 1, 2020. For Q3, this reduced depreciation and amortization by $634 million and increased net income by $479 million; for the first nine months, the reductions were $2.1 billion and $1.6 billion, respectively.

Q3 segment sales were $59.373 billion in North America, $25.171 billion internationally, and $11.601 billion for AWS. Operating income was $2.252 billion, $407 million, and $3.535 billion, respectively; International had shifted from a $386 million operating loss in Q3 2019 to positive operating income. For the first nine months, North America, International, and AWS sales were $160.936 billion, $66.945 billion, and $32.628 billion.

COVID-19 increased demand for household staples, essential goods, and home products but also created fulfillment constraints and higher costs. Amazon hired more than 250,000 employees beginning in February 2020 and incurred over $2.5 billion of COVID-19-related costs in Q3, totaling more than $7.5 billion for the first three quarters.

As of September 30, Amazon had $32.2 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, including $10 billion issued in June 2020, $725 million of commercial paper borrowings, and $413 million outstanding under its secured credit facility. Total contractual commitments were $180.992 billion. Amazon reported no common-stock repurchases during the first nine months of 2019 or 2020. It also disclosed approximately $3.0 billion of tax contingencies and resolved its IRS audits for 2007 through 2012 at amounts materially consistent with its accrual.

This patent application (a continuation of U.S. patent applications Ser. No. 16/867,034, 16/405,377, and 15/834,939, claiming benefit of Provisional Ser. No. 62/433,204) concerns systems and methods for plasma processing of substrates, specifically for creating arbitrarily shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDFs) using shaped-pulse bias.

Background: In a typical reactive ion etch chamber, an RF bias generator supplies RF voltage to a power electrode embedded in the electrostatic chuck (ESC). The non-linear, diode-like plasma sheath rectifies the applied RF field, producing a DC self-bias between cathode and plasma that determines average ion energy, ion directionality, feature profile, and selectivity. With RF bias, the IEDF typically has two peaks, with an intermediate ion population reflecting oscillation of the cathode-to-plasma voltage drop. Low-frequency bias (e.g., 2 MHz) yields a significant energy difference between peaks; low-energy ions etch more isotropically and can cause feature wall bowing, while high-energy ions better reach feature corners but sputter masks more.

A special shaped-pulse bias scheme maintains a nearly constant sheath voltage: a periodic series of short positive pulses on a negative DC offset, keeping sheath and substrate voltage constant for about 90% of each bias cycle. The waveform includes a positive jump to remove charge accumulated on the chuck capacitance, a negative jump (V_OUT) that sets the sheath voltage (V_SH) and is divided between chuck and sheath capacitances, and a negative voltage ramp that compensates for ion current during the ion current compensation phase. Other waveforms may substitute a constant-voltage phase when chuck capacitance greatly exceeds sheath capacitance.

Summary of embodiments: One method applies shaped-pulse bias while modulating the amplitude of the negative voltage jump (and hence V_SH) in a predetermined manner so the relative number of pulses at each amplitude determines the relative ion fraction at the corresponding ion energy. Other embodiments use the described waveform with an ion-compensation ramp having a more negative slope (overcompensating for ion current) or a less negative slope (undercompensating).

Detailed description: A substrate processing system includes a substrate support assembly with a pedestal, power electrode, and ceramic layer, plus a bias supply (and optionally a controller) with memory and processor for controlling electrode voltage. Ion energy is controlled by modulating the amplitude and frequency of the shaped-pulse signal using bursts of pulses and trains of bursts, repeated over a process step, with on/off phases set by duty cycle and burst frequency. The relative number of bursts at each amplitude sets the ion fraction at that energy; examples include a train of three high-amplitude bursts and one low-amplitude burst ("HHHL") for a two-peak IEDF with 75%/25% split, and "HML" for three equal peaks. A single burst of one amplitude yields a single-peak, mono-energetic IEDF. Overcompensation produces a wider, double-peaked IEDF whose width is set by minimum and maximum wafer voltage jumps (V_min, V_max), offering greater precision than mixing two RF frequencies; undercompensation produces a wider, single-peaked IEDF. Wider IEDFs can benefit high-aspect-ratio hard-mask open etching. Flow diagrams outline methods of applying a negative jump to set wafer voltage, optionally preceded by a positive jump to neutralize the wafer surface, followed by a ramp that overcompensates or undercompensates for ion current.
The Fourth Circuit affirmed the district court’s denial of Nagy’s Rule 60(b) motion, finding no reversible error.

A Kazakh man died and another was hospitalized after falling debris from a Russian Soyuz 2.1a launch triggered a steppe fire near Zhezkazgan. Roscosmos cited extreme heat and strong winds; both men were clearing debris for NPO Mashinostroyeniya.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces doubled FP32 throughput, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X support, PCIe Gen 4, third-generation NVLink, and concurrent graphics, ray tracing, and compute processing. The full GA102 GPU contains 28.3 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, 84 Streaming Multiprocessors, 112 ROPs, and a 384-bit memory subsystem with 6 MB of L2 cache. Its SMs support FP32 and INT32 operations on separate datapaths, while larger unified L1/shared-memory capacity improves bandwidth. RTX 3080 delivers 30 shader TFLOPS, 58 RT TFLOPS, and 238 sparse Tensor TFLOPS.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads, and accelerate motion blur on moving or deforming geometry. Third-generation Tensor Cores add structured sparsity, TF32, and BF16 support, doubling effective throughput for supported sparse workloads and accelerating AI denoising, DLSS, Broadcast, and Canvas.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to reach 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s peak bandwidth. RTX IO, working with DirectStorage, moves compressed asset loading and decompression to the GPU, reducing CPU demands and improving I/O performance. The RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24 GB of GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA Cores; the RTX 3070 uses GA104 without NVLink and ships with GDDR6.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing with 48 GB of GDDR6, PCIe Gen 4, vGPU support, and NVLink scalability to 96 GB. The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB for professional workstations and can combine two boards for 96 GB. Ampere GPUs also support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 for high-resolution displays, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 decoding, seventh-generation NVENC, and GDDR6X error detection and replay. NVIDIA reports up to 1.9x greater power efficiency than Turing at equivalent performance.

The Princeton Offense is an unstructured, motion-based team system popularized by Pete Carril. It relies on constant movement, defensive reads, patient ball control, counteractions, and back-door cuts, with all five players involved. Success requires outside shooting, passing and driving with either hand, court savvy, unselfishness, and strong conditioning. Coaches must be fully committed because player freedom can initially reduce their sense of control.

The offense typically starts in a 2-3 high-post alignment and proceeds through three phases: entries, constant exchanges and down screens, and post action following a high-post basket cut. Entries include guard rubs, mid screens, dribble clears, zipper passes, and high-post actions. Players must maintain 12- to 15-foot spacing to spread the defense, limit help, and create passing and post opportunities.

Tempo is controlled through patient, safe passing, often 15 to 20 passes per possession, while remaining alert for transition opportunities. Back cuts are the signature counter to defensive overplays and lapses. Dribbling is used sparingly for spacing, exchanges, counters, and special actions, although players may drive when advantageous. Post-ups mainly collapse the defense for kick-out passes. Quick-hitting sets address late shot-clock or end-of-period situations. Teams must prepare for presses and 2-on-1 or 3-on-2 opportunities. The low-possession, motion-heavy approach can pressure opponents through fatigue and turnovers while remaining consistent and relatively independent of shooting results.

The team said its road performance provided a huge boost, praising four-line play, strong skating and clogging the neutral zone. A confident scorer’s excellent first period set the tone. Hoping to continue that style at home in Edmonton, the team aims for another win to force a game. It disputed being outplayed in the third period, noting the opposition had only two shots.

Bertie Secor, as administrator of John S. Secor’s estate, sued James and Elizabeth Siver to enforce a deficiency judgment and enjoin their alleged fraudulent conveyances of Iowa town properties to their sons. After a temporary injunction was issued before the deeds were recorded, the trial court dismissed the petition. James and Elizabeth counterclaimed that John Secor fraudulently induced their exchange of a New York house and lot for a farm, misrepresenting its orchard, soil, house, sawmill, timber, pasture, and $3,500 value.

The majority held that competency objections must state specific grounds. A general assertion that witnesses were “incompetent and unqualified” was insufficient, while an objection based on personal “transactions” with the deceased did not necessarily encompass distinct personal “communications.” James and Elizabeth remained competent to describe the properties, state their reliance on the representations, describe the property’s condition, and report conversations they did not participate in. The court found sufficient admissible evidence to create a factual issue and concluded that the Sivers were grossly overreached in the exchange. It affirmed the dismissal and the taxation of costs against the administratrix in her official capacity.

Judge Stevens, joined by Judges Ladd and Salinger, dissented, arguing that the objection sufficiently invoked the deceased-person statute because the witnesses participated in the challenged communications and transactions, requiring reversal.

Volunteer surveys led by Waterwatch across southern New South Wales and the ACT are collecting baseline data on the elusive, near-threatened platypus. In the Upper Murrumbidgee River near Cooma, volunteers have surveyed the same five-kilometre stretch for four years, providing the area’s only formal platypus monitoring; results indicate stable numbers. One outing found no platypus but recorded a native water rat, a nationally declining species. Citizen-science sightings could support conservation as platypus decline in eastern Australia and Tasmania due to habitat change, reduced river flows, carp, and discarded fishing gear and traps. Waterwatch encourages residents to report sightings and advises searching in August and September, early morning or late evening, for ripples, bubbles, a rounded back or concentric rings.

A coach reviews a playoff win over Boston: out-muscled in the second period, his team adjusted its work ethic and dominated the late stages of that period and the third, with the Twins line wearing down Boston's defense to tie the game before an overtime goal — rare for Boston to give up a lead. He praises a key forward who plays five-on-five, on the power play and kills penalties, and Manny, back in the lineup, for strong faceoffs and a scoring chance.

With much at stake, the club keeps lineup information private, as the NFL does, to prevent opponents exploiting players' traits; he jokes it took three years to tell twins Danny and Henrik apart.

A player returning from a long injury will be eased in for faceoffs and defensive situations, but not with his old linemates, since the Torres-Lapiere-Hansen line is playing well. He wants fewer offensive-zone penalties and a stronger power play.

The lecture reviews Wald’s identity for a random walk formed from IID increments. For a stopping time \(J\) when the walk crosses an upper or lower threshold, the identity extends the moment-generating-function calculation for a fixed endpoint to a stopping time. Using Markov’s inequality, the probability of crossing an upper threshold \(\alpha\) is bounded by \(e^{-\alpha r^*}\), where \(r^*\) is a second root of the increment’s moment-generating function. This root is identified as a key parameter for threshold-crossing probabilities.

The lecture then connects random walks to sequential hypothesis testing. Posterior odds equal prior odds multiplied by a likelihood ratio, leading to the MAP threshold rule. Taking logarithms turns the likelihood ratio into a sum of IID variables under one hypothesis, so sequential testing becomes a random-walk threshold problem. A sufficient statistic is any statistic from which the likelihood ratio can be calculated. Fixed-sample error probabilities are related through Chernoff bounds and the Neyman–Pearson tradeoff between the two kinds of error.

Sequential tests prespecify upper and lower stopping thresholds, select a hypothesis when one is crossed, and balance error probability against expected sample size. This procedure is compared with automatic repeat request in communications. Wald’s equality is used to express expected stopping time in terms of expected log-likelihood increments and the stopping boundary.

Differentiating Wald’s identity at \(r=0\) yields Wald’s equality,
\[
E[S_J]=E[J]E[X].
\]
A second derivative, when the increment has zero mean, gives
\[
E[S_J^2]=\sigma_X^2E[J].
\]
For a simple symmetric random walk with thresholds \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta<0\), the expected stopping time is \(-\alpha\beta\).

The lecture introduces a martingale as a sequence whose next conditional expectation, given the entire past, equals its current value. The tower property implies that conditioning only on an earlier term gives that earlier term as the conditional expectation. Examples include zero-mean random walks, sums of dependent increments with zero conditional means, and product martingales with independent unit-mean factors. A “double-or-nothing” product martingale demonstrates that limits and expectations cannot always be interchanged: the capital converges almost surely to zero while expected capital remains one.

Finally, submartingales and supermartingales replace equality with inequalities, and Jensen’s inequality is stated for convex functions:
\[
h(E[Z])\le E[h(Z)].
\]

The passage highlights 10 AI tools for content creation in 2025. ChatGPT supports written content, while Canva Magic Studio generates on-brand graphic and social media designs. RunwayML enables professional video effects and object removal, and Midjourney V6 creates consistent, brand-aligned visuals. Synthesia produces multilingual AI-presenter videos, Descript simplifies audio and video editing with transcription and filler-word removal, and ElevenLabs generates multilingual voiceovers with natural speech, accents, and emotional expression. Tribescaler uses trend analysis to optimize content for virality, Clickable creates platform-optimized advertising variations from brand assets, and CopyAI generates conversion-focused marketing copy across formats. Together, the tools are presented as ways to save time, scale high-quality content, and improve creative workflows. The article notes that creators’ own voices and visions remain essential and that listed features and pricing may change. It also discloses that it contains affiliate links through which the publisher may earn a commission from premium purchases.

Narrow bezels leave smartphone makers seeking room for selfie cameras and sensors. Xiaomi moved components to the bottom, Apple introduced a notch, and Vivo’s Apex concept used a pop-up camera and under-screen fingerprint sensor to eliminate bezels, though its mechanism adds cost and bulk. The passage proposes transparent OLED displays, placing the selfie camera behind the screen and using per-pixel opacity to create transparency only when needed. Video calls may require temporary letterboxing. Transparent OLEDs already exist in televisions and smart windows; the next step is adapting them for smartphones.

The Socket 940 requires molded “SOCKET 940” and directional lock markings, plus a triangular package-orientation symbol that remains visible after mating. Its UL approval symbol and lot traceability mark must remain visible after PCB mounting; the lot mark may be inked, lasered, or impact marked. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy with minimum 1.27 µm nickel plating and 0.76 µm gold on mating areas. SMT attachment uses 0.76 mm tin/lead (63/37 ±5%) balls, 0.64 mm PCB pads, a solder barrier, and 0.20 mm coplanarity. No lubricants may be present on mating areas. A stainless-steel lever provides toolless actuation. Insertion/extraction force must not exceed 2 kgf, closed-position extraction requires at least 0.013 kgf per pin, and lever force must be below 3.6 kgf. Pin displacement must remain below 1.0 mm, and the socket must withstand 50 actuations. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact, less than 30°C temperature rise, and maximum 25 mΩ initial and final LLCR per contact, along with specified inductance, capacitance, impedance, delay, withstand-voltage, and insulation-resistance limits.

A study examined traditional yogurt making with red wood ants in Bulgaria and Turkey. Researchers placed four live ants in warmed raw cow’s milk and buried the jar in an ant mound overnight. Ant- and bacteria-derived lactic and acetic acids, formic acid, and milk-digesting enzymes acidified and thickened the milk into tangy, herbaceous yogurt. Living ants worked better than frozen or dehydrated ants, whose microbes fermented milk less effectively. Researchers cautioned against making yogurt this way at home because live ants can rarely carry parasites that cause liver or gastrointestinal disease.

A hockey player describes unexpectedly being given a chance to contribute during the Stanley Cup Finals after coach Burns expressed belief in him. Recalled from Albany during his third season with the organization, he credited the team’s veterans and playoff experience for keeping him calm and mentally ready. Although he did not expect to score, he felt good and wanted to help in any way, including winning a key draw or delivering a big hit. He praises the team’s depth, the contributions of several players throughout the playoffs, and Marty’s leadership and presence. The team made simple plays that wore down its opponent, while the bench became increasingly chaotic as the game progressed.

Dr. Jesus Jara was selected as Clark County School District superintendent on May 2, 2018, following a contentious, divided vote. He had served as Orange County Public Schools’ deputy superintendent since 2012 after leading Monroe County Public Schools. Jara pledged to work with district staff, listen to the community and advance student achievement. Chief student achievement officer Mike Barton also drew substantial support but was defeated 4–3 before Jara won. Six finalists were interviewed after 77 applications. The board plans negotiations before Jara’s anticipated June start, ahead of retiring superintendent Pat Skorkowsky’s departure.

The TMPM command moves up to 128 SNP guest pages within system physical address space and can replace PAGE_MOVE. A 2M page must consist of physically contiguous 4K pages and be 2M-aligned; noncontiguous 2M pages cannot be directly migrated. DMA is unsupported, and concurrent DMA may be aborted. CPU access must be prevented, typically by making pages non-present. Sources must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, and destinations Pre-Migration; afterward, destinations assume the source states and sources return to Pre-Migration.

For each migration-list entry, firmware validates platform state, addresses, guest context, page states, exclusive RMP access, and matching page sizes. It invalidates and synchronizes the TLB, copies the data, and updates the source and destination RMPs. An end-of-sequence command can request an interrupt on completion.

Command-content errors cause rejection, while migration-list errors may cause partial success. Ring-buffer errors are reported through PM_STATUS; hardware errors appear in command status and/or MCA. On timeout, clients should log an MCA and take corrective action, potentially saving state or terminating VMs. Hardware failure may make an entire batch unrecoverable, though software can save data and system state before reboot.

The passage examines gamification in higher education, applying game mechanisms such as points, levels, feedback, competition, and cooperation to increase motivation, concentration, strategic thinking, and participation. It discusses four projects conducted at the Institute of Pedagogy at the University of Wrocław.

The Kulturalny Wrocław project used a location-based game to combine cultural education with information technology. Teams located cultural sites in Wrocław, exchanged photographs, solved riddles, completed a crossword, and reached a final point. Students rated the game highly for its educational and social value, outdoor setting, autonomy, and reduced hierarchy between students and supervisors. Although some questioned how much content could be covered compared with a regular lesson, participants believed the location-based experience supported lasting knowledge. The game had clear rules, simple mechanics, low costs, and was subsequently incorporated into the curriculum.

A five-day Lower Silesian career-management seminar combined expert lectures with a science-fiction space-mission game. Missions increased in difficulty, while points, badges, prizes, team competition, and a final game-based examination encouraged engagement. Participants achieved high exam results, integrated rapidly, and reported increased self-knowledge and competence in course design. However, instructors emphasized the substantial preparation required and considered the format effective mainly when repeated or externally funded.

The “Become an Entrepreneur” location-based game linked movement, intellectual tasks, simulated money, and entrepreneurship lessons. Teams completed quests, accumulated coins, and avoided symbolic obstacles. Students praised its social character, combination of fun and education, and potential for developing teamwork and other soft skills. Competition and reliance on internet information were viewed ambivalently, while weather, unfamiliar locations, and organizational difficulties were identified as possible weaknesses.

The “Spell of the Black Magic Master” LARP required students to interpret texts, prepare props and costumes, and perform a fantasy scenario to neutralize a spell within 120 minutes. Participants developed negotiation, communication, group-management, and creative skills. Students with previous RPG or LARP experience were more satisfied, while novices struggled with complex rules, role-playing, and group integration. The game’s complexity reduced satisfaction and required extensive preparation and pilot testing.

Overall, educational games should match students’ prior experience, subject matter, available time, and budget. Simple games with clear rules and strategic choices can fit into curricula, while complex games can complement externally funded programs. Longer or more complicated games should include preliminary social activities and tutorials.

Action on Smoking and Health holds the tobacco industry responsible for marketing an addictive, deadly product and argues that no smoking-related deaths are acceptable. It cites the Cape Town Declaration on Human Rights and a Tobacco-Free World, endorsed by more than 150 organizations, and calls for swift action toward a tobacco-free world.

Eddie Woo, a Sydney mathematics teacher at Cherrybrook Technology High School, became an unlikely celebrity after posting classroom videos on YouTube in 2012 for a seriously ill student. His free Wootube channel now has more than 200,000 subscribers and over 12 million views.

In 2018, Woo was named Australia’s Local Hero and became one of 10 finalists for the $1 million Global Teacher Prize. He also became a NSW Department of Education “master teacher”, travelling across the state to mentor students and teachers while retaining his school position.

His energetic approach, which presents mathematics as play, exploration and storytelling, has drawn packed audiences in regional NSW. Education officials praised his ability to explain mathematical complexity and expand the reach of his classroom through technology. Woo sees students who claim they dislike mathematics as a personal mission to inspire. Although his increased fame and busy schedule have strained his time at work and with his family, he says the opportunity to share his enthusiasm makes the effort worthwhile.
The Court dismissed the appeal because the order sustaining a demurrer to the amended petition, without further disposition of the action, was not final and therefore not appealable.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted tax brackets and deductions for 2026 to offset rising living costs and limit bracket creep. The standard deduction will rise to $32,200 for joint filers, $16,100 for single filers and $24,150 for heads of household. The 37% top tax rate will apply above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for couples. The estate tax exemption will increase to $15 million, EITC and child tax credit thresholds will be adjusted, and a new $6,000 deduction will apply to taxpayers aged 65 and older beginning with 2025. Analysts described the changes as limited household relief, while economists cautioned they may not fully counter renewed inflation.

The Sansa Fuze is a portable digital audio/video player with a 1.9-inch color screen, internal storage, a rechargeable battery, an integrated FM tuner where applicable, a built-in microphone, and a microSD/SDHC expansion slot. It supports MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, Audible content, audiobooks, podcasts, MPEG-4 video, and JPEG photos. Battery life is stated as up to 24 hours for audio or five hours for video.

The power switch turns the player on and off and resets it, while the thumbwheel navigates menus, adjusts volume, and controls track progress. A hold switch locks the controls to prevent accidental activation without stopping playback. The internal, nonreplaceable battery can be charged through a computer USB port, AC adapter, or car adapter; playback is unavailable while connected directly to a computer.

Files can be transferred by drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player synchronization, Audible Manager, or Sansa Media Converter. The converter can crop, rotate, and resize photos before transferring photos or videos to internal memory or a microSD card. Firmware updates are available through SanDisk’s support website. Formatting the player deletes all its content.

Music, audiobook, video, photo, slideshow, FM radio, and voice-recording functions are covered, including navigation, repeat and shuffle modes, MusicEQ, Go Lists, ratings, bookmarks, deletion, slideshow timing, and video brightness. The FM radio supports manual and automatic presets, up to 30 stations, and recording of broadcast audio. Users must comply with copyright and intellectual-property laws when recording and using copyrighted material.

In consolidated appeals, the New Jersey Supreme Court addressed when New Jersey’s Anti-Injunction Act requires costs and counsel fees.

In the strike case, United Steelworkers represented 670 of the company’s approximately 885 employees before a 1959 contract expiration. After negotiations failed, the union struck and conducted mass picketing that obstructed access to the company’s plant. The company obtained temporary restraints and, after a hearing, an interlocutory injunction. The Appellate Division found that the evidence provided a substantive basis for injunctive relief but reversed the injunction because of procedural deficiencies, principally the trial court’s delay in issuing findings, missing findings of basic facts, and overbroad restraining language. The company did not appeal, and the trial court later denied the union’s requests for costs and counsel fees.

The Supreme Court affirmed, holding that mandatory costs and fees under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-53 apply when injunctive relief is denied or reversed on the merits. Following Westinghouse, the court reasoned that the provision protects labor against unsuccessful or wrongful injunction suits. Because the strike suit had meritorious grounds and was reversed only for procedural reasons, the union was not entitled to fees.

In the arbitration case, a discharged striker sought arbitration under the new collective bargaining agreement. The company sued to declare the grievance nonarbitrable and temporarily enjoined the arbitration. The Appellate Division held that the striker was covered by the agreement and that his discharge was arbitrable. The Supreme Court held that this declaratory action, with an ancillary request to stay arbitration, fell outside the Anti-Injunction Act because it was not a suit to restrain unlawful labor activity, and therefore no counsel fees were available. Ordinary appellate costs had already been taxed, and the successful union defendants could seek statutory trial-court costs. The judgments were affirmed, with costs awarded only in the arbitration case.

Central Huron Council heard a proposal from Huron County Library officials to renovate Clinton Library so it can meet accreditation standards and provide improved, more accessible services. In 2015, the county library and 11 branches received five-year accreditation, but Clinton was denied because of accessibility and insufficient space.

The county is responsible for library staff, materials, furniture, equipment and services, while the municipality maintains the building and covers utilities. County and municipal staff will assess Clinton’s service needs, determine required space and agree on facility components before working with an architect to prepare draft designs for public consultation. Standards include adequate square footage, accessible layouts, lower shelves, wider aisles and flexible, community-focused spaces.

Provincial grant funding may be possible, but Wark said a shovel-ready project would strengthen the request. If the municipality commits to changes, the county may invest in the library’s interior. Council will continue discussions with the county.

At the Old Bailey, 18-year-old Charlie Alliston denied manslaughter and causing bodily harm by dangerous driving after colliding with Kim Briggs, 44, on Old Street in February 2016. Alliston was riding a fixed-wheel bicycle without a front brake at about 20mph when Briggs, crossing during her lunch break, stepped into his path. She suffered two skull fractures and brain bleeding and died a week later.

Alliston said he warned Briggs twice, but she ignored him and stopped in his path; he also claimed witnesses and officers supported his account. The prosecution said his unlawful, dangerous riding contributed to the collision and that evidence showed he could have stopped in time with a front brake. He had removed the brake from a previous bicycle and bought the brakeless Planet X bike a month before the crash. The court heard that fixed-wheel bicycles were permitted on public roads only if fitted with a front brake. CCTV and crash reconstructions were presented to the jury.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, as the Lobos beat Boise State 78-73. Brown made 13 of 14 free throws, while Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each scored 14 and Ajet added five blocks. Chandler Hutchison led the Broncos with a career-high 31 points, and James Reid added 18; Boise State never led. New Mexico survived a late rally, with Brown and Jordan Hunter helping fuel a decisive 12-2 run. The win left New Mexico with five conference losses, one behind Colorado State and Nevada, while Boise State had four. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game with a foot injury.

A Harvard Institute of Politics poll found that 65% of millennials aged 18–29 favored Democrats in 2018, versus 33% for Republicans. Only 14% said America was headed in the right direction, Trump’s approval was 25%, and 61% supported stricter gun laws.

A retrospective cohort study analyzed more than 2.2 million pregnant and postpartum hospitalizations from 2017–2019 using the HCUP National Inpatient Sample. Among 168,729 hospitalizations (7.4%) involving a mood-disorder diagnosis, peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) occurred more often than in those without mood disorders (0.12% vs. 0.05%). Composite adverse cardiac events were also more frequent (0.36% vs. 0.14%).

After adjustment for demographic and clinical differences, mood disorders remained associated with PPCM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.36, 95% CI 1.03–1.80), composite adverse cardiac events (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37–1.81), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39–1.89). Other individual cardiac outcomes were not significantly associated after adjustment. Maternal mortality did not differ significantly between groups. PPCM incidence among patients with mood disorders was approximately 1 in 827.

The findings support further investigation of mood disorders as a risk factor for PPCM and peripartum cardiac events and suggest potential roles for mental-health referral, screening, and optimization in pregnancy and postpartum care. Limitations included reliance on ICD-10 codes, restriction to inpatient data, inability to assess post-discharge outcomes or establish causation, and insufficient data for some rare outcomes.

Preempt announced new integrations for its Preempt Behavioral Firewall, adding context from Okta, Azure Active Directory and VPN gateways to improve internal-network threat detection. Integrations with SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator and HP Aruba ClearPass enable organizations to block, notify or challenge users to verify identity. The firewall combines UEBA with adaptive, automated responses to detect and stop breaches, malicious insiders and risky behavior in real time.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a redesigned streaming multiprocessor (SM), real-time ray tracing, AI-accelerated graphics, higher-speed memory, and advanced rendering controls. Each SM includes 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 cores, eight Tensor Cores, one RT Core, independent thread scheduling, and concurrent floating-point and integer execution. Four processing blocks per SM share 96 KB of configurable L1 data cache/shared memory. Moving integer instructions to a parallel pipe provides an effective 36% increase in floating-point throughput, while the SM changes collectively deliver a reported 50% improvement in performance per CUDA core.

Turing’s unified cache design doubles L1 hit bandwidth per TPC versus Pascal and allows the cache/shared-memory split to be reconfigured. Its GDDR6 subsystem operates at 14 Gbps and offers 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X implementation. Improved signal integrity, including 40% less crosstalk, larger L2 caches, and enhanced memory compression increase effective memory bandwidth by approximately 50%. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice that of GP102.

Turing Tensor Cores add FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision modes and accelerate deep-learning training and inference. They support NVIDIA NGX services such as Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. DLSS uses neural networks trained against 64-times-supersampled references to produce image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X renders at final resolution and approximates 64-times-supersampled quality. NGX InPainting synthesizes replacement content, AI Slow-Mo generates interpolated frames, and AI Super Rez enlarges images or video by 2x, 4x, or 8x.

The Turing-based Tesla T4 targets data-center and edge inference. It contains 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivers up to 130 INT8 TOPS or 260 INT4 TOPS, and provides up to 40 times the inference performance and more than 50 times the energy efficiency of CPU-based systems. It also supports enhanced video decoding, Volta-era Multi-Process Service, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s of bandwidth.

Turing adds a new display and video engine with DisplayPort 1.4a, Display Stream Compression 1.2, support for two 8K displays at 60 Hz, native HDR processing, and BT.2100 tone mapping. Its NVENC encoder supports HEVC 8K at 30 fps and provides bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, while NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR support. USB-C and VirtualLink provide display, power, and data over a single connector for VR headsets. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for SLI transfers, providing substantially more bandwidth than Pascal’s SLI bridge.

Real-time ray tracing is enabled by dedicated RT Cores, which accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and advanced BVH structures, these cores make ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, reflections, refractions, and indirect lighting practical on a single GPU and are reported to accelerate ray tracing about tenfold over Pascal. NVIDIA RTX technology supports ray tracing through NVIDIA libraries, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API. Rasterization remains effective for visibility and primary rays, while ray tracing is applied to effects where it provides greater visual benefit.

Additional rendering features include mesh shading, variable-rate shading (VRS), texture-space shading (TSS), and multi-view rendering (MVR). Mesh shading adds cooperative Task and Mesh Shaders, reducing CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enabling scenes with hundreds of thousands of objects. VRS allows each 16-by-16-pixel region to use a different shading rate, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering while optionally increasing sampling for multisample anti-aliasing. TSS computes and stores shading in texture space, decoupling visibility and appearance sampling and allowing shaded results to be reused across frames or views. MVR supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API, expanding Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection capabilities for stereo, shadow, and multi-instance rendering.

TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores and is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores; it powers the GeForce RTX 2070 and does not support NVLink or SLI.

Turing’s hybrid-rendering workload combines Tensor operations at 20% utilization, CUDA cores at 80%, RT Cores at 40%, and INT32 pipelines at 28%. NVIDIA’s RTX-OPS metric weights each operation type by its expected workload share, producing a reported value of 78 for the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti.

During card identification, the host resets and identifies each card separately over CMD, validates its operating-voltage range, and requests an RCA; identification-mode communication uses CMD only. CMD0 software-resets cards to Idle State, except Inactive cards. After power-up or CMD0, cards use default RCA, driver-strength, and clock settings, while UHS-II cards retain their Device ID and RCA. CMD8 checks interface voltage using the VHS field and check pattern: compatible cards echo both, while incompatible cards remain idle without responding. CMD8 must precede the first ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC initialization.

Washington police will announce charges against 12 Turkish security agents over violence during Erdogan’s May visit: seven for felonies and five for misdemeanors. Sinan Narin was arrested on aggravated assault; Eyup Yildirim on assault with significant bodily injury and aggravated assault.

The speaker reflected on a difficult playoff loss, praising his teammates’ effort and the opposing team, whom he said deserved to win. He noted that home ice and loud crowds played a major role and credited his coaching staff’s preparation, emphasizing aggressive play, energy, and readiness. After Patrick’s retirement, he considered Patrick the game’s best player and congratulated him. Looking ahead, he planned to proceed one game at a time toward the playoffs. He also said his main motivation for winning the Stanley Cup was his ailing mother and resolved to move forward after the loss.

iOS 11.4 launched AirPlay 2, enabling multi-room streaming, stereo HomePod pairing, a larger network buffer, and playback continuity during calls. HomePod Siri gained calendar management and room-to-room music transfers, but without voice recognition, anyone can access the calendar. AirPlay 2 is supported by Bose, Pioneer, Sonos, Bang & Olufsen, and Bowers & Wilkins, though an iOS device must act as the streaming hub. The update also launched Messages in iCloud, syncing messages, SMS, photos, and attachments across devices while consuming more iCloud storage.

Meeker’s Internet Trends report found Chinese short-form video viewing climbed 360% in 2017, approaching long-form viewing, though 76% of consumers used only one such app. Douyin and Kuaishou each reported roughly 100 million daily active users. Long-form video advertising spending surpassed network TV spending in China.

U.S. stocks rebounded Wednesday as hopes that Italy could avoid new elections lifted banks and energy shares, while smaller companies posted outsized gains. The S&P 500 and Dow each rose 1.3%, the Nasdaq gained 0.9%, and the Russell 2000 hit a record. Rising bond yields aided banks, and crude jumped 2.2%. European markets mostly advanced as trade tensions involving China and proposed U.S. tariffs on EU steel and aluminum remained in focus.

At NVIDIA Corporation’s May 16, 2018 annual meeting, stockholders elected 11 directors to one-year terms, approved advisory executive compensation, and ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent auditor for the fiscal year ending January 27, 2019. Stockholders also approved increases of 23 million shares in the 2007 Equity Incentive Plan and 13.5 million shares in the 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The amended plans were filed as exhibits to the Form 8-K dated May 21, 2018.

A University of Rochester Medical Centre study in mice found that low-dose alcohol, comparable to about 2.5–2.6 daily drinks for a 70 kg person, improved glymphatic activity, reduced brain inflammation and enhanced cerebrospinal fluid movement and waste clearance. These mice performed no differently from teetotal controls in cognitive and motor tests. Intermediate and very high doses suppressed glymphatic function, while prolonged high exposure increased inflammation and impaired cognitive and motor abilities. The findings were published in Scientific Reports.

The appellate court modified the Supreme Court’s order on the law and, as modified, affirmed with costs to plaintiff. Summary judgment should not have been granted on the bad-faith settlement claims because evidence supported a jury finding that the defendant failed timely to offer its policy limits, depriving plaintiff of an opportunity to negotiate a more favorable settlement. Testimony concerning a $1 million acceptance and an earlier $500,000 offer was direct, non-speculative evidence of damages, and credibility was for the jury to determine. The court affirmed dismissal of plaintiff’s fourth cause of action under Insurance Law § 2601.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters operating up to 2 MHz. They require external gate drivers and support buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

In external synchronization mode, RT is left floating and a clock is applied to SYNC at twice the desired switching frequency. The clock must range from 200 kHz to 4 MHz with a 40% to 60% duty cycle; 50% is recommended. The controller inverts this clock, which must be present before OUTA and OUTB become active. In primary-secondary mode, the primary controller has RT populated and drives SYNC, while the secondary controller has RT floating and receives the primary clock at SYNC. The controllers can synchronize independent converters or form an interleaved converter with shared SYNC, VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC connections. Secondary clock inversion produces a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding primary outputs.

Primary outputs include OUTA or dual OUTA/OUTB, and synchronous-rectifier outputs include SRA or SRA/SRB. Each output has roughly 150-mA peak capability, so external gate drive is recommended. OUTB is supported by the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP and is active only with the 50% duty-cycle configuration. SR outputs remain off during soft start and begin switching when SS exceeds 1 V.

The TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP provide two independently programmable dead times, while the TPS7H5003-SP uses a fixed typical dead time of 50 ns. PS and SP resistors must be between 10 kΩ and 300 kΩ; leaving them floating produces a minimum typical dead time of 8 ns. Leading-edge blank time is fixed at a typical 50 ns for the TPS7H5003-SP and resistor-programmable for the other devices, requiring 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ. Pulse skipping limits minimum on-time during high-frequency operation. It occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V at the clock’s rising edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%; SR outputs remain off if pulse skipping begins during soft start.

The DCL pin configures maximum duty cycle: connecting it to VLDO permits 100%, leaving it floating permits 75%, and connecting it to AVSS imposes 50%. The 50% option and associated dual outputs apply to the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. External synchronization provides the most precise duty-cycle limiting with a 50%-duty-cycle system clock.

Peak-current-mode control uses CS_ILIM to sense primary current and turn the primary output off when the sensed signal reaches COMP/2, with a 150-mV comparator offset. CS_ILIM also detects overcurrent using a resistor to AVSS. When CS_ILIM reaches 1.05 V, the controller enters cycle-by-cycle current limiting and charges CHICC with an 80-µA current. At 0.6 V, switching stops and SS is discharged; HICC is pulled to 1 V and then discharged until 0.3 V, after which soft start restarts. CHICC should be at least 3.3 nF.

The FAULT pin supports user-defined protection logic. A typical rising threshold of 0.6 V must persist for 0.4 µs to 1.4 µs to trigger shutdown. After FAULT falls below a typical 0.5 V, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay before restarting soft start; a renewed fault restarts the delay.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The recommended ramp equals the inductor’s falling-current slope; greater compensation provides no additional stability benefit. RSC sets the ramp through a resistor to AVSS. The transconductance error amplifier supports Type 2A or Type 2B compensation, selected by choosing RCOMP, CCOMP, and optionally CHF. Compensation design begins with crossover frequency, power-stage transconductance, and compensation-zero placement, with topology-specific transformer and current-sense ratios included.

Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and permits the power-up sequence to restart below 160°C.

A synchronous GaN push-pull example uses the TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz and 5 V. Selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ RTOP and 1.4-kΩ RBOT feedback resistors, approximately 25-ns dead time using 20.5-kΩ RPS and RSP resistors, a 49.9-kΩ RLEB resistor, a 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms of soft start, a transformer turns ratio of 2.5 and actual primary inductance of 40 µH, 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs, and a 0.47-µH output inductor. At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is calculated, while 2.3 mF is used for radiation-induced transient mitigation. A 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation with RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, CHF = 47 pF, and RSC = 102 kΩ are also specified.

The controllers operate from a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and require at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably low-ESL ceramic. Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and control traces from switching nodes and power magnetics, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide current traces, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, and connecting CFP-package backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.

Modern spread formations, RPOs, and Air Raid concepts have created many run-fit approaches, making shared terminology important. Coaches should translate “coach speak” into executable schemes rather than treat it as a universal formula, because run fits vary with talent and philosophy.

Run fits are shaped by two factors: whether the front ends in even or odd spacing and the coverage played behind the fit. Even spacing places the primary open bubble in the B gap; traditional Over fronts leave it away from the tight end. Odd spacing moves the open gaps to the C gaps, as in Tite/Mint fronts. The numbers in seven-, eight-, and nine-man spacing describe defenders in the box or run fit relative to offensive personnel.

Seven-man spacing gives the defense one fewer box defender than the offense. It is called out-gapped or a light box and commonly uses middle-of-field-open coverage. Overhangs remain outside the fit and pass-first, creating an extra gap. Defenses can use two-gapping linemen, stunts or slants, stack-track-and-fallback against zone, and spill-overlap against gap schemes.

Eight-man spacing gives the defense an equal number of box defenders and the offense. It is called gapped-out, commonly pairs with middle-of-field-closed coverage such as Cover 1 or Cover 3, and uses one-gap fits. Zone schemes can use indicator fitting based on tight-end movement; gap schemes commonly use lever-spill-lever.

Nine-man spacing, or maxed out, gives the defense one more box defender than the offense and is commonly associated with blitz fits and Cover 0, including quarters concepts. Defenders can play aggressively because every gap has a defender. Against zone, an end may remain in the C gap, the nickel may fit outside, and the safety may track the tight end or play sky force. Against gap schemes, the extra defender is commonly the nickel.

In 3-4 defenses, odd and even front spacing still apply. Tite/Mint examples include stack-track-fallback, spill-overlap, indicator fits, and lever-spill-lever. Overhangs may be taught to “fill or freeze” based on the back’s location. A Tite front can be viewed as a gap-exchanged even front, with the five-technique starting in the B gap.

Kentucky sophomore forward Wenyen Gabriel declared for the 2018 NBA draft and will begin his professional career, leaving the Wildcats without a scholarship junior or senior for the time being. Gabriel, 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds per game, led Kentucky in blocked shots and scored 23 points while making seven three-pointers in an SEC Tournament semifinal win over Alabama. Coach John Calipari praised his versatility, growth and potential. Gabriel did not receive an NBA scouting combine invitation but received feedback from teams that worked him out. Kentucky has also lost Kevin Knox, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Hamidou Diallo to the draft, while PJ Washington will return. Stanford graduate transfer Reid Travis could join the roster, and Gabriel could begin professionally overseas or in the NBA’s developmental league.

The lecture explains light forces using the dressed-atom picture. Diagonalizing the two-level atom–laser Hamiltonian produces dressed states that are superpositions of bare ground and excited states. In the strong-Rabi, secular limit, population and coherence equations decouple, allowing steady-state populations, relaxation times, spontaneous-emission rates, and the carrier and sideband components of the Mollow triplet to be calculated.

Spontaneous emission has different but complementary descriptions in the two bases. In the bare-state picture, photon emission produces antibunching because the atom must be excited again before it can emit another photon. In the dressed-state picture, transitions alternate between blue- and red-detuned sidebands. Temporal resolution reveals antibunching, whereas spectral resolution reveals the sidebands.

The dressed levels are separated by the generalized Rabi frequency and experience opposite dipole forces. The net stimulated force is the population-weighted sum of these forces. For red detuning, the ground state correlates with the lower dressed level, producing an attractive force; for blue detuning, it correlates with the upper dressed level, producing a repulsive force. At resonance, equal dressed-state populations make the average force vanish, although force fluctuations cause heating.

Finite population-relaxation times produce a lag as an atom crosses a laser beam. This nonadiabatic lag creates an extra force and hence friction. In a blue-detuned standing wave, it yields cooling, the phenomenon known as blue molasses. The corresponding cooling rate depends on the friction coefficient, while momentum diffusion from force fluctuations determines the heating rate; their ratio gives the limiting temperature.

During radiative cascades, atoms switch between dressed levels and the force abruptly reverses. These fluctuations, rather than spontaneous-emission recoil, dominate heating in strong laser fields. At higher velocities, where atoms traverse several lattice periods before spontaneous emission, a blue-detuned standing wave produces Sisyphus cooling: emission usually occurs near an antinode and transfers the atom from the upper to the lower dressed level, removing potential energy and reducing its kinetic energy.

In the far-detuned perturbative limit, the dressed states are mainly the bare states, and the light-shift potential, dressed-state transition rates, friction, momentum diffusion, and limiting temperature can be derived in a simple form. The resulting temperature scales with the standing-wave potential depth, so laser cooling of a two-level atom in a standing wave cannot localize atoms within individual lattice wells. Lower temperatures require accounting for recoil and using physics beyond the two-level model.

The lecture also relates the dipole potential to the Optical Bloch Equations, the dressed-atom description, and driven-oscillator polarizability. A refractive-optics analogy extends the picture to mesoscopic and macroscopic objects: red-detuned light with refractive index above one pulls objects toward high intensity, while blue-detuned light with index below one repels them. This principle is used in optical tweezers to manipulate microscopic objects and biological samples.

Andrew Lo discusses severe financial-market fear during a liquidity crisis, noting that low borrowing rates and Federal Reserve efforts to maintain liquid markets may be helping, though uncertainty over rescue efforts and other events has left banks and investors reluctant to lend or invest. He suggests that better pricing transparency for complex securities could create opportunities for new market technologies.

Lo strongly opposes suspending mark-to-market accounting. He argues that security prices are determined by actual transactions between willing buyers and sellers, not by management’s own valuations. Suspending mark-to-market would delay recognition of losses rather than improve markets.

The lecture then introduces forward and futures contracts as tools for reducing uncertainty. Forwards are binding, customized over-the-counter agreements to buy or sell an asset at a price and date fixed in advance. Their initial market value is zero because supply and demand determine a fair forward price. Forward prices implicitly convey market expectations and incorporate costs such as storage, financing, and opportunity costs. Although forwards can secure needed quantities and prices, they are illiquid and expose parties to default risk.

Futures adapt the forward contract through standardization, exchange trading, daily mark-to-market adjustments, and an intermediary clearing corporation. These features reduce counterparty risk, improve liquidity and transparency, and require margin deposits that must be maintained as market prices change. Most futures are cash-settled, although some permit physical delivery.

Lo also argues that speculators are essential because they supply the opposite side of hedging transactions. Companies may hedge inputs, exchange-rate exposure, and other business risks, but views differ on whether hedging creates value, reduces financial distress, or is unnecessary because shareholders can hedge themselves. Examples from gold mining illustrate policies ranging from no hedging to hedging output prices for earnings stability and partial hedging.

At least 11 North Carolina counties offer child care academies that train new early childhood educators faster and at little or no cost to participants. Programs last two to six weeks, require 20 to 64 hours of instruction and are tailored to local workforce needs. The state House included $1.476 million for an expansion pilot in its budget, but the funding did not reach the final General Assembly budget. Separately, the Division of Child Development and Early Education is offering grants of up to $50,000 to as many as 10 UNC-system institutions to run academies from Oct. 15, 2025, through July 31, 2026.

Academies generally use one of two models. The classroom-ready model requires at least 20 hours of training and helps students complete registration, health and safety training, and background checks, qualifying them to work in licensed child care facilities but not as lead teachers. The teaching credential model adds instruction formerly provided through the semester-long EDU 119 course. Graduates receive EDU 3119 continuing-education credit, which applies toward an associate degree at any of North Carolina’s 58 community colleges and qualifies them to serve as licensed child care lead teachers and elementary school teaching assistants.

Programs are administered through collaborations involving Smart Start partnerships, community colleges, and child care resource and referral organizations. They also provide access to local resources, job fairs, apprenticeship information and other career pathways.

In Wayne and Johnston counties, Camber Foundation funding supports roughly 60-hour academies; the partnerships have graduated 63 students, with more than half entering child care or higher education. Johnston’s three academies produced 26 graduates, 14 of whom secured child care jobs, at a cost of about $430 per student. Stanly County’s classroom-ready program has graduated 13 students and placed five to 10 in jobs. McDowell Technical Community College’s two-week teaching credential academy graduated six lead-teacher candidates, four of whom entered child care classrooms, with a three-year Dogwood Health Trust grant covering $500–$600 per student and supporting associate-degree tuition and materials. Durham County’s six-week, bilingual academy received 140 applications for 20 slots and cost an average of $1,264 per student, funded by a Duke Community Affairs grant and Durham PreK.

MIT 6.832 Lecture 9 presents trajectory optimization as policy search. Control policies can be parameterized by a vector of control values; an open-loop policy may be represented as a piecewise-constant, zero-order-hold trajectory. For a fixed initial condition, the objective is minimized numerically over the policy parameters.

Shooting methods simulate the system forward and iteratively adjust parameters to reduce cost or satisfy final-state conditions. Gradients can be computed with an adjoint method, also called backpropagation through time, or with forward-only real-time recurrent learning (RTRL). Backpropagation through time carries a state-sized vector but requires a forward-and-backward pass; RTRL avoids the backward pass but carries a potentially large state-by-parameter sensitivity matrix. While gradient descent requires learning-rate tuning, sequential quadratic programming methods such as SNOPT often converge faster and efficiently support action bounds, final-state constraints, and trajectory constraints.

Direct collocation adds state and control variables to the optimization vector and enforces dynamics as explicit constraints, allowing cost and gradients to be evaluated without forward simulation. These methods are typically fast and handle many constraints efficiently, though their fixed discretization can make them less accurate than shooting methods. Intelligent initialization may help find different solutions. Demonstrations covered pendulum swing-up, acrobot trajectories, and path planning. Although these local methods can encounter local minima, different valid trajectories may still satisfy the task. Stabilizing optimized trajectories with LQR feedback was deferred to a later lecture.

The Paschell family of Norwalk, Iowa, lost their only water source—a 68-year-old well—when Department of Transportation highway expansion along I-35 damaged it. For two months the family of four has hauled gallons daily and cannot bathe their children or do laundry at home. The DOT says it is investigating and offered a hotel stay and reimbursement for cleaning supplies. Waiting for Warren County's rural water system, Mark Paschell dug a 300-yard trench and laid a water line himself. The family says it will never get the well back.

A retrospective review of 377 COVID-19 patients undergoing percutaneous tracheostomy at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital, Kuwait, from March 2020 to March 2022 was described as the largest reported single-center series. Bedside, bronchoscopy-guided procedures were generally performed after at least seven days of intubation, with open tracheostomy reserved for selected cases. The approach aimed to reduce staff exposure, cross-contamination, and transfer risks while facilitating pulmonary care and weaning.

Mean time from intubation to tracheostomy was 17.4 days. Patients had a mean age of 56.2 years, 59% were male, and common comorbidities included diabetes (50%) and hypertension (48%); 29% were receiving ECMO and 23% dialysis. Complications occurred in 85 cases (23%): minor bleeding was most common (14%), followed by tracheoesophageal fistula (2%), peristomal infection (2%), and one tracheoinnominate fistula. No deaths were attributed to the procedure.

Of 377 patients, 203 (54%) were weaned from sedation after a mean 7.5 days, and 156 (41%) were weaned from mechanical ventilation after a mean 12.9 days. There were 236 deaths (63%), all attributed to COVID-19 complications, and 141 discharges; 53 discharged patients were decannulated, a mean of 36.5 days after tracheostomy. Longer sedation and mechanical ventilation were associated with lower survival.

The authors concluded that percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed in COVID-19 patients and recommended performing it as soon as feasible after day seven, while noting that optimal timing remains unresolved. Limitations included no open-tracheostomy comparison, no long-term post-decannulation follow-up, and no objective staff PCR surveillance.

Florida Panthers goaltenders Roberto Luongo and James Reimer could return next week, with coach Bob Boughner saying both felt well after skating and might practice Monday. Luongo has a .928 save percentage in 15 games, while Reimer has a .911 mark over 17 starts. Harri Sateri has performed well in their absence, and Samuel Montembeault could be sent to AHL Springfield if either goalie returns. Jamie McGinn will return from an upper-body injury and play on the third line.

Using Yahoo Finance data from 2014, the authors backtested 100 Bitcoin turn-of-the-month strategies by optimizing entry before and exit after the start of a new month. The initial strategy averaged a 3.3% gain per trade, with a 41.8% CAGR, 16% time in the market, and a 25% maximum drawdown. Although somewhat curve-fitted, it outperformed the 1.33% average gain for random periods of the same length, and nearly all entries and exits around the turn of the month performed better than random periods. Modifying the entry criteria and adding another variable reduced trades and CAGR but produced a smoother equity curve with fewer drawdowns. Recent performance was flat during a Bitcoin crash. The authors withheld the specific strategy and concluded that Bitcoin has a positive end-of-month effect that may support a turn-of-the-month trading strategy.

Demand remained sensitive to housing, unemployment, consumer spending, and general economic conditions, and the stock was not considered a source of major growth opportunities.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. It supports a speed-boost mode that samples a user-selected analog input pair at up to 8 MSPS while leaving the other six channels idle.

Reset is triggered by pulling RESET low or writing 1b to the RESET field in bank 0, register 0x00. Power-down is controlled by the PWDN pin or the PD_CH field in bank 1, register 0xC0. After power-up or reset, a required register-write initialization sequence configures the device, with a free-running sampling clock connected beforehand. User settings include data-interface lane configuration, analog input ranges and bandwidths, power references, common-mode ranges, averaging, test patterns, PRBS/XOR functions, gain-error correction, and speed-boost controls.

The 16-bit configuration registers are divided into three banks with 8-bit addresses. SPI writes select a bank through register 0x03 and then write the target register. Register reads require SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE to be enabled and use separate SPI frames.

For daisy-chain configurations, CS and SCLK are shared, SDI and SDO are linked between ADCs, and register operations require N × 24 SCLKs. DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the chain length excluding ADC1. Register reads and writes in daisy-chain mode use bank selection and read-enable sequences before transferring data from the selected addresses.

In ATE applications, the ADS9803 can measure PMU signals directly or through multiplexers. It provides low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, with wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5 µs for multiplexed signals. Post-calibration total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C for a ±5 V range.

The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Recommended layout includes close-proximity 0.1-µF supply bypass capacitors, separate reference decoupling, short ground connections, and isolation of analog and reference signals from digital and noise sources.
