A longitudinal, nonrandomized study enrolled 691 vaccine-naïve adults aged 18–45 across four sites in Bengaluru and Pune between June 2021 and January 2022; 506 completed both vaccine doses and follow-up without symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection. Participants received Covaxin at four-week intervals or Covishield at 12-week intervals and were grouped by baseline serostatus.

Both vaccines increased anti-spike antibodies, but Covishield consistently produced stronger responses. Among baseline-seronegative participants, seroconversion after the first and second doses was 93.2% and 98.3% with Covishield versus 36.6% and 74.4% with Covaxin; second-dose antibody GMTs were 1,272.1 and 75.4 BAU/ml, respectively. Among baseline-seropositive participants, at-least-twofold titer increases occurred in 95.2% and 91.7% of Covishield recipients versus 51.8% and 66.9% of Covaxin recipients. Higher pre-vaccination titers were associated with nonresponsiveness.

Covishield also elicited significant authentic-virus neutralizing antibody responses in both baseline serostatus groups, whereas Covaxin’s increases were not statistically significant. ACE2-inhibition responses were broader and more potent with Covishield. Neither vaccine elicited detectable Omicron-specific activity in seronegative participants, while one Covishield dose produced measurable activity in seropositive participants without further increase after the second dose.

In a subset from the earliest cohort, both vaccines increased spike-specific CD4 T cells in seronegative participants, but the increase was significant only with Covishield; spike-specific CD8 responses were detected only with Covishield. Neither vaccine significantly increased spike-specific CD4 or CD8 cells in seropositive participants.

Overall, the vectored Covishield vaccine elicited stronger and broader antibody and cellular responses than inactivated Covaxin. However, Omicron exposure, probable asymptomatic infection, and sparse sampling confounded durability assessments and some vaccine comparisons. The study did not measure non-neutralizing antibody functions, establish correlates of protection, or support inferring efficacy from immunogenicity alone.

The speaker accepts his sudden, weighty responsibilities, citing his past commitment to free government and popular rights as assurance of his future conduct. He asks for encouragement and support from patriots as the government faces present perils.

A study of Antarctica’s Amundsen Sea and Sabrina Coast found that rapidly melting glaciers can pool warm water beneath ice shelves, preventing normal cooling and creating a feedback loop that accelerates melting. This process is already underway and may increase the risk of ice-shelf collapse and a sudden sea-level “pulse.” Current models project Miami could see seas 7–8 feet higher than in 1900 by 2100, while a pulse could raise South Florida’s seas by 10–30 feet. Reduced Antarctic bottom water formation could also slow ocean currents, potentially contributing to superstorms and faster atmospheric warming. Researchers said the process may resemble one that triggered 16 feet of sea-level rise after the last glacial period, though many uncertainties remain.
Zebronics introduced the Buddy wireless speaker for Rs. 1,699, featuring 5-watt RMS output, RGB LEDs, Bluetooth, three hours of battery playback, FM radio, and USB, microSD, and AUX connectivity.

The passage argues that expanding workforce development should not come at the expense of traditional construction apprenticeships, whose selective entry requirements exclude students needing extra support. It recommends pre-apprenticeships: short-term programs that expose participants to careers and employers, build skills, provide mentorship, prepare them for entry assessments, and may lead to credentials such as OSHA certification.

Pre-apprenticeship programs need sustained investment and strong connections to unions, employers, and registered apprenticeships. They should offer wraparound support, including transportation, childcare, and help with lost wages, financed through approaches such as zero-percent loans or emergency credit that participants repay only when earnings increase. Programs should also collect outcome data demonstrating graduation, apprenticeship placement, and longer-term employment. Strategic collaboration among employers, unions, government agencies, and philanthropies could attract additional funding, improve access to construction careers, strengthen the talent pipeline, and support economic mobility.

An experiment showed that AI can scan Reddit conversations to help public health workers identify harmful experiences with cannabis products. Researchers developed Waldo, trained it on 10,000 manually reviewed posts, and tested it on the remainder. Waldo examined more than 430,000 cannabis-related Reddit posts and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing adverse effects; researchers found that 86% of 250 sampled flagged posts described problematic experiences. Waldo produced fewer false positives than ChatGPT but did not surpass human reviewers. Researchers said the approach could supplement traditional monitoring but cautioned that its effectiveness may not transfer to other products and that ethical use would require privacy protections.

The paper presents Robodoc, a prototype medical chatbot that integrates specialized diagnostic models through OpenAI API function calling. An Angular/TypeScript interface accepts text messages or uploaded images, selects an appropriate model, and converts model outputs into user-facing responses.

Three diagnostic models are used. A TensorFlow.js neural network, trained on 2,000 equally distributed Kaggle samples, predicts diabetes from age, BMI, HbA1c, blood glucose, hypertension, and heart disease. Two Google Teachable Machine transfer-learning models analyze medical images: an X-ray model distinguishing normal lungs, viral pneumonia, and bacterial pneumonia, and an OCT model classifying normal images, drusen, choroidal neovascularization, and diabetic macular edema. The chatbot extracts diabetes parameters from conversations and can request missing information. Medical appointment scheduling for image cases is implemented as a stub based on perceived urgency.

The demonstration generally behaved as expected, with minor errors. The diabetes model reached about 90% validation and training accuracy. Pneumonia classification achieved 97% accuracy for normal images and 66% for viral pneumonia, with most errors occurring between viral and bacterial pneumonia. OCT accuracy ranged from 88% for drusen to 98% for choroidal neovascularization, with 99% training and 91% testing accuracy reported. Errors included confusing diabetic macular edema with drusen, failing to mark it urgent, marking viral pneumonia urgent, and occasionally classifying normal X-rays as pneumonia. These examples demonstrate behavior rather than constitute a statistical validation.

The literature review identifies extensive research on medical-image transfer learning but limited work integrating specialized models into task-oriented chatbots. The paper positions chatbots as accessible interfaces or assistants rather than replacements for healthcare professionals and notes risks from incorrect outputs, misdiagnosis, and deployment without human oversight. Proposed future work includes integrating image and text pathways, adding COVID-19 detection and other models, improving model selection, and exploring external APIs for real appointment scheduling.

Most surveyed enterprises outsource HPC: 87% prefer or plan external or cloud infrastructure, and 74% operate or plan colocation. Only 6% have on-premises HPC, while 28% plan it within two years. Forty-three percent use or plan research institutions, though long waits limit suitability.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture combines Tensor Cores, RT Cores, an updated streaming multiprocessor, and enhancements to memory, video, display, and software to support AI-assisted and real-time ray-traced rendering.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 operations and accelerate matrix multiplication for neural-network training and inference. They also power NVIDIA NGX services, including Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. DLSS uses neural networks trained against 64× supersampled references to reconstruct high-quality images with less shading work; DLSS 2X combines full-resolution inputs using a larger network. InPainting synthesizes missing image content, AI Slow-Mo generates intermediate video frames, and AI Super Rez enlarges images or video by 2×, 4×, or 8×.

The Tesla T4 is a Turing-based inference accelerator with 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s of bandwidth. It provides up to 130 INT8 TOPS and 260 INT4 TOPS and is reported to deliver up to 40× the inference performance and more than 50× the energy efficiency of CPU-based systems, while offering up to twice the energy efficiency of the preceding Tesla P4. The full TU104 configuration contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one second-generation x8 NVLink link.

Turing’s memory subsystem introduces redesigned GDDR6 interfaces operating at 14 Gbps with 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, while improved memory compression and higher raw bandwidth produce approximately 50% greater effective bandwidth than Pascal. Turing also supports DisplayPort 1.4a, Display Stream Compression 1.2, 8K output, native HDR and tone mapping, H.265 8K encoding, additional HEVC and VP9 decoding formats, and USB-C with VirtualLink for single-connector VR operation. TU102 uses two x8 NVLink links and TU104 uses one, with 25 GB/s per direction per link; Turing NVLink supports two-way but not three- or four-way SLI.

RT Cores provide dedicated acceleration for bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. Combined with RTX software, BVH structures, denoising, and hybrid rendering, they allow ray tracing and rasterization to operate together on a single GPU. The passage reports roughly tenfold higher ray-tracing performance than software-based Pascal ray tracing. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections can provide physically correct effects, including contact-hardening shadows and artifact-free glossy reflections.

Turing also introduces mesh shading, with task and mesh shaders processing object lists cooperatively to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and select level-of-detail geometry. Variable Rate Shading controls work at 16×16-pixel granularity and supports content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility from appearance sampling, stores results in texture space, and reuses them across pixels, frames, or views. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API, while Turing adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The full TU106 GPU contains 36 streaming multiprocessors, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, with a 256-bit memory interface but no NVLink or SLI support. RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based performance metric combining FP32 CUDA, Tensor, RT, and INT32 operations according to their modeled use within a frame.

The article evaluates six swing-trading indicators—Williams %R, WilliamsVixFix, Bollinger Bands, Stochastic, Internal Bar Strength (IBS), and RSI—using SPY as a proxy for the S&P 500. Swing trading generally lasts from one day to a few weeks, with a recommended indicator timeframe of 1–15 days.

Williams %R is ranked best because it produced stable results across tested variables and had the lowest average maximum drawdown, supporting better risk-adjusted returns. It is a mean-reverting oscillator ranging from 0 to −100, with high readings indicating overbought conditions and low readings indicating oversold conditions. Tests favored low entry levels, simple exits, and holding periods of about three days. A 10-day setup entering at −90 and exiting at −80 produced relatively low drawdowns and only two negative years since 1993.

Stochastic performed well with lookback periods below five days, though one tested strategy appeared potentially curve-fitted. IBS showed relatively stable profit factors and a reasonable equity curve despite the 2008–09 drawdown. Bollinger Bands produced favorable results with 6–10-day lookbacks but substantial drawdowns and high market exposure. WilliamsVixFix delivered roughly 8.5% annual growth with about 50% exposure, but experienced high, frequent drawdowns. A tested RSI strategy performed poorly after 2015 and suffered a 30% drawdown in 2020.

Risk-adjusted return is calculated by dividing annual geometric return by market-exposure percentage and is considered alongside maximum drawdown. Results may vary by asset, and mean-reversion performance on stocks is not guaranteed.

NASA ambassador Theo Wellington told the Wilson County Commission that the total solar eclipse could become the largest U.S. public one-day event, with populations along the 70-mile path expected to double. Wilson County is near the path’s center, where totality lasts up to 2 minutes and 40 seconds; the fairground is two seconds short of that maximum. The last total eclipse visible in Tennessee occurred in 1869. The commission approved service-weapon retention for eligible retired sheriffs and deputies; Commissioners Terry Ashe and Gary Keith abstained. It also approved $10,000 for training and certification of a school resource officer at Springdale Elementary, which is slated to receive students rezoned from Stoner Creek and Elzie D. Patton elementary schools.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for methods and apparatuses that encode and decode video signals, particularly HEVC video. It proposes improving prediction efficiency by addressing brightness changes, inaccurate motion information, prediction-sample errors, and intra-prediction mode signaling.

For inter-prediction, a current block may inherit motion and weight-prediction information from a neighboring block or use separately encoded motion information and an optional weight-prediction parameter. The parameter may include multiplication and addition values derived through regression analysis or from reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current and reference blocks. Encoding and decoding apparatus may also derive matching weight parameters without transmitting them explicitly, and may transmit merge flags, neighbor indices, parameter differences, or parameter-set indices as appropriate.

For intra-prediction, the current prediction sample may be corrected using reconstructed neighboring pixels. Correction coefficients, including multiplication and addition coefficients, may be derived from a previously coded block having a similar intra-prediction mode and similar reconstructed-pixel characteristics. The encoder may signal whether correction is performed and identify the relevant block or coefficient, while the decoder reproduces the correction.

The application also describes motion-vector precision adjustment using reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current block, intra-prediction mode coding through candidate modes or mode differences, and prediction of individual sub-blocks when a current block is divided. Encoder and decoder architectures include block division, intra/inter prediction, transform, quantization, entropy coding or decoding, inverse processing, filtering, and memory for reconstructed video.

Organized patriotism, substituting national loyalty for merely local or sectional loyalty, is essential to national growth. Capitalists and wageworkers, as well as industrial and agricultural classes, must cooperate to realize the country’s potential. Efficient education is therefore crucial, although federalism limits national leadership in technical education and leaves much of it to the states. The National Government should use its control of District of Columbia schools to advance commercial training, including foreign trade, and especially industrial and technical education. Training limited to literary accomplishments can discourage or unfit workers for industrial life, so schools should develop manual dexterity and industrial intelligence to prepare Americans for competition with highly trained foreign labor. The government should support wageworkers, broadly interpret the interstate commerce clause, and enact advanced child-labor and factory laws in the District as examples for the states. Farmers are equally vital to national welfare. Their work requires increasingly technical and scientific methods, practical training, better cultivation, and improved organization. National success must rest not only on material prosperity but also on the moral, mental, and physical development of workers and farmers.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 reported revenue of $20.379 billion, down 12% from $23.201 billion, primarily due to lower More Personal Computing revenue, reduced phone sales, and a net $1.3 billion Windows 10 revenue deferral, partly offset by Intelligent Cloud growth. Gross margin fell 12% to $13.172 billion, operating income declined 1% to $5.793 billion, net income increased to $4.620 billion, and diluted EPS rose to $0.57 from $0.54. Operating cash flow was $8.594 billion.

Segment revenue and operating income were $6.306 billion and $3.105 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $5.892 billion and $2.400 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $9.381 billion and $1.562 billion for More Personal Computing. Corporate and Other reported a $1.274 billion operating loss. Operating highlights included Windows 10 running on 110 million devices, a commercial cloud annualized run rate above $8.2 billion, 18.2 million Office 365 Consumer subscribers, more than doubled Azure revenue and usage, and 39 million Xbox Live monthly active users.

At September 30, 2015, Microsoft held $5.431 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $93.924 billion in short-term investments, with total assets of $172.896 billion, liabilities of $95.451 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $77.445 billion. The company repurchased 89 million shares for $4.0 billion, declared a $0.36 quarterly dividend, and had $17.9 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization.

Microsoft recast prior-period segment information after adopting three operating segments, without affecting consolidated net income or cash flows. It recognized Windows 10 license revenue over device lives of two to four years and had recorded phone-restructuring charges of $780 million under a plan to eliminate up to 7,800 positions. The filing disclosed $11.9 billion of tax contingencies, pending patent litigation, a China regulatory investigation, and potentially $1.5 billion of adverse legal outcomes beyond recorded amounts. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications needed to the unaudited interim financial statements.

In Singapore, OCBC and DBS led banking gains, UOB declined, and several property stocks rose. Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode using SYNC. The primary’s populated RT pin sets the switching frequency, while its SYNC output, running at twice that frequency, drives the secondary’s SYNC input; the secondary operates in external synchronization mode with its RT pin floating. This mode can synchronize two otherwise independent converters or create a single interleaved parallel converter by also connecting VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC. The secondary inverts the received clock, causing a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding outputs depending on synchronization timing.

The article demonstrates how to backtest a classic MACD trading strategy in Python using Apple’s daily historical data from Yahoo Finance. It uses yfinance to download prices, pandas for data manipulation, and matplotlib for charts. The MACD is the 12-period closing-price EMA minus the 26-period EMA, with a 9-period EMA signal line and a histogram calculated as the signal line minus the MACD. The strategy records a positive regime when the histogram is nonnegative and applies signals from the following row because purchases occur at the signal day’s close. It produced a 15.04% CAGR versus 19.07% for buy and hold while invested 51.13% of the time.

Jean Chrétien and Steven Del Duca addressed a Vaughan Liberal rally after the Yonge Street van attack, urging unity and blood donations. Del Duca called for campaign support despite polls suggesting Doug Ford could defeat the Liberals, and praised Kathleen Wynne’s transit, hospital, wage and tuition achievements. The IRS is cracking down on tax-related identity fraud, but consumers and businesses remain warned to beware of con artists seeking personal data.

Under the 2018 federal tax law, many employees should receive more take-home pay beginning in February as employers adopt updated withholding tables. About 90% of workers are expected to see additional cash, though amounts vary with income, children, pay frequency and W-4 allowances. A married couple earning $90,000 with two children could receive about $61 more per semi-monthly paycheck, while a single $35,000 earner without children could receive nearly $32 more.

The child tax credit increased to $2,000 per qualifying child, allowing more higher-income families to claim it. The standard deduction rose to $24,000 for married couples and $12,000 for singles, while deductions for home equity interest ended and combined personal property, real estate and state and local tax deductions were capped at $10,000. Mortgage interest remains deductible within stated limits.

A revised W-4 form is expected, and taxpayers are advised to review their withholding and 2017 deductions to avoid owing taxes in 2019. The IRS plans to update its withholding calculator by the end of February.

Bonus withholding fell to 22%. A $5,000 bonus would therefore have $1,100 withheld rather than $1,250.

Four-star defensive end Bill Norton committed to Georgia over 10 other schools, including Alabama, LSU, Tennessee and Ohio State. The 6-foot-6, 270-pound Christian Brothers prospect was the nation’s 11th-ranked strong-side defensive end.

3DPCNet is a compact, pose-only module that maps estimated 17-joint 3D skeletons from arbitrary camera-centered views into a fixed body-centered canonical frame. It uses parallel GCN and Transformer branches to capture anatomical and long-range joint relationships, fuses them through cross-attention and adaptive gating, and predicts a continuous 6D global rotation converted to an SO(3) matrix via Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization. An optional residual head provides minor joint-position corrections. Training uses synthetically rotated poses and a composite loss combining pose reconstruction, geodesic rotation error, cycle consistency, perceptual structure, and regularization.

On MM-Fi cross-subject and cross-environment evaluations, 3DPCNet reduced MPJPE from 63–65 mm to 46–49 mm and rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4°, with little degradation across evaluation domains. Its non-zero PA-MPJPE of 37–38 mm reflects learned non-rigid corrections absent from the rigid geometric baseline.

Evaluations using MotionBERT and DDH poses on TotalCapture showed more stable wrist trajectories and stronger qualitative agreement with motion-capture trajectories and synchronized IMU accelerations than the geometric baseline, despite no TotalCapture training or fine-tuning. Limitations include non-rigid residual deviations, inability to recover absolute scale, sensitivity to poor input poses, and reliance on sampled pose-space rotations rather than real multiview imagery. Proposed future work includes rigid residual constraints, temporal modeling and uncertainty estimation, scale and gravity alignment, and end-to-end clinical and performance validation.

Dick Tuck, a former Democratic Party operative known for political pranks, died in Tucson at 94, longtime friend and estate executor Lorraine Glicksman said. Beginning as a UC Santa Barbara student in 1950, Tuck repeatedly tormented Richard Nixon through deceptive events, bogus fortune-cookie messages and a Chinese sign referencing the Hughes loan. His 1962 Chinatown stunt reportedly prompted Nixon to tear up the sign; Nixon later destroyed multilingual “Nixon’s the one” buttons fearing another prank. Tuck also worked for Robert F. Kennedy’s 1968 campaign and unsuccessfully ran for California Senate in 1966. At 90, he proposed a holiday marking Nixon’s 1974 resignation, calling it “Nixmas.”

Mathieu Henderson completed his four-year Ontario Hockey League career with the Flint Firebirds, finishing ninth among OHL defencemen in scoring with 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games. He credited his coaches and parents, Randy and Brenda, for his development and said improved defensive play created more offensive opportunities. After Flint’s 4-1 playoff loss to Sault Ste. Marie, Henderson played three ECHL games with the South Carolina Stingrays before roster space became limited. He described the experience as exciting and welcomed by the team. Still deciding between professional hockey in North America or Europe and school, he remains committed to the sport, which he said has been central to his life and opened many opportunities.

Since the 1990s, ICT adoption, digital policies, and telecommunications deregulation have expanded online education across African universities, although the continent still faces low internet penetration, a pronounced urban–rural access gap, weak ICT infrastructure, limited digital materials, inadequate lecturer training, pedagogical challenges, and resistance to technology. Warfare compounds these problems by destroying educational infrastructure, disrupting programmes and safety, reducing household affordability, displacing academics and students, and weakening ICT deployment. Online learning can sustain education and broaden access during conflicts, but requires targeted training and effective technological adaptation.

The study used bibliometric analysis to examine research on wartime and online education. Scopus was searched for publications from 2000–2024, with 2,140 records initially screened, 90 retrieved after narrowing the query, and 53 included after further screening. Excel and VOSviewer were used for analysis and visualisation. The 53 documents came from 14 countries or territories, including five unidentified; the United States led with 21 publications, followed by Ukraine with 10. Publications increased sharply to 12 in 2023 before falling to five in 2024. Articles comprised 76.9% of the corpus, followed by book chapters at 17.3%; social sciences was the largest subject area at 55%.

No included study originated from an African country. A narrower search including war, education, and online learning produced five publications from Ukraine, Austria, and the United States. Keyword analysis identified separate clusters concerning learning and warfare. The authors conclude that research on wartime online learning in African higher education is seriously deficient, emphasising the need for further study of organisational sustainability, brain drain, psychological trauma, and inclusive access for people with disabilities. The analysis was limited to Scopus and did not examine authorship, affiliations, citations, or reference connections.

GST is scheduled for July 1. The civil aviation ministry requested a two-month deferral, citing airlines’ need to adapt systems and unresolved tax concerns involving aircraft parts, ticket distribution and operating costs; the finance ministry maintained the launch was on track.

The lecture reviews VCG mechanisms for private-value social-choice problems, in which players privately know their types, utilities depend on allocations and transfers, and social alternatives need not be simple goods. A mechanism maps strategy profiles to allocations and payments. The utilitarian solution selects the alternative maximizing total utility; second- and first-price auctions implement this outcome in dominant-strategy and Bayesian Nash equilibrium, respectively. The VCG mechanism implements the utilitarian solution by having players report their types, choosing the utilitarian allocation based on those reports, and charging each player the negative externality imposed on others. Truth-telling is a dominant-strategy Bayesian Nash equilibrium. VCG is not budget balanced, and dominant-strategy implementation cannot generally be budget balanced. Its practical limitations include enormous action and bidding spaces, as illustrated by the simultaneous auction of cellular-service licenses in 394 U.S. cities.

The lecture then turns to Google, described as the dominant global search engine, with reported worldwide market share above 90% and revenues of about $100 billion. Its search profits support ventures including Android, Gmail, Chrome, Chrome OS, Google Docs, Google Cloud, and Google Meet. The U.S. Department of Justice and several states have accused Google of monopolizing search or online advertising. Every Google search conducts an advertising auction, and the number and placement of ads vary with the commercial nature of the query. The lecture contrasts this with Yahoo!’s earlier unweighted first-price auctions, which produced rapid bid cycling and irrelevant ads, and with Google’s quality-weighted system.

Advertisers submit standing per-click bids based on queries, audience characteristics, and other criteria. Google multiplies each applicable bid by a quality score, ranks advertisers by the product, and selects up to 11 ads. A clicked advertiser pays an amount based on the next-ranked advertiser’s bid, with the quality weights helping prevent ads unlikely to satisfy users from winning merely because of high bids. Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz model this system as a clock or English-auction equivalent to a generalized second-price auction. It differs from VCG because bidders report only one-dimensional per-click values rather than values for every possible page arrangement, and truthful bidding is not generally optimal. Their equilibrium analysis shows bid shading, but the resulting equilibrium payments reproduce VCG payments. This equivalence makes the mechanism ex post equilibrium, supports efficient allocation, and gives Google protection against competitors undercutting ad prices while retaining efficient ad selection. It also directs payments from advertisers to Google.

The quality weights are therefore central to the system, and Google also uses reservation prices that can prevent ads from appearing on pages. Athey and Ellison extend the position-auction model by adding consumers with search costs, advertiser quality that is private information, and consumer needs. An ordering of ads by quality can guide consumers through a top-down search process. In their model, reserve prices need not reduce welfare: they can signal that displayed ads are worth reading and thereby increase clicks and consumer surplus. With uniformly distributed search costs, the reserve price that maximizes consumer surplus also maximizes social welfare. The authors note a conflict between Google and advertisers: a higher reserve may benefit Google by reducing consumer surplus and advertiser surplus, while the consumer-optimal reserve benefits both groups.

The lecture briefly reviews Anderson and Renault’s model of endogenous seller pricing, in which top-position firms may lower prices to prevent consumers from searching lower positions, producing multiple equilibria with different consumer and firm welfare. It also summarizes Armstrong and Zhou’s analysis of platform information design for Amazon-like marketplaces. Revealing which product consumers prefer can improve product matching but also give sellers market power, whereas minimal preference information can intensify price competition. Their results suggest that platform information mainly redistributes surplus between consumers and producers rather than greatly changing overall equilibrium welfare. The next lecture will address empirical research on online markets, particularly online retail and consumer preferences.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for tax year 2026, applying to returns filed in 2027. The standard deduction rises to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single filers. The 37% top rate applies to taxable income above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 or more for joint filers. The IRS also updated long-term capital gains brackets, estate and gift tax exemptions, and earned-income and child tax credit eligibility. The announcement followed the IRS’s decision to furlough nearly half its workforce amid the government shutdown.

The passage describes embodiments for managing indexed data in computing environments, particularly optimizing index-file size based on storage conditions associated with indexed data. It identifies growing volumes of machine-generated data as a challenge: indexes accelerate retrieval, but their increasing storage requirements raise storage and operating costs.

Most of the text presents an event-based data intake and query system similar to SPLUNK Enterprise. Forwarders ingest, segment, annotate, and route raw data to indexers; indexers determine event boundaries and timestamps, apply optional transformations, build keyword indexes, and store timestamped events in time-based buckets. Search heads distribute query portions among indexers and combine returned events or partial results. A late-binding schema applies extraction rules at search time, enabling fields from heterogeneous sources to be extracted and correlated through common field names or a common information model.

Client applications may contain monitoring code that collects network, device, and application performance data. Hierarchical data models define searches, fields, and inherited event subsets, supporting reports, filtering, aggregation, and visualization. Acceleration methods include parallel searching, keyword indexes, summarization tables, and intermediate summaries for recurring reports.

The system may operate on premises or as a cloud service and can provide security-threat monitoring, alerts, data-center performance analysis, dashboards, and correlation of logs, events, and performance metrics. Drawings depict system architectures, ingestion and search flows, reporting interfaces, and a process and file diagrams for optimizing index-file size.

The passage specifies the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines GHCB and MSR fields for protocol-version negotiation, obtaining the page-table encryption bit, CPUID requests, termination reasons, GHCB GPA selection, registration and unregistration, and page-state changes. It describes GHCB negotiation, #VC and VMGEXIT processing, VALID_BITMAP handling, error reporting, and supported non-automatic exit events, including SNP guest, extended, and TIO requests; AP creation; APIC ID discovery; Secure AVIC backing pages; and termination. It also covers SNP secrets and CPUID pages, EFI configuration, AP reset-hold and jump-table procedures, and the SNP AP Creation alternative to hotplug. Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing pending-event and EOI-assist fields, with specified host APIC emulation and atomic guest acknowledgment requirements. The specification states that SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported, while vCPU hotplug is supported through SNP AP Creation.

Egyptian archaeologists unveiled the Fifth Dynasty tomb of Hetpet, an Old Kingdom priestess of Hathor, in Giza’s western cemetery. Its rare, well-preserved wall paintings depict Hetpet hunting, fishing, receiving offerings, and scenes of music and dancing, including a monkey dancing before an orchestra. The tomb also contains a purification basin engraved with Hetpet’s name and titles. Excavation will continue.

SOS full-court pressure disrupts offenses, changes tempo, creates turnovers, rushed shots, and transition chances. “Shadow” primary presses use a second defender behind the on-ball defender; “Blitz” secondary presses deny first passing lanes and trap in the backcourt. Presses vary by personnel and situation. Success requires SOS fundamentals, including forcing the ball to side or corner checkpoints and denying middle penetration. Except for “hold” actions, presses end in Base Go Red; pressure stops if the shadow defender cannot position or an outlet pass enters the middle.

The invention relates to localizing and classifying abnormalities in medical images and to training adaptable medical-image deep-learning models. Embodiments address lesions, bleeding, and other abnormalities across various anatomical structures, imaging modalities, and image dimensionalities, with prostate lesions and multi-parametric MRI used as examples.

A jointly trained multi-task network uses an encoder-decoder localization network to generate a binary or probability heat map identifying an abnormality and a neural classification network to classify it from the input image and heat map. Training occurs in multiple phases: the localization network is trained first, the classification network is then trained using the localization network’s weights, and both are subsequently fine-tuned jointly. Binary cross-entropy losses may be combined with weighting factors. Training uses annotated images, lesion contours or center-based Gaussian-blurred maps, binary labels, false-negative cases, and optional anatomical masks. Post-processing may use lesion size, intensity statistics, radiomic features, and lexicon-based features such as PI-RADS to produce clinical-relevance maps and reduce false positives.

A multi-modality fusion network processes images acquired under different MRI protocols through separate localization networks, combines their localization maps by concatenation, summation, or nonlinear merging, and supplies the combined map and source images to the classification network. Preprocessing may register modalities, standardize dimensions and spacing, normalize intensities, align images around the target anatomy, and interpolate diffusion images to a common b-value. A regression network can additionally score lesions, such as with PI-RADS scores, through scored heat maps or cropped patches classified by a multiclass neural network.

Another embodiment detects abnormalities by learning normal tissue. Portions of an input medical image are removed using stencils or other deletion patterns to create incomplete images. A trained generative adversarial network synthesizes normal tissue into the deleted regions. A synthesized image depicting the healthiest tissue is selected as the normal image, in one case by maximizing its distance from the input image. A detector compares the input and normal images to produce a localization map for the abnormality. The detector may be trained using ground-truth masks with Dice and binary cross-entropy losses. During adversarial training, a generator produces realistic normal-tissue completions while a discriminator distinguishes real from synthesized images; the discriminator is not used during inference.

The invention also provides two-stage training for clinical datasets from multiple sites. A model pretrained on a large source dataset is fine-tuned iteratively with smaller site datasets ordered by similarity to the source. Each update is retained only when cross-validation performance is at least as good as that of the pretrained model and the model trained on the pooled data. During deployment, labeled samples from the target site are ordered by uncertainty, determined from pseudo-label posterior probabilities and annotations. The model is selectively updated with these samples when performance improves relative to both the existing model and a model trained solely on the labeled deployment data, while maintaining multi-site performance within a defined tolerance. The resulting optimized model is stored or transmitted for deployment.

Perineuronal nets (PNNs), extracellular-matrix structures that stabilize synapses and restrict plasticity, may contribute to the persistence of drug-associated reward memories and cue-induced relapse. This study examined PNNs, WFA-labeled glia, and gene expression in postmortem hippocampi from people with substance use disorder (SUD; n=20), SUD with major depressive disorder (MDD; n=24), MDD alone (n=20), and psychiatric controls (n=20), along with rhesus macaques with or without chronic alcohol self-administration.

Compared with controls, subjects with SUD had increased PNN densities in CA1 stratum oriens and several additional hippocampal regions, along with increased WFA-glia in CA4 and the dentate gyrus. Pvb and Vamp2 expression increased, while Mmp9 and Ctss expression decreased and Chsy1 increased; Acan and Gfap did not differ significantly. MDD alone generally produced opposite PNN changes, including reduced densities in CA1 and increased density in CA4. Comorbid SUD/MDD showed mixed PNN and glial changes, increased Acan and Chsy1 expression, and decreased Gfap expression, indicating that depression can mask or amplify pathology associated with SUD.

Rhesus macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration also had increased PNN densities in the combined hippocampus, CA1 stratum oriens, and CA3 strata, as well as increased WFA-glia in the dentate gyrus granule cell layer.

The findings provide human and nonhuman-primate evidence that increased hippocampal PNNs and reduced ECM proteolytic gene expression accompany chronic substance use, supporting a possible role in stabilizing contextual reward memories. Comorbid MDD substantially influences these measures and should be considered in SUD pathology and treatment strategies. Limitations include polysubstance use, medication effects, WFA labeling of only part of the PNN population, and the inability to determine which cell types account for qPCR expression changes.

University of Virginia Health System’s first-year review of its thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery program found shorter hospital stays, reduced opioid use, and lower costs without increased surgical complications or readmissions. Compared with more than 220 previous patients, the multidisciplinary program standardizes preoperative preparation, nutrition, fluid management, pain prevention, and patient engagement. Offensive goal kicks aim to retain possession and initiate an attack rather than immediately return the ball to opponents. Under Law 16, a goal kick follows an attacker sending the ball over the defending end line. It may be taken from anywhere in the goal area, with the ball stationary, and opponents must remain outside the penalty area until the kick. The ball becomes live once kicked and visibly moves; no player may then touch it except the original kicker.

For players generally 10 and under, smaller fields and build-out lines help teams play out from the back. Defenders must retreat beyond the build-out line before challenging. Coaches can use a designated kicker and nearby target player, with a secondary upfield option, emphasizing kicks toward the sideline, keeping the ball wide and moving upfield, and never sending it across the defending goal.

For players 11 and above, target positions become more advanced. The kick may go to a player near the sideline, a farther-wide target, or an uncovered supporting midfielder. Targets should move forcefully toward the ball, and teams should prepare formations for both sides of the goal area. Coaches add passive and active defenders so players learn to account for coverage and realistic kicking distances.

At the adult level, advanced players may use short kicks to advancing teammates, prearranged targets, or deep kicks to runners. The goalkeeper commonly takes the kick to avoid removing an attacking player. Coaches should also explain that a goal kick is a direct restart and that wind or other field conditions can cause it to score, be returned toward the kicking team’s goal, or lead to a corner.

A prospective descriptive cross-sectional study assessed scorpion-sting cases admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in Eritrea’s Gash-Barka region from June 2019 to May 2020. Among 165 patients, 48.5% were male and 51.5% female; 61.8% were at least 15 years old, 57% lived in urban areas, and shepherds, students, and farmers were the most common occupational groups. Most stings occurred at night, indoors, and on the foot or hand. Cases peaked during summer, particularly September and October.

Using Abroug’s classification, 20.6% of cases were Class I, 35.8% Class II, and 43.6% Class III. The most common manifestations were localized pain, sweating, vomiting, paraesthesia, relative bradycardia, restlessness, and fever. Eight patients died, giving a case-fatality rate of 4.8%. Class III envenomation was associated with fatality, while age under 15 and no formal education were reported as possible predisposing factors for severity; sex, scorpion color, and number of stings were not significant risk factors. Although adults accounted for more cases, severe manifestations were more frequent among children.

Mild cases were generally treated with local anesthesia and oral analgesics; diazepam was used for convulsions, shock, or restlessness, while 15.2% received nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom for moderate-to-severe symptoms. Treatment efficacy could not be determined because antivenom and prazosin were unavailable.

The study was limited by its single-hospital setting, unregistered cases, incomplete post-discharge follow-up, and difficulties recording scorpion color and urban-rural residence. The authors recommended preventive education, protective footwear and mosquito nets, storing firewood away from homes, improved access to essential medicines and updated treatment guidelines, further clinical and habitat studies, and better documentation and reporting of scorpion stings.

The passage explains random walk theory and its application as a passive trading strategy. First associated with Louise Bachelier and popularized by Burton Malkiel in *A Random Walk Down Wall Street* (1973), the theory holds that stock-price changes are random and independent, making historical analysis and attempts to forecast prices unreliable. The strategy therefore uses random entries and exits while diversifying across stocks or investing in a broad-market index fund, because prices are assumed equally likely to rise or fall.

The random walk theory is related to the efficient market hypothesis (EMH), associated with William Sharpe. Both imply that consistently outperforming the market is nearly impossible and favor passive, diversified investing. However, they differ: random walk describes market movements as irrational and random, while EMH says prices reflect available information. The passage also notes challenges to both theories, including delayed price adjustments, market trends, behavioral patterns, and successful investors.

Malkiel’s view was tested through the Wall Street Journal’s Dartboard Contest. Across 140 contests, experts won 87 and darts won 55, but experts did not beat the Dow Jones Industrial Average by a statistically significant margin, suggesting that passive funds’ lower fees may offer an advantage.

In an Amibroker backtest with 12 random entries annually, the S&P 500 ETF produced an average trade gain of 0.37%, a 1.7 profit factor, and a 13% maximum drawdown. A similar gold ETF test produced an average loss of 0.08% and did not replicate the stock-market result. The main takeaway is to avoid market timing and use diversification to manage risk while benefiting from the market’s long-term upward tendency.

The report traces a long-standing U.S. policy opposing foreign interference in Hawaii while contemplating annexation. It cites proposals for a U.S. protectorate or statehood in 1850, a conditional cession agreement in 1851, and a draft annexation treaty in 1854. Subsequent officials increasingly favored annexation when it conflicted with reciprocity or Hawaii’s strategic importance. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, U.S. administrations defended exclusive American commercial rights and supported Hawaii’s existing government so long as it protected U.S. interests. Secretary Blaine described Hawaii as key to American dominance in the Pacific and indicated that an “American solution” would be sought if benevolent neutrality became impracticable. The report was submitted by John W. Foster on February 15, 1893. A second document begins a history of official U.S.–Hawaiian relations, noting that John C. Jones was appointed in 1820 as U.S. agent for commerce and seamen, with responsibility for supervising American interests and reporting to the Department of State.

Official fuel-economy figures use urban, extra-urban and combined results from the NEDC test cycle. The NEDC has been criticised as unrealistic and easy to manipulate: it allows a 4% reduction in results, omits sustained motorway driving, permits eco mode and disabled electrical loads, and allows cars to be made lighter through removed equipment or inflated tyres. It was due to be replaced by the tougher WLTP cycle from September 2017, with all new cars sold in the UK required to use WLTP figures from September 2018.

Which? conducts rolling-road tests using cold, hot and motorway WLTP cycles in the same controlled lab. Cars are tested in their default mode with electrical loads operating, without removing equipment, overinflating tyres or adjusting results. Motorway testing reveals cars that are economical at low speeds but consume more fuel at higher speeds. Hybrid testing uses defined battery-charge levels and accounts for electricity used. Which? found annual fuel costs for medium-sized hatchbacks could differ by more than £800.

The same testing measures NOx, carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and particulate matter; heavily polluting vehicles cannot receive a Best Buy rating. Additional on-road Portable Emissions Measuring System tests can expose attempts to manipulate laboratory results, although controlled laboratory testing remains necessary for repeatability. The passage cites Volkswagen’s 2015 defeat-device scandal and reported recalls affecting 8.5 million European cars, including 1.2 million in the UK. Which? publishes mpg figures for every reviewed car, covering more than 700 vehicles, and tests around 120 new cars annually.

Red anthuriums, or “tongues of fire,” come from South America and filter ammonia and xylene, though their sap and leaves can cause allergies. They need bright indirect light, humidity, 18–21°C, winter misting, and yearly repotting.

The study uses a quasi-experimental approach to assess how college teaching modalities affect nearby county COVID-19 cases and deaths. It matches similar colleges that selected in-person, hybrid, or online instruction and compares outcomes across those pairs. The evidence indicates that reopening—especially with in-person teaching—increases community cases and deaths over time. The analysis accounts for endogenous modality selection, testing increases, delayed deaths, other schools, and differences in reopening dates, while using cellphone mobility data and reweighting. County-level outcomes are examined because students may transmit the virus to nonstudents and vulnerable community members.

The paper studies finitely generated right Gorenstein-projective modules over the dual integer ring \(\mathbb Z[\varepsilon]=\mathbb Z[T]/(T^2)\). It relates them to torsionless modules, perfect differential structures of abelian groups, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups, while noting the category lacks Krull–Remak–Schmidt uniqueness. Its main theorem establishes equivalences among five stable categories: Gorenstein-projective modules modulo projectives, submodules of finitely generated free modules modulo projectives, \(D^b(\mathbb Z)/[1]\), perfect differential structures, and stable perfect differential structures. The result also extends to any principal ideal domain. A chain of dense functors connects bounded complexes of free abelian groups, Gorenstein-projective modules, their stable category, and finite abelian groups; composing functors modulo shifts, projectives, and maps factoring through stalk objects produces a cube with commutative faces.

An IDC survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland examined IT-based simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC).

More than half of respondents already use simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping to test product feasibility and functionality, reducing physical prototypes and accelerating development. Digital twins, IoT, and sensor data can create feedback loops that provide operational insights, support process optimization, and enable services such as Product-as-a-Service. Digital visualization, cloud-based engineering workstations, AR/VR, mathematical optimization, and high-performance data analytics further expand these capabilities.

Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise substantially: only 8% currently report high demand, but nearly half are expected to do so within two years. Half report that calculations take too long, while 42% say their simulations are already outdated or inaccurate. Four out of five decision makers regard HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables complex calculations, faster and more extensive analysis, new usage scenarios, and greater agility.

More than one-quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, and another 39% are planning or piloting it. Most favor external infrastructure: 87% of HPC users prefer or plan external services, 74% operate or plan colocation environments, and 43% use or plan to use research institutions. Only 6% currently operate on-premises HPC infrastructure. Major challenges include security, cost, insufficient expertise, energy consumption, computing capacity, availability, scalability, and the complexity of maintaining systems.

IDC expects public-cloud and hybrid-cloud HPC to become the leading architectures, followed by prebuilt systems. HPC-as-a-Service offers flexible capacity, cost optimization, rapid access to modern hardware and methods, collaboration, and support for new data-based business models; 81% of enterprises already using HPC intend to develop such models. Recommendations include implementing virtual development, creating a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, selecting an HPC operating model based on utilization and security needs, prioritizing scalability and energy efficiency, and obtaining external expertise when required.

This preprint introduces a hierarchical Bayesian multinomial modeling approach for estimating the growth and prevalence of competing viral variants from sparse genomic sequence data, and applies it to SARS-CoV-2.

**Motivation and data landscape.** Viral genome sequencing has shifted from retrospective research toward near-real-time analysis, enabling variant characterization that informs public health practice, forecasting, and vaccine, therapeutic, and diagnostic development. However, genomic data are highly unevenly distributed: 90% of publicly available SARS-CoV-2 sequences come from just 10% of countries. As of July 1, 2022, the United States and United Kingdom had contributed 54.9% of sequences submitted to GISAID, and 10% of submitting countries produced 90.3% of sequences; most high-capacity countries are in the Global North, while most African and Middle Eastern countries submitted only a few thousand sequences. Sparsity reflects both limited "sequencing capacity" and limited "sequencing effort." Sequencing also accelerates over the life of a variant—slow linear growth at low prevalence, then exponential growth once a variant reaches high-capacity countries—meaning surveillance of emerging variants is largely confined to a few high-resource geographies.

**Method.** Established regression approaches (multinomial or logistic) account for changing sampling intensity but require large numbers of sequences, handle geographic heterogeneity poorly, and are inaccurate at small sample sizes, causing under- or over-estimates of variant fitness. Pooling sequences across countries is complicated by differing immune landscapes and seeding dynamics. The authors address this with a hierarchical mixed-effects Bayesian multinomial model with two levels of hierarchy: country-specific variant fitness advantages are drawn from a shared distribution of each variant's global fitness advantage, and variants' global mean fitness advantages are drawn from a shared normal distribution across all variants. This shrinkage yields robust estimates even with extremely sparse data, estimating within-country prevalence, within-country growth rate, and global relative fitness. Assumptions include random sampling within countries, no prioritization of one variant over another, correct lineage assignment, even mixing within a country, time-invariant relative fitness, and equal generation intervals; estimates may remain robust to sampling biases if sequences come from a consistent population subset.

**Results for SARS-CoV-2.** From April to July 2022, global BA.2 prevalence declined while BA.4 and BA.5 expanded. Invasion dynamics were heterogeneous: BA.4 and BA.5 rose in parallel in South Africa, BA.5 grew substantially more in Israel and Bangladesh, and Senegal had not experienced substantial BA.5 invasion by July 1, 2022. Estimated BA.5 prevalence was 56.5% (CI 21.2–83.4%) in Bangladesh versus 13.8% (CI 1.1–17.6%) in India. Country-specific fitness advantages were heterogeneous within variants: BA.5 was 1.31 (CI 1.29–1.33) in the US and 1.21 (CI 1.17–1.24) in the UK versus 0.42 (CI 0.34–0.52) in India and 0.35 (CI 0.31–0.41) in South Africa; BA.2.12.1 was 0.29 (CI 0.29–0.30) in the US but 0.66 (CI 0.64–0.69) in the UK. Global mean relative weekly fitness advantages were 0.94 for BA.5 (CI 0.85–1.03), 0.67 for BA.4 (CI 0.59–0.73), 0.45 for BA.2.12.1 (CI 0.40–0.50), and −0.24 for BA.1 (CI −0.27 to −0.21), all relative to BA.2.

**Validation.** Retrospective validation across five reference dates (April 30, May 16, May 27, June 4, June 27, and July 1, 2022) compared the multicountry model with single-country MLE multinomial fits, using BA.5's emergence in Portugal as a case study. The multicountry model gave lower Brier scores at early dates (0.34 and 0.32 versus 0.42 and 0.73) and produced more stable country-specific fitness estimates; the single-country model could not estimate fitness for variants with fewer than three sequences in a country, while the multicountry model could. Global mean fitness estimates were highly stable over time, though country-specific estimates from the multicountry model showed a transient positive bias. Statistical regularization reduced overfitting to noisy emergence data and the resulting overestimates of growth rates seen with standard multinomial regression.

**Discussion and methods.** The approach provides stable growth-rate characterization and improved nowcasting of variant prevalence, complements sequencing capacity building, and is relevant for lower- and middle-income countries. It was also applied to influenza strain dynamics and to sub-country analyses (AL1 in Brazil and Argentina; US state-level data), and a live dashboard nowcasts variant prevalence and fitness advantage globally. Future work will extend to additional pathogens and explicitly include immune-landscape drivers (prior infections, vaccine coverage), mobility, and assortative mixing.

For modeling, GISAID line-list metadata were aggregated by country, collection date, and Pango lineage; lineages with fewer than 50 sequences were grouped as "Other." Relative growth rates were converted to weekly fitness advantage via f = e^(7r) − 1. Model outputs were compared against observed data using 100 bootstrap resamples and the Brier score across calibration and 21-day forecast periods.

On Oct. 30, 2001, Enron shares fell roughly 18%–20% to about $11, an eight-year low, after Moody’s cut the company’s senior unsecured debt rating from Baa1 to Baa2, placed its commercial-paper rating under review, and Enron sought additional bank credit lines. The stock had lost 83% for the year and more than $15 billion in market capitalization over two weeks. Enron had reported a $1.01 billion quarterly loss, asset write-downs, and a $1.2 billion reduction in equity, while the SEC investigated off-balance-sheet partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow, who was dismissed. Enron bond default-insurance costs doubled, major trading partners continued doing business while limiting exposure, and NYMEX introduced over-the-counter clearing to help counterparties manage credit concerns.

New CFO Jeff McMahon said Enron Industrial Markets would continue its forest-products business without reducing capital. Its newsprint trading volume rose from under 5,000 metric tons in January to 60,000 tons in July, with officials projecting 120,000 tons by year-end. McMahon aimed to make Enron a leading North American newsprint marketer, change how publishers and producers manage price risk, and create a pricing benchmark. He acknowledged hurdles including publishers’ concerns about paper quality and said long-term hedging could reduce price volatility while supporting demand for Enron’s financial products.

U.S. stocks also fell as consumer confidence dropped to 85.5, its lowest level since February 1994, amid job losses, post-Sept. 11 concerns, and fears of recession. Commentary argued that Enron’s ultimate stock bottom would depend more on when the Janus fund finished selling its large position than on the company obtaining credit or its financial fundamentals.

Germany’s cartel office warned it might sue four grid operators unless they changed how they charged competitors for balancing energy, practices that smaller entrants, including Enron Capital & Resources, said burdened them.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis received the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in a macroscopic superconducting circuit in the 1980s. Their Josephson-junction experiments showed that quantum effects could operate at a chip scale and helped establish the basis for superconducting qubits. Similar circuits are now used in quantum computers. Martinis later led Google’s quantum-computing team, which claimed in 2019 to have achieved a calculation beyond classical capabilities.

The push-pull converter design uses an 80-V GaN synchronous rectifier FET for an expected maximum secondary voltage of about 20 V, with a parallel Schottky diode to reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp limits switch-node overshoot; initial resistor and capacitor values are calculated from allowable overshoot, leakage inductance, primary current, and capacitor ripple, then optimized through testing. The selected output inductor is 0.47 µH with a target ripple current of 40%. Output-capacitance calculations for 2% voltage ripple and 2.5% maximum transient deviation require at least 1.3 mF; approximately 2.3 mF is used for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. This is provided by seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors with a combined ESR of 0.86 mΩ. An optional LC filter can further reduce output noise, with resistor damping available for high-frequency peaking.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current. Primary current is sensed through a 1:100 current-sense transformer, and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor was selected. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover; selected values are 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF. A 102-kΩ resistor connects RSC to AVSS for slope compensation.

The controllers operate from a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and require at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably X5R or better ceramic, with added bulk capacitance for remote supplies. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control signals from power components and switch-node traces, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loop areas, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and filtering CS_ILIM as needed. SYNC routing must avoid sensitive pins, and the HICC-to-AVSS capacitor should be at least 3.3 nF. CFP packages require backside metallization to be connected to AVSS through multiple vias.

The passage recounts the emergence of “open source” in February 1998, when Christine Peterson proposed the term at a meeting prompted by Netscape’s decision to release its source code. “Open source” was intended as a commercially palatable alternative to Stallman’s “free software,” though both emphasize source-code availability and user freedom. After the Open Source Definition was published, open-source practices spread widely. Major technology companies, including Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, and Microsoft, came to depend on open-source software, while Linux and Darwin underpinned Android and iOS devices. Microsoft notably embraced open source despite Steve Ballmer’s earlier criticism of Linux and the GPL. Red Hat’s Tim Burke said open-source projects initially sought alternatives to proprietary applications but have since become a center of innovation rather than simple cloning.

J. Bernstorff reported that the blockade would end if a conference could be convened on reasonable terms; delivery of the official translation was delayed. Ambassador Gerard said Zimmermann provided submarine materials and that Bernstorff was authorized to communicate Germany’s peace terms confidentially and urge Wilson to pursue peace and remain quiet for two months, expecting submarine warfare to force England to seek terms. Reported German terms included relinquishing Belgium while retaining control of railways, forts, ports, and commerce; a French border rectification; limited restoration of Serbia; freedom for Bulgaria regarding Romania; and German indemnities. Greece said the Entente would permit essential food pending the blockade’s lifting but alleged unaccounted rifles. Austria-Hungary maintained that it was fighting defensively and sought a “peace without victory” based on Wilson’s proposal, arguing that Entente aims to dismember it prevented peace. It said submarine-war changes required allied consultation and could not reach submarines already at sea, and asked Wilson to influence the Entente and halt U.S. war supplies.

Energy storage can absorb grid or locally generated power and release it later, but must provide savings greater than capital, charging and round-trip efficiency costs. Technologies suit different scales: lithium-ion batteries are lightweight and efficient for small-scale use but costly; pumped hydro is efficient and inexpensive per unit for large-scale storage; flywheels dispatch rapidly and support frequency stability. Compressed air, liquid air, flow batteries and hydrogen also offer distinct advantages and drawbacks.

Lithium-ion costs fell from US$1,200 to US$600 per kWh in five years, excluding installation. In the example household, a 7kWh battery must cost below A$7,000 installed to break even, placing current batteries near viability. Retail tariffs may overstate wholesale price differences, making battery economics less favorable. Avoided network upgrades provide savings only where electricity demand is growing. Pumped hydro costs about A$100 per kWh and is easier for the market operator to control, but its use is geographically limited. Despite this, distributed lithium-ion storage may ultimately prevail because of human behavior rather than economics.

The Korean diet is based on traditional Korean eating habits and emphasizes whole, unprocessed foods, including vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fermented foods, and broth-based dishes. It limits processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy, and generally uses smaller portions, although Western influence has modernized it. Its plant-based, high-fibre, antioxidant-rich foods and fermented products are presented as supporting overall wellbeing and gut health; combined with physical activity and portion control, the diet may aid weight loss. Considerations include potentially high sodium from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium due to limited dairy, high carbohydrate content in foods such as rice and noodles, and spices that may irritate digestive issues. It can be adapted for vegan, low-carbohydrate, and gluten-free diets through alternatives such as tofu, tempeh, gluten-free soy sauce, and rice-based noodles.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end for ATE applications. Its speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS by converting a user-selected analog input pair on every sampling clock while the other six channels remain idle. The data-output interface is unchanged in this mode, and speed-boost settings are controlled through registers including 37h, C5h, and 19h.

The configuration interface provides 16-bit registers in three banks with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible, while REG_BANK_SEL at address 03h selects banks 1 or 2. Register writes require SPI_RD_EN to be cleared and can select a bank before writing the target register. Register reads require SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE to be set, followed by an address frame and a frame that returns the 16-bit register value; read access is then disabled.

Multiple ADCs can be connected in an SPI daisy chain with shared CS and SCLK and chained SDI/SDO connections. DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the number of devices after ADC1 and must be configured after power-up or reset. A write to N chained devices requires N × 24 SCLKs. Daisy-chain register reads use address frames containing 0xFE followed by data-return frames containing 0xFF, 0xFF, and 0xFF.

Register descriptions cover SPI and daisy-chain modes, bank selection, data formatting and averaging, XOR and PRBS functions, digital test patterns, user-defined output bits, speed-boost channel selection, gain-error correction, analog bandwidth and power-down control, reference selection, output-lane configuration, common-mode range, and initialization settings.

For ATE signal-chain use, the ADS9803 supports separate PMU-output connections or multiplexing multiple PMU outputs to one ADC channel. Its bandwidth modes are low-noise, up to 22.7 kHz, and wide-bandwidth, up to 700 kHz; wide-bandwidth operation settles to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. With external offset and gain calibration, total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed 109 patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage who underwent aneurysm clipping or coiling at Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital from 2013 to 2021. All patients received external ventricular drainage and an EVD challenge; those with failed challenges or subsequent hydrocephalus underwent ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery. Multivariate logistic regression identified three independent predictors of shunt-dependent hydrocephalus: age ≥65 years (OR 3.94), aneurysm clipping rather than coiling (OR 4.36), and Hunt and Hess scale ≥3 (OR 3.59). A nomogram assigning one point to each predictor was developed to estimate hydrocephalus risk. Its predictive performance had an AUC of 0.753 (95% CI 0.66–0.84), and calibration testing showed a Hosmer–Lemeshow p-value of 0.963. Aneurysm location, Fisher grade, and NLR, PLR, and PNR were not significant predictors in this cohort. The authors concluded that the nomogram may aid clinical risk assessment, but noted its retrospective design, limited sample size, and need for prospective validation.

Nike reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.72 billion, up 1% and above Wall Street expectations despite previously forecasting a mid-single-digit decline. Researchers found live specimens of the giant shipworm *Kuphus polythalamia* in a lagoon at an abandoned log farm in the Philippines. Scientists are studying microbes in its single gill for potential antimicrobial substances, with findings published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Its elephant-tusk-like shells can reach five feet and often wash ashore. Researchers said the species likely evolved from wood-eating shipworms but that its life cycle, age, and other populations remain unknown.

Climate change is bringing earlier, warmer, drier springs to northern Rocky Mountain streams, threatening native cutthroat trout adapted to cold, small waterways. Warmer, lower-flow streams favor introduced rainbow trout, which interbreed with cutthroats, producing less-fit hybrids and eroding locally adapted genes. A study of hundreds of locations found hybridization widespread, especially where rainbows were stocked. Some states are removing rainbows to prevent the cutthroat’s possible extinction.

A nationwide study of 221,789 adults over 67 newly diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease and more than 1.1 million controls found that estimated exposure to outdoor trichloroethylene (TCE) was associated with increased Parkinson’s risk. Using Medicare data and 2002 EPA air-pollution estimates linked to residential ZIP+4 codes, researchers found a 10% higher risk among people in the highest TCE-exposure group after adjusting for age, smoking and fine particulate pollution. Higher risks were also observed closer to two of the three highest TCE-emitting facilities, with hotspots especially in the Rust Belt. TCE is used in metal degreasing, dry cleaning and other industrial applications and persists in U.S. air, water and soil. The study demonstrates association, not causation, and its reliance on outdoor 2002 exposure estimates and Medicare-aged participants may limit applicability.

Chalmers University of Technology researchers used machine-learning-enhanced simulations to determine the low-temperature structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a high-performing halide perovskite material. A pregnant writer explains that after the fifth month, sleeping on her back can compress the vena cava and lower blood pressure, stomach sleeping becomes impossible, and only left-side sleeping is recommended because right-side lying may reduce placental blood flow.
