Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018 identifies the company as a large accelerated filer whose common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “AMZN.” The aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was $693.9 billion as of June 30, 2018, and 491,202,890 shares were outstanding as of January 23, 2019. Amazon was incorporated in Washington in 1994, reincorporated in Delaware in 1996, and completed its initial public offering in May 1997.

Amazon operates through North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It serves consumers through online and physical stores, third-party sellers, digital services, Amazon Prime, and devices such as Kindle e-readers, Fire tablets and TVs, and Echo devices. Its seller programs generate fixed fees, sales percentages, per-unit fees, interest, or combinations thereof. AWS provides compute, storage, database, and related services to developers and enterprises, while Kindle Direct Publishing, Amazon Publishing, and other programs serve authors and content creators. Whole Foods Market results have been consolidated since its acquisition on August 28, 2017. The company emphasizes selection, price, convenience, fulfillment reliability, and customer service, and identifies customer obsession, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking as its guiding principles.

The filing describes intense competition across retail, e-commerce, media, technology, logistics, cloud computing, and payments. Amazon identifies material risks from competition; rapid expansion; limited experience in new products and geographies; fluctuating sales and growth; international operations and regulations, including those in China and India; fulfillment and data-center capacity; seasonality; commercial agreements; acquisitions and investments; foreign exchange; loss of key personnel; data and security breaches; system interruptions; inventory; intellectual property; stock-price volatility; evolving regulation; taxes; suppliers; government contracts; product liability; payments; and unlawful seller activities. It also states that forward-looking statements are uncertain and that the global economic climate amplifies many risks.

As of December 31, 2018, Amazon reported 277.2 million square feet of leased facilities and 11.2 million square feet of owned facilities, including 520 North American and seven international stores. It owned and leased its Seattle headquarters and had announced plans for additional headquarters in New York City and Arlington, Virginia. The company had 2,315 shareholders of record as of January 23, 2019, with no recent unregistered securities sales or issuer purchases of equity securities.

Selected financial results showed net sales increasing from $89.0 billion in 2014 to $232.9 billion in 2018. Operating income rose from $178 million in 2014 to $12.4 billion in 2018, while net income improved from a $241 million loss to $10.1 billion. For 2018, diluted earnings per share were $20.14, operating cash flow was $30.7 billion, total assets were $162.6 billion, and long-term obligations were $50.7 billion.

In 2018, North America generated $141.4 billion in sales and $7.3 billion in operating income; International generated $65.9 billion in sales and a $2.1 billion operating loss; and AWS generated $25.7 billion in sales and $7.3 billion in operating income. Consolidated sales grew 31% over 2017, with growth of 33% in North America, 21% internationally, and 47% in AWS.

At year-end 2018, Amazon held $41.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Operating cash flow was $30.7 billion, investing activities used $12.4 billion, financing activities used $7.7 billion, and cash capital expenditures were $11.3 billion. Purchase obligations totaled $13.1 billion. Amazon stated that available cash flows, marketable securities, and borrowing arrangements should meet operating cash needs for at least the following 12 months. Critical accounting estimates primarily involved inventory valuation and income taxes; each additional 1% of inventory valuation allowance at year-end would have increased cost of sales by approximately $190 million.

Major 2018 operating expenses included $139.2 billion of cost of sales, $34.0 billion of fulfillment, $28.8 billion of technology and content, $13.8 billion of marketing, and $4.3 billion of general and administrative expenses. Shipping costs included in cost of sales were $27.7 billion.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses a 9-period exponential moving average to identify short-term market swings and generate buy and sell signals. A buy signal occurs when price moves above the EMA, while a sell signal occurs when it moves below. The EMA gives greater weight to recent prices.

Backtests produced 284 Bitcoin trades from 2014 onward, averaging a 2.65% gain per trade with an 83% maximum drawdown. Adding a 200-day moving-average trend filter reduced trades to 153 while increasing average gain to 4%. The strategy performed well in trending Bitcoin but poorly in mean-reverting stocks, where it created whipsaws; the added filter improved SPY results but did not make them tradable. A longer lookback period may be needed for stocks.

Traders can confirm signals with RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD, volume, candlestick patterns, or longer-term moving averages. Risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, defined exits, avoiding excessive leverage and emotional trading, and considering market conditions.

The strategy can be applied to forex, stocks, commodities, options, and cryptocurrencies, but the passage states that it is most likely unsuitable for mean-reverting stock markets.

Mark Palmer forwarded a class-action complaint to several Enron executives, noting that a reporter said Enron’s suit would look the same. The complaint, filed in San Diego Superior Court by retail electricity customer Pamela R. Gordon, names Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and 100 unidentified defendants.

The complaint alleges that beginning May 22, 2000, the defendants used confidential real-time generation, outage, and transmission data to manipulate California’s wholesale electricity market by withholding capacity, underbidding forward markets, exporting or parking electricity, and creating artificial shortages and congestion. It says these practices inflated spot-market use and prices, producing major consumer overcharges. FERC, the CPUC, and CAISO reportedly found the prices unjustified or attributable to market power, with the CPUC estimating a $4 billion summer 2000 overcharge.

Gordon seeks certification for approximately 1.2 million SDG&E customers and treble or statutory damages, restitution, disgorgement, interest, fees, and injunctions under California antitrust, unfair-trade, consumer-protection, and unconscionability laws.

GOLDWOOD PLY, one of the top plywood manufacturers in Yamunanagar, Haryana, offers plywood, block boards, and flush doors. The company emphasizes uncompromised quality, timely delivery, transparency, responsible operations, and sustainable development focused on people, growth, and environmental safety.

The passage argues that legislation often has greater practical effect when it attracts little public attention, emphasizing the proposed bill’s importance because the Government had begun pursuing criminal cases involving trusts and interstate commerce. After initially using civil enforcement, the Government justified criminal proceedings because they had produced many successes and deterred wrongdoing through fines and imprisonment.

Judge Holt described illegal railroad rebates as deliberate, premeditated, large-scale discrimination that threatened competitors and was more heinous than crimes arising from passion or temptation. He noted that railroad corporations received valuable public privileges and were obligated to treat customers fairly. Because such violations were secret and difficult to prove, successful prosecution was rare. Holt concluded that the clear, flagrant offense required a serious penalty, primarily imposed on the corporation because the traffic manager appeared to have acted without personal advantage.

The Missouri Student Union held its annual Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, participating in the National Remembrance Day Roll Call by reading the names of MU student veterans killed. Keynote speaker Col. Roderik Cox, an MU alumnus with more than 12 years of combat, peacekeeping and covert-mission experience, defined a veteran as anyone who swore to support and defend the country. Speakers and Veterans Center director Robert Ross emphasized honoring veterans’ sacrifices, hoping for world peace and rejecting Hollywood stereotypes. Ross said the event also allowed veterans to recognize the country’s gratitude; the MU Veterans Center supports more than 400 student veterans. A reception followed at Bengal’s Lair.

The Konektadong Pinoy Act, signed into law on August 24, 2025, aims to remove barriers to Philippine telecommunications competition and enable virtual network operators to compete with PLDT. The author warns that new entrants could intensify pressure as PLDT’s growth slows and profitability declines, while excess investment in a mature, highly penetrated market could further reduce industry profits. Despite PLDT’s attractive valuation, the author considers these risks sufficient to remain on the sidelines.

Joy Williams, a Louisiana registered nurse, will be featured in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare. She earned her practical nursing diploma in 2009 and a BSN in 2016, and advocates continuing education.

U.S. passports expire two years after issuance and require a new application for renewal. A naturalized citizen may use the old passport instead of a naturalization certificate if the prior application contains sufficient naturalization information. One passport may cover an eligible wife, minor children, or servant, with children’s ages and the servant’s allegiance stated; others need separate passports. Applications require a $1 fee in currency or postal money order payable to the State Department’s disbursing clerk; drafts and checks are not accepted. The Secretary of State may reject applications involving unlawful or improper purposes or noncompliance with rules.

In U.S. insular possessions, applications are made to the chief executive; abroad, to a U.S. diplomatic representative, consul general, or consul. Applicants must owe U.S. allegiance. A sworn, attested application must state birth date and place, occupation, and permanent residence, and declare an intent to travel temporarily and return to the United States or an insular possession to reside and perform citizenship duties. Two witnesses are required for mark-signed applications.

The passage reviews small-group differentiation as a strategy for improving learning outcomes and fostering inclusion amid increasing cultural, linguistic, socioeconomic, and disability-related diversity in U.S. schools. Cited enrollment data show changing racial and ethnic demographics, while the proportion of people speaking a non-English language at home rose from 11% in 1980 to 20.3% in 2010. In 2021–22, 7.3 million students received special education or related services.

A systematic search of Ebsco, Embase, Google Scholar, Microsoft Academic Search, and ProProxy covered papers from 2000–2023. Guided by constructivist and sociocultural theories, the review describes differentiation as tailoring teaching methods, content, processes, products, assessments, and learning environments to students’ readiness, interests, abilities, linguistic needs, and backgrounds.

Elementary and higher education require different implementation approaches. Elementary teachers generally provide more direct guidance and foundational instruction, whereas higher education emphasizes specialized content, student independence, self-directed learning, and changing student cohorts. Recommended practices include forming groups based on student profiles, using instructional-level materials, scaffolding with explicit explanations and visuals, gradually increasing task complexity, encouraging student-led discussion and reflection, and regularly assessing and adjusting instruction.

The five cited principles of differentiated learning are flexibility, ongoing assessment, respectful and challenging experiences, collaboration, and student autonomy. Reported benefits include stronger engagement, accountability, repeated practice for struggling students, richer dialogue, deeper relationships, a sense of belonging, and improved support for culturally and linguistically diverse students. Inclusive environments, diverse learning materials, and attention to students’ social-emotional needs are also associated with better learning experiences.

Challenges include substantial planning time, large classes, limited administrative support, insufficient resources, teacher preparation, and the need to understand students before grouping them. The review identifies limited comparative evidence, difficulty assessing relationships among instruction, learning outcomes, and benchmarks, and a shortage of studies comparing small-group instruction with test scores. It recommends longitudinal research across educational levels and studies examining outcomes by learning style.

The paper introduces the open-source **Atlas of Human-AI Interaction**, a framework that uses large language models to synthesize empirical findings across human-AI interaction research. Abstracts were collected from ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer Nature Link, and arXiv in September 2025, yielding 1,888 papers. Claude Opus 4.1 extracted 2,037 findings from 1,124 papers and converted them into structured `[cause, relationship, effect]` triplets, including classifications for subjects, features, relationship direction, and outcome valence.

A five-stage pipeline embedded and normalized the extracted terms, merged synonyms with DBSCAN, clustered entities with k-means, and constructed a knowledge graph containing 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges. The resulting interactive visualizer provides three complementary views: a 3D graph for exploring the field and spotting gaps, a Sankey-style cause-effect view for tracing relationships, and a paper view for searching individual studies. The Atlas is intended to reveal structural patterns, support evidence-based design, and enable continuous integration of new findings.

Analysis produced 24 thematic clusters across human, AI, and conceptual entities. Recurring research areas included education, explanations and trust, design processes, decision support, and self-referential human-AI effects. Louvain community detection identified 126 research communities, while structural-hole analysis highlighted large language models, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and agents as concepts connecting otherwise isolated domains. Proposed research directions include universal LLM interaction patterns, generative-AI collaboration models, transferable trust mechanisms, unified agent-interaction theory, and cross-domain testing frameworks. Longitudinal effects, reciprocal adaptation, broader user populations, and nonprofessional contexts remain underexplored.

A mixed-methods usability study with 20 HAI experts found that Atlas supported landscape visualization, relationship discovery, gap identification, and rapid validation of hypothesized connections. Participants rated its gap-identification and cause-effect functions positively and valued its spatial and multimodal exploration, while noting limitations in paper-level detail, technical or formula-heavy domains, corpus coverage, and temporal analysis. Overall, the study presents AI-assisted literature synthesis as a way to transform research from topic-based catalogs into navigable maps of empirical relationships, while identifying opportunities for improved extraction, broader coverage, richer relationship types, and updated longitudinal analysis.

The 4-3 defense—four defensive linemen, three linebackers and four defensive backs—is among football's most popular schemes. Tom Landry brought it to the NFL with the New York Giants, Jimmy Johnson modernized it at Miami and brought it to Dallas, and Tampa Bay's early-2000s "Tampa 2" version won a Super Bowl in 2003.

In a traditional Under front, the alignment uses two 5-technique ends, a 1-technique nose and a 3-technique tackle, the last widely regarded as the defense's most important player. Linebackers go from big to small: the Sam is largest, the Mike is a sideline-to-sideline defender who must stop the run and cover passes, and the Will is smallest and most athletic. The defensive backs are a strong safety (larger) and a free safety.

Strengths include run defense with seven defenders in the box, gap soundness since each player owns one gap, and four backs allowing multiple coverages. Weaknesses include struggles against modern spread offenses, whose 2x2 formations pull linebackers out of the box, and personnel sensitivity, as larger linebackers struggle in coverage; many teams remove the Sam and use nickel personnel. Offenses attack by spreading, matching the Sam with a speedy receiver, running to the edge with in-line blockers, or hooking the 5-technique end to gain numbers on the edge.

Common blitzes include the Will edge blitz, which puts a hat in every weak-side gap, and the DE drop blitz, a five-man rush with 3-under, 3-deep coverage. Coverages include Tampa 2, where safeties take deep halves, corners play the flats and the Mike drops into the deep hole, and cover 3, where the strong safety disguises the look and falls to linebacker depth.

Teams associated with the defense include the 2000s Buccaneers (Warren Sapp, Derrick Brooks, John Lynch, Simeon Rice), the 2006 NFC champion Chicago Bears under Lovie Smith with Bryan Urlacher, and Montini Catholic High School, where Mike Bukovsky used the 4-3 to win state titles in 2005, 2009–2012 and 2015.

Google has launched Gemini Enterprise, an AI platform for business customers seeking secure, large-scale integration. Built on Google Cloud, it provides Gemini Ultra models, data governance, security, regulatory compliance, proprietary-data fine-tuning, explainability, access controls, traceable outputs, and privacy safeguards. It integrates with Google Workspace and third-party software ecosystems and is positioned for regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and manufacturing. Google is emphasizing transparency and accountability amid competition from Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI. Early feedback has been positive, but the platform’s success will depend on reliability, measurable returns, and seamless integration with existing corporate systems.

The mother appealed a dissolution judgment awarding her $31 per month in support for each of two children, which abated the father’s obligation during visitation, when the children were in his care about half the time. The court agreed that his visitation expenses should be considered but found the award inadequate. Due to difficulties estimating income and applying support formulas, it modified the judgment to require the father to pay $65 per month per child, with no costs to either party.

“Please, Continue (Hamlet),” created by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages Hamlet’s trial for Polonius’ murder in a real courtroom using local judges, barristers and legal teams. Twelve audience members form the jury and have 20 minutes to acquit or convict. Adapted from each country’s laws, the production has toured 12 countries since 2011 and is limited to jurisdictions with jury systems. Inspired by the Guantanamo military commissions and research into criminal trials, it integrates a real case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father. The creators’ conflicting judgments of that case inspired the work’s aim of exposing jurors to competing reasoning and the complexity of justice. Audience members commonly change their views during the trial, while jury participation can alter their perceptions of punishment and personal responsibility.

Ray Dalio and Bridgewater Associates developed the All Weather Portfolio as a diversified, defensive strategy intended to perform across inflation, deflation, stagflation, and other economic conditions. It combines stocks, bonds, and commodities, using diversification and risk balancing to smooth returns and reduce drawdowns. Its risk-parity approach allocates capital based on each asset class’s volatility, although the backtests described do not adjust allocations for volatility.

The portfolio’s long-term returns are lower than those of stocks, but its maximum drawdown is substantially smaller. A backtest from July 2007 produced a 4.5% CAGR with daily rebalancing, or 4.15% with annual rebalancing, before reinvested dividends. Its maximum drawdown was 17%, compared with 55% for the S&P 500 during the 2008/09 financial crisis. It also fell roughly 6% during Covid-19 and 12% in 2022, outperforming stocks during each period. It tends to lag stocks in bull markets but outperform them when stocks perform poorly.

The article describes implementation using ETFs, annual or semiannual rebalancing, and preferably tax-deferred accounts. Rebalancing more often than quarterly is generally viewed as unnecessary. At 1.5 times leverage, the backtest’s CAGR rose to 6.5%, while the maximum drawdown increased to 25%; interest costs were not deducted. Alternative asset weightings produced modestly different returns and drawdowns.

Overall, the All Weather Portfolio prioritizes capital preservation, lower volatility, and smoother performance over aggressive growth. It may suit risk-averse investors, retirees, and FIRE investors, but can underperform stocks and 60/40 portfolios over long periods and does not guarantee future results.

The passage defines the metaverse as a three-dimensional digital environment that merges physical and virtual reality through avatars, enabling immersive interactions and economic activity. In education, it supports interactive, collaborative, and autonomous learning, although adoption depends on perceived usefulness, ease of use, technical training, and user familiarity.

This study uses PRISMA-based systematic review and descriptive bibliometric analysis to examine metaverse education research published in Scopus from 2015 to July 2024. It screened 270 English-language journal articles and analyzed them with VOSviewer 1.6.19. Publications began in 2020 with four articles annually in 2020 and 2021, rose to 36 in 2022, peaked at 131 in 2023, and reached 91 by July 2024. South Korea, China, and the United States were the most productive countries, while South Korea, the United Kingdom, and China led in citations. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies had the most articles, and Sustainability had the most citations. Dwivedi et al. (2022) was the most cited article.

Keyword analysis identified 22 terms in six clusters, led by “metaverse,” “virtual reality,” “education,” “augmented reality,” and “artificial intelligence.” Research themes included creating virtual educational environments through VR, AR, and AI, and examining teachers’ and students’ perceptions and adoption intentions. Identified gaps include limited longitudinal evidence on long-term effectiveness and scalability, geographic concentration in East Asia and the United States, and insufficient cross-cultural comparisons. Future research should assess sustained outcomes, adaptability across classroom formats, and adoption across diverse educational, cultural, and institutional settings.
Order affirmed with $10 costs; Thomas dissented because the ex parte order denied Jones her right to reply.

Michigan State Police and Emergency Management and Homeland Security urged residents to join a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday, with nearly all state facilities participating. Residents were advised to identify a low shelter area, conduct regular drills, monitor weather broadcasts, distinguish tornado watches from warnings, recognize warning signs, and prepare 72-hour emergency supply kits. Tornadoes typically provide only 10–15 minutes of lead time. If severe weather occurs April 19, the drill will move to 1 p.m. Thursday.

The passage presents basketball strategies for improving defensive transition, emphasizing that it begins with disciplined offense: secure the ball, make good shot choices, eliminate unforced turnovers, attack the offensive glass, and maintain defensive balance so opponents cannot easily push the ball.

Defenders should sprint back, remain ahead of and see the ball, get set, and attack rather than retreating passively. The “level of the ball” rule, playing up the lane in a ball-opponent triangle, forcing extra passes, denying long passes, and using help and rotations are central to gaining a numerical advantage and preventing easy baskets.

Training should include outnumbered situations. Against one-on-none, defenders pursue from behind and attempt a low block before rebounding. In two-on-one situations, they contain the dribbler, anticipate the pass, take a charge, and wait for help. In three-on-two situations, players communicate, pressure the ball, use tandem defense, stay or rotate according to the pass, and rebound to counterattack.

After missed shots or blocks, the closest defender jams the rebounder while the point guard’s defender denies the outlet pass. Defenders then match up, sprint back, and use sideline pressure to slow ballhandlers. Outlet passes can be disrupted through aggressive denial, charging or forcing a travel, forcing a premature pass, and trapping.

After turnovers and steals, defenders must recover quickly, contain the ballhandler, chase from behind, block low, and prevent easy follow-up baskets. Coaches should scout opponents, enforce sprint-back effort, use full- or half-court pressure after made baskets, teach transition defense through the whole-part-whole method, and include it in every full-court scrimmage.

The Navy’s free Pier Pressure mobile app uses interactive games to help Sailors make responsible drinking choices. It includes a calorie counter, estimates the pushups needed to burn consumed calories, and integrates with Uber and Lyft for rides home. Available through iTunes and Google Play, the app had been played more than 30,000 times as of April 2017.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday, with the Dow down 424.56 points amid interest-rate fears and Caterpillar’s warning. The S&P 500 fell 1.3% and Nasdaq 1.7%, while 3M cut its profit forecast and the 10-year Treasury yield topped 3%.

In this wrongful-death appeal, Florence O. Summers and her children sought damages for J. W. Summers’s death in a collision with Clennon C. Hemsell, an employee of Columbian Fuel Corporation. A jury awarded $30,890.

The court held that several jury instructions were reversible error. The instructions improperly fixed the husband’s life expectancy at 34½ years and the mother’s at approximately twenty years, although mortality tables were not conclusive and life expectancy was a fact for the jury. The court also erred by permitting consideration of the minor son’s loss of love and affection while providing no instruction excluding grief, sorrow, companionship, and other nonpecuniary losses; recoverable damages were limited to measurable pecuniary benefits, including the monetary value of nurture, care, and education. Directing the jury to consider a possible college education lacked evidentiary support and invaded the jury’s province. Requested issues on sole proximate cause lacked evidentiary support or were unnecessary because proximate-cause issues were submitted, and the record did not support an instruction concerning a new independent cause. Finally, counsel’s inflammatory criticism of opposing counsel for admitting divorce records was improper, and the court should have instructed jurors to disregard it. The judgment was reversed and the cause remanded.

Security researcher Michael Myng found a keylogger-like debug trace in Synaptics’ SynTP.sys touchpad driver across more than 450 HP devices. Although disabled by default, a registry change could let a malicious actor with administrative privileges monitor keyboard activity. HP confirmed the issue and released patches on Nov. 7, advising users to update affected devices; HP and Synaptics said they had no access to customer data. This followed a May finding of debug code in Conexant audio drivers that also enabled keylogging on numerous HP laptops.

Police shot dead three knife-wielding assailants in Xinjiang after they killed five people and injured 10 in Pishan County. Authorities restored “social order,” launched an investigation, and released no details about the victims’ or attackers’ ethnicity.

An MLS roundup highlights four midweek games. Philadelphia’s unbeaten run features standout play from Borek Dockal, while Ilsinho scores against Chicago’s Bastian Schweinsteiger. The piece also criticizes a slow cross to Josef Martinez and notes that New England drew 1–1 after a late Teal Bunbury penalty.

- **GHCB/NAE protocol:** SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests communicate with the hypervisor through Guest-Hypervisor Communication Blocks (GHCBs) and non-automatic exit (NAE) events. The GHCB VALID_BITMAP identifies every field supplied by either side. Guests set SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2; hypervisors set SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. The bitmap is reset before each event, and its bit position is derived from the relevant field’s qword offset.

- **Standard VMGEXIT handling:** A guest may invoke VMGEXIT from its #VC handler or para-virtualize the faulting instruction. Software must protect each VMGEXIT invocation on its issuing vCPU by disabling interrupts and preemption while updating or accessing the GHCB. During NMI handling, a separate GHCB or saved GHCB state is recommended. Standard processing copies required guest state into the GHCB, sets the exit fields, points the GHCB MSR to the block, advances RIP after return, and restores returned register state.

- **Error reporting:** A nonzero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] reports a hypervisor error. A value of 1 requests exception injection, with the EVENTINJ value in SW_EXITINFO2. Other codes identify malformed VMGEXIT input, an unregistered GHCB, invalid SW_SCRATCH data, missing VALID_BITMAP entries, invalid NAE input, or hypervisor-specific conditions.

- **Instruction and memory events:** IOIO_PROT and MSR_PROT require the guest to decode the faulting instruction or para-virtualize it. VMMCALL register requirements are hypervisor-specific. For #NPF/MMIO reads and writes, nested-page-table reserved bits must generate an #NPF, and decrypted data is transferred through the GHCB shared buffer at offset 0x800 using SW_SCRATCH and, if necessary, multiple VMGEXIT calls.

- **Page State Change:** Guests can request page-state changes through a Page State Change structure in the shared buffer, which can hold up to 253 entries. Operations can make pages private or shared, update the SNP RMP table, or provide PSMASH and UNSMASH hints. The hypervisor updates the current entry and page so processing can resume after interruption and reports invalid structures, firmware errors, already-satisfied requests, RMP overlaps, and other failures through SW_EXITINFO2.

- **SNP guest requests:** SNP Guest Request uses separate shared request and response pages; the hypervisor temporarily assigns the response page to firmware, invokes the SNP_GUEST_REQUEST API, reclaims the page, and saves the return code. Requests must be retried in sequence to avoid AES-GCM IV reuse, and rate limiting is recommended. SNP Extended Guest Request can also return VCEK or VLEK certificates using a GUID-indexed data table. SNP TIO Guest Request binds and accesses trusted devices and can return measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report through shared data pages.

- **Other SNP services:** AP Creation creates, updates, or removes AP vCPUs using guest-marked VMSA pages and permits vCPU hotplug. Other events manage #HV doorbell pages, IPI delivery, virtual APIC timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL changes, Secure AVIC backing pages, termination requests, and unsupported exits. Restricted Injection uses per-vCPU doorbell pages for host notifications, with GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and CLEAR actions.

- **Guest identification and AP startup:** SEV-ES guests identify hypervisor and SEV support through specified CPUID properties. Because measured SEV-ES or SEV-SNP AP register state cannot be freely changed, first AP startup uses initial measured values, while later startups use reset-hold procedures and an encrypted, aligned AP jump table. SEV-SNP AP Creation provides an alternative using RMPADJUST and VMSA state. Hotplug is unsupported by the AP-jump-table method but supported through SNP AP Creation.

- **Other platform behavior:** NMI delivery requires intercepting #DB rather than IRET and using an “NMI Complete” message. Hardware debug-register virtualization uses VMSA state when supported; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and writes are cached. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

- **#HV doorbell protocol:** The shared doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. PendingEvent identifies interrupt vectors and non-maskable events, including NMI and virtual #MC, while NoEoiRequired indicates whether an explicit EOI is needed. The host emulates APIC ready, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior and presents the highest-priority interrupt. The guest atomically clears pending state, validates observed vectors, and performs an explicit EOI when required. HLT handling must avoid missing pending events, and an improperly timed #HV notification is grounds for a guest panic under normal operation.

Timberwolves’ Johnny Juzang is making a case for a roster spot after Nickeil Alexander-Walker’s offseason departure. On a non-guaranteed contract, Juzang scored 20 points in 14 preseason minutes and has shot 9-for-15 from three this preseason.

Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic researchers compiled peer-reviewed evidence and published a JAMA Internal Medicine guideline recommending that CK-MB testing be eliminated for suspected heart attacks because it adds no diagnostic value; cardiac troponin is the preferred biomarker. Their report details quality-improvement efforts showing CK-MB can be safely removed and provides a four-step blueprint: hospitalwide education, removal from routine order sets with clinical stakeholders, computerized ordering alerts, and measurement of test use, care quality, and safety outcomes. The report notes that 77% of nearly 2,000 U.S. laboratories used CK-MB in 2013 despite earlier guidelines. Researchers estimate all heart-attack blood testing costs $416 million annually. HVPAA faculty are also developing guides to reduce other unnecessary tests, treatments, and monitoring.

Indian-origin surgeon Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri was struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal found he abused his position by sending a love letter to a female patient. He has apologized and intends to appeal.

Effective March 11, 2021, Jerome Guillen transitioned from Tesla’s President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking. Since September 2018, Guillen had overseen Tesla’s vehicle programs, supply chain, and service infrastructure and helped develop leaders, organizations, and processes for passenger vehicle operations. He will now lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including related charging and servicing networks.

The study examines whether redshifted self-absorption line profiles reliably measure infall velocities in collapsing prestellar cores. It combines smoothed-particle hydrodynamic simulations of a 5 M⊙ collapsing core with time-dependent gas-grain chemistry and radiative-transfer modelling. Synthetic observations of C18O, N2H+, HCO+, H13CO+, CS, and C34S are analyzed at 0.81 and 0.87 Myr using apertures of 0.05 and 0.2 pc.

Infall velocities derived from the Myers et al. (1996) profile-shape method are compared with the simulation’s true mass-weighted velocities. All measurements underestimate the true values, which are 0.153 and 0.228 km s−1 at the two times. CS yields the closest estimates, reaching only about half the true velocity, while HCO+ can underestimate it by an order of magnitude because chemical and radiative-transfer effects alter the separation between its blue and red peaks. The similar line profiles at the two timesteps produce similar inferred velocities despite substantial physical evolution.

The discrepancy is attributed to applying constant-velocity, two-slab models to cores with radially varying velocities. Self-absorption features generally arise in outer, slower-moving regions rather than near the core center where infall speeds peak, systematically lowering inferred velocities and mass-accretion rates. Optically thin velocity dispersions, which in these simulations arise entirely from infall and are typically within a factor of two of the true velocity, may provide a better infall-speed diagnostic, although this may not hold in more complex turbulent environments.

Compass Minerals International remains rated “Buy,” citing attractive valuation, rising salt and plant-nutrition revenue and volumes, and cost cuts boosting cash flow and EBITDA. Lower multiples than peers and projected 2025 growth offer upside potential, though higher net debt and leverage limit the rating from “Strong Buy.”

Sony’s U.S. instant rebate and trade-in program, running through September 30, 2017, offers up to $300 off select cameras, plus $500 when trading in an interchangeable-lens camera. A7 cameras receive up to $200 off, and selected lenses and accessories up to $100, with free shipping.

William O’Neill developed CANSLIM to identify strong stocks using seven factors: current and annual earnings, new products, new management, new highs, supply and demand, leader or laggard status, institutional sponsorship, and market direction. The method emphasizes strong fundamentals and uptrends and is primarily intended for long-term investing.

Backtests indicate that CANSLIM has beaten the S&P 500 since 2003, but with higher volatility, larger drawdowns, and significant small-cap exposure. It tends to perform well in bull markets but decline sharply in bear markets. Recent performance has been weaker, with substantial underperformance relative to the S&P 500. Risks include market volatility, capital loss, and poor company performance.

Implementing and backtesting CANSLIM is demanding because it combines fundamental and technical data, requires subjective judgment, and involves high turnover. Investor’s Business Daily’s proprietary IBD 50 list provides computer-generated, mathematically ranked stocks meeting the seven criteria. The article also discusses the Innovator IBD 50 ETF and identifies O’Neill’s *How to Make Money in Stocks* as the leading resource on the method.

A hockey team is two games into a playoff series it had been winning throughout. The player credits Rucchin's two goals and Jiggy's play in the latest win, saying the team needed it and played well overall, though he personally was not at his best and contributed more offensively. He believes they controlled the game, and that the key to success is preparation, continuing what has worked, and letting the team do in big games what it has already done successfully. He leads by example rather than talking before or during games.

He says the first two games in New Jersey were an aberration caused by missing their legs and pace, and that both teams have held serve, so they must change that tomorrow; they must tighten up defensively while staying with their offensive play, since three road goals should earn at least a tie. He dismisses any animosity as simply playoff hockey and notes the check he took from a stick was extremely hard but that he was cleared to return. He is focused on tomorrow's game, eating well and sleeping, and remembers watching the Stanley Cup as a child, without letting that distraction affect his focus.

Golden State’s repeated second-half rallies drew concern from coaches Mark Jackson and Jeff Van Gundy that the Warriors’ habit of digging deep deficits could eventually hurt them. Jackson praised the team’s ability to adjust without panic, noting Golden State led the NBA in third-quarter scoring and erased large deficits against Houston in Games 6 and 7 of the Western Conference finals. But the strategy failed in Games 2, 4 and 5 because of defensive, shooting or turnover problems. Comparisons to notable comebacks by the A’s and Dave Wottle underscore that such heroics cannot always be sustained.

Investors are buying exchange-listed closed-end equity mutual funds at discounts to NAV, potentially benefiting if they hold until maturity and redeem at NAV. Poor liquidity and lock-in periods contribute to the discounts, which vary with remaining maturity and tax considerations. Reliance and HDFC schemes are trading roughly 6–10% below NAV. Because many listed closed-end funds see little trading, experts recommend schemes with assets under management above ₹250 crore.

Airbus is developing Project Vahana, an autonomous, helicopter-style vehicle intended to carry several riders as an airborne taxi. The company aims for a fully functional prototype in 2017 and availability for short-haul trips by 2021, while emphasizing clean technology, reduced congestion, and lower infrastructure costs. Other initiatives include Uber’s proposed VTOL network, Urban Aeronautics’ Cormorant passenger drone, AeroMobil’s road-and-air vehicle, and flying-car startups backed by Skype’s co-founder and Google co-founder Larry Page.

Peter Crouch made a widely shared Twitter joke following the birth of the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge’s third child, prompting a humorous reply from his wife, Abbey Clancy. Kate Middleton delivered an 8lb 7oz boy at St Mary’s Hospital, with Prince William present; mother and baby were doing well. Crystal Palace jokingly suggested Crouch’s tweet revealed the baby’s name.

A letter from abruptly fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary accused DOJ leadership of prioritizing punishment of President Trump’s perceived enemies over public safety and national security. Ben’Ary said a false social media post identifying him as a Lisa Monaco ally apparently led to his firing during terrorism cases connected to the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. The letter also criticized removing career officials from U.S. attorney’s offices and the FBI.

The passage describes a light-emitting diode device and its manufacturing method. The device includes a thin-film-transistor substrate, first and second diode electrodes, a first passivation pattern, and multiple cylindrical micro light emitting diodes positioned between the electrodes. Each micro LED contains light-emitting material with sequentially arranged p-type, intermediate, and n-type semiconductor layers, surrounded by an insulating protective layer. First and second bridge patterns electrically connect the diode electrodes to opposite sidewalls of the micro LEDs. Aligning the micro LED sidewalls with the first passivation pattern creates substantially continuous surfaces, reducing steps that could break the bridge patterns and improving connection reliability.

In manufacturing, barrier ribs and diode electrodes are formed on a buffer layer over the thin-film-transistor substrate. A first passivation material layer is deposited, micro LEDs are placed and aligned by applying a voltage between the electrodes, and a second passivation material layer is formed. The passivation layers are patterned in one mask process using two etch steps: a longer, more anisotropic first etch and a shorter, more isotropic second etch. Bridge patterns and intervening passivation layers are then formed.

The disclosed display device includes a luminescent panel with addressable light-emitting units and a panel driving unit containing a scan driver, data driver, power supply, and timing controller. An example light-emitting unit uses three thin-film transistors, one capacitor, and a light-emitting diode composed of multiple micro LEDs.

Three MLB wild-card series are headed to winner-takes-all Game 3s after all six teams won Game 2, only the second time baseball has hosted three decisive games in one day. The Dodgers clinched an NLDS berth, while the Yankees, Cubs and Guardians forced Game 3s. Detroit’s offense is a major concern after stranding a franchise-record 15 runners and hitting .079 with runners in scoring position across three potential elimination games. Padres starters Yu Darvish and Jameson Taillon may be limited by quick hooks and workload, making the team that reaches 14 or 15 outs important. A home run could decide the expected low-scoring Padres-Tigers game. Boston also used six relievers after Alex Cora pulled Brayan Bello after 28 pitches, creating bullpen concerns against New York’s potent lineup.

Aspen will replace its Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute, 50-drone patriotic show at Wagner Park due to wildfire risks and state fire restrictions. Organisers said it may have been inspired by the 2018 Winter Olympics drone display.

Simon Black of SovereignMan.com reports that the U.S. national debt passed $21 trillion for the first time on a Friday afternoon. He notes debt grew $73 billion in a single day, $215 billion in February alone, and more than $1 trillion over six months, despite a supposedly strong economy and no crisis requiring fiscal stimulus. He emphasizes that debt growth is outpacing GDP growth: last year the economy grew 2.5% in real terms (4.4% with inflation) while debt grew 6%, expanding proportionally 36% faster; since the end of 2008 the economy rose from $14.5 trillion to $19.7 trillion (36%) while debt climbed from $9.4 trillion to over $21 trillion (123%). Black argues the debt does matter, since default would bankrupt Social Security, the banking system, and the Federal Reserve. He describes three public camps — ignoring the debt, dismissing it, or preparing for future consequences — and promotes his free "Perfect Plan B Guide."

Jio’s Galaxy Club offers the Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo instant cashback of Rs 2,750, paid as 55 vouchers of Rs 50, plus data benefits on Rs 198 or Rs 299 plans. The J2 offer includes 100GB extra data, reducing its effective price to Rs 5,440; the J7 Duo provides doubled daily data. Offers run through September 30. The phones cost Rs 8,190 and Rs 16,990 at launch and feature 2GB/4GB RAM, respectively.

New CFPB rules would require payday and auto-title lenders to assess borrowers’ ability to repay within 30 days and limit unauthorized account debits, potentially forcing many lenders from business. The rules target costly rollovers: a CFPB study found over 80% of payday loans were rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. Consumer advocates support the protections, while the industry warns they could cut loan volume in half, close many of 16,000 stores, and push customers toward unregulated lenders. Republicans in Congress oppose the CFPB and could roll back the rule, slated to take effect in 2019. Separately, the OCC lifted restrictions on banks making small-dollar loans. A Pew poll found 70% of surveyed adults wanted more payday-lender regulation.

Meagan Holt journals about her 3-year-old daughter Madeline, whose Zellweger syndrome is likely fatal. A Seattle Children’s program encourages parents to express emotions through writing, offering relief and helping them focus on being present. The program relies on donations.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 27, 2022, announcing its third-quarter 2022 financial results. Exhibits included the earnings press release and information on non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Pretreatment RNA-sequencing profiles from 67 patients with more than 10 sarcoma subtypes enrolled in three immune checkpoint inhibitor trials were analyzed to identify immune and genomic features associated with treatment outcomes. Tumors clustered into “immune-hot” and “immune-cold” groups. Immune-hot tumors had higher objective response rates (30% vs. 8.1%) and longer median progression-free survival (3.65 vs. 1.7 months; HR 0.43) than immune-cold tumors after adjusting for histologic subtype.

Immune-hot tumors had higher expression of selected transposable elements (TEs), the epigenetic regulator and transcription factor IKZF1, immune-checkpoint genes, and pathways involving interferons, antigen processing, and CD8+ T-cell effector activity. Higher TE scores and IKZF1 expression were associated with longer progression-free survival and higher response rates, although the TE-score response difference was not statistically significant. Conditional-independence analysis was consistent with, but did not establish, a model in which IKZF1 regulates TE expression to influence immune type.

Findings were replicated in 190 TCGA sarcoma samples: immune-hot tumors had better overall survival, and high TE score or IKZF1 expression was associated with improved survival. The study identified TE score and IKZF1 as potential predictive biomarkers for ICI response, while noting the small, heterogeneous original cohort, differences between validation cohorts, and the need for functional and clinical validation.

Happy Home Furnishers’ managing director said the company would close its 33-year-old Neath store because of disruption caused by street improvements, anti-social behaviour, limited free parking and rising business rates. Director Mike Semmens said months of paving and road-narrowing work harmed nearby businesses, while years of confrontations around a council-installed bench led staff to encounter fights, rowdiness, waste, broken glass and drug needles. Customers also avoided crossing the road to enter the store, particularly during summer.

Other retailers reported seasonal anti-social behaviour, although its impact varied. A nearby food seller said it did not significantly affect his business, while a health-store worker described drunkenness and youths taking legal highs. Two shop workers avoided public toilets because they had found needles there.

Neath Council said the street works were completed years ago, the benches were intended to assist people with mobility issues, and they were removed about a year ago after anti-social use. It said it supports police efforts to tackle anti-social behaviour. The council also cited low shop vacancy, a new 600-space car park, free parking on its top level after 3pm, regeneration and events attracting visitors.

Semmens called for more free short-stay parking and said business rates had risen substantially, although they were no worse in Neath than elsewhere. The Welsh Government said the 2017 revaluation adversely affected some towns and that high-street relief supports nearly 15,000 small and medium-sized businesses, alongside £110 million in annual relief. Happy Home Furnishers will continue operating at other locations and may seek another site in Neath.

The Ravens traded slumping pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a fifth-round 2026 pick to the Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman. Baltimore acquired Gilman and veteran safety Gardner-Johnson to address a defense that has allowed an NFL-leading 35.4 points per game and ranks 31st in pass defense. The 1-4 Ravens tied their worst start in franchise history. Oweh, 26, recorded 10 sacks last season but none in his first five games this year, and his playing time fell to a career-low 45%. The trade frees about $8 million in cap space. Gilman, 28, helped the top-ranked Chargers defense last season before moving primarily to nickel. Oweh, in the final year of his contract, could fill the Chargers’ need for an edge rusher and potentially develop into an impact player.

At the 18th VADA Forum in Lilongwe, Treasury Secretary Ben Botolo urged African countries to use modern technology and electronic fiscal monitoring to combat tax non-compliance and improve revenue collection. Malawi has made progress with electronic monitoring, while VADA develops African solutions and shares expertise to strengthen tax compliance and domestic revenue mobilization.

The paper addresses an underexplored topic: physics teachers' views on science education research, framed by the theory–practice gap and the assumed practical value of evidence-based teaching. It defines science scepticism towards science education research (SSSE) as scepticism about the potential positive impact of such research on teaching practice, treating it as an attitudinal construct.

The study used a two-step mixed-methods design addressing three research questions: (1) physics teachers' attitudes towards the value of physics education research for practical teaching; (2) identifiable types of sceptical teachers; and (3) associations between professional variables and SSSE. Step one comprised guideline-based interviews with 13 purposefully selected in-service German physics teachers, analysed via structuring content analysis with consensual coding (κ = 0.77), yielding seven main attitude categories and 19 subcategories. Step two surveyed 174 German and Austrian physics teachers (convenience sample) using 22 items derived from the interviews.

Interview results showed both sceptical and non-sceptical attitudes. Most frequent were the sceptical views that research findings play only a minor role compared with personal experience (11 of 13) and cannot be implemented in practice (11 of 13), plus claims of poor research–practice cooperation (9 of 13); eight teachers also affirmed research's relevance for teaching, and perceived its importance as greatest early in careers.

An exploratory factor analysis identified four factors: relevance for the individual teacher, feasibility for teaching practice, relevance for general teaching practice, and cooperation between research and school practice (14 items retained). Latent profile analysis selected a four-class solution, yielding: The Sceptical Ones (N = 24, 14%), The Uncertain Ones (N = 47, 27%), The Undersupplied Ones (N = 71, 41%), and The Research Advocates (N = 32, 18%). Multinomial logistic regression (significant overall, McFadden R² = 0.132) showed the frequency of reading instructional journals as the only significant predictor, raising the likelihood of membership in The Uncertain Ones and The Research Advocates relative to The Sceptical Ones; teaching experience, teacher education, school type, and doctoral degree were not significant.

Discussion conclusions: teachers are not generally sceptical, but notable scepticism persists, and all profiles question research–practice cooperation (an "ivory tower" perception). Implications include integrating research into physics teacher education and professional development, closer researcher–teacher collaboration, and improved communication of findings. Limitations include small exploratory samples, potential affinity bias, Hawthorne effects, probabilistic profile assignment, and untested multicollinearity.

The lecture reviews free scalar-field propagators, interpreting two-point functions heuristically as transition amplitudes and as correlations of field values. Retarded, advanced, Feynman, and time-ordered functions correspond to different contour choices around propagator poles; an \(i\epsilon\) prescription shifts the poles instead of changing contours.

General \(n\)-point functions can be computed using ladder-operator expansions, and vacuum correlators in the free theory factorize into products of two-point functions. Composite operators such as \(\phi^2\), the Hamiltonian density, and the stress tensor can exhibit coincident-point singularities, illustrating the need for renormalization.

The lecture then introduces interactions through a nonlinear \(\phi^4\) Lagrangian with coupling \(\lambda\). Its equations cannot be solved exactly, so treatment is perturbative in small \(\lambda\). Scattering is identified as a primary experimental method for studying interactions. The \(S\)-matrix contains transition amplitudes between asymptotic initial and final particle states; it is unitary, respects symmetries, and conserves total momentum. For weak interactions it is written as \(S=1+iT\), with the nontrivial interaction amplitude \(M_{\alpha\beta}\) extracted from \(T\). The LSZ theorem relates this scattering amplitude to time-ordered correlation functions in the interacting theory. The next lecture will introduce the path-integral approach.

The President clarified that he did not deny Congress the constitutional power to regulate the deposit, custody, removal, and disposition of U.S. public money and property. He disclaimed any executive authority over such property unless granted by law, while retaining constitutional responsibility for officers appointed by him alone or jointly with the Senate. He requested that this clarification be entered with his earlier message in the Senate Journal.

The speaker says Philadelphia’s strong road performance should not make Detroit complacent, though home crowds and good wishes cannot decide games. He recalls earlier distractions and says veterans such as Vernon, Murphy, and Kocur understand the importance of staying focused. Home ice is not an automatic advantage, so Detroit must play every game all out, create its own opportunities, and avoid late penalties that strain the penalty kill and bench.

He praises the confidence and resilience of Detroit’s goaltending tandem of Mike and Chris, noting Mike’s previous playoff success against Grant Fuhr and Patrick Roy without dwelling on those comparisons. He defends an aggressive goalie play that narrowly failed to score. Detroit’s players are praised for avoiding retaliation, while discipline and controlling scrums and penalties remain important in close games.

He credits Detroit’s defensive success against New Jersey, including improved penalty killing and Kirk Maltby’s contribution at left wing. The pairing of Fetisov with Konstantinov and Murphy with Lidstrom has worked well. He also believes Detroit’s pregame travel and rest routine will help the team prepare for the next game.

This continuation of International Application No. PCT/CN2019/119114 describes sidelink positioning methods and apparatuses for communication systems such as LTE, 5G/NR, and V2X. It addresses positioning methods controlled by a core network, in which positioning error can increase with the distance between a terminal and a network device, making accurate positioning difficult in some scenarios.

A first terminal and a second terminal exchange sidelink positioning reference signals. The second terminal measures the first terminal’s reference signal, and the first terminal may measure the second terminal’s reference signal. Measurement values can include an Rx–Tx time difference, a sidelink angle of arrival, or both. The first terminal’s position is determined from one or both measurement values and the second terminal’s position, either by the first terminal, the second terminal, or the network device.

A network device may receive a position request from the first terminal, optionally containing a zone identifier, and host or coordinate the positioning process with core-network authorization or preauthorization. It sends positioning configurations to both terminals specifying time-frequency resources, sequence information, optional port, spatial-beam and power information, information about the second terminal, and measurement-reporting methods. Measurements may be reported directly between terminals through the PC5 interface or to the network through the Uu interface. The network device may return measurements or a calculated position to the first terminal.

Disclosed embodiments cover one-way angle-of-arrival measurement, one-way Rx–Tx time-difference measurement, and reciprocal signal exchange. The arrangements allow a second terminal that supports sidelink measurement to measure on behalf of a first terminal that does not. Uu reporting may use RRC, MAC control elements, or UCI over PUSCH or PUCCH, while PC5 reporting may use PC5 RRC, PC5 MAC control elements, or sidelink control information over PSSCH or PSCCH. For reciprocal time-difference measurement, the second terminal’s difference is based on its reference-signal reception and transmission times, while the first terminal’s difference is based on its corresponding reception and transmission times.

The background describes existing DL-TDOA, UL-TDOA, DL-AoD, UL-AoA, E-CID, and multi-RTT positioning controlled by a location management function, as well as antenna-array phase-based angle estimation. It explains that angle-based positioning errors increase with terminal-to-base-station distance. Using a nearby terminal as the positioning reference reduces this distance and improves accuracy, while avoiding core-network transfer of measurement values reduces positioning latency.

The application also provides terminal and network-device apparatuses implemented through functional modules or processors coupled to memory and communication interfaces, including chip and chip-system implementations. It further describes computer program products, computer-readable storage media, and a communication system containing the network device and terminal device.
Figures show perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views of first and second embodiments of an analytical instrument design. Broken-line features are not part of the claimed design.

Retired Toronto civil litigator Marcel Strigberger discarded his McGill University law schoolbooks after considering their continued usefulness and recalling memorable contract and property cases. He later regretted selling one book that now lists for more than C$1,000. He recycled the books and kept one thick volume, using it as a reading stand at his desk.

In June 2014, *The Wall Street Journal* reported that Hertz would restate three years of financial results because of accounting problems, and Hertz’s stock fell about 9%. Automotive industry analyst Abby Devins investigated whether the issues were related to Hertz’s large rental fleet and its future vehicle acquisition plans.

The U.S. car rental industry generated approximately $36 billion in revenue in 2013, serving leisure and business travelers through airport and off-airport locations. Revenue declined during the 2008–09 recession and recovered with the subsequent economic recovery. Three companies—Enterprise Holdings, Avis Budget Group, and Hertz—held a combined 71% market share.

Hertz originated in Chicago in 1918 and was taken public in 2006 after several ownership changes, including periods under General Motors and Ford. At the end of 2013, it had more than 30,000 employees, nearly 12,000 rental locations in 145 countries, and a fleet exceeding 700,000 vehicles. Following its 2012 acquisition of Dollar Thrifty, Hertz expanded into the budget leisure market, launched the Firefly brand, and acquired a 20% stake in China Auto Rental. Its Donlen subsidiary provided commercial fleet leasing and management services, while the company also operated an equipment-rental business.

Hertz’s earnings fell sharply during the financial crisis, rebounded in 2011, and reached record revenue and EBITDA in 2013. Between 2011 and 2013, revenue increased roughly 30% and net income attributable to common shareholders more than doubled. Depreciation averaged about 25% of total expenses, reflecting the capital-intensive nature of the business, while revenue-earning equipment represented more than half of total assets in 2012 and 2013.

Depreciation allocates an asset’s depreciable cost over its useful life, based on acquisition cost less residual value. In the passage’s example, a vehicle costing $50,000, with a $10,000 residual value and a five-year useful life, generates $8,000 of annual straight-line depreciation. Disposal produces a gain or loss equal to the difference between sale proceeds and net book value.

Hertz depreciates rental equipment straight-line over estimated holding periods. Its estimates consider historical mileage and utilization, targeted disposal ages, vehicle make and model, condition, sale location, and disposition channel. Management reviews depreciation rates quarterly and adjusts them for changing market conditions, economic conditions, natural disasters, fuel prices, and manufacturer incentives.

Hertz distinguishes between program cars purchased under manufacturer repurchase or guaranteed-depreciation programs and non-program cars exposed to residual-value risk. Program cars represented 18% of U.S. purchases and 57% of international purchases in 2013. Devins compiled revenue-earning equipment balances, depreciation expense, and gains or losses on equipment sales for Hertz and Avis Budget from 2006 through 2013 to assess depreciation’s possible significance in Hertz’s accounting issues.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 25, 2018, announcing its third-quarter 2018 financial results. Exhibit 99.1 contains the results press release, while Exhibit 99.2 provides information about non-GAAP financial measures; both are incorporated by reference.

TI’s TLV32xx comparator guidance covers unused inputs, outputs, protection, startup, hysteresis, and layout. Unused inputs must not be tied together; instead, they should be connected to voltages within the input range with at least 50 mV differential separation. The family has 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis based on threshold voltage, input offset, and hysteresis voltage. TLV321x push-pull outputs can source or sink current, while unused outputs must remain floating; TLV322x open-drain outputs support external pull-ups up to 5.5 V, logical ORing, and logic-level translation, with recommended pull-up currents of 100 µA to 1 mA. Series current-limiting resistors are recommended where output shorts may occur. Internal ESD protection limits input overvoltage to 0.2 V beyond the rails, and series input resistors should limit clamp currents to 10 mA or less. During power-on reset, outputs remain low for up to 32 µs after the 1.65 V threshold is crossed.

Comparator operation depends on VIN relative to VREF and includes propagation delay affected by overdrive voltage. External hysteresis can reduce chatter through positive-feedback resistor networks for inverting and non-inverting configurations. A low-side current-sensing example triggers a logic-high alert above 1.1 V. Proper high-speed PCB design requires close, low-ESR 0.1 µF supply bypassing, minimized output-to-input coupling, and careful routing of long or ringing-prone connections.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Ezenwo Wike urged the United States to establish a visa office in Port Harcourt for the South-South and South-East. He accused the NDDC of diverting resources to politicians’ election campaigns and failing to fund the Mother and Child Hospital as agreed, prompting the state to take over construction. Wike called for the cleanup of Ogoni land and sought U.S. partnership in agriculture, oil and gas, industrialization, and investment.
