The passage defines SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication mechanisms. The SNP AP Creation NAE event (VMGEXIT 0x80000013) lets a guest create, update, or remove an AP vCPU at a specified VMPL and APIC ID. Before creation, the guest must mark a page as a VMSA using RMPADJUST. A VMSA may be installed immediately or deferred until an INIT-SIPI sequence. Removing a VMSA prevents the vCPU from running at that VMPL until another is assigned. The hypervisor must validate VMPL and APIC IDs, use the SPA backing the specified VMSA GPA, and support specified VMPLs only when Multi-VMPL is advertised.

The #HV Doorbell Page NAE event lets SNP guests obtain, set, query, or clear a per-vCPU doorbell used to deliver pending-event notifications when Restricted Injection is enabled. The hypervisor may return a preferred, page-aligned GPA; otherwise the guest may select one and make the page hypervisor-owned and shared. The #HV Send IPI event uses an x2APIC Interrupt Command Register format to send IPIs between guest vCPUs. The #HV Timer event provides emulated APIC timer SET and GET operations for the Timer LVT, Divide Configuration, and timer count registers. These events use Restricted Injection delivery rules; without that feature, standard VMGEXIT error processing may signal a #GP exception.

The APIC ID List event returns the guest’s assigned APIC IDs in hypervisor-owned, contiguous pages. The list contains a 4-byte entry count followed by 4-byte APIC IDs. The hypervisor validates page capacity and reports the required page count in RAX if insufficient. The SNP Run VMPL event changes the current vCPU’s VMPL by associating a unique VMSA with that level; requesting a level without a VMSA is an error. A VMPL may also have a unique GHCB.

The SEV-TIO extension allows SNP guests to bind trusted devices into their private address space. Support is discovered through PCIe capabilities, and binding occurs on the first SNP TIO Guest Request. Setup may be performed by VMPL0 firmware or the guest OS and includes device information, interface-report validation, MMIO configuration, and IOMMU configuration. Requests include a guest PCI ID, an MMIO range and desired validated state, and TDISP status. Optional, contiguous, hypervisor-owned data pages can carry a 32-byte measurement nonce and receive measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report. Returned data is described by GUID, offset, and length entries. The hypervisor must validate that enough pages were supplied and report the required count in RBX if they were not.

Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state through a private backing page per vCPU. REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE provides a page-aligned GPA that must remain present in the vCPU’s nested paging table while it runs; UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE removes that requirement and returns the former GPA or zero. Secure AVIC support is implied by its SEV_FEATURES setting. A Termination Request event asks the hypervisor to terminate the guest, optionally supplying 64 bits of information and custom termination reason codes. Unsupported nonautomatic NAE events must use the “Unsupported Event” VMGEXIT code.

SEV-ES guests identify hypervisor and SEV support through CPUID: ECX[31] indicates a hypervisor, EAX[1] indicates SEV support, and EBX reports the encryption bit position and reduced physical-address width. Because measured vCPU register state cannot be changed after launch, traditional INIT-SIPI AP booting requires the AP to run initially with predetermined CS and IP values and use an AP Reset Hold request for later resets. During UEFI-to-OS transitions, an encrypted, page-aligned 4 KB AP jump table supplies the next reset vector; UEFI communicates its GPA to the hypervisor and places it in the SEV-SNP Secrets Page for OS use. Traditional booting cannot support vCPU hotplug, whereas SNP AP Creation permits it and removes the need for AP Reset Hold.

For NMI injection, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB and use the guest’s “NMI Complete” message to determine when another NMI may be injected. Hardware debug-register virtualization is used when supported and enabled in SEV_FEATURES; otherwise DR7 reads and writes are intercepted, and writes are cached rather than applied to the physical register. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

The common #HV doorbell data provides OS-level host notifications. Its first bytes contain a 16-bit PendingEvent field and a NoEoiRequired byte; remaining space is reserved or available for virtualization-stack-specific formats. The backing page must be host-owned rather than RMP-assigned, and guest accesses use C=0. PendingEvent defines NoFurtherSignal, a virtual #MC indicator, an NMI indicator, and an 8-bit interrupt vector. Doorbell configuration uses GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and clear operations.

The host emulates APIC ready, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior. It writes the highest-priority ready vector while the vCPU is stopped, sends #HV as needed, may replace an unacknowledged vector with a higher-priority one, and uses NoEoiRequired to avoid explicit EOI exits when only one interrupt is pending. It marks an interrupt in service when the guest clears the vector and performs an EOI when the guest clears NoEoiRequired or writes the emulated EOI register. Non-maskable events set their corresponding bits and NoFurtherSignal.

The guest must use atomic exchanges to read and clear PendingEvent, preventing it from acting on a vector that the host has already replaced. It may defer ordinary interrupt dispatch, but must prepare to dispatch non-maskable events even when EFLAGS.IF is clear. EOI uses an atomic exchange with NoEoiRequired; if the previous value was zero, the guest must explicitly write the x2APIC EOI MSR. Because a non-cooperative host may supply invalid data, the guest must validate observed vectors, and receipt of an unexpected #HV while NoFurtherSignal is set is grounds for a system panic.

The speakers discuss a championship victory made especially rewarding by the team playing without one of its two best defensemen and having Vladi in the building. They credit renewed desire, closeness, unselfishness, and unity—strengthened by the accident and recoveries of Vladi and Sergei—for the team’s success. Although the team monitored their recoveries, it did not use the accident as motivation. In an emotional pregame moment, Shanahan asked who would receive the Cup; the answer was Ozzie, with Vladi also receiving it if he was on the ice. He was, making the moment significant after he and Sergei had been told they might not live.

One speaker hopes to play five more seasons, is not considering retirement, and is having the most fun of his career, though the Olympics, frequent games, playoffs, and constant preparation left him exhausted. Another expects much of the young core to remain together and keep the team competitive. The four-game finals sweep was described as deceptive because Washington could have won the first two games, while the Dallas series was considered the toughest. The team is characterized as defense-oriented, deep, physically large, fast, and capable of deploying four effective lines. The speakers hope coach Scotty returns, crediting him with keeping players motivated, humble, and competitive.

Carroll County Public Schools’ Board of Education has asked county commissioners to reconsider moving the school system’s Central Office from Westminster to the former North Carroll High School building in Hampstead, despite approval of the move in the county budget. Most board members oppose the relocation because the site is not central; member Marsha Herbert recused herself. Superintendent Stephen Guthrie said the move could increase annual operating costs and require cuts or added funding. Staff projections indicate officials would drive about 50% more miles and spend 30% more time visiting schools. The board will send commissioners another letter with detailed cost figures. Commissioners allocated $6 million in FY2018 for the move and $6 million in FY2019 to expand other county offices in the Winchester Building.

Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, the year’s second Prime Day event ahead of Black Friday, features WIRED-selected discounts on smartphones, tablets, e-readers, cameras, smart-home devices, TVs, networking gear, laptops, and accessories. Featured deals include the Pixel 9a, OnePlus 13R, an 11-inch iPad, a $70 10-inch tablet, Kindle Colorsoft models, GoPro Hero 13, Echo Show, TCL’s 65-inch 4K QLED TV at $948, Orbi 770 mesh Wi-Fi, Arlo cameras, Anker Solix C1000, and a 13-inch M4 MacBook Air at $799. WIREH highlights strong displays, battery life, fast charging, smart detection, portability, and multitasking. Some options require subscriptions or sold-separately accessories, while certain products have model, ecosystem, or port limitations. WIRED independently selects the featured products but may receive retailer or purchase compensation.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces dedicated hardware for real-time ray tracing and AI, alongside new rendering, connectivity, and multi-GPU technologies. Its video encoder provides higher quality than Pascal-generation GPUs and the fast x264 software encoder while using substantially less CPU, making 4K streaming feasible on typical systems.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an open standard for delivering display, power, and data through one USB-C connector. VirtualLink supports four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes and a SuperSpeed USB 3 link, reducing VR headset cable requirements and enabling VR support on smaller devices. For SLI, Turing TU102 and TU104 replace MIO and PCIe transfers with second-generation NVLink. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 one, each providing 25 GB/s per direction; Turing supports two-way SLI but not three- or four-way configurations.

RT Cores in Turing TU102, TU104, and TU106 accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. Combined with NVIDIA RTX software, ray tracing, rasterization, and denoising become practical on a single GPU. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where effective and ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, and shadows. NVIDIA reports Turing ray-tracing performance roughly ten times that of Pascal.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only deep-learning stack using Tensor Cores for AI-enhanced graphics and applications. Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) uses trained neural networks to reconstruct high-resolution images from lower-resolution inputs, producing quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with about half the shading work. DLSS 2X combines final-resolution inputs to approximate 64x supersampled output. Other NGX services include inpainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez, which can double, quadruple, or octuple image or video resolution.

Turing also adds mesh shading, Variable Rate Shading (VRS), Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR). Task and mesh shaders process large object lists cooperatively, reducing CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enabling real-time rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects. VRS independently selects shading rates for each 16×16 screen region and supports content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. TSS stores shading results in texture space, allowing visibility and appearance sampling to use independent rates, grids, or timelines while reusing prior results. MVR supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views, with applications including stereo VR, canted-panel headsets, multiple character poses, shadow maps, and cascaded shadows.

Turing’s resource model adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and permits different resource types to share heaps. For VR, its improvements include VirtualLink, expanded MVR, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration of NVIDIA VRWorks Audio.

The TU104-based full chip contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and one x8 NVLink link. The Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 40 multiprocessors, 2,560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. The TU106 in the GeForce RTX 2070 has 36 multiprocessors, 2,304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and a 256-bit memory interface, but supports neither NVLink nor SLI.

The document also defines RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 throughput. Its example workload assigns Tensor operations 20% utilization, CUDA cores 80%, RT cores 40%, and INT32 pipes 28%.

An appendix explains ray tracing, ray casting, BVH construction and refitting, denoising, and the use of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. The closing text provides NVIDIA’s accuracy, warranty, licensing, product-use, liability, trademark, and copyright notices.

This preprint presents a problem-based political economy analysis of medical oxygen access in Peru, conducted through 13 key-informant interviews and a review of academic literature, grey literature, and national policies. The study examined how regulation, stakeholder interests, political instability, and economic factors shaped Peru’s oxygen system.

Although oxygen was classified as an essential medicine, Peru lacked a national oxygen strategy. Its fragmented health system, decentralized procurement across public, social-security, private, and regional institutions, and absence of national demand and supply data contributed to shortages. A requirement for more than 99% purity—above the WHO-recommended 93%—restricted competition to a few large suppliers and prevented smaller providers from entering the market.

During COVID-19, demand sharply exceeded supply, especially in Andean, jungle, and rural areas where production and distribution infrastructure were limited. Regulatory changes allowing 93% oxygen took two laws, three ministerial resolutions, and seven months. Slow and fragmented government procurement, inadequate data, limited accountability, and prioritization of ICU beds over oxygen access contributed to the crisis. The RENOXI supplier and stock registry was launched eight months after being mandated and later lost data in a cyberattack.

Civil society, religious organizations, and private-sector companies donated plants, cylinders, and supplies as government procurement lagged. Although 496 oxygen plants had been installed by the end of the pandemic, nearly 200 were later unused, broken, or abandoned because of inadequate maintenance plans, legal clearance delays, funding constraints, staff turnover, and shortages of trained personnel and service providers.

The authors recommend a National Oxygen System integrating demand forecasting, supply-chain management, equitable distribution, quality control, equipment inventories, maintenance funding, infrastructure investment, and trained personnel to strengthen local availability and preparedness for future emergencies.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 28, 2020 reported second-quarter net sales of $58.313 billion, up 1% from $58.015 billion a year earlier. Product sales declined to $44.965 billion, while Services sales rose to $13.348 billion. Gross margin was $22.370 billion, operating income was $12.853 billion, net income was $11.249 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.55. For the first six months, net sales increased 5% to $150.132 billion, net income rose to $33.485 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $7.56.

Second-quarter sales declined 7% for iPhone, 3% for Mac, and 10% for iPad, while Wearables, Home and Accessories increased 23% and Services increased 17%. By geographic segment, quarterly sales were $25.473 billion in the Americas, $14.294 billion in Europe, $9.455 billion in Greater China, $5.206 billion in Japan, and $3.885 billion in the rest of Asia Pacific.

At March 28, 2020, Apple reported total assets of $320.400 billion, total liabilities of $241.975 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $78.425 billion. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $40.174 billion, and current and non-current marketable securities totaled $152.670 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $43.827 billion; share repurchases totaled $39.280 billion and dividend payments were $6.914 billion. Apple had $175 billion of repurchase authorization, later increased by $50 billion on April 30.

Apple adopted new lease and hedging accounting standards in the first quarter, recording $7.5 billion of right-of-use assets, $8.1 billion of lease liabilities, and a $136 million reduction in retained earnings from the hedging standard. The filing also disclosed debt, investments, tax contingencies, lease obligations, segment data, and legal matters, including a proposed settlement of iPhone performance-management claims and a €1.1 billion French competition fine.

COVID-19 disrupted manufacturing and supply chains, closed stores outside China, required remote work, and weakened demand during the quarter’s final three weeks. Its future operational and financial impact remained uncertain.

South Africa reported more than 159 cash-in-transit heists in 2018, up from 2017, with vehicle losses of R1.1 million to R1.4 million. In attacks in Mthatha and near Bloemfontein, robbers shot at armed trucks and attempted to bomb them but retrieved no cash. Drivers suffered minor injuries, their guns were stolen, and police reported no progress.

ARS research indicates cotton farmers can plow Palmer-amaranth-infested fields for one year, then return to conservation tillage for two years, using a high-residue cover crop. This offers second- and third-year savings of about $25.57 per acre, or $15,342 annually on a 600-acre Alabama cotton farm.

Spicer said Trump’s returns could not be released because the president was under audit, despite the IRS saying audits do not prevent disclosure. He declined to say whether Trump would ever release them.

The speaker argues that modern life has increased opportunities for crime, weakened social restraints, and encouraged lawlessness, while government cannot fully prevent these problems or moralize society. Government can maintain order, administer justice, deter wrongdoing, and support education, but enforcement depends on a public determination to obey the law, which government cannot create.

The speaker contends that religion supplies this moral foundation. Although church and state are separated in the United States, American ideals of freedom, equality, self-government, and representative government have been shaped by religious convictions. Without faith and an enlightened conscience, government would rely increasingly on external force, punishment would merely suppress symptoms without reforming individuals, and enlightened civilization would be endangered.

Education is also presented as valuable, but intellectual and scientific progress without moral development can increase society’s capacity for wrongdoing. Historically, religious leaders such as Thomas Shepherd, Thomas Hooker, and John Wise advanced education and sound government because of their moral and spiritual leadership. Government cannot rise above the character of the people it governs.

The speaker therefore urges broader, nonsectarian reliance on religion, including religious teaching, devoted citizens, social example, and piety in the home. He identifies sacrifice as religion’s essence and argues that renewed faith is necessary to strengthen moral standards, preserve liberty, reform society, and improve the nation’s moral and spiritual life. Despite contemporary dangers, he finds grounds for confidence in the nation’s institutions and in the continued growth of religious conviction.

This scoping review mapped methods used to measure socioeconomic status (SES) in health research across sub-Saharan Africa. Following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework, five databases were searched from January 2012 to June 2024; 65 articles from 22 countries were included. South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana were most represented. Most articles were research articles (93.8%), and cross-sectional studies were the most common design (52%). SES assessment and maternal and child health were the leading research themes, each accounting for 31% of studies.

The review identified 41 SES measures grouped into 11 categories. Asset-based wealth indices predominated (61.9%), with the Wealth Index and its variants representing 28.6%. Common indicators included household assets, housing quality, access to utilities, land and livestock ownership, financial services, transportation, education, and employment. Principal component analysis was the predominant calculation method, used alone in 57.7% of asset-index cases and with other methods in 9.6%.

The findings indicate that SES measurement varies substantially by population, data availability, objectives, and national context. Asset-based measures may identify disadvantage where income data are unreliable, while multidimensional and subjective measures capture additional dimensions. The review did not critically appraise study quality, and methodological heterogeneity limited comparability and continental conclusions. It recommends greater standardization of SES measurement in Africa while allowing local contextual adjustments to support equitable policies, interventions, and reductions in health disparities.

Researchers, including Binghamton University anthropologist Carl Lipo, used 3D modeling, physics, archaeological evidence and field experiments to determine how Rapa Nui people transported moai statues. They found that forward-leaning statues with wide, D-shaped bases could be rocked upright and moved in a zigzagging motion using rope and relatively few people. An 18-person team moved a 4.35-ton replica 100 meters in 40 minutes. The island’s 4.5-meter-wide, concave roads provided stability and further support the “walking moai” hypothesis, challenging theories that statues were transported lying down.

Sudan, the world’s last male northern white rhinoceros, died in Kenya at 45 after a severe leg infection left him unable to stand, prompting euthanasia. Captured in Sudan in 1975, he moved to Kenya’s Ol Pejeta Conservancy in 2009 but never reproduced with the two remaining females, Najin and Fatu. About 2,000 northern white rhinos lived in 1960 before war and poaching drove them to extinction in the wild. Scientists preserved his sperm and are pursuing assisted reproduction, but neither female can carry a calf. The only option is to collect their eggs and implant fertilized eggs in a southern white rhino—a never-attempted procedure that could kill the females.

Poway Unified School District is recognizing 28 high school teachers who are retiring. Seven teachers with at least 30 years of service reflected on their careers, the changing demands and technology in education, memorable students and their retirement plans.

Traci Barker-Ball retires after 35 years at Poway High, where she served as student services coordinator, coached softball and advised clubs. She plans to volunteer locally, visit family and focus on her health. Don Jones retires after 34 years, primarily teaching health science and coaching track at Rancho Bernardo High. He will garden, coach track, care for his grandson and relax. Melinda Watson retires after 34 years of teaching math at Mt. Carmel High. She plans to visit her family, exercise, continue teaching swimming, travel with her husband and eventually move to Palm Desert. Patsy Malta retires after 33 years of teaching physical education and coaching volleyball and badminton at Mt. Carmel. She will remain in San Diego and continue officiating and coaching volleyball. Lori “Brick” Brickley retires after 32 years, including 28 as a founding Rancho Bernardo High faculty member teaching biology. She plans to remain in the area and pursue work that makes the world kinder. Keith Koelzer retires after 32 years of teaching mathematics at several high schools. He will stay in the area and remain active. Robert Saxton retires after 31 years teaching art and sustainable agriculture at Abraxas High. He plans to surf, travel, make art and garden.

The other retirees are Mark Dufva, Spanish, 29 years; Kenneth Matson, mathematics, 29; Joan Quesada, business, 29; Jayne Lutgen, mathematics, 27; Lynne Olps, social science, 26; John Carolan, special education, 25; Davette McFadden, social science, 24; Christian Michel, Spanish, 22; Kenneth Faverty, auto courses, 21; Anne Rego, mathematics and work experience, 21; Jane Wakeham-Lopez, English, 19; Richard Willard, mathematics, 19; Jeannine Ugalde, English, 18; Marie Metzgar, English, 17; Emilia “Emily” Gomez, career, technical and adult education, 16; Lisa Schick, special education, 14; Jacquelyn Whitaker, mathematics, 14; Tamarah Neuhaus, Advanced Placement computer science, 13; Mai Sciarratta, world languages, 13; Katherine Powell, library services, 12; and Randall Wright, health and physical education, 10.

Essential maternal services, including antenatal care and health-facility delivery, remain underused and unevenly accessed in Ethiopia, particularly among women facing intersecting socioeconomic, environmental, and behavioral disadvantages. This study developed and tested a maternal vulnerability segmentation tool (MVST) to identify pregnant women at increased risk of home delivery and inadequate antenatal care.

Baseline data came from a 2024 community-based quasi-experiment in four woredas in Oromia. Investigators screened 1,614 households, identified 1,189 pregnant women at least five months pregnant, and analyzed a baseline sample of 470. A desk review and analysis of the 2019 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey identified predictors of service use, including literacy, distance to facilities, parity, decision-making authority, media exposure, and household assets. These informed a 20-item MVST covering economic, social, information, and service-access factors.

Exploratory and confirmatory analyses retained four items for urban-rural and pre-urban settings and six for rural settings, with acceptable reliability and model fit. Higher vulnerability scores were associated with lower antenatal-care use and greater likelihood of home delivery. Scores above three indicated greater risk of home delivery, while scores of one or more indicated greater antenatal-care vulnerability. Mediation analysis found that antenatal care partly mediated the relationship between vulnerability and facility delivery.

The authors describe the MVST as a practical, low-literacy population-segmentation tool that community health workers could use to guide targeted interventions and reduce disparities. However, it is not itself an intervention, requires further real-world validation across diverse settings, may need refinement for different stages of pregnancy, and should also be tested against maternal and child health outcomes.

Castle Gardens in coastal Invergordon provides dementia, nursing, residential and end-of-life care. All bedrooms are wheelchair-friendly and en suite, with TV and nurse call systems. Facilities include a GP service, visiting hairdresser, kitchenette and permitted small pets. Activities include arts and crafts, baking, quizzes, animal visits, music, church services and trips. A mature garden includes a greenhouse and potting shed. The provider advises checking that a home suits individual circumstances and notes that facility details are supplied by the home and may contain inaccuracies.

Changing lifestyles, skipped meals, Westernization, and demand for convenient foods have increased global consumption of cheese snacks, particularly savory products such as extruded snacks and salted chips. The market is projected to grow at a 5.2% CAGR from 2017 to 2025. Baked, frozen, and processed cheese products are gaining popularity as consumers seek filling, inexpensive, and healthier options. Manufacturers are emphasizing taste, quality, and cheese’s nutritional benefits, with key companies including Sargento Foods, PepsiCo, McCain Foods, TINE, UTZ Quality Foods, ITC, and General Mills.

Soumya Swaminathan, a pediatrician who currently heads the Indian Council of Medical Research as its Director General, will take up the post of Deputy Director General (programmes) at the WHO in Geneva in the latter half of November, becoming the first Indian in the role. She says her priorities will align with those of WHO Director General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, including universal health coverage, proper handling of epidemics, addressing non-communicable diseases, and access to diagnostics and drugs, with the WHO playing a stewardship and coordination role. For India, she identifies wide internal disparities in infant mortality and urges greater emphasis on preventive and promotive healthcare through health and wellness centres. Her father, Dr M S Swaminathan, believes international exposure brings valuable perspective, and she hopes her WHO stint will be a learning experience enabling her to return and contribute to India.

Goldman Sachs data show that labor-force participation among 22- to 27-year-olds without college degrees has declined more sharply than among degree holders. Meanwhile, the share of disconnected 18- to 24-year-olds reached roughly 12%, according to Dallas Fed data. Experts cite economic, cultural, and psychological factors, including reluctance to accept available jobs, stigma toward non-degree and blue-collar work, mental-health and substance-use struggles, greater reliance on family support, and possible undercounting of young gig workers. Proposed solutions include expanding internships and apprenticeships in high school and community college and reducing stigma toward non-degree career paths. Experts see greater prospects for younger cohorts than for young adults already disconnected from work.

The SPREAD offense is a 3–2 motion set requiring all five players to pass and handle effectively, read defensive overplays, and use basic cuts and continuity. Overplayed players should back cut rather than fight pressure; unsuccessful cutters clear to corners. Ball handlers should attack when the defense overplays the passing lane, then kick out if help arrives. Wings may break into the middle for back-door entries when overplayed or late in the shot clock.

Deepa Das Acevedo argues that attacks on tenure are decades old but accelerating amid defunding of higher education, topic restrictions, and retaliation for faculty speech following Charlie Kirk’s assassination. She rejects the claim that politicians are addressing a genuine problem by making tenured faculty easier to dismiss, arguing instead that tenure provides employment security and protects academic freedom.

Acevedo says evidence does not support the stereotype that professors become less productive after earning tenure; available data show only a brief productivity increase before tenure. She also notes that tenure does not make faculty immune from discipline: serious misconduct can justify termination, though institutions often fail to act.

Recent rapid dismissals after social-media posts demonstrate, in her view, universities’ growing willingness to disregard established procedures, notice, and faculty input. Although tenure provides legal protections, its practical meaning—and that of academic freedom—depends heavily on institutional choices. Her book seeks to provide a vocabulary and framework for defending academic labor and tenure.

Research involving 549 participants across 29 countries found that smiley emojis in formal work emails did not increase perceived warmth and reduced perceived competence. Emails without smileys prompted more detailed, content-rich responses, while smiling photos increased perceptions of competence and friendliness. Emailers using smileys were also more often assumed to be women. Researchers advise avoiding smileys in initial workplace interactions.

This qualitative study, part of a deanery quality improvement project prompted by the 2021 anaesthetic curriculum changes, examined regional Stage 1 anaesthetic teaching across five hospital trusts. Six trainees and eight trainers participated in semi-structured focus groups, and transcripts were analysed thematically.

Participants described the expanded Stage 1 programme as demanding and unsettled, with heterogeneous trainee needs, substantial clinical, examination, CV and extracurricular requirements, and dissatisfaction with some scientific FRCA teaching. Provision varied considerably between hospitals, creating inequalities, isolation and competition, while trainer time and compensation were limited. Potential regional delivery also raised concerns about travel, rotas, group size, space, funding, quality control and stakeholder support.

Despite these concerns, participants supported a regional programme to deliver consistent, exam-focused teaching, share expertise, improve fairness, provide wider non-exam content and strengthen social networking. Trainers prioritised trainee preferences and supported a coordinated, quality-assured programme with experienced leadership, regular feedback, evaluation and adaptation.

The findings led to plans for a Stage 1 trainee survey, clarification of teaching policies and budgets, and recruitment of consultants to lead hospital-based sessions. Limitations included a small, potentially self-selecting trainee sample and possible interviewer bias.

Neonatal jaundice occurs in 50–90% of births and usually resolves without treatment, but phototherapy is needed in roughly 5–10% of newborns. Severe cases can cause neurotoxicity, cognitive impairment, kernicterus, and death. Although bilirubin metabolism and several genetic and environmental risk factors are known, most of the genetic basis of neonatal jaundice remained unexplored.

The study conducted the first GWAS of neonatal jaundice using neonatal, maternal, and paternal genomic data from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study, including nearly 30,000 families, and attempted replication in 6,902 Danish newborns. Cases were newborns requiring jaundice treatment, primarily phototherapy. The neonatal GWAS identified two genome-wide significant loci, at UGT1A* and CHRDL1. The strongest signal was a missense variant in UGT1A4, rs6755571, whose protective allele was associated with approximately fivefold lower risk in the discovery cohort and was replicated in Denmark. The effect was restricted to the neonate’s transmitted allele and was independent of parent of origin. Colocalization linked the signal to UGT1A1 expression in the colon, but not the liver; the authors considered regulation of intestinal UGT1A1 a possible mechanism while stating that the causal pathway remains uncertain. The protective effect was not modified by maternal-fetal ABO incompatibility and was stronger among full-term and post-term newborns.

The CHRDL1 locus on the X chromosome was also replicated and appeared to reflect a neonatal effect through transmitted alleles, but its mechanism is unknown. The maternal GWAS identified three loci: UGT1A*, an X-chromosome locus, and ABO. The ABO association was consistent with tagging maternal-fetal blood-group incompatibility rather than having a direct effect after adjustment for incompatibility. The paternal GWAS identified only the UGT1A* locus.

Comparison with adult bilirubin genetics showed substantial differences. The principal adult UGT1A* variant was virtually unrelated to neonatal jaundice after conditioning on rs6755571, and neonatal and adult associations were not supported as sharing a causal variant. The adult-associated SLCO1B1 locus was also not associated with neonatal jaundice. An adult bilirubin polygenic score predicted neonatal jaundice only when it included chromosome 2, indicating that the shared signal was concentrated in the UGT1A* region. Neonatal jaundice had relatively modest polygenicity, with 90% of estimated heritability concentrated in 23.4% of the genome.

The findings indicate that neonatal jaundice has developmental and tissue-specific genetic mechanisms that differ from adult bilirubin regulation. The study was limited by uncertain mechanisms and its emphasis on Nordic European ancestry, leaving the effects and clinical importance of the variants in other populations unclear.

Houlton Border Patrol agent Larry O’Neal was indicted on one felony count of possessing child pornography and pleaded not guilty. Investigators found child and adult pornography on his home computer and external drive, but found no evidence he stored it on his work computer or used government property. His trial was scheduled for June 6.

The patent describes portable shelters and campers that transition between an expanded, rigid enclosure and a collapsed, low-profile hard case. In expanded form, a roof, floor, front and rear panels, and folding side panels form a weather-tight, lockable, optionally insulated shelter providing space for sleeping, sitting, crawling, or standing. Side and end panels may be bi-, tri-, or multi-folded and connected with hinges, latches, weather seals, tracks, and manual or powered mechanisms for opening and closing.

When collapsed, the panels and optional mattress or fixtures fit inside a compact case that can be carried, placed on vehicle roof racks or pickup beds, mounted on trailers or wheels, or towed by cars, trucks, motorcycles, bicycles, or people. Embodiments include adjustable bed systems that can be raised for standing room or lowered for sleeping, with space below for kitchen, bathroom, dinette, and storage fixtures. Optional features include windows, doors, climate control, lighting, electrical systems, solar panels, batteries, plumbing, water and waste storage, and heating or cooling equipment. The disclosure also describes methods for transporting and unfolding a shelter at a destination and illustrates embodiments, hinge systems, bed tracks, and tongue-and-groove joints.

The statistical analysis plan specifies reporting through tables, listings, and figures using ICH numbering conventions. Unless otherwise stated, tests are two-sided at the 0.05 significance level, with P values ≤0.05 considered significant. Continuous variables are summarized with means, standard deviations, medians, minima, maxima, and valid counts; PK parameters other than Tmax include geometric means and geometric percent coefficients of variation. Categorical variables are summarized by counts and patient percentages, with missing values excluded from category percentages and special denominator bases documented in footnotes. Analyses are classified as a priori or post hoc based on whether they were defined before unblinding.

The trial groups are dasiglucagon liquid 1 mg/mL, 0.6 mL; GlucaGen 1 mg lyophilized powder; and placebo liquid 0.6 mL. The safety set includes randomized patients who received at least one dose, with treatment based on what was received. The full analysis set includes all safety patients, with treatment and injection-site stratification based on randomization and planned site. The per-protocol set includes full-analysis patients without relevant protocol deviations. Primary efficacy is analyzed in the full analysis set, with a supportive per-protocol analysis; safety analyses use the safety set. Protocol-deviation relevance is determined before unblinding. Disposition, country, center, US/non-US distribution, demographics, diabetes history, medical history, body measurements, BMI, screening assessments, and protocol deviations are summarized or listed.

Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment are coded with WHODrug Global and summarized by WHO ATC class and preferred name. Prior medication stopped before first study-drug administration, while ongoing medication at first intake or medication starting thereafter is concomitant; medications with unclear dates are treated as concomitant.

The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp without rescue IV glucose, assessed only through 45 minutes. Glucose values are converted from mmol/L to mg/dL using a factor of 0.0555. Secondary endpoints are recovery within 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes without rescue glucose and changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is the last non-missing pre-dose value, including unscheduled visits when applicable. Primary models adjust for age group and injection site. Only observed data are analyzed, with no imputation or last observation carried forward, and no interim analyses are planned.

Confirmatory comparisons of dasiglucagon 0.6 mg versus placebo use a hierarchical, two-sided 0.05 procedure, testing the primary endpoint followed by the four recovery-rate endpoints and four glucose-change endpoints until the first failure. GlucaGen comparisons are outside the hierarchy, and center is not included in the primary model. Kaplan–Meier analyses use actual sampling times through 60 minutes. Patients requiring rescue IV glucose before recovery are censored and classified as not recovered at 45 minutes, as are patients not recovering by 45 minutes. A stratified log-rank test compares treatments while adjusting for age group and injection site.

Supportive analyses include alternative rescue-handling methods, a stratified Wilcoxon test, recovery histograms, and linear interpolation of recovery times. A discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model may be used descriptively if proportional-hazards conditions are met and no more than two-thirds of recovery times are censored per treatment group. It includes treatment, age group, injection site, and baseline glucose, with hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals, pairwise treatment comparisons, and separate homogeneity models for sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, and US/non-US status.

Secondary recovery rates use actual sampling times and are compared with Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel tests stratified by age group and injection site, with a non-stratified Fisher test if cell counts are too small or zero. Responder rates and 95% confidence intervals are presented. Glucose changes are analyzed at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes using ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site; rescue-time glucose values are used when rescue occurs before the relevant endpoint. Adjusted treatment means, confidence intervals, and dasiglucagon-versus-placebo comparisons are reported.

Plasma dasiglucagon and GlucaGen concentrations are measured from predose through 300 minutes, and PK metrics are derived by noncompartmental analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin. Predose samples are assigned time and concentration zero; planned times are used in summary tables and actual times in individual curves. Below-quantification values are treated according to timing relative to Tmax and subsequent quantifiable results, while missing postdose values are not replaced. Listings, summaries, and original- and log-scale concentration figures are planned.

Plasma glucose is measured from predose through 45 minutes, with 60-minute sampling for patients weighing at least 21 kg. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is area under the glucose effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes, calculated in SAS. Glucose raw listings, treatment-group summaries, changes from predose, mean concentration curves, and individual curves are required.

Safety reporting covers insulin and glucose administration during hypoglycemia induction, trial-drug administration, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratories, vital signs, ECG, physical examinations, pregnancy and alcohol testing, and immunogenicity. Most adverse-event summaries concern treatment-emergent events, including worsening of preexisting events after dosing. MedDRA coding is applied, with patients counted once per preferred term and event totals also reported. Possible and probable relationships are classified as related; unresolved missing causality is treated as related, while missing severity remains missing. Summaries include adverse events of special interest, injection-site reactions, related events, serious events, deaths, and special searches including QT prolongation and hepatic disorders.

Laboratory summaries include descriptive statistics, reference-range flags, categorical results, and changes from screening to follow-up. ECG outputs include investigator assessments, descriptive parameters, QTcF thresholds above 450, 480, and 500 ms, and changes above 30 and 60 ms. Antidrug antibody incidence is assessed descriptively for treatment-induced antibodies and baseline-positive patients with at least five-fold titer increases, using evaluable postdose patients as the denominator.

Analyses and tabulations use SAS Version 9.4 or later, with Phoenix WinNonlin Version 6.4 or later for PK/PD work and ASCII or RTF output. Presentation standards cover precision, percentages, P values, footnotes, sorting, dates, derived variables, missing dates, and treatment-group totals. SAS programming QC addresses naming, documentation, validation, log and output review, Pinnacle 21 checks, patient-level spot checks, figure verification, and retention of supporting documentation. Changes from the protocol include reworded primary-endpoint analysis, added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changed secondary-endpoint terminology from “within” to “at” specified minutes.

On January 26, 2016, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015. Pivot points are price levels derived from the previous trading day’s high, low, and close, with a central pivot and additional support and resistance levels calculated using a five-point formula. They were invented by floor traders and are used to identify possible entry and exit points, often alongside other technical indicators. Their advantages include simplicity, objectivity, versatility, and confirmation of support and resistance; disadvantages include lagging prices and relatively low win rates in the cited backtests.

Lewis Borsellino reportedly used pivot points daily but did not specify his methods. Six strategies were backtested from 2010 using one-minute data for the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, and USD/CHF. None proved consistently tradeable. The best result was an erratic Nasdaq strategy averaging 0.16% across 172 trades with a 62% win rate. Some strategies might be improved by reversing trades or further research, but the overall conclusion was that pivot points are overly hyped and create more market noise than usefulness.

RWE Supply & Trading expects LNG derivatives trading to double or triple this year from 1.5 million tonnes in 2017, driven by Asian spot-market growth and physical cargo price-risk management. JKM swap volumes quadrupled in 2017 and continued rising.

The passage discusses research on the identification of racial, ethnic, and language-minority children as disabled in U.S. special education. Although minority overrepresentation has previously been reported, the cited longitudinal, nationally representative study found no evidence of disproportionate overrepresentation. After adjusting for factors such as socioeconomic status, academic achievement, and behavioral functioning, minority children were generally less likely than otherwise similar White children to be identified with disabilities, and language-minority children were less likely to be identified with learning or speech/language impairments. Other factors also affected identification: stronger academic achievement and behavioral self-regulation reduced disability identification, while externalizing behaviors shifted identification toward health impairments or emotional disturbances. The passage notes that federal legislation and proposed monitoring policies seek to reduce minority overrepresentation and concludes by questioning the consequences of mainstreaming children who might benefit from special education.

The lecture reviews the number four-vector, \(N^\alpha=n_0u^\alpha\), whose covariant divergence expresses conservation of particle number and can be rewritten in any frame as an energy-like density balance with flux through a volume boundary.

The main topic is the stress-energy tensor. For identical dust particles of rest mass \(m\), the rest number and energy densities are \(n_0\) and \(\rho_0=mn_0\). In a moving frame, energy density becomes \(\rho=\gamma^2\rho_0\), showing that it is neither a Lorentz scalar nor a four-vector component. It is instead the time-time component of a tensor:
\[
T^{\alpha\beta}=N^\alpha p^\beta=\rho_0u^\alpha u^\beta.
\]
Its components describe energy density, energy flux, momentum density, and momentum flux. In units with \(c=1\) and including rest energy, energy flux and momentum density are symmetric and equal. A torque-based physical argument motivates the requirement that spatial stress components be symmetric, while the symmetry of the time-space components follows from the related behavior of energy and momentum.

A perfect fluid is defined as having no energy flow in its rest frame and no lateral stresses or viscosity. In that frame, its stress-energy tensor is \(\operatorname{diag}(\rho,p,p,p)\). Its covariant form is
\[
T^{\alpha\beta}=(\rho+p)u^\alpha u^\beta+pg^{\alpha\beta}.
\]
Dust is the zero-pressure case. Stress-energy tensors are also illustrated for a point particle, represented with a spacetime delta function, and for electromagnetic fields, whose energy density is \((E^2+B^2)/(8\pi)\), whose time-space components form the Poynting vector, and whose spatial components represent anisotropic electromagnetic stresses and pressures.

The covariant conservation law
\[
\nabla_\alpha T^{\alpha\beta}=0
\]
combines conservation of energy and momentum; in a chosen frame, these become separate differential and integral flux-balance equations. The lecture also argues that a relativistic gravity theory cannot use only one stress-energy component, as Newtonian gravity does, because all components of the tensor must source the gravitational field.

The lecture then begins a transition toward curvature and gravity by examining flat spacetime in curvilinear polar coordinates. It introduces coordinate bases with varying, non-normalized basis vectors, coordinate-transformation matrices distinguished from Lorentz transformations, and the expectation that the metric acquires a nontrivial functional form in such coordinates.

More than 80% of Minnesota public school districts provide student mental health services, but nonprofit programs supplement school-based care with specialized support. Know the Truth, founded in 2006 as an offshoot of Minnesota Adult and Teen Challenge, brings people with lived experience in addiction and recovery into schools to speak with students about substance use and provide peer support.

Youth peer specialist Tiffany White draws on her history of alcohol addiction, depression and recovery to support students individually and in groups at three Twin Cities schools. She also provides community-based support, hosts school support groups, and uses a harm-reduction approach intended to help students make informed decisions about substance use. Her position at Hastings High School was eliminated because of federal funding cuts, though she continued working at another alternative learning center, where she said trust grew over time.

The organization trains educators about refugee experiences and cultural influences on behavior, and offers screening groups, individual therapy, suicidal monitoring and culturally grounded mind-body practices. State funding has supported expanded youth services and school-based work in several Minnesota cities.

During an in-play penalty kick, the ball becomes live once the kicker touches it and it clearly moves forward; the referee’s whistle or motion does not permit defenders to enter the penalty area or arc early. Under Law 14, all players except the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field, and outside the penalty area.

Defenders must immediately occupy designated positions, beat attackers to key locations, and avoid jostling. A defender who arrives first should hold position; one arriving second should stand beside the attacker. Defenders must pursue rebounds, turn or shield the ball to protect their goal, and clear it. If the goalkeeper secures the ball or the defense clears it, the team should immediately counterattack through an outlet pass.

The kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does, usually the goalkeeper; a rebound from the goal frame does not qualify. Defenders also need preparation for rare “tap” or “two-man” penalty kicks, where a light touch allows a teammate to shoot. If a defender enters the area or arc early, a goal stands; otherwise, the kick is retaken. The article recommends practicing positioning, rebounds, counterattacks, and tap kicks, but notes that shootout kicks have different rules and allow no follow-up.

The disclosure describes a gaming machine, control method, and program that synchronize in-game event displays with the beat of background music (BGM). The controller starts the game and BGM, uses stored tempo data containing beat information to determine event timing, dynamically configures animation data for those timings, and displays the animation. Event timing may depend on player input, random event content, rhythm-pattern data, or BGM tempo.

In the described slot-game embodiment, the controller determines reel stop positions and frame counts, generates spin and stop animations, and stops each reel on an on-beat. Rhythm patterns can control sequential reel stops and synchronize reel-stop sounds with the BGM. A bonus game can likewise time an object’s jumps and other movements to the BGM beat. Event sounds and illumination may also be synchronized with the determined timing.

The gaming machine includes upper and lower displays, speakers, an operation unit, bill/ticket identification and printing units, player tracking, illumination, and a controller connected through graphic, input, sound, and illumination controllers. Game and system applications store reel, paytable, graphic, sound, BGM-related, and rhythm-pattern data. Winning combinations, paylines, dividends, bonus triggers, and player credits are managed by the controller. The disclosed technique addresses delays between event sounds and visual events and applies to slot and other games, including poker, blackjack, bingo, keno, wheel games, pachinko, and pachinko slot machines.

This qualitative study examined infectious disease diagnostics stakeholders’ views on the clinical utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and barriers to its routine use. mNGS offers culture-independent, hypothesis-free detection of pathogens and simultaneous assessment of antimicrobial resistance, functional genes, and virulence, but its implementation is constrained by cost, turnaround times, infrastructure, workforce expertise, accreditation and validation requirements, data systems, and interoperability.

Using an interpretive phenomenological approach, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with 10 purposively recruited participants from clinical and academic roles across England. Interviews conducted via Microsoft Teams lasted 30–60 minutes and were transcribed and thematically analysed. Five themes emerged:

1. **Diagnostic choice:** mNGS was viewed as a complementary rather than universal diagnostic, with appropriate use determined by clinical need. Funding disparities limited access, particularly at smaller hospitals, while delayed results that could not guide treatment reduced its value.

2. **Infrastructure:** Participants cited inadequate laboratory space, computational and data-storage capacity, bioinformatics training, staffing, accreditation, standardisation, and clinically useful reporting. Research-only reagents and the difficulty of validating workflows using limited or varied clinical samples impeded clinical accreditation.

3. **Open data sharing:** Genomic research’s open-data culture conflicts with confidentiality requirements in clinical diagnostics. Local data contributed to centralised repositories could improve disease surveillance, epidemiological understanding, and public-health response.

4. **COVID-19:** COVID-19 sequencing demonstrated the public-health value of rapid genomic analysis and helped build manufacturing capacity, platform availability, public visibility, and support for routine sequencing.

5. **Communication:** Better communication was needed within hospitals, between hospitals, and among healthcare, academic, commercial, and funding stakeholders. Cross-departmental collaboration, shared experiences, and partnerships with manufacturers were viewed as supporting efficient adoption.

Participants supported mNGS as part of the infectious-disease diagnostic toolkit. The findings emphasise locally situated services, clinically actionable turnaround times, equitable access, workforce development, suitable digital and physical infrastructure, validated and accredited workflows, and evidence of cost-effectiveness and clinical utility. COVID-19 was identified as a learning resource for advancing routine clinical metagenomics and disease surveillance.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi received the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs)—porous molecular structures whose gaps can store gases, water and other chemicals in large quantities. Potential applications include collecting water from air, capturing industrial carbon dioxide and extracting “forever chemicals.” Robson developed a diamond-like copper-and-organic-compound structure with useful cavities in the late 1980s. Kitagawa later created MOFs capable of taking up methane, nitrogen and oxygen, while Yaghi developed an exceptionally stable, highly porous framework in 1999. A sugar-cube-sized amount of Yaghi’s material had the surface area of a soccer field and could absorb large amounts of gas. The three scientists share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

Andrew Lo explains how limited information affects prices using an auction of a wrapped iPod and his hedge-fund book. The iPod, worth $150 retail, sold for $45, while the book, worth $45 retail, sold for $60 despite Lo’s autograph reducing its resale value. He uses this example to illustrate why uncertainty depresses bids and draws a parallel to securities issued by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

Lo outlines the federal government’s intervention in Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which purchased mortgages to support lending and housing markets. Their financial difficulties threatened the broader system, leading the government to guarantee their obligations and protect counterparties, while shareholders lost most of their investment. He discusses possible inflation, taxpayer costs, market disruption, and the institutions being “too big to fail.”

The lecture then introduces present-value analysis. Lo defines an asset at a given time as a sequence of current and future cash flows, excluding the past; negative cash flows characterize liabilities. He treats cash flows at different dates like different currencies, requiring market-derived exchange rates, or discount factors, to convert them into a common value.

Under certainty, known cash flows, frictionless conversions, and market-observed exchange rates, net present value is the sum of all cash flows expressed in today’s dollars. Introducing an interest or opportunity-cost rate \(r\), Lo shows that date-\(t\) discount factors are \(1/(1+r)^t\), while forward growth uses \((1+r)^t\). He applies this method to an investment with a $100,000 positive net present value and notes that subsequent lectures will address annuities, perpetuities, uncertainty, inflation, compounding, and fixed-income valuation.

CUPA-HR’s 2024 report examines Title IX staffing in higher education, including office placement, position prevalence, workforce size, staff composition, compensation, and recommendations for strengthening compliance capacity. Title IX regulations, first issued in 1975 and substantially expanded in 2020 and 2024, have created complex procedures requiring institutions to maintain specialized expertise.

A CUPA-HR poll of 432 institutions found that Title IX staff are most commonly housed in Human Resources (29%) and Student Affairs/Dean of Students/Student Services (28%). Other placements include Compliance and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (11% each), Legal Affairs (5%), the President’s Office (5%), Academic Affairs (4%), and Business or Operations (3%).

CUPA-HR tracks three dedicated positions: heads of institutional Title IX compliance, deputy heads, and investigators. Heads oversee complaints, education, training, policy communication, and systemic issues; deputy heads manage specific compliance areas; investigators conduct investigations and draft findings. From 2019–20 to 2023–24, the share of institutions with at least one dedicated full-time Title IX position rose from one-third to 43%. In 2023–24, 31% had a compliance head, 16% had an investigator, and 12% had a deputy head. The total reported workforce grew 38%, from 542 to 746 positions, while investigators increased 85%, deputy heads 58%, and heads 7%.

In 2023–24, 56% of institutions had no dedicated full-time Title IX position, 26% had one, and 17% had two or more. Among institutions with any Title IX position, 39% had multiple staff. Dedicated positions were most prevalent at doctoral institutions: 64% had at least one, compared with 45% of baccalaureate, 39% of master’s, and 19% of associate’s institutions. Thirty-six percent of doctoral institutions had multiple positions.

Women held 77% of Title IX positions, compared with 62% of all higher-education professional positions. Black women held 13% of Title IX roles, versus 6% of professional positions overall, while Asian professionals held 2%, compared with 6% overall. Median salaries were $96,714 for compliance heads, $84,931 for deputy heads, and $75,000 for investigators, all above the $66,000 median for professional positions. Women and people of color in these roles generally earned at least as much as White men; Black women earned $1.16 for every $1 earned by White men.

The report recommends that institutions reassess officers’ workloads, provide adequate time and resources for Title IX duties, increase dedicated staffing where needed, and prepare for either the 2020 regulations or new guidance based on regulatory and legal developments.

This study examines kindergarten teachers’ views, teaching practices, and challenges related to visual arts in early childhood education, with attention to curriculum integration and the possible support of migrant and refugee students. A mixed-method questionnaire—comprising 16 closed and five open questions—was completed electronically in February 2024 by 65 public and private kindergarten teachers across the Municipality of Piraeus. Participants were selected through voluntary response sampling, and responses were analyzed with SPSS and thematic analysis.

Most respondents were women, held four-year degrees, had five or fewer years of experience, and lacked specialized visual-arts training. Teachers overwhelmingly regarded visual arts as crucial to preschool education and believed they support creativity, imagination, intellectual development, emotional expression, social interaction, cooperation, and self-confidence. Teachers also reported that children generally respond positively to art activities and showed high interest and participation.

The preferred teaching approach was the “Free Approach,” emphasizing experimentation, discovery, and exploration with varied materials and tools. Group teaching and guided approaches were also reported. Teachers emphasized positive feedback, flexible methods, and activities adapted to children’s developmental stages, interests, and abilities. Although most considered visual arts reasonably integrated into the curriculum, major barriers included classroom management, insufficient time, limited materials and space, large groups, and teachers’ limited specialized knowledge.

Recommended responses included patience, individual support, classroom roles, games, rewards, varied artistic techniques, continuous feedback, professional-development programs, adequate art supplies and equipment, and dedicated art spaces. Demographic characteristics did not significantly affect teachers’ perceptions of visual arts. Limitations included the geographically restricted sample and the inability of an electronic survey to provide the depth attainable through qualitative interviews.

The German ambassador, newly returned from Berlin, outlined Germany’s willingness to state confidential peace terms: relinquish Belgium while retaining certain Meuse travel rights; maintain Holland, Denmark, and Belgium as neutral buffer states; leave France the entire French coast as an independent power; restore Russian territory; treat Serbia and Romania properly; and indemnify Belgium despite questionable neutrality. He believed Britain’s maximum allied terms were impractical, while its minimum terms would likely provoke allied disagreement, and suggested American pressure might prompt Britain to reveal its terms.

The Greek chargé d’affaires welcomed the U.S. peace initiative as humane and favorable to an honorable, stable peace. He described Greece’s suffering from foreign occupation, blockade, disarmament, and hunger despite its neutrality. Greece supported the effort but remained excluded from communications with one belligerent pending resolution of its difficulties. It favored cooperation among neutral nations and readiness to participate in establishing peace that would protect all states’ rights, sovereignty, and independence.

The SOS defense disrupts side-screen actions in three ways. Below the free-throw line extended, defenders aggressively trap the ball handler before the screen is set, apply hard double teams, and rotate into SET, SNUGGLE, FRONT, and helpside I positions. Skip passes and passes into the low post prompt additional closeouts and traps.

Above the free-throw line extended, defenders use an aggressive contact switch: one defender bumps the screener and hedges into the ball handler’s path, forcing a checkpoint. The defender then smothers the ball handler, fronts the screener, and places the remaining defenders in weak-side I positions.

An all-out SOS disruption traps the point guard before any screen or pass develops, forcing the offense into a “free lance” situation. Defenders rotate using the near-player concept, deny return passes, front posts, and maintain helpside positions. A pass to the rolling post player can trigger a baseline post trap, followed by further rotations and coverage of drives through “Base Go I” or “Base Go Red.” All rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

On November 18, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. entered a 364-day revolving credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and other lenders. The unsecured facility permits borrowings of up to $10.0 billion for general corporate purposes, including backstopping notes issued under Amazon’s commercial paper program. It may be extended for an additional 364 days. Initial interest on outstanding balances is the Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 0.45%, with a 0.05% commitment fee on undrawn amounts. The agreement includes customary representations, warranties, covenants, and default provisions but no financial covenants. Uncured or unwaived defaults may accelerate unpaid amounts and terminate commitments. The agreement was filed as Exhibit 10.1 to Amazon’s Form 8-K.

Task-Force-Southwest tested the Instant-Eye drone for surveillance and reconnaissance in confined areas before a scheduled Afghanistan deployment. Marines trained with M67 grenades, while 91-year-old Lee Anderson received the Purple Heart for injuries sustained at Iwa Jima.

He reports efforts to secure the western frontiers through treaties and military action against hostile tribes, continued peace overtures, and recommendations for impartial justice, regulated land sales, equitable commerce, and penalties for treaty violations. Measures authorized by the distilled-spirits tax law have been implemented, though compensation rates may require revision; public discontent is expected to ease through explanation and reasonable modifications.
