The nearly completed census indicates a population approaching four million. Loans have been secured in Holland, substantial portions of public and state debts have been subscribed, and existing revenues appear adequate without new taxes, absent unforeseen needs.

Congress is urged to address current appropriations, the militia and national defenses, post offices and roads, establishment of a mint and uniform weights and measures, and sale of vacant public lands as a means of reducing public debt and avoiding new taxes.

Hampton and Newport News police located a 15-year-old suspect allegedly involved in a Tinee Giant robbery. Officers found the teen with a handgun near a Ford SUV on Newsome Drive. He was charged with firearm, concealed-weapon and tobacco offenses, but no robbery charge.

Critics of higher education say colleges lack viewpoint diversity, noting that faculty have long leaned politically left, but the concept is inconsistently defined and may reduce plurality. The Trump administration demands viewpoint diversity while offering nine universities competitive federal funding if they adopt its conditions, including race- and sex-based hiring and admissions bans, a five-year tuition freeze, an international enrollment cap, standardized testing, and a “marketplace of ideas.” The administration is also considering grants based on how “patriotic” an institution is. Students increasingly choose colleges by political viewpoint and reportedly pay over $2,000 more to attend institutions with fewer students who oppose their beliefs, pressuring colleges to promote and advertise diversity strategies. The author warns that tying funding to a political agenda could substitute presidential priorities for genuine intellectual diversity.

A Sarasota couple was charged after accepting a package intercepted by authorities and identified as carfentanil, a synthetic opioid the DEA says is 10,000 times more potent than morphine. A search found over 7 grams of fentanyl in a false electrical outlet, plus other drugs and paraphernalia.

The passage describes display-device embodiments that detect cracks and other panel defects while protecting defect-sensing circuitry from static electricity. A substrate includes a display area with pixels and data lines, a peripheral area, a circuit area containing a crack-sensing circuit, a pad area, and optionally a bending area. Crack-sensing lines extend around the display area and through the bending area, with their ends connected to input pads and test data lines. Switching elements apply test voltages to corresponding data lines, while matching resistors compensate for sensing-line resistance so damage can be identified through bright pixel columns.

Static-electricity discharge elements, including capacitors or sub-capacitors, are connected near the sensing-line ends to store or discharge static charge, reduce leakage in switching elements, and prevent erroneous defect detection. Alternative embodiments include separate connection wires, different circuit-area placements, and sensing lines dedicated to bending-area damage. The disclosure also describes the panel’s stacked conductive and insulating layers, including transistors, signal lines, pixel electrodes, encapsulation, and optional touch-sensor layers.

Alexander Zverev survived a five-set marathon at the French Open, defeating Dusan Lajovic 2-6, 7-5, 4-6, 6-1, 6-2 to reach the third round. The 21-year-old German, ranked third and already a three-time Masters champion, still seeks his first Grand Slam quarterfinal and major victory over a top-50 opponent.

Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori also recovered from two sets to one to advance, while Dominic Thiem beat Stefanos Tsitsipas in three sets. World No. 1 Simona Halep recovered from a slow start to defeat Alison Riske in straight sets despite admitting pre-match nerves. Novak Djokovic progressed after being pushed by qualifier Jaume Munar, and Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina won in straight sets.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported that Fidelity Investments was selected as the new recordkeeper for its 401(k) Plan. During a blackout period expected from January 2, 2020 through the week of January 12, 2020, participants could not exchange or reallocate assets, take loans, or request withdrawals or distributions. Amazon notified Section 16 officers and directors that they would face trading restrictions on company equity and derivative securities acquired through their employment or service during the blackout.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for indicating wireless channel status in digital communications, particularly 5G NR beam failure recovery. In high-frequency deployments such as mmWave, beamforming addresses path loss, but a failed beam may require recovery and updated quasi-co-location (QCL) information for decoding PDCCH and PDSCH transmissions.

Example embodiments allow a UE, after selecting a new beam during recovery, to temporarily assume that the new beam is QCL-related to a channel’s reference signal or DMRS and use the corresponding spatial receive filter until updated QCL/TCI configuration is received. Other embodiments suspend QCL use after recovery and rely only on the channel’s DMRS until TCI states are updated. The disclosure also describes access-node procedures for updating TCI tables and DCI mappings, handling TCI-field values, and decoding control and data frames. These mechanisms are intended to reduce post-recovery signaling overhead and improve communications performance.

Editors of the Foreign Relations series have access to State Department central, decentralized, Executive Secretariat, and overseas diplomatic post files. State Department records from 1981–1989 will eventually be transferred to the National Archives, as will decentralized files selected for permanent preservation, after declassification and processing. Research also uses restricted records at the Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies; some material published has been extracted from documents that remain classified.

Documents are arranged chronologically by their Washington, DC, time, with memoranda of conversations dated by when conversations occurred rather than when drafted. Editorial treatment follows established office and historical-publication guidelines, reproducing original text and marginalia while silently correcting obvious typographical errors. Brackets identify corrections, additions, unrelated omitted passages, and material remaining classified; underlining is represented in italics. Original abbreviations, capitalization, punctuation, and ellipses are preserved. Withheld documents are listed chronologically with source notes and the number of pages omitted. First footnotes provide sources, original classification and distribution information, drafting details, important policy context, and presidential or advisers’ readership. Reagan Library records scanned for the Remote Archive Capture project sometimes created uncertainty about whether attachments accompanied original documents, which editors note as “Not found attached.”

The commentary says children often give brief or vague answers and may hesitate to ask questions, while rote questions from adults can signal disinterest. It recommends five strategies for parents and caregivers:

1. Ask specific, open-ended questions.
2. Engage with children’s questions, explain your reasoning, and model how problems are solved.
3. Admit uncertainty and demonstrate how to find answers using sources, manuals, labels, glossaries, indexes, and multiple searches.
4. Paraphrase what children say, clarify misunderstandings, and highlight meaningful parts of their responses.
5. Give children undivided attention, make eye contact, avoid distractions, and ask follow-up questions.

Modeling curiosity, active listening, and persistence can encourage children to ask questions, express their thinking, and continue learning.

This cross-sectional study examined self-esteem, physical activity, and their relationship among 10th- and 11th-grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul during the 2022–2023 school year. Of 278 eligible students, 225 participated (80.93%); 16 were excluded from MET-related analyses because they recorded zero MET scores. Data were collected by observed questionnaire in March 2023 using sociodemographic questions, the IPAQ-SF, the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and self-reported height and weight for BMI calculation. Ethics approval and parental and student consent were obtained.

Participants were 71.6% male and 27.6% female. Based on IPAQ-SF results, 23% were inactive, 61.7% minimally active, and 15.3% HEPA-active; males had higher MET scores than females (p=0.031). Males also had higher self-esteem scores (p=0.002). Students reporting regular exercise had higher self-esteem than those who did not (p=0.034), and self-esteem was positively correlated with MET scores (r=0.140, p=0.045). Higher self-esteem was also associated with greater height (r=0.146, p=0.029) and greater self-reported school success (p=0.001). No significant self-esteem differences were found across BMI categories.

The researchers concluded that greater physical activity was correlated with higher self-esteem in this sample. However, causation remains unestablished, and the results may not generalize beyond this selective science high school population because height, weight, and school success were self-reported.

The ADS868xW provides input and AVDD alarms. Input-alarm low and high thresholds and hysteresis are user-programmable. For NTC thermistor sensing, resistance decreases as temperature rises, while divider output voltage increases. Properly adjusted hysteresis prevents noise near the thresholds from causing false or missed alarms and improves noise immunity.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, which can be set independently within their permissible ranges. A minimum 10 µF and 1 µF capacitor are required for each AVDD supply, with the 1 µF capacitor placed close to the pins; a minimum 10 µF capacitor should also be placed near DVDD. Decoupling improves power-supply rejection ratio.

Two programmable low-power modes support lower-throughput operation. NAP mode places internal blocks in a low-power state after conversion when CONVST/CS remains high; a falling edge wakes the device, but a new conversion must wait until tNAP_WKUP elapses. Power-down mode is entered on the rising edge of CONVST/CS by setting PWRDN after unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG. It powers down analog blocks while keeping the interface active and retaining registers. Clearing PWRDN starts wake-up, after which the host must wait tPWRUP before initiating a conversion.

Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital sections, keeps analog and reference routing away from digital lines, uses close, low-impedance bypass connections, connects ground pins to the ground plane, and specifies decoupling for AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO.

The remaining sections cover documentation-update notifications, TI E2E support, ESD precautions, revision history, package and orderable information, and TI’s resource and liability disclaimers.

Researchers analyzed blood samples from more than 2,800 people in Toronto and estimated that about 1% of the population has celiac disease, with 90% of cases remaining undiagnosed. The study aimed to determine whether celiac disease contributes to poor nutrition through impaired vitamin and mineral absorption, potentially causing conditions such as fatigue, bleeding gums and brittle bones.

Researchers noted that diagnosis is difficult because symptoms overlap with other illnesses and many people adopt gluten-free diets without confirmed disease. Antibody testing and duodenal biopsy should be performed while patients consume gluten to avoid false-negative results; biopsy is considered the diagnostic standard. The study could not distinguish latent celiac disease from actual disease and may not represent all Canadian provinces. Researchers also cautioned that gluten-free foods can be more expensive and less nutritious. The study was funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research, and researcher Ahmed El-Sohemy founded a company providing nutritional genetic testing.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage point to 1%–1.25% and said it would begin gradually reducing its $4.5 trillion balance sheet sometime in 2017, without specifying the timing or pace. Stocks reacted mutedly: the S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.9%, and the Dow briefly reached a record high. Weak May inflation and retail-sales data, along with a 3.7% decline in oil futures, pressured markets, Treasury yields and the dollar, while gold rose 0.6%. Chairwoman Janet Yellen still expected inflation to reach 2% next year. Strategists said the Fed could raise rates three times in 2017, though soft data might prompt a pause. Tesla gained 0.6%, oil stocks fell more than 5%, H&R Block surged 9% on strong earnings, and Alexion rose 8.7% after naming a new CFO. European stocks slipped, while Asian markets closed mixed.

Disclosed systems and methods use insulin-delivery records from automated insulin delivery (AID) or artificial pancreas applications to update basal insulin settings for manual or open-loop control. A processor determines total basal and bolus insulin delivered over a selected period, calculates the basal proportion of total insulin, and compares it with a threshold. If the threshold is exceeded, the system calculates an average or modified basal dosage, generates an instruction for a wearable insulin pump, and updates the dosage to substantially maintain the calculated average over a subsequent period. Basal doses delivered near bolus doses may be excluded, and historical delivery data may be segmented or clustered to generate time-dependent, potentially hourly, basal profiles.

Thresholds may reflect clinical data, expected basal-bolus distributions, user activity, or individual physiology, and may be reduced when glucose-control data indicate excessive time in hypoglycemia. The disclosed system may include a processor, memory, wireless communications, an artificial pancreas/AID application, a continuous glucose monitor, a personal diabetes management device, a smart device, a wearable drug-delivery device, and cloud services.

The District of Columbia Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of alien enemies’ claims for return of property seized during World War I under the Trading with the Enemy Act. Public Resolution No. 53 had postponed deliveries under the Act and the Settlement of War Claims Act of 1928 while Germany was in arrears on certain obligations. Following Cummings v. Deutsche Bank, the court held that recovery was a matter of grace that Congress could withdraw or suspend. Appellants’ contention that the property had been unlawfully seized did not distinguish their case, because the same contention had been immaterial in the earlier case.

Schneider Electric’s Edge Module is a turnkey, self-contained edge-computing solution for telecom cell-tower sites and other distributed deployments. It integrates power, cooling, software, and IT components, supports single- or three-phase power, N+1 cooling, externally mounted package cooling, and configurable rack arrangements. Its single-phase, 208-volt design can scale to 48 kW. EcoStruxture software enables metering, remote monitoring, and control for autonomous or “lights out” operations, while security options include locks, cameras, exterior lights, and a key reader. The module aims to standardize remote edge endpoints and support consistent efficiency, reliability, and operations.

The excerpt defines IPD, IPU, and DIS as internal pulldown active, internal pullup active, and internal pull disabled, representing default post-reset pull states. Boot-configuration pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot modes and GPMC functions. At reset, BTMODE[10] selects GPMC mux options A or B for XIP NOR boot modes, BTMODE[9:8] determines Ethernet PHY mode in EMAC mode, and BTMODE[4:0] is sampled for ARM boot configuration. After reset, the pins serve as GPMC multiplexed data/address lines, including GPMC_D[10], GPMC_D[7:5], and GPMC_D[4:0].

U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday after stronger-than-expected January employment and wage gains revived inflation concerns and pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 2.845%, its highest since January 2014. The Dow dropped 665.75 points (2.54%), its largest daily point decline since December 2008, while the S&P 500 lost 2.12% and Nasdaq 1.96%; all three posted their worst weeks in two years. All S&P sectors declined, and volatility rose. Exxon, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple fell, while Amazon gained 2.9%. Analysts still expected 13.6% fourth-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth, and some investors viewed the pullback as overdue.

At OpenAI’s Developer Day, the company previewed an Apps SDK that lets developers build third-party apps directly within ChatGPT using open standards. Distribution is initially limited, and demos showed Spotify, Canva, and Zillow responding to prompts, including creating business materials and displaying homes for sale. OpenAI plans new monetization methods, including an “agentic commerce protocol” enabling purchases and instant checkout in ChatGPT.

The initiative reflects OpenAI’s aim to make ChatGPT a chat-driven platform and a center for AI agents that perform tasks for users. It also introduced AgentKit, a drag-and-drop tool for building AI agents, and said its Codex coding model would become generally available alongside Slack-based code questions and edits, an SDK, and business analytics. OpenAI is pursuing developers amid competition from Google, Anthropic, Amazon, Meta, and DeepSeek, while expanding data-center capacity through a proposed 6-gigawatt AMD chip deal.

Tail risk, or “fat tails,” refers to rare, extreme market events occurring more frequently than a normal distribution suggests. Left-tail events produce severe losses, while negatively skewed strategies can accumulate many small gains before a few large losses erase years of profits. Nassim Taleb argues that unexpected financial-market extremes are more common than standard models imply. Investors may hedge tail risk to limit catastrophic losses, avoid leverage-driven ruin, survive long-term, and reduce panic-driven mistakes, but protection generally requires sacrificing some returns.

Six alternatives are presented: out-of-the-money put options on broad market indexes; foreign real estate, bonds, and commodities; cash and bonds; Cambria’s TAIL ETF; Ray Dalio’s diversified All Weather Portfolio; and trend-following strategies. Puts function like insurance but require costly rolling and create pin risk. Cash can provide protection during crises despite long-term inflation risk, while diversification reduces dependence on stocks. Trend following has a low win rate and frequent small losses but can produce rare large gains that offset them.

Meb Faber’s illustrative strategy allocates 10% to monthly 5% out-of-the-money S&P 500 puts and 90% to 10-year U.S. bonds. It performed best among the compared assets during selected bear markets when crisis timing was perfect, but continuously holding it significantly reduced overall returns while lowering drawdowns. Cambria’s TAIL ETF primarily holds out-of-the-money puts and intermediate Treasuries; it is expected to lose money during rising markets but protected portfolios during the 2018 selloff, March 2020 pandemic decline, and 2022 weakness. Allocations of 5%–10% reduced downside and contributed 1.28%–2.56% during Covid-19, while larger allocations further reduced drawdowns at the cost of lower returns.

Tail-risk hedging is psychologically difficult because protection may expire worthless for years before producing a payoff. The authors stopped buying SPY puts in 2019 because of this experience and missed a subsequent Covid-19 profit. The appropriate hedge depends on individual preferences and trade-offs, particularly as retirement approaches and withdrawals from stock portfolios become more sensitive to major declines.

Part 1 of an ABA Journal “Mind Your Business” primer explains that generative AI creates content from existing data, while agentic AI analyzes information to produce insights, predictions or recommendations. Although AI can improve legal practices, client service and efficiency, it is not a panacea; lawyers should determine whether it suits each task, leaving nuanced judgment and creative problem-solving to humans and using templates for standardized materials.

The article identifies document review, legal research and client communication as useful applications, citing Vincent AI, Case Status and AI chatbots. Listed tools include Vincent AI, Copilot, ChatGPT, AI features built into legal software, and custom tools for firm-specific workflows. The author cautions against entering client information into the free ChatGPT version. Part 2 will address effective AI use, integration into legal practices and future developments. Jordan L. Couch, a Palace Law partner focused on workers’ compensation and personal injury litigation, wrote the column.

Real Madrid, featuring prolific goalscorer Cristiano Ronaldo, face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last 16, chasing a European treble not achieved since Bayern Munich in the 1970s. Five English clubs feature, with first legs on 13/14 and 20/21 February.

The thesis examines how web and digital technologies can support digitized event organization and management. It also describes a mobile application intended to give attendees information about events and facilitate services such as sensor-based booking of nearby facilities and drone-camera monitoring of multiple stages. The theoretical section distinguishes digital business, which encompasses online business processes, from e-commerce, which specifically involves electronic buying and selling. It discusses cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things, and mobile business, alongside risks such as business consolidation, reduced SME activity, income disparity, and cybersecurity threats. Common protections include antivirus software, firewalls, encryption, and digital certificates.

The research used web mining to compile event-management websites, with data collected from 1 August to 15 September 2017. Descriptive statistics and inductive conclusions were applied to 200 websites—17 Croatian and 183 foreign—using 103 binary criteria. A five-part analytical model covered website content, social networks and Web 2.0, public relations and user support, multimedia and mobile technologies, and user experience and technical specifications.

Among the foreign websites, 83% had privacy policies, 89% had terms and conditions, and 90% linked to Facebook. Twitter and LinkedIn profiles were also widespread. Email and telephone were the main support channels. All analyzed foreign websites used photographs, 86% used animations, and 19% used video. Most performed strongly on loading speed and homepage size, while only eight used HTTPS. Croatian organizations ranked substantially below foreign organizations; the highest-ranked Croatian site was 40th of 200, and the lowest was 200th.

The conclusions emphasize that strong online presence, user experience, social-media participation, mobile applications, and multimedia are increasingly important for event organizations. Recommended improvements include faster-loading pages, less unnecessary content, stronger use of newer social platforms, more mobile applications, and effective multimedia. Video is often outsourced to platforms such as YouTube to limit page size and loading time. The study identifies its selected-country sample as a limitation and recommends future research from customers’ perspectives, including the relationship between marketing activities and event-management strategies.

Minnesota Wild winger Kirill Kaprizov signed an eight-year, $136 million extension through 2033-34, the NHL’s richest contract in total value and average annual value at $17 million per year. The deal takes effect next season; Kaprizov will finish the current season under his five-year, $45 million contract. It includes substantial signing bonuses over its first four years and followed prolonged negotiations in which he rejected a $16 million annual offer. Kaprizov recorded 25 goals, 31 assists and a plus-19 rating in 41 games last season. The 28-year-old has 185 goals and 386 points in 319 games for Minnesota, where he holds single-season franchise records for points, goals and power-play goals. He also won the Calder Trophy and is one of the Wild’s top players. New NHL labor rules will limit future team re-signings to seven years and free-agent contracts to six.

Photographer Mark Bickerdike, of Mirfield, spent several years documenting Ricky's School of Rock in Linthwaite, capturing pupils on the school's 10-week RockJam courses and around 50 gigs ending in a performance for friends and family. His final RockJam marked the end of the project, which he said had let him photograph talented young musicians; his portfolio also includes Bruce Springsteen and REM's Michael Stipe. Founder and guitar tutor Ricky Comiskey said many pupils have gone on to form bands and that quiet children become confident performers, adding that the school also runs courses for adults. Mark's son Tom was among the pupils who formed Fading Sunlight, a band that has played in Huddersfield, Leeds, Barnsley and Sheffield. Ricky said the photos, shown to parents at the end of each gig, let families see children grow up in 10-week increments.

The lecture develops the operator–field mapping in AdS/CFT. In semiclassical Einstein gravity around AdS, canonical normalization makes quadratic fluctuations dominate, allowing free-field quantization. For a massive scalar, the near-boundary solutions scale as \(z^{\Delta_+}\) and \(z^{d-\Delta_+}\), where \(\Delta_+=d/2+\sqrt{d^2/4+m^2}\). The BF bound ensures real scaling exponents and stability; violating it produces exponentially growing modes.

Standard quantization retains the \(z^{d-\Delta_+}\) mode, while the coefficient of the non-normalizable \(z^{\Delta_+}\) mode specifies the field’s boundary value and acts as a source for the dual operator. Alternative quantization reverses these roles, replacing the operator dimension by \(d-\Delta_+\). Normalizable modes represent states of the dual theory, whereas changes in non-normalizable modes correspond to different boundary actions or theories. The same reasoning gives dimension \(d-1\) for a conserved current dual to a Maxwell field and dimension \(d\) for the stress tensor dual to metric perturbations.

Finally, source-generating functionals turn on boundary operators, and their derivatives produce correlation functions. The field-theory partition function should equal the gravity partition function, which can be evaluated at leading order in the semiclassical limit using the saddle-point approximation.

A qualitative study examined the anticipated challenges and training needs of pre-service physical education teachers in Quebec. Four focus groups involved 18 participants from francophone universities, with a mean age of 25 years. Participants identified classroom management and students’ lack of motivation as their main overall challenges. Motivational challenges included student heterogeneity, selecting activities that sustain motivation, student engagement, managing disengaged students, and gender differences, particularly difficulties motivating girls.

Participants wanted teacher education programs to provide more support in planning motivational strategies, explain concretely how to implement them, and offer additional practical experience. The study recommends explicitly connecting motivation with course content, including planning, assessment, didactics, and classroom management, and strengthening coordination between theoretical learning and practicum training. These recommendations support Quebec’s new professional competency, “support students’ love of learning,” and an empowering motivational climate that addresses students’ autonomy, competence, and relatedness. Teacher educators may themselves require additional preparation in motivational theory and its practical application.

The findings indicate that current programs are not perceived as adequately meeting pre-service teachers’ motivational-support needs. Limitations include the small sample, the restriction to Quebec universities, and the possibility that other challenges were overlooked because of the focus on motivation.

A Tom Thomson sketch given as a gag gift sold for $481,250 at a Heffel auction in Toronto after experts verified its authenticity. The 118-work sale raised $14.1 million, led by a record-setting $3.6 million for Paul-Émile Borduas’s “Figures schematiques”; Lawren Harris’s “Morning, Lake Superior” sold for $1.1 million.

California women’s basketball coach Lindsay Gottlieb said a Southwest Airlines employee asked for proof that her 1-year-old biracial son was hers after noting their different last names, requesting a birth certificate and a Facebook post. Gottlieb called the encounter demeaning and suspected her son’s skin color prompted it. Southwest apologized if the questioning caused discomfort, said it verifies the ages of lap children and does not require surnames to match on domestic flights, and promised to address the employee’s conduct. Other parents criticized the incident, while Chrissy Teigen defended similar checks as a child-trafficking precaution.

The VIX measures implied volatility in S&P 500 index options and generally moves inversely to the S&P 500. It is presented as a mean-reversion indicator: a rising VIX and risk premium may signal an opportunity to buy stocks, while a falling VIX may suggest selling. The article describes a Bollinger-band strategy with several standard-deviation settings, notes that products such as VXX cannot fully replicate the spot VIX, and recommends independent backtesting.

UAE Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazroui said OPEC and other producers plan to announce an exit strategy from their supply-cut pact in June, not necessarily end the pact then. Kuwait said producers would study the possibility beforehand. Russian Energy Minister Alexander Novak said withdrawal should be gradual, taking three to six months depending on market conditions and crude demand. The pact cuts supply by about 1.8 million barrels daily.
Nigeria’s May inflation fell to 16.25% from 17.28%, while monthly price growth rose to 1.88%. Food inflation edged down to 19.27% as several staple prices increased.

The paper develops an exact method for computing Nash equilibrium in multiplayer imperfect-information games. It generalizes the sequence-form representation to multiple players, formulates equilibrium conditions as a nonlinear complementarity problem, and models that problem as a quadratically constrained feasibility program solvable using nonconvex quadratic optimization.

In strategic-form experiments on uniformly random games, the approach was faster than a direct mixed-integer bilinear formulation across all tested player and strategy counts, although newer, more complex bilinear methods outperformed it. The primary experiment used reduced three-player Kuhn poker with dominated actions removed. The new method solved the game in 2.47 seconds with maximum unilateral deviation gain of \(1.4 \times 10^{-17}\), producing expected payoffs of approximately \(-0.0208333\) for players 1 and 2 and \(0.0416667\) for player 3. Its strategies matched a previously derived infinite family of equilibria except at two information sets that are never reached under the computed profile, indicating additional equilibria. The method could not solve the full game within 24 hours.

Most Gambit algorithms were inapplicable or ineffective on reduced three-player Kuhn poker. Logit quantal response equilibrium tracing was the only successful Gambit method, taking 43 seconds through the graphical interface and 49 seconds from the command line, with a maximum deviation gain of \(1.667 \times 10^{-5}\). It also produced an approximate solution for the full game in 2 minutes 34 seconds, demonstrating greater scalability but lower exactness.

The results position the new approach as an exact and fast method for smaller multiplayer imperfect-information games, while logit tracing offers a global-convergence guarantee for moderate-sized games the exact method cannot solve. For very large games, iterative methods such as counterfactual regret minimization and fictitious play remain practical but lack convergence guarantees. The paper notes that specialized nonlinear complementarity solvers and further bilinear-program improvements could improve performance.

Box reported first-quarter adjusted EPS and revenue above Wall Street estimates, added about 3,000 paying customers, and forecast second-quarter results above consensus. Despite the beat, its shares fell 4.6% after hours after trading up nearly 2%.

The Texas appellate court affirmed a jury verdict awarding the appellee 117½ acres of land and rents in Bell County. The appellee proved title through a duplicate land certificate and patent issued to Willard Chamberlain, an 1850 transfer of the certificate to Joseph P. Sneed through Chamberlain’s agent, and a later deed to N. T. P. Simmonds.

The court held that the transfer was properly admitted because it came from proper custody, was not facially suspicious, and the jury found it genuine. Being more than thirty years old, it created a conclusive presumption that the agent had authority to execute it. The transfer sufficiently identified the certificate issued to Chamberlain. A Land Office affidavit claiming ownership of the same certificate and a later augmentation certificate were inadmissible or irrelevant to disproving that identification. The court also held that a party cannot place his own character in issue merely because his testimony conflicts with another’s evidence. The remaining jury instructions were sufficiently favorable to the appellant, and the evidence supported the verdict.

Certified records show that Thomas Scullun, master of the American bark Cape Horn Pigeon, agreed with J. and W. R. Wing to sail from San Francisco by December 1, 1891, on a whaling voyage, receiving a one-twelfth lay. The 201-ton vessel, manned by 44 men, cleared at San Francisco on December 7, and Scullun swore that its outward manifest accurately listed all cargo intended for whaling.

In 1892, Lieutenant von Cube of the Imperial navy, commanding the English schooner Maria, suspected the Cape Horn Pigeon had visited Aniva and Patience bays, where foreign fishing was forbidden, and took it to Vladivostok. Scullun said von Cube instead considered the Sea of Okhotsk closed to foreign whalers. A commission found that the vessel had navigated within Russian territorial waters but ordered no confiscation, concluding that the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding. The vessel was promptly returned to its owners.

This continuation patent application discloses methods, storage media, and electronic devices for an auditory digital-assistant interface supporting media exploration. The assistant receives natural-language speech requests, identifies media using search parameters, and permits spoken refinements during playback to obtain different media without restarting the search. It can provide a spoken response while playing related media, offer alternative recommendations based on consecutive non-affirmative responses until a threshold is reached and then request user input, and merge multiple users’ preference profiles to select media. These techniques are described as reducing user inputs and cognitive burden while improving interaction efficiency.

The digital assistant may interpret spoken or textual requests, infer user intent, execute tasks through services, and return audible or visual output. It can operate through client-server components, as a standalone application, or through a second device acting as a proxy. Detailed embodiments describe portable and nonportable multifunction devices with touch-sensitive displays, audio components, communications circuitry, sensors, tactile outputs, event handling, and modules for media and other applications. The application also claims priority to 2017 U.S. and Danish applications and continues earlier U.S. applications filed in 2018, 2019, and 2021.

Dusty Baker, who managed Jeff Kent for six seasons, says the second baseman deserves Baseball Hall of Fame induction. Eligible since 2013, Kent has remained near 15% of ballots, far below the 75% required, despite 377 home runs and the 2002 NL MVP award.

Carol Moore and others say Jane Sanders’s 2010 land deal caused Burlington College’s closure. Authorities are examining Sanders’s representations of donations used as loan collateral; Moore also criticized a Driscoll’s school agreement as favoring Sanders’s stepdaughter.

QuantifiedStrategies.com offers TradingView strategies and translates selected ones into PineScript. Visitors can subscribe for availability notifications. The site warns that trading involves risk and past performance does not indicate future results.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told generals and admirals summoned worldwide that the force was “gone soft” and “woke”; Pentagon reporter Greg Jaffe discussed the speech.

## Summary

The passage is an excerpt from NVIDIA's "NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture In-Depth" whitepaper (© 2020), describing the A100 GPU, its supporting software, and the DGX A100 system.

**Architecture and process.** The A100 is based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and the GA100 die, built on TSMC's 7nm N7 FinFET process, which provides higher transistor density, better performance, and better power efficiency than the 12nm FFN process used for the Tesla V100. A full GA100 comprises 8 GPCs, 8 TPCs per GPC, 2 SMs per TPC, 128 SMs, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores (8,192 in full GA100), four third-generation Tensor Cores per SM (512 per full GPU), 6 HBM2 stacks, and 12 512-bit memory controllers. The shipping A100 has 108 SMs, 4,320 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 Tensor Cores, 5 HBM2 stacks, and 10 memory controllers.

**Tensor Cores.** Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data. Each A100 Tensor Core performs 256 FP16/FP32 FMA operations per clock (versus 64 in Volta/Turing), so each SM delivers 1024 dense FP16/FP32 FMAs per clock, a 2x per-SM increase. With 108 SMs, A100 provides up to 312 TFLOPS dense FP16/FP32 — 2.5x the V100's mixed-precision Tensor Core throughput and 20x V100's standard FP32 FFMA throughput. TF32 runs 10x faster than V100 FP32 (20x with sparsity); FP16/FP32 and FP64 Tensor Core operations run 2.5x faster than V100; INT8 with sparsity runs up to 20x faster. BF16 runs at the same rate as FP16. TF32 is the default for deep learning training (up to 8x FP32 throughput), while FP16/BF16 mixed precision gives up to 2x over TF32 and up to 16x over FP32. For HPC, A100 delivers 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64, 2.5x V100, using a new DPMA instruction that replaces 8 V100 DFMA instructions.

**Mixed-precision HPC.** cuSOLVER's Tensor Core Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver (TCAIRS) automates mixed precision for iterative refinement. Across 37 SuiteSparse problems, TF32 was fastest and most robust, with geomean speedups of 2.0x over the FP64 solver (vs 1.9x FP16, 1.8x BF16), and up to 4x for large complex matrices of roughly 40K size.

**Sparsity.** A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern (two non-zero values in every four-entry vector), enabling 2x compute throughput and 2x reduced data footprint and bandwidth. Sparse MMA instructions skip zero entries, halving matrix-multiply cycles. NVIDIA provides a train-dense → prune → fine-tune recipe that yields virtually no inference accuracy loss across vision, detection, segmentation, NLP, and translation networks.

**Memory subsystem.** A100 has 40 GB of HBM2 (five active stacks, 1215 MHz DDR) delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth, more than 1.7x V100. It includes 40 MB of L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100), divided into two partitions of 40 slices each, with 5120 bytes/clk read bandwidth (2.3x V100). Compute Data Compression yields up to 4x DRAM read/write bandwidth, 4x L2 read bandwidth, and 2x L2 capacity. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1, and register files.

**SM features.** A100 combines 192 KB of shared memory and L1 cache (1.5x V100), with up to 164 KB of SMEM allocation (1.7x). A new asynchronous copy instruction loads global memory directly into shared memory, bypassing L1 and the register file. A new shared-memory-based asynchronous barrier unit separates barrier "arrive" and "wait" operations, enabling overlap of copies with computation, producer-consumer patterns, and synchronization at arbitrary thread subsets within a block. A100 also adds L2 cache management and residency controls, warp-level reduction instructions supported by Cooperative Groups, and simultaneous full-throughput FP32 and INT32 execution.

**CUDA 11 advances.** CUDA 11 provides programming and API support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 residency controls. The async copy API offers BYPASS (bypassing L1 and RF) and ACCESS (saving to L1) variants. Asynchronous barriers are exposed as ISO C++-conforming barrier objects. L2 persistence can be set aside in 1/16th increments (2.5 MB) via address-range windows or per-access controls, boosting a global-memory histogram example by 2.5x over V100 and 43% over A100 without residency control; set-aside is disabled in MIG mode. Cooperative Groups adds group-wide async copy collectives, multi-stage pipelines, and a hardware-accelerated reduce API. CUDA Task Graphs (introduced in CUDA 10) separate graph definition from execution for define-once/run-repeatedly execution; A100 accelerates them with launch optimizations and dependency-aware execution, reducing CPU launch overhead and grid-to-grid latency.

**MIG.** Multi-Instance GPU partitions an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances, each with dedicated and isolated paths through the memory system (crossbar ports, L2 banks, memory controllers, DRAM buses), providing QoS and fault isolation while leaving the CUDA programming model unchanged. The GPU contains seven GPU slices (each with a Sys Pipe, one GPC, an L2 slice group of 10 slices, and frame buffer memory); in MIG mode each slice's GPC enables seven TPCs (14 SMs). A GPU Memory slice isolates L2 and frame buffer among instances. Compute Instances group compute resources, enable simultaneous context execution with independent context switching, and support Volta-style MPS, with client counts proportional to instance size. MIG supports vGPU migration between instances and GPUs, enabling job packing and servicing without killing jobs.

**NVLink, PCIe, and resiliency.** Third-generation NVLink offers 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair, four lanes per direction, and 12 links for 600 GB/s total (vs 300 GB/s in V100); writes are non-posted to allow requester-side synchronization and error attribution. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 and supports SR-IOV, allowing a single GPU to be virtualized across processes/VMs. New fault-handling technologies improve error attribution, isolation, and containment, including remote page-fault reporting over NVLink.

**Additional features.** A100 adds a five-core hardware JPEG decode engine (NVJPG), a hardware optical flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved atomics (11x FP16, 2.7x FP32 over V100), and five NVDEC units (vs one in V100). The GPU omits display connectors, RT Cores, and NVENC. Compute capability is 8.0.

**DGX A100 and software.** DGX A100, a 6U, 8-GPU system, delivers 5 PFLOPS of AI performance with six NVSwitches and 4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth, up to 6x the AI training performance of DGX-1, and up to 56 isolated accelerators via MIG on one system. It includes eight Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters at 200 Gb/s, supports Magnum IO scaling to tens of thousands of GPUs, and pairs with NVIDIA GPU Cloud. The DGX software stack includes the CUDA Toolkit, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and NGC Private Registry containers for deep learning, inference (TensorRT), analytics (RAPIDS), and HPC (CUDA-X HPC, OpenACC).

**Appendix.** The appendix explains pruning of dense networks, contrasts fine-grained (irregular, load-imbalancing) with coarse-grained (removes sub-networks, risking accuracy) sparsity, and describes fine-grained structured sparsity, which balances workload across nodes while retaining accuracy, with evaluation tables comparing 2:4 sparsity fine-tuning accuracy against dense training. The whitepaper concludes with standard NVIDIA disclaimers regarding accuracy of specifications, limited warranties, liability, patent rights, and trademark notices.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019 reported net sales of $59.7 billion, up 17% from $51.0 billion in Q1 2018. Product sales were $34.3 billion and service sales were $25.4 billion. Operating income rose to $4.4 billion from $1.9 billion, while net income increased to $3.6 billion from $1.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $7.09, compared with $3.27.

North America generated $35.8 billion of sales and $2.3 billion of operating income; International reported $16.2 billion of sales and a $90 million operating loss; and AWS generated $7.7 billion of sales and $2.2 billion of operating income. Consolidated sales categories included $29.5 billion from online stores, $4.3 billion from physical stores, $11.1 billion from third-party seller services, $4.3 billion from subscription services, $7.7 billion from AWS, and $2.7 billion from other sales. Total operating expenses were $55.3 billion, with increases in marketing, technology and content, fulfillment, cost of sales, and general and administrative expenses.

Q1 2019 operating cash flow was $1.8 billion, compared with a $1.8 billion outflow in Q1 2018. Investing activities used $8.1 billion and financing activities used $2.4 billion. For the trailing twelve months, operating cash flow was $34.4 billion, free cash flow was $23.0 billion, and free cash flow after principal repayments of finance leases and financing obligations was $15.1 billion. At March 31, 2019, total assets were $178.1 billion, stockholders’ equity was $48.4 billion, cash and cash equivalents were $23.1 billion, marketable securities were $13.9 billion, and inventories were $16.4 billion. Long-term lease liabilities were $33.3 billion and long-term debt was $23.3 billion. Amazon had 492,331,776 common shares outstanding as of April 17, 2019.

Amazon adopted new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities without retrospectively adjusting prior periods. It also adopted guidance requiring substantially all episodic television production costs to be capitalized, adding approximately $130 million of capitalized film costs. Present value of total lease liabilities was $44.1 billion, and principal contractual commitments totaled $131.3 billion. Amazon had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, $539 million borrowed under its secured credit facility, and no borrowings under its commercial paper program or revolving credit agreement. Stock-based compensation expense was $1.3 billion, and no common shares were repurchased during either Q1 2018 or Q1 2019.

The Q1 2019 income tax provision was $836 million. Tax contingencies were approximately $3.6 billion and were expected to grow in 2019. The IRS was seeking approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax related to transfer pricing, while approximately €250 million related to the European Commission’s state-aid decision was deposited into escrow pending appeals. Amazon also disclosed possible indirect-tax liabilities, an ongoing review of orders involving sanctioned individuals and entities, and several patent proceedings involving Dynamic Data Technologies, Saint Lawrence Communications, Data Scape, and Vocalife. Amazon disputed these allegations and intended to defend the matters.

Management identified inventory valuation and income taxes as critical accounting judgments. Each additional 1% of inventory valuation allowance as of March 31, 2019 would have increased cost of sales by approximately $185 million. Amazon stated that operating cash flow, cash and marketable securities, and borrowing arrangements were expected to meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least the following twelve months, while noting substantial uncertainty and risks affecting future results.

The article explains, backtests, and attempts to improve a 20-day exponential moving average (EMA) trading strategy. It generates buy signals when price moves above the 20 EMA and sell signals when price falls below it. Tested on SPY using unadjusted data, the strategy produced low CAGR despite being invested about 70% of the time and experienced significant drawdown. Adding another technical indicator as a filter improved performance and nearly matched buy-and-hold risk-adjusted CAGR, though drawdown remained unchanged. The same crossover rules performed better on Bitcoin from 2014 onward, which the article attributes to Bitcoin’s strong momentum.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate, also called ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, copperas, or green vitriol, is soluble in water and acids and has octahedral molecular geometry. It is produced as a sulfate co-product during titanium dioxide manufacture from ilmenite or by crystallizing and cooling hot sulfate solution. The product contains 18–20% iron, at least 4% free moisture, and up to 3% free sulfuric acid; crystals may clump and become dusty, while residual acid can attack storage containers. Its applications include treating iron deficiency and iron chlorosis, textile dye fixation, leather blackening, ink production, water purification and phosphate removal, chromium reduction in cement, and supplying iron in agriculture. WHO lists it as an essential medicine.

The lecture applies the asymptotic equiprobable property (AEP) to discrete memoryless sources. For a source sequence, the sample average of the negative log probability approaches the entropy \(H(X)\) as sequence length increases. Consequently, a typical set contains most of the probability mass, and its size is approximately \(2^{nH(X)}\), with each sequence having probability approximately \(2^{-nH(X)}\). Source coding can achieve about \(H(X)\) bits per symbol with rare failures, while rates below \(H(X)-\epsilon\) asymptotically encode almost no sequences.

The lecture then extends these ideas to finite-state, ergodic Markov sources, defined as labeled transitions on irreducible, aperiodic chains. These chains have unique stationary state probabilities approached exponentially from any initial distribution. Using block coding conditioned on the current state yields an expected rate approaching the conditional entropy \(H(X\mid S)\), which accounts for source memory and is no greater than the unconditional entropy.

Finally, the lecture introduces the universal Lempel–Ziv approach, particularly LZ77. Unlike Huffman coding, it requires no predefined probability model and can discover changing or unrecognized statistical structure. LZ77 initially sends the first window of symbols uncompressed, then repeatedly finds the longest unencoded sequence matching earlier text in a sliding window. It encodes the match length with a unary–binary code and the match position using a fixed-length window address; unmatched symbols are sent literally. Typical-set analysis suggests that matching achieves asymptotically the same rate as a model-specific coder for a Markov source. Window size balances search speed, overhead, and responsiveness when source statistics change.

President Bush thanks West Point’s leaders and cadets, using recent sports losses to emphasize that setbacks should be met by giving one’s best, learning from defeat, and moving forward. Addressing cadets as commander in chief, he says the Cold War’s end offers greater democratic cooperation and reduced nuclear risk, but war, dictatorship, weapons proliferation, and terrorism remain threats. The United States should remain engaged abroad and help build a world order based on democratic, tolerant, economically free governments and peaceful resolution of disputes.

Such leadership requires engagement rather than isolationism, but neither unilateralism nor universal intervention. Military force should be used only through judgment, when stakes and likely benefits justify its costs, limited scope, and human sacrifice. The United States should seek international support and shared military and economic burdens when possible, while remaining prepared to act alone when necessary. Any intervention requires a clear mission, realistic plan, and achievable withdrawal criteria. Examples discussed include operations in Kuwait, Iraq, Somalia, Panama, and the Philippines.

Effective defense also requires modern forces, including peacekeeping capabilities, but weapons alone are insufficient: leadership, training, people, meritocracy, education, and equal opportunity are essential. The all-volunteer military is praised as a model of service and personal responsibility.

The president tells cadets that military service embodies duty, honor, country, sacrifice, and a purpose beyond oneself, while encouraging public service through government, volunteering, and community work. Recalling that he left school and enlisted in the Navy on his eighteenth birthday in 1942, he says he has never regretted the choice. He wishes the cadets well and grants them amnesty.

The Paris arbitration tribunal held that the treaties’ reference to the “great ocean commonly called the Pacific Ocean” included the Bering Sea and, by the same reasoning, the Okhotsk Sea. It noted that Russia had restricted its Bering Sea jurisdiction to cannon-shot range and had not exercised exclusive rights over seal fisheries beyond territorial waters. The tribunal rejected exclusive control over large seas connected to an ocean, emphasizing the freedom of open seas for navigation and fishing. Coastal restrictions may protect a bordering state’s security but cannot deprive connected waters of their open-sea character; states cannot unilaterally impose laws, judge foreign mariners, or detain and search foreign ships there.

The passage establishes a fine-grained hierarchy of quantum replica advantage for estimating nonlinear state properties. A \(k\)-replica protocol may jointly measure at most \(k\) copies of an unknown state. For estimating \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{\otimes(k+1)}O)\), the work proves that \(k\)-replica protocols require exponentially many samples in the system dimension for broad classes of observables, whereas \((k+1)\)-replica measurements make the task efficient with constant sample complexity. In the stated setting, the lower bound is \(\Omega(\sqrt d/(k\varepsilon^{1/(k+1)}))\), while direct \((k+1)\)-replica estimation uses \(O(k/\varepsilon^2)\) samples. A further upper bound shows that \(\lceil(k+1)/2\rceil\)-replica protocols suffice with complexity \(\widetilde O(\max\{k\sqrt d/\varepsilon,k/\varepsilon^2\})\). These results yield constant-versus-exponential, polynomial-versus-exponential, and subexponential-versus-exponential separations depending on \(k\).

The central technical tool is an indistinguishability principle for Haar-assembled ensembles: ensembles formed from tensor products and mixtures of Haar-random states, with arbitrary multiplicities, unitaries, and fixed states. Any one-replica protocol needs \(\Omega(\sqrt{d_{\min}/(m a_{\max}^2)})\) samples to distinguish such an ensemble from its average with constant success. The proof combines Haar integrals, permutation operators, concentration of measure, one-sided likelihood-ratio bounds, and Le Cam’s two-point method.

Lower-bound hard instances use probability distributions whose moments agree through degree \(k\) but differ at degree \(k+1\). Chebyshev polynomials provide an optimal moment gap of \(2(2(k+1))^{-k}\). Haar-random mixtures built from these distributions are indistinguishable by \(k\)-replica protocols but can be separated using a \((k+1)\)-degree property. A subspace restriction handles possibly traceless observables, while a Gram–Schmidt-based rounding step yields spectrum-testing instances with exact target spectra.

The principle also yields lower bounds for spectrum testing, rank testing, and estimation of non-integer trace powers. When two spectra agree through degree \(k\) and each has at most \(m\) nonzero entries, \(k\)-replica spectrum testing requires \(\Omega(\sqrt d/(m\sqrt{\ln m}))\) samples. Rank testing consequently requires \(\Omega(\sqrt d/(k\sqrt{\ln k}))\) samples. These results identify unavoidable dimension dependence under bounded-replica protocols, unlike unrestricted methods.

Upper bounds combine generalized swap tests, splitting the replica count into two nearly equal groups, and distributed inner-product estimation. The passage identifies open questions concerning improved error dependence, the precise precision threshold for hardness, broader spectrum-testing regimes, and lower bounds that account for the number of working qubits rather than only replica count.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture spans GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs, the A40 data-center GPU, and the RTX A6000 workstation GPU. GDDR6X memory uses PAM4 signaling, encoding two bits per clock edge across four voltage levels spaced in 250 mV increments. MTA encoding limits extreme voltage transitions to improve signal-to-noise ratio, alongside new training, adaptation, equalization, and signal-integrity measures. GDDR6X supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, with pseudo-independent memory channels benefiting BVH ray traversal.

NVIDIA RTX IO addresses bottlenecks in traditional file systems and storage APIs by working with Microsoft DirectStorage to transfer compressed assets directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU. It offloads lossless decompression from potentially dozens of CPU cores to the GPU, with NVIDIA claiming up to 100-times I/O performance versus hard drives and traditional APIs. RTX IO is intended to improve loading times, frame rates, texture streaming, and reduction of object pop-in and stutter, while also supporting professional visualization and rendering workflows.

The A40 combines second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, 48 GB of memory, and PCIe Gen4 connectivity. NVIDIA reports up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI-training throughput of a Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity. Two A40 GPUs can be linked with NVLink for 96 GB of combined memory. The GPU also supports vGPU virtualization, Quadro Sync, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including Display Stream Compression and dynamic HDR support. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs provide the first AV1 hardware decoding implementation and can decode 8K60 HDR content with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC, reducing CPU demand and exceeding x264 Fast quality while matching x264 Medium in cited streaming tests.

GA10x offers up to twice the performance of the prior architecture in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance and adds motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity for twice their effective throughput. The RTX 3090 uses GA102, 24 GB of GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores and is reported as 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X, lacks NVLink, and is reported as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti.

The RTX A6000 includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 48 GB of GDDR6, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, motion blur, and AI denoising; pairing two cards through NVLink provides 96 GB of memory. GDDR6X’s Error Detection and Replay feature detects failed transmissions and replays them until successful, with declining useful bandwidth indicating when overclocked memory has reached its practical limit, though it cannot prevent every crash. The passage concludes with NVIDIA’s disclaimers that specifications may change, materials are provided as-is, and suitability for particular applications requires customer validation.

An email chain forwards Mimi Swartz’s November 2001 Texas Monthly article, “How Enron Blew It,” described as worth reading. The article examines Enron’s rapid transformation, internal culture and resulting decline.

Under Ken Lay, Enron evolved from a heavily indebted pipeline company into a global energy trader. Jeff Skilling developed the “Gas Bank,” which guaranteed gas supply and prices, then built a trading operation that quickly dominated the market. Enron’s revenue rose from $40 billion to $100 billion between 1985 and 2000, while its stock increased 1,700 percent. Skilling and Lay expanded the model into electricity, online commodity trading, bandwidth and other businesses, including EnronOnline and a Blockbuster movie-delivery agreement.

Enron recruited highly educated, ambitious employees through intense interview processes and rewarded performance with uncapped bonuses, extensive perks and access to senior leaders. Its emphasis on “intellectual capital,” aggressive deal-making and speed also produced forced-ranking reviews, high employee turnover, workaholism, monitored communications and growing paranoia. Skilling’s Performance Review Committee became known for routinely removing lower-ranked workers. Workers increasingly viewed one another as competitors, while teamwork and loyalty weakened.

Enron also used mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale, booking most projected profits for long-term deals immediately and relying on its own valuation of transactions. Because Enron created and dominated many of its markets, it often controlled deal terms and could abandon projects when expected returns declined. As old asset-based businesses were shed, Rebecca Mark was assigned to build Enron’s water company, Azurix. Its difficulties, alongside troubles at the Dabhol power plant in India, reflected management’s preference for rapid results over difficult, long-term operations.

Skilling became CEO in February 2001 as Enron faced public criticism during California’s electricity crisis, questions about its accounting, executive stock sales and the collapse of its telecommunications investments. The stock fell from $80 in January to below $40 by late August. Lay returned as CEO, and Skilling resigned abruptly after visiting the families of three employees killed at a plant in England. Lay pledged to narrow Enron’s focus and reconsider the Performance Review Committee.

The article attributes Enron’s decline partly to the economic downturn but emphasizes the culture of immediate profits, ruthless internal competition and weakened loyalty. Skilling later said 90 percent of his net worth remained in Enron and expressed interest in future technology and commodity-trading ventures.

Its integrated military forces and political unity have deterred war, strengthened stability, and maintained the security of the Atlantic community. The speaker warns that reliance on separate national action contributed to the world wars, while collective action has deterred war since 1945.

The United States intends to work with its 13 NATO allies to preserve and strengthen the alliance’s deterrent capacity and extend common planning where useful. The speaker also urges all allies to resume their shared responsibilities. The Atlantic community’s strength in arms, industry, ideas, and peaceful purpose offers hope for reconciliation between Western and Eastern Europe, but achieving that hope requires ending destructive national rivalries, preserving unity, and applying human solidarity.

A penalty-kick shoot-out may determine the winner when a soccer match remains tied after regulation and any extra time and competition rules require a decisive result. It is governed by IFAB Laws 10 and 14, which determine the outcome and the procedure for taking penalties. Competition-specific modifications apply.

Each team designates an order of eligible players, beginning with five kickers each who alternate kicks from the 12-yard penalty mark. Only players on the field at the end of play, or temporarily absent because of injury or equipment adjustment, may participate. If teams have unequal numbers of players, the larger team must reduce its number to match. A team may stop early if the other has an insurmountable lead. If the score is tied after five kicks each, sudden death begins with paired kicks until one team scores and the other misses. Each eligible player must kick once before anyone kicks again. Players excluded under “reduce to equate” cannot participate further, except as a replacement for an injured goalkeeper.

The referee selects the goal through a coin toss unless safety concerns dictate otherwise, conducts another toss to determine which team kicks first, supervises compliance, and records the results. Only the designated kicker and goalkeeper may touch the ball. A goal counts when the ball crosses the goal line without touching another player, official, or outside agent, although it may touch the goalkeeper, posts, or crossbar. The shoot-out result is added to the match score, but its goals do not count toward individual statistics. An injured goalkeeper may be replaced by an available substitute, an excluded player, or another eligible player; if a goalkeeper is sent off, another player who finished the match must take the role. If another player is injured or sent off, the opposing team must reduce its numbers. A kicker who leaves the field and fails to return forfeits the kick, and the match continues even if a team falls below seven players.

Coaches should review applicable rules, designate players for the coin tosses, practice the full procedure, identify and rank up to eleven likely kickers, analyze opponents, and prepare goalkeepers to handle each kick independently. Before extra time ends, coaches should keep likely shooters on the field, confirm the kick order, avoid a defensive letdown, and maintain a calm approach. After the match, teams should review tactics and performance and give constructive feedback regardless of the result.

On June 24, 2020, Tesla entered a 90-day indemnification agreement with CEO Elon Musk. During the bridge term, Musk will provide, from personal funds, up to $100 million in directors’ and officers’ indemnity coverage for amounts not indemnifiable by Tesla. Tesla will pay a one-time fee of $972,361 and may pay an additional amount if greater to reconcile the fee to the prorated premium for a $100 million liability insurance quote, discounted by 50%. Tesla is resuming its evaluation of indemnification coverage options and will seek a binding market quote.

The Wells Fargo Reflect Card is a no-frills, $0-annual-fee credit card aimed at paying down debt or financing large purchases. It offers 0% introductory APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. Its 5% balance-transfer fee, with a $5 minimum, may be costly for large transfers, and it charges a 3% foreign-transaction fee. Benefits include up to $600 in cellphone protection against theft or damage, subject to a $25 deductible and limited to twice yearly, and personalized offers through My Wells Fargo Deals. The card offers no ongoing rewards after the introductory period and may not suit travelers or consumers seeking long-term perks. A good or excellent credit score of 670–850 is recommended, though approval is not guaranteed. Motley Fool states that advertising compensation may affect offer placement but not product ratings.

Sony’s Xperia XZ Premium is slated for an Android Oreo update in 2017, adding a 3D scanning app, predictive smile capture, and improved phase-detection burst shooting; Sony did not specify the release date.

The court affirmed the denial of Patrick Sutherland’s parole application, finding that the parole board considered the required statutory factors and did not act irrationally. Although the presentence report stated that Sutherland shot an individual despite the related charges having been dismissed, he neither refuted the report before the board nor sought its correction or challenged it at sentencing. The board was therefore entitled to rely on the report. The judgment was affirmed without costs.

The author is bullish on AGNC Investment, citing recent and expected Fed rate cuts that could reduce financing costs and boost mortgage-backed securities valuations and book value. Co-developed by Toshiba and a government research institute, the probe has cameras and a radiation detector to inspect areas that disabled earlier robots.

The president calls for reform of American programs and institutions as the nation enters the 1970s, with peace as its first priority. He reports progress toward ending the Vietnam War and advocates sharing responsibility for defense and development with other nations, strengthening alliances, and pursuing negotiations with the Soviet Union and Communist China.

Domestically, he proposes replacing the welfare system with income support, job training, and work incentives; restoring power to states and local governments through “New Federalism”; and expanding equal voting rights, employment opportunities, and property ownership. He attributes inflation primarily to federal deficits, calls for a balanced budget, and urges Congress to enact pending crime legislation, especially against organized crime, narcotics, pornography, and street crime, with increased federal support for local law enforcement.

He also presents a long-term environmental and urban-growth agenda, including a $10 billion clean-water program, preservation of parks and open spaces, stricter vehicle-emission standards, pollution-related regulations, and coordinated development of cities, suburbs, and rural communities. Concluding with a vision of an America marked by peace, opportunity, material progress, and moral and spiritual leadership, he urges citizens and elected leaders to help shape the nation’s future.

Andrea Conti’s agent says the 23-year-old’s time at Atalanta is over and he wants to move to Milan, urging the club to cooperate rather than block the transfer. Conti scored eight goals and provided four assists in 33 Serie A appearances that season.

The passage profiles Nassim Nicholas Taleb’s background, writings, and investment philosophy. It describes his upbringing in Lebanon, studies and career in France and the United States, work as a proprietary trader and academic, co-founding of Empirica Capital, and advisory role at Universa Investments with Mark Spitznagel. His *Incerto* books—*Fooled by Randomness*, *The Black Swan*, *Antifragile*, and *Skin in the Game*—address randomness, luck, uncertainty, cognitive bias, rare events, fragility, incentives, and decision-making.

Taleb argues that forecasting is often futile, success may reflect luck rather than skill, and investors should prioritize avoiding ruin and benefiting from unexpected shocks. His barbell strategy combines mostly low-risk assets with a smaller allocation to high-risk, potentially high-reward positions, avoiding a middle ground. Examples include low- and high-beta stocks, defensive stocks paired with leveraged or speculative holdings, and short- and long-term bonds. Rather than earning consistently, such a strategy seeks small losses or limited returns for much of the time and large gains during tail events. Taleb distinguishes Mediocristan, where risks remain contained, from Extremistan, where disruptions can spread and multiply.

The passage also explains antifragility as the ability to benefit from volatility and disorder, contrasting it with fragility and mere resilience, and describes *Skin in the Game* as emphasizing accountability through personal financial exposure. Universa’s tail-risk-hedging approach is presented as an institutional example of the barbell strategy. Taleb’s quoted conclusions stress preparation rather than prediction, humility about uncertainty, decentralization, experimentation, limiting errors, and judging advisers by their actions and holdings rather than their words.

Malawi Heath Equity Network urged the government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils, citing research in Ntcheu that found their absence was undermining public-fund management, accountability and transparency. Government officials said deployment plans were at an advanced stage and urged councils to support auditors rather than treat them as investigators. The research also identified weak coordination between councils, NGOs and civil society groups, limited rural participation in budget preparation, and funding of K7 million for training council members in budget tracking and transparency.

The lecture examines initial coin offerings (ICOs) as a form of crowdfunding in which a startup sells crypto tokens to raise money. ICO investors often expect the tokens to appreciate. J.R. Willett proposed the concept in 2010 as an application layer on Bitcoin. Ethereum raised $18 million in 2014, and the market expanded sharply from mid-2017 to mid-2018, when approximately $25 billion was raised. Major offerings included EOS at $4.2 billion and Telegram at $1.7 billion, after which fundraising declined substantially.

Most ICOs raise funds before their networks are operational, and roughly 75% are marketed primarily as ideas. During the 2018 boom, many lacked published source code at the time of sale, and development was generally centralized even when described as open source. Tokens are generally fungible and transferable, while promoters retain part of the supply. Some offerings use simple agreements for future tokens (SAFTs) to sell claims on tokens delivered later, partly in response to regulatory concerns.

Most tokens incorporate a monetary or supply policy, although some permit unrestricted issuance. Changes to such policies can create blockchain forks, though consensus mechanisms may allow changes without a hard fork. Researchers have limited evidence about which policies work best.

Although ICOs resemble Kickstarter and other crowdfunding models, they differ in offering digital assets, using market-driven pricing, facilitating secondary-market trading, and emphasizing potential appreciation rather than delivery of a specified product. Their rationale depends on whether a blockchain and native token are genuinely needed to address a use case.

Suggested evaluation criteria include:

- The viability and value proposition of the token’s use case.
- Whether an append-only ledger, consensus, cryptography, and a native token are necessary.
- The clarity of the white paper and the planned use of proceeds.
- Available source code and the team’s experience.
- Venture-capital participation and reputable investors.
- Community size and interest, while recognizing it may reflect momentum or FOMO.
- The token’s monetary policy, distribution, founder allocation, and offering process.

Revenue treatment varies. ICO proceeds may be recorded as deferred or current revenue, or less commonly as a liability. Some tokens circulate among network users, while others return to the issuer. Transactions involving tokens used to purchase services generally constitute taxable income, valued at market value when the service is delivered. Issuer revenue models may include initial sales, retained tokens, and later sales of those tokens.

In the United States, the SEC regulates ICOs as securities offerings, and many offerings have not complied with registration requirements. Regulation varies by jurisdiction. The lecture also identifies scalability, performance, privacy, security, network coordination, interoperability, and competition as important blockchain considerations.

Third-quarter 2018 data showed approximately 1.8 billion dollars raised, down 78% from the second quarter. Monthly published offerings had fallen from roughly 400–500 to about 200. Approximately 84% used Ethereum, 57% raised less than $100,000, 67% were classified as unsuccessful, 76% were based only on an idea, and very few had source code or were fully ready. Gensler predicted that more than 90% of ICOs would eventually fail and that the ICO wave would diminish, while cautioning that this would not mean blockchain technology itself was ending.
