The passage studies ML-definability and ML-separability of modal µ-calculus formulas over pointed Kripke structures, including words and trees with bounded or unbounded outdegree. A formula ψ separates φ and φ′ when φ entails ψ and ψ entails ¬φ′. Definability is the special case of separating φ from ¬φ, while Craig interpolation additionally requires the separator to use only common symbols.

The analysis uses parity-game semantics, nondeterministic parity tree automata, bisimulation, and joint consistency under finite-depth bisimulation. Exponential-size tree automata can represent µML formulas, enabling complexity and construction arguments.

ML-definability is ExpTime-complete over all models and trees of outdegree at least two. ML-separability is ExpTime-complete over all models and binary trees, but 2-ExpTime-complete for trees of outdegree at least three. Over words, both definability and separability are PSpace-complete. Separator construction takes exponential time over words, doubly exponential time over all models and binary trees, and triply exponential time for higher-arity trees. Word separators are optimal; unrestricted and binary constructions are optimal under mild assumptions, while optimality for higher-arity trees is conjectured.

ML has Craig interpolation over all models, words, and binary trees, but lacks it over trees of outdegree at least three. Consequently, the modal logic K⊕alt_d has Craig interpolation exactly when d ≤ 2. Craig-interpolant existence over higher-arity trees is coNExpTime-complete.

With graded modalities, using graded modal logic for both definability and separability makes both problems ExpTime-complete. Using ordinary ML instead gives ExpTime-complete definability but 2-ExpTime-complete separability for graded µML formulas.

The DAWn-Plasma study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial comparing supportive care plus convalescent plasma with supportive care alone in adults hospitalized with COVID-19. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines and required ethics approval and informed consent. Of 499 patients assessed, 489 were randomized 2:1 to plasma plus supportive care (n=326) or supportive care alone (n=163). The full analysis set excluded one patient without confirmed COVID-19 and five who withdrew immediately after randomization, leaving 320 and 163 patients, respectively.

Intervention patients received four 200–250 mL units of convalescent plasma, totaling 800–1,000 mL, with the first infusion within 12 hours. Plasma required neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1/160, and 80.7% of administered units had titers of at least 1/320. Median time to first transfusion was five hours, and median plasma volume was 884 mL.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at day 15; secondary endpoints assessed clinical status, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, mortality, safety, antibody titers, laboratory measures, and quality of life. The primary outcome did not differ between groups: 83.7% with plasma plus supportive care versus 84.1% with supportive care alone (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No secondary endpoint showed a statistically significant difference, and results were similar in the per-protocol population. Neutralizing-antibody titers increased from baseline to day 6 regardless of intervention, while higher baseline and day-6 titers correlated with better outcomes.

Safety was similar between groups. Any adverse events occurred in 28.13% and 30.06% of patients, serious adverse events in 20.62% and 20.68%, and fatal adverse events in 10.31% and 9.82%, respectively. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 intervention patients (6.0%), with no TRALI cases reported. Overall, early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not improve the primary or secondary outcomes.

Inspired by Elle Woods, she used her attorney skills to prepare a final speech anticipating arguments and counterarguments. The President transmitted to Congress the report of James Bronson Reynolds and Commissioner Charles P. Neill, appointed to investigate Chicago stock yards, urging legislation for drastic federal inspection of stockyards, packing houses, and their products in interstate or foreign commerce.

He called the Chicago conditions revolting and existing law inadequate: yards and packing houses were kept unclean, meat handling was dangerous to health, and the government lacked power to enforce inspection of prepared meat products in interstate commerce, though uninspected meat could not be shipped abroad. Inadequate appropriations left establishments without inspectors, and the government lacked power to remedy alleged chemical and dye abuses.

He directed that meat labels state only that the carcass was inspected at slaughter, saying he would order inspection labels and certificates on canned products discontinued absent inspection at all stages. He recommended a law enabling inspection "from the hoof to the can," financed by a fee per animal slaughtered, never exceeding 8 cents per head. Because the investigation was unfinished, he could not report on chemical abuses or doctoring of tainted meat, and he urged passage of Senate amendment No. 29, the "Beveridge amendment."

This quantitative bibliometric study analyzed STEAM education with gamification using Scopus documents published from 2017 to 2023, with a final dataset of 34 English-language papers. It examined publication trends, citations, sources, authors, subject areas, keywords, country collaboration, and research topics.

Publication output increased from 2017, reaching eight papers in 2022. The most cited article was Wannapiroon and Pimdee’s study on Thai undergraduates’ STEAM creative-thinking and innovation development, with 30 citations. The leading authors were Kummanee, Nilsook, Wannapiroon, Lee, and Piriyasurawong, each with three publications. Thailand had the most publications and citations, followed by Italy and Malaysia in publication volume, while Bulgaria was also identified as a leading contributor.

Computer science accounted for 37.7% of the papers, followed by social sciences at 20.5%, engineering at 16.9%, decision sciences at 7.2%, and business, management, and accounting at 4.8%. The most frequent keywords were gamification, STEAM, STEAM education, and computational thinking.

Malaysia had the greatest total link strength in the country network, while Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France formed an active collaboration cluster. Factorial analysis grouped the literature into educational methodologies and interaction tools, student-centered learning environments, and educational technologies and engagement strategies. Overall, the study documented growing international interest in STEAM education with gamification.

He said the shift would support a fully integrated mining complex and the company’s long-term strategy. The article examines a dialogic educational intervention developed for emergency remote teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using Freire’s critical pedagogy and Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT), Arthur Santiago and Christiano Mattos adapted a face-to-face activity for 19 physics teacher-education students at a Brazilian federal university. The seven-stage activity addressed conflicting views on reopening schools, the reliability of information sources, and scientific communication. Students researched COVID-19 materials, discussed opposing positions, and collaboratively produced an infographic on the benefits and risks of returning to in-person classes.

Discord served as the intervention’s teaching environment. Its text and voice channels, group spaces, recorded discussions, shared resources, and unrestricted student access supported dialogue, movement among groups, and participation without constant teacher mediation. Qualitative analysis of four meetings found that students discussed pandemic-related time management, domestic responsibilities, and lost face-to-face interaction before connecting these experiences to the broader sociopolitical issue of school reopening. Students divided tasks, exchanged information, met independently, and produced and disseminated materials collaboratively, demonstrating increased autonomy and agency.

The authors concluded that Discord’s familiarity among students and its support for self-organization expanded dialogic interaction and linked students’ immediate concerns with wider social contradictions. They also emphasized that emergency remote education was an improvised response that often reinforced inequalities and reduced student voice, particularly in Brazil’s under-resourced public schools.

Under Fran Horowitz, Abercrombie & Fitch has rebounded from its former trend-driven, exclusionary image to record revenue approaching $5 billion. Since taking over in 2017, she decentralized management, raised clothing quality and shifted away from chasing “cool” toward becoming a long-lasting lifestyle brand. Sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion from 2019 to 2024, while Hollister also grew; the two brands’ combined sales are expected to exceed $5 billion this year. To sustain momentum, Abercrombie is expanding partnerships, including selling Abercrombie Kids at Macy’s and becoming the NFL’s first fashion partner, offering merchandise for all 32 leagues. Horowitz sees the NFL deal as an opportunity to better serve female fans while boosting customer acquisition and brand awareness.

A spring 2025 quasi-experimental study at a large R1 public university compared three laboratory approaches to teaching electric potential and equipotential lines in an introductory physics course for life sciences. Students were assigned to a traditional physical-equipment lab, a prebuilt AI-designed simulation, or an AI-engagement lab in which students prompted Claude Sonnet 4 to generate, technically and scientifically validate, and iteratively refine their own simulations.

Both simulation groups scored significantly better than the physical-equipment group on immediate conceptual questions (Kruskal–Wallis H(2) = 58.718, p < .001, η² = .359), while no significant overall difference occurred between the two simulation groups. No significant group differences appeared on the midterm or final exam. Students using either digital approach reported more favorable attitudes than those using physical equipment on all five survey questions; the prebuilt simulation was rated more favorably than AI development on one question.

The findings indicate that AI-guided simulation development can support conceptual learning as effectively as using a validated prebuilt simulation while also providing practice in modeling, validation, debugging, and productive AI use. The authors identify prebuilt simulations, AI-guided simulation development, and physical equipment as complementary approaches supporting different learning goals. Limitations include differences in task abstraction, free-tier AI restrictions and technical assistance, and the examination of one topic at one institution with a predominantly life-sciences student population. Possible effects on modeling and experimental skills remain preliminary.

This patent application is a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 16/777,879 (filed Jan. 30, 2020), itself a continuation of Ser. No. 16/109,048 (filed Aug. 22, 2018), claiming priority to Provisional No. 62/553,241 (filed Sep. 1, 2017).

Background. The disclosure relates to electronic gaming, and more particularly to gaming machines (EGMs) offering wagering games such as slots, video poker, blackjack, roulette, bingo and keno. A player establishes a credit balance and places wagers on a base game; bonus or secondary games may be triggered by a base-game outcome and can award extra credits, jackpots, progressives or other awards. Slot games display symbols in a grid with matching combinations along paylines, with awards shown in a pay-table and wager levels adjustable. A random number generator determines outcomes, and RTP and RNG randomness are highly regulated. Some games include an element of player skill. Bonus games follow rules differing from the base game and may award prizes distinct from base-game prizes.

Summary. The invention covers gaming systems, methods and machines providing a stop-based bonus game (e.g., a wheel or reel with multiple stops) whose stops are associated with two classes of awards: first awards (typically large-denomination jackpots) and second awards (typically small-denomination credit prizes or non-jackpot awards). When a player selects a stop associated with a second award, that stop is thereafter associated with a first award, increasing the odds of winning a first award in later play.

Described embodiments include a method in which a processor, upon a primary game outcome, initiates a bonus game, displays a bonus wheel with a plurality of stop positions (at least one associated with a secondary jackpot wheel), selects a first stop position, determines that it is associated with the secondary jackpot wheel, displays that wheel with stops associated with jackpot awards or credit prizes, selects a stop associated with a credit prize, awards that credit prize (optionally before replacement), and replaces it with a jackpot award so the stop thereafter shows the jackpot instead. Additional implementations select a second stop position on the bonus wheel associated with a second credit prize and replace it with a second jackpot award, and update the displayed wheel accordingly. Corresponding system and article-of-manufacture claims are provided.

Further embodiments describe a bonus game construct with stop positions each associated with a first or second award, having graphical indicators; selection occurs in response to trigger events (a base-game outcome, a second bonus wheel's selected stop, a player input signal after such selection, or a free-play award), and a selected stop associated with a second award is re-associated with a first award. First awards may be jackpot or progressive awards worth at least 4× to 40× (or more) the highest non-jackpot award; second awards may be fixed credits, multiplier bonuses, wild symbols, free plays of the bonus game or a base game, additional stop selections, or no-value awards. Constructs may be wheels, reels, dice or a grid-based treasure map. Associations may persist across base-game play and from one player to the next, may be randomized for grid-type games, and may reset to default associations after a first award is won (optionally reducing the number of stops associated with that award). Dice-type games may select multiple stops, with first-award payout contingent on all or a subset of stops being first awards.

Detailed Description. Example gaming devices (Relm XL, Arc and Helix models) may be networked with central determination, TITO, player tracking, progressive and casino management servers, or operated stand-alone; they may include reels, main and secondary displays, topper wheels or screens, bill validators, ticket printers/readers, card readers, player tracking interfaces, speakers and information panels. Gaming hardware and software differ from general-purpose computers due to regulatory, environmental, security, fault-tolerance and componentry requirements. Credits are inserted via coin acceptor or bill validator, wagers decrease the balance and wins increase it, and the player cashes out via a ticket printer. Bonus games are initiated during or after the primary game and may be tiered.

FIGS. A–J depict a bonus wheel initially having one stop associated with a "Jackpot" award and seventeen stops associated with fixed credit awards (e.g., 4000, 150, 2000 and 50 credits). Each credit win re-associates that stop with the Jackpot award, so the number of jackpot stops grows with play; in the example the jackpot is won once 50% of stops are associated with the first award. A specific implementation uses a bonus wheel with spinning inner and outer wheels plus four jackpot wheels (GRAND, MAJOR, MINOR, MINI), where the inner wheel yields credit prizes or free games and the outer wheel yields features such as "Wilds Added," with a player-selected spin option initiating the wheel spins.
Some dogs show an irresistible attraction to toys, and their play may parallel human behavioral addictions.

Stanford psychologists found that appealing, taste-focused vegetable labels increased selections by 25% over basic labels, 35% over positive health labels, and 41% over restrictive health labels among nearly 28,000 dining-hall students. Students also piled more produce on their plates. With only about 10% of adults and 1% of teens and tweens meeting vegetable recommendations, the article encourages making vegetables more appetizing through flavorful names and preparations. Suggested recipes include grilled carrots with chipotle-lime aioli, nacho-cheese kale chips, chili-lime corn salad, beet chips, cauliflower fried rice, and green beans with bleu cheese and walnuts.

A Hubble Space Telescope image shows the arachnid-shaped Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus) and the blue Honeycomb Nebula. ESA research suggests the Honeycomb’s unusual bubble-like form results from interactions between old and new supernovae and our viewing angle.

The March 2006 AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 Specification Update documents known deviations affecting the PIT, PIC, DMA, PMC/ACPI, GLIU/PCI, USB, LPC, SMBus, ATA/UDMA, UART, KEL, clock gating, and power-management features. Most entries provide a description, operational impact, and workaround or resolution. Several defects affect only debug or diagnostic functions, have negligible normal-operation impact, or have not been observed in real systems.

Notable issues include nonstandard PIT command cancellation and count-mode behavior; a hanging GLIU debug port; duplicate interrupts from XPIC AEOI mode; incorrect DMA rotating-priority order; and failed UART or LPC I/O during block and demand DMA modes. Software DMA from LPC does not write memory, while invalid PCI I/O addresses of 10000h or higher can hang the system. Thermal alarms in standby rely on power cycling for recovery, and Sleep Clock must remain enabled in the PMC when related sleep options are used.

The CS5535 does not meet the USB overvoltage protection specification and requires external protection; USB and UART clock gating also cause unreliable operation in some modes. UDMA defects include CRC corruption after device termination, PRD prefetch hazards, and possible ATAC hangs from non-DWORD-aligned PRDs. ATAC drivers should use DWORD alignment, define PRD tables before transfers, and issue PIO commands before enabling bus mastering. The ATAC SSMI debug feature does not correctly block IDE I/O.

GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs may be lost when clock gating is enabled, and GLIU error flags do not always report unexpected addresses. PCI retry handling, back-to-back reads, and IRDY#/DEVSEL# timing deviations are also documented. Byte access to ACPI PM1_STS or PM1_EN hangs, while word and byte writes to PMC registers can corrupt other registers; DWORD access or an SMI trap is recommended. Most GPIO wake inputs do not work from ACPI S3, requiring PWRBTN# or external circuitry. Other documented problems affect RTC RAM access, KEL emulation, SMB NEGACK handling, GPIO writes after suspend, LOWBAT_FLAG reporting, LPC synchronization, and SLEEP_X/SLEEP_Y deassertion. Recommended workarounds include disabling affected clock-gating modes, using single-transfer DMA, applying read-modify-write operations after suspend, clearing SMB status twice, and programming sleep delays below the PM_SED delay.

The lecture develops electroweak unification by combining weak and electromagnetic interactions. Heavy gauge-boson mediation mitigates their different strengths, while weak vector-axial couplings are recast through chiral projections and left-handed neutrino-electron doublets. The electromagnetic current separates into left- and right-handed components without mixed terms, explaining why QED conserves helicity.

Weak isospin is organized into triplet currents \(W_1,W_2,W_3\), while hypercharge forms a singlet. A neutral current is defined as twice the electromagnetic current minus twice \(W_3\), incorporating the right-handed coupling needed for electrons to interact with the \(Z\) boson. The charged \(W^+\) and \(W^-\) bosons are linear combinations of \(W_1\) and \(W_2\). Mixing \(W_3\) with the hypercharge singlet \(B\) using the weak mixing angle \(\theta_W\) produces the photon and \(Z\) boson, consistently recovering the observed gauge bosons. The passage also notes, but defers, the complication that mass eigenstates need not be weak-interaction eigenstates.

Cleveland coach Kevin Stefanski said there is no single thing rookie Shedeur Sanders must do to earn the backup quarterback job, emphasizing player development and readiness. Dillon Gabriel remains the starter, with the backup role open between Sanders and Bailey Zappe. Sanders is expected to remain third string, while Jerry Jeudy praised his professionalism and preparation.

The article advises five strategies for Abalone: avoid rushing into offense early, plan moves by anticipating the board and opponents’ mistakes, move pieces safely toward the center for greater mobility, begin defensively but eventually attack as eliminating five counters first reduces an opponent’s ability to recover, and split opponents’ counters into smaller groups, ideally pushing them toward the edge while watching for counterattacks.

The President reports national progress in strength, comfort, education, knowledge, morality, and peace, while presenting the challenges of a growing nation as requiring factual judgment, common purpose, and conciliation.

Foreign policy is described as centered on peace, international cooperation, and reduced military tensions. The Kellogg-Briand Pact has committed 54 nations to renounce war, and the administration seeks adherence to the International Court of Justice without entering the League of Nations. A London conference is planned with Britain, France, Italy, and Japan to limit naval armaments. The arms embargo on Mexico has been lifted, and relations with Mexico and other Latin American countries are being strengthened. American mediation has contributed to settlements involving Chile and Peru, Bolivia and Paraguay, and Guatemala and Honduras. Regular international air-mail service has begun. U.S. Marines remain in Nicaragua, Haiti, and China, but reductions are underway, especially in Nicaragua and China, while a commission will examine the Haitian situation. Additional resources and experienced diplomatic personnel are sought for the State Department and Latin American missions.

The Army and Navy are considered adequate for national defense, but their rapidly increasing cost is a concern. Federal defense expenditures are projected to exceed $730 million, and potentially costly naval construction may follow the Washington treaty unless international limits are reached. Military forces are to remain defensive and proportionate to national needs, while National Guard improvements and advances in aviation strengthen security.

Government finances are described as sound. Public debt has declined substantially from its 1919 peak, and projected surpluses of approximately $225 million for fiscal 1930 and $123 million for fiscal 1931 support provisional tax reductions. Recommended individual income-tax rates would fall from 5, 3, and 1.5 percent to 4, 2, and 0.5 percent, while the corporate rate would decline from 12 to 11 percent, reducing 1930 income taxes by an estimated $160 million.

Settlements of foreign debts are nearing completion. Agreements have been concluded with Greece and ratified by France; Austria’s agreement remains contingent on approval by other creditors, while Russia and Armenia remain unsettled. A revised settlement with Germany is being prepared. Foreign governments owe the United States $11.579 billion in funded debt, requiring substantial annual interest payments and eventual repayment of principal. Nearly all seized alien enemy property, originally valued at about $625 million, has been returned.

Despite broad prosperity and gains in production, distribution, and living standards, a speculative stock-market crash reduced consumption and employment. Because Federal measures and strong banks prevented impairment of the credit system, capital is returning to business, foreign trade has expanded, and no commodity inflation or serious overstock occurred. Voluntary cooperation among governments, business organizations, and local authorities is supporting wages, construction, and employment, restoring confidence, and preventing a more severe depression.

Agricultural conditions are improving. Farm income and farmer confidence have risen, bankruptcies have declined, and land values have stabilized. The Federal Farm Board is organizing grain, cotton, livestock, and wool marketing, supporting cooperative and farmer-controlled organizations, reducing waste, and strengthening farmers’ bargaining power.

The tariff should retain an effective agricultural protection while permitting limited revisions where economic shifts have caused substantial employment losses. Changes should consider national trade interests and preserve a flexible tariff that permits prompt adjustments after investigation by the Tariff Commission. No fundamental conflict exists between farmers, workers, or the country’s regions.

The address also urges expanded public-building authorization, additional river, harbor, flood-control, and highway appropriations, and completion of inland-waterway improvements. The Ohio River has been canalized to a uniform nine-foot depth, while other Mississippi projects and farm-to-market roads require accelerated work.

Post Office deficits and costly leases require reform, along with revised air-mail rates and expanded South American service. Commercial aviation has developed rapidly through federally improved airways, private operation, expanding airports, and extensive passenger, mail, and express networks. Railroads are physically and financially sound, but consolidation procedures require simplification. Merchant marine policy is transferring government lines to private ownership and using mail contracts and construction loans to expand American shipping, though additional authority and larger future contracts are needed.

Banking law should be reviewed to address chain banking, credit concentration, rural bank failures, and restrictions on national branch banking. Full-time Federal Power Commissioners, stronger interstate power coordination, and a permanent national Radio Commission are also recommended. Muscle Shoals facilities should be leased in a way that reserves revenues and research capacity for agriculture. Boulder Dam power contracts should recover all government outlays. A conservation commission will address oil and gas permits, overgrazing, reclamation policy, and division of responsibilities between federal and state governments.

Federal social policy should preserve local responsibility while providing research, information, temporary aid, and leadership in education, health, housing, recreation, employment, and child welfare. Public health should be organized through competent local units supported by state and federal cooperation. Federal prisons are overcrowded and require new institutions, improved probation and parole, and a Bureau of Prisons. Immigration restriction should continue, but admission priorities should favor physical fitness, character, training, and national need.

Veterans’ benefits should continue and administration should be consolidated into one agency. Competitive civil-service examinations should extend to third-class postmasters. Government reorganization should group related activities under unified leadership, separate administrative functions from boards and commissions, and delegate some authority to the executive.

Prohibition enforcement should be strengthened by consolidating detection and prosecution in the Department of Justice, simplifying minor-offense procedures, codifying prohibition laws, and creating a unified Coast Guard border patrol. The National Commission on Law Observance and Enforcement will study crime, organized crime, and judicial shortcomings, while additional personnel and appropriations are needed for federal prosecutors, clerks, and marshals. The address concludes that government should sustain local self-government, justice, ordered liberty, opportunity, prosperity, education, knowledge, religious tolerance, the family, and peace.

This divisional application describes automated cryogenic storage and retrieval systems for biological or chemical samples. Embodiments include one or more insulated storage vaults with rotating racks, storage trays, and vertical shuttles, connected to a sample handling module (SHM). A robotic arm with an insulated gripper transfers samples between vaults, external ports, and removable portable cryogenic workstations while maintaining samples below their glass-transition temperature during brief exposure to non-cryogenic environments. Refrigerant coils, dry-gas flow, and humidity monitoring regulate temperature and dew point, while a controller coordinates transfers, tray positioning, barcode-based sample identification, and database updates. Sealed covers, locking mechanisms, datum pins, maintenance hatches, and docking interfaces support safe handling. Additional embodiments address retrieval procedures, tray jams, a four-stage disaster-recovery process, cryogenic camera and alternative rack designs, and a cryotrap-based system for accelerating dehumidification after maintenance access.

This cross-sectional study characterized plasma Alzheimer’s disease (AD) biomarkers in 1,067 Amish adults aged 65 and older enrolled in the Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project in Ohio and Indiana. Participants were classified as cognitively unimpaired, mild cognitive impairment, cognitively impaired but not AD, or cognitively impaired due to AD. Researchers measured plasma Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/Aβ40, total tau, p-tau181, Aβ42/t-tau, and Aβ42/p-tau181 and used regression, ROC analyses, cross-validation, and k-medoids clustering.

Aβ40, Aβ42, and Aβ42/Aβ40 did not differ significantly across diagnostic groups. Compared with cognitively unimpaired participants, those with AD had higher p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181. After covariate adjustment, p-tau181 was strongly associated with AD among APOE ε4 carriers but not noncarriers. Aβ42/Aβ40 was associated with cognitive preservation at the threshold of significance, while lower p-tau181 and higher Aβ42/p-tau181 were associated with cognitive preservation in analyses excluding mild cognitive impairment. Models containing all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau181 classified AD with an AUC of 0.83; the best cognitive-preservation model achieved an AUC of 0.71, increasing to 0.77 when mild cognitive impairment was excluded.

Two-cluster analysis separated participants into a low-risk profile with higher Aβ42/Aβ40 and lower p-tau181 and a high-risk profile with lower amyloid measures and higher p-tau181. The high-risk cluster contained more APOE ε4 carriers and AD cases. Secondary analyses supported three clusters with distinct amyloid and tau profiles. Limitations include the small, nonrepresentative Amish sample, diagnoses based mainly on medical history and cognitive testing without imaging or CSF confirmation, the indirect nature of plasma biomarkers, and the cross-sectional design. The findings support p-tau181, Aβ42/Aβ40, and Aβ42/p-tau181 as promising noninvasive indicators, but longitudinal validation is needed.

The coach praised the team’s puck-pursuit strategy, which forces opponents’ defensemen to turn and chase pucks while wearing them down. He emphasized that players must keep responding to adversity, make quick decisions, avoid feeding San Jose’s transition game, use speed and skating to create space, and trust the process. Veterans have led this approach.

Sid was described as an relentless, complete player who excels at faceoffs, puck battles, defense, scoring, and creating offensive threats. His work ethic and attention to detail inspire teammates. Phil scores dangerous goals through his shot release and velocity, has strong chemistry with his linemates, and helps generate timely offense. Geno is creating primary and secondary chances, while Bryan remained a game-time decision after skating that morning.

San Jose was credited with strong low-zone puck protection and effective use of its defensemen. The coaching staff plans to continue improving shot-lane coverage, stick play, and puck disruption to keep opponents off the score sheet.

Conor’s quickness makes him highly effective, but the staff is monitoring his workload because the demanding playoff schedule has caused him to tire. Veteran players have helped him adjust, develop consistency, and understand NHL expectations.

Chris creates havoc through forechecking, physical play, turnovers, and playmaking. The team’s defenseman contributes through mobility, puck retrieval, first passes, rushing, and offensive instincts, and is deployed situationally to use those strengths. The forwards provide balanced line matchups and an offensive threat against opponents’ top lines, while Bones and Haggy offer penalty killing and defensive skill. Rusty generates offense through speed, tenacity, his shot, and willingness to go to the net.

The coach also stressed continual improvement in communication, video use, and player development, advocating patience, opportunity, and supportive environments for young players.

This continuation application concerns deuterated heterocycle fused gamma-carbolines of Formulas I–IV, in free form or as pharmaceutically acceptable salts such as p-toluenesulfonate. The compounds are intended for disorders involving serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, serotonin transporters, and dopamine D-receptor pathways, including schizophrenia and other psychotic, mood, anxiety, sleep, dementia, Parkinson’s-related, behavioral, and impulse-control disorders.

The application identifies N-dealkylation, alpha-oxidation at the piperazine ring, and carbonyl reduction as major metabolic pathways of related gamma-carbolines. Deuteration of the N-methyl group, the adjacent methylene, or both is used to limit these pathways while retaining activity comparable to non-deuterated analogs. The disclosed compounds antagonize 5-HT2A receptors, inhibit serotonin reuptake, modulate dopaminergic protein phosphorylation, and exhibit unexpectedly improved metabolic stability. Embodiments cover specified deuterium-enrichment levels, substantially pure diastereomers, and free or salt forms.

Pharmaceutical compositions include immediate-release preparations, injectable depot formulations containing compounds in biodegradable polymeric matrices, particularly PLGA, and osmotic-controlled oral delivery systems. Depot formulations may provide controlled or sustained release for approximately 14–180 days. The osmotic systems use multilayer drug and push layers or gelatin capsules with barrier, expandable, semipermeable, and orifice structures to provide controlled oral delivery.

Methods are described for treating or preventing central nervous system disorders, including residual and negative symptoms of psychosis, depression, anxiety, sleep disorders, dementia-related agitation, autism, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, Parkinson’s disease, dyskinesia, post-traumatic stress disorder, and intermittent explosive disorder. Compounds may be administered orally, parenterally, or transdermally, either alone or with antidepressants, antipsychotics, hypnotics, Parkinson’s treatments, cholinesterase inhibitors, NMDA antagonists, and other therapeutic agents. Combination therapy may permit lower doses and reduced side effects. Oral doses generally range from 1 to 100 mg daily, with lower ranges disclosed for sleep disorders and combination treatment.

Examples describe preparation of trideuterated N-methyl, dideuterated methylene, and combined deuterated compounds, including their p-toluenesulfonate salts. In mice, the disclosed deuterated compounds produced less relative amide-metabolite formation than the non-deuterated compound—0.31–0.54 versus 0.79—while retaining similar serotonin-receptor, dopamine-receptor, and serotonin-transporter binding profiles. One compound produced 98% inhibition of the human 5-HT2A receptor at 0.1 µM.

In rats, oral dosing of a dideuterated compound produced a Q-1 metabolite AUC of 67.8 ng·hr/mL versus 128.2 ng·hr/mL for the non-deuterated compound, representing an approximately 55% reduction in relative metabolism; intravenous Q-1 exposure was about 1% of parent exposure. In dogs, sublingual dosing produced approximately 72% higher parent-compound AUC for the dideuterated compound, with the Q-1 metabolite undetectable, while subcutaneous dosing yielded comparable parent exposure and metabolite ratios between the deuterated and non-deuterated compounds.

Alex Ovechkin said receiving the award meant a great deal and thanked his teammates, coaching staff, and family. He described switching from left wing to right wing as difficult but successful, credited the coaching staff’s guidance, and said he was happy to be back on track. Ovechkin also discussed a broken foot caused by a blocked shot, his decision to continue playing during the playoffs, and his readiness to return to left wing if necessary. He remained optimistic about his health and the team’s chances to win the Stanley Cup.

The Triangle Rotation offense attacks a Triangle & Two zone with three-player clockwise and counterclockwise rotations. After penetration to an elbow, O4 can pop to the opposite elbow, feed O5 on a baseline cut, or lob to O1 cutting to the basket. O4 and O1 can set side screens for a weak-side shooter. As a secondary offense, it should remain simple and emphasize fundamentals, coordination, recognition, timing, and experience. Coaches should scout opponents, explain reads and counters, vary entries and alignments, and attack weaker defenders. Instruction includes breakdown drills and scrimmages. In Triangle & Two, three players form a zone while two chasers deny passes and rebounds.

STAT’s Morning Rounds newsletter highlights metal-organic frameworks winning the chemistry Nobel and reports that Peter Marks joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases after Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. forced him to resign from the FDA. Other headlines cover measles vaccination, conversion therapy, coverage, drug pricing, telehealth, dementia, and Wall Street.

Michael Johnson, Babson College provost and marketing professor, was named John Carroll University’s first lay president in its 131-year history. The board approved a five-year contract; Johnson, 61, starts July 1. He succeeds retiring Rev. Robert Niehoff and will join JCU’s management, marketing and supply chain faculty following a national search.

This article examines ChatGPT’s development, educational applications, and the accuracy and validity of its responses. A PRISMA-guided systematic review searched Google Scholar, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost, identifying 18 eligible peer-reviewed empirical studies for thematic analysis across medicine, writing, business, finance, chemistry, academic advising, physics, social science, and programming.

Studies report potential educational benefits, including personalised learning, feedback, tutoring, course-material and assessment development, collaboration, engagement, and support for critical and creative thinking. However, concerns include plagiarism, cheating, bias, unreliable or false information, and difficulties detecting machine-generated writing. Findings indicate that ChatGPT can produce coherent, precise, well-structured writing and pass several undergraduate and professional examinations, sometimes at high scores. It performs particularly well on essay-based and memorised tasks but struggles with complex scientific questions, calculations, depth of understanding, argumentation, judgement, and higher-order thinking. It may also produce hallucinations, misunderstand nuanced prompts, and give inconsistent answers to identical questions.

The review recommends validating generated content, carefully structuring text prompts, redesigning assessments around higher-order skills, developing institutional policies and student guidance, and using ChatGPT constructively. Limitations include restricted database access, the search cutoff of 26 October 2023, and analysis only of eligible empirical, peer-reviewed English-language studies.

This institution-based cross-sectional study assessed pregnant women’s awareness, attitudes, and factors influencing their consideration of labor epidural analgesia (LEA) at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Between June 3 and August 30, 2024, 267 third-trimester pregnant women were recruited and 230 were analyzed after incomplete or unreturned questionnaires were excluded. Data were collected through structured, self-administered questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression.

Although 78% of participants had heard of LEA, only 34% had received explanations from healthcare providers during antenatal care. Previous users, family or friends, and the internet were the main information sources. While 47% believed LEA was effective for labor pain relief, only 14.3% planned to consider it; 47.8% had no plan and 37.8% were undecided. Major concerns included cost, perceived maternal side effects, fetal safety, and interference with natural labor.

Education level, monthly family income, perceptions of fetal risk, and beliefs about LEA’s pain-relieving effectiveness were significantly associated with the decision to receive LEA. The findings indicated a need for comprehensive antenatal education and counseling to address misconceptions and support informed decisions. Limitations included the single-center setting, inability to assess previous epidural experience because few women had prior exposure, and inability to track whether participants ultimately received LEA.

An analysis of 49 studies involving 266,939 people found that regular physical activity was associated with lower odds of developing depression across all age groups and continents, even after accounting for BMI, smoking and physical health. Researchers called for policies and environments that enable people to remain active.

The Four Down offense, also called Four Low or Four Flat, is primarily used for a period’s final shot but can also serve as a spread offense. It places four players along the baseline, including the best shooters in corners, creating space for an isolated ballhandler. Primary reads are a drive or pull-up jumper; defensive help allows drop passes to posts or kick-out passes to shooters. Under pressure, corners pop out for relief passes and may assume the ballhandler’s role. Crunch-time options include the Mid Screen, Triple Base Screen, and Misdirection Double, which use screens to create shots, passing lanes, or post opportunities.

The 2-3 zone is the most commonly used zone defense. Its packed alignment protects the basket and post area, limits dribble penetration, and works well against poor outside shooting, but it is vulnerable to strong outside shooters. It is effective against less quick or skilled opponents, can become an aggressive trapping defense with quick, agile players, and can contain talented or large low-post players. The post defender stays between the ball and basket, while the guards and baseline defenders shift according to ball location, move in unison, and pursue rebounds. Wing defenders may deny corner return passes or drop to assist against dominant posts. Against ball reversals, a baseline defender temporarily pressures the receiver until a guard takes over. A 1-1-3 variation uses tandem alignment to extend the point defender and disrupt offensive spacing. Trap options include corner traps, surprise point traps, and traps that force the ball away from an outstanding wing shooter. Against a dominant low-post or tall player, the post defender fronts the post while nearby defenders provide support and double- or triple-team the post when it receives the ball.

Intercontinental Exchange, parent of the New York Stock Exchange, invested $2 billion in cash in Polymarket at a $9 billion valuation and will distribute the prediction market’s data. The companies will also collaborate on tokenization initiatives. Founded in 2020, blockchain-based Polymarket gained prominence during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, with daily trading peaking near $400 million the day after the election before falling to $40 million–$80 million. Competitor Kalshi is also pursuing substantial funding as investor interest in prediction markets grows.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Caesars Entertainment Corporation (NASDAQ:CZR) from Buy to Hold. The Las Vegas-based company provides casino, hospitality, food and beverage, convention, and non-gaming entertainment services, operating primarily under the Harrah’s, Caesars, and Horseshoe brands.

Other analysts included a BidaskClub upgrade to Buy, a ValuEngine upgrade to Hold, and initiations of Buy by SunTrust with a $14 target, Outperform by Wolfe Research with a $16 target, and Outperform by Imperial Capital with a $15.50 target. Ratings were one Sell, three Hold, and seven Buy, with an average Buy rating and $14.39 consensus target.

CZR fell 0.76% in midday trading to $13.00 on volume of 4,884,465 shares. Its market capitalization was $1.94 billion. Caesars reported quarterly EPS of negative $0.21 versus a $0.26 estimate and revenue of $1 billion versus an estimated $2.11 billion. Analysts forecast $0.06 EPS for the fiscal year. Institutional investors owned 76.68% of the stock, and several major investors recently increased their positions.

The UC1825B-SP uses a sense resistor to detect transformer ripple current and shut down the switching cycle when peak current exceeds the set limit. The CS-pin threshold is approximately 1 V, and shutdown current should exceed the design’s expected maximum. Its regulated input supply range is 10–30 V; remote operation may require additional bulk capacitance, typically 100 μF. It supports push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full-bridge topologies.

Layout guidance emphasizes low-EMI inductors, keeping feedback traces direct and away from noisy power paths, placing input, optional feed-forward, and compensation capacitors near the IC, and using short, thick power traces. Switching loops should run in the same direction. A ground plane is required, with power ground separated or carefully managed from signal ground. VCC and VREF require ceramic bypass capacitors, and a high-current Schottky clamp is required between VCC and PGND. The document also covers test results, support resources, ESD precautions, packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

An email from Enron's Steven Kean forwards a compilation of February 2001 news articles on California's electricity crisis and its regional effects.

**California supply shortfall and Davis's strategy:** A Dow Jones column argued Gov. Gray Davis and the Legislature have focused on utility solvency rather than the coming summer's electricity shortage, and disputed the California Energy Commission's outlook, citing aging plant capacity, out-of-state power sales, low hydropower, and expected unplanned outages. Industry estimates put available supply near 44,000 MW against a need of 51,000 MW, and the author urged immediate rate increases to cut demand rather than rely on blackouts and long-term overpriced contracts. A separate Dow Jones piece reported that key lawmakers gave only partial support to Davis's plan to buy the three investor-owned utilities' transmission lines (agreement in principle with Southern California Edison for $2.76 billion, roughly 2.3 times book value; about $7.5 billion for 26,000 miles of lines), aimed at restoring the utilities to solvency and restructuring nearly $13 billion in undercollected power costs. Republican lawmakers and consumer groups opposed the plan, and one advocate threatened a 2002 ballot initiative.

**Peaker plant delays:** The Los Angeles Times reported construction of 29 small "peaker" plants had stalled because the Department of Water Resources sought to revise four-month-old contracts, extending three-year terms to ten years. Cal-ISO had contracted in fall 2000 for 1,279 MW of peaking capacity costing $214 million a year for three years, and hired Navigant to renegotiate after replacing Cal-ISO, whose creditworthiness fell as Edison and PG&E neared bankruptcy. The state's stated target was 1,000 MW.

**Western states:** A Times story reported other Western states face similar shortages, with a forecast of a 6% regional shortfall and 150–275 hours of rolling blackouts, largely in California, and attributed California's role to requiring utilities to buy spot power while barring cost pass-throughs. Western leaders sought to renegotiate ties with California through efforts to take over the Bonneville Power Administration, Arizona's approval of 10 new plants with eight more under consideration, and Utah's use of recall rights against the Intermountain Power Project.

**Business opinion and governor's politics:** NFIB polling found four in ten small companies said the crisis dimmed their view of California, about 20% were exploring a move, 43% said their view changed, 71% lost confidence in state leadership, and 69% had no intention of leaving; other surveys showed consumer support for electricity competition and most firms unprepared for retail competition. A Times news analysis said Davis had shifted into campaign mode, pushing a state takeover of transmission systems costing over $7 billion, spending about $1 billion a month on electricity, and offering $400 million for conservation, while risking blame if the plan failed.

**Usage and market data:** An Associated Press article reported California ranks 47th of 50 states in per-capita energy use and 49th in electricity consumption (60% of the national average), with only Texas consuming more total energy, attributing this to mild climate, conservation programs since the 1970s, and industry location. Reuters reported lower Western spot power prices on Feb. 26 as units at Navajo, Ormond Beach, and Moss Landing returned to service, listed numerous planned and unplanned outages, and noted mild temperatures reduced loads.

The New York Court of Appeals held that Manhattan Community Board 7 lacked the capacity to bring an Article 78 proceeding challenging the City Planning Department’s denial of its Freedom of Information Law request for documents concerning the proposed Trump City development. The Court distinguished capacity to sue from standing: while governmental entities generally have standing to challenge denials of records access, a legislatively created entity must derive its capacity to sue from express authority or necessary implication and show no legislative intent foreclosing suit. Although the board had an advisory role in reviewing the land-use proposal, the Charter did not authorize community boards to sue for information, denied them subpoena and independent-counsel powers, and specifically regulated the materials they could receive. Legislative history also showed that proposed authority to sue City agencies was omitted during the 1975 Charter revision. Because the board’s advisory responsibilities could be performed without a FOIL lawsuit, the Court found no implied capacity to sue, reversed the lower courts’ decisions, and dismissed the proceeding.

Two U.S. government studies exposing rats and mice to unusually high cellphone radiation found a small increase in an unusual heart tumor in male rats, but no significant problems in female rats or mice and no hard evidence concerning brain tumors. The FDA said existing safety limits remain acceptable, and study lead author John Bucher and American Cancer Society chief medical officer Dr. Otis Brawley said the animal findings do not reflect real-life use and won't change public advice, though Brawley suggested concerned users wear an earpiece. Exposure levels far exceeded typical use, and exposed rats oddly lived longer, which Bucher attributed possibly to chance. The final results dropped an earlier hint of brain tumors but found "equivocal evidence" of DNA damage and some cancers, with unclear links to phones. Longtime critic David Carpenter said the studies were too small to uncover rare problems and the brain-tumor findings "cannot be dismissed," noting cellphone use is not nearly as dangerous as cigarettes. A 2011 International Agency for Research on Cancer working group called cellphones "possibly carcinogenic," while large prior studies found little or no brain-tumor risk, including among heavy users, and a Danish study found no risk even after more than 13 years of use. California issued guidance in December for reducing radiofrequency exposure.

Cboe’s Sunday launch of U.S. bitcoin futures was volatile but orderly, with nearly 3,700 contracts traded by Monday afternoon among about 20 firms. The most-active contract rose 20% and triggered a five-minute halt before reopening normally. CEO Ed Tilly said the debut could build confidence for additional cryptocurrency products, including futures options and ETF-related options. Cboe will wait for several one-month futures settlements before developing new crypto derivatives. Three fund managers refiled for SEC approval of bitcoin ETFs, while Cboe appealed an SEC ruling blocking Gemini’s proposed ETF. Tilly also anticipated futures on other cryptocurrencies as demand grows.

Premium subscriptions include Lex, Editor’s Choice, FT Newsmine, Martin Sandbu’s Free Lunch, EM Squared, daily FT ePaper and exclusive weekly emails, offering investment commentary, macroeconomic analysis, global economic insights and editor-led newsletters.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. It can enter power-down mode through a logic-low PWDN pin or by setting PD_CH to 11b in register C0h of bank 1. Following power-up or reset, a free-running sampling clock must be connected before the initialization register-write sequence is performed. User-defined configuration can then select the data interface, analog input ranges and bandwidths, and common-mode ranges. A free-running sampling clock is required for normal operation.

Speed-boost mode supports sampling rates up to 8 MSPS for a selected pair of analog input channels while the other six channels remain idle. The selected pair is converted on every sampling clock, and the sampling rate equals the clock frequency. The data-output interface specifications remain unchanged in this mode.

The configuration interface provides SPI access to 16-bit registers divided among three banks. Bank 0 is always accessible; banks 1 and 2 are selected through REG_BANK_SEL at address 03h. With SPI_RD_EN cleared, register writes select the target bank and then write the addressed register. Register reads require SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE to be set, use separate frames to select the bank and retrieve the register value, and must restore write mode afterward.

Multiple ADCs can be configured in an SPI daisy chain with shared CS and SCLK signals and serial SDI-to-SDO connections. Data passes through each ADC with a 24-SCLK delay while CS is active. DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the number of ADCs excluding the first device. A chained register write requires N × 24 SCLKs in one SPI frame, so a four-device chain requires 96 SCLKs. Chained reads use separate address and data phases for all devices.

The documented registers control SPI and daisy-chain operation, bank selection, initialization, power-down, reference and output-lane settings, common-mode ranges, averaging, data formatting, PRBS XOR, digital test patterns, user-defined output bits, speed boost, and gain-error correction. Reserved fields are designated not to be changed from their reset values.

For automated test equipment, separate PMU outputs can be connected to individual ADC channels or multiplexed onto one channel. The ADS9803 provides low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz; wide-bandwidth operation settles multiplexed PMU signals to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. ADC accuracy is characterized by total unadjusted error, and the application guidance specifies offset and gain calibration at a defined temperature and supply voltage.

The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies, with no required power-up sequence; VDD_1V8 and IOVDD may use a common 1.8-V supply. Layout guidance calls for 0.1-µF bypass capacitors near each supply, separate reference decoupling near REFIO and REFM, short ground-plane connections, and avoidance of vias between supply or reference pins and their bypass capacitors. Digital routing should not cross analog signal paths, and analog and reference signals should remain away from noise sources.

Texas Instruments also provides development tools, documentation-update notifications, E2E support resources, and electrostatic-discharge handling guidance.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit successive-approximation ADC-based data-acquisition device with an integrated analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, precision reference, and reference buffer. It supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs with straight-binary output; LSB size equals FSR/2¹⁶.

External-reference mode is selected by setting `INTREF_DIS` in `RANGE_SEL_REG` to 1 and applying a filtered 4.096 V reference to REFIO. The internal buffer drives REFCAP, requiring at least 10 µF between REFCAP and REFGND plus 1 µF decoupling near REFCAP. The buffer must not drive external loads. Its typical temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C, with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C over −40°C to +125°C.

An active-high alarm output supports programmable high- and low-input thresholds with common hysteresis and fixed AVDD thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active alarm flags clear after each conversion, while tripped flags remain set until `ALARM_REG` is read. Alarm status can be accessed through the pin, registers, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports four standard SPI modes, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation with internal or external clocks. It also supports daisy-chained devices configured identically, with an optimal frame of 32 × N clock edges for N devices. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. A falling CONVST/CS edge starts a data-transfer frame, and a rising edge ends the frame and initiates conversion. Frames of 32 clocks support valid reads and writes; shorter frames permit reads only, while longer frames use the final 32 shifted bits as the command.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output data, ranges, alarms, and thresholds. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device addresses, input ranges, alarm flags, and parity.

An eight-channel industrial input-module design combines the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to measure bipolar, unipolar voltage, and current inputs. It uses the input alarm with hysteresis for NTC-thermistor temperature monitoring. The device requires separate AVDD and DVDD supplies with 10 µF and 1 µF decoupling. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce power use, and recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital routing and places reference and supply capacitors close to their pins.

PPL shares rose $0.19 to $37.65 despite $29.88 million in net selling. Analysts have a consensus “Hold” rating and $38.94 target. Quarterly EPS of $0.52 beat expectations, while revenue of $1.73 billion and revenue growth declined year over year. PPL paid a $0.395 dividend, with a 4.24% yield and 66.11% payout ratio. Insiders sold 47,163 shares, while several institutional investors increased first-quarter holdings. PPL is a utility holding company serving electricity and natural gas customers in the U.K. and several U.S. states.

The passage examines Europe’s ageing population and the growing cost of tax-funded health and social care. It proposes a proactive approach focused on people aged 60–75, using digital wellness services to sustain physical, intellectual, social and emotional well-being before functional impairment becomes more prevalent at 75 and above. This group represents 18–23% of the EU population and was projected to number about 97 million by 2020.

The proposed intervention uses omnivore smartphone platforms, wearable devices and cloud services to collect routine data, summarize users’ progress and provide tailored guidance. Services should be co-designed with users through action design research, rapidly prototyped and adaptable rather than requiring users to conform to predetermined routines. A commercially viable ecosystem, advanced analytics and cloud infrastructure are considered necessary to sustain both the services and the resulting wellness routines. Finland’s BeWell research programme tests this approach using the Wellmo platform and Tieto cloud services.

Preliminary research included about 100 user workshops and an Åland Islands survey with 101 usable responses. About 73% of respondents used smartphones, and mobile apps received high ratings for usefulness, ease of learning and continued use. Respondents considered wellness issues important, especially intellectual stimulation, while generally reporting good physical health. Younger, working, more highly educated and higher-income respondents showed some more favourable attitudes toward mobile technology or wellness.

The findings provide preliminary support for young elderly as a viable user group and for designing services with, rather than merely for, them. However, the small regional sample limits generalizability, and the authors call for larger studies and field validation before drawing complete conclusions.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 26, 2018, reporting its first-quarter 2018 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release announcing the results and information about non-GAAP financial measures included in Amazon’s public disclosures. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Chicago players reflected on their success against Los Angeles, noting that they stayed with their approach and scored despite not varying much when opportunities arose. After Brent Seabrook’s overtime winner tied the Boston series, the team credited its strong regular season, depth, hard work, and collective five-man play. Patrick Kane and Seabrook emphasized speed, backchecking, puck movement, support for defensemen, and contributions from players such as Marcus Kruger and Dave Toews. They also praised the Blackhawks’ logo, colors, and history.

Kane said Boston may open up as the series continues, but Chicago needs stronger defense, improved shot blocking and lane control, and better penalty killing. The players said teammates’ familiarity makes line combinations less important and praised contributions from across the roster.

Bryan Bickell and Seabrook highlighted the importance of physical play against Boston’s large, physical defenseman, saying checks can create momentum, obstruct the goaltender’s view, and open ice. They described becoming more aggressive after the first three games. Kane noted that Boston scored five goals through short-handed situations, rebounds, point shots, and getting to the net.

Seabrook urged one forward to stop focusing on his positive contributions and instead keep scoring while maintaining confidence. He and Kane also said Chicago must improve in all zones and be prepared for closer, lower-scoring games.

FreeNAS 11, based on FreeBSD 11-STABLE, adds bhyve virtualization, AWS S3 compatibility, Slack and HipChat integration, selectable startup services, FreeBSD jails, and a beta Angular GUI. Docker support is deferred, and release-candidate testers reported few complaints.

The study examined the introduction, spread, and evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam during 2021 using whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic, phylogeographic, and phylodynamic analyses. Of 1,365 selected samples, 1,303 genomes were obtained, including 1,222 Delta and 74 Alpha sequences, with no recombinants detected. Delta’s AY.57 lineage accounted for 1,212 sequences.

Alpha was detected from January to May, with multiple introductions producing sporadic clusters that were contained by rapid contact tracing, testing, quarantine, and local restrictions. Delta was first detected in late April and became the only variant detected from June onward, accompanying an outbreak that caused 1,727,398 infections and 32,359 deaths from May through December.

AY.57 was estimated to have a most recent common ancestor on March 14, 2021. It was introduced into northeastern Vietnam and subsequently spread from northern and Red River Delta regions to the southeast, which later seeded infections northward and elsewhere. Frequent movement between localities was not observed, and localized clusters formed under strict travel and border controls.

Genetic diversity increased sharply from April to August during the nationwide outbreak, then remained relatively stable before declining slightly in late November. Overall evolution reflected weak purifying selection, although ORF1b, ORF3a, envelope, and ORF7a showed positive selection. The estimated evolutionary rate was 5.29 × 10⁻⁴ substitutions per site per year. Referral-hospital sampling and home management of mild or asymptomatic cases from July were identified as potential limitations. The findings emphasized the importance of genomic surveillance in informing pandemic responses.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. reduced its DeVry Education Group holding by 9.6% in the third quarter, selling 53,234 shares and retaining 499,104 shares worth $11.51 million. UBS, PNC, Retirement Systems of Alabama, and KBC Group increased their positions, while M&T Bank initiated a roughly $229,000 position. DeVry reported quarterly EPS of $0.39 versus $0.41 expected, revenue of $449.9 million versus $443.62 million expected, and 1.9% year-over-year revenue growth. Shares traded at $31.20. The company paid a $0.18 semiannual dividend, yielding 1.29%. Analysts had a consensus “Hold” rating and an average $26.11 target, with one sell, seven hold, and four buy ratings. Value Advisers International sold 3,272 shares at an average $27.92, and insiders own 5.61%. DeVry is a global education-services provider with three segments: Medical and Healthcare; International and Professional Education; and Business, Technology and Management.

This preprint presents a PROSPERO-registered systematic review of human evidence on marijuana or endocannabinoid use and microbiome changes. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through July 20, 2022, with risk of bias assessed using NOS and ROBINS-I. Of 4,022 records identified, nine studies were included: six cohorts, one case-control study, and two clinical trials involving 2,526 participants from four countries between 1983 and 2021. Most participants were women, and ages ranged from 17 to 101.

Qualitative findings indicated associations between cannabis use and microbial changes in people with HIV, inflammation, obesity, cognitive impairment, and oral conditions. In HIV cohorts, marijuana use correlated with changes in bacterial taxa, while users had a higher prevalence of bacterial vaginosis and gonorrhea. Exercise-related increases in endocannabinoids were associated with reduced inflammatory cytokines and changes in short-chain-fatty-acid-producing bacteria. In an obesity trial, oleoylethanolamide supplementation decreased energy and macronutrient intake and increased Akkermansia muciniphila. Marijuana users showed altered oral microbiota, dietary patterns, mitochondrial function, and lower Prevotella:Bacteroides ratios, but causation was not established. Reported adverse effects included coughing, wheezing, drowsiness, night sweats, and systemic aspergillosis; these resolved after smoking cessation in the cited study. Limited and heterogeneous evidence prevented meta-analysis, and further research was recommended.

Chinese textile businesses are increasingly using North Korean factories to reduce labor costs, with garments often labeled “Made in China” and exported globally. Agents in Dandong broker orders between Chinese suppliers and buyers worldwide. Textiles were North Korea’s second-largest export in 2016, worth $752 million, while total exports reached $2.82 billion. U.N. sanctions do not ban textile exports, although newer measures prohibit coal exports.

China supplies North Korean factories with fabrics and other raw materials, and its exports to North Korea rose nearly 30% to $1.67 billion. Manufacturers can reportedly save up to 75% by producing in North Korea, where factories are state-owned and reportedly operating at capacity. Thousands of North Korean workers also work in Chinese factories for about half the wages of Chinese workers; much of their earnings is remitted to the North Korean government, which the U.N. says helps fund its nuclear and missile programs. New sanctions bar countries from increasing North Korean overseas employment, while Chinese employers describe the workers as requiring managed housing, instruction and specialized support staff.

Ostersunds earned an Europa League last-32 draw against Arsenal, their first European meeting with a Swedish side since 1999–2000. Champions League dropouts Borussia Dortmund, Atlético Madrid and Napoli face Atalanta, Zenit and RB Leipzig respectively.

Glenner Town Square is an 8,500-square-foot Alzheimer’s and dementia daycare in Chula Vista designed to evoke long-term memories through a 1950s-style downtown. The 13-storefront village includes a cinema, diner, library, boutique, auto shop with a 1959 Ford T-Bird, pet store, hospital and nursery. It opened in April 2018 at 2678 Main St.; reservations, fees and schedules are available at glenner.org.

The passage also lists licensed San Diego County adult day programs for cognitively impaired adults: Clairemont Villa Adult Day Health Center; College Avenue Older Adult Center at Congregation Beth Jacob; George G. Glenner Adult Day Care Center in Hillcrest and Encinitas; Hope Adult Day Health Care Center in Mira Mesa; Loving Care Adult Day Health Care Center in San Diego; Neighborhood House Association in Logan Heights; St. Paul Senior Day Program in Bankers Hill; AltaGolden Adult Day Care Memory Program in Rancho Bernardo; Americare Adult Day Health Care in San Marcos; and Fallbrook Adult Day Care Center. Services include meals, transportation, nursing, medication management, therapies, exercise, classes, social activities, caregiver support groups and dementia-specific programming. Addresses, hours, fees, phone numbers and websites are provided.

A hockey team is making its third consecutive Finals appearance, seeking the championship after earlier disappointments. The player praises the team’s hard work, dedicated fans, and strong season, and expects a tight series against the experienced Philadelphia Flyers.

Ben Rice was born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, and attended Noble and Greenough School in Dedham after playing hockey in childhood. A Yankees fan who idolized Derek Jeter, Rice wrote “Yankees Rule” on Fenway Park’s Pesky Pole. He played college baseball at Dartmouth, where the COVID-19 pandemic limited him to 110 career plate appearances before the Yankees drafted him in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft. After a brief 2024 debut, he became a regular in 2025, hitting 26 home runs in 138 games while playing first base, catcher, and designated hitter. He also homered in Game 2 of the 2025 Wild Card Series against Boston.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for a third consecutive quarter to 1%–1.25%, citing strong job growth and moderate economic expansion despite weaker inflation. It lowered this year’s inflation forecast to 1.6%, retained 2% for next year, and said unemployment could fall below 4%.

The speaker credits bipartisan cooperation with reversing declining national confidence and reports an economic recovery: inflation fell from 12.4 to 3.2 percent, interest rates declined, taxes were reduced and indexed, purchasing power and after-tax income increased, and four million jobs were created in 1983. He acknowledges continued unemployment and calls for renewed opportunity.

He outlines four goals. First, sustained economic growth requires limiting government growth, reducing deficits and regulation, controlling spending, simplifying the tax code, and allowing a line-item veto and balanced federal budget. He proposes a bipartisan $100 billion deficit-reduction plan over three years and rejects placing additional financial burdens on families.

Second, developing America’s “next frontier” means advancing space exploration. He orders NASA to develop a permanently manned station within a decade, encourages private investment and international participation, and calls for greater environmental protection, including addressing hazardous waste, acid rain, Chesapeake Bay pollution, and offshore resource development.

Third, he emphasizes education, family, faith, work, freedom, and peace. His proposals include stronger educational standards, discipline, merit-based rewards, tuition tax credits, parental authority, school prayer, protection of unborn children, tougher action against crime and family violence, fair housing and women’s rights, and enterprise zones for high-unemployment areas.

Fourth, he advocates a meaningful peace through stronger Soviet relations, nuclear arms reductions, allied cooperation, peacekeeping efforts, anti-terrorism measures, and freer trade, while appealing to Soviet citizens to prevent nuclear war.

The speech concludes by praising military personnel, volunteers, and others who serve others, and expresses confidence that America’s democratic and economic renewal will continue.

The study used a compartmental model and Poisson-based simulations to assess community-wide screening and isolation in a semi-isolated population when vaccines and medicines are unavailable. The model incorporated disease transmission, recovery or death, external infection influx, screening efficiency, and delays between infection and isolation. Theoretical analysis showed that longer isolation delays make control difficult, while increasing screening efficiency has only a weak effect on the allowable delay.

Simulations indicated that daily screening with 90% efficiency controlled an infection with a basic reproduction number (R₀) of 3 and remained effective at R₀ = 6, although it failed at R₀ = 8, where additional measures such as social distancing and mask use were needed. For R₀ = 3, screening every three days controlled transmission; weekly screening performed substantially worse, particularly at 70% efficiency, and screening every two weeks failed at both tested efficiencies. Infection levels increased with external influx, demonstrating the need for strict border control.

The discussion identifies PCR-based testing as a promising mass-screening method, while noting the variable performance and disease-specific limitations of fever screening. Overall, the results suggest that regular, periodic screening can control serious disease transmission in semi-isolated communities without medication or vaccination, provided screening is sufficiently frequent and border influx is limited. Practical implementation may still face operational costs and resident psychological effects.

Agent Don Yee says Brady intends to return in 2018 and beyond, potentially into his mid-40s, though he has not committed to the upcoming season. Brady has stayed fit and focused, while owner Robert Kraft says his contract is not an issue and the team is not seeking a new deal.

MultiChoice CEO Calvo Mawela said Netflix’s popularity in South Africa had contributed to falling DStv Premium subscribers and average revenue per customer. DStv’s total subscribers rose to 13.476 million, while Premium declined by 41,000. MultiChoice is moving toward a streaming-only package and appealed to ICASA to avoid overregulation, warning that restrictions could cost South African jobs.

At Joppatowne High School’s 45th commencement, more than 130 of 138 graduates received diplomas at APG Federal Credit Union Arena. About 95 percent planned to enter college, technical school, the military or law enforcement.

Graduate Amya Hill, whose family wore purple shirts bearing her image, planned to study nursing at Albany State University in Georgia. After academic struggles in her first two years, she improved and encouraged students to keep pushing. Fellow graduate Zachary Wagmun planned to enter an electrician’s apprenticeship at Harford Community College.

Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun urged students to pursue their goals, while class president Breea Stevenson offered three lessons: step beyond one’s comfort zone, separate from negative influences, and focus on the present while moving forward toward a better future. Stevenson said these lessons were especially important because of deadly mass shootings.

State Sen. Robert Cassilly also asked graduates to consider the sacrifices of Baltimore County police officer Amy Caprio and Maryland National Guard Sgt. Eddison “Eddie” A. Hermond, who died while serving or rescuing others.

The Tampa team plans to stay after the game before traveling Sunday to maximize rest and recovery from a long flight. The coach says Calgary faces the pressure and is expected to win, while Tampa’s focus is simply to extend the series. He emphasizes hockey battles, the importance of big plays at key moments, and giving an unnamed Calgary star credit for his contributions. The team reportedly feels confident about its chances. He also discusses the mental strain of approaching an elimination game at home, noting that players can become distracted by expectations and what winning the Cup might bring, which may have affected Tampa’s performance the previous night.

CoreWeave rebounded on AI optimism and OpenAI ($22.4B) and Meta ($14.2B) deals, diversifying its customer base, but Microsoft remains a revenue-concentration risk. Aggressive, debt-funded capex and a high forward revenue multiple raise sustainability concerns; fully priced-in optimism and elevated risks may lead to a pullback.

Exact diagonalization of a continuum model for half-filled second moiré bands in approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe₂ reveals an intermediate intervalley superconducting phase between a ferromagnetic Chern insulator and a non-Abelian fractional quantum spin Hall insulator. The phase diagram is controlled by the intervalley screening length \(d\): weak screening favors ferromagnetism and valley polarization, while strong screening decouples the valleys and permits paired Pfaffian states.
