The intermediate phase has a unique, paramagnetic ground state and is identified as superconducting by intervalley entanglement, enhanced pair binding, a dominant eigenvalue in the pair-density matrix, and finite superfluid stiffness. Its pairing is time-reversal symmetric, nodal extended \(s\)-wave between opposite-spin holes at opposite momenta.

The superconducting and fractional spin Hall states undergo a continuous transition near \(d/a_M\approx0.33\), with symmetry and topology changing together. A Chern–Simons field theory based on two coupled Pfaffian states describes the transition through condensation of a shared matter field. Replacing the moiré bands with idealized uniform first Landau levels removes the intermediate phase, whereas non-uniform quantum geometry reproduces its key features, indicating that realistic band geometry is important. Hartree–Fock calculations account for interactions involving higher moiré bands, while exact diagonalization is performed for finite system sizes. The authors suggest that screening could be tuned through gating or substrate engineering, potentially making the phase experimentally accessible.

A letter from abruptly fired Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Ben’Ary alleged that Justice Department leadership prioritized punishing perceived presidential enemies over protecting public safety and national security. Ben’Ary said a false social media post led to his firing while he was prosecuting the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing, which killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. He also claimed he participated in internal resistance to the indictment of former FBI Director James Comey.

OTC markets are decentralized electronic marketplaces where parties trade directly through dealer and market-maker networks rather than a central exchange. U.S. networks are operated by entities such as OTC Markets Group and regulated by FINRA. OTC markets support stocks, bonds, derivatives, ETFs, commodities, currencies, and foreign-company ADRs. They provide companies that cannot meet exchange-listing requirements with access to capital and allow flexible, customized contracts, including derivatives for hedging.

The market offers privacy and less burdensome reporting requirements than major exchanges, but also less transparency, weaker liquidity, counterparty and credit risk, manipulation, speculation, and fraud. OTC-listed companies often disclose less information than exchange-listed companies, making valuation harder. Penny stocks are particularly associated with volatility, “pump-and-dump” schemes, and severe losses. The passage cites a 2001–2010 study of 10,000 OTC stocks showing an average return of negative 27% and a median return of negative 37%, and states that more than 90% of penny stocks fail.

Crypto can be traded on exchanges with public order books or over the counter through large off-market desks and peer-to-peer platforms. The passage concludes that OTC stocks are generally unsuitable for long-term investment and that short-term or day trading is also unattractive because of thin trading, wider bid-ask spreads, slippage, and broker restrictions. It advises thorough research and limiting investments to amounts that can be lost.

OptumCare offers a 12-week “Brainsaver” course combining physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive activities, education, socialization and brain-healthy foods. The holistic program aims to support brain health and decrease chances of Alzheimer’s disease. Classes serve adults from their mid-50s to late 80s at locations in Deer Valley, Goodyear and Chandler.

A federal shutdown appeared more likely after President Donald Trump met with top congressional leaders at the White House. Vice President JD Vance blamed Democrats, while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said the parties had “very large differences,” though he believed Trump heard Democratic objections “for the first time.” Republicans want a stopgap funding bill through late November; Democrats want it to include key measures, particularly extended enhanced Obamacare tax credits. Both sides blamed each other. Earlier competing short-term bills failed in the Senate, where 60 votes are required.

Fremont mother of four Moina Shaiq launched a “Meet a Muslim” program after friends hesitated to ask about her religion. Drawing about 100 people initially, she has since spoken at libraries, restaurants, coffee shops, churches, clubs and homes, discussing Muslim practices, women’s rights, Sunni-Shia differences and the experience of being an American Muslim. Similar post-9/11 outreach programs have appeared at libraries and college campuses as anti-Muslim incidents and rhetoric have increased. Shaiq’s talks have also prompted threats. Advocates view local dialogue as a way to counter Islamophobia and xenophobia, while some activists argue that policy change is more effective than changing bigots’ minds. Shaiq says her goal is to educate Americans, share compassion and peace, and emphasize that Muslims are human.

This continuation disclosure describes methods and devices for transmitting and receiving sounding reference signals (SRS) in a wireless communication system, particularly in new radio systems. It proposes configuring or indicating a guard period for antenna switching when SRS is adjacent to PUSCH or PUCCH transmission.

A base station may signal guard-period information through higher-layer, MAC, or DCI signaling. The information can include the guard period’s start position, number of symbols, presence, and placement relative to SRS resources and adjacent uplink channels. The number of guard-period symbols may depend on subcarrier spacing, and configuration may vary by SRS resource set or uplink bandwidth part. The guard period may be assigned the same priority as SRS when it collides with a specific uplink channel.

The disclosure further addresses beam and antenna-port relationships using SRS resource indicators and transmit precoder matrix indicators. If no guard period is configured, the UE may determine and report one, rate-match or puncture PUSCH, shift SRS or PUSCH symbols, or provide related feedback.

Collision-handling options include grouping guard-period symbols with SRS resources, dropping the guard period, PUCCH, SRS resources, or entire SRS resource sets, puncturing or rate-matching colliding symbols, shifting transmissions to later symbols or slots, and applying priority rules between periodic, semi-persistent, and aperiodic SRS resource sets. These mechanisms are intended to reduce uplink distortion and performance degradation caused by antenna-switching collisions.

Turing Tensor Cores accelerate deep-learning matrix operations and add INT8/INT4 inference modes. They power DLSS, which uses neural networks to combine details across frames with fewer samples than TAA.

Tesla Motors, Inc. reported that on January 3, 2016, it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1 and furnished under Form 8-K Items 2.02 and 7.01. The information was not deemed “filed” for Section 18 purposes or incorporated by reference unless expressly cited. General Counsel Todd A. Maron signed the report on January 4, 2016.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, was sentenced in absentia to 13 years for wounding with intent after admitting to shaking his four-month-old son twice. He absconded before sentencing, was arrested eight days later and received a further 10 days’ imprisonment for breaching bail. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, suffered catastrophic brain injuries and other serious harm requiring lifelong medication, nursing care and support.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defense with no safety over the top. Defensive backs and linebackers cover eligible receivers without safety help, while additional defenders stunt or blitz, often creating a six-player rush. It pressures the quarterback while maintaining coverage of all eligible receivers.

Its strengths include simple, adjustable assignments, reliable coverage against motion, and extra defenders in the box to help against runs and run-pass options. Coverage defenders can focus on their assignments rather than reading run or pass, while quarterback pressure limits short, deep, and screen opportunities. Cover 0 can also be disguised pre-snap as Cover 4.

The scheme is high-risk because coverage defenders receive no help. A beaten receiver can produce a large gain, while draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays can exploit the lack of middle or deep help. The post route and middle of the field remain open; Raiders owner Al Davis prohibited the coverage for this reason.

In a common version, cornerbacks cover outside receivers, safeties cover the tight end and slot receiver, and linebackers cover the running back or blitz from the box. Variations include Cover 0 “Rat,” which rushes five and uses a floating linebacker against crossing routes and quarterback runs, and dropping a hybrid defensive lineman into coverage against a running back.

Astronomers report that Oumuamua, the first confirmed interstellar object detected in our solar system, is likely an asteroid ejected from a binary star system during planet formation. The red, cigar-shaped object is moving away from Earth and the Sun at over 16 miles per second. Researchers also found it tumbling, possibly after a collision, and suggest such systems may produce most interstellar objects.

The coach praised Chicago’s culture of commitment, consistency, accountability, open communication and making teammates better, crediting the leadership of top players. He described healthy competition and mutual support between goaltenders Corey Crawford and Scott Darling, highlighting Darling’s strong relief performance and Crawford’s excellence throughout the year. Chicago adjusted forward combinations, and he encouraged players such as Kaner to shoot more rather than wait for the perfect play, while stressing that trust should be earned through sound defensive work, puck management and positional awareness. He also noted the value of reliable performances in high-pressure situations and an emerging player’s creativity, patience and play recognition. As the playoffs deepened, he said the team needed to play faster, accept narrow margins and find ways to win against difficult defensive matchups.

The article examines holistic education in Indian higher education, arguing that success requires integrating intellectual, emotional, physical, social, aesthetic, and spiritual development rather than prioritizing material achievement alone. It relates holistic education’s Latin roots—*educere* (“to draw out”) and *educare* (“to train or mold”)—to the philosophies of Tagore, Osho, Swami Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo, all of whom integrated material and spiritual development. Contemporary initiatives, including India’s National Education Policy 2020, UN Sustainable Development Goal 4.7, and the ISEE framework, similarly emphasize learner-centered, human-centered, and multidimensional education.

The study uses a comprehensive literature review followed by a PRISMA-guided systematic review of Scopus and Semantic Scholar. It screened 472 English-language original articles published before 2021 and retained eight for thematic analysis in MAXQDA. Open coding, double coding by two researchers, and qualitative comparative analysis were used to validate dimensions of holistic education.

International examples show holistic principles embedded in policies and reforms in North America, Europe, Singapore, Taiwan, and New Zealand, while also emphasizing contextual and culturally relevant implementation. Social-emotional learning connects academic goals with self-awareness, emotional regulation, empathy, relationship-building, and responsible decision-making. Although several globally used frameworks cover cognitive, emotional, social, and values domains consistently, identity and perspectives remain underrepresented. The culturally grounded LIBRE/EMC² framework addresses this gap through whole-brain learning and four dimensions: empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry.

The systematic review confirmed consistent support for all four dimensions. Empathy included cultural awareness, communication, relationship-building, collaboration, and global citizenship. Mindfulness encompassed self-awareness, emotional regulation, resilience, spiritual awareness, self-knowledge, and inner purpose. Compassion involved care, respect, social responsibility, stewardship, community values, and integrity. Critical inquiry included analytical thinking, problem-solving, information literacy, interdisciplinary synthesis, reflective practice, and self-directed learning. Foundational themes also emphasized whole-person development, holistic pedagogy, balanced and inclusive learning environments, lifelong learning, global competence, clear institutional goals, and the need for standardized holistic-assessment instruments.

The discussion links these dimensions to ancient Indian educational philosophies and to contemporary policies such as NEP 2020 and SDG 4.7. It positions mindfulness and compassion as reflecting the drawing out of inner capacities, while empathy and critical inquiry reflect the shaping of socially directed capacities. Classroom-level assessment is presented as a feedback mechanism that can inform institutional planning, curriculum design, and policy reform.

The study concludes that the review supports empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry as core holistic-education dimensions in the Indian higher-education context and provides a foundation for culturally grounded assessment tools and standardized curricula. Limitations include reliance on two databases and exclusion of the *Holistic Education Review* journal; future research should broaden source coverage, develop culturally sensitive measurement instruments, and examine implementation across diverse educational settings.
Angel Commodities said soybean May futures rose weekly as supplies diminished and soy meal exports supported crushing demand; April arrivals fell to 97,040 tonnes from 164,286 tonnes in March.

A UMD study of 1,099 college students found that persistent high-caffeinated energy drink consumption was associated with greater likelihood of cocaine use, nonmedical prescription stimulant use, and alcohol use disorder risk at age 25. Intermediate consumption also increased stimulant-use risk, while declining consumption and non-use showed no elevated risk.

Consumer advocates reported intermittent “no plans available” errors on HealthCare.gov during final ACA enrollment days. The message incorrectly appeared for some consumers seeking financial assistance, even though every county had an insurer offering 2018 plans. The administration said the issue was resolved, though advocates reported continued problems.

Enrollment for subsidized coverage through HealthCare.gov in 39 states ends Dec. 15 at midnight Pacific time, or 3 a.m. Saturday on the East Coast. Heavy traffic and long call-center waits were expected. Hurricane-affected residents could request extensions until Dec. 31, while state-run marketplaces generally had later deadlines, including Jan. 31 in California and New York. Marketplace enrollment was estimated at 9 million to 10 million people. Increased subsidies may make some plans cheaper, including bronze plans with no monthly premium. It remained unclear whether consumers with unfinished applications would receive grace-period extensions.

President Woodrow Wilson proclaimed on April 6, 1917, that a state of war existed between the United States and the Imperial German Government. He directed government officers to uphold the war effort and urged citizens to remain loyal and support the constitutional authorities.

The proclamation defined “alien enemies” as German males aged fourteen or older within the United States who had not been naturalized. They were required to preserve the peace, obey U.S. laws, and refrain from hostility or assistance to U.S. enemies. Law-abiding alien enemies were to remain undisturbed in peaceful occupations, subject to necessary safety restrictions, while violators faced restraint, security, removal, or deportation.

Regulations prohibited alien enemies from possessing weapons, aircraft, wireless or signaling devices, and coded documents; approaching military installations; publishing threats; committing hostile acts; entering prohibited areas; or entering or leaving the country without authorization. They could be required to register and were subject to summary arrest and confinement when reasonably suspected of aiding the enemy, endangering public safety, or violating the regulations or criminal law. The rules applied throughout U.S. jurisdiction, including its land and insular waters.

The Nationals are weighing A.J. Cole, Erick Fedde and minor-league signee Jeremy Hellickson for their fifth rotation spot, with the decision potentially extending beyond opening day. Hellickson, 30, received a contract that would pay $2 million if added to the 40-man roster, with up to $4 million in performance bonuses and a late opt-out. Washington may leave him in minor-league camp after Friday’s start to build arm strength, though general manager Mike Rizzo said the rotation already has depth. Cole struck out six in four innings in his latest outing and, if he does not start, is expected to join the bullpen; Fedde has options and is likely headed to the minors. Max Scherzer was named opening-day starter, followed by Stephen Strasburg, Gio Gonzalez and Tanner Roark. Hellickson, the 2011 AL Rookie of the Year, went 8-11 last season and struggled after being traded to Baltimore, but Washington cited delivery adjustments he has worked on. Trea Turner left camp to treat an ingrown toenail and could return Tuesday.

Tesla announced lower-priced Standard versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, priced at $36,990 and $39,990, respectively. The Model Y Standard has an estimated 321-mile range but omits features including Autosteer, an LED lightbar, adaptive high beams, and FM/AM radio. Buyers save $5,500 with the Model 3 Standard and $5,000 with the Model Y Standard versus their Premium rear-wheel-drive counterparts. Estimated availability is November–December for the Model Y and December–January for the Model 3. New York rebates could reduce prices to $34,990 and $37,990 for eligible buyers. Tesla shares fell 4.45% after the announcement, which followed expiration of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit.

John Ortiz appealed his conviction of simple assault after being charged with assault with a deadly weapon. Ortiz followed his wife to San Francisco’s Ferry Building, saw her with Albert Donaso, and returned home with police assistance. Finding the door locked, he broke a bedroom window and entered, where he and Donaso struggled and Donaso was repeatedly cut with a pocketknife.

The court held that the district attorney could cross-examine Ortiz by having him demonstrate how he drew and opened the knife, because Ortiz claimed he cut Donaso in self-defense after Donaso approached him with a knife. The court also treated Ortiz’s alleged threatening letters as a collateral issue because the jury’s question was whether the cutting occurred in self-defense. Exclusion of related testimony did not warrant reversal. The judgment was affirmed.

This passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture, its neural shading technologies, and the associated GeForce RTX 50 series product specifications.

**Ray tracing and DLSS:** Ray Reconstruction (RR) uses AI to generate additional pixels in ray-traced scenes, replacing hand-tuned denoisers with a supercomputer-trained network that produces higher-quality pixels between sampled rays. A transformer model for RR yields larger quality gains, especially in scenes with challenging lighting, and significantly reduces typical denoiser artifacts. DLAA applies DLSS super-resolution technology at native resolution for higher image quality, increased temporal stability, and detail in motion.

**Neural shaders:** Blackwell was designed with neural shaders as the future predominant shader technology, requiring many architectural changes for performance and efficiency. The text traces shader evolution from the fixed-function pipeline through programmable vertex, pixel, geometry, tessellation, compute, mesh, and primitive shaders to DirectX ray tracing, and onward to Blackwell's unified AI/traditional shaders. Neural shaders train AI models to approximate what shader code would compute. NVIDIA's new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, developed with Microsoft and paired with Slang's differentiable shading features, exposes Tensor Cores to any shader type, enabling neural texture compression (up to seven-to-one VRAM compression over block-compressed formats), RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

**Neural technologies:** RTX Neural Materials replaces a material's mathematical model with a neural approximation, enabling film-quality assets at game frame rates. Neural Texture Compression compresses and decompresses textures more efficiently, with the demo using 333 MB versus 1,110 MB for standard materials (over 3x savings); Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré and runs fast due to Blackwell's 2x point-sampled filtering rate improvements. Neural Radiance Cache trains tiny neural networks on live game data, inferring lighting for many bounces from path-traced rays after one bounce to improve performance and indirect lighting quality. RTX Skin brings film subsurface scattering techniques to real-time path tracing. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model, trained from thousands of offline images and TensorRT optimized, to infer natural-looking faces from a rasterized face plus 3D pose data.

**Specifications:** GB202 (flagship, RTX 5090) has 92.2 billion transistors, 12 GPCs, 96 TPCs, 192 SMs, a 512-bit interface, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, 768 Texture Units, 192 ROPS, and 131,072 KB L2 cache. The court held that appeals from a justice of the peace to a district court are trials de novo in the district court as a court of original jurisdiction, not proceedings to correct errors in the justice’s judgment. The transcript serves only to establish that the case originated in the justice’s court, a judgment was rendered, and a proper appeal was taken; apparent transcript errors do not justify dismissal. Parties may file accounts and assert set-offs as in an original action.

In Archibeque’s suit for damages caused by Miera’s cattle, the district court properly overruled a motion to dismiss and permitted Archibeque to file an account claiming forty almudes of wheat. The jury found for Miera and denied Archibeque’s motion for a new trial. Because conflicting testimony left doubt whether the damage was caused by Miera’s cattle, Archibeque’s cattle, or other animals, the issue belonged to the jury. As no clear preponderance of evidence contradicted the verdict, the judgment was affirmed.

The passage lists records from January 1–March 8, 1945, covering U.S. consultations with the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, China, and France on unresolved Dumbarton Oaks issues and Yalta decisions, submissions concerning the proposals, and conference invitations to 39 United Nations governments. It reproduces a December 29 circular noting that nine American governments submitted memoranda on Dumbarton Oaks proposals and that preparations for a Conference of American Republics would help the republics participate more effectively in the general international-organization conference and cooperate in building an enduring international peace structure.
Both teams struggled early, affecting special teams, while the crowd was a strong ally. The speaker conceded games were given away and hoped two home games would improve the situation.

The passage outlines the Base Cross basketball offense, emphasizing size mismatches, precise baseline-screen execution, strong posting, ball reversal, coordination, and opponent scouting. In the standard action, O1 enters O3 and makes a give-and-go cut; if the cut is not open, O1 sets a baseline screen for O5. O5 then posts or shoots, while O1 pops to the free-throw line against a switch or moves to the weakside wing off a down screen. Variations include dribble-clear, UCLA high-post rub, and Hawk entries, differing mainly in who sets the baseline screen.

Defensive reads include trailing defenders, low or high post deployment, switches, inside or outside mismatches, anticipated show-and-recover, and fronting the post. Counteractions include back cuts, going over or under screens, screen-and-pop mismatches, slipping to the basket, post lob passes, and ball reversal. Effective posting requires basic post moves, awareness of defensive positioning, solo cuts, two-person action, and post splits; cutters clear out when they do not receive the ball.

When no shot is available, the offense reverses to O2 and uses weakside down, mid, or side screens to find O3, O4 rolling, or additional screening action. If the reversal is denied, O2 back cuts and O3 replaces him. Teaching recommendations include mastering fundamentals, whole-part-whole drills, two-player entries, 3-on-3 combinations, scrimmages, and individual skill work. Game strategy includes scouting or observing opponents, anticipating defensive responses, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. Teams should also understand how to defend the Base Cross offense.

The passage criticizes the Carter administration for helping replace moderate, U.S.-friendly autocrats in Iran and Nicaragua with revolutionary leaders whose intolerance and rejection of constitutional government suggested worsening conditions. It argues that Washington lacked a realistic policy for responding to Soviet-backed challenges to nondemocratic governments and that administration officials favored leftist movements largely because of prevailing intellectual fashion, despite the risks of reactionary theocracies, Soviet client states, or extremist fanatics.

Kirkpatrick distinguishes traditional autocracies from revolutionary ones. Traditional rulers generally preserve established social hierarchies and are less repressive, more susceptible to liberalization, and more compatible with U.S. interests. Revolutionary autocracies tend to create brutality, poverty, and social disorder. Vietnam and Cambodia are cited as evidence, along with comparisons of China and Taiwan and North and South Korea. The passage concludes that Carter’s foreign policy failed because of unrealistic assumptions about autocracy, not because of a lack of good intentions.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts resigned effective immediately after being detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The Guyana-born superintendent allegedly evaded arrest; ICE said agents found a handgun, hunting knife and $3,000 in cash in his vehicle. ICE also said he entered the country on a student visa and received a final removal order in May 2024.

Roberts’ attorney said a prior letter indicated his immigration case had closed successfully. The attorney is seeking to reopen the case and has requested a stay in federal immigration court in Omaha. Roberts remains detained at Woodbury County Jail in Sioux City.

His Iowa teaching license was revoked, and the school board moved to end his employment contract. His resignation followed scrutiny of his hiring process: DMPS said Roberts completed required I-9 verification, while the background-check firm Baker-Eubanks said it does not verify legal authorization to work. U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn said the Justice Department confirmed Roberts’ final removal order.

The study used ensemble decision-tree machine-learning models to test whether sleep quality predicts individual depressive symptom severity (DSS) and whether anxiety and brain measures contribute. Models were trained in HCP-Young (1,101 adults aged 22–35) using nested 10-fold cross-validation, then validated in HCP-Aging (378 participants) and eNKI (334 participants), including longitudinal data from 66 eNKI participants.

Sleep quality predicted DSS in HCP-Young (r=0.43, R²=0.18), and adding anxiety substantially improved prediction (r=0.67, R²=0.45). Models generalized to HCP-Aging (r=0.57 for sleep; 0.72 for sleep plus anxiety) and eNKI (r=0.50 and 0.66). Baseline sleep quality and anxiety also predicted later DSS longitudinally (r=0.61 and 0.66). Findings remained robust after excluding participants with a lifetime depression history and when PSQI component scores replaced individual items. Reverse prediction of sleep quality from DSS was weaker. Daytime dysfunction, sleep disturbance, and subjective sleep quality were the most important sleep predictors.

Anxiety alone predicted DSS and mediated 52.6% of the covariance between sleep quality and DSS. Gray-matter volume and resting-state brain-function measures did not improve prediction or mediate the association. Longitudinal prediction was strong among participants who did not receive neurofeedback between assessments but not among those who did.

The authors concluded that sleep quality robustly predicts depressive symptoms across three cohorts, with anxiety strengthening the prediction, whereas measured brain structure and function did not contribute substantially. The predominantly cross-sectional design and small longitudinal sample limit causal conclusions.

The Investing.com outlook describes a sharp risk-off turn driven by weaker employment data, policy uncertainty, fading technology momentum and profit-taking. Major indexes broke down from all-time highs in confirmed bearish-engulfing patterns, falling 2.2%–4.2% during the reviewed week. Volume and market breadth weakened, nearly every sector except utilities declined, and regional banks and transports broke down sharply. Internals turned decisively negative and moderately oversold, while the risk gauge moved fully risk-off, with strength in utilities and Treasuries.

Economic indicators were mixed. GDP grew 3%, above the 2.5% expectation, although tariff-related import volatility distorted the data and personal spending was soft. Nonfarm payrolls rose only 73,000 versus expectations of 100,000, with the prior two months revised sharply downward—the largest revision since 1979 except during the pandemic. Unemployment edged up to 4.2%, while the labor force contracted 0.5% over three months, reducing the effect of slower job creation.

The Federal Reserve’s two dissenting votes were its first since the 1990s. Chair Powell emphasized patience and dependence on incoming data amid tariff-related inflation risks and changes to the labor force. By week’s end, markets priced more than a 75% chance of a September rate cut and three cuts by January, although the Fed remained concerned about inflation.

Earnings remained strong: 82% of reporting companies exceeded EPS estimates, while 79% of S&P 500 companies exceeded revenue estimates. Upward earnings revisions reached a 43-month high globally and a 24-month high in the U.S. Expectations point to improving growth into 2026, but investors sold into favorable earnings and major technology stocks, suggesting profit-taking and limited buying interest.

Political developments included President Trump’s removal of the labor-statistics commissioner, new tariff announcements, military moves toward Russia and Federal Reserve Governor Adriana Kugler’s resignation, potentially giving Trump another opportunity to influence the Fed. Seasonality remained modestly positive for August except for small caps, while value weakened, growth stayed in a bull phase, emerging markets outperformed developed foreign markets, and commodities remained under pressure. The analysis favors tactical positioning and downside-risk management while saying the correction may be healthy and that its durability remains uncertain.
Police arrested a suspect after a two-hour Kansas-Missouri pursuit. Officers found drugs and loaded weapons in his vehicle and hospitalized him following alleged methamphetamine ingestion.

The Patient Charter, also known as the NHS Constitution, combines patients’ legal rights, NHS commitments beyond legal requirements, and patient responsibilities. It covers free-at-the-point-of-use care with some exceptions, equal access, waiting-time standards, safe professional treatment, privacy, consent, treatment choices, NICE-recommended medicines, routine vaccination, and transparent disclosure when care goes wrong. Patients can complain, seek Ombudsman review or judicial review, and claim compensation for harm caused by negligence. The NHS must also plan services around community needs and continually improve care. Patients are expected to use services fairly, respect staff and others, follow treatment plans or discuss difficulties, participate in vaccination and screening, and maintain their health where possible. Overall, the Charter presents the NHS as a partnership based on trust, shared responsibility, patient empowerment, and accountability.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended January 28, 2018. The Delaware corporation is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. It reported 605 million shares outstanding as of February 26, 2018, while non-affiliate holdings of voting stock had an aggregate market value of approximately $94.31 billion as of July 28, 2017. NVIDIA was identified as a large accelerated filer.

The company states that it invented the graphics processing unit (GPU) and expanded its focus to artificial intelligence, virtual reality and high-performance computing. Its unified GPU and CUDA architecture supports four principal markets: gaming, professional visualization, datacenter and automotive. Its two reportable segments are GPU and Tegra Processor. GPU products include GeForce, GeForce NOW, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, DGX and cryptocurrency-focused GPUs. Tegra-based offerings include DRIVE, SHIELD and Jetson TX 2.

In gaming, NVIDIA provides GPUs, cloud gaming, gaming devices, development tools, VRWorks and GeForce Experience. Its professional visualization products include Quadro and the DesignWorks and Holodeck software and VR environments. Its datacenter platform combines GPUs, CUDA, libraries such as cuDNN and TensorRT, NVLink, DGX systems and NVIDIA GPU Cloud for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. The company reports that GPUs can accelerate parallel applications by 10–75 times versus CPUs and that it works with major cloud providers, server manufacturers and thousands of organizations using AI. Under the DRIVE brand, NVIDIA provides hardware and software for autonomous driving and works with more than 320 automakers, suppliers, research organizations and startups.

NVIDIA’s strategies include advancing its GPU computing platform, extending its leadership in AI and visual computing, advancing autonomous vehicles, and leveraging intellectual property through licensing and development agreements. It reports more than 700,000 CUDA developers worldwide, partnerships with universities and more than 2,000 startups through Inception, and more than $15 billion invested in research and development since its inception.

The company uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries, assembly and testing subcontractors, contract manufacturers and component suppliers. It generally maintains substantial semiconductor inventory and focuses on forecasting demand platform by platform. Consumer products have typically generated stronger revenue in the second half of the fiscal year, although it does not assure that this pattern will continue. As of January 28, 2018, NVIDIA had 11,528 employees, including 8,191 in research and development. Research and development expense was $1.80 billion in fiscal 2018, $1.46 billion in fiscal 2017 and $1.33 billion in fiscal 2016.

The filing identifies intense competition based on factors such as performance, product breadth, customer and partner access, software support, standards, manufacturing, pricing and system costs. Named competitors include AMD, ARM, Imagination Technologies, Intel, Xilinx, Ambarella, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Renesas, Samsung and Texas Instruments. NVIDIA protects intellectual property through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, licensing arrangements and foreign laws.

Principal risk factors include failure to anticipate market and technology changes; stronger competition; cybersecurity breaches; product defects, security vulnerabilities and recalls; dependence on third-party foundries and subcontractors; manufacturing delays or low yields; natural disasters and business disruptions; inaccurate demand forecasts and inventory write-downs; international operations, trade restrictions and regulatory changes; difficulty attracting and retaining personnel; unsuccessful acquisitions or investments; intellectual-property litigation; privacy and data-protection requirements; tax-law changes; legal and regulatory proceedings; and provisions that may impede a change in control. International sales represented 79% of total revenue in fiscal 2018, and approximately 47% of employees were located outside the United States.

NVIDIA’s headquarters comprise ten leased buildings totaling 963,317 square feet and seven owned commercial buildings totaling 1,496,006 square feet on 36 acres. The company also leases or owns facilities in the United States and internationally for research, sales, administration and datacenter capacity.

The company increased its quarterly cash dividend from $0.14 to $0.15 per share in November 2017 and paid $341 million in cash dividends during fiscal 2018. Since 2004, it has repurchased 251 million shares for $5.5 billion through January 28, 2018, with authorization remaining for up to $1.82 billion through December 2020. For fiscal 2019, NVIDIA intended to return $1.25 billion through dividends and repurchases. It also issued 33 million shares in connection with convertible-note settlements and withheld approximately four million shares for restricted-stock-unit tax obligations at a cost of $612 million.

A study by Alexandra Tinnermann and colleagues at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf found that perceived price affects the nocebo effect. Volunteers given fake creams said to increase pain sensitivity reported more pain with the expensive-looking cream (nearly 30% more) than the generic one (about 3% more). Brain imaging showed differing activity in the prefrontal cortex and periaqueductal gray, regions of the neural pain pathway also implicated in placebo effects. The results may help clinicians minimize nocebo effects when discussing medications.

Goal side is the basic defensive position on an imaginary line between the defended goal and opponents. Coaches can teach young players to get in opponents’ way or keep them in front without blocking them or extending their arms. Defenders should move out from goal, stop before reaching forwards, and recognize their position relative to the goal. If behind an opponent, they must sprint beyond and turn around. Practice should cover right, center, and left positions, adjustment to opponent movement, and quick glances at the goal or penalty-area markings, progressing from slow, ballless drills to ball work and faster movement.

The Alabama Court of Civil Appeals denied James F. Robertson III’s mandamus petition seeking a default judgment in his divorce case. Although Robertson attempted service by publication, the trial court file lacked proof of publication and the Rule 4.3(d)(5) affidavit required from the publisher. The trial court denied his default-judgment motion and his request for reconsideration. Because Robertson had not established a clear legal right to the requested order, the petition was denied.

In an appeal by the United States over the appraised value of imported fishing equipment, the court held that the merchandise’s export values were the entered values less specified shipping, consular, insurance, and incidental charges. It treated conceded outside-packing charges as dutiable and allowed an unexplained 26.557-yen invoice deduction because no evidence showed it was improper.

Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. sought to enforce a 1977 Colorado promissory note signed by Conrad Lapp individually and on behalf of Joslyn Fruit Company, his premarital business. Lapp’s wife did not sign. After the note went unpaid and the Lapps moved to Washington, the trial court and Court of Appeals held the marital community was not liable.

The Washington Supreme Court reversed, applying the “most significant relationship” test. The majority concluded that Colorado law governed because the transaction occurred there, the Lapps were domiciled there when the note was signed, performance was expected there, and both parties expected Colorado law to apply. Under Colorado law, a debt incurred solely by a husband may be collected from his property and earnings, but not his wife’s separate property; therefore, Lapp’s Washington community assets, including his wages and later acquisitions, could satisfy the debt.

Justice Horowitz, joined by Chief Justice Utter, dissented. Agreeing that Colorado law governed the note’s validity, the dissent argued that Washington law should govern which property may be used to collect the judgment, thereby protecting community assets from Lapp’s separate business debt.

WMCC’s modern cabinetry and construction class built cabinets and countertops for the Kidder United Methodist Church kitchen, which is being upgraded to serve as a disaster relief center. The article explains cryptocurrency trading as buying and selling digital assets for profit or speculation and surveys 20 strategies. These include day trading, whale watching, swing and dark-pool trading, trend following, range trading, fork and breakout trading, mean reversion and dollar-cost averaging, arbitrage, grid trading, sentiment and social-media analysis, newly launched coins, technical analysis, zombie coins, proof-of-stake staking, quantum trading, Ichimoku Cloud, and NFT trading. It stresses that cryptocurrencies differ from stocks, stock strategies may not transfer directly, and strategies should be backtested because volatility, limited historical data, fees, slippage, scams, lost private keys, technological complexity, and limited regulation create risks.

A Bitcoin trend-following backtest from late 2014 produced 135 trades, a 42% win rate, and an average gain of 7% per trade because winners averaged 21% while losers averaged 4%. It reported an 87% annual return, a 66% drawdown, and investment in the market 56% of the time. The study found trend following historically more effective than mean reversion.

The article also examines how halvings can reduce new-coin supply and trigger anticipatory buying; how hard forks can create new chains and coins while increasing uncertainty and volatility; and how DeFi, macroeconomic and regulatory events, and Tether may affect prices, liquidity, costs, and market sentiment. The best strategy depends on investment goals and risk tolerance.

The St. Louis Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court judgment based on its prior decision in the same-facts case of Century Realty Co. v. Frankfort Marine, Accident and Plate Glass Insurance Company.

The professor recaps class topics including business plans, customer discovery, pitching, business models, and financial projections, then introduces a financing-sources panel featuring former entrepreneur and venture capitalist Axel Bichara, clean-tech founder and venture capitalist Julianne Zimmerman, and Polaris managing partner Amir Nashat.

The panel emphasizes that every form of capital has a specific use, benefit, and cost, and that venture capital is not necessary for every successful company. Financing options include equity, convertible notes, angels, venture capital, incubators, accelerators, grants, crowdfunding, customer revenue, and other creative sources. The appropriate choice depends on the company’s stage, market, team, objectives, and desired dilution.

Convertible notes can provide quick, inexpensive interim financing and may convert into equity during a later round, but they remain debt unless converted and can give creditors substantial power if the company fails. Equity avoids repayment obligations but dilutes ownership. Panelists recommend understanding an investor’s objectives, ensuring interests are aligned, and defining success consistently.

Entrepreneurs should carefully vet investors through references, examine their behavior in difficult situations, and select people who ask useful questions, listen, and fit the company’s needs. They should avoid raising more money than the opportunity can justify, since excessive capital creates pressure for rapid growth and can constrain flexibility. Strategic investors may create conflicts over time, while many small investors can make future decisions difficult if unanimous approval is required.

For fundraising, the panel identifies direct outreach, referrals, and cold submissions as the main channels, while emphasizing strong introductions, early networking, and mentorship. Founders should begin financing conversations early without making formal pitches merely to gain feedback. For impact-oriented ventures, investors should be identified narrowly, and sustainable business models should align benefits for providers, beneficiaries, and investors. Ultimately, founders should repeatedly ask why the venture, team, timing, financing amount, instrument, and investor are appropriate.

Simulation-based inference (SBI) enables Bayesian parameter estimation from simulators but is vulnerable to model misspecification, where simulator and real-data likelihoods differ. Such mismatch can produce biased or overconfident posteriors, especially with deep generative models and limited real observations.

The paper introduces Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation (FMCPE), which combines abundant low-cost simulations with a small calibration set of high-fidelity parameter–observation pairs. First, neural posterior estimation trains an approximate simulator-based posterior. FMCPE then learns a simulation-space flow transporting observations toward simulator-generated outcomes, creating a reweighted proposal posterior that serves as the source for a parameter-space flow transporting samples toward the corrected posterior. The two flows are trained jointly, allowing the source to improve as the transport becomes more accurate. The method requires no explicit specification of the misspecification, can use off-the-shelf SBI posteriors as proposals, and supports amortized inference and post-processing.

Experiments compare FMCPE with NPE and MFNPE on Gaussian, damped-pendulum, wind-tunnel, and light-tunnel tasks using jC2ST, Wasserstein distance, and mean squared error. Performance improves as calibration data increase, but FMCPE consistently outperforms both baselines, particularly with small calibration sets. It produces better-calibrated, more accurately centered posteriors, captures parameter dependencies more effectively, and shows lower variability across calibration samples than MFNPE. The results indicate that scarce high-fidelity data can substantially improve SBI under misspecification, although severe high-dimensional mismatch may require larger calibration sets.

The excerpt defines version 6.00 of the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification and the Mc-EX interface extension. It classifies cards as SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (over 2–32 GB), and SDXC (over 32 GB–2 TB), covering standard, miniSD, and microSD form factors. High-voltage cards operate at 2.7–3.6 V, while UHS-II adds a 1.70–1.95 V VDD2 supply. Both read/write and ROM cards are described.

The specification covers command, response, and data transfers, CRC-protected single- and multiple-block operations, session addressing, four-line wide-bus operation, card registers, reset procedures, and host-controlled card selection. Speed modes include Default Speed up to 25 MB/s, High Speed up to 50 MB/s, UHS-I modes through SDR104 at 104 MB/s and DDR50, and UHS-II modes FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624; FD624 is identified as the maximum UHS-II mode at 624 MB/s.

Initialization uses CMD0 to reset cards, CMD8 to verify operating voltage, ACMD41 to specify voltage and capacity support, CMD2 to obtain the CID, CMD3 to assign an RCA, and CMD7 to select a card for data transfer. UHS-I initialization can request a switch from 3.3 V to 1.8 V signaling through ACMD41 and CMD11, with CMD19 used for sampling-point tuning. UHS-II initialization proceeds through PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization stages.

Read and write operations use block data with CRC protection, support abort through CMD12, and indicate busy or programming status on DAT0. Write operations may be buffered, interleaved across cards, or preceded by ACMD23 pre-erasing. Erase sequences use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38, including DISCARD for deallocated blocks and FULE for logical erasure of the user area.

Write protection can be mechanical, internal to the card, or password-based through CMD42. Card Ownership Protection adds Force Erase Password management, COP-specific commands, and restricted access after reset. ROM cards treat specified write and erase commands as unsupported. Other features include bus-speed and driver-strength selection, speed classes, Application Performance Class, caching, self-maintenance, and voluntary or sequential command-queue modes.

South Carolina headlines cover the 2018 governor race, constitution-restoration funding, a $38 million Cooper River office sale, Charleston’s Medicare cardiac-care pilot, the mayor’s first year, and new laws.
Apple replaces eligible batteries at no charge for 13-inch MacBook Pros without Touch Bar built between October 2016 and October 2017; owners can check eligibility via Apple’s support page.

Researchers studied 173 women aged 25–50 who drank less than a litre of water daily. Adding 500 ml to breakfast promoted weight loss, while other studies found that drinking 500 ml burns 23 extra calories, equivalent to 2 kg of fat per year.

Balfour argues that the Central powers’ brutality in Belgium and submarine warfare was intended to terrorize neutrals as well as defeat enemies. He maintains that peace achieved through such methods would undermine international law and treaties, and that durable peace requires Allied success. Three conditions are necessary: reducing causes of international unrest, discrediting aggressive aims and unscrupulous methods among the Central powers’ own peoples, and creating international sanctions to deter aggressors. Accordingly, he supports continued sacrifices of blood and treasure to secure peace, civilization, and international reform. Separately, Greece’s minister reports acceptance of the Entente’s ultimatum, with difficulties over political prisoners and internal control. The U.S. Secretary of State notes Persia’s endorsement of the President’s peace note and Persia’s request that the United States help preserve its integrity and rights at a future peace conference.

The paper introduces DS-STAR, an LLM-based agent for autonomously solving data science tasks across heterogeneous file formats. DS-STAR first analyzes each input file to generate a concise description of its structure and content. It then generates Python solutions through iterative planning, coding, execution, and verification. A verifier agent judges whether the cumulative plan and execution results sufficiently answer the query. If not, a router agent either adds a new step or removes an erroneous step for regeneration. Additional debugging and embedding-based retrieval modules support error correction and large data collections.

Experiments on DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code show DS-STAR outperforming existing agent frameworks. With Gemini-2.5-Pro, it reaches 45.24% hard-task accuracy on DABStep, 44.69% on KramaBench, and 38.5% overall on DA-Code. Ablation results identify both file analysis and routing as important: removing file descriptions reduces DABStep hard-task accuracy to 26.98%, while removing the router reduces it to 39.95%. Easy tasks require an average of 3.0 refinement rounds, compared with 5.6 for hard tasks, and accuracy generally rises as the maximum number of iterations increases. The authors identify human-in-the-loop collaboration as a direction for future work.

“Sell the rip” means selling an asset—closing an open long position or opening a short—when its price appears overvalued and poised for correction. It is a mean-reversion approach often used by short-term traders to profit from overbought conditions, particularly in fundamentally weak stocks inflated by market sentiment or overreaction. It is generally considered unsuitable for long-term investing or strong-growth assets because prices may continue rising, creating substantial risk for short sellers.

Common indicators include RSI, Stochastic, Williams %R, IBS, Bollinger Bands, and moving averages. A simple RSI strategy on SPY bought when the three-day RSI was below 30 and sold when it crossed above 70. It produced 391 trades, a 0.61% average gain, a 75% win rate, and a 1.6 profit factor, but its large, prolonged drawdowns made it untradable in the authors’ view. A modified exit criterion shortened holding periods, increased trade frequency, reduced the average gain to 0.48%, and materially improved the equity curve and drawdowns. The article says the strategy performed well in the S&P 500 over the past three decades but is less successful in trending markets such as commodities, and recommends backtesting each market.

The Yankees and Red Sox face off in a best-of-three 2025 AL Wild Card series starting Sept. 30 in New York. ESPN will televise the games. New York is the No. 4 seed and Boston the No. 5. The matchup is their sixth postseason series, with Boston holding a 3–2 edge.

At the expanded Scripps National Spelling Bee, longtime associate pronouncer the Rev. Brian Sietsema covered two of five preliminary groups, pronouncing for about 180 spellers while Jacques Bailly paced himself to protect his voice over three days. Sietsema, a Greek Orthodox priest, former linguistics professor and Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor, called the experience exciting. More than 500 contestants took the written test, which selected 41 semifinalists; bee director Paige Kimble said a test thought to be easy proved difficult. Twelve-year-old Shruthika Padhy, last year’s seventh-place finisher, was among the top scorers. Veteran Rebekah Zeigler reached her goal by correctly spelling “yarrow” in an onstage round she had never previously reached. Reagan Remmers was reinstated after judges accepted “Balaklava,” the name of a Ukrainian city, because the assigned word “balaclava” had an undisclosed homonym and she had not requested its definition. Alaska’s Daniel Doudna spelled deliberately, reviewing each letter mentally after previously making mistakes by rushing.

The article examines how AI-driven personalized learning can increase student autonomy and self-determination without requiring an abrupt replacement of existing schooling. Although curriculum, teaching methods, assessment, and technology have evolved, schools retain a largely standardized structure in which teachers, students, and the prescribed curriculum remain central. Curriculum acts as the education system’s anchor by determining what is taught, how it is taught and assessed, how students are grouped, and how school time is used. State-mandated curricula, standardized testing, and tiered schooling have strengthened this prescription over two centuries, leaving students little control over what, how, when, with whom, or where they learn.

Using panarchy theory from ecology, the article describes education as a nested, multi-layered system whose resilience, adaptability, and transformability shape change. Education has typically absorbed technologies such as computers, the internet, and generative AI without fundamentally transforming its structure. Most innovations occur at the teacher, school, or policy level but preserve the prescribed curriculum and centralized control. Transformative innovations, such as Montessori, Dalton, Waldorf, and democratic education, have often remained outside mainstream public systems.

The article proposes a balanced curriculum that retains some state-controlled content while allocating time for student-directed learning. Systems, schools, teachers, students, and families would determine the balance according to students’ age, experience, capacity, and available support. Autonomy would be facilitated rather than unlimited, with teachers acting as coaches and advisers. Such curriculum change could also reshape classroom organization, schedules, facilities, teacher roles, and assessment.

Transformation may begin with small, autonomous “school-within-a-school” subsystems that use personalized, project-oriented learning and AI while remaining connected to the larger system. If successful, they could influence and spread across schools and eventually transform the wider education system. Examples include Hongfan Middle School’s ICEE program, which occupies about one-third of its curriculum and expanded from two selected classes to six cohorts and high-school offerings; one-year programs in Australian schools; and new school entities such as The Studio School and ScotsX. The examples also show that leadership support, public testing, and the ability to remain active long enough to be evaluated are important. The article concludes that gradual, subsystem-based change offers a pathway through the education system’s growth, conservation, release, and reorganization phases toward greater student autonomy and educational transformation.

The passage lists major American foreign-policy statements issued in 1945, with citations from the Department of State Bulletin and the Public Papers of Presidents Roosevelt and Truman. Roosevelt’s entries address the Yalta Conference, America’s world role, and the proposed United Nations. Truman’s statements cover his succession, the San Francisco Conference and ratification of the UN Charter, Germany’s surrender, continued war with Japan, the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, the Potsdam Conference, Japan’s surrender, atomic energy, defense aid, and foreign-policy issues. Other listed statements include Cordell Hull’s comments at the UN Conference and Secretary of State James F. Byrnes’s addresses on the Council of Foreign Ministers, world cooperation, neighboring nations, and U.S. policy in China.

The speaker credits the team’s defense, particularly its four top players and contributions from Yannick Weber and Matt Irwin, for helping manage strong opponents with multiple top centers. Their availability has been important throughout the regular season and playoffs. He describes an emphasis on continual learning from veteran players, coaches, and experience, while using scheduled breaks for team meetings and resetting. Reaching the playoffs required sustained hard work and shaped the team’s identity. Although the team is enjoying playing in June, he stresses that success depends on daily preparation and a business-like approach across players and staff. He says both teams remain hungry for the Cup and must be ready to play the decisive game.

On August 28, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. completed its acquisition of Whole Foods Market, Inc. under the June 15, 2017 merger agreement. Amazon’s wholly owned subsidiary, Walnut Merger Sub, Inc., merged into Whole Foods, which survived as a wholly owned Amazon subsidiary. Each eligible Whole Foods share converted into the right to receive $42 in cash. Options and cash-settled stock appreciation rights were cashed out based on the $42 consideration, with awards priced at or above $42 canceled; restricted stock awards and units received $42 per covered share. Total consideration was approximately $13.55 billion, financed with net proceeds from previously disclosed debt financing. Amazon planned to amend the Form 8-K with acquired-business financial statements, pro forma information, and the merger agreement as Exhibit 2.1.

The Martingale strategy doubles a losing trade’s size to recover prior losses plus an initial-stake profit if the next trade wins. Originally used in gambling and associated with 18th-century mathematician Paul Pierre Levy, it assumes equal win/loss probabilities and eventual mean reversion. It differs from double-down, which adds only the original position size, and from averaging down, which follows a planned investment schedule.

The method can produce a high win rate, but losses may be exceptionally large. Unlimited capital is theoretically required because a prolonged losing streak can exhaust funds and cause severe drawdowns. Its use in stocks is particularly risky because stocks can fall to zero; long-only application to broad-market index ETFs may reduce this risk. Positive carry can lessen losses in certain forex trades.

A backtest on SPY produced 409 trades, an average gain of 0.64% per trade, 8.68% annual returns, and a 23% maximum drawdown. A modified RSI-based version performed poorly. The article does not recommend Martingale trading and instead suggests diversifying equity across uncorrelated, data-driven strategies.

A New York Times survey found widespread dissatisfaction among responding federal judges with Supreme Court emergency docket decisions involving President Trump’s policies. Of 65 respondents, 12 said the Court made appropriate use of the emergency docket, while 47 disagreed and six were neutral. Twelve said lower courts received sufficient guidance, compared with 48 who disagreed and five who were neutral. Among 54 respondents, 42 said the docket harmed public perceptions of the judiciary, 10 saw no effect and two saw improvement. Many emergency orders benefited Trump, and at least seven of roughly 20 lacked stated reasoning, though they had broad practical effects. The survey drew criticism for potential response and district-selection bias.

The article examines how dance education can be integrated with social studies education in U.S. schools to support holistic student development and civic engagement. It argues that standardized testing, which separates subjects and largely excludes dance, reinforces disciplinary silos and limits interdisciplinary education.

A literature review and a 12-question Qualtrics survey of 91 U.S. dance-education graduates examined whether dance curricula address social studies concepts. The survey, conducted in March and April 2024, found that every concept was addressed by at least some respondents. The strongest emphases were individual development and identity (97%), people, places and environments (94%), time and continuity (75%), individuals, groups and institutions (69%), and global connections (66%). Culture, science and technology, governance, and civic practices were also present. Responses showed that educators incorporated these concepts either literally through curriculum content or implicitly through classroom practices, including inclusion, cooperation, cultural exchange, and relationships with the natural world.

The study found that dance can meaningfully function as social studies, but explicit, prescriptive curricula and limited professional guidance often prevent educators from recognizing these connections. Dance educators also appear to work largely independently when broadening their curricula.

The article recommends less prescriptive dance curricula, stronger professional development on the relationship between pedagogy and curriculum, and education-policy changes that support interdisciplinary arts learning. Limitations include the small, non-randomized U.S.-only sample, the IRB’s restrictions on survey content, limited generalizability, and the absence of social studies teachers’ perspectives. Further international and in-depth research was recommended.

Colorado’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted to cap payments for Amgen’s Enbrel at $600 per unit, the first such action in the nation. The ceiling applies to government agencies and commercial health plans covering state residents, equating to about $30,350 annually per person versus roughly $53,000 paid by the average state insurance plan in 2023. The move may prompt other states to pursue similar prescription-drug spending controls.

Turkey’s government planned to extend the state of emergency for three months from April 19, citing threats from FETO, which Ankara blames for the July 2016 coup. The move followed a public vote shifting Turkey to an executive presidency.

The ADS868xW supports four legacy SPI-compatible protocols—SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, and SPI-11-S—for configuration writes and data reads. SPI-00-S is used after power-up or asynchronous reset. The SDI_MODE[1:0] bits in SDI_CTL_REG select another protocol; the selection write itself uses SPI-00-S, while subsequent transfers use the selected protocol for both reads and writes. A valid write requires at least 32 SCLK cycles per data-transfer frame.

For SPI reads, SDO_MODE[1:0] must be set to 00b in SDO_CTL_REG so the output follows the selected SPI protocol. RVS remains low during SPI transfers. Short frames can read only the required MSBs, while a long frame with SDO_CNTL_REG[7:0] = 00h enables daisy-chain operation. Optional dual-SDO operation is enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b, which assigns the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin to SDO-1 and launches two data bits per SCLK edge. Single-SDO mode uses half as many clock cycles as dual mode to output the same number of bits.

The multiSPI interface also supports source-synchronous operation, in which the device supplies an output clock synchronous with the data on RVS. The clock can be internal or external, with the external clock supplied on SCLK and the selection controlled by SSYNC_CLK. SRC mode supports single or dual output buses.

Nine configuration registers span byte-addressed ranges: DEVICE_ID_REG at 00h–03h, RST_PWRCTL_REG at 04h–07h, SDI_CTL_REG at 08h–0Bh, SDO_CTL_REG at 0Ch–0Fh, DATAOUT_CTL_REG at 10h–13h, RANGE_SEL_REG at 14h–17h, ALARM_REG at 20h–23h, ALARM_H_TH_REG at 24h–27h, and ALARM_L_TH_REG at 28h–2Bh. These registers control device identification for daisy-chains, reset and low-power behavior, SPI and SRC protocols, output framing, reference and input-range selection, and alarms. Writes to RST_PWRCTL_REG require the protection sequence of writing 69h to address 05h. DATAOUT_CTL_REG can include the device address, alarm flags, and range setting in the output stream, append even-parity bits, or output zeros, ones, and alternating patterns.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential-input data-acquisition device based on a 16-bit SAR ADC, with an integrated analog front end and buffered precision reference. An industrial reference design combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 to provide eight software-configurable voltage or current channels. It supports standard industrial voltage and current ranges, settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs, has input bandwidth up to 400 kHz at −3 dB, and includes an internal PGA, ADC driver, reference, overvoltage protection, and input and AVDD alarms.

Programmable input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis support an NTC-thermistor temperature-sensing example. Hysteresis prevents noise near a threshold from causing false alarms and improves noise immunity.

AVDD and DVDD are independently configurable supplies. Decoupling guidance calls for close high-frequency capacitors on both supplies, with additional bulk capacitance on AVDD. PCB layouts should separate analog and digital routing, use short ground paths, and avoid vias between supply pins and their bypass capacitors. REFCAP requires 1 µF and 10 µF ceramic capacitors, with the 10 µF capacitor having ESR below 0.2 Ω; REFIO requires at least 4.7 µF when the internal reference is used.

Two low-power modes are available. NAP mode places internal blocks into a low-power state after conversion while CONVST/CS remains high; a falling edge wakes the device, and conversion can restart after the specified wake-up time. Power-down mode shuts down analog blocks while retaining the interface and registers. It is entered by setting PWRDN on a rising CONVST/CS edge; clearing PWRDN starts wake-up, indicated by RVS, after which the host must wait the specified power-up time.

The document also directs users to TI notification and support resources, warns that integrated circuits require ESD precautions, and records that ADS8685W and ADS8689W documentation changed from advance information to production data in Revision A.

The Dolphins ended a winless stretch dating to the 2024 season with a win over the Jets, but the victory was overshadowed by star receiver Tyreek Hill’s dislocated left knee. Hill was carted off in the third quarter and is expected to miss the rest of the season, leaving Miami without a central figure in its offense. Tight end Darren Waller caught two touchdowns in his first game action since January 2024, providing Miami with a possible major replacement.

The Jets rushed for 197 yards, including an 81-yard performance featuring a 43-yard touchdown, while Miami’s defense allowed a season-high 120-plus rushing yards for the fourth consecutive game. Aaron Glenn’s team committed three turnovers and 12 penalties for 101 yards, trailed 10-3 at halftime and lost three fumbles for the first time since 2023. Quarterback Fields supplied the Jets’ only highlight with a 43-yard touchdown scramble, but had more rushing than passing yards through three quarters. The loss left New York 0-4, matching the longest losing streak to begin a Jets coach’s tenure; no coach has started 0-5.

A proposed method for detecting alien civilizations would search exoplanet transit data for signs of massive swarms of artificial satellites. Astronomer Hector Socas-Navarro suggests that advanced extraterrestrial societies could have billions or trillions of geostationary satellites, producing slight dips in starlight before and after a planet’s transit, especially when viewed edge-on. Unlike searches for radio or laser signals, this approach requires no synchronicity with aliens and could detect artifacts that survive their extinction. It would also use existing exoplanet-observation data without new telescopes or experiments, though its chances of success are uncertain.

China’s foreign exchange system will expand its trade-weighted currency basket from 13 to 24 currencies at the start of 2017, reducing the U.S. dollar’s weighting from 26.4% to 22.4%. It is the basket’s first weighting adjustment since December 2015 and aims to reduce focus on the yuan-dollar rate. The yuan lost about 7% against the dollar in 2016, its worst major Asian currency performance that year. Chinese officials maintain the yuan is stable and attribute its weakness to a strong dollar. The change comes amid U.S. President Donald Trump’s accusations of Chinese currency manipulation and concerns over U.S.-China trade.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 28, 2022, reporting its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2022. The related press release was included as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

The lecture concludes the discussion of Arnoldi and introduces conjugate gradients. Arnoldi is presented as a Gram–Schmidt-like procedure that constructs an orthogonal Krylov basis and produces a factorization relating \(A\), the basis matrix \(Q\), and an upper-Hessenberg matrix \(H\). For symmetric \(A\), \(H\) is symmetric and tridiagonal. Truncating Arnoldi after a modest number of steps and computing the eigenvalues of the resulting tridiagonal submatrix produces Ritz values, which often efficiently approximate the low eigenvalues of a large matrix; ARPACK is mentioned as a software package for this purpose.

Conjugate gradients is described as an iterative method for symmetric positive-definite linear systems. It recursively constructs iterates \(x_k\), residuals \(r_k\), and search directions \(d_k\), with scalar coefficients \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Its corrections are orthogonal in the natural \(A\)-inner product, while the residuals are mutually orthogonal. Each iteration requires one multiplication by \(A\), two inner products, and roughly two or three vector updates; with a sparse matrix, its cost is therefore relatively low. Its convergence estimate depends on the matrix’s condition number.

The method is also interpreted as minimizing the quadratic energy
\[
E(x)=\tfrac12 x^T Ax-b^T x.
\]
Because \(A\) is positive definite, this energy has a unique minimum whose gradient is \(Ax-b\), so minimizing the energy is equivalent to solving \(Ax=b\). Steepest descent follows successive negative-gradient directions and may zigzag across a long, narrow valley. Conjugate gradients instead chooses \(A\)-orthogonal directions, appearing as right angles in the \(A\)-inner product, and therefore approaches the minimum more directly. The same idea can also motivate nonlinear conjugate-gradient methods.

When \(A\) is not symmetric positive definite, conjugate gradients may fail because denominators can vanish. Minimum residual (MINRES) is introduced as a safer but more expensive alternative for symmetric systems. It uses Arnoldi’s orthogonal Krylov basis to minimize the Euclidean norm of \(b-Ax_k\), reducing the problem to a small least-squares problem. Unlike the symmetric Arnoldi case, the associated Hessenberg matrix is not tridiagonal, making the computation more costly.

The lecture closes by contrasting these recurrence-based Krylov methods with simpler iterations such as Jacobi and Gauss–Seidel, and by noting that choosing between iterative methods and direct elimination requires numerical comparisons.

IMI plc has a consensus “Hold” rating from 18 analysts: two sell, 12 hold and four buy. The average 12-month target is GBX 1,027.29 ($12.84). BNP Paribas raised its target to GBX 1,400 with an “outperform” rating; Barclays reaffirmed “overweight,” while Goldman Sachs, Credit Suisse and JPMorgan reaffirmed “neutral.” The stock opened at GBX 1,216, has a GBX 3.29 billion market capitalization, and a 52-week range of GBX 751–1,223. IMI is a UK-based engineering company focused on flow, motion, heating and cooling controls.

Police are warning shoppers to guard against festive-season fraud, while Crimestoppers is seeking information on people making, buying or selling counterfeit banknotes. In the first half of 2017, more than 237,000 fake notes with a notional value exceeding £4.88 million were removed from UK circulation. Counterfeit notes have conned retailers, businesses, schools, charities and elderly people and are linked to serious organised crime. Crimestoppers and the Bank of England launched a scheme in October to train cash-handling businesses and reduce acceptance of fake notes. Information can be reported anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or via its online form.

GSK announced that chief commercial officer Luke Miels will become CEO on Jan. 1, succeeding Emma Walmsley, who led the company since 2017. Walmsley oversaw the consumer health care spinoff into Haleon and a refocus on specialty medicines and vaccines, though investors have questioned GSK’s strategy amid HIV patent losses and vaccine challenges. AstraZeneca also plans to list ordinary shares on the New York Stock Exchange while retaining its London listing and remaining listed in Stockholm. The U.S. listing would simplify access for American investors but is expected to be viewed as another blow to the U.K., where drugmakers have criticized pricing and the commercial environment.

Zimbabwe’s veterinary services face FMD vaccine shortages, inconsistent supplies, staffing below 30%, and weak logistical, financial, and technical capacity. Uncontrolled livestock movement, damaged or absent boundary fences, ineffective animal identification, and wildlife conservancy non-cooperation have contributed to spread in five provinces and active infections in four areas. Zimbabwe has no FMD-free zones. Zonal controls would limit regular revaccination to about two million cattle, while outbreaks currently require repeated vaccination every four months.

Cheltenham Town face a second summer battle to retain Harry Pell, with an unnamed League Two rival interested in the 26-year-old midfielder. Contracted until 2018/19, the fans’ favourite has made over 120 appearances, previously rejecting Blackpool. Recently used centrally and as a forward, he scored three goals in five games but missed Cambridge United after wisdom-teeth removal.

Pseudo Programs ceased operations and laid off all 175 employees after efforts to raise funding or find a buyer failed, though it continued seeking a buyer. Broadbase agreed to acquire Servicesoft in a stock deal valued at approximately $645 million. Enfrastructure launched with more than $100 million in backing, Interregnum opened a $105 million technology investment fund, and Q9 Networks raised $26.5 million in Series A financing. These include Darwin Networks’ $91 million Series B, IPG Photonics’ $75 million second round, Wheelhouse’s $52 million second round, $50 million rounds for Everdream and Nishan Systems, $42 million for Onehealthbank.com, $40 million for CosmoCom, $36 million rounds for StorageWay and MobileSys, $35 million for Portera, $31 million for Skulogix, $30 million rounds for Internet Machines and iPass, and $20 million rounds for BuyMedia and Orsus. Other reported financings included BarterNet’s $21.4 million Series B, RiskMetrics and ipVerse at $21.8 million each, Currenex’s $16 million second-round closing, Mapletree’s $15 million, Viveca’s $14.5 million first round, and Appro’s $22 million first round. Everypath disclosed an additional $10 million, bringing its total funding above $95 million. Six companies added directors, including Bidder’s Edge, Unica, Hudson Williams, Looking Glass Networks, TeamLinux, and SupplySpot.com. CityReach International named former IBM executive Sanjaya Addanki CEO, while RewardsPlus named former Insweb executive M. Gordon Gaddy CEO and moved founder Ken Barksdale to president and chief operating officer.
