Active lifestyles can reduce the risk of knee injuries by maintaining a healthy weight, strengthening the muscles that support the knees and body, preserving flexibility and range of motion, and keeping joints mobile. Recommended exercise includes gradually increased resistance work targeting the hamstrings, quadriceps, glutes and hip flexors, plus stretching. Low-impact cardiovascular activities such as cycling and swimming support circulation and knee cartilage while reducing impact on the joints.

If an injury occurs, early physiotherapy, appropriate exercises and continued activity can aid recovery, reduce the risk of further problems and potentially delay or avoid surgery. Recommended exercises include quadriceps contractions, bridges, wall squats and stretches for the calves, hamstrings, hips and front of the thigh. Persistent pain that limits mobility should be assessed by a physiotherapist, who can provide a tailored treatment plan. Knee pain should not be ignored, but staying active helps prevent stiffness and compensate for reduced mobility.

Knee problems become more common with age because of lifelong wear and tear, although surgery is not inevitable. When a knee is too damaged for rehabilitation, surgery can significantly improve quality of life, though it carries risks including infection and deep vein thrombosis. More than four in five total knee replacements and seven in ten unicondylar replacements were reported to last 25 years. Physiotherapy and regular exercise can improve recovery after surgery and protect the replaced knee.
During a televised Oval Office welcome for French President Emmanuel Macron, Trump praised their “special relationship,” brushed dandruff from Macron’s shoulder, and called him “perfect.”

This study examined behavioural changes and their cognitive and neuroanatomical correlates in behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) and semantic dementia (SD). Participants included 47 people with FTD—26 with bvFTD and 21 with SD—and 18 age-matched controls. Behaviour was assessed with the CBI-R, AMI-CG and CamQUAIT, alongside neuropsychological testing and structural MRI.

Both FTD groups showed impairment across a wide range of behaviours, although bvFTD generally had more severe abnormalities. Behaviours significantly more prevalent in bvFTD were not found to be disproportionately common in SD, indicating quantitative rather than qualitative double dissociations. Principal-component analysis identified three behavioural dimensions: apathy, challenging behaviours and activities of daily living. Apathy was more severe in bvFTD and was associated with impaired executive function, particularly Brixton Spatial Anticipation performance, and anterior cingulate atrophy after accounting for global atrophy. Daily-living impairment was associated with FTD severity and medial prefrontal, precentral and insular grey-matter loss, although these associations disappeared after global atrophy was controlled for. No grey-matter correlates were found for challenging behaviours, and no association was found between social-semantic knowledge or anterior temporal-lobe volume and questionnaire-measured behaviour change.

Semantic memory was poorer in SD, whereas executive function was poorer in bvFTD. Together, these neuropsychological measures discriminated the diagnoses more accurately than behavioural measures, achieving an AUC of 95.1%. Patient self-ratings of apathy did not differ significantly from control ratings and were poorly concordant with caregiver ratings, particularly in bvFTD.

Left- and right-dominant SD groups had strongly overlapping behavioural profiles, with no behaviour specific to right-dominant atrophy. The authors therefore conceptualised SD as a graded disorder rather than two distinct diseases, while noting that the study’s cross-sectional design, UK sample and incomplete coverage of behavioural domains limited its conclusions. Longitudinal research with more comprehensive, diverse measures was recommended.

The passage warns that popular government is threatened both by violent demagogues who exploit class fears and by corrupt plutocrats who exploit workers, noting that the two often collaborate. It urges passage of a bill limiting railroad employees’ working hours and supports gradually reducing labor hours toward an eight-hour day, while allowing for unsuitable industries, communities, or tropical regions such as Panama. It calls for strict enforcement of existing federal eight-hour laws, summer half-holidays for government employees, a truant court in the District of Columbia, and thorough investigations of child and women’s labor. It also urges immediate enactment of strict child-labor laws for the District of Columbia and U.S. territories to promote uniform state action.

Actors Daisy McCrackin and Joseph Capone were allegedly kidnapped and held for ransom for nearly three days by a meth-fuelled gang. Police arrested Keith Andre Stewart, Johntae Jones and Amber Neal, who were charged with 17 offences including kidnapping, assault, grand theft, mayhem and conspiracy. The indictment alleges they entered McCrackin’s home, pistol-whipped Capone, hooded both victims, held Capone naked in a bathtub for 30 hours and forced McCrackin to obtain at least $10,000. She escaped on May 4 and alerted police. The accused face a July 23 hearing.

This transcript of *Wall Street Week With Louis Rukeyser*, produced December 29, 2000, reviews a difficult year for investors and the outlook for 2001. The Dow lost just over 6%, the S&P 500 fell a bit more than 10%, and the Nasdaq dropped nearly 40%, while the broader exchanges posted small gains. The dollar was the year’s strongest major currency, gaining 12% against the yen. Economic growth slowed despite a nearly decade-long expansion; unemployment remained near 3.9–4%, consumer inflation reached 3.4%, oil prices exceeded $37 before retreating, and the trade deficit set another record.

Panelists identified corporate earnings, Federal Reserve policy, mutual-fund cash flows, consumer confidence and the dollar as key factors for 2001. Brian Rogers expected 5–7% corporate-profit growth and some early market choppiness; Barbara Marcin said more reasonable valuations and falling technology shares could support a broader market but warned that declining consumer confidence and possible layoffs could cause a recession; Lou Holland estimated a greater-than-even chance of recession and favored Federal Reserve rate cuts; and Elizabeth Dater emphasized interest rates, consumer confidence, foreign investment and capital preservation.

The four panelists’ 2000 recommendation portfolios returned more than 42.5% for Rogers, more than 40% for Marcin, more than 28% for Holland and more than 7.5% for Dater. For 2001, they forecast Dow highs of 12,175–13,000, lows of 9,781–10,500 and closes of 11,740–12,504; Nasdaq highs of 2,834–3,200, lows of 2,000–2,500 and closes of 2,250–3,000. Their stock recommendations included technology and telecommunications, selected beaten-down large companies, and, for Dater, 25% in three-year Treasury notes. Rogers expected the Federal Reserve to cut rates twice and short-term yields to fall 50–75 basis points. An appendix lists similar forecasts and recommendations from all 22 panelists.

Invictus MD Strategies Corp. received $5,777,267 from warrant and option exercises during the fiscal year beginning February 1, 2018. The exercises involved 4,346,731 warrants and 337,500 options, bringing common shares outstanding to 96,623,857. Proceeds are expected to support construction and operations. Invictus projects combined cannabis production capacity of 262,000 square feet by year-end 2018 and 846,000 square feet by year-end 2019.

The company has approximately 9.9 million warrants and 9.4 million options outstanding, which could provide an additional $19.7 million and $14.9 million, respectively. It also granted 120,000 incentive stock options at $1.50 each, vesting in thirds over 15 months and exercisable for five years.

Invictus operates licensed cannabis facilities in Alberta and Ontario through Acreage Pharms and AB Labs, holds land for future cultivation through AB Ventures, and has a binding letter of intent involving OptionCo in British Columbia. Its other businesses include Poda Technologies, which developed a zero-cleaning vaporizer system, and Future Harvest Development, a fertilizer and nutrients manufacturer. The release cautions that projected capacity, funding use, regulatory approvals and timelines are forward-looking and subject to risks and uncertainties.

The 4-Verticals concept is a full-field passing play designed to stretch defenses vertically and horizontally while allowing quarterbacks to throw downfield quickly. All four receivers release vertically to create one-on-one matchups or occupy open zones. It is most effective against man coverage, where quarterbacks can target favorable matchups, and Cover 3, where looking off the safety opens seam windows over linebacker level. It is less effective against Cover 4, because deep defenders cover the quarters, and soft zone coverage, where timing becomes difficult and more horizontal concepts may be preferable.

Assignments vary by defensive look. Against two-high safeties, the slot receiver may cross the field safety; against one-high coverage, he works the seam, while outside receivers run go routes and convert to comeback routes if separation is not achieved at 15 yards. Quarterbacks must identify safeties, coverage type, and matchups before the snap, look off safeties, find a downfield matchup or zone void, and check down to the running back. Variations from 3x1 or empty formations preserve receiver landmarks while creating reads against safeties, blitzes, and coverage that drops deeper.

Yunnan Lucky Air, a Kunming-based low-cost airline founded in 2004, modeled its operations on Southwest Airlines. It grew rapidly, serving 1.2 million passengers and generating US$104.3 million in revenue in 2007, becoming profitable within three years. Its routes initially exploited its near-monopoly within Yunnan, but it later expanded beyond the province.

China’s aviation market was growing rapidly, although regulation and intensifying competition constrained airlines. Lucky Air’s costs were only about 5% below industry averages because government controls affected fuel prices, landing fees, aircraft leasing, taxes, ticket pricing, and distribution costs. Most tickets were sold through agents, while only 1% of all tickets were purchased directly by consumers on luckyair.net.

China’s e-commerce sector was still developing. Internet penetration, credit-card use, online banking, and online purchasing were low, particularly in Yunnan, and online travel represented less than 1% of the travel market. Ctrip and eLong dominated online travel distribution.

Lucky Air’s IT-supported website offered online ticket purchasing, refunds, validation, flight information, destination content, a passenger community, and loyalty rewards. It enabled fully online transactions without a call-center back end and offered lower fares, but attracted few direct consumers. Lucky Air nevertheless viewed it as a way to increase brand recognition, build loyalty, and gain an advantage over competitors.

Research on U.S. and European airlines highlighted customer relationship management, Web 2.0 communities, customer reviews, conversion optimization, self-service, alternative online payment methods such as PayPal, and targeted offerings for corporate travelers, students, and loyalty-program members. With airport expansion and potential regulatory easing promising growth, Lucky Air considered whether to pursue e-commerce leadership, bundled tour packages, or other strategies, requiring careful investment in technology and staff amid intensifying competition.

Brent Honeywell allowed four hits, struck out seven and issued no walks over six scoreless innings as Triple-A Durham shut out Columbus 11-0. Rays prospect Brent Honeywell earned praise for his command, changeup, count control and ability to adjust his delivery. The 2014 first-round pick has made 11 starts for Durham, recording a 4.22 ERA, 1.32 WHIP and 71 strikeouts. Brad Boxberger struck out three in the seventh before Ryne Stanek and Adam Kolarek completed the shutout. Wilson Ramos caught seven innings and went 1-for-3, while Shane Peterson drove in two runs and finished a triple short of the cycle.

Education Department restarted forgiveness for some IBR borrowers who paid on time for 25 years. Borrowers could opt out by Oct. 21, with discharges generally processed within two weeks; a shutdown may delay processing.

The president announced an accelerated withdrawal of U.S. troops from Vietnam, bringing 100,000 additional soldiers home between May 1 and December 1. Total withdrawals would reach 365,000, more than two-thirds of the 540,000 troops present when he took office. He attributed this progress to “Vietnamization,” the strengthening of South Vietnamese forces, and operations in Cambodia and Laos, which he said reduced enemy supply capabilities without delaying withdrawals or increasing American casualties.

He called on Hanoi to begin serious negotiations, accept an immediate cease-fire, and release all prisoners of war unconditionally. While affirming the goal of complete American withdrawal, he opposed announcing a fixed deadline, arguing that it would surrender a bargaining advantage, increase risks to remaining U.S. forces, and potentially enable a Communist takeover of South Vietnam.

Acknowledging reports of atrocities, he defended the broader character of American servicemen and cited their humanitarian work in South Vietnam. He described the war’s end as necessary to secure peace, honor U.S. sacrifices, and give South Vietnam a chance to determine its future. Recalling Medal of Honor recipient Sergeant Karl Taylor, he emphasized ending the war in a way that might allow future generations to live without war.

Researchers from the University of Washington, Texas A&M University and the Western Australian Museum discovered a new genus and species of clingfish, the duckbilled clingfish (*Nettorhamphos radula*), after finding two preserved specimens collected off southern Australia. The finger-sized fish has a broad, flat snout and an estimated 1,800–2,300 backward-pointing conical teeth—about ten times those of other known clingfishes. Its unusual jaw and teeth justified placement in a new genus.

Because the only known specimens could not be dissected, researchers used CT scanning to examine their skeletons, mouths and jaws noninvasively. Digital scans also enabled enlarged 3-D prints for analysis. The species was described in *Copeia* on April 14.

Clingfish can use suction to hold up to 150 times their body weight, and researchers hope studies of their biomechanics may aid surgical device design and whale tagging and tracking. The discovery also demonstrated the value of museum collections in identifying previously unknown species. The work was funded by the National Science Foundation.

Lattice Semiconductor shows early signs of a revenue rebound, driven by data-center strength and opportunities in high-end chips for robotics, vision systems, and security, while automotive and industrial markets remain weak. Inventories are gradually normalizing, cash generation is strong, the company has no debt, and Q3 guidance implies further growth. The author raised the target price to $70 but retained a HOLD rating because of the expensive valuation and thin margin of safety. LSCC designs low-power programmable chips, including FPGAs, for multiple industries. The article also describes the author’s growth-focused analysis approach and provides standard position, compensation, and risk disclosures.

During finals, Lehigh’s libraries become crowded, leaving some students stressed and unable to find quiet study spaces. After FML added tables and open space on its sixth floor, students have increasingly sought private alternatives, including academic buildings, nearby cafes and libraries. Some arrive early, while others reserve study rooms through the Center for Career and Professional Development, which offers coffee and snacks and can reduce stress. FML will remain open 24 hours daily from Dec. 11 at 7:45 a.m. through Dec. 20 at 10 p.m.; Packard Lab, the University Center, Rauch and Williams will also extend their hours. Final exams are held Dec. 12–20.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and energy-storage products and operates as a single reportable segment focused on electric vehicles. It sells Model S and Model X vehicles directly through company-owned stores, galleries and service centers and supports them through a global Supercharger network.

Model S deliveries began in June 2012, and more than 107,000 had been delivered worldwide by year-end 2015. It offered range of up to 288 miles under the U.S. EPA combined city/highway test, performance and all-wheel-drive options, advanced autopilot features and over-the-air updates. Model X customer deliveries began in the third quarter of 2015; the seven-seat SUV offered up to 257 miles of range and production was being expanded in the United States, with European and Asian sales planned for 2016. Tesla planned to unveil the lower-priced Model 3 in early 2016 and begin production and deliveries in late 2017.

Tesla’s technology included proprietary battery packs, power electronics, motors, gearboxes, control and infotainment software, dual-motor all-wheel-drive systems and autopilot hardware. It also sold the 7 kWh and 10 kWh Powerwall and 100 kWh Powerpack under the Tesla Energy brand. Vehicles were manufactured in Fremont and Lathrop, California, and Tilburg, Netherlands, while the Gigafactory near Reno, Nevada, integrated battery-material, cell, module and pack production. Tesla and Panasonic partnered on the Gigafactory, which was expected to reach full production capacity in 2020, with sufficient capacity for approximately 500,000 vehicles annually and 50 GWh of battery-pack production.

At December 31, 2015, Tesla operated 208 sales and service locations, including 118 service locations, and had opened 584 Supercharger stations worldwide. More than 3,100 wall connectors were installed at over 1,800 destination locations. Tesla had 13,058 full-time employees and offered vehicle warranties, maintenance plans, financing, leasing and resale-value guarantees.

Principal risks included delays or cost overruns in producing Model X and Model 3; uncertain consumer acceptance; battery safety and product defects; dependence on single-source suppliers and Panasonic for battery cells; Gigafactory execution; raw-material and labor costs; foreign-exchange exposure; residual-value and credit risks from leasing; product-liability claims; volatile demand and intense competition; difficulties expanding service and charging infrastructure internationally; reduced government incentives; and reliance on key personnel, particularly Elon Musk and JB Straubel.

The statistical analysis plan specifies that 12-lead ECG investigator assessments will be classified as normal, clinically significant abnormal, or abnormal but not clinically significant and summarized with counts and percentages. ECG parameters will be described by treatment group and visit, with categorical QTcF summaries reporting patients above 450, 480, and 500 ms and postbaseline changes greater than 30 and 60 ms.

ADA occurrence will be analyzed descriptively by treatment group without statistical tests. Overall ADA incidence will include treatment-induced ADA, defined as baseline-negative to post-treatment-positive status, and treatment-boosted ADA, defined as at least a fivefold titer increase in baseline-positive patients. The denominator will be evaluable patients with an appropriate post-treatment sample; baseline-positive patients without post-treatment samples will be excluded. Results from unscheduled dosing visits must also be considered.

Changes from the protocol include reworded primary-efficacy analysis, added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and replacement of secondary-efficacy terminology from “within” specified minutes to “at” specified minutes.

The appendices specify presentation and programming standards, including permitted characters, table and listing organization, decimal and percentage precision, zero-count categories, source and program-information footnotes, figure legends, and standard sorting, date, and time formats. Conservative rules will apply to missing or incomplete dates. Derived variables include durations, converted height, weight, and temperature, BMI, and change from baseline. SAS QC requirements cover program documentation, log and output review, Pinnacle 21 validation, dataset and listing checks, patient spot-checks, figure-to-table comparisons, population-total verification, and retention of validation evidence and QC status documentation.

Planned outputs include plasma-glucose recovery summaries, Kaplan–Meier curves, sensitivity analyses, histograms, recovery rates and glucose analyses at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes; adverse-event, serious-adverse-event, ECG, laboratory, vital-sign, local-tolerability, and ADA summaries; PK/PD concentration tables and figures for dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and glucose; and supporting listings for disposition, demographics, medical and diabetes history, concomitant medication, exclusions, compliance, drug concentrations, samples, laboratory measurements, and adverse events.

Scientists are increasingly examining whether highly engineered ultraprocessed foods can produce addictive effects resembling those of alcohol, nicotine and opioids. Concentrated sugars, fats and salts, flavor additives, appealing textures and packaging may stimulate the brain’s reward system, contributing to cravings, loss of control, withdrawal and tolerance. Animal and human studies have found neurochemical, structural and brain-activity changes similar to those associated with addictive substances, although researchers still debate terminology, individual risk and how well the addiction framework applies.

Using the NOVA classification system, ultraprocessed foods include products such as hot dogs and potato chips. They now account for more than half of calories consumed in the United States, and their share of calories consumed at home rose from about 51% in 2003 to just over 54% in 2018. They also overlap substantially with “hyperpalatable” foods engineered to be especially appealing, and studies of children’s cereals have found declines in fiber and protein alongside increases in fat, salt and sugar.

On the Yale Food Addiction Scale, about 14% of adults and 12% of children meet criteria for food addiction, while preliminary research found that ultraprocessed diets increased consumption among 18- to 21-year-olds, including when they were not hungry. Nonetheless, substance use disorders involve broader behavioral, emotional and social factors, and the proposed DSM-5 criteria for food addiction remain debated.

Policy responses under consideration include federal scrutiny, school restrictions, improved labeling, taxes and marketing limits. Chile’s package warnings, taxes and marketing restrictions have shifted purchases toward products with less sugar, salt, saturated fat and calories. Experts argue that an addiction lens may require protecting people from harmful products rather than relying solely on individual dietary advice.

The 2018 Nuclear Posture Review updates US nuclear policy by modernizing command systems, infrastructure, bombers and dual-capable aircraft, and adding low-yield warhead options, including modified SLBM warheads and a planned nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. It emphasizes flexible and extended deterrence, arms control, non-proliferation, nuclear counterterrorism and the testing moratorium, while ruling out nuclear threats against compliant non-nuclear NPT states. The review cites Russia, China, North Korea and Iran as threats and notes Russia’s nuclear escalation strategies; Pakistan is not discussed.

Canada’s federal government and all 14 provincial and territorial jurisdictions agreed to a two-year framework giving provinces and territories 75% of legalized marijuana tax revenue. Ottawa will retain 25%, up to $100 million annually, with any excess going to the provinces. The revenue will help cover municipal costs, including law enforcement, although each province will decide how to allocate its share. The government expects about $400 million in tax revenue during the first two years and will reassess the agreement in December 2018. Provinces may also set markups above the federal taxation model. The deal is intended to keep prices low and reduce the black market over time. Ministers also discussed equalization payments, the Canada Pension Plan review, the global economy, and measures to improve corporate ownership information and combat financial crime.

ANU and the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris used experiments and computer modelling to find that alumino-silicate glass has organized structures at the nanometre scale. Sodium and potassium atoms form clusters and percolation channels, while calcium, magnesium and other elements affect flexibility, fracture resistance and how cracks begin or stop. The findings could help manufacturers develop more fracture-resistant phone screens as Samsung prepares foldable devices and glass-bodied iPhones raise durability and repair concerns.

The address outlines an extensive federal program. It pledges to continue the predecessor’s reforms against abuses of power by railroad and industrial combinations, while easing certain antitrust restrictions on legitimate business. It proposes federal oversight of railroad bond and stock issuance, coordinated enforcement among the Department of Justice, Bureau of Corporations, and Interstate Commerce Commission, and legislation distinguishing legitimate combinations from monopolies designed to control prices.

Tariff revision is presented as the most immediate priority. The administration plans to call Congress into an extra session on March 15 to revise the Dingley Act, provide adequate revenue, protect domestic industries by tariff differentials, and authorize higher tariffs against countries with discriminatory trade policies. A projected $100 million federal deficit requires increased revenue, potentially including a graduated inheritance tax if import duties are insufficient. The address stresses economy while warning against cutting expenditures needed for an effective government.

Federal responsibilities include agricultural research, regulation of large businesses, conservation of forests and waterways, and completion of the Panama Canal. Permanent works such as the canal and major river improvements could be financed through bonds, distributing costs between present and future beneficiaries. Expenditures on a capable army, navy, and coastal defenses are also defended as necessary to protect American rights, influence, and international interests despite the country’s preference for peace.

The administration favors arbitration and peaceful international cooperation but believes strong armed forces are necessary to deter exploitation of the United States. It also seeks federal enforcement of treaty rights for aliens, protection of Americans abroad from racial and religious discrimination, and continued regulation of Asian immigration while minimizing friction and preventing violence against treaty-protected foreigners.

Domestic financial reforms will seek greater currency elasticity to reduce the danger of financial panics. Congress is also urged to establish a postal savings bank that would guarantee deposits, attract savings at low interest, and increase capital available for investment. The administration plans to encourage foreign trade through direct steamship lines, expanded commerce with the Orient, South America, and the Philippines, and use of the tariff’s minimum and maximum provisions against foreign trade discrimination.

The lock design of the Panama Canal is reaffirmed, and the administration vows to support its prompt completion. Free trade with the Philippines is expected to improve conditions there while limiting injury to domestic sugar and tobacco interests. Progress is also reported in Puerto Rico and in the expansion of civil liberties and popular control in both dependencies.

On Southern and racial issues, the address calls for observance of the Fifteenth Amendment, fair enforcement of voting protections, and state electoral qualifications consistent with the Constitution. Voting may be withheld from ignorant and unqualified people of any race. The administration urges greater Black industrial education, economic progress, and civic participation, while advocating careful use of appointments to avoid intensifying racial hostility and rejecting federal interference with compliant state regulation.

Labor policy supports expanded protections for railroad and government employees, including compensation for injuries, comparative-negligence rules, child-labor restrictions, arbitration, and railway safety devices. The government should bear responsibility comparable to that of interstate railroad employers for employees injured in its service. The address also defends federal courts’ authority to issue injunctions in labor disputes, rejects making secondary boycotts lawful, and supports statutory limits on temporary restraining orders issued without notice.

Moody’s is expected to keep South Africa’s local- and foreign-currency debt at its lowest investment-grade level this week, reflecting improved confidence following Cyril Ramaphosa’s leadership. All 15 economists and analysts surveyed by Bloomberg said the country would likely avoid a junk rating, while S&P and Fitch downgraded it last year. However, weak growth, missed fiscal targets and proposed expropriation without compensation could trigger a later downgrade. A junk rating could exclude South Africa from major bond indexes, risk capital outflows of up to 100 billion rand and increase borrowing costs.

The paper presents AMR-EnsembleNet, a genomic antimicrobial-resistance prediction framework designed to combine local SNP sequence context with complex feature interactions. It uses the GieSSen dataset of 809 E. coli isolates, each represented by 60,936 ordered SNP features, to predict resistance to ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and gentamicin. Resistant-class proportions range from 23.24% for gentamicin to 45.24% for ciprofloxacin.

The framework combines a lightweight 1D CNN with XGBoost through unweighted soft voting. The CNN embeds nucleotide tokens, applies six hierarchical convolutional blocks to learn local genomic motifs, and uses global max pooling and an MLP head for classification. XGBoost captures non-local interactions among SNP features. These models were compared with each other and with Random Forest using stratified splits, class weighting, and multiple classification metrics.

AMR-EnsembleNet matched the highest accuracy for ciprofloxacin and achieved the best reported results for cefotaxime, including resistant-class recall of 0.8611. For gentamicin, it achieved the highest Matthews correlation coefficient (0.4030) and macro F1-score (0.6908), balancing the CNN’s high recall with XGBoost’s higher precision. For ceftazidime, Random Forest performed best, while the ensemble provided a more balanced result than its individual components.

SHAP analysis of XGBoost identified influential SNPs and mapped them to AMR-associated genes, including gyrB, marR, rpsL, parC, fusA, ampC, acrD, and ftsI. The authors propose extending the framework to quantitative MIC regression, integrating transcriptomic data, and applying advanced explainability methods to the CNN to support marker discovery. Code and data are publicly available.

The dollar rose broadly Monday as investors unwound bearish positions after easing U.S.-North Korea tensions, with the dollar index up 0.3%. Gains in U.S. and global equities also supported the currency, while investors awaited Tuesday’s U.S. retail sales report for inflation clues.

Saskatoon proposes spending $1.2 million over two years to remove and replace black ash trees damaged by European cottony ash psyllids. After insecticides failed to slow the decline, the plan calls for removing about 1,000 affected trees and replacing them with other species; 92 trees have already been removed in three business districts and 29 along 22nd Street this year. First-year funding of $757,000 comes from reserve funds, while $423,000 for the second year has not been identified. The invasive lice, present in the city since 2006 and again since 2015, defoliate trees and are identified by white cotton on leaves and curled or discolored foliage.

Gary Gensler reviews student papers, emphasizing critical reasoning rather than summarizing readings or study questions, and notes that class participation accounts for 30% of the grade. He then outlines three themes: financial institutions, regulation, and technology.

Finance intermediates money and risk by allocating, moving, and pricing both. Its functions include capital allocation, market making, payments, liquidity provision, storing value, and credit. Key sectors include commercial and investment banks, brokerages, insurance, asset management, collective investment vehicles, exchanges, and clearinghouses. Gensler distinguishes primary markets, where securities are first issued, from secondary markets, where existing securities are traded; secondary markets generally have greater volume, while primary markets can offer more profit opportunities.

Ledgers record economic transactions and financial relationships and are embedded throughout finance. Payment systems transfer value by authorizing transactions, clearing them, and amending or recording them in ledgers. Because blockchain’s immutability is most relevant to records of value, Gensler sees potential applications in more immediate or final settlement, while expressing skepticism about uses unrelated to ledgers.

Gensler describes regulation as a centuries-long response to finance’s economic centrality. Its traditional priorities include financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and, more recently, illicit financial activity. Financial instability arises partly because leveraged intermediaries hold mostly financial assets and can amplify economic cycles. Consolidation and regulation raise concerns about market power, “too big to fail,” and moral hazard, illustrated by discussion of Citigroup and Sheila Bair’s view that it might have been restructured or allowed to fail. Regulation tends to tighten after crises and ease during later periods.

Technology and finance have long interacted, from carrier-pigeon trading to electronic records, cryptography, and blockchain. Large incumbents’ reliance on legacy systems may create opportunities for targeted blockchain-based disruptors. Gensler identifies AI, machine learning, biometrics, open banking, big data, robotic process automation, cloud computing, open APIs, and chatbots as financial technologies. Fiat currency is described as a liability of commercial banks supported by central-bank and reserve-account ledgers.

Credit is borrowing value with an agreement to repay. Gensler presents U.S. debt, bond, equity, and household-debt figures to illustrate the scale of modern credit markets, noting that mortgage and student debt are major household obligations. He discusses market, credit, underwriting, operational, counterparty, human-capital, cyber, legal, compliance, reputational, political, and expropriation risks, with liquidity, funding, settlement, and model or correlation risks especially important during crises.

For the 2008 financial crisis, Gensler identifies weak underwriting, predatory lending, a housing bubble, prolonged easy credit and low interest rates, leverage through credit-default swaps, model-based capital rules, poor risk management, asymmetric compensation incentives, and conflicts involving rating agencies. He says some risks were known but insufficiently addressed, while other harmful practices went unnoticed. He later notes that banks have more capital and are stronger than before the crisis, but high asset valuations, concentration, and unequal economic gains remain concerns. The policy choice between supporting large institutions and individuals remains contested.

For blockchain projects, Gensler emphasizes data-intensive uses, potential economic rents, concentrated risks, and infrastructure costs. He closes by previewing a guest lecture and a discussion of blockchain economics, including readings critical of the technology.

The study investigates liquid-assisted capillary densification as a scalable method for strengthening electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns. Loosely assembled yarns were rolled with water or ethanol, dried, and optionally annealed at 110 °C for 5 hours. SEM-based Fourier and OrientationJ analyses quantified fiber alignment, while binary image analysis measured in-plane packing density. Tensile tests at a strain rate of approximately \(1.5\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\) assessed mechanical response.

All yarns exhibited five deformation regimes: geometric uncrimping, linear elasticity, nonlinear transition through fiber recruitment, an extended stress plateau, and progressive failure. Liquid treatment increased stiffness and strength but reduced failure strain. Water-treated yarns generally performed best because water’s slower evaporation and stronger capillary forces promoted greater compaction than ethanol, whose rapid evaporation limited consolidation and whose induced fiber swelling reduced intrinsic strength. Annealing created fused fiber junctions and further increased stiffness and strength but caused abrupt, brittle failure at roughly 15% strain.

Mechanical performance increased strongly as yarn diameter decreased; yarns below 10 μm approached the stiffness and strength of individual PAN nanofibers. In segments cut from one parent yarn, water-treated and water-plus-heat-treated specimens carried median peak loads near 9–10 mN, compared with approximately 5–6 mN for untreated yarn, representing about a 70% increase. ANOVA confirmed a significant treatment effect, with treatment explaining about 34% of peak-load variance.

Fiber alignment and packing density each correlated strongly with peak load (\(R^2=0.68\) and 0.75, respectively), while a combined regression achieved \(R^2=0.80\), indicating complementary effects: tighter packing increased inter-fiber contact and load transfer, whereas better alignment distributed strain and reduced stress concentrations.

A stochastic mean-field constitutive model incorporated Weibull-distributed fiber recruitment and failure, elastic-perfectly plastic behavior, orientation averaging, packing-dependent load-transfer efficiency, and post-failure load retention. The model reproduced the observed nonlinear stress–strain regimes and linked its inferred microstructure parameters closely to SEM-measured packing and alignment (\(R^2=0.91\)). The results provide a quantitative process–structure–mechanics framework for tailoring electrospun yarn strength and ductility.

Physicists developed a method for making mixed, immiscible liquids self-organize into patterned droplets. By confining oil, water, and alcohol in droplets or thin straws, researchers induced de-mixing to proceed inward, producing tunable stripes and enabling stepwise release of inner droplets. Their model matched experimental data and predicted layer lifetimes, potentially supporting advances in pharmaceuticals and other emulsion-based products.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Jose Verastegui’s convictions and concurrent 120-month sentences for felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry. The court found no abuse of discretion in the upward departure under U.S.S.G. § 4A1.3 or the variance under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a), despite an advisory guideline range of 63–78 months. His guideline-calculation challenge was foreclosed by circuit precedent. His constitutional challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) were also foreclosed, but he raised them to preserve them for Supreme Court review. The opinion was designated nonprecedential.

OnePlus began the global Android Nougat rollout for the 3 and 3T, with broader availability expected within two days. Both receive identical builds featuring redesigned menus, multi-window support, and notification replies.

The Enjifit workout-partner app launched for iOS on July 3, 2018, connecting users with nearby partners and personal trainers who share similar goals and interests. Features include user filtering, messaging, workout reminders, accomplishment tracking, posting sessions, and finding people ready to work out within the next hour. The app is free, with a monthly PRO subscription for trainers and nutritionists to feature their services. Founder Nicole Garcia hosted a July 1 launch event for more than 150 attendees, and an Android version is planned.

The lecture introduces the nuclear force as the residual strong interaction between quarks in different hadrons and describes it using a mean-field approach. Experimental information comes from nucleon–nucleon scattering, binding energies, precise nuclear masses, and nuclear structure data such as energy levels, spins, parities, and electromagnetic moments. The force depends on nucleon separation, spin, and angular momentum, with spin-orbit and tensor components. It is short range, vanishing beyond about 2 femtometers, and strongly repulsive below about 0.5 femtometers. Binding-energy scaling, reaction distances, and nuclear densities indicate dense packing and interactions mainly among nearby nucleons. The force is charge independent, as proton-proton, proton-neutron, and neutron-neutron scattering agree after electromagnetic contributions are subtracted. Comparisons of mirror nuclei can therefore probe charge-independence corrections and help determine properties of unstable nuclei that decay too quickly for direct study.

Independent developer Milky Tea announced that HyperBrawl Tournament will launch on Steam Early Access in June 2017. The combat sports arena game combines no-rules, high-speed handball with competitive PvP combat. Players select from 10 warriors and 10 weapons, battle in six featured arenas, and compete in eight mini-games to improve skills and unlock skins, weapons, and characters. It supports local and online multiplayer for up to four players in 1v1 and 2v2 tournaments, with rage attacks, special aftertouch abilities, and potential as an esports party game.
Pepsi Nigeria’s “No Shakin’ Carry Go” campaign will send 10 fans on an all-expenses-paid, three-day VIP trip to the One Africa Music Fest in Dubai in November.

The disclosure describes a machine-learned system for estimating a scene’s depth map from a single color image using models trained with monocular video, stereoscopic image pairs, or both. Training uses depth and pose models to generate synthetic frames, then minimizes per-pixel photometric reconstruction errors to refine model parameters. For monocular video, adjacent frames are projected onto a target frame; for stereoscopic pairs, each image is projected onto the other. The loss can use the minimum or average error from multiple projections, upsampled depth features, and masks that discount static features to reduce occlusion, motion, border, and texture artifacts. Depth and pose estimation may be separate or implemented as a shared-parameter hybrid model.

A trained model can receive an image, optionally with camera intrinsics, and output per-pixel depth or disparity values. In a location-based parallel reality game, a game server trains and distributes the model to client devices. Client devices capture monocular or stereoscopic imagery, track real-world player locations, and map those locations to a virtual world. Depth information supports generation of virtual content and augmented real-world imagery, such as characters that move behind or interact with physical objects. The game system includes client-server networking, game data storage, positioning and gaming modules, and modules for universal gameplay, commercial activities, data collection, events, and depth-model training.

Technology megacaps lost $770 billion in market value as the Nasdaq fell 3.6% and the S&P 500 dropped 2.7%, their worst day since April. Nvidia, Amazon and Tesla each declined about 5% following President Trump’s threat to sharply increase tariffs on Chinese products. After Friday’s close, Trump announced a 100% tariff on China and export controls on critical software; the three stocks then fell about 2% in extended trading. Nvidia lost nearly $229 billion in value, Microsoft $85 billion and Amazon $121 billion, briefly disrupting a sustained technology-stock rally.

An Accenture survey of 1,300 investors found that clients across ages and wealth levels prefer hybrid wealth management combining robo advisers with human expertise, especially for complex situations, while expecting rapidly evolving online tools.

Kennesaw State won the 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan, edging Lipscomb by one shot. Jake Fendt and Pablo Rodriguez-Tabernero tied for second at 2-under, and the Owls secured an NCAA regional berth for a seventh straight year. Lipscomb’s Dawson Armstrong won the individual title at 6-under 210, following an opening 70 with a 69 and three final-day birdies. It was his sixth college victory, and he was named ASUN Player of the Year in consecutive seasons. Jacksonville finished third at 5-over and North Florida fourth at 7-over, with both considered likely NCAA regional recipients.
Episode four of UFC 216 Embedded documents fighters’ preparations, a children’s cancer center visit, media day interviews, and faceoffs ahead of the October 7 event.

On April 13, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of seven series of registered notes: $1.5 billion of 2.730% notes due 2024; $1.5 billion of 3.000% notes due 2025; $2 billion of 3.300% notes due 2027; $1.5 billion of 3.450% notes due 2029; $2.5 billion of 3.600% notes due 2032; $2.5 billion of 3.950% notes due 2052; and $1.25 billion of 4.100% notes due 2062. The offering had an aggregate public offering price of $12.719 billion and estimated net proceeds of approximately $12.692 billion before offering expenses. Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Morgan Stanley served as underwriters. The notes were issued under Amazon’s 2012 base indenture, as supplemented by an April 13, 2022 supplemental indenture naming Computershare Trust Company as successor trustee. North Wales Police are seeking witnesses after a man attempted to force a woman in her 30s into a car on Sisson Street, Rhyl, at 8.25am. She escaped unharmed; the man, described as being in his 40s and of oriental appearance, fled in a silver vehicle. Police consider the incident isolated and the motive unknown. Alerts initially sent to schools and parents after a child was mistakenly believed involved were later confirmed unnecessary.

Pupils asked President Mnangagwa to suspend the November 2018 public examinations because teachers’ electoral duties disrupted their preparation. His response was not disclosed. Schools were asked to provide holiday lessons and open the third term early on September 4 to recover lost teaching time.

In July 2015, NASA’s New Horizons became the first spacecraft to fly by Pluto. Its extended mission targets Kuiper Belt Objects, with a planned Jan. 1, 2019 encounter with 2014 MU69, nicknamed “Ultima Thule.” Located about 1.6 billion kilometers beyond Pluto, MU69 was selected for its research opportunities and fuel efficiency. The object may be a single elongated body, a close binary, or multiple objects. “Ultima Thule” is a working name; NASA and the New Horizons team will submit a formal name to the International Astronomical Union after the flyby.

Exome sequencing was used to characterize clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) in 454,803 UK Biobank participants and 173,585 Geisinger MyCode participants, identifying 27,331 and 12,877 CHIP carriers, respectively, across 23 recurrently mutated genes. CHIP prevalence increased with age and was associated with heavy smoking. Common-variant analyses identified 27 susceptibility loci, including 24 novel loci, while rare-variant and gene-burden analyses implicated 20 variants and five genes, including ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2. Most signals replicated in the second cohort.

Gene-specific analyses demonstrated shared, subtype-specific, and opposing genetic effects. Protective variants in PARP1 and LY75 were associated specifically with DNMT3A-CHIP, while the TCL1A locus increased DNMT3A-CHIP risk but reduced several other CHIP subtypes. CHIP shared germline risk factors with mosaic loss of sex chromosomes but remained largely distinct from mosaic chromosomal alterations. Exome analyses also identified novel rare-variant associations for mosaic phenotypes and telomere length.

Phenotype-wide analyses found subtype-specific associations with hematologic, cardiovascular, neoplastic, infectious, endocrine, ophthalmologic, and adiposity traits. High-VAF CHIP was associated with severe COVID-19, modestly increased cardiovascular disease risk, substantially increased blood and myeloid cancer risk, increased lung cancer risk in smokers and nonsmokers, and elevated all-cause mortality. TET2 mutations drove much of the cardiovascular and blood-cancer risk, whereas DNMT3A-only CHIP was not associated with incident lymphoid cancer; DNMT3A was associated with solid tumors. A DNMT3A polygenic risk score predicted several cancers and multiple CHIP subtypes. Overall, CHIP was characterized as a heterogeneous composite of somatic-mutation subtypes with shared genetic etiology but distinct clinical risk profiles.

Attacking runs are spontaneous off-ball movements by offensive players into open space among, between, or behind defenders to receive a pass. Unlike designed runs for crosses or planned runs for set plays, they arise from immediate decision-making. Effective runs depend on recognizing or creating open space, choosing an appropriate route, breaking away from a defender, reaching open space, proper timing, receiving a suitable pass, and communication.

Run selection should advance the attack, create a shot opportunity, and make the pass easier to complete. Common runs include bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, and wide runs. Runners should exploit a head start, keep defenders uncertain, use feints or sudden acceleration, and maintain separation. Timing must exploit space without leaving the runner offside; if the expected pass does not arrive, the runner should turn parallel to and in front of the next-to-last defender. The pass should match the anticipated space, direction, and speed of the run, and runners should complete initiated runs rather than stopping or changing direction abruptly. Teammates communicate through speech, hand signals, and eye contact, though nonverbal signals are less likely to alert defenders.

Coaching can progress from demonstrating and practicing each run with cones, to adding passes, stationary defenders, restricted defensive movement, additional attacking players, and finally full movement. Coaches should reward open teammates with accurate passes, discourage ball-watching and standing still, and teach support runs, deception, and give-and-go combinations.

The passage is a transcript of NHL draft-event interviews with several prospects in Columbus. James van Riemsdyk is asked about his New Jersey roots, the U.S. development program, Team USA, attending the University of New Hampshire, and potential draft teams. The Clock (1-3-1) offense attacks a Diamond & One defense by placing the star player in the middle, where the chaser’s emphasis on pass denial leaves them less prepared for post defense. The offense creates open looks, layups, offensive rebounds, and one-on-one post opportunities for the star.

Basic actions include corner pass-and-cut, post entry, quick ball reversals, post rolls, dribble clears, and high-post triangle action. Triangle action uses drop passes for layups, kick-out passes for open shots or dribble penetration, and middle flashes for shooting or passing. Players may use right- or left-side alignments and exchange positions through dribble clearing.

The inside triangle creates a three-on-two offensive rebounding advantage on outside shots, leading to putbacks and second efforts. The baseline player may also back-screen the star’s defender.

Successful execution requires coordination, communication, timing, and preparation for screens and post-ups. Coaches should scout opponents when possible, identify defensive reads and matchups, observe in-game adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and move players against weaker defenders.

Written by Uncapher and Kendall-Taylor, this commentary argues that education initiatives stall not because the ideas are bad but because their stories are never designed. Illustrating with a district AI pilot that parents framed as "surveillance" and voted down, the authors trace similar patterns in No Child Left Behind, Race to the Top, and Common Core, identifying three default stories: top-down control, data equals danger, and tech replacing people.

The piece proposes treating narrative as designable, using a Frame → Test → Iterate → Scale cycle: clarify core ideas and map how audiences already make sense of the topic; build values, metaphors and explanations and pressure-test them through street interviews, small-group conversations and surveys; refine through co-design with teachers, principals, parents and students; and package the strategy into toolkits, visuals, model language, training and coaching.

Suggested applications include reframing standards and testing around "clear signposts for students' future success" and casting AI as a "teaching assistant" rather than a monitor. Other guidance: lead with widely shared values, give people tested metaphors they can picture, explain the mechanism from cause to effect, center teachers and students so technology is the helper, name and neutralize risks with guardrails, and avoid "silver bullet," crisis-only and "us vs. them" framing.

The authors conclude that innovation lacks narrative infrastructure, so districts should fund, time-box and test narrative prototyping alongside policies and programs, letting communities see safeguards and benefits and shifting debate toward how to do the work well.

The Las Vegas Aces rallied past the Phoenix Mercury 90-88 in Game 3 of the 2025 WNBA Finals, taking a 3-0 lead and moving within one win of a championship sweep. A’ja Wilson scored 34 points and grabbed 14 rebounds. The Aces credited their advantage to Becky Hammon’s varied defensive schemes, timely reserve contributions, and cohesion among Wilson, Jackie Young, Chelsea Gray and Jewell Loyd. After hovering near .500 early in the season, Las Vegas won 16 straight games before reaching the Finals. Phoenix, which entered the playoffs with momentum, has lost all three games and faces elimination Friday. Mercury forward Sabrina Sabally is out with a concussion.

The Texas Supreme Court issued a tentative opinion that the ABA "should no longer have the final say" on whether law school graduates may sit for the Texas bar exam, and solicited public comments by Dec. 1. The court plans no added accreditation burdens but may rely on another multi-state accreditor; the ABA is reviewing the order.
Akure-based lawyer Morakinyo Ogele gave the EFCC seven days to publicly apologize to Sun Newspaper management for invading its premises and pay N1 billion in compensation.

Guilford and Milford police are investigating repeated shoreline car break-ins and thefts, prompting residents to lock doors and use outdoor lights. Authorities say groups of youths target vehicles, sometimes steal keys and cards, and flee recklessly; two suspects are sought in Milford.

U.S. stock indexes fell as Trump threatened a 100% tariff on China starting November 1. The S&P 500 closed Friday at its lowest level since early July, down 1.6% and 3.33% over two days, but was expected to rebound Monday; futures traded near 6,300. The broader correction may persist, with earnings, stretched valuations, and macro risks prompting defensive positioning. The VIX reached 21.90, its highest since June 23. Oil fell as OPEC+ announced a 547,000-bpd September production increase, while weak jobs and PMI data, tariff uncertainty, and possible U.S. sanctions on Russian oil created competing concerns. Goldman Sachs forecast Q4 2025 oil at $64. Palantir and AMD earnings were highlighted, while investor sentiment remained slightly improved.

The coach said his team played well for much of the game and did a strong job defensively, but a five-on-three redirect off one of its defensemen changed the course of the game. The Penguins’ speed and ability to capitalize were credited, while Nashville continued to forecheck and create chances, including a late penalty-kill sequence that led to a loose puck and a quick pass to Freddy for a difficult shot. He praised Pekka as the team’s backbone and said he had delivered in previous big moments. The defensemen outside the top four were also praised for their consistent regular-season and playoff play and ability to handle top-line matchups. The coach said the team had gained valuable experience after an earlier loss to Chicago, maintained consistent preparation and routines, and learned to handle playoff pressure. He noted that speed becomes increasingly important in later rounds and praised Filip for maturing into a leader and difference-maker. Despite disliking the result, he said the loss reduced Nashville’s opportunities to win four games, making the next game important.

Output capacitance must meet both load-transient deviation and voltage-ripple limits, using the larger calculated value; at least 1.3 mF is required, with derating for aging, temperature, and DC bias. Space-grade SET mitigation may require additional capacitance, and 2.3 mF total was used. An optional LC filter can further reduce output noise and ripple, with resonance selected between crossover and the switching frequency/ESR zero and damping added for peaking. Cycle-by-cycle limiting starts near 35 A, about 45% above the 24.25 A peak inductor current; current-sense resistor calculations account for a 1:100 transformer ratio.

Congress convened in Philadelphia despite a contagious illness, and the president proposed an amendment authorizing postponement of future meetings when public health requires it. He expressed gratitude for domestic tranquillity, prosperity, civil and religious liberty, and support for national sovereignty.

Envoys to the French Republic proceeded to Paris to negotiate on terms compatible with U.S. safety, honor, and interests. Because European conflict and declining respect for treaties endangered American commerce, the president urged unity and continued military precautions, including national defense.

Spain had not completed its troop withdrawal and boundary demarcation under the treaty with the United States, requiring continued readiness to receive posts and survey the boundary. Foreign agents were attempting to turn Indian nations against the United States, prompting a recommendation for stronger punishment of such practices.

British and Spanish treaty commissions addressed disputed boundaries, British creditors’ claims, and American claims for wartime losses. British compensation awards to American claimants had been paid, while Congress needed to provide for U.S. compensation obligations to British subjects. French and Spanish seizures of American vessels had created consular expenses and hardship for stranded seamen. The consular law therefore required revision to improve support and return procedures and authorize inspection of ship registers and sea letters to detect forged American flags and papers.

For national defense and government, the president recommended funding these needs as much as possible through immediate taxes and as little as possible through loans. He closed by urging firmness and unity amid Europe’s threatening conditions.

An IWC report found 122 of 333 minke whales killed in Japan’s latest Antarctic hunt were pregnant and 114 were juveniles. After an ICJ ruling against “research whaling,” Japan cut its 2014 quota from 900 to 333.

A July 17, 2001 news digest covered Enron and the energy industry:

- California Secretary of State Bill Jones urged state authorities to investigate whether seven energy consultants violated conflict-of-interest rules through stockholdings and whether exemptions from disclosure requirements were lawful. The Davis administration disputed the allegations and said relevant consultants had been recused where necessary while the state reviewed past power purchases and contracts.
- The London Metal Exchange fined Enron Metals £190,000, or $264,000, for seriously inadequate compliance procedures, including late warrant deliveries and failure to enter trades into the matching system. Enron admitted the breaches and said it had cooperated and taken corrective steps.
- Terremark Worldwide reported a $103.9 million fiscal-year loss, warned that it needed additional financing, and received an auditors’ going-concern warning. Its Miami network access point had signed customers and generated revenue, but financing difficulties threatened planned expansion.
- A California Senate committee was expected to drop its contempt charge against Enron if the company supplied documents and signed a confidentiality agreement for an investigation into wholesale electricity pricing. Enron had also filed a lawsuit challenging the committee’s subpoena.
- SmartMoney.com investor-panel members shifted toward diversified portfolios after technology-stock losses, expressed skepticism toward Wall Street analysts, and generally did not expect a sustained market rally before the fourth quarter.
- The Alliance for Retail Energy Markets opposed California Assembly Bill ABX 2 82, arguing that it would suspend retail energy choice, benefit Edison and harm customers. 
- Dutch traders urged the electricity watchdog to require generators to disclose plant outages amid sharply rising spot prices, while generators resisted citing commercially sensitive information.
- Northwestern utilities, including Portland General Electric and Avista Energy, faced $611 million in claims that they had overcharged other regional providers during California’s energy crisis.
- India rejected a proposal for state-run National Thermal Power Corp. to buy Enron’s stake in Dabhol Power Co., citing the project’s losses. Dabhol’s construction had been halted after lenders stopped funding it, and its sole customer had stopped buying power amid unpaid bills.

This document outlines defensive tactics against the Power Offense, noting that continuous screening action means hung-up defenders create open shots for opposing shooters, and that "Bigs" screening for "Smalls" discourages switching because shooters would fade to the corners and the screener would post up against a smaller defender. Two approaches are described. Under "Show and Recover," defenders disrupt down and base screens by stepping out to force shooters wide, then quickly recovering to their assignments with three-quarter pass denial; defenders may also physically block baseline crossings, and the final matching-up phase has the ball handler pressured, the post defender denying entry or playing behind, weakside players packing toward the ball, and trapping post mismatches with a double team. Under "All Out SOS Disruption," the defense initiates action by trapping a wing shooter, forcing the offense into unplanned "free lance" play. The described phases include a sideline push to prevent mid penetration, inverting positions to keep bigs inside, contact switches on baseline and down screens with Snuggle denial, a wing double team, and rotations on the pass out of the trap, with base-go-I and base-go-red scenarios and basic SOS rules applying once screening begins.

Quantum-correlated phonon pairs are generated in an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity by implementing Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions simultaneously in one optical pulse. This effective high-order optomechanical spontaneous four-wave mixing process produces a degenerate correlated phonon pair, analogous to spontaneous parametric down-conversion. A second red-detuned pulse retrieves the pair, whose nonclassical correlations are verified using the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. Pulse-duration-dependent weight engineering controls the interaction’s linear and quadratic terms, demonstrating a route toward phonon-state resources for mechanical quantum computing.

Since Florida’s 2023 takeover of New College of Florida under Gov. Ron DeSantis, the college’s per-student spending has risen to roughly $134,000—more than ten times the State University System average—while graduation rates, retention and national rankings have declined. The college has nearly fallen 60 ranking positions among liberal arts colleges, prompting criticism of poor returns on state investment.

Faculty and alumni say the college is recruiting larger classes to replace departing students, has lost legislative support and may lack broad backing within the institution. Critics also contend that administrative changes, including reinstating grades, are weakening New College’s distinctive identity.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. An internal oscillator initiates the primary gate-drive output, while an external resistor senses switch current. The sensed signal is compared with a stepped-down COMP voltage, turning off the power switch when the threshold is reached. The controllers require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with GaN devices in buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters.

A TPS7H5001-SP example demonstrates a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter with 5 V output. Selected values include a 205 kΩ timing resistor, 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ output-feedback divider resistors, and 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns dead time. A 49.9 kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor provides an initial value of about 50 ns, subject to optimization for PCB parasitics, sensed-current spikes, and gate-driver delay. A 33 nF soft-start capacitor produces an approximately 7.5 ms soft start.

The transformer design targets a 35% duty-cycle limit for margin below the controller’s 50% limit, a 2.5 turns ratio, and magnetizing current equal to 6% of output current. The calculated primary inductance was 33 μH, but 40 μH was used. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a maximum 36 V input, while 80 V synchronous rectifier FETs are used despite an expected maximum stress of about 20 V. A parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start and dead-time conduction losses. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node voltage, with initial values requiring testing and optimization.

A 0.47 μH output inductor was selected for 40% ripple current. Output-capacitance calculations for 2% ripple and 2.5% maximum load-transient deviation required at least 1.3 mF; approximately 2.3 mF was used to provide additional single-event-transient mitigation. An optional output filter can reduce noise further, with resonant frequency selected appropriately and resistor damping available if peaking occurs.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25 A peak inductor current at maximum load. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5 Ω sense resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10 kHz crossover with a calculated power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. The design uses 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF compensation components and a 102 kΩ slope-compensation resistor; compensation may require tuning during testing.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least a 0.1 μF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor. X5R-or-better ceramic capacitors placed close to the controller are recommended, with additional bulk capacitance when the supply is remote.

Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and other noise-sensitive traces from power components and the high-dv/dt switch node, minimizing high-di/dt and high-dv/dt loop areas, separating analog AVSS from power ground except at a single connection point, using short and wide high-current traces, and placing filtering, bypass, compensation, and VSENSE components near their associated pins. High-dv/dt gate-drive traces should remain away from sensitive control signals, RC filtering may be needed at CS_ILIM, and CFP packages require multiple vias connecting the backside metallization to the AVSS plane.

Application curves show output soft-start at 10 A and a 5 A load-step response. Related documentation includes evaluation-module guides, radiation reports, and characterization reports. Revision F added QMLP options for TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP and introduced a SN0022HFT “no die” package option; Revision E added the TPS7H5001-SP QMLP option.

The study applies a sub-pixel shift-and-add reconstruction method to electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) patterns acquired using a 256 × 256-pixel, 55 µm Timepix-based direct electron detector. Patterns collected at sub-detector-pixel stage offsets were registered for scale, rotation, and translation, transformed into a common frame with bicubic interpolation, and summed to create a super-resolution pattern.

The reconstructed patterns contained more high-frequency information and achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of about 70 at an effective exposure time of one second, compared with a limiting value of approximately 30 for conventional single-frame or frame-integrated acquisition. A tenfold upsampled 2560 × 2560-pixel image reproduced fine diffraction features visible in camera-retracted data and a high-quality dynamical simulation, including higher-order Laue zone rings, additional poles, and fine band structure.

The method requires a common lattice and orientation across the mapped region, as demonstrated for a silicon single crystal. Proposed extensions include sub-pixel camera movements, stage movements, and other approaches for complex samples. The reconstruction can improve pattern indexing, strain and lattice-rotation measurements, unit-cell analysis, centrosymmetry evaluation, and resolution of pseudosymmetry issues, without hardware modification.

Based on a 2022 California Department of Education data request, interviews with staff from 12 districts, and a literature review, the report finds that California’s newcomers—students recently arrived in U.S. schools—have distinct academic, social-emotional, and material needs that are often obscured by treating them as English learners. Most have limited English proficiency, 67% are socioeconomically disadvantaged, and many have experienced interrupted schooling or trauma. Federal rulings guarantee English learners and immigrant minors access to a free, appropriately tailored public education, but many California districts appear unable to staff or support programs meeting the Castañeda standard.

California identified 151,996 Title III immigrant students in 2020–21, or 2.5% of its K–12 enrollment. Fifty-eight percent were enrolled in five urban counties, 43% had Spanish as their home language, and roughly nine in ten were likely English learners. Only 19% were in high school, although research and programs often focus on high school. The state lacks accessible newcomer and statewide SIFE data; Oakland Unified’s arrival-year and SIFE tracking system is presented as a promising local model.

California provides several state and federal supports, including LCFF funding, CalNEW, Opportunities for Youth, Title III, and refugee programs, but funding is insufficient and uneven. California ranks near the bottom nationally in education spending and had the nation’s highest teacher-to-student ratio in 2021. Title III’s enrollment-growth requirement left 77.6% of Title III immigrant students without Immigrant Student Program funding, including high-need districts such as Oakland.

Successful newcomer education combines specialized instruction with integration, collaboration, oral-language development, translanguaging, and grade-level content. Effective models also include extended learning time, modified schedules, robust enrollment intake, transcript articulation, welcoming environments, targeted social-emotional and mental-health support, family engagement, and partnerships providing legal, housing, food, and health services. Major gaps include inadequate curricula, insufficient teacher preparation and planning time, limited program capacity, and assessment and accountability systems poorly suited to newcomers’ language levels and varied educational histories.

The report recommends coordinated state, federal, nonprofit, and philanthropic action: establish state leadership capacity and structured CDE–CDSS collaboration; include newcomers and SIFE in state data systems; continue Opportunities for Youth; adjust LCFF funding for late-arriving students; direct the Instructional Quality Commission to address newcomer curricula; invest in open instructional resources and research; and advocate for federal inclusion of newcomers in data systems and removal of Title III’s growth requirement.

Red Same, Red Opposite, and Red Rover are brief SOS midcourt disruptions used to change tempo, create easy baskets, disrupt half-court offenses, and take the ball from a good penetrating point guard. They trap the ballhandler near the sideline hash mark, use Triangle I positioning, initiate nearest-player rotations as the passer releases the ball, and end with either Base Go I or Base Go Red as predetermined by the coach. The initial trap distinguishes each scenario: Red Same uses X1 with X3; Red Opposite uses X2 with X1; Red Rover 4 uses X4 with X1; and Red Rover 5 uses X5 with X1. After the ball escapes the trap, defenders close out, deny passes, front the low post, and release to the high post. Red Same and Red Opposite also include Post Front rotations when O2 feeds O4, while Red Opposite adds a smother against O2’s vision into the post.

Recruiters and hiring experts caution against using AI to write job descriptions, arguing it removes deep thinking about a role's needs and the human connection with candidates. She noted AI can help if recruiters already know whom they need to hire. Conversely, Xiid CEO Steve Visconti writes his own posting, generates an AI version, merges the two, and uses AI to fill gaps in required skills such as cloud native, Kubernetes, and OpenShift.

Astronomers led by Naoki Koshimoto used gravitational microlensing and multi-telescope follow-up observations to discover the super-Jupiter MOA-2016-BLG-227Lb. The planet has about 2.8 Jupiter masses and likely orbits an M- or K-dwarf star of roughly 0.29 solar masses in the Galactic bulge at approximately 1.67 AU. Its radius and orbital period remain undetermined. A Bayesian analysis combining light-curve data, the angular Einstein radius, and Keck images considered several possible sources of excess flux and found it unlikely that much of the excess came from the lens star. The event was detected by the MOA collaboration and followed up using UKIRT, CFHT, Keck II, VST, and C28 telescopes. The results were posted as arXiv:1704.01724, and researchers recommended further observations with HST, Keck adaptive optics, JWST, GMT, TMT, and ELT.
