Their annual return now delights birdwatchers, while immature eagles are often mistaken for golden eagles or hawks.

Residents of Oshiyie in the Greater Accra Region have petitioned the Inspector General of Police over unrest traced to an 18-year chieftaincy dispute between the Nii Afadi Annoh Royal Family faction and the Kofi Akrashie faction, a case before an Arbitration Committee of the Ngleshie Alata Traditional Council. The petition, filed by family head Abusuapayin Paul Ameni Annoh, alleges that the Akrashie faction violated an agreement not to sprinkle "Kpokpoi," later held a banned anniversary celebration, and on dates within a 10-day court-ordered ban rampaged through town, assaulting women, children and the elderly, destroying properties, and burning fishing nets and canoes. Named leaders Albert Akrashie Okine, Newland Ansah Baah and Amadu are cited in the attacks. Police arrests were made, but complainants say innocent members of the Nii Afadi Annoh faction were detained without bail and are being persecuted for a murder case. The petition also blames land guard Adjei Brown, accuses police investigators of bias, and requests intervention.

The Trump administration is weighing sales of parts of its $1.6 trillion federal student loan portfolio while pursuing the Education Department’s shutdown, which would require transferring the loans. The law reportedly permits sales only if taxpayers lose no money, but private loans may offer fewer protections, prompting criticism from borrower advocates.
A car bomb and gunmen attacked a Kabul ministry, killing at least one policeman and wounding five. Daesh claimed responsibility; Afghan forces stopped the attackers before they reached buildings.

The passage promotes a custom essay-writing service, claiming it provides affordable, high-quality, plagiarism-free papers, quick turnaround, and help with research and formatting. It notes that students regularly complete essays and research papers, which can be frustrating and exhausting.

Backtesting simulates trading strategies against historical market data to evaluate profitability, risk, and potential effectiveness without risking real capital. Reliable results depend on accurate, representative data covering varied market conditions and including delisted or failed assets to limit survivorship bias. Traders should define goals, entry and exit rules, parameters, asset class, and trading costs, while modeling slippage and other real-world expenses.

Overfitting can be reduced through diverse datasets, in-sample and out-of-sample testing, sensitivity analysis, realistic cost assumptions, and written testing plans. Statistical analysis, risk-adjusted metrics such as the Sharpe ratio, and measures such as net profit, drawdown, win rate, and closed trades help assess performance and guide strategy refinement.

Backtesting supports disciplined trading, risk management, portfolio optimization, and adaptation to changing markets, but it cannot guarantee future success. It is also subject to biases, inaccurate data, over-optimization, and the omission of psychological factors affecting live decisions. Forward performance testing, scenario analysis, walk-forward testing, market replay, and paper trading can complement historical tests. When selecting software, traders should consider usability, customization, historical-data accuracy, performance-analysis tools, and support for their strategy and asset class. Specialized applications include forex, cryptocurrency, futures, options, CFDs, equities and derivatives, high-frequency and algorithmic trading, with each presenting distinct data, cost, leverage, volatility, and modeling challenges.

The second annual Addiction & Recovery Awareness MusicFest is scheduled for July 7, from noon to 10 p.m. at Buck Miller Arena in Westminster. The festival features local musicians, food vendors, and addiction and recovery speakers, including Brandon Novak of “Jackass” and Tim Ryan of A&E’s “Dope Man.” General admission is $20, and VIP passes are $50. Proceeds will benefit Rising Above Addiction, the Push HOPE Project, and the Up and Out Foundation. Last year’s festival raised more than $6,000 and drew nearly 600 people; organizers hope to expand the annual event. The festival aims to provide sober entertainment, fellowship, treatment support, and raise awareness of addiction’s impact, as Carroll County recorded 37 drug and alcohol overdose deaths in the first five months of 2018.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives surfaced alleged blog posts from his private site criticizing Donald Trump during his first term. Written before Rosenzweig joined the U.S. attorney’s office in September 2020, the posts included claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” Rosenzweig, who worked in the economic crimes section, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Justice Department also fired three other prosecutors from the district who had worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith criticized the dismissal of career public servants and attacks on the rule of law.

The court held that corporate creditors are preferred to stockholders and that members may not retain personal profits that diminish the corporate fund for the corporation’s benefit until creditors are paid. Although bonus stock and second-mortgage bonds were valid between the Bridge Company and its stockholders, they could not be enforced against creditors where they enriched stockholders at the corporation’s expense or increased corporate liabilities without valuable consideration.

Stockholder and director Gerard B. Allen received a 40% credit on 75 bonus shares without paying that amount. He also paid five $5-per-share calls and received $20,612 in second-mortgage bonds, which he sold for $15,904.59. The Circuit Court correctly held Allen liable as for unpaid stock to the amount realized from those bonds.

The court rejected the view that an individual stockholder’s liability becomes fixed when an execution against the corporation is returned nulla bona. Because the statute requires written notice and a court order before execution may issue against a stockholder, his specific liability is fixed only when the motion is filed after notice. Stock transferred before notice may therefore avoid liability, while transfer after notice does not. Accordingly, Allen was liable only for the 24 shares he owned when the motion was filed, rather than the 741 shares he held when the execution was returned. The judgment was reversed and the cause remanded.

The Blackwell GPU architecture and GeForce RTX 50 Series introduce GDDR7 memory with Enhanced CRC and always-enabled, die-level ECC supporting single-bit error correction without a performance penalty. Blackwell also supports EDR technology and fifth-generation Tensor Cores with FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8, FP6, and new FP4 operations. FP4 quantization uses less than half the memory of FP16 while providing more than twice the prior generation’s performance and, with NVIDIA’s TensorRT Model Optimizer, virtually no quality loss. It can reduce models such as FLUX.dev from more than 23 GB to under 10 GB and substantially accelerate image generation.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add support for Mega Geometry, Opacity Micromaps, Linear Swept Spheres, and related hardware-accelerated geometry functions. Mega Geometry uses cluster-level acceleration structures to reduce BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude, enables GPU-driven LOD management, and introduces persistent Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures for large scenes. It supports DirectX 12 through NVAPI, Vulkan extensions, and native OptiX 9.0 support. Linear Swept Spheres accelerate ray tracing of strand-like geometry, rendering hair about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth the VRAM.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves GPU thread scheduling for divergent ray-tracing and neural workloads. Its reorder logic is twice as efficient and more precise, and existing applications using SER can benefit without code changes. The AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts on the GPU, reducing CPU involvement, latency, stuttering, and communication overhead while coordinating AI and graphics workloads.

Blackwell adds H.264 and HEVC 4:2:2 encoding and decoding. Its ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode with another 5% improvement, and supports up to three encoders and two decoders in the RTX 5090. The sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed and adds 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps through UHBR 20, supporting 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with DSC and a DP80LL-certified cable.

Blackwell’s Max-Q power technologies add finer clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, including independent GPU-core and memory controls. Clocks adapt to workloads up to 1,000 times faster than on previous architectures, while the deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada. In a small-language-model inference example, these improvements produced power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the preceding frame-generation method, while enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine. New transformer-based models improve Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, providing greater temporal stability, reduced ghosting, improved motion detail, lighting detail, and fewer denoising artifacts.

Blackwell also advances neural shading through the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan and differentiable Slang features. Proposed techniques include RTX Neural Materials, neural texture compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural texture compression can provide up to seven-to-one compression over block-compressed formats; the cited material example reduces storage from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Neural Radiance Cache trains on live game data to infer indirect lighting from limited ray paths, RTX Skin provides real-time ray-traced subsurface scattering, and Neural Faces uses optimized generative AI to construct realistic faces from rasterized geometry and pose data.

The architecture is represented by GB202, with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA cores, used in the RTX 5090; GB203, with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores, used in the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and GB205, with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores, used in the RTX 5070. NVIDIA provides the specifications as-is with extensive disclaimers, usage restrictions, and liability limitations.

Coaches praised a conscientious young player, emphasizing fundamentals, puck battles, wall play, and disciplined play over scoring. His minutes were reduced during his first professional season to improve productivity and help him adjust to the NHL schedule and demands of a long playoff run.

The staff said the team believes in its ability to score but focuses on limiting opponents’ chances, defending when necessary, and avoiding high-risk plays. Players should shoot either to score or to create a subsequent opportunity, depending on the situation. The group was described as resilient, competitive, and willing to sacrifice for the team.

Sid was credited with helping young players feel comfortable and confident through leadership and informal conversations. Line combinations featuring elite scorers were adjusted to create balance, multiple threats, and difficult matchups, while separating or combining players as needed. The coaching staff also relied on video analysis, scouting, and preparation to identify tactical opportunities and improve the team.

Additional players were praised for forechecking, skating, physical play, puck retrieval, and creating separation. Overall, the staff emphasized speed, efficient exits from the defensive zone, hard work, stick possession, and playing the game correctly as central to the team’s success.

The patent application describes dry, self-supporting electrode films for energy-storage devices, particularly lithium-ion batteries. The films contain active materials such as graphite, a fibrillizable binder such as PTFE, and a microparticulate non-fibrillizable binder having a median particle size of about 0.5–40 μm. Suitable non-fibrillizable binders include cellulose derivatives such as carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF).

Fabrication methods may involve jet-milling the non-fibrillizable binder, mixing it with fibrillizable binder and active material, and calendering the mixture into a free-standing film without solvents. An alternative parallel process nondestructively mixes active material with the microparticulate binder, separately high-shear mixes active material with a structural binder, and then combines the mixtures to form the film. Smaller binder particles may improve material distribution, cohesion, tensile strength, processability, and specific capacity while reducing holes, cracks, surface pits, and defects associated with calendering.

In one example, a dry graphite anode contained 96 wt.% graphite and 4 wt.% binder comprising PTFE, CMC, and PVDF. Jet milling reduced the median CMC particle size from about 70 μm to about 10 μm. Milled-CMC anodes achieved charge and discharge capacities of 384 and 349 mAh/g, respectively, with 90.9% first-cycle efficiency, compared with 386 and 348 mAh/g and 90.2% efficiency for as-received CMC. Jet-milled CMC also produced fewer visible defects and greater tensile strength—1.74 N versus 0.936 N for as-received CMC.

The 3-3-5, also called the 3-5-3 or 3-3 stack, is a high-risk, high-reward defense using three defensive linemen, three inside linebackers, and five defensive backs. It relies on fast, athletic players; larger linebackers may play defensive line, while athletic defensive backs can fill linebacker roles. Its main strength is flexible, versatile coverage and pressure options. From the same pre-snap shell, defenders can play Cover 1 or Cover 3, add rushers from varied positions, create over or under fronts, blitz stacked linebackers, and adjust easily to formations.

The edges are its main vulnerability. Sweeps, outside zone plays, seam routes, and four verticals can exploit it, especially when blockers create favorable numbers. Trips formations force adjustments that can leave only five defenders in the box, weaken edge support, and create a vulnerable single-receiver side.

Common blitzes include the 3-3-5 Sam, which slants the line and sends a stackbacker or overhang off the edge, and the SAW blitz, which sends two stackbackers and pinches the line to bring five. In Cover 1, corners cover #1 receivers, overhangs cover #2 receivers, and stackbackers divide backfield coverage. In Cover 3, corners and the free safety take deep thirds, overhangs cover the flats, Sam and Will cover curls, and Mike covers the hook if not blitzing.

Joe Lee Dunn is credited with inventing the defense; Matt Campbell and Iowa State, Tony Gibson at NC State, and Tim Racki are also cited for using it.

The S&P 500 closed Friday at its lowest level since early July, down 1.96% on the day and 2.36% for the week after retreating from a record 6,427.02. Futures near 6,300 pointed to a rebound, with resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. Investor sentiment was slightly improved, with 40.3% of individual investors bullish and 33% bearish. The VIX reached 21.90, but no strong bearish signals were evident, although a potential topping pattern and deeper correction remained possible.

Oil fell 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 barrels per daily, its sixth consecutive monthly increase. Analysts said the added supply could pressure prices, while possible U.S. sanctions on Russian oil and concerns about slowing demand created uncertainty.

The commentary expected a short-term rebound but warned it could be part of broader consolidation or a downtrend. Earnings, low volatility, seasonal weakness, stretched valuations, and macroeconomic risks could make defensive positioning increasingly important.

PDT Partners increased its Northwest Natural Gas stake 1.4% in the second quarter, acquiring 269 shares to hold 19,969 shares worth $1.195 million. Bank of New York Mellon, Comerica Bank, Swiss National Bank, UBS Asset Management Americas and Parametric Portfolio Associates also reported increased stakes in the first quarter. Institutional investors and hedge funds owned 63.32% of NWN.

The stock has a consensus “Hold” rating and an average analyst target of $66. Zacks upgraded it to “buy” with a $74 target, BidaskClub downgraded it to “hold,” and Sidoti maintained “buy” with a $75 target.

Vice President Grant Yoshihara sold 2,000 shares for $132,060, while CEO David Hugo Anderson sold 8,000 shares for $535,760. Insiders sold 13,202 shares worth $879,666 over three months and owned 1.48% of the company.

NWN reported quarterly EPS of $0.10, beating the $0.06 consensus estimate, and revenue of $136.24 million, up 37.4% year over year. It declared a quarterly dividend of $0.4725, and analysts anticipate $2.17 in fiscal-year EPS. Northwest Natural Gas distributes natural gas through local distribution and storage operations in Oregon, Washington and California.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019 describes a company that designs, manufactures, sells and leases electric vehicles and energy generation and storage products. Its two reportable segments are automotive and energy generation and storage. Vehicle offerings include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with Cybertruck, Tesla Semi and a new Tesla Roadster planned. Energy products include Powerwall, Powerpack, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof. The company sells directly to customers, operates global service and Supercharger networks, provides warranties and financial services, and had 48,016 full-time employees at year-end.

Manufacturing occurs primarily at facilities in the San Francisco Bay Area, Nevada, New York and Shanghai, with a planned Berlin factory. Tesla reported 181,341,586 common shares outstanding as of February 7, 2020, and a non-affiliate market value of $31.54 billion as of June 30, 2019.

The report’s risk factors highlight potential delays and cost overruns in vehicle and energy-product development, manufacturing ramps, global retail expansion, deliveries, service capacity and charging infrastructure. Additional risks include uncertain consumer demand, competition, supplier dependence and disruptions, difficulties scaling Gigafactory Nevada and reliance on Panasonic for battery-cell production. It also identifies changing vehicle-safety, dealership, battery, solar, tax-incentive and self-driving regulations as potential constraints.

New York’s early intervention program, which serves about 70,000 children with developmental delays and disabilities, has provided many providers no substantive pay increase in roughly 30 years. State-set reimbursement rates have declined since the 1990s: a standard 30-minute visit averaged $79 in 1994 and $69 in 2022, while advocates estimate rates would need to rise 240% to retain their previous purchasing power. At the same time, caseloads, travel, reporting, paperwork and other demands have increased. Veteran special education teacher Emily Lengen, who serves children from birth through age 3, says she now works harder while earning less. Physical therapist Sandra Ribeiro, who also left the field, cited reimbursement delays, inadequate compensation and reduced support for collaboration among providers.

Low pay and administrative burdens have driven substantial provider attrition, leaving many children without timely speech, physical and occupational therapy and other services, with rural communities especially affected. Katie Wheeler’s 3-year-old daughter lost months of services after an agency closed and virtual providers quit following a pay cut; Wheeler said her daughter subsequently regressed. Similar staffing and compensation problems have been reported in Texas, Rhode Island and Illinois.

New York lawmakers authorized a 5% increase for in-person services in 2024, plus 4% for rural and underserved areas. Federal approval for the 5% increase remained pending, while the 4% increase was approved without a clear implementation schedule. Anticipated Medicaid cuts could prevent or delay additional funding. Advocates say the crisis also reflects long-standing political and social neglect of young children with disabilities and a predominantly female workforce. Despite these concerns, Lengen remains in early intervention because she values the work and the families she serves.
The appeal by Xavier Pulido from an October 20, 1989, Kings County Supreme Court judgment was dismissed, with five judges concurring.

Although U.S. adults consume 35% to 55% more protein than the recommended daily allowance, protein sources are not nutritionally equivalent. Animal foods generally provide higher-quality protein because they contain all essential amino acids and are more readily digested, while plant proteins may be limited in certain amino acids or less bioavailable.

Protein quality is especially important for adults over 70, some of whom may not consume enough high-quality protein, increasing risks of muscle loss, weakness, falls and sarcopenia. Animal-protein meals produced greater muscle protein synthesis than plant-protein meals in a study of younger adults, while an omnivorous meal produced 47% greater muscle protein synthesis than a complete-protein vegan meal in older adults. Consequently, some scientists recommend raising protein recommendations for adults 65 and older from 0.8 to as much as 1.5 grams per kilogram of body weight.

Researchers argue that guidelines should prioritize the nine essential amino acids rather than treating ounce-equivalent protein foods as identical. Under the proposed EAA-9 scoring system, an egg scores 15.77 and a tablespoon of peanut butter 4.04, meaning roughly four times as much peanut butter or more than twice the standard serving of kidney beans would be needed to match an egg’s amino-acid benefits.

Plant-rich diets can still supply adequate protein through larger portions, complementary foods, preparation methods and occasional dairy, eggs or meat. Combining legumes with rice, for example, balances their amino-acid profiles, while soaking, sprouting or fermenting legumes can improve digestibility. The Netherlands has incorporated legumes, fish, dairy, nuts, fruits and vegetables into guidance for diets with less meat.

Experts caution that pregnant, breastfeeding, older and athletic individuals may need additional protein, while most younger adults in developed countries can safely replace some animal protein with plant protein. Plant-rich diets may also support blood sugar, bowel and cholesterol health, and reducing meat production can lower greenhouse gas emissions, biodiversity loss and land-use changes. Most protein should still come from whole foods rather than processed products with added protein.

The January 14, 2002 compilation reported that an Enron employee had warned CEO Kenneth Lay in August 2001 about concerns involving partnerships, auditor Andersen’s accounting treatment and their effect on Enron’s financial statements. Lawmakers described the employee’s letter as raising a “veil of secrecy.” Enron reported its first quarterly loss in more than four years on October 16, including a $1.2 billion equity charge related to partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow.

Enron’s proposed sale of its core energy-trading business to UBS Warburg gave Enron and its creditors no upfront cash but 33% of pretax profits for at least two years. UBS could reduce the payment to 22% in the third year, 11% the following year and eventually zero, although Enron’s share could increase to as much as 45% if UBS did not exercise those options by the fifth year. UBS was also expected to rent Enron’s Houston offices and hire most trading employees. The arrangement still required bankruptcy-court approval.

Rep. John Dingell said there was “pretty strong evidence” of insider trading and false accounting at Enron and that Andersen was involved; Andersen had admitted destroying Enron documents. Shareholder litigation, congressional investigations and probes by the Justice Department and SEC were underway. The Senate Banking Committee scheduled a February 12 hearing on accounting and investor protection, with five former SEC chairmen invited to testify.

Former CEO Jeffrey Skilling shorted AES Corp. stock after leaving Enron, according to his spokeswoman, who said he did not use inside information. The trade could have produced more than $15 million in profit.

Treasury Secretary Paul O’Neill and Commerce Secretary Donald Evans said Enron officials sought advice or assistance during Enron’s collapse but received no government bailout. O’Neill said he did not tell President Bush about calls from Kenneth Lay, while Evans said he discussed Enron with Bush but omitted Lay’s calls. The political response to Enron intensified as details emerged about Andersen’s document destruction and Enron’s contacts with administration officials.

Cash-strapped Dabhol Power was near shutting its Indian operations after layoffs, unpaid staff and closures. It blamed Maharashtra State Electricity Board payment defaults and lenders’ refusal to release funds. Enron, General Electric and Bechtel, holding 85% combined, planned to exit the project.

Meanwhile, BG Group continued renegotiating a $388 million purchase of Enron’s Indian upstream assets amid unresolved disputes over operating three offshore fields with ONGC.

Enron’s collapse prompted tighter credit standards and balance-sheet repairs across the energy-trading sector, including debt reduction, asset sales and equity offerings. Investors considered short-term liquidity issues largely addressed while awaiting firmer energy prices.

Research from a survey of 2,000 British adults found that the average Brit wakes three times nightly, while one in ten wakes seven to ten times. Common reported causes of poor sleep were nighttime toilet trips (47%), snoring (41%), being edged out of bed (25%), pain (19%), tossing and turning (10.5%), and nightmares (11%); anxiety and disruptive partners were also cited. Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene and sleep cycles. He recommended consistent bedtimes, limiting food and drink, avoiding screens in bed, and maintaining a comfortable, low-disturbance environment to aid returning to sleep.

The analysis evaluates Apple’s valuation multiples against the growth metrics they reflect rather than comparing them with competitors. Apple’s shares have traded in an ascending channel since 2012 and are near its upper boundary, while prior DCF analysis considered $190 adequate but captured only long-term growth. Regression models show positive relationships between valuation multiples and EPS, EBITDA, and free-cash-flow growth. Current P/E, EV/EBITDA, EV/Operative FCF, and EV/FCF multiples exceed projected levels based on recent growth, though model fit varies (R²=0.05–0.57). The author concludes that Apple is overvalued and buying its shares at current prices is a bad investment decision.

Donald Blakeslee identified limestone boulders in Tami and Greg Norwood’s backyard as a still-functioning Wichita Nation sacred shrine. Carved basins and channels use flowing water to connect the sky, earthly, and underground realms, reflecting beliefs that water is sacred, transformational, and linked to spirits and prayer. Nearby depressions were used by women praying for successful pregnancies, while springs and cave pools served as sacred portals. The sites around Arkansas City and Etzanoa may reveal more about Wichita mythology, though Gary McAdams said beliefs and practices have changed.

Intel postponed a Fourth of July drone show at Travis Air Force Base near San Francisco because forecast winds of 30 mph exceeded the drones’ 18 mph limit. Rescheduled for July 5, the 500-drone performance was to feature synchronized red, white and blue imagery and music. The show highlights drones’ potential as a safer alternative to fireworks in wildfire-prone northern California; similar Arizona displays proceeded unaffected.

The article surveys selected results on transformer expressibility and trainability through logic, automata, and circuit complexity, with the goal of motivating further work in formal languages, verification, and programming languages. It defines transformers as compositions of length-preserving sequence transformations with token embeddings and an acceptance test. Piecewise-linear feed-forward functions modify individual vectors, while attention aggregates them through normalized scores. Softmax attention uses probability weights; unique hard attention (UHAT) selects the leftmost maximum-scoring position; average hard attention (AHAT) averages all maximum-scoring positions. Position information can be introduced through masking or position embeddings. Chain-of-thought transformers are excluded because they are known to be Turing-complete.

The central UHAT result is that UHAT with position embeddings recognizes a strict subset of AC0, the class solvable by constant-depth, polynomial-size Boolean circuits. Consequently, it cannot recognize languages such as PARITY or MAJ. Conversely, first-order logic with monadic numerical predicates, FO[Mon], is expressible by UHAT with position embeddings and by masked UHAT with finite-image position embeddings. Masked NoPE-UHAT corresponds exactly to first-order logic and star-free languages. Position-embedding UHAT can express all regular languages in AC0 and can also recognize palindromes. Verification of masked NoPE-UHAT is decidable, with the emptiness, universality, equivalence, and containment problems being EXPSPACE-complete.

AHAT’s averaging mechanism supports counting and arithmetic. AHAT can recognize MAJ, and all languages recognized by AHAT lie in TC0, AC0 extended with majority gates. Counting LTL with unary numerical predicates is expressible by AHAT with position embeddings, while its fragment Kt[#] is expressible by masked NoPE-AHAT. Counting LTL can express PARITY, whereas Kt[#] cannot. If TC0 is strictly contained in NC1, AHAT with position embeddings contains all regular languages in TC0. A complete characterization states that NoPE-AHAT recognizes precisely the permutation-invariant languages with semialgebraic Parikh images; consequently, checking whether such a transformer recognizes a nonempty language is undecidable.

The relationship between these hard-attention models and practical softmax transformers remains incomplete. Softmax transformers with position embeddings can recognize PARITY and therefore are not subsumed by UHAT, while the exact relationship with AHAT is unknown. Uniform-attention AHAT, AHAT[U], appears to approximate softmax attention closely enough that every language it recognizes is also recognizable by a softmax transformer; Kt[#] languages and languages with semialgebraic Parikh images are likewise recognizable by softmax transformers.

Expressibility also does not guarantee efficient trainability. PARITY is expressible by softmax transformers but appears difficult to train accurately, a phenomenon linked to its sensitivity to single-letter changes; MAJ, by contrast, is efficiently trainable. The RASP-L conjecture connects length generalization with short RASP-L programs, and a formalized version using limit transformers and Kt[#] excludes PARITY while admitting MAJ. The article closes by emphasizing that the surveyed results cover only part of the rapidly expanding FLaNN field and identifies numerous open problems concerning hard-versus-soft attention, trainability, and transformer expressibility.

Three unusual animal partnerships are described: pearlfish shelter in sea cucumbers’ anuses, leaving at night to hunt, though some parasitize their hosts and eat their gonads. Gobies guard pistol shrimps’ burrows, while the shrimps maintain the burrow and clean the gobies. Threatened arid bronze azure butterfly larvae chemically mimic queen ants, gain entry and protection in their nests, then consume the ants’ brood for food.

An 11-member committee will visit six states, examine liquor’s impact and report within three months. The government has made no final prohibition decision; with 712 liquor shops, it will not open more outlets but will run unsold ones. Village BMVs focused on prohibition have joined the committee.

The lecture examines gender discrimination and identity, focusing on persistent differences in earnings, workplace beliefs, family decisions, and task allocation.

Studying gender differences is justified by equality and fairness, greater productivity and welfare when talented people are not excluded, and insight into how personality and social preferences develop. Although women’s educational attainment, labor-force participation, and earnings have improved substantially over the past half century, large gaps remain. For recent cohorts, women earn roughly 20–30% less than men; in 2010, the mean and median annual earnings ratios for full-time, full-year workers aged 25–69 were 0.72 and 0.77, respectively, even controlling for hours and education. Gains are attributed to reduced educational disparities, technologies that expanded women’s work options, shifts from agriculture and manufacturing toward services, stronger regulation, and greater competition. Women’s labor-force participation has nevertheless plateaued since the early 1990s.

Technological interventions can reduce but not eliminate discrimination. Evidence from Goldin and Rouse indicates that blind orchestra auditions promoted impartial hiring and increased women’s representation, although incomplete blinding and small samples at later rounds complicate interpretation. Other studies document racial discrimination: identical applications with white-sounding names received callbacks 50% more often than those with African American-sounding names, which may reflect preferences based on identity or beliefs about performance. Algorithms can reproduce such biases when trained on biased human decisions, but they can also be designed with explicit equity objectives.

Research on beliefs shows that employers may interpret identical information differently by gender. Sarsons found that physicians sharply reduced referrals to female surgeons after adverse outcomes while referrals to male surgeons merely stagnated. Negative outcomes also generated spillovers to other female surgeons. Good outcomes produced a doubling of referrals to male surgeons but only a 70% increase for female surgeons. These asymmetries can reduce women’s opportunities, skill accumulation, promotion, wages, and employment, while underrepresentation leaves fewer opportunities to correct biased judgments.

Gender identity norms also matter as women’s earnings increase. Bertrand and colleagues found a missing mass of couples just above the point where wives earn half of household income, consistent with the norm that men should earn more. The pattern is attributed to marriages being less likely to form, more likely to end in divorce, and women reducing paid work or accepting more unpaid caregiving when they outearn their husbands.

The arrival of children creates substantial disparities. Danish evidence cited in the lecture shows a long-run penalty for women of nearly 20% in earnings and about 10% in hours, with no comparable decline for men; these penalties may also transmit across generations. Policies that stop both parents’ tenure clocks are not necessarily gender-neutral: one study found that adoption reduced women’s tenure rates while increasing men’s.

Marriage-market incentives may also suppress women’s career investment. Studies of female MBA students found lower observable participation and reported ambitions when single women expected classmates—especially single men—to see their preferences, consistent with concerns that visible ambition could be viewed negatively.

Finally, the lecture distinguishes demand for non-promotable work from women’s willingness to supply it. Women are more likely to volunteer for service-oriented tasks that do not advance careers. In mixed-sex threshold public-good experiments, women invest more because they are more likely to believe someone else will not act; the gender difference disappears in single-sex groups. Because women are also more likely to be asked to take on such tasks and more likely to comply, expectations amplify their heavier workload. Understanding these demand-and-supply dynamics may help explain vertical segregation and identify interventions to reduce gender gaps.

An April 18–19, 2001 email compiles reports on Enron, its businesses, and related industries.

- **Sycamore Networks:** Williams Communications generated more than 90% of Sycamore’s fiscal 2000 sales. Sycamore projected quarterly revenue of $50 million–$60 million rather than $151 million and a 16-cent loss rather than a five-cent profit, cut 12% of its workforce, and warned of further losses. Delays to its SN16000 optical switch gave rivals Ciena and Corvis opportunities to win Williams business, although Williams described its purchases from rivals as part of a multivendor strategy rather than dissatisfaction with Sycamore. The ADS868xW begins conversion on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, ignores further signal transitions until tconv expires, and then returns to acquisition. The host can detect completion through a low-to-high RVS transition or wait for tconv_max. It has nine configuration registers and supports host writes for configuration and host reads for data retrieval.

A data-transfer frame starts on the falling edge of CONVST/CS, loads the previous output word into a 32-bit output shift register, and ends on the next rising edge, when the input command is decoded and a new conversion begins. A 32-clock frame provides an optimal command; shorter frames permit partial reads but invalidate writes, while in longer frames the last 32 input bits form the command. Byte and half-word commands support register reads, writes, setting bits, and clearing bits. HWORD commands ignore the address LSB. Output data can contain fixed test patterns, 8- or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result, with optional device-address, range, AVDD-alarm, input-alarm, and parity flags.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI protocols for writes and offers single-SDO, dual-SDO, and source-synchronous options for reads. SPI protocol selection is controlled by SDI_MODE, while SDO and source-synchronous options are controlled by SDO_CTL_REG. Dual-SDO mode outputs two bits per clock and reassigns ALARM/SDO-1/GPO as SDO-1. Source-synchronous mode provides a data-synchronous clock on RVS, with selectable internal or external clock sources.

The register map includes DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. These provide device identification, reset and power control, interface configuration, output formatting, input-range selection, alarm status, and programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Writes to protected reset-control bits require the 69h key.

The ADS868xW is a fully differential, 16-bit SAR data-acquisition device with an integrated analog front end, ADC driver, programmable gain, and buffered precision reference. An example eight-channel industrial input module combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 and supports software-selected voltage or current inputs. The converter settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and includes input, AVDD, and overvoltage protections. Programmable input alarms with hysteresis support applications such as NTC thermistor temperature monitoring and help prevent false triggering.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires close decoupling for improved power-supply rejection. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at low throughput. NAP is entered after conversion when enabled and CONVST/CS remains high; wake-up requires a falling edge and the specified wake-up delay. Power-down is entered on a rising edge after PWRDN is set, powers down analog blocks while retaining the interface and registers, and requires the specified startup delay after exit. PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital routing, using low-impedance ground paths, placing bypass capacitors near supply and reference pins, and avoiding vias between device pins and their capacitors.

This study, part of the NIHR STIMULATE-ICP project, examined barriers to care and stigma among people with probable Long Covid who had not received a clinical diagnosis. Long Covid is prolonged ill health following SARS-CoV-2 infection and can involve fluctuating, multisystem symptoms, including fatigue, breathlessness, cognitive problems, pain, disturbed sleep, and neuropsychiatric symptoms. It can affect employment, finances, social participation, and access to healthcare. The study also drew attention to pre-existing health inequalities, which the COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated.

A Community Advisory Board co-produced the study design, interview materials, eligibility criteria, and dissemination plans. Participants were recruited through community leaflet distribution in Camden, Merton, and Derbyshire. Twenty-three people with symptoms consistent with Long Covid but no known clinical diagnosis completed semi-structured interviews between August 2022 and May 2023. Interviews explored barriers to obtaining care and experiences of enacted, anticipated, and internalised stigma. The transcripts were analysed thematically, informed by the Long Covid Stigma Scale.

Four themes were identified. First, limited awareness and self-doubt impeded help-seeking. Some participants did not know Long Covid existed or did not recognise their symptoms as possible Long Covid. Others attributed symptoms to ageing, menopause, stress, or existing conditions. Healthcare professionals’ failure to consider Long Covid could reinforce these doubts, and participants generally trusted professional judgments.

Second, participants described multiple barriers to healthcare engagement, including reluctance to burden the NHS, concern about further investigation or medication, fear that parenting abilities would be questioned, and primary-care limitations such as long waits, short appointments, and attention to only one symptom. Fluctuating or relapsing symptoms were sometimes absent during consultations, while other symptoms could be overlooked or attributed to mental health or pre-existing conditions.

Third, participants reported discrimination, anticipated stigma, and internalised stigma. Experiences included ageism, gender bias, dismissal or belittling by healthcare professionals, lack of empathy, social exclusion, being viewed as lazy, and skepticism from employers and colleagues. Participants anticipated judgment, disbelief, being labelled as hypochondriacal or awkward, and employment consequences. Many internalised shame, felt less valuable, compared themselves with faster recoverers, or concealed symptoms. The findings describe layered or intersectional stigma where multiple disadvantages interacted with Long Covid, and relate these experiences to testimonial and hermeneutical epistemic injustice.

Finally, support outside the NHS was widely used, including private care, alternative therapies, supplements, lifestyle changes, and advice from family or friends who were healthcare professionals. Peer, community, and social prescribing support was considered useful, while financial, employment, hybrid-working, and flexible-work support was also valued. Participants wanted easier access to longer appointments, greater validation and reassurance, advice and referrals, dedicated Long Covid services, and the option to access support without first visiting a GP.

The co-designed active case-finding approach identified people who might not otherwise have sought support. The authors recommend greater public and healthcare awareness, action against stigma, better listening to people with lived experience, and earlier signposting to health and wider support services. Although participants met symptom-based eligibility criteria, the study did not constitute clinical diagnosis, and alternative diagnoses remained possible. Participants under 29 were not included, limiting conclusions about younger adults.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation through dedicated RT Cores, Tensor Cores, and a revised streaming multiprocessor design. Turing improves memory bandwidth and latency with redesigned GDDR6 interfaces operating at 14 Gbps, offering 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X. Larger L2 caches, including 6 MB in TU102, and improved lossless compression further increase effective bandwidth. Combined memory and compression improvements provide roughly 50% more effective bandwidth to the RTX 2080 Ti than the Pascal-based 1080 Ti.

Turing’s display engine supports higher resolutions, refresh rates, HDR, tone mapping, DisplayPort 1.4a, and DSC 1.2, including dual 8K displays at 60 Hz. Its enhanced NVENC unit supports H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps and offers bitrate savings, while NVDEC adds support for additional HEVC, VP9, and high-bit-depth HDR formats. USB-C and VirtualLink provide a single-cable VR solution carrying power, display, and data. Turing also replaces MIO/PCIe-based SLI transfers with second-generation NVLink, providing higher bandwidth for two-way SLI and new display topologies.

Real-time ray tracing is enabled through RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, allowing streaming multiprocessors to perform other work. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and BVH acceleration, this makes real-time effects such as reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion practical on a single GPU. Turing reportedly achieves more than 10 times Pascal’s software-based ray-tracing performance and supports NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and planned Vulkan ray-tracing APIs.

NVIDIA NGX applies deep neural networks through Turing Tensor Cores. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) reconstructs high-quality images from lower-resolution inputs using networks trained against 64-times-supersampled references, achieving TAA-like quality with roughly half the shading work and contributing to reported RTX 2080 Ti performance twice that of the GTX 1080 Ti. DLSS 2X uses a larger network to upscale target-resolution inputs. Other NGX features include AI-based inpainting, slow-motion frame interpolation, and 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video super-resolution.

Turing also introduces mesh shading, with cooperative task and mesh shaders that process object lists in parallel, reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, support dynamic level-of-detail selection and geometry manipulation, and enable real-time rendering of very large numbers of objects. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently at 16-by-16-pixel regions, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering while potentially increasing shading rates for MSAA. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading, stores shading results in reusable texture-space texels, improves temporal stability, and can reuse work between stereo views. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views for stereo, instanced, shadow, and multi-projection rendering. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The passage describes TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 configurations. TU104 includes 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and one x8 NVLink link. The passage details NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture and associated GeForce RTX 30-series, A40, and RTX A6000 GPUs. GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, and a 384-bit memory subsystem with 6 MB of L2 cache. Third-generation NVLink provides four x4 links, offering 112.5 GB/s aggregate bandwidth between two GPUs, while PCIe Gen 4 provides up to 64 GB/s peak bandwidth through a x16 slot.

Each GA10x SM has four partitions, 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, a second-generation ray-tracing core, 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory, and dual FP32 datapaths that double FP32 throughput relative to Turing. The ROPs were moved into GPCs to increase their number and improve raster performance. Shared-memory bandwidth and total L1 capacity were also increased.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur, including moving and deforming geometry. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and structured sparsity, which can double matrix-operation throughput. Ampere-based DLSS also supports a 9x scaling factor, enabling some ray-traced games to run at 8K/60 fps.

GA10x uses GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding. It supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/s. Error Detection and Replay detects failed GDDR6X transmissions and retries them, helping identify memory-overclocking limits.

NVIDIA RTX IO, combined with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves game-asset loading and decompression from the CPU to the GPU. The passage reports up to 100x greater I/O throughput, substantially lower CPU use, reduced pop-in and stutter, and support for high-quality texture streaming.

GA10x supports DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 8K60 and 4K120 output. Its fifth-generation NVDEC decoder provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 AV1 playback at low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated H.264 and HEVC encoding up to 8K with low CPU utilization.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 and has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA Cores. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X. The data-center A40 has 48 GB of memory, supports NVLink expansion to 96 GB, virtualization, Quadro Sync, and the EGX platform. The RTX A6000 includes GA102, 48 GB of GDDR6, 10,752 CUDA Cores, and NVLink expansion to 96 GB. The passage reports up to twofold gains in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI performance over Turing, and up to 1.9x greater power efficiency at equivalent performance.

The double-down trading strategy adds an equal-sized position to a losing trade to lower the average entry price and seek a faster breakeven after a reversal. For example, after buying 100 Amazon shares at $136 and seeing them fall to $100, buying another 100 shares would produce a breakeven if the price rose $18. However, continued declines can magnify losses, and focusing on average price can become anchoring rather than assessing probabilities.

Unlike planned scale-in strategies, double-downing is rarely planned. It also differs from Martingale, which doubles the trade size after each loss and therefore increases risk more substantially, and from the repair strategy, which uses call options to offset a losing stock position.

Backtests on SPY, a mean-reverting asset, showed improved performance when doubling down: trades fell from 518 to 236, while average gain rose from 0.56% to 0.97%, though one large loser could still cause severe losses. Tests on HYG, a trending asset, showed fewer trades but a higher average loss, rising from 0.19% to 0.22%.

The strategy therefore tends to work better in mean-reverting assets and poorly in trending assets. Traders should assess market conditions, recovery prospects, risk management, and success probabilities; double-downing is rarely part of a rational plan and is often a trading bias.

Layout guidance includes minimizing output-to-input coupling, placing input series resistors near the device, adding a resistor below 100 Ω in series with outputs when needed to damp ringing or reflections, and using controlled-impedance traces with back termination for long routes.

The passage examines how the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming global ICT competition, productivity, and business strategy. It distinguishes the earlier computer-driven ICT productivity paradox from a newer Internet-driven paradox, in which rapid technological progress may coexist with slowing innovation, fewer new industries and jobs, and GDP that fails to capture significant benefits. Sources of uncaptured GDP include free cultural services, consumer surplus generated by online markets, new free digital goods and services, online intermediaries, and hard-to-measure investment and social benefits.

The transition from a “Product of Things” society to an IoT society shifts data creation from people to connected things and broadens the meaning of products to include devices, software, services, data flows, and applications. The paper argues that global ICT firms should replace functional ICT strategies with integrated digital business strategies that capture value beyond traditional revenue measures.

An empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms from 2005 to 2016 finds that sales are significantly related to accumulated R&D investment and follow logistic growth. High-R&D-intensive firms increasingly face declining marginal ICT productivity, while lower-R&D firms show rising productivity; the number of high-R&D firms in a declining-productivity cycle rose from 16 in 2005 to 25 in 2016. The paper attributes this decline to the Internet’s “two-faced nature”: freebies, easy copying, and standardization lower technology prices despite functional advances.

Firms are responding by activating a self-propagating function through soft innovation resources, including trust, sleeping resources, consumer gratification, memories, untapped resources, and preferences for value beyond economic utility. Cases involving Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, and Amazon illustrate this transformation toward trust-based, ICT-driven disruptive business models. The lecture introduces nuclear binding energies and uses solar-system elemental abundances to motivate why some nuclei are more common. Binding energy is defined as the combined mass of constituent protons, neutrons, and electrons minus the nuclear mass. Average binding energy per nucleon is roughly 7.5–9 MeV for most elements, peaks near iron, and decreases toward lighter and heavier nuclei, allowing energy release through fusion and fission.

The Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula, also called the liquid-drop model, parameterizes binding energy using five terms: volume, surface, Coulomb, neutron-proton asymmetry, and pairing. The dominant volume term reflects a short-range nuclear force and tightly packed nucleons; the surface term accounts for reduced binding at the nuclear boundary; and the Coulomb term reflects proton repulsion. The asymmetry term is linked to filling nuclear energy states under the Pauli exclusion principle, while the pairing term lowers the energy of even numbers of protons and neutrons relative to odd combinations. Together, these terms reproduce the observed binding-energy curve and its maximum near iron.

President John Tyler reported on December 30, 1842, that U.S.–China trade was substantial and growing, with 1841 exports totaling $715,000 in domestic products and $485,000 in foreign merchandise, while American goods also reached China indirectly. He recommended Congress fund a qualified commissioner resident in China to protect American citizens and property, monitor commercial interests, and communicate with Chinese authorities.

An overlap sends an unmarked fullback from the back into an attack, typically beyond the midfielder near the sideline, requiring space and a clear lane. It may begin with a straight run or give-and-go and usually ends with a cross; if the fullback is covered, the ball may return to the midfielder. Unlike a vertical offensive switch, the midfielder remains in the attack. An underlap sends the fullback inside the midfielder, often creating a shot. Overlaps can occur anywhere in the attacking end but are less common centrally because of congestion. Coaches should use these tactics only when they suit the team’s existing attack and vary them as appropriate.

Ross Nelson appealed a judgment sustaining Peter John’s demurrer in an action for specific performance of a 1892 contract involving land allotted to Puyallup Indians John and Chekudakai Salerhand. The court affirmed, holding that treaty-based restrictions on alienation were valid because the government treated tribal members as wards and intended the restrictions to protect them. The restrictions were not void as repugnant to a fee-simple grant, and the Bland Act granting citizenship did not impliedly repeal them. Washington’s removal legislation and Congress’s March 3, 1893 Wilson Act did not validate earlier conveyances; Congress delayed removal of restrictions for ten years, making land-sale contracts entered before removal void.

The U.S. government sold the 106-meter Russian superyacht Amadea through a sealed-bid auction, with the buyer and price undisclosed. Seized in Fiji in 2022 and valued at $230 million in court documents, the yacht cost taxpayers nearly $1 million monthly to maintain. The article develops and analyzes a nine-compartment SEIR-like ordinary differential equation model for SARS-CoV-2 transmission, separating susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased populations. Model parameters account for vaccination, disease progression, recovery, hospitalization, intensive-care admission, and death. Hospitalization and death rates are derived from seven-day moving averages of reported infections, hospitalizations, and deaths. To reduce the number of unknowns, severe, critical, and asymptomatic transmission rates are fixed proportions of the mildly infectious transmission rate, which is treated as a time-dependent parameter.

Under the assumption that all parameters are continuous and strictly positive, the model is shown to have a unique nonnegative solution on finite intervals and, when parameters are bounded, on the nonnegative real line. Susceptible and exposed populations remain positive, infectious compartments remain nonnegative, and the total population is conserved.

The article then defines a parameter-to-solution map from bounded Sobolev-space transmission functions to model solutions. The map is shown to be well defined, injective, continuous in the Sobolev norm, and sequentially closed under weak convergence. Its vector field is differentiable in the state and transmission parameter, and the solution map is shown to be Fréchet differentiable in the interior of its transmission-parameter domain, with its derivative determined by a corresponding variational ODE system. The broader analysis addresses the inverse problem of estimating time-dependent transmission from observed incidence using Tikhonov-type regularization, with a numerical example based on real data planned.

RTX Neural Texture Compression uses neural networks through neural shaders to compress and decompress material textures more efficiently than traditional methods. In the Neural Materials demo, neural materials use 333 MB compared with 1,110 MB for standard lantern and fabric materials, saving over 3x while providing higher visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering randomizes texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré when traditional filtering is impractical, supports cubic or Gaussian filtering with one point sample, and runs fast on Blackwell GPUs due to improved point-sampled texture-filtering rates.

Neural Radiance Cache uses a neural shader and tiny neural networks trained on live game data to approximate indirect illumination. It infers final lighting for many bounces from rays after one bounce, reducing GPU ray-tracing work while improving performance, global illumination, scalability, and adaptability. RTX Skin introduces film-rendering-style subsurface scattering into real-time path tracing for translucent skin. RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative AI model to infer natural-looking faces from a rasterized face and 3D pose data, with training based on offline images across angles, lighting, emotions, and occlusion.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine identified peroxisomes as an alternative heat-producing system in brown fat. In mice, cold increased peroxisome numbers, which could compensate when mitochondria lacked uncoupling protein 1. Peroxisomes burned fatty acids and generated heat through the protein ACOX2. Mice lacking ACOX2 had poorer cold tolerance, lower body temperatures, reduced insulin sensitivity, and greater weight gain on high-fat diets, while mice engineered to produce more ACOX2 showed the opposite benefits. The findings suggest possible dietary or drug interventions involving certain fatty acids or direct ACOX2 activation, but these possibilities require further study in humans.

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (EWI), created in 2003, contains the same 500 U.S. companies as the traditional S&P 500 but assigns each stock 0.2% at quarterly rebalances rather than weighting it by market capitalization. Sector weights therefore reflect the number of constituent stocks, giving smaller companies greater influence.

Invesco RSP tracks the equal-weight index, while State Street SPY tracks the market-cap-weighted index. RSP requires rebalancing to maintain equal weights. Historical outperformance is attributed to the small-cap effect: smaller companies have tended to grow faster than larger ones. Equal weighting may also provide some protection during declines in mega-cap technology stocks because smaller constituents can offset losses.

A simple strategy is to own the equal-weight index instead of the market-weighted S&P 500. The passage says equal weighting has outperformed historically, though not over the past decade, and notes that higher fees on many equal-weight products reduce the advantage. For example, with dividends reinvested, $10,000 invested in RSP in 2004 reportedly grew to $60,000 after 18 years, versus $55,000 in SPY; RSP’s annual expense ratio was 0.2%, compared with SPY’s 0.0945%.

Choked gamma-ray bursts in hydrogen-rich blue and red supergiants may hide TeV–PeV neutrinos and accelerate ultra-high-energy cosmic rays. Although a relativistic jet is blocked by the dense envelope, its high-pressure cocoon can drive shocks that break out, potentially producing brief X-ray/UV flashes and longer optical transients.

The study uses 2.5D spherical relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations with the PLUTO code and a Taub–Matthews equation of state. Separate one-dimensional calculations for 39,000 parameter combinations provide scaling relations for jet breakout and choking times. A choked-jet criterion compares the jet head’s progress with a near-luminal tail, while shock cells are identified using converging flow, pressure jumps, temperature–density gradient alignment, and Mach number above one.

The preliminary simulation used a 15-solar-mass, 50-solar-radius blue supergiant, a \(10^{51}\) erg/s jet with initial Lorentz factor 7, magnetization 0.01, a 2-degree injection cap, and a 5-second engine duration. By engine shutdown, the jet head reached about \(0.03R_*\), while the cocoon extended roughly \(0.004R_*\) transversely. External cocoon, head termination, and internal collimation shocks formed. The head remained causally disconnected from the tail and continued moving through the simulated 30 seconds, so choking did not occur within that interval. As stellar density declined, the external shock accelerated, the collimation shock faded, and the forward cocoon shock and residual termination shock became the main energy-dissipation and potential particle-acceleration sites. Overall estimates indicate that the jet would choke roughly one minute after launch.

Future work will examine blue and red supergiant progenitors over multiple luminosities, Lorentz factors, and viewing angles to predict detectable neutrino and electromagnetic signatures.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces higher-bandwidth memory, improved display and video capabilities, hardware-accelerated real-time ray tracing, AI-based graphics, and more flexible rendering pipelines. TU102 supports 14 Gbps memory signaling and includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice GP102’s 3 MB. Lossless memory compression and traffic reduction provide about 50% higher effective bandwidth on Turing than Pascal, including in the RTX 2080 Ti versus GTX 1080 Ti.

Turing’s display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, 8K at 60 Hz on two displays, USB-C connectivity, and native HDR processing with BT.2100 tone mapping. Its enhanced NVENC encoder supports H.265/HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps and provides bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR support.

USB Type-C and VirtualLink provide power, display, and data for VR headsets through a single connector while supporting four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes and a SuperSpeed USB 3 link. For SLI, TU102 uses two x8 second-generation NVLink links and TU104 uses one, each providing 25 GB/s per direction between GPUs. Turing NVLink supports two-way SLI but not three- or four-way configurations.

RT Cores in each Streaming Multiprocessor accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing shader cores for other work. Turing can process more than 10 billion rays per second and is described as roughly ten times faster than software-based ray tracing on Pascal. Hybrid Rendering combines rasterization for visibility and fast shading with ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Denoising further reduces the number of rays required.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only deep-learning stack that uses Tensor Cores for pre-trained AI services. Its Deep Learning Super-Sampling system produces image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X approaches 64-times-supersampled quality. Other NGX features include Inpainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez, which can enlarge images and video by 2x, 4x, or 8x and perform real-time 1080p-to-4K upscaling.

Turing also introduces Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. Mesh shading adds task and mesh shader stages to process large object lists cooperatively and can increase real-time object counts by more than an order of magnitude. Variable Rate Shading independently controls shading rates for each 16×16-pixel region and supports content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility from appearance, stores shading results in texture space, and reuses them across pixels, frames, and stereo views. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and 32 at the API level, expanding Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection capabilities. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and permits different resource types within the same heap.

The full TU104 contains 48 Streaming Multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and a 256-bit memory interface. TU106 has 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but does not support NVLink or SLI. The Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, a 256-bit interface, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering. It weights peak Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput by expected utilization; for the RTX 2080 Ti, the resulting value is 78.

Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections provide more realistic lighting than traditional shadow-map, screen-space, and probe-based methods. Their efficiency relies on hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH acceleration, and RT Cores, which together bring real-time ray tracing to a single GPU. The document concludes with terms stating that specifications are provided without warranties, limiting NVIDIA’s liability, reserving rights to revise or discontinue products, and providing no implied intellectual-property license.

The Sporting News provided live updates and highlights from Game 2 of the 2025 American League Wild Card Series between the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox, played Wednesday, October 1 at 6 p.m. ET at Yankee Stadium and broadcast nationally on ESPN. Boston held a 1-0 series lead and could advance to the ALDS, where it would face the Blue Jays; a Yankees loss would end New York's postseason. Carlos Rodon (18-9, 3.09 ERA) started for New York against Brayan Bello (11-9, 3.35 ERA), with Boston 5-0 in series-clinching games under Alex Cora.

Ben Rice hit a two-run homer in the first for a 2-0 lead, and Boston scored twice in the second after loading the bases. Cora pulled Bello after 2.1 innings and used lefty Justin Wilson, who was replaced by Justin Slaten. Rodon worked five innings, allowing two runs with five strikeouts, and the game was tied 2-2 after four. A Jarren Duran error on Aaron Judge's liner into left field allowed Trent Grisham to score, though it was ruled a hit.

Regular-season notes: Rodon allowed 11 hits and 10 earned runs in 15.2 innings against Boston, which hit .258 with 51 homers against left-handed pitching; Bello pitched 19 scoreless-earning four runs over three starts, and Boston went 2-1 in those games. New York managed seven hits in the Game 1 loss. The passage also includes author Daniel Mader's biography.

Ken Research forecasts Thailand’s frozen foods market to grow at a 5.9% CAGR from 2017 to 2022E. Growth is expected from rising export demand, especially for processed seafood and meat, along with increased demand from hotels, restaurants, hospitals, offices, quick-service outlets, online retailing and canned-food usage. Other expected drivers include vegetarian ready meals, natural sweetener blends, diverse processed fruits, health-focused snacks for children and government-backed sustainable fisheries initiatives.
