The President proposed a global peace framework based on the Monroe Doctrine, national self-determination, government by consent of the governed, freedom of the seas, reduced armaments, and avoidance of entangling alliances. Italy’s foreign minister called the ideas idealistic and difficult to implement but expected them to generate attention. Spain expressed interest in cooperation, viewing the address favorably and itself as uniquely positioned among neutral nations. Hungary’s prime minister welcomed peace efforts and continued discussions but warned that proposed Allied conditions threatened the Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman Empires, conflicting with the President’s demand that every people receive guarantees of free existence, religious liberty, and individual and social development.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and computer-readable media for automating orthodontic treatment planning by capturing and applying dental professionals’ explicit and historical clinical preferences. A preference database links each user or group to key text instructions and corresponding clinical behaviors, including tooth movement restrictions, interproximal reduction, attachments, extractions, spacing, and leveling strategies. The database may be built from explicit instructions or historical treatment data and updated as users modify generated plans.

Preferences may be identified through machine-learning text classification, including bag-of-words, random forest, or word2vec methods, and similarity searching using Damerau-Levenshtein distance, confidence thresholds, text normalization, and manual or semi-automatic verification. Statistical analysis may also identify clinically consistent behaviors over time, including changes in user practices, to derive preferences when wording is inconsistent or unstated.

A treatment-planning engine receives a patient’s dentition or digital model and the professional’s instructions, matches them with stored preferences, and generates a patient-specific treatment plan incorporating corresponding clinical behaviors. The plan may be reviewed, approved, and used to fabricate orthodontic appliances, with user corrections used to update the preference database.

Monitoring tools compare automatically applied options with finalized plans, report positive, neutral, and negative cases, and support quality control and correction of outdated preferences. One reported implementation reduced plans requiring user modification from 12.48% to 8.5%.

Three-year-old Liam Radcliffe walked about half a mile home from Barassie Early Years nursery in Ayrshire after leaving through two sets of doors and an unlocked gate. Staff failed to notice his absence for up to 20 minutes. His mother, Sarra Reid, found him crying at her home and returned him to the nursery, where staff had not realized he was missing. The nursery subsequently alarmed the main door, padlocked the gate and added staff. Sarra welcomed the changes but said she had lost confidence in the nursery and that Liam would soon move elsewhere. South Ayrshire Council said child safety was taken seriously.

The passage argues that judicial decisions should be open to public criticism, which promotes careful, just rulings, professional consistency, and judicial accountability. Fair and dispassionate criticism is beneficial, while unjust attacks should be answered through the strength of judicial opinions. Opposing all criticism would encourage irresponsible attacks and endanger confidence in the judiciary. Turning to crime, the author calls for an awakened public conscience and effective legislation to address corruption and delays in justice. Lynching and mob violence are condemned, especially where victims are tortured in retaliation for crimes such as rape, thereby reducing mob participants to the level of the criminals they punish.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, require external gate drivers, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Switching stops when the sensed switch current reaches the internally stepped-down COMP voltage.

The FAULT pin allows external circuitry to implement protections such as overcurrent or overvoltage detection. A fault occurs when its voltage exceeds 0.6 V typically for 0.4–1.4 µs. Detection discharges SS, stops switching, and holds outputs low. After FAULT falls below 0.5 V, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay before restarting soft start; a new fault restarts the delay.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation when duty cycle exceeds 50%. It uses a voltage ramp subtracted from the scaled error-amplifier output; the minimum stable slope is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, while 1 times that slope is recommended. Frequency compensation supports Type 2A or Type 2B schemes. Type 2A adds CHF in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection begins with crossover frequency and RCOMP, followed by CCOMP and optional ESR-zero compensation.

Internal thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts the power-up sequence below 160°C.

A design example uses a TPS7H5001-SP in a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter with 5-V output. Selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ and 1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ RPS and RSP resistors, a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge-blank-time resistor, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor giving about 7.5 ms. The transformer turns ratio is 2.5, with 40 µH actual primary inductance. Primary GaN FETs are rated 170 V for a 36-V maximum input; an 80-V synchronous rectifier is used, with an optional parallel Schottky diode.

The output inductor is 0.47 µH for a 40% ripple target. At least 1.3 mF output capacitance is required for 2% ripple and 2.5% transient deviation; 2.3 mF is used for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation, implemented with seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors. An optional LC filter can reduce output noise, with damping available for high-frequency peaking.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at roughly 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover; selected values are 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF. A 102-kΩ RSC resistor sets slope compensation.

The controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, with additional input capacitance recommended for improved noise and radiation performance. Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and other sensitive signals from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing high-di/dt and high-dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection, using short and wide current traces, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, routing high-dv/dt outputs away from sensitive pins, and connecting CFP-package backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.

The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July, gaining 7.8% year to date and 8.6% including total return. It marked the third consecutive month above its 10-month moving average, though an early-August decline and weakening 50-day breadth signaled short-term risks. July was broadly risk-on, with stocks up, bonds down, Frontier Markets leading monthly returns, and U.S. large-cap stocks ranking third. Medium- and long-term trends remained healthy, but momentum showed early warnings as volatility and credit spreads increased seasonally. Investors continued shifting toward technology stocks, while U.S. electricity demand reached a record high. Other headlines covered gold above $4,000, Bitcoin retreating, a possible U.S. government shutdown, Goldman Sachs’ view that stocks were not yet in a bubble, and Bank of England warnings about market corrections. Investing.com also disclosed that market data may not be real-time or accurate and that financial and cryptocurrency trading involves substantial risk.

On October 4, 2001, BG Group agreed to buy Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million. The conditional deal covers Enron’s 30% interest in the Tapti gas field and Panna/Mukta fields and its 62.64% interest in the CB-OS/1 exploration block. The assets have more than 170 million barrels of proven and probable oil-equivalent reserves and equity production of about 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Analysts considered the price of less than $2.30 per barrel of oil equivalent below market value, noting that a $400 million offer from ONGC had previously been rejected. Completion required Indian government approval and agreement among partners for BG to become operator. ONGC sought operating control, creating uncertainty over the transfer. BG planned further investment to expand production and develop the Indian gas market.

Enron was separately seeking to sell its 65% controlling stake in the Dabhol power project, India’s largest private-sector power plant, reportedly for $1.2 billion; Tata Power and BSES were identified as possible buyers. The project faced prolonged payment disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, a power shutdown and a stalled expansion. Dabhol Power Co. also defaulted on a $24 million interest payment due to lenders on its 96%-complete second phase.

U.S. technology stocks led a broad market rally. The Nasdaq Composite rose 5.93% to 1,580.81, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.93% to 9,123.78. Cisco rose 22%, Extreme Networks gained 22%, and Enron advanced 9.4%. Analysts had recently reduced earnings forecasts before beginning to emphasize valuations, while some real-estate stocks and Eli Lilly declined.

A California settlement would let Southern California Edison repay more than $3 billion of roughly $3.9 billion in debt through continued higher customer rates and diverted cash and dividends, prompting consumer advocates to warn of a ratepayer bailout and possible additional increases. The agreement required federal court approval.

Former Enron executive and retired Army Brig. Gen. Thomas White was appointed the Pentagon’s liaison for homeland security under Gov. Tom Ridge.

An Enron archive log lists email subjects, creators, and dates, primarily covering California electricity and gas issues from September 2000 through July 2001. Topics include CPUC hearings, CAISO, FERC, state power purchases, rates and price caps, supply shortages, legislation, Governor Davis, PG&E and SCE, bankruptcy, power contracts, transmission, and related press and public-opinion materials.

A vehicle-code stop in Chino led to the arrest of Mark William Ellis, 36, on suspicion of grand theft and vehicle theft. Investigators linked him to more than $200,000 in stolen property from thefts dating to 2006, with some possibly occurring earlier. Ellis allegedly took items from vehicles, homes, businesses and schools and hoarded them in six storage units rather than selling them. Authorities confirmed more than 50 vehicle burglaries affecting 40 victims and recently returned about $63,000 in property. Ellis, who was on probation, was held without bail, charged, and pleaded not guilty. He is scheduled to return to court March 21, and investigators are seeking additional victims.

Centana Growth Partners raised $250 million for its first fund, targeting $5 million to $30 million per financial-services startup. Since 2015, it has invested in four companies, including One and Jumio, and is seeking more candidates.

Obamacare changed Medicare, employer-sponsored insurance, the individual insurance market, Medicaid and the requirement to maintain coverage. President-elect Donald Trump and congressional Republicans pledged to repeal the law, starting with subsidies, Medicaid expansion, taxes and mandates, while possibly retaining coverage for children under 26.

Repeal would likely raise premiums, deductibles and cost-sharing for 57 million Medicare beneficiaries and disabled Americans, restore Medicare’s prescription-drug “donut hole,” and end free preventive services. It would increase Medicare spending by $802 billion over 10 years, according to the Congressional Budget Office. Since 2010, Obamacare has saved more than 11 million people an average of over $2,100 on prescription drugs. Higher-income Medicare enrollees could receive some financial benefit from repeal.

For employer-sponsored insurance, repeal would end the employer mandate, potentially lead firms to offer coverage only to employees working at least 35 or 40 hours, remove free contraceptives and preventive screenings, and end dependents’ eligibility until age 26. Employers could also lose protections involving pre-existing conditions, required benefits, age-based premiums and annual or lifetime benefit limits.

In the individual market, repeal could remove subsidies and exchanges, along with protections for pre-existing conditions, maternity, mental health and prescription drug coverage. Medicaid expansion, which added nearly 17 million enrollees in 31 states and the District of Columbia, would end, potentially leaving millions uninsured. The individual mandate and its penalty of $695 per adult or 2.5% of household income would also disappear.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is based on the Ampere architecture and targets AI, deep learning, and high-performance computing. Its third-generation Tensor Cores accelerate general matrix-matrix multiplication, \(D=A*B+C\). Each A100 Tensor Core performs 256 FP16 fused multiply-add operations per clock with FP32 accumulation, while each streaming multiprocessor contains four Tensor Cores and delivers 1,024 FP16 FMAs per clock. With 108 SMs and 432 Tensor Cores, the GPU provides up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance—2.5 times the Tensor Core performance of Tesla V100 and 20 times its standard FP32 throughput.

A100 Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, binary, TF32, BF16, and FP64 data. TF32 uses FP32 range with reduced internal precision and is enabled by default for training, requiring no script changes. FP16 or BF16 mixed-precision training can deliver up to twice the throughput of TF32 and up to 16 times the throughput of FP32 on A100. A100 also supports IEEE-compliant FP64 acceleration, reaching 19.5 TFLOPS and up to 2.5 times V100’s FP64 performance. In cuSOLVER mixed-precision iterative refinement tests, TF32 produced the fastest and most robust results, with a geometric-mean speedup of 2.0 times over the FP64 solver.

A100 introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, allowing two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse matrix instructions skip zero entries, doubling Tensor Core throughput while halving compressed weight storage and bandwidth requirements. A dense-training, structured-pruning, and fine-tuning recipe produced virtually no inference-accuracy loss across evaluated vision, detection, segmentation, language-modeling, and translation networks.

The memory hierarchy includes 192 KB per SM of combined L1 cache and shared memory, 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s, and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s read bandwidth. Compute Data Compression can improve effective DRAM read/write bandwidth, L2 read bandwidth, and L2 capacity by up to four, two, and two times, respectively. HBM2, L2, L1, and register files are protected by SECDED ECC. L2 residency controls allow persistent data to be prioritized in cache, and CUDA 11 supports address-range and per-access persistence management.

A100 improves Tensor Core efficiency through wider data sharing across warps, larger matrix operations, fewer register-file accesses, and asynchronous direct copies from global memory to shared memory. Hardware asynchronous barriers support producer-consumer pipelines and fine-grained thread synchronization. CUDA 11 also adds accelerated task graphs, cooperative-group asynchronous copies and reductions, and improved dependency handling for complex workflows.

Multi-Instance GPU capability can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, L2 cache, memory bandwidth, quality-of-service, and fault-isolation guarantees. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances, which can run simultaneous contexts and Volta-style MPS workloads. MIG supports migration between matching GPU Instances or GPUs, allowing workloads to be consolidated without interrupting jobs.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s of aggregate GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 x16 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction and supports SR-IOV virtualization. A100 also adds improved error detection, attribution, isolation, and containment for multi-GPU and multi-tenant environments.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units. A100 does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and provides 4.8 TB/s of bidirectional interconnect bandwidth. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and optimized containers for deep learning, analytics, and HPC. The DGX A100 platform also supports NVIDIA GPU Cloud, DeepOps, Kubernetes, and large-scale InfiniBand networking.

The instructor outlines the class logistics: there is no textbook, recitation, or exam. Five biweekly problem sets account for 75% of the grade, while a final 8–10-page review or calculation on a chosen holographic-duality topic accounts for 25%. Materials will be posted online, and students are encouraged to ask questions and provide feedback. The syllabus is flexible and may cover only part of the proposed outline.

The lecture begins with the distinction between gravity and the other fundamental interactions. Electromagnetism, weak interactions, and strong interactions are understood through gauge theories in fixed spacetime, while a complete quantum theory of gravity remains unresolved. Open questions include the quantum behavior of spacetime, whether spacetime remains continuous, black-hole quantum properties, and the universe’s origin.

The lecture introduces holographic duality as a proposed equivalence between a gravitational theory with dynamical spacetime in a higher-dimensional space and an ordinary nongravitational quantum field theory in a lower-dimensional fixed space. These are presented as two descriptions of the same quantum system. The instructor emphasizes that the relation’s conceptual basis remains unclear and describes the course’s goal as developing a dictionary between the two descriptions and explaining their use and implications.

The lecture connects this idea to earlier suggestions that gravity can emerge from nongravitational systems, including Sakharov’s proposal and parallels between general relativity and hydrodynamics. It then discusses the 1980 Weinberg–Witten theorems, which prohibit massless charged particles of spin greater than 1/2 in theories with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current and massless particles of spin greater than 1 in theories with a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor. These results prevent theories such as QCD from producing a graviton in the same spacetime, but holographic duality avoids that restriction by placing gravity in a different, higher-dimensional spacetime. A largely kinematic proof of the theorems using Lorentz symmetry, particle states, charges, momentum, and rotational transformations concludes the lecture.

**Summary**

This preprint presents a protocol for BioRecall, a cross-sectional biobank-recall pilot study designed to collect lifestyle and environmental exposure data and combine it with genotype, biological sample, and clinical outcome data from biobanks. The rationale is that non-communicable diseases (NCDs) cause over 70% of deaths worldwide, that genetic risk scores have limited individual-level predictive power, and that environmental and lifestyle exposures are expected to have larger effects on disease risk. Individuals also shape their own environments based on genetically regulated preferences, creating gene–environment interactions that require large datasets to study. Biobanks currently lack sufficient lifestyle and environmental data, and the exposome framework (general external, individual, and internal environment) is presented as a holistic alternative to reductionist exposure analyses.

The pilot is conducted in the Central Finland Biobank with the University of Jyväskylä, the Finnish Biobank Cooperative (FINBB), and the University of Eastern Finland. Eligible participants are adults with a type 2 diabetes diagnosis (ICD-10 E11.x), available genome-wide genotype data, and consent to recontact; a feasibility assessment identified 1,386 eligible participants. Recruitment uses the Fingenious® service, with the biobank creating pseudonymized IDs so that survey data can be linked to registry data without researchers knowing participant identities. Invitations are sent mainly electronically via the OmaHyvis healthcare portal, with mailed invitations as a fallback, plus two electronic reminders and, if needed, a paper questionnaire.

Data collection occurs through an electronic questionnaire (REDCap) accessed via the MyBiobank portal with Suomi.fi authentication, taking approximately 30–40 minutes and requiring electronic consent for participation and archiving of data in the biobank. Measures include physical activity (GPAQ plus new muscle-strengthening and balance questions, life-long activity history), diet quality and alcohol consumption (Healthy Diet Index, based on the D2D Food Intake Questionnaire), anthropometrics and weight-loss history, smoking and substance use, medical history, self-rated health, women's health questions, work characteristics (work ability, occupational loading, effort–reward imbalance, work engagement), emotional states (PANAS), sleep (Jenkins Sleep Scale), and residential environment linked via postal code to open-source spatial, air quality, land cover, and socioeconomic data. Automated feedback is provided on physical activity, diet, waist circumference, work stress, and sleep relative to national recommendations.

Data collection is scheduled to begin in February 2025, with manuscript and theses production during 2025 and extension to all Central Finland Biobank donors planned for autumn 2026. No formal sample size calculation or statistical analysis plan was performed. Ethical approval (1671/13.00.04.00/2023) and biobank approval (BB24-0333-A01) were obtained. Strengths include low-cost scalability, an extensive exposome dataset, automated feedback, and novel activity questions; limitations include limited pilot sample size, a single regional biobank, absence of wearable data, a lengthy questionnaire that may reduce adherence, possible better response rates via postal contact, and untested use of automated feedback in this patient group. Funding came from the University of Jyväskylä, the Research Council of Finland, the Juho Vainio Foundation, the Päivikki and Sakari Sohlberg Foundation, the Regional Council of Northern Savo, and JACARDI; data are accessible through Fingenious services, and novel physical activity questions and HDI feedback materials are available from the authors or FOODNUTRI project on reasonable request. Patients and the public were not involved in the research.

As Sony prepared for the November 17, 2006 launch of the $599 PlayStation 3, it faced Microsoft’s early lead with the Xbox 360, Nintendo’s low-priced Wii, and a standards war between Blu-Ray and Toshiba-Microsoft’s HD-DVD. The PS3 doubled as a game console and Blu-Ray player, making its success important beyond gaming. Sony’s previous format efforts, BetaMax and UMD, had failed because competing technologies and limited content undermined demand.

The case traces the home-video-game industry from Atari’s launches and 1983 market collapse, caused by console saturation, poor software, and the costly failure of E.T., through Nintendo’s tightly controlled rise to more than 90% of the U.S. market by 1990. Nintendo combined quality standards, licensing controls, restrictive retailer terms, and scarce inventory. Its successor faced stronger competition from Sega, while Sony entered in 1994 with the 3D PlayStation, CD storage, and a broad game library. The PlayStation reached 60% of the U.S. market by 1999. Its successor, the PS2, added DVD playback and captured 55% of the console market by early 2006.

Console manufacturers generally earned little or lost money on hardware and relied on software royalties, typically $5–$7 per unit. Rising development costs and longer schedules created a blockbuster-driven market, while independent developers formed specialized studios and publishers acquired successful teams to secure talent and intellectual property. Microsoft’s $375 million purchase of Rare and Ubisoft’s $43 million acquisition of Red Storm illustrate this consolidation.

Internet connectivity renewed competition among console makers. Sega’s Dreamcast introduced a built-in modem and online console gaming, but hardware sales lagged. Sony gave PS2 developers broad freedom to implement networking, whereas Microsoft created the standardized Xbox Live service, required broadband, and monetized premium downloadable content through Xbox Live Marketplace and Xbox Live Arcade. Nintendo planned a Virtual Console offering older games, while Sony’s PlayStation Network Platform would support online play, communication, downloadable games, and third-party servers.

Sony and Microsoft primarily targeted core gamers, especially males in their twenties, while Nintendo shifted toward simple, accessible games for a broader audience. The Nintendo DS and the success of Nintendogs supported this strategy, which continued with the Wii and its motion-sensitive controller. The resulting competition became a three-way struggle among the PS3, Xbox 360, and Wii.

Concerns about increasingly realistic game violence also prompted regulatory scrutiny. A lawsuit linking violent games to the Columbine shootings was dismissed, but criticism of the Entertainment Software Ratings Board led to the addition of an Everyone 10+ rating. State restrictions were invalidated, while the proposed Family Entertainment Protection Act sought to restrict sales of mature games to minors.

Despite these challenges, analysts predicted the PS3 would hold just over 50% of the next-generation installed base by 2010, compared with 28.6% for Xbox 360 and 21.2% for Wii. The exhibits also show substantial hardware-related losses and rapidly declining game operating income for Sony, underscoring the financial cost of competing for leadership.

This week's Relist Watch column surveys the Supreme Court's relisted cert petitions early in its new term. The court denied review in several cases, including one on exceptions to appeal waivers in plea agreements; a death-penalty ineffective-assistance case, where Justice Sotomayor filed a dissent joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson; a Seventh Amendment jury-trial incorporation case, with Justice Gorsuch filing an opinion; and a school-district transgender policy case, where Justice Alito filed a dissent joined by Justices Thomas and Gorsuch. It also denied a Section 230 immunity case, and denied without recorded dissent two previously relisted "lost causes" involving the FDA's cell-removal policy and California's unclaimed property law.

The column's central focus is four consolidated petitions challenging 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3), which bars firearm possession by unlawful users or addicts of controlled substances, under the Second Amendment framework set out in *New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen*. The Fifth Circuit had held the statute unconstitutional as applied to most such users, and the Eighth Circuit reached a narrower holding; the government seeks review, with *Hemani* as lead case and the other three petitions held for it. Because the government's brief in *Hemani* is not due until month's end, the other cases will likely be resolved first.

The author also highlights *Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction, Inc.*, asking whether judicial estoppel can bar a plaintiff who failed to disclose a personal-injury claim in bankruptcy absent evidence of bad faith. The Fifth Circuit affirmed under its "rigid and unforgiving" rule, while Keathley argues this categorical approach conflicts with the intent-based approach of the Fourth, Sixth, Seventh, Ninth, and Eleventh Circuits; the government contends no true circuit split exists. The author calls this a serious candidate for grant.

Finally, four pro se prisoner petitions (three handwritten) raise procedural-error and other claims, including Miranda warning adequacy, First Step Act and habeas issues, wrongful conviction and alleged waste of federal funds, Section 230 and state-law liability for Twitter under Elon Musk's leadership, and probable cause and ineffective assistance of counsel. Additional relisted cases address religious accommodation preemption, servicemember tort claims, pre-handcuffing restraint, child-witness screens, courtroom closure, tribal criminal jurisdiction, dismissal of January 6, 2021 cases, peremptory strikes against Black venire members, and AEDPA deference.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 include a PMU with brown-out reset, early warning, and low-power core regulation; a clock module supporting internal and external oscillators, multiple power domains, and clock outputs; and a DMA controller with two full-feature channels, one basic channel, configurable triggers, transfer sizes, ping-pong interrupts, cascading, stride, and gather modes. An event manager supports peripheral-to-CPU interrupts, DMA triggers, and direct peripheral events.

The devices provide nonvolatile flash with in-circuit programming and 1KB erase sectors, zero-wait-state SRAM with 1KB-granularity write protection, up to 45 GPIO pins with filtering and low-power wakeup, and programmable IOMUX pad and peripheral-signal routing. Analog features include a 12-bit ADC operating up to 1.6 Msps, an internally connected temperature sensor with factory calibration, selectable 1.4V or 2.5V or external references, and a comparator with timer blanking, wakeup, fault handling, and an 8-bit reference DAC.

The LFSS contains a 32kHz real-time clock and an independent watchdog. The devices also include CRC-16 security, three UARTs, I2C supporting SMBus 3.0 and up to 1Mbps, SPI supporting multiple frame formats and up to 16Mbits/s, windowed and independent watchdog timers, general-purpose and advanced timers with PWM, capture/compare, quadrature encoding, cross-triggering, and fault handling. A two-wire SWD interface and DEBUGSS provide debugging, peripheral control, mailbox communication, reset and mode-change requests, and security features.

A typical application uses 10µF and 0.1µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000pF pulldown, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain I/O. TI provides development tools, documentation, support resources, device nomenclature guidance, revision history, package drawings, and orderable-part information.

Anthony Rizzo’s seventh home run and a two-run ninth-inning single helped the Chicago Cubs defeat the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0 Monday in Pittsburgh. The defining moment was Rizzo’s hard, leg-first slide at home in the eighth, which injured catcher Elias Diaz and allowed two runs. The play was ruled legal after review, prompting Pirates manager Clint Hurdle’s ejection and debate over modern MLB slide rules. Rizzo apologized, while Diaz said he remained in the game despite pain.

Spot starter Mike Montgomery, replacing injured Yu Darvish, carried the Cubs’ pitching, retiring the first 13 batters, allowing two singles over 5⅔ innings, striking out five and issuing no walks. Chad Kuhl allowed only Rizzo’s solo home run before losing, and Addison Russell added a pinch-hit two-run homer.

The Pirates fell to 2-8 in their last 10 games. Chicago recalled Luke Farrell and optioned Justin Hancock; Pittsburgh released George Kontos. David Freese and coach Joey Cora were separated after a dugout confrontation. The Cubs’ Ian Happ returned after shoulder soreness, while the Pirates shut down closer Felipe Vazquez because of forearm discomfort; no structural damage was found. Jon Lester was scheduled to face Pittsburgh Tuesday, with rookie Nick Kingham replacing Ivan Nova, who went on the 10-day disabled list with a sprained right ring finger.

DNA origami uses sequence-specific base pairing between a scaffold strand and shorter staple strands to form predefined nanostructures. Researchers led by Ralf Jungmann report in Nature Communications that DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy can visualize individual strands within assembled structures. Imaging showed that assembly remains robust despite variations in several physical parameters, including formation speed, but staple-strand incorporation efficiency depends on the target sequence’s position. Additional staples can improve efficiency, although some sites remain unoccupied in some structures. The method can guide nanomachine construction and may enable quantitative structural biology by measuring labeling efficiency for antibodies, proteins, and nucleic acids.

The paper studies modal extensions of logics based on lattice semantics, where each world uses values from a common lattice rather than necessarily the two-valued Boolean algebra. It introduces lattice terminology, designated values, filters, matrices, valuations, and modal extensions. A regular modal extension satisfies the principle that necessity means truth in every accessible world. On a complete lattice, the normal modal valuation interprets necessity as the meet of a formula’s values across accessible worlds; incomplete lattices may leave some modal formulas without a value.

The central result shows that the normal modal valuation yields a unique regular extension exactly when the designated values form a filter whose meet is designated. For finite lattices, regularity is equivalent to the designated values forming a filter. Examples illustrate failure of regularity with certain fuzzy designated sets and with non-principal ultrafilters over infinite Boolean algebras.

Further results connect modal validities to lattice structure. In complete lattices, every frame validates \((2\varphi \lor 2\psi)\to2(\varphi\lor\psi)\) exactly when the designated values are implicative. With a strictly deductive implication, validity of axiom K is equivalent to the lattice being linear outside the designated set. With implication defined as \(-x+y\), K is valid exactly when the lattice is implicative, provided negation is anti-monotone, involutive, and down-distribution holds. A twist-algebra construction provides a paraconsistent example in which every frame validates K precisely when the designated set contains all values whose first coordinate is 1. The paper also identifies the finite-model property of normal modal extensions as a subject for future research.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on October 29, 2020, announcing its third-quarter 2020 financial results. The filing incorporated a results press release and information on non-GAAP financial measures as exhibits and was signed by Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky.

South Carolina golfers Katelyn Dambaugh, Ainhoa Olarra and Ana Pelaez earned Golfweek All-America honors. Dambaugh made the First Team, while Olarra and Pelaez were Honorable Mention selections. No. 12-ranked Carolina was one of seven schools with at least three honorees. Dambaugh’s five career All-America selections set a program record; Olarra earned five top-10s, and freshman Pelaez posted a 73.12 scoring average and a regional medal.

The paper addresses data-driven modeling of noisy, high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems, where first-principles simulation may be unavailable or costly. It reviews dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) as a finite-dimensional approximation of Koopman and Perron–Frobenius operators, noting its usefulness for nonlinear and stochastic systems, dimensionality reduction, forecasting, and control. It also discusses reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and Gaussian process (GP) regression as nonparametric methods offering interpretable features, probabilistic predictions, and established convergence and consistency guarantees.

The authors combine these approaches by developing a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator and modifying extended DMD (EDMD). Their formulation uses noisy measurements, provides uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions, and integrates hyperparameter optimization with sparse dictionary learning. The method is presented as a special case of EDMD and therefore retains its limitations.

To improve the computational trade-off of kernel-based DMD, the work applies variational free energy to kernel Koopman operators. The formal model lifts training data into an RKHS, assumes isotropic Gaussian measurement noise, and uses operator-valued kernels to handle infinitely many output channels, yielding a posterior GP associated with the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture features a professor recapping entrepreneurship basics: planning is dynamic rather than static, the goals are to create and harvest value, investors ask three Whys (why this, why now, why this team) plus why it won't work, and time is the scarcest resource. He then introduces serial entrepreneur Bob Jones, who speaks on finding customers.

Jones argues that the only non-negotiable requirement for a business is customers, and that a product must be important and unique to someone. He advises selling benefits rather than products, identifying who will write the check and who influences them, understanding what customers actually want, and talking to them directly rather than relying on surveys or email. He recommends segmenting the market by motivation, starting with those feeling the most pain ("be a jockey, not a horse"), and notes that virtue is a tough sell.

Two case studies illustrate these points. Regain, a nutrition bar for dialysis patients, failed because Jones surveyed clinicians rather than the actual buyers, who were unlikely to change habits, had little money, and bought through pharmacies demanding slotting fees. NiteBite, a bar for nocturnal hypoglycemia developed with Harvard Medical School doctors, succeeded after Jones spoke with patients and parents, used a non-medical name, cold-called diabetes educators frustrated by patient non-compliance, generated demand first, and paid no slotting fees; the business was later sold to a billion-dollar pharmaceutical company.

Jones also describes his current sleep-drink prototype, arguing for testing whether a product works before polishing its packaging, and cites a classmate's pancake mix as a minimum viable product. He closes with questions for entrepreneurs: where customers seek help, how to reach them, who will write the first check, what evidence they will pay, and who will handle sales.

The team credited good goaltending, a simple approach, and getting pucks to the net for its first Stanley Cup Finals win. Ron Francis, Sami Kapanen, and Arturs played well. Baidu is adding NVIDIA Tesla P40 GPUs and deep learning software to Baidu Cloud for autonomous-driving AI, citing greater inference throughput and lower latency than CPUs. Its ADU is developing Level 4 automation, with commercialization targeted for 2018 and mass production for 2020.

The American Indian College Fund launched a two-year study, funded by a $600,000 Strada Education Network grant, to assess the economic and social returns of five North Dakota tribal colleges and universities. Working with the North Dakota Association of Tribal Colleges, the project will examine graduate employment, statewide and institutional returns on investment, and the value of Native American values through a Gallup survey of 5,000 College Fund scholars. A pilot study will also examine how tribal colleges preserve languages and culture and strengthen American Indian nations. The project is scheduled to conclude in September 2019, with results to be shared with state and federal policymakers. Participating institutions are Nueta Hidatsa Sahnish College, Sitting Bull College, United Tribes Technical College, Turtle Mountain Community College, and Cankdeska Cikana Community College.

An Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine-learning potential was developed for YBCO using DFT data covering equilibrium structures, all vacancy and interstitial defects, amorphous-like configurations, and oxygen Frenkel-pair transition states. The 1,368-configuration dataset produced accurate energy and force predictions and outperformed the Buckingham–Coulomb classical potential for the equation of state, lattice parameters, migration barriers, and defect formation energies.

Large NPT simulations reproduced YBCO’s orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition near 800 K, compared with approximately 1000 K experimentally. The transition results from oxygen migration from CuO-chain O1 sites, and to a lesser extent apical O4 sites, to interstitial O5 sites between the chains, randomizing their occupation and making the a and b directions equivalent. The transition is primarily entropy-driven, while thermal expansion lowers oxygen Frenkel-pair formation energy and facilitates disordering. The lower simulated transition temperature is consistent with experimental oxygen loss, which is absent from the particle-conserving simulations.

The potential enables accurate studies of oxygen diffusion and mass transport in complex cuprates and may support optimization of annealing strategies for radiation-damaged high-temperature superconducting tapes. Future work requires variable oxygen content and advanced simulation techniques to access experimentally relevant conditions and timescales.

This non-empirical article critically reviews how artificial intelligence affects inclusive education, focusing on theoretical foundations, practical applications, benefits, limitations, and recommendations. It defines inclusive education as providing all students—regardless of background or disability—with equal opportunities, belonging, accessibility, appropriate support, and curriculum adaptations. Persistent barriers include inadequate teacher training and technology skills, inaccessible or poorly organized materials, overcrowded classes, insufficient infrastructure and resources, weak communication, educator prejudice, labeling, and lack of parental and community involvement.

The review, conducted from September 2023 to March 2024 following PRISMA guidelines and using Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore, finds that AI can personalize instruction, provide rapid feedback, identify learning weaknesses, support adaptive and self-directed learning, increase engagement and motivation, improve communication, and assist students with disabilities. AI tools such as text-to-speech, speech-to-text, writing aids, chatbots, virtual assistants, and educational platforms may broaden access to resources, support language learners, raise awareness of diversity and unconscious bias, and automate grading, scheduling, data management, monitoring, and tutoring. However, educators remain essential for guidance, emotional support, creativity, critical thinking, and understanding students’ complex needs.

The article identifies limitations including biased or unrepresentative training data, curriculum bias, high implementation and maintenance costs, reduced human interaction, overreliance on technology, weakened critical-thinking and problem-solving skills, diminished social and emotional learning, privacy and security concerns, possible job displacement, physical effects of some technologies, and insufficient preparation for users. AI’s educational effects are not automatic and depend on thoughtful implementation, teacher involvement, collaboration, evaluation, culturally appropriate design, and diverse data.

An inclusive syllabus should incorporate accessible formats, assistive technologies, Universal Design for Learning, multiple options for representation, engagement, and expression, flexible and asynchronous access to materials, and offline alternatives where connectivity is limited. Educators should use technology to strengthen—not replace—human teaching and ensure meaningful mentoring, participation, and belonging. Further empirical research involving students, educators, families, and marginalized groups is needed to examine specific technologies, social and cultural contexts, and first-hand experiences. Recommendations include integrating AI into child-centered teaching, embedding inclusion in curricula and policy, creating safe and accessible classrooms, encouraging participation and awareness of inclusion, providing continuous professional development, and training educators in inclusive practices.

This final MIT OpenCourseWare lecture compares ion traps with neutral-atom traps and concludes with trapped-ion quantum computing. Unlike neutral atoms, ions can be confined by strong Coulomb forces, permitting room-temperature trapping, while Doppler, evaporative, and sideband cooling reduce their motion. Both platforms support atomic clocks, precision measurement, quantum information processing, and quantum simulation.

The lecture focuses on dynamic ion traps because a static electric potential cannot confine an ion in all directions. Penning traps combine electrostatic axial confinement with magnetic cyclotron confinement in the radial directions and have enabled highly precise ion-mass measurements. Paul, or RF, traps instead rapidly alternate between confinement and anti-confinement along different axes. Their micromotion produces an averaged restoring force and an effective harmonic potential for slow secular motion.

The lecture then explains the Cirac–Zoller gate as a simple trapped-ion quantum gate. Single-qubit operations are implemented through Bloch-sphere rotations, while a two-ion controlled-phase gate uses the ions’ shared center-of-mass vibration as a “data bus.” Sideband laser pulses transfer a control ion’s state into this vibrational mode, conditionally change the target ion’s phase, and then return the information to the control ion. This enables two-qubit operations between ions in a chain. The original gate requires center-of-mass motion to be cooled to its absolute ground state and becomes slower as the ion chain grows, motivating alternatives such as geometric and Sørensen gates.

Cadillac sold 35,020 vehicles globally in September 2017, up 16.5% year over year and extending its growth streak to 16 months. Year-to-date sales rose 20.9% to 256,613, putting the brand on pace to exceed 2016’s total. China grew 37.6%, and the XT5 led 2017 deliveries with 103,645 units.

On May 29, 2018, more than 400 Black-owned coffee businesses around the U.S. were expected to participate in National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day, promoting them as alternatives to Starbucks as it closed over 8,000 U.S. units for diversity training. The campaign also encouraged economic forums and circulating Black dollars within Black communities.

On November 29, 2016, NVIDIA’s Board amended and restated the company’s bylaws to implement proxy access and revise advance-notice requirements for stockholder director nominations. Effective immediately, Section 5(h) permits a stockholder or group of up to 20 holders, continuously owning at least 3% of NVIDIA’s voting power for three years, to include director nominees in annual meeting proxy materials, subject to the bylaws. Nominees may constitute the greater of two directors or 20% of the Board. Beginning with the 2018 annual meeting, non-proxy-access nominations require notice 90–120 days before the prior annual meeting’s anniversary, rather than 120–150 days. The bylaws also adjust notice deadlines for changed meeting dates and include related administrative and conforming changes.

A medRxiv preprint examined whether blood pressure (BP) relates differently to longitudinal cognitive decline in older Black and White adults. The study combined data from three harmonized aging cohorts and included 2,284 participants aged 55 or older who self-identified as Black or White, completed at least two cognitive assessments, and had at least two annual BP readings.

Participants were classified by race and BP status: normal, high, or variable BP. Cognitive performance was assessed with 19 neuropsychological tests covering global cognition and episodic memory, semantic memory, working memory, processing speed, and visuospatial ability. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated cognitive change over time while adjusting for age, sex, education, and diagnosis; results were corrected for multiple comparisons and tested in sensitivity analyses.

Normal BP was generally associated with similar cognitive-decline rates across racial groups, although some domain-specific exceptions appeared in the detailed results. White adults with high BP declined faster globally and in processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory than Black adults with high BP, while rates of episodic-memory and visuospatial decline were similar. White adults with variable BP declined faster globally and across all five cognitive domains than Black adults with variable BP; the detailed analyses also reported faster decline than all three Black comparison groups in each domain.

Secondary analyses indicated that lower baseline cognitive performance did not explain the reduced BP-cognitive association among Black adults. Results remained unchanged when cohort was modeled as a random effect and when time was modeled as a random slope.

The authors proposed autonomic nervous system dysregulation, chronic stress, and cumulative allostatic load—including disproportionate exposure to racism-related stress—as possible explanations, but these mechanisms were not directly tested. Limitations included not accounting for BP medication adherence and excluding a comprehensive medication history. The study supports maintaining healthy BP across racial groups and developing interventions tailored to racial disparities in cognitive decline.

AMD shares surged over 20% in premarket trading after the company announced a multiyear deal to supply OpenAI with high-performance AI accelerators, beginning with the MI450 series. OpenAI will receive warrants for up to 10% of AMD’s equity upon meeting production and performance milestones. Analysts said the agreement could generate tens of billions in potential revenue and strengthen AMD’s challenge to Nvidia amid competition from Intel. The announcement coincided with AMD’s $6 billion share-buyback plan, though analysts warned of production complexity, supply-chain bottlenecks, margin pressures, and uncertain demand.

Judges are sanctioning lawyers who submit briefs containing AI-generated false citations, quotations, and cases. In Puerto Rico, several firms will share $24,492 after opposing solo practitioners filed at least 55 defective citations; a judge reduced their initial $88,000 request and said the volume of errors suggested AI use despite denials. In California, Amir Mostafavi must pay $10,000 to the court for including fake quotes and off-topic cases in appellate briefs. Opposing counsel will receive no fees because they failed to detect the errors, raising questions about lawyers’ duty to identify hallucinations in opponents’ filings.

Following President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s death, the speaker assumes office and calls on Americans to remain united in defense of freedom, justice, tolerance, and democratic progress. He vows to continue the war against Germany and Japan without pause, rejects partial victory and compromise, demands unconditional surrender, and insists that war criminals be punished. He urges Congress and the American public to support the continuing Allied strategy and the creation of a strong United Nations organization to resolve international disputes and prevent future wars. Emphasizing that hope alone is insufficient, he argues that lasting peace requires cooperation among peace-loving nations, respect for international law, and collective defense. He also calls for expanded international trade and mutual economic progress, while reaffirming America’s obligations to its fallen soldiers, democratic ideals, and role in assisting liberated nations. The address concludes with a prayer for wisdom and the ability to serve the American people faithfully.

The contracting parties considered development work in the Congo to increase product supplies, including government missions, private procurement, and forest cultivation; Belgium agreed to facilitate such activity without restrictions. Belgian officials favored sending Congo supply-and-requirement memoranda primarily through the British Foreign Office. The article presents a monthly ETF momentum-rotation strategy that ranks SPY (S&P 500), EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets), and TLT (20-year Treasury bonds) by the previous month’s performance, invests in the strongest, holds it for one month, and repeats. SPY represents the most-followed stock index, EEM has lower correlation with SPY, and TLT is often considered a safe haven. A two-decade backtest outperformed buy-and-hold with lower drawdowns before poor performance in 2022 and the following five to six years. From an initial $100,000 in 2003, CAGR was 11% before commissions, slippage, and taxes; maximum drawdown was 22% before 2022, when the portfolio fell 41% from its peak. Trades occur at month-end, dividends are reinvested, and tax-deferred accounts are recommended because of frequent rotation.

Charlie Javice, founder of student financial-aid platform Frank, was sentenced to 85 months in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase by inflating the startup’s customer numbers before its 2021 acquisition for $175 million. Frank claimed to have served more than five million students but had fewer than 300,000 real customers; synthetic identities created with a data scientist made up the rest.

A jury convicted Javice and chief growth officer Olivier Amar on three fraud counts and one conspiracy count. Javice expressed remorse and asked for forgiveness. She also received three years of supervision, $22.36 million in forfeiture and $287 million in restitution to JPMorgan, and will remain on bail while appealing. Prosecutors had sought 12 years, while Javice’s attorney argued for a lighter sentence.

Ineos shut down the 450,000-bpd Forties Pipeline System, a key North Sea artery, after a hairline crack discovered last week widened; repairs could take "weeks." Brent crude rose nearly 2% on Monday, above $64.50 a barrel—a two-year high. The Forties system carries nearly 40% of the UK's North Sea oil production and links 85 offshore fields, and the BBC reported more than 80 platforms would need to shut down. A three-week closure could disrupt up to 10 million barrels, while OECD inventories stood only 140 million barrels above the five-year average (IEA, September). The UK would need to buy crude elsewhere, tightening an already pressured Atlantic Basin market. The outage also widened the Brent-WTI premium to nearly $7 a barrel, boosting demand for U.S. crude and potentially U.S. exports and inventory draws. Analysts expect a jittery Brent market for weeks, with the disruption echoing the recent Keystone pipeline spill.

The Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a divorce judgment granting shared legal custody of the parties’ four children, physical custody of the two older children to Wesley Wiechmann, and physical custody of the twins to Sylvia Wiechmann. This literature review examines artificial intelligence-assisted or AI-based training as a form of distance education for pandemic, disaster, and normal educational contexts. It notes that COVID-19 disrupted formal education, accelerating distance learning, whose effectiveness depends on infrastructure and access. It also argues that universities’ claims about digital transformation require further improvement.

The review defines artificial intelligence as systems that automatically perform programmed tasks, including machine and deep learning that enable computers to learn from large datasets. Examples such as Watson, AlphaGo, BabyX, and autonomous vehicles demonstrate advances in learning, decision-making, and problem-solving. AI currently resembles human performance at some lower competency levels but falls short at the highest levels.

Educational applications include personalized instruction, intelligent education systems, administration, data management, game-based learning, examinations, and spelling analysis. Intelligent Education Systems combine domain, pedagogy, and learner models, using data, feedback, and adaptive activities. Three proposed teaching models are AI-supported face-to-face education, face-to-face teaching by AI through screens or human-like robots, and simulation-based education. These may use human-defined algorithms or deep learning in which AI independently personalizes curricula and instructional decisions.

Learning environments may be classroom-based with virtual teachers or online through virtual and augmented reality. Immersive simulations could provide realistic experiences and access to learning otherwise unavailable. Cited studies associate AI-supported systems with improved motivation, learning, prediction accuracy, and student emotions.

Potential benefits include lower training costs and risks, scalable individualized instruction, better decision-making, and alternatives to conventional schooling. Risks include human control, privacy and cybersecurity threats, isolation, psychological and personality effects, confusion between simulation and reality, educator unemployment, and uncertain consequences of machine-only education. Because computers still lack human mental capacity, the review concludes that society should prepare for further development, research AI-based distance education, simulation, and augmented reality, and carefully examine their social, philosophical, and ethical implications.

The Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1, winning nine of 10 games and moving 13 games above .500 for the first time since 2014. The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification defines AMD’s process for developing, validating, distributing, and deploying runtime firmware patches. SFS enables nonpersistent updates to selected AMD-provided firmware on microprocessors without a BIOS reflash or system reboot. It targets priority runtime issues in AMD binary components included in AGESA releases, such as ASP firmware, modules, and register settings, but excludes customer BIOS and other x86 components such as SMM, AGESA, UEFI, and run-once code such as ABL. Updates do not survive reboots and are intended as interim fixes between BIOS releases.

Customers are responsible for deciding whether to deploy patches, testing them in their own environments, and operating an SFS Deployment Agent that communicates with the PSP/ASP driver to track and apply updates. Patches can be applied during OS boot, immediately after boot, or during normal operation and must be reapplied after every reboot. Packages are tied to a specific PI release, base patch, and firmware level and include release notes.

AMD cryptographically signs every package. Customers may optionally co-sign packages to retain approval authority over updates. During early boot, before `BOOT_DONE`, customer BIOS code must provide an RSA public key to the ASP; the key cannot be changed afterward. The ASP verifies the customer signature, when required, followed by AMD’s signature. BIOS developers explicitly enable SFS and co-signing through APCB tokens, both of which are disabled by default. OEM/ODM firmware generally owns the root of trust for updates, while the ASP serves as AMD’s root of trust for detecting and validating signed firmware.

SFS uses three version levels. The monotonic SFS Patch Level identifies the installed package and prevents rollback. Individual firmware components retain firmware and Security Patch Level versions. The monotonic System Patch Level records run-once code executed by SFS since the last reboot. The host OS can query these and the underlying firmware versions through an SFS command.

A package may modify registers or other values, replace a complete microprocessor firmware image, or update portions of a firmware package. Patches check current version and patch levels before applying. Multi-socket and multiple-package deployments are handled sequentially. SEV updates are committed to prevent rollback and require a reboot to revert; SNP systems require update pages to be HV-FIXED through `RMPUPDATE`.

Packages are validated as a whole to avoid partially applied updates and firmware version mismatches. If any portion cannot be fully applied, the package should not be applied, avoiding a forced reset. Attestation evidence and measurements are made available through interfaces such as SPDM and DPE.

To issue commands, the customer agent creates a 2 MB-aligned `TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER`, appends any co-signing header, AMD package, and customer signature, and passes the buffer’s physical address to the primary ASP. The ASP protects the package memory from x86 access, validates the required signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Separate commands report firmware and patch versions.

Packages are named `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg`, with a monotonically increasing package number. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal expected performance impact. Some operations may require brief quiescence; for example, SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for an SEV firmware update, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating during the update.

Portable air cleaners and improved ventilation may offer a low-cost way to improve student outcomes. Following a natural-gas leak in Aliso Canyon, California, one study found that students in schools with air filters gained about three months of math learning and nearly as much in English, with gains persisting or increasing over time. The filters cost roughly $30 per student, compared with about $7,000 per student for the class-size reduction discussed. Other cited research found lower absenteeism and improved test scores and pass rates after air-quality interventions, although larger trials are needed.

The passage identifies three potential benefits: cleaner air may support cognition by reducing harmful particulate exposure and inflammation; fewer respiratory illnesses may improve attendance and instructional continuity; and air cleaning may benefit students in low-income communities who are more likely to attend schools near pollution sources or in poorly ventilated older buildings. Unlike class-size reductions or high-dosage tutoring, portable air cleaners require relatively little administrative work. The author recommends reconnecting unused units, replacing filters, piloting and expanding air-cleaning programs, monitoring attendance and other outcomes, and funding further research.

El trabajo analiza la aplicación del neuromarketing en el sector audiovisual, definida como el uso de técnicas de neuroimagen para comprender la conducta humana en los mercados. Desde los años noventa, su incorporación como complemento del marketing tradicional busca mejorar la competitividad y el retorno de la inversión de las empresas ante los cambios impuestos por las plataformas digitales y las nuevas formas de consumo audiovisual.

En el ámbito internacional, empresas como Viacom, Cartoon Network, ESPN y The Weather Channel utilizan estas técnicas para testar contenidos, evaluar promociones y mejorar bloques publicitarios. El análisis de 104 webs de miembros de la Nmsba encontró referencias a servicios para la industria del entretenimiento en 19 casos (18%), con presencia主要集中在 Estados Unidos y Reino Unido.

El objetivo del estudio es determinar el estado del neuromarketing en el sector audiovisual español, analizar el perfil del profesional, sus prácticas y desarrollo futuro, identificar las empresas que lo emplean y valorar sus beneficios y limitaciones. Se采用了 una metodología cualitativa basada en 18 entrevistas en profundidad realizadas entre junio y septiembre de 2015 con consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos.

Los resultados confirman que el estudio neurocientífico del consumidor audiovisual es factible, aunque presenta dificultades relacionadas con la ética, la interpretación y aplicación de los datos y la obtención de muestras representativas. Su aplicación requiere equipos multidisciplinares con especialistas en neurociencia, marketing, comunicación y, en algunos casos, ingeniería biomédica. La especialización impide hablar todavía de un profesional integral del neuromarketing; por ello, resulta necesario seguir el método científico en el diseño, recogida e interpretación de las investigaciones.

En España, esta práctica es incipiente y emergente, y se concentra principalmente en Atresmedia y Mediaset España. Entre las barreras señaladas destacan el desconocimiento y la desconfianza hacia el neuromarketing, ambos mencionados por el 80 % de las consultoras, la falta de actitudPDATIVA, la mala praxis de terceros y el coste de los estudios. Los servicios se orientan al análisis de contenidos y a la mejora de la eficacia publicitaria. Mediaset ha-tested ficción en horario prime time mediante registros de actividad electrodérmica complementados con encuestas; Atresmedia ha recurrido a EEG, EMG, conductancia galvánica y actividad cardíaca para estudiar anuncios, aunque abandonó una línea de prueba de contenidos al no poder identificar con precisión las causas de los resultados. TVE no participó en el estudio.

Las productoras cinematográficas y televisivas muestran interés por medir el engagement y reducir sesgos de las metodologías tradicionales, pero todavía invierten poco debido a sus presupuestos, la falta de una cultura de investigación y la ausencia de intermediarios dentro de las producciones. Se considera que el neuromarketing podría utilizarse en fases intermedias de producción y para evaluar audiencias exteriores, aunque no resolvería problemas esenciales de las películas.

La evolución futura se considera positiva, aunque dependent de avances tecnológicos, estandarización, mejor interpretación de los datos, aumento del conocimiento, reducción de costes y demostración de su eficacia. También se confía en una mayor transferencia universidad-empresa. El trabajo concluye que el neuromarketing audiovisual es una aplicación todavía emergente en España, con posibilidades de crecimiento, pero aún limitada por la tecnología, la interpretación, el precio, la cultura empresarial y la necesidad de demostrar su utilidad.

A study in *Nature Climate Change* describes sudden, catastrophic ecosystem shifts across Australia caused by gradual climate change combined with extreme weather. Although many ecosystems are near-pristine and adapted to Australia’s variable climate, these pressures are overwhelming their resilience and producing abrupt, potentially irreversible changes, including population collapses, local extinctions, loss of ancient ecosystems, and novel communities invaded by new species.

Since the start of the 19th century, Australia’s average air and sea temperatures have risen about 1°C. Heatwaves, extreme fire weather, fire seasons, rainfall shifts, and droughts are becoming more frequent, intense, or prolonged, with shorter intervals between events. Examples include kelp forests becoming seaweed turf after a 2011 marine heatwave, wildfire destruction of Gondwanan refugia in 2016, Murray River floodplain dieback after the 2001–2009 drought, alpine forest conversion to shrubland through repeated fires, arid-zone boom-and-bust after extreme rain, and Gulf of Carpentaria mangrove dieback after a weak 2015–2016 monsoon.

Most affected systems had little prior human disturbance, showing that undisturbed ecosystems are not necessarily more resilient. Extreme events can push systems past tipping points, while cascading interactions can cause ecosystem-wide responses. Collapse can eliminate fisheries, forest resources, carbon storage, tourism, and water supplies. Predicting collapses is essentially impossible. Targeted interventions may help but are costly, increasingly difficult as events recur sooner, and carry uncertain consequences; the authors argue that doing nothing may increasingly pose greater risks than acting.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us Research Program Registered Tier v7 data to develop models predicting healthy aging from social determinants of health (SDOH). Eligible participants were aged 50 or older, had responded to SDOH surveys, and had electronic health records. Healthy aging was defined using a composite of modified Charlson Comorbidity Index, mild cognitive impairment, and assisted-living status, with primary and more stringent age-based cohorts.

The primary cohort included 99,936 participants, of whom 44,109 (44.1%) met the healthy-aging definition; the secondary cohort included 62,475 participants, of whom 6,648 (10.6%) did so. Logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost models were trained and evaluated with oversampling and undersampling approaches. All achieved AUROC values above 0.7. XGBoost with random oversampling performed best, with AUROCs of 0.795 and 0.862 in the primary and secondary cohorts, respectively. The model demonstrated predictive parity across race and sex groups, with no evidence of bias in accuracy or positive predictive value.

SHAP analysis identified health insurance type as the strongest predictor, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. These findings indicate that health insurance is an important correlate of healthy aging. Limitations included the study’s operational definition of healthy aging, possible selection bias and limited representativeness of volunteer All of Us participants, unmeasured confounding, and unexpected positive associations for substance and alcohol use.

The Bengals acquired 40-year-old quarterback Joe Flacco from the Browns for a 2026 fifth-round pick, receiving a sixth-round selection in return. The study simulates replacing internal-combustion vehicles with battery electric vehicles using anonymized UnipolTech telematics data from 10,441 private-car users in Asti, Italy, covering October 2023–September 2024. After cleaning, the dataset contains 10.14 million trips and more than 98.9 million kilometers. Recorded trips are replicated exactly for four BEV models with different battery capacities, road-specific consumption, and ranges, under four charging policies involving workplace, overnight, threshold-based AC, and fast DC charging.

State of charge is updated per trip, and feasibility, monthly charging frequency, and post-trip state of charge are measured. Workplace-only charging performs worst, allowing an average of 64–88% of trips. Overnight and fast-charging policies perform better. Under the best case—50 kW DC charging with the Audi A6 e-tron—95% of users are considered suitable and 72% can complete all their trips without changing driving habits, but 5% remain unserved. With overnight charging, even the Fiat 500e is suitable for 35% of users.

Fast charging and low-state-of-charge AC charging require roughly half as many sessions as overnight charging for the Audi, although frequent charging remains burdensome for smaller vehicles. Overnight charging produces the highest average post-trip state of charge, above 70% for every model. The analysis assumes constant energy consumption and charging power, treats charging as available at every parking event, excludes costs, and requires testing in other regions to establish generalizability.

U.S. stocks rallied on October 22, 2001, as better-than-expected earnings outweighed concerns about anthrax and the Afghanistan conflict. The Dow gained 1.9% to 9,377.03, the Nasdaq rose 2.2% to 1,708.06, bonds were mixed and the dollar strengthened. American Express, semiconductor stocks, U.S. Steel, 3M, Conoco and USX-Marathon rallied, while SBC Communications fell. Fourth-quarter profit forecasts remained cautious, and the Conference Board’s leading economic indicators fell 0.5% in September, their largest monthly decline since January 1996.

Enron disclosed that the SEC had requested information about related-party transactions involving LJM Cayman and LJM2, partnerships created and run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron called the request an informal inquiry, pledged cooperation and said auditors and attorneys had reviewed the arrangements, the board had approved them and they were disclosed in SEC filings. Enron shares fell 21% to $20.65, losing roughly $4.2 billion in market value and extending their 75% decline for the year.

Enron had disclosed a $35 million partnership-related charge and said it would repurchase 55 million shares to unwind its involvement, reducing shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. It also recorded a $1.01 billion third-quarter charge largely tied to failed investments. Analysts raised concerns that dismantling other Enron-affiliated entities could cost as much as $3 billion and dilute shareholders. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt on watch for a possible downgrade.

An Enron shareholder filed a Texas derivative lawsuit alleging that the board breached its fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to operate partnerships that transacted with Enron and presented a conflict of interest. Shapiro Haber & Urmy also filed a securities-fraud class action for Enron stock purchasers from July 13 through October 16, alleging that material facts about the partnerships were misrepresented or concealed. Enron said it had not seen the derivative lawsuit and did not comment on pending litigation.

Separately, UniPrime Capital signed a letter of intent with Jessel Enterprises for a partial interest in an Enron Wind ground lease covering more than 3,000 acres in California’s Tehachapi Valley. The project was rated at approximately 64 megawatts, could serve about 40,000 residential customers and was projected to generate $96 million annually.

Institute boss Kevin Deery was frustrated by his side’s third consecutive draw, against Larne at Drumahoe on Friday. He believed Institute deserved all three points but lacked finishing and showed poor decision-making in both penalty areas. The club has scored only two own goals in 180 minutes, while several chances hit the woodwork or were ruled offside. Virginia defeated North Carolina 71–63 in the ACC Tournament championship at Barclays Center, where the tournament is expected to return. The event also featured Duke–UNC rivalry games, Marvin Bagley III’s NBA draft prospects, and Clemson’s first NCAA Tournament berth in seven years.

A February 6, 2002 news compilation detailed the investigations and fallout from Enron’s collapse. Before congressional committees, Enron director William Powers testified that off-balance-sheet partnerships inflated earnings, concealed debt and losses, and enriched senior executives. He said Enron knew its partnerships were losing money but continued transferring stock to Raptor to offset the losses. Powers criticized the oversight failures of Chairman Kenneth Lay, former CEO Jeffrey Skilling, former CFO Andrew Fastow and other executives, though he declined to characterize investors as defrauded. Fastow, Skilling and Michael Kopper were scheduled to testify, while Congress subpoenaed Lay after he canceled a voluntary appearance; Lay was expected to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights.

Hearings also examined the effects on employees and investors. Labor Secretary Elaine Chao discussed retirement protections, while witnesses described retirement-account losses and a three-week restriction on stock sales affecting more than 20,000 participants. Arthur Andersen’s Joseph Berardino faced criticism over the firm’s consulting and auditing of Enron, while the company maintained that information had been withheld from auditors.

Enron’s debtor-in-possession financing was projected to shrink from $1.5 billion to between $250 million and $500 million as banks struggled to syndicate it. Other developments included roughly $440,000 in unpaid broadband-unit taxes, a dispute over the Astros’ “Enron Field” naming agreement, and a Spanish regulatory investigation into Enron’s distribution operations. Commentary also addressed broader investor distrust of corporate accounting, widening bond spreads, professional conflicts of interest, and whistleblower Sherron Watkins’s warning to Lay that Enron could “implode in a wave of accounting scandals.”

IES Holdings, a diversified U.S. infrastructure services provider with roots in electrical contracting and operations at 130-plus locations, has nearly doubled year to date and outperformed infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks. Data-center projects are helping its next two largest divisions despite residential weakness. Backlog exceeds $2 billion and is growing 20% year over year, with stronger cash flow and record cash. The author recommends waiting for a pullback, citing overextension, a non-subpar FCF yield, and higher insider sales.

The Maui News confirmed that former Maui County Councilmember and mayor candidate Mike Victorino struck two teenagers on April 13. Police said the teens were not in a crosswalk, speed and alcohol were not factors, and both sustained nonlife-threatening injuries. The older teen’s mother disputed the crosswalk detail, while Victorino expressed sorrow and wished both youths a full recovery.

Linebackers are second-level defensive players positioned 3–5 yards behind the defensive line. They align teammates, relay coaching calls, and contribute to both run and pass defense. Their name reflects their original role supporting the defensive line in football’s run-heavy early era. Common positions include Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack. Required traits include vision, agility, explosiveness, tackling strength, block-shedding ability, violent hands, and a high motor; a typical listed build is 5'10"–6'5", 215–255 pounds, and lean-muscular. The passage highlights Hall of Fame linebackers Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor and their numerous career honors. Although the value of inside linebackers has declined as offenses become more pass-oriented, versatile linebackers remain important for rushing the passer, covering receivers, stopping runs, and creating mismatches. Typically, three to six linebackers are selected in the first round of each NFL draft.

During the first two on-campus gamedays, attendance was 37,583 and 27,038. Entry queues and concession-line congestion at the opener improved by the second game. ASCSU reported low awareness of the tailgat lot, which many students used only for parking, and plans to rebrand it and add pregame programming.
