Transportation options performed well: 7,000 attendees used transit at the first game, while MAX, park-and-ride, bicycles, and other alternatives were popular. Student re-park also worked well, though 50 vehicles were towed from campus gameday lots each weekend; similar numbers were towed from neighborhood permit zones, and owners’ affiliations were unknown.

The Canadian dollar rose nearly to 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday, about 2% above the prior week, as market expectations of economic strength outweighed the Bank of Canada’s preference for a weaker currency to support exporters. After reaching a May 4 low of 72.73 cents, the loonie has lacked clear direction amid conflicting signals. Oil prices below US$45 and a widening Canada-U.S. interest-rate gap have pressured it, while strong first-quarter growth, employment and business investment suggest economic recovery. Recent Bank of Canada comments led CIBC to forecast a rate hike in the fourth quarter rather than 2018.

The Great Southern Storm have named a 45-player colts squad for the Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin next month. Glynn Verbruggen replaces long-serving coach Phil Gilbert, who has moved to Perth. North Albany has the most representatives (12), followed by Railways (eight), and Albany and Royals (seven each). The squad will hold two training sessions at Railways on June 4 and 11 at 5.30pm before a travelling team is selected.
A district sessions court sentenced four murder convicts: Shehzado to death, Ajab and Fateh Khan, and Dilbar Khan to 25 years’ imprisonment, with fines ranging from Rs. 105,000 to Rs. 200,000.

Allen Iverson discussed his memoir, “Misunderstood,” and his journey to sobriety with Stephen A. Smith on ESPN’s “First Take.” He called his 2013 divorce from Tawanna Turner, which coincided with the end of his NBA career, his lowest point and a catalyst for deep self-reevaluation. The experience of seeing “Iverson vs. Iverson” on divorce papers brought him to tears. Iverson recognized alcohol as a major problem and pursued sobriety because it was contributing to negative experiences. He and Turner, married in 2001, separated in 2008 and finalized their divorce in 2013, but have since reunited. His memoir covers his difficult childhood and rise to NBA stardom. Iverson also praised his influence on younger players, saying he helped them feel comfortable expressing themselves.

An online 4×2 mixed experiment evaluated whether role-taking and literacy interventions reduce reliance on demographic and appearance cues during social-engineering decisions. The 139 eligible participants were assigned to Persuader, Persuadee, Literacy, or control groups. They rated trust and hotspot acceptance for 16 face-validated personas before the intervention and one week later. Role-taking participants completed three scenarios involving financial advisors and letting agents, while the Literacy group received two educational sessions on stereotypes, trust, and decision-making.

Repeated-measures analyses found no statistically significant pre-to-post changes in risk-taking or trust across age, gender, ethnicity, or attire, and Bayes factors generally supported the null hypothesis. Word-of-mouth responses also remained stable. Issue involvement decreased significantly overall, while one small interaction involving self-esteem and attire affected trust ratings. Covariate analyses did not materially change the main findings.

Participants described the intervention as engaging, eye-opening, and thought-provoking, although some requested more varied and interactive materials. Limitations included hypothetical scenarios, short intervention duration, potential demand and social-desirability effects, and the static comic format. The study concludes that role-taking may promote reflection and awareness but that brief educational or immersive interventions alone may not alter deeply ingrained biases; longer-term, more interactive, and immersive designs warrant further investigation.

Texas’ HB 8 will replace STAAR in the 2027-28 school year with three shorter tests at the beginning, middle and end of the year. Districts may choose from TEA-approved national assessments for the first two exams, while the agency will develop the third. All three will use percentile rankings, and the final test will assess curriculum mastery. Results are expected within two days, allowing teachers to adjust instruction more quickly.

The law bans practice and benchmark tests for grades 3-8 and directs the Texas Education Agency to examine reducing testing’s weight in school accountability ratings. However, that report is not due until 2029-30, its recommendations are not required, and a new student-progress measure will not be ready when the system launches. As a result, the end-of-year test and existing accountability pressures are expected to remain largely unchanged.

Supporters say the law will reduce testing time and preparation while giving educators more insight into student growth. Critics counter that three exams could increase stress, particularly if TEA applies STAAR’s lockdown procedures, which include lengthy tests, spaced seating and controlled restroom breaks. Parents and teachers also want fewer restrictions and greater educator input. Some districts favor including MAP, an adaptive, norm-based test that measures growth and is widely viewed as less stressful than STAAR. HB 8 creates an educator committee to review the final exam, while also requiring TEA to track pre-K, extracurricular and workforce participation, though those factors will not affect school ratings.

The passage frames Germany's "Berlin-Bagdad" problem as how effectively it can organize the territory under its political and military influence to use the resources and manpower of Middle Europe for its own foreign purposes. Four critical political problems follow: the Poles, the Czechs, the South Slavs, and Bulgaria. If these peoples become willing accomplices or helpless servants, Berlin will hold mastery of Central Europe. U.S. policy, it argues, need not obstruct free economic and cultural interplay or unification in the region, but must disestablish a system in which adventurous and imperialistic groups in Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest exploit that area's resources for a selfish foreign policy directed against neighbors and the rest of the world. The U.S. interest lies primarily in the nature of the control rather than in economic unity itself.

Present control rests on an alliance of interests among the ruling powers at Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, Constantinople, and Berlin: the common interests of Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest in subordinating Poles, Czechs, and Croats; Berlin's control over Austria-Hungary's external affairs and military and economic resources; Vienna and Budapest's German-Magyar ascendency; Sofia's tie through Germany's exploitation of Bulgaria's wrong under the Treaty of Bucharest; Constantinople's partly bought, partly coerced interest and the possibility of nominal Turkish integrity within the German alliance; and, after the war, the debts of Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria, and Turkey to Germany.

Two U.S. assets are described. The first is the economic weapon: control of outer-world commerce and the possibility of excluding Germany from raw materials, rich markets, and communication routes. This weighs heavily on German minds because demobilization requires raw materials and markets, and without them the army becomes discontented and dangerous. Coupled with a vision of world cooperation, it exploits fear and hope and can win major concessions, especially after the peace conference assembles, when protracted negotiation gives added bargaining power. Its appeal is broad — revolution to the dynasty and ruling classes, financial ruin to commercial classes, prolonged inability to demobilize to the army, and continued hardship to the poor.

The second asset is in Austria-Hungary: the nationalistic discontent of the Czechs and probably South Slavs, which, with a possible Poland, could break the coalition of Austrian Poles and German Austrians. The Emperor and ruling powers wish to emerge with Francis Joseph's patrimony unimpaired, manifesting as a policy of no annexations and a sincere desire for disarmament and a league of nations, motivated by Austria's inability to sustain armaments and its search for a guarantee of the status quo. The more turbulent the subject nationalities and the more the Magyar-Austrian ascendency feels threatened with extinction, the more fervent Austria-Hungary's wish to become a fit partner in a league of nations. U.S. policy therefore should first stir nationalist discontent, then refuse its extreme logic of dismembering Austria-Hungary; threatening the German-Magyar combination with uprisings while offering a mode of safety would reduce its resistance and accelerate its independence from Berlin in foreign affairs.

The paper proves that strong pseudorandom unitaries exist in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM), where parties have oracle access to a Haar-random unitary and its inverse. A strong PRU is efficiently computable and computationally indistinguishable from a Haar-random unitary even when adversaries can query both the constructed unitary and its inverse.

The construction uses three key components \(k_1,k_2,k_3\) and defines
\[
G_U(1^\lambda,k)=X^{k_3}U_\lambda X^{k_2}U_\lambda X^{k_1},
\]
where \(U_\lambda\) is a Haar-random oracle. It makes two Haar-oracle queries and requires only \(O(\log^{1+\epsilon}(n))\) random bits for any constant \(\epsilon\), while remaining secure against polynomial-query adversaries.

The security proof extends the Ma–Huang path-recording framework. Haar-random oracles are replaced by path-recording isometries that record queries in left and right databases. The paper introduces an approximate isometry \(S\) that merges two independent databases into one while simulating the three keys. A query-by-query analysis establishes negligible operator-norm differences between the relevant forward and inverse oracle orderings. A sequence of hybrid arguments then connects the real PRU experiment to two independent Haar-random unitaries, using Haar invariance and modified operators with independent left and right records.

The work fills a gap left by prior results: pseudorandom states and function-like state generators were known in the QHROM, while forward-only PRUs were known in the weaker inverseless variant.

The work introduces LAPIS, an MLIR-based compiler framework intended to combine performance, portability, and productivity for computational science and AI/ML. Traditional HPC frameworks such as Kokkos emphasize performance and portability but offer less productivity, while frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow emphasize productivity but require manual integration with optimized libraries and can be difficult to extend to new architectures. The paper identifies a second interoperability problem: large C++ scientific simulations commonly incorporate machine-learning surrogates written in Python, requiring substantial boilerplate and effort. LAPIS aims to compile Python-based ML functions into Kokkos C++ source that can be integrated directly with scientific applications.

LAPIS uses the MLIR compiler infrastructure to provide an automatic, end-to-end pipeline from high-level MLIR to portable parallel C++. Its contributions include a custom Kokkos-inspired dialect, mappings for Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations, lowering passes for accelerator support and hierarchical parallelism, a portable memory-reference model, and a Kokkos emitter that generates C++ source. The dialect represents parallel loops, reductions, synchronization, memory operations, and dense matrix operations such as GEMM and GEMV.

The framework accepts linalg-on-tensors MLIR and supports the torch-mlir and MPACT frontends. Dense PyTorch programs can be exported through TorchScript and torch-mlir, while MPACT supports dense and sparse Torch modules through TorchFX. LAPIS lowers linear algebra into parallel loops or Kokkos Kernels calls, maps those loops to Kokkos execution policies, estimates team sizes and vector lengths, and inserts required synchronization. Loop depth determines whether Kokkos range, team-thread, or thread-vector policies are used. Runtime estimates are generated for dynamically sized sparse traversals, including CSR-like patterns, and vector lengths are clamped to backend limits.

LAPIS also introduces Kokkos-style memory constructs, including DualView handling and automatic device synchronization, to support heterogeneous systems while avoiding unnecessary overhead in single-memory environments. The custom dialect is intended to fill gaps in MLIR’s architecture-specific dialects and incomplete lowering paths.

The paper demonstrates one sparse and two dense linear algebra operations on AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs, reporting performance comparable to hand-optimized implementations. It also demonstrates coupling scientific computing and AI/ML workloads in SciML and image-processing use cases across the same three architectures.

The related-work review compares LAPIS with TACO, COMET, MPACT, Triton, DaCe, DISTAL, SpDistal, and LegateSparse. It highlights limitations such as TACO’s lack of AMD GPU support, COMET’s CPU focus, Triton’s emphasis on dense matrix multiplication and CUDA/HIP, and the distributed-memory focus of several other systems. LAPIS builds on MLIR and Kokkos to simplify extension to new architectures while supporting performance portability.

The State Bar of Michigan’s May 23, 2001 e-Journal contains case summaries covering bankruptcy, civil rights, constitutional and criminal law, employment, family law, insurance, litigation, municipal and real-property law, negligence, and intentional tort. In *In re Hood*, the Sixth Circuit Bankruptcy Appellate Panel held that the Tennessee Student Assistance Corporation lacked sovereign immunity in an educational-loan discharge action. Unpublished Michigan Court of Appeals summaries address employment discrimination, jury instructions, discovery sanctions, ineffective assistance, parental-rights termination, insurance loss-payable clauses, expert-witness deadlines, zoning variances, and negligence and premises liability. The issue also lists practice-area attorneys, bar events, classified advertisements, employment openings, contacts, archived e-Journals, and instructions for obtaining a text version or managing subscriptions.

Customers criticized Chipotle’s new queso for its $2.95 price and taste; small orders cost $3.95 and large orders $6.25. Chris Arnold said 63% of testers were more likely to visit more often, but no price cut was planned due to its whole ingredients.

Peggy Mahoney forwarded an August 25, 2000 Energy Central Deregulation Public Forum email to several Enron colleagues. The new question notes that natural gas supplies 25% of U.S. electricity but is expected to fuel nearly 95% of planned power plants, and asks whether policy should encourage gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf to address possible shortages and record winter prices. Responses were requested by September 15, 2000, with selected responses to be published.

The previous question asked whether generators manipulated California’s wholesale market, raising San Diego Gas & Electric bills, and whether price caps should protect ratepayers. Respondents disagreed: some attributed price spikes to supply shortages, high fuel costs, weather, regulatory constraints, or market design, while others alleged withholding, collusion, or insufficient competition. Proposed responses included expanded generation and transmission, market-based solutions, cost-based regulation, price caps, greater efficiency, consumer education, and allowing new market entrants to address shortages.

Paul Clement is set to become Swansea manager after Bayern Munich permitted him to speak to the club. The 44-year-old is Swansea’s first choice to replace Bob Bradley, with a proposed deal until 2019 and a possible £30 million transfer budget. Owners Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan are willing to invest while the club sits 19th in the Premier League after conceding 44 goals in 19 matches.

Riots in East Berlin in 1953 and Poznán in 1956 were suppressed by Soviet troops, but Hungary’s 1956 revolt was nationwide, and its brutal Soviet repression marked a turning point for the Soviet Union and NATO. Hungary’s Communist government, led by Mátyás Rákosi, had eliminated political opponents and pursued collectivization and rapid industrialization, generating widespread discontent. Soviet de-Stalinization, the example of Titoist Yugoslavia, economic failure, and developments in Poland further emboldened Hungarian dissidents. After Mikoyan’s visit led to Rákosi’s replacement by Ernő Gero, the release of Władysław Gomułka in Poland inspired a student rally in Budapest. A subsequent confrontation with state police triggered nationwide revolutionary councils advocating nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet withdrawal.

Soviet tanks entered Budapest on 24 October, briefly withdrew, and returned after massing forces while international attention was diverted by the Suez crisis. The Soviet Union launched a major invasion on 3–4 November. Hungarian resistance fighters fought courageously but were gradually defeated; resistance ended by 30 November. Approximately 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers were killed.

A federal judge dismissed Drake’s lawsuit over Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us,” calling the “certified pedophile” lyric nonactionable opinion and hyperbolic language from a heated rap battle. The court also dismissed Drake’s claims against Universal Music Group, and Drake plans to appeal.

The case examines how Mexico-based CEMEX became a global building-materials leader through four stages of internationalization: laying groundwork, stepping out, growing up, and stepping up. Between 1982 and 2007, CEMEX grew from a privately held cement producer with 6,500 employees and $275 million in revenue to a public company with 65,000 employees, operations in 50 countries, and $21.7 billion in annual revenue.

Under CEO Lorenzo Zambrano, CEMEX prepared for globalization by divesting noncore businesses, developing export opportunities, investing in satellite communications, and implementing an Executive Information System that gave managers access to operational data and enabled virtual inspections. Its 1989 acquisition of Tolteca made it Mexico’s second-largest cement producer and a top-ten global producer, while competition from Holcim and U.S. trade duties reinforced the need to expand abroad.

CEMEX entered Spain in 1992 by acquiring Valenciana and Sanson for $1.8 billion, gaining a 28% market share. The acquisition countered Holcim’s growing Mexican position, provided access to lower-cost capital, and offered linguistic and cultural advantages. Applying CEMEX’s Mexican operating practices generated $120 million in annual benefits and raised operating margins from 7% to 24%. CEMEX also adopted the Spanish plants’ use of petroleum coke and formalized its post-merger integration process.

As CEMEX expanded through acquisitions in Venezuela, Colombia, the Caribbean, the Philippines, and Indonesia, it learned that integration required both transferring standardized practices and learning from acquired companies. This approach became known as the “CEMEX Way,” emphasizing global knowledge management, dissemination of best practices, standardized processes, information and Internet technologies, and innovation. Multinational functional teams cataloged acquired practices in a central database, benchmarked them, and promoted superior practices across the company. By some estimates, 70% of CEMEX’s practices came from acquisitions, while integration time fell from 25 months for the Spanish transactions to less than five months for Southdown. Middle managers were central to transferring standards and identifying valuable local capabilities. Applying the process to CEMEX’s own Mexican operations in 1996 identified $85 million in savings.

CEMEX subsequently acquired Southdown in 2000, becoming North America’s largest cement producer. It bought U.K.-based RMC for $5.8 billion in 2005, broadening its geographic presence and increasing its exposure to aggregates and ready-mix concrete. Despite RMC’s financial weakness and decentralized culture, CEMEX’s integration produced more than $200 million in synergies within a year and was expected to generate over $380 million in 2007. In 2007, CEMEX acquired control of Rinker for $15.3 billion. Its share price subsequently fell sharply during the 2008 global downturn and credit crisis, partly because of debt taken on for Rinker.

The cement industry was highly localized because transportation costs were high relative to product value. Global capacity had consolidated among multinational firms, while developing markets accounted for most consumption and were expected to grow faster. Developing-market customers generally purchased bagged cement, whereas developed-market customers bought bulk cement and prioritized reliable delivery and logistics.

Springfield Officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action after writing “Hahahaha love this” on Facebook about Heather Heyer’s death when a driver plowed into counter-protesters at a white nationalist rally in Virginia. Lariviere apologized and denied being racist. Commissioner John Barbieri ordered an internal review, while Mayor Domenic Sarno condemned the comments. The driver, James Alex Fields Jr., was charged with second-degree murder.

Williams & Connolly confirmed that hackers accessed a small number of attorney email accounts through a zero-day exploit. The firm said no evidence showed confidential client data was extracted from other parts of its IT system, including client-file databases. It believes the threat actor is a nation-state group linked to attacks on law firms and companies. Mandiant warned that Chinese-government-linked hackers sought U.S. national-security and international-trade information.

DAWN-PLASMA is a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, open-label proof-of-concept trial comparing supportive standard of care alone with standard of care plus convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19, using a 2:1 allocation. Its primary objective is to evaluate clinical efficacy and safety. The primary endpoint is the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at day 15. Secondary endpoints include clinical status at days 15 and 30; time to sustained improvement or life discharge; mechanical ventilation or death within 30 and 90 days; venous thromboembolism; transfusion-related effects; neutralizing-antibody titers; quality of life; severe adverse events and serious adverse events; laboratory data; and vital signs. Exploratory assessments include SARS-CoV-2 PCR, NT50 measurements, and comparisons based on pre-existing COVID-19 antibodies. Outcomes were partly based on the draft WHO master protocol to facilitate data pooling.

The rationale was that hospitalized COVID-19 care is mainly supportive, with mortality benefits demonstrated for dexamethasone and tocilizumab in oxygen-requiring patients but limited therapeutic options during viral replication. Findings on convalescent plasma have been inconsistent. The study hypothesized that early administration of high-volume plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation.

The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Independent Ethics Committees at participating centers approved protocol amendments and consent documentation and were to be notified of serious or unexpected adverse events. Signed, dated informed consent was required, with witnessed, documented verbal consent permitted when signing was prevented by transmission-control restrictions.

Eligible participants were consenting adults aged 18 years or older, including non-pregnant women, with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and qualifying illness findings. Exclusions included mechanical ventilation before or at randomization, unacceptable safety hazards, a grade 3 allergic reaction to fresh frozen plasma, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and rituximab or another anti-CD20 antibody within the preceding year.

Patients received 800–1,000 mL of plasma in four 200–250 mL doses. The first dose was administered within 12 hours of randomization, and the second pair of units 24–36 hours after the first two ended. Plasma below a 1/160 neutralizing-antibody titer was prohibited; 1/160 was permitted only in exceptional scarcity. Five patients withdrew before intervention and one non-COVID screen failure was replaced by six new randomized patients; no patients were lost to follow-up.

Video output terminals map the eight MSBs of G/Y/YC, B/CB/C, and R/CR data to RGB, YUV444, Y/C, and BT.656 modes; some chroma signals are multiplexed or unused in BT.656. The text also defines I/O-state symbols, internal pull defaults, and supply-voltage notation.

Coppin State University, a historically Black university in Maryland, has more than quadrupled out-of-state enrollment over two years through Expand Eagle Nation, which offers in-state tuition to students from 41 states and territories without an HBCU and the District of Columbia. Qualifying students increased from 81 in fall 2023 to 195 in 2024, and 416 of 1,000 incoming students came from qualifying states this fall. Overall enrollment is up 26%.

Coppin has pursued wider recognition through high-school visits, advertising on buses and billboards, community-college transfer partnerships, and outreach to regional college-search organizations. It also prepared for growth by adding faculty and courses, constructing a dormitory for next fall, and using six off-campus apartment complexes with resident assistants and campus shuttles.

The university’s growth coincides with demographic concerns, increased interest in HBCUs following the Supreme Court’s 2023 affirmative-action ruling, and Coppin’s relatively low cost. However, some prospective students and parents distrust the tuition offer because they expect hidden conditions or financial traps.

The speaker presents the transfer of government to Democrats as more than partisan victory, marking a national awakening and fresh scrutiny of established policies. America’s material prosperity, moral strength, and system of government are praised, but the passage also acknowledges widespread waste, human suffering caused by industry, depleted natural resources, and government corruption through private interests.

The nation’s task is described as restoration: correcting injustice and corruption while preserving the strengths of existing institutions. Proposed areas of reform include tariffs, banking and currency, industrial organization, labor conditions, agricultural efficiency and credit, conservation of natural resources, public health, and the protection of individual and property rights. Government should serve humanity, with justice—not sentiment—as its foundation.

The speaker rejects both blind haste and destructive change, arguing that reforms should be based on facts, careful study, and counsel. The central motto is justice, applied to economic, social, and political life. Although the transition is not a day of triumph, it is a day of dedication requiring cooperation from honest, patriotic, and forward-looking citizens.

Indianapolis Public Schools is seeking community input on a proposal to close three of its seven under-enrolled high schools by the 2018-19 school year. A taskforce report found enrollment declined from 109,000 students in 1967 to 30,000, with five high schools at less than half capacity. It said three schools could serve current enrollment, while four would offer greater flexibility. Meetings are scheduled for April 26, May 1, May 11 and May 15; the administration is expected to recommend closures in June, followed by a board vote in September.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They operate from 4 V to 14 V, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and use external gate drivers. EN can be tied to VLDO, driven externally or by PGOOD, or connected to a resistor divider for programmable UVLO. The devices use a 1.23 V bandgap reference and 0.613 V error-amplifier reference; output voltage is set with a VSENSE divider, and soft-start duration is controlled by an SS capacitor. RT and SYNC configurations select internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary operation.

Primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs have roughly 150 mA peak-current capability, so external gate drive is recommended. Dead time and leading-edge blank time are programmable on applicable devices, while pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time constraints. The DCL pin configures supported maximum duty cycles. CS_ILIM senses peak primary current, and reaching 1.05 V initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting and hiccup restart. FAULT accepts external fault signals, RSC sets slope compensation, and typical thermal shutdown occurs at 175 °C with restart below 160 °C.

A 5 V, 500-kHz synchronous push-pull example using the TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs selects a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback resistors, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors, 49.9 kΩ LEB resistor, 33 nF soft-start capacitor for approximately 7.5 ms, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V secondary FET ratings, 0.47 µH output inductor, 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, and a 102 kΩ slope-compensation resistor.

Layout and supply guidance calls for a regulated input with at least 0.1 µF of ceramic VIN-to-AVSS bypass, short and wide high-current paths, minimized switch-node area and switching loops, a single-point AVSS-to-power-ground connection, close low-ESL bypass and compensation components, and separation of feedback, CS_ILIM, SYNC, and gate-drive traces from noisy switching nodes.

The paper proposes LG-CD, a language-guided multimodal method for detecting changes between bi-temporal remote sensing images. A shared SAM2 encoder extracts multi-scale visual features, while lightweight multilevel convolutional adapters refine and fuse features from both periods. CLIP encodes natural-language prompts into word-level and global semantic embeddings. The Text Fusion Attention Module uses multi-head cross-attention, with visual features as queries and word embeddings as keys and values, to direct attention toward text-relevant change regions. A visual-semantic fusion decoder then combines visual and textual information through cross-attention to generate change-detection masks. Experiments reportedly show improved semantic understanding, accuracy, robustness, and generalization, particularly in complex scenes and for detecting varied targets.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr following her racist tweet, which led ABC to cancel her sitcom, but President Trump and press secretary Sarah Sanders insisted ABC owed the president an apology for its coverage of the administration. Sanders, citing remarks by Jemele Hill, Joy Behar and Keith Olbermann, called it media bias and a double standard, and lamented that networks did not air Trump's remarks on a "right to try" bill.

Ahead of the team’s final on-field practice before returning to camp in late July, head coach Kyle Shanahan said the offense started strong and the defense responded strongly in the red zone, though both sides still have areas to improve. He described his father as an informal adviser who watches film and offers ideas, but not as part of his staff. Shanahan said having someone focused solely on studying football provides valuable additional perspective as a first-time head coach. He also plans an extended family trip to Mexico after the season, aiming to relax without following a schedule or watching football-related material. Shanahan emphasized the importance of play-action, saying it can put defenses on the heels, relieve pressure on the offensive line and quarterback, create explosive plays and keep defenses honest.

The lecture focuses on post-flop poker strategy using hand examples. Because a preflop aggressor has a stronger range, opponents often check to that player, who should generally bet: value bets with strong hands, bluffs with weak hands, and checks medium-strength hands. Betting very small after a check is generally inferior to checking because it gives opponents a free opportunity to check-raise. Suggested flop betting is about half the pot, increasing to roughly 60–70% on later streets and potentially the full pot on the river. Coordinated flops and continuation bets against many players generally make bluffing difficult.

Calling decisions depend on equity, draws, board texture, position, and stack depth. Most weak or drawless hands should fold to a half-pot bet. Stronger pairs and draws may warrant calling, while deep stacks often favor calling over raising to avoid being played only by stronger hands. At 40 big blinds or more, raising generally requires two pair or better, though exceptional combinations of strength and equity can justify it. Flop leads may be useful when the board favors the caller’s range, but they require careful balance and are presented as an advanced tactic.

The lecture also explains implied and reverse implied odds through calculations and examples. Suited draws can justify calls when future streets add value, while weak hands may have poor post-flop play despite favorable immediate odds. Bluffing should generally use hands with substantial outs, because callers are likely to hold stronger hands. Bluffing must also account for what strength is being represented and when the opponent’s range is sufficiently strong that continuing is unwise.

An email sent by Miyung Buster on July 18, 2001, under the subject “Energy Issues,” circulated press clippings about California’s electricity crisis.

Lawmakers considered competing proposals to prevent Southern California Edison from bankruptcy, including purchasing its transmission lines, shifting debt payments to businesses or ratepayers, or directly financing the debt. Edison faced more than $3.5 billion in debt, while Gov. Gray Davis’s $2.76 billion transmission-line proposal drew limited support. Alternatives included a $2.4 billion purchase price, a five-year state option to buy the lines for about $1.2 billion, and a direct bailout funded by consumer fees. Consumer and business groups raised concerns about rate increases, costs passed to consumers, and the state acquiring only part of an expensive transmission system.

PG&E sued California over long-term electricity contracts the governor seized in January, arguing that the state benefited without compensation. The state said the contracts’ value should be determined by a court; estimates ranged from about $150 million to $348 million. An editorial argued that Edison, generators, the state, and consumers would all need to share the financial burden of the crisis.

The state’s consumer advocate also criticized Davis’s proposed $1 billion purchase of San Diego Gas & Electric’s transmission lines as excessive. Meanwhile, California sold surplus electricity at steep losses after buying power at an average of $138 per megawatt-hour, though officials said lower demand and costs had reduced blackout risk.

Other reports covered rising June consumer inflation, a $1.7 million Contra Costa County building-efficiency project, proposed solar-fee waivers in San Diego County, tribal concerns over an SDG&E transmission line, and a 27 percent increase in Duke Energy’s quarterly profit.

Prof. Cyril Dim describes cervical cancer as a malignant condition of the cervix, caused in almost all cases by high-risk human papillomavirus, particularly types 16 and 18. HPV is sexually transmitted; men can acquire and spread it, although the interview states that sex with a woman who has cervical cancer poses no direct risk to the man.

Cervical cancer may develop through an asymptomatic precancerous stage, which can be detected with Pap smears and treated before invasive cancer develops. Early-stage cervical cancer may also produce no symptoms but can be cured. Symptoms can include bleeding after sex, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, abnormal vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain, weakness, anaemia, weight loss, and loss of bladder or bowel control. Diagnosis involves examination and sampling of cervical tissue, with confirmation through biopsy and histology; imaging may be used to determine the stage.

The interview emphasizes the importance of screening, stating that women of reproductive age should have Pap smears at least every three years and every five years later in life. Nigeria lacks a structured screening programme, contributing to late presentation. It reports about 500,000 new cases and 200,000 deaths globally each year, with 80% of deaths occurring in developing countries. Nigeria is estimated to have 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths annually, while cervical cancer accounts for about 67 of every 100 female genital cancers in Enugu. It ranks after breast cancer among cancers affecting Nigerian women, although the interview notes that both may share the leading position.

Treatment depends on the stage. Early-stage disease may be treated with radical surgery or radiotherapy, while late-stage treatment focuses on prolonging life through radiotherapy, often with chemotherapy. Women with early-stage disease may become pregnant, but this is generally not possible in late stages. Vaccination against common cancer-associated HPV types is available.

Additional health information lists multiple sexual partners, smoking, birth-control pill use, and early sexual contact as risk factors. Precancerous changes may be treated with cryosurgery, cauterization, or laser surgery, and imaging options include X-rays, CT, MRI, and PET scans. Prognosis depends on the cancer’s stage and type and tumour size.

Polynomial functionals of an m-qubit state enable precise estimation of purity and higher-order moments that determine Rényi entropies. They are fundamental in quantum information science, statistical mechanics, and many-body physics, and underpin entanglement and coherence measures and randomness-certification protocols. The passage also introduces general real polynomial functionals of the state.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed Spencer Elden's 2021 suit against Nirvana over the 1991 Nevermind cover photo of him as a 4-month-old naked baby floating underwater toward a dollar bill, ruling the image is not child pornography. Elden sued under a federal law for victims of certain crimes as minors; Olguin found only the child's nudity met any statutory factor and compared the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

The Ottawa hockey team believes it is stronger than its two-game playoff showing and must now prove that assessment. The coach expects some games to go well and others poorly, emphasizing discipline against a disciplined opponent that forechecks effectively, outpositions and outdefends Ottawa, and capitalizes on mistakes. He plans to make adjustments rather than continue making risky home-run passes, with better puck possession, speed, forechecking, and faceoff execution needed to generate sustained attacks.

Chris Neil was given the day off because his wife was expected to give birth. The visiting goaltender played well and gave Ottawa chances to win, though he was not sufficiently tested.

Centre iceman must improve at winning faceoffs and helping wingers, while Pahlsson’s line has contributed physical play, faceoff wins, puck protection, and clock control. Ottawa has committed too many turnovers and struggled to create offensive plays for players such as Alfie and Mike Comrie. The coaching staff expects players to return to the stronger form they showed earlier in the year, drawing on video preparation and the emotional support of the home crowd. The fourth line, which recently supplied hits and speed, is expected to receive more ice time in Game 3.

The coach praised Rob Niedermayer as a strong, versatile and important player who became a valuable role player after concussion and whose line is crucial to the series.

A hockey player describes being surprised and grateful to return to the lineup after two weeks. Nervous at first, he focused on doing his part alongside teammates he credited for controlling the game. He praised his coach’s discipline and no-nonsense approach, saying the team had built a solid foundation despite roster changes and a difficult season.

An analysis by Notre Dame Law professor Derek Muller found that lawyers and staff at 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms gave 92.45% of their 2023–24 campaign contributions to Democrats—about $52 million versus $4 million for Republicans. The roughly 12-to-1 Democratic advantage rose from 6-to-1 for 2017–20. Among top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb had the highest Democratic-contribution rate (99.7%), while Nelson Mullins had the lowest (66.4%).

This position paper examines how artificial intelligence is transforming higher education and how institutions can integrate it responsibly. The authors argue that AI should help develop human capital and 21st-century competencies through learning, self-correction, and reasoning. Their review of documents in the B-ON and SCILIT databases also draws on the authors’ reflexivity as university teachers with more than 20 years’ experience.

AI can transform teaching and learning, research, organizational management, and relationships between higher education institutions and their environments. Applications include personalized learning and tutoring, automated grading, learning-management recommendations, data analysis and visualization, translation, plagiarism detection, predictive analytics, speech recognition, student support, text analysis, virtual assistants, and virtual reality. It can also support research and administrative work while increasing accuracy, speed, accessibility, and efficiency.

However, adoption presents challenges involving equitable access, inclusion, bias, diversity, data ethics and security, privacy, teacher training, student needs and autonomy, costs, organizational resistance, policy development, and the limitations of AI itself. Traditional teaching practices and institutional cultures may also generate anxiety and affect the academic profession.

The paper recommends institution-wide, participatory implementation and AI literacy for all stakeholders, including the ability to evaluate and collaborate with AI critically. Teachers require competencies in understanding AI’s educational applications, analyzing data, managing AI resources, and assessing its use critically. Their roles, classroom practices, and interactions with students must therefore be reshaped. The authors conclude that higher education cannot remain static in response to AI, but should guide its use through discussion, research, and preservation of academic freedom.

This lecture (MIT OCW 8.323, Lecture 18) covers discrete symmetries and fermionic path integrals.

**Discrete symmetries in quantum mechanics and field theory.** A complex scalar theory classically has parity P (flipping spatial coordinates, x → −x), time reversal T (t → −t), and charge conjugation C (φ → φ*). Quantum mechanically these are implemented by unitary operators except time reversal, which must be anti-unitary. Working from a time-reversal-invariant system where U_T commutes with H, applying U_T to the Schrödinger equation shows that reproducing the equation with t → −t requires U_T to send i → −i, i.e., U_T must be anti-linear. The adjoint of an anti-linear operator is correspondingly defined with an extra complex conjugation, and the anti-unitary condition adds an extra star.

In quantum field theory the scalar Lagrangian is invariant under these transformations, each implemented by a unitary operator U_P, U_T, U_C acting on φ with phases η_P, η_T, η_C. Since performing a transformation twice must return the system to itself, each η equals ±1; +1 corresponds to a "scalar" and −1 to a "pseudoscalar" (these labels are conventions: pions are pseudoscalars, the Higgs an ordinary scalar). The three η's are independent. Acting on creation/annihilation operators, parity and time reversal send a_k → η a_{−k} and b_k → η b_{−k}, since momenta reverse sign under reflection; charge conjugation exchanges particles and antiparticles, a_k ↔ η_C b_k.

**Dirac fields.** Because spinors reshuffle under Lorentz transformations, parity on a Dirac field requires a matrix D acting on spinor space, not merely a phase. Parity invariance means the transformed field satisfies the same Dirac equation in the reflected space; γ-matrices are numbers and do not change. Comparing the two equations requires D to commute with γ^0 and anticommute with γ^i, so D is proportional to γ^0 (with an additional phase, whose allowed value is left aside). For charge conjugation, a matrix C must relate ψ̄^T to ψ′; it exists because −γ^μ^T satisfies the same Clifford algebra and all matrix representations are equivalent, though C is representation-dependent. For time reversal, D_T is an ordinary matrix and satisfies γ^μ^T = D_T^T γ^μ D_T^{−1T}; taking D_T^T ∝ C^{−1}γ^5 supplies the extra minus sign, so knowing C gives D_T. The lecturer notes that parity, time reversal, and charge conjugation are independent discrete transformations, not related by Lorentz boosts; there is only one parity in any dimension; and because conservation equations are covariant, a quantity conserved in one frame is conserved in all (though charges differ).

**Path integrals for fermions.** Feynman introduced the path integral in 1948 and immediately generalized it to scalars, but failed for fermions for many years because Dirac fields obey anticommutation rather than commutation. In the early 1960s Berezin resolved this by postulating that the path integral integrates over Grassmann variables — objects that anticommute with themselves, so θ² = 0. Functions of Grassmann numbers truncate to a constant plus terms linear (or bilinear) in the variables, and left versus right derivatives differ by a sign; the convention adopted is to differentiate from the left.

Integration is defined by two requirements: linearity, and that the integral of a total derivative vanishes. These fix the rules up to a constant, resolved by setting ∫dθ θ = 1, which yields ∫dθ f(θ) = f₁ — integration coincides with differentiation for a single variable. An odd variable commuted out of the integral picks up a minus sign, and change of variables behaves unusually: with θ′ = aθ, dθ′ = (1/a)dθ. The lecturer emphasizes that Feynman missed not a trivial idea but an entire calculus for anticommuting objects.

The next lecture is scheduled for Wednesday, since Monday is a holiday.

The disclosure describes systems, devices, and methods for spatially and temporally synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more cameras. Camera sensing-element rows are aligned with the LIDAR’s rotation axis, and a controller sequences rolling-shutter image pixels to correspond with the order and timing of emitted LIDAR beams. Timing, exposure delays, row order, and capture start times may be adjusted according to the LIDAR’s rotation rate, direction, pointing direction, and beam arrangement. Embodiments include a rotating platform, stationary platform, camera ring, curved or flexible image-sensor arrangements, and overlapping camera fields of view. The synchronized data can be associated by time and viewing direction and combined to generate colored three-dimensional representations, point clouds, depth information, or other environmental mappings.

U.S. stock futures rose Thursday as strong early earnings and rebounding oil prices offset caution over U.S.-North Korea tensions and France’s close presidential election. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures gained 41, 6.5 and 17.5 points, respectively. Of 57 reporting S&P 500 companies, 75.4% beat earnings expectations; Qualcomm rose and eBay fell after contrasting results and forecasts.

Quantbot Technologies increased its Zoe’s Kitchen stake 114.5% in the second quarter to 17,056 shares, while other major investors also raised holdings or opened positions. Director A. Alexander Taylor II bought 3,100 shares for $39,897 and now directly owns 7,508. Analysts were mixed: the stock’s consensus rating was “Hold,” with a $17.55 target price. ZOES opened at $12.39 and had a $242.04 million market capitalization. Quarterly EPS of $0.06 exceeded consensus estimates by $0.04, while revenue of $74.3 million fell below the $75.11 million estimate but rose 12.1% year over year. Zoe’s Kitchen develops and operates fast-casual restaurants serving Mediterranean-inspired food.

The appellate court affirmed Bradford Washington’s convictions and sentences for second-degree murder, weapons possession, reckless endangerment, and child endangerment under Indictment No. 999/05, and his second-degree murder guilty plea under No. 1000/05. It found his evidentiary and consciousness-of-guilt claims unpreserved and meritless, rejected his contention that the prosecution shifted theories, and noted that he raised no independent challenge to the second indictment.

Darren Osborne was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 43 years for driving a van into worshippers outside Finsbury Park mosque in June 2017. He was convicted of murdering Makram Ali and attempting to murder nine other people. During the trial, Osborne said a BBC drama had “brainwashed” him into Islamophobia and claimed he wanted to kill Sadiq Khan and Jeremy Corbyn. Ali’s family welcomed the guilty verdict and described him as a peaceful, innocent man. Police said the attack had failed to create divisions, noting that communities across London and the UK had united in response.

Major hedge funds reduced healthcare holdings in the second quarter of 2017 even as S&P 500 healthcare stocks rose 6.7%, versus 2.6% for the broad index, as Republican efforts to repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act weakened. Jana Partners fully exited nine healthcare companies, while Third Point cut stakes in Humana and Baxter International. Funds also sold energy holdings as the sector fell 7%; overall, hedge funds gained 1%.

Facebook’s new “Trending News” section in its iOS and Android apps aggregates stories from various sources and ranks them by how many publications share them. Users can access headlines, videos, photos, and related posts through Explore.

The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Massachusetts resolved the remaining damages issues in litigation between Access Cardiosystems, Inc. and its investors against the company’s founder, Randall Fincke. Access and the investors had previously obtained findings that Fincke breached fiduciary duties and violated Massachusetts securities law, Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2), by falsely stating in an October 2002 Business Plan that Access had received advice from patent counsel that its defibrillator did not infringe known patents.

The court denied Fincke’s motion to reconsider the securities-law finding. Although Fincke argued that the investors understood the statement to refer to a formal patent opinion, the court found that no advice had been given by counsel, formal or informal. Viewed objectively, the statement was false and material to a reasonable investor because it suggested that a patent professional had reviewed the intellectual property. The investors’ conflicting testimony concerning the statement’s wording was immaterial to that objective determination.

For damages under § 410(a)(2), the court held that a securities sale must have a causal nexus with the misrepresentation, although investors need not prove reliance or loss causation. The investors’ testimony that the Business Plan influenced every investment was found not credible, largely because it was mechanistic, inconsistent with earlier testimony, and appeared tailored after most of their other fraud claims had been rejected.

The court therefore found that only Joseph Zimmel’s purchases of $1 million in Access stock in October 2002 and $500,000 in stock in November 2002 were made “by means of” the Business Plan’s misstatement. Fincke’s testimony that the Business Plan was distributed to all investors, including Zimmel, supported that finding notwithstanding the lack of credible reliance testimony. The April 2003 recapitalization was not sufficiently connected to the Business Plan because it followed a new Company Overview, extensive negotiations, Access’s financial needs, and changes in corporate governance. Later advances also were not recoverable under § 410(a)(2), both because the Business Plan lacked a sufficient nexus to those transactions and because no additional Access stock was purchased after April 2003.

The court entered judgment for Zimmel against Fincke of $1.5 million, plus six-percent annual interest from May 25, 2007, the disposition date of the securities, and costs. It also entered judgment for Access against Fincke of $281,534.62 on the previously determined fiduciary-duty breaches concerning repayment of his personal loans, plus twelve-percent annual prejudgment interest from July 6, 2004, and costs. Federal postjudgment interest applies to both awards.

The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge digital library and GLAM professionals, who understand collections and users, with computational researchers who can apply technologies such as machine learning, NLP, large language models, and retrieval-augmented generation. It will explore practical challenges, including differing access requirements, limited computing resources, and restrictions on using external AI services, while encouraging innovative research systems and effective access paths.

The full-day, in-person TPDL workshop requires no paper submissions. Its program includes a keynote on successful practitioner–researcher collaboration, scientific speed-dating, a panel with 5–7 diverse participants, and breakout discussions on topics including LLM use, OCR, interface evaluation, and novel access paths. Breakout groups may also form around shared interests identified during speed-dating.

Expected outcomes include establishing a continuing workshop series, identifying common digital library challenges, connecting domain experts with researchers at different career stages, producing a SIGIR Forum report, and discussing possibilities for subsequent conference workshops. The event primarily targets practitioners and researchers interested in digital library systems, especially students and library representatives, with approximately 25 participants expected. It is organized by Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll.

The application discloses electronic smoking devices, including electronic cigarettes, cigars, pipes, and cartomizers, with a coil-less atomizer that combines liquid delivery and heating in woven fiber tubes. The device includes a housing, a liquid supply, and one or more hollow, electrically conductive fiber tubes whose ends contact the liquid. Liquid reaches a resistive heating section through capillary action within the tube, through its porous wall, or both.

The heating section is positioned between conductive leads or electrical contacts and has greater resistance than adjacent sections, causing it to heat while the liquid-contacting ends remain relatively cool. Suitable tube materials include carbon fiber, nickel-chromium, steel, titanium, ceramics, Dacron, and composites combining resistive and wicking fibers. Tubes may be U-, C-, or L-shaped and can have uniform or varying diameters, parallel arrangements, direct wall contact, or different heating and supply sections. These configurations can increase wicking, create staged aerosol delivery, or reduce thermal inertia.

The application also describes an electronic-cigarette housing containing a battery, control electronics, optional airflow sensor or manual switch, LED, atomizer, liquid supply, airflow passage, and mouthpiece. User inhalation activates the heating element, which vaporizes liquid into an aerosol drawn through the device. The atomizer may use free-flowing or porous liquid supplies and may be disposable, refillable, or replaceable.

Manufacturing methods include mounting fiber tubes on a board, masking selected portions, and coating unmasked conductive sections to modify electrical resistance. Fiber surfaces may also be treated to improve wicking or conductivity. The disclosed coil-less elements are intended to reduce component count and size, permit controlled resistance, and support efficient mass production. Related patent applications are incorporated by reference.

On August 17, 2022, Apple Inc.’s Compensation Committee approved the Apple Inc. Executive Cash Incentive Plan. The plan permits cash awards for eligible executive team members, including named executive officers, based on performance goals established by the committee. The committee sets performance periods, goals, achievement levels, maximum payout opportunities, and other award terms. Awards are paid in cash after performance is assessed and are generally forfeited if a participant leaves before payment, unless the committee determines otherwise.

Apple’s Board also adopted amended and restated bylaws, effective the same day. The amendments permit special board meetings with less than 48 hours’ notice, expand disclosures and procedures for shareholder nominations and proposals, update special-meeting and written-consent requirements, require soliciting shareholders to use a non-white proxy card, allow reduced procedures during emergencies, and clarify authority over shareholder meeting locations and meeting rules. The filing attached the amended bylaws and the incentive plan as Exhibits 3.2 and 10.1.

The Ohio Supreme Court upheld the one-year residency requirement for divorce and annulment under R.C. 3105.03, except for alimony-only actions, and affirmed the judgment. Applying strict scrutiny under *Shapiro* and *Dunn*, the court found that the requirement did not penalize the constitutional right to interstate travel because divorce is a statutory privilege, unlike fundamental rights such as receiving welfare or voting. Ohio has a compelling interest in regulating marriage and its dissolution, ensuring its laws do not govern nonresidents, and promoting marital stability. The one-year requirement was the least restrictive means of establishing domicile and encouraging reconsideration and reconciliation without preventing divorce applicants from moving to Ohio. Justice Schneider concurred, emphasizing the case’s particular facts, available support and separation remedies, and the reasonableness of the one-year period.

Oliver Stone's Wall Street, released December 11, 1987, has remained the most enduring film about finance for 30 years. It succeeds by blending the rags-to-riches parable, the Hero's Journey, and a fairy tale, immersing viewers in the mid-'80s bull market while making them question whether the protagonist is rooting for the villain. The film's magic comes largely from its '80s excess—junk bonds, corporate raiders, contrast-collar suits, and lavish lifestyles rendered with nostalgia.

At the film's center is Michael Douglas as Gordon Gekko, who was cast after Warren Beatty and Richard Gere declined. Douglas won the Best Actor Oscar, and Gekko became a lasting symbol of financial greed, though his targets were corporations rather than ordinary Americans, giving the film balance instead of a simplistic "money is bad" lecture. Phrases like "Greed is good" and "blue horseshoe loves anacott steel" remain instantly recognizable touchstones, making the film a time capsule of the era built on a cautionary tale.

Google Camera was modified to enable HDR+ on Android phones with Snapdragon 820, 821 or 835 processors. Amazon is offering refunds for dubious solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses to pay hackers amid leaks of shows and emails, including upcoming episodes. Waymo patented technology to soften vehicle bodies before pedestrian impacts.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016. Incorporated in Washington in 1994 and reincorporated in Delaware in 1996, Amazon is headquartered in Seattle, completed its IPO in May 1997, and trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “AMZN.” It had 477,170,618 shares outstanding as of January 25, 2017, a non-affiliate market value of $280.1 billion as of June 30, 2016, and had never paid cash dividends.

Amazon serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. Its consumer business operates retail websites and mobile apps offering first- and third-party merchandise, Kindle e-readers, Fire tablets and TVs, Echo devices, media content, and Amazon Prime. Seller programs generate commissions and other fees, while AWS provides global compute, storage, database, and related services. The company also offers advertising, co-branded credit cards, Kindle Direct Publishing, and Amazon Publishing. Amazon reported approximately 341,400 employees at year-end. Fourth-quarter revenue represented 32%–33% of annual revenue during 2014–2016.

Principal risks include intense competition, strains from global expansion and new offerings, international regulatory restrictions, fulfillment-network and data-center capacity, seasonality, commercial agreements, acquisitions, foreign exchange, loss of key personnel, data and system security breaches, inventory management, intellectual property, stock-price volatility, tax liabilities, supplier dependence, product liability, payment-processing requirements, and potential liability for seller misconduct. Operations in China and India face particular licensing, ownership, and regulatory uncertainties.

The filing reported 2016 net sales of $135.987 billion, up 27% from 2015, operating income of $4.186 billion, net income of $2.371 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $4.90. North America generated $79.785 billion in sales and $2.361 billion in operating income; International generated $43.983 billion in sales and a $1.283 billion operating loss; and AWS generated $12.219 billion in sales and $3.108 billion in operating income. Operating cash flow rose to $16.443 billion in 2016.

At December 31, 2016, cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $26.0 billion, total assets were $83.402 billion, and long-term obligations were $20.301 billion. Cash capital expenditures were $6.7 billion, and purchase obligations and open purchase orders totaled $8.5 billion. Management stated that operating cash flows, marketable securities, and available borrowing should meet anticipated cash needs for at least the following 12 months, including the maturity of $1.0 billion in unsecured senior notes. Critical accounting judgments included inventory valuation and uncertain income-tax liabilities, including pending IRS transfer-pricing litigation and a European Commission state-aid investigation.

The Simons Observatory’s Large Aperture Telescope uses SMuRF warm electronics and microwave frequency multiplexing to read out nearly 31,000 transition-edge sensor detectors. Its receiver cabin and coaxial cables experience diurnal temperature changes that can alter cable lengths and dielectric properties, producing systematic RF phase drift that may mimic detector signals.

The study uses untracked off-resonance “pilot” tones, which pass through the warm cables and cryogenic circuit without resonating, to measure this drift. Analysis of 290 tones from 30 AMCs over 22.6 hours on June 2, 2025, found that signal delays correlate with ambient temperature and vary by a few picoseconds over a daily cycle, with delays grouped by RF transmission-line circuit.

The measured phase drift was converted into an inferred TES noise-equivalent current using calibrated resonator offsets and measured SQUID response curves. During a 40-minute constant-elevation scan, the resulting noise contribution was smaller than the readout noise of a representative 150 GHz on-sky detector, fell within the readout-noise budget, and was not expected to affect the telescope’s mapping speed. The results indicate that diurnal phase drift in the LAT’s warm RF cables is a small contributor to overall detector noise.

SCOTUSblog is publishing excerpts from retired Justice Anthony Kennedy's memoir, released Oct. 14, with a full review to follow. The passages cover his views on judicial decision-making, constitutional interpretation, controversial cases, and personal matters.

On decision-making, Kennedy stresses judicial humility and integrity, noting that the Court earns respect by making difficult decisions properly and clearly, especially in close cases, and that justices may learn in retrospect that they were wrong, as he did regarding executing minors. Kennedy is neither a self-described originalist nor a pragmatist and rejects both as insufficient: originalism's meaning cannot simply be "plucked" from an old dictionary, while pragmatism may be "too unclear to give helpful guidance." Instead, he suggests that over time "the right answers can and will continue to be found" without the Constitution itself changing.

On major cases, Kennedy discusses the 5-4 campaign-spending decision in Citizens United, emphasizing the Court's limited role in reviewing a specific congressional statute and the power of voters; the 5-4 decision establishing a constitutional right to same-sex marriage, which he researched extensively and which prompted a personal attack from Justice Scalia; the presidential election case, where he focused on legal issues rather than which candidate prevailed; and the flag-burning case, in which he concurred while acknowledging the cost of protecting expression that shocks or offends.

Kennedy also recounts Scalia's dissent at the same-sex marriage case, the fallout with Scalia, and their eventual reconciliation shortly before Scalia's death. He disliked being called the "swing justice," saying "the cases swung, not me." On abortion, Kennedy states that though he considered it wrong, a moral wrong is not necessarily a legal wrong, and he decided to remain on the Court rather than resign.

Other passages address presidential deference to the Court, a meeting with Vladimir Putin that left Kennedy with an impression of Putin's willingness to use law only when convenient, his opposition to courtroom cameras, his family's home being ransacked after he declined to lower bail for a Manson family member, and his family's music tastes, including Tom Petty. The post closes by noting the seriousness of considering Tom Petty "avant-garde."

Evelyn Montiel grew up helping run her family’s ice cream truck and frozen fruit stand in East Oakland while excelling in high school. Students Rising Above supported her through college, helping her transfer to USC after leaving an East Coast school during a bout of depression. She thrived at USC and secured internships. After graduation during a recession, SRA connected her with a finance job interview, and she now works as a broker at a Silicon Valley startup.

Tesla’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022 states that it designs, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles and energy-generation and storage products and provides related services to accelerate the sustainable-energy transition. Its two reportable segments are automotive and energy generation and storage.

Automotive products include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X. Tesla began early production and deliveries of the Tesla Semi in December 2022 and planned additional models including Cybertruck and a new Roadster. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, Solar Roof and retrofit solar systems, supported by remote-control and optimization software. Tesla sells directly through its website, stores and galleries, operates service and charging networks, and offers vehicle financing, leasing, insurance and paid software upgrades.

The company manufactures vehicles and energy products in California, New York, Texas and Nevada, as well as Shanghai and Berlin-Brandenburg. It relies on extensive global supplier and raw-material networks while developing proprietary battery cells, powertrains, vehicle software, full self-driving technology and AI applications such as Optimus. Its products and operations are affected by government incentives, vehicle, battery, energy and environmental regulations, and policies governing autonomous vehicles and dealer sales.

As of December 31, 2022, Tesla reported 127,855 full-time employees, 29,000 more than a year earlier. It emphasizes sustainable operations, responsible sourcing, workplace safety, workforce development and governance oversight.

The filing identifies material risks involving macroeconomic and pandemic conditions, production-ramp delays, supplier and battery-cell shortages, raw-material costs, demand forecasts, intense competition, international operations, product defects and liability, financing and residual-value exposure, customer credit, obligations under its Gigafactory New York agreement, dependence on key personnel including Elon Musk, and cybersecurity incidents. It cautions that forward-looking plans and expectations may differ materially from actual results.

The September 26, 2000 VentureWire issue reports private-company financing, product launches, acquisitions, board changes, executive appointments, and venture-fund news.

Top stories included Chiaro Networks securing more than $100 million in third-round funding; Bertelsmann and iSyndicate forming the 50%-owned iSyndicate Europe; Novalux raising $109 million; online jewelry retailer Miadora closing; Sun Microsystems launching a $50 million Asian investment program intended to provide $250 million through co-investments; and Mayfield Fund appointing Jennifer Jones as marketing partner.

Numerous financing announcements included $75 million rounds for Nexsi and Netigy, $50 million for Nonstop Solutions, $47 million for Epylon, $45 million for Predictive Networks, $35 million for Telecruz, $32.5 million each for Hart InterCivic and qServe, and $26 million for Artesia Technology. Strategic investments included Motorola’s $22.5 million purchase of an 8% Lineo stake, Ford’s investment in Captura, Expedia’s stake in eGulliver, and Siemens’ participation in Sitara Networks’ $20 million Series G.

Product news covered SmartPipes’ beta launch of Global IP Services, PocketPass.com’s prepaid-card system for online purchases, Fujitsu-ICL and Foursan’s formation of Middle Eastern venture 4Mena Systems, and w-Trade Technologies’ name change to w-Technologies. Autodaq acquired MarketWise, Burley House Weddings merged with Confetti Network under the Confetti name, and DeepBridge Content Solutions acquired Online Communications.

The issue also reported numerous board and executive appointments, including David Lockwood at @TheMoment, IBM executive John Landry at E-smith, Mitchell York as ePromos.com president and CEO, Philip Letts as Internet Barter CEO, and George Schad as Authentor CEO. Venturelab Partners launched a $100 million second fund, Atle Fvretagskapital restructured a subsidiary as Atle Ventures, Net Value Holdings became Stonepath Group, and Edgar Masri joined Matrix Partners. VentureWire clarified that Sharing Technologies’ $15 million third round comprised $9 million in equity and a $6 million IBM bridge loan, and corrected the investor list for epipeline.com.

On November 27, 2001, Dynegy confirmed it was discussing restructuring its proposed acquisition of Enron, including lowering the exchange ratio from 0.2685 to below 0.15 Dynegy shares per Enron share. The revised all-stock transaction would value Enron at roughly $5 billion instead of about $9 billion. The talks also involved additional cash funding for Enron, extending debt maturities, and addressing concerns that Enron’s liabilities could allow Dynegy to terminate the deal.

Enron’s financial and liquidity problems had sharply reduced trading activity and credit confidence. Major energy companies had stopped selling to Enron in spot markets, while others traded only on a limited basis. Enron disputed a broker’s estimate that its over-the-counter volume had fallen to 25% of the prior month’s level, saying transactions had declined only slightly. Enron’s equity trading unit was reportedly being closed, with about 60 employees laid off.

Enron was also seeking up to $2 billion in outside financing, but several investors, including Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal, Blackstone, and Carlyle, declined to participate. Moody’s left Enron’s Baa3 rating unchanged for the day but had it under review for downgrade. Enron needed financing to meet substantial obligations and support operations during the merger.

Market reaction was mixed. Enron shares briefly fell below $4 before recovering on reports of renewed negotiations and closed at $4.14; Dynegy shares rose $1.64 to $40.89. Enron bonds also rebounded, though arbitrageurs and analysts remained skeptical because the revised deal had not been finalized and Enron could still face bankruptcy if it collapsed. Analysts said any new agreement would need to restore confidence in Enron’s core trading business and clarify its financial exposure. Enron also faced shareholder lawsuits and employee retirement-plan litigation, while Dynegy retained rights to the Northern Natural Gas Pipeline regardless of the merger’s outcome.

Molecules in optical cavities have electron–photon interactions described by the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, while free-space quantum-chemistry methods are inadequate. The nonlocal, long-range coupling requires precise representation of varied wavefunction features. The orthonormal, systematically improvable sinc basis is promising, but direct two-electron integrals cost O(N⁴); rapidly decaying off-diagonal tensor elements enable sparse or low-rank approximations.

The DAWn-Plasma study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II proof-of-concept trial comparing standard of care plus convalescent plasma with standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 were randomized 2:1 to plasma plus standard of care (n=326) or standard of care alone (n=163). Participants received four units of convalescent plasma, totaling approximately 800–1,000 mL, with the first dose within 12 hours after randomization; 80.7% of units had neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1:320.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. In the full analysis set, this was 83.7% with plasma versus 84.1% with control (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No significant between-group differences were found in secondary or exploratory outcomes, including mortality, ventilation, clinical status, hospitalization, laboratory measures, or quality of life. A prespecified subgroup analysis showed an interaction with age (p=0.023).

Adverse-event frequencies were similar between groups: 139 patients experienced adverse events, 49 experienced fatal adverse events, and 100 experienced serious adverse events. Five adverse events led to treatment discontinuation, all in the plasma group, and two led to study discontinuation. Transfusion-related effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma-group patients, with no TRALI cases reported. Neutralizing-antibody titers increased by Day 6 regardless of treatment, and higher baseline and Day 6 titers correlated with better outcomes. The protocol followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH-GCP guidelines and required ethics approval and informed consent.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The Delaware corporation is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “NVDA.” It reported approximately 589 million shares outstanding as of February 24, 2017, and a non-affiliate market value of about $28.98 billion as of July 29, 2016.

The filing says NVIDIA invented the GPU and has expanded from PC graphics into artificial intelligence. Its GPU, Tegra Processor, and related hardware, software, algorithms, libraries, systems, and services serve four markets: gaming, professional visualization, datacenter, and automotive. Brands include GeForce and GeForce NOW for gaming, Quadro for professional design, Tesla and DGX for AI and accelerated computing, GRID for cloud graphics, and Tegra-based DRIVE PX and SHIELD platforms. CUDA, cuDNN, and NVLink support deep learning and parallel computing; the filing states that GPUs can accelerate parallel applications by 10–75 times versus CPUs and accelerate neural-network training by as much as 12 times. NVIDIA also develops automotive AI, virtual-reality, robotics, drone, cloud-gaming, and mobile-cloud technologies.

Business strategies include extending leadership in AI and visual computing, promoting GPU parallel processing, expanding into mobile and cloud platforms, licensing intellectual property, and serving its four principal markets. Sales are conducted largely through a partner network, with additional e-tail and retail channels. ASUSTeK Computer represented 12% of fiscal 2017 revenue. NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries such as TSMC and Samsung and independent subcontractors for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Cash and marketable securities increased 35% to $6.80 billion at fiscal year-end, which management said was sufficient for operating requirements for at least the following 12 months.

The company conducts substantial research and development across GPU and Tegra architectures, software, systems, algorithms, and related technologies. It had invested more than $13 billion in research and development since inception. Fiscal-year research and development expense was $1.46 billion in 2017, $1.33 billion in 2016, and $1.36 billion in 2015. As of January 29, 2017, NVIDIA had 10,299 employees, including 7,282 in research and development.

Principal risks identified include intense competition and rapidly changing technology; failure to develop products or win designs; manufacturing-yield problems; cybersecurity breaches and product defects; reliance on third-party foundries and subcontractors without long-term capacity commitments; supply, pricing, quality, and delivery disruptions; natural disasters and geographically concentrated operations; dependence on major customers; inventory forecasting errors; international trade, regulatory, currency, and political risks; unsuccessful acquisitions or investments; intellectual-property disputes; fluctuating results; privacy concerns; headquarters construction and lease-financing obligations; debt and convertible-note dilution; and anti-takeover provisions. Competitors named include AMD, ARM, Imagination Technologies, Intel, Xilinx, Ambarella, Apple, Broadcom, Mobileye, Qualcomm, Renesas, Samsung, and Texas Instruments.
