NVIDIA’s properties include eight leased commercial buildings in Santa Clara totaling 896,565 square feet, six owned commercial buildings on 36 acres, a headquarters construction project targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018, leased facilities in the United States and internationally, and an owned research and development building in Hyderabad, India.

The quarterly dividend was increased in November 2016 from $0.115 to $0.14 per share. NVIDIA paid $261 million in cash dividends in fiscal 2017. Its repurchase program had acquired 245 million shares for $4.59 billion through January 29, 2017, with approximately $2.73 billion of remaining authorization through December 2020. For fiscal 2018, the company intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders through dividends and repurchases. It also issued $2 billion in notes in 2016 and had $827 million of convertible notes outstanding at year-end; associated warrant settlements resulted in share issuance and potential dilution.

Using pooled 2009–2020 NHANES data, this cross-sectional study analyzed dietary recalls from 32,498 US adults older than 20 and used principal components analysis to identify four empirical dietary patterns. Survey-weighted, adjusted models examined associations with prevalent cardiovascular disease (CVD), a social determinants of health (SDOH) score, and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation.

The four patterns were American (refined grains, meats, milk, oils, solid fats, and added sugars), Prudent (vegetables, meats, poultry, seafood, eggs, and oils), Legume (vegetables and legumes), and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy (fruit, whole grains, soy, nuts/seeds, milk, and yogurt). The American pattern was most common and had the lowest HEI-2020 score; the Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy pattern had the highest score.

CVD was associated with greater adherence to the American pattern but not the other patterns. Each additional SDOH risk factor was associated with 2.5 percentage points more American-pattern adherence, 1.3 points more Legume-pattern adherence, and 1.9 points less adherence to each healthier pattern. SNAP participation was associated with more American-pattern and less Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy pattern adherence. Associations with SDOH and SNAP status, but not CVD, varied by race and ethnicity.

The findings indicate that dietary patterns differ by cardiovascular health and especially socioeconomic vulnerability, supporting interventions tailored to at-risk groups. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, self-reported exposures, and dietary assessment based on two 24-hour recalls.

The State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for June 4, 2001, provides case summaries, editorial material, fields-of-practice listings, classified advertisements, news and moves, bar events, and links to archived e-Journals. It also includes instructions for obtaining a plain-text version and lists contacts for advertising, subscription, event, editorial, and technical matters.

Case summaries address business law, civil rights, contracts, criminal law, employment and labor law, family law, litigation, and negligence and intentional tort. In Helwig v. Vencor, Inc., the Sixth Circuit reversed in part the dismissal of securities-fraud allegations and remanded for discovery. In Anchrum v. Airtouch Cellular, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed dismissal of a racial-discrimination claim. In Kiphart v. Saturn Corp., the Sixth Circuit reversed and remanded after finding sufficient evidence under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Sudul v. Donnell was affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded regarding an excessive jury award. Rock Constr., Inc. v. Onyebuchi was affirmed and reversed in part. The court affirmed In re Bonaroti, People v. Baskin, People v. Gilders, People v. Rivera, People v. Stoutmiles, United States v. Mader, In re Breon, and Creer v. Hills.

The issue also contains attorney and service listings across numerous practice areas, including mediation, administrative law, antitrust, appeals, automobile warranty law, construction, criminal and environmental law, health care, immigration, intellectual property, labor and employment, litigation, medical malpractice, real estate, special education, tax disputes, transportation, and workers’ compensation. Classified advertisements cover document destruction, expert witnesses, lawsuit financing, legal research, office space, attorney and paralegal positions, services, and typing, as well as a campaign advertisement for State Bar Commissioner Greg Ulrich.

A player was praised for his composure, skill, size, and strength, particularly his ability to perform under pressure and score big playoff goals. The team emphasized puck possession, defensive pressure, and adjustments after conceding many goals in the first two games. Following an inspired Game 3, it focused on short-term goals rather than historical statistics and sought to repeat that performance in Game 4.
A study reports that biased online images train AI to perceive women as younger and less experienced, evidencing workplace discrimination against older women.

Wham is a run concept resembling Trap, but with a tight end or fullback pulling to kick out a defensive lineman instead of a guard. It creates favorable, often unexpected running angles and serves as an effective change-up, particularly when defenses rarely see it. Its main drawbacks are complicated, time-consuming installation, the need for precise front recognition and assignments, and the risk of allowing a defender free if any player makes an error. Successful use generally requires a predictable formation and a strong, powerful blocker. The passage provides assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, plus variations including a gun H-back Wham RPO and Shotgun Influence Wham.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on March 13, 2020, reporting that co-founder and Board member Bill Gates resigned effective that date. The filing included Microsoft’s press release announcing Gates’ plans as Exhibit 99.1.

President Donald Trump has nominated Travis Hill as chair of the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), according to Bloomberg News. Hill, a senior adviser at the Treasury Department, requires Senate confirmation. The nomination comes amid tighter credit conditions, elevated interest rates, and concerns about smaller banks' resilience. Hill is expected to favor a pragmatic approach balancing stability with lighter regulatory burdens, consistent with Trump's deregulatory stance. If confirmed, he would oversee deposit insurance, set bank assessments, address bank failures, and shape debates on deposit insurance limits, risk management, and crisis intervention. The appointment is expected to draw congressional scrutiny and represents both continuity and change in U.S. banking oversight.

Hepatitis C is a major global public-health problem, with more than 170 million infections, 71 million chronic cases, and about 1.4 million annual deaths from complications. Rwanda’s reported prevalence is approximately 4%. Household exposure may increase transmission through contact with blood, saliva, shared needles, toothpaste, razors, sexual practices, and parenteral transmission during childbirth.

This descriptive cross-sectional study at CUSP in Huye District, Rwanda, assessed household transmission, risk factors, and awareness among household members of HCV-positive patients. Data were collected from January 2 to February 2, 2021, using questionnaires, HCV antibody rapid tests, and ELISA confirmation. Participation was voluntary and confidential, with ethical approval and written consent.

Thirty families with 148 participants were included. Sixteen participants (10.8%) were reactive by both rapid testing and ELISA, while 132 (89.2%) were non-reactive. Unprotected sex, reported HBV, and reported HIV were significantly associated with HCV positivity (p=0.016 and p=0.001, respectively). Most positive participants had been exposed to unprotected sex. Blood transfusion was not significantly associated with HCV (p=0.058). Only 9 participants (6.1%) answered awareness questions correctly; awareness was not significantly associated with test results (p=0.079).

The findings support early screening of household members of HCV-positive patients, follow-up and monitoring of diagnosed patients, and education on transmission and prevention. The cross-sectional design could not determine the source or direction of household transmission; phylogenetic and non-cross-sectional studies and a countrywide assessment were recommended.

A man threatened and duct-taped two female employees during a Tuesday robbery at Summerland Antique Collective, then fled with cash and merchandise. A customer found the employees about 20 minutes later; neither appeared seriously injured.

Iqaluit-Tasiluk MLA George Hickes told Nunavut’s legislature that some civil servants say senior government managers have threatened them or directed them not to speak with MLAs, reviving concerns he raised in 2014. He said employees should know they have the right to approach their MLA without retaliation, particularly in small communities where complaints may be identifiable and formal processes can fail. Public Service Minister David Akeeagok denied that the Public Service Act prohibits such communication or that such directives exist, saying employees are protected and can contact an ethics officer. Hickes argued MLAs remain an important channel for constituent feedback.

This year’s Mining Expo & Conference will be held April 25–26 at the Windhoek Show Grounds under the theme “Maximising the multiplier effect from Namibia’s mining sector.” Nedbank Namibia CIB’s Mining and Resources team will showcase its financing capabilities, tailored funding solutions and a networking lounge while discussing foreign investment and industry trends. Nedbank supports mining development through equity and debt capital and notes that mining contributes about 11% of Namibia’s GDP.

The speaker discusses a playoff hockey game characterized by physical play and several fights, which he considers part of playoff hockey. He identified an offensive faceoff turnover, a resulting penalty, and the opponent’s power-play goal as important turning points, noting that his team played sloppily and lost momentum after conceding the first goal. He emphasized winning the next faceoff, maintaining puck possession and momentum, and responding after setbacks rather than dwelling on one game.

Faceoffs were described as crucial, while the team’s seven-player lineup was attributed to strong individual performances, depth, and chemistry rather than strict depth-chart considerations. An injured player’s replacement, Pratt, had performed well. The speaker also said the team was physically and mentally ready despite travel and altitude.

Rusty was struggling and was given a more grinding role to improve his involvement and mental adjustment, which the speaker said had helped him. Marty St. Louis was praised for using his opportunity to prove critics wrong, with proving people wrong serving as a major motivation.

An October 18, 2001 Commissioner.COM/SportsLine fantasy-football report combines advertisements with extensive NFL injury news, expected lineups, and start-or-sit advice dated October 14–18. Updates include Todd Heap being questionable, Jeff Garcia expecting to start October 28, Drew Bledsoe remaining doubtful, Tyrone Wheatley’s knee injury, and Chris Weinke’s uncertain thigh injury. Several players—including Herman Moore, Robert Thomas, Jamal Anderson, Chad Johnson, and Justin McCareins—are expected to miss extended time. Recommended fantasy plays include Mark Brunell, Keenan McCardell, Jimmy Smith, and Shaun Alexander. A “Luccis Losers” section adds team-specific notes on players such as Charlie Garner, Duce Staley, Steve McNair, Cris Carter, and Mike Alstott.

Patents expire, enabling entrepreneurs to commercialize 3D-printing processes for broader use. All FDM-like desktop printers trace their roots to Scott Crump’s 1992 patent; his company, Stratasys, now produces industrial printers capable of printing parts up to 36″×24″×36″. Industrial and desktop systems both print layer by layer but differ greatly in price, scale, and applications. Stereolithography and powder-bed fusion are also major industrial methods, with metal printers averaging $566,570 versus $1,094 for desktop machines under $5,000.

Industrial printers support numerous plastics, metals, ceramics, and foundry sands, while Cincinnati’s BAAM system can build parts up to 240″×90″×72″. Industrial throughput increasingly competes with traditional manufacturing; one HP Jet Fusion 4200 can match the output of 163 Ultimaker 3 machines.

NASA uses metal additive manufacturing for propulsion components, while GE applies it to lighter, longer-lasting LEAP engine fuel nozzles and other redesigned helicopter-engine parts. The 2017 Wohlers Report, a 343-page industry reference covering additive-manufacturing technology, vendors, software, and materials, is recommended for professionals.

The paper introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework to analyze computational problems through both their internal constructions and observable behavior. CDF represents a function as a triple of structural property sets: syntactic space \(S_{\mathrm{syn}}\), containing symbolic patterns and generative structure; semantic space \(S_{\mathrm{sem}}\), encoding input-output relations and interpretations; and logical space \(S_{\mathrm{log}}\), containing proof-theoretic or computational realizations. Three mappings connect these layers: \(\alpha\) from syntax to semantics, \(\beta\) from semantics to logic, and \(\gamma\) directly from syntax to logic.

For a function and fixed basepoint, CDF generates the syntactic orbit of iterated applications, the semantic graph of the function, and hierarchical proof or computation trees. Examples illustrate CDF for the linear function \(f(x)=x+1\) and recursive factorial function. Recursive inputs can deepen computation trees and destabilize the mappings, a behavior the paper associates with the expanding structures of NP problems.

CDF defines stable mappings as polynomially bounded and explosive mappings as growing faster than polynomially on polynomially bounded inputs. A structurally coherent function satisfies \(\gamma=\beta\circ\alpha\). The framework classifies problems as ComCDF when this coherence and a stable semantic mapping hold, ExpCDF when coherence fails or the semantic mapping is unstable, and Semi-ExpCDF when coherence is partial. CDF-complete functions have definable components, balanced mappings, and stable mappings. The framework also interprets the layered mappings as potential semantic paths and direct computation as actual logical realization.

The paper contrasts 2-SAT and 3-SAT. Binary 2-SAT clauses yield local implications, compositional reasoning, graph-based polynomial-time solution, and stable CDF mappings. Ternary 3-SAT clauses create non-local interactions, an exponential semantic space of \(O(2^n)\), and unstable logical reasoning; 3-SAT is classified as NP-complete. The paper attributes this semantic explosion to 3-SAT’s clause-level structure and argues that stabilizing it would require transforming it into a structurally different problem.

European shares rose 0.4% on Wednesday, with little reaction to Theresa May’s formal notification that Britain would leave the EU and begin a two-year negotiation process. The STOXX 600 reached its highest close in nearly 16 months, while the DAX also gained 0.4%. Daimler rose after forecasting record first-quarter Mercedes-Benz sales. EU antitrust authorities blocked the London Stock Exchange–Deutsche Boerse merger. Banks fell amid concerns that the ECB would keep policy easy; Deutsche Bank and its rights rose. Engie and 3I advanced on analyst upgrades, while Scout24’s weak results and outlook sent shares lower. Aurelius plunged over 35% as investors remained skeptical of its response to a short-seller report.

China has emerged as a global clean-energy leader as other countries retreat from climate commitments. At the UN Climate Summit, Xi Jinping pledged to reduce China’s greenhouse-gas emissions by 7–10% by 2035, marking a shift from previous promises merely to peak emissions. Although this would amount to roughly 1% annual reductions—slower than several industrialized countries—the commitment was considered significant and potentially achievable.

China also targeted 3,600 gigawatts of installed wind and solar capacity by 2035, six times its 2020 level, and more than 30% renewables in its energy mix. It plans to make electric vehicles mainstream, expand carbon-emissions trading into more sectors, and increase forest coverage to 34 billion cubic meters. Support comes from major battery and automotive companies, access to rare-earth minerals, and strong research institutions.

China invested $625 billion in clean energy last year, nearly one-third of the global total. Its large domestic market, research, and rapid technology adoption have sharply reduced renewable-energy costs, replaced coal domestically, and reshaped global green-technology markets.
Paulo Dybala is fit and likely to start against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-final second leg. He chose to renew his Juventus contract until 2022 after scoring twice in the first leg.

An open-label randomized controlled trial in western Cambodia compared 14-day primaquine regimens for preventing *Plasmodium vivax* recurrence. After seven days of artesunate, G6PD-normal patients were assigned to primaquine 3.5 mg/kg/day, 7.0 mg/kg/day, or no primaquine; G6PD-deficient patients received no primaquine. Patients were relocated for 90 days to a malaria-free area to reduce reinfection.

Among 156 allocated patients, recurrence by day 90 occurred in 81.4% without primaquine, 24.4% with 3.5 mg/kg, and 4.7% with 7.0 mg/kg. High-dose primaquine significantly reduced recurrence compared with low dose (hazard ratio 0.17; p=0.0229), with the advantage persisting to day 180. Both regimens were generally well tolerated, with no serious adverse events and no significant safety difference between them. Increased methaemoglobin was more frequent with the high dose but was clinically silent and resolved after treatment.

The authors concluded that 7.0 mg/kg over 14 days was more effective than 3.5 mg/kg and recommended its use for G6PD-normal patients in Cambodia and potentially elsewhere in Southeast Asia. Limitations included the small single-center sample, inability to distinguish all relapses from recrudescence, and the supervised treatment setting.

Sebi permits debt issuers to request credit-rating reviews with supporting documents. Reviews must be considered by CRA committees with a majority of independent members. CRAs must disclose unaccepted ratings and related details for 12 months, upload half-yearly summaries within 15 days, and separately report securities and other financial-instrument ratings.

Melinda Rosetti-Spence was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling about $266,600 from Pink Hearts Fund, where she volunteered as treasurer. She pleaded guilty after writing 132 checks to herself from March to July 2016. The judge ordered her to repay about $181,000; her family is paying the balance.

The U.S. government froze about $18 billion in federal funding for New York City infrastructure projects over concerns that contracts used unconstitutional race- or gender-based DEI criteria. The freeze, confirmed by the Office of Management and Budget, affects projects including the Second Avenue Subway extension and Hudson River Tunnel, with $300 million in payments already suspended. Federal audits will determine whether grants violated anti-discrimination rules. City officials warn that delays could disrupt construction, threaten thousands of jobs and increase costs, while the government shutdown adds further uncertainty. If violations are found, New York may have to renegotiate grants or lose funding; if cleared, funds could resume. The action signals broader scrutiny of DEI-linked programs.

English local authorities are owed millions in refunds after the Ministry of Justice said council tax summons fees had been set too high since 2013–14 due to an administrative error. Councils had overpaid by about £9m annually, including £2.50 per application above recovery costs. Officials promised reduced fees and a reimbursement scheme.

LG plans to release webOS-powered TVs later this month, with Sky’s EPG compatible from launch. The integrated guide will enable Sky viewing and control through LG’s Magic Remote gesture and voice controls, while the Today menu aggregates options from apps, online platforms, and live TV.

STAT’s personnel feature highlights enGene’s hire of Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer. Sweiti previously led oncology clinical development at Johnson & Johnson globally. The subscriber-exclusive article includes related coverage of drug-industry developments such as tariffs, layoffs, FDA policy, pricing, antibacterial innovation, dementia, and women’s health.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions, representing seven agencies overseeing 3,000 degree-granting institutions, issued a nonbinding statement encouraging colleges to use AI to improve transfer-credit evaluations. Manual reviews are often inconsistent, slow and inequitable, contributing to lost credits, repeated courses, reduced aid and students abandoning degree programs. A 2024 Public Agenda survey found that 58% of adults who tried to transfer credit lost some of it.

AI can compare course descriptions, enrollment data and learning outcomes to identify existing or new equivalencies, speed evaluations and reduce administrative work. A 59-institution pilot is testing a platform that applies AI to course matching. CRAC urges institutions to apply credits toward degree completion unless required learning outcomes are not met and to base decisions on evidence rather than anecdotes, assumptions or past practices. Accreditors and researchers emphasize that institutions should retain human oversight, verify AI results and establish reliable safeguards, noting that the technology’s accuracy and large-scale implementation remain important challenges.

Cryotherapy places users in chambers reaching 180°F below zero for short sessions. Enthusiasts claim it aids muscle recovery, reduces inflammation and joint pain, improves circulation, relieves anxiety and depression, elevates mood, boosts immunity and burns calories, though scientific support is limited. Developed in the 1970s by Japanese doctor Toshima Yamauchi for arthritis, it is now offered by Polar Brrr Cryo in West Michigan. Introductory packages cost $25 for one class or $90 for three; regular sessions cost $55. The facility serves athletes, office workers and others and provides supervision during three-minute sessions. It is not FDA-approved, carries warnings about frostbite, burns and eye injuries, and advises people with heart problems or hypertension to consult a doctor. An unsupervised 2015 death was reported.

The Israel Antiquities Authority announced a 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment discovered in Jerusalem in 2015, bearing “Hyrcanus” in Hebrew letters. Because Hyrcanus was common in the Hasmonean period and was the name of two rulers, the IAA said its owner and purpose—royal possession, ordinary use, or special tribute—cannot be determined. The fragment was found beneath a mikvah complex at the Givati parking lot in the City of David, near the Seleucid Akra fortress. Chalk vessels were used by Jews because they were considered incapable of becoming ritually unclean.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that shareholders held its annual meeting on March 1, 2019. James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner were elected to the board. Shareholders approved Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent registered public accounting firm for 2019 and approved an advisory resolution on executive compensation. Two shareholder proposals—“Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “True Diversity Board Policy”—were not approved.

The article examines holiday and calendar effects in U.S. stocks, focusing on the S&P 500 and SPY, with index data extending to 1960. Holiday effects are described as small, abnormal seasonal patterns rather than guaranteed get-rich-quick opportunities. Proposed explanations include reduced holiday liquidity, optimism, limited macroeconomic news, and risk-reduction selling before holidays followed by gradual price recovery.

Monthly benchmarks show the strongest S&P 500 period running from October through April. Tests of individual holidays found little or no effect around Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President’s Day, Memorial Day, and Labor Day. Independence Day produced stronger results: 28 trades, a 1.01% average gain, a 68% win rate, a 2.97 profit factor, and 4% maximum drawdown. Thanksgiving also performed well, with 28 trades, a 0.82% average gain, a 65% win rate, and a 2.72 profit factor. Applying the same Thanksgiving strategy to a retail fund produced slightly better results. A post-Christmas trading strategy generated 60 trades, a 1% average gain, a 67% win rate, a 4.8 profit factor, and a 2.9% maximum drawdown.

Post-holiday tests found no gains from holding through the holiday itself, while the second trading day after a holiday generally performed best. A separate overnight strategy achieved an average gain of 0.56%, a 71% win rate, a profit factor of 4, and an annual return of 3.5% while invested only 1% of the time.

The article concludes that holiday effects are real but modest and that the clearest tradeable patterns are associated with Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. It emphasizes that results depend on strategy design and notes that other interpretations may produce different outcomes.

Scottish councils can raise the band D council tax by up to 3%, ending the government’s long-running freeze. Some councils plan the maximum increase, while others may continue the freeze voluntarily.

MSPs approved higher multipliers for council tax bands E-H from April, affecting about 700,000 of Scotland’s 2.6m homes regardless of local decisions and raising around £100m annually. The average band E household will pay about £2 more weekly and the average band H household about £10 more, before any local rate increase. This will generate more in areas with many higher-band properties: 56% in East Renfrewshire, compared with 18% in East Ayrshire, 37% in Edinburgh, 27% in Aberdeen, 16% in Glasgow and 14% in Dundee. The raised money will be spent locally, while schools will receive extra funding from elsewhere.

Council tax bands remain based on 1991 property values; analysis suggested 57% of properties would have changed band in 2014. The government says revaluation could cost up to £7m, take several years and cause significant bill changes.

Most council funding comes from government grants. A budget agreement with the Greens added £160m in direct funding, but Labour says core council budgets remain £170m lower, while the Greens describe the reductions as less severe. The government expected £70m from maximum council tax increases, though not all councils are expected to impose them.

The passage presents a guide to Bollinger Bands, a volatility-measurement tool developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s. Bollinger Bands consist of a middle simple moving average and upper and lower bands placed a specified number of standard deviations above and below it. The typical configuration is a 20-day SMA with two standard deviations, although the moving-average period, standard deviation, and moving-average type can be adjusted; a 9-period, two-standard-deviation setup is recommended for scalping.

Band width reflects volatility: bands widen during high volatility and contract during calm or consolidating markets. A squeeze or volatility-contraction setup may precede a larger directional move, although false breakouts or “head fakes” can occur. Breakouts above or below the bands may indicate bullish or bearish momentum and should be confirmed with other analysis.

The guide describes strategies involving breakouts, squeeze and pinch-play setups, %B positioning, trend walks, band bounces, double-band trend following, bandwidth, RSI divergence, reversals, volatility contraction, and triple-band analysis. %B measures a price’s position within the bands, while reversals may be identified through double tops or bottoms interacting with the bands. Other indicators—including RSI, MACD, and the Stochastic Oscillator—can help confirm signals.

Risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, and confirmation from price action and additional indicators. Limitations include delayed signals, false overbought or oversold readings in strong trends, equal weighting of older and recent prices in the SMA, and sensitivity to market noise on short timeframes.

Testing produced mixed, asset-dependent results. A mean-reversion strategy underperformed buy-and-hold and was losing since 2018, while some breakout approaches showed promise in gold but not stocks or stock indices. The passage emphasizes that no single setting, timeframe, indicator, or strategy works across all markets.

Headlines roundup: Amazon is designing an AI chip for Alexa, whose Super Bowl ad topped YouTube views, and Amazon revealed Alexa will power the Big Mouth Billy Bass talking fish. CES reveals included Sony's Aibo robot dog and a foldable television. Amazon and Google discounted home speakers so deeply they likely lost money per unit, Apple's flagship speaker was delayed past Christmas, and a rogue Alexa played music at 2 a.m.

The document combines an AMD specification agreement with the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification. Recipients may use the specification only to design AMD-compatible products and provide feedback; they may not duplicate it, remove notices, or transfer it or their rights. AMD retains all rights, provides the specification “AS IS,” disclaims warranties and liability, and states that its products are not intended or warranted for life-support, surgical implant, or other applications where failure could cause severe harm. Users must comply with export laws, and U.S. government users receive restricted rights. Feedback may be used and commercialized without restriction or confidentiality, provided it does not violate third-party intellectual property or licensing terms. California law governs disputes, which must be brought in Santa Clara County.

Technically, the specification standardizes communication between SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors through a 4 KB decrypted, shared Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block modeled on the VMCB save area. Version 2 adds hypervisor feature advertisement and initial SEV-SNP support. Later revisions cover 64-bit guest-request sequences, error reporting, VLEK GUIDs, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPLs, page-state changes, the SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC. It defines GHCB MSR negotiation and GPA registration, automatic and non-automatic exits, VMGEXIT processing and validation, SNP firmware and certificate requests, application-processor creation and SMP booting, Restricted Injection mechanisms, NMI handling, and debug-register behavior. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

India’s top 1% captured 22% of national income—the highest share since income tax began in 1922—up from 6% in the early 1980s, according to Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty. They linked the reversal after 1983–84 to policies retreating from the public sector and encouraging business, entrepreneurship and foreign investment. Inequality declined from the 1950s through the 1970s, when bottom 50% and middle 40% incomes grew faster than average.

This collection of news reports, mostly dated October 29, 2001, documents Enron's credit and stock collapse and the market reaction.

**Ratings and losses.** Moody's cut Enron's senior unsecured long-term debt rating from Baa1 to Baa2 (two notches above junk), placed all long-term obligations on review for downgrade, and put its P-2 commercial paper rating on review for downgrade. Moody's cited "deterioration in Enron's financial flexibility" from write-downs and charges tied to previously undisclosed partnership investments, which it said reduced investor confidence and would raise nominal leverage to somewhat over 50 percent while slashing earnings; it also downgraded the Marlin and Osprey trusts (to Baa2 and Baa3). Standard & Poor's affirmed a BBB+ rating with a negative outlook, and Fitch maintained triple-B-plus with a negative Rating Watch.

**Causes.** Enron reported a third-quarter net loss of $638 million including a $1.01 billion charge for ill-fated investments, plus a $1.2 billion write-down of shareholder equity linked to partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, who was ousted after the SEC began an inquiry into possible conflicts of interest. CEO Jeff Skilling had quit in August, with Chairman Ken Lay returning to the CEO role. Analysts noted the size of Enron's earnings expectations had also become a target for political criticism.

**Stock and bonds.** Shares fell about 10 percent, to roughly $13.81–$13.99, their lowest since December 1994, down more than half since October 17 and about 82 percent over 12 months, erasing some $15 billion in market value in a week (market capitalization reported variously from $62.7 billion to $10.5 billion). The 6.4 percent notes due 2006 fell from par to about 80 cents on the dollar, with yields rising to 12.1 percent, before improving slightly Monday; about $15.8 billion of Enron bonds were outstanding, nearly $9 billion due 2003–2006. Bond analysts said lenders would demand harsher terms and collateral.

**Liquidity actions.** Enron drew down roughly $3.3 billion in credit lines, using about $2 billion to repay commercial paper, and said it was seeking $1–2 billion in new loans from banks including Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase. It also planned a $2.9 billion sale of Portland General Electric to Northwest Natural Gas, with about $1.8 billion of proceeds earmarked for debt reduction. Moody's called the revolver drawdown a smart business move but retained concerns about Enron's credibility.

**Trading partners and markets.** U.S. wholesale gas and electricity traders said dealings with Enron remained at normal levels, though some European energy groups froze trades over credit concerns and discussed letters of credit; no liquidity impact was yet evident, including in the U.K. power market. A newsletter reported Royal Dutch/Shell might be interested in acquiring Enron, which the company declined to comment on.

**Commentary.** GimmeCredit said a junk rating was unlikely and bonds could be undervalued if off-balance-sheet obligations were no more than $3 billion. Rating agencies also warned of a broad credit deterioration, with S&P expecting more than 200 companies and about $100 billion in debt to default in 2001, against $42.3 billion in 2000. Opinion pieces noted insider buying in power producers Calpine, AES, Mirant and NRG (with Enron excluded for continued insider selling), warned that Enron's debacle could undermine confidence in the wider market, and argued Enron's contributions to Houston deserved thanks and that its troubles should not be prejudged.

Russia has classified Ukrainian drone pilots as high-value targets and is intensifying efforts to locate and kill them with missiles, bombs, and heavy bombardments. Ukrainian personnel said operators are increasingly targeted because their ability to disrupt enemy missions makes them force multipliers, while pilot deaths have risen sharply. Drones now gather intelligence, assist artillery targeting, and destroy armored vehicles, with recent assessments attributing about 70% of casualties on both sides to drone use. Ukraine also targets Russian drone operators, while Ukrainian pilots use stronger shelters, deeper underground positions, and frequent rotations to reduce their vulnerability.

The article reports a daily intake of 6–8 glasses (1.2 liters), with water also coming from food, and cites research suggesting drinking according to thirst may be preferable to a fixed schedule. Excessive intake can rarely cause water intoxication, particularly after exercise-related dehydration. In a 12-week study of 48 adults aged 55–75, those drinking two cups of water before meals lost an average of 15.5 pounds versus 11 pounds and consumed 75–90 fewer calories. It recommends water instead of sugary drinks while warning against excessive intake.

The study introduces Doublethink, a Bayesian model-averaging method for systematically identifying direct effects of non-genetic variables in biobank-scale data. It addresses limitations of candidate risk-factor studies, including unmeasured confounders, multiple testing, publication bias, mediation, reverse causation, and collider bias. Unlike machine-learning methods, which measure predictive contribution, Doublethink estimates each variable’s direct effect while averaging over uncertainty about which other variables to include.

Under a specified prior and large-sample assumptions, Doublethink converts model-averaged posterior odds into asymptotically valid adjusted p-values. The procedure is a closed testing procedure, simultaneously controlling the Bayesian false discovery rate and the frequentist familywise error rate. Prior parameters affect statistical power but not the asymptotic null distribution.

Doublethink was implemented with Markov chain Monte Carlo in R and Python and applied to 1,912 variables and 201,912 UK Biobank participants, comprising 1,917 COVID-19 hospitalization cases and 200,000 controls. Variables included 184 covariates, 865 binary encodings of factor levels, and 863 pre-2020 ICD-10 codes. At a posterior-odds threshold of 10 and familywise error level of approximately 0.00047, nine individual variables were significant. These included dementia, acute lower respiratory infection, tendency to fall, prior carer support, medication count, psychoactive-substance history, educational qualifications, and other physical therapy. Nine predefined variable groups were also significant, including groups representing age, sex, deprivation, and obesity-related measures. Group testing recovered signals diluted by correlations among highly related variables.

Post-hoc grouping identified additional significant combinations, including measures of obesity and deprivation and a combination of constipation and urinary tract infection that might reflect kidney disease. Such grouping allowed extensive searches without inflating the false discovery rate or familywise error rate. Comparisons with 127 published UK Biobank COVID-19 studies found support for direct effects of established categories such as age, sex, obesity, socioeconomic status, and smoking, as well as lung disease, alcohol intake, comorbidity, kidney disease, and educational attainment. Diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension lacked evidence of direct effects, although the authors cautioned that this did not exclude mediated effects. Psychiatric disorders, infection, dementia, and aging showed strong direct effects despite receiving limited attention in prior studies.

The approach estimates direct rather than total effects, so results cannot establish the consequences of hypothetical interventions and depend on the variables measured and included. Other limitations include selection and measurement biases, data curation, reliance on large samples and specific priors, sensitivity to prior choices, and substantial computational demands. The analysis required 3,500 CPU hours and could not examine interactions, nonlinear effects, or rare variables extensively. The authors conclude that Doublethink offers a systematic framework for direct risk-factor discovery while linking Bayesian and frequentist inference, while further theoretical and empirical validation is needed.

The passage traces how algorithms and object-oriented design patterns established reusable, shared programming practices, and how open-source communities extended collaborative development to distributed systems. Patterns let developers learn from prior experience, communicate through a common vocabulary, and build reusable components. The goal is to apply similar structure and predictability to distributed-system design.

Containers are presented as the basis for single-node patterns because they isolate resources, clarify ownership, separate concerns, and support modular deployment. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a helper that adds functionality, such as HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, monitoring, or Git-based deployment. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, stable APIs, and clear documentation. The ambassador pattern brokers communication with external services, supporting sharding, service discovery, and request-splitting experiments. The adapter pattern translates inconsistent application interfaces into common formats for monitoring, logging, and health checks.

The passage then introduces microservices and multi-node patterns, highlighting their agility, independent scaling, and API-based decoupling, alongside increased debugging and architectural complexity. Replicated, load-balanced stateless services provide redundancy and scale, use readiness probes, support session tracking, and can include caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services divide data or state among specialized replicas, improving storage capacity but making individual shard failures more consequential. Replicating each shard combines sharding with fault tolerance for highly available systems.

This coaching guide covers three jump ball situations—defensive, even, and offensive—and how teams should prepare for each.

Defensive jump balls occur when the opponent has a definite advantage and control is doubtful. Defenders must prioritize a stop if the opponent gains possession, since "a basket saved is a basket made." Defenders should rotate early against opponents with a six-inch or greater height advantage, watch the jumper's eyes and hands for telegraphed tips (most right-handed jumpers tip forward to their left; left-handed players tip forward to their right), and maintain contact with the jumper. Box alignment rotations require X1 and X2 to establish strong pass-denial positions while the two non-jumpers rotate into open spots; diamond alignment rotations have X3 and X4 taking the two spots in line with the basket with non-jumpers boxing out. Additional defensive alignments include a defensive alignment versus box, a defensive alignment versus diamond with clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations on a predetermined signal, and a "Y" alignment placing two defenders back to eliminate easy shots when the opponent has a superior jumper.

Even jump balls resemble offensive rebounds: players box out, establish inside position, anticipate and rotate early, and rotate clockwise or counter-clockwise on a predetermined signal (such as a hand on the hip or head) to crash open spots.

Offensive jump ball plays can be run when a team has a six-inch or greater height advantage, generally tipping forward to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance and flowing into set or motion offense if the defense recovers. Proven plays include Ball Possession, Double Tap, Post Split (diamond and box alignments), Jumper Fly, Jumper Fly (unbalanced alignment), Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem Left, and Loop, each with detailed assignments for tipper, receivers, screens, and defensive balance.

After the Pittsburgh Penguins won the Stanley Cup, the speaker described his excitement and credited Fleury’s strong performance, including a crucial late save, while noting that his own two goals did not reflect his best stick handling. He praised the team’s sacrifices, Geno’s Conn Smythe Award, and the collective effort to win for an injured leader. He emphasized hockey’s mental demands, confidence, and the importance of believing in teammates, expressing particular happiness for his close friend Fleury, whom he called a winning goaltender. The speaker also called Sidney Crosby the team’s heart, soul, and leader, admiring his consistency, work ethic, and respect for the game. Finally, he credited Mario’s role in keeping the franchise in Pittsburgh and said winning the Cup with Crosby was a deeply meaningful achievement, making it the best day of his life.

The author told Mr. Toivola that an intercepted Tokyo broadcast allegedly attributed to the Finnish Legation dismissed reports of a Soviet-Finnish peace as “nothing but Anglo-American machinations.” The author doubted the statement and said that, if made, it would hurt Finland’s interests because the U.S. Government had no role in the rumors; Toivola was disturbed, but the discussion was friendly. Finland’s minister clarified that travel restrictions applied to all foreign diplomats, Helsinki was a war zone, and Finnish citizen staff were subject only to general Finnish restrictions, while other foreign missions reportedly faced no similar limits. The British Embassy reported that a Soviet minister sought secret, unofficial contact with Finland and hinted that more favorable peace terms might come sooner. A State Department memorandum recorded British-American agreement not to encourage Finland’s continued policy and proposed telling Witting to temper his optimism about peace negotiations.

Survivors and relatives of the 72 victims of the Grenfell Tower fire testified during the first phase of a public inquiry, recounting their losses and criticizing authorities over safety failures. The inquiry, chaired by retired judge Martin Moore-Bick, aims to establish how the June 2017 disaster unfolded and recommend prevention measures, but began by centering victims’ identities and relatives’ suffering.

Ahmed Elgwahry described hearing his mother and sister die by phone. Paulos Tekle said repeated instructions to remain inside delayed his family’s escape, and his five-year-old son died. Marcio Gomes recounted the death of his prematurely born son, while Karim Mussilhy described the terror visible in the tower’s smoke-blackened staircase.

Witnesses criticized the local council, building manager, government officials and fire authorities, including advice to stay in apartments as flames engulfed the building. Survivors urged the inquiry to address inequalities affecting residents and systemic failures that left homes unsafe.

Trump faced backlash over his response to the white-supremacist rally in Charlottesville. Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from the American Manufacturing Council, citing intolerance and extremism; Trump criticized his drug pricing. Frazier joined Elon Musk and Disney’s Robert Iger, who resigned after Trump withdrew from the Paris Climate Accord.

Research and Markets added its “Global Industrial Hybrid Stepper Motors Market 2018-2022” report, forecasting revenue above $1 billion by 2022. The report covers market sizing, segmentation, regional and vendor analysis, drivers, challenges and trends such as miniaturization, robotic design advances and IoT-enabled stepper motors. Rising demand for automated industrial equipment is a key driver, while competition from servo and conventional stepper motors is a challenge. Vendors include AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons’ Nidec and Schneider Electric.

The article examines two stocks offering forecast dividend yields of 7.1%. Taylor Wimpey’s planned £450m dividend for 2017 is comfortably covered by £511.6m in 2016 free cash flow and expected profits. Despite the cyclical housing market and likely temporary special dividends, demand remains strong, making the yield affordable and sustainable.

Connect Group’s expected 9.8p dividend is covered by strong cash flow, but its £141.7m net debt, negative £151.8m tangible asset value, and sensitivity to trading or lending conditions create dividend risks. The pending Education sale may not resolve these issues, so risks currently outweigh potential rewards.
A Regina Police survey found high satisfaction and integrity, but nearly 25% perceived insensitivity toward Indigenous people; reconciliation training began in January.

Baseline out-of-bounds plays require dedicated defense because defenders have a 5-on-4 numerical advantage, and offensive players attack directly toward the basket, making defensive errors costly. Screen-and-roll actions also make automatic zone coverage vulnerable.

Four defensive approaches are presented. The “Jam” option uses no-switch, physical pressure to deny screens, cuts, passing lanes, and the inbounder, potentially producing five-second violations, offensive fouls, or turnovers. The “Jump Switch” option attacks passing lanes with aggressive switches, denies rolls, smothers the inbounder, and applies pressure after the pass; it is especially useful with less than five seconds remaining, provided lanes are aggressively denied. The “Trap” option doubles the inbounder, follows the pass to trap the receiver, rotates defenders, and pressures reversals and the post.

Combination defenses adapt to offensive formations. “Box & One” uses one chaser and four defenders in a box zone, “Diamond & One” uses one chaser with a diamond alignment, and “Triangle & Two” uses two chasers with a three-player triangle zone. All protect against quick lobs or cuts, deny the inbound pass, and transition to normal positioning or matchups once the ball is inbounded.

A multicentre study used excised nerves from 22 adults with Morton’s neuroma and 11 control participants to investigate local molecular changes in chronic peripheral neuropathic pain. RNA sequencing and histological analyses found substantial differential expression in Morton’s neuroma nerves, with upregulated genes associated with immune and inflammatory responses and downregulated genes related to nervous-system development, axon guidance and myelination. WGCNA and cell-deconvolution analyses linked immune and neurogenesis modules and increased macrophage populations to symptom severity, particularly paroxysmal pain. Elevated expression of MARCO, CD163 and STAB1 indicated a glucocorticoid-associated M(GC) macrophage subset; MARCO expression correlated with paroxysmal pain and paraesthesia.

Immunofluorescence confirmed demyelination, increased intraneural T-cell density and increased CD163+ and MARCO+ macrophage populations in Morton’s neuroma. Overall CD68+ macrophage density correlated with burning pain, although subtype-specific macrophage densities were not significantly associated with pain. No significant group difference in β-tubulin III staining was found, though lower axonal staining correlated with pain.

The findings implicate persistent local neuroinflammation, including macrophages and the MARCO+ M(GC) subset, in chronic neuropathic pain associated with focal nerve injury. Limitations included small samples, unequal sex distributions, control nerves from varied anatomical and functional sites, human-tissue variability and validation restricted to selected findings.

The passage frames diffusion models and flow matching as special cases of learning stochastic dynamics between distributions, and reviews the Schrödinger bridge problem and iterative proportional fitting (IPF), which solves forward and reverse half-bridge problems until the processes are time reversals. Standard diffusion training is presented as a one-step IPF special case, but existing IPF variants require samples from both endpoint distributions.

The paper extends IPF to data-to-energy and energy-to-energy settings, where one or both marginals are available only as queryable unnormalised densities with unknown normalizers. The resulting algorithm is described as the first general method for these bridge types and uses reinforcement-learning losses and diffusion-sampler stabilization techniques for efficient training. Experiments show that it learns low-cost stochastic bridges comparable to data-to-data IPF with oracle samples. Time discretization also enables learning both drift and diffusion coefficients, improving existing data-to-data IPF methods. Finally, the method is applied to latent prior-to-posterior translation, yielding a scalable, data-free image-to-image translation approach. The background formalizes Schrödinger bridges as KL-minimizing processes subject to fixed endpoint marginals and relates them to dynamic and entropy-regularized optimal transport.

The speaker describes a one-goal hockey game in which the lone goal came on a second-period penalty. His team had promising chances but missed them and must capitalize on limited opportunities against strong opponents. He emphasizes that the team’s success depends on speed and skating rather than physical play, crediting those strengths in victories over Detroit and against Vancouver and San Jose. He plans to improve last-change deployments, line usage, and player matchups without changing the team’s style. The team tried to extend the series and did everything possible to win. He also discusses draft and restricted-free-agent preparations, business relationships between the teams’ organizations, a productive player whose criticism came largely from outside the team, and the constraints of the collective-bargaining environment. He prefers other coaches to handle media questions and notes that players need time between periods for treatment, refocusing, and reviewing the game plan.

Overnight trading means buying at the close and selling at the next day's open or close, typically holding for 24 hours. The article notes that the average gain from the open to the close has been zero over the last 30 years, so it focuses on the "overnight edge" and on infrequent excessive returns occurring under specific conditions, rather than on averages.

Using SPY backtests since 1993 (with ES futures giving similar results), the article presents several strategies: Turnaround Tuesday; a holiday seasonality (94 trades, 0.55% average gain, 70% win rate); an end-of-month effect (233 trades, 0.3% average, 66% win rate); another weekday effect (305 trades, 68% win rate); a mean-reversion pattern (373 trades, 0.34% average, 60% win rate); two options-week-expiration variants; and a mixed portfolio of mean-reversion, breakout and gap strategies (237 trades, 0.41% average). Combined as one non-overlapping portfolio, the strategies performed well on system performance metrics; they were developed in 2017 and traded from 2021, with out-of-sample results from 2018 averaging 0.34% per trade, helped by windfall 2020 profits.

The authors argue returns are realistic (near-zero commissions, small slippage), that curve fitting and survivorship bias are limited (few variables, all 2017 strategies included, no data mining), while cautioning that backtests are approximations. The main drawback is the need to trade at the close, requiring automated or mechanical execution.

Portfolio construction guidance stresses uncorrelated strategies, diversification across asset classes (e.g., oil, gold, Bitcoin) and time frames, and avoiding overlapping signals (such as multiple mean-reversion strategies on the same index, since SPY/ES trades coincide with DAX trades). Avoiding worst drawdowns helps compounding. Stocks tend to mean-revert short term and trend long term; trend-following has low win rates; most short strategies perform poorly, yet can still reduce downside risk and improve overall CAGR. Because most gains come from few days, trading like a "barracuda" can improve risk-adjusted returns.

The May 26–27, 2001 clippings center on Enron, California’s electricity crisis, and related political and business developments. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay urged continued deregulation during a private Beverly Hills meeting with Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan, actor Arnold Schwarzenegger, financier Michael Milken and other business leaders. Enron’s four-page plan proposed that ratepayers assume public-utility debt, that price-manipulation investigations be curtailed, and that electricity supply increase through conservation and peak-use pricing. Governor Gray Davis’s administration rejected the proposal, while meeting participants reportedly remained noncommittal and signed none of the attached open letter supporting Lay’s position.

Californians were widely reducing energy use despite higher electricity costs. A Field Poll found that 63 percent had cut consumption by at least 10 percent and nearly one-quarter by at least 20 percent. Politically, Senator Dianne Feinstein sought hearings into possible improper influence between Federal Energy Regulatory Commission members and energy companies. The Senate confirmed Pat Wood III and Nora Brownell to FERC, while Vice President Dick Cheney favored Wood over Chairman Curtis Hebert. Reports also said Enron executives interviewed regulatory candidates and supplied preferred names to White House personnel. Hebert said he rejected Kenneth Lay’s offer of support if he favored Enron’s deregulation principles; Lay said Hebert sought Enron’s intervention with the White House. A projected shift in Senate committee control could advance a Feinstein-Smith bill imposing temporary restraints on Western wholesale power sales, although President Bush and Cheney opposed price controls.

A Houston Chronicle compensation survey found that eight of the ten highest-paid Houston executives worked in oil and gas, including four of the top six from Enron. Nabors Industries’ Eugene Isenberg ranked first at $63.9 million. Enron Broadband Services’ Kenneth Rice ranked second at $47.4 million, while Lay ranked sixth at $35.7 million because he held fewer stock options.

India’s Maharashtra State Electricity Board and Enron-controlled Dabhol Power Company continued their dispute over unpaid bills, electricity rates and Dabhol’s startup performance. MSEB sought cancellation of the power-purchase agreement and damages of about 7 billion rupees, while Dabhol had issued a preliminary termination notice and rejected a roughly $39 million April payment because it was submitted under protest. Dabhol said the utility could not simultaneously rescind the contract and affirm it through payment. Indian lenders planned to meet foreign financiers in Singapore to discuss continued disbursements, deferred guarantees and reported cost overruns of about $400 million, while Enron was seeking ways to lower the tariff.

Saudi Arabia was preparing multibillion-dollar gas-development agreements with foreign oil companies. Exxon was appointed to lead the Red Sea project with Occidental Petroleum and Enron, while South Ghawar and Shaybah participants were still awaiting confirmed leadership. A report said Saudi Arabia required companies seeking core gas projects to accept state-owned Aramco as a partner and give it majority voting rights on key issues.

Other reports said Enron India, after deciding against new Indian investment, redeployed most of its roughly 100 employees to Dabhol and Broadband Solutions; sources described the Indian operation as largely a holding company and said several employees had resigned. Separately, financial disclosures showed Republican Greg Ganske potentially entering the 2002 Iowa Senate race against Tom Harkin with substantially greater personal wealth, although both candidates had relied primarily on campaign fundraising.

The speaker credits the team’s success to strong player depth, collective support, and learning from veteran players such as Ray Bourque. He advises respecting opponents’ strengths, maintaining good positioning, containing dangerous forwards, and avoiding unnecessary battles. He describes the long playoff run as evidence of the league’s competitiveness, requiring preparation, confidence, and management of injuries, emotions, and pressure. Despite outside expectations, the team remains determined, plans to reset, and aims to keep its approach simple.

Small-sided soccer games (SSGs) feature two teams with fewer than 11 players each on a reduced field; team sizes need not be equal. Used in practice and competition, they increase ball touches and meaningful participation. Practice games range from 3v3 to 9v9, are fast-paced and confined to small spaces, and address specific themes such as possession, passing, attacking, defending, transitions, shooting, player movement, goalkeeping and rondos. Formats progress with age from U6 through U16, with younger players using fewer players, smaller areas and simpler games. Fields may be square, ranging from 20 to 60 yards, or rectangular, ranging from 20x40 to 50x70 yards.

U.S. Soccer’s 2017 Player Development Initiatives establish national small-sided competitive standards for ages U6 through U12. Standards vary by age and adjust player numbers, field, goal and ball dimensions, game duration and rules. Beginning at U9, build-out lines regulate goalkeeper restarts and offside calls; offside is not permitted before U9. Headers and goalkeeper punts and drop kicks are also prohibited.

“Peace-loving states” in Chapter III were intended as a membership criterion emphasizing the organization’s commitment to peace. Determining which states qualified would affect initial membership and admission procedures. Under the Dumbarton Oaks proposal, the Security Council would recommend admission and the General Assembly would decide, although further discussion was needed. Mexico and Venezuela emphasized permanent peace through international cooperation.

Chapter IV identified the principal organs while leaving room for subsidiary groups. The Economic and Social Council and Military Staff Committee were omitted to clarify responsibilities: the Security Council would handle peace and security, the General Assembly would foster conditions conducive to peace, and the International Court of Justice would address legal matters. The Economic and Social Council’s subordination to the Assembly could still be changed.

Chapter V addressed Assembly representation, including a Mexican proposal for three delegates per country and other support for unrestricted representation. Although critics questioned the Assembly’s limited powers, it could initiate discussion and make recommendations on international peace and security. Its role remained subordinate where the Security Council had primary responsibility, requiring a continuously available body for urgent action. The organization’s success would depend on broad international support; failure by the Assembly to address international-relations problems would leave the Security Council powerless.

SpaceX launched an uncrewed Dragon to the ISS from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, carrying about 6,400 pounds of supplies, mostly experiment gear and ice cream. The first stage lands upright for reuse. It is NASA's last brand-new Dragon; SpaceX will fly only flight-proven hardware, under a contract extended from 12 to 20 flights.

At Geneva talks due to begin February 23, Syria’s opposition seeks direct negotiations on political transition. High Negotiations Committee spokesman Salim al-Muslit said President Bashar al-Assad should have no role and called for discussing a transitional body with full powers under the 2012 Geneva communique.

A Northern California jury convicted Gonzalo Curiel of torturing, starving and beating two children whose bodies were found in a storage unit, as well as torturing their older sister. Tami Huntsman, the children’s relative and Curiel’s former girlfriend, pleaded guilty to two murder counts. Both were scheduled for sentencing; Curiel could not receive the death penalty.

The disclosure describes focused sterilization for in vivo analyte monitoring systems, including continuous glucose monitoring. Conventional two-piece systems package the sensor and sharp separately from electronic components because electron-beam radiation may damage electronics, while ethylene oxide sterilization may damage sensor chemistry. Such systems require separate packaging, sterilization, and final user assembly, increasing complexity and potential user error.

The disclosed one-piece architecture places a fully assembled sensor control device within a sensor applicator. A cap-mounted collimator defines a sterilization zone that receives the sensor and insertion sharp. Radiation is directed through this zone to sterilize those components while the collimator blocks radiation from reaching sensitive electronics. Embodiments also describe internal and external collimators, radiation shields for electronic processors, and seals that create a protected sterile region around the sensor and sharp.

Additional embodiments cover the sensor control device’s electronics housing, plug assembly, sensor, sharp, printed circuit board, battery, applicator, reader device, and wired or wireless data communications. The assembled applicator delivers the sensor beneath the skin, retracts the sharp, and retains the device with an adhesive patch. The one-piece design reduces parts, packaging, fabrication and assembly steps, and the stated risk of user error or contamination.

An email circulated Nov. 1, 2000, to multiple Enron recipients compiled several press clippings concerning Enron and energy, financial, and regulatory developments.

The Financial Times reported growing interest in weather-risk management as storms caused flooding and infrastructure disruptions in Britain. Weather derivatives were valued at $3 billion–$8 billion, mainly in the United States, while Europe was developing futures, hedge funds, insurance programs, and trading sites, including 17 sites Enron planned to launch. Barriers included imbalanced demand for warm-winter hedges, limited liquidity, costly weather data, and low corporate awareness. The emerging market was expected to have a primary market for tailored deals and a secondary wholesale market.

Ahead of a Houston arena referendum, supporters and opponents debated the proposed venue. Supporters cited downtown development and economic benefits; opponents argued that the deal improperly benefited team owner Les Alexander at taxpayers’ expense. The dispute remained contentious, and the email did not report the referendum result.

Azurix shareholder Thomas Turberg sued Azurix and Enron over Enron’s proposed $275 million financing of a $7-per-share take-private transaction, alleging that the price undervalued Azurix. The suit sought class-action status, an order stopping the transaction, and damages. Separately, Dow Jones reported that Enron’s financing arrangement would leave an Atlantic Water Trust holding 67 percent of Azurix, potentially allowing Enron to streamline the company before selling it as a whole. Azurix’s Wessex Water stake backed a £400 million credit facility, restricting a sale of that asset separately. Azurix had missed earnings expectations, accumulated $1.3 billion in long-term debt, and experienced the resignation of CFO Rebecca Mark; its shares had fallen more than 80 percent since its 1999 public offering. The article identified four large European water companies as possible buyers.

The Globe and Mail described C.I. Global Fund as a $3.2 billion, broadly diversified global equity fund whose 10-year annualized return was 17.7 percent, versus 13.7 percent for peer funds. Recent returns were nearly flat. Manager William Sterling was reducing U.S. and European exposure because of concerns about technology-stock volatility, rate increases, and corporate earnings. The portfolio included major technology holdings as well as Enron, which represented 1.6 percent.

A FERC committee recommended changes to California’s wholesale electricity market after an investigation into power prices that tripled during the summer. Generators welcomed the finding of no price collusion and recommendations allowing utilities to buy from multiple suppliers and use forward markets. Concerns remained over a $150-per-megawatt soft cap and possible refunds. Enron delayed plans for 300 megawatts of new California generation because of uncertainty but saw opportunities for its price-risk management business. Power companies expected continued debate and said additional capacity was still needed.

A train derailment near Transwestern’s New Mexico pipeline cut gas flows by about 250 million cubic feet, or 25 percent, with no reported injuries and no estimate for restoring full capacity. The outage redirected gas toward western markets and contributed to price changes. Nymex December natural-gas futures settled at $4.686 per million Btu, up 19.6 cents, while physical prices mostly rose; storage constraints, the outage, and winter forecasts shaped trading.

The patent application discloses metal-assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters based on benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine ligands and analogues, including cyclic Pt(II) and Pd(II) complexes represented by General Formulas I-XIII and octahedral Ir(III) complexes represented by General Formulas XIV-XVII. These emitters can exhibit both singlet and triplet excitons, potentially providing unity internal quantum efficiency and short lifetimes. Extending ligand conjugation can lower singlet energy with little or no change in triplet energy, creating a small singlet-triplet gap that enables thermally assisted delayed fluorescence while remaining triplets emit through phosphorescence.

The disclosure defines permitted ligand, linker, and substituent groups and describes OLEDs containing a substrate, anode, hole-transport layer, light-processing layer, electron-transport layer, and metal cathode. The compounds are proposed for full-color displays, lighting, photovoltaic devices, and luminescent displays.

Provided examples describe nitrogen-protected ligand formation in DMSO using copper iodide, picolinic acid, and a potassium phosphate reagent, followed by metalation in acetic acid using palladium acetate or a platinum salt and tetrabutylammonium bromide to produce complexes MC1-MC31. Figures include emission spectra for MC3, MC12, and MC27 and OLED performance data for Example 46. The invention was supported by Department of Energy award DE-EE0007090, with certain government rights retained. The application is a continuation of U.S. patent application No. 16/668,010 and claims priority to earlier patent and provisional applications.

On March 3, 2015, Tesla Motors’ Board amended its 2010 Equity Incentive Plan to prohibit transactions that reprice equity awards and adopted bylaws requiring a majority vote in uncontested director elections while retaining plurality voting in contested elections. Neither amendment required stockholder approval, and both were filed as exhibits to the Form 8-K.

Kitty Holland reported on a pregnant, suicidal girl detained under the Mental Health Act after her psychiatrist declined an abortion. A guardian ad litem secured a second assessment, which found no evidence of a mental health disorder, and the girl was released. The writer argues that unwanted pregnancy can worsen mental illness.

The author questions psychiatry’s definitions and evidentiary standards, distinguishing brain illness from mental illness. She recounts her grandmother being sectioned, forcibly subjected to ECT and medication trials that worsened her psychosis. Her own depression diagnosis was based on a DSM symptom count, yet the cause of depression remains untested and the chemical-imbalance theory is disputed. Citing Thomas Szasz, she notes that mental-disorder definitions have reflected cultural and political changes, including classifying homosexuality until 1980. She also notes that only about 40% of people taking SSRIs report improvement, complicating conclusions about efficacy and placebo effects. While acknowledging that psychiatric intervention can help some people, she argues that the field should face more rigorous testing and that little is understood about mental illness’s true nature.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that Andrew R. Jassy will become President and Chief Executive Officer on July 5, 2021, when he will also join the Board of Directors. Amazon approved a restricted stock unit award covering 61,000 common shares, to vest over ten years, and appropriate security arrangements. Jassy will also enter an indemnification agreement matching the form used by other directors. He joined Amazon in 1997 and has led Amazon Web Services as senior vice president from April 2006 to April 2016 and as CEO since April 2016.

Coupling a single optical-cavity mode to a magnetic system across a quantum critical point can amplify its optical response. For a transverse-field Ising model, direct coupling to the critical magnetization mode lowers the critical light–matter coupling required for a superradiant phase transition; at the quantum critical point, this coupling vanishes, allowing superradiance at arbitrarily weak cavity coupling. Large-spin analysis and DMRG calculations confirm the resulting phase diagram. Near the transition, quantum critical fluctuations enhance intrinsic quadrature squeezing and quantum Fisher information beyond the standard Dicke model, indicating stronger light–matter entanglement and improved metrological precision. Coupling to a noncritical mode instead makes superradiance compete with magnetism, producing a complex phase diagram and tricritical behavior near the quantum critical point. The suppression of the critical coupling is also supported by the ferromagnetic XY model. The framework may extend to driven-dissipative systems and could be tested using cavity-coupled magnetic materials such as CoNb₂O₆, LiHoF₄, and CrI₃.

This lecture (MIT 6.5630 F23, Lecture 9 Part 1) begins constructing SNARGs (Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments) from two ingredients: BARGs (batch arguments, presented in the prior class by Zhengzhong) and somewhere extractable hash functions, also called somewhere statistically binding (SSB) hashes.

**BARG.** Three PPT algorithms: Gen(λ, k, n) outputs a CRS (λ in unary, k and n in binary); Prover(CRS, x₁…x_k with witnesses) outputs a proof depending only polylogarithmically on k; Verifier(CRS, instances, proof) accepts or rejects. Completeness holds with probability 1 over CRS generation. For soundness, the professor distinguishes non-adaptive, adaptive, and semi-adaptive soundness: in the semi-adaptive case the cheating prover picks its instances adaptively after seeing the CRS but must commit beforehand to the index i at which it cheats, and may win only with negligible probability. Fully adaptive soundness is non-trivial because guessing i succeeds with probability 1/k, switching the CRS to hardwire i via the SSB hash may simply shift the cheating location, and language membership cannot be efficiently tested.

**SSB hash.** Algorithms Gen(λ, i, n) → (hash key, trapdoor), Eval(hk, x) → v, Open(hk, x, j) → opening ρ_j, Ver → accept/reject, Extract(trapdoor, v) → bit. Properties: completeness (honest openings verify; extraction returns the correct bit), index hiding (hash keys for different indices are indistinguishable), and somewhere statistical binding (even an all-powerful adversary given the hash key cannot produce two accepting openings, to 0 and to 1, at the bound index, except with negligible probability). Corollary: index hiding plus FSB at one location gives computational binding at all locations for PPT adversaries. Repeating the construction ℓ times yields a hash binding on ℓ locations, with remaining indices still hidden even if some trapdoors are revealed; the hash value grows with ℓ while the key can stay succinct when indices have succinct descriptions. BARGs for index languages let the verifier run in time depending on a succinct description of the instances rather than on k. BARGs need not themselves be somewhere-extractable: one can hash all witnesses with an SSB hash and BARG the upgraded language.

**SSB hash construction sketch.** A naive Merkle-style scheme based on homomorphic encryption (hash key = encryption of the index; openings resembling oblivious transfer) fails binding, since a malicious prover can supply garbage ciphertexts. The fix uses a chain of layer-specific key pairs: at each node, the homomorphic evaluation decrypts both children with sk_{j−1}, outputs the one selected by i_j, and re-encrypts under the next public key, so path ciphertexts are well-formed even if sibling ciphertexts are malformed; the verifier repeats the same computation. Only bounded-depth FHE is required; a single public key with circular security is an alternative.

**SNARG construction.** Gen outputs CRS = (SSB hash key binding on ℓ locations, BARG CRS with k = number of circuit gates). The prover computes all wires of the verification circuit, hashes them into v, and produces a BARG proof π over statements (hash key, v, j), one per gate, whose witness consists of openings of the two input wires and the output wire that verify and satisfy the gate. The verifier accepts iff the BARG accepts. The proof grows polylogarithmically in k, the hash value grows with ℓ (ideally ℓ = polylog k), and because the statements form an index language, verifier runtime does not grow with k. The security analysis is deferred to the next session.

Preparations for an inquiry are underway across several areas. Files will review Central Powers newspapers for economic and political policy, compile a “Who’s Who” for the Central Powers, Russia, Poland, the Balkans, and Scandinavia, and summarize outstanding treaty obligations. Briefs will describe grievances, demands, aspirations, organizations, and leaders of subject nationalities between the Baltic Sea and Persian Gulf. Materials on Poland and five urgent areas—Poland and the Baltic provinces, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, Asian Turkey, and Central Africa—will include historical sketches, authoritative indexed volumes, accounts of governmental participation and restrictions, and studies of government structures. A chart will compare fourteen plans for international organization, and another will chart important international events since 1870 by year and country. A collection on declarations, proposals, and practice concerning the creation of a new Poland is also being prepared. The Geography Division will supply maps and analyses covering relief, transportation, navigation, soils, climate, agriculture, mineral resources, labor, forests, and related economic and geographic features.

An ESPN MLB playoff roundup covers roster and managerial news, playoff predictions, and division-series previews. In the featured report, Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio injured his hamstring after crossing first base during a 9-3 NLDS win over the Cubs. Milwaukee scored a franchise-record six runs in the first inning, while Chourio contributed a leadoff double, a two-run single, and an RBI single before departing. The 21-year-old underwent an MRI, and manager Pat Murphy said his recovery timeline was unknown.

JM Smucker sued Trader Joe’s in the U.S. District Court for the Northern Ohio, alleging its frozen crustless peanut butter and jelly sandwiches copy Uncrustables’ trademarked design through similar crimped edges and packaging color. Smucker seeks disposal of Trader Joe’s sandwiches and marketing materials and payment of profits, citing consumer confusion.
