Uncrustables is described as a nearly $1 billion brand producing 1.5 billion sandwiches annually. Trader Joe’s did not comment.

The patent application discloses a Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) for enabling autonomous power-cartridge exchanges for unmanned aerial vehicles and other unmanned systems. The RPS includes a configurable landing zone, a Dynamic Terminal Landing System with visible or non-visible markers that generate scalable composite images for guided landing, modular power bays, a universal cartridge-swapping mechanism, a central processor, sensors, and wired or wireless communications. It can house cartridges containing batteries, fuel cells, fossil fuel, payloads, or other media in various sizes and configurations.

A UAV’s onboard Universal Integrated Swap System includes a Swap Cartridge Receptacle, a Universal Swap Cartridge Processor, cameras, transmitters, receivers, and identification markers. The processor communicates cartridge health, type, power, and payload data and can transmit telemetry and receive landing instructions.

During an exchange, a UAV requests permission to land and may be placed in a queue. The RPS guides it to the landing zone, secures it, establishes mechanical and electrical connections, locates its onboard swap system, removes depleted cartridges, and transfers them to modular power bays for storage or replenishment. A compatible energized cartridge is retrieved, elevated to the landing zone, and installed before the UAV undergoes safety and flight-readiness checks and departs. Environmental conditions, component status, power availability, and mission data are monitored and communicated by the central processor. The RPS may use internal or external power and can also support ground, underground, surface-water, underwater, and space vehicles.

Experiments show that electrical currents can generate orbital angular momentum currents through the bulk orbital Hall effect and interfacial orbital Rashba–Edelstein effect. Because conventional magnetization responds primarily to spin, orbital angular momentum must be converted into spin angular momentum, either within a ferromagnet or through an additional layer such as Pt or a 4f transition metal. Torque measurements are the most common probe, but other approaches include magnetoresistance, reciprocal orbital pumping and THz emission, direct imaging by magneto-optical or electron microscopy methods, and orbital Hanle magnetoresistance. These measurements reveal material-dependent torque efficiency, unusually long orbital transport lengths, and torque signs that can identify orbital contributions. CuOx has been identified as a strong orbital-angular-momentum source, while transition metals such as Nb, Ta, and Ru have been predicted to exhibit large orbital Hall effects. Orbical torque has also been observed in antiferromagnets, two-dimensional systems, perpendicular ferromagnets, and single layered compounds. In bilayer transition-metal dichalcogenides, the orbital Hall effect provides a more appropriate description of orbital transport than the valley Hall effect.

The orbital Hall effect is described theoretically as a universal phenomenon in conducting solids, arising from momentum-space orbital textures that can exist without spin-orbit coupling. Strong orbital–lattice coupling can generate large orbital Hall conductivities but is also expected to dissipate orbital angular momentum rapidly. Nevertheless, experiments report orbital relaxation lengths much longer than spin relaxation lengths, and calculations predict either long-range orbital torques or extremely short orbital diffusion lengths. Orbital relaxation therefore remains unresolved.

Potential orbital-torque applications include MRAM, oscillators, random-number generators, logic devices, THz emitters, and unconventional computing. Light metals such as Ti, V, and Cr could provide low-resistivity, integration-compatible alternatives to conventional spin-orbit-torque materials. However, MRAM deployment requires greater torque efficiency, compatibility with high-tunneling-magnetoresistance CoFeB/MgO systems, and smaller layer thicknesses. One orbital-torque device with a 100-nm perpendicular ferromagnetic dot reported a 50% reduction in switching power relative to a spin-orbit-torque Pt device.

The outlook is that improved understanding of orbital generation, long-distance and interfacial transport, orbital-to-spin conversion, and crystal- or interface-controlled orbital textures could enable efficient, robust, tunable orbitronic technologies using abundant materials and interactions with photons and phonons.

The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly saw noisy scenes and opposition walkouts over alleged attacks on Kashmiri students outside the state, particularly in Haryana. The government said an FIR was filed, one student suffered minor injuries, and three people were arrested. Opposition members demanded stronger action against perpetrators. The government also clarified that an all-party meeting on upcoming panchayat elections was a Cabinet decision whose outcome would return to the Cabinet. BJP members noted the deaths of three Army personnel in an avalanche in Gurez and praised the rescue of a civilian despite adverse weather. Question-hour proceedings were otherwise largely peaceful, aside from a BJP walkout over an unsatisfactory answer concerning farmers.

Ryan Dempster, now a Cubs special assistant, said seeing Kyle Hendricks succeed brought personal pride because the Cubs acquired Hendricks in the 2012 trade that sent Dempster to Texas. Hendricks, then a Class A pitcher, later won an ERA title, beat Clayton Kershaw in an NLCS clincher and started the Cubs’ World Series Game 7 victory before starting Game 1 of the playoffs against Washington. Dempster rejected a trade to Atlanta for Randall Delgado before accepting the Rangers deal for Hendricks and Christian Villanueva, calling the sequence serendipitous.
Habeas corpus application denied; all listed judges concurred.

MIT OCW guest lecture by Jason Ku, president of the MIT origami club OrigaMIT and a mechanical engineering PhD student whose research involves folding at micro and nano scales. He discusses the artistic perspective on origami design, focusing on representational origami (creating forms that represent real-world subjects, as distinct from patterning, tessellation, polyhedra, and abstract art) and on the tree method of design. He draws an analogy between origami and music, noting that composers and performers are usually the same person in origami, and notes that both fields involve substantial mathematics alongside artistic complexity.

Ku begins with Akira Yoshizawa (1911–2005), widely regarded as the father of modern origami, who created many new models and pioneered wet-folding, which weakens paper with water so it can be shaped and dried. He contrasts the traditional style, characterized by straight, precise creases, flat folds, and clean polygons, exemplified by Hideo Komatsu's work on 22.5-degree grids and box pleating (multiples of 45 degrees), with a non-traditional style built on extensive shaping and curved folds, exemplified by David Brill, Michael LaFosse (a paper maker, former chef, and marine biologist), and Eric Joisel (a former clay sculptor known for textured models, expressive masks, and human figures, who argued that a piece reproducible exactly is not really art). He notes that models are folded largely by hand using wet-folding, clips, and braces; that color is sometimes added; and cites Robert Lang's broad definition of origami as any work whose primary structure is defined by folding, mentioning multi-sheet work by Joseph Wu.

Ku then surveys designers working at the extreme of complexity: Robert Lang, a pioneer of algorithmic origami who codified tree theory, wrote the TreeMaker program, and left a NASA laser physics position for full-time origami work, known for complex insect models, the "Bug Wars" competition, modular origami, tessellations, and a Klein bottle; Brian Chan, an MIT alumnus (PhD 2009) known for complex folding, a one-piece color-change rose, anime figures such as "Rozen Maiden" and "Neko Bus," a kraken-and-ship model, and the MIT seal; and Satoshi Kamiya, regarded as the foremost pioneer of super-complex origami, whose work features exact creases and texturing and whose widely cited most complex single work, taking a year to fold, contains thousands of scales from one uncut square. Ku also recommends Lang's *Origami Design Secrets* and the documentary *Between the Folds*.

Turning to design method, he reviews tree theory: drawing a subject as a one-dimensional stick figure, matching it to a base with appropriately sized and connected flaps, then shaping the model. He explains uniaxial bases (Erik Demaine's definitions), in which flaps lie along or straddle a single line and hinge perpendicular to it, so the projection yields the stick figure; flaps correspond to quarter-octagon regions of paper, and circle/river packings map uniquely to trees while trees admit multiple packings. He leads the class through practice matching trees and space allocations to one another, and explains that a line separated from the model provides thickness (e.g., a butterfly wing), while pleating shrinks usable paper. Using his own dragon model, he shows how hinge-crease analysis, extra flaps, and texture cover the gaps between legs and create toes, noting the square sheet was roughly a meter across.

Finally, Ku demonstrates TreeMaker with a crab: drawing a tree of legs, body segment, claws, and eyes, specifying relative edge lengths, packing circles, scaling to remove crossings, and building a crease pattern. He describes active paths, under-constrained nodes, failed mountain-valley assignments, and options such as symmetry constraints, perturbation, and triangulation, then shows a separately designed non-uniaxial crab with 22.5-degree folds, underbelly texture, and a folded proof of concept. He closes by inviting questions via the OrigaMIT website and Sunday workshops, and shows letters made from a single model with a 3-by-4 grid of flippable color-change squares.

An Enron news digest dated Nov. 19, 2001 covered the company’s financial crisis, proposed acquisition, asset sales, and wider financial-market developments.

- Falling share prices threatened companies that issued zero-coupon convertible bonds. Investors could return the bonds after as little as one year if stocks failed to rise enough for conversion, exposing companies to roughly $65 billion in repayments over three years. Potential consequences included refinancing costs, reduced earnings, and shareholder dilution. Calpine, Solectron, and Enron were among issuers facing significant exposure. Tax advantages continued to attract issuers despite the risks.

- A Wall Street Journal commentary said Enron had produced enduring innovations in energy-market deregulation, customized power contracts, internal market pricing, network flexibility, risk controls, and corporate culture. It argued that Enron’s collapse resulted more from partners’ concerns about financing its trading activity and the erosion of shareholder equity than from trading losses. The proposed sale to Dynegy risked losing Enron’s research capacity and innovative culture.

- Investors awaited Enron’s delayed third-quarter filing, which could disclose additional debts and cost-cutting measures connected with Dynegy’s proposed purchase. Enron had reduced reported net income by $586 million over four years, while an SEC investigation and credit downgrades threatened the merger and raised concern about Enron’s liquidity and viability.

- The Dynegy transaction faced complex regulatory review. The companies estimated six to nine months, while experts said approval could take as long as two years. FERC had to assess market power in energy trading, and the companies also needed approval from the Justice Department or Federal Trade Commission and relevant states. Enron’s trading partners reduced exposure and prepared contingency plans because a failed deal could create broader energy-market and derivatives risk.

- Enron was seeking to sell noncore assets. WestLB was among several bidders for Britain’s Wessex Water, although any sale would face regulatory scrutiny. In India, BSES planned to complete due diligence on the $2.9 billion Dabhol power project by January 2002, while Dabhol Power Co. waited for a Bombay High Court ruling before deciding whether to terminate its contract with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board.

- In a Wall Street Journal stock-picking survey, J.P. Morgan’s recommended portfolio fell 8.6%, the smallest quarterly decline among 15 firms and better than the S&P 500’s 14.7% loss. Goldman Sachs fell 23.2% and Credit Suisse First Boston 30.1%. Edward Jones had the strongest five-year result, gaining 85%.

- Corporate bond issuance was projected to exceed $600 billion in 2001, but most proceeds were being used to refinance short-term commercial paper rather than fund new investment. About $135 billion in investment-grade bonds had been sold since Sept. 11. Enron drew $3.3 billion from its emergency credit line and sought another $1 billion loan to repay commercial-paper investors. Treasury yields rose sharply as investors anticipated economic recovery and fewer Federal Reserve rate cuts.

- The Pilgrim Russia Fund gained 53% during 2001 while the S&P 500 fell nearly 14%, although weak financial institutions, contract enforcement, corporate governance, reporting standards, and dependence on oil and gas created risks. Janus Capital reduced several technology holdings and its Enron position while increasing investments in Microsoft, Berkshire Hathaway, and Philip Morris.

- A commentary on Indian power-sector reform argued that separating generation, transmission, and distribution had not resolved high distribution losses, payment defaults, or governments’ reluctance to set cost-covering tariffs. It maintained that institutional restructuring could not substitute for stronger governance and enforcement.

American Christian Beasley, 32, escaped from Bali’s overcrowded Kerobokan prison by sawing through a ceiling and jumping over a 6-meter wall, according to officials. Fellow American inmate Paul Anthony Hoffam was captured attempting to flee. Authorities were investigating possible guard involvement amid severe staffing shortages.

A hockey player reflected on scoring an overtime goal to help his team tie the Stanley Cup Finals series against New Jersey. He credited teammates’ effort and Jiggy’s leadership after the team had played poorly in the first two games. The goal came after a shot by Ozolinsh was saved, with the player collecting the rebound and scoring. He also discussed being unexpectedly traded from Chicago to Anaheim before the playoffs, expressing surprise and gratitude for the opportunity. He praised his teammates’ complementary skills, his coach’s belief in him, and his family’s support. Looking ahead, he said New Jersey was a strong defensive team, but his team’s overtime success and confidence gave them a good chance to win if the game reached a tie late.

The coach said his players have been emotionally attached and frustrated by disappointing results, but praised their ability to refocus, follow the game plan, and keep competing. He emphasized emotional control, particularly for a net-driving player, while noting the bench’s support helps players reset quickly.

The coach praised Crosby’s performance and said playoff media responsibilities are shared among players rather than centered solely on Crosby and Dan Bylsma. He described every game as unique and said the next matchup may produce different looks.

Despite being outshot and outchanced over two games, the coach said his team has struggled against the opponent’s superior net-front presence, crease scrambles, loose-puck battles, and timely “dirty” goals. Every line must improve its work around the net, protect its goaltender, generate second chances, and maintain pressure. A player added speed and scoring chances but remained out of the lineup to help manage minutes in back-to-back games. The coach’s central message was to avoid distraction, keep working, and return home more determined to break through.

HHH defended excluding women from the Greatest Royal Rumble, citing cultural differences and expressing hope that women will compete in Saudi Arabia within the next few years. He described WWE’s Abu Dhabi women’s match as a cultural shift and emphasized WWE’s role in supporting that change.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture and Compute Capability 8.0 to accelerate HPC, AI, and data-analytics workloads. Its SXM4 board includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory organized into five active stacks of eight dies, delivering 1,555 GB/s—more than 1.7 times Tesla V100 bandwidth. HBM2’s on-package placement saves power and area compared with GDDR5/6 designs. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2 and L1 caches, and register files.

A100 has a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7 times larger than V100’s. Its two-partition, shared cache provides 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth and supports cache-coherent GPU-wide access. L2 residency controls let applications prioritize persistent data, while Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM read/write bandwidth by up to four times, L2 read bandwidth by up to four times, and effective L2 capacity by up to two times.

A100 has 108 streaming multiprocessors versus V100’s 80 and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting peak mixed-precision performance 16 times that of standard FP32 FMA operations. Its Tensor Cores share data across all 32 threads in a warp, support up to four times larger matrix dimensions per instruction, issue eight times fewer instructions, and perform 2.9 times fewer register-file accesses than V100. A new asynchronous copy instruction transfers data directly from global memory to shared memory, bypassing L1 and the register file, while asynchronous barriers improve synchronization. Maximum shared-memory allocation per SM rises to 164 KB from 96 KB.

CUDA 11 supports the new Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, L2 residency controls, and CUDA Graphs. Task graphs reduce repeated CPU launch overhead and let A100 optimize complex execution dependencies. CUDA also adds an asynchronous global-to-shared copy API, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, and Cooperative Groups support for pipelined copies and hardware-accelerated reductions.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances for concurrent workloads. Each instance receives dedicated compute resources and isolated paths through the crossbar, L2 cache, memory controllers, and DRAM, providing predictable performance, quality of service, and fault isolation without changing the CUDA programming model. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances, which support Volta-style MPS and independent context switching. MIG migration can move compatible virtual GPUs between instances or physical GPUs to consolidate workloads and permit maintenance without terminating jobs.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s of total GPU bandwidth, twice V100’s total, with peer-memory access, error detection, packet replay, and requester-side synchronization. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 at 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and SR-IOV virtualization. Enhanced fault attribution, isolation, and containment help prevent failures in one process, VM, or GPU from affecting others.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, five NVDEC units versus one in V100, and global-memory atomics with 11-fold higher FP16 and 2.7-fold higher FP32 throughput than V100. A100 has no display connectors, RT Cores, or NVENC encoder.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional bandwidth and up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system. It supports eight ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters at 200 Gb/s and can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators through MIG. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, GPU-accelerated frameworks, and NGC containers, models, Helm charts, and SDKs for deployment on large Slurm or Kubernetes clusters.

The appendix explains that neural-network pruning removes low-value nodes or connections to reduce computation, memory traffic, energy use, and model size. Fine-grained sparsity irregularly removes individual weights, while coarse-grained sparsity removes whole subnetworks. A100 supports 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, which preserves balanced workloads and, according to NVIDIA’s evaluations, produces virtually no loss in accuracy across tested neural networks.

WHO reported 503,484 suspected cases and 1,975 deaths from Yemen’s waterborne disease outbreak since late April, with an estimated 5,000 people affected daily. Infrastructure collapse, deteriorating sanitation and limited clean water have made it the world’s largest outbreak. Hospitals, medicines and water are insufficient, and some health workers are unpaid. Over 15 million lack basic healthcare; Tedros urged warring parties to seek peace.

Tooth-whitening products include over-the-counter gels, strips and toothpaste, dentist-provided home trays, and in-office treatments. The FDA treats them as cosmetics and does not require premarket approval, though it has found no currently marketed ingredients unsafe. The ADA Seal indicates that an independent panel reviewed a product for safety and effectiveness; many non-sealed products may still work as directed. Whitening commonly causes temporary sensitivity, and leaking products can inflame gums.

Dentist-made trays cost about $400, require one to two hours of daily use for up to four weeks, and better contain and distribute the gel. In-office bleaching costs more than $1,000 but can lighten teeth dramatically in one or two hours using higher concentrations of hydrogen peroxide. Insurance rarely covers it, although procedures increased 29 percent in 2015.

Dentists recommend checking for cavities and other oral problems before whitening. Surface stains from coffee, tea, wine, spices and tobacco may respond to brushing, flossing and professional cleaning. Aging, enamel cracks and thinning can cause deeper stains that bleach can lighten by two to seven shades. Trauma, tetracycline and excessive fluoride can cause permanent discoloration requiring crowns or veneers. All bleaching results are temporary and require touch-ups. The ADA says there is no evidence that charcoal, baking soda or lemon juice effectively whiten teeth.

In an April 26, 1879 proclamation, President Rutherford B. Hayes warned persons preparing to settle Indian Territory west of Arkansas without authorization that they would be removed under U.S. law. He invoked possible military assistance to protect Indian nations and tribes and enforce laws governing residence and trade in the territory. Secretary of State William M. Evarts attested the proclamation.

The Second Circuit affirmed the United States’ dismissal from the case and held that Red Star could not limit its liability for damages from the 1974 grounding of the oil-laden Barge New London and resulting Hudson River oil spill. The tug Ocean Prince struck a charted rock near Bear Mountain Bridge while pushing the barge at night during icy conditions.

Red Star failed to designate a captain or inform its pilots of their assignments. Reimer lacked Hudson River experience, while Kiernan’s experience and willingness to assist could not excuse Red Star’s failure to provide a qualified master and crew. The court rejected the district court’s reliance on customary industry practices, holding that conformity to custom does not establish due care. Red Star’s management knew the seasonal ice and navigation-aid conditions but failed to take adequate precautions, making the casualty a result of negligence and unseaworthiness within Red Star’s privity and knowledge.

The district court also erroneously found that the failure to post a lookout did not contribute to the collision. A competent lookout could have sighted Con Hook Light and enabled the vessel to establish a danger bearing, and Red Star’s failure to maintain a lookout violated both maritime practice and statutory requirements.

Under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, Red Star’s combined failures to designate command, disclose Reimer’s inexperience, and require a lookout amounted to intentional omissions and reckless disregard of foreseeable consequences. The court therefore found willful misconduct within Red Star’s privity and knowledge, defeating the Act’s $100-per-gross-ton cleanup-cost limitation. It vacated the limitation orders, directed judgment for Pittston and the United States on their damages, affirmed the remaining rulings, and remanded for further proceedings.

A Dec. 13, 2000 email titled “Enron Mentions” circulated Reuters and Dow Jones reports. Colombia postponed the privatization of the 1,636-megawatt state power generator ISAGEN, valued at about $450 million, to June 30, 2001, citing legal issues, possible repricing and paperwork. Enron had previously been named as a leading potential bidder. Repeated delays had resulted from grid sabotage, labor litigation and an injunction, which Colombia’s Council of State later overturned, and antitrust objections raised by Empresas Públicas de Medellín.

Dow Jones market commentary reported that investment banks were holding liquidity at historically high levels amid credit concerns. Congressional gridlock could delay parts of President-elect Bush’s agenda, although rebel Democrats might help pass tax cuts. A provider-lawsuit ruling was considered a minor victory for HMOs, with varying effects on major insurers. March S&P futures fell as technology and semiconductor earnings warnings weakened market fundamentals, while Toronto’s TSE 300 traded near significant support.

Company news included downgrades for Applied Materials and Alza, a possible Celestica purchase of a NEC unit, a modest chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut, earnings concerns at Charles Schwab, bids for Vlasic Foods, and a raised SonicWall revenue forecast. Linux-related stocks rallied following IBM’s planned $1 billion Linux investment, while bond issuance declined 25% and Veritas remained pressured by weakness in Sun Microsystems’ server business. Enron chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said categorically that he would remain with Enron and would not join a Bush administration.

AMD provides the publication without warranties, disclaims product liabilities, reserves the right to change specifications or discontinue products without notice, grants no intellectual-property licenses, and prohibits uses involving surgical implants, life support, or other high-risk applications.

The FDA indicated it would approve Epidiolex, a pharmaceutical-grade, THC-free CBD oral medicine from GW Pharmaceuticals, for seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes in patients aged 2 and older. Studies found substantial evidence of effectiveness, with acceptable risks, though how CBD works remains unclear. The carefully tested product differs from unregulated CBD products marketed for unproven uses. Both syndromes are rare, severe forms of epilepsy that can cause prolonged seizures, brain damage, cognitive impairment, injury, or death. Parents and physicians described significant improvements in some children, while broader uses for conditions such as autism, anxiety, and inflammatory or autoimmune disorders remain under investigation.

The Single/Double set offense uses double-baseline and down screens to create shots for an outstanding shooter. Its initial attack goes through the middle, challenges both sides of the defense, and gives the shooter options to move in either direction off screens. O3 and O4 set a double screen while O5 sets a single screen for O2; O3 moves opposite O2. When defenders switch, the screeners can create post mismatches or isolate the shooter against a slower defender.

Precise execution and coordination are essential. Against defenders who chase under the double screen, the shooter curls for a shot or layup. If the defense cheats over, the shooter can fade to the baseline or back-cut. When defenders switch, the offense can post up the baseline screener or clear the screeners to isolate the shooter one-on-one. If a defender shows and recovers, the screener can slip to the basket or lob a pass. If the on-ball defender overplays the passing lane, the ballhandler can drive or drop-pass to an open teammate. The second shooter uses the opposite screen when O2 takes the first option.

Double screens also create opportunities for the screeners. The topside screener can set a down screen for the baseline screener, who may pop out, roll, or slip to the basket. Conversely, the baseline screener can set a back screen for the topside screener, producing a roll, lob, or over-the-top pass.

Down screens have similar reads and counters. Shooters curl against chase-out defenders, curl to the basket against late chasers, fade when defenders cheat over, and back-cut against early cheats. Against switches, the receiver can pop out while the screener seals and rolls, or the offense can isolate a post mismatch or wing one-on-one. When the screener’s defender shows, the screener can immediately slip to the basket.

If the defense focuses on shooters, O1 can feed O4 or O5 in the post. Players should be proficient at strong posting and basic post moves. The offense also creates an offensive-rebounding advantage by maintaining inside positions and two weak-side rebounders. Effective rebounding requires anticipation, hustle, determination, and boxing out under the assumption that every shot will miss.

The offense can operate from any alignment suited to the personnel, with the shooter repositioned to prevent defenders from anticipating the action. If the initial screens do not produce a shot, the offense continues through motion, side-screen action, or drive-and-kick. Motion includes pass-and-screen-away, reversals, crossing, and repeated down-screen actions. Side screens are particularly useful late in the shot clock, while drive-and-kick begins with a dribble handoff, penetration, and kick-out passes that can continue from player to player.

Successful implementation requires players to understand down screens, double screens, posting, screening, and breaking screens as one coordinated unit through timing and nonverbal communication. Teaching is recommended through a whole-part-whole method, combination drills, scrimmages, and individual work on assigned fundamentals. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads and counters, observe in-game adjustments, vary alignments and entries, attack weaker defenders, and use side screens as the game or shot clock winds down. Defending the offense also requires understanding its reads, counters, and techniques.

Google’s Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL appear similar in marketing but differ significantly in physical design and build quality. The HTC-made Pixel 2 has large bezels, squared and chamfered edges, louder, tinnier speakers, and a less premium feel. The LG-made Pixel 2 XL features curved glass, rounded corners, better-rounded speakers, and superior construction. Although their specifications are largely identical except for the display, Google’s promotional material obscures these physical differences.

The author contrasts the inconsistent pair with the first Pixels, whose unified design established Google’s hardware identity, and describes the Pixel 2 as a confusing “Pixel 1.5” while considering the XL closer to Google’s intended design. The Pixelbook also conflicts with the new Pixels’ design language. Overall, the phones are judged acceptable individually, but their manufacturer-specific differences represent a step backward for Google’s “Made by Google” vision, though the newly hired HTC engineers may improve future models.

Payton Leutner, 12, survived 19 stab wounds following a birthday sleepover near Milwaukee. Her friends, Morgan Guyser and Anissa Weier, were initially missing but were later found and questioned by police; a five-inch knife was found in one girl’s bag. Investigators discovered a goodbye note on Anissa’s phone, while Payton’s father and surgeon described her injuries, including a wound near her heart that missed an artery. The girls said they had planned the attack for months, inspired by the “Slender Man” creepypasta and a belief that killing someone would prove the character existed and make them proxies. Payton initially could not speak and communicated in writing.

Ion traps support long-coherence, high-fidelity qubits, but entangling gates based on ion vibrations are relatively slow, while the ions’ charge-to-mass ratio also complicates ion transport in QCCD chips. Although Rydberg-dipole entanglement shortens gate times to 700 ns, free electrons offer potentially faster responses because of their much lower mass. Electron-based quantum computing remains immature, particularly regarding spin manipulation, collective-state control, cooling, scalability, and integration with other quantum technologies.

The paper proposes a planar, two-frequency Paul trap designed to simultaneously confine laser-cooled Ca⁺ ions and electrons detached from them. The intended proof-of-concept system contains one Ca²⁺ ion and one trapped electron. Calculations indicate three electronic-state regimes: bound atomic states below the ionisation threshold, transitional Rydberg-like states affected by the trap, and trap-bound motional states above the ionisation threshold. The energy spectrum changes gradually from hydrogen-like spacing to a harmonic-oscillator ladder, with intermediate regions containing closely spaced, potentially tunable transitions. These states are to be prepared through photoionisation, selective excitation, control transitions, and stimulated recombination.

Optical coupling could use electromagnetically induced transparency to detect control transitions, while a magnetic field could separate electron spin states and provide distinguishable optical transitions for quantum-information encoding. Proposed extensions include shared-electron ion-entanglement states and radio-frequency-to-optical conversion. The trap is sized to allow sympathetic cooling of Ca²⁺ by other laser-cooled ions, although this produces narrow electron-state gaps, restricts ion-trapping strength, and may produce suboptimal ion separations. A ring-electrode design is presented to provide symmetric confinement around 1 mm from the electrodes while avoiding static fields that would destabilise oppositely charged particles.

Unverified reports may affect Spanish stocks: OHL proposed a €0.349 interim dividend; Gas Natural abandoned an Italian LNG project; Minor bid about €6 per share for 26.3% of NH Hotel; Acciona declared a €3 dividend; Dogi proposed a name change; and Parques Reunidos’ H1 loss narrowed to €58.6 million.

The disclosure describes ultrasonic fingerprint sensor systems for authentication in electronic devices, particularly sensors positioned beneath flexible, curved, or bezel-less OLED displays. An ultrasonic transmitter sends waves through a platen or display, and reflected waves from fingerprint ridges and valleys are detected, converted into electrical signals, and processed into fingerprint images.

Disclosed embodiments include a display, an underlying ultrasonic sensor system, and layers positioned in the acoustic path. These layers may include a non-porous light-blocking layer, a grounded conductive electrical shielding layer, a mechanical stress isolation layer, and a reworkable adhesive layer. The layers can be discrete or combined into a multifunctional film. The light-blocking layer reduces visible-light penetration, the shielding layer limits electromagnetic interference and aids heat dissipation, the stress-isolation layer reduces display distortion, and the adhesive permits sensor separation, replacement, or refurbishment. Suitable materials include plastic, pressure-sensitive adhesive, epoxy-based adhesive, PET, PEN, polyimide, and thermoplastic ink.

The sensor may use a sensor substrate containing pixel circuits, a piezoelectric transceiver layer, electrode and passivation layers, and an FPC. Separate piezoelectric transmitter and receiver layers or one layer serving both functions may be used. Piezoelectric materials include PVDF, PVDF-TrFE, PZT, and AlN, with example operating frequencies of about 1–100 MHz. Flexible substrates, high- and low-acoustic-impedance layers, foam backers, stiffeners, air cavities, housings, edge seals, focusing layers, and acoustic matching layers are also described.

Manufacturing methods bond the sensor and selected functional layers to the display. Implementations address obstacles posed by porous display backers, air gaps, and thick shielding layers by using substantially non-porous light-blocking layers, thin conductive shielding, and transparent filling materials. The disclosed advantages include increased active display area, bezel-free designs, flexible sensor placement, reduced interference between electrical and acoustic systems, improved acoustic reflections, and continuous authentication across a display area.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Time Warner from buy to hold, citing strong one-year performance, digital expansion and more than 20 consecutive quarterly earnings surprises, balanced against declining advertising spending and currency headwinds. The company suspended its share repurchase program after AT&T agreed to acquire it for $85.4 billion.

Other analysts issued mixed ratings: FBR reaffirmed buy, Wedbush raised its target to $107.50 with an outperform rating, while Drexel Hamilton and Albert Fried retained hold ratings and MKM Partners downgraded the stock to neutral with a $107.50 target. Analysts collectively rated the stock Hold with a $97.87 target.

Time Warner reported quarterly EPS of $1.25 and revenue of $7.90 billion, beating consensus estimates. Revenue rose 11.5% year over year. The company declared a $0.4025 quarterly dividend, and several institutional investors increased their stakes.

Time Warner operates through Turner, Home Box Office and Warner Bros., spanning television, streaming, film, home video and videogame production and distribution.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that on April 30, 2018, the Superior Court of California for Santa Clara County preliminarily approved a settlement in In re Apple Inc. E-Book Derivative Litigation. The court approved the settlement notice and scheduled a July 20, 2018 hearing to consider the settlement’s fairness, attorneys’ fees and expenses, and service awards. AMP coordinates and schedules workloads to provide predictable performance, reducing first-response latency for LLMs and preventing game-engine stuttering.

Blackwell adds hardware H.264 and HEVC support for 4:2:2 chroma sampling, balancing file size and bandwidth against color accuracy. Its ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds 4:2:2 encoding and an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. The sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed and supports 4:2:2. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, while DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps through UHBR 20. Blackwell’s Max-Q design uses advanced clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, frequency switching up to 1,000 times faster than earlier architectures, and sleep entry up to 10 times faster than Ada. An SLM inference example reports power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can produce three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using a model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM. Enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine. New transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing use self-attention and twice as many parameters, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ray-traced image quality.

Blackwell also supports neural shaders through Microsoft’s Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Potential applications include neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Materials approximate complex multilayer optics, while a demonstration reduced texture memory from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Neural Radiance Cache infers indirect lighting after one ray bounce and trains on live game data. RTX Skin introduces ray-traced subsurface scattering in games, and Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model to infer realistic faces from rasterized geometry and pose data. The passage presents neural shading as a future direction for real-time rendering.

The GPU family includes the flagship GB202, with 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, used by the RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and a 256-bit interface, powering the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and a 192-bit interface, used by the RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that the specifications are believed accurate as of publication, reserves the right to change them, and disclaims warranties and liability for specified uses.

The President reported to Congress that the Cuban war had harmed U.S. trade, investment, commerce, and citizens while straining the nation’s neutrality policy. Spain’s reconcentration policy had devastated rural Cuba, driven more than 300,000 people into garrison towns, and caused starvation and mortality exceeding 50 percent among the reconcentrated population by March 1897.

American relief efforts delivered nearly $200,000 in money and supplies, while Spain revoked reconcentration orders, appropriated $600,000 for relief, and authorized public works. Diplomatic efforts—including mediation, offers of reform, and an armistice proposal—had not ended the fighting. Spain proposed that Cuba’s insular parliament prepare the peace terms and indicated it would suspend hostilities if the insurgents requested it.

The President rejected immediate U.S. recognition of Cuban belligerency or independence as premature and potentially counterproductive. Nevertheless, he argued that neutral intervention was justified by the war’s humanitarian toll, the danger to American lives and property, serious losses to U.S. commerce, and threats to national peace. He also cited the destruction of the USS Maine in Havana harbor, which an American naval inquiry concluded resulted from an external explosion.

The President asked Congress to authorize U.S. military and naval action to secure a final end to hostilities, establish a stable Cuban government, and protect American and Cuban citizens. He also urged continued food distribution and additional public funding for relief. At the end of the message, he reported receiving notice that Spain’s Queen Regent had directed a suspension of hostilities, though its duration and terms were not yet known.

Shalah Dawn Nelson pleaded guilty to animal cruelty for tying an elastic hair band around a neighbour’s dog’s testicles in December 2016. The dog required surgery. Two Criminal Code charges were stayed. Nelson was fined $1,000, ordered to pay $850 restitution, and placed on 12-month probation with no contact with the dog’s owner.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2 MSPS data-acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. Conversion data can use straight-binary or two’s-complement formatting, with LSB size determined by the selected input range. A free-running differential or single-ended sampling clock is required; stopping it invalidates the output data, data clock, and frame clock. SMPL_SYNC synchronizes channel sequencing and frame-clock alignment across multiple ADS9803 devices.

The device includes a precision, low-drift internal reference, with a recommended 10 µF ceramic bypass capacitor at REFIO. An external reference can be used by disabling the internal reference through the SPI or SDI/EXTREF pin.

The source-synchronous interface supports two- or four-lane SDR or DDR operation. The 20-bit result is transmitted MSB first in a 24-bit packet, with the final six bits zeroed. Data-clock frequency depends on sampling frequency, data rate, and lane count. Optional data randomizer XORs conversion data with the result LSB or an appended PRBS bit. Simple averaging halves the output data rate, while moving averaging does not. Fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns can replace channel data for interface debugging.

Reset and power-down functions initialize registers to default values and require subsequent initialization register writes. The 16-bit configuration registers are organized into three banks with 8-bit addresses. SPI register reads and writes, including daisy-chained configurations for multiple devices, are described in detail.

Speed-boost mode converts only a selected channel-pair at up to 8 MSPS. For ATE applications, the ADS9803 can measure PMU signals directly or through a multiplexer, with low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes and specified settling performance. Layout guidance emphasizes separate supply decoupling, short ground and reference connections, and isolation of analog and reference paths from digital noise.

An Investing.com analysis argues that recent market moves are abnormal: gold rallied strongly Friday and the dollar fell, yet silver, mining stocks, and platinum barely rose. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF failed to meaningfully rally and closed below its April closing high for a third consecutive session, which the author views as bearish and as an early sign of a larger decline. YouTube reportedly plans to launch a music service called Remix in March next year, with Warner Music Group’s support and talks involving Sony, Universal, Merlin, and artists.

A small study comparing 12 boys aged about 10, 12 untrained male university students, and 13 male endurance athletes found that during high-intensity stationary cycling, the boys’ muscles fatigued at a rate similar to elite athletes and recovered faster. Their blood also cleared lactic acid faster. Researchers said children’s less-developed anaerobic systems may limit lactate production, while their aerobic fitness is relatively strong; this does not mean they are as fit overall as endurance athletes. The findings could help guide youth training toward skills, strength, and sprint ability. The study also found that muscle-level aerobic fitness declined significantly as children moved into adulthood, prompting further research into whether this is related to age-related disease risk. Limited access to elite athletes and ethical constraints involving children restricted the sample size.

Bleacher Report listed Braves legend Chipper Jones as the “wildest” candidate for Atlanta’s open manager position, calling the idea “very wishful thinking.” The eight-time All-Star, who spent all 19 seasons with Atlanta, managed one side of the 2025 Futures Game.

The study developed an NLP-based system to identify goals-of-care (GOC) discussions documented in EHR notes for seriously ill patients. GOC discussions are guideline-recommended and linked to improved outcomes, but they are often infrequent, delayed, and inconsistently recorded outside dedicated Advance Care Planning (ACP) notes.

The researchers collected 776 inpatient notes—400 ACP and 376 general notes—from patients with advanced serious illness across five University of Pennsylvania hospitals. Annotators labeled 30,533 utterances, with specialist adjudication of disagreements. GOC content was rare in general notes, producing a 155:1 imbalance between negative and positive examples. Five base classifiers—regular expressions, logistic regression, BERT, BioClinicalBERT, and RoBERTa—were evaluated alone and in ensembles using average, weighted-average, and decision-tree aggregation. Active learning iteratively selected uncertain examples for annotation and was compared with passive training and training on all examples.

The best active-learning weighted-average ensemble achieved F1 scores of 0.557 for utterance classification and 0.629 for note classification. It identified 13 of 18 GOC-positive test notes (72%) and incorrectly flagged 13 of 158 negative notes. Active learning improved precision and required annotation of only 3,200 additional general-note utterances, 30% of the unlabeled pool, while generally matching or outperforming models trained on all examples.

Performance remained moderate because the classifiers analyzed individual utterances without surrounding context. The fixed unlabeled pool also limited exploration because it contained only 51 positive examples. Prior studies were difficult to compare because datasets and GOC definitions vary. The authors concluded that the classifier could support clinical review and that combining keyword retrieval with confidence-ranked results could provide a nearly exhaustive search for GOC discussions.

Daniel Ricciardo said Red Bull’s straight-line deficit at the Japanese Grand Prix was not solely engine-related and linked it to the car’s high downforce. Jenny Han, author of the young-adult books behind “To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before” and “The Summer I Turned Pretty,” achieved success after working as an Olive Garden server, nanny, and school librarian. Her 2014 teen trilogy became a Netflix film series acquired in 2018 and led to a spinoff. Han now has millions of international followers and says authors must learn to sell themselves and their books.

The lecture develops perturbative matching, running, and power corrections in heavy-quark effective theory (HQET).

- The one-loop heavy-quark wave-function renormalization constant \(Z_h\) is calculated in dimensional regularization with the \(\overline{\mathrm{MS}}\) scheme and Feynman gauge. A parameter method is used to evaluate an integral containing both linear and quadratic propagator denominators, after which the ultraviolet divergence is removed by a counterterm. Calculations in \(\overline{\mathrm{MS}}\) and on-shell renormalization should yield the same matching.

- Heavy-to-light currents require renormalization of both quark fields and the local operator. Combining the one-loop vertex and wave-function graphs produces a nonzero ultraviolet divergence and anomalous dimension. Unlike the corresponding conserved QCD current, the HQET current has renormalization-group evolution below the heavy-quark mass because heavy-mass logarithms have become ultraviolet divergences. The anomalous dimension is independent of the chosen spin structure.

- For heavy-to-heavy currents with velocities \(v\) and \(v'\), the counterterm and anomalous dimension depend nontrivially on \(w=v\cdot v'\). Wilson coefficients can therefore depend on \(v\), \(v'\), the heavy-quark masses, \(\alpha_s\), and the renormalization scale. In the example \(B\to D^*\ell\nu\), \(w\) is fixed by external kinematics and varies with momentum transfer; the stated allowed range is 1 to 1.5. Heavy-quark symmetry ensures that the anomalous dimension remains independent of the spin structure.

- Renormalization-group evolution resums the heavy-quark and QCD logarithms. At leading-log order, a Wilson coefficient is normalized at the heavy-quark mass and evolved to a lower scale, with the coupling running according to the anomalous dimension. Matrix elements are also scale dependent and are evolved from the heavy-quark mass to a chosen perturbative cutoff, typically around \(1\) or \(1.5\) GeV rather than down to \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\).

- Matching full QCD to HQET requires full-theory loop calculations, LSZ finite residues, effective-theory graphs, and subtraction to obtain Wilson coefficients. A heavy-to-light vector current produces two HQET vector-current structures because both the external Lorentz index and the HQET velocity \(v^\mu\) are available. Heavy-to-heavy matching likewise has \(w\)-dependent coefficients.

- A shortcut uses dimensional regularization for both ultraviolet and infrared divergences with on-shell external momenta. HQET loop integrals are then scaleless: their ultraviolet poles vanish after \(\overline{\mathrm{MS}}\) subtraction, while their infrared poles cancel the corresponding full-theory poles. Thus, if this infrared cancellation is trusted, the matching can be obtained from the renormalized full-theory calculation without explicitly calculating the HQET graphs. Ultraviolet counterterms must still be included; formally scaleless bare graphs are zero even though their renormalized contributions are nonzero.

- Higher-order power corrections are obtained by expanding in \(1/M_Q\). Integrating out the heavy field through its equations of motion produces \(L_0\) and \(L_1\). The \(1/M_Q\) kinetic term breaks flavor symmetry but not spin symmetry, while the magnetic-moment-type \(\sigma_{\mu\nu}G^{\mu\nu}\) term breaks both spin and flavor symmetry.

- A bottom-up operator construction must respect power counting, gauge symmetry, discrete symmetries, and Lorentz symmetry. Because introducing a velocity breaks part of Lorentz symmetry, HQET also requires reparameterization invariance:
  \[
  v^\mu\rightarrow v^\mu+\frac{\epsilon^\mu}{M_Q},\qquad
  k^\mu\rightarrow k^\mu-\epsilon^\mu,\qquad v\cdot\epsilon=0.
  \]
  This hidden symmetry restores small-boost invariance and connects operators at different orders in \(1/M_Q\). It fixes the kinetic Wilson coefficient to one at all orders, provided the scheme and regulator preserve the symmetry. The magnetic coefficient is not fixed by this symmetry, must be calculated, and has an anomalous dimension involving a non-Abelian adjoint-Casimir power of the coupling.

President Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron marked the Trump administration’s first state dinner at the White House, toasting the Franco-American alliance and recent joint U.S.-French airstrikes in Syria as part of their shared fight for freedom. The professor briefly discussed the midterm and grading: results were compressed, homework performance was steady, grades would follow an approximate half-A/half-B guideline, and the final would carry substantial weight. He then began the second half of the course, shifting from block codes for the additive white Gaussian noise channel to convolutional codes.

Shannon had shown that random codes can approach channel capacity, and random linear codes can do so with polynomial-complexity encoding. Maximum-likelihood decoding is exponential, while algebraic codes such as Reed–Solomon, BCH, and Reed–Muller codes permit efficient decoding but cannot reach capacity because they are generally bounded-distance and cannot fully exploit reliability information. The second half will therefore preserve linear structure while adding structure that supports efficient maximum- or quasi-maximum-likelihood decoding.

Convolutional codes were introduced through a rate-1/2, constraint-length-2 encoder. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), its outputs satisfy
\[
y_{1k}=u_k+u_{k-2}, \qquad y_{2k}=u_k+u_{k-1}+u_{k-2}.
\]
This encoder is both linear-time invariant and a four-state finite-state system. The finite-state structure enables efficient decoding with the Viterbi algorithm.

The professor defined convolutional codes using semi-infinite Laurent input sequences with a definite starting time and an all-zero initial encoder state. Their \(D\)-transforms provide compact generating-function representations. Laurent sequences form a field: their definite starting times make convolution well defined, and long division produces inverses. Rational sequences are ratios of polynomials and are equivalently eventually periodic. Causal, rational impulse responses characterize encoders realizable with finite memory; an encoder with constraint length \(\nu\) has \(2^\nu\) states.

For rate-\(1/n\) encoders, rational causal scalar multiples generate equivalent codes. A canonical equivalent encoder uses a feedback-free polynomial realization with the lowest possible constraint length.

Finally, the example code was shown to be linear over \(\mathbb F_2\), so its minimum distance equals its minimum nonzero codeword weight. Its free distance is five, as confirmed through direct analysis and its four-state transition diagram. The next topics are trellis diagrams, catastrophicity, and the Viterbi algorithm.

Travis Stork, a former math major turned MD who worked at a Washington, D.C. free clinic after college, shares health advice on “The Doctors.” He recommends sustainable weight-loss changes, such as walking 30 minutes daily, reducing soda, and choosing whole grains, rather than focusing on the scale. For Super Bowl snacks, he suggests bean or whole-grain nachos with guacamole, jalapeños, salsa, Greek yogurt, and real cheese while avoiding fried chips, sour cream, and nacho cheese sauce. He also advises couples to cook healthy meals and exercise together, noting that support networks improve their chances of success.

Teurlings Catholic High announced several appointments. Robert Boudreaux, an alumnus, parent and coach, became director of institutional advancement after serving as Knights of Columbus state office administrator since 1992. Maria Latiolais Hanes, a 1998 graduate and longtime admissions director, was named development director and will retain her admissions role while overseeing development, fundraising, public relations and communications. Rev. Dustin Dought, pastor of St. Leo the Great and a 2005 graduate, became chaplain and the first alumnus on the school’s Board of Pastors. Father Hampton Davis remains chancellor.

The Diamond & One is a variation of the Box & One in which four defenders play zone and the fifth applies strong pass denial to the opponent’s scoring ace. It is best used against odd-front or one-guard offenses. It effectively protects the middle but concedes the corner; defenders should switch to a Box & One if the corner becomes problematic. X5 remains low between the ball and basket, X3 and X4 cover the extended free-throw-line area through the corners, and X1 defends the high post. Defensive shifts rotate players among the ball, elbows, middle, and weakside baseline as the offense moves. Against an odd front, defenders push the ball handler away from the star, deny passes, protect the high post, and anticipate weakside rebounds. The scheme also supports double-teaming a post player: X4 denies the post, X5 doubles with X4, X1 protects the high post, and the outside defenders cut off escape passes. The chaser’s strong denial is central to disrupting the star player’s participation and the offense’s continuity.

Kano State flagged off distribution of 10,000 free delivery kits across its 44 local government areas, costing N145 million, to help prevent childbirth infections among mothers and newborns. The kits contain basic delivery supplies and instructions and are intended for traditional birth attendants, midwives, and women delivering alone. WHO research cited by the report says clean delivery kits can reduce neonatal and maternal illness and deaths from cord infection, tetanus, and puerperal sepsis.

The government also reported training 1,936 traditional birth attendants, renovating more than 300 health facilities, establishing specialized hospitals, training health workers, compiling data on pregnant women, and planning incentives for women using clinics. WHO representatives supported the initiative, while the report cited an estimated 50,000 annual maternal deaths in Nigeria.

Zambia’s parliament suspended 48 UPND lawmakers for 30 days after they boycotted President Edgar Lungu’s assembly address and refused to recognize him as leader. The opposition called the action unconstitutional, while Amnesty International described related treason charges as “trumped up.”

The California Supreme Court affirmed judgment reforming a land-sale agreement, ordering specific performance, and awarding the unpaid purchase price, interest, and costs. Ward and Yorba claimed competing titles to Los Angeles property worth $9,000. Ward sold his interest to Yorba for $4,750, with $100 paid and the balance due in thirty days. Although the written contract required Ward to convey a “good and perfect title,” the evidence supported the finding that the parties intended only a transfer of Ward’s interest and that the clause was inserted through mistake. Yorba knew the relevant title facts and entered the agreement on counsel’s advice, so he was not entitled to rescission for mistake. The agreement also had adequate consideration because it settled competing claims, extinguished Ward’s rights, transferred possession, and avoided litigation.

Malformed commands or migration-list entries cause rejection or partial success. Ring-buffer errors are reported in PM_STATUS; hardware errors in command status and/or via MCA. Failures return status codes, though memory may be unrecoverable. Clients detecting timeouts should log an MCA, attempt correction, and consider saving state, terminating VMs, or stopping commands.

The passage explains trading options on Apple (AAPL). Options are contracts giving buyers the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price by a specified expiration date. Calls provide purchase rights, while puts provide sale rights. Option prices are influenced by Apple’s stock price, time to expiration, market volatility, interest rates, dividends, and corporate or macroeconomic news. Rising stock prices generally increase call prices and reduce put prices, while higher volatility increases both. Time decay reduces option value as expiration approaches.

Strategies described include buying or selling calls and puts, covered calls, protective puts, straddles, and strangles. Calls can speculate on price increases, puts can hedge declines or generate income, protective puts hedge while shares are held, and straddles or strangles can profit from volatility or moves in either direction. Delta hedging uses opposing positions to limit losses. The passage emphasizes that options are complex, highly leveraged, zero-sum instruments whose losses can exceed the initial investment, and that naked short calls carry potentially unlimited risk.

Apple options are described as highly liquid and volatile, allowing trades near desired prices but also producing potentially large gains or losses. Costs include contract premiums, broker commissions, transaction fees, taxes, and slippage. Profits are generally subject to capital gains taxes, while the passage states that option losses may not offset gains from other investments under wash-sale rules.

Traders can use market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders. Limit orders are recommended for entering and exiting at predetermined prices. Stop-loss and trailing stop-loss orders can limit losses or protect profits, but adverse gaps may cause prices to move beyond the order’s trigger. American-style options may be exercised before expiration and are generally more expensive than European-style options, which can be exercised only at expiration. Both are exposed to early-exercise considerations.

Analytical tools include charting and other technical-analysis software, company financial and market information, the Black-Scholes model, and Monte Carlo simulations. The passage recommends quantitative backtesting and proper trading rules while expressing skepticism about relying on technical analysis or financial news. Fundamental and options analysis can assess company prospects, option values, risks, and potential trades. Changes in interest rates, inflation, volatility, company news, earnings, product announcements, dividends, and strike prices can materially affect options, but many such movements are difficult to predict.

Other derivatives discussed include futures, forwards, and swaps. The passage repeatedly cautions that most traders may have better odds trading AAPL stock directly and should carefully assess their competitive advantage before entering the options market.

In an Oct. 14, 2025 Motley Fool Money article, the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card is presented as a leading no-annual-fee rewards card. It offers unlimited 2% cash back on all purchases, a $200 bonus after $500 in spending during the first three months, and 12 months of 0% introductory APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by an 18.99%–28.99% variable APR. Benefits also include Visa Signature concierge service and up to $600 of cell phone damage or theft protection with a $25 deductible.

The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card offers unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% back on hotels, vacation rentals and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, no annual or foreign transaction fees, and a $300 welcome package consisting of a $100 travel credit and a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases. It also provides 15 months of 0% introductory APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers before an 18.99%–28.99% variable APR.

A Citi offer provides 2% cash back on purchases when paid on time, 5% back on certain travel booked through Citi Travel, and $200 after $1,500 in purchases within six months. Its 18-month 0% introductory rate applies only to balance transfers, which carry fees of 3% during the first four months and 5% afterward, with a $5 minimum. The recommended credit score for all three offers is 670–850, but approval is not guaranteed. The page discloses that commissions may affect offer placement and coverage but not product ratings.
A headline roundup covers a cellphone-saving survivor of an Istanbul nightclub attack, criticism of Trump, a 2017 horoscope, Fort Bliss disappearances, fitness tips and Ivanka Trump in Hawaii.

The passage describes a simple mean-reversion strategy for the SPY ETF using the Relative Strength Index (RSI), an indicator that measures price-movement speed and change to identify potential overbought or oversold reversals. Trades are entered when specified RSI conditions occur and exited when defined criteria are met. The backtest from 1993 onward reports a 0.57% average gain per trade, 75% win rate, 23% maximum drawdown, and 2.3 profit factor. The strategy reportedly performs comparably to buy-and-hold while spending less time in the market and experiencing roughly half the drawdown. Adding one parameter reduced trades from 470 to 377 while increasing total returns; the additional indicator is reserved for subscribers. RSI is described as a commonly used professional trading tool that can be traded on its own.

After PlayStation Russia posted a cryptic image featuring a PS4 and an “X,” users speculated about new hardware, PlayStation Now’s launch in Russia, cross-play, or PlayStation Online and store updates. The author considered an internet-related announcement most likely, while noting next-generation announcements remained premature.

This qualitative case study examined AI integration throughout an applied university course, “Digital Photography in Nature.” Guided by TPACK, constructivist learning theory, and the MRK instructional-design model, it explored effects on creativity and technical development, the instructor’s design and implementation experiences, and conditions for effective, ethical use. Semi-structured interviews with 38 associate-degree students and one instructor at a public university in eastern Türkiye were analyzed through content analysis.

The instructor redesigned the course around micro-level AI integration, flipped-classroom instruction, collaborative project-based work, weekly themed photography assignments, AI-assisted photo analysis, peer critique, and AI-generated assessment rubrics. ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Flikia AI, Krea AI, and other applications supported feedback, technical analysis, content development, presentation design, learner analysis, and editing. Reported benefits included stronger technical knowledge and vocabulary, more precise and personalized feedback, faster information access, improved AI literacy and engagement, and more systematic assessment. Students variously regarded AI as an assistant, guide, teacher, and aid to critical thinking.

The study also identified infrastructure gaps, unequal access to devices and paid tools, hallucinations, misinformation, contradictory responses, passivity, over-reliance, reduced originality, and risks to independent analysis and learning. It concludes that AI should supplement rather than replace instructors. Recommended measures include AI-literacy and educator training, reflection-based assignments, human and peer feedback, source verification, ethical use, equitable access, and continuous monitoring. Limitations include the single-course, single-instructor, qualitative design and absence of a control group; longitudinal and comparative research is needed.

All Education Department rule-making sessions have been virtual since the COVID-19 pandemic began. The department is working to clarify graduate loan caps and consolidate income-driven repayment plans before their July 1, 2026, effective date. A potential federal shutdown could disrupt the current session and furlough nearly 87% of employees, though rule-making staff would remain. Experts said tight timelines and possible staffing losses complicate finalization. Under the shutdown plan, student aid and loan payments would continue, civil-rights investigations would pause, and grantmaking would cease, though previously awarded grants would remain accessible.

At Apple Inc.’s March 4, 2022 annual meeting, shareholders approved the 2022 Employee Stock Plan, effective immediately, authorizing stock options, stock appreciation rights, stock grants and restricted stock units for employees and consultants. Its share reserve begins with 510 million shares, includes specified carryover and forfeiture amounts, and is capped at 1,274,374,682 shares; full-value awards count as two shares per share issued. Grant authority under the 2014 Plan ends once the 2022 Plan is registered on Form S-8.

Shareholders elected nine directors, ratified Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent auditor for 2022, and approved an advisory vote on executive compensation. Proposals on deeper-purpose reincorporation, transparency reports, forced labor and pay equity were rejected, while proposals for a civil rights audit and a report on concealment clauses were approved. The filing included the 2022 Employee Stock Plan and forms of restricted stock unit and performance award agreements as exhibits.

A second generic version of the abortion pill mifepristone was approved by the FDA. Amgen reported that Repatha reduced the combined risk of heart-disease death, heart attacks and strokes in a 12,000-patient trial, supporting hopes for broader PCSK9 inhibitor use. A new NIH office will focus on reducing animal testing.

Tyson Foods received a consensus “Buy” from 17 covering brokerages, with an average 12-month price target of $72.96. Analysts included Zacks upgrading to “Buy” with a $73 target, BMO Capital Markets maintaining “Outperform” with a raised $78 target, Mizuho affirming “Buy” with a $76 target, RBC retaining “Sector Perform” with a $70 target, and Pivotal Research affirming “Sell” with a $40 target.

Tyson reported quarterly EPS of $1.28, beating the $1.18 estimate, and revenue of $9.85 billion versus $9.49 billion expected. Revenue rose 4.8% year over year. The company announced a $0.225 quarterly dividend. CFO Dennis Leatherby sold 145,100 shares for $9.57 million, while director Mikel Durham bought 2,809 shares for about $184,748. Hedge funds and other institutional investors owned 71.89% of the stock.

An international team found that tumor-associated bacteria, including *E. coli*, produce 2-methylisocitrate (2-MiCit), a metabolite that weakens colorectal cancer cells and enhances chemotherapy. Experiments in worms, human cancer cells, and flies showed that 2-MiCit inhibits a key mitochondrial enzyme, disrupting cancer-cell metabolism, damaging DNA, and reducing cancer progression. Combined with 5-fluorouracil, it killed cancer cells more effectively than either treatment alone. Patient microbiome modeling indicated that tumor bacteria can produce 2-MiCit, and researchers created a modified synthetic version with greater potency, suggesting potential new cancer drugs and relevance to personalized medicine.

Montreal reports 11 hot-weather deaths; four more were reported in the Eastern Townships. Urgences-Santé says calls are 30% above normal and urges residents to reserve 911 for emergencies. A heat warning spans parts of Ontario and Quebec into the Atlantic region, with hot, humid conditions likely through Thursday.

NuVasive will host an Industry Lunch and Learn at AANS on Monday, April 30, from 1:10–1:55 p.m. in Room 272-273, focused on lateral single-position surgery for L4–S1, advanced 3D-printed implants, and LessRay radiation-reduction technology.
