The device integrates an ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem with a general-purpose, Harvard-architecture processor supporting full memory management, hardware and software debug, NEON SIMD, VFPv3 floating point, and separate instruction and data caches. Its AINTC prioritizes peripheral service requests and generates IRQ or FIQ signals, although general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation to the ARM. Real-time trace uses an ETM interface whose unpinned trace port connects to a 32KB system ETB. The embedded PLL_ARM generates subsystem clocks from the device clock, while an arbiter connects the processor to a 128-bit DMM port for DDR access and a 64-bit L3 port for other device modules.

The C674x DSP subsystem includes 32KB of L1 program/cache memory with error detection, 256KB of unified L2 RAM/cache with error correction, and little-endian operation. Its CPU has eight functional units, two 32-bit register files, and support for 8-, 16-, 32-, 40-, and 64-bit data. The units perform multiplication, arithmetic, logical, branch, load, and store operations, with one instruction per cycle per unit. Features include extended and Galois-field multiplication, complex multiplication, parallel and saturated arithmetic, MIN2/MAX2 operations, packing and unpacking, SPLOOP software-pipelining support, compact instructions, enhanced exception handling, user and supervisor privilege levels, memory-page protections, and a stall-insensitive time-stamp counter.

All C674x MDMA accesses pass through the system MMU, which remaps them to physical addresses, protects ARM memory regions, and permits direct user-space buffer allocation. EDMA transfer channels 0 and 1 can optionally use the MMU. The Media Controller manages the HDVPSS and ISS modules. The HDVICP2 accelerator supports encoding, decoding, and transcoding for major standards including MPEG, H.264, VC-1, RV9/10, AVS-1.0, and ON2 VP6.2/VP7. The Face Detection module performs in-memory face detection and tracking for encoding, autofocus, or red-eye removal, using QVGA 8-bit luma input and 51.25KB of DDR working memory.

The Spinlock module provides 128 hardware semaphores using single-read locking. The Mailbox module supports ARM–DSP and interprocessor communication through message registers, four-message FIFO queues, and interrupts assigned to the ARM, C674x, and Media Controller. The device uses a unified memory map where possible, with separate L3 and L4 mappings and limited C674x peripheral access. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4GB range for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; only HDVPSS and ISS can access the full range, while other masters access one view through the base 512MB TILER region.

James Madison returned the internal-improvements bill to the House of Representatives without his signature, arguing that Congress lacked constitutional authority to fund and construct roads, canals, and navigable waterways. He maintained that the interstate commerce power did not authorize such construction and that the common defense and general welfare clause could not grant Congress general legislative power or override state authority and judicial review. State consent could expand federal power only as the Constitution permitted. Despite recognizing the potential benefits of internal improvements, Madison opposed the bill because it required an overly broad interpretation of federal powers and threatened the constitutional division between national and state governments, suggesting that the bill’s objectives be pursued through proper constitutional amendments.

Russia remained a central concern. In Afghanistan, NATO planned to expand Resolute Support from 13,000 to about 16,000 personnel. It also joined the coalition confronting ISIS, trained nearly 500 Iraqi trainers and announced a new Iraqi training mission and additional regional support.

The article defines scalping as trading small price movements over seconds or minutes and argues that it is unusually difficult and likely unprofitable for most traders. Scalpers compete with sophisticated traders, banks, hedge funds, and high-frequency firms with superior software, capital, market access, and execution speed, while facing substantial market noise and randomness.

Commissions, bid-ask spreads, and especially slippage can quickly consume the small profits sought by scalpers. Short-term backtests often fail to reflect live trading because they inadequately capture execution problems, transaction costs, and randomness. Scalping also creates substantial stress, requires automation in practice, and exposes traders to costly automated-system errors.

The article says profitable scalping opportunities are rare, few strategies work reliably, and realistic edges are easier to identify on longer time frames. It recommends seeking strategies and edges with greater profit potential over longer horizons, while noting that some traders may prefer patient, diversified long-term investing. Although consistent scalping profits may be possible, the article considers it very difficult and inferior to alternatives in terms of risk and reward.

DFT calculations were used to investigate three previously unstudied o-MAX phases, Mo₂A₂AlC₃ (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), with hexagonal P6₃/mmc structures. GGA-PBE and PBEsol functionals, phonon calculations, stress–strain methods, Mulliken analyses, quasi-harmonic thermal models, and optical calculations were applied to evaluate their properties.

All three phases are chemically, dynamically, and mechanically stable. Their formation energies are negative, with Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃ showing the greatest chemical stability. No imaginary phonon frequencies were found. Electronic band structures and densities of states confirm metallic behavior and directional anisotropy, while Mo–C bonding is predominantly covalent and Mo–Al bonding is metallic. Mulliken analyses indicate mixed ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding, with Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ exhibiting the strongest bonding and highest predicted stiffness, fracture toughness, and Vickers hardness. The compounds are mechanically anisotropic and classified as brittle.

Thermodynamically, Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ has the lowest predicted minimum thermal conductivity, while Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ has the highest melting temperature. Their thermal expansion coefficients, Debye temperatures, thermal conductivities, heat capacities, and Grüneisen parameters indicate potential for high-temperature thermal-barrier coatings. Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃ provides greater damage tolerance, and Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ shows the greatest resistance to crack propagation.

Optical calculations reveal Drude-like metallic behavior, anisotropic absorption, and high infrared reflectivity. Reflectivity across the infrared, visible, and mid-ultraviolet ranges exceeds the threshold cited for coating applications, suggesting possible use in solar heat-shielding layers. Overall, the three compounds are identified as promising candidates for thermal-barrier and other high-temperature applications.

This conceptual, non-empirical paper examines how generative AI can be incorporated ethically and practically into contemporary and imagined education systems. Drawing on Anders, Foucault, Freire, Bloom’s revised taxonomy, and Arendt, it argues that AI presents risks to human agency, knowledge, and truth while potentially supporting more humanizing education.

Anders’s “Promethean discrepancy” highlights the gap between technological capabilities and humanity’s ability to imagine their consequences, while Foucault’s analysis of regimes of truth frames AI as a power-laden technology that can outsource thought, normalize errors, replicate biases, and shape what educators and learners accept as knowledge. Freire’s concepts of conscientization, dialogue, and humanization suggest that educational technology is not inherently harmful when used critically to advance students’ agency and capacity to transform the world.

The paper supplements Bloom’s taxonomy—which spans remembering through creating—with Arendt’s hierarchy of labor, work, and action. AI performs across Bloom’s levels, generally more successfully at lower cognitive levels, but these classifications alone cannot establish whether educational use is ethical. Arendt’s framework adds a normative direction toward building durable works and enabling public, deliberative action rather than merely reducing education to consumption and repetitive labor.

On this basis, the authors propose a framework for assessing student AI use across online, blended, and in-person education. It places AI-assisted textual and multimodal work on a spectrum from consumptive labor to humanizing action, considering students’ perspectives, critical engagement, meaningful effects, and capacity to act in the world. Illustrative applications include community-based political action and Socratic AI-supported research that culminates in community engagement. The paper concludes that educators and instructional designers must continually adapt, reassess AI’s consequences, redesign pedagogy, and conduct research in ethically ambiguous use cases so education remains centered on human agency and meaningful action.

This continuation patent describes methods and apparatus for managing reduced processing time in low-latency cellular systems using configurable or short transmission time intervals (TTIs). A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) determines processing capabilities or limits based on criteria including TTI length, transport-block size, transmission or reception type, channel type, scheduling or HARQ timeline, resources, coding, MIMO, waveform, and numerology. The WTRU may report its capabilities to an eNodeB, receive a capability configuration, and limit timing advance or receive-transmit time difference for a given TTI length.

The WTRU may measure processing value, calculate processing headroom, and report proximity conditions. Embodiments determine available processing time from downlink control information, grants, or downlink transmissions and compare it with a capability threshold to decide whether to transmit scheduled uplink data or HARQ feedback. If processing headroom is insufficient, uplink transmissions may be suspended or dropped. The disclosure also covers timing-advance behavior, timing-alignment timers, HARQ buffer management, and LTE, LTE-Advanced, and NR system architectures.

India’s trucking market is expected to transform by 2027, driven by rapid population growth, urbanisation and rising demand for freight transport. The rollout of BS VI emissions standards, skipping BS V, will require more efficient and powerful trucks. Long-distance freight routes are also expected to expand if the Goods and Services Tax removes delays at state borders. Increased speeds will necessitate major infrastructure investment and could strengthen the position of international manufacturers such as BharatBenz, Scania, Volvo and AMW, with Hyundai also targeting heavy-duty trucking. Future trucks are therefore expected to be larger, faster, more connected and efficient, while government policy changes create uncertainty. Electrification and autonomous driving are unlikely to reach India’s roads for several more decades.

The disclosure describes a device and method for implementing fundamental computational primitives using a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA) coupled to a processor. Control software configures one or more streaming engines to transfer data from memory in the required order and configures the MMA’s formatting, row-offset, and nonlinearity components before executing the primitive. The primitives support applications including speech recognition, industrial control, object recognition, and vision.

An exemplary processor is a digital signal processor with L1 data cache, L2 unified cache, and two streaming engines. The MMA includes a 1×32 A-matrix buffer, two 32×32 B-matrix buffers used as ping-pong buffers, and two 32×32 C-matrix buffers used as foreground and background result buffers. Each cycle, a load-store-execute (LSE) instruction can load data, multiply an A-buffer vector with a B-buffer matrix, and store the resulting row in a C buffer. It can also load a B-buffer row, store a C-buffer row, and assign, add, subtract, or otherwise process the multiplication result.

Configurable format components support several numeric input and output types and fixed-point Q-point settings. The A-format component can expand 4-bit lookup-table data to 16 bits, while the row-offset component controls the destination row of each element loaded into a B buffer. A configurable ReLU nonlinearity replaces negative output values with zero. Processor-side input formatting includes zero padding, even/odd vector generation, scalar replication, known-matrix generation, and linked operations. Output formatting includes seam and stride removal, zero padding, and matrix transposition.

The streaming engines are programmable with a stream’s starting address, element size and type, formatting, and multidimensional address sequence. Their nested-loop addressing permits regular multidimensional memory-access patterns. Control software configures the engines and MMA, starts the streams, executes the LSE sequence, and invokes any required processor-side formatting.

Described implementations use matrix multiplication to perform batched and large matrix multiplication, pointwise multiplication, matrix addition, small vector-matrix multiplication, vector summation, and affine transformation. Batched operations load matrices, vectors, or filters diagonally or in replicated blocks and use row offsets to position them. Two-dimensional convolution converts feature maps into a filtering matrix, applies filter blocks through tiled matrix multiplication, and handles seams, strides, and padding through tile sizing and output formatting. Row and column permutations use permutation matrices.

The device can also perform complex-to-complex FFTs, DCTs, one-dimensional convolution and filtering, correlation, matrix assignment, and matrix transposition. FFT implementations use DFT matrices, pointwise twiddle-factor multiplication, and matrix transposition; DCTs use analogous real-valued processing. Large one-dimensional filters are recursively divided into smaller fragments, whose shifted results are added, balancing MMA throughput against the number of fragments. Matrix assignment uses multiplication by an identity matrix, while transposition uses an MMA copy mode that writes A-buffer elements into successive B-buffer columns. Other embodiments permit different processor types and different MMA buffer dimensions.

The passage introduces NVIDIA’s eighth-generation data center GPU, the A100 Tensor Core GPU, built on the Ampere GA100 architecture and TSMC’s 7nm N7 process. It succeeds the Tesla V100 and targets AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads across workstations, servers, clusters, cloud data centers, edge systems, and supercomputers. The GA100 contains 54.2 billion transistors and occupies 826 mm².

A100’s third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, IEEE-compliant FP64, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary operations, as well as fine-grained structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput. Reported comparisons with V100 include 10x faster TF32 processing, or 20x with sparsity; 2.5x faster FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance, or 5x with sparsity; equal BF16 and FP16 throughput; and 20x faster sparse INT8 performance.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3x V100’s read bandwidth. Its L1 and shared-memory capacity is 192 KB per SM, compared with 128 KB on V100. It also adds cache-residency controls and Compute Data Compression for potential gains in memory bandwidth and cache capacity.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated memory-system paths, quality-of-service guarantees, and fault isolation for multi-tenant deployments. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s of aggregate bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, NVSwitch, and Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet technologies support larger multi-GPU and multi-node systems.

Additional hardware and CUDA 11 improvements include asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, faster task-graph execution, and improved error detection, isolation, and containment. Collectively, these capabilities are presented as improving performance, scalability, utilization, programmability, and multi-tenant flexibility over the prior generation.
An 80-year-old man was treated on a Gujranwala hospital floor during a bed shortage. PML-N workers celebrated Yaum-e-Takbeer, honoring Nawaz Sharif for making Pakistan a nuclear power.

Apple edged past Samsung in fourth-quarter smartphone sales for the first time in two years, selling 77 million iPhones (17.9% share) to Samsung's 76.8 million (17.8%), per Gartner. Apple's holiday-season strength and Samsung's Galaxy Note7 recall, which cost it 10–15% of sales plus brand damage, drove the result. Samsung's March flagship could restore its lead, since Apple waits until September, when the iPhone turns 10 and buyers may delay purchases. Over 2016, Samsung led with 20.5% share to Apple's 14.4%. Chinese firms ranked third through fifth: Huawei (9.5%), Oppo (6.2%) and BBK (5.6%), with BBK China's top smartphone brand.

Unidentified gunmen attacked U.N. peacekeeping bases in Timbuktu and Douentza, Mali, killing seven people in Timbuktu and a Malian soldier and U.N. peacekeeper in Douentza. MINUSMA said six assailants were killed in Timbuktu and two in Douentza. The attacks brought the number of U.N. peacekeepers killed that year to nine. Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the attacks, warned they may constitute war crimes, and praised regional anti-terrorism efforts. The U.N. is investigating possible links, and mission commander Mahamat Saleh Annadif called for those responsible to be brought to justice.

Arizona ammunition dealer Douglas Haig was charged with manufacturing armor-piercing ammunition without a license after his fingerprints were found on unfired bullets in the Mandalay Bay hotel room. Records do not show whether the bullets were used. Haig sold Stephen Paddock 720 tracer rounds before the Las Vegas attack, noticed nothing suspicious, and denied contributing to the shooting that killed 58.

The Treasury Department recommended rolling back key Obama-era Wall Street regulations, including repealing Dodd-Frank’s CEO pay-ratio disclosure requirement. The second of four reviews ordered by President Trump, the report also proposes easing initial public offering rules, allowing confidential “testing of the waters” discussions, and raising the annual crowdfunding limit for private companies from $1 million to $5 million. It further calls for the SEC and CFTC to harmonize derivatives oversight. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said streamlining regulations could promote economic growth, while critics warned the proposals were broadly deregulatory and could weaken post-crisis safety controls. Some recommendations require congressional action, although much could be implemented by regulators. The House has passed legislation gutting key Dodd-Frank provisions, but the Senate has not taken up similar legislation.

LLMs can serve as low-cost synthetic respondents and agents for social research, reproducing some survey patterns, experimental effects, and behavioral trends. However, their outputs arise from pattern matching and sampling over learned language distributions, not from coherent Bayesian inference or draws from defined human populations. Their apparent probabilistic behavior can therefore be misleading, especially when synthetic samples are treated as evidence about human beliefs.

Repeated LLM queries can violate exchangeability and forecast invariance, making predictions depend on the order in which synthetic participants are generated. This order dependence contributes to “introspective hallucination,” in which adding model-generated observations systematically shifts subsequent predictions. Larger, instruction-tuned models have sometimes performed worse on statistical-coherence tests than smaller foundational models. Fine-tuning and alignment may improve contextual prediction while encouraging specialized mimicry, overfitting, and brittleness rather than generalizable explanations of human behavior.

Researchers should therefore treat LLMs as high-capacity predictors under explicit conditioning, not calibrated sources of posterior belief. They should measure and report algorithmic fidelity, subgroup calibration, response dispersion, and human-baseline accuracy; flag unnaturally low variance and systematic distribution shifts; down-weight or exclude overly confident synthetic evidence; and use confidence sets and effective-sample caps that reflect mismatch with humans. Synthetic data may complement human measurements for instrument pretesting, identifying failure modes, sample allocation, and sensitivity analysis, but should not replace human inference.

Robust agents should be anchored to individual-level human data and specific tasks, tested for out-of-domain generalization, and evaluated under varied prompts, contexts, and experimental setups. Pipelines should avoid in-prompt self-conditioning, randomize item order, fix decoding settings, and test independence, position effects, and order invariance. Studies should disclose failures, generalization limits, subgroup performance, and methodological details sufficient for reproducibility, including prompts, model versions, decoding parameters, seeds, and ensemble variance. The paper concludes that LLM-based social simulation has substantial near-term value as a set of domain-specific analytic tools, but not as a universal or mechanistically interpretable model of human behavior.

NIST’s revised password guidance recommends simple, long, memorable passphrases using lowercase letters and typical English words rather than special characters or mixed capitalization. It says passwords need not expire and opposes routine 90-day changes because users often make only minor alterations. Longer passwords are harder to crack, while password managers remain useful but are not considered necessary for security.

The final Friday Burrito of 2000 reviews three turbulent weeks in California’s electricity market, including FERC orders, emergency filings, rate stabilization, data subpoenas, credit problems, and price spikes. The author argues that industry public relations should focus on consumers’ primary concern—how much their electric bills will increase—rather than on complex restructuring issues. He proposes three priorities: adding generation, expanding consumer choice, and maintaining a provider of last resort.

The newsletter satirizes Senator Steve Peace’s criticism of high Mid-C electricity prices and his claims that prospective refunds would not adequately discipline marketers. It also describes SCE CEO John Bryson’s call to re-regulate California’s electric system by having utilities plan and acquire sufficient power and charge cost-based rates. The author links this position to Pacific Northwest producers’ credit constraints, noting delayed payments, frozen retail rates, utility debt, and the leverage of SCE and PG&E as major buyers. The CPUC reopened rate-stabilization applications for PG&E and Edison after initially suspending them.

President Lynch stated that California had ample power and no shortage, but attributed rolling outages to poor daily management and unavailable plants. She cited 41,000 megawatts of available capacity, suspicious summer bids, the ISO’s utility-dominated governance, San Diego’s exposure to price volatility, and the controversial PX practice of paying every bidder the highest accepted price. The author planned to debate Lynch and Netie Hogue on KQED.

Energy Secretary Richardson invoked a rarely used Federal Power Act provision to require out-of-state generators and marketers to sell power to California on demand, and ordered BPA and WAPA to ship as much power as possible. BPA supplied roughly 1,500 megawatts from hydro reserves and PowerEx delivered another 400 megawatts, relieving an ISO Stage 3 alert but potentially jeopardizing BPA’s later obligations and salmon runs. The author also recalled a voluntary staggered Christmas-lighting program and described an internal ISO tariff amendment that could impose more direct demand controls.

The Power Exchange asked FERC to replace the ISO’s $250-per-MWh hard cap on adjustment bids with an energy-price equivalent, enabling forward trading and reducing pressure on the real-time market. WPTF supported the motion, while the ISO opposed it and offered an alternative plan.

Mailbag responses addressed industry public relations and changing workforce demographics. Writers supported a coordinated consumer-education effort focused on competition’s value, the costs of returning to cost-based regulation, and California’s business climate, while noting the need for funding, documentation, and institutional support.

WPTF’s general meeting was scheduled for February 8–9, 2001, at the Marriott Resort in Old Town Scottsdale, Arizona, with sessions on Desert STAR, AISA, California power markets, and national energy policy.

The newsletter also included humorous election poems portraying the unresolved 2000 presidential election and a personal story about the author’s son interviewing him about his childhood during a drive to hockey practice. It closed with holiday wishes and reflections on the preceding year’s energy crisis.

Balaji and Pyari (2023) assessed early childhood education (ECE) programs in 71 Anganwadi centers (AWCs) across 25 villages of Nuh Block, Mewat district, Haryana, using a mixed qualitative-quantitative approach with a checklist, observations, and interviews with Anganwadi workers (AWWs), including 36 telephonic semi-structured interviews. Findings showed widespread deficiencies: 41 centers had boundary walls, 39 had gates, 23 had safe building structures, and 14 had leveled floors; most lacked mats, desks, chairs, lights, fans, play equipment, learning resources, and basic health and hygiene facilities such as toilets, drinking water, and kitchens. All centers kept attendance registers, but none had a pre-school timetable. Most AWWs had low educational qualifications, limited awareness of school readiness and the five developmental domains, infrequent training, and relied mainly on repetition and memorization rather than activity-based teaching. The authors note that these problems are common in rural India and affect equity in preschool education, and discuss NEP 2020's emphasis on quality, play-based ECE for children aged 3–6, trained educators, parental and community engagement, and monitoring. Recommendations include standardized non-negotiable infrastructure, training AWWs in child development and curriculum, parent awareness programs, and state government partnerships with parents, communities, NGOs, and CSR bodies.

The passage identifies overfitting, data contamination, static benchmarks, and complex AI mechanisms as barriers to evaluating LLMs on unforeseen tasks. It proposes future benchmarks that dynamically generate samples, vary task difficulty, and analyze individual capabilities using adapted psychometric principles. Evaluation should also consider cultural and ethnic values and human safety. DyVal addresses these needs with a DAG-based framework that generates low-duplicate, reproducible samples at varied complexity levels, provides computable ground truth, and supports randomized risk control for comparing models.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 specification update catalogs chipset deviations affecting the PIT, interrupt controller, DMA, GLIU debug features, thermal and sleep controls, PCI and USB behavior, and ATAC/ACC data transfers. Issue numbers may be omitted when resolved.

- **PIT:** An uncompleted counter-latch command is not canceled by a subsequent read-back command, so the counter value is supplied before the status byte; read-back should wait for latch completion. In count mode 3, a new count is loaded immediately instead of after the current count finishes.
- **Interrupts and DMA:** XPIC automatic end-of-interrupt mode may send duplicate interrupts because the IRR bit clears one clock late. AEOI should only be used when nested interrupts are unnecessary. Legacy DMA rotating priority does not reliably preserve request order, although transfers complete. UART writes during block or demand 8237 DMA are discarded and reads return all ones; software should wait for DMA completion or use single-byte mode. LPC software-DMA writes from the bus fail without operational impact.
- **Clock gating:** A PIC edge input remaining high after local-bus clock gating can cause missed interrupts and a system hang; automatic clock gating should not be used in this situation.
- **GLIU:** The debug port hangs when detecting debug packets and should not be used. Packet-pattern detection does not work, and its related registers should remain at their defaults. Unexpected-address MSR requests fail to activate the expected error flags.
- **Power management:** A thermal alarm causes Faulted Standby, but the PMC cannot recover autonomously because the alarm is in the Work domain. SLEEP_X, SLEEP_Y, and SLP_CLK_EN require Sleep Clock to be enabled in the PMC before it can be controlled through the GPIO.
- **PCI, USB, and DMA addressing:** PCI I/O addresses of 10000h or higher are incorrectly claimed and can hang the system; such cycles and ATAC/Diverse Device LBAR values should be avoided. The CS5535 does not meet USB 1.1 overvoltage-protection requirements, so external protection circuits are required.
- **ATA/ACC transfers:** Eight-byte PRD prefetch can expose part of the next PRD when tables are only four-byte aligned. PRD tables should be defined before transfers, and live changes should be kept at least two tables ahead. A preceding host-terminated UDMA read can cause incorrect CRC values during a later UDMA write; ATAC Error MSR bit 8 UDMA I/O blocking is recommended to prevent host terminations. During IDE master DMA, the PIO SSMI feature fails to block IDE I/O, but the feature is only intended for debugging and workarounds.

Host environments must include and call these native assembly macros to establish or destroy a stack in stackless execution mode. The routines omit segment declarations and do not depend on host-defined segment names. Each host must create a local file defining its execution environment and use the INCLUDE directive to include the stack source file. The code can be included in assembly host files or, with care, C-language host files.

An ESPN combat-sports page features headlines on Dana White’s Contender Series, UFC and PFL rankings and results, Conor McGregor’s suspension and potential comeback, Alex Pereira’s title win, and other MMA and boxing stories.

Toll purchased Denver property from Charles D. McKenzie’s widow after McKenzie’s friend Casey had used an unrecorded deed, a new warranty deed, and a substituted trust deed to conceal the minor daughters’ undivided interest. Toll later learned of the arrangement and alleged that McKenzie and Casey had constructively defrauded the minors and conveyed defective title.

McKenzie and Casey then agreed through “Contract A” to probate McKenzie’s will, establish a guardianship, disclose the transaction, and perfect Toll’s title through court proceedings at their expense. The probate court approved the executrix’s sale, and McKenzie, as guardian, accounted for the minors’ share. Toll later sought to set aside those proceedings and challenged Casey’s foreclosure.

The court held that the fraud was constructive, that the parties resolved their good-faith dispute through Contract A, and that the disclosed proceedings effectively cured any title defect, even though the contract was not followed literally. However, Toll’s challenge created further title doubts, and Casey had not fully performed his contractual obligations. The probate judgment was affirmed with costs allocated; the foreclosure judgment was affirmed subject to Toll paying Casey the outstanding debt, with interest and specified offsets, by June 1, 1931, after which Casey was ordered to release the trust deed. On rehearing, the latter case was remanded to implement the modified judgment and permit up to a thirty-day extension.

Micro E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures (MNQ) are electronically traded on CME Globex and provide exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index, comprising the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq. They are one-tenth the size of E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures, with a contract value equal to the index value multiplied by $2. They are cash-settled using the index’s special opening quotes, with trading ending at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Contracts are listed quarterly for five consecutive quarters.

The minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points, or $0.50 per outright contract; calendar spreads have a $0.10 tick. Globex trading runs Sunday at 6 p.m. to Friday at 5 p.m. ET, with a daily break from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m.

The discussed strategy requires tested entry and exit rules, risk management, position sizing, and an understanding of market psychology. Its undisclosed setup has three buy variables and one sell variable. A daily-bar backtest using continuous, back-adjusted CME data was performed without risk-management parameters and indicated stronger seasonality in spring and fall than in winter and summer.

TradingView data cited an all-time high of 16,676.50 in November 2021 and a low of 6,628.75 in March 2020. Leverage creates potentially substantial losses.

Trading requires a funded futures-broker account. Unlike futures, broker-offered CFDs trade continuously without expiry or rollover requirements.

The passage lists 13 household and personal uses for hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), including disinfecting and cleaning, whitening, and plant care. Suggested uses include diluted peroxide as a weekly gargle for bad breath, a spray mixture to gradually lighten hair, drops for ear infections, food-grade peroxide for washing produce, and a baking soda mixture for whitening teeth. Cleaning uses include disinfecting toilet bowls, removing baked-on food, sanitizing cutting boards, wiping toys and play areas, soaking feet to soften calluses and diminish foot fungus, removing stains, and disinfecting reusable bags. Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sushrut Babhulkar, with veterinary doctors from MAFSU, plans to fit a prosthetic limb on Sahebrao, a male tiger rescued after a poachers’ steel trap caused a front-paw amputation. They described it as a possible world first. After evaluating and treating his painful neuroma, they plan to use a silicone prosthesis from AO Foundation in Germany and arrange a portable X-ray to minimize stress.

The 6-quart Instant Pot Ultra is on its first sale for $120 at Amazon and Sur La Table, down from $150. It adds customizable temperature, pressure, and time controls, nine presets, cooking-status information, and a quick-release button.

Leveraged ETFs use debt and financial derivatives to amplify the daily returns of an underlying index, commonly at 2:1 or 3:1 ratios or inversely. They magnify both gains and losses, and fees, transaction costs, daily rebalancing, and volatility decay make them generally unsuitable for long-term holding.

The passage presents leveraged ETF trading as a short-term strategy best suited to index speculation or capturing short-term momentum. Day trading is favored because it captures the day’s return without exposure to subsequent daily rebalancing; swing trading is another option. Holding periods should generally be only a few days.

Key risks include amplified losses during unfavorable market moves, potentially severe drawdowns, and heavy losses during prolonged bear markets. Risk-management methods include stop-loss orders, diversification across markets and ETF types, combining directional and inverse ETFs, and adjusting positions according to market conditions and volatility. ETF selection should consider the tracked index and its components, fundamental conditions, liquidity, fees, and risk-adjusted measures such as the Sharpe ratio, Jensen’s alpha, and appraisal ratio.

For U.S. citizens and residents, ETF profits generally receive the same capital-gain tax treatment as stock profits. Short-term profits are taxed at short-term rates, while profits held more than one year may qualify for lower long-term rates, though leveraged ETFs are generally not intended for such holding periods. Only net capital gains are taxed, and taxation varies by domicile.

The article’s example strategy produced an average trade gain of 1.25%, annual returns of 7.6%, an 18% maximum drawdown, and 100 trades while invested only 9% of the time. Applied to QLD, it averaged 2.25% per trade with 98 trades and 13.6% annual returns, slightly below QQQ’s 14.2% buy-and-hold return; QLD’s average gain was less than twice QQQ’s, likely because of time decay. The strategy lost more than 35% during the 2008–09 financial crisis. A less robust RSI strategy produced divergent results and a QLD maximum drawdown above 55%, illustrating that strong strategies can still generate psychologically difficult losses. The central warning is that leverage can be lethal when losses are magnified.

Former Trump aide Sebastian Gorka endorsed John McCann for New Jersey’s 5th district Republican primary, citing his loyalty to Trump and “America First” agenda. Across Phases 1 and 2/3, injection-site reactions within seven days of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2 were well tolerated and resolved shortly; most were mild or moderate, with injection-site pain most common. Systemic events were also well tolerated and short-lived, mostly mild or moderate; tiredness and headache were most common. Similar patterns occurred among Phase 3 BNT162b2SA and booster groups.

All tested 10-, 20-, and 30-µg doses of BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 in Phase 1 were well tolerated, except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of injection-site reactions or systemic events. The 30-µg BNT162b2 dose was selected for Phase 2/3. No Phase 1 participant left the study because of medical problems.

In Phase 2/3, 30 µg BNT162b2 was well tolerated. During blinded follow-up, 32 of 21,926 vaccine recipients and 36 of 21,921 placebo recipients left because of medical problems, each representing less than 1%. Most medical problems were mild or moderate, and most among vaccine recipients involved injection-site reactions or systemic events.

Serious medical problems were uncommon, with no single serious problem reaching 1% in Phase 2/3 groups. Researchers generally did not consider them vaccine-related, although some temporarily occurring cases among older vaccine and booster recipients were judged possibly related.

No Phase 1 participant died. During Phase 2/3, deaths occurred among 85 of 23,141 initial BNT162b2 recipients, 62 of 21,371 initial placebo recipients who later received BNT162b2, and 23 of 23,141 placebo recipients who never received BNT162b2. Researchers did not believe the deaths were caused by BNT162b2. No deaths occurred in Phase 3 among participants receiving BNT162b2SA without prior BNT162b2.

TLV321x/TLV322x comparators feature open-drain outputs that support logical ORing and logic-level translation. Outputs can be pulled up externally from 0 V to 5.5 V, independent of the supply voltage. TI recommends pull-up currents of 100 µA to 1 mA; smaller resistances speed rising edges but increase VOL and power dissipation, while resistances above 1 MΩ slow rising edges. Series current limiting is recommended if output shorts are possible. Unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−.

Internal ESD protection clamps signals to the supply rails, with input overvoltage limited to 0.2 V beyond them. Series input resistors are recommended for low-impedance sources, limiting clamp current to 10 mA or less.

An internal power-on reset holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses the 1.65 V VPOR threshold. The output then reflects the differential input once the supply reaches its minimum operating voltage and the delay ends.

A basic comparator compares VIN with VREF, producing a logic-low output when VIN is below VREF and logic-high when above it; swapping inputs reverses the polarity. Propagation delay differs for rising and falling input transitions, and smaller overdrive generally increases delay. Because the devices provide only 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis, external positive-feedback hysteresis can reduce chatter near the switching threshold. The passage describes three-resistor inverting and two-resistor non-inverting implementations and their trip-point calculations.

A low-side current-sensing example uses an amplifier to amplify a shunt-resistor voltage drop, with the comparator changing state at 1.1 V. Recommended layout practices include placing a 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitor close to the supply pin and ground, minimizing input/output coupling, placing input series resistors near the device, and optionally adding an output resistor below 100 Ω to damp ringing on long traces.
Zachary Steele was arrested after allegedly punching his father, stealing a vehicle and fleeing. A bean bag incapacitated him after he held a knife to his throat and threatened self-harm.

The Franklin County Court of Appeals reversed a judgment awarding Gail A. Erdy, Tamara D. Wolford, and Monica Jones $5,225 each for breach of contract. The plaintiffs had contracted with Paraprofessional Institutes of Ohio, whose assets were sold to Educational Leadership Corporation before classes began; the plaintiffs completed their training and were certified. ELC later sold the school’s assets to Technology Education Corporation.

On appeal, TEC argued that it was not liable for the claims because it did not expressly or implicitly assume ELC’s liabilities and was not a continuation of ELC. The court applied Ohio’s successor-liability exceptions and held that the incorporated asset purchase agreement excluded liabilities arising before the sale, including student-contract claims. TEC’s knowledge of the pending lawsuit did not establish implicit assumption because parties may allocate liabilities by contract and no bona fide-purchaser requirement applied. The record also did not establish that TEC was merely a continuation of ELC.

Finally, because this was a contract claim rather than a strict-liability case, the plaintiffs still had to prove the merits of their claims. The record contained little evidence beyond their allegations, and the matter had been resolved on TEC’s motion to dismiss. The judgment was therefore reversed and the case remanded.

Namibia’s defence minister said budget cuts and furloughs for thousands of soldiers are temporary cost-saving measures that preserve national security. Savings target utilities and prioritise training and transport; 70% of troops remain deployable, with recall procedures in place.

This continuation patent application describes endpoint-agent techniques for detecting and blocking ransomware before it encrypts important files. An endpoint agent using a filter driver monitors file-system activities, including file opens, metadata changes, writes, deletions, renames, and directory enumeration. For configured protected directories and volumes, it injects spoofed honeypot file and folder entries at the beginning and end of enumeration results and redirects attempts to open them to real decoy files or directories maintained on disk. This increases the likelihood that ransomware targets decoys first and allows detection of delete-on-close, deletion, rename, and write operations before genuine files are affected.

Policies can block the operation, terminate the associated process, alert users, and/or monitor and log activity. Protected paths, process exceptions, honeypot attributes, response settings, and user alerts are configurable through policies and graphical interfaces. Event reports may include the source process, process hash, attempted file paths, blocked operation, rename target, device and user information, versions, and critical SIEM severity. The agent also protects newly mounted volumes and can conceal virtual entries from interactive users. Windows embodiments use a mini-filter driver and I/O request callbacks, with corresponding implementations described for macOS, iOS, Linux, and other desktop, mobile, server, and cloud devices.

Jamie Dimon, JPMorgan's CEO and chairman and a longtime Bitcoin critic, said at the Fortune Most Powerful Women Summit that "blockchain is real," predicting stablecoins and the bank's deposit token will have real-world uses. He said decentralization complicates agreement on permissions and rules, which is why JPMorgan's Kinexys blockchain is private and permissioned, giving the bank control over who uses it and how. He said blockchain will replace some "clunky" systems that aren't 24/7, such as intraday repos, but cautioned it isn't the only solution and won't replace everything. Dimon declined to comment on Bitcoin, joking about headlines and death threats. JPMorgan uses Kinexys for client money movement and is developing an internal token, while the pro-crypto Trump administration has pushed Wall Street firms toward stablecoins pegged to the U.S. dollar, which could reduce fees and processing times.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson announced conditional support for federal media ownership reforms after the Coalition agreed to require greater ABC wage transparency, review its regional commitment, and provide an extra $12 million for community radio. The reforms would scrap the 75% “reach rule” and “two-out-of-three” ownership rule. Labor and the Greens oppose the changes, arguing they would weaken media diversity. The legislation was expected before Parliament that week.

The Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO), created by Tushar Chande in his 1994 book *The New Technical Trader*, measures market momentum by comparing the sum of recent higher closes with the sum of recent lower closes. It is calculated as 100 × (SHc − SLc) / (SHc + SLc) and ranges from −100 to +100. Positive and negative readings indicate strength or weakness relative to the prevailing trend. Readings above +50 are considered overbought, while those below −50 are considered oversold, though these signals are trend-dependent and can persist in strong markets. Bullish and bearish divergences between CMO and price swings may signal potential reversals. Traders may also add a nine-period moving average as a signal line.

CMO is generally used with trend indicators such as moving averages or trendlines to identify when a pullback is ending and to position for the next directional move. In sideways markets, it can support mean-reversion trades near support and resistance. Optimal periods and timeframes depend on the strategy and should be determined through backtesting.

A Python backtest using the SPY ETF, a nine-day CMO setting, and a five-day maximum holding period produced lower drawdown and a higher risk-adjusted return than buy-and-hold, although longer holding periods reduced returns. The CMO can suffer false signals and performs poorly in highly volatile, directionless markets because prices may spike without sustained momentum. It can be added to supported trading platforms directly or through a custom indicator.

The Nasdaq hit an all-time high, the Dow was on track for its best day since March 1, and all 30 Dow stocks rose. At 10:58 a.m. ET, the Dow gained 0.84%, the S&P 500 0.67%, and the Nasdaq 0.53%. Europe’s five largest economies warned that proposed U.S. tax legislation may violate international trade rules and unfairly benefit American companies. Germany, France, Britain, Spain, and Italy objected to House and Senate provisions taxing cross-border corporate payments and financial transfers, as well as a Senate measure that could subsidize U.S. exports. Republicans are working to reconcile the competing bills and deliver a final agreement to President Trump before Christmas.

Research Report Insights’ “Corrugated Packaging Market by 2020” predicts the global market will grow at a 4% CAGR from 2014 to 2020, reaching US$173.6 million in 2020. Growth drivers include e-commerce, rising population and incomes, increased shipments, and demand from medicine, rubber, food, consumer durables, and petroleum industries. Low costs, ease of handling, reliability, and sustainability support adoption. Packaging includes liner and container boards, sheets, and boxes in flute types A, B, C, E, and F. This study maps the intellectual structure and emerging trends in primary school science education research through bibliometric analysis. It addresses the fragmentation of research on inquiry-based learning, teacher development, STEM integration, and digital pedagogy, as well as implementation barriers including limited resources, inadequate teacher preparation, rigid curricula, and unequal digital access.

Using VOSviewer 1.6.20, the authors analyzed 2,295 peer-reviewed English-language articles from the Web of Science Core Collection, published from 1997 through December 31, 2024. Bibliographic coupling and co-word analyses identified influential works, scholarly networks, dominant themes, and research gaps; authors independently reviewed and reached consensus on cluster labels.

Bibliographic coupling produced five clusters: augmented and virtual reality with ICT; equity, engagement, and teacher competence; cognitive and metacognitive supports; dialogic and integrative pedagogies with teacher beliefs; and artificial intelligence, computer science, and computational thinking. Co-word analysis produced four clusters: dialogic argumentation, discourse, and scientific literacy; teacher beliefs, pedagogical knowledge, and professional development; achievement, engagement, and conceptual change; and computational thinking and technology integration in STEM. The results indicate a shift from content transmission toward inquiry-based, student-centered, digitally mediated, and equity-oriented science education, while highlighting persistent gaps in culturally responsive computational thinking and teacher identity.

Based on these findings, the study proposes DIG-EDU-QUEST, a framework combining culturally responsive inquiry, pedagogical practices, technological affordances, and sociocultural equity. It recommends inclusive digital integration, sustained teacher development, culturally responsive teaching, interdisciplinary curricula, and policy support for infrastructure and formative assessment. Future research should incorporate qualitative methods, broader and non-English databases, and further analysis of collaboration, geography, citation bursts, and global perspectives.

Ron Clark Academy students in Atlanta will use “Black Panther” and its comic books across subjects, including imperial history, African art, math, science, and gym. Teachers Wade King and Susan Barnes devised the curriculum connection, and the students reacted with dancing and excitement after the announcement.

Microbes are now recognized as essential to health, contributing to digestion, metabolism, immune responses, and inflammation, while disruptions in gut microbiota may contribute to conditions such as asthma, obesity, colitis, and colon cancer. Recent studies indicate that microbiota activity follows a daily circadian rhythm. In mice, microbial metabolites circulating in the blood altered the expression of liver genes and the liver’s circadian physiology. Antibiotics, altered feeding schedules, and time of day affected these patterns; acetaminophen overdose was less toxic at dawn and more toxic at dusk. The findings suggest that microbiota may help regulate the liver’s detoxification cycle and that medication timing could affect drug effectiveness and side effects, although broader human applicability remains to be established. Advances in DNA sequencing, analytics, and computing have made it possible to study diverse microbial communities, which function interdependently rather than as isolated species. The research may also be relevant to people taking long-term antibiotics or working night shifts, both of whom can experience metabolic changes associated with increased risks of obesity and metabolic syndrome.

Ahead of Theresa May’s formal Article 50 notification on March 29, sterling traded in a narrow range and modestly outperformed major peers against the dollar, reaching $1.2584. Analysts said the trigger would be largely symbolic, with the EU’s response and Britain’s economic health the main drivers. Stronger UK inflation and expectations of Bank of England rate rises supported sterling, while Brexit uncertainty, fears of a hard exit and possible Scottish independence referendum weighed on it. Retail customers buying euros for European property showed particular anxiety, while companies increased hedging.

Under GST, consignments valued above Rs50,000 generally require e-way bills once the central government notifies the provision and NIC software is ready. The GST Council exempted 153 items, including household LPG, kerosene, jewellery, currency, food products, animals, puja goods and contraceptives. E-way bills are unnecessary for non-motorised transport and certain customs movements. They are optional below Rs50,000, while conveyance details are unnecessary for intra-state transport under 10 km.

Integrating AI with multi-organ imaging genetics may advance precision medicine by introducing quantitative endophenotypes. Progress has been driven by large collaborative datasets, open access to GWAS summary statistics, and computational methods such as LDSC and Mendelian randomization, although some rely on sensitive assumptions. The genetic basis of AI-derived endophenotypes for pleiotropic disease endpoints remains largely uncharted. The authors previously developed 2,024 multi-organ AI endophenotypes—2,003 brain structural covariance networks, nine disease-subtype measures, and 12 biological-age gaps across nine organ systems—and released associated UK Biobank GWAS statistics through the MEDICINE portal. Using publicly available data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, this study aims to characterize the genetic architecture of these endophenotypes and 525 disease endpoints, benchmark multiple statistical methodologies, and compute SNP-based heritability.

Center for Diagnostic Imaging Miami offers diagnostic imaging and preventive screening services, including X-rays, PET and PET/CT, CTA, MRI and open MRI, ultrasound, 3D mammography, nuclear medicine, and full-body scans. Its Full Body Scan package uses high-resolution CT scans of major body regions, cardiac calcium scoring, and a physician consultation within 24–48 hours. These scans screen for conditions including cancer, heart disease, vascular abnormalities, lung disease, and organ abnormalities. CDI Miami also provides breast, ovarian, and prostate cancer screening, along with thallium stress, bone, and thyroid scans.

Police closed roads around the Cambridge Mill restaurant, where a man climbed onto the roof and chimney. Over four hours of negotiations, he smoked, read, and tossed items to the ground; some recovered items are being investigated as stolen. After becoming agitated and pacing the roof, he walked to negotiators and surrendered. He was taken to Cambridge Memorial Hospital for a mental health assessment, with charges pending. Energy Central Professional Dispatch for January 30, 2002, compiles 97 articles on electric power, gas, trading, regulation, corporate finance, and renewable energy. Much of the issue focuses on Enron’s collapse and aftermath. Enron named restructuring expert Stephen Cooper as acting CEO; congressional and regulatory investigations examined its accounting, lobbying spending, influence on energy policy and power prices, and Arthur Andersen’s role. Former employees sued over retirement-plan losses, while reports covered effects on employee 401(k) plans, public pension funds, Houston’s economy, and Enron Australia’s liquidation. President Bush and House Speaker Dennis Hastert supported Vice President Cheney’s refusal to release White House energy-task-force records as congressional inquiries continued.

Other power-industry developments included an agreement by NYISO and ISO New England to develop a common electricity market, a federal audit recommending an independent replacement for California’s electricity board, slowing power-project construction, transmission initiatives, and a new market-design forum involving MISO, PJM, and SPP. Trading, corporate, environmental, and international news included CFTC findings of no Enron futures-market manipulation, ICE plans for U.S. clearing and European power trading, utility earnings and rate cases, emissions legislation, wind and other renewable projects, nuclear-policy developments, and a planned $3 billion GMS Power investment in the Greater Mekong Subregion. The passage argues that existing federal and state employers’ liability laws are inadequate because workplace accidents and deaths are unavoidable costs of industry. The entire “risk of a trade” should fall on employers, who would incorporate compensation costs into prices and distribute them among consumers; federal coverage should include workers in navy yards, arsenals, and similar facilities.

It also supports compulsory government investigation of disputes between employers and employees. An impartial commission could promote conciliation and prevent strikes and lockouts, which reportedly caused $450 million in losses to employers and employees from 1881 to 1900, with further losses to the public. Commission decisions would not legally bind the parties but could shape public opinion and encourage settlements.

Massachusetts probation officials sought clarification of Michelle Carter’s stayed sentence, including probation sequencing and violation consequences. Convicted of involuntary manslaughter, Carter received 2½ years with 15 months suspended; a hearing is scheduled for August 21.

Quest Diagnostics grew from a New York pathology laboratory founded in 1967 into the largest U.S. diagnostic-testing company by revenue. After core business performance declined and UnitedHealthcare switched to competitor LabCorp, CEO Steve Rusckowski began a turnaround in 2012 centered on operational excellence, growth, organizational simplification, diagnostic services, and disciplined capital deployment. Quest competed through lower prices, an extensive testing and service-center network, and technology such as Care360, QuestConnect, and MyQuest.

Customer service had been consolidated in 2013 from 20 regional centers into two National Customer Service centers in Lenexa, Kansas, and Tampa, Florida, supported by approximately 250 remote representatives. The hurried transition left regional operating practices and incompatible systems in place, caused many experienced employees to leave, and produced inconsistent answers. The centers handled about 55,000 calls daily, 70% of them inbound requests for results. Customers often waited more than two minutes, representatives frequently transferred calls, and Quest was losing clients.

Employee turnover was especially severe in NCS. Sixty percent of new representatives left during their first year, and turnover across Quest cost an estimated $50–70 million annually. New representatives received six weeks of classroom training and were intended to shadow experienced colleagues, but understaffing often prevented this nesting. It took an average of 90 days after training to become productive. Representatives were evaluated on speed to answer, calls completed per hour, and attendance. Supervisors handled staffing, workforce planning, employee relations, and escalated calls, sometimes working 14-hour days, while unplanned absenteeism reached 12.4%.

MaryAnn Camacho joined in July 2015 as NCS executive director. She observed operations, interviewed staff, and listened to calls. Initial improvement efforts were narrowed to four priorities: introducing step-based pay tied to skills, creating career paths, strengthening supervisors, and developing coordinated workforce planning. Camacho concluded that additional changes were needed to reduce answer times, improve first-call resolution, and make NCS a more inspiring workplace, but had to decide whether to begin with operations, staffing and representatives’ work, employee compensation and retention, or several issues simultaneously.

After Hawaii’s king ratified a reciprocity treaty, he sent a commissioner to Japan to negotiate a commercial treaty. The U.S. minister at Honolulu opposed it, fearing reduced American trade and increased British competition. In 1868, President Johnson told the Senate that reciprocity would protect U.S. revenues and promote international goodwill until Hawaiians voluntarily sought admission to the Union. Annexation sentiment was growing in Honolulu, but Secretary Seward deferred consideration because of Reconstruction. U.S. protests against the importation of coolies did not halt the trade, which continued under British and other influences. In February 1871, Minister Henry A. Pierce urged renewed consideration of annexation, presenting it as Hawaii’s likely political destiny. President Grant transmitted Pierce’s dispatch confidentially to the Senate and requested its views without making a recommendation. The dispatch cited Hawaiians’ wishes, the declining native population, increasing foreign control, arguments for U.S. acquisition, Lord Palmerston’s opinion, and relevant Hawaiian history.

Clemson food scientist Paul Dawson found that double-dipped chips transferred far more bacteria than single-dipped chips: water exposed to a double-dipped chip had 1,000 more bacteria per milliliter. Double-dipped salsa had five times more bacteria than thicker chocolate or cheese dips, though its acidity lowered the count after two hours. Communal dipping can spread disease.

Kejriwal also sought Sibal’s apology; Amit Sibal had filed a defamation suit over allegations concerning a Vodafone tax demand.

- **UHS-II physical interface:** UHS-II standard-size card contacts and dimensions are defined in Figure 3-13 and the Mechanical Addenda. SD bus contacts 7 and 8 carry RCLK. In UHS-II mode, the card must not drive unused CLK, CMD, or DAT[3:2] lines; DAT[2] may instead serve as an interrupt line for UHS-II SDIO cards. The host must hold unused lines at defined levels, with implementation-dependent methods such as pull-ups for CMD and DAT[3:2] and driving CLK low. Unused lines must be set low before VDD1 is turned off for hibernation.

- **ROM cards:** ROM cards are read-only and exclude writable cards protected only temporarily or permanently. CMD24, CMD25, CMD27, CMD28, CMD29, CMD30, CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 are unsupported and illegal. CMD42 and security commands are optional; unsupported features must be indicated through the relevant CSD or SD status fields and treated as illegal. CMD42 support requires preset-password lock and unlock functions. ROM cards cannot write or erase protected areas, and full-size ROM cards have no write-protect switch.

- **UHS-I:** UHS-I provides up to 104 MB/s over a four-bit SD bus and supports DS at up to 25 MHz and 3.3 V, HS at up to 50 MHz and 3.3 V, SDR104 at up to 208 MHz and 1.8 V, and DDR50 at up to 50 MHz and 1.8 V. It applies to SDHC and SDXC, not SDSC. DDR50 is mandatory for microSD and optional for standard-size cards. The 104 MB/s maximum requires an SDR104-capable host and UHS104 card; otherwise performance is limited to 50 MB/s. UHS-I operates only in SD mode and only in four-bit mode. CMD0 initially selects SD or SPI mode, while ACMD41 negotiates 1.8 V signaling and CMD11 invokes the voltage-switch sequence. Once switched to 1.8 V, the card cannot return to SPI or 3.3 V signaling without a power cycle. CMD6 selects bus speed, driver strength, and current limit. CMD19 supplies tuning blocks for sampling-point adjustment; tuning is mandatory for SDR-VD hosts and optional for SDR-FD hosts, with 40 CMD19 executions required within 150 ms.

- **UHS-II:** UHS-II retains the SD bus modes and adds FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624 interfaces. At 52 MHz, their stated throughputs are 156 MB/s, 312 MB/s, 312 MB/s, and 624 MB/s respectively; HD312 is optional and cannot be used in ring topology. A UHS-II host must support both the legacy SD interface and UHS-II interface. After power-up, both card interfaces are enabled. The host supplies RCLK and STB.L to lane D0 and checks whether lane D1 changes from EIDL to STB.L; if this does not occur within the card-defined 200 µs period, initialization proceeds through the SD interface. UHS-II initialization comprises PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization. SD-TRAN encapsulates SD commands in UHS-II packets, and CMD0 restarts SD-TRAN initialization. The UHS-II interface is disabled before ACMD41 completion, and VDD2 must remain supplied if it was provided during SD-interface initialization.

- **Performance features and UHS-III:** Defined Application Performance Class thresholds include write performance of 500 IOPS and read performance of 1,500 IOPS, with sustained sequential writes of 10 MB/s; command queue and cache operation specify 2,000 write IOPS, 4,000 read IOPS, and 10 MB/s sustained sequential writes. Random performance uses 4 KB operations. Cache may use faster, potentially volatile memory, so cached data can be lost if not flushed before power-off. Self Maintenance permits internal background data management, while Command Queue supports voluntary task reordering and sequential execution. The low-voltage interface enables initialization using 1.8 V I/O instead of legacy 3.3 V I/O. UHS-III introduces FD624 at 624 MB/s and supports Ranges A through D, whereas UHS-II supports Ranges A and B.

- **Command framework and identification:** The host controls all communication using broadcast and addressed commands. Card identification mode uses only the command line and covers reset, voltage validation, card identification, and RCA publication. Data transfer mode uses point-to-point communication with one selected card. CMD0 resets a card to Idle and initializes a default RCA, 400 kHz clock, and default driver strength; in UHS-II mode, CMD0 preserves the Device ID rather than clearing the RCA to zero. CMD8 verifies operating voltage and communication using the voltage, CRC, and check pattern, and is mandatory before the first ACMD41 for SDHC or SDXC initialization. CMD55 must precede ACMD41.

- **ACMD41 and card identification:** ACMD41 communicates the operating-voltage window and Host Capacity Support through OCR. A zero voltage window performs an OCR query without starting initialization; a nonzero first invocation starts initialization, and subsequent invocations must use the same argument. The card completes initialization within one second, and the host repeats ACMD41 for at least that period or until ready. HCS indicates host support for SDHC/SDXC, while CCS identifies the card as SDSC, SDHC, or SDXC. Incompatible cards enter Inactive State. The host then issues CMD2 to obtain each CID and CMD3 to publish an RCA. SDXC initialization follows SDHC initialization and requires a user-area capacity of at least 32 GB.

- **Data transfer:** During identification, the host remains at the identification frequency; afterward it may use the performance frequency range. CMD9 retrieves CSD data, optional CMD4 configures DSR and changes the clock rate, and CMD7 selects one card for the Transfer State. Read and write transfers can be stopped with CMD12, and writes must be stopped before deselection. Buffered writes allow one block to be sent while another is programmed, with DAT0 indicating busy; CSD writes, write-protection operations, and erase do not support buffering. Parameter-setting and read commands are prohibited during programming, while CMD0 or CMD15 can terminate programming and may destroy data. ACMD6 selects four-bit bus operation but is rejected while the card is locked.

- **Blocks, writes, and erase:** Block-oriented transfers use CRC protection. The basic read-block unit is 512 bytes; CMD17 reads one block and CMD18 reads multiple blocks until CMD12. Misaligned partial blocks cause ADDRESS_ERROR and abort transmission. For block writes, CMD16 must set 512 bytes even when the CSD permits larger maximum lengths; smaller partial blocks are allowed only when WRITE_BL_PARTIAL is enabled. CRC failures discard the affected data. ACMD23 may pre-erase blocks before CMD25, while ACMD22 reports how many blocks were successfully written. CMD32 and CMD33 define an erase range for CMD38. DISCARD makes affected data unspecified and is supported only by SDHC and SDXC cards, with a 250 ms busy timeout. FULE logically erases the complete user area, has a one-second busy timeout, and is also limited to SDHC and SDXC cards. Both are unavailable through SPI.

- **Write protection and lock management:** The specification defines mechanical write protection, optional internal write protection, and password protection. Passwords are stored in nonvolatile 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers; COP cards may also use FEP and FEP_LEN. A set password causes automatic locking after power-up. CMD42 lock, unlock, password-setting, password-change, and password-clearing operations require a selected card in Transfer State. Incorrect passwords or invalid operations set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. Unlocking applies only to the current power session unless the password is cleared.

- **Card Ownership Protection:** COP protects cards against reuse without the designated password. When FEP is set, the card becomes COP-locked after reset and blocks ordinary CMD42 operations until CMD42[1Fh] unlocks the COP function set. CMD42 version 2.0 adds FEP management, protected force erase, and restrictions on resetting the PWD. Setting FEP disables ordinary Force Erase and PWD-reset operations. FEP Force Erase requires the matching FEP and erases the user area and PWD while retaining FEP; force erase does not erase the secure area. Locked cards accept basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, lock-related commands, CMD11, and CMD40, while other commands are illegal. Three lock-function card types are defined: Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 or COP.

- **Application-specific and switch commands:** CMD55 causes the following command to be interpreted as an ACMD. A defined, legal ACMD is handled as an application command; an undefined but legal ACMD is treated as the corresponding regular command. Illegal commands produce an Illegal Command Error. The listed proprietary ACMD numbers are reserved for manufacturer use. CMD6 has four function groups: access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. It is valid only in Transfer State and is mandatory for cards compliant with Physical Layer Specification 1.10 or later; hosts can check support through the SCR’s SD_SPEC field or CSD CCC bit 10.

Xiao Yan, a 23-year-old from Guizhou, China, was born with congenital melanocytic nevus. Doctors removed her painful facial mole after worrying it could become cancerous and used four expanding balloons to grow skin for grafting. She needs regular fluid injections, and five more months of treatment were planned. Her family supports her and is raising funds.
