President Donald Trump said his administration will use the ongoing government shutdown to permanently cut programs popular with Democrats but unpopular with Republicans, while blaming Democrats for the impasse. He did not identify the programs. The shutdown began Oct. 1 after Congress failed to pass appropriations. Republicans seek short-term funding, while Democrats demand additional health-care protections. The administration has frozen some infrastructure and climate funding and is considering canceling $12 billion in clean-energy earmarks.

Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 reported revenue of $5.985 billion, up from $4.541 billion, including automotive revenue of $5.132 billion, services and other revenue of $560 million, and energy generation and storage revenue of $293 million. Gross profit rose to $1.234 billion from $566 million, and operating income was $283 million versus a $522 million loss. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $16 million, or $0.09 per share, compared with a $702 million loss, or $4.10 per share, in the prior-year quarter.

At March 31, 2020, Tesla reported $37.250 billion in assets, including $8.080 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $4.494 billion of inventory, and $26.518 billion in liabilities. Stockholders’ equity rose to $9.173 billion. Operating activities used $440 million of cash, investing activities used $480 million, and financing activities provided $2.708 billion, including $2.309 billion of net proceeds from a February 2020 common-stock offering.

COVID-19 caused temporary production suspensions at Gigafactory New York, Fremont, Nevada and portions of Gigafactory Nevada, while Panasonic suspended Nevada operations for 14 days. These disruptions delayed vehicle deliveries and energy-product deployments and created uncertainty regarding estimates, demand and the pace of production resumption.

The company adopted the current expected-credit-loss standard on January 1, 2020, increasing its allowance for MyPower customer notes by $37 million. Net MyPower notes receivable was $358 million at quarter-end, with a $45 million allowance. Inventory increased as delivery and installation capacity was constrained. Current debt and finance leases totaled $3.217 billion and long-term debt and finance leases totaled $10.666 billion; Tesla remained in material compliance with its debt covenants.

The 2018 CEO performance award had achieved milestones of $20 billion in annualized revenue and $1.5 billion in annualized adjusted EBITDA, while $35 billion of revenue and $3 billion of adjusted EBITDA were considered probable. No market-capitalization milestone had been achieved, so no award shares had vested. The filing also described operating-lease commitments at Gigafactory New York and Shanghai and litigation involving the SolarCity acquisition, Model 3 production disclosures, the CEO performance award and a potential going-private transaction.

The Money Flow Index (MFI) is a 0–100 momentum indicator that combines price and volume data to measure money flowing into and out of a security, identify overbought and oversold conditions, and signal potential price reversals. It resembles a volume-weighted RSI and differs from Chaikin Money Flow, which uses price data and exponential moving averages.

The MFI generates overbought, oversold, and bullish or bearish divergence signals. The passage generally cites 80/20 as the standard thresholds, while also referring to 30 as an oversold level. Traders can use divergence trendlines and reversal signals, but should align signals with the prevailing trend. The default lookback period is 14 days; longer periods produce fewer signals, while shorter periods produce more signals, including more false ones. Optimal settings depend on the market and strategy and should be backtested.

A proposed strategy combines MFI overbought and oversold conditions with bullish and bearish engulfing patterns. Reported stock backtests were favorable: PEP produced 581 trades since 2000, a 71% win rate, a 1.8 profit factor, a 0.42% average gain, and a 10.4% annual return versus 9.8% for buy-and-hold. SPY returned 10.6% annually versus 9.7% for buy-and-hold, while a combined PEP/SPY portfolio returned 15% annually. Gold performed poorly, which the passage attributes to mean reversion being unsuitable for commodities. Overall, MFI can assist trade timing, but effectiveness depends on its application and backtesting.

The team stayed composed in a tight game. A lucky goal, after beating Tikkanen and deflecting the puck off Kolzig’s foot, gave Holmer an open net. They had a solid first period but couldn’t score again.

The Nanocrystal Glass Market report examines industry challenges, policies, production costs, manufacturing capacity, R&D, raw-material sourcing, and technology sourcing. It covers regional, type, and application-based production, pricing, sales, revenue, supply-consumption gaps, and import-export figures. It also profiles leading companies, provides distribution and contact information, and includes SWOT and new-project feasibility analyses. The market is segmented by product, region, and end use.

This study content-analyzed 273 modern physics education studies conducted in Turkey between 2000 and 2023 using the Modern Physics Education Publication Classification Form. Research peaked in 2019, with most studies published as Turkish-language articles. The most studied topics were atoms, the photoelectric effect, relativity, nuclear energy, the Compton effect, and Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle. Common objectives were evaluating instructional methods, materials, curricula, textbooks, and students’ cognitive and affective characteristics.

Quasi-experimental, descriptive survey, and case-study designs predominated. Studies generally used purposive sampling, education-faculty undergraduates, and samples of 31–100 participants. Interviews, tests, and questionnaires were frequent data-collection tools, while frequency/percentage analysis, t-tests, and content analysis dominated data analysis. Although interventions often improved achievement, knowledge concretization, problem-solving, and positive attitudes, classical-physics thinking and conceptual misconceptions persisted. Curricula and textbooks were criticized for insufficient attention to modern physics, unclear content, limited visual support, and poor alignment with students’ needs. Validity and reliability reporting and literature-supported discussions were often inadequate. Recommendations included using mixed and varied analytical methods, larger and more diverse samples, longer interventions, revised curricula and textbooks, simulations and interactive materials, stronger validity and reliability evidence, and further research on underexplored topics and participant groups.

The disclosure describes systems, methods, and storage media for automated recognition of objects in video or image content. A media device or media server receives content, selects frames according to an adjustable frame selection rate, partitions selected frames into image blocks, and uses machine-learning algorithms to identify regions containing objects. Likelihood metrics incorporating product and merchant information, algorithm error rates, and frame selection rates are compared with thresholds to determine whether recognition is accurate. Low-confidence regions undergo iterative, progressively focused analysis, while frame rates, partitions, and algorithm parameters may be adjusted manually, automatically, or through feedback from other devices and servers.

Recognized objects can be displayed to viewers and added to digital shopping carts containing descriptions, prices, availability, vendors, and related product recommendations. Shopping carts may be personalized using transaction, browsing, social media, and messaging data. The system may also use image matching, audio analysis, title profiles, viewer corrections, advertisements, and merchant links to support product identification and purchasing.

Employee recognition is crucial across industries: 49% of employees are dissatisfied with the recognition they receive, 69% would work harder if better appreciated, and 50% say manager thanks strengthen relationships. Altermagnetism is a compensated magnetic phase distinct from ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, characterized by spin-split bands and symmetry-protected nodal structures. This study combines group theory with density-functional calculations of real-space spin density to identify symmetry-allowed atomic magnetic multipoles, their relative phases, and their magnitudes. In MnF₂, antiparallel collinear dipoles cancel while in-phase octupoles establish d-wave altermagnetism; higher-order 32-poles also contribute. In CrSb, dipoles and octupoles cancel, making the in-phase collinear 32-pole the lowest uncompensated multipole and identifying it as a g-wave altermagnet. Symmetry-allowed noncollinear spin densities vanish without spin-orbit coupling, whereas symmetry-allowed noncollinear octupoles and 32-poles emerge linearly with SOC; collinear multipoles change only quadratically and minimally. Noncollinear components can therefore reveal altermagnetic multipoles more clearly than seemingly spherical collinear spin density. In KMnF₃, magnetic ordering combined with fluorine-octahedron rotations breaks anti-translation symmetry and induces altermagnetism, with an in-phase 32-pole proportional to the rotation angle. The results connect these multipoles to macroscopic response tensors, including piezomagnetism and second-order magnetoelectric effects, and show that noncollinear spin density, higher-order multipoles, SOC, and crystallographic symmetry are important for predicting altermagnetic behavior.

The study uses CiteSpace 6.2.R2 to analyze 2012–2023 literature on open and vocational education from CNKI and Web of Science, examining keyword networks, research-hotspot timelines, and citation bursts. The report defines a lipid profile as total cholesterol (TC), HDL cholesterol (HDL-C), triglycerides (TG), and LDL cholesterol (LDL-C). Hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia denote elevated blood cholesterol and triglyceride levels, respectively. HDL transports cholesterol from tissues to the liver, whereas LDL transports it from the liver to tissues; higher HDL and elevated LDL are associated with lower and higher coronary heart disease risk, respectively.

HIV/AIDS remains a major global health problem, including in Rwanda, where prevalence has been reported at approximately 3.2–3.1% among adults. Although antiretroviral therapy (ART) reduces HIV-related morbidity and mortality, HIV infection and ART regimens—including nevirapine, norvir, abacavir, lamivudine, and efavirenz—have been associated with lipid abnormalities and increased cardiovascular risk. Dyslipidemia is common among people living with HIV, while atherosclerosis and inflammation contribute to elevated cardiovascular disease risk. The study therefore aimed to assess cardiovascular risk by determining lipid profiles and their relationship with HAART among patients receiving ART at University Teaching Hospital of Butare (CHUB).

A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to February 2021 at CHUB in southern Rwanda. It included 199 participants: 150 HIV-positive patients receiving ART and 49 HIV-negative controls. Participants were recruited systematically. Those with hepatitis B/C, thyroid abnormalities, pregnancy, hypertension, kidney disease, diabetes, alcoholism, or obesity were excluded. Serum TC, TG, HDL-C, and LDL-C were measured using Cypress kits and a Humalyzer 3500 spectrophotometer. Data were analyzed in Excel and SPSS, with p-values ≤0.05 considered significant. Ethical approval and informed consent were obtained, and participant confidentiality was maintained.

Among the 150 ART-treated participants, 99 (66%) were female and 51 (34%) male; ages ranged from 29 to 75 years, with a mean of 49.4 years. Participants had received ART for more than one year: 108 were on first-line therapy, 39 on second-line therapy, and 3 on third-line therapy. Triglycerides were normal in 42%, borderline high in 26%, and high in 32%. LDL-C was normal in 84.6%, borderline high in 7.3%, and high in 8%. Total cholesterol was normal in 60.6%, borderline high in 24%, and high in 15.3%. HDL-C was above 60 mg/dL in 61.3%, 40–59 mg/dL in 19.3%, and 40 mg/dL or below in 19.3%.

Compared with controls, the ART group had significantly different lipid distributions for triglycerides (p=0.046), LDL-C (p=0.039), HDL-C (p=0.021), and total cholesterol (p=0.045). The authors concluded that ART-treated HIV patients had an increased prevalence of lipid abnormalities and recommended incorporating lipid-profile testing into routine biological assessment for cardiovascular risk, alongside tests such as troponin, creatine kinase-MB, CRP, and electrolytes. Further studies in other district and referral hospitals were recommended.

- **Ambassador pattern:** Sharded backends can be integrated with applications that expect a single storage endpoint by either embedding routing and a stateless load balancer in the sharded service or placing a single-node ambassador beside the client. The former simplifies clients but complicates service deployment; the latter simplifies the backend but adds client-side complexity. A client ambassador exposes a localhost endpoint, routes requests to the appropriate shard, and returns results, separating application logic from sharding logic. Kubernetes examples deploy sharded Redis or Memcached with StatefulSets and DNS Services, then configure twemproxy through a ConfigMap as the ambassador. A shared, replicated routing service is an alternative that reduces per-pod complexity but requires its own scaling and adds network latency.

- **Ambassadors for brokering and experimentation:** An ambassador can inspect the runtime environment and connect an application to the appropriate service, such as MySQL, while applications always use localhost. It can also split requests between production and experimental implementations, returning production responses while ignoring experimental ones. Nginx demonstrates this with IP hashing for consistent user assignment and a 90/10 production-to-experiment traffic split. Such functionality may run client-side or as a separate microservice, depending on usage frequency and operational preferences.

- **Adapter pattern:** Adapters modify an application’s interface to conform to a predefined convention without altering the application container. This supports consistent monitoring, logging, and health-check interfaces across heterogeneous or third-party software. Separate adapters can translate metrics for Prometheus, normalize application logs through Fluentd, collect Redis slow-query logs and Apache Storm data, or run rich database health queries through an HTTP endpoint. Keeping adapters separate enables reuse, independent upgrades, isolation of resource use, and avoids maintaining modified copies of externally supplied images.

- **Microservices and distributed patterns:** Single-node container groups are tightly coupled, while multi-node distributed systems communicate over networks with looser synchronization. Microservices divide an application into small, API-connected components that teams can deploy and scale independently. This improves agility and scaling but makes architecture, debugging, and failure diagnosis more difficult. Standard distributed patterns can reduce these challenges by documenting recurring communication and coordination designs.

- **Replicated stateless services:** Identical service instances sit behind a load balancer that may use round-robin distribution or session stickiness. Replication provides redundancy and horizontal scaling, while readiness probes distinguish running containers from instances prepared to receive traffic. Kubernetes examples deploy multiple instances of a Node.js dictionary service behind a Service. Session-tracked variants direct each user to one replica for in-memory caching or stateful interactions; IP hashing works internally but is less effective through NAT, while cookies are preferable externally. Consistent hashing minimizes user remapping when replica counts change.

- **Caching, rate limiting, and SSL:** A Varnish caching tier can avoid repeated backend work and improve request throughput and latency. Deploying it as a sidecar couples cache scaling to application scaling and wastes memory through duplicated content, so a separate replicated tier with fewer, larger cache instances is often preferable. Cookies or HTTP headers are needed to preserve session affinity through the cache. Reverse proxies can also enforce request-rate limits, return HTTP 429 responses, and report remaining quota. Because Varnish does not terminate SSL, a replicated Nginx tier can terminate HTTPS before forwarding traffic to the cache and application. The complete example therefore uses three replicated layers: Nginx for SSL termination, Varnish for caching, and the application tier.

- **Sharded services and caches:** Unlike replicated services, whose instances handle every request, shards each handle a subset, and a routing root selects the appropriate shard. Sharding primarily addresses state too large for one machine and permits data-oriented scaling. Replicated caches duplicate entries across instances, whereas sharded caches store distinct data and therefore use aggregate memory more efficiently. Shard failures can cause sustained cache misses, and cache hit rates materially affect capacity and latency, making testing with and without caches important. Replicating each shard improves failure tolerance, permits rolling upgrades under load, and allows overloaded “hot” shards to scale independently.

- **Sharding implementations:** Sharding functions commonly use a deterministic, uniform hash reduced with modulo. The selected key should group requests with equivalent responses without being unnecessarily specific: a path may suffice, while location-sensitive content may require country and path. Changing shard counts with modulo hashing can remap many keys and temporarily behave like a cache failure. Consistent hashing limits remapping during resizing. Kubernetes examples route Memcached or HTTP requests through twemproxy or Nginx using shard-specific DNS names. Sharding also applies beyond caching, such as grouping multiplayer game state by player location.

- **Scatter/gather:** A root simultaneously sends a request to multiple leaves, which return partial results that the root combines. This parallelizes mostly independent computation across machines and can reduce latency beyond the limits of a single processor. Term-based document search may divide words among leaves and intersect their result sets, while data-sharded search sends the request to every shard and unions their results. Added leaves eventually increase coordination overhead, and latency is determined by the slowest leaf. The straggler problem also affects availability because every leaf is required. Replicating each shard and load-balancing requests among healthy replicas improves reliability, upgrade safety, and scale.

- **Functions and event-driven processing:** Function-as-a-service is presented as an event-driven form of serverless computing, though serverless systems such as container platforms need not be event-driven and event-driven FaaS need not be serverless. FaaS shortens the path from source code to running service, automatically scales and restarts instances, and provides stateless, modular building blocks. Its forced decoupling complicates system-wide visibility, dependency tracing, debugging, and monitoring, making rigorous alerting essential. Bounded execution times make it poorly suited to generic long-running background processing, while loading large datasets into memory can increase request latency. Per-request pricing favors sparse workloads, whereas long-running services remain active and incur costs even when idle.

UTIs are common bacterial infections that may cause severe renal complications if untreated, and proteinuria is an important indicator of associated kidney damage. This open-blinded, cross-sectional study evaluated the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (P/C ratio) in adults aged 20–65 with symptomatic, drug-naive UTIs and suspected proteinuria at a diagnostic center in Bangalore, India.

Eighty patients were recruited by random sampling; 27 were excluded for urinary creatinine below 20 mg/dL and seven for absent proteinuria, leaving 46 participants. The final group had a mean age of 38.11 ± 7.3 years and included 31 women and 15 men. Urine specimens underwent microscopy for pyuria, culture and sensitivity testing, reagent-strip protein screening, sulfosalicylic acid protein quantification, and spectrophotometric creatinine measurement.

Using KDIGO P/C-ratio categories, 12 participants had Stage I proteinuria (<15 mg/mM creatinine), 16 had Stage II (15–50 mg/mM), and 18 had Stage III (>50 mg/mM). Mean P/C ratios were 9.0 ± 3.6, 30.4 ± 8.0, and 180.6 ± 142.9 mg/mM, respectively. Urinary creatinine was significantly lower across all stages than the reference interval (p<0.001), although it did not significantly differentiate the UTI stages. Stage III participants had markedly elevated urinary protein (48.5 ± 46.0 mg/dL) compared with the reference interval (9.0 ± 2.6 mg/dL; p<0.001).

The findings indicated an association between proteinuria and UTI severity and supported the P/C ratio as a convenient marker for identifying and monitoring UTI-associated renal impairment. Longitudinal studies were recommended to assess its prognostic and therapeutic value.

The message briefly records objections to a returned appropriations bill and promises fuller discussion of the constitutional questions it raises. It argues that the Constitution grants the federal government only enumerated powers and does not authorize a general system of “internal improvements.” Because the phrase is undefined and could encompass roads, canals, bridges, education, hospitals, libraries, and other national activities, it cannot supply an independent grant of power. Neither the preamble nor the general-welfare clause creates such authority, and federal ownership of public property permits only improvements necessary to administer that property.

Other enumerated powers—war, navy, army, post roads, commerce, and territorial authority—may support particular projects when those works are necessary to exercise the granted power, but they cannot justify an expansive federal improvement program. Such a program would entail enormous expenditures, expand federal patronage, burden the Treasury and public debt, and displace state legislation and private enterprise. The constitutional clause concerning federal districts and purchased sites likewise depends on a separate, enumerated power to acquire the property.

The message distinguishes federally supported aids to navigation from broader river and harbor improvement. Congress has long funded lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and public piers, which mark obstacles and make navigation safer, whereas dredging channels or constructing harbors alters waterways and belongs to the disputed general-improvement question. Statutes of 1789 and 1845, sustained by Supreme Court decisions, place salt- or freshwater seas, lakes, and rivers under federal maritime jurisdiction when navigable by vessels of specified size and used in foreign or interstate commerce. Although this statutory standard is variable, it applies to inland waters as well as coastal waters.

Because no fixed rule divides national from local river and harbor improvements, the executive must exercise caution, especially when spending is justified chiefly by commercial revenue rather than military or naval needs. The message endorses President Jackson’s practical guideline of limiting appropriations to places below established ports of entry, while acknowledging congressional discretion. It also recommends requiring permanent federal harbor works to be accompanied by cession of the land and jurisdiction, considering each project in a separate bill, and limiting federal appropriations to works necessary to exercise unquestionably constitutional powers. Other improvements should remain with private enterprise or the states, which may finance them through their own resources or authorized tonnage duties.

The disclosure describes autonomous vehicle systems that use a machine-learned yield model within a yield controller and motion-planning system. Perception and prediction systems use sensor and map data to identify objects, determine their states, and forecast their movements. Features describing objects—such as relative position and path, required acceleration or deceleration, traffic-signal timing and locations, and predicted traffic gaps—are provided to the model. The model, which may use tree-based, ensemble, or neural-network methods, outputs whether to yield or proceed, stops the vehicle, or selects and scores gaps for unprotected turns.

Gridlock analysis may be performed independently or combined with gap analysis to prevent an autonomous vehicle from entering or blocking a congested intersection. The motion planner incorporates yield decisions into cost functions, gap penalties, and trajectory generation, then optimizes motion plans that either traverse a selected gap or stop before the conflicting area. Vehicle controls execute the selected plan.

The yield model can be trained using real-world or simulated driving logs labeled manually or through scoring functions, including comparisons between gap trajectories and stop plans. The systems may operate onboard an autonomous vehicle or divide model use and training between onboard and remote computing systems. Claimed benefits include fewer hand-crafted rules, easier retraining and localization, rapid and low-latency decisions, lower memory requirements, improved safety and comfort, and better scalability and adaptability.

Justice Nganjiwa lost his bid to stay proceedings in his EFCC trial over alleged $260,000 fraud and N8.6 million corrupt enrichment. His lawyer argued that, pending an appeal, the lower court should refrain from continuing the case.

A study in Nature Communications found that two grape-derived compounds, dihydrocaffeic acid and malvidin-3′-O-glucoside, promoted resilience against stress-induced depression-like behavior in mice. DHCA modulated inflammation, while Mal-gluc affected synaptic plasticity. Researchers said the compounds may eventually help treat depression and anxiety in some people.

Japan’s Financial Services Agency said it had long warned Coincheck about network weaknesses before hackers stole $530 million in NEM cryptocurrency. The regulator conducted a surprise inspection after imposing a business improvement order and requiring all Japanese cryptocurrency exchanges to report on system risk management.

The FSA cited Coincheck’s use of a “hot wallet” rather than a more secure “cold wallet,” its lack of multi-signature security and its unauthorized pending-registration status. Inspectors reviewed customer compensation, finances, system management and consumer protection.

Coincheck has said it will repay approximately 46.3 billion yen ($425 million), though the FSA has not confirmed it has sufficient funds. Police and regulators in several countries are investigating the theft.

The incident has intensified scrutiny of Japan’s cryptocurrency regulation and fintech ambitions. Other exchanges have suffered major hacks, while Bitcoin fell sharply amid regulatory concerns and a Facebook advertising ban.

A May 20, 2001 digest covers U.S. energy policy, Texas electricity deregulation, Qatar’s gas-export plans, and the Enron-backed Dabhol Power project.

- **U.S. energy policy:** The Los Angeles Times says the Bush administration’s plan responds to projected rapid growth in electricity use by promoting natural gas, nuclear power, expanded exploration and pipelines, and modernized transmission infrastructure. Coal currently supplies 52% of U.S. electricity and natural gas 16%; gas is projected to reach 33% in 20 years, while coal’s pollution and carbon dioxide emissions are expected to reduce its relative role. The policy could lower natural-gas prices, sustain exploration and production, increase imports, and generate investment and construction work.

- **Political and industry disputes:** The Washington Post reports that converting the plan into legislation will pit coal utilities, electricity marketers, public-power providers, cooperatives, regions, and environmental groups against one another. Disputes include environmental enforcement, utility mergers, state authority over transmission lines, creation of a national electricity grid, and repeal of the Public Utility Holding Company Act. The plan may provide relief to older coal plants, drawing opposition from environmental groups and eastern natural-gas utilities. Enron chairman Kenneth Lay advocates deregulation and open grid access, while Southern Co. has resisted opening its regulated markets. The utility industry contributed $18.9 million to political parties and candidates in the previous election.

- **Texas pilot:** Texas’s residential electricity deregulation pilot began slowly. ERCOT delayed the start to July 6, and only 21% of available statewide residential slots had been filled, compared with 45% in Houston. Officials cited consumer confusion, inertia, comparisons with California’s crisis, and the expectation of lower summer bills; commercial enrollment was stronger. Full deregulation was scheduled for January 1, with a 6% “price-to-beat” rate reduction for many residential and small-business customers, a provider of last resort, and expectations that the retail market would eventually consolidate.

- **Qatar:** Qatar’s energy minister said gas-export talks with Kuwait and Bahrain were progressing, including consideration of about one billion cubic feet per day for Kuwait. He said he had received no official confirmation that Enron was withdrawing from the Dolphin project and hoped to sign a production-sharing agreement before September. He also said OPEC was unlikely to change production at its June meeting and favored a $25-per-barrel price.

- **Dabhol Power:** Enron-sponsored Dabhol Power Company served a preliminary termination notice on the Maharashtra State Electricity Board concerning the $2.9 billion power-purchase agreement. DPC blamed failures to honor offtake commitments and obtain central assistance, rejected Maharashtra’s Rs. 402 crore penalty notices, and left room for continued discussions. Lenders were deciding whether to authorize termination proceedings. India’s central government sought to limit its exposure, while Maharashtra officials reviewed strategic options. DPC sought continued purchase of both project phases, totaling 2,184 MW, and central guarantees for any replacement buyer.

A federal judge indicated she was “99 percent sure” to dismiss mail fraud charges against Dallas County Commissioner John Wiley Price even if a jury convicted him, reducing his potential sentence from up to 20 years to three to five years for the remaining bribery and tax-related counts. Devon and Cornwall Police was charged under the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974 over Thomas Orchard’s 2012 death in custody. Studies summarized in the passage indicate that near work—such as reading or using computers, televisions, and smartphones—is not an important cause of childhood myopia. In a 20-plus-year study of 4,979 children, greater outdoor exposure was associated with a reduced likelihood of developing nearsightedness and needing corrective lenses. For children with two nearsighted parents, low outdoor time raised the estimated risk of needing glasses to about 60 percent; roughly 14 hours outside each week lowered it to about 20 percent.

Outdoor time had little or no effect on prescription changes in children already nearsighted. The leading proposed mechanism is that brighter outdoor light stimulates retinal cells to release dopamine, slowing abnormal eye growth. Other possibilities include exercise and increased vitamin D from ultraviolet exposure.

Myopia typically begins in early elementary school, can require lifelong glasses or contact lenses, and may increase the risk of retinal detachment or degeneration later in life. Regular childhood eye examinations are important. Because ultraviolet exposure can harm skin and eyes, the passage recommends sunscreen and sunglasses alongside outdoor activity.

At the signing of the Americans with Disabilities Act, the president praised the bipartisan coalition that made the legislation possible. He described it as a landmark civil-rights measure promoting equality, independence, and access for 43 million Americans with disabilities. Its provisions prohibit employment discrimination, require access to public accommodations and transportation, and mandate equivalent telephone services for people with speech or hearing disabilities. He called on society and businesses to remove physical and social barriers, cited children with disabilities playing alongside volunteer buddies in Little League, and rejected concerns that the law was vague or excessively costly. He then signed the act, declaring that the “wall of exclusion” was finally falling.

The lecture introduces link-cut trees for maintaining dynamic forests of rooted, unordered, potentially unbalanced trees. Updates include creating a tree, linking the root of one tree as a child of a node in another, and cutting a node from its parent. Queries can find a node’s root and aggregate weights along root-to-node paths, such as minimum, maximum, sum, or product. The goal is \(O(\log n)\) time per operation. Link-cut trees were originally developed to accelerate network-flow algorithms.

The represented tree is decomposed into preferred paths determined by the most recent access within each subtree. Each preferred path is stored as an auxiliary splay tree keyed by depth, so an in-order traversal recovers the path. Auxiliary-tree roots store path-parent pointers identifying the parent of a path’s top node in the represented tree. Together, these structures form the tree of auxiliary trees.

The central operation, access, makes the root-to-node path preferred and moves the accessed node to the root of the tree of auxiliary trees. It splays the node, separates its former preferred continuation, then moves upward through path parents, switching preferred children and merging auxiliary trees while preserving path-parent information.

Other operations reduce largely to access. Find-root accesses the requested node, finds the leftmost node of its auxiliary tree, and splays it. Path aggregation accesses the node and computes an aggregate maintained in its auxiliary tree. Cut accesses the node and detaches the portion containing its ancestors. Link accesses both endpoints and connects the resulting auxiliary trees.

A preliminary analysis gives \(O(\log^2 n)\) amortized time per operation because each access performs one splay per preferred-child change. Heavy-light decomposition defines an edge as heavy when the child’s subtree exceeds half its parent’s subtree; each node has at most one heavy child, and any root-to-node path contains \(O(\log n)\) light edges. Counting light preferred-edge creations and heavy preferred-edge destructions bounds total preferred-child changes by \(O(m\log n)\) for \(m\) operations.

Using the weighted splay access lemma, with a potential based on subtree sizes in the tree of auxiliary trees, the splay costs within an access telescope to \(O(\log n)\) plus the number of preferred-child changes. This yields \(O(\log n)\) amortized time per operation. A worst-case variant instead maintains heavy-light decomposition with weight-balanced trees, but its operations are more complicated.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 18, 2018, disclosing its 2017 Letter to Shareholders under Item 7.01. The letter, attached as Exhibit 99.1, accompanied the company’s annual report for the year ended December 31, 2017. The filing was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky.

The paper examines how early-stage startups develop Internet-of-Things systems, addressing the research question: “How do startups develop their Internet-of-Thing systems in their early-stages?” It frames IoT development as interdisciplinary, requiring software, hardware, electronic, and domain expertise, and notes that existing methodologies lack empirical validation for startup contexts. Related work covers digital startup classifications, Minimum Viable Products, the three-layer IoT architecture—perception, network, and application—and adaptations of Agile methods to embedded systems.

An exploratory multiple-case study used purposive sampling. Eight IoT startups were selected from 241 candidates, based on having at least two full-time members, operating for at least six months, having a running prototype, and deriving their core value proposition from IoT products or services. Data came from 12 semi-structured interviews with CEOs, CTOs, and hardware engineers, along with company documents and publicly available information. Thematic analysis was organized around the SEMAT Essence elements of Team, System, Work, and Way of Working. The cases covered aquaculture monitoring, connected cameras, an underwater drone, shipment tracking, muscle-operation measurement, smart homes, and a smart wheelchair; seven startups were early-stage and one was more mature.

Teams were a central factor in development. Most internal engineering capability centered on software, while six of eight startups relied on external consultants, component or cloud providers, and manufacturers. Missing internal expertise created dependencies on external parties. Teams also needed product-design, hardware, electronic, finance, and marketing capabilities.

The systems implemented startups’ value propositions through Internet-centric services using and analyzing sensor data, Thing-centric hardware offerings, or combinations of both. Development generally began at either the application or perception layer.

The study identified three progressively more capable MVP types. Type 1, “looks-like,” reproduced the final user experience while functionality was performed manually, often using mock-ups, wireframes, and 3-D printing; it supported ideation, design, and presentation and was frequently discarded afterward. Type 2, “functional works-like,” demonstrated core functionality through hardware design, sensor integration, backend development, and operation with real data. Type 3, “quality works-like,” emphasized nonfunctional qualities such as performance, scalability, security, and integrated hardware-software testing. All cases began with Type 1, generally progressed to Type 2, and sometimes reached Type 3. The transition from Type 2 to Type 3 shifted effort from hardware toward software, data visualization, processing, and quality attributes.

Common working practices combined in-house design with outsourced implementation and manufacturing, rapid prototyping, reuse-oriented development, and Agile or iterative methods. Local contractors accelerated experiments and made activities easier to scale down when funding or direction changed, while manufacturing was commonly planned in China. CAD tools and 3-D printing enabled rapid physical prototyping. Startups reused commercial or open-source components, including Arduino, Raspberry Pi, and third-party sensors, and frequently reused software. Hardware iterations required longer than software iterations, and frequently shipping physical products was costly; consequently, Types 2 and 3 often changed little after their initial design. Agility was associated with limited upfront planning, short-term evolution, rapid time to market, collaboration, and frequent workarounds.

The discussion notes that focused hardware research and experimentation can suit waterfall-like methods, but hardware-software co-design and integration lengthen prototyping cycles. Outsourcing hardware can reduce early effort while introducing vendor, platform, and competence dependencies. Agile practices were not applied systematically; instead, IoT MVP development resembled software-startup development through iterative, opportunistic work and workarounds. Limitations include sparse interviews, possible coding bias, and a sample restricted mainly to Pakistani and Scandinavian early-stage startups with bootstrap financing, limiting direct generalizability.

The study concludes that IoT startups evolve MVPs while combining diverse internal and external competencies, rapid prototyping, reuse, outsourcing, and iterative development. It identifies these practices as a foundation for methodologies that accommodate both startup conditions and the hardware characteristics of integrated IoT systems, and recommends broader comparisons with practices such as Lean startup and studies involving more varied cases.

Its customizable cash-back card includes a $200 bonus, 6% back in a selected category during the first year, 2% at grocery stores and wholesale clubs, and 1% elsewhere. Fixed rates remain relatively stable and require notice before changes, while variable rates generally follow the Prime Rate. Promotional periods commonly last six or 21 months at rates from 0% to 3.99%, after which a regular variable APR may apply. An investigation found that about 30% of Scotland’s A-roads and 35% of B-roads needed repair or inspection between 2015 and 2017, compared with 3% of A-roads and 5% of minor roads in England, though data collection differed. Around 2,220 km of A-road and 2,571 km of B-road required attention. Scotland spent £657.61 per head on local roads and £621.46 on national roads, above UK averages of £436 and £312. Argyll and Bute had the highest repair proportion at 45%, followed by the Western Isles at 44%, while West Lothian recorded 18%. Experts attributed poorer conditions to cold, wet weather. Politicians said council maintenance budgets had fallen 21% since 2011, while the Scottish Government cited increased trunk-road funding and major infrastructure projects.

All women have postpartum bleeding after vaginal delivery or C-section because the placenta site continues to bleed and shed tissue (lochia) until it returns to its pre-pregnant state. In the first days after a C-section, bleeding resembles a heavy period, with some passing small clots; it lightens daily and resolves within four weeks. Call a physician if bleeding lasts beyond six to eight weeks, if you soak a pad hourly for two hours, pass large clots, or show signs of a low blood count (racing heart, shortness of breath, dizziness). A fever over 100.4°F also warrants contacting a doctor. Because a C-section is major surgery, the APA advises low activity, avoiding lifting more than your baby and most housework, staying hydrated, eating healthy meals, and avoiding tampons, douching, baths, pools, hot tubs, exercise, sex, and stairs.

An American Psychological Association study of 2,324 university students in eight countries found that people who experienced more of the emotions they desired reported greater life satisfaction and fewer depressive symptoms, whether those emotions were pleasant or unpleasant. Participants generally wanted more pleasant and fewer unpleasant emotions, but 10 percent wanted more anger, hatred or similar feelings, while 11 percent wanted fewer transcendent emotions such as love and empathy. Published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, the study was the first to identify this relationship for unpleasant emotions. Researchers cautioned that the results show association, not causation. The study examined only unpleasant “negative self-enhancing” emotions, so future research should test fear, guilt, sadness and shame. Links between desired emotions, personal values and cultural norms were not directly examined.

The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) is a price-based momentum oscillator that compares a security’s current price with its average price over a specified period. High readings may indicate overbought conditions, while low readings may indicate oversold conditions. Its formula uses the typical price, calculated from the high, low, and close, together with a moving average and mean deviation.

CCI was developed by Donald R. Lambert in 1980 for commodities but is now used across financial markets. It can identify trends, cyclical reversals, and bullish or bearish divergence, although divergence may only serve as a warning rather than a reliable reversal signal. Conventional thresholds are above +100 and below -100, but traders should examine each security’s historical readings because reversal levels vary.

The article recommends using CCI on daily charts with a short lookback period, generally 5–9 periods, primarily for stocks and bonds. A SPY backtest used a 9-day lookback, bought the CCI at -90, and sold when the close exceeded the previous day’s high. It produced a profit factor of about 1.8, an average gain per trade of 0.55%, and a 23% maximum drawdown, though the results may be susceptible to curve fitting.

CCI’s advantages include identifying extreme price conditions and producing quantifiable results. Its limitations include being a lagging indicator, providing limited help with market timing or trend detection, and potentially remaining overbought or oversold for long periods. Similar indicators include RSI, Rate of Change, Stochastics, and MACD.

The Second Circuit reversed and vacated a preliminary injunction entered in Jackson Dairy’s diversity action against H. P. Hood & Sons. Jackson was Hood’s exclusive distributor of “Schedule 3B” products in a Vermont–New Hampshire territory. Hood began supplying Grand Union and First National Stores directly from warehouses outside that territory, and the chains shipped the products to their retail outlets within Jackson’s territory, bypassing Jackson.

The court held that preliminary injunctive relief requires irreparable harm—harm inadequately compensable by money—plus either a likelihood of success on the merits or sufficiently serious merits questions and a balance of hardships favoring relief. Jackson’s claims of lost profits and disruption of delivery routes were readily compensable in damages, and the contract’s termination-notice provision did not make customer losses noncompensable. Accordingly, the injunction was vacated.

Judge Mansfield concurred, preferring reversal because Jackson had not shown a meritorious basis for relief: the contract did not obligate Hood to police its customers outside the territory, and there was no evidence that Hood controlled, instigated, or participated in the chains’ transshipments.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended September 24, 2016. The company, a California corporation founded in 1977 and headquartered in Cupertino, designs, manufactures and markets mobile devices, personal computers, portable media players, software, services, accessories and digital content. Its offerings include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple Watch and Apple TV; iOS, macOS, watchOS and tvOS; iLife and iWork; the iTunes Store, App Store and other content stores; Apple Music; iCloud; AppleCare; and Apple Pay. It also supports third-party developers through its developer programs and Xcode.

Apple’s strategy centers on integrating its hardware, operating systems, applications, services and digital-content distribution. It sells directly through retail and online stores and a direct sales force and indirectly through carriers, wholesalers, retailers and value-added resellers. Its reportable segments are the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. In 2016, direct channels represented 25% of net sales and indirect channels 75%; international sales represented 65% and domestic sales 35%. Customers include consumers, small and mid-sized businesses, education, enterprise and government markets, and no single customer accounted for more than 10% of net sales during 2016, 2015 or 2014.

The company faces intense competition, pricing pressure and rapid technological change. Risks include economic weakness, dependence on resellers and third-party developers and content, inventory and purchase-commitment risk, component shortages and price increases, reliance on outsourced manufacturing concentrated primarily in Asia, product-quality issues, intellectual-property litigation, regulatory and international risks, retail-store costs, acquisitions, system failures, cybersecurity and privacy threats, key-personnel dependence, natural disasters, foreign-exchange movements, credit exposure and tax changes. Substantially all hardware manufacturing is outsourced, manufacturing purchase obligations generally extend up to 150 days, and R&D expense was $10.0 billion in 2016, $8.1 billion in 2015 and $6.0 billion in 2014.

As of September 24, 2016, Apple owned 7.1 million square feet and leased 22.3 million square feet of building space, primarily in the United States, and owned 2,583 acres of land. It employed approximately 116,000 full-time equivalent employees. Management stated there was no reasonable possibility of a material loss beyond recorded accruals for asserted legal claims, although litigation outcomes remained uncertain; certain matters settled in the fourth quarter of 2016 had no material impact.

Apple’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under “AAPL.” It paid $12.0 billion in dividends during 2016 and $11.4 billion in 2015, expected to pay $0.57 per share quarterly subject to board declaration, and planned annual dividend increases subject to the same approval. Its repurchase authorization increased from $140 billion to $175 billion in April 2016; $133 billion had been used by September 24, leaving $42 billion available. The company also reported 5,332,313,000 common shares outstanding as of October 14, 2016.

Personal trainer Liz Letchford says eccentric exercises—slow, controlled movements performed while muscles lengthen—build strength but can cause significant soreness by creating muscle damage. Examples include slowly lowering from a pull-up and six- to eight-second negative push-ups. She says stronger muscles increase the body’s energy demands and calorie use, and that a “long, lean” appearance comes from strength training rather than hypertrophy, combined with a healthy diet. She also says women generally lack the testosterone needed to become bulky without an extreme training, diet, and supplement regimen.

Streptococcus pneumoniae commonly colonizes healthy people but can cause invasive disease, including bacteremia, meningitis, osteomyelitis, and septic arthritis, particularly among children, older adults, and susceptible populations. In China, six serotypes—3, 6B, 14, 19A, 19F, and 23F—mainly caused invasive pneumococcal disease in children and adults. Although PCV13 and PPV23 are available, neither is included in China’s national immunization program, and uptake remains low. Sinovac developed a preservative-free PPV23, approved in 2020 for people aged two years and older, especially high-risk groups. A phase 4, randomized, double-blind, noninferiority trial initiated at the NMPA’s request compares its immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety with Pneumovax in Chinese children, adults, and elderly populations (NCT05477693).
