IDC’s December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers in industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland found that HPC, simulations, modeling, and data analytics are increasingly essential for product development, manufacturing, supply-chain and sustainability optimization, and digital products and business models. HPC-as-a-service (HPCaaS) can improve scalability and agility without major upfront infrastructure investment; 81% of respondents already implementing HPC intend to develop HPC-based business models. However, cloud-based HPC still requires skilled personnel to configure, operate, program, and analyze it. IDC recommends establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, ensuring lifecycle transparency and a common data source, selecting an HPC operating model based on utilization, budget, performance, security, and skills, prioritizing scalable, secure, and energy-efficient solutions, and seeking external expertise when needed.

Inflation is a broad, gradual rise in prices that reduces a currency’s purchasing power and is measured using a weighted basket of goods and services. Its major causes include growth in the money supply, excess demand, higher production and wage costs, and expectations that prices will continue rising.

High inflation is generally unfavorable for stocks in the short term. It increases market volatility, reduces consumer spending and money available for investment, raises corporate costs, and may lead central banks to increase borrowing costs. Value stocks tend to perform better as inflation rises, while growth stocks with high price-to-earnings ratios tend to underperform. Dividend-paying stocks may also decline if dividends fail to keep pace with inflation. In the long term, companies may pass higher prices to consumers and resume their upward trends.

Inflation can reduce the real value of savings, benefit borrowers through repayment with less valuable money, and benefit lenders through higher interest rates. Real estate values may increase. Suggested investments during rising inflation include index funds, stocks, bonds, commodities, gold, real estate or REITs, and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS), which are presented as government-backed inflation hedges.

A 60-year S&P 500 backtest that used inflation to determine interest rates and interest rates to value stocks produced poor performance, ending with less money than the initial investment and supporting the conclusion that high inflation hurts stocks in the short term.

The coach said his team won many games and played consistently throughout the year, despite perhaps remaining under the radar. He praised acquisitions Mike Commodore and Cory Stillman as Stanley Cup–experienced, easygoing and well-liked teammates who became major contributors. Commodore has been a defensive mainstay alongside Bret Hedican and is popular with the organization and fans. Stillman was described as a quietly valuable player and the team’s leading playoff scorer; he was seventh in league scoring when acquired and remained effective despite injuries.

He expressed pride as a U.S.-born coach and called John Tortorella excellent, crediting him with helping make Tampa Bay competitive. He also cited his parents’ character, high-school coach Bob Luccini’s competitiveness, Tim Taylor’s hockey knowledge and Bobby Francis’s preparation and player management as key influences, saying coaching systems evolve through adjustment.

An unnamed defenseman was praised for overcoming injuries, reaching top form, and contributing leadership, experience, speed and two-way play.

The message transmits to the Senate a treaty signed with Nicaragua for construction of an interoceanic canal, explaining that such a waterway was essential to connect the Atlantic and Pacific coasts, strengthen national unity, commerce, and defense, and provide shorter shipping routes between the United States, Europe, and Asia.

The treaty would preserve Nicaraguan sovereignty and rights, while stating that the United States sought no territorial acquisition or political control. Nicaragua would provide the territory and the United States the funding. The canal would be open to all nations on equal terms, with preferential treatment reserved for the two countries’ coastal trade. Its protection would also address security concerns. A railway and telegraph could be constructed as supporting infrastructure.

The proposed route would use Lake Nicaragua, requiring six locks at the Pacific end and five at the Atlantic end. Total canal excavation was estimated at 43½ to 53½ miles, with 119 miles of lake and river navigation. The lake’s fresh water, depth, length, and harbors were presented as favorable, and a dam on the San Carlos River would extend navigable water toward the canal.

The message emphasized substantial travel-time savings, expanded trade, lower transportation costs, and broader commercial and national benefits. It also argued that the canal would attract investment, support repayment of a four-million-dollar loan to Nicaragua, and become a major route for world trade. The work could, it asserted, be completed more cheaply and effectively by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

Kimberly A. Rupp, a Lackawanna County Prison counselor, faces a misdemeanor retail theft charge for allegedly leaving a Dickson City Walmart without paying for $206.77 in merchandise. She was also charged with third-degree felony retail theft for attempting to steal $3,194 in jewelry and clothing from Kohl’s. Rupp was released on $10,000 unsecured bail.

Foreign investors recorded net ADX purchases of Dh406 million in January 2017, with purchases of Dh3.13 billion exceeding Dh2.723 billion in sales. The ADX general index rose 0.03%, led by investment and financial services (18.07%). Market capitalization fell 1.32%, while traded value reached Dh7.741 billion across 61,907 deals involving 57 companies.

Lake Louise ski resort pleaded guilty to two federal charges after employees cut endangered whitebark pines along a ski run, an incident revealed in 2013. Sentencing arguments, which will consider expert testimony on the number of trees destroyed and environmental impact, were delayed seven months because earlier court dates were unavailable due to a clerk shortage. The Crown alleges at least 39 whitebark pines were felled. A six-day sentencing hearing is scheduled to begin July 9. Maximum fines are $300,000 per tree under the Species at Risk Act and $250,000 under the Canada National Parks Act.

This systematic review examines bibliotherapy—using books to help readers address problems—in educational settings. It distinguishes developmental bibliotherapy, which supports students’ development without requiring psychological or behavioral difficulties, from therapeutic bibliotherapy, which targets mental health concerns. Bibliotherapy involves interaction among the reader, the reading process, and the text, with principles including identification, catharsis, insight, and universalization. Forms include cognitive bibliotherapy using self-help or nonfiction texts, affective bibliotherapy using fiction or poetry, group reading, writing-based activities, and online book platforms. Historically, reading was used as therapy from ancient times; the term first appeared in 1916, and developmental applications expanded during the 1930s and 1940s.

Following PRISMA-P and PICO, the review searched ERIC, Elsevier, Research Gate, and Google Scholar for English-language, peer-reviewed studies published from 2006 to 2021. Thirty-five articles using quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods were included; methodological variation prevented meta-analysis. Findings were organized into five themes. Practitioners reported benefits but limited awareness and formal training, along with constraints involving time, resources, student reluctance, reading difficulty, and boredom. Bibliotherapy generally reduced aggression and social anxiety, encouraged appropriate social and cooperative behavior, and improved emotional awareness, particularly among children with autism or emotional and behavioral disorders. Academic benefits included improvements in reading comprehension, vocabulary, writing, articulation, English language, and mathematics. Studies also found significant improvements in self-esteem, hope, and resilience. For mental health outcomes, bibliotherapy reduced anxiety and depression, with mixed findings for stress, and enabled students to discuss traumatic experiences without directly treating their effects.

The review concludes that bibliotherapy may support socio-emotional, academic, and psychological goals in education, but evidence remains limited. Many studies had small samples or covered few institutions, methodological and intervention details were sometimes unclear, and geographic variation may have introduced cultural differences. Careful book selection, practitioner training, clearer reporting, and a unified practice framework are needed.

The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ekiti State nominated Chief Adebisi Adegboyega Egbeyemi as its deputy governorship candidate to pair with former Governor Kayode Fayemi in the July 14, 2018 election. The JKF Campaign Office said party leaders selected Egbeyemi after prolonged meetings and public speculation about the ticket.

A lawyer and former Executive Chairman of Ado-Ekiti Local Government, Egbeyemi studied Biology, Physical Education and Law before being called to the Nigerian Bar in 1981. His political career included service in the Ondo State House of Assembly, leadership of the Unity Party of Nigeria and United Nigeria Congress Party, a cancelled House of Representatives election, and appointments as Commissioner of Education and Commissioner for Justice and Attorney General. He later joined the Action Congress and became a leading APC figure in Ekiti State.

Huawei aims to become the world’s top PC vendor within five years, citing PC market recovery, nearly $19 billion in cash, a large smartphone and server customer base, and extensive retail and service channels. TBR says Huawei could gain share from HP, Lenovo, and Dell. Challenges include U.S. espionage concerns and securing channel partners with established vendor relationships.

The team adjusted its lines, stayed physical, and focused on its game plan after falling behind two games. Despite limited production and unfavorable bounces, the team settled down, controlled the puck, and generated power-play opportunities through confident play. The speaker emphasizes continued hard work, sustained pressure, and staying focused for the next game rather than celebrating the win.

Jurors convicted Joseph Percoco on three counts—two for conspiracy and one for solicitation of bribes—over allegations that he sold his governmental influence. COR Development’s Steven Aiello was acquitted of bribery but convicted of conspiracy; Joseph Gerardi was acquitted, while the jury deadlocked on CPV executive Peter Galbraith Kelly Jr., accused of disguising bribes through payments to Percoco’s wife. Defense attorneys planned to seek further review, including a motion to set aside Aiello’s verdict. Sentencing is scheduled for June 11 for Percoco and June 14 for Aiello. Gov. Cuomo said he respected the verdict and called for stronger safeguards to protect public trust.

The paper proposes Virtual Node-based Heterogeneous Graph Convolutional Network (VN-HGCN), which learns long-range dependencies without predefined meta-paths. It augments a heterogeneous graph with randomly connected type-level virtual nodes and a central virtual node that links the type-level nodes. This structure allows any two original nodes to communicate through a path of length four, regardless of their original distance. At each of four layers, VN-HGCN transforms node types into a shared semantic space, performs node-level aggregation using normalized adjacency matrices, and applies attention to combine intra- and inter-type information. Drop-edge is used to reduce overfitting, and the model has time complexity of \(O(N|A|(|V|+|E|))\).

Experiments on node classification over ACM, DBLP, and IMDB compare VN-HGCN with metapath2vec, HAN, MAGNN, HGT, HetSANN, SimpleHGN, and ie-HGCN across training ratios from 20% to 80%. VN-HGCN performs best in most settings, particularly with limited training data, while recursively aggregating models generally outperform meta-path-based approaches. Adding virtual nodes to ie-HGCN improves its performance at lower training ratios and increases its sensitivity to perturbations from nodes several hops away, supporting improved long-range message passing.

Parameter analysis on IMDB shows that VN-HGCN is robust to hidden-layer dimension and the number of type-level virtual nodes. Performance improves from two to four layers but declines beyond four, consistent with over-smoothing; the authors state that whether over-smoothing is fully mitigated remains unresolved. The paper also presents VN-HGCN’s virtual-node strategy as a general framework that can be integrated into existing heterogeneous graph models and identifies scalability, additional tasks, and dataset-dependent virtual-node counts as future research topics.

Postoperative hyperglycemia is common after cardiac surgery and is associated with infections, acute kidney injury, arrhythmias, longer hospital stays, and mortality. Protocol-based insulin titration often fails to accommodate rapidly changing patient conditions and individual variability, contributing to hyperglycemic and hypoglycemic episodes.

The study developed GLUCOSE, a distributional offline reinforcement-learning model that recommends personalized hourly regular insulin doses during the first 24 hours after cardiac surgery. The model combined conservative Q-learning with Implicit Quantile Networks, enabling it to represent the distribution of potential outcomes and associated uncertainty. It evaluated more than 70 clinical features hourly, including glucose history, demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, vital signs, medications, mechanical ventilation, and SOFA score. Recommended doses were rounded to whole units and capped at 10 units per hour.

Using MIMIC-IV for development and eICU-CRD for external validation, the study included 6,148 and 649 patients, respectively. Among 200 trained models, the selected model had significantly better estimated performance than clinician dosing in both datasets. Glucose time in the target range of 70–180 mg/dL was highest when clinician-administered doses matched GLUCOSE recommendations and declined as the dosing difference increased. SHAP analysis identified current glucose, recent glucose values, weight, and mechanical-ventilation status as important model inputs.

In human evaluations, GLUCOSE’s hourly dosing had lower mean absolute error than observed clinician dosing in both datasets: 0.90 versus 1.97 units internally and 1.90 versus 2.24 units externally. Differences from senior and junior intensivists and nurse practitioners were not statistically significant, but GLUCOSE showed a trend toward lower error than junior clinicians and nurse practitioners. A blinded expert panel rated GLUCOSE’s regimens as comparable to or better than all human policies for safety, effectiveness, and acceptability.

For eICU patients excluded because of ambiguous medication records, model action distributions remained similar to the main validation cohort, with average dose differences below half a unit and considered clinically insignificant. Limitations include the retrospective design, validation only during the first postoperative day, no explicit dietary input, and exclusion of patients with incomplete medication documentation. Prospective studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to confirm effectiveness and safety in diverse clinical settings.

SimulRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation framework for grounding LLMs in long-form scientific question answering. It introduces a generalized simulator retrieval interface that uses a question and simulator handbook to extract parameters, convert them to JSON, execute the simulator, and transform outputs into textual context through templates. Its claim-level generator produces multiple answers, decomposes them into atomic claims, deduplicates the claims, and selectively verifies and updates them using simulation evidence.

The framework combines uncertainty estimation with simulator boundary assessment (UE+SBA) to limit verification to uncertain claims that fall within simulator operating boundaries. Closeness centrality in answer–claim entailment graphs estimates claim confidence, while GPT-4o assesses boundary compatibility. Verified claims are retained if aligned with simulation output, revised if contradicted, or left unchanged if indeterminate. High-confidence claims are then assembled into the final answer.

The authors created long-form QA benchmarks for climate modeling and epidemiology using a CMIP6-trained climate emulator and the GLEAM-AI influenza emulator. Each benchmark contains 200 free-form questions; ground truths were derived from simulator outputs and verified by human domain annotators. Experiments with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet showed that SimulRAG outperformed adapted RAG baselines by an average of 30.4% in informativeness and 16.3% in factuality. UE+SBA consistently surpassed random, verbalized-uncertainty, and uncertainty-only selection across F1, AUPR, and AUROC at 15%, 25%, and 45% verification budgets, with AUPR and AUROC improvements reaching 6.2% and 6.3%. Simulator boundary assessment filtered an average of 34.5% of climate claims and 41% of epidemiology claims. With 15% verification, SimulRAG outperformed no-RAG generation, while 45% verification produced results comparable to verifying all claims. The main limitation is that questions are assumed to relate to available simulators; future work could automatically detect question–simulator relevance.

The speaker urges Congress to complete the United States’ postwar readjustment by creating a new social and economic order rather than restoring prewar conditions. Despite progress in reconstruction, unemployment, strikes, agricultural distress, and industrial conflict continue to hinder recovery. Government relief and wider credit have helped farmers, but Congress should permanently expand credit through the Farm Loan Bureau, provide production and livestock credit suited to agricultural turnover, increase land-loan limits, and pursue broader transportation improvements.

Transportation is presented as a national necessity that is inadequate and becoming more inadequate as population and freight traffic grow. Railroads should be coordinated with coastal shipping and inland waterways, while motor trucks should serve as railway feeders rather than competitors supported by public highways. Railway managers should improve cooperation through pooled freight cars, interchangeable equipment, terminal efficiency, and consolidated facilities. Government ownership is rejected as a solution; instead, managers must find economies while maintaining fair returns. The partisan Railroad Labor Board should be replaced by an impartial labor division within the Interstate Commerce Commission, composed of representatives from the country’s rate-making territories. Negotiations should handle ordinary disputes, while a government tribunal should resolve public-interest matters and have enforceable decisions, preserving fair wages and working conditions without allowing strikes to paralyze essential service.

The speaker also supports flexible tariff adjustments to protect American industry and consumers while encouraging trade. Domestic policy priorities include stronger enforcement of Prohibition through state and federal cooperation, registration of immigrants, overseas examinations before admission, expanded opportunities for immigrant education and Americanization, and federal assistance to local schools. Constitutional amendments are proposed to authorize regulation of child labor and to limit tax-exempt securities and public borrowing.

Congress should also approve reclamation and irrigation projects, forest protection and replanting, and further study of fuel, consumer prices, and cooperative marketing and purchasing. A completed survey of power resources in the eastern industrial region could support unified power distribution and substantial freight savings, while a proposed survey of national resources would prepare the country for possible future defense needs without expressing fear of war.

Internationally, the United States should use its position as a creditor nation to encourage reconstruction, trade, currency stabilization, peace, and international understanding without seeking dictation or permanent control of other nations. The speaker favors respecting national rights, consultation, and arbitration over armed conflict; supports the Washington Conference’s naval limitation policy and the Four-Power Pact; and rejects both commercial isolationism and any supergovernment or armed-alliance commitment incompatible with American traditions.
Officials report an aggressive fox near Wood River Road showing possible rabies signs. People should avoid it, keep dogs’ rabies vaccinations current, and report it to ADF&G in Dillingham.

Morgan Stanley expects a middling outcome for FAANG stocks (Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Alphabet) in 2018, following their strong 2017 gains that helped drive the market to repeated records. The five stocks accounted for about 27.5% of the S&P 500's market-cap growth, the third-highest bull-market concentration in 20 years, and it is rare for a year's leaders to repeat. Still overweight the group, citing substantial competitive moats and intact secular growth, the bank warns of macro risks, exposure to consumer spending and advertising, and questions whether growth over value can remain a meaningful driver of returns. It sees wide outcome ranges—for Amazon, nearly 10% in the base case and over 70% in the bull case.

Federal agents searched Cleveland City Hall, seizing records tied to city engineering manager Khalil Ewais’s side business, Pioneer Engineering, projects on three avenues, and paving contractor Burton Scot Contractors. Authorities, citing an ongoing investigation, did not disclose the search’s purpose.

Ewais resigned in 2015, citing low pay and expanded duties, then rescinded after officials promised hires and considered restructuring. In a 2017 audit questionnaire, Ewais said he had no business dealings or financial interest involving the city, though he had said Pioneer would not interfere with his city work. He was scheduled to seek approval for Pioneer to pave two parking lots at Assad’s Bakery properties. Burton Scot, awarded at least $7.4 million in city paving contracts, said it would answer investigators.

An analysis found that 92.45% of 2023–2024 campaign contributions from lawyers and staff at 100 top-grossing firms and 50 large plaintiffs-side firms went to Democrats, a roughly 12-to-1 ratio that increased from 6-to-1 in a 2017–2020 analysis. The group contributed about $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups and $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Cleary Gottlieb, Fried Frank, and Mintz Levin had the highest percentages of Democratic contributions, while Nelson Mullins, Lewis Brisbois, and Ogletree Deakins had the lowest among top-grossing firms.

An October 25, 2001 email circulated Arundhati Roy’s essay “Brutality smeared in peanut butter,” arguing that the U.S.-led bombing of Afghanistan should stop. Roy criticizes the invasion’s lack of a UN mandate, dismisses the bombing as another act of terror, and questions the coalition’s record of war, weapons sales, and support for authoritarian regimes. She describes civilian casualties, food shortages, unsafe aid deliveries, Northern Alliance advances, and fears of a humanitarian crisis. She also warns that retaliatory violence fuels terrorism and hatred, that surveillance threatens civil liberties, and that governments are exploiting public fear. The essay links the conflict to defense and oil interests, including weapons manufacturers, energy companies, and regional pipelines, criticizes restricted war reporting, and urges readers to reject militarized and propaganda-driven responses.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed an order granting Annetta Gibson specific performance of her property settlement with former husband Max Gibson and requiring him to pay her attorney fees and costs. Their agreement required Max to provide insurance securing maintenance payments after his death and prohibited him from impairing that security. Although they substituted whole-life insurance for term insurance, the court found Max’s trust provision allowing him to borrow against or use the policies’ cash value could defeat the agreement’s purpose.

The court rejected Max’s arguments that the judgment altered the agreement, that Annetta enforced a different agreement, and that Platte County lacked venue because the parties had contractually designated the dissolution court to enforce the settlement. It also found that a claim against Max’s estate was not an adequate legal remedy and that Max’s failure to perform entitled Annetta to contractual attorney fees and costs.

USD/CAD remains range-bound at 1.2968–1.3211 with neutral intraday bias. A break above 1.3387 targets 1.3598; below 1.2968 turns bearish. The rise from 1.2460 is corrective within the decline from 1.4689; breaking 1.2460 targets 1.2075. Above 1.3838 could signal reversal.

The lecture examines taint tracking for Android security, focusing on TaintDroid. Android permissions grant access to devices or resources but do not express restrictions on transmitting particular sensitive data, allowing apps to exfiltrate contacts, phone numbers, location, IMEI, and credentials. Simply preventing apps from accessing both sensitive data and the network is impractical because it breaks legitimate apps and fails to address side channels, app collusion, or tricks that induce other apps to disclose data. Malware may also track users, steal credentials, impersonate them, or turn phones into spam bots.

TaintDroid assigns taint labels to information sources such as GPS, other sensors, contacts, and IMEI data, and monitors how those labels propagate toward network sinks. It uses 32-bit vectors, supporting up to 32 distinct sources, and combines labels with bitwise operations according to Dalvik opcode semantics. Arrays, IPC messages, and files receive single aggregate tags, producing conservative rather than fine-grained results. Taint metadata is stored alongside Java locals, arguments, object fields, static fields, and arrays to improve cache efficiency. Native methods require manually defined policies because their internal behavior is generally invisible to the Dalvik interpreter.

At network interfaces, TaintDroid can block data carrying taint, alert the user, or redact sensitive portions. Evaluations found apps sending location, phone numbers, and other data to servers without clearly disclosing those practices in their licenses. Reported overhead was approximately 3–5% additional memory and 3–29% additional CPU usage.

The system primarily handles explicit data flows and does not fully capture implicit flows through branches or hidden behavior inside native code. Proposed program-counter tainting could address some branch-based leaks but may over-taint results. Lower-level x86 or ARM tracking offers broader coverage and can support offline audits, but is costly, difficult to implement correctly, and can cause “taint explosion.” Scanning outputs for sensitive patterns is insufficient because encoding or compression can evade it. Richer label systems can support programmer-defined policies and compile-time leak detection, although runtime enforcement failures may themselves become covert channels.

For legacy C or C++ programs, the lecture introduces TightLip. It creates scrubbed copies of sensitive files and runs a “doppelganger” process using the altered data in parallel with the original process. Divergence in system-call behavior, especially an attempted network transmission, indicates that sensitive data influenced the process. TightLip requires accurate per-file-type scrubbers and kernel support; faulty scrubbers may cause crashes or allow leaks to go undetected.

The passage outlines a “Box & One—Chase” offense designed to counter a defense that denies an outstanding player the ball. The star can be freed by isolating him in the middle, where the chaser’s limited post defense can be exploited against multiple outside feeders. Primary options include shuffle-cut entries, screen-and-roll, back screens, and give-and-go actions, with weak-side two-game or single/double continuity following failed feeds. Success requires coordinated movement, defensive recognition, communication, timing, varied entries, and attacking weaker defenders. The Box & One defense uses four players in a box zone and one “Chaser” responsible exclusively for aggressive pass denial and preventing rebounds.

At Suzuka, conditions were dry and nearly sunny, though damp patches remained after earlier rain. During the sole practice session, Fernando Alonso received a 25-place grid penalty following an engine change after a hydraulic leak was discovered in his power unit; Carlos Sainz and Valtteri Bottas also incurred grid penalties.

Alonso led the opening laps, while Gasly set the first time. Hamilton and Bottas soon traded the lead on soft tires, with Bottas posting the session’s quickest time. Bottas later ran wide at Spoon and struck the barriers, damaging his front wing and right-rear area. The session was red-flagged, his damaged floor compromised the rest of his running, and Mercedes confirmed his entire right rear required repair.

Raikkonen then crashed at Degner, suffering significant right-side damage and prompting another red flag. Magnussen’s car was worked on after a hydraulics issue, while Vettel and Ricciardo ran wide and Sainz missed a red light.

Bottas finished fastest, ahead of Hamilton, Vettel, Verstappen, Ricciardo, Ocon, Hulkenberg, Alonso, Perez and Palmer. Ferrari used the latter part of the session for qualifying simulation.

The 52-week high is the highest daily closing price a stock reached during the preceding 52 weeks. The 52-week low is its lowest closing price over the same period; intraday breaches that do not close beyond these levels do not alter the range. The high and low form resistance and support levels within the annual price range.

The 52-week high is used in technical analysis to assess a stock’s position and calculate its percentage below the high: (Current Price − 52-Week High) ÷ 52-Week High. It is also viewed by some traders as a sign of bullish sentiment. Breakouts beyond the range may attract buying or selling interest and are sometimes accompanied by increased trading volume.

The 52-week high investment strategy buys stocks trading near their annual highs, contrary to the conventional “buy low, sell high” approach. Academic research cited in the passage found that stocks closer to their 52-week highs generally produced better subsequent returns than those farther away.

Backtests covered individual stocks and the S&P 500, using SPY as an index proxy. One cited momentum backtest reportedly beat the S&P 500 over two decades, while the article’s simpler moving-average and crossover strategies produced equity curves described as difficult to trade and not worth further attention. The authors suggest these index results may not reflect the cited individual-stock research because the S&P 500 is weighted toward large companies.

According to a New York Times report, Rose McGowan settled with Harvey Weinstein for $100,000 in 1997 after a hotel-room incident, without admitting harassment. The report also detailed Ashley Judd’s allegations; Weinstein subsequently took leave from his company.
The Department of Energy approved nearly $67 million for 85 nuclear research projects at university and government laboratories to promote safety, efficiency and U.S. energy independence.

The Patient Charter, also known as the NHS Constitution, combines patients’ legal rights, NHS commitments beyond the law, and patient responsibilities. It covers free care at the point of use, with some exceptions, equal access, waiting-time standards, safe professional care, continuous quality improvement, access to NICE-recommended medicines and vaccinations, consent, privacy, treatment choice, and transparency when errors occur. Patients may complain, seek Ombudsman intervention or judicial review, and claim compensation for negligence. They are expected to look after their health, respect staff and other patients, follow treatment plans or discuss difficulties, and participate in vaccination and screening. Overall, the Charter presents the NHS as a partnership based on fairness, trust, accountability, and shared responsibility.

Registered dietician Samantha Rigoli says fruit is nutrient-dense and rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and phytonutrients, and should be eaten daily. Though higher in carbs and natural sugars, it is not comparable to calorie-dense foods like cookies. She recommends considering glycemic index and food quality.

Lorna Gibson concludes a lecture by reviewing biomimetic and biologically inspired lightweight structures. Examples include wood-derived silicon carbide replicas, fiber-reinforced 3D-printed honeycombs, foamed-metal coatings and implants resembling trabecular bone, synthetic and natural tissue-engineering scaffolds, lightweight sandwich panels, and palm-inspired density gradients in concrete. She also discusses plant stems, porcupine quills, hedgehog spines, toucan beaks, feathers, and engineered mimics that combine dense outer shells with foam or honeycomb cores. These structures use dense outer shells with foam or honeycomb cores to resist wrinkling and buckling efficiently while remaining lightweight, strong, and stiff.

The remainder is a course review. Gibson discusses the Wednesday test, allowing one 8.5-by-11-inch cheat sheet, and identifies key formulas for open-cell foams and honeycombs. She answers questions about a bicycle-helmet energy-absorption problem involving polymethacrylate foam, normalized peak stress, strain rate, and energy absorbed, and explains how stress-strain, energy-absorption, density, and strain-rate graphs are constructed. She also clarifies idealized aluminum-foam curves, including elastic, stress-plateau, and densification regions, and how transition points can be calculated without explicitly finding strain. The test will cover foam thermal conductivity, trabecular bone, sandwich panels, and energy absorption. She also announces a future lecture about becoming a professor and considers organizing similar talks by other MIT faculty.

California’s recreational marijuana launch has been hindered by a complex regulatory system, slow licensing and heavy local taxes. Recreational dispensary sales totaled $339 million through February 2018, below state expectations, while experts estimated 85–90% of the existing industry remained unlicensed. Municipal licensing failures and bans in 85% of cities and counties limited legal retail coverage, sustaining black-market demand. Taxes layered throughout local supply chains produced effective rates near 80%, raising prices and reducing retailer profitability. Experts said earlier legal markets offered useful lessons; Colorado’s tax revenue initially fell below projections before later exceeding them.

This case-control study aims to analyze long COVID epidemiology and risk factors among healthcare workers at Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein in São Paulo, Brazil. Long COVID comprises new, returning, or ongoing health problems occurring at least four weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection and may follow mild or severe illness. Vaccination has been associated with symptom improvement and lower prevalence, although some vaccinated individuals remain susceptible.

Adult healthcare workers with RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 between March 1, 2020, and July 15, 2022, were evaluated over 180 days. Cases had compatible symptoms lasting more than four weeks without an alternative diagnosis; controls recovered within four weeks. Symptoms included general, respiratory and cardiac, neurological, digestive, and other manifestations. Symptomatic workers received free institutional testing, four vaccines were available, and diagnosis used nasopharyngeal specimens and specified RT-PCR kits.

HeartLands Conservancy is gathering community input for the Cahokia Creek Watershed Planning project, which will create plans for the Indian Creek and Canteen Creek watersheds in western Madison County to address stormwater, flooding, and water quality. Open houses in Edwardsville and Glen Carbon identified priority projects and focus areas, including flooding-prone areas, inadequate stormwater infrastructure, pollution, mining subsidence, and recreational and wildlife concerns. Input will help guide infrastructure and land-management efforts and support funding. The project is part of Madison County’s stormwater management planning and is led by HeartLands Conservancy with Madison County and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

The passage compiles November 22, 2001 media reports on Enron’s financial crisis, its proposed acquisition by Dynegy, and the effects on employees, creditors, assets and financial markets.

Enron’s 401(k) plan was severely affected by the company’s stock decline, which had erased 94 percent of its value. More than half of the plan’s $2.1 billion in year-end assets was invested in Enron stock, and assets were frozen on October 17 as financial problems became public, preventing workers from changing investments. Employees at Portland General Electric lost substantial savings, and nearly all company stock options were reportedly worthless. A class-action lawsuit alleged that Enron violated fiduciary duties by promoting its stock as a retirement investment and freezing the plan before accounting disclosures. Enron said most Enron shares in the plan were employee-selected and that the freeze resulted from a previously planned administrator change.

Enron closed at $5.01, down 28 percent and more than 94 percent for the year. Lenders postponed a $690 million repayment to mid-December, and Enron tapped the remaining $450 million of a $1 billion credit line. The company was negotiating to restructure $9.15 billion in debt due by the end of 2002. Credit-rating agencies kept its rating one step above junk because a downgrade could trigger immediate repayment of $3.9 billion. Fitch said bankruptcy was highly possible if Dynegy abandoned the merger, while Goldman Sachs downgraded the shares and questioned whether the proposed cash infusion could restore trading-partner confidence.

Dynegy continued due diligence on its roughly $9 billion all-stock takeover and said it was encouraged by Enron’s financing progress, but officials considered possible renegotiation. At the same time, they noted no legal grounds for unilateral termination and concern that renegotiation could further undermine confidence. Trading partners were reducing exposure and demanding more collateral, while investors discussed possible equity investments in Enron pipeline assets. Enron’s cash reserves, debt burden and reduced transaction activity remained major obstacles.

The reports also described asset sales and business reviews. Enron Japan was considering retaining, selling or partly selling its operations amid pressure on Enron bonds held by Japanese investors and money-market funds. Enron’s 65 percent stake in India’s Dabhol Power project might sell for below $700 million following payment defaults. At least four financial institutions expressed interest in buying Wessex Water, though Enron could face a $650 million charge if its water holdings lost substantial value. Portland General was also being sold to raise cash.

Enron’s bonds and partnership securities fell sharply, with major investors including Prudential and Pimco among those holding Osprey Trust bonds. Analysts warned that a failed Dynegy acquisition could push bond prices below 50 cents on the dollar and raise broader market concerns.

Broader U.S. markets declined for a second day as investors took profits and questioned the sustainability of a recent rally, despite improved jobless-claim and consumer-sentiment data. The Dow fell 0.7 percent, the S&P 500 0.5 percent and the Nasdaq 0.3 percent, with weakness led by technology stocks.

A 10-year-old PGI school student reported an alleged abduction attempt by youths in a black car near a Vekra Booth. Police responded, but no complaint was filed and a precautionary DDR was lodged; local residents said they saw no attempt. Central Alabama is under a flash flood watch until 7 p.m.; saturated ground and heavy storms could flood creeks and streams. Showers and thunderstorms are possible today. **Summary**

This article (United Soccer Coaches, *Soccer Journal*, May/June 2021) explains how soccer coaches should prepare players for varying field conditions, which occur even at the highest levels, and how to inspect fields before each match to identify hazards or determine unplayability.

**Field surface:** Artificial turf produces faster ball pace and requires lighter ground passes; it can become very hot, requiring hydration, shorter warm-ups, monitoring for heat exhaustion, and judicious substitutions. Fields with high crowns can hide the ball from players near one sideline, who should move toward midfield; balls rolling down a crown can gain speed. Infill (crumb rubber, cork) sticks to sweaty skin and should be ignored unless near the eyes, where it must be addressed by a coach or trainer. Natural ground may be hard, soft, or suitable, which determines cleat choice and prevents slippage; balls bounce higher and farther on hard surfaces and die faster on soft ones. Tall fescue and Bermuda grass play similarly if maintained, but tall, improperly cut grass slows the ball and drags on players' legs, requiring more weight on ground passes. Field slope (flat end-to-end or corner-to-corner) gives an advantage to playing downhill in the second half.

**Wet conditions:** On wet ("greasy") fields the ball skips and keeps speed, so receivers must turn their hips and square their bodies to the ball, keep legs together, and goalkeepers must practice saving low, fast ground shots; attackers should shoot low and send through balls early, and goalkeepers should avoid drop kicks and keep a dry towel. Large standing-water areas, especially in front of goals, usually make the surface unplayable and warrant rescheduling, with league/administrative resources and the referee involved.

**Field anomalies:** Hard dirt causes higher bounces, faster ground balls, and poor cleat grip; soft dirt reduces bounce and causes loss of footing; clumps of grass produce strange bounces and deflections; uneven surfaces (gullies, holes, depressions, ridges) must be pointed out with cautions about dangers and odd bounces. Weather after-effects include puddles (the ball sticks and must be lifted out with the instep), mud (stuck cleats; multi-stud cleats collect mud and reduce traction), ice (very dangerous; small areas broken up and covered with sand, large areas make the field unplayable), blown branches and twigs (removable), and a fallen tree (unplayable). Rocks and gravel are dangerous; pointed protruding rocks should be dug down or covered with a disk, and loose gravel must be collected. Repairs (sand, dirt, new sod) can cause poor footing. Sprinkler heads are extreme trip hazards; if they cannot be retracted, the field is unplayable. Worn artificial surfaces with split seams are trip hazards and must not be used until repaired or replaced. Fields shared with baseball may contain pitching mounds, rubbers, holes, and bases; an area including a pitching mound is essentially unplayable.

**Field size:** Goal lines range 50–100 yards, touch lines 100–130 yards, with equal-length lines of each type and a rectangular shape; a typical professional field is about 75 x 120 yards. Long fields require extra fitness and extra weight on chips and through balls; short fields require earlier, slower chips and through balls. Wide fields require extra weight on passes to wide players and on crosses and centering passes from near the sidelines; narrow fields call for short inter-passing, small-group tactics, and less weight on crosses and centering passes. Large and small fields combine the "long/wide" or "short/narrow" adjustments respectively. Players must adapt to the size of the field they play on.

**Weather:** Severe storms (hurricanes, tropical storms, tornadoes, severe winds, blizzards) require cancellation, and coaches should monitor forecasts via alerts and apps. Lightning demands immediate evacuation to cars or buildings, never under trees or canopies, with thunder as a signal to vacate; after a storm, at least a 30-minute clock (USSF standard) must run before play resumes. At or below about 40°F, supplemental clothing, including warm underclothing matching shirt and short colors per Law 4, is required. Dew, fog, mist, and frost act like wet grounds. High heat and humidity risk hyperthermia, with effects ranging from dehydration, fatigue, cramps, and heat exhaustion to heat stroke (body temperature can exceed 104°F in 10–15 minutes); players must stay hydrated and coaches should postpone or abandon games, with special caution on artificial surfaces. Light rain has minimal impact unless it intensifies; light snow is usually fine until it accumulates, at which point the field is unplayable unless packed snow is playable with contrasting painted lines and a brightly colored ball, and cold-weather gear, undersocks, and rewarming feet are needed. Light wind has little effect; strong wind requires adjustments: with the wind at the back, attackers take pace off and defenders go to meet the ball; into the wind, kick harder and lower; goalkeepers into the wind may see balls go over their heads, while those with the wind behind may see balls hang up. Crossed balls into the wind should be kicked low and hard; with the wind, weight should be taken off. Perpendicular wind has similar effects, and going with the wind in the second half is advantageous when possible.

**Referees:** Procedures should be in place for referees who fail to appear. The ball remains live if it rebounds off a referee inside the field of play, and players should react as to a goal or flagpost rebound without improperly anticipating it. Referees differ in interpretation, so players must play fairly and judiciously, avoid emotional reactions that lead to avoidable cards, and adapt to decisions such as advantage. Assistant referees vary in recognizing offside, so players must never assume the flag will go up or that a whistle will follow; they must "play to the whistle," while attackers adjust runs and defenders never stop defending on assumption.

**Perimeter factors:** Advertising and "dasher" boards placed too close to the field cause players to jump over them, so players must know what lies beyond and check the outside ground during the walk-through; fence proximity should be noted. Sharply graded drainage ditches and open culverts (exposed or grated) are dangerous; openings near the field should be covered with brightly painted plywood and marked with cones. Running tracks and sidewalks should always be crossed slowly in cleats, since this is like running on ice. Players must stay alert to authorized and unauthorized persons; letting the ball go may be preferable to crashing into people, and fans entering and remaining on the field ends the match. Crazy fan behavior must be ignored and reported; thrown objects must be reported immediately to officials, the coach, and any security, and players have a right to safety. Crowd noise is only problematic if oral communication cannot be heard, in which case non-verbal communication is used. Overhanging branches are usually governed by local rules (e.g., the ball stays in play if it hits a branch).

**Lighting:** Sunlight becomes an issue when it shines into defenders' or goalkeepers' eyes; caps, anti-glare eye-black strips, shading with one hand, and keeping the ball low are remedies, and going with the sun into the opponents' eyes in the second half is advantageous. Abrupt transitions between sunlit and shaded sections affect vision. Floodlights rarely affect play except for the odd ball coming from a light path, but coaches must know the administrative response should all or some lights fail. Glare is usually handled by looking away, shading, wiping sweat from around the eyes, and using peripheral vision, and may be worse for contact-lens wearers. Games where goals are not visible from the center mark should be abandoned, and games clearly ending after sunset in full darkness should not be started.

**Equipment:** Combination soccer/football goals are subject to local rules (a hit on the football crossbar or uprights is out of play, with a corner kick or goal kick). Unbalanced or poorly anchored goals are extremely dangerous—children have been killed by falling goals—and make the field unplayable; rusted, rotted, tilted goals or insecure crossbar joints also render the field unplayable. Missing corner flags should be replaced with cones at each corner, sharp-pointed posts are dangerous and should be replaced, and young players must never remove or throw flags. Missing nets are a nuisance and not necessarily a reason to cancel, but holes in nets can disallow goals; coaches should check and secure nets and players should report gaps. Goal shapes (square, rectangular, round, elliptical) produce different rebounds that players, especially goalkeepers, must learn to anticipate.

**The ball:** An extra ball on the field is dangerous and re-starts must wait until it is cleared. Multiple game balls must be identical in size, make, and model, inflated to the same pressure, and conform to Law 2. Players should report and replace defective balls (lost stitching, torn panels, bubbles, out of round, over- or under-inflated) and wrong-sized balls. Balls at the low end of Law 2's ranges feel "light" and may float or knuckle; those at the high end feel "heavy"; balls with more plasticizer may feel "sticky" on new surfaces. Players should be exposed to all these types. Wet balls behave like wet grounds, and waterlogged balls are dangerous for heading and instep drives, must be reported and immediately replaced, and if only one is available the game should be abandoned.

**Field markings:** Players must learn all markings in Law 1 and why they exist, since fields are sometimes improperly marked. Missing lines may require postponement, though many local rules expect the game to proceed; coaches need cones for the four corners and halfway-line/touchline intersections and at penalty/goal area line intersections, plus saucers for the interior corners of penalty areas (and optionally goal areas). Missing lines may be addressed the same way or with paint, markers, and string, prioritizing perimeter lines, then penalty areas, then the halfway line. Fields marked in multiple colors for several sports require players to identify the soccer color and ignore the rest. Non-parallel or wavy lines require a mutual decision by coaches and referee to either correct them with lines, cones, and saucers, or play with them as marked, with players informed.

**Coaching tips:** Use practice to teach how balls react in wet surfaces or high winds (especially for goalkeepers); simulate conditions by filling holes with water, filling depressions with sand for the goalkeeper, and soaking balls for wet-ball drills; never miss discussing proper clothing and demonstrate Law 4 color-matching requirements; establish a pre-game routine with adequate field-inspection time; treat rest-room access as a field condition; know local rules and how to find field status and weather information; with captains, choose which goal to defend first based on conditions (e.g., defend the downhill or wind-into-face goal first for second-half advantage); remember hydration is needed in winter too; recognize that injury and illness risks rise in wet weather, so stretch more often, remove wet clothes quickly, and use warm-ups and rain gear correctly. Most safety concerns apply equally to practices.

This medRxiv preprint compared REM sleep microstructure in 20 controls, 20 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), and 20 patients with Parkinson’s disease and RBD (PD+RBD) using video-polysomnography. iRBD was associated with increased phasic REM sleep and REM arousals. PD+RBD was associated with reduced REM duration, longer REM latency, shorter REM bouts, and greater REM sleep without atonia. PD+RBD also had fewer and shorter sawtooth-wave bursts, while both patient groups showed altered sawtooth-wave spectral distributions favoring higher frequencies. NREM/REM transition duration increased progressively from controls to iRBD to PD+RBD, and sawtooth waves preceded muscle atonia more often in patient groups. These findings indicate that RBD-related REM abnormalities extend beyond loss of muscle atonia; their evolution and prognostic value require longitudinal investigation. Limitations included small samples, no PD-without-RBD group, medication effects, limited EEG coverage, and time-consuming manual analyses.

The lecture models the in-plane and out-of-plane behavior of hexagonal honeycombs. For hexagonal honeycombs, the elastic moduli scale with the square or cube of relative density, while compressive collapse can occur through elastic buckling, plastic yielding, or brittle crushing. Brittle crushing is modeled as cell-wall fracture governed by bending stress; the fracture moment is derived from a triangular elastic stress distribution, and for regular hexagons the crushing plateau stress is approximately \(4/9\,\sigma_{fs}t/l^2\). Tensile elastic moduli equal their compressive counterparts, tension does not cause elastic buckling, and plastic collapse stresses are nearly the same in tension and compression.

For brittle honeycombs under tension, the lecture uses continuum fracture-mechanics assumptions: the crack is large relative to the cell size, deformation is dominated by bending, axial forces are neglected, and cell walls have constant rupture strength. Balancing the moment on the bent wall ahead of the crack tip against the fracture moment gives a cell-size-dependent fracture toughness proportional to \(\sigma_{fs}t/l^{3/2}\).

Triangular honeycombs deform primarily through axial forces and behave like pin-jointed trusses. Their modulus scales as \(t/l\), rather than the \(t/l^3\) dependence of bending-dominated hexagonal honeycombs. For equilateral triangular cells, the geometric constant is 1.15, making them much stiffer.

The lecture then addresses the five remaining elastic constants needed to describe the nine-constant orthotropic behavior of hexagonal honeycombs. Out-of-plane loading stretches or contracts the cell walls axially rather than bending them, producing much greater stiffness and strength than in-plane loading. The out-of-plane Young’s modulus is approximately the solid modulus multiplied by relative density; the out-of-plane Poisson ratios equal the solid Poisson ratio, while reciprocal ratios are near zero for small \(t/l\). Out-of-plane shear moduli also scale approximately with \(t/l\), with \(G_{13}=G_s(t/l)/\sqrt{3}\) for regular hexagons.

Approximate out-of-plane compressive-strength models are presented for elastic buckling and plastic buckling. For regular hexagonal honeycombs, elastic buckling is estimated as about \(5.2E_s(t/l)^3\), while a simple plastic-buckling estimate gives about \(2\sigma_y(t/l)^2\); a more exact calculation gives \(5.6\sigma_y(t/l)^{5/3}\). Uniaxial yielding may also govern in sufficiently dense honeycombs.

Out-of-plane tensile strength depends on wall integrity. For defect-free walls, fracture strength equals relative density times the solid fracture strength. For cracks spanning multiple cells, fracture toughness is approximated as relative density times the solid toughness. Brittle compressive crushing strength is estimated as approximately 12 times relative density times the solid’s rupture strength.

These honeycomb models provide the basis for subsequent foam modeling using dimensional arguments. The lecture concludes by previewing discussions of wood and cork as natural cellular materials, including Robert Hooke’s illustrations of cork in *Micrographia*.

The article argues that forex trading should generally be avoided in favor of markets such as stocks, where it claims more robust strategies and long-term wealth creation are possible. It cites 12 reasons: leverage can magnify small losses and wipe out trading capital; minor market movements have disproportionate effects; exchange rates are volatile; forex is a zero-sum game without long-term inflation or productivity tailwinds; numerous participants and factors make rates difficult to predict; erratic moves reduce the effectiveness of risk-management systems; scams and unsupported promises are common; brokers create counterparty and insolvency risks; 24-hour trading encourages overtrading; systematic and algorithmic trading requires substantial effort; most forex strategies lack rigorous backtesting and often fail during incubation; and the market attracts impulsive gamblers. It recommends considering why an account is being opened and evaluating the strategy’s historical performance before trading.

Turing’s streaming multiprocessor unifies the L1 data cache and shared memory, doubling L1 hit bandwidth per TPC compared with Pascal and allowing the cache and shared-memory allocation to be reconfigured between 32 KB and 64 KB configurations. Turing also increases L2 cache capacity, and the SM changes deliver a 50% improvement in performance per CUDA core.

Enhanced Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4, accelerating matrix operations used in deep-learning training and inference. They power NVIDIA NGX services, including Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), AI InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS produces quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work in standard mode, while DLSS 2X approaches 64× supersampled quality. InPainting synthesizes replacement image content, AI Slow-Mo generates intermediate frames, and AI Super Rez enlarges images or video by 2×, 4×, or 8×.

The Turing-based Tesla T4 targets data-center, enterprise, and edge inference. It includes 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 INT8 TOPS and 260 INT4 TOPS. NVIDIA reports up to 40× higher inference performance and more than 50× higher energy efficiency than CPU-based inference. The T4 also provides 16 GB of memory, 320 GB/s bandwidth, enhanced video decoding, improved Multi-Process Service behavior, and support for image classification, video analytics, language processing, speech recognition, and intelligent search.

Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory. Its redesigned interface operates at 14 Gbps and improves power efficiency by 20% over Pascal’s GDDR5X, while package and board design reduces signal crosstalk by 40%. TU102 has 6 MB of L2 cache, twice the prior generation’s 3 MB. Combined GDDR6 bandwidth and improved memory compression produce roughly 50% greater effective bandwidth over Pascal.

Turing’s display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, two 8K displays at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, HDR, tone mapping, and USB-C 8K output. Its enhanced NVENC supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps and reduces HEVC and H.264 bitrates, while NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 high-bit-depth formats. USB-C and VirtualLink consolidate VR display, power, and tracking data into one connector. Turing also replaces the SLI bridge with NVLink, providing 25 GB/s per direction per link and new display topologies, though only two-way SLI is supported.

Turing introduces hybrid rendering, which combines rasterization with real-time ray tracing. Each SM includes an RT Core that accelerates bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing CUDA cores for other work. The passage reports throughput above 10 billion rays per second and approximately tenfold improvement over software ray tracing on Pascal. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, combined with denoising, provide more realistic results and can replace shadow maps, screen-space ambient occlusion, and screen-space reflections in appropriate scenes. BVH acceleration and denoising reduce the computational cost of tracing.

Turing also adds mesh shading, with task and mesh shaders using cooperative thread models to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, support level-of-detail selection, and manipulate geometry. Variable Rate Shading can assign different rates to each 16×16-pixel region, enabling content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility from appearance sampling and caches texel results for reuse across frames and views. Multi-View Rendering supports four views per hardware pass and up to 32 views at the API level, improving stereo VR, shadow, and multi-instance rendering. Turing also extends DirectX 12 resource support to bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and permits different resource types to share heaps.

The TU104 contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores and is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores and supports neither NVLink nor SLI. NVIDIA’s RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, CUDA, RT, and integer operations by their modeled workload utilization to provide a combined measure for hybrid rendering.

Lake Havasu City is Arizona’s hottest city, reaching 128°F on June 29, 1994, a state record. The court held that transferring a suit from chancery to the law side did not confer jurisdiction over defendants who had not been served with process in the county where the action was brought. Under the governing statutes, transitory actions at law required service on at least one defendant in the proper county. The defendants’ appearance and answer in chancery, and their counsel’s discussion of transfer and filing deadlines, did not waive their right to challenge personal jurisdiction after the declaration was filed. The motion to dismiss was therefore well founded, and the writ of mandamus was granted.
