Yael Kalai introduces MIT 6.5630 as a course on the evolution of proof systems in computer science and cryptography, from the mid-1980s to current research. The course has 11 weekly meetings, requires scribed notes except for a guest lecture by Oded Regev and a cryptography day, and will include one problem set. Students are encouraged to use a survey on proof systems by Justin Taylor as background reading. Planned topics include interactive proofs, doubly efficient interactive proofs, the GKR protocol, PCPs, MIPs, Shamir’s \(IP=PSPACE\) theorem, cryptography-based succinct proofs, the Fiat–Shamir paradigm, batch proofs, and succinct non-interactive arguments.

The lecture traces the shift from classical, line-by-line proofs to interactive randomized proofs. This change arose with the development of zero-knowledge proofs around 1985 by Goldwasser, Micali, and Rackoff, although the course focuses on new proof systems rather than zero knowledge itself. A traditional polynomial-time verifier characterizes NP. Interactive proofs add interaction and verifier randomness; without randomness, interaction provides no added power because the prover could anticipate the verifier’s messages. Noninteractive randomized proofs, represented by MA, may be stronger than NP, but this is unknown.

A randomized example shows how randomness can speed up verification: checking whether \(C=AB\) can be done in \(O(n^2)\) time by comparing \(Cv\) and \(ABv\) for a random vector \(v=(1,r,\ldots,r^{n-1})\). A false equality is accepted with probability at most \((n-1)/|F|\), based on the number of roots at which two distinct polynomials can agree.

An interactive proof is formally a protocol between a potentially unbounded prover and a polynomial-time verifier, with completeness for true statements and soundness against cheating provers. Standard completeness and soundness values are \(2/3\) and \(1/3\), and repetition can amplify these toward 1 and 0. Shamir’s 1992 result showed that interactive proofs can verify every language in PSPACE.

The lecture then develops the sum-check protocol for proving that a multivariate polynomial \(f:F^m\to F\), of degree at most \(d\) in each variable, has a specified sum \(\beta\) over \(H^m\). In successive rounds, the prover sends univariate polynomials obtained by fixing earlier variables and summing over the remaining coordinates. The verifier checks each polynomial’s degree and its consistency with the preceding round, then chooses a random field element. In the final round, the verifier checks the claimed polynomial against the oracle or circuit for \(f\) at random inputs.

The protocol has \(m\) rounds and \(O(md)\) communication in field elements. Completeness is perfect. For soundness, a cheating prover must move from an incorrect polynomial to the correct one in some round; distinct degree-\(d\) polynomials agree at at most \(d\) points. A union bound therefore bounds the cheating probability by \(md/|F|\), independent of \(H\), provided the field is sufficiently large. The polynomial error-correction property permits many problems to be encoded through low-degree extensions, making sum-check a foundational protocol for interactive proofs and their applications.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2021 describes a Santa Clara-based, Delaware-incorporated company whose common stock trades on Nasdaq under “NVDA.” The filing reports two segments—Graphics and Compute & Networking—serving Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive markets. NVIDIA’s platform combines GPUs, CUDA and related software, interconnects, systems, algorithms, and services to accelerate AI, scientific computing, gaming, visualization, and autonomous vehicles. The company has invested more than $24 billion in research and development since inception and reported 18,975 employees across 29 countries.

NVIDIA completed the approximately $7 billion Mellanox acquisition in fiscal 2021 to expand its networking and data-center capabilities. It also had a pending $40 billion agreement to acquire Arm Limited, involving $2 billion paid at signing, $10 billion in cash and 44.3 million NVIDIA shares at closing, possible additional consideration of up to $5 billion or 10.3 million shares, and up to $1.5 billion in restricted stock units for Arm employees. Closing required regulatory approvals and other conditions.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing strategy, relying on foundries, subcontractors, contract manufacturers, and other suppliers. Its stated strategies include advancing accelerated computing and AI, extending visual-computing leadership, developing autonomous-vehicle platforms, and leveraging intellectual property through licensing and development agreements.

The risk factors identify rapidly changing markets and standards, intense competition, dependence on third-party manufacturers and component suppliers, demand-forecasting and inventory risks, product defects and security vulnerabilities, cybersecurity breaches, business and natural-disaster disruptions, geopolitical and regulatory changes, COVID-19 effects, and risks involving acquisition completion, integration, and expected benefits.

The invention provides a rotorcraft landing device with a landing portion, position-recognition component, and remote-control component. It enables a rotorcraft without onboard image capture to land by using cameras positioned on the landing device, distance measurement to control descent, and drone identification to authorize landing. Optional features include movable plates that form a funnel and center delivered packages, an opening/closing housing that protects the device between landings, and an ascending/descending mechanism for carrying packages into a residence.

In the delivery embodiment, a management system assigns drones and routes using drone, route, and weather databases. After a user accepts a delivery, a warehouse loads and launches a package-carrying drone, which navigates by GPS until approaching the destination. The landing device then remotely controls the drone, receives the package, conveys it to the residential space, and enables the drone to return to the warehouse. Positioning the landing device above the residential area reduces interference from people, animals, debris, and obstacles, while the closable housing supports operation during snow and protects the cameras and other components.

Additional modifications include integration with household ventilation or smoke-exhaust systems, local weather observation, emergency landing acceptance, portable landing devices for disaster relief, warnings for approaching camera-equipped drones, battery monitoring, black-box recording, takeoff inspections, designated flight routes, beacon infrastructure, and drone-security measures ranging from warnings and flight restrictions to observation, blocking, and interception.

A New York grand jury indicted Harvey Weinstein on rape and criminal sex-act charges involving two women, one unidentified. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance said the indictment moves Weinstein closer to accountability and that the investigation remains active, potentially allowing additional charges. Vance also urged other accusers with relevant information to come forward.

Weinstein’s attorney, Ben Brafman, said the indictment merely repeats existing charges and adds nothing new. Weinstein plans to plead not guilty, seek dismissal and, if tried, expects to be acquitted. Brafman said Weinstein would not testify before the grand jury because his lawyers had insufficient time to prepare and access to critical information.

Weinstein surrendered to police Friday and was charged with first- and third-degree rape and first-degree criminal sexual misconduct. His lawyers said one accuser had a decade-long sexual relationship with him that continued after an alleged 2013 assault. Brafman argued the indictment resulted from political pressure on Vance, whose 2015 decision not to pursue an earlier complaint had drawn criticism. Weinstein, free on $1 million bail and restricted to New York and Connecticut, has consistently denied having nonconsensual sex.

SUDEP is the non-traumatic, non-drowning death of a person with epilepsy. Poor control of generalized tonic-clonic seizures is its strongest risk factor, particularly during sleep and in the prone position. Prone positioning may contribute to central apnea and autonomic instability, and SUDEP risk after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure is over 60 times higher in prone versus non-prone positions. Terminal apnea and asystole can begin within 25 seconds after a seizure and occur in virtually everyone by 180 seconds, creating a narrow window for intervention.

The study developed Korus, an autonomous nighttime repositioning mattress intended to move prone patients after a seizure. The twin-XL mattress contains 32 inflatable cells arranged in an 8-by-4 matrix, with 1,152 pressure-sensing nodes. A random forest algorithm detects prone, supine, left lateral, and right lateral positions, while an iOS/Android app displays and controls the system. Eighteen control subjects were enrolled, including 10 who underwent formal testing.

Cells reached their target 14-inch inflation within seven seconds. Manual repositioning from prone to recovery position succeeded in all tested participants, averaging 21.75 seconds. Prone-position detection accuracy was 96.8%, and overall position-recognition accuracy was 92.4%, with most errors involving side positions and no prone-to-supine or supine-to-prone confusion. During extended sleep recording, the correct position was detected 97.3% of the time; false changes were attributed to supine positions being misidentified as side positions.

Further work is required before Korus can function as a fully autonomous SUDEP-prevention system, including improved position mapping, computing optimization, and a biomechanical framework. The authors propose that Korus could also integrate seizure-detection algorithms or wearable devices and state that successful implementation could potentially reduce SUDEP risk by more than 50%.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output. It combines a current-feedback input stage, an internally matched gain-resistor network, and a four-resistor differential output stage. Three digital gain-select pins provide eight binary gain settings from 0.5 V/V to 100 V/V. The input circuitry operates linearly within 3 V of either supply, and the device has one functional mode requiring input- and output-stage supply conditions above their specified thresholds.

External DA_IN− and DA_IN+ pins allow capacitors to be placed in parallel with the output amplifier’s 6.67 kΩ feedback resistor for noise filtering, noise shaping, or custom attenuation. The internal resistor network has accuracy of 0.01% or better, supporting CMRR of at least 80 dB, but has ±15% absolute variation. Pin leakage can degrade CMRR and cause offset errors. These pins must not be treated as outputs or used to source or sink current.

A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1 MSPS SAR ADC. It uses ±15 V for the PGA848 input stage, 5.3 V for the output stage and ADC, a REF6250 5 V reference, and an OPA192-buffered 2.5 V PGA848 reference. Three filters reduce EMI/RFI, shape output noise, and provide ADC charge-reservoir filtering. A 75 pF feedback capacitor gives a nominal cutoff of 318 kHz, falling to 277 kHz at the high feedback-resistor tolerance limit. With all filters, nominal f–3dB bandwidth is 318 kHz, or 277 kHz at the high tolerance limit, while maintaining −0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. C0G capacitors are used throughout the signal path.

The OPA192 reference buffer uses a dual-feedback network with a 20 Ω isolation resistor, 2 kΩ direct feedback, and 2 nF feedback capacitor, providing 86° phase margin. Its noninverting input includes a 1 kΩ/10 nF low-pass filter. Stability components must be recalculated if load capacitance changes, and stability should be verified with more than 60° phase margin.

Nominal performance is specified at ±15 V supplies. Output-stage supplies are clamped within the input-stage levels; supplies above 40 V (±20 V) can permanently damage the device. Recommended layout includes symmetrical input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, trace separation, minimized parasitic capacitance and leakage, and reduced thermal gradients. TI also provides TINA-TI and PSpice simulation tools, related documentation, E2E support, and design resources. Developers remain responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance, and integrated circuits require appropriate ESD precautions.

California avoided the summer blackouts once widely predicted, with no statewide outage reported after May 8. Mild weather, stronger-than-expected conservation, new generating capacity, and federal regulations reduced peak power use by as much as 14%. Governor Gray Davis’s crisis response improved his political prospects, though polls showed fewer than one-third of Californians favored his reelection. His administration still faced budget strains from utility bailouts, litigation over state power purchases, drought, and potential Democratic primary opposition. California’s increasingly Democratic electorate also placed Republican candidates at a structural disadvantage.

Southern California Edison’s proposed rescue would let it issue $2.9 billion in bonds repaid largely by businesses, in exchange for the state receiving a five-year option to buy transmission lines for about $2.4 billion. Consumer groups opposed the plan, while PG&E’s bankruptcy prompted experts to consider whether court proceedings might spread Edison’s losses more fairly. PG&E had filed for Chapter 11 protection, and Williams filed a $591 million claim against it.

Davis’s use of more than two dozen executive orders to authorize state power purchases, accelerate plant construction, and bypass regulatory reviews drew criticism for weakening legislative and oversight roles, though supporters credited the actions with maintaining power supplies. Fitch rated California’s $5.7 billion revenue anticipation notes F1+, but anticipated power-purchase reimbursement was delayed and revenues had been revised downward. The state also faced scrutiny over 55 long-term power contracts worth roughly $45 billion that might cost above-market prices through 2010, while its broader infrastructure needs lacked a comprehensive funding plan.

The European Space Agency’s Gaia observatory, deployed in 2013, has cataloged more than a billion astronomical objects to support the largest and most precise 3D map of the Milky Way. A University of Toronto team led by Jason Hunt combined Gaia’s initial data with the RAVE survey to determine that the Sun orbits the galactic center at 240 km/s. By analyzing stellar velocities, including stars with near-zero angular momentum, and correcting the proper motion of Sagittarius A*, the team estimated the Solar System’s distance from the galactic center at 7.6–8.2 kiloparsecs, or about 24,788–26,745 light-years. The study, published in the Journal of Astrophysical Letters in November 2016, narrowed the range of previous estimates. Researchers expected later Gaia data releases to further refine the measurements.

Rabbi Aaron Brafman, long-time Menahel of Yeshiva Derech Ayson–Yeshiva of Far Rockaway, died on Erev Shabbos, 19 Av, aged 73. An educator and communal leader, he spent over 20 years at Torah Vodaath, where he studied, taught and was a talmid of Rabbis Yaakov Kamenetsky, Gedaliah Schorr and Avrohom Pam. He became the yeshiva’s Menahel in 1970. Known for his diligence, caring guidance and humility, he taught baalei batim, supported a tzedakah fund for needy residents and addressed community concerns. He married Susie Schwartz in 1964. After a levayah at the yeshiva, he was buried in Beit Shemesh. He was survived by his wife, siblings, children and many grandchildren.

Motley Fool Money’s October 1, 2025 roundup highlights several cash-back credit cards. The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card offers unlimited 2% back on all purchases, a $200 bonus after $500 in spending within three months, 12 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, no annual fee, concierge service, and up to $600 in cell-phone protection with a $25 deductible. Variable APR afterward ranges from 18.99% to 28.99%.

The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Card provides unlimited 1.5% back on purchases, 5% back on hotels, vacation rentals, and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, a $100 first-year travel credit, a $200 bonus after $500 in spending within three months, no annual or foreign-transaction fees, and 15 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers.

A Citi offer provides 2% back on purchases when the minimum is paid on time, 5% back on travel booked through Citi Travel, and $200 back after $1,500 in spending within six months. It also features an 18-month, balance-transfer-only 0% APR offer.

Applicants are generally recommended to have a 670–850 credit score, but approval is not guaranteed. Motley Fool discloses that partner commissions may affect which offers appear and their placement, but not product ratings.

Enrique Marquez Jr. agreed to plead guilty to federal charges for purchasing two assault rifles used in the 2015 San Bernardino attack, admitting he was a straw buyer paid by Syed Rizwan Farook. He also admitted conspiring with Farook in 2011 and 2012 to target Riverside City College and Southern California freeway traffic, though those plots were never carried out. Prosecutors said there is no evidence Marquez participated in or knew of the attack in advance. He faces up to 25 years in prison.

Venezuelans and TPS holders asked the Supreme Court to uphold a federal judge’s ruling that DHS Secretary Kristi Noem unlawfully ended Venezuela’s Temporary Protected Status designation and extension. Judge Edward Chen found the action violated federal law and was motivated in part by racial animus. The Supreme Court previously paused Chen’s preliminary order, but the Ninth Circuit declined to stay his final judgment. The challengers argued that the limited earlier stay did not bar litigation on the merits and that the later ruling relied on a developed record and different statutory authority.

Bitcoin fell below $8,000 after Indian Finance Minister Arun Jaitley vowed to eliminate cryptocurrency use in illicit financing and payments. India’s government and central bank have repeatedly warned against digital currencies, prompting banks to suspend accounts linked to major exchanges. A government committee will study cryptocurrencies before further action, while India may explore blockchain for digital payments. Despite fears that regulation could hinder growth, industry figures expect clearer rules and continued adoption, noting India accounts for 2%–3% of global cryptocurrency trade.

The coach described his team’s run to the Stanley Cup Finals as outstanding, noting that the players worked hard, competed, never quit, and took pride in reaching the finals. Despite the loss, he praised the team’s resilience, strong home record, and the support of its fans. He said the opponent was the better team and deserved to win, while acknowledging that the loss would hurt but might feel easier in a few days.

Costamare (CMRE) is presented as an attractive stock as its shares rebound amid improving global trade and economic conditions. The author attributes the 2014–2016 decline to shipping-industry weakness and sees signs of a bottoming price pattern and potential fundamental upswing. Costamare owns and charters containerships; its fleet comprises 71 vessels totaling about 466,000 TEU. Since the prior quarter, it chartered 16 ships with none laid up, while contracted revenue totals $1.2 billion over roughly three years, primarily from major charterers. Charter rates have risen, the idle fleet is 1.8%, and the orderbook is below 13%, signaling tightening supply and demand. The company has reduced net debt from $1.7 billion in 2013 to $1 billion and holds about $219 million in cash. The author is buying CMRE, citing potential revenue, earnings, and share-price gains from stronger fundamentals and expansion opportunities.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. Its operations are organized into North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees. The company sells products through online and physical stores, manufactures electronic devices, produces media content, offers Prime and other subscriptions, provides seller programs, cloud services, publishing tools, and advertising, and operates fulfillment networks and data centers.

The filing identifies material risks from intense competition, expansion into new products and countries, seasonal demand fluctuations, inventory management, seller misconduct, intellectual-property claims, foreign exchange, growth-related resource strain, payment processing, data and system security, personnel retention, suppliers, commercial agreements, acquisitions, evolving regulation, litigation, product liability, taxes, and government contracts. Amazon employed approximately 1,541,000 people at year-end and operated 617,483 thousand leased and 43,927 thousand owned square feet.

Management emphasizes sustainable free-cash-flow growth, customer experience, operating efficiency, and investment in technology, content, AWS, infrastructure, and new initiatives. In 2022, operating cash flow was $46.752 billion, compared with $46.327 billion in 2021; cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $70.0 billion. Critical accounting estimates include inventory valuation and income taxes. AMZN trades on Nasdaq; 10,247,259,757 shares were outstanding as of January 25, 2023.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020 identifies Tesla as a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “TSLA.” Tesla is a large accelerated filer; the non-affiliate market value of its common stock was $160.57 billion as of June 30, 2020, and 959,853,504 shares were outstanding as of February 1, 2021.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases electric vehicles and energy-generation and storage products and provides related services. It operates two reportable segments: automotive, including vehicle sales, leasing, regulatory credits and services; and energy generation and storage. Its vehicle lineup includes Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, while Cybertruck, a new Tesla Roadster, Tesla Semi and a lower-cost vehicle are planned. Energy products include Powerwall, Powerpack, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof.

The company emphasizes direct sales through its website, stores and galleries, supplemented by service centers, mobile technicians, body shops, Superchargers and other charging infrastructure. It develops battery and powertrain technology, control and infotainment software, and autonomous-driving systems using vision and radar. Current Autopilot and FSD offerings provide driver-assistance functions while the driver remains responsible for vehicle control. Tesla also provides warranties, extended service plans, vehicle financing and leasing, insurance in California, and financing options for energy products.

Manufacturing facilities include Fremont, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai. Tesla is expanding capacity and localization and was constructing Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas. Its supply chain relies on hundreds of suppliers, often single-source, for thousands of purchased components. Government incentives and regulations support electric vehicles, renewable energy and energy storage, while vehicle safety, self-driving, battery transport, dealer licensing, solar net metering and energy-system rules create compliance requirements.

Tesla faces competition from established and emerging automobile manufacturers, alternative-fuel vehicle producers, energy-storage companies, utilities and solar providers. It protects its intellectual property through patents, trademarks, trade secrets and contractual measures, and has pledged not to sue parties acting in good faith for electric-vehicle patent infringement. At December 31, 2020, Tesla and its subsidiaries employed 70,757 full-time workers.

The risk factors highlight COVID-19 and macroeconomic uncertainty; production-ramp and new-factory delays; inaccurate demand forecasts; supplier, component and battery-cell shortages; raw-material price volatility; intensifying competition; international regulatory and operating risks; product defects and software failures; battery and solar-system safety; product-liability exposure; the need to maintain public credibility; and regulatory, residual-value, financing and credit risks associated with Tesla’s leasing, loan and resale-guarantee programs.

John Ternus, Apple’s 50-year-old senior vice president of hardware engineering, is viewed by industry observers and Apple insiders as the most likely successor to CEO Tim Cook. His prospects increased after Jeff Williams, previously considered Cook’s natural successor, stepped down and announced he would leave Apple by year’s end.

Ternus joined Apple’s product design team in 2001 and has overseen major products including iPhones, iPads, Macs and AirPods, as well as Apple’s transition to Apple Silicon and the Vision Pro. Apple has also increased his public visibility and expanded his influence over product road maps, features and strategy.

Ternus studied mechanical engineering at the University of Pennsylvania and was a competitive swimmer. He later worked at Virtual Research Systems on virtual-reality headsets and interfaces before joining Apple.

Apple’s internal succession planning also comes amid potential departures involving senior executives. Cook has signaled that he will always want to work, while reports indicate he may eventually become chairman. Selecting Ternus would continue Apple’s practice of internal promotion and place greater emphasis on technical leadership as Apple develops AI and mixed-reality products.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit data-acquisition system operating up to 2 MSPS. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS by continuously converting one selected analog-input channel pair while leaving the other six channels idle. Multiple ADS9803 devices can share SMPL_CLK and SMPL_SYNC; a positive SMPL_SYNC pulse centered on SMPL_CLK’s falling edge synchronizes channel selection and FCLKOUT so corresponding channels are sampled simultaneously.

The internal low-drift voltage reference is filtered with a 10 µF ceramic capacitor at REFIO. An external reference can be used by disabling the internal reference through the SPI interface or the SDI/EXTREF pin.

The source-synchronous data interface supports two- and four-lane SDR and DDR modes. Conversion results are transmitted MSB first as 20-bit values within 24-bit packets, with six trailing zero bits. DCLKOUT supplies the capture clock, while FCLKOUT delimits two-channel data frames. Optional bitwise XOR randomization reduces interference between data transmission and analog performance. Simple averaging reduces output data rate, while moving averaging preserves it; both improve SNR. Fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns can replace data for two channel groups.

Reset, power-down, initialization, analog and interface configuration, and speed-boost operation are controlled through registers. The 16-bit registers occupy three banks: bank 0 is always accessible, and banks 1 and 2 are selected through REG_BANK_SEL. SPI register operations use 24-bit frames. Configuration supports daisy-chained ADCs, with access-frame length scaled by the number of devices.

For ATE and PMU applications, calibrated total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. Low-noise bandwidth extends to 22.7 kHz, while wide-bandwidth mode reaches 700 kHz and settles multiplexed signals to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. Layout guidance includes separate 0.1 µF bypass capacitors for AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD, reference decoupling near REFIO and REFM, short ground connections, and separation of analog and reference paths from digital signals and noise sources.

Inclusive education has become a global agenda grounded in the 1994 Salamanca Declaration and the 2006 Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. International agreements promote equal access to quality education and, in many cases, learning in regular schools alongside non-disabled peers. The literature identifies social, communication, and societal benefits, while also recognizing the specialized instruction, safety, and sense of belonging provided by special schools. There is no global consensus on which setting is preferable.

Myanmar ratified the CRPD in 2011 and introduced inclusive-education provisions through education and disability-rights laws enacted in 2014–2015. Nevertheless, enrollment among children with disabilities remains limited, and public awareness of available special schools is low, particularly in rural areas.

A qualitative case study conducted in Yangon in February 2019 examined education for children with visual impairment. It used interviews, teacher focus groups, school observations, and document reviews involving 12 visually impaired students, nine parents, 18 teachers, four principals, and education officials. The research covered two special schools, Special Schools A and B, and their connected regular schools, Schools C and D.

The resulting system was termed “limited inclusive education in phase.” Children received primary education at special schools while registered in regular schools, then transitioned to lower-secondary classrooms in regular schools. Special schools provided Braille instruction, life-skills and computer training, supplementary instruction, and secure learning environments. Regular schools were valued for developing communication and social skills, fostering empathy among non-disabled students, and enabling peer support. Teachers and principals also considered these benefits important despite reported teasing and bullying.

The study identified several limitations. Special- and regular-school staff had little opportunity to exchange information or coordinate, partly because the schools operated under different ministries. Regular-school teachers sometimes depended on special-school expertise rather than fully addressing visually impaired students’ needs. Students with and without disabilities interacted mainly within classrooms and rarely formed close relationships outside class; only one of the 12 visually impaired participants reported a close non-disabled friend. Age differences, bullying, limited recreational options, and established friendships at special-school dormitories contributed to separation. Some visually impaired children were also refused admission to local regular schools, and many parents were unaware of special-school opportunities.

The study concluded that Yangon’s phased model effectively used existing school resources and addressed educational, life-skills, practical, and emotional needs. It recommended training, policies, and mutual exchanges between special- and regular-school staff, as well as programs promoting inclusion, diversity, and camaraderie among all students. It also argued that education systems, particularly in low-income countries, should develop models suited to their resources and contexts through cooperation between education and social-welfare authorities.
The coach says the time off helped preparation; Dallas is a great shot-blocking team. No specific adjustments yet; they may watch film later and aim to play their best tomorrow night.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for creating an artificial neural bridge that decodes a user’s intended movements from neural activity in real time and converts them into electrical stimulation. The stimulation may actuate a body limb, prosthetic limb, wheelchair, computer cursor, exoskeleton, remote-control device, or robotic arm, allowing users with neural injuries or motor impairments to control movement through thought.

In a continuous control loop, neural activity is measured, artifacts are removed, features such as signal amplitude, frequency-band or wavelet power, and firing rate are extracted, and trained decoders identify the desired movement and level of effort. Decoder outputs are combined with a physics-based body-state observer, movement-sensor data, feedback history, and user-specific activation profiles to generate continuously updated stimulation patterns. High-definition transcutaneous stimulation can selectively activate individual muscles or muscle groups, while multiplexed, interleaved signals enable simultaneous compound movements without electrical interference. Neural activity may be captured through EEG, ECoG, or implanted microelectrode arrays such as Utah or Michigan arrays.

Training can use visual or other cues, attempted or imagined movements, body-state feedback, and machine-learning methods including nonlinear support vector machines. The system supports both discrete movements, such as individual finger, wrist, and forearm motions, and rhythmic movements modeled with a central pattern generator. Graphical interfaces can cue desired movements, provide feedback, and configure stimulation patterns.

In one experiment, a quadriplegic participant used decoded cortical activity, a virtual CPG oscillator, and neuromuscular electrical stimulation to initiate, sustain, and switch among imagined thumb flexion, extension, and rhythmic wiggle. The reported overall accuracy across movement and rest states was 77.4% ± 0.9%.

On August 1, 2016, Microsoft Corporation entered an underwriting agreement for a public offering of seven series of senior unsecured notes totaling $19.75 billion: $2.5 billion of 1.100% notes due 2019; $2.75 billion of 1.550% notes due 2021; $1.5 billion of 2.000% notes due 2023; $4 billion of 2.400% notes due 2026; $2.25 billion of 3.450% notes due 2036; $4.5 billion of 3.700% notes due 2046; and $2.25 billion of 3.950% notes due 2056. The notes were issued under Microsoft’s May 18, 2009 base indenture, as supplemented by an Eleventh Supplemental Indenture dated August 8, 2016, with U.S. Bank National Association as trustee. Interest is payable semiannually on February 8 and August 8, beginning February 8, 2017. The notes rank equally with Microsoft’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt and may be redeemed in certain circumstances. The filing included the underwriting agreement, form of supplemental indenture, forms of global notes, and legal opinions.

The passage lists official papers concerning the continuation and spread of the war, peace efforts before U.S. entry, and neutral rights afterward. Topics include Allied and Central Powers’ responses to the president’s December 18, 1916 peace suggestion and January 22 Senate address; German and Austro-Hungarian peace terms and assurances; Mexican peace proposals; U.S. intercession for Greece; Germany’s constitutional struggle; and Greece’s request for recognition. Part II covers German submarine warfare, the severance of U.S. relations with Germany and declaration of war, treatment of neutral and captured American seamen, and Latin American responses. It also records submarine incidents and ship sinkings, regional conference proposals, severances of relations or declarations of war by several Latin American countries, and related U.S. and regional actions.

The study estimates India’s pandemic mortality burden using verbal autopsies of deaths reported in the nationally representative Consumer Pyramids Household Survey. Of 30,447 deaths reported from 2018–2021, 22,178 verbal autopsies were completed, a 72.8% response rate; after excluding 1,719 deaths occurring before 2018, the final sample included 20,453 decedents. WHO-compliant electronic interviews with relatives were coded independently by two physicians, with a third adjudicating disagreements. U07 and U08 ICD-10 codes were treated as potential SARS-CoV-2 deaths, and excess deaths were measured relative to average 2018–2019 rates. Estimates were adjusted for survey sampling and non-response, delayed death reporting, and verbal-autopsy non-response.

SARS-CoV-2-related deaths in the sample peaked during the 2020 lockdown and India’s two major waves. Estimated population SARS-CoV-2 death rates reached annualized peaks of 0.8% in May 2020, 0.9% in June 2020, and 1.1% in May 2021. The all-cause death rate in 2020–2021 was 81.19% higher than in 2018–2019. SARS-CoV-2 was associated with 17.93% of all pandemic-period deaths and 33.15% of excess deaths. Cardiovascular disease accounted for 27.18% of all deaths and 23.15% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths declined by an amount equal to 1.52% of excess deaths.

SARS-CoV-2 death rates increased significantly with age and were highest among people over 80, although most deaths occurred among those aged 61–80 because of population size. Rates were higher among females, urban residents, and the highest-income quartile, but these differences were not statistically significant; rural areas had more total deaths. State-level excess rates were lowest in several Gangetic Plain states and highest in Goa, Meghalaya, and Tripura.

The authors note that verbal-autopsy coding, delayed reporting, non-response adjustments, and the inclusion of vaping-related disorders in U07 codes may introduce error or over- or underestimate SARS-CoV-2 mortality. The modified COVID verbal-autopsy procedure had not been validated, and statistical corrections could not address unobserved non-response or deaths reported after four years. Alternative date assignment reduced SARS-CoV-2’s relative prominence by shifting some cardiovascular and other deaths between periods.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture and associated RTX products, emphasizing improvements in graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, storage, display, and video processing.

- In a Wolfenstein: Youngblood benchmark, shader-only rendering took 51 ms, or about 20 FPS. Concurrent shader and RT Core rendering reduced this to 20 ms, or 50 FPS, while Tensor Cores with DLSS reduced frame time to 12 ms, or about 83 FPS. With Ampere’s broader improvements, an RTX 3080 rendered the frame in 6.7 ms, or 150 FPS.
- GA10x’s second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance over Turing and add hardware-accelerated motion blur for moving or deforming geometry. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit generates time-dependent triangle positions, enabling accurate ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than on Turing. Blender 2.90, Chaos V-Ray 5.0, Autodesk Arnold, and Redshift Renderer 3.0.X support this acceleration through OptiX 7.0. An RTX 3080 measured up to 5x faster motion-blur rendering than an RTX 2080 Super in a Blender Cycles test.
- Third-generation Tensor Cores accelerate deep-learning matrix operations and add TF32 and BF16 support. FP16 and BF16 provide four times the math throughput of standard FP32, while TF32 provides twice the throughput. Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a 2-out-of-4 nonzero pattern to reduce weight storage and bandwidth by 2x and double math throughput, with virtually no inference-accuracy loss in tests across dozens of networks.
- DLSS uses a neural network to combine details from multiple frames. Ampere’s third-generation Tensor Cores and 9x Super Resolution support make 60 FPS 8K ray-traced gaming feasible on the GeForce RTX 3090.
- GA10x introduced GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance coding. It supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s peak bandwidth, more than 52% above the TU102 in the RTX 2080 Ti. The higher bandwidth also assists BVH traversal and ray-traced workloads.
- NVIDIA RTX IO, combined with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves loading and lossless decompression from the CPU to the GPU. The passage reports up to 100x I/O improvement over hard drives and traditional storage APIs, lower CPU utilization, faster loading, reduced stutter, and support for high-quality texture streaming and large professional datasets.
- The GA10x architecture supports 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz. It includes DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth and dynamic HDR, and HDCP 2.3 and 1.x support. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 HDR AV1 playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC while freeing the graphics engine and CPU.
- The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU and includes 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X; the passage reports it is 1.5x faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.
- The NVIDIA A40 provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI throughput, or 10x with sparsity, compared with the Quadro RTX 6000. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through two A40 GPUs connected with third-generation NVLink, and supports vGPU, Quadro Sync, DisplayPort, and the EGX platform.
- The RTX A6000 includes 48 GB of GDDR6, hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and support for combining two cards into 96 GB of GPU memory. Its published benchmarks cover professional rendering, HPC, and deep-learning workloads.
- GDDR6X memory on GA10x GPUs also includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transmissions and retries them until a successful memory transaction occurs.

The lecture reviews a difficult quiz averaging about 78–79, announces that the quiz and solutions will be posted, and notes that final assessment will combine two quizzes, participation, and homework.

The main topics are full factorial designs for any number of factors, including coded factor levels, contrast tables, interaction columns formed by multiplying factor columns, and equivalence between contrast-based effect estimates and regression coefficient estimates. ANOVA and F-tests are used to assess the significance of main effects and interactions and decide which model terms to retain. A break-forming example with punch depth and material type shows how replicated data, regression, and ANOVA identify significant effects.

Residual analysis is used to distinguish replication noise or omitted factors from inadequate model form. The lecture recommends examining residual trends, variance, and normality, and considering transformations when assumptions are violated. Model inadequacy can be tested for curvature by adding replicated center or other additional points and applying ANOVA to the resulting lack-of-fit term. Without replication, even an added center point can fit a quadratic term exactly, preventing a meaningful test.

The lecture concludes with an introduction to nuisance factors, blocking, randomization, and confounding. It recommends balancing nuisance effects across experimental settings or deliberately confounding them with interaction terms rather than main effects, and previews fractional factorial designs for reducing the number of experimental runs.

The 3-4 defense uses three down linemen, four linebackers, and four defensive backs. It relies on strong defensive linemen playing a two-gap approach, hybrid outside linebackers who can rush or cover, and a two-safety setup. Its flexibility allows pressure from multiple positions and varied coverage combinations, including cover 1, 3, 4, and cover 2 man. Weakside edge and Crossfire blitzes create different pre- and post-snap looks.

The formation can struggle against modern spread offenses and trips formations because outside linebackers must cover receivers, reducing the defense to a five-man box against the run. The 3-3 stack, replacing a safety with another linebacker, has emerged as a response. Cover 4 is effective against deep and underneath passes but vulnerable in the flats.

The 3-4 is associated with Bill Parcells and Bill Belichick, who used it with Lawrence Taylor to win two Super Bowls with the New York Giants. Belichick’s coaching tree includes Matt Patricia, Romeo Crennel, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart. Since 2005, coaches from this tree have won nine college football national championships and seven Super Bowls. Saban won seven national titles at LSU and Alabama, while Smart won four at Alabama and two consecutive titles as Georgia’s head coach.

The prospective Neofoot diagnostic-accuracy study evaluated newborn foot length as a proxy for identifying low birth weight (LBW) and preterm birth (PTB) in Papua New Guinea. Researchers enrolled 342 newborns from 335 mothers at three clinics in Madang Province. Birth weight, gestational age, and two right-foot measurements were obtained within 72 hours of birth. Nine trained community volunteers also measured 123 newborns.

Among the newborns, 21.0% had LBW and 7.3% were preterm. A foot-length cut-off of <7.7 cm had 84.7% sensitivity and 69.6% specificity for LBW, with positive and negative predictive values of 42.7% and 94.5%. For PTB, the same cut-off had 88.0% sensitivity and 61.8% specificity, with positive and negative predictive values of 15.4% and 98.5%. Areas under the ROC curves were 87.0% for LBW and 85.8% for PTB.

Researcher and volunteer measurements differed by an average of 0.07 cm, with 95% limits of agreement from −0.55 to +0.70 cm; 7.3% of paired measurements were outside these limits. Measurements were frequently rounded to full or half-centimetre marks.

The study found foot-length measurement simple and feasible without adverse events, but noted limited generalizability beyond one province, possible unblinded measurement bias, digit preference, and the potential referral workload caused by low positive predictive value for PTB. Further implementation research was recommended to optimize cut-offs, reduce measurement errors, and assess referral and health-system effects.

Iran’s parliament initially approved a bill allocating over $260 million each for Tehran’s ballistic missile program and the IRGC’s Quds Force in response to new U.S. sanctions. It requires a second parliamentary vote and final clerical approval before becoming law.

Blackwell adds rapid clock-tree gating, including for memory, and separate GPU-core and memory voltage rails. These enable workload-specific optimization and frame-level shutdown of idle chip sections, reducing dynamic and leakage power.

MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices provide five operating modes, ordered by decreasing power consumption: RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN. The CPU executes code in RUN mode, while peripheral interrupts can wake the device from SLEEP, STOP, or STANDBY. SHUTDOWN disables the internal core regulator and can be exited only through NRST, SWD, or a logic-level match on certain I/Os. Two power domains support configurable performance and power policies: PD1 contains the CPU, memories, and high-performance peripherals, while PD0 contains low-speed, low-power peripherals. PD1 is powered in RUN and SLEEP; PD0 remains powered through STANDBY; both are disabled in SHUTDOWN.

The power management unit provides regulated core supplies, external-supply supervision, a bandgap reference, brown-out monitoring with three programmable warning thresholds, and parity-protected trim that triggers a power-on reset if corrupted. The clock module supports internal 32-kHz and high-frequency oscillators, external low- and high-frequency crystal or digital sources, and a system PLL producing 32-to-80-MHz outputs. It distributes clocks for the processor, buses, and peripherals, including low-power clocks that remain active in STANDBY and high-speed clocks used in RUN and SLEEP.

The DMA controller provides six full-featured channels with repeated transfers and six basic channels with single transfers. It supports 8- through 128-bit and mixed transfers, transfer counts up to 64K, configurable triggers, interrupts, early interrupts, cascading, and stride mode. The event manager routes events from publishers to subscribers through static and programmable routes, supporting CPU interrupts, DMA triggers, and direct peripheral-to-peripheral actions through point-to-point or splitter routes.

Flash memory includes up to 256 or 512 KB in a dual-bank program area plus a separate 16-KB data bank. Features include ECC, in-circuit programming and erasing, 1-KB erase sectors, selectable high-endurance sectors, and bank swapping for over-the-air firmware updates. Up to 128 KB of zero-wait-state SRAM is divided into two 64-KB banks. Bank 0 is protected and available through STANDBY; Bank 1 is unprotected and can be selectively powered down in STOP. SRAM contents are lost in SHUTDOWN, and configurable write-execute partitioning can prevent execution from read-write regions.

GPIO ports provide up to 93 pins, multi-bit set, clear, and toggle operations, shutdown wake through “Standard with Wake” pins, and low-power wake from STOP or STANDBY through “FastWake.” IOMUX provides programmable pad characteristics and pin multiplexing. Two 12-bit ADC modules support simultaneous single-ended sampling at 4 Msps with greater than 11 ENOB, hardware averaging for 14-bit effective resolution at 250 ksps, internal or external references, and operation in RUN, SLEEP, and STOP. The device also includes a calibrated temperature sensor, selectable 1.4-V or 2.5-V voltage reference, comparators with low-power wake and timer blanking, and a buffered DAC with FIFO, DMA, event-trigger, and 8- or 12-bit output support.

Security features include AES-128/256 acceleration, flexible code and data firewalls, secure storage for as many as four AES keys, CRC-16 and CRC-32, a true random number generator, an AES advanced accelerator, a keystore controller, and a hardware math accelerator. Communication peripherals include UARTs with programmable baud rates, parity, LIN mode, FIFOs, and loopback; I2C controllers supporting 7- and 10-bit addressing and rates up to 1 Mbit/s; SPI supporting controller and peripheral roles and rates up to 32 Mbit/s; and CAN-FD supporting CAN 2.0 and CAN-FD communication up to 5 Mbit/s.

The low-frequency subsystem includes a 32-kHz RTC_B with calendar counters, customizable and periodic alarms, calibration and temperature-drift compensation, and clock output, plus an independent watchdog timer that generates a power-on reset after a programmable timeout. A windowed watchdog supports reset or interrupt supervision and timer-only operation. General-purpose and advanced timers provide multiple counter modes, prescaling, interrupt and DMA triggers, cross-peripheral triggering, and specialized functions such as quadrature encoding, Hall sensing, complementary PWM, programmable dead-band insertion, and rapid fault handling.

A two-wire SWD interface provides debug access. The boot strap loader supports programming and configuration through UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, can be disabled, and is enabled by default for production programming. It can be invoked through its invoke pin, an unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or a runtime system-reset command. Read-only factory constants provide device capabilities, identification, revision data, and calibration trim information.

Recommended schematic implementation includes 10-µF and 0.1-µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS, a 47-kΩ NRST pullup with a 10-nF pulldown, a 0.47-µF VCORE capacitor, a 100-kΩ precision resistor between ROSC and VSS when SYSOSC frequency correction is used, and pullups for open-drain I/O. TI supports the devices through the MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, CCS, IAR, Keil MDK, and GNU Arm Embedded tools. The document also provides development-tool guidance, nomenclature distinguishing experimental X devices from qualified MSP production devices, revision information, package drawings, orderable information, and automotive-qualified G3518 and G3519 variants.

Spouses often make each other sole heirs in a Berliner Testament, with their children as final heirs, providing the survivor financial security until both parents die. However, its strong binding effect prevents unilateral changes, even after one spouse dies, potentially leaving new partners empty-handed or children as heirs. Amendment clauses and inheritance-tax allowances should be considered with succession-law advice.

Delta expects premium-cabin revenue to surpass main-cabin revenue next year as demand for first-class and other upscale seats remains strong. Premium revenue rose 9% year over year to nearly $5.8 billion last quarter, while main-cabin revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. Delta’s main-cabin share of 2024 revenue fell to 43% from 60% in 2010, while premium seats and loyalty generated nearly 60% of revenue last year. Airlines are expanding elaborate premium seating, and CEO Ed Bastian sees no sign of slowing demand.

CFDs are contracts that let traders speculate on price movements in assets such as stocks, commodities, currencies, and indices without owning them. Profit or loss depends on the difference between opening and closing prices, making CFD trading zero-sum.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a 0–100 momentum oscillator that measures average gains and losses. Traders commonly use it to identify overbought and oversold conditions, potential trend reversals or price pullbacks, and possible buy or sell signals. Readings below 30 generally suggest oversold conditions, while readings above 70 suggest overbought conditions.

RSI thresholds and time frames should be adapted to the asset, market trend, and trading strategy. Day traders may use short intervals such as 15 or 30 minutes with more extreme thresholds of 15 for oversold and 85 for overbought. Shorter time frames are more sensitive and erratic; longer ones are smoother but may generate fewer signals. Combining a longer-term RSI for trend direction with a shorter-term RSI for entries is possible, though it does not guarantee improved performance.

Mean-reversion strategies seek price movements that revert toward an average. Other approaches include a two-day RSI strategy that buys below 10 and exits when the close exceeds the previous day’s high, and an RSI momentum strategy using a 100-day lookback and 14-day RSI to trade bullish trends. Bullish and bearish RSI divergences may also signal buying and selling opportunities.

Backtesting RSI strategies with historical data is essential. In one SPY test, adding the new exit increased trades from 313 to 355, reduced average return per trade from 0.86% to 0.67%, but produced smaller, smoother drawdowns. Traders should also combine RSI with volume, relative performance, or other factors and account for commissions, slippage, taxes, leverage, and risk controls.

Researchers are investigating ways to enhance memory, attention, and intelligence. Caffeine and nicotine promote focus by blocking sleep-promoting adenosine and mimicking acetylcholine, respectively. Tim Tully’s team is searching for people with exceptional memory to identify genetic targets for a “memorization pill” and has created fruit flies with photographic memories by manipulating CREB activators. Other projects seek genes linked to intelligence and develop deep-brain-stimulation devices that monitor abnormal brain activity and electrically intervene, though these approaches remain experimental and controversial.

This study compares models for forecasting annual fatal opioid overdoses at the census-tract level in Cook County, Illinois, and Massachusetts to help public health agencies target limited intervention resources. It evaluates simple baselines, including zero, last-year, and historical-average forecasts; weighted historical averages; Poisson GLMs; gradient-boosted trees; Gaussian processes; Bayesian spatiotemporal models; negative binomial models with spatially lagged features; and the CASTNet neural network. Inputs included prior overdose counts, location, time, and optional Social Vulnerability Index covariates.

Models were assessed using RMSE, MAE, and a proposed intervention-focused metric, percentage of Best Possible Reach (%BPR), which compares fatalities in the K model-selected tracts with fatalities in the K highest-burden tracts under perfect hindsight. Results varied by metric. In Massachusetts, BST with SVI and NBSpLag with SVI achieved the highest %BPR at 62.0%; BST also outperformed Gaussian Process on %BPR, potentially identifying 18 additional fatalities annually among the top 100 tracts. In Cook County, Poisson GLM with SVI achieved the highest %BPR at 79.4%, exceeding gradient-boosted trees by 2.3 percentage points despite their better error-based scores and potentially reaching 15 more fatalities annually. A tuned historical-average baseline performed competitively with more complex models in both locations.

The authors released open-source modeling software, preprocessing code, and the cleaned Cook County dataset. Limitations include reliance on only two jurisdictions, incomplete Cook County medical-examiner coverage, use of a fixed intervention budget of 100 tracts, BPR’s emphasis on existing burden rather than rates of change, and the possibility that jurisdictions could benefit from additional covariates such as EMS calls, insurance claims, and linked administrative data.

The passage defines host-environment requirements for integrating AMD AGESA/AGESATM software. The host must establish a valid stack, populate the standard header, and route all AGESA calls through module dispatchers. A host bridge locates the binary image entry point and invokes the AMD dispatcher. AGESA call-outs pass through a common host-implemented router that translates function identifiers into host procedure addresses.

For UEFI, AGESA supports SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime stages across 16-, 32-, and 64-bit execution modes. Platform options are customized through `<plat>Options.c`; build control files, environment variables such as `AGESA_ROOT` and `AGESA_OptsDir`, and addendum reference files support integration. Core files can be supplied as binary modules through a common dispatcher or integrated as source and built with the host tool set.

Native assembly routines provide early silicon controls and pre-memory stack creation and removal for x86-64 systems. `AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK` initializes cache and allocates per-core stack space before main memory is available, while the teardown procedure disables Cache-as-RAM after relocation. AArch64 systems with PSP do not use these routines because the PSP initializes DRAM. Host code must not alter MTRRs during the Cache-as-RAM period.

The UEFI implementation uses PEI modules for early processor initialization, post-reset memory initialization, and coordinated reset handling. These modules publish PPIs and a memory-information HOB. A DXE driver invokes `AmdInitLate`, generates informational tables, and publishes `AgesaDxeProtocol`; the GPU VGA-control driver conditionally enables processor-GPU VGA decoding.

Host service procedures support structure creation and release, DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI address discovery, current-core identification, FRU memory-device location, pre-memory execution-cache sizing, MMIO range allocation, and event-log retrieval. Most require an established stack and, where applicable, operational coherent HyperTransport links.

The documented initialization sequence includes `AmdInitReset` for minimal processor and execution-cache setup, `AmdInitEarly` for fuller processor initialization, `AmdInitPost` for memory initialization and pre-memory-stack shutdown, `AmdInitEnv` for transferring artifact data into permanent memory, `AmdInitLate` for graphics and system-table preparation, and `AmdInitRtb` for saving suspend state. Resume procedures restore memory and processor state and perform final silicon reinitialization before operating-system handoff.

The host must also implement `AgesaAllocateBuffer` and `AgesaDeallocateBuffer`. Allocation occurs after main-memory initialization, must return sufficient persistent memory when requested, and must correctly reserve and release any host-specific storage associated with a buffer.

The speaker accepts his assigned duties with gratitude and a heightened sense of honor and responsibility to a free nation. Despite unprecedented American prosperity, the country faces grave difficulties caused by international conflict, arbitrary edicts, and retaliatory principles contrary to reason and acknowledged law. Confident that U.S. neutrality and just conduct have warranted no such action, he trusts national unity will protect the nation’s honor and interests.

He pledges to foster peace, maintain neutrality, pursue amicable settlements, resist foreign interference, preserve the Union and Constitution, and respect state authority, popular rights, religious freedom, private liberties, and freedom of the press. He also promises economical government, debt reduction, a limited standing military and effective militia, support for agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, science, and information, and efforts to bring Indigenous neighbors into civilized life. Confident in his predecessors, fellow citizens, and divine guidance, he enters the arduous service with a strong sense of duty.

Former Langley City mayor and Liberal MLA Peter Fassbender is considering another mayoral run, with a decision expected by early August. He left the mayor’s office after winning an MLA seat in 2013. Two councillors have declared for mayor.

The Supreme Court agreed to review a case involving a Texas defendant’s waiver of his right to appeal. A federal judge required Hunter to take prescribed mental-health medication, told him he could appeal, and sentenced him to 51 months, three years’ supervised release, and over $235,000 restitution. The 5th Circuit dismissed his appeal under the waiver. Arguments are likely early next year, with a decision expected by summer.

The Colorado Supreme Court affirmed judgment for real estate brokers who sued their principals for commission. Della B. Thuro signed a sale contract for herself and, without authority, for George W. Thuro; the purchasers took possession and made payments before abandoning the contract. Whether George Thuro ratified the contract and whether Charles Tallman was bound were immaterial because the brokers had fulfilled their duty by procuring at least one bound purchaser, and a principal cannot avoid a broker’s commission by refusing to be bound by a sale contract produced by the broker. The alleged variance between pleading and proof did not affect the parties’ substantial rights. Refusal to instruct the jury on immaterial issues and refusal to strike certain allegations from the replication were also harmless.

Montecito Union School District settled a sexual abuse lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers who alleged that former superintendent and principal Stanford Kerr molested them between 1972 and 1978. The brothers had sought $35 million. The settlement equals about 40% of the 350-student district’s 2025-26 budget; the district plans to use a hiring freeze, staff attrition and capital-repair funds, avoiding layoffs.

The district admitted no liability and had no insurance coverage for the period of alleged abuse. Superintendent Anthony Ranii said potential damages from the scheduled trial posed a severe financial threat and settling would stabilize operations. A third plaintiff had settled separately for $1 million. The case, filed in 2022, was set for a 17-day trial before reaching a final payment hearing scheduled for Nov. 19.

The settlement follows concerns about Assembly Bill 218, which removed statute-of-limitations protections for certain childhood sexual abuse claims against public agencies. Lawmakers declined to advance Senate Bill 577, which sought to restore a limitations period, though its sponsor plans to reintroduce it. One projection estimates California school districts could face up to $3 billion in settlements and jury awards, with particularly severe risks for small districts.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler pitched eight scoreless innings against the White Sox in Game 3 of the AL Wild Card Series, striking out 12 and allowing five hits. Scout Matt Hyde called the performance “unbelievable.” Schlittler became the first MLB pitcher to record the feat without issuing a walk.

The author argues that traditional percentage-based definitions of bull and bear markets—such as a 20% decline or rally—are arbitrary, lack empirical support, and provide little practical value for risk management or capital allocation. Examples from 2011 and 2015 show how these thresholds can classify markets differently without indicating what investors should do.

He instead defines secular bull and bear markets using market performance, long-term economic trends, and investor psychology, particularly valuations. A secular bull market typically lasts 10 to 20 years, reflects broad economic shifts that support corporate revenues and earnings, reduces volatility, and features investors paying increasingly higher multiples for each dollar of earnings. A secular bear market reverses these conditions, with greater volatility, cyclical rallies and retreats, economic challenges, and contracting earnings multiples.

The author emphasizes the direction of price-to-earnings ratios rather than their absolute level. He estimates that rising multiples accounted for three-quarters of the S&P 500’s gains during the 1982–2000 bull market: earnings more than doubled, broad indexes rose 1,000%, and the index’s P/E ratio increased from about seven to 34. Investors should therefore focus on the economic, earnings, and psychological forces driving markets rather than arbitrary percentage labels.

This study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with explainable machine learning for detecting technical and procedural outliers in multicenter plantar-pressure data. Experts annotated 1,031 samples from 703 participants as valid or as one of four outlier types: general acquisition error, double-foot capture, inverted orientation, or incorrect side annotation. Synthetic outliers expanded the dataset to 2,798 samples.

SPM used affine registration and pixel-wise nonparametric cluster testing against separate left- and right-foot normative datasets. The comparison method used a CNN incorporating foot-side metadata, with SHAP providing pixel-level explanations. Subject-grouped nested five-fold cross-validation showed that the CNN outperformed SPM, with F1 scores of 0.99 ± 0.00 versus 0.93 ± 0.01 and Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.96 ± 0.01 versus 0.78 ± 0.02. Pathological but valid feet commonly caused false positives, while SPM frequently missed incorrect side annotations.

In a survey of 16 experienced evaluators, both approaches were rated positively for clarity, correctness, usefulness, relevance, understandability, trustworthiness, and completeness, with no statistically significant differences between them. SPM was descriptively considered simpler, while 43.48% of preferences favored the SHAP explanations, 34.78% favored SPM, and 17.39% favored both approaches. The findings support automated, interpretable quality-control workflows while identifying further research needs involving improved anatomical alignment, realistic synthetic anomalies, additional XAI methods, and broader evaluation of explanation quality.

STAT’s Pharmalittle reports that planned 100% tariffs on branded pharmaceuticals were delayed after the Trump administration said it would prepare tariffs on companies that neither build U.S. facilities nor accept drug-pricing agreements. Pharmaceutical executives are receiving near-daily outreach from White House, HHS, and Commerce officials as the administration seeks industry commitments ahead of the 2026 midterms, including requests for increased insulin, drug production, and a possible U.S. headquarters.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8% stake in Dubai-based private equity firm Abraaj Holdings, a sale made more urgent by the bank's restructuring and by Abraaj's dispute with investors over alleged misuse of their money. Deutsche, which cut eight Dubai equities research positions and classifies the stake as non-core, declined to comment. Abraaj has not disclosed its debt, complicating valuation; one banker estimates its investment management unit could be worth up to $500 million, though sources said any sale would be at a big discount. Abraaj, which denies wrongdoing, faces investigation by four investors, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the International Finance Corporation, concerning a $1 billion healthcare fund. Its CFO and COO have resigned.

The passage outlines two defensive approaches against the High Post Split Offense: basic NBA “Show & Recover” and Basic SOS disruption. In the standard defense, guards and wings sag toward the high post to prevent cuts, handoffs, and direct drives, while the post defender pressures the receiver toward the weak-hand corner. Against down screens, defenders usually show and recover rather than switch, since switching could allow the screener to post up against a smaller defender.

Basic SOS defense pressures the ballhandler early, uses switches on high-post splits and down screens, and traps passes to the wing or low post. Its phases cover disrupting the high-post feed, defending the split, contesting down screens with contact switches and strong pass denial, and double-teaming a wing. Rotations occur as the passer releases the ball, with defenders denying low-post entries, maintaining help positions, and fronting or trapping posts when necessary.

The passage outlines ways to attack a Box & One defense, noting that its middle is vulnerable. A baseline post player can flash into the middle while the ballhandler splits the defense, creating a shot opportunity or a pass to a wing player back-cutting when the post defender challenges. High/low post feeds, drop passes, fake-shot passes, and single/double screens provide continuations when the initial action fails. Variations include using a base screen for the star player or an entry pass to a wing followed by a corner cut and elbow exchange before a back-cut feed. Success depends on preparation, coordination, communication, timing, and strong post play. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads and matchups, observe adjustments, vary alignments, and attack weaker defenders. Box & One uses four defenders in zone areas while a “Chaser” focuses solely on denying the ball and rebounds.

The study examines teachers’ knowledge, perceptions, readiness, and potential applications of the metaverse in education. The metaverse is described as a hybrid virtual platform combining gaming, social media, and digital communities, with four types: augmented reality, lifelogging, mirror worlds, and virtual reality. Its educational appeal includes immersive, collaborative, personalized, practical, and risk-free learning, but it also presents monitoring, infrastructure, cost, accessibility, teacher preparation, and health concerns and is not expected to replace conventional classrooms.

An online survey was administered to 333 teachers in Türkiye. The 28-question questionnaire included demographic information and multiple-choice and open-ended items, was reviewed by three educational technology experts, and was analyzed through descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Most respondents worked in private or public schools, held bachelor’s or master’s degrees, and had 6–10 years of teaching experience.

Teachers’ average knowledge score was 5.25/9, although 78.1% reported prior metaverse-related experience, generally through virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual environments rather than the contemporary concept of the metaverse. Teachers followed metaverse research moderately, held a positive attitude toward its educational use, and rated its perceived advantages highly. Frequently identified benefits included attracting students’ interest, enabling practice, learning by doing, familiarizing students with new technologies, removing educational limitations, and supporting digital competence and personalized learning.

Despite this positivity, teachers expressed substantial concerns, particularly technical problems, addiction and other psychological issues, unequal access, data security, teacher readiness, content-development difficulties, physical discomfort, cost, and classroom management. Nevertheless, average willingness to use the metaverse was high, as were ratings of lesson suitability and willingness to receive training.

Teachers considered information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics most suitable for metaverse applications, particularly for abstract-concept instruction, experiments, collaborative learning, and realistic simulations. They generally regarded the education system and its stakeholders as unprepared, though students were perceived as relatively more ready, and most anticipated effective educational use within five years.

The study recommends gradual, low-risk implementation; stronger infrastructure and device access; diverse, age-appropriate, engaging content; pre-service and continuing teacher training; attention to physical and mental health; cooperation among educators, developers, policymakers, and researchers; regular user feedback; and clear behavioral rules.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated February 11, 2015, announcing fourth-quarter and fiscal 2015 results for the period ended January 25, 2015. The filing furnished the press release and CFO Colette M. Kress’s commentary as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2.

The speaker praises his wife during their baby’s birth, says his team regrouped and played hard after a teammate was injured, and notes that a high-speed hit on Drury will likely be reviewed by the league.

Their doctor reported that the MCL is tight but torn, requiring surgery after the series; a brace will help, and the speaker is not worried.
