H. B. Fuller disclosed in an SEC filing that VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares on Oct. 2 for $315,184.80, at an average price of $58.40. Quarterly EPS was $0.65, below the $0.67 consensus, while revenue of $562.87 million exceeded the $553.66 million estimate. The company announced a $0.15 quarterly dividend, payable Nov. 2 to shareholders of record Oct. 19, representing $0.60 annualized and a 1.06% yield.

Analysts’ ratings totaled two sells, five holds and one buy, with an average “Hold” and a $57.40 consensus target. Baird initiated neutral coverage with a $60 target, while Deutsche Bank kept hold and raised its target to $58. Bank of America, Principal Financial, Prudential and BlackRock increased stakes; Westfield Capital opened a position. Institutional investors own 92.37% of the stock. H.B. Fuller manufactures and markets adhesives, sealants and other specialty chemical products across six segments.

The Supreme Court will hear on August 17 Lt Col Prasad Shrikant Purohit's challenge to his bail rejection and Nisar Ahmed Bilal's plea to cancel co-accused Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur's bail in the 2008 Malegaon blast that killed at least six. The NIA cleared Thakur but said charges against Purohit were serious.

The preprint introduces LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), an R Shiny web tool integrated with the LUKB UK Biobank platform to identify temporal disease trajectories from electronic medical records (EMRs). Its workflow filters diseases associated with a selected exposure using Cox regression, detects and assigns directions to candidate disease pairs using binomial tests, validates those pairs with matched conditional logistic regression, and concatenates confirmed pairs into trajectories. It calculates conditional risk and can be deployed locally for secure analysis.

A COVID-19 case study used UK Biobank ICD-10 diagnoses and dates, analyzing 183,386 individuals, including 8,411 with COVID-19, and 274 diseases or conditions. Cox regression identified 90 diseases associated with COVID-19. Of 8,010 pairs formed, 2,410 showed significant temporal association, 527 passed directionality testing, and all 527 were confirmed by conditional logistic regression. The resulting trajectories primarily involved SARS-CoV-2-related conditions and other medical care; immune-related diseases were not identified, potentially because the UK Biobank diagnosis data did not fully capture COVID-19 cases or later outcomes.

The full analysis took 55 minutes using eight computation cores. Limitations include reliance on processed diagnostic records and the construction of trajectories from statistical disease pairs rather than direct patient histories. The authors recommend comprehensive, representative datasets and caution against using the trajectories for patient clustering.

The paper presents TalBot, an LLM-powered robotic language intervention combining ChatGPT with the Furhat conversational robot. TalBot leads the Alias word-retrieval game, generates clues, gives feedback and additional hints, redirects off-topic dialogue, manages turn-taking, and displays emotions and nonverbal cues. Preliminary co-design testing with 13 preschool children with language vulnerabilities and seven educators showed that TalBot could manage group turn-taking, respond to mispronunciations and speech-recognition errors, and offer promising support for children’s communication difficulties.

The authors propose extending TalBot to morphological learning by generating varied grammatical input, consistently modeling target structures such as verb forms and pluralization, and demonstrating strategies to educators. They argue that an LLM-based robot could provide scalable exposure beyond limited therapy sessions, while educators and speech-language therapists remain essential for guidance and support.

Development will proceed through laboratory co-design, preschool field studies comparing robot- and educator-led sessions, and a feasibility study with 5–10 children. Assessments will examine morphological skills, dosage of targeted forms, educator learning, usability, and children’s emotional responses, ultimately informing possible randomized controlled trials and interventions for multiple languages. Data protection, EU AI Act requirements, long-term effects on children, educator and child acceptance, motivation, cost, and practical integration remain key concerns.

David Ellison praised CBS News and said he wants it to become a highly trusted news destination appealing to center-left and center-right Americans. After acquiring The Free Press and naming Bari Weiss editor in chief, he said its values align with Paramount and CBS News. He declined to specify needed changes and rejected claims that CBS News would become a media arm of Trumpworld.

Brantford, Haldimand and Norfolk school officials are considering combining high school sports into a single district league, with public and Catholic boards aiming for consistent rules, equal game opportunities and more inclusive competition. Currently, only football includes some cross-county play through the Haldimand-Norfolk league. The proposal is not finalized; no timeline has been set, though sources indicated a new system could take shape in 2019-20. Extended travel for Norfolk teams was identified as a major concern.

At 17, students are expected to choose college and career paths despite uncertainty; such choices may change as technology reshapes industries and reduces the dominance of petrol- and diesel-powered engines. Over a 40–50-year career, many roles will evolve unpredictably. Employees should maximize the value of their work by developing expertise or scarce skills that make them worth more than minimum wage. The contrasting examples of a burger seller and a highly trained throat surgeon illustrate differences in earning power. No job will be enjoyable every day, and work may sometimes be merely a means to support a meaningful life outside employment.

The push-pull converter design uses Type 2A frequency compensation with a 10-kHz target crossover frequency and a calculated power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. Seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors provide the required 2.3-mF output capacitance, with an equivalent ESR of 0.86 mΩ used to determine the ESR-zero frequency and CHF. Selected compensation values are RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF; compensation may be tuned during testing. Slope compensation is set through the RSC pin to match the output inductor’s falling slope for sub-harmonic damping, using a 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V input supply. The supply should be regulated and properly bypassed with at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS. Additional X5R-or-better ceramic capacitance placed close to the controller can improve noise and radiation performance, and bulk capacitance is recommended when the supply is remote.

PCB layout recommendations include routing feedback away from magnetics and switch-node traces, minimizing switch-node copper and high-di/dt/dv/dt loop areas, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point, and using short, direct, wide high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere. VIN, REFCAP, and VLDO bypass capacitors and external COMP components should be placed near their associated pins. Other guidance covers keeping the VSENSE divider nearby, isolating high-dv/dt output and gate-drive traces from sensitive signals, filtering CS_ILIM signals when required, routing SYNC away from sensitive circuitry and using at least 3.3 nF for HICC noise reduction, and connecting CFP-package backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. The document also provides application curves, CFP and TSSOP layout examples, related TI resources, revision history, and mechanical and ordering information.

Scotland will abolish all local-authority burial and cremation charges for people under 18, following an agreement between the Scottish government and Cosla. The government will provide £500,000 to cover the costs, bringing Scotland into line with England and reducing financial burdens on bereaved families.

The passage describes AGESA host-environment interfaces, UEFI build integration, PEI/DXE initialization components, early stack services, and related utility procedures.

In the binary image build model, all AGESA core call-outs use a single interface portal. The host environment must implement and load a router address in the standard header; the router filters and dispatches functions by translating a function number into an execution address. Its interface accepts a function identifier, function-specific data passed without conversion, and a configuration pointer containing the standard header. Calls use 32-bit protected-mode flat addressing, may return `AGESA_UNSUPPORTED`, and generally require an established stack.

UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases. AGESA core files are arranged into libraries, with additional UEFI libraries producing build targets for the platform. MASM 6.15 is used for 16-bit SEC code; Microsoft Macro Assembler and C/C++ compiler versions 8.00.50727.762 and 14.00.50727.42 are used for 32-bit SEC and PEI development; versions 8.0.40310.39 and 14.0.40310.41 are used for 64-bit DXE and runtime development. Platform options are selected through `<plat>Option.c`. During UEFI porting, the first reserved standard-header element stores the PEI_Services handle, and special environment-specific library routines connect AGESA to UEFI services.

The SEC phase establishes the C execution environment, enters 32-bit mode, and creates a stack through `AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK`. The PEI driver is divided into processor and memory-related PEIMs. The processor PEIM initializes processor components, publishes early and post-initialization PPIs, and publishes a memory-information HOB after `AmdInitPost`, except during `BOOT_ON_S3_RESUME`. The memory PEIM initializes memory subcomponents, publishes post-memory and memory-initialization PPIs, and signals processor cleanup and configuration; system memory remains unavailable for general use until the standard EfiMemory PPI is posted. A separate PEIM coordinates warm-reset requests from northbridge, southbridge, and processor PEIMs, generating a reset when required or publishing a reset-complete PPI otherwise.

The DXE driver performs late AMD initialization and publishes data tables through `AgesaDxeProtocol` for use by other drivers. `AmdGpuVgaControlDxe` monitors `PciIo` requests and enables processor-GPU VGA resource decoding only when requested by the host environment.

The `\Addendum` directory contains reference implementations and platform option files, including `Cpcar32.asm`, `<Plat>Options.c`, and `<Plat>RecoveryOptions.c`. UEFI control files such as `AgesaPei0Libs.inf`, `AgesaPei1Libs.inf`, and `AgesaDxe0Libs.inf` must be integrated into platform and host build systems. Required environment variables identify the AGESA root, platform tip build directory, and target platform solution. Integration copies and edits platform options and `OptionsIds.h`, sets environment variables, and generates or locates documentation. Cache-as-RAM must be enabled before `AmdInitReset` using the `ByHost` allocation method, with structure space allocated beforehand. The host must not alter SS or ESP while CAR is enabled or modify cache controls such as MTRRs from reset until the final return from `AmdInitPost`.

AGESA core files can be built as binary modules through a common routed entry point or source-integrated into the host environment’s ROM build. Platform solutions group related or compatible AMD products and have assigned names such as Danube and Maranello. Build customization proceeds by selecting the platform solution, build method, and individual options, with defaults provided through `<plat>Options.c`.

Stack procedures are native assembly macros intended for x86-64 APUs and must be included and called by the host. `OEM_SEGMENT1_START` supplies very early AMD initialization controls and must precede stack setup and entry into 32-bit mode. Stack establishment divides pre-memory cache among processor cores, maps it into global address space, configures MTRRs, creates a `UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF` frame, and runs on every core. In protected mode, SS must already reference a GDT descriptor with a zero base; real mode uses a 16-bit segment:offset stack. EBX is preserved for stackless return, and status codes cover success, stack reentry, and unknown processor families. Stack removal is performed once main memory is available, only by the BSP, without changing the synchronized MTRR map; it disables CAR and flushes cache lines. AArch64 APUs with a PSP do not use these stack and very-early macros because the PSP initializes DRAM.

`AmdCreateStruct` allocates, default-initializes, and returns an AGESA parameter structure. It supports pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, and host-preallocated storage. With `ByHost`, the host must provide sufficient space and avoid modifying the standard header, because the initialized structure overlays the original parameter block. `AmdReleaseStruct` releases that storage, and the creation and release procedures must be paired.

Other host services obtain DIMM data-eye bitmaps, APIC addresses, pre-memory execution-cache capacity, processor-die PCI addresses, and the socket, die, and core of the executing processor. A memory-address service maps an address to its socket, channel, DIMM, chip select, bank, row, and column for FRU identification and error-location reporting. Additional interfaces merge requested MMIO ranges into processor mappings and read successive entries from a circular event log, returning the oldest entry, application-specific status and data fields, and a zero `EventInfo` when the log is empty.

NVIDIA Corporation reported that Stephen C. Neal was appointed to its Board of Directors on March 30, 2019. Under NVIDIA’s 2007 Amended and Restated Equity Incentive Plan, Neal received 1,419 restricted stock units vesting semiannually over three years and 139 pro-rated annual restricted stock units vesting on May 15, 2019. He also received a pro-rated annual cash retainer of $10,890 and entered into an indemnification agreement related to his board service.

Cover 2 is a zone coverage commonly used in a 4-3 defense to stop short routes while two safeties protect against deep throws. The corners and three linebackers play underneath, with each safety responsible for a deep half. It allows defenders to read routes while watching the quarterback. Its strengths include coverage of hitches, slants, quick passes, and smoke screens, as well as support against perimeter runs because hard corners can attack quickly. Its weaknesses include multiple vertical routes and trips formations, which can overload a safety, plus run vulnerabilities against 2x2 and trips formations due to insufficient box support or a lack of weak-side overhang. Standard assignments are flat zones to the corners, deep halves to the safeties, hook/curl zones to the outside linebackers, and the middle hole to the Mike linebacker. “Switch” Cover 2 has corners bail to deep halves while safeties play the flats; a 1-high-looking variation disguises the actual two-high shell and uses a safety in the middle hole.

Emirates Airlines reversed its plan to remove Hindu meals after negative customer feedback, especially from Hindus, and said it would continue offering the option. Hindu passengers could still choose from a variety of regional vegetarian and non-vegetarian meals.

The study analyzes all 1,076 articles published in the Information Systems Education Journal from 2003–2024, using co-occurrence networks of author-supplied keywords grouped into five periods and visualized with VOSviewer. It identifies distinct eras: foundational IS education topics in 2003–2007; broader pedagogy and student concerns in 2008–2012, the most diverse period with 12 clusters; cybersecurity, big data, analytics, and pedagogy in 2013–2017; COVID-19-related education topics and separate business and data analytics clusters in 2018–2022; and reduced topical diversity in 2023–2024, with three clusters centered on pedagogy, analytics, and artificial intelligence. Across the full network, pedagogy and curriculum remained central themes. The authors note limitations from relying only on author-supplied keywords and the potential inflation of terms through special issues. They recommend future analyses incorporating titles and abstracts, allowing the data to define eras, and monitoring the growing prominence of artificial intelligence and generative AI.

US January non-farm payrolls rose 200,000, above expectations, while unemployment held at 4.1%. Hourly wages rose 0.3% monthly and 2.9% annually, the fastest annual gain since 2009. The data strengthened the case for a March Fed rate rise and potentially additional hikes, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield above 2.8% and the 2-year yield to its highest since September 2008.

On November 27, 2001, FERC extended NYISO’s Automated Mitigation Procedures (AMP) through April 30, 2002, rather than the requested October 31, 2002, and waived prior notice so the extension could take effect November 1. NYISO must file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, effective May 1. The proposal must address AMP refinements, coordination with existing and proposed mitigation measures, possible exemptions for new generation and energy-limited resources, and must-run mitigation consistent with ISO-NE and PJM. FERC also urged collaboration on a unified Northeast mitigation plan.

The AMP prospectively mitigates bids during day-ahead security-constrained unit commitment when prices exceed $150 and conduct and impact thresholds are met, eliminating the one-day delay in manual mitigation. NYISO committed to limiting mitigation to zones and hours failing the impact test and exempting bids at or below 50 MW unless market power is demonstrated. Supporters considered AMP necessary to prevent market power, while opponents, including Enron, alleged flawed calculations, unnecessary mitigation, barriers to efficient market participation, and inadequate consultation. FERC recognized these concerns while finding AMP a temporary means to protect customers pending further review.

Ryan Carter said no significant changes were needed and that the team would rely on playoff experience and locker-room confidence. The 5-day low overnight strategy takes a position in the S&P 500 when it opens at a five-day low and closes above its opening price, entering at the close and exiting at the next open. It exploits mean reversion and the market’s upward bias, with an average 0.04% return from close to next open. A SPY backtest from 1993 onward reported performance from 2005 forward: 15.93% average profit and 0.26% average return per trade; excluding a 6% October 2008 winner, average profit was 0.17%.

New York’s Excelsior Scholarship Program is changing how students and families compare public and private colleges by offering tuition-free SUNY or CUNY attendance to eligible graduates from households earning below $110,000. The last-dollar program covers $6,670 in annual tuition but not fees, room, board or books. This year’s budget includes $118 million for about 27,000 students, and the income ceiling will eventually rise to $125,000.

For 17-year-old Gianna Ruffle, cost is her leading criterion. Her parents encouraged her to use Excelsior at the College at Brockport if she were admitted, while she awaits decisions from St. John Fisher, Roberts Wesleyan and Nazareth. Her family is comparing private-college scholarships and financial aid while seeking to minimize loans. A high school counselor reports that more students are considering SUNY, CUNY and Monroe Community College since Excelsior began.

The program places particular pressure on small regional private colleges that draw heavily from local economies. Administrators fear declining in-state enrollment and further financial strain, while selective institutions such as Columbia, Cornell and Colgate are less affected because their reputations outweigh cost. Private colleges collectively enroll nearly 500,000 students and employ about 180,000 people.

Several private institutions have introduced tuition reductions and aid initiatives in response. Canisius lowered tuition by about $8,000 after enrollment fell roughly 6 percent and offers a limited number of $6,000 Enhanced Tuition Awards. Roberts Wesleyan guarantees qualifying students will graduate in four years or the college will pay remaining schooling costs and guarantees at least $8,000 annually in merit aid. Le Moyne’s “Promise NY” offers New York students $10,000 over four years, regardless of income, along with an internship and alumni mentor. St. Bonaventure increased scholarships by up to $4,000 annually, while St. John Fisher welcomed its largest freshman class and Nazareth reported a strong incoming class.

Regional colleges argue that Excelsior favors public institutions and that expanding the existing Tuition Assistance Program would have been a fairer solution. Some administrators also question the long-term sustainability of publicly funded free tuition.

Text messaging has become a popular, immediate communication method, prompting apps that extend traditional texts with media and other features. Music Messenger lets users send selected songs for free. WhatsApp provides free messaging between users with different phone types, supporting photos, videos, sound clips, emoticons, personalized backgrounds, and automatic contact syncing. Facebook Messenger offers media sharing, HD video chats, sound clips, group chats, customizable emojis and text colors, and is free without advertising.

The disclosure describes an image-processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and computer-readable storage medium for placing an object, such as an advertisement, into a video. The method obtains a multi-frame video, places a target three-dimensional model on a target plane in a first frame, and establishes calibration feature points on a model surface of the model. It determines the feature points’ three-dimensional world coordinates and first-frame pixel coordinates, then calculates the first-frame camera pose.

The target plane is tracked to determine camera poses for subsequent frames. In some embodiments, frame-to-reference homography matrices are calculated and optimized using image correlations, with occluded pixels excluded; feature-point matching is an alternative. A perspective-n-point algorithm can then calculate each camera’s position and orientation from feature coordinates, pixel coordinates, and camera intrinsic parameters. The target three-dimensional model is replaced with a target model, positioned in the world coordinate system, projected into each frame according to the corresponding camera pose, and synthesized into a target video.

A neural network may identify planes for user selection, while model placement and pose adjustment may be manual or automatic. Claimed benefits include lower computational requirements, faster processing, convenient operation, high accuracy, and applicability to varied videos. The apparatus implements these functions, and the method may also be executed using blockchain-stored video and advertisement data.

The Federal Reserve proposed changes to the Volcker Rule that would apply its strictest limits to banks engaged in the most trading, seeking to reduce uncertainty for banks. Part of Dodd-Frank and named for former Fed Chair Paul Volcker, the rule bars large banks from using depositors’ money for risky proprietary trading.

The proposal comes as the Trump administration and Congress move to loosen post-2008 financial regulation. Congress recently rolled back parts of Dodd-Frank, easing oversight, capital requirements and Volcker Rule compliance for about two dozen banks below new thresholds. Consumer advocates warn that weakening the rule would allow banks again to use customers’ money for high-risk investments, while banking lawyers say proprietary trading desks are unlikely to return.

Fed Chair Jerome Powell has said post-crisis rules could be improved, while Fed Governor Randal Quarles has advocated overhauling, but not eliminating, the regulatory package.

Lotte Chemical plans to list its Malaysian petrochemical subsidiary, Lotte Chemical Titan, on Bursa Malaysia in Q3 2017. The IPO, previously shelved amid fraud investigations, could raise $1–$1.5 billion to expand facilities in Indonesia and Malaysia.

Gary Gensler frames Bitcoin as the first use case of blockchain technology and explains that understanding its inner workings helps establish ground truths about its operation. Bitcoin is presented as a timestamped, append-only log of transaction blocks maintained through distributed consensus. Key design features include cryptographic hash functions, digital signatures, Merkle trees, block headers, peer-to-peer networking, nodes, proof-of-work consensus, nonces, native currency, and transactions.

Hash functions map inputs of any size to fixed-size outputs and are designed to be deterministic, efficient, preimage-resistant, collision-resistant, and resistant to predicting outputs from partial inputs. They connect blocks, compress transaction data, and help detect tampering, although Bitcoin’s immutability is probabilistic rather than absolute and depends on the continuing security of its hash functions.

Bitcoin block headers contain a version number, the previous block’s hash, a Merkle root, a timestamp, a difficulty target, and a nonce. Merkle trees efficiently summarize and verify large numbers of transactions. Lightweight nodes can download headers rather than complete transaction histories.

Asymmetric cryptography uses public-private key pairs. A private key creates digital signatures that a corresponding public key verifies. Secure random-number generation is essential for key creation. Bitcoin addresses are distinct from public keys and are produced by hashing the public key twice and encoding the result in Base58.

Bitcoin uses a transaction ledger with inputs, outputs, and lock times to address double spending. Mining creates Bitcoin as an incentive for maintaining consensus; rewards have declined through periodic halving, and the supply is capped at 21 million Bitcoin. As mining competition and electricity costs increase, miners increasingly join pools. Future lectures will address consensus protocols and transactions in greater detail.

Solar power’s expansion was driven by energy independence, environmental benefits, and concern about rising greenhouse-gas emissions. Atmospheric CO₂ had reached 380 ppm in 2006, and IPCC data projected substantial further increases without major policy changes. The Kyoto Protocol created a growing carbon market, while more than 1,000 pro-solar policies and public subsidies expanded worldwide support. Renewables supplied 13% of global energy in 2006, but photovoltaics provided only 0.04% of electricity.

Commercial photovoltaic cells, introduced in the 1950s, reached efficiencies of 10%–20% by 2006. Although solar electricity still cost two to three times as much as conventional power, photovoltaic production grew 41% annually from 2003 to 2006 and was expected to continue growing rapidly. Japan led global shipments, Europe ranked second, and China became the third-largest producer in 2006, exporting more than 90% of its products. Global PV demand reached 2,500 MWp in 2006.

The industry’s value chain comprised silicon production, ingot and wafer manufacture, cell and module production, and system installation. Silicon and wafer producers held the highest margins, while module production was highly fragmented and low-margin. Rapid manufacturing growth created a silicon shortage, raising input prices and prompting substantial capacity expansion. Solar systems generally cost $25–50 cents per kWh, compared with $4–6 cents for conventional generation. Residential installations became the largest market segment, while commercial customers used solar as a hedge against electricity prices or for public-relations benefits. Large utility-scale projects had encountered operational and financial difficulties.

SunPower was founded in 1987 by Stanford professor Richard Swanson to commercialize solar-concentrator technology before shifting toward flat-plate cells. Projects for Honda and NASA demonstrated the need for larger-scale production. A partnership with Cypress Semiconductor, begun in 2001, brought semiconductor manufacturing expertise, enabled commercial cell production in late 2004, and preceded SunPower’s 2005 NASDAQ listing. SunPower produced about 20 MW in 2005, expected approximately 65 MW in 2006, and projected revenues above $220 million for 2006, when it recorded its first profitable quarter. It subsequently expanded into modules and wafers, secured silicon through an agreement with DC Chemical, formed a Chinese ingot-manufacturing venture, and acquired large-installation firm PowerLight for $335 million.

SunPower’s principal capability was its commercially available high-efficiency back-contact solar cells, whose design exposed more silicon to sunlight and produced a uniform black appearance. The design required about twice as many manufacturing steps as a typical cell process and elevated capital costs. Process development occurred in the Philippines, while manufacturing was conducted in the United States. Higher efficiency allowed more generating capacity in limited spaces, reduced installation requirements, and earned installer willingness to pay at least a 10% premium. SunPower targeted average cell efficiency of at least 22% by early 2007 through lower silicon use per watt and thinner wafers.

Competition included market leader Sharp Solar, fast-growing Q-Cells, vertically integrated REC Group, thin-film manufacturer First Solar, rapidly expanding Chinese producer SunTech, and Citizenre’s alternative ownership and electricity-service model. With the competitive landscape evolving rapidly, SunPower faced strategic choices involving module pricing, manufacturing improvements, or a combination of both.

A North Korean missile launched near Sinpo on Sunday failed almost immediately. The White House described it as medium-range, while the Pentagon provided no details. Analysts said the failure may have involved a new, immature system; unnamed U.S. officials identified it as a liquid-fueled KN-17 Scud variant potentially capable of hitting ships. Another expert said it may have been a previously untested design displayed in Saturday’s Pyongyang parade. Despite speculation that U.S. cyberattacks caused the failure, John Schilling said the missiles lacked digital or electronic propulsion systems that could be hacked. Separately, Jim Mattis ordered a review of the U.S. nuclear deterrent.
Jim Dowd chose New Hampshire over Michigan because it was closer to home. He plans to stay until NHL-ready, called the game exciting, and is accompanied by his father.

Equity represents ownership in a corporation and returns come through dividends and capital gains. Common stockholders are residual claimants after bondholders, giving them unlimited upside while limiting losses to their investment. Limited liability, voting rights, and access to public markets support innovation and capital formation. Short sales also improve market efficiency by incorporating negative information into prices.

Equity markets are divided into primary markets, where securities are first issued, and secondary markets for existing securities. Primary issuance, including IPOs, is highly cyclical and sensitive to business and credit conditions. Secondary-market trading is less cyclical and has grown substantially due to internet trading, electronic communications networks, and electronic order routing, making trading faster, cheaper, and more accessible.

The Dividend Discount Model values a stock as the present value of expected future dividends discounted at risk-adjusted rates. Unlike bonds, equities involve uncertainty in both future cash flows and discount rates. Market prices determine appropriate discount rates based on the risks of particular cash flows and overall market conditions.

With constant dividends and discount rates, the model becomes the perpetuity formula, \(P=D/r\). With constant dividend growth, the Gordon growth model is \(P=D_1/(r-g)\), requiring \(r>g\) for a sustainable perpetuity. Large or unexpectedly changing growth expectations can produce major price swings. Rearranging the model shows that the required return equals dividend yield plus expected growth, emphasizing that future investment opportunities contribute to corporate value beyond current dividends.

These simplified formulas apply primarily to steady-state situations. When dividends change, analysts must forecast the full dividend path or value separate periods with annuity formulas, though such long-range forecasting is difficult and inaccurate. Dividend policies also tend to remain stable because cuts are viewed negatively, although temporary suspensions and extraordinary dividends can occur.

The offside trap is a defensive maneuver in which all back defenders move upfield together just before a forward pass, leaving the leading attacker offside. If the attacker receives the ball and gains an advantage from the offside position, an indirect free kick should be awarded. Although widely adopted around the mid-20th century, the tactic has become riskier because offside laws have changed and attacks increasingly use short passes rather than through balls.

The trap exposes the goalkeeper if it fails. Failure commonly results from defenders not moving simultaneously or an attacker remaining still to avoid involvement, allowing an onside teammate to play the ball. Coaches should consider players’ understanding and coordination, their goalkeeper’s ability to handle consequences, the opponent’s style, and the team’s formation. The tactic is generally more suitable against teams relying on through balls and less effective against teams using quick, short passes and skilled, fast attackers. A flat back four facilitates execution more readily than a stopper-sweeper alignment.

Before executing the trap, defenders must align across the field, move in unison, maintain awareness of teammates and attackers, anticipate forward passes, and communicate continuously. At least one attacker must be in the defending half and ahead of the ball, with sufficient space around the defenders.

One defender, usually the upfield defensive coordinator, must exclusively call for the trap using a unique verbal or non-verbal signal. A non-verbal signal may be preferable in noisy stadiums, though opponents may observe it. When attackers begin forward runs and the passer appears ready to pass, defenders must immediately sprint forward together, generally three to five yards, to create clear space between the attacker and the next-to-last defender.

The trap may be used in normal play or on free kicks and requires extensive, varied practice. Opponents may scout the tactic, adapt after its first use, and learn to defeat it, so overusing it increases the risk of goals.

This protocol outlines a systematic review of rapid response team (RRT) service implementation and redesign in hospitals. It will include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies examining novel RRT services or changes to established services, without restrictions on publication status, language, year, or comparator. The review aims to describe implementation methods, reasons for change, implementation timelines, and measures of implementation success.

Searches will cover Medline, CINAHL, Embase, The Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, reference lists, conference abstracts, and expert contacts. Records will be screened and extracted independently by two authors, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Data will cover study and team characteristics, implementation methods, and quantitative and qualitative outcome assessments. Risk of bias will be assessed using the JBI checklist, and findings will be synthesized narratively with simple descriptive statistics and additional statistical analysis in SPSS if required.

The review follows Cochrane and PRISMA guidance, with a PRESS-based search strategy. It has been registered on medRxiv, requires no ethical approval, and has no external funding. Expected limitations include heterogeneity in team names, composition, resources, and outcome reporting, as well as limited studies on service implementation and change management.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit SAR data-acquisition device with an analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and precision reference buffer. Each analog input has a resistive impedance of at least 1 MΩ independent of ADC and signal frequencies, allowing direct sensor or source connection without external amplifiers. Matching external source resistance between AIN_P and AIN_M helps minimize offset error.

Internal overvoltage protection is provided on all analog inputs, although external devices are still recommended for surges, ESD, and EFT events. Input resistors and antiparallel diodes limit input current; with AVDD at 5 V, the internal protection is described as withstanding up to ±20 V. Protection also operates with floating AVDD, although internal transistor breakdown is noted beyond ±15 V. The PGA supports nine programmable input ranges through RANGE_SEL[3:0], with a default range of ±3V × VREF. A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter at the PGA output typically has a 500 kHz cutoff.

The device supports an internal or external 4.096 V reference selected through INTREF_DIS. The internal reference is factory-trimmed and temperature-compensated from −40°C to +125°C, but its initial accuracy can shift after mechanical or thermal stress and PCB solder reflow. It requires at least 4.7 µF at REFIO. External-reference mode uses the internal buffer, with a minimum 10 µF at REFCAP plus nearby 1 µF decoupling. The reference buffer’s typical and maximum temperature drifts are specified as 0.5 ppm/°C and 2 ppm/°C.

Single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs are supported using straight-binary output. The LSB size equals FSR/2¹⁶. Alarm features include programmable high and low input thresholds with common hysteresis and fixed AVDD thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. An active-high alarm can be routed through the multifunction pin, while active and tripped flags are stored in ALARM_REG.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous protocols with internal or external clock sources. Devices can operate individually or in daisy-chain configurations; an N-device chain requires an optimal 32 × N SCLK capture edges and returns data from device N through device 1. The interface operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, with configurable application reset or full power-on reset.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and 32-bit commands. A transfer frame starts on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on its rising edge. A 32-clock frame is optimal; short frames permit partial reads but invalidate writes, while long frames use the last 32 shifted bits as the command. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device addresses, range settings, alarm flags, and parity.

An application example combines an ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to provide eight configurable industrial voltage or current channels. Other guidance covers alarm hysteresis for NTC temperature sensing, separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, supply decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, analog/digital PCB partitioning, and reference-capacitor placement.

Air cargo containerization supports rapid intermodal transport by commercial and military operators. Demand is driven by global shipping needs, expanding cargo fleets, and defense requirements, while lightweight, IATA-standard containers accommodate varied loads. Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeffrey McMahon, head of the Industrial Markets division and a former treasurer, to restore investor confidence. Fastow was placed on leave after the SEC opened an informal inquiry into his management of the LJM Cayman and LJM2 partnerships, which conducted financing, hedging and asset transactions with Enron. Fastow had left the partnerships in July amid conflict-of-interest concerns; Enron denied wrongdoing and said it was cooperating with the inquiry, which had not yet included subpoenas. McMahon reportedly had raised concerns about the arrangements while serving as treasurer.

The partnerships generated a $35 million charge and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity when Enron ended its relationships with them, including repurchasing 62 million LJM2 shares for $1.2 billion. Enron also reported a $618 million third-quarter loss and $1.01 billion in write-offs. Investors remained concerned about complex off-balance-sheet partnerships, inadequate disclosure, potential obligations exceeding $3 billion tied to Marlin and Whitewing, possible stock dilution and a credit-rating downgrade. Moody’s had placed $13 billion of Enron debt on watch.

Enron’s shares fell 17% to $16.41, a six-year low, after the announcement and roughly halved in about a week, while Dynegy and other energy traders also declined. Analysts were divided over whether Fastow’s removal demonstrated responsiveness to investors or instead suggested wrongdoing; several continued to recommend selling the stock and called for fuller disclosure. Enron maintained that its operations were functioning normally and that it remained financially strong and liquid.

Shareholder lawsuits alleged that Enron misstated asset values, concealed related-party arrangements and obligations involving its stock, and that executives traded on inside information. Other included reports covered proposed grading of corporate directors, modest gains in small-cap stocks, falling utility shares amid Enron’s troubles and lower power-profit expectations, and mixed European trading.

The passage argues that China’s one-child policy and emphasis on grades have produced overly protected children while neglecting character, morality, independence, and individual development. It criticizes knowledge- and discipline-centered education for suppressing students’ interests and cites poor practical skills, emotional and behavioral problems, and severe responses to adversity among young people. Earlier judgments of American and Chinese education are presented as having later proved mistaken.

Recommended reforms include equal access to higher education, guidance toward personal interests, moral and humanity education, and teaching children to give selflessly and contribute to society. Traditional Chinese moral education is presented as a valuable foundation, emphasizing unity of moral teaching and personal cultivation, knowledge joined with practice, and humanity’s integral relationship with nature. The case of student Yao Jiaxin illustrates concern that academic achievement does not necessarily reflect moral behavior.

An international geoarchaeological team led by Angus Graham conducted the most comprehensive survey of Karnak Temple near Luxor, analyzing 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments. The evidence indicates that regular Nile flooding made the site unsuitable for permanent occupation before about 2520 BCE, while pottery supports earliest occupation during the Old Kingdom (2591–2152 BCE). Karnak began on an island of high ground formed by Nile channels; as the channels diverged and silted up, construction expanded across them. The eastern channel was more defined—and possibly larger—than the previously emphasized western channel. Researchers also found that ancient Egyptians deposited desert sand into channels, potentially creating buildable land. The island’s emergence from surrounding water resembles Old Kingdom accounts of a creator god or “primeval mound” rising from the “Waters of Chaos,” suggesting that Karnak’s location may have had religious significance.

On March 26, 2020, NVIDIA entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured senior notes: $1.5 billion of 2.850% notes due 2030, $1.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2040, $2.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2050, and $0.5 billion of 3.700% notes due 2060. Net proceeds were approximately $4.97 billion after underwriting discounts and estimated offering expenses and will be used for general corporate purposes, potentially including debt repayment.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Output voltage is programmed with a VSENSE resistor divider referenced to 0.613 V. A capacitor on SS controls soft start; synchronous-rectifier outputs activate after the SS voltage exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set by an internal RT oscillator over 100 kHz to 2 MHz, by an external SYNC clock at twice the desired switching frequency, or through primary-secondary synchronization between two controllers. Models have single or dual primary outputs and synchronous-rectifier outputs; external gate drivers are recommended because each output has roughly 150 mA peak capability.

Programmable dead time, leading-edge blank time, and duty-cycle limits support multiple topologies and operating modes. Pulse skipping reduces minimum-on-time problems at high frequencies. CS_ILIM senses primary current against COMP/2 for peak-current-mode PWM and triggers protection at 1.05 V. Overcurrent conditions initiate cycle-by-cycle limiting followed by hiccup delay, shutdown, and soft-start restart. The FAULT pin supports external fault protection, while slope compensation and Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation address peak-current-mode stability and control-loop response. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts below 160°C.

A synchronous GaN push-pull design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz and 5 V output. Selected values include a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns, a 49.9 kΩ LEB resistor, a 33 nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40 μH primary inductance, 170 V primary FETs, 80 V synchronous-rectifier FETs, a 0.47 μH output inductor, 2.3 mF total output capacitance, 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, 102 kΩ slope-compensation resistor, and Type 2A compensation components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 μF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control signals from switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, joining analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, and placing filtering, compensation, and bypass components close to their associated pins.

The article backtests two trend-following strategies and one momentum strategy for Bitcoin using free Yahoo Finance BTC-USD data from 2015 through April 2021, excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes. A 100/250-day simple-moving-average crossover returned 115% CAGR versus 94% for buy-and-hold, made three trades, and avoided the worst drawdowns, although its maximum drawdown was 65% in 2018. A momentum strategy comparing Bitcoin’s close with its close 25 days earlier also beat buy-and-hold and reduced drawdown despite a low win rate. Nobel Prizes honor major scientific discoveries but recognize only a few fields and a small number of contributors. Many disciplines, including ecology, ocean, weather, climate and geology studies, do not qualify, while hundreds of researchers behind recognized discoveries may go uncredited because no more than three people can share a prize.

The prizes have also been criticized for demographic and geographic bias. Winners are predominantly white men from wealthy scientific hubs in the United States and Western Europe. Underrepresented scientists face barriers to leadership, funding and access to major research institutions. Long nomination and career timelines further favor established researchers.

Katalin Karikó’s 2023 medicine prize recognized her mRNA work, which enabled rapid COVID-19 vaccine development. Nobel rules are unlikely to change substantially because they are largely fixed by Alfred Nobel’s will. Despite their limitations, the prizes remain influential in publicizing science and demonstrating its societal value.

NFL kickers specialize in extra points, field goals, and kickoffs. Extra points are worth one point, while field goals, typically attempted from 25–60 yards, are worth three. Kickers also direct kickoffs, seek touchbacks, and execute onside kicks to create possession opportunities. Their reliability can determine fourth-down decisions, field position, and outcomes in close games.

The position requires accuracy, lower-body power, consistent technique, and flexibility. NFL kickers are generally smaller and slim, estimated at 5'10"–6'2" and 180–210 pounds. Kickers and punters are usually separate positions, though kickers often substitute for injured punters.

Notable kickers discussed include Justin Tucker, Morten Andersen, and Adam Vinatieri, who hold records for field-goal accuracy, longest field goal, consecutive field goals made, and NFL scoring.

This continuation patent application describes systems, methods, and articles of manufacture for using deep convolutional neural networks to detect splice sites and aberrant splicing in genomic sequences. An atrous convolutional neural network (ACNN) uses dilated convolutions, residual blocks, skip connections, batch normalization, and ReLU layers to capture long-range sequence context while using relatively few parameters. The ACNN processes one-hot-encoded nucleotide sequences and outputs donor-splice-site, acceptor-splice-site, and non-splicing scores for each target nucleotide; normalized scores support classification.

Several ACNN configurations are described: SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000. These vary in upstream and downstream context length, residual-block groups, convolution-window sizes, and dilation rates, with dilation progressing non-exponentially across groups. The disclosure also describes conventional CNN implementations, parallel processing, and separate training and production servers.

For aberrant-splicing detection, reference and variant sequences are scored independently and compared nucleotide by nucleotide. Differences exceeding a predetermined threshold classify a variant as causing aberrant splicing and therefore pathogenic; differences below the threshold classify it as benign or non-aberrant. Threshold selection using benign common variants and pathogenic rare variants is also described, along with applications to autism spectrum disorder and developmental delay disorder.

High-κ dielectrics for transistors and capacitors require both high permittivity and wide band gaps, but current materials such as SiO₂, perovskite oxides, and HfO₂ have limitations involving leakage, processing temperature, integration, or attainable capacitance. Machine-learning screening is promising, although prior models predict ionic dielectric constants less accurately than electronic contributions.

The study developed a joint model that separately predicts Born effective charge tensors with an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network and phonon force constants with the SevenNet machine-learning potential, then analytically combines them to calculate ionic dielectric tensors. The charge model achieved an average R² of 0.982 across 928 oxides containing 45 elements. The joint ionic-dielectric model achieved R² = 0.843 and RMSE = 0.129, substantially outperforming a direct model with R² = 0.418.

A stepwise screen of 8,717 nonmetallic, nonmagnetic Materials Project oxides used phonon stability and a figure of merit defined as average dielectric constant multiplied by band gap, followed by first-principles validation. This identified 38 previously unreported high-κ oxide candidates; 12 exceeded the validated figure of merit of KTaO₃. Ionic contributions exceeded 90% of total dielectric response for the identified materials and nine qualifying training oxides. Thirty-six candidates contained d⁰ transition metals, and most featured flexible perovskite-related oxygen-octahedral frameworks. Ten had already been synthesized, including LiBi₄Nb₃O₁₄ and LaYO₃ under ambient conditions, but their dielectric properties remain unmeasured. Proposed extensions include non-oxides, finite-temperature effects, band alignment, and defect studies.

The higher highs and higher lows pattern generally signals an uptrend, but backtests of SPY, GLD, and TLT found weak short-term performance. The pattern is a short-term reversal pattern but is too weak to serve alone as a trading signal or short strategy.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is an eighth-generation data center accelerator built on the Ampere GA100 architecture using TSMC’s 7nm process. Its 108 streaming multiprocessors contain 432 third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, binary, and 2:4 structured-sparsity operations. Compared with Tesla V100, A100 provides 2.5× FP16 mixed-precision performance, 5× with sparsity, 10× TF32 performance, 2.5× FP64 performance, and up to 20× sparse INT8 performance. Fine-grained structured sparsity reduces storage and bandwidth requirements while doubling Tensor Core throughput.

A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3× V100 read bandwidth, larger combined L1/shared memory, compute data compression, cache-residency controls, asynchronous copy and barrier instructions, and improved task-graph execution. Its Multi-Instance GPU feature securely partitions the device into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, and migration support.

Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4, NVSwitch, Magnum IO, and Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet support multi-node scaling. CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, L2 residency controls, asynchronous operations, and improved Cooperative Groups reductions. A100 also adds hardware JPEG decoding, optical-flow acceleration, five video-decoding units, and improved atomic operations.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitch devices, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and 4.8 TB/s of aggregate bidirectional bandwidth. Its networking includes eight 200 Gb/s Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters, and MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators within the system.

University of Edinburgh researchers analyzed DNA from more than 52,000 mostly middle-aged men in the UK BioBank, identifying 287 independent genetic signals associated with male pattern baldness. Forty signals were on the X chromosome, which men inherit from their mothers. The genetic patterns were only somewhat predictive of hair-loss severity but may help identify men at greatest risk and potential treatment targets. Researchers said the findings advance understanding of hair loss’s genetic causes but remain a long way from accurately predicting an individual’s pattern.

Kenya’s urban slums lacked adequate sanitation, forcing many Nairobi residents to use unsafe public facilities or “flying toilets.” Sanergy, founded in 2011 by three MIT Sloan students, developed a business spanning the sanitation value chain. Its nonprofit Fresh Life franchises prefabricated toilets to entrepreneurs, landlords and schools; Sanergy collects the waste, treats it through co-composting, and sells the resulting Evergrow organic fertilizer through its Farm Star business.

By 2015, Fresh Life had franchised 615 toilets serving about 32,000 people. Sanergy set ambitious expansion targets, including 887 toilets by the end of 2016 and 36,000 by 2020, although Fresh Life had missed its 2015 growth goals. Farm Star sold 118 tons of fertilizer in 2015 and aimed to exceed 2,000 tons annually by 2018.

Communications manager Medora Brown was tasked with developing a social media strategy that would support each brand despite limited resources. Her challenges included selecting platforms, producing consistent content, demonstrating return on investment, and addressing distinct audiences: toilet franchisees and users, farmers, investors, donors and other stakeholders.

Kenya had rapidly expanding internet and mobile-phone access and a growing social media sector. Facebook was the dominant platform, while Twitter and LinkedIn also had substantial audiences. However, slum residents had limited and infrequent access, generally using cybercafés for practical purposes such as finding work or requesting financial help. Farmers were more active online, using Facebook and WhatsApp to discuss farming and products. Personal contact and trust remained important, particularly when selling sanitation franchises, fertilizer or fundraising.

Sanergy maintained separate Facebook pages for Fresh Life, Farm Star and its corporate brand, while also using WhatsApp, Twitter, Instagram and a corporate blog. Brown proposed making the blog a central content repository whose material could be adapted across brands.

Fresh Life primarily relied on door-to-door outreach, events, referrals, SMS and other personal approaches to recruit franchisees and encourage residents to use its toilets. Farm Star used Facebook advertising and customer testimonials to generate leads, with promising early costs, while testing WhatsApp and SMS-based educational content. For corporate fundraising, Sanergy sought foundations and major donors through media coverage and thought leadership, while its founder remained skeptical that social media could reach major investors accustomed to personal networks.

The case leaves open whether social media could build sufficient trust, expand adoption among slum residents, support consultative fertilizer sales, and attract major funders in Kenya.
