The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with GaN devices in buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN converter example operates at 500 kHz with a 5-V output. Selected values include a 205-kΩ frequency resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ PS/SP resistors, a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing approximately 7.5 ms of startup time. The transformer design targets a 35% duty cycle and 2.5:1 turns ratio, with 40 μH primary inductance used. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while an 80-V synchronous rectifier is used; a parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start and dead-time losses. The converter uses a 0.47-μH output inductor, a 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor with a 1:100 current-sense transformer, a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, and Type 2A frequency compensation targeting 10 kHz. At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is required for ripple and load transients, but 2.3 mF was used for additional single-event-transient mitigation. An optional LC filter can reduce output noise, with damping available if high-frequency peaking occurs. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, versus a 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load.

The controllers operate from 4 to 14 V and require at least a 0.1-μF input bypass capacitor; ceramic X5R or better capacitors placed close to VIN and AVSS are recommended. PCB guidance addresses isolating feedback and control traces from noisy switching signals, minimizing switch-node copper and high-di/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, and using multiple vias to connect the CFP backside metallization to AVSS.

The document also lists application curves, related radiation reports and evaluation-module guides, documentation-update and support resources, ESD precautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The Hawk Offense is a high-post offense derived from the UCLA high-post rub and shuffle offense. Introduced to the NBA by Hubie Brown in Atlanta, it is designed primarily to exploit mismatches at off-guard or shooting guard, while also supporting wing isolation and post play.

The basic action uses a point guard dribble entry, a high-post back screen for the off-guard, and a rub cut toward the basket. The off-guard may also post up against a smaller defender. Defensive counters include bump-backs against defenders going under screens, post rolls and isolation after switches, slips against anticipated switches, and ball reversals against double teams. If no good shot develops, the offense reverses the ball and uses weakside down-screen and post actions.

Continuities include Flex, which uses continuous “pick-the-picker” screening; the Triangle Game, an inside screening game featuring wing shooters; and the Motion or Passing Game, which uses five-player movement to open the middle. Other variations include side screen, single/double, back screen, pin down, base screen, and post lob.

Successful implementation depends on spacing, execution, coordination, timing, nonverbal communication, and defensive recognition. Teaching recommendations include fundamental drills, combination and scrimmage work, and individual skill development. Game strategy emphasizes scouting opponents, identifying defensive reads, varying alignments and entries, attacking weaker defenders, and using organized screen actions as the shot clock winds down.

Grin is a secretive blockchain project using Harry Potter-themed identities and intended to implement Mimblewimble, a “scriptless” privacy technology derived from Confidential Transactions. Mimblewimble cancels spent outputs against inputs, verifies transaction balance and key ownership, and uses blinding keys, eliminating arbitrary scripts and reducing functionality to group or individual transfers. Its compression lets validators discard full transaction history and check only signatures and current unspent outputs, though it lacked wallet support and was estimated to be about 18 months from broader use.

Grin will initially issue Grin and a test currency. Andrew Poelstra’s accepted proposal permits a later soft fork adding a Bitcoin peg, with Bitcoin, test coins, and Grin coins indistinguishable to outside observers to share privacy.

Poelstra developed “scriptless scripts” to restore limited functionality. By having signatures sign script conditions, he demonstrated how ordinary signatures could support simple Lightning-style payments, while Schnorr signature differences could enable atomic swaps without extra blockchain space or explicit links between transactions. He also developed methods to link transactions across chains using different elliptic curves and to chain transactions like Lightning channels, with discrete logarithms providing the linkage. A Mimblewimble sidechain would remain larger than Bitcoin in real time but could become smaller for future validators because spent outputs and inputs could be deleted after verification.

Gamma-ray astronomy developed in the 1950s to study high-energy processes in astrophysical objects. Because cosmic gamma rays are not deflected by magnetic fields, they can identify their sources directly, but Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. Satellite instruments such as AGILE and Fermi avoid this limitation, yet their small effective areas limit sensitivity to faint, high-energy fluxes. Ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes instead use the atmosphere as a calorimeter, detecting Cherenkov light from particle showers with effective areas of roughly \(10^4\) m². Arrays such as MAGIC, H.E.S.S., and VERITAS combine multiple telescopes to reconstruct gamma-ray events and reject charged-cosmic-ray backgrounds.

The planned Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will provide full night-sky coverage, improved energy and spatial resolution, and a sensitivity range from about 20 GeV to 300 TeV. Large-Sized Telescopes will target 20–150 GeV, Medium-Sized Telescopes 150 GeV–5 TeV, and Small-Sized Telescopes 5–300 TeV. Arrays are planned in La Palma and Chile, with telescope prototypes and upgrades already underway. During CTAO’s first decade, 40% of observing time will be reserved for consortium Key Science Projects, including dark matter and fundamental-physics studies.

One major CTAO program will search for weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) through annihilation or decay gamma rays from dense targets such as the Galactic Center, the Large Magellanic Cloud, the Perseus Cluster, and dwarf spheroidal galaxies. Simulations indicate substantially improved constraints on TeV-scale WIMP annihilation, while searches for monochromatic gamma-ray lines could constrain annihilation cross-sections orders of magnitude below the thermal benchmark.

CTAO will also observe active galactic nuclei to study non-standard photon propagation over cosmological distances. Key topics include axion-like particle oscillations, the extragalactic background light, intergalactic magnetic fields, and Lorentz-invariance violation. Initial axion-like-particle constraints from NGC 1275 are described as not highly competitive but potentially improvable through other sources and analysis methods. Overall, CTAO is expected to enable multi-TeV source surveys and strong constraints on dark matter and exotic physics.

This scoping review aimed to identify maternal and fetal or neonatal genes that may influence susceptibility to prenatal Zika virus–induced brain injury and congenital Zika syndrome (CZS). Following PRISMA and PRISMA-P guidance, researchers searched multiple databases, screened 3,777 records after duplicate removal, assessed 59 full texts, and included 13 articles. These studies identified 23 candidate genes—six maternal and 17 fetal/neonatal—some associated with injury and others potentially protective. Reported candidates included TREM1, IL4, ADCY3, ADCY7, IL28B, and TLR3 in mothers, and DDIT4L, FOXG1, LHX2, CDK5RAP2, miR-124-1, TP53, NOS2, VEGFA, MTOR, TNF, IL12RB2, CXCL8, and CXCL10 in offspring. Their functions involve brain development, immune and inflammatory responses, angiogenesis, cell-cycle regulation, and cellular stress. The findings do not support a monogenic model for CZS. Small cohorts, multiple testing, population stratification, and limited functional validation constrain conclusions. The authors recommend larger pooled or genome-wide studies and cellular or animal gene manipulation to validate these genes, improve early risk prediction, and inform neuroprotective strategies. The findings may also guide research on brain injury caused by other prenatal viral infections.

A Finnish study of 5,800 public-sector employees found that sleep problems became less common after retirement. Researchers suggested that removing work-related stress and altered sleep timing may support better sleep, though some effects of poor working conditions may persist.

Gov. Gray Davis’s administration fired five consultants for possible conflicts of interest, while spokesman Steve Maviglio disclosed buying 300 Calpine shares for $12,000 and said the purchase relied on public information and created no conflict. Jones called for Maviglio’s dismissal and updated financial disclosures. Political consultants Mark Fabiani and Chris Lehane separately agreed to forgo state compensation and end their work under a settlement of a taxpayer lawsuit concerning their consulting for both Davis and Southern California Edison.

India’s state electricity boards reportedly lost $5.5 billion because of rising subsidies and power thefts. Enron sought to sell its 65% stake in the stalled $2.9 billion Dabhol project to the Indian government or lenders. India’s government directed IDBI-led financial institutions to arrange financing or a new investor to complete the project’s second phase, which needed $550 million, including $230 million not yet committed. The plant had stopped operating amid a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board.

Houston internet providers prepared for the Code Red worm’s expected reactivation, which could slow websites and overwhelm targeted servers; a Microsoft IIS patch was already available. Separately, Band-X, a bandwidth exchange operating since 1997, continued adapting to the market and reported $80 million in bandwidth trades in 2000 while expanding into telecommunications-minute and colocation exchanges.

DAFWA research found that deep ripping reduces compaction but may not improve water penetration and can worsen surface repellence when topsoil is dry. A 2016 trial found greater benefits from soil inversion or rotary spading. Strategies include avoiding dry sowing, delaying cereal seeding until after substantial rain, increasing seeding rates, applying banded wetting agents, and using other soil amelioration methods.

Digital leaders view a strong data culture as central to successful digital transformation, emphasizing learning mindsets, transparent data access, clear metrics, and organizational alignment. Culture coordinates employee efforts by aligning leadership beliefs, company values, and daily behavior. Digital laggards may value data-driven cultures but struggle due to entrenched habits, skills gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors is the hardest part of transformation and requires compelling, well-understood reasons, but organizations can advance by building on their strengths.

Technologically mature firms distinguish themselves through beliefs in learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement, reflected in company values and daily practices, though mature organizations must continue developing culturally. Organizations generally fall into four maturity patterns: data novices, insight-ready firms, tech-enabled firms, and data-reliant firms, each needing targeted actions to strengthen its data culture.

The lecture examines how long-term climate risk affects real estate values, investment decisions, and policy. Within the four-quadrant market model, climate impacts may affect rental cash flows and net operating income, or risk perceptions, financing, and capitalization rates. Responses also differ depending on whether tenants, owners, investors, or financiers initiate the market response.

Empirical studies cited suggest that climate-risk price adjustments often occur through cap rates rather than immediate rent changes. Properties with greater exposure to flooding or sea-level rise were about 3% less valuable when climate risk was more salient to buyers, despite no comparable rent change. Following Hurricane Sandy, even properties that were not directly damaged experienced roughly 9% lower prices than before the storm, while damaged properties eventually stabilized. These patterns were interpreted as investors updating long-term expectations about future risk and damage rather than experiencing current disruptions to property income.

Discount rates are especially consequential because climate risks may materialize over 50–100 years, making small changes in discount rates capable of materially changing present values. A Boston Seaport resilience example projected sea-level rises of 9 inches by 2030, 21 inches by 2050, and 40 inches by 2070, with potential damages ranging from about $140 million to $8 billion. Proposed protections could cost $500 million–$1 billion initially and $7 million–$15 million annually in maintenance. Whether the investment has a positive net present value depends heavily on the selected discount rate; in the example, rates below 4% make it positive. The discussion also emphasized uncertainty from changing projections, nonlinear climate processes, and tipping points, as well as differences between governments’ willingness to fund projects and private owners’ valuation of future risks.

Public investment could also create moral hazards by increasing developers’ confidence and concentrating new construction in areas that remain physically hazardous. The amount of damage would depend partly on continued development because protection is a district-wide public good. Conversely, sparsely developed areas would face lower expected damages, making protection harder to justify.

Climate beliefs are presented as an important source of valuation differences. Buyers may not accept scientific projections uniformly, and their beliefs affect both current bids and expected resale prices. Yale’s Climate Opinion Maps illustrate geographic and political variation: 72% of U.S. adults surveyed believed global warming was occurring, 14% did not, and the remainder were uncertain. Public prioritization of climate change also varied with economic conditions and partisan affiliation.

A study of Florida housing from 1997 to 2017 found that flood-zone properties consistently received a price discount, but the discount was about 7% larger in communities with stronger climate-change beliefs than in communities characterized as deniers, despite similar physical exposure. At the individual level, developers may prefer such communities because lower risk-related price discounts can increase expected profits. At the aggregate level, concentrating housing in hazardous locations can transfer future losses to residents, insurers, banks, and households unable to relocate.

Because climate risks are partly an information problem, the lecture reviewed disclosure requirements, including the addition of climate-risk information to home-seller disclosures. Evidence presented indicated that disclosure can prompt migration from risky locations, increase vacancies, and weaken affected housing markets. Related laboratory projects use natural-language processing to measure social-media sentiment across more than 100 countries, link extreme temperatures to an “emotional toll,” and study how hurricane information travels through Twitter networks and changes beliefs.

For estimating climate effects on housing, the lecture reviewed hedonic regression, matching, and difference-in-differences. Hedonic controls cannot eliminate omitted characteristics correlated with flood risk, such as ocean views or neighborhood decline, and matching compares similar properties at one point in time. Difference-in-differences compares treated and untreated properties before and after an event and requires parallel trends: without the event, both groups were assumed to have grown at similar rates.

The cited Hurricane Sandy study found a persistent 8% housing-price penalty for properties in flood zones, with penalties around 15% for properties suffering heavy damage. Other studies reported temporary or full recovery, depending on the hurricane, data, insurance conditions, and repair capacity; one commercial-property study found full recovery after two years. A lending study showed that flood-zone price differences were absent initially, appeared after Hurricane Fran, and increased further after Hurricane Floyd as risk beliefs changed. Open questions included whether insurance premiums, repair responsibilities, and government rebuilding support could produce temporary price effects or encourage continued building in hazardous areas.

This preprint proposes a high-impedance microstrip transmission-line resonator for multichannel RF coils at 10.5T, where high frequencies, parasitic capacitance, radiation losses, and electromagnetic coupling complicate coil-array design. Two 8 × 8 cm resonators were built from 3 mm copper tape on Teflon and evaluated using network-analyzer measurements with a human head phantom and Ansys simulations. The high-frequency mode was tuned to 447 MHz and matched to 50 Ω, achieving −21 dB interchannel coupling at a 10 mm gap. It remained decoupled at a 2 mm gap, whereas the 116 MHz mode showed strong coupling and a split resonant peak. Simulations produced distinct B1 distributions for each channel and a maximum B1+ of 2 μT/√W. The results support this approach as a practical method for designing robust, decoupled transceiver arrays for ultrahigh-field MRI.

Facebook apologized after its search auto-fill function produced suggestions involving sexual acts with minors when users typed "videos of," though the company said the predictions reflected what people search for rather than actual site content, and it does not allow sexually explicit imagery. Earlier in March 2018, Facebook sent a survey asking how pedophiles requesting pictures from a 14-year-old girl should be handled; vice president Guy Rosen called it a mistake and said it was unacceptable, adding the company works with authorities on such cases. Separately, Bloomberg reported that data on 50 million users was revealed during the 2016 presidential race, and Facebook's stock fell 8.1 percent to $170.06, its largest single-day drop since 2015.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 30, 2020, announcing its first-quarter 2020 financial results. Exhibit 99.1 contains the press release, Exhibit 99.2 provides information on non-GAAP financial measures, and Exhibit 101 includes the Inline XBRL cover page. The filing was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky.

Facing shrinking budgets, declining enrollment and rising specialized-needs caseloads, school districts are treating master schedules as an untapped resource. The authors argue AI optimization can turn scheduling into a strategic tool by analyzing teacher workloads, class sizes and thousands of possible schedules. Lubbock ISD and Edgewood ISD used AI-optimized schedules to rebalance classes and workloads, share staff and reinvest savings without layoffs, saving $2.2 million across 14 Lubbock schools and $1.05 million districtwide in Edgewood. Rather than replacing educators, AI freed scheduling teams to make faster, student-centered decisions. The authors conclude that districts should move beyond traditional schedulers and spreadsheets to allocate resources transparently and support educational priorities during fiscal uncertainty.

Sterling has averaged 2% April gains over the past 12 years, with consistent April strength against the dollar emerging only after 2004. With speculative short positions near records, analysts cited tax-year effects, corporate dividends, and a weaker dollar as possible supports for another April rise.

**Active Surfaces Case Summary**

Active Surfaces, founded in 2022 from MIT research, develops ultra-lightweight, flexible solar panels applicable to nearly any surface, manufactured using roll-to-roll printing for efficiency and low cost. Co-founders Dr. Richard Swartwout (Ph.D., Solar R&D and Printed Electronics, MIT) and Shiv Bhakta (MS/MBA, MIT; former Department of Energy and ExxonMobil) lead the company's solar R&D and commercial strategy.

The case posits 14 fictional transactions for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, including a $1,000,000 common stock issuance, a $24,000 two-year insurance payment, a $1 million revolving credit line (drawn $400,000; repaid $420,000), $2,000 of office supplies, $650,000 of manufacturing equipment, a $25,000 legal retainer (with $1,500 refunded), a $500,000 pilot project with $350,000 cash costs, a 20% down payment on a $1 million order, $325,000 of raw materials, and year-end depreciation of $65,000 and one year of insurance expense.

Assignment questions ask students to record the transactions via the balance sheet equation (ignoring taxes), prepare a December 31, 2023 balance sheet, and calculate fiscal 2023 net income and cash flow.

Audi’s battery-electric e-tron prototype has a drag coefficient of 0.28 and a WLTP range exceeding 400 kilometers; Audi says each 0.01 reduction can add about five kilometers. More than 1,000 hours of testing informed aerodynamic features that reduce drag by nearly 0.07 versus a comparable combustion-powered vehicle, adding about 35 kilometers per charge. These include narrow virtual camera mirrors, adaptive air suspension that lowers the body above 120 km/h, a fully enclosed underbody, dimpled battery protection, controllable cooling-air inlets, streamlined wheel-arch ducts, flat 19-inch wheels, and ultralow-resistance tires with recessed lettering.

Year 6 pupils and the PTA cleaned a bus at Swallowdale Primary School for conversion into a reading space. With seats removed and the bus made safe, it will be carpeted and painted as a woodland scene featuring children’s chosen characters.

The paper surveys graph similarity and distance methods, noting that similarity is difficult to define because it is multidimensional. Early approaches include Sussenguth’s exact graph matching, Zelinka’s distance based on the largest common induced subgraph, and extensions for graphs with different vertex counts. Inexact methods include graph edit distance, graph kernels, and measures based on topological indices or feature vectors. Most prior topological approaches use a single index, while a recent 20-index method loses information through binary conversion and reduces sensitivity.

The paper defines similarity and distance measures without requiring metric axioms, showing that they can be converted using \(d=1-s\), \(s=(M-d)/M\) for bounded distances, or \(s=1/(1+d)\) for unbounded distances. It introduces a method for connected graphs that scales at least three topological indices to \([0,1]\) and applies a \(p\)-distance measure. The approach is presented as less computationally demanding, comparable to an established metric, and more sensitive to subtle structural differences. Preliminary analyses cover random network models and the similarity of decane isomers.

A Jefferies analysis of Morning Consult data found that sentiment toward Disney and Disney+ fell to multiyear lows after the company temporarily halted and later restored Jimmy Kimmel’s show following his comments and pressure from the Trump administration. Both Democrats and Republicans reacted negatively, with Democrats showing the sharper decline. Disney also faced criticism for raising Disney+ subscription prices by $2 to $3 and for what some viewed as compromising free speech. However, Disney’s brand awareness reached a two-year high, while Disney+ awareness rose less, suggesting a potentially limited impact on streaming churn. Shares fell 6% over the past month, but analyst James Heaney retained a buy rating and $144 price target.

Functional emulsifier blends combine substances with specific or complementary emulsifying functions, mainly for oil- and water-based emulsions. Rising food-safety concerns, broader industrial use, and benefits such as improved texture and required hydrophile-lipophile balance support demand. Processed-food growth, health awareness, formulation innovations, and adoption in bakery and confectionery also favor the market.

North America is expected to lead because of major food-production centers and the presence of ADM and Cargill, while investment in food processing in emerging APAC countries is expected to drive the fastest growth. Food and beverages are projected to be the largest application segment, led by bakery, although personal care is expected to grow faster. Major companies include Futura Ingredients, FDL, BASF, Danisco, Evonik, Kerry, AkzoNobel, Cargill, Solvay, Clariant, ADM, Acme Hardesty, McKinley Resources, and Lotte Foods. Challenges include complex processing requirements and restrictions on GMO-based blends in some countries.

The passage traces America’s transition from independence through the Confederation to the adoption and operation of the Constitution. Revolutionary ardor preserved order, but the Confederation, modeled on the Batavian and Helvetic confederacies, could not govern such a large country effectively. Neglect of its regulations and authority produced political paralysis, interstate rivalries, declining commerce and manufactures, falling land values, weakened public and private credit, and eventually unrest and insurrection. In response, the people sought a stronger union, and public deliberations produced the Constitution to secure justice, domestic tranquility, defense, general welfare, and liberty.

Having read the Constitution while serving abroad and later returned to public office, the author praised its suitability for the country, supported it, and found its operation beneficial to peace, order, prosperity, and happiness. He considered representative government admirable because its authority derives from an informed and virtuous people. However, he warned that corruption, manipulation, fraud, violence, or foreign influence in elections could cause government to serve a party or foreign power rather than the nation.

The passage also commends the recently retired leader’s prudence, justice, patriotism, and success in securing independence, peace, and prosperity, urging successors to follow his example. The author expresses support for the Constitution and state governments, equality among the states, education, justice, economic development, humane treatment of Native nations, peace and neutrality, trade negotiation, friendship with France, and Christian morality. He concludes with confidence in the Constitution and invokes divine blessing for the nation and its government.

During her visit to the 10th Sharjah Children’s Reading Festival at Expo Centre Sharjah, Sheikha Jawaher Al Qasimi toured the halls, publisher stands, joined children’s workshops and attended a reading session. She praised the festival for inspiring reading, knowledge and creativity across diverse cultures, called Sharjah a platform for global cultural exchange, commended the Sharjah Book Authority, and urged families and institutions to attend.

In a wartime address, the President urged coal miners to end a strike and return to work, arguing that uninterrupted coal production was essential to factories, power plants, railroads, and military supplies. He placed the mines under the authority of the Secretary of the Interior, promised protection for miners seeking to work, and said any wage adjustment approved by the War Labor Board would be retroactive to April 1. He attributed the crisis to United Mine Workers leaders who had refused fact-finding and hearings despite earlier labor pledges against strikes. While affirming miners’ union rights and the government’s efforts to improve working conditions, he emphasized national unity and warned against violence. He also described government price controls, rent reductions, stable clothing prices, and efforts to reduce food-price increases as necessary wartime measures.

The study examines how social studies didactics and judicial perspectives can guide human rights education content selection in Norwegian early childhood education and care (ECEC), using UN Day observances as an example. It identifies four content-selection dimensions: children’s ages and developmental levels, progression, human rights knowledge anchored in social studies, and children’s own interests.

Theoretical content analysis was applied to 73 Idebroen posts describing UN Day activities. The ideas addressed human rights, diversity, fundraising, or combinations of these. Activities were commonly adapted to individual child groups, included cross-curricular learning, and used creative methods to make abstract concepts tangible. However, progression was rarely addressed, and although 29 posts mentioned human rights, only three identified specific rights. Many activities emphasized values, diversity, or fundraising rather than legally grounded rights knowledge.

The findings indicate opportunities to develop deeper initial education, connect activities to children’s lived contexts, and support judicial consciousness. Challenges include age-appropriate treatment of rights and violations, avoiding adult responsibilities imposed on young children, ensuring legal precision and plurality of perspectives, and evaluating whether NGO and government resources meaningfully support children’s interests. The dimensions offer a structured framework for subject-specific content discussions, while further development of ECEC guidance, teacher support, and empirically grounded research is needed.

Google’s Pentagon Project Maven, which developed AI to analyze drone footage, prompted over 3,100 employees to sign a petition and roughly a dozen to resign. Google is now developing ethical guidelines for defense contracts, reportedly precluding AI in weaponry, though their impact remains uncertain.

The passage is a collection of The 74’s education and youth-related story headlines. Its lead item says Colton Harris-Moore, dubbed “the Barefoot Bandit,” evaded police for years and committed 67 felonies in three countries by stealing six airplanes, 15 cars and robbing more than 34 homes. Other items cover school integration, desegregation, accountability, teacher and student achievements, college access, COVID learning impacts, Native American and civil-rights topics, school meals, funding, and innovative education programs. Additional headlines address a gymnast, a baseball draft pick, Grammy camp, community awards, flooding, English-language policy, Supreme Court decisions and Barbie’s diabetes.

The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons was interpreted as a signal for the United States and North Korea to negotiate and as indirect support for the Iran nuclear deal. The U.S. rejected the campaign-backed nuclear weapons ban treaty, which 122 countries adopted without participation from any of the nine nuclear-armed states. Amid escalating U.S.-North Korean threats, North Korea’s largest nuclear test yet, and reported preparations for a long-range missile test, the award was presented as drawing attention to nuclear escalation and urging Kim Jong Un, Donald Trump, and others toward diplomacy.

The TTC will return 67 of 89 Bombardier-built streetcars for preventive repairs to inferior frame welds; no safety risk was identified. Bombardier will cover costs at its Quebec welding centre, with all repairs expected by 2022.

Ohio State University researchers identified a previously unknown stress pathway, TexPSR, as a major driver of T-cell exhaustion in cancer. In exhausted T cells, TexPSR accelerates protein production, causing misfolded proteins, stress granules, and toxic aggregates to accumulate and impair tumor-attacking function. Blocking key drivers of TexPSR restored T-cell activity and improved immunotherapy in preclinical models. High TexPSR levels in patient T cells were associated with poor clinical responses to immunotherapy. The mechanism was validated across lung, bladder, liver, and leukemia models, suggesting a potential strategy to enhance cancer treatment by targeting protein stress.

President Buchanan transmitted the Lecompton Constitution to Congress and urged Kansas’s admission as a state. He argued that the convention was lawfully elected, that the Topeka government was a rebellious usurpation, and that Kansas voters had submitted the slavery question to the ballot before electing state officers under the Lecompton Constitution. He maintained that admitting Kansas as a slave state would promote peace, reduce sectional conflict, and permit federal troops to leave, while rejection would revive the slavery agitation and endanger the Union.

In a separate proclamation, Buchanan declared Utah in rebellion after residents opposed federal officials, obstructed courts, and attacked an Army supply train. He ordered military enforcement of federal authority, offered a full pardon to those who submitted to federal law, specified that the government was not targeting their religion, and warned that persistent resistance would receive rigorous punishment.

The address mourns President Harding, emphasizing his character and public affection for him, and pledges those associated with him to continue his service to the country.

On foreign affairs, the United States should pursue peace, justice, national independence, and peaceful dispute settlement without joining the League of Nations or surrendering freedom of action. The Permanent Court of International Justice should nevertheless receive favorable consideration, with explicit reservations preventing adherence to the League. American assistance to Russia should be substantial but conditioned on recognition of international obligations, repayment of debts, and compensation for American citizens. Foreign debts may be adjusted, but financial and moral obligations must be honored; American claims against Germany and other governments should be protected. These policies also serve European recovery and international stability.

Domestic fiscal stability is the foremost concern. The budget system has reduced expenditures and should be strengthened, enabling reductions in federal, state, and local taxation. War taxes, excess-profits taxes, and tax-exempt securities should be eliminated or restricted, while earned incomes and moderate investment incomes receive relief. The existing tariff has produced revenue and prosperity and should remain, with limited presidential authority to adjust rates when production-cost disparities warrant it.

The government should transfer its merchant fleet to private ownership as soon as adequate defense and commercial service can be secured. It should pursue flood control, inland waterways, hydroelectric development, the St. Lawrence River project, good highways, and reforestation. Railroad law should guarantee fair returns while awaiting Supreme Court action on excess-earnings provisions. Voluntary regional and route consolidations should be encouraged, freight-rate structures reorganized, and labor disputes settled by agreement or continued impartial board intervention.

Legal reforms should include updated federal laws, additional judges, simplified court procedures, improved prisons and reformatories, and criminal-identification services. Prohibition should be enforced through stronger Coast Guard operations, anti-smuggling measures, and regulation of production and interstate traffic. The constitutional rights of Black citizens require protection against lynching, expanded vocational and medical education, and locally supported interracial understanding. The classified civil service should expand, especially to postmasters and prohibition personnel.

Legislation is also urged on maritime pollution, aviation, radio interference, vessel loading, navigation laws, Federal Trade Commission procedure, and Alaskan fisheries. Army and Navy strength should be restored through additional aircraft, submarines, and Panama defenses. The government should improve its departments and public buildings, address insular territories responsively, and provide stronger veterans’ hospitals, rehabilitation, compensation, and dependent support, though it should not grant a veterans’ bonus.

Education and welfare require federal encouragement while preserving local choice and personal responsibility. National action should address public health, child labor, women’s minimum wages, illiteracy, education, and general welfare. Immigration should remain selective and restricted, with alien registration. Coal policy should preserve private ownership while improving production, distribution, labor relations, and emergency regulation.

Agricultural relief should emphasize reduced taxes, lower freight rates, cheaper fertilizer, farmer-created organization, cooperative marketing, diversification, emergency credit, and export assistance rather than permanent price controls. Muscle Shoals should be sold under conditions protecting wartime use and requiring experimentation toward cheap domestic fertilizer. Reclamation contractors should receive flexible relief where necessary without surrendering federal control. The Monroe Doctrine must be maintained as an independent, strong republic assumes greater responsibilities, uses moral power, and promotes justice, confidence, and peace.

Flexible working can help employed carers balance work and caring responsibilities. Options include altered hours or days, compressed hours, flexible start or finish times, working from another office or home, term-time or part-time work, and job sharing.

Employees in England, Scotland and Wales may request flexible working after at least 26 weeks with their employer and may make one application in any 12-month period; Northern Ireland has different rules. Employers must consider requests but may refuse them for good business reasons. Where no internal procedure exists, a statutory request must be made in writing, dated, and include the proposed arrangements, start date, business impact and mitigation, and previous application details. Applicants need not provide full personal circumstances or a reason, though explanations may strengthen the request.

Employers must respond within three months unless an extension is agreed and, if they accept, confirm the new hours and start date in writing and amend the contract. Refusals require a valid business reason and explanation. Concerns may be raised through the employer’s appeal process or an employment tribunal within three months, but a request cannot be appealed solely because it was rejected; the handling must have been unreasonable or unfair.

The Iowa City VA Health Care System is investigating reports that mailed prescriptions, including hydrocodone-acetaminophen, have gone missing or been tampered with for veterans in Galesburg and Abingdon, Illinois. Veterans report lost or shorted medication; police have logged two cases.

NVIDIA Corporation reported first-quarter fiscal 2021 results for the period ended April 26, 2020. Revenue was $3.080 billion, up 39% from $2.220 billion a year earlier. Gross margin increased to 65.1% from 58.4%, operating income rose to $976 million from $358 million, and net income increased to $917 million from $394 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.47, compared with $0.64. Operating expenses increased 10% to $1.028 billion, primarily due to employee additions, compensation, infrastructure and stock-based compensation.

The company changed its reportable segments to Graphics and Compute & Networking. Graphics generated $1.906 billion of revenue and $836 million of operating income, while Compute & Networking generated $1.174 billion and $451 million. By market platform, gaming revenue was $1.339 billion, professional visualization $307 million, data center $1.141 billion, automotive $155 million, and OEM and other $138 million. Data Center growth reflected increased demand from vertical industries and hyperscale customers, while automotive revenue declined because of lower legacy infotainment revenue. Revenue billed outside the United States represented 84% of total revenue.

At April 26, 2020, NVIDIA held $16.354 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Total assets were $23.254 billion, total liabilities $10.155 billion, and shareholders’ equity $13.099 billion. Long-term debt increased to $6.959 billion following the March 2020 issuance of $5.0 billion of notes, which generated $4.97 billion of net proceeds. Operating cash flow was $909 million, investing activities used $1.055 billion, and financing activities provided $4.744 billion.

NVIDIA paid $98 million in dividends and made no share repurchases during the quarter. It remained authorized to repurchase up to $7.24 billion of stock through December 2022 and remained committed to quarterly dividends. The company stated that it had sufficient liquidity for operating requirements and capital expenditures for at least the following 12 months.

Subsequent to quarter-end, NVIDIA completed the approximately $7.0 billion cash acquisition of Mellanox Technologies on April 27, 2020. Mellanox revenue will be included in the Compute & Networking segment beginning in the second quarter and in the Data Center market platform.

COVID-19 disrupted supply chains, logistics and demand during the quarter, particularly for gaming, automotive products and customers and suppliers in Asia. Management said an extended pandemic could materially harm operations, liquidity and financial results. Legal proceedings included consolidated securities and derivative lawsuits concerning statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining; NVIDIA had not accrued liabilities because potential losses were not considered probable. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective and reported no material changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter.

This passage is an NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture whitepaper describing the TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs and their features.

**Streaming Multiprocessor (SM):** Turing's new SM pairs 64 FP32 cores with 64 INT32 cores in four processing blocks, plus eight Tensor Cores, one RT Core, a 256 KB register file, and a 96 KB unified L1 data cache/shared memory that can be split in several configurations. A second parallel integer execution unit runs alongside the FP32 datapath, yielding roughly 36% additional floating-point throughput for typical shader mixes and an overall ~50% performance gain per CUDA core. Turing also supports concurrent FP32/INT32 execution and independent thread scheduling.

**GPU configurations:** The TU102 includes six GPCs, 36 TPCs, 72 SMs, 12 32-bit GDDR6 controllers (384-bit), 96 ROPs, 6 MB of L2 cache, 6144 CUDA cores, 576 Tensor Cores, 144 FP64 units, and two NVLink x8 links giving 100 GB/s aggregate bidirectional bandwidth. The TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, Tesla T4) has six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink link. The TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070) has three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

**Memory, display, and video:** Turing is the first architecture to use GDDR6, delivering 14 Gbps signaling rates with 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X and 40% less signal crosstalk. Improved memory compression plus GDDR6 yields ~50% higher effective bandwidth over Pascal. The new display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, HDR with BT.2100 tone mapping, and two 8K displays. NVENC adds H.265/HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps with bitrate savings; NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit support.

**Tensor Cores and NGX:** Turing Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 modes alongside FP16, doubling INT8 throughput, enabling real-time deep learning in games. NVIDIA NGX provides pre-trained AI features including DLSS (trained against 64x supersampled references, with a DLSS 2X mode), AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. Combined with Tensor Cores, the RTX 2080 Ti reaches twice the performance of the GTX 1080 Ti.

**Data center:** The Tesla T4 provides 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, up to 130 TOPS of INT8 and 260 TOPS of INT4, 16 GB memory at 320 GB/s, an enhanced video engine, and improved Multi-Process Service. It delivers up to 40X the inference performance and more than 50X the energy efficiency of CPU-based inferencing.

**Ray tracing:** Each SM includes an RT Core that accelerates BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading work from shader cores and producing roughly 10X the ray throughput of Pascal (10+ Giga Rays/sec versus ~1.1). NVIDIA advocates a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing, supported by denoising algorithms and the BVH structure, and applies ray tracing to shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

**Other technologies:** Mesh shading adds task and mesh shaders to eliminate CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rate per 16x16 pixel region for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading decouples shading from the screen-space pixel grid and supports stereo VR reuse; Multi-View Rendering expands Pascal's SMP to four views per pass (32 at the API level); VirtualLink and USB Type-C support simplify VR connectivity via a single connector; and a workload-based RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput by expected usage.

The passage concludes with standard NVIDIA disclaimers regarding accuracy, liability, and license.

Ferrari’s 2025 “controlled growth” strategy seeks to expand its leadership in luxury performance vehicles while preserving its heritage and exclusivity. During the preceding decade, vehicle shipments nearly doubled, and revenue rose from $3.2 billion in 2015 to $7.2 billion in 2024. Planned growth depends on new models, expansion in growth markets, attracting younger customers, and introducing the company’s first fully electric vehicle in 2025.

The global premium and luxury passenger-vehicle market exceeded 10 million units and $770 billion in retail sales in 2024. Ferrari defines luxury performance vehicles as two- or four-door cars and SUVs priced above €180,000 with engines producing more than 500 horsepower; more than 85,000 were sold globally in 2024. Luxury-vehicle sales were forecast to grow 9%–14% annually from 2021 to 2031. The segment includes century-old luxury brands such as Rolls-Royce, Bentley, Bugatti, Aston Martin, and Maserati, as well as newer supercar producers such as Automobili Pininfarina and W Motors.

Ferrari’s history links racing, technological innovation, and road-car exclusivity. Enzo Ferrari founded Scuderia Ferrari in 1929 and incorporated Ferrari S.p.A. in 1947, when the V12-powered 125 S debuted. Road cars generated funds for racing, while racing success attracted customers and stimulated demand for road models. Ferrari entered Formula 1 in 1950, achieved sustained competitive success, and treated continuous improvement as a core principle. After Fiat acquired a 50% stake, Ferrari went public in 2015. Benedetto Vigna became CEO in 2021.

In 2024, nearly 90% of Ferrari’s revenue came from cars and spare parts; the remainder came from Formula 1 sponsorships, merchandise, and, through 2023, engine sales to Maserati. Only 8% of revenue came from mainland China. Ferrari estimated a 14% share of the overall luxury performance market and 23% of the two-door sports-car segment. Its total shareholder returns since 2015 exceeded those of luxury peers. Rather than rely on traditional advertising, Ferrari uses Formula 1 to gain global visibility, while its Lifestyle business licenses watches, apparel, collectibles, and other branded goods.

Ferrari divides customers into sports-car drivers and track-oriented pilots. Its active client base grew 10% between January 2022 and January 2023, with 40% of new clients under 40. Existing customers bought 81% of new cars in 2024, and repeat customers were estimated to generate 80% of revenue and 86% of EBITDA. Ferrari centrally allocates limited-edition cars and supercars based on clients’ engagement with the brand. It cultivates loyalty through regional clubs, factory visits, road trips, car shows, and owner races. Its 178 authorized dealers operate 200 sales points in 60 markets, while Ferrari enforces service standards through training, monitoring, and technical support. The Classiche program restores and certifies historic vehicles.

The portfolio comprises Range models, limited-production Special Series, Icona, and supercars. Range models account for more than 90% of shipments, while Icona and supercars generate higher revenue and margins. Ferrari launched 15 models from 2018 through 2022—including the SF90 Stradale, SF90 Spider, and Purosangue SUV—and planned another 15 from 2023 through 2026. Customers can choose extensive personalization, and vehicles are built only after orders are placed, limiting unsold inventory. Waitlists generally range from 12 to 18 months.

Ferrari transfers technology from Formula 1 to road cars, including hybrid energy-recovery systems. Manufacturing is divided between Modena, where body shells are made, and Maranello, where engines and vehicles are assembled. Ferrari retains critical components and production capabilities in-house while outsourcing transmissions and brakes. In 2024, its Italian workforce totaled 1,797 engineers, technicians, and production workers.

Electrification creates both opportunity and uncertainty. Hybrid vehicles rose from 2% of Ferrari shipments in 2020 to 51% in 2024. Ferrari targeted a 2026 sales mix of 55% hybrid, 40% internal-combustion, and 5% fully electric vehicles, while maintaining a technology-neutral stance. It plans to handcraft electric powertrains and assemble externally sourced battery cells in Maranello. In 2024, Ferrari opened an e-building for electric powertrain development and a laboratory for battery research. However, slower-than-expected luxury EV demand led Aston Martin and Bentley to revise their electrification schedules; charging infrastructure gaps and falling used Ferrari hybrid values also created obstacles. Ferrari remained focused on Formula 1 and did not enter Formula E.

Ferrari identifies risks from unfamiliar growth markets, new dealer networks, stronger competitors, changing consumer preferences, and internal capabilities it may lack. Its strategic questions concern the future attractiveness of the luxury performance market, the sources and durability of its competitive advantage, major threats and potential disruptors, and the most profitable opportunities for growth.

The passage identifies five foundational principles for early childhood education and care (ECEC) for children aged 1–5:

1. **Prioritize holistic development in the early years**, recognizing brain plasticity, sensitivity to positive and negative experiences, social and emotional development, and the importance of early experiences as a foundation for future learning.
2. **Create nurturing environments** that are safe, inclusive, respectful, stimulating, and emotionally supportive. Family, ECEC services, and the wider community shape children’s development.
3. **Focus on ECEC quality**, including warm teacher-child interactions, age-appropriate and child-centred curricula, evidence-based practices, inclusion, and continuous professional development.
4. **Engage families** through educator collaboration, regular communication, cultural understanding, and access to resources and support. Children should also be encouraged to explore and learn from mistakes.
5. **Promote continuous professional development** so educators remain equipped with current knowledge, skills, and best practices.

Together, these principles support children’s cognitive, social, emotional, physical, and motor development and strengthen their prospects for future learning and well-being.

The lecture reviews minimal trellis representations for binary linear block codes, with the same principles applicable to codes over general fields or groups. The state space theorem gives the dimension of the state space at a cut time as the code dimension minus the dimensions of the past and future subcodes. Using a trellis-oriented generator matrix, the past and future subcodes are generated by rows supported wholly in the past or future; rows active across the cut generate the state code.

A trellis-oriented generator matrix can be obtained from any generator matrix by greedily adding pairs of generators to cancel coincident starting or ending positions. When no further shortening is possible, all starting times and all ending times are distinct. The number of generators active at a cut then gives the state-space dimension at that cut. Examples include the single-parity-check and repetition codes. Self-dual codes exhibit a special pattern in which starts and ends coincide, but this property alone does not establish self-duality. A dual state-space theorem states that a code and its dual have the same state-space dimensions and sizes, although their trellises and branching structures can differ.

A minimal trellis is realized by treating each generator as a one-dimensional memory element that is active only over that generator’s span, then summing the generator outputs in a linear time-varying finite-state machine. Generator starts cause trellis divergence, generator ends cause convergence, and simultaneous starts and ends can produce crossings. Branches, represented by state, output, and next-state triples, form a vector space. At each symbol time, the branch-space dimension equals the number of active generators.

Branch complexity, defined by the maximum branch-space size, is more directly related to Viterbi decoding cost than state complexity because Viterbi processing requires work for every branch. Sectionalization can make the displayed state complexity appear smaller, but it cannot reduce branch complexity. The suggested sectionalization heuristic is to enlarge sections as much as possible without increasing branch complexity.

A generator of span \(S\) contributes \(S-1\) to the sum of state-space dimensions and \(S\) to the sum of branch-space dimensions. Consequently, the average state dimension is at least \(k(d-1)/(n-1)\), while the average branch dimension is at least \(kd/n\), the code’s nominal coding gain. These bounds also apply to convolutional codes when averaged over time.

For a good sequence of codes, both rate and relative distance remain bounded away from zero, so nominal coding gain grows linearly with block length. Minimal-trellis branch complexity therefore grows exponentially with length. Viterbi decoding with a minimal trellis provides a simpler optimal maximum-likelihood alternative to exhaustive decoding, but its complexity remains exponential for such sequences. One possible way to avoid this growth is to accept finite nominal coding gain and relatively poor minimum distance while preserving nonzero rate; the lecture cites turbo codes as an example, while noting that not all capacity-approaching codes have poor distance.

Finally, the lecture relates projections of a code to its subcodes and gives an equivalent state-space theorem based on the difference between the dimension of a past projection and the dimension of the past subcode. This method yields the central trellis dimensions of Reed–Muller codes, including dimension 2 for the \((8,4,4)\) code and dimension 6, or 64 states, for the \((32,16,8)\) code.

This Cookie Policy from zeenews.india.com explains how and why cookies and similar tracking technologies are stored on and accessed from users' devices when visiting the company's websites, and is meant to be read alongside its Privacy Policy. Continued browsing constitutes agreement to such use. Cookies are small text files placed on devices; related tracking technologies work similarly, storing small data files or monitoring website activity to collect usage information and recognize devices. The sites use these technologies to store and receive information, identify users and their interests, remember preferences, track site use, control access to content, protect the sites, process requests, administer the sites, and conduct research; third-party service providers are contracted to track and analyze statistical usage and volume data. The policy distinguishes first-party cookies (set by zeenews.india.com) from third-party cookies (sent by embedded content hosts or social networks when users share content), noting it does not control third-party cookie settings. It describes persistent cookies, which record acceptance of the cookie policy to remove the initial cookie message, and session cookies, which are temporary and deleted when the browser closes. Cookie categories covered are essential cookies (site navigation, features, login status, session memory, security), analytical/performance cookies (usage patterns, frequently visited content, viewing history, visitor locations), functionality cookies (remembering choices and customizations between visits), and advertising cookies (targeted advertising based on activity on the sites and other sites, including by third-party providers such as social media platforms). Data collected is not kept longer than necessary for the stated purposes and remains in the database until the user gives explicit consent to remove stored cookies. Users may refuse or withdraw consent by adjusting browser settings to reject all or some cookies and receive alerts when cookies are placed, though blocking cookies may limit access to parts of the sites, and manually deleting cookies does not prevent further placement unless settings are adjusted. Additional information is available at youronlinechoices.eu for users in Europe and aboutads.info/choices in the United States. Questions about the Cookie Policy, privacy practices, or grievances can be emailed to response@zeemedia.esselgroup.com.

The passage defines a standardized Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. These technologies encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access. Automatic exits do not expose guest state, while Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs) allow the guest to select state for disclosure through the GHCB before invoking VMGEXIT.

The GHCB is a 4 KB, page-aligned, decrypted guest page whose layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save area while exposing only information required by the hypervisor. Its address is accessed through MSR 0xc001_0130, whose lower 12 bits carry GHCB MSR protocol requests and whose upper bits carry the page address. The hypervisor must not intercept this MSR. The protocol supports version negotiation, obtaining the page-table encryption bit position, CPUID values, preferred and registered GHCB addresses, and unregistering a GHCB. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use; separate registrations may be maintained for each VMPL when Multi-VMPL is advertised.

Version 2 adds a hypervisor feature bitmap for advertising optional capabilities, including base SEV-SNP, AP VMSA creation, Restricted Injection and its timer support, APIC ID lists, Multi-VMPL, SEV-ES page-state changes, trusted I/O, and GHCB unregistration. Revisions through 2.04 also cover 64-bit SNP guest-request sequence numbers, malformed-input and VMGEXIT error reporting, VLEK GUID definitions, the EFI Confidential Computing Blob protocol, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and a new GHCB MSR function.

NAEs are surfaced to guests through VMM Communication (#VC) exceptions. The guest determines which fields to expose, sets the required VALID_BITMAP entries, and executes VMGEXIT. The hypervisor processes the exit, returns information through SW_EXITINFO fields, and reports errors through defined status values. Supported events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access through #NPF, page-state changes, SNP guest requests, extended SNP requests, SNP AP creation, #HV doorbell, IPI, and timer operations, APIC ID lists, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing-page management, termination requests, and unsupported events.

Page-state changes use entries in the shared GHCB buffer to request private, shared, smashed, or unsmashed pages, with resumable progress and specific error codes. SNP guest requests pass sequential requests to SNP firmware through shared request and response pages; the hypervisor returns firmware status and may request retries to protect sequence-number synchronization and avoid denial-of-service conditions. Extended guest requests can return GUID-identified VCEK or VLEK certificates. TIO requests return device measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation data.

Secure AVIC manages a private APIC backing page per vCPU through registration and unregistration actions. SNP AP creation permits guests to create, update, remove, or immediately activate an AP’s VMSA at a specified VMPL, providing an alternative to AP Reset Hold and enabling vCPU hotplug.

SMP booting requires special handling because measured AP register state cannot be changed by the hypervisor. SEV-ES and SEV-SNP use AP Reset Hold and an AP jump table to transfer APs between environments, while SNP AP Creation offers a VMSA-based method. The SNP secrets page can convey the jump-table address and guest-request sequence numbers between operating environments.

SEV-ES NMI handling requires the hypervisor to intercept #DB but not IRET, with the guest signaling when another NMI may be injected. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported through SEV_FEATURES; otherwise, DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated by the guest handler. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

With Restricted Injection, host notifications to SNP guests use a shared #HV doorbell page containing a PendingEvent vector and a NoEoiRequired field. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior, while guests use defined HLT and interrupt-processing conventions to avoid missing or prematurely dispatching events.

NVIDIA Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the first quarter of fiscal 2017, ended May 1, 2016, reported revenue of $1.305 billion, up 13% from $1.151 billion a year earlier. The company issued $1.5 billion of 1% convertible senior notes due in 2018; their $1.421 billion carrying value remained classified as current because holders could convert them. NVIDIA resolved its intellectual-property disputes with Samsung and terminated its claims against Qualcomm. It also settled litigation with Advanced Silicon Technologies and paid $16 million for patent licenses.

The session examines reverse logistics and closed-loop supply chains through discussion of ReCellular and Whirlpool. ReCellular collects and repurposes donated cellphones for resale in different markets. Participants debated its prospects: supporters cited its e-commerce strategy, adaptability to changing technologies, and opportunities in developing markets, while critics emphasized declining resale values, shrinking margins, faster product turnover, and the need to buy used phones rather than rely on donations. Genco was presented as a diversified alternative with retailer partnerships, unlike ReCellular’s specialized focus.

For Whirlpool, participants considered three responses to extended producer responsibility: joining an industry-funded organization (IFO), establishing a company-operated closed-loop system, or opposing regulation. The existing recycling system was said to recover roughly 95–99% of appliances through normal markets, but concerns included volatile commodity prices, hazardous materials such as mercury and refrigerants, and disposal practices that normalize leaving unwanted products curbside. Alternatives to broad producer responsibility included phasing out hazardous materials and improving existing recyclers’ practices.

The class compared costs and networks. Student estimates placed IFO costs at roughly $24–35 million, while discussion compared reverse-logistics costs of about $80 per appliance with forward distribution costs of about $70 per unit. Whirlpool’s Canadian network was described as 17 factories, 24 distribution centers, and 2,400 retailers. An IFO would provide scale and shift collection to dealers and processors but weaken Whirlpool’s consumer relationship. A closed loop could strengthen customer loyalty, brand control, and material recovery, but would require new systems, space, labor, incentives for retailers, and substantial investment. Whirlpool ultimately attempted a closed loop, though its first trial proved more expensive than expected. The class concluded that volume, efficiency, product homogeneity, and collaboration with partners were key to feasibility.

Students then briefly presented projects involving green initiatives at Zara, Hewlett-Packard and Dell, BMW, and Philip Morris International, with discussion of life-cycle impacts, industry regulations, and carbon offsets. A sales-calculation assignment was due by Wednesday morning.

Soccer individual defending requires a defender to reach the ball carrier quickly while remaining goal-side, balanced, and aware of teammates’ coverage. Aggressive defending is appropriate when teammates are positioned; it involves cutting off the ball, tackling, interposing, or preventing the attacker from turning toward goal. If the defense is unsettled, the defender should stall the attack while teammates recover.

One-on-one tactics include staying goal-side, maintaining proper foot alignment and distance, avoiding overreaction to fakes, blocking passes or shots, slowly giving ground, restricting vision, jockeying, shepherding the attacker toward the sideline, and stealing the ball when it becomes loose. Once the defender’s permitted backward space is exhausted—determined by field position, opponents’ shooting ability, and the defensive line—they must stand ground or prepare to tackle. If beaten, they should immediately turn and chase.

Teammates must verbally guide the on-ball defender because the defender cannot monitor the entire field. “Contain” means holding position and confining the attacker; “delay” and “jockey” mean giving ground while controlling direction; “stand him up” means containing until support arrives. “Challenge,” “tackle,” “take him,” and “take him on” authorize an attempt to win the ball. If a teammate takes over, the original defender should switch defensively.

Coaches should teach stance and movement from the right, center, and left, progressive ball work, goal-side positioning, all techniques, and the meanings of each communication command.

The disclosure concerns controlling uplink data transmission when a wireless device operates in an enhanced coverage state, particularly to reduce power consumption caused by repeated transmissions. It is a continuation of several earlier U.S. applications and patents.

Enhanced coverage functionality extends a base station’s coverage area but requires multiple transmissions, increasing battery use. LTE supports coverage enhancement modes A and B, with PUSCH repetitions ranging from 8–32 in mode A and 192–2048 in mode B. Similar coverage levels and repetition mechanisms are described for NB-IoT, while EC-GSM-IoT uses coverage classes. The disclosure discusses two solutions:

1. An application queries a modem for radio-coverage information, such as coverage-enhancement level, mode or class, repetition count, signal strength, or signal quality. It then decides whether to send uplink data. Queries and reports may use AT commands or APIs, including solicited responses or unsolicited notifications when coverage status changes.

2. An application instructs the modem to send specified or future uplink data only under defined conditions. Instructions may accompany the data or identify traffic by socket, bearer, PDP context, application, or destination address. The modem applies the restriction and may drop unsent data or retain it for later transmission.

Restrictions can depend on coverage level, mode, class, repetition count, signal quality, data type, QoS or priority, timers, transmission-attempt counters, device movement, battery level, and whether the device is connected to power. Emergency data may be exempt from restrictions, while non-emergency location data may be deferred. Restrictions can also expire after a specified time or number of skipped transmission opportunities, or be revoked when the device becomes stationary. Location, speed, battery, and power-status information may be obtained from sensors, an operating system, or a device interface.

The disclosure proposes AT command changes for coverage reporting and transmission restrictions, including fields or commands associated with +CREG, +CIOTQCEL, +CSODCP, and +CEUDR. Restrictions may be predefined by manufacturers or standards, configured locally by users or applications, or supplied by the network through NAS, RRC, USAT, device-management, system-information, and bearer-related messages. Example network-controlled parameters address permitted coverage levels, duration, battery thresholds, power connection, QoS classes, and traffic categories.

A similar process may be applied to mobile-terminated messages, with an application server or service capability server using network-supplied coverage information before forwarding traffic. The disclosure also describes example network-node and user-equipment architectures.

Using 2007–2010 NHANES data, this cross-sectional study examined whether depression, obesity, hypertriglyceridemia (HTG), and inflammatory status affect the association with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Among 4,136 eligible adults, 305 reported RA. Depression was defined by PHQ-9 score ≥10, obesity by BMI ≥30 kg/m², HTG by triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, and inflammation by CRP categories.

RA was associated with depression, obesity, HTG, hypertension, stroke, and diabetes. RA and each of depression, obesity, and HTG were associated with higher CRP levels, and RA prevalence increased as CRP rose. Coexisting depression and obesity or depression and HTG was associated with substantially greater RA prevalence than either condition alone, particularly at medium CRP levels (1–3 mg/L). At this CRP level, RA prevalence was 27.2% with depression and obesity and 34.9% with depression and HTG. The association varied by CRP level: obesity influenced the depression–RA relationship across all levels, whereas HTG was most evident at medium CRP. Adding HTG to obesity did not increase RA prevalence.

The findings indicate synergistic associations but cannot establish causation because the data are cross-sectional. RA was self-reported, potentially overestimating prevalence, and CRP is a nonspecific inflammation marker. Too few participants had all three conditions for meaningful analysis, and broader inflammatory-marker panels and longitudinal studies are needed.
