The paper argues that information systems research is shifting from technologically deterministic, positivist approaches toward human, social, interpretive, and mixed-method perspectives. It focuses on two related developments: complexity science and User Experience (UX). Both emphasize time, nonlinearity, self-organization, and irreversibility, presenting information systems as dynamic entities that continuously adapt as users, technologies, and organizational conditions change.

Complexity science, developed largely through computational evolutionary biology, distinguishes complex systems from merely complicated ones. Complex systems have shifting relationships, open environments, emergent properties, nonlinear effects, and outcomes that cannot be fully predicted from existing conditions. At bifurcation points, chance can produce major changes, while flows of matter and energy can generate stable yet evolving “dissipative structures.” Systems also retain history, so their past shapes present behavior, and their complexity cannot be reconstructed through reductionist analysis.

UX extends beyond operational usability measures such as task times, clicks, and errors to address subjective concerns including look, feel, satisfaction, motivation, and expectations. It therefore requires mixed methods that combine numerical usability analysis with social and experiential research. Examples including HTML5, AI-based applications, user-generated content, and multi-device information flows illustrate the shift from rigid, predictable systems toward open, human-centered ones. User experiences are durational and irreversible, so temporary technical measures cannot restore lost contextual or emotional dimensions.

The paper reviews efforts to apply complexity to information systems and criticizes approaches that separate human requirements from technological development, as well as universal reliance on hierarchical decomposition. It argues that self-organization better describes contemporary information systems. A Knowledge Transfer Partnership between the University of Salford and UX specialists Sigma Ltd will investigate how time and irreversibility affect user research, design, usability, complexity, and success. The paper concludes that information systems should be understood as complex and continually adapting, with flexibility and ongoing adaptation built into future designs.

The paper presents a knowledge graph embedding framework for ontology alignment (OA), the task of identifying correspondences between semantically equivalent entities across ontologies. It positions OA within the Semantic Web and symbolic AI, while noting that large language model approaches are popular and knowledge graph embeddings remain comparatively underexplored for OA.

The proposed OntoAligner-based approach has three stages. The parser converts source and target ontologies into RDF-style metadata containing IRIs, labels, and class-role information. The encoder merges their triples into a unified triple factory using natural-language entity and relation text, enabling shared structural and semantic patterns to be learned across both ontologies. The aligner trains a PyKEEN knowledge graph embedding model with a link-prediction objective, including negative sampling, and computes cosine similarities between normalized source and target embeddings. Each source entity is matched with its most similar target entity, after which one-to-one cardinality constraints and a confidence threshold filter the results.

The framework supports 17 KGE models: ConvE, TransD, TransE, TransF, TransH, TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, HolE, RotatE, SimplE, CrossE, BoxE, CompGCN, MuRE, QuatE, and SE. Ten were selected for frequent use in OA, while seven were added for their performance and versatility in broader knowledge graph tasks. The collection spans translation-based, bilinear, convolutional, complex, quaternion, hyperbolic, and graph-convolutional approaches, supporting systematic experimentation with KGEs for OA.

DAWN-PLASMA was a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial comparing standard of care alone with standard of care plus convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP principles, with ethics committee approval and informed consent. Participants were randomized 2:1 to plasma plus standard of care or standard of care alone.

The plasma intervention totaled 800–1,000 mL in four doses, with the first administered within 12 hours of randomization; plasma with neutralizing antibody titers below 1/160 was prohibited. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints assessed clinical status, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, sustained improvement, mortality, thromboembolism, transfusion reactions, antibody titers, safety, quality of life, laboratory data, and vital signs.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized, including 326 assigned to plasma and 163 to control. The Day 15 visit was completed by 434 patients and the Day 30 visit by 423. The full analysis set excluded one patient without confirmed SARS-CoV-2 and five who withdrew consent immediately after randomization without treatment or post-baseline data. The per-protocol analysis excluded protocol violations, including incomplete plasma dosing and plasma administration in controls.

In the full analysis set, the median time to first transfusion was five hours and the median plasma volume was 884 mL. The primary endpoint did not differ between groups: 83.7% of the plasma group and 84.1% of controls were alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). Results were similar in the per-protocol set. A prespecified subgroup analysis found a significant interaction with age, but further details were not provided in the passage.

The match-up zone combines person-to-person and zone principles through a series of defensive rules. It prevents offensive alignments from splitting defenders, makes overloads easier to defend, and can confuse opponents. It is a passive defense that reacts to offensive movement and permits perimeter ball movement, though aggressive traps may be added. Success depends on knowledgeable players and communication. The defense can dictate offensive alignment by displaying one zone on the first possession and switching to match-up rules afterward.

Basic assignments are adjustable for personnel: X1 generally matches the point, X2 the first player left of X1, X3 the first player right, and X4 and X5 the remaining interior or baseline players. Against 2-3 offense, X1 takes the right-side point in a two-guard front, X4 takes the second player left, and X5 takes the post. Against 1-3-1, X4 takes the second player right; against 1-2-2, X4 takes the second player left and X5 the baseline player right; against 1-4, X4 and X5 match the left and right posts.

Basket cuts are usually denied for three steps and met with switches involving weak-side defenders. Defenders may instead interchange roles when suitable, which can simplify certain cuts and confuse the offense. Detailed protocols address point, wing, baseline, post, flash, and high-post-roll cuts against 1-3-1, 1-2-2, 2-3, and 1-4 offenses. Defending 2-3 cutters generally relies on positional interchanges, while similar frontcourt players can interchange roles in several situations. The 1-4 alignment uses two mobile post players who can shoot outside, but match-up rules are described as effectively addressing it.

Match-up rules can also be extended into half-court and full-court trapping. Traps are triggered when the ball enters a primary trap zone, such as a corner, and can be used after timeouts or free throws or when trailing late. Listed trap concepts include a quarter-court “X,” a half-court “SOS” press, and full-court shadow presses.

The S&P 500 reached its 9.1% average annual return mark before reacting negatively amid weak July economic data, downward payroll revisions, elevated valuations, and expectations for seasonally weak trading from August through October. July payrolls rose by 73,000, while prior months were revised down by 258,000. Q2 earnings remained strong: 15 of 17 megacap companies beat earnings expectations, and 16 beat sales expectations, lifting S&P 500 earnings growth to 11.2% and sales growth to 5.6%. AI has supported the market, but the article says the economic slowdown is not necessarily a recession and could create a buying opportunity later in the year. Up years have averaged 17% returns since 1958. The page also promotes AI-selected stock portfolios and includes trading-risk and data-accuracy disclosures.

The passage describes patterns for building reliable, scalable distributed systems through modular containers and networked services. On a single machine, tightly coupled container groups can share resources such as filesystems, network namespaces, and process IDs. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a companion that adds functionality, such as HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, resource monitoring, or Git-based deployment. The ambassador pattern separates an application from external interactions by routing requests to shards, discovering services, or splitting traffic between production and experimental systems. The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to conform to common monitoring, logging, or health-check conventions, enabling reuse without changing third-party applications. Reusable containers should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`.

Across multiple machines, microservices divide an application into independently developed and scaled components connected through APIs. This approach supports team autonomy, independent releases, and service-specific scaling, but increases architectural and debugging complexity. Replicated load-balanced services use identical instances behind a load balancer for redundancy and horizontal scaling; readiness probes ensure instances are prepared for traffic. Session tracking may use IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing. Complete stateless serving stacks can add a separately scaled caching tier, rate limiting, and replicated SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among machines, with a router directing requests to the appropriate shard. Sharding allows state and load to scale beyond one machine and can improve cache memory utilization, while shard failure affects only requests mapped to that shard. Replicating each shard improves resilience and enables independent shard scaling, at the cost of greater complexity. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, commonly using a hash modulo the shard count, and should use keys that group requests with identical responses. Consistent hashing minimizes request remapping and cache disruption when the number of shards changes.

DomeShelter Australia’s Container Mounted DomeShelter (CMDS) is a robust, relocatable, weather-resistant shelter for harsh Australian conditions and Wind Regions A–D. Its container-compatible design eases shipping and logistical disruption. It offers rain and UV protection for oil and gas, heat and moisture protection for livestock, and a cool, naturally lit space for events and tourism.

The disclosure describes a smart-home fluid-flow measuring and control device for plumbing. Installed at a single common location, it combines flow measurement, shutoff control, backflow detection, appliance-level consumption analysis, abnormal-use detection, and leak detection. Most fluid travels through an unobstructed main channel, while a calibrated parallel bypass directs a known proportion through a chamber containing a rotating flowmeter wheel. Dual movement sensors determine wheel direction and net flow, including backflow, while a transceiver sends flow and optional temperature data to a computer.

The device may include a solenoid valve and pressure sensors upstream and downstream of it. The computer compares measured data with recorded water-usage signatures to identify individual appliances, detect abnormal consumption, and instruct the valve to close. When flow does not match a known signature, the valve is temporarily closed and pressure differences are measured to distinguish leaks from normal use. Small or medium pressure drops indicate a leak and keep the valve closed; no drop or a high drop suggests normal use and permits reopening. Baseline leakage can be recorded, allowing additional leaks to be distinguished.

Methods are also described for training appliance-specific flow signatures, comparing recurring measurements, identifying overuse, deterioration, and occupancy proxies, and notifying users through a remote server or mobile device.

This patent application (a continuation of three earlier applications titled "Systems and Methods for Providing User Interfaces Based on Actions Associated with Untrusted Emails") describes a system, referred to as "Second Chance," for providing user interfaces that confirm whether a user should review or proceed with actions associated with untrusted emails and untrusted domains.

Background: Phishing attacks seek sensitive information by masquerading as trustworthy entities, often via malicious attachments or links. Anti-ransomware products detect and remove such threats but provide no training and give users no decision-making role. Simulated phishing attacks are used to measure user vulnerability and target remedial training.

Description of the solution: The system gives users autonomy. When a user performs an action (e.g., accessing a URL, opening an attachment, or responding) involving an email or domain identified as untrusted, the action is paused and the user is prompted to either proceed or revert and review the action. The user console resolves the URL (e.g., Punycode, shortened links), queries the server for its trusted/untrusted status, displays a configurable notification, records the user's response, and then resumes or discards the action.

Client-side architecture: A driver monitors process creation and termination and notifies the user console; the user console determines whether a process warrants monitoring and spawns an injector that injects a monitor library into the process; the monitor library detects user access to an untrusted domain or attempts to open a file obtained from a phishing email, and pauses the request; a core library uses shared memory for bidirectional communication with the injected libraries; the user console runs in the user's session to raise prompts. A client service running as administrator ensures a user console runs for each logged-in user, and a watchdog service restarts it. For browser-based email clients, URL navigation monitoring is provided either by injected code or a browser extension (with a Browser Intermediary Application to bridge browser security restrictions); monitoring activates after a successful email login.

Server-side configuration: The server maintains a plurality of settings (message title, text fields, OK/cancel button content, help link and destination, remember checkbox, foreground/background colors, element visibility) and hashes per user group. The client computes a client settings hash by concatenating and hashing its stored settings values and sends it with queries; if it mismatches the server hash, updated settings and the new server hash are returned and stored locally. Company administrators can customize notifications through a console without involving the security awareness system administrator, and can create distinct notifications for different user groups. An alternative update-detection mechanism using "last updated" dates is also described.

Benefits and uses: real-time phishing training, a "second chance" to rethink actions, targeted training based on recorded behavior, insight into user behavior for administrators, alert actions such as Ignore, Report, Prompt, or Prevent, restrictions for users not yet trained, and possible SaaS delivery. Drawings cover network/cloud environments, computing devices, flow charts of the methods, and configurable notification examples.

An analysis of district and school data suggests that elementary schools generally perform consistently across core subjects rather than specializing. Among districts identified as exceptional, 140 appeared on both reading and math lists; only 14 were strong in one subject but significantly below expectations in the other, with 12 of those stronger in math than reading. In Mississippi, school-level reading and math scores had a 0.87 correlation, while growth patterns were similarly aligned. None of the 50 schools with the greatest reading gains had below-average math growth; only two of the 50 with the lowest reading gains reached average math growth. Florida showed similar relationships between proficiency and growth. The author cautions that proficiency is closely linked to socioeconomic status and that state growth models vary, favoring growth measures to assess schools’ effects on learning.

Corner-kick defense requires a clear, practiced plan that every player understands and can execute immediately. Coaches should assign players specific responsibilities based on position and abilities, while the goalkeeper retains command of the defense. Defenders must move quickly to their locations, aggressively contest the ball, clear it high, far, and upfield when possible, and organize an outlet and fast-break transition. They should also maintain basic defensive principles, including goal-side positioning, blocking shots, covering opponents, winning second balls, and communicating.

Zone defense is generally introduced first because it is easy to teach and allows defenders to move forward toward the ball. The goalkeeper covers the area between the posts and six yards out, two defenders guard the posts, three defend on the six-yard line, and three more position themselves in the penalty area. A defender blocks the kick from 11 yards away, while a striker prepares for a clearance near the corner arc. Zone defense’s weaknesses include zones being overloaded and defenders hesitating to leave a ball to a teammate.

Man-to-man defense requires each defender to track one attacker, remain goal-side and close enough to react, and maintain awareness of both the attacker and the ball. It prevents opponents from flooding a zone, but defenders may run backward toward goal, struggle to mark everyone, or lose focus. Assignments are typically made from the nearest attackers outward, with the goalkeeper and defensive coordinator ensuring coverage.

A mixed defense places the two post defenders and three defenders on the six-yard line in zones while the remaining defenders mark attackers man-to-man. This approach is described as producing the lowest likelihood of conceding corner-kick goals.

Training progresses from positioning and simulated corners to live opposition, emphasizing rapid responses, attacking clearances, communication, concentration, and fast breaks. Coaches should scout opponents and adjust plans accordingly. The goalkeeper should remain centrally positioned and visible, while the player marking the kicker acts as a one-man wall, maintains the required distance, and quickly covers quick corners.

Crystal morphology strongly affects the sensitivity and performance of energetic materials: smooth, near-spherical PETN and RDX crystals are less shock sensitive than needle-like crystals, while morphology also controls packing density and thus detonation velocity and pressure. The same concern applies to pharmaceuticals. Morphology is commonly predicted via Wulff constructions using BFDH (inverse interplanar spacing), SE (surface energy), and AE (attachment energy) models, but each deviates from experiment: BFDH neglects energetics, while SE and AE remain sensitive to the chosen plane set, fail to capture true morphologies for low-symmetry lattices such as β-HMX, ignore edge and corner effects in small crystals, and give only steady-state shapes without growth kinetics. A prior Monte Carlo scheme for PETN facets used Metropolis–Hastings sampling, which follows Boltzmann statistics without kinetics.

The authors therefore introduce a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) technique predicting morphology from intermolecular interaction parameters alone, implemented as the open-source Python package cgkmc, and apply it to PETN growth, agreeing with AE predictions and experiment.

In the model, the system is a colored, undirected graph whose nodes are supercell sites with binary occupation variables and whose edges carry symmetric shell-based interaction weights Q; total energy is a quadratic binary-programming objective. From the adjacency matrix and coordination numbers, solid and liquid interfacial sites are identified, giving candidate evaporation and adsorption sites. Adsorption rates scale as Dn∞/(σR) for a spherical crystal, while evaporation rates follow harmonic transition state theory with barrier equal to the lost intermolecular interaction energy, using a prefactor νt updated dynamically so that average adsorption and evaporation rates balance at a target crystal radius and size. A residence-time algorithm then time-evolves occupancy via these adsorption and evaporation events.

Combined L1 data cache and shared memory, introduced with Volta V100, improves performance and simplifies tuning. The subsystem provides low-latency, high-bandwidth access; A100 offers 192 KB/SM versus V100’s 128 KB/SM.

The Mid Screen Offense is a widely used NBA and WNBA set offense, also usable as a late-clock action. A high-post screener frees the point guard to drive, pull up, return the ball to the post, or kick out to wing shooters. Because it is often executed from the center of the floor with shooters spaced outside, it limits weak-side help defense.

Offensive reads and counters include driving against chasing defenders, passing to shooters against sagging defense, dropping the ball to the post against baseline help, driving opposite when defenders cheat over the screen, lobbing to the screener when the screen is overplayed, and pulling up when defenders go under. Options against switches include post rolls and isolation; against anticipated switches and zones, the screener may slip. Traps are countered by spreading the defense and moving the ball quickly.

Mid Screen action can flow into motion or passing offenses, flex continuity, inside-triangle action, and side-screen continuity. Variations include screen-and-pop, Horns with two high-post screeners, 1–4 low alignment, post isolation, and the Two Game.

Success requires coordinated execution, defensive recognition, communication, timing, and experience. Teaching recommendations include breakdown drills, scrimmages, and individual skill development. Game strategy includes scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, varying alignments and entries, moving players to attack weaker defenders, and remaining prepared to defend against the Mid Screen Offense.

The speaker described making a two-on-one chance in the second period, passing on a power-play opportunity to Marty, and turning the puck over while diving to recover a missed chance. With the Devils ahead in the series and playing the next game Thursday, he said they want to finish the series rather than extend it, drawing on their previous comeback experience. He has reached the finals in each of the past two years in Finland and credited those pressures for helping him prepare.

Adjusting to Dallas was a key focus. He praised the Stars’ speed, hard shifts, puck cycling, support play, and ability to create open space, making it important for New Jersey to take away their time. New Jersey has tried to match Dallas’s top lines defensively, use all four lines, and improve discipline after having too many players on the ice against Florida. He also praised a veteran teammate’s conditioning, playoff improvement, and increased minutes.

Mittelstadt could join Rochester on an AHL or amateur tryout contract for the regular season and playoffs, gaining professional experience but using a year of his three-year Minnesota contract and forfeiting NCAA eligibility. An NHL entry-level contract now would prevent Rochester assignment; Buffalo prefers one starting in 2018-19.

The passage presents a design example for a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter using TPS7H500x-SP controllers and GaN FETs. Selected values include a 205-kΩ frequency-setting resistor, a 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ output feedback divider, approximately 25 ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors, and a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor. The 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides approximately 7.5 ms of soft start. Leading-edge blank time may require optimization for PCB parasitics, ringing, gate-driver delay, and minimum on-time limits.

The transformer design targets a 35% duty cycle for margin below the controller’s 50% limit, a 2.5 turns ratio, and magnetizing current equal to 6% of output current. Although calculated primary inductance is 33 μH, 40 μH is used. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a maximum 36-V input, while 80-V synchronous rectifier FETs are selected despite an expected maximum stress of approximately 20 V. A parallel Schottky diode may reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node overshoot and requires testing-based optimization.

The output inductor is 0.47 μH with a targeted 40% ripple current. Output-capacitance calculations require at least 1.3 mF, while 2.3 mF is used to provide radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. The implementation uses seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors with a combined ESR of 0.86 mΩ. An optional LC output filter can further reduce ripple, with damping available if high-frequency peaking occurs. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins at approximately 35 A; with a peak inductor current of 24.25 A, this provides about 45% margin. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω RCS resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF.

Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover with a calculated power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. Selected compensation values are 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF. A 102-kΩ resistor is used for slope compensation.

The controllers operate from a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and require at least a 0.1-μF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably ceramic X5R or better and placed close to the device. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt loop areas and switch-node copper, separating analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, filtering CS_ILIM if required, routing SYNC away from sensitive signals, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. PCB layout examples are provided for CFP and TSSOP packages. Remaining sections cover related documentation, support resources, ESD handling, revision history, mechanical and orderable information, and TI disclaimers.

BMW’s video explains SAE’s five self-driving levels. Levels 1 and 2 automate acceleration, braking and some steering but still require constant driver attention. Level 3 allows hands-off driving in limited situations, with takeover within seconds; BMW expected it for the 2021 iNext. Level 4 allows minutes to retake control and can stop safely if the driver fails. Waymo operates limited Level 4 cars. Level 5 requires no driver and was not expected before the late 2020s.

The disclosure describes systems, methods, and computer-readable media for detecting abnormal cardiac activity using deep learning with cardiac and motion data. It addresses limitations of continuous ECG monitoring, including cumbersome or invasive sensors, short-term costs, missed asymptomatic atrial fibrillation, and motion-related noise in wearable PPG data. Cardiac data may include ECG or PPG, while motion data may include accelerometer data collected by wearable devices such as smartwatches.

Data are divided into windows and preprocessed to remove noise and outliers. Cardiac and motion signal-quality indices are determined, along with cardiovascular features such as beat-to-beat variability, entropy, and standard deviation. Optional subject contextual information includes medical history, medications, demographics, and activity. Cardiac and motion data may be transformed into time-frequency tensors using wavelet, short-time Fourier, Gabor, or cross-wavelet transforms.

A deep learning architecture uses a convolutional neural network to extract features from each tensor, a bidirectional recurrent neural network to assign class probabilities using temporal information and quality, cardiovascular, and subject features, and an attention network to weight windows and produce period-level classifications. Classes can include normal, abnormal, and noisy cardiac activity. Outputs may identify abnormal activity, its type and burden, and the window in which it occurred, and can be compiled into reports for clinicians.

JPMorgan Chase is expanding AI across its global operations, deploying its proprietary generative-AI platform to all 200,000 employees and investing roughly $18 billion in technology this year. Applications include customer service, payments, account management, wealth-management research, credit assessments, onboarding, fraud detection and risk management, with more than 175 active use cases. The bank reports significant productivity gains, while facing transparency, compliance, bias, model-risk, security, legacy-integration and cost challenges.

Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) increase short- and long-term cardiovascular disease risk, making postpartum blood pressure evaluation an important prevention opportunity. This planned secondary retrospective cohort study analyzed harmonized electronic health records from two academic health systems in the southeastern United States. It included women aged 13–54 with HDP who delivered in 2014–2017 and had blood pressure measured 15–90 days postpartum. Participants with pre-existing hypertension or implausible gestational ages were excluded, leaving 2,514 women. Cox proportional hazards models with multiple imputation assessed predictors of provider-diagnosed incident hypertension after the postpartum measurement.

Among eligible women with HDP, nearly 40% had no documented 15–90-day blood pressure check, and only 20% had one within 14 days. At 15–90 days, 32% had normal blood pressure, while 55% had readings in the stage 1 or 2 hypertension range. Overall, 315 participants (13%) were subsequently diagnosed with hypertension.

Higher systolic blood pressure, older age, and severe HDP were associated with greater hazards of incident hypertension. Comparing 140 versus 120 mmHg systolic blood pressure, the hazard ratio was 1.70; severe preeclampsia/eclampsia versus gestational hypertension, 1.49; and age 35 versus 25 years, 1.46. A later postpartum check was associated with a lower hazard. Modeled 12-month hypertension diagnosis risk was 4.7% at 110/65 mmHg and 13.0% at 140/90 mmHg. Provider-specialty sensitivity analyses produced similar findings.

Limitations included retrospective data, possible missing measurements from care outside the systems, selection differences among excluded patients, reliance on diagnosis codes, and limited generalizability beyond the U.S. South. The authors recommend consistent postpartum screening, early identification and management of hypertension and other cardiovascular risk factors, and interventions such as home monitoring, telehealth, and home visitors to overcome access barriers.

Wandera research on 50,000 iPhones and iPads found that iOS 11 drained batteries much faster than iOS 10, with estimated use falling from 240 to 96 minutes; older iPhones performed worse than newer models. Although some users reverted to iOS 10.3.3, Wandera advised against it because updated software offers greater security. iOS 11.0.1 improved battery life to 159 minutes. Users can limit background app refresh and location access and enable low-power mode while awaiting further fixes.

Enron shares fell to multiyear lows on October 29, 2001, losing more than half their value in two weeks and about $14 billion in market capitalization. The sell-off followed disclosures of a $618 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in write-offs, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. The transactions raised concerns about financial transparency and conflicts of interest, prompting an SEC inquiry and Fastow’s removal.

Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured debt from Baa1 to Baa2, two levels above junk, kept its commercial-paper rating under review, and warned of further downgrades. Standard & Poor’s also revised its outlook to negative. Analysts said Enron’s weakened credit standing could increase borrowing costs and collateral requirements from trading partners.

After drawing roughly $3.3 billion in bank credit lines to repay commercial paper, Enron sought another $1 billion to $2 billion from banks. Analysts viewed the request as a sign of desperation and expected lenders to impose harsher terms. Enron also pursued asset sales, including the planned $2.9 billion sale of Portland General Electric, and considered shifting away from its asset-light strategy.

European energy firms limited or suspended trading with Enron, while some remained active under restrictive terms. Senior departures, concerns about disclosure quality, and nearly worthless employee stock options also threatened Enron’s ability to retain talent.

At least five shareholder lawsuits challenged Enron’s private partnerships and potential conflicts of interest, with billions of dollars in possible shareholder losses alleged. Separately, Moody’s reported a broad deterioration in U.S. corporate credit, placing 122 companies under review for downgrade against 22 considered for upgrade.

This AMD specification-update excerpt identifies CS5535 companion-device errata and workarounds. Reading Port 60h can incorrectly clear AuxOutputFull, so interrupts should manage USB keyboard and mouse traffic in PS/2 emulation. IDE tACK does not affect UDMA timing, which remains fixed at 30 ns and meets requirements. ATAC can hang with WORD-aligned PRDs; ATAC drivers should use DWORD alignment. The LPC controller may abort transactions involving late defined SYNC patterns; an LPC-bus PLD can provide a workaround. SMB NEGACK may be delayed and inconsistently cleared; it should be cleared by writing 1 to SMB_STS[4], then writing 0x00 to SMB_STS. GLPCI’s retry limit also counts other PCI-bus retries and may stop retrying early. After suspend, atomic GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Register writes clear nonselected bits, requiring a read-modify-write. LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to record low-battery conditions during Normal or Restart Standby. Sleep exit may leave SLEEP_X/SLEEP_Y asserted and PCI/IDE signaling disabled; related delay counters should be set below PM_SED. The excerpt also flags short SMBus data hold time, but its details are truncated.

Connaught Public School students attempted a tunnel ball world record, with over 250 participating against Australia’s record of 120. The attempt awaits Guinness verification and raised $10,000 for planned playground, basketball court, soccer field, and tree improvements.

An analysis of 25 cities estimates the income needed to buy a home using median sale prices, a 20% down payment, and a 30-year fixed mortgage at 3.75%, including taxes and insurance. Estimates range from $7,359 annually in Detroit to $226,577 in San Francisco; Seattle’s median price of $553,000 implies a $2,668 monthly payment and $106,709 annual income.

Seattle and King County have experienced sharp price growth amid fears of a housing bubble, but experts cited in the article see little evidence of conditions similar to the 2008 crisis. King County’s median price rose 18.6% year over year to $658,000 in July 2017, while inventory fell more than 13%. Experts attributed the market’s relative strength to high credit scores, substantial down payments, and homeowner equity. They expect prices and inventory to level off rather than collapse, though practices enabling purchases by buyers with low credit scores or debt remain a concern. A survey finding that 71% of Washington homeowners feared a bubble was based on a limited national sample of 1,079 respondents.

Billionaire tech CEOs widely reject or reject the concept of work-life balance, with many portraying relentless work as essential to success. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos prefers “work-life harmony,” arguing personal happiness and professional performance reinforce each other. Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman calls the idea that greatness can be achieved in a 38-hour week “mind-boggling,” while Scale AI cofounder Lucy Guo says people needing balance may be in the wrong job, despite her own 90-hour workweeks. Zoom CEO Eric Yuan says “work is life, life is work,” though he prioritizes family in conflicts. LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman says founders seeking balance are not committed to winning, while Alibaba cofounder Jack Ma praises China’s demanding “996” schedule as an opportunity many workers lack.

U.S. consumer confidence rose to 128.7 in April from 127.0 in March, nearing February’s 18-year high of 130. Analysts linked the improvement to a strong labor market, tax cuts, reduced stock-market volatility and easing trade-war fears, but warned that sluggish real-income growth may limit spending.

NEC has established the NEC Satellite Operation Center, scheduled to become fully operational in April. It will operate ASNARO-2 using GroundNEXTAR, support multiple satellites simultaneously, and enable NEC and JEOSS to market ASNARO-2 images from September.

Precise ring-buffer halting requires the halt command to be queued last; precise error halting requires queuing one command at a time because commands may be distributed among multiple execution units. Interrupt status can be cleared only when the queue is empty or processing is paused, and interrupt generation resumes with processing. The ring-buffer tail may advance while paused.

With SMEE or SME-MK, page-migration addresses use system physical address encoding. The C-bit indicates encrypted memory, and migration parameters specify Hypervisor or Guest memory; firmware selects the encryption key ID. Addresses must be well-formed and within appropriate ranges, while the physical address space may be smaller than 52 bits.

PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports firmware capabilities and versions. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes 1–128 pages and can move DMA-active pages, updating IOMMU host page-table entries. It is restricted to Hypervisor-owned pages in SNP systems and to specified memory encryption states in SEV systems. Software must prevent CPU access and handle ATS/IOMMU synchronization before migration. In SNP systems, source and destination pages must remain in the Hypervisor state. Direct 2M-page migration is unsupported; pages must be split into 4K pages. Firmware validates addresses, page states, RMP access, and page sizes; invalidates TLBs; flushes DMA; copies data while preserving encryption; and updates page-table and migration state.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST moves 1–128 SNP guest pages. It requires aligned, physically contiguous 4K pages for 2M migrations and does not support concurrent DMA. Sources must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destinations must be Pre-Migration, and firmware validates RMP state, context, access, and page sizes before copying data and updating RMPs. A completion command marks the end of migration-command sequences.

Command-format errors cause rejection; migration-entry errors may cause partial success. Status and sub-status are reported through commands and migration lists, ring-buffer errors through PM_STATUS, and hardware failures through command status or MCA. A batch may contain up to 128 pages, and hardware errors can make the entire batch unrecoverable.

No. 1 McEachern visited Harrison on Friday night in Kennesaw, Georgia, with the game beginning at 8 p.m. Both teams entered 5-0 after a bye week. McEachern sought Top 25 consideration, while Harrison aimed to gain prominence with a win over the state’s top-ranked team.

Astronomers using LOFAR and the RAD@home citizen-science platform have discovered the most distant and powerful odd radio circle (ORC) yet identified. The double-ringed structure, RAD J131346.9+500320, dates to when the universe was about half its current age and is only the second known ORC with intersecting rings. Researchers propose that superwinds from spiral host radio galaxies, rather than black-hole mergers, may create these structures.

The team also identified two unusual giant radio galaxies in massive galaxy clusters. Each has a bent black-hole jet ending in a radio ring, likely shaped by interactions between magnetized plasma and surrounding hot gas. Together, the discoveries suggest ORCs and related radio rings belong to a broader family of exotic plasma structures shaped by jets, winds, and their environments. Future observations with the SKA, DESI, and Vera C. Rubin Observatory are expected to clarify their origins and evolution.

The TPS7H500x-SP uses an OTA error amplifier and supports Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation. Type 2A adds CHF in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Compensation selection begins with the crossover frequency; RCOMP is calculated using the typical 1800 µA/V error-amplifier transconductance and 0.613 V reference, while CCOMP places the compensation zero at the power-stage dominant pole. CHF may be added to create a high-frequency pole that compensates the output-capacitor ESR zero. Power-stage transconductance calculations depend on converter topology, transformer and current-sense turns ratios, sense resistance, and the COMP-to-current-limit scaling factor.

Thermal shutdown stops switching when junction temperature exceeds 175°C typically and restarts the power-up sequence below 160°C. The controllers use fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode control: an internal oscillator initiates the primary gate-drive output, and the power switch turns off when the externally sensed current reaches the stepped-down COMP voltage.

The radiation-hardness-assured controllers are intended for space-grade DC-DC converters, require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with GaN semiconductors in buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A TPS7H5001-SP example designs a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull GaN converter. Selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, a 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ VSENSE divider, 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ RPS and RSP resistors, and a 49.9-kΩ RLEB for an initial 50-ns leading-edge blank time. Blank time may require optimization for PCB ringing and gate-driver delay and can limit maximum switching frequency. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides approximately 7.5 ms of soft start.

The transformer design targets a 35% duty-cycle limit despite the controller’s 50% limit, uses a 2.5 turns ratio, and targets magnetizing current equal to 6% of output current. Although the calculated primary inductance was 33 µH, the design uses 40 µH. Primary GaN FETs are rated 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while 80-V synchronous rectifier FETs are selected for an expected maximum stress of about 20 V. A parallel Schottky diode is suggested to reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node overshoot and requires test-based optimization.

The output inductor is 0.47 µH with a targeted 40% ripple current. Output-capacitance calculations use a 2% ripple target and 2.5% maximum load-transient deviation, requiring at least 1.3 mF. Radiation-induced single-event transients may require additional capacitance; the example uses 2.3 mF total, provided by seven 330-µF polymer-tantalum capacitors with 0.86-mΩ equivalent ESR. An optional LC output filter can reduce output noise, with its resonant frequency selected above the crossover frequency but below the switching frequency and bulk-capacitor ESR zero; a resistor may be added to damp peaking.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω RCS are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover with 16.2 A/V power-stage transconductance and uses RCOMP of 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP of 15 nF, and CHF of 47 pF. A 102-kΩ resistor between RSC and AVSS sets slope compensation.

The controller supply range is 4 V to 14 V. At least 0.1 µF is required from VIN to AVSS, with X5R-or-better ceramic bypass capacitors placed close to the controller and additional bulk capacitance when the supply is remote.

Layout guidance emphasizes keeping feedback and control traces away from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, separating AVSS from power ground except at a single connection, using short and wide high-current traces, placing bypass and compensation components near their pins, filtering CS_ILIM if required, and routing high-dv/dt output and SYNC signals away from sensitive pins. For CFP packages, backside metallization should connect to the AVSS plane through multiple vias.

Peter Marks, the former top FDA vaccine regulator ousted by RFK Jr., joined Eli Lilly to lead molecule discovery and infectious diseases. His appointment drew criticism over the revolving door between government and industry. Marks said he aims to advance infectious disease products for public health.

Louisiana sued the “Banking Department” of the Citizens’ Bank for an unpaid banking-business license, alleging that the department was a separate corporation. The bank’s president objected that no such corporation existed and that he could not represent it. The court held that the statutes and compact created no separate corporation authorized to sue and be sued; the Citizens’ Bank of Louisiana was the proper corporate entity and had not been made a party. Because *Hope & Co. v. Board of Liquidation* involved the Citizens’ Bank itself rather than its purported department, it did not support the state’s claim. The court limited its ruling to the defect in citation, reversed the judgment for the defendant, and dismissed the suit as in the nature of a nonsuit. Justice Monroe dissented.

A February 25 Enron industry-news roundup reported:

- Enron’s pipelines and power plants remained its principal sources of steady income and were expected to form the core of the company after bankruptcy. UBS Warburg had hired most of Enron’s trading staff and agreed to give Enron 33% of the new operation’s profits. Enron continued pursuing asset sales, including its Portland General Electric utility, broadband unit, wind subsidiary, and Indian oil and gas assets, while Brazil and Bolivia operations appeared likely to be retained. Creditors were expected to seek cash, future payments, and equity in the reorganized company, and Enron proposed retention bonuses and severance packages for employees.

- FERC acknowledged 25 contacts between senior officials and Enron executives from August 2000 to June 2001. Chairman Pat Wood denied that Enron improperly influenced the agency, saying his tenure began after most contacts occurred. Senator Barbara Boxer cited the meetings as evidence of improper closeness, while FERC said its officials followed ethics rules.

- Nuon reportedly was considering replacing Azurix as operator of Buenos Aires province’s waterworks concession when the contract ended. Azurix sought $150 million to $200 million in compensation, citing concession rights and other investments, amid quality and service problems.

- BG Group planned to more than double its Indian investment from about $500 million to $1.3 billion over three to five years, targeting upstream oil and gas and LNG. It had acquired Enron’s Indian assets for $350 million, was developing an LNG terminal at Pipavav, and planned offshore drilling, while continuing to dispute management of the fields with Oil & Natural Gas Corp.

- Enron Japan’s assets appeared unlikely to generate meaningful creditor repayments. Its mainly office equipment, modest deposit, and unsellable trading system were outweighed by possible closure costs, and employee salary and bonus claims had priority.

- Enron-related overseas power projects received $1.2 billion in government-backed loans from OPIC and the Export-Import Bank, which remained owed $453 million and $512 million, respectively. Enron’s bankruptcy did not jeopardize the loans because separate corporations held the projects. Four OPIC-backed Enron projects were operating and paying on time, while the India Dabhol plant remained idle and was the subject of a $200 million political-risk insurance claim.

- The Senate prepared for broad energy legislation focused on Alaska’s Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, vehicle fuel economy, renewable fuels, tax incentives, and federal oversight of electricity markets. Republican proposals favored expanded production and producer tax breaks; Democratic proposals emphasized conservation, efficiency, renewables, and natural gas. Several disputes threatened the bill’s progress.

- California Gov. Gray Davis was considering delaying the state’s MTBE ban until 2005 after an economic analysis warned that replacing MTBE with ethanol could cause gasoline shortages and price increases because California lacked sufficient storage, terminal, and pipeline capacity. The EPA had rejected Davis’s request for a waiver that would have allowed the state to avoid both MTBE and ethanol.

The paper proposes a Bucketized Hysteresis Controller (BHC) for budget pacing in real-time advertising auctions, aiming to align actual spending with target rates despite volatile traffic, auction dynamics, and market changes. BHC uses multiplicative, variable-step updates based on discretized error bands: large errors trigger larger adjustments for faster convergence, while small errors trigger smaller steps for stability. This contrasts with proportional or integral feedback methods that may oscillate or require delicate tuning.

In the described auction setup, bids are based on maximum bid and event probability, while a pacing multiplier adjusts bids to influence win rates and spending. The production baseline adaptively changes its update scale according to recent trajectory fluctuations, increasing it for smooth trends and decreasing it for oscillatory behavior.

The paper’s contributions include implementing BHC, developing an analytical framework for parameter selection and personalized spend-rate tracking, and validating the method in real-world auction experiments. The authors report significant improvements over legacy feedback-based pacing, particularly for small-budget campaigns, and describe BHC as the first multi-step hysteresis approach applied to budget pacing in real-time auctions.

In Windows 10, adjust the mouse pointer through **Settings > Ease of Access > Mouse**, changing its size or color. For more control over shape and size, use **Control Panel > Mouse > Pointers**.

In Safari on an iPhone, close all tabs by pressing and holding the **Tabs** button and selecting **“Close xx Tabs.”** If the tab page is already open, press and hold **Done** instead. Restarting Safari will not close them because it restores the previous session’s tabs.

NASA released the closest-ever images of Ceres’s Occator Crater, revealing its bright sodium carbonate deposits, or faculae, from a new Dawn orbit about 22 miles above the surface. The June 14 image shows Vinalia Faculae in the crater’s east, while a June 22 image captures Cerealia Facula at its center and a prominent mound on its western side. Their origin remains uncertain; possibilities include exposure by mineral-laden subsurface water or brines rising through fractures. Dawn’s extended mission is using gravity measurements and spectral observations to investigate Ceres’s interior and composition. With its ion-engine fuel nearly depleted, the spacecraft is approaching the end of its mission and will remain in its final orbit to avoid contaminating Ceres.

Canadian Pacific Railway says service changes in Vancouver and North Dakota can deliver imported goods to key U.S. markets up to 48 hours faster than rival Canadian National Railway, including five-day container trips to Detroit. The rail says quicker transit lowers shipper costs, while Hapag-Lloyd welcomes more efficient market access.

Euro zone stocks climbed to their highest level in over a year as the bloc’s manufacturing PMI reached 54.9, lifting major indexes, although thin holiday trading raised volatility concerns. The euro fell 0.3% below $1.05 while the dollar index gained 0.4%. Italian, Spanish and Portuguese 10-year bond yields fell about 8 basis points amid improved risk appetite. The Istanbul nightclub attack, claimed by Islamic State, had little immediate market impact; the Turkish lira slipped toward a record low, while the yen remained near an 11-month low against the dollar. China’s manufacturing sector expanded for a fifth month, though growth slowed, and the yuan lost nearly 7% in 2016. Bitcoin topped $1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

- IRS witnesses urged the agency to broaden proposed hedging regulations to replace the existing risk-reduction standard with Congress’s broader risk-management standard. Recommendations included hedging treatment for ordinary-course commodities transactions, weather and energy derivatives, dividend and profitability risks, life insurers’ gap hedges, services income from converting commodities, and weather-related price risks.

- BIS data showed that growth in outstanding over-the-counter derivatives slowed in the second half of 2000. Notional value rose 1% to $95.2 trillion, versus nearly 7% in the first half. Interest-rate derivatives represented 68% of the market; euro-denominated contracts declined 7%, while dollar interest-rate swaps grew about 10%. Gross market values rose 24% to $3.2 trillion.

- The Federal Home Loan Bank of New York implemented full FAS 133 compliance using Principia Partners’ PAS, which supports derivative valuation, accounting, hedge-effectiveness assessment, market valuation and reporting.

- A former CFTC chairman identified dual CFTC-SEC regulation, higher margin, lower trading volumes than stock options and a three-year ban on options on single-stock futures as potential drawbacks. Meanwhile, CME and CBOE created a joint venture, with CBOT holding a limited stake, to introduce electronically traded single-stock futures through CBOEdirect and GLOBEX2. The venture would operate as a separately managed, regulated for-profit exchange and was negotiating clearing arrangements with the Options Clearing Corporation.

- FASB’s Derivatives Implementation Group issued a guideline allowing option fair-value changes to be recorded in other comprehensive income until the hedged transaction affects earnings, provided the option exactly matches the underlying exposure. FASB maintained that no amendment to FAS 133 would be made.

- Basel Committee officials defended the proposed capital charge on credit-derivative positions, saying it addressed material legal, documentation and payout risks and could not be eliminated merely through insurance. The UK FSA favored applying Basel prudential standards to insurers, faster agreement on the new Accord and stronger unified regulation of UK financial markets.

- The UK Treasury proposed legislation allowing building societies to use credit derivatives for risk management, including hedging borrower defaults, while retaining restrictions against speculative positions.

- Heavy credit-linked note issuance led dealers to offset short credit-default-swap positions, sharply widening negative swap-to-bond bases and creating arbitrage opportunities. A shortage of bonds and improving credit sentiment amplified the effect, with WorldCom’s large corporate deal illustrating falling swap quotes.

- Lightrade planned to connect its neutral bandwidth pooling-point network between New York and Los Angeles by the end of June, deploy seven or eight additional US centers and explore European sites. Energy traders used its switches for about 75% of current bandwidth trading, while carriers remained reluctant to interconnect with the neutral intermediary.

- ISDA finalized a restructuring supplement for its 1999 Credit Derivatives Definitions. It limits delivery of physical securities after a restructuring to obligations maturing within 30 months of the restructuring date or at the restructured loan’s extended maturity, and defines eligible transferees for certain deliverable obligations. The changes addressed concerns about “cheapest-to-deliver” settlement following Conseco’s restructuring.

The Horns Offense uses high-post screening and can create easy layups or open shots against unprepared defenses. Because a big typically screens a smaller defender, switching may allow the screener to post up; defenders should instead influence ballhandlers toward weaker threats or away from strong post players. NBA “Show and Recover” defense progresses from showing the screen and providing help, to recovering and rotating against the roller, to final pressure, post defense, and pass denial. “All Out SOS” defense traps the point guard before any screen or pass, disrupting planned routes and enabling coordinated rotations, on-ball setups, helpside positioning, and baseline or post traps.

Roger Poole, chairman of Petworth and Bognor Angling Club, says the new coarse-fishing season requires reassessing baits, tactics and swims as rivers change. The closed season allows fish to spawn and regain strength, so varied baits should be offered alongside natural foods such as bugs, worms, flies and grubs. He encourages clubs to attract young people, noting children’s enthusiasm during fishing events, and says adults can support angling’s future by taking children fishing. National Fishing Month, backed by the Environment Agency and promoted by Jeremy Wade, Nick Hancock and the angling trade, runs from July 27 to September 2, with more than 250 UK events for children and adults; under-16s can enjoy a free licence. Early-season fishing at the club’s ponds and the Rother and Arun includes active tench, chub in river margins, and methods targeting dace, roach, perch, bream, chub and occasional barbel. Poole recommends experimenting with baits.

The passage contrasts the arrest of Travis Reinking, who allegedly shot four people at a Nashville Waffle House, with police violence against unarmed Black people. After James Shaw Jr. tackled and disarmed Reinking, officers located him in the woods, handcuffed him without firing, and found a handgun and ammunition in his backpack. The passage also cites the forceful arrest of Chikesia Clemons at an Alabama Waffle House and argues that racial bias affects policing in the U.S.

Guyana’s Office of Climate Change opened a three-day Greenhouse Gas Inventory workshop to prepare for the Third National Communication, due for submission in 2019. The workshop seeks to strengthen national technical and institutional capacity, create a pool of trained experts, improve climate reporting, and integrate climate priorities into development strategies. Other TNC components—mitigation, national baselines, and vulnerability and adaptation—will be addressed later. National Project Coordinator Marlon Velloza said the inventory findings could advance Guyana’s green agenda and urged public education and participation. Overseas experts provided sessions, with certification planned for workshop participants.

Napheesa Collier suffered a Grade 2 tear of three ankle ligaments and a shin muscle during a Friday collision, requiring at least six weeks of recovery. The top-seeded Minnesota Lynx were eliminated by the Phoenix Mercury in Game 4 of their semifinal series. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve was ejected during Game 3 and received a one-game suspension for her reaction to the injury-causing play.

The Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator is defined as (Close − Low) / (High − Low) and ranges from zero to one. It applies mean reversion: low readings are considered bullish, while high readings are bearish in the short term. The article reports strong long-term results for stocks and broad stock indices, with weaker performance in commodity-related stocks, Norwegian and Australian markets, gold, and metals.

Backtests using SPY and QQQ produced favorable results before slippage and commissions. A modified SPY strategy had a 15.3% CAGR, a 74% win rate, a 22% maximum drawdown, a 2.73 profit factor, and a 1.7 Sharpe ratio. QQQ returned 0.56% per trade and compounded at 16.6%, versus 9% for buy and hold. Performance was strongest during volatile bear markets. Adding a VIX volatility filter or limiting entries when SPY was no more than 5% above its 200-day moving average improved results, although the latter carried substantial curve-fitting risk.

Execution is the strategy’s main weakness because it requires entering near the closing price; delaying until the next open significantly reduced returns. The article recommends combining IBS with other indicators or factors and adapting strategies to each market rather than expecting universal performance across asset classes.

NEC will extend warranties from three to five years for four P-series professional signage displays; P404, P484 and P554 qualify from first shipment, while P703 applies to purchases on or after August 1, 2017.

The passage promotes a functional food therapeutic lifestyle-change program and Maxwell Chan’s book as alternatives to conventional high-cholesterol treatment. It claims that conventional care lowers cholesterol without addressing underlying causes, requiring lifelong statins and exposing patients to side effects. It describes hyperlipidemia as a complex metabolic condition involving the liver, kidneys, and spleen, with causes and treatments varying by cholesterol type. The book reportedly identifies 14 common underlying causes and related solutions, while the program uses individualized assessments of lifestyle, environment, genetics, and family influences. The author presents this practitioner-patient approach as a natural, side-effect-free method for addressing chronic disease.

The passage describes the new Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge, which replaced the Tappan Zee Bridge. Its 3.1-mile crossing includes a 2,230-foot elevated main span designed to last 100 years without major maintenance, supported by eight towers and cable stays. Project Director Jamey Barbas discussed its innovative design, environmental safeguards, labor coordination, safety planning, and public outreach. Construction required specialized concrete plants, modular components, and the 328-foot floating crane “I Lift NY,” which can hoist 1,900 tons. More than one million design hours and nearly nine million work hours from 7,000 people contributed to the project.

University of Alabama student Kelsey Hall wore a Christmas tree costume to class for the rest of the semester after her Twitter challenge received 30,000 retweets. The attention became stressful, and she may avoid future social media challenges.

“High School Sports Talk,” hosted by Matthew Hatfield and Coach Ed Young, airs Saturdays from 10 a.m. to noon on ESPN Radio 94.1. The fourth Nike Elite Youth Basketball League session was recorded at Boo Williams Sportsplex in Hampton before the July Peach Jam, featuring Chris Duhon, Jalen Lecque, David Teel, Cam Bacote, Bryan Kersey, Ed Miller, and Keyontae Johnson. A full program replay and individual segments were available via Dropbox.

Alpha Theory’s analysis of clients’ historical data identifies recurring position-sizing biases. Managers often do not reduce exposure after large price gains despite lower probability-weighted returns, and they tend to build positions gradually, missing some potential returns. Re-underwriting at unacceptable PWR levels is recommended as a check against holding winners into reversals. More disciplined managers, with greater price-target coverage and sizes closer to optimal, outperform less disciplined ones; positions without explicit targets underperform. The largest holdings are generally smaller names with high batting averages, but expanding into many lower-PWR names can dilute the benefit. A Monte Carlo study using 2011–2016 data found concentrated portfolios outperformed diversified ones by 2.2% on an alpha basis. Optimal sizing could have improved 2016 returns by 5.1%.

The lecture reviews the development of experimental design from Sir Edward John Russell’s preference for simple, one-question-at-a-time experiments to R. A. Fisher’s complex factorial designs. Fertilizer trials at Rothamsted were complicated by declining effects, pests, and field variation, leading Fisher to emphasize that statistical planning should occur before experiments are run. Fisher’s balanced \(2^3\) factorial design reduced the influence of nuisance factors and doubled efficiency relative to a single-factor experiment, but full factorials scale poorly as the number of factors increases.

Fractional factorial designs reduce experimental size by deliberately sacrificing information. Their projection properties can provide full-factorial coverage for whichever few factors are most important, but interactions may be confounded with main effects. This creates a trade-off between experimental efficiency and the ability to identify causes accurately.

Robust parameter design uses controllable factors to reduce sensitivity to uncontrollable or “noise” factors. Taguchi popularized orthogonal and factorial arrays crossing control and noise factors, although crossarrays can become large. Combined-array approaches were developed to reduce this burden. These methods became entrenched in industry through programs such as Six Sigma, despite a reported validation study finding that some theoretically promising procedures can fail.

An audit of an agricultural-equipment manufacturer helped motivate further study. Of 30 planned robust-design experiments, only five had written reports; the rest were unfinished because of equipment failures, time constraints, and similar reasons. This raised the possibility that adaptive one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experiments might be preferable when experiments may be canceled, because completed results remain easy to analyze.

In an empirical comparison of 66 chemical, mechanical, and electrical systems, adaptive OFAT experiments performed at least as well as fractional factorials when experimental error was about 25% of the combined factor effect or interactions were sufficiently strong. A theoretical model attributes adaptive improvement to main effects and interactions and shows that interaction exploitation becomes more likely as the experiment progresses. For seven two-level factors, eight adaptive experiments reportedly achieved about 80% of the possible improvement, compared with 128 trials for a full factorial. Factor order had relatively little effect, while a promising informed starting point substantially improved results.

For robust design, the lecturer combined adaptive control-factor adjustments with factorial experiments over noise factors. Validation using sheet-metal spinning and paper airplanes found that Taguchi-style crossed arrays improved signal-to-noise ratios, while adaptive procedures often performed slightly better; informed starting points performed best. At high experimental error, fractional factorials could be marginally better unless informed starts were used, though adaptive methods showed less case-to-case variability. Fractional factorials are optimized to minimize experimental error but are especially vulnerable to uncertainty about where interactions occur.

When larger experimental budgets are available, ensembles of four adaptive OFAT runs can outperform a \(2^{7-2}\) fractional factorial and become increasingly robust as experimental error rises. Practical constraints also favor factorial designs when experiments must be parallel or measurements are delayed. Adaptive methods are most appropriate when rapid system improvement matters more than precise effect estimation or reusable archival knowledge.

The final “streamlining” analysis concluded that relatively inexpensive experiments can deliver about 80% of the benefit of more rigorous studies at roughly one-tenth the cost. When organizations are uncertain about where their largest quality problems lie, conducting many broader experiments may be better than a few expensive ones; the latter approach requires very high confidence, around 95%, that the critical problems are correctly identified. The broader conclusion is to make robust-design methods widely accessible and apply them to nearly every new or uncertain system rather than reserving them for a few highly targeted studies.

Showstoppers Theatre presents “Foiled Again!” at La Colina Junior High School. The children’s musical theater program covers acting, singing, choreography, costumes, sets, lighting, and sound; no experience is required. Children 12 and younger are free, while general admission is $7.

Parise urged his team to generate more shots, block the goalie’s vision, use offensive-zone pressure and rebounds, and try to move the series back to New Jersey. He credited the opposing defense for strong gaps and box-outs while noting his team needs better puck movement and greater pressure on the goalie. He said all three games felt winnable and emphasized winning tonight.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the first quarter of fiscal 2016, ended April 26, 2015. Revenue was $1.151 billion, up 4% from $1.103 billion a year earlier. GPU revenue rose 5% to $940 million, driven by GeForce gaming GPUs and increased Tesla sales for deep learning and cloud projects; Tegra Processor revenue rose 4% to $145 million due to automotive, custom-development and SHIELD sales, partly offset by lower smartphone and tablet sales. “All Other” revenue remained $66 million, primarily from an Intel patent cross-license.

Gross profit increased to $653 million from $604 million, and gross margin rose to 56.7% from 54.8%, primarily reflecting a richer mix of Maxwell-based GeForce products and higher Tesla and GRID sales. Tegra gross margin declined because automotive and SHIELD products have lower margins than smartphone and tablet products. Operating income was $176 million versus $151 million. Research and development expense was nearly unchanged at $339 million, while sales, general and administrative expense rose 16% to $138 million, including $16 million of litigation-related legal fees.

Net income declined to $134 million from $137 million as the effective tax rate increased to 22.0% from 16.4%. Basic and diluted earnings per share were $0.24 in both periods. Operating cash flow increased to $246 million from $151 million, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $4.792 billion at quarter-end. Total assets were $7.291 billion, total shareholders’ equity was $4.556 billion, and long-term debt was $1.391 billion.

GPU segment operating income was $278 million, compared with $235 million a year earlier. Tegra Processor reported an operating loss of $57 million, compared with $62 million, while the “All Other” category reported a $45 million loss, compared with $22 million. The company’s principal GPU brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla and GRID, while Tegra integrates GPUs and multi-core CPUs into processors for mobile and automotive applications.

During the quarter, NVIDIA launched the GeForce GTX TITAN X, introduced the Quadro M6000 and Quadro Visual Computing Appliance, announced Iray 2015 and the Pascal architecture, and launched NVIDIA SHIELD, a Tegra X1-powered entertainment device. It also announced NVIDIA DRIVE PX for self-driving vehicle applications.

NVIDIA returned $99 million to shareholders during the quarter through $53 million of share repurchases and $46 million in dividends. In May 2015, the board extended the repurchase authorization through 2018 and added $1.62 billion, leaving $2.00 billion available for future repurchases. The company increased its quarterly dividend 15% to $0.0975 per share and raised its intended fiscal 2016 shareholder return to $800 million. On May 11, it entered a $400 million accelerated share repurchase agreement and initially received 14 million shares.

NVIDIA announced the wind-down or possible sale of its Icera modem operations, with estimated fiscal 2016 restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million if no sale occurs and a potential reduction of approximately 500 employees, primarily in the United Kingdom and France.

The company remained involved in securities litigation and patent disputes with Samsung and Qualcomm. The securities class action had been dismissed and the dismissal affirmed on appeal; NVIDIA opposed a subsequent petition for Supreme Court review. NVIDIA also brought patent claims against Samsung and Qualcomm, while Samsung asserted separate patent claims against NVIDIA. No loss accrual was recorded because potential liabilities were not considered probable and could not be reasonably estimated.

Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, reported no material changes in internal financial controls, and noted no material changes in financial market risks. The unaudited interim statements were prepared under U.S. GAAP, and there were no material changes to significant accounting policies.

Major indexes fell 2.2%–4.2% for the week, forming bearish engulfing patterns as market breadth, volume and volatility confirmed a short-term risk-off shift. Nearly every sector declined except utilities, while weakness spread to regional banks and transports. Stronger-than-expected GDP was distorted by tariff-related import volatility and low personal spending. Nonfarm payrolls rose only 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with the prior two months revised sharply downward and the labor force contracting. The Fed remained patient and data-dependent amid tariff and immigration uncertainty, while markets priced in a greater than 75% chance of a September rate cut and three cuts by January. Q2 earnings remained encouraging: 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies exceeded EPS estimates and 79% exceeded revenue estimates, with upward revisions also increasing. The article attributes the pullback to profit-taking, economic uncertainty, policy noise and a lack of new buyers, advising tactical positioning and downside-risk management.

The 2-1-2 zone is a compact variation of the 2-3 zone that protects the middle rather than the baseline and corners. It places an athletic defender in the middle and the “Bigs” near the basket for rebounding, but is vulnerable to outside shooting. It is mainly used against teams with poor perimeter shooting or against high-post offenses such as the 1-3-1. Defenders shift according to ball position: X5 protects the middle and low post, X1 and X2 cover the ball and elbow areas while moving in unison, and X3 and X4 alternate between baseline and weak-side rebounding positions. When the ball enters the middle, X5 pressures the ballhandler toward a corner while the other defenders collapse to protect against high- and low-post passes.

A teardown of Google Wallet version 20 suggests upcoming security changes, though the findings are speculative and the features may not yet be widely available. Wallet is expected to support fingerprint unlocking, replacing the need to enter a frequently forgotten PIN. It may also replace its dedicated Payments PIN with the Google Account PIN already used by services such as Google Play and G Suite, reducing the number of PINs users must remember. Additional strings indicate that Wallet users may eventually be able to access the app without any PIN, particularly if their phones are securely locked or no payment methods are configured. The Google-signed APK upgrades the existing app and is available for manual installation.

A fake WhatsApp link claims PM Narendra Modi is giving everyone ₹500 in free recharge. It requests a mobile number, operator, and state, then asks users to share it with 15 friends. The article says the site is fake, possibly operated by hackers who could misuse submitted information, and is unaffiliated with telecom companies. Users are urged not to click the link, provide details, or share it.

AMZN options trading allows investors to speculate on stock-price movements or hedge existing positions without owning the stock. It offers leverage and potentially limits risk through spread strategies, but requires substantial research, a broker margin account, enough capital to cover premiums and fees, and a thorough understanding of leverage and potential losses.

Strategies include buying calls or puts, writing covered or naked calls or puts, and spread trading. Covered strategies generate premium with some downside protection, while naked options carry potentially unlimited or substantial losses. Spreads combine options with different strike prices or expirations to limit risk and exploit premium differences.

Key risks include rapid losses from leverage, expiration—most options expire worthless—loss of premiums, limited liquidity, and margin calls. Call prices generally rise as AMZN rises and fall as it declines, while put prices move inversely; delta measures sensitivity to stock-price changes. Strike prices determine exercise prices and potential payoffs.

Traders can place market, limit, and stop orders. Expirations are usually on the third Friday of the month, though some brokers offer weekly or monthly options. The paper investigates classical unit-vector spins with bilinear–biquadratic interactions on partially anisotropic triangular lattices composed of isosceles triangles. The four interaction parameters are bilinear couplings \(K,L\) and biquadratic couplings \(A,B\). The problem reduces to one triangular plaquette, allowing global ground states to be constructed for lattices of identical triangles. The spin angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) occupy a tetrahedron, whose surface represents coplanar configurations. Minimizing the plaquette energy over its vertices, edges, faces, and interior yields ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, coplanar, Sp, and noncoplanar configurations. Interior solutions satisfy \(\cos\alpha=K/(2A)\) and \(\cos\beta=\cos\gamma=L/(2B)\), while additional face solutions and validity conditions are derived. Ground-state phase diagrams for the Heisenberg and XY models are presented for selected values of \(A\), distinguishing continuous and discontinuous transitions.
