Electrical specifications cover recommended operating and absolute-maximum conditions, power consumption, POR/BOR behavior, flash endurance and timing, reset and wakeup timing, internal and external clocks, digital I/O, ADC, VREF, temperature sensor, comparator, SPI, UART, and thermal performance. MCLK, CPUCLK, and ULPCLK support 32 MHz with one flash wait state or 24 MHz with no wait states.

The devices include a three-channel DMA, event manager, GPIO and IOMUX, 12-bit 1.6-Msps ADC, comparator with an 8-bit reference DAC, internal temperature sensor, CRC-16, security firewalls, advanced and general-purpose timers, watchdog timers, RTC, three UARTs, one SPI, and two I²Cs. Five power modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—are supported across two power domains. The document also covers SWD/debug support, factory constants, typical application circuitry, development tools, nomenclature, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The hockey series has been tight and evenly balanced, with neither team separating itself and no games reaching overtime. Jonathan Toews says both teams are confident, emphasizing home-ice energy, contributions from all four lines, defensive work, a strong penalty kill, and the importance of every player performing in key situations. Kimmo Timonen praises the veteran players’ dedication and preparation, while Trevor van Riemsdyk highlights their work ethic and competitiveness. Players are encouraged to focus on the next shift, shake off mistakes, and avoid dwelling on the season’s finish line; Timonen says the team must concentrate on Saturday’s game while pursuing its larger goal. Toews identifies the opponent’s coordinated five-man units and defensemen joining the rush as major threats, requiring strong backchecking and puck possession. The team also stresses winning battles, body position, speed, and small details to prevent the opponent from establishing its open, puck-moving style. Timonen acknowledges that the team did not play its best in the previous game, praises Corey’s performance, and says the priority is improving for Saturday.

Queensland Firebirds goalshooter Romelda Aiken is unlikely to leave despite rival clubs’ decade-long pursuit, saying a strong support system has always made staying easy. She will make her 150th national league appearance against Collingwood after the Firebirds’ 71-61 win over West Coast Fever moved them to third. Since debuting in 2008, Aiken has won three MVPs, a grand-final MVP and three championships, and made 5,576 shots from 6,583 attempts. She is seeking greater versatility and continued improvement.

George Azar’s Good Beer Company bought Paddington’s Four in Hand Hotel for $7 million, keeping it operating as a pub after locals opposed a residential conversion. The company, run by Azar’s nephew John, is keen to expand the venue’s craft-beer range and also operates two other pubs. The sale followed protests, Woollahra Council’s heritage protection of the facade and a petition signed by more than 12,000 people.

Henrico County Economic Development Authority executive director Gary McLaren said Facebook’s planned $750 million data center at White Oak Technology Park benefits county residents and taxpayers. White Oak’s existing semiconductor-era infrastructure includes excess water and sewer capacity, multiple fiber providers, transatlantic cables, and dual power feeds capable of supporting data-center operations.

McLaren said Henrico also lowered taxes on computers and related equipment to compete with Northern Virginia data-center hubs, acknowledging that the cut created a windfall for existing local centers but claiming Facebook’s arrival more than offsets the lost revenue. Detailed net-gain figures were withheld because they contain proprietary information. Facebook also received an $863,000 credit toward a roughly $2 million water-sewer connection fee; McLaren said this used previously issued infrastructure credits and adds no county liability.

McLaren noted that Henrico already hosts numerous data centers and hoped the Facebook project would attract more. He cited the county’s ability to move quickly with projects, which he said Facebook valued, and said regional power constraints may limit development elsewhere in Northern Virginia.

WSCUC’s Senior College and University Commission adopted revised 2023 standards removing diversity, equity and inclusion references. Changes replace DEI commitments with language promoting institutional excellence and success for all students. The revisions followed a public-comment process and pressure on accreditors to end DEI requirements.

The lecture reviews the convergence criterion \(\lvert x_n-x\rvert\to0\), the squeeze theorem, and the binomial theorem. It proves that, for \(p>0\), \(n^{-p}\to0\), \(p^{1/n}\to1\), and \(n^{1/n}\to1\), using elementary inequalities and the binomial theorem. It also notes that positive real powers can be defined without introducing exponentials or logarithms.

For a bounded sequence \((x_n)\), it defines
\[
a_n=\sup\{x_k:k\ge n\},\qquad b_n=\inf\{x_k:k\ge n\},
\]
and then defines \(\limsup x_n\) and \(\liminf x_n\) as the respective limits of \(a_n\) and \(b_n\). The sequence \(a_n\) is shown to be decreasing and bounded, while \(b_n\) is increasing and bounded; hence both limits always exist, with \(\liminf x_n\le\limsup x_n\).

Examples include \((-1)^n\), whose limsup is \(1\) and liminf is \(-1\), and \(1/n\), whose limsup and liminf are both \(0\).

The lecture proves that every bounded sequence has a subsequence converging to its limsup and another converging to its liminf. This immediately yields the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem: every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence. Finally, it proves that a bounded sequence converges if and only if its limsup and liminf are equal, in which case both equal its limit.

This single-center retrospective study compared tenecteplase with alteplase for acute ischemic stroke in 264 patients treated at Ningbo University’s First Affiliated Hospital from 2022–2023. Tenecteplase’s enhanced fibrin specificity, longer half-life, and rapid intravenous administration were expected to improve thrombolysis workflow. Compared with alteplase, tenecteplase was associated with shorter onset-to-treatment, door-to-needle, and door-to-puncture times; higher rates of treatment within the 45-minute door-to-needle and 120-minute door-to-puncture targets; greater 24-hour NIHSS improvement (64.17% vs. 50%); and shorter hospital stays (6 vs. 8 days). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage rates did not differ significantly. Regression analysis identified tenecteplase as an independent predictor of target door-to-needle and door-to-puncture times and 24-hour NIHSS improvement. Limitations include the single-center, nonrandomized design, short-term outcomes, and predominantly mild-to-moderate strokes; larger multicenter studies and longer follow-up were recommended.

This qualitative study examines digitalization in education within private-sector organizations. Data were collected through a researcher-developed, five-question semi-structured interview form sent by email to 20 education managers; five participants were interviewed via Zoom for 30 minutes. Interviews were analyzed inductively through content analysis.

Participants described adapting to digitalization through online and hybrid training, digital education systems, online academies, training videos, educational platforms, technological tools, workshops, and projects. Reported benefits included time and cost savings, time- and place-independent access, equal access opportunities, broader participation, improved accessibility, personalized learning, increased motivation, and expanded e-learning and gamification content.

Challenges included technological problems, insufficient financial resources, unsuitable educational content, limited participation, lack of digital materials and applications, resistance to change, difficulty adapting quickly, unequal opportunities, low digital literacy, and distractions. Negative effects included reduced concentration, detachment from learning, insufficient face-to-face interaction, difficulty with practical activities, reduced efficiency, cyberbullying, challenges in measuring outcomes, and cheating. Participants associated digitalization primarily with technological opportunities and easy access to education.

The study recommends that educational institutions adapt to digitalization while retaining face-to-face education. It emphasizes technologically redesigned content, virtual-reality materials, gamification, and the use of private-sector practices to support digital adaptation in national and higher education.

The Hawaiian (Sandwich) Islands were strategically important to U.S. Pacific possessions, and the United States would not accept their transfer to another maritime or commercial power. As Hawaii’s government appeared to be nearing decay, the United States sought information on population, trade, industry, resources, debt, and conditions over time before deciding its policy. Its representative was directed to encourage interest in annexation without committing the United States and discreetly ascertain Hawaiian authorities’ views, including possible terms and conditions.

The passage recounts the 1874 succession crisis after King Lunalilo died and David Kalakaua was elected. Amid threats of violence and attacks on government buildings, U.S. and British naval forces landed to preserve order; the British intervention was later regularized by a backdated request. Kalakaua later visited the United States to advance reciprocity negotiations, despite opposition from the British and French commissioners.

An enhanced DiffCSP workflow was developed for inverse design of superconductors. A foundation model was pretrained on 1,857,222 Alexandria crystal structures to learn plausible structural priors, then fine-tuned using 7,183 labeled superconductors to condition generation on target critical temperatures. Classifier-free guidance generated 200,000 candidates. Guidance shifted generations toward a 10 K target, but an out-of-distribution 110 K target was not achieved.

Multi-stage screening combined machine learning and DFT to assess novelty, metallicity, superconducting propensity, thermodynamic stability, dynamical stability, and critical temperature. This reduced 200,000 structures to 34,027 unique candidates and ultimately identified 773 candidates with DFT-calculated \(T_c>5\) K and \(E_{\text{hull}}<200\) meV/atom. The 2.3% hit rate was about 135 times the element-substitution baseline and yielded roughly 31 times more candidates than a previous generative approach.

Eighteen candidates were selected for arc-melt synthesis and characterization. Nine showed superconductivity above 4.2 K, generally at temperatures below predictions, but X-ray diffraction showed that predicted structures rarely formed; samples were predominantly disordered BCC solid solutions or multiphase mixtures of known binaries.

The results indicate that generative screening can improve computational candidate discovery but that incomplete reference data and unmodeled disorder can make apparently stable structures unsuitable for synthesis. Proposed improvements include experiment-in-the-loop active learning, local DFT convex-hull refinement, disorder-aware screening, multiobjective optimization, learnable property embeddings, alternative guidance methods, discrete diffusion, and other generative backbones.

The disclosure describes a UE method and apparatus for channel state information (CSI) reporting in wireless communication systems, including 5G/NR beam operation. A UE configured with at least two CSI-RS resources measures them, generates multiple CSIs—at least one based on measurements from multiple resources—and reports at least one generated CSI. The document also discusses MIMO systems; analog, digital, and hybrid beamforming; high-frequency coverage and TRP beam considerations; and 3GPP Release 13 procedures for periodic PUCCH and aperiodic PUSCH CSI reporting, including reporting modes, timing, resource classes, subband and wideband feedback, and CQI, PMI, RI, CRI, and PTI. The application continues U.S. application Ser. No. 15/663,689 and incorporates by reference that application and Provisional Application Ser. No. 62/368,415.

Japan and China’s relations over Korea were critical, with hostilities reported imminent. Japan expanded its troop presence after Chinese forces were dispatched, blamed the rebellion on corruption and oppression, and demanded Korean reforms while denying territorial designs. The United States urged both countries to withdraw troops and considered using its good offices to protect Japanese archives and subjects in China, subject to Chinese assent. China was described as conciliatory despite Japan’s aggressive action and sought a peaceful settlement through Britain and Russia. Britain asked the United States to join a friendly intervention, but Washington declined, saying it had already acted as a friendly neutral and lacked authority to join another power. Japan maintained that its troops insured order and Korean independence and would remain until reforms and lasting stability were assured. China’s viceroy then asked the United States to lead the powers in demanding Japanese withdrawal.

Zimbabwe Yadzoka/Mayibuye iZimbabwe launched a campaign urging Zimbabweans abroad to register and vote in the 2018 election. Targeting major diaspora cities first, it plans protests against Robert Mugabe and urges citizens to expose Zanu-PF excesses and press opposition leaders to form a coalition to defeat the ruling party.

Crook County Medical Services District is beginning renovations to its emergency department and CT scanner, with the project expected to finish by September. The work will place updated imaging and x-ray equipment near the emergency department and convert an existing x-ray room into a modern trauma room. The district also purchased a wheelchair-accessible, ADA-compliant van for long-term care patients, replacing an older vehicle, and added family rooms for end-of-life care. The nursing home received a Women’s Choice Award as one of America’s Best for Extended Care and successfully met recent regulatory survey requirements.
Maikel Kieftenbeld’s red-card appeal for Birmingham City’s 2–1 win over Bristol City succeeded. He can now play against Bolton Wanderers and may start.

This study uses bibliometric analysis to examine the development, structure, themes, and collaboration networks of research combining special education with mathematics and mathematics education. English-language articles in the Web of Science database were searched through January 2024 using “special education and mathematics” and “special education and mathematics education,” with 487 articles from 1980–2023 analyzed using R and the bibliometrix package.

Publication growth increased notably in 2017, declined in 2018–2019, and accelerated again in 2020; no studies appeared in 1981–1986 or 1988–1990. The corpus comprised 120 sources, 1,093 authors, 17,813 references, 3.11 coauthors per article, 9.035% international coauthorship, and an average of 24.94 citations per article. Most publications appeared in special education journals, particularly the *Journal of Special Education* and *Remedial and Special Education*. Bouck Ec was identified as the most influential author, while Nese Jft, Shanley I, and Elliott Sn led in author collaboration.

Keyword and co-occurrence analyses identified six clusters, with “students,” “mathematics,” and “children” forming the largest and most connected cluster and serving as the most prominent terms. Students and children were also the primary participants in the reviewed studies. Country collaboration was led by the United States, followed by the United Kingdom, while the University of Florida, Purdue University, and Vanderbilt University were prominent institutional collaborators. Overall collaboration between different research groups remained limited.

The discussion associates recent research growth with inclusive education, STEM, educational reforms, new research areas, increased awareness, and pandemic-related learning loss. Recommended future work includes involving teachers and families as research participants, examining digital tools and artificial intelligence for individualized instruction, strengthening international and institutional collaboration, and incorporating disciplines such as psychology, educational technology, and linguistics. The study is limited to Web of Science data, bibliometrix and R, and publications matching its specified topics.

Rent-A-Center shares rose 3.63% in the latest session, closing at $9.99. Analysts’ 12-month average price target is $10.79, based on seven opinions, with a range of $5 to $15. The average brokerage recommendation is 2.5 from eight recommendations; three analysts rate the stock Buy, five Hold, one Underperform, and none Sell or Outperform. Its industry ranks 183rd of 265 by average brokerage recommendation. ATR-14 is 0.42, weekly volatility is 3.80%, monthly volatility is 4.72%, and RSI is 58.84. Market capitalization is $567.33 million, with 56.79 million shares outstanding. Latest trading volume was 1.01 million shares versus an average of 1.71 million.

New Brunswick's recreational marijuana stores will be named CannabisNB, run by an NB Liquor subsidiary that filed a trademark, with 20 stores planned in 15 communities. The legal age is 19; public smoking is banned, users may carry 30 grams, and home storage must be locked. Sites were selected using demographics, 2016 census income, liquor sales and traffic data.

Amazon’s two best-selling espresso machines, the Ninja Luxe Cafe Premier and Breville Barista Express, are each $100 off ahead of Prime Day’s October sale. The Ninja is at its lowest-ever price and features a 25-setting burr grinder, built-in scale, cold-brew and drip options, and excellent milk steaming. The Barista Express, Amazon’s best seller for years, combines an accessible price, built-in grinder, ease of use, and Breville’s customer-service reputation. Its discount is good, though not its lowest price, which has been $550.

SynDoc is a hybrid framework for domain-specific visually rich document understanding, combining a discriminative “warmer” with a generative MLLM for zero-shot question answering. Its synthetic data generator uses OCR or PDF parsing to extract text and layout, generates semantic and spatial question-answer pairs, and filters them through meaningfulness and answer-consistency verification. The warmer, built on a vision-language pretrained backbone, combines textual, visual, layout, and structural features and uses entity-retrieval, span-based QA, and grid-matching heads. It is tuned first for structural adaptation and then for semantic extraction on synthetic data, optionally using prior MLLM outputs as references. During recursive inference, the warmer and MLLM cross-feed retrieved entities and generated answers until predictions stabilize.

Experiments on FormNLU, CORD, EPHOIE, and FUNSD used ANLS and compared SynDoc with Idefics2, InternVL2, Qwen2-VL, GPT-4o, and Gemini. Structural adaptation and synthetic tuning substantially improved the warmer, while meaningfulness verification was consistently beneficial. Top-K retrieval hints and multiple recursive iterations generally improved MLLM performance, although additional hints could introduce noise, particularly in OCR-challenging or cross-domain settings. Overall, SynDoc improved domain-specific extraction and produced more accurate zero-shot predictions, but further work is needed for cross-domain generalization and robustness.

ISDA’s April 30, 2001 press report covers derivatives, energy, banking regulation, interest rates, federal debt and weather-linked products.

- **ISDA Master Agreements:** Smaller, non-rated derivatives customers should prioritize liquidity when negotiating an ISDA Master Agreement, especially restrictions on dealers’ termination rights. The report examines cross-default provisions, including the definition and threshold of specified indebtedness and the case for requiring cross-acceleration. It also covers credit events upon merger, additional termination events, delayed termination payments and shortened cure periods, all of which can intensify a customer’s liquidity problems.

- **Brazil’s energy crisis:** Patchy rainfall has left southeastern reservoirs at roughly one-third capacity, normally about half, while more than 90% of Brazil’s electricity comes from hydroelectric plants. Officials have ordered 10% energy cuts and anticipate rationing. Underinvestment, inflation-related fiscal constraints, slow growth in generating capacity, continued public ownership of generation and inadequate transmission have limited the benefits of liberalization and privatization. Businesses are creating their own power facilities, while Petrobras is investing in gas-fired plants. The March sinking of an offshore platform and other environmental incidents have tarnished perceptions of deregulation, although Petrobras reported record 2000 profits.

- **Merchant-banking capital proposal:** The Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency proposed capital charges of 8%, 12% or 25% on financial holding companies’ nonfinancial investments, depending on whether they represent less than 15%, 15%–25% or more than 25% of Tier I capital. Banking and securities groups argued that the charges are excessive, would create inequities between financial holding companies and other merchant banks, and should instead rely on internal capital models. They also sought broader exemptions for SBICs and pre-existing investments, less restrictive treatment of mixed-activity companies and periodic review of the rules. Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer described the proposal as a bridge toward an internal-model approach.

- **Swap spreads:** The 10-year U.S. dollar swap spread narrowed from 104 basis points on December 28 to 80 on April 30 as rate-cut expectations steepened the yield curve. Analysts expected further narrowing, while euro swap spreads, at 44 basis points, were forecast to remain sideways or temporarily widen because anticipated European rate cuts were modest. Concern about emerging markets and equities restrained dollar spreads.

- **Federal debt paydown:** In a Bond Market Association speech, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said projected budget surpluses could eliminate publicly held Treasury debt. He said debt reduction supports lower interest rates, investment, productivity and incomes, but noted that once debt reaches an irreducible minimum, additional surpluses would accumulate in government funds and risk politically driven distortions in capital allocation. He also described Treasury securities’ roles as risk-free assets, benchmarks and liquid hedging instruments, said private alternatives could replace them at some transitional cost, and outlined possible Federal Reserve adjustments. Demographic pressures are expected eventually to produce deficits and renewed Treasury issuance.

- **Enron weather note:** Enron began offering a structured note through its Internet trading platform, providing exposure to weather in 19 U.S. cities. Enron guaranteed a secondary market in the instrument and expected demand from investors seeking assets with low equity-market correlation. The product mirrored the weather-risk component of a Koch Energy Trading bond.

JAXA launched the world’s smallest orbital rocket, carrying the University of Tokyo’s three-kilogram Earth-imaging microsatellite, after a 2017 failure and several postponements amid growing private demand for small satellites.

AUSTRAC is suing Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA), alleging serious and systemic money-laundering and counter-terrorism financing breaches involving nearly 54,000 suspicious transactions and potential fines amounting to billions of dollars. CBA plans to fight the lawsuit, blaming an automated teller machine coding error for most breaches while acknowledging other allegations.

The case involves meat exporter CC&B International Pty Ltd and Jizhang Lu, a Chinese national who pleaded guilty to helping launder A$3.2 million in alleged drug proceeds and was jailed for two years. Police documents said Lu made eight trips to CC&B’s Sydney premises, received receipts for fake meat purchases, and deposited up to A$530,200 in cash per visit into CBA branches. AUSTRAC alleges CBA accepted A$17.7 million in crime proceeds from CC&B between February and August 2015.

Two CC&B employees were charged with dealing in criminal proceeds, while director Ka Chun Leung was considered a potential co-accused and has left Australia. Lu said he was recruited in Chatswood and did not understand the English receipts.
Young U.S. adults’ self-reported cognitive struggles nearly doubled since 2013; causes remain unknown.

Two schools exceeded lead limits, and both say the issue was resolved. Two daycares responded with bottled water or filters. More than 640 schools and daycares provincewide failed lead tests over two years, and stricter sampling rules are expected to increase failures. Lead exposure can impair intellectual development, especially in young children and fetuses.

The lecture shifts from cosmology to constructing the spacetime of a compact, spherically symmetric body whose exterior is vacuum. For a static spherical spacetime, the metric can be written in diagonal Schwarzschild coordinates as  
\(ds^2=-e^{2\phi}dt^2+e^{2\lambda}dr^2+r^2d\Omega^2\).  
The coordinate \(r\) is an areal radius, defined by the surface area \(4\pi r^2\) of nested spheres, but it does not generally equal proper radial distance. Isotropic coordinates are also introduced as an alternative that emphasizes equivalent spatial directions but removes the areal interpretation of \(r\).

The curvature components are calculated and the body is modeled as a static perfect fluid with pressure \(p(r)\), density \(\rho(r)\), and a normalized four-velocity. Outside the body’s surface \(r_*\), the stress-energy tensor vanishes, so the exterior equations reduce to \(R_{\mu\nu}=0\). Solving these equations gives \(\phi=-\lambda\), up to a rescaling removable through the time coordinate, and then  
\(\phi=\tfrac12\ln(1+a/r)\).  
Matching the resulting weak-field radial acceleration to Newtonian gravity requires \(a=-2GM\), yielding the Schwarzschild metric. The lecture recounts that Carl Schwarzschild derived this first exact solution while ill during military service, shortly after Einstein published the field equations.

Birkhoff’s theorem is used to show that the Schwarzschild metric also describes the exterior of any spherically symmetric body, even one whose internal source varies with time while preserving spherical symmetry. A time-dependent metric initially allowed in the exterior is shown to reduce to the static Schwarzschild form through a time-coordinate redefinition. Consequently, the exterior possesses a timelike Killing vector and a conserved-energy notion. The theorem is compared to Gauss’s law because the exterior depends on the source’s mass, not its radial distribution. Spherically symmetric pulsations do not produce gravitational waves because they cannot create a varying quadrupole moment.

For the fluid interior, the metric is rewritten using a mass function through \(e^{-2\lambda}=1-2Gm(r)/r\). The Einstein equations give  
\(m(r)=4\pi\int_0^r \rho(r')r'^2\,dr'\).  
This gravitational mass differs from the baryonic mass computed using the curved-space volume element; the difference reflects gravitational binding energy. The radial Einstein equation and conservation of fluid stress-energy supply a second differential equation, while the mass equation supplies the third. Together they form the TOV equations for relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium.

To construct a stellar model, one selects a central density and an equation of state relating pressure to density, integrates the coupled equations, and matches the interior solution to the Schwarzschild exterior at the stellar surface. The next lecture will cover solving these equations, including an illustrative special solution and numerical models for more realistic equations of state.

Yael T. Kalai began with administrative updates, including a correction to problem set 2B and a schedule for a keynote on batch arguments (BARGs) that will lead into the course’s final treatment of succinct noninteractive arguments (SNARGs).

He recapped interactive proofs, GKR, PCPs, the Kilian–Micali protocol, and Fiat–Shamir. The lecture focused on whether Fiat–Shamir remains sound when its random oracle is replaced by a concrete hash function in the standard model. Kalai noted that random-oracle security has been a strong practical proxy, but theoretical counterexamples exist.

The motivating protocol proves Hamiltonian-cycle membership in zero knowledge. It commits to the graph’s adjacency information after applying a random permutation. A challenge of zero opens the purported cycle, while a challenge of one reveals the permutation and opens only nonedges. The unrepeated protocol has only one-half soundness, but parallel repetition using fresh permutations yields security in the random-oracle model.

To prove standard-model Fiat–Shamir security, the commitment was replaced with bitwise public-key encryption under a common reference string. Semantic security provides hiding, while openings reveal the encryption randomness. A secret trapdoor allows the analysis to identify, for each first message, the unique challenge that a cheating prover could exploit.

Exposing that trapdoor in the hash function would destroy zero knowledge. Instead, the construction uses fully homomorphic encryption and a Fiat–Shamir key containing an FHE public key and an encrypted circuit. The actual key encrypts an all-zero circuit, which is evaluated homomorphically. In the soundness proof, semantic security and a circular-security assumption allow the encrypted circuit to be replaced by a special circuit that computes the bad challenge, decrypts it, and alters it so that the resulting challenge can never equal the bad challenge. An efficient successful cheating prover would therefore distinguish the two encryptions, contradicting semantic security. The presentation assumes circularly secure FHE, believed to follow from circularly secure LWE; later work removes this requirement.

This 2019 result by Canetti, Lombardi, and Wichs resolves a long-standing problem and provides a broader Fiat–Shamir technique applicable to protocols such as sum-check, with significance for noninteractive zero knowledge, SNARGs, and batch arguments. The lecture also addressed the apparent tension between zero knowledge and Fiat–Shamir and noted that parallel repetition need not preserve zero knowledge.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K output at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2 compression, USB-C 8K output, native HDR processing, and BT.2100 tone mapping. Enhanced NVENC supports H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps and provides bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8-, 10-, and 12-bit decoding and VP9 10- and 12-bit HDR support.

Turing supports USB-C and VirtualLink, an open standard for powering and connecting VR headsets through one connector while carrying display, power, data, and motion-tracking information. For SLI, TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink instead of MIO and PCIe interfaces. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 one, each providing 25 GB/s per direction; only two-way SLI is supported.

Real-time ray tracing is enabled by RT Cores in each streaming multiprocessor, working with NVIDIA RTX software, BVH acceleration structures, denoising, and APIs including Microsoft DXR and OptiX. RT Cores handle BVH traversal, bounding-box tests, and ray-triangle intersections, freeing shader cores for other work. Turing combines ray tracing with rasterization through a hybrid rendering model and is described as delivering more than 10 billion rays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance.

NGX applies deep neural networks through Turing Tensor Cores. DLSS produces quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X uses a larger network to approach 64-times supersampled quality from target-resolution input. Other NGX features include AI-based inpainting, frame interpolation for slow motion, and 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video super-resolution.

Turing also adds task and mesh shaders for processing large object lists efficiently; variable-rate shading with fine-grained, per-16-by-16-pixel control; texture-space shading that decouples and reuses visibility and appearance samples; and multi-view rendering with up to four hardware views per pass and 32 API-level views. Variable-rate shading supports content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Turing also supports bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and more flexible resource heaps.

TU104 contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, while TU106 contains 36 multiprocessors, 2,304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores; TU106 does not support NVLink or SLI. The Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 40 multiprocessors, 2,560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

For hybrid workloads, RTX-OPS weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 peak operations by their modeled utilization. The document also explains ray tracing, BVH building and refitting, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, along with VR-focused improvements and associated legal and trademark notices.

Nova Scotia is seeking public feedback on a minimum marijuana-use age of 19, sales through a Crown corporation, permitted use locations, and drug-impaired driving. Its online survey runs until Oct. 27 ahead of planned legalization next summer. The province aims to protect health and safety, encourage responsible use, and minimize organized crime. Other provinces are considering different ages and retail models, while Ottawa maintains the planned July 1 start date despite concerns about regulatory complexity.

This medRxiv preprint reports a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial of intranasal SA58, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody, in healthy adult workers at 21 Beijing construction sites with an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. Participants had contacted an infected person within 72 hours and were randomized 3:1 to SA58 or placebo. Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 entered the full analysis set; 99 baseline RT-PCR-positive participants were excluded from efficacy analysis.

SA58 was self-administered as a 1 mg nasal dose five or six times daily. Among baseline-negative participants, laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 occurred in 7 of 824 SA58 recipients and 14 of 299 placebo recipients, yielding estimated protective efficacy of 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%). SA58 also reduced RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). All sequenced infections were Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred during monitoring.

Adverse events were reported by 25% of SA58 recipients and 22% of placebo recipients, with no significant difference between groups. All events were grade one; no serious adverse events, adverse events of special interest, withdrawals, or deaths were reported. Common events included nasal dryness, runny nose, fever, nasal congestion, headache, cough, and throat dryness.

The study ended early below its target sample size after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted. Its limitations included short follow-up, a small sample, concurrent infection-control measures, and restriction to generally healthy workers, limiting generalizability. The authors concluded that SA58 showed promising efficacy and safety as post-exposure prophylaxis and should be evaluated further in high-risk populations.

A goalie in the Stanley Cup Finals appreciates the opportunity and urges the team to try to win the Cup, while disputing the media's portrayal of the team as unorthodox. He credits goalie coaches who taught new techniques without trying to change his game, for his growth. A year earlier, freshly out of hip surgery, he focused on recovering and never imagined being in the Finals. As success came, he wondered whether the team had what it takes to win the Cup, though you never know until you get there. The team finished as the East's third seed after finding many ways to win, serving them well in the playoffs.

Cho’s Technology Research reiterated Netflix as a long-term buy-and-hold while lowering its stance from High Conviction Buy and raising its price target from $144.46 to $160.73, citing diminished upside and heightened expectation risk. The key data point is whether Netflix guides to at least 52 million international subscribers in Q2 2017, with estimates and valuation hinging more on subscriber growth than margins. The firm raised its revenue estimate from $10.9 billion to $11.285 billion, compared with consensus of $11.23 billion, and increased diluted EPS estimate from $0.97 to $1.16. Contribution margins are expected to improve along historical trends, making profitability easier to improve than revenue targets. Limited remaining subscription growth levers and potential competition from Apple’s media efforts warrant caution, but the investment thesis remains intact.

An April 16, 2001 email compiles reports on bandwidth trading and the U.S. electricity market.

- **Bandwidth contracts:** After nine months and four missed deadlines, carriers and trading companies continued developing standardized bandwidth contracts. Enron and Williams publicly attached their names to agreements, while other participants remained anonymous. A third agreement allowed parties to opt out of otherwise firm commitments. Traders favored firm contracts for market efficiency, while carriers preferred best-efforts terms; confidential, individually negotiated contracts also existed. Carriers’ concerns about competing with their own trading desks and relations with other market participants slowed standardization.

- **Sierra Pacific:** Shares fell 8.3% to $13.29 after Sierra Pacific Resources canceled its May dividend to conserve cash amid soaring power costs. The utility had lost hundreds of millions buying electricity it could not pass to customers, despite a 17% Nevada rate increase. Its planned $2 billion purchase of Enron’s Portland General Electric unit, including $1 billion in debt, was delayed by California restrictions on utility asset sales. Its Mohave coal-plant stake sale to AES was also affected. Southern California Edison separately agreed to sell transmission lines to California for $2.76 billion amid major losses and bankruptcy concerns.

- **California power trading:** Houston-based Enron, Reliant, Dynegy and Duke operated influential wholesale power markets amid deregulation, supply shortages and high natural-gas costs. California utility bills had risen nearly fourfold to $27.1 billion and were projected to reach $70 billion; PG&E had filed for bankruptcy, Southern California Edison was near insolvency, and the state was spending about $50 million daily on electricity. Wholesalers blamed gas prices and state policy, while lawsuits and investigations alleged withholding, price-fixing and other market abuses. A state grid report said 98% of trading bids showed noncompetitive behavior and that wholesalers received as much as $6.9 billion in unjust rates, although attorneys had not produced concrete evidence of price fixing. Energy trading remained exempt from routine CFTC oversight, though FERC planned increased monitoring. Enron denied benefiting from California prices and reported sharply higher profits from energy trading.

- **Independent producers:** Higher energy prices, trading volumes and natural-gas prices led Williams, Calpine, Dynegy, Mirant, Enron and Reliant to expect strong or on-target first-quarter results. California utilities’ inability to pay generators created receivable risks, though most companies had cash reserves. FERC ordered 13 producers to justify California charges or issue refunds, including $45.8 million for Dynegy and $29.6 million for Williams. Potential price caps and state seizure of low-cost contracts remained future risks.

- **Seattle City Light:** The utility spent a record $92 million on purchased power in March, compared with $90 million for all of 1999. Drought-related low reservoir levels increased its need for market purchases, which accounted for about 15% of its power but more than 90% of its costs. Enron supplied $25.5 million, while Puget Sound Energy and Avista Energy charged higher average prices than Enron. City Light increased rates 28% and conserved water for future generation. New hydroelectric and gas-fired contracts expected by October were intended to reduce reliance on the open market, although BPA rates could rise sharply.

Cisco announced two webcast financial conferences for February 2017: the Goldman Sachs Technology and Internet Conference, featuring CEO Chuck Robbins, and the Morgan Stanley Technology, Media & Telecom Investor Conference, featuring David Goeckeler.

Police are investigating unconnected gangs that stole tens of thousands of pounds in jewellery in 28 recent offences. One group threatened a newborn and held knives to women; another used screwdrivers. British police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury, Wiltshire, following possible exposure to an unknown substance. Both remain hospitalized in critical condition. Tests are underway after initial suspicion of contaminated drugs, and counterterrorism officers are assisting. Officials said there is no believed significant risk to the public.

Autoliv plans to spin off and separately list its electronics business, which develops radars, vision systems and driver-assistance software, in the third quarter of 2018. The unit will receive a cash injection to preserve Autoliv’s investment-grade rating, while the passive-safety business, including airbags and seatbelts, will retain the Autoliv name. Autoliv expects the separation to create value by addressing two distinct markets; its shares have risen 20% since the plan was announced.

Tuberculosis remained the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent globally despite being curable and preventable. In 2019, an estimated 10 million people developed TB and 1.5 million died. Zambia had a high TB burden, and most TB patients were managed at primary-care facilities, while complicated cases were referred to secondary and tertiary hospitals, where most TB deaths occurred.

A retrospective audit analyzed 74 TB-attributed mortality files from Kitwe Teaching Hospital in Zambia between June 2018 and June 2019. Data collected included demographics, symptoms, HIV status, hospital stay, diagnoses, comorbidities, vital signs, laboratory results, and radiological findings. SPSS and Excel were used for analysis.

Most deaths occurred among males (67.6%), and the mean age was 39.2 years. HIV positivity was reported in 81.1%, while 83.8% of patients came from high-density residential areas. Common symptoms included cough (41.9%), fever (40.5%), diarrhea (29.7%), productive cough (27.0%), headache (21.6%), and shortness of breath (16.2%). Before death, patients had lower mean arterial pressure and respiratory rates but remained tachycardic. Laboratory findings included anemia in 39.2%, hypoalbuminemia, renal dysfunction, and elevated liver enzymes. Chest radiographs showed miliary patterns, consolidation, cavities, and opacities.

The authors concluded that TB deaths at the hospital were associated with male sex, age under 50, HIV positivity, high-density residence, and unstable hemodynamics. They recommended early recognition of clinical instability, particularly among young and middle-aged HIV-positive men, and a prospective study to identify mortality predictors and assess whether malignancy contributed to deaths among patients with TB/HIV coinfection. The retrospective review was limited by incomplete or missing records and failure to investigate malignancy.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 27, 2015, reporting financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 26, 2015. The filing attached a press release and related data sheet as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and stated that the information was not deemed filed or incorporated by reference except when expressly referenced. Taj Haider said Bilawal Bhutto Zardari would begin campaigning in Punjab next week, starting in South Punjab. He urged authorities to ensure fair polls, saying PPP supported democracy despite past rigging.

A European Commission Joint Research Centre study found that the Amazon’s 2024 fire season caused its worst forest disturbance in more than two decades. Fires released an estimated 791 million tons of carbon dioxide—roughly Germany’s annual emissions and seven times the 2022–2023 average—and affected 3.3 million hectares. For the first time in the study period, fire-driven degradation surpassed deforestation as the main source of emissions, driven by drought, climate change, forest fragmentation, and land-use mismanagement. Brazil recorded its highest degradation emissions, while fires affected over 9% of Bolivia’s remaining intact forest. Satellite analysis and Monte Carlo simulations identified degradation that can retain forest cover while substantially reducing biomass and ecological function. Researchers called for coordinated fire reduction, stronger forest protections, support for local and Indigenous stewardship, and climate finance addressing degradation as well as deforestation.

Under an expanded strategic agreement, Dell Technologies will extend Salesforce’s cloud-based CRM and sales and marketing tools to nearly 40,000 global sales employees and give worldwide contact centers access to the Service Cloud Einstein AI platform. Dell and Salesforce will also use Dell Boomi to share large volumes of data through the cloud, supporting Dell’s salesforce and roughly 200,000 channel partners. Service Cloud Einstein provides customer-service analytics, machine learning, and a mobile app for field service employees.
Drawings depict a portable fan; broken lines mark portions outside the claimed design.

The application describes a feedback-controlled nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF) system for therapeutic tumor treatment. NsPEF pulses can induce apoptosis in cancerous cells while substantially sparing surrounding normal tissue and may stimulate an immune response; immune biomarkers can be monitored, and treatment may be paired with a CD47-blocking antibody. The system uses a controller, power supply, pulse generator, electrodes, and sensors to generate high-voltage, controllable pulses and adjust characteristics such as amplitude, polarity, width, rise or fall time, frequency, pulse count, and duty cycle based on measured current, voltage, temperature, tissue, or system parameters. Control methods include PID, lookup tables, and fixed-step adjustments.

The pulse generator uses a low-impedance Marx-switch-stack hybrid with power MOSFETs, parallel panels to increase current, and serial units to increase voltage. Transformer-based switch drivers, snubber circuits, and overcurrent protection support rapid switching and pulse-duration control. Seven-needle and two-pole suction electrodes apply nsPEF pulses to tumors. Flowchart methods describe measuring pulse amplitude, width, charge, energy, average power, and tissue temperature, then modifying power-supply or pulse-generator controls to approach desired values or reduce delivered power when specified limits are exceeded.

The patent application describes an orthopedic surgical system and methods for preoperative planning, implant and guide design, intraoperative guidance and tracking, postoperative monitoring, and medical education. Mixed reality, virtual reality, and extended reality visualization systems display patient anatomy, three-dimensional bone and implant models, cutting and drilling guidance, tool information, checklists, and virtual surgical plans. Preoperative workflows include imaging, pathology classification, automated and manual plan development, plan review, and patient-specific surgical item selection. Intraoperative systems can register virtual models with patient anatomy, track instruments, guide bone preparation and implant placement, and modify plans. Additional embodiments cover range-of-motion simulation, depth tracking, tool identification, deep neural network analysis of shoulder conditions and recommended procedures, remote and collaborative education, and MR-guided shoulder and ankle arthroplasty.
NASA’s TESS launched aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral on April 18 to search for nearby exoplanets, identifying candidates for follow-up by the James Webb Space Telescope.

Canada's main stock index, the S&P/TSX composite, hit a record high Wednesday morning, gaining 97.66 points to 16,414.19 after 90 minutes of trading, just below its intraday high of 16,424.82, above the prior record of 16,421.42. Energy, financial, technology and health care sectors — the latter including major Canadian marijuana companies — all rose, helped by Tuesday's Senate passage of the government's cannabis bill legalizing recreational marijuana later this year. In New York, the Dow fell 60.80 points to 24,639.41 while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained. The loonie weakened to 75.22 cents US amid rising U.S. interest rates and NAFTA trade fears. August crude rose 71 cents to US$65.61 a barrel, July natural gas rose six cents to US$2.96, while gold fell $2.30 to US$1,276.30 an ounce and copper fell two cents to US$3.03 a pound.

The passage references L4 Fast and Slow Peripheral memory maps and configuration resources. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range through a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views, accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS; other masters can access one view through the base map’s 512-MB TILER region. Package pin maps and terminal-function tables cover signal names, multiplexing, ball numbers, pin types, internal pulls, supply voltage, and pin functions. Boot-configuration pins are multiplexed with Cortex-A8 boot inputs sampled through BTMODE at reset, then operate as GPMC data/address pins; BTMODE[11] also controls RSTOUT_WD_OUT reset behavior.

The team fell behind early and struggled defensively in the first period, but improved and had chances to tie the game. Uzbekistan’s sum gained about 9% on the black market over seven days amid expectations of full exchange-rate liberalization. After easing exporter sales rules, authorities may permit full convertibility and align official and market rates; meanwhile, individuals face rates well above the official 4,100 sums per dollar.

The article presents eight Vanguard retirement funds: Target Retirement 2060, 2050, 2040, and Income, plus LifeStrategy Growth, Moderate Growth, Conservative Growth, and Income. Passive investing has gained popularity since the 2008/09 financial crisis because it requires less time and effort, can reduce cognitive mistakes, and offers satisfactory retirement returns. The Back Cut offense exploits the corners and middle of a Diamond & One defense, creating open looks, layups, putbacks, and opportunities to free the star with baseline screens. Rotations progress through back cuts, weak-side screening, corner cuts, dribble penetration, base screens, and a fake cross that counters defenders cheating over screens.

Success requires coordinated execution of double screens, base screens, and strong post-ups, supported by defensive recognition, nonverbal communication, timing, and experience. Diamond & One uses four defenders in zone and a fifth in pass denial against the opponent’s scoring ace. It is best suited to odd or one-guard-front offenses.

The address presents the speaker’s acceptance of the nation’s highest office as a sacred public trust requiring humility, divine guidance, and citizen cooperation. It credits post–Great War recovery with greater national strength, prosperity, freedom, institutional confidence, and international influence, while warning that self-government remains threatened by crime and the failure of justice.

The criminal justice system is identified as a major danger. Rising crime and declining confidence in swift justice are attributed not only to the Eighteenth Amendment but also to longstanding procedural complexity and weak enforcement. Proposed reforms include reorganizing federal justice functions, simplifying procedures, improving juries and investigative and prosecutorial agencies, transferring enforcement activities to the Department of Justice, and creating a national commission to study the federal justice system. Enforcement of the Eighteenth Amendment requires action by federal, state, and local officials and citizen support; patronage of illegal liquor supplies rewards for crime. Citizens who oppose a law are urged to discourage its violation and seek its repeal rather than selectively disregard it.

The administration favors regulating private enterprise rather than government ownership or operation. Laws should enforce competition in ordinary industries and regulate the services and rates of public utilities. Federal regulation should remain within constitutional limits and apply chiefly where states cannot protect citizens, though federal authority should be exercised firmly when it exists. Government should cooperate with civic, state, municipal, and private organizations to promote stable employment, public welfare, health, recreation, education, and stronger homes.

Although education is primarily a state and local responsibility, the nation must advance universal, increasingly advanced education to ensure an informed electorate and draw leadership from all citizens. Public health should likewise be organized universally, because disease control can yield major economic and social benefits.

American progress is presented as inseparable from global peace and prosperity. The United States rejects territorial or economic domination and imperialism, supports limiting armaments and peaceful dispute settlement, and favors the Permanent Court of International Justice, while declining League of Nations membership that could commit the country to foreign disputes. It supports the independence, stability, and prosperity of Western Hemisphere republics. Permanent peace requires self-restraint, friendliness, helpfulness, and respect for the capacity for defense.

Political parties are presented as necessary instruments for expressing the popular will and ensuring governmental accountability. Government must faithfully execute the platform entrusted to it, while election animosities and partisan interests should not displace concern for the common good.

The speaker requests a special congressional session to address agricultural relief and limited tariff changes. Other election mandates include constitutional integrity, vigorous law enforcement, economical government, regulated business without government competition, avoidance of foreign entanglements, departmental reorganization, expanded public works, and education and home-welfare programs. These policies are grounded in self-government, ordered liberty, equality of opportunity, individual initiative, public integrity, religious tolerance, knowledge, and peace. The address closes with confidence in the country’s future and a request for citizens’ tolerance, assistance, and cooperation.

It cited new U.S.–EU tariffs of up to 15% on European imports, risks to Italian exporters and reduced competitiveness from a strong euro. From the PNP Custodial Center, where she is detained on drug charges, Senator Leila de Lima rejected defeated candidate Francis Tolentino’s 2016 election-fraud protest. Occupants escaped by jumping from the elevated first floor and were rescued by kayak. Investigators have found no evidence of arson or a prefire explosion; a reported explosion may have resulted from fire spreading to nearby vehicles. Goodstein recently blocked state election officials from sharing voter-registration data with the federal government, but the South Carolina Supreme Court reversed her order.

Care Compliance Expert aims to improve elderly care through dementia-care expertise, professional advice on care-home health and safety, and input on regulatory changes. It states that higher standards can improve residents’ treatment, mood, quality of life, and safety.

France's 4-3 win over Argentina was powered by 19-year-old Kylian Mbappé, who scored twice and a penalty, his €180m PSG transfer now looking a bargain. Scientists have documented the first modern case of "river piracy," blaming global warming. On May 26 last year, meltwater from the Kaskawulsh glacier in northwest Canada abruptly shifted from the Slims River to the Alsek River, redirecting drainage from the Arctic's Bering Sea toward the Pacific as a 30-metre canyon formed at the glacier's end. Dan Shugar and Jim Best published their findings in Nature Geoscience, noting the shift took about a day, unlike river piracy that unfolds over tens of thousands of years. The researchers ruled out rainfall changes and estimated only a one-in-200 chance that the retreat and rerouting are entirely natural without human-caused warming, using observations and computer simulation. The glacier covers about 25,000 square kilometres and has retreated nearly 1.9 million kilometres since 1899. Glacial expert Richard Alley praised the study as significant and sensible.

SpaceX plans to launch a reused Falcon 9 rocket carrying a previously flown Dragon capsule with nearly 5,000 pounds of supplies and experiments to the International Space Station. NASA says the recycled rocket’s launch risk is comparable to that of a new vehicle, though not zero. The booster will attempt to return to Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, whose launch pad was rebuilt after a 2016 explosion. SpaceX aims to reduce costs through repeated rocket reuse and expand human spaceflight.

Lexington County officials are searching for a woman accused of making over 60 baseless 911 calls between March 25 and April 14, mostly from Saint Andrews. They released a call for voice recognition and said false emergencies delay responses and endanger deputies and motorists.

Fort Bend ISD crews worked around the clock after high temperatures caused air-conditioning problems at Quail Valley Elementary and Marshall High School. Quail Valley’s system was repaired overnight, while Marshall students endured hot classrooms and hallways cooled by fans until its AC was fixed. The half-day and final days of school left most students accepting the discomfort.

Prakash Karat said Tripura’s February 18 assembly election would indicate India’s political direction and pitted the BJP against the Left Front after Congress leaders and supporters joined the BJP. At a Belonia rally, he alleged the BJP-IPFT alliance linked IPFT to former insurgents and sought to block the Left Front’s return, but predicted an eighth government under Manik Sarkar.

A first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study evaluated oral AT-752, a pan-serotype dengue virus polymerase inhibitor prodrug, in 65 healthy adults. Single ascending doses ranged from 250 to 1,500 mg, while multiple regimens included 1,000 mg once daily, 750 mg twice daily, and 750 mg three daily; food and ethnic effects were also assessed. AT-752 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or adverse-event-related discontinuations. Treatment-emergent events were generally mild or moderate and resolved by study end, without treatment-related trends in laboratory, vital-sign, or ECG findings.

After single dosing, AT-281 was rapidly eliminated with a half-life of approximately 0.5 hours, whereas AT-273, a surrogate for active intracellular AT-9010, had a half-life of 15–25 hours. Exposure increased across the 250–1,500 mg range. Food delayed and reduced peak concentrations but had limited effect on total exposure, allowing administration with or without food. Pharmacokinetics were similar in Asian and mostly Caucasian cohorts. During multiple dosing, AT-273 accumulated and steady state was essentially reached by Day 3; 750 mg three times daily produced and maintained levels above the in-vitro DENV inhibition EC90 of 0.64 µM. The findings support further clinical evaluation of AT-752.

The passage defines night trading as holding positions from the market close until the next open, distinguishing it from after-hours trading. It claims that since SPY’s 1993 inception, all S&P 500 gains came from overnight holdings, while buying at the open and selling at the close produced no gains. Average overnight returns were reported as 0.04% for the S&P 500 and 0.03% for gold, with a stronger long-term edge in gold miners, whose open-to-close returns averaged -0.09%. Inflation and earnings growth are suggested as possible reasons for the overnight bias.

Because these edges are small, the passage says strategies must overcome slippage, commissions, and overnight risk. It cites a 2014 strategy that remained profitable over seven years of out-of-sample data and three close-to-close strategies whose combined backtest recorded 950 trades averaging 0.33%, enough to offset trading costs. Overall, overnight strategies are presented as potentially profitable with reasonable risk, though not as a simple route to wealth.

Two clinical trials found that daily oral GLP-1 drugs can help people with obesity lose weight. Oral semaglutide at 25 mg produced an average weight loss of nearly 14% among more than 300 participants over up to 64 weeks. Eli Lilly’s oral small-molecule drug orforglipron produced average losses of about 11% at its highest dose among more than 3,000 participants over up to 72 weeks.

Both pills require no refrigeration or injector and may be cheaper and easier to manufacture than injectable GLP-1 medications, potentially improving access. Researchers observed typical gastrointestinal side effects, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, but no liver toxicity. Longer-term studies are needed to establish safety and benefits, and cost and insurance coverage remain unknown. Researchers hope both drugs could reach consumers by 2026, pending FDA approval.

The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, tsunami, and Fukushima nuclear crisis devastated Japan, killing or injuring more than 25,000 people, damaging 125,000 buildings, and causing estimated economic losses of ¥16.9 trillion. About 80% of Japanese automotive plants suspended production, while industry output fell nearly 60% in March and April. The disruption affected global automakers because overseas plants depended on components sourced from Japan.

Nissan, Toyota, and Honda all suffered damage and supply-chain constraints. Nissan had six damaged production facilities and roughly 50 impaired suppliers. Its response reflected a decentralized, flexible supply chain, a crisis-oriented culture shaped by its 1999 rescue by Renault, and extensive preparedness. These included seismic reinforcement, business-continuity planning, disaster simulations, designated risk owners, and an earthquake response plan emphasizing human safety, prevention of secondary disasters, rapid recovery, and community support.

After the earthquake, Nissan’s Global Disaster Control Headquarters convened within 15 minutes, and a Recovery Committee coordinated global supply-chain restoration. Its main practices were sharing information across regions, allocating constrained components according to priorities such as margins, managing production around anticipated bottlenecks, and delegating authority for rapid decisions. Nissan also developed alternative supplies, used air freight, adjusted production schedules and vacations, and sent regional representatives to Japan to support recovery.

Following the disaster, Nissan announced plans to raise localized production in the Americas from about 70% to 90% by 2015, halve Japanese components shipped to North America by fiscal 2013, extend continuity planning to critical lower-tier suppliers, and improve understanding of supply-chain dependencies. The case concludes that more comprehensive business-continuity planning, robust suppliers, and stronger risk management remained necessary.

Los Angeles subway expansion crews are routinely uncovering Ice Age fossils, prompting paleontologist Ashley Leger and other monitors to carefully excavate sites when large bones appear. Since work on the Purple Line extension began in 2014, remains have included a rabbit jaw, mastodon tooth, camel foreleg, bison vertebrae, and horse tooth and ankle bone. The most notable find was an intact skull with both tusks of an 8- to 12-year-old juvenile Columbian mammoth, excavated over 15 hours. Named Hayden, the several-hundred-pound skull was taken to La Brea Tar Pits and Museum, where it is being studied and publicly displayed in the Fossil Lab.

California’s environmental rules require scientists at certain construction sites; paleontologists have monitored all L.A. subway excavation since the inaugural line began in the 1990s. Similar urban projects have yielded mammoth and whale fossils and ancient seashells in San Diego, while a Boston development exposed a possibly 18th-century wooden boat. Museum officials praised safeguards integrating science with construction but noted that treasures may have been lost before protections took effect in the early 1970s.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on January 29, 2020, announcing its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2019. The update was posted on its website and attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Cuba’s provisional government will end after peaceful, orderly elections and inauguration. The United States urges Cubans to preserve justice, order, and independence but warns that continued independence is impossible if elections become a farce or insurrection persists, in which case U.S. intervention would again be required. The Third International Conference of American Republics, held in Rio de Janeiro from July 23 to August 29, reached substantial agreement on expanding trade, improving communications, and removing barriers to intercourse among American nations. Its harmonious, efficient sessions demonstrated improved cooperation. The U.S. Secretary of State, the conference’s honorary president, toured several South American countries with a message of peace, friendship, and mutual helpfulness, receiving warm welcomes.

March 7–8, 2001 reports detailed California’s electricity crisis and responses to shortages, high wholesale prices, and the near-bankruptcy of Pacific Gas & Electric and Southern California Edison. The utilities had accumulated roughly $13 billion in debts, prompting the state Department of Water Resources to buy power on their behalf. Gov. Gray Davis announced about 40 long-term contracts and tentative accords worth approximately $40 billion to supply nine million homes over a decade, averaging $69 per megawatt-hour. Confidentiality provisions and above-market prices drew criticism from consumer advocates.

Davis also pursued the purchase of utility transmission grids. The state offered PG&E at least $7 billion, potentially more, while PG&E reportedly sought as much as $10 billion. Under the proposed structure, the state would upgrade and lease back the lines; utilities would halt legal efforts to raise customer bills, sell generated power for a decade, and receive parent-company support for debt. Similar negotiations were underway with Edison and San Diego Gas & Electric.

The state faced difficulty financing purchases through $10 billion in revenue bonds because utility revenues under existing rate structures were insufficient and legislative debt limits restricted borrowing. Thermoelectric performance depends on balancing power factor and thermal conductivity, while strong electron–phonon coupling makes this difficult. Although Bi2Te3-based materials perform well near room temperature, n-type Bi2Te3–Se alloys lag behind p-type counterparts because of strong crystallographic anisotropy and intrinsic point defects. Existing doping, microstructure, and texture methods can degrade electrical transport or present processing and scalability challenges.

This study demonstrates a simple annealing strategy for n-type Bi2Te3–Se polycrystals produced by melting–hot pressing. The optimal composition was Bi2Te2.6Se0.4, with Se substitution increasing the absolute Seebeck coefficient and reducing lattice thermal conductivity; before annealing, it reached a peak ZT of 0.67 at 373 K. Annealing at 723 K caused Te(Se) volatilization and formed cation vacancies and other point defects. These defects reduced carrier density and electronic thermal conductivity while increasing carrier mobility, improving the power factor, and strengthening phonon scattering to lower lattice thermal conductivity. After 100 h, the sample had a room-temperature mobility of 295.97 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and lattice thermal conductivity of 0.48 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. It achieved a room-temperature ZT of 0.78, a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K, and an average ZT of 0.99 over 300–423 K. Annealing improved both hot-pressed and spark-plasma-sintered samples, with the optimized material showing quality factors and ZT values among the highest reported for n-type Bi2(Te,Se)3 alloys.

The Supreme Court allowed Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to remain on the Fed’s Board of Governors while it considers whether President Donald Trump had legal cause to remove her. The court deferred Trump’s request to stay an injunction until oral arguments in January 2026; the argument date has not been set.

Trump alleges Cook committed mortgage fraud based on statements in applications for two Michigan and Georgia homes. Cook denies wrongdoing and has not been charged. Trump’s first effort to remove her came after he unsuccessfully pressed her and other Fed officials to lower interest rates.

The ruling lets the Fed continue operating through year-end. Cook is expected to vote at the October and December FOMC meetings and possibly in January. The Fed cut its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage point in September, with further similar cuts expected. Cook voted for that cut, while Governor Stephen Miran dissented in favor of a 0.5-point reduction.

The case could become a landmark test of the Fed’s political independence. Cook’s lawyers welcomed the ruling, while the White House maintains that Trump lawfully removed her for cause and expects to prevail in January.

This protocol describes a systematic review of structural interventions for HIV evidence-based interventions in the United States. The review addresses persistent HIV disparities linked to social and structural determinants of health, unequal access to and uptake of PrEP and antiretroviral therapy, and barriers such as housing instability, limited transportation, stigma, and structural racism. It aims to identify implementation determinants, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions relevant to the adoption, feasibility, reach, effectiveness, sustainability, cost, and equitable delivery of structural HIV interventions; assess literature gaps; and distinguish these intervention categories.

A May–July 2024 search covered MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Sociological Abstracts, Google, ProQuest, and CDC structural-intervention sources, yielding 8,098 records. Natural-language processing classified 8,092 titles and abstracts across five domains, with 405 labeled for inclusion across all domains and 4,285 requiring further inspection. Investigators will conduct duplicate title/abstract and full-text reviews in COVIDENCE, resolve disagreements by consensus, and extract data on populations, settings, study designs, implementation outcomes, and intervention types.

Determinants will be coded in MaxQDA by valence, level, intervention type, and CFIR 2.0 domains. Implementation strategies will be mapped to ERIC, while adjunctive interventions will be mapped to TDF and COM-B. Analyses will combine tabulation, stratification, and NLP-generated thematic descriptions. The initial search and automated screening are complete, title/abstract review is underway, and extraction, analysis, publication, conference presentations, and dashboard dissemination are planned through 2026. The findings are intended to clarify implementation gaps and inform scaling of structural interventions under the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative.

The study develops a classification, mathematical model, and evaluation methods for the ISO 25023 “Accessibility” subcharacteristic, focusing on users with visual impairments. It addresses the lack of standard methodologies for determining key accessibility parameters and weighting coefficients.

The model divides accessibility into four weighted subproperties: perceptiveness, operability, understandability, and localization. Perceptiveness covers alternative text, color contrast, and subtitles or audio descriptions. Operability covers keyboard and structured navigation. Understandability covers clear instructions, input assistance, and correct input support. Localization measures language availability, with weights tailored to a Ukrainian context: Ukrainian 0.6, English 0.2, German and French 0.08 each, and other languages 0.04. Individual metrics and subproperties are combined through weighted formulas to produce accessibility and supported-language adequacy scores.

The methodology was applied to the Vasyl Stefanyk Precarpathian National University website, with automated tools used to check image alternative text and color contrast. The overall accessibility score was approximately 0.68, classified as “excellent.” Weak areas included subtitles or audio descriptions and input assistance, both scoring zero; alternative text scored 0.15, and structured navigation scored 0.47. Color contrast scored 0.99, while keyboard navigation and clear instructions each scored 1.

The study concludes that the expanded model provides a more detailed and objective assessment of web accessibility, identifies areas needing improvement, and supports practical evaluation of digital products against ISO 25023 and WCAG requirements.

The Supreme Court granted review of five cases for its 2025–26 term, including a challenge to Hawaii’s restrictions on concealed handguns on private property and in “sensitive places.” The challengers dispute the Second Amendment’s application and argue that the appeals court improperly relied on post-Reconstruction laws rather than the nation’s founding-era tradition.

The Court will also decide whether Exxon Mobil and Havana Docks can pursue claims under the Cuban Liberty and Democratic Solidarity Act for property confiscated by the Cuban government. This cross-sectional study examined relationships among self- and other-oriented mentalization, attachment insecurity, and personality pathology under the DSM-5 Alternative Model of Personality Disorders (AMPD). The sample included 109 adults—60 psychiatric inpatients and 49 community participants—of whom 54% met criteria for a personality disorder. Self-mentalizing was assessed with the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire, while other-mentalizing facets were measured with the Movie for the Assessment of Social Cognition. Criterion A functioning, Criterion B traits, attachment anxiety, and attachment avoidance were also assessed.

Self-mentalizing deficits were the strongest and broadest predictor, positively relating to both self- and interpersonal functioning difficulties and all five maladaptive trait domains. Correct other-mentalizing uniquely predicted fewer interpersonal functioning difficulties, while hypermentalizing, undermentalizing, and nonmentalizing generally had few independent predictive effects. The models explained 18%–55% of outcome variance.

Attachment anxiety predicted most personality functioning and trait outcomes, whereas avoidance primarily predicted detachment. Correct other-mentalizing weakened the relationship between attachment anxiety and interpersonal impairment, while other-hypermentalizing strengthened it. Self-mentalizing moderated relationships between attachment anxiety and both negative affectivity and detachment. For attachment avoidance and detachment, correct other-mentalizing was protective, whereas undermentalizing and nonmentalizing strengthened the association.

The findings suggest that self-mentalizing may have a foundational role across personality pathology, while other-mentalizing is more specifically relevant to interpersonal difficulties and detachment. The authors recommend prioritizing self-mentalization in treatment while tailoring other-mentalization work to attachment-related interpersonal patterns. Limitations include the small, heterogeneous sample, cross-sectional design, differing assessment methods, unassessed comorbid disorders, and lack of longitudinal, healthy-control, or person-centered analyses.

Remaining public lands should be reserved for actual settlers and home builders, and laws enabling large-scale acquisition and unlawful fencing of public domain should be corrected. Alaska needs liberal land and homestead laws to encourage permanent settlement, protection of forests and game, regulated timber use by settlers, and preservation of salmon fisheries under the Commission of Fish and Fisheries. Policies toward Indians should support gradual integration into broader society without forcing rapid assimilation.
