The paper reports thermal characterization of aluminum and titanium-nitride kinetic inductance detectors in the 280 GHz module of Mod-Cam, a testbed for the Prime-Cam receiver on the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope. Cold-load and optically open configurations were used to assess intrinsic thermal stability and near-field-ready cryogenic performance. Thermal-interface upgrades reduced the 40 K stage’s temperature drift from 0.2 K/day to below 0.1 K/day.

During an eight-hour, 10 Hz measurement at a servo-controlled 100 mK setpoint, the detector stage exhibited an RMS temperature fluctuation of \(3.2\times10^{-5}\) K. Measurements of 2,409 aluminum and 1,886 titanium-nitride detectors gave median thermal responsivities of \(1.995\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}\) and \(-6.081\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}\), respectively.

These values were converted into thermally induced equivalent optical-power noise. At a 5 pW optical load, the values were 0.20 fW for aluminum and 0.11 fW for titanium nitride, corresponding to 0.0040% and 0.0023% of the incident power. At 9 pW, the corresponding values were 0.27 and 0.13 fW. The results indicate that cryogenic thermal fluctuations make a negligible contribution to the detector noise budget and validate Mod-Cam’s thermal design and control system. Future work will directly measure optical responsivity under loading from a cryogenic blackbody source.

The Missouri Supreme Court will consider two cases asking whether the Missouri Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, which are not expressly listed in the statute.

In *R.M.A. v. Blue Springs R-IV School District*, a transgender teen whose birth certificate lists him as male sued after the district denied his request to use boys’ restrooms and locker facilities. R.M.A’s attorneys argued that gender identity is a gender-related trait protected by the Act. The district argued that gender identity is not covered and that a school district is not a “person” subject to the Act. A trial judge dismissed the case, and an appeals court affirmed.

In *Lampley and Frost v. Missouri Commission on Human Rights*, gay state employee Harold Lampley alleged sex discrimination because he was treated poorly for not appearing or behaving stereotypically male. Co-worker Rene Frost alleged discrimination and retaliation for friendship with him. The Human Rights Commission denied both claims, but an appeals court ruled that discrimination based on insufficient masculinity can constitute sex discrimination regardless of whether an employee is gay or straight. The state appealed, arguing that Lampley alleged sexual-orientation discrimination rather than sex discrimination.

The lecture introduces MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures and surveys topics including temporal data structures, higher-dimensional geometry, dynamic optimality, memory hierarchies, hashing, integer data structures, dynamic graphs, strings, and succinct data structures. Course policies include weekly problem sets with one-page answers, revising lecture notes, and optional open-problem sessions.

The lecture defines a pointer machine as a memory model of nodes with a constant number of fields containing data or pointers, with one distinguished root node. It then introduces persistence, in which updates create new versions without destroying earlier ones. Four levels are described: partial persistence, where only the latest version can be updated; full persistence, where any version can be updated and versions branch into a tree; confluent persistence, where two versions can be combined into a new version and versions form a directed acyclic graph; and functional data structures, where nodes are never modified and all operations create new nodes.

For partial persistence, any pointer-machine data structure with constant maximum indegree can be transformed with constant amortized time overhead and constant additional space per modification. The implementation stores backward pointers and modification records containing a version, field, and new value. When a node’s modification capacity is exhausted, it is copied and pointers in the current version are recursively updated; amortized analysis shows the recursive work can be charged to accumulated modifications. Partial persistence can also be deamortized to achieve a constant worst-case slowdown.

Full persistence uses similar records but maintains backward pointers across all versions. Because versions form a tree rather than a linear timeline, they are linearized using an order-maintenance data structure that supports insertion and relative-order tests in constant time. A modification applies only along the queried version’s ancestor path. Full nodes are split by partitioning their modification tree into balanced subtrees, and affected pointers are recursively redirected. A potential based on unused modification slots provides the constant amortized bound. Constant worst-case overhead for full persistence was described as an open problem.

Confluent persistence is harder because versions form a DAG and operations such as splitting and concatenation can double data-structure size, producing exponential growth after a linear number of updates. A general result based on a version’s effective depth gives logarithmic overhead in the number of updates, which can become linear in pathological cases; corresponding worst-case space lower bounds exist. Restricting combinations to versions with no shared nodes permits logarithmic overhead using techniques including link-cut trees and fractional cascading. Whether constant overhead can be achieved for both updates and queries remains open.

Functional data structures provide all persistence capabilities by forbidding mutation. Path copying supports balanced search trees with logarithmic operation times and can also implement link-cut trees. Functional deques support constant-time concatenation, while functional tries can support version-tree copying and pasting. The lecture concludes that functional structures may be separated from ordinary structures by a logarithmic factor, leaving further improvements as open problems.

The paper proposes an active-learning queue-prioritization algorithm for scientific workflows combining generative AI with costly candidate simulation. An XGBoost surrogate predicts an expensive score and its uncertainty; an acquisition function combines these predictions with inexpensive properties to reorder generated candidates before simulation. The surrogate is periodically retrained as results arrive.

The method is demonstrated in a DiffLinker workflow for discovering zinc-based metal-organic frameworks, where molecular-dynamics simulations estimate internal strain while synthesizability and similarity to known frameworks provide additional objectives. Across 1,000 novel candidates, prioritization with active learning produced an average of 604 high-performing candidates, compared with 281 without prioritization, at an estimated computational overhead below 1%. Reordering also mitigated generative-model decay, including a setting that yielded about 30% more stable MOFs.

Experiments showed that balanced exploration and exploitation using upper confidence bound outperformed purely exploitative or exploratory strategies. Weak exploration achieved both the lowest strain-prediction error and the most stable MOFs. Multi-objective acquisition functions also supported prioritizing stability, synthesizability, and similarity, while excessive emphasis on synthesizability reduced the number of stable structures.

Professor Noelle Selin outlined the science, policy, and supply-chain implications of global mercury regulation. Mercury travels across national borders, enters ecosystems as toxic methylmercury, and accumulates in food chains, creating neurological risks for children and pregnant women and cardiovascular risks for adults. Major sources include coal combustion, product use and disposal, cremation, and artisanal and small-scale gold mining, whose emissions are significant but highly uncertain. Reducing U.S. deposition therefore requires addressing both local sources and globally transported emissions.

Selin described negotiations leading to the 2013 Minamata Convention, widely regarded as the first major global environmental treaty in more than a decade and the first international convention organized around the full life cycle of a chemical. A 2002 global scientific assessment established the case for international action. The United States initially favored voluntary programs, while the European Union and developing-country blocs pressed for a binding treaty. The Obama administration’s domestic mercury regulations and the 2012 Mercury and Air Toxic Standards helped secure U.S. support. The treaty was signed after five negotiating sessions and accepted by the United States without Senate ratification.

Product controls cover measuring devices, switches, batteries, fluorescent lighting, dental amalgam, industrial processes, cosmetics, antiseptics, pesticides, and biocides. Negotiators rejected a blanket ban with exceptions in favor of listing restricted products and processes, while allowing exemptions for uses such as vaccine preservatives and certain dental applications. Phaseout dates were often negotiated compromises among countries rather than product-specific scientific determinations. Trade in mercury is restricted except for exempted uses, and mercury waste is addressed partly through the Basel Convention.

Selin also examined artisanal and small-scale gold mining, where mercury is purchased through informal or black-market channels, used to form gold amalgam, and burned off to recover gold. This releases mercury locally, contaminates waterways and air, and connects mining communities to the international gold market. The treaty addresses these harms mainly through capacity building, safer technologies, formalization, and efforts to reduce mercury dependence without eliminating mining livelihoods.

International enforcement is weak, so compliance relies on national laws, transparency, diplomatic pressure, funding, technical assistance, and awareness raising. The treaty interacts with the Stockholm, Rotterdam, and Basel conventions and with organizations including the World Health Organization and International Labour Organization. She noted that domestic regulation often shaped international standards, with the EU now frequently leading global chemical rules and developing countries sometimes adopting U.S., German, or other established thresholds. Businesses participated through lighting manufacturers, mercury-free product advocates, and industry representatives seeking to protect products from restrictions.

Selin concluded that the treaty was more immediately important as a legal and political signal than as a means of reducing environmental mercury levels. Her modeling suggested it could stabilize mercury concentrations, but further reductions would likely require stricter emissions technology rules. For companies, the treaty encourages consideration of mercury-free alternatives, product redesign, supply-chain impacts, and evolving international standards.

After praising Snap following 72% year-over-year revenue growth and comparing it to early Facebook, Jim Cramer reversed course amid the app’s controversial redesign. Researchers from the NeuroPiano Institute and Sony Computer Science Laboratories confirmed that pianists can alter a piano’s timbre through controlled fingertip and key movements, resolving a century-old question. Using the non-contact Hackkey sensor system, they measured all 88 keys at 1,000 frames per second and 0.01-millimeter spatial resolution while 20 renowned pianists performed with varied timbral intentions. In listening experiments, 40 participants—including pianists and people without musical training—consistently perceived the intended timbres, even when volume and tempo were controlled; pianists showed greater sensitivity to timbral differences.

Data analysis identified specific movement features, including acceleration during escapement and deviations in hand synchronization, that produced timbre differences. Experiments varying only these features provided the first empirical evidence of a causal relationship between key movement and timbre. Published in PNAS, the findings could support evidence-based music instruction, visualization of expressive movements, and research in neuroscience, skill transfer, rehabilitation, and human-interface design.

The passage describes patterns for deploying containerized applications using Kubernetes. The ambassador pattern separates application logic from external concerns: service-broker ambassadors discover and connect applications to environment-specific services, while request-splitting ambassadors route a configurable share of traffic to experimental implementations. Nginx can implement a 10% experiment using IP hashing so users receive consistent service versions.

The adapter pattern adds a separate container that translates an application’s heterogeneous monitoring, logging, or health-check interfaces into standardized interfaces without modifying the application container. Examples include a Prometheus exporter for Redis, Fluentd adapters for normalizing logs and collecting Redis slow queries or Storm data, and an HTTP health-check adapter that runs diagnostic queries against MySQL. This decoupling supports reuse, independent updates, and dedicated resources.

Multi-node architectures are introduced through microservices, which divide applications into independently developed and scaled services connected through APIs. Microservices improve team autonomy, release flexibility, reliability, and scaling, but make debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns provide reusable solutions for these challenges.

Replicated, load-balanced stateless services use multiple identical replicas, a load balancer, and readiness probes to provide redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Session tracking can direct a user’s requests consistently to one replica through IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing. Additional replicated layers can provide caching with Varnish, rate limiting and denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services divide data among shards, with a root routing requests using a deterministic and uniform sharding function. Appropriate shard keys should group requests with equivalent responses, and consistent hashing minimizes remapping when shard counts change. Replicating individual shards improves failure tolerance and enables hot shards to scale independently. Kubernetes examples use memcached with either a local ambassador or a shared shard-routing service.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing by sending work to multiple leaves and combining their partial results at a root. It can accelerate searches and other independent computations, and leaves may themselves be sharded when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. However, coordination overhead, slow “straggler” leaves, and leaf failures become more significant as leaf count grows; replicating each shard improves reliability and upgrade safety.

Finally, the passage examines functions as a service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment, automatically scales and restarts stateless functions, and supports modular services, but introduces operational complexity, requires external state, is unsuitable for some long-running or memory-intensive workloads, and can become costly under sustained request processing. A FaaS decorator pattern transforms requests or responses independently; Kubeless demonstrates adding default values to REST API calls before processing.

The medRxiv preprint describes KaviKrishna’s three-decade participatory action research (PAR) and community-based participatory research (CBPR) approach to tuberculosis control in rural Assam, India. It combines an Indigenous Knowledge System (IKS) temple-based communication network, the Indigenous Kamarupa Information Network (IKIN), telemedicine, student volunteers, patient and caregiver participation, and modern molecular, genomic, and stem-cell methods. The program supports TB screening, contact tracing, diagnosis, nutrition assistance, treatment monitoring, relapse surveillance, and follow-up in communities underserved by conventional top-down programs.

Clinical studies included treated pulmonary TB patients from the Idu-Mishmi community in Arunachal Pradesh, from whom sputum, blood, and bone marrow were collected longitudinally. The authors reported dormant MTB within bone-marrow mesenchymal stem cells of successfully treated patients. A subsequent cohort of 250 patients, including MDR-TB cases from across Northeast India, is being monitored for relapse and MDR evolution using telemedicine and whole-genome sequencing. Preliminary findings identified rpoB and rpoC mutations in MTB recovered from stem-cell populations, suggesting—but not establishing—that the hypoxic bone-marrow stem-cell niche may contribute to MDR evolution.

Laboratory methods described include sputum decontamination, Löwenstein–Jensen culture, optimized phenol-chloroform DNA extraction, proportion-based drug-susceptibility testing, PCR for MTB and nontuberculous mycobacteria, immunomagnetic stem-cell sorting, qPCR, lineage analysis by MIRU-VNTR and spoligotyping, and Illumina whole-genome sequencing with genomic and phylogenetic pipelines. The identified lineages included Beijing, CAS/CAS1-Delhi, and orphan strains. Sequencing data have been deposited in NCBI under PRJNA1054003.

In an auxotrophic MTB mouse model, viable nonreplicating bacteria were recovered from mesenchymal stem-cell populations in bone marrow and lungs. Viral coinfection induced oxidative stress and stem-cell reprogramming, released dormant MTB, and produced pulmonary granulomas, supporting the authors’ proposed mechanism for reactivation. Additional protocols measure drug minimum inhibitory concentrations and killing duration using Alamar Blue assays and identify viable-but-nonculturable MTB through modified most-probable-number testing.

The authors propose that IKS-based CBPR could complement existing TB programs by linking community engagement with patient-specific surveillance, molecular epidemiology, and precision treatment. They emphasize that several MDR, stem-cell, and reactivation findings remain preliminary or under preparation and require further clinical and in-vivo investigation. Clinical and stem-cell studies received institutional ethical approval and informed consent; patient follow-up data are provided as supplementary material.

In the final use-case session, Gary Gensler and students examined blockchain applications in supply-chain management and digital identity. They discussed how blockchain could improve supply-chain traceability and transparency, particularly where current supplier assessments are difficult to verify and information is asymmetrical.

The class explored identity from philosophical and practical perspectives: identity as inherent personal characteristics, verifiable attributes, claims, credentials, and third-party attestations. They distinguished authentication from authorization and reviewed identity providers, attribute authorities, certificate authorities, public-key cryptography, digital signatures, and their role in securing internet transactions.

Major identity-management problems included identity theft, forged credentials, data breaches, outdated personal information, privacy concerns, and the burden of replacing compromised payment cards. Blockchain was presented as potentially reducing fraud and verification costs and supporting privacy and provenance, but also raising challenges involving immutability, deletion rights under laws such as GDPR, changing attributes, private-key loss, biometric security, public policy dependence on Social Security numbers, and the adoption costs involving banks, merchants, and governments.

Estonia’s X-Road and India’s Aadhaar were examined as large-scale identity systems not based on blockchain. Aadhaar was praised for rapid enrollment, financial inclusion, and efficient benefit distribution, but criticized for security failures, system errors, and cases in which people lost recognized access to assistance.

Self-sovereign identity was defined around individual control, direct access without intermediaries, portability of identity attributes, and interoperability. Participants questioned whether such a model could function given corporate market power, required identity disclosures, and dependence on traditional financial and governmental systems.

Several decentralized-identity initiatives were mentioned, including Sovrin, Civic, Existence, Bitnation, the Distributed Identity Foundation, ToIP, W3C work, and Bits on Blocks. Gensler concluded that blockchain has both workable applications and elements of hype, emphasizing the need to distinguish between them and that blockchain applications may offer more promise than digital-native tokens.

A confidential memorandum proposes preparing U.S. Peace Conference negotiators with condensed, reliable briefing materials. Experts would write secret, comprehensive articles on history, commerce, and international law, with additional topics including disarmament, international guarantees, arbitration, and analysis of foreign constitutions and political institutions. Qualified historians, political economists, and jurists would receive detailed instructions and prepare pamphlets capped at 10,000–15,000 words. One coordinator, assisted as needed, would assign subjects, select writers, issue instructions, review submissions, and oversee secret printing and indexing; appendices of documents, statistics, and quotations would also be compiled. Related questions ask how far the United States should participate in determining European boundaries and redistributing colonies; what criteria should govern territorial settlements; how competing claims, conquest, and enforced colonization should affect them; and whether colonial possessions should be guaranteed without conditions concerning government, commerce, or economic access. Colonel E. M. House tells Secretary of State Lansing that the President considers the memorandum admirable and useful for organizational planning and hopes to discuss the assignment in Washington.

Tennessee middle schooler Keaton Jones went viral after his mother recorded him describing the bullying he endured at school. Celebrities, including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo, expressed support for him and opposition to bullying.

Defendants were charged with possession of burglar’s tools, attempted petit larceny, and resisting arrest. Testimony showed they attempted to sever a bicycle’s chain with bolt cutters but abandoned the attempt after speaking with a bystander. The court instructed the jury on renunciation as a defense to attempted petit larceny but refused to apply it to possession of burglar’s tools. The jury convicted them of possession of burglar’s tools and acquitted them of the other charges. The court held that Penal Law § 40.10 did not permit renunciation as a defense to possession of burglar’s tools, despite noting concerns about the result, and denied the defendants’ motion to set aside the verdict.

Insecticides India plans to invest Rs 200 crore over three years, expand its Dahej and Chopanki plants, and establish new units in Gujarat and Rajasthan. It expects 10–15% revenue growth this fiscal, aided by a normal monsoon and four new crop-protection products. Expansion will be funded through internal accruals, debt and equity.

The Supreme Court said the CBI-led MDMA probe into the larger conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination had made little headway and could be “endless.” It arrayed the Centre in convict A G Perarivalan’s plea to suspend his life sentence until the probe concludes, with a hearing set for January 24. Perarivalan was convicted of supplying batteries allegedly used in the bomb.

The paper introduces OSCAR, a one-shot causal discovery method for high-dimensional, multi-label event sequences. OSCAR uses two autoregressive Transformers—one for next-event prediction and one for label prediction—to estimate conditional mutual information between each event and label given prior events. Per-label thresholds identify each label’s Markov boundary, while causal indicators in \([-1,1]\) quantify the expected change in label probability associated with an event.

The method models sequences as sequential Bayesian networks and parallelizes independence testing, avoiding the label- and event-cardinality-dependent costs of classical methods. Its theoretical guarantees assume temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, causal sufficiency, and accurate density estimators.

OSCAR was evaluated on 300,000 vehicle sequences containing approximately 29,100 diagnosis trouble codes and 474 vehicle error patterns. In a 50,000-sample comparison, OSCAR achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1 in 11.7 minutes. Five local structure-learning baselines failed to return Markov boundaries within a three-day timeout. The authors position OSCAR as a scalable, interpretable approach for explaining vehicle defects and supporting diagnostic rule refinement.

South Carolina Rep. Trey Gowdy and Sen. Tim Scott are close friends who frequently joke about Gowdy’s hair and co-authored *Unified: How Our Unlikely Friendship Gives Us Hope for a Divided Country*. After aggressively defending Republicans during the Benghazi hearings, Gowdy grew disillusioned with partisan politics and announced on Jan. 31, 2018, that he would not seek re-election, citing his desire to return to law and its rewards of fairness. He subsequently challenged Republican claims about the Russia investigation, criticized Devin Nunes’s memo and the Steele dossier, supported Robert Mueller, warned President Trump against firing Mueller, and condemned Trump’s behavior.

Despite disappointment over the loss, the speaker remains optimistic about the team’s ability to compete and win. The team squandered two-goal third-period leads and must learn from its mistakes, stick to its game plan and systems, and persevere. With supportive fans behind it, the team is focused on the next game and treating every game as essential in the cup series.

For very large sparse systems \(Ax=b\), direct elimination can be prohibitively expensive in time and storage, while sparse matrix-vector multiplication is fast. Iterative methods therefore seek approximations quickly, with convergence aided by choosing a preconditioner \(P\) that resembles \(A\) but is simpler to use.

Common preconditioners include the diagonal of \(A\) for Jacobi, its lower-triangular part for Gauss-Seidel, weighted combinations in successive overrelaxation, and approximate triangular factors from incomplete LU, which discard selected fill-in. For stationary iteration, the error satisfies
\[
e_{k+1}=P^{-1}(A-P)e_k=Me_k,
\]
where \(M=I-P^{-1}A\) is the iteration matrix. Convergence from an arbitrary initial error requires every eigenvalue of \(M\) to have magnitude below one. The spectral radius determines the rate, with the eigenvalue closest in magnitude to one controlling the slowest error decay.

Using the one-dimensional tridiagonal matrix with 2s on the diagonal and \(-1\)s on adjacent diagonals, Jacobi uses \(P=2I\). Its iteration eigenvalues are \(\cos(j\pi/(n+1))\), so its spectral radius is close to one and convergence may require order \(n^2\) iterations. Jacobi quickly suppresses high-frequency error components but leaves low-frequency components, causing slow convergence. The residual \(b-Ax_k=Ae_k\) can decrease faster than the solution error because \(A^{-1}\) may be large.

Weighted Jacobi changes \(P\) to the diagonal divided by a weight \(\omega\); its iteration eigenvalues become \(1-\omega+\omega\cos\theta\). This can improve high-frequency damping but does not adequately address low frequencies.

Gauss-Seidel immediately uses newly computed components, reducing storage compared with Jacobi and squaring the corresponding iteration eigenvalues. It improves convergence but remains insufficient for these large problems. The lecture therefore anticipates multigrid, which addresses problematic low frequencies by viewing them as higher frequencies on a different grid, and notes conjugate gradient as highly effective for symmetric positive-definite systems.

After New Jersey swept Detroit in four straight Stanley Cup Final games, the speaker said he was disappointed but proud of his team’s rapid improvement and Final appearance. He believed Detroit won in many areas, though not by large margins, and credited New Jersey’s greater Finals experience and his team’s mistakes. He praised New Jersey’s top-level goaltending by Ozzie, experienced defense, four offensive lines, and the leadership and consistency of Stevie, while also calling Olaf Kolzig outstanding. He noted the team’s support for injured players and the city’s strong interest in hockey. Rejecting suggestions that the swept team should be embarrassed, he said many teams would have considered reaching the Finals an achievement. He and George had begun building a foundation and instilling a new attitude, and he expected the team to rebound after teaching its young players valuable lessons about commitment and handling disappointment.

The ADS868xW uses a multiSPI digital interface composed of input and output shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit. Data output can be host- or device-controlled and use system-synchronous or source-synchronous timing.

Host-to-device configurations include a single device using all multiSPI options, a minimum-pin standard SPI interface, and multiple devices in a daisy chain. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, and their SDO-0 outputs feed the next device’s SDI input. All devices require identical configuration and SDO_CTL_REG bits 7–0 set to 00h. An optimal frame requires 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices, with data returned in reverse device order; system throughput decreases as device count increases.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, or CONV states. The active-low RST pin can trigger either an application reset, which resets configuration registers, or a power-on reset, which resets internal circuitry including the PGA, ADC driver, and voltage reference. Reset exits to ACQ after the specified delay. ACQ acquires the analog input and supports low-power NAP mode, while CONV performs a conversion using an internal clock and ignores additional CONVST/CS transitions until conversion completion.

Programming supports data reads and writes using nine configuration registers. A transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS, loads the 32-bit output shift register, and shifts input data into the LSB while shifting output data from the MSB. Pulling CONVST/CS high ends the frame and transfers the input word to the command processor. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames permit partial output reads but invalidate writes, while longer frames use the final 32 shifted input bits as the command. Input commands are 32 bits, support byte and half-word operations, and HWORD commands ignore the address LSB.

Output data for the next frame depends on the preceding command and DATA_VAL setting. It can be a fixed test pattern, 8- or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional appended fields include device address, input range, AVDD and input alarm flags, and parity.

Writes use one of four legacy SPI-compatible protocols. Reads support single- or dual-SDO legacy SPI protocols and source-synchronous modes. The default protocol after power-up or asynchronous reset is SPI-00-S, with subsequent protocol selection controlled by SDI_MODE. Dual-SDO operation is enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG to 11b, making the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin an SDO-1 output. Source-synchronous mode supplies a clock on RVS that can be synchronous to either SCLK or the internal device clock.

Configuration registers provide device identification for up to 16 daisy-chained devices, reset and power controls, SPI input-protocol selection, output-protocol and bus-width control, output flags and test patterns, input-range and reference settings, alarm status, and programmable alarm thresholds.

An industrial application combines the single-channel ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to provide eight software-configured voltage or current channels. The ADS868xW is a fully differential 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated AFE, PGA, ADC driver, and buffered reference. It settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and has up to 400-kHz input bandwidth. Programmable input alarms include adjustable high and low thresholds and hysteresis; an NTC thermistor example illustrates temperature monitoring.

The device uses separate analog AVDD and digital DVDD supplies. Recommended decoupling includes 1-µF and minimum 10-µF capacitors near the supply pins, separate analog and digital PCB regions, short ground paths, and specified reference-pin capacitors. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption; power-down leaves the interface active and retains register contents. The document also provides alarm, board-layout, support, ESD, packaging, revision, and TI disclaimer information.

A Trump administration amendment lets U.S. employers deny contraception coverage to workers on religious or moral grounds, reversing an Obamacare requirement. Reproductive-rights advocates objected, conservative Christians supported it, and California pledged to challenge the policy.

This phenomenological qualitative study examined 45 pre-service teachers who voluntarily took a special education course through distance education at a private university during the 2022–2023 academic year. Data were collected through researcher-developed, semistructured interviews and analyzed by themes and subthemes.

Most participants were satisfied with the distance education course, and the majority recommended distance education because of its effectiveness, flexibility, home-comfort advantages, individualized learning opportunities, technological familiarity, and lower financial burden. However, participants reported internet connectivity problems, distractions, limited interaction, insufficient technical and material support, and difficulty with applied courses. Face-to-face education was regarded as more effective and permanent by some participants, particularly because it enabled easier dialogue and immediate consultation.

Participants emphasized the importance of course participation for learning and success, although some argued that attendance need not be mandatory because motivated students could learn through recordings and not everyone had reliable devices or internet access. Recommendations included improving distance education systems, internet infrastructure, technical support, digital materials, and free access to the internet. The researchers also noted the study’s limited sample and recommended larger studies, quantitative research, and research involving other courses.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K dated January 28, 2020, reported financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. The related press release was attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report stated that the information was furnished, not deemed filed under Section 18, and was not incorporated by reference except as expressly specified. Apple common stock and ten series of notes were listed as Nasdaq-registered securities. The report was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

The article counters bearish market warnings as major equity indexes reach record highs, using Ray Dalio’s bubble-diagnosis framework. It argues that bearish theses sound more compelling and action-oriented, while historical data favors patient, “boring” strategies that do little or nothing; excitement is also the “worst enemy of return.” The piece promotes Envision Research’s investing community, describes its services and model portfolios, outlines author Lucas Ma’s background and holdings disclosures, and includes Seeking Alpha disclaimers and chart metadata.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Its display engine natively supports HDR and BT.2100 tone mapping. An enhanced NVENC encoder supports H.265/HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps, with up to 25% HEVC and 15% H.264 bitrate savings, while NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR decoding. Turing’s hardware encoder provides higher quality than fast x264 software encoding with substantially lower CPU use and makes 4K streaming practical.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, allowing VR headsets to receive power, display data, and tracking data through one connector. TU102 and TU104 replace MIO and PCIe SLI links with second-generation NVLink, providing 25 GB/s per direction per x8 link and enabling two-way SLI with new display configurations, but not three- or four-way SLI.

Real-time ray tracing is accelerated by dedicated RT Cores in each streaming multiprocessor. RT Cores perform bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, freeing other GPU resources for additional work. The passage reports roughly tenfold ray-tracing performance improvements over Pascal. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization for visibility and primary-ray work with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects where it provides greater visual benefit. BVH acceleration and denoising reduce the computational cost, and the technology supports NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API.

NGX is a Turing-only neural graphics stack that uses Tensor Cores for pretrained AI services. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) uses neural networks to reconstruct high-quality target-resolution images from lower-resolution inputs. Standard DLSS is reported to match temporal anti-aliasing quality with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X produces output approaching 64-times supersampling. Together with Tensor Core acceleration, DLSS enables the RTX 2080 Ti to reach twice the performance of the GTX 1080 Ti. Other NGX features include AI-based inpainting, slow-motion frame interpolation, and 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Turing also introduces task and mesh shaders for cooperative, object-list-based rendering. Mesh shading can eliminate CPU draw-call bottlenecks, select geometry levels of detail dynamically, perform spatial cutaways, and render more than an order of magnitude more objects at real-time frame rates. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently from visibility for each 16×16-pixel region, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering as well as increased shading for multisample anti-aliasing. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading, reuses previously shaded texels across frames and views, and can reduce work in stereo VR rendering. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and 32 API views, extending Pascal’s stereo and surround capabilities to more varied projections.

Turing extends DirectX 12 resource binding to bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, supports Tier 2 resource heaps, and permits different resource types to share heaps. Its VR technologies include VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, foveated Variable Rate Shading, and RT Core acceleration for ray-traced audio.

The full TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores and supports one x8 NVLink link. It is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The Tesla T4 targets data-center, enterprise, and edge inference workloads. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based performance metric that weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput according to their modeled utilization in hybrid rendering. The passage also explains ray casting, BVH construction and refitting, denoising, and the advantages of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections over shadow maps, screen-space ambient occlusion, and screen-space reflections. It concludes with NVIDIA’s disclaimers concerning specification accuracy, warranties, product suitability, intellectual property, and liability.

This April 16, 2001 collection of clippings (compiled by Ann M. Schmidt for Jeff Dasovich) covers energy markets, layoffs, renewables, technology stocks, and India.

**Energy and utilities:** Sierra Pacific Resources, owner of two Nevada utilities, suspended its 25-cent quarterly dividend citing high power costs from the Western energy crisis, saving under $20 million while continuing administrative cost cuts, including eliminating executive incentive pay. The company lost $39.8 million (51 cents a share) in 2000 after an unexpected $889 million fuel-and-electricity expense, and benefited from a 17% Nevada rate increase (about $300 million). It still hopes to complete a $2 billion purchase of Enron's Portland General Electric unit (assuming $1 billion of debt), though the deal has been delayed by a California law blocking sales of power plants; Enron CEO Jeffrey Skilling put the odds of completion at "5%." Separately, Enron said its 15,000 b/d MTBE plant at Morgan's Point, Texas restarted after a March 9 maintenance turnaround; Enron also owns a La Porte, Texas plant making 400,000 b/d methanol.

**India/Dabhol:** A Maharashtra committee (Godbole panel) said Dabhol phase II would keep the Maharashtra State Electricity Board financially sick despite MSEB improvements, urged deferring power purchase agreements with independent producers, and noted Dabhol's annual burden of roughly Rs 6,000 crore. The panel also recommended renegotiating the tariff, removing dollar linkage, and deferring DPC payment obligations for at least five years (preferably 15). Enron owns 65% of Dabhol Power Co., which charges 7.1 rupees/kWh versus 1.5 by other suppliers; Enron invoked an Indian government counterguarantee in March over MSEB's unpaid 1.02 billion rupee December bill and sent a political force majeure notice. Trade unions cited high Dabhol tariffs in preparing an April 25 Maharashtra bandh against globalisation, unemployment, and WTO-related farm policy impacts.

**Renewables:** The Crown Estates issued seabed leases for 13 UK offshore wind projects (seven Irish Sea, six North Sea) worth up to £1.6 billion, adding 1,500 MW by 2004 to serve 1.1 million homes; lease holders include Innogy, Powergen, Scottish Power, Enron, and TXU Europe. Separately, U.S. solar-thermal plants near Barstow serve 350,000 homes, and high gas prices are drawing large utilities into renewables (Sharp, BP Solar, Shell Renewables, and Enron's purchase of Zond). California, deriving 12% of power from renewables, aims to add 5,000 MW by July, with 16% renewable, backed by a $202 million state subsidy program.

**Layoffs and disclosure:** Internet rumor boards accelerate layoff decisions; companies print memos or issue statements to control messaging, while SEC rules on layoffs remain fuzzy and Regulation FD narrows selective disclosure. Enron publicly denied broadband layoff rumors, and its stock rallied to $59.40 from a low of $51.51.

**Markets and other items:** Tech stocks rallied (Nasdaq up 14% in a four-day week to 1961.43) ahead of first-quarter earnings from Intel, Microsoft, IBM, Apple, Enron and others, amid weak economic data and concerns the Nasdaq bear market may continue. Kenneth Lay said the administration's global-warming action went too far, and President Bush was expected to nominate Enron executive Thomas White Jr. to head the Army. In technology media, the DivX format threatens film distribution as MP3 did music, prompting MPAA to plan 20,000 cease-and-desist letters. A Business Standard essay argued India's rulers retain a "Divine Right" immunity from blame, citing the Ketan Parekh and Enron cases.

A “Reversal Day” is a substantial upward or downward change in a stock or market index after an extended trend, often accompanied by heavy trading volume. A bullish reversal follows a downtrend, may take out the previous low, and closes above the previous day’s high. A bearish reversal follows an uptrend, may set a higher high, and closes below the previous day’s low.

Reversals may be driven by changes in investor sentiment, economic conditions, company news, or technical trading patterns. Potential signals include trend changes, volume spikes, support and resistance breaks, RSI or MACD divergence, moving averages, Bollinger Bands, and broader market cycles. Stocks, currencies, commodities, and bonds can all experience reversals under different conditions.

The article backtests bullish and bearish Reversal Day strategies in gold using Amibroker, with exits after 1–25 trading days. The bullish strategy produced generally strong profit factors but relatively few trades, with a highest average gain of 2.02% for a 24-day exit. The bearish strategy produced losses because of gold’s upward overnight-session drift and had substantially lower average gains. The backtests indicate that the reversal-day concept has merit, although rules and market context remain important.

Cocoa futures are standardized contracts to buy or sell 10 metric tons of cocoa at a predetermined price on a future date. They trade on ICE Futures US under the symbol CC and on CME Globex/NYMEX under CJ. ICE contracts are settled by physical delivery, while CME contracts are financially settled. Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December, and trading terminates on the day before the last notice day. The minimum price fluctuation is $1 per metric ton, or $10 per contract.

Cocoa futures can be accessed through a futures broker using leverage. CFDs based on cocoa are also available through CFD brokers. On ICE, trading runs from 9:15 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. London time, with pre- and post-market hours. CME Globex trading runs Sunday through Friday, 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily break. Charts are available through platforms such as TradingView, MultiCharts, Yahoo Finance, and YCharts.

A cocoa futures strategy may combine fundamental and technical analysis with precise entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management. In the cited backtest, the strategy recovered after 30 trades and recorded 96 trades, a 2.3 profit factor, and a 74% win rate. Cocoa futures historically perform better in summer and worse in spring and fall.

Prices are driven by factors affecting cocoa supply and demand. As of November 25, 2022, cocoa traded at $2,484 per metric ton, making a 10-metric-ton contract worth $24,840. The all-time high was $5,379 in July 1977; the lowest price since 1979 was $707 in December 2000. Major risks include leveraged losses from adverse price movements and limited liquidity.

Trading cocoa futures can support hedging, portfolio diversification, speculation, and arbitrage. The iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB) provides cocoa-futures exposure by tracking contracts with three expiration dates.

Health savings accounts (HSAs), a decades-old Republican concept receiving renewed attention as a possible Affordable Care Act replacement, allow tax-free investment growth and tax-free withdrawals for qualified medical expenses. They are limited to people with high-deductible insurance plans; in 2015, about 20 million of 176 million insured people participated.

Participation is limited by upfront costs, psychological barriers to saving, and broader difficulties with long-term financial planning. Research suggests loss aversion can motivate behavior and that automatic enrollment, similar to some 401(k) plans, might boost participation, though it would cost the government. HSA users generally use less health care and spend less on prescriptions, but emergency-room visits increased, particularly among lower-income families, and improved health is uncertain. Determining future medical costs is also difficult. Experts say HSAs are useful only for people with sufficient cash and emergency savings, and broader participation would require people to take future health and financial needs more seriously.

MLPs outperformed the S&P 500 in 2016, with the AMZE total return at 22.5% and the traditional cap-weighted Alerian index up 18.3%. Performance varied by weighting; Enterprise Products Partners’ unusual underperformance affected the adjusted index, while fund flows supported its roughly 20% weighting. December’s 4.4% return extended positive streaks and ended two consecutive negative Decembers, with recent momentum suggesting the sector’s recovery could continue.

Global Partners led the sector for a second week; Plains All American, ONEOK Partners, Boardwalk, and Natural Resource Partners were among the laggards. SunCoke Energy Partners led the year, while Ferrellgas was the worst performer. General partners and corporations underperformed for a second week.

Capital-markets activity included Plains GP Holdings’ plan to sell up to $500 million of common units at the market. Shell Midstream Partners announced Gulf of Mexico pipeline acquisitions at a 7.7x EBITDA multiple, with no purchase price disclosed.

The article examines the S&P 500 Information Technology sector, which holds over 25% of the index’s market capitalization and includes companies developing or distributing technology, software, services, semiconductors, and hardware. Major tracking ETFs are VGT and XLK, while the five largest stocks listed are Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Adobe.

Two mean-reversion-based technology strategies are presented. The first recorded 245 trades, a 0.96% average gain, 10% CAGR, 18% maximum drawdown, 71% win rate, and 3.1 profit factor. The second recorded 212 trades, a 1.05% average gain, 9.5% CAGR, 15% maximum drawdown, 70% win rate, and 2.85 profit factor. The article notes that technology-sector strategies may correlate strongly with the broader market and provide limited diversification. Strategy code and logic are available through the website’s subscription package.

The passage debates whether MDC-T leader Morgan Tsvangirai has strengthened or weakened Zimbabwe’s opposition, citing his 2008 victory, 2013 defeat, party split, and illness. It praises his alliance-building but urges leadership renewal and retirement in favor of a stronger successor.

The Simplified Specification/Addendum is a non-confidential subset of the SD Card Association’s full specification, provided “AS-IS” without warranties or liability for damages or IP infringement. Implementation may require a license; no rights are implied.

A descriptive cross-sectional study examined burnout among Ghana Prison Service officers at Nsawam Medium Security Prison. Proportionate stratified random sampling recruited 266 officers from a population of 608; 243 questionnaires were analyzed, giving a 92% participation rate. Self-administered tools adapted from the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist assessed burnout, workplace conditions, perceived causes, and coping strategies.

Overall burnout prevalence was 9%. Emotional exhaustion was high in 42.0% of officers, depersonalization was distributed across low (35.4%), moderate (32.1%), and high (32.5%) levels, and 68.7% had low personal accomplishment. Leading perceived causes were irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and inadequate training and development opportunities (47.7%). Officers reported strengths in teamwork, workplace pride, control of their work, and peer support, but limited recognition, constructive feedback, supervisory trust, and administrative support.

Shift allocation was associated with emotional exhaustion, with the main shift having the highest proportion of high-exhaustion cases. Rank was associated with depersonalization, which was more common among junior officers. Sex was associated with burnout: females represented 54.5% of burned-out officers, and males had 69% lower adjusted odds of burnout. Officers with diploma/certificate qualifications also had lower adjusted odds than postgraduates.

The most common coping strategies were talking with colleagues (62.5%), looking forward to time off duty (60.1%), and talking with family (54.3%); keeping thoughts and feelings private was also reported (42.1%), while alcohol use was the least common (29.2%). The authors recommended addressing irregular shifts, workload, training, development opportunities, and psychosocial working conditions to reduce burnout.

The passage criticizes Stanford’s mandatory Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR) for failing to teach rigorous academic writing. It argues that broad, vague topics and minimal instruction encourage formulaic work, while lenient grading and high A-range grade distributions undermine meaningful assessment. It also describes PWR’s curriculum and events as overtly political and calls for conservative alternatives. The authors reject a proposed PWR minor, arguing that the department should instead improve its existing courses. They recommend a rigorous, standardized, source-based class designed by experienced humanities professors and taught by junior faculty, as well as allowing already proficient writers to take advanced placement.

Montecito Fire crews will teach 800 elementary students emergency preparedness, including Stop, Drop and Roll, crawling low in smoke, identifying home fire hazards, calling 9-1-1, and exiting safely. Oct. 3–6 activities were canceled due to weather and will be rescheduled; parents are urged to practice family emergency plans.

The early BMW M8 prototype appears unfinished, with provisional lighting, standard brakes, and downgraded wheels. BMW has not released specifications, but the car reportedly uses the CLAR platform and a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8, with standard all-wheel drive and more than 600 horsepower. It may rival Ferrari and Lamborghini, while the revived M8 nameplate could compete with the S-Class Coupe and Cabriolet. The original M8 never entered production, although its V12 later powered the McLaren F1.

Ottawa police are investigating an alleged assault and robbery near Innes and O’Toole roads. Around 5:30 p.m. Saturday, a woman claiming a broken-down car and no phone allegedly lured a driver about a kilometre to her vehicle, where she and two men attacked him and stole cash before fleeing. The victim was treated in hospital. Police released suspect descriptions and details of a dark-coloured, older North American four-door sedan.

At a Code Conference panel, Aileen Lee, Megan Smith, and Sukhinder Singh Cassidy discussed diversity and inclusion in tech. Lee urged the industry to remove bias from hiring, funding, and business processes and rejected avoiding one-on-one meetings between men and women. Smith highlighted that women of color are the most excluded.

StockX added BAPE and PALACE to its streetwear category, which launched in October 2017 with an exclusive Supreme collection, making StockX the world's largest seller of authentic Supreme merchandise. At launch, StockX will operate the largest authenticated marketplaces for BAPE (over 4,000 products dating back to 2010) and PALACE (more than 3,000 products), led by general managers Scotty Newman and Kenny Locklier, respectively. BAPE was founded by NIGO in 1993 and acquired by I.T. Group in 2011; PALACE was launched by Lev Tanju in 2010. Founded by Josh Luber, Greg Schwartz and Dan Gilbert, StockX launched in February 2016 with over 200 team members and more than $2 million in daily sales.

Vertigo, an iOS music-sharing app, announced integration with both Spotify and Apple Music, becoming the first iOS app to enable cross-platform sharing. Users can import playlists from either service, search catalogues, and share songs so friends can listen using their own subscriptions. Beyond song sharing, playlist creation and ad-free listening, Vertigo offers "live sessions": live-streamed listening with video, photos, real-time chat, and audio commentary, shareable with individual users, a "core" friend group, or the app community. Because only paid subscribers may participate, Vertigo pays royalties to rights holders, increased with each listener. Positioned against the Apple Music–Spotify competition, Vertigo may fill a social gap in Apple Music, which has de-emphasized social features.

Glen Campbell’s family says music comforts him as he battles late-stage Alzheimer’s, sometimes prompting him to smile and sing along. His final recording, “Adios,” originally made in 2012 and released June 9, preserves his voice and love of music despite the disease.

In October 2022, a reporter used a seven-day Eurail pass to travel by rail through Germany, Austria, Italy, and Switzerland, taking eight rides between six cities and paying $560 including upgrades and overnight-train fees. The pass cost $477 and covered unlimited travel on many routes; first- and business-class seats were affordable, while comparable plane tickets were more expensive. Compared with flying, rail travel offered greater comfort, easier and faster boarding, better scenery, fewer issues such as ear popping and dehydration, and a lower carbon footprint, leading the reporter to prefer trains for future European trips.

Brazilian stocks gained Thursday as Vale rallied up to 4.9% after record year-on-year first-quarter iron ore production, despite a seasonal quarterly decline. Itaú BBA retained an “outperform” rating. Usinas Siderúrgicas de Minas Gerais rose after reversing a quarterly loss amid signs of industrial recovery. The real was volatile amid geopolitical and election concerns, though polls favoring Emmanuel Macron over Marine Le Pen eased anxiety.

At the 73rd annual Colorado 4-H June conference at Colorado State University, Rio Blanco team members Macy Collins and Marryn Shults placed third and seventh overall, respectively. Collins also placed third in oral reasons and made the Colorado State 4-H Livestock All State team; Shults placed fourth in beef and fifth in sheep/goat. Collins earned fifth in beef, third in swine, fourth in sheep/goat and eighth overall. Because her 2015 national-qualifying team participation no longer counted, Collins competed individually. Jilly Bumguardner and Tatumn Kennedy gained experience as the other senior team members. Collins will attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full academic and judging scholarship after being praised for her leadership and accomplishments.

This study developed a laboratory-ready workflow using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) to analyze and report optical genome mapping (OGM) data for myeloid neoplasms, extending an International Consortium implementation framework. Ten retrospective cases—nine acute myeloid leukemia and one myelodysplastic syndrome—received five to six blinded reviews by independent technologist/director teams. Bionano Access and Solve data were processed through standardized VIA views, guideline panels, custom variant classifications, copy-number and allelic-imbalance checks, technologist review, director review, and automated report generation. Consensus analysis included structural and copy-number variants reported in at least two reviews; allelic-imbalance/absence-of-heterozygosity calls were excluded.

OGM detected all standard-of-care findings; six cases were positive by both methods and four were negative by both. OGM identified additional findings in five of six positive cases, including large 4q and 9q losses, trisomy 8, IKZF1-region deletions, a KMT2A::MLLT10 fusion, an unbalanced t(2;17), chromosomal gains, and a SETD2-overlapping deletion. Sentinel standard-of-care findings were consistently classified as Tier 1A in five cases, while reporting and classification varied for nonsentinel variants.

Average technologist review time was 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for two complex cases. Custom views and linked tracking reduced manual filtering, and VIA often reduced review time by approximately 50% compared with Access alone. The workflow detected all standard-of-care variants, revealed additional abnormalities, and streamlined interpretation and reporting, although variability persisted for lower-tier findings.

President Donald Trump warned Iran Tuesday not to restart its nuclear program, saying they would face "bigger problems," as he and French President Emmanuel Macron met in the Oval Office seeking common ground on saving the 2015 nuclear accord. Trump scorned the Obama-era deal as "terrible," citing Iran's ballistic missiles and involvement in Yemen and Syria. Iran has said it will ramp up its program if the deal collapses, and a senior official said Tehran might quit the nuclear non-proliferation treaty if Trump scraps it. Trump said he and Macron were close to understanding each other. Macron urged Trump to remain in the agreement, calling it the best chance to constrain Tehran. Other agenda items included exemptions from Trump's 25 percent steel tariffs, the Paris climate accord, and U.S. troops in Syria. Trump is also arranging a summit with Kim Jong Un.

The football holder positions the ball for extra points and field goals, catching the snap and placing it precisely for the kicker. Success requires soft hands, consistent and quick placement, the ability to rotate the football with laces away from the kicker, and calm execution under pressure. Holders often are punters, backup quarterbacks, receivers, or other players. On fake field goals, they may pass, flip, or run the ball. Though overlooked and rarely statistically tracked, a holder’s accuracy can be decisive in converting or missing scoring opportunities.

The Daily Examiner is shifting from metered digital access to a premium model, with some stories reserved for subscribers while public-safety information and selected local stories remain free. Existing subscribers retain unlimited website, app, newsletter, alerts and other News Corp access; subscriptions are available online or by phone.

Thailand recorded 390 road deaths during Songkran week, an 11% annual decline following junta anti-drink-driving enforcement. It was the first reduction after repeated campaigns, though 28% of crashes involved drunk driving. Authorities seized 5,600 motorbikes and 1,800 cars; speeding, low helmet use and corrupt traffic policing remained concerns.

The EU, spearheaded by Germany and France, is preparing to urge multilateral development banks to align financing more closely with the Paris Agreement, redirect lending from fossil fuels, and accelerate green energy, climate resilience, and sustainability investments. The draft also calls for greater transparency, local-currency financing, risk mitigation, and data-sharing to attract private capital and support emerging economies’ development and decarbonisation. EU officials plan to promote the initiative at upcoming World Bank and IMF meetings. The U.S. opposes the shift, warning it could distract banks from economic growth and poverty reduction. Although development banks invested a record $137 billion in climate projects in 2024, EU leaders consider this insufficient, while adoption remains uncertain.

Canada’s Supreme Court unanimously ruled that confidential residential-school assessment records may be destroyed after 15 years, balancing victims’ privacy against preserving historical evidence. The court emphasized that settlement negotiators and participants intended the process to remain private, and records concern more than 37,000 compensation claims.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning to lead the Milwaukee Brewers to a 2-0 win over the Minnesota Twins on July 3, 2018. Thames reached base three times and has three homers in six games; eight of his 12 season homers have scored Milwaukee’s first run, and seven have given the Brewers the lead. Nate Orf pinch-hit, walked and stole second before Thames’s homer off Jake Odorizzi.

Junior Guerra pitched five scoreless innings for Milwaukee, allowing two hits while walking three and striking out eight. Josh Hader pitched three hitless innings in relief, and Corey Knebel struck out the side for his ninth save. Odorizzi allowed two runs and four hits in five innings.

The Twins fell to 1-7 on their nine-game road trip. Joe Mauer became the first first baseman since Edwin Encarnacion in 2012 to play a full game without a putout or assist. Milwaukee also reported injuries involving Christian Yelich, Lorenzo Cain and Zach Davies. José Berrios is scheduled to start Wednesday’s series finale against Chase Anderson.

**Summary**

On December 8, 2000, Enron's Steven Kean forwarded to Mark Schroeder, Richard Shapiro, and Elizabeth Linnell a note from McKinsey's Suzanne Nimocks (December 7, 2000) containing an attached presentation ("Intlmail 3 exhibits.ppt"). The attachment is a McKinsey memorandum from Carol B. White and Pru Sheppard (EU – EPNG R&I), dated December 6, 2000, titled "Power sector restructuring: international activity, June–November 2000," described as a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring.

**Overall findings:** Privatization and restructuring activity continues apace. Governments facing growing power demand but lacking funds are opening generation markets to foreign investors even where privatization is not formally on the agenda; state-owned utilities are unbundling; competition is being introduced at wholesale and retail levels; some international players have scaled back international investments and shifted portfolios to less risky markets such as the U.S. and Europe; the EU Directive has spurred European competition; recovering Asian economies are again advancing unbundling plans; and Latin American privatizations have restarted at a slower pace after currency devaluations.

**Structure and coverage:** The memo summarizes developments in Europe, Central and Eastern Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa, with country-by-country entries. Europe covers Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the U.K. (e.g., ENEL's required divestitures, Germany's utility mergers, U.K. full choice since May 1999 with the New Electricity Trading Arrangements postponed to early 2001, and the Endesa–Iberdrola merger). Central and Eastern Europe covers Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Moldova, Romania, Russia, the Slovak Republic, Turkey, and Ukraine. Asia-Pacific covers Australia, China, India (including a draft Electricity Bill 2000), Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Pakistan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. Latin America covers Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, and the Virgin Islands. Africa and the Middle East cover Algeria, Ghana, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and the United Arab Emirates. Most Middle Eastern and African countries have moved no further than allowing IPPs; five Sub-Saharan countries (Côte d'Ivoire, Gabon, Guinea, Mali, Senegal) have privatized their power systems. Hydro reliance and droughts have raised prices, and regional transmission links are noted (Mozambique Transmission Company, a 16-country West African Power Pool, and a six-country link among Egypt, Jordan, Iraq, Syria, Turkey, and Lebanon).

**Exhibits and closing:** Exhibits 1–4 are maps of restructuring status in Europe, Asia, Latin America, and Africa/Middle East; Exhibit 5 is a "slippery slope" exhibit; Exhibits 6–8 show market-opening timelines by region. The memo invites local corrections, comments, exhibit suggestions, and updates, notes that removal requests should go to Carol Brotman White, provides contacts for regional information (European EPNG R&Is, Pru Sheppard for Asia, Carol Brotman White for Latin America/Middle East/Africa), and lists its sources, including McKinsey's Private Power Database, Financial Times, and various trade publications.

Prosecutors told jurors that former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory provided a Chinese spy with human-asset and other classified information for $25,000. Defense lawyers said Mallory contacted the CIA before the Chinese recruitment attempt and fed the recruiter false documents to expose an intelligence operation. Testimony established that Mallory contacted CIA contacts in February 2017, before a Shanghai trip during which customs agents found $16,500 in undeclared cash. Investigators later found classified documents on computer drives and text exchanges on a Chinese-provided Samsung phone. Mallory faces up to life in prison.

Each Inauguration Day has marked a national task: creating the nation, preserving it from internal disruption, and now saving it and its institutions from external disruption. Americans must pause to assess their place in history and avoid isolation and inaction. Although national longevity depends on the human spirit rather than years, democracy has repeatedly revived and grown, drawing on the informed will of free citizens and permitting unlimited progress. The Constitution continues to function, while civil liberties and free elections remain intact.

America, like a person, requires a body, a mind, and a spirit. Its body needs material security and opportunity; its mind must remain informed, alert, and aware of other nations; and its spirit—the faith of America—is the most essential. Democratic ideals have deep historical roots and are reflected in the Mayflower Compact, Declaration of Independence, Constitution, and Gettysburg Address. The nation must address undeserved poverty and self-serving wealth while preparing citizens for the future. Amid great perils, preserving the spirit of liberty and protecting democracy remain America’s highest purposes, warranting sacrifice and continued action.

Olean’s Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant. Proposed projects include redevelopment of the former Manufacturers Hanover building, business incubator funding, expanded theater options, and pedestrian and park improvements. Olean could also receive more than $2 million through Buffalo Billion. The application was due 22 hours after approval, with Mary George’s staff credited for preparing it in three weeks. Jamestown Community College’s John Sayegh supported the bid and offered to help upgrade the Cutco Theater.

IDC’s December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at discrete and process manufacturers with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland examines IT-based simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC).

Simulation and modeling are increasingly used to accelerate product development, reduce costs, improve quality, and support decisions. Three-quarters of respondents prioritized innovation, while 57% viewed these tools as important for improving product and service quality and preventing defects. About half already used them in product development, production and process planning, or quality management, with deployment expected to approach 90% within two years. However, departmental data silos can produce inconsistent analyses. IDC therefore recommends a holistic data strategy and a shared “single source of truth” across the product life cycle.

Current technologies include virtual prototyping, CAD/CAM/CAE, 3D visualization, IoT, mathematical optimization, high-performance analytics, and digital twins. More than half of respondents already use virtual testing, 42% use high-performance data analytics, and 39% seek to simulate as many physical processes as possible. Digital twins can monitor products and plants, test hypothetical changes, integrate ecosystem data, and enable services such as usage optimization, “Product as a Service,” and outcome-based models. IDC also identifies combinations of these technologies as enabling varied industrial applications.

Growing simulation complexity has increased demand for HPC. Although only 8% currently report very high demand, almost half are expected to within two years; half say calculations take too long, and 42% report that some simulations are outdated or inaccurate. Four in five decision makers consider HPC a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables complex calculations, faster and more frequent analysis, new use cases, and greater agility. More than one-quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while another 39% are planning or piloting it.

Most surveyed HPC users prefer external infrastructure, including public clouds, while many operate or plan systems in colocation datacenters. Challenges include security concerns, cited by 72%; energy consumption and sustainability, cited by 58%; insufficient expertise, cited by 42%; computing capacity, availability, scalability, remote access, licensing, investment, and operating costs. IDC expects public-cloud HPC to become the leading architecture, followed by hybrid-cloud systems, and recommends comparing on-premises, HPC-as-a-Service, and hybrid models according to utilization, performance, budget, flexibility, security, and skills. HPCaaS can reduce upfront costs, provide scalable and current technology, and support new HPC-based services and business models.

Uber's panic button lets riders dial 911 from the app's home screen. Announced in April after alleged sexual assaults, the feature shows the rider's real-time location for relay to 911 operators. In a seven-city pilot, the app automatically sends location and vehicle details—color, make, model, year and licence plate—to dispatchers.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 specification update catalogs silicon errata and workarounds across clock gating, interrupts, DMA/ATA, ACPI power management, KEL, PCI/LPC, USB, UART, and SMBus.

Automatic Diverse Device clock gating can prevent an edge-configured PIC from returning to Idle when its interrupt source remains high, causing missed interrupts and possible system hangs. Similar gating issues affect GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs, UART operation in CEIR mode, and USB controllers. The update recommends disabling automatic clock gating where specified.

ATA issues include incorrect CRC continuation after device termination, UDMA failure when bus mastering precedes a PIO command, bus-master resets caused by unexpected early device interrupts, and ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRDs. Recommended measures include blocking host terminations, using the normal PIO-before-bus-master sequence, and DWORD-aligning PRDs. ATAC and ACC eight-byte PRD prefetch can expose part of the next PRD when tables are not 8-byte aligned; PRD tables should be defined before transfers, with on-the-fly changes kept sufficiently far ahead. DMA-mode SSMI also fails to block IDE I/O and should not be used.

ACPI PM1_EN and PM1_STS byte accesses can hang because only WORD and DWORD accesses are supported. WORD or BYTE PMC writes may corrupt the same or unrelated registers, requiring restricted accesses or SMI/BIOS trapping. GPIO[27:24] transitions do not wake the system from S3; PWRBTN# and optional external OR circuitry are recommended. Sleep exit can also leave SLEEP_X/SLEEP_Y asserted when delay-counter values are too high.

Other documented issues include KEL inability to distinguish writes to I/O ports 060h and 064h, improper KEL state changes in Snoop mode, delayed or missed SSMIs when interrupts coincide, unsupported 8259 polling mode, ATAC and SMBus timing and status anomalies, LPC aborts and DMA-related I/O blocking, incorrect PCI timing margins, RTC CMOS read errors, GPIO corruption after suspend, missing LOWBAT_FLAG, and loss of SSMI reliability. Suggested workarounds include disabling affected clock-gating modes, storing and restoring KEL state, using single-transfer LPC DMA, writing SMB_STS twice to clear NEGACK, performing GPIO read-modify-writes after suspend, and adding small capacitors to IRDY# or DEVSEL# if timing problems arise.

The speaker criticizes his team’s loss to Detroit, saying they generated few chances, surrendered early goals, and played unevenly despite a generally even game. He notes that the power play failed, acknowledges Detroit’s strong defense, and says the team must improve and contribute more.

In spring 1953, the United States contrasts the shattered hope for peace after World War II with a Cold War division between a cooperative, free world and a Soviet system based on force and power. Soviet rearmament has compelled free nations to remain strong, unite through NATO and a European Defense Community, and confront aggression in Korea and Southeast Asia. The continuing arms race risks atomic war and diverts resources from food, housing, health, education, and development.

Following Stalin’s death, the United States urges the new Soviet leadership to demonstrate peaceful intent through concrete actions. It calls for an honorable Korean armistice, free elections in unified Korea, an end to attacks in Indochina and Malaya, an Austrian treaty, broader European cooperation including a free and united Germany, and just settlements concerning Eastern Europe. It also proposes verifiable disarmament through limits on armed forces and strategic production, international control of atomic energy, restrictions on destructive weapons, and United Nations inspection. Savings from disarmament should fund global aid and reconstruction.

The United States declares that deeds, not rhetoric, will determine Soviet intentions and asks whether Moscow will support genuine peace, self-determination, and disarmament. Failure would leave the world divided and armed, but renewed trust and cooperation could replace fear with a just and lasting peace.

This study examines how digital customer experience through e-commerce practices and electronic word of mouth affect sustainable supply chain performance in Indonesian ICT companies, with brand image and supply chain image as key constructs. Data were collected from employees involved in product distribution: Indonesia was divided into 15 clusters, 10 were randomly selected, and 568 questionnaires were distributed, yielding 315 valid responses. Analysis used partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), and the measurement model demonstrated reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity.

All seven hypotheses were supported. Digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth positively affected brand image (β = 0.214 and 0.745, respectively). Brand image positively affected supply chain image (β = 0.752), which strongly affected sustainable supply chain performance (β = 0.907). Brand image mediated the relationships of digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth with supply chain image, while supply chain image mediated the relationship between brand image and sustainable supply chain performance.
