The model explained 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance, and all reported relationships and mediation effects were statistically significant. The findings indicate that strengthening brand image through e-commerce-based digital customer experiences and electronic word of mouth can improve supply chain image and sustainable performance.

Apple Inc. reported that on February 8, 2021, it completed the sale of six series of notes: $2.5 billion of 0.700% notes due 2026; $2.5 billion of 1.200% notes due 2028; $2.75 billion of 1.650% notes due 2031; $1.5 billion of 2.375% notes due 2041; $3 billion of 2.650% notes due 2051; and $1.75 billion of 2.800% notes due 2061. The notes were issued under a February 1, 2021 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities and Morgan Stanley as representatives, and under a 2018 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. Interest is payable semiannually, beginning August 8, 2021. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms and legal opinion as exhibits.

This divisional patent application, supported by NASA under Contract No. NNC14CA32C, describes hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion systems, particularly their operation during aircraft descent. It notes that conventional gas turbines are optimized for takeoff or top-of-climb and are less efficient at lower-power modes. Operating the core during descent solely to provide bleed air or avoid thermal cycling consumes additional fuel.

An exemplary two-spool turbofan includes a fan, low- and high-pressure compressors, a combustor, and low- and high-pressure turbines. The low-pressure fan, compressor, and turbine share an inner shaft, while the high-pressure compressor and turbine share an outer shaft; a gear reduction system may drive the fan more slowly than the low-pressure spool. An electric motor/generator is incorporated with the low-speed shaft. This arrangement permits the engine to be undersized relative to conventional takeoff or climb thrust requirements, with either physical sizing or engine-flow control keeping the high-pressure turbine at maximum inlet temperature during cruise.

During descent, a controller lowers engine temperature by reducing fuel, airflow, or both, either shutting down the core or maintaining it at the minimum temperature needed to avoid an additional thermal cycle. The core thereby produces no thrust. Aircraft systems that normally use engine bleed air or engine power are switched to electricity supplied by stored energy or an electric compressor that replaces compressor bleed air.

The fan may also windmill as air passes through the bypass duct, rotating the low-speed spool and motor/generator to produce electricity for the aircraft power distribution system. This electricity can supplement stored energy or fully power aircraft systems. If excess energy is stored, it can instead drive the motor as a motor to rotate the fan and generate thrust sufficient to match conventional descent thrust or overcome engine drag. Energy generated during other flight modes can be stored in a battery, supercapacitor, or similar device for later use. These features may be used individually or in combination and are also applicable to other turbofan architectures.

Cloud-based HPCaaS gives manufacturers rapid, flexible access to advanced analytics, simulation methods and state-of-the-art hardware. Fifty-two percent of respondents view this access as central to innovation. Faster calculations and new data-processing methods provide deeper insights and enable digital products, services and business models. Cloud HPC can also improve computational energy efficiency and help firms overcome capacity, hardware-freshness and infrastructure-cost constraints, although Bridgestone is adopting cloud gradually.

IDC states that simulations, modeling and data analytics help manufacturers respond to disruption and competitive pressure by accelerating product development and manufacturing. Applications include evaluating alternative materials and processes, optimizing supply chains, energy use and sustainability, and developing digital offerings. As simulations become more complex, HPC is becoming a prerequisite; public cloud and HPCaaS can extend in-house clusters or replace them entirely.

Manufacturing innovation, productivity and competitiveness depend on integrating accessible data into a single source of truth across the product lifecycle. IDC recommends establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, creating lifecycle transparency and a holistic data strategy, and choosing among on-premises, HPCaaS or hybrid operating models based on utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security and skills. Solutions should be scalable, secure and energy-efficient, with external expertise or ecosystem partners used when internal capabilities are insufficient.

The findings come from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology-related decision-makers from industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 30, 2022 reported third-quarter revenue of $5.93 billion, down 17% year over year, gross margin of 53.6% versus 65.2%, operating income of $601 million, net income of $680 million, and diluted EPS of $0.27, compared with $7.10 billion, 65.2%, $2.67 billion, $2.46 billion, and $0.97 a year earlier. Nine-month revenue rose 9% to $20.92 billion, while net income fell to $2.95 billion and diluted EPS to $1.17, including a $1.35 billion Arm acquisition termination cost.

Compute & Networking revenue increased 27% to $3.82 billion, led by 31% Data Center growth, while Graphics revenue fell 48% to $2.12 billion. Gaming revenue declined 51%, Professional Visualization fell 65%, Automotive increased 86%, and OEM and Other declined 69%. A $702 million inventory provision, partly offset by a $70 million warranty benefit, drove the quarterly gross-margin decline; nine-month inventory provisions totaled $2.01 billion.

At October 30, 2022, total assets were $40.49 billion, liabilities were $19.14 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $21.35 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $13.14 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $3.39 billion, investing activities provided $7.38 billion, and financing activities used $9.96 billion.

NVIDIA repurchased $3.65 billion of shares and paid $100 million in dividends during the quarter; nine-month repurchases totaled $8.99 billion and dividends $300 million. The company had $8.28 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization through December 2023.

The planned Arm acquisition was terminated because of regulatory challenges, resulting in the $1.35 billion write-off of the signing prepayment. NVIDIA cited supply constraints, long lead times, architecture transitions, channel inventory adjustments, cryptocurrency-related demand volatility, COVID-19 disruptions in China, and new U.S. export restrictions affecting China and Russia as business risks. It paused direct sales to Russia and subsequently closed its Russian operations. Related securities and derivative lawsuits remained pending, with no loss accrual recorded because liabilities were not considered probable.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 *Nevermind* album cover, depicting a naked baby underwater, does not constitute child pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit, finding that factors such as genital focus, sexual suggestiveness and intended arousal were absent. He compared the image to a family photograph of a nude child bathing.

Donna Adelson was sentenced to life in prison for the 2014 murder-for-hire of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, and 30 additional years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. At sentencing, she denied involvement, claimed Markel would be appalled by the lack of evidence and justice, and said she would have stopped the plot had she known. Judge Stephen Everett warned that he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors said the motive was to force Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to move to South Florida with their children; Wendi was not charged.

Myrna LaPlante supports National Inquiry chief commissioner Marion Buller and opposes a “reset” that could require her family’s story to be removed from the public record. Her aunt Emily Osmond has been missing since 2006. After the Assembly of First Nations called for Buller’s resignation without consulting families, LaPlante supported extending the inquiry deadline by two years and incorporating community partnerships. Some Saskatchewan families backed Buller’s resignation, citing poor communication, disorganized hearings, missing family stories and inadequate attention to community trauma.

With interest rates rising and average 30-year fixed mortgage rates near 5%, borrowers may improve their borrowing power by reducing debt, since lenders consider recurring minimum payments when calculating debt-to-income ratios. A co-signer can add borrowing capacity but shares equal mortgage liability. Switching loan programs, such as from Freddie Mac or conventional financing to Fannie Mae or FHA loans, may also affect approval. Larger down payments can help but typically less than paying down debt. Borrowers should carefully consider changing from hourly or self-employed work to a salaried or W-2 position in the same or a similar field before applying. Each option should be researched for the borrower’s circumstances.

Singapore’s development from a resource-poor nation into a prosperous, globally competitive city-state has made education and workforce preparation central to its success. Its meritocratic, multicultural society and stable governance under the People’s Action Party have supported long-term educational planning. Before 2004, special education was largely operated by welfare organizations, religious bodies, philanthropists, and health services, creating a dual system of separate special and mainstream schools. Mainstream provision focused more on integration than meaningful inclusion, schools could refuse students with disabilities, and Singapore had no legislation requiring special education in mainstream schools.

The year 2004 became a watershed when the government promoted an inclusive society and greater integration into mainstream schools. Enabling Masterplans, the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and subsequent reforms expanded support for people with disabilities. Special schools are now government funded but remain operated by social service agencies, while mainstream and special schools are viewed as part of one national education continuum. Mainstream enrolment of students with special educational needs rose from 2,500 in 2005 to 35,500, with about 80% served in mainstream schools and 20% in special schools. The 2019 Compulsory Education Act requires students with special educational needs to attend mainstream primary schools or government-funded special schools.

Special education personnel preparation has expanded alongside these changes. The National Institute of Education began training Special Needs Officers in 2005; they were later renamed Allied Educators and then Special Education Needs Officers. A one-year full-time Diploma in Special Education equips them to identify needs, assess difficulties, and plan interventions. Since 2005, the Certificate in Special Needs Support has provided in-service professional development for mainstream teachers, while a 2020 roadmap requires all mainstream educators to develop basic special-needs competencies. All pre-service teachers also complete coursework on diverse learners. Special-school teachers historically progressed from a three-year part-time Certificate in Special Education to the current one-year full-time Diploma, followed by an Advanced Diploma, a master’s degree, and doctoral options. Nevertheless, special education remains less comprehensive than mainstream teacher preparation, and NIE does not offer an undergraduate degree in the field.

Reforms have been supported by centralized policy-making and school-level implementation, close cooperation among the Ministry of Education, NIE, and schools, and the government’s tripartite approach. Mainstream schools increasingly use tiered support systems and collaborative teams involving teachers, special education personnel, counsellors, and psychologists. Stable political continuity has enabled sustained, long-term reform.

Key remaining concerns include the division of responsibility for special schools between the Ministry of Education and social service agencies, lower salaries for special-school teachers, limited mainstream options for students with higher support needs, and insufficient depth and duration in special educator preparation. As Singapore shifts toward holistic, student-centred education and greater social inclusion, the role of special education is expected to expand in partnership with mainstream schools.

A July 31, 2001 IEP News digest collected reports on California’s electricity crisis and related energy-policy developments. Commentary by Kathleen Connell and Peter Navarro argued that the Davis administration’s $43 billion in long-term power contracts and $8 billion in short-term purchases created billions in “stranded costs,” required $12.4 billion in bonds and placed pressure on the state budget. The commentary attributed California’s improving power conditions to cooler weather, conservation, reduced demand and federal price caps.

The SEC began a preliminary inquiry into whether Davis administration energy consultants traded power-company stocks using inside information. Five consultants were fired over potential conflicts after holding shares in Calpine or Enron. Spokesman Steve Maviglio also disclosed buying 300 Calpine shares worth about $12,000 and holding Enron stock, while another official disclosed recently selling Williams stock. Consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed under a lawsuit settlement to accept no compensation for their state work. Separately, California officials planned to appeal a FERC decision limiting electricity refunds to roughly $3.9 billion, down from the approximately $9 billion sought; FERC excluded direct purchases by the Department of Water Resources and required a hearing to determine refund amounts.

A Salon article described difficulty assembling a state bailout for insolvent Southern California Edison, which claimed nearly $4 billion in debt. Competing legislative proposals differed over state acquisition of transmission lines, and opponents favored bankruptcy or a less costly deal. The article also detailed Davis’s ties to Edison and the utility’s campaign contributions to him.

San Francisco voters were scheduled to consider two November measures creating public power authorities: a municipal utility district serving San Francisco and Brisbane, and a city-only municipal water and power agency. PG&E opposed the proposals, while supporters argued elected boards would provide local control and lower rates.

Other reports examined Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed separation from Constellation Energy, with regulators concerned about $2.4 billion in remaining debt, and Texas’s launch of a deregulation pilot allowing up to 5 percent of customers to choose new providers before broader implementation in January 2002.

The digest attributed California’s crisis to high demand, costly wholesale power, transmission problems, scarce Northwestern hydropower and maintenance at aging plants. It said Southern California Edison and PG&E had lost nearly $14 billion since June 2000, PG&E had filed for bankruptcy, and the state was buying power for nearly 9 million customers as regulators approved rate increases ranging from 15 percent to 49 percent by customer class.

Sony released an A7R III firmware update to fix the “Set File Name” function and improve overall camera stability. Installation problems appear limited to unsupported macOS High Sierra 10.13; earlier Mac OS versions can install it, while affected users may temporarily use Windows.

On Feb. 14, The New York Times reported that Russian intelligence officials contacted Trump’s 2016 campaign chairman Paul Manafort, though officials found no evidence the campaign cooperated with Russia on election interference. The FBI interviewed former national security adviser Michael Flynn after Trump’s inauguration about his interactions with a top Russian official; Flynn was later ousted amid concerns he had misled administration officials. Republican Sens. Rob Portman and John Thune withheld support for labor secretary nominee Andrew Puzder, citing his delayed payment of taxes for an unauthorized housekeeper. The Senate confirmed Linda McMahon as Small Business Administration leader, 81-19, and unanimously confirmed David Shulkin as Veterans Affairs secretary. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation of Flynn and asked Attorney General Jeff Sessions to recuse himself.

Michael Lewis recounts Lew Goldberg’s 1968 study, in which doctors disagreed on whether individual ulcers were malignant and gave contradictory diagnoses for repeated images of the same ulcers. An algorithm based on the doctors’ stated reasoning outperformed every doctor, though the account leaves unclear how conflicting answers were handled and how images reached the computer. The passage notes that human input may still have influenced the results and concludes that experts created the rules used by the program, while raising questions about the growing role of artificial intelligence and big data in diagnosis.

The lecture concludes a PDE unit and begins a probability unit that will lead into models versus data. Homework 7 requires solving a two-dimensional drug-diffusion problem both in COMSOL and with a custom finite-volume code. A drug diffuses from a patch into a shear flow with no reactions. Because the drug’s diffusivity is small relative to the flow’s shear rate, the characteristic length is tiny and the Peclet number is large, producing very sharp concentration gradients, especially at the patch’s upstream edge. Mesh refinement in both directions may therefore be required, and rectangular cells could provide greater resolution where gradients are strongest.

The instructors stress that solver output alone does not establish physical correctness. Convergence should be tested by refining the mesh and by solving simplified problems with progressively more distant zero-concentration boundaries, which are expected to approach the full solution from above. Finite-volume cells are treated as well-mixed control volumes: one balance equation is written per cell, with net inflow and outflow fluxes equal to accumulation, or zero at steady state. Cell concentrations are approximate averages, while fluxes across cell faces are computed directly. Boundary conditions include zero flux at impermeable walls and prescribed concentration at the drug patch. Patch fluxes may be estimated directly or through ghost-cell interpolation. Velocities and fluxes are evaluated between cell centers, which can improve numerical stability.

The resulting system is linear and sparse. MATLAB’s sparse backslash solver is suggested, while BiCGSTAB is presented as an option for very large, matrix-free sparse systems; iterative methods may require an initial guess and can have convergence difficulties. The lecture also introduces the CFL condition for time-dependent calculations: the time step should be no greater than, or at most of the same order as, the distance traveled per step divided by velocity. Larger time steps can move material across multiple cells between updates and produce unreliable results. Reducing spatial resolution therefore requires smaller time steps and increases computational cost. Adaptive meshes can improve accuracy but are prone to bugs, while COMSOL’s automatic meshing is described as a carefully implemented alternative.

Probability is introduced through measurement and physical fluctuations. Repeated measurements vary because of both experimental noise and intrinsic fluctuations in the measured system. Continuum equations describe averages rather than individual molecular behavior, and quantum mechanics likewise provides probability distributions rather than definite individual outcomes. Consequently, reported measurements are estimates accompanied by distributions or error bars.

Basic discrete probability, joint events, and conditional probabilities are demonstrated with coin flips, emphasizing careful accounting to avoid double counting. Bayes’ theorem is introduced as  
\(P(A\mid B)=P(B\mid A)P(A)/P(B)\), together with the total-probability rule for summing over mutually exclusive possibilities. For continuous variables, sums become integrals and probability densities have units inversely related to the variable, so probabilities must be specified over intervals rather than at exact points. A cumulative distribution function \(F(v_*)=P(v\le v_*)\) is also introduced, with an example of determining the fraction of gas molecules below specified speeds in a supersonic nozzle.

Which? research following the November base-rate rise from 0.25% to 0.5% found 48% of 327 instant-access savings accounts and ISAs unchanged, while only 10% of 95 providers passed the full increase to all customers. Meanwhile, 53% of standard variable mortgage providers raised existing borrowers’ rates, and average two-, three- and five-year fixed deals rose. Which? alleged double standards; UK Finance said rates reflect multiple costs and competition.

The United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch the Imagination Library in Carroll County on March 28, 2018, at 10 a.m. at the Mt. Carroll Township Public Library, providing books to children ages 0–5.

Wave-like clouds were spotted over Bristol and shared on Twitter. The Met Office identified them as Asperitas, a newly classified supplementary cloud feature. Their formation remains uncertain, with possible links to post-thunderstorm conditions or changing wind direction.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 data sheet describes a low-power MCU with a 32-kHz Low-Frequency Sub-System containing an RTC and asynchronous IWDT. Analog features include selectable 1.4-V or 2.5-V internal or external voltage references, a comparator with selectable inputs, an 8-bit reference DAC, wakeup support, and timer fault-handle integration. Security features include flexible code and data firewalls and customizable CRC-16.

Communication peripherals include three UARTs with configurable parity, baud rates, LIN mode, separate FIFOs, and loopback; I²C supporting 7- and 10-bit addressing, controller and target modes, clock stretching, SMBus 3.0, DMA, wakeup, and rates up to 1 Mbps; and SPI supporting controller or peripheral operation, programmable frames and prescalers, DMA, multiple frame formats, and rates up to 16 Mbits/s.

The independent watchdog timer has its own power and clock source and can trigger a power-on reset, while the windowed watchdog can generate a reset or interrupt. RTC_B provides calendar counters, programmable alarms, periodic and interval wakeups, leap-year correction, and crystal-offset and temperature-drift compensation. General-purpose and advanced timers support counting, prescaling, QEI, cross-triggering, capture/compare, PWM with dead-band insertion, and fault handling.

Additional subsystems include IOMUX-controlled digital I/O and wakeup logic, an Arm-compatible two-wire SWD interface, DEBUGSS debugging and mailbox services, and memory-mapped factory constants containing device identification and trim data. Recommended application circuitry includes 10-µF and 0.1-µF VDD/VSS decoupling capacitors, a 47-kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000-pF pulldown, required crystal bypass capacitors, and pullups for 5-V-tolerant open-drain I/O.

The document also presents TI development resources, device naming conventions, the September 2025 revision history, support resources, ESD guidance, mechanical package drawings, orderable information, and disclaimers concerning technical data, development resources, and component suitability.

Open strings quantized on D-branes contain massless gauge and scalar fields; their fluctuations make the branes dynamical, with scalar fields describing brane motion. A D-brane’s mass or tension is identified with the vacuum energy of all open-string modes living on it. This energy is calculated through a Euclidean path integral over surfaces with boundaries, weighted by \(g_s^{-\chi}\), where \(\chi=2-2h-b\). At weak string coupling, the disk term dominates, giving a D-brane mass proportional to \(1/g_s\).

The interaction between two D-branes can be represented by a cylindrical surface with two boundaries. Viewed along one axis, this is closed-string exchange between the branes; viewed along the other, it is a one-loop open string connecting them. This geometric equivalence, called channel duality, hints at the relation between closed-string gravity and open-string gauge theory.

At low energies, the massless D-brane fields have a Dirac–Born–Infeld-type action, a nonlinear generalization of Maxwell theory that also describes the relativistic motion of a \(p\)-dimensional brane. Transverse scalar fields have no potential because their positions reflect broken spacetime translation symmetry; they therefore behave like Goldstone bosons.

Topology counting relates the open-string coupling \(g_o\) to the closed-string coupling through \(g_s\propto g_o^2\), so \(g_o\) is proportional to \(\sqrt{g_s}\).

For \(N\) coincident oriented D-branes, open strings have endpoint labels \((i,j)\), giving \(N^2\) copies of each excitation and promoting fields to matrices. String joining naturally produces matrix multiplication, and the system has a global \(U(N)\) symmetry that becomes a gauge symmetry on the brane world volume. The resulting low-energy theory is \(U(N)\) Yang–Mills theory, with gauge fields in the adjoint representation and transverse scalars as matter fields. Separating the branes stretches strings between them, gives formerly massless modes masses, and breaks \(U(N)\) into product groups such as \(\prod_i U(n_i)\), analogous to a Higgs mechanism in which transverse scalar expectation values determine the brane locations.

Residents in Belleville and nearby areas are advised to watch for Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillars, which appear from July to September in nut trees such as hickory, walnut and oak. Their front and rear hairs can release venom when touched, potentially causing a poison-ivy-like rash, redness, burning, swelling, pain, headache, nausea or allergic reactions. Wash exposed skin promptly, apply calamine lotion or cortisone for itching, and seek medical attention for severe reactions. The caterpillars are generally not a health hazard unless disturbed; children may be more reactive.

The FAQ explains that options trading in META is a derivatives strategy in which contracts provide the right to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price by a specified date. Call options grant purchase rights, while put options grant sale rights. Options are available on META and other stocks, indices, commodities, and currencies, with different strikes and expirations.

Opening an account generally requires registration and personal information. The stated minimum deposit is $100, although broker requirements may differ. Margin is typically similar to single-stock options and depends on leverage and the asset traded. Leverage ranges from 1:1 to 1:100 and may increase both profits and losses. Orders are placed by selecting the asset, call or put, expiration, strike price, and number of contracts. The minimum trade is one contract.

META charges no options commissions, but brokers may charge financing, slippage, and inactivity fees. Brokers provide options chains, watchlists, charts, technical indicators, market analysis, and risk tools such as stop-loss, take-profit, and trailing-stop orders. Educational resources include webinars, tutorials, video courses, and a META demo account for practicing with virtual money.

Available strategies include calls, puts, covered and naked positions, straddles, strangles, and spreads. The FAQ emphasizes that options are highly leveraged and speculative, can cause substantial losses—especially when shorting options—and should only be traded with funds the investor can afford to lose. It also recommends backtesting, while noting that options are difficult to backtest because of the many strikes and expirations.

The FAQ describes a mean-reversion strategy for SPY/S&P 500 using Internal Bar Strength (IBS) and Relative Strength Index (RSI). It presents backtest equity curves since January 2000, starting with $100,000, full compounding, and no taxes, plus performance statistics and inverted-parameter results. It also promotes code for the strategy and more than 70 other trading strategies.

The report analyzes the global nuclear medicine market by manufacturer, region, product type, application, and sales channel. It reports average annual growth of 6.27%, from $3.5 billion in 2013 to $4.2 billion in 2016, with $5.89 billion projected by 2021. Key manufacturers include GE Healthcare, Bracco Imaging, Mallinckrodt, Lantheus Medical Imaging, and Bayer.

EdReports CEO Eric Hirsch will leave at the end of the school year as the board searches for a successor. Since founding the organization in 2014, Hirsch has overseen more than 1,100 reviews of instructional materials, which many states and districts use when selecting curricula. His departure comes as EdReports revises its review criteria, expands into pre-K materials and faces criticism for being slow to reflect reading-science research. A November report placed greater emphasis on phonics, fluency and phonemic awareness. Hirsch also said research indicates that adopting strong curricula is insufficient because teacher training, assessments and curriculum often do not align, while many districts do not pilot or evaluate materials before districtwide adoption. The next leader will need to understand AI’s role in curriculum and support teachers in adapting lessons and supplemental materials.

A 2021 background note by Amanda Silver, Sarah Kalloch, and Zeynep Ton traces the history of “unskilled” work in the United States, including how occupational classifications reflected job content, worker identity, barriers to entry, wages, and social status.

The U.S. Census Bureau began collecting occupational data in 1820. Alba Edwards formalized a six-group classification system in 1917, placing manual and trade work into skilled, semiskilled, or unskilled categories, while professional, managerial, and clerical work was distinguished by property, credit, and business or executive ability rather than skill. Worker demographics also shaped classifications; occupations staffed largely by children, young people, or women were sometimes labeled semiskilled. In 1930, 14 million workers—28% of the workforce—were classified as unskilled in farm labor, factory labor, other labor, and servant occupations. Seventy-five percent of employed African American workers held these jobs, compared with 20% of native-born white and 30% of foreign-born white workers.

By the 21st century, “low-skill” work was commonly defined through education and experience requirements or analyses of job content. Automation contributed to job polarization: middle-paid sales, administrative, and production work grew more slowly, while low-paid in-person service employment increased. In 2018, more than half of the labor force held jobs whose typical entry-level education requirement was a high school degree or less, with a median annual wage of $33,473. Home health and personal care aides and fast-food workers were projected to be among the fastest-growing occupations from 2019 to 2029.

Farm labor historically depended on enslaved African Americans, child and family labor, sharecropping, convict leasing, and low-wage immigrant labor, including Mexican and Chinese workers. Its physical demands, low pay, limited benefits, pesticide exposure, extreme weather, and seasonal insecurity persisted even as mechanization and consolidation reduced agricultural employment. By 2019, agriculture employed 1.3% of the U.S. workforce, and farm workers received an average of $12.11 per hour.

Factory work developed from artisan production into industrial mass production employing immigrants, children, and women. Ford’s moving assembly line exemplified the division of work into repetitive, rapidly trained tasks, while Black workers were disproportionately assigned to hazardous foundry jobs. Automation, offshoring, and production changes reduced manufacturing employment by 67% from 1965 to 2020. Low-wage manufacturing also persisted through prison labor and sweatshops; prison workers produced more than $2 billion in goods annually in 2020 while earning as little as $0.23 per hour.

Domestic and personal service work included unpaid or exploited household labor, restaurant work, caregiving, and cleaning. Appliances and rising restaurant consumption reduced private household employment while expanding food, retail, hospitality, childcare, and health-related services. In 2019, retail sales workers and fast-food workers numbered approximately 4.6 million and 3.9 million, respectively, with median hourly wages of $12.29 and $11.18. Just-in-time scheduling, repetitive work, tipped wages, and limited benefits contributed to instability. Direct-care work was physically and cognitively demanding, and nursing assistants were three times as likely as typical U.S. workers to suffer job injuries.

Technology also created new forms of low-entry-barrier work through app-based transportation and delivery, on-demand retail and elder care, online microtasks, outsourced content moderation, and independent contracting. These arrangements often used algorithmic management and paid low wages; Mechanical Turk workers typically earned $2–$3 per hour, while some were paid only after completing unsatisfactory work.

Education and training alone did not substantially improve employment conditions. Government regulation through the Fair Labor Standards Act and National Labor Relations Act established minimum wages, workweek limits, and organizing rights, but agricultural, domestic, tipped, and contract workers were often excluded from protections. Median hourly compensation rose alongside productivity through much of the 20th century but stagnated from the 1970s as productivity continued rising. Strikes and unions improved wages, safety, and working conditions, although union membership fell from 34.8% of the workforce in 1954 to 6.2% in 2020. New farmworker and domestic-worker organizations promoted wage gains, overtime, and sick leave, while employers such as Ford, Toyota, Costco, QuikTrip, and In-N-Out Burger used higher wages, employee participation, training, and redesigned work to improve productivity and job quality.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, nearly 70% of essential workers were in “unskilled” jobs and 80% held low-wage occupations. They worked in healthcare, food and agriculture, transportation, warehousing, and other services, often without adequate protective equipment. The pandemic highlighted both the economic importance of these workers and their low wages and social status. Concluding that job quality—not technology-driven job loss—was the central challenge for lower-wage workers, the note raises questions about how society should value, organize, and compensate work historically categorized as “unskilled.”

The Gann Fan is a technical-analysis tool developed by early-20th-century trader W.D. Gann. It plots nine diagonal lines from a significant swing high or low to identify potential support, resistance, breakout, and reversal levels. The central 1:1, or 45-degree, line represents equal price and time intervals; other lines use ratios including 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 8:1, 1:8, 1:4, 1:3, and 1:2. Price holding above the 1:1 trendline may indicate a strong bull market, while breaking below it may signal bearish conditions.

Trading rules involve identifying the trend, selecting a starting point, drawing Gann angles, and observing where price intersects those lines. Example setups include a trend-following buy and a short-selling reversal after price reaches the 1:1 line. Traders may use Gann Fans to identify entries, exits, and price targets, preferably alongside chart patterns, indicators, trendlines, and moving averages.

Risk management should include stop-loss orders, position sizing, risk-reward ratios, clear entry and exit points, and a plan for managing losses. The tool can also be applied to forex to identify support, resistance, trends, and possible reversals.

Unlike Fibonacci fans, which use Fibonacci percentages, Gann Fans emphasize price-time relationships. However, Gang angles do not reliably govern price movements, and indicated support or resistance may not hold. Backtesting can assess historical performance, but past results do not guarantee future returns. The passage notes that meaningful Gann Fan backtesting is difficult because the strategy is subjective and requires numerous rules, leading the authors to advise against trading classical chart patterns without objective testing and to use diversified strategies rather than searching for a single best strategy.

Cover 1 (“man-free”) assigns every receiver man coverage while a free safety patrols deep and a linebacker or strong safety may drop underneath. It limits vertical throws and lets defenses funnel routes toward middle help, blitz, bracket receivers, or add run defenders, but creates exploitable outside matchups. Offenses can attack the perimeter with pick plays, double moves, and routes that deliver the ball on the move, including wheel, out, and deep crossing routes to create yards after catch. Examples from Ohio State, Oklahoma, and Georgia include an incomplete back-pylon throw, a scramble touchdown, an incompletion against disguised Tampa 2 coverage, a goal-line catch after Jerry Rice motion, and a touchdown from a scissors/snag-wheel combination.

Christine Milligan was surprised when hospital staff asked whether her family should revoke the organ-donation wishes of her daughter, Cassidey Ouellete. Ouellete, who signed a donor card at 16, was pronounced brain dead after a car accident the day before her 20th birthday. Milligan wants her brother Robert Milligan’s 2012 bill reintroduced, proposing that only donors revoke registration and that Ontario adopt presumed consent with opt-outs.

Ontario law currently allows families to block donations when donors have expressed regret. Trillium Gift of Life Network CEO Ronnie Gavsie said families overruled donors’ wishes in about 10% of cases in 2016, down from 21% in 2015, usually in exceptional circumstances. Trillium encourages people to discuss their wishes with family. Gavsie opposed presumed consent, citing public support for opt-in donation and research finding no evidence it increases donors.

S&P Global Platts will launch low-sulphur marine gasoil and diesel assessments at Asian bunkering ports from June 1, 2017, reflecting fuels with a maximum 0.1% sulphur content, as global sulphur limits tighten. Singapore low-sulphur marine gasoil sales rose nearly sixfold in three years to a record 1.14 million tonnes in 2016.

Motley Fool Money’s Oct. 2, 2025 credit-card roundup highlights the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card as one of the best cash-back cards for most people. It has no annual fee, unlimited 2% rewards on all purchases, a $200 bonus after $500 in spending within three months, and 12 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by an 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% variable APR. It also offers Visa Signature concierge service and up to $600 of cell-phone damage or theft protection with a $25 deductible. Applicants are advised to have good/excellent credit (670–850), though approval is not guaranteed.

The roundup also lists the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Card, offering unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% back on Capital One Travel hotels, vacation rentals, and rental cars, no annual or foreign-transaction fees, a $300 welcome package, and 15 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers. A Citi offer earns 2% on purchases, 5% through Citi Travel, and a $200 bonus after $1,500 in six-month spending, plus an 18-month balance-transfer promotion.

The site discloses that advertiser compensation may affect offer placement or coverage but not product ratings, and states that its editorial opinions are independent.

The author rejects the widespread South American belief that the Monroe Doctrine asserted U.S. superiority or a protectorate over other American republics, saying the misunderstanding hindered intercourse, capital, and trade. Secretary Root’s July 31 address to the Rio conference sought to dispel it, affirming no territorial gains, no sovereignty over others, equal rights for all republics, and shared prosperity rather than domination. Root also urged cooperation, anti-colonization, peace, justice, and an all-American public opinion to prevent war and European military burdens. The address was acclaimed across South America. Argentine minister Doctor Drago similarly described U.S. policy as opposing oppression and European control without superiority or preponderance. The author notes South American honors for prominent Americans, Brazil’s naming of the conference building “Palacio Monroe,” and thanks to the governments and peoples visited for their hospitality. He also recalls his December 5, 1905 message warning that forced collection of debts from American republics could cause embarrassment and permanent territorial occupation.

The speaker praises a teammate as a skilled, positionally strong player who controls the game and consistently makes the right plays with the puck. They describe Carolina as a family-friendly place they enjoy living, noting the team atmosphere, growing fan support after a winning stretch, and hopes that success will turn supporters into season-ticket holders. They believe the team can attract Canadian fans and promote hockey in smaller and southern markets through entertaining, higher-scoring games and continued winning. The speaker also highlights increased youth participation in places such as Tampa and encourages more children to play hockey. Hoping to finish their career in Carolina, they believe the team’s depth, emerging stars, and ability to challenge other teams will continue attracting players.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth-generation farmer at Boglily Farm near Kirkaldy, has embraced social media to promote The Buffalo Farm, share farming life and offer deals. The farm markets buffalo meat to health-conscious consumers. Its 2016 Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Award for buffalo fillet steak enhanced credibility and opened doors with major clients. Entries for the 2018 awards were invited from Scotland’s food and drink sector.

A white van deliberately mounted a curb south of Finch Avenue and struck pedestrians along Yonge Street, killing at least two people and injuring at least 10. Witnesses described the driver zigzagging at high speed and apparently targeting people. The driver and van were taken into custody; the driver threatened officers and said “kill me.” Police blocked off the area, launched an investigation and advised the public to stay away. Sunnybrook Hospital received 10 patients, including two fatalities, and North York General received four. Emergency responders and hospital staff were praised, while authorities reported no apparent connection to the G7 meetings or public-security threat.

Researchers developed Waldo, an AI tool that scans Reddit posts for reports of harmful cannabis side effects. Trained on 10,000 manually reviewed posts, Waldo analyzed more than 430,000 posts and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing adverse effects. In a reviewed sample of 250 flagged posts, 86% described problematic cannabis experiences. Waldo outperformed ChatGPT by producing fewer false positives, though researchers caution that its effectiveness for other products is uncertain and ethical use would require privacy protections.

The Trump administration withdrew the United States from UN negotiations on a global migration compact, citing concerns that the process could undermine U.S. sovereignty and immigration law. The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops expressed disappointment and urged reconsideration, emphasizing international cooperation and protections for refugees and other vulnerable migrants. Catholic teaching recognizes national authority over borders but also obligations to uphold human rights and accommodate migration.

Three days of UN negotiations in Puerto Vallarta advanced a nonbinding framework for the planned 2018 Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration. Priorities included migrant children’s education, support for countries hosting migrants and refugees, prevention of labor exploitation, and continued humanitarian assistance. Pope Francis supported the negotiations and called participants to welcome, protect, promote and integrate migrants and refugees.

Immigrationrestriction advocates welcomed the U.S. decision, arguing that the proposed compact was too broad and could conflict with U.S. laws on unauthorized employment and border detention. UN officials said an international framework was necessary while implementation remained a sovereign-state responsibility. Experts said global migration requires international cooperation and that wealthy nations, including the United States and Europe, should assume greater responsibility.

Edmonton officials say a calcium chloride pilot on 2,800 kilometres of streets, sidewalks and bike paths saved $4.2 million in operating costs and reduced sand use by 68%. Engineer Arthur Potts told council costs to private vehicle owners would be ten times the savings and the salt could rust vehicle parts, damage concrete and affect bridges. Residents reported increased rust, while officials dispute Potts’s claims but acknowledge the chemical and inhibitor were not tested in Edmonton. Environmental monitoring remains incomplete, and collision data is unavailable. The committee will consider continued use, specialized equipment and possible fall funding.

King Edward VI Grammar School’s quiz team placed second in the national schools University Challenge, losing 315–280 to Southend High School for Boys after missing four questions. Headmaster James Lascelles praised their confidence and development.

Indian Railways requires trains and eateries in malls and theatres to display “if no bill, your food is free,” aiming to deter overcharging. IRCTC is promoting the policy, deploying 120 inspectors and planning more. Overcharging prompted over 7,000 complaints last year and stricter vendor enforcement, including fines, licence cancellations, and contract terminations.

Hascall Steel Company is a US steel service center offering cold-reduced, blanked, slit, flat-rolled, hot-rolled black, aluminized, and coated steel. It processes inventory to customer specifications, using trained technicians and in-house multipoint laboratory testing. The company has served customers for over 45 years and emphasizes quality assurance, competitive rates, shorter lead times, and reduced supply-chain costs.

The government shutdown has intensified the U.S. air traffic controller shortage, with thousands expected to work without pay calling out sick and staffing reportedly cut by 50% in some areas. Airports including Newark, Phoenix, Denver and Los Angeles have experienced staffing shortages and flight delays, while safety experts have linked understaffing to near misses.

The shutdown compounds a longstanding problem: at the start of 2025, 285 of 313 FAA facilities—91%—met recommended staffing levels, with New York and Long Island particularly strained. Training is lengthy, costly and rigorous, requiring 16 months to several years; about one-third of trainees wash out. The pandemic disrupted coaching, many experienced controllers retired, and workers must retire by 56, while the FAA will not hire applicants older than 31.

Candidates must be U.S. citizens under 31 and meet medical, security, testing, English and education or experience requirements; fewer than 10% are accepted into training. Qualified controllers earn an average of $144,580 annually. The BLS projects 3% job growth from 2023 to 2033 and 2,200 openings annually, despite long hours, unpredictable shifts and mental-health concerns.

Tesla’s Form 8-K dated February 28, 2019, disclosed that the standard Model 3, offering 220 miles of range, was now available for $35,000. A Standard Range Plus Model 3 with 240 miles of range and premium interior features was priced at $37,000 before incentives. Tesla shifted vehicle sales worldwide to online only, began winding down many stores, and allowed returns within seven days or 1,000 miles for a full refund. It expected online sales and other efficiencies to reduce vehicle prices by about 6% on average. Firmware upgrades were announced to increase the Long Range Rear-Wheel Drive Model 3’s range to 325 miles, raise the Model 3 Performance’s top speed to 162 mph, and add about 5% peak power to Model 3 vehicles. Tesla said it did not expect first-quarter 2019 profitability but considered second-quarter profitability likely.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU introduces Ampere-generation features for HPC, AI, and data analytics. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support larger mixed-precision operations and deliver up to 16 times the peak performance of standard FP32 FMA operations. In cuSOLVER, the Tensor Core Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver supports FP32, FP16 with input scaling, BF16, and TF32. Across 37 SuiteSparse tests, TF32 produced the fastest and most robust results, with geometric-mean speedups over the FP64 solver of 2.0× for TF32, 1.9× for FP16, and 1.8× for BF16; speedups reached 4× for large complex matrices. A prior V100 fusion study achieved a 3.5× solver speedup, while the same technology tripled Summit’s HPL-AI performance.

A100 supports 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, requiring two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zero-value computations, doubling math throughput and reducing data footprint and bandwidth by half. NVIDIA’s pruning recipe—dense training, structured pruning, and fine-tuning—produced virtually no inference-accuracy loss across dozens of tested networks. Training acceleration requires introducing sparsity early and remains an active research area.

The GPU combines 192 KB per SM of L1 cache and shared memory, up from 128 KB on V100, and includes separate FP32 and INT32 cores that can operate simultaneously at full throughput. Its HBM2 subsystem provides 40 GB of memory and 1555 GB/s of bandwidth, more than 1.7 times V100’s bandwidth. The 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s and provides 2.3 times its bandwidth. L2 residency controls prioritize persistent data, while compute data compression can improve DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and effective L2 capacity by up to four, four, and two times, respectively. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files.

Deep-learning optimizations include sharing data across all 32 threads in a warp, larger Tensor Core instructions, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies that bypass L1 and the register file, and up to 164 KB of shared memory per SM. Together, these features reduce instructions, register accesses, memory traffic, and synchronization overhead. CUDA 11 adds support for these features through Tensor Core APIs, task graphs, asynchronous copies and barriers, L2 residency controls, cooperative groups, and Multi-Instance GPU management.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can divide an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory-controller, and DRAM pathways. GPU and Compute Instances provide quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, simultaneous context execution, Volta-style MPS support, and migration between compatible instances to improve utilization and reduce hardware fragmentation.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links, 600 GB/s of total GPU bandwidth, peer-memory access, and improved error detection and recovery. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 at 31.5 GB/s per direction and SR-IOV virtualization. Additional reliability features include fault attribution, isolation, containment, and remote page-fault reporting. Other accelerators include a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow and stereo-disparity accelerator, improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s of bidirectional interconnect bandwidth and up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators. It is stated to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and includes high-speed InfiniBand networking and software for AI, analytics, and HPC deployment through CUDA, NGC containers, and related tools. An appendix explains neural-network pruning, the benefits and challenges of fine- versus coarse-grained sparsity, and A100’s balanced 2:4 structured-sparsity approach.

The paper introduces T-Tamer, a model-agnostic framework for balancing conflicting objectives such as accuracy, latency, and cost in cascaded inference. It represents bi-objective trade-offs as a weighted sum of losses and formulates routing and termination as costly exploration over directed acyclic graphs whose nodes are sub-models and whose edges encode precedence, costs, and performance dependencies.

The paper proves an information-theoretic impossibility for no-recall strategies: even with only two models and bounded distributions, they cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to the offline optimum. This establishes fundamental limitations of confidence-threshold and similar heuristics.

For recall-based strategies, the paper derives an optimal dynamic-indexing policy for a directed line. The policy maintains the best observed loss, uses precomputed dynamic thresholds to decide whether to continue, and returns the best model inspected. Dynamic programming computes the policy efficiently, with constant-time decisions per visited node.

Dynamic indexing is extended to directed trees through subtree contraction and to the transitive closure of a directed line by considering all possible next models. These generalizations remain theoretically optimal and computable in polynomial time, while requiring linear inference time per input.

T-Tamer implements this framework as a data-driven learner that uses input-output pairs from all sub-models, updates performance beliefs at inference time, and computes routing and termination decisions without requiring case-specific retraining. Experiments on synthetic data and vision and NLP early-exit workloads show favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs, including reducing vision latency to 45% of the original with less than 7% accuracy sacrifice and reducing language-model latency by up to 90%.

**Summary**

This medRxiv preprint describes an intervention research study of a Training of Trainers (TOT) cascade for maternal and newborn health (MNH) in-service training in Palghar district, western Maharashtra (2019–2022), a scale-up of an earlier Pune pilot (2016–19).

**Background:** A competent public health workforce requires continual in-service training and professional development. Passive didactic methods such as lectures have little effect on learning outcomes, whereas case-based learning, clinical simulation, skills practice and feedback improve knowledge, skills and confidence. The TOT model strengthens workforce capacity through carefully selected trainers who acquire, transfer and sustain knowledge and skills, and qualified trainers can act as facility-based mentors. Evidence on trainer selection and TOT pedagogies in India is limited.

**Setting:** Palghar has a population of 2,990,116, mostly tribal communities in six of eight rural blocks, with high-risk factors including low birthweight, teenage pregnancy and anaemia. Its primary health system comprises 46 Primary Health Centres and 311 Health Sub Centres.

**Methods – Phase 1 (preparing for scale-up):** Eight of 38 Pune pilot participants (seven General Nurse Midwives and one doctor) were selected as Core Trainers (CTs) for their teaching skills and commitment. Training content was adapted to add local-context subjects (low birthweight management, anaemia, malnutrition) and to include additional cadres (medical officers, staff nurses, community health officers, GNMs, ANMs). Materials were reviewed and endorsed by the State Family Welfare Bureau. CTs received a four-day refresher plus virtual continuous learning sessions over three months, including lectures, clinical skill demonstrations, critical feedback and a session on becoming an effective trainer.

**Methods – Phase 2 (building a local cadre of master trainers, MTs), six steps:** (1) Pre-TOT screening of 48 candidates on work profile, training experience, commitment and teaching skill demonstration yielded 32 selected (25 medical doctors, seven GNMs); (2) TOT using adult-learner-centric, simulation-based methods with pre- and post-assessments (written exam, mannequin-based observation, teaching checklist) resulted in 18 MTs scoring ≥85% and 14 scoring 70–84%; (3) staggered induction, pairing intermediate-scoring MTs with highest scorers until independent; (4) continuous support from one Pune CT per batch of 20–25, with clinical guidance, pedagogy coaching and reverse demonstration; (5) three virtual quality-assessment and feedback sessions by UK experts, who identified initial difficulties with case-based teaching and noted rapid corrective improvement; (6) virtual refresher sessions on key MNH skills (partograph, eclampsia, newborn resuscitation, abdominal palpation) over ten months starting six months after TOT, using the ECHO virtual platform. A mixed-methods design was used, with Excel analysis of quantitative data and thematic analysis of process documentation, observations and interviews (UK experts n=3, Pune CTs n=5, Palghar MTs n=12); ethics approval was obtained.

**Results:** Each of the six steps had distinct advantages. Post-training scores for 463 health providers (505 trained) rose significantly: clinical knowledge 66.1%→79.3%, abdominal palpation 36.4%→75.5%, newborn resuscitation 35.4%→74.5%, eclampsia management 28.7%→84.2% (all P=0.000). Palghar MTs reported three gains: increased clinical competency (internalising protocols, leadership and mentoring roles, use of DR ABC and SBAR referral practices, abandonment of harmful practices), increased confidence as trainers applying adult-learning pedagogy, and career growth through recognition and motivation. Cadre breakdown of the 505 trained: 304 ANMs, 73 CHOs, 66 medical officers, 38 GNMs, 18 LHVs, six staff nurses.

**Discussion:** Given India's projected shortfall of about 0.7 million skilled health workers by 2030, the cascade of Pune CTs, Palghar MTs and health providers demonstrated a way to upskill existing public health staff. Key elements identified were right selection of trainers, appropriate adult-learner-centric and simulation-based pedagogy, a hybrid virtual/in-person platform that worked during COVID-19, longer time frames with supportive supervision beyond a one-off TOT, and enabling conditions (embedded refresher training, supplies, infrastructure, accreditation, protected time for trainers), since attrition is likely without them. Limitations noted: no systematic long-term evaluation of retention of competency or MNH care effects, and costing research is needed for scaling up and institutionalisation.

Astrophysical evidence—including unexpectedly large galaxy-cluster velocity dispersions and discrepancies between spiral-galaxy rotation curves and stellar masses—indicates a missing mass component. Cold dark matter (CDM) remains the leading enduring model because its non-relativistic particles permit rapid small-scale structure formation, but simulations still face the core-cusp, missing-satellites, too-many-satellites, and too-big-to-fail problems. Other candidates include axion-like particles, primordial black holes, warm and self-interacting dark matter, and modified gravity.

Constraints on dark matter are derived from the CMB power spectrum, hot gas in galaxy clusters, cosmic shear, and gravitational lensing. Candidate searches include collider, direct-detection, and indirect-detection experiments, for which no dark matter particles have yet been observed. Coordination among astronomy, cosmology, astroparticle physics, and particle physics is therefore essential.

The ESCAPE Dark Matter Test Science Project provides an EOSC-based platform for storing and sharing FAIR data, software, and workflows through the ESCAPE Data Lake, Open Source Scientific Software Repository, and Virtual Research Environment (VRE). It supports reproducible analyses and the production of dark-matter summary plots comparing constraints from different experiments. Supported efforts include ATLAS searches for a \(Z'\) dilepton resonance and t-channel semi-visible jets, neither of which produced a new signal over background; DarkSide-50 liquid-argon analyses for high- and low-mass WIMPs; Fermi-LAT searches using machine-learning background models for dwarf spheroidal galaxies and brown dwarfs; and a KM3NeT instrument-response tool also used with CTA data. Additional reusable resources include the Baler machine-learning compression tool, Aladin Lite, Gammapy, and Virtual Observatory tutorials.

Astrophysical constraints can be connected to particle-physics results through several observables. Gravitational-lensing image distortions and flux ratios can constrain CDM and warm-dark-matter free-streaming lengths, particle masses, and SIDM interaction cross-sections through halo substructure and core-collapse signatures, although modelling degeneracies remain. Dwarf spheroidal galaxies provide favorable targets for gamma-ray searches because they have high dark-matter densities and limited astrophysical backgrounds. Their expected annihilation flux combines particle-physics terms with the astrophysical J-factor, which depends on the squared line-of-sight dark-matter density and is affected by uncertain stellar membership, halo profiles, and unresolved substructure.

Existing tools include pyHalo and lenstronomy for lens modelling; GAMBIT’s DarkBit and CosmoBit modules for jointly fitting particle-physics, astrophysical, and cosmological constraints; AxionLimits for summary plots of ultralight particles; and the SuperCDMS Dark Matter Limit Plotter for interactive comparison with existing limits. The review aims primarily at astronomers and describes efforts to incorporate astronomical searches and constraints into ESCAPE services, supporting open, reproducible, and collaborative combinations of complementary astronomy and particle-physics limits.

Knee injuries and joint damage accumulate with age and can cause pain, limited mobility and surgery. Healthy weight, regular activity, strong supporting muscles, and flexibility can reduce the risk of joint, cartilage and ligament damage. Recommended exercises include strengthening the hamstrings, quads, glutes and hip flexors, stretching, and low-impact cardio such as cycling or swimming, which supports circulation and cartilage health without excessive impact.

Persistent knee pain may require physiotherapy for diagnosis and a tailored treatment plan. Strength and flexibility exercises, often adapted to the injury, can improve recovery, restore range of motion, prevent recurrence and sometimes delay or avoid surgery. Staying active is important, although pain should not be ignored. Online physiotherapy may offer greater convenience.

Most people requiring knee replacement are aged 50 or older, with about half over 70. Wear and tear, ageing and conditions such as osteoarthritis contribute to the need for surgery. When a knee is severely damaged, surgery can significantly improve quality of life, though it carries risks including infection and deep vein thrombosis. Most replacements now last for decades: more than four in five total knee replacements and seven in ten unicondylar replacements are expected to last 25 years. Physiotherapy and regular exercises can improve postoperative recovery and protect the new knee.

The ADS868xW supports standard SPI and multi-device daisy-chain operation. A standard interface uses CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0, with RST tied to DVDD and RVS optionally monitored. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, are configured identically, and pass data serially through SDO-0 and SDI. An optimal frame requires 32 × N SCLK capture edges, data returns from device N toward device 1, and system throughput decreases proportionally as devices are added.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST input can provide an application reset or full power-on reset. ACQ acquires the analog input, while a rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion. Further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored until conversion finishes, after which the device returns to ACQ. The host can monitor the RVS transition or wait for the maximum conversion time.

Data-transfer frames begin with a falling CONVST/CS edge and end with its subsequent rising edge. During the frame, commands shift in through SDI and output data shift out MSB-first through SDO-x. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames cannot write commands but can provide output data, while in longer frames the last 32 input bits form the command. The device supports byte and half-word reads and writes. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device addresses, range and alarm flags, and parity.

Four legacy SPI protocols, single or dual SDO output, and source-synchronous modes are supported. SPI-00-S is used after power-up or reset, and other SPI modes are selected through SDI_CTL_REG. SDO_CTL_REG configures output mode, clock source, and optional dual-SDO operation.

Nine configuration registers provide device identification, reset and power control, SPI and SDO control, output formatting, input-range selection, alarm status, and programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis. An eight-channel industrial input-module example combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 to support voltage, current, and thermistor sensing.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires specified decoupling. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital signals, uses close bypass and reference capacitors, and provides low-impedance ground paths.

This continuation disclosure concerns absorbent hygiene products and an absorbent core for collecting urine, fecal material, blood, menses and vaginal fluids. The core has front, back and crotch portions with substantially interconnected channels that extend longitudinally and across the core’s width to rapidly distribute liquid from discharge areas. Channel geometries may include funnel, U-, V-, pie- and semi-hourglass shapes, varying widths and depths, and multiple interconnected or disconnected channels. Preferably, channels between bonded nonwoven webs are substantially free of three-dimensional absorbent material and superabsorbent polymer. They are intended to limit localized saturation and improve perceived dryness and comfort. The core may also provide three-stage distribution: fastest through channels, slower through three-dimensional absorbent material and slowest through superabsorbent polymer.

The core may be used in disposable diapers or pants, incontinence products, sanitary napkins and panty liners between topsheet and backsheet. Contrasting colors can make channels visible before and after use. An acquisition and distribution layer may be positioned so channel ends or connecting portions remain exposed to improve distribution and reduce material use.

To manufacture the core, a first nonwoven web, three-dimensional absorbent material and second nonwoven web are applied to a vacuum mold containing an inverse-shaped 3D insert. Vacuum evacuates the insert area, forming channels substantially free of absorbent material. Optional bonding creates differing bonding-strength zones so selected regions may separate during swelling while stronger regions preserve channel integrity.

The passage defines sector trading as investing in securities within a specific economic sector, such as technology or energy, and notes that it is generally riskier than broad-market investing. An industry is a specific branch of economic activity, while a sector groups multiple industries; S&P divides the stock market into 11 sectors.

Drawing on a 2015 JP Morgan study of the Russell 3000 from 1980–2015, the article examines catastrophic losses, returns, and success rates across sectors. A catastrophic loss is defined as a decline of at least 70% from a peak followed by recovery of less than 60% of that loss. Telecom, information technology, and energy had the most such losses, while utilities had the fewest; overall, 40% of the stock universe experienced a catastrophic loss. Utilities, information technology, energy, and materials are identified as the worst sectors by median returns, although rankings vary by metric. The study finds that a small number of spectacular winners enabled strong index returns despite many poor-performing stocks, with the median stock producing negative lifetime returns. It advocates inverse thinking: studying failures and avoiding losers may be as valuable as studying winners, illustrating this principle through Charlie Munger’s ideas and Nassim Taleb’s barbell strategy.

The paper studies inverse problems for complex systems in which governing physical parameters cannot be observed directly, but experimental observations can be linked to them through a process model. It introduces the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP): given repeated observations generated by an unknown distribution of parameters, find a parameter distribution whose pushforward under the observation map reproduces the observed output distribution.

Because the observation map is generally not one-to-one, the eSIP can have multiple solutions. The paper adopts a Bayesian formulation that uses prior information to select a unique posterior distribution. Using measure disintegration, it represents the posterior through conditional measures concentrated on generalized contours—the parameter values compatible with each observed output. Under compactness, regularity, and geometric assumptions on the observation map, these contours are smooth manifolds and the conditional integrals become surface integrals.

Under suitable absolute-continuity and differentiability conditions, the posterior has an explicit density analogous to the nonparametric form of Bayes’ theorem. Its density is generally continuous almost everywhere. The posterior obtained from a uniform prior has maximum entropy among absolutely continuous solutions, making the uniform prior a default when no informed prior is available. The paper also presents a random-sampling method based on importance reweighting; under general conditions, its estimator is asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent, with asymptotic variance and error estimates.

The posterior is intended for estimating probabilities of parameter events and forecasting new quantities of interest, rather than producing point estimates or recovering the unknown data-generating distribution. Examples include an exponential-decay model whose posterior forms ridges along observation contours, a random point in a disk, and a discrete inverse problem. The eSIP differs from classical calibration and single-trial data-assimilation problems because its output variability arises from repeated experiments with randomly varying physical parameters rather than primarily from observational noise.

AMD’s Security Processor (ASP) serves as the root of trust for detecting and verifying AMD-signed boot firmware. For runtime firmware updates, OEM/ODMs normally retain the update root of trust, optionally using Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) co-signing; unless AMD Platform Secure Boot is enabled, they also remain responsible for detection of their own firmware. Early OEM/ODM firmware must restrict ROM access before untrusted code executes.

SFS is disabled by default and must be enabled through BIOS configuration. When co-signing is required, the customer supplies an RSA public key during early boot, immediately after SMM setup and before `BOOT_DONE`; the key cannot be changed afterward. Updates must carry an AMD signature and, when configured, the customer’s RSA-PSS co-signature. If early trusted code is compromised, its ability to replace the co-signing key can undermine this protection.

Systems boot with baseline firmware, and patches are applied at runtime. Updates are nonpersistent across warm or cold reboots, must be reapplied, and, when multiple packages are used, applied sequentially. Multi-socket systems route patches through the first socket’s ASP for application to appropriate sockets. Each patch checks applicable firmware and patch levels and may modify registers, firmware images, or firmware components.

SEV updates are committed automatically, requiring reboot to revert. SNP updates require all package pages to be HV-FIXED using `RMPUPDATE`. Attestation evidence is obtained through interfaces such as SPDM or DPE, while certain restricted firmware components are not modified. Update packages must validate required dependency versions and apply completely or not at all.

SFS commands use a 2 MB-aligned `TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER`, followed by the update package and any co-signature header and signature. The ASP protects the buffer from x86 access, verifies the customer and AMD signatures, executes the validated patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Packages align with AGESA releases, use `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg` naming, and must match the system’s specific firmware and patch-level combination. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, although some operations may require brief quiescence or VM restart.

The passage documents AMD AGESA initialization and host-environment interfaces from system reset through OS handoff, suspend, and resume. Early routines perform minimal processor and FCH initialization, configure platform settings, and allocate aligned execution-cache regions from nonvolatile storage under specified address, size, and boundary rules. BSP and AP cores execute separate tasks. Later phases perform full processor and DRAM initialization, support memory interleaving, ECC, training, context restoration, UMA allocation, and AMP features, configure MTRRs, transfer HOB artifact data, and initialize display and controller hardware. Late initialization generates ACPI and DMI tables and prepares final processor power states and registers.

Suspend procedures save critical processor context in nonvolatile and volatile storage; resume procedures restore memory and silicon state, reload registers, and prepare for OS restart. The host environment must provide stack setup, memory, and required call-outs for buffer allocation, deallocation and lookup, resets, SPD reads, and application-processor task execution, waiting, and idling. Optional hooks support IDS data, heap relocation, memory timings and voltages, training, FCH/GNB customization, and platform-specific controls.

Legal documents filed in Los Angeles by Isaiah Silva, Frances Bean Cobain’s former husband, allege Courtney Love and others conspired to murder him to recover Kurt Cobain’s 1959 Martin guitar. Silva says he received the guitar in his divorce settlement and alleges Love’s manager, an actor and another man entered his home on June 3, 2016, pounding on his locked bedroom door while demanding police open it. Denver snapped a two-game skid by routing the Joe Burrow-less Bengals 28-3 on Monday night. Bo Nix delivered his best passing performance of the season, while Denver’s defense controlled Cincinnati and a 101-yard rushing performance ended the Broncos’ 37-game regular-season streak without a 100-yard rusher. Free-agent addition Albert Engram had three catches for 18 yards and a drop on six targets, and coach Sean Payton wants him more involved against nickel defenses. All four Denver opponents have opened games with field goals, and the Bengals face Detroit and Green Bay next.

Researchers at Clarkson University studied older adults averaging age 75 performing a six-minute walking test before and after cognitively tiring tasks. They measured gait speed and stride length and related these to self-reported mood, motivation, and energy. Gait remained unchanged for the first 30 seconds after cognitive fatigue, but walking speed and stride length later decreased significantly among participants reporting greater cognitive fatigue, not reduced physical energy. The findings were presented at Experimental Biology 2018 in San Diego.

WWE has five-year linear-TV deals keeping “Raw” on USA Network and moving “Smackdown Live” to Fox. Chief Brand Officer Stephanie McMahon said WWE may distribute its flagship programs digitally after those deals expire. Digital platforms could help WWE reach younger viewers, attract sponsors, promote its other digital properties and WWE Network, and potentially create new subscribers.
