A 16-year-old driver, Bradd Rudolph, failed to stop at a rural “T” intersection on a dark, foggy night, crossed a ditch and embankment, and plunged into Bayou Bartholomew. Two back-seat passengers, including 15-year-old Michael Hill, drowned. Hill’s father sued the Morehouse Parish Police Jury and its insurer. The trial court found that Rudolph was intoxicated and traveling about 65 mph, but also that the police jury knew the intersection was dangerous and had failed to maintain a double-arrow warning sign. It assigned 20% fault to the police jury and 80% to Rudolph.

On appeal, the court found that the missing sign would have been visible in Rudolph’s headlights and could have increased his reaction time, making the police jury’s failure a contributing cause of the accident. The court affirmed liability, increased the police jury’s fault allocation from 20% to 35%, reduced Rudolph’s share to 65%, and affirmed the $150,000 general-damages award as not an abuse of discretion. Costs were assessed against the defendants.

Harvey may have damaged or destroyed up to a dozen Texas Gulf Coast habitats, including marshes, nesting sites, and coastlines. Whooping crane feeding grounds were damaged, and as few as 10 of 60 Attwater prairie chickens are believed to have survived. Oyster beds sustained losses, while freshwater inflows may have injured dolphins. Scientists linked stronger storms to climate change.

The study assessed open access and self-archiving potential for 1,897 clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers published between 2010 and 2020. Using Unpaywall, 54% were openly accessible, while 46% (871) were closed. Shareyourpaper identified sufficient self-archiving information for 85% of closed publications (736), all of which permitted archiving an accepted or published version in an institutional repository once applicable embargoes had elapsed; most embargoes were 12 months. Exclusive repository access was found for 143 publications, indicating substantial unrealized green open access potential. The automated, open-tool approach could help institutions identify and deposit eligible papers at scale. Limitations included the accuracy and coverage of Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper, exclusion of some additional archiving routes, and the lack of direct verification of existing repository deposits’ permissions, versions, or locations.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 3% and Alphabet spending concerns weighed on markets. Toronto’s index dropped 75.06 points, but gains in gold and materials stocks, including Barrick Gold, limited losses.

Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne’s suggestion that older white voters should stop voting so younger people and minorities could prevail is condemned as ageist, racist, and divisive identity politics. The passage acknowledges differences in voter turnout but argues Wynne should encourage all groups to participate rather than demonize one demographic, especially given her advocacy of an inclusive, colour-blind society.

Global stocks rose after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen said the U.S. central bank could raise rates as soon as March, citing economic strength, job-market improvement and modest inflation. European benchmarks gained, most Asian markets advanced, and U.S. futures were little changed; bank shares benefited. Markets assigned a 34% chance of a March rate hike. Chinese inflation increased, raising concerns about tighter policy, though analysts saw no sign of a policy change. The dollar strengthened, while U.S. and Brent crude prices fell.

Natural gas settled Tuesday at $3.27/MMBtu within a descending wedge. European LNG demand supports U.S. exports, but North American surpluses weigh on prices; seasonal softness and Canadian supply shocks elevate volatility. Traders Union offers forex broker reviews and ratings.

Digital laggards tightly control and silo data, favor experience-based “culture of genius” over evidence, and often set poorly grounded goals that discourage measurement and weaken alignment with strategy. Entrenched leadership, resource constraints, skills gaps, and power dynamics can prevent data-driven practices, although these organizations are not doomed to stall.

Digital leaders emphasize transparent data access, meaningful metrics, continuous tracking, and ambitious measurable goals. Standardized APIs are far more common among digital leaders than laggards (88% versus 27%). At leading firms, measurement supports employee autonomy, innovation, experimentation, and risk-taking rather than rigidly controlling work. Transparent, top-down and bottom-up goal-setting connects teams to shared organizational objectives, while common data models and access improve collaboration. Leaders must balance analysis with human judgment so data does not become an excessive burden.

A digitally transforming retailer upgraded its data systems after an acquisition and rapidly launched real-time sales reporting. Sales data now reaches the dashboard three times daily, enabling leaders to make faster decisions about inventory, marketing, supply chains, and other areas.

At digital leaders, beliefs, values, and daily behaviors reinforce a strong data culture centered on learning, transparency, measurement, and risk-taking. Laggards often show gaps between stated values and actual practices. Organizations fall into four maturity patterns: data novices, insight-ready firms, tech-enabled firms, and data-reliant firms that may over-rely on data and discourage critical thinking. Each can build on its strengths through targeted cultural, operational, and technical changes.

Renewed interest in psychedelics supports drug-facilitated psychotherapy. A pooled analysis of six Phase II MDMA-assisted therapy trials found 54% of patients no longer met PTSD criteria, with acceptable safety, prompting FDA breakthrough therapy designation. A Phase III multisite study confirmed its efficacy and safety for severe PTSD versus placebo plus therapy.

On January 28, 2016, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K announcing its fourth-quarter 2015 and year ended December 31, 2015 financial results. Exhibit 99.1 contains the announcement, and Exhibit 99.2 provides information on non-GAAP financial measures.

Gary Gensler, a Senior Lecturer at MIT Sloan and advisor at the MIT Media Lab, opens 15.S12, a course on blockchain and money. The semester's two study questions are what blockchain is and why it might be a catalyst for change in finance. Polling the class, Gensler finds roughly 45% have owned cryptocurrency and about a third have worked on blockchain-related projects. Students are asked to anonymously write their semester goals on index cards, and results will be shared the following Tuesday. Student reactions to the assigned readings range from Tom's view that blockchain enables improved profitability to Alin's view that, from a technical standpoint, it is mostly hype, with little to show after ten years since Bitcoin's launch.

Tracing history, Gensler describes the internet's early layers—Ethernet, TCP/IP, and HTTP, associated with Tim Berners-Lee—and their commercialization through firms such as 3Com, Cisco, and Amazon. In 1995 PizzaNet became the first online pizza sale, but online payment was impossible. Cryptography, defined as communication in the presence of adversaries, developed from ancient ciphers through the Enigma machine (cracked by Polish mathematicians and later Turing) to 1970s public/private-key cryptography developed at MIT, which underpins both the internet and Bitcoin. SSL/TLS secures internet traffic, and early attempts such as David Chaum's failed. Pre-Bitcoin digital money included PayPal (1998), earlier failed currencies, innovations by Nick Szabo (smart contracts) and Adam Back (Hashcash), Alipay in China, and M-Pesa in Kenya, which converted mobile minutes into a currency for the unbanked and now has about 20 million Kenyan customers.

The core riddle, Gensler says, is how to move value peer to peer without a centralized intermediary. Satoshi Nakamoto's October 31, 2008 email proposed "a new electronic cash system that's fully peer-to-peer with no trusted third party." Gensler defines blockchain as time-stamped append-only logs forming an auditable database, noting that Satoshi did not invent it—Stuart Haber worked on it at Bell Labs in the early 1990s. Students are assigned to find the longest-running blockchain, running since the mid-1990s, with a New York Times clue. Blockchain rests on hash functions, digital signatures based on asymmetric cryptography, and consensus protocols that address the cost of trust and the Byzantine Generals problem, which Nakamoto solved. Gensler recounts that in May 2010 Laszlo offered 10,000 bitcoins (then worth about $41) for two pizzas, marking the first use of bitcoin as a medium of exchange; May 22 is now observed as Pizza Day. Blockchain technology, in his words, verifiably moves data on a decentralized network, trading higher consensus costs for lower reliance on central authorities, and the data moved can be money or executable code (smart contracts).

Turning to finance, Gensler notes money's roles as medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account, and describes finance as moving money and risk through intermediation, allocating and pricing, generating economic rents. Finance represents 7.5% of the US economy (about $1.5 trillion), with payment systems at $100–200 billion. Challenges include centralized intermediaries, fiat instability, legacy payment systems, interchange fees of 2.5–3%, and 1.7 billion unbanked people worldwide. Blockchain's own problems include performance and scalability (Bitcoin handles about 7 transactions per second versus Visa's 20,000–70,000), privacy and security since blockchains are public, interoperability, and governance difficulties in updating decentralized software. Gensler contrasts permissioned chains, where known participants control nodes (e.g., the Australian Securities Exchange using Hyperledger with three nodes, and the Depository Trust Company), with permissionless chains such as Bitcoin, noting crypto finance of about $200 billion—more than half Bitcoin—compared with global equity (~$80 trillion), bond markets (~$250 trillion), and gold (~$7 trillion).

On public policy, Gensler outlines illicit use, financial stability, capital controls, and investor protection and SEC oversight of initial coin offerings, recommending the "duck test" and the statute's wording. Incumbents are drawn to crypto's volatility, trading volumes, and spreads, citing Coinbase's 20 million accounts and Robinhood's 5 million free-trading members, while startups face asymmetric regulatory risk. The course is organized in three acts: fundamentals, a pivot to economics, and financial sector use cases, including payment systems, central bank digital currency, secondary market trading, venture capital and ICOs. Grading comprises 30% participation, two individual critical-reasoning write-ups, and a team project of three or four proposing a finance use case. Using Larry Lessig's framework of technology, markets, law, and social norms, Gensler plans to review both minimalists (Roubini, Krugman, Stiglitz, Buffett) and maximalists, aiming to separate assertion from hype; Lessig, attending as a student, expressed the view that blockchain could radically reduce the cost of trust and benefit developing nations.

Next week's questions cover money's roles and characteristics, fiat currency, ledgers and double-entry bookkeeping, and where Bitcoin fits in that history, with readings totaling under 50 pages including a short video; only Nakamoto's cover email is required. Gensler closes by noting that money is a social and economic consensus and blockchain may be a catalyst for change, and he recounts his career: 18 years at Goldman Sachs in investment banking, trading, and as co-CFO with responsibilities for Asia; Treasury assistant and undersecretary in the late 1990s during the Asian and Russian debt crises; work on the E-Signature bill with Senator McCain, currency redesign, Sarbanes-Oxley, serving as Hillary Clinton's CFO in the 2008 and 2016 campaigns; and running the CFTC post-crisis to bring transparency and central clearing to the swaps market. He joined MIT via Simon Johnson's Media Lab digital currency initiative and has three daughters.

The Cleveland Browns traded Joe Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick to the Bengals for a 2026 fifth-round pick, leaving rookie Shedeur Sanders and another quarterback on the active roster. Coach Kevin Stefanski said he would wait before deciding whether Sanders, the 144th pick in this year’s draft, will be the permanent No. 2. Sanders had served as the third-string and emergency quarterback through five games but was listed as No. 2 on this week’s unofficial depth chart. Stefanski also did not say whether Bailey Zappe will be activated to provide emergency-quarterback depth. Dillon Gabriel, who started after Flacco was benched, could receive help from Sanders and Zappe. Stefanski said the trade surprised him and that Cincinnati initiated contact. Deshaun Watson remains on the physically unable to perform list while rehabbing an Achilles injury.

A University of Michigan study of more than 2,000 older Americans found that 21% of women and 10% of men aged 50–64 meet criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, compared with 12% of women and 4% of men aged 65–80. Researchers used the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0, which assesses cravings, unsuccessful attempts to cut back, withdrawal, and social avoidance.

The study associated addiction with overweight status, fair or poor mental and physical health, and social isolation. Overweight women were more than 11 times as likely to meet the criteria, and overweight men 19 times as likely. People reporting isolation were more than three times as likely to meet the criteria.

Researchers suggested that 1980s marketing of low-fat and diet-focused processed foods to women may have contributed to the generational pattern. They also raised concerns that highly processed foods marketed as healthy may be especially appealing to people concerned about weight. Because children and adolescents consume higher proportions of calories from ultra-processed foods than today’s middle-aged adults did, future generations could face greater addiction risks, highlighting the importance of early intervention.

The Bank of England will retain the £5 polymer note and issue the £10 note in September despite objections over tallow. It delayed £20 contracts and launched consultation on plant-based alternatives for future £5 and £10 production.

Ireland is highly exposed to exchange rates: the weak euro draws record American tourists while weak sterling deters UK visitors. The euro has risen against the dollar from $1.05 to $1.18 on expectations of ending ECB quantitative easing and rising eurozone rates — appreciation the author sees as greater than ECB chief Mario Draghi would like, since ECB policy favours a low rate for export-led recovery. At a euro average of $1.35, parity against sterling could follow within 12–18 months, though ECB decisions and Brexit make the outlook uncertain. Tourism firms have little hedging scope; UK importers earn windfall profits and should hedge to lock them in, while weak sterling floods the market with cheap UK second-hand cars and makes UK exports a nightmare, so firms should incur costs in the currency of the country they sell into.

The article reviews career-transition research in higher education, noting that prior studies have emphasized organizational needs, rarely addressed education personnel, and seldom examined adaptation and effects from the perspectives of affected employees. It also identifies limited application of Schlossberg’s transition theory beyond students.

Using an interpretive, qualitative grounded-theory approach, the study examines career transitions among Indonesian lecturers and civil-servant education personnel who hold both their original positions and additional campus leadership duties. Six key informants were selected through maximum-variation snowball sampling: one lecturer and one education staff member from each of three types of state higher-education institutions. Data came from semi-structured interviews, career-history documents, observations, photographs, and recordings. Interview transcripts were analyzed iteratively in NVivo through open, axial, and selective coding.

The findings extend Schlossberg’s four transition factors—situation, self, support, and strategies—and show that they interact reciprocally. New tasks shape assessments of personal strengths and weaknesses, support from family, colleagues, and organizations, and the selection of strategies. Informants sought information for unfamiliar tasks and acted directly when familiar.

Career transitions produced changes in behavior, roles, learning, and perception. Reported behavioral changes included burnout, motivation, competence, self-discipline, and identity. Dual roles increased time-management and self-discipline demands, while employees sometimes sacrificed performance in their primary positions; organizational responsibility generally took priority. The study also identified two career anchors—competence and managerial ability—contrasting with the single-anchor assumption of career-anchor theory.

The article recommends careful organizational preparation for role changes, competency- and education-based functional appointments, clearer functional positions, and recognition of additional duties in performance assessments. Limitations include the study’s narrow institutional scope, limited generalizability, omission of race and gender, and potential researcher subjectivity.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reported that Bob Iger resigned from its Board of Directors on September 10, 2019. The filing was signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on September 13, 2019.

Qarlinngua, a massive pants-shaped sea arch in Nunavut’s Arctic, was confirmed by local sources and geologists after CBC North’s photograph prompted online skepticism. The formation stands over 50 metres high in the uninhabited Brodeur Peninsula on northern Baffin Island, roughly 80–90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay. It is reachable only by boat during a short summer window when sea ice permits travel.

Geologists identified layered sedimentary sandstone and explained that rising seas, wind and water gradually erode coastal cliffs to form natural arches. They noted that similar formations are uncommon in the Arctic, though more frequent farther south. Estimates of when Qarlinngua might collapse vary from decades to thousands of years; erosion of the cliff behind it could also produce new arches.

The remote site has recently attracted tourism interest. Arctic Bay Adventures is the only company offering tours, while Nunavut’s tourism department plans to promote the formation to affluent, older travellers despite expensive travel and limited seasonal access.

A player said he felt comfortable after being evaluated for a head injury, although he remained concerned about being run into the boards. A CT scan showed sufficient healing for him to play, and he said his risk was no different than it would be in September. He experienced minor cramping after travel but felt fine and planned to resume his normal routine at home. He credited his teammates and said he was thankful to contribute to the team’s Stanley Cup opportunity. Following a loss, he cited poor execution and a lack of passion, questioned the shot clock’s accuracy, and hoped for a strong start and sustained effort. The decision to arrange the scan followed a comment he made after learning of Doug’s injury, and the process reassured his family.
The judgment for Collis P. Huntington was affirmed with costs, on the opinion of the trial judge.

Mathematics anxiety is a global concern affecting children and adults. Defined as tension, worry, or fear that interferes with mathematics performance, it can cause avoidance of mathematical learning, disrupt classroom focus, and hinder mathematics achievement. The study used bibliometric analysis to examine research on mathematics anxiety in mathematics education from 2013 to 2023. Relevant articles were collected from Scopus, filtered and cleaned, and analyzed with VOSviewer and Biblioshiny; 324 journal articles remained for analysis.

Research output generally increased during the decade, with fluctuations in 2016 and 2020, and peaked at 56 documents in 2022. Social sciences accounted for 35.1% of publications and psychology for 30.7%. Keyword mapping identified seven clusters and 53 terms, showing connections between mathematics anxiety and cognitive and affective variables, including achievement, performance, motivation, beliefs, self-efficacy, gender differences, skills, teachers, and students. Thematic analysis found mathematics anxiety and math anxiety to remain dominant throughout the period.

The topic appeared in 168 journals. Frontiers in Psychology published the most articles, with 39 documents, while the ten leading journals were ranked between Q1 and Q3. Garcia-Santillan was the most productive author, with ten publications and 143 citations; Pekrun Reinhard and Goetz Thomas each had seven publications. Author collaboration was generally limited.

Seventy-eight countries contributed research, led by the United States with 62 documents, followed by the United Kingdom with 48 and Germany with 32. The United States had the broadest international collaboration network, while Germany received the most citations. Among 160 contributing institutions, the University of Barcelona ranked first with 23 documents, followed by the University of California and the University of Oxford with nine each. The study was limited to Scopus-indexed journal articles.

North Korea warned the U.S. of nuclear retaliation while displaying intercontinental and submarine-launched ballistic missiles at Kim Il-sung’s 105th-birthday parade. China warned that conflict could erupt at any moment and have no winner.

The application describes a detection-model training method, apparatus, storage medium, and terminal device for detecting target objects, including lesion targets and colorectal polyps. It addresses limited labeled medical-imaging data, costly physician annotation, and accuracy reductions caused by differences among hospitals.

An initial training model combines an initial detection model with an adaptive domain-classification model. Training data include labeled source-domain images containing target identifiers and unlabeled target-domain images, both with domain labels. A shared feature extractor feeds the detection and domain-classification modules. The models produce detection and domain-classification results, which are compared with the available labels through detection and adaptive loss functions. Model parameters are iteratively adjusted using optimization and, optionally, gradient reversal to produce domain-invariant features. Training ends upon convergence or after a preset number of updates.

The resulting final model detects whether an image contains a target and may also determine its type and location. In a colorectal-polyp embodiment, a CNN-based model detects and classifies polyps in images from a new hospital without requiring target-domain polyps to be manually labeled, thereby increasing usable training data and supporting more accurate cross-hospital deployment.

NVIDIA Corporation reported unaudited results for the quarter ended July 26, 2020. Second-quarter revenue was $3.866 billion, up 50% year over year, with operating income of $651 million, net income of $622 million, and diluted earnings per share of $0.99. Gross margin declined to 58.8% from 59.8%, reflecting a $161 million nonrecurring inventory step-up and $84 million of intangible amortization from the Mellanox acquisition. For the first half, revenue was $6.946 billion, net income was $1.539 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.47.

NVIDIA completed its $7.134 billion acquisition of Mellanox on April 27, 2020. The acquisition contributed about 14% of consolidated quarterly revenue and generated preliminary goodwill of $3.431 billion and intangible assets of $2.970 billion. Following a segment-reporting change, Graphics revenue rose 16% to $2.085 billion, while Compute & Networking revenue increased 130% to $1.781 billion. Gaming revenue rose 26% to $1.654 billion and Data Center revenue increased 167% to $1.752 billion; Professional Visualization and Automotive revenue declined 30% and 47%, respectively.

At quarter-end, cash and cash equivalents plus marketable securities totaled $10.981 billion, long-term debt was $6.960 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $13.914 billion. First-half operating cash flow was $2.476 billion, while business acquisitions used $7.171 billion. NVIDIA paid $197 million in dividends during the first half and had remaining stock-repurchase authorization of $7.24 billion through December 2022.

COVID-19 negatively affected professional visualization and automotive demand, while its duration and effects remained uncertain. NVIDIA also disclosed securities and derivative litigation concerning statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency-mining effects on GPU demand; no related loss accrual was recorded because losses were considered possible but not probable.

Teams should prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump-ball situations. In defensive situations, players should rotate early, watch the jumper’s eyes and hands, maintain contact after the tip, and use box, diamond, or “Y” alignments to deny, box out, or anticipate open areas. Even situations require boxing out, establishing inside position, and coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations. When the team has a height or jumping advantage, it can tip forward to its tallest player, maintain defensive balance, and transition into set or motion offense. Proven offensive plays include tipping back for possession, double tap, post split, jumper fly, forward fly, spread, tandem left, and loop, each using screens, cuts, or wing movement to create scoring or passing opportunities.

A May 25, 2001 collection of news clippings centered on Enron’s political influence, the troubled Dabhol power project in India, and broader energy-market developments.

The lead New York Times report detailed Curtis Hebert Jr.’s claim that Enron chairman Kenneth Lay offered continued Enron support if Hebert changed his position on electricity deregulation and transmission-grid access. Hebert said he refused; Lay denied linking Enron’s support to Hebert’s job or policy views. The report nevertheless described Enron’s extensive access to the Bush administration, including Lay’s campaign contributions, input on FERC nominees, and influence over transmission policy. Hebert was expected to be replaced as chairman by Pat Wood. The article also noted a FERC inquiry into complex electricity-market arbitrage involving Enron.

In India, Maharashtra State Electricity Board canceled its seven-year power-purchase agreement with Enron’s Dabhol Power Co., citing failure to deliver full capacity within three hours and alleging contract misrepresentation. Dabhol disputed the board’s legal authority, said it was owed roughly $48 million to $64 million for December and January power, and noted that related claims were already in arbitration. Negotiations continued through an Indian panel, although an expert said the panel lacked authority to impose a solution. Members disagreed over whether a judicial inquiry should precede renegotiation. Indian and state governments had guaranteed Dabhol payments and could face substantial obligations if the project ended. Bechtel, the project contractor and a minority shareholder, threatened to withdraw by May 31 over unpaid dues and stopped site work, while lenders withheld about $250 million in committed funds. The government considered possible NTPC or private-sector takeovers of Enron’s 65% stake, and Maharashtra was reported likely to pay April’s electricity bill under protest.

Additional coverage addressed California’s electricity crisis. A Los Angeles Times editorial urged Governor Gray Davis and the Bush administration to cooperate, seek legal remedies against generators, and impose temporary wholesale price controls. A San Francisco Chronicle report said Davis’s job approval had fallen 18 points since January, while rival gubernatorial candidates also trailed him, and highlighted California Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s threats to prosecute energy generators.

Markets closed moderately higher as investors weighed economic weakness and Senate political changes before Alan Greenspan’s speech; the Dow gained 0.2%, the Nasdaq 1.7%, and the S&P 500 0.3%. Portland General Electric reported record wholesale-power revenue but sharply higher electricity and fuel costs.

Other articles reported that India and Australia signed an energy and mining cooperation protocol with proposed Australian investment of $3 billion; argued that the internet was transforming corporate structures despite the dot-com downturn; described renewed interest among MBAs and executives in energy careers; and detailed El Paso chairman William Wise’s agreement to testify in a FERC hearing over alleged manipulation of California natural-gas prices.

Tropical Depression 02W made landfall in the eastern Visayas on April 15, 2017, then weakened while crossing the Philippines and entering the South China Sea. NASA’s Terra satellite observed an elongated cloud area over the remnants on April 17. JTWC said wind shear and dry air were expected to prevent re-intensification.

Apple removed several apps that document or track Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity, including Eyes Up, DEICER, ICEBlock, and Migrant Insider, amid claims by U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi that such tools endanger ICE officers. Apple did not explain the removals but reportedly cited a prohibition on “defamatory, discriminatory, or mean-spirited” content in DEICER’s case. Google also removed ICE-monitoring apps and said it considers ICE officers a vulnerable group.

Developers are challenging the bans. Eyes Up developer Mark says he will appeal every rejection and that the app remains available through Google Play and its website. ICEBlock developer Joshua Aaron says the app has a legal team and will fight Apple’s decision.

Legal experts told WIRED that the removed apps publish truthful, constitutionally protected speech about matters of public interest. The bans have also intensified the Trump administration’s threats against Aaron and raised concerns about Apple’s control over its closed device ecosystem, which researchers describe as making the company a single point of failure for app availability and free expression.

The Supreme Court heard argument on whether the Double Jeopardy Clause permits separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. Although lesser-included offenses generally cannot receive both, precedent allows cumulative punishment when Congress clearly indicates that intent. Barrett and the government relied on statutory structure but viewed § 924(c)(1)(D)(ii)’s consecutive-sentence language as insufficient because it presumes another sentence has already been imposed. The government’s “in addition to” language applies only to underlying violence or drug-trafficking offenses, not § 924(j). McCloud urged the court to find clear congressional intent through statutory structure and purpose. Justices also questioned the penalty scheme and the constitutional rationale for requiring explicit congressional intent. The issue remained undecided.

Alberta Education Minister David Eggen said the province could allow parents to pay school bus fees again despite Bill 1, which eliminated fees for students living at least 2.4 kilometres from their designated school. Rocky View Schools faces a $1 million transportation shortfall and is considering longer rural commutes, changed bell times and relocated urban stops. Parents cited safety concerns about walking younger children, while the board may seek more time to decide.

Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) lacks widely applicable objective biomarkers, while rs-fMRI classifiers face limitations in accuracy, generalisability, test–retest stability, and disorder specificity. This study aimed to develop a clinically applicable classifier and assess whether diagnostic functional connections (FCs) could also serve as trait, state, or staging markers.

Two independent, multisite datasets were harmonised using prospective and retrospective methods. LASSO classifiers based on 100 subsamples achieved 79.6% accuracy and an AUC of 0.876 in the 1,015-person discovery dataset, and 77.3% accuracy with an AUC of 0.824 in the 683-person validation dataset. Validation sensitivity was 69.2%, specificity 81.1%, and MCC 0.490, with highly significant AUC and MCC. Performance varied by site, with particularly low sensitivity at JHU. Forty-seven FCs were identified as important, and group-difference patterns were reproduced for 44 in the validation dataset.

Voting classifiers increased sensitivity and reduced disparities between disease-severity subgroups, although their AUC of 0.841 did not differ significantly from LASSO. Voting performance was partly influenced by age, whereas LASSO was unaffected by assessed confounders. Frequently implicated regions also showed left–right imbalances, except in the cerebellum. The study further aimed to evaluate aggregate and individual FCs as trait, state, and staging markers.

The section presents Texas Instruments’ current mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, subject to change. Footnotes explain lifecycle status, preproduction parts and restrictions, RoHS classifications, lead/ball finishes, MSL and reflow ratings, and part markings. Tape diagrams define carrier and component dimensions and pin 1 orientation. TI disclaims accuracy and warranties for partly third-party-based information, notes that proprietary details such as CAS numbers may be withheld, and limits liability to the affected parts’ annual purchase price. Technical, design, and safety resources are provided “as is” for skilled developers, who are responsible for product selection, design validation and testing, and applicable requirements. Resource use is limited to applications involving the described TI products; users must indemnify TI for claims arising from their use. Products remain governed by applicable sales terms, and TI rejects additional or different terms.

The passage reviews the Jabra Elite 65t ($170), among the first earbuds using Amazon's new mobile accessory kit to integrate Alexa. Alexa in earbuds currently works only with Android phones, with iOS support via Jabra's Sound+ app said to be coming soon. Testing showed notable limitations compared with Alexa on smart speakers: Amazon Music is the only supported streaming service (no Spotify, iHeartRadio, TuneIn, or Sirius XM), voice commands cannot place calls, and text messaging, Drop In, reminders, and navigation are unsupported, though timers and alarms can be set without notifications. Amazon Music responds well and multi-room audio control works. The earbuds also support Google Assistant on Android and Siri on iPhone, with Google Assistant offering more features (auditory notifications, message reading, 40-language translation, navigation). Voice shopping is a strength, using order history, and a cited survey projects up to $40 billion in U.S. voice shopping by 2022. Sound quality is praised as stellar, the fit is comfortable and improved over Elite Sport, and a HearThrough ambient-sound mode activated by double-tap works as advertised. Downsides include five-hour battery life with only 10 extra hours from the case (versus 24 total for Pixel Buds and AirPods) and no tracker feature for lost earbuds. Overall, the earbuds deliver excellent audio but a weak Alexa experience for calls, music, reminders, and navigation, though Amazon says feature updates are on the way.

The Sporting News tracked Shohei Ohtani’s live stats in Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS between the Dodgers and Phillies, scheduled for October 4 at Citizens Bank Park. Ohtani made his first postseason pitching appearance against Christopher Sanchez. In 14 regular-season appearances, he went 1–1 with a 2.87 ERA, 62 strikeouts and 15 earned runs over 47 innings. He retired Turner, Schwarber and Harper in the first inning before striking out in his first plate appearance. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said the team hoped Ohtani could pitch through six innings into the seventh. The game was set for TBS and truTV, with an HBO Max stream.

Digital leaders use sensible risks, experimentation, feedback, and adaptation to compete. They value experiments’ market, product, and process insights, plan carefully to limit costs, and invest in long-term training in problem-solving, statistics, and design thinking.

After the Las Vegas Route 91 Harvest shooting killed 58 and injured more than 500, country musicians debated gun control and concert safety. Charlie Daniels called the attack an anomaly, warned against widespread fear, opposed broader calls for stricter gun laws and supported regulations on bump-stock devices. He criticized politicians’ knowledge of guns and argued that stricter laws would not prevent violence and could leave people defenseless. Rosanne Cash urged country musicians to stand up to the NRA, while Eric Church sang a tribute to a fan killed in the attack.

The speaker supports the new NHL team in Winnipeg, citing the city’s passionate fans, the strong organization under Mr. Chipman, and his positive experiences playing AHL games there, including a whiteout and “We Want the Jets” chants. He praises the intimate MTS Centre and expects strong NHL support. He also describes learning to recognize Henrik and Daniel by their speech, noting that Henrik has always been the more vocal captain, and explains how he studies opposing goalies to select effective shots, exploit rebounds, and account for defensive coverage and large goaltenders.

Using Mauna Loa Observatory’s minute-by-minute solar-radiation data, Willis Eschenbach compared maximum and average direct and diffuse radiation during the two years following the El Chichón and Pinatubo eruptions with non-volcanic periods. Maximum sunlight at Mauna Loa was largely unchanged since 1980 except after eruptions, while radiation levels following the two eruptions were nearly identical despite their differences in size and location.

During volcanic periods, average downwelling total solar radiation was 24.5 W/m² lower than during non-volcanic periods. Clouds partially offset this reduction: rather than the predicted 31.3 W/m² loss, the observed loss was 24.5 W/m², implying that cloud rearrangement added about 7 W/m², particularly around midday.

Mauna Loa temperatures did not change during the two-year volcanic periods despite receiving less solar energy. Records from Hilo, Molokai, Barbers Point, and Lihue likewise showed no discernible eruption-related cooling, and wind-speed differences were within the data’s uncertainty. The passage notes that the cited IPCC comparison would require CO₂ to rise from 400 to 43,250 ppmv to produce an equivalent 25 W/m² change.

Eschenbach states that the reason for the absence of cooling is unknown and questions the expectation that reduced solar energy must lower temperatures. He proposes that climate-system responses tend to restore the previous state under the Constructal Law and Le Chatelier’s Principle.

Energy-sector trading provides exposure to multiple energy stocks for diversification and potential profit through sector ETFs such as XLE and VDE or a portfolio of individual stocks. The S&P 500 energy sector includes oil and natural-gas exploration, refining, product distribution, and related equipment, materials, and service companies. As of July 18, 2022, the passage cites a one-year energy-sector total return as high as 52.81%, compared with approximately −9.28% for the S&P 500.

Trading the sector is described as difficult because oil prices are influenced by macroeconomic factors and are difficult to predict. Two XLE strategies are presented without their rules. The first has an average holding time near three days, 198 trades, 0.61% average gain, 6.4% CAGR, 65% win rate, 13% maximum drawdown, and 2.1 profit factor. The second has 335 trades, 0.21% average gain, 59% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, 1.75 profit factor, and a 3% annual return.

The five largest listed energy stocks are Exxon Mobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Schlumberger, although the list may change. The passage emphasizes diversification and portfolio stability over finding a perfect strategy.

Canadian big-five banks declined from February highs, with TD and BNS falling more than 7%, but their current valuations were presented as attractive. Five small-cap lenders were compared with the banks using beta, earnings yield, dividend yield, payout ratio, and dividend history. MCAN Mortgage ranked first, CIBC second, and Atrium Mortgage third. MCAN and Atrium offered dividend yields above 7% and had maintained or increased dividends, though their payout ratios were relatively high. First National, Home Capital, and Equitable Group had cut dividends; Equitable ranked last with the highest beta and lowest dividend yield. Smaller lenders may provide higher yields and smaller price swings, but offer less liquidity and less diversified services than the big banks. The author disclosed holdings in AMIVF, CM, TD, and BNS.

The Hawk Offense uses wing isolation, a high-post shuffle cut, and a weakside post-up. It resembles the “UCLA” Offense because a guard cuts toward the basket off a high-post back screen. Defenders show help against wing isolation, recover when the ballhandler stops, and must beware hesitation and fake drives.

Against the shuffle cut, defenders influence the cutter away from the ball and behind the screen, show the cutter wide, chase over the screen, recover to assignments, and establish pass-denial positions. Down-screen defense uses show-and-recover tactics before finishing with aggressive on-ball defense, pass denial, and weakside help.

An all-out SOS strategy traps the ballhandler in the sideline wing area, taking advantage of the off-guard’s low position and the difficulty reversing the ball. It combines individual fundamentals with coordinated rotations: defenders trap, deny the high post, contact-switch cutters, front the low post, and rotate as the pass leaves the passer’s hands. Once matched up, baseline penetration triggers “Base Go Red” rotations, while a post pass triggers “Post Trap” rotations.

AMD returns to high-end graphics with the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56, competing against Nvidia’s GTX 1080 and GTX 1070. Vega 64 is not expected to outperform the GTX 1080 Ti, though three-way CrossFire offers an advantage over Nvidia’s two-way SLI. Vega 56 is priced below the GTX 1070 in the US but faces less favorable UK pricing. AMD’s advantages include the cheaper, more widely available FreeSync ecosystem and new Enhanced Sync driver support, while improved minimum frame rates may help Vega exploit FreeSync.

Snap and Francis were convicted and fined $50 each for shooting and wounding a mare trespassing in an oat field protected by an insufficient fence. The court held that both statute and common law forbade intentionally injuring trespassing livestock. Property owners could expel animals or use necessary force to protect crops but could not inflict unnecessary injury. The judgment was affirmed.

Safeties are defensive backs positioned deeper than other defenders and serve as the last line against explosive pass and run plays. A free safety roams the middle without a specific man assignment, often providing deep coverage, while a strong safety plays closer to the line, fills running gaps, tackles, and may cover receivers or zones. Other names for the strong safety include “Rover” and “Star”; Canadian football uses “defensive fullback” and “defensive halfback.”

Safeties need coverage skills, speed, tackling ability, communication, and a comprehensive view of the field. Their responsibilities include covering receivers and tight ends, limiting big plays, creating turnovers, supporting cornerbacks, and preventing quarterbacks from targeting vulnerable areas.

Notable safeties include Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, Steve Atwater, Ronnie Lott, Brian Dawkins, Emlen Tunnell, Larry Wilson, and Sean Taylor. The passage also notes that 17 safeties belong to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Great safeties can increase their defense’s confidence, deter throws, create turnovers, and earn substantial long-term contracts.

Researchers found the Great Barrier Reef survived five near-extinction events over 30,000 years by moving across the seafloor as conditions changed. Fossil cores from 16 sites showed migration rates of 20 centimetres to 1.5 metres annually in response to exposure, sea-level rise and sediment buildup. Researchers warned that rapid warming and acidification, bleaching and projected changes may exceed the reef’s adaptive capacity. Nearly a third of its coral was killed in a 2016 heatwave. The reef will probably die again within thousands of years if past patterns hold, but whether climate change will hasten it is uncertain.

The report, prepared by Ministry of Education-affiliated researchers under the “Hope Initiative,” responds to the Arab Summit’s commitment to free, appropriate education for Arab children. Citing a 2018 UNESCO report, it notes that more than 10 million Arab children aged 5–15 were out of school. Using the Syrian conflict as a case study, it examines how displacement, poverty, damaged schools, insecure conditions, shortages of trained teachers and learning materials, and limited psychosocial support disrupt early childhood education and contribute to trauma, developmental delays, dropout, and long-term instability. The literature review also highlights the educational challenges faced by approximately 400,000 Syrian refugee children in Turkey.

The study used a descriptive, triangulated design combining interviews, an online questionnaire for Arabic-speaking participants, and a case study of Ahmed, a Syrian child in Alkhabor. Interviews with a conflict-affected parent and child described destroyed schools, repeated relocation, absences, inadequate books and internet access, unsafe communal learning spaces, PTSD symptoms, and community efforts to sustain learning despite scarce resources.

The proposed response has two components. Immediate and remedial measures include targeted emotional and psychological support and academic interventions for children affected by war. Proactive and sustainable measures include the Hope Initiative, an integrated system combining immediate assistance with long-term educational frameworks, regional and international collaboration, and preparation for future conflicts. The report concludes that resilient education can support children’s recovery, empowerment, national reconstruction, and long-term peace.
Jane Goodall died October 1 at 91; her legacy encompasses enduring skeletons, loss, and avoiding waste.

The September 19 earthquake combined with renewed activity at Popocatépetl has left residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, Morelos, stressed and fearful. Although the indigenous community has long lived in the volcano's shadow and found its intermittent eruptions preferable to earthquakes, authorities in Tetela del Volcán advised residents to keep important documents and change of clothes ready for a possible eruption. Hueyapan, 18 kilometers from the volcano, was among the towns hardest hit by the quake, with many losing homes and others suffering severe damage; Araceli Soberanes Estrada lost two of three rooms in her house, including her weaving workshop, though she continues weaving with help from state representatives. El Popo continues to emit steam, with ashfall reported in Tetela del Volcán and Zacualpan de Amilpas. Source: El Universal.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced in Manhattan to 50 months in prison and fined $500,000 on two Mann Act counts for transporting sex workers and girlfriends across state lines for drug-fueled sex performances. A jury convicted him of transportation to engage in prostitution but cleared him of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy. Prosecutors sought at least 11 years, while his defense requested no more than 14 months.

Combs apologized to his victims, his seven children and his mother, calling his conduct “disgusting, shameful, and sick.” Judge Arun Subramanian said Combs’s history of good works could not excuse his abuse of power over women. His children addressed the court, while the judge chastised his attorneys for an “inappropriate” letter that discouraged a complaining witness from appearing. Combs also faces ongoing civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault, rape, drugging and other violence.

Paper £10 notes cease to be legal tender in the UK on 1 March but may be exchanged for polymer notes at banks, building societies, post offices or the Bank of England. The Jane Austen note entered circulation in September 2017, has enhanced security and accessibility features, and is expected to last five years. A polymer £20 note is planned for 2020; no £50 update is planned.

Backtests indicate a positive futures-expiration-week effect for DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50, whose contracts expire on the third Friday of March, June, September, and December. During expiration week, DAX 40 averaged a 0.39% gain with a 57% win rate, versus 0.12% in a random week; December performed best. Euro Stoxx 50 averaged a 0.3% gain with a 54% win rate, versus 0.18% in a random week, making the effect smaller; December was best and June averaged a large loss. Expiration can increase volatility because of options “pin” risk.

For the week after DAX 40 expiration, the test did not use futures backtesting. It invested with 100% margin, entered at the close of expiration Friday, exited one week later, made four annual trades, and excluded commissions and slippage. This strategy averaged a 0.1% loss with a 47% win rate. December performed best, followed by March and June, while September was the only losing month and was profitable just 25% of the time. DAX 40 is considered attractive because of its high trading volume, and expiration-period performance patterns may inform trading strategies.

The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III’s conviction and 20-year sentence. It rejected his arguments that Judge McMahon should have recused, that any alleged bias made the sentence unreasonable, that medical needs warranted a downward departure, and that he deserved additional cooperation credit. The court found no partiality and held the sentence reasonable given his lengthy criminal history and the large amount of money involved.

An RCD clamp limits UC1825BEVM-CVAL switch-node voltage. Starting resistor and capacitor values depend on allowed overshoot, parasitic inductance, and clamp-voltage variation; Kclamp = 1.5 is recommended for 50% overshoot.

The application is a divisional of U.S. Ser. No. 16/424,721, a continuation-in-part of PCT/IB2017/057557, which claims priority from PCT/IB2016/057226. It concerns elastomeric compositions containing carbon black particles, particularly silicone elastomers incorporating hydrophilic or oxidized carbon black.

Disclosed methods contact hydrophilic carbon black with a silicone-compatible dispersant, optionally reduce the particle size in the presence of the dispersant, mix the treated particles into a curable hydrophobic silicone prepolymer, and cure the mixture to produce an elastomer with dispersed carbon black. The dispersant is miscible in the silicone prepolymer and contains a carbon-black-affinic moiety, such as an amino, acrylate, or epoxy group, that associates with oxygen-containing groups on hydrophilic carbon black surfaces. This association allows the dispersant to anchor to and at least partially envelop the particles, rendering them sufficiently hydrophobic and silicone-affinic for stable dispersion.

The dispersants may be branched, siloxane-based molecules with affinic groups positioned on the backbone or branches to reduce steric hindrance. Amino-silicone, silicone-acrylate, and epoxy-silicone dispersants are described, including amino-silicone oils, acrylate-containing silicones, and commercially available examples. Amino-silicone dispersants are selected with controlled amine numbers to balance particle dispersion against interference with addition curing. Dispersants are generally water-immiscible but sufficiently hydrophobic for miscibility in silicone matrices.

Both addition-curable and condensation-curable silicone systems are disclosed. Addition-curable compositions may contain cross-linkers, platinum or tin catalysts, accelerators, retarders, and hydrophobic fumed silica as a three-dimensional network former. Condensation-curable embodiments may use dispersants separately or may use prepolymers bearing carbon-black-affinic groups. Curable dispersions may also be diluted with volatile solvents or applied to substrates before curing.

The carbon black is characterized by one or more properties including particle size, volatile matter, oxygen content, pH, acid value, surface zeta potential, BET surface area, DBP absorption, and Raman-spectroscopic D-band/G-band intensity and area ratios. Desired particle sizes range from submicron sizes to several micrometers, with many embodiments favoring a Dv90 of 1.3 μm or less. FTIR may detect epoxy, hydroxy, carboxylic, amine, amide, or acrylate groups, while Raman analysis may assess oxidation and defective carbon-black structure. Dispersibility in water, hydrophobicity after treatment, and phase separation are also described as diagnostic characteristics.

The disclosed mechanism is a non-covalent association between affinic dispersant groups and polar surface groups on carbon black. The resulting dispersant-coated particles are not covalently bound to the silicone network but may be physically entrapped within it. The passage reports that sufficiently homogeneous dispersions can be achieved even at high carbon-black loadings, while acknowledging that non-covalent attachment may reduce mechanical strength.

Potential applications include intermediate transfer members for indirect printing, layered articles, sealants, and radiation-absorbing materials. Dispersed carbon black may provide reinforcement, thermal or electrical conductivity, pigmentation, and radiation absorption. The drawings compare dispersed, unmilled, aggregated, and collapsed carbon-black samples using FIB-SEM imaging, illustrate UV-Vis-NIR absorbance of silicone samples, and present Raman spectra for carbon blacks with different oxidation levels.

In Brooks v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co., the Supreme Court reversed and remanded the Eighth Circuit’s judgment. Philip Brooks sought a November 3, 1955, seniority date as a journeyman mechanic at North Little Rock because his military service interrupted his apprenticeship. The District Court found that his advancement would have been automatic and that he probably would have attained that status absent military service. Following Tilton, the Court held that possible future supply-and-demand conditions could not defeat a veteran’s statutory seniority rights and awarded Brooks the requested status.

The passage describes an ADS8860 ADC application using the PGA848 front end with ±15 V supplies, a 5 V ADC reference, and three filters: an input EMI/RFI filter, a feedback capacitor filter, and an ADC charge-reservoir filter. With a 75 pF feedback capacitor and 6.67 kΩ feedback resistors, the nominal front-end bandwidth is 318 kHz, decreasing to 277 kHz at the high resistor-tolerance limit while maintaining −0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. The ADC input range is 0–5 V; a buffered, precision-divider-generated 2.5 V PGA848 reference shifts the signal to midscale. The OPA192 reference buffer uses dual feedback and isolation components for an 86° phase margin, with stability requiring verification when loads change.

Supply voltages above ±20 V can permanently damage the PGA848. Recommended PCB layout includes symmetrical input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, trace separation, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, reduced thermal junctions, and placement away from heat sources.

The passage also identifies PSpice-for-TI and TINA-TI simulation resources, related TI documentation, support channels, update notifications, mechanical and orderable information, ESD-handling precautions, and disclaimers concerning the accuracy and use of TI technical resources.

U.S. equities rose Monday, led by the S&P 500 and Nasdaq as technology and semiconductor shares offset energy weakness; the Dow also edged higher. Investors continued to price in a modest Federal Reserve rate cut despite hawkish comments and stronger economic data. A potential government shutdown and delayed economic releases added uncertainty, highlighting resilient but fragile markets.

Arkady Babchenko appeared alive at a Ukrainian Security Service news conference after police reported that the Kremlin critic had been shot dead outside his Kiev home, explaining that his murder had been staged as part of an operation linked to an alleged Russian plot. The SBU said a Ukrainian intermediary was detained and had allegedly arranged the killing, while also seeking weapons and explosives for terrorist attacks. Babchenko said he could not discuss the operation but believed his life was saved and larger attacks prevented. Ukrainian prosecutor general Yuri Lutsenko defended the operation and criticised politicians and civil groups that had accused the government of permitting contract killings.

The passage says Americans spent over $100 billion on summer vacations and advises travelers to control costs by setting a budget, comparing hotel, flight, and fuel prices online, using a credit card without foreign transaction fees, limiting roaming charges, traveling off-season, booking early, considering trip insurance, watching airline newsletters for short-term deals, and seeking local coupons, attraction passes, and discount books.

A study found PortMiami had an economic impact exceeding $41 billion in 2016, supporting about 300,000 direct and indirect jobs and contributing $288 million in state and local taxes. Containerized cargo rose nearly 1 million tons since 2012, while cruise passengers reached a record 5.1 million. The Miami Herald questioned the study’s figures, but Mayor Carlos Gimenez defended them.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Subsystem provides master control and configuration of the device’s subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It integrates the Cortex-A8 processor with ARMv7 ISA, Thumb2, JazelleX, Media Extensions, AINTC, Harvard architecture, separate L1 caches, NEON SIMD, enhanced VFPv3, and a 128-bit interconnect. Real-time trace uses an ETM and a 32KB system ETB; the trace port is not pinned out.

A National Weather Service San Diego zone forecast issued July 4, 2018 covers coastal, valley, mountain, and desert areas of Orange, San Diego, Riverside, and San Bernardino counties. An excessive heat watch runs from Friday morning through Saturday evening, with Friday and Saturday temperatures reaching the upper 90s and low 100s in many inland areas and up to 112–117 degrees in the hottest deserts. A high surf advisory is in effect from 6 p.m. Wednesday to 9 p.m. Friday for Orange and San Diego coastal areas.

Low clouds and fog give way to mostly sunny skies Wednesday and Thursday. Winds are generally light, with afternoon west winds around 15 mph and gusts up to 25 mph in many zones; stronger gusts occur in deserts and mountain passes. Conditions become partly cloudy after Friday, with slight chances of afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms in several mountain zones from Saturday through Tuesday. Temperatures gradually ease late in the week but remain hot inland.

President James Madison, following Congress’s request, recommended that Americans observe the third Thursday in August 1812 as a day of public humiliation and prayer, seeking forgiveness, repentance, divine guidance and protection during wartime, and the restoration of peace.

As spring approaches, Blue Ridge Poison Control Center warns of poisonous plants, mushrooms, black widow spiders, and snakes. It advises wearing appropriate clothing, checking boots, staying aware, and avoiding harmful self-treatment of toxins.

The passage presents IEX as having two competing identities. “IEX One” uses its speed bump to offer superior execution to buy-side traders sending large market orders, but this strategy remains dependent on the SEC’s National Market System (NMS), whose subsidies and barriers favor incumbent exchanges and allow them to neglect competition based on service quality. The speed bump is therefore an implicit cost benefiting market orders at the expense of resting orders, not a true market disruption.

“IEX Two” represents IEX’s broader ambition to serve all traders more efficiently, balance buy- and sell-side interests, and restore liquidity as a competitive goal. Although IEX benefits from dissatisfaction with incumbent exchanges’ fees, rebates, and greed, goodwill alone will not produce dominance unless customers receive liquidity and patronage.

The author argues that IEX must abandon or overcome IEX One’s narrow tactics and bypass the SEC’s NMS through a new trading vehicle. Such a move would require support from brokers and traders and would challenge the regulatory structure that, according to the passage, protects established exchanges at traders’ expense. IEX’s share of market volume remains below 3%, underscoring its limited success to date.

Federal economists reported that U.S. employers added 200,000 jobs in January, unemployment held at 4.1%, and average hourly pay rose 2.9% from a year earlier. Economists cited minimum-wage increases in 18 states, affecting 4.5 million workers, as a possible contributor to wage growth. Job growth in 2017 was similar to 2016, while Black unemployment rose from 6.8% in December to 7.7% in January despite a longer-term decline since 2010. Analysts said it was too early to attribute trends to Trump-era policies and cautioned that monthly job figures have a roughly 100,000-job margin of error and are subject to revision. Broader economic conditions and automation also influence employment.

ESPN’s transition from cable-based distribution to direct-to-consumer streaming is examined against declining traditional television economics and intensifying competition. At its early-2010s peak, ESPN collected more than $7 monthly from over 100 million cable and satellite subscribers, alongside substantial advertising revenue, making it a major Disney earnings source. By 2023, however, subscribers had fallen to an estimated 70 million, live-rights costs were rising, consumers were shifting toward streaming, and Netflix, YouTube, Amazon, and other platforms were expanding sports and entertainment offerings.

Disney acquired BAMTech and launched ESPN+ in 2018 as a supplementary streaming service. ESPN+ reached about 25 million subscribers, with average revenue per user of $6.30, while gradually adding exclusive and premium content such as UFC events and NHL games. Disney announced that the flagship ESPN networks would become directly available without a cable subscription in 2025. It also joined Warner Bros. Discovery and Fox in the equally owned Venu Sports streaming venture, slated to launch in fall 2024 with each company’s sports networks.

ESPN’s growth historically came from combining affiliate fees and advertising. Affiliate fees began in 1983–84, while NFL rights, satellite competitors DirecTV and Dish, demand for additional channels, and Disney’s distribution bundles expanded ESPN’s reach and negotiating leverage. Premium live sports attracted audiences and supported fees, while SportsCenter and other news programming supplied advertising value and encouraged viewers to remain across ESPN’s platforms. Internet experimentation, including ESPN websites, mobile apps, social media, WatchESPN, and ESPN+, progressively prepared the company for streaming.

The shift requires ESPN to move from a relatively stable business-to-business model toward business-to-consumer operations involving customer acquisition, retention, data, technology, and profitability. Disney reported Q2 FY24 ESPN Domestic revenue of $3.866 billion, up 4%, but operating income fell 9% to $780 million amid affiliate losses and higher content costs. ESPN+ had 24.8 million subscribers, down slightly from the prior quarter, while higher prices raised average revenue per subscriber. Industry reports cited annual ESPN rights obligations exceeding $10 billion.

The broader sports-media ecosystem remains interdependent among incumbent broadcasters, technology companies, sports leagues, cable and satellite operators, and fans. Streaming has increased consumer choice but also fragmentation, subscription costs, churn, discoverability challenges, and piracy. Live sports remain highly valuable, with U.S. rights spending projected to exceed $30 billion by 2025, although some European soccer fees have begun to moderate. ESPN’s future therefore depends on balancing declining linear-TV revenue against streaming growth while managing costly rights, expanding direct offerings, and remaining attractive to younger fans.

IT Central Station’s 68-page report compares Oracle Exadata and HPE Vertica using enterprise user reviews. Users praise Exadata’s Smart Scan and Vertica’s columnar storage while criticizing Exadata’s patching process and Vertica’s documentation.

The author praises Coronation Street for sensitively portraying Aidan’s suicide and the grief, anger, and disbelief it causes, noting that the storyline has renewed discussion of suicide. The author recounts an unsuccessful suicide attempt as a teenager while struggling with their sexuality and says they now love life. Cheryl Fialka describes her husband John’s suicide aboard a cruise ship after five happy years together. With no note, warning signs, or known depression, his death left her questioning why and enduring profound sadness and anger for decades. The author wonders whether people who take their own lives realize the devastation they leave behind.

Competitive Capabilities International and R&G Global Consultants partnered to create Stable Operations TRACC, a data-driven solution for scaling reliable manufacturing and supply-chain improvements across sites. It combines big-data analytics, the TRACC methodology and blended training to address capacity utilization, service delivery and CAPEX avoidance. Cargill was the first client and helped facilitate the partnership. CCi says the product can increase clients’ capacity by 15–20% within six months of implementation.

The paper examines barriers to women’s education in rural Pakistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, where the reported female literacy rate is 40.8%, compared with 51.9% nationally and 73.3% for men. It reviews education as a fundamental right and as important to women’s empowerment, economic growth, and national development. The study objectives are to identify problems affecting women’s education, examine the effects of patriarchal culture and motivational barriers, and draw government attention to rural women’s education.

Data were collected through quantitative, open-ended surveys of literate and illiterate women in remote areas. Thematic analysis found shared barriers involving household and caregiving workloads, limited time and resources, poverty, inflation, transportation and health problems, illiterate family environments, lack of parental and societal support, patriarchal restrictions, early marriage, religious expectations, and limited educational facilities. Additional issues reported by literate women included network and electricity problems, curriculum and language difficulties, restricted subject choices, and inadequate teacher training and technology use.

Long distances to secondary schools, absent transport, unsafe travel, poor infrastructure, and a lack of girls’ toilets also discouraged attendance. Early marriage frequently ended girls’ education, while poverty and low family incomes limited the ability to pay fees and purchase books and uniforms. Despite these barriers, both literate and illiterate respondents considered women’s education necessary and expressed confidence and hope for the future. The paper recommends public awareness seminars involving parents and women, media programs highlighting female education, compulsory women’s education legislation, and expanded open and distance learning.

Pakistan Cricket Board pledged top-level security for the PSL final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium after a bombing killed 13 people, raising doubts about foreign players' participation. PSL chairman Najam Sethi said a February 22 draft would let franchises replace international stars unwilling to travel. Army chief Gen. Qamar Javed Bajwa backed the event, and Pakistan has not hosted major test teams since 2009.

After her 20-year marriage ended, the author discovered she knew little about the couple’s accounts, investments, and retirement savings. With help from a friend and a financial planner, she gathered documents, created a budget, and developed a retirement plan. She then re-entered the workforce, secured steady income and health insurance, and regained professional confidence. Since learning to make major purchases and handle household projects herself, she has built financial independence and plans to retire on her own terms.

The LifeCLEF 2014 plant identification task continued the ImageCLEF plant-identification campaigns by evaluating realistic, citizen-science-oriented plant retrieval. Its PlantCLEF dataset contains 60,962 images from 19,504 observations of 500 tree, herb, and fern species in a European region centered on France, contributed by 1,608 people. Images cover seven plant views—entire plant, branch, leaf, leaf scan, flower, fruit, and stem—and include contextual, taxonomic, social, and image-quality metadata.

The main task used multi-image plant observations as queries and ranked the correct species among retrieval results. The data were divided into training and test sets, with one-third of images used for testing. Primary evaluation measured inverse-rank scores averaged by contributor and plant; a secondary metric evaluated single-image predictions.

Seventy-four groups registered, ten submitted main runs, and six submitted 14 complementary image-level runs. Methods included Fisher vectors, convolutional neural networks, bags of visual words, matching, global descriptors, and metadata-based approaches. IBM AU achieved the best results, led by a run combining Fisher vectors, CNNs, and segmentation, scoring 0.471; IBM AU’s Fisher-vector and combined runs also placed highly. PlantNet’s matching method was the next strongest family of runs. CNN-only approaches generally underperformed Fisher vectors, while metadata use was limited and textual metadata degraded one team’s visual results. Combining multiple images from the same observation generally improved performance over individual-image prediction. Leaf scans and flowers produced the strongest category-level results.

The challenge expanded from 250 to 500 species and highlighted the difficulty of scaling plant recognition to realistic ecological applications. A possible 2015 extension would cover approximately 5,000 French flora species.

A writer who first visited Maine 24 years ago recounts his enduring affection for the state and argues that inland Maine, long overshadowed by the coast, contains a timeless wilderness central to the state's identity. He calls the creation of the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, formed from a private donation of more than 87,000 acres in northern Penobscot County, a positive development, noting it cost Maine taxpayers nothing and included $40 million in privately donated park funding, promising tourism, investment, and optimism for rural communities.

The piece criticizes Gov. Paul LePage for seeking federal repeal of the monument designation, portraying his position as inconsistent with his fiscal conservatism and shaped by distrust of federal involvement. Sens. Susan Collins, Angus King, and Rep. Chellie Pingree are cited as publicly supporting the designation. Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke is visiting the monument during a Maine trip, planning to canoe and meet local businesspeople; the author, noting Zinke's upbringing near Glacier National Park in Montana, hopes he recognizes the cultural and economic value of preserving the land for future generations.

Tanzania's CAG 2015/16 report, released by Prof Mussa Assad, identifies weaknesses in public procurement. Eight sampled contracts worth Sh63 billion and $1 billion (Sh2.2 trillion) were poorly managed; irregularities were found in goods and services worth Sh23.98 billion procured without competitive quotations; projects costing Sh23.32 billion were delayed; and MDAs procured Sh2.48 billion without tender board approval. Ten public entities bought goods and services worth Sh11.253 billion without valid contracts. Asset management also remained poor, with 12 of 34 embassies having 37 dilapidated buildings and ten undeveloped embassy plots abroad.

In soccer, an offensive switch is an exchange of positions by two attacking teammates used as a tactic to beat defenders. Also called "crossover runs," switches may be "called" (via an oral "Switch" command) or "natural," and may be performed with or without the ball. In the basic switch, two nearby teammates run diagonally forward in opposite directions, forming an "X," with each assuming the other's duties and responsibilities until they return to their usual positions. The "lateral" or "horizontal" switch exchanges players side-to-side toward opposite touchlines and can be used against the offside trap. The "vertical" switch exchanges positions back-to-front or front-to-back toward opposite goal lines and involves an actual position exchange, unlike an overlap. The objective is to free runners for a pass by forcing defenders to choose or be confused about marking. Players formally call "Switch back" when returning to their original positions.

On September 25, 2022, Tesla, Inc. appointed Joseph Gebbia to its Board of Directors. Gebbia is eligible for Tesla’s standard outside-director compensation but waived cash compensation until further notice and joined the Board in waiving equity compensation until July 2023, pending new Board determinations. He was not appointed to any Board committees, though appointments may be considered in the ordinary course. Tesla disclosed no related-party transactions requiring disclosure under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. A September 28, 2022 blog post announcing the appointment was attached as Exhibit 99.1.

The paper introduces MatterMech, a benchmark of 4,800 questions across eight nanomaterial-synthesis subdomains, designed to evaluate LLMs’ ability to reason about physicochemical principles and synthesis hypotheses. Questions were generated from approximately 17,000 papers using Claude-3.5-Sonnet, refined through Worker–Reviewer–Critic multi-agent discussions to reduce hallucinations, converted between multiple-choice and text-infilling formats, and validated by human reviewers. Multi-agent refinement improved source alignment, while human ratings of logic, distractors, and question quality were high. The authors also release MatterDB, containing 31,735 papers linked to extracted synthesis mechanisms.

Evaluation of 14 LLMs found that Qwen-Max achieved the highest multiple-choice accuracy (61.99%), while Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct led text infilling (35.25%). Models generally performed better at logical option selection than precise terminology completion, and reasoning-focused models showed larger gaps between these tasks. Performance improved with model size, while principle-guided prompting outperformed automatic chain-of-thought prompting in accuracy, output length, and stability. Limitations include the absence of expert annotation and the benchmark’s static coverage of an evolving field.

The passage covers device pin configuration and boot behavior for a Texas Instruments DaVinci processor data manual. It notes that some Cortex-A8 memory-map regions decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 are not physically part of L4 Slow and are reserved for other masters, and that the DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range enabled by a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; this full range is accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters reach a single view through the 512-MB TILER region in the base 4-GB map.

Terminal Functions tables (Sections 4.1–4.2) list external signal names, pin multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, pin types (I, O, Z, S, A, GND), internal pull states (IPU, IPD, DIS), supply voltage sources, and pin functions. The MUXED column identifies multiplexed peripheral functions, the controlling PINCNTLx register, de-selected input state (DSIS), and the Multi-Muxed (MM) option. Peripheral groups covered include camera I/F, DCAN, DDR2/DDR3 controllers 0 and 1, EMAC[0] and EMAC[1] ((R)(G)MII/RMII), GP0–GP3, GPMC, HDMI, I2C[0]–[3], McASP0–McASP6, PCIe, RESET/interrupts/JTAG, SD0–SD2, SPI0–SPI3, oscillators/PLLs/clocks, timers, UART0–UART5, USB0/USB1, Video Input 0, Video Output 0 and 1, analog TV output, and supply voltages, including the requirement that several 1.8-V and 3.3-V rails always be connected even when unused.

Boot state is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] when reset is de-asserted, latching the values into the CONTROL_STATUS register. BTMODE[4:0] select the boot mode order (XIP NOR, NAND Flash, NAND I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, UART), BTMODE[15:11] set GPMC CS0 configuration, BTMODE[7:5] are reserved and pulled down, BTMODE[9:8] select Ethernet PHY mode, BTMODE[10] selects GPMC XIP pin muxing, and BTMODE[15:12] set PCIe addressing. XIP Option B reconfigures pull state to IPD. Pin multiplexing is controlled by MUXMODE bits in PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270, defaulting to 0x0 (tri-stated); inputs are generally routed to all sharing peripherals.

The passage also advises enabling internal pull resistors or external pullup/pulldown resistors to avoid floating inputs, particularly on boot configuration pins that are routed out and 3-stated, and gives selection criteria (target below VIL or above VIH, largest feasible resistance, leakage currents, tolerances), noting 1-kΩ and 20-kΩ typical values.

Dr. Edith Mbagwu recommends SMART goal setting to help people establish and maintain realistic weight-loss goals. SMART goals are specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-based. Goals should define exercise frequency, calorie targets, activities, and foods; track motivating measures such as weight, body-fat percentage, calories, clothing size, or lifting capacity; be achievable and manageable; and include a schedule. Smaller milestones can support larger goals, such as burning 500 calories daily for an estimated one-pound weekly fat loss. Motivation can also improve adherence.
