A hockey speaker urges the team to keep attacking, shoot the puck, stop worrying about mistakes, and use rebounds, emphasizing they must win with their backs against the wall.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 29, 2019 reported unaudited consolidated financial results. Third-quarter net sales were $53.809 billion, up 1% from $53.265 billion, primarily due to higher Wearables, Home and Accessories and Services sales, partly offset by lower iPhone sales and unfavorable foreign-currency effects. Gross margin was $20.227 billion, operating income was $11.544 billion, net income was $10.044 billion, and diluted EPS was $2.18, compared with $2.34 a year earlier. For the first nine months, net sales were $196.134 billion, operating income was $48.305 billion, net income was $41.570 billion, and diluted EPS was $8.86.

Third-quarter sales were $25.986 billion for iPhone, $5.820 billion for Mac, $5.023 billion for iPad, $5.525 billion for Wearables, Home and Accessories, and $11.455 billion for Services. Nine-month segment sales were $87.592 billion for the Americas, $45.342 billion for Europe, $32.544 billion for Greater China, $16.524 billion for Japan, and $14.132 billion for the Rest of Asia Pacific.

At June 29, 2019, Apple reported $322.239 billion of assets, $225.783 billion of liabilities, and $96.456 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $50.530 billion, while short- and long-term marketable securities totaled $44.084 billion and $115.996 billion, respectively. Nine-month operating cash flow was $49.481 billion, investing activities generated $46.694 billion, and financing activities used $69.937 billion, leaving $52.151 billion of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. Apple repurchased 252.6 million shares for $49.2 billion during the nine months, including an accelerated share repurchase, and paid $10.640 billion for dividends and dividend equivalents. The board increased the repurchase authorization to $175 billion, of which $78.2 billion had been used by quarter-end.

Apple adopted several accounting standards in the first quarter of 2019, including Topic 606 for revenue recognition, ASU 2016-01 for financial instruments, ASU 2016-16 for intra-entity asset transfers and ASU 2016-18 for restricted cash. Topic 606 did not materially change prior-period sales, while ASU 2016-16 resulted in $2.7 billion of deferred tax assets and a $2.6 billion increase in retained earnings. Deferred revenue was $8.0 billion, with 68% expected to be recognized within one year. Product revenue is generally recognized upon shipment, while service revenue is recognized over time.

Apple held marketable debt and equity securities, non-marketable securities and derivatives to support its operations and manage liquidity, credit, interest-rate and foreign-currency risks. Total cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities had a fair value of $210.610 billion, including $19.5 billion restricted from general use. The company reported $10.0 billion of commercial paper and $98.3 billion of term-debt principal, with term-debt fair value of $102.5 billion.

Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $14.8 billion, including $8.1 billion that could affect the effective tax rate. The European Commission’s 2016 State Aid Decision required recovery of €13.1 billion of taxes plus €1.2 billion of interest; Apple appealed the decision and had funded the full amount into restricted escrow.

Legal matters included VirnetX patent litigation, with damages from two verdicts totaling $943 million and appeals ongoing, and litigation concerning iOS performance-management features. Apple and Qualcomm settled their worldwide litigation in April 2019 and entered multi-year license and supply agreements.

Apple identified supply-chain concentration, outsourced manufacturing, foreign exchange, tax disputes and legal proceedings as potential sources of risk. It also reported that Q1 sales are historically higher because of holiday demand and that product launches can materially affect sales and costs. During the quarter, Apple announced iOS 13, macOS Catalina, watchOS 6, tvOS 13 and iPadOS, which it expected to be available in fall 2019.

The article examines how the COVID-19 pandemic’s shift from face-to-face to distance education affected university foreign language education. Although distance education offers flexibility, wider access, recorded lessons, and reduced time and space constraints, it can create technological, motivational, interactional, assessment, and teacher-preparedness problems. These limitations are particularly significant for language learning, which depends on dialogue, imitation, speaking practice, and teacher feedback.

An online survey of 294 German and English undergraduate and graduate students used a 53-item, six-subscale distance education problems scale. Students rated the overall method as problematic and considered it unsuccessful in foreign language teaching. Internet and computer problems were rated highest, especially connection interruption or freezing, while teacher-related problems were lowest. Other prominent difficulties included insufficient mutual communication, lack of motivation, low participation, inadequate preparation, and difficulties evaluating skill-based learning. Male students reported more student-related problems than female students, while German and English students showed no significant differences. Students without training in educational programs, a separate study space, or home internet access reported more problems across all dimensions.

The study recommends awareness and training for students and teachers, improved preparation of distance materials and assessment, stronger virtual-classroom and communication skills, and a hybrid model combining face-to-face and distance foreign language education.

Yellen said the economy should expand moderately, with stronger employment and inflation gradually reaching 2%. Further federal funds rate adjustment would likely be appropriate if expectations hold, but policy would remain data-dependent amid uncertainty. Waiting too long to tighten could force rapid rate increases, disrupt financial markets and push the economy into recession. She cited improving labor conditions, including 4.8% January unemployment and faster wage growth, as well as recovering business investment and sentiment. Market-based inflation compensation remained low but rose, while survey-based long-term inflation expectations changed little. She emphasized productivity-enhancing policies and a sustainable fiscal path.

Standard canonical quantization of the Dirac field with commutators yields an unbounded Hamiltonian and symmetric bosonic statistics. Replacing commutators with anticommutators makes the quantization self-consistent and gives a positive-definite Hamiltonian. Expanding the field in momentum and spin modes produces annihilation and creation operators satisfying fermionic anticommutation relations. Their vacuum is the lowest-energy state, while the divergent ground-state energy is associated with fermionic harmonic oscillators, each contributing \(-\tfrac12\omega_k\).

The creation operators square to zero, so each mode can be occupied only once, realizing the Pauli principle. The modes have momentum \(k\), two possible polarizations, and create particles with corresponding antiparticles. A conserved \(U(1)\) current provides a charge operator; after removing an infinite constant, particles and antiparticles have opposite charges but the same mass and spin \(1/2\). Applied to electrons, this identifies the antiparticle as the positron, which Dirac’s theory predicted before its discovery.

The lecture states the spin-statistics connection: half-integer-spin fields require anticommutators and obey Fermi–Dirac statistics, whereas integer-spin fields can use commutators and obey Bose–Einstein statistics. In \(2+1\) dimensions, anyonic statistics may also occur. Wightman, retarded, and time-ordered fermionic Green functions are derived and related to scalar-field propagators, with fermionic time ordering introducing an additional minus sign when field order is reversed. The lecture concludes by introducing chiral fermions, based on two-component complex spinors, and Majorana fermions, based on four real components, as subjects for further discussion.

This exploratory study analyzed genetic, lifestyle, and environmental data from AMP-PD, Fox Insight, and a Tunisian Arab-Berber cohort, including 486 patients with LRRK2-associated Parkinson’s disease and 9,259 with idiopathic Parkinson’s disease. A standardized mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS), based on nine SNPs shared across cohorts, was associated with earlier age at onset in LRRK2-PD but not overall in idiopathic PD. The association was stronger in European/White patients and weaker in Tunisian/Arab patients.

Lifestyle and environmental analyses were restricted to Fox Insight and the Tunisian cohort because comparable questionnaire data were unavailable for AMP-PD. Smoking was associated with later onset in idiopathic PD; black tea with later onset in LRRK2-PD; coffee with later onset in idiopathic PD; caffeinated soda with earlier onset in both groups; and occupational pesticide exposure with earlier onset in idiopathic PD.

MGS-by-environment interactions were found for coffee and caffeinated soda consumption in LRRK2-PD, caffeinated soda in idiopathic PD, and occupational pesticide exposure in idiopathic PD. Among consumers, higher MGS scores were generally associated with earlier onset; for example, caffeinated-soda consumers with high versus low MGS had median onset ages of 50.0 versus 61.5 years in LRRK2-PD and 60.9 versus 62.7 years in idiopathic PD. No interactions were detected for smoking, black or green tea, or exposure duration. Limitations included cohort differences, limited diversity, differing genotyping methods, questionnaire caveats, and no correction for multiple testing. Overall, the findings indicate that lifestyle and environmental exposures modify the relationship between the MGS and age at Parkinson’s disease onset.

On November 21, 2001, Enron closed the remaining $450 million of its $1 billion secured credit facility, collateralized by Northern Natural Gas assets. A prior $550 million tranche, secured by Transwestern Pipeline assets, had closed November 16. Enron’s lead bank also committed to extending the maturity of a $690 million note due November 27 to mid-December, giving the company more time to restructure its debt and address liquidity concerns.

Enron disclosed that it had $1.2 billion in cash on November 16 and faced potential debt obligations of $9.15 billion through 2003. It was also seeking to postpone a partnership debt deadline that could have triggered nearly $4 billion in additional payments and liquidation of Brazilian natural-gas assets.

Enron and Dynegy reaffirmed their commitment to the merger announced November 9. Dynegy continued confirmatory due diligence and efforts to accelerate regulatory approvals, while JPMorgan Chase said it would help develop a plan to strengthen Enron’s finances through the merger, which was expected by the end of the third quarter of 2002. ChevronTexaco, which owned 26 percent of Dynegy, reiterated its confidence in the deal.

Goldman Sachs removed Enron and Dynegy from its recommended list and downgraded both to “market perform,” citing Enron’s liquidity problems, lost business, and concerns that Dynegy’s support might not restore customer confidence. Other analysts also questioned Enron’s viability and the merger’s prospects.

Enron shares fell roughly one-third on Wednesday, touching a 10-year low, while Dynegy shares dropped about 6 percent. Enron bonds also declined, and trading partners reduced activity because of concerns about Enron’s creditworthiness.

The ADS868xW supports multiSPI communication with configurable legacy SPI or source-synchronous protocols. A data-transfer frame begins when the host pulls CONVST/CS low, causing RVS to go low, loading the 32-bit output shift register, and resetting the internal configuration register to a NOP command. During SCLK activity, SDI data enters the input shift register while output data is shifted from the OSR’s MSB on the selected SDO pins. Pulling CONVST/CS high transfers the input word to the command processor and starts conversion. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames are treated as NOP commands even though their output data remains valid, while in longer frames the final 32 input bits constitute the command.

Register programming is synchronous to SCLK and supports byte and half-word operations. HWORD commands operate on 16-bit register groups and ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address. Commands are executed on the rising edge of CONVST/CS. The following frame’s output is determined by the prior command: fixed programmed data, 8- or 16-bit register data followed by zeros, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional output flags can append device address, input-range flags, AVDD alarm flags, input alarm flags, and parity.

Four legacy SPI-compatible protocols are available for configuration: SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, and SPI-11-S. SPI-00-S is used at power-up or after asynchronous reset; subsequent transfers use the protocol selected through SDI_MODE. Legacy reads use single or dual SDO outputs. Dual mode is enabled with SDO1_CONFIG=11b, making the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin serve as SDO-1 and reducing the clock count needed to transfer a given number of bits. Source-synchronous operation provides an output clock on RVS and supports internal or external clock sources and one- or two-bit output widths.

Nine 32-bit configuration registers control device identification, reset and power-down, input and output protocols, output data formatting, input/reference range selection, alarms, and alarm thresholds. Writes to RST_PWRCTL_REG require the protection key 69h. SDI_CTL_REG selects the SPI mode, while SDO_CTL_REG controls output protocol, clock source, and SDO-1 behavior. DATAOUT_CTL_REG controls optional data flags, parity, and fixed output patterns. RANGE_SEL_REG controls the internal reference and nine selectable input ranges. ALARM_REG reports active and tripped input and AVDD alarms, and separate registers define high-threshold hysteresis and low thresholds.

The ADS868xW is a fully differential, 16-bit SAR ADC with an integrated analog front end, ADC driver, internal programmable gain amplifier, and buffered precision reference. An example industrial analog-input module combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer. Each channel can be software-configured for voltage or current input, including common industrial voltage and current ranges. The ADS8681W settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs, has approximately 400-kHz high-bandwidth input, accepts signals up to ±12.288 V from a single analog supply, and includes overvoltage protection and input and AVDD alarms.

Programmable input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis support NTC-thermistor temperature monitoring. Proper hysteresis adjustment prevents noise near a threshold from causing false alarms or masking threshold crossings. The device also supports NAP and power-down modes. NAP is entered by setting NAP_EN while holding CONVST/CS high and exited by a falling edge, followed by the specified wake-up delay. Power-down is entered by setting PWRDN; analog blocks are powered down while the interface and registers remain active, and operation resumes after clearing PWRDN and waiting the specified power-up time.

AVDD and DVDD are independent supplies. Recommended layout and decoupling include at least 10 µF and 1 µF capacitors for AVDD, at least 10 µF near DVDD, separate analog and digital PCB regions, short ground paths, and reference-pin capacitors of 1 µF and 10 µF, plus at least 4.7 µF at REFIO when the internal reference is used. The document also notes ESD-handling precautions, support resources, and that ADS8685W and ADS8689W status changed to Production Data in Revision A.

This disclosure is a continuation of earlier applications and patents concerning periodic beam failure measurements in digital communications, particularly 5G high-frequency or millimeter-wave systems where path loss and blockage can interrupt beamformed links.

Example embodiments allow a UE to determine a beam failure measurement period using the periodicity of beam failure detection reference signals (BFD RSs) that the UE actually monitors, such as CSI-RS resources, SS blocks, or PBCH blocks having a quasi-co-located relationship with DMRSs of monitored PDCCH receptions. The period may be based on the shortest or longest monitored BFD RS periodicity, optionally combined with a specified value such as 2 ms.

During each period, the UE evaluates the monitored BFD RSs. If all evaluated signals fail to meet a quality threshold—such as signal quality falling below a threshold or BLER exceeding one—the UE reports a beam failure instance to a higher layer, such as its MAC layer. A specified number of consecutive instances can trigger declaration of beam failure, optional confirmation that all assessed BFD RSs failed at least once, candidate-beam identification, and transmission of a beam failure recovery request.

The disclosure addresses periods containing no assessed or transmitted BFD RS, which can otherwise reset the consecutive-failure counter and conceal failures. Proposed handling includes ignoring such periods, counting them as failures, or reporting whether BFD RS transmission occurred.

U.S. stocks closed lower Tuesday but recovered from session lows as tensions involving Russia, Syria and North Korea weighed on sentiment and boosted safe-haven assets and the VIX above 15. Investors awaited corporate earnings, expected to rise 10% for S&P 500 companies in the first quarter. The Dow fell 0.03%, the S&P 500 0.14% and Nasdaq 0.24%. Trump said his administration was working to reduce regulations and possibly replace Dodd-Frank, while United Continental shares dropped 1.1% amid backlash over a removed passenger; its CEO later apologized.

The paper introduces MOTO, a three-layer optimization framework for systematically mapping local transition-state networks on differentiable potential-energy surfaces. MOTO combines a multi-objective explorer that generates diverse, feasible masked perturbations; a bilayer minimum-mode-following kernel that uses Hessian-vector-product-based Lanczos or LOBPCG to estimate low-curvature modes and minimum-mode-force ascent to locate index-1 saddles; and deterministic two-sided saddle descent to certify connectivity and archive connected minima. The explorer balances candidate diversity, physical and geometric feasibility, and minimum-mode spectral separability. HVP operator calculations avoid assembling the full Hessian and support O(N) memory scaling.

Benchmarks on atomistic-spin systems found that HVP-based eigensolvers closely matched explicit-Hessian minimum-mode accuracy while using less time and memory, particularly at larger sizes. The explorer increased spectral separation and diversity before plateauing, while L-BFGS and conjugate-gradient ascent robustly approached index-1 saddles with \(\lambda_1<0<\lambda_2\). The implementation was reported to handle \(10^6\) spins, computing two curvature modes with under 1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 seconds wall time. On a \(70\times70\) system, the HVP approach reduced incremental peak memory to about 0.01% of the explicit-Hessian method and delivered a tenfold speedup.

Applied to a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) model, MOTO mapped twelve saddles and up to 32 pathways around a Néel skyrmion and an antiskyrmion. It identified meron- and antimeron-mediated duplication, annihilation, chiral-droplet formation, and other charge-transfer routes, including connections to bi-antiskyrmion and two-skyrmion states. Tests on an artificial Bloch spin model recovered established mechanisms and revealed additional saddle families.

For a Cartesian Ni(111) heptamer benchmark, the unchanged algorithmic core recovered edge, corner, and concerted rearrangement motifs below 1.6 eV and mapped their connected minima, demonstrating applicability beyond spin manifolds. Limitations include sensitivity to masks, objective design, Krylov settings, line search, and near-degenerate curvature. Proposed future directions include automated hyperparameter tuning, coverage-based stopping rules, and coupling with two-ended path solvers for kinetic-pathway identification.

NVIDIA Corporation filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 30, 2017, reporting 595 million common shares outstanding as of May 19, 2017. First-quarter fiscal 2018 revenue was $1.937 billion, up 48% from $1.305 billion a year earlier and down 11% sequentially. Gross profit was $1.150 billion and gross margin was 59.4%, compared with 57.5% a year earlier and 60.0% sequentially. Operating expenses rose 18% year over year to $596 million. Operating income increased 126% to $554 million, while net income rose 144% to $507 million and diluted earnings per share increased 126% to $0.79. The company paid $0.14 per share in dividends.

GPU revenue increased 45% year over year to $1.562 billion, driven by high-end GeForce gaming products, professional visualization and a 186% increase in datacenter revenue to $409 million. GPU operating income was $602 million. Tegra Processor revenue increased 108% to $332 million, aided by gaming development platforms and services and 24% growth in automotive revenue to $140 million; segment operating income was $47 million versus a $38 million loss a year earlier. All Other revenue was $43 million, reflecting the final revenue from the Intel patent license agreement, which ended March 31, 2017.

At April 30, 2017, cash and cash equivalents were $1.989 billion, marketable securities were $4.217 billion, and total assets were $9.410 billion. Total liabilities were $3.271 billion and shareholders’ equity was $6.132 billion. Short-term convertible debt declined to $215 million from $796 million, while long-term debt was $1.984 billion. Operating activities provided $282 million of cash, investing activities provided $754 million, and financing activities used $813 million. The company stated that existing cash and anticipated operating cash flows were sufficient for at least the next 12 months.

NVIDIA settled $605 million principal of 1.00% Convertible Notes during the quarter, issued 24 million shares for excess conversion value and recorded a $14 million loss on early conversions. At quarter-end, $222 million principal remained outstanding. Additional conversion notices totaling $136 million were expected to be settled in the second quarter, with an equal number of shares expected under the note hedges.

The company paid $82 million in dividends and intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders during fiscal 2018 through dividends and repurchases. Since 2004, it had repurchased 245 million shares for $4.59 billion and remained authorized to repurchase up to $2.73 billion through December 2020.

Stock-based compensation expense was $76 million, compared with $53 million a year earlier. The effective tax rate fell to 5.5% from 13.7%, primarily due to stock-based compensation tax benefits and a lower proportion of U.S.-taxable earnings. Early adoption of guidance on intra-entity asset transfers reduced retained earnings by $28 million. Future lease accounting was expected to increase both lease assets and liabilities, while the forthcoming revenue-recognition standard was not expected to have a material impact. Available-for-sale securities were classified as appropriately valued, with no other-than-temporary impairment charges.

NVIDIA continued construction of its Santa Clara headquarters through an off-balance-sheet build-to-suit operating lease, with bank funding commitments of up to $380 million and a maximum aggregate guarantee of generally 87.5% of construction costs. Inventory purchase obligations totaled $799 million.

Polaris Innovations had patent litigation pending in the United States and Germany, and NVIDIA had requested inter partes reviews of asserted patents. NVIDIA had not accrued a liability for these matters because it considered losses possible but not probable, and any potential loss range could not be reasonably estimated.

Management concluded that disclosure controls and procedures were effective, and no changes during the quarter materially affected internal control over financial reporting. No material changes were reported in previously disclosed risk factors or financial-market and foreign-exchange risks.

James Damore was dismissed by Google after circulating an internal memo arguing that innate biological sex differences explain women’s underrepresentation in technology. The memo claimed women have stronger people-oriented interests and greater neuroticism, while men have a stronger drive for status. The passage says conventional psychological categories of male and female differences have been dismantled, with many aptitudes and traits shown to exist on a spectrum. It also describes brains as mosaics of characteristics that can change through experience, challenging the idea that sex differences are fixed. Spatial-cognitive gaps can narrow through training, while stereotype threat, status perceptions and negative self-criticism can affect anxiety, brain activity and performance. Empowerment and mindset interventions may alter these effects. The passage argues that stereotypical, deterministic environments may contribute to the problems identified in the memo, and that diversity training could help change them.
DoLE-6, DoT-6, local governments, and TESDA are preparing job fairs, skills upgrades, and worker profiling to assist an estimated 17,000 Boracay workers if a proposed closure displaces them.

Lamar Jackson suffered an apparent hamstring injury in the third quarter of Baltimore’s Week 4 loss to Kansas City and did not return. His initial prognosis was 2–3 weeks, with him likely to miss Week 5 against Houston and doubtful for Week 6 against the Rams. Jackson missed practice for a second straight day in Week 5, and a source said he was not expected back until after Baltimore’s Week 7 bye. Head coach John Harbaugh said there was no way Jackson could have re-entered the game.

Medicare-funded hospital-at-home programs are pausing or shrinking ahead of a possible government shutdown and the Sept. 30 expiration of their temporary waiver. CMS told hospitals that, without congressional action, Medicare patients in the programs must be discharged or returned to medical centers by midnight Tuesday. UMass Memorial stopped admitting patients to its program, which serves about 20 patients daily; Hackensack Meridian discharged its census, ChristianaCare stopped accepting Medicare patients, and Mass General Brigham reduced its census from 60 to 40. Experts estimate national capacity at roughly 1,000 beds. Hospital-at-home programs can ease overcrowding by treating patients at home and freeing hospital beds, but they remain limited and are not a complete solution. Repeatedly extended waivers have discouraged hospitals from investing or expanding, while a bipartisan five-year extension is under consideration.

This study examines how ICT and CALL technologies are integrated into tertiary EFL initial teacher education in southern Vietnam and identifies factors affecting that integration. Guided by Hong’s (2010) model, it considers CALL teacher education, individual factors, and contextual influences.

A convergent mixed-methods study was conducted with 67 final-year EFL pre-service teachers and three teacher educators at a Vietnamese teacher-education institution. Data came from a four-point Likert survey, a focus group with six pre-service teachers, and interviews with all three educators. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively in SPSS, while interview and focus-group transcripts underwent inductive thematic analysis in NVivo.

Pre-service teachers generally perceived substantial opportunities to learn CALL-related knowledge, particularly ICT pedagogies, searching for and downloading online resources, using word-processing software, creating multimedia lessons, and using projectors. Opportunities were less extensive for organizing files, supervising online work, selecting suitable online exercises, using mobile devices for language learning, and troubleshooting digital equipment. Teachers most frequently used ICT for resource discovery, archiving lessons, exchanging information, and developing teaching materials. All three educators reported using ICT weekly, with some incorporating it into every lesson through tools such as PowerPoint and Moodle.

Barriers included educators’ limited confidence, time concerns, fear of change, and need for professional development; unreliable internet connections and outdated equipment; slow technical support; and pre-service teachers’ variable engagement. The institution had no clearly communicated official ICT or CALL requirements or guidelines, contributing to inconsistent practices. The study recommends stronger continuing professional development for educators, improved administrative and technical support, and explicit institutional policies and guidelines. It also notes limitations involving the small sample, single-institution setting, and the absence of analysis of educators’ evaluations and the curriculum’s influence on ICT integration.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court held that Senator William Flinn’s trusts became effective at his death, notwithstanding the five-year period allowed for estate administration and the trustee’s later receipt of the stocks. Fixing the value of the directly held stocks at death protected the life tenants and avoided an unlawful accumulation of income.

Because Booth & Flinn Company was a separate corporate entity, its Gulf Oil and Colonial Trust stock interests received by the executors in January 1925 were valued when the dividend was received, rather than at Flinn’s death. The Court also upheld the lower court’s method of estimating Gulf Oil’s undistributed earnings through the date of death by prorating average annual earnings on a per diem basis. The decree was affirmed as modified, with costs assessed against the estate.

The team needs to calm down after being overly motivated, avoid consecutive penalties, and return to disciplined play. Coach Mike Ramsey’s adjustments and a patient, selectively aggressive approach have made penalty killing a strength, but overcommitting creates gaps against Dallas’s quick offense. Dallas features elite players such as Zubov, Sydor, Modano, Hull, and Lehtinen, along with dangerous second-unit forwards. Dallas’s defense, smart breakouts, and Lehtinen’s hard work were key to the previous game. Staying out of the penalty box is crucial tomorrow.

The article argues that global citizenship education should be supplemented by international politics theory. Although it promotes transnational engagement, civil society, NGOs, human rights, environmental action and peaceful cooperation, its agenda underemphasizes military and economic security, state power, nationalism and the causes of interstate conflict.

Because international politics is anarchic, with no supreme authority, security is a central state priority. Relative power, alliances and national interests shape state behavior. Three perspectives are examined: realism emphasizes power, survival and self-interest in explaining rivalry and conflict; regionalism stresses shared interests, economic integration and trade blocs as means of containing conflict; and institutionalism examines how enduring rules and organizations constrain states, provide predictability and shape international responses. Together, they clarify the Russia–Ukraine war, including NATO’s role, the failure of economic integration to deter invasion, Russia’s turn toward China, and the limited capacity of the UN.

International cooperation depends on state interests and the nature of the issue. Cooperation can provide global public goods through single-country action, the efforts of all states, or cumulative action. It can also involve coordination around common standards. Such cooperation is possible without global citizenship, although established institutions provide arenas for activism. Examples include European integration and Arctic fishing-quota cooperation between Norway and Russia.

Citizens can engage internationally through NGOs, online platforms and transnational advocacy, but engagement with their own country’s foreign policy is also important. Foreign policy pursues security, economic welfare, status and ideological values through negotiation, information and propaganda, economic measures and military means. Since states remain the principal drivers of international change, teaching should address how citizens can influence national foreign policy.

The article recommends broadening global citizenship education beyond its European perspective and incorporating history, power, dependencies, conflict, cooperation, media manipulation, disinformation, polarization and propaganda. Teachers should speak truthfully about international problems, consider students’ readiness to address frightening conflicts, and retain global citizenship education’s commitments to environmental, social-justice and development issues.

After the armistice was signed on November 11, 1918, President Wilson announced that America’s war aims had been achieved and pledged continued support for establishing just democracy through example, counsel, and material aid. Secretary of State Robert Lansing conveyed American congratulations and admiration to Britain and France for their wartime valor. France, Japan, and Greece expressed gratitude for America’s role in the victory and its contribution to freedom, while Wilson praised British Prime Minister David Lloyd George’s address and their shared approach to the peace settlement.

A mixed-methods phenomenological study examined whether music software could be integrated into the general music education course at a Caribbean university to deliver specific content to pre-service early childhood and primary teachers. The course had traditionally relied on lectures, discussions, instrument playing, and limited use of the university’s learning management system.

Participants were 24 students—22 female and two male—enrolled in the course: 15 in Bachelor of Education–Primary Education and nine in Early Childhood Care and Education. Data were collected concurrently through an anonymous, pilot-tested questionnaire and a Sibelius music-notation assignment requiring eight bars of music in selected time signatures. Students received weekly instruction over three weeks and had two weeks to complete the assignment.

The assignment was completed with 90% accuracy, with most participants successfully placing the required beats in each measure. Most students reported that the software enhanced their understanding, although some were uncertain and six did not agree. Half felt very or somewhat comfortable using it, while most gave neutral responses about motivation; nevertheless, 67% supported continued use of technology in the music program and 75% wanted additional training. About half did not feel comfortable using the software during school practicum, while approximately 30% did.

The findings indicated that Sibelius could be integrated without extra cost, additional instructor training, or more class time. Students appeared to understand the taught concepts and skills, and their assignment performance and reported comfort suggested positive effects on performance and motivation. The researchers concluded that software provided an appropriate introductory strategy for selected course content and could complement traditional teaching.

Recommendations were to continue using music software, establish tiered training for lecturers and students, include technology-based assessment criteria in practicum rubrics, and add technology-related learning outcomes and final assessments to music education courses. The study also positioned the work as a benchmark for further institutional research, training, and development in technology-enhanced music education.
The order dismissing habeas corpus and remanding Gracy was affirmed; Justice Manning dissented.

The passage introduces the “Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model” to explain ventricular repolarisation and ECG deflections. It represents the heart as an egg-shaped mass centred on Wilson’s Central Terminal, with repolarisation expanding outward like a yolk. Each ECG lead detects signals along its vector: components moving toward the lead produce positive deflections, those moving away produce negative deflections, and their net difference determines the trace.

The model reproduces the isoelectric ST segment and subsequent T-wave. During normal repolarisation, opposing signals initially balance; a positive deflection appears when the signal reaches the asymmetric “T-zone” and ends when it exits this region. It therefore defines the QTp interval as extending from the onset of the Q-wave to the T-wave peak, while QTc extends from the Q-wave to the signal’s exit from the T-zone.

Electrically inert or damaged areas alter the balance of signals, producing ST depression or elevation depending on their location relative to Wilson’s Central Terminal and the lead. The model can also generate high, flattened, inverted, and biphasic T-waves through different combinations of damage and hypertrophy, although ion imbalance may also contribute to high T-waves.

The authors propose that repolarisation begins with the Q-wave and continues through the T-wave, making the ST and T intervals a unified process rather than separate components. They also caution that reciprocal leads can show ST elevation alongside ST depression, complicating interpretation of these changes as indicators of ischaemia or infarction and supporting assessment of the location of myocardial abnormalities alongside other methods such as cardiac enzyme analysis.

QTc measurement is described as vulnerable to variation among correction formulae and interference from U- or P-waves. QTp is presented as more clearly defined and reliably calculable; the highest peak is used for biphasic waves and the lowest trough for inverted waves, while neither interval can be determined for flat T-waves. The authors recommend QTp, particularly for assessing QT-prolonging medication effects and arrhythmia risk, while acknowledging the need for further validation. Future work will examine the U-wave, atrial repolarisation, and modelling coronary artery distributions and occlusion.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and software for creating interactive virtual game environments from real-world objects. A user selects physical objects according to detectable properties such as shape, dimensions, color, texture, or transparency; arranges them into a physical scene; and uses a camera, including a depth-sensitive 3D camera, to scan the scene. The resulting point cloud, mesh, or other digital 3D representation is converted into a virtual toy construction model composed of virtual construction elements, generally at a scale corresponding to the physical objects.

Conversion rules translate physical properties into virtual properties and may depend on detected scene characteristics, object recognition, user input, location, time, or game theme. Recognized objects can select suitable rules, game elements, and surrounding scenery. A library of known objects may provide 3D representations, attributes, themes, and functions. A recognized physical object may be removed from the scanned scene and replaced by its stored virtual counterpart, while nearby portions of the environment are modified according to the object’s theme or properties.

Game-controlling elements can give virtual locations active or animated behavior, including growth, movement, resource spawning, environmental changes, character creation, and triggered events. Tasks may require the user to modify and rescan the physical model to produce particular property combinations. The resulting environment supports action, resource, nurture, racing, battle, and role-playing games.

The disclosure also describes an efficient voxelization method that maps surface elements onto voxels by distributing points across each surface element and identifying their corresponding voxels. Surface attributes such as color can be transferred to voxels through weighted interpolation. A color-matching method selects the closest color from a discrete palette by representing colors in 3D space and restricting the search to candidates within a calculated distance from the origin.

A detailed mesh-to-voxel process creates a bounding box around a colored triangle mesh, divides it into voxel-sized cells, samples each triangle, and assigns intersecting voxels the nearest palette color. Raw colors may be calculated from the average vertex color or from a higher-quality intersection-based blend. The voxel output can be converted into an LXFML virtual construction model containing brick identifiers, designs, materials, positions, and rotations.

The disclosed interactive game system includes a capturing device, display, storage, and processor, which may be integrated into a mobile device. The processor converts scan data into a virtual construction model, defines game segments, and outputs the playable environment. Gameplay may follow a cycle of building and scanning a physical scene, playing in the resulting virtual environment, earning rewards or unlocking features, and beginning a new cycle. Physical toy construction characters and tool models may correspond to unlockable virtual characters, tools, skills, or powers.

A Northwestern University-led team used NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and archival Hubble observations to directly identify the progenitor of Type II supernova SN2025pht in the spiral galaxy NGC 1637, about 40 million light-years away. The progenitor was a massive red supergiant visible to JWST in infrared but hidden from Hubble by dense circumstellar dust before the explosion. Although emitting about 100,000 times more light than the Sun, the star appeared over 100 times dimmer in visible light because of the dust.

This was JWST’s first confirmed direct detection of a supernova progenitor and the clearest pre-explosion view yet of a dying red supergiant. Its unexpectedly carbon-rich dust suggests strong convection may have transported carbon from deep within the star to its surface. The findings support the hypothesis that many red supergiant explosions are obscured by thick dust, explaining why their progenitors are rarely observed despite models predicting that they produce most core-collapse supernovae.

Detected on June 29, 2025, SN2025pht is now being used to search for similar dusty red supergiants. NASA’s upcoming Roman Space Telescope may help detect and monitor these hidden stars.

The article examines programme leaders responsible for education-related undergraduate degrees in further education colleges in England, using Hodgson and Spours’ four-level lifelong learning ecology: macro-level policy and qualification structures, exo-level institutional relationships, meso-level professional practice and micro-level learners’ personal and community contexts. It traces the growth of college-based provision through teacher-education initiatives, the 1997 Dearing report, widening participation, foundation degrees and partnerships with higher education institutions.

A British Education Studies Association-funded project used an online questionnaire completed by 70 programme leaders—14 in English further education colleges, 46 at post-92 universities and 10 at Russell Group or other pre-92 universities—and interviews with 11 participants, including four further education leaders. Questionnaire fieldwork ran from February to September 2020 and interviews from July to November 2020.

Further education leaders commonly entered their roles through informal routes, internal progression or temporary assignments. All 13 respondents reporting their highest qualification held master’s degrees, while three held or were nearing doctorates. Compared with higher education colleagues, they were less likely to hold Higher Education Academy fellowships, and limited time, institutional support and competing responsibilities constrained research and scholarly activity.

The study identifies three overlapping strands of programme leadership: administrative and organisational work involving colleges, validating or franchising universities, quality assurance, recruitment and assessment; provision of academic and pastoral support for diverse, often non-traditional students; and responses to students’ wider social, emotional and economic needs. These responsibilities were frequently poorly defined. Small teams, combined with substantial teaching and line-management duties, required leaders to be hands-on across every level. They also managed small cohorts, combined students from different programmes and qualification levels, and balanced specialist higher education cultures against wider college systems and policies.

Participants described programme leaders as “keystone species” whose accumulated professional, academic and personal experience anchored local learning environments. Their commitments to students and communities included promoting access, supporting progression into teaching and related careers, and providing personal and mental-health support. However, policy, regulatory and institutional demands could obscure this work and create tensions between vocational and academic provision, student-centred support and standardised college processes.

The article concludes that programme leaders are fundamental to the health and sustainability of these programmes, but their “sightlines” are often directed inward toward immediate institutional pressures. Greater research and scholarly activity, academic engagement, and partnerships with employers and local higher and further education networks could help them work beyond their institutions and improve provision. Higher education leaders face comparable difficulties, but these are often amplified in further education because of its distinct ecology and weaker access to established academic networks and support structures.

The UAE unveiled the Mars 2117 Project on 14 February, aiming to establish the first human settlement on Mars by 2117. Led by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, it will partner with international research institutions and initially involve Emirati scientists to develop faster travel to Mars. The initiative builds on the UAE’s 2015 Mars Probe announcement. Elon Musk also presented plans to colonize Mars and reduce travel costs through reusable transportation.

This divisional application discloses a novel compound represented by Chemical Formula 1 and an organic light emitting device containing the compound. Formula 1 defines two Ar groups and an L linkage, with L selected from specified structures or a direct bond and Ar optionally selected from additional defined ring structures. Defined substituents include hydrogen, deuterium, halogens, alkyl, aryl, and heterocyclic groups. The compound may be incorporated into emitting, hole injection, hole transport, electron injection, electron transport, hole blocking, or electron blocking layers of multilayer, normal, inverted, top-emission, bottom-emission, or dual-emission devices. Organic layers may be formed by vacuum deposition or solution coating.

Preparation examples describe coupling aldehyde- and amidine-containing precursors, followed by palladium-catalyzed reactions with boronic acids to produce numerous compounds. Example devices used an ITO substrate, hole injection and transport layers, a host-dopant emitting layer, a compound/LiQ electron transport layer, and LiF/Al negative electrodes. At 10 mA/cm², compounds tested in Examples 1–15 operated at 3.76–3.91 V with current efficiencies of 5.19–5.46 cd/A, compared with 3.96–4.13 V and 4.89–5.18 cd/A for seven comparison compounds. The passage reports that the disclosed compounds provided lower driving voltage, higher current efficiency, and longer lifetime, with potential lifetime benefits from thermal stability.

U.S. District Judge Paul W. Grimm sentenced Maryland residents Gbenga Ogundele, also known as Benson Ogundele, and his wife, Moji Popoola, for conspiring to commit wire fraud and money laundering through an internet dating scam that defrauded vulnerable victims of millions of dollars. Ogundele received 234 months in prison, and Popoola received 18 months, each followed by three years of supervised release. Ogundele was also convicted of aggravated identity theft and ordered to forfeit $2,195,103.36. Popoola was ordered to forfeit approximately $165,000, pay $34,100 in restitution, and serve her supervised release in home detention.

Ogundele’s brother, Babatunde Popoola, received 12 years in prison and was ordered to pay $465,170.76 in restitution. Co-conspirator Victor Oyewumi Oloyede was sentenced to 234 months, while three others pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering and were awaiting sentencing. In a related case, Funmilayo Joyce Shodeke received 13 months of probation and was ordered to forfeit $29,900.

From January 2011 to May 18, 2015, conspirators used dating websites and electronic communications to develop relationships with victims nationwide. They solicited money through false claims involving hospital bills, travel, overseas businesses and foreign taxes. Victims deposited funds or sent checks to controlled “drop accounts,” paying between $1,720 and $50,000. Conspirators also used victims’ identity information and moved the proceeds through other accounts and instruments to conceal their source and control.

Martyn Waghorn returns to the Stadium of Light with Ipswich Town on Saturday, his seventh club since leaving hometown Sunderland. The 28-year-old striker credits former youth coach Kevin Ball with restoring his career after nearly being released at 15 and teaching him football’s fundamentals. Ball now has an ambassadorial role at the stadium, where five academy players hope to feature for the hosts.

Maria Saliagas, who has multiple sclerosis, says Delta Air Lines employees tied her to a regular wheelchair with someone else's blanket when flying from Atlanta to Amsterdam on April 1, because no strapped chair was available; her son reports bruising. Delta expressed regret and offered 20,000 SkyMiles, which the family calls insufficient, seeking policy change.

This medRxiv protocol describes a descriptive, register-based cohort study of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) revisions after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). It will use Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register data from all public and private orthopedic departments for 1995–2022, following adults who underwent primary THA from surgery until death or first revision, for up to 28 years and at least 90 days. Hemiarthroplasty and simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty are excluded. PJI is defined as deep infection reported by the surgeon during revision surgery.

Annual revision trends will be reported for DAIR, one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange, with PJI revisions further grouped by time since primary surgery: within four weeks, four to 12 weeks, and more than 12 weeks. Second-revision risk after each approach will be assessed using Kaplan–Meier plots and Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex.

The long observation period and comparison of all three revision approaches are identified as strengths. Limitations include incomplete reporting in some private clinics, surgeon-reported PJI diagnoses that may be misclassified, the descriptive nature of the observational analysis, and reliance on Danish data, which may limit generalizability. The study received no external funding, and its protocol has not yet been uploaded to OSF.

GPS directions are sending increasing numbers of trucks through a steep, winding stretch of Arkansas 43 near Ponca, where seven vehicles crashed in 2½ years. Traffic through Ponca has risen from six 18-wheelers a year to at least six daily, while about 450 vehicles use the highway daily. Drivers say maps fail to show a 1,300-foot elevation drop and sharp curves, sometimes causing burned brakes and rollovers. Some crashes have injured drivers, endangered tourists, and contaminated the Buffalo River with diesel; a fatality occurred four years ago. Hawkeye Transportation advises drivers hauling over 30,000 pounds to avoid Ponca in wet weather. The Highway Department plans warning signs reading, “Crooked and steep next 3 miles. Drive with care,” though a practical detour would require signs 25 miles north in Harrison. Local officials hope the signs will reduce runaway-truck incidents.

Australia dominated the Philippines 89–53 in a FIBA World Cup qualifier, with Gilas trailing 57–32 at halftime and shooting poorly against the taller, faster Boomers. The game became increasingly physical before a brawl involving punches, thrown chairs and water bottles. RR Pogoy’s shove, Daniel Kickert’s response, confrontations involving coach Chot Reyes and player Terrence Romeo, and a post-fight group selfie overshadowed the result.

Australia and the Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas both apologized, with the SBP saying violence had no place in sports and that it had breached Filipino hospitality. The article argued that although Australia contributed to the escalation, the Philippine team bore greater responsibility for its response and should not have used violence or excuses. Romeo’s suggestion that critics should convert to Australia was also criticized.

The incident was viewed as damaging the Philippines’ international standing and potentially setting back its World Cup preparations. Beyond apologies, the article urged stronger player discipline, greater focus on restraint and meaningful consequences as FIBA sanctions approached, warning that maintaining the status quo would be unacceptable.

The Give & Go isolation offense uses a 2-1-2 spread with the post on the weakside and relies on the two primary ball handlers. Players pass and hard-cut to the basket, repeating the action when the pass is denied. Wings back-cut, drive around soft defenders, or use spins and behind-the-back dribbles against aggressive defenders. The post provides pressure-release passing, and weakside help can restart the action with return passes or cross-court passes. Weakside players may exchange positions or set stationary down or back screens when defenders sag, while avoiding moving-screen fouls.

Wigan Athletic manager Leam Richardson dismissed reports of a serious tunnel confrontation after the Fleetwood game, saying Ivan Toney and Nathan Pond simply came together in a brief pushing and shoving incident that players later found funny. Wigan now seek an FA Cup third-round win over AFC Fylde, leading to a Premier League tie with Bournemouth.

The application describes a floor cleaner with a pivotally movable body and base, a supply tank containing cleaning fluid, a distribution nozzle, a vacuum source, a suction inlet, and a recovery tank. The nozzle dispenses fluid onto the surface being cleaned, while the vacuum source draws used fluid and debris through the suction inlet into the recovery tank. A handle includes a grip and actuator for controlling fluid flow, and a rechargeable battery powers the vacuum source. Component placement is configured so the cleaner’s center of gravity remains behind the handle axis and along or rearward of the steering axis as tank levels change.

The recovery tank has a tank body, removable cover, lid seal, upwardly extending inlet duct, baffle, suction-air outlet, cage, filter, shutoff float, and removable strainer. The baffle redirects incoming air and fluid downward, separates fluid from the suction airflow, and limits fluid entering the suction outlet. The cage contains screens, while a downstream filter has a pull tab and angled sidewalls that permit one-handed removal and pivoting. The float moves along the inlet duct and closes the suction outlet when the fluid exceeds a desired level. The strainer has a perforated body and accessible handle, traps debris, and is frictionally retained on the inlet duct. The tank is held in a body recess by a latch, with projections and recesses maintaining alignment when the narrow tank-recess portion flexes.

A link or yoke connects the body and base and enables steering while constraining their movement. Slots, stops, and pivoting ranges limit movement about the body-base pivot and steering axes. The yoke carries a suction conduit, a supply-fluid conduit, and electrical wires through separate chambers.

The base includes a motor-driven brushroll that agitates and wipes the surface. Embodiments describe brushrolls with hydrophobic textile cleaning media, optional hydrophilic bristles, and fiber sets of different diameters, with smaller fibers providing wiping action and larger, stiffer fibers providing agitation and vibration damping. The brushroll may also expose a forward portion for cleaning low vertical surfaces.

The brushroll cover is removable for brushroll access, cleaning, or replacement. Opposing slide actuators operate latches, and spring-loaded cam surfaces permit reattachment without actuating the release controls. Fluid couplings maintain communication between the supply tank and removable nozzle when the cover is installed.

LEDs direct light toward the visible spray pattern and may function as headlights or indicate fluid flow, vacuum power, or operating status. The base also includes a first squeegee that pushes fluid toward the suction inlet and a second squeegee that removes fluid and debris from the brushroll and directs them toward the suction conduit while reducing air ingress. An optional secondary nozzle can wet the brushroll before surface contact, and rollers support the base.

The application describes electronic devices with enhanced touch-sensor and display structures that address hand occlusion, viewing-angle limitations, and the inconvenience of physical controls. An enclosure may include transparent and opaque front, rear, and sidewalls, with display layers beneath transparent portions and touch-sensor layers beneath both transparent and opaque portions. Overlapping display and touch layers provide touchscreen areas, while nonoverlapping touch layers provide touch-only inputs. Sidewalls may be vertical, sloped, planar, or curved.

Touch sensors may use capacitive, resistive, acoustic, force-based, light-based, or other technologies, while displays may use LCD, electrophoretic, plasma, OLED, LED, electrowetting, or other pixel technologies. Touch and display layers may be rigid, flexible, deposited as coatings, or attached to walls with adhesive.

The application also describes foldable devices with flexible wall portions, continuous or segmented displays, touch layers spanning multiple surfaces, and hinge structures using flexible layers, accordion structures, or pivoting members. Fabrication may involve molding, deposition, patterning, photolithography, printing, coating, and lamination. Bendable structures may include stress-tolerant features such as thinned substrates, serpentine traces, neutral-plane adjustments, redundant conductive paths, and bend-resistant materials.

This study examined teachers’ views on culturally responsive education in the Turkish education system. Using Q methodology, 21 purposively selected public-school teachers from Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa sorted 30 literature-derived statements into a forced agreement scale. Participants were interviewed online, and responses were analyzed through principal components and varimax rotation.

The analysis identified three factors: Unification, Student Support, and Teacher Support. Seventeen participants loaded significantly onto these factors, while four did not. The Unification group emphasized bringing cultures together, shared human values, and global citizenship; it most strongly recognized inequalities among cultures. The Student Support group prioritized equality among cultures, psychosocial and academic support, and cultural competence, while rejecting the treatment of different cultures as threats. The Teacher Support group emphasized teacher development and culturally relevant teaching, although participants did not favor using diverse cultural examples in the curriculum or offering elective courses for different cultures.

The strongest overall agreement concerned developing students’ cultural competence, presenting general cultural practices, and supporting the academic and social development of students with local culture. The strongest disagreements concerned anti-discrimination measures, viewing different cultures as threats, and treating the classroom as a reflection of society. Participants declined to explain their most extreme responses, so the proposed reasons for divergent opinions could not be analyzed.

Overall, teachers regarded the system as accepting cultural diversity while still containing inequalities and insufficiently developing culturally responsive curricula, materials, classroom practices, and student and teacher support. The study recommends stakeholder workshops, teacher professional development, support for students’ cultural expression, further research, and wider dissemination of cultural knowledge. Limitations included participants’ reluctance to comment and their concentration in southeastern Türkiye.

Progressive (PGR), the fourth-largest U.S. auto insurer and a top-20 home insurer, beat February 2018 estimates, reporting an 87.8% combined ratio, a 19% year-over-year increase in net earned premiums to $2.2047 billion, and 18% year-to-date premium growth to $4.8943 billion. All business lines grew at least 16%, while the year-to-date combined ratio improved to 87.6%. February net income was $129 million, down 4% from a year earlier despite improved underwriting profit.

Progressive priced $600 million of 4.20% senior notes due 2048 and 500,000 preferred shares, generating $1.0834 billion in net proceeds for general corporate purposes. It also expanded commercial auto coverage for an Uber subsidiary into three states and recognized $70 million in additional net premiums.

The author expects book value to grow more than 10% and 2018 EPS to approach the upper end of a $2.50–$4.30 range. Estimated intrinsic value is about $48 per share based on current metrics and $50–$54 using projected 2018 figures. Although Progressive is considered slightly overvalued, it is viewed as well managed, with steady growth and strong operating performance. Estimated 2018 annual dividends are $0.76–$1.85 per share.

Gary Antonacci’s dual momentum strategy is a trend-following investment method that combines absolute momentum—an asset’s own price change over time—with relative momentum—its performance compared with other assets. It generally buys assets with positive absolute momentum that outperform their peers and, where shorting is practical, sells assets with negative absolute momentum that underperform other declining assets. The approach seeks to avoid buying the best-performing asset within a generally losing group.

Momentum is calculated as current price divided by the price at a specified earlier period, multiplied by 100; values above 100 indicate positive momentum and values below 100 indicate negative momentum. To apply the strategy, investors first calculate each asset’s absolute momentum, compare positively performing assets to select the strongest for a long position, and compare negatively performing assets to select the weakest for a short position. Absolute and relative momentum can conflict, so both conditions are considered.

The strategy is commonly implemented with monthly rebalancing and ETFs. A modular approach compares two related sectors or portions of one sector over a chosen period, usually the preceding 12 months, and buys the stronger performer if its absolute momentum is positive; otherwise, it may use Treasury or investment-grade bonds. Sector rotation versions rank a universe of ETFs by absolute momentum and periodically rotate into the best performers. The approach can also be applied to individual stocks, futures, and other securities.

In the example comparing the S&P 500 and gold over three months, the S&P 500 had 110% absolute momentum versus gold’s 105%, so the S&P had positive relative and absolute momentum and was selected for investment through an ETF such as SPY. In the futures example, crude oil’s 90% absolute momentum versus natural gas’s 95% indicated that crude had the stronger negative momentum and was the preferred short position.

Relative-momentum research by Jagadeesh and Titman in 1993 found profitable opportunities over periods of roughly one to 12 months but weaker results outside that range. Antonacci introduced the dual-momentum extension in his 2012 book, “Dual Momentum Investing: An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk,” reporting that adding absolute momentum reduced relative-momentum volatility.

Antonacci’s hypothetical GEM backtest from 1950 to 2018 held U.S. or non-U.S. equity indices when stocks were strong and bonds when they were weak. It averaged 1.5 trades annually, with monthly-return correlations of 0.60 to a global allocation benchmark and 0.50 to the S&P 500. These results are simulated and hypothetical and do not reflect actual investor returns, fees, or index trading costs.

A cited monthly ETF backtest returned 6.75% annually with a 30% maximum drawdown. It outperformed the world index but did not beat the S&P 500’s 9.2% annualized return, while the S&P’s maximum drawdown was about 55%. Overall, dual momentum may offer lower volatility and better bear-market protection than buy-and-hold, but it can underperform during strong bull markets or sharp rebounds.

The Break, a longtime Five Points South restaurant and billiards hall, is set to be demolished for high-rise apartments. Some longtime customers support the change as the area declines, while residents question rising rents and want more affordable housing. No closure date has been set.

Neiman Gracie criticized Dillon Danis’s trash talk after offering to fight him at Bellator 180; Danis declined because he did not want to miss the IBJJF World Championship for a preliminary spot. Gracie will instead face Dave Marfone at Madison Square Garden on June 24. He said Danis should stop talking and earn a professional fight before they meet.

The advance-decline indicator, also called the A/D line, is a cumulative market-breadth measure of the difference between advancing and declining stocks within an index. It is primarily calculated daily and can confirm an index trend; divergence between the indicator and index may signal a potential reversal. A rising value suggests market momentum, while a falling value may indicate weakening momentum.

Advance/decline issues are stocks trading above or below the previous day’s close. Advance/decline distribution shows the number and trading volume of advancing and declining stocks in an index, exchange, or basket, helping assess overall breadth and sector sentiment. The Advance/Decline Volume Line similarly cumulates the difference between advancing and declining share volume; it can indicate buying or selling pressure and potential trend reversals.

The NYSE A/D line tracks the cumulative daily difference between advancing and declining NYSE stocks. A backtest using SPY produced 229 trades, an average gain of 0.6%, and a 1.55 profit factor—below the stated 1.75 threshold—with inconsistent results. Multiple strategy versions did not yield a successful strategy, leading the article to recommend considering other oscillating indicators such as RSI, Williams %R, and IBS instead.

Researchers analyzing over 10 million secondary students’ scores across 13 years found that a half-degree rise in average annual temperature was associated with a 1% drop in exam scores. In the UK, June heat coincides with exams, and limited air conditioning may worsen results. Changing the academic year is complicated by synchronized institutions and rigorous concurrent marking, though annual grade boundaries may prevent lasting disadvantages.

Hervey Bay dive operators disagree on the tourism impact of the ex-HMAS Tobruk’s unplanned landing on her side. Glenn Bowman expects reduced income due to limited access, while Ed Gibson believes the wreck remains accessible and tourism can thrive. A safety inspection is underway before the government assesses future dive opportunities.

The July 10–11, 2001 IEP News compilation focuses on California’s electricity crisis. Fifteen days of mediated negotiations with power generators ended without settlement. California demanded $8.9 billion in refunds for alleged wholesale overcharges dating from May 2000, while generators offered about $716 million and disputed California’s calculations. Administrative law judge Curtis Wagner recommended applying federal price restraints retroactively to October 2000, limiting potential refunds to hundreds of millions or about $1 billion and noting that suppliers may themselves be owed more. FERC is expected to hold hearings before deciding the amount. Gov. Gray Davis said California would pursue the full claim in federal court if necessary. Other Western states have filed refund claims totaling roughly $6 billion.

Related coverage said Calpine purchased 236 billion cubic feet of Texas and New Mexico gas reserves for $355 million plus debt, increasing its reserves to about 1.5 trillion cubic feet. Edison International’s refinancing and asset sales were expected to stabilize the company, but Southern California Edison’s rescue plan remained dependent on legislative approval, despite nearly $1 billion in defaulted debt. A bankruptcy judge also ruled that PG&E customer refund claims were regulatory matters unrelated to the utility’s bankruptcy.

An Electric Power Research Institute report warned that overloaded Western transmission systems, deferred maintenance and inadequate investment could produce cascading outages, estimating that $10 billion to $30 billion in transmission upgrades was needed over ten years. It also urged greater use of plant upgrades and warned against excessive reliance on natural gas.

House Republicans sought to advance a limited energy bill before the August recess, covering clean-coal subsidies, household assistance and energy-efficient televisions. Broader proposals involving Arctic drilling, conservation, fuel economy, nuclear liability, California electricity pricing and other energy issues remained stalled by partisan and industry disagreements.

A Texas Public Utility Commission brochure attributed differences between Texas and California electricity markets to greater generation reserves, fuel diversity, infrastructure, planned retail competition and more power-plant construction. In a CNBC interview, Shaw Group CEO James Bernhard said demand for new and replacement power plants supported strong, long-term construction prospects despite regulatory uncertainty.

A New York Times feature documented harsh working and living conditions among California’s approximately 800 predominantly Peruvian and Chilean guest-worker shepherds. The article described long hours, limited days off, inadequate trailers and exclusion from minimum-wage protections, while noting proposed legislation requiring rest periods and better housing and strong opposition from ranchers concerned about costs.

Generative AI and LLMs are rapidly transforming sectors such as finance, healthcare, and education, but their rapid iteration, complexity, market competition, and connection to national power create legal and ethical challenges, including misinformation, malicious deepfakes, bias, and discrimination. Regulation must balance innovation with preventing societal harm, and existing frameworks may be inadequate for these evolving systems.

Although the EU, US, and China have introduced AI regulations and companies such as Microsoft have issued responsible-AI principles, forums, and internal policies, governance remains fragmented. Industry-government communication gaps and inconsistent national rules complicate compliance and may increase innovation costs. Some LLM risks emerge only in real-world use, including jailbreak prompts that bypass content filters.

The passage calls for human-centered, safe, secure, and trustworthy AI governance through industry-academia-policymaker collaboration, forward-looking rules, and both top-down and bottom-up approaches. Developers, users, researchers, and communities should transparently report issues; governments and companies should create channels to investigate risks and promptly update regulations; and social-computing techniques should help identify regulatory needs in specific communities. The whitepaper is a joint Microsoft Research Asia Societal AI effort involving industry and academic researchers.

Detroit’s defense has restricted shooting lanes and applied high pressure, while strong goalies and tight team defense have created a physical net-front battle. Ron Francis hit the post, and the team is close to scoring. Fans have energized the team throughout the playoffs.

PGMC renewed its contract to supply 1.5 million WMT of medium-grade, higher-iron nickel ore to Guangdong Century Tsingshan for the 2018 mining season at prevailing market prices. The subsidiary targets six million WMT of shipments this year, subject to weather, and has supplied the Chinese company since 2014. Global Ferronickel’s 2017 income surged over 20 times to P779.7 million, while revenue rose 54% to P5.8 billion, shipments increased 39%, and average realized prices rose 5% to $19.29 per WMT. Shares fell 2.70% to P2.52.

Rich celebrities have frequently turned fortunes and family money into eponymous business ventures, and most of the ventures profiled failed to make a profit.

Millie Mackintosh, 28, whose great-grandfather invented Quality Street, launched her bohemian clothing range in 2014 through Asos after fame on Made In Chelsea. Her umbrella company Cammac Trading lost £182,833 in its first year; liquidators were brought in over £548,000 owed to Cammac Ventures, she reportedly lost £178,000, and she is shutting the business down, discounting her clothes online by up to 75 per cent.

Healthy eating blogger Ella Mills (Deliciously Ella), 26, born into an estimated £40 million, opened three London delis in 12 months in 2015 via The Mae Deli Limited, run with husband Matthew Mills. It lost £723,811 in its first year; she has closed the Marylebone and Herne Hill shops, leaving one open, with the future of around 40 staff unclear. Her separate main Deliciously Ella firm made £545,497 last year.

Trinny Woodall, 54, co-presenter of What Not To Wear, launched a 59-product make-up range, Trinny London, in March 2014. It made an initial £56,281 profit then a £70,089 loss, but backers including Charles Saatchi have invested £2.7 million, lifting assets to £1.83 million.

Bernie Ecclestone's daughters also struggled. Tamara's Show Beauty haircare, priced up to £199 and sold at Harrods, lost £102,547 in its first year and £8.23 million in later years; after investing £15 million she resigned as director in 2015, transferring 75 per cent to a Seychelles investment company, and the renamed SBD International recorded a £4 million loss. Petra's handbag company Stark (£400–£3,000 bags) was put on hold in 2015 as losses grew from £706,005 to £1.4 million and debts reached £4.23 million; she convinced Companies House four times not to dissolve it before applying to wind it up in January.

Alexa Chung's Alpha Charlie, launched in 2015, lost £65,248, £75,000 and £1.5 million in successive years and owes creditors over £260,000. Wealthy friends have pumped in nearly £3 million, leaving £1.4 million in the bank; her TV production firm The Last Battalion was liquidated with a £3.4 million surplus.

Kate Rothschild's Roundtable Records, founded in 2010 to sign Jay Electronica, owed her £365,606 in 2014 against £6,826 in assets and £761 in cash, with its website shut; she wound it up in 2016.

Sadie Frost co-founded Frost French with Jemima French in 1999 and won an Elle Designers of the Year award in 2004, but debts reached £4.2 million by 2008. A Norwegian film producer's investment and a renaming did not stem losses; the King's Road flagship closed in 2011 and the company was dissolved last year, with a planned relaunch never happening though Floozie swimwear remains at Debenhams. Additional reporting: Alun Palmer.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson’s 2022 investiture ceremony occurred after she had served on the Supreme Court for three months. As the most junior justice, she records notes during private conferences.

A possible government shutdown could force federal courts to delay trials and hearings because of limited budgets, while the Supreme Court is expected to continue operating using permanent funds. The Roberts Court marked 20 years under Chief Justice John Roberts and entered a new term facing disputes over elections, free speech, executive power, and other major issues. Nearly half of state attorneys general asked federal officials to support challenging a 2008 ruling barring the death penalty for child rape when the victim survives. Separately, 300 former Michigan athletes plans to appeal the dismissal of their NIL rights lawsuit against the NCAA and Big Ten Network.

Venezuelan citizens asked the Supreme Court to preserve a temporary order protecting their status in the United States. The justices were considering certiorari petitions, with the 2025–26 term beginning October 6.

The passage also recounted Warren Burger’s private discussions with President Nixon, Burger’s role in establishing a test for obscenity, and the unanimous decision in United States v. Nixon. It noted renewed Supreme Court consideration of ending birthright citizenship and other pending litigation involving the Trump administration.

The ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1942, Volume II: Europe* was generated on May 28, 2018. It reproduces the full volume in a portable format with full-text search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access. The edition seeks fidelity to the printed original; readers are advised to cite persistent document numbers rather than page numbers. Older volumes also include bracketed document numbers corresponding to cross-referenced pages.

The preface presents the compilation and editing principles set out in Department of State Regulation 045 of December 5, 1960. *Foreign Relations* is designated the official record of U.S. foreign policy and includes, subject to security considerations, documents comprehensively documenting major policy decisions and relevant background. Editing is to follow historical objectivity, without altering text, making undisclosed deletions, or omitting facts important to decisions. The Historical Office, Bureau of Public Affairs, supervised preparation under G. Bernard Noble, with E. R. Perkins directing the Foreign Relations staff. Rogers P. Churchill, Francis C.
