Prescott, Herbert A. Fine, and N. O. Sappington compiled sections of the volume, while the Division of Publishing Services handled copy editing, proofreading, and indexes.

Salem, Oregon, warned that an algae bloom in Detroit Lake produced low levels of cyanotoxins in drinking water. Children under 6, pregnant or nursing women, immunocompromised people, dialysis patients, people with liver conditions, and pets were told not to drink tap water and to use bottled water for drinking, formula, ice, and food preparation. Bottled-water shortages drove residents to Woodburn, while officials planned no distribution points. Retailers expected shipments, fresh test results were due Thursday, and some businesses closed amid reports of price-gauging.

Eurozone stocks slumped as the euro pressured the dollar and traders awaited US payrolls data. Frankfurt’s DAX fell 1.7%, Paris’ CAC 40 1.6%, and STOXX 600 1.4%; Deutsche Bank dropped 6.21% after tax reforms caused a last-year loss.

The paper addresses learning finite-trace Linear Temporal Logic (LTLf) formulas that separate positive traces from negative ones. It proposes treating Boolean and temporal operators separately through Boolean Set Cover, a weighted problem of constructing a minimal positive Boolean formula that covers all positive elements and no negative elements. The problem is NP-complete, but solution existence can be checked in polynomial time.

The framework first enumerates LTLf formulas with the optimized VFB algorithm, which uses bottom-up enumeration, bitwise characteristic tables, and observational equivalence. It then collapses tables into characteristic vectors, applies domination-based pruning, and combines generated formulas using beam search and divide-and-conquer. The resulting Rust tool, Bolt, is released with a consolidated suite of 15,595 tasks across ten benchmark families.

Experiments show that Bolt substantially improves over Scarlet, solving 14,374 versus 11,468 tasks, returning solutions over 100 times faster on most benchmarks, and producing smaller or equal formulas in 98% of cases. Bolt is competitive with the GPU-based algorithm despite the latter’s greater parallelism and operator restrictions. Ablation results confirm that Boolean Set Cover enables more hard tasks to be solved. The authors also identify applications beyond LTLf learning, including regular expressions, Boolean circuits, and bit-vector programs.

On February 9, 2017, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The filing included Exhibit 99.1, a press release titled “NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for the Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2017,” and Exhibit 99.2, CFO Commentary from Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress. The materials were furnished, not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act, and could not be incorporated by reference into NVIDIA’s SEC filings.

End interviews promptly and confidently. After a good conversation, stand, offer a quick handshake, thank the interviewer, and leave without asking when a decision will be made. Strong candidates focus on the opportunity, ask needed questions, and convey confidence rather than desperation.

Cornell researcher Adam Anderson and Daniel H. Lee found that people can identify six basic emotions—sadness, disgust, anger, joy, fear and surprise—from eye expressions alone. Participants consistently matched eye expressions with corresponding emotions, and eye openness was the strongest feature for interpreting mental states. Narrowed eyes were associated with discrimination-related states such as suspicion and disapproval, while open eyes were linked to sensitivity-related states such as curiosity. Other features, including eyebrow position and wrinkles, conveyed positive or negative emotions. Comparisons with other facial regions showed that eyes provide more robust emotional cues. The findings support Darwin’s theory that facial expressions originally evolved for sensory functions before being used for social communication.

Funding shortages and teachers’ SSLC-evaluation and election-related duties led Karnataka’s education department to cancel this year’s summer camps for government schools. The free programme, launched in 2017-18, taught Mathematics, Science, and extracurricular activities to Class 5 and 6 students.

Football offensive positions involve specialized roles aimed at advancing the ball, gaining field position, and scoring.

- **Quarterback:** Leads the offense, handles the ball on every play, analyzes the defense, and passes or hands off. Quarterbacks may call an “audible” before the snap to change the play or pass routes.
- **Running back:** Primarily carries the ball on rushing plays but may also catch passes and block. He follows offensive linemen’ blocks, finds gaps, and secures the ball against defenders.
- **Tight end:** Combines the duties of a wide receiver and offensive lineman. He blocks on running plays, runs routes on passing plays, and may create space for others. “Sniffer” tight ends typically play away from the line, move before the snap, emphasize blocking, and catch passes; attached tight ends line up next to the offensive tackle and are more of a vertical passing threat.
- **Offensive line:** Five linemen—two tackles, two guards, and a center—block for running and passing plays. Tackles defend the outside edges, with the left tackle protecting a right-handed quarterback’s blind side. Guards commonly use double-team or pulling blocks. The center, positioned in the middle, touches the ball on every play and communicates defensive adjustments.
- **Wide receiver:** Catches passes, runs routes, changes direction quickly, creates separation, and may block on running plays. The three main types are the physical split end (X), the faster flanker (Z), and the smaller slot receiver, who operates between the outside receiver and tackle.

Vegreville’s study predicts that relocating the federal immigration processing centre to Edmonton would cause lasting population loss, lower property values and higher unemployment. The centre employs 236 workers.

Brendon Naidoo, DJ Zinhle’s boyfriend, was granted R50,000 bail on multiple fraud charges involving an alleged foreign-exchange trading scam. He must report to Sandton Police twice weekly and return to court on May 5.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for demonstrating macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting electric circuits.

Job interviews range from conventional to elaborate “disruptor” processes involving silly hypothetical questions and riddles. When asked whether you have questions, candidates are advised to take control by asking their own.

A non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint investigated antimicrobial resistance in untreated wastewater across metropolitan and non-metropolitan Western Uttar Pradesh, India, during 2020–2021. Fifteen triplicate samples from drainage systems in three zones underwent culture, bacterial identification, susceptibility testing against 19 antibiotics in eight classes, ESBL screening, and colistin testing. Of 150 Enterobacteriaceae isolates identified, 93 were E. coli, 36 were K. pneumoniae, 12 were other Enterobacteriaceae, and nine were unidentified mixed populations. Overall, 111 isolates (74%) resisted at least one tested antibiotic, including 88 ESBL-producing isolates; carbapenem resistance was 36.05%, and ciprofloxacin resistance was 67.5%. The reported multidrug-resistant population included E. coli (57.14%), K. pneumoniae (28.57%), and Pantoea agglomerans (5.71%). Zone 1 had the highest overall MDR proportion, although differences among zones were not significant (p=0.85); MDR prevalence was significantly higher in K. pneumoniae than E. coli (p=0.0081). Colistin resistance was detected in Zones 1 and 2 and in other Enterobacteriaceae, including Pantoea species. The authors associated these findings with indiscriminate antibiotic use during COVID-19 and inadequate wastewater treatment, and recommended periodic AMR surveillance, molecular studies of resistance genes, improved infrastructure, and stronger antimicrobial stewardship and policy.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed Eric Simmons’s and Anthony Davis’s convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in more than three grams of cocaine and affirmed Davis’s 40-year sentence. Simmons and Davis participated with Der-rius Purtee, Miko Harris, and Antonio Dawson in packaging and selling cocaine in Marion, Indiana. Two controlled purchases at the 9th Street apartment involved 1.61 and 1.51 grams of cocaine, and two additional purchases occurred that day at the Boots Street apartment.

The court held that Indiana law does not categorically bar aggregating cocaine involved in multiple transactions when proving conspiracy. The coordinated transportation, packaging, and sales, considered together, sufficiently supported a finding of an intentional agreement to deal in at least three grams. Davis could not challenge inconsistent verdicts because only one charge remained against him. Simmons’s conspiracy conviction and dealing acquittal were reconcilable because the conspiracy required only one alleged overt act, and Davis—not Simmons—directly sold cocaine to the informant.

Davis argued that his sentence violated Blakely because the trial court relied on improper aggravators. Although his probation status and need for correctional treatment could not support enhancement, his criminal history alone would have justified the same 40-year sentence beyond a reasonable doubt, making the error harmless.

PLL and analog supply rails should use ferrite beads with at least one device-side capacitor; an additional input capacitor can form a Pi filter. Place filters near device pins, with the device-side capacitor closest. Adjacent PLL pins may share a supply, while analog pins require individual filters. TI recommends 0.1 µF decoupling capacitors in the smallest practical package, no larger than 0402, at least one per two power pins, and one 10 µF-or-larger bulk capacitor per roughly ten power pins. Excessive capacitance must not alter supply startup sequencing, and reset should remain asserted until supplies are stable.

The device supports power-on, external warm, emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold and warm, test, and module-local resets. POR resets the entire chip, including test, emulation, and EMAC logic; warm resets exclude test and emulation logic and may leave the EMAC Switch isolated. POR requires supplies and input clocks to be stable before deassertion, while warm-reset supplies and clocks should already be stable. During reset, most I/O pins enter Hi-Z, PRCM modules are reset, PLLs operate in bypass mode, and BTMODE is latched before the Cortex-A8 starts from the Boot ROM. Simultaneous reset requests are resolved by priority. RSTOUT_WD_OUT reflects reset status, is always asserted for watchdog resets, and is three-stated during POR or external RESET assertion.

PCI Express and the EMAC Switch support reset isolation. PCI Express software must idle the subsystem before reset and re-enumerate the bus afterward; device-level resets other than Test Reset also reset it and require a downstream hot reset. Setting RESET_ISO.ISO_CONTROL isolates the EMAC Switch, its reference PLL, selected registers, and some pin multiplexing during applicable resets except POR. Each power domain also has dedicated warm and cold resets triggered by global reset types or power-state transitions. Reset timing requires stable clocks and valid BTMODE setup and hold intervals.

Device clocks derive from DEV and optional AUX inputs through PLLs and dividers. DEV is generally 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under specified restrictions; optional AUX clocks also support 20–30 MHz. Inputs may use external crystals with internal oscillators or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. Crystal circuits require load capacitors connected to the associated oscillator ground, with components placed close to the MXI, MXO, and ground pins. SERDES requires a low-jitter differential clock with AC-coupling capacitors near the processor. The device contains 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs, all entering bypass mode after reset; PLL_USB must operate at 960 MHz. PLL, SYSCLK, and module-clock limits must be observed. AINTC prioritizes up to 128 requests for the Cortex-A8, while the C674x controller combines 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts and supports multiplexing of selected events.

AC timing uses a 1.5-V reference for 3.3-V signals and a 4-V/ns input slew rate. Board-routing delays are not included in specified timings; TI recommends IBIS-based analysis, except for the DDR2 interface, which has dedicated PCB routing rules.

Peripheral guidance covers two DCAN interfaces; a 64-channel EDMA controller with access to 512 parameter entries; Advanced Event Triggering with breakpoints, watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing; Cortex-A8 and system trace; and JTAG emulation and boundary scan. The three-port gigabit EMAC switch supports MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII, 10/100/1000-Mbit/s operation, MDIO PHY management, and 3.3-V PHYs. Four 32-channel GPIO modules provide configurable inputs, outputs, and interrupts. The GPMC supports multiplexed 8/16-bit external-memory interfaces up to 512 MB across eight chip selects, while the ELM locates NAND errors using BCH syndromes. The HDMI 1.3a interface requires controlled TMDS impedance, DDC pullups, and ESD protection with no more than 5 pF capacitance. HDVPSS provides display processing, video capture, compositing, format conversion, and digital outputs. Video DAC layouts require short, isolated analog paths, matched 75-Ω impedances, and close placement of feedback resistors and external amplification components. Four I2C modules support Philips specification 2.1, 10–400-Kbps operation, seven- and ten-bit addressing, multimaster modes, and 32-byte FIFOs.

Construction began at Fort Buford in 1866 near Williston, where the Missouri and Yellowstone rivers meet. The post served until Sitting Bull surrendered there in 1881. Poor cooking and scarce fruits and vegetables caused scurvy, while frozen rivers disrupted steamboat supplies. Boredom and alcohol led some soldiers to wound themselves to leave the army. A 1876 report described insanity cases and a well-stocked library. A museum opened in 1963, and other structures have since been restored.

Flippy, a burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has begun working as a grill cook at a Caliburger restaurant in Pasadena. The wheeled robot uses AI, sensors, cameras, and interchangeable tools to grill about 150 burgers per hour, but staff must add patties, cheese, condiments, and wrap sandwiches. Miso and Caliburger say Flippy works alongside employees rather than replacing them. Caliburger has six months of exclusive use, after which other vendors could buy it for about $60,000 per unit.

John Essey’s Pittsburgh-area home uses Internet of Things technology to unlock doors, adjust lights and thermostats, and detect leaks. Carnegie Mellon researcher Gierad Laput’s team developed a wall-plug sensor that monitors about a dozen environmental factors, including sound, vibration, and light, and wirelessly reports activity to a computer. He sees domestic and commercial uses, such as detecting an active stove or low supplies. Critics warn that manufacturers may prioritize surveillance and profit over security, while insufficient device security could enable more precise, potentially harmful automated actions.

Deutsche Telekom, Nokia and the Hamburg Port Authority will test 5G across Hamburg’s 8,000-hectare port, including traffic-light management, sensor data processing, environmental monitoring and VR for infrastructure safety. The trial will test multiple live network slices, a first in Germany, to adapt networks to different application requirements.

The team attributes its playoff success to focusing on one game at a time, with two wins still needed, rather than dwelling on the larger picture. A key player is praised for his hard work, few mistakes, and leadership, and he could prove decisive late in the season. The goaltender says poor ice and glass make puck retrieval difficult, requiring more defensive play, while noting that winning the Stanley Cup allows players to share it with loved ones and causes such as a children’s cancer hospital. An Avalanche player is described as fast, talented, and difficult to contain. The team has greater offensive skill this postseason but continues to emphasize goaltending and defense. With the series nearly complete, it expects a difficult finish and must play a solid game to advance.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 26, 2021 reported third-quarter net sales of $81.434 billion, up 36% from $59.685 billion a year earlier. Product sales were $63.948 billion and services sales were $17.486 billion. Gross margin increased to 43.3% from 38.0%, while operating income rose to $24.126 billion, net income nearly doubled to $21.744 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased to $1.30 from $0.65. For the first nine months, net sales were $282.457 billion, net income was $74.129 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $4.38.

Third-quarter sales increased across all categories: iPhone rose 50%, Mac 16%, iPad 12%, Wearables, Home and Accessories 36%, and Services 33%. Growth also occurred in every geographic segment, led by Greater China at 58%, followed by Europe at 34%, Americas at 33%, Japan at 30%, and Rest of Asia Pacific at 28%. Product gross margin benefited from higher volume, product mix, foreign-currency strength, and improved leverage, while Services margin benefited from higher sales, services mix, foreign-currency strength, and leverage.

At June 26, 2021, Apple reported $329.840 billion of assets, $265.560 billion of liabilities, and $64.280 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $34.050 billion, and current and non-current marketable securities totaled $159.594 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $83.838 billion. Apple repurchased 515 million shares for $65.5 billion during the period and declared $10.755 billion of dividends and dividend equivalents.

The filing described revenue-recognition policies, financial instruments and hedging practices, debt, taxes, share-based compensation, and segment reporting. It also disclosed the European Commission State Aid Decision, under which an adjusted €12.7 billion recovery amount excluding interest remained restricted in escrow pending legal proceedings. Material legal matters included an appealed $503 million VirnetX verdict, a court-approved $310 million iOS performance-management settlement, an appealed €1.1 billion French Competition Authority fine, and the pending Optis proceedings. Management also reported continuing effects of COVID-19 on retail operations and employees, although substantially all offices and stores had reopened subject to restrictions.

Prosecutors dropped attempted murder and aggravated-assault charges against 18-year-old Jack Sawyer, who was accused of planning a mass shooting at his former Vermont high school, after the state Supreme Court ruled that preparation alone did not prove attempted aggravated murder. Sawyer will face lesser charges of criminal threatening and weapon carrying and has pleaded not guilty. His bail was set at $100,000, with conditions including a curfew, supervision by his father and no contact with school personnel. The case led to Vermont gun restrictions that do not apply retroactively.

Only 12 albums have spent at least 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 since 2000. Taylor Swift and Morgan Wallen each have three, while Adele has two. Adele’s “21” logged 24 nonconsecutive weeks; Wallen’s “Dangerous: The Double Album” debuted with 10 straight No. 1 weeks; Bad Bunny’s “Un Verano Sin Ti” spent 13 weeks atop the chart; and Swift’s “The Tortured Poets Department” recorded 12 consecutive weeks and 17 overall. Wallen’s “One Thing at a Time” surpassed “Un Verano Sin Ti” for the most weeks at No. 1 this decade.

The device supports reset isolation for the PCI Express and Ethernet Switch subsystems. The PCI Express subsystem can be reset independently: in Root Complex mode, software must place it in IDLE before resetting through the PRCM, then re-enumerate the bus and treat all endpoints as newly connected. In Endpoint mode, an in-band reset generates an interrupt that software handles by entering IDLE and asserting the local reset. Device-level resets other than Test Reset also reset PCI Express, requiring a downstream hot reset and bus re-enumeration. Ethernet Switch isolation is enabled through the RESET_ISO ISO_CONTROL bit; when enabled, eligible resets do not disrupt switch traffic or reset the switch function, its reference-clock PLL, selected control registers, or affected pin multiplexing.

RSTOUT_WD_OUT indicates device reset status, remains asserted during watchdog reset, and is tri-stated with its internal pull disabled during power-on or external reset. When BTMODE[11] is latched low, it is also asserted for power-on and external warm resets. Each power domain has dedicated warm and cold resets associated with global resets and transitions between OFF and ON states. Except for Test Reset, resets generally place I/O pins in Hi-Z, with exceptions for emulation pins, isolated Ethernet Switch pins, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT. DDR pins are tri-stated during reset and subsequently driven according to their internal pull-reset values, while PINCNTL registers return to defaults unless Ethernet Switch isolation prevents selected resets. After reset, the Cortex-A8 begins executing Boot ROM code that configures pins for the primary and backup boot modes.

Device clocks derive from DEV and optional AUX inputs, which may use internal oscillators with external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. The DEV clock is generally 20 MHz but may range from 20–30 MHz under specified exceptions; AUX supports 20–30 MHz and can feed the audio or video PLLs. The PCI Express PHY requires a low-jitter differential clock that is AC-coupled and placed near the device. Optional AUD_CLKIN inputs support up to 50 MHz, CLKIN32 can provide a 32.768-kHz reference, and CLKOUT0/1 can select among several clock sources. The device has 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs, generally referenced by the DEV clock, with selected PLLs able to use AUX. All PLLs start in bypass mode, require filtered external supplies, and must be programmed within defined reference, intermediate, output, SYSCLK, and module-frequency limits.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller prioritizes up to 128 requests and generates IRQs or FIQs with programmable priorities; general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. The C674x controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts, permits events 15–95 to be selected from 24 multiplexed events, and controls CPU exceptions, NMI, and emulation interrupts. Timing specifications use a 1.5-V reference for 3.3-V signals and a 4-V/ns input slew rate. Board-routing delays must be included in timing analysis, with IBIS models recommended except for DDR2.

Two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0A/B, configurable message-object masks and FIFOs, loopback, automatic bus-on recovery, test-mode Message RAM access, configurable CAN pins, and interrupts. EDMA provides up to 64 channels, and each synchronization event may be mapped to any of 512 parameter entries. Advanced Event Triggering supports hardware breakpoints, data watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing. Real-time trace can export Cortex-A8 or system trace data to an embedded buffer or five-pin interface without affecting execution. JTAG supports debugging and boundary scan, includes an internal TRST pulldown, and identifies the device with a JTAG ID of 0x0B8F202F.

The Ethernet MAC Switch is a three-port gigabit switch with one internal and two external ports. External ports support 10Base-T, 100BaseTX, and full-duplex 1000BaseT through MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes. A shared MDIO interface polls 32 addresses and controls multiple external PHYs. Ethernet I/O operates at 3.3 V, and transmit underflow errors are signaled by intentionally corrupting frame CRCs rather than using MTXER. CPPI provides 2,048 words of buffer-descriptor memory for up to 512 descriptors.

The GPIO subsystem contains four 32-channel modules, providing up to 128 configurable 1.8-V/3.3-V pins with input, output, set/clear, interrupt, keyboard, and open-drain functions. The GPMC supports glueless external-memory interfaces for NOR and NAND flash, SRAM, Pseudo-SRAM, and custom devices through an 8- or 16-bit bus, up to eight chip selects, and 512 MB of addressing. The ELM locates NAND errors from BCH syndromes for 4-, 8-, and 16-bit error correction and can report completion.

The HDMI transmitter supports HDMI 1.3a video and audio, DDC, optional CEC, multichannel L-PCM, and specified video/color-depth modes. PCB guidance requires controlled TMDS impedance, paired vias, DDC pullups, grounded TMDS shields, and an ESD protection device with no more than 5 pF of capacitance. The HDVPSS provides input capture, output interfaces, scaling, deinterlacing, alpha blending, color conversion, compositing, and graphics layers. Analog video outputs support internal-amplifier Normal mode or TVOUT Bypass mode and require matched, short 75-Ω routing.

Four I2C modules support Philips I2C 2.1-compatible standard and fast modes from 10–400 Kbps, seven- and ten-bit addressing, multimaster operation, noise filtering, and a 32-byte FIFO, but not CBUS devices or fail-safe buffers. The Imaging Subsystem accepts parallel or serial camera data, performs ISP corrections, color processing, compression, and RGB/YUV conversion, and supports flash-strobe and shutter control. The dedicated memory interface supports DDR2 and DDR3 devices with 16- or 32-bit paths, capacities from 64 Mb to 4 Gb, two chip selects, independent PHYs, dynamic interleaving, associated electrical timing, and mandatory PCB routing rules.

On October 22, 2001, U.S. stocks rose on stronger-than-expected earnings despite anthrax concerns. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.9% to 9,377.03, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 2.2% to 1,708.06. American Express and semiconductor stocks led gains, while warnings about fourth-quarter profits tempered the rally. The Conference Board’s U.S. leading-indicators index fell 0.5% in September, its largest monthly decline since January 1996.

Enron shares fell about 21% to $20.65 after the company acknowledged that the SEC had requested information concerning related-party transactions involving partnerships managed by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron called the request an informal inquiry, pledged full cooperation and said auditors, attorneys and the board had reviewed, approved and disclosed the arrangements. The company had announced a $35 million partnership-related charge, the repurchase of 55 million shares that reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion, and a third-quarter loss of roughly $618 million to $638 million after $1.01 billion in charges and write-downs. Analysts raised concerns that dismantling other affiliated partnerships could cost as much as $3 billion and dilute shareholders.

A Texas shareholder filed a derivative suit alleging that Enron’s board breached fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to operate the partnerships and benefit from conflicts of interest. A separate securities-fraud class action covered Enron stock purchases from July 13 through October 16, 2001, and alleged that the defendants misrepresented and concealed material facts about the partnerships. Enron said it had not yet reviewed the derivative suit and did not comment on pending litigation.

UniPrime Capital also announced a letter of intent with Jessel Enterprises for a partial interest in an Enron Wind ground lease covering more than 3,000 acres in California’s Tehachapi Valley, with projected annual revenue of $96 million.

The Secretary and Dobrynin discussed possible expansion of US-Soviet bilateral cooperation, including an inventory of agreements categorized as cancelled, lapsed, ongoing, or close to agreement. Dobrynin identified arms control, especially INF and START, as the most important area for progress, while the Secretary preferred negotiations in Geneva but did not object to discussing them in a future Shultz-Gromyko meeting. Other proposed topics included radiological and chemical weapons, conventional arms transfers, Indian Ocean deployments, nonproliferation, South Africa, the Middle East, the Prague Declaration, and regional conflicts. The Secretary maintained that human rights and regional issues, including Poland, Kampuchea, Afghanistan, and Central America, must remain on the agenda.

An accompanying memorandum expressed uncertainty about whether constructive change in US-Soviet relations was possible because of Soviet leadership changes and limited prior effort. It argued that US military, economic, and diplomatic recovery had restored American strength and that Soviet military setbacks made direct conflict unlikely, favoring negotiation to restrain US military expansion.

Clio founder and CEO Jack Newton discusses the company’s $1 billion acquisition of global legal research platform vLex, which expands Clio’s nearly end-to-end legal practice management capabilities. The deal follows Clio’s growth, a $3 billion valuation last year, and acquisitions of ShareDo and Lawyaw. Newton also addresses AI and what to expect from Clio, whose Cloud Conference is scheduled for Oct. 16–17 in Boston with Esther Perel and JJ Velazquez among the featured speakers.

Tyreek Hill suffered a season-ending knee dislocation after twisting his left leg late in the third quarter of Miami’s Week 4 game against the Jets. He had six catches for 67 yards before being carted to the locker room and taken to a hospital for imaging and evaluation. The full extent of ligament and tendon damage remains unknown, and no official return timeline has been established. He is not expected to return in 2025, and a lengthy recovery and possible surgery are anticipated.

UFC 216 in Las Vegas will feature Demetrious Johnson seeking an 11th consecutive title defense against Ray Borg and an interim lightweight title fight between Tony Ferguson and Kevin Lee. The card follows Sunday’s mass shooting, which killed 58 and injured nearly 500; UFC pledged $1 million for victims and families.

The study examines how science education contributes to citizenship education in Turkey through a review of the 2018 science curriculum and interviews with eight science teachers. Curriculum and teacher data were analyzed thematically. Although the curriculum adopts a science-technology-society-environment approach and emphasizes scientific, technological, and environmental literacy, it does not explicitly link science to citizenship education. Teachers nevertheless associated science lessons with scientific literacy, critical thinking, inquiry, problem-solving, environmental responsibility, health and safety, civic duty, patriotism, and active participation. The strongest connections involved the environment, society, and scientific literacy, while links between technology and citizenship were limited. Teachers reported that exam-centered instruction, overcrowded classrooms, inadequate laboratories and materials, curricular limitations, and communication difficulties hindered these goals. The study recommends explicitly incorporating citizenship skills, socio-scientific issues, environmental education, hands-on activities, and democratic participation into science curricula, while providing teachers with training and support aligned with Sustainable Development Goals.

The passage examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and educational robotics in early childhood education and how future preschool and primary school teachers perceive robots. It emphasizes that AI can personalize learning, provide feedback, and support digital, computational, and algorithmic competencies. Educational robots can enrich preschool environments, support inclusive education and children with special needs, foster social-emotional and inquiry skills, and encourage interest in engineering and science. Their integration requires trained teachers, suitable curricula, attention to children’s needs, physical safety, privacy, and equitable access.

The study used a mixed-method approach and analyzed drawings and open-ended responses from 121 final-year students at the University of Belgrade’s Faculty of Education: 75 future preschool teachers and 46 future primary school teachers. Participants completed a Draw-And-Answer-Test, describing a robot, its perceived environment and role, and their reasons for depicting it. Two independent evaluators coded the responses, achieving a Pearson correlation of 0.99.

Most participants accurately represented robots, while 22 of the original 143 respondents held misconceptions: robots were mistakenly depicted as electrical appliances, humanoid figures, virtual-reality equipment, or avatars. Most of the final sample had encountered robots in person, and future preschool teachers reported substantially more direct experience than future primary school teachers.

Animal-shaped robots were the most common depiction, representing 47.1% of responses, followed by typical robots at 24.8%, mechanical objects at 24%, and humanoid robots at 4.1%. Most drawings conveyed no emotion. Educational functions were most frequently attributed to robots, followed by assistive functions; animal-shaped robots were primarily associated with education, while mechanical robots were commonly viewed as assistive.

Most participants first encountered robots at their faculty, often through animal-shaped educational robots such as Bee-Bot. Robot choices were most often explained by practical and cognitive considerations, followed by personal interest and direct experience, although 26.4% could not clearly identify the basis for their choice.

The findings indicate generally sound understandings but also a need to address misconceptions. The authors recommend more purposeful use of educational robots, curriculum development by specialized teams, and continued teacher training to support safe, inclusive, and pedagogically effective robotics education.

Veteran tackle Byron Bell agreed to join the Green Bay Packers, adding competition at right tackle. Bell started 56 of 62 games at right tackle for Carolina and all 16 games for Tennessee. With Bryan Bulaga recovering from a torn ACL, Bell could compete for the starting job.

The passage frames Education 4.0 within the Fourth Industrial Revolution, emphasizing adaptable, future-ready learners with critical, creative and higher-order thinking skills. It presents India’s National Education Policy 2020 as supporting personalized, flexible and competency-based learning through technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain and smart devices. Teaching and learning should move beyond rote instruction and memory-based assessment toward individualized, inclusive and skill-based approaches.

Digital games and gamification are identified as engaging pedagogical tools that can promote intrinsic motivation, meaningful and immersive learning, incidental learning, problem-solving and the development of cognitive and non-cognitive skills. Their elements—goals, rules, challenges, feedback, interaction and multiple solutions—closely align with effective instructional design. Digital Game-Based Learning can use commercial games or customized games built around defined learning outcomes. It supports multimodal environments, adaptive and learner-centered assessment, and the identification of higher-order skills such as analytical thinking, decision-making, adaptability and critical judgment.

Digital games can also support flexible, competency-based assessment through observable gameplay data, immediate feedback and adaptive testing. Stealth Assessment embeds assessment within gameplay, allowing learning to be measured continuously without explicit learner awareness or excessive test anxiety. AI-based machine-learning algorithms analyze digital traces of performance and infer competencies such as problem-solving, creativity, persistence, attention and reading comprehension, then provide suitable new challenges and tailored support.

Effective stealth assessment depends on evidence-centered design, machine-learning algorithms, formative assessment and feedback. Evidence-centered design identifies relevant competencies, observable evidence, suitable tasks and reliable links between gameplay indicators and competency models. Its development requires multidisciplinary contributions from education, psychology, technology, programming and related fields.

Challenges include limited adoption among teachers, insufficient evidence, the complexity of customized game development, possible cognitive overload, and the need to calibrate difficulty appropriately. The validity and reliability of digital game-based learning and assessment remain underdeveloped, requiring extensive research across technological and educational dimensions.

Out-of-bounds plays require preparation, simple execution, practice, and knowledge of baseline, sideline, and full-court rules. Coaches should focus first on inbounding successfully, then getting the ball to the best players for a high-percentage shot. Players need to master passing, vision, communication, timing, and defensive reads while using simple cuts, give-and-go actions, and appropriate lob passes. Teams should scout opponents, anticipate defensive tactics, and teach counters. The designated inbounder cannot be replaced, must pass within five seconds, and cannot touch the ball until another player does. Timeouts must be requested before five seconds elapse. Movement from the throw-in spot is generally limited to one step, though after a made basket the inbounder may move along the baseline. Passing into the backcourt is legal, an untouched out-of-bounds pass returns to the original throw-in spot, and throwing over the backboard or directly into the basket is prohibited. Defenders reaching over the out-of-bounds plane to touch the ball receive a technical foul. Coaches should test players’ rule knowledge and review missed questions.

Medina City School District will place a permanent 5.2-mill substitute levy on the May 8 ballot, replacing its expiring five-year 5.9-mill operating levy. At a Kids First Medina rally, supporters said the levy would maintain and expand programs, including reinstating high school French and funding free all-day kindergarten. They also said homeowners could see a slight tax decrease when a bond issue ends.

The lecture surveys experimental studies of neutrino oscillations, comparing sources, baseline lengths, energies, mass sensitivity, and neutrino flavors. Sources include Big Bang relics, supernovae, cosmic-ray showers, the Sun, accelerators, and reactors.

Solar experiments found fewer electron neutrinos than predicted. While the Homestake chlorine experiment measured this deficit, SNO found the total neutrino count consistent with theory, indicating flavor change rather than loss. Atmospheric neutrinos arise from pion and kaon decays; measurements showed energy- and direction-dependent disappearance of muon neutrinos. Accelerator facilities such as CERN, Fermilab’s NuMI, and T2K use near and far detectors to compare total flux with appearance or disappearance. Reactor experiments measure antielectron-neutrino disappearance through inverse beta decay and probe oscillation survival probabilities over long baselines. The lecture emphasizes the rapid growth of neutrino research and evidence for oscillations after 2000.

After many years, the speaker is excited to have reached this point and says the feelings from playing and winning championships remain strong. They prepare through a pregame skate, brief practice, and stick work, relying on routine and avoiding overthinking to maintain mental energy.

APU students attended The GIG, one of the university’s two formal dances, at La Cañada Flintridge Country Club on Feb. 10. The La La Land–inspired event cost $20 per ticket and featured two dance floors with a DJ and live jazz combo. Organized by the Office of Communiversity, it also offered a cartoonist, photography station, piano area, and outdoor seating overlooking the grounds and city. Students praised the music, atmosphere, activities, and venue, calling the event memorable and among APU’s best dances.

An Ernakulam court convicted Assam migrant labourer Muhammed Ameerul Islam of raping and murdering a 30-year-old Dalit law student in Perumbavoor in April 2016. Judge N Anil Kumar found him guilty of murder and rape-related offences, but not evidence destruction or SC/ST atrocities provisions; sentencing was scheduled for the following day. The trial examined 100 witnesses, while police questioned over 1,500 people and examined 5,000 fingerprints and 20 lakh phone calls.

The discussion paper argues that AI policy and compliance requirements increasingly affect the AI development lifecycle, while AI policy is largely absent from computer science curricula. It synthesizes regulatory developments in the United States and European Union and proposes a framework for incorporating AI governance into computing courses.

The United States has not enacted comprehensive federal AI legislation. Its approach has relied largely on nonbinding initiatives, including the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the American AI Initiative, and the Biden administration’s Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights. Biden’s Executive Order 14110 established policy areas including safety, consumer protection, and privacy, but President Trump rescinded it on January 20, 2025. Trump’s replacement, Executive Order 14179, prioritizes American global AI dominance, economic competitiveness, human flourishing, and national security, and directs agencies to identify potentially inconsistent actions under EO 14110. The shift illustrates ideological polarization between US policies emphasizing safety and trust and those emphasizing economic leadership.

The EU AI Act, approved in March 2024, broadly defines AI systems and regulates them according to risk. High-risk practices face additional management, transparency, and oversight requirements; unacceptable practices, including social scoring and certain biometric surveillance, are prohibited, with limited law-enforcement exceptions. General-purpose AI models face additional transparency and copyright-compliance obligations.

The paper identifies three cross-cutting themes: the rapidly changing and politically volatile US policy landscape; the difficulty of translating abstract or vague policy demands into precise technical controls; and the cross-border effects of regulation, exemplified by the EU’s GDPR-driven “Brussels Effect.” It suggests that AI developers need both technical expertise and policy vocabulary to adapt to shifting demands, recognize technical limitations, and collaborate with policymakers.

The proposed teaching framework combines three perspectives—socio-political, translational, and technical—with three dimensions: scope, power, and agency. The translational perspective connects principles to practices through standardized definitions, measurable reliability and accuracy, consideration of edge cases, and policymaker–developer collaboration. Scope addresses requirements and technical implementation; power examines creators, beneficiaries, harms, oversight, and missing perspectives; agency considers who participated, how practitioners can influence policy, and how implementation choices are measured. Guiding questions combine each perspective and dimension. The flexible framework can support discussions across different courses and policy environments, with future work proposed on targeted classroom activities and applying requirements-engineering practices to AI policy implementation.

An Italian man identified by police as Luca Traini, 28, opened fire on African migrants in Macerata on February 3, 2018, injuring six people, one seriously, in what police called a racially motivated attack. During a penalty kick awarded in normal play, the ball is live and in play once kicked, and action resumes after a save, block, or rebound. Except for the kicker and goalkeeper, attackers must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field, and outside the penalty area. They must wait until the ball is touched and clearly moves forward before entering the penalty area or arc. Players must position themselves promptly, hold ground if they arrive first, and avoid jostling defenders. Every attacking player must be prepared to follow up a save, block, or rebound. The kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does and should clear the way for a teammate after a goal rebound. If the goalkeeper secures the ball, attackers must immediately defend against a counterattack. Procedural offenses result in a retaken kick if the ball enters the goal; otherwise, play is restarted with an indirect free kick.

The study develops and experimentally validates a multiscale framework linking atomic-scale solid–melt interface energetics to macroscopic GaN growth kinetics during self-catalyzed molecular-beam epitaxy. Molecular dynamics simulations show that liquid Ga forms ordered, polarity-dependent layers at GaN interfaces, while charge redistribution is confined mainly to the first one or two layers. Metadynamics-derived free-energy landscapes reveal a “Ga lubrication” mechanism: interfacial liquid Ga lowers nitrogen-adatom migration barriers to about 0.56 eV on Ga-polar and 0.34 eV on N-polar interfaces, compared with roughly 1.1 eV on a clean Ga-polar surface. Step-edge Ehrlich–Schwoebel barriers exceed 0.6 eV and can impede downward step crossing.

Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations parameterized by these barriers show that high nitrogen flux produces rough joint-island growth, whereas lower flux supports diffusion-controlled, layer-by-layer growth. Practical MBE conditions are expected to favor this diffusion-limited regime. A parameter-free continuum model based on concentration and chemical-potential gradients, with inputs from metadynamics, molecular dynamics, and solvation calculations, predicts facet-dependent GaN growth rates of 0.01–0.04 nm/s. The predicted trends agree with GaN particle radii and facet-growth statistics obtained from HRTEM/STEM measurements of particles nitrided for one and five minutes.

The results establish interfacial nitrogen adsorption and migration free-energy profiles as decisive controls on GaN growth because nitrogen has very low solubility in liquid Ga. The framework is presented as transferable to other low-solubility III-V/catalyst systems without empirical fitting. Limitations include omitted impurities, uncertainty in machine-learning interatomic potentials, and simplifying assumptions such as steady-state one-dimensional transport, constant diffusivity, and negligible interfacial accumulation.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition device with a programmable gain amplifier, integrated ADC driver, precision voltage reference, analog front end, alarm functions, and multiSPI interface.

The PGA conditions single-ended or differential inputs, adjusts their common-mode level, and maximizes ADC dynamic-range use. Input range is selected through the four-bit RANGE_SEL field, whose power-on setting of 0000 corresponds to ±3V × VREF. A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter is located at the PGA output, with a typical −3 dB cutoff of 500 kHz. The ADC output uses straight-binary format for bipolar and unipolar ranges, with FSR defined as PFS minus NFS and LSB equal to FSR/2¹⁶.

The device supports an internal or external 4.096 V reference. The internal reference is factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated from −40°C to +125°C, and exposed at REFIO when INTREF_DIS is 0; it requires at least 4.7 µF of decoupling and can shift following soldering or reflow stress. In external-reference mode, REFIO is an input and the internal buffer drives REFCAP, requiring at least 10 µF and a nearby 1 µF capacitor. Neither reference output nor buffer may directly drive external loads.

Active-high alarms are available through ALARM/SDO-1/GPO. Input alarms compare converted values against independently programmable high and low thresholds with common hysteresis. The AVDD alarm uses fixed typical thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Each alarm has an active flag, cleared after the current conversion, and a tripped flag, cleared only when ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status can be accessed through the alarm pin, ALARM_REG, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports SPI-compatible read and write protocols, optional dual SDO outputs, and source-synchronous operation with internal or external clocking. Data transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on its rising edge. An optimal frame contains 32 SCLK cycles; shorter frames cannot write commands, while longer frames use the last 32 shifted bits as the command. Output words can contain conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device addresses, input-range data, alarm flags, and parity.

Single-device configurations support standard SPI or expanded multiSPI pin arrangements, while daisy-chained devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK and require identical configuration-register settings. Devices sample on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, and an N-device chain uses an optimal frame of 32 × N SCLK cycles, returning data from the last device through the first.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Its active-low RST input supports either an application reset or a full power-on reset. Conversion begins on the rising edge of CONVST/CS and ends by returning to ACQ; RVS indicates completion. Data-transfer commands are processed at the end of a frame, with command decoding, output shifting, and status handling coordinated by the interface’s shift registers and protocol unit.

Programming uses nine configuration registers covering device identification, reset/power control, input and output protocols, data-output formatting, range and reference selection, and alarms. Register access supports byte and half-word read, write, set, and clear operations.

An eight-channel industrial input-module example combines an ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to support software-configured voltage or current channels. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and provides NAP and power-down modes for reduced-power operation. Recommended layout and decoupling include separate analog and digital sections, close high-frequency supply bypassing, at least 10 µF plus 1 µF on AVDD, at least 10 µF on DVDD, and specified REFIO or REFCAP capacitors.

A support defender positions themself behind and inside the first defender, goalside and far enough back to react if the attacker is beaten in either direction. Verbal calls include “support,” “you have help,” “jockey/contain,” and “take him/tackle.” If the first defender is beaten, the support defender may take over through a defensive switch. Drills should demonstrate correct positioning, relative movement, and clear communication at half- and full speed.

This study compared air- and bone-conducted auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in 64 infants aged 0–6 months, including 50 who completed testing. Infants were categorized by frequency as having normal hearing or conductive hearing loss (CHL) based on ABR results, with tympanometry and otoacoustic emissions used as cross-checks.

At 500 Hz, infants with CHL had significantly elevated air-conduction ABR and ASSR thresholds compared with normal-hearing infants, while bone-conduction thresholds did not differ significantly between groups. Both methods produced larger air-bone gaps in the CHL group: mean gaps were 36 versus 15 dB for ABR and 21 versus 12 dB for ASSR. However, ASSR showed greater overlap between groups and more poorly separated results than ABR. ABR and ASSR thresholds were poorly correlated, as were their air-bone gaps. No CHL was identified at 2000 Hz.

Minimum normal intensities were 35 dB nHL for 500-Hz air-conduction ABR, 20 dB nHL for bone-conduction ABR, and 40 and 30 dB HL, respectively, for ASSR. At 2000 Hz, minimum intensities were 30 dB nHL for ABR and 40 dB HL for ASSR under both presentation modes.

Air-conduction ABR threshold measurement had the highest sensitivity and specificity for identifying CHL, compared with tympanometry/otoacoustic-emission screening and ASSR measures. The authors concluded that ASSR thresholds and air-bone gaps were insufficiently reliable for distinguishing mild, low-frequency CHL under the tested parameters. ABR remains the recommended primary diagnostic method in Canadian early hearing detection and intervention programs. Limitations included the small sample, mild CHL limited to 500 Hz, lack of sensorineural-loss cases, absence of acoustic-reflex testing, and the inefficient research protocol.

The study examines global, regional, and Ethiopian legal frameworks supporting inclusive education and assesses educational leaders’ awareness of these frameworks in Addis Ababa’s inclusive education resource centers. It addresses a research gap in prior Ethiopian studies, which had focused more on infrastructure, resources, and teacher preparedness than on legal frameworks and policy awareness.

A qualitative case-study design was used. Fifteen participants—school principals, itinerant teachers, classroom teachers, and Ministry of Education inclusion experts—were purposively selected from three resource centers. Data came from semi-structured interviews and reviews of international, regional, national, and school documents, with interviews transcribed and analyzed thematically. Participants provided informed consent, were identified by pseudonyms, and reviewed transcripts for validation.

The document review identified global frameworks including the UDHR, ICERD, Convention on the Rights of the Child, Salamanca Statement, CRPD, Marrakesh Treaty, and Sustainable Development Goals. African frameworks included the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, and African Disability Protocol. Ethiopian frameworks included the Constitution, Proclamation No. 1263/2021, Education and Training Policy 2023, Education Sector Development Plan VI, Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy, and National Children’s Policy. Although these documents provide a favorable legal and policy environment, one Ministry expert noted the absence of a dedicated, stand-alone inclusive education policy.

Awareness varied substantially. Ministry of Education experts and itinerant teachers, many of whom had relevant qualifications and training, demonstrated greater knowledge of international, regional, and national frameworks. School principals generally recognized the importance of inclusion but had limited knowledge of specific policies, while classroom teachers were largely unaware of them and often viewed inclusion primarily as an issue of compassion and fairness. The findings indicate that insufficient policy-focused training and professional development may hinder effective implementation.

The study recommends regular training for educational leaders, incorporation of inclusive education law into teacher and administrator curricula, policy-driven curriculum and school planning, and Ministry-level monitoring of policy awareness. Effective implementation ultimately depends on leaders understanding and applying legal frameworks in leadership and teaching practices.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a Hybrid Rendering model that combines real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores in each Streaming Multiprocessor handle bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing shader multiprocessors for other graphics and compute work. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and efficient BVH structures, RT Cores make ray tracing roughly ten times faster than software-based ray tracing on Pascal GPUs.

Turing ray tracing supports realistic reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. It can improve ray-traced area-light shadows, ambient occlusion, and glossy reflections while producing fewer artifacts than shadow maps, screen-space ambient occlusion, and screen-space or cubemap reflections. NVIDIA also applies ray-tracing acceleration to physics, collision detection, particle and audio simulation, AI visibility queries, and non-real-time path tracing.

NGX is NVIDIA’s Turing-only, deep-learning technology stack. It uses Tensor Cores and provides pre-trained services through a thin API for graphics, rendering, and other client applications. Its features include DLSS, Inpainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained against high-quality 64-times-supersampled references to produce target-resolution images with roughly half the shading work of temporal anti-aliasing; DLSS 2X renders at final resolution and uses a larger network to approach 64-times-supersampled quality. Inpainting synthesizes replacement image content, AI Slow-Mo generates interpolated video frames, and AI Super Rez doubles, quadruples, or octuples image or video resolution using AI-generated pixels.

Mesh Shading adds task and mesh shader stages that use cooperative thread models. Developers can submit many objects at once, choose geometry level of detail dynamically, and cull or modify geometry for effects such as spherical CAD cutaways. This reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enables more than an order-of-magnitude increase in the number of real-time objects.

Variable Rate Shading allows each 16-by-16-pixel region to use one of several shading rates while leaving visibility sampling unchanged. Applications include content-adaptive shading for low-detail or slowly changing regions, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that reduces peripheral shading. VRS can also increase shading up to the applicable multisample count.

Texture Space Shading computes and stores appearance values in texture space, decoupling visibility sampling from appearance sampling. It supports multiple resolutions, temporal stability, cached shading results, and reuse across frames or views, including efficient stereo VR rendering. Multi-View Rendering draws up to four hardware-supported views per pass and up to 32 views through the API, sharing fetched and shaded geometry while supporting view-dependent attributes. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and permits different resource types to share heaps.

Turing improves VR through USB Type-C and VirtualLink support, Multi-View Rendering, foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated ray-traced audio. The TU104 full chip contains six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and one x8 NVLink link. TU106, used by the GeForce RTX 2070, contains three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. The inference-oriented Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with five GPCs, 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

For hybrid workloads, NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS by weighting peak Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations according to representative utilization. The stated example assigns Tensor operations 20%, CUDA cores 80%, RT cores 40%, and INT32 pipelines 28%, producing a reported RTX-OPS value of 78 for the RTX 2080 Ti. The document closes with NVIDIA’s accuracy, warranty, liability, product-use, reproduction, and trademark notices.

Oprah Winfrey told Vogue that she experienced a six-week depression after the 1998 film adaptation of Toni Morrison’s *Beloved* failed at the box office. She described suppressing her feelings, turning to food, and feeling as though a veil separated her from the world. The experience strengthened her gratitude practice and taught her not to place all her hopes and expectations in a film’s commercial success. The President submits a report on Texas and explains why the Executive has not acknowledged its independence, noting Congress previously resolved that recognition should follow satisfactory evidence of a functioning civil government. He argues that recognizing a forcibly separated state can risk war and appear hostile, so U.S. policy has been to avoid interference, await clear evidence, and recognize established authority. Because recognition is not expressly delegated and may involve war, he endorses congressional participation while maintaining the Executive’s duty to state its views.

Although Mexican authority in Texas had been expelled and its forces defeated, Mexico was regrouping and threatening another invasion, making Texas’s independence precarious. Further concerns arose because Texas had once been claimed by the United States, contained many American emigrants, adopted a similar government, and sought admission to the Union. Early recognition might therefore appear to facilitate U.S. acquisition. The President recommends continued nonrecognition until Mexico or another major power recognizes Texas, or until time and events conclusively establish its ability to sustain separate sovereignty.

Classical Maxwell solvers efficiently model nanostructures but cannot capture nonclassical photon correlations or entanglement. Exact quantum methods address these effects but scale poorly and do not naturally couple to Maxwell solvers, while semiclassical approximations may miss nonclassical photon statistics. The paper introduces a stochastic Bloch-vector approach based on SDEs, without wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, or operator-valued noise, to connect open-system quantum dynamics with FDTD-propagated classical fields. It is validated using the resonance-fluorescence Mollow triplet of a coherently driven two-level system, whose sidebands can exhibit nonclassical photon correlations and support photon generation and entanglement schemes. The formulation extends conventional symmetric-diffusion factorization to complex, non-symmetric diffusion matrices, allowing asymmetric noise correlations associated with noncommuting quantum operators.

Chris Pronger received a one-game suspension for a hit to Dean McAMond’s head, and a team representative said the decision must be accepted. He argued, however, that Chris Neil’s hit on Andy McDonald was more dangerous, describing it as deliberate, while calling Pronger’s hit a reaction play. The Executive transmitted to the Senate official departmental reports containing all requested information. Upon taking office, he found California’s military commandant serving as civil governor under arrangements inherited from his predecessor and did not interfere, make an appointment, expand the commandant’s authority, or increase compensation. To aid congressional action under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, he sent Thomas Butler King and other officers to California and New Mexico. He encouraged the territories’ peoples, if prepared to comply with the U.S. Constitution, to draft republican state constitutions and seek admission, while emphasizing that Congress must consent and that domestic policy must originate with the people without executive interference. He had no information about laws passed by a supposed California government or censuses in either territory.

He urged Congress to admit California and New Mexico as states to reduce sectional agitation over involuntary servitude and resolve territorial questions. California’s proposed constitution was nearing submission, and he recommended approval if constitutionally compliant. He advised delaying any congressional territorial government for the remainder of California and opposed organizing one in New Mexico before resolving Texas’s boundary claim, because either including or excluding the disputed district would effectively prejudice the claim. He noted that New Mexico retained Mexican-derived municipal protections and a military presence.

The Executive warned that imposing domestic conditions on California contrary to residents’ wishes would violate self-government, and pledged neither threats nor support for coercion. He expected residents of the remaining Mexican cession, once admitted as a state, to determine their own domestic policy. Finally, he recommended awaiting developments already underway, avoiding geographic parties and unnecessary controversy, and preserving sectional harmony and the strength of the Union.

Saudi Arabia’s government has approved the University of New Haven to establish a branch campus in Riyadh, which the university expects to open next fall and potentially grow to 13,000 undergraduate and graduate students within a decade. The English-language campus will offer preparatory and ESL courses, executive education, microcredentials, and three colleges covering business and digital innovation, engineering and advanced manufacturing, and arts and applied sciences. It is expected to have coed students and faculty, with no anticipated restrictions on academic freedom.

New Haven’s ties to the Saudi royal family and a prior security-college partnership have drawn scrutiny. The university ended that partnership after Saudi agents killed journalist Jamal Khashoggi in 2018 but maintained that it had modernized the college and developed its undergraduate program. Other universities are pursuing Riyadh campuses, including the University of Wollongong. New Haven still needs approval from the New England Commission of Higher Education.

The document standardizes the 4 KB, 4 KB-aligned Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperability between guest operating systems and hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. These technologies encrypt guest register state during world switches. The GHCB mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state layout and defines the minimum state guests expose for Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), while limiting hypervisor access to guest data.

Version 2 introduces initial SEV-SNP support and a hypervisor feature-advertisement bitmap. Revisions add 64-bit SNP guest-request sequence numbers and error reporting, VLEK certificate identifiers, guest APIC ID discovery, multiple VMPL levels, page-state-change support, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, and initial Secure AVIC support.

The GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 for requests. Defined operations include protocol negotiation, CPUID retrieval, AP reset hold, preferred or registered GHCB GPA requests, unregistering a GHCB GPA, page-state changes, VMPL changes, feature discovery, and termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a shared GHCB GPA before using it for VMGEXIT. During an NAE, the guest receives a #VC exception, copies required state into the GHCB, sets the VALID_BITMAP and exit fields, and invokes VMGEXIT. Hypervisor errors are reported through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Supported events include IO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, page-state change, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests with certificates, AP creation, doorbell management, restricted IPI and timer requests, APIC ID lists, and guest-requested termination.

Under SNP Restricted Injection, a shared host-owned doorbell page uses PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to deliver interrupt vectors, NMIs, and machine-check events. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior, while the guest follows defined HLT and interrupt-processing conventions.

The document also addresses SEV-ES and SEV-SNP application-processor booting, including AP Reset Hold and SNP AP Creation, NMI completion handling, debug-register virtualization, and SEV-SNP secrets-page reserved data. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported, while SEV-SNP AP Creation permits vCPU hotplug.

WKSU’s Exploradio reports on NASA Glenn’s Venus research in Cleveland. The Glenn Extreme Environments Rig, described as the largest and most accurate simulator of other-planet conditions, reproduces Venus’s atmosphere, pressure, and temperature. After an 80-day run, researchers examined rock and mineral samples altered by Venus-like conditions and tested electronics designed to withstand the planet. A durable computer chip operated for 21 days, marking the first multi-week operation of electronics in a Venus environment and potentially enabling longer missions. The segment also outlines Venus’s extreme surface environment, where supercritical carbon dioxide, high pressure, and heat damage materials, while its upper atmosphere is cooler and calmer around 30 miles above the surface but contains sulfuric acid clouds. Researchers say studying Venus can improve understanding of Earth’s climate and may help determine whether life exists in Venus’s more Earth-like atmospheric region.

Viridor and the Somerset Waste Partnership are building a £252 million resource recovery centre at Avonmouth that, once operational in 2020, will convert non-recyclable household waste into electricity for the National Grid, potentially powering 44,000 homes. The facility is intended to reduce reliance on landfill and will launch alongside expanded recycling collections. He was acquitted of abusing a girl’s friend. Witnesses described a culture of fear and intimidation involving violent and sexual abuse. Meat consumption did not significantly affect odor attractiveness, though it tended to make odor more intense. Researchers measured skin carotenoid levels, assessed eating patterns, and had women rate the odors of men’s sweat after exercise. Scientists noted that diet affects body odor indirectly: skin bacteria metabolize compounds in sweat rather than food odors passing directly into it. Earlier research also linked non-meat diets with more appealing odor, but the study did not examine same-sex couples.
