This study evaluates machine-learning potentials (MLPs) for predicting material surface properties outside the bulk-material training domain of universal interatomic potentials (UIPs). Four strategies were compared: training from scratch on surface data (TS), using a pre-trained UIP without adaptation (zero-shot, ZS), fine-tuning the UIP on surface data (FT), and multi-head fine-tuning with bulk and surface datasets (MHFT). Benchmarking pre-trained models on diatomic interactions led to the selection of MACE as the foundation model.

Across unary gold (Au), binary ruthenium oxide (RuO2), and ternary bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) surfaces, FT consistently produced lower energy and force errors than TS for equivalent training-set sizes. Increasing training data improved all models, but FT reached comparable or better accuracy with far fewer surface calculations. On Au, 40 fine-tuned examples reduced errors from 14.8 to 4.3 meV/atom for energies, while TS models trained on 2,000 examples performed similarly to or worse than FT models trained on 40–200 examples. FT also generated more physically reasonable diatomic potentials and avoided unrealistic short-range interactions seen in TS predictions.

The benefits of FT persisted for the more complex RuO2 and BiVO4 surfaces, where force prediction was more difficult because of varied coordination, multiple species, and transition-metal electronic structure. On BiVO4, FT achieved the lowest force RMSE, 0.17 eV/Å, compared with 0.24 eV/Å for TS and 0.42 eV/Å for ZS. It also reduced large-force outliers from 13 for TS to three, comparable to the two ZS outliers. Fine-tuning mitigated the low-force overprediction bias observed in the zero-shot model, which was attributed to insufficient surface coverage in bulk training.

However, fine-tuning only on Au degraded surface-energy predictions for Ag, Cu, Pt, and Ir relative to the zero-shot foundation model, indicating catastrophic forgetting and poor transfer to some novel surfaces. MHFT, trained jointly on Au surface data and 200,000 sampled MPTrj bulk configurations, improved out-of-domain surface-energy RMSE to 16 meV/Å², compared with 27 meV/Å² for ZS and 88 meV/Å² for FT. It preserved bulk-model performance and slightly reduced gold-surface accuracy, but the increase remained within typical DFT reproducibility limits. MHFT required roughly 100 times more training time than FT because losses from the much larger pre-training dataset were evaluated each epoch.

The study concludes that FT is data-efficient and generally more accurate and physically realistic than TS for surfaces, while MHFT is preferable when preserving pre-trained knowledge and generalizing to new surfaces is important. It recommends aligning computational conditions and energy references between pre-training and fine-tuning datasets, particularly for MHFT, and comparing adapted models against the zero-shot baseline when only limited target data are available.

The article examines trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE) in higher education through a structured review of literature from education, social work, psychology, medicine and legal practice. It argues that human rights education remains concentrated in law schools and international law, often avoiding emotionally challenging historical cases and contemporary threats. This limited approach can alienate students and retraumatise learners with lived or intergenerational experiences of violence, abuse, persecution, displacement or other rights violations.

The article recommends that educators first clarify their values, motivations and teaching persona, recognise unconscious biases and understand their own position and privilege. Trust can be strengthened through authenticity, empathy, personal support and awareness of students’ backgrounds. Course content should apply the UN framework of learning about, through and for human rights, combining knowledge with rights-respecting relationships and action. Educators should use flexible and collaborative design, student co-creation, project-based learning, practical skills development and structured reflection to support learners’ agency, self-belief and capacity for advocacy.

Trauma-informed teaching should avoid graphic material, retraumatisation, “trauma porn” and romanticised accounts of suffering or resilience. Educators may provide advance notice of difficult content, wellbeing check-ins and opportunities for discussion and self-care. Reflective exercises can help learners analyse emotional responses and identify concrete human rights actions.

Finally, the article advocates dialogic teaching based on equality, mutual respect and shared responsibility. Course design should enable dialogue among learners and interactions with survivors and practitioners, including substantive question-and-answer sessions. Such engagement develops critical thinking, communication, confidence, coalition-building and advocacy while connecting academic study with lived experience. The central aim of TIHRE is to place wellbeing, dignity and agency at the heart of learning and move educators and learners from avoidance toward hope, healing, reconciliation and rights-based action.

This IDC white paper examines how simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC) can advance manufacturing amid geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy prices, material shortages, supply-chain disruptions, labor constraints, sustainability demands, and rapid digitalization. IT-based simulation is already established in CAD, CAM, and CAE workflows and can accelerate product development, reduce costs and defects, optimize resources, improve quality, and support connected, cross-departmental processes. The paper emphasizes integrating data into a unified “single source of truth” to avoid conflicting analyses caused by data silos.

Based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers at discrete and process manufacturers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, simulation, modeling, and analytics are viewed primarily as innovation drivers, with usage and planned investment expected to expand across development, production, and quality management. Virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT, AI/ML, AR/VR, and engineering workstations as a service create additional use cases and may enable new products, services, and business models.

HPC addresses increasingly complex calculations that conventional infrastructure cannot perform quickly or accurately enough. Most respondents view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables sophisticated simulations, faster iterations, improved quality, and greater agility. However, adoption is constrained by security and intellectual-property concerns, substantial investment, operating and licensing costs, infrastructure complexity, and high energy consumption. Most enterprises favor external cloud or colocation infrastructure over operating HPC systems on-premises.

The paper examines whether soft information in earnings press releases predicts announcement-day stock returns. Using 134,354 press releases from 2006–2023 covering more than 6,000 firms, the study compares earnings surprises with text representations generated by LDA, online LDA, BERT, MPNET, and FinBERT. Rolling-window methods avoid look-ahead bias, while regression and SHAP values assess predictive power and explainability.

Soft information explains a share of return variation comparable to earnings surprises. FinBERT performs best, with soft information accounting for 52% of SHAP importance versus 48% for earnings surprise; online LDA improves thematic interpretability. Textual signals do not explain returns before announcements, suggesting limited routine leakage. Topic analysis indicates that companies describe internal performance factors more positively and external or sector factors more negatively, consistent with self-serving bias.

Trading tests find no sustained profits when press-release signals are used after the market opens, consistent with market efficiency. However, when release information is obtained in advance, combining textual signals with earnings surprises identifies 44%–52% of the top 10 positive- and negative-return stocks. The authors propose incorporating conference-call text and audio in future research.

The Federal Reserve’s fourth rate hike in 18 months raises costs for credit cards, home equity lines and some adjustable-rate mortgages. A $5,000 credit-card balance with minimum payments would cost about $700 more over the loan’s life. Borrowers with poor credit may face larger increases, particularly on used-car loans, though overall effects are expected to remain mild because rates remain historically low.

Fixed mortgage and auto loan rates have barely changed because they do not directly track the Fed’s short-term rate. Mortgage rates follow the 10-year Treasury and other market forces; the 30-year fixed rate recently stood at 4.04%, nearly its December 2015 level.

Higher U.S. rates can attract overseas investment, strengthen the dollar, make U.S. exports costlier and draw capital from developing countries, potentially weakening their currencies and complicating dollar-denominated debt repayment.

Savings rates have increased slightly, with the best CDs and accounts offering more than major banks. Retirees holding bonds are advised to remain diversified and gradually replace short-term securities with higher-yielding ones as rates rise.

U.S. Treasury yields rose after a jobs report showed 33,000 job losses, 2.9% wage growth and unemployment at 4.2%. Traders focused on potentially inflationary wage gains while attributing payroll weakness to hurricanes. The 10- and two-year yields rose for a fourth consecutive week before paring gains amid concern about Catalonia and ahead of three debt auctions. Fed futures implied an 88% chance of a December rate increase, while some analysts questioned the market’s emphasis on wages over job losses.

Amsterdam’s De Ceuvel is an experimental, temporary regeneration project in the Buiksloterham docklands. Renovated houseboats on a polluted former shipyard form a co-working hub for artists, entrepreneurs, and sustainability researchers, connected by a boardwalk and a garden of plants that remove toxins from the soil. The site uses composting toilets, waste recycling, aquaponics, solar panels, and heat exchangers to minimize its environmental impact. Offices earn “Jouliettes” for generating surplus solar power, which can be exchanged for electricity. Designed to remain for ten years, De Ceuvel will then be dismantled and the land cleaned. It offers an inclusive, low-cost alternative to the luxury development that had begun in the area before the financial crisis.

After 27 days, Kilauea’s eruption continues to destroy communities on Hawaii’s Big Island, with lava from Fissure 8 advancing at about 600 yards per hour and threatening more homes in Leilani Estates and Lanipuna Gardens. Lava fountains, ash, volcanic glass fibers, earthquakes and high gas emissions have prompted evacuations, including efforts to remove Kapoho residents before isolation. Approximately 22 fissures have opened, at least 40 homes have been destroyed, more than 2,000 acres have been covered by lava, and about 200 people are in shelters. Volcanic haze has traveled to Guam, reducing visibility and potentially affecting people with respiratory conditions, while vog is expected to spread across the island. The USGS also warned that roasting marshmallows over volcanic vents is unsafe.

North Park Elementary School in San Bernardino reopened a week after Cedric Anderson killed his estranged wife, Karen Smith, and 8-year-old Jonathan Martinez, then fatally shot himself. Peel police believe the three men who beat a 29-year-old autistic man at a Mississauga mall are from British Columbia’s Lower Mainland and recently traveled to the GTA. Police released descriptions and clothing details and asked residents near Vancouver, Surrey, Abbotsford and Richmond to review the surveillance video.

Don Davis, who received a last meal, could be executed within 10 days if Attorney General Leslie Rutledge prevails. The Eighth Circuit also lifted a federal judge’s temporary halt on all eight executions, finding the planned lethal-injection method did not create undue severe pain.

Tests indicate that RSI works on Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies as a momentum indicator, but not as a traditional mean-reversion strategy. Buying low RSI readings and selling high ones produced weak results and few trades on Bitcoin; the best variation made only three trades and was considered unusable for prediction. Similar results appeared for Ethereum and Dogecoin. Momentum strategies performed substantially better. In one Bitcoin example, buying when five-day RSI crossed above 50 and selling below 50 achieved a 122% CAGR versus 101% for buy-and-hold, with a 39% drawdown versus 83%. Strong results were also reported for Ethereum and Dogecoin.

The manuscript advances quantitative criticalism as an epistemological and methodological approach for education research. Intended for scholars, students, institutional researchers, practitioners, and methods instructors, it examines how critical perspectives can address tensions and opportunities in quantitative scholarship. The authors argue that quantitative research is never fully objective because researchers’ biases, assumptions, social identities, and lived experiences shape inquiry. Positionality should therefore be made explicit and examined throughout research.

The authors describe their own positions: Jay is a white cisgender queer scholar studying queer and trans students, while Jimmy is a Vietnamese-Chinese American institutional researcher concerned with aggregated racial data, stereotyping, and institutional power. Their experiences demonstrate how social identities and professional roles shape research questions, methods, interpretations, and applications.

Quantitative criticalism combines quantitative methods with critical epistemologies oriented toward social justice, equity, and dismantling oppression. Numbers are not neutral, and critical quantitative research challenges existing policies, theories, measures, and conventional research questions. Criticality should inform every stage of scholarship, including question development, construct and variable operationalization, sampling, data collection, coding, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination. The approach also emphasizes methodological reflection, community partnership, solidarity, data sovereignty, transparent authorship, and engagement with marginalized communities throughout research design and interpretation.

The manuscript identifies several persistent tensions. Statistics have white-supremacist and cisheteropatriarchal foundations, and defining a sufficient threshold of criticality is difficult. Researchers must negotiate intentions and effects; essentialist demographic categories and the measurement of fluid identities; limited data and statistical options for underrepresented populations; individual-level explanations versus analyses of systemic oppression; and community-specific nuance versus broad generalizability. Categorization is necessary for quantitative analysis but conflicts with queer theory’s emphasis on fluid identities. Mixed methods and methodological adaptations may relieve some tensions while creating others.

Four studies illustrate applications of critical theory. Through critical race theory and a QuantCrit approach, Sablan operationalized the community cultural wealth model into four scales representing aspirational, familial, navigational, and resistant capital, though validation across broader populations remains necessary. Using queer theory, Garvey advocated including “queer” as a sexual-identity option and testing for within-group differences, while acknowledging the conflict between categorization and identity fluidity. Applying intersectionality, Szymanski and Lewis used interaction effects and a moderator to examine gendered racism among African American women, facing limitations in instruments and sample diversity. Wilson and Urick used latent class analysis to examine the opportunity gap and offered a different method for incorporating intersecting categories. These examples demonstrate multiple approaches but no consensus on the best way to integrate intersectionality quantitatively.

The authors urge methods educators to teach both methods and epistemology, describe criticality as a continuum, and emphasize that incremental or partial adoption of critical principles may still reproduce harm. They ask scholars to consider their intentions, whether historically white-supremacist methods can serve justice, and what threshold of criticality they require. Ultimately, the manuscript calls for collective, reflective, adaptable quantitative scholarship grounded in equity, justice, and liberation, while openly confronting methodological discomfort and uncertainty.

A global learning crisis has been intensified by pandemic-related school closures, climate change, conflict, and economic slowdown. Children not learning cost an estimated US$129 billion annually. In 2023, 20% of young people worldwide were not in employment, education, or training, while nearly 40% of employers reported skills shortages. By 2030, 39% of skills needed for today’s jobs may transform or become obsolete.

GPE supports lower-income countries through policy dialogue, financing, knowledge investments, and public-private partnerships. Its approach combines foundational literacy, numeracy, and socio-emotional skills with creativity, analytical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and preparation for changing labor markets. Initiatives include a planned $40 million foundational-learning investment in Ghana, a competency-based early-years curriculum in Kenya, and teacher training in socio-emotional skills and creative thinking in El Salvador. GPE also supports relevant assessment tools and research through the A4L Initiative and KIX.

SpinGPT is an LLM-based agent designed for three-player Spin & Go poker, a format in which player counts, stack sizes, and chip values change during play. The system uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a two-stage training pipeline. First, supervised fine-tuning on 320,000 decisions from 8,800 professional Spin & Go games teaches the model poker actions and strategy through structured text prompts. Second, offline reinforcement learning with ORPO combines 270,000 InstaGTO-generated near-optimal decisions with 50,000 original human decisions to shift behavior toward GTO play while retaining learned patterns.

On professional-data evaluation, the SFT model achieved 80% exact accuracy, 86% macro F1, and 0.61 BB bet-size mean absolute error. After reinforcement learning, professional exact accuracy remained similar at 79%, while MAE improved to 0.30 BB and MAPE to 12%. On solver data, the final model achieved 72% exact accuracy, 78% tolerant accuracy, and 77% macro F1.

In gameplay tests, a minimally patched SpinGPT-SFT earned 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 against Slumbot over 30,000 hands. The final SpinGPT earned 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100 against SpinGPT-SFT over 10,000 duplicate-format hands.

Limitations include the mismatch between Slumbot’s deep-stack cash format and Spin & Go, the lack of a final-model evaluation against Slumbot, and numerical hallucinations such as incorrectly ordering decimal values. Proposed improvements include stronger models, higher-quality hands, retrieval of GTO charts, chain-of-thought reasoning, opponent adaptivity, natural-language explanations, and combining an LLM with a solver for heads-up post-flop decisions.

The passage lists 17 common weight-loss mistakes and how to avoid them. Drinking water from plastic bottles exposes you to Bisphenol-A, which promotes fat storage; switch to stainless steel. Cutting sweets out entirely is harmful—substitute sweet fruits for artificial sweeteners, and if you want sugar, eat it just before a workout to burn it off. Emotional eating should be replaced with exercise, and store-bought protein bars and energy drinks, full of artificial sweeteners that trigger insulin release, should be swapped for coconut water or nuts. Avoid scolding yourself for setbacks, and don't surround yourself with people who undermine your goals. Judge success by following a routine, not by the scale. Meal-replacement supplements increase hunger and cravings, so eat real food. Don't eliminate carbohydrates entirely; cut refined carbs and use whole grains instead, and include healthy fats rather than eating only fat-free products, since fats are essential to the brain and cells. Get at least seven hours of sleep, and don't eat too little while working out more, as starvation mode halts fat burning. Change your exercise routine weekly, since the body adapts and plateaus. Don't drink your calories, as liquids leave you hungry. Don't restrict your diet too strictly too soon, which leads to abandoning the plan, and don't copy someone else's routine, since the right plan depends on your body type, metabolism, and health.

The MACD histogram represents the difference between the MACD line and its signal line, indicating momentum changes and potential reversals. Its crossover strategy buys when it crosses above zero and sells when it crosses below zero. Presented as a mean-reversion system, it enters at the close and exits when the close rises above the previous close, with the reverse for shorts. A backtest across 77 ETFs produced 6,669 trades, with longs performing better than shorts. A leveraged QLD backtest covering over 18 years recorded 85 trades, a 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, a 19% maximum drawdown, and only 5% market exposure.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces hardware and software technologies for high-resolution displays, real-time ray tracing, AI-enhanced graphics, VR, and more efficient rendering. Its display engine supports 8K output at 60 Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, USB-C, HDR processing, and BT.2100 tone mapping. Turing supports two 8K displays at 60 Hz, each with its own cable. Enhanced NVENC encoding adds 8K HEVC at 30 fps and bitrate savings, while NVDEC supports higher-bit-depth HEVC and VP9 HDR streams.

For VR, Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, allowing power, display data, and USB data to travel through one connector. VirtualLink supports four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes alongside SuperSpeed USB and can enable VR on smaller devices. Turing also replaces MIO and PCIe SLI transfers with second-generation NVLink. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 has one, supporting two-way SLI with substantially greater bandwidth and new display configurations.

Turing adds RT Cores to each streaming multiprocessor to accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests. Combined with NVIDIA RTX software, these dedicated cores make single-GPU real-time ray tracing practical and are reported to accelerate ray tracing by roughly ten times over Pascal. Turing supports a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization with ray tracing, using each for tasks where it is most effective. It works with RTX libraries, OptiX, Microsoft DirectX Ray Tracing, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API. Ray-traced effects can address artifacts and limitations associated with rasterized shadows, screen-space ambient occlusion, and screen-space reflections.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only deep-learning technology stack that uses Tensor Cores and pretrained neural-network models. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) trains against 64-times-supersampled reference images to reconstruct high-quality images from lower-cost input rendering. Standard DLSS can approximate temporal anti-aliasing quality with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X takes target-resolution input and produces output approaching 64-times-supersampled quality. Other NGX features include Inpainting for replacing removed image content, AI Slow-Mo for generating interpolated frames, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Turing also introduces mesh shading through task and mesh shaders. Task shaders process object lists in parallel, select level-of-detail variants, and launch mesh shaders, reducing CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enabling hundreds of thousands of objects to be rendered efficiently. The shaders can also cull or modify geometry for effects such as dynamic CAD cutaways.

Variable Rate Shading allows each 16-by-16-pixel region to use one of several shading rates independently of its visibility rate. Applications include content-adaptive shading for spatially or temporally uniform regions, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that reduces detail away from the viewer’s focus. Shading rates can also be increased for multisample anti-aliasing.

Texture Space Shading computes appearance in a reusable texture-space grid rather than directly on screen pixels. It decouples visibility and appearance sampling, supports multiple resolutions, reuses texels across frames and views, and improves temporal stability and VR efficiency. Multi-View Rendering fetches and shades geometry once while producing as many as four hardware-supported views per pass and up to 32 API-level views, supporting stereo VR, canted HMD panels, multiple character instances, shadow buffers, and cascaded shadow maps. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and allows different resource types to share heaps.

The TU104-based full GPU contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and one x8 NVLink link. The Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

NVIDIA introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering. It weights peak tensor, FP32, RT-core, and INT32 operations according to their observed utilization: 20%, 80%, 40%, and 28%, respectively.

The document explains ray casting, BVH construction and refitting, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. BVH traversal reduces the number of triangle tests required, while denoising permits fewer rays per pixel and produces cleaner results. Together with hybrid rendering and RT Cores, these techniques enable real-time ray-traced effects that can produce physically correct contact-hardening shadows, ambient occlusion, and glossy reflections.

Onesmo Rupil began using drugs at 17 and was discontinued from his University of Dodoma commerce and accounting studies in 2013 because of substance-related poor performance. Now recovered, the 23-year-old manages Philimisana Foundation Sober House, home to about 30 people in rehabilitation.

Rupil committed crimes to fund expensive heroin habits and was arrested in 2015 over the theft of more than 200 laptops. He spent six months in Isanga Prison before attending rehabilitation in Dar es Salaam.

According to Dr. Kassian Nyandindi, 550,000 people were affected by drug abuse in 2014, including an estimated 25,000 addicts, but only 3,500 were treated at four methadone hospitals in Dar es Salaam. He reported HIV infection among drug users at 20–50% and warned that marijuana’s THC can damage the corpus callosum and contribute to mental disorders among some young people undergoing rehabilitation.

The study developed an automated system for monitoring clinical guideline adherence in intensive care by combining FHIR-encoded, computer-interpretable recommendations with patient data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model. Six COVID-19, ARDS, and sepsis-related recommendations were selected from 41 guidelines, encoded and reviewed by clinical and technical experts, and implemented across five university hospitals with different IT infrastructures. The system analyzed 82,015 intensive care episodes from January 2020 to May 2023.

In a validation involving three hospitals, seven intensive care physicians, and expert-established ground truth, the system achieved 97.0% accuracy compared with 86.6% for physicians, with significantly higher precision and F1 score. It processed more than 2,000 patient-days per second, whereas human review required about 30 seconds per patient, day, and recommendation. More than 80% of discrepancies were attributed to human errors; most system errors resulted from relevant information being stored in unstructured free text that was not transferred to OMOP.

Observed adherence generally ranged from 10% to 60% and varied by recommendation and hospital. Reported influences included limited guideline awareness, incomplete documentation, strict interpretation, and imprecise recommendations. Limitations included retrospective validation, potential expert-labeling bias, reliance on data availability and quality, and evaluation of only six recommendations. The authors concluded that the interoperable system provides a scalable and reliable approach to automated guideline-adherence monitoring and decision support.

Coaches described the series as tough but rejected fatigue as an explanation, attributing the physical, low-scoring style to both teams battling for every inch. They said their team still has energy and must generate more shots, spread scoring, and improve execution. New Jersey was praised as balanced, defensively strong, and highly cohesive, with effective puck placement, quick transitions, and dangerous line combinations. Matchups and defensive containment were left to the coaching staff. The team expects a tight, low-scoring fight while emphasizing Stanley Cup Final urgency, preparation, and a desperate performance in the next game.

A 2018 Journal of Climate paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry estimates substantially lower climate sensitivity than CMIP5 models. Using globally complete temperature data, it derives a median equilibrium climate sensitivity of 1.66°C (5–95%: 1.15–2.7°C), compared with 3.1°C for 31 CMIP5 models, and a transient climate response of 1.33°C (5–95%: 1.15–1.9°C), compared with 1.9°C. The study concludes that high model estimates are inconsistent with observed warming since 1850 and implies future warming will be 30–45% below central simulation projections. It finds sensitivity estimates relatively insensitive to the analysis period and reports that potential biases from forcing efficacy, sea-surface temperature patterns, and temperature data are minor when globally complete data are used. Allowing for time-varying climate feedback raises median ECS to 1.76°C but does not materially change the comparison with CMIP5 models.

The passage specifies safety analyses and reporting requirements for the ZEA-DNK-02170 statistical analysis plan. Plasma glucose and pharmacodynamic metrics will be summarized by treatment group and time point, including changes from pre-dose, with mean and individual concentration-time curves on the original scale.

Safety analyses will use the safety set and cover insulin administration and hypoglycemia induction, trial medication administration, rescue glucose infusion, and local tolerability. Time to first IV glucose infusion will be summarized descriptively without statistical testing. Adverse-event analyses will focus on treatment-emergent AEs, defined as events occurring after dosing or worsening during the study, and will use MedDRA version 21.0 or higher. Investigator causality assessments will classify possible or probable events as related; unresolved missing assessments will be treated as related. Missing severity will not be imputed. Summary and frequency tables will include overall events, events of special interest, injection-site reactions, related events, serious events, and deaths, with ordering based on incidence in the dasiglucagon group. Special searches will cover QT prolongation, drug-related hepatic disorders, and externally supplied preferred-term files.

Laboratory data will be tabulated by treatment group, visit, and time point using descriptive statistics, reference-range categories, categorical counts, and change-from-baseline analyses. Hematology, clinical chemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy testing, alcohol breath testing, vital signs, and physical examinations will also be summarized. ECG outputs will include overall assessments, parameter statistics, categorical QTcF thresholds above 450, 480, and 500 ms, and postbaseline changes exceeding 30 or 60 ms. Immunogenicity will be assessed descriptively, counting treatment-induced and treatment-boosted ADA-positive patients among evaluable patients; no statistical tests are planned.

Changes from the protocol include rewording the primary efficacy analysis, adding sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changing secondary terminology from “within” specified minutes to “at” those minutes. Planned efficacy outputs include time-to-glucose-recovery summaries, Kaplan–Meier curves, sensitivity analyses, histograms, interpolation analyses, recovery rates, and glucose changes at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes. Reported methods include Cox proportional-hazards modeling, Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel testing, and ANOVA.

The appendices define table, figure, and listing formats; decimal precision; percentage and P-value rounding; sorting; date/time conventions; unit conversions; BMI and baseline-change formulas; and conservative handling of missing dates. SAS quality-control requirements cover program structure, log and output review, dataset validation, patient-level source-data checks, Pinnacle 21 validation, figure verification, and documentation of findings and resolutions.

Janet Yellen said the Federal Reserve should continue gradual interest-rate increases to stabilize job growth, prevent economic overheating and move inflation toward 2%, warning that tightening too slowly or too quickly carries risks. After February payrolls rose 313,000, she estimated sustainable monthly job growth at 90,000–120,000, which would slowly lower unemployment without sharply accelerating inflation.

Arizona has long been a center of U.S. school choice, with district open enrollment for 30 years, charter schools for more than 25 years, and a private-school tax credit program. It became the first state to enact parent-directed Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) vouchers in 2011 and the first to make them universal in 2022. That expansion followed voters’ rejection of a capped expansion in 2018. Arizona provides more than $1 billion annually for private education, homeschooling, and related tax credits.

A Grand Canyon Institute (GCI) analysis finds that Arizona’s universal ESA program is a net cost to the state general fund. Enrollment rose from 12,127 in 2022 to 61,689 in 2023, 74,578 in 2024, and 87,602 by the third quarter of FY2025. Before universal eligibility, most targeted participants were required to attend a district or charter school for at least 45 days, and about 97% had done so. Universal participants have no such requirement.

GCI estimates that nearly three-quarters of universal ESA participants in FY2025 had never attended a district or charter school, although nearly all new FY2025 entrants came from those schools, with about half coming from charters. The program can therefore save modest state funds when students transfer from charters, but creates new costs when students transfer from districts or would not otherwise have attended public school. GCI estimates the FY2025 net universal-voucher cost at $346.3 million, plus $3.2 million in administrative costs, totaling about $349.5 million. It estimated the FY2024 net cost at at least $332 million.

ESA awards are set at 90% of charter-school funding and are usually below $8,000, though awards for students with certain needs can exceed $30,000. GCI estimated that FY2023 allocations were at least $415 million, with $304 million spent. Of that spending, $173 million went to private schools: 51% to religious schools and 44% to schools serving special-needs students. Evangelical Christian and Catholic schools received 86% of religious-school expenditures, while secular private schools received less than 5%, or $7.8 million. GCI also found that no more than 40% of ESA participants used allocations for private-school tuition, indicating substantial use for homeschooling or extracurricular activities. Unspent account balances totaled an estimated $175 million at the end of FY2023 and $360 million by the end of FY2024.

ESA participation has remained concentrated in higher-income ZIP codes, though income differences have narrowed. An initial analysis found that 45% of universal applicants came from the state’s wealthiest quartile, while 32% came from ZIP codes with median household incomes below $60,000. In May 2023, participation rates ranged from 2.6% in the lowest-income group to 7.7% in the highest; by March 2025, they ranged from 4.4% to 10.9%. Overall enrollment grew 54% during that period.

GCI says Arizona provides little transparency or accountability for private entities receiving public subsidies. Only FY2023 account-balance data had been verified; requests for some FY2024 balance and school-payment information were denied or remained pending.

The passage frames curriculum evaluation as a systematic process that identifies students’ and teachers’ needs, corrects program weaknesses, and guides curriculum revision. Teachers’ views are important because they develop and implement curricula in classrooms. Previous physical education studies identified limited implementation, insufficient course hours, crowded classrooms, inadequate materials and equipment, and gaps in teachers’ knowledge as barriers.

This quantitative descriptive study examined pre-service teachers’ opinions of the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum for grades 5–8 regarding its achievements, content, teaching-learning processes, and assessment and evaluation practices. The researcher developed a questionnaire, tested it with 50 pre-service teachers, and obtained a 0.85 consensus from three doctoral-level field experts. The sample included 100 students from four departments at Bayburt University’s Faculty of Sports Sciences, with 25 students from each department.

Candidates generally viewed the program achievements positively: 43% considered them suitable for students’ levels, while 64 believed they were placed under the correct learning areas and 70 found them understandable. Most candidates agreed that the content was meaningfully ordered, although many were undecided about its scientific accuracy, age appropriateness, and comparability with programs in other countries. Fifty-six percent reported that teaching processes were enriched with activities, and 61% said concrete materials were used. However, 60 rejected the statement that varied methods and techniques were employed. Candidates were frequently undecided about developmental suitability, interdisciplinary activities, and assessment-method variety, although 43 agreed that different assessment forms were used. Overall, the findings indicated positive views of the objectives but insufficient knowledge concerning program content, scientific accuracy, and international comparability. The study recommends additional research, informational seminars or congresses, and curriculum-review courses in teacher education.

This divisional patent application describes methods for forming three-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays. A primary embodiment uses damascene local vertical bit lines and two-step etching of local word lines, reducing patterning aspect ratios, mitigating ribboning and alignment variability, and improving word-line-stack stability. The process forms multilayer stacks above global interconnect lines, creates trenches and word-line strips, selectively removes silicon nitride, fills resulting cavities with metal, and forms elongated vias containing tunneling, charge-storage, blocking, channel, optional liner, and sacrificial layers. Repeated via formation and semiconductor filling create source and drain regions connected to global bit lines. Staircase structures provide contacts to local word lines. Additional embodiments use dielectric pillars or stacked masks to support high-aspect-ratio word-line stacks during fabrication. Related patent and provisional applications are incorporated by reference.

**Mega Geometry** — A new RTX technology that dramatically increases geometric detail in ray-traced applications, letting engines such as Unreal Engine 5 with Nanite-style LOD systems ray trace geometry at full fidelity without low-resolution proxies, improving shadows, reflections, and indirect illumination, and bringing displaced subdivision surfaces into real-time ray tracing. It consists of new RTX API extensions, a high-performance driver implementation, and Blackwell RT Core optimizations addressing two hurdles:
- *Cluster-based LOD updates:* Nanite-style systems change LODs in ~128-triangle clusters each frame, requiring BVH builds that would overload existing ray tracing. Mega Geometry introduces Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) of up to 256 triangles, generated on demand and cached; because each CLAS covers roughly 100 triangles, subsequent BVH builds require two orders of magnitude less processing. APIs are fully batched with inputs driven from GPU memory, letting LOD selection, animation, and culling run on the GPU and nearly eliminating CPU BVH-management overhead.
- *High object counts:* A new Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) aggregates objects into partitions and updates only those that changed (e.g., static world sectors plus a dynamic "global partition" rebuilt each frame), reducing runtime.

Mega Geometry is supported on all RTX GPUs from Turing via DirectX 12 (NVAPI extensions), Vulkan vendor extensions, and OptiX 9.0. Blackwell's 4th-generation RT Cores add cluster engines with new compression schemes and up to 2x the ray-triangle intersection rate of 3rd-generation cores, reducing VRAM footprint of typical Nanite scenes by several hundred MB.

**Linear Swept Spheres (LSS)** — Blackwell RT Cores add hardware ray-intersection testing for LSS primitives (spheres swept along linear segments with varying radii), also supporting plain spheres for particle systems; hair rendering is about 2x faster than DOTS with about 5x less VRAM.

**SER 2.0** — Enhanced shader execution reordering: core reorder logic twice as efficient, higher precision enabling smarter coherence extraction and developer-supplied hints, a small control API, and new flexibility in ray tracing shader invocation; it also routes coherent neural workloads to Tensor Cores.

**AMP** — A fully programmable GPU context scheduler implemented with a dedicated RISC-V processor, offloading GPU task scheduling from the CPU and matching Microsoft's HAGS model, yielding lower latency, reduced CPU burden, smoother frame rates, and faster first response for LLMs.

**Video and display** — Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled H.264/HEVC, presented alongside 4:4:4 and 4:2:0 trade-offs (4:2:2 uses two-thirds the data of uncompressed 4:4:4 and offers 2x the color resolution of 4:2:0). Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1/HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds 4:2:2 encoding and an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode worth an extra 5% (up to 15% combined), also planned for RTX 40 Series at lower quality. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders (over 50% faster export generation-over-generation, 4x the RTX 3090), and the 6th-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decode speed and adds 4:2:2 decode. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps using UHBR 20, enabling 8K@165Hz and 4K@480Hz (both requiring DSC and a DP80LL certified cable).

**Max-Q power efficiency** — Advanced power gating (whole clock-tree gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, frame-granularity rail gating), accelerated frequency switching (clocks adjust 1000x faster than prior architectures), and low-latency sleep (10x faster to enter than Ada) combine to save up to 50% power in an example running inference on small language models.

**DLSS 4** — Multi Frame Generation produces up to three additional frames per rendered frame using a model that is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame; hardware optical flow is replaced by an efficient AI model, and Flip Metering moves pacing logic to the display engine, which has twice the pixel processing capability. DLSS shifts from CNNs to transformer models with 2x more parameters, improving Super Resolution (temporal stability, less ghosting, detail in motion), Ray Reconstruction (fewer denoiser artifacts, especially in challenging lighting), and DLAA.

**Neural shaders** — Blackwell is presented as the start of developer-created neural shaders, with the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan (with Slang) letting any shader access Tensor Cores. This enables RTX Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM compression), RTX Neural Materials (a demo's materials shrinking from 1110 MB to 333 MB), Stochastic Texture Filtering (randomized sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré; faster on Blackwell's 2x point-sampled filtering rate), Neural Radiance Cache (inferring lighting for many bounces from one-bounce path-traced rays, trained on live game data in real time), RTX Skin (real-time ray-traced subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (a TensorRT-optimized generative AI model taking a rasterized face plus 3D pose input, trained from thousands of offline images). A history of shader evolution from fixed-function pipelines through RTX to Blackwell neural shaders is included.

**GPU lineup** — GB202 (92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, 512-bit memory) for the GeForce RTX 5090; GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, 256-bit) for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti; GB205 (31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, 192-bit) for the RTX 5070.

Strong second-quarter S&P 500 earnings—11% growth, the fastest consecutive quarters since 2011—did not lead to upward earnings revisions. Six of 11 sectors saw 2018 profit forecasts cut, and the average 2018 EPS estimate slipped 0.2%. Goldman expects forecasts to fall another 5%, citing excessive optimism about energy earnings. U.S. stocks beating earnings and revenue forecasts barely outperformed after reporting, while revenue misses drew greater selling. BlackRock’s Richard Turnill saw investor fatigue but still forecast solid fundamentals and returns.

The Jan. 26, 2001 newspaper clippings focus on Enron, California’s electricity crisis, Wall Street performance, and Maharashtra’s dispute with Enron.

A Times of India commentary described California’s emergency, rolling blackouts, near-bankrupt utilities, and state financial intervention. It attributed the crisis to flawed deregulation policies, retail-price caps, restrictions on long-term power contracts, declining in-state generation, and rising demand, including from Silicon Valley data centers. It argued that power markets require adequate long-term capacity, that regulation should moderate volatility without distorting prices, and that transitions to deregulated markets must be managed carefully.

Wall Street investors favored blue-chip stocks and sold technology shares while focusing on 2001 earnings forecasts. The Dow rose 82.55 to 10,729.52, while the Nasdaq fell 104.87 to 2,754.28 and the S&P 500 slipped 6.79 to 1,357.51. Corning plunged nearly 20% after warning of reduced customer orders. Enron rose $2.25 to $82 after indicating that 2001 profits would likely exceed analysts’ predictions.

A San Francisco Chronicle report described Lamorinda Democrats using gallows humor before hearing University of California Energy Institute director Severin Borenstein discuss California’s energy crisis. Borenstein proposed time-of-use electricity pricing, with higher peak-period charges and lower off-peak rates to encourage conservation.

The Wall Street Journal reported that wind power was returning as a partial response to California’s blackouts. The 7,000 turbines at Altamont Pass generate electricity for less than half the cost of natural-gas power. FPL was building a 470-turbine, 300-megawatt project near the Columbia River, while Enron operated 2,000 turbines in the Tehachapi Mountains and had deployed several hundred more in other states. Wind was described as inexpensive and quick to build but intermittent, and it supplied only about 1.5% of California’s electricity.

Reports on Maharashtra said the cash-strapped Maharashtra State Electricity Board was expected to miss a deadline for paying 1.59 billion rupees ($34.3 million) to Enron’s Dabhol Power for December electricity. Enron could seek payment through state and federal guarantees. A Business Standard editorial said U.S. officials had pressured Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh over the contract and criticized efforts to avoid raising tariffs, arguing that Maharashtra should follow tariffs set by its electricity regulator.

Boston Globe columnist David Nyhan announced a four-month fellowship at Harvard’s Kennedy School. He also highlighted Enron’s profits from California’s energy shortage and reported campaign contributions associated with the company and President George W. Bush.

Finally, the Houston Chronicle described Enron’s new forced employee-ranking system, which assigns workers to five categories from “superior” to “needs improvement” or “issues.” Workers and human-resources specialists raised concerns about relative comparisons, managerial bargaining, secrecy, and motivation. Human-resources executive Cindy Olson denied that ratings were being traded, said they were not fixed, and acknowledged that some workers might not fit Enron’s entrepreneurial culture.

Every second Saturday, InnerDancer Performing Arts hosts a monthly dance for teens and adults with developmental disabilities at the Gloria McClellan Adult Activity & Resource Center in Vista. Founder Caroline Bossmeyer uses adaptive instruction to make movement and self-expression accessible, emphasizing that dancing need not be perfect. Attendees, ages 17 to 80, socialize, exercise and enjoy snacks in an inclusive atmosphere; the two-hour event costs $12.
