The passage proposes Digital Ecosystems as engineered software systems that exploit biological ecosystem properties—robustness, scalability, self-organization, and adaptation—to solve complex, dynamic problems efficiently. These systems are presented as a distinct use of the term “digital ecosystem,” unlike internet infrastructure, commercial e-business services, business or ICT ecosystems, and Artificial Life models that may lack genuine ecological properties.

Digital Ecosystems are described as multi-agent architectures combining a decentralized peer-to-peer network of habitats with local evolutionary algorithms. Agents contain executable and ontological components, and evolving populations combine them into sequences that satisfy users’ semantic application requests. Fitness landscapes are expected to be dynamic and responsive to changing user needs. Designers must balance user-defined fitness criteria with autonomous self-organization so agents remain useful while preserving diversity, avoiding premature convergence, and retaining the ability to find distant or complex solutions. Stability and diversity must likewise be balanced against adaptive efficiency and the risk of disruptive state transitions.

Spatial structure and connectivity are important for diversity and for mediating local versus global evolutionary search. Digital connectivity is based on information or semantic proximity rather than geography. The proposed architecture uses reconfigurable, bidirectional habitat links whose migration probabilities change through Hebbian learning: successful agent exchanges strengthen connections, while unsuccessful exchanges weaken them. This enables the network to adapt toward the topology of its user community.

Distributed evolutionary computing is used to accelerate evaluation and help avoid premature convergence. Unlike conventional island models in which populations address one identical problem, each Digital Ecosystem habitat can address a different but related request, allowing populations to share solutions for similar problems. Agent populations are seeded from local agents, previously evolved sequences, and relevant sequences developed elsewhere. Evolved sequences migrate to other habitats where they may help satisfy additional requests.

A simulation used an Ecosystem-Oriented Architecture with 100 simulated SME users and randomly connected habitats. Users produced service agents and semantic business-application requests represented by numeric tuples. Each user initially deployed five agents and deployed another after three requests; equal numbers of users joined and left. Habitat populations evolved agent sequences under artificial selection based on request-derived fitness functions, with dynamic population sizes increasing as average sequence length grew. The provided passage ends during the fitness-function formulation, before simulation outcomes are reported.
Reporter Coral Davenport says OMB director Russell Vought plans to bypass Congress’s budgetary powers to advance Trump’s agenda.

President Donald Trump said the government shutdown created an “unprecedented opportunity” to cut Democratic-leaning federal agencies and projects. His administration said it froze about $18 billion for New York infrastructure projects and canceled $8 billion in climate projects in Democratic-leaning states, while an OMB memo urged agencies to prepare for possible layoffs. Trump plans to meet OMB Director Russell Vought, a Project 2025 author, to consider which agencies and projects to cut and whether cuts would be permanent; officials said layoffs could number in the thousands.

The shutdown began Wednesday after Congress failed to pass funding legislation. Republicans sought a stopgap bill through late November, while Democrats demanded extended Affordable Care Act tax credits. Competing bills failed in the Senate, and another Republican vote is scheduled for Friday after Thursday’s vote was postponed for Yom Kippur.

Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation challenged the NRC’s 2009 transfer of regulatory authority over radioactive materials at its Newfield, New Jersey facility to the state. After the transfer, New Jersey rejected Shieldalloy’s pending plan for on-site disposal of radioactive slag and dust. Shieldalloy argued that the transfer was arbitrary and capricious and that New Jersey’s program was incompatible with the NRC’s.

The D.C. Circuit focused on Criterion 25 of the NRC’s compatibility policy, which requires arrangements preventing interference with licensed activities or the processing of license applications. The court found the NRC’s responses inadequate: it dismissed Shieldalloy’s transition concerns, relied on New Jersey’s general authority to continue pending licensing actions, and rejected retention or partial transfer of jurisdiction without adequately explaining either the smooth transition of Shieldalloy’s decommissioning process or the availability of a limited transfer. The NRC’s Oklahoma transfer practice demonstrated that site- or material-specific exclusions had previously been approved. The court also declined to defer to the statutory interpretation first advanced by NRC counsel at oral argument.

Because the NRC failed to provide a rational connection between the facts and its decision, the court held the transfer arbitrary and capricious. It granted Shieldalloy’s petition, vacated the transfer, and remanded the matter for proceedings consistent with its opinion. The court did not decide Shieldalloy’s other claims concerning decommissioning standards, ALARA, restricted use, radiation limits, exemptions, or regulatory fairness, but noted the NRC Criteria Document’s unexplained omission of the NRC’s license termination rule.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine provides optional SEV/SNP extensions for copying page contents between physical memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses. It supports tiered-memory optimization by moving frequently accessed data to faster memory and safely migrating pages subject to concurrent DMA or protected by Secure Nested Paging (SNP). TMPM requires IOMMU enablement, and software must verify the PM_STATUS ENGINE_READY bit before communicating with the engine.

TMPM commands are submitted through a dedicated ring buffer. The software controls the write pointer, firmware controls the read pointer, and commands may execute in parallel without guaranteed ordering. Commands can contain up to 128 migration entries; entries need not be contiguous, may reference multiple guests, and have no order dependency. Overall and per-page statuses report success, partial success, or failure. PM_SUCCESS indicates all pages migrated, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires inspecting entry statuses, and PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE can be retried after an RMP conflict.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO moves non-SNP pages or SNP Hypervisor-owned pages, including pages undergoing DMA. It coordinates with IOMMUs, marks and updates host page-table entries, invalidates and synchronizes TLBs, flushes DMA, copies page data while preserving encryption as applicable, and remaps the destination. Software must prevent CPU access and update CPU host-page-table mappings after successful migration. Direct migration of 2M pages is unsupported; they must first be split into 4K pages.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages and requires RMP enforcement, exclusive source and destination RMP entries, and a valid guest-context page. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, while destination pages must be in the new Pre-Migration state. After migration, destination pages assume the source state and source pages return to Pre-Migration. DMA during this operation is unsupported. A Pre-Migration page uses a platform-specific ASID, cannot be validated by a guest, and is restored to Hypervisor state through RMPUpdate.

PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports firmware capabilities and versions, while PM_NOOP can mark the end of a command sequence. System physical addresses use 46- or 52-bit encoding depending on system-encryption configuration and must be properly formed and aligned.

The ring buffer supports initialization, shutdown, pausing, resuming, low-water, empty, completion, and error notifications through a shared interrupt. Software must not alter its configuration during operation and must prevent concurrent modification of IOMMU host-page-table entries referenced by TMPM. Migration is restricted to 4K-aligned pages; IOMMU structures, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, the TMPM ring buffer, and argument pages cannot be migrated.

Performance is highest with 16 or more pages per command, peaking at 128 pages. Keeping the ring buffer supplied and interrupting only after a sequence of commands is recommended.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only while no operations are in flight; software must pause processing and tear down the ring buffer before using the BIOS-to-PSP reload protocol. Reload firmware must be the same version or newer. For EPYC Family 19h, identified through PM_GET_CAPABILITIES with FW_VER_Major value 71, the updated image and reload header are submitted through ASP mailbox registers.

Command-format errors cause rejection, migration-entry errors may produce partial success, ring-buffer errors are reported through PM_STATUS, and hardware failures are reported through command status and/or Machine Check Architecture. Clients detecting timeouts should log an MCA and determine whether to preserve state, terminate guests, or stop issuing commands.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture on effective field theory (EFT) with fine tuning considers cases where naive dimensional power counting labels an operator irrelevant although it must be retained at leading order, requiring a modified power counting that corresponds to expanding around an interacting rather than trivial fixed point. The example is two-nucleon EFT, a non-relativistic theory (p ≪ m_π) in which exchange particles are integrated out, leaving contact interactions and their derivatives, and in which all loops can be computed to all orders.

The lecture begins with elastic two-particle scattering in the center-of-mass frame, partial-wave phase shifts, S-matrix unitarity, and the effective range expansion, the fact that p cot δ admits a Taylor expansion in p for a short-range potential. The EFT reproduces this theorem without specifying a potential: the Lagrangian contains a kinetic term and four-nucleon contact operators with 2M derivatives and Wilson coefficients, with fermionic antisymmetry restricting allowed spin-isospin channels (isotriplets have S+L even, isosinglets odd), yielding simple tree-level Feynman rules.

A bubble loop shows why the naive power counting fails: retaining only the ∂_t kinetic term, as in HQET, leaves an ill-defined integral with a pinch singularity, so the kinetic energy term of order p²/2M must be kept, as is generally true for two heavy particles (the same issue arises in non-relativistic QCD and QED). Keeping it removes the pinch pole, and the loop supplies the imaginary part required by unitarity.

Power counting gives a 1/M scaling for the C_{2M} coefficients and for both tree-level and loop amplitudes; the bubbles decouple, so the complete amplitude sums to a geometric series. Matching to experiment reproduces the effective range expansion, identifying the S-wave scattering length a and effective range r0 with combinations of the coefficients (Ĉ0 = a, Ĉ2 = r0/2 − a²); the P-wave scattering length is 1/Ĉ2. Measured values are a ≈ 23 fm (1S0) and 5 fm (3S1), corresponding to 1/a ≈ 8.3 MeV and ≈ 36 MeV, far below the pion scale (~138 MeV), while r0 has its expected size. The large scattering lengths constitute the fine tuning, requiring C0 to be promoted from irrelevant to relevant so that ap can be of order one or larger.

Because MS-bar does not track power-law divergences, the lecture introduces off-shell momentum subtraction (evaluating the amplitude at P = iμ) and the power-divergence subtraction scheme in dimensional regularization (subtracting poles at D=3 as well as D=4). Both track the power divergence, give the same answer, and yield a one-loop-exact running of C0 with solution C0 ∝ 1/(Mμ). The beta function for C0 has three fixed points: a = 0 (non-interacting) and a = ±∞ (interacting, scale invariant, with conformal symmetry and an enhanced SU(4) spin-isospin symmetry); its pole at a = 1/μ corresponds to a bound state, the deuteron, invisible to perturbation theory. Propagating the fine-tuning enhancement through the running of the other coefficients (e.g., C2 is enhanced by two powers) yields a momentum expansion in which the amplitude is independent of μ. Such effective theories are used for precision calculations of deuteron physics, including deuteron formation in the sun.

European shares headed for a fifth consecutive session of losses and their biggest weekly decline since November 2016, with the STOXX 600 down about 1.8% amid rising bond yields and euro strength. Germany’s DAX, previously a market leader, fell more than 5% in eight sessions and turned negative year to date. Deutsche Bank was expected to drop 4%-5% after reporting a larger-than-expected €497 million loss for 2017, its third consecutive annual loss; Caixabank and Sabadell also declined following mixed results. STOXX 600 fourth-quarter earnings were nevertheless forecast to rise 11.9% year on year. Bank of America Merrill-Lynch’s “Bull & Bear” indicator issued a Sell signal, leading its strategists to adopt near-term caution while remaining constructive longer term on expected global growth and double-digit earnings growth. Rising yields also increased funding and unwinding risks for leveraged investors. Markets awaited U.S. payroll data on February 2, while European technology stocks reacted to results from major U.S. companies, including Apple, Amazon, Facebook and Alphabet.

The paper experimentally evaluates whether large language models can autoformalize hybrid physics problems from natural language into differential game logic, preserving continuous dynamics and discrete transitions. Twenty benchmarks derived from challenging undergraduate kinematics problems were used, alongside four solved examples for few-shot prompting. The pipeline asks an LLM to propose and revise dGL models, uses KeYmaera X parser feedback for syntax repair, and applies Delphyne, Z3, and Mathematica for semantic checking.

The checker symbolically executes each model to test equivalence with the expected solution and performs static analysis to ensure enough variables are modified, ruling out models in stasis. A running mean-velocity example shows how symbolic checking can expose subtle modeling errors and unstated assumptions, such as positivity and nonzero distance.

The system was tested with GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and OpenAI o3 under zero-shot and few-shot prompting. GPT-4o failed every benchmark without examples, while few-shot prompting substantially improved all models. Reported success rates were 20% for GPT-4o, 45% for GPT-4.1, and 70% for o3. Six problems remained unsolved because their optimization, non-polynomial, or otherwise complicated dynamics exceeded checker capabilities, caused tool failures or timeouts, or produced models too complex to verify. Proposed improvements include extending solvers with techniques such as continuous invariant generation and guiding models toward useful abstractions, coordinates, auxiliary variables, and checking hints. Future applications include runtime formalization by autonomous systems using vision and sensor data.

Mark Valladares, Monday Editor of Liberal Democrat Voice, reports from Creeting St Peter, Suffolk, after snow, and notes ministers’ efforts to undermine Theresa May’s EU deal. Simon Coveney’s quotation stresses that Article 46 commitments must be upheld, while the writer questions leadership and the possible consequences. The programme previews House of Lords business, especially Liberal Democrat contributions, including Paul Walter’s award scheme for young activists in by-election campaigns and the Samaritans’ work supporting lonely people. It ends with a musical “goodbye” interlude and invites submissions.

This study aims to improve psychiatric assessment of depression and anxiety by identifying objective, data-driven biomarkers from clinical interviews. Researchers at Shanghai Mental Health Center collected more than 15,000 minutes of speech recordings from 1,160 Mandarin-speaking outpatients aged 12–80 with 25 diagnoses between August 2023 and January 2024. Diagnoses used the Chinese ICD-10, and recordings were manually de-identified.

The recordings were preprocessed, transcribed automatically, and manually corrected. Psychiatrists helped define clinical entities, and a pretrained large language model (LLM) was fine-tuned with their annotations to identify clinical concepts, symptom disclosures, and assessment-scale components from transcripts. Linguistic and acoustic features were also extracted. An ensemble machine-learning pipeline combined these modalities to predict diagnostic groups and major symptoms, achieving moderately high accuracy and identifying salient patterns across diagnostic groups.

The work addresses limitations in current research, including subtle speech markers, LLM interpretability, restricted clinical data, overlapping depression and anxiety symptoms, and the semantic gap between patients’ descriptions and clinicians’ terminology. The authors conclude that LLM-derived clinical cues combined with other behavioral markers may support more efficient and effective psychiatric diagnosis and assessment.

Theo Walcott scored the only goal in Everton’s 1-0 Premier League win over Newcastle, netting in the 51st minute at Goodison Park after an even opening half. His shot followed Yannick Bolasie’s cross, a defensive ricochet and a touch to his right.

Cover Zero is a high-risk, all-out pressure defense that forces quarterbacks to make quick decisions and discourages third-and-long situations. However, blitzing leaves coverage defenders isolated, opens the middle of the field, and allows quick-hit plays to punish the defense. Effective answers include perimeter weapons, slants, shallow crossing routes, pick plays, rubs, and pre-snap motion. Examples from Ole Miss, Oregon, Michigan, Wake Forest, and a Jerry Rice motion concept demonstrate how offenses create separation, exploit leverage, or find uncovered receivers for first downs and touchdowns.

Former Aberdeen manager Steve Paterson suggested Pittodrie host the funeral of Neale “Tattie” Cooper, who died in hospital aged 54 after falling downstairs. Cooper, a member of Aberdeen’s 1983 European Cup Winners’ Cup team, drew widespread tributes, with the club saying it would follow his family’s wishes.

FlowMotion ONE is a wearable smartphone stabilizer that eliminates shake and vibration using sensors and high-precision motors. Its 3-in-1 design works with camera mounts, a joystick-equipped handle, or an extension pole, and it weighs less than a pound. Its Kickstarter campaign raised over $600,000 from more than 2,700 backers against a $30,000 goal and was funded within one hour. Founded in 2015 by Lars Flesland, Julie Bauge, Eirik Dyrseth and Didrik Dimmen, the 10-person company develops hardware and software for smooth, cinema-quality smartphone video. FlowMotion has offices in Palo Alto and Trondheim, Norway, and has received several business and product awards.

Global cancer incidence increased from 12.7 million cases in 2008 to 19.3 million in 2020. Cervical cancer causes substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in low-resource regions; Africa has the highest age-standardized incidence and cumulative risk. HPV types 16 and 18 accounted for an estimated 72% of cervical cancer cases globally in 2018. Although HPV vaccination and screening can prevent cervical cancer or enable early detection, screening coverage remains low in many low- and middle-income countries. The study assessed cervical cancer and screening awareness among women aged 15–49 in Benin and Cameroon using nationally representative 2017–2018 Demographic and Health Survey data.

The analysis included 21,322 women: 7,706 from Benin and 13,616 from Cameroon. Of these, 7,010 women who had heard of cervical cancer were also asked about cervical screening awareness. Outcomes were measured as yes/no responses to French-language questions. Demographic characteristics and media use were assessed using weighted descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and survey-adjusted multivariable logistic regression, with countries analyzed separately.

Only 9.5% of women in Benin and 46.1% in Cameroon were aware of cervical cancer. Among women aware of cervical cancer, 51.4% in Benin and 59.7% in Cameroon were aware of cervical screening. Descriptively, awareness was higher among urban, more educated, wealthier, and professional women and among women using television, radio, newspapers, or the internet.

After adjustment, cervical cancer awareness was associated with older age, higher education, and frequent internet use in both countries. In Benin, higher education was associated with approximately six times greater odds of awareness compared with no education, while women aged 45 or older had 1.89 times the odds of women aged 15–24. In Cameroon, the corresponding adjusted odds ratios were 9.36 for higher education and 2.91 for age 45 or older. Wealth was also associated with awareness in Cameroon, with the richest quintile having 3.46 times the odds of the poorest quintile. Daily internet use was associated with awareness in both countries, although weekly newspaper reading was associated with lower adjusted odds in Benin.

For cervical screening awareness, the adjusted associations differed by country. In Benin, women aged 25–34 had higher odds of awareness than those aged 15–24, higher education was associated with greater awareness, and weekly radio listening was associated with higher odds. In Cameroon, awareness increased with age; current or former marriage, secondary or higher education, and daily internet use were also associated with greater awareness.

As of 2021, neither country had a national HPV vaccination or cervical cancer screening program, and fewer than one in ten women in either country had been screened within the previous five years. The study recommends stakeholder engagement, implementable national screening programs, stronger awareness and public-education efforts, age-appropriate information for younger women, and use of radio and internet media. It also identifies a need to address awareness inequalities related to poverty and residential segregation in Cameroon. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small screening-awareness subsample, potential sampling bias, interviewer-assisted self-reporting, recall bias, and unmeasured confounding.

An Oklahoma veterinarian removed 21 pacifiers from Dovey’s stomach after X-rays estimated seven to nine. The dog had slowed eating and vomited phlegm. Following surgery, Dovey recovered and went home.

SARS-CoV-2 RNA monitoring in wastewater is a critical surveillance tool, but conventional concentration methods typically require 50–250 mL samples and centrifugation, creating challenges for resource-limited laboratories. Nanotrap hydrogel particles can capture, separate, and protect analytes, preserve viruses and nucleic acids for up to three days, and concentrate multiple pathogens. Previous studies applied Nanotrap particles to SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus in wastewater.

Grab sampling is simple but represents only a snapshot; composite sampling is more representative but costly and time-consuming; and passive sampling provides a sensitive, low-cost alternative. The study used weekly Atlanta wastewater samples collected from June through August 2021, including 24-hour Moore swabs at community manholes and 500 mL grab samples from treatment-plant influent lines. Grab samples underwent membrane filtration, while the more turbid Moore swab samples used skim-milk concentration.

The study evaluated how pH, temperature, incubation time, sample volume, RNA extraction, and one-step Nanotrap versus two-step skim-milk-plus-Nanotrap concentration affect SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection. It also compared automated high-throughput processing with manual 10 mL Nanotrap methods and assessed whether 10 mL manual Nanotrap concentration approaches remain as sensitive as membrane filtration of 150 mL grab samples and skim-milk concentration of 250 mL Moore swab samples.

The passage compiles reports and commentary published December 11–12, 2000, concerning Enron, electricity and natural-gas markets, and retail energy competition.

Electric utility stocks rose 36% year to date before flattening, while analysts said a technology-stock recovery could divert investment from utilities. Tight generating capacity was expected to persist for two or three years, supporting energy traders such as Enron and Dynegy. Analysts expected utility earnings to remain strong but questioned whether this year’s roughly 20% average profit growth could be repeated. Views cited favored companies including Calpine, Progress Energy, American Electric Power and Xcel Energy, while California utilities were criticized as heavily indebted.

India’s Enron unit, Dabhol Power, received 450-basis-point loan-rate cuts from four lenders, reducing rates to 16.5% and potentially lowering the tariff charged to the Maharashtra government for the $1.9 billion, 2,184-MW project. The company expected to switch from costlier naphtha to natural gas in 2001. Critics said the agreement imposed excessive consumer costs and benefited political and bureaucratic interests. A retired judge said the 1993 power-purchase agreement could be nullified on public-interest grounds, citing fixed annual charges, power costs far above alternatives, lack of competitive bidding and alleged exploitation.

Natural-gas prices reached a record $9.413 per million British thermal units on NYMEX. Terra Industries, Mississippi Chemical and Seneca Resources began selling gas rather than using it in fertilizer, chemical and oil-production operations, while Kaiser Aluminum planned to sell contracted electricity associated with closed smelters. Industry participants expected more companies to face financial pressure from energy costs and volatility, while some anticipated gas prices returning to historical levels of $2–$3.

Activate, a majority-owned CMGI digital-media company, reported more than 8,000 business clients, 40,000 webcasts and over 100 million streams in 2000. It expanded facilities and geographic operations, coordinated content-distribution networks including Enron, received industry awards, and built market positions in financial, entertainment and advertising webcasting.

Green Mountain Energy applied to become Texas’s first renewable-power retail electricity provider when competition opens January 1, 2002. Other applicants included Enron units, the Enron-IBM-AOL New Power Company, Shell Energy Services and utility affiliates; a 5% customer pilot was scheduled for June. The New Power Company was also certified as a Georgia retail natural-gas marketer and planned to begin serving customers in 2001, following acquisitions totaling about 300,000 gas and electricity accounts.

Internet energy exchanges were gaining traction, especially in natural gas and power, although oil traders remained cautious. EnronOnline reported average daily volume of $10.5 billion and 35,000 transactions in more than 30 commodities, while IntercontinentalExchange also led smaller online competitors. Dynegydirect recorded more than $1.5 billion in November trading with over 400 companies and planned to add coal, emissions allowances, weather derivatives, international products and bandwidth. Analysts predicted greater online trading as commission costs fell, followed by consolidation among exchanges.

A retrospective analysis of Wisconsin Poison Center records in the National Poison Data System identified 59 kratom exposure calls from January 2010 through September 2022. Calls increased from one in 2011 to a peak of 15 in 2020 and were concentrated in southeastern Wisconsin. Most exposed individuals were male, and the mean age among 52 people with age data was 35.3 years. Three unintentional exposures involved infants under age two, and one exposed person was pregnant.

Agitation, tachycardia, confusion, and central nervous system depression were the most frequently reported findings. Of 50 cases with known outcomes, 19 had moderate or major outcomes. Seven of 36 people with known healthcare utilization required critical care; one patient died, with postmortem toxicology identifying kratom as contributory. Approximately 44% of exposures involved multiple substances, most commonly alcohol and benzodiazepines.

The authors noted limitations including small case numbers, passive surveillance, inconsistent toxicology testing for mitragynine, unregulated product composition, and co-ingestion. They recommended increased provider awareness and documentation of kratom exposure, caution regarding concurrent substance use, education for adults who use kratom, safe-storage messaging for adults with children, and continued research to clarify kratom’s risks and benefits.

Ben Baby’s Texas A&M mailbag considers whether a loss to Alabama would make Florida a must-win for coach Kevin Sumlin, noting the Aggies need strong finishes to reach eight wins for a fourth straight season. The field will honor Gene Stallings and the 1967 Cotton Bowl team; no throwback uniforms are planned. Other questions address fall weddings during games, an ignored Aggie DJ request, a Steve Austin promotion for the UTSA game, the “Go Mean Green” nickname, Arsene Wenger, and Chipotle as the preferred burrito spot.

Investing.com’s market page reports a risk-on July: the S&P 500 gained 2.2% for the month and 7.8% year to date, despite slipping 1.6% on August’s first trading day. U.S. large-cap stocks ranked third for July but were mid-table year to date as global stocks led. Volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, investors are increasing tech allocations, and U.S. electricity demand reached a record. Short-term technicals show weakening breadth, bearish divergence and building selling pressure, while longer-term trends remain healthy. Other coverage includes muted Asian stocks, U.S. shutdown concerns, gold above $3,800 per ounce, dollar weakness and AI investment strategies. The page warns that trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies carries substantial risk and that quoted data may not be real-time or accurate.

Randomized, open-label 48-week trial of 1,112 NVAF subjects receiving apixaban compared SOC information with an education program. At 24 weeks, education recipients were rerandomized to continue education or revert to SOC. Electronic monitoring assessed 24-hour adherence; one missed dose counted as adherence, while two consecutive misses constituted nonadherence.

Questions remain over whether a suspect arrested in Germany acted for the Federal Intelligence Service (FIS), and whether Swiss authorities exposed him. The OAG watchdog denied involvement in spying or leaking his identity through unredacted files. The former policeman is under investigation for trading stolen banking data, while sources questioned information from his lawyer and a parliamentarian. The government confirmed FIS help was requested and faced calls for transparency and parliamentary inquiry.

Memphis police said a 2-year-old girl shot in the head in a parking lot has died. Her mother reported an argument with another driver before being followed and shots being fired. No arrests have been made.

Players credited the team’s success to long-standing cohesion, trust, and comfort built over years, helping them handle difficult stretches and integrate new players. Dustin Brown said a lead against Chicago provided physical and emotional breathing room, while acknowledging the team was not in its desired position. Anze Kopitar said the win despite slow legs and a poor start showed character. Both emphasized focusing on the next game, resetting after each playoff round, and reflecting later.

Brown praised Drew Doughty’s development from Olympic exposure and the Sochi championship, citing improved play and emerging leadership on and off the ice. He described the team’s playoff style as making it difficult to beat in a seven-game series and stressed the distinction between contending for a division title and a Stanley Cup.

Kopitar said “Gabby” fit a room full of established leaders and quickly felt comfortable because of the group’s closeness. Brown described Justin Williams as laid-back but increasingly focused before games. He attributed the team’s bond to years together, voluntary workouts, a lack of cliques, and easy integration of newcomers, contrasting it with the high roster turnover of his early years. Kopitar also said games between major cities increase interest in hockey through media coverage, excitement, and city pride.

Cayman Islands prison authorities plan to transfer selected, risk-assessed low-risk inmates from overcrowded HMP Northward to a cordoned-off section of the Immigration Detention Centre at Fairbanks. The move could free about 22 places amid security, rehabilitation and offender-management concerns while a permanent solution is pursued. Officials say separating prison and immigration detainees will maintain safety and compliance, though the centre is at capacity and nine asylum-seeking detainees have begun a hunger strike.

The application, a continuation of earlier U.S., international, and Chinese applications, concerns 5G wireless communication processing for radio bearers in which PDCP data is duplicated across first and second RLC entities or paths. One embodiment allows a terminal device to report the data volume of one duplication path to a radio access network. The path may be selected by network indication, priority, or buffered data volume, and the report may be sent through a corresponding or alternative cell or cell group, reducing signaling overhead compared with reporting every path.

Another embodiment manages activation and deactivation of duplication mode for a radio bearer. The radio access network may determine activation based on channel quality, cell load, measurement reports, or high-priority data, and may control uplink and downlink modes separately. Flexible MAC or RRC indication-message formats identify whether duplication is active and may identify affected radio bearers or paths. The terminal manages duplicated data and data-volume reports, communicates duplicated-data numbering or count differences, and, upon deactivation, may discard unnecessary duplicate data to reduce resource waste. Maximum RLC retransmissions on a second path need not trigger radio-link failure or re-establishment because the first path can continue transmitting.

The description also covers radio-bearer protocol architectures, including carrier aggregation, dual connectivity, and CU-DU deployments; mappings between paths, logical channels, cells, and cell groups; and communications apparatus comprising processing, receiving, and sending units, as well as processor-based devices and computer storage media.

Environment Canada issued a special weather statement for Edmonton and surrounding areas, including regions south and east to the Saskatchewan border, as conditions favoured funnel clouds Wednesday afternoon. Weak-rotation funnel clouds could develop, with a slim chance of becoming landspout tornadoes with winds near 100 km/h. Sightings were reported near Namao, where students were kept inside. Environment Canada urged people to seek shelter if funnel clouds appeared.

Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.2% to 7,476.12, heading for its fourth straight decline and worst week in nearly six months, as disappointing BT and AstraZeneca earnings outweighed gains elsewhere. BT dropped over 5% to a five-year low amid stagnant divisions, patchy metrics and pension concerns. AstraZeneca fell 1.7% on a disappointing profit outlook. Anglo American, Antofagasta and Rio Tinto gained 0.3%-0.9% as copper strengthened, while Shell and BP rose 0.7% and 0.4%. Capita climbed over 5% after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to equal-weight.

Microsoft Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the quarter ended September 30, 2020. Revenue was $37.154 billion, up 12% from $33.055 billion in the prior-year quarter. Gross margin rose 15% to $26.152 billion, operating income increased 25% to $15.876 billion, net income increased 30% to $13.893 billion, and diluted EPS rose 32% to $1.82.

Revenue and operating income increased across all three reportable segments. Productivity and Business Processes generated $12.319 billion of revenue and $5.706 billion of operating income; Intelligent Cloud generated $12.986 billion and $5.422 billion; and More Personal Computing generated $11.849 billion and $4.748 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 31% to $15.2 billion, with Azure revenue up 48%, Office 365 Commercial up 21%, and Dynamics 365 up 38%. Xbox content and services revenue rose 30%, Surface revenue increased 37%, and search advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs declined 10%.

At September 30, 2020, total assets were $301.001 billion, total liabilities were $177.609 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $123.392 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $137.977 billion. Net cash from operations was $19.335 billion, while investing and financing activities used $5.371 billion and $10.289 billion, respectively. Research and development expense increased 8% to $4.926 billion.

Microsoft increased the estimated useful lives of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years, increasing quarterly operating income by $927 million and net income by $763 million, or $0.10 per basic and diluted share. The company also agreed to acquire ZeniMax Media for $7.5 billion in cash, expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2021.

COVID-19 increased demand for cloud, gaming, and Surface products but reduced advertising spending and transactional licensing. Remaining performance obligations totaled $111 billion. Deloitte reviewed the interim financial information and reported no material modifications.

The court granted summary judgment for defendants on all remaining claims. Melissa Jennings alleged that UNC women’s soccer coach Anson Dorrance made sexually explicit comments about players, made personal inquiries into her dating life, and dismissed her from the team in May 1998. Assistant coach William Palladino participated less frequently. Jennings reported the conduct to university officials, after which complaints were reviewed and Dorrance apologized and was directed not to discuss sexual matters with players.

The court found no genuine dispute that the alleged conduct was not sufficiently severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive to support hostile-environment harassment under Title IX or § 1983. The comments occurred less than weekly, arose largely in player-initiated conversations, were not threatening, and did not prevent Jennings from participating in soccer or academics. The isolated personal inquiries did not violate constitutional privacy rights because Jennings was not forced to disclose information, her reproductive decisions were not impeded, and her refusal did not lead to dismissal. Because Dorrance and Palladino’s conduct did not violate constitutional rights, the court did not reach whether university supervisors knew of the conduct or were deliberately indifferent. Dorrance’s conduct also did not meet North Carolina’s egregious, intrusive standard for common-law invasion of privacy.

The court denied Jennings’s motion to strike defendants’ amended answer and seek default judgment because Dorrance’s inability to recall all pre-practice conversations did not clearly contradict the pleading and no bad faith was shown. It also denied her motion to strike Exhibits C–H because the documents were authenticated and qualified as regularly conducted records admissible at trial. The motion to submit additional evidence under seal was denied.

Treasury minister Mel Stride assured Labour MP Mel Onn that British fish fingers would be “safe in the hands of this Government.” Onn sought continued customs arrangements to prevent delays and protect Great Grimsby’s time-sensitive fish trade, processing sector, and 5,000 jobs.

This continuation application describes an event-based data intake and query system for collecting, indexing, storing, and searching large volumes of machine-generated data from data centers and other IT environments. Raw or minimally processed data are retained as timestamped events with metadata such as host, source, source type, and time. A flexible late-binding schema applies configurable extraction rules, including regular expressions, at search time, allowing fields to be added, modified, or removed and enabling unified searches across disparate data sources.

In typical deployments, forwarders receive, annotate, transform, parse, and route data; indexers determine event boundaries and timestamps, create keyword and field-value inverted indexes, and store events in time-based buckets; and search heads execute and aggregate queries. Systems may operate on-premises, in the cloud, or in hybrid configurations and search external “virtual indices” through External Result Provider processes that translate native queries into external formats. These processes can operate in streaming mode, reporting mode, or both.

The disclosure also covers client-side monitoring of network, device, and application performance; hot, warm, cold, quarantine, and frozen storage buckets; replication for availability and disaster recovery; and indexer-based filtering, categorization, grouping, and counting of search results.

This qualitative study examines how information technology and management strategies can support language education in Indonesia within the Education 4.0 context. It reviews alternatives to in-person learning, particularly online platforms and mobile learning, and reports that COVID-19 accelerated digital adoption. The study combines descriptive and comparative analysis, literature review, observation, and framework development. Of 1,010 Scopus articles related to IT and management in language education, 151, or 15.1%, were considered strongly relevant, with multiple researchers involved in triangulation.

Challenges include insufficient teacher training and technological proficiency, difficulty maintaining student engagement, limited or unequal access to devices, connectivity, and instructional resources, and difficulties assessing speaking and listening remotely. University students also faced weak self-regulation, reduced motivation, lost social interaction, and limited real-time language practice. Wider barriers included infrastructure disparities, cultural differences in adapting to online learning, and fragmented support.

Technologies discussed include augmented and virtual reality, IoT, AI, learning management systems, gamification, 3D printing, blockchain, cloud computing, robotics, and big data. Automatic Speech Recognition provides real-time pronunciation feedback and supports vocabulary learning, while task-based and game-based approaches promote active practice, contextual vocabulary use, motivation, and retention.

Recommended management strategies include digital platforms for synchronous and asynchronous learning, teacher professional development, AI-based language support and translation tools, international virtual exchanges, cloud and mobile infrastructure, data-driven decision-making, and inclusive IT policies. Students generally view technology positively, but resistance, low digital literacy, unreliable tools, and unequal access remain concerns. Effective integration therefore requires technological support, accessible resources, teacher guidance, collaborative learning opportunities, and careful alignment with teaching methods and student needs.

The agreement is severable and governed by California and federal law, excluding the CISG. Santa Clara County courts have exclusive jurisdiction. Exports must comply with U.S. law, and amendments or waivers require signed written authorization.

A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit accusing the College Board and 40 selective private institutions of conspiring to fix tuition prices. U.S. District Judge Sara Ellis said the plaintiffs failed to plausibly allege an agreement to collude. The court acknowledged that requiring both custodial and noncustodial parents’ financial information inflated tuition, but found no evidence the schools shared aid decisions or agreed on a common formula.

Prosecutor-General Martha Imalwa described human trafficking as the third-largest international crime, generating $32 billion annually, with 20–30 million people enslaved and 600,000–800,000 trafficked across borders yearly. Her office sought UNODC assistance to train Namibians in detecting, assisting victims of, and prosecuting trafficking. Police recorded 25 cases from 2010–2017: six await trial, three prosecutions were declined, one conviction and one acquittal occurred, and 14 remain under investigation.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the intranasal, self-administered SA58 monoclonal antibody spray as post-exposure prophylaxis among healthy adult workers at 21 construction sites in Beijing with Omicron BF.7 outbreaks. Eligible participants had contacted a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 case within 72 hours. Of 1,694 screened people, 1,634 were randomized; the full analysis included 901 SA58 and 321 placebo recipients, while efficacy analysis excluded 99 baseline RT-PCR-positive participants.

In the efficacy population, symptomatic COVID-19 occurred in 7 of 824 SA58 recipients and 14 of 299 placebo recipients, corresponding to estimated protective efficacy of 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%). SARS-CoV-2 infection occurred in 32 participants in each group, yielding estimated efficacy of 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). All 21 sequenced infections were Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred.

Adverse events were generally mild: at least one occurred in 25% of SA58 and 22% of placebo recipients. All were grade 1, with no serious adverse events, adverse events of special interest, withdrawals, or deaths. Nasal dryness, runny nose, fever, nasal congestion, headache, cough, and throat dryness were among the most common events, with no significant differences between groups.

The study ended early before reaching its planned sample size and had limited follow-up. Results may not generalize beyond predominantly healthy workers to older, medically vulnerable, or high-risk groups. Larger, longer studies and evaluation in such populations were recommended.

The passage describes an airway-management medical system for assisting rescuers during endotracheal intubation and rapid sequence intubation (RSI). It incorporates airway sensors, physiological sensors, positioning sensors, electrodes, a patient-monitoring device, portable computing devices, wrist-worn devices, and optional central-facility connectivity. Sensors may measure oxygen, carbon dioxide, flow, pressure, volume, oxygen saturation, ETCO2, ECG, acoustic information, transthoracic impedance, blood pressure, motion, position, and imaging data.

The system uses these measurements to detect procedure steps and provide context-sensitive guidance. RSI guidance covers the “7 Ps”: Preparation, Preoxygenation, Pretreatment, Paralysis with induction, Protection and Positioning, Placement with Proof, and Post-intubation management. It can initiate preoxygenation and procedure timers, determine when tube placement begins, detect patient-positioning needs, calculate drug dosage, generate alarms for hypoxemia, and display prioritized clinical information and feedback.

For endotracheal-tube verification, the system detects airway airflow and uses capnography, transthoracic impedance, or acoustic measurements to determine whether ventilation reached the lungs. A timer, including predefined or user-defined intervals of 5–15 seconds, may confirm initial placement. Continued placement can be assessed using ETCO2, impedance, or acoustic values compared with initial or dynamic moving-average baselines and predetermined criteria. Alarms indicate improper placement or displacement.

Displays may provide visual, audible, or haptic feedback through monitors, tablets, smartphones, laptops, smartwatches, or head-mounted devices. The system may also record procedure events, timers, alarms, physiological data, and completed or incomplete tasks for quality-assurance reports and debriefing. The passage additionally identifies priority applications and numerous drawings depicting system components, workflows, dashboards, tube verification, and RSI stages.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, requiring major AI developers to disclose safety protocols, report serious incidents to the state, protect whistleblowers, and face civil penalties for noncompliance. The law also launches CalCompute, a public computing consortium for safe and ethical AI research. It focuses on transparency rather than liability and applies to companies using enormous computing resources; firms with less than $500 million in annual revenue are exempt from certain obligations.

Industry response was divided. Anthropic supported the law, while Meta expressed support and OpenAI, which did not endorse the bill, welcomed its potential to align state and federal standards. Critics warned that compliance costs could disadvantage startups, entrench larger companies, and create a patchwork of state rules. Other experts called the penalties weak and said stronger reporting thresholds and independent evaluations are needed. Because 32 of the world’s 50 leading AI companies are based in California, the law may influence broader AI oversight.

Cleveland forward Kevin Love reflected on a turbulent season marked by physical injuries, relentless criticism, trade rumors and his longstanding anxiety and panic attacks. After disclosing his struggles in a Player’s Tribune essay, Love received thousands of supportive messages and credited counseling with making him more empathetic and strengthening relationships, while maintaining that basketball remains his safe space. His postseason has been uneven: he struggled against Indiana and the Raptors before rebounding, then suffered a concussion in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference finals. His status for Cleveland’s fourth straight NBA Finals opener remained uncertain, but he said his time with the Cavaliers has been worthwhile.

Tropical Storm Nate, formed off Nicaragua and blamed for at least 17 deaths in Central America, was forecast to cross the eastern Yucatán Peninsula Friday night, strengthen into a hurricane, and approach the northern Gulf Coast early Sunday. Pensacola was within the warning cone, with officials expecting the area on Nate’s eastern side, where higher wind gusts, storm surge and tornadoes were more likely.

Escambia and Santa Rosa counties were under a tropical storm watch, with heavy rain, flash flooding and tornadoes possible Saturday through at least Sunday. Forecast winds were 35–45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph in Escambia County and 15–25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph in Santa Rosa County, with 3–5 inches of rain expected. Eglin Air Force Base was at Hurricane Condition 4.

Residents were urged to obtain supplies, follow local media and prepare sandbags; free sand was available, but residents needed to bring shovels. Gov. Rick Scott declared emergencies in 29 Florida counties, including Escambia and Santa Rosa. The National Guard was available for deployment, and officials prepared shelters, evacuation support, utility assistance and fuel planning; no fuel shortages were reported.

UWF closed Saturday through Monday, while its football game was moved to Friday. Several other events were canceled, postponed or rescheduled. Gulf Islands National Seashore closed, and Fort Pickens and Davis Bayou campers were ordered to evacuate by noon Friday.

Three comic-book superhero films—Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Wonder Woman and Spider-Man: Homecoming—dominated the 2017 summer box office and drew praise from audiences and critics. Most other genres produced only one notable success: Despicable Me 3 led with more than $920 million worldwide, while Girls Trip, Annabelle: Creation, Dunkirk, Baby Driver, 47 Meters Down, The Big Sick and Everything, Everything also performed relatively well.

Outside these hits, many films underperformed, including Cars 3, The Emoji Movie, King Arthur: Legend of the Sword, Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets, The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight and War for the Planet of the Apes. Overall, the season offered limited diversity at multiplexes as superhero movies crowded out other big-budget releases. The author argues that Hollywood’s response to franchise fatigue and other lessons from 2016 may not appear until 2019 because many release schedules were set years in advance.

Researchers at UC Irvine and other institutions introduced a satellite-based GRACE Drought Severity Index for global drought monitoring. Using NASA Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity observations, the index incorporates groundwater storage into assessments that commonly rely on precipitation. It enables consistent regional and global monitoring, including areas where ground measurements are difficult, and tracks groundwater changes affecting soil-moisture recharge and drought recovery. The 2002–2014 dataset will be extended through ongoing missions and a GRACE follow-on mission planned for early 2018. Evaluations in the continental United States found significant agreement with the Palmer index and vegetation and soil-moisture measures. The work was presented at the American Geophysical Union fall meeting.

At Birmingham’s BIMM Music Institute, Tony Iommi announced details of the BIMM Birmingham Scholarship, which he sponsors. Prospective students experienced the Digbeth college, while Iommi said the business requires persistence despite knockbacks and dislike.

A May 24, 2001 collection of reports examined California’s electricity crisis, Enron’s overseas ventures and energy-sector corporate activity.

- A Houston Chronicle opinion column criticized California Governor Gray Davis and Attorney General Bill Lockyer for targeting Texas energy producers and Enron during the state’s electricity crisis. It argued that Enron should have challenged Lockyer’s crude jail-cell remark and demanded a retraction or apology.

Generators cited operational and insurance reasons for withholding capacity, while federal regulators rejected the practice of reserving power from the spot market.

Analysts anticipated more scrutiny of drug and HMO companies, possible weakening of credit-card bankruptcy reforms, greater conflict over defense, energy and tobacco policy, reduced prospects for telecommunications deregulation, and benefits for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
- Brazil imposed electricity rationing to address a drought-driven power shortage, asking consumers and businesses to reduce usage by 15% to 25%. The government estimated that generation capacity needed to expand by 31,000 megawatts by 2008 at a cost of about $14 billion. Currency risks had delayed several gas-fired power projects, while Enron continued with plans for about 800 megawatts of new capacity.
- Republican gubernatorial candidate Bill Simon Jr. sought to minimize scrutiny of his investments and former board role at Hanover Compressor, an Enron partner. He supported expanded California drilling and temporary wholesale price caps but opposed offshore drilling and had no detailed energy plan.
- India appointed a federal representative to a Maharashtra panel negotiating with Enron’s Dabhol Power Co. over disputed power tariffs and unpaid bills. The government said it would consider acceptable settlement proposals. Panel chairman Madhav Godbole initially resigned after criticism from Sharad Pawar but withdrew his resignation following support from the state government.
- Central Europe’s gas markets were expected to change as Poland considered a Russian-gas transit pipeline and Slovakia and the Czech Republic prepared privatizations of major gas companies and infrastructure. Analysts also identified substantial growth potential for Poland’s gas market but warned that additional import contracts could overcontract distributors.
- Spain’s Endesa planned to auction its Electra de Viesgo subsidiary, valued at more than €2 billion, to finance expansion elsewhere in Europe. Enron, AES and other European energy companies were invited to bid.

The long-short equity strategy combines long positions in stocks expected to appreciate with short positions in stocks expected to decline. It seeks profits from both price movements while diversifying and potentially reducing risk. Hedge funds often apply a long bias, such as the 130/30 structure, because markets generally trend upward and profitable short ideas are historically harder to find.

The strategy requires identifying relatively undervalued and overvalued stocks through research. In the article’s example, a fund buys Merck shares at $85 and shorts Thor Industries shares at $75; subsequent price movements generate profits on both positions, though such outcomes are not guaranteed. Long and short legs may be selected from different sectors to reduce correlation. Because the strategy is complex, capital-intensive, and often reliant on leverage and derivatives, it is described as more suitable for institutional investors than retail investors.

Edward Thorp is identified as a pioneer of quantitative investing who used mechanical models to exploit market inefficiencies. He founded Princeton Newport Partners in 1969, which reportedly recorded no losing year through 1988 and compounded returns at 19.1%.

An illustrative Coca-Cola and Pepsi-Cola pair-trading backtest produced a 3.8% annual return, a 0.45% average gain across four trades, a maximum drawdown of about 11%, and 42% invested time. The article emphasizes using many pairs rather than depending on only one or two.

The study presents a machine-learning-assisted inverse-design workflow for identifying diammonium organic spacers that produce targeted energy-level alignments in Dion–Jacobson 2D perovskites. It uses a tailored, invertible 12-digit molecular fingerprint representing aromatic backbones, ammonium groups, heteroatom substitutions, and side chains. Molecular morphing expanded 21 known spacers to 21,306 fingerprint patterns corresponding to 4,887,100 hypothetical candidates, including all known spacers.

High-throughput DFT calculations for 3,239 candidates generated HOMO/LUMO training data. LASSO regression was selected for interpretability, achieving R² scores of 0.95 for both properties, while nonlinear models reached 0.99 for HOMO and 0.97 for LUMO. Feature analysis showed that ammonium-group structure and aromatic-ring count strongly influence frontier levels, with conjugation, electron richness, and heteroatom type providing additional design rules.

A two-step feasibility screen combined PubChem availability as a synthetic-accessibility proxy with a five-descriptor formability score; the score classified 27 of 29 known spacer cases correctly. DFT validation identified eight type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates, but no feasible type Ib candidates because those candidates were absent from PubChem. Constrained inverse design then identified two type Ib, 12 type IIa, and 42 type IIb candidates. Type Ib spacers required at least five linearly fused aromatic rings, including two pentacene-based candidates; type IIa candidates generally used extended acene or oligothiophene conjugation, while type IIb candidates typically had one primary ammonium group and multiple pyridine-type nitrogen substitutions.

The workflow remains limited by heuristic synthesis-feasibility estimates, unmodeled solubility and reaction conditions, fixed-length fingerprints, and the absence of experimental synthesis and energy-level characterization.

Ryan, the six-year-old star of Ryan ToysReview, ranked among Forbes’ top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars in 2017; the channel reportedly earned $11 million. Started in 2015, it surpassed 10 million subscribers and eight billion views. His parents say reviews will end if he loses interest.

A New York Times survey of federal district and appellate judges found widespread dissatisfaction with Supreme Court emergency docket decisions related to President Trump’s second-term policies. Of 65 respondents, 12 said the Court made appropriate use of the docket, while 47 disagreed and six were neutral; 12 said lower courts received sufficient guidance, compared with 48 who disagreed and five neutral. Of 54 judges addressing public perception, 42 said the docket harmed it, 10 saw no effect and two saw improvement. Some judges strongly criticized the orders, while a Trump appointee said they exposed anti-democratic rulings but warned of secretiveness or arbitrariness. The survey was sent to more than 400 judges. The Times cautioned that respondents may not represent the judiciary, while the Volokh Conspiracy criticized possible response bias and oversampling. At least seven of about 20 orders lacked reasoning, and nearly all benefited Trump, according to the Times.

The passage describes a circuit for driving the 16-bit, 1-MSPS ADS8860 SAR ADC with the PGA848. The PGA848 accepts single-ended or differential signals, uses ±15 V input-stage and 5.3 V output-stage supplies, and powers the ADC output stage from the 5.3 V supply to prevent ADC input overload during PGA overdrive. A REF6250 provides the ADC’s 5 V reference. A precision 10 kΩ-to-10 kΩ divider and OPA192 buffer generate a nominal 2.5 V PGA848 REF voltage, shifting the signal to ADC midscale.

Three filters suppress EMI, RFI, and noise; compensate for feedback-resistor tolerance; and provide charge-kickback compensation at the ADC inputs. With 75 pF CFB, the nominal PGA848 bandwidth is 318 kHz, or 277 kHz at the high feedback-resistor tolerance, while maintaining −0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. The OPA192 uses a dual-feedback network with RF = 2 kΩ, CF = 2 nF, and RISO = 20 Ω, providing 86° phase margin. Stability components must be recalculated if the REF bypass capacitance changes, and phase margin above 60° should be verified by simulation.

The PGA848’s nominal performance is specified with ±15 V input and output supplies. Output-stage supplies are clamped within input-supply levels, and supplies above ±20 V can permanently damage the device. Recommended layout practices include matched input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive and noisy traces, minimal leakage and parasitic capacitance, reduced thermal junctions, and distance from heat sources. The passage also describes TINA-TI and PSpice simulation resources, related TI documentation, support resources, ESD precautions, mechanical and ordering information, and TI’s resource disclaimers.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded Teck Resources (TECK) from “hold” to “buy,” setting a $25 price target, 8.84% above the stock’s then-current price. The diversified resource company focuses on copper, metallurgical coal, zinc, gold and energy, with interests in oil sands and mining activities across the Americas, Asia Pacific, Europe and Africa. Shares opened at $22.97, with a 52-week range of $14.56 to $26.60. The company reported a $13.27 billion market capitalization, 13.01% return on equity and 17.93% net margin. Analysts expected $3.52 EPS for the current year. Several institutional investors acquired second-quarter stakes, while institutional investors and hedge funds owned 46.80% of the stock.

Quarter Circle Games announced The Peterson Case for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC. Set in 1947 near the Roswell incident, it follows Detective Franklin Reinhardt investigating a missing family in a deserted house while pursued by an unearthly presence.

In 2002, federal agents destroyed six medical marijuana plants belonging to Diane Monson after she had grown them legally under California’s Compassionate Use Act. Monson and Angel Raich, who used cannabis to alleviate life-threatening illnesses, challenged the federal ban, arguing that Congress could not regulate their local, noncommercial activity through the interstate commerce clause.

The Supreme Court ruled 6–3 for the government. Justice John Paul Stevens’s majority opinion concluded that regulating intrastate medical cannabis was necessary to enforce Congress’s ban on the interstate marijuana market, accepting the government’s assumption that legal medical marijuana would otherwise reach the black market. Justice Antonin Scalia separately grounded the decision in the Necessary and Proper Clause while acknowledging limits on federal power.

Chief Justice William Rehnquist and Justices Sandra Day O’Connor and Clarence Thomas dissented. O’Connor warned that allowing Congress to package local activity into broad regulatory schemes would eliminate meaningful limits on the commerce clause. Thomas argued from an originalist interpretation that “commerce” covered buying, selling, bartering, and transportation—not production or personal use—and that Congress could not define the limits of its own power.

The decision was characterized as a major setback for limits on congressional commerce power and for federalism. Randy Barnett later brought a similar commerce-clause challenge to the Obamacare individual mandate; five justices rejected federal authority over inactivity, though the mandate was upheld as a tax. Raich’s later appeal claiming a constitutional right to life failed, although the court noted she might have a defense to prosecution. Medical marijuana is now widely legal at the state level, while federal efforts to reclassify it have stalled. Thomas has continued advocating a narrow, originalist understanding of the commerce clause.

At a press briefing, reporter Brian Karem asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders about her experience with sexual harassment and empathy for accusers. Sanders declined to discuss her experience, saying her role was to relay information for Trump, but said she had empathy for anyone sexually harassed.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 datasheet excerpt describes:

- **Analog peripherals:** The temperature sensor provides a linear voltage output connected to an ADC channel and includes a factory single-point calibration value measured in 12-bit mode with a 1.4-V internal reference at the trim temperature. The calibration value and temperature coefficient can be used to estimate device temperature. VREF provides selectable 1.4-V and 2.5-V internal references or an external reference and requires decoupling capacitors on the VREF pins. The comparator compares two input voltages and supports blanking, low-power wakeup, timer fault handling, and selectable pin or internal inputs. The buffered DAC supports 8- or 12-bit output, offset calibration, binary or two’s-complement formatting, sampling-rate generation, FIFO/DMA operation, and an event-fabric trigger. DAC_OUT shares the PA15 pin with COMP0/1_IN3+, so external circuitry on PA15 is not recommended when routing DAC_OUT.

- **Security and data integrity:** Device security features include AES-128/256 acceleration, flexible code and data firewalls, secure storage for as many as four AES keys, and CRC-16/CRC-32 with custom polynomials. The TRNG generates 32-bit random numbers approximately every 128 clock cycles for use with a deterministic random-number generator. The AESADV module performs hardware encryption and decryption of 128-bit blocks with 128- or 256-bit keys in several CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR/ICM, CCM, and GCM modes. The Keystore securely manages up to four 128- or 256-bit keys and is designed to resist partial-key modification attacks. The CRC-P module supports CRC16-CCITT and CRC32-ISO3309. MATHACL offloads selected 32-bit mathematical operations from the CPU.

- **Serial communications:** UART0, UART1, and UART3–UART7 support configurable start/stop/parity formats, baud generation with 16-, 8-, or 3-times oversampling, LIN mode, DMA-capable transmit/receive FIFOs, and loopback. I2C supports 7- and 10-bit addressing, controller and target operation, clock stretching, standard, fast, and fast-plus modes up to 1 Mbit/s, SMBus 3.0, DMA, low-power address-match wakeup, glitch filtering, and eight-entry FIFOs. SPI supports controller and peripheral modes, programmable prescalers, data frames from 4 to 16 bits, FIFO/DMA operation, TI/Motorola/Microwire formats, and rates up to 32 Mbit/s, with speeds above 16 Mbit/s restricted to HSIO signals. CAN-FD supports CAN 2.0A, 2.0B, and CAN-FD communication up to 5 Mbit/s under ISO 11898-1:2015, with configurable FIFOs, queues, and dedicated transmit and receive buffers.

- **Low-frequency and timing peripherals:** LFSS_B combines a 32-kHz low-frequency clock, the RTC_B real-time clock, and an independent watchdog timer. RTC_B provides calendar counters, customizable alarms, multiple periodic interrupt rates, crystal-offset and temperature-drift calibration up to ±240 ppm, clock output, and timestamp capture. IWDT_B monitors execution and generates a power-on reset if not serviced, with selectable periods from 2 ms to 2 hours. WWDT can generate a reset or interrupt, stops automatically in sleep mode, and can operate as an interval timer. TIMGx general-purpose timers support up/down/up-down counting, prescaling, QEI and Hall-sensor inputs on selected instances, synchronization, cross-triggering, and interrupt/DMA generation. TIMAx advanced timers add complementary PWM with programmable dead time, fast fault response, safe fault states, and additional capture/compare channels.

- **I/O, debug, and identification:** IOMUX selects digital functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wakeup logic; available pin features vary by device. A two-wire ARM-compatible serial wire debug interface provides access to device debugging functions. The boot strap loader supports memory programming and configuration through UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, and can be disabled. It can be invoked during boot, automatically on an unprogrammed device, or at runtime through a reset command. The memory-mapped FACTORY region contains read-only capability, identification, revision, and factory-trim information. DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008.

- **Implementation guidance:** Recommended supply decoupling is 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitors placed close to VDD and VSS. NRST requires a pullup to VDD; a 47-kΩ pullup with a 10-nF pulldown is recommended for typical applications. SYSOSC frequency correction requires a 100-kΩ, 0.1% resistor between ROSC and VSS with a temperature coefficient of 25 ppm/°C or better. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47-µF tank capacitor and no other circuitry. Pullups are required for 5-V-tolerant open-drain I/O used by I2C and UART.

- **Support and documentation:** TI provides LaunchPad hardware, the MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, and the GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental X-prefixed devices from fully qualified MSP production devices, while suffixes identify temperature range, package, and distribution format. The excerpt also covers documentation resources, E2E support forums, ESD precautions, April 2025 revision changes, mechanical and package drawings, orderable-part information, and TI’s disclaimers concerning the accuracy and suitability of its technical resources.

A severe flu season has killed 53 children, with high activity in 42 states and widespread transmission except Oregon and Hawaii. Predominant H3N2 is linked to more severe illness. Despite 17% effectiveness against H3N2 reported in Canada, officials recommend vaccination, early antivirals, and flu shots for everyone six months and older.

The University of Minnesota Morris occupies land formerly used as an Indian boarding school, where Native children were often separated from their families and taught English and assimilation. One original boys’ dormitory now houses the multi-ethnic resource center. Native American students have discussed campus experiences and the lingering trauma of boarding schools; some have relatives who attended. Morris joined the UMN system in 1960 after serving as an agriculture school. State law guarantees tuition-free attendance for Native students, a waiver believed to be one of only two at nontribal U.S. colleges. The campus has about 1,800 students, roughly 20% Native American, making it the UMN system’s most racially diverse campus.

The disclosure describes computer graphics and 3D reconstruction techniques for artificial-reality passthrough. External-facing HMD cameras capture the physical environment; because camera viewpoints differ from the user’s eyes and captured images lack depth, the system estimates depth, constructs a 3D representation, and re-renders the scene from each eye’s viewpoint to provide perspective and parallax. High-performance systems may use GPU-based optical flow to create dense point clouds, while resource-limited systems may use video-encoder motion vectors, camera-geometry filtering, and temporal voting to obtain sparse reliable depth measurements. These measurements can deform a coarse 3D mesh that approximates the environment’s contour.

Inaccurate depths and mesh interpolation can cause under-occlusion or over-occlusion between passthrough objects and virtual objects. Embodiments generate instance-segmentation masks, such as with Mask R-CNN, and associate each detected object instance with a representative depth derived from corresponding 3D-model depths, either by averaging them or using the instance’s centroid depth. A padded boundary around each mask is assigned a greater depth to create a pronounced edge. During per-pixel visibility testing, the renderer uses these representative depths to determine whether passthrough or virtual content should appear in front, while using model depth for pixels outside identified instances. The resulting rendering improves occlusion boundaries and reduces artifacts.

The described artificial-reality system may include an HMD, cameras, controllers, inertial measurement units, and integrated or separate computing hardware, with SLAM used to determine headset pose and eye viewpoints. The passage also describes network, social-VR, storage, and general computer-system environments capable of implementing the disclosed methods.

Bitcoin rose more than one-third to about $9,300, its first increase above that level since March. Version 6.00 of the Physical Layer Simplified Specification defines the SD Memory Card system, including card capacities (SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC up to 32 GB, and SDXC up to 2 TB), read/write and ROM configurations, supply voltages, speed classes, form factors, bus topologies, protocols, pins, registers, and operating features.

The specification covers SD, SPI, UHS-I, and UHS-II interfaces and their speed modes, including default, high-speed, SDR, DDR, and UHS-II operation. It details card identification and initialization through commands such as CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3; operating-voltage negotiation and switching; signal tuning; command and response formats; CRC protection; data reads, writes, erasing, locking, content protection, and card state transitions.

Additional sections define card and SD status data, speed and application-performance requirements, cache, self-maintenance, command queues, function extensions, power management, hardware electrical characteristics, and SPI-mode transactions and timing. The document also lists normative references, terminology, host-design guidance, tuning procedures, power-delivery design information, and simplified mechanical drawings for standard SD and microSD cards.
