Digital laggards set aspirational goals that are insufficiently grounded in data and poorly connected to strategy. Employees may avoid measurement because they expect to fall short, leading to qualitative, process-focused practices that discourage adaptation and inhibit innovation. Digital leaders instead establish structured goals and metrics through transparent, shared processes, often combining top-down and bottom-up input to build employee buy-in and organizational alignment. They also balance data-driven analysis with human judgment to avoid excessive analytical overhead.

A strong data culture coordinates work vertically by connecting individual and team objectives to company goals and horizontally by supporting collaboration through common data models and transparent access. It is reinforced by leadership beliefs, company values, and daily behaviors centered on learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Laggards may recognize the importance of this culture but struggle to change entrenched habits, skills gaps, and inconsistent leadership priorities.

Digital transformation is not limited to laggards, and mature leaders still face cultural tensions. Organizations may fit into four maturity patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—each requiring targeted action, including addressing overreliance on data where it discourages critical thinking.

This NVIDIA technical whitepaper introduces the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data center GPU built on the Ampere GA100 architecture, and describes its hardware, software, and supporting systems.

**Background:** Tensor Cores debuted in the 2017 Tesla V100; Turing-based T4 with TensorRT accelerated data center inference, while Volta and Turing GPUs won MLPerf training and inferencing categories and Jetson AGX Xavier led commercial SoC inference. Over a decade, CUDA, CUDA-X libraries, the CUDA Toolkit, NGC containers, and Kubernetes support have accelerated GPU applications.

**A100 hardware:** Fabricated on TSMC 7nm N7 with 54.2 billion transistors and an 826 mm² die, the full GA100 has 128 SMs while the A100 has 108 SMs, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and five HBM2 stacks. Third-generation Tensor Cores double dense throughput per SM versus V100 and add TF32, BF16, and IEEE FP64 to FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary. A new Sparsity feature doubles throughput again: TF32 runs 10x faster than V100 FP32 FMA (20x with sparsity), FP16/FP32 mixed precision 2.5x (5x sparse), sparse INT8 20x, and FP64 2.5x versus V100.

**Memory and system:** A100 offers 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, a 40 MB L2 cache nearly 7x larger than V100 with 2.3x the read bandwidth, L2 residency controls, Compute Data Compression, and SECDED ECC. Combined L1/shared memory is 192 KB per SM, and new asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, warp-level reductions, and Cooperative Groups reduce API cut latency and overhead.

**MIG:** Multi-Instance GPU partitions an A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated compute, L2, and memory paths, giving defined QoS, fault isolation, and up to 7x more instances at no extra cost. GPU slices, Sys Pipes (GigaThread Engine), Compute Instances with MPS support, and vGPU migration enable multi-tenant and single-tenant deployments in compute mode only.

**Connectivity:** Third-generation NVLink provides 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair, twelve links, and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (versus 300 GB/sec on V100), with NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, Magnum IO, Mellanox InfiniBand/Ethernet support, and enhanced error detection, isolation, and containment.

**Sparsity and HPC:** Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity uses a prune-then-fine-tune recipe that yields virtually no inference accuracy loss. cuSOLVER's TCAIRS mixed-precision iterative refinement solver showed TF32 as fastest and most robust, roughly 2x geomean over the FP64 solver and up to 4x on large matrices.

**Systems and software:** CUDA 11 and the CUDA Toolkit support the new data types, sparsity, task graphs, MIG, and L2 controls; NGC provides PyTorch, TensorFlow, MXNet, TensorRT, RAPIDS, and CUDA-X HPC containers. DGX A100 pairs eight A100s with six NVSwitches (4.8 TB/s bidirectional), delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in 6U, up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators, up to 6x the AI training performance of a V100-based DGX-1, and eight 200 Gb/s ConnectX-6 InfiniBand adapters, forming the basis for DGX SuperPOD systems.

An appendix explains pruning, fine- versus coarse-grained sparsity, and how structured sparsity balances workload while preserving accuracy.

PSA is the most widely used prostate cancer biomarker, but it is not cancer-specific, produces false positives in up to 47% of cases, and may miss clinically significant disease when combined with multiparametric MRI. Biopsies provide histological confirmation but are invasive and carry risks including sepsis and acute urinary retention. Circulating YAP1 nucleic acid and androgen receptor mRNA variants, including AR-FL and AR-V7, were investigated as prognostic biomarkers associated with disease progression, advanced stage, and reduced survival.

The study optimized plasma RNA extraction and developed point-of-care assays using reverse-transcription proton-mediated loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-pHLAMP) on an ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) Lab-on-Chip. TRIzol LS extraction was more sensitive and quantitatively reliable than the commercial Norgen method, allowing detection of synthetic YAP1 RNA down to 30 copies per reaction, AR-FL mRNA to 1,000 copies, and AR-V7 mRNA to 100 copies. The YAP1 assay could detect both RNA and circulating DNA, whereas the AR-FL and AR-V7 assays were specific to mRNA.

In plasma from 13 prostate cancer patients, including 11 hormone-sensitive and two metastatic cases, benchtop RT-pHLAMP detected YAP1 nucleic acid in the same samples as RT-qPCR, apart from one low-concentration sample. YAP1 was detected in 8 of 13 samples, and results were obtained within 12 minutes. AR-FL RT-pHLAMP results had 100% concordance with the corresponding large-fragment RT-qPCR assay. Single-well and dual-well ISFET detection produced results fully concordant with benchtop assays for YAP1 and AR-FL, although device time-to-positive was slightly longer. AR-FL mRNA was detected in one metastatic and one high-risk patient.

After unblinding, AR-V7 testing was performed in selected metastatic and intermediate-risk patients. AR-V7 mRNA was detected in the metastatic sample P12 by both benchtop RT-pHLAMP and the ISFET device, while the other tested samples were negative. Simultaneous AR-FL and AR-V7 detection was also demonstrated on the device.

YAP1 positivity was associated with higher clinical stage (p=0.043) and higher PSA at diagnosis (p=0.035). The authors describe the device as the first handheld ISFET biosensor for detecting circulating cancer nucleic acids and the first handheld system for circulating mRNA-based prostate cancer prognosis. However, TRIzol extraction is not suitable for direct point-of-care use, and larger cohorts, particularly of metastatic patients, are required. Proposed future developments include point-of-care-compatible extraction, a housekeeping-marker assay, and simultaneous detection of a broader marker panel including TMPRSS2-ERG.

The underlying December 2000 report covers international electricity-sector privatization and restructuring from June through November. Central and Eastern European governments are continuing privatizations and market openings while the IMF conditions funding on reform. Asian economies are recovering and restarting unbundling plans, though power-purchase agreements and missing government guarantees continue to hinder independent producers. Latin America has mixed progress, with some privatizations delayed by inflation, currency instability, and drought-related hydropower shortages, while regulatory reform and transmission concessions continue. African and Middle Eastern countries are increasingly opening to foreign investment, mostly through independent power projects and regional transmission links, but full privatization remains limited. Compass Minerals International, formed after Apollo Management affiliates acquired IMC Global’s salt and sulphate-of-potash businesses in 2001, completed its IPO on December 12, 2003, under CEO Michael Ducey. The case reviews salt’s history, production, economics, environmental effects, and Compass Minerals’ position as a newly public company.

Salt is produced through rock-salt mining, mechanical evaporation, or solar evaporation. Production methods differ substantially in cost and purity: brine is cheapest, rock salt is generally the cheapest and least pure dry salt, and vacuum-pan salt is the purest and most expensive. U.S. salt production averaged about 40 million metric tons annually from the 1970s onward, while recent prices averaged roughly $25 per metric ton. Highway deicing accounted for about one-third of annual U.S. consumption, with the remainder used in chemicals, food processing, water treatment, agriculture, and other applications.

The industry became increasingly concentrated and capital intensive as firms consolidated and expanded existing facilities rather than building new ones. Mine depth, deposit thickness, economies of scale, plant location, and transportation costs strongly affected production economics. Producers sold deicing salt through competitively tendered public contracts and other industrial salt through privately negotiated agreements.

Road salt creates significant environmental harm by contaminating soil, groundwater, streams, and rivers with sodium and chloride. Contamination can persist for decades, and trends in paved surfaces, population, and automobile use suggested worsening impacts. Road salt was not regulated as a freshwater pollutant in the United States at the time, although regulation was under consideration in Canada.

At IPO, North American Salt was the third-largest U.S. salt producer. General-trade products generated just over half its revenue, with Sifto and more than 70 private-label brands; highway deicing accounted for about 40% of salt sales in 2002. The company operated mines, evaporation plants, packaging facilities, and roughly 75 deicing depots across North America and the United Kingdom. It had 1,541 employees, about 37% represented by unions. For the twelve months ended September 30, 2003, sales were $564.2 million, operating earnings $97.5 million, and total debt $601.6 million.

The case closes with Ducey considering how to position Compass Minerals to investors while sustaining performance. Potential regulation of road salt posed a threat, but salt remained a large market with few substitutes, and new applications were emerging in areas such as document storage and nuclear-waste disposal.

The paper studies optimal pricing for a monopolist selling a single indivisible item that becomes worthless upon expiration. The market is modeled as a Stackelberg game: a time-sensitive seller commits at time zero to a public, continuous, non-increasing price schedule over a finite horizon, while buyers are patient but strategic. Buyers arrive according to a Poisson process, privately observe uniform valuations in \([0,1]\), and choose target purchase times after observing the schedule. The earliest buyer purchases at the scheduled price; if no one buys, the item expires unsold.

Buyers balance the possibility of lower future prices against the risk of stockout from competing arrivals. To make their equilibrium tractable, the paper introduces Value-Based Threshold strategies, which map each buyer’s valuation to a target purchase time and thereby separate valuation from arrival time. It derives necessary conditions, including an ordinary differential equation, and sufficient verification conditions to establish existence and uniqueness of buyer equilibria for continuous valuations.

Using this framework, the paper derives pricing schedules for two stylized regimes. In thin markets, where competition is negligible, a constant price neutralizes delaying incentives and induces immediate purchase decisions. In thick markets, where preemption risk is high, buyers behave myopically and a linear discounting schedule is optimal; the paper also proves that this policy induces a unique equilibrium under fully strategic behavior. Simulations confirm the near-optimality of these policies and show that optimal schedules shift from end-loaded for patient sellers, to constant for moderately sensitive sellers, and to front-loaded discounting for impatient sellers. The model is distinct from standard dynamic-pricing models in assigning time-dependent disutility only to the seller.

The toss play is a widespread outside run in which the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back heading toward the defense’s edge. It is simple to teach and install, quickly delivers the ball to the perimeter, and consistently gains yardage when paired with a fast running back and an offensive line capable of blocking in space. Its primary weakness is that it requires that specific personnel and is vulnerable to immediate edge pressure, including overload edge and corner blitzes. The passage outlines blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, emphasizing reach and combination blocks, the fullback’s lead-blocking responsibilities, and defensive assignments for the quarterback and receivers. Two variations are also described: Flexbone or “Rocket Toss,” which uses pre-snap motion and a quarterback fake to delay the defense, and Single Back Toss G Pull, which uses the pulling guard as the lead blocker instead of a fullback.

The Missouri Court of Appeals vacated and remanded the property division in David v. David. Diane David challenged the dissolution judgment, which awarded Joseph the marital farm, equipment, truck, cattle, household goods in his possession, and responsibility for marital debts and $3,500 of her attorney fees. Diane received Joseph’s pension and 401(k), personal property in her possession, a car, and household goods.

The court found no abuse of discretion in awarding the farm to Joseph, noting that the law does not require the custodial parent to receive the marital residence and that Joseph was better equipped to farm the property. It also determined that the parties had not reached a binding agreement concerning an equal division. Diane’s teacher retirement account was separate property and should not materially affect the division, but testimony that she could receive Social Security distinguished the case from precedent relied upon by the trial court.

Nevertheless, the court found a mathematical error: Diane’s distribution was $59,182, not $62,781. Because this error affected the decision not to require an equalizing payment, the court remanded for reconsideration. The court also rejected Diane’s tax-contention argument because she had not raised it at trial. On remand, the trial court may adjust any interrelated property issues or adopt a new division proposed by the parties.

Tesla, Inc.’s fiscal 2016 Form 10-K describes two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Tesla designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles, including the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, and planned volume production and deliveries of the lower-priced Model 3 in the second half of 2017. It also develops residential and utility-scale energy storage products, including Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2, and sells or leases solar-energy systems following its November 2016 SolarCity acquisition.

The company operates a global network of stores, galleries and service centers, sold 265 retail and service locations and operated 790 Supercharger stations at year-end. Its proprietary technology includes battery packs, power electronics, dual-motor powertrains, vehicle-control and infotainment software, and autopilot hardware. Manufacturing occurs primarily in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada, with solar products manufactured in Buffalo, New York.

The report identifies significant risks, including delays in designing, manufacturing and ramping vehicles and other products; execution and cost challenges associated with Model 3 and Gigafactory 1; dependence on suppliers, particularly for battery cells; uncertain consumer adoption of electric vehicles; product defects and battery safety incidents; increasing material and production costs; product-liability claims; regulatory restrictions on direct vehicle sales; and intense competition from established and emerging automotive, energy-storage and solar companies.

The passage is an excerpt from the TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processor data manual covering device architecture, memory, peripherals, revision history, and pin assignments. The C674x is a high-performance floating-point DSP compatible with the C64x and C67x generations. It includes 32KB each of L1 program and data memory, configurable as cache, 256KB of ECC-enabled L2 RAM that can serve as SRAM, cache, or both, and uses the system MMU for L3 and external-memory accesses.

The ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem provides master control and configuration of device subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It supports ARMv7, Thumb2, JazelleX, NEON SIMD, VFPv3, separate L1 caches, ETM trace through a 32KB ETB, and an AINTC that prioritizes peripheral requests and generates IRQ or FIQ signals. It accesses DDR through a 128-bit DMM port and other modules through a 64-bit L3 port.

The C674x CPU has eight functional units, two 32-register files, and support for packed 8-, 16-, 32-, 40-, and 64-bit data. Its enhancements include parallel and complex multiplication, Galois-field multiplication, dual 16-bit arithmetic and comparisons, packing and unpacking instructions, compact instructions, SPLOOP software pipelining, exception handling, privilege modes, and a free-running time-stamp counter. DSP MDMA accesses are remapped by the MMU to protect ARM memory and support user-space buffers; EDMA transfer controllers 0 and 1 may also use the MMU.

Additional subsystems include a Media Controller for HDVPSS and ISS, the HDVICP2 accelerator for major MPEG, H.264, VC-1, RV9/10, AVS, and ON2 video codecs, a QVGA face-detection module, 128 hardware spinlocks, and a four-message mailbox system for ARM–DSP and Media Controller communication. The device uses a unified memory map, and its TILER interface provides an additional 4GB range for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views, primarily accessible to HDVPSS and ISS.

Device-pin tables identify package balls, multiplexed functions, pin types, supplies, internal pulls, deselected-input states, and pin-control registers. They cover boot configuration, camera and DCAN interfaces, dual DDR2/DDR3 controllers, Ethernet MII/RMII/RGMII modes, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, reset/interrupt/JTAG, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, and digital video input/output. The revision history records updates to operating points, DDR support and timing, power sequencing, oscillator and audio-clock requirements, EDMA registers, McASP timing, McBSP addresses, GPIO pin multiplexing, latch-up ratings, and other device characteristics.

After Vladimir Putin won Russia’s so-called election for a fourth presidential term, a key priority is developing a post-Soviet national ideology. Russia’s identity crisis, Putin’s dominance, economic stagnation, entrenched corruption, and falling oil prices have weakened earlier promises of prosperity and stability. His government will seek to codify an alternative worldview as a patriotic mission, source of regime legitimacy, and legacy distinct from Western liberal democracy. Such ideology would support Russia’s great-power ambitions without accepting Western norms of governance and diplomacy. The West should expose the vision’s hollowness rather than accept it as justification for the regime, while overcoming political division in the United States and Europe to maintain a positive vision capable of winning the competition of ideas.

A new Sheffield partnership, Create Sheffield—Adventures in Cultural Education, brings together education, arts, culture and voluntary-sector organisations to expand children and young people’s access to arts and culture. The partnership aims to improve school attainment, quality of life and employability by developing creative skills and exposing young people up to age 25 to cultural activities.

Oregon public schools have among the nation’s lowest four-year graduation rates, with one in four students not graduating, while students average about 165 instructional days annually compared with 180 nationally. Education Board member Kim Sordyl and some parents argue that limited instruction time contributes to low graduation rates, noting Washington students receive 15 additional days each year, equivalent to an extra school year over 12 years. Other contributing factors include large classes, early start times, absenteeism, poverty, and budget deficits. Lawmaker Diego Hernandez said the legislature has not studied the correlation and that adding school days without adequate support and quality would not solve the problem. At Tualatin High School, which has one of the state’s highest graduation rates, administrators emphasize attendance and say every missed class creates significant curriculum gaps. Oregon sets instructional time by hours rather than days; the 165-day estimate assumes six-hour school days.

The article examines copper as a possible leading indicator for stocks because its broad industrial use and demand from electric vehicles and green energy can reflect economic activity. Rising copper prices may signal economic growth, while falling prices may foreshadow slowdown. A strategy was backtested using SPY data since 2000: buy SPY for the following week when copper’s prior four-week return was positive; otherwise, hold cash. Results showed decent returns, smaller drawdowns than buy-and-hold, and positive risk-adjusted performance, but the strategy largely stagnated from 2008 to 2016. Copper and subsequent SPY returns were weakly correlated, particularly during 2011–2016. The article concludes there is no concrete evidence that copper reliably predicts stocks and that the strategy’s performance may reflect luck; copper may be more useful for identifying business cycles.

NVIDIA Corporation reported unaudited results for its second quarter and first half of fiscal 2017, ended July 31, 2016. Quarterly revenue rose 24% year over year to $1.428 billion, driven by gaming, datacenter and professional visualization GPUs and Tegra automotive systems. Gross margin increased to 57.9% from 55.0%, operating income rose to $317 million from $76 million, net income increased to $253 million from $26 million, and diluted earnings per share reached $0.40 versus $0.05. For the first half, revenue was $2.733 billion, operating income was $561 million, net income was $449 million, and diluted earnings per share were $0.73.

GPU revenue increased 25% year over year to $1.196 billion, led by GeForce gaming products, 110% growth in datacenter revenue and 22% growth in professional visualization revenue. Tegra Processor revenue rose 30% to $166 million, driven by 68% growth in automotive revenue. Quarterly revenue by market was $781 million for gaming, $214 million for professional visualization, $151 million for datacenter, $119 million for automotive, and $163 million for OEM and intellectual property. Operating expenses declined 9% to $509 million, primarily because the prior-year quarter included $89 million of Icera restructuring charges.

At July 31, NVIDIA reported $7.461 billion of assets, $2.909 billion of liabilities and $4.480 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $426 million and marketable securities were $4.453 billion. First-half operating cash flow was $493 million, investing activities used $93 million and financing activities used $570 million, including $509 million for share repurchases and $124 million for dividends. The company returned $633 million to shareholders during the first half and intended to return approximately $1 billion during fiscal 2017.

NVIDIA continued launching Pascal-based GeForce products, including the GTX 1080, 1070 and 1060, introduced Tesla M10 and P100 products, and expanded datacenter, visualization and automotive offerings. The company also continued winding down Icera operations, recording $2 million of restructuring charges in the quarter and $3 million in the first half.

The company carried $1.5 billion principal of 1% convertible senior notes due December 2018, with a $1.428 billion balance-sheet carrying value classified as current because the notes remained convertible. NVIDIA settled intellectual-property disputes with Samsung and Qualcomm and licensed patents from Advanced Silicon Technologies, recording a $10 million cost-of-revenue charge. First-half stock-based compensation was $111 million, and $392 million of stock-based compensation remained unearned at quarter-end.

Serious medical problems were uncommon in the Phase 1, Phase 2/3, and Phase 3 studies of BNT162b2/BNT162b2SA. Phase 1 had two serious problems after Dose 2—one each in the 20- and 30-µg BNT162b2 groups—and neither was considered vaccine-related; other groups reported none. After two 30-µg Phase 2/3 doses, no single serious problem occurred in at least 1% of any group. Among participants aged 16 or older, three vaccine recipients and three initial placebo recipients later given vaccine each had one temporary serious problem, considered possibly vaccine-related. A separate BNT162b2SA group had four serious problems among 324 participants (1%), none considered related. After 30-µg Phase 3 boosters, no event occurred in more than one participant and none was considered related; one event after a 5- or 10-µg booster was also not considered related. After a 30-µg Phase 2/3 booster, 65 of 22,470 participants had serious problems; two participants aged 16 or older had possibly vaccine-related events. One additional-booster serious problem was not considered vaccine-related.

The message reported that armed trespassers, chiefly from neighboring British Provinces and without provincial authorization, entered disputed Maine territory watered by the Aroostook River and extensively cut and destroyed timber. After obtaining legislative authorization, Maine dispatched its land agent with a force to stop the depredations. The agent and two Maine citizens were captured and taken to Fredericton, prompting Maine to deploy an armed posse. New Brunswick demanded their withdrawal and said British troops were prepared to support its jurisdiction; Maine refused and notified the federal government.

The United States maintained that no agreement gave Great Britain exclusive possession or jurisdiction over the disputed territory pending a final boundary settlement. It noted reciprocal restraint: Maine and Massachusetts had stopped selling land, the federal government had deferred construction of a military road, and Britain had suspended timber licenses and a railroad survey.

The message distinguished Maine’s effort to protect timber and arrest trespassers from a military effort to occupy and hold the territory by force. The federal government preferred arbitration, a commission with an umpire, or referral to a third power and declined to support a forcible state occupation. If New Brunswick attempted such an occupation, however, the President would consider Maine entitled to federal assistance in repelling an invasion.

Expectations were expressed that detained agents on both sides would be released and Maine’s assembled militia peacefully disbanded. The President urged Congress to consider measures that could prevent the need for an extraordinary session while emphasizing the danger of armed conflict and the need for an amicable settlement.

From 1950 to 2022, the S&P 500 recorded 1,526 all-time highs—nearly 21 annually and on 8.3% of trading days—meaning it traded below its previous high 91.7% of the time. All-time highs often coincide with strong business activity, earnings, momentum, bullish sentiment, and investor FOMO, although inflation can distort nominal highs. Historically, the market tended to perform well during the year after reaching a new high.

The strategy buys the S&P 500 when it is less than 5% below its all-time high and sells when it falls more than 5% below. In a daily, non-dividend-adjusted backtest, it returned a 3.20% CAGR, spent 43.2% of its time invested, achieved a 7.40% risk-adjusted return, and had a 33.75% maximum drawdown. Its cash management is crucial: earning 3% annually on cash held while the index is more than 5% below its high substantially improved performance. Overall, the strategy illustrates trend following and momentum with lower drawdowns than buy-and-hold.

The disclosure describes a respiratory mask system for delivering respiratory therapy, including continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and non-invasive ventilation (NIV). The mask interface includes a seal that forms an airtight seal around a patient’s nose and/or mouth and a frame that supports the seal, connects to a gas conduit, and attaches to headgear that holds the interface against the patient’s face.

The frame may include an angled, elliptical gas inlet and an outlet vent, optionally containing a diffuser. A projecting seal flange and a seal lip secure the seal to the frame. Alternative seal assemblies use inner and outer clips forming a collar, with a divider separating the gas inlet from the vent. Projections, recesses, snap-fit features, tapered fits, and seal channels locate and retain these components.

The frame front may include a longitudinal recessed channel for receiving a headgear yoke. Vents positioned within or near this channel can exhaust gas through gaps between the frame and yoke. The yoke has a narrower middle portion and wider side portions, may be tapered or curved, and can carry a stretchable textile covering. Locating members and surfaces help center and orient it within the frame.

Various yoke-to-frame connections are described, including friction or clamping retention, textile coverings, tabs, latches, snap-fits, magnets, hooks and posts, complementary recesses and projections, retention bumps and notches, and anti-rotation grooves and tongues. The yoke may also serve as a hollow collector for headgear filaments, with upper and lower line tracks, end caps, filament-entry holes, and washer housings for self-adjusting headgear and directional locks. Rear, upper, and front headgear straps connect to the yoke through snap-fit, threaded, or hooked connections.

Additional embodiments describe a nasal seal with a body and nasal prongs, a shallow bridge between the prongs, specified depth, width, height, sealing-area and wall-thickness limits, and a generally D-shaped inlet. A removable clip assembly connects the nasal seal to a frame and may define the inlet and a diffuser-equipped vent. The accompanying figures show assembled and exploded mask, frame, seal, clip, and yoke configurations, including cross-sections and comparisons with prior-art nasal seals.

The Federal Government planned to release N750 billion to government agencies for 2017 capital projects, bringing total capital releases to N1.2 trillion, including N450 billion already disbursed. Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun met 30 French firms and investors interested in banking, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture, services and youth empowerment.

The article presents three mean-reversion strategies: deviation from a recent high in XLP, an IBS short strategy in FXI, and a 5-day-low strategy for the S&P 500. Their historical equity curves and results are shown, though the passage does not provide complete trading rules or exact returns.

Mean reversion is defined as prices gravitating toward and around a moving average over time, with abnormal rises or falls tending to reverse. It generally produces a high win rate, many small gains, and occasional large losses, while trend following tends to produce many small losses and fewer large gains.

The article reports that mean reversion works best in stocks and can be particularly effective during bear markets, where increased volatility and explosive rallies create opportunities; historically, the long side has performed better than the short side. During the S&P 500’s roughly 50% decline from May 2008 to early March 2009, there were 99 up days and 104 down days, with explosive gains still occurring despite the overall decline.

Proposed reasons for mean reversion include arbitrage between stocks and futures, selling pressure after price rises, increased buying after declines, and short covering during bear-market rallies. The strategy is also described as suited to short-term trading because volatility supplies opportunities.

The disclosure describes high-bandwidth communications and power-distribution infrastructure for buildings with optically switchable “smart” windows, including electrochromic and other switchable optical devices. Control panels linked by coaxial, twisted-pair, twinax, MoCA, wireless, or other high-speed connections can form backbones and daisy-chained trunk lines carrying data and power to window controllers and other devices. Enhanced window controllers may add Ethernet, Wi-Fi, cellular, video, and related functions.

Digital architectural elements, digital wall interfaces, and associated controllers can integrate processors, network interfaces, sensors, displays, speakers, microphones, antennas, lighting, and energy storage or harvesting. Applications include environmental and occupancy sensing, acoustic mapping and noise cancellation, communications, security, media delivery, HVAC and lighting control, and window tint and glare management. Distributed sensor data can be analyzed automatically, including with machine learning, to identify or predict building conditions and locally or globally adjust HVAC, lighting, security, and window operation. Systems may also detect and locate sounds or threats, trigger alerts or emergency responses, and alter window tint to identify sound locations or support safety and egress.

Witting said Finland’s 1940 effort to secure a Finnish-Swedish common-defense agreement failed because of Swedish timidity and Soviet objections. He considered the objection shortsighted, since the agreement might have allowed both countries to remain neutral. Russian troop concentrations and preparations raised Finnish fears of another Soviet attack, making the Finnish-German transit agreement a major relief.

Although Finland did not wish to join a wider war, its fighting had long been driven by Soviet offensive tactics, including costly operations around Poventsa. Finland’s dependence on German supplies severely limited its freedom of action, although Witting argued that geography similarly constrained Sweden and the United States. The Finns hoped to avoid actions interfering with German supply shipments to Russia but were prepared for enforced cooperation with Germany.

Witting concluded that military necessity made peace with the Soviet Union unlikely and that Finland would not voluntarily worsen its position with anti-Axis forces. Swedish contacts doubted Sweden could influence Finland. Finland emphasized its dependence on Germany while promoting its territorial annexations through Professor Jaakkola’s *Finland’s Eastern Problem*.

Patanjali launched Kimbho, a real-time messaging app positioned as a Swadeshi challenge to WhatsApp. Initially advertised on Google Play, it was later unavailable there but remained on the iOS App Store and accessible to existing users. Features included direct and group messaging, broadcast lists, media sharing, doodling, and free phone and video calls. CMR’s Faisal Kawoosa reported around 5,000 installations and reviews highlighting concerns, while questioning whether being Swadeshi alone could help it compete with WhatsApp. The launch followed Patanjali’s Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards, which offered discounts on Patanjali products.

A study published in Nature Astronomy by researchers from Caltech, the University of Oxford, and the University of Leicester confirmed that Uranus's atmosphere contains foul-smelling hydrogen sulfide. The gas was detected in the planet's cloud tops by dissecting light captured by the Gemini North telescope, providing the strongest proof yet of its presence. Professor Patrick Irwin noted that anyone descending through Uranus's clouds would face suffocation and temperatures near negative 200 degrees Celsius in an atmosphere of mostly hydrogen, helium, and methane long before encountering the odor, which resembles rotten eggs. Scientists say the discovery may shed light on how and when Uranus formed.

This prospective longitudinal study used the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development cohort to examine whether multidimensional unintended pregnancy—mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness—was associated with children’s psychosocial problems from preschool through adolescence. The analytic sample included 7,784 mothers and children, with data collected around 16 weeks’ gestation and at ages 5–6, 11–12, and 15–16 years. Structural equation modeling assessed internalizing and externalizing problems while controlling for maternal, child, and family risk factors.

At preschool age, pregnancy mistiming was significantly associated with both internalizing and externalizing problems, while unwanted pregnancy was associated only with internalizing problems; pregnancy unhappiness was not significantly associated with either outcome. These effects were small. After adjustment for co-occurring risks, no unintended-pregnancy dimension was significantly associated with psychosocial problems during early or middle adolescence, and sensitivity analyses using adolescent-reported outcomes showed the same pattern.

Preschool-age analyses indicated that maternal bonding problems mediated associations between all three unintended-pregnancy dimensions and both types of psychosocial problems. Maternal psychosocial distress specifically mediated the links between pregnancy mistiming and internalizing and externalizing problems. Direct associations between mistiming or unwantedness and internalizing problems remained after accounting for mediators and controls.

The authors concluded that supporting maternal mental health and bonding may be more important for reducing young children’s psychosocial problems than addressing unintended pregnancy itself. Limitations included possible selection bias from dropout, reliance on maternal reporting, and omission of paternal or co-parent mental health. The findings may apply particularly to settings with abortion policies and cultures similar to the Netherlands.

The Bengals acquired 40-year-old quarterback Joe Flacco from the Browns in exchange for a sixth-round draft pick, with Cleveland receiving a fifth-round pick. Cincinnati, 2-3 and on a three-game losing streak, has been outscored 113-37 while starting quarterback Jake Browning threw eight interceptions in parts of four games. Flacco completed 58.1% of his passes for the Browns, with 815 yards, two touchdowns and six interceptions. Coach Zac Taylor did not commit to Flacco immediately starting but said the team would evaluate its quarterback options ahead of a game at Green Bay. Joe Burrow remains on injured reserve after toe surgery and is expected to miss at least three months. Flacco’s departure could give Browns rookie Shedeur Sanders a chance to move from third string to backup behind Dillon Gabriel; the team listed Sanders as its No. 2 quarterback on an unofficial depth chart.

The group praised Manny’s return, leadership, friendship, and behind-the-scenes contributions. They emphasized moving past the win to focus on Boston. The speaker said it was his first NHL game in Boston and their first shutout against the Bruins.

The speaker outlines the “Great Society” as America’s continuing challenge: using material wealth and technological progress to advance liberty, end poverty and racial injustice, enrich education and culture, protect nature, and improve the human spirit. He identifies three priorities: rebuilding rapidly growing cities to provide adequate housing and transportation while preserving community and natural surroundings; protecting the country’s natural beauty from pollution and development; and expanding educational opportunity by improving teacher training, pay, facilities, curricula, and access for poor and inadequately educated students. He proposes working groups, White House conferences, and renewed cooperation between federal and local governments to address these issues. Urging the university’s graduates to participate, he calls for a society based on equality, an escape from poverty, enduring peace, and a richer intellectual and spiritual life built upon America’s material progress.

The coach said his team played two strong periods and opened the third decisively before becoming overly conservative while protecting its lead. Buffalo’s goaltender, Hasek, held the Sabres together, but skilled players from throughout their lineup eventually created the comeback that continued into overtime. He praised Buffalo for never being overwhelmed and continuing to compete, while emphasizing that Hasek was important but not the team’s sole contributor.

The coach identified second- and third-chance opportunities, loose-puck control, and the boards, slot, blue lines, and areas around the net as decisive. His team controlled these areas for nearly two and a half periods but backed off in the latter part of the third, allowing Buffalo to exploit them. He also noted that Buffalo won more loose-puck battles and was quicker to turn draws into opportunities.

Although the power play generated numerous chances, it failed to convert. The coach credited the unit’s puck movement and seam passing, expressed satisfaction with its recent improvement, and said finishing opportunities would determine its effectiveness. He viewed the game as hard-fought and expected a competitive series between two strong teams.

Possible lineup changes were discussed, with Hrkac and Plante ready to play, along with leaning more on offensive players and potentially younger players for quickness. The coach praised the team’s unity, emotional resilience, and ability to respond to adversity. He also dismissed accusations that Brian Skrudland was cheating as a personal jab from Buffalo coach Lindy Ruff, and said players and coaches should enjoy the opportunity despite the pressure of expectations.

The patent discloses an active organic light-emitting display device with a through hole in its substrate, surrounded by pixels. The substrate includes a display area and non-display areas, including an inner area around the through hole and an outer area surrounding the display area. Data lines curve around the through-hole perimeter to connect pixels on opposite sides, while scan lines may terminate near the hole. Curved data lines can be arranged at alternating layers, including layers separated by an organic passivation layer, to reduce line pitch and the area required around the hole without overlap.

Various embodiments alter the data-line and passivation-layer structures, including curved portions connected to straight portions through contact holes and layers shared with pixel electrodes, source/drain electrodes, or storage-capacitor electrodes. Thin-film encapsulation uses inorganic and organic layers, with a dam positioned near the through hole to restrict organic-layer flow. Inorganic layers contact near the hole to improve moisture resistance, and inorganic or organic-inorganic composite passivation layers can cover the curved data lines.

The embodiments are described as reducing the non-display area around the through hole while maintaining or improving sealing and moisture-barrier performance. Applications include mobile-phone cameras or buttons, smartwatch hands, and vehicle dashboard instruments positioned within one or more through holes.

The “Box and One” uses four defenders in a box zone and one chaser assigned solely to deny a specific opponent the ball and rebounds. X4 and X5 shift like a 1-2-2 zone, while X1 and X2 shift like a 2-3 zone. Against even- and odd-front offenses, defenders push the ball handler away from the star, force passes toward the sidelines or baseline, protect the low post and elbow, and close out on skip passes. The chaser maintains aggressive pass denial and receives support against penetration. Strong denial is the defense’s key element, disrupting the opponent’s set plays and continuities.

The article demonstrates how to backtest a simple trading strategy in Python using pandas, yfinance, and matplotlib. Historical SPY data is downloaded from Yahoo Finance, then simple and exponential moving averages are calculated, with the first 200 rows removed. A “regime” signal equals 1 when the closing price is above both moving averages and is applied to the following row. Daily SPY returns are calculated with `pct_change()` and compounded only during active positions, then plotted with matplotlib. The strategy’s accumulated returns were 804.82%, compared with 1505.31% for buy and hold, so it underperformed. The article concludes that Python makes strategy backtesting accessible without requiring finance or computer science degrees.

Customers must provide an RSA public key during early-boot SMM setup, before `BOOT_DONE`, for SFS package verification; the key cannot be changed afterward. The x86 supplies an `MBOX_BUFFER_HEADER` containing the key size and OEM co-signing key. Customers generate 2048- or 4096-bit RSA keys and sign AMD update packages with RSA-PSS using SHA-256 or SHA-384, respectively.

SFS patches check applicable patch and firmware versions and may modify registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. Packages must verify prerequisite firmware versions and dependencies before applying any changes and should not apply partially. SEV updates are committed and cannot be rolled back without rebooting. SNP updates require update pages to be HV-FIXED using `RMPUPDATE`. Attestation data is obtained through interfaces such as SPDM or DPE, and components protected by applicable attestation schemes are not modified.

Updates are nonpersistent across reboots and may be applied during OS boot, immediately afterward, or during operation. SFS commands require a 2 MB-aligned `TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER`, with output or package data starting 4 KB after it. A customer deployment agent creates the buffer, appends any co-signing header, the complete AMD package, and the co-signature, then submits the buffer’s physical address through TEE mailboxes to ASP firmware.

ASP protects the buffer from x86 access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, validates the package, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. A separate two-page command reports firmware versions, patch levels, supported firmware, and security patch levels; for SNP systems, its output page must also be HV-FIXED.

Packages are named using the format `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg` and must match the system’s specific firmware and patch-level combination. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV virtual machines may need to stop and restart during SEV firmware updates.

During an XXL Cloudbreak swell in Fiji, Dane Gudauskas paddled out alone in stormy, windy conditions and caught a massive left wave after narrowly avoiding a barreling set. The wave overwhelmed him, spun him around, and caused him to wipe out and break his board. He rode his brother Patrick’s 8-foot-6-inch Channel Islands with quad fins, then switched to Tanner’s 8-foot-10-inch backup, though he said a longer board might have performed better. Gudauskas compared the swell’s power and speed with his 2016 Cloudbreak wave, describing it as far more energetic, wild, and raw. The day involved roughly 30 boats, difficult positioning, tow-in surfers, and coordinated safety efforts. He called it his most intense surfing experience and remained physically sore and adrenaline-driven afterward.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022 presented unaudited financial statements and related notes. Q3 net sales rose 15% to $127.1 billion, while operating income fell to $2.5 billion and net income was $2.9 billion. For the first nine months, net sales were $364.8 billion, operating income was $9.5 billion, and net loss was $3.0 billion, versus net income of $19.0 billion a year earlier. The nine-month period included a $10.4 billion Rivian investment valuation loss. North America and International reported Q3 operating losses of $412 million and $2.47 billion, respectively, while AWS generated $5.40 billion of operating income on $20.54 billion of sales. Nine-month operating cash flow was $17.6 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $58.7 billion at quarter-end. Amazon completed the $6.1 billion MGM acquisition, agreed to acquire One Medical for $3.9 billion and iRobot for $1.7 billion, and repurchased $6.0 billion of stock. The filing also covers leases, commitments, taxes, litigation, segment results, and a 20-for-1 stock split.

Augustine Heard reported that Seoul remained quiet after April 20 and that the U.S.S. Alert was told no immediate danger required its presence; it left Chemulpo on April 29. Although reports mentioned disturbances, a Korean investigator found no Tong Hâk assemblages in the districts named in incendiary placards. Heard nevertheless warned that official exactions and widespread discontent could revive unrest.

Later reports said thousands of Tong Hâk were gathering at Po-eun, drilling, displaying anti-foreign and anti-Japanese flags, and intending to march on Seoul. The government sent 800 drilled troops with Gatling guns toward Suwen and possibly Chong-ju. Heard doubted that the Tong Hâk posed direct danger, describing them as peaceful and primarily seeking rehabilitation of their founder and permission to practice their tenets, but noted that they had attracted many poor and discontented followers and might be controlled by an unidentified political party seeking trouble.

The Crude Oil Seasonality Strategy buys oil assets at Thursday’s close to target Friday price increases. Historical analysis from April 2006 to the present reported a 56.96% profit and loss across 98 trades, with 60 winners and an average profit of 0.58% per trade. Performance was stronger when Thursday was a down day, so buying on every Thursday is not recommended. One filter requires USO to fall by at least 0.75 times its 25-day average high-low range.

This 2008 case examines Biocon India Group’s expansion strategy and the risks posed by its clinical-research subsidiary, Clinigene. Founded by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw in 1978, Biocon moved from enzyme manufacturing into generic drugs and then established Syngene in 1994 to provide contract research and development services. By early 2003, it employed 800 people and generated annual revenue of US$75 million.

India’s pharmaceutical industry expanded rapidly after 1970 regulations permitted generic reproduction and government control of drug prices. Its growing outsourcing market was supported by an educated, English-speaking, relatively inexpensive scientific workforce, diverse patient populations, and government biotechnology initiatives. Outsourcing opportunities included research and development, clinical trials, and manufacturing, with clinical trials offering particularly high value.

Biocon’s subsidiaries pursued an integrated drug-development model. Syngene developed capabilities in synthetic chemistry, molecular biology, informatics, and early-stage drug discovery. Clinigene, launched in 2000, developed clinical-laboratory services, bioequivalence and bioavailability studies, and hospital partnerships to fill Biocon’s missing clinical-trials capability.

Biocon’s culture—based on openness, trust, collaboration, accessibility, limited hierarchy, and team-based rewards—had helped drive its growth. Clinigene’s expansion could, however, divert resources, alter that culture, overshadow Biocon and Syngene, and weaken employee loyalty to the parent group. Clinigene also faced market-positioning constraints: Indian CROs primarily handled lower-value bioequivalence and bioavailability studies, while foreign firms concentrated on data management and Phase III trials.

Clinical trials introduced financial, ethical, and reputational risks, including informed-consent concerns, patient compensation, potential political scrutiny, and accusations of Western exploitation. The case presents three broad choices: expand Clinigene aggressively, restrict it temporarily to safer services while awaiting Syngene’s drug pipeline, or acquire an established clinical-services CRO. The decision required balancing market growth and Biocon’s integrated-development ambition against cultural, operational, ethical, and financial risks.
