Police reported one drug/narcotic violation, one liquor-law violation, three children receiving trespassing warrants, an investigation into a smashed mailbox, and destruction of 75 pounds of unused prescription drugs. Kennedy was cited for speeding, marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia; Preston was charged with minor possession of alcohol and third-degree forgery. Total calls: 204.

The ADS868xW family consists of single-channel, 16-bit SAR ADCs with integrated analog front ends, precision references, ADC drivers, and overvoltage protection. They operate from a 5 V analog supply and support differential or single-ended, unipolar or bipolar inputs up to ±12.288 V. Their input impedance is at least 1 MΩ and remains independent of sampling frequency. A programmable PGA selects nine input ranges, a second-order antialiasing filter has a typical 500 kHz cutoff, and an integrated driver enables rapid settling. Input paths should be impedance-matched for DC accuracy. Floating inputs produce invalid ADC readings but do not damage the device.

With a 4.096 V reference, bipolar ranges are ±12.288, ±10.24, ±6.144, ±5.12, and ±2.56 V; unipolar ranges are 0–12.288, 0–10.24, 0–6.144, and 0–5.12 V. Internal protection withstands inputs up to ±20 V when powered and approximately ±15 V when the analog supply is floating, although external surge, ESD, and EFT protection is recommended. The device can use its nominal 4.096 V internal reference or an external reference through an internal buffer. Reference decoupling and filtering are specified, and reflow-induced internal-reference shifts are discussed.

An active-high alarm output supports programmable input high/low alarms with hysteresis and fixed AVDD alarms at 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped alarm flags are available through the ALARM register, the alarm pin, or the output data stream.

The multiSPI interface supports four SPI-compatible modes, single- or dual-SDO output, source-synchronous operation, and daisy chaining. Programming uses 32-bit commands and nine configuration registers covering device identification, reset and power control, input and output protocols, data formatting, input ranges, and alarms. Operational states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV; programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce power use.

An example industrial module combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 for PLC-style voltage/current inputs. Recommended implementation includes separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, specified bypass capacitors, reference capacitors, low-impedance grounding, and separation of analog and digital PCB routing.

The address reports rapid national growth, westward expansion, and a growing native population. Differences in climate and industry are said to complement rather than divide the states, while the division of authority between national and state governments promotes unity. Agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, navigation, government revenue, fortifications, and naval expansion are all advancing.

Foreign relations are generally friendly, and the government seeks fair, reciprocal trade. The 1822 navigation convention with France remains in force, although claims for wartime spoliations remain unsettled. Commercial intercourse with Britain rests on reciprocal arrangements, but West Indian trade has not yet been settled to U.S. satisfaction. One boundary under the Treaty of Ghent has been established, another is being negotiated, and a third is expected to be settled soon. Britain and the United States have not finalized cooperation against the slave trade: the United States rejected mutual search as inappropriate in peacetime and proposed treating the trade as piracy, but ratification of a 1824 convention faced remaining obstacles, so negotiations were suspended pending Congress’s views. Sweden has a reciprocal treaty, while Russia, the Netherlands, Prussia, the free Hanseatic cities, Oldenburg, and Sardinia have equivalent arrangements through mutually agreed regulations. A convention concerning the Northwest coast was signed with Russia and submitted to the Senate.

Relations with Spain and Portugal remain friendly despite political upheaval, and the United States recognized the independence of several South American governments. Brazil had received an American chargé d’affaires, with recognition by Portugal expected. American missions and commerce with Colombia, Chile, Guatemala, Buenos Aires, and Mexico were expanding; a Colombian trade treaty had been concluded, negotiations with Buenos Aires were delayed by the death of Minister Rodney, and improvements to the Tunis treaty had been obtained. The government also sought negotiations on neutral and belligerent maritime rights, while claiming indemnities from several European powers for seized vessels and cargoes.

The financial condition is presented as strong. Current-year receipts excluding loans were estimated at more than $18.5 million, with a prospective Treasury balance above $3 million after expenditures and debt payments. Two loans of $5 million each were authorized, one to replace higher-interest war debt and another to pay Florida treaty awards. Receipts in 1825 were expected to cover expenditures and the $10 million sinking-fund appropriation. Public debt was estimated at $86 million, or effectively about $79 million after excluding government-held Bank of the United States stock, and the address expresses hope that it could be discharged within ten years without unexpected events. Public investment had supported fortifications, arsenals, naval expansion, public buildings, pensions, Florida’s acquisition, and the extinguishment of Indian title to large tracts.

The military was described as efficient and well managed. The Army’s scientific and disciplinary condition was highly respectable, and the military academy was advanced, although dispersed artillery units required improved instruction; eleven companies were assembled at Old Point Comfort as an artillery school. Fortification and internal waterway projects were underway, including work on the Mississippi, Ohio, Presqu’ Isle Harbor, and Plymouth Beach. A board of engineers was surveying canals and nationally important roads, including the Potomac–Ohio route and a proposed southern road to New Orleans. Congress was urged to enlarge the military and topographical engineer corps.

Relations with most Indian tribes remained friendly, and many were advancing toward civilization through federal policy and 32 schools serving 916 students. Certain tribes around the Missouri, Upper Mississippi, and Upper Lakes remained hostile, killing or plundering citizens, and treaty negotiations and military escorts were delayed until the next season. Peace efforts among the tribes were under way. Congress was also urged to consider relocating tribes to districts west of present state boundaries, with civil governments and schools, as a gradual means of protecting them and enabling incorporation into the U.S. system.

The Mediterranean squadron was maintained and was to be augmented with the North Carolina because of possible hostilities involving Algiers. Gulf forces continued suppressing piracy, but the practice remained extensive and was attributed largely to land-based robbers and weak local government; augmentation was recommended. Enforcing the ban on the Atlantic slave trade found no American vessels engaged in it, although the trade continued under other flags. Pacific commerce and fisheries were growing, leading to recommendations for a Pacific squadron and a military post near the Columbia River. Post Office receipts were expected to exceed expenditures despite increased mail transportation.

General Lafayette visited the United States and was warmly honored. In recognition of his Revolutionary services and sacrifices, Congress was asked to provide a fitting grant.

Internationally, wars between Turkey and Greece and between Spain and the new American governments were described as favorable to independence, liberty, and humanity. Greece’s resistance commanded admiration. The new South American states were establishing representative governments, and the United States maintained a policy of noninterference. The address concluded that the nation was prosperous but must preserve its institutions, strengthen coastal defenses and the navy, improve transportation, maintain harmony between federal and state governments, and defend American rights and interests abroad.

Mali’s gold exports are declining as legacy mines wind down and new discoveries fail to offset the loss. The Sadiola mine is crucial to maintaining production, government revenue and employment, particularly because gold generates about 25–30% of government revenues. It is jointly owned by IAMGOLD (41%), AngloGold Ashanti (41%) and Mali’s government (18%).

Sadiola’s oxide-processing capacity is nearing depletion, reducing output from 600,000 ounces in 2000 to under 200,000 ounces. However, the mine contains 3.4 million ounces of proven and probable hard-rock reserves. IAMGOLD and AngloGold Ashanti plan to invest $380 million to modify the plant and process these reserves, potentially extending production for another decade and creating or preserving jobs. The project requires a government agreement whose negotiations have reportedly stalled, creating uncertainty ahead of Mali’s 2018 elections.

Industrial production rose only slightly from 46.5 tonnes in 2015 to 46.9 tonnes in 2016, while exports fell from 70 tonnes to 67 tonnes. Morila is due to close in 2019, Yatela has closed, and no new mines are expected before 2018. Sadiola currently employs about 1,000 people, 93% of them Malian nationals, and its expansion would improve infrastructure, including grid connectivity for nearby communities.

NVIDIA’s RTX IO works with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to stream data from NVMe SSDs directly to RTX GPUs and perform lossless decompression on the GPU. NVIDIA says this reduces CPU overhead, improves I/O performance and frame rates, accelerates game loading, reduces pop-in and stutter, and can reduce download and install sizes. RTX IO also supports large CAD, scientific, rendering, and virtual-reality workloads.

The NVIDIA A40 is presented as an Ampere-based data center GPU for visual computing, AI, and scientific applications. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to five times the AI-training throughput, 48GB of expandable memory, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, virtualization support, and compatibility with NVIDIA EGX.

GA10x Ampere GPUs support up to twice the performance of the prior generation in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. They include second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X support. The RTX 3090 has 24GB of GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC. Their fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports several codecs, including AV1 hardware decoding up to 8K60 HDR, while the seventh-generation NVENC encoder offloads video encoding and supports up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The RTX A6000 provides 48GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96GB through two NVLink-connected boards. GA10x GDDR6X memory also includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transmissions and retries them. NVIDIA notes that specifications are provided without warranties, reserves the right to change them, and does not warrant products for safety-critical applications.

The disclosure describes portable ground stations that provide landing, charging, and protective storage for vertical-takeoff aerial vehicles, including multicopters and rocket-propelled vehicles. Each station has a protective casing and an extendable landing pad that transitions between a compact closed configuration and an open configuration large enough for landing. A raised base platform supports the vehicle, while side flaps or extensions, bridging lobes, or telescoping wings enlarge the landing surface. Optional elevator, centering, locking, and windbreaker mechanisms assist deployment, positioning, securing, and landing.

Charging terminals may be positioned in the base platform, landing-pad extensions, casing walls, or top closure to contact corresponding vehicle terminals. Power may come from electrochemical cells, fuel cells, photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, piezoelectric units, or mains power. Homing aids can include contrasting visual patterns for high- and low-altitude guidance and infrared, radio-frequency, LED, visual, audio, or ultrasonic beacons. Additional modules may provide weather detection, transport, vehicle mounting, suspension, carrying, batteries, communications, sensors, radar, and night-vision functions.

Multiple networked ground stations can extend an aerial vehicle’s operating range by allowing it to land, recharge, and continue operating. In a described landing sequence, the station raises and extends its landing pad, the vehicle identifies and lands on it, a centering mechanism guides the vehicle onto the base platform, and the platform retracts into the casing for charging.

This study presents the first near-infrared spectra of cryogenic grain mixtures of water ice, epsomite, and halite to support compositional analysis of Europa’s surface using data from Europa Clipper and JUICE. A nitrogen-purged cryogenic facility was used to prepare crystalline water ice and commercial epsomite and halite in four grain-size bins, create pure and 50/50-volume mixtures, and acquire spectra at roughly 100–120 K. A small peak near 2.38 µm was attributed to contamination on the gold reference.

Hapke-based linear and intimate mixture models were compared with laboratory measurements. For water ice, both models generally reproduced laboratory spectra within about 10%, with no clear advantage for intimate mixing, though neither consistently reproduced both continuum slopes and absorption features. Increasing grain size reduced reflectance and saturated absorption bands, while fine particles could influence mixed spectra disproportionately. Epsomite showed numerous additional cryogenic absorption features, but its published optical constants may have been mislabeled as cryogenic; partial desiccation to hexahydrite was also proposed as an explanation for discrepancies. Halite’s 1.95 µm feature was attributed to adsorbed water, and halite–water-ice mixtures were nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice.

The results indicate that quantitative spectral unmixing should consider both linear and intimate models, potential grain-size observational bias, and uncertainty in epsomite optical constants when determining Europa’s surface composition and abundances.

An Uzbek court convicted U.S. citizen Zokir Aliyev of calling for the government’s overthrow and joining an extremist group, but fined him only $67 for offenses dating to 1999. Aliyev denied links to the militant Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, saying he attended only opposition meetings in Turkey in the 1990s. Authorities suspected he had IMU ties and training in Afghanistan.

In response to a Senate request, the President reported an alleged forcible resistance to federal law enforcement in Boston. He transmitted Deputy Marshal Patrick Riley’s affidavit, noting that unofficial accounts supported its main facts but official information was incomplete and some implicated persons disputed details. He condemned the violence as contrary to law and to the sentiments of Boston and Massachusetts, describing it as sudden and insufficiently prepared for.

He reviewed congressional resolutions requiring states to provide jails for federal prisoners or permitting marshals to obtain temporary facilities. After Massachusetts repealed its jail-access requirement in 1843 and prohibited assistance in enforcing the Fugitive Slave Act, the Massachusetts marshal was reminded of his duty to secure another detention place, but no official confirmation that he had done so was received. The President said he would issue directions if necessary. He transmitted a proclamation and military instructions related to the incident.

Citing his constitutional duty to execute federal laws, the President proposed amending the 1795 militia statute so that a prior proclamation would not be required when troops assist civil officers, with the United States paying their expenses. He also suggested congressional clarification of the 1807 act governing the Army and Navy and affirmed his readiness to suppress forcible resistance to federal law.

An appended proclamation warned against organizing an unauthorized expedition against Cuba, a Spanish colony, while the United States was at peace. It declared participation a high misdemeanor punishable by up to $3,000 and three years’ imprisonment, called on citizens to prevent such expeditions, and directed government officers to arrest offenders.

NVDA options trading can provide leveraged returns based on the stock’s volatility. When buying calls or puts, losses are limited to the premium paid, although the risk-reward profile varies by strategy, and options are complex.

Traders can use calls, puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, and collars, with strategy selection depending on investment goals and risk tolerance. Strategies aimed at maximizing returns include leverage, buying deep in-the-money options, writing covered calls, and using bullish spreads or straddles. To limit losses, traders may use stop-loss orders, protective puts, hedging, diversification, and position sizing.

Option prices are influenced by NVDA’s stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, and dividends. Rising stock prices generally increase call prices and decrease put prices, while the reverse occurs when prices fall. Higher implied volatility or unstable markets generally increase option prices; lower volatility or stable markets decrease them. Dividends generally reduce call prices and increase put prices. The passage recommends pricing options with models such as Black-Scholes.

Key considerations include option and transaction costs, potential profit or loss, margin requirements, and liquidity. NVDA options are generally liquid, and buying options typically requires less margin than writing them. Analysis should combine quantitative and qualitative methods, with greater emphasis on quantitative data. Useful tools include technical analysis, pricing models, trading software, and current news.

Major risks include adverse stock-price movements, time decay, volatility, and liquidity. Protective puts can hedge against declines, while calls and puts can express expectations of rising or falling prices. Tax treatment depends on the situation; trading is generally treated as capital-gains activity, so investors are advised to consult a tax professional.

Arun Jaitley’s final full Union Budget before the 2019 elections was criticized for lacking a dedicated section on women and for perpetuating traditional gender roles rather than addressing barriers to women’s participation and employment. Economists offered mixed assessments of its impact on women.

The National Health Protection Scheme, offering ₹5 lakh in annual family insurance and aiming to cover 10 crore vulnerable families, was praised as potentially improving rural and low-income women’s access to healthcare. However, its implementation and funding were questioned, especially because health allocations rose only 2.7%, the health ministry’s share of the Budget declined, and National Health Mission funding fell by 2.1%. Greater investment in preventive healthcare was also urged.

MSME credit support, corporate tax relief, sanitation facilities and the proposed expansion of Ujjwala were identified as potentially beneficial. However, maternity entitlement funding was reduced, and critics said many Ujjwala recipients could not afford cylinder refills. Overall, the Budget was seen as largely continuing existing policies without creating new pathways for women’s economic participation.

The rupee fell for a third session as importer demand exceeded remittance inflows, ending at 158.60/75 per dollar. It is down 3.4% this year. Rising Fed rates, the U.S.-China trade war and higher oil prices added pressure. A $584 million Chinese port payment eased pressure. The IMF cited debt and refinancing needs, while foreign investors’ year-to-date government-security outflows reached 29 billion rupees.

After seven or eight months in Quebec, the speaker feels at home and is happy family will attend the game. He credits success to hard work, preparation, and creating one’s own luck. Facing a strong home team, he says they must match its intensity and desperation, take it one game and shift at a time, and execute their game plan. He believes the first 10 minutes will be crucial and hopes to quiet the crowd.

USB-C and USB-A describe connector shapes rather than performance. USB-C is reversible and supports higher power delivery, while older USB-B and Micro-USB ports remain common. USB specifications determine transfer speeds and power delivery, but connections operate at the slowest link in the chain, making speed ratings more useful than inconsistent USB 3.x labels.

USB4, introduced in 2022, supports 20–40 Gbps and exclusively uses USB-C. USB4 Version 2 was announced and certified with potential speeds up to 120 Gbps, but adoption remains limited. USB Power Delivery 3.1 supports up to 240 watts, though adapters, hubs, devices, and cables must have sufficient wattage ratings.

DisplayPort Alternate Mode carries audio and video over one USB-C cable, with capabilities determined by the DisplayPort generation. USB4 requires DisplayPort 2.0 support.

Thunderbolt uses USB-C connectors and is cross-compatible with USB devices. Thunderbolt 4 is built on USB4 and guarantees up to 40 Gbps, 100 watts, and two 4K displays at 60 Hz. Emerging Thunderbolt 5 offers up to 80 Gbps bidirectional bandwidth, 120 Gbps unidirectional bandwidth via Bandwidth Boost, expanded display support, and 240-watt power delivery. Its adoption is still early.

Cable capabilities can limit device performance, so users should check rated speeds and wattage or use the cable supplied with the device.

The passage argues that the policy intended to end the slavery agitation had instead allowed it to intensify, leaving the nation divided between a free and slave status. It presents the Nebraska doctrine and the Dred Scott decision as parts of a coordinated mechanism designed to expand slavery. The Nebraska bill repealed Congress’s exclusion of slavery from territories and asserted popular sovereignty; the resulting electoral endorsement of the policy and the Supreme Court’s ruling supplied additional gains.

The ruling, together with Senator Stephen Douglas’s policy of “caring not whether slavery is voted down or voted up,” is described as advancing three goals: denying Black people citizenship and its protections; prohibiting Congress and territorial legislatures from excluding slavery from territories; and leaving the status of people held as slaves in free states for state courts to determine. Although the speaker says preconcert cannot be absolutely proven, he portrays the sequence of political and judicial actions as closely fitted to a common plan. He predicts that another Supreme Court decision may declare that states cannot prohibit slavery, making slavery lawful throughout the country.

Rejecting Douglas as an effective ally because his principles did not oppose slavery’s expansion, the speaker calls for the cause to be led by committed Republicans. He recalls that more than 1.3 million Republicans had united against slavery and expresses confidence that continued resistance would ultimately prevail.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed Henry J. Adams III’s conviction and sentence for armed bank robbery. Adams served as a lookout, recruited Veronica Johnson to drive him, and knew the robbery and escape plan in exchange for a share of the proceeds. His guidelines range was 84 to 105 months, but the district court imposed 140 months plus four years of supervised release.

The court denied Adams’s request for a two-level minor-participant reduction, finding no clear error because he knowingly participated in and helped plan the robbery. It characterized the sentence as an upward variance based on the statutory sentencing factors, rather than a departure subject to the guidelines’ departure requirements. Considering Adams’s extensive criminal history, repeated reoffending, the seriousness of the offense, deterrence, public protection, and the need to support a lawful lifestyle, the court found the sentence reasonable and rejected Adams’s sentence-disparity argument.

Chelsea, Real Madrid and Tottenham are competing for Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. Spurs plan a £28m bid, while Chelsea and Madrid prepare counteroffers. Sanchez wants to leave for Premier League and Champions League football.

In this State of the Union address, the speaker says the United States faces decisive challenges at home and abroad but remains strong, united, and confident. Citing education reform, the Department of Homeland Security, tax relief, and corporate-accountability reforms as a starting point, he calls for making scheduled income-tax cuts permanent, ending double taxation of dividends, and limiting discretionary spending growth to about 4 percent. Domestic goals also include broader health insurance, Medicare reform with prescription-drug choices, medical liability reform, and an energy strategy emphasizing efficiency, cleaner technology, reduced power-plant pollution, forest protection, and hydrogen-powered cars. He further proposes faith-based service, mentoring for disadvantaged youth, expanded addiction treatment, protection for infants at birth, and a ban on human cloning.

Internationally, he cites progress in Afghanistan and the Middle East, proposes a $15 billion, five-year AIDS initiative for Africa and the Caribbean, and calls for continued counterterrorism cooperation, Project BioShield, improved intelligence coordination, and stronger homeland defenses. He warns of nuclear, chemical, and biological threats, particularly from Iran, North Korea, and Iraq. He accuses Saddam Hussein of defying disarmament requirements, concealing weapons programs, and supporting terrorists. He says the United States will seek a U.N. Security Council meeting on February 5 and, if Hussein does not fully disarm, lead a coalition to disarm him, while promising food, medicine, supplies, and freedom for Iraqis. He closes by affirming confidence in America’s armed forces, unity, faith, and commitment to defending freedom and peace.

Drug retailers’ shares fell after reports Amazon was considering online prescription drug sales, discussing pharmacy benefit managers and hiring to assess the market; Walgreens, Rite Aid and CVS shares each dropped about 5%.

The study examines how values are conveyed through vocabulary in Turkish reading texts from second- through fourth-grade Ministry of National Education textbooks. It frames values education as important for behavior, character, decision-making, and citizenship and notes that textbooks communicate values explicitly and implicitly.

The corpus comprised 88 prose reading texts; first-grade texts and poems were excluded. ABBYY FineReader, TextMate, and Text Wrangler were used for conversion, tokenization, and cleaning, producing 3,637 unique words. Three applied-linguistics experts classified each word’s internal meaning as positive, negative, or neutral using introspection and dictionary definitions.

Results showed 172 positive words (4.72%), 159 negative words (4.37%), and 3,306 neutral words (91.43%). No observable relationship was found between grade level and the values conveyed. The study concludes that textbooks lack established value-education standards for vocabulary and recommends corpus-based text selection and construction aligned with intended values and grade levels. Digitizing print textbooks is also recommended to support further research.

The lecture introduces a course connecting extremal graph theory and additive combinatorics. Schur’s attempt to prove Fermat’s Last Theorem through modular arithmetic is shown to fail: for every fixed exponent \(n\), nontrivial solutions to \(x^n+y^n=z^n\) exist modulo all sufficiently large primes \(p\).

Schur’s Theorem states that every finite coloring of the positive integers contains a monochromatic solution to \(x+y=z\). Its equivalent finitary form says that for each number of colors \(r\), there is an \(N(r)\) such that every \(r\)-coloring of \(\{1,\dots,N(r)\}\) contains such a solution. The two forms are shown equivalent by diagonalization, although optimal bounds remain difficult.

Ramsey’s theorem for triangles states that every \(r\)-coloring of the edges of a sufficiently large complete graph contains a monochromatic triangle. After an inductive proof, it is used to prove Schur’s Theorem by coloring the edge between \(i\) and \(j\) according to the color of \(j-i\). A monochromatic triangle then produces a monochromatic solution to \(x+y=z\), illustrating the flexibility gained by reformulating number-theoretic problems as graph-theoretic ones.

The lecture then surveys additive combinatorics. Van der Waerden’s theorem guarantees arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions; Roth proved the three-term case for positive-density sets; and Szemerédi proved the full Erdős–Turán conjecture. Szemerédi’s theorem prompted developments in ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis, hypergraph regularity, and the Polymath project. Its generalizations include multidimensional “constellations,” polynomial patterns in positive-density sets, and Green–Tao’s theorem that the primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. The recurring theme is the distinction between structure and randomness.

Roth’s finitary theorem is presented as the bound that a subset of \(\{1,\dots,N\}\) avoiding three-term arithmetic progressions has size \(o(N)\), with a substantial gap between known lower and upper bounds. The course will next examine extremal graph problems involving forbidden subgraphs. Course logistics include collaborative lecture-note writing, a Wikipedia contribution, and additional office hours.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives surfaced old blog posts allegedly criticizing President Donald Trump from his first term. The posts included claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” Rosenzweig joined the U.S. attorney’s office in September 2020 and worked on complex economic crimes cases. The Justice Department also fired three other prosecutors in the district who formerly worked with special counsel Jack Smith. Smith criticized the targeting of political opponents and attacks on the rule of law. After Smith’s speech, U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert left his position amid Trump’s pressure to indict Letitia James and James Comey.

Weekly trading focuses on weekly price action and can include position trading, using the weekly chart for broader market context, weekly rotation, or swing trading based on weekly price bars. It trades less frequently than daily strategies and may produce larger gains. Most weekly-chart traders are long-term position traders, commonly seeking range-bound markets and holding trades for six to twelve months.

A common weekly range strategy involves identifying support and resistance, then trading setups at those levels. Setups may use reversal candlestick patterns such as hammers, shooting stars, engulfing patterns, or harami, as well as oscillator overbought/oversold or divergence signals. Weekly trend-following trades can last several years and may resemble buy-and-hold investing. Some daily trend followers also use the weekly chart to assess broader market structure, locate entries, and set stops and targets, because a daily trend may be only a swing within a weekly range.

Weekly highs and lows can act as support or resistance on lower timeframes. On H4, traders can use breakouts or reversals at these levels for swing trades, with exits at the weekly close, a channel boundary, or the opposite weekly level. Once broken, a weekly high may become support and a weekly low may become resistance. Similar opportunities can be used on H1, M30, and M15 for day trading, with exits at the daily close or nearby support and resistance.

The best timeframe depends on the strategy and should be determined through backtesting. Position trading generally suits weekly and daily charts, weekly swing strategies often combine weekly and H4 analysis, and day trading or scalping is unsuitable for weekly charts. Backtesting appears more powerful on daily bars than weekly bars in the stock market.

Stocks can also be traded weekly using a strategy with regular setups and stock screeners. Traders must account for price gaps, account limits, and risk tolerance. FINRA’s pattern-day-trader rule requires at least $25,000 when four or more day trades occur within five business days and exceed 6% of total margin-account trades over that period; otherwise, traders are limited to three day trades per week. Weekly swing traders are unaffected by this requirement.

One backtested weekly long-only sector-rotation strategy ranked four ETFs each week. It recorded 728 trades, a 0.4% average gain before slippage and commission, 15.1% annual returns, and a 43% maximum drawdown in 2008. Its monthly version produced 166 trades, 12.1% annual returns, and a 21% maximum drawdown.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court’s grant of summary judgment to AMCO Insurance Company and denial of George Morello’s motion for reconsideration. The record showed no genuine dispute that AMCO reasonably investigated Morello’s claim, relied on expert medical opinions, and did not unreasonably delay benefits or a settlement offer. Conclusory contrary expert opinions were rebutted by the record, and mediation communications were inadmissible for the bad-faith claim. Because the bad-faith claim failed, Morello’s derivative claims for intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and Unruh Act violations also failed. Reconsideration was unwarranted because there was no clear error or intervening change in controlling law.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing concept used in West Coast-style offenses, letting the quarterback decide quickly and release the ball fast. With five eligible receivers downfield, the quarterback has options to either side, and the stick route runner is typically the primary target, adjusting his route to coverage shown.

Against man, the quarterback can throw to the tight end on the stick cut or to the X receiver on a slant; against Cover 3 and 4, he reads the flat defender. Against Cover 2, the cornerback becomes the flat defender post-snap and can undercut the arrow route, making the hole-shot throw to the Z receiver a legitimate option requiring a strong arm and anticipation.

Pre-snap, the quarterback identifies the flat defender (the nickel in a Nickel-Sam look) and throws off his movement: if the nickel honors the tight end or fails to widen, throw the arrow; if he widens, go to the stick route.

Versus man, the tight end releases vertically then runs a speed-out path, the back and slot run arrows, the X receiver runs a three-step slant, and the Z receiver runs a go route; versus zone, the tight end bursts and settles in the void.

Variations include a 2x2 condensed formation read outside-in with a check-down to the running back, and a Trips Flex "sticko" look with double moves, a delayed slot slant, and a sluggo route.

NVIDIA Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 2, 2021 reported revenue of $5.661 billion, up 84% year over year. Gross profit was $3.629 billion, operating income was $1.956 billion, net income was $1.912 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $3.03. Gross margin declined to 64.1% from 65.1%, primarily due to Mellanox-related intangible amortization and Data Center product mix.

Graphics segment revenue was $3.451 billion with $1.786 billion of operating income; Compute & Networking revenue was $2.210 billion with $861 million of operating income. Revenue by market was $2.760 billion for Gaming, $2.048 billion for Data Center, $372 million for Professional Visualization, $154 million for Automotive, and $327 million for OEM and Other.

At May 2, 2021, NVIDIA held $978 million of cash and cash equivalents and $11.689 billion of marketable securities. Total assets were $30.796 billion, total liabilities were $12.022 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $18.774 billion. The company generated $1.874 billion of operating cash flow, used $1.272 billion in investing activities, and used $471 million in financing activities. NVIDIA paid $99 million in dividends and did not repurchase shares during the quarter.

NVIDIA completed its $7.13 billion Mellanox acquisition in April 2020. Its pending $40 billion Arm acquisition required regulatory approvals and other closing conditions; NVIDIA had paid $2 billion at signing and would owe $10 billion in cash plus 44.3 million shares upon closing, with a potential additional earn-out of up to $5 billion or 10.3 million shares.

The board declared a four-for-one stock split, subject to shareholder approval, with additional shares expected to be distributed on July 19, 2021. Management identified pandemic-related demand and supply uncertainty, cryptocurrency-market volatility, and anticipated supply constraints as risks. Disclosure controls were concluded to be effective, with no material changes in internal financial-reporting controls during the quarter. A securities lawsuit was dismissed, plaintiffs appealed, and related derivative suits remained stayed; no loss contingency was accrued.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes 1–128 migration entries and moves pages in SNP- and non-SNP-enabled systems. SNP systems permit only Hypervisor-owned pages, while SEV systems allow only unencrypted or host/hypervisor-encrypted memory. The command supports pages in use by DMA, updates IOMMU host PTEs, and requires software to prevent CPU access and update CPU page tables after migration. Non-SNP ATS users must set hPTE.PMS, issue ATS invalidations, and synchronize before the command. SNP source and destination pages must be in the Hypervisor state, and 2M pages must be split into 4K pages. Firmware validates addresses, page states, RMP access, and page sizes; invalidates and synchronizes TLBs; flushes DMA; copies data while preserving encryption; updates mappings and RMPs; and clears migration status.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST moves 1–128 pages belonging to an SNP guest and requires RMP_ENFORCE=1. Sources must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, and destinations must be Pre-Migration; afterward, destinations take the source state and sources become Pre-Migration. DMA is unsupported and may be aborted if concurrent. A 2M entry must be aligned and consist of physically contiguous 4K pages. Firmware validates the guest context and RMP state, obtains exclusive RMP access, invalidates and synchronizes the CPU TLB, copies data, and updates both RMPs.

A final command marks the end of a migration sequence and can interrupt on completion. Format errors reject commands, list-entry errors may permit partial success, ring-buffer errors are reported through PM_STATUS, and hardware errors appear in command status or via MCA. A timeout should be logged as an MCA, after which software may save state, terminate VMs, or stop further commands. Hardware failure may make an entire 128-page batch unrecoverable, though software can attempt to save data and system state before reboot.

Under GST, consignments over Rs 50,000 require e-way bills, though they are optional below that value. The GST Council exempted 153 items, including household LPG, PDS kerosene, currency, jewellery, food products, animals, handicrafts, personal effects and certain medical items. Postal baggage, non-motorised transport and goods moving from international ports to hinterland ports for customs clearance are also exempt. The requirement will begin after permit software is ready; bills detail the goods, route, supplier, recipient and transporter but are unnecessary for intra-state journeys under 10 km.

Infiniti’s Q Inspiration concept will inspire an electrified platform supporting up to five models over five years in China, likely as global models. Its clear lines, distinctive lights and grilles will inform coupe and crossover designs.

School systems nationwide are equipping yellow buses with GPS tracking, turn-by-turn navigation, electronic student manifests, live interior and exterior cameras, route-optimization tools, engine monitoring and family tracking apps. Kansas City Public Schools made these features a central part of its five-year, $100 million contract with Zum, allowing drivers to navigate routes and record pickups and drop-offs while dispatchers monitor bus locations, speeds and schedules.

School officials and vendors say bus technology can improve safety and reliability, reduce fuel and labor costs, support drivers, optimize routes, monitor maintenance and student behavior, provide quicker incident response, reduce parent calls and help address driver shortages. Bentonville Schools pays about $90,000 annually for Transportant’s tracking and camera services, while Transportant typically charges roughly $3,600 per bus upfront plus $69 annually. Some districts purchase separate products to avoid dependence on one vendor.

Privacy advocates warn that GPS records, video, boarding data and student photographs create security and long-term retention risks as the bus technology market grows amid limited regulation. Districts report storing data separately and routinely deleting videos, while Transportant says it encrypts devices and does not sell student data. St. Johns County School District stores video on its own servers and blurs student faces in public-records responses. Affordability remains a factor for districts considering adoption.

Fiat Chrysler rejected a merger proposal from an unidentified Chinese automaker because the financial terms were inadequate, despite reported interest from several Chinese automakers and joint-venture partner Guangzhou. FCA had long pursued mergers or acquisitions, including approaches to General Motors and Volkswagen, while CEO Sergio Marchionne preferred partnerships and was reluctant to sell the company. Chinese interest may be driven by the government’s “China Outbound” policy and efforts to enter the U.S. market; FCA’s debt-reduction goals, history, distribution network, and product lineup make it attractive.

SOS pressure defense emphasizes acting first, taking initiative, and committing to repeated, methodical drilling. Coaches can build acceptance through positive, encouraging feedback and by demonstrating the value of defensive success. The on-ball actions are Set, On, and Smother. Set forces the ballhandler to dribble rather than shoot or pass by using a low, wide stance, close hand position, and active passing-lane denial. On then guides the dribbler toward a sideline or baseline checkpoint through quick slides, with a “Sprint and Recover” response when beaten. Smother applies maximum pressure when the ballhandler picks up the ball, crowding the shooter, extending both arms, and disrupting vision.

The off-ball actions are Snuggle, Off, and Strike. Snuggle denies passes to an offensive player one pass away, using a low stance, arm position, and short slides; it can reverse after a back cut or become a full Post Front against a low-post player. Off moves decisively between the opponent and ballhandler to deny a cut to the basket or a return pass and can begin from any on-ball action. Strike is the weakside strategy: the defender moves quickly into position, denies entry toward the three-second area, covers post lobs, helps against beaten defenders, blocks layups, boxes out, and rebounds. When a weakside player receives a crosscourt pass, the defender closes out from Strike into Set and directs the ballhandler toward the nearest corner or baseline checkpoint.

Xiaomi is preparing for its biggest 2018 launch event, expected to feature the Mi 8, Mi 8 SE, Mi Note 5, and Mi Band 3. The Mi A2 may not launch in India, but more Android One devices are planned, and the Mi 6X could receive a new name. Xiaomi is also preparing the dual-camera Redmi S2/Y2 for India.

A railroad passenger train broke down in freezing weather when a locomotive driving-wheel tire came off and the others slipped, leaving the engine unable to move. The plaintiff brakeman was assigned to flag and protect the train’s rear for several hours and sustained frostbite to both feet and injuries extending into his legs.

The plaintiff alleged violation of the Federal Boiler Inspection Act and negligence under the Federal Employers’ Liability Act. The jury found that the breakdown proximately caused his injuries, awarded $12,000, but also found the locomotive safe, the accident unavoidable, and neither party negligent. The district court entered judgment for the railroad.

The Fifth Circuit held that the special issue concerning locomotive safety lacked necessary instructions on the Boiler Inspection Act and incorrectly allowed the jury to decide the issue without being informed of the railroad’s absolute duty to maintain safe equipment. Because the undisputed evidence showed that the locomotive and necessary driving wheels failed while in service, the breakdown violated the Act as a matter of law. The plaintiff was not responsible for the failure, and the jury had already found the breakdown proximately caused his injuries. The court reversed and instructed the district court to enter judgment for the plaintiff in the amount of $12,000.

North American markets ended the week with steep losses as strong U.S. jobs data raised concerns about inflation and further interest-rate hikes. The Dow Jones fell 2.5%, while the S&P 500 lost 2.1% and the Nasdaq dropped 2%, all posting their worst weekly losses since 2016. Payrolls rose by 200,000 in January, unemployment held at 4.1%, and wages recorded their strongest annual growth since 2009. Rising bond yields and weak corporate earnings weighed on stocks; Apple fell 4.3% after iPhone sales missed expectations. In Canada, the S&P/TSX Composite lost 1.6% amid falling oil and gold prices and continued declines in marijuana stocks. Mazabuka’s sugar boom attracted migrant workers, predominantly men, and a local sex industry, contributing to Zambia’s severe AIDS epidemic along key transport routes. At the epidemic’s peak, treatment was unavailable, HIV-positive patients filled hospital beds, and Zambia recorded about 70,000 AIDS-related deaths annually in 2003.

Zambia has since expanded HIV testing, education and treatment, while reducing new infections by 27 percent since 2010 and AIDS-related deaths by 11 percent. The local NGO DAPP leads a door-to-door “Total Control of the Epidemic” campaign using military-style organization to encourage testing, condom use and behavior change. It has reached more than 1.5 million of Zambia’s 16.5 million residents through community outreach involving former sex workers, truckers, field officers and traditional leaders. District officials and residents credit improved awareness, treatment and reduced stigma with helping people manage HIV and limit its spread.

The paper examines how AI ethics is integrated into computer science curricula at leading Indian engineering institutions. Researchers manually collected publicly available syllabi from CS and AI-related programs at the top 100 institutions in India’s 2024 NIRF rankings, obtaining 3,395 courses. Two researchers reviewed topics and explicit learning outcomes, cross-verifying findings and identifying implicit ethics content through themes such as privacy, fairness, safety, human rights, societal impact, and policy.

Only 75 courses, or 2.21%, incorporated AI ethics content. Of these, 60% addressed it in one session, 20% in two sessions, 13% across three to five sessions, and 7% were dedicated courses; 92% were offered at undergraduate level. Common topics were privacy, legal issues, and data governance (42%); accountability and policy (32%); ethical frameworks and moral reasoning (24%); human-AI interaction and agency (24%); algorithmic bias and fairness (18%); safety and robustness (16%); generative-AI concerns (11%); and social impact and justice (8%). Learning outcomes focused on identifying privacy risks, understanding fairness and explainability, critiquing ethical dilemmas, comparing governance frameworks, and applying ethical reasoning.

Fewer than half of the institutions publicly provided detailed curricula. Over 90% of relevant courses relied on general AI or machine-learning textbooks, and no course documented an assessment explicitly dedicated to AI ethics. The authors conclude that such education in India is limited, superficial, inconsistent, and lacking shared resources and assessment practices. They recommend consensus learning goals, open contextual teaching materials, meaningful assessments, faculty development, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and greater curriculum transparency. Limitations include possible bias toward institutions with public materials, missed or outdated syllabi, and restriction of the sample to top-ranked institutions, making the findings preliminary rather than fully representative.

Heart attacks and strokes have fallen 30% in the UK over two decades but remain major health hazards. Cholesterol- and blood-pressure-lowering medicines have contributed significantly. Statins are widely prescribed, but their reported side effects may be influenced by the nocebo effect: blinded users experienced no more side effects than placebo users, while reported effects increased once they knew they were taking statins.

New lipid-lowering injections, including Repatha, Praluent and six-monthly Leqvio, can reduce LDL cholesterol by around 50%, but are generally reserved for very high-risk people whose cholesterol is not controlled by tablets.

Lifestyle measures can improve cholesterol and heart health. Quitting smoking, exercising regularly, eating oily fish or omega-3-rich plant foods, and increasing soluble fibre through oats, barley, fruit, vegetables, beans, nuts and seeds may help. Exercise can lower LDL and raise HDL even without weight loss. Cooking from scratch can reduce hidden sugar and salt; replacing standard salt with potassium-containing alternatives may lower blood pressure and reduce heart-attack, stroke and early-death risks. Fortified products such as Benecol and Flora ProActiv, along with soya foods, can also help lower cholesterol. The TLC (Therapeutic Lifestyle Changes) diet combines dietary and lifestyle changes to reduce cholesterol and protect heart health.

Walter Camp is credited with developing modern American football from rugby by establishing consistent rules, 11-player teams, the line of scrimmage, quarterback position, downs-based possession, and the scoring system. Variations were played at northeastern colleges, including Harvard and Yale, and the name “football” reflects a combination of European soccer and rugby.

American football is not currently an Olympic sport, though flag football may appear at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Its development and professional talent are concentrated in North America, particularly the United States. Each team fields 11 players, while the CFL uses 12. Professional and collegiate games last 60 minutes in four 15-minute quarters; high-school quarters last 12 minutes.

A football field is 100 yards between goal lines, has 10-yard end zones, and is 160 feet, or 53.3 yards, wide. Scoring consists of six points for a touchdown, one for an extra point, two for a conversion or safety, and three for a field goal.

Common penalties include offsides, encroachment, false start, pass interference, holding, defensive holding, personal fouls, roughing the passer, and illegal formation. A catch generally requires possession, control, two feet in bounds, and a football move, with exceptions for end-zone catches and certain sideline catches.

Turnovers include interceptions, fumbles, and turnover on downs. The line of scrimmage separates the teams before the snap, while the neutral zone is the area between them where only the center may stand before the snap. Special teams include kickoffs, returns, punts, field goals, extra points, blocks, and free kicks. An audible is a quarterback’s late play change, a down is one offensive play, and the red zone is the area between the goal line and 20-yard line.

The paper develops a quantitative methodology for studying digital business ecosystems (DBEs), particularly which firms are likely to prosper or decline in a closed, static system with asymmetric competitive interactions. It builds a simulated DBE whose companies and products share statistical properties with an observed ecosystem. Companies have SELL and WANT lists, while trust and mistrust are represented separately; product attributes may be numeric or symbolic, and qualitative trust categories are converted into relative numerical weights using the Weber–Fechner law.

Inspired by asymmetric neural interactions, the ecosystem is modeled as a fully connected self-organizing network. Each company has an abstract fitness variable governed by coupled nonlinear differential equations. Fitness decays without interaction, increases through self-excitation after a critical threshold, and receives weighted excitatory signals when desired and supplied products match. Excitation depends on product similarity, the supplier’s fitness, and the buyer’s trust. Companies also exert inhibitory signals on one another when they sell similar products. Company-specific and shared background inputs can also be included.

The equations are solved iteratively: companies below a fitness threshold may be removed, while new firms may enter with the average fitness of existing firms. Preliminary experiments use a simulated ecosystem of 100 companies trading 20 products and examine survival over time; one parameter set produces a monopoly after 12 iterations.

The authors identify future needs: tie dynamical parameters to measurable real-world data, account for inhibition arising from firms competing to buy the same products in finite closed markets, and introduce new companies randomly.

Introduced in 1989 by bond trader Nick Scott, the Camarilla pivot extends the classical floor-trader pivot and uses the previous day’s closing price to calculate four support and four resistance levels. Day traders use these nine levels to identify intraday support and resistance, potential trend reversals, entries, exits, and risk-management levels, with trading methods depending on market conditions. Various strategies can be applied across financial markets, including trades based on the opening position relative to the previous close and pivot levels. Fibonacci pivots instead use retracement, projection, and extension levels. A referenced ordinary-pivot backtest produced no “super profits,” and readers are encouraged to backtest their own strategies using historical data.

Lung cancer remains a leading cause of death, and symptomatic diagnosis often occurs at an advanced stage. Although annual low-dose CT screening reduces mortality and downstaging, adherence is limited by access, clinical workflow bottlenecks, radiation concerns, and high false-positive rates. Blood-based biomarkers may complement screening, but single-omics approaches can have limited sensitivity for early-stage tumors because of low circulating tumor DNA levels and difficulty distinguishing cancer signals from smoking- or comorbidity-related effects.

The observational MOSAIC case-control study enrolled 2,513 adults at 77 U.S. sites, including 2,094 clinically eligible participants with lung cancer or non-cancer controls. Deep untargeted plasma proteomics, RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and four targeted immunoassays were used to develop an XGBoost lung cancer classifier. Of 1,623 participants with complete quality-controlled data, 1,225 were used for training and 398 for blinded validation.

In the training set, a clinical-only classifier achieved an AUC of 0.78, while a proteomics classifier achieved 0.91. The combined multi-omics classifier achieved AUCs of 0.96 for all-stage cancer and 0.93 for stage I disease. In the held-out validation set at a fixed threshold, overall sensitivity and specificity were both 89%; stage-specific sensitivities were 80% for stage I, 88% for stage II, and 99% for stage III-IV.

The final model contained 682 features representing 149 proteins, 346 genes, and 77 metabolic pathways, with no single omics type dominating. Of these features, 412 (60.4%) were significantly associated with cancer stage. The findings support development of a blood-based assay for early lung cancer detection, but prospective validation in the intended high-risk screening population is required and ongoing. The study was funded entirely by PrognomiQ, Inc.; affiliated authors reported salary and equity compensation.

Longstanding concerns—including research fraud, paper mills, inadequate peer review, pharmaceutical influence, high subscription and article-processing costs, and “publish or perish” incentives—are fueling Trump administration attacks on scientific publishing. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH Director Jayanta Bhattacharya have changed policies and promoted reforms focused on bias, misinformation, access, and reproducible research.

The administration has terminated hundreds of NIH grants, proposed cutting the NIH budget by 40 percent, targeted major medical journals, and considered a government-run journal, potentially increasing federal control over scientific publishing. Critics say these efforts exploit genuine problems to advance an ideological agenda and could worsen conditions, while a new conservative-linked public health journal could provide a platform for dubious research.

The NIH has rescinded a federal public-access deposit policy and plans to cap journal article-processing charges in the $19 billion for-profit publishing industry. Supporters say these policies could reduce costs and alter damaging incentives, but others argue that open access alone will not restore trust, artificial caps may simply shift costs, and meaningful reform requires scientists and academic institutions to change how researchers are evaluated and rewarded.

The invention reduces real-time graphics-rendering resources during user saccades. A processor renders a simulated scene, detects the onset of a saccade that causes saccadic masking using eye-movement measurements, and lowers CPU or GPU usage for at least part of the saccade. Detection may use changes in eye direction, speed, or acceleration; EMG signals; or optical, range, image, and audio sensors.

The system may predict saccade duration using an eye-movement model and onset measurements. During the reduction period, it can skip or repeat frames, lower frame rate, resolution, texture detail, polygon count, or lighting effects, with the reduction adjusted according to detection confidence and position within the saccade. Saved resources may support complex lighting updates or other processes, reducing power consumption and potentially extending battery life. Calibration can compare predicted and measured saccade durations to update an individualized eye-movement model. Embodiments include methods, systems, and storage media, and the technique may be combined with gaze tracking and foveated rendering.

The article demonstrates how to build and test an RSI-based trading strategy in TradingView using Pine Script. The example uses DOT on five-minute charts with a 14-period RSI, entering long positions when RSI exits oversold at 35 and short positions when it exits overbought at 65, then closing positions when RSI crosses 50. It explains adding and configuring RSI, creating a strategy template, defining entry and exit conditions with `strategy.entry`, `strategy.close`, and `if` statements, and adding editable user inputs for RSI parameters. After adding the script to a chart, TradingView displays performance data including equity, net profit, drawdown, and win rate. Pro accounts can conduct deep backtests over available history and review metrics such as Sharpe Ratio and average risk-reward ratio, while trade data can be exported to CSV with a paid account. The article cautions that RSI alone has not performed consistently and should be complemented with other indicators or criteria.

The study aimed to identify requirements and develop strategies for achieving excellence in vocational education among institutions under Thailand’s Office of Vocational Education Commission amid Industry 4.0, technological disruption, economic change, and labor shortages. Using a two-phase research and development approach, researchers reviewed relevant literature, surveyed 206 respondents from 424 institutions across eight institution types, analyzed current and desired conditions using a modified priority needs index and SWOT analysis, and examined practices at three exemplary vocational institutions. Phase two developed and refined a strategic framework and implementation manual through focus group discussions with nine experts.

Current management conditions were rated high and desired conditions highest. The greatest needs were curriculum development (PNImodified = 0.198), cooperation networks (0.196), and personnel (0.193). The resulting framework included a vision, mission, objectives, strategies, and key performance indicators across six areas: professional management efficiency; competency-based curricula aligned with international standards; teaching and learning quality; teacher and staff expertise; comprehensive workforce-development networks; and graduate quality. It emphasized digital management and learning, employer collaboration, dual vocational education, professional certification, active learning, ethical development, and alignment with labor-market needs. Experts rated the strategies’ suitability and feasibility at the highest level.

Recommendations were to prioritize internationally aligned competency-based curricula, adapt implementation to each institution’s context and SWOT findings, and integrate strategies with existing plans. Future research should address curriculum models linking professional competencies with qualification systems and methods for strengthening digital-content production and compliance with international competency standards.

David Dickinson, a freelance science writer, Air Force veteran, and amateur astronomer, reflects on finally witnessing his first total solar eclipse on August 21 after previously seeing partial and annular eclipses. He describes eclipse chasers, or “umbraphiles,” as a small community that travels widely and plans for totality, an experience fellow chasers describe as singular and transformative. Dickinson plans to view the eclipse at the Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute in North Carolina for 107 seconds, while dedicated chasers favor areas such as Wyoming and Idaho for better weather.

The eclipse will cross the United States from Oregon to South Carolina, producing up to two minutes and 40 seconds of totality along a 70-mile-wide path, though officials anticipate traffic, communication, and supply disruptions. Dickinson emphasizes using ISO 12312-2 solar glasses or properly filtered telescopes or binoculars during partial phases; only totality permits unprotected viewing, and some vendors are selling bogus glasses. He recommends a pinhole projector for partial viewing and focusing on the experience rather than photography. He also notes that the moon’s gradual recession will eventually end total solar eclipses and that another U.S. eclipse is scheduled for April 8, 2024.
