This study evaluated the maturity of peer-reviewed AI-in-healthcare publications from 2019–2021 across 34 medical specialties. PubMed records were assessed using a BERT-based classifier, and mature articles were manually annotated for data, model, disease, specialty, and geographic distribution. Overall, only about 5% of 7,062 publications were classified as mature, with rates of 6.01% in 2019, 7.7% in 2020, and 1.81% in 2021. Radiology had the most mature publications, while COVID-19 research had low maturity rates of 4% in 2020 and 1.6% in 2021. Mature publications were geographically concentrated in the United States and China, with regions including South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa underrepresented. Image data dominated mature publications, whereas text data increased modestly and tabular data declined to zero in 2021. Deep-learning models were most common, followed by traditional machine-learning approaches. The findings indicate a need for more clinically relevant, deployable, geographically diverse AI research and suggest opportunities to use heterogeneous datasets and models across healthcare domains.

The London breakout strategy is a forex day-trading approach that trades price breaking above or below the range established before the London session opens. The range is typically formed during the Asian session, and breakouts usually occur within the first three hours of London trading. Upside breakouts prompt long positions; downside breakouts prompt short positions. The strategy seeks to benefit from the London session’s high liquidity, volatility, and influence on the day’s trend.

The pre-London range can be defined either by the Asian session’s highest and lowest prices or by its highest and lowest opening and closing prices, excluding candle wicks. Breakouts can also occur before London opens, during the Frankfurt and other European trading hours.

A London breakout indicator is a custom forex tool that displays buy and sell signals, entry levels, stop-loss and take-profit levels, and sometimes fake-breakout signals. Some indicators provide one daily signal based on the previous Tokyo-session range and can be used to automate trading.

In an EUR/USD backtest, buying breakouts above the range lost money, while buying breakouts below the range performed somewhat better but produced average gains near zero. The authors conclude that the strategy requires additional parameters and risk management and express skepticism about its general profitability, describing forex edges as close to zero while suggesting stocks and bonds may offer better risk and reward.

Bulk MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals were grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method and characterized by TEM-EDX, SQUID magnetometry, and X-band magnetic resonance. Four ingot regions showed progressive structural and compositional changes caused by melt flow and manganese redistribution. Sample A contained predominantly MnBi₂Te₄ with local MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ inclusions and exhibited antiferromagnetic transitions at 26 and 13.5 K. Sample B had septuple layers separated by one or two quintuple layers and showed a 13.5 K Néel transition. Samples C and D had larger septuple-layer separations, approximately 7 ± 2 and 4–5 quintuple layers, respectively, and displayed ferromagnetic-like transitions near 11 and 9 K. Their lower Mn content, particularly within septuple layers, was associated with reduced Curie temperatures and magnetic anisotropy; Sample D also showed increased stacking disorder.

Four growth regimes were identified. Turbulent flow suppressed early MnTe precipitation and enabled nearly pure MnBi₂Te₄ formation. Rapid MnTe precipitation then sharply reduced Mn concentration from about 14 to 7 at.% and initiated mixed MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ growth. Under stationary flow, diffusion-limited competition between MnBi₂Te₄ layer edges produced ordered superlattices, with septuple-layer spacing inversely related to MnTe supersaturation. When flow ceased, diffusive transport, Mn depletion within septuple layers, defect formation, and structural inversion increased.

The study establishes that closely spaced, Mn-complete septuple layers support antiferromagnetic ordering, whereas wider spacing and Mn-deficient layers produce ferromagnetic-like behavior. It identifies melt composition and flow dynamics as key controls on layer spacing, structural coherence, magnetic ordering, and the growth of magnetic topological materials.

A bank support worker warned that scammers at ATM galleries may ask customers to receive transfers and withdraw cash, claiming they have exceeded withdrawal limits. The transfers can originate from stolen phones or hacked accounts, leaving recipients’ accounts frozen, BVNs flagged, transactions blocked, and police reports or arrest memos issued. He cited an 18-year-old held at gunpoint and an adult asked to withdraw ₦50,000, both unaware they were receiving fraudulent funds. He advised people to refuse ATM transfer requests, even from friends or church members.

The study examines antiferromagnetic domain-wall dynamics driven by spin-orbit torque, motivated by AFMs’ lack of stray fields, robustness to moderate fields, and dynamics distinct from ferromagnets. It reviews possible optical, electrical, and current-induced manipulation and notes that spin-orbit torques can move antiferromagnetic walls faster than ferromagnetic walls.

The authors formulate a discrete spin-chain model with antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, perpendicular anisotropy, damping, and torque from injected polarized electrons. A continuum model based on tetramers compatible with a two-dimensional square lattice extends the nonlinear σ-model for the Néel vector with damping and torque. In this description, magnetization is proportional to \( \mathbf n \times \dot{\mathbf n} \). Numerical calculations use a 14,200-site lattice and are related to scaled continuum parameters and velocities.

For polarization along the perpendicular axis and no DM interaction, a static 180° wall evolves into a steady state in which all spins precess at constant frequency. A fixed spatial profile with uniform azimuthal precession yields damped dynamics whose asymptotic frequency is \( \omega=-\beta/\alpha \).

The paper also reports constant-speed wall propagation that is not simply a Lorentz-transformed static wall and, for polarization with both in-plane and perpendicular components, periodic motion between two wall positions. The framework explicitly includes damping-induced Lorentz-invariance breaking.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife re-approved Newhall Ranch’s plan after resolving concerns about greenhouse gas emissions and protection of the unarmored three spine stickleback, as directed by the 2015 Supreme Court review. Newhall Land revised its “Net Zero Newhall” emissions plan and proposed construction changes that avoid water contact, making its 2010 fish collection and relocation measures unnecessary. The Air Resources Board found an adequate basis that the revised project would produce no net additional emissions. The 15,000-acre, nine-phase project, if fully built, includes 12,000 homes and 11.5 million square feet of commercial and industrial space.

Young African entrepreneurs showcased technology-driven solutions at the 2017 Young Africa Works Summit to strengthen food security, create jobs and help agriculture withstand climate change. Rwanda’s Habona Ltd employs 25 young people to convert organic waste into cooking fuel and fertilizer, reducing open-fire emissions while producing 50 tonnes of fuel monthly. Malawi’s Bunda Female Students Organisation sponsors female science students who train poor women farmers in water conservation and drought- and flood-tolerant crops, reaching 360 farmers. Kenya’s UjuziKilimo developed a handheld soil sensor; extension agents relay crop and input recommendations to farmers by mobile phone, with plans to reach 200,000 farmers. U.N. Environment Programme coordinator Richard Munang said agriculture could reduce African poverty two to four times faster than other sectors and urged youth to engage across entire agricultural supply chains, including technology, logistics, clean energy, processing and market access.

Multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) comprises autosomal-dominant hereditary cancer syndromes involving two or more endocrine tumors. MEN1 is associated with inactivating MEN1 mutations; MEN2 with activating RET mutations and includes MEN2A, MEN2B, and familial medullary thyroid carcinoma; and MEN4 is associated with inactivating CDKN1B mutations and resembles MEN1 but has later onset and fewer gastrointestinal and pituitary tumors.

The study classified RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B variants reported in IndiGen, ClinVar, and Mastermind databases using ACMG/AMP guidelines and population-frequency, computational, literature, and clinical annotations. A total of 1,324 unique variants were classified, and the expanded MAPVar database contains 3,280 variants: 1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 variants of uncertain significance. MAPVar provides searchable variant details, population frequencies, computational predictions, and ACMG classifications.

IndiGen data identified two likely pathogenic RET variants, yielding an estimated carrier frequency of nearly 1 in 341 Indians. One variant was absent from 18 comparison datasets, while the other occurred at low frequencies elsewhere but at a higher frequency in IndiGen, with significant population differences. MAPVar searches identified seven relevant cases in the GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort, including four provisional MEN diagnoses and three suggestive of pheochromocytoma, with five unique variants detected.

A multiplex next-generation sequencing panel covering all coding regions of RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B was developed with 38 amplicons in two pools, spanning 65 kb and 33 exons. Testing of 72 endocrine-disorder patients resolved three cases with known pathogenic MEN1 variants. The authors concluded that MEN remains understudied in India, that RET-associated MEN appears prevalent, and that further Indian variant studies, particularly for CDKN1B, are needed.

On February 13, 2020, Tesla, Inc. entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to publicly offer 2,650,000 common shares. The underwriters received a 30-day option for 397,500 additional shares and exercised it in full on February 18. The offering closed February 19, generating net proceeds of approximately $2.31 billion after underwriting discounts, commissions, and estimated expenses. Certain security holders waived registration rights related to the offering. The Form 8-K, filed February 19, includes the underwriting agreement, waiver, legal opinion, consent, press release, and cover-page XBRL data.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, including $2.7 million in acquisition and core-system conversion charges. Assets rose $175.3 million to $1.8 billion, loans increased 14%, and non-interest income rose 38%.

The Supreme Court debated whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government may be sued for intentionally failing to deliver mail. The case arose from landlady Lebene Konan’s allegations that postal workers withheld mail as racial harassment, disrupting her rental business and causing emotional distress. A district court dismissed the suit, but the Fifth Circuit allowed claims against the Postal Service and United States to proceed. Justices examined the Federal Tort Claims Act’s “postal exception,” which shields the government from claims involving the “loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission” of mail. Some justices rejected the government’s broad reading of “loss,” while others worried that allowing Konan’s claim could produce a surge of litigation over delayed or intentionally mishandled mail. Konan’s attorney argued such long-term mistreatment is rare, and justices noted that intentional-nondelivery allegations would still face a high plausibility bar. A decision is expected by early July.

At the Silverbluff Audubon Center in remote Aiken County, South Carolina, a bald eagle pair has nested since 1994. Staff naturally support the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl, though they initially feared the birds would not appear on Sunday; one eventually took flight.

A compilation of November 20, 2001 reports centered on Enron’s financial and legal troubles. In a delayed SEC filing whose figures remained under review by Arthur Andersen, Enron widened its third-quarter loss to $664 million, or 87 cents per share, and said financial statements from 1997 through mid-2001 should no longer be relied upon after restatements reduced reported profits by $586 million.

A credit-rating downgrade triggered a $690 million partnership obligation due November 26 or 27 unless Enron repaid it, provided collateral or secured a waiver. Failure could allow the partnership’s Brazilian gas assets to be liquidated. A further downgrade below investment grade could trigger $3.9 billion in additional payments, including $2.4 billion owed by Osprey Trust and $915 million by Marlin Water Trust. Enron also warned of a possible $700 million pretax fourth-quarter loss and said adverse developments could jeopardize its ability to continue as a going concern. It sought lenders’ cooperation, additional financing, asset sales and the divestiture of $8 billion in non-core businesses.

Bankers feared Dynegy’s rescue merger could collapse if it invoked a “material adverse change” clause, while shareholder lawsuits created additional transaction risk. ChevronTexaco, a major Dynegy shareholder, provided financial support. Representative John Dingell requested a special investigation of Arthur Andersen’s audits of Enron and Waste Management.

Additional clippings covered ChevronTexaco’s expected merger savings, ConocoPhillips’ decision to base its combined company in Houston, executives declining severance, a law-firm mentoring program, ZipRealty’s hiring plans and other corporate and stock-market developments.

R. Thomas Beach of Crossborder Energy submitted rebuttal testimony on behalf of indicated electric generators in California Public Utilities Commission proceeding I. 99-07-003. He supports the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement and opposes SCGC/TURN’s Post-Interim Settlement Agreement because it would defer unbundling SoCalGas intrastate transmission.

Beach argues that PG&E and SoCalGas faced similar restrictions on competitive access, their backbone and local transmission systems are operationally comparable, and statewide consistency is increasingly important to electric generators operating across utility territories. He cites PG&E city-gate gas prices as providing savings of $0.05–$0.11 per Dth over border purchases plus backbone transportation and says the Comprehensive Settlement would lower electric-generator rates by about $3 million annually in 2002, or $0.01 per Dth.

He further contends that the settlement would reduce generator risks by assigning backbone cost recovery risk to SoCalGas, using embedded-cost rates and a defined load factor, lowering storage-service risk, and creating opportunities to purchase city-gate gas, balancing services, and storage. SCGC/TURN’s demand-charge analysis is criticized as based on unrealistic contracting and capacity assumptions. Beach states that interruptible service would raise annual fixed costs by only 0.6%, while excess transmission and storage capacity, capacity trading, and city-gate purchases would further mitigate demand charges. He also disputes claims that the settlement would cause plant closures, reliability problems, or a gas-and-electric price squeeze.

VOT targets Tibet on 11.510, 9.510, and 15.565 MHz and via ASIASAT 7 at 4146 MHz. It broadcasts 24/7 in alternating 30-minute Mandarin and Tibetan segments; shortwave frequencies require frequent retuning.

Radford University narrowed its Vice President for Student Affairs search to Thomas C. Segar and Ann Marie Klotz, who visited campus for forums on September 11 and 12, 2017. The position opened in spring 2017 when Irvin Clark left, and Susan Trageser has served as interim vice president. Segar, Shepherd University’s vice president with more than 26 years in student affairs, emphasized student success, belonging, social justice, experiential learning, strong student services, institutional pride, and proactive advising. Klotz, an NYIT dean since 2014, highlighted adaptability, mentorship, student-centered programming, Radford’s welcoming community, and using social media to promote the university’s story.

Four analysts favor Dariush over Evan Dunham, with three predicting unanimous decisions and one predicting a second-round submission. They cite Dariush’s superior all-around skill, grappling, and Dunham’s accumulated wear and fatigue.

Nick Kyrgios beat Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4, leveling Australia’s 2018 Davis Cup tie with Germany 1-1 after Alexander Zverev defeated Alex de Minaur in five sets. The tie resumes Saturday with doubles, followed Sunday by Kyrgios versus Zverev and, if needed, Struff against de Minaur.

As U.S.-North Korea tensions escalated over nuclear threats, global markets sold off amid renewed volatility. Jeffrey Saut of Raymond James said technical damage had been done, advised trimming positions, and expected a possible pullback, but maintained the secular bull market had six to eight years of upside. He considered war unlikely, warned conflict could push oil to $150 a barrel, and expected a shift toward earnings-driven growth. Chantico Global CEO Gina Sanchez forecast heightened volatility.

The article addresses the gap between institutional commitments to global education and low student participation in study abroad, noting that only about one percent of students enrolled in U.S. higher education participate. Although virtual, collaborative, and globally oriented coursework can provide more accessible alternatives, international travel offers distinctive benefits for intercultural understanding, language development, leadership, cross-cultural communication, and personal and professional growth. Financial costs, logistical complexity, and the lack of replicable planning frameworks remain major barriers to expanding sustainable programs.

Drawing on more than two decades of experience designing programs and advising institutions across six continents, the authors present a methodology for building education-abroad business models. The central premise is that curricular, operational, and financial logistics are interdependent and should be considered together, while learning outcomes should remain the primary basis for program design.

Curricular logistics include defining measurable learning outcomes; deciding whether participation is elective or required; determining credit amounts and whether credit is earned before, during, or after travel; and incorporating assessment, reflection, and learning consolidation. Programs must also consider alignment with host-institution priorities, competition with existing offerings, appropriate locations, risks, daily activities, engagement modalities, and duration. Activities may include academic coursework, site visits, research, service learning, and entrepreneurial design-build projects, with lengths ranging from one to ten days to semester-long programs.

Operational logistics involve assigning decision-making and coordination responsibilities and compensating faculty, staff, students, and external partners. Programs require comprehensive risk management covering student safety, insurance, emergency response, legal protections, data security, and institutional reputation. Faculty leadership is generally preferred for academically rigorous programs because it supports academic integrity and continuity, often with a co-leader for contingency coverage. Additional planning considerations include travel timing, organization, flights, lodging, partner coordination, local transportation, communications, meals, entertainment, emergency preparation, student orientation, student well-being, and access to ongoing support.

Financial logistics require program expenditures to remain at or below generated income. Major costs include faculty and staff time, external services, projects, and coordination. Potential income comes from student tuition, program fees, internal funding, scholarships, government grants, endowments, and corporate sponsorships. Student fees generally flow directly to a program and are often more efficient than tuition returns. Funding should be sought after total expenses are calculated, and internal funding may be distributed broadly or offered as need- or merit-based scholarships.

The article identifies twelve business models based on a review of two journals and fourteen interviews with faculty, staff, and students. These fall within three broad categories: external-party-led programs, faculty-led programs, and student-led programs. External organizations may manage all curricular and operational work and charge a comprehensive student fee, reducing faculty burden but increasing costs and potentially limiting access. Faculty-led programs can use student payments, program-generated revenue, corporate donations, or grants as primary revenue drivers. Student-led programs, often organized through clubs and generally non-credit, typically rely on charitable donations, student activity fees, and corporate sponsorships. The models are presented as adaptable and combinable rather than fixed.

The article concludes that sustainable global learning programs require careful alignment of each program’s learning objectives, destination, activities, risks, constraints, and resources with an appropriate business model. Corporate support, community-engagement revenue, dedicated staff, and selective delegation to students can reduce financial and logistical burdens while supporting broader access, educational value, and program longevity.

Mouse research suggests black tea may aid health and weight loss by increasing gut microbes linked to lean mass and reducing those linked to obesity. Both teas are prebiotics, while green tea also acts in the liver, so a combination may be helpful.

Microsoft Corporation reported on July 8, 2021 that it will redeem all €1.75 billion of its 2.125% Notes due December 6, 2021, on September 6, 2021. The redemption price will equal the outstanding principal plus accrued and unpaid interest through, but excluding, the redemption date. The filing is not the formal notice; noteholders should consult the trustee’s notice.

Police accused Parker Hogan of causing or aiding roommate Michael Buskey’s suicide, including directing how he held the gun and removing a phone afterward. Buskey, 19, was found dead May 8. Hogan pleaded not guilty, posted bail, and faces a July court date.

The goalie adjusted against Zdeno on the first power play, then chose to leave the bigger opponent alone. He called the low-space game exciting, praised Timmy’s early saves and Tico’s goal, and expected overtime. He emphasized hard practice, hard play, and fundamentals after layoffs. The team took the win in a seven-game series and planned to focus on Saturday.
Jacob Allen sued Richard Knight and Hannah, executrix of Hope Allen’s estate, for about £64; the jury awarded his portion and 41s. 5d. costs.

Officials marked the completion of the 179-megawatt Switch Station 1 and 2 solar projects at Apex Industrial Park north of Las Vegas. Commissioned Dec. 11, 2017, the arrays supply Switch data centers in Reno and Las Vegas and are designed to generate enough electricity for 46,000 Nevada homes. Their completion brings Nevada’s solar plant total to 16.

The telegram assesses Andropov’s foreign policy as essentially unchanged from Brezhnev’s, maintaining a hard line on Afghanistan, Poland, and Southern Africa while prioritizing relations with the United States. It recommends greater emphasis on arms control to reduce the risk of nuclear war, improve U.S.–Soviet relations, and counter Soviet exploitation of perceived Western weaknesses. The U.S. zero-zero INF negotiating position is viewed as nearing the end of its usefulness and should be changed. The telegram says Moscow seeks to block U.S. INF deployments without reducing Soviet forces, using moderate concessions and propaganda to influence European public opinion and blame U.S. rigidity. Without an early U.S. response, the NATO deployment schedule may be endangered. Historically, deploying GLCMs and Pershing-IIs was primarily a political decision to reassure Europe of U.S. nuclear protection; the 572-warhead limit was intended to balance Soviet SS-20 capabilities with U.S. credibility rather than reflect a sacrosanct numerical target.

**Summary**

This article (Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education–TOJDE, July 2024, Vol. 25, No. 3, Art. 13226; authors Serap Ugur, Gokhan Deniz Dincer, Didem Pasaoglu Bas) examines how advanced technologies used in the digitalization of higher education institutions offering distance education services will change managerial contexts, in order to make future predictions and provide a roadmap.

The literature review establishes that technology affects organizational work, structure and management, with Perrow's work on the relationship between organization and technology serving as the theoretical basis. It reviews artificial intelligence (from its 1956 Dartmouth coinage through artificial general intelligence, superintelligence and technological singularity), wearable technologies and the metaverse, brain–computer interfaces and the Neuralink project, and blockchain applications such as ECTS credit transfer, micro-credentials via Ethereum smart contracts, and integration of IoT, AI, VR and AR into open and distance learning. It also notes that Business Education must adopt new technologies to remain relevant and prepare students for changing labor-market demands.

The study uses a qualitative case-study design. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with four academics at Anadolu University with at least 20 years' experience in open and distance education and 10 years in distance education management; transcripts totaled 2,442 words. Researcher triangulation, content analysis (Braun and Clarke; George) and Nvivo 1.7.1 were used for validity and coding.

Findings on three questions: (1) Advanced technologies will significantly affect educational environments and require organizations to adapt and reorganize; they entail high initial investment but long-term savings; AI must be continually trained with accurate, current data; participants noted distrust of unmanned systems, AI's future presence at all management levels, augmented reality for practice/internship departments, blockchain for control and recognition of prior learning, a shift from hierarchical to horizontal/network structures, displacement of non-tech-adaptable employees by knowledge workers, customized learning experiences and AI assistants, brain chips for prior-learning recognition, and universities repositioning around assessment and evaluation. (2) Economically, careful cost–benefit analysis before integration is required, and technology should not be adopted merely for fashion; unemployment and loss of entry-level white-collar jobs are expected, while productivity, profits, exports and new business areas and human-resource needs increase, alongside new infrastructure costs. Cited literature projects AI adding roughly 14 percent to global GDP (about USD 15.7 trillion) by 2030 (PwC) and doubling global economic growth by 2035 (Accenture). (3) Socio-culturally, both benefits and harms appear: laziness, dependency and screen-time increases, alongside calls for technology literacy training; a collectivist and feminine culture is said to be unprepared for AI; virtual addiction and psychological/biological problems are anticipated; and a "meta-culture" of people existing in both physical and virtual worlds will emerge, requiring studies on rights, legal and ethical regulation.

Conclusions identify education and management as the main themes, with educational dimensions (technology, processes, services, content) and managerial dimensions (management, employment, economy, culture). Recommendations include developing and testing AI assistants and managers, blockchain-based certification and recognition applications, adaptive synthetic content, new teaching systems and virtual selves for the metaverse, and further research on brain–computer interfaces and brain chips, supported by larger-scale qualitative and quantitative studies across geographies and institutions.

KGI Securities’ Ming-Chi Kuo expects cellular and non-cellular Series 3 models in 38mm and 42mm sizes with LTE-only connectivity, likely launching this fall alongside new iPhones. Annual Apple Watch sales are forecast at 17.5–18 million, including 2.8–3.6 million LTE units.

The continuation application describes neural-modulation systems and methods, particularly spinal cord stimulation, that shape electrical fields through electrode current fractionalization. Systems include leads, electrodes, a modulation generator, and a programming interface that calculates anodic and cathodic current percentages from target multipoles. Progressively stacking target poles on opposing sides of a center creates a broad linear electric field that is stronger and wider than a conventional bipole field while reducing the voltage gradient associated with dorsal-column activation, potentially favoring dorsal-horn or dorsal-root modulation and sub-perception pain therapy.

The passage reviews spinal cord anatomy, conventional dorsal-column stimulation, associated paresthesia, and differing neural responses to electrical modulation. It also describes electrode calibration, directional electrodes, forward and inverse modeling, transfer matrices, and least-squares solutions for mapping desired fields to electrode polarities and current distributions. Programming features include user-defined anatomical or pain regions, angle, focus, spread, and gradient controls, automatic target movement, and search heuristics for optimizing field geometry and strength. Implementations may use percutaneous, paddle, multiple, staggered, or directional leads, implantable generators, external trial systems, and clinician or patient controls.

On June 14, 2001, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York granted DOCS’s motion to dismiss John Bryant’s claims against the New York State Department of Correctional Services and Sing Sing Correctional Facility, and directed dismissal of those defendants on the court’s own initiative.

Bryant’s § 1983 complaint arose from a Code Blue lockdown at Sing Sing lasting at least twenty days after Officer Hanser Hernandez falsely reported that ammunition had been found. Bryant alleged that inmates’ cells were searched, their mail and property were disregarded, and they were denied showers, recreation, library access, telephone and mail privileges, hot meals, clean linen, religious services, and routine medical and dental care. He also alleged violations of state labor laws due to inadequate inmate compensation and the inability to bargain collectively.

The court held that DOCS and Sing Sing were arms of New York State and were therefore entitled to Eleventh Amendment immunity. Because New York had not consented to federal suit and Congress had not abrogated its immunity through § 1983, the court lacked subject matter jurisdiction over claims against those entities. Bryant’s claims against Hernandez in his individual capacity could proceed if proper service was made. Bryant was required to report the status of service by June 29, 2001.

A Senate committee issued 50 recommendations for rethinking Canada’s criminal justice system, rejecting rigid trial deadlines. Senators warned tens of thousands of charges could be dismissed under the Supreme Court’s Jordan ruling.

The Government is consulting on reforms to hold directors accountable following major insolvencies such as Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to recover money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling companies and expanding Insolvency Service powers. The measures aim to prevent directors from avoiding consequences or profiting from failures while workers, suppliers and taxpayers bear losses.

The Grand River Conservation Authority will spend $1.8 million over five years to use LiDAR to create digital, three-dimensional maps of most floodplains along the Speed and Conestogo rivers and the entire Grand River floodplain. Integrated with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers forecasting software, the maps will support near-real-time forecasts and identify downstream areas and properties at risk. The project will replace hard-copy maps, some more than 40 years old, and capture riverbed features and changes over time. It was underway before June’s unexpected rainfall.

Engineers developed a rapid, nonlethal optical method for screening the crystalline structure of natural and synthetic proteins as they flow past individually. Using femtosecond and picosecond lasers with time-domain thermo-transmission, the method measures crystallinity in milliseconds before heating alters the structure and can analyze proteins inside living cells. The proof-of-concept work included synthetic strands adapted from water-resistant squid ring teeth proteins. A DURIP grant will support scaling up the high-throughput system, which was also backed by the Army Research Office.

The paper proposes a time-based method for a trusting agent to assess the probability of failure before interacting with a probable trusted agent in a digital business ecosystem. Interaction risk depends on both the likelihood and consequences of failure.

The proposed “FailureLevel” metric represents an agent’s probable inability to satisfy the interaction criteria. Risk is treated as dynamic, so the analysis period is divided into non-overlapping time slots, with a FailureLevel determined for each slot. Previous FailureLevels (PFL) cover the pre-interaction period; Future FailureLevels (FFL) cover the interaction period.

PFL is derived from past interaction histories or recommendations from other agents. Recommendations are filtered by trustworthiness, timing, and relevance to the intended interaction criteria, weighted according to recommender trustworthiness and recency, then combined with criterion significance to produce a crisp FailureLevel. FFL is predicted from accumulated FailureLevels using a Gaussian distribution, yielding probabilities for failure levels 0–5 rather than a single value. For each post-interaction slot, the most probable level is selected as the agent’s FailureLevel.

An example compares two logistics agents, B and D, for a one-week shipment valued at $20,000, showing how their failure probabilities can be estimated from three prior weekly FailureLevels. The method supports agent selection, while determining consequences of failure remains future work.

Cincinnati's 38-30 win over 14th-ranked Iowa State in week 6 handed the Cyclones their first defeat of the season and ended their unbeaten run, as the Bearcats built a 31-7 halftime lead that Iowa State's comeback never overcame. The result opens the Big 12 race, echoing last season's chaos, when BYU and Arizona State tied with Iowa State and Deion Sanders' team for the regular-season title while Kansas State (5-4 in conference), Oklahoma State (no conference wins) and Utah fell short. The piece also headlines Alabama–Vanderbilt, Arch Manning dropping out of ESPN's top 40 quarterbacks, Clemson's record-worst start, Texas's playoff doubts and Penn State's hopes after an Oregon loss. Author Calvin Barrett writes freelance for The Sporting News.

Children get more ice time when NHL players are not skating, which they enjoy. Before a “must-win” game against Detroit, the team will focus on responsibilities, review defensive tapes, avoid giving up shots, and improve play along the boards. Players see the Cup chance as once in a lifetime, while Detroit’s strong lines make matchups less important.

A memorial football match for Kirkcaldy Raith fan Aidan Sutherland, who died from diabetes complications shortly after turning 20, will be held at Stark’s Park on Sunday. Organised by his friend Ben Graham, it will raise awareness of diabetes and donate to the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation. Friends, former teammates and players including Colin Cameron and Darren Dods will participate in a day of family activities. Kick-off is at 1pm.

The study examines inclusive education for students with disabilities in Kazakhstan, focusing on distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic. It reviews Kazakhstan’s inclusive-education targets, UNESCO’s three dimensions of inclusion, disability-rights requirements, and the challenges and opportunities of technology-based distance learning.

A qualitative case study used online, semi-structured interviews with ten special education teachers from Kazakhstan. Interviews lasted approximately 30–35 minutes and were analyzed thematically. Teachers reported using online lessons, videos, homework review, online activities, and mobile applications. Seven teachers preferred formal education, two considered both formats similar, and one favored distance education. Six teachers considered distance education insufficient for meeting students’ individual needs. Reported family-participation barriers included anxiety, inadequate technology, poor communication, and insufficient online family education. Teacher-student and peer interaction was also viewed as weak, limited by time, and sometimes unqualified or disorganized.

The study recommends diversifying technology-based teaching methods and infrastructure, creating content tailored to students’ individual needs, organizing online seminars to support families, and providing regular social activities and technology-supported programs to strengthen teacher-student and peer interaction.

Players say difficult conversations and learning from setbacks promote improvement. They emphasize discipline, emotional control and depth, with four lines and six defensemen contributing at this stage. Despite injuries, teammates have stepped up, including Fabbri, as the team returns home to show fans what it can do.

This preprint study examined the relationship between Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and epilepsy using transcriptomic data from the Knight ADRC, Mount Sinai Brain Bank, and ROSMAP cohorts. It analyzed a severe AD molecular profile characterized by synaptic plasticity dysfunction, more severe neurodegeneration, astrogliosis, cognitive decline, and shorter survival. Differential-expression, pathway-enrichment, and cell-proportion analyses found that AD, particularly the synaptic plasticity dysfunction profile, shares molecular features with epilepsy.

Of 105 epilepsy-associated genes examined, 16 were dysregulated across all three cohorts. Fifteen were consistently downregulated, including synaptic and ion-channel genes such as ARHGEF9, GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, NECAP1, SCN1A, and SCN8A; only CERS1 was consistently upregulated. Nine shared genes were predominantly synaptic and highly expressed in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons. The AD profile was enriched in glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, ion-channel, synaptic-transmission, and related pathways.

ROSMAP analyses showed concordant dysregulation of 25 epilepsy-associated genes in early and late AD, with larger effects at later stages. Overall, the findings support a bidirectional association between epilepsy and AD and suggest shared abnormalities in synaptic, neurotransmitter, and neuronal-excitability pathways. They also suggest that epilepsy-related mechanisms may precede or coincide with early AD pathology, while AD pathology may increase seizure susceptibility. The order and timing of the two conditions remain uncertain, and the findings identify potential shared genetic vulnerabilities and targets for stratified or personalized treatment.

Uranium’s recent decline is viewed as a correction rather than a collapse, with the Global X Uranium ETF (URA) suggesting prices remain above the November 2016 floor. Analysts cited were generally bullish, citing expected demand growth and expanding nuclear capacity. The World Nuclear Association reported about 440 reactors operating in 31 countries and Taiwan, over 160 planned and more than 300 proposed. Dundee Capital Markets’ David Talbot forecast 6% annual uranium-demand growth through 2020, while Morningstar’s David Wang expected prices around $65 per pound by 2019. Negative sentiment, intensified after Fukushima, may continue to obscure fundamentals.

Technically, URA showed short-term weakness and possible oversold conditions, but seasonal patterns favor stronger April and spring prices toward a July high. Key support was near the April low and $14.40, with the 200-day moving average as a possible lower support. The article presents URA as the easiest uranium investment route, with options also available, while noting technical risks and the need for the April low to hold.

The President bids farewell as authority passes to his successor after half a century of public service. He expresses gratitude for cooperation with Congress, wishes the incoming administration success, and urges continued agreement between Congress and the President on major national issues.

Despite four major wars during the century, the passage describes America as strong and influential, while stressing that its leadership depends on using its power to promote world peace and human improvement. The global conflict presents a prolonged ideological threat requiring sustained sacrifice, steady effort, and a commitment to liberty. Government policy must balance national security, public and private economic activity, costs and benefits, present needs and future welfare, and national responsibilities against individual liberties.

The permanent military establishment and vast armaments industry are necessary for security but create a risk that the military-industrial complex could gain improper influence and endanger democratic institutions. An informed citizenry must preserve the proper balance between defense and liberty. Similarly, the technological revolution has made research increasingly dependent on federal funding and organized scientific institutions, creating dangers both of excessive government control over scholars and of policy becoming captive to a scientific-technological elite. Statesmanship must integrate these forces within democratic principles.

The nation must also avoid exhausting future resources for present convenience, protecting not only material assets but also the political and spiritual inheritance of future generations. Internationally, America should pursue mutual trust, equality, disarmament, and peaceful resolution of differences rather than war. Although peace has been avoided and progress achieved, much remains undone, and the President vows to continue supporting that effort as a private citizen.

He closes by thanking the American people, reaffirming devotion to principle and the national goals, and expressing a prayer for freedom, justice, opportunity, charity, and a world united by mutual respect and love.

The Tax Court held that gifts made by personal check were not complete when the checks were delivered to the donees in December 1980, but became complete when the bank paid them in January 1981. The relation-back doctrine, previously applied to charitable gifts, was not extended to these noncharitable gifts because the estate had not proven unconditional delivery, intent to gift, or sufficient funds in the account. The unexplained 35-day delay before payment also cast doubt on the checks’ unconditional delivery.

Under Oklahoma law, a check was not itself an assignment of funds, the bank was not liable until it accepted the check, and the donees could not assert rights as holders in due course because they gave no consideration. The donor therefore retained dominion and control and could have stopped payment. The court concluded that Oklahoma would treat a donor’s personal check as merely a promise to give until payment or bank acceptance.

The gifts consequently qualified as 1981 gifts, were ineligible for the $3,000 annual exclusion, and the entire $36,000 was included in the decedent’s estate. The stipulated consequences were that the six-year estate-tax assessment period applied and the estate-tax deficiency was not time-barred. The determined deficiencies were $70,841.04 in gift tax, a $17,710.26 addition to tax, and $369,644.05 in estate tax.

The passage details NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture, its GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs, and related data-center and professional products.

Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity applies a 2:4 non-zero pattern after dense training, followed by fine-tuning. Tests across numerous vision, detection, segmentation, language, and translation networks showed virtually no inference-accuracy loss, while compressing weights and bandwidth requirements by half and doubling Tensor Core math throughput through zero-skipping operations. DLSS uses neural networks and multiple frames to improve image quality and performance; third-generation Tensor Cores and 9x Super Resolution make 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible.

GA10x supports GDDR6X memory developed with Micron. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling, MTA encoding, and new training and equalization methods to achieve data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec, more than 52% above the TU102 GPU in the RTX 2080 Ti. NVIDIA RTX IO, combined with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, moves compressed assets directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU for GPU-based lossless decompression. It can accelerate I/O by up to 100x versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs, offload work from dozens of CPU cores, reduce game loading times and stutter, and improve frame rates and texture streaming.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI-training throughput of the Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, PCIe Gen4, display outputs, virtualization support, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

GA10x GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with Display Stream Compression, including 8K60 and 4K120 output and support for two 8K60 displays. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x supports AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR with substantially lower CPU usage than software decoding. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC while offloading work from the CPU and graphics engine.

The architecture provides up to twice the performance of the prior generation in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance, adds ray-traced motion-blur acceleration, and supports concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute.

The GeForce RTX 3090 has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores. The RTX 3070 supports the GA104 architecture and GDDR6X but uses GDDR6 and lacks NVLink. GDDR6X also adds Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transactions and retries them to improve overclocking reliability and indicate when performance is limited by memory errors.

The GA102-based RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 48 GB of GDDR6 memory expandable to 96 GB via NVLink, second- and next-generation RT Cores, hardware-accelerated motion blur, AI denoising, and professional display, virtualization, and certification features. The publication concludes with standard NVIDIA disclaimers concerning specification accuracy, warranties, liability, licensing, product suitability, and changes to products and services.

A WIRED article rounds up discounted toys available before Amazon Prime Day ends, aimed at holiday shoppers. Featured deals include Squishmallows 20-inch Diane Peach Bigfoot Plush (more than half off), the 5-inch Austin the Avocado Plush for $5 ($5 off), and the 12-inch Maui the Pineapple Plush for $9 ($8 off); Magna-Tiles 32-piece sets reduced from $50 to $35; and a retired Lego Icons Dried Flower Centerpiece set with gerbera daisies, roses, and sugarcane plastic, available only from third-party merchants. Other items mentioned are a Play-Doh trove, a Lego build with a skeleton minifigure, a 60-piece colorful construction pack, blind boxes, a Melissa & Doug Wooden Scoop and Serve Ice Cream Counter for $36 ($35 off), a Crayola Color Wonder Magic Light Brush Station for $16 ($16 off), and a Blue Marble National Geographic Rock Tumbler Kit for $52 ($13 off). The article notes that featured products are independently selected by editors and that compensation may be received from retailers or purchases.

This prospective observational study of 103 cerebral cavernous malformation patients, including 42 followed for four years, evaluated five SNPs in PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A alongside plasma cytokines to identify markers of symptomatic disease. PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC genotypes were more frequent in asymptomatic patients and were associated with altered cytokine levels. A weighted model combining PTPN2rs72872125 CC genotype and GM-CSF differentiated symptomatic from asymptomatic patients with an AUC of 0.663, 41.3% sensitivity, and 85.7% specificity. During follow-up, FCGR2Ars1801274 GG was associated with symptomatic events, with AUCs of 0.796 and 0.875 before and after propensity matching. In silico analysis identified an H131R substitution in a region conserved mainly in higher primates. VDRrs731236 AA was associated with later symptom onset, whereas VDRrs11568820 CC was associated with earlier onset. The authors proposed that inflammatory and immune mechanisms may contribute to aggressive CCM behavior.

The passage presents a coupled transport–mechanics model for the growth of individual methane bubbles in fine-grained aquatic mud. Treating post-pore-scale bubbles as Mode I tensile cracks under Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics, the model simulates initial elastic cavity expansion followed by localized sediment fracturing. In a symmetric half-domain, a penny-shaped seed with an initial radius of 4 mm grows through diffusion-fed dissolved methane until it forms an inverted tear-drop bubble with a closed tail.

A finite-element model implemented in COMSOL solves aqueous methane conservation and sediment force equilibrium, including overburden and gravitational loading. Diffusive methane flux supplies the bubble; Henry’s law and the ideal gas law determine gas concentration and internal pressure, which drives elastic expansion. Mode I stress intensity factors are calculated using displacement/stress extrapolation, while crack direction and front increments follow the strain-energy-density criterion. Fracturing occurs when the maximum stress intensity factor exceeds the sediment’s fracture toughness.

The simulations use PARDISO, refined tetrahedral meshes, and mesh deformation and remeshing. Numerical bubble shapes and sizes agree with analytical solutions across tested fracture toughness values; lower toughness produces smaller, flatter bubbles, while higher toughness produces larger, more inflated bubbles. The model is limited to individual bubbles, and upscaling bubble behavior into effective properties of gassy muds remains unresolved.

Amazon received a patent for a delivery-drone “directed fragmentation” system intended to prevent catastrophic failures from causing uncontrolled crashes. It would continually update a fragmentation sequence based on flight path, weather, and terrain, then release components in a calculated order to alter the drone’s weight, drag, momentum, and trajectory. Parts could be jettisoned over suitable areas using latches, hooks, springs, explosive charges, or compressed gas. The sequence would consider component cost, weight, drag, and function and could respond to extreme weather or battery, rotor, flight-control, or sensor failures. The patent does not guarantee deployment.

The literature review frames diagnosing student learning problems as observing students’ performances during cognitively aligned teaching activities and identifying reasons learning objectives are not met. Collaborative inquiry supports diagnosis through collaborative lesson preparation, classroom observation, evidence collection, post-lesson analysis, and instructional adjustment. Teacher education students require training because untrained observers often focus on teachers rather than documenting specific student performances. Panoramic cameras can supplement observation records by capturing wide-angle video and audio, enabling reviewers to examine different viewing angles, specific students, worksheets, and group discussions.

The study implemented a semester-long “Professional Teaching Practicum” with 22 teacher education students in five groups. A five-week preparation stage covered collaborative inquiry, lesson planning, behavioral observation, analysis, and panoramic-camera operation. During a 12-week second stage, teams of four or five alternated teaching and observation roles in paired junior high school classrooms over four three-week cycles. Observers recorded student responses to each activity and used panoramic footage as supplementary evidence. Teachers then compared student performance with their instruction, discussed learning difficulties, reflected, and revised their lesson plans.

Data were collected through 76 observation reports, evaluated with a three-level diagnostic rubric, and a 12-item questionnaire measuring perceived capabilities in lesson preparation, connecting observation to instruction, and adjusting plans after discussion. Diagnostic observation scores improved across the four cycles, from an average of approximately 0.47 to above 1.88 out of 2. Questionnaire post-test results were significantly higher for all three capability areas, with reported Z-values of −4.025, −3.535, and −3.536 and p-values below 0.05. The researcher concluded that the course and its collaborative, camera-supported observation model were feasible and improved participants’ diagnostic and perceived instructional-design abilities. A remaining limitation was that participants’ limited teaching experience made it difficult to determine whether their proposed instructional adjustments actually improved student learning.

Major social media networks are strengthening moderation policies, adding staff, and redesigning algorithms to address hate speech, extremism, fake news, and other violations. A.I. can identify offensive text in multiple languages and recognize prohibited images or symbols, but it is not foolproof. It may misinterpret context, evolve with language, reproduce biases in human-created training data, and fail to determine intent, as seen in Facebook’s removal of anti-hate posts and mislabeling of images. Such errors can spread when developers share training datasets. A.I. therefore serves mainly as an initial screening and prioritization tool rather than a fully automated moderator. It can help human reviewers work faster and at greater scale, including identifying suicide-risk posts and alerting emergency responders, while Facebook has doubled its review team to 20,000. Overall, A.I. is making moderation more efficient, but human judgment remains necessary, and technology is advancing faster than ethics and policy can respond.

The message presents the United States as a stable, peaceful government after sixty years and stresses Congress’s duty to preserve its free institutions, honor treaties, and maintain neutrality. It reports improved relations with France, reciprocal British navigation privileges, a convention negotiated to satisfy American claims against Brazil, separate treaties with Central American states, and continued friendship with Mexico under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo. The government stopped American assistance to a German war steamer to uphold neutrality and treaty commitments and ended its Frankfort mission because no German Empire had been definitively constituted. It suppressed an expedition against Cuba, secured the return of an allegedly abducted foreigner, and recommended legislation against abduction. The United States did not intervene in the Austrian-Hungarian conflict but was prepared to recognize an independent Hungary. Portuguese claims against the United States remained unsettled and were to be submitted to Congress in a special message.

Further recommendations included strengthening laws against the African slave trade, particularly misuse of sea letters, while preserving lawful shipping and property transfers; supporting a Nicaraguan canal under multinational guarantees and private enterprise without a federal appropriation; considering Tehuantepec and Panama transportation routes; and maintaining the independence of the Sandwich Islands. The government also sought friendly relations and offered mediation among American states as Pacific commerce expanded.

The boundary survey between the United States and Mexico was underway but required additional funding and possibly government counsel. Complaints over Panamanian mail transportation were presented to New Granada, while the end of Venezuela’s civil war created an opportunity to redress American grievances.

Treasury receipts for the past fiscal year totaled $59,663,097.50, while expenditures reached $57,631,667.82. Projected deficits were $5,828,121.66 for July 1850 and $10,547,092.73 for July 1851. The message recommended borrowing to cover the deficit, strict economy, tariff revision based on specific duties to increase revenue and support domestic industry, modification of the subtreasury system, and establishment of an agricultural bureau.

California had formed a constitution and was expected to seek admission, while New Mexico was expected to do likewise. Recommendations included expanding customs facilities, conducting coastal surveys, extending Indian agencies, establishing a California branch mint, examining land titles, surveying public lands, conducting geological and mineralogical explorations, and first surveying proposed railroad routes from the Atlantic or Gulf to the Pacific. Congress was also urged to fund river and harbor improvements, increase Army forces at western posts, improve Army retirement provisions, reorganize the Navy, and establish a retired list for disabled officers.

Further measures included revising postal laws for California and Oregon, reducing single-letter postage to five cents, financing congressional franking through the Treasury, implementing the British postal treaty, and completing the census. Congress was urged to protect the District of Columbia and respect the constitutional separation among legislative, executive, and judicial powers, using the veto only in extraordinary circumstances. The message concluded by emphasizing representative independence and the preservation of the Union as essential to national happiness and future generations.

Connecticut municipal lobbyists asked Gov. Dannel Malloy to ease financial pressures on towns and cities by reducing costly mandates, allowing local cost-control reforms, revising pensions and arbitration rules, retaining more land-transfer fees, removing barriers to service sharing, and adjusting prevailing-wage requirements. Malloy called the session with COST and CCM leaders productive and said the six-week budget stalemate is making work harder. Lawmakers are addressing an estimated $3.5 billion deficit after $1.5 billion in union concessions, while municipal pension plans and small-town cost pressures have been overlooked. Senate President Pro Tempore Martin Looney also disputed lobbyists’ statements about seeking continued municipal aid.
