The application discloses a method and system for digitally planning orthodontic treatment and manufacturing orthodontic appliances. The process measures a patient’s tooth positions, receives tooth-movement constraints and diagnostic settings, diagnoses malocclusions, and generates multiple branched treatment plans. Branches may address open bite, posterior crossbite, bi-protrusion, molar and canine class II or III relationships, and overjet, with possible bicuspid or anterior extraction and interproximal reduction. Interim and final tooth positions are calculated and adjusted for each branch, after which a dental professional may select a plan.

For the selected plan, incremental treatment stages, appliance models, and fabrication instructions are generated. The appliances are removable tooth-repositioning shells that progressively move teeth toward a target arrangement and may include attachments, auxiliary components, varied thickness, stiffness, or material composition, and overcorrection. Appliance geometry and force systems may be analyzed and iteratively modified through digital or biomechanical simulation.

Fabrication may use direct methods such as stereolithography, selective laser sintering, fused-deposition modeling, material jetting, continuous direct fabrication, and multi-material fabrication; indirect thermoforming over a mold; or combinations thereof. The disclosed system can include processors, storage, scanners, and a connected fabrication machine.

This retrospective French study evaluated COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in 112 hospitalized patients with hematological malignancies between May 2020 and April 2021. All received four ABO-compatible units. Ninety-day overall survival was 64.9% overall: 77.5% for B-lymphoid neoplasms, 20% for myeloid neoplasms, and 36.8% for plasma-cell neoplasms. By day 7, temperature and inflammatory markers decreased and PCR cycle thresholds increased. Adverse events were uncommon.

A propensity-weighted comparison of 81 CCP-treated B-cell neoplasm patients with 120 untreated patients focused on anti-CD20-pretreated patients alive 16 days after hospitalization. CCP was associated with a 63% reduction in death risk (95% CI 31%–80%); sensitivity analyses estimated reductions of 40%–63%. Older age, hypertension, and COVID-19 severity were associated with poorer survival.

The authors considered CCP promising, particularly for B-cell-depleted patients unable to mount a humoral response. However, the nonrandomized retrospective design limited causal conclusions, viral strains were not assessed, and no patients were vaccinated.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018 (Commission File No. 001-34756), reporting as a large accelerated filer with 171,732,775 shares of common stock outstanding as of October 26, 2018. The filing includes a forward-looking statements disclaimer and unaudited consolidated financial statements, MD&A, risk factors, legal proceedings, and other items.

Balance sheet: Total assets were $29.26 billion at September 30, 2018 versus $28.66 billion at December 31, 2017. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.97 billion, inventory $3.31 billion (up from $2.26 billion), property, plant and equipment $11.25 billion, and solar energy systems leased and to be leased $6.30 billion. Total liabilities were $23.41 billion, redeemable noncontrolling interests $551.3 million, and total stockholders' equity $4.51 billion.

Results of operations: Total revenues were $6.82 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2018 ($6.10 billion automotive, $399.3 million energy generation and storage, $326.3 million services and other) versus $2.98 billion a year earlier; nine-month revenues were $14.24 billion versus $8.47 billion. Gross profit was $1.52 billion for the quarter and $2.60 billion for the nine months. Operating income was $416.8 million for the quarter versus a $535.5 million loss a year earlier, while the nine months produced an $801.6 million operating loss. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $311.5 million for the quarter ($1.82 basic, $1.75 diluted per share) versus a $619.4 million loss a year earlier; the nine months resulted in a $1.12 billion net loss ($6.56 per share) versus a $1.29 billion loss. Noncontrolling interests absorbed net losses of $157.1 million for the nine months. Deferred revenue on automotive sales totaled $761.5 million at period end, with $284.7 million expected to be recognized within 12 months.

Cash flows: For the nine months ended September 30, 2018, operating activities provided $863.2 million of cash (versus $570.5 million used in 2017), investing activities used $1.97 billion, and financing activities provided $686.1 million; cash and restricted cash decreased $442.0 million to $3.52 billion.

Accounting policies: On January 1, 2018 the company adopted ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) using the modified retrospective method, recording a $623.2 million decrease to beginning accumulated deficit. Vehicle sales with resale value guarantees are generally now recognized as sales with a right of return upon delivery rather than as operating leases or collateralized borrowings; two international/partner programs continue to be accounted for as operating leases and interest-bearing collateralized borrowings, respectively. Automotive regulatory credit sales are recognized as automotive revenue. Energy generation and storage revenue is recognized on delivery for residential/small commercial sales and over time using percentage-of-completion for large commercial and utility-scale projects, with solar leases and power purchase agreements accounted for as operating leases. Restricted cash and ASU 2016-18 were also adopted in 2018, combining restricted and unrestricted cash in the cash flow statements.

Notes disclosures: Intangible assets totaled $291.5 million, including $47.0 million of indefinite-lived SolarCity IPR&D, for which a $13.3 million abandonment loss was recognized in the second quarter and remaining work is expected to complete in the fourth quarter of 2018. Money market funds ($1.47 billion) were Level I and interest rate swaps ($17.6 million) Level II, with no level transfers in the period. Inventory write-downs were $54.3 million for the nine months. Property, plant and equipment includes construction in progress for Gigafactory 1 and 2, with $604.1 million and $649.5 million respectively transferred to land and buildings during the period, plus $1.14 billion cumulatively capitalized under the Panasonic production equipment arrangement. Accrued warranty was $644.5 million at period end. Customer deposits were $905.8 million.

Debt: Total debt was $10.90 billion ($7.60 billion recourse, $3.30 billion non-recourse), with $1.83 billion current, including convertible senior notes maturing 2019–2022, 5.30% senior notes due 2025, solar and automotive asset-backed notes, and a credit agreement amended in May 2018 to permit inclusion of Fremont Factory facilities and vehicles bound for Belgium in borrowing bases. The 2018 notes were fully settled in the first half of 2018; related-party promissory notes were repaid; $546.1 million of Automotive Asset-backed Notes Series 2018-A were issued; and warehouse agreements were amended to extend maturity to September 2020. The company was in compliance with all debt covenants.

Equity: Under the 2010 Equity Incentive Plan, 10,069,978 shares remained available for issuance. In March 2018 stockholders approved a 2018 CEO Performance Award of 20,264,042 stock options vesting in 12 tranches based on operational and market milestones and continued service.

Recent accounting pronouncements: ASU 2016-02 (Leases) is expected to be adopted January 1, 2019 with a material balance sheet effect (right-of-use assets and liabilities) and no expected material impact on the statement of operations; ASU 2016-13 (credit losses) is planned for January 1, 2020; ASU 2017-12 (hedging) is planned for January 1, 2019; and no measurement period adjustments have been made under SAB 118 for the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, with none expected to be material.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 issue list covers sleep and clock controls, GLIU and high I/O addressing, DMA/UDMA, UART/USB clock gating, interrupt and ACPI behavior, ATA/ATAPI, LPC, SMB, GPIO, standby, and PCI timing. Issue numbers are nonsequential because resolved issues are omitted.

Detailed findings state that the PIT supplies the counter value before status after an incomplete latch sequence; read-back commands should wait until the preceding latch command completes. In count mode 3, a new count is loaded immediately rather than after the current count finishes, potentially breaking dependent software. The GLIU debug port recognizes debug packets but hangs instead of forwarding them to LPC and should not be used. The XPIC clears an IRR bit one clock after the second interrupt acknowledge, causing AEOI to send two interrupts instead of one; AEOI is unsuitable where nested interrupts are required. DMA transfers complete, but rotating priority does not always preserve the expected request order. During a thermal alarm, the system enters Faulted Standby, while the PMC cannot recover autonomously because the alarm resides in the Work domain and its timer is blocked in Standby; the timer restarts if the alarm remains asserted. Sleep Clock must be enabled when optional sleep features are desired, and disabling it through GPIO has the same effect as disabling it in the PMC.

On September 12, 2017, Apple Inc. completed a $5 billion senior unsecured notes offering: $1 billion of 1.500% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.100% notes due 2022, $2 billion of 2.900% notes due 2027, and $1 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. Interest is payable semiannually on March 12 and September 12, beginning March 12, 2018. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The transaction was governed by a September 5, 2017 underwriting agreement and Apple’s April 29, 2013 indenture. Apple furnished the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms, and legal opinion and consent as exhibits.

Diana Containerships reported quarterly EPS of ($0.66), beating the consensus estimate of ($0.77) by $0.11, but revenue of $5.40 million missed the $7.50 million estimate. Revenue fell 63.8% year over year. The stock opened Tuesday at $2.71, with a $24.82 million market cap. Renaissance Technologies increased its stake 94.4%, and Zacks upgraded the rating from “sell” to “hold.”

The March 27–28, 2001 news compilation covers corporate developments, energy regulation and Enron’s international expansion. Viacom abandoned its planned Blockbuster spin-off after the video-rental chain’s financial and market-share recovery; its Blockbuster video-on-demand venture with Enron had been terminated. President Bush appointed Patrick Wood III and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, potentially influencing its response to California’s electricity crisis.

Enron increased Chairman Kenneth Lay’s 2000 bonus to $7 million from $3.9 million; his unchanged salary was $1.3 million, alongside $7.5 million in restricted stock and options potentially worth $35 million. CEO Jeffrey Skilling projected 2001 revenue of $160 billion–$170 billion, compared with $100.8 billion in 2000.

Enron and Orix’s EnCom submitted a plan for a 2,000-megawatt LNG-fired power plant and terminal in Aomori, Japan. Construction was targeted for 2004 and operation for 2007 or later, but costs were uncertain and the project faced environmental, regulatory and transmission hurdles. Enron and TotalFinaElf each held 24.5% of Dolphin Energy, which was developing a Qatari gas supply project for Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

In India, the central government planned to prevent financially strained states from negotiating directly with multilateral lenders. Enron and PowerGen withdrew from bidding for a 26% stake in Karnataka’s Vijayanagar power project, prompting talks with Larsen & Toubro. Enron Wind also sought approval for an Indian wind-power subsidiary with an initial $2 million investment.

On energy policy, California approved electricity-rate increases of up to 46%. Skilling said the increases could reduce shortages but maintained that California needed further deregulation, while readers criticized regulators, utilities and Enron. He said Texas’s impending market was better designed and projected California’s summer power deficit at 5,000 megawatts. Texas’s June pilot program allowed up to 5% of customers to choose providers; Enron spinoff New Power had signed more than 5,000 customers.

Britain’s new electricity-trading system was expected to favor flexible generators such as Powergen and Innogy, while presenting difficulties for nuclear and renewable producers. Enron and other U.S. exporters also urged the Export-Import Bank to permit private “market-window” financing for overseas sales, amid opposition to a proposed 25% budget cut.

Roanoke College’s Bittle tree, planted by President David Bittle, was removed after a century due to lightning and wind damage. Its wood was used for the Bittle Tree of Life Cross, designed by Dean Chris Bowen and built by George Arthur for Antrim Chapel, symbolizing the College’s roots and future.

Steve Yzerman said Tampa Bay’s sustained success depends on homegrown talent, careful drafting, and patient development rather than a fixed timeline. Although free agency and trades could accelerate the process, he emphasized there are no quick fixes and credited scouting and minor-league development for producing a core that includes Steven Stamkos, Victor Hedman, Ondrej Palat, Nikita Kucherov, Tyler Johnson and others. He described Anton Stralman as an important right-shot defenseman and said the club seeks high-character players suited to its winning program.

Coach Jon Cooper said the Lightning learned through adversity, made adjustments and repeatedly recovered from deficits; the team’s belief, leadership and willingness to accept different roles drove its playoff run. He credited veteran leadership for helping young prospects develop and said promoting several rookies together gave them shared expectations. Stamkos increasingly carried the load as captain while Palat, Killorn, Johnson and others emerged as leaders. He accepted defensive and faceoff responsibilities without complaint.

Yzerman praised Stamkos’s maturity, character, humility and all-around development. He also characterized Kucherov and Johnson as exceptional, game-changing players with different styles, and said Jonathan had become a bigger, stronger, more complete and defensive-minded player.

May Baxter-Thornton and Emma Lewis, both survivors of child sexual abuse, have joined IICSA’s victims and survivors panel to advise on reaching and listening to Welsh victims and survivors. Lewis was taken into care at 10 and disclosed abuse at 12; Baxter-Thornton has supported abuse survivors for 16 years.
The Louisiana Supreme Court granted review, ordered the record sent up in duplicate, and notified counsel.

ERW pipes transport petroleum and gas under high and low pressures. Made from hot-rolled coil, they offer low-cost production with material savings. Unlike seamless pipes, they contain strip welds; quality control addresses seams and removes burrs to 0.2–0.5 mm. Wall thickness is controlled within ±0.2 mm, and pipe ends follow API or GB/T 9711.1 standards. Widely used in urban gas networks.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for identifying audio content in networked media playback environments. A playback device receives digital audio data, sends a portion to an identification system, receives associated information or metadata, and forwards it to a control device while playing the audio through wired speakers. The control device may command the playback device to retrieve identification information and display it or related metadata obtained from a metadata-curating device. Identification may be triggered by a user command, detected discontinuities in the audio stream, or periodic sampling. The playback device may decode data, convert sample rates, select data from different stages of its audio-processing pipeline, or segregate frequency ranges before identification. The environment includes networked playback and control devices, configurable playback zones and zone groups, synchronized, bonded, or consolidated playback, playback queues, and local or network audio sources. Corresponding apparatus, methods, and non-transitory computer-readable media are also described.

The passage argues that health care should be a right and favors Medicare for all, criticizing Rep. Ken Buck’s description of health care as a commodity and claiming Medicare costs less than private insurance. It also faults a Longmont Tribune headline for omitting that a teen killed by police was driving a stolen car toward an officer. The author sympathizes with the teen’s family while arguing that her actions were criminal, questioning the settlement, and defending police officers.

The disclosure describes directional illumination apparatus and display devices using imaging directional backlights, waveguides, illuminator arrays, and spatial light modulators to provide large-area illumination through viewing windows. Unlike conventional non-imaging backlights, which direct light into a common viewing zone, imaging directional backlights form separate optical windows corresponding to individual light sources.

A stepped-waveguide optical valve receives light along an input end, guides it by total internal reflection to a reflective end, and returns it to extraction features that redirect it through an output surface. Curved or linear extraction features and a curved reflective end can produce uniform viewing windows. Synchronizing selectively operated illuminators with a fast spatial light modulator enables time-multiplexed autostereoscopic 3D, observer tracking, multi-viewer displays, and directional privacy displays.

Embodiments also use input, output, and additional polarizers with passive and switchable liquid-crystal retarders, including A-plates, C-plates, and O-plates. Their orientations and applied voltages can reduce off-axis luminance for snoopers while maintaining head-on luminance and wide-angle operation. Switchable retarders, region-specific electrodes, and camouflage patterns permit adjustable privacy levels. Control systems can coordinate viewing-window width, retarder voltage, snooper location, and temporally multiplexed images. The displays may also be used in vehicles to reduce visibility of windscreen reflections.

Deloitte’s survey found consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles rose: 49% considered self-driving cars unsafe, down from 73%, while 53% trusted established brands and 51% preferred traditional manufacturers over technology firms. Most respondents favored engine-powered cars, citing range, price, and charging infrastructure, though lower running costs could attract EV buyers. The UK government is launching a safety inquiry ahead of expected deployment.

The passage examines Yale Hirsch’s four-year Presidential Election Cycle, a theory that U.S. stock-market returns tend to follow a repeating pattern around presidential terms. Historical backtests identify the pre-election year as the cycle’s strongest and election year as second strongest. Since 1952, the S&P 500 averaged 12.5% in election years with an incumbent seeking reelection, compared with 6.7% across all election years and −1.5% when no incumbent was running. Midterm years, particularly presidents’ second years, have generally been weak until the fourth quarter, when performance improves and volatility tends to increase.

Over roughly 90 years, stocks and bonds also performed less well in the year before presidential elections, although major shocks such as the Great Recession disrupted these patterns. The theory cannot predict every market movement, and congressional control often shapes whether presidential policies can pass.

Healthcare and energy sectors may face greater election-related volatility because of regulatory, legislative, trade, and renewable-energy policy differences. The passage advises investors to consider policy effects on specific sectors and the global economy, remain invested, and rebalance portfolios amid election-related volatility.

Intel’s Management Engine (ME) is a small, closed-source subsystem embedded in many modern Intel CPUs. It evolved from Trusted Platform Modules and Active Management Technology and remains powered on when the computer is off, with connections to storage and network interfaces. According to the passage, its inclusion was requested by the NSA, and it runs the Minix operating system. Researchers long knew the ME existed but could not assess its vulnerabilities because its code was closed source.

At Black Hat Europe, Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy presented an exploit enabling arbitrary code execution on the ME platform. The “Evil Maid” exploit requires physical access and affects ME versions above V.11; arbitrary execution was later demonstrated using a USB stick. No network-based ME exploit is known, making the current exploit less significant in threat models where physical access already provides control, though earlier ME versions may remain vulnerable.

Mitigation is fragmented. System76 released firmware to disable the ME, and Dell offered a rugged Latitude 14 with it disabled by default. Intel provides a detection tool, but there is no universal way to disable the ME because implementation varies by manufacturer. Without valid ME firmware, a computer shuts down after 30 minutes. The me_cleaner workaround renders the ME ineffective while allowing the computer to operate, but existing solutions remain incomplete. Overall, the ME’s always-on, opaque, connected design illustrates the security concerns raised by unauditable proprietary code.

New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities and increasing family involvement in their care. It authorizes twice-yearly unannounced inspections of group homes, requires injury notifications to parents or guardians within two to eight hours, and mandates at least twice-yearly family meetings.

This qualitative literature review examines Mortimer J. Adler’s philosophy of perennialism in relation to Christian and global education, posthumanism, and education management. Primary sources include Adler’s books on curriculum and Christian education, while secondary sources address philosophy, education, posthumanist thought, and management.

The review links Adler’s curriculum ideals to enduring values, rational inquiry, tradition, and holistic learner development. Docility and obedience are presented as complementary values, with docility involving postponed judgment and respect for trusted authority rather than surrendering independent thought. Education and democracy should proceed together, while education should develop children’s capacities and curiosity rather than merely prepare them for employment. The authors criticize Adler for not distinguishing between women and men and argue that women require support to participate equally.

Posthumanism is discussed as challenging human supremacy and examining technology, artificial intelligence, cyborgs, environmental dependence, rights, and humanity’s future. Studies reviewed address Christian family meals, spirituality and chronic illness, moral and character education, cross-cultural student agency, Christian business values, Kenyan institutional transformation, diaspora disaster management, and Christian business identities.

The paper concludes that just education should empower women, avoid treating children as failed adults, and hold teachers, parents, and the state responsible for educational failure. Educational management should extend beyond administration to learners’ ethical and intellectual formation, prioritize timeless values over immediate achievement, and test theory against field realities.

Venezuelan Temporary Protected Status holders and the National TPS Alliance asked the Supreme Court to leave intact a federal ruling barring the Trump administration from terminating Venezuelan TPS protections. TPS, created by Congress in 1990, allows Homeland Security to designate nationals who may remain and work in the United States when extraordinary conditions in their home country prevent safe return. DHS Secretary Kristi Noem ended Venezuela’s 2023 designation and 2025 extension. U.S. District Judge Edward Chen temporarily blocked the termination, then ruled on Sept. 5 that Noem acted unlawfully. The challengers also alleged racial animus. The Ninth Circuit declined to pause Chen’s ruling, and Solicitor General D. John Sauer asked the Supreme Court to intervene, arguing its earlier limited stay required lower courts to stop. The challengers countered that the prior stay addressed only preliminary relief, while Chen’s final judgment relied on different statutory authority and a more developed record, including a new claim. They noted that the law directing courts to “set aside” unlawful agency actions applies to the final judgment. UCLA law professor Ahilan Arulanantham warned that disturbing the order would cause “massive injuries” to affected Venezuelans and their families, including American children.

Ed Sachse, 56, is president of property services at Kennedy Wilson, overseeing brokers and 21 million square feet of U.S. retail, office, industrial and apartment properties. As a Detroit high school student, he and a friend bought a window-washing business for $400, gaining early lessons in entrepreneurship. He studied accounting at Michigan State, worked at Arthur Andersen, and later became CFO of Douglas Emmett’s mortgage banking company after moving to Los Angeles. He left accounting for commercial brokerage at Coldwell Banker, where selling an empty school helped launch his career.

Sachse moved into property management and founded his own brokerage and management company in 1993. In 2001, he was diagnosed with stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma but kept working through six years of treatment, including a bone marrow transplant and two stem cell transplants. During the Great Recession, his company suffered cutbacks and layoffs. After seeking work from 40 contacts in 2009, he visited Kennedy Wilson and offered to handle its worst property. Kennedy Wilson instead proposed acquiring his company. He accepted and has since overseen its brokerage and property management operations.

The invention concerns an optical waveguide display in which image-bearing light is diffracted into a waveguide, propagated by total internal reflection (TIR), and diffracted out for viewing. In prior-art displays, the field of view is limited by the waveguide’s TIR characteristics and by the wavelength to which its input Bragg grating is tuned. Light of other wavelengths may be diffracted at unsuitable angles, causing it to escape the waveguide and reducing the wavelength-dependent field of view.

The disclosed apparatus includes an optical waveguide with a first diffractive part that receives display light and diffracts it for guided propagation by TIR, and a second diffractive part that receives the guided light and diffracts it for output. External surfaces against which the guided light reflects internally are coated with a material having a positive refractive index substantially equal to or less than about 1.0 at optical wavelengths. The coating reduces the critical angle for TIR, allowing light from outside the conventional field of view to be retained and guided, thereby increasing the field of view and/or extending the usable wavelength range for wider-band or multicolour displays.

The coating may be a low-index metamaterial formed as a periodic fish-net or mesh nanopotonic structure. One disclosed unit cell contains a magnetic resonator positioned between opposing conductive wire meshes. The resonator may comprise an alumina layer between parallel conductive plates, while the meshes comprise crossed conductive lines or strips. Structural dimensions and materials can be optimized to obtain a real refractive index between 0 and 1 and to control optical attenuation. At an index near one, the coating can also optically mimic air while protecting exposed waveguide surfaces and surface-profile gratings from damage and contamination.

A multilayer embodiment includes component slab waveguides with separate input and output gratings tuned to different colours. A low-index metamaterial layer can lie between and bind the component waveguides, while additional coatings cover their outer TIR-reflecting surfaces. Optional plastic outer layers can add strength, rigidity, shock absorption, or scratch resistance. Alternatively, coating windows may be left over input or output gratings to avoid attenuation of light passing through the metamaterial.

The first and second diffractive parts may be mutually conjugated so that the output grating diffracts light in the opposite order from the input grating. This reduces image distortion and substantially negates chromatic dispersion, particularly with broadband sources such as LEDs. The diffractive parts may be transmissive or reflective and may comprise Bragg or surface-profile gratings.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 are low-power 32-bit MCUs featuring an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU operating up to 32 MHz, with instruction prefetch, a two-line I-cache, SysTick, and an NVIC with four programmable priority levels. RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN power modes use two power domains to balance performance and consumption. Shutdown disables both domains and can be exited through NRST, SWD, or certain I/O logic-level matches. The PMU supplies regulated core power, brownout monitoring, and power-on reset, while the clock module supports internal and external low- and high-frequency oscillators and distributes clocks to the processor, buses, and peripherals.

DMA_B provides two full-feature channels and one basic channel, with triggers from ADC, UART, SPI, and timer peripherals; it supports multiple transfer widths, repeated transfers, gather and stride modes, and ping-pong-buffer interrupts. An event manager routes peripheral events to CPU interrupts, DMA triggers, or other peripherals. Nonvolatile flash uses 1KB sectors and supports up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on selected sectors, or across the entire 32KB in 32KB devices. Zero-wait-state SRAM supports dynamic 1KB write protection and is retained through STANDBY but lost in SHUTDOWN. GPIO supports up to 45 pins with FastWake and shutdown wake capability, while IOMUX provides programmable pin multiplexing and pad settings.

Peripheral support includes a 12-bit ADC operating up to 1.6 Msps, an internal temperature sensor, selectable internal or external voltage references, and a comparator with reference-DAC and wakeup features. The device also includes three UARTs with LIN support, I²C with SMBus 3.0 and address-match wakeup, SPI up to 16 Mbit/s, general-purpose and advanced timers, independent and windowed watchdogs, an RTC with calendar alarms and periodic wakeups, CRC and security functions, and a low-frequency subsystem containing the RTC and independent watchdog. Two-wire SWD and DEBUGSS support processor and device debugging, configurable peripheral behavior, a software mailbox, lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Factory constants provide device identification and trim data.

Recommended layout includes 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR VDD/VSS decoupling capacitors placed close to the pins, a 47kΩ NRST pull-up with a 1000pF pull-down, crystal bypass capacitors, and pull-ups for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs used for logic-high outputs. TI support resources include SysConfig, Resource Explorer, GUI Composer, cloud tools, TI Arm-Clang, development boards, and E2E support. The September 2025 revision updates power modes, package information, electrical specifications, CPU, ADC, debug, and identification details. Additional sections cover ESD precautions, part-number nomenclature, development and production status, mechanical package drawings, thermal-pad requirements, board-assembly guidance, and orderable-part information.

After developing sepsis from a scratched hand while visiting Glasgow in 2015, the author spent three months in a coma and another year recovering. Sepsis starts with an infection but becomes life-threatening when the body’s immune response becomes uncontrolled, causing vital-organ failure. It affects over 30 million people annually and kills an estimated six million, including nearly two million children; 40% of survivors develop post-sepsis syndrome. Warning signs include pale, mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering, muscle pain, not urinating for a day, nausea, and vomiting. Immediate emergency care and asking whether it could be sepsis are advised. Antibiotics can treat the original infection, but no specific cure exists. Research includes metformin and gene therapy targeting NF-kB, while improved awareness among the public and medical professionals and use of the Sepsis6 protocol are seen as key current defenses.

The paper presents a real-time facial anonymization system for AI-assisted scientific experiment education, where student privacy must be protected without obscuring instruments, hand movements, or experimental procedures. Existing tracking, clustering, and GAN-based methods are not tailored to faces occluded by thin, transparent, or motion-blurred apparatus.

The proposed system combines MSFF-YOLOv8, BOTSort tracking, and Gaussian blurring. MSFF-YOLOv8 retains low-level features, adds multi-scale feature fusion, and supports joint object detection and semantic segmentation. Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR), applied during training, expands face–occlusion boundaries toward the face to reduce misclassification of instruments and actions. Primary operators receive detailed face blurring, while non-primary operators are processed using bounding boxes.

The researchers created a dataset from 51 experiment videos, including 1,049 annotated images, 7,590 face labels, 5,240 instrument labels, and 1,530 tracked poses. Evaluation against YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM used FPS, Sensitive Object Blur Accuracy (SOBA), and Over Blur Rate (OBR). At 1920-pixel input, MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR achieved 96.02% accuracy, an OBR of 0.0159 on the full dataset, and 22.67 FPS for 1080p processing. The authors note that further work is needed for precise edge classification during real-time inference.

The lecture reviews renewal theory as a foundation for analyzing countable-state Markov chains. Three results are discussed: the strong law for renewals, under which the long-run arrival rate on almost every sample path is \(1/\bar{x}\); the elementary renewal theorem, which gives the same limiting rate for the expected number of renewals but does not control sample-path fluctuations; and Blackwell’s theorem, which shows that renewal rates eventually become regular. For arithmetic renewal processes with span \(\lambda\), the probability of renewal at \(m\lambda\) tends to \(\lambda/\bar{x}\), while the nonarithmetic version gives an average increment rate of \(1/\bar{x}\). Long-time and small-interval limits cannot generally be interchanged in the nonarithmetic case.

Age and duration are then examined for arithmetic renewal processes. Age is the time since the last renewal, while duration extends from the last renewal through the next one. Their asymptotic joint distribution is determined by the inter-renewal interval \(X\). The limiting probability that duration equals \(k\) is \(kP(X=k)/\bar{x}\), giving an expected duration of \(E[X^2]/E[X]\). The age distribution follows by summing over possible durations, and the expected age in the integer-time discussion is \(E[X^2]/(2E[X])\). The factor of \(1/2\) is attributed to observing age at integer times, when an arrival can reset age to zero.

The lecture then turns to countable-state Markov chains. For a random walk on the integers with upward probability \(p\) and downward probability \(q\), the state’s variance grows linearly with time, and its distribution spreads over a \(\sqrt n\) scale with an approximately Gaussian shape. The probability of any fixed state tends to zero, so there is no steady-state probability distribution. This chain is irreducible and has period two.

A birth-death chain on the nonnegative integers is introduced. When \(p<1/2\), the chain is recurrent; when \(p>1/2\), it is transient and drifts toward infinity. The critical case \(p=1/2\) returns with probability one but has no steady-state distribution and an infinite expected return time. Finite truncations have uniform stationary probabilities at \(p=1/2\), while for \(p>1/2\) their probability mass shifts toward the upper boundary as the truncation grows.

Finally, first-passage probabilities \(f_{ij}(n)\), representing the probability of first reaching state \(j\) at time \(n\), are distinguished from the ordinary transition probabilities \(p_{ij}^{(n)}\). Their recursions condition on the first transition before reaching \(j\), and their cumulative probabilities define a possibly defective first-hitting-time distribution. A state \(j\) is recurrent when \(\sum_n f_{jj}(n)=1\), meaning that it is eventually revisited with probability one. Successive returns to a recurrent state form a renewal process. Communicating states share recurrence or transience, and recurrent states may have finite or infinite mean return times, distinguishing positive recurrence from null recurrence.
