The lecture explains how auctions set prices in government procurement, Treasury bill sales, online advertising, and spectrum licensing. It develops the independent private values model: risk-neutral bidders observe independent signals, each value depends only on the bidder’s own signal, and the signal can be treated as the bidder’s value.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the highest bidder wins and pays the second-highest bid. Bidding one’s true value is weakly dominant, although other equilibria can exist; with continuous distributions, truthful bidding is the unique symmetric equilibrium. Expected revenue is the expected second-highest value. For uniform values, revenue is \((n-1)/(n+1)\), approaching the highest value as the number of bidders grows. A rising button auction implements equivalent behavior: bidders remain active until the price reaches their value. However, sealed-bid auctions reveal bidders’ values, while button auctions reveal only when bidding stops.

In a first-price sealed-bid auction, the highest bidder pays its own bid, so symmetric equilibrium bidding involves shading below value. The lecture derives general equilibrium bid formulas and shows that uniform values imply bidding \((n-1)/n\) of one’s value. The optimal bid can also be interpreted as the expected second-highest value conditional on having the highest value. Consequently, first- and second-price auctions generate the same expected revenue under the model’s assumptions.

The revenue equivalence theorem extends this result to symmetric independent private-value mechanisms that award the object to the highest-value bidder and give the lowest type zero surplus. Such mechanisms produce the same expected seller revenue and bidder expected utility, called the bidder’s information rent. The theorem can also be used to solve other auctions, such as the all-pay auction, by equating equilibrium utility to the information rent.

The theorem has important limitations. It assumes risk neutrality, independent values, and allocation to the highest-value bidder. With risk-averse bidders, first-price auctions generate more revenue; with positively correlated values, second-price auctions generate more. It also excludes mechanisms that may withhold the object.

For a second-price auction, an optimal reserve equals the seller’s monopoly price, determined before values are drawn. Competition does not eliminate the value of a reserve. Nevertheless, reserves reduce welfare when all bidders’ values fall below the reserve, may discourage entry and bidding effort, and require commitment not to reverse the reserve later.

The lecture then turns to common-value auctions, where value depends on all bidders’ signals. Winning can reveal that one’s signal was more optimistic than rivals’, producing the winner’s curse. Rational bidders therefore bid on their expected value conditional on learning that they won rather than simply on their private signal.

Hendricks and Porter’s study of U.S. offshore oil leases illustrates this problem. Incumbent firms bidding on adjacent drainage tracts possess both informational and cost advantages. Such tracts were more likely to contain oil and had higher average value than remote wildcat tracts, yet attracted fewer bidders and generated higher incumbent profits. The paper’s mixed-strategy model predicts that disadvantaged bidders enter cautiously, incumbents win more than half the time, incumbents earn positive profits, and incumbent bidding rises with tract value and rivals’ signals but does not depend on the number of rival bidders. Evidence from 114 drainage tracts auctioned between 1959 and 1969 broadly supports these predictions, suggesting that asymmetric information and the winner’s curse deter entry. The lecture also suggests that bundling drainage-tract advantages into competition for initial wildcat tracts could avoid some of these distortions.

This qualitative study examines how university students in face-to-face tour guiding programs in Türkiye perceived emergency distance education (EDE), which became widespread during the Covid-19 pandemic. EDE is defined as the temporary transfer of face-to-face education into an online environment during a crisis and differs from planned online or distance education. The study focuses on theoretical and practical requirements of tour guiding education, including communication, field experience, classroom interaction, motivation, and professional skills.

Data were collected from 81 students in tour guiding departments at three Istanbul universities during the 2022–2023 academic year. Participants had experienced at least one semester of pandemic-era hybrid or distance education and were selected through purposive sampling. Semi-structured interviews and a 13-question online questionnaire were analyzed thematically with MAXQDA. Responses were confirmed by participants, and two researchers validated the coding.

Students generally considered EDE insufficient for tour guiding education. The main reasons were inadequate vocational training (46.1%), ineffective communication (32.2%), and motivation problems (21.1%). They emphasized that the profession requires field trips, presentations, group interaction, body language, storytelling, foreign-language practice, and direct contact with instructors. Accordingly, 59.2% regarded distance education as inadequate for practical training. Most students (81.4%) perceived clear differences between face-to-face and distance education, describing face-to-face instruction as more efficient, communicative, social, conducive to concentration, and supportive of self-expression.

Distance education nevertheless offered several advantages: effective time management (46.5%), the ability to repeat or make up courses (18.6%), independence from location (11.6%), savings (5.8%), and easier access to materials and recordings (4.6%). Its principal disadvantages were perceived inappropriacy for tour guiding education (29.7%), lack of motivation (23.4%), insufficient communication (18%), technical problems (9.5%), and poor attendance (6.3%). Despite these drawbacks, 88.8% reported that they could understand the distance courses, with associate students rating their understanding more highly than undergraduate students.

The findings show a continuing dilemma: students appreciated distance education’s flexibility and convenience but preferred face-to-face education because it better supports communication, socialization, practical learning, and professional preparation. The authors recommend practical field-based courses, effective online communication systems, hybrid options, technology-supported professional development, and separate evaluation of established distance programs and EDE. The study is limited by its exploratory qualitative design, its focus on İstanbul, and the exclusion of students already enrolled in regular distance-education programs.

This September 2022 ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988, Volume I: Foundations of Foreign Policy* provides portable, searchable, offline access while preserving the printed edition’s content. Readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers.

The FRUS series, established in 1861, documents major U.S. foreign-policy decisions and diplomatic activity. State Department historians prepare its volumes under regulations and a 1991 statute requiring comprehensive, accurate, reliable, and objective records, disclosure of deletions, inclusion of important facts, and publication within 30 years. Most sources used for this volume are declassified and available at the National Archives.

The riding’s Conservative association chose Brad Vis to run in next year’s federal election. After narrowly losing to Liberal Jati Sidhu in 2015, Vis criticized Liberal spending and highlighted seniors on fixed incomes and young families’ housing struggles.

A strong data culture supports vertical and horizontal organizational alignment: shared metrics connect employees’ work to company goals, while common data models and transparent access improve cross-functional collaboration. Digital leaders commonly adopt a learning mindset, provide open data access, track progress with clear metrics, and maintain consistency among leadership beliefs, stated values, and employee behavior.

Technologically mature firms embed learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement in their values and daily practices. Digital laggards may recognize data’s importance but face barriers from entrenched habits, skills gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors is the hardest part of transformation, although mature leaders still require ongoing cultural growth.

Organizations fall into four patterns: data novices lack enabling culture and systems; insight-ready organizations encourage risk but lack advanced analytics capabilities; tech-enabled organizations possess data and technology but limit experimentation; and data-reliant organizations over-rely on data, potentially discouraging critical thinking.

The speaker reflected on his team’s defeat, praising the Devils for outplaying and outskating them. He credited Friesen’s patience on the first goal, noting that he went down too early, and said he did not see the puck bounce to the opposing player’s stick after the first shot. He said the team must use its speed better, shoot more, create traffic around the net, and execute its usual style to succeed against the opposing goaltender. He also praised Patrick as an excellent goaltender, said his decision should be respected, and denied that time off caused the defeat. Believing the result reflected adversity and possibly nerves, he said the team must improve, match the Devils’ intensity, and be ready for the next game. With two weeks remaining in the season, he urged everyone to keep playing and give their best effort.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015 describes a company incorporated in Washington in 1994, reincorporated in Delaware in 1996, headquartered in Seattle, and listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “AMZN.” Beginning in 2015, its reportable segments were North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Amazon serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through retail websites, third-party marketplaces, Kindle and Fire devices, Prime, AWS, Kindle Direct Publishing, advertising, and co-branded credit-card services.

Amazon faces intense competition across retail, e-commerce services, digital content, consumer electronics, and cloud infrastructure. Other identified risks include managing rapid expansion; operating results and growth fluctuations; international operations and regulatory exposure, particularly in China and India; fulfillment and data-center capacity; seasonal inventory demands; commercial agreements, acquisitions, and investments; foreign exchange; loss of key personnel; data and system security breaches; intellectual-property disputes; stock-price volatility; evolving regulation and potential tax liabilities; supplier, government-contract, product-liability, payment, and seller-fraud risks.

The company operated 129.954 million square feet of leased space and 5.036 million square feet of owned space as of December 31, 2015, principally across North America, Europe, and Asia. It had no unresolved SEC staff comments, had never paid cash dividends, and reported no issuer purchases of equity securities or recent sales of unregistered securities.

Net sales in 2015 were $107.006 billion, up 20% from $88.988 billion in 2014; operating income was $2.233 billion, and net income was $596 million, compared with a $241 million loss in 2014. Diluted earnings per share were $1.25. Operating cash flow increased to $11.920 billion, total assets reached $65.444 billion, and long-term obligations totaled $18.161 billion. Segment sales were $63.708 billion for North America, up 25%; $35.418 billion for International, up 6%; and $7.880 billion for AWS, up 70%. Foreign-exchange changes reduced 2015 net sales by $5.2 billion.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $19.8 billion at year-end. Investing activities used $6.450 billion, including $4.6 billion of capital expenditures, while financing activities used $3.763 billion. Amazon had no borrowings under its $2.0 billion credit agreement and stated that operating cash flows, marketable securities, and available credit should meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least 12 months, subject to uncertainty. Critical accounting judgments included inventory valuation, goodwill impairment, stock-based compensation, and income taxes. Amazon employed approximately 230,800 full- and part-time workers and historically generated about one-third of annual revenue in the fourth quarter.

Suzanne Nimocks forwarded a December 6, 2000 McKinsey memorandum, “Power sector restructuring: international activity, June–November 2000,” by Carol B. White and Pru Sheppard. Attached exhibits cover restructuring status and market-opening timelines. The report says privatization, unbundling, and competition were advancing worldwide as governments sought capital for growing electricity demand. Some international investors were shifting toward less risky markets in the United States and Europe, while Asian and Latin American reforms resumed more slowly after economic and currency crises.

Europe was implementing the EU electricity directive and liberalizing wholesale and retail markets. France accelerated opening, Italy required ENEL to divest generation and separate its functions, the Netherlands expanded customer choice and created a power exchange, and the UK consolidated supply after full market opening. Germany’s consolidation continued despite grid-access and regulatory obstacles. Other developments included Denmark’s phased retail opening, Spain’s faster-than-required liberalization and proposed Endesa-Iberdrola merger, Nordic power-market integration, and planned reforms in Austria, Greece, Ireland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, and Turkey. Central and Eastern Europe continued privatizations and unbundling, often to attract capital and meet IMF and EU requirements, with notable programs or proposals in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Moldova, Romania, Russia, the Slovak Republic, and Ukraine.

Asia-Pacific governments resumed restructuring as economies recovered. Australia planned full customer choice by 2003, China pursued interconnection while reform mechanisms remained limited, and India proposed state-utility unbundling, independent transmission, regulation, and reduced barriers to independent producers. Japan opened its large-customer market, though transmission fees limited competition. Restructuring and privatization were also under way in Malaysia, New Zealand, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. Indonesia, Pakistan, and the Philippines continued to face power-purchase agreement disputes, payment problems, government-guarantee issues, or delays in reform legislation.

In Latin America, privatization of distribution and generation was largely complete in major economies except Venezuela and Mexico. Several countries postponed further sales because of inflation, currency volatility, ownership restrictions, political uncertainty, or investor concerns. Transmission concessions and privatizations were increasing, while droughts and heavy dependence on hydropower caused shortages and discouraged investment. Brazil launched a wholesale market despite hydro dependence and projected shortages; Chile proposed distribution and transmission reforms; Argentina auctioned transmission assets; and Colombia delayed asset sales amid strikes and attacks. Privatization or regulatory reforms were also discussed in Bolivia, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, and the Virgin Islands.

African and Middle Eastern governments were increasingly opening their sectors to foreign investment, though most primarily permitted independent power producers. Côte d’Ivoire, Gabon, Guinea, Mali, and Senegal had privatized their systems, while partial privatizations, unbundling, and regulatory reform were being considered elsewhere. Regional transmission initiatives included the Mozambique link, West African Power Pool, Six-Country link, and a proposed Gulf grid. Notable developments included South African utility restructuring, Egypt’s planned regional stake sales and competitive IPP procurement, and IPP or restructuring plans in Algeria, Ghana, Morocco, Nigeria, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and the United Arab Emirates. The authors requested local updates and offered country spreadsheets and regional contacts.

This study (Language Teaching Research Quarterly, 2024, Vol. 42, 163–187) examines the relationship between multilingualism proficiency and cultural awareness among university students in Indonesia, a topic the authors note has received limited prior classroom-based research. Grounded in anthropolinguistics and sociocultural studies, and drawing on second-language acquisition theory (Krashen, Ellis, Vygotsky) and Duranti's concept of culture, the study tests hypotheses that multilingualism learning variables are significantly related to one another, that cultural awareness variables are significantly related, and that multilingualism learning variables are related to cultural awareness.

The embedded mixed-methods design used a QUAN(qual) model with a survey as the primary quantitative strategy. The population was 537 students from six institutions (State Universities of Makassar, Surabaya and Jakarta, the University of Northern Sumatra, Timor University, and Palangka Raya State Islamic Institute); 388 respondents were selected by simple random sampling using Slovin's formula with an e-value of 0.05, and 60 participants contributed qualitative data. Data were collected in January–February 2024 via a Google Form questionnaire whose validity and reliability were tested, with Cronbach's α values of 0.610–0.686. Variables covered Multilingualism Competency (MC), Multilingual Learning Process (MLP), Psychological Factors (PF) and Social Interaction (SI), plus Cultural Knowledge and Communication (CKC), Cultural Practices and Participation (CPP), Sociocultural Context (SC) and Capacity and Attitude towards Cultural Learning (CAC). Analysis used Pearson's r in JASP 0.18.3 and thematic analysis in Nvivo 14; Q–Q plots indicated approximately normal distributions.

Results showed MC averaging 3.369 (SD 0.542), indicating moderate competence, with MLP at 3.454 and PF at 3.384; SI (3.300) and CKC (3.184) were lowest, indicating room for further development, while CPP had the lowest SD (0.422), indicating consistent participation, and SC (3.479) and CAC (3.418) were highest. Ethnically, Jawa was the largest group (25.77%), followed by Bugis (17.78%) and Makassar (15.72%). Indonesian was the dominant mother tongue (61.08%), ahead of Javanese (8.76%), Bugis (6.96%) and Makassarese (5.67%). Javanese (26.80%), Bugis (17.01%) and Makassarese (16.75%) were the most studied local languages, while English (63.40%), Korean (12.11%), Arabic (8.25%), Japanese (6.96%) and German (4.90%) led foreign language study. Indonesian was mainly learned through lectures (38.92%) and school (36.86%), local languages mainly through independent study (58.25%), and foreign languages mainly through school (34.28%).

All correlations were significant at p < .001: MC–MLP r = 0.568, MC–PF 0.537, MC–SI 0.504, MLP–PF 0.559, MLP–SI 0.371, PF–SI 0.381; CKC–SC 0.483, CKC–CPP 0.267, CPP–SC 0.421, CPP–CAC 0.338, SC–CAC 0.523; and across domains MC–SC 0.553, MC–CAC 0.495, MC–CKC 0.378, MC–CPP 0.341, PF–SC 0.530, SI–CAC 0.523 and MLP–SC 0.497.

Qualitative findings proposed multilingual learning strategies (educator training, technological support, cultural integration in curricula, proficiency enhancement, motivation and confidence, self-directed learning, community engagement, intercultural collaboration) and cultural awareness strategies (attitudinal adjustment, learning openness, communication skills, inclusive content, active cultural participation, adoption of cultural practices, cultural identity exploration, attention to societal norms). Student responses emphasized diverse and inclusive content, technology supporting adaptive learning, affordable and accessible language resources from governments and institutions, and intercultural collaboration. The conclusion holds that multilingualism education is an important means of raising cultural awareness in Indonesia, offering practitioners and policymakers an empirical basis for inclusive strategies and policies, with future research suggested on virtual reality and language learning applications.

Seventy-seven-year-old Jeong-Suk Cha provides most of the daily care for her 48-year-old son Alex, who has cerebral palsy and severe spinal cord damage. She often transfers him using a lift, while relatives and personal support workers provide additional help. The physical and emotional strain has contributed to her injury, arthritis and limited respite. Alex’s sister Jin organizes his care, medical appointments and workers, and has created detailed instruction binders. His personal support worker allocation is only 90 hours per month, temporarily increased to 140.

Alex has waited more than a decade for residential care at Participation House, where 40 spaces serve 60 to 90 people on its waiting list. Ontario’s Ombudsman reported in 2017 that 9,700 people were waiting province-wide for residential care. Alex and his family oppose placement in a seniors’ long-term-care home, which he says would be “a death sentence.”

A $100-million class-action lawsuit has been filed against Ontario, alleging that the government administers developmental-disability service wait lists in an ad hoc, inconsistent and unreasonable manner. In the South West LHIN, 296 seniors and adults with moderate physical disabilities were awaiting personal support services, while officials acknowledged inadequate data about other complex-needs applicants. Alex’s case was raised in the legislature, where the health minister promised further review but acknowledged that disabled residents need more help.

The paper proposes a methodology enabling a trusting agent in a digital business ecosystem to assess interaction risk and determine beforehand the probability of not receiving the full benefit of its invested resources. Risk is treated as the probability of interaction failure and its consequences, while a trusted agent’s “FailureLevel” quantifies its possible inability to satisfy the interaction’s criteria.

The proposed process divides the interaction’s time space into non-overlapping time slots. Before interaction begins, the trusting agent assigns a crisp FailureLevel in each slot using prior interaction history or recommendations. After interaction begins, it determines the probability of occurrence of each failure level and uses pre-interaction levels to predict future failure probabilities.

The methodology then models financial investment through an Amount Invested Curve (AIC), which represents the probability of a net amount being at stake throughout each slot according to mutually agreed behavior and the timing of investments. A Factual Amount Invested Curve (FAIC) is derived by convolving the AIC with the trusted agent’s FailureLevel using the cumulants method. The FAIC represents the increased probability or amount needed to achieve the desired outcomes when failure is considered.

Finally, the Loss of Resource Benefit (LORB) is calculated as the ordinate of the FAIC at the end of the AIC. It gives the probability that the trusting agent will not receive the full benefit of resources invested in a slot because the trusted agent fails to deliver promised outcomes. In the paper’s example, the LORB for the first post-interaction slot is 0.35, or 35%. These probabilities can be used alongside overall interaction risk to choose the most suitable trusted agent.

This ebook is the U.S. Department of State Office of the Historian’s electronic edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1917, 1917 Supplement 1: The World War*. Generated May 26, 2018, it presents the FRUS series in a portable, searchable format with bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access. The editors sought fidelity to the printed edition and recommend citing document numbers rather than page numbers.

The supplementary papers chiefly concern the period of U.S. neutrality and follow the preceding supplements’ arrangement. Some subjects continue beyond April 6, 1917; Latin American policy papers cover the full year, while China and Siam materials extend through China’s August 14 declaration of war, and some Liberian material follows Liberia’s August 4 declaration. Brackets mark supplied text, suggested corrections, omissions, or garbling. Parentheses are original and may contain decoder suggestions. Translations were corrected when faulty, but important texts were not significantly altered.

The Shuffle offense, a predecessor of the Princeton, Flex, Hawk, and Reverse Action offenses, originated with Bruce Drake at Oklahoma. It uses continuous movement, teamwork, and passing to create high-percentage shots while limiting defensive help and double-teams. Its rotating sequence incorporates all five players, making it suitable for teams lacking height and requiring little dribbling but emphasizing passing, receiving, spacing, screening, rebounding, and ball security.

Continuity begins with reversal passes and options involving screens, cuts, pop shots, and weakside rebounding. A corner player can flash into the middle, back cut for a lob, or set a screen, with roles rotating among rebounder, shooter, and screener.

The central rub cut includes counters for defenses chasing over screens, playing inside in pass denial, switching, cheating under, or showing and recovering. Corresponding responses include cutting over or under, using a double screen, feeding the post directly, or popping out. Defensive overplays can be countered with back cuts, a dribble-clear action, a point back door, or a post lob.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces PCIe Gen 4 connectivity, a redesigned GPU hierarchy, and major gains in graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory bandwidth, and storage I/O. The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory interface, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Each SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, a 256 KB register file, four texture units, a second-generation ray-tracing core, and 128 KB of configurable L1 cache/shared memory. Dual FP32/INT32 datapaths double FP32 throughput versus Turing, while unified cache and shared-memory bandwidth is also substantially improved.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection performance, accelerate ray-traced motion blur, and allow ray tracing to run concurrently with graphics or compute workloads. Motion-blur acceleration can render effects up to eight times faster than on Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores are twice as powerful as Turing Tensor Cores, add TF32 and BF16 support, and implement fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity that can double matrix throughput. Enhanced DLSS supports a 9x scaling factor, enabling 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps on the RTX 3090.

GA10x GPUs are the first to use GDDR6X memory, which uses PAM4 signaling to reach 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s peak bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves asset loading and lossless decompression to the GPU, reducing CPU demands and accelerating storage throughput by up to 100x versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs.

The architecture supports 4K120 and 8K60 displays through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 AV1 playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. GDDR6X memory interfaces also include Error Detection and Replay, which retries corrupted memory transactions.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 and provides 24 GB of GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA Cores. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X. For data centers, the GA102-based A40 provides 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB through NVLink, and supports virtual GPUs and the EGX platform. The RTX A6000 also provides 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96 GB with two boards, along with professional visualization, rendering, AI, and virtual-workstation capabilities. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power efficient than Turing GPUs at equivalent performance.

The AEGEAN study evaluated adherence to, persistence with, and safety of apixaban in patients initiating therapy for atrial fibrillation. In Part 1, 1,162 subjects were randomized to Primary SOC or an Additional Educational Program; 1,054 completed the 24-week visit, and 108 (9.3%) discontinued by then. At week 24, mean adherence was 91.64% with Primary SOC and 91.88% with additional education, with no significant difference. Persistence was also similar at 91.7% and 91.3%, respectively. Mean compliance exceeded 95% at weeks 4, 12, and 24.

In Part 2, 524 subjects were randomized to Secondary SOC or Continued Additional Education, and 1,003 completed the 48-week visit. Adherence from weeks 24–48 was comparable across Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Education groups, as was persistence at week 48. Adherence declined significantly in later intervals in both initial groups, and no significant differences were found in the proportion fully adherent at weeks 24 or 48.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups. Before week 24, bleeding occurred in 6.5% of Primary SOC subjects and 9.0% of Additional Education subjects; major bleeding occurred in 0.7% and 1.1%, respectively, with one fatal bleeding event in the Additional Education group. Between weeks 24 and 48, bleeding occurred in 4.1%, 4.0%, and 3.2% across the three groups, with two fatal events. Twenty-four deaths were reported, no pregnancies occurred, and laboratory review found no concerning hepatic or renal signal. Overall, adherence and persistence were high through 48 weeks, and the proactive educational program did not provide additional benefits.

At its final 2017 meeting, the Brunswick school board began the multi-step process of renewing the 10-year, $4.67 million emergency levy, which expires next year without increasing taxes. It authorized up to $10 million in notes for a new middle school to replace Visintainer and Edwards and other district improvements. Fiscal Year 2018 appropriations were revised to reflect increased grant funding, including IDEA Part B, Titles I and II, and the OHSAA Tournament fund. Four donors gave $5,000, $1,500, $125 and $65 for district programs and students. Lisa Durichko was recognized at her final meeting after 12 years of service. The board held an executive session on employment, discipline and complaints, with no action taken.
The building and fans can benefit Philadelphia when the team is playing well. The goalie remains calm, makes big saves, and shrugs off physical pressure.

SD Memory Cards have User and Protected Areas and are classified as SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (over 2 GB through 32 GB), or SDXC (over 32 GB through 2 TB). Hosts supporting higher-capacity cards must also support lower-capacity cards. Five speed classes define minimum performance: Class 0 for legacy cards, and Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 for minimum transfer rates of 2, 4, 6, and 10 MB/s.

Communication uses host-controlled command, response, and data tokens. Commands may be broadcast or addressed, data transfers use single or multiple blocks with CRC protection, and cards are addressed through assigned relative card addresses. Standard, wide-bus, and SPI protocol formats are defined, along with command coding, error detection, busy signaling, and initialization and card-identification sequences. During identification, the host resets and initializes cards, checks operating voltage, sends ACMD41, obtains card IDs with CMD2, and assigns addresses with CMD3. Data-transfer mode uses CMD7 to select one card and supports addressed commands, block reads and writes, status polling, aborts, and programming operations.

UHS-I supports Default Speed, High Speed, SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 modes on a four-bit bus, with performance up to 104 MB/s. It requires 1.8 V signaling for higher-speed modes, uses CMD11 to switch voltage, and can use CMD19 tuning blocks to optimize sampling. UHS-II adds FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624 interface modes, reaching up to 624 MB/s, and supports a separate initialization sequence involving PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-command transport initialization. UHS-III terminology refers to extended UHS-II functions, including FD624.

Physical characteristics include standard card dimensions of 24 × 32 mm with thicknesses of 2.1 or 1.4 mm, SD and UHS-II pad assignments, card-detection and mode-selection circuitry, and registers for identification, addresses, capacity, configuration, status, and driver strength. Cards reset through power cycling or CMD0. ROM cards prohibit write and erase commands.

The specification also defines application performance classes, caching, self-maintenance, command queuing, and low-voltage initialization. Cache contents may be lost if not flushed before power-off.

Block transfers generally use 512-byte units, enforce address and length rules, verify CRCs, support partial-block conditions, and detect misalignment. Multiple-block writes are faster and may buffer data while programming; CMD12 stops transfers. Erase, DISCARD, and Full User Area Logical Erase operations apply to SDHC and SDXC cards.

Write protection can be mechanical, internal to the card, or password-based. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, password replacement, and forced erasure. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password and COP Unlock operation, restricting card access until the required COP sequence is completed.

NVIDIA Corporation reported that on November 6, 2017, wholly owned subsidiary NVIDIA Land exercised a purchase option to terminate ground and real property leases with Wachovia and purchase the property containing NVIDIA’s new Santa Clara campus building for approximately $350 million. The price includes repayment of participants’ investment, capitalized interest, accrued unpaid rent, and related expenses. Construction was substantially completed on October 31, 2017. After completion, NVIDIA Land will hold the property free of secured financing, and title transfer is expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018. NVIDIA also announced its third-quarter and first-nine-month fiscal 2018 results on November 9.

The player says two championships and his experience convinced him it was time to try the NHL, so he stayed in Finland longer. He credits the team’s scoring chances, urges them to shoot more and get pucks to the net, and says their first Stanley Cup Finals win calls for continued effort. He praises the Sharks’ organization and leadership.

TDSAT temporarily barred penalties against Airtel and Idea Cellular for unreported tariffs until further orders, though Trai may seek details of discounts or concessions. It stayed rules on tariff reporting and significant market power after Airtel received a show-cause notice. Trai’s 16 February norms require new tariffs to be reported within seven working days, retention offers disclosed online, and discounts, rebates or waivers treated as new tariffs. Reporting violations can incur ₹5,000 per day, capped at ₹2 lakh, while predatory tariffs by operators with at least 30% market activity may incur penalties up to ₹50 lakh per plan per circle.

MIT and Cambridge researchers found that jets and bubbles from the Phoenix cluster’s central supermassive black hole create 20,000-light-year filaments of cold gas, suggesting the black hole recycles hot gas into star-forming fuel and may help regulate star formation. Their ALMA observations, published in The Astrophysical Journal, offer insight into how black holes and galaxies evolve together.

This study examined whether placental biomarkers measured during the first and second trimesters are associated with retained placenta and/or postpartum hemorrhage requiring transfusion (RP/PPH). The analysis used 2,192 nulliparous participants from the NuMoM2b cohort; because blood-loss quantity and PPH diagnosis were unavailable, RP/PPH served as a proxy for severe bleeding. Sixty-seven participants (3.1%) experienced RP/PPH.

Compared with participants without RP/PPH, those with RP/PPH had higher second-trimester levels of soluble endoglin, β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1, as well as higher first-trimester sFlt-1 and sFlt-1/PlGF ratios. PlGF levels did not differ significantly. RP/PPH was also associated with preeclampsia, cesarean birth, and instrumental delivery. Among participants without preeclampsia, second-trimester β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 remained significantly elevated in those later experiencing RP/PPH; no biomarker significantly distinguished RP/PPH among preeclamptic participants. Biomarker changes from the first to second trimester also varied by preeclampsia status.

The findings identify early placental biomarkers as potential targets for further study of PPH risk prediction. Limitations include the small number of RP/PPH cases, reliance on retained placenta or transfusion-requiring hemorrhage rather than direct blood-loss measurements, overrepresentation of adverse pregnancy outcomes, and the exploratory nature of the analysis.

Five Gor Mahia players — Meddie Kagere, Musa Mohamed, Kenneth Muguna, Jacques Tuyisenge and George Odhiambo — head the 2017 Kenyan Premier League MVP shortlist, which could give the club a third consecutive player of the year award. After KPL management postponed their awards, the Sports Journalists Association of Kenya (SJAK) will host its own event, sponsored in part by LG, on December 18 with eight categories including Golden Glove, Defender, Midfielder, Golden Boot, MVP, Young/New Player, Coach and a special SJAK Award. Goalkeeper Patrick Matasi leads his category seeking to defend the title.

Patterns provide distributed-systems developers with a shared vocabulary, enabling quicker understanding, knowledge sharing, and further learning. Common names and definitions reduce arguments over terminology and let teams focus directly on core concepts, details, and implementation, as demonstrated by the container community’s adoption of “sidecar.”

Former firefighter-paramedic Luis Garcia used nearly $40,000 of his savings to buy 800 doses of naloxone, commonly called Narcan, and has traveled Florida training businesses, residents and law enforcement while distributing it free. After responding to about 3,000 overdoses during 28 years with the Boynton Beach Fire Department, Garcia began carrying Narcan and administering it with CPR at public overdoses, reviving five of six people he assisted in the previous year and a half. At a 2018 Treasure Coast Substance Awareness Coalition event in Shepard Park, he gave about 50 doses to attendees who received 30-minute instruction. His South Florida Opioid Crisis Mortality Reduction Project supplies businesses and educates agencies that lack Narcan. Treasure Coast law enforcement increasingly carried the drug as overdose deaths rose from 2014 to 2016; in 2017, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office used it 62 times while responding to 153 overdose cases. Coalition co-founder Frank Bianco said stigma surrounding addiction remains, while participants praised the event for spreading awareness and treatment needs.

U.S. home prices rose 0.9% in the latest quarter, while annual growth increased to 6.1%, the highest year-over-year rate since February 2015. Regional quarterly growth was 0.8% in the Midwest, 0.7% in the Northeast, and 1.0% in both the South and West. San Jose and Hartford each posted 0.3% quarterly declines, while Portland grew nearly 2% and was the fastest-growing market. Eight major metros grew at least 1.5% quarterly, compared with three a year earlier. Sixteen of the 50 largest metropolitan housing markets exceeded their housing-bubble price peaks, and record-setting major and micro markets represented about one-third of national housing stock. Another 5% was within 5.8% of 2006 price levels. Clear Capital projected 2–3% annual price growth in 2017; if growth approached 2016 levels, nearly 40% of homeowners who bought during the housing bubble could be above water by year-end.

The Steelers have won eight consecutive games, including a 39-38 win over Baltimore, and will host the Patriots in Week 15 with the AFC’s top seed at stake. Four of their last five wins were by three points or fewer, Ryan Shazier is injured, and Brady is playing at an MVP level.

Oversold markets or stocks have declined significantly over a defined period and may exhibit mean reversion, with short-term rebounds followed by longer-term returns moving toward average levels. The passage advocates objective criteria, such as a three-day RSI below 20, and backtesting. The example strategy buys at the close when RSI is below 20 and sells when the market closes above the previous day’s high. Reported S&P 500 backtest results from 1985 onward include a 0.64% average gain per trade, 75% win rate, and 26% maximum drawdown, with trade counts, CAGR, and profit factor reported as either 484, 7.7%, and 2.5 or 448, 7.6%, and 2.4. Dividends were excluded. The strategy performed poorly before 1990, and the passage cautions that historical mean reversion may not always persist.

This secondary analysis assessed the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s COVID-19 vaccination programme from April 2021 to March 2022 using Ministry of Health and WHO African Region data. Sixteen of 26 provinces began vaccination. By March 2022, 5.7% of the population had received at least one dose and 1.03% were fully vaccinated. Full-vaccination coverage was highest in Kasai-Oriental (6.91%) and lowest in Tshuapa (0.03%), Kwilu (0.07%), and Équateur (0.02%). Functional vaccination sites increased over time but remained unevenly distributed, with Kinshasa consistently reporting the most. Monthly uptake peaked at 378,782 doses in February 2022 before declining, while second-dose uptake showed little change. Men outnumbered women among vaccinated people in every province except Kasai-Oriental. Completed primary vaccination was reported for 8,302 healthcare workers and 46,495 older adults.

AstraZeneca was the least requested vaccine (2%), while Janssen accounted for 48%, Moderna 25%, and Pfizer 17%. Compared with nine Central African countries, the DRC had received 14.4 million doses but administered 1.14 million, or 8% of those received; 2% of its population had received at least one dose.

The authors attributed low and uneven coverage to AstraZeneca-related safety concerns and vaccine hesitancy, competing Ebola and other disease outbreaks, limited health-worker capacity, strikes, vaccine expiry and logistics problems, and inadequate targeting of high-risk groups. A national acceleration plan reportedly led to more than 2.5 million vaccinations in three months, but the country missed its target of vaccinating 11 million people by April 2022. The authors call for stronger health systems, community engagement, and integration of COVID-19 vaccination with primary healthcare. Limitations included uncertain high-risk-group denominators, incomplete vaccination histories, aggregated data, limited generalizability, and likely underestimation of comorbidities.

London’s recent surge in IPO listings has revived hopes for the Stock Exchange as a major listing venue after hosting only three IPOs, representing 2% of Europe’s market, early in 2025. Deals span consumer goods, fintech, and real estate, with Beauty Tech Group’s £300 million debut, Shawbrook’s potential £2 billion listing, and Princes Group’s planned offering adding momentum. Analysts say sustained success depends on strong order books and post-listing trading, while Norway’s Visma is considering a large 2026 London float.

The passage traces the rise of “social capital” from James Coleman’s late-1980s research to Robert Putnam’s early-1990s work on Italian democracy. Putnam linked northern Italy’s stronger civic engagement and economic performance to its history of independent city-states, contrasting it with southern Italy’s autocratic rule and mafia culture. His claim that civic-group membership correlated with regional growth differences is presented as correlation rather than causation.

Putnam’s 1990s book *Bowling Alone*, which argued that declining group participation and social connectedness contributed to social problems, helped popularize social capital among academics and policymakers and made him a highly cited scholar. The passage distinguishes competing definitions: civic or group engagement and generalized trust. A 1996 Knack-Keefer study reportedly found generalized trust, but not civic membership, significantly associated with European economic growth.

It also distinguishes “bridging” social capital, which connects groups, from “bonding” capital, which reinforces in-group solidarity. Putnam has found that ethnic fragmentation and diversity generally do not increase measured social capital, a result criticized as depressing but also appropriated by ethnonationalists and Trump supporters as a vindication of bonding capital.

Tesla Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2019 reported revenue of $6.35 billion, compared with $4.00 billion a year earlier. Automotive revenue rose to $5.38 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $368.2 million, and services and other revenue reached $605.1 million. The First Circuit dismissed the government’s interlocutory appeal because the district court’s orders were not reviewable under 18 U.S.C. § 3731. In the underlying prosecution, Anthony Spera was a key witness linking defendants Watson and O’Hearn to the charged crimes. Although the prosecutor asked Immigration and Naturalization Service officials to defer Spera’s deportation and notify them of custody changes, the request was overlooked, and Spera was deported to Italy shortly before trial.

The government sought a continuance to arrange Spera’s return or take his deposition abroad. The district court denied both the initial and renewed continuance motions, citing the case’s age, the Speedy Trial Act, the government’s negligence in losing the witness, and the likely six-to-twelve-month delay. It then denied the deposition request as moot.

The court held that § 3731 authorizes appeals only from pretrial orders directly suppressing or excluding evidence. Although the statute is construed liberally and substance controls over form, an order’s incidental effect on the government’s ability to gather or present evidence is insufficient. Because the challenged orders were routine case-management decisions intended to prevent further delay, rather than rulings on the admissibility of Spera’s testimony, they fell outside § 3731. The appeal was therefore dismissed for lack of appellate jurisdiction.

Based on Micheal A. Gayed’s 2015 paper, the article develops a lumber/gold ratio strategy for allocating between stocks and bonds. Lumber futures serve as a leading economic indicator, while gold offers diversification and low correlation with other assets. Gayed’s original rules invested in stocks during risk-on periods and long-term Treasuries during risk-off periods. The modified backtest used WOOD, GLD, SPY, and TLT. Editorial notes supplement the printed documents with omitted material, source locations, related-document references, event descriptions, and cited public statements; memoirs and other firsthand accounts are used where appropriate to clarify the official record. Index numbers refer to documents, not pages. The Advisory Committee on Historical Diplomatic Documentation monitors compilation and editorial processes and advises on series preparation and declassification, reviewing volumes as needed rather than necessarily reviewing each one. A 2015–2019 Department of State review sought to release all information except where national-security requirements applied, with concurrence from relevant bureaus, agencies, and foreign governments. The review withheld one document, removed a paragraph or more from 13 documents, and made minor excisions in 20. The Office of the Historian considers the resulting documentation a thorough, accurate, and reliable record of Reagan administration policy toward the Soviet Union from January 1983 to March 1985.

This volume documents U.S.–Soviet relations during that period and, drawing on National Security Decision Directive 75, examines the administration’s four-part agenda: arms control, human rights, regional issues, and bilateral relations. It focuses on policy development by George Shultz, William Clark, Robert McFarlane, and Jack Matlock, particularly through the National Security Council and Department of State, and their promotion of these policies in meetings with Soviet Ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin and Foreign Minister Andrei Gromyko. Although Reagan did not meet Soviet General Secretaries Yuri Andropov or Konstantin Chernenko, the documents show how his administration assessed Soviet leadership and formulated policy toward whoever was in charge.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a hybrid rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Each Streaming Multiprocessor includes an RT Core with dedicated units for bounding-box tests and ray-triangle intersection testing. RT Cores autonomously traverse Bounding Volume Hierarchies and return hit or no-hit results, freeing the SM for vertex, pixel, and compute shading. The driver manages BVH building and refitting, while applications manage ray generation and shading. Combined with denoising, optimized BVH structures, and RTX-compatible APIs, RT Cores enable more than 10 billion rays per second and approximately tenfold faster ray tracing than Pascal’s software implementation.

NGX is a Turing-only deep-learning technology stack within NVIDIA RTX. It uses neural networks and Neural Services, accelerated by Turing Tensor Cores, to provide pre-trained AI features through a thin API integrated with CUDA 10, DirectX, Vulkan, and TensorRT. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) is trained against 64-times-supersampled reference images and matching lower-quality inputs. Standard DLSS produces TAA-like quality with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X produces images approaching 64-times-supersampled quality. DLSS also improves temporal stability and handles complex motion and transparency better than TAA.

Other NGX features include Inpainting, which synthesizes replacement content for removed image areas; AI Slow-Mo, which analyzes frames and motion to generate interpolated slow-motion frames; and AI Super Rez, which uses AI to enlarge images or video by 2x, 4x, or 8x while preserving detail and depth of field.

Mesh Shading adds task and mesh shader stages with cooperative thread models. Task shaders dynamically process object lists, launch mesh shaders, select level-of-detail versions, and eliminate per-object CPU draw calls. This enables real-time rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects and supports geometry culling and manipulation such as spherical CAD cutaways.

Variable Rate Shading allows each 16-by-16-pixel region to use a different shading rate without changing its visibility rate. Supported algorithms include content-adaptive shading for regions with little color change, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that reduces shading away from the viewer’s focus. VRS can also increase shading rates when using MSAA, up to the sample count.

Texture Space Shading stores shading results as texture-space texels, separating visibility sampling from appearance shading. It enables independent sampling rates and grids, reuse of spatial and temporal shading results, MIP-map-based rate control, improved temporal stability, and efficient stereo VR rendering in which one eye’s shaded texels can serve the other eye.

Multi-View Rendering supports up to four views per hardware pass and up to 32 at the API level. It fetches and shades geometry once while sharing view-independent computations and calculating view-dependent attributes per view. Turing’s implementation expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection capabilities and supports varied VR projections, multiple character poses, and multiple shadow buffers in a single pass. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, mixed-resource heaps, USB Type-C and VirtualLink support, foveated VR rendering, and expanded VRWorks Audio.

The TU104 configuration contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and 13.6 billion transistors. The Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth for data-center inference. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, has 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, a 256-bit interface, and 10.8 billion transistors; it does not support NVLink or SLI.

Turing’s RTX-OPS metric weights operation types according to representative hybrid-rendering use. One workload model assumes tensor operations at 20 percent, CUDA cores at 80 percent, RT cores at 40 percent, and INT32 pipelines at 28 percent, producing 78 RTX-OPS for the RTX 2080 Ti example.

Ray tracing casts rays backward from the camera to efficiently model reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. BVH trees reduce intersection tests by progressively testing smaller bounding volumes, while denoising reduces the number of rays required. Ray-traced shadows can reproduce contact hardening from area lights, ray-traced ambient occlusion provides more realistic geometric definition than screen-space occlusion, and ray-traced reflections avoid the holes and artifacts of screen-space and probe-based methods. Hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH traversal, and dedicated RT Cores together bring these effects to real-time graphics.

This patent disclosure concerns augmented-reality systems, particularly localization of the position and orientation of users’ heads, hands, totems, haptic devices, and other physical objects for accurate placement of virtual content. It is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 15/898,212 and claims priority to Provisional Patent Application Ser. No. 62/459,802, filed February 16, 2017.

The background describes challenges in rendering stable virtual objects within real-world environments as users move their heads. Accurate, low-latency head tracking is needed to prevent visual instability, sensory mismatch, motion sickness, and simulator sickness. Existing localization methods are described as insufficiently fast or precise, particularly when correlating real-object coordinates with virtual coordinates.

Described embodiments include a head-mounted AR display that monitors sensor information and triggers retrieval and presentation of identified virtual content. Another embodiment uses stacked waveguides with different wavefront divergences and focal depths, cameras to capture the ambient environment, and QR-code recognition to obtain a network address from which virtual content is requested. Content-sharing embodiments transmit an activation gateway after a first user interacts with virtual content, solicit acceptance from another user, and then send the content or a sharing credential enabling direct transfer.

The detailed description presents a wearable architecture comprising a headset with a display, frame, and speakers, a local processing and data module, and optional remote cloud processing and storage. Sensors may include cameras, microphones, inertial measurement units, accelerometers, compasses, GPS receivers, radios, and gyroscopes. A cloud-based passable world model may store tagged imagery, two- and three-dimensional points, and other environmental information for distributing updated scene data among users.

Electromagnetic tracking is described in detail. Orthogonal emitter coils establish a known field, while orthogonal sensor coils attached to tracked objects measure induced behavior to calculate three-dimensional position and orientation. Electromagnetic data may be combined with IMU, camera, depth-sensor, and other data. Compact emitters may be incorporated into handheld controllers, totems, haptic devices, or belt-mounted packs, with sensors placed on the headset, belt pack, or body. Reduced duty cycles and IMU-assisted tracking may lower power use. Electromagnetic tracking is presented as accurate and low-latency, although field strength declines cubically with distance, favoring close sensor-to-emitter spacing.

Additional embodiments address component miniaturization, integrated and distributed sensing coils, ferrite cores, time-division multiplexing, dynamically tunable resonant circuits, electromagnetic interference cancellation, summing amplifiers, calibration patterns, and calibration based on cameras, depth sensors, ultrasonic timing, and virtual targets. The disclosure also compares passive stereo, active stereo, structured-light, modulated time-of-flight, and direct time-of-flight depth sensing, including their respective limitations involving texture, lighting, field of view, computation, resolution, multipath errors, size, and cost.

Vision-based pose estimation using outward-facing cameras is described through feature extraction, triangulation, sparse 3D mapping, 2D-to-3D correspondence, and camera-pose estimation. The process may use new key frames as viewpoint changes and may divide operation into pre-tracking, tracking, low-latency mapping, latency-tolerant bundle adjustment, and post-mapping cleanup. IMU-derived pose priors may support feature prediction, while semantic segmentation or object detection may exclude moving people, vehicles, and other nonstatic features. The passage also describes IMU, optical, electromagnetic, and depth sensor fusion for faster pose updates and resolving ambiguities. Drawings depict numerous AR applications, including navigation, gaming, training, healthcare, shopping, workplace collaboration, communications, education, and entertainment.

The paper develops scalable Boltzmann Generators for equilibrium sampling of large crystalline materials. It introduces a local augmented coupling-flow architecture that uses graph neural networks to encode particle environments, trains from the potential energy without target-distribution samples, and scales linearly with system size by using a fixed number of neighbors. Models can be trained on small cells and transferred to much larger systems, while conditioning on thermodynamic state, box shape, or interaction parameters amortizes training costs.

Tests on Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber crystals, including monatomic water, silicon, and germanium, show that models trained on 216–256 particles generate structures and energy distributions consistent with molecular dynamics after transfer to systems exceeding 1,000 particles. Local models achieve higher effective sample sizes and substantially lower training costs than global attention-based models, though efficiency decreases as system size grows.

The trained generators provide accurate Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies, including absolute values, phase free-energy differences, and Gibbs estimates under volume fluctuations, largely agreeing with MD+MBAR references. Conditional models reproduce crystal phase behavior across interaction strength, temperature, and pressure, including the silicon coexistence line. The work identifies liquid sampling and broader generalization across chemical space as future directions.

The passage outlines several SOS defensive disruption schemes. Baseline defense pushes wing ballhandlers toward the corner or baseline checkpoint, applies a hard “smother” if the dribble stops before the checkpoint, and uses automatic “Base Go I” traps when the ballhandler penetrates inside it. During the trap, the low helpside defender locks up while the remaining defenders rotate into help positions, deny passes, front posts, and close out. A no-trap rule applies when there is no penetration inside the checkpoint.

“Base Go Red” is a predetermined early sideline trap used briefly to disrupt the offense, change tempo, and create easy baskets. The nearest defender traps immediately, while the others rotate into Triangle I positions and apply SOS near-player rotation rules.

For side-screen offenses above the free-throw line, defenders use aggressive contact switches to deny quick jump shots and middle penetration. Below the line, they trap the ballhandler before the screen develops, deny return passes, front rolling post players, and cover pass-outs, skip passes, and post entries through double teams, snuggle denials, and helpside rotations.

The “All Out” disruption attacks the point guard before the first screen or pass option, forcing a “free lance” situation. If the ballhandler passes to the rolling post, a secondary baseline trap is used. Rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands, after which matched-up players resume basic SOS fundamentals.

At American University’s commencement, the president praises the institution’s commitment to learning and public service and urges graduates to serve their nation and time. He calls for genuine world peace—not peace imposed through weapons or the “security of the slave,” but peace that allows people and nations to grow, build better lives, and protect future generations.

Arguing that nuclear total war is irrational, he says human problems are man-made and therefore solvable. Practical peace requires gradual institutional change, concrete agreements, tolerance, and peaceful settlement of disputes. Americans should reject fatalistic views of conflict and reassess their attitudes toward the Soviet Union, recognizing Russian achievements, shared fears of war, and common interests in ending the arms race.

He urges policies that make peace beneficial to all parties, including nonprovocative and controlled weapons, avoidance of dangerous confrontations, a stronger United Nations, expanded communication, arms-control negotiations, and staged disarmament. He announces that he, Khrushchev, and Prime Minister Macmillan have agreed to high-level Moscow discussions toward a comprehensive nuclear-test-ban treaty. He also declares that the United States will not conduct atmospheric nuclear tests while other states refrain and will not be the first to resume them.

Finally, he connects foreign peace with freedom, human rights, and responsible government at home. Americans must protect civil rights, respect law and others’ rights, and ensure that peace and freedom exist within the country as well as internationally. The United States will not start a war, but will remain prepared, seek to prevent conflict, and work toward a world in which the weak are safe and the strong are just.

The disclosure describes technologies for configuring and reducing resource use in time-aware networks (TANs) and time-sensitive applications (TSAs), emphasizing low-latency, scalable gate control, shared physical links, and time-aware energy-efficient communication.

It reviews IEEE TSN and Precision Time Protocol architecture, including gPTP domains, PTP end and relay instances, grandmaster selection via BMCA, PTP and arbitrary timescales, timestamped event messages, and media-specific implementations. It also explains IEEE 802.1Q transmission selection using traffic classes and strict-priority, credit-based, or enhanced transmission-selection algorithms, along with IEEE 802.1Qbv scheduled traffic using per-queue transmission gates controlled by gate control lists.

A described NIC implementation moves the gate control list from dedicated on-chip memory into host memory while retaining two banks and a small prefetch buffer. A dedicated DMA/RDMA channel allows the MAC to prefetch and parse gate entries, prepare payloads for queues scheduled to open, and alternate between banks as software programs the next list. This arrangement supports lower cycle times and finer scheduling granularity while reducing NIC memory, silicon area, and power consumption compared with continuously clocked on-chip gate-list memory.

The disclosure further presents complex end-station configurations that allow multiple talker applications to share one physical network interface. Such devices may appear to centralized management as multiple virtual end stations connected through a virtual switch or bridge. The text discusses stream reservation, talker and listener declarations, VLAN registration, resource allocation, and dynamic configuration intended to reduce interference among applications and remain independent of higher-level protocols and orchestration frameworks. Example deployments include IoT, industrial automation, data centers, telecommunications, audiovisual systems, vehicles, and power grids.

In this inaugural address, the speaker affirmed that democracy had prevailed and that the peaceful transfer of power was proceeding on Capitol grounds where violence had recently sought to disrupt it. He noted that former President Carter, unable to attend, was saluted for his lifetime of service, and marked the swearing-in of Kamala Harris as the first woman elected to national office.

He described the nation's crises: a once-in-a-century virus that killed as many Americans in a year as were lost in all of World War II, millions of jobs lost, hundreds of thousands of businesses closed, a long-awaited cry for racial justice, a cry from the planet, and rising political extremism, white supremacy, and domestic terrorism. He argued that overcoming these challenges required unity against anger, hatred, extremism, lawlessness, violence, disease, joblessness, and hopelessness. Drawing on Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation and the nation's history through the Civil War, the Depression, the world wars, and 9/11, he said Americans' "better angels" had always prevailed and could do so again. He called for ending the "uncivil war" between red and blue, rural and urban, conservative and liberal, treating each other as neighbors with dignity and respect, rejecting manufactured facts, and ensuring disagreement did not lead to disunion. He pledged to be a president for all Americans, calling peaceful dissent the nation's greatest strength, and named opportunity, security, liberty, dignity, respect, honor, and truth as the shared American values.

He urged Americans to set aside politics and face the pandemic as one nation, to repair alliances and reengage with the world leading by example, and requested a silent prayer for the 400,000 Americans lost to the pandemic. He closed by pledging to level with the country, defend the Constitution, democracy, and America, and serve the public good, writing together an American story of hope, unity, healing, and goodness.

ProShares UltraPro QQQ (TQQQ) is an ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100 and offers exposure to the technology sector. Unlike stock trading, option trading involves contracts granting the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying security at a predetermined price within a specified period. TQQQ offers American- and European-style options, as well as puts and calls with varying expiration dates and strike prices.

Common TQQQ option strategies include buying calls for anticipated price increases, buying puts for anticipated declines or hedging, writing covered calls for income, writing puts to acquire shares at a lower price or collect premiums, and combining these approaches. The appropriate strategy depends on market conditions, investment goals, risk tolerance, time horizon, and available capital.

Options provide leverage and potentially higher returns, but they are speculative and can produce losses exceeding the amount invested. Risks include unfavorable price movements, changes in option terms or market sentiment, leverage, broker margin requirements, slippage, and commissions. The passage therefore emphasizes setting a maximum loss, investing only what can be lost, using risk-management tools such as stop-loss orders, diversifying, and avoiding leverage until strategies have been tested.

Traders are advised to select liquid options, consider volatility and expiration dates, and backtest strategies before committing money. Entry and exit timing should align with expected price movements and target prices. Fair value can be estimated with the Black-Scholes model, supplemented by fundamental and technical analysis.

Broker requirements determine the minimum capital needed, while trading costs generally include commissions, contract fees, and slippage. Profits are generally subject to capital gains tax, depending on individual and jurisdictional circumstances. Applicable regulations may cover capital, leverage, margin calls, stop-loss orders, and hedging, so investors should consult qualified brokers about local rules and tax specialists about taxation.

University at Albany chemists synthesized manganese diboride (MnB₂), a boron-rich compound reported to be over 20% more energetic by weight and about 150% more energetic by volume than aluminum used in solid rocket boosters. It remains stable until ignited with an agent such as kerosene, potentially reducing rocket fuel mass and storage volume. The compound was produced by compressing manganese and boron powders into a pellet, heating it to 3,000°C in an arc melter, and rapidly cooling it. Computational models showed that its skewed, strained atomic structure stores substantial potential energy released upon combustion. Researchers also see potential applications in more durable catalytic converters and plastic-breakdown catalysis.

For games, Vagnoni and his wife, Dawn, host 125 to 175 friends and family in their 2,000-square-foot home locker room, featuring a 35-foot bar, 16 televisions and extensive Eagles memorabilia, including turf from Veterans Stadium. Guests wear Eagles gear and follow family-friendly rules. Vagnoni leads cheers and plays a drum while Dawn handles food, security and photography.

The couple planned to welcome more than 100 people for Super Bowl LII with entertainment and free food and drinks. Vagnoni called the gatherings his lifelong passion and said his late father would have been thrilled to see the Eagles reach the Super Bowl.

Gaps are price intervals with little or no trading between one session’s close and the next open, often caused by news or market imbalances. Overnight daily gaps are most common. Major categories include common, exhaustion, runaway, and breakaway gaps.

Gap strategies either fade gaps toward the prior close or follow them in the gap direction. Stocks generally show more mean reversion, while other assets are less likely to revert. Smaller gaps are filled more often; 25 years of E-mini S&P 500 data showed same-day fill rates of 59–61% for gaps of at least 0.1%, 42–43% for 0.5%, and 28–33% for 1%.

Gap trading has become less profitable as increased computing power, participation, and arbitrage have eliminated easier opportunities. Reliable backtest data and more selective filters are necessary, though over-filtering increases curve-fitting risk. Simple intraday examples were unprofitable or only marginally improved. An overnight swing strategy produced an average gain near 0.5% per trade and a 1.8 profit factor. Predicting gaps in advance is considered nearly impossible, although backtesting may improve trading odds.

A review of 10 trials involving 77,917 people with prior heart attacks, strokes, diabetes, or other cardiovascular risks found that omega-3 supplements did not reduce deaths from heart disease, nonfatal heart attacks, strokes, or procedures to reopen clogged arteries. Small apparent reductions in some outcomes were not statistically significant and could have occurred by chance. The findings question guidelines recommending supplements for cardiovascular prevention in patients with prior coronary heart disease, though study authors noted variation in trial designs and missing smoking and cancer-history data. Outside experts said omega-3 supplements are inexpensive and generally safe, advised current users not to stop, and noted regular fatty fish consumption and possible benefits for weight, cognition, and eye health.

Boscov’s downtown Wilkes-Barre store is thriving as Bon-Ton and Sears close, with loyal customers citing longtime staff, personal service, convenience, and a hometown atmosphere. Physical-store sales rose by a single-digit percentage, and officials say Boscov’s supports other downtown shops. The company plans to open a 47th store in Connecticut.

Schools require comprehensive pedagogical renewal to respond to rapid societal and technological change while developing learners as whole personalities. Education must shift from digital to generative pedagogy as physical and cyber worlds, artificial intelligence, blended learning, and the Net generation reshape knowledge acquisition and teaching. Tracing technological waves from industrialization through digital networks to generative AI reveals both creative opportunities and destructive disruptions. AI will increasingly function as an educator’s partner, transforming the teacher’s role, knowledge production, and assessment while raising unresolved questions about authority, values, and human–AI symbiosis.

Bayard’s annual audit received an “unmodified” state rating, despite two minor findings: a $700 deficit caused by underbudgeting revenue in a new federal block-grant fund and $64 in mileage calculation errors.

The City Council unanimously supported Santa Clara’s effort to obtain management of Fort Bayard without city financial involvement. Santa Clara plans to rehabilitate the deteriorating property for economic development, including renting office space to the U.S. Forest Service, though council members questioned the village’s financial and personnel capacity. The state owns the fort, while the Department of Health manages it.

Mayor Pro Tem Chon Fierro also reported plans to restore the historic Bayard train depot. The city owns the building, but the railroad owns the underlying ground, and city officials are working with railroad representatives to resolve associated issues.

Camps combine horse and farm-animal activities with hay rides, park exploration, and outings; summer camp includes weekly Texas Station visits and a Friday water slide. Reduced rates are available for veterans, military personnel, law enforcement, teachers, and nurses, while teen volunteers can earn community-service hours. The nonprofit also offers riding lessons, parties, field trips, workshops, and test rides at its Floyd Lamb at Tule Springs facility.
