The President returned House Bill 1471 without approval because it would double Andrew J. Hill’s pension, while Pension Bureau records and medical evidence identified the intended beneficiary as Alfred J. Hill. He argued that special pension legislation should be rare and exceptional, and that the Pension Bureau should be empowered or reorganized to handle claims fairly. Of nearly 240 special pension bills reviewed, the President approved 81 whose claims were denied for insufficient proof, assuming they were meritorious and waiving full proof. Unable to object within the constitutional deadline, he allowed the remaining bills to take effect without his approval, estimating their annual cost at more than $35,000.

Motley Fool Money’s review highlights the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card as a $0-annual-fee option for paying down debt or financing a large purchase. It offers 0% intro APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. Balance transfers must be made within 120 days and carry a 5% fee, with a $5 minimum. The card includes up to $600 of cellphone protection for theft or damage, subject to a $25 deductible, but no ongoing rewards and a 3% foreign transaction fee. A recommended credit score of 670–850 does not guarantee approval. The review concludes that the card is best suited to borrowers who can use the introductory period, not those seeking ongoing perks.

Both Mi 8 models include a Snapdragon 845, 6GB RAM, a 6.21-inch AMOLED screen, dual-frequency GPS, dual 12MP rear cameras, and AI-enabled studio lighting. The budget-focused Mi 8 SE is the first device with Snapdragon 710, has a 3,120mAh battery and 12MP/5MP rear cameras, and starts at 1,799 yuan.

The Mid Screen offense, a common tactic in which a big screens for a smaller ballhandler, creates dribble-penetration and post-up or shooting problems. Because switching allows the dribbler to flare to the wing and the screener to post up a smaller defender, NBA teams generally prefer a three-phase Show & Recover: the on-ball defender pushes toward the sideline while the screener’s defender shows, with help and pass-denial assignments; after the screen, the defender recovers to the post; the final defense denies passes, pushes handlers toward corners or baselines, and uses weak-side help. An alternative All Out SOS strategy disrupts the offense by trapping the point guard before the first screen or pass. Defenders rotate as the pass leaves the passer, apply closeouts, deny return passes, and maintain help positions, with optional baseline, Base Go I/Red, and post traps.

Xu Yan, wife of detained Chinese human rights lawyer Yu Wensheng, said police prevented her from leaving her neighborhood and told taxi drivers not to take her. Yu was charged with inciting subversion after calling for constitutional reform and open presidential elections, amid a crackdown on legal activists.

ChatGPT is an OpenAI conversational AI based on the GPT architecture that generates human-like text and code. For trading, it can help create technical indicators, strategies, algorithms, sentiment analysis, forecasts, risk-management insights, and market-monitoring prompts by processing historical data, financial news, and social media posts.

The passage recommends treating ChatGPT as a development tool rather than a complete trading system. Traders must review and debug generated code, backtest strategies on historical data, validate predictions with other sources, and potentially test profitable strategies with small live positions. ChatGPT cannot identify the most profitable strategies, automate trading by itself, or guarantee correct results.

In one test, ChatGPT produced logical mean-reversion rules based on the Relative Strength Index, but the strategy generated few trades, while its AmiBroker code contained numerous errors. The conclusion is that ChatGPT is useful for hints and code generation, but human review, experience, and validation remain essential.

AI pattern trading uses algorithms to detect recurring patterns in large amounts of historical market data, potentially improving speed and adaptability, though unpredictable market behavior and algorithmic bias remain challenges. The passage also notes that ChatGPT differs from traditional strategies and ready-made automated trading systems because it is a flexible tool used to create custom systems rather than a deployable trading product.

The volume documents Shultz’s bureaucratic efforts to advance the four-part NSDD 75 agenda, secure access to President Reagan, and preserve U.S.-Soviet dialogue. It covers the 1983–85 tensions surrounding the KAL 007 downing, Reagan’s Strategic Defense Initiative, the Euromissiles crisis, and the Able Archer exercise. Following the Soviet walkout from INF negotiations, the administration sought to restart arms-control talks, with disputes over SDI remaining a major obstacle. In January 1985, Shultz and Gromyko agreed to three-track Nuclear and Space Talks covering START, INF, and defense and space. The volume concludes that the talks would begin as Soviet leader Chernenko died and a younger leader emerged. It also acknowledges the assistance of government agencies, archives, and individuals who supported the volume’s research and review.

Cell2Text is a multimodal generative framework that converts single-cell RNA-seq profiles into biologically grounded natural-language descriptions. It uses a frozen, pretrained Geneformer encoder to produce gene-level embeddings, a lightweight two-layer adapter to project them into a language model’s semantic space, and an instruction-tuned LLM decoder based on Llama-3.2-1B or Gemma3-4B. Training included full fine-tuning and LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Llama-3.2-1B.

The training and evaluation dataset contains 1 million cells from CELLxGENE, spanning 7,331 donors, 783 cell types, 347 tissues, and 128 diseases. Descriptions combine metadata, Cell Ontology definitions, and the two most active pathways identified from 34 Hallmark pathways using pySCENIC. Data were split by donor into 80/10/10 training, validation, and test sets.

Generated descriptions achieved strong lexical overlap and biomedical semantic fidelity, including BioBERT F1 scores above 93%. Fully fine-tuned Cell2Text models outperformed Geneformer classification-head and LightGBM baselines in cell-type, tissue, and disease prediction; Gemma3-4B achieved 77.83% cell-type and 73.04% tissue accuracy, while Llama-1B achieved 77.84% disease accuracy. A Cell Ontology Personalized PageRank evaluation showed that predictions were biologically related even when incorrect, with Gemma3-4B reaching 85.62% average similarity. Pathway prediction was competitive, exceeding the Geneformer-head baseline but generally trailing LightGBM on ranking metrics.

This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study examined how intranasal and oral oxytocin (OT) affect responses to social touch. A final sample of 171 healthy Chinese adults received 24 IU of intranasal OT, oral OT, or placebo. Participants received 15-minute sessions of gentle stroking at 5 cm/s, intended to activate CT fibers, and medium-pressure massage at the same velocity, intended primarily to activate non-CT pressure receptors. Pleasantness, arousal, intensity, and willingness to pay were assessed, while fNIRS measured orbitofrontal cortex, posterior superior temporal sulcus, and somatosensory cortex activity. Skin conductance, heart-rate variability, and plasma OT concentrations were also measured.

Both OT routes increased plasma OT, with a larger initial increase after intranasal than oral administration. OT groups rated both stimulation types as more pleasant than placebo overall, but the treatment-by-condition interaction showed that both intranasal and oral OT specifically increased pleasantness ratings for gentle stroking, not medium-pressure massage. Massage was rated as more pleasant, intense, and arousing than gentle stroking, with greater willingness to pay. OT did not significantly affect arousal, intensity, or willingness to pay.

Gentle stroking produced greater activity in the medial and mediolateral orbitofrontal cortices and posterior superior temporal sulcus than massage, whereas massage produced greater somatosensory cortex activity. Both OT routes enhanced activity in the medial and mediolateral orbitofrontal cortices and posterior superior temporal sulcus during gentle stroking only, with no significant effects in the lateral orbitofrontal cortex, somatosensory cortex, or during massage. OT also prolonged rather than clearly increased the initial neural response to gentle stroking. These regional time courses discriminated intranasal OT from placebo with 70.1% accuracy and oral OT from placebo with 64.3% accuracy, but did not significantly distinguish intranasal from oral OT. OT did not affect skin conductance or heart-rate variability.

Post-treatment plasma OT concentrations correlated with pleasantness and mediolateral orbitofrontal activity during gentle stroking. Mediation analyses indicated that increased plasma OT fully mediated the effects of both OT routes on pleasantness, but not the neural effects. The findings support selective enhancement of hedonic and neural responses to CT-fiber-mediated gentle touch by both routes, primarily through peripheral OT changes. The precise peripheral mechanism remains unresolved. Limitations included fNIRS measuring only superficial cortical activity, the unnatural leg-massage setting, no direct measurement of applied pressure, and limited blood sampling during stimulation.

The address cites abundant harvests, flourishing commerce, unexpectedly high revenue, and preserved peace with foreign nations as grounds for gratitude to Providence. Negotiations with Great Britain opened over general commerce and unresolved disputes, while the existing commercial convention was extended for at least eight years to prevent an interruption in trade.

Relations with Spain remain largely unsettled. Although Spain ratified the 1802 convention addressing some spoliation claims, other claims, boundary issues, and compensation remained unresolved. The message attributes insecurity in the Floridas to the collapse of Spanish authority, which allowed adventurers, fugitives, escaped slaves, and Indian tribes to evade U.S. laws, undermine revenue, and attack American citizens. After adventurers occupied Amelia Island, the United States suppressed their establishment. Major-General Jackson was then authorized to pursue the Seminoles in Florida. Spanish officers were accused of encouraging the war and supplying the Seminoles, prompting Jackson to seize St. Marks and Pensacola. The government ordered the posts returned to Spanish representatives to avoid altering relations, while holding Spain responsible for treaty violations and long-delayed compensation.

The Spanish civil war in South America continued. Buenos Ayres, Chile, and Venezuela had declared independence; other regions remained independent or outside direct Spanish control. Allied powers were mediating but appeared unlikely to use force. The United States therefore continued its existing policy of neutrality. Relations with France, Russia, and other powers remained friendly.

Treasury receipts for the first three quarters exceeded $17 million, with more than $2 million expected to remain after appropriations. Customs revenue reached $21 million and was estimated for the year at no less than $26 million, while public-land sales exceeded those of previous years. Stronger enforcement of revenue laws benefited domestic manufactures, though further protection was submitted for congressional consideration. Frontier surveys, fortifications, and plans for naval depots were underway.

Treaties with the Quapaw, Great and Little Osages, tribes in Indiana and Ohio, Michigan Territory, and the Chickasaws produced extensive territorial cessions on terms described as satisfactory. Negotiations with tribes in Illinois Territory and the Choctaws continued. Posts were being established near the northern frontier for security. The address argued that independent tribal communities could not coexist indefinitely with a settled population and urged congressional consideration of measures that would end their independence, strengthen federal control, and encourage agriculture, land ownership, and civilization.

A strong naval presence was maintained in the Mediterranean, Gulf of Mexico, southern coast, and Pacific to protect commerce and preserve relations with the Barbary Powers, while the navy continued expanding. Illinois’s admission to the Union was welcomed as advancing representative federal government, strengthening state confidence, encouraging western commerce and navigation, and binding distant regions through mutual interest. Congress was also urged to consider revising the arrangement under which it directly governs the District of Columbia. The address concluded by calling for gratitude to the Divine Author for the nation’s blessings.

A multinational team led by UT Austin researchers assessed how built and proposed hydroelectric dams could affect the Amazon basin. Their Nature study introduced the Dam Environmental Vulnerability Index to rate risks from land-use change, erosion, pollution, trapped sediment and river alterations. Of 428 proposed dams, 140 are built or under construction. The Marañón, Ucayali and Madeira rivers face especially high risks. Researchers estimate that 68–80% of areas upstream of planned Marañón and Ucayali dams would remain vulnerable to dam effects, including reduced flooding and sediment storage and risks to thousands of species. The Madeira’s sediment concentration fell 20% after two large dams were built, while 25 upstream dams could trap additional sediment. If all planned dams are constructed, cumulative changes to Amazon sediment flow could alter regional rainfall and storm patterns and affect the Atlantic Ocean and climate.

The disclosure describes a smart gateway platform for industrial automation and Industrial Internet of Things applications. It is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/384,106, filed Apr. 15, 2019.

The platform applies domain expertise to select, model, normalize, and contextualize relevant industrial data before AI, machine-learning, or statistical analysis. Model templates stored in the platform are associated with industry-, machine-, and business-objective-specific goals, such as reducing downtime or failures, maximizing output, improving quality, and optimizing energy use or emissions. Each template defines relevant data inputs, correlations, causalities, and sometimes the type of analytics to perform.

Users select a template and map its generic inputs to standard or smart data tags on available industrial devices. The platform then collects the mapped data, contextualizes and aggregates it, adds modeling and AI metadata, synchronizes related values, and may calculate missing measures. Described smart-tag types include State, Rate, Odometer, and Event tags, each with configurable metadata.

The resulting structured, contextualized data can be supplied to analytics systems operating on the gateway, devices, edge systems, enterprise networks, or cloud platforms. These systems may generate recommendations, dashboards, alerts, predictive insights, or direct control outputs. The gateway can also incorporate historian, MES, maintenance, work-order, inventory, and other enterprise data. Restricting and structuring analytics inputs is presented as reducing storage and processing demands, accelerating useful insights, and limiting spurious correlations.

The patent discloses cationic lipid compounds of Formula (I), including specified structures IA–ID, and their pharmaceutically acceptable salts, tautomers, prodrugs, and stereoisomers. These lipids can be combined with neutral or charged lipids, steroids such as cholesterol, and polymer-conjugated lipids, including PEG-lipids, to form lipid nanoparticles for delivering therapeutic agents, particularly nucleic acids, in vitro or in vivo. The nanoparticles are intended to protect nucleic acids from plasma or nuclease degradation, improve intracellular uptake and delivery, support systemic administration, and provide acceptable tolerability and therapeutic index.

Compositions containing a disclosed lipid and a therapeutic agent, optionally with neutral lipids, steroids, or polymer-conjugated lipids, are provided. Suitable nucleic-acid payloads include mRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, plasmid DNA, miRNA, miRNA inhibitors, siRNA, and related nucleic acids. Uses include inducing expression of a desired protein, upregulating endogenous proteins through miRNA inhibition, or reducing target gene and protein expression. The nanoparticles may also co-deliver different nucleic acids and may be used to treat or prevent diseases, including infectious conditions and protein deficiencies.

Representative lipid compounds and preparation methods are listed, and disclosed formulations include specific molar ratios of cationic lipid to neutral lipid, cholesterol, and PEG-lipid. Described lipid nanoparticles generally have mean diameters of about 30–150 nm, are substantially non-toxic, and can be serum-stable and resistant to nuclease degradation.

The specification also discusses preparation of mRNA payloads. mRNA may be produced by in vitro transcription from plasmid or PCR-amplified DNA templates and purified by methods including extraction, precipitation, chromatography, or electrophoresis. Purification to remove double-stranded RNA contaminants can reduce innate immune activation and improve translation. Additional approaches to improve mRNA stability and translation include 5′ capping, 3′ poly(A) tails, optimized untranslated regions, and modified nucleosides.

Pharmaceutical compositions and administration methods are described for treating patients, with formulations available for oral, injectable, topical, transdermal, rectal, inhaled, and other routes, as well as lipid nanoparticles delivered systemically or locally. Figures depict mouse-liver luciferase expression, MC3 pKa calculation, and comparative luciferase activity for different lipids.

Robots planning in unstructured, partially observed environments often rely on the most recent cost map, but sensor noise, occlusion, estimation errors, and incomplete observations create inconsistencies between maps. With deterministic planners such as KEASL, these inconsistencies can produce abrupt trajectory changes and oscillations around obstacles. The paper proposes computing search-edge costs from multiple temporally sampled world maps, treating the latest map as the primary hypothesis and prior maps as additional hypotheses that guide search.

Four multi-hypothesis approaches are described. Valid in Every Hypothesis (VEH) permits an expansion only when it is collision-free in every map, ensuring safety but producing overly conservative paths. Per-Edge Hypothesis (PEH) allows expansions valid in at least one map and reroutes invalid expansions within each hypothesis, but its repeated sub-searches made it impractical for field use. Goal-Edge Hypothesis (GEH) defers hypothesis checking until a goal edge is found, then reroutes from each divergence point and averages costs; however, it concentrates search near the goal. Goal-Edge Graph Revision Hypothesis (GEGRH) adds graph revision so search focuses on hypothesis divergence points, improving efficiency while retaining the latest map’s validity requirement for final plans.

Experiments used online perception maps from an unmanned ground vehicle to create 221 planning problems, each tested with two or three successive maps under ARA* search and a one-second planning limit. Against VEH, GEGRH reduced average planning time by 15.4% with two hypotheses and 29.27% with three, while reducing path duration by 6.64% and 18.72%, respectively. Both multi-hypothesis methods required more planning time and produced longer paths than single-hypothesis planning because they were more conservative. Case studies showed that GEGRH can exploit uncertain choke points to shorten trajectories, while VEH can outperform GEGRH when rerouting overhead causes GEGRH to return a suboptimal plan within the time limit.

The results demonstrate that deterministic kinodynamic search can explicitly account for perceptual uncertainty. Future work includes incorporating more hypotheses, representing non-binary information such as ground height and semantics, using nonuniform hypothesis cost weighting, and estimating hypothesis certainty to improve planning efficiency and robustness.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2019 reported unaudited GAAP results. Quarterly revenue was $36.906 billion, up 14%; gross margin was $24.548 billion, up 22%; operating income was $13.891 billion, up 35%; net income was $11.649 billion, up 38%; and diluted EPS was $1.51, up 40%. For the six months, revenue was $69.961 billion, operating income was $26.577 billion, and net income was $22.327 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 39% to $12.5 billion, including 62% Azure growth and 27% growth in Office 365 Commercial.

Revenue growth occurred across all three segments. For the quarter, Productivity and Business Processes reported $11.826 billion of revenue and $5.182 billion of operating income; Intelligent Cloud reported $11.869 billion and $4.531 billion; and More Personal Computing reported $13.211 billion and $4.178 billion. Office Commercial grew 16%, LinkedIn 24%, Dynamics 12%, server products and cloud services 30%, Windows OEM 18%, and Windows Commercial 25%, while Xbox content and services declined 11%.

At December 31, 2019, Microsoft held $134.253 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, with total assets of $282.794 billion, liabilities of $172.685 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $110.109 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $24.498 billion. Financing activities used $19.124 billion, including $10.118 billion for share repurchases and $7.396 billion for dividends, while investing activities used $7.812 billion.

Notes addressed investments, derivatives, taxes, leases, unearned revenue, contingencies, and stockholder returns. Remaining performance obligations totaled $93 billion, including $90 billion of commercial revenue, with about half expected to be recognized within 12 months. Unrecognized tax benefits and other income-tax liabilities were $16.0 billion. Microsoft remained under IRS examination for 2004–2017 tax years, with transfer pricing identified as a potentially material unresolved issue. The company had 50 patent cases pending, none individually or collectively material, and accrued $319 million for legal liabilities, with additional aggregate outcomes of approximately $900 million considered reasonably possible. A new $40 billion share-repurchase authorization was approved in September 2019, and quarterly dividends were $0.51 per share.

Management attributed higher margins to a shift toward higher-margin businesses, while noting adverse foreign-currency impacts and risks from competition, changing technologies, macroeconomic conditions, and quarterly seasonality. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications needed to the interim financial information.

After the deadly Charlottesville protests, President Trump condemned white supremacists, the KKK, neo-Nazis and other extremists, calling racist violence criminal. The statement followed his earlier “many sides” remark and nearly 48 hours of silence. Trump also criticized Merck CEO Ken Frazier after Frazier resigned from his manufacturing council, linking the resignation to lower drug prices.

After the Yankees’ 2025 playoff elimination by Toronto, a Sporting News prediction projects Steven Kwan as New York’s 2026 leadoff hitter and Josh Naylor at first base, with New York moving on from Trent Grisham and Paul Goldschmidt.
Christopher Koziana, 29, of Essex, was charged with impaired driving and exceeding 80 mg blood alcohol after crashing into a gas meter. Uninjured, he will appear in Windsor court June 13.

Matthew Lane, a 19-year-old Massachusetts resident and Assumption University student, pleaded guilty to the 2024 ransomware attack on education technology company PowerSchool and is scheduled for federal sentencing. Prosecutors said Lane and at least one unnamed co-conspirator used stolen credentials to enter PowerSchool’s network and transfer sensitive files to a leased server in Ukraine. They demanded about $2.85 million in Bitcoin and threatened to leak student and educator data worldwide if payment was not made. The breach affected records of more than 60 million students and 10 million educators and cost PowerSchool over $14 million, according to court documents.

Prosecutors and Cyble threat intelligence researchers described Lane as a seasoned, sophisticated cybercriminal whose crimes dated to at least 2021, rather than an isolated offender. They said he targeted at least eight victims, including a Massachusetts athletic association, private companies, foreign governments, a U.S. wireless telecommunications company and an Indonesian telecommunications company. His methods included VPNs, eSIMs, anonymized email addresses and phone numbers, stolen credentials and foreign servers. Cyble linked aliases including “g0re” and “netsaosa” to Lane and said his activity progressed from identifying security flaws to leaking breaches and committing extortion. Researchers also found evidence that Lane’s early BreachForums account exposed his home IP address, suggesting his operational security deteriorated over time.

Lane was physically reserved and known locally as a quiet, skilled computer programmer and gamer. Online, he adopted flamboyant personas and appeared interested in reputation and attention as well as money. Prosecutors said he initially fabricated a story about receiving cash packages and denied extortion before confronting evidence in text messages. A sentencing report said he wanted to spend nearly $3 million on designer clothing, jewelry, luxury vehicles, upscale rentals and fast food; he returned about $160,000, while roughly $3 million remained unaccounted for. Prosecutors seek seven years in prison and more than $14 million in restitution.

The stolen data was subsequently used in secondary extortion attempts against school districts. Texas’s attorney general sued PowerSchool, alleging it misrepresented its cybersecurity capabilities. Researchers found no evidence that the ShinyHunters group participated in the original hack, but concluded Lane was not acting alone.

Gartner analysts Stephen Kleynhans and Michael Silver argue that Microsoft is turning Windows 10 Pro into an unsuitable enterprise product by limiting support and enterprise management features. Although Pro has long been the most common preinstalled version on business PCs, Microsoft has increasingly separated it from Windows 10 Enterprise. Enterprise and Education releases received a six-month extension beyond the standard 18 months of support, while Pro did not; Pro 1709 support ended April 9, 2019, versus October 2019 for Enterprise 1709. Paid supplemental servicing, adding 12 months of support, is also restricted to Enterprise and Education. Gartner recommends that organizations using Pro monitor Microsoft’s lifecycle announcements and budget for Windows 10 Enterprise as Pro becomes more consumer- and small-business-oriented.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended its seven-day winning streak. Ray Dalio said investors should allocate up to 15% of their portfolios to gold, comparing current conditions with the early 1970s amid inflation, high government spending and heavy debt. Gold rose above $4,000 an ounce and gained more than 50% this year amid fiscal deficits and global tensions. Dalio described gold as a diversifier and hedge against monetary debasement and geopolitical uncertainty.
John Howendobler is in custody after reporting he choked his wife in his sleep; she told officers he woke suddenly and began choking her.

In 2016, International Medical Corps advisor Dr. Inka Weissbecker visited South Sudan’s only mental health facility and found severe neglect, including sedated patients, an unattended traumatized child, and people with schizophrenia without medication. Donors initially dismissed mental health as a lower priority, though civil war later attracted funding for traumatized civilians. Untreated disorders are linked to unhealthy lifestyles, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, obesity, and substance abuse, while low-income countries face psychiatrist shortages and devote less than one percent of health budgets to mental health. Stigma, institutional care, and limited outreach and prevention worsen the crisis. The passage calls for funding and training, community-based mental health services, reduced stigma, and recognition of mental health as a human right under the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 29, 2018 reported net sales of $84.31 billion, down 5% from $88.29 billion a year earlier. iPhone sales fell 15%, while Mac sales rose 9%, iPad sales 17%, Wearables, Home and Accessories sales 33%, and Services sales 19%. Gross margin was $32.03 billion, or 38.0%, compared with 38.4% a year earlier. Operating expenses increased to $8.69 billion, operating income declined to $23.35 billion, and net income was nearly unchanged at $19.97 billion. Diluted earnings per share increased to $4.18 from $3.89. The effective tax rate fell to 16.5% from 25.8%.

Geographically, net sales increased 5% in the Americas and 1% in Rest of Asia Pacific, while declining 3% in Europe, 27% in Greater China, and 5% in Japan. Apple attributed lower iPhone sales, partially offset by growth in Services and other categories, to the overall revenue decline and cited unfavorable foreign currency effects.

At quarter-end, Apple had $44.77 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $200.26 billion in short- and long-term marketable securities, $373.72 billion in total assets, and $117.89 billion in shareholders’ equity. Operating activities generated $26.69 billion of cash. Apple repurchased 38 million shares for $8.2 billion and paid $3.6 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

Apple adopted the new revenue standard, financial-instruments guidance, and intra-entity asset-transfer tax guidance during the quarter. The tax guidance adoption resulted in $2.7 billion of net deferred tax assets and a $2.6 billion increase to retained earnings. The company also reclassified amortization of bundled Maps, Siri, and iCloud services from Products to Services sales.

The company expected second-quarter gross margin to range from 37% to 38%. Disclosed contingencies included the European Commission State Aid Decision, VirnetX patent litigation, Qualcomm disputes, and iOS performance-management cases.

President Donald Trump announced a deal with UK-based AstraZeneca to offer discounted prescription drugs through the government’s TrumpRx platform under “most-favored-nation” pricing. AstraZeneca pledged $50 billion in U.S. investment over five years for drug research and onshore manufacturing, and committed to offering Medicaid prices comparable to the lowest prices charged in other countries. The announcement followed a September agreement with Pfizer involving reduced TrumpRx and Medicaid pricing in exchange for a three-year tariff exemption. TrumpRx aims to reduce drug costs by eliminating intermediary companies.

Liverpool jewellery business Say It With Diamonds, founded by Charlotte Donoghue and Steph Porter in 2016, has opened its first city-centre store at Cavern Walks. The Instagram-founded brand, known for affordable wedding and engagement rings, hopes to expand its loyal customer base and become Liverpool’s premier jewellery store.

Shriram Transport Finance said promoters were discussing with SVL Group to secure timely repayment after its shares fell nearly 12% on debt concerns. It had guaranteed SVL’s Rs 870 crore debentures due in June 2019.

The patent disclosure concerns methods, chemical formulations, tooling, and apparatus for vacuum-forming fiber-based containers and packaging as alternatives to single-use plastics. The process uses pulp-and-water slurries containing application-specific additives, including moisture barriers such as alkyl ketene dimer, oil barriers, vapor barriers, retention aids, and dry- or wet-strength additives. Fiber sources include old corrugated containers, newsprint, softwood, bagasse, and bamboo, with refining used to improve fiber bonding and drainage. Unused slurry may be recirculated in a closed-loop system that monitors and replenishes chemical constituents.

Embodiments address produce containers, microwavable and oven-safe food containers, meat trays, beverage lids, utility containers, and other packaging. Produce containers may incorporate rolled edges, skirts, ribs, shelves, moisture barriers, and enlarged vent holes. Modified rinse tooling directs spray nozzles with horizontal components toward mold inserts, removing excess pulp and producing larger vent holes without changing the underlying molds. Microwavable containers use embedded or topical moisture, oil, and vapor barriers, while meat trays primarily use moisture and optional oil barriers to retain rigidity and structural integrity.

Beverage lids use moisture barriers and strengthening additives and may include an inclined platform, sip hole, vent aperture, crown, and lock ring. A vacuum tool with a pneumatically retractable piston unlocks lids formed with zero or negative draft. Additional embodiments describe structurally reinforced food and utility containers, coating methods for reducing porosity, and a corrugated-pulp shipping kit for flat-screen televisions. The disclosure also notes that the fiber-manufacturing concepts may extend beyond slurry vacuum forming to techniques such as 3D printing.

Co-operative Group reported a 2016 pretax loss after writing off its 20% stake in Co-operative Bank at nil amid efforts to sell the lender. Operating profit rose 32% to 148 million pounds, while supermarket like-for-like sales grew 3.5%. The group said its supermarkets, funeral services and insurance businesses gained market share. It is buying more British farm products in response to customer demand, partly cushioning import-price inflation of roughly 1.5%–2%.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2021 (Q3 FY2021) reports total revenue of $41,706 million versus $35,021 million in the prior-year quarter, and $121,936 million versus $104,982 million for the nine months. Net income was $15,457 million versus $10,752 million (nine months: $44,813 million versus $33,079 million), with diluted EPS of $2.03 versus $1.40 (nine months: $5.88 versus $4.30). Total assets were $308,879 million (June 30, 2020: $301,311 million), including $13,702 million cash and $111,705 million short-term investments; total stockholders' equity was $134,505 million versus $118,304 million. Cash from operations was $22,179 million for the quarter and $54,030 million for the nine months, offset by financing outflows of $13,192 million and $37,115 million and investing outflows of $9,684 million and $16,724 million.

Notable items include a July 2020 change in estimate extending the useful life of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years, which raised operating income by $611 million and net income by $505 million ($0.07 per share) in the quarter, and by $2.3 billion and $1.9 billion ($0.25 per share) for the nine months. The company adopted the new credit loss standard on July 1, 2020 (not material) and will adopt the new income tax guidance on July 1, 2021. On March 9, 2021, Microsoft completed the $8.1 billion (primarily cash) acquisition of ZeniMax Media Inc., allocating $5,554 million to goodwill and $1,947 million to intangibles, reported within More Personal Computing. Total debt was $58,058 million (face value $63,867 million), including an $8.2 billion 2021 issuance, with an estimated fair value of $67.4 billion. The effective tax rate fell to 10% from 16%, helped by a $620 million benefit from an India Supreme Court ruling on withholding taxes and a $1.7 billion IRS audit settlement payment; unrecognized tax benefits were $15.8 billion. Unearned revenue was $32,714 million, and remaining performance obligations totaled $121 billion, about 50% expected within 12 months.

Contingencies include 66 pending patent cases, settled Canadian antitrust class actions, an ongoing China SAMR investigation, 40 cell phone lawsuits, and accrued legal liabilities of $336 million with approximately $500 million in additional reasonably possible adverse outcomes. Share repurchases under the September 2019 $40 billion program totaled $16,770 million (77 million shares) in the nine months, with $14.9 billion remaining; quarterly dividends were $0.56 per share. Reportable segments are Productivity and Business Processes (nine-month revenue $39,224 million, operating income $17,916 million), Intelligent Cloud ($42,705 million, $18,339 million) and More Personal Computing ($40,007 million, $14,566 million); commercial cloud revenue rose 33% to $17.7 billion for the quarter and $49.6 billion for the nine months, with Azure up 50% and Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers at 50.2 million. U.S. revenue was $20,373 million for the quarter. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim statements. As a subsequent event, on April 11, 2021, Microsoft agreed to acquire Nuance Communications, Inc. for $56.00 per share in an all-cash deal valued at $19.7 billion, expected to close by the end of calendar 2021. MD&A notes a dynamic, competitive industry, currency effects on international results, and continued COVID-19 impacts on operations.

Founded in Boston in 2010 by Joe De Sena, Spartan Race grew into a leading obstacle-course race provider, raising $15 million through private equity investments in 2012 and 2016. In 2017, while considering an initial public offering, De Sena asked Spartan’s financial planning director and controller how a new revenue-recognition standard would affect the company’s financial statements. Spartan had reported one million global participants at roughly 130 events across more than 25 countries in 2016.

Obstacle-course racing experienced rapid growth around 2010, with an estimated 4.5 million U.S. finishers in 2015, although growth later slowed and some organizers ceased operations. Spartan competed with Warrior Dash, Rugged Maniac, and Tough Mudder but distinguished itself through timed races, varied distances, obstacles emphasizing individual athleticism, and penalties for failed obstacles. Its race fees remained its primary revenue source, supplemented by sponsorships and media partnerships with Reebok, NBC Sports Group, and Daily Burn. De Sena also expressed an interest in seeing obstacle racing included in the Olympics.

The new standard required five steps: determine whether a contract exists, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price among multiple obligations, and recognize revenue when those obligations are satisfied. Spartan would need to assess contract commitments, probable collection, variable consideration such as discounts and refunds, delayed-payment discounts, fair value for noncash exchanges, and whether customers controlled products or received services over time.

Spartan’s revenue sources included walk-up and advance race entries, annual passes, merchandise, sponsorships, SGX training certification, and international races conducted by licensees paying royalties. The case ends with De Sena awaiting guidance on how these varied activities would be reported under the standard.

MotoGP heads to Austin after the Argentina GP, where Marc Márquez has won every race he has started and 75% of its events. After Maverick Viñales won in Qatar and Argentina, pressure falls on Márquez. Viñales leads the standings with 50 points, ahead of Valentino Rossi (36) and Andrea Dovizioso (20). FP1 is Friday at 9:55 GMT−5; the race is Sunday at 14:00.

Maryland’s offense benefited from strong receiver play, effective rushing and protection, converting 9 of 16 third downs against Minnesota. Ohio State plans to use healthy Mike Weber and freshman J.K. Dobbins together. Chris Worley is probable, while Dre’Mont Jones and Erick Smith will miss out, and Antonio Williams is questionable.

The South Dakota Department of Agriculture urges producers who suspect dicamba crop damage to complete an online survey. Results will assess the products’ statewide impact on tolerant soybeans. Producers may also complete the survey at its Dakotafest booth in Mitchell, Aug. 15–17.

In his 2017 inaugural address, Donald Trump declared that power was returning to the American people and pledged an “America First” agenda focused on restoring jobs, manufacturing, national wealth, and secure borders. He criticized prior leaders for favoring other countries over American workers and promised action on infrastructure, education, safety, poverty, and crime. He called for “Buy American” and “Hire American,” renewed alliances, defeating radical Islamic terrorism, unity without prejudice, and government action backed by patriotism and faith.

McLaren’s 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 M840T will debut in the 720S, producing 720 metric horsepower (710 hp; 529.5 kW). McLaren says it enables 0–200 km/h in 7.8 seconds and a 10.3-second quarter-mile. Features include reduced turbo lag, an optional exhaust and an illuminated engine bay, with improved fuel efficiency and emissions.

NVIDIA Corporation filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for its fiscal 2018 third quarter ended October 29, 2017. The company reported two operating segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, serving gaming, professional visualization, datacenter and automotive markets.

Third-quarter revenue was $2.636 billion, up 32% year over year and 18% sequentially. Gross profit was $1.569 billion, with a 59.5% margin. Operating expenses rose 24% to $674 million, operating income increased 40% to $895 million, and net income increased 55% to $838 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.33, up 60%. For the first nine months, revenue was $6.803 billion, up 44%; gross margin was 59.1%; operating income was $2.137 billion; net income was $1.928 billion; and diluted earnings per share were $3.05.

GPU revenue reached $2.217 billion, up 31%, while Tegra Processor revenue was $419 million, up 74%. Third-quarter revenue by market was $1.561 billion from gaming, $501 million from datacenter, $239 million from professional visualization, $144 million from automotive and $191 million from OEM and intellectual property. Growth was driven by GeForce gaming products, datacenter products for deep learning and accelerated computing, professional visualization products and Tegra-based gaming and automotive offerings.

At October 29, 2017, NVIDIA held $2.802 billion in cash and equivalents and $3.518 billion in marketable securities, totaling $6.320 billion. Total assets were $9.830 billion, total liabilities were $3.477 billion and shareholders’ equity was $6.352 billion. Operating activities generated $2.144 billion of cash during the first nine months, compared with $951 million a year earlier.

NVIDIA repurchased $909 million of stock and paid $250 million in dividends during the first nine months. It intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2018 and again in fiscal 2019. The quarterly dividend was increased from $0.14 to $0.15 per share. Remaining convertible notes totaled $24 million in principal, while long-term debt consisted of $1 billion each of 2.20% notes due 2021 and 3.20% notes due 2026. Outstanding inventory purchase obligations were $1.16 billion.

Stock-based compensation was $265 million for the first nine months, and the effective tax rate was 8.9%, down from 14.2% a year earlier, primarily because of greater stock-compensation tax benefits and lower earnings subject to U.S. tax. NVIDIA adopted guidance on tax effects of intra-entity asset transfers, reducing retained earnings by $28 million, and expected no material impact from forthcoming financial-instrument and revenue standards, while lease accounting would increase both lease assets and liabilities.

The company faced patent litigation from Polaris Innovations in the United States and Germany. No liability was accrued because losses were not considered probable, and the potential loss range could not be reasonably estimated. NVIDIA also planned to purchase its Santa Clara campus property for approximately $350 million. As of October 29, 2017, there had been no material changes in previously reported investment, interest-rate or foreign-exchange risks.

Philadelphia City Council meets Thursday on bills advancing the Kenney Administration's "Rebuild" project: $500 million over seven years to rehab up to 200 parks, rec centers and libraries. Council twice rejected the plan but added amendments; the mayor wants passage so work can start once beverage tax challenges are settled.

James Hodgkinson, 66, of Belleville, Illinois, opened fire during a charity baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, injuring Rep. Steve Scalise and others. Scalise was critically injured, while Hodgkinson was killed in a shootout with police. The FBI investigated Hodgkinson’s social media, associates, whereabouts and possible motives. Rep. Claudia Tenney also received a threatening email.

The ADS7828’s SAR architecture is sensitive to transient glitches on power, reference, ground, and digital inputs just before the comparator output is latched; an n-bit conversion has n vulnerable windows. Use clean, well-bypassed power, placing a 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor close to the device and, if the +VDD connection has high impedance, 1–10 µF. The external reference provides no inherent noise or voltage-variation rejection, so supply noise and ripple, particularly at 50 or 60 Hz, can directly affect results. Connect GND to a clean analog-ground point away from microcontroller or DSP grounding.

The passage also includes product-status, preproduction, RoHS, MSL/reflow, and part-marking notes; package dimensions and pin-1 orientation guidance; and Texas Instruments disclaimers about information accuracy, warranties, liability, intellectual property, application responsibility, and sales terms.

In 1935, the California Supreme Court held that a Los Angeles Superior Court presiding judge lacked jurisdiction to place an ex parte “Report of Presiding Judge” in a divorce case file. Although the report’s findings could support separate judicial or disciplinary action against counsel, it was unrelated to the divorce decree and improperly entered in the case records. The court ordered the document struck from the file.

The passage describes a packet-processing pipeline for reconfigurable match-action hardware switches in software-defined networking. Each ingress and egress pipeline includes a parser, match-action unit (MAU), and deparser. The parser separates packet headers from the payload and divides header fields into a primary packet header vector (PPHV), containing fields that may be matched or modified by the MAU, and a secondary packet header vector (SPHV), containing fields the MAU will not process. The PPHV passes through the MAU’s match-action stages, while the SPHV and payload bypass the MAU and go directly to the deparser, which reconstructs the packet from processed and unprocessed header data.

A control-plane compiler generates MAU and parser configuration from switch code, potentially P4, using control and table flow graphs and a parse graph. A configurator distributes this configuration to the switch. The parse graph specifies how packet headers are extracted based on values such as EtherType, and identifies which fields belong in the PPHV or SPHV. This separation reduces MAU resource usage and allows the fixed-size PPHV to carry relevant fields from deeper packet headers, including in tunneled traffic.

The description is a continuation application that incorporates specified prior U.S., international, and provisional applications by reference, along with an XML sequence listing submitted on compact discs and an earlier ASCII sequence-listing copy.

DNA methylation regulates gene expression, and aberrant methylation is associated with diseases, including cancer. Although methylation sequencing and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing may identify diagnostic methylation patterns, WGBS is described as unsuitable for routine product assays because most genomic regions provide weak classification signals, deep sequencing is cost-prohibitive, control groups may be small or variable, and methylation at neighboring CpG sites is correlated.

The disclosure provides targeted cancer assay panels, or bait sets, for capturing cell-free DNA fragments containing cancer-specific methylation patterns. Embodiments describe large sets of oligonucleotide probes, paired or overlapping probes, 2×-tiled designs, affinity-conjugated probes such as biotinylated probes, specified probe lengths and CpG densities, and off-target filtering. Probe regions may be selected from Lists 1–8 and may target preferentially hypermethylated or hypomethylated genomic regions.

Methods are provided for identifying differentially methylated genomic regions by comparing converted cfDNA from cancer and non-cancer subjects, classifying anomalous methylation patterns using CpG-site counts and p-value rarity, and selecting regions based on cancer and non-cancer occurrence counts. Additional methods cover in-silico probe design, removal of probes with excessive off-target matches, synthesis of the resulting bait sets, and use of bisulfite or enzymatic conversion to convert unmethylated cytosine to uracil before hybridization capture and sequencing.

The sequence reads or derived feature vectors can be applied to trained classifiers to determine cancer presence, stage, type, or tissue of origin and, in some embodiments, to guide administration of an anti-cancer agent. Specified classifiers include kernel logistic regression, random forests, mixture models, convolutional neural networks, and autoencoders. Listed embodiments state performance ranges including AUC values above 0.70 and specified sensitivity levels at high specificity for multiple cancer types. The description also defines methylation-state vectors, anomalous patterns, CpG and UpG sites, and related terminology, while the drawings depict probe designs, training and analysis workflows, assay validation, ROC curves, and tissue-of-origin confusion matrices.

- The Ethernet MAC switch contains a three-port gigabit switch with one internal and two external ports. External ports support 10/100/1000-Mbps operation and MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII interfaces. EMAC I/O is 3.3 V only. A shared MDIO interface polls all 32 addresses, controls multiple PHYs, and supports host configuration and status monitoring.

PCB guidance requires controlled differential impedance, paired vias, appropriate pullups, and an ESD-protection device with no more than 5 pF capacitance. E-mini S&P 500 futures are CME financial derivatives introduced in 1997, one-fifth the size of the standard S&P 500 futures contract. They track the S&P 500, are among the most frequently traded and liquid equity-index futures, and enable speculation or hedging through CME Globex.

A futures strategy incorporates technical and fundamental analysis, defined entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management. The article’s paywalled example is a mean-reversion strategy with one buying and one selling variable. Its MultiCharts backtest uses daily bars, trades at the close, and relies on continuous, back-adjusted Norgate CME data from the contract’s inception, without stops or other risk controls. The article reports stronger winter and spring performance than during summer.

One contract equals $50 times the index value; at the quoted 4,020.25 level on November 30, 2022, its value was $201,012.50. Trading requires a futures broker, funded account, and margin; CFD alternatives are also discussed. Charts are available through CME, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, and MultiCharts.

This MIT 6.262 lecture (Lecture 5) concludes the professor's treatment of Poisson processes and introduces superposition, splitting, and conditional arrival-epoch distributions.

**Review and definitions.** The lecture recaps that a Poisson process is an arrival process with IID exponentially distributed interarrival times, and that it can be viewed three equivalent ways: as a sequence of interarrival times, as arrival epochs (S₁, S₂, …), or as the counting process N(t). Specifying any one of these (including the joint law of the epochs, or N(t) for all t) determines the process completely. The interarrival times are memoryless, so conditional on N(t) = n and on the time Sₙ of the last arrival, the remaining waiting time Z is still exponential regardless of the conditioned values, which implies Z is unconditionally exponential. Counts over disjoint intervals are stationary and independent Poisson variables, depending only on interval length, and N(t) has the PMF e^(−λt)(λt)^n/n!. The professor notes that sums of independent Poisson random variables are Poisson with means adding, which avoids discrete convolution arguments. Three alternate equivalent definitions of a Poisson process are presented: the arrival-process/PMF characterization, and an incremental condition in which the probability of zero arrivals in an interval of size δ is 1 − λδ + o(δ), one arrival is λδ + o(δ), and two or more is o(δ), where o(δ) is any function vanishing faster than δ. The professor declines to use differential equations, noting the text's treatment. He also notes that specifying only the marginal distributions of N(t) (as in a Bernoulli-type process) is insufficient without the independence property.

**Superposition.** The sum of two independent Poisson processes with rates λ₁ and λ₂ is Poisson with rate λ₁ + λ₂. The professor gives a short incremental proof: the probability of exactly one arrival in the combined process is the sum of the "one in process 1, none in process 2" and "none in process 1, one in process 2" cases, and multiplying out and discarding terms of order δ² yields δ(λ₁ + λ₂) + o(δ), the required incremental property. He observes that this tedious argument is unnecessary if one simply invokes the theorem that independent Poisson variables add to Poisson. More broadly, he notes that the sum of many small independent arrival processes tends to be Poisson even when the individual processes are not, since independence across processes overcomes dependence within each process (illustrated by internet traffic). He characterizes this as a plausibility argument requiring many conditions to prove, saying the text's proof is not quite right.

**Splitting.** Combining a Poisson process of rate λ with an independent Bernoulli process that independently sends each arrival one way with probability p produces two independent Poisson processes with rates λp and λ(1−p). The professor gives intuition via the small-increment argument, noting that the independence of the two output processes is hidden in the o(δ) terms and that a careful proof requires the text. He emphasizes that combining and splitting are typically used together — viewing separate processes as one combined process and then splitting again — and says this technique should be used repeatedly in the week's problem set.

**Last-come, first-served queue.** The professor uses LCFS service as an application of combining and splitting. Service completions form a Poisson process of rate μ (with low-priority work to keep the server busy), independent of the arrival process of rate λ, giving a combined process of rate λ + μ. The probability that a customer who has begun service is interrupted by a new arrival is λ/(λ + μ), and the probability of completing service is μ/(λ + μ). The probability of no further interruption after an interruption is (μ/(λ + μ))². He notes the rule is not unfair since it applies to everyone, and that it can favor customers with small service requirements when service times are heavy-tailed, though for exponential service it helps no one.

**Non-homogeneous Poisson processes.** Motivated by optical transmission, where a modulated photon stream with variable rate λ(t) carries information, the lecturer notes that counting-process formulas still hold: the number of arrivals in an interval is Poisson with parameter equal to the average rate over that interval. Combining and splitting non-homogeneous processes works as in the homogeneous case, but the interarrival-time view no longer applies since interarrival times are not exponential, yielding only half the available results.

**Conditional distribution of arrival epochs.** Given N(t) = 1, the arrival epoch has conditional density 1/t, uniform on (0, t) and independent of λ, which the professor verifies by a limit argument in which all exponential factors cancel. For N(t) = 2 the joint density is 2/t², and in general the joint density of the ordered epochs is n!/tⁿ over the region 0 < S₁ < … < Sₙ < t. The professor explains the otherwise puzzling n! factor using order statistics of n IID uniform random variables on (0, t): their joint density is 1/tⁿ on the cube, which by symmetry is partitioned into n! disjoint equal-volume regions corresponding to the n! orderings, each of volume tⁿ/n!. He notes this mirrors the earlier appearance of n! in the airline/Poisson density derivation. The same order-statistic view yields the distribution of the first arrival given n arrivals by time t: P(S₁ > s) = (1 − s/t)ⁿ, and E[S₁] = t/(n + 1), consistent with the n + 1 equal-probability intervals cut by n arrivals. Mapping the (S₁, S₂) region into interarrival times (X₁, X₂) shows the density is again 2/t² over the region X₁ + X₂ < t, with the square mapping to a parallelepiped of equal volume, requiring linear algebra in higher dimensions.

**Inspection paradox.** The lecture closes with a paradox: the mean interarrival time of a Poisson process is 1/λ, but the interval between the last and next arrival around an arbitrary observation time t has mean (1 − e^(−λt))/λ, which is larger. The professor's partial explanation is that choosing a random t is more likely to land in long intervals because they occupy proportionally more area of the sample path; he defers a full explanation to the study of renewal processes and ends the lecture there.

Fifth Third Bank agreed to acquire Comerica in a $10.9 billion all-stock deal, creating the ninth-largest U.S. bank with about $288 billion in assets. Board-approved and awaiting regulatory clearance, the transaction would expand Fifth Third’s Sunbelt presence and strengthen payments and wealth-management operations. Comerica holders would receive just under 1.9 Fifth Third shares per share, about $82.88, a 20% premium. The deal is expected to close in early 2026, while critics warn that greater consolidation could heighten systemic risk.

The coach reflects that elite goaltenders prepare meticulously and considers the position uniquely demanding and skilled. His teams have featured several prominent goalies, although he says he had little influence over how they played. He argues that comparing the current team with Montreal’s four-year dynasty is difficult because the era and competitive landscape differed, while noting that many Hall of Fame players emerged during sustained periods of team success.

During the playoffs, the team is evaluating roster options after receiving a late call, and one player will miss at least the remainder of the series. Reserve players have worked hard and may be ready, but the coach says ice time, freshness and the tendency to limit changes must be monitored. He views the postseason as a rare opportunity rather than added pressure and says experienced players can help teammates navigate it.

He also discusses a disciplined goalie’s preparation and strong playoff performance, and says an injured forward moved to the wing has had an effective fit alongside a teammate, contributing in key situations.

Poland will invest 20 billion zlotys ($5.5 billion) to connect its national fuel pipeline with NATO’s Central Europe Pipeline System, including roughly 300 kilometres of new infrastructure and additional storage facilities. NATO has committed 60 million zlotys for planning and design, with construction expected to take several years. The project aims to strengthen military logistics, improve supply-chain resilience and integrate Poland into a European pipeline network. Officials regard it as a major security investment, though coordination, regulatory compliance, delays and rising costs present risks.

This cross-sectional study examined determinants of wasting, stunting, and undernutrition among 185 children aged 6–59 months receiving treatment at government CMAM centers in four villages in southern Punjab, Pakistan. Eligible children had severe wasting or stunting based on WHO anthropometric criteria. Parent interviews collected sociodemographic, feeding, medical, immunization, and healthcare data, while qualified staff performed anthropometric assessments. Data were analyzed using t-tests and multivariate linear regression.

Most participants were female (56.2%), had monthly family income of 15,000 PKR or less (69.2%), had at least two siblings (77.8%), did not receive exclusive breastfeeding (80.5%), and had poor complementary feeding practices (89.2%). Multivariate analysis identified monthly income and complementary feeding as significant determinants of wasting; tuberculosis contact history and exclusive breastfeeding as significant determinants of stunting; and monthly income and exclusive breastfeeding as significant determinants of undernutrition. The authors concluded that malnutrition is associated with feeding practices, household size, family earnings, and infection history. They recommended coordinated efforts to incorporate dietary needs and other factors affecting child growth into nutrition programs, while noting that the cross-sectional design limited causal conclusions.

The buy-and-hold strategy, also called position trading or long-term investing, involves buying stocks, ETFs, or funds and holding them for years or decades while disregarding short-term price fluctuations. Investors may sell limited portions when they need money. This contrasts with active trading, which seeks to time market highs and lows.

The strategy is based on the long-term tendency of stocks to appreciate and is consistent with the Efficient Market Hypothesis. Investors should select securities using long-term investment theses, strong business fundamentals, and reasonable prices, then maintain diversification across stocks, sectors, or passive index funds. Growth, value, dollar-cost averaging, and index-fund approaches can all complement buy and hold.

Reported benefits include lower trading costs, deferred and potentially favorable long-term capital-gains taxes, low-cost passive funds, reduced manager risk, less stress, and less time spent monitoring markets. Long-term shareholders also receive dividends, voting rights, and a stake in corporate profits. Studies cited in the passage indicate that buy-and-hold investors tend to outperform active management and most active traders over long periods after fees.

The strategy also has drawbacks. It involves substantial market drawdowns, carries the risk of holding unsuccessful companies, and requires difficult stock selection because few stocks become major long-term successes and most have poor lifetime returns. Investors also give up opportunities to time market peaks or sell at optimal prices.

Examples cited include an Amazon investment growing from $1,000 in 2001 to approximately $218,793, and an SPY investment growing from $100,000 in 1993 to $1.584 million after 29 years, with dividends reinvested. A backtested portfolio of trading strategies showed fewer drawdowns and smoother performance than buy and hold, although it excluded commissions and slippage. The passage concludes that buy and hold is generally effective when based on strong companies or a broad, diversified portfolio and is a simple wealth-building option for many investors.

Patterns for distributed systems let developers learn from prior experience, communicate through a shared vocabulary, and reuse well-tested components. They also support modularity, maintainability, independent scaling, and more reliable deployments. Single-node container patterns are presented as foundational building blocks for distributed systems. Splitting an application into containers provides resource isolation, clear team ownership, separation of concerns, reusable modules, smaller deployments, and more reliable rollouts.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a colocated container that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing dynamic configuration through a shared filesystem, exposing process resource usage through a `topz` interface, and automatically deploying Git changes in a simple PaaS. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized, define stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile metadata such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`.

The ambassador pattern places a colocated proxy between an application and external services. It can route requests to storage shards, discover and connect to environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. Client-side and centralized approaches offer different deployment and complexity trade-offs. Examples use Redis with twemproxy and nginx for percentage-based experiments.

The adapter pattern converts heterogeneous application interfaces into consistent interfaces. It can adapt monitoring endpoints for Prometheus, normalize logs from different applications through Fluentd, and provide rich database health checks without modifying vendor-supplied containers. These adapters improve reuse, isolate failures, and permit application and tooling upgrades independently.

Multi-node architectures are more loosely coupled and communicate through network calls. Microservices divide applications into focused services with formal API contracts, enabling independent team releases and service-specific scaling, while making debugging, design, and coordination more difficult. Distributed patterns can codify common solutions and apply lessons learned across systems.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless instances behind a load balancer for redundancy and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when instances can accept requests. Session tracking keeps a user’s requests on one replica, using IP hashing within clusters, cookies or headers externally, and consistent hashing to minimize remapping during scaling. A caching tier can improve latency and capacity, while reverse proxies provide rate limiting and denial-of-service defenses. A complete web-serving pattern may place SSL-terminating nginx servers in front of replicated Varnish caches and application instances.

Sharded services divide state or requests among shards, commonly for stateful systems whose data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches distribute unique data more efficiently than replicated caches, but a failed shard affects all requests mapped to it. Replicating each shard improves availability and permits independent scaling, at the cost of greater complexity and resource use. Requests can be routed by client-side ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs involving deployment complexity, latency, and scaling. Sharding functions typically use hashing and modulo to map requests deterministically and uniformly across shards.

A Death Cross occurs when a short-term moving average, typically the 50-day, crosses below a long-term moving average, usually the 200-day. It is a lagging signal associated with potential short-term weakness and often prompts investors to exit positions defensively.

S&P 500 backtests found that Death Cross signals produced below-average returns over periods shorter than 30 days, while longer-term returns were generally positive and similar to random long-term market returns. Selling at a Death Cross and reentering at a Golden Cross generated an annual return of 0.4%, reflecting premature exits and missed recoveries. Conversely, buying at a Golden Cross and selling at a Death Cross produced a 7% CAGR, slightly below buy-and-hold, with 30% less time in the market and substantially lower drawdowns. The signal can therefore reduce drawdowns and serve as a defensive tool, but it may cause investors to miss bull-market recoveries.

The disclosure describes medical neuromodulation systems, particularly spinal cord stimulation, and methods for automatically identifying effective stimulation parameter sets. An implantable pulse generator delivers programmed electrical pulses through electrodes, while external programmers, remote controls, trial stimulators, and sensors support programming, monitoring, and feedback.

The automated search uses patient input, including pain, satisfaction, activity, VAS, NRS, and global-impression scores; clinician input, including selected programs, parameter dimensions, ranges, thresholds, and evaluation criteria; and automatic input, including activity, heart rate or variability, and field potentials. Candidate neuromodulation parameter sets are evaluated and the optimal set is used to program the neuromodulator.

Proposed search techniques include patient-scored sorting with threshold-based pruning, gradient descent or ascent for optimizing a parameter, regression-based sensitivity analysis, genetic algorithms, binary search, and simplex processes. The systems support closed-loop feedback, wash-in and wash-out periods, user-configurable objectives, program ranking interfaces, best-so-far programs, and rotating schedules to reduce neurological conditioning.

The passage also describes spinal cord anatomy, conventional and sub-perception stimulation, selective modulation of dorsal horn or dorsal root tissue, and implementations for pain treatment using spatial, temporal, and informational pulse-pattern control.

- CMD19 tuning consists of consecutive executions without intervening commands. A card must complete 40 executions within 150 ms, excluding host processing time; normal tuning is typically shorter.

- Until identification ends, the host remains at fOD and may use fPP during data transfer. CMD9 retrieves CSD data, while optional CMD4 configures identified cards’ DSR registers and switches the clock from fOD to fPP. CMD7 selects one card for transfer; selecting another card releases the previous selection, and RCA 0x0000 deselects all cards.

- Data transfers are point-to-point with the selected card. Read and write commands can be stopped with CMD12. Writes must be stopped before deselection. Successful writes lead to the Programming State; failed transfers return to the Transfer State. Block writes may use buffering, while CSD programming, write protection, and erase commands do not. Parameter and read commands are prohibited during programming. Selecting another card disconnects it and releases the DAT line without terminating erase or programming, while reset can terminate pending operations and destroy data.

- Bus width is selected with ACMD6, defaults to one bit, and cannot be changed on a locked card. For 2 GB cards, READ_BL_LEN and WRITE_BL_LEN are 1024 bytes, but CMD16 block length remains limited to 512 bytes.

- Reads use synchronous, CRC-protected block transfers. CMD17 reads one block and returns to the Transfer State; CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12. Address and length errors prevent transfer. Misaligned partial blocks cause ADDRESS_ERROR and abort transmission; CMD12 may be required to recover. At the end of the user area, OUT_OF_RANGE may be ignored if the CMD18 sequence was otherwise correct.

- Writes use CRC-protected blocks and reject block-length or address errors. Block writes require a 512-byte CMD16 length; optional partial writes can use smaller byte-aligned blocks. CRC failure discards the affected data. ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks before a multiple-block write, while ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks. Hosts may interleave operations on separate cards by isolating busy DAT lines.

- Erasing uses CMD32 and CMD33 to define a range, followed by CMD38. Out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET, and protected sectors are skipped with WP_ERASE_SKIP. Erase progress is indicated by a low DAT0 line. Post-erase data may be either 0 or 1 according to the card and SCR setting.

- DISCARD is similar to ERASE but makes discarded contents “don’t care”; it requires CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 with argument 00000001h. FULE logically erases the entire user area using CMD32 and CMD33 followed by CMD38 with argument 00000002h. Both are supported only on SDHC and SDXC cards, not through SPI, and have busy timeouts of 250 ms and one second respectively.

- Write protection can be mechanical, card-internal, or password-based. Password data is stored in nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP and FEP_LEN registers. Locked cards accept only limited commands and cannot access stored data. CMD42 is available in the Transfer State and carries lock, unlock, password-setting, clearing, and erase functions in a CRC-protected data block.

- Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds ownership-specific CMD42 functions. When FEP is set, the card remains COP-locked after reset until CMD42[1Fh] unlocks the COP function set. CMD42 version 2.0 adds FEP management, FEP-protected force erase, and restrictions on resetting PWD. Force erase clears the user-area contents and PWD/PWD_LEN and leaves the card unlocked; FEP force erase requires the matching FEP and leaves FEP unchanged. Incorrect passwords, invalid lengths, unsupported combinations, and forbidden operations set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED.

- CMD55, APP_CMD, causes the immediately following command to be interpreted as an application-specific command. Defined legal ACMDs retain APP_CMD status; undefined legal commands are treated as regular commands; illegal commands return an error. Certain ACMD numbers are reserved for proprietary applications.

- CMD6 switches card functions through six function groups, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum power, while Mode 1 selects functions; Function 0 is default and 0xF retains the current function. An invalid Mode 1 selection cancels all changes, and busy functions cannot be switched. CMD6 returns an R1 response and a 512-bit status block, has a 100 ms timeout, and requires at least eight clocks before changed bus behavior is used. The default power limit is 0.72 W and must account for host supply capability, connector limits, and heat release.

- High-Speed mode provides 25 MB/s using a 50 MHz clock. It is optional, and the host must drive only one card with one-to-one CLK, CMD, and DAT connections. CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57 are reserved for switchable command-system extensions.

- CMD8 is issued before ACMD41 during initialization. It checks whether the card supports the host’s supply voltage; an accepting card returns R7 with the voltage range and check pattern echoed.

- ACMD41’s CCS value distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths. SDHC and SDXC use block addressing, fixed 512-byte transfer blocks, and do not permit partial or misaligned access. They also do not support write-protected groups.

- The host may lower or stop the bus clock while preserving valid transfers, subject to frequency limits. After ACMD41, the clock must run at 100–400 kHz or be polled at intervals below 50 ms. Eight clock cycles must follow command, response, read, or write transactions. A busy card may continue programming without a clock, but a clock edge is needed to release its busy indication.

- CRC7 protects commands, most responses, CID, and CSD; CRC16 protects each transferred data block and is calculated separately on each line in wide-bus mode. A CRC failure or illegal command produces no response, leaves card state unchanged, and sets the corresponding error bit.

- Read timeouts are the lower of 100 times typical access time or 100 ms for SDSC, while SDHC and SDXC use at least 100 ms. Write timeouts are the lower of 100 times typical program time or 250 ms for SDSC; SDHC busy time is limited to 250 ms. SDXC may indicate up to 500 ms in specified write or stop situations, except speed-class writes, which remain limited to 250 ms.

В обзере рассматриваются история, преимущества, архитектура и применение RFID в ритейле. Внедрение технологии в 2000-е годы сопровождалось высокой стоимостью меток, незрелостью стандартов и сложностями интеграции, из-за чего амбициозные проекты вроде тотального маркирования товаров Metro Group не достигли исходных целей. Цифровая трансформация бизнеса создала новые предпосылки для развития RFID: автоматизированные данные стали важны для принятия решений в реальном времени.

RFID представляет собой систему автоматической идентификации и сбора данных на основе электромагнитных полей радиочастотного диапазона. Она обеспечивает идентификацию, аутентификацию и определение местоположения объектов, а также автоматическую передачу данных. В ритейле технология применяется для управления цепочками поставок и активами, инвентаризации, отслеживания перемещений товаров и покупателей, выявления краж, автоматизации приёмки и оплаты, а также работы умных примерочных.

Современные RFID-системы обеспечивают точность учёта запасов около 98–99%, ускоряют инвентаризацию, выявляют несогласованность остатков и цен, сокращают отсутствие товаров на полках, логистические издержки и потери от краж. Они также улучшают клиентский оплект, ускоряют кассовое обслуживание и повышают точность выполнения онлайн-заказов. Архитектура RFID включает беспроводную подсистему идентификации, корпоративную подсистему обработки и анализа данных, а также организационную подсистему обмена информацией между участниками цепочки поставок по стандартизированным протоколам, включая EPCIS.

Исследования, включённые в обзор, подтверждают потенциал RFID для отслеживания потребительского поведения, анализа перемещений покупателей, персонализации, управления запасами и цепочками поставок, интеграции с IoT, позиционирования объектов и развития безчиповых технологий. Система сбалансированных показателей предлагает оценивать RFID не только по финансовым метрикам, но и по клиентским и операционным эффектам. Среди целевых показателей названы ROI 20–30% за два года, снижение потерь от краж до 75%, сокращение затрат на логистику и инвентаризацию на 30%, рост продаж на 5–10%, сокращение времени кассовых операций на 50%, точность онлайн-заказов до 98% и улучшение показателей удовлетворённости клиентов на 20%.
