Daisy-chain mode is enabled after power-up or reset by configuring the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register with the number of ADCs in the chain excluding ADC1. Register writes require N × 24 SCLKs in one SPI frame; four ADCs therefore require 96 SCLKs. Configuring the chain length uses N SPI frames.

To read registers from N daisy-chained ADCs, the controller selects a register bank using REG_BANK_SEL and enables reads with SPI_RD_EN = 0b. It then sends an N × 24-bit frame containing {0xFE, 0x00, address}, followed by an N × 24-bit {0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF} frame that returns the 8-bit register address and 16-bit register data.

Registers provide controls for SPI versus daisy-chain mode, read access, chain length, register-bank selection, conversion data format, averaging, XOR and digital test patterns, speed-boost mode, gain-error correction, analog bandwidth, power, reference selection, output lanes, and common-mode range.

The passage provides PCB-layout guidance for the UC1825B-SP. Keep the feedback trace direct and relatively thick, away from the inductor and other noise sources, preferably on the opposite side of the board with a ground plane between them. Place input filter capacitors near VIN, optional output-to-feedback feed-forward capacitors and compensation components near the IC, and use surface-mount parts to minimize lead inductance and noise coupling. Keep high-current traces short, direct, and thick, with a recommended minimum of 15 mils per ampere on standard PCBs. Position the inductor, output capacitors, and output diode close together. Connect relevant grounds directly to a ground plane; consider ground planes on both PCB sides and separate power and signal planes on multilayer boards. Arrange switching-current loops in the same direction to reduce radiated EMI.

Each output driver supports 2-A peak currents. Use a dedicated power-ground section for high-di/dt paths, connect it to PGND, MOSFET sources, input power returns, and the bulk input capacitor, and bypass VCC directly to it. Clamp the output with a high-current Schottky diode to VCC and PGND; no other circuitry should connect to power ground. Bypass VREF and analog circuitry to signal ground, using recommended low-ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors.

The passage also covers documentation-update subscriptions, TI E2E support resources, ESD-handling precautions, package and orderable-information limitations, and TI’s resource and liability disclaimers.

Harvard researcher Ian Wallace and colleagues examined more than 2,000 skeletons from archaeological collections, unclaimed morgues, and medical-school donations, looking for eburnation, a polished knee-bone surface indicating joint rubbing. They found that knee osteoarthritis prevalence doubled from roughly 8% in earlier skeletons to 16% in more recent ones, even after adjusting for age and weight. The findings challenge the view of arthritis as simple “wear and tear” caused by aging or obesity. Researchers hypothesize that physical inactivity may be a major factor, as stronger supporting muscles and thicker cartilage can help joints withstand stress. Exercise may help even after arthritis develops, though sudden activity can be inappropriate when joints are severely damaged. The study does not establish inactivity as the cause or guarantee that exercise prevents arthritis; other lifestyle or environmental factors may contribute, and further research is needed to identify them and determine how to counteract the rise in osteoarthritis.

This medRxiv preprint examines how contact-network structure affects COVID-19 transmission. Researchers modeled synthetic networks of about 3,000 people, matching 2019 age and household-size distributions for Florida and Texas, with household, classroom, workplace, and low-rate community interaction layers. A modified discrete-time SEIR model simulated symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, recovery, and mortality under three behavioral scenarios: full participation, vulnerable individuals avoiding work or school, and entire households with vulnerable members avoiding those interactions. The study found that isolation by vulnerable individuals alone did not sufficiently reduce their infection risk; age and household structure had varied, counteracting effects; and coworker interactions generally contributed more to disease spread than school interactions.

Using eQTLGen expression data and Mendelian randomization, this study identified genes whose genetically predicted expression is associated with prostate cancer risk. UK Biobank data (3,269 cases; 459,664 controls) served for discovery, yielding 151 candidate genes, while FinnGen data (6,311 cases; 74,685 controls) replicated 12: HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, and HLA-A were positively associated with risk, whereas PPARGC1A, FLOT2, TKT, CARNS1, GPBAR1, CSF1R, and TRAV21 were negatively associated. No significant heterogeneity or pleiotropy was detected.

GO and KEGG enrichment analyses implicated metabolic and cancer-related pathways, including insulin signaling and the pentose phosphate pathway. A STRING protein–protein interaction network was constructed for the 12 genes. DSigDB predicted five candidate drugs: tauroursodeoxycholic acid, Adehl, GDP366, decanoic acid, and GW612286X. AutoDock molecular docking produced seven drug–target results, with binding energies ranging from −4.8 to −11.1; the lowest was for tauroursodeoxycholic acid and GPBAR1.

The findings provide genetically supported target genes and potential drug candidates for prostate cancer. However, environmental and lifestyle factors were not considered, and the targets and drugs require experimental validation and clinical trials to establish safety and efficacy.

British officials sought to mediate between Chile and Argentina over naval expenditures prompted by Chile’s warship purchases. British minister Lowther relayed Chile’s interest in disarmament to Barrington in Buenos Aires, who proposed canceling Argentine ironclad orders; Argentina refused, and the British government had not authorized the proposal. Chilean minister Concha later offered a more limited halt to armaments, but Argentina had already ordered two ironclads that would preserve its naval advantage. Mitre’s article advocating noninterference in Pacific affairs drew opposition but support from Chile for improved relations. Under British mediation, the governments continued secret negotiations, temporarily interrupted by Alcorta’s death. The presidential message described optimistic financial conditions that drew criticism, noted progress toward a boundary settlement and arbitration, praised the armed forces, and mentioned plans to promote colonization and settlement.

Amgen reported that Repatha reduced cardiovascular death, heart attack and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial, potentially broadening the market for the cholesterol-lowering drug. Repatha generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024, up 36% from the prior year, while analysts highlighted the opportunity to reach patients who have not met LDL-C goals.

This study evaluated first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1), measured by transthoracic echocardiography, in 207 adults with chest pain who underwent coronary angiography. Patients were grouped by maximal stenosis severity: mild (<50%; n=73), moderate (50–69%; n=39), and severe (≥70%; n=95). LVEF-1 was calculated as the percentage of left ventricular volume change from aortic valve opening to peak aortic flow velocity relative to end-diastolic volume.

LVEF-1 decreased as stenosis severity increased, whereas conventional LVEF did not differ significantly among groups. LVEF-1 was negatively correlated with the Gensini score (r=-0.694) and BNP and independently predicted stenosis ≥50% and ≥70%. Its AUC was higher than that of other echocardiographic indicators. Cutoffs of 27.9% and 26.9% predicted ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis with respective sensitivities of 82.8% and 89.5% and specificities of 83.6% and 83.9%.

Among 82 patients undergoing PCI, LVEF-1 and GLS increased and E/e′ decreased after four days, while LVEF did not significantly change. Gensini score and stent diameter independently influenced the change in LVEF-1. The findings indicate that LVEF-1 may detect early myocardial dysfunction and post-PCI myocardial recovery more sensitively than LVEF. Limitations include the small sample, differences between centers, absence of coronary functional or microcirculatory testing, and possible medication effects.

NXP shares fell 5% after China’s warning against U.S. trade threats weakened hopes for Beijing’s approval of Qualcomm’s $44 billion acquisition. The deal has cleared eight of nine regulators, with China pending, although antitrust talks were reportedly on hold.

The passage traces the concept of an “ownership society” to Peter Drucker and David Howell, whose use of “privatisation” influenced Margaret Thatcher’s programme, and notes that George W. Bush later popularized the phrase. It says that despite India’s extensive state involvement, reforms since 2014 under Narendra Modi seek to reduce it and encourage individual financial autonomy. Measures cited include banking restructuring and insolvency laws, reduced political interference, consolidation of public-sector banks, cuts to LPG and kerosene subsidies, and UDAY for state electricity boards. It concludes that a true ownership society requires ending government handouts and expanding privatisation.

Over 500 flu cases were reported in the Show-Me State last week, but severity was not yet known. A nurse advised seeing a doctor, antivirals within 72 hours of symptoms, fluids, rest, and avoiding work or others while ill.

Among participants without prior COVID-19, a BNT162b2 booster produced antibody responses against the original strain comparable to responses one month after Dose 2. One BNT162b2SA booster produced Beta-variant responses comparable to original-strain responses after two BNT162b2 doses; among those without prior BNT162b2, two BNT162b2SA doses produced similar Beta-variant responses. Researchers considered these results unlikely to be due to chance.

In Phase 1, a few participants had temporary lymphocyte reductions 1–3 days after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, with counts returning to normal by days 6–8. Injection-site reactions and systemic events within seven days were temporary and mostly mild or moderate; injection-site pain, tiredness, and headache were most common. All Phase 1 doses were well tolerated except 100 µg BNT162b1, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions. The 30 µg BNT162b2 dose was selected for Phase 2/3, where it was well tolerated; fewer than 1% in either the vaccine or placebo group left the blinded phase because of medical problems.

Serious medical problems were uncommon, and no single problem affected at least 1% of Phase 2/3 participants after the primary series. No vaccine-related serious problems were reported among participants aged 12–15, while a small number of temporary serious events in older recipients were considered possibly vaccine-related. Most serious problems after boosters, BNT162b2SA primary vaccination, or lower-dose boosters were not believed vaccine-related.

No Phase 1 participant died. During Phase 2/3, deaths occurred among initial BNT162b2 recipients, initial placebo recipients who later received BNT162b2, and placebo-only recipients. Researchers did not believe the deaths were caused by BNT162b2. No participant who received BNT162b2SA in Phase 3 died.

The TPS7H500x-SP family (TPS7H5001/2/3/4-SP) comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They operate with internal or external clocking, require external gate drivers, support frequencies up to 2 MHz, and suit buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

Dead time: the TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50-ns (typical) dead time, while the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP allow two independent programmable dead times (TDPS via a resistor from PS to AVSS; TDSP via a resistor from SP to AVSS) of 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ; floating PS/SP yields a minimum 8 ns (typical). Synchronous rectifier outputs are disabled during soft start, so dead time is observed afterward. Leading edge blank time is fixed at 50 ns (typical) for the TPS7H5003-SP and programmable (10 kΩ–300 kΩ, must not float) from LEB to AVSS on the other devices; it also contributes to the device minimum on-time.

Pulse-skipping mode addresses minimum-on-time problems at high frequency: primary outputs stop switching periodically, SRA/SRB stay on if soft start has ended (and off if soft start is in progress), and pulses are skipped when COMP is below 0.3 V at the rising clock edge and the previous duty cycle was under 25%. With a 50% duty limit and both OUTA and OUTB active, equal pulse skipping preserves volt-second balance and avoids transformer saturation.

Duty cycle is set by the DCL pin: VLDO gives 100%, AVSS gives 50% (only TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP), and floating gives 75%. The TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50% (DCL to AVSS). The 50% limit supports push-pull designs; some variation occurs with external synchronization clock duty cycle.

Current sense: CS_ILIM carries a signal representative of primary-side current and is compared to COMP/2 (with a 150 mV offset) for peak current mode control; a resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS supports PWM operation and overcurrent protection, with a 1.05 V nominal current-limit threshold (hiccup entry). ILIM calculation differs by topology (forward with a sense resistor, buck with a current sense transformer), and margin between normal peak current and the trip point is required.

Hiccup: cycle-by-cycle limiting continues until CHICC reaches 0.6 V, which discharges SS and stops switching; HICC is pulled to 1 V (~1 mA) then discharged by 1 µA until 0.3 V, triggering a new soft start (normal operation resumes if overcurrent is gone). Minimum CHICC of 3.3 nF is recommended.

External fault: the FAULT pin allows user protection logic; exceeding 0.6 V (typical) for the 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width shuts down switching and discharges SS. Recovery occurs below 0.5 V after a delay of about 15 switching cycles plus an internal logic delay, then soft start restarts; a new fault during the delay restarts the sequence.

Slope compensation (RSC resistor to AVSS) mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; the minimum for stability is 0.5× the inductor falling current slope and 1× is recommended. Frequency compensation supports Type 2A or 2B schemes (Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation), with RCOMP calculated from the desired crossover frequency using gmea of 1800 µA/V (typical) and a 0.613 V reference, CCOMP placing the compensation zero, and optional CHF for ESR zero compensation; power stage transconductance depends on topology, turns ratios, RCS, and CCSR. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175 °C (typical) and restarts below 160 °C.

Example design: a 500-kHz GaN synchronous push-pull converter (RT = 205 kΩ) with 5 V output (RTOP = 10 kΩ, RBOT = 1.4 kΩ), 25 ns dead time (RPS = RSP = 20.5 kΩ), ~50 ns blank time (RLEB = 49.9 kΩ), 33 nF soft-start capacitor (~7.5 ms), turns ratio 2.5, magnetizing current 6% of output current, 40 µH primary inductance, 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, RCD clamp (KCLAMP = 1.5), 0.47 µH output inductor (40% ripple), minimum 1.3 mF output capacitance increased to 2.3 mF for SET mitigation (7 × 330 µF polymer tantalum, 0.86 mΩ equivalent ESR) plus an optional output filter with damping, cycle-by-cycle limiting near 35 A output (~45% margin over 24.25 A peak), 1:100 current sense transformer with RCS = 7.5 Ω, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation at 10 kHz crossover (RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, CHF = 47 pF), and RSC = 102 kΩ.

Power supply and layout: VIN range is 4–14 V with at least 0.1 µF of ceramic (X5R or better) bypass to AVSS, plus bulk capacitance if the supply is remote. Layout guidance covers isolating the feedback trace from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing switch-node copper and high di/dt/dt loops, joining AVSS and power ground at a single point, using wide short current traces (≥15 mil/A), placing bypass and compensation components near the pins, keeping the VSENSE divider close, routing OUTA/OUTB/SRA/SRB away from sensitive pins, filtering CS_ILIM, treating SYNC noise near HICC (with ≥3.3 nF on HICC), and connecting the CFP package backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias.

The passage promotes a made-to-order academic writing service, emphasizing customization, quality, fast delivery, and customer support. It advises comparing providers, requesting quotes, reading reviews, and contacting writers. The company claims it rejects mediocre work and helps customers meet assignment requirements and deadlines.

Pittsburgh unveiled new throwback jerseys modeled after the Steelers’ 1978 uniform, featuring block numbers and shorter sleeves. The team will wear them against Cleveland in Week 8 and use them for at least two seasons, replacing the “bumblebee” throwbacks while commemorating Super Bowl XIII and XIV’s 40th anniversaries.

Using Yahoo Finance daily NIFTY 50 data from 2008 onward, the backtest buys at the close of December’s second Friday and sells at the close of the first trading day of the new year. Reinvesting all equity produced an average trade gain of 1.2%, a 71% win rate, a profit factor of 6, and 7% maximum drawdown. The untradable cash index serves only as a proxy.

On February 25, 2019, Amazon.com, Inc. elected Indra K. Nooyi to its Board of Directors and appointed her to the Audit Committee. Nooyi served as PepsiCo’s CEO from 2006 to 2018 and as chairman from May 2007 to February 2019. She also received a restricted stock unit award for 549 Amazon common shares, vesting in three equal annual installments beginning May 15, 2020, subject to continued service, and entered the company’s standard-form indemnification agreement.

Digital leaders foster a data culture built on transparency, collaboration, learning, and measurement. They make relevant data broadly accessible while applying controls for privacy, ethics, and governance. Leadership sponsorship helps establish an organization-wide mindset in which ideas and decisions draw on data from across teams. In contrast, digital laggards restrict access on a “need-to-know” basis, maintain departmental data silos, and often use data to justify decisions already made. They favor individual judgment and process adherence, set goals insufficiently grounded in data, and discourage measurement when it may reveal missed expectations.

Digital leaders use detailed metrics and continuous feedback to track objectives and performance, often supplemented by 360-degree reviews. Clear, measurable goals provide structure while supporting autonomy, innovation, experimentation, and calculated risk-taking. The research found standardized APIs across 88% of digital leaders, compared with 27% of laggards.

One transforming retailer upgraded its data systems and implemented real-time sales dashboards. Sales data is pushed to reports three times daily, enabling leaders to make faster decisions about inventory, marketing, supply chains, and other areas.

Digital leaders align teams through transparent objectives linked to corporate strategy, often combining top-down priorities with employee input to secure buy-in. Excessive instrumentation or analysis can, however, undermine intuition. Effective data cultures align employees vertically with company goals and horizontally across functions through shared metrics, common data models, and open access. Successful transformation requires leadership, cultural change, skills, and consistent alignment between stated values and daily behavior. Organizations are categorized as data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant, with each requiring targeted actions to develop a stronger data culture.

Stocks represent ownership in a company and have historically been the strongest-performing asset class, but they can lose capital, sometimes even over ten-year periods. Diversification across companies, industries, and stock types is recommended to reduce risk. Some stocks pay dividends, which are not guaranteed and may change over time.

Bonds involve lending money to a company or government agency rather than obtaining ownership. They generally have fixed interest payments and a maturity date, are less risky than stocks, and are paid before shareholders in bankruptcy. Risk and interest rates vary with maturity, credit quality, and liquidity. Sovereign bonds have historically helped cushion stock-market losses during turmoil, while corporate bonds may face greater recession and credit risks.

Historical performance favors stocks, but the appropriate allocation depends on an investor’s goals, risk tolerance, and time horizon. For example, someone nearing retirement might reduce stocks and increase bonds. A backtested 60% stock/40% bond portfolio produced lower returns than an all-stock portfolio but also lower volatility and drawdowns.

A separate “Sell in May and go away” strategy tests selling stocks in May and reinvesting in November, including investing in countries during their winter months. Its backtest used equally weighted regional ETFs and measured CAGR, maximum drawdown, and standard deviation. The strategy did not perform as expected.

This continuation application (U.S. Ser. No. 17/764,509; PCT/US2020/056133) describes muscle-targeting compositions, engineered recombinant AAV capsids, related vector systems, and therapeutic uses. It incorporates by reference four provisional applications and an electronic sequence listing. Conventional AAVs primarily transduce the liver after systemic delivery and have limited tropism for other tissues; treating nonhepatic diseases therefore may require high doses that cause liver toxicity and complicate manufacturing. Species-specific differences in transduction also limit the accuracy of mouse studies.

Disclosed embodiments combine a cargo with a targeting moiety containing one or more RGD or non-RGD n-mer motifs of about 1–20 amino acids. The motifs may be displayed externally from engineered AAV capsids at defined positions in AAV9 or analogous positions in other AAV serotypes to confer muscle-specific or species-specific tropism. Engineered particles, capsid polypeptides, vector systems, producer cells, pharmaceutical formulations, kits, and administration methods are described.

Vector systems can encode targeting motifs and optionally include cargo, regulatory elements, muscle-specific promoters, and AAV rep proteins. Cargo may comprise oligonucleotides, therapeutic transgenes, peptides, CRISPR-Cas components, dystrophin exon-skipping agents, or mini- or micro-dystrophin genes. Potential applications include muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, neuromuscular, glycogen-storage, and expanded-repeat diseases, as well as autoimmune, cancer, viral, and progeroid disorders.

Methods generate capsid-variant libraries by inserting n-mers into AAV capsids, producing variant particles, and selecting variants through muscle-specific expression and transduction, including across mouse strains and species. Figures and tables describe library construction, promoter-based expression, variant selection, biodistribution, DMD correction with CRISPR, integrin-mediated entry, and ranked CK8, MHCK7, and combined capsid variants.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2020 presented unaudited GAAP financial statements. Quarterly revenue was $43.076 billion, operating income was $17.897 billion, net income was $15.463 billion, and diluted EPS was $2.03, compared with $36.906 billion, $13.891 billion, $11.649 billion, and $1.51, respectively, a year earlier. For the six months, revenue was $80.230 billion, net income was $29.356 billion, and diluted EPS was $3.85. Operating cash flow was $12.516 billion for the quarter and $31.851 billion for the six months. At December 31, total assets were $304.137 billion, total liabilities were $173.901 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $130.236 billion.

Commercial cloud revenue increased 34% to $16.7 billion in the quarter. Azure revenue grew 50%, Office 365 Commercial revenue grew 21%, Dynamics 365 revenue grew 39%, LinkedIn revenue increased 23%, and Xbox content and services revenue increased 40%. Microsoft reported three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing.

Microsoft increased the estimated useful lives of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years, raising six-month operating income by $1.7 billion and net income by $1.4 billion. It also entered an agreement to acquire ZeniMax Media, the parent of Bethesda, for $7.5 billion in cash.

The company repurchased $6.535 billion of stock and paid $4.230 billion in dividends during the quarter. Other disclosures covered investments, derivatives, debt, leases, taxes, legal contingencies, and adoption of expected-credit-loss accounting guidance without a material impact. Deloitte’s review identified no material modifications to the interim financial information.

European stocks rose Monday, led by banks in thin holiday trading; London and U.S. markets were closed. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.5%. Italian banks rallied on Monte dei Paschi’s planned €15 billion debt issue. Eurozone manufacturing PMI was due Monday, with inflation data later in the week.

In a prospective NORPACT2 cohort study, serum indole 3-acetate (3-IAA) was measured before chemotherapy in 124 patients with nonmetastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, including 68 with borderline resectable and 56 with locally advanced disease. Thirty-five patients provided a second sample 2–4 months after starting chemotherapy. Most received FOLFIRINOX. Median pretreatment 3-IAA was 290 ng/mL and was associated with age, but not tumor diameter, CA19-9, treatment group, or chemotherapy response defined by CT or CA19-9 decline. Concentrations also did not significantly distinguish patients who underwent resection or survived one year, and the nonsignificant increase after chemotherapy was not supported statistically.

Median overall survival was 499 days. Pretreatment 3-IAA was not associated with overall survival in univariable analysis (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.74–1.16; p=0.52) or after adjustment for age, ECOG performance status, CA19-9, and tumor classification (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.68–1.12; p=0.28). Censoring patients at surgical resection also yielded no evidence of an association.

Thus, the study did not reproduce the reported association between 3-IAA and chemotherapy response in metastatic PDAC. Differences in disease stage, tumor burden, patient characteristics, tumor biology, and possibly assay methods were considered potential explanations, although the wide confidence interval limited certainty about the presence or absence of an effect. The authors proposed geographically distinct validation in metastatic PDAC before controlled trials designed to increase circulating 3-IAA as a chemotherapy adjuvant.

A Michigan family is seeking answers after alleging that two Highview Elementary School teachers taped their five-year-old son’s mouth shut, discarded his lunch and told him not to tell his parents. The boy’s parents filed a police report and plan to sue the Crestwood School District, which removed one teacher while disputing earlier abuse allegations. Police are investigating, and the family will not allow the boy to return until the other teacher is fired.

Researchers at McGill University and the University of Toronto propose a theoretical model that treats gaslighting as a learning process based on prediction error minimization. In this framework, gaslighters violate the expectations of trusted people and repeatedly attribute the resulting surprise to a target’s poor grasp of reality, gradually teaching the target to doubt their own perceptions. Because people rely on others, especially close relationships, to form their sense of self and reality, the model holds that anyone could be targeted if they trust the wrong person. Future research should test the model, examine whether attachment styles or trauma affect susceptibility, and improve support for victims.

Reagan Library 1980 Transition Papers include an undated paper prepared by Richard Allen for the Foreign Policy Advisory Board's November 21, 1980 meeting (Tab I of his binder; agenda, press release, Tabs II–IV and minutes missing), and a December 22, 1980 National Security Group report on the State Department transition team (Tabs A–S, attached but unprinted). The advisory committee, announced October 25, was to monitor and assess international developments through the January 20 inauguration; members were Allen, Baker, Casey, Clements, Ford, Haig, Kirkpatrick, Kissinger, McCloy, Rostow, Rumsfeld, Shultz, Tower, and Weinberger. The transition team's Office of Executive Branch Management was headed by William Timmons; Robert Neumann led the State Transition Team, reporting to national security team leader D. Abshire, with Adelman, Brower, Codevilla, Crocker, Drischler, Hackett, McFarlane, Pipes, Rashish, Sanjuan, Stern, Tiller, Weiss, Winsor, and Zapanta also serving. An editorial note quotes Reagan's November 20, 1975 announcement of his candidacy for the 1976 Republican nomination, challenging Ford and citing the economy, government, foreign energy dependence, military superiority, détente, and unresponsive leadership.

Builder Eric Woodward has begun work on a pop-up park at the vacant Fort Langley site of a cancelled mixed-use project that included a boutique hotel. The park will feature community gathering and family play areas and is expected to be substantially complete by early July.

The study addresses domain shift and limited sample sizes in neuroimaging by transferring features learned from the 40,000-subject UK Biobank (UKB) to the OASIS-3, IXI, and ABIDE datasets. It uses simple fully connected convolutional networks for structural-MRI age and sex prediction. The transfer-learning pipeline pre-trains the network on UKB, reshapes and retrains the classifier when output dimensions differ, and then fine-tunes the full model on the target dataset.

Direct transfer showed reduced performance across scanners, especially on ABIDE and IXI, although transferred models remained better than random classification. Feature visualizations and classifier-only fine-tuning indicated that learned features are task-specific and most reusable when pre-training and target tasks match. Full fine-tuning generally improved results, with some overfitting in OASIS sex prediction and IXI age prediction.

Transfer learning substantially outperformed PCA-based elastic-net regression across all datasets and tasks, approximately halving age-prediction error, and generally outperformed training from scratch. The exception was ABIDE sex prediction, where the age range and scanner diversity caused negative transfer. Results also improved over reported age-prediction performance on OASIS and ABIDE. Transfer learning converged faster, worked accurately for OASIS age prediction with as few as 50 training samples, and required more than 400 samples to outperform final-layer-only training for ABIDE sex prediction.

The findings suggest that UKB can provide domain-specific pre-training features for neuroimaging, although its limited scanner coverage and lack of disease-specific data remain constraints. Future directions include feature harmonization, style-transfer methods, and transferring across prediction tasks.

Sea of Thieves is Rare’s fastest-selling game since NPD began tracking sales in 1995. It ranked second-best-selling for March and eighth for 2018 year-to-date in dollar sales, though NPD excludes Game Pass subscribers. The game demonstrates strong demand for major platform-exclusive titles, though its ranking will change when NPD’s April report includes God of War.

Teuvo Teräväinen and Antoine Vermette describe their team’s late-season opportunity as exciting, emphasizing confidence, perseverance, and capitalizing on chances to advance. They say Tampa Bay began strongly but their team improved in the second and third periods, with Teräväinen scoring twice in the win. Vermette praises Tampa Bay’s speed, puck possession, pressure, positioning, and skill, while noting that successful teams must overcome adversity. Teräväinen reflects on scoring before family and friends in Finland, his father’s support, and working hard despite being smaller than many teammates.

The study develops an AI-based system for classifying citation intents in Turkish Computer Science articles, addressing a gap in Turkish citation-intent research. It introduces the first large-scale, publicly available Turkish dataset for this task: 723 research articles yielded 20,026 extracted citation instances, which were curated into 2,650 labeled sentences. Annotations used five Web of Science categories—Background, Basis, Support, Differ, and Discuss—and combined academic experts with GPT- and Gemini-assisted in-context learning.

Experiments compared manual in-context learning, DSPy’s MIPROv2 prompt optimization, and ensemble methods using GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. Revised manual prompts substantially improved accuracy over initial prompts. DSPy optimized instructions and few-shot demonstrations, reaching 86.5% accuracy. Few-shot counts had inconsistent effects: both Gemini Flash and GPT-4o reached 88.4% zero-shot, while additional examples sometimes reduced performance.

A majority-vote ensemble achieved 90.2%, a logistic-regression stacked model 91.0%, and the final XGBoost-based stacked ensemble 91.3%. Major challenges were severe Background-class imbalance, confusion between semantically similar Support and Differ labels, and inconsistent LLM predictions. Proposed future work includes hierarchical classifiers, targeted or synthetic data for rare classes, and broader document context.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 3% for the first time in four years, raising corporate borrowing concerns, while quarterly results disappointed. The S&P 500 and Dow posted their biggest drops in two-and-a-half weeks; the Dow lost a fifth straight day and the S&P 500 is down 1.5% year-to-date. Technology and industrial stocks dragged on indexes: Alphabet (GOOGL.O) fell 2.77%, erasing year-to-date gains as expenses and shrinking margins outweighed better-than-expected profit; Caterpillar (CAT.N) dropped on steel price worries despite beating estimates; 3M (MMM.N) was the Dow's biggest drag after in-line profits, an operating miss and a lowered 2018 forecast; Apple (AAPL.O) fell on soft high-end smartphone demand, underscored by Corning's screen glass sales decline; and Facebook, Amazon and Netflix also weighed. Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) declined despite beating and raising forecasts. Of the 24% of S&P 500 companies reporting first-quarter results, 77.1% beat consensus, with estimated earnings growth of 21.1%. Consumer confidence rebounded in April, and oil rose above $75 a barrel before reversing on U.S.-European pledges to resolve Iran differences.

On April 27, 2018, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into an amended and restated unsecured revolving credit agreement with Bank of America, N.A. as administrative agent and participating lenders. The agreement increased Amazon’s borrowing capacity from $3.0 billion to $7.0 billion and extended its term through April 27, 2021. Borrowings may fund general corporate purposes and backstop commercial paper notes.

Amazon also established a private placement commercial paper program allowing it to issue unsecured notes with maximum aggregate outstanding amounts of $7.0 billion and maturities of up to 397 days. Amounts may be reborrowed, and proceeds are expected for general corporate purposes.

Hockey players emphasize resting, preparing, and maintaining a businesslike focus as they face the challenge of closing out the Stanley Cup Finals with one game remaining. They say winning cannot be assumed and requires mental and emotional readiness. The team is encouraged by veterans’ experience but remains cautious about the stakes. An injured teammate may not play, so others must step up. Players also note that pressure differs between home games, which resemble a circus, and road games, where success can be shared more privately with teammates and families.

Research co-authored by Ross Levine finds that easier credit conditions encourage businesses to invest in pollution reduction. More available credit finances environmental projects, while lower interest rates increase the payoff from green investments. Using deposit windfalls from the fracking boom to isolate the effects of credit, the authors found benzene emissions fell 26% in non-gas-producing counties with the largest credit gains, while other pollutants declined similarly. Firms whose lenders received these windfalls also reduced toxic emissions, earned better environmental ratings, and advocated green issues more than comparable firms. The study does not assess fracking’s environmental effects; Levine plans to examine how borrowing conditions affect worker safety.

Ryan Malone and Brian Gionta could give the 2018 U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team Olympic experience despite its lack of active NHL players. Malone signed an AHL tryout contract with the Iowa Wild, while Gionta remains under consideration for the PyeongChang roster.

Business Insider reports that David Ellison, backed by father Larry Ellison after their Paramount acquisition, is widely expected to pursue Warner Bros. Discovery, though no formal bid exists and he has not confirmed plans. A combination could merge Paramount’s streaming services with HBO Max, combine studios, add Warner’s sports rights, and consolidate back-office functions, potentially creating a major streaming competitor. WBD is valued at roughly $44 billion and has about $35 billion in debt; Larry Ellison’s wealth and reported Apollo interest could help finance a bid. The paper introduces edit-distance realizations of the interleaving distance for constructible multiparameter persistence modules over \(\mathbb{R}^d\). It reviews poset theory, Galois connections, constructibility, graded modules, and finite presentations, showing that for \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-persistence modules, constructibility is equivalent to finite presentedness.

Two categories of constructible modules are defined using finite join-semilattices and finite \(d\)-grids, with morphisms required to have right adjoints. Edit paths consist of such module morphisms, and their lengths are the sums of the morphisms’ distortions. The main theorem proves that, for every \(d\), the interleaving distance between constructible \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-persistence modules equals the resulting edit distance in both categories. The proof combines a Galois-connection construction with the characterization of interleaving modules by presentations differing by a translation, together with an “easy-edit lemma” and interpolation.

The equality also gives an order-theoretic view of interleaving distance and shows that interleaving stability of an invariant is equivalent to edit stability; stability under a single edit suffices. The edit distance is shown to be NP-hard to compute. The results extend earlier one-parameter Galois-insertion results to constructible multiparameter persistence and provide tools for studying stable invariants in multiparameter persistent homology.

This week’s top posts cover DomTerm’s browser-based GUI toolkit, open-source development history, container runtimes, and the 20th anniversary of “open source software.” An Ontario middle school’s Linux program has kept more than 200 old computers in use, while community members are recognized for the site’s eighth anniversary.

Fourth-grader Lexi Bergeron sold handmade stretchy straw fidgeters to help classmates afford hot school lunches in Grand Haven, Michigan. Inspired by reports of students facing lunch-account debts, she raised $11 in her first week. Her mother, Sara, created a GoFundMe campaign that exceeded its initial $188 target and aimed to raise $2,200 by the end of December to eliminate lunch debts districtwide.

The TPS7H500x-SP series uses fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode control to regulate converter peak current and duty cycle. The internal clock initiates the primary gate-driver outputs, and switching stops when the sensed current reaches the stepped-down COMP voltage; the PWM comparator’s sensed-current signal includes a 150 mV offset. OUTB waveforms apply only to the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP.

CS_ILIM senses transformer primary current through an external resistor connected to AVSS. The COMP/2 voltage serves as the peak-current reference, while a nominal 1.05 V CS_ILIM threshold triggers current limiting. Current-limit calculations must account for the converter topology and transformer or current-sense-transformer turns ratios, with sufficient margin between normal peak current and the trip point.

At 1.05 V, the controller performs cycle-by-cycle current limiting and charges the CHICC capacitor with an 80 µA pulsed current. At 0.6 V, switching stops and the soft-start pin is discharged. HICC is then pulled to 1 V with approximately 1 mA and discharged by a 1 µA restart current until it reaches 0.3 V, after which soft start resumes if the overcurrent has cleared. CHICC controls both the cycle-by-cycle limiting delay and restart interval; 3.3 nF is the minimum recommended value.

The FAULT pin supports additional external protection. A typical threshold above 0.6 V lasting within the specified 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse-width range causes shutdown, soft-start discharge, and cessation of switching. After FAULT falls below 0.5 V, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay before restarting. A renewed fault restarts the delay.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles above 50%. The minimum stable compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, and the recommended value is equal to that slope; the RSC resistor sets the desired ramp. Because the controller uses a transconductance error amplifier, Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported. Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection is based on crossover frequency, power-stage transconductance, the 0.613 V reference, and the 1800 µA/V typical error-amplifier transconductance.

Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175 °C junction temperature and permits power-up reinitialization below 160 °C.

The devices are radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers intended for space-grade DC-DC converters, require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A 500 kHz, 5 V synchronous push-pull GaN converter example uses a 205 kΩ timing resistor; 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ feedback resistors; 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns; a 49.9 kΩ leading-edge-blank-time resistor for approximately 50 ns; and a 33 nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms. The transformer turns ratio is 2.5, and its selected primary inductance is 40 µH. Primary GaN FETs use a 170 V rating, while 80 V synchronous rectifiers are used with parallel Schottky diodes.

The example uses a 0.47 µH output inductor, at least 1.3 mF of output capacitance, and 2.3 mF total to provide additional single-event-transient mitigation. Seven 330 µF polymer-tantalum capacitors provide the selected capacitance with an equivalent ESR of 0.86 mΩ. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins near 35 A, versus a maximum-load peak inductor current of 24.25 A. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5 Ω sense resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation uses a 10 kHz target crossover, 16.2 A/V power-stage transconductance, 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF. A 102 kΩ RSC resistor sets slope compensation.

The controllers operate from a 4–14 V input and require at least a 0.1 µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor; X5R or better ceramics are recommended, with additional capacitance or bulk decoupling where needed. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, and using multiple vias to connect CFP backside metallization to AVSS.

The study examines relapse of Plasmodium vivax, whose dormant liver hypnozoites can reactivate and cause recurrent bloodstream infections. It distinguishes short-latency “tropical” and long-latency “temperate” strains and considers intrinsic biological timing alongside proposed external triggers such as fever, haemolysis, seasonal changes, and mosquito bites.

The authors developed analytical likelihoods for an “exponential clock” model in which hypnozoites activate independently at a constant rate without external triggers, while accounting for variable mosquito bites, sporozoite batch sizes, hypnozoite versus immediate-development outcomes, age-related anti-disease immunity, and treatment-related prophylaxis. The model predicts relapse rates proportional to hypnozoite burden, lengthening intervals as reservoirs are depleted, overdispersed hypnozoite burdens, and nonlinear age-related relapse patterns.

The model was fitted to longitudinal data from the SPf66 vaccine trial, in which 1,344 children aged 2–15 on the Thailand–Myanmar border were monitored daily for 21 months. The trial recorded 2,504 symptomatic vivax and 1,164 symptomatic falciparum infections over 1,988 person-years, with up to 13 symptomatic vivax episodes per child. Estimated average hypnozoite carriage was 171 days, with a half-life of 118 days; the estimated relapse-to-primary-infection ratio was 3.4, implying that about 75% of observed symptomatic vivax infections were relapses. Elevated vivax incidence after artesunate-treated falciparum monoinfections was compatible with external triggering, while mefloquine’s approximately one-month prophylactic effect may have masked such effects in patients receiving artesunate–mefloquine.

Researchers identified two grape-leaf bacterial strains that degraded guaiacol, a volatile phenol linked to smoky wine flavors, within 96 hours. Deleting a gene responsible for guaiacol degradation prevented one strain from consuming the compound. The strains did not grow on similar smoky chemicals, indicating that other bacteria may be needed to address additional causes of smoke taint. The microbial approach could offer winemakers a more targeted alternative to filtration, which can also remove desirable wine components. More research is needed into the grape microbiome and other smoke-taint compounds.

The Department of Education will hold its first School Safety Conference on June 26 at Okkodo High School, with about 400 support staff attending. Topics include bullying, harassment, suicide, sexual identity, legal issues, school climate, drugs and alcohol, crisis response, and mental health. The article advocates an ecological, sociocultural perspective on English education policy and practice, arguing that learning and teaching must be understood within the broader social, cultural, economic, and educational contexts of learners’ lives. Focusing on Malaysia and Thailand, it reviews curriculum goals, proficiency targets, teacher capability, classroom conditions, and sociolinguistic factors affecting school English.

In both countries, mandated communicative approaches and CEFR-based targets have often not met intended outcomes. Malaysia’s national targets exceeded baseline proficiency at most grade levels, while rural students consistently performed below urban peers. The communicative approach widened socioeconomic and urban-rural inequalities, partly because English was used more at home in affluent urban communities. Teachers often resorted to Malay to support comprehension, reflecting the language’s contested relationship with Malay identity and limited societal use outside school.

Thailand’s modified CEFR framework similarly sets ambitious progression targets, while low O-NET results reveal socioeconomic and regional disparities. Thai remains the dominant language of communication and national identity, limiting students’ opportunities to practise English naturally. Teacher proficiency is also a concern: 29% of surveyed Malaysian primary teachers were below B2, while 59.9% of Thai teachers attending training courses were below the B1 target. However, standardized proficiency tests do not measure pedagogical effectiveness or reflect teachers’ own educational experiences.

Classroom research reveals large classes, mixed abilities, examination pressure, limited resources and teacher support, unsuitable curriculum assumptions, and indigenous-language backgrounds. Teachers’ departures from prescribed methods may therefore reflect context-specific adaptations rather than deficiencies. The article concludes that unrealistic targets are self-defeating and that curriculum outcomes should be aligned with local sociolinguistic realities, educational capacity, and classroom conditions, with teachers and students involved in policy development.

Delays to U.S. tax reform and nerves ahead of Trump’s China summit also weighed. Wall Street closed 0.3% lower, Treasury yields and the dollar fell, and most Asian and European stocks were lower.

NVIDIA Corporation reported third-quarter fiscal 2020 results for the period ended October 27, 2019. Revenue was $3.014 billion, down 5% year over year but up 17% sequentially. Gross margin increased to 63.6%, operating income declined 12% to $927 million, and net income declined 27% to $899 million; diluted earnings per share were $1.45. For the first nine months, revenue fell 18% to $7.813 billion and net income fell to $1.845 billion from $3.575 billion.

GPU revenue declined 8% for the quarter to $2.565 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue rose 10% to $449 million. By market, Gaming revenue was $1.659 billion, Professional Visualization $324 million, Data Center $726 million, Automotive $162 million, and OEM and Other $143 million. Higher GeForce margins, including sales of previously written-off components and lower component costs, supported gross margin, while operating expenses rose 15%, largely due to employee additions, compensation, infrastructure, and stock-based compensation.

At October 27, 2019, NVIDIA held $9.765 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $4 million in marketable securities, with total assets of $15.810 billion, liabilities of $4.596 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $11.214 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $3.296 billion. The company paid $292 million in dividends and intended to return the remaining $2.01 billion of its planned $3 billion fiscal 2020 shareholder returns through dividends and repurchases, without repurchasing shares before closing the Mellanox acquisition.

NVIDIA agreed to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion. Mellanox shareholders approved the transaction; U.S. and Mexican approvals had been received, while European and Chinese reviews remained pending, and closing was expected in early 2020.

The company adopted lease accounting in fiscal 2020, recognizing $470 million of lease assets and $500 million of lease liabilities. It reported $624 million of nine-month stock-based compensation, $1.99 billion of long-term debt, and no borrowings under its $575 million credit facility or commercial paper program. NVIDIA also disclosed securities and derivative lawsuits concerning channel inventory and cryptocurrency-mining effects, with no contingent liability accrued because potential losses were not considered probable.

Fenerbahce have reportedly offered the midfielder a lucrative deal, but his family is settled in London, and remaining in the Premier League could support his hopes of an England recall. Education Department officials, higher education leaders and advocates concluded the first round of negotiated rulemaking on student loan provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act with cautious optimism but no consensus. Talks will resume November 3–7.

The central dispute was which graduate programs qualify as professional and can borrow up to $200,000 rather than $100,000. After initially limiting eligibility to 10 programs, the department proposed a one-year expansion covering qualifying programs designated as professional before July 4, 2025. Committee members raised concerns about the proposal’s clarity, legal standing, cost and effects on health-care fields, while submitting alternative approaches.

The shutdown also prevented the department from publicly posting updated proposals and other materials, limiting transparency.

Repayment rules were another major topic. Nearly all income-driven repayment plans except Repayment Assistance will end July 1, 2026. Existing borrowers must apply by that date to remain in the grandfathered Income-Based Repayment plan. Committee members representing legal aid and consumer groups urged the department to simplify a lengthy transition process for Parent PLUS borrowers, but their proposed changes were not adopted.

In a prospective observational analysis of 451,355 UK Biobank participants, including 22,451 with diabetes, ethnicity-specific BMI categories were associated with cardiovascular biomarkers, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, and mortality. Among participants without diabetes, increasing BMI was associated with greater carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, cardiac contractility, lower ejection fraction, and higher cardiovascular event rates. These relationships were less marked among participants with diabetes, who exhibited adverse cardiovascular phenotypes even at normal BMI, particularly in terms of arterial disease and cardiac contractility. Normal-weight participants with diabetes had cardiovascular imaging findings broadly comparable to those of participants with obesity without diabetes.

During 5,3 million person-years of follow-up, cardiovascular mortality increased across BMI categories in both groups. Compared with normal-weight participants without diabetes, adjusted cardiovascular mortality IRRs were 2.45 for normal-weight diabetes, 2.90 for overweight diabetes, and 4.34 for obese diabetes; among participants without diabetes, IRRs were 1.09 for overweight and 1.70 for obesity. Non-fatal myocardial infarction and ischaemic stroke showed similar patterns.

Adiposity measures were more strongly correlated with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes duration or HbA1c, although all correlations were weak. Normal-weight diabetes was also associated with greater visceral adiposity and suboptimal physical activity, blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, and smoking. The authors concluded that obesity and diabetes are additively associated with cardiovascular disease and that additional factors may underpin the elevated risk in normal-weight diabetes. Limitations included incomplete imaging data, selection bias, no diabetes-type stratification, inability to infer causality, recruitment before SGLT2 inhibitor use, and limited representativeness of the UK Biobank.

Defendant faced 13 counts arising from six allegedly extortionate incidents at three Chinese restaurants over two months and moved to sever charges arising from separate incidents. The court explained that under CPL 200.20(2)(b), offenses based on different transactions may be joined when proof of one would be materially admissible in chief at the trial of another, and such charges cannot be severed. Applying the *Molineux* principles of common scheme, identity, and intent, the court found that the incidents within Groups A and C suggested a common plan, although the three groups as a whole did not. A distinctive modus operandi—speaking Mandarin, demanding money for his “brothers,” and claiming membership in the Eagles gang—made identity in one incident probative of identity in others. Because identity had not been conclusively established and an alibi might be raised, other-incident evidence could rebut that defense. Earlier extortionate demands were also admissible to prove knowledge and intent in Groups B and C because the demands did not necessarily establish criminal intent on their face. Accordingly, all counts were properly joinable under CPL 200.20(2)(b), and the motion to sever was denied.

This observational study examined associations between arterial stiffness, measured by brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), and renal function in Chinese adults. The cross-sectional analysis included 67,060 participants, while the longitudinal cohort included 12,324. Renal function was assessed using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and microalbuminuria.

Cross-sectionally, participants with chronic kidney disease (CKD) had higher baPWV than those without CKD, and eGFR was independently and negatively associated with baPWV. During follow-up, incident CKD prevalence increased across ascending baPWV tertiles (18.68%, 27.11%, and 54.11%). After full adjustment, the highest baPWV tertile was associated with greater CKD risk (HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.26–3.76). Conversely, the lowest eGFR category was associated with increased arterial stiffness risk (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.02–1.44). Cross-lagged analysis indicated that declining kidney function preceded increases in arterial stiffness, with the path from baseline eGFR to follow-up baPWV (β=-0.077) stronger than the reverse path (β=-0.063). The authors proposed a mutually reinforcing cycle between renal dysfunction and arterial stiffness. Limitations included use of serum creatinine-based eGFR rather than the 51Cr-EDTA reference method and reliance on an observational population from central China.

This case study examined whether repeated in-lab lateral spinal cord stimulation (SCS), used to restore missing-foot sensation, affects muscle activation and gait in a woman aged 60–65 with a left transtibial amputation. Percutaneous epidural leads delivered stimulation during prosthetic-limb stance, with amplitude modulated by plantar pressure. EMG and motion capture were recorded during self-paced walking at early (day 30) and late (day 63) time points with and without SCS.

At day 63, muscle activation profiles with and without SCS were highly similar, with more than 90% cross-correlation and gait-cycle timing shifts below 6% for several muscles. Residual tensor fasciae latae and vastus lateralis activity increased over time without stimulation by 77.6% and 81.7%, respectively. With late SCS, tensor fasciae latae activity was 93.6% higher than at the early time point without stimulation; other muscles changed by less than 8%. Co-contraction between the residual vastus lateralis and biceps femoris decreased significantly from 1.57 early to 1.05 later without SCS and 0.95 with SCS.

Residual tensor fasciae latae changes corresponded with increased pelvic obliquity range-of-motion and pelvic drop. Range-of-motion was 8.08° early, 9.20° later without SCS, and 8.80° later with SCS; the late SCS condition differed significantly from the early condition. Residual-limb pelvic drop increased from 3.62° early to 4.76° later without SCS and 4.46° later with SCS, with both late values significantly above baseline.

Overall, repeated SCS-mediated sensory feedback was associated with altered residual-limb muscle activation, reduced knee-muscle co-contraction, and greater pelvic motion, corresponding to improved knee and hip stability during walking. Because the study included one participant and stimulation was delivered only in laboratory sessions, additional participants are needed.

Bear Grylls criticised schools for prioritising exam results and league tables over empowering children for adult life. North Texas has seen a slow start to severe weather season, with four tornadoes reported and most occurring in April and May. Oklahoma and Kansas have recorded no tornadoes in 2018, but activity can increase sharply in May.

This retrospective study developed SCIseg, an open-source deep-learning method for jointly segmenting the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in volumetric MRI. The three-site cohort included 191 patients and 231 scans from multiple scanner manufacturers, field strengths, orientations, resolutions, treatment settings, and traumatic or ischemic etiologies. A region-based nnU-Net model was trained in three phases using 196 scans, including active-learning corrections and additional multi-site data. SCIseg 3D outperformed its 2D variant across all lesion-segmentation metrics. Across both test sites, mean spinal-cord segmentation Dice score was 0.92 and relative volume error was −0.67%; lesion Dice scores were 0.48 at Site 1 and 0.76 at Site 2, with poorer Site 1 performance associated with metal artifacts and varying injury phases. Active learning significantly improved total lesion-volume estimation at both sites and lesion-length estimation at Site 1. The model also produced reasonable segmentations in unseen degenerative cervical myelopathy cases, including severely compressed spinal cords. Automatically derived lesion volume, length, and maximal axial damage ratio did not differ significantly from manually derived biomarkers. Discharge pinprick scores correlated with all biomarkers, while lower-extremity motor scores correlated with lesion volume and maximal axial damage ratio. Limitations include reliance on a single T2-weighted contrast, treatment of edema and hemorrhage as one lesion class, and constraints from data quality and sample size. Code, scripts, and results are freely available through the Spinal Cord Toolbox and GitHub.

Medvedev said Russia’s economy had entered a growth phase, with industrial output rising 1.3% at year-end and agriculture growing 5% the previous year. Agricultural machinery production, including harvesters and tractors, increased 60%, alongside growth in agribusiness.

Anyone can dine at more than 1,600 Exchange restaurants worldwide. Visitors, contractors, and DoD civilians may also buy grab-and-go food and beverages at 300-plus Express locations if consumed on the installation, while shopping privileges remain limited to Soldiers, Airmen, and their families.

The team says it has stayed calm, refocused after games, and consistently executed its plan to wear opponents down, but expects Dallas to be difficult to beat on Sunday. Players emphasize mental toughness, experience in big games, and handling adversity. The team believes it must start better after Dallas took control early in the previous game, with both sides expected to give full effort. Dallas’s goaltender was praised for limiting second-chance opportunities and rebounds. The team credits a collective road effort, using every player against tough lines, and plans to remain aggressive by forcing opponents into plays they avoid and taking away their skilled players early.

On July 25, 2019, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting its second-quarter 2019 financial results. The filing incorporated Exhibit 99.1, the results announcement press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. It was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky.

Athletes Unlimited (AU) was founded by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros to address the chronic underinvestment, limited media exposure, low compensation, and poor working conditions experienced in women’s professional team sports. After consulting athletes, sports executives, researchers, and former NPF commissioner Cheri Kempf, the founders launched AU in March 2020 as a public benefit corporation, initially with professional softball and later with volleyball, lacrosse, and basketball.

AU replaced traditional league structures with a player-led model. Its leagues have no owners or coaches, and five-member Player Executive Committees give athletes authority over competition formats, schedules, venues, uniforms, policies, player recruitment, and other operational matters. Players also help recruit team members and receive performance bonuses, equity-like interests, and participation in long-term profit distributions. AU’s “Mission Equity” structure caps investor returns and directs at least half of any surplus to players.

Competition is designed to emphasize both individual achievement and team success. Teams are rebuilt through weekly drafts, a point-based leaderboard ranks players, and top performers become captains who draft teams and select starters. Each season lasts five weeks, includes three games per week, and is played at a single venue. Team wins generate the greatest individual point rewards.

AU treats athletes as professionals by providing meals, laundry services, trainers, workout facilities, childcare, paid parental leave, and support for pregnancy and breastfeeding without requiring pregnancy disclosure. It also promotes social impact through the Power in My Voice initiative, the Athlete Causes Program, and youth clinics designed to expand participation and professional opportunities.

More than 200 athletes have played in AU’s four leagues. AU secured broadcast and streaming partnerships, raised $30 million in capital, and was named one of Fast Company’s 10 most innovative sports companies in 2023. During the COVID-19 pandemic, AU softball became the only professional softball league operating worldwide. A 2022 fan survey found strong engagement with broadcasts and streaming, broad approval of AU’s innovative format and storytelling, and greater excitement than in existing leagues.

AU’s continuing challenges include achieving economic sustainability, expanding without weakening its athlete-driven mission, deciding whether to emphasize broadcasting or in-person experiences, and determining which additional sports and partnerships fit its model.

This continuation patent application describes trigger-based allocation of wireless resource units in a multiple-BSSID WLAN. A transmitted BSSID (Tx BSSID) and non-transmitted BSSIDs (non-Tx BSSIDs) may be managed by one access point through virtual APs. The AP can prioritize random RUs among BSSs based on station count, traffic priority, security and access privileges, device types, QoS, latency requirements, and bandwidth capabilities.

Using a group-AID mapping in the partial virtual bitmap of a traffic indication map element, the AP allocates random-access resources and advertises them in a trigger frame. AID values can identify particular stations, groups, selected BSSIDs, or all stations. A non-Tx BSSID’s index can designate random RUs for its associated stations; AID 0 designates associated stations of the transmitting BSSID, and AID 2045 designates unassociated stations. When sent from the Tx BSSID, the trigger frame’s transmitter address uses its MAC address; when sent from a non-Tx BSSID, it uses the BSSID index.

The disclosure also covers Multiple BSSID, BSSID-index, non-Tx capability, FMS descriptor, and RAPS/UORA elements; AP and STA architectures; directed and wildcard trigger frames; dedicated and random RU scheduling; OFDMA RU layouts; and contention procedures. Targeted random-RU allocation is presented as improving shared-medium efficiency and fairness while avoiding disproportionate allocation among BSSs.

The speaker honors Amherst’s tradition of public service and urges its graduates to use their education, talent, and privilege for the public interest. Amid domestic inequality and domestic and global challenges, educated citizens must provide leadership, compassion, and service to strengthen democracy.

He presents Robert Frost as an artist and American whose realism, skepticism, and faith in the human spirit questioned power and revealed society’s weaknesses. Frost’s poetry strengthened national life by preserving individual vision, exposing human failings, and keeping power from becoming arrogant or corrupt. In a free society, artists must remain independent of ideology and propaganda and serve truth.

The speaker envisions an America that matches military and economic strength with moral restraint, wisdom, cultural achievement, environmental stewardship, and social harmony. Concluding that Frost’s work and Amherst’s legacy have expanded humanity’s “hold on the planet,” he expresses confidence in the college’s graduates’ continued commitment to democratic and national ideals.

The CAT offense uses a 2-1-2 spread and sharp passing to exploit traps, double teams, and zone presses. Its post should be a skilled triple threat. Baseline players back-cut when the ball goes middle, while the post rolls to the basket on corner passes and back-cuts if denied. Opposite-corner skip passes and limited dribble penetration help relieve pressure.

Tight ends remain increasingly important in football’s pass-heavy offenses because their size, strength, speed, and athleticism create difficult matchups for defenses. They typically run short-to-medium routes, receive over the middle and underneath, and provide value in the red zone. They also block defensive linemen and linebackers in both run and pass plays, giving offenses greater flexibility and production. The position demands strong hands, route-running ability, blocking skills, speed, and physicality; elite players are generally comparable in height to linemen but lighter and more athletic. The term “tight end” originated when receivers moved farther from the line of scrimmage, distinguishing players who remained tight to the formation. Prominent tight ends include Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe. Overall, tight ends combine a wide receiver’s pass-catching ability with an offensive lineman’s blocking value, making them versatile and dangerous offensive weapons.

Guangdong Province is experiencing China’s largest recorded chikungunya outbreak, with more than 4,000 confirmed infections since late July. Shunde District in Foshan accounts for over 3,600 cases, while infections have also appeared in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. The mosquito-borne disease causes fever and severe joint pain but does not spread directly between people. Authorities are encouraging residents to eliminate standing water and reduce mosquito breeding sites. Climate change, urbanization, and international travel are contributing to the wider spread of mosquito-borne viruses. WHO has issued new clinical guidelines and strengthened its Global Arbovirus Initiative, while researchers call for expanded genomic surveillance, community participation, and global cooperation. Chikungunya has spread to more than 110 countries since first being identified in Tanzania in the 1950s. There is no specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine; care focuses on symptom relief, and recovery usually takes about a week, although prolonged symptoms can occur.

During nationwide World No Tobacco Day activities, Coalition for Tobacco Control–Pakistan officials urged the government to prioritize health over tobacco business. Citing WHO data, they said tobacco kills more than seven million people globally each year, costs countries $1.4 trillion annually, and is associated with 108,800 deaths in Pakistan. They called for strict enforcement of tobacco-control laws, immediate implementation of 85% pictorial health warnings announced in 2015, and higher tobacco taxes. They said continued low taxation of third-tier cigarettes has doubled consumption, reduced revenue, and increased access for children. Pakistan’s 2004 ratification of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control remains insufficiently implemented.

The study implemented a Julia-based minorization-maximization algorithm for ML and REML estimation in multivariate variance-components linear mixed models, supporting multiple phenotypes and cis-/trans-SNP variance components. Applied to PsychENCODE gene and isoform expression, it found local variants have sparse but large effects, distal variants have small individual but large collective effects, and cis-SNPs show greater genetic sharing. Isoform-level analyses detected more signals than gene-level analyses, including associations with autism spectrum disorder, suggesting value for identifying disease genes and interpreting GWAS findings.

The paper introduces Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings (SoDaDE), a data-driven fingerprint designed to improve solvent representation for molecular modelling, particularly for niche chemistry where general representations may not generalise. SoDaDE is pre-trained using Spange’s dataset of 191 solvents and up to 12 molecular properties. The dataset is augmented by randomly shuffling property-value pairs, producing up to 12! sequences per solvent. A decoder-only transformer combines solvent-type tokens, ChemBERTa fingerprints, property labels, and numerical values, then predicts masked properties using causal and missing-value attention masks.

The model uses 64-dimensional embeddings, 16 attention heads, five layers, and a hidden dimension of 256. It achieved a normalised validation MSE of 0.107 during pre-training. On held-out solvent property prediction, SoDaDE obtained an average MSE of 0.170, outperforming Gaussian process, random forest, and training-set average baselines at 0.335, 0.550, and 4.23, respectively.

SoDaDE was evaluated on the Catechol Benchmark for predicting reaction outcomes with single solvents and solvent mixtures. For mixtures, solvent fingerprints were averaged. Without fine-tuning, SoDaDE achieved MSEs of 0.0029 for full data and 0.0044 for single solvents; fine-tuning improved the full-data result to 0.0026 while leaving the single-solvent result unchanged. These results surpassed all compared representations, including ACS PCA, DRFPs, RDKit fragprints, Spange descriptors with Gaussian-process imputation, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa. The authors conclude that SoDaDE provides an effective solvent fingerprint, performs particularly well for solvent mixtures, and can be created effectively from small datasets. Data and code are provided publicly.

Texas football’s recruiting weekend is set for Dec. 15–17, centered on the annual football banquet. Nearly all 19 committed recruits and most remaining targets plan to visit. Ten players remain serious candidates for the final six or seven scholarships: defensive tackle Tommie Harris, linebacker Derrick Johnson, defensive lineman Kaelen Jakes, tight end James Moses, defensive end Jonathan Jackson, offensive linemen Jamie Hightower and William Winston, safety Dewayne Brandon, athlete Quan Cosby, and defensive tackle Paul Broussard. Tai Dillard scored 17 points, while Tracy Cook added 12 and JoRuth Woods scored 11 with seven rebounds and five assists. Texas also won 72–47 against Wichita State. The newsletter criticized the Texas Athletic Department for scheduling early games and canceling television coverage of long road trips to Colorado and Kansas, arguing that television accommodations for fans should include reciprocal benefits.

Texas baseball coach Augie Garrido signed 12 high school prospects, including pitchers Luis Cortez, Joey Guajardo and Donald Levinski, shortstop Michael Hollimon, utility players Kole Strayhorn and Huston Street, catchers James Sweeney and Curtis Thigpen, and Seth Johnston, Ryan Olivo, J.D. Reininger and Chas Taylor.

Conradt signed four prominent women’s basketball recruits: Oklahoma All-American Kala Bowers, Texas standout Heather Schreiber, Canadian Junior National Team member Jody Bell and All-State guard Colencia “Coco” Reed.

Men’s basketball coach Rick Barnes signed point guard T.J. Ford and center Chris Wright, completing Texas’s available scholarships for the season. Ford led Willowridge to a Class 5A state title and was rated the nation’s top point guard recruit, while Wright was rated the No. 25 center prospect.

Volleyball coach Jim Moore signed middle blocker Bethany Howden and outside hitter LaTonya Coates. Softball coach Connie Clark signed six prospects led by nationally ranked pitcher Catherine “Cat” Osterman, along with Tiffany Anders, Wynter Turner, Melanie Jarrett, Alexis Garcia and Jill Vaughn.
