Residential customers prioritized levelized electricity cost, installation and distribution expenses, power per unit area, and sometimes appearance. Commercial customers emphasized levelized cost, power density, installation costs, and reliability. Utility buyers weighed power density where space was constrained, cost per kilowatt-hour otherwise, installation track records, and proven technology and reliability. Commercial and utility projects commonly used leases or power-purchase agreements under which developers financed, installed, operated, and maintained systems for 10 to 25 years.

First Solar originated as a glass company in 1984, became Solar Cells, Inc. in 1990, and was renamed First Solar in 1999. It went public in 2006, raising $450 million. Its proprietary vapor-deposition process placed thin cadmium sulfide and cadmium telluride layers on glass before lasers divided the coating into cells. First Solar controlled production internally, avoiding multiple supply-chain operators and batch-processing steps used for crystalline silicon. By 2011 it operated 36 production lines in Ohio, Germany, and Malaysia; Malaysian plants had the lowest costs, while other locations offered R&D or market advantages. Its Frankfurt plant added 250 megawatts of annual capacity, and plants were under construction in Arizona and Vietnam. Despite capacity to produce 2.5 gigawatts, First Solar produced 1.7 gigawatts in 2011.

Beginning in 2007, First Solar acquired system integrators, a project pipeline, a contractor, a developer, and a component supplier, extending its business from component manufacturing into complete systems. The acquisitions increased proximity to customers but also raised selling, general, and administrative expenses. Systems increased from 5% of sales in 2009 to 25% in 2011. Components remained more profitable and generated more cash, while systems had less margin variability because ongoing services were less dependent on material prices. Vertical integration reportedly doubled shipment rates and enabled systems with performance up to 5% better than competitors.

First Solar maintained substantially less debt than SunPower, Suntech, and Yingli and generally funded capacity expansions with half cash and half equity. Its strategy emphasized a strong balance sheet, lower customer borrowing costs, and the ability to finance projects. The company also sought to diversify from subsidy-dependent European markets, which had supplied 74% of 2008 sales through Germany alone, by selling directly to utilities in high-sunshine markets across Africa, the Middle East, and the Americas.

Competition intensified as Chinese crystalline-silicon manufacturers produced panels rapidly and inexpensively with government support, lower R&D spending, and exports exceeding 90% of production. Chinese subsidies for demand supported rapid installation growth, while subsidies and other advantages reduced manufacturing costs. A U.S.-China study estimated an 18%–20% Chinese cost advantage, with the WTO attributing one-fifth of that advantage to direct subsidies. Excess production contributed to inventory accumulation, anti-dumping litigation, and sustained price pressure. In the United States, First Solar held about 41% of the 2011 market, SunPower 38.5%, and smaller firms 20.5%.

Cheap Chinese panels and reduced European subsidies contributed to bankruptcies among Evergreen Solar, SpectraWatt, and CIGS manufacturer Solyndra. SunPower, Suntech, and Yingli also reported 2011 net losses of approximately $604 million, $1.018 billion, and $519 million, respectively. First Solar recorded a $393 million goodwill impairment and $60 million in restructuring charges in 2011, while maintaining its position as the lowest-cost producer among the companies compared in the case.

As a quarterly board meeting approached, Chief Operating Officer Tymen deJong needed to address whether First Solar remained profitable, whether its systems business was an advantage or distraction, how to respond to Chinese entrants and falling silicon prices, and which markets to emphasize if the company retrenched.

A lecture demonstrates sampling, aliasing, and properties of discrete-time linear systems using a programmable digital filter with adjustable coefficients, word lengths, and sampling rate. The system includes a continuous-to-discrete converter, digital filter, discrete-to-continuous converter, and smoothing low-pass filter.

With the digital filter set to an identity system, sampling creates periodic spectral replicas. Frequency normalization converts the spectral period to \(2\pi\) in digital frequency. The reconstruction filter selects one replica, recovering the input exactly when its bandwidth is sufficiently below the sampling frequency. Otherwise, overlapping replicas cause aliasing. For a sinusoidal input, the output follows the input frequency below half the sampling frequency; above that point, the output frequency decreases to \(\omega_s-\omega_0\). Scope and audio demonstrations confirm this reversal and show beating near half the sampling frequency due to the nonideal reconstruction filter’s transition band.

A symmetric low-pass digital filter with a linear-phase response is then inserted. Its digital cutoff is \(\pi/5\), one-tenth of \(2\pi\), and its frequency response is periodic every \(2\pi\). The equivalent continuous-time response has the same shape but a rescaled frequency axis, with digital frequency replaced by \(\omega T\). Consequently, the analog cutoff is \(\pi/(5T)\), or one-tenth of the sampling frequency.

Additional demonstrations show the overall system’s symmetric impulse response, the staircase-like digital-to-analog output, and its smoothing by the reconstruction filter. Frequency sweeps show attenuation in the stopband and periodic passband returns near multiples of \(2\pi\). Changing the sampling rate scales the cutoff accordingly: 40 kHz gives a 4 kHz cutoff, 20 kHz gives 2 kHz, 10 kHz gives 1 kHz, and 5 kHz gives 500 Hz. Lower sampling rates are also applied to live audio before restoring 40 kHz sampling for improved quality.

Tesla reported that CFO Deepak Ahuja plans to retire after serving since 2008, aside from a 14-month gap, and will advise the company during the transition. Tesla intends to appoint Vice President of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations Zachary Kirkhorn as his successor. Kirkhorn joined Tesla in 2010 and has led key cost, manufacturing, Gigafactory 1, Model X, and Model 3 initiatives.

Sun Waa Chinese takeaway in Littleover received a one-star food hygiene rating after inspectors found fried rice left at room temperature for six hours, blocked washing facilities, food debris, cross-contamination risks, poor surface cleaning, insect webbing and a broken thermometer. Council officers later reported significantly improved hygiene, and the manager expected a five-star rescoring in March. TripAdvisor averaged three and a half stars from six reviews, while Just Eat scored it five and a half out of six.

A Sarnia judge praised Tarren Joseph Titus’s efforts to recover from drug abuse and sentenced him to three months’ house arrest with a curfew, followed by one year of probation. He pleaded guilty to possessing hydromorphone and two probation-order violations and must continue counseling while staying away from drugs.

Week 6’s major college football results were UCLA’s 42-37 upset of Penn State and Florida’s 29-21 win over Texas, damaging the College Football Playoff prospects of the preseason top two teams. UCLA became the first team at 0-4 or worse to beat a top-10 opponent since UTEP upset defending champion BYU in 1985. After leading 27-7 at halftime, UCLA survived Penn State’s rally and sealed the victory with a fourth-and-2 stop. Nico Iamaleava passed for 166 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 150 yards and three scores. Penn State’s offense performed well, but its defense struggled; SP+ dropped the Nittany Lions from fourth to 16th and projects a 7-5 finish.

Florida quarterback Lagway completed 21 of 28 passes for 298 yards and two touchdowns against the nation’s top-ranked defense. Texas quarterback Arch Manning completed 16 of 29 passes, threw two interceptions and continued to struggle with pressure and offensive-line support. Texas fell to 20th in SP+ and is projected to finish 7-5.

Missed upset opportunities also shaped the week. Vanderbilt’s turnovers prevented it from overcoming Alabama, while Florida State’s three turnovers left it down 28-3 against Miami. Cincinnati ended Iowa State’s unbeaten run, and Texas Tech dominated Houston; both strengthened their positions in the Big 12 race. SP+ particularly praised Florida, UCLA, Northwestern, Notre Dame and Old Dominion, while Penn State experienced the largest drop.

Iamaleava was the clear weekly Heisman contender, with Ohio State’s Sayin also rising. Ty Simpson led the six-week points race, while Illinois quarterback Luke Altmyer posted three consecutive top-two finishes. Lower-level games featured last-second wins by Georgetown, West Liberty, Arkansas State and Baylor, along with several overtime finishes.

Players emphasize focusing on their jobs and avoiding distractions as they pursue another Stanley Cup, regardless of home or road advantage. Veteran leadership, prior playoff experience, and coaching that adjusts matchups and line combinations have helped the team remain composed and prepared. Players say the intensity of the playoffs creates lasting memories, while family members attending the games can be as nerve-wracking as the competition itself.

Tampa Bay is described as a dangerous opponent capable of making plays in difficult situations, with every game expected to be close and hard-fought. Health, recovery, disciplined preparation, line chemistry, and contributions from every player are considered important.

The team also recognizes how competitive the league is, noting that every contender believes it can win the Cup. Against Anaheim, players stress patience, puck management, sustained focus, and taking away the opponent’s growing confidence. One veteran praises his teammate’s offensive talent, defense, work ethic, and leadership as especially impressive.

New York University researchers Michelle Munson and Sarah Narendorf are studying how marginalized young adults understand their mental health conditions and treatment. Their research finds that individuals’ beliefs about the causes of their symptoms, feelings such as fear and shame, perceptions of professional help, and experiences with stigma influence treatment engagement and self-care.

Using in-depth interviews and qualitative analysis, the researchers found that young people’s narratives vary and shape how they respond to care. They argue that providers should combine clinical expertise with each young adult’s perspective through a collaborative, culturally humble approach. Mental health systems’ communication with young adults can also influence whether their transition to adulthood is harmful or hopeful.

The studies focus on young adults facing poverty, discrimination, disability, young parenthood, reliance on safety-net services, or involvement with multiple public systems. The researchers propose training providers to understand these narratives and developing technology-based interventions to support them. They call for replication, longitudinal research, and broader access to care, noting that many marginalized young adults do not receive needed treatment and do not feel heard or respected by providers.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, an Uzbek immigrant and U.S. citizen, received a private tour of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener connected him with his research-astronomer brother. Murad, who dreamed of becoming an astronaut after seeing space images at age three, explored the center’s clean room, spacecraft testing facilities, laser lab, and black-hole research. An accelerated high school student, he aims to attend Caltech and hopes eventually to join a Mars mission. His family’s naturalization has made his ambitions feel more attainable and given his mother a stronger sense of belonging. Murad also plans to watch the total solar eclipse from Kansas City.

Radio 4 presenter Anita Anand was told less than 24 hours before an Any Answers edition that she could not host a discussion of the BBC’s gender pay dispute because she had publicly supported equal pay. Julian Worricker presented instead, though the iPlayer listing still displayed Anand’s image. Critics called the decision insulting to women, while the BBC said impartiality decisions are made case by case. Anand was expected to return the following week.

The NRA said YETI had ended its business relationship with the NRA Foundation and would no longer sell products to it. YETI disputed the explanation, saying it was eliminating outdated discount programs and offering the foundation and other organizations a broadly available alternative customization program. Some NRA supporters responded with a boycott and a social media campaign destroying YETI products. YETI maintained its support for the Second Amendment.

This study benchmarked 15 summary-level Mendelian randomization (MR) methods using real-world GWAS data. The methods included fixed and random IVW, Egger, RAPS, weighted-median, weighted-mode, MR-PRESSO, MRMix, cML-MA, MR-Robust, MR-Lasso, MR-CUE, CAUSE, MR-APSS, and MR-ConMix, grouped into IVW-class, outlier-removal, model-based, and outlier-robust approaches. Evaluation covered type I error control under population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounding; causal-effect accuracy; and replicability and power.

Type I error was assessed using negative-control trait pairs, including 1,130 pairs for population stratification, 77 for pleiotropy, and 82 for family-level confounding. MR-APSS, Egger, and weighted-mode generally controlled inflation best, although CAUSE produced deflated p-values, did not adequately control strong population stratification, and had p-values inconsistent with its confidence intervals. Family-based GWAS data produced calibrated results for all methods, whereas population-based data exposed substantial family-confounding effects. For most methods, relaxing instrument-selection thresholds increased p-value inflation and bias, showing that results were highly sensitive to instrument selection.

Causal-effect accuracy was tested using six trait pairs in which the same trait served as exposure and outcome, giving a known effect of one. MR-APSS produced the most accurate estimates and consistently covered the true effect; weighted-mode was comparable at the strictest threshold, and Egger was unbiased at that threshold but overestimated effects with weaker instruments. Most other methods showed bias toward the null and poor confidence-interval coverage. MRMix was unstable across thresholds, while MR-Lasso sometimes classified all instruments as invalid and returned no estimate.

In the LDL-C–coronary artery disease case study, CAUSE and MR-APSS had the most consistent estimates across six exposure GWAS datasets and multiple instrument thresholds. Larger samples improved consistency and reduced weak-instrument and selection-bias effects. Results were generally insensitive to minor-allele-frequency thresholds and to LD reference panels matched to the study ancestry.

The authors recommend using negative controls, testing multiple instrument-selection criteria, and combining data from independent sources. Limitations include potentially coexisting confounders, limited true-positive cases, inability of the same-trait design to assess pleiotropy, and restriction to summary-level methods.

Four women describe their experiences in winemaking. Zita Kovács says early-career prejudice gave way to respect and creative control over labels and wine names. Zsófi Laposa credits technological development with opening the traditionally male-dominated profession to women, whose presence brings gentleness and uniqueness. Krisztina Csetvei balances winery ownership with caring for her daughter Panna and has created “Panna Rose.” Andi Gere manages the family winery jointly with her father and says women’s elegance complements men’s bold wines, enriching Hungary’s wine palette.

Broccoli, asparagus, citrus fruits, legumes, avocado, lady’s finger, nuts and seeds, cauliflower, beetroot, carrots, and corn are listed as folate-rich foods. The passage gives folate amounts for asparagus, oranges, avocado, lady’s finger, broccoli, cauliflower, beetroot, carrots, and cooked corn, including 33% of daily needs from one cup of boiled asparagus and 28% from one cup of avocado. It also notes vitamins K, C, and A and manganese in asparagus, fatty acids and dietary fiber in avocado, and antioxidants in beetroot.

The passage describes a continuation patent disclosure for structurally colored articles, including footwear, apparel, sporting equipment, containers, electronic equipment, and vision wear. Structural color is produced through optical effects such as scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, and diffraction involving micro- or nanoscale surface features, rather than solely through dyes or pigments.

Optical elements can be affixed to or incorporated into article components, including footwear uppers, soles, bladders, and foams. Each element contains at least one optical layer, such as a multilayer reflector or filter, and may include textured surfaces, primer layers, protective layers, or polymeric layers. Layer materials, refractive indices, thicknesses, numbers, and fabrication methods are selected to produce single, multicolor, or iridescent structural color, which may vary with viewing angle.

Textured surfaces may contain nanometer- to micrometer-scale projections and depressions, including structures forming diffraction gratings, photonic crystals, or selective mirrors. Primer layers may comprise paint, ink, degraded polymers, metals, or metal oxides and can contain crosslinked polymers, dyes, pigments, crosslinkers, and solvents.

Structural color is characterized using CIE 1976 L*a*b*, CIELCH, and Pantone color systems at specified observation angles. The disclosure also describes thermoplastic and thermoset polymers, particularly polyurethanes and thermoplastic polyurethanes, along with their material and testing parameters.

Several acquisition announcements indicated renewed merger activity among junior mining companies, especially gold producers, after a slow start to 2018. Hecla proposed a US$462 million acquisition of Klondex Mines, potentially increasing Hecla’s annual gold production to about 370,000 ounces. Alio Gold proposed a $128 million acquisition of Rye Patch Gold, while Anaconda Mining offered to combine with Maritime Resources. Analysts and executives said consolidation could help junior miners diversify, reduce risk and improve access to capital. Canadian metals and mining mergers totaled six by the time of the report, compared with 19 in 2017.

Detroit is considered the strongest opponent faced so far, combining scoring power and an elite goaltender. Officials are calling infractions closely, so penalties—especially against Detroit’s power play—must be avoided. The team also needs smarter puck decisions, rather than relying solely on intensity. Detroit has talented penalty killers and a potent line centered by Kris Draper, who is praised as underrated and highly effective.

Players are encouraged to ignore family concerns, ticket requests, and other distractions and focus on the upcoming home game in the finals. After a penalty-filled loss, the team must generate more offense, improve faceoff performance, and regain puck possession against Detroit’s strong faceoff specialists. Nicklas Lidström is regarded as the league’s best defenseman because of his positioning and puck movement. The home arena is expected to provide a loud atmosphere, though the speaker’s growing beard is also creating concern.

MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs based on Arm Cortex-M0+, operating up to 32 MHz. They support 1.62–3.6 V and −40–125°C, with 64 KB flash, 8 KB SRAM, analog and digital peripherals, and LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, SMBus, and PMBus communications.
Pusa, a Congress member and former Nagaland minister, died aged 63. He was first elected independently in 1993 and was buried in his native Viswema village.

India’s state-run banks posted a record combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees ($12.65 billion) in fiscal 2017/18 as bad-loan provisions surged after tighter RBI rules. Nineteen of 21 majority state-owned banks lost money in the March quarter, while gross nonperforming loans rose 15% to 8.96 trillion rupees. New Delhi plans 2.11 trillion rupees over two years to recapitalize the banks.

A Zillow analysis of central air conditioning in 35 major U.S. metro areas found that homes with it sold for 2.5% more, an average premium of $5,486. Sale premiums were highest in San Antonio at 5.8% and Cincinnati at 5.7%. Sixty-two percent of buyers considered air conditioning essential, compared with 48% who prioritized private outdoor space. Overall, 66.1% of homes sold had air conditioning, rising to 99.1% in Las Vegas and 97.9% in Phoenix.

Rentals with central air conditioning also carried a premium, averaging 2.8% or $40 per month. The largest rent premiums were in New York at 11.6% or $275, Las Vegas at 10.4% or $135, and Phoenix at 10.3% or $141. Zillow attributed renters’ higher valuation partly to their limited ability to install central air or HVAC systems.

The analysis covered homes sold or listed for rent from June 2017 through May 2018 and controlled for home size, age, bedrooms, bathrooms, and location.

IWM options trading involves buying and selling call and put contracts. Calls give buyers the right to buy shares at an agreed price; puts give them the right to sell shares at an agreed price. Options provide leverage, speculation without owning the underlying shares, and hedging against market declines. Specialized contracts, depending on the broker, may include butterfly spreads and straddles.

Available orders include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Investors can use directional strategies such as buying calls for expected price increases or puts for expected declines, sell covered calls, or buy protective puts. Contract selection should consider the expected price movement, expiration date, and strike price.

Traders should research the underlying asset, available contracts, and relevant strategies. A trading plan should define entry and exit points and incorporate technical indicators such as moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD, and stochastics, along with news and economic data. Strategies should be backtested before committing funds.

Options can lose their entire value, and short calls may carry unlimited risk. Risk controls include stop-loss orders, limiting the amount risked per trade, diversifying positions, and maintaining a margin of safety. Margin trading and short selling are allowed, but both carry substantial risk.

Requirements include being at least 18, having a valid address and sufficient funds, using a margin account, and understanding option terms, risks, and applicable regulations. Trades are not permitted when the stock closes below $2. Minimum account balances vary by broker but are generally around $2,000. Investors are advised not to allocate more than 10% of their portfolio to IWM options.

Broker fees typically include per-trade commissions. Taxes may apply to short- or long-term option profits and premiums. Current information is available through online news, research sites, financial publications, forums, and discussion boards. The passage advises beginners not to trade options until they understand the activity.

Gov. Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program to train administrators at schools without a resource officer to carry a firearm on campus and respond to active shooters. Participants must complete training, obtain approval from the superintendent, school board and county sheriff, and use secured weapon storage. The program adds security while the state seeks to expand its school resource officer corps.

The Bank of England warned that soaring AI-related valuations may be approaching unsustainable, dot-com-like levels, with optimism outpacing near-term profitability. It highlighted risks from gains concentrated in Nvidia, Microsoft and Meta, and bottlenecks in power, semiconductor capacity and data infrastructure. Although the UK financial system remains broadly stable, a sharp AI sell-off could trigger global market volatility and affect Britain through capital outflows and equity repricing. The IMF has expressed similar concerns about inflated AI-linked asset prices.

The passage describes systems and methods for blockchain transaction risk management, automated money-flow tracing, and related machine-learning techniques. A risk-management architecture receives on-blockchain and off-blockchain data—including blockchain addresses, transaction identifiers, timestamps, user and device information, IP addresses, business types, and exchange or custodian data—through a digital-asset intake engine. An entity knowledge base contextualizes the data using blockchain records and blacklist, device-intelligence, and computer-network intelligence databases.

A machine-learning risk-classification engine identifies behavioral categories for blockchain entities, including exchanges, mixers, bots, hackers, terrorists, and bad-actor clusters. It uses statistical, topology, temporal, linkage, derived, and sequential transaction features. A machine-learning regression engine then assigns risk scores based on entity classifications, transaction history, external information, and graph connectivity to known actors. Scores range from 0 to 100 and are categorized as Safe, Legitimate, Unknown, Suspicious, or Risky. A rules-based policy engine evaluates deviations, while a security-control system approves normal transactions or, for high risk, blocks transactions, freezes assets, suspends accounts, or issues alerts. Risk scores may decay over time through an exponential time-decay factor.

Automated tracing uses transaction data from a blockchain ledger, address labels from a blockchain ecosystem intelligence database, clustering labels, and trace parameters such as direction, time range, minimum transaction value, and maximum hops. An AI graph-search algorithm selects paths between source, intermediate, and destination addresses using methods such as breadth-first search, Dijkstra search, A*, D*, or IDA*. Outputs include result graphs, interactive journey boards, destination statistics, suspicious-address reports, expandable money-path visualizations, and proactive alerts. Address clustering groups similar addresses using transaction behavior, intelligence labels, and real-world entity information.

The passage also describes AutoML pipelines for preparing labeled data, extracting and transforming features, training models in parallel, evaluating metrics, selecting and serializing the best model, and deploying it through offline-training or online-prediction pipelines. Supporting discussions cover neural networks, decision trees, gradient boosting, linear and nonlinear regression, model selection, cross-validation, gradient descent, and regression metrics such as RMSE and adjusted R-squared. Applications include anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism-financing compliance, blockchain forensics, fraud detection, investigation, and tracing cryptocurrency transfers into fiat banking systems through exchange KYC mappings.

Plum School District will begin preliminary 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday, hoping to avoid a third consecutive tax increase. The district entered the year more than $4 million in debt; its $66 million June budget included a 0.866-mill property-tax increase and no program cuts. It also approved a 12-year, $5.6 million bond. Tuesday’s agenda includes recruiting Chinese tuition students, elementary construction, consolidation and redistricting, and beginning closure proceedings for Regency Park Elementary, which require state notice and public hearings.

More than 80% of 100 financial services professionals surveyed by Infosys Finacle expected commercial blockchain adoption by 2020; over half were investing or planning to invest, with average project investment of $1 million this year. Private blockchain was preferred by 69%.

Pump and dump schemes are described as scams that are generally illegal and immoral, benefiting only a small number of promoters and early participants while leaving latecomers exposed to significant losses. In such a scheme, a promoter accumulates shares—typically of thinly traded penny stocks—artificially raises the price through false or misleading information, then sells into the resulting frenzy, causing the price to collapse. The passage compares this to a Ponzi scheme and notes that fear of missing out (FOMO) can extend such schemes over days, weeks, or months.

Historically, schemes spread through word of mouth and "boiler rooms," as depicted in *The Wolf of Wall Street*; today they spread via social media. A cited example describes a promoter who made nearly a million dollars from penny stock promotions, reached an out-of-court settlement with the SEC in 1999, and paid back most of his gains.

The scheme is rare on major regulated exchanges, where large stocks are difficult to manipulate, but is common in the OTC market and the largely unregulated crypto market, where low-volume, small-exchange tokens are especially vulnerable; organizers are said to coordinate via messaging services such as Telegram.

A study of 421 schemes using German bank data from 2002–2015 found 6,569 investors made over 20,000 purchases, average returns of –28%, and average losses of at least €1.2 million per scheme. The passage advises avoiding such schemes, not letting FOMO or easy-money temptation drive decisions, and trading systematically with backtesting while thinking long-term.

The disclosure addresses paging in new-generation high-frequency wireless systems, where beamforming limits each transmit port’s coverage and paging information is repeated across beams. Under LTE paging procedures, an idle UE cannot predict beam or port scheduling across subframes or timeslots, making energy-saving discontinuous reception difficult or impossible.

The disclosed methods define a paging occasion (PO) as a group of paging resources for one or more preset beams or ports, potentially corresponding to a synchronous signal burst set or sweeping resources. A first communication node calculates the PO’s time-domain position and transmits paging downlink control information, a paging message, or both within that PO; a second communication node calculates the same position and receives the information. PO determination may use a DRX cycle, paging transmission interval, number of transmissions per DRX cycle, device identifier, and PO offset, with the starting radio frame and, when needed, starting subframe calculated accordingly. Paging information may be transmitted on all beams or ports within a paging interval.

The disclosure also describes signaling or preconfiguration of quasi-co-location relationships between paging-related reference signals and sweeping signals or channels, allowing a UE to determine the resource, port, and receive beam used for paging. Corresponding transmitter and receiver apparatuses, systems, storage media, base-station and terminal hardware, and computer program products are also provided.

Orbital ATK reported fiscal Q2 2017 sales of $1.12 billion, slightly exceeding estimates and rising 3% year over year. Adjusted earnings beat expectations by $0.13 per share, but GAAP earnings fell 3%, operating margins declined, and free cash flow turned negative at $55.8 million. Management remained optimistic, citing $1.4 billion in new orders, $220 million in option exercises, a 10% increase in firm backlog, and expected acceleration in revenue, earnings, and free cash flow during the second half. The company raised full-year sales and earnings guidance while retaining its free-cash-flow forecast.

Argus Research upgraded Orbital ATK from hold to buy with a $120 price target, citing raised guidance, expected defense spending, and potential free-cash-flow growth. However, the article’s author argued that the stock, after gaining 44% over 12 months, was too expensive at 22 times trailing earnings and more than 40 times enterprise value to trailing free-cash flow, particularly given projected annual profit growth of no more than 10%.
The Eighth Circuit dismissed Pink C. Jenkins’s appeal against the United States upon the appellee’s motion and the appellant’s consent.

**Summary**

This MIT Sloan teaching case (revised November 2010) by Cate Reavis examines the turnaround of Boston's Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) under director Jill Medvedow.

The ICA, founded in 1948 from the Harvard Society of Contemporary Art (1936 Boston Museum of Modern Art), was Boston's only contemporary art museum for over 50 years, but operated in a city weak in arts funding, collector activity, and critical mass. When Medvedow took over in March 1998, the museum had no money, few members, no permanent collection, a converted police station on Boylston Street, 25,000 annual visitors, and a budget under $1 million — what Medvedow called "striving to be marginal."

Medvedow, an art historian and founder of the public art organization Vita Brevis, brought that organization into the ICA, assembled a business planning group, and set out to broaden the museum's audience and outreach. Seeking a waterfront location, she competed successfully for the Pritzker family's Fan Pier Parcel J, winning it in November 1999 over proposals from the Wang Center/Boston Ballet/Opera collaboration and a performing arts and film center. She hired Paul Bessire as director of external relations, launched a capital campaign that grew from $50 million to $62 million, and added 13 new board members, mostly from finance, by early 2001.

Rather than a paid architecture competition, the ICA shortlisted 30 firms to four (Studio Granda, Office d'A, Peter Zumthor, and Diller + Scofidio) and held a public presentation at the Copley Theater, choosing Diller + Scofidio in April 2001. Challenges included dozens of state and city approvals, the Pritzker family's 2003 decision to sell the surrounding land, and the collapse of contractor Macomber, which delayed the opening by months.

The new $51 million building opened December 10, 2006, to more than 8,000 visitors. The museum raised over $75 million and welcomed over 280,000 visitors in its first year and more than 450,000 combined in 2008–2009. Meanwhile, a February 2009 arrest of street artist Shepard Fairey outside the ICA's "Supply and Demand" exhibition proved good publicity: 130,000 people attended the show through its August close.

This study proposes "whole human pedagogy," a novel framework for decolonial, holistic education abroad praxis built on four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. It draws on three literatures—education abroad and experiential learning (Kolb's experiential learning cycle of experience, reflection, conceptualization, and experimentation), decolonial theory rejecting Euro-U.S. epistemological dominance (Stein, 2021; Sicka & Hou, 2023), and alternative pedagogies such as contemplative and critical approaches—and addresses the scarcity of literature on alternative pedagogies abroad. The framework derives from conceptual mapping of Thompson's (2017) "tenderness pedagogy" and hooks' (1994) "engaged pedagogy."

Methodologically, this qualitative study used purposive and snowball sampling to recruit 17 education abroad practitioners at U.S.-based organizations serving undergraduates. Semi-structured virtual interviews of 60–90 minutes were conducted in Fall 2023 after IRB approval, transcribed, and analyzed in NVivo using primarily inductive coding; results are not generalized to the broader population.

Findings: Participants viewed approaching students as whole human beings as central to their work and expressed enthusiasm for further research. Embodiment involved physical immersion, place-based sensory learning, mindfulness, activity type and duration, interpersonal mannerisms, and intersectional identity. Emotions centered on culture shock, expectation-setting, normalization of feelings, and structured individual and group reflection. Belonging featured communal rather than hierarchical facilitator roles (friend, mentor, "tía"), knowing students individually, reciprocity, co-created knowledge, vulnerability, and trust. Becoming emphasized transformation, self-knowing, and self-sufficiency.

Discussion: The framework serves as a general posture centering collaboration, presence, mutuality, creativity, and wellbeing, destabilizing values like competition, perfection, separation, and monoculturalism. Significance: theoretically, it responds to calls for intentional intercultural learning interventions and resists dehumanization (Freire); practically, it can guide program development, assessment, and professional development, and provide a basis for future research.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for transporting girlfriends and male sex workers across state lines for drug-fueled sexual encounters. With one year already served, he is expected to be released in about three years. Combs was convicted under the Mann Act but acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges that could have resulted in life imprisonment.

The nearly two-month Manhattan trial included testimony that Combs beat, threatened, sexually assaulted and blackmailed people. He apologized for the harm he caused, requested leniency, and said he hoped to become a better father, son and community leader. His daughters and five other children asked the judge to allow their family to heal together. Judge Arun Subramanian said the offenses continued for so long because Combs had the power and resources to sustain them and had not been caught.

The passage surveys several container and distributed-system patterns. Sidecars augment an application container without changing its source: nginx can terminate HTTPS and proxy to a legacy service on localhost, a configuration sidecar can synchronize API-driven settings through a shared filesystem, and a topz sidecar can expose process metrics through a shared PID namespace. A Git-synchronization sidecar paired with an auto-reloading Node.js server can implement a simple PaaS. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, stable and backward-compatible APIs, and documentation through Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

Ambassadors broker communication between an application and the outside world. They can route requests to sharded Redis or Memcached services, discover appropriate backing services across environments, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. Client-side ambassadors simplify the sharded service but add a container to each application pod; shared routing services offer the opposite deployment and scaling trade-offs.

Adapters modify heterogeneous application interfaces to conform to common standards. Examples include exposing Redis metrics through a Prometheus exporter, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and providing rich HTTP health checks for an unchanged MySQL container. Separating these functions into adapters enables reuse, independent updates, and resource isolation from application containers.

The passage then introduces multi-node patterns and microservices, noting that formal APIs and independent services improve team autonomy and scaling but make debugging and architecture more difficult. Replicated, load-balanced stateless services provide redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Their design includes readiness probes, session tracking, and optional caching, rate limiting, and SSL-termination layers. Sharded services divide state among shards when data cannot fit on one machine. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, and shard keys must include all request attributes that affect the response. Consistent hashing minimizes data redistribution during resizing, while replicated shards improve failure tolerance and allow overloaded shards to scale independently. Finally, scatter/gather distributes request computation across parallel leaves and combines their partial results to reduce response time.

The ultimate oscillator (UO) is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 that measures price momentum across the 7-, 14-, and 28-period timeframes. It calculates buying pressure and true range, averages them for each timeframe, then combines the results in a 4:2:1 weighting and scales the value from 0 to 100. The shorter timeframe receives the greatest weight. Readings below 30 are considered oversold, while readings above 70 are considered overbought.

Buy signals require bullish divergence from oversold territory followed by the oscillator rising above the divergence high; sell signals require the opposite bearish divergence. Backtests indicate that UO can support a stable mean-reversion strategy, although default 7/14/28 crossover settings produced poor results. An optimized example recorded 355 trades, a 78% win rate, an average gain of 0.77% per trade, a 25% maximum drawdown, and a profit factor of 2.5, with only two down years.

The double bottom is a bullish reversal formation featuring two swing lows near the same level with a swing high between them. It typically appears after a downtrend or during a prolonged pullback in an uptrend. The lows establish support, while the intervening high creates resistance called the neckline; the pattern is complete when price breaks above the neckline.

Aggressive traders may enter while the second low forms, seeking reversal signals such as bullish candlesticks or RSI leaving oversold territory. Conservative traders wait for price to close above the neckline with increased volume. Targets are generally set by projecting the pattern’s height upward from the neckline. Stops may be placed near the pattern’s midpoint for a 2:1 reward-to-risk ratio or below it for greater safety but a poorer ratio.

The passage notes that coding and backtesting the strategy is difficult because it requires numerous precise rules and settings. Bulkowski’s research on 500 stocks over five years found that 68% of double bottom formations reached their targets, but the authors caution that the manually identified patterns, short bull-market study period, and possible survivorship bias limit the findings.

UDMA write CRC corruption can occur when a preceding UDMA read with host termination leaves the `host_pio_term` state corrupted. If an IDE device terminates a later UDMA write, the ATAC may continue the prior CRC instead of generating a new one, causing CRC errors. A host-initiated I/O may reset the CRC, but this cannot be relied upon. The recommended resolution is to enable UDMA I/O blocking using bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed dismissal of Sea Breeze Salt and Innofood’s antitrust action against Exportadora de Sal (ESSA) and Mitsubishi entities. Plaintiffs alleged that ESSA, 51% owned by the Mexican government, conspired with Mitsubishi to terminate outside distribution contracts and sell Mexico’s salt exclusively through Mitsubishi.

The court held that ESSA’s decisions concerned the exploitation and distribution of Mexico’s sovereign natural resources and constituted official acts of a foreign sovereign performed in Mexico. Granting plaintiffs any of their five claims—under federal antitrust law, California antitrust law, and California contract-interference laws—would require invalidating Mexico’s policy of distributing its salt output exclusively through Mitsubishi. The Sabbatino factors further favored applying the act of state doctrine because there was no international consensus against exclusive resource arrangements, the case implicated foreign relations, and Mexico remained a sovereign state.

The court did not need to decide whether the act of state doctrine has a commercial exception; any such exception would not apply because ESSA exercised sovereign powers over a state-owned natural resource. The FSIA did not bar jurisdiction because its commercial-activity exception applied, and private parties may invoke the act of state doctrine. Sea Breeze’s temporary corporate suspension did not require dismissal because its powers had been restored during the appeal. The court emphasized that its holding was limited to this challenge to Mexico’s control of its salt resources.

Interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry was developed as a nondestructive, wide-area method for characterizing CVD-grown hBN. Dual-polarization SHG imaging maps crystallographic orientation, while interferometric detection distinguishes antiparallel domains that produce out-of-phase SH fields and destructive interference.

Across ten CVD growth conditions, SHG intensity varied by up to three orders of magnitude, substantially more than Raman intensity. Compared with mechanically exfoliated bulk references, CVD samples had Raman intensities of 25–100%, Raman linewidths two to three times broader, and much wider orientational distributions. Orientation disorder alone caused only modest SHG reductions, whereas a mixed-domain simulation showed that nearly equal populations of oppositely oriented domains can suppress SHG by two to three orders of magnitude.

Interferometric measurements confirmed that antiparallel domains and boundaries are widespread, including in films that appear unidirectionally aligned on high-symmetry substrates. Boundary signals contained smaller antiparallel subdomains, and phase shifts of π were detected even when domains were smaller than the approximately 1 μm² probing area.

The resulting framework correlates SHG intensity and orientational spread with Raman intensity and linewidth as quantitative indicators of hBN crystallinity. SHG intensity is especially sensitive to destructive interference from antiparallel domain populations, while orientational spread captures lattice disorder. The methodology is also applicable to transition metal dichalcogenides and other non-centrosymmetric two-dimensional crystals for large-area structural imaging, quality assessment, growth optimization, and domain engineering.

In a prospective multicenter cohort of 22 adults with cirrhosis undergoing TIPS, investigators analyzed peripheral-vein and hepatic-vein plasma before and after shunt placement and before discharge, with hepatic encephalopathy (HE) severity monitored for up to one year. Untargeted LC-MS/MS, feature-based molecular networking, and chemical proportionality analysis identified substantial post-TIPS changes in circulating metabolites, particularly bile acids. The largest metabolomic shifts occurred between the immediate post-TIPS and pre-discharge samples rather than immediately after the procedure. Bile-acid abundance fell acutely and returned near baseline by discharge overall, but participants who developed more severe HE had larger post-TIPS decreases and lower levels of three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids. These levels were also lower during HE-related readmission in two participants and increased after HE treatment.

Greater pre-to-post-TIPS dissimilarity in hepatic-vein metabolomes was associated with subsequent HE. The authors interpreted this as evidence that participants with less pre-existing intrahepatic shunting, and therefore less prior exposure to portal toxins, may be more susceptible to HE after TIPS. Chemical networking also implicated post-TIPS changes in glycerophosphocholine and bilirubin clusters, including altered biliverdin reduction and oxidation associated with severe HE.

The small cohort, incomplete metabolite coverage, reliance on library-based and often subclass-level annotations, and absence of paired microbiome analyses limit interpretation and validation. Larger studies, noninvasive measurement of intrahepatic shunting, and direct testing of bile acids and related metabolic pathways are needed before these metabolites can be established as biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update documents silicon limitations, operational consequences, and recommended workarounds.

- **Legacy DMA and UART/LPC access:** Unlike early x86 systems, the Geode GX/CS5535 does not hold the CPU during 8237 block or demand DMA. CS5535 UART writes are discarded and reads return all ones; LPC I/O may also fail or return invalid data. Software should avoid these accesses during block/demand DMA, wait for the terminal-count IRQ, or use single-transfer mode.
- **ATA/UDMA:** PRD tables should be DWORD-aligned. ATAC PRDs should be defined before a transfer begins, while ACC PRD changes should be at least two tables ahead of the active entry to avoid incorrect prefetch. UDMA writes can incur CRC errors after device termination when preceded by a UDMA read with host termination; UDMA I/O blocking is recommended to prevent host terminations. IDE commands must be sent in PIO mode before enabling bus mastering. The SSMI feature does not properly block IDE I/O during DMA and should not be used.
- **Interrupts and clock gating:** An edge-configured PIC input that remains high can prevent the PIC from becoming idle after automatic clock gating, causing missed interrupts and possible hangs. GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs can also be lost when domain-zero clock gating is enabled. UART clock gating is incompatible with CEIR mode, and USB controller clock gating causes some idle-state register reads to fail; these clock-gating features should be disabled where specified. The CS5535 also does not support standard 8259 polling mode.
- **PCI, USB, and ACPI:** The CS5535 must not claim or use PCI I/O addresses or ATAC/DD LBAR values at or above 10000h. It does not meet the USB 1.1 over-voltage protection specification, requiring external protection circuitry. ACPI PM1_EN and PM1_STS support only WORD and DWORD accesses; byte accesses may hang. WORD or BYTE PMC writes may corrupt register data, so an SMI I/O trap is recommended.
- **Power management:** GPIO wake inputs do not work from ACPI S3; PWRBTN# should be used, with external circuitry if multiple events must be combined. Premature sleep-delay counter resets can leave SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y asserted and PCI/IDE signaling disabled; related delay counters must be programmed below the PM_SED delay. The low-battery flag may not be recorded after abnormal standby.
- **Other components:** RTC extended-to-legacy RAM access ordering can return incorrect data. SMB NEGACK handling requires two specified writes when clearing the status bit. GLPCI retry limits count unrelated PCI retries and may need adjustment or disabling. GPIO High Bank atomic writes after suspend require read-modify-write transactions. LPC-to-ISA bridges can trigger random aborts, for which a programmable logic device workaround is described. KEL limitations affect port 060h/064h differentiation, snoop-mode state, and AuxOutputFull behavior. Several timing or diagnostic issues have no operational impact; one PCI timing issue may be addressed with 10–50 pF capacitors if necessary.

The passage describes adapter containers as a way to integrate third-party applications with common interfaces without modifying vendor-maintained images. Examples include adding a Prometheus exporter to Redis, using Fluentd adapters to normalize logs and capture Redis slow queries, and providing an HTTP health-check adapter for MySQL. These adapters preserve modularity, simplify updates, and allow reusable components to be shared across applications.

Microservices architectures divide applications into independently developed, API-based components. This supports team autonomy, independent releases, reliability, and service-specific scaling, but makes debugging, system design, and operational troubleshooting more difficult.

Replicated stateless services use identical instances behind a load balancer, with readiness probes indicating when instances can receive traffic. Multiple replicas provide redundancy and allow deployments without downtime. Session-tracked variants route a user’s requests consistently using IP affinity, cookies, or consistent hashing. A replicated caching tier can improve performance, support rate limiting, and reduce load on application servers. An nginx tier can provide SSL termination before traffic reaches the cache and application layers.

Sharded services divide data among shards, with a root routing requests to the appropriate subset. Sharding allows state too large for one machine to be distributed and improves memory utilization in caches. Replicated shards add failure tolerance and allow individual hot shards to scale. Requests can be routed through per-application ambassadors or shared routing services. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, commonly using a hash modulo the shard count; choosing an appropriate key is essential. Consistent hashing minimizes data redistribution when the number of shards changes.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes each request to multiple leaf nodes in parallel and combines their partial results at a root. It can accelerate independent computations and support both term-sharded and data-sharded document searches. However, coordination overhead and slow “straggler” nodes can negate parallelization benefits and reduce availability, so each shard may itself be replicated.

Function-as-a-service (FaaS) provides automatically managed, scaled, stateless functions for event-driven processing. It simplifies deployment but introduces operational complexity, requires external state storage, is poorly suited to long-running background work or large in-memory datasets, and may become expensive under sustained request volume. Example FaaS patterns include request/response decorators, asynchronous two-factor authentication, and event pipelines for workflows such as new-user signup.

The Illinois Appellate Court affirmed judgment for Boncar Construction Co. following a jury verdict and the pretrial dismissal of plaintiff James D. Rone’s claim under the Illinois Structural Work Act.

Rone, a line foreman employed by Dan Raymond Construction Co., was injured when a cable on a Boncar-operated backhoe severed his fingers as he climbed down from the backhoe’s gantry after holding telephone wires above it. Boncar and Raymond were joint venturers on the sewer project.

The court held that the Illinois Structural Work Act could not apply to an accident in Indiana. Although dismissal of that count was appealable because it involved a distinct statutory claim, Rone waived review by failing to perfect his appeal after the appellate court dismissed it without prejudice.

The court further held that conflicting inferences from the undisputed facts made negligence and contributory negligence questions for the jury. The jury had to determine whether Boncar lacked a statutory communication system, whether that lack proximately caused Rone’s injuries, and whether Rone’s conduct contributed to the accident. Evidence of safer alternatives and his ability to use the gantry rail rather than a movable cable supported submission of contributory negligence to the jury.

Rone’s argument under the Indiana Employers Liability Act failed because the Act applies to employee actions against employers and because any statutory violation remained a jury question. The court also found no error in refusing his proposed instructions because their points were adequately covered by other instructions.

In the AEGEAN study of subjects initiating apixaban for atrial fibrillation, the time from informed consent (or EMD monitoring start) to apixaban initiation averaged 1.8 days in the Primary SOC group and 1.6 days in the Additional Educational Program (AEP) group. Drug exposure and interruption were comparable across groups; roughly 86-88% received 5 mg BID, with dose modification in 2.3-4.1%. Compliance exceeded 95% at Weeks 4, 12 and 24 and was similar across groups, exceeding 94% at Week 48.

Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% (Primary SOC) versus 91.88% (AEP), with no significant difference; adherence was comparable at Weeks 4 and 12 but was significantly lower from Week 12 to Week 24 than from first dose to Week 12 (p<0.0001 in both groups). From Week 24 to 48, adherence was 87.59%, 87.51% and 88.41% in the Primary SOC, Secondary SOC and Continued AEP groups with no significant differences; first-dose-to-Week-48 adherence was 89.52% versus 90.93%, also non-significant. Persistence was 91.7% versus 91.3% at 24 weeks and 85.2%, 87.8% and 86.1% at 48 weeks, with no significant differences. Fully adherent subjects were 28.1% versus 26.5% at 24 weeks and 14.8%, 14.9% and 14.5% at 48 weeks.

Logit models identified non-adherence predictors including alcohol consumption, technical occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation and lower MMSE scores.

Safety was similar across groups: before Week 24, AEs occurred in 51.2% (Primary SOC) and 52.0% (AEP), with bleeding in 6.5% and 9.0% and one fatal bleeding (AEP). Between Weeks 24 and 48, AEs occurred in 33.8%, 40.8% and 38.6%, with bleeding in 4.1%, 4.0% and 3.2% and two fatal bleeds. Twenty-four deaths were reported; no pregnancies and no concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals occurred. Adherence and persistence were high through 48 weeks, with no additional benefit from the proactive educational program.

Opening range breakouts (ORBs) occur when price breaks beyond the high or low of a defined opening interval, often the first few minutes of trading. Backtests presented in the article show that simple ORB strategies in S&P 500 futures generally perform poorly without filters: upside breakouts averaged at most 0.04% per trade, while downside breakouts performed worse. Tests on Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil produced similarly negative results.

Daily or weekly filters based on trends, volume, reversal patterns, or overbought/oversold conditions may improve results. One strategy using one-minute breakouts plus a daily filter recorded 198 trades, an average gain of 0.27%, a 65% win rate, and a 2.0 profit factor.

The article attributes ORBs’ diminished effectiveness to frequent false breakouts, gains shifting to the night session, competition from automated strategy scanning, and daily highs and lows tending to occur during the first and last hours. Traders can use strategy optimization to develop ORB parameters, but should avoid overfitting and curve fitting. Overall, the article recommends adding daily filters and exercising caution, particularly with heavily traded futures and ETFs.

This aggressive trapping matchup zone runs from a 1-1-3 alignment: one defender pressures the ballhandler while the other four defend zones, requiring quick guards and creating steals and transition opportunities. Defenders rotate among the point, wings, high and low post, and help positions based on passes, dribbles, and reversals. The system includes wing and corner traps, an X-cut post/wing exchange, skip-pass and guard/wing-interchange coverage, and double-team options. It also counters two-guard fronts with a triple team in the high post and denies passing lanes and lob attempts.

An emulated-trial study using Veterans Health Administration electronic health records compared 198,938 Veterans with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection with 992,036 matched uninfected comparators. During one-year follow-up, infected Veterans had higher risk of suicide attempts (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41, 95% CI 1.30–1.54) and other self-directed violence (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.26–1.51). Associations were strongest during the first 30 days, with HRs of 2.54 for suicide attempts and 1.94 for self-directed violence, and remained elevated from days 31–365. Overall, 0.258% of the cohort had at least one suicide attempt and 0.242% experienced self-directed violence.

Associations varied by age, with consistently elevated risks among ages 18–45, 46–59, and 65–74. Relative hazards were highest among Veterans without prior suicide attempts or self-directed violence, although analyses of those with prior events were underpowered and did not show significant differences. Unvalidated suicide deaths did not differ significantly between groups.

Limitations included possible ascertainment bias from differences in healthcare use, undetected infections among comparators, and unobserved confounding. The findings support early and continued monitoring and suicide-prevention efforts following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Overbought describes a market or asset whose price has risen significantly over a defined period, potentially signaling a short-term reversal or weaker returns; it is generally viewed as bearish, while oversold is the opposite condition. This reflects mean-reversion, or regression to the mean: strong deviations from a trend often reverse over time. An RSI-based backtest defines overbought as a two-day RSI above 95 and finds that returns during the first five days are significantly below the long-term average of about 0.05% per day, with returns later converging toward that average. These statistical findings are not presented as a readily tradable short-selling strategy. Media coverage can intensify sentiment by creating FOMO through positive reporting or panic through negative reporting.

The passage applies container design patterns to logging, health monitoring, and distributed systems. Fluentd acts as an adapter that normalizes logs from applications with different formats, using plugins to monitor Redis slow queries and Apache Storm data. Adapter containers can also perform rich MySQL health checks without modifying the database image, supporting modularity, reuse, and shared expertise.

Microservices divide an application into independently developed components that communicate through defined APIs. This approach gives small teams greater autonomy, decouples release schedules, and enables component-specific scaling, but it also makes system design and debugging more difficult because failures span multiple processes and machines. Established distributed patterns can reduce these challenges.

Stateless services are commonly replicated behind a load balancer, with readiness probes indicating when instances can accept requests. Multiple replicas provide redundancy and support horizontal scaling. Session-tracked variants route a user’s requests to the same replica using IP affinity or application-level methods such as cookies; consistent hashing limits remapping during scaling. A caching tier can further improve performance. Varnish may be deployed as a separate replicated layer, with fewer, larger cache instances used to maximize stored data. Caching can require cookie- or header-based session tracking rather than IP affinity. The caching layer can also provide rate limiting, returning HTTP 429 responses and reporting remaining requests. An nginx tier performs SSL termination with certificates separate from those used by internal services. The complete Kubernetes example uses replicated application, Varnish, and nginx deployments connected by load-balancing services.

Sharded services differ from replicated services because each shard handles only a subset of requests, with a root routing traffic. Sharding is generally used for stateful systems whose data cannot fit on one machine. In a sharded cache, assigning unique data to shards improves memory utilization, but a failed shard increases cache misses and latency for requests mapped to it. Cache capacity and failure tolerance therefore depend on hit rate and require testing with and without caching. Replicating each shard improves resilience, supports rolling upgrades, and permits individual hot shards to scale. Sharding functions commonly use a deterministic, uniform hash followed by modulo; selecting an appropriate key is crucial, so factors such as request path and country may be used while irrelevant fields are excluded. Consistent hashing reduces the number of keys remapped when the shard count changes. Kubernetes examples cover a sharded memcache deployment using either a per-pod ambassador or a shared routing service, which trades deployment simplicity for extra network latency and a shared scaling requirement.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes each request simultaneously to multiple leaves, which perform portions of the computation before a root combines their results. It reduces request latency by parallelizing independent work and can dynamically avoid slow nodes. Document-search examples use either term-specific leaf searches or data-sharded leaves whose result sets are combined. Adding leaves eventually creates coordination overhead and a straggler problem because the root waits for every leaf, making tail latency and availability especially important. Replicating each leaf shard provides load balancing, failure tolerance, and safer rolling upgrades.

Functions as a service (FaaS) simplifies deployment by automatically scaling and restarting stateless functions in response to events. It is well suited to request or response decorators, isolated event handlers, two-factor authentication workflows, and event pipelines composed of functions or webhooks. However, forced decoupling complicates debugging and requires strong monitoring and alerting. FaaS runtimes are generally time-bounded, making them poor fits for long-running background processing, and startup latency can make them unsuitable when large datasets must be loaded into memory. Per-request pricing is also less attractive for continuously busy services.

The passage concludes by introducing distributed ownership and master election as a way to assign work among replicated processes. A singleton service offers simplicity and receives automatic restart or rescheduling guarantees from container orchestrators, but it cannot run old and new versions simultaneously during upgrades and therefore incurs deployment downtime.

This continuation patent disclosure describes systems, methods, and devices for wirelessly transmitting glucose data between an analyte sensor system, display devices, and partner devices such as insulin pumps. It addresses interoperability, communication synchronization, and changing device requirements involving battery capacity, accuracy, protocols, regulation, and operating time.

A diabetes management partner interface allows authorized partner devices to modify stored configuration parameters, including wireless connectivity, access control, and analyte data settings. Configurable features include whitelisting and timeout rules, advertisement structures and device-specific advertisement slots, display-device access limits, calibration periods, factory calibration codes, remote-server services, bolus calculation parameters, and bolus recommendations.

Additional embodiments select operating modes for partner devices, medicament-delivery devices, displays, or other remote devices; restrict advertisements and connection requests by device class; transmit mode indicators; and switch modes after a partner device times out. Partner devices may connect sequentially, with authorization and system requirements retrieved from a server, while prior sensor settings can be restored when a partner-specific mode ends. The disclosure also covers selecting intermittent or continuous connection models based on device and power requirements.

Further methods exchange pairing, dosage, analyte, configuration, and device-status information between sensor, partner, and display applications; configure and route alerts with primary and secondary notification devices; and monitor medicament-delivery operability using reservoir, rewind, priming, cannula-fill, pressure, and analyte data.

- The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Controller input voltage is 4 V to 14 V.

- Three synchronization arrangements are supported. In internal oscillator mode, a required RT resistor sets the switching frequency, and SYNC outputs an in-phase clock at twice that frequency. In external synchronization mode, RT must float and an external 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock with a 40% to 60% duty cycle is applied to SYNC; the controller internally inverts the clock. Primary-secondary mode connects the primary controller’s SYNC output to the secondary controller’s SYNC input, with RT populated on the primary and floating on the secondary. This supports synchronized independent converters or interleaved parallel operation. The secondary inverts the clock, producing a 90° or 270° phase shift.

- Devices provide either OUTA alone or OUTA/OUTB primary outputs, plus optional SRA/SRB synchronous-rectifier outputs. Each output has roughly 150 mA peak-current capability, requiring external gate-drive solutions. OUTB and SRB are available only in the 50% duty-cycle configuration on specified devices; SRB exists only on the TPS7H5001-SP. Synchronous-rectifier outputs remain off during soft start and begin switching after the SS voltage exceeds 1 V.

- Dead time and leading-edge blank time are programmable on applicable devices. Independent dead times are programmed through the PS and SP pins; floating these pins gives a typical minimum dead time of 8 ns, while populated values require resistors between 10 kΩ and 300 kΩ. The TPS7H5003-SP instead has a typical fixed 50-ns dead time. Leading-edge blank time is fixed at 50 ns typical on the TPS7H5003-SP and resistor-programmable on the other devices; LEB cannot float, and its resistor must be between 10 kΩ and 300 kΩ.

- Duty-cycle limits are selected through DCL: VLDO permits 100%, AVSS selects 50%, and floating selects 75% on supported devices. The TPS7H5004-SP requires the 50% setting. OUTB and SRB are active only in the 50% configuration. During high-frequency operation, pulse skipping can prevent minimum-on-time problems and excessive inductor current. Pulses are skipped when COMP is below 0.3 V at the rising clock edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%.

- CS_ILIM senses primary-side current for PWM control and overcurrent protection. The PWM comparator compares sensed current against COMP/2 with a 150-mV offset. Reaching the nominal 1.05-V CS_ILIM threshold initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting and charges CHICC. At 0.6 V, switching stops and soft start is discharged; restart occurs after HICC falls to 0.3 V, followed by a new soft-start sequence. CHICC should be at least 3.3 nF. The FAULT pin can trigger shutdown when driven above a typical 0.6 V, after which outputs remain off until the voltage falls below 0.5 V and a frequency-dependent delay expires. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C and permits restart below 160°C. RSC provides slope compensation to mitigate subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported.

- A 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses a 205-kΩ RT resistor, a 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 20.5-kΩ dead-time resistors, a 49.9-kΩ LEB resistor, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms of soft start. The example selects a transformer ratio of 2.5 and 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous-rectifier FETs, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and 2.3 mF total output capacitance. Other selections include a 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor, and Type 2A compensation components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF.

- Layout recommendations include isolating feedback and other sensitive signals from switching nodes and magnetic components, minimizing high-d/dt and high-dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection, using short and wide high-current traces, placing bypass and compensation components near their pins, filtering CS_ILIM if required, and connecting CFP-package backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.
