A May 24, 2001 IEP news digest focused primarily on California’s electricity crisis and related political developments. Gov. Gray Davis proposed paying businesses to operate diesel backup generators during Stage 3 power alerts, a reversal of his administration’s earlier opposition to routine use of generators because of their pollution. Environmental and air-quality groups criticized the plan, noting that most of California’s 17,200 backup generators lack pollution controls and produce far more emissions than natural-gas plants. Davis also planned to require at least one hour’s notice of rotating blackouts, with broader 24- and 48-hour warnings under consideration.

State Public Utilities Commission President Loretta Lynch said investigators found evidence that some generators reduced plant output during shortages and increased it when prices rose, potentially maximizing profits. Generator companies said output changes had legitimate operational and contractual reasons. Separately, El Paso Merchant Group President Ralph Eads denied that his company manipulated California natural-gas prices, testifying that hedging contracts cost it hundreds of millions of dollars during price spikes; regulators continued considering whether it had abused monopoly power.

Reliant Energy offered to cut electricity bids by 80 percent if state regulators stopped counting emergency operation against permitted plant hours, though air-quality officials disputed the proposal’s logic. President Bush agreed to meet with Davis, whose demands for federal wholesale electricity price controls conflicted with the administration’s policy.

Sen. James Jeffords’ expected departure from the Republican Party could give Democrats control of the Senate, potentially strengthening California Democrats’ efforts to obtain federal price controls and advance energy, conservation and environmental measures. A Field Poll found Davis’s ratings had declined, while utilities, out-of-state providers, Bush and federal regulators received still lower marks; most respondents expected the crisis to last at least a year.

Stackless native-assembly routines use register passing. The enable routine allocates and maps a pre-memory stack across cores, configures x86-64 MTRRs, sets SS/ESP, creates a UEFI PEI handoff, and runs on every core. It reports allocation, reentry, or unknown-family status and preserves EBX. AARCH64 PSP systems instead let the PSP initialize DRAM. The disable routine, once memory is available, disables CAR and removes the pre-memory stack without changing MCRRs.

The Trump administration’s reductions to federal support for multilingual learners have canceled professional development, closed newcomer centers, suspended hiring for English learner teachers, and curtailed guidance and oversight. These changes affect more than 5 million English language learners in K-12 public schools. Proposed 2026 funding cuts could further eliminate tutoring, translation services, family engagement and other programs; Oklahoma and Virginia could lose $6.4 million and $17.5 million, respectively. Fear of immigration enforcement has made some students reluctant to disclose their origins or accept services, while reduced enrollment has prompted program consolidations and staff reassignments. Educators and immigrant-student advocates describe the cuts as devastating, noting that shortages of language-qualified staff and classroom aides also harm broader school communities. With reduced federal monitoring, states are increasingly responsible for ensuring they meet legal obligations to educate multilingual students.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 28, 2019 reported net sales of $91.8 billion, up 9% from $84.3 billion a year earlier, primarily due to higher iPhone and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales. Net income rose to $22.2 billion from $20.0 billion, diluted earnings per share increased to $4.99 from $4.18, and gross margin was $35.2 billion. Product sales increased 8% for iPhone and 37% for Wearables, Home and Accessories, while Mac sales fell 3%, iPad sales fell 11%, and Services sales rose 17%.

By geographic segment, sales increased 12% in the Americas, 14% in Europe, 3% in Greater China and 6% in Rest of Asia Pacific, while Japan sales declined 10%. Gross margin percentage rose to 38.4% from 38.0%, while operating expenses increased to $9.6 billion from $8.7 billion. The effective tax rate declined to 14.2% from 16.5%.

At December 28, 2019, Apple reported $340.6 billion of assets, $251.1 billion of liabilities and $89.5 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $207.1 billion. Operating activities generated $30.5 billion, investing activities used $13.7 billion and financing activities used $25.4 billion. The company repurchased $20.0 billion of stock and paid $3.5 billion of dividends and dividend equivalents.

Apple adopted new lease and hedging accounting standards, recognized $7.5 billion of right-of-use assets and $8.1 billion of lease liabilities, and recorded a $136 million increase in accumulated other comprehensive income from the hedging standard. Disclosed contingencies included the European Commission State Aid Decision, VirnetX litigation, iPhone performance-management cases and an outstanding French competition investigation. Apple stated that its available liquidity was sufficient to meet its operating and capital requirements over the following 12 months.

Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov completed a record-setting 8-hour, 13-minute spacewalk outside the International Space Station—the longest by Russians and fifth longest overall. They replaced an electronics box to upgrade a communications antenna, but it became lodged and ended up 180 degrees beyond its expected position. Although the antenna was still working, Russian officials convened a team to assess whether further action was needed. The discarded 60-pound box was pushed away from the station and will burn up upon reentry. The spacewalk exceeded its planned six-hour duration and the previous Russian record of 8 hours, 7 minutes.

If the SanDisk SSD is not recognized, disconnect all other USB devices. Clone data from the existing internal HDD to the SSD by selecting the “IDE” drive as the source and the SSD as the destination. After cloning, shut down and disconnect power, remove the notebook battery if applicable, and remove the old HDD. Transfer any brackets or adapters, install the SSD in the drive bay, and reconnect the SATA data and power cables. Desktop SSDs may require a 3.5-inch mounting adapter. Reassemble the computer, restore power, and boot; an upgrade-complete message may appear. The old HDD can be retained as a backup.

Running back James Cook has 401 rushing yards, five touchdowns and three straight 100-yard games after settling contract concerns. Josh Allen said the resolved negotiations let Cook play “free and loose,” calling him an “all-time teammate.” The 4-0 Bills host New England in Week 5, with Cook expected to play a major role in their bid for an early AFC East sweep.

The SOS low-post disruption system emphasizes aggressive fronting as the primary defense against strong post offenses, supplemented by coordinated traps. With Post Front, the post defender extends one arm high into the passing lane and keeps the other low against the offensive player’s leg while pushing the post toward the three-second area, limiting entries, touches, and shots.

Additional disruption options include:

- **Base Go:** A low-post trap used when the post is moved off the block or the post defender is late. The passer is pressured toward the baseline, the post is turned toward the baseline, and the low Helpside defender rotates for a hard double team.
- **Go Top:** A high-post trap for posts that turn toward the middle. The post defender pushes the post inside while the high Helpside defender releases for a double team.
- **Go Wing:** A wing-assisted trap used when the post defender is caught behind the post or when the opposing wing is a poor outside shooter. The wing follows the pass and joins the post defender in a double team.
- **Hold:** The post defender plays one-on-one in a three-quarter denial position while the other four defenders stay home and aggressively deny kick-out passes and open three-point shots.
- **Yo-Yo:** A non-shooting wing may sag toward the post for a double team while the remaining defenders deny kick-out passes. If the post passes back, the wing closes out toward the baseline while teammates establish Helpside positions and box pressure against ball reversal.

Right- and left-side variants specify simultaneous defensive rotations as the ball leaves the passer’s hands, including double teams, closeouts, fronting, pass-denial “SNUGGLE” positions, “SET” positioning, and Helpside I assignments.

Research from Yale’s Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution found no “discernible disruption” to U.S. jobs since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. Occupational changes were largely underway in 2021, and AI exposure, automation, and augmentation measures were not associated with employment or unemployment changes. Recent graduates faced slightly greater difficulty landing roles, but the data does not establish AI as the main cause. Some employers are delaying hiring while evaluating AI’s productivity benefits. Researchers cautioned that the sample was small, the analysis is not predictive, and AI could affect employment more directly as models and workplace adoption improve.

Meta will use conversations with its AI assistant to personalize ads and recommendations across Facebook and Instagram beginning December 16, without offering an opt-out for Meta AI users; it said conversations involving religion, politics, sexual orientation, health, race, or ethnicity will not be used. Former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab launched Tinker, a tool for fine-tuning frontier AI models. The startup raised $2 billion before releasing the product.

OpenAI launched Sora 2, a video and audio model with improved motion, speech generation, and user “cameos.” Copyright holders must opt out of having their material used. ChatGPT co-creator Liam Fedus and former DeepMind scientist Ekin Dogus Cubuk founded Periodic Labs, which recruited more than 20 researchers from major AI companies. The $300 million-funded startup plans to use robotics for large-scale scientific experiments.

Seventy-two percent of S&P 500 companies disclosed AI-related material risks this year, up from 12% in 2023. Reputational risk was most commonly cited, followed by cybersecurity, based on Form 10-K filings available through August 15, 2025.

The gold overnight strategy buys gold futures, GLD, GDX, or GDXJ at the market close and sells at the next open to capture overnight price changes caused by global conditions such as interest-rate changes or political events. GDX averaged a 0.12% overnight gain versus a 0.09% loss when bought at the open and sold at the close, though the overnight gain may be too small to trade. GLD’s overnight results were erratic, with reported annual returns of 8.4% versus 8.2% for buy-and-hold, but its average overnight gain was only 0.04%. Its open-to-close gain was practically zero despite a 317% overall rise.

Additional tested long and short overnight variants used simple variables and produced average gains of 0.17% and 0.7%, respectively. The passage stresses that gold is volatile, unpredictable, and difficult to trade, and that commodity strategies often weaken over time. Successful implementation requires market analysis, a defined trading plan, disciplined entries and exits, risk controls, stop-loss and profit-taking orders, cautious leverage, diversification, patience, and emotional control.

This ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1894*, generated by the U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian on May 26, 2018, provides searchable, portable access to full volumes, with bookmarking, note-taking, and offline use. Document numbers are recommended for citation; older volumes’ page numbers are paired with corresponding document numbers. The volume contains two presidential messages: President Benjamin Harrison’s February 6, 1893 transmission of an uncompleted 1854 U.S.-Hawaiian treaty and related correspondence, and his February 16, 1893 submission of Andrew H. Allen’s report and extensive correspondence on U.S. relations with the Hawaiian Islands from September 1820 to January 1893.

Reports collected on November 5, 2001, described Enron’s worsening financial and regulatory crisis. The Wall Street Journal reported that Enron paid $35 million in March 2001 to Chewco Investments LP, an entity managed by former Enron North America executive Michael Kopper. The payment appeared to conclude a series of transactions that kept hundreds of millions of dollars of debt off Enron’s balance sheet. Chewco had reportedly acquired Calpers’ interest in JEDI, a partnership created by Enron and Calpers that enabled substantial borrowing not reflected on Enron’s books. Enron later consolidated JEDI, whose holdings included 12 million Enron shares, and said it repaid about $620 million of third-party debt. Enron maintained that its transactions were legal and properly disclosed and said it would cooperate with the SEC’s formal investigation.

Kopper and former CFO Andrew Fastow had established LJM2 Co-Investment LP in 1999, a partnership involved in billions of dollars of transactions with Enron. Partnership documents indicated that Fastow and possibly Kopper received millions of dollars in fees and investment gains. Fastow was replaced as CFO. Short seller James Chanos said Enron’s filings had revealed red flags, including opaque related-party disclosures, low returns on capital, a high valuation, insider share sales and questionable telecommunications investments. Enron’s stock fell 86% in 2001 to $11.30 following its third-quarter loss and disclosure of a $1.2 billion shareholder-equity reduction.

Enron’s board created an independent committee to review related-party transactions and hired Deloitte & Touche, while auditor Arthur Andersen faced scrutiny over whether its disclosures were sufficiently understandable. Andersen had not been named as a defendant or told it was an SEC investigation subject. Critics said Enron’s complex transfers of assets, notes and shares obscured the transactions’ effects and motives, while Enron said they complied with reporting requirements. Commentary from James Cramer questioned why Enron needed the partnerships and raised possible hypothetical purposes involving concealed trading information, market manipulation, private profit or debt.

AFL-CIO-sponsored funds holding 3.1 million Enron shares and Amalgamated Bank’s Long View Funds called for broader governance reforms, including reviews of insider transactions, executive compensation, director independence and conflicts of interest. After another credit-rating cut and a roughly $20 billion loss in market value, investment bankers said Enron might need to sell power plants, pipelines and trading assets or break itself up.

Enron’s Indian subsidiary served notice on the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid power-purchase payments, beginning an asset-valuation process tied to possible cancellation of the Dabhol contract and a damages claim. Enron sought buyers for its 65% stake in the $2.9 billion project, including Tata Power and BSES, while lenders assessed their $1.4 billion exposure. Separately, BG sought operator status for Indian offshore assets acquired for $388 million, facing opposition from ONGC and Reliance. Enron was also reported to be discussing the sale of its 50% interest in a Korean natural-gas joint venture with SK Corp., likely at a loss.

Cabinet sustained the finance minister’s action, and the claimants were remanded to the courts. In 1881, Secretary Blaine instructed Major Wodehouse that Hawaii could not grant privileges exclusively accorded the United States by the 1875 treaty without violating it and that the United States would support Hawaii in honoring its obligations. Blaine also called for the Hawaiian Islands’ “benevolent neutrality” as key to American Pacific dominion, warning of an “American solution” if neutrality became impracticable. Correspondence also addressed coolie immigration, the Lackawanna incident, and British claims under the reciprocity treaty. In 1883, the United States declined Hawaii’s proposed protest against British and French territorial expansion in Polynesia. A convention of December 6, 1884, renewed the reciprocity treaty for seven years and granted the United States exclusive coaling and repair rights at Pearl River Harbor. It was not ratified until November 1887, amid sugar-industry and congressional opposition; Britain also opposed renewal and the harbor cession. Earlier recommendations included acquiring Pearl Harbor and controlling the Sandwich Islands. Hawaii later authorized a cable subsidy, and an 1891–92 survey charted routes from California to Honolulu.

Strokes require rapid action because delays can prevent lifesaving care. The American Stroke Association’s FAST mnemonic warns of face drooping or an uneven smile, arm weakness or inability to keep both arms raised, and speech difficulty or slurring; T means it is time to call 911 if any symptom appears, even if it resolves. Responders should note when symptoms began. An alternative, STR—Smile, Talk, Raise both arms—calls for the same urgent response if any action is difficult.

The passage compares when children worldwide receive their own mobile phones and smartphones. Sophia Zaske’s daughter showed little interest in owning a phone while living in Germany, where few third-graders had smartphones, but wanted one after moving to the U.S. and becoming the only fourth-grader in her class without one. Her family plans to provide a flip phone before high school but delay a smartphone until then.

About 51% of German children ages 6–13 own a mobile phone. Across seven European countries, 46% of children ages 9–16 own smartphones, although school restrictions and cost-saving practices vary. In the U.S., 45% of children ages 10–12 have their own smartphone service plan, while 42% of children age 8 or younger own tablets.

Ownership generally begins later outside the U.S. and Europe. In South Korea, 72% of children have smartphones by ages 11–12 and may use them for up to 5.4 hours daily. Taiwanese cell phone use rises from 45% among 11-year-olds to 71% among 15-year-olds. Turkish parents most often chose ages 12–17 for a child’s first phone. Mobile phone access is also reported among South African, Ghanaian and Malawian children, with substantial increases from 2007 to 2014. Australian studies found a median first-phone age of eight.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no “right” age, recommends limiting young children’s screen use and monitoring media, and advises avoiding screens as the sole calming method, before bed and during meals.

The passage examines the best-performing stock markets since 1900, drawing on Credit Suisse's Global Investment Returns Yearbook (with the London Business School and Cambridge University), which tracks 23 countries. The top ten include Australia, the United States, South Africa, New Zealand, Denmark, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Switzerland, and the Netherlands, with the top five discussed in detail. Australia ranks first, with ASX returns above 6.5% yearly in U.S. dollars, attributed to limited WWII damage, a strong banking and service economy, dividends supplying 53% of total gains (versus 42% in the U.S.), commodity export leadership, low corruption, transparent legislation, and appeal to foreign investors. The U.S. market returned 6.5% annualized after inflation, turning $1 invested in 1900 into $3,806 by end-2019, and holds the largest equity market at just over 54% of global free-float capitalization, with Japan second at 7.7%. South Africa's average return is 7.2% (6.4% in USD), supported by natural resources and diversification into finance, technology, and services; New Zealand annualized at 6.4%; Denmark ranked fifth, benefiting from World War I neutrality and trade but suffering an 80-year inflation-adjusted bear market from 1898 to 1980, with consistently high real returns only in the past 35 years.

Globally, equities grew at a real 5.2% annually from 1900–2019, versus 2% for bonds and 0.8% for Treasury bills, outpacing bonds by 4.3% per year, due to post-crisis rebuilding, technological innovation, and recession-driven interest rate cuts. Listed advantages include potential returns (around 10% annually since 1926 versus 5–6% for long-term bonds), inflation protection, dividends, ownership, liquidity, diversification, and low entry barriers via commission-free brokers and fractional shares. A 2017 study by Hendrik Bessembinder found that only a tiny fraction of stocks produce all the gains, making stock picking difficult. The S&P 500 returned 8%–12% annually over 50 years, growing $10,000 to more than $380,000, though it falls three years in ten, and past performance does not guarantee future results.

The author recounts making a film about a Frenchman who froze his deceased wife, adopting a deeply skeptical view of revival. They outline Robert Ettinger’s 1964 proposal to preserve bodies in liquid nitrogen for future resuscitation and note that 2,000 people have paid for cryopreservation, while pets and celebrities have also expressed interest. Despite this interest, no scientist believes frozen brains or bodies can be revived. The author calls cryonics an exploitation of fear of death that robs death of dignity and urges that it end.
On World Wetlands Day, South Louisiana’s Beignet the Nutria predicted a mild hurricane season by not seeing his shadow, while Punxsutawney Phil forecast six more weeks of winter.

The United States supports France’s recovery of Alsace-Lorraine but would not insist on fighting for it beyond France’s own willingness, since an unfulfillable commitment would be unwise. Italy is entitled to boundary rectifications based on defensive and nationalist considerations, free commercial access to Trieste, and cultural autonomy for its inhabitants, but not broader Adriatic ambitions.

The Treaty of Bucharest is rejected as unjust to all Balkan peoples. Any lasting settlement requires the evacuation of Rumania, Serbia, and Montenegro, restoration of Serbia and Montenegro, and fair consideration of nationalist and economic interests while ending great-power interference and unity through massacre. Provisional Balkan arrangements include returning most of the Dobrudja to Bulgaria, revising Bulgarian boundaries, providing Serbia access through Saloniki, postponing a decision on Macedonia, and avoiding an independent Albania.

An independent, democratic Poland should have boundaries balancing national and economic interests and ensuring access to the sea. Its government and relations should be determined by its people. Complete Polish unification is impractical, and a democratic foundation is essential to prevent internal friction from weakening Poland.

Montreal topped the QS Best Student Cities 2017 ranking, followed by Paris, London and Seoul. The rankings assess university quality, student facilities, affordability, city desirability, employer access, international character, tolerance, pollution and safety. Montreal ranked first, Vancouver tenth and Toronto eleventh, reflecting Canada’s growing appeal to international students. Paris fell because of costs and reduced desirability, while London rose to third despite Brexit-related concerns. Germany’s Berlin and Munich also ranked highly, and the country charges overseas students no tuition fees. Asian cities performed strongly, led by Seoul, while Kuala Lumpur and Surabaya were the most affordable and Stockholm and New York the most expensive. More than one million overseas students attended US universities, contributing an estimated $36 billion to its economy.

South Korean prosecutors raided Korean Air Lines’ headquarters and are investigating Chairman Cho Yang-ho and his family for alleged tax evasion, embezzlement and breach of trust. They are examining inherited overseas assets and suspicious money flows involving family members and associates. The inquiry followed increased scrutiny of the owning family and public pressure that led Cho to step down as Jin Air’s co-CEO.

A case prepared by Deborah Ancona and Cate Reavis (July 2014) traces the founding of car-sharing startup Zipcar by Robin Chase and the financial crisis she faced four months after launch.

Chase, the daughter of an American diplomat raised largely in the Middle East, learned respect for all people from her father and flexibility from her artist mother. After studying at the American College in Paris and Wellesley College and managing USAID contracts at public health firm John Snow Inc., she was rejected by MIT Sloan for low GMAT math scores, retook the test, and was admitted to the Class of 1986. She earned an A and the highest grade in the hard finance course, gaining confidence she could master any subject. After graduating, while raising three children, she heard about car-sharing in Berlin from Harvard geochemist Antje Danielson in September 1999 and saw the fit with the Internet and emerging wireless technology. Zipcar was incorporated in January 2000, with Chase as CEO and Danielson as vice president under a 50-50 ownership arrangement.

Networking—through her brother Mark, adviser Peter Nessen (her "reality check"), and Benoît Robert of Communauto, the largest North American car-sharing organization—shaped her plan; she knew prior car-sharing ventures had failed financially but believed wireless technology would change the economics. First investor Jean Hammond provided a $50,000 convertible loan in February 2000.

The team included husband Roy Russell (servers and in-car technology), Mark Chase (business development), Stephen Oakley (operations), and Larry Slotnick (marketing, later fleet manager). President Keefer Welch, hired a month before launch, left after three months; his severance was costly and one investor cut his commitment from $200,000 to $50,000. Chase rejected a first proximity-card/keypad prototype and had Russell and MIT students build a simpler wireless-ready system; initially any Zipcard could unlock any car. Leasing cars, securing parking, arranging insurance, and setting up credit cards took far longer than expected, and Cambridge's RFP process took nearly six months.

Facing a collapsing market (NASDAQ down 28% between February and May 2000) and no offers after more than 100 fundraising meetings, Chase had only $68 left three days before launch until angel Juan Enriquez supplied $25,000 for car deposits. Her pricing model included a $300 deposit, $50 annual membership fee, $4.50/hour for regular cars and $7.00/hour for premium cars plus $0.40/mile, and $44/day up to 125 miles; she estimated break-even at 70 cars used six hours a day, and Harvard Business School professor David Bell advised her to stop modeling and set prices. Zipcar launched in June 2000 with four Volkswagens near four Red Line subway stops, earned national press, and relied on guerrilla postcard marketing; by mid-September it was adding 35 members a week.

In mid-October, with 10 cars, over 400 members, and a $1.3 million round about to close, Chase and MIT student Jim Grube found utilization at 22% versus her 40% estimate (under 5.5 hours per day versus 9.6) and revenue per trip and September revenue roughly half her projections, implying the company could not break even. She wept for two hours, then determined the daily rate was the culprit: with 50% of revenue from daily rentals, the daily rate would need a 20% increase to break even. Raising prices was difficult given inflexible financial systems and back-end engineering work, while Mark and others warned it broke promises to members and risked backlash just before the Series A close; Chase grew angry that no founder stories had warned of this.

The team refuses to give up despite unfavorable bounces and a score that did not reflect its play at times. It plans to create more traffic, work shift by shift, and score early against an outstanding opposing goalie while relying on heart and belief in its system.

Penny Mordaunt became the first minister to use sign language in Parliament, signing and speaking during Commons questions. Speaker John Bercow also signed his reply. Mordaunt announced a July 24 global disability conference in London, organized by the UK and Kenyan governments and the International Disability Alliance.

The team needs to improve defensive-zone play, especially limiting Carolina’s offensive time, disrupting forechecks and entries, blocking shots, and reducing giveaways while generating takeaways. Players should focus on their own game rather than trying to do too much under Stanley Cup Finals pressure. The speaker reflects on Rem’s journey and emphasizes minimizing opponents’ small advantages, such as faceoff stick interference on home ice.

The TPS7H500x-SP series consists of fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers intended for radiation-hardness-assured, space-grade DC-DC converters. The devices support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, require external gate drivers, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A transconductance error amplifier compares VSENSE with the lower of the soft-start voltage or the 0.613-V reference. Its typical transconductance is 1800 µA/V and DC gain is 10,000 V/V. Output voltage is programmed with a VOUT-to-VSENSE resistor divider using the 0.613-V reference; resistors with tolerances of 1% or less are recommended. A capacitor from SS to AVSS controls soft-start timing, using a typical 2.7-µA charging current. Synchronous-rectifier outputs become active after SS exceeds 1 V.

Three switching-frequency modes are supported. In internal oscillator mode, a required RT resistor sets a frequency from 100 kHz to 2 MHz, and SYNC outputs an in-phase clock at twice the switching frequency. In external synchronization mode, RT floats and SYNC receives a 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock with a 40% to 60% duty cycle; a 50% duty cycle is recommended. Primary-secondary mode synchronizes two controllers using the primary controller’s SYNC output, either as independent converters or as a parallel interleaved converter with shared VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC connections. The secondary controller inverts the clock, producing a 90° or 270° phase shift.

Primary outputs are OUTA or OUTA/OUTB, depending on the device, while synchronous-rectifier outputs are SRA and, where supported, SRB. Each output has roughly 150-mA peak capability, making external gate-drive solutions necessary. OUTB and SRB are active only with the 50% duty-cycle configuration on applicable devices, and remain off during soft start.

The TPS7H5003-SP has a typical fixed 50-ns dead time, while the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP support independent programmable primary-to-synchronous and synchronous-to-primary dead times through the PS and SP pins. Floating PS and SP pins select a typical minimum dead time of 8 ns; populated values require resistors from 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ. Leading-edge blank time is fixed at a typical 50 ns for the TPS7H5003-SP and resistor-programmable for the other devices through LEB, using 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ.

At high frequencies, pulse skipping prevents problems caused by minimum on-time and can reduce startup inductor current. Pulses are skipped when COMP is below 0.3 V at the rising clock edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. With dual 50%-limited outputs, both skip pulses equally to maintain volt-second balance and avoid transformer flux walking.

Duty-cycle limits are configured through DCL: connection to VLDO provides 100%, connection to AVSS provides 50% on supported devices, and leaving DCL floating provides 75%. The TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50% and requires DCL connected to AVSS.

Current sensing uses CS_ILIM, which receives a signal representing primary-side current and also controls overcurrent protection. Primary outputs turn on with the internal clock and turn off when the sensed peak reaches a stepped-down COMP voltage with a 150-mV comparator offset. A sense resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS is required. At the nominal 1.05-V threshold, the controller enters hiccup operation, with sufficient margin required between normal peak current and the trip level.

During hiccup operation, the controller performs cycle-by-cycle current limiting while charging CHICC with an 80-µA pulsed current. At 0.6 V, switching stops and SS is discharged; HICC is then pulled to 1 V and discharged with a 1-µA restart current. Restart soft start occurs when HICC falls to 0.3 V, provided the overcurrent has cleared. CHICC controls both the limiting-delay and restart intervals, and at least 3.3 nF is recommended.

The FAULT pin supports external overcurrent, overvoltage, or other protection logic. A typical voltage above 0.6 V sustained for the specified 0.4-to-1.4-µs pulse window triggers shutdown. Once FAULT falls below a typical 0.5-V falling threshold, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay before restarting soft start.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles above 50%. The minimum stability slope is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, while the recommended slope is equal to that slope. RSC sets the compensation. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported; Type 2A adds a high-frequency capacitor, CHF, across RCOMP and CCOMP.

Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and permits reinitialization below 160°C.

A detailed 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter example uses a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 5-V output, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, approximately 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors, 49.9-kΩ LEB resistor, and 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing approximately 7.5 ms of soft start. The example uses a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous-rectifier FETs, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and 2.3 mF total output capacitance. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω RCS provide cycle-by-cycle limiting at roughly 35 A. Type 2A compensation uses 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF for RCOMP, CCOMP, and CHF, while RSC uses 102 kΩ.

The controllers operate from a regulated 4-V-to-14-V supply and require at least 0.1 µF of VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching nodes and power magnetics, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, and using short, wide high-current traces.

Consilium Software, a Cisco Preferred Solution Partner, has launched Consilium UniRSM™ worldwide through Cisco SolutionsPlus as a replacement for the end-of-sale Cisco Remote Silent Monitoring product. Designed for Cisco Contact Center Enterprise environments, it enables remote supervisors and managers to monitor and coach live calls from any phone without a network connection to the Cisco environment. The product includes silent monitoring, whisper coaching, multi-call monitoring, high availability, VVB and VXML support, web-based reporting, and Windows and Linux compatibility. It incorporates customer and partner feedback and improvements over Cisco RSM, which is unsupported in CCE release 11.6(x).

Broker-reported statistics from 13 randomly selected CFD brokers show that 62%–82% of retail CFD traders lose money. The passage cites FCA estimates that roughly 80% lose over a year, while disciplined traders making up about 20%–25% can profit through cost control, risk management, and proven strategies.

Reasons given include CFDs being zero-sum, leverage magnifying losses, bid-ask spreads and overnight fees, wider spreads and price gaps in volatile or illiquid markets, counterparty risk, limited trading knowledge, and absent trading plans. Most CFD traders are retail, and few professionals trade them. The passage also states that only 1%–20% of day traders make money, while 70%–90% of short-term traders fail.

CQC rated ULHT “requiring improvement,” though 72% of inspected areas were good. Council leader Martin Hill urged health bosses to publish future service plans, saying the STP was delayed until 2019 despite £1.2 million spent. The trust remains in special measures amid recruitment concerns and service issues in Boston and Lincoln; Grantham and Louth were rated “good,” while Boston was “inadequate.”

The passage describes a scalable information management system for protecting, storing, and managing organizational data, particularly virtual machine data in network or cloud environments that do not natively support changed-block tracking. The disclosed methods generate virtual machine disk images at different times, compare them to identify changed blocks, create a map of those blocks, and use a virtual server agent to extract the changed blocks for differential or incremental backups. The system also accommodates differences between hypervisor-specific block formats and formats supported by the information management system.

The architecture includes a centralized storage manager, data agents on client computing devices, media agents on secondary storage computing devices, primary and secondary storage subsystems, management databases, indexes, policies, scheduling, reporting, and user interfaces. These components coordinate data movement, processing, recovery, and administration. Supported operations include full, differential, incremental, and synthetic-full backups; archives; snapshots; replication; deduplication; reference copies; and hierarchical or lifecycle storage management. Secondary copies may be compressed, encrypted, deduplicated, indexed, and retained for recovery, analysis, retention, and regulatory purposes.

U.S. stocks advanced as investors grew cautious over record valuations, with the S&P 500 up about 15% and the Nasdaq nearly 19%, led by AI and technology companies. The S&P 500’s forward price-to-earnings ratio reached about 23 versus its 10-year average of 18.7. The IMF warned elevated prices could create systemic risks, while Jamie Dimon anticipated a possible correction. Goldman Sachs cited earnings and productivity growth but acknowledged concentration risks. Record call-option trading suggested short-term speculation, though optimism persisted on Fed easing and softer inflation. Earnings and central-bank commentary are expected to shape whether the rally remains sustainable into 2026.

Donald Trump’s December 6 recognition of Jerusalem as Israel’s capital was condemned internationally and by the Arab League. An expert said Trump sought support from Jewish Zionists, abandoned prior neutrality and described the Israeli-Palestinian peace process as a sham. The Arab League adopted a resolution without punitive measures and was characterized as weak and dependent. Tarik Skubal tied the Tigers’ franchise postseason record with 14 strikeouts, helping Detroit beat the Cleveland Guardians 2-1 in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. During Jason Rohde’s murder trial, Sergeant Marlon Appollis told the Western Cape High Court that no suicide note or other sign of suicide was found near Susan Rohde’s body at a Spier hotel room in July 2016. Susan was found hanging behind the bathroom door, but there was no chair, table or other object to stand on. Appollis found a burnt note indicating an extramarital affair. The autopsy concluded that Susan had been manually strangled, and the case was changed to murder. Jason Rohde, accused of staging the suicide, pleaded not guilty. Tests were ordered to determine whether the bathroom door hook could support Susan’s 51kg weight, and the trial was postponed for the defence to prepare.

This study sequenced SARS-CoV-2 from 12 RT-qPCR-positive respiratory samples collected in Esteio, Rio Grande do Sul, between April 9 and June 29, 2021. Mean initial Ct was 23.83; mean genome coverage was 98.26%, with mean depth of 292.23×. All 12 genomes belonged to the Gamma clade: 10 to P.1 and two to P.1.17. Sixty-eight nucleotide substitutions were detected, including 36 nonsynonymous changes. Common substitutions included NSP12:P323L, S:K417T, S:T1027I, ORF8:E92K, and N:P80R. S:E484K and S:N501Y occurred together in two samples. Several mutations were reported for the first time in Rio Grande do Sul, including D1208A, first identified in Brazil, and NSP12:I136V, previously undescribed on GISAID.

A GISAID dataset containing 4,706 Rio Grande do Sul genomes collected from March 2020 through May 2022 documented successive lineage waves: B.1.1.33 predominated in 2020; Zeta, B.1.1.28, and P.7 followed; Gamma became prevalent from February to July 2021; Delta was first sequenced in June 2021 and predominated from August through year-end; and Omicron exceeded 90% of sequenced genomes from January through April 2022. Gamma represented 57.1% and Delta 32.30% of sequences collected in 2021.

Global searches found close relatives for eight study genomes in Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Canada, and the United States, while four had no identifiable matches. A broader search recovered 424 unique related genomes, 638 genomes in total, at genetic distances of nine or less. Low sequence coverage, high undefined-base rates, and collection dates preceding some matched genomes prevented definitive conclusions about migration or other epidemiological relationships.

Local maximum-likelihood phylogenomics identified monophyletic clades for Alpha, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron with at least 97% branch support; P.2 and P.7 also formed supported groups. All 12 study genomes clustered within Gamma, including supported P.1, P.1.2, and P.1.17 sublineages.

HyPhy analyses found no positively selected sites in the envelope protein, but codons 25 and 63 showed negative selection. The membrane protein had two sites under positive selection, 94 and 125, and 12 under purifying selection. The nucleocapsid protein had 14 positively selected sites and 46 under negative selection, with nine and 20 sites, respectively, identified by multiple methods. DynaMut2 predicted that M-protein substitutions at site 94 could stabilize or destabilize the protein, whereas all tested substitutions at site 125 were stabilizing. N-protein substitutions D63G and D63Y were stabilizing, P151L and P151S were destabilizing, and most tested C-terminal-domain mutations were destabilizing except Q289L. The authors noted that further study is needed to clarify the consequences of these structural changes for SARS-CoV-2 host-pathogen interactions.

This study examined preschool teachers’ views on sensory education and its implementation in early childhood classrooms. Sensory development is presented as fundamental to learning, with seven senses categorized as external (sight, hearing, touch, smell, taste) and internal (vestibular and proprioceptive). Using a phenomenological qualitative design, 20 preschool teachers from varied educational settings and demographic backgrounds were selected through maximum diversity sampling. Data were collected through 12-question semi-structured interviews and analyzed using content analysis.

Three themes emerged: the importance of sensory education, its relationship to the preschool education program, and difficulties and limitations. Teachers consistently regarded sensory education as important, particularly in early childhood, and believed it supports language, cognitive, social-emotional, and self-care development. They incorporated sensory experiences into everyday activities through art, music and rhythm, games, drama, experiments, visual and auditory studies, tactile activities, and balance exercises. Teachers also described using observation, developmental records, questions, and family cooperation to evaluate these activities.

Although sensory education appeared in the preschool program’s outcomes and indicators, participants felt it was not sufficiently or explicitly stated. Reported barriers included inadequate materials, unsuitable physical facilities, limited time, insufficient knowledge of sensory integration, and the need for teacher training. Family participation was identified as important. Recommendations included in-service training, occupational-therapist support, improved classroom materials and facilities, greater inclusion of sensory education in undergraduate curricula, and preparation of sample sensory-education activities.

Stanford researchers developed “biofilm lithography,” using blue light and genetically engineered E. coli to create patterned bacterial biofilms at 25-micrometer resolution. The bacteria secrete a sticky protein when illuminated, causing them to adhere in selected areas and form designs such as dots, stripes, and circuits. The technique is faster, simpler, and higher-resolution than other bacterial patterning methods and works in varied environments, including microfluidic devices. It could advance research on bacterial communities, synthetic microbial systems, biomaterials, metabolic biosynthesis, and biocomputation. Surprisingly sharp patterns suggested bacteria remain weakly attached to surfaces while repeatedly jumping on and off them. Researchers are also pursuing multispecies communities and studying how biofilms share antibiotic resistance.

**Summary**

This protocol describes a three-arm, parallel, randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the Digital-MindCAN programme, an eight-week digital mindfulness psychoeducation intervention developed specifically for cancer survivors. The study is registered with the ISCTN Clinical Trial Registry (ISRCTN10756933) and approved by the NHG Domain Specific Review Board, Singapore (2021/00083).

**Background:** Technology-based mindfulness interventions have been delivered to cancer survivors via online video, teleconference, telephone and mobile apps, and are perceived as cost-effective and accessible, especially during COVID-19. Existing mindfulness interventions show positive effects on anxiety, depression, stress, fatigue, quality of life and post-traumatic growth, but gaps remain: most focus on practice without cancer-specific knowledge, it is unclear whether such interventions prevent symptoms or enhance psychological well-being and resilience, qualitative data are overlooked, and objective stress measures are rarely used. The Digital-MindCAN programme was developed to address these gaps. It is guided by a psychological well-being promotion model created by the researchers based on Neuman's systems theory and Ryff's psychological well-being, positing that prevention interventions help restore well-being; the programme is positioned as a secondary prevention intervention.

**Design and participants:** 150 cancer survivors will be recruited from a cancer center at a tertiary hospital in Singapore and randomized 1:1:1 to Digital-MindCAN plus standard care, Palouse Mindfulness plus standard care (active control), or a wait-list control. Eligible participants are adults aged 21–65 of any gender with stage 0–III cancer who completed all cancer and related treatments (except hormonal therapy) between 2 weeks and 2 years after diagnosis; exclusions are pregnancy, severe mental disorders and severe medical conditions requiring hospitalization. Sample size (based on effect size 0.35, 80% power, two-sided 5% level) was 142, rounded to 150. Randomization involves sequence generation by the principal investigator using Excel, concealed allocation released only after consent, and implementation via unique participant IDs. Blinding of participants and assessors is difficult, though detection bias may be reduced by physiological measures. Participants receive a SGD 100 honorarium. Recruiters liaise with clinical staff; anticipated low recruitment (pandemic) will be addressed via flyers on social, hospital and university websites and research assistants stationed at the cancer center.

**Interventions:** Digital-MindCAN comprises eight weekly group sessions of 90 minutes delivered in real time by researchers via videotelephony, combining education on cancer-specific stressors (treatment side effects, surgery scars, recurrent thoughts, fear of recurrence, depression, anxiety, relationships with caregivers and professionals) with practices such as mindful breathing, STOP breathing, body scan, the five-step PAIN process, mindfulness of positive emotions, letting-go meditation, mindful sitting and loving-kindness meditation. The active control, Palouse Mindfulness, is an internet-based MBSR programme of eight 90-minute sessions without cancer-specific content, covering awareness, attention and the brain, thoughts, stress, difficult emotions and pain, communication, compassion, and developing one's own practice (sitting, body scan, mountain, lake, loving-kindness and rain meditations). Both groups practice at home 10–30 minutes daily, keep a Mindfulness Practice Diary, receive an education booklet, and join a mobile messaging platform for communication and weekly reminders. Treatment fidelity is documented through attendance records and facilitator weekly logs.

**Measures:** Data come from self-report questionnaires, physiological measurements and focus group interviews. Primary outcomes are objective stress (peripheral skin temperature via stress thermometer, heart rate and SpO2 variability via pulse oximeter) and subjective stress (DASS-21, also yielding depression and anxiety). Secondary outcomes are psychological well-being (Ryff's 18-item scale), perceived relaxation (visual analogue scale), mindfulness (MAAS) and resilience (Connor-Davidson scale). Objective stress and perceived relaxation are measured before and after each session (16 data sets); psychological well-being, subjective stress, mindfulness and resilience are assessed at baseline, after session 4 and after session 8. Focus groups of 4–8 participants per intervention group, lasting about an hour and audio-recorded, explore perceptions of the programmes after session 8. Demographic and health information are also collected.

**Analysis:** Data will be entered and checked in SPSS v28, with data cleansing, intent-to-treat analysis and multiple imputation for missing data, and baseline comparability tabulated. Mean differences in subjective stress, depression, anxiety, mindfulness, resilience and psychological well-being across three assessment points and three groups will be tested by ANCOVA with baseline scores as covariates; differences in skin temperature, heart rate, SpO2 and perceived relaxation by repeated-measures ANOVA, with partial eta squared (0.01, 0.06, 0.14 for small, medium, large effects). Qualitative data will undergo realist analysis in five steps: transcription and indexing, interpretation and theorization, contrastive demi-regularities, retroduction and concretization.

**Discussion:** The trial aims to test whether the eight-week group-based Digital-MindCAN programme is non-inferior to Palouse Mindfulness and superior to the wait-list control in improving psychological outcomes. Positive results would add knowledge on digital mindfulness interventions for cancer survivors in Singapore and may inform clinical practice, including offering the programme as an alternative service. Attrition over the eight-week period is anticipated and mitigated by honoraria, mobile-platform reminders and support; future research could explore mobile applications, virtual reality, augmented reality and artificial intelligence.

The speaker said the team’s quick defensive play protected the front of the net and limited second and third chances, but frequent rushes out of the zone left them chasing the puck and unable to generate much neutral-zone movement. He also said the building created substantial pregame anticipation, but once play began, the team that executed best and played hardest would win.

CMD42 requires a block large enough for its data structure; otherwise its result is undefined and the card may lock unexpectedly. Invalid passwords or lengths outside 1–128 bits cause errors. Failures set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED; CARD_IS_LOCKED reflects lock-state changes.

Agilent shares rose about 22% in a month, but the author views them as overpriced and recommends selling or avoiding them. Despite shareholder-friendly management, dividend growth, manageable debt, substantial cash, and improved recent results, revenue and net-income growth have been uninspiring. A conservative forecast assumes 6% dividend growth through 2021, yielding about 6.7% annual returns over four years—insufficient given risks from variable research budgets, economic conditions, and policy uncertainty. Technically, a close below $58.50 is projected to precede a decline to $53 over three months; the proposed put-option trade has a stop above $60.50. Agilent’s 15% premium to the broader market and valuation near its recent high support the “avoid” rating.

The paper examines collective academic exile and the higher education projects (HEPs) created or relocated abroad by Russian scholars following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It frames these initiatives through “education in emergencies,” focusing on their relationship with a conflict-affected homeland. “Relocation,” a term used by Russian emigrants to avoid the status of exile, is characterized as involuntary departure, often experienced as temporary and linked to political dissent. The resulting “exiled consciousness” combines departure with an enduring expectation of eventual return, shaping how HEPs operate and what futures they envision.

State repression and censorship following the invasion drove thousands of academics from Russia through politically motivated dismissals, “foreign agent” designations, pressure on faculties, and closures. Some emigrants joined foreign institutions individually, while others relocated existing institutions or re-established them with former colleagues. Their identities remain ambiguous because their departures were political but did not always meet the legal or personal criteria of exile or refugee status.

The study examines four projects ranging from informal online courses to accredited, campus-based programs. It considers their differing levels of institutionalization through formalization, legitimacy, and autonomy. Data include semi-structured interviews with project leaders and discourse analysis of promotional materials, presentations, publications, and discussions. Thematic and conversational discourse analyses are triangulated to identify shared ideas and narratives.

Three forms of self-conceptualization emerge. First, HEPs act as “safe havens,” supporting displaced scholars and students through Russian-language education, scholarships, positions, visa assistance, and continuity of academic work. They also provide intellectual freedom, solidarity, belonging, and continuity of professional identity, while navigating integration into host academic communities.

Second, HEPs seek to preserve and transform academic heritages damaged by war and repression. They reproduce Russian-language scholarship, schools of thought, liberal arts education, and critical approaches to teaching, while collaborating internationally to reinterpret inherited practices. This reconceptualization remains limited and inconsistent: hierarchical teaching, inherited assumptions, and unexamined biases persist despite commitments to democratic education and broader transformation.

Third, HEPs convert anticipation of return into a “hope-making praxis.” They pursue feasible present action regardless of whether return becomes possible, envisioning educated, democratic futures for Russia and investing in humanities and social sciences. This praxis generates both transformation and hope, but its proposed futures require further scrutiny for colonial attitudes, exclusions, and marginalization.

The paper concludes that HEPs combine sanctuary, heritage preservation, pragmatic action, and future-oriented hope. It recommends further research into how geographical and organizational contexts shape inherited practices, how international influences alter them, the gap between declared missions and everyday teaching, changing conflict conditions, and the broader international-education structures that encourage emigrant scholars to establish separate projects.

A Markov state-transition cohort model evaluated whether RATIONS-style nutritional supplementation would be cost-effective for reducing TB incidence and mortality among 100,000 HIV-negative household contacts of people with TB in India. The modeled intervention provided a six-month food basket containing a daily multivitamin, rice, and lentils; individuals developing TB also received higher-calorie, higher-protein support during treatment. Outcomes and costs were assessed over the cohort’s lifetime from governmental and societal perspectives.

Compared with usual care, the intervention reduced lifetime TB cases from 7,718 to 6,749 per 100,000 and TB deaths from 1,529 to 906, while averting 13,775 disability-adjusted life years. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $229 per DALY averted from the governmental perspective and $184 from the societal perspective, both below India’s willingness-to-pay threshold of $550 per DALY averted. Sensitivity analyses found the intervention generally cost-effective, and probabilistic simulations favored it in more than 99% of runs at the $550 threshold.

The study did not model effects on relapse, treatment disengagement, transmission, pre-diagnosis costs, drug-resistant TB, or broader nutritional and productivity benefits. The authors concluded that RATIONS-style nutritional support could be cost-effective in Indian populations with high burdens of TB and undernutrition.

The lecture examines the open problem of dynamic optimality for binary search trees: whether one online algorithm can perform every successful search within a constant factor of the optimal binary search tree algorithm for each access sequence. The model permits pointer traversal and rotations but excludes insertions and deletions. Although \(\log n\) time per search is unavoidable in the worst case, performance on particular sequences can be much better.

Several amortization properties characterize such performance. The sequential access property supports ordered searches in constant amortized time. The dynamic finger property bounds cost by the logarithm of the key distance from the previous access. The entropy bound gives a cost based on access frequencies and is optimal for static trees that cannot change during searches. The working-set property charges the logarithm of the number of distinct keys accessed since the current key’s previous access; it implies the entropy bound. The unified property combines temporal recency and spatial proximity, charging the logarithm of their sum. More powerful pointer-machine structures can satisfy this property, but whether a binary search tree can do so remains unknown; the best known binary-search-tree bound has an additional \(\log\log n\) cost.

Dynamic optimality would require an online algorithm whose total cost is within a constant factor of the best offline algorithm, which may be tailored to the complete access sequence. This remains open. The best known guarantee is a \(\log\log n\) competitive factor, while balanced binary search trees give a \(\log n\) factor.

Splay trees move each accessed node to the root through zig, zig-zig, and zig-zag rotations and have \(O(\log n)\) amortized access time. They satisfy the sequential access, working-set, entropy, and dynamic finger properties. Whether they satisfy the unified property or are dynamically optimal is unknown.

The lecture then presents a geometric interpretation. An access sequence is plotted with key order on one axis and time on the other, and each node touched during a search contributes a point. A theorem states that a point set represents a valid binary search tree execution exactly when it is “arborally satisfied”: every nonzero-area rectangle determined by two points that do not share a horizontal or vertical line must contain another point. Search cost is proportional to the number of touched points. Thus, offline dynamic optimality becomes the problem of finding a minimum-size arborally satisfied superset of the required access points. The exact complexity and solution remain unknown, and only a \(\log\log n\) approximation is known.

A treap-based construction implements this geometric formulation. Keys form a binary search tree and are heap-ordered by their next touch times. At each search, the nodes to be touched form a connected subtree containing the root; rotations rearrange that subtree into a local treap based on updated touch times. Arboral satisfaction ensures that the resulting tree remains globally heap-ordered.

A greedy geometric algorithm processes accesses in time order, adding points to repair unsatisfied rectangles. Its tree interpretation follows the search path and rearranges the touched nodes according to future access times. It is a plausible offline-optimal method, but its optimality is unproved. The geometric view also permits an online version using split trees, which can move a requested node to the root and partition the remaining keys in constant amortized time. This simulates the offline treap behavior with balanced search trees, though the required parallel-search machinery is not itself a standard binary search tree.

A finite-temperature CFT on flat space is described by a black hole with a planar horizon whose topology matches the boundary. For a CFT on a sphere, the gravity description is global AdS with periodic Euclidean time. The sphere introduces a curvature radius \(R\), so unlike the flat-space case, physics depends on the dimensionless temperature \(RT\). The corresponding Euclidean metric remains nonsingular, unlike its planar counterpart.

Global AdS admits three thermal saddle points: thermal AdS, a large black hole, and a small black hole. The small black hole has negative specific heat and is unstable; it exists only above a minimum temperature and never dominates. The stable phase is determined by the lowest free energy, equivalently by comparing Euclidean actions in the large-\(N\) saddle-point approximation. Thermal AdS dominates at low temperatures, while the large black hole dominates at high temperatures. They have equal free energy at a critical temperature \(T_c=2\pi R/(d-1)\), when the horizon radius equals the AdS radius. This Hawking–Page transition is first order: the free energy is continuous, but its first derivative is discontinuous at leading order in \(N\).

Taking \(R\) to infinity maps the sphere theory to the flat-space theory and corresponds to the high-temperature, large-black-hole limit.

A field-theory toy model uses two \(N\times N\) matrices of free harmonic oscillators subject to an \(SU(N)\) singlet constraint. At low temperature, only low-energy states contribute and the free energy is of order \(N^0\). At sufficiently high temperature, the exponentially large density of states at energy of order \(N^2\) overwhelms thermal suppression, producing an order-\(N^2\) free-energy change and the same Hawking–Page transition. The mechanism is tied to the large-\(N\) density of states rather than the toy model’s detailed interactions.

Faviola Dadis accused Steven Seagal of sexually assaulting her during a 2002 casting session in a Beverly Hills hotel room, when she was 17. She said she later experienced depression, anxiety, PTSD, and difficulty trusting men. Los Angeles prosecutors said her case was under review.
