Bemidji’s Blue Ox won the Region 10C tournament, defeating Crookston 7-3 after taking a 5-0 lead. Ben Thoma earned the win with seven innings, seven strikeouts and one run allowed, while Cody Benson went 3-for-5. Crookston, the runner-up, had earlier beaten Moorhead 3-2 in extra innings to earn a state berth. As region champion, Bemidji received a first-round bye in the 48-team state tournament.

Dale Capstick’s Coxheath home has hosted nightly visits from dozens of palm-sized giant house spiders since August, including about 30 killed by her husband. Charles Andrews captured one, which Calum Ewing of the Nova Scotia Museum confirmed as Eratigena atrica, or European house spider. The harmless species has bodies 10–18 millimetres long and leg spans up to 10 centimetres. Native to western Europe and present in Nova Scotia since the mid-1990s, they often enter sinks or bathtubs and build nonsticky, funnel-shaped webs in dark corners. Their presence indicates a plentiful insect population; once the prey disappears, they leave or starve.

Meizu has cut the Chinese prices of its Pro 7 and Pro 7 Plus smartphones by 600 Yuan, with the series starting at 1,999 Yuan from December 12. Both feature Super AMOLED displays, dual rear cameras, and Flyme OS 6.

Rushin Shah, Apple’s former head of Siri Natural Language Understanding, left after five years to join Facebook, where he will work on natural language and dialogue understanding. He helped develop Siri’s voice recognition, conversational classification, and intent interpretation. His departure comes amid increased competition from Alexa and Google Assistant and as Apple expands Siri to Mac and a smart speaker. No replacement has been named.

At HPE Discover 2017, HPE introduced its Edgeline Services Platform, Data Aggregation App, and Address Translation App as “Software Defined OT” tools for combining IT and operational technology data. The platform runs IoT applications where equipment is located—such as factories, refineries, vehicles, and cities—rather than in traditional data centers or the cloud. The apps aggregate data from devices including PLCs and SCADA systems and translate network addresses for subsets of larger networks, with remote management capabilities. The offerings build on HPE’s Edgeline Converged Edge systems and provide customers with a full solution from a single vendor.

The podcast examines how investors can balance cost, simplicity and convenience in an investment plan. Guest John Robertson, author of the revised second edition of The Value of Simple, discusses indexing options, robo-advisors, and the AutoInvest.ca cost-comparison tool; he also offers a Canadian index-investing course. The episode also assesses Vanguard’s new one-fund asset-allocation ETFs, which charge 0.22%, against index mutual funds. Their lower fees may not make switching worthwhile: fee savings depend on portfolio size, while mutual funds and robo-advisors support automatic investing and may be easier for inexperienced investors. One-fund ETFs are best for straightforward TFSA/RRSP portfolios and 60% or 80% equity targets. They offer less flexibility for multiple accounts, taxable holdings, or other allocations; the 60%-bond Conservative ETF is described as less attractive than GICs for conservative investors.

ESA inaugurated New Norcia 3, a 35-meter deep-space antenna at its New Norcia station in Western Australia. Expected to enter service in 2026, it will expand ESA’s communication capacity for current and planned Solar System missions, including Juice, Solar Orbiter, BepiColombo, Mars Express, Hera, Plato, Envision, Ariel, Ramses and Vigil. The antenna uses components cooled to about −263°C to detect weak distant signals and a 20kW amplifier to transmit commands across millions or billions of kilometers. It can also provide cross-support to NASA, JAXA, ISRO and commercial missions.

The €62.3 million project involved European and Australian companies, with €3 million from the Australian Space Agency, and is locally operated by CSIRO. New Norcia will become ESA’s first ground station with two deep-space antennas, complementing stations in Argentina and Spain. The inauguration also highlighted growing European-Australian cooperation in space communications, safety and mission operations.

Researchers led by UCL and Imperial College London used atomic force microscopy and biochemical experiments to reveal how polymyxin B kills Gram-negative bacteria. The antibiotic triggers surface bulges, causing active cells to rapidly produce and shed their protective outer membrane. This excessive shedding creates gaps that allow the drug to enter and kill the cell. Dormant bacteria do not produce the membrane, so polymyxins bind to them but cause little damage and do not kill them. When sugar awakened dormant cells and restarted membrane production, polymyxin B killed them after a 15-minute delay. The findings suggest that combining polymyxins with treatments that wake dormant bacteria or promote membrane production could improve effectiveness, and that antibiotic assessments should account for bacterial activity levels.

The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court’s ruling that General Hugh Mercer Corporation wrongfully terminated three at-will Holiday Inn cleaning maids for refusing required polygraph tests. It held that West Virginia public policy questions are matters of law and that an employer may not discharge an at-will employee for refusing such testing, even though exceptions may apply under W. Va. Code § 21-5-5b. Although the statute postdated the plaintiffs’ termination and was not controlling, the court viewed it as reflecting the state’s public policy protecting individual privacy. The case was remanded for further proceedings.

Justice Miller, joined by Justice Neely, dissented, arguing that no established public policy prohibited the discharges when they occurred, that the later statute should govern future cases, and that applying the majority’s new rule retroactively was unfair and unnecessary.

- After bus activation, the host initializes each SD card using ACMD41, which sets operating conditions and the OCR’s HCS bit. HCS=1 indicates support for SDHC/SDXC, while HCS=0 indicates support for neither. CMD8 expands ACMD41 with HCS and CCS; cards that do not respond to CMD8 require HCS=0. The host repeats ACMD41 for at least one second or until the OCR busy bit indicates readiness, issuing only CMD0 between attempts. Initialization must finish within one second. A ready response uses CCS=0 for SDSC and CCS=1 for SDHC or SDXC. SDXC initialization matches SDHC, with user-area capacity specified by C_SIZE and required to be at least 32 GB.

- Identification proceeds with CMD2 to obtain the card’s CID and CMD3 to assign a shorter relative card address. The card moves from identification to standby state after receiving an RCA, and the process is repeated for each card. Incompatible cards enter the inactive state. In UHS-I mode, the host repeats ACMD41 with HCS=1 and S18R=1 until ready, then checks CCS and S18A. If S18A=1, CMD11 initiates the 1.8 V voltage-switch sequence; if CMD11 receives no response, the host should power-cycle the card. CMD11 is legal in ready state, including while the card is locked. Sampling-point tuning uses repeated CMD19 transfers, mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD and optional for HOST-SDR-FD; a sequence of up to 40 CMD19 executions must complete within 150 ms.

- During identification, the host remains at fOD; data-transfer mode permits fPP operation. CMD9 retrieves the CSD, optional CMD4 configures identified cards, and CMD7 selects one card for transfer. Only one card can be in the transfer state at a time, while CMD7 with the reserved RCA 0x0000 returns all cards to standby. Data communication in transfer mode is point-to-point between the host and the selected card.

- Block reads use a maximum block size of 512 bytes and append CRC data. CMD17 reads one block, while CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12 stops the transfer. Writes likewise use CRC-protected blocks. Misaligned partial accesses are detected and reported through ADDRESS_ERROR, while write-protected regions produce WP_VIOLATION. CSD programming uses CRC-protected data and must match any ROM-backed portion of the register. Cards may buffer writes and indicate programming or a full buffer by holding DAT0 low; CMD13 reports status. Deselecting a card can interrupt its connection without stopping an active write, allowing host-managed interleaved operations on multiple cards.

- ACMD23 can specify a number of blocks to pre-erase before CMD25. If the write is stopped early, pre-erased blocks may contain either erased data or old data. Erase sequences use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; out-of-sequence commands reset the sequence and set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR. Write-protected sectors remain intact and set WP_ERASE_SKIP. Post-erase data is either 0 or 1 according to the SCR DATA_STAT_AFTER_ERASE field.

- DISCARD uses CMD38 with argument 00000001h and makes discarded contents “don’t care.” It is supported by SDHC and SDXC cards, not through SPI, and has a 250 ms busy timeout. FULE uses argument 00000002h to logically erase the entire user area, is likewise limited to SDHC/SDXC outside SPI, and has a one-second busy timeout. Unsupported cards execute normal ERASE instead.

- SD cards support mechanical, internal, and password-based write protection. Password data and length are stored in nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers. Locked cards accept basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and CMD42, but reject data access. Card lock/unlock operations require selection with CMD7, a block length set with CMD16, and a CRC-protected CMD42 data block containing the mode, password length, and password data.

- Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds a Force Erase Password in FEP and FEP_LEN. When FEP is set, normal force erase and password clearing are disabled, and CMD42[1Fh] COP Unlock is required after reset before other COP functions can be used. COP mode 2 supports FEP management, conditional force erase, and restriction of PWD reset while FEP is set. Force erase deletes the user area and PWD data, while leaving the secure area unchanged and clearing temporary and group write protection after completion. FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP and preserves the FEP registers. Failed lock, unlock, password, or COP operations set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. ACMD6 bus-width changes are rejected while the card is locked.

- CMD55 APP_CMD causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command. Defined, legal ACMDs are acknowledged with APP_CMD set; undefined but legal ACMDs are treated as regular commands; illegal ACMDs produce an illegal-command error. CMD56 GEN_CMD is reserved for application-specific use.

- CMD6 switches or queries card functions through mode 0 and mode 1. Its 512-bit status reports supported and selected functions, busy states, and maximum current or power consumption. Function 0 is the default and 0xF retains the current selection. Defined groups include access mode, command-system extension, UHS-I driver strength, and power limit; groups 1 and 3 are unused in UHS-II mode. UHS-I and UHS-II cards require power-limit configuration for higher performance. Selected functions must be ready before they can be changed.

- High-Speed mode is optional, uses a 50 MHz clock for a 25 MB/s interface, and requires the host to drive only one card with one-to-one CLK, CMD, and DAT connections. CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57 may be interpreted according to the selected command-system function.

- CMD8 is issued in idle state before ACMD41 to verify the host’s supply voltage. A compatible card returns R7 with the voltage range and check pattern echoed; an incompatible card does not respond.

- SDSC uses byte-addressed memory commands and a CMD16-selected block length. SDHC and SDXC use block addresses, fixed 512-byte blocks regardless of CMD16, and prohibit partial or misaligned access. SDHC and SDXC do not support write-protected groups.

A three-game Stanley Cup series against Tampa Bay has both teams eager for the opportunity. Despite strong performances by both goaltenders, Tampa Bay won the fast, hard-fought game. The losing team struggled to generate quality scoring chances and needs better breaks and a killer instinct over the next three games, though some players may benefit from rest.

Bishop Hassan Kukah of the Catholic Diocese of Sokoto urged politicians to deliver quality governance and warned that continued frustration could trigger military coups, while praising the military's patience in remaining in the barracks over 17 years of democracy. He criticised Nigeria's worsening governance, which he said has made the country "a laughing stock," and condemned politicians' use of religion to mask misgovernance, insisting that only those with the requisite skills should hold office regardless of faith. Kukah said Nigerians share blame for poor governance because they lack the courage to interrogate leaders' promises. On calls for a new coalition, he noted that issues surrounding the last elections persist and that the country is more divided than before the 2015 elections, and he urged government tolerance of opposing views. His centre launched a leadership forum, with Ghana's President Nana Akufo Addo due to deliver a lecture on sustaining democracy in Africa.

Police Chief Brian Manley appealed to those responsible for an 11-day package-bombing campaign in Austin, asking them to contact authorities before more people are harmed. Three bombings killed Draylen Mason, 17, and Anthony Stephan House, 39, and injured two women, one critically. All victims were Black or Hispanic, and authorities were investigating the attacks as a possible hate crime. Manley said the reward for information had increased to $100,000, plus $15,000 from the governor. With help from about 500 federal agents, police are seeking additional tips.

UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves has left open the possibility of tax increases ahead of November’s budget while reiterating her commitment to fiscal discipline. At Labour’s conference, she declined to rule out breaking manifesto tax pledges, including avoiding VAT increases, citing geopolitical instability, new U.S. tariffs and rising borrowing costs. Chief Treasury Secretary Darren Jones also declined to dismiss tax caps being broken. Market watchers cite a possible fiscal shortfall of up to £30 billion, though higher taxes could alienate voters expecting growth without additional household burdens. Reeves’s ambiguity preserves flexibility but leaves businesses and households uncertain, while signaling a preference for market credibility over firm political commitments.

On January 29, 2020, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K furnishing a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2019. The filing states that the report and Exhibit 99.1 are not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act and are not incorporated by reference except by specific reference.

A May 9, 2001 press roundup reported that Questia Media, an online college library and research service backed by Enron Chairman Ken Lay, cut 139 jobs, reducing its workforce to about 140 as it slowed book digitization because of difficulties raising additional capital. The company said paid subscribers had increased from just over 1,000 in early April to more than 5,000, and projected positive cash flow in about 18 months.

U.S. markets were mixed ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting. The Dow fell 51.66 points to 10,883.51, while the Nasdaq gained 25.20 points to 2,198.77. First-quarter worker productivity declined 0.1%, fueling inflation concerns and modestly raising long-term Treasury yields. Enron shares fell $1.93 to $56.11.

Enron officials said Japan’s deregulated electricity market lacked real competition because of regulatory barriers, costly transmission access and other obstacles; newcomers supplied only 0.2% of power. They called for an independent regulator, citing concerns about the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry’s ties to incumbent utilities. Williams also planned a London-based European operation with 25 employees to provide energy trading and risk-management services, initially covering the UK, Germany, Scandinavia and Benelux, with Spain and Italy as early targets.

Most coverage concerned Enron’s troubled Dabhol project in India. The Maharashtra State Electricity Board denied underusing its own capacity to justify purchasing Dabhol power, said 95% of that power supported grid frequency, and maintained that expanding its Uran plant would be uneconomic because of high fuel costs. MSEB said it faced no federal pressure to continue the agreement, while an RSS-linked organization demanded a judicial probe and cancellation of the deal.

An unsourced report said families of Enron executives were relocating from Mumbai to Singapore and security had been tightened, potentially indicating preparations to withdraw; Enron declined to comment. MSEB appointed a former high-court judge as arbitrator in a London-based arbitration, while lenders indicated support for terminating the power purchase agreement. Enron had invoked guarantees and political force majeure after MSEB withheld payments and assessed penalty bills.

Prize Petroleum also sought Enron’s 30% interest in the Panna, Mukta and Tapti offshore fields, valuing it at about Rs 600 crore within a planned Rs 1,900 crore investment.

The California Court of Appeal affirmed the denial of the mother’s request for custody of her young son, Edward. The court found it unnecessary to determine whether the Nevada divorce decree validly awarded custody because the father had undisputed actual custody from 1946 until a 1949 visit, after which the mother retained Edward contrary to his father’s wishes. Although both parents were equally fit and had suitable homes, the child’s best interests, stability of his home life, and continuity of his established living arrangements were controlling. The court found no abuse of discretion in continuing Edward’s custody with the father and held that the trial judge’s remarks could not impeach the judgment.

The lecture introduces ordinary differential equation initial value problems (ODE-IVPs), written as \(dy/dt=f(y)\), with all initial conditions specified at one value of \(t\). Higher-order equations can be converted to first-order systems by introducing state variables, enabling the use of MATLAB solvers such as ODE45. Numerical solutions typically return a vector of time points and a matrix of corresponding \(y\)-values, useful for plotting or obtaining final values. Integration may proceed forward, backward, or in both directions.

Forward Euler applies a first-order Taylor approximation, \(y_{n+1}=y_n+\Delta t\,f(y_n)\). Its local error is order \(\Delta t^2\), but accumulated global error is only order \(\Delta t\), making improved accuracy computationally expensive. Trapezoidal and midpoint methods yield second-order accuracy, while higher-order Runge–Kutta methods cancel additional low-order errors. A second-order Runge–Kutta method estimates the midpoint state using Forward Euler and requires two function evaluations. MATLAB’s ODE45 combines fourth- and fifth-order estimates and uses their difference to adapt the step size.

Numerical stability depends on the matrix \(I+\Delta t\,dg/dy\). Errors are amplified when this matrix is too large; stable methods diminish earlier errors. Equations with positive Jacobian eigenvalues are intrinsically unstable, as in explosions and positive-feedback systems. Even intrinsically stable equations can become unstable through an unsuitable numerical method. For example, Forward Euler applied to \(dy/dt=-2y\) with \(\Delta t=1\) produces an oscillating sawtooth, while larger steps cause explosive oscillations; steps below \(1/2\) behave more reasonably. The textbook discusses stability conditions for various methods, and homework requires writing and comparing ODE solvers.

The ADS868xW devices support single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs with straight-binary output. The full-scale range equals the positive and negative full-scale voltages, and each LSB equals FSR/2¹⁶.

Alarm functionality includes programmable high- and low-input thresholds with adjustable hysteresis and fixed AVDD thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. An active-high ALARM output, internal active and tripped flags, or appended output flags can report alarm conditions. Input and AVDD alarms are enabled by default and can be disabled independently.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI programming and single- or dual-SDO data reads, including source-synchronous operation with internal or external clock sources. Daisy-chain configurations share CONVST/CS and SCLK, propagate data through SDO-0, and require an optimal frame of 32 × N SCLK edges for N devices.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST input supports application reset or full power-on reset. A CONVST/CS rising edge starts conversion, after which the device returns to ACQ; the host can monitor RVS or wait for the maximum conversion time.

Data-transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on its rising edge, which also initiates conversion. The device presents a 32-bit input/output shift register. Short frames cannot write commands, optimal 32-clock frames provide valid commands, and in long frames the last 32 bits constitute the command. Byte and half-word read, write, set, and clear commands are supported. Output data can contain conversion results, register data, fixed test patterns, device addresses, range flags, alarm flags, and parity according to programming.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power functions, SDI and SDO protocols, output data formatting, input-range and reference selection, alarm status, and input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Writes to protected reset/power-control bits require the key 69h.

An industrial input-module example combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to provide eight software-configured voltage or current channels. The example supports standard industrial ranges and uses the ADC’s integrated reference, driver, programmable gain, fast settling, and alarm protections.

The device uses separate analog and digital supplies. Recommended decoupling includes at least 10 µF and 1 µF capacitors on AVDD and a minimum 10 µF capacitor on DVDD. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption while retaining low-power operation and, for power-down, interface activity and register contents. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital sections, keeps supply and reference decoupling close to device pins, minimizes vias, and uses low-impedance ground paths.

The chapter presents a framework for representing and validating digital business processes in extended enterprises, where organizations collaborate across company boundaries. Its Model Driven Architecture approach divides business process models into three complementary layers: a static domain model describing actors, resources, and other entities; a workflow model specifying activities and their orchestration; and a value model describing value exchanges and profitability. Shared business-rule terminology links these layers.

Business rules are commonly expressed through controlled natural languages such as Attempto Controlled English and SBVR, which support knowledge sharing while enabling translation into formal logic. The chapter discusses grounding rules in description logics, OWL, RuleML, and SWRL, and argues for hybrid reasoning that combines description-logic reasoning for open-world knowledge with Horn-rule execution for complete, closed-world data. Particular attention is given to distinguishing open and closed entities, preserving incomplete information, combining OWL and SWRL without losing semantics, and interpreting alethic and deontic business-rule modalities without sacrificing tractability or expressiveness.

Process flows may be represented graphically with standards such as BPMN and UML Activity Diagrams or more formally through Petri nets, π-calculus, situation calculus, and temporal logic. Because dynamic and concurrent behavior can cause state-space explosion, symbolic model checking and fairness constraints are discussed. Declarative representations remain useful for consistency checking, data export, and annotation. A BPMN example illustrates how static concepts, task relationships, exchanged messages, and runtime log data can be used to verify structural and dynamic process requirements.

Value models describe actors, value transfers, dependencies, and expected profitability. The chapter presents graphical approaches based on REA and e3-value modeling and a Prolog-style first-order logic representation in which constructs, connections, quantities, and estimated values become predicates and equations. These models permit a priori calculation of collaboration profitability and support decision-making.

The three model layers are related through consistency checks rather than equivalence because they address different aspects of the same system. Static consistency compares value exchanges with process messages and dependencies; semi-dynamic consistency tests whether value-model forecasts are achievable by the workflow; dynamic consistency compares expected behavior with operational system logs. Monitoring tools can compare realized exchanges with original estimates and reason about their effects, while process mining can derive process models from logs. Persistent issues include identifying changes needed when a model fails, representing stakeholders’ reasons for actions, and incorporating customer perspectives.

The article examines digital storytelling (DST) in African higher education and teacher training through a qualitative document analysis. Fifteen studies published from 2000 onward were selected from 35 records using a PRISMA-based process. The literature was sourced from Google Scholar, ERIC, JSTOR, ResearchGate, and other platforms, with most included studies adopting qualitative methods.

Digital storytelling combines digital and traditional media—such as text, images, narration, music, and video—to create and share personal narratives. Its production involves pre-production planning, visualization and narration, assembly of media elements, and presentation to an audience for feedback.

The reviewed studies indicate that DST promotes empowerment and identity expression, cultural enrichment, student engagement and motivation, creativity, collaboration, digital and media literacy, critical and reflective thinking, problem-solving, technological competence, and improved communication skills. It has supported community building among culturally diverse students, oral proficiency, map-reading, postgraduate research participation, cultural and linguistic preservation, and social activism. Applications include pre-service teacher education, geography instruction, language learning, rural education, research documentation, and assessments, although narrative content should be emphasized over the technology itself.

Despite these benefits, implementation is constrained by inadequate electricity, equipment, infrastructure, time, curricular rigidity, limited technological proficiency, and low teacher confidence. Group work using smartphones was proposed as one way to address equipment shortages. Overall, the literature presents DST as an adaptable educational approach that combines cultural knowledge, creative expression, and technology while requiring attention to practical and contextual barriers.

Steve Wynn’s attorneys said in March 2018 court documents that he settled in 2006 with a second woman who accused him of sexual misconduct. After the Wall Street Journal reported several allegations against him, the woman sought to speak publicly; Wynn and an attorney accused her of extortion, while her attorney denied it. Wynn denied the misconduct allegations and resigned as chairman and CEO of Wynn Resorts.

Jeremy Corbyn’s taxpayer-provided Ford Galaxy waited 40 minutes on double yellow lines outside his Islington home before driving him to Westminster. The diesel car emits 189g of CO2, averages 36 mpg and falls in the £280-a-year vehicle tax band, prompting criticism of hypocrisy from Tory MP Andrew Bridgen over Corbyn’s frequent air-pollution advocacy. Corbyn, a keen cyclist who owns no car, accepted a Government Car Service vehicle with a chauffeur in 2015, reportedly for security reasons, despite living near a Tube station. The report also notes his disputed 2016 claim that he was forced to sit on the floor of a crowded Virgin train, and Labour’s commitments to phasing out diesel cars, introducing clean-air zones and passing a new Clean Air Act.

Brazil’s CPFL Energia launched Envo to serve growing demand for residential solar power, offering equipment, installation, grid connection, and sale of excess electricity. The company aims to capitalize on rising grid connections and consumer interest in lowering bills and addressing environmental impacts; Santander Brasil will finance customers.

The lecture introduces atomic, molecular, and optical (AMO) physics as a low-energy quantum field centered on atoms, molecules, photons, and electromagnetic fields. Its paradigmatic systems are the hydrogen atom, two-level systems, and harmonic oscillators. The field has evolved from studying individual gas-phase particles and collisions toward few-body and many-body physics, entanglement, quantum gases, and overlap with condensed-matter physics, including optical control of mechanical oscillators.

AMO physics is distinguished by its ability to control nature, not merely observe it. Progress has moved from controlling internal states through optical pumping, to controlling motion through laser cooling and Bose–Einstein condensation, and then to manipulating single atoms and photons. Current aims include assembling these building blocks into entangled, strongly correlated, many-body states. This progress has been enabled by increasingly accessible and robust solid-state lasers, ultrashort and high-intensity laser pulses, frequency combs for precise frequency control and metrology, and high-finesse cavities for single-photon research.

The course, MIT 8.422, is the second part of a graduate AMO sequence and may be taken before or after 8.421. Its topics include QED and light–atom interactions, the dipole approximation, spontaneous emission and dissipation, open-system methods, mechanical forces of light, trapping and cooling, single photons, quantum information, and many-body quantum gases. It excludes high-energy collisions, advanced atomic structure, and high-intensity or short-pulse laser topics. Students complete ten problem sets and a term paper, with no midterm or final.

An extended example uses atoms in an optical lattice to connect several course topics. Two interfering laser beams create a periodic potential that can be described through classical, quantum-optical, photon-based, and microscopic perspectives. Spontaneous emission enables Sisyphus cooling, while deep lattices isolate atoms for high-precision optical clocks; magic wavelengths decouple clock transitions from lattice motion. Shallow lattices permit tunneling and exhibit band structure, Bose–Einstein condensate–Mott-insulator transitions, and fermionic Mott behavior. Pulsed lattices can act as beam splitters in atom interferometers for measuring gravity, rotation, acceleration, and other inertial quantities, and can impart energy and momentum to strongly interacting many-body systems to measure their dynamic structure factor. The lecturer’s own work with Bose–Einstein condensates illustrates how an experiment intended for atom interferometry became a many-body physics experiment, encapsulating the field’s combination of precision control, entanglement, and many-body research.

The passage presents a broad HBO Max viewing guide covering drama, comedy, crime, true crime, documentary, science fiction, fantasy, anime, and reality programming. It recommends new or returning seasons alongside older favorites, including Peacemaker’s second season; the Joel and Ellie fungal-pandemic zombie drama; Deborah Vance and Ava Daniels’s mentorship story; the Gemstone televangelist satire; the Roy family’s media-empire succession drama; the Barry hitman series; and a Pittsburgh hospital drama told in real time. Comedic selections cover luxury-resort mysteries, New York high society, 18th-century pirates, teachers at an underfunded school, and a space captain dealing with catastrophe.

Documentaries focus on Ruby Franke and Jodi Hildebrandt, the 1991 Austin murders, Robert Durst, murders of gay men during the AIDS crisis, and the ethics of keeping a chimpanzee as a pet. Reality programming includes The Challenge and Project Greenlight, while genre entries include a Frank Herbert prequel, a Targaryen-family prequel, and two anime series. The guide also notes awards, acclaimed casts, renewals, cancellations, and upcoming seasons.
Labubu, inspired by Hong Kong’s toy culture and popularized by a Thai K-pop star, became 2025’s biggest Gen-Z cultural trend.

Stettinius urged negotiators to approach the general conference with open minds, few formal commitments, and flexibility, since fixed positions would be difficult to revise. Dumbarton Oaks proposals were deliberately kept informal in case modification was needed. Discussions addressed objections to the proposed name “United Nations,” the possible enumeration of organizational principles, and Security Council voting procedures. Roosevelt reportedly anticipated compromise with Soviet demands for unanimity.

In January 1945, Stettinius directed that six Latin American “associated nations” be warned they could be excluded from the initial United Nations Conference unless they declared war on an enemy. He also accelerated preparations for the Big Three, conference arrangements, and the American delegation. The Yalta Conference was considered especially important, although Stettinius’s Crimea notes were not found in Department files.

University of Utah researchers mapped the shallow geology and hydrothermal plumbing beneath Old Faithful using 133 portable seismometers, ambient-vibration analysis, and hydrothermal features as seismic sources. A 2015 survey detected about 60 minutes of intense tremors before eruptions, followed by roughly 30 minutes of quiet; eruptions occurred at the end of the tremors rather than at their peak. The researchers estimated that Old Faithful’s reservoir—a network of water-filled cracks and fractures—has a diameter of about 200 meters and holds approximately 300,000 cubic meters of water, compared with about 30 cubic meters released per eruption. The study, prompted in part by the National Park Service’s need to manage structures built over thermal features, was published in *Geophysical Research Letters* with Sin-Mei Wu as first author. Ongoing work includes examining how air temperature affects seismic waves, modeling earthquake-wave reverberation, and applying similar methods in Norris Geyser Basin.

The First Circuit affirmed the denial of Ronald L. Johnson’s habeas petition challenging the admission of his confession to armed robbery and the killing of a police officer. After being apprehended, Johnson was held for approximately eight and one-half hours, underwent four lineups, and then made a recorded confession during a forty-minute interrogation without having been advised of his right to counsel or given Miranda warnings.

Applying the pre-Escobedo and pre-Miranda “totality of the circumstances” standard, the court independently reviewed the record and found the confession voluntary. Although Johnson had suffered injuries, had slept and eaten little, had a sixth-grade education and an IQ of 86, encountered large numbers of police, and received no rights warnings, these factors did not establish coercion. Police had not inflicted his injuries or threatened him, and he remained alert and actively resisted police during booking, participated in the lineups, and challenged the witnesses’ identifications. His prior police experience and confrontational conduct also weighed against the claim that his will was overborne. The court therefore declined to address whether Lego applied retroactively or whether the trial court had failed to consider the totality of circumstances.

Eighteen researchers, including 13 based in the U.S., received French President Emmanuel Macron’s “Make Our Planet Great Again” climate grants to conduct research in France. Camille Parmesan plans five years at an experimental ecology station in the Pyrenees, while Benjamin Sanderson will work in Toulouse. Both welcomed France’s support amid declining U.S. climate research funding and support under President Donald Trump.

The study evaluated the Healthy Davis Together program, launched in Davis, California, in September 2020 and expanded to Yolo County as Healthy Yolo Together in July 2021. The program provided free asymptomatic testing alongside public education, protective-equipment distribution, isolation support, community engagement, and local economic assistance. From November 18, 2020, through June 30, 2022, HDT/HYT conducted 770,165 tests among 89,924 Yolo County residents, including 53,869 Davis residents. This represented approximately 41.1% of Yolo County’s population and 78.4% of Davis residents. Most tests were saliva-based PCR tests (98.4%), with 1.6% rapid antigen tests.

Testing was analyzed across Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, and Post-Omicron periods. Daily testing per 100,000 residents rose from 422 before Delta to 746 during Delta and peaked at 895 during Omicron before falling to 435 after Omicron. New participants declined from 39,819 in the initial period to 2,788 after Omicron. Omicron had the highest testing volume, frequent-test participation, and proportion of positive cases. Overall, 12,626 tests were positive among 11,545 people.

Participation was at least 25% across race/ethnicity and age groups below 85, while the group older than 85 had the lowest participation. Highest positivity occurred among American Indian/Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander, and Latino participants and among people aged 20–44.

Among adults, 12,591 of 67,083 participants were frequent testers, defined as testing multiple times within 15 days. Frequent testing was most common among women, people aged 19–34, and White participants. The authors concluded that the program broadly engaged residents and retained users throughout the pandemic. Proposed contributors to the post-Omicron decline included pandemic fatigue, reduced risk perception associated with vaccination, availability of home tests, distrust, and misinformation; however, the data could not establish the reasons for observed differences.

Worcester paid over $11 million in overtime in 2017; police, fire and Public Works workers collectively received more than $7 million. Police earned $4,399,365, and officials attributed overtime to late calls, training, protests, grants and specialized programs rather than understaffing. Police detail pay totaled $9,326,718; George Kelly earned $100,384, exceeding his $75,508 salary. John Towns had the most police overtime at $59,577, while Hermes Rivera received the most Public Works overtime at $40,122. Worcester had 7,287 city employees, 223 earning over $100,000. City Manager Edward Augustus Jr. was the highest-paid employee, and only two of the top 50 earners were women.

The article examines how walking, an ordinary bodily and sensory activity, can become an aesthetic experience through art-based practices. Drawing on place-based critical art education and aesthetic inquiry, it presents walking as a means of questioning identity, place, community, and social hierarchies while developing sensory and critical awareness.

A 10-week study was conducted in 2023 with seven prospective teachers in an undergraduate fine arts program in western Türkiye. Following online instruction after the 2023 earthquake, participants incorporated walking into their daily routines. Data included visual diaries, course texts, class recordings, artworks, and final interviews. The researchers used art-based and interpretive methods, thematic analysis with axial coding, triangulation, participant validation, and multiple coders.

Participants wrote about their prior understandings of walking, documented walking moments in diaries, examined Francis Alÿs’s *The Collector* through aesthetic inquiry, took and questioned photographs, and created artworks based on their experiences. Initially, they regarded walking as simple physical movement; through repeated walks, sensory observation, visual inquiry, and artistic production, they developed broader and more personal interpretations involving freedom, self-discovery, health, technology, memory, urban life, social issues, and environmental conditions. Their observations of people, animals, buildings, sounds, city rhythms, isolation, and belonging shaped works including videos, performances, collages, and digital art.

The study found that art-based engagement helped participants connect daily life with art and education, expand multiple perspectives, strengthen visual and aesthetic awareness, and reconsider their relationships with place. Walking also emerged as a possible teaching tool for incorporating subjective everyday experience into lesson plans. Participants nevertheless reported difficulties visualizing feelings, selecting subjects, producing visually appealing work, working with materials, filming, and performing in public. The authors conclude that participatory, community-based art and walking-based research can support aesthetic experience and the training of teachers whose work connects art, life, and education.

India’s Supreme Court has ordered that parties may no longer seek votes based on religion, caste, community or language. The author argues that the ruling wrongly treats identity-based politics as inherently harmful and overlooks how marginalised groups have used voting and political organisation to challenge entrenched hierarchies and gain representation. The article distinguishes this mobilisation from rabid communalism, which fuels riots and insecurity, and says it persists because of impunity and weak enforcement rather than judicial bans. It contends that Hindutva must be confronted politically as voters increasingly prioritise development, delivery and public goods alongside identity concerns. The order is also described as impractical because identity-based appeals remain widespread across Indian elections and the court lacks an enforcement mechanism.

Indiana reported 278 flu deaths, and IU Health said flu season could last until mid-April. Experts said contaminated surfaces can spread influenza and norovirus; flu may survive about a day, while norovirus can remain viable for days or weeks. A handwashing test found 15 bacterial types on hands, with little difference before and after washing, prompting advice to scrub harder and longer. A phone test found normal mouth, throat and skin bacteria, but phones can transfer pathogens to the face. Experts advised using regular soap, washing for 20–30 seconds, scrubbing thoroughly, and washing before eating and after bathroom use, diaper changes or caring for sick people.

Mr. Kim and Mr. Gates have argued that large pools of private capital can earn substantial returns by investing in developing markets, and Mr. Kim has frequently cited Abraaj founder Arif Naqvi as a model. Abraaj’s $1 billion health care fund raised $545 million starting in late 2016 to buy hospitals in Nigeria, Pakistan and India. By September, investors said more than $200 million was uninvested. After Naqvi cited regulatory delays and a 60-day repayment requirement, he returned over $100 million in December. Investors requested an independent auditor and proof that the money had not financed Abraaj’s operations; Abraaj hired KPMG, and a World Bank review found no evidence of wrongdoing. The World Bank had invested $300 million in Abraaj, including $100 million in the fund, while the Gates Foundation invested $100 million. The fund invested only about half its capital. Its $145 million purchase of hospital network CARE saw annual earnings fall from $14 million to $8 million, and Abraaj did not mark down the investment. Naqvi was seeking to raise $6 billion for a new fund focused on 30 developing countries.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal third quarter ended July 1, 2023 reported third-quarter net sales of $81.797 billion, down 1% from $82.959 billion a year earlier. The decline primarily reflected lower iPhone and iPad sales, partially offset by higher Services sales. Gross margin increased to $36.413 billion, or 44.5%, while operating income remained nearly unchanged at $22.998 billion. Net income rose to $19.881 billion from $19.442 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased to $1.26 from $1.20.

For the first nine months, net sales declined 3% to $293.787 billion, operating income fell to $87.332 billion, and net income declined to $74.039 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $4.67, compared with $4.82. Research and development expense increased, primarily because of higher headcount-related expenses. The effective tax rate fell to 12.5% for the quarter and 14.6% for the nine months.

Third-quarter sales increased 8% for Services and 2% for Wearables, Home and Accessories, while iPhone sales fell 2%, Mac sales 7%, and iPad sales 20%. By geographic segment, third-quarter sales rose 5% in Europe and 8% in Greater China, but declined 6% in the Americas, 11% in Japan, and 8% in the rest of Asia Pacific. Currency weakness against the U.S. dollar adversely affected sales, particularly in Japan and Greater China.

At July 1, 2023, Apple held $28.408 billion in cash and equivalents, $34.074 billion in current marketable securities, and $104.061 billion in noncurrent marketable securities. Total assets were $335.038 billion, total liabilities were $274.764 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $60.274 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $88.945 billion, while financing activities used $85.335 billion. Manufacturing purchase obligations totaled $38.4 billion, with $38.1 billion payable within 12 months.

Apple repurchased 102.673 million shares for $18.0 billion during the quarter and paid $3.8 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. It also authorized an additional $90 billion share-repurchase program in May 2023.

The European Commission’s State Aid Decision remains under appeal, with a European Court of Justice decision expected in 2024. The App Store external-links injunction involving Epic remains stayed pending further appeal. Apple’s disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes in internal control over financial reporting, risk factors, or market risk during the reporting period.

The passage examines how Canada’s #MeToo reckoning prompted rapid political resignations, including Nova Scotia PC leader Jamie Baillie, Ontario PC leader Patrick Brown, and Liberal MP Kent Hehr, despite allegations remaining unproven. It rejects claims that #MeToo is inherently unfair, arguing that parties must hold leaders to higher standards and that responses to misconduct reveal how they value women. Although skepticism about delayed allegations can be valid, current disclosures reflect a climate in which women are increasingly believed. Fairness requires initially presuming accusers are truthful until evidence emerges, while recognizing the presumption of innocence. The author concludes that #MeToo must be fair but that dismissing women perpetuates abuse and cannot be defended as the status quo.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018 reports:

- **Financial results:** Q3 net sales were $56.576 billion, up 29% from $43.744 billion a year earlier; nine-month sales were $160.504 billion, up 37% from $117.413 billion. Q3 product and service sales were $33.746 billion and $22.830 billion, respectively. Operating income rose to $3.724 billion from $347 million in Q3 and to $8.635 billion from $1.979 billion for the nine months. Net income increased to $2.883 billion from $256 million in Q3 and to $7.046 billion from $1.176 billion for the nine months. Diluted EPS was $5.75 for Q3 and $14.10 for the nine months, compared with $0.52 and $2.39.

- **Segments:** Q3 North America, International, and AWS sales were $34.348 billion, $15.549 billion, and $6.679 billion, respectively, representing growth of 35%, 13%, and 46%. Nine-month sales were $97.242 billion, $45.037 billion, and $18.225 billion, up 41%, 24%, and 48%. Q3 operating income was $2.032 billion in North America and $2.077 billion in AWS, while International reported a $385 million operating loss. For the nine months, North America and AWS generated operating income of $5.015 billion and $5.119 billion, respectively, and International’s operating loss was $1.499 billion. North American and International growth primarily reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller sales, advertising sales, and slower expense growth; AWS growth primarily reflected increased customer usage and cost productivity.

- **Cash and balance sheet:** Operating cash flow was $8.588 billion in Q3 and $14.246 billion for the nine months, compared with $3.777 billion and $6.007 billion in the prior-year periods. Nine-month investing and financing cash flows used $8.797 billion and $5.925 billion, respectively. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash ended at $21.032 billion, while cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $29.8 billion at fair value. Total assets were $143.695 billion and stockholders’ equity was $39.125 billion at September 30, 2018.

- **Acquisitions, debt, and commitments:** Amazon acquired Ring for approximately $839 million and PillPack for approximately $753 million, net of acquired cash, plus other acquisitions totaling $46 million. The combined $1.638 billion purchase price included $1.222 billion of goodwill and $671 million of intangible assets. The company had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and $535 million drawn under its seller-receivables credit facility. It also established $7.0 billion commercial paper and revolving credit programs, with no borrowings outstanding at quarter-end. Contractual commitments totaled $124.425 billion, while purchase obligations and open purchase orders totaled $15.7 billion.

- **Accounting changes:** Amazon adopted new revenue-recognition guidance on January 1, 2018 using the modified retrospective method, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million. Prime memberships became a single performance obligation recognized over the membership period, contributing to a $2.6 billion reclassification from product sales to service sales for the nine months; advertising reclassifications increased service sales by approximately $2.0 billion. New income-tax guidance increased retained earnings by approximately $250 million, and restricted cash was added retrospectively to the cash-flow statements. Operating leases exceeding 12 months will be recorded as assets and liabilities beginning January 1, 2019.

- **Taxes and contingencies:** Tax contingencies increased to approximately $3.4 billion and were expected to grow. The IRS was seeking approximately $1.5 billion of additional federal tax related to transfer pricing and had appealed the U.S. Tax Court’s decision. Luxembourg deposited an estimated €250 million state-aid recovery into escrow, and both Luxembourg and Amazon were appealing the European Commission’s decision. Amazon also faced potential indirect-tax liabilities, including a South Carolina assessment concerning third-party seller transactions, and remained under OFAC and BIS review regarding orders involving sanctioned individuals and entities that could result in penalties.

- **Estimates and liquidity:** Critical estimates included inventory valuation and income taxes. Each additional 1% of inventory valuation allowance would have increased cost of sales by approximately $175 million. Amazon stated that operating cash flow, cash and marketable securities, and borrowing arrangements were sufficient to meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least the following 12 months.

Indiana is considering outcomes-based contracts with private tutoring companies to improve reading among sixth- and seventh-graders with poor scores, tying much of the payment to student gains. Education Secretary Katie Jenner said contract terms and funding sources—including state money, donations and grants—remain unsettled.

The approach expanded after the pandemic as districts used relief funds for incentive-based tutoring. Research has found promising results and improved collaboration and data tracking, but evidence remains limited and mixed. Attendance, motivation and imperfect progress measures create risks for vendors. Other states and districts have reported some gains, though some abandoned or are still evaluating the model.

The Center for Outcomes-Based Contracting, which supports 60 districts and agencies, reports that about half of 2025 contract goals were achieved and vendors earned roughly 68% of possible bonuses. It recommends making at least 40% of contracts contingent on clearly defined student gains. Indiana officials acknowledge that improving outcomes among struggling readers will be especially difficult.
